title: Asymmetries in Legal Status and Market Conditions Between Southeast European and Eu Transport Operators
abstract: The economic and legal disparities between transport operators from Southeast Europe and those based in the European Union significantly influence competitiveness, market access, and operational efficiency within the international transport sector. This paper analyzes the consequences of differing regulatory frameworks, licensing requirements, labor standards, and financial obligations that shape the business environment for non-EU carriers. Special emphasis is placed on cabotage restrictions, bilateral transport agreements, compliance with EU road transport regulations, and the impact of the EU Mobility Package on third-country operators. From an economic perspective, the study examines cost structures, barriers to market entry, competitive pressures, and the resulting asymmetries in service pricing and fleet modernization. Legally, it evaluates issues related to jurisdiction, enforcement, permit quotas, and alignment with EU acquis. The findings indicate that unequal regulatory burdens create structural disadvantages for Southeast European carriers, affecting their long-term sustainability, regional integration, and capacity to compete fairly within the European transport market. The paper highlights potential pathways for harmonization and policy adjustments aimed at fostering a more balanced and equitable transport ecosystem. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The dynamics of customer participation in service recovery: The roles of failure severity, quality signals, and responsiveness
abstract: In high-contact hospitality settings, service failures can disrupt encounters in ways that prompt customers to intervene. Drawing on control theory and signaling theory, we conceptualize customer participation (CP) as a solution-oriented behavioral response through which customers attempt to influence recovery when service delivery is disrupted. We examine how quality signals and frontline employee responsiveness shape the extent to which participation translates into recovery outcomes. Across five studies, we show that severe service failures can prompt solution-oriented participation, but this response is contingent on contextual conditions. Quality signals attenuate the likelihood that failure severity translates into participation by shifting perceived responsibility toward the firm, creating a conditional quality signaling paradox. Employee responsiveness strengthens the positive effects of participation once enacted, but cannot compensate when participation is not initiated. These findings advance an understanding of CP by distinguishing between participation initiation and effectiveness, with managerial implications for balancing quality signaling and responsive frontline behavior. © 2026

title: The Methods of User Journey Map Development and Deployment with Cost-Benefit Evaluation
abstract: The article outlines the methods of creating and developing Customer and User Journey Maps (CJM, UJM) as a tool for forming an effective user experience in digital products. A brand-new hybrid approach to CJM building was introduced, combining graph models and Markov chains to map customers’ behavior on the web. Special attention was paid to UX/UI design principles integration, accessibility, and customer testing tools. The algorithm of prioritizing interface design changes based on a multi-criteria quality function was presented. The multi-criteria quality function addresses rejection factors, levels of user satisfaction, and compliance with WCAG standards indicators. An experimental approbation of the approach based on the web-platform prototype with relevant users’ interaction data was held. The obtained results show a decrease in rejection probability along with upscaling usability and accessibility levels. The suggested method is recommended for implementation in website development, mobile app development, and interactive service development to enhance business process efficiency and user experience quality. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Women in Business in the 21st Century: Challenges of the Socio-Economic Transition in Specific Contexts
abstract: This paper explores the perspectives of women in business in specific contexts of the Western Balkans, with a focus on Bosnia and Herzegovina with additional data. Women in business are increasingly recognized as a vital driver not only of economic growth and poverty reduction, but of overall improvements in living standards within transition contexts. Despite the significant progress made by women in business in the Western Balkans region, they continue to face numerous socio-economic challenges that hinder their full potential. The paper provides an analysis of the key obstacles and stereotypes that persist for women in business in the 21st century in these specific contexts. Particular attention is paid to the challenges of reconciling professional and family responsibilities, which often limit women’s participation in business activities, especially in rural and smaller communities. On the other hand, the paper also highlights new opportunities and positive developments in recent years, as digital technologies, social media and online platforms offer women wider market access and flexibility in organizing their business operations. The paper concludes that empowering women in business is crucial both for sustainable economic development, but also for fostering needed social equality and broader progress for contexts in transition. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: State-Owned Enterprises in Bosnia And Herzegovina: Footprint, Performance and Fiscal Impact
abstract: This paper assesses the footprint, performance, and fiscal impact of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s SOEs within a fragmented, multi-level governance system. Using a consolidated dataset of 542 SOEs (2021–2024), we benchmark outcomes against private firms and regional norms via ratio analysis focusing on ROA, ROE/ROC, revenue per employee, leverage, and liquidity metrics. Findings show persistent structural underperformance. SOEs control assets near 82% of GDP and employ 9% of the workforce yet record negative returns and roughly 50% lower productivity. Using a conservative repayment-capacity screen, we estimate high-risk short-term liabilities of about 5.4% of GDP that are likely to require government intervention. While leverage ratios are comparable to those observed in peer countries in Central and Eastern Europe, rising liabilities, weak short-term repayment capacity, tax arrears, and reliance on budget transfers indicate increasing fiscal risks. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The hub location and pricing problem under a tree topology: a bilevel formulation and a co-evolutionary algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces the bilevel tree-of-hubs location and pricing problem, a multiple-allocation hub location problem in which both the design and pricing of a tree-shaped hub backbone network are determined. Two types of decision-makers are considered: a leader, who defines the network structure and sets usage prices, and a follower, who selects the optimal way to use the network for shipping commodities. The leader aims to maximize profit, while the follower seeks to minimize transportation costs. A bilevel optimization formulation is proposed and reformulated into a single-level equivalent model. To solve it efficiently, we develop a Co-Evolutionary Algorithm (Co-EA) and test it on three well-known datasets adapted to our problem. The novelty of the proposed Co-EA lies in the interaction between its co-evolving populations: rather than representing leader and follower solutions separately, each population is associated with a subset of the leader's decision variables. For each leader decision, the follower's optimal response is computed, ensuring bilevel feasibility. Extensive computational experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed Co-EA compared with general-purpose solvers applied to the reformulated model. The best Co-EA solutions are also used as warm-starts for the exact solver, confirming the quality of the heuristic results. Finally, managerial insights are derived regarding how the number of hubs affects the backbone network configuration. The paper concludes with directions for future research on bilevel hub location and pricing models. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

title: What Matters to Them? Generation Z and Their Expectations as Future Employees: A Research Path Towards Comparing Two Contexts
abstract: The focus of this paper is on Generation Z (Gen Z), currently consisting of young people, as it is the latest generation that is entering the labor market. As other generations, Gen Z is distinguished by its characteristics, influencing their working behaviors. Yet, despite being called a global generation - as they share common elucidation that influences them worldwide - Gen Z do not share the same personal values and life experiences. This presents a challenge for researchers to reveal an insight into their differences regarding life values and work attitudes, for business endowment. The aim of this paper is to portray a research path for analyzing the differences related to life values and work attitudes of Generation Z in two different contexts of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Slovenia. Research opportunity is interesting nowadays, as two countries share deep interrelationship as part of intense changes in global work boundaries due to migration, as implies possible direction to human resource (HR) attraction and retention strategies, as well as multicultural and multigenerational management HR strategies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Model for the Assessment of Financial Reporting Quality in Contemporary Management
abstract: The quality of financial information is a key assumption for making efficient business decisions. Assessing the quality of financial statements, as a complex non-financial aspect of information, requires consideration of several factors that influence their reliability and relevance. This paper analyzes the quality of financial statements based on the structure and oscillations of their elements, as well as through key financial and analytical indicators. The goal of the paper is the development of a model that enables a quick and simple assessment of the level of quality of financial statements and the level of confidence in the presented information, including the assessment of the probability of the existence of a significant substantive error. Empirical research was conducted on a sample of companies from Bosnia and Herzegovina whose securities were traded on the Sarajevo and Banja Luka Stock Exchanges for a period of 6 years, and the sample includes a total of 100 companies. The condition for the selection of the sample was the continuous six-year public publication of financial and audit reports. Binomial logistic regression was used for modeling, where the dependent variable is the quality of financial statements, and the independent variables are selected, characteristic elements of financial statements. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Basic Principles of Motivation as an Object of Management Influence on the Innovative Activities of Business Entities
abstract: The article focuses on the need to determine the basic principles of motivation as an incentive to increase the economic potential of business entities. The assessment of the impact of the motivation system on the innovative activity of business entities as a component of the system of enterprise tools is presented and determined. The components of the motivational mechanism of innovative activity of business entities and the impact of the motivation system on expanding innovative opportunities and strengthening the competitiveness of enterprises are considered. The complex of motivation-forming factors that can cause changes in the motivational structure of the entity, such as positive and negative, is considered. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Analysis of Transactional Factors and Logistics Characteristics of Delivery in E-Commerce Using Multiple Linear Regression
abstract: The aim of this research is to analyze the impact of logistics and transactional factors on the timely delivery of products in e-commerce. A dataset with 10,999 records was used, which includes data describing transactional and logistical factors. The selected method for analyzing this data is multiple linear regression. The results of the analysis indicate that transactional have a statistically significant impact on delivery timeliness, while logistical factors in aggregate form do not show statistical significance, with the exception of as the only logistical indicator with a measurable effect. Graphical analysis and ANOVA further confirm the regression results. The conclusions obtained provide insight into the planning of logistics processes and the optimization of business decisions in e-commerce systems. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Female Entrepreneurs 4.0 in Bosnia and Herzegovina: Is 4IR an Opportunity or a Threat?
abstract: The Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) is bringing fundamental changes to the global social context, ushering technologies such as automation and artificial intelligence. For female entrepreneurship in Bosnia and Herzegovina, this era represents a specific duality: on one hand, digitalization offers opportunities to overcome traditional gender barriers and facilitates easier access to the global market; on the other hand, it poses a threat by further deepening the digital divide and marginalizing sectors where women-led businesses are traditionally most prominent. The paper explores the position of female entrepreneurs in Bosnia and Herzegovina by analyzing current trends in both, the accessibility and utilization of 4IR resources. The objective is to answer a key question: does technological disruption serve as a catalyst for gender equality or as a new barrier within the transitional economic landscape of Bosnia and Herzegovina for women-led micro and small enterprises? While answering specific research questions, this paper is yet offering actionable strategic recommendations for policymakers, emphasizing the need for specific digital inclusion programs for female entrepreneurs in Bosnia and Herzegovina in the 4.0 era. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Comparison of the E-Commerce Markets in Slovakia and Bosnia and Herzegovina
abstract: E-commerce has affected all business sectors and it has essentially changed the shopping behaviour of consumers. The online purchase represents the standard way of getting possession of goods and services. E-commerce in Slovakia, as well as in Bosnia and Herzegovina has been gaining the popularity very fast in the last 10 years. There are essential differences present between the e-commerce market in Slovakia and Bosnia and Hercegovina despite the mutual similarity of these countries, either concerning the market directly or e-commerce companies and the number of customers. People feel more and more comfortable when shopping online in Slovakia and in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The aim of this paper is to analyse the development and current state of online shopping in the selected countries of Slovakia and Bosnia and Hercegovina in the period of 2014 till 2030. The growing e-commerce trend is going to continue also in the future. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Advancing decarbonization strategies: a techno-economic study of hydrogen-based SOFC cogeneration systems
abstract: China’s industrial sector accounts for approximately 36% of the nation’s total greenhouse gas emissions and confronts mounting decarbonization pressure under the Dual Carbon targets, which mandate carbon peaking before 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060. The pulp and paper manufacturing sector, a cornerstone of China’s light industry, requires sustained high-temperature process heat that cannot be readily electrified using current grid-based technologies, making it a priority candidate for hydrogen-based energy solutions. This study proposes and rigorously evaluates a hydrogen-fuelled Solid Oxide Fuel Cell (SOFC) cogeneration system purpose-built for the pulp and paper industry in China, with scalable relevance to other energy-intensive manufacturing domains. Three cogeneration configurations are comparatively analysed: a conventional gas turbine operating on natural gas (C1), an SOFC system utilizing grey hydrogen derived from steam methane reforming (C2), and a fully integrated SOFC system powered by green hydrogen produced on-site via a renewable energy-driven multi-energy system comprising photovoltaic panels, electrolyzers, compressors, and hydrogen storage units (C3). The system is calibrated to the solar resource conditions of Shandong Province, the energy price structure under China’s National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) tiered tariff framework, and domestic equipment costs expressed in Chinese Yuan. Employing a comprehensive techno-economic modelling framework, the study assesses each configuration in terms of net present cost (NPC), Levelized Cost of Hydrogen (LCOH), thermal and electrical outputs, and associated CO2 emissions across a 20-year project horizon. The findings reveal that the green hydrogen-powered SOFC system achieves near-complete grid independence and delivers an LCOH of 38.6 CNY/kg, decreasing to 34.8 CNY/kg when accounting for electricity sales revenue under Shandong Province’s distributed generation feed-in tariff. Furthermore, the hybrid SOFC system reduces CO2 emissions by 31% relative to the gas turbine baseline while reducing the mass flow of high-pressure steam by approximately 75%, a critical process integration consideration. Sensitivity analysis confirms that electricity export tariff policy is the dominant economic lever, whilst natural gas price volatility exerts the greatest influence on overall NPC. Policy scenarios under China’s National Hydrogen Strategy, including NDRC green hydrogen incentives and the national carbon emissions trading scheme, are evaluated to determine their combined impact on system viability. The results support a forward-looking policy framework that prioritises capital investment incentives and regulatory support for decentralised green hydrogen infrastructure and advanced SOFC technologies to accelerate industrial decarbonization in China. title: Hospitality recovery disconnect: Why diligent responses to online reviews fail to boost ratings
abstract: This study investigates a critical challenge in online hospitality management: the perplexing failure of high-quality managerial responses to improve business ratings on platforms like Yelp. Through analysis of 329,658 hotel and travel reviews with a computational linguistics framework measuring empathy, specificity, and action‑orientation, a systematic effort‑reward disconnect is uncovered. Contrary to conventional service wisdom, businesses providing more diligent responses received significantly lower average ratings (3.11 versus 3.50). High-quality recovery proves contingent on speed, occurring primarily within a 30-day window, while incremental quality improvements beyond a basic threshold yield no meaningful benefit. These findings necessitate a strategic shift from perfecting individual responses toward re-engineering operations for rapid response and platform-driven visibility optimization, demonstrating how digital architecture fundamentally reshapes service recovery effectiveness in hospitality. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Multi-horizon solar irradiance forecasting under variable sky conditions through CNN–TCN feature learning and XGBoost
abstract: Multi-horizon solar irradiance nowcasting is highly sensitive to rapidly varying atmospheric conditions. Traditional statistical models such as persistence and autoregressive integrated moving average are computationally efficient but often degrade under strong atmospheric variability, whereas physical models based on numerical weather prediction remain constrained by spatial resolution, initialization delay, and computational cost. Machine learning methods such as extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) improve nonlinear regression performance, but when used alone they do not explicitly capture temporal dependencies. Deep learning models, including convolutional neural network (CNN) and temporal convolutional network (TCN), can learn temporal patterns, yet maintaining stable accuracy across multiple forecast horizons remains challenging. To address this issue, this study proposes a hybrid CNN–TCN–XGBoost framework in which CNN and TCN extract multi-scale temporal features and XGBoost performs horizon-specific regression. The model is evaluated over forecast horizons from 1 to 30 min using independent 2018 and 2021 datasets covering clear-sky, mixed, overcast, and highly variable atmospheric regimes. The results show notable improvements over the 2-State benchmark, including normalized root mean square error (nRMSE) reductions of approximately 8% at 2 min and 22% at 10 min in the aggregated 2018 evaluation, while preserving smooth error growth with increasing horizon. Day-level validation across six representative atmospheric regimes provides further evidence of regime-dependent forecasting performance: on a highly variable day, error reductions reach about 38% at 10 min and 29% at 30 min, while on a stable clear-sky day the reduction reaches nearly 87% at 30 min. For the clear-sky subset, nRMSE is typically below 0.016 and remains below 0.032 even on the most challenging day. Therefore, the proposed CNN–TCN–XGBoost framework is best interpreted as a model that provides strong short- and intermediate-horizon performance and best or near-best accuracy across most evaluated regimes, while long-horizon performance remains dependent on atmospheric regime across diverse atmospheric conditions. These findings make it a promising solution for reliable real-time solar irradiance forecasting and photovoltaic operation. © 2026 The Authors. title: Towards embodied AI in manufacturing: Review, Evaluation, and Future directions
abstract: Embodied artificial intelligence (AI), which integrates perception, decision-making, and execution through interaction with the physical world, has recently emerged as a promising paradigm for enabling autonomous and adaptive manufacturing systems. While AI has been extensively explored in various manufacturing tasks, the major body of work remains fragmented across different processes, model paradigms, and task stages, lacking a unified basis for assessing how far current technologies have actually progressed towards system-level manufacturing intelligence. To address this gap, this paper introduces a task-oriented analytical framework grounded in the Perception, Decision–making, Execution (P-D-E) loop, which provides a common structure for systematically organizing, comparing, and evaluating AI contributions across heterogeneous manufacturing domains. Four representative processes including additive manufacturing (AM), machining, welding, and assembly are examined to map how AI technologies participate in each stage of the manufacturing task cycle. A six-dimensional evaluation criterion covering autonomy, adaptability, objective alignment, domain expertise, physical interaction, and industrial readiness is further proposed to assess the embodied AI readiness of each domain. The cross-process analysis yields several findings that go beyond individual process descriptions: the primary bottleneck towards embodied manufacturing intelligence is not the absence of capable models but the fragmentation of existing AI functions into isolated task-specific subloops; perception and reasoning capabilities have matured considerably faster than safe, reliable physical intervention; and different processes require fundamentally different embodiment pathways shaped by their physical coupling characteristics and deployment conditions. Based on these findings, the paper argues that near-term progress should follow a hierarchical and modular embodiment strategy, consider the problem from a task requirement-driven perspective, and establish standardized workflows and shared platforms to enable scalable, interoperable, and reproducible manufacturing AI systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Adapting the business model to ensure resilience: The case of michelin-starred french restaurants during the Covid-19 crisis
abstract: The Covid-19 pandemic exposed the vulnerabilities of the fine-dining hospitality sector and reignited debates on organizational resilience. While the literature distinguishes operational, functional, and strategic resilience, it often conflates temporary business model adjustments enacted under crisis conditions with genuine strategic reconfigurations, leaving the boundary between short-term adaptation and strategic resilience theoretically ambiguous. This article elaborates on these distinctions by drawing on a longitudinal, processual case study of Michelin-starred restaurants in France, based on 33 semi-structured interviews, 316 press articles, and archival data, which were analyzed. Our findings identify three empirically distinct response trajectories: (1) a bounce-back trajectory based on preservation mechanisms, characterized by a suspension of restaurant activity made possible by public subsidies; (2) a bounce-back trajectory grounded in continuity mechanisms, involving temporary and reversible business model adaptations; and (3) a bounce-forward trajectory driven by irreversible transformation mechanisms, marked by durable business model reconfigurations. Despite the apparent continuity of bounce-back trajectories, they mask a post-crisis erosion of key BM components, questioning the idea of a complete return to pre-crisis configurations. This study contributes to the literature by (i) clarifying the relationship between strategic resilience and business models through a component-level, processual analysis using the RCOV framework, (ii) challenging the implicit equation between BM change and strategic resilience, and (iii) showing that bounce-forward trajectories—rather than bounce-back responses—constitute the core mechanism of strategic resilience in hospitality contexts. © 2026 The Authors

title: Adaptive threshold estimation for uncertain differential equations with jumps
abstract: This study presents a parameter estimation methodology for uncertain differential equations with jumps, which are widely used to characterize complex phenomena in finance, physics, engineering, and other interdisciplinary fields. Specifically, we propose an adaptive threshold estimation method tailored to these equations. Using maximum likelihood estimation, we construct a feasible parameter estimation framework via an algorithm. Illustrative experiments based on a simulation example and a real-world empirical dataset are carried out to validate the proposed approach. Furthermore, we compare our method with state-of-the-art approaches. Finally, we discuss future research directions and summarize the main conclusions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Inventory management: A strategic approach to profitability in microenterprises in La Candelaria – Medellín
abstract: The objective of this research was to analyze inventory management from a strategic perspective, with a focus on profitability, in microenterprises in the commercial sector of La Candelaria, Medellín. It was developed using a descriptive qualitative methodology that incorporated fundamental quantitative analysis in the processing of the results. Simple random sampling was used to select 137 participating microenterprises, which were then interviewed using a previously validated semi-structured interview guide. The instrument explored four central themes: daily inventory management practices, tools used to control stock, product storage and rotation strategies, and the perceived relationship between inventory management and business profitability. The findings were classified into three categories: organizational practices in inventory management and control; inventory optimization: strategies and challenges; and inventory management as a factor in business success. It was found that most microenterprises review their inventories monthly, although the frequency varies according to product turnover. Seventy-eight percent of microenterprises do not utilize specialized software, instead relying on manual controls and traditional methods. Turnover is measured by tracking sales, counting units, and comparing initial and final stock, without resorting to technical indicators or formal accounting formulas. Factors affecting turnover include the season of the year (45.99%), fashion trends (31.39%), and poor internal management (22.62%). Microenterprises employ promotions, offers, and sales to accelerate inventory turnover. All respondents recognize the strategic importance of inventory management for decision-making, stock adjustment, and competitive advantage. 59.12% indicate that effective turnover increases profits, 24.09% that it improves cash flow, and 16.79% that it facilitates the incorporation of new products. Although these productive units have a solid empirical base and show interest in optimizing inventories, operational weaknesses remain—especially in data systematization for strategic decisions—whose improvement would strengthen competitiveness, efficiency, and long-term sustainability. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Human-Centered AI in Live Streaming: A Developer’s Perspective
abstract: With AI technology more often being introduced to the masses with the help of live-streaming platforms and tools; it is most essential to know how developers take into consideration the hu-man-centered principles when coming up with these systems. The paper aims at re-examining the views of developers regarding the design and development of the AI technology within a live-streaming environment, as well as the ethical, technical, and user-centered difficulties. Our qualitative approach involved the use of semi-structured interviews with the developers, designers and product managers who work in the Canadian live-streaming sector. This study involves the results concerning real-life motivation, design used, and the issues associated with matching the AI tools in a user-oriented manner as a part of a live-streaming service. The results show that developers, designers, and product managers appreciate transparency, fairness and user safety, although they tend to apply ethical principles and business-driven results of scaling, features, and engagement perspectives. The paper concludes that to enable the designers, design managers, and engineers to adopt human-centered approach, the infrastructure should support interdisciplinary work, provide more explicit ethics commitment, and processes that meaning-fully lead to giving developers more power to make accountable and ethical decisions in the context of AI design. These findings will be important contributions to the current debate about ethical AI and will base the debate upon the practice that designers and developers have in the field. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Hotel resilience to prolonged uncertain disruptions: A business model dynamics analysis
abstract: This study examines how hotels adapted their business models to sustain operations during the prolonged uncertainty of COVID-19. Using Business Model Dynamics as a systems lens and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) on data from 53 Thai hotels, the study identifies multiple equifinal configurations of strategic, operational, and financial adjustments that generated high resilience. Results show that high resilience emerged not from isolated actions but from coherent alignments among innovation, resource redeployment, and financial preparedness, with minimal cost restructuring shared across resilient hotels. Less resilient hotels followed distinct, asymmetric configurations, confirming that the drivers of low resilience differ from those of high resilience. The findings advance hospitality resilience research by extending Business Model Dynamics through configurational causality, showing how adaptive operational resilience depends on the fit among business model elements during a prolonged disruption. The study offers context-specific insights for tourism-dependent hotels and provides a foundation for future cross-country and longitudinal validation of the Configurational Business Model Dynamics (CBMD) framework. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Review and Experimental Evaluation of ML Models for DDoS Detection
abstract: —DoS and DDoS attacks overload targets (servers) with unnatural and large amounts of traffic, resulting in the disruption of online services. Such attacks can have direct impact on regular business operations and can result in a loss of reputation as well as money for organizations. The aim of this study is to explore multiple ML algos. and compare the different possibilities when it comes to classification models to reduce these risks. ML facilitates the detection of anomalous activity and helps identify patterns in network traffic. We aim to evaluate multiple machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest, Decision Tree, and XGB (eXtreme Gradient Boosting), using the UNSW-NB15 dataset. Accuracy, Precision, recall and F1 score are the four metrics used for evaluation. The results show that XGB performs very well, attaining 89% accuracy with baseline hyperparameter tuning. The results indicate that Machine Learning models, particularly the gradient boosting algorithms like XGB/CatBoost, can result in a more efficient detection of DDoS attacks. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Edge-AI Powered Malware Detection in Resource-Constrained IoT Environments
abstract: The fasts proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has come with unprecedented cybersecurity risks due to restricted resources that would otherwise prevent any traditional malware detection strategies in the environment. The paper suggests an Edge-AI-based malware detection framework that can run effectively on low power and low memory Internet of Things devices. Using lightweight machine learning models and on-the-edge inference, the system will be able to detect anomalies on-demand and infer about threats without being connected to the cloud all the time. Our method combines efficient feature preprocessing, privacy-afraid federated learning updates to models, and edge-efficient neural analytical arrangements to trade off visual information identifications with their implementing expenditure. The test on benchmark datasets of IoT malware shows that the suggested solution has low resistance to latency and energy and a high detection rate. This article highlights the viability and efficiency of Edge-AI in businesses to improve security posture of IoT networks of the next generation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Cyber Security in the Modern Era: Challenges, Ethics, and Emerging Trends
abstract: The world has been exposed to high exposure of cyber threats due to high speed digitalization of key services, business and social life. The recent cyber-attacks are more massive, sophisticated, and devastating as they focus on individuals and organizations and even national infrastructure. The provided paper will offer the general view of cybersecurity in the modern world by commenting on the primary issues and concerns, ethical issues, and new technological trends that impact the threat environment. The present cyber-attacks of 2024–2025 are further assumed to identify the practical risks and the tendency of attacks. The study discusses emerging trends such as artificial intelligence-driven malware, ransomware-as-a-service, zero-trust architecture, risk of quantum computing, and attack on supply chain. Moreover, the social media concerning the escalation of cyber security threats is covered. This paper attempts to consolidate the new research, industry reports and case study to provide a chronological perspective of the existing problems in the domain of cybersecurity and in support of the need to adopt an active, ethical and adaptable security practice. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Co-designing Alternatives of Adaptive Reuse: The Case of the Church of the Holy Name of Jesus in Moncalieri
abstract: This paper presents a participatory co-design process focused on the adaptive reuse of the Chiesa del SS. Nome di Gesù, a deconsecrated church in the historic centre of Moncalieri, Northern Italy, developed within the PRIN TREE 2022 research project on circular economy models for architectural heritage reuse. Through a full-day participatory workshop with 14 participants and semi-structured validation interviews with seven key informants, the study employed a Circular Business Model Canvas to bridge participatory outputs and governance planning. Findings consistently identify the Church as a potential generative infrastructure for a new intergenerational community, a civic common where different generations, cultural backgrounds, and forms of knowledge enter into durable relationship. Three co-generative value dimensions are mapped (cultural, social, and economic) alongside a polycentric governance model. Interpreted through the concept of heritage community as defined in the Council of Europe’s Faro Convention, the results suggest that the most sustainable form of religious heritage reuse is one that simultaneously activates a new community of meaning around the heritage site. Implications for heritage governance, participatory design methodology, and Faro Convention operationalisation are discussed. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Simulation-Based Data Generation for On-Demand Bus-as-a-Service Analytics
abstract: On-demand mobility systems, such as bus services, are gaining importance due to their role in sustainable urban transport. Their flexible and context-specific nature poses challenges for planning, optimization, and performance evaluation, particularly due to the scarcity of related operational data needed to support data-driven decision-making. This work is motivated by a real-world Bus-as-a-Service (BaaS) project, where the lack of available data limited the development of analytical tools. To address this gap, this paper proposes an artifact for the generation of event data (i.e., operational data) related to an on-demand bus service. Thus, the main contributions of this paper include the artifact tailored for on-demand bus services, but also the methodology that was followed for this instantiation. The purpose is that such methodology can be replicated in other cases to generate synthetic data. Without access to real data and without the possibility of gathering data from an existing on-demand bus service, the first step consisted of gathering customers’ requirements and analyzing similar business models, resulting in the definition of an Entity-Relationship Diagram that allowed us to identify the data that needed to be generated by the artifact. This artifact simulates the required operational processes, capturing critical elements such as passenger requests, vehicle routing, and other service constraints. The results show that this artifact produces valid simulations for multiple scenarios and enables the generation of structured datasets that meet predefined analytical requirements. Thus, the obtained datasets can be consumed by data-driven analytics. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Classification of Postal Distribution Centres
abstract: This work was conducted in the context of industrial mathematics, in partnership with CTT-Correios de Portugal, S.A., highlighting the strong link between academia and the business world. It addresses the classification of Postal Distribution Centres using multivariate statistical methods combined in a less common way. First, a correlation analysis was conducted on the variables selected for the study, revealing several statistically significant associations. To mitigate collinearity, Principal Component Analysis was applied to derive uncorrelated components, which were then used as inputs to Cluster Analysis. Both hierarchical and partitional clustering methods were applied, and solution quality was assessed using graphical inspection, silhouette coefficients, and within- and between-cluster sums of squares. Ward’s method, k-means, and k-medoids produced consistent and similar groupings; in this paper, the k-means results are considered. Linear Discriminant Analysis and Multinomial Logistic Regression were used to assign new Postal Distribution Centres to the previously identified groups. The second classifier was used to corroborate the classification results obtained by LDA, since some LDA assumptions are violated and one of the clusters is small. The classification results from both methods showed a high degree of agreement. To avoid inflated accuracy caused by using the same data throughout all stages of the pipeline (standardisation, PCA, CA, LDA/MLR), the leave-one-out cross-validation method was applied across the entire pipeline, rather than only at the classification stage. As a result, the accuracy value obtained is a more realistic estimate of the model’s performance. All analyses were conducted in R. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: From Text to Economic Exposure: Measuring Intrinsic Risk in Urban Real Estate
abstract: Corporate disclosures usually describe the firm’s strategies, expectations, and perceived risks. Beyond purely numerical indicators, these narratives provide a broader and often more nuanced view of the firm. In this sense, working with textual information allows researchers to capture and organize these insights in a more structured and meaningful way. The starting point of this paper is that traditional classifications, such as sector categories or fixed developer typologies, are often too rigid to reflect the diversity of the firms that are operating in the built environment. In practice, mixed-use models, infrastructure-linked assets, and the changing nature of urban functions tend to blur these boundaries. For this reason, the study has adopted an approach that considers firms as interpreters of economic and urban change, drawing on their own published language to capture underlying exposure. The empirical strategy builds a textual corpus for each firm, using sources such as regulatory filings, investor presentations, earnings calls, and business descriptions. Embeddings then convert these texts into semantic representations, enabling them to position firms within a continuous economic space. Rather than assigning each firm to a single category, similarity within this space is used to infer partial exposure to different economic narratives. This makes it possible to identify shared sensitivities to structural drivers, such as financing conditions, tenant composition, logistics demand, retrofit pressures, technological change, and urban redevelopment. Afterward, it incorporates these semantic exposures into a multi-factor risk model, which distinguishes common structural risk from firm-specific residual risk. By incorporating semantic exposures into a multi-factor risk model, the analysis distinguishes common structural risk from firm-specific residual risk. Real estate benefits particularly from this framework. Interest-rate shocks, liquidity stress, and capital allocation changes can alter firm risk in real estate before conventional classifications fully capture these alterations. More broadly, the study links firm-level narratives, asset pricing, and urban transformation, showing how the analysis of corporate text can contribute to a more adaptive understanding of risk. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: A Comparative NLP Study of Semantic and Thematic Changes in AI Research Pre - and Post-generative AI
abstract: With the advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly with the emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs), has significantly influenced the scope, accessibility, and dissemination of scientific research. This evolution raises important questions regarding how AI-related scientific discourse has changed over time. This study search lexical, semantic, and thematic changes in a dataset of approximately 50,000 AI-related publications retrieved from the Web of Science (WoS), comparing a pre-GenAI period (2015–2019) with a post-GenAI period (2022–2025). Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques were applied, including TF-IDF for lexical analysis, Logistic Regression for temporal classification, and BERTopic for topic modeling. The results achieved an accuracy of 89%, revealing a clear separability between the two periods based on textual features. The analyses reveal a transition from predominantly technical and methodological terminology, focused on algorithms and infrastructure, toward more application-oriented and generative themes, including GenAI and LLMs. Furthermore, topic modeling shows the growing prominence of interdisciplinary domains such as education, healthcare, and business applications in the post-GenAI period. Overall, the findings suggest a significant lexical and thematic evolution in AI-related scientific discourse, reflecting broader transformations in research priorities and application domains following the emergence of GenAI technologies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Capital structure adjustments of Hotel SMEs in Portugal's hospitality industry during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic triggered an unprecedented economic shock, disrupting business operations and demand across sectors. This study examines the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the capital structure of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the Portuguese hotel sector, a core segment of the hospitality industry and one of the most severely affected by the crisis. Using a panel dataset of private hotel firms in Portugal, we find a significant reduction in total debt during the pandemic. Decomposing debt by maturity reveals that firms reduced short-term borrowing while expanding long-term financing, indicating a recomposition of the debt structure during the pandemic. Furthermore, when firms are segmented by size, the reduction in total leverage was concentrated among smaller, financially constrained firms, while the expansion in long-term financing was observed among larger, financially unconstrained firms. A further decomposition of total liabilities into financial and operating components reveals that financial and operating liabilities responded in opposite directions during the pandemic: operating liabilities contracted, while financial liabilities, notably long-term financial debt, increased. This study contributes to the literature on capital structure, corporate finance, and crisis management by providing one of the first empirical assessments of COVID-19's effects on SME financing in a tourism-dependent, bank-reliant economy, a context that remains understudied. It also extends prior research by focusing on private rather than public firms. By examining a highly vulnerable sector, the findings offer insights into financial resilience during crises and provide policy implications for improving liquidity access and strengthening financial stability among tourism-dependent hotel SMEs. © 2026 The Authors

title: Healthcare Resources, In-Hospital Management Measures, and Outcomes for Acute Ischemic Stroke in China: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Objectives To assess how province-level healthcare resource configuration relates to in-hospital management and outcomes for acute ischemic stroke in China. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study of 1 055 971 adults with acute ischemic stroke treated at 1456 secondary and tertiary hospitals in the Chinese Stroke Center Alliance, 2015 to 2019. Hospital-level management and outcome measures were linked to province-level resource indicators from the China Health Statistics Yearbook, including physician:nurse ratio, nurse:bed ratio, density of medical institutions, and total health expenditure. Associations were estimated using patient-number–weighted linear regression models adjusted for hospital level, provincial gross regional product per capita, admission timing, and year, with cluster-robust standard errors at the province level. Results Substantial interprovincial variation was observed. Most healthcare resource indicators were not significantly associated with composite adherence, although physician:nurse ratio showed a borderline positive association (β = 0.018 per 0.1 increase, 95% CI, −0.0004 to 0.036). Secondary prevention adherence was positively associated with health expenditure (β = 0.007; 95% CI, 0.0003-0.014). For thrombolysis within 4.5 hours, physician:nurse ratio was negatively associated (β = −0.062; 95% CI, −0.119 to −0.006), whereas nurse:bed ratio was positively associated (β = 1.232; 95% CI, 0.066-2.397). In contrast, healthcare resource indicators were not clearly associated with in-hospital outcomes. Conclusions Healthcare resource configuration showed modest associations with stroke management but limited associations with in-hospital outcomes, suggesting that resource availability alone may not fully explain variation in stroke outcomes. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Bidding and market dynamics in the Brazilian structural demand response program
abstract: This paper studies the Structural demand response Program (SP) in Brazil from a consumer's perspective. We begin by formalizing the SP's operational and financial mechanisms, and then develop a strategic bidding methodology that follows a two-stage decision-making process, formulated as a nonconvex bilevel optimization model. In the first stage, consumers determine optimal bids that balance program revenues with production-related opportunity costs, while the second stage models the all-or-nothing market-clearing process as a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming problem. To address computational challenges posed by the strategic bidding model, the nonconvexities are linearized via binary relations, and the bilevel model is reformulated as an equivalent single-level problem solved via a tailored Column-and-Constraint Generation algorithm. Empirical evidence from a case study based on data from the Brazilian power system and market environment suggests that the SP's design incentivizes energy-intensive consumers with flexible demand profiles. In contrast, baseline constraints hinder broader participation by price-responsive consumers. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Leveraging large language models for agentic process analytics assistants: Assessing accuracy in process mining tasks
abstract: To leverage Large Language Models for enhanced data-driven decision-making in Process Mining, this study introduces a framework that establishes an extended process analytics question taxonomy, including case, activity, resource, temporal, discovery and variant, and what-if and predictive dimensions. The proposed framework evaluates state-of-the-art Large Language Models on their ability to generate executable Python-based visual analytics, bridging the gap between raw Process Mining insights and non-technical users. Performance is assessed for recent models, such as GPT-4.1 and Claude 3.7, using an LLM-as-Judge approach and a specific Visualisation Error Rate. The framework works both as a benchmarking instrument and as a conceptual and practical basis to guide the development of deployable agentic assistants within AI-Augmented Business Process Management Systems. Results indicate that GPT-4.1 achieves on a bounded 1-10 evaluation scale (higher is better), an LLM-as-Judge score of (Formula presented), (Formula presented) and a Visualisation Error Rate of 25%. A key finding reveals a significant performance disparity: while models have an increased performance with widely adopted libraries, they face substantial challenges with domain-specific tools like PM4Py. These insights provide the necessary evidence to guide model refinement to fully support automated visual insight generation in Process Mining contexts, including the ones backed by other tools and languages, such as bupaR with R, and ProM with Java. © 2026 The Authors. title: NS-S2FM: An auditable neuro-symbolic expert decision system for scenario-aware franchise operations under uncertainty
abstract: Sports franchise operation provides a high-uncertainty testbed for expert decision systems because competitive performance, market demand, injury exposure, star-player dependency, financial pressure, and league-level events are tightly coupled. This study proposes NS-S2FM, an auditable neuro-symbolic, scenario-aware expert decision system for uncertain franchise operations. The framework turns heterogeneous signals and institutional rules into a decision object that reports an action, a diagnosed scenario, constraint and risk evidence, and an explanation. We evaluate NS-S2FM through controlled simulation, rule-defined franchise profiles, a WNBA 2022–2024 sports-performance and attendance panel with semi-real business variables, ablation analysis, sensitivity analysis, CVaR-style and CPPO-style constrained comparators, explanation-augmented baselines, and statistical evidence checks. The evidence supports three bounded decision-support findings: strong multi-objective DSS behavior in controlled settings, pre-specified operator-preference diagnostic scores under conservative, growth-oriented, and risk-averse scalarizations, and stronger traceability and scenario adaptability in the real-world panel evaluation. Results from the real-world panel also show the intended trade-off: unconstrained and profit-focused baselines remain competitive on short-horizon numerical scores. Evaluation-index sensitivity and constraint-binding analyses make this interpretation scope explicit by showing metric sensitivity and limited feasibility-mask binding. The contribution is an auditable, constraint-aware, and preference-diagnostic DSS mechanism under transparent proxy-based evidence; stronger claims about audited business outcomes, manager-validated usefulness, or organizational intervention effects require future data. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Smart Innovations in Biosphere Reserves
abstract: The paper aims to define the smart innovations in biosphere reserve from the theoretical point of view and subsequently, identify the examples of good practice in their real conditions, based on it summarize the key features of smart innovation in biosphere reserves. The smart innovation is interpreted as a comprehensive ecosystem of solutions based on the use of digital technologies, data analytics, and interconnected systems enhancing process efficiency and support the sustainable development of regions. The paper draws on the theoretical foundations of innovation theory and collaboration models, particularly the Quintuple Helix model, which emphasizes collaboration between the public sector, the business sector, the academic community, civil society, and the natural environment. Special attention is given to the application in the context of biosphere reserves, where it is essential to respect nature conservation requirements while simultaneously supporting socio-economic development. The empirical part of the paper presents selected examples of good practice in smart innovations within biosphere reserves, which are subsequently analysed and discussed in relation to theoretical frameworks. The results highlight the importance of linking technological solutions to the needs of the area and the necessity of local stakeholder participation. The conclusion emphasizes that smart innovations represent a tool for achieving a balance between biodiversity conservation and sustainable development, with biosphere reserves serving as experimental sites for their implementation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises as Providers of Regional Environmental Open Data: Connecting LCA Indicators with ESG Reporting and Sustainable Regional Development
abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) generate considerable amounts of environmental data in their everyday operations, but much of this information remains unused outside the enterprise. These data could support regional policymaking, especially if they were collected and shared in a structured form. In practice, business-generated data often do not meet the standards required for integration into public databases. This paper examines how SMEs can contribute to regional environmental open data, with a focus on Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), ESG reporting, and sustainable regional development. The study combines preliminary empirical evidence from Slovak SMEs with a systematic review of relevant literature. It investigates whether SMEs monitor environmental indicators more frequently in the earlier stages of the product life cycle, particularly procurement and production, than in the later stages, such as consumption, use, and end-of-life treatment (H1). Five specific indicators are examined: product origin transparency (H2a), energy consumption in production (H2b), fuel consumption (H2c), average product lifespan (H2d), and the proportion of repaired products compared with discarded products (H2e). The findings show that SMEs tend to focus mainly on indicators linked to internal processes. Indicators from downstream life cycle phases are monitored less frequently. The paper contributes to the discussion on how SME-generated environmental data can be transformed into regional open data and used more effectively in sustainability-oriented policy and reporting. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The Corporate Social Responsibility in Agrifood System: An Integrated Methodological Approach to Assessing Corporate Integration and Communication
abstract: In recent decades, companies have developed innovative sustainable business management models capable of integrating green, resilient and inclusive approaches. Recently, partly as a result of EU and international regulatory guidelines, Corporate Social Sustainability (CSR) is becoming more diffuse in business models through which companies have attempted to integrate the three dimensions of sustainability (economic, social and environmental). The CSR approach has directed companies to revise their “mission” and business functions, shifting the focus from operating income to environmental and social impact. Several studies have analyzed the relationship between CSR and firm performance, between CSR and value chain, but few studies in the literature investigate the mode to communicate CSR to stakeholders, particularly through websites and in livestock enterprises. The objective of the paper is to present the methodological approach of the research, which is currently in progress, focusing on the analysis of the processes of CSR integration into business management and the related online communication of implemented sustainable actions. The integrated methodological approach is based on the analysis of the websites of Italian agribusinesses, in particular in livestock companies, using the “7S” model of analysis, supplemented by specific Focus Groups, to acquire qualitative information about the motivations toward sustainable actions, directly from a sample of companies. In the paper, the methodological approach will be proposed, as the research is in progress and includes among the objectives, the identification of key drivers and the implementation of strategies for a CSR in line with the SDGs related to the corporate ecosystem. The paper will propose the methodological approach and initial results obtained by the analysis of the websites of a sample of livestock enterprises. The research, still in progress, will identify key drivers for the development of strategies for CSR in line with the SDGs related to the business ecosystem and could have operative developments for the application of recent European Union legislation (CSRD 2022). © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Renewable peak shaving via integrated biomass gasification, fuel cell, and storage systems: Biomass selection, life cycle assessment-driven exergoenvironmental analysis, and machine-learning optimization
abstract: Integrated biomass-fed systems offer a viable alternative to conventional plants, aiming to meet the growing global demand for clean and reliable power. This research investigates a hybrid biomass-fed system designed for energy storage and peak shaving. The configuration includes biomass gasification combined with heat recovery, incorporating a CO2-based power cycle and an organic Rankine cycle. Here, the syngas derived from biomass gasification is used as the primary fuel for a molten carbonate fuel cell integrated with a heat generation component and a Kalina cycle. The system also incorporates compressed air energy storage to enhance load balancing. Utilizing Chlorophora excelsa (BW4), identified as the most suitable biomass fuel among several candidates, the system's performance is assessed from exergy, sustainability, environmental, and life cycle assessment-driven exergoenvironmental perspectives. Afterward, a hybrid machine learning optimization framework is developed, employing artificial neural networks (ANN) with a non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm-II (NSGA-II). The optimization targets three key metrics: total exergy destruction rate, overall sustainability index, and overall specific exergoenvironmental impact. The optimization shows these objectives at 56.69 MW, 1.297, 5.86 mPts/GJ, respectively, indicating a balanced trade-off between thermodynamics and ecological impact. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of machine learning in advancing environmentally responsible energy system design. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Performance optimization strategy of nanometal oxide-functionalized graphene composite electrodes for efficient CO2 reduction in microbial electrolysis systems
abstract: Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) offers a promising carbon sequestration strategy for climate change mitigation, which also provides a sustainable pathway for biomass accumulation and bioenergy resource recovery. However, one key factor that governs electrosynthesis efficiency is electrode material. In this work, four electrodes including graphene electrodes (Gr), high-temperature calcined graphene electrodes (HG), graphene composite nanometal oxide with Fe2O3 (HFG) and TiO2 (HTG) were prepared to investigate the electroreduction effect on CO2 reduction activity, aiming to optimize the conversion of carbon resources into high-value biomass and renewable bioenergy products. The cathodic surface properties affect biofilm biomass and carbon-fixing bacteria abundance obviously. The biomass and electron transfer system activity (ETSA) were negatively correlated with charge transfer resistance. In comparison with the unmodified carbon felt as the cathode in the MES reactor, the acetic acid production in the subsequent four groups (388.62, 402.23, 441.77, and 489.81 mg/L) was significantly higher than that in the CF group (330.19 mg/L). As a typical bioenergy intermediate product, acetic acid is closely related to microbial biomass metabolism. Total carbon-fixing bacteria abundance was strongly positively correlated with acetic acid production (r = 0.914, p < 0.01). The Fe2O3 and TiO2 modified graphene cathodes enhanced both biofilm growth and carbon sequestration bacterial abundance respectively, optimized hydrogen evolution reaction kinetics and promoted the acetic acid production significantly. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Enhanced degradation of bamboo shoot shells via a two-step process: Sodium chlorite pretreatment and xylanase hydrolysis for xylooligosaccharides production
abstract: To improve the high-value utilization of bamboo shoot shells (BSS), a two-step strategy combining sodium chlorite pretreatment and hydrolysis with a thermostable xylanase from Thermomyces lanuginosus Q231 was developed to produce xylooligosaccharides (XOS). The xylanase exhibited an optimum pH of 6.0 and an optimum temperature of 70°C, while maintaining good catalytic performance at 50–65°C. The effects of sodium chlorite concentration (1%–8%, w/v) on the chemical composition, structural characteristics, and enzymatic hydrolysis performance of BSS were investigated. The results showed that sodium chlorite selectively removed lignin in a concentration-dependent manner, thereby increasing hemicellulose exposure and xylanase accessibility while largely preserving the cellulose crystalline structure. The optimal pretreatment concentration was 6% (w/v), at which the XOS yield reached 22.30%. HPLC analysis showed that xylotetraose (X4) and xylopentaose (X5) were the major components, and the xylose/XOS ratio remained at a low level of 0.06 after 2 h of enzymatic hydrolysis, indicating high product selectivity. Under the optimized conditions, 50.50 g of XOS was obtained from 1 kg of pretreated BSS. These results suggest that the proposed process has strong potential for the valorization of BSS and offer valuable insights for further research on enzymatic XOS production from lignocellulosic residues. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Activating pro-environmental behavior in hospitality settings: A multi-level communication framework
abstract: The hospitality industry is both a contributor to environmental degradation and a key player in promoting sustainable practices. While previous research has examined pro-environmental behaviour (PEB) in hospitality workplaces, the interplay between personal and corporate environmental values remains underexplored. This study addresses this gap by investigating how different types of employees engage in PEB within an international hotel chain. Using an embedded case study approach, the study draws on 45 semi-structured interviews, participant and non-participant observations, and document analysis across hotel units in the UK and Vietnam. The findings identify four employee typologies: Value Initiator-Teller (VIT), Internal Messenger (iM), Receiver-Doer (RD), and Influencer (Ir), each playing distinct roles in environmental communication and action. The study contributes to the existing PEB framework by integrating corporate environmental values as an additional analytical layer and by examining how organisational communication pathways are associated with employee engagement. The findings suggest that tailoring sustainability communication strategies to employee roles and cultural contexts may support more consistent engagement with PEB, offering practical insights for multi-level environmental management within hospitality businesses. © 2026 The Authors

title: Attention-boosted DistilBERT and Bi-GRU for cyber-attacks detection in electric vehicle charging networks
abstract: The global transition to the Electric Vehicles (EVs) represents a major change of the transportation and energy industry, which is driven by a breakthrough in battery technology, positive government policies, and increased consumer demand. As the use of electric cars is becoming more accepted, it is necessary to implement Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) in the power grid to support the ecosystem. The interconnectivity, in its turn, makes the grid and EVSE infrastructure vulnerable to a variety of cybersecurity threats. The availability, dependability, and security of electric vehicle charging networks may be compromised by the vulnerabilities such as Denial of Service (DoS), Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, data manipulation, and malware threats. These attacks can disrupt power charging processes, cause financial damages, cause bodily injuries, or even destabilise the power systems. This paper introduces a hybrid architecture comprising of deep contextual proficiency of DistilBERT, the sequential modelling efficacy of Bi-directional Gated Recurrent Units (Bi-GRU) and an attention mechanism to detect cyber-attacks on Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) systems. The model is tested on CICEVSE2024 dataset, a high-rate collection of power consumption and network traffic data, which is based upon benign and harmful contexts. The results show that the classification accuracy is 94 percent, precision is 98 percent, recall stands at 95 percent, and F1-score is 96 percent, thus validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach in identifying the occurrence of cyber-attacks in complex and real-life contexts. The study highlights the potential of AI-assisted methods of real-time cybersecurity monitoring in the framework of electric vehicle grid integration, which is steadily advancing, and explains the need to implement resilient and scaleable solutions to mitigate the increasing cyber threats. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A multi-scale approach to hydrothermal liquefaction of two-phase olive mill waste: From laboratory test to regional biorefinery in Andalusia
abstract: The olive oil industry produces over 3 Mt of two-phase olive mill waste (TPOMW) annually in Andalusia. Its management presents a significant environmental challenge due to its high moisture content and phytotoxicity. Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) is a promising valorization route utilizing the water content in the waste as a reaction medium, saving energy (no drying is needed). In this study a multi-scale approach has been used, integrating physicochemical characterization, laboratory scale experiments, kinetic modelling and a GIS-based location assessment for the location of HTL treatment plants. TPOMW shows high moisture (72 wt%) and a significant lipid content (16.4 wt% db), with a high heating value of approx. 23 MJ/kg. Kinetic results indicate that the solid fraction is the primary product for the first 22 min, after which the aqueous phase dominates due to rapid organic matter hydrolysis, obtaining a bio-oil yield around 20%. According to the resulting reaction network a model with three first order equation that can predict the behaviour of the process has been proposed. Finally, a GIS-based location-allocation analysis has been performed, proposing a decentralized network of 15 HTL plants across Andalusia. Results show a framework for the implementation of HTL-based biorefineries, supporting the transition toward a circular bioeconomy in the Mediterranean area. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: From trash to treasure: How exclusivity influences quality perception across different recycled materials in luxury fashion
abstract: Luxury fashion brands increasingly respond to corporate social responsibility expectations by integrating recycled materials into their products to reduce environmental impact. However, little is known about how these brands should communicate their use of recycled materials on social media without compromising product evaluation. To address this issue, through two between-subjects experimental studies, this paper examines whether and how luxury fashion products crafted from different types of recycled materials (natural vs. synthetic) affect product evaluation on social media, and whether exclusivity moderate this effect. Study 1 (N = 149, 63.09% male, Mage = 41.12, SDage = 13.48) shows that luxury fashion products made from recycled synthetic (vs. recycled natural) materials significantly reduce product evaluation, an effect fully mediated by perceived product quality. Study 2 (N = 199, 59.30% male, Mage = 35.64, SDage = 12.30) further indicates that this negative indirect effect through perceived product quality emerges under high exclusivity, and is not significant when exclusivity is attenuated. These findings contribute to sustainable luxury fashion literature by identifying material type as the key dimension differentiating consumer evaluations of recycled materials in luxury fashion. The findings also show that exclusivity is the critical contextual trigger that activates this material-driven effect through perceived product quality. Managerially, luxury fashion brands are advised against pairing exclusivity cues with their products made from recycled synthetic materials on social media, while such cues remain viable for recycled natural materials. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Wireless mobile charging for emergency electric vehicle routing: A mixed-integer and metaheuristic framework for in-motion energy transfer
abstract: As electric vehicles (EVs) become central to decarbonization efforts, the need for uninterrupted power supply in time-critical logistics, particularly in medical transportation, poses unique challenges for power systems integration. Conventional fixed or mobile charging infrastructure requires vehicle downtime, which makes them unsuitable for nonstop operations such as organ delivery. This work introduces the Wireless Mobile Charging Electric Vehicle Routing Problem, a novel framework in which mobile charging trucks wirelessly transfer energy to moving EVs via inductive coupling, eliminating the need for stationary charging stops. We formulate a mixed-integer programming model that co-optimizes routing and in-motion energy transfer between heterogeneous vehicle fleets under temporal and spatial alignment constraints. To address computational complexity, we develop a hybrid Bitmask Dynamic Programming and Large Neighborhood Search algorithm, tailored to arc-level charging decisions and dual-fleet synchronization. Experiments using real-world hospital logistics data from Singapore demonstrate significant runtime improvements and higher-quality solutions compared with commercial solvers. This study advances computational power system modeling by incorporating dynamic, motion-based energy delivery that is both time- and space-dependent. The results provide actionable insights into planning mobile energy infrastructure, enhancing demand-side flexibility, strengthening resilience in emergency logistics, and integrating wireless charging into urban power systems to support flexible and zero-carbon electrified mobility. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Decoupling physical and chemical effects in underground hydrogen storage: A multiscale evaluation of carbonate and shale rocks
abstract: Underground hydrogen storage (UHS) impacts on reservoir and seal integrity necessitate a thorough understanding. Previous studies have not decoupled hydrogen-specific effects from those caused by pressure, temperature, and fluid saturation. This study systematically evaluates calcite-rich limestones ('95% CaCO3) and Eagle Ford shale for hydrogen storage conditions, integrating high-pressure laboratory experiments with molecular dynamics (MD) and density functional theory (DFT) simulations. Limestones (dry and brine-saturated) were exposed to H2 and control gas (N2) at 3.4 MPa and 50°C for 30 days, and shale at 6.0 MPa and 80°C. Post-exposure characterization revealed porosity variations within ± 2%, while permeability decreased in high-permeable samples and increased in tighter ones. Young’s modulus decreased by ' 20% in shale and by ∼ 13% in saturated limestone, but increased by 50% in dry limestone; unconfined compressive strength showed sample-dependent changes, with similar trends under H2 and N2, indicating that these responses were not hydrogen-specific. Similar observations were observed for H2 and N2 exposure, indicating that physical processes, rather than chemical processes, governed the responses. MD and DFT analyses confirmed negligible hydrogen reactivity, showing weak physisorption on calcite [CaCO3-(104)] surfaces, negligible charge transfer, unchanged band gaps, and no structural alteration. X-ray diffraction confirmed mineralogical stability, with minor gypsum dissolution. These results demonstrate that the tested calcite-rich limestones remained mineralogically stable under the investigated hydrogen exposure conditions. For Eagle Ford shale, the experimental observations showed no clear hydrogen-specific mechanical degradation during the tested exposure period, although direct mineralogical characterization was not performed in the present study. Overall, the observed short-term variations primarily reflect physical effects. The findings provide a mechanistic basis for predicting caprock and reservoir behavior during hydrogen storage, suggesting that, in the absence of cyclic loading, hydrogen may not degrade the carbonate-bearing formations if used as a storage medium, while shales may serve as effective seals. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Explicit reward mechanisms for local flexibility in renewable energy communities
abstract: Incentivizing flexible consumption of end-users is key to maximizing the value of local exchanges within Renewable Energy Communities. If centralized coordination for flexible resources planning raises concerns regarding data privacy and fair benefits distribution, state-of-the-art approaches (e.g., bi-level, ADMM) often face computational complexity and convexity challenges, limiting the precision of embedded flexible models. This work proposes an iterative resolution procedure to solve the decentralized flexibility planning with a central operator as a coordinator within a community. The community operator asks for upward or downward flexibility depending on the global needs, while members can individually react with an offer for flexible capacity. This approach ensures individual optimality while converging towards a global optimum, as validated on a 20-member domestic case study for which the gap in terms of collective bill is not more than 3.5% between the decentralized and centralized coordination schemes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
