title: Edupreneurship management in vocational education: Case study in vocational high school in East Java
abstract: Vocational education is required to produce graduates who are not only ready to work but also able to create jobs. Edupreneurship is a strategic approach to meet these demands by integrating an entrepreneurial spirit into educational management and practices. This study aims to explore and analyze the model and implementation of edupreneurship management in vocational education in East Java Province. The study uses a qualitative approach with a case study method in several vocational education programs that are considered to have good edupreneurship practices. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with institutional leaders, teachers/lecturers, and students; participant observation; and document analysis. The results of the study indicate that effective edupreneurship management is built through five main pillars: (1) visionary leadership oriented toward innovation and the market; (2) an integrated curriculum that combines technical competencies, entrepreneurship, and real-life project-based learning; (3) strong strategic partnerships with the industrial and business world for cocreation and quality assurance; (4) the development of an internal entrepreneurial ecosystem (such as teaching factories, business centers, and production units) that directly involves students; and (5) an organizational culture that encourages creativity, measured risk, and learning from failure. The main challenges faced include the gap between the educational and entrepreneurial mindset among educators, limited supporting infrastructure, and the rapidly changing dynamics of market demand. This study concludes that the successful implementation of edupreneurship in vocational education in East Java is highly dependent on holistic managerial commitment, an agile curriculum design, and symbiotic collaboration with the business ecosystem. The findings of this study are expected to serve as a reference for policy makers and vocational education practitioners in designing and managing sustainable and economically impactful edupreneurship strategies. title: Parametric analysis of ethanol-based recycling of mixed plastic waste in a circular economy
abstract: Growing concerns over the persistence and environmental impact of plastic waste highlight the need for recycling strategies that enable a circular economy by converting waste into valuable products. Despite this, integrated process models for chemical recycling of mixed plastic waste (MPW) remain limited. The novelty of this study lies in the integration of gasification of MPW to syngas, fermentation to ethanol, dehydration to ethylene, and polymerization to high-density polyethylene (HDPE) within an Aspen Plus process simulation framework, coupled with process optimization, heat integration, and energy-related GHG assessment, aiming to reduce waste and dependence on fossil resources. The framework was validated against published experimental and other data, with deviations of 0.12–4.0% across all process stages. Operating conditions were optimized through parametric analysis to maximize product yield and minimize energy consumption. Optimal gasification conditions were identified at an equivalence ratio of 0.21, steam-to-plastic ratio of 0.45, and temperature of 1000°C, producing 901.5 tonnes/day of syngas from a 500 tonnes/day plant. This syngas yielded 382 tonnes/day of ethanol, which was dehydrated at 450°C and 1 bar to produce 229 tonnes/day of ethylene. Polymerization of ethylene resulted in 228.4 tonnes/day of HDPE. The overall carbon conversion efficiency was 50.2%, corresponding to the carbon retained in HDPE relative to the carbon entering through the MPW feedstock. Heat integration reduced total heat demand by 56.1 MW (35.23%) and power consumption by 1.5 MW (6.12%), while lowering greenhouse gas emissions associated with energy consumption by 27.8% to 3.9 kg CO2e/kg HDPE. This approach supports scalable, energy-efficient plastic recycling and provides key insights for process design and implementation. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Can stablecoin instability threaten emerging tourism payment infrastructure?
abstract: Stablecoins are increasingly discussed as an emerging form of digital tourism payment infrastructure. This study examines whether instability in stablecoins creates vulnerabilities in emerging tourism payment ecosystems by analysing the UST and USDC depeg events. Drawing on tourism systems theory, tourism resilience theory, and financial economics, the analysis combines high-frequency market data, on-chain transaction activity, and tourism payment indicators. The results show that depeg events degrade market quality by widening bid–ask spreads, reducing market depth, and increasing transaction costs. Large market participants also reduce risk-bearing and withdraw liquidity during periods of stress. In addition, depeg events strengthen dynamic correlations among closely linked stablecoins. Evidence from tourism payment activity suggests that severe depeg events may reduce the use of stablecoin-based payments within crypto-native tourism ecosystems. The findings suggest that instability in stablecoins may introduce settlement uncertainty and payment frictions within tourism ecosystems experimenting with blockchain-based payment infrastructure. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: KGIA-Model: A Knowledge Graph-Driven Text-To-SQL Model for Intelligent Auditing
abstract: Automated interpretation of regulatory documents is essential for realizing intelligent auditing. To address the limited semantic understanding and rule extraction in existing approaches, this paper proposes KGIA-Model, a novel Text-to-SQL framework for audit automation. The model constructs an audit-oriented knowledge graph through semantic extraction and alignment from regulatory texts, then applies an expert cognition-inspired fine-tuning strategy with graph-driven prompt optimization and adaptive learning. Leveraging the fine-tuned language model, it dynamically generates SQL queries that transform audit rules into executable operations. Experiments on institutional, business, and synthetic datasets show that KGIA-Model outperforms six state-of-the-art Text-to-SQL baselines, achieving 80.3% execution accuracy and 68.4% exact match rate. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of expert cognition and knowledge graph collaboration in enhancing audit performance. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: AD-SQL: An Optimization Model for Text-To-SQL Based on Audit Prompt Fusion and Step-By-Step Strategies
abstract: Text-to-SQL technologies play a critical role in intelligent auditing by converting natural language or policy texts into executable SQL, thereby enhancing audit efficiency. However, due to the insufficient integration of domain knowledge, existing methods often demonstrate limited accuracy and adaptability to business needs when handling complex queries. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a new model named AD-SQL (Audit Prompt Adaptation and Decomposition SQL), a query optimization model integrates audit prompts technology and query decomposition process. The model employs a three-stage architecture. First, an enhanced RAG framework integrates audit rules and a knowledge base to encode structured knowledge into prompt vectors. Second, the query generation model recursively decomposes natural language queries into single-table queries, multi-table joins, and nested queries, applying customized strategies for each type. Finally, a structural integration mechanism synthesizes the subqueries into a complete SQL statement. A multi-loss supervision mechanism is introduced to jointly optimize SQL generation, execution consistency, and rule alignment losses. Experiments on both public and self-built audit datasets demonstrate that the overall accuracy of AD-SQL reaches 67.7%, with the accuracy of complex queries improving to 53%. Ablation studies confirm that the step-by-step decomposition strategy increases the query success rate by 4.4%. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Ultrasensitive SERS detection of explosive molecules via iodide-enhanced concentrated silver nanoparticles
abstract: Trace detection of nitroaromatic explosives such as 2,6-dinitrotoluene (2,6-DNT) and trinitrotoluene (TNT) is of great significance in the fields of homeland security, anti-terrorism monitoring and environmental governance. Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) has become a research hotspot in the field of chemical sensing owing to its unique ‘fingerprint identification’ capacity and high detection sensitivity. Nitroaromatic molecule analytes exhibit weak binding affinity toward conventional citrate-stabilized Ag NPs, which limits the effective adsorption of target molecules to the Ag NPs surface. These conventional substrates only enable detection of 2,6-DNT and TNT at concentrations as high as 10−1 M and 10−2 M, respectively. In this study, a surface regulation strategy is proposed by pretreatment highly concentrated Ag NPs with KI to fabricate a high-performance SERS sensing platform on a low-cost aluminum foil substrate. Benefiting from iodide-mediated surface modulation, the detection performance is greatly improved, with distinct characteristic Raman peaks of 2,6-DNT observable at an ultralow concentration of 10−10 M. I− can be used as a cleaning agent to effectively remove citrate from Ag NPs surface and provide abundant active sites for the analytes adsorption. In addition, the AgI shell formed on Ag NPs surface by reaction of I− and Ag+ can provide additional chemical enhancement through charge transfer mechanism. This strategy enables highly sensitive detection of nitroaromatic explosives and provides a very competitive solution for the monitoring of trace explosives in the field of public safety. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Policy Recommendations for Promoting the Utilization of Economic Partnership Agreements (EPAs) in Japan: Insights from Singapore’s Initiatives to Enhance the Use of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and EPAs
abstract: This study compares policies and institutional frameworks for promoting FTA/EPA utilisation in Singapore and Japan. Singapore is identified as one of the most advanced countries in FTA utilisation promotion, supported by a wide FTA network and a coordinated system of government agencies such as MTI, Enterprise Singapore, SME Centres, the Singapore Business Federation, and Singapore Customs. These institutions collectively provide structured guidance, financial support, advisory services, and digital tools (DX), enabling firms to identify applicable FTAs, understand rules of origin, and reduce administrative burdens. As a result, FTA awareness and perceived benefits among firms are relatively high, although challenges remain, particularly for SMEs in understanding rules of origin and managing certification processes. In contrast, Japan also provides extensive institutional support through METI, JETRO, the SME Agency, Customs, and the Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry. However, firm-level studies and consultation cases reveal persistent operational challenges, including complex origin determination due to large numbers of components, difficulties in obtaining supplier declarations, and HS code classification inconsistencies across countries. These issues can lead to rejection of preferential tariff treatment despite existing FTAs. The study highlights that a key bottleneck in both countries is the administrative complexity of rules of origin and HS classification, especially under CTC-based origin determination. It concludes that future improvements—particularly through the use of digital technologies such as AI to support classification and origin determination—could significantly enhance FTA/EPA utilisation by firms. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: A Heterogeneous Sharding Architecture for Privacy-Preserving Consortium Blockchains
abstract: Consortium blockchains are increasingly used for collaboration between organizations such as supply chains and e-government. However, deployments must isolate sensitive business data across organizations while preserving global auditability, and confidentiality mechanisms based on heavyweight modules often incur substantial overhead. To address these issues, we conduct the following research. Firstly, we propose a heterogeneous “parallel privacy shard” architecture. In this architecture, each organization runs an independent Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) in a privacy shard to maintain its private state, while a mainchain provides request scheduling, routing, and state anchoring. Secondly, we design a mainchain-coordinated execution protocol that enforces organization-level data isolation while preserving public verifiability for transaction confirmation. Finally, we implement a prototype on ChainMaker and evaluate it on AWS EC2. When scaling the number of privacy shards from 1 to 5, throughput improves by about 4.2× while latency increases by only 8.8%. With 5 shards, state-updating contract calls achieve 7.8030 ktx/s throughput with 1.1508 s latency. Results show that our system achieves high throughput and near-linear scalability with only marginal latency increase. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: SwanMixer: Fine-Grained Channel Modeling with Sliding-Window Adaptive Normalization for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting (MTSF) is important for decision-making in many real-world applications, including business decision-making, financial investment, and resource planning. Although recent Transformer-based models have improved long-horizon forecasting, two limitations remain. Existing channel dependence methods mainly rely on global interactions and therefore model cross-channel relations too coarsely, while existing normalization strategies are often too coarse to handle strong local distribution shifts in non-stationary data. To address these limitations, we propose SwanMixer, a forecasting architecture that combines Sliding Window Adaptive Normalization (SWAN), Patch Embedding, and GroupMixer. SWAN performs dynamic normalization within sliding windows to align local distributions while preserving informative non-stationary variations. On top of patch-level representations, GroupMixer introduces a hierarchical channel interaction scheme with intra-group and inter-group attention, which captures fine-grained local dependencies and aggregates global channel information efficiently. Experiments on Weather, Electricity, Traffic, and Solar-Energy show that SwanMixer consistently achieves superior or competitive results and obtains the largest number of best results among the compared methods. These results show that combining local adaptive normalization with fine-grained channel interaction is effective for MTSF. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: A dominant-subordinate generative approach to imbalanced deceptive review detection
abstract: Online reviews play an important role in both consumer purchase decisions and business performance analysis. However, deceptive reviews reduce the reliability of decisions based on online reviews. Although several studies developed algorithms to detect deceptive reviews, most of them ignored the negative impact of class imbalance, where legitimate reviews far outweigh deceptive reviews in practice. In this paper, we propose a deep generative approach called dominant-subordinate conditional variational auto-encoder and generative adversarial network (DC-VAEGAN) to address the class imbalance problem in deceptive review detection. Specifically, a dominant-subordinate condition structure is designed to generate and fine-tune deceptive review data at the review veracity and polarity levels. Empirical results show that the DC-VAEGAN provides statistically characterized, but not uniformly large, improvements in imbalanced deceptive review detection. The method is most useful for improving threshold-level balance indicators such as G-mean, while several Macro-F1 and AUC differences remain modest or non-significant. Further, interpretable analysis indicates that the augmented data helps the models learn reviewer-behavior and review-content anomalies more effectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Securing Small Businesses in the Late 2020’s Against Cyberattack
abstract: The cyber-resilience of small businesses is important to the economy of every nation. This is because small businesses form the majority of all businesses and because they can function as subcontractors to larger businesses and governments. The security scene of small businesses in Finland was studied by looking at what instructions and guides national security agencies have published for small businesses and what security products are available from the biggest internet service providers. The assumption being that a small business will most probably procure their cybersecurity solutions from the same instance that they get their internet subscription from. A list of the most relevant threats was then compared to the information publicly available on the web pages of these organisations to find the level of security that a small business will obtain. The results show that most technical threats are controlled against but the importance of a good security policy and training is also highlighted. No security certifications are required in Finland, except when sensitive or confidential information is being generated, stored or handled. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Multi-scale, multi-dimensional data mining for agentic AI micro-dramas recommendations
abstract: Micro-dramas, also known as micro-short dramas, are ultra-short, serialized video series optimized for mobile viewing, with episodes typically lasting 1–20 min. Multi-scale, multi-dimensional data mining (MSMD-DM) involves extracting patterns from complex datasets that vary across spatial, temporal, or hierarchical scales while managing high-dimensional features. Agentic AI recommendation refers to an autonomous, interactive, and goal-oriented AI system that transcends traditional recommendation paradigms. This study proposes an integrated framework that combines multi-scale (nominal and ordinal scale), multi-dimensional (demographics, preferences, intentions, and actual actions) data mining approach, K-means clustering, and association rule mining to support Agentic AI recommendations for micro-dramas. The framework addresses challenges related to data heterogeneity, dynamic user interactions, and context-aware decision-making. Using a sample of 3,016 Taiwanese consumers, we first segmented users into three distinct clusters via K-means analysis. Subsequently, association rules were mined within each cluster to uncover behavioral patterns and preferences related to micro-drama consumption and cross-screen e-commerce activities. The results provide actionable insights for micro-drama producers and e-commerce operators, enabling the design of personalized content and integrated business strategies. Theoretical and empirical analyses indicate that this integration not only provides a structured knowledge foundation for future agentic recommenders but also Agentic AI system architecture optimization, verifying an example of micro-drama recommendation, providing a structured knowledge foundation for future agentic recommenders, but also endows AI agents with recommendation capabilities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: DoRA-Based Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models for Corporate Compliance Determination
abstract: Corporate compliance determination plays an important role in enterprise risk management, as it requires not only judging whether business conduct conforms to relevant rules but also producing explanations that can support lawful operation and regulatory risk prevention. Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently been explored for compliance review and legal risk identification, yet their direct use in this setting is still limited by strict rule constraints, low tolerance for errors, and the need for interpretable and consistently structured outputs. These requirements expose the limitations of general-purpose foundation models, which may produce inaccurate judgments, unstable reasoning processes, or inconsistent report structures. To improve adaptation under such constraints, we propose DoRA-Variant, a Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) framework built on Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation (DoRA). DoRA-Variant introduces two modifications. First, the Frozen-A and Adaptive Learning Rates (FA) mechanism keeps the A matrix fixed and assigns asymmetric learning rates to the magnitude parameter m and matrix B, thereby restricting the update space and promoting more stable adaptation under small-sample conditions. Second, Directional Strength Calibration (DSC) rescales the directional update increment during inference, allowing the effective strength of directional adaptation to be controlled without additional training. Experiments on three public commonsense reasoning benchmarks and a controlled low-resource corporate compliance evaluation setting indicate that DoRA-Variant achieves a favorable trade-off between task performance and parameter efficiency compared with representative PEFT baselines. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: TabRLLM: Tabular Data Generation via Local-to-Global Rule Extraction in Low-Data Regimes
abstract: Machine learning on tabular data is often constrained by data scarcity, especially in domains where data collection is expensive or highly sensitive. Although data generation is widely adopted to alleviate this problem, existing approaches frequently fail to capture complex cross-feature dependencies and implicit business rules. To address these challenges in low-data regimes, we propose TabRLLM, which leverages large language models for semantic feature grouping. It extracts partial-table integrity rules and integrates them into full-table constraints. TabRLLM further combines these rules with statistical constraints, including marginal distributions and feature correlations, and converts them into prompts to guide data generation. Experiments on six real-world datasets demonstrate that TabRLLM achieves strong downstream performance across multiple datasets, with strong correlation preservation and competitive fidelity. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: A Multi-agent AI System with Collective Intelligence and Adaptive Reasoning for Automotive Fault Diagnosis
abstract: As AI (artificial intelligence) technology improves quickly, more and more businesses are using AI-powered systems to make their work more efficient and accurate. When it comes to car maintenance, traditional manual troubleshooting models are changing a lot. They are moving toward automated diagnostic workflows that are backed up by AI agent systems. As the designs of modern cars become more complicated, the need for maintenance support that is quick, accurate, and flexible is growing. This makes automotive fault diagnosis an important area for intelligent agent research to explore in the future. In times gone by, accurate diagnostics depended a lot on the knowledge and manual inspections of experienced technicians. This process is not only time-consuming and expensive, but it is also very prone to mistakes made by people. Current onboard diagnostics (OBD) systems give standardized fault reports, but they don’t let you easily understand them and don’t have the important ability to reason about context. Additionally, current systems have trouble understanding natural language inputs or combining unstructured data, like driver complaints, which are important for finding complex problems. As cars become more reliant on software and sensors, there is an urgent need for intelligent agent systems that the can conduct multimodal analysis and adaptive reasoning in the near future. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: From Implementation to Impact: Technology Acceptance, Absorptive Capacity, and the Productivity Paradox of Cashless Payment Systems
abstract: This study investigates how the implementation of cashless payment systems translates into organizational outcomes through the mediating roles of technology acceptance and absorptive capacity. Drawing on the productivity paradox literature, we argue that digital payment systems do not generate performance gains automatically; instead, their effects depend on post-implementation organizational processes. Using survey data collected from 266 firms in the retail and trading sectors, we tested a research model that links cashless payment implementation to supply-side and demand-side outcomes via technology acceptance and absorptive capacity. The results of covariance-based structural equation modeling reveal that while advanced implementation enhances technology acceptance, it does not directly increase absorptive capacity. Technology acceptance positively influences absorptive capacity and supply-side outcomes, whereas demand-side outcomes are shaped primarily by absorptive capacity and prior operational improvements. These findings indicate that the benefits of cashless payment systems emerge in a sequential and non-synchronous manner, highlighting the limitations of evaluating digital transformation initiatives based solely on short-term or single performance indicators. By integrating technology acceptance and absorptive capacity into a unified model, this study extends cashless payment research beyond adoption and provides a process-based explanation of the productivity paradox in contemporary digital transformation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Hurt at home, loafing at work: Spillover effect of family ostracism on hospitality employees’ cyberloafing and its mitigation through self- and others’ care
abstract: In the hospitality industry, employees’ cyberloafing is more visible to customers, potentially harming key business outcomes such as customer experience and satisfaction. Given these detrimental effects, it is critical to examine the underlying drivers that trigger cyberloafing behavior among hospitality employees. From this perspective, this study examines the influence of interpersonal stressor in the home domain—specifically, family ostracism—on cyberloafing among hospitality employees. Guided by the work-home resources framework, the present study explores a spillover process whereby family ostracism exacerbates hospitality employees’ cyberloafing via family emotional exhaustion. Additionally, it explores how these adverse effects can be mitigated through self-care efforts (self-compassion) and others’ care (family-supportive coworker behavior). Data were obtained from a three-wave survey involving 291 employees and their coworkers at two five-star hotels located in Southeastern China. The results confirm an indirect spillover effect wherein family ostracism leads to cyberloafing via family emotional exhaustion. However, this effect becomes insignificant when employees demonstrate high self-compassion or benefit from family-supportive coworker behavior. This study discusses both the theoretical implications derived from the findings and the practical contributions to the hospitality industry. © 2026

title: Microstructure and bulk rheology of heat-induced emulsion-filled pea protein gels: Effect of high-pressure homogenization
abstract: High-pressure homogenization (HPH) is often applied to process protein-stabilized emulsions. However, it remains unclear how HPH affects the interactions between protein-gel matrix and interfacial protein-coated oil or fat droplets, as well as the consequent network breakdown of the system. We investigated the differences in microstructure and rheological properties of emulsion-filled gels structured by unhomogenized or homogenized 8.5% commercial pea protein isolate containing 0, 10, or 20% lipid. Confocal images showed that the unhomogenized systems exhibited large protein-depleted regions, whereas the homogenized systems formed densely-packed networks. Small amplitude oscillatory shear (SAOS) temperature sweeps showed that gels containing 10% lipid were not significantly stiffer than gels without lipid, and their large amplitude oscillatory shear (LAOS) strain-amplitude sweeps showed similar yield points, yielding regimes and flow points. At 20% lipid, gel stiffness decreased notably, and yielding began at lower strain amplitude (γ0[jls-end-space/]). In contrast, HPH markedly increased gel stiffness, with further stiffening at higher lipid contents. Meanwhile, these gels yielded at lower γ0 over a broader range at higher lipid contents, and their loss modulus overshoot coincided with the rise in shear-thickening ratio. Moreover, sequence of physical processes (SPP) analysis showed that, as γ0 increased, the deltoid area changed more dramatically for 20% oil than for 20% fat, indicating that HPH shifted interfacial protein-coated lipid droplets from inactive fillers to active fillers that integrate into gradually yielding, denser networks. Fat droplets were more resistant to stretching and rupturing than oil droplets. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: AI-Enabled Knowledge Extraction and Transformation: Comparative Case Studies from Taiwanese Firms
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being adopted not only as a tool for automation and prediction but also as a mechanism for extracting, codifying, and transferring organizational knowledge. This study examines how AI contributes to knowledge transformation in Taiwanese business contexts through a qualitative multiple-case-study design. Based on semi-structured interviews conducted in Taiwan in March 2026, the study analyzes three firms operating in different domains: manufacturing automation, industrial AI platforms, and labor/legal advisory services. The findings show that AI-enabled knowledge transformation does not occur in a uniform manner. Instead, firms differ in how they extract knowledge from operational processes, expert judgment, and legal or advisory experience, and in how such knowledge is codified into digital systems and reused through organizational infrastructures. Across the three cases, a common pattern can be identified in the progression from AI-enabled knowledge extraction to codification, infrastructure formation, and knowledge transfer. At the same time, each case highlights a different organizational function of AI: process replication, analytical support, and expert knowledge formalization. The study contributes to the literature by showing that AI in business should be understood not only as a productivity-enhancing technology but also as an organizational mechanism for transforming tacit and experience-based knowledge into reusable forms. It also offers practical implications for firms seeking to preserve expertise, strengthen learning, and build scalable knowledge systems through AI. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Business Plan in Digital-Green Transitions: A Case Study of the NEXUS Agenda
abstract: This study examines the adaptation of business planning frameworks for large-scale, multi-stakeholder initiatives in fragmented sectors like logistics and transport. Through a qualitative single case study of the NEXUS Agenda - a collaborative project developing an Open Data Platform for Sines’ multimodal corridors - this research tests an integrated analytical model combining traditional business plan structures with the business model design. Findings reveal that conventional planning models are insufficient for complex, sustainability-oriented ecosystems, requiring hybrid frameworks that explicitly address stakeholder dynamics, inter-organisational governance, and shared-value creation. The study makes three main contributions: (1) conceptually, it extends business planning theory to collaborative digital-green contexts; (2) methodologically, it proposes a replicable hybrid framework linking structured analysis with visual business modelling; and (3) educationally, it demonstrates how such tools can foster strategic thinking and collaborative competencies in higher education. The results underscore the need for flexible planning approaches that balance analytical rigour with ecosystem adaptability, offering practical guidance for similar sustainability-driven initiatives and pedagogical applications. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Ohmic-assisted in-package processing combined with vacuum packaging as a multi-hurdle strategy to improve safety and temperature-dependent stability of frozen cooked shrimp
abstract: This study evaluated the effectiveness of integrating in-package ohmic-assisted thermal processing with vacuum packaging as a multi-hurdle strategy to enhance microbial safety and storage stability of frozen white shrimp. Shrimp were packaged under vacuum (V) or atmospheric (A) conditions and processed by ohmic heating (OH) or conventional retort (RE) treatment to an equivalent pasteurization condition (72 °C for 15 s). Samples were stored for 10 months at −18, −15, −10 °C, or under fluctuating temperature (FT) conditions simulating cold-chain variability. OH reduced come-up time by approximately 60% (12.75 vs. 32.00 min), thereby limiting thermal exposure. During storage at −18 °C, sensory acceptability of OH-V samples remained relatively stable (8.00–7.60), whereas RE-A samples under FT declined markedly (7.10–4.40). Oxidative deterioration showed a similar trend: TBARS values reached 1.27 mg MDA/kg in OH-V under FT compared with 2.43 mg MDA/kg in RE-A, while carotenoid losses remained below 3% in OH-V at −18 °C but exceeded 9% in RE-A under FT. Kinetic analysis confirmed quality deterioration within the frozen storage range (R2 = 0.908–0.999; Q10 = 2.10–3.82). Notably, OH-V samples exhibited lower activation energy and Q10 values, indicating reduced temperature sensitivity and improved tolerance to cold-chain fluctuations. Principal component analysis revealed coordinated oxidative, microbial, and sensory quality changes during storage. No target pathogens were detected, supporting microbiological safety. These findings demonstrate that ohmic-assisted in-package processing combined with oxygen-restricted packaging can reduce deterioration kinetics and improve cold-chain stability, supporting its potential as a preventive food control strategy for frozen shrimp. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A Clustering-Enhanced LLM Pipeline for Large-Scale Electoral Data Analysis
abstract: Integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into Business Intelligence is often hampered by context limits and hallucinations when processing raw data. This paper proposes a hybrid framework that integrates unsupervised clustering with Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) to analyze the 2025 Portuguese Legislative Elections. We utilized socio-economic indicators to benchmark K-Means, Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) and Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) algorithms for the segmentation of national voting behaviors. Although DBSCAN demonstrated superior separation metrics, we chose K-Means due to its better interpretability. Then, these cluster summaries were analyzed using two quantized LLMs: Mistral-7B and Mixtral-8×7B. The results indicate that Mixtral vastly exceeds standard models in both factual veracity and strategic logic, notably identifying nuances such as high urban unemployment. This study confirms that clustering serves as a vital preprocessing layer to ensure the reliability and scalability of GenAI in political science. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Evolution and Models of Business Plans: A Literature Review Applied to Business Planning
abstract: The business plan is a central tool of corporate planning, supporting strategic goal setting, feasibility assessment and resource structuring. This literature review analyses the role of business plans in organizational management, their historical evolution and their relevance across different business stages. It also examines their classical structure, key components, the need for audience-oriented customization and their specific impact on microenterprises. Finally, it presents the main business plan models (traditional, agile, simplified and hybrid), highlighting their characteristics, advantages, and limitations. Findings show that no single model is universally superior, as suitability depends on context and strategic objectives. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Motivational Configurations in GenAI-Supported Management Learning: a Qualitative Exploration
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) tools such as ChatGPT are increasingly used in management education. Beyond technological affordances, sustained engagement depends on motivational alignment. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this study explores how epistemic curiosity (EC) and teacher support (TS) interact in shaping Gen AI use. A four-quadrant typology is proposed and examined through semi-structured interviews with business students. Results indicate that aligned high EC and TS foster deeper engagement, whereas misalignment results in limited learning. The findings provide qualitative insights into motivation-aware AI-integrated pedagogy. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Consumers' servitization experience: Implications for perceived social value and preference for local brands
abstract: This study examines how consumers’ servitization experience may reshape the symbolic and social meanings associated with local brands in sustainable consumption contexts. The increasing adoption of service-based consumption models in retail and consumer services is transforming how consumers interact with brands. While prior research has examined the functional and relational benefits of servitization, less is known about how service-based consumption experiences shape the social meaning of brand consumption and influence consumer preferences in sustainability contexts. The findings suggest that servitization experience may function as a double-edged mechanism: it enhances the social signaling value of local brands while simultaneously weakening direct brand preference. Drawing on a survey of 396 consumers in the automotive sector and using structural equation modeling, the findings indicate that servitization experience is positively associated with the perceived social value of local brands, which is strongly associated with brand preference. At the same time, a negative direct effect on brand preference is observed, revealing trade-offs between experiential benefits and reductions in ownership-based symbolic meaning. Additionally, sustainability-oriented consumers are more likely to engage with servitized offerings and perceive higher social value in local brands. These results contribute to retailing and consumer services research by showing that service-based consumption experiences may reshape not only functional and relational value, but also the social meaning of consumption. Managerially, the findings highlight the importance of designing service-based offerings that enhance the communicative value of sustainable consumption while mitigating potential negative effects on brand attachment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Study on the effects of policy intervention on lithium-ion batteries recycling industry via an innovative AI-enabled dynamic business model
abstract: With the rapid expansion of the electric vehicle (EV) market, a large number of spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have gradually become a serious threat to resource conservation and environmental management. Proper and effective recycling of spent LIBs requires not only coordinated value chain operations but also policy instruments capable of steering industrial behavior and optimizing resource allocation. Thus, this study develops an artificial intelligence-enhanced dynamic business model (AI-DBM) that integrates system dynamics, the business model canvas, and AI-based analytical methods, addressing the limitations of existing policy analysis in characterizing business model logic and explaining the mechanisms underlying policy effect. Taking China's LIBs recycling industry as an empirical case, this study systematically and quantitatively evaluates the dynamic impacts of six policy intervention strategies, including collection subsidy, tax incentives, promoting repurposing, integrating into carbon trade market, recycling technology-driven, and mixed policies, on value chain performance, profit distribution, and industrial sustainability. Results reveal pronounced heterogeneity and nonlinear responses across value-chain stakeholders under different policies. While single policy instruments improve performance in specific segments to varying degrees and exhibit clear nonlinear marginal effects, coordinated implementation of multiple policies proves more conducive to the development of the LIBs recycling industry, boosting industry's net profit to 123.20 billion RMB by 2040 and driving collection recycling rate beyond 50%, substantially outperforming any single policy and signaling a structural upgrade of the recycling system. Overall, dynamically coordinated and diversified policy portfolios are essential for steering China's LIBs recycling industry toward a sustainable circular economy. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Biomimetic PD-1-Functionalized Immunostimulatory Nanomedicine Enables STING Activation and Durable Antitumor Immunity in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) responds poorly to immune checkpoint blockade, largely because of an immunologically cold tumor microenvironment (TME) characterized by deficient antigen presentation and impaired cytotoxic T cell responses. Analysis of numerous HCC clinical cohorts, including our institutional datasets, reveals that stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway activity is positively correlated with patient survival, enhanced antigen presentation capacity, and an immune-activated TME. However, achieving effective and controllable STING activation in immune-cold HCC tumors remains challenging. Here, we develop a biomimetic nanomedicine that integrates photothermal therapy (PTT), STING pathway activation, and immune checkpoint blockade to treat refractory HCC. A coordination nanomedicine MCI-NP is engineered by co-encapsulating the STING agonist MSA-2 and indocyanine green (ICG) via Cu2+-mediated chelation, enabling stabilized PTT-induced immunogenic cell death together with robust STING-driven innate immune activation. Further cloaked with PD-1-overexpressing cell membranes, MCI-NP@mPD-1 achieves an approximately fivefold increase in tumor accumulation compared with uncoated MCI-NP and enables localized PD-1/PD-L1 axis blockade. Following a single treatment, MCI-NP@mPD-1-based photothermal immunotherapy effectively suppresses primary tumor growth and significantly prolongs survival by remodeling the TME toward an immune-active state, while inducing durable systemic immune memory that effectively limited postoperative lung metastasis. Without introducing additional nanocarriers or excipients, MCI-NP@mPD-1 offers a promising therapeutic paradigm for photothermal immunotherapy of immune-cold HCC. title: Future Trends in Sustainable Supply Chain Development
abstract: Sustainable supply chain development has evolved from a peripheral corporate initiative into a central pillar of global business strategy. As industries confront climate change, geopolitical uncertainty, and digital transformation, the sustainability of supply chains has become a determinant of long-term competitiveness and resilience. This study reviews the current literature and proposes a conceptual synthesis of future trends that will shape sustainable supply chain development. Through an integrative review of studies published between 2020 and 2025, the discussion identifies six main paths: (1) circular economy integration, (2) digitalization and artificial intelligence, (3) decarbonization and renewable energy adoption, (4) stakeholder collaboration and social equity, (5) data transparency and governance, and (6) resilience through regionalization and risk diversification. The paper argues that future sustainable supply chains will be characterized by intelligent, data-driven systems embedded in circular and low-carbon business models. It concludes by outlining managerial and policy implications, emphasizing the need for collaborative frameworks, digital literacy, and global governance mechanisms to enable the transition toward sustainable, resilient, and inclusive supply networks. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Gamified Marketing as a Tool for Sustainable and Positive Educational Change
abstract: Gamification offers new opportunities for organizations seeking to encourage responsible behavior and foster positive engagement in sustainable practices. This work investigates the potential of gamified marketing to drive conscious consumption and support environmental, social, and economic causes. Employing a mixed-methods approach, the study integrates company campaign observation, and consumer and brand inquires to examine the impact of gamification elements across digital platforms. Findings show users are highly familiar with gamified initiatives and significantly value both economic and ecological rewards. Case analyses reveal that well-designed gamified interventions can strengthen consumer loyalty and incentivize the adoption of sustainable behaviors, simultaneously aligning organizational objectives with broader values of sustainability. The results highlight gamification’s capacity to reinforce emotional connection, motivation, and positive habits, contributing to a more holistic well-being in educational and organizational ecosystems. This research proposes a practical and theoretical analysis model for brands aiming to use gamification as a tool to promote sustained, responsible behavior change. By linking marketing innovation and gamified strategies, this study helps build resilient, flourishing communities through human-centric digital transformation and supports embedding sustainable development goals into long-term educational strategies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Managers’ Educational Level and Sustainability. Its Impact on the Well-Being of C-Top Managers: A Literature Review
abstract: This literature review explores how C-level education connects to corporate sustainability and executive well-being. Drawing on upper echelons and human capital perspectives, prior literature links higher education to stronger corporate social responsibility (CSR) engagement and green innovation. The well-being implications, however, are less consistent. Education can support self-efficacy and a sense of purpose, but it can also intensify role overload and moral strain when organisational priorities conflict with sustainability values. We conclude by outlining key gaps and directions for future research. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Relationships that Shape the Future: Stakeholder Management and Relationship Marketing in the Twin Transition
abstract: This paper examines how relationship marketing strategies can mitigate stakeholder conflicts and foster alignment during the twin transition, understood as the simultaneous green and digital transformation of organizations. A PRISMA-based systematic literature review was conducted, resulting in a final sample of 35 articles from Scopus and Web of Science in the fields of business, management and marketing, which evidences a recent surge of interest in this topic. The findings show three main tension clusters – economic, rational and legitimacy – arising from the misalignment between cost efficiency, data-driven tools and stakeholders’ emotional and ethical expectations. Relationship marketing emerges as a critical mediator, translating digital tools into sustainable value through relational/service-oriented approaches, transparency-enhancing technologies, and emotional engagement/personalization. The study contributes by consolidating a fragmented body of knowledge and clarifying the central role of relationship marketing in governing the twin transition. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: An Integration Between Blockchain Technology and Artificial Intelligence in the Urban Population
abstract: Nowadays, cities face diverse issues, including traffic congestion, disorganized urban planning, rising house prices, and the consequent increase in CO2 emissions. In this vein, this study aims to examine the benefits and drawbacks of integrating cutting-edge technologies, specifically Blockchain Technology (BT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI), to advance sustainability and align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in the urban population. This research conducted a systematic literature review analysing 25 research papers published between 2009 and June 2025, indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) database. Findings show that applying AI and BT in urban populations improves road conditions for smart mobility, enhances citizen security and participation, improves waste management, reduces counterfeiting in supply chains, and diminishes energy consumption in smart buildings. Nonetheless, there is a series of concerns, among them, economic, social, legal, educational, and environmental. Implementing groundbreaking technologies could lead not only to positive implications but also to negative consequences, such as unemployment, privacy issues, a lack of knowledge, or excessive energy consumption. Moreover, this study proposes diverse ideas to make cities more environmentally friendly, such as gamified apps, crypto payments, or AI systems, to name but a few. Furthermore, this paper contributes theoretically by explaining the relationships among AI, BT, and urban sustainability, and practically by providing policymakers and businesses with insights to improve various sectors of smart cities. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: GenAI Mock Interviews for Business Chinese Learners: Benefits, Challenges, and a TAM 3 Analysis
abstract: Grounded in Technology Acceptance Model 3 (TAM 3), this study examines intermediate-level learners’ acceptance of a generative-AI interview teaching agent (ChatGPT) for simulated Chinese job-interview practice through three constructs: perceived ease of use (PEOU), perceived usefulness (PU), and behavioral intention (BI). Ten foreign learners of Business Chinese (all master’s-level students) participated in a ChatGPT-based interview practice activity using speech recognition and spoken output to approximate real interview interaction, followed by semi-structured interviews. Findings show polarized perceptions of ease of use: some participants found the system easy and effective for practice, whereas others reported difficulties with voice input, particularly inaccurate recognition of Mandarin tones and certain words, which reduced usability. Perceived usefulness was generally positive: learners reported that generative AI helped them familiarize themselves with interview structures and procedures and provided immediate, relatively neutral feedback. However, participants also noted important limitations: the AI could not adequately correct pronunciation and intonation, showed limited tolerance for speech errors, and often provided feedback lacking depth and humanized understanding, thereby constraining learning gains. Regarding behavioral intention, most learners expressed willingness to continue using the tool—especially if speech recognition improves—and to recommend it to learners with strong self-directed learning needs. Nonetheless, they did not view AI as a replacement for teachers or face-to-face interaction. Overall, the study indicates moderate acceptance of AI-assisted interview practice and highlights the need to combine generative AI with human guidance in CFL instruction. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Robustness in deepfake speech detection: A survey of failure mechanisms including an experimental case study
abstract: In recent years, the emergence of disruptive deepfake technology (referring here to computer-generated speech/audio, images, video and text) has raised significant concerns surrounding the privacy, security, and credibility of digital content. Although detection systems report high benchmark performance, most are evaluated on in-domain datasets, codecs, and generative models seen during training. In real deployment, however, detectors must contend with out-of-domain instances, that is, a mismatch between the data seen during training and the conditions encountered in deployment (e.g., unseen generative methods, unfamiliar codecs, or signals degraded by transmission channels). Under these conditions, performance often degrades sharply. While robustness has been acknowledged in the literature, it remains underexplored. This work presents a robustness-focused survey and experimental study of deepfake speech detection. Rather than broadly cataloguing existing methods, we organise the literature around three factors that influence robustness to distribution shift: dataset design, feature representations, and model architecture. To complement this synthesis, we conduct a cross-dataset evaluation with Wav2Vec2, HuBERT, WavLM, and Whisper self-supervised speech models, trained on the ASVspoof 2019 LA and evaluated on the ASVspoof 2021 Deepfake dataset. The experimental results show that robustness varies considerably across models and conditions. HuBERT demonstrates comparatively stable performance across codec and dataset shifts, while Wav2Vec2 and WavLM experience substantial degradation, particularly under MP3-based compression and neural vocoder synthesis. A diagnostic analysis further reveals that robustness failures are strongly associated with codec-induced masking of synthesis artefacts and with dataset-dependent synthesis pipelines. By combining a robustness-oriented survey with cross-dataset experimental evidence, this work puts theory to practice, highlighting key factors that limit the generalisation of current detectors and outlining practical directions for improving robustness, including diversified dataset design, feature fusion, and evaluation under realistic cross-domain conditions. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Financial and Performance Indicators of Supply Chains: An Econometric Analysis
abstract: This study aims to contribute to the understanding of how intellectual capital efficiency and innovation influence financial performance in European ports operating within maritime supply chains, particularly under systemic shocks and crisis conditions. Using the Value Added Intellectual Coefficient as a measure of intangible asset management, the study assesses whether ports’ innovation capacity and intellectual capital efficiency enhance financial performance and resilience during adverse macroeconomic environments. Empirically, the analysis employs System GMM estimators to account for unobserved heterogeneity across ports and the dynamic nature of financial outcomes. The sample comprises 23 European ports observed from 2018 to 2023, encompassing disruptive events such as the COVID-19 pandemic, geopolitical conflicts, and economic uncertainty. Financial performance is modelled as a function of VAIC, innovation variables, port size, and macroeconomic controls. Results indicate that intellectual capital efficiency has a positive and significant impact on port financial performance, even during crisis periods. Innovation further strengthens value creation, competitiveness, and adaptive capacity within maritime logistics chains. This study advances port economics by integrating an adapted VAIC and innovation as organizational resilience drivers. Diverging from cross-sectoral analyses, the research demonstrates the strategic primacy of intangible assets in sustaining performance and viability during exogenous shocks. The results provide a robust framework for academics and policymakers to enhance the maritime sector’s adaptive capacity through intellectual capital. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Progress and Constraints in the E-commerce Sector: A 2023–2025 Study of Webshops in Bosnia and Herzegovina
abstract: This paper examines the evolution of the e-commerce landscape in Bosnia and Herzegovina (B&H) between 2023 and 2025 based on three consecutive annual surveys of 423 webshops (162 in 2023, 154 in 2024 and 107 in 2025) conducted in cooperation with the eCommerce Association in B&H. The study adopts a descriptive and exploratory approach, without testing causal relationships. The findings indicate gradual market maturation, reflected in the increasing share of long-established and domestically owned webshops, as well as the continued prevalence of omnichannel business models. Operational practices improved unevenly – logistics and administrative digitalization advanced steadily, while payment modernization lagged, with cash-on-delivery remaining the dominant method across all three years. Merchants consistently identified similar barriers, including customer habits, informal competition, market size limitations, regulatory ambiguity, and skills shortages, while emphasizing product quality, competitive pricing, delivery reliability, payment security and branding as key success factors. Overall, the results suggest that further development of the e-commerce sector in B&H requires parallel improvements in firm-level capabilities and the broader institutional and market ecosystem. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Evaluation of Generative AI Tools for Process Modeling with Educational Purposes
abstract: Process modeling is an important topic that has faced multiple advancements, as a result of its integration with artificial intelligence. However, it still challenges students, regardless of their previous experience with the modeling domain. This paper focuses on the exploratory qualitative evaluation of three AI-based tools: Eraser AI BPMN Diagram Generator, BPMN GPT, and ProcessMaker, which can generate process models in Business Process Modeling Notation (BPMN). This study includes an empirical experiment with engineering students, who worked on generating and refining BPMN diagrams using iterative prompts, to match ground-truth diagrams. A structured document template was employed to monitor their work, including prompt versions, tool observations, and reflection-dedicated sections, allowing them to critically assess AI-generated diagrams in an educational setting. Results showed that in-built editing options, friendly visual appearance, or code control are the top preferences of engineering students. Iterative prompts allowed them to observe the power of key elements when requesting AI-generated diagram. Additionally, human-in-the-loop is still highly relevant for this field, as shown by the below results. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Evaluating Students’ AI Literacy and Reflective Capacity in an Entrepreneurship Course Using Professor E
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has the potential as a powerful tool to enhance and strengthen student learning experiences. Students depend on GenAI for immediate answer generating rather than cultivating genuine reflection. To fill this gap, the researchers created a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-enabled chatbot, Professor E, which assists students in reflection using Gibbs’s reflective cycle. The researchers used an exploratory methodology to assess students’ AI literacy, reflective capabilities, and their impressions of the system’s educational design. This exploratory study examines students’ AI literacy and reflective capacity, as well as their impressions of the system’s educational design. The researchers gathered data through AI-student conversations to discern the principal themes arising from collaborations between students and AI in an entrepreneurship course in a Hong Kong business school. The focus group interview results highlighted students’ concerns on technical, practical, critical, and ethical factors when utilising Professor E for reflective purposes. The implementation of protected systems, role-playing, and RAG creation helped students in articulating personal thoughts, fostering empathy, and obtaining relevant, customised guidance linked with their project endeavours. This work advances the field of AI-human collaboration by highlighting how pedagogically built GenAI systems can improve students’ reflective thinking abilities. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: An Unsupervised Contrastive Learning Approach for Cold-Start Question-Answering Systems
abstract: In the current wave of digital transformation, Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) answering systems have become a key technology for replacing traditional manual customer service and efficiently handling high-frequency user inquiries. This paper focuses on the cold-start phase of FAQ question-answering systems, aiming to ensure that such systems can be effectively initialized under no in-domain labeled data conditions. To this end, we investigate an FAQ question-answering system based on question semantic similarity, specifically designed for the cold-start scenario. To mitigate the anisotropy problem commonly observed in pre-trained language models, we propose an unsupervised text augmentation method to construct high-quality positive samples for contrastive learning. This approach enables the learning of a improved embedding geometry, which serves as a strong foundation for subsequent fine-tuning in low-resource downstream tasks. We refer to this method as LACSE (Large-model Augmented Contrastive Sentence Embeddings). Experimental results demonstrate that LACSE produces higher-quality sentence embeddings and effectively adapts to cold-start requirements across different business scenarios, providing a more robust semantic representation basis for subsequent supervised fine-tuning. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Towards faster and deeper hoeffding trees: Fractional bounds and correlation-preserving multi-index statistics
abstract: This paper presents two complementary enhancements to the Very Fast Decision Tree algorithm for data stream mining. The first contribution introduces the fractional Hoeffding bound, a relaxed splitting criterion where the original threshold is scaled by a factor f<1. Experimental evidence shows that with this modification, the resulting trees not only grow faster but also achieve higher accuracy compared to the original Very Fast Decision Tree. The second contribution proposes a novel data structure, called extended statistics, which extends the traditional sufficient statistics used in the Very Fast Decision Tree by maintaining additional information about attribute co-occurrences. This allows child nodes to inherit richer knowledge from their parent, leading to deeper trees with accelerated convergence to the target accuracy. Numerical experiments on synthetic data streams demonstrate that the combination of fractional bounds and multi-index statistics yields significant accuracy gains, particularly in the early phases of learning. The extended statistics improvement, however, comes at the cost of increased memory and computational requirements, emphasizing the trade-off between predictive performance and resource usage. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Ethnomedicinal use and cytotoxicity of medicinal plants used in soft porridge for infant health issues in Vhembe District, South Africa
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: In South Africa, the Vhavenda tribe traditionally feed infants Tshiunza/Khongoḓoli, a very light, warm, and soft porridge prepared with medicinal plant concoctions. This practice is believed to prevent, manage, or treat various diseases and provide nutritional support. Aim of the study: The aim of the study was to document the medicinal plants administered through soft porridge, including preparation methods and dosages for infant illnesses, among the Vhavenda tribe of Vhembe District, South Africa, and to determine the cytotoxicity of selected medicinal plants. Materials and methods: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with caregivers, elderly women, and traditional healers. Cytotoxicity assay of five selected medicinal plants was conducted using the MTT assay on African monkey kidney cells (Vero cells). Results: Seventy-two medicinal plants were documented, of which 38 were used in the preparation of Tshiunza/Khongoḓoli. Roots were the most frequently used plant part, and the dominant preparation method involved soaking plant material in water and using the extract to make the soft porridge. These plants were commonly used to treat fontanelle-related illnesses and stomach problems. Combretum molle R.Br. ex G.Don. and Gymnosporia buxifolia (L.) exhibited low cytotoxicity with IC50 of 476.7559 and 276.4863 μg/mL, respectively. Conclusion: This study provides novel ethnomedicinal evidence on medicinal plants administered through soft porridge, a culturally important infant-feeding practice among the Vhavenda people. However, the cytotoxicity of Combretum molle R.Br. ex G.Don. and Gymnosporia buxifolia (L.) underscores the need for further toxicological evaluation of medicinal plants used in infant foods, especially for infants under 3 months old, whose physiological and metabolic systems are still developing. © 2026 The Authors. title: Probabilistic ordered weighted averaging distances for tariff networks: an application to emerging countries
abstract: This study develops a probabilistic ordered weighted averaging (OWA) tariff-distance framework to measure tariff cohesion among emerging economies. The proposed probabilistic OWA weighted average tariff distance (POWAWATD) extends the probabilistic OWA weighted average distance logic to tariff schedules by decomposing tariff dissimilarity into three interpretable layers: ordered tariff gaps, policy-importance weights and trade-salience probabilities. Generalized and quasi-arithmetic variants are also introduced to adjust the sensitivity of the measure to large tariff spikes, moderate discrepancies and flow-relevant deviations. The framework is illustrated using BRICS and BRICS+ economies. In the balanced specification, Brazil–India records a higher tariff distance than China–Russia, with POWAWATD values of 0.1070 and 0.0658, respectively. Under spike-vigilant and flow-salient specifications, the Brazil–India distance increases to 0.1186 and 0.1219, showing that its tariff misalignment is concentrated in upper-rank and economically salient product lines. The results indicate that POWAWATD provides a transparent and flexible tool for comparing tariff structures, identifying cohesion patterns and assessing how trade-policy distances respond to alternative aggregation attitudes. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: BACHunter: An Automated Fuzzing Framework for Discovering Broken Access Control Vulnerabilities in Java Web Applications
abstract: Broken Access Control (BAC) remains one of the most critical security threats in Java Web applications. Existing automated analysis techniques often struggle with the complex business logic and execution overhead inherent in these sys-tems. To the best of our knowledge, we present BACHunter, the first fuzzing-based framework designed for discovering BAC vulnerabilities in Java Web applications. BACHunter combines an in-memory service dispatcher to elimi-nate network-induced performance bottlenecks, a hierarchical mutation engine to systematically explore diverse authorization scenarios, and an entity-centric dif-ferential oracle for precise vulnerability verification. We evaluated BACHunter on a benchmark of 15 representative CVEs drawn from real-world open-source projects. It detected all vulnerabilities in this benchmark with a 100% detection rate and an average discovery time of 17 s, while showing better perfor-mance than prior BAC detection approaches. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Computing the Distribution of the Traces of a Business Process by Their Lengths
abstract: Business process models may generate large sets of execution traces whose size and structure depend on control-flow constructs such as choice, parallelism, and iteration. While their qualitative behavior is well understood, computing exact trace-length distributions remains challenging, and existing structural approaches are limited in scope. We propose a region-based method to compute trace-length distributions directly from the structure of a BPMN model. Each region is associated with a length-indexed vector, enabling query-oriented analysis such as length-bounded counting, multiplicity constraints, and bounded loop unfolding, while preserving a reachability-free and compositional approach. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Security testing of RESTful APIs: Approaches and research challenges
abstract: RESTful APIs have become a fundamental component of modern cloud-native and microservice-based applications, enabling seamless integration between distributed services. Since these APIs often expose sensitive data and business logic through publicly accessible endpoints, they have become attractive targets for cyberattacks. Recent security incidents and the growing number of API-related vulnerabilities demonstrate that traditional web application security mechanisms are insufficient for protecting RESTful APIs. Although numerous testing approaches have been proposed, existing research remains fragmented and often focuses primarily on functional validation rather than systematically addressing security vulnerabilities and adversarial exploitation patterns. This survey provides a comprehensive review of RESTful API testing approaches with a particular focus on those identifying security vulnerabilities. Based on a systematic analysis of 69 primary studies, we examine common RESTful API vulnerabilities and present a structured taxonomy that distinguishes between application-level weaknesses and configuration or deployment-level issues. We further analyze the attack patterns that exploit these vulnerabilities and review state-of-the-art testing approaches, including specification-based, model-based, property-based, and AI/ML-driven techniques. In addition, we analyze existing tools, datasets, and evaluation metrics used to assess the effectiveness of RESTful API testing methods. Finally, the survey identifies several critical research gaps that limit the effectiveness of current approaches, particularly around authenticated, context-aware testing and the detection and validation of logic-based security violations. We discuss emerging trends and outline potential research directions, including dependency-aware testing frameworks and AI-driven techniques for automated vulnerability discovery. This work aims to guide researchers and practitioners toward developing more systematic and robust frameworks for RESTful API security testing. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Food authentication technologies in Sub-Saharan Africa: Regulatory integration, analytical capacity, and governance challenges in preventive food safety systems
abstract: Food fraud and mislabeling represent persistent threats to food safety and public health, particularly in Sub Saharan Africa where fragmented supply chains, dominant informal markets, and limited regulatory capacity increase vulnerability to adulteration and misrepresentation. The growing complexity of global food systems has intensified the need for reliable authentication and traceability tools as integral components of preventive food safety frameworks. This review critically examines the current landscape of food authentication technologies in Sub Saharan Africa, with emphasis on their analytical performance, practical applicability, and integration into regulatory control systems. A systematic narrative review approach was adopted, guided by structured evidence synthesis principles. Peer reviewed literature published between 2010 and 2026 was analyzed across major scientific databases, focusing on spectroscopic, chromatographic, molecular, and isotopic analytical methods, alongside digital traceability systems and artificial intelligence-driven data analytics. The review employed thematic and comparative synthesis to evaluate technological effectiveness, adoption patterns, and regulatory relevance. The evidence indicates that spectroscopic techniques enable rapid screening, while chromatographic and molecular methods provide high precision confirmatory analysis. Isotope ratio analysis supports origin verification, while digital traceability systems, including blockchain-based ledgers, improve supply chain transparency, while artificial intelligence and machine learning tools function as analytical decision-support systems that enhance pattern recognition and predictive analytics for fraud detection. However, significant limitations persist, including inadequate context specific validation, high costs, limited infrastructure, and weak integration into preventive food safety systems. Technology adoption remains uneven, with concentration in urban laboratories and limited coverage in informal markets. Strengthening food authentication in Sub Saharan Africa requires coordinated investment in low cost technologies, context specific validation frameworks, and regulatory harmonization. Integrating authentication into risk-based food safety systems is essential for improving surveillance, enhancing consumer protection, and aligning regional practices with international standards. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Development of an adaptive governance model for managing overtourism in sustainable tourism destinations
abstract: The phenomenon of overtourism has emerged as a critical challenge in global destination management, precipitating severe environmental degradation, sociocultural disruptions, and declining quality of life for host communities. Conventional top-down strategies have proven inadequate in addressing the complex dynamics of excessive tourist influx. This study aims to develop a contextual adaptive governance model designed to effectively control overtourism while promoting sustainable tourism development. Employing a qualitative descriptive-analytical approach, the research focuses on Penglipuran Village, a prominent culture-based destination in Bali, Indonesia. Primary data were gathered through in-depth interviews with twenty-four key informants, comprising traditional leaders, village officials, tourism business operators, local residents, and domestic and international tourists, alongside participatory observation and comprehensive document analysis. The data were processed using rigorous thematic analysis techniques. The findings reveal that overtourism management necessitates a flexible, multi-dimensional framework rather than rigid regulatory measures. The developed model highlights three pivotal components: institutional flexibility that integrates customary laws with formal policies, structured multi-stakeholder collaboration fostering synergistic decision-making, and a continuous learning mechanism enabling iterative policy adaptation. Results further indicate that while tourism generates substantial economic benefits, it simultaneously triggers cultural commercialization, shifts in local social values, and intensified environmental strain. Critical governance gaps were identified, particularly the fragmentation between traditional and formal institutional systems, reliance on manual monitoring, and the absence of systematic coordination structures. By embedding social negotiation and cultural legitimacy into governance processes, the proposed model successfully balances economic imperatives with ecological and sociocultural preservation. Theoretically, this research enriches the tourism governance literature by systematically integrating adaptive governance principles within the overtourism discourse. Practically, it provides destination managers and policymakers with a scalable, context-sensitive framework that leverages local wisdom, digital monitoring, and collaborative institutional design to ensure long-term destination resilience and sustainability in the face of escalating tourism pressures. title: A Scalable Framework for Entity Resolution and Corporate Network Inference in Large Business Data
abstract: Modern business environments produce large, complex data containing duplications, inconsistencies, and fragmented representations of ownership and control. Resolving these data into accurate and consolidated representations is critical for downstream use cases, including fraud detection, risk analysis, and regulatory compliance. Our work proposes a scalable and multi-stage entity resolution and network inference framework for business datasets from a payroll company. The framework integrates graph-based modelling and advanced analytics to eliminate redundant entities, identify ownership structures, and discover implicit relationships between them. Developed using Apache Spark and deployed in Microsoft Fabric, the pipeline achieves 85.2% resolution coverage with an estimated false positive rate of less than 3.5%, discovered over 400 tightly-knit business communities, and identified 2.3% anomalies. Our approach establishes a reproducible model for organisational datasets where unique identifiers and schemas are absent, contributing an explainable new framework for corporate transparency and network-based risk analysis. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.
