title: Deep-QLP and Spline based Quadrature Rules for Fredholm Integral Equations of the First Kind
abstract: In this paper, we propose a numerical method to construct an approximate solution to Fredholm integral equations of the first kind. These equations are common in image processing, spectroscopy, and other engineering sciences but are often ill-posed. Moreover, the right hand side of such equations could be error-contaminated. To effectively tackle the mentioned challenges, we propose suitable quadrature rules to discretize the continuous problem. The resulting discrete system is solved in a regularized least-squares framework by adopting the Deep-QLP factorization: a novel algorithm that automatically computes an approximate truncated singular value decomposition based on a user-defined tolerance. Additionally, two regularization approaches are introduced. In the first one, given a perturbed right-hand side, a Hankel matrix is constructed and then, the so-called de-Hankelization is performed by adopting the same Deep-QLP algorithm. In the second approach, we rely on locally refined discretization spaces to increase the accuracy of the computed approximate solution, by keeping low the number of the used degrees of freedom. Numerical experiments are conducted on some famous Fredholm integral equations available in the literature. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: AI-Based System for Automatic Backlog Generation and Preliminary Estimation from Requirement Documents
abstract: In the context of digital transformation and Agile software development, requirement analysis and backlog preparation remain largely manual processes that rely heavily on individual experience and interpretation. These activities are time-consuming, error-prone, and often inconsistent, particularly in large-scale software projects. This paper presents an AI-based system for automatic backlog generation and preliminary effort estimation from requirement documents, designed to support Business Analysts (BAs) and Project Management Offices (PMOs) in Agile environments. The proposed system automatically analyzes software requirement documents, such as User Requirement Documents (URD) and Requirement Specification Documents (RSD), and generates structured Agile backlog artefacts, including Epics, User Stories, Acceptance Criteria, and Tasks/Sub-tasks, together with preliminary effort estimations. The system integrates large language models with rule-based estimation logic and provides seamless integration with enterprise project management platforms through REST APIs, enabling automatic synchronization with tools such as Jira and Confluence. The end-to-end workflow includes document ingestion, requirement extraction, contextual analysis, backlog generation, estimation computation, and structured export to project management systems. Experimental evaluation on real-world software requirement documents demonstrates that the proposed system significantly improves backlog preparation efficiency. The results show that the system can reduce backlog preparation time by approximately 75%, simplify the backlog creation workflow, and generate backlog items with a high level of accuracy and consistency compared to traditional manual approaches. These findings highlight the practical potential of AI-assisted systems in automating requirements engineering activities and improving productivity in Agile software development processes. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Reliability analysis of cloud-based machine learning services under poisoning attacks
abstract: Cloud-based Machine Learning as a Service (CMLaaS) platforms provide businesses with on-demand machine learning capabilities, accelerating the commercial adoption of ML technologies. However, these platforms are vulnerable to poisoning attacks that compromise service integrity. In this paper, we introduce a service-attack framework based on a retrial queueing model to evaluate CMLaaS performance in the presence of such attacks. In our model, external adversaries launch targeted poisoning attempts that remain undetected unless specifically checked; if an attack is not neutralized (i.e., repaired) before service completion, the resulting output is deemed invalid. To address the need for rapid and precise reliability assessment in engineering practice, this paper introduces an algorithm based on Monte Carlo simulation to estimate instantaneous reliability. Then, the strategic behavior of customers in self-interested and altruistic cases is analyzed, revealing the important role of curbing selfish behavior in improving system reliability. In addition, the optimization problem of the cost-effectiveness ratio (CER) under different cost structures is studied to provide a more comprehensive analysis of operational strategies for CMLaaS platforms with different purposes. Finally, the benchmark model is extended to the cases of imperfect detection, imperfect repair and finite capacity. The model is validated through numerical experiments, demonstrating the necessity of enhancing repair capability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: What do feature branches tell us about feature implementation in open-source projects?
abstract: Although “feature” is a common term across requirements engineering, product-line engineering, and agile methods, its operationalization in practice–especially through feature branches–has received little empirical attention. Feature branches are widely recommended on platforms like GitHub; yet, empirical evidence on how they are actually used is scarce. This study investigates feature-branch development practices in open-source software (OSS) projects. We conducted a large-scale empirical analysis of 27,103 feature branches from 3,388 popular GitHub repositories. Using branch-naming conventions, we identified feature branches and measured their lifespan, commit history, and commit-share distributions among contributors. In addition, we profiled contributors according to their opened issues, opened pull requests, number of followers, and total stars. Our analysis revealed that feature branches in open-source projects are long-lived, with a median lifespan exceeding two years, diverging from the short, agile iterations typically employed in software development. Commit intensity is low and irregular, averaging fewer than two commits per day. Contribution is highly unequal within feature branches: a small share of contributors accounts for most commits, revealing strong dependence on a small subset of developers. These findings have several practical implications. Our findings suggest that monitoring contribution concentration within feature branches– for instance, by computing the share of commits attributable to the top contributor or a Gini coefficient over the branch’s commit history–can help maintainers identify branches where development knowledge is held by very few individuals. Likewise, rolling commit intensity–computable directly from commit timestamps–may serve as an early signal of branch stagnation in OSS projects. Moreover, these findings establish an empirical baseline for future studies, including analyses of proprietary repositories. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Intelligent Collaborative Edge Caching via Contextual Bandits and Convex Relaxation
abstract: Edge Data Caching (EDC) enables low-latency delivery and alleviates backhaul congestion by caching data in close proximity to end users. However, current learning-driven methods struggle to capture the multi-dimensional business value of data. Consequently, inefficient resource allocation degrades critical services and compromises the Quality of Service (QoS). Moreover, physical node failures are insufficiently addressed, risking severe backhaul delays. To address these issues, we formulate the Value and Failure-aware Collaborative Edge Data Caching (VF-CEDC) problem as a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model jointly optimizing business value and expected latency under physical uncertainties. To solve this, we propose an Online Learning and Convex Relaxation Algorithm (OLCRA). First, OLCRA leverages a Contextual Multi-Armed Bandit (CMAB) to adaptively infer data values. Second, it resolves the discrete caching topology via convex relaxation and probabilistic rounding, yielding near-optimal polynomial-time decisions. Extensive experiments on a real-world dataset show that OLCRA reduces average system cost by 32.3% and expected latency by 38.3% against eight competing methods. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Least-cost optimal scenarios to a net-zero energy system: integration of battery energy storage, hydrogen storage, and carbon capture and storage
abstract: The rapid economic development and industrialisation in worldwide, result in rising electricity consumption, which primary supplied based on fossil fuels. Emissions reduction technologies and economic drivers are important in the transition towards carbon neutral system. Ireland has set a net-zero emissions target to achieve climate goals established under Paris Agreement. This study compares four energy policy transition pathways to achieve net-zero emissions by 2040, integrating multiple fuel technologies into a long-term optimisation framework, and assessing their economic viability, policy alignment, and technological feasibility. A linear power system optimisation model was developed in Python to investigate four scenarios. Scenario 1 integrates lithium-ion battery storage; Scenario 2 incorporates fossil-fuelled combined-cycle gas turbines with carbon capture; Scenario 3 introduces power-to-hydrogen technology for long-duration storage; and Scenario 4 introduces floating photovoltaic generation. The results indicate that an electricity system dominated by offshore wind can meet hourly demand requirements and ensure supply continuity. Scenario 4 reduces the offshore wind capacity requirement by up to 26.29 GW, while Scenario 3 lowers the required battery capacity by up to 479.27 GWh. Scenario 2 achieves the lowest levelised cost of electricity, ranging from 82.99 €/MWh to 118 €/MWh. The study highlights the critical role of integrated power to hydrogen to power, natural gas flexible generation with carbon capture and storage, battery storage, and floating photovoltaic in achieving net-zero energy system and offers a policy-informed assessment of multiple scenarios. The study compare economics, technics and emissions metrics to achieve net-zero while ensuring resilience and energy security under realistic constraints of the power system. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Tailoring the multiphase colloidal network of batters through controlled pre-gelatinization and oil droplets filling: Enhancement effects on quality of deep-fried battered clams
abstract: Deep-fried battered foods are widely consumed but face significant quality challenges, primarily excessive oil uptake and the rapid loss of textural crispness during post-frying storage. In this study, effects of targeted pre-gelatinization and oil droplets filling on the rheological properties and colloidal network of batters were investigated, along with their subsequent impact on the color, texture, fat content, volatile flavor components of deep-fried battered clams. Results showed that the starch-flour-hydrocolloid (flaxseed, guar, or xanthan gum) based batters with lipid-anchored micro-domains exhibited higher apparent viscosity and viscoelastic moduli after pre-gelatinization, further enhancing the multiphase stability. The pick-up ratios of the batter in the untreated (CK) and oil-added (CKO) controls were 17.4% and 19.3%, respectively, whereas the corresponding value in the pre-gelatinized group with oil droplets filling and flaxseed gum (G-FGO) reached 72.1%. The improvement in the batters was related with the formation of dense and ordered networks filled with oil droplets, which might function as robust multifunctional barriers regulating the rapid evaporation of moisture during frying. The marked reduction in oil uptake and increasement of fracture force were observed in the sample treated with gelatinization, lipid incorporation and flaxseed gum (G-FGO group), guar gum (G-GGO group), or xanthan gum (G-XGO group), when compared to the CKO group. Furthermore, the specific flavor compounds including hexanal, nonanal, (E,E)-2,4-decadienal, E−2-undecenal, etc., in battered clams increased significantly after treatment. These findings provided us that regulating the multiphase colloidal network of batters via gelatinization and oil droplets filling offers a potential industrial application for the production of high-quality fried seafood. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Blockchain-powered traceability systems in high value agri-food supply chains: a systematic literature review featuring insights from the olive oil sector
abstract: The olive oil supply chain, faces persistent challenges related to fraud, counterfeiting and lack of transparency, undermining consumer trust and product authenticity. Blockchain technology has emerged as a promising solution to enhance traceability, transparency, and quality assurance. This study examines the adoption of blockchain technology in the olive oil supply chain, organizing the existing literature into four thematic clusters (traceability and consumer trust; quality management; transparency; technological integration). The findings highlight blockchain's potential to improve supply chain integrity, especially when combined with internet of things sensors and smart contracts, while identifying technological, financial and organizational barriers to widespread adoption. © 2026 The Authors

title: Method-level technical debt detection based on source code and comments
abstract: Technical debt (TD) refers to suboptimal code resulting from compromises made by developers to meet business budgets or time constraints. Existing studies mainly focus either on code or comments, which restricts their applicability. Additionally, current research often overlooks the granularity of TD, which can lead to inaccurate identification and inefficient remediation of technical debt. To address these challenges, this paper introduces TDD-TCNN, a novel deep-learning approach for method-level TD detection through source code and comments from multiple perspectives. We first collect method-level source code and comments from nine open-source projects to construct a large method-level technical debt dataset, containing 103,006 validated Java methods, all of which have undergone thorough manual verification. Afterward, we use the dataset to train a deep learning model combining Convolutional Neural Network and Transformer for method-level TD detection, integrating local syntactic features with global contextual dependencies from code snippets to enhance accuracy and robustness. Experimental results demonstrate our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, with precision of 83.26%, recall of 80.84%, and F1-score of 81.92%. This work provides developers with actionable code quality improvement suggestions through precise TD localization at the method level. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: AI failures in the eyes of the downstream developer: a first look at concerns, practices, and challenges
abstract: With the advancement of AI models, more software systems are adopting AI as a component to facilitate automation. Pre-trained models (PTMs) have become a cornerstone of AI-based software, allowing for rapid integration and development with lower training cost. However, their adoption also introduces failure modes such as data leakage and biased outputs, that may require careful handling by downstream developers. While previous research has proposed taxonomies of these technical concerns and various mitigation strategies, how downstream developers address these issues during the development of general AI-based software when reusing PTMs remains unexplored. Understanding downstream developers’ perspectives is essential because they directly influence how these potential failure concerns translate into practice, such as determining whether immediate risks like data leakage or model bias are recognised, mitigated, or inadvertently overlooked in real-world deployments. This study investigates downstream developers’ concerns, practices and perceived challenges regarding practical AI failures during the development of AI-based software. To achieve this, we conducted a mixed-method study, including interviews with 16 participants, a survey of 86 practitioners, and an analysis of 874 AI incidents from the AI Incident Database. Our results reveal that while developers generally demonstrate strong awareness of potential AI failures, their practices, especially during the preparation and model selection phases, are often inadequate. The lack of concrete guidelines and policies leads to significant variability in the comprehensiveness of their approaches throughout the development lifecycle, with additional challenges such as poor documentation and knowledge gaps, further impeding effective implementation. Based on our findings, we offer suggestions for AI model contributors, developers of AI-based software, researchers, and policy makers to enhance the integration of failure mitigation measures aimed at mitigating direct harms from AI failures. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: A structure and splitting approximation based preconditioning method for solving space-time fractional advection-diffusion equations
abstract: This paper focuses on the fast numerical solution of initial-boundary value problems for space-time fractional advection-diffusion equations. The forward difference formula and Grünwald formula are used to discretize the equations, resulting in a structured linear system. To accelerate the convergence of the GMRES method for solving this system, an approximate inverse preconditioner is constructed and applied. The proposed preconditioning method is first based on the splitting approximation of the coefficient matrix. Then the inverse is approximated row by row and the involved Toeplitz matrix is approximated by the τ matrix. The spectral distribution of the preconditioned matrix is theoretically analyzed, demonstrating that its eigenvalues cluster around 1. Numerical results compared with other preconditioning methods show that the proposed preconditioner exhibits higher computational efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Asymptotic behavior of systemic risk measures in a bidimensional compound risk model
abstract: Consider a bidimensional compound risk model with stochastic premiums and returns, in which the claims within the same business line possess a specific weak dependence structure, while the accident-arrival processes across different lines are arbitrarily dependent. To assess the risk contagion between an insurer and each of its business lines, this paper investigates the asymptotic behavior of two specific systemic risk measures: conditional mean excess and systemic expected shortfall. Specifically, the former captures the insurer's instantaneous mean excess loss when a business line experiences a crisis, while the latter quantifies the corresponding business line's instantaneous expected loss contribution to the insurer's systemic distress. Within a regular variation framework, our asymptotic formulas illustrate how the heavy-tailedness of the claims influences these risk measures, whereas weak dependence exerts no contributory effect. Numerical studies are also conducted to verify the accuracy of the resulting estimates for these two measures, and to investigate the sensitivity of systemic expected shortfall with respect to several key parameters. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Based on window function optimization and DFT verification to establish terahertz fingerprint of triphenyl phosphate for non-destructive analysis
abstract: Triphenyl phosphate (TPHP), an emerging pollutant with neurotoxic and reproductive toxicity, severely threatens global food safety and human health through environmental exposure risks and bioaccumulation. A rapid and non-destructive detection method for TPHP was established using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS). This study systematically analyzed the impact of window functions on TPHP fingerprint spectra and integrated DFT calculations, chemometric analysis, and baseline correction algorithms for TPHP quantitation and qualitation in real samples. Boxcar window optimally retained absorption peaks of TPHP at 0.94, 1.21, 1.45, and 1.70 THz. B3LYP-D3/6-31G(d,2p) basis set effectively corrected the frequency shift caused by weak intermolecular interactions, resulting in a high degree of agreement between the theoretical and experimental spectra in 0.1–2.0 THz range. AirPLS algorithm effectively eliminated matrix interference in real samples, enabling accurate analysis of TPHP with a LOD of 0.09%, which advanced the practical application of THz-TDS in food safety and environmental monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: When public meets private: How dual digital channels reshape subscription E-commerce
abstract: Leveraging online private-domain channels, retail-controlled platforms accessible only to designated customer segments, for subscription commerce has become a cornerstone for many retailers seeking stable revenue streams and deeper customer engagement. In pursuit of an omnichannel presence, however, an increasing number of retailers have begun to roll out subscription offerings through online public-domain channels: third-party platforms open to all users. The impact of this strategic expansion on their existing private-domain subscription business remains ambiguous. Drawing on Decision Field Theory and granular subscription-order data from a leading subscription retailer, we employ a multi-period difference-in-differences design to assess how the introduction of public-domain channels affects subscription volume and subscription cycle length in private-domain channels. Our findings reveal that public-domain entry negatively affects both subscription volume and subscription cycle in the private-domain channel. However, these adverse effects are attenuated for products whose consumer bases exhibit higher pre-treatment subscription frequency or longer prior subscription cycles. This research offers both theoretical insights and actionable guidance for retailers seeking to calibrate their multi-channel subscription strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Non-destructive biochemical profiling of goldenberry ripening using confocal micro Raman spectroscopy coupled with machine learning
abstract: The accurate monitoring of the fruit ripening is crucial for maintaining quality and prevention from post-harvest economic losses. Goldenberry, being rich in vitamins, minerals, and carotenoids, yet its ripening assessment relies on variable and often subjective traditional approaches. To address this, the present study utilises rapid and non-destructive techniques using confocal micro-Raman and UV-Vis spectroscopy to track biochemical changes in both the exocarp and mesocarp of goldenberry fruit across five ripening stages: pre-mature, mature, pre-ripe, ripe, and post-ripe. The analysis of Raman spectra of exocarp shows an increase in carotenoid bands up to ripe stage, followed by a decrease at post-ripe stage, while the mesocarp exhibits a continuous increase in carotenoid intensity through stage post-ripe. The UV-Vis spectral analysis supports these observations, indicating increasing carotenoid content alongside a reduction in chlorophyll as ripening progresses. Among different machine learning (ML) approaches, unsupervised clustering demonstrates strong performance of k-means and agglomerative nesting, with high rand index values (>0.97). In supervised domain, support vector machine, logistic regression, random forest, decision tree, and principal component-linear discriminant analysis achieves the highest values of performance metrices including accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, ROC/AUC values, and cross validation scores. Moreover, partial least squares regression analysis demonstrates excellent predictive power, with R2 = 0.93 (calibration) and 0.70 (cross-validation) for exocarp and R2 = 0.91 (calibration) and 0.89 (cross-validation) for mesocarp. The combined use of Raman with ML enables a practical and reliable framework for assessing fruit ripening, with promising applications in quality control and post-harvest management. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Impact of intellectual capital on the competitiveness and business performance of microenterprises
abstract: This study examines the influence of intellectual capital, understood in its human, structural and relational dimensions, on the competitive advantages and business results of microenterprises located in the canton of La Maná, province of Cotopaxi, Ecuador. With a quantitative approach, a structured survey was applied to owners of microenterprises; the data were analyzed through exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling with partial least squares. The sample comprised 867 valid responses from microenterprise owners in the canton of La Maná, covering different economic activities in the local microenterprise structure. The structural model included five blocks, defined as human capital, structural, relational, competitive advantages and business results. The reliability indices (Cronbach's alpha and Dillon-Goldstein's rho) and convergent validity (AVE) were satisfactory in most of the blocks, especially structural capital and relational capital. The overall goodness of fit of the model (GoF = 0.4396) was adequate. Among the key findings, structural capital significantly influences competitive advantages, which, in turn, influence business results. Human capital has a moderate direct effect on competitiveness and a smaller indirect effect on business results. Furthermore, the study identifies specific managerial practices for enhancing intangible assets and outlines avenues for future research on sector-specific variations in the dynamics of intellectual capital accumulation. Relational capital showed a weak influence on competitive advantages and business results, suggesting that external networks in this local microenterprise context may be informal, weakly institutionalized or insufficiently consolidated. The results highlight the relevance of structural capital and competitiveness as key elements for improving business performance in microenterprises and offer practical implications for their strategic strengthening. These insights contribute broadly to the discourse on intangible asset management and sustainable competitiveness in developing regions. The study tested five hypotheses linking human, structural and relational capital with competitiveness and business performance using PLS-SEM. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Exploring the Impact of Facebook eWOM and Conformity Behavior on Consumer Purchase Behavior: Using Subjective Norms as the Mediator
abstract: With the rise of the internet, many businesses have gradually started operating on social media, making it one of the platforms for trading goods. This trend shows that social media is becoming a new choice for mass consumption channels. Therefore, exploring the factors that promote purchasing intentions on social networks has become a current research trend. This study investigates the impact of conformity behavior, electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM), and subjective norms on behavioral intentions in Facebook community shopping. title: Knowledge-Driven E-Business in Cultural Heritage: A Framework for Design and Evaluation
abstract: Cultural heritage institutions implement E-business information systems to integrate enjoyment, economic sustainability, and public purpose. This study presents a comprehensive framework that systematically connects cultural data (shared models and vocabularies, digitally described content) with operational processes (bookings, online sales, membership, and public relations) through integration utilising documented interfaces and event exchange. This approach produces a distinctive information model that connects objects, individuals, locations, and events, while also quantifying the impact of architectural decisions on measurable outcomes: data quality and alignment, service response times, booking completion rates, membership renewal rates, and decreased absenteeism. The methodological component establishes reproducible protocols for collecting and analysing evidence, considering seasonality and contextual factors, while incorporating data protection and accessibility standards throughout the design process. We examine the anticipated outcomes and ramifications for sustainability, experiential quality, and system governance. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Exploring the Role of Digital Management Capability in Shaping Ethical Leadership and its Impact on ESG: A Dynamic Capabilities Micro-Foundations Perspective
abstract: Drawing on the micro-foundations of dynamic capabilities, this study examines the interplay among digital management capability, ethical leadership, and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance within E-Business Information Systems. Analyzing survey data from 357 Chinese small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), the results demonstrate that digital management capability positively influences both ESG performance and ethical leadership. Furthermore, ethical leadership positively affects ESG performance and significantly mediates the relationship between digital management capability and ESG outcomes. Notably, digital management capability positively moderates the ethical leadership—ESG performance link, suggesting that digitally competent ethical leaders are better positioned to drive sustainability. This research extends the micro-foundations perspective by emphasizing the human-specific aspects of digital information systems management. Practically, the findings underscore the need for SMEs to integrate ethical and digital leadership to enhance sustainability in the digital era. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Autoencoder-Based Intrusion Detection: A Hybrid Deep Learning Approach
abstract: Cyberattacks are an increasing threat to individuals and businesses, with ransomware and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks among the most prevalent. This paper proposes a novel intrusion detection system (IDS) utilizing a sequence-based convolutional autoencoder (CAE) to model normal network behavior and detect anomalies. It further explores a hybrid classification approach combining unsupervised and supervised learning to enhance detection accuracy, particularly for previously unseen attacks. © ICST Institute for Computer Sciences, Social Informatics and Telecommunications Engineering 2027.

title: The Impact of Luxury Value on Luxury Purchase Intention: A Case Study of Luxury Cars in an Emerging Country
abstract: This study investigates the impact of luxury value on luxury purchase intention through positive emotions, utilizing the C-A-C framework. A survey was conducted with 348 responses in the context of luxury cars. This study highlights the key role of luxury value in shaping consumer behavior in Vietnam’s luxury car market. It shows that dimensions like functional, financial, social, and personal benefits positively affect consumers’ emotional responses, which in turn increase purchase intention. The findings also confirm that luxury value directly influences buying decisions and that positive emotions mediate this relationship. Overall, emotional engagement is crucial in the luxury automotive consumer journey. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Calibrated penalty based variable selection for partially linear single-index varying coefficient spatial autoregressive models
abstract: In this paper, we consider the variable selection for a class of partially linear single-index varying coefficient spatial autoregressive models. By combining bias correction and penalized estimation method, we propose a calibrated penalty based variable selection method. Under the appropriate conditions, we demonstrate that the proposed variable selection method can consistently select the true important covariates, and can also identify the significance of spatial effects. The asymptotic normality of the estimators for nonzero parameters is also derived under some regularity conditions. Several simulation analyses are conducted for further illustrating the performance of the proposed variable selection method, and the simulation results demonstrate that the proposed bias correction mechanism is effective and proposed variable selection method is workable under finite sample sizes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Workplace Satisfaction and Organizational Culture in Thailand: An Explainable Machine Learning Approach Using SHAP
abstract: The study examines workplace satisfaction and organizational culture in Thailand by using SHAP-based feature selection within an explainable machine learning framework. The analysis uses survey data from 1,059 respondents from the Global Labor Market Status Survey. In response to concerns about model transparency and causal interpretation, this revised study explicitly treats SHAP as a variable-selection and prediction-interpretation method rather than as a causal estimator. Four predictive models were compared: linear regression, ridge regression, random forest, and XGBoost. XGBoost produced the strongest holdout performance among the compared models, with a test R2 of 0.381 and RMSE of 0.931. SHAP values were then used to identify the organizational culture items that most strongly contributed to the model prediction. The most important variables were respect for individual values, mutual understanding, and flexible thinking. Additional checks using permutation importance, SHAP-selected reduced models, and repeated random-seed stability analysis support the robustness of these variables as predictors. The strongest XGBoost model using the top 15 SHAP-selected variables achieved a test R2 of 0.436 and RMSE of 0.889, indicating that SHAP-based feature selection improved predictive parsimony. The findings suggest that workplace satisfaction in Thailand is increasingly associated with respect for individual values, mutual understanding, and organizational flexibility, while the results are interpreted as predictive associations rather than causal effects. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The Couscous Game: An Academic Case Study on Advancing Gamification in Operations and Supply Chain Management Education
abstract: Gamification has been used since the early days of computers as an experiential learning approach in Operations and Supply Chain Management education. This paper presents the Couscous Game, an open-source web-based simulation improving on the well-known Beer Game with automated calculations, customizable demand patterns, and real-time visualizations. Players progress through competitive and collaborative phases, ultimately managing entire supply chains. Testing with 60 participants (50 undergraduates, 6 MBA students, and 4 faculty) shows strong learning outcomes: 76.67% agreed the game effectively taught supply chain concepts, 88.33% preferred it over traditional lectures, and 91.67% would recommend it for other courses. The game particularly excels at demonstrating the bullwhip effect and the value of supply chain coordination through direct experiential learning aligned with Kolb’s Experiential Learning Theory. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Warehouse Features and Activities as the Cornerstone in Both the Service and Manufacturing Supply Chain Sectors in the Jordan Market
abstract: The increasing importance of a well-structured supply chain has drastically increased during the last decade. This has resulted in both the service and manufacturing sectors paying more attention to their competitiveness level to stay in the market. Moreover, in order to act effectively, the warehouse and warehousing sub-processes and activities in a real-life example are suggested to be analyzed and focused on. This study, therefore, conducts a site visit and an extensive literature review and searches for commonalities and differences to draw final recommendations to improve the service level in a pre-selected sample. The findings show that the manufacturing warehouse throughput is considered high in terms of volume and low in terms of the number of SKUs, while the service sector warehouse is a total contrast; since the service sector generally handles a huge number of SKUs that vary in terms of size, shape, weight, and other specs, the warehouse manager should adopt as many storage systems as possible to cover this wide range of stock-keeping units in the most efficient and optimal way possible. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Structural and Algorithmic Limitations in LLM-Driven BPMN Generation: A Rapid Review of Empirical Evidence
abstract: Business Process Management (BPM) demands formalized models, yet manual BPMN construction remains labor-intensive and error-prone. Large Language Models (LLMs) present opportunities for automated text-to-model translation, though their effectiveness remains underexplored. This rapid review synthesizes 11 empirical investigations published from 2023 to 2025, revealing a nascent field dominated by GPT-4 (55% adoption) and prompt-based methodologies (64% prevalence). Our analysis uncovers critical structural deficiencies: LLMs demonstrate fundamental incapacity for graph-theoretic reasoning and set-theoretic spatial optimization required for valid BPMN layouts. Specifically, 55% of surveyed approaches fail with non-trivial process complexity, while 64% lack reproducible artifacts. Execution of all 4 available implementations (S4, S6, S7, S8) confirmed severe degradation when confronted with hierarchical structures, parallel gateways, or spatial coordinate systems (Diagram Interchange). We conclude that current approaches conflate linguistic pattern matching with algorithmic reasoning—a categorical error that mandates hybrid architectures combining LLM semantic extraction with specialized graph layout algorithms. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Ontology-Grounded Fact-Checking for E-Commerce: A Neuro-Symbolic, Claim-Centric Approach
abstract: Misinformation in e-business—discounts based on volatile prices, fictitious stock levels, erroneous certifications, and implausible delivery commitments—erodes trust, competition, and regulatory adherence. This study introduces EBFN-Detect, a neuro-symbolic framework for claim-centric verification that incorporates a domain ontology (EBFN-O), a commercial knowledge graph, and natural language processing models. The pipeline extracts claims from diverse sources, conducts entity linking for products, brands, and sellers, retrieves ontology-guided evidence (RAG on KG), and assesses truthfulness by integrating a claim-evidence aware classifier with symbolic verifications of temporal consistency, price plausibility, and regulatory compliance. The output generates calibrated probabilities and verifiable explanations derived from supported or refuted chains with provenance. The work delineates the method, introduces EBFN-O in accordance with schema.org/GoodRelations/PROV-O, presents a multi-source corpus annotated at three tiers (claim, linking, truth) with reproducible guidelines, describes a RAG + KG pipeline featuring transparent fusion and calibration, and proposes an evaluation protocol that integrates metrics of accuracy, retrieval quality, and explanatory utility. Consequently, EBFN-Detect demonstrates enhancements in macro F1 and Brier/ECE relative to pure neural baselines, exhibiting significant benefits in time-sensitive scenarios and in categories characterized by substantial variant ambiguity, thereby delineating a feasible approach to dependable, traceable, and contestable verification in digital commerce. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Building a Service Ecosystem Through the Metaverse
abstract: This paper develops a conceptual and empirically illustrated framework for constructing a service ecosystem through the metaverse by integrating servitization and decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs). We synthesize top-journal research on service ecosystems, digital servitization, metaverse platform ecosystems, and DAO governance to identify a central challenge: the metaverse expands the design space for service experiences and resource integration, yet its ecosystem-level coordination demands governance mechanisms that can scale across heterogeneous actors, assets, and jurisdictions. We propose a layered model in which servitization modularizes and operationalizes metaverse services, while DAOs instantiate programmable, auditable ecosystem governance (incentives, rules, and collective decision rights). A Japanese manufacturing case illustrates feasibility via digital twin, enabled service delivery and platform partnerships, and clarifies implementation requirements for DAO-based ecosystem coordination. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Structural Equation Modeling in Digitised and Sustainable Supply Chains Research: A Bibliographic Review (ID: 383)
abstract: Digital technologies and sustainability are the main trends that impact supply chains. This study seeks to expand the knowledge of Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) in digital and sustainable supply chains within social sciences, business and management fields. It presents a bibliometric analysis of the SEM statistical method applied to digitised and sustainable supply chain management. It also analyses the different types of SEM used: classic SEM, PLS-SEM, Bayesian SEM, and Multilevel SEM. The paper focuses on constructs and latent variables, dependent and independent variables, and the main theories utilised by other authors. Web of Science Core Collection is the source database, addressing these research areas. The results show that SEM, PLS-SEM and sustainability-related topics are analyzed mainly. The limitation is that the research focuses solely on one statistical method (SEM) to analyse digitised and sustainable supply chains, which could be solved in further studies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Innovation Platform Activity and Scope: Case Evidence and Future Research Directions
abstract: Innovation platforms are increasingly prevalent, yet we know little about the activities such platforms can and should support and how their scope can expand over time for effective platform positioning and revenue generation. This study examines three established innovation platforms—InnoCentive, GitHub, and Kaggle—to identify the different activities they enable for participants and how these differ across the three cases. Drawing on the literature on transactions, online communities, and innovation, a set of platform activities is identified. In this study, we assess how strongly each platform supports different activities and visualize the results using spider graphs. While innovation activities are strongly supported across the three cases, the level of support differs across specific innovation activities from one platform to another. In addition to support for innovation activities, some also broaden their scope to support engagement and/or transaction. These findings show that our approach is effective in identifying platform activity and scope for innovation platforms. In future work we will expand these cases to examine what drives platform activity support choices, how the activities and their scope evolve over time, and how platforms monetize these innovation, transaction, and engagement activities. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Human-Centered E-Business Systems Based on Situation Awareness: A Contextual Framework Driven by Artificial Intelligence
abstract: In recent years, e-business ecosystems have evolved into complex and data-driven information systems, where adaptability to the context has become a critical success factor. Traditional decision-making models, however, often prove inadequate to manage the dynamism and uncertainty of today’s digital environments, creating a gap between the richness of available data and the ability of systems to exploit it proactively. This article proposes an innovative framework integrating Artificial Intelligence and Situation Awareness to develop human-centered and adaptive E-Business Information Systems (EBIS). Our approach combines the Situation Awareness (SA) paradigm, which is the ability to perceive, understand, and project future states of the context, with a multilevel software architecture. By leveraging the integration of data from the Internet of Things (IoT), the formalization of knowledge through semantic ontologies, and the predictive power of Bayesian probabilistic models, the framework enables systems to react and anticipate user needs. The validation of the framework, conducted through a use case in the domain of smart cultural tourism at the Archaeological Park of Pompeii, demonstrated the effectiveness of our approach by defining a solid methodological basis for the creation of next-generation e-business systems, capable of learning and reacting dynamically, improving the resilience of processes and placing the user at the center of an intelligent and personalized digital experience. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Major Trends in the Development of Airports from Central and Eastern Europe between 2010 and 2024
abstract: After the liberalisation of air transport in Europe in the nineties, the policy for the aviation market has changed, the European Union becoming a single aviation market. The airline-airport relationship has developed and the European airports compete now to attract the services of airlines, especially for having aircraft bases which can bring essential business development. These new features of the air transport market have had a great influence on governmental policies regarding the development of airports in Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) over the last 15 years. In order to provide airports with strategic information for building development strategies, this paper presents a comparative analysis of the main parameters of airport development. We use an external and internal benchmarking approach focused on macroeconomic parameters and airport operational parameters: airport connectivity, passenger traffic, as well as the strategy of airports in relation to economic development The overall conclusion on the air transport in the 12 countries of CEE is that its development and volume are conditioned by a complex combination of economic, demographic, infrastructural, and connectivity factors. Countries with strong economies and large populations, such as Poland, Greece, and Romania, have the highest air traffic, supported by a large number of airports and excellent connectivity, especially in urban and tourist areas. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Data-Driven Innovation in Cybersecurity for E-Business Information Systems: A Case Study on CVE Report Generation via LLM
abstract: The backbone of modern digital economies, e-business information systems (EBIS), is security, which is an essential factor in ensuring business continuity and digital trust. One of the most complex challenges in this area is efficiently managing vulnerabilities, which requires fast and accurate reporting processes. This study explores the application of artificial intelligence as a data-driven innovation to automate the generation of structured cybersecurity reports. To this end, we analyzed the performance of four open-source large language models (LLMs) by implementing an adaptive two-step prompt chaining architecture. The system, tested on a dataset of 30 Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs), simulates a realistic analysis and review workflow. The assessment, based on quantitative and qualitative metrics, produced results that, although preliminary, confirm the feasibility of integrating LLMs into EBIS cybersecurity processes. The study also highlights crucial challenges related to scalability and reliability, which are key determinants of the governance of these systems. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Optimization of Energy Consumption in Battery-Operated Real-Time Systems
abstract: Real-time applications emphasize worst-case scenarios due to their precise timing demands. However, many critical applications of embedded systems have other requirements, such as energy consumption. The results of this study can inform the e-commerce infrastructure, including payment gateways, online transactions, and data-driven logistics. This would be especially beneficial in terms of energy savings and improving operational costs for embedded systems in e-business. This study presents a model for work scheduling that minimizes energy usage by implementing a suitable scheduling algorithm for dynamic power management (DPM) and dynamic voltage scaling (DVS) and evaluating the effectiveness of power management approaches. Applying DVS leads to an 84.03% reduction in energy consumption, while using DPM reduces the total energy consumed by devices by 66.76%. Combining DPM and DVS yields similar energy savings to DVS alone (83.22%) but with the potential for more significant energy savings due to external device involvement. While this combination can lead to longer execution times, a significant reduction in energy consumption makes it a worthwhile trade-off for energy-efficient computing. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Makeup and Skincare Endorsement by Virtual Influencers: Product-Influencer Congruence and Persuasion Outcomes
abstract: Social media influencers effectively promote beauty products, and virtual influencers offer novel opportunities for promotion in this domain. However, their artificial nature raises questions about their ability to endorse products that rely on sensory experience. Drawing on the sensory marketing literature, we examine whether product type (makeup vs. skincare) affects the perceived congruence, product attractiveness, influencer credibility, and purchase intentions associated with a virtual influencer endorsement. An experiment with 126 French Instagram users reveals that product type does not significantly affect these perceptions. However, a multi-group analysis shows that the persuasion mechanism differs: for makeup, product attractiveness drives purchase intentions, whereas for skincare, influencer credibility is the dominant driver. These findings suggest that while virtual influencers may promote both product types, the underlying persuasion process is product-dependent, with implications for how brands should design virtual influencer campaigns in the beauty sector. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Industry 5.0: Between Theory and Practice
abstract: Digital transformation has become a new research trend in the last few years, unveiling complicated and creative technologies to change various features of an organization, such as its business models, value chain, products, and services. In the literature, this concept has been linked to Industry4.0 (I4.0) and Industry 5.0 (I5.0) contexts in particular. Although the two paradigms bear some similarities from a technological perspective, the emerging I5.0 paradigm is transitioning from merely representing a technological advancement to establishing a more human-centric, resilient and sustainable manufacturing system. Consequently, it has become a strategic objective for companies to remain competitive and manage uncertainties, particularly in today's era, where demand volatility, changing consumer behavior, geopolitical turmoil and environmental concerns are the norms. This study systematically maps the literature with three primary objectives: (1) to identify application fields and usage environments, (2) to compare theoretical and empirical models employed, and (3) to establish critical success factors (CSFs) for implementation. Several reviews have outlined I5.0 as a rapidly evolving topic. Ongoing efforts are focused on tracking trends, delineating and guiding future research in the fields of manufacturing and engineering. This study contributes by categorizing seven CFSs under dominant frameworks, thus providing a wide picture of implementation and presenting pragmatic insights for researchers and stakeholders. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Toward a Zero Trust Architecture for 6G-Enabled E-Business Ecosystem
abstract: E-Business Information Systems (EBIS)—encompassing digital payment platforms, e-commerce order management, logistics orchestration, and B2B integration layers—face growing security challenges as they converge with 5G-Advanced and pre-6G ultra-connected environments. Heterogeneous actors and sensitive data flows render traditional perimeter-based models inadequate, requiring continuous verification and adaptive controls. Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), as defined in NIST SP 800-207, provides a promising paradigm but demands domain-specific adaptation for the unique constraints of mobile networks. This paper bridges the gap between standardization-driven research and practical E-Business security needs. We first present a critical review of prior 5G/6G security surveys, identifying the lack of holistic ZT integration and E-Business domain mapping as key research gaps. Subsequently, we evaluate the applicability of all thirteen candidate solutions outlined in 3GPP TR 33.794 (Release 19) against four criteria—transaction integrity relevance, cross-domain applicability, deployment feasibility, and latency impact—assessing their suitability for digital commerce. We derive operational guidelines for adapting these standardized mechanisms to EBIS environments, with particular attention to deployment path differentiation and regulatory compliance. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Toward Digital Invoicing: A Layered Approach
abstract: Automated invoice digitization presents substantial challenges due to extreme layout variability, degraded scan quality, and vendor-specific formatting conventions. Traditional approaches based on optical character recognition OCR or neural Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) models frequently fail to maintain structural consistency and logical validity under such heterogeneous conditions. In this paper, we introduce a unified three-layer architecture for invoice digitization that integrates visual, semantic, and structural information within a coherent reasoning framework. The architecture comprises three sequential stages: (i) a Pre-Processing Layer that standardizes and prepares scanned invoice documents for reliable downstream analysis; (ii) a Processing Layer that executes structured information extraction through integrated visual layout analysis, text understanding, and semantic reasoning including specialized modules for non-tabular field extraction and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for table detection and reconstruction; (iii) a Post-Processing and Validation Layer that enforces domain-specific constraints, validates extracted fields against business rules, and normalizes outputs into a standardized structured format. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that our implemented system achieves consistent performance across diverse invoice layouts, formats, and degrees of quality. Compared to commercial OCR solutions and state-of-the-art IDP models, our approach provides measurable improvements in critical field extraction accuracy and table reconstruction while maintaining competitive computational efficiency. These results indicate that a modular architecture integrating semantic reasoning with domain-aware validation scales at a practical level for invoice processing applications. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Integrating Benefits Management and Case Study Research: A Methodological Approach to Studying Analytics-Enabled Benefit Realization
abstract: This paper explores how Benefits Management (BM) can serve as a methodological approach in qualitative Information Systems research. A multi-case study of benefits realization from big data analytics capabilities demonstrates how BM provides a structured framework for analyzing how organizations generate, enable, and sustain benefits from data analytics initiatives. Specifically, BM supports the identification of enabling changes and contribution relationships, enhancing understanding of the mechanisms behind benefit realization. BM was integrated with case study research guiding data collection, shaping coding strategies, and facilitating cross-case comparisons. By incorporating a practitioner-focused, process-oriented framework into academic research, this approach bridges the gap between practice and theory, enabling researchers to capture the temporal and relational dynamics of socio-technical phenomena. Overall, this paper offers methodological guidance for IS scholars aiming to study complex scenarios where technology is introduced, providing lens that support the advancement of theorization of business benefits realization, thus, targeting an increasingly relevant topic as organizational processes become more digital and interconnected. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Enhancing Sentiment Analysis Performance Through GAN-Based Data Augmentation for Addressing Data Imbalance
abstract: In recent years, the development of the Internet has led businesses to increasingly focus on collecting online public reviews for text mining, with sentiment analysis emerging as a prominent application in this field. However, obtaining a balanced dataset remains a significant challenge. Data imbalance can introduce significant biases in the model’s training and prediction processes, decreasing the predictive performance of minority classes. To address this issue and mitigate the effects of data imbalance, this study employs generative adversarial network (GAN) models as a data augmentation technique to generate sufficient samples to correct the imbalance in the dataset. Furthermore, it compares the sentiment prediction results before and after the application of the data augmentation model. The experimental results indicate that the additional sample data generated through the data augmentation model significantly improves the accuracy of the sentiment analysis model, thereby optimizing and enhancing the machine learning model. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: When Security Meets Ethics: Balancing Control, Privacy, and Trust in Digital Systems
abstract: As digital systems become increasingly embedded in education, business, government, and everyday life, the boundary between technological security and ethical responsibility has grown more complex. This paper examines how the pursuit of digital security—through practices such as data collection, monitoring, automation, and AI-driven decision-making—often intersects with, and occasionally undermines, the ethical principles of privacy, autonomy, fairness, and transparency. Using ethical frameworks including deontology, consequentialism, and virtue ethics, the study analyzes key challenges such as algorithmic bias, digital surveillance, cybercrime, and digital burnout. It argues that achieving a sustainable balance between control and trust requires not only robust technical protections but also clear institutional policies and user-centered ethical guidelines. By synthesizing current literature and offering a structured set of best practices, the paper proposes an integrated approach to the governance of computing technologies—one that ensures security while safeguarding human dignity, agency, and well-being. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Enhancing Business Performance Through Balanced Scorecard and Lean Management
abstract: The increasing competitive pressure in global markets requires organizations to strengthen their planning and control mechanisms. In the industrial sector, this need is even more pronounced due to the constant demand for efficiency and waste reduction. In this context, the Balanced Scorecard (BSC) and the Lean methodology stand out as complementary tools to support strategy implementation and monitoring. This study analyzed the combined contribution of these approaches in an industrial company operating in the automotive, home appliances, and metallurgical sectors, employing a qualitative methodology based on interviews and direct observation. The research resulted in the proposal of an integrated framework that combines the four perspectives of the BSC with Lean principles, oriented toward value creation, waste elimination, and continuous improvement. The findings indicate that the coordinated application of the BSC and Lean reinforces strategic alignment, competitiveness, and operational efficiency, potentially serving as a reference for other organizations. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: A Tool for Learning About Outdated Software Vulnerabilities and End-of-Life
abstract: This study presents a tool for enhancing E-Business Information Systems (EBIS) resilience by identifying outdated operating systems and installed applications on offline computers. While most EBIS vulnerability-management tools rely on network connectivity, our approach extends protection to isolated or legacy business environments through the development of a two-fold solution: a scanner app that reads and stores software information from individual computers, and a summary app that combines this data with software versions, Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE), and End-of-Life (EOL) support details from vendors. The summary app integrates EBIS data flows with machine-learning models that synthesize CVE descriptions, generating executive summaries to support managerial risk decisions. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Artificial Intelligence as an Information and Knowledge Management Capability: A Comparative Systematic Literature Review of Managerial Impacts in Africa and Europe
abstract: Artificial intelligence has evolved into a strategic organizational capability that shapes information and knowledge management and managerial decision-making. This study conducts a comparative systematic literature review of AI-enabled Information and Knowledge Management across Africa and Europe from 2005 to 2025, following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. From an initial corpus of 100 records, 21 peer-reviewed studies were retained and analyzed using descriptive, thematic and bibliometric techniques. Quantitative evidence reveals the presence of pronounced regional asymmetries. European organizations demonstrate higher AI readiness (avg. 1.01), adoption (avg. 0.83), and knowledge maturity (avg. 0.85), supported by sustained R&D investment (2.2% of GDP) and harmonized regulatory frameworks. African contexts exhibit lower readiness (avg. 0.59), adoption (avg. 0.51), yet show accelerated post-2018 growth driven by mobile-first and frugal-AI innovations. Across regions, AI enhances decision accuracy and firm performance primarily when it is used to reconfigure organizational and managerial processes, whereas automation-led deployments yield mixed efficiency outcomes. This study advances theory by extending the Knowledge-Based View toward a Dynamic Managerial Capabilities perspective, positioning AI as a context-dependent knowledge transformer, and providing actionable insights for aligning AI deployment with inclusive and sustainable knowledge strategies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Strategic Planning in B2B Marketing for the MedTech Industry: A Literature-Based Analysis
abstract: The MedTech industry operates in a highly regulated, innovation-driven, and competitive environment, where effective strategic planning in B2B marketing is critical for organizational performance and long-term sustainability. This paper presents a literature-based analysis of strategic planning in B2B marketing within the MedTech context, synthesizing academic contributions that address market dynamics, performance orientation, competitive intelligence, and regulatory constraints. Rather than adopting a descriptive perspective, the paper integrates strategic and analytical viewpoints to examine how B2B marketing planning supports value creation, market positioning, and decision-making in MedTech organizations. The analysis highlights the distinctive characteristics of the MedTech B2B environment, including complex stakeholder structures, extended decision cycles, and compliance requirements, while identifying key challenges and emerging research directions. By consolidating fragmented literature streams, the paper contributes to a clearer understanding of strategic B2B marketing planning as a critical managerial capability in the MedTech industry. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Mapping the Intersection of AI, BI, and Sustainability: A Bibliometric Approach
abstract: This paper presents a bibliometric analysis of research at the intersection of artificial intelligence, business intelligence, and sustainability. Using data from Web of Science, the study examines publication trends, thematic patterns, and intellectual structures. The results show a rapid growth in research activity, with a stable core of themes centred on AI, machine learning, big data, and sustainability, alongside several emerging but weakly integrated topics. Citation and collaboration analyses reveal a globally distributed research community and a concentration of influential journals in sustainability and engineering domains, while business- and management-oriented outlets remain less represented. The study provides an integrated overview of this fragmented research landscape and highlights opportunities for future research that combines technological innovation with organisational and sustainability perspectives. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: An innovative modified biochar derived from antibiotic mycelial dreg: Enhanced tetracycline adsorption performance and underlying mechanism
abstract: Use of antibiotic mycelial dreg (AMD) for biochar production is an eco-friendly and cost-effective strategy to achieve the goals of hazardous waste management. However, the low adsorption capacity of pristine AMD-derived biochar limits its practical application. Thus, KMnO4-modified biochar was developed to enhance tetracycline (TC) removal from aqueous solution in this study. Various characterization experiments showed that the modification process introduced MnOx on the surface of pleuromutilin mycelial dreg (PMD) derived biochar and resulted in a higher BET surface area, well-developed pore structure, more oxygen-containing surface functional groups, and altered elemental components. Batch adsorption studies indicated that the pH of the solution had a significant impact on the adsorption of TC by pristine biochar, but had little impact on the modified biochar. TC adsorption by pristine and modified biochar was a combination of physical and chemical adsorption, but the chemical adsorption was dominant. The maximum adsorption capacity of MBC500 and MBC700 was 802.4 mg/g and 894.6 mg/g, which were 16 and 22 times larger than that of pristine biochar, respectively. TC adsorption by both pristine and modified biochar was spontaneous (ΔG < 0), endothermic (ΔH > 0), and a randomness-enhanced process (ΔS > 0). The adsorption mechanisms of pristine biochar included pore filling, π–π interaction, and charge-assisted hydrogen bond (CAHB). KMnO4 modification efficiently improved these interactions as well as increasing the complexation and redox interaction, resulting in an excellent adsorption capacity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Artificial Intelligence and Organizational Performance: A Literature Review on ESG-Oriented Management Practices
abstract: The growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping organizational practices across industries, particularly in how firms pursue performance improvements while addressing environmental, social, and governance (ESG) objectives. This paper presents a structured literature review examining the role of AI in enhancing organizational performance through ESG-oriented management practices. By synthesizing recent academic contributions, the study explores how AI-driven tools and data analytics support decision-making, operational efficiency, risk management, and sustainability-oriented strategies. The review highlights key mechanisms through which AI contributes to economic performance while simultaneously enabling greater transparency, accountability, and social and environmental responsibility. In addition, the paper discusses emerging challenges and limitations identified in the literature, including ethical concerns, data governance, algorithmic bias, and energy consumption. The findings contribute to a clearer understanding of the strategic implications of AI adoption in organizations and identify avenues for future research on the integration of AI and ESG principles within management practice. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Beyond RSRP: UE-Side Detection of Multi-stage Fake Base Station Attacks Through NAS/RRC Layer in 5G Networks for Secure Mobile E-Business Services
abstract: Fake base station attacks enable threats such as denial of service, user tracking, and security downgrades in modern mobile networks. Since many devices remain vulnerable, on-device detection has become an important defense mechanism. However, existing approaches relying on signal-strength metrics such as RSRP become unreliable when attackers manipulate radio conditions or perform protocol-level attacks. This study proposes an on-device detection framework that incorporates protocol-layer information by analyzing RRC and NAS signaling sequences alongside conventional signal features. Using a self-generated dataset capturing realistic FBS scenarios, we evaluate both classical machine-learning and deep-learning models across multiple feature configurations. Experimental results show that protocol-layer features significantly improve detection accuracy and reduce false positives compared to RSRP-only approaches. By improving resilience against fake base station attacks, the proposed framework contributes to maintaining reliable mobile connectivity supporting digital transactions and mobile-based e-business services. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Life cycle–informed process optimization of microwave-activated biochar from agri-residual biomass for sustainable wastewater treatment
abstract: The growing generation of food and agro-industrial waste, coupled with rising pressures from climate change, resource depletion, and carbon emissions, has intensified the demand for sustainable engineering solutions aligned with circular bioeconomy principles. However, the environmental implications of waste-derived functional materials and their underlying production processes remain insufficiently assessed, creating a critical gap in understanding their overall sustainability. In this study, brewers’ spent grain (BSG), a major by-product of the brewing industry, was converted into activated biochar through microwave-assisted phosphoric acid (H3PO4) activation and evaluated as an adsorbent for wastewater treatment, integrating experimental process optimization with a cradle-to-gate life-cycle-based sustainability assessment. The highest adsorption capacities of 46.9 mg/g for CV and 49.5 mg/g for Or-II occurred under the most intensive activation conditions tested, but life cycle assessment (LCA) showed that such conditions were not environmentally optimal: the production phase overwhelmingly dominates environmental impacts, and the associated low biochar yield increased energy and chemical demands, whereas the application phase contributes minimally. In contrast, milder activation conditions substantially reduced life-cycle impacts while maintaining effective adsorption performance (34.3 mg/g for CV and 45.1 mg/g for Or-II). These findings demonstrate that technical and environmental optimality do not necessarily coincide, and highlight the need for life-cycle-informed optimization to balance adsorption performance with resource efficiency and environmental sustainability in waste-derived biochar systems. © 2026 The Authors. title: Integrated Model of Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0–Case Studies
abstract: Siemens integrates Industry 4.0 (digitalization, automation, IoT, cyber-physical systems, and data-driven efficiency) with Industry 5.0 (human-centric collaboration, resilience, sustainability, and AI augmentation) through its Siemens Xcelerator open digital business platform. Core Foundation (Industry 4.0 Legacy) are: Builds on digital twins (DT), Industrial IoT (eg, Insights Hub, formerly MindSphere), edge computing, and comprehensive portfolios like NX, Teamcenter, and SIMATIC for end-to-end integration across product lifecycle, production, and supply chains, and Enables vertical/horizontal integration, predictive maintenance, and mass customization in smart factories. Evolution to Industry 5.0 are: Emphasizes human-machine synergy: AI augments rather than replaces workers, with collaborative robotics (cobots) and ergonomic designs; Introduces agentic AI and Industrial Copilots: Generative AI interfaces coordinate autonomous AI agents (Siemens-developed and third-party) for tasks in design, planning, engineering, operations, and maintenance-shifting from assisted automation to orchestrated autonomy; Integrates Industrial Metaverse (via NVIDIA Omniverse) for immersive, real-time simulations and multi-user collaboration, and Focuses on sustainability and resilience: AI-optimized resource use, circular economy tools, and adaptive systems for decarbonization and disruption resistance. Siemens’ model views Industry 5.0 as a seamless extension of Industry 4.0-not a replacement-delivering resilient, sustainable, and personalized production where humans, AI, and machines co-create value. This approach positions Siemens as a leader in transitioning industries toward adaptive, ethical, and profitable digital futures. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Design of a Conversational Analytics Model Based on NLP Applied to Sales for Companies
abstract: The widespread adoption of instant messaging platforms as a business channel has created a paradox for organizations: the more active they are on these channels, the greater the volume of conversational data they produce, and yet, the less capable they are of leveraging it. WhatsApp Business, with over 200 million active business users worldwide, has become the primary sales channel for organizations seeking to maintain direct contact with their customers in an accessible and cost free manner. However, empirical evidence shows that 78.3% of organizations do not have any system to analyze the data generated on this channel not due to a lack of interest, but rather to a lack of accessible tools. A four module conversational analytics model based on natural language processing (NLP) was designed and implemented for organizations with limited technological resources. This model transforms digital sales conversations into strategic knowledge management indicators without requiring specialized infrastructure or programming knowledge. It was validated using 1,052 real messages from business conversations and a survey of 42 organizations. Results demonstrate the model closes that gap in a technically viable, economically accessible, and operationally replicable manner. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Enterprise Information Exchange via IE-BSE Framework: A Case Study on E-invoicing
abstract: Digitalization has enabled enterprises to adopt API-centric business services to manage complex business operations. Consequently, leading businesses are progressively employing Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) to support digital transformation. Despite the existence of several open API marketplaces, API utilization remains limited and is often restricted to internal organizational boundaries. Thus, enterprises struggle to identify suitable APIs from diverse backgrounds and integrate them into their business operations. To address the issues, the research article employs Design Science Research Methodology (DSRM) and proposes an IE-BSE framework, namely an Information Exchange Business Service Ecosystem, which enables enterprises to acquire and utilize openly available APIs in their business processes that involve document exchange. The framework features a service discovery method that allows enterprises to identify suitable APIs and a service composition mechanism using a Business Process (BP) Builder tool to compose appropriate Business APIs, providing them with clear technical aspects and handling complex business processes. The framework is implemented in the E-invoicing domain and analyzes business APIs within our generated IE API Repository, a Knowledge Hub for E-invoicing APIs (KHEA). Results determine possible business processes, integrating diverse APIs and enabling the user to select a particular BP. This generates automatic business workflows via Amazon Web Services (AWS) Step Functions. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Conceptual Normalisation as a Foundation for Clear and Correct Organisational Models
abstract: Organisational models frequently suffer from semantic ambiguities and structural redundancies that hinder consistency, maintainability, and correct system interpretation. This paper proposes that these issues stem from conceptual redundancy and can be addressed through a principled application of Conceptual Normalisation (CN) - a theory based on the ontological premise that the real world contains no redundancy. By introducing four Conceptual Normal Forms (CNFs), this method provides a systematic approach to model refinement. The paper illustrates how CN can serve as a foundational methodology for developing correct, comprehensible, and transformation-ready organisational models. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.
