title: MetaTwin: A reconfigurable digital twin framework
abstract: Digitalization initiatives have led to the widespread adoption of digital twins (DTs), particularly in manufacturing. The explosive growth of DTs makes us think about what the most abstract parts in building the DT systems are and how to promote the reconfigurability of DTs so that they can be agile to adopt the flexibility needs from Industry 4.0 manufacturing systems. However, the heterogeneous granularity and dynamic evolution of manufacturing systems present significant challenges to the reconfigurability of their corresponding DTs. To address these challenges, this paper presents MetaTwin, a reconfigurable DT framework as an integrated solution to abstract DTs into general domains. To be more specific, a novel Domain-Meta structure is first proposed, which addresses the granularity misalignment problem by decoupling the system into stable Domains and reconfigurable Meta units. Then, a dual-dimensional reconfiguration mechanism decomposes complex reconfigurations into macro and micro dimensions, achieved by composing Meta units and reconfiguring their internal pattern-driven Meta Models. A prototype-based case study involving the progressive reconfiguration from an assembly-only DT to a printing-and-assembly DT illustrates how MetaTwin supports reconfiguration scope identification, macro-level structural changes, micro-level behavioral adaptations, and runtime coordination. Furthermore, implementation-level indicators further suggest that the MetaTwin-based implementation localizes changes more effectively than a conventional implementation in the case setting. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Thermo-mechanical mechanism of asperity-induced micropitting in rough mixed-lubricated gear contacts
abstract: This study develops an asperity-resolving, mechanism-oriented thermo-mechanical framework for investigating micropitting initiation in rough mixed-lubricated gear contacts, using differential planetary gears as a representative high-power-density application. The framework sequentially maps transient gear-scale loading and sliding conditions onto a local representative volume element and iteratively couples thermal mixed elastohydrodynamic lubrication with mechanism-based strain-gradient plasticity. Micromorphic regularization is introduced to regularize highly localized plastic deformation under severe asperity contact. For the baseline operating condition, the coupled solution predicts a peak asperity pressure of 1.58 GPa and a localized flash temperature approaching 300 °C. Constitutive decomposition of the converged state indicates a crossover between near-surface thermal softening and subsurface geometrically necessary dislocation-mediated strengthening at approximately 1.62 μm. The associated fatigue-driving field is concentrated within a 0.63–2.30 μm subsurface band and reaches a maximum 34.6% above its surface value. Comparison with published experimental observations provides mechanism-level corroboration of the predicted damage-depth scale and preferential subsurface localization. The framework does not directly predict component-level fatigue life; rather, it provides topography-resolved, temperature- and size-dependent initiation fields that can serve as physically enriched local inputs to future macroscopic fatigue assessments. Explicit crack propagation, progressive material removal, and damage feedback remain outside the present scope. These findings clarify how frictional heat accumulation, high-frequency micro-slip, and strain-gradient strengthening jointly govern the early localization of micropitting damage in rough mixed-lubricated gear contacts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Ready to blossom? African city skylines, an empirical puzzle, and a proposed solution
abstract: This paper shows that global skyscraper construction both accelerated and globalized after the 2001 attacks on the Twin Towers in New York, into the twenty-first century. Despite being increasingly incorporated into the global economy as a ‘new frontier’ for global investors, Sub Saharan Africa (SSA) did not share in this construction boom. This paper demonstrates that the absence of skyscrapers in SSA is an empirical puzzle. The key drivers of skyscraper construction – economic growth, population increase and migration, globalization, and vanity-driven competition – should all be pushing SSA into building upwards. The key to resolving the empirical puzzle of why SSA doesn't build skyscrapers lies in land markets: better functioning land markets would directly increase the supply and indirectly increase the demand for skyscrapers. This paper suggests a mechanism to allow city governments to focus their capacity on protecting the property rights of developers building skyscrapers, allowing a skyscraper project to be granted the status of a standalone Special Economic Zone (SEZ). The resulting construction of skyscrapers may simply increase the supply of luxury residential accommodation and office space and displace any pre-existing informal construction to a less advantageous location on the city periphery. The demand for formal residential accommodation is also influenced by more than price – culture matters. Consequently, the paper concludes by noting that inclusive or affordable housing construction needs to be rooted in a more holistic development strategy. © 2026 .

title: Reliability assessment modeling of multi-component series systems considering phase-type shocks and multiple degradation pathways
abstract: In order to solve the reliability evaluation problem of multi-component series systems affected by multiple impact sources, this paper proposes a unified modeling framework. Traditional approaches typically assume mutual independence among degradation paths and between degradation and shock processes, which may lead to errors. The proposed framework is capable of joint modeling (1) the dynamic impact of each shock source on multiple components, and (2) the strong statistical dependence among multiple degradation paths within each component. Specifically, vine copulas are employed to flexibly capture high-dimensional dependencies among degradation processes without restrictive parametric assumptions, while phase-type distributions are used to represent cumulative damage from mixed-type shocks in a tractable and general manner. Under this framework, an analytical reliability function for the system is derived and its effectiveness is validated through a case study on MEMS oscillators and sensitivity analyses. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Patent-Market Correlations via Fuzzy Technology Transfer Analysis
abstract: This paper presents an interpretable methodology to analyze Technology Transfer (TT) by combining Fuzzy Logic with t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE). The approach builds a “Technological Print”, i.e., a fuzzy vector that summarizes a firm’s technological orientation by matching patent abstracts and business filings. We analyze approximately 300 companies and over one million patents. t-SNE is used as an exploratory visualization tool to verify whether the resulting prints align with known market sectors. In the Technology sector, we observe a strong temporal correlation (R2=0.9594) between patent activity in the G16H (Healthcare Informatics) subclass and sectoral growth over 2000–2021. The contribution is an explainable correlation framework that supports strategic interpretation of patent-market relationships without relying on opaque embeddings. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Methodological Aspects of the Fears Mitigation of Change Management in Wartime: Textual Data Analyses and Practical Solutions
abstract: The organizations of Ukraine are faced with different issues under wartime. The bigest problem of 19000 organizations was related to relocations. Managers of these organizations tried to react fast during decision making process in time constraint. The main challenge was understanding of employees’ fears in order to launch key first steps change successfully. The described situation can arise in different countries close to country aggressor. This situation inspired us to analyse fears which were identified by learners from business and universities. The results of the analyses have become the basis of developed Fears Mitigation of Change Management Methodology. The proposed methodology is novel and shows the algorithm of textual data analyses based on similarity approach and the data collection tool in change management sphere. Also proposed methodology can be the foundation for developing applied artificial tool for decision makers in order to receive information to solve issues. The authors clear identified steps for decision making process, and presented the main results of the investigation. The authors proposed the approach for creating AAI tool of fears similarity calculus that can be the basis for decision-makers during crises or wartime. Also, these results are the basis for solving data classification, that still paramount the main issue of large language models. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Predictive Process Monitoring Through the Lens of Deep Online Learning
abstract: Predictive Process Monitoring (PPM) leverages historical event data recorded during historical business process executions, to forecast future scenarios of new ongoing process executions. Traditional PPM methods assume that business processes remain in a steady state over time. However, this is often not the real-world case due to concept drifts. This paper presents a PPM method, named ATLAS, which uses an online learning strategy coupled with a LLM, to develop a LSTM model for predicting the next-activity of ongoing process executions (running cases). It keeps the PPM model continuously updated each time a new event is observed. The evaluation assesses the performance the proposed approach in terms of accuracy and computation time also compared to several related online PPM approaches. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Advanced Time Series Analysis via Deep Learning
abstract: Deep learning time series analysis is a method of using sophisticated neural network theory to present or generally forecast information taken or documented at specific points in time over a duration of time. This method has gained significant ground based on its ability to measure complicated designs and situations in time series information. Stock-trade refers to a meeting of sellers and buyers of stocks in publicly listed businesses or companies. The current world of value and fruitful investments has made financial analysis a challenging aspect in the modern world. The fast advancements of smart machines and automated learning strategies, the availability of large amounts of data, the enhanced computational abilities of the machine allow the prospect of creation of new advanced methods of stock price prediction methods. Deep learning processes have evolved soon as promising forecasting tools in the stock market. The current term paper is an exploration of the use of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) systems. LSTMs are recurrent artificial neural networks that are used in the investigation and estimation of stocks. The LSTM frameworks are especially suitable in consideration of sequential data, including stock prices, as a result of their ability to embrace long-term circumstances. The article discusses the usefulness of LSTM models in predicting stock prices. The paper is based on past stock market data to train and test LSTM models Various hyper-parameters, including the number of LSTM units, dropout, and optimization calculation are known to streamline the performance of the model. As the paper proceeds, it gets the focus on the influences of specific input characteristics, such as technical indicators and fundamental ones, on the forecasting accuracy. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Deep Learning and IoT Framework Using Dark Net-Based CNN for Automated Papaya Growth Monitoring and Yield Prediction
abstract: The tropical fruit papaya is excellent for business. From early development until ripening, monitor its development for the optimum production and quality. Traditional and present Internet of things (IoT)-deep learning (DL) systems for papaya growth monitoring have several issues. Because they lack preprocessing and employ broad model designs, they are hard to use, do not operate well in varied situations, and are inaccurate. Many models do not react quickly and rely on human observation, which costs resources and delays decisions. A novel IoT-based Dark Net Convolutional Neural Network (IoT-DNetCNN) approach for Papaya Growth Tracking and Productivity Enhancement was established to overcome these limits. The IOT-DNetCNN model constantly takes papaya photos using ESP32-CAM modules. Video frames and cloud-based semantic analysis are used. Gabor filtering normalizes and finds, and a hybrid DarkNet-19 convolutional neural network extracts features. The Python-based IOT-DNetCNN model can identify papaya ripeness and predict yield using regression. The proposed model has a high accuracy (0.98), low MAE (0.02), and low RMSE (0.14). Overall, in classification and regression it performed better than benchmark models. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Current Status of Bowel Preparation for Colonoscopy in Japan: A Web-Based Survey of Endoscopists (PRESS Survey)
abstract: Objectives: The increasing number of patients with colorectal cancer underscores the importance of colonoscopy. Adequate bowel preparation is essential to ensure the quality and safety of colonoscopic examinations; however, data on the current practices in Japan remain limited. This study aimed to clarify the current status of bowel preparation, use of bowel-cleansing agents, and associated challenges among physicians performing colonoscopies. Methods: In March 2026, we conducted a nationwide web-based cross-sectional survey of physicians performing colonoscopies in Japan. The survey assessed bowel preparation practices, use of bowel-cleansing agents, constipation, and renal function before colonoscopy. Responses were obtained from 300 physicians who performed at least 10 colonoscopies per month. Results: Low-volume polyethylene glycol (PEG) plus ascorbate preparations were the most commonly used bowel-cleansing agents, followed by high-volume PEG preparations and magnesium-based agents. Cleansing efficacy and safety were the most highly valued characteristics of bowel-cleansing agents. 64.7% of physicians reported that the perceived frequency of inadequate bowel preparation was >10% among their patients. Although 64.3% of the physicians reported always assessing constipation, only 32.7% reported always evaluating renal function before colonoscopy. Compared with hospital-based physicians, those working in clinics reported a significantly lower proportion of inadequate bowel preparation, but a significantly lower rate of renal function assessment. Conclusion: Although cleansing efficacy and safety are prioritized in bowel preparation for colonoscopy in Japan, physicians perceived inadequate bowel preparation to occur in a substantial proportion of patients. Thus, further optimization of bowel preparation strategies and more consistent assessment of renal function before colonoscopy are needed. title: Foodborne microplastics: Occurrence in food matrices, health implications, analytical challenges and multi-tiered control strategies
abstract: This review critically synthesizes current knowledge on foodborne microplastics (MPs) to establish a scientific foundation for risk assessment and control. Despite their widespread presence in food systems, research is hindered by a lack of standardized detection methods and unresolved uncertainties regarding their health implications. Our synthesis shows that the toxicity of MPs arises from a combination of physical abrasion, chemical leaching, and a “Trojan horse” mechanism that carries co-pollutants, collectively triggering oxidative stress and inflammation. A primary challenge remains the absence of harmonized analytical protocols, especially for nanoplastics. Key conclusions emphasize the need for a multi-tiered control strategy, spanning from source reduction to the development of safer alternatives. While vigilance is warranted, the likely existence of a dose-response relationship argues against undue alarm. Future work should focus on standardizing methods and using human-relevant models to inform evidence-based food safety policies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Ag-doped ZnTi-LDH-derived ZnO/TiO2 heterojunctions promote charge separation to achieve highly efficient photocatalytic H2O2 production
abstract: To achieve high-efficiency photocatalytic H2O2 production, it is essential to modulate the charge-carrier lifetime of the photocatalyst. Herein, a series of xAg-ZnO/TiO2 (x = 0, 20, 30, 40 mg AgNO3) materials are synthesized by pyrolysing Ag-doped ZnTi-LDH. Among these, compared with pristine ZnTi-LDH, the 30Ag-ZnO/TiO2 sample shows a 113.7-fold higher photocatalytic H2O2 generation rate, reaching 4.6 mmol g−1 h−1. Meanwhile, Ag-ZnO/TiO2 retains the two-dimensional morphology of ZnTi-LDH, and a 9.8-fold increase in specific surface area is observed for 30Ag-ZnO/TiO2 relative to pristine ZnTi-LDH. The presence of Ag optimises charge distribution and introduces impurity levels near the Fermi level, narrowing the bandgap. Concurrently, the ZnO/TiO2 heterojunction further accelerates carrier separation and migration, enabling highly efficient photocatalytic H2O2 production. Furthermore, the photocatalytic mechanism of two-step single-electron ORR (O2 → •O2− → H2O2) is confirmed via XPS, EPR and DFT. This research can act as a reference for the fabrication of heterojunctions through metal doping and in-situ derivation, as well as practical guidance for the green synthesis of H2O2. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Fall Detection Using RAFT-Based Optical Flow and LSTM Networks
abstract: Falling can cause injuries careless of age. For older people, it may lead to serious health issues and subsequent social issues. Therefore, improving a reliable and timely fall detection system is important for families, organizations, business environments and healthcare providers. To address this need, this study proposed a method that extracts temporal optical flow features using the RAFT model and analyzes them with an LSTM network to predict fall events. For practical evaluation, the HQFSD dataset was employed, and 97% accuracy was attained using the proposed method. This outcome shows how well the method works for reliably identifying fall incidents. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Heterogeneous edge AI orchestration: A systematic review, taxonomy and future directions
abstract: The confluence of Machine Learning (ML), Edge, and containerization has resulted in the emergence of Edge AI, which enhances reliability, fault tolerance, data security and privacy, inference time and accuracy. On one hand, accelerated hardware and advanced interconnects have reduced training times and improved accuracy. Leveraging this, the orchestration engines automate workload management but often struggle with limited features and sub-optimal policies. Edge offers a myriad of interconnected devices employing hardware and orchestration engines, but these devices are inherently distributed and resource-constrained, which adversely impacts Edge AI adoption. Moreover, leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Edge orchestration to optimize resource provisioning, scheduling, and management without compromising the quality of service has been the driving motivation. However, integrating these components to enable Edge AI poses substantial challenges encompassing the hardware, interconnects, orchestration engines, computational, application, and workload heterogeneities. Additionally, training data scarcity, constrained and heterogeneous resources, control plane management overhead, delayed data traversal, and other factors exacerbate Edge AI orchestration challenges. Considering these challenges and opportunities, this paper establishes a top-to-bottom architectural view to investigate cross-layer Edge AI orchestration progress across three layers. At the bottom layer, NVLink, Compute Express Link, and other heterogeneous interconnects that manage the underlying hardware are discussed and compared in terms of offered bandwidth, latency, topology, and other features. In the middle layer, heterogeneous container orchestration engines and their high/low-level runtimes are contrasted for Edge AI. For the top layer, a systematic review of research works empowering heterogeneous Edge AI orchestration which proposed heuristic, meta-heuristic, optimization, and AI/ML solutions for container migration, autoscaling, ML/DL model-switching, resource forecasting, and scheduling is conducted. Furthermore, this article investigates the employment and position of Generative AI in Edge computing. Subsequently, taxonomies of optimization models, ML/DL models, orchestration engines, runtimes, and orchestration objectives are provided. Finally, the identified research gaps and possible future directions conclude this article. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Counterfactuals to Manage Ongoing Business Process Deviances
abstract: Business Process Deviance (BPD) refers to the phenomenon of business process executions (traces) that deviate with respect to the desirable outcome. BPD detection is a Predictive Process Monitoring (PPM), which covers predictive methods designed to distinguish deviant traces from non-deviant traces. In this paper, we focus on the task of predicting BPD cases without waiting for the completion of process executions. To this purpose, we describe a PPM methodology, named FIREFOX, to monitor ongoing traces of a business process, to early identify process executions that are expected to deviate from the desirable outcome. FIREFOX equips BPD predictions with counterfactual recommendations of actions to perform in the near future, to avoid the detected deviance risk. A preliminary evaluation explores the effectiveness of the proposed methodology on traces recorded for some business processes. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Fractional class-specific weighted random forest optimization
abstract: Random forests are a cornerstone of ensemble learning due to their robustness and scalability. However, their potential is constrained by a rigid voting structure. By assigning equal weight to every tree, the standard model overlooks the heterogeneous performance inherent to individual trees across diverse target classes. In this paper, we introduce the Fractional Class-Specific Weighted Random Forest (f CWRFO). This approach refines tree level confidence weights through fractional order gradient descent. Indeed, it expands the optimization landscape beyond standard integer derivatives which only represent a specific instance of our framework (α =1). This mechanism introduces a history-dependent fractional scaling of the weight updates, which adaptively modulates the optimization trajectory and improves convergence stability. Comprehensive benchmarks on 40 UCI datasets demonstrate that f CWRFO improves generalization accuracy and stability, outperforming both standard Random Forests and classical integer-based weighting schemes. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Local and global uncertainty quantification for a family of fuzzy multi-criteria sorting models
abstract: This paper introduces a family of FMAVT-Sort models based on a fuzzy extension of the Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) method MAVT, alongside a framework for Uncertainty and Distinction Quantification (UQ and DQ) of the model outputs. The models differ in approaches to evaluating functions of fuzzy numbers (FNs), employing both precise and approximate techniques, and utilize four fuzzy ranking methods: defuzzification-based approaches (Centroid Index and Integral of Means), and two methods designed for ranking dependent FNs. The models are applied to a case study on university teacher evaluation. Assessment of local (within the case study) UQ and DQ and global (across a space of independent multicriteria problems) DQ is performed using algorithms that process output values from a large number of fuzzy multicriteria sorting problems simulated via Monte Carlo techniques in a fuzzy environment. A set of UQ indices, combined with a pre-uncertainty analysis stage, is implemented in a General Algorithm for Multicriteria Sorting, designed to support the decision-making process. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of UQ indices for decision support in multicriteria sorting and reveal significant distinctions among FMAVT-Sort models, underscoring the impact of model selection on final sorting outcomes. These findings hold scientific, methodological, and practical significance. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Collective identity, organizational commitment, and environmental conservation: An integrated model for U.S. hotels
abstract: The study tests a new approach to linking collective environmental identity (CEI) and high organizational identity (HOI) to environmental conservation through affective, normative, and continuance commitment. We used PLS-SEM version 4 to examine these connections using cross-sectional data from hotel workers across the US. The results show that collective environmental identity is linked to affective, normative, and continuance commitment, and that a strong organizational identity further strengthens these commitments. Affective, normative, and continuance commitment also shape the link between employees' environmental conservation and collective environmental identity. These results show how important it is to have dedicated workers who support sustainable practices. Companies, especially those in the rapidly growing US hotel industry, can use this framework to embed sustainability in their business plans by engaging and empowering employees. This study contributes to the hospitality literature by demonstrating how identity-based commitments lead to concrete actions that benefit the environment. This has not been examined in the context of hotel employees before. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Singing praises vs. venting frustration: Multi-dimensional satisfaction gaps as drivers of high-quality hotel reviews
abstract: High-quality reviews reveal consumer satisfaction with product attributes and greatly affect the decisions of others. However, without incorporating consumer expectations, the motivations to share high-quality remain poorly understood. Drawing on expectation confirmation theory and motivation–hygiene theory, this study constructs positive and negative satisfaction gaps between expectations and evaluations and examines how these gaps affect the sharing of high-quality reviews. We adopt NLP and hierarchical clustering to identify satisfaction dimensions and generate sentiment scores and assess review quality using LLM. An analysis of 10,492 customer reviews from TripAdvisor shows that high-quality reviews are driven more by satisfaction than by dissatisfaction. Positive and negative satisfaction gaps differ in the dimensions involved and their effect sizes. The findings have meaningful practical implications for businesses to improve product performance and customer satisfaction and for review and e-commerce platforms to recommend high-impact reviews. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Gender Imbalance and the Leadership Legitimacy Gap: Post-conflict Transformation of Classroom Discourse in Ukrainian Business Education
abstract: Periods of war and large-scale social disruption frequently reshape educational environments, altering patterns of participation, authority, and identity formation within the classroom. Ukraine’s ongoing war has accelerated demographic and institutional changes across higher education. Wartime conscription, migration, and displacement have produced classrooms in which women significantly outnumber men, particularly in business education programs. This demographic shift has not only changed the composition of the classroom but has also transformed the nature of discourse, leadership expression, and perceptions of legitimacy among students. Drawing on qualitative field observations from teaching and residence in Kyiv and Dnipro, this study examines how gender imbalance influences leadership dynamics and classroom interaction in a wartime academic context. Data were collected through semi-structured and informal interviews with approximately 35 undergraduate and graduate business students, complemented by direct classroom observation. The study adopts an interpretive, practice-based approach, focusing on how students construct and negotiate leadership roles in real time within an evolving institutional environment. The findings identify the emergence of what this study conceptualizes as a “Leadership Legitimacy Gap”— a divergence between rapidly evolving leadership practice and slower institutional recognition among female students and the slower adaptation of institutional norms, expectations, and recognition structures. Unlike traditional gender-based leadership barriers, the Leadership Legitimacy Gap reflects a temporal mismatch between evolving leadership practice and slower institutional recognition under conditions of disruption. While women increasingly assume active roles in discussion, decision-making, and professional aspiration, institutional frameworks and inherited cultural expectations do not always fully acknowledge or reinforce these shifts. At the same time, the absence or reduced presence of male students alters the diversity of perspectives and reshapes the dynamics of classroom discourse, leading to new forms of consensus, contestation, and identity formation. This study contributes to cultural and educational studies by highlighting how post-conflict conditions reconfigure not only access and participation but also the symbolic and discursive foundations of leadership. It extends existing literature on gender and leadership by situating these dynamics within a wartime, post-Soviet context, where institutional transformation lags behind social and demographic change. The concept of the Leadership Legitimacy Gap offers a framework for understanding similar dynamics in other post-conflict and rapidly transforming educational environments. The study contributes to leadership and knowledge management literature by demonstrating how legitimacy shapes knowledge recognition, participation, and influence, particularly in disrupted educational environments where authority and contribution are no longer aligned. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Digital Twins in the Energy Industry and Emerging Three Innovation Ecosystems: Battery Factory, Data Center, and Greenhouse Farming Business Ecosystems: A Knowledge-based Scoping Review for Strategic Industrial Foresight Processes in Finland
abstract: This study investigates three emerging innovation ecosystems and their Digital Twins: (1) the Data Center business innovation ecosystem, (2) the Battery Factory innovation ecosystem, and (3) the Greenhouse farming innovation ecosystem, together with Digital Twin (DT) energy industry solutions, aiming to identify technological potential, pathways for ecosystem/cluster growth and development, and policy implications. A systematic review of DT applications was conducted across conventional and renewable energy production, storage, and multi-energy systems. Both conventional and less conventional energy DTs were identified and reported. The three innovation business ecosystems were conceptualized and defined as summary tables integrating technological, organizational, and market dimensions. The study analyses how DT solutions can be mobilized to foster competitive new innovative industrial cluster business ecosystems and evaluates the associated strategic policy measures. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: A Smart Framework for Integrating Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, and IoT in Construction Project Management
abstract: The construction sector continues to face persistent structural challenges, including execution delays, recurring cost overruns, low productivity, fragmented communication among stakeholders, and limited levels of technological maturity. These issues are particularly acute in developing economies, where small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) dominate the industry. This study aims to formulate and validate a comprehensive framework that supports the effective integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Data Science, and the Internet of Things (IoT) into construction and civil engineering project management, with a specific focus on SMEs while remaining applicable to larger organizations. A mixed-methods approach was adopted, comprising four stages: a bibliometric analysis of academic literature published between 2015 and 2024 to identify trends, methodologies, and application areas of emerging technologies; a 21-item Likert-type survey administered to 55 Colombian construction-related companies to assess their level of digital maturity; the formulation of the Comprehensive Model for incorporating Technologies into Construction and Civil Engineering Project Management (CMTCCPM); and its validation through a two-round Delphi study involving five international experts. The results indicate an average digital maturity level of 2.8 out of 5, with relatively higher development in customer and supplier management and significant weaknesses in Industry 4.0 strategy and experience. The proposed model integrates interoperable BIM 5D/6D, connected digital twins, AI-assisted predictive maintenance, advanced analytics, circular material tokenization, smart certifications, and ethical AI frameworks to enhance planning, risk management, automated execution, intelligent operation and maintenance, sustainability, and digital governance. Expert validation yielded an average score of 4.51 out of 5, highlighting high relevance, feasibility, innovation, and impact, and recommending the inclusion of implementation roadmaps, key performance indicators, and ROI-oriented business cases. Overall, the CMTCCPM provides a strategic pathway for advancing efficiency, sustainability, and competitiveness in digitally integrated construction ecosystems. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Reimagining Knowledge Management Education in South Africa for the Artificial Intelligence Era
abstract: Knowledge Management (KM) education in South Africa has developed unevenly across higher education institutions, frequently embedded within Library and Information Science, Information Systems, or Business disciplines rather than institutionalised as a coherent professional qualification. Building on the integrated five-perspective KM curriculum framework developed from a South African perspective [1], this paper argues that the rapid emergence of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, has shifted the epistemic conditions of KM education from repository-centric management toward AI-mediated knowledge ecosystems. While the integrated model remains structurally foundational, it does not explicitly theorise AI as an epistemic co-actor in knowledge processes. The paper reconceptualizes KM education by treating AI as a mediator in knowledge processes, embedding governance and assessment integrity as core curriculum requirements, and positioning Indigenous Knowledge Systems as equal knowledge pillars rather than contextual additions. Anchored in South Africa’s higher education transformation landscape and AI governance trajectory, the paper proposes an AI-mediated KM epistemology framework, maps curriculum implications across the five perspectives, and presents a phased implementation roadmap for South African universities [5]. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: A Deep Learning-Based Model for Identifying Abnormal Access Behavior and Security Protection in Low-Carbon Park Networks
abstract: The network system of low-carbon parks is responsible for various important tasks, including energy control, equipment status monitoring, and user service support. However, abnormal access behavior caused by network attacks not only directly affects the normal operation of business, but may also lead to a sudden increase in energy consumption during emergency response, further causing an increase in carbon emissions. The commonly used anomaly detection methods based on rules or statistical features are often difficult to handle the rapid changes and complex situations of network behavior patterns. Therefore, this article proposes a multimodal anomaly recognition and dynamic protection framework that combines deep learning mechanisms. On the basis of summarizing existing research results, this article carefully analyzes the shortcomings of existing methods and focuses on designing lightweight feature extraction modules, adaptive threshold adjustment strategies, and low resource consumption protection mechanisms. This model not only maintains high detection accuracy, but also fully considers the overall energy efficiency of the system, providing a feasible technical route for network security management in low-carbon parks. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Inertial bregman proximal iteratively reweighted algorithms for a class of nonconvex nonsmooth regularized problems
abstract: In this paper, we study a class of nonconvex nonsmooth regularized optimization problems whose objective consists of a continuously differentiable loss function and a structured nonconvex regularizer. To solve this class of problems efficiently, we first propose an inertial Bregman proximal iteratively reweighted algorithm for the case where the loss function has a Lipschitz-continuous gradient. An explicit and verifiable condition for selecting the extrapolation parameters is established. We then extend the proposed framework to the relatively smooth setting, where the loss function is differentiable but not necessarily gradient-Lipschitz continuous. In both settings, we prove that any accumulation point of the generated sequence is a critical point of the problem. Moreover, under the Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz property of suitable Lyapunov functions, the global convergence of the whole sequence is established. Numerical experiments on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that the proposed algorithms are efficient in terms of both computational time and solution quality. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Transboundary cascading economic impacts and efficiency dynamics of power shortages induced by extreme heatwaves: An integrated weather-shock input-output data envelopment analysis framework for China
abstract: Efficiency analysis is critical for evaluating economic impacts of extreme heat-induced power shortages. It detects inefficient sectors and resource misallocation to boost economic resilience. However, existing studies only examine associated economic losses, ignoring post-shock efficiency analysis. This limitation impedes the full assessment of cascading socio-environmental risks and the design of targeted resilience policies. This study constructs an integrated Weather-Shock Input-Output Data Envelopment Analysis framework. Empirical results reveal: First, macroeconomic risks triggered by heatwaves stem from two sources: the direct physical impacts of heatwave shocks and the institutional rules that shape power rationing schemes. Under our baseline scenario where energy-intensive industries bear priority cutbacks, indirect economic losses are roughly twice as high as direct losses; however, both the scale and composition of total losses vary significantly when adopting alternative power rationing policies. Second, this study differentiates the functional roles of various sectors in risk transmission. While agricultural and financial sectors act as passive absorbers, sectors like food & tobacco processing and leasing & business services are identified as key amplifiers that propagate supply-chain shocks. Third, power shortages widen disparities in efficiency, with more than 90% of this inequality attributable to within-group heterogeneity, a pattern prominent in western China and secondary industries. The findings support a transition from “one-size-fits-all” energy rationing toward supply-chain-based strategies that protect loss transmission pathways and optimize cross-regional resource reallocation. © 2026

title: Corporate social responsibility and environmental performance in the lebanese travel and tourism sector: Through the lens of green practices
abstract: This study examines the impact of green human resource management (GHRM) and green innovation (GI) on environmental performance (EP) in the Lebanese travel and tourism sector, with corporate social responsibility (CSR) as a mediator. In addition, the study investigates the moderating role of green transformational leadership (GTL). Grounded in NRBV theory, the study conceptualizes green practices and CSR as internal resources and capabilities that contribute to improved EP. Data were collected from 397 employees and managers through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The measurement items were adopted from well-established scales and assessed using a five-point Likert scale. The results indicate that both GHRM and GI have significant positive effects on environmental performance. Furthermore, CSR plays a significant mediating role, suggesting that organizations adopting green practices are more likely to engage in broader CSR initiatives, which ultimately improve environmental performance. The findings also demonstrate that GTL moderates the relationship between GI and EP, highlighting the importance of visionary leadership in maximizing the environmental benefits of innovation. Interestingly, the results indicate that GTL does not moderate the relationship between GHRM and environmental performance, suggesting that the effectiveness of GHRM may depend more on organizational systems than on leadership influence alone. The coefficient of determination (R²) was 0.68, indicating that 68% of the variance in EP is explained by the variables included in the model. The study provides important theoretical and practical implications. From a theoretical perspective, the findings extend NRBV theory by demonstrating how green practices and CSR jointly contribute to environmental performance. Practically, the results suggest that tourism organizations can improve their EP by integrating GHRM, green innovation, and CSR initiatives into their operational strategies, thereby enhancing sustainability while maintaining competitiveness. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Exploring the correlation between community empowerment and social innovation in faith-based enterprise: Basis for a university extension program
abstract: Faith-based enterprises (FBEs) play a pivotal role in community empowerment and social innovation by integrating moral, spiritual, and entrepreneurial principles to address social, economic, and environmental challenges. This study employed a descriptive correlational research design to examine the influence of FBEs on community well-being among 85 residents of Nampicuan, Nueva Ecija. Data were collected via a validated and pilot-tested structured questionnaire (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.87) and analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation coefficients. Focus group discussions provided additional contextual insights. Results revealed significant positive correlations between community empowerment and social innovation practices (economic: r = 0.63–0.68; social: r = 0.69–0.73; spiritual: r = 0.78–0.79, p < 0.05), as well as between empowerment and sustainability and mission integrity of FBEs (economic: r = 0.64–0.70; social: r = 0.71–0.75; spiritual: r = 0.70–0.76, p < 0.05). Social innovation variables, particularly entrepreneurial innovation, spiritual leadership, and ethical governance, were strongly associated with sustainability outcomes (r = 0.71–0.82, p < 0.05). These findings indicate that FBEs enhance economic self-reliance, social cohesion, ethical leadership, and innovative capacity, while strengthening organizational sustainability and mission alignment. Based on the results, an extension program integrating faith-driven entrepreneurship, product development, marketing, and capacity-building was developed to address the community’s holistic needs. This study highlights FBEs as transformative hybrid organizations that combine economic activity with social and moral objectives, fostering sustainable social innovation and community well-being. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Mapping the evolution from incentives to insights: A bibliometric analysis of executive influences on corporate risk-taking (1996-2025)
abstract: This bibliometric analysis examines 252 peer-reviewed publications (1996–August 2025) to map the evolution of research on executive influences on corporate risk-taking. By integrating data from both the Web of Science and Scopus databases, this study offers a more comprehensive view of the research landscape compared to previous analyses that often relied on a single source. Relying on a single database risks overlooking contributions published in niche-exclusive journals or regionally concentrated outlets, which disproportionately feature emerging-market research and interdisciplinary studies not uniformly indexed across repositories. We reveal a paradigm expansion from Agency Theory's focus on compensation and equity incentives to integrated perspectives incorporating Upper Echelons Theory's emphasis on psychological and demographic characteristics. Using Biblioshiny and VOSviewer for performance analysis, network construction, and clustering, we document three evolutionary phases: agency-dominated research (1996–2010), demographic integration (2011–2019), and theoretical synthesis (2020–2025). China leads in publication volume (186 articles) while the United States dominates citation impact (28.88 citations per article), reflecting different research priorities and institutional contexts. Keyword co-occurrence analysis identifies five thematic clusters, demonstrating the field's evolution from pure incentive-based studies to behavioral and psychological analyses. Temporal analysis shows compensation research maintaining consistent presence while psychological attributes such as CEO overconfidence and executive power gained prominence post-2020. The findings highlight the growing theoretical integration between agency and behavioral perspectives, with the most influential papers increasingly bridging internal attributes and external incentives. This synthesis provides critical insights for boards, compensation committees, and policymakers seeking to integrate behavioral considerations into executive selection, incentive design, and risk governance frameworks in contemporary complex business environments. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis of Thalassemia Screening Cascade Efficiency: Single-Sample Versus Multivisit Protocols in Malaysia
abstract: Objectives Malaysia's National Thalassemia Screening Program uses multivisit sequential testing (protocol 1), with a dropout rate of 20%, disproportionately affecting rural and underserved populations in Sabah and Sarawak. Protocol 2 proposes 3-tier testing from a single retained blood sample, eliminating visit-based dropout. Previous deterministic evaluation demonstrated favorable incremental cost per carrier detected but did not quantify parameter uncertainty. Methods Probabilistic sensitivity analysis was conducted using 2018 administrative data covering 65 990 students in Sabah and Sarawak. Monte Carlo simulations (10 000 iterations) assigned probability distributions to all parameters: gamma distributions for costs (15% coefficient of variation) and beta-binomial for dropout rates. Cost-effectiveness acceptability curves estimated probabilities across willingness-to-pay thresholds of MYR 10-50 per additional carrier detected. Scenario analyses tested protocol 2 dropout rates ranging from 0.5% (base case) to 5% (pessimistic). Results Mean probabilistic incremental cost-effectiveness ratios matched deterministic estimates (Sabah: MYR 20.8; Sarawak: MYR 10.3) with narrow 95% credible intervals (Sabah: 18.7-23.2; Sarawak: 9.2-11.5). At MYR 25-50 thresholds, protocol 2 has a > 91% probability of cost-effectiveness in Sabah and ∼100% in Sarawak. Under pessimistic 5% dropout scenarios, probabilities remained ≥70%, indicating substantial implementation tolerance. Conclusion Probabilistic sensitivity analysis demonstrated that protocol 2 maintained favorable screening cascade efficiency across plausible operational scenarios. The lower incremental cost-effectiveness ratio in Sarawak suggests potential equity advantages in higher dropout settings. Illustrative willingness-to-pay thresholds of MYR 10-50 per additional carrier detected were explored for scenario interpretation rather than as normative policy thresholds. These findings support future prospective pilot evaluations and health technology assessment to inform screening implementation decisions. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Dynamic shelf-life prediction for foods in intelligent packaging: AI-driven multimodal sensing and closed-loop decision-making
abstract: As conventional static shelf-life labels fail to account for environmental fluctuations across the supply chain, food waste and safety risks have become pressing challenges. Current intelligent packaging systems integrate multimodal sensing technologies, creating new opportunities for real-time monitoring of the food microenvironment. However, effectively predicting remaining shelf life (RSL) from multisource, heterogeneous sensor data—and translating these predictions into reliable decisions—remains a major research challenge. This review examines artificial intelligence (AI)-driven dynamic shelf-life prediction (DSLP) models for intelligent packaging, discusses the roles and applicability of different signal types in DSLP, and analyzes the distinct requirements of different food systems for prediction accuracy and decision-making. Compared with conventional approaches, intelligent-packaging-based DSLP models can handle diverse signal inputs more effectively and characterize food deterioration more accurately under complex environmental conditions. This review further organizes sensing evidence into environmental, state, and risk information, and clarifies three major DSLP outputs, including RSL, quality-state trajectory, and probability of spoilage. By linking these outputs with warning, inventory, distribution, and cold-chain management actions, the review highlights the transition from passive monitoring to closed-loop decision support. By integrating convolutional temporal models, multimodal fusion strategies, and interpretability analysis, intelligent packaging systems may enable multimodal-sensing-driven dynamic shelf-life updating, thereby supporting quality monitoring and evidence-based decision-making across food supply chains. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Natural nano-fish bone as novel Pickering stabilizers: the emulsifying property
abstract: Particles in the micrometer or nanometer range are widely used as stabilizers in Pickering emulsion systems. Nano-fish bone (NFB) could be an excellent stabilizer for Pickering emulsions, as it has the advantages of environmental friendliness and others. In this work, we prepared NFB particles through wet media milling treatment to investigate the mechanism behind the effect of adding NFB and peanut oil (PO) on Pickering emulsion formation and stability. The results suggested that increasing NFB resulted in increased particle coverage on the droplet surface, increased emulsion apparent viscosity, and improved stability. Similar changes in both apparent viscosity and emulsion stability were observed as the amount of PO increased. Therefore, the emulsifying properties and packing behavior of Pickering emulsions could be affected by NFB and PO content. This study provides a reference for the development of functional food-grade Pickering emulsions based on NFB stabilization. © 2026

title: Microwave effects on the flavor and storage quality of ‘Nongke Nuo 336’ sweet corn
abstract: Microwave (MW) technology, characterized by its convenience and efficiency, has demonstrated significant effects on extending the shelf life of agricultural products. This study investigated the impact of MW on flavor compounds, gene expression, and metabolic processes in sweet corn. The results indicated that after 6 days of storage at room temperature, MW-treated corn maintained 12.22% soluble solids content, reduced weight loss by 9.71%, and slowed the rate of hardness increase by 41.55%. MW treatment delayed sucrose breakdown by upregulating the expression of sucrose synthase genes (ZmSUS1, ZmSUS2, ZmSUS6) and sucrose-phosphate phosphatase 2 (ZmSPP2). Simultaneously, it reduced the expression of genes such as α-amylase (ZmAMY1), thereby hindering the conversion of sugars into starch. MW treatment significantly downregulated the expression of key enzyme genes involved in abscisic acid biosynthesis (ZmZEP, ZmCHIL2, and ZmCFAT), delaying postharvest senescence in sweet corn. Furthermore, MW treatment upregulated the expression of antioxidant enzyme-related genes, including peroxidase (POD), among others, enhancing the stress resistance of sweet corn and thereby extending its shelf life. Metabolomics analysis further revealed that MW treatment activated the corn's defense system, leading to the accumulation of isoquercitrin, and hyperoside, which improved its stress resistance. Notably, esters, ketones, alcohols, aldehydes, and methylated compounds, which are the main flavor components, significantly enhanced the flavor characteristics of sweet corn. These findings provide valuable insights into the effects of MW on the storage quality and flavor of sweet corn. © 2026

title: Hydraulic lobe-pump inter-operational transportation of cheese spreads
abstract: When pumped from one production unit to another, molten cheese spread is a highly viscous liquid, which inevitably affects all hydraulic calculations for optimal pipeline characteristics. However, such calculations often miss out the effect of the viscosity on the pump efficiency. This article introduces a new method for determining the optimal pipe diameter to transport liquid media during food production. It takes into account the viscosity of the liquid and the technical characteristics of the rotary lobe pump. The research featured a lobe-pump hydraulic system for transporting highly viscous cheese spreads. The calculations involved the technical parameters of the lobe pump and pipelines, as well as electricity tariffs. To determine the annual electricity costs, we used electricity tariffs for small businesses as of June 2024 in three random regions of the Russian Federation. The parameters of different cheese spreads (55–95°C) came from scientific publications in the public domain. Among the various factors that affected the optimal pipe diameter, the greatest impact belonged to the temperature-related changes in viscosity. As the operation time of the lobe pump increased, so did the share of electrical energy costs. As a result, the optimal diameter of the pipeline increased significantly to compensate for the hydraulic pressure losses and energy costs. The optimal diameter also depended on the investment parameters. Bigger Life-Cycle values correlated with larger optimal pipe diameters, i. e., the reduced costs went down. Higher interest rates, on the other hand, correlated with smaller optimal pipe diameters, i. e., the reduced costs went up. In general, the overall efficiency of the pumping station depended quite strongly on all the factors featured in this research. The new method made it possible to determine the optimal pipe diameter for inter-operational transportation of cheese spreads in particular and highly viscous laminar fluids in general. It relied on viscosity values and lobe pump specifications. Numerically, it was based on a step-by-step calculation of economic and hydraulic parameters. The method demonstrated good prospects for food pipeline design. © 2026, Akhmedova et al. title: Authentication and traceability of tea as a high-risk product: A comprehensive review of spectroscopic and chemometric solutions
abstract: Food fraud poses a serious threat to the tea market, impacting sellers, consumers, and the entire supply chain. Chemometrics combined with spectroscopic techniques has gained increasing attention as a rapid, non-destructive, and cost-effective alternative to conventional methods for tea authentication. This review provides a comprehensive overview of these combined approaches, summarizing recent progress in detecting common fraudulent practices, including misrepresentation of variety, origin, and grade, as well as adulteration through substitution and addition. Beyond summarizing existing studies, this review also examines the practical limitations that constrain the translation of these methods from laboratory research to real-world application. Future directions, including the development of online monitoring systems and the integration of emerging technologies and metabolomics, are also discussed. Overall, this review highlights both the promise and the current challenges of spectroscopy and chemometrics in safeguarding the authenticity and traceability of tea products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Temporal asymmetries in hotel performance: Evidence of a 4.4-month quality-price phase gap creating predictable occupancy opportunities
abstract: Purpose: This study examines whether hotel quality dimensions systematically lead financial performance through phase angle differentiation within business cycles, challenging the temporal homogeneity assumption in revenue management. Design/methodology/approach: Fourier decomposition integrated with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) analyzes 420 monthly U.S. hotel observations (1990–2024) under a Bayesian Prior → Likelihood → Posterior architecture. Phase angles (θ) quantify temporal positioning; cross-spectral coherence (C² ≈ 0.71) and Bai-Perron diagnostics confirm spectral stability. Findings: Quality metrics peak at θ ≈ π/6 (Month 17.5 post-trough) while financial metrics peak at θ ≈ π/4 (Month 21.9), yielding a posterior gap of 4.4 months (95% credible interval: 3.4–5.4, p <.001). Bayesian model comparison places 71% posterior probability on the phase structure model (log Bayes Factor = 3.1). During the quality-price gap window (Months 17–21), occupancy lift averages + 12.5 %age points across six cycles (Bayes Factor ≈ 18.4). Research limitations/implications: Analysis relies on U.S. national aggregates comprising six independent business-cycle realizations; the design is observational. Associations are consistent with but do not establish causal mechanisms. Property-level replication is needed. Practical implications: Phase-aware cycle positioning may complement conventional forecasting. Expected revenue per available room advantage: $12.40/room/night (90% posterior predictive interval: $6.80–$17.90); probability that the phase-aware strategy outperforms uniform strategy = 0.89. Originality/value: Among the first hospitality studies applying Bayesian inference and Fourier phase analysis to hotel performance temporality, complementing conventional revenue management with a frequency-domain approach. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Qualitative Versus Quantitative Risk Assessment in Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Audits: How European-Based Auditors Interpret Probability Under International Council for Harmonisation Guideline (ICH) Q9 (R1)
abstract: Purpose: Under ICH Q9 (R1), risk is defined as a function of probability and severity of harm. Although probability may be expressed quantitatively, little empirical evidence exists regarding how EU GMP auditors assess probability in practice. This study explored probability assessment approaches among auditors and the use of qualitative and quantitative methods. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional questionnaire was administered to 52 EU-based GMP auditors with at least two years of auditing experience. Participants (21 in total) completed structured multiple-response questions on probability and optional free-text comment fields addressing probability assessment practices (response rate: 40.4%). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and cross-tabulation; no inferential analyses were performed. Results: Qualitative probability assessment approaches were the most frequently reported method (14/21), while 8/21 respondents reported using quantitative approaches (multiple responses permitted). Probability assessment was commonly described as context-dependent and informed by professional judgement rather than purely numerical models. Qualitative approaches were reported across all experience categories and levels of English proficiency. Participants highlighted limited availability of robust historical data, contextual complexity, and reliance on prior audit experience as key factors influencing probability assessment. Respondents (4/21) suggested that no single clear definition of probability assessment was consistently applied in practice. Conclusion: Although some participants reported using quantitative approaches, probability assessment remained predominantly qualitative and experience-based in audits. Participants frequently described using structured risk matrices and categorical probability scales (e.g., High/Medium/Low) to support probability assessments. The findings highlight variability in how probability is operationalised and suggest that additional practical guidance may be useful. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Business interruption risk modeling framework for polymetallic nodule deep-sea mining
abstract: Deep-sea polymetallic nodule (PMN) mining is emerging as a potential source of critical minerals for global energy and technology supply chains. Yet it operates under extreme environmental uncertainty and limited operational experience, exposing projects to substantial business interruption (BI) risk. This paper develops a probabilistic framework for modeling aggregate BI loss distributions in PMN mining under data-scarce conditions. To our knowledge, no existing study provides a system-level actuarial loss model that integrates causal dependency, restoration dynamics, and economic valuation. The proposed approach combines a Bayesian Belief Network (BBN) with expert-elicited conditional probabilities. Results show that interruption probability ranges from 19.3% under favorable conditions to 77% under adverse regimes. Sensitivity analysis identifies several operational subsystems and managerial factors as dominant contributors to interruption probability. However, cost-based analysis indicates that the highest BI losses are driven by a smaller subset of technical components. For single interruptions, expected restoration times range from 17.6 ± 3.8 days to 52.7 ± 20.4 days. Modeling annual exposure as at most one major interruption per policy year, insurance premiums supporting system recovery range from approximately $0.9 M to $10.9 M. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Evaluating the technical and economic viability of 3-hydroxypropionic acid production from biomass
abstract: This study presents a techno-economic assessment of a conceptual 3-hydroxypropionic acid (3-HP) biorefinery integrating ionic liquid (IL) pretreatment with lignocellulosic biomass conversion. This work provides a novel comparative techno-economic assessment of corn stover (CS) and brewer's spent grain (BSG) as feedstocks for IL-based 3-HP production. A literature-based process model was developed for the continuous production of 50,000 t/year of 3-HP and evaluated using both feedstocks. IL pretreatment was selected for its recyclability and potential to reduce chemical consumption compared with conventional pretreatment methods. Biomass-to-3-HP conversion efficiencies (on a dry basis) of 25.63% and 23.31% were obtained for CS and BSG, respectively, reflecting the lower fermentable sugar recovery achieved from BSG. Economic assessment yielded break-even selling prices (BESP) of $2472/tonne 3-HP for CS and $2643/tonne for BSG, indicating that both configurations are economically competitive with literature-reported bio-based 3-HP values. Sensitivity analysis identified yeast consumption as the dominant cost driver, followed by enzyme and IL requirements. The results highlight the potential of IL-assisted lignocellulosic biorefineries for competitive 3-HP production and identify the optimisation of yeast production and recycling, enhanced IL recovery and recycling, and co-product valorisation through bioethanol and lignin recovery as key opportunities to further reduce production costs. © 2026 The Authors. title: A Chaos Engineering Based Simulation Method for Blockchain Consensus Protocol Reliability
abstract: The security and reliability of blockchain systems are critically dependent on their consensus mechanisms; however, a significant gap exists between theoretical design and engineering implementation in terms of security transformation and environmental adaptability. This research proposes a simulation testing methodology and implementation platform, ChaosConsensus, based on chaos engineering principles, for systematically verifying the robustness and fault tolerance of blockchain consensus protocols in complex production environments. Through proactive fault injection and abnormal behavior simulation, ChaosConsensus constructs a multilayered, cross-protocol verification environment that overcomes the limitations of traditional testing approaches, which are typically confined to unit-level testing and simplistic fault simulation. The platform is capable of providing simulation support for diverse failure scenarios that may occur across various blockchain system environments. The primary innovations of this research encompass four key aspects. First, we propose a universal hierarchical and domain-partitioned consensus fault test case framework that integrates multiple fault-tolerance model use cases. This framework exhibits two distinctive features: (1) it integrates both BFT-type and CFT-type fault tolerance models within a unified test case structure, and (2) drawing upon the upper-lower tester methodology from the international standard ISO 9646 for protocol conformance testing, it introduces a three-layer tester architecture consisting of “upper tester - inner tester - lower tester” to enhance the mapping and correspondence of test cases. This framework achievement has been further refined and incorporated into the ITU-T international standard for blockchain stability testing entitled “Stability assessment methods for distributed ledger technology platforms” (Document No. ITU-T T22-SG16–240415-TD-WP1–0258). Second, we propose a high-precision fault injection mechanism based on the message constructor and HOOK methods, which enables precise intervention in the fine-grained behaviors of consensus protocols. Third, we propose a universal multichain multiconsensus adaptation scheme decoupled from the business layer, thereby enhancing the platform’s portability and practical deployment capabilities. Fourth, we design a multidimensional simulation evaluation system incorporating both primary and secondary metrics, providing a unified benchmark for comprehensive quantitative assessment of consensus protocol fault simulation. In terms of practical applications, this solution has been tested and validated across multiple national-level financial blockchain payment systems and electricity trading blockchain systems that deploy various consensus protocols, including Dasheng, Dino, Raft, Tendermint, and HotStuff. The testing and verification were conducted in testing environments, preproduction environments (with configurations identical to production systems), and production environments. The results demonstrate that the platform is capable of discovering deep-seated issues that are difficult to detect using traditional testing methods, significantly enhancing the security and reliability of critical infrastructure and providing a valuable complement to existing blockchain system testing methodologies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Distributed Robust Control Mechanisms for Power Wireless Network Control Systems
abstract: Modern electric power systems include numerous distributed generation and energy storage devices, but the existing wireless communication network lacks the means to ensure secure and reliable access for a large number of distributed control terminals. Traditional distributed control methods assume ideal communication between distributed generators. As the power grid expands and business demands increase, the integration of 5G technology enhances the smart grid’s access and transmission capabilities. Wireless Networked Control Systems (WNCS) offer advantages over traditional control systems, such as low cost and ease of maintenance. However, wireless networks introduce inevitable issues such as delays and data loss, which can destabilize control systems. Moreover, WNCS are vulnerable to network attacks that threaten system stability if not properly monitored and mitigated. This article reviews wireless network and control models for electric power systems, proposes a control model that aims to stabilize voltage and minimize reactive power, designs a distributed robust control mechanism based on the MA-DDPG multi-agent reinforcement learning framework, and validates the effectiveness of the proposed system through simulation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: An intelligent and adaptive algorithm for reliability enhancement of an energy harvester under fractional-order control and stochastic excitation
abstract: This paper proposes an intelligent adaptive algorithm for enhancing the reliability of a tri-stable piezoelectric energy harvesting system under fractional-order proportional-integral-derivative control and Gaussian white-noise excitation. The controlled electromechanical system is reduced using an equivalent decoupling procedure and an improved stochastic averaging method. The conditional reliability function is obtained from the backward Kolmogorov equation, while the mean first-passage time is evaluated using the generalized Pontryagin equation. An adaptive particle swarm optimization method combined with a Logistic basis function neural network is then developed to solve the reliability equation and simultaneously optimize the two fractional orders. For the considered parameter set, the optimized controller increases the time-averaged reliability by 6.3% and extends the mean first-passage time by 29.2% relative to the uncontrolled case. The network solution achieves a mean error of 0.0044 compared with Monte Carlo simulations. Finally, a sensitivity analysis is discussed to assess the effects of the main algorithm parameters. The proposed algorithm provides an efficient reliability-oriented tool for the optimal fractional-order control of strongly nonlinear energy harvesting systems under random excitation. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: Konjac glucomannan-modified ferrous fumarate emulsions with interpenetrating polymer networks: Physicochemical stability, microstructure, and bioaccessibility
abstract: Ferrous fumarate (FF), a iron-rich organic fortificant, exhibits high oxidation stability; however, its poor solubility and severe sedimentation in neutral media limit bioaccessibility. This study developed an FF-loaded emulsion based on an interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) formed by whey protein concentrate (WPC), xanthan gum (XG), and konjac glucomannan (KGM). It investigated the physicochemical stability, microstructure, intermolecular interactions and iron bioaccessibility of the emulsions at different KGM concentrations. Increasing the KGM concentration reduced the emulsion particle size from 946.07 to 346.70 nm and raised the absolute zeta potential from 50.34 ± 1.17 mV to 53.34 ± 0.89 mV, thereby improving physical stability. The emulsions showed enhanced apparent viscosity with shear-thinning behavior and dominant elastic responses within the linear viscoelastic region. Microstructural analysis revealed that KGM incorporation converted a layered structure into a robust IPN architecture, confining FF near the oil–water interface and suppressing droplet aggregation. Spectroscopic results indicated strengthened intermolecular hydrogen bonding and increased β-sheet content. The incorporation of KGM effectively maintained the Fe2+ retention rate (∼95%) during thermal processing. The IPN emulsion achieved an iron bioaccessibility of 73.18%, representing an 11.86-fold increase over free FF. This study demonstrates the efficacy of IPN-structured emulsions in delivering poorly soluble active ingredients, providing a promising strategy for developing iron-fortified foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: DAIKG: Disentangled attribute interaction based on knowledge graph for fine-grained fashion preference prediction
abstract: Mass personalized customization requires translating user characteristics into design specifications. Existing graph-based methods often learn entangled representations, weakening the alignment between design attributes and user physical profiles. These challenges are further compounded by (1) data sparsity in fine-grained preference records, limiting the learning of comprehensive user profiles, and (2) imbalanced attribute distributions, which introduces bias and degrades performance on less common yet important attributes. To address these issues, we propose a Disentangled Attribute Interaction based on Knowledge Graph (DAIKG) framework for fine-grained fashion preference prediction. First, to alleviate data sparsity, we construct a multi-modal fine-grained fashion knowledge graph and employ Relational Graph Convolutional Networks (R-GCN) to capture attribute dependencies while enriching user profile-attribute representations. Second, we implement a dynamic routing mechanism to decouple attribute preferences, ensuring that requirements from distinct physical profiles are accurately represented. Finally, recognizing that attributes are not entirely independent, we incorporate a self-attention mechanism to explicitly model the interactions among these disentangled attributes, enhancing predictive accuracy. Our study evaluates the proposed framework under a profile-to-attribute prediction setting based on reconstructed user profiles derived from event-based data. Experimental results within this setting demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms adapted graph-based and recommendation baselines across multiple runs. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Adaptive reinforcement learning for medical image classification
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are widely used in medical image classification, yet their performance is often hindered by data imbalance, limited adaptability, and overfitting. This study aims to improve CNN robustness by introducing a reinforcement learning (RL) framework based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradients (DDPG) to automatically optimize data augmentation parameters. We propose an RL-driven optimization framework in which a DDPG agent autonomously adjusts data augmentation parameters to improve classification performance. The framework is evaluated across several benchmark datasets, including breast cancer, brain tumor, and COVID-19 X-ray images. Seven publicly available CNN architectures and a transformer model are used for comparison. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) using Grad-CAM is employed to validate model attention and prediction reliability. The proposed RL-based approach enables CNNs to rapidly identify optimal augmentation parameters, yielding superior performance compared to seven state-of-the-art CNN baselines and existing RL-integrated models. The DDPG agent demonstrates significant capability in automatically adapting augmentation strategies, consistently improving classification accuracy across medical. Grad-CAM visualizations further confirm improved feature focus and enhanced prediction consistency. The RL-driven DDPG framework effectively enhances image classification performance by autonomously optimizing augmentation parameters and improving CNN adaptability. Validation on multiple datasets and architectures—including transformers—shows that RL contributes to varying degrees of performance gains, establishing the proposed method as a promising direction for robust medical image analysis. The code is accessible at https://github.com/AIPMLab/DDPG. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.
