title: A Large Language Model Agent-Assisted Method for Generating Formally Verifiable Code and Its Applications in Blockchain
abstract: Protocols in blockchain systems, including consensus protocols, cryptographic algorithms, smart contract interaction protocols, and business transaction flow protocols, exist in the form of natural language documents such as research papers, standard specifications, and technical proposals during the design and specification phases. Natural language descriptions of blockchain protocols inherently suffer from ambiguity and imprecision in interpretation, which can lead to significant risks during the engineering phase due to misunderstandings or unclear descriptions. Generating formally verifiable descriptions represents a viable approach to addressing these issues. However, existing formal verification methods (taking model checking as an example) face multiple challenges. First, manually writing formally verifiable code makes it difficult to guarantee completeness and reliability. Second, the manual development of formally verifiable code is labor intensive and highly inefficient. Currently, there is a lack of formal verification (model checking) methods that can generate formally verifiable code with higher efficiency and broader applicability. Taking the model checking technical approach in formal verification as an example and addressing the demand for formally verifiable code generation for blockchain protocols, this solution proposes a large language model (LLM) agent-assisted method for generating formally verifiable code, which can significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of formally verifiable code generation for blockchain protocols. Building upon the fundamental code generation capabilities of LLM agents, this solution incorporates several innovative approaches. First, we propose an RTTF (real-time tool feedback) mechanism for optimizing and iterating formally verifiable code generation: when the LLM generates formally verifiable code for blockchain protocols, it performs self-learning and continuous optimization based on feedback from formal verification tools (such as NuSMV), thereby achieving automatic correction and refinement of the formally verifiable code. Second, through the MCP (Model Context Protocol), we implement closed-loop feedback between the LLM’s formally verifiable code generation process and the formal verification tool’s execution process. Third, to mitigate the hallucination problem inherent in single large language models, we propose a multimodel “degate” consensus mechanism for generating formally verifiable code. Compared to existing solutions, this approach can effectively enhance both the efficiency and correctness of formally verifiable code generation. Compared to existing solutions, this approach can effectively enhance the efficiency and correctness of formally verifiable code generation. The proposed method has been validated in modelling and verifying various blockchain consensus and smart contract protocols. Experimental results demonstrate substantial improvements in generation efficiency, model correctness, and verification success rates compared to traditional manual formal modelling approaches. This research provides an intelligent, automated, and practical pathway for the formal modelling and verification of blockchain protocols. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Media reach and the market reaction to negative ESG media stories: do industry affiliation and ESG performance matter?
abstract: Using an event study of U.S.-listed firms, we examine how media reach conditions the stock market reactions to adverse environmental, social, and governance (ESG) news across firms with different ESG performance and industry affiliations. On average, we find that a one-unit increase in media reach is associated with a decrease of 0.13 percentage points in cumulative abnormal returns, indicating an economically meaningful valuation effect. Further analysis shows that this effect is mainly concentrated among low-ESG firms in controversial industries. For high-ESG firms in these industries, media reach makes stock price declines significantly less severe than for low-ESG firms, indicating a media reach insurance effect. However, unless adverse news receives the highest-reach media coverage, we do not find evidence that high ESG performance provides an overall insurance effect. By identifying media reach as a key moderator, this study refines the ESG insurance hypothesis and clarifies when markets value ESG performance. © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier Inc. title: Environmental values, climate awareness and willingness to pay for green savings: The direct and moderating effect of perceived greenwashing
abstract: The transition to a low-carbon economy depends critically on mobilizing household savings toward green financial products. Using a survey experiment on a representative sample of 1061 French adults, we examine how perceived greenwashing shapes willingness to pay for a green savings account and whether environmental impact disclosures influence it. We find that individuals are, on average, unwilling to pay a premium to green their savings, and that willingness to pay does not increase when the stated environmental impact is scaled up. Perceived greenwashing plays a dual role: it directly reduces willingness to pay and moderates the relationship between pro-environmental attitudes and financial behavior. Green consumption values raise willingness to pay only when sustainability claims are perceived as credible; climate awareness follows the same pattern. When perceived greenwashing is high, these relationships become statistically insignificant, even among environmentally motivated individuals. At the individual level, willingness to pay declines with subjective financial literacy, whereas climate-related emotions play no robust role. These results suggest that impact disclosure alone is insufficient to shift household financial behavior, and that the perceived credibility of environmental claims is a necessary condition for translating pro-environmental values into green financial choices. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Teachers’ skills as a moderator in the relationship between entrepreneurial self-efficacy and entrepreneurial intention among form six students in Malaysia: A cross-sectional PLS-SEM study
abstract: Entrepreneurship is increasingly promoted as a key career pathway for future graduates; however, many students remain reluctant to pursue it. They prefer to work with someone rather than being a boss for their own business. This study explores the relationship between self-efficacy and entrepreneurial intention among Form Six students in Malaysia, emphasizing the moderating role of teachers’ skills. Using a quantitative research design, data were collected from 269 Business Studies students across Perak through structured questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). This cross-sectional survey investigates the relationship between entrepreneurial self-efficacy and entrepreneurial intention among 269 Form Six students in Perak, Malaysia. Using PLS-SEM, the study tests the moderating role of teachers’ skills. Entrepreneurial self-efficacy significantly predicts entrepreneurial intention (β = 0.651, p < 0.001). Teachers’ skills do not directly predict intention; however, the interaction term is significant (β = 0.240, p = 0.028), indicating that teachers’ skills strengthen the self-efficacy–intention relationship. The findings highlight the importance of integrating psychological empowerment with instructional competence in entrepreneurship education. The results indicate a strong and statistically significant positive relationship between self-efficacy and entrepreneurial intention. Although teachers’ skills do not have a direct effect on entrepreneurial intention, they significantly moderate the relationship between self-efficacy and entrepreneurial intention. Specifically, students with high self-efficacy are more likely to develop entrepreneurial aspirations when guided by teachers with strong pedagogical and business-related skills. These findings underscore the importance of equipping educators with the necessary competencies to strengthen entrepreneurship education. The study provides new insights into how psychological and instructional factors interact to influence students’ career choices and offers practical implications for educational institutions and policymakers aiming to cultivate entrepreneurial mindsets in pre-university education. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Progress in extraction, purification, chemical structure, bioactivities, and food preservation applications of polysaccharides from Portulaca oleracea L
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Portulaca oleracea L. is a classic medicinal–edible herb with longstanding traditional use in treating inflammatory disorders, dysentery, skin infections, and metabolic conditions such as diabetes and hyperlipidemia. Polysaccharides (POPs) are among its major bioactive macromolecules and are considered key contributors to these therapeutic effects, supporting high translational value in foods and medicines. Aim of the study: To systematically review advances in extraction–purification, structure, bioactivities, mechanisms and food preservation applications of POPs (2015–2025), and provide a theoretical basis for structure–activity research and industrial development. Materials and methods: Literature and patents were searched from CNKI, PubMed, Web of Science and patent databases using core keywords related to Portulaca oleracea, polysaccharides, extraction, purification, structure and bioactivities. Results: Among the extraction methods reviewed, ultrasonic–enzymatic extraction was associated with the highest reported yield (21.2%), while hot water extraction was noted for its low cost. Purification methods include ethanol precipitation, column chromatography and macroporous resins. POPs are classified into neutral, acidic and heteropolysaccharides; their bioactivities have been linked to medium molecular weight (104–105 Da), high galacturonic acid content, and specific glycosidic linkages. Reported signaling pathways include NF-κB and PI3K/Akt, through which POPs exert antioxidant, cardiovascular-protective, anti-inflammatory, hypoglycemic, antitumor and immunomodulatory effects in preclinical studies. They also show potential applications in edible films and natural preservatives. Conclusions: POPs have diverse structures, potent preclinical bioactivities and favorable safety profiles, making them promising functional ingredients and preservatives, though clinical evidence remains limited. Key challenges are unclear structure – activity relationships, high costs and unstable quality. Future work should clarify structure – activity links, optimize green production and expand applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Decoding market dynamics with financial knowledge graphs and cross-modal transformers
abstract: Stock trend prediction is intrinsically challenging due to stochastic volatility, information heterogeneity, and the complex coupling between explicit market signals and implicit business logic. Although recent multimodal approaches have attempted to fuse quantitative data with textual sentiment, they suffer from two fundamental limitations: (1) Shallow Integration: Simple concatenation mechanisms fail to capture the dynamic, non-linear modulation between unstructured sentiment and structured technical indicators; (2) Lack of Structural Priors: Data-driven models often struggle to understand the intrinsic transmission logic of financial risks (e.g., supply chain dependencies) underlying numerical fluctuations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel Knowledge-Aware Global Cross-Modal Interaction Network (KG-GCM). First, to bridge the semantic gap between general language models and specific market micro-sentiments, we introduce a domain-adaptive extractor leveraging FinBERT with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) and a task-specific semantic projection backbone. Second, we construct a Heterogeneous Financial Knowledge Graph (FKG) and propose a Side-Info-Aware Graph Attention Network (SI-GAT) to explicitly model the topology of capital flows and supply chains. Crucially, we design a Knowledge-Guided Contextual Gating mechanism that utilizes static graph embeddings to dynamically weigh the importance of time-varying financial reports and policy texts. Finally, these heterogeneous features are projected into a unified manifold and fused via a Global Transformer to form a holistic market state representation. To ensure robust optimization, we implement a Two-Stage Curriculum Learning strategy with differential fine-tuning. Extensive experiments on real-world A-share datasets demonstrate that our framework consistently outperforms competitive baselines under the strict point-in-time protocol. Notably, it improves directional accuracy by 5.60% while substantially elevating ranking signal stability, achieving a Rank IC of 0.057 and ICIR of 0.55, thereby providing a stable cross-sectional predictive ranking signal in complex market environments. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Conformance checking on event streams: A comprehensive survey
abstract: Event streams have become a core abstraction for building modern software systems, from cloud services and IoT deployments to cyber-physical and data-intensive applications. In such settings, developers and operators increasingly need runtime conformance monitoring: assessing whether ongoing executions comply with a prescriptive model or constraint set while decisions can still be taken. Classic offline conformance checking is ill-suited because streams are potentially unbounded, arrivals may be delayed or out of order, and monitoring must satisfy strict operational requirements, such as bounded state, low latency, and robustness to imperfect observations and evolving behaviour. This survey reviews the state of the art in online conformance checking. We derive a baseline of functional and non-functional requirements for online conformance checking and introduce a taxonomy that organises approaches across imperative, declarative, and emerging object-centric paradigms. Assessing the surveyed approaches against this baseline, we synthesise recurring design patterns and clarify the trade-offs that shape deployability on stateful stream-processing platforms. We find that existing techniques typically address only subsets of the requirements, and we identify underexplored challenges, including standardised benchmarking, principled state eviction, object-centric monitoring at scale, integrated handling of concept drift and model evolution, and unifying infrastructural robustness with expressive conformance feedback. Finally, we propose a reference architecture that maps these requirements to standard streaming operators and managed state, providing a blueprint for implementations and a concrete agenda for future research. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: An interpretable uncertainty-aware intelligent framework based on generalized multi-scale formal contexts and Bayesian deep neural networks
abstract: Modeling uncertainty and interpretability remains challenging in intelligent systems, particularly where complex decision boundaries and ambiguous feature-label relationships coexist. Although Bayesian deep neural networks (BDNNs) offer principled uncertainty quantification, they are constrained by limited prior knowledge, feature redundancy, and opacity. We propose the generalized multi-scale formal context BDNN (Λ-BDNN), an interpretable and uncertainty-aware framework. Λ-BDNN integrates formal concept analysis with Bayesian deep learning. It constructs multi-scale contexts containing conditional and decision attributes to explicitly represent information granularity while preserving semantic structures. Mutual information quantifies attribute interdependencies to enable effective feature selection and reduce redundancy. Furthermore, non-redundant decision rules are derived to filter samples and improve data quality. To enhance robustness, Bayesian optimization is employed to establish a surrogate probabilistic model for automatic hyperparameter configuration. The optimized BDNN subsequently performs intelligent classification under uncertainty-aware constraints. Experimental results on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms ten representative methods. Additionally, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are used for feature analysis; the strong consistency between SHAP and mutual information-based selection further validates the framework's interpretability, effectiveness, and applicability. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Tackling data imbalance in high-end business markets: A multi-expert capsule network approach
abstract: In the digital era, luxury businesses face a unique marketing challenge: identifying potential customers from vast user pools rather than helping users find products. This reversed recommendation scenario presents two key technical challenges: (1) the imbalance between large user pools and limited premium items and (2) the difficulty of capturing diverse user preferences with a limited set of items. We introduce MEICN-GAT (Multi-Level and Expert Interest Capsule Network with Graph Attention), a novel recommendation system designed for business-centric marketing. MEICN-GAT addresses these challenges with three key innovations: (1) a dual-layer structure that captures complex user-product relationships at multiple levels, effectively managing the user-item ratio imbalance; (2) a multi-expert system that evaluates user interests from diverse professional perspectives, alleviating data sparsity; and (3) an edge enhancement strategy that adds reliable, high-utility connections to sparse graphs. Using the luxury hotel industry as a case study, empirical evaluations on real-world datasets show that MEICN-GAT significantly outperforms existing methods in customer identification accuracy, ranking quality, and matching success rates. Although our evaluation focuses on luxury hotels in major cities, the model provides a strong foundation for business-centric marketing systems across various high-end sectors. The source code is available at https://github.com/MorrisYUJQ/MEICN-GAT. © 2026

title: Synergistic management of nitrogen budgets and non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions in China's livestock sector: A scenario-based assessment
abstract: Livestock production supplies dietary protein and supports agricultural development, but it also contributes substantially to nitrogen pollution and non-CO2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Amid growing pressures related to climate change, resource scarcity, and environmental protection, enhancing nitrogen use efficiency and curbing pollution have emerged as important objectives for the green transformation of the livestock sector. This study combined a livestock-centred coupled human and natural systems (CHANS) accounting framework, the IPCC emission-factor approach, and a spatial-equilibrium trade model to quantify provincial nitrogen budgets, non-CO2 GHG emissions, and trade-induced virtual transfers of environmental pressures in China's livestock sector from 2000 to 2024. A business-as-usual (BAU) baseline and four mitigation scenarios were developed to assess dietary adjustment, improved feed conversion efficiency, enhanced manure recycling, and their combined implementation through 2050. The results showed that total livestock-sector non-CO2 GHG emissions peaked at 546.98 Mt. CO2-eq in 2005 and subsequently declined with fluctuations to 415.59 Mt. CO2-eq in 2024. CH4 from enteric fermentation was the main non-CO2 GHG source. The livestock sector maintained a persistent nitrogen surplus, and NH3 volatilization remained the dominant nitrogen-loss pathway. Relative to BAU in 2050, dietary adjustment was projected to reduce non-CO2 GHG emissions by approximately 42%, whereas improved feed conversion efficiency and enhanced manure recycling were projected to reduce nitrogen losses by approximately 28% and 31%, respectively. The combined mitigation scenario was projected to achieve the strongest co-mitigation effect, reducing non-CO2 GHG emissions and nitrogen losses by approximately 45% and 50%, respectively. These findings suggest that coordinated dietary adjustment, feed-efficiency improvement, and manure-management optimization may offer considerable potential for synergistically reducing nitrogen losses and non-CO2 GHG emissions, providing a scientific basis for regionally differentiated, whole-chain mitigation strategies and the green transformation of China's livestock sector. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

abstract: For α>0, it is known that, among conformally invariant function spaces of index α , Hα is the only Hilbert space up to the equivalence of norms. title: On transformations of boundary value problems for functional differential equations
abstract: We present simple techniques which allow one to reduce a wide class of boundary value problems with linear conditions to initial value problems for functional differential equations with finite-dimensional perturbations. Using this approach, we formulate certain general solvability conditions of linear boundary value problems. © 2026 The Author.

title: Customer ducation in sales: A ystematic iterature eview
abstract: Customer education in sales (CEd) is an emerging research area, yet the literature remains fragmented across multiple fields with inconsistent terminology and conceptualizations. This fragmentation has hindered the development of cumulative knowledge and left fundamental questions about CEd’s effectiveness, mechanisms, and theoretical foundations unanswered. We conduct a systematic literature review of 42 journal articles, examining CEd research across four dimensions: (1) industry contexts and business settings, (2) delivery modes and their outcomes, (3) mechanisms and boundary conditions, and (4) the application of pedagogical theories. Our analysis reveals that across seven distinct delivery modes, CEd generally produces positive, sales-supporting outcomes, such as customer loyalty. Frontline interactions are the most studied mode, while formal programs show the strongest return on investment. However, significant gaps remain: B2C research predominates, direct financial outcomes are understudied, and few studies engage with pedagogical theory. We offer several avenues for future research. © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier Inc. This is an open access article under the CC BY license. http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Bound tightening guided ABB with transformer assisted search reordering for exact P-graph optimization of complex process systems
abstract: P-graph provides a graph-theoretic representation and structure-generation algorithms for process network synthesis and material scheduling, and the Accelerated Branch-and-Bound (ABB) algorithm guarantees solution exactness through the maximal structure, decision mapping, and feasibility-based pruning. However, with increasing operating-unit scale, multiple alternative material pathways, and additional constraints, conventional branching orders may incur substantial inefficient node visits. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes a Bound tightening guided ABB with transformer assisted search reordering(BTG-ABB) framework, which encodes material nodes, operating-unit nodes, search states, and bound information in the P-graph as a unified structured sequence. Rather than eliminating candidate branches, BTG-ABB advances high-scoring branches in the visiting order, enabling earlier upper-bound tightening and facilitating the subsequent pruning of low-value branches by the original ABB rules. Experimental results show that BTG-ABB reduces the number of nodes visited in the Top-10 exact search in Case 1 by approximately 18.51%. In the ethylene feedstock scheduling case, the Top-1 hit rate is improved to 77.5%, and Top-3 to Top-10 all reach 100%. BTG-ABB provides an interpretable basis for intelligent branching strategies in the synthesis of complex process systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: The relations between executive function, spatial skills, and building complexity during block play in young children
abstract: This study investigated the associations between executive function (EF), spatial skills, and both the average levels and developmental trajectories of building complexity in preschoolers during block play, across two instructional contexts. Data were drawn from a large block play intervention study that included three conditions: free play, semi-structured, and business-as-usual (BAU). Intervention included 15-minute small group sessions that occurred twice per week for eight weeks. The present sample focused on 142 preschoolers (Mage = 54 months) who were randomly assigned to the free play and semi-structured conditions. Only participants in these two conditions engaged in block-play sessions, thereby yielding data on block-building complexity. Results indicated that children in both conditions generally showed a decline in building complexity scores over the 8-week intervention. However, after the introduction of picture prompts, children in the semi-structured condition exhibited an initial decline followed by subsequent improvement in block building complexity, whereas no clear patterns were observed in the free play condition. There was a significant positive association between children’s baseline spatial skills and their average building complexity across the intervention, which aligned with the hypothesis. Marginally significant positive associations were observed between baseline aggregate EF and the developmental change of building complexity over the course of the intervention. Implications for future research are discussed. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of biomass energy carbon reduction in China
abstract: This study assesses the spatiotemporal evolution, driving mechanisms, and future potential of biomass energy carbon reduction (BCR) in China using data for 31 mainland provincial-level units and a balanced 30-province analytical sample from 2012 to 2022, with projections to 2030. BCR is defined as the theoretical CO2 reduction from replacing coal-fired electricity with energy recovered from agricultural residues, forestry and orchard waste, livestock manure, sewage-derived organic matter, and municipal solid waste; it is not a project-level life-cycle estimate. Biomass-resource accounting was integrated with Moran's I, standard deviational ellipses, fixed-effects STIRPAT, spatial dynamic panel models, Random Forest with PDP/SHAP, and province-specific GA-LSTM forecasting. Results show significant positive spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I = 0.143–0.193, p < 0.05) and a northeast-to-southwest centroid shift. Population scale and energy consumption structure show significant positive linear associations (coefficients 0.66 and 1.05, p < 0.01), whereas environmental regulation and industrial structure show negative associations. Random Forest achieved R2 = 0.844, RMSE = 13.98 Mt CO2, and MAE = 6.43 Mt CO2; population scale (38.25%) and environmental regulation (30.59%) were the leading predictors, with nonlinear and threshold-like responses. Spatial dynamic estimates confirm path dependence (0.103) and cross-provincial spillovers. GA-LSTM projects aggregate BCR to increase from 1.854 Gt CO2 in 2023 to 2.092 Gt CO2 in 2030, led by Heilongjiang, Henan, and Shandong. These findings support differentiated infrastructure investment, cross-regional logistics, regulatory coordination, and technology transfer. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: How does blockchain address breach of contract issues in transactions?
abstract: Blockchain, as an emerging technology, facilitates transactions in supply chain finance. This paper explores how blockchain addresses the information asymmetry between contracting parties before and after contract signing, thereby resolving corporate breach of contract issues. We conducted a two-stage game evolution analysis, demonstrating that under the blockchain model, when the marginal profit of information sharing is greater than zero and with the costs of concealing corporate breaches are high or the benefits derived from such breaches are diminished, both parties will adopt a strategy of fully sharing information and fully performing contracts. Furthermore, through empirical analysis, we emphasize the average positive effect of blockchain use in improving corporate breach of contract issues. Additionally, the heterogeneity analysis in this paper indicates that the internal factor of a company’s life cycle and external factors such as the company’s competitive intensity and media attention, respectively, influence the company’s default by affecting the completeness of information transmission, the benefits of default, and the costs of concealing a default. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: ID-free STFormer: An identity-free spatio-temporal transformer for day-ahead EV charging demand forecasting
abstract: Day-ahead electric vehicle (EV) charging demand forecasting at the traffic analysis zone (TAZ) level is challenging owing to strong spatial heterogeneity and long-tailed demand distributions. Existing models commonly use node-identity embeddings to represent spatial heterogeneity; however, their direct injection into predictive representations may encourage location-specific memorization and local overfitting under long-tailed demand. We propose the Identity-Free Spatio-Temporal Transformer (ID-Free STFormer), which excludes explicit node-ID embeddings from the temporal forecasting representation while retaining spatial adaptation through graph-based feature aggregation. The model combines a fixed physical graph for local proximity, an adaptive graph for global context, and a Transformer-GRU module for 168-h-input to 24-h-ahead forecasting. Experiments on the UrbanEV dataset covering 275 TAZs in Shenzhen show that ID-Free STFormer achieves the lowest root mean square error (RMSE) and the highest coefficient of determination R2=0.91, reducing RMSE by 15.7% over the strongest graph-based baseline. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of ID-free modeling for peak-sensitive forecasting on fixed urban TAZ networks and motivate further validation across cities and unseen regions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: HyITS: Interpretable tree-stacking framework via feature selection and hybrid resampling for imbalanced fraud detection
abstract: Fraud detection in medical reimbursement claims and credit card transactions is challenged by high-dimensional feature spaces, extreme class imbalance, and limited interpretability of ensemble decisions. This paper presents HyITS, an interpretable tree-stacking framework for imbalanced fraud detection. HyITS comprises three stages: (1) importance-guided feature selection with sample rebalancing to compress the feature space and alleviate class imbalance; (2) a two-layer tree-stacking ensemble to enhance minority-class recognition; and (3) a hierarchical SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) post-hoc analysis to attribute predictions at both the base-learner and meta-learner levels. Extensive experiments on two highly imbalanced fraud datasets—a public benchmark and a real-world business case—demonstrate that HyITS consistently outperforms a range of state-of-the-art and representative baseline methods. Specifically, it achieves a remarkable reduction in feature dimensionality (approximately 43.3% and 59.4%, respectively) while setting new benchmarks in imbalance-sensitive metrics: on the public benchmark, AUPRC reaches 0.9375 and the F1-score attains 0.9178; on the real-world dataset, AUPRC is 0.9988 and the F1-score is 0.9689, indicating robust performance across scenarios. The SHAP analysis further identifies key risk-related features and their influence patterns, thereby significantly enhancing model auditability and providing actionable insights for decision-makers in high-stakes financial and healthcare applications. © 2026 The Authors. title: Efficient nonconvex low-rank tensor recovery with a new t-fraction function penalty
abstract: In recent years, low-rank tensor recovery has become an essential technique in computer vision and machine learning with many important applications, such as color image denoising, video recovery, and subspace clustering. Existing approaches typically leverage convex or nonconvex surrogates to approximate the intractable tensor rank. However, many of these methods treat rank components uniformly, neglecting their differential structural importance and thus leading to suboptimal reconstruction. To alleviate this issue, in this paper we propose a novel nonconvex fractional function that serves as a tighter and more adaptive surrogate for the tensor multi-rank. Unlike existing weighted schemes, the proposed function facilitates adaptive penalization of singular values without the need for heuristic weight assignment. With it, a principled low-rank minimization model is formulated to more faithfully characterize the intrinsic low-rank structures of tensors. Meanwhile, we develop an efficient algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), where each subproblem admits an analytical closed-form solution. Moreover, the convergence of the proposed algorithm is rigorously established through theoretical analysis. Extensive experimental results on both synthetic and real-world data demonstrate that our method achieves significant advantages over several state-of-the-art low-rank tensor recovery methods. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: The Impacts on Malaysia’s Logistics, Ports and Shipping Companies in the COVID-19 Pandemic Situation
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic affected global economics, and this economic shock has impacted logistics, ports, and shipping businesses. One of the measures introduced to curb the pandemic with implementation of quarantine that imposed by authorities, limiting the movement of people. This measure affected the operation of logistics ports and the shipping business. Quarantine measures resulted in a decrease in demand for cargoes, directly affecting the demand for logistics services, ports experiencing plunges in container throughput and shipping companies experiencing a reduction in chartering. The pandemic directly affected the performance of logistics, ports and shipping companies and the intention of this research is to rank the performance of Malaysia’s logistics, ports, and shipping companies before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. Conducting this research, it helps to evaluate and understand the impact of the pandemic on these companies’ performance. This research has identified eleven companies listed in Bursa Malaysia that are involved in logistics, ports, and shipping activities. Financial reports from each of these companies were gathered from 2017 to 2021. Data from these financial reports is then separated between the period before COVID-19, from 2017 to 2019, and the period of COVID-19 from 2020 to 2021. Eight financial ratios were identified for evaluation, consisting of current ratios, net profit margin, return on assets, total assets turnover, current assets turnover, debt to asset ratio, debt to equity ratio, and return on equity. The technique of order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS) method has been utilised to rank the performance by using these eight financial ratios. Results of the ranking indicate that port operating companies were among top performer companies compared to shipping companies in the period before COVID-19 and during COVID-19. It also found that logistics companies that were involved with consumer logistics performed better compared to companies involved with project logistics within both periods. It was found that shipping companies were not performing in ranking compared to logistics and port companies. This research also found that shipping companies involved in the oil and gas energy sector performed better compared to those in other sectors. Future research is recommended to study the effect of Malaysia’s logistics, ports, and shipping companies in regard to the post-COVID-19 pandemic. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Mechanistic insights into KOH activation temperature for enhanced electrochemical performance of ammonolysis-pretreated lignite-derived carbon
abstract: Lignite is an abundant and low-cost carbon precursor for sustainable energy storage, yet its direct carbonization yields materials with limited porosity and electrochemical activity. In this work, a two-step strategy combining ammonolysis pretreatment with temperature-controlled KOH activation was proposed to convert lignite into high-performance electrode materials, focusing on the mechanistic role of activation temperature. The results demonstrated that the activation temperature critically modulates the hierarchical pore architecture, nitrogen configuration, defect density, and graphitic ordering. At lower temperatures (400–500 °C), KOH predominantly reacts with oxygen-containing functional groups, generating micropores while preserving abundant heteroatoms and defects, which contribute to pronounced pseudocapacitance. In contrast, higher temperatures (600–900 °C) promote metallic potassium intercalation and carbon skeleton etching, facilitating the formation of a hierarchical porous network alongside enhanced graphitization, thereby favoring electric double-layer capacitance. Optimal performance is achieved at 500 °C, which features a well-balanced hierarchical pore structure, obvious carbon detects, and high nitrogen and oxygen content (1.6 and 30.6 at. %) enriched in electrochemically active pyridinic-N and pyrrolic-N. Consequently, KCSPN‑5 delivers a high specific capacitance of 320.4F/g at 0.5 A/g in a three‑electrode system, with excellent rate capability (61.4 % at 100 A/g) and outstanding cycling stability (93.1 % after 10,000 cycles). Kinetic analysis reveals a mixed charge storage mechanism with a b‑value of 0.742, confirming the synergistic contributions of surface‑controlled pseudocapacitance and diffusion‑controlled processes. This work establishes a rational temperature-guided activation protocol for upgrading lignite into high-value carbons and provides fundamental insights into the temperature-dependent interplay among porosity, defects, and heteroatom doping. title: Cascading failure and robustness in supply chain networks: A case study of new energy vehicles
abstract: The increasing complexity and vulnerability of new energy vehicle supply chain networks (NEVSNs) pose significant challenges to sustaining industrial robustness and mitigating cascading risks. This study evaluates the robustness of NEVSNs under multi-source disturbances, emphasizing the interactive roles of innovation capability, resource dependence, and network heterogeneity in collectively enhancing supply chain robustness. A dynamic four-layer directed weighted network model is developed to integrate these factors, incorporating a load-capacity interaction mechanism and probabilistic node failure to simulate cascading disruptions. Empirical data from Chinese NEV manufacturers and core suppliers are used for calibration and validation. Simulation results reveal that (1) enhancing innovation improves network efficiency and redundancy, while high resource dependence and centralization increase fragility; (2) battery and critical component suppliers are most sensitive to shocks, while network resilience is strengthened by diversified resources and collaboration; and (3) the proposed robustness metrics better capture vulnerability and recovery than conventional measures. These findings offer insights and recommendations for risk mitigation, network optimization, and robustness enhancement in NEV supply chains. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Multi-output stability prediction of salt cavern energy storage using optimized machine learning model with interpretable features
abstract: Salt cavern stability prediction is essential for the safe operation and risk prevention of underground energy-storage systems. In this study, a multi-output machine learning framework was developed to simultaneously predict maximum wall displacement (MD) and volume reduction rate (RV) of salt caverns. Fifteen machine learning algorithms were first compared using the Friedman test and Nemenyi post-hoc test, and multi-layer perceptron (MLP) was selected as the optimal base learner. Subsequently, four metaheuristic algorithms, including Jellyfish Search Optimizer (JSO), Tunicate Swarm Algorithm (TSA), Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), were used to optimize the MLP hyperparameters. The results show that JSO-MLP provides the best overall performance. For MD prediction, the R2 values of the training and test sets are 0.9937 and 0.9854, respectively; for RV prediction, the corresponding R2 values are 0.9711 and 0.9606. Furthermore, Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis indicates that MD is mainly influenced by cavern depth (CD), low operational pressure (LP), years of operation (t), and stress exponent (n), whereas RV is mainly affected by CD, LP, t , and high operational pressure (HP). These results demonstrate that the proposed JSO-MLP framework can provide an accurate and interpretable tool for salt cavern stability assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Development, CT characterization, and IAEA TECDOC-1583-based dosimetric evaluation of a low-cost heterogeneous thoracic phantom for radiotherapy TPS quality assurance
abstract: Background and Purpose : Accurate verification of treatment planning systems (TPS) dose calculations in heterogeneous media is essential for radiotherapy quality assurance (QA). However, commercial heterogeneous phantoms are often inaccessible in resource-limited settings. This study aimed to design, fabricate, and dosimetrically validate a low-cost heterogeneous phantom using locally sourced surrogate materials and to compare selected measurements with a commercial CIRS IMRT Thorax Phantom. Materials and methods A semi-elliptical phantom measuring approximately 30 × 20 × 23 cm3 was fabricated using paraffin wax as the bulk soft-tissue-equivalent material with embedded particleboard, bovine tibia, and Styrofoam inserts representing adipose, bone, and lung-equivalent regions, respectively. The fabricated and CIRS phantoms were scanned using a 120 kVp CT simulator, and material HU values, mass densities, and electron densities were characterized. Treatment plans were generated in Eclipse using the Anisotropic Analytical Algorithm with a 2.5 mm calculation grid. The fabricated phantom was evaluated using the complete IAEA TECDOC-1583 test matrix, comprising 8 test cases and 14 measurement points. In addition, selected comparative measurements were performed using a commercial CIRS phantom for representative open-field and RapidArc cases at two measurement positions. Absolute point-dose measurements were performed using calibrated ionization chambers with temperature-pressure, polarity, and ion-recombination corrections. Results Paraffin wax and bovine tibia showed reasonable agreement with soft-tissue and bone reference values, respectively. Styrofoam approximated the low-density behavior of the CIRS lung insert but was substantially less dense than average human lung. Electrometer readings across the TECDOC-1583 points ranged from 18.92 to 21.26 nC. Ten of 14 measurement points met the predefined agreement criterion, with the largest deviations of approximately 8%. Selected CIRS phantom measurements for open-field and RapidArc deliveries remained within ±5%. However, because the commercial CIRS phantom was tested only for selected cases, the comparison with CIRS should be interpreted as supportive rather than comprehensive benchmarking. Conclusion The fabricated phantom provides a practical low-cost platform for preliminary heterogeneous TPS QA and demonstrated acceptable agreement for most tested conditions. Larger deviations in low-density or heterogeneous regions indicate the need for improved lung-equivalent material selection, detailed uncertainty analysis, and further validation using advanced dose algorithms and two-dimensional dosimetry. With further refinement and validation, the phantom could provide an accessible option for heterogeneity-focused TPS verification in radiotherapy centers with limited access to commercial phantoms. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Multimodal cross-domain recommender systems using image–text fusion: A gated contrastive approach for scalable service computing
abstract: Cross-domain recommender systems (CDRS) mitigate data sparsity and cold-start problems by transferring preference knowledge between information-rich source domains and data-scarce target domains. However, most existing CDRS methods depend exclusively on interaction signals or on a single content modality, neglecting the complementary information carried by item imagery and textual descriptions. In this paper, we propose MIT-CDRec, a multimodal cross-domain recommendation framework that (i) integrates frozen CLIP-ViT visual embeddings and BERT textual embeddings through a novel Cross-Modal Gated Fusion (CMGF) module that learns per-item modality weights; (ii) projects fused representations into a shared domain-invariant latent space via a weight-tied multilayer perceptron; and (iii) aligns cross-domain representations of overlapping users with an InfoNCE contrastive objective. We evaluate MIT-CDRec on three Amazon cross-domain benchmarks (Books↔Movies, Clothing→Sports) against eight strong baselines spanning single-domain, classical CDR, graph-based, sequential, and LLM-augmented families. Under a leave-one-out evaluation protocol with 99 sampled negatives, MIT-CDRec achieves the best results among the compared methods on every benchmark, achieving an average improvement of 8.26% in Recall@10 and 10.87% in NDCG@10 over the strongest prior baseline, with all gains statistically significant at p<0.01 across five seeds. We further provide a theoretical account of why the method transfers stably, bounding the target-domain error through an HΔH-divergence argument and showing empirically that the contrastive objective halves the cross-domain discrepancy. Beyond accuracy, we evaluate robustness to feature noise, interaction noise, and missing modalities, extend the study to multi-domain transfer, and report beyond-accuracy metrics, including diversity, novelty, coverage, and exposure fairness, on all of which MIT-CDRec improves over the strongest baseline. We further strengthen the analysis with a transfer-specific account of why per-item gating reduces cross-domain divergence, a geometric treatment of the contrastive objective, and new studies of partial/zero user overlap, encoder provenance (pretrained vs. random vs. domain-adapted), and industrial-scale caching and synchronization cost. These results show that principled multimodal fusion combined with domain-invariant contrastive alignment is a robust approach for scalable cross-domain recommender systems. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: A predictive–prescriptive framework for operating room scheduling: Transformer-based duration estimation and system-coupled robust multi-resource optimization
abstract: Operating room scheduling (ORS) is complicated by uncertain surgical durations, downstream recovery limitations, and workforce constraints. This study develops a two-phase predictive–prescriptive decision-support framework (DSF) for tactical perioperative planning. In Phase I, heterogeneous clinical, procedural, and provider information is integrated within a Transformer-based regression model using fixed BioBERT-derived diagnostic representations. The resulting out-of-fold predictions and empirical residual distribution are used to construct residual-calibrated duration bounds, thereby creating a data-driven connection between prediction uncertainty and scheduling decisions. In Phase II, these inputs are transferred to a mixed-integer convex quadratic System-Coupled Robust Operating Room Scheduling (SC-ORS) model that coordinates OR utilization, daily aggregate PACU capacity, surgeon availability, and workload balance. The complete predictive pipeline outperforms the selected machine-learning (ML) benchmarks under leakage-controlled cross-validation, while the residual-based intervals provide internally calibrated uncertainty information for the optimization phase. Computational experiments show that SC-ORS can reduce realized overtime exposure under several moderately constrained conditions, identify emerging PACU bottlenecks, and support schedule adjustments under limited surgeon availability disruptions. The results also reveal that the value of robustness depends on the demand-to-capacity ratio and on managerial preferences regarding OR utilization, downstream capacity, and workload balance. The proposed framework contributes primarily through the explicit integration of heterogeneous surgical-duration prediction, residual-calibrated uncertainty, and multi-resource tactical optimization. It provides a structured basis for moving from OR-centric planning toward coordinated perioperative decision support, while hospital-specific calibration, intra-day sequencing, and prospective validation remain necessary before operational deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Succinic acid production from pineapple-derived waste within a biorefinery framework: A review of technological approaches, process integration, and technology readiness
abstract: The industrial scale production of succinic acid remains constrained by feedstock availability, process integration challenges, and immaturity of upstream and downstream processes. Among emerging lignocellulosic resources, pineapple waste represents a promising feedstock for succinic acid production due to its renewable nature, abundance, favorable economic potential, and high cellulose and polysaccharide content. However, studies on the utilization of pineapple waste as a feedstock for succinic acid production are still very limited. This study aims to present a comprehensive summary of recent technological approaches for succinic acid production from pineapple waste to assess their potential for future implementation. This study commences by providing an overview of succinic acid production, both through chemical and biological conversion. Additionally, an overview of pineapple waste, including national and global production data, is provided. Furthermore, this study critically examined the challenges and opportunities associated with the current technology regarding the succinic acid production, covering the entire process chain from upstream to the downstream. This analysis is conducted based on the technology readiness level (TRL) to identify significant deficiencies in the transition of laboratory-scale development to industrial implementation. Through this study, it is expected to provide guidance for advancing succinic acid production technologies for large scale industrial applications, with a specific emphasis on utilizing pineapple waste. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Alleviating gradient conflict via bias disentanglement and noise suppression for robust autoencoder recommendation
abstract: Autoencoders have been widely adopted in recommender systems due to their strong nonlinear representation capability. However, the global shared encoder parameters often lead to gradient conflicts in the parameter space when faced with heterogeneous rating samples, which undermines the training stability and personalized modeling capability of the model. To address this issue, we propose an improved autoencoder-based recommendation method integrating bias disentanglement and noise suppression. Specifically, the observed ratings are decomposed into rating bias and personalized residual preferences through bias disentanglement, thereby reducing the interference of rating bias on the update of encoder parameters. Additionally, a diffusion model is introduced to denoise rating bias, suppress the negative impact of noise on the training process, and enhance the model’s robustness. Extensive experimental results on three public datasets demonstrate that our model significantly alleviates gradient conflicts and, compared with all baseline methods, achieves average improvements of 7.95% and 7.72% in Precision@5 and NDCG@5, respectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Time-accurate and highly-stable explicit two-step Runge-Kutta methods for stiff differential equations
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the Time-accurate and highly-stable explicit two-step Runge-Kutta methods (TASE-TSRK) for solving stiff ordinary differential equations, inspired by the technique presented in Calvo et al. [1]. The objective of the methods is to improve the stability characteristics of explicit TSRK methods by pre-multiplying the vector field with a suitable TASE operator. In this work, the related order conditions are analyzed, and then a complete study of stability properties is carried out for TASE-TSRK methods with order k ≤ 4. By appropriately selecting the free parameters of the TASE operator family, we demonstrate that the 2nd-order method is strongly A-stable, the 3rd-order and 4th-order methods can be nearly strongly A-stable. Some numerical experiments are performed to show that the new TASE-TSRK schemes are competitive with TSRK methods and potentially more advantageous for stiff problems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Clickstream user behavior clustering using graph time series
abstract: Introduction: Internet banking has become the primary channel for many customer interactions with financial institutions. The availability of banking services via internet banking platforms has presented new organizational challenges for financial institutions, necessitating adaptation and the creation of new strategies to enhance customer engagement on these platforms. Objective: This paper proposes a model to characterize user behavior when using an internet banking solution through time series analysis. Two specific objectives were achieved: (1) grouping customers with similar behavioral patterns associated with clickstreams (sequences of user interactions with the application) across different time series, and (2) identifying customer profiles related to the use of a specific service offered by the banking institution (checking account). Methods: A dataset with 500 million clickstream records from 2.4 million users was used. Unsupervised techniques and complex networks were employed to perform time series clustering based on the similarity of subsequences of clickstreams. Results: Users were segmented into 89 clusters that exhibited distinct behavioral profiles when using the banking services available on the institution's internet banking platform. An interactive web tool was developed to support data analysis. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: The Symmetric and Asymmetric Impacts of Foreign Capital Inflows and Trade Openness on Africa’s Economic Growth: Evidence from Linear and Nonlinear Panel ARDL Models
abstract: This study investigates the symmetric and asymmetric impacts of foreign capital inflows and trade openness on economic growth in 37 African countries from 2000 to 2021 using linear and nonlinear panel autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) models. To examine the dynamic panel threshold effect, the study employed dynamic panel threshold estimation for each of the independent variables. The results indicated that trade openness, foreign direct investment, and official development assistance have significant threshold levels at 24.24%, 23.44%, and 23.21%, respectively. This suggests that the effects of foreign capital inflows and trade openness operate across two regimes—base and high—defined by these thresholds. Comparative analysis of symmetric and asymmetric effects without threshold considerations showed that trade openness consistently exerts positive long- and short-term influences on economic growth, both symmetrically and asymmetrically. Conversely, foreign direct investment (FDI) does not demonstrate a significant symmetric effect but exhibits an asymmetric long-term impact on growth. Additionally, official development assistance (ODA) shows an asymmetric effect that surpasses its symmetric influence on economic growth, highlighting the vulnerability of African economies to financial shocks. Negative shocks in the interaction between FDI and ODA have a more pronounced effect on growth than positive shocks. In the long run, variables such as capital, the globalization index, and political stability positively and significantly impact economic growth, while the labor force has a negative effect. Overall, the findings underscore the importance of creating policy environments that strengthen the capacity to absorb foreign capital, manage trade openness effectively, and coordinate aid and investment policies to foster sustainable economic growth across Africa. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Convergence of Implicit Gradient Descent for Training Two-Layer Physics-Informed Neural Networks
abstract: The optimization algorithms are crucial in training physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), as unsuitable methods may lead to poor solutions. Compared to the common gradient descent (GD) algorithm, implicit gradient descent (IGD) outperforms it in handling certain multi-scale problems. In this paper, we provide convergence analysis for the IGD in training over-parameterized two-layer PINNs. We first derive the training dynamics of IGD in training two-layer PINNs. Then, over-parameterization allows us to prove that the randomly initialized IGD converges to a globally optimal solution at a linear convergence rate. Moreover, due to the distinct training dynamics of IGD compared to GD, the learning rate can be selected independently of the sample size and the least eigenvalue of the Gram matrix. Additionally, the novel approach used in our convergence analysis imposes a milder requirement on the network width. Finally, empirical results validate our theoretical findings. ©2027 Global-Science Press

title: Humans Shaping a Landscape - Ethnobiology, Hunting Traditions, and Wildlife Conservation of Diverse Language Communities in the Indus Kohistan, Pakistan
abstract: Wild fauna has been hunted by humans for many purposes, including meat consumption, sport, ornamentation, and traditional medicine. Hunting, especially for meat, remains widespread across the Himalayan region, yet ethnozoological hunting practices in the Kohistan region of the Hindu Kush–Himalaya remain poorly documented. We gathered data from five linguistic communities, i.e. Shina Kohistani, Indus Kohistani, Gujjari, Pashto, and Batteri Kohistani, using semi-structured questionnaires, complemented by direct observations. Hierarchical cluster analysis and ordination techniques were used to analyze the data. The local fauna was utilized for multiple purposes, including zootherapy, food, culture, decoration, and recreation. Meat was the most frequently utilized animal part, while the most treated health conditions were sexual dysfunction, respiratory diseases, and skin diseases. Our cross-cultural analysis showed that the Gujjari, Shina Kohistani, and Indus Kohistani groups exhibited the highest similarity in fauna use (14% overlap), potentially reflecting their seasonal migration and geographic interactions. The least overlap (3%) was observed between Gujjari and Batteri groups, consistent with their limited seasonal interaction and narrower shared geographic range. The study identified six culturally associated indicator species across the five linguistic groups, highlighting taxa that may warrant attention in community-based conservation initiatives. In Shina Kohistani and Indus Kohistani, Capra falconeri and Lophophorus impejanus had significant indicator values (p ≤ 0.05) across both communities. In the Gujjari linguistic group, Capra sibirica and Moschus leucogaster were indicator species. Columba livia and Nemorhaedus goral were indicator species for the Pashto and Batteri linguistic groups, respectively. Common hunting methods included 12-bore repeater shotguns (chari), snares (kurki), pit traps (Dhoko), and netting (Jal). Most species (43%) were hunted occasionally, 30% commonly, and 27% rarely. Our study indicates that linguistic and cultural differences are associated with distinct patterns of wildlife use across the Kohistan region. With the development of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), associated socioeconomic changes may affect traditional knowledge and biocultural relationships in the region. To our knowledge, this is the first cross-cultural ethnozoological assessment of these communities and provides baseline information for conservation and sustainable-development planning, with potential relevance for protecting wild fauna, traditional knowledge, and cultural heritage. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: From AI use to AI capability: Developing responsible, reflective and employable learners in management education
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has entered management education faster than many business schools have redesigned pedagogy, assessment, and employability development. This study examines how management students’ AI use can be transformed into responsible, reflective, and employable AI capabilities. Using a pre- and post-intervention design with 412 management students across two comparable course sections, the study compared a conventional AI access condition with a guided AI capability condition. The guided condition included four pedagogical modules on task alignment, evidence verification, responsible reflection, and employability translation. Data was collected through survey measures, AI use logs, reflective journals, rubric-based project assessment, and structural equation modelling. The results show that the guided group achieved substantially higher gains in task-aligned AI use, responsible reflection, AI capability, and employability confidence. Project performance data confirmed this pattern, with the largest difference in ethical awareness between the two groups. The structural model shows that AI readiness does not directly influence employability confidence. Instead, readiness influences confidence through task-aligned use, responsible reflection, and AI capability. This study contributes by shifting attention from AI adoption to AI capability and by positioning responsible reflection as the key mechanism through which AI use becomes learning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Unpacking the effects of pro-environmental attitudes on green eWOM from a big data– and LLM-driven perspective: moderating roles of product characteristics
abstract: As consumers become more concerned about sustainable development, they increasingly share electronic Word-of-Mouth (eWOM) about products and services’ sustainability practices and environmental impacts. However, little research has investigated the drivers of green eWOM and their interactive effects with the product’s multi-dimensional characteristics. Grounded in attitude-behavior-context and theory, this study examines the effect of pro-environmental attitudes on green eWOM leveraging big data (512826 consumer reviews across 2000+ beauty products) and large language models. This study further investigates the moderating roles of the product’s internal characteristic (environmental disclosure) and the product’s external characteristic (popularity). The findings reveal that pro-environmental attitudes positively influence green eWOM behavior, while this positive effect is weakened by product environmental disclosure and popularity. This research contributes to the nascent green eWOM literature, with implications for digital marketing and sustainability strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Exploring generation Z nurses' experiences of shift work in intensive care units: A qualitative analysis
abstract: Objectives: Generation Z nurses are entering the workforce with distinct expectations regarding work–life balance, professional recognition, and organisational support. Intensive Care Units (ICUs), characterised by rotating and night shifts, are associated with significant psychophysical and organisational demands. This study explored how Generation Z nurses perceive and manage ICU shift work and its impact on well-being, coping strategies, professional integration, and career sustainability. Methods: A qualitative interpretative descriptive study was conducted in ICUs of a tertiary-care academic hospital in northeastern Italy. Thirty Generation Z nurses working rotating 24-h shifts participated (mean age 25.2 years; mean ICU experience 1.7 years). Semi-structured interviews were conducted between June and September 2025, audio-recorded, and transcribed verbatim. Data were analysed inductively using Braun and Clarke's thematic analysis. Coding was performed independently by two researchers and refined through team-based analytic discussion and consensus. Results: Three themes emerged: (1) Experiencing psychophysical imbalance; (2) Seeking stability in an unstable context; and (3) Navigating professional identity. Participants described fatigue, circadian disruption, sleep disturbances, and anticipatory anxiety related to shift work. Nurses adopted coping strategies including structured routines, emotional regulation, and digital boundary-setting. Peer support facilitated professional adaptation and resilience. However, limited organisational recognition, communication barriers, and perceived undervaluation of competencies contributed to disillusionment and uncertainty about future career development. Participants questioned the long-term sustainability of shift work and considered pursuing further education or alternative career pathways. Conclusions: Generation Z nurses experience ICU shift work as demanding and potentially unsustainable early in their careers. Organisational recognition, supportive leadership, and structured transition processes appear important to promote well-being, professional integration, and workforce retention. Implications for clinical practice: These findings highlight the need for supportive leadership practices, mentorship programmes, and structured transition pathways to support the well-being, professional development, and retention of Generation Z nurses in ICUs. © 2026 The Authors. title: Co-creation in sustainable family entrepreneurship
abstract: This study examines how co-creation unfolds in sustainable family entrepreneurship across nine co-creation cases in two family firms in Mexico and Colombia. Drawing on family embeddedness and entrepreneurial co-creation, we show that sustainable family entrepreneurship emerges through a relational process in which family and non-family actors negotiate sustainability meanings, organise participation and control, and generate outcomes over time. The findings identify three aggregate dimensions of sustainable family co-creation: family sustainable drivers and motivations, family sustainable management and control, and family co-created sustainable outcomes. These dimensions operate through six mechanisms: generating a shared view, conveying different interpretations, family coupling, family decoupling, family inclusion, and family separation. The study contributes to family entrepreneurship research by explaining how family embeddedness influences entrepreneurial action through evolving forms of family engagement. © 2026 The Authors. title: To show or not to show? how human vs. digital entrepreneur streamers shape brand attitudes through trust mechanisms
abstract: Live streaming is reshaping business development, with entrepreneur live streaming emerging as a prominent trend. Despite the growing impact of digital human entrepreneurs, the effects of varying live streamer types on consumer outcomes remain underexplored. This study investigates how entrepreneur live streamer typologies (Real human vs. Digital human) and influence levels (High vs. Low) interact to affect brand attitudes. Grounded in non-evaluative meaning transfer theory and the ELM, we identify distinct mechanisms through which different streamer characteristics enhance brand attitudes. Analyzing 7,631 social media comments and conducting two situational experimental studies (N = 1004), we provide empirical support for our hypotheses. The results indicate that high-influence real-human entrepreneurs boost brand appeal by fostering affective trust, while low-influence digital entrepreneurs enhance communication effectiveness by strengthening cognitive trust. This research broadens the understanding of the live streaming ecosystem and offers insights for businesses to develop strategies optimizing entrepreneur live streaming effectiveness. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: When AI ads backfire: Deconstructing consumer backlash to GenAI advertising
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is moving from back-end support into the creative core of advertising, raising questions about how consumers respond when brands use GenAI for visible, consumer-facing content. This study investigates the consumer backlash to GenAI advertising by analyzing 7822 YouTube and Reddit comments on Coca-Cola's AI-generated remake of its iconic Holidays Are Coming campaign. Using large-scale data collection and a LLM-assisted, researcher-validated thematic analysis, we identify a three-dimensional pattern of aversion against GenAI ads, which we organize as the CPS (Content–Psychological–Socio-ethical) framework. The framework consists of content-related judgments focused on visual realism, execution quality, and contextual fit; psychological reactions centered on authenticity, creativity, and human connection; and socio-ethical attributions involving corporate motives, labor displacement, and broader ethical concerns. The findings demonstrate that backlash against GenAI ads emerges not only from perceived inferiority to human work, but also from what the use of GenAI signals to consumers about a brand's values and intentions. Built on real-world consumer discourse from a GenAI-enabled ad campaign, the CPS framework empirically grounds how backlash develops along the three dimensions. For practitioners, the framework offers a diagnostic tool to anticipate potential backlash from using GenAI in ads. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Mesoporous nanoreactor with accelerated ion transport for high-performance SnO2-based anodes in sodium-ion batteries
abstract: Tin dioxide (SnO2) is a promising anode material for sodium-ion batteries owing to its high theoretical capacity, yet its practical application is severely hindered by drastic volume expansion and intrinsically sluggish Na+ diffusion kinetics. Herein, we report a mesoporous yolk–shell SnO2-based nanoreactor (SnO2 mCNR) constructed via a facile interfacial polymerization assembly and selective etching strategy. The architecture features a SnO2 nanocube core, an internal void space, and a mesoporous carbon shell permeated with interconnected channels (∼7 nm). This unique design simultaneously accommodates the large volume changes during sodiation/desodiation and provides low-resistance pathways for rapid Na+ transport. Compared with its non-porous counterpart (SnO2 CNR), SnO2 mCNR exhibits a ∼ 3.5-fold higher Na+ diffusion coefficient and a transition toward pseudocapacitive-dominated charge storage (b-value of 0.90). Consequently, SnO2 mCNR delivers a high reversible capacity of 650.3 mAh g−1 at 0.05 A g−1, excellent rate capability (218.7 mAh g−1 at 5 A g−1), and outstanding cycling stability with 95.1% capacity retention over 1800 cycles at 1 A g−1. A full pouch cell assembled with a Na3V2(PO4)3-based cathode achieves a high energy density of 292.2 Wh kg−1, indicating promising application potential at the electrode-material level. This work establishes shell porosity engineering as a generalizable design principle for high-performance conversion/alloying-type anodes in sodium-ion batteries. © 2026

title: Procurement performance-based project success estimation and management strategy using symbiotic-attention sequential learning
abstract: In the construction industry, procurement processes influence approximately 80% of a project’s value and directly affect key outcomes such as cost, schedule, and quality. However, existing research typically focuses on isolated procurement tasks (e.g., cost estimation or supplier evaluation), with limited attention to linking real-time procurement performance to overall project success. Inefficiencies in procurement frequently lead to delays, cost overruns, and quality issues, highlighting the need for advanced predictive tools. This study develops a Procurement Performance-Based Project Success Prediction (PP-BPSP) model to preemptively estimate project success based on ongoing procurement performance. The proposed model employs a Symbiotic-Attention Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (SABiGRU), which integrates bidirectional sequence learning with a self-attention mechanism and is optimized using the Symbiotic Organisms Search (SOS) algorithm. The model analyzes procurement metrics such as contract price variance, delivery performance, quantity sufficiency, and material quality to predict key project outcomes. The main contributions include: (1) developing a SABiGRU architecture that enhances sequential learning through attention mechanisms; (2) establishing quantitative relationships between procurement performance indicators and project success; and (3) validating the model using real-world construction project data. Results show that the PP-BPSP model significantly outperforms conventional approaches in predictive accuracy. From a practical perspective, the model enables continuous monitoring of procurement performance, provides early warnings of potential project failure, and identifies critical procurement factors requiring intervention. These capabilities support improved decision-making, cost control, schedule adherence, and quality assurance in construction project management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Institutional clearing priorities, behavioral feedback, and systemic fragility in dynamic multilayer real–financial networks
abstract: Modern real–financial systems are increasingly exposed to cross-sector contagion, where shocks originating in the real economy may be transformed into banking-sector fragility. A key yet underexplored driver of this transformation is institutional clearing priority, namely the creditor hierarchy governing loss allocation upon default. This study develops a dynamic tri-layer contagion engine that integrates firm trade-credit networks, bank–firm lending, and interbank exposures into a configurable simulation-based stress-testing framework. Alternative clearing priority regimes—bank-first, firm-first, and pari passu—are implemented as institutional modules, enabling controlled counterfactual analysis under identical network structures and shock environments. The system executes a round-based contagion cycle that combines default identification, priority-based clearing, multilayer loss propagation, behavioral feedback, endogenous network updating, and joint stabilization checking. Using Monte Carlo simulations, the framework produces decision-oriented outputs capturing cross-layer loss routing, the Cross-layer Loss Transformation Index (CLTI), default allocation, systemic amplification, tail risk, and stabilization dynamics. The results show that the systemic relevance of corporate distress depends strongly on shock scope and network position. More importantly, clearing priority operates primarily as an institutional loss-routing and systemic-burden allocation mechanism: it determines whether firm-originated losses remain concentrated in trade-credit networks or are transformed into banking-sector stress. Behavioral feedback and network adaptation affect the adjustment path and persistence of contagion, but do not overturn the loss-routing role of creditor hierarchy. The analysis further shows that clearing priority generates more visible differences in systemic-burden allocation than in aggregate amplification, implying that aggregate risk measures may conceal important redistribution effects across real and financial layers. Overall, the proposed framework positions creditor hierarchy as a configurable institutional input in comparative stress-testing analysis, providing decision-relevant insights for systemic risk assessment and institutional stress testing in interconnected real–financial networks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: An agent based model to support secondary critical materials markets development
abstract: The development of Secondary Materials Markets (SMMs) is a promising approach to diversify and strengthen critical materials supply chains. SMMs involve the recovery of valuable materials from discarded products and reintroduce valuable materials into the economy through cooperative business partnerships. This research addresses the need for analytical tools, which can enable SMM stakeholders to evaluate potential outcomes under various operating conditions and make informed decisions regarding SMM participation and development. A novel agent based model, integrated with existing techno-economic analysis and lifecycle assessment metrics, is developed to quantitatively evaluate the feasibility and impacts of SMMs for enabling secondary critical material feedstocks. Multiple interdependent factors are considered simultaneously, including techno-economic developments, demand uncertainty, inconsistent used product management scenarios, and changing stakeholder business strategies and interactions. The model’s analytical capabilities are demonstrated using a hypothetical-realistic photovoltaic (PV) waste management case study. Under the baseline tested conditions, the model estimated recovery of approximately 72 % of regional PV waste providing secondary materials to meet the demands of co-located manufacturing firms. For example, approximately 45 % of the aluminum demand was met via recovered materials leading to 23 million USD (approximate) in savings for the partner firm buying recovered aluminum under baseline tested conditions. In this manner, this research lays the foundation for analytical tool development to support decisions related to critical material recovery through SMMs. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.
