title: Measuring success: A refined methodology for estimating long-term continuous improvement
abstract: Successful resource management systems require current and detailed feedback on operational and corporate-level performance. As corporate accountability concerns intensify, the precision and reliability of these performance metrics have become crucial. Traditional savings estimation methods can be difficult to understand, particularly linear regression, and can provide varying results. This paper reviews common efficiency metrics and highlights underlying mathematical inconsistencies when estimating total and percent savings with current methods. A refined approach to calculating long-term utility savings is proposed that simplifies current methodologies utilizing ratios to define an adjusted baseline, allowing for consistent and fair aggregation of results across multiple scales from resources to corporate performance. A simplified example demonstrates how the proposed methodology improves upon existing methods, especially in intermediate years. This paper’s major contributions are the simplified approach for converting modeled utility usage into estimated savings and the consistent roll-up methodology enabling more comparable, aggregable, and actionable results across scales. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: How contribution streaks form and their role in long-term retention in OSS projects
abstract: Contributor turnover is a major challenge in open-source software (OSS) projects, affecting project sustainability, quality, and many other dimensions of project performance. Although turnover has been widely studied in the OSS context, the importance of sustained contribution periods to long-term contributor survival remains poorly understood. In this context, contributor survival refers to the probability of sustained activity over time. We investigate the effect of contribution streaks, defined as consecutive months of contribution, on long-term survival, and analyze what kind of engagement, at different levels of ownership, predicts short-term contribution streaks. Using five years of data from 14 open-source projects, we applied landmark analysis to understand long-term survival based on peak streak lengths and logistic regression to identify the activities supporting short-term streaks. In both cases, we identified a three-month contribution streak to be an important threshold for sustained contributions. We found that development and communication related activities across ownership levels are important predictors of whether contributors continue their streaks, even though the relative importance shifts over time. In addition, we found that prior experience plays a stronger role early on, but its effect diminishes during later streak months. These findings suggest that contribution streaks are important predictors of long-term survival and provide practical insights for open-source practitioners on how to improve the retention of new and existing contributors through supporting short-term contribution streaks. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Quantifying compressibility-induced hydrodynamic deviations from isothermal assumptions in immersed top-blowing reactors
abstract: Current designs of high-temperature top-blowing reactors predominantly rely on isothermal water models or incompressible simulations. These approaches inherently neglect gas thermal expansion, leading to a systematic underestimation of actual mixing capacity and equipment wear. To explicitly quantify these compressibility-driven effects, a compressible volume of fluid (VOF) model was established for an industrial-scale reactor. By contrasting a high-temperature condition (1473.15 K) against a cold baseline (293.15 K) representing conventional isothermal assumptions, this study isolates the hydrodynamic contribution of thermal expansion. The results are as follows: i) Thermal expansion-driven mechanism: The primary driver of liquid agitation is the rapid thermal expansion and pressure release of the injected gas. The resulting volumetric expansion strengthens gas–liquid momentum transfer, increases the required upstream supply pressure, extends gas residence time, and slows the periodic oscillation of the impinging cavity. ii) Enhanced liquid mixing capacity: Thermal expansion expands the impinging cavity volume to twice that of the cold state. Consequently, the total liquid kinetic energy increases by a factor of 2.31, the net gas–liquid interfacial area expands by 81%, and the dead zone volume fraction sharply decreases from 58.41% to 22.40%. iii) Intensified splashing and scouring: The thermodynamically enhanced mixing inherently triggers more violent interfacial dynamics, yielding a 2.47-fold increase in splash volume. This intensification corresponds to a fourfold escalation in reactor wall shear forces and a 62.2% rise in lance shear force. This study explicitly quantifies the physical deviations embedded in traditional isothermal models. These findings provide a quantitative reference for correcting isothermal modeling assumptions in the design and wear-risk assessment of high-temperature gas–liquid reactors. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Blockchain adoption decisions and pricing strategies under consumer privacy concerns in competing mHealth platforms
abstract: Blockchain technology has been increasingly promoted as a means of enhancing privacy traceability and trust in mobile health (mHealth) services. As consumer concerns about privacy grow and price competition intensifies, mHealth platforms face strategic decisions regarding whether and when to adopt blockchain-based privacy infrastructures. This study develops four duopoly game-theoretic models to analyze competing platforms’ pricing strategies and the market conditions under which blockchain is adopted to implement privacy traceability, thereby providing decision support for platforms’ strategic management. The results indicate that the decision of mobile healthcare platforms to adopt blockchain is influenced by consumer privacy concerns, platform market share, price competition intensity, and blockchain implementation costs. When the two platforms are technologically homogeneous, the platform with a larger market share is usually in a stronger position to improve traceability and charge higher service prices, whereas the smaller platform tends to focus on cost containment to preserve its low-price advantage. The timing of blockchain adoption and implementation costs critically shape market outcomes. When privacy concerns are strong and price competition is relatively weak, early adoption of blockchain technology to protect consumer privacy can enhance a platform’s competitive advantage. However, when privacy concerns are low, price competition is intense, and fixed adoption costs are high, blockchain adoption is more likely to undermine platform profitability and destabilize its market position. Moreover, market competition also creates higher technological entry barriers for late entrants. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Molecular insights into aldehyde-mediated assembly and bioactivity of peptide–polysaccharide composite hydrogels
abstract: Inflammation and oxidative stress are central pathological drivers of numerous diseases and infections, necessitating the development of bioactive peptide-based hydrogels with integrated anti-inflammatory and antibacterial functionalities. This study reported the construction of novel composite hydrogels via synergistic integration of enzymatic yak bone collagen peptides with carrageenan-xanthan gum, functionalized with aromatic aldehydes including anethole aldehyde, vanillin and protocatechuic aldehyde. Rheological and microstructural analyses revealed that protocatechuic aldehyde-loaded hydrogel (COP-PC/CX) exhibited superior viscoelastic stability (crossover strain 22.1%), uniform porous architecture, and robust network connectivity compared with anethole aldehyde-loaded hydrogels and vanillin-loaded hydrogels. FTIR, 1H NMR and XRD confirmed that aldehyde-loaded hydrogel stabilization was governed by cooperative hydrogen bonding and dynamic Schiff base crosslinking, and different aromatic aldehydes altered the structure–function relationships of the peptide–polysaccharide hydrogels. The composite hydrogel of COP-PC/CX showed exceptional broad-spectrum antibacterial efficacy and antioxidant capacity, achieving inhibition rates of up to 97.18% against E. coli. Functionally, the treatment of COP-PC/CX hydrogel showed the most intense response to attenuate pro-inflammatory macrophage activation by downregulating TNF-α and IL-6 via cytokine signaling and leukocyte migration pathway modulation, while reducing intracellular ROS levels, which were corroborated by transcriptomic analysis of macrophages treated by these aldehyde-loaded hydrogels. This work advanced a sustainable design that valorized animal by-products through plant-derived bioactive integration, establishing a molecularly informed strategy for synergistic dual-functional biomaterials in food preservation and biomedical applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Influence maximization in online social networks: Models, algorithms, and trustworthy decision-making
abstract: Influence Maximization (IM) in online social networks has traditionally been formulated as selecting a budgeted set of seed users to maximize expected spread under a diffusion model. This classical view enabled foundational hardness, submodularity, and approximation results, but it is increasingly insufficient for realistic online social systems, where users differ in behaviors and opinions, networks evolve, diffusion is context-dependent, objectives go beyond coverage, and influence may generate negative, unfair, privacy-sensitive, or harmful consequences. This survey provides a unified review of IM from the perspective of trustworthy influence decision-making. We first develop a six-layer Online Social Influence-Maximization Stack that links network representation, behavior and context, diffusion mechanisms, objective design, algorithmic optimization, and governance. We then synthesize diffusion and objective models through a model–objective–algorithm perspective, covering classical, context-aware, behavioral, economic, opinion-aware, competitive, harm-aware, and learned diffusion settings. Next, we compare algorithmic paradigms ranging from greedy and lazy-greedy methods to sampling, sketching, mathematical programming, evolutionary search, non-submodular search, learning-based seed selection, and adaptive policies, with respect to their theoretical guarantees, time and space complexity, and information requirements. We further discuss realistic online social network settings, including dynamics, heterogeneity, multiplexity, cyber–physical contexts, partial observability, and group-level influence. Finally, we identify robustness, fairness, privacy, harm control, causal validity, explainability, accountability, benchmarking, datasets, and reproducibility as central requirements for next-generation IM, with particular attention to their interaction with scalability. Across these developments, four tensions recur: realism versus tractability, prediction versus optimization, observability and privacy versus scalable estimation, and trustworthiness versus scalability. This survey argues that IM should be understood as trustworthy, adaptive, and utility-aware influence decision-making in complex social systems, rather than as spread-only seed selection. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Joining schools of thought on value propositions: a review and research agenda
abstract: The value proposition (VP) is foundational to business research, yet literature devoted to it remains fragmented, hindering the theoretical development and practical application of this key concept. To consolidate and unify the field, the current article presents an analysis of its conceptual and intellectual structure, which distinguishes two dominant schools of thought: a strategic school and a service school. Building on this analysis, the authors propose an integrative framework to bridge these perspectives, which in turn reveals how they can be mobilized jointly to address complex, multilevel, value co-creation dynamics. Finally, a research agenda outlines key questions and thematic priorities—particularly related to sustainability, technology, and innovation—to guide further theoretical integration and the continued evolution of VP scholarship. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: Ethics practices in ai development: An empirical study across roles and regions
abstract: Recent advances in AI applications have raised growing concerns about the need for ethical guidelines and regulations to mitigate the risks posed by these technologies. In this paper, we present a mixed-methods survey study - combining statistical and qualitative analyses - to examine the ethical perceptions, practices, and knowledge of individuals involved in various AI development roles. Our survey comprises 414 participants from 43 countries, representing various roles such as AI managers, analysts, developers, quality assurance professionals, and information security and privacy experts. The results reveal varying degrees of familiarity and experience with AI ethics principles, governance initiatives, and risk mitigation strategies across roles, regions, and other demographic factors. Our findings underscore the importance of a collaborative, role-sensitive approach that involves diverse stakeholders in ethical decision-making throughout the AI development lifecycle. We advocate for developing tailored, inclusive solutions to address ethical challenges in AI development, and we propose future research directions and educational strategies to promote ethics-aware AI practices. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Bridging the perception–behavior gap through digitalization in the OCOP market: the role of QR code–enabled blockchain systems and consumers’ literacy
abstract: The development of QR code–enabled blockchain (QRB) technology creates new opportunities for OCOP (One Commune One Product) products. This study examines how consumers' experiences with a QRB system impact their perceptions and purchase decisions. A comparative empirical study was conducted using a quota–sampled survey of two independent groups: Study 1 (400 inexperienced consumers) and Study 2 (400 consumers exposed to QRB). The results indicate that consumers exposed to QRB would perceive transparency and traceability. These stimuli could enhance perceived trustworthiness and novelty, reduce greenwashing, and promote consumers' purchase decisions. Furthermore, a key contribution of this study is the moderating role of consumers’ QR code–enabled blockchain literacy in bridging the perception–behavior gap based on the New Literacies Theory. Based on these findings, businesses could encourage consumers to experience QRB to enhance their purchase decisions. Finally, this study also proposes future research directions by exploring additional psychological factors. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Green debt for nature-based solutions: aligning municipal budgeting and banking practices
abstract: Local governments face growing risks from climate change, which require substantial investments in climate adaptation to safeguard future generations. Nature-based solutions (NBS) have been recognized as a cost-efficient strategy to redevelop public space, to create greener and more climate adaptive urban environments. However, development of NBS is hindered by a lack of financial resources to fully scale up the transformation. To overcome this barrier, literature calls for clear sustainable finance frameworks and business model approaches to include private financing in the development of public NBS. In our research we consider the perceptions of municipalities and banks, as institutional lenders, towards using green debt-financing to finance NBS. We draw on sustainability transitions literature to theorize NBS as a niche innovation within established banking-municipal relations. Using qualitative interviews with Belgian banking experts and urban and financial planners from Flemish cities, we reveal competing financial logics between municipal financing practices and banking requirements, limiting the uptake of green debt for NBS. While NBS are mostly absorbed in traditional municipal deficit financing, this conceals their value and prevents market development. Alternatively, project finance remains difficult due to capacity constraints and differing valuation logics. Emerging sustainable finance frameworks create opportunities but shift administrative burdens onto municipalities. Overall, current practices mainly support NBS to fit and conform, rather than transform established debt-practices. Substantial upscaling of NBS will require changes in both banking practices and municipal financing approaches, including explicit integration of physical climate risk and collective financing mechanisms. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Coupled supply and demand forecasting in platform accommodation markets
abstract: Tourism demand forecasting is methodologically mature, but it usually treats accommodation supply as fixed, exogenous, or slow-moving. This Progress in Tourism Management article develops a narrated, conceptually focused review of forecasting in platform-mediated short-term rental markets, where supply is elastic, decision-driven, and jointly shaped with demand through pricing, information design, host participation, and policy intervention. The article reframes realized booked nights as a constrained outcome generated by latent demand, effective supply, and matching frictions. It synthesizes tourism forecasting, revenue management, two-sided market economics, causal inference, and compositional time-series methods; articulates a three-layer coupling framework spanning intervention, behavioral, and informational channels; and uses a stylized model experiment to illustrate one supply-shock failure mode. The contribution is a theoretical and methodological map: where platform accommodation forecasting has developed, what remains under-specified, and how future work can validate coupled supply–demand forecasting. It does not attempt a completed comparative empirical evaluation. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: The power of effortful communication in recovering from woke-washing allegations: impact on brand morality and firm outcomes
abstract: Brands are increasingly seen as agents of social change through brand activism, with some consumers expecting brands to use their moral authority to influence others. However, allegations of inauthentic brand activism, often referred to as “woke-washing,” present significant challenges and can undermine consumers’ brand perceptions. Across a pilot thematic analysis and four experimental studies, we offer insights into woke-washing and its consequences and provide guidance for effective brand response strategies. Findings suggest that brand response strategies perceived as high-effort (versus low-effort), particularly internal and external policy changes, mitigate the adverse effects of woke-washing allegations, regardless of firm size. Specifically, high-effort responses increase purchase intentions and positive word-of-mouth through a sequential process involving perceived brand communication authenticity and perceived brand morality. By distinguishing message-level communication authenticity from actor-level brand morality, the findings clarify how effortful recovery can help brands repair perceptions after woke-washing allegations. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Digital transformation and supply chain Resilience: Inverted U-shaped effect and mechanisms with dual Moderation—Evidence from China’s A-share listed firms
abstract: Against the background of rising global supply chain risks and deepening digital transformation, this study draws on the resource-based view and dynamic capabilities perspective and uses data from Chinese A-share listed firms from 2013 to 2023 to examine the effect of digital transformation on supply chain resilience. Findings reveal a significant inverted U-shaped effect: moderate levels of digital transformation strengthen supply chain resilience, whereas excessive levels of digital transformation weaken it. Absorptive, innovative, and adaptive capabilities partially mediate this nonlinear effect. Further analysis shows R&D intensity steepens the inverted U-shaped curve, whereas firm size flattens it. Moreover, the inverted U-shaped effect is more pronounced among firms in regions with higher factor market development and among firms with higher supply chain concentration and lower financing constraints. These findings help firms identify an effective range of digital transformation based on their capabilities and resources and inform differentiated government support policies. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: Perceptions of expertise and its development among critical care trainees and staff physicians: A qualitative interview study
abstract: Background In highly specialized fields such as critical care medicine (CCM), understanding how expertise is defined and developed is essential for both clinical practice and education. While expertise has been widely studied, its characteristics and developmental trajectory among critical care physicians remain incompletely understood. Methods The qualitative interview study involved purposively sampled CCM trainees and experienced staff physicians. Two systems-design researchers interviewed, recorded and transcribed the interviews verbatim. One researcher inductively coded all transcripts, while another researcher reviewed the codes and representative quotations. A CCM physician contributed to theme development, and interpretations were refined through team discussion. Results 36 participants were interviewed (18 trainees and 18 staff physicians). Expertise in CCM was described as multifaceted, encompassing knowledge, experience, technical and non-technical skills, communication, performance, and personal attributes. Mental model development emerged as a central indicator of progression toward expertise. Trainees and staff physicians largely shared similar views; however, trainees emphasized confidence in decision-making and the role of experts as mentors and leaders. Discussion Expertise in CCM extends beyond technical competence to include cognitive and interpersonal dimensions. The importance of mental models and decision-making under uncertainty highlights the role of experiential learning and reflective practice. Differences in perception between trainees and staff physicians suggest that confidence and teaching ability may serve as key markers of expertise from a learner perspective. Conclusion Expertise in CCM is complex and evolving, shaped by experience, reflection, and cognitive development. These findings provide a foundation for optimizing ICU training strategies and supporting clinicians' progression toward expert performance in high-stakes environments. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Sustainable aviation fuels: a review of production technologies, life-cycle emissions, and key challenges
abstract: The aviation sector is essential for global connectivity and economic growth but remains one of the most difficult industries to decarbonize due to its reliance on energy-dense liquid fuels and the anticipated increase in both carbon dioxide (CO2) and non-CO2 climate impacts. As the industry pursues net-zero emissions by 2050, Sustainable Aviation Fuels (SAFs) have emerged as the most practical near- and medium-term decarbonization pathway because they are compatible with existing aircraft and fuel infrastructure. However, uncertainties persist regarding the sustainability, scalability, economic viability, and long-term climate benefits of different SAF production routes. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of SAFs by integrating feedstock availability, conversion technologies, fuel properties, life-cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, techno-economic performance, and future deployment prospects within a unified sustainability framework. Major SAF pathways, including Oil-to-Jet (OTJ), Gas-to-Jet (GTJ), Alcohol-to-Jet (ATJ), and Sugar-to-Jet (STJ), are critically evaluated, with particular focus on ASTM D7566-certified fuels such as Fischer–Tropsch Synthetic Paraffinic Kerosene (FT-SPK), Hydroprocessed Esters and Fatty Acids (HEFA-SPK), and Hydroprocessed Algae-Based Fuels (HC-HEFA). Comparative analysis reveals significant differences in feedstock requirements, process efficiencies, production costs, fuel composition, and scalability. Life-cycle assessment (LCA) studies indicate GHG emission reductions ranging from 60% to over 100% relative to conventional jet fuel, with FT-SPK and FT-SPK/A offering the highest mitigation potential. Feedstock cultivation, resource extraction, and fuel conversion are identified as the most emission-intensive stages, underscoring the need for upstream process optimization. The review further examines critical barriers to large-scale SAF deployment, including feedstock scarcity, supply variability, high energy and hydrogen requirements, infrastructure constraints, and high production costs. While HEFA dominates current commercialization, scalable aviation decarbonization will require accelerated deployment of FT, ATJ, and Power-to-Liquid (PtL) pathways, supported by technological innovation, sustainable feedstock expansion, and enabling policies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A critical analysis on homomorphic searchable encryption architectures and security models over multi-medium data
abstract: Cloud computing has become a dominant platform for large-scale data storage and processing; however, outsourcing sensitive information to untrusted cloud servers introduces major privacy and security concerns. Homomorphic-based searchable encryption enables secure search and computation over encrypted data without revealing plaintext contents or query information. This paper presents a systematic survey of homomorphic-based SE schemes for multimedia data including text, audio, and image representations. Cloud computing is now a major data storage and processing platform, but sharing sensitive data with external organizations on semi-trusted cloud servers poses significant privacy and security issues. Homomorphic SE allows for secure search via computation on encrypted data without disclosure of the plaintext data or the information of the query. This paper provides a systematic survey of SE schemes for multimedia data such as text, audio and image representations that are based on homomorphic operations. The study offers a comprehensive analysis of homomorphic encryption techniques employed in cloud-assisted retrieval systems. Special focus is given to the security of search patterns, access pattern protection, probabilistic trapdoor generation, privacy preservation, and formal security models such as IND-CPA, IND-CKA, semantic security, forward as well as backward privacy and ORAM-assisted retrieval. The research also covers emerging architectures like MPC-assisted search, FHE-ORAM hybrid architectures, as well as recent developments in FHE acceleration using GPU-based implementations and hardware-assisted optimizations. This work provides a consolidated reference framework and future research roadmap toward secure, scalable, and privacy preserving homomorphic SE systems for cloud-assisted multimedia domains. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Plasmon-assisted and electrostatic-driven photocatalysis at the sharp tips of au nano-bipyramids in aqueous phase
abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) combined with plasmonic photocatalysis is an effective method for the in-situ analysis of molecular reaction mechanism, which has been widely employed to study the transformation process and reaction mechanism of azobenzene molecules. However, achieving highly sensitive monitoring of reactant molecules and precisely controlling the catalytic products remain significant challenges. In this study, citrate-capped gold nanobipyramids (cit-Au NBPs) were used as the plasmonic substrate, which not only utilize the “lightning rod effect” at the tips of the bipyramids to construct an extremely strong localized electric field, but also precisely drive positively charged reactants (such as p- nitroaniline) to the catalytic region at the tips through electrostatic adsorption by the negatively charged citrate on the surface. Based on this synergistic effect, the highly sensitive in-situ SERS monitoring of complex reaction process was achieved. Specifically, the plasmon-driven oxidative coupling and reduction process of p- nitroaniline under light irradiation and after the addition of NaBH4 were clearly defined. Furthermore, comparative studies on nanoparticles with different morphologies and surface ligands demonstrated the critical roles of tip-induced plasmonic enhancement and electrostatic driving in this highly efficient catalytic system. In addition, the feasibility and promising selectivity of this strategy were verified by the catalysis of p- aminophenol and o- phenylenediamine. This strategy significantly improves the efficiency of plasmonic catalysis and the SERS detection sensitivity of trace intermediates, providing an excellent platform for in-situ monitoring of complex and rapid catalytic reactions. title: Continuum modeling of granular segregation accounting for wall friction
abstract: Sidewall friction significantly influences particle mobility within the flowing layer and plays a key role in the formation and transition of granular segregation patterns. This paper introduces a wall friction term into the traditional convection-diffusion model to consider the influence of wall friction on granular segregation, and analyzes the granular segregation characteristics within the rotating drum under different rotational speeds and filling degrees using the discrete element method. The results show that the improved convective diffusion model can effectively measure the granular concentration distribution and segregation rate distribution in the drum; at the center position of the flowing layer, the shear rate and granular velocity gradually decrease along the depth of the flowing layer, and the segregation rate shows a trend of increasing first and then decreasing; as the rotational speed increases, the shear rate and granular velocity in the flowing layer gradually increase, the segregation rate also increases, and the concentration of small granules gradually decreases, promoting the segregation pattern to change from a striped shape to a nuclear shape; when the filling degree decreases, although the segregation rate increases, the change in the concentration of small granules in the flowing layer is not obvious, so the segregation pattern always remains nuclear. The research results help to reveal the mechanism of granular segregation pattern formation and provide reference data for improving the granular segregation model. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Reliability modeling and evaluation for discrete competing failure processes
abstract: There are many engineering systems that can fail due to both the internal degradation of the system itself and the effects of external shocks. The external shocks also affect the degradation of the system. In this paper, discrete analogues of the competing failure processes previously studied in the literature for the continuous case are considered. Exact reliability equations are obtained for a system that is exposed to both internal degradation and external shocks over periods when the shock magnitudes have a discrete probability distribution. The computationally efficient reliability equations are also presented for the particular case when the random quantities involved by the model have phase-type distributions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Detection and differentiation of Salmonella Typhimurium and Salmonella Enteritidis in poultry meat using a machine learning-enabled paper chromogenic array sensor approach
abstract: Rapid and accurate detection of Salmonella serotypes associated with foodborne illness is critical for maintaining food safety. This study developed and evaluated the capability of a machine learning-enabled paper chromogenic array sensor (ML-PCA) approach for non-destructive, continuous, and simultaneous detection and differentiation of Salmonella Typhimurium (ST) and Salmonella Enteritidis (SE) in chicken breast in the presence of background microflora during storage at room temperature and refrigerated temperature (4°C). At room temperature, the ML-PCA approach achieved accuracies of 80–88% for detecting ST and SE in mono-serotype, dual-serotype, and serotype cocktail as early as 6 h. At 4°C, ST and SE could be detected as early as 1 d, with testing accuracy exceeding 80%. These results demonstrated that the ML-PCA approach enabled non-destructive, continuous, and simultaneous detection and differentiation of ST and SE on poultry meat. This methodology offers a potential tool for continuous Salmonella monitoring across the food system. © 2026 The Authors

title: Optimal reinsurance, investment and dividend strategies with square-root factor model
abstract: This paper studies the optimal reinsurance, investment and dividend strategies for an insurer who aims to maximize the expected discounted utility of dividend payments together with a discounted terminal value at ruin. The insurer can invest in a risky asset with price dynamics given by a square-root process, which includes the CEV, Heston and 4/2 models as special cases. We consider two types of instantaneous dividend utilities: exponential and logarithmic functions. The problem is formulated as a stochastic control problem with double stochastic state processes and nonlinear optimization objectives. Using dynamic programming, we derive the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations with nonlinear gradient components and provide analytical solutions for optimal strategies under both utilities. Our results show that the square-root factor process significantly influences the optimal policies, specially for the optimal investment. We also conduct numerical analyses under the 4/2 model to illustrate the impact of various parameters on optimal strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Strategic packaging mechanization with sensor technologies for non-destructive in-situ quality and safety assessment of ready-to-eat fresh-cut fruits and vegetables
abstract: The surging demand for convenience-based, ready-to-eat (RTE) fresh-cut fruits and vegetables (FCFV) is driven by health-conscious consumers for effortless food accessibility. Escalating mass demand for convenience, aesthetic appeal and intact nutrition has prompted immense research efforts for enhanced efficiency and functionality of the value chain performance of RTE foods. Perishability of FCFV, exacerbated by air exposure, limits their availability and shelf life. Developing preservative-free and effective technoscientific alternatives is still an arduous problem that involves a multidisciplinary response. SMART Packaging technologies embedded nanoparticles and antimicrobial coatings can help reduce the spoilage and increase the shelf life, while integration of the pacakging with advanced digital technology i.e sensors (RFID, biosensors, freshness sensors, etc.), indicators (time temperature indicators, nanoemulsion coating with pH sensitive dyes), 3D food printing, 4d Food printing, Digital Twin, Near infrared and hyperspectral imaging, Deep convolutional neural network (DCNN), Spatial computing technology, long short term memory (LSTM) devices, customer relationship management application platforms, Blockchain technology propels quality tracing and predictive maintenance along the supply chain. This review focuses on the current state of the FCFV sector, emphasizing key challenges, recent advancements in integrated packaging approaches with smart packaging innovations for ensuring quality and shelf life. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Barriers and Facilitators of Utilizing Real-World Evidence to Support Policy Decisions in Central and Eastern Europe
abstract: Objectives We aimed to identify drivers and solutions to overcome the barriers of the effective use of real-world data (RWD) and real-world evidence (RWE) in Central and Eastern Europe. Methods First, a targeted literature review was followed by an experts’ workshop aiming to refine and complement the identification of current barriers and drivers. Next, we performed a gap analysis on the barriers based on their importance and actionability. The scores of importance and actionability for each barrier were determined through a questionnaire completed by the experts. Finally, a second experts’ workshop was held to develop recommendations to overcome the most important actionable barriers and to collect case studies of RWD/RWE utilization. Results A total of 22 publications were included in the data extraction phase of the targeted literature review. After the first experts’ workshop, 16 barriers and 9 drivers were identified. At the second workshop 9 solutions were proposed in 4 main intervention areas. In addition, 13 case studies were provided from the 4 countries, where RWD/RWE was used effectively. Conclusions The effective use of RWD/RWE in health-policy decision making still faces several barriers in Czechia, Hungary, Poland, and Slovakia. This research highlighted the most important barriers and collected recommendations by key experts on how to improve the utilization of RWD/RWE. In addition, we have identified several drivers for the use of RWD/RWE, alongside with 13 case studies, in which RWD/RWE was used effectively. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Enhancing Startup Success: Leveraging Machine Learning for Business Category Recommendation
abstract: Today recommendation systems in business are at the core of the personalization process for the mutual good of startups. This chapter introduces a cutting-edge system based on NLP and machine learning that uses NLP and machine-learning algorithms to provide the recommendations platform. Its foremost goal is to help businesses understand who can supply them with financially and the order in which this should take place. It examines one of the most important problems faced by startups that is finding the right investors. How to do it better and more efficiently, using the Word2Vec model for NLP by Google. The viable method to use the two given text input and grasp the meaning of their business is to convert user prompts into tokens and vectors, after which the mentions of individual business categories are notated and their similarities calculated. In addition, it also explains details the implementation of three machine learning models - Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Support Vector Machines (SVM) for precise recommendation models. Through rigorous evaluation and comparison, the ANN manifests as the optimal solution from the multiplicity of alert systems revealing the highest predictive accuracy magnets for investor engagement and business growth. Our business recommendation and investor engagement platform are deservingly called a solid tool for all those businesses who desire to improve investor engagement tactics and create economic growth in the market place. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Exploring Metadata in Enterprise Architecture by Applying Conceptual Graphs—Formal Concept Analysis (CGFCA) to Moregraph
abstract: Enterprise Architecture (EA) is increasingly driven by heterogeneous metadata drawn from cloud-based APIs, ERP systems, and platform reference architectures. This paper revisits Moregraph, a metadata-driven EA platform that combines OData API metadata parsing, force-directed graph visualisation, and extends its specification with Conceptual Graph – Formal Concept Analysis (CGFCA). Moregraph’s specification is expressed as a Conceptual Graph (CG), which captures the overarching architectural concepts of metadata-driven EA. The CG is expressed in the Conceptual Graph Interchange Format (CGIF), which is part of the interoperable family of logics in the ISO/IEC 24707:2018 Common Logic standard. The CGIF encodes thirteen architectural concepts that include [Application: Moregraph], [Solution Architecture], [Business Data Graph], [SAP Graph], and [Microsoft Graph], connected by seventeen relational triples. The CGFCA algorithm transforms these triples into a 13×17 binary Formal Concept Analysis (FCA) context in Burmeister format, identifies seven direct pathways from the single input concept [Application: Moregraph] to the single output concept [Enterprise Architecture], all mediated by [Technical Debt]. We show that the combination of CG and FCA in CGFCA provides a principled foundation for navigating, validating, and analysing complex EA metadata landscapes. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: An Enhanced System Usability Scale for Evaluating Organizational Systems with Database and Knowledge Management Components
abstract: When designing organizational systems, usability evaluation is crucial to show that the system is efficient to complete tasks and that the user is satisfied and can process information effectively. Though the traditional usability assessment techniques, such as the widely used System Usability Scale (SUS), have been applied to mobile applications, e-commerce systems and business platforms, they may not be sufficient to measure usability requirements in a database-supported and knowledge-intensive organizational setting. This study suggests an Extended System Usability Scale (Enhanced SUS) framework that adds some organizational usability attributes to the traditional SUS dimensions: accessibility, responsiveness, information accessibility, information retrieval, trustfulness, personalization and collaboration support. Thirty participants participated in a quantitative approach, which consisted of task-based usability testing and questionnaire-based assessment. Participants were then asked to perform tasks related to the organization that involved interacting with the database and retrieval of information and/or sharing of knowledge, prior to answering the SUS and Enhanced SUS questionnaires. Descriptive statistical analysis and SUS scoring techniques were used to analyse the collected data. The results show that the proposed Enhanced SUS framework could provide more comprehensive usability information than traditional SUS, as organizational usability attributes related to the management of information and database-supported environments have been added. The result of reliability analysis showed Cronbach’s alpha value was 0.881, which was good internal consistency. However, further psychometric validation involving larger samples and factor analysis is required before the framework can be considered a fully validated usability measurement instrument. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Advancing Metadata-Driven Enterprise Architecture Management Tools Using Conceptual Structures
abstract: Metadata-driven Enterprise Architecture (EA) is critical for aligning business strategy with digital execution, yet metadata often remains fragmented across systems and tools. Moregraph uses Conceptual Graphs as its formal specification and SAP Graph as an exemplar, visualising 4,560 clean-core data objects—but visualisation alone does not ensure governance. This paper extends Moregraph with a formal Metadata-to-Governance Transformation (MGT): a principled, deterministic mapping from OData entity type metadata to structured Data Object governance records, grounded in five design principles and delivered via two pathways (real-time API and Excel bulk import). Demonstrated using SAP LeanIX across four SAP Graph namespaces, functional validation confirms correctness, completeness, and efficiency gains over manual documentation. The approach generalises to any OData-compliant source and any EA platform supporting programmatic or bulk import. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Meta-analysis of antecedents and consequences of customers’ perceived advertisement value
abstract: The literature has frequently studied the effect of privacy concerns, irritation, trust, incentives, enjoyment, innovativeness, usefulness, ease of use and subjective norms on mobile advertising value. However, the findings are inconsistent regarding the real effect of these antecedents, leaving practitioners uncertain about which antecedents to rely upon to design effective mobile advertisements triggering a problem for them. Using a meta-analytic approach, the current research synthesises 211 empirical studies to test the relationship between these antecedents and advertisement value, which subsequently influences attitudes, intentions, and actual behaviour of receiving mobile advertisements. In terms of findings, our study suggests that usefulness is the strongest driver of advertisement value, whereas irritation is the strongest mitigator, and subjective norms have minimal influence. Similar patterns were observed for the effect of the antecedents on attitudes and intentions. Findings also suggest that strength of these relationships varies depending on contexts and methodological approaches adopted in prior studies. Specifically, the effects of antecedents on the outcome variables are comparatively stronger in recent studies, published in high-quality journals, in developed countries, younger samples, experimental designs, smartphone contexts, customized ads, permission-based and location-aware ads, and in-app formats. Accordingly, this study resolves the inconsistent findings of previous research which makes a novel contribution to the mobile advertising literature. Regarding implications, we recommend mobile advertisers use precision targeting using customers’ geographical area and age group, prioritise customised content over generic campaigns, and adopt permission-based communication as a standard practice. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Opening the black box of democracy in international business: polity, politics, and policy distances
abstract: In the current context of democratic backsliding, different political systems, such as democracies and autocracies, as well as political differences between democracies, play an important role in shaping economic relationships. Yet, studies of political factors in international business mostly focus on destination country politics or political distance, conceptualized as cross-country differences in political institutions. We argue that these approaches do not capture the full range of political differences between countries. We disaggregate political distance into polity distance (the difference between political institutions), politics distance (ideological differences between governing parties), and policy distance (substantive differences in policies). In a novel cross-country panel dataset, we combine firm internationalization with country-level political characteristics. We find that polity, politics, and policy distances negatively impact firm internationalization, with polity distance having a stronger negative effect on the internationalization of firms from more democratic countries, and politics distance having a stronger negative effect on firms from countries with right-wing governments, highlighting that these distances have both absolute and directional effects. © 2026 The Author(s). title: The board of directors characteristics research: A bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer and Rstudi
abstract: The Board of Directors (BOD) is widely recognized as a central governance mechanism influencing corporate effectiveness, strategic decision-making, and organizational performance. As corporate governance challenges have intensified in the post–global financial crisis era, scholarly interest in board characteristics has expanded significantly, generating a rapidly growing and fragmented body of literature. In response, this study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis to systematically map the intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and emerging research trends in studies on board of directors’ characteristics over the period 2014–2025. Using 862 peer-reviewed journal articles retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, this study applies performance analysis and science mapping techniques with the support of Bibliometrix (R) and VOSviewer. The analysis includes descriptive statistics, citation and co-citation analysis, bibliographic coupling, keyword co-occurrence, three-field plots, and thematic evolution analysis. The results show that publication output has grown a lot since 2018, with Spain, the United States, the United Kingdom, and China being the most important contributors. The bibliographic coupling and cocitation analyses identify three dominant thematic clusters: (1) corporate governance, corporate social responsibility (CSR), and firm performance; (2) board characteristics and firm outcomes; and (3) ownership structure, governance mechanisms, and firm performance. Furthermore, thematic evolution analysis highlights a gradual shift from traditional board structure and agency-oriented research toward emerging themes related to board diversity, ESG (environmental, social, and governance), audit committees, executive roles, and sustainability-oriented governance. By extending the temporal scope beyond earlier bibliometric reviews and incorporating advanced visualization techniques, this study provides updated and more nuanced evidence on the evolution of board characteristics research. The findings contribute to the corporate governance literature by illustrating the field’s theoretical transition toward broader stakeholder-oriented perspectives and provide helpful suggestions to scholars, practitioners, and policymakers seeking to enhance governance effectiveness in an increasingly sustainability-driven business environment. © 2026 The Beryl Institute. title: Alkaline-thermal and enzymatic pretreatment of PLA/PBAT plastics boosts methane production from anaerobic co-digestion with food waste
abstract: The co-treatment of food waste (FW) and biodegradable plastics in anaerobic digestion (AD) is challenged by the slow degradation of polylactic acid and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PLA/PBAT) blends. This study systematically evaluated alkaline-thermal (AT) and enzymatic pretreatment of two PLA/PBAT plastics—starch-containing (PLA/PBAT/ST) and mineral dust-containing (PLA/PBAT/MD)—followed by anaerobic co-digestion with FW. AT pretreatment significantly enhanced methane production. The highest cumulative methane yield (223.40 ± 5.62 mL/g VS) was obtained with PLA/PBAT/MD pretreated at 140℃, a 25.2 % increase over the untreated control (CK-MD), while PLA/PBAT/ST showed an 8.6 % increase (197.60 ± 2.49 mL/g VS). Enzymatic pretreatment led to only marginal improvements. Scanning electron microscopy and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy revealed that AT at 140℃ induced extensive surface erosion, pore formation, and ester bond cleavage, thereby increasing surface hydrophilicity and microbial accessibility. Microbial community analysis indicated that AT-pretreated plastics selectively enriched hydrogenotrophic methanogens ( Methanobacterium ) and syntrophic bacteria ( Syntrophomonas ), and showed higher relative abundance of genes putatively involved in electron bifurcation and methanogenesis (e.g., K14126). In contrast, enzyme-pretreated plastics promoted hydrolytic bacteria (Synergistota) and glycolysis-related genes, causing volatile fatty acids accumulation and metabolic imbalance. These findings demonstrate that AT pretreatment is a promising strategy to enhance methane recovery from FW and biodegradable plastic co-digestion, providing mechanistic insights for process optimization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A weighted multiple conditional value-at-risk approach to energy portfolio under market and environmental uncertainty
abstract: Climate change and global energy restructuring have increased the demand for optimizing energy asset portfolios under uncertainty. However, existing models based on probability theory or fuzzy set theory fail to capture extreme market and environmental uncertainties effectively. To address this gap, an uncertain mean-weighted multiple conditional value-at-risk energy portfolio model is proposed based on uncertainty theory. Specifically, we define the weighted multiple conditional value-at-risk as the core risk measure within the uncertainty theory framework. The model integrates practical constraints including carbon tax, investment risk control, carbon risk, socially responsible investment demand and budget constraints. Meanwhile, we derive its analytical expressions under the assumptions of normal and linear uncertainty distributions, providing theoretical support for model solution. Numerical simulation and sensitivity analysis are carried out. The results indicate that the proposed model is capable of yielding portfolio schemes that balance economic and ecological benefits, thereby providing a feasible reference for portfolio optimization under uncertainty. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Differential Utility of Explainable AI in Churn Mitigation
abstract: Competitive markets are fundamentally concerned with mitigating customer churn. Although highly accurate predictive AI models are extensively utilised for this objective, they tend to act as “black boxes,” preventing businesses from translating predictive insights into clear and actionable retention strategies. There is a significant discrepancy between the predictive performance of sophisticated machine learning models (such as CatBoost or XGBoost) and their practical efficacy for managers in real-world business. While Explainable AI (XAI) methods such as SHAP and LIME have been proposed as potential solutions, the differences in their value across strategic and operational decision-making tiers are not quantified. This study provides a systematic comparison of interpretations produced by SHAP and LIME using a high-performance churn model. Within the context of the Actionability Score—a novel, business-focused metric—we measure the managerial utility of local explanations for front-line agents. We compared global feature importance ranks for strategic planning and local interpretations for operational interventions, using the Actionability Score to quantify the ratio of controllable features identified. The analysis delivers a dual utility: (1) for strategic alignment, the global explanations of SHAP and LIME are closely related and equally satisfactory for supporting higher-level strategic budgeting; (2) operationally, SHAP achieves a higher Actionability Score than LIME, demonstrating its superiority in bridging the gap between predictive modelling and front-line business intelligence. The study presents a prescriptive Dual-Level XAI Decision Framework, applying SHAP to generate trustworthy, real-time retention intervention scripts for operational success. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: A Hybrid Conversational Framework for Interactive Data Analysis and Time Series Forecasting Using Large Language Models
abstract: The integration of conversational artificial intelligence with data analysis enables broader access to insights. Currently, powerful AI-enabled prebuilt tools such as Tableau GPT, Power BI Copilot, Looker, and OAC are used for data preparation, data analysis, visualisation and faster decision making operating within platform-specific ecosystems. Existing methods of forecasting and dataset exploration present accurate and reliable analysis connecting to data sources linked to them but often rely on technical skills and complex interfaces that may limit their use by non-expert users requiring them to follow predefined workflow. To address this, we present a conversational AI-powered framework that integrates natural language querying, dataset exploration, visualisation and time-series forecasting in a single chatbot interface without the need to download and install the application or purchase license. The framework relies on large language models via Azure OpenAI, LangChain and Prophet library. Users can upload CSV datasets and pose queries through natural language prompts with the system providing text-based outputs. Evaluative measures ensure forecasting reliability and accuracy of the chatbot. We also describe experiments to demonstrate the system’s ability to interpret forecasting results, identify temporal patterns, enhanced by visualisations to illustrate analysis. The framework shows promise in terms of its performance and future work will concentrate on extending the framework through contextual memory, multimodal dataset input and large-scale evaluation adaptable across diverse data sources such as education, health care and business intelligence. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: From Opportunity to Growth: A Case Study of THIRD POLE AI as an AI-Native Operating System
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is moving from experimental chat interfaces to embedded business infrastructure. Yet many organizations still adopt AI through fragmented tools that produce isolated outputs instead of integrated operational value. Agencies, consulting firms, development organizations, event companies, startups, enterprises and government contractors often manage opportunities, strategy, proposal writing, creative production, client management, events, project delivery, talent sourcing and reporting through disconnected systems. This paper presents THIRD POLE AI as a case study and implementation model for an AI-native operating system that connects these functions into one intelligent workspace. The paper frames generative AI not merely as a content generation layer, but as an operating model for turning opportunities into strategies, strategies into creative and proposals, proposals into projects, and projects into measurable growth. Drawing on retrieval augmented generation, large language model orchestration, AI agents, prompt engineering, human-in-the-loop review and responsible AI governance, the paper proposes pragmatic architecture, workflow methodology, governance model and evaluation framework. A small retrospective internal pilot using anonymized opportunity and proposal workflows is added to test the model against baseline manual workflows. The pilot indicates material reductions in preparation time and revision cycles, while improving compliance completeness and source traceability. The contribution is to identify the operational gap between AI experimentation and business transformation, and to show how an AI-native business operating system can improve speed, quality, delivery discipline and institutional learning while keeping humans accountable for commitments and public claims. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Motivated by differentiation or assimilation: How consumer motives shape luxury channel use
abstract: The rapid digitization of luxury retail has changed how consumers interact with luxury products and services, expanding the range of both online and offline channels. In this evolving landscape, understanding the factors that can influence consumers' online channel use is critical for luxury businesses. This research explores the role of two core social identity motives in luxury consumption, differentiation (the desire to stand out) and assimilation (the desire to fit in), in shaping consumers' luxury channel choices. Using a proprietary dataset of 1,879 verified luxury consumers from eight major Chinese cities, we provide empirical evidence that differentiation reduces exclusive online channel use, whereas assimilation increases it. Additionally, we demonstrate that status signaling amplifies the negative effect of differentiation on exclusive online channel use, whereas social engagement strengthens the positive effect of assimilation. These findings offer novel insights by applying social identity motive theory to the context of digital luxury consumption and examining luxury channel choice, an understudied aspect of luxury behavior. This study highlights the importance of symbolic and identity-driven motives in shaping luxury channel usage, providing practical guidance for multi-channel retailers to align channel strategies with consumers' diverse identity needs. © 2026 The Authors

title: Reconceptualizing strategic partnerships islamic philanthropy networks in Indonesia
abstract: This study aims to reconceptualize the framework of strategic partnerships within the Islamic philanthropy sector through an interdisciplinary integration of Strategic Partnership Theory, Network Theory, and General Systems Theory (GST). Amid digital disruption, there is an urgent theoretical and practical necessity to understand how the Islamic philanthropy ecosystem—specifically comprising Zakat, Infaq, Sadaqah, and Waqf (ZISWAF)—can transform into a highly adaptive socio-economic system oriented toward sustainable values. Employing a descriptive qualitative method with a conceptual approach based on systematic literature synthesis, this research analyzes contemporary literature on management and organizational theory to develop an original model that positions Islamic philanthropy as a holistic, interconnected, and dynamic ecosystem. The findings indicate that the effectiveness of strategic partnerships no longer relies on simple bilateral relationships, instead, it requires sophisticated multidimensional synchronization among the input (resource mobilization), process (digital transformation), and output (social impact) subsystems. A systemic analysis reveals that the integration of Maqasid al-Sharia serves as a critical regulatory parameter ensuring that collaboration among managing institutions, the fintech sector, the government, and the public leads to sustainable value co-creation. Consequently, this study identifies digital governance and donors’ religious behavior as primary catalysts for strengthening the resilience of philanthropic networks against global economic volatility.The conclusions confirm that the success of Islamic philanthropy as an adaptive system depends on its capacity to manage systemic interdependencies among stakeholders. Although limited to a theoretical model, the practical implications provide a strategic roadmap for designing inclusive cross-sectoral collaboration frameworks. Socially, this model has the potential to accelerate equitable resource distribution and broader financial inclusion. The originality of this research lies in its unique synthesis of three management pillars to analyze Islamic philanthropy as a multi-actor adaptive system, filling a critical literature gap at the intersection of strategic management and economic theology. © 2026 The Beryl Institute. title: Molecular and environmental indicators of Listeria monocytogenes persistence in food processing facilities: a multi sector approach
abstract: Listeria monocytogenes is a foodborne pathogen capable of persisting in food processing environments. This persistence results from interactions between strain-specific traits and environmental conditions. This study aimed to identify molecular and environmental indicators associated with L. monocytogenes persistence across high-risk food production sectors. Three environmental sampling events were conducted in nine facilities from seafood, vegetable, and pork (n = 3 each) sectors. In total 1097 samples were analysed for the presence of L. monocytogenes, the temperature, and surface characteristics, pH, humidity, temperature, and surface characteristics. L. monocytogenes was detected in 114 samples (≈10%), with the highest prevalence observed in the vegetable sector. Isolates were characterized by Whole Genome Sequencing and classified into persistent or transient clusters based on core genome multilocus sequence typing profiles. Persistent clusters were defined by ≤ 7 allelic differences and repeated detection across at least two sampling events, whereas transient isolates were detected only once. We identified 13 persistent clusters including 67 isolates, of which 42 were assigned to CC121, 9 to CC5, 5 to CC31, 4 to CC101, 4 to CC155, and 3 to CC412. Pangenome analysis identified several loci enriched among persistent isolates, including prophage-related loci, genes encoding transport systems such as TatA, TatC and EfeO, and genes involved in stress response mechanisms. Persistence was associated with higher total microbial counts and high humidity, with persistent isolates mainly detected under conditions exceeding 5–6 log CFU/mL of total microbial counts and 80% relative humidity. Overall, results highlight persistence arising from the interplay between bacterial genetic traits and environmental conditions, emphasizing the importance of integrated approaches for monitoring and control in food processing environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: How do consumers react to unfair reviews? Examining the matching effects of review type and response strategy on purchase intentions
abstract: Unfair negative reviews can harm businesses by damaging brand image and reducing customer trust. This research examines how tourism and hospitality businesses should respond to different types of unfair reviews through three scenario-based experiments. The findings reveal a congruity effect: rational responses are more effective in improving third-party consumers’ purchase intentions for low-arousal unfair reviews, while emotional responses are more effective for high-arousal ones. The results further show that social distance mediates this effect. In addition, in high-arousal cases, weak victimization responses are more suitable than strong reprimands. These findings enrich theories related to Communication Accommodation Theory and contribute to the literature on unfair negative reviews. They also provide practical guidance for tourism and hospitality businesses on how to effectively handle online consumer unfair reviews. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Data-driven decision-making in retail: Impacts on firm performance and consumer outcomes
abstract: Concept: Big data and advanced analytics have radically transformed the retail industry's strategic landscape. In response, companies have adopted data-driven decision-making (DDDM) models as a competitive weapon to address these challenges. Objective: This study examines the multidimensional relationship between the intensity of DDDM adoption and two outcomes: firm performance and consumer welfare. It also investigates how firm size and retail subsector moderates these relationships. Tools: Using a mixed-methods design, we surveyed 386 retail firms across six subsectors and surveyed retail executives regarding application domain barriers in the United States. Quantitative methods included multiple regression, one-way ANOVA, and hierarchical moderated regression, supplemented by surveys from 1200 consumers measuring privacy percept (β = 0.61, p < 0.001, R2 = 0.492). Hierarchical modeling confirmed that firm size (ΔR2 = 0.026, p = 0.001) and specialized sectors like electronics and grocery retail act as significant positive moderators. Consumer satisfaction, product availability, and shopping experience quality improved significantly with increasing DDDM intensity. However, 61.3% of consumers express concern about excessive data collection, while 53.6% acknowledge that personalized offers enhance their shopping experience, revealing a 7.7 percentage point privacy paradox accompanied by a notable trust deficit (only 31.6% consumer trust). Application: These findings provide retail managers with ROI estimates (ranging from 2.4× to 3.2×) for analytics investments across application domains while identifying key infrastructure bottlenecks (52% legacy system friction). They also offer policymakers evidence for data governance frameworks and guide practitioners on balancing personalization benefits with privacy protection. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: EIT digital innovation and entrepreneurship study: Distributed learning activities between Madrid and Aalto
abstract: The EIT Digital Master School includes in its last year of the various technical majors the Innovation and Entrepreneurship Study course, within the Innovation and Entrepreneurship Minor. This paper describes the innovative teaching methods implemented since 2019 in Madrid; one of the KIC, of the EIT Digital. This long term experience that was described, ended in 2025. The collaboration continues in a different way, but in the period of analysis between 2019–2025 consisted of an institutional cooperation between the two universities -on the academic side, and several companies, charities, and other organizations on the entrepreneurship side. Both the academic, and the market-based results for students, including professors on the academic side, and students and institutions on the market side, have been very successful. All relevant details are mentioned in this paper, provided that this longlasting collaboration will help pave the way for future collaborations and inspire others in their business-related education. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Critical Success Factors for AI Adoption: A Multivocal Literature Review and a Top Management Perspective
abstract: The strategic adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a critical determinant of competitive advantage, yet organizations face high failure rates. This paper aims to identify and categorize the Critical Success Factors (CSFs) that influence successful AI adoption by synthesizing academic and practitioner knowledge from a top-management perspective. We conducted a multivocal literature review of 57 academic and 20 practitioner sources, screened per PRISMA. From vote-count synthesis we identified 16 CSFs grouped via the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework, with organizational factors dominating such as leadership support, AI literacy, and cultural readiness. Practitioner evidence corroborates most academic CSFs and adds implementation-centric aspects (e.g., AI scalability, use-case–value alignment, partnerships). Implications for top management/Chief Information Officers include prioritizing data governance, change capability, and portfolio-level value realization. From a theoretical perspective, the paper supports continued relevance of the TOE framework for AI while highlighting the amplified importance of its organizational dimension. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Salesperson performance in the wake of customer interest in digital technology: The role of job engagement as a resilience cushion
abstract: Despite growing interest in salespeople’s social media use, the role of customers in motivating and shaping such use has received limited scholarly attention. Moreover, little is known about whether—and how—social media use enhances salespeople’s effectiveness in managing service recovery situations. Using the conservation of resources theory and analyzing matched survey responses from B2B salespeople and their managers, we find that while customer interest in digital technology has a curvilinear (inverted U-shape) relationship with salesperson social media use, this relationship decreases at higher levels of job engagement, indicating that salespeople with high job engagement have greater resources to manage the stress caused by customer interest in digital technology. Moreover, social media use improves manager-rated salesperson service recovery performance. The study offers significant implications for both theory and practice. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Defining family firms: A survey of empirical criteria
abstract: We survey 153 empirical studies of family firms and document 192 operational definitions representing 25 distinct definition types. These definitions can be decomposed into five recurring, codable dimensions: ownership, management, board representation, embeddedness, and succession. We relate these dimensions to economic mechanisms including agency conflicts, residual control rights, transaction costs, and dynastic control. Alternative definitions select systematically different populations and yield materially different estimates of firm performance and innovation. Definition choice is largely unrelated to the research question, except in succession studies. Ownership thresholds track private enforcement of self-dealing rules, but not statutory shareholder rights or rule of law. We conclude that the family firm is a family of related constructs rather than a single latent construct. Definitions should therefore match the family-firm construct implied by the research question, and results should be reported across alternative classification rules. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Low-Code Platforms Adoption: A Motivational Adoption Process Perspective
abstract: The growing demand for digital transformation in organizations, coupled with a shortage of skilled-IT workers, presents a challenge that can be addressed through the utilization of low-code platforms (LCPs). While existing literature examines organizational drivers of LCPs adoption, our human-centered study shifts the focus toward the individu, investigating motivations of non-technical users adopting LCPs on their own initiative for professional needs. Through qualitative interviews and by refinement of Keller’s ARCS Motivational Model, an adoption framework emerged in the form of a five-stage motivational adoption process (interest, need, ability, learning, reinforcement). By effectively articulating key motivational factors in the adoption of LCPs by citizen developers in this cohesive framework, it can help organizations better foster low-code initiatives. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Wearable, Display-less AI as Extended Reality in Business Education
abstract: Wearable artificial intelligence technologies are emerging as a new class of extended reality (XR) interfaces that operate without traditional visual displays. Devices such as Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses, first-generation consumer release, combine first-person audiovisual capture, voice-based AI interaction, and real-time access to information. This short paper reports an exploratory, faculty-led technology-probe study examining how AI-enabled wearable glasses might be integrated into business administration curricula. Structured experimentation and reflective analysis were used to identify pedagogical affordances (e.g., first-person feedback for presentations, documentation of experiential activities, and instructor ‘hands-free’ access to contextual information) and to surface ethical risks (privacy, consent, and academic integrity). Findings suggest that display-less AI wearables can extend XR practice beyond immersive head-mounted displays by enabling embodied, context-aware interaction in authentic learning settings, but responsible adoption requires explicit instructional design and institutional governance. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Design of a Query Expression for Multi-Dimensional Graph Warehousing
abstract: This study presents an extension of the conventional data warehouse query paradigm by introducing Multi-dimensional Graph eXpression (MGX), a multidimensional query framework designed to support Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) over graph-based business intelligence data. MGX extends the traditional Multi-Dimensional eXpression (MDX) syntax used in relational data warehouses by incorporating SQL-style analytical constructs, including GROUP BY, HAVING, and ORDER BY, thereby improving the expressive capability and flexibility of multidimensional analysis over graph warehouses. By bridging relational data warehousing technologies with graph-based analytical environments, the proposed framework addresses key limitations of traditional MDX in supporting graph-oriented analytics. It enables more effective exploration of semantically rich and socially connected knowledge embedded in networked datasets. Overall, MGX provides a practical methodological foundation for advancing graph warehousing and supporting next-generation network-centric business intelligence applications. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Is competition good or bad for employee innovation? Examining the double-edged sword effect of team and individual responses
abstract: Amid an increasingly competitive environment, fostering innovation among employees has emerged as a central concern for both academia and the business community. Drawing upon the conservation of resources (COR) theory, this study develops a multi-level framework to examine the underlying mechanisms and boundary conditions of competitive psychological climate (CPC) on employees' innovative work behavior. By gathering data from 386 hotel employees and their leaders spanning 60 teams throughout four provinces along China's southeastern coast, the results indicated that CPC facilitated employees' innovative work behavior by increasing team cooperative orientation (i.e., resource-gain pathway); simultaneously, it inhibited innovative work behavior by eliciting workplace anxiety (i.e., resource-depletion pathway). Furthermore, psychological capital buffered the resource-depletion pathway, while error tolerance reinforced the resource-gain pathway. The results advance theoretical insight into CPC's dual influence mechanism and offer practical guidance for motivating employees to innovate in the highly competitive hospitality sector. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Mapping Capabilities with LLMs: Requirements and Feasibility Assessment of Capability Broker
abstract: Capabilities provide a structured and stable business-centric view of what an organization is able to do, when, and under what conditions. Capability has become a standard design element of enterprise architecture frameworks such as NAF, TOGAF, ArchiMate and many others. Despite its usefulness, clear modularity, and purpose of the capability notion, many companies struggle becoming capability-aware and being able to continuously and efficiently manage their capability portfolios. To support this process, this paper presents requirements and an early design prototype of Capability Broker – an LLM based tool for discovering capabilities from organizational documents and creating capability models. The feasibility of the tool is demonstrated with an example case. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.
