title: Comprehensive Performance Evaluation of Indian E-Bikes
abstract: The transportation and power generation industries profit significantly from electric vehicles and renewable energy sources. Electric vehicles (EVs) are becoming more popular as a result of sociological and economic trends. Electric automobiles are now available from all major manufacturers. In recent years, there has been a moderate shift in consumer preferences from internal combustion engine-powered two-wheelers to electric two-wheelers in the Indian market due to the rising popularity of electric cars. The goal of this research is to perform a thorough examination of five significant contributors from the electric two-wheeler market. In this analysis, important vehicle factors are taken into account. Insights into vehicle performance analysis using a mathematical model using MATLAB/SIMULINK is the aim of this study. By varying the e-bike’s speed, the model enables dynamic testing and offers real-time insights into performance variances across various operational settings. For customers that value long-distance travel and extended business hours, Bajaj is the best option. While Okinawa and TVS provide balanced performance, Hero delivers remarkable energy efficiency, and Ather is best for consumers who value rapid recharging. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Crowdshipping for reverse logistics: unlocking sustainability, trust, and fairness
abstract: This study investigates the integration of crowdshipping (CS) into e-commerce reverse logistics, specifically applied to the parcel transport stage between return points and transhipment facilities. Several barriers have limited CS adoption in forward logistics, such as trust, privacy, and security concerns due to direct customer–crowdshipper interaction, and the inability to offer bundled CS tasks that would enable attractive compensation schemes, but these constraints are mitigated in this transport-stage-focused reverse logistics setting. The proposed CS-integrated system operates in a business-to-business (B2B) context, eliminating customer contact and allowing bundled CS task assignment, thereby providing a more secure and operationally efficient setting for CS deployment. In this study, operational and external costs (i.e., per-kilometre social costs) for both conventional and CS-integrated reverse logistics systems are modelled and simulated across diverse spatial and demographic contexts, system scales, configurations, and levels of CS supply and behavioural dynamics. These simulations generate a large database that identifies the conditions under which the CS-integrated system can achieve operational and/or environmental advantages compared with the conventional system. Using a comprehensive simulation experiment based on systematically generated parameter combinations (45,000 simulation runs) and applying decision tree analysis, we find that the CS-integrated system reduces operational costs in nearly all cases, with savings reaching up to 70 % , particularly under conditions with sufficient CS supply and high participation willingness (i.e., low sensitivity to detour and compensation). However, environmental benefits are more context-dependent, emerging mainly in low-density, large-area settings where detours remain minimal. The study underscores the potential of CS to enhance the cost efficiency of reverse logistics while highlighting the importance of policy interventions that limit detours and induced travel demand in the CS-integrated system to ensure that sustainability gains are fully realised. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Neuro-symbolic predictive process monitoring for multi-attribute suffix prediction
abstract: Leveraging historical process execution data to predict the evolution of an ongoing process is a challenging task in Business Process Management. In recent years, transformer-based models have shown promising results in multi-attribute sequence prediction, which refers to the task of forecasting not only the next activity in a process but also its associated attributes (e.g., timestamp, resource, and data values). However, although the accuracy of these models is generally high, there are specific situations in which background knowledge about the process can be beneficial. In particular, such knowledge can improve prediction quality for outlier executions in the training data and in scenarios where process changes occur due to concept drift in the test data. In this paper, we propose a principled method for integrating prior knowledge into an autoregressive transformer-based model for multi-attribute sequence prediction at test time. This knowledge is expressed using Multi-Perspective Declare, a process modeling language capable of describing process behavior from multiple perspectives, including control flow (i.e., the expected sequence of activities executed in the process), data flow (i.e., the data attributes associated with these activities during process execution), resources, and timestamps. We evaluate our method on real-life event logs and demonstrate that incorporating background knowledge consistently improves the performance of multi-attribute sequence prediction, especially in rare and exceptional situations. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Boosting baijiu fermentation efficiency through designed microbial community coalescence: Enhanced substrate conversion and flavor output
abstract: In this study, we designed a synthetic community (SynCom) for directedly monitoring the yield of phenolic compounds and other flavor compounds of Baijiu, through inoculating the coalescence of synthetic community and autochthonous starter culture (Daqu). Compared with the fermentation endpoint, this SynCom, comprised of Wickerhamomyces anomalus, Pantoea agglomerans and Bacillus altitudinis, significantly enhanced the substrate utilization and metabolites formation.Specifically, the consumption of starch and protein was increased by 42.68% and 24.37%, respectively, calculated as the relative increase in consumption from the initial to the endpoint in the model group over that in the control group. Meanwhile, the yield of targeted aromatic compounds increased by 25.9%, with 4-methylguaiacol exhibiting a particularly marked increase from trace levels. Furthermore, we deduced W. anomalus exerted a strong priority effect to constitute over 90% niche of the fungal community and reduce 25% diversity of the community in the front fermentation stage. Therefore, the priority species provided a competitive starving and metabolism of the upcoming species (P. agglomerans and B. altitudinis), and their synergism contributed to the enhancement of targeted phenolic compounds and specific esters in the later stage of fermentation. Our study provided insight into monitoring and controlling the formation of desired compounds through the coalescence of a designed community and a common starter culture. This study also provided a validated framework for the rational designed consortia to control and improve the quality and function of complex fermented foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Artificial Intelligence - Driven Supply Chain Green Innovation: Its Impact on Sustainable Development
abstract: In the context of globalization and rapid technological advancement, traditional supply chains face mounting pressure to address environmental challenges like high energy use, waste, and carbon emissions. Growing sustainability awareness compels firms to innovate. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a key enabler of green supply chain transformation, offering advanced data processing, pattern recognition, and decision optimization to enhance both efficiency and sustainability. This study examines how AI-driven green innovation affects sustainable development across economic, environmental, and social dimensions. Using a mixed-methods approach—comprising a literature review, enterprise surveys, and case studies—the research quantifies AI’s benefits, including cost savings, lower emissions, and reduced waste, while identifying barriers such as high implementation costs, poor partner coordination, and inadequate infrastructure. Findings indicate that AI significantly advances sustainability by optimizing logistics, improving demand forecasting, cutting energy use, and enabling integration with technologies like blockchain and IoT to boost transparency and resilience. The study contributes theoretically by clarifying how AI fosters green innovation and offers practical guidance for businesses and policymakers to support AI adoption in pursuit of sustainable development goals. Despite limitations like potential sampling bias, it highlights AI’s transformative role in building sustainable supply chains. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Self-Organizing Map Implementation Improvements
abstract: Self-organizing maps are among the most commonly used unsupervised neural networks proposed by Teuvo Kohonen in the last century. They are widely used in a variety of tasks, like clustering, dimension reduction, and many others. In this study, several techniques are proposed for the improvement of a software implementation of self-organizing maps from a practical point of view. First, the standard mathematically described algorithm is presented from the theoretical point of view, and then the practical implementation details are shown with some ideas for the reduction of the computational complexity. The algorithms proposed here are realized by the author in the well-known programming language Java from scratch without any existing libraries. The algorithm is also integrated into some bigger software projects, and the improvement of the computational time leads to optimization of the business logic calculations. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: When digital reach Pays Off: capability bundles and differential export paths in software firms
abstract: This study examines how internal capability configurations shape the effectiveness of digital export channels among software firms. Drawing on configuration and strategic fit perspectives, we argue that digitalization enhances export performance only when supported by coherent bundles of entrepreneurial, resource, technological, and local-execution capabilities. Using survey data from 308 Korean firms, we adopt a two-stage approach: k-means clustering identifies three capability archetypes, and multigroup mediation analysis tests performance mechanisms. Results show strong indirect effects via geographic scope for high-tech firms, partial effects for well-rounded firms, and no effect for capability-lagging firms. Complementary fsQCA reveals multiple equifinal pathways, including compensatory configurations among lower-capability firms. Overall, the findings highlight that the benefits of digital export strategies are configuration-dependent and contingent on internal capability coherence across diverse market environments and institutional contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Combining Large Language Models with Named Entity Recognition to Automate Market Research Interview Transcription and Customer Journey Mapping – Empirical Feedback by Business Professionals
abstract: This paper presents an automated pipeline combining large language model inference with named entity recognition to extract structured customer journey insights from interview transcripts. The system, built on Langextract library, identifies pain points, journey stages, emotions, competitors, and stage transitions with structured attributes. A human expert feedback study with 66 business professionals, each serving as both interviewee and assessor, evaluated outputs across seven quality dimensions using three LLM backends. Overall quality was rated good to very good (M = 4.2/5). Gemini 2.5 Flash significantly outperformed alternatives on pain point characterization (g = 1.14). Thematic analysis identified input quality dependency and oversimplification as principal limitations. Results suggest that LLM-based extraction can meaningfully accelerate qualitative market research while requiring human validation. Beyond the pipeline itself, the study positions LLMs as a structured analytic instrument for qualitative market research and contributes a reusable seven-dimension evaluation rubric for assessing LLM-extracted customer journey artifacts. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Insights from Triage Processes for Fairness-Aware Process Redesign
abstract: The integration of Fairness, Accuracy, Confidentiality, and Transparency (FACT) into BPM practices is a recently increasing concern. While there are redesign heuristics, process design space related guidelines, and recommendations for general process design, research lacks an understanding of what makes a fair process design in order to inform design decisions. In this paper, we address this research problem by reviewing case study papers from the domain of triage processes in emergency rooms. This is a unique and specific process setting where fairness has strongly been considered during the COVID-19 pandemic. We organize our findings in a framework that integrates dimensions from social justice theory. In this way, our contribution provides a conceptual basis for fairness-aware process redesign along the BPM life cycle. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Novel intuitionistic fuzzy-enhanced deep learning network with squeeze-and-excite block model for assessment of bronchopulmonary dysplasia
abstract: Early prediction of bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) in very low birth weight (VLBW) preterm infants is essential for timely clinical intervention. However, neonatal chest radiographs are often characterized by high diagnostic uncertainty and limited annotated data, which restrict the performance of conventional deep learning models. Therefore, this study proposes a hybrid intuitionistic fuzzy-enhanced deep learning framework that combines uncertainty-aware image enhancement with SE-block-enhanced U-Net and GoogLeNet classifiers. Specifically, an intuitionistic fuzzy (IF) transformation is first applied as an uncertainty-aware preprocessing step to enhance ambiguous radiographic patterns before image classification. Subsequently, squeeze-and-excitation (SE) blocks adaptively recalibrate channel-wise feature responses to emphasize clinically relevant lung structures. To further improve the effectiveness of the proposed framework, a genetic algorithm (GA) was employed to jointly optimize the intuitionistic fuzzy parameter (α) together with the learning rate, dropout rate, and training epochs. The GA serves as an integral component of the proposed framework to identify an effective parameter configuration, thereby improving the stability and predictive performance of the CNN classifiers under limited-data conditions.Experiments conducted under a standard 8:1:1 training–validation–testing split demonstrated that the proposed model achieved a mean accuracy of 0.857, together with favorable Recall (Sensitivity) and F1-score for the BPD-positive class, indicating competitive predictive performance among the evaluated deep learning models. Furthermore, under a more challenging 6:2:2 data-constrained partition, the proposed IF-U-Net with the SE block maintained a mean accuracy of 0.818, demonstrating stable predictive performance across different evaluation settings. Representative Grad-CAM visualizations qualitatively showed that the proposed framework focused on clinically relevant lung regions during prediction, providing interpretable insight into the model’s attention in representative cases. The experimental results suggest that integrating IF modeling with evolutionary optimization improves predictive performance and robustness under limited-data conditions. The proposed framework therefore provides a promising decision-support tool for early BPD prediction in clinical environments where labeled data are limited. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Bridging Learning and Employability: The Evolving Role of Teaching, Technology, and Faculty Development in Business Schools
abstract: In an era marked by rapid digital transformation and changing labour market demands, Business Schools are under increasing pressure to demonstrate their contribution to graduate employability through pedagogical innovation and institutional renewal. This study examines how Teaching Approaches (TAs), Educational Technologies (ETs), and Faculty Development Initiatives (FDIs) adopted by leading international Business Schools interact to influence perceived learning effectiveness and employability outcomes. Using a quantitative survey design, data were collected from faculty members across top-ranked institutions and analysed through linear regression models to assess the relationships among pedagogical, technological, and developmental dimensions. The findings reveal that active and experiential teaching approaches, as well as technology-enhanced learning practices, are positively associated with perceived effectiveness in promoting both student learning and employability. Faculty development initiatives emerged as the strongest predictor, suggesting that professional learning and institutional support indirectly facilitate the integration of employability-oriented outcomes into curricula. Overall, the results support a systemic model of academic innovation in which pedagogical design, digital transformation, and faculty development co-evolve to enhance educational quality and graduates’ readiness for the workplace. These insights contribute to the ongoing debate on how Business Schools can align teaching innovation with employability goals in a rapidly changing educational landscape. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Towards a Meta-model for Complex Performance Indicators: A Systematic Literature Review and an Illustration in the Cardiology Domain
abstract: Complex Performance Indicators (CPIs) aggregate heterogeneous data streams into multidimensional constructs supporting strategic decision-making, yet their engineering remains fundamentally challenging. Organizations face information overload, governance opacity, and extended development cycles that existing Self-Service Business Intelligence platforms fail to address. Model-Driven Engineering (MDE) promises accessible CPI implementation through intuitive abstractions, but current frameworks remain fragmented and incomplete. This work-in-progress presents a Systematic Literature Review identifying 18 MDE frameworks for indicator modeling and extracting a 31-features inventory across three dimensions: Language Expressiveness, Business User Empowerment, and MDE Capabilities. Analysis reveals that no framework achieves more than 70% feature coverage. The findings justify developing a novel Domain-Specific Modeling Language, with the inventory serving as specification blueprint for future meta-model construction. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Counting with or without fingers: The specific role of fingers in improving addition skills in preschoolers
abstract: Training kindergarteners to count on their fingers has been shown to improve their performance in addition. However, it remains unclear whether these benefits depend specifically on the finger dimension of the training program or more generally on its counting dimension. This study addresses this question in a sample of 190 preschoolers aged 4–5 years. Two training settings, finger counting and counting on a number line, were compared to a business-as-usual condition. The results first show that the positive effect of finger counting training observed in kindergarteners extends to preschoolers. Critically, finger counting led to greater improvement in children’s addition performance than counting on a number line training, which did not produce significant gains. These findings, indicating that the finger dimension plays a central role in supporting children’s arithmetic skills, are discussed in the context of the embodied cognition framework. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Auditable multimodal decision support for ordinal real estate price-band classification: Source-aware and leakage-controlled fusion
abstract: Residential decision-support systems increasingly combine structured property attributes, listing descriptions, and photographs. With small labeled samples, however, an additional representation may duplicate its source rather than add reproducible signal. This study presents a source-aware, leakage-controlled framework for five-class ordinal classification of posted asking-price bands. Structured attributes (N), native listing text (L), photo-derived caption text (C), and frozen verified-photo features (P) are evaluated separately, while C and P are recognized as representations of the same visual source. The final analysis set contains 422 unique address–photo entities. Ten-fold entity/image-safe outer validation prevents related cases from crossing the train–test boundary, and stream-model and fusion-weight selection are confined to three-fold inner splits. Structured attributes achieved 0.666 accuracy and 0.894 quadratic weighted kappa (QWK). Photo-derived caption text was the weakest individual stream, with 0.329 accuracy and 0.439 QWK. The caption-excluded N+L+P configuration produced the best multimodal point estimates, with 0.680 accuracy and 0.892 QWK, whereas the complete N+L+C+P diagnostic configuration attained 0.664 and 0.889, respectively. The complete diagnostic configuration showed no statistically detectable advantage over the predefined controls after Holm adjustment, and fixed XGBoost produced the highest overall point estimates, with 0.697 accuracy and 0.906 QWK. Global-band performance degraded sharply in held-out markets, identifying a clear need for local recalibration and revalidation. Integrated CPU inference beginning with a model-ready listing record and an archived background-removed photograph averaged 12.96 s per listing; the preceding third-party background-removal operation was outside the measured interval. The framework therefore provides an auditable basis for evidence-based representation selection: it separates representation format from source lineage, identifies redundant streams, preserves traceable uncertainty and case-level decision paths, and exposes conditions that require deferral or external revalidation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Combining multiple endogeneous information sources for improved efficiency in covariance and correlation matrix estimation
abstract: This paper proposes efficient covariance and correlation matrix measures using high-frequency data. The proposed matrix measures are the multivariate extension of the Parkinson volatility measure that incorporates High, Low, Open and Close price information distinct from the classical approaches based solely on one information type such as closing price information when constructing the sample covariance matrices. The proposed novel matrix measures facilitate new developments for multivariate time series modelling of dependence structures, including the extension of volatility models such as Conditional Autoregressive Range models to multivariate settings. Model results will provide important risk measures to practitioners for portfolio or investment strategies that deal with a large number of stock assets. Through simulation studies, the proposed matrix measures are shown to perform well under heteroskedastic variance conditions and are positive semi-definite. A demonstration is provided for hypotheses testing applying the estimated variance–covariance matrices to various one and two samples tests. Results show that the proposed matrix measures outperform the classical single source of information based sample covariance and correlation matrix measures. © 2026 The Authors. title: Unpacking complementarities in emerging circular economy innovation ecosystems: The case of industrial plastic waste from the Norwegian aquaculture industry
abstract: Despite growing awareness of plastic waste, industrial plastic use continues to rise, while recycling rates remain low. Addressing this challenge requires a transition toward a circular economy (CE), in which value depends on interactions among independent yet interdependent actors across sectors. CE innovation ecosystems and complementarities offer lenses for understanding such interdependencies. This paper explores how orchestrators facilitate complementarities in emerging CE innovation ecosystems by drawing on an embedded qualitative case study of plastic waste from Norwegian aquaculture. Four types of complementarities are identified—materials data, from waste to resource, recycling capacity, and regulations—conceptualized along two dimensions: resource flow and infrastructure complementarities. This illustrates where orchestrators facilitate value at present and where their role is constrained by limited infrastructure and regulatory requirements. This study advances research on CE innovation ecosystems by adding a process perspective on how complementarities evolve through orchestration and by highlighting how data can support circularity. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Analyzing structural, operational, and performance impact of process-aware information system updates
abstract: Digital transformation often entails small-scale updates to the business functions exposed by enterprise systems, which support the execution of organizational business processes. These changes may increase operational friction in process execution, decreasing the process performance, increasing the complexity of maintenance activities, and making system documentation and training obsolete. Detecting and understanding their impact on process execution is therefore crucial to maintain smooth operations. Previous research contributions concerning the tracking and impact analysis of information systems updates are limited in scope, functionality, and tool support. In this paper, we propose a data-driven approach that uses the recently developed Digital Twins of Organizations (DTOs) to assess the impact of (process-aware) information systems updates. We model the updates using the configuration of DTOs and the newly introduced concept of actions in DTOs. The impact of the application of actions in a given configuration is quantitatively assessed by different types of impacts: structural, operational, and performance-related. We show the feasibility of the proposed approach by discussing a software prototype implementing it, a case study involving artificially-generated data from a standard ERP procure-to-pay process, and a case study using real-world data from a loan application process. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Subgroup testing for change-plane Cox models in heterogeneous credit risk data
abstract: Change-plane analysis has emerged as an effective tool to detect subgroups with distinct effects on the response of interest. Notably, the change-plane Cox model has gained significance in the subgroup analysis of survival data. Testing for the existence of a change plane can provide valuable insights into optimal decisions for the specific subgroups. However, classical supremum testing methods often suffer from limited efficiency in practical. To address this drawback, we propose a novel testing procedure designed to enhance statistical power. Our approach calculates the weighted average of the squared score test statistic (WAST) over the space of parameter that defines the subgroup, significantly improving power in practice. Moreover, we derive the asymptotic distributions of the test statistic under both the null and local alternative hypotheses. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated by extensive simulation studies, exhibiting better size control and higher power than existing testing approaches. Additionally, we illustrate the practical application of our approach using the Lending club loan dataset and the German credit dataset, showing its ability to identify subgroups with different default risks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Quantifying the safe operating space of Chinese provinces through a dual-dimension water planetary boundary and trade framework
abstract: Quantifying human water use relative to planetary boundaries is critical for limiting hydrological degradation. Here, we integrated a dual-dimension framework for blue- and grey-water planetary boundaries with virtual water trade analysis to assess water-related pressures across 30 Chinese provinces from 2002 to 2017. Grey water footprints dominated changes in boundary transgression, reaching a maximum in 2012 and declining by 49% by 2017 following the implementation of stringent national pollution control policies. This massive biophysical relief increased the number of provinces operating within the regional safe space from 10 in 2012 to 17 in 2017. Notably, no province transgressed the blue-water boundary alone, indicating that assessments excluding grey water may overlook the principal source of water-related boundary exceedance. Cumulative stress revealed hidden biophysical risks where aggregate pressure exceeds the regional boundary despite individual components remaining compliant. Highly stressed exporting regions such as Hebei support consumption in wealthier importing regions, including Beijing. The import dependence index and the export contribution index demonstrated that provinces with high export contribution remain in transgression, while provinces with high import dependence improved but rarely entered the absolute safe operating space. Structural decomposition analysis suggested that consumption structure shifts, rather than technological efficiency gains alone, drove the post-2012 restoration. These findings support the development of spatially differentiated regulatory strategies that align production, consumption and trade within regional hydrological limits. © 2026

title: Disruptive technological innovation strategies in manufacturing based on strategic niche management
abstract: Disruptive technological innovation (DTI) in the manufacturing industry holds significant economic and strategic value. However, traditional innovation management frameworks based on Strategic Niche Management (SNM) theory struggle to accurately capture members’ decision-making behaviors and the “valley of death” phenomenon. This study focuses on the technology supply side to analyze the strategic decisions of manufacturing enterprises, research and development (R&D) institutions, and government in the DTI process. Based on SNM theory, we construct a delayed differential game model with niche differentiation to analyze the optimal strategies and benefits of all members. Through dynamic system stability analysis and controller-based simulations, we investigate the dynamic evolution patterns of the overall technological innovation system and derive the boundary threshold for escaping the “valley of death”. Furthermore, we conduct numerical simulations to examine the influence of different parameters on benefits and extend the model to a nonlinear technology accumulation environment. Finally, a case study is conducted to illustrate the consistency between the model conclusions and real-world observations. We find that DTI levels and total system benefits increase with niche evolution. However, when the decline in technological reserves surpasses new technological accumulation, the system enters a low-level dynamic equilibrium known as the “valley of death”. This phenomenon typically occurs at the end and transition phases of niches. Government subsidies serve as an effective incentive, significantly enhancing the engagement of manufacturing enterprises and R&D institutions. Increased time delay, self-benefit distribution coefficient, effort response coefficient, and technological sensitivity coefficient positively influence the benefits of all members. Furthermore, under a nonlinear technology accumulation environment, DTI exhibits a Matthew effect: fields with high endogenous technological growth rates accelerate their development, while those with low endogenous growth rates are highly prone to falling into the “valley of death”. Overall, we construct a DTI ecosystem for manufacturing based on SNM theory. It reveals the stages and causes of the “valley of death” and advances the application of SNM in managing DTI. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Mechanistic interpretability of Mamba's selective gate in financial markets: A leakage-controlled study
abstract: Selectively gated state-space models (SSMs), notably Mamba, are increasingly used for financial time series, yet how they internally represent market regimes (bull, bear, sideways) remains opaque. This paper applies Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) to a six-layer Mamba trained on approximately twenty-one years of daily data for a point-in-time set of S&P 500 constituents plus macroeconomic and Fama-French factors, decomposing per-layer hidden states with Top-K Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs). Our central contribution is methodological and cautionary. A prior, uncontrolled configuration recovered market regimes from SAE features at F1 = 1.00. Under a controlled protocol that (i) removes the three input features that overlap the HMM label definition, (ii) disables the auxiliary regime-classification head, (iii) uses a point-in-time constituent universe, and (iv) evaluates against labels disjoint from the inputs, the same regime label is recovered at only F1 = 0.398, indistinguishable from a logistic baseline on raw inputs (0.435) and from an SAE trained on a randomly initialized, untrained Mamba (0.364). A 2 × 2 attribution grid shows the near-perfect result is an interaction of auxiliary supervision and label-defining inputs: neither factor alone exceeds F1 ∼ 0.40. Effect sizes with block-bootstrap inference show the residual selective-gate (Delta t) regime effect is statistically detectable but economically negligible and uniform across layers rather than layer-specialized; the apparent polysemanticity gradient disappears under continuous, theory-grounded measures. We contribute a reproducible leakage-control protocol for interpretability evaluation of financial SSMs, a quantified demonstration that previously reported regime structure is a label-contamination artifact, and a modest economically grounded feature subset that genuinely survives the controls. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Balancing productivity and safety: a risk-aware framework for human-robot collaborative workflows
abstract: This paper addresses the Assembly Line Balancing Problem (ALBP) in the context of Human-Robot Collaboration (HRC), integrating task failure risks through Process Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (PFMEA)-inspired framework. The framework captures multiple categories of failure effects including safety and translates them into an Alternative Risk Priority Number (ARPN). A Constraint Programming (CP)-based optimization model is developed at the tactical level of decision-making, where task-to-workstation and workforce allocation is determined. Unlike existing research focused mainly on design-phase risk assessments or dynamic operational level controls, this study embeds ARPN directly into the tactical ALBP model, enabling a bi-objective optimization of Cycle Time (CT) and failure risk. Additionally, a safety-aware constraint is introduced to limit the severity of safety consequences during parallel human-cobot task execution. Computational experiments across diverse assembly configurations reveal the role of human skills and cobots in objectives trade-off. They also demonstrate the model's ability to reduce hazardous task overlaps, especially under limited worker skill availability. By establishing risk-informed decision-making at the tactical layer, the study advances HRC-ALBP modelling toward safe and productive assembly systems, thereby bridging the gap between theoretical optimization frameworks and practical safety requirements. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Digital service nudges and consumer adoption of reusable packaging in online retailing: From convenience to circular responsibility
abstract: Online retailers increasingly offer reusable express packaging, but adoption remains difficult because sustainable options can conflict with the convenience expectations that define online retailing. This article examines reusable packaging adoption as a circular retail service conversion problem. Across three studies with adult online shoppers, we test how digital service nudges and responsibility framing influence adoption through perceived service friction, perceived environmental efficacy, and sustainable service trust, and how these effects depend on return convenience. Study 1 uses a quota-based, post-stratification-weighted survey to show that decision-relevant service nudges reduce perceived service friction and increase adoption intention, while responsibility framing increases perceived environmental efficacy and sustainable service trust. Study 2 uses a discrete choice experiment to estimate trade-offs among nudge timing, return convenience, deposit/refund rules, delivery delay, environmental benefit visibility, and responsibility framing. Study 3 uses an incentivized simulated checkout task to test behaviorally consequential reusable-packaging choice at the decision point. The results show that return convenience and deposit clarity are stronger adoption drivers than generic environmental claims, and that consumers penalize delivery delay more strongly than they reward verified environmental-benefit information. Decision-point nudges increase reusable-packaging checkout choice more than post-checkout reminders, especially when return convenience is high. The findings contribute to retail service convenience, digital nudging, and circular retailing research by showing that sustainable retail adoption depends on service-touchpoint design, not only on environmental attitudes. We position the model as a middle-range service-conversion framework grounded in service convenience, limited-attention decision-making, and sustainable-consumption efficacy and trust. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: One cart, many channels: How real-time inventory visibility shapes trust and purchase continuity in cross-border omnichannel retail
abstract: This study isolates inventory data latency as an operational primitive of omnichannel retail, evaluating its impact on cross-channel purchase continuity and consumer trust. Utilizing a dual field design, a randomized customer-level feature-flag experiment was coupled with a staggered rollout of real-time inventory visibility (RTIV) infrastructure across 142 store nodes, capturing 812,406 sessions from 96,318 loyalty customers. Multilevel logistic regressions and Cox survival frameworks demonstrated that transitioning from a 4-h batch baseline to a 60-s real-time window significantly increased checkout completion rates from 34.7% to 41.9% (F = 256.63, p < 0.001; OR = 1.71) and suppressed the instantaneous hazard of cart abandonment by 26% (HR = 0.74, p < 0.01). Parallel mediation profiling confirmed that this operational lift functioned through behavioral trust restoration rather than technical page-rendering speed; real-time visibility systematically minimized programmatic verification loops, reducing behavioral Price-Check Exits from 22.6% to 9.8% (F = 190.45, p < 0.001). Cross-level interactions showed that performance gains concentrated heavily within time-sensitive buy-online-pickup-in-store paths (OR = 1.45, p < 0.01). High-dimensional stacked Difference-in-Differences models and price dispersion sensitivity matrices confirmed the causal robustness of these findings against localized promotional, competitive, and pricing confounders. Financially, the empirical conversion lift offsets upfront cloud and micro-services infrastructure costs, projecting a clear 13.8-month capital payback horizon. This study replaces traditional psychometric scales with objective digital trace logs, proving that underlying data processing latency acts as a structural constraint on corporate conversion velocity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A dynamic, physics-driven life cycle model for citrus supply chain: Evidence from a South Africa–Netherlands maritime trade route
abstract: Agri-food chains, especially fruit, produce about 10% of global GHG emissions, with more than half arising after harvest. Yet current methods, such as life cycle assessment (LCA), lack the spatial, temporal and physiological detail needed to resolve stage-specific drivers of environmental impact. We aim to overcome these limitations by developing a spatio-temporal, physics-based life cycle model that quantifies climate change (CC) and fossil resource use (RU,f) impacts for individual fruits and shipments across a transcontinental maritime supply chain. The proposed framework is demonstrated using a case study of the citrus supply chain connecting production in South Africa to consumption in the Netherlands. We show that variability among fruits and between shipments substantially alters CC and RU,f impact outcomes, demonstrating the need for dynamic rather than static supply-chain assessment. Energy use, maritime transport and food loss dominate impacts, with the farm-to-packhouse and overseas shipping stages contributing up to 0.5 kg CO₂-eq kg⁻¹ and 2 MJ kg⁻¹ of fruit consumed, depending on local conditions and cold-chain management. Stage-specific interventions, such as reducing field heat prior to forced-air cooling or increasing shipping temperatures from −1 °C to 1–3 °C under validated phytosanitary conditions, can meaningfully lower impacts. This dynamic framework offers a more realistic basis for identifying and achieving feasible decarbonization in global fruit supply systems. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier B.V. title: Data-driven virtual engine framework for predicting performance and emissions of biomass waste-derived biofuel engine
abstract: This research study aims to develop virtual engine models with biofuel blends to forecast their characteristics in terms of combustion, performance and emission by employing multimodal data driven modelling through artificial neural networks. In addition to training the artificial neural network-based virtual engine models with experimental datasets, they were subjected to hyperparameter optimization thereby determining the correlation between input and output parameters. A combustion endoscope captured the in-cylinder combustion flames during the experiment while the digital image processing technique identified the average flame pixel intensity at maximum burning conditions and incorporated them into the machine learning models. A superior combustion efficiency, performance and exhaust emission was exhibited in a blend comprising 90% Gasoline and 10% pine oil than observed in other biofuel combinations. The artificial neural network biofuel engine models that were rigorously trained and hyperparameter optimized precisely forecasted the combustion, performance and emission characteristics of all the biofuel blends with coefficient of determination values ranging between 0.97 and 0.99, while the mean absolute percentage error values range between 0.4% and 5.2% and the root mean square error values ranging between 0.04 and 3.2. The precise performance and error metrics indicates the efficacy of the hyperparameter-optimized neural networks in predicting the characteristics of biofuel blended spark ignition engine. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Multi-cue judgments of food healthfulness: Evidence for distinct consumer decision strategies
abstract: Consumers frequently evaluate the healthfulness of packaged foods based on multiple on-pack cues presented simultaneously. While prior research has extensively examined individual signals such as nutrition labels or claims, less is known about how consumers integrate competing information and whether they rely on consistent or heterogeneous decision strategies. This study addresses this gap by investigating how different types of product-related cues jointly shape perceived healthfulness and by identifying distinct patterns of cue weighting across consumers. Using a mixed-methods design, we first conducted focus groups to explore how consumers conceptualize healthfulness in real-world evaluation contexts. Building on these insights, a full-profile conjoint experiment with a UK sample recruited by quota sampling on age and gender quantified trade-offs among four on-pack cues: ingredient composition, health-related claims, calorie information, and vitamin tables. At the aggregate level, ingredient-related information exerted the strongest influence, followed by claims and vitamin information, while calorie information played a more limited role. However, segmentation based on individual-level importance weights revealed three distinct health inference strategies: consumers primarily guided by ingredient simplicity, those anchored in energy-related information, and those relying on claim-based cues validated by nutrition tables. Accounting for these strategies substantially improved explanatory power, indicating that heterogeneity in healthfulness judgments is systematic rather than random. The findings contribute to research on consumer information processing by demonstrating that perceived healthfulness reflects distinct, strategy-based patterns of cue weighting rather than uniform cue effects and suggest the need for more nuanced approaches to food labeling and retail communication. © 2026 The Authors

title: SPSS concept customization driven by full-service scenarios with validation through an improved COMA and supersystem digital twins
abstract: With the development of next-generation information technologies, smart product-service system (SPSS) has gradually emerged as an effective alternative to traditional product-service system for realizing value co-creation among stakeholders. The flexible integration of smart connected products and embedded digital services enables differentiated customization of SPSS concepts, making it an important research topic. However, most existing studies on customization focus primarily on service content in requirement analysis, with limited consideration of service processes and service scenarios. This focus confines requirement representation to a static perspective, limiting the ability to response differentiated and scenario-dependent requirements. Accordingly, this paper proposes a scenario-driven SPSS concept customization framework, with the objective of deriving more well performance SPSS concepts in full-service scenarios. First, stakeholders’ personalized requirements are elicited and mapped to personalized full-service scenarios through requirement-scenario mapping matrix. Second, to address conflicts among optimization objectives across scenarios and stakeholders, a multi-objective optimization model for scenario-driven SPSS concept customization is constructed. Then, the counterfactual multi-agent policy gradients (COMA) method is introduced and further improved to enable the dynamic solution. The improvements significantly extend the standard COMA by introducing contribution-guided sequential decision-making, Bi-LSTM-encoded joint action representation for evaluation network during centralized training, and scalarized multi-objective reward. As a result, the coordinated optimal global SPSS customized concept is generated across multiple scenarios. Third, to verify the performance of the customized concept in a rapid, cost-effective, and efficient manner, supersystem digital twin is introduced to develop the virtual prototype and scenario model. Finally, a case study involving an electric van smart product-service system for urban last-mile logistics distribution is conducted to validate the proposed framework, with experimental comparisons and in-depth analysis demonstrating its effectiveness and reliability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: An Analysis of Mobility Styles and Carsharing Adoption Intentions in Major Urban Areas of Japan: Evidence from Tokyo, Osaka, and Kanagawa
abstract: This study links mobility styles with carsharing intentions and next-generation vehicle preferences in urban Japan. An online survey of licensed drivers in Tokyo Metropolis, Kanagawa Prefecture, and Osaka Prefecture captured mode use frequencies and stated preferences by travel purpose. Cluster analysis identified three mobility styles: private-car users, public-transport users, and a diversified, high-carsharing group. The diversified profile combined high carsharing participation with high private-car ownership, indicating that carsharing can complement rather than replace existing car access. Random Forest results indicate that age, car usage frequency, and income best distinguish carsharing users from non-users. Carsharing preferences varied substantially by stated-use context. For daily and business trips, most respondents prefer carsharing stations within 400 m and short distances; for tourism and hometown visiting, they accept longer access to carsharing stations and longer trips. Compact and Kei cars (Japanese light vehicles) in Japan dominate daily use, while minivans and SUVs gain importance for leisure. Gasoline and hybrid vehicles are most preferred, with limited willingness to pay extra for electric vehicles. The findings support segment- and purpose-specific carsharing station placement, fleet composition, and gradual electrification strategies in mature, transit-rich metropolitan areas. © 2026 Hong Kong Society for Transportation Studies

title: Unpacking the speed of MNE Internationalization: theoretical insights and future directions
abstract: The phenomenon of multinational enterprises (MNEs) internationalization speed as a time-based dimension has drawn significant attention from international business researchers over the last two decades. However, the theoretical foundations and synthesis of the literature remain fragmented, thus calling for a critical assessment and review. We use an inductive approach and qualitative content analysis to review 122 articles published in prominent international business and management journals. We highlight conceptualization issues and provide a theoretical synthesis of the literature on antecedents and outcomes of internationalization speed. Finally, we provide future research directions based on the gaps in the existing literature. © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier Inc. title: The enhanced ARAS method within the interval-valued neutrosophic set framework: a novel approach for climate change performance assessment
abstract: Climate change is a global crisis caused by both natural and man-made activities. Global urgent precautions like environmentally sustainable policies, strategies for the adaptation of renewable energy, and public incentive arrangements should be taken to prevent the harmful effects of increasing greenhouse gases, including carbon emissions. For this reason, many parties, such as policy makers, academics, and researchers, are conducting many studies to analyze the current situation of the countries and the issues that need to be focused on urgently. Different from other studies, this study presents the enhanced Additive Ratio Assessment method in the interval-valued neutrosophic set environment (IVN-ARAS) and integrates the enhanced IVN-ARAS method with the interval-valued neutrosophic cross-entropy (IVN-cross-entropy) method. The applicability and effectiveness of the presented method are demonstrated in the environmental performance of G20 countries in terms of climate change. For this purpose, the linguistic data in the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) is analyzed, and the new ranking scores are recalculated within an interval-valued neutrosophic set (IVNS) environment. Due to the uncertainty in the index variables, IVNS and entropy methods are preferred. In this context, index variables are weighted with the IVN-cross-entropy method, and country rankings and new ranking values are found with the enhanced IVN-ARAS method. Then, the validity of the country rankings from the enhanced IVN-ARAS method is tested with sensitivity and comparative analyses. Additionally, the IVN-ARAS method and CCPI rankings of the G20 countries are compared. The tests performed have shown that the presented method provides reliable and effective decisions in solving the decision problem under consideration. The findings also demonstrate that the uncertainty in the data is analyzed better using interval-valued neutrosophic numbers (IVNNs). Additionally, this study contributes to understanding the position of countries in combating climate change and developing sustainable policies in an uncertain environment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Robust firm-level revenue forecasting using stacked hybrid ensemble frameworks: Evidence from the semiconductor industry
abstract: Accurate revenue forecasting is essential for financial planning, resource allocation, and strategic decision-making in the volatile semiconductor industry. This study proposes the Stacked Hybrid Ensemble (SHE) framework, a novel forecasting architecture that integrates long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, Transformer models, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) to predict monthly revenue for Taiwan-listed semiconductor firms. Our approach incorporates time series decomposition to analyze trend, seasonality, and residual components, and examines how firm size impacts forecast accuracy. The proposed SHE framework combines stacking ensemble with a dynamic weighting mechanism to adaptively fuse model predictions. Experimental results demonstrate that SHE outperforms all individual models across four error metrics, achieving up to a 35.4% improvement in mean squared error (MSE). Through rigorous statistical validation using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, we confirm that SHE’s performance superiority is systematic and statistically significant ((Formula presented) ) across all 26 companies, providing high reliability for practical applications. For business practitioners and investors, these findings offer substantial value: (1) financial managers can enhance budgeting accuracy and cash-flow planning; (2) operations directors can improve production scheduling and inventory management; and (3) investors gain more reliable tools for company valuation and risk assessment. The framework’s consistent performance across different firm sizes makes it particularly valuable for portfolio analysis and supply-chain decision-making in the cyclical semiconductor sector. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Does circular transformation matter for firm value?
abstract: Corporate adoption of circular solutions has become a prominent pathway for generating new sources of value. This study examines the value-shaping effects of corporate circular transformation using panel data for 351 Chinese listed companies spanning 2015–2024. Five circular transformation indicators based on more than 7000 annual reports and corporate social responsibility reports were constructed. Results show that circular transformation significantly enhances firm value. Among specific circular practices, circular material substitution exerts the strongest positive effect, followed by product life extension and macro-strategic response, whereas circular working modes do not exhibit a significant influence on firm value. The analysis further identifies investor sentiment and supply chain resilience as mediating mechanisms, alongside positive moderating effect of digital transformation and institutional pressure. These findings provide important implications for promoting circular transformation at the micro level. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: ORBIT-FL: Scene-aware and budget-adaptive federated continual learning for multi-UAV environmental monitoring
abstract: Multi-Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) systems are increasingly critical for large-scale environmental monitoring, offering agile data acquisition through distributed sensing. However, applying state-of-the-art deep learning to these systems is hindered by the impracticability of centralized data transmission due to privacy concerns and communication limitations. While Federated Learning (FL) presents a promising decentralized alternative, standard FL approaches are inadequate for the unique challenges of real-world UAV deployments. These challenges include highly heterogeneous non-IID data distributions with few-shot labels, the need for continual adaptation to evolving sensing tasks without catastrophic forgetting, and strict, disparate onboard resource constraints. To address these issues in a unified manner, this paper proposes ORBIT-FL, an orbit/scene-aware, retrieval-augmented, and budget-adaptive FL framework. ORBIT-FL departs from single-model convergence, instead maintaining a composable model universe. It tackles non-IID and few-shot scenarios via a scene-conditioned hyper-adapter that generates lightweight, personalized parameters based on privacy-preserving context tokens. To support evolving missions, it introduces a retrieval-augmented federated continual learning mechanism using a time-indexed memory graph of semantic prototypes. Furthermore, ORBIT-FL incorporates budget-conditioned training and anytime inference routing to dynamically adapt to the heterogeneous compute and energy constraints of different UAV platforms. This framework enables robust, privacy-preserving environmental awareness across diverse and dynamic UAV fleets. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Discovering Relationships in Data Lakes Using Large Language Models: An Industrial Case
abstract: Data lakes rely on metadata to remain usable, yet this metadata is often limited or weakly informative for column relationship discovery, especially in ERP-derived datasets with coded or abbreviated schema labels. We propose ColRel, a two-stage method that builds column embeddings from metadata and data available at ingestion time. In difficult cases, such as coded schemata, business dictionaries help interpret column names and support the generation of short natural-language descriptions used in the second stage. Experiments on public benchmarks and an industrial ERP dataset show that ColRel is particularly effective in semantically related, weak-signal settings. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: FlightLLM: few-shot interval forecasting for airline passenger and baggage demand
abstract: Airline demand forecasting for passengers and baggage is critical for resource and service planning. As airline networks move toward higher density and complexity, travel patterns vary widely across routes, and historical demand is hard to share or transfer. At the same time, frequent route launches, seasonal shifts, and schedule changes create many cold-start routes with scarce data, posing significant challenges for forecasting. Under few-shot conditions, previous forecasting methods lack sufficient accuracy and stability, and deep learning models are uninterpretable and fail to incorporate aviation business rules or quantify uncertainty. To address these challenges, this study proposes FlightLLM, an LLM-driven two-phase framework for few-shot airline demand interval forecasting that integrates business-feasibility constraints and business-related priors into the learning and adaptation process. The offline phase generates high-quality pseudo-labels using a five-stage search guided by process reward modeling, followed by curriculum-based self-training and meta-learning to build a generalized initializer. In the online phase, the model rapidly adapts to cold-start routes using minimal real-world samples. It produces joint passenger and baggage forecasts in an interpretable “point estimate ± interval half-width” format. The proposed method introduces a new way for few-shot demand forecasting by leveraging large language models to unify data-driven generalization and rule-constrained generation, where business-feasibility constraints and business-related priors are embedded into interval prediction via meta-initialization and reliability-aware adaptation. Empirical evaluations on real cold-start route data show that FlightLLM achieves a substantially more favorable coverage–width trade-off than conventional interval baselines while maintaining competitive point-forecasting accuracy, underscoring the insight that effective few-shot demand forecasting requires the complementary strengths of empirical adaptability and operational consistency. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Development and characterization of an active and smart gelatin-alginate based packaging enriched with eggplant anthocyanin-rich extract
abstract: Bio-functional films were developed based on a gelatin-alginate hydrocolloid matrix, incorporated with anthocyanin-rich powder extracted from eggplant peels at different concentrations (0.5-2 mg/mL). The incorporation of anthocyanin-powder induced significant modifications in the physicochemical and structural properties of the films. FTIR, XRD and DSC/TGA analyses revealed that anthocyanins promoted intermolecular interactions within the matrix, leading to a reorganization of the polymer structure, reduced crystallinity and enhanced thermal stability. These structural changes were associated with more homogeneous morphology and modified mechanical behavior, as evidenced by variations in tensile strength and elongation at break. In addition, anthocyanins incorporation significantly improved the optical properties, reducing lightness (L*) and yellowness (b*), and increasing redness (a*) of the films as well as the total color difference (ΔE), and subsequently, increasing their opacity, contributing to the global enhancement of the light barrier of the films.Regarding functional properties, the incorporation of anthocyanin-powder enhanced biological properties of the films in a dose-dependent manner at multiple endpoints: increased antioxidant activities against DPPH, ABTS and reducing power, in addition to antibacterial capacities against Gram positive (Bacillus cereus and Staphylococcus aureus) and Gram negative (Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherishia coli) bacteria, which was directly associated with their phenolic content. Moreover, the films exhibited pronounced pH-responsive colorimetric behavior and high sensitivity to ammonia, enabling rapid and visible changes in color which highlight their potential as intelligent indicators for monitoring food freshness.Overall, our findings demonstrate that gelatin-alginate films incorporating anthocyanin extract powder from eggplants peels holds as promise dual-functionality as smart and active packaging, suitable for real application on food products in order to enhance the quality and extending their shelf-life. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Evaluating the Parallelization Capabilities of State-of-the-Art Agentic Large Language Models
abstract: Advancements in large language models (LLMs), including base model improvements, various chain-of-thought approaches, and agentic tool use, have substantially increased their capacity for autonomous programming and software engineering. Their performance on such tasks is widely studied, tracked, and publicized; however, the majority of evaluations are based on Python, Java, or other high-level languages, with application domains in the web, business logic, or data analysis. From the perspective of parallel language, programming interface (API), and systems research in the field of high-performance computing (HPC), the question arises whether these results translate to the capability of effectively parallelizing applications. In order to answer this question, we design and carry out a comprehensive study, tasking 8 state-of-the-art LLM agents with the parallelization of 11 small-to-medium-sized HPC benchmark applications. For each, we evaluate shared-memory, distributed memory, accelerator, and hybrid parallelization goals with appropriate APIs, and multiple agent invocations are performed for every data point to quantify random variance in outcome quality. Our experimental setup includes validation in several steps, comprising semantic inspection, compilation, monitored execution, internal result checking, and external verification via known-good comparisons. For all valid programs, we also perform comparative performance benchmarking on a production supercomputer. We synthesize overall conclusions and quantify to what extent parallelization performance of LLMs correlates with time and tokens spent. All benchmark code, experiment and evaluation scripts, and generated data are fully available for analysis, replication and extension. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Reinventing the package holiday: Consumer preferences and optimal pricing for hotel room upgrades
abstract: We examine a tour operator initiative enabling consumers to select their hotel room before departure for a supplementary fee. Using a stated-preference discrete choice experiment with 691 UK package holidaymakers, we estimate conditional and mixed logit models to identify drivers of upgrade acceptance, derive willingness-to-pay (WTP) estimates, and compute the uptake probability as a continuous function of the fee. Room facilities command the highest WTP (£8.04 per unit), and room location the second-highest (£3.67 per unit); hotel location is insignificant. The revenue-maximizing fee is £33.1 per person, yielding a predicted uptake of 54.1%. Latent class analysis identifies three consumer segments with distinct price sensitivities, and segment-specific revenue optima reveal meaningful variation across hotel categories, lengths of stay, and party types, supporting differentiated fee structures. These findings provide tour operators with a replicable framework for maximizing ancillary revenue from upgrade initiatives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Are corporate venture capital and R&D complements or substitutes? A process view of absorptive capacity
abstract: While both corporate venture capital (CVC) and R&D are essential vehicles for innovation, the literature has largely overlooked whether and when they act as complements or substitutes in generating firm innovation outcomes. Drawing on a process view of absorptive capacity, this paper argues that the CVC-R&D relationship depends on how firms coordinate knowledge acquisition, assimilation, transformation, and exploitation. Analyzing a sample of US firms engaged in CVC or R&D activities from 1993 to 2016, this paper finds that CVC and R&D act as substitutes in generating innovation outcomes. Furthermore, this paper finds that the substitutive relationship weakens when firms use formalized and dedicated CVC structures, and it shifts toward complementarity as firms accumulate CVC investing experience. This paper contributes to the CVC-R&D relationship literature by highlighting the role of absorptive capacity process coordination, and to the organizational learning literature by showing how experiential and deliberate learning mechanisms moderate this relationship. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Optimal service and charging scheduling of electric vehicle demand-responsive connectors considering multiple trips
abstract: Demand-responsive connectors have emerged as a promising solution to the first- and last-mile transit connectivity challenge, particularly for linking metro stations with surrounding communities. This paper investigates the optimal service and charging scheduling problem of electric vehicle demand-responsive connector (EV-DRC) system, in which each vehicle serving multiple consecutive trips to minimize total cost (i.e., sum of the vehicle deployment and daily operational costs). This multi-trip electric vehicle routing problem (MTEVRP) is first formulated as an arc flow model, and then reformulated via Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition into a set-covering problem that can be solved by column generation. Subsequently, we propose an exact branch-and-price algorithm incorporating tailored acceleration strategies, including route classification, column selection, and interior point stabilization. Extensive computational experiments demonstrate the algorithm’s exceptional effectiveness − it achieves global optimality in 29 out of 30 test instances with up to 60 customer nodes, while reducing the runtime by a maximum of 71% compared to a standard branch-and-price. Sensitivity analyses reveal key insights regarding the impacts of vehicle capacity, battery specifications, and customer time windows on operational performance. These findings provide valuable guidance for operators to design economically viable EV-DRC services that meet high standards of customer satisfaction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Solar solutions to double dividends: Examining the impact of China's photovoltaic poverty alleviation pilot on pollution and carbon emissions from county-level cities
abstract: Understanding whether renewable energy programs with social objectives can generate joint pollution and carbon benefits is important for assessing their broader environmental value. This study evaluates China's Photovoltaic Poverty Alleviation Pilot (PPAP) using panel data for 2594 counties from 2010 to 2023 and a multi-period difference-in-differences design, supplemented by heterogeneity-robust estimators. PPAP reduces county-level pollution and carbon intensity. County innovation capacity and household wealth accumulation may help unlock the environmental potential. The NEBP analysis finds more evident environmental gains in counties with favorable solar conditions and moderate slopes, as well as in poverty-stricken counties. Higher information and stronger local governance capacity are also associated with more pronounced environmental benefits. These findings support regionally differentiated policy expansion that aligns project deployment with local resource conditions and implementation capacity. More broadly, PPAP offers lessons for linking poverty alleviation with low-carbon rural development in less-developed areas. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Enhancing flood impact assessment accuracy: A comparison of IRIO-Flood predictions using HAZUS- and insurance claims-based business interruption estimates
abstract: While input–output models are widely used to assess the economic impacts of natural disasters, their results strongly depend on how disaster shocks are specified. This paper examines two alternative characterizations of flood-induced business interruptions, and their effect on total economic losses. We compare restoration time estimates derived from the Hazus-Flood framework with a novel approach based on micro-level insurance claims data, which allows for partial reductions in plants’ productive capacity during the restoration phase, rather than assuming full inoperability.Using georeferenced plant-level data and high-resolution flood maps, we calibrate flood shocks for four major Italian flood events and simulate their propagation through the economy using the IRIO-Flood model. We find that Hazus-based specifications generally produce larger and more dispersed estimates of productive capacity contractions, leading to greater GDP and sectoral output losses – particularly in the short term – and to stronger spillovers to regions not directly affected by the flood. Despite these substantial differences in magnitude, both approaches identify broadly similar patterns in terms of the most affected sectors and regions, with discrepancies emerging more frequently when considering the medium-term propagation of losses.These results highlight the importance of accurate shock specification and suggest that the two proposed methods can be viewed as complementary tools for flood impact and risk assessment. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: A decomposition-aware dual-stream framework with component-adaptive masked self-supervision for industrial time series forecasting
abstract: Accurate forecasting of key performance indicators is essential for the safe and efficient operation of complex industrial processes. However, industrial time series are commonly affected by non-stationary dynamics, weak periodicity, complex inter-variable coupling, and label scarcity caused by low-frequency offline assays. These characteristics limit the effectiveness of conventional supervised forecasting models and frequency-decomposition methods that rely on strong periodic assumptions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes DeMAP, a decomposition-aware dual-stream framework with component-adaptive masked self-supervision for industrial time series forecasting. Specifically, a Decomposition-Aware Dual-stream Network (DeDNet) decouples process signals into long-term trend and transient residual components. Adaptively learned graphs are used to model trend-related topological dependencies, while multi-scale residual convolutions capture high-frequency local fluctuations. A trend-guided cross-attention mechanism further fuses heterogeneous component representations, and task-specific prediction heads support deterministic point forecasting and probabilistic interval forecasting. To improve representation learning under limited labels, a Component-Adaptive Masked Pre-training (CAMP) strategy is designed with different masking tasks for trend and residual components, enabling the model to exploit latent spatiotemporal structures from unlabeled data. Experiments on the Tennessee Eastman process and a real metal smelting process demonstrate that DeMAP consistently improves deterministic prediction accuracy, interval prediction reliability, and robustness under reduced training data. The results indicate that decomposition-aware modeling and component-specific self-supervision provide an effective solution for industrial forecasting under non-stationarity and label scarcity. © 2026

title: Development and validation of an ATP degradation model for predicting K-value progression in chilled greenling under variable temperature conditions
abstract: Temperature fluctuations during refrigerated distribution can accelerate postmortem ATP degradation and complicate freshness management; therefore, a temperature-responsive model is needed to predict K-value progression under practical cold-chain conditions. In this study, a temperature-responsive kinetic model was developed to predict the K-value, a widely used indicator of fish freshness, using greenling (Hexagrammos otakii) as the model species. The pooled variable A = ATP + ADP + AMP was modeled as converting to IMP and then to H = HxR + Hx through two first-order processes governed by empirical effective rate coefficients k1 and k2. The coefficients were calibrated at 0 and 5 °C, while 2.5 °C and intermittent 0–5 °C data were reserved for validation. Across the 24 observations reserved for validation, K-value predictions yielded an RMSE of 7.976 percentage points, an MAE of 5.180 percentage points, and an R2 of 0.885. During commercial transport, the representative prediction at approximately 51 h was 12.48%, compared with a measured group median of 11.97%, without parameter re-optimization. The model provides a practical framework for predicting K-value progression in greenling under the examined refrigerated conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: UDA2L: Unsupervised deformation-aware adaptive learning for medical image registration
abstract: Medical image registration plays a key role in diagnosis, therapeutic strategy design, and longitudinal studies. However, the existing methods are prone to misregistration when encountering complex anatomical changes, making it difficult to effectively maintain the topological consistency of anatomical structures. To address these problems, we propose an unsupervised deformation-aware adaptive learning method (UDA2L) for medical image registration, in which deformation information is explicitly used to guide high-risk region perception, hierarchical feature interaction, and consistency regularization. Specifically, an adaptive High-risk Deformation Area-Aware Mechanism (HDA2M) introduces deformation-field gradient information into the attention modeling process, enabling the network to emphasize regions with unstable or large local deformations. A Triple-view Hierarchical Feature Integration (THFI) module jointly integrates fixed-image features, moving-image features, and deformation-field representations through a coarse-to-fine pyramid structure, thereby strengthening deformation-appearance coupling and capturing both fine-grained anatomical details and global contextual information. Moreover, Cross-Cycle Consistency (C3) learning imposes bidirectional deformation consistency and residual-level reconstruction constraints to improve local alignment accuracy and enhance the topological stability of the learned deformation field. Experimental results on multiple 3D brain MRI image datasets (including three single-modality and one cross-modality) show that UDA2L achieves relatively ideal performance and efficiency in the image registration task, demonstrating its application prospects in this field. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Selective partitioning of plant proteins during emulsification impairs foam stability: conformational changes of aqueous-phase residues relative to animal proteins
abstract: The foam instability restricts the industrial application of plant protein-based whipped cream. Most current studies focus on the intrinsic properties of proteins, while there remains a lack of in-depth understanding regarding whether the emulsification process alters the protein composition in the aqueous phase and subsequently affects foaming performance. This study shows that during emulsification, aqueous-phase proteins undergo selective partitioning or depletion, altering remaining protein components and thus determining subsequent foam performance. Using animal proteins (sodium caseinate, SC; goat milk protein, GMP) as benchmarks, emulsions were formulated with plant proteins (pea protein isolate, PPI; soy protein isolate, SPI). Analysis of the results indicated that during emulsification, specific components of plant protein (66–175 kDa and 16 kDa) were preferentially depleted from the aqueous phase. Compared to animal proteins, this selective partitioning led to significant changes in the structure and surface properties of the residual protein in the aqueous phase: an increase of approximately 10% in β-sheet content, formation of more compact aggregates, and a reduction in surface hydrophobicity by over 39%. Ultimately, during whipping, the remaining plant protein exhibited lower diffusion and rearrangement rate constants at the air-water interface, resulting in slower interfacial dynamics, insufficient foam coverage, reduced whipping capacity (287%–308%), and faster foam breakdown. These results suggest that protein molecular characteristics, processing history, and non-protein components may collectively drive the selective partitioning process, with preferential adsorption at the oil-water interface potentially playing a key role. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
