title: Data-center expansion and the dynamic regional redistribution of the water-energy-food stress in Texas
abstract: Data centers are Texas's fastest-growing electricity and water claimants, with interconnection requests exceeding 400 GW against an 86 GW peak. We develop a four-region system dynamics model that endogenizes compute demand, siting, and cooling choice around a within-region allocation cascade with irrigated agriculture as residual claimant. The model is anchored to Texas Water Development Board and ERCOT data and reproducing four independent observations without fitting. Results showed that local siting restraint never relieves nexus pressure. It displaces the buildout into water-scarce agricultural regions in a closed state, or exports the industry once demand turns footloose. Under a drought of record, irrigation absorbs nearly all shortage, accumulating 6.3 million acre-feet of foregone Panhandle supplies, while an 80% irrigation-protection reservation changes nothing. A dry-cooling mandate cuts direct water 78% at a 1.6% indirect penalty, and chip efficiency moves 2050 outcomes more than any policy lever. Governance must target allocation and siting jointly, not volumes alone. © 2026 The Author. Published by Elsevier B.V. title: The influence of mineral composition on coal wettability and pore structure evolution: experimental study and molecular simulation
abstract: The wettability of coal dust is crucial for promoting green mining and clean utilization of coal. However, the mechanism of mineral components in this process remains unclear, hindering the development of the mineral-organic matter synergistic regulation theory. This study combines macro-characterization, Monte Carlo simulations, and molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate the influence patterns of single and composite minerals on the wettability of coal organic matter. A model for the doping of coal organic molecules with minerals was constructed. Parameters such as water adsorption capacity, isothermal adsorption heat, and hydrogen-bond network were analyzed, and the pore-structure evolution induced by composite minerals and water molecules was investigated. The results indicate that the effectiveness of different minerals in enhancing wettability follows this order: quartz > muscovite > calcite > kaolinite > gypsum > pyrite. Water molecules are primarily physically adsorbed, with adsorption capacity positively correlated with isothermal adsorption heat. Mineral surfaces feature both primary and secondary adsorption sites. Composite mineral doping increased the maximum adsorption capacity from 80 mg/g to 120 mg/g, primarily due to enhanced electrostatic forces, hydrogen bond network restructuring, and the transfer of the strongest adsorption sites. Additionally, water molecules preferentially clog pores larger than 4 Å in diameter, resulting in reduced specific surface area, pore volume, and connectivity. These findings provide theoretical insights into the systematic regulation of coal wettability by mineral components and support the advancement of efficient coal dust prevention technologies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: State estimation with unknown input rejection under non-Gaussian disturbances
abstract: In practice, system models are often subject to unmeasurable unknown input disturbances. Furthermore, communication networks are typically corrupted by non-Gaussian noise. To solve the composite disturbance in state estimation, this paper presents a maximum correntropy Kalman filter with unknown input disturbance rejection (MCKF-UIR), without making any prior assumptions about the unknown inputs. Specifically, the equivalent measurement injection is adopted as a disturbance compensation method to suppress the effects of unknown inputs on the state. Based on the modified state equation, this paper constructs an augmented state model using prior state estimates and measurement vectors. A lower-triangular decorrelation transformation is then introduced to eliminate the cross-correlation terms in the error covariance matrix, yielding a block-diagonal covariance structure. Moreover, the maximum correntropy criterion-based (MCC) optimization function along with fixed-point iteration (FPI) approach are employed to derive the optimal gain matrix and state estimate. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that compared with the traditional Kalman filter with unknown input rejection (KF-UIR), the proposed MCKF-UIR exhibits stronger adaptability to compound disturbances comprising both unknown inputs and non-Gaussian noise. Furthermore, it eliminates the need for explicit unknown input estimation and avoids the iterative computations required for solving the MCC-based optimal unknown input estimate, reducing computational complexity. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Thermo-mechanical analysis of energy piles with different pipe configurations using numerical simulations and machine learning models
abstract: Energy piles, which combine structural support and ground heat exchange, are a promising technology for shallow geothermal utilization. However, systematic frameworks for rapidly evaluating the coupled thermo-mechanical responses of energy piles with different pipe configurations remain limited. In this study, five pile configurations, namely U-type, W-type, 2U-type, 3U-type, and double-helix-type, were investigated using a validated three-dimensional thermo-mechanical numerical model. A dataset of 8000 cases was generated through Latin hypercube sampling and a Python-COMSOL automated workflow. Based on this dataset, four machine learning models, including linear regression, random forest, back-propagation neural network, and XGBoost, were developed to rapidly predict outlet water temperature, pile head displacement, and axial forces under different design and operating conditions. Among them, the XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance, with an R2 value of 0.9938 for the training set and 0.9697 for the test set. Then, a systematic comparative framework was established to evaluate the thermo-mechanical performance and parameter sensitivities of different pipe configurations. The results showed that the 2U-type pile achieved the highest heat exchange efficiency owing to its more uniform pipe arrangement. In addition, the sensitivity analysis indicated that the outlet water temperature was mainly governed by inlet water temperature, pile length, mass flow rate, and soil thermal conductivity, whereas pile head load, inlet water temperature, and pile length had significant effects on pile displacement and axial forces. The proposed framework provides an effective tool for rapid prediction, systematic comparison, and preliminary design evaluation of energy piles with different pipe configurations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A balanced WINGS method for power-influence analysis: Simulation-based comparison with DEMATEL
abstract: The WINGS method is derived from DEMATEL and incorporates both the influence among system elements and the power (importance) of each element into causal analysis to provide a more accurate assessment of a system. This study investigates the performance of the WINGS method in comparison with DEMATEL across systems of different sizes. The results show that as the number of elements increases, the effectiveness of the WINGS method decreases due to an imbalance between power and influence, causing its results to gradually converge toward those of DEMATEL. To overcome this limitation, a balanced WINGS (BWINGS) method is proposed, and its performance is evaluated against the two existing methods using Monte Carlo simulation under varying network sizes and inter-factor relationship complexities. The results of statistical tests confirm the scalability and robustness of the proposed method. © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: Beyond wear scar diameter: A multi-technique investigation of lubricity enhancement and tribofilm formation in biodiesel blends with ultra-low sulphur diesel and bio-hydrogenated diesel
abstract: Bio-hydrogenated diesel (BHD) and ultra-low sulphur diesel both exhibit poor intrinsic lubricity owing to the absence of polar functional groups. This study evaluated the lubricity of BHD and petroleum diesel blended with palm methyl ester (PME) and soybean methyl ester (SBME) using the High Frequency Reciprocating Rig test in accordance with ISO 12156-1:2023, with SBME at 2–70% v/v and PME at 2–15% v/v. Complementary surface analyses including 3D laser profilometry, scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, and attenuated total reflectance Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy were employed to characterise wear mechanisms and tribofilm formation.Both pure base fuels exceeded the DOEB lubricity threshold of 460 μm. Addition of 2% v/v biodiesel restored compliance in all blend systems, yet film formation data, wear depth profiles, and ATR-FTIR analysis collectively suggested that this concentration does not sustain reliable surface protection, with intermittent film breakdown and peripheral wear debris deposits persisting throughout the test. A minimum of 5% v/v was required for stable film formation, and 10% v/v for effective suppression of disc material loss. At 2% v/v, SBME produced a significantly lower wear scar diameter than PME in the diesel system (p = 0.001), consistent with earlier and more persistent ester tribofilm formation confirmed by ATR-FTIR, while no statistically significant difference was observed in the BHD system (p = 0.072). From 5% v/v onward, no significant difference was found between feedstocks in either base fuel system (p > 0.05), indicating convergence of tribological performance regardless of feedstock. BHD blends achieved near-complete disc surface protection at 5% SBME while diesel required 10%, attributable to the less competitive adsorption environment of the paraffinic BHD matrix. These findings demonstrate that wear scar diameter alone underestimates actual wear protection at low biodiesel concentrations and support a practical blending recommendation of 5 to 10% v/v for both feedstocks in diesel and BHD fuel systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: An enhanced polar lights optimizer with the near-distance to multi-target strategy and rebound boundary handling for feature selection
abstract: Feature selection can improve predictive accuracy and reduce computational cost in high-dimensional data analysis. However, wrapper-based methods may converge prematurely when the associated discrete search space is large. This study integrates a near-distance to multi-target (NDM) strategy and a rebound boundary handling (RBH) mechanism into the polar lights optimizer (PLO), yielding NPLO. NDM introduces a proximity-aware auxiliary objective for environmental selection, whereas RBH preserves directional information through mirror reflection at a violated bound. On the 12 IEEE CEC 2022 functions, NPLO obtained the best Friedman average ranks of 2.5833 against 11 baseline algorithms and 1.7500 against 11 enhanced competitors, although alternative algorithms remained superior on individual functions. Search-trajectory and population-diversity analyses further characterize its exploration–exploitation behavior. A binary implementation, bNPLO, was evaluated for feature selection on 24 datasets with eight established binary metaheuristics. It achieved the lowest or tied-lowest classification error on most datasets while generally retaining compact feature subsets. These results support the competitiveness of NPLO on the evaluated continuous and discrete problems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Frequency-selective transmission of geopolitical risk to day-ahead electricity prices: Evidence from variational mode decomposition, wavelet transform coherence, and double machine learning
abstract: Electric vehicles, AI data centres, and electrification are raising electricity-demand volatility, while post-2022 conflicts have repeatedly disturbed global fuel markets. This paper studies a hard empirical test: whether geopolitical risk reaches a regulated Chinese provincial market where price caps and administered fuel pricing mute indirect fuel-chain pass-through. In Guangdong day-ahead prices from 2021-11-01 to 2026-06-07, the aggregate signal is weak: 0.038 with the Caldara–Iacoviello composite GPR index and 0.112 with the GPR-threat sub-index. The muted average points to institutional attenuation, with transmission appearing only in selected horizons and fuel states. Variational mode decomposition and wavelet coherence indicate that the relevant relation is concentrated in a short-pulse 2–8 day band: GPR threats and prices co-move with same-band correlation 0.348, and phase arrows show threats leading prices. In the pure-fuel reference specification, double machine learning estimates a positive conditional association for the threat index of 0.078 CNY/MWh per index unit; the association remains positive across carbon, demand, weather, macro-financial, supply-side, bootstrap, and EPU robustness exercises. Walk-forward forecasting indicates statistically significant, state-dependent out-of-sample signal value under the Clark–West nested-model test, concentrated in high-risk periods. Leave-event-out DML counterfactuals show that crisis premia are compound states; within the fuel block, the dominant component follows physical chokepoints, gas for Russia–Ukraine and oil for Hormuz. A cross-market comparison reverses sign in coal-based Shanxi and is strongest in directly disrupted European markets, supporting fuel-chain exposure as the organizing mechanism. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Geopolitical tensions and foreign R&D subsidiaries’ innovation performance: Evidence from emerging economy MNEs
abstract: In an era of intensifying geopolitical rivalries, emerging economy multinational enterprises (EMNEs) face unprecedented challenges in sustaining cross-border innovation, particularly as technological competition becomes increasingly entangled with national security agendas. Integrating the literature on geopolitics in international relations with EMNE subsidiary innovation, this study investigates whether and to what extent inter-country geopolitical tensions influence the innovation performance of EMNEs’ R&D subsidiaries in advanced economies. Using a sample of Chinese listed firms’ foreign R&D subsidiaries, we find that escalating geopolitical tensions between home and host countries significantly reduce the innovation output of these subsidiaries. Furthermore, the number of host-national innovation partners of a foreign R&D subsidiary can help mitigate the negative effect of geopolitical tensions on its innovation pursuits, while its local same-parent sisters can exacerbate this adverse impact. Our study enhances the understanding of how international politics affect EMNE subsidiary innovation and advances the political risk literature by revealing the role of subsidiary-level networks in shaping firm vulnerability to geopolitical disruptions. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Turning Inward and/or Outward: Which socioemotional skills pay for agribusiness entrepreneurs in Nigeria?
abstract: Socioemotional skills programs are widely used to promote economic empowerment, yet their returns may depend on the type of skills targeted and social context. We study this question using a randomized controlled trial (RCT) among 4,500 aspiring agribusiness entrepreneurs in Nigeria within a large-scale government program. Participants were randomly assigned to an interpersonal-skills curriculum, a combined interpersonal and intrapersonal-skills curriculum of the same length, or a control group. Both trainings substantially increase women's business performance, raising average profits by 50%. The two trainings generated broadly similar economic impacts overall. Effects are largest in communities with more liberal gender norms, where women report improvements in interpersonal skills such as empathy and negotiation, and better relational outcomes. Despite large economic gains, we find no corresponding increases in women's empowerment or intrahousehold decision-making. For men, interpersonal-skills training increases household income, while the combined curriculum raises profits but only in the most gender-liberal environments. The results show that the returns to socioemotional skills programs depend not only on which skills are taught, but also on whether prevailing social norms permit individuals to express and deploy those skills. Translating gains into broader empowerment may require complementary programs that relax gender norms. © 2026

title: From fabrication to function: Electrochemical characterization of hyaluronic acid-based biomimetic hydrogels in aqueous ethanol
abstract: Oral flavor perception currently relies predominantly on human sensory evaluation, and artificial sensory systems capable of mimicking oral interfaces remain limited. While hydrogels have been explored as soft substrates, most are designed as passive matrices or signal transducers. Here, we move beyond conventional hydrogel sensors by reconstructing a chemically relevant oral mimetic interface using two indispensable and physiological components of the oral cavity: hyaluronic acid (HA) and mucin. Inspired by biology, we investigate a biomimetic hydrogel that combines human tongue–like properties with electrochemical responsiveness and apply it to aqueous ethanol systems. We demonstrate that this hydrogel functions not merely as a structural mimic but as a dynamic electrochemical interface. Comprehensive characterization of its structure, rheology, and biosafety confirms its suitability as a biomimetic material. Electrochemical analyses further demonstrate its capability to operate as a responsive interfacial in aqueous ethanol environments. The hydrogel exhibits solid-like viscoelastic behavior and good biocompatibility, providing a stable and secure soft interface for studies related to artificial sensory systems. Overall, this work establishes a biomimetic hydrogel for oral-inspired sensing and advances artificial sensory systems toward mechanisms rooted in interfacial biophysics rather than solely pattern-based recognition. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: A knowledge graph–enhanced retrieval-augmented framework for automated SysML model generation in MBSE
abstract: Model-based systems engineering (MBSE) has become an important approach for modelling complex systems. However, transforming natural-language requirements into formal Systems Modeling Language (SysML) models remains difficult because of the complexity, multi-domain coupling, and knowledge-intensive nature of system design. To address this problem, this study proposes a knowledge graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation (KG-RAG) method for automatic SysML model generation. First, a domain-oriented SysML knowledge graph (KG) is constructed on the basis of the SysML metamodel and domain-specific knowledge. Second, a retrieval-augmented prompting strategy is developed to guide a large language model (LLM) in generating structured SysML artefacts under explicit syntactic and semantic constraints. Third, an automated transformation mechanism is established to convert the generated structured artefacts into tool-native editable SysML models. The proposed method is validated through a fixed-wing aircraft flight control system case study. The results show that the method can automatically generate eight types of SysML diagrams, including requirement, block definition, internal block, use case, activity, state machine, sequence, and parametric diagrams. Quantitatively, the automatically generated models achieve an average element-level model coverage rate of 90.42 ± 1.46%. These results indicate that the proposed method can reduce repetitive manual modelling effort and improve modelling efficiency, demonstrating its potential to support practical MBSE-based system design. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Multi-scale design and techno-economic optimization of copper-mesh reactors for methanol steam reforming
abstract: Structured copper-mesh catalysts offer axial heat conduction for endothermic methanol steam reforming (MSR), yet deployment requires optimizing geometry, operating conditions and economics. We present a multi-scale Python framework integrating (i) Peppley-type Langmuir-Hinshelwood kinetics calibrated on 36 points (R2 = 0.955; the lumped Ea = 37.1 kJ mol−1 is an empirical coefficient; the model-free apparent value is 89–96 kJ mol−1). (ii) Finite-volume modeling of the plain-weave unit cell, giving 3-fold radial-to-axial conductivity anisotropy. (iii) A 1-D plug-flow reactor justified by a 270-point dimensionless analysis. (iv) A techno-economic model across 1575 configurations on the measured voidage. Because the dry reformate contains 75–8090 ppm CO, LCOH is route-dependent: 7.7–8.7 $ kg−1 with vacuum-swing adsorption, 2.9–3.5 $ kg−1 feeding a high-temperature PEM directly, and 3.3–3.9 $ kg−1 with two-stage preferential oxidation to 10 ppm for a stationary low-temperature PEM with anode air bleed, each dominated by methanol and electricity. Against two commercial Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 pellets within the same system boundary, the mesh meets the same hydrogen duty in one third of the volume at about 10 % lower cost and 18–28 % lower cost at equal reactor volume, with the gap arising from heat transfer and packing density, not activity. Electricity price is the principal cost driver (S1 = 0.77–0.81), a ranking that is range-dependent, heater efficiency leading under normalized ± 25 % ranges and the methanol price held fixed in the index set; geometry remains decisive for pressure drop, productivity and scale-up. Before route-specific purification is costed, the seven structures are economically indistinguishable, so no optimal structure is claimed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: From conventional multi-vendor failover to adaptive API routing: An industrial experience report on resilient third-party service integration
abstract: High-scale online services often rely on third-party APIs in user-facing flows such as authentication, messaging, payments, fraud detection, and identity verification. Integrating alternate providers and operating conventional failover controls is a common resilience baseline, but redundancy alone does not make provider selection adaptive, explainable, or policy-aware. This paper reports an anonymized industrial experience evolving a conventional multi-vendor SMS-provider failover arrangement in a large marketplace setting into configuration-driven adaptive API routing. The approach uses operation-specific pluggable factor lists to separate routing policy from application code, combines hard eligibility gates with normalized weighted provider scoring, and closes the loop with business-outcome telemetry, decision logs, traffic-shift controls, and recovery safeguards. The report includes de-identified operational evidence, including before/after windows, a representative incident timeline, shadow-mode validation records, policy-tuning history, score-normalization snapshots, provider-attribution examples, feedback-bias controls, and sensitivity analysis. The evidence suggests that adaptive provider routing can reduce dependence on incident-time interpretation when the operation is critical, telemetry volume is sufficient, and organizational controls exist for policy ownership, explainability, and safe traffic movement. The paper concludes with practitioner guidance and transferability conditions for teams considering similar architectures. © 2026

title: Topological focusing in large language models: Alignment-conditioned semantic transition patterns and information quality
abstract: This study proposes the Topological Focusing framework, which models semantic transition probability in large language models (LLMs) as (Formula presented), where α is an empirical focusing exponent. We collected 2055 semantic transitions from GPT-3.5-turbo and GPT-4o under three alignment-expression conditions (Baseline, Aligned, and advanced Reference). Results demonstrate that Euclidean distance explains negligible variance in semantic propagation (R2 < 0.02), while generation probability exhibits robust power-law decay with rank, which is used as an operational proxy for topological reachability. The aligned prompting condition is associated with higher α (2.18 to 6.60) ((Formula presented) = 4.42, (Formula presented) ). Cross-model replication on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, an independent model family with a distinct alignment pipeline, provides convergent evidence for power-law dynamics and condition-associated α amplification (Baseline α = 3.27, Aligned α = 13.40, (Formula presented) = 10.13). A separate temperature-ablation experiment indicates that this pattern is not reproduced by inference-time scaling. In the ablation dataset, α remains invariant across five temperature settings (ANOVA p = 0.296, η2 = 0.004). External validation reveals a stronger positive association between external embedding distance and generation probability under the aligned condition (β = +3.07, p = 0.004): the aligned condition preferentially generates embedding-distant concepts, a pattern consistent with a shift toward utility-oriented generation. The stronger positive distance–probability association was consistently observed across two independent embedding models. Separately, condition-associated α amplification was observed in a preliminary Chinese replication using DeepSeek-V4-Flash. In a 100-query polysemous disambiguation task, topology-aware reranking achieves a 30.0% absolute precision improvement and near-perfect disambiguation (Precision@2 = 99.0%, MRR = 1.000) at full rerank depth. The results indicate that aligned prompting is associated with systematic changes in rank-probability focusing. This perspective has important implications for the design of retrieval-augmented generation systems and the evaluation of information quality. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Efficiency and vulnerability in natural monopoly ferry infrastructure under peak load
abstract: The ferry services on many islands operate under market conditions that make it possible for one company, in practice, to provide the service at the lowest cost. This situation is due to the very high fixed costs required for ferry operations and the need to offer a continuous service. However, in the event of increased demand, vulnerable systems may suffer as congestion grows and the utilisation limit of ferry services is reached. The paper introduces the Natural Monopoly Ferry Framework (NMFF). The framework is developed through a conceptual synthesis of natural monopoly theory, ferry economics and infrastructure vulnerability research. It is suggested that even if a ferry service operates effectively, it may still be put under stress due to a sudden increase in demand. In particular, the paper argues that even the economic efficiency of a ferry service is not always enough to make the service operate well. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Optimization model and MIP-based heuristics for aircraft routing with crew assignment in the on-demand air transportation
abstract: On-demand air transportation services have experienced significant growth in the business aircraft industry over the past decades. This sector requires complex decision-making in a highly dynamic environment, with associated high operating costs and requiring strict adherence to civilian aviation rules. In this context, we focus on the aircraft routing and crew assignment tasks, motivated by the collaboration with an airline that operates in the sector. The company seeks to determine which routes each aircraft must perform, considering the fleet characteristics, operating costs and crew legislation, such as working hours limit, minimum rest time, breaks, overtime payments, among others. These characteristics have been barely explored in the literature addressing on-demand air transportation services. We propose an effective mixed-integer programming (MIP) model to appropriately represent and solve the studied problem, and MIP-based heuristics, known as relax-and-fix and fix-and-optimize, to cope with large-scale instances. Computational experiments with real-world data provided by the company show that a general-purpose MIP solver finds optimal solutions within reasonable computing times for most instances when using the proposed MIP model. The MIP-based heuristics reduce computing times and reveal greater cost reductions in instances that were not solved to optimality. These results indicate the high potential for application of these approaches to effectively support decision-making in on-demand air transportation services. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Organizational design for digital transformation: A systematic literature review
abstract: Digital transformation has become a central topic in management research over the past decades. This systematic review of 109studies from 2000 to 2025 clarifies the role of organizational design in digital transformation. Synthesizing insights from the literature, we identify eight organizational design dimensions and integrate them into a framework of three interdependent stages of digital transformation. The Align stage connects digital leadership, digital governance, and digital culture; the Execute stage mobilizes digital strategy, digital organization, as well as digital resources and capabilities; and the Transform stage establishes digital operating and business models. Our analysis further reveals a distinct tradeoff at each stage: balancing control and autonomy during alignment, stability and adaptability during execution, and optimization and reconfiguration during transformation. We build on these insights to develop a research agenda and derive implications for managerial practice. © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier Inc. title: Circular biomass waste valorisation into biolubricant for sustainable energy systems
abstract: Scalability of biolubricant production is frequently hindered by feedstock, and valorisation of biomass waste offers a potential solution. This review examines biolubricant production pathways alongside their emerging application as transformer insulating oil. Natural ester (NE) oil offer superior biodegradability, moisture tolerance, and fire safety compared to mineral oils. Moreover, studies have already proven that biomass-derived insulating oil are technically viable and environmentally superior, but the remaining question is how to scale them up for actual use in the existing electrical grids. Therefore, it is proposed that grid-scale adoption is achievable provided that interdependent barriers of validation under real operational stresses and targeted policy that supports sustainable research are systematically addressed. To address these gaps, integration of technical, economic, and policy perspectives were conducted to provide actionable insights for biomass-derived insulating oil technology advancement. Malaysia's National Energy Transition Roadmap and complementary regulatory frameworks provide a foundation for sustainable energy infrastructure, yet with data center electricity demand expected to reach 20.9 GW by 2040, a circularity-oriented policy roadmap is essential to mitigate environmental hazards from conventional mineral oil disposal and enhance long-term grid stability. Our analysis identifies triple-helix collaboration between academia, industry, and government as essential for accelerating technology maturation, supported by targeted incentives that complement existing frameworks to ensure circular economy implementation. By addressing these aspects, transformer lifespan can potentially be extended while creating new revenue streams from biomass products. This work also mitigates environmental risks associated with mineral oil disposal and reduces reliance on fossil-based resources, while supporting UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and ensure resource circularity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Unboxing the dynamic-capability microfoundations of springboard internationalization: strategic brand transformation in emerging-market firms
abstract: Emerging-market firms (EMFs) increasingly transform from brandless manufacturing subcontractors into international brand competitors, yet springboard internationalization theory has left the internal organizational dynamics of this leap underspecified. Integrating a dynamic-capability mechanism into the springboard framework, this study theorizes the 3A architecture—Adaptability, Ambidexterity, and Amalgamation—as the EMF-specific tailoring of dynamic capabilities, anchoring each at a distinct layer of internal transformation. Organizational learning culture (Adaptability) activates two complementary knowledge-development streams (Ambidexterity), which enable two strategic levers (Amalgamation) that build brand-based differentiation advantage and, in turn, superior international performance. We test this processual model with a mixed-method design combining qualitative evidence from ten transformed EMFs and a two-wave longitudinal survey of 1,114 Taiwanese firms analyzed through cross-lagged structural equation modeling. Results support the full hypothesized sequence, robust across endogeneity, heterogeneity, and confounding checks. The study specifies the dynamic-capability microfoundations of springboard internationalization and repositions brand as a rent-yielding strategic resource. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Strategic capability prioritisation for logistics service providers: a consistency-calibrated reliability-weighted fuzzy FUCOM–MARCOS framework
abstract: Logistics service providers (LSPs) have yet to receive guidance, supported by empirical data, on which organisational capabilities should be prioritised for development to enhance competitiveness and survival in the dramatically changing environment they face. Although previous research has explained the relationship between capabilities and competitiveness, it has offered little empirical support to help managers direct limited resources towards specific capability types.Thus, this study aims to introduce a novel hybrid multi-criteria decision-making framework for strategic capability prioritisation in LSPs, which determines the relative priority of critical capability domains and evaluates alternative capability development scenarios.The proposed methodology incorporates six capability dimensions for evaluating five strategic capability scenarios. Structured elicitation from 17 senior managers of leading LSPs based in Türkiye forms the empirical data set. This methodology contributes by transforming each expert’s deviation from full consistency into an endogenous reliability weight during the aggregation of individual weights. CCR-FUCOM weights are then used to calculate scenario scores via fuzzy MARCOS.Results show that operational capabilities and dynamic capabilities form a priority cluster. The scenario analysis converges on the same priorities: the operational leader configuration attains the highest system-level utility, with the digital pioneer second and the resilience champion third. Resilience is nevertheless the decisive contingency: it is the capability whose weight most readily reorders the leading configurations as turbulence intensifies.The study reconceptualises competitiveness as a function of scenario-based capability prioritisation under environmental turbulence and introduces a consistency-sensitive decision framework for expert-based MCDM. It also provides LSP practitioners with a systematic, replicable tool for making capability investment decisions under uncertainty and resource constraints. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Explainable AI in dyslexia diagnosis and intervention: A systematic review and a novel conceptual multimodal framework
abstract: Dyslexia is a common neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by difficulties in reading, writing, and language processing. Early diagnosis is essential, as prompt intervention can significantly improve educational outcomes and quality of life. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning and deep learning, have enabled automated dyslexia detection. However, most of these models function as “black boxes,” lacking the transparency required for personalized intervention and clinical trust. This systematic review, conducted according to PRISMA guidelines, critically analyzes research from the past decade on the use of Explainable AI (XAI) in dyslexia diagnosis, classification, and intervention. It highlights how XAI techniques enhance the interpretability of AI models, making them more applicable in clinical and educational settings. The review covers a range of XAI approaches, including LIME, SHAP, Grad-CAM, attention mechanisms, and inherently interpretable models. Findings show that while traditional AI often achieves high predictive accuracy, the lack of explainability hinders practical use. In contrast, XAI methods reveal interpretable patterns, such as irregular handwriting, atypical eye movements, or neuroimaging features, enabling clinicians and educators to better understand and trust model decisions. To bridge the gap between high-performing algorithms and actionable clinical insights, future research should focus on developing multimodal, interpretable systems suited for real-world application. Based on our synthesis, we propose a novel conceptual framework outlining a longitudinal, XAI-driven pipeline for dyslexia diagnosis and personalized intervention. This framework integrates multimodal data fusion, explainability techniques, and adaptive support strategies, paving the way for more transparent and personalized dyslexia management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: COLF: Disentangled forecasting for non-stationary time series via contrastive learning
abstract: Non-stationary time series are widely prevalent in real world, characterized by changing temporal patterns, which greatly challenges the out-of-distribution generalization ability of forecasting approaches. Most existing approaches seek to achieve sequence stationarization through normalization methods, whose effectiveness is still limited since non-stationarity is not simply reflected in shift in mean and variance. Given this, we consider addressing non-stationarity from another perspective by pattern disentanglement, i.e., to distinguish between stable and unstable patterns according to temporal persistence and utilize them separately for forecasting. Considering the lack of supervised signals for disentanglement as temporal persistence is challenging to measure explicitly, we achieve this in a self-supervised manner and propose a model COLF. Specifically, COLF is designed with two contrastive learning mechanisms at different levels: the across-sample contrastive learning to disentangle stable and unstable patterns at sequence level, and the within-sample contrastive learning to further extract persistent components from unstable patterns under the local smoothness assumption at subsequence level. The final forecasted result is obtained by integrating the predictions derived from both stable patterns and the persistent components within unstable patterns. COLF is evaluated on six real-world datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate that COLF achieves overall superior performance compared to state-of-the-art approaches across different forecasting horizons and evaluation metrics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Signaling for success in university research funding applications
abstract: Signaling theory explains how organizations convey credible information under conditions of information asymmetry. Yet, while recent work highlights that signals often interact—reinforcing or substituting—most studies have treated signals as independent and additive, and empirical evidence of configurational interaction patterns remains limited. This study addresses this limitation by examining how multiple institutional signals jointly shape evaluators’ judgments in peer-reviewed university research funding. Using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), we identify distinct configurations of capability, reputation, and status signals that lead to both high and low funding success. The findings reveal that no single signal ensures success; rather, outcomes emerge from specific portfolios of signals whose effects depend on their combinations. We extend signaling theory by demonstrating that signals can also suppress or neutralize one another, and by introducing a configurational perspective that captures synergy, substitution, and suppression within signal portfolios. © 2026 The Authors. title: The evolving nature of collaboration in business academia: Network structures and the role of editorial proximity in publishing
abstract: Scholars have long suggested that network structures within academia may play a significant role in how knowledge is produced and disseminated, thus abetting the very research success of academics and their institutions. The nature of these structures, how they have evolved over time, and how individuals come to occupy certain positions requires further empirical exploration. This study examines the evolving structure of academic collaborations within business research from 2016 to 2024. Using publication metadata for 1,323,092 records from 530 business journals, we use network analysis to map co-authorship collaboration patterns while also assessing the structural benefits that may accrue from having journal editors as co-authors. Findings indicate that research networks have become increasingly collaborative over time, increasing to an average of 2.84 unique collaborations per author in 2024 from 1.72 in 2016. Despite this increase, we observed a 12.3 % increase in clustering during our study window, suggesting fewer bridges between authors publishing in different parts of the academic business literature. We replicated these analyses, focusing on journals in the Financial Times 50 (FT50). We found these trends were generally more pronounced in this subset. Research connections to journal editors likely fueled some of these growth patterns. Collaborating with an editor was positively related to both volume (degree) and type (betweenness) of collaborations in every year examined. This latter finding is particularly noteworthy because an increase in clustering suggests the occurrence of fewer bridging opportunities but publishing with an editor relates to increased bridging opportunities. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Industrial robot and cross-border M&As
abstract: Using panel data of Chinese listed firms over 2007–2023, we examine the impact of industrial robot penetration on cross-border merger and acquisition (M&A) decisions, constructing a firm-level penetration measure from industry-level statistics. Baseline results show that a 1% increase in robot penetration raises firms' likelihood of conducting cross-border M&A by 4.89%, and this finding remains robust after addressing endogeneity concerns and performing a battery of robustness checks. Mechanism analysis reveals that robot adoption facilitates cross-border M&A by improving profitability, alleviating financing frictions, and most critically, enhancing corporate risk-taking. Cross-sectional tests further indicate the positive effect is more pronounced for private firms and firms with top management teams lacking overseas education experience, where technology-driven risk-taking substitutes for traditional advantages in international expansion. Overall, our findings highlight technological capacity as a new firm-specific advantage reshaping global growth strategies of emerging market firms. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Buffer or burden? The role of corporate reputation in the market valuation effects of suppliers’ human rights controversies
abstract: Does corporate reputation buffer firms from reputational spillovers, or can it backfire when controversies arise? This study examines how corporate reputation shapes the market-valuation consequences of suppliers’ human-rights controversies, recognizing that shareholders may hold focal firms accountable for upstream misconduct. Using an international panel of RepTrak® Pulse firms from 2011 to 2023, we show that supplier-related human-rights controversies are associated with lower market valuation and that corporate reputation amplifies this negative association, consistent with a reputational “boomerang” effect. We further theorize and test firm visibility as a boundary condition: the reputational burden is stronger when the focal firm receives higher media coverage, reflecting greater public visibility and stakeholder attention. We estimate interaction-based dynamic panel models using two-step System GMM to address endogeneity and complement coefficient estimates with marginal-effects analyses to facilitate interpretation of conditional relationships. Robustness checks using market-to-book yield qualitatively similar inferences. The findings suggest that highly reputed and highly visible firms need supply-chain governance mechanisms that can anticipate, detect, and respond to upstream human-rights controversies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: When ethical signaling amplifies technological harm: Hypocrisy-based amplification of corporate digital responsibility on artificial intelligence hallucination and sustainable innovation
abstract: Based on the social construction of technology perspective, we examine how generative artificial intelligence (AI) hallucination undermines sustainable business model innovation (SBI) and competitive advantage by weakening the transactive memory system. In Study 1, we analyze cross-sectional data from 201 hotels in Eastern China. In Study2, we analyze multiwave, multisource data from 205 hotels in Western China. After testing a hypocrisy-based amplification mechanism, we find that corporate digital responsibility is at a high level and that the negative indirect effect of generative AI hallucination on SBI and competitive advantage is significantly strengthened. This occurs because organizational members perceive a pronounced inconsistency between external digital ethics and internal knowledge integrity. These findings extend research on the dark side of AI, enrich the knowledge management theory, and advance social construction of technology research. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Evaluating LLM–NACE divergence in firm classification: A multi-metric analysis in the experience industry
abstract: This study examines whether patterns of divergence between large language model (LLM) firm classifications and the Statistical Classification of Economic Activities in the European Community (NACE) are more consistent with between-model inconsistency, information-availability effects, or taxonomic ambiguity. Using a registry dataset of 43,931 Finnish firms, of which 29,565 received at least one Experience Industry classification, we compare GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Gemini 1.5 Flash, and Llama 3 70B. LLMs were prompted using company name and identifier only, and the resulting keywords were mapped to sector profiles, enabling comparison between model outputs and formal taxonomic assignments without external descriptive text. We evaluate agreement with Krippendorff’s α, cosine similarity, and normalized HHI-based concentration measures, and examine variation by firm revenue, size, and sector-level keyword reliability. Using raw LLM-derived profiles, inter-LLM similarity is high (cosine 0.89–0.95), whereas LLM–NACE alignment is substantially lower (0.19–0.24). Confidence-level adjustment increases LLM–NACE similarity, as expected, because adjusted profiles partly incorporate NACE information. Agreement increases in revenue-weighted and larger-firm analyses, but declines in sectors with low keyword reliability and diffuse boundaries. Across all weighting schemes and size classes, inter-LLM similarity exceeds LLM–NACE similarity. The findings suggest that LLM–NACE divergence is more consistent with information-availability effects and taxonomic ambiguity than with large between-model inconsistency. The study contributes a multi-metric framework for evaluating classification under unstable category systems and shows how LLM-based profiling can complement formal industry coding in hybrid sectors. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Using vertical integration to safeguard against unfavorable bargaining position
abstract: This paper examines the effect of a change in bargaining power on the decision to engage in vertical integration. Market contracts are inherently incomplete; when contingencies arise, firms rely on conventions to facilitate non-contractable adaptations. The perceived flexibility of informal agreements increases as the firm’s bargaining power weakens. Using data on the U.S. airline market (2006-2011), I find that buyers (mainline carriers) are more likely to vertically integrate when they have low bargaining power vis-à-vis suppliers (regional partners). Furthermore, mergers are associated with increased outsourcing on routes and contexts where independent regional airlines were previously absent, but with reduced or unchanged outsourcing on routes where independent regional airlines are already present, especially among rival carriers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Filling the legitimacy void: The value of sustainability orientation across investor segments in venture financing
abstract: When and why does sustainability attract entrepreneurial funding? Drawing on legitimacy theory, we argue that prior institutional backing segments ventures into distinct contexts in which public investors value sustainability orientation differently. Without such backing, sustainability can compensate for missing commercial validation by providing an alternative source of moral legitimacy. When institutional backing already certifies pragmatic legitimacy, sustainability may conflict with return-oriented expectations. Examining 2222 token-based crowdfunding campaigns, we find that sustainability orientation is positively associated with funding among non-backed ventures but negatively associated with funding among institutionally backed ventures. Consistent with this segmented valuation logic, non-backed ventures display stronger sustainability orientation. An LLM-based decomposition shows no statistically significant difference between the extent to which substantive and symbolic sustainability attenuate the funding disadvantage of non-backed ventures; their greater sustainability orientation is most clearly concentrated in symbolic social content. Our findings position sustainability not as a universally beneficial cue, but as a compensatory source of legitimacy whose value depends on what other types of legitimacy ventures already possess. title: Collaborating with GenAI: A blessing or a curse for creativity?
abstract: Recent advances in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) are increasingly shifting creative work from individual creation toward human–AI collaboration. Drawing on evidence from various creative domains, such as writing, design, and product ideation, this review highlights the gains and constraints of collaborating with GenAI, distinguishing between outcome-related and process-related effects. While GenAI can increase the number of ideas, enhance idea quality, accelerate idea generation, and reduce cognitive load, it may also lead to idea homogenization, diminished perceptions of authenticity and ownership, reduced independent creative engagement, and weakened team collaboration. To clarify when GenAI supports rather than hinders creativity, this review identifies four key moderating factors: 1) when GenAI is used (i.e., timing of GenAI involvement), 2) how it is used (i.e., interaction design), 3) what it is used for (i.e., task characteristics), and 4) by whom it is used (i.e., user expertise). The findings highlight the need for future research on how to better structure human–AI collaboration to support both creative performance and the development of human creative capabilities. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: BenchPDM: Benchmarking pattern detection methods in microservice-based systems using automatically generated pattern-assisted testbeds
abstract: Microservices architecture (MSA) is an increasingly popular trend in software architecture design. While the use of microservices offers numerous benefits, such as enhanced flexibility and scalability, it also introduces specific challenges and complexities. To address these challenges, various design patterns have been applied in system implementations, each aimed at resolving specific issues within microservices-based systems (MBS). Understanding the design patterns employed in a large software system can significantly enhance comprehension of the system’s functionality. However, organizations often lack strong documentation regarding the types of patterns used, the number of patterns, and their locations within the system. To date, various pattern detection methods (PDMs) have been developed with the goal of identifying design patterns within software systems. The effectiveness of these PDMs may vary depending on factors such as the scale of the software system, the types of patterns used, and etc. Therefore, the selection of an appropriate PDM is highly dependent on the specific software system being targeted. Consequently, there is a critical need for a tool that can evaluate and compare PDMs from various perspectives. Although several benchmarks have been proposed for MBSs, none have focused on assessing PDM. In this article, we present a benchmark named BenchPDM aimed at benchmarking PDMs in MBS using automatically generated pattern-assisted test beds. To achieve this, BenchPDM includes two fundamental modules. In the PBMC module, pattern-assisted microservices-based systems (PAMBS) are generated with varying degrees of complexity to simulate real-world MBSs of small, medium, and large scales. The PDM-ES module then evaluates and compares the performance of PDMs using the generated PAMBS from different factors. To assess the performance of BenchPDM, we conducted experiments on five PDM methods, two of which are among the most popular and commonly adopted approaches, SVM-based and graph-based methods. The experimental results demonstrated that BenchPDM can effectively evaluate and compare PDMs across various factors. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: A real-time concurrent packing and safety framework for consolidated electronics manufacturing services
abstract: Warehousing and logistics play a crucial role in supply chain efficiency. Achieving Just-in-Time (JIT) delivery without waste remains a key goal for reducing manufacturing costs. Excess transportation of materials increases operational expenses and causes inventory buildup at production sites, leading to holding costs and complicating quality traceability. In today’s highly competitive environment with short product life cycles, upstream logistics planning and execution must ensure synchronized arrivals and safe transit. Under Industry 4.0, improving material flow efficiency is the main challenge beyond automation. This study examines emerging warehousing and logistics needs in the EMS (Electronics Manufacturing Services) industry by consolidating planning tasks for small and medium-sized businesses within large-scale distribution centers. Materials are dispatched based on customer-specific requirements and delivered just before production line demand, requiring near real-time efficiency in packing space utilization and transportation safety. This research moves away from traditional algorithms that focus solely on packing arrangements or load stability, opting instead for a balanced hierarchical method. It efficiently identifies load patterns in the Bin Packing Problem (BPP) and evaluates packing safety using fuzzy logic. Unlike previous work that applied constraints in a strict hierarchy, this approach allows natural-language descriptions and considers multiple constraints simultaneously. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed concurrent tier framework surpasses some earlier methods and reduces computational resources needed to find near-optimal load patterns while accommodating a broader range of loading constraints. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Techno-economic optimisation and operational assessment of hydrogen-integrated renewable microgrids for remote communities
abstract: Hydrogen-integrated renewable microgrids represent a promising pathway for sustainable decarbonisation of remote communities; however, conventional techno-economic optimisation often overlooks the operational behaviour of hydrogen subsystems, leading to optimistic performance estimates and less practically deployable designs. This study proposes an integrated framework combining Hybrid Optimisation of Multiple Energy Resources (HOMER) Pro-based techno-economic optimisation with Python-based post-optimisation operational assessment. The framework evaluates operational indicators, including minimum-load compliance, start-stop cycling, large-ramp events, and hydrogen storage utilisation, using hourly dispatch data and literature-informed criteria. A scenario-based design-space exploration is conducted for a remote off-grid community in Australia, followed by operational feasibility screening and Pareto-based multi-objective analysis balancing economic performance, renewable energy utilisation, and electrolyser operation. The optimised reference configuration achieves zero operational CO2 emissions with a levelised cost of energy (LCOE) of 0.258 AUD/kWh and a levelised cost of hydrogen (LCOH) of 6.77 AUD/kg. Post-optimisation assessment reveals that 5,912 h of reported electrolyser operation reduces to 4,775 h of acceptable operation; the excluded 1,137 h (19.2%) correspond to low-load periods, indicating an overestimation of effective electrolyser utilisation of up to 23.8%. Threshold sensitivity analysis identifies hydrogen tank near-full hours as the most sensitive indicator, while core screening outcomes remain stable under low-load and ramp-event threshold variations. Operational feasibility screening reduces the 22 candidate designs to 15 feasible configurations, demonstrating that techno-economic attractiveness does not necessarily ensure operational viability. The proposed framework provides a practical methodology for operational assessment and design selection of hydrogen-integrated renewable microgrids, supporting informed planning and deployment of reliable, low-carbon energy systems. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: An End to End Trustworthiness Evaluation Framework for Enterprise AI Systems
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are becoming integral parts of modern enterprise systems to facilitate intelligent automation, decision-making processes, and enterprise knowledge management at scale. Nowadays, transformer models, such as foundation models and instruction-tuned models, are being integrated into intricate business workflows routinely. While these practices are common, they are still primarily model focused, with a focus on individual measures of performance and a lack of transparency of the operational reliability, accountability, and systemic risk. This difference creates what we call the Fragmented Trust Evaluation Problem, in which existing assessment methods do not support the detection of in-win failures due to the interaction of modules, propagation of errors and lack of traceability. To meet this challenge, we propose a System-Level Trustworthiness Evaluation Framework whose key principles are the introduction of common reliability, provenance coverage, and failure containment metrics for end-to-end application pipelines. The experimental studies performed on compliance management and policy assistance data sets show that systems evaluated and optimized with trustworthiness-aware criteria outperforms conventional evaluation methods with regard to operational reliability (16.3%), traceability coverage (34.7%), and failure impact reduction (28.5%). © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: A Practical Predictive Maintenance Pipeline Integrating Machine Learning and Deep Learning on the Scania Component X Dataset
abstract: This study focuses on evaluating predictive maintenance (PdM) classification models using the SCANIA Component X dataset released in 2025. The dataset is highly imbalanced, as Component X operates in a healthy state for about 97% of the time, while failures occur only around 3% of the time. This imbalance reflects real maintenance conditions in industry and creates both challenges and opportunities for applying machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models to PdM tasks. The main objective of this study is to develop a complete and practical pipeline for supervised learning models that achieves high prediction performance while reducing maintenance-related costs, thereby providing real business value. The proposed pipeline is structured into four main steps: (1) Business Understanding, (2) Data Understanding, (3) Modeling, and (4) Evaluation. Several models are trained and evaluated, including Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), XGBoost (XGB), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), and Transformer Encoder (TE). In particular, DL models consistently outperform traditional ML approaches under severe class imbalance, with BiLSTM and TE achieve the best performance, with balanced accuracy scores of 0.7767 and 0.7907, and cost per prediction values of 3.1519 and 2.3816 on test set, respectively. In addition, Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis is applied to improve model interpretability. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Machine learning-based recommendation of over-the-counter treatments and exercise modalities for knee joint pain using long-tail classification
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis is a widespread chronic condition that significantly affects quality of life, yet selecting effective over-the-counter (OTC) medications and exercise modalities remains largely a trial-and-error process due to substantial inter-patient variability. Existing machine learning studies have primarily focused on disease diagnosis and progression prediction, while personalized conservative treatment recommendation has received limited attention, particularly under highly imbalanced long-tail treatment distributions. In this study, we analyzed clinical and demographic data from 1687 patients and developed a machine learning framework for personalized recommendation of OTC medications and exercise modalities. To address the severe class imbalance across 36 OTC categories and 53 exercise modalities, we systematically investigated class reweighting, SMOTE, and missing-label utilization strategies, and compared six representative machine learning and deep learning models, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Focal Loss Neural Network, LightGBM, TabNet, and Sentence-BERT. Experimental results show that LightGBM combined with SMOTE consistently achieved the best overall performance, reaching 47.3% accuracy for OTC recommendation and 62.7% for exercise recommendation while substantially improving balanced accuracy and Macro-F1 for minority classes. Additional experiments demonstrate that advanced deep learning models do not outperform LightGBM on this moderate-sized structured clinical dataset. These findings demonstrate the potential of machine learning to provide practical decision support for personalized conservative treatment recommendations and reduce reliance on trial-and-error approaches in knee pain management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Secure and adaptive user gait authentication framework for metaverse
abstract: The Metaverse requires persistent and non-intrusive authentication for avatars across heterogeneous virtual environments. An individual’s walking pattern, or gait, provides a continuous and comparatively spoof-resistant verification mechanism compared with face, voice, or iris biometrics. However, gait-based authentication in avatar-mediated Metaverse environments remains vulnerable to algorithmic and statistical attacks, including synthetic gait generation, exploitation of feature dependencies, behavioral imitation, replay, and model drift. Conventional machine-learning, deep-learning, and transformer-based models also exhibit limited robustness to environmental variation, sensor noise, session variability, and adaptive adversaries. To address these challenges, we propose a secure and adaptive ensemble gait-authentication framework for continuous avatar verification that integrates Bagging, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Extra Trees classifiers through a Secure Majority-Voting Scheme (SMVS). The framework employs a dynamic per-session acceptance threshold that adjusts the required voting condition according to session-level gait dispersion, noise, pose variability, and feature stability, thereby reducing false accepts while preserving authentication usability. We also introduce MetaGait, a large Unity-simulated avatar-gait dataset grounded in biomechanical principles and designed to support realistic multi-session evaluation. Experimental validation is conducted on MetaGait, CASIA-B, and OU-ISIR-C using leakage-safe subject-disjoint grouped cross-validation, together with explicit cross-dataset transfer experiments in which models trained on MetaGait are tested on CASIA-B and OU-ISIR-C. The proposed framework achieves up to 97.2% accuracy, 94.1% precision, 99.7% recall, and 97.0% F1-score, while attaining a low Equal Error Rate (EER) of 3.3% and outperforming traditional machine-learning, deep-learning, and transformer-based authentication models. Furthermore, formal game-based security analysis with probabilistic bounds, supported by comprehensive empirical attack simulations, shows SMVS’s resilience against Adaptive Brute-Force Attacks (ABFA), Constrained Behavioral Attacks (CBA), and Model Drift Invasion Attacks (MDIA). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Effective training and support of ICU teams: The cornerstone for improved patient and staff outcomes
abstract: Background ICU care is inherently multiprofessional, and communication failures and team dysfunction are implicated in a substantial proportion of preventable adverse events in critical care. However,et training frameworks remain fragmented, built around individual brilliance and siloed disciplines. Aim To present an integrated, evidence-based framework for building, training, assessing, and sustaining high-performance ICU teams. Methods Narrative review using a targeted, non-systematic search of the databases PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science for manuscripts published between 2000 and June 2026. Grey literature from ESICM, SCCM, ANZICS was also searched. Data were synthesized by the authors from complex clinical scenarios and team behaviors, rather than by pooling empirical data. Themes, communication patterns, and organizational challenges emerged organically from the selected texts and case descriptions. Key findings ICU team effectiveness rests on four pillars: deliberate multiprofessional composition with explicit role delineation; multimodal training combining simulation, just-in-time training, and structured debriefing; rigorous measurement through structure, process, and outcome indicators; and organizational conditions, including unit design and psychological safety, that sustain safety culture and provider wellbeing. Current evidence remains heterogeneous, particularly across cultural, organizational, and resource contexts, limiting direct comparison across settings. Building on these pillars, practical recommendations for ICU leaders to translate this framework into daily practice are proposed. Conclusion A whole-team approach to ICU team selection, training and support, extending beyond physician-centric models, is clinically necessary and is operationally feasible when adapted to local resources and organizational conditions. The framework presented is adaptable to diverse and various intensive care settings, with each pillar mapped to actionable strategies for team composition, training, assessment, and sustainability. © 2026 The Authors.

title: The Max–Min Kano framework: A context-sensitive method for evaluating office design features
abstract: Product and building-related features are sometimes perceived differently across studies because they are experienced in different environmental contexts. The proposed Max–Min Kano methodology evaluates office design features under two contrasting contexts: a minimal environment with few positively appraised attributes and a maximal environment with many. Office-relevant attributes were identified through participatory elicitation and then evaluated using a Kano questionnaire (N = 32). Perceptual robustness was defined as retention of a Kano classification across the two contexts, while participant-level bootstrapping assessed sampling stability. View-related variables, window size, biophilic views, fewer façade obstructions, and proximity to windows were stable across contexts. They were Attractive, meaning they added satisfaction even when not strictly expected. In contrast, privacy provided by partitions emerged as a Must-be quality, while the presence of windows and ceiling height showed a One-dimensional relationship with satisfaction in both contexts. Other attributes, such as the seated-desk view, density, partition height, focal points, color, and materiality, were more sensitive to the baseline context. Adaptation-Level Theory, Stress Recovery theory, Attention Restoration theory, and Prospect–Refuge theory help explain these results. Overall, the Max-Min Kano approach helps identify features that remain perceptually robust across contexts, making it useful for prioritizing design features in real-world settings. The study shows that Kano categories are context-expressive rather than being intrinsic properties of features. For this reason, baseline context should be reported when evaluating user preferences across different spatial conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Grandparents raising grandchildren and women’s entrepreneurial exit: influence of social roles on resource utilization
abstract: From a family embeddedness perspective, previous research has suggested that time resources provided by family support can reduce women’s exit from entrepreneurship. However, this effect may be reversed when considering paid employment as an alternative to entrepreneurship and the influence of social roles on resource utilization. Grandparents raising grandchildren (GRGs), which are a prevalent form of family support, provide time resources for Chinese women with young children and thereby offer a valuable context for exploring the role of family support in women’s entrepreneurial exit. Using data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), we find that GRGs significantly reduce the likelihood of women transitioning from entrepreneurship to unemployment, while increasing the likelihood of women transitioning from entrepreneurship to paid employment. The overall effect of GRGs on women’s entrepreneurial exit is positive, and this effect is stronger for women living in areas with strong clan culture or those holding rural hukou. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Random discrete copulas
abstract: We introduce the notion of a bivariate random discrete copula on an equidistant mesh and explore its stochastic properties. A random discrete copula is a discrete random field, hence, its value at a given point on the mesh is a random variable. We determine the distribution of this random variable and calculate its expected value and variance. We also consider bilinear extension of a random discrete copula to a random field over the whole unit square. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Between mission pull and governance burden: Geographic distance and deal realisation in impact investing
abstract: Impact investing is widely expected to direct capital to locations where social and environmental challenges are most severe. Yet such opportunities are often found in places geographically distant from major pools of investment capital. We examine how geographic distance affects the realisation of impact investment deals and how host-country conditions alter that relationship. Integrating transaction cost economics with the location logic of the eclectic paradigm, we argue that impact investment decisions reflect the joint consideration of anticipated transaction value and governance costs. Distance raises the costs of screening, contracting, monitoring, and supporting ventures, while severe sustainability challenges can increase a location's mission-specific attractiveness by signaling greater unmet need and potential scope for additionality. By contrast, trade and investment risk increases transaction hazards that make distant deals harder to execute. We test these arguments using PitchBook data on 3126 impact deals closed in 2022–2023. We analyse 3606 realised investor–venture ties against matched unrealised alternatives in a choice-based sampling design. Distance reduces the likelihood of deal realisation. Challenge severity modestly weakens the distance penalty for a subset of sampled dyads, whereas trade and investment risk strengthens it across most observations. These findings contribute to impact investing by explaining why severe unmet need does not automatically translate into realised investment relationships. They extend transaction cost reasoning in entrepreneurial finance by incorporating mission-adjusted transactional value. They refine international business location logic by distinguishing mission-specific locational attractiveness from host-country transaction hazard. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Multi-Task learning for predictive process monitoring with temporal graph neural networks on Object-Centric event logs
abstract: Predictive Process Monitoring (PPM) forecasts the future trajectory of ongoing process instances, including next activities and remaining execution times. While deep learning has advanced the field, modeling irregular temporal dynamics and long-range dependencies remains a significant challenge, especially within complex object-centric environments.We propose a multi-task predictive framework based on the Temporal Graph Attention Network (TGAT). By transforming object-centric event logs into temporal graphs with time-aware edges, our approach explicitly encodes continuous time intervals directly into the attention mechanism. This allows the model to capture subtle temporal irregularities often missed by sequence-based methods. A shared temporal graph encoder is jointly optimized for three critical tasks: next activity prediction, next timestamp estimation, and remaining time prediction.We evaluate our framework using four real-world BPI Challenge datasets (2014, 2016, 2017, and 2019). The results demonstrate that our model consistently outperforms or matches state-of-the-art sequence-based, graph-based, and Transformer architectures. Furthermore, attention visualizations and ablation studies confirm that integrating temporal graph modeling with multi-task learning significantly enhances predictive accuracy in complex process environments. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Metatranscriptomic analyses coupled with phenotypic and metabolic verification revealed competition mechanisms between grass carp spoilage bacteria in synthetic communities
abstract: Bacterial competition is a major factor influencing microbiota succession in fish. However, the competition mechanisms among dominant spoilage bacteria in grass carp remain to be systematically investigated. Therefore, this study aimed to elucidate the mutual competition relationships and mechanisms among five representative spoilage bacteria isolated from grass carp. To this end, we constructed synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) with these five strains and employed metatranscriptomics coupled with phenotypic verification to demonstrate their interactions at both transcriptional and phenotypic levels. The results showed that bacterial competitiveness largely determined the microbiota composition in SynComs. Aeromonas rivipollensis ranked the most competitive bacterium by both inhibiting the virulence phenotypes (siderophore production, biofilm, and swimming motility) and disrupting the carbohydrate/amino acid metabolisms of Shewanella putrefaciens and Pseudomonas putida . Concurrently, A. rivipollensis enhanced its own siderophore production and motility when interacting with these competitors, which further promoted its advantage. In contrast, S. putrefaciens was the second most competitive, as it potently utilized amino acids and enhanced its siderophore production and motility in response to P. putida . Collectively, this study reveals that bacterial competition in fish is mediated by both phenotype interference and metabolism disruption, suggests siderophore as a new target for controlling microbiota succession and quality deterioration in fish, and therefore provides theoretical guidance for developing new fish preservation strategies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Dual replacement strategies for systems with dependent failures under lemon laws
abstract: Lemon laws mandate vehicle replacement or refund when repair attempts or downtime exceed statutory thresholds. While providing essential consumer protection, these regulations also create substantial warranty cost challenges for manufacturers, particularly in modern vehicles where component failures often exhibit positive dependence. This paper develops a comprehensive maintenance optimization framework for systems with dependent failures under lemon laws by integrating the Multivariate Poisson Generalized Gamma Process (MPGGP) into statutory maintenance analysis. Within this framework, two representative manufacturer replacement strategies, namely Replacement First and Replacement Last, are systematically evaluated. Closed-form expressions for the long-run expected cost rate are derived, and an efficient hierarchical coordinate descent algorithm is developed to determine the optimal maintenance decisions. Based on the analytical model and numerical optimization, we establish a policy selection phase diagram that characterizes the relative economic performance of the two replacement strategies under varying replacement costs and dependence levels. The results show that the proactive replacement strategy is generally more cost-effective under moderate replacement costs and stronger failure dependence, whereas the conservative strategy becomes economically competitive as replacement costs increase substantially. These findings provide quantitative insights into maintenance optimization under dependent failures and practical decision support for manufacturers operating under lemon law regulations.
