title: Digital Marketing Challenges and Opportunities: A Bibliometric Review
abstract: This research analyses the challenges and opportunities of digital marketing in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) through a bibliometric and systematic literature review. Using Scopus as the main database, scientific production from the last decade was examined with tools such as VOSviewer and Bibliometrix to identify research trends, influential authors, and thematic clusters. The analysis highlights the main digital tools used in SMEs —including social media platforms, customer relationship management systems (CRM), analytics solutions, and automation software— and discusses how their strategic integration can drive competitiveness and sustainability. Findings reveal that success in digital marketing depends not only on the availability of tools but also on their functional integration, continuous innovation, and the ability to adapt to technological change. This study contributes to the academic debate by providing a functional classification of digital tools (interaction, analysis, and automation) and by identifying knowledge gaps that can guide future research on SMEs’ digital transformation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: A Static Approach to Android Malware Detection Using Ensemble Techniques and SMOTE-Based Data Balancing
abstract: Android devices are widely used in various activities, including social, business, and communication. Malware, malicious code designed to disrupt or damage computer systems, networks, and devices without user knowledge, is growing exponentially. Traditional signature-based malware detection systems are not effective for detecting obfuscated and encrypted malware, as they lack advanced and updated datasets. To overcome the above challenges, a novel fusion based ensemble technique is proposed to combine with static approaches employing five different classifiers like Extra Tree (ET), Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree (DT) and Random Forest (RF) for the android malware detection to enhance security. Moreover, some classifier gives more accuracy for a particular set of features but not for another set of features. So, the fusion of different classifiers covers all features and gives more accuracy. Prediction accuracy of model also depends on the proportion of different samples. That is why Synthetic Minority Over Sampling Technique (SMOTE) is used to make dataset homogeneous. For prominent feature selection, Variance Threshold (VT) statistical approach is used to train the model. The eminent features like Application Program Interface (API), permissions and network traffic are passed as input to the model. The proposed Android Malware Detection System (AMDS) has been tested on three different datasets namely, TUANDROMD, MALGENOME and DREBIN-215. The outcome of the proposed model demonstrates that our approach successfully detect malware with the accuracy 99.54% along with F1 score of 99.56%. The results outperform better than the existing solutions for detecting the malware. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The evolution of Italian airport ownership
abstract: The ownership of commercial airports is increasingly essential for national competitiveness and regional economic development. Airport ownership directly influences the planning of airport infrastructure and air transport policies at both a local and national level. In Italy, historically, tight control by the state permitted the implementation of long-term development plans and ensured that the needs of local communities were addressed, but today, there are very few airports, and among the larger ones, almost none, without an equity share held by the private sector. In light of current debates surrounding the future viability of Italian airports following the COVID-19 pandemic, this paper aims to examine the evolution of Italian airport ownership compared to significant international experiences, such as the UK, in which airport privatisation followed the 1986 Airports Act. This paper critically examines the evolution of Italian airport ownership, focusing on the underlying drivers and consequences of these changes and comparing them with the UK case, by considering different ownership models, the nature of the private entities involved, the proportion of passengers flying through airports with different ownership structures, and the number of owners per airport. The analysis involves the main 33 Italian airports, controlled by 25 airport companies, and covers the period 1997-2024, which is analysed in three specific phases: 1997/2008-2009/2019, and 2020/2024. Among the primary outcomes of this research, there is a better understanding of how airport ownership has evolved in Italy compared with other international settings and whether airports can be considered public utilities or private assets to provide valuable recommendations for airport management and policymakers regarding the industry's future viability. title: Privacy‑by‑Design Customer Data Platform for Hyper‑Personalized, Cost‑Efficient B2B‑SaaS Lead Acquisition
abstract: Escalating privacy regulations and siloed customer signals drive up acquisition costs for Business-to-Business (B2B) Software as a Service (SaaS) firms, yet most Customer Data Platform (CDP) still treat consent, identity resolution, and segmentation as disconnected tasks. This paper introduces a privacy‑by‑design CDP that unifies explicit‑consent capture, hybrid deterministic-probabilistic identity resolution, and combined behavioural and psychographic‑based segmentation into a single event‑driven pipeline that feeds automated multichannel campaigns. Deployed for 28 live campaign‑days at a mid‑market SaaS provider, the platform lowered cost‑per‑lead by 84% and lifted budget‑normalized lead volume by 6.4 to 7.0 times, relative to the incumbent batch process. Robustness checks, including placebo rotation, interaction terms, and an E‑value of 12.98, underscore causal credibility. Three contributions emerge: (1) field evidence that privacy-by-design can be profit-by-design for CPL-based B2B SaaS lead acquisition where “profit” is operationalized as acquisition-economics efficiency rather than accounting profit; (2) an open, modular architecture designed to scale horizontally under production traffic while propagating consent end-to-end to support GDPR and Thailand PDPA requirements; and (3) a statistical playbook linking granular cost metrics to data-ecosystem investments. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Economic Diplomacy and Urban Innovation: Pioneering Smart Cities in Morocco
abstract: This article explores the concept of “smart cities” in Morocco, highlighting the pivotal role of economic diplomacy, innovation, and entrepreneurship in urban development. It begins with a review of the smart city concept and its key components from existing literature to frame the study. The research then analyzes smart city implementations in Morocco through case studies of Casablanca, Benguerir, and the Zenata Eco-City, illustrating practical applications and the significance of international partnerships in fostering technological and economic advancement. Additionally, the article investigates how economic diplomacy strategically supports innovation and entrepreneurship to drive sustainable urban growth. By examining Morocco’s diplomatic efforts, it reveals how collaboration and investment attraction enhance digital business ecosystems aligned with smart city goals. Using a qualitative approach, the study analyzes official reports, academic sources, and institutional publications, supplemented by detailed case study evaluations. The findings demonstrate that integrating economic diplomacy with innovation and entrepreneurship is essential for successful smart city initiatives, promoting sustainable economic development and positioning Morocco as a leader in digital urban transformation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: From Illicit Economies to Social Production Models: Academic Knowledge Management in Post-conflict Entrepreneurship in Colombia
abstract: This paper analyzes the role of academia in knowledge management and transfer to strengthen entrepreneurship in post-conflict contexts in Colombia, particularly in Putumayo and Cauca. Through collaboration between universities, indigenous communities, and international programs, applied knowledge—in marketing, brand identity, and value chain development—has contributed to the substitution of illicit economies and the consolidation of social productive models. The analysis is based on Moritz et al. [8] conceptual model of entrepreneurship in post-conflict environments, highlighting how knowledge generated in the classroom is transformed into practical solutions for communities. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Entity Linking Visualization and Refinement with KOALA-UI and the Crocodile Framework
abstract: Entity linking (EL) on tabular data often produces many ambiguous cell annotations that are costly to review. We present KOALA-UI, a lightweight web interface for inspecting and refining EL results on spreadsheets and CSV-like tables. KOALA-UI provides table navigation, cell-level candidate panels, color-coded scores, simple filtering, and in-place edits with export. To enable reuse across backends, KOALA-UI consumes a compact JSON schema and responses compatible with the W3C Entity Reconciliation specification, allowing integration with potentially any EL backend. We illustrate KOALA-UI with the Crocodile EL framework and demonstrate a human-in-the-loop (HITL) workflow. In addition, we report a preliminary user study, a real business use case, and a validation of pipeline execution through TAO–a workflow engine, where Crocodile was integrated as a module. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Circular economy transition pathways for AI adoption in Indian municipal waste management: Scenario-based forecasts to 2050
abstract: Indian urban local bodies generate approximately 62 million tonnes of municipal solid waste annually, with collection coverage near 75 percent and scientific processing below 30 percent (CPCB, 2023). The Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 and the Extended Producer Responsibility regime for plastic packaging impose binding obligations on ULBs and registered producers, while capability and infrastructure gaps constrain implementation. AI applications in route optimization, vision-based sorting at material recovery facilities, IoT-enabled containerization, and dealer-network digital platforms offer compliance pathways whose value is conditional on organizational capability, stakeholder legitimacy, and secondary-market depth. This study develops scenario-based forecasts to 2050 by operationalizing four theoretical frames, the circular economy framework, diffusion of innovation, the resource-based view, and stakeholder theory, into a hybrid simulation model with parameters calibrated through systematic review of 147 studies, of which 28 represent Indian or South-Asian contexts. Analysis of 100 simulated municipalities across four scenarios generates conditional projections of recycling rates, material recovery, and circularity outcomes against SWM Rules 2016 benchmarks and SDG 11.6 indicators. Under Capability-First assumptions, model outputs indicate 68 percent conditional probability of meeting the 2035 processing benchmark against 34 percent under Baseline assumptions. Technology-Led scenarios achieve 60 percent adoption by 2035 with 52 percent recycling rate, reflecting the model's capability-moderation specification. Sensitivity analysis identifies 2026 to 2029 as a decision window where capability investment timing alters simulated trajectories. Findings offer conditional roadmaps for ULB administrators, state governments, producer-responsibility organizations, and technology vendors operating in the Indian MSWM ecosystem, subject to empirical validation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Educational strategies grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour for sustainable food safety culture evolvement
abstract: Food safety (FS) culture is a behavioural phenomenon that shapes the food safety and hygiene behaviour of people across all organisational levels, contributing to the prevention of foodborne diseases. Although interventions can strengthen FS-culture, evidence on how to systematically develop it remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of interventions grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) in improving food handlers’ behavioural intentions and strengthening the prevailing FS-culture within a Brazilian military food service. A quasi-experimental study was conducted between 2022 and 2025 with 137 food handlers and seven quality managers. Data collection occurred at three time points (t = 0 in 2023, t = 1 in 2024, t = 2 in 2025). FS-culture was evaluated using a mixed-methods approach, while TPB constructs (i.e., subjective norms, perceived behavioural control, attitude, and intention) were measured through a validated questionnaire. Educational interventions were designed to address the lowest-scoring FS-culture element and the TPB constructs most strongly associated with behavioural intentions. FS-culture changed from active (score 2) at t = 0 to active–proactive (score 2-3) at t = 1, with significant improvements in knowledge and communication elements. At t = 2, FS-culture remained at an active-proactive level. Perceived behavioural control was the strongest predictor of intention at baseline (β = 0.27, p = 0.004). Interventions were associated with an increase in attitude scores between t = 0 and t = 1 (p = 0.002) and t = 1 and t = 2 (p = 0.009). These findings support the effectiveness of TPB-based educational interventions in strengthening FS-culture in food services. © 2026 The Authors

title: Private Quantised Neural Network Inference
abstract: Neural networks based machine learning models are used in many classification problems yet privacy issues in model usage are mostly unresolved. When a model owner provides their model to other parties for inference, either the model owner has to share the parameters of the model or the model user must share their query and result with the model owner. Depending on the usage scenario, the user’s query or query result could contain sensitive information that the model provider should not see. And on the other hand, the model parameters themselves could be a valuable business secret or leak private training data. In such cases, neural network inference must be performed in a privacy preserving manner, for example, using secure multi-party computation (MPC). We propose protocols for the private inference of neural networks and evaluate them within the Sharemind MPC secure computation framework. Our protocols are based on the per-tensor quantisation scheme in PyTorch which maps floating point model parameters to 8-bit integer values. Quantisation improves the efficiency of our protocols and our protocols are interoperable with models trained using PyTorch. We extend constant round integer convolution and matrix multiplication protocols for quantised model weights, propose constant round protocols for re-quantising values and analyse the optimal secret share bit width for efficient re-quantisation. The resulting protocols are used to evaluate the VGG16 image classification network with an amortised throughput of 24.3 s per image classification in a LAN setting. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models for End-to-End Diagram Recognition
abstract: Graph-structured diagrams (GSD) are frequently used in documents to visualize processes or relationships in an easily understandable way for humans. Extracting the underlying information from the diagram images in a structured format is important for various downstream applications. In contrast to prior work, which either focuses on visual question answering (VQA) for diagram understanding or relies on computer vision pipelines for full diagram recognition, we systematically test three open-weights multimodal large language models (MLLM) for end-to-end graph parsing under different experimental settings and compare to an object-detection baseline. We curate a publicly available dataset of 843 hand-drawn and machine-generated diagrams from related work covering flowcharts, business process modeling diagrams, and others. We evaluate the extractions with string matching against ground truth. Our findings show that MLLMs can compete with traditional computer vision approaches on simple diagrams but still struggle with complex layouts and relational extraction. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Design and Implementation of a Service Scheduling Mechanism for Ship Task Scheduling
abstract: In modern naval operations, ship formations need to realize cross-platform coordination (e.g., anti-aircraft, anti-submarine, and maritime strike), and the traditional single-orchestration paradigm service orchestration technology has gradually shown its limitations in the face of complex business challenges such as long transaction coordination, real-time event response, and dynamic business rule changes. In this paper, we propose an innovative Hybrid Service Orchestration Rule Model (HSORM), which systematically integrates the three major orchestration paradigms of process-driven, event-driven and rule-driven, and defines a unified model that contains service nodes, orchestration processes, event triggers, business rules, compensation processors and contexts. Define unified model elements and combination mechanism, which include service nodes, event triggers, business rules, compensation processors and contexts, and realize flexible declarative description of complex business logic. We design a YAML-based rule description language (DSL) to support business people to define hybrid orchestration logic in a near-natural language, and propose dynamic coordination strategies such as main process-driven branch event processing and event-triggered process fragments. Compared with the traditional single-orchestration paradigm, the development and maintenance workload is reduced by more than 50%, the additional performance overhead is controlled within 150 ms, the peak processing capacity is increased by 20%, and the operational efficiency is increased by 90%. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: TierServe: Revenue-Maximizing LLM Inference Scheduling Across Multiple Subscription Tiers
abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference systems serve clients across multiple subscription tiers with heterogeneous latency requirements and revenue contributions. Existing schedulers optimize throughput or service-level objectives (SLO) attainment, treating all requests as equally valuable. In multi-tier settings, this leads to a fundamental mismatch: a scheduler that maximizes goodput may allocate substantial resources to low-tier requests while high-tier requests miss their stricter SLOs, resulting in suboptimal operator revenue. We present TierServe, a revenue-driven LLM inference scheduler that jointly leverages both subscription-tier priority and per-request SLO slack. TierServe prioritizes high-value requests while dynamically utilizing available slack to improve overall efficiency, aligning scheduling decisions with both business value and latency urgency. We evaluate TierServe across a range of workloads and load conditions. Results show that TierServe consistently improves system revenue over state-of-the-art baselines while maintaining competitive per-tier latency. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Artificial Intelligence in a Fast-Food Advertising
abstract: This study analyzes the perceptions of eighth- and ninth-cycle systems engineering students at a private Peruvian university regarding the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the creation of visual narratives for digital advertising, with a focus on the “Te la creíste mi King [You believed it, my King]” spot. As AI transforms the development of visual narratives, this study analyzes how future professionals perceive the use of AI in developing visual narratives, including their concerns and attitudes toward creative automation. Fifteen semi-structured interviews were conducted to collect data. The findings highlight how students’ academic and technical backgrounds shape their views on AI integration, providing key insights for the implementation of innovative and consumer-accepted strategies. This study contributes to a deeper understanding of the coexistence of technology and creativity in modern digital advertising. In conclusion, participants recognize the spot as showcasing a visual narrative that successfully highlights the potential of artificial intelligence in digital advertising. The analysis of the visual narrative and humorous tagline shows how AI can enhance visual contrast to reinforce Burger King's message of product authenticity and quality. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Political patronage, rent-extraction, and social costs: Evidence from China's environmental cleanup
abstract: This paper investigates how informal political patronage subverts environmental regulation and local economic performance in China. We demonstrate that patronage provides local officials with political insurance, enabling them to safely shield polluting firms from top-down enforcement. Contrary to the promotion tournament hypothesis, this forbearance does not drive GDP growth. Instead, it is sustained through localized rent extraction. Utilizing firm-level data and shocks induced by provincial party secretary turnover, we find that connected officials extract a political tax, measured via perk expenditures, from both polluting and non-polluting enterprises. This systemic extortion generates broad negative spillovers: while shielding incumbent polluters, patronage crowds out productive investment and deters clean market entrants, ultimately degrading both environmental outcomes and the regional business environment. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Poverty mapping: Data, models and applications
abstract: Poverty mapping is increasingly important for monitoring Sustainable Development Goal 1 (SDG 1) of the United Nations 2030 Agenda, which aims to end poverty in all its forms everywhere. Yet timely and fine-resolution poverty estimation remains difficult because conventional census- and survey-based approaches are costly, infrequent, and often sparse precisely where deprivation is most severe. As poverty emerges from complex socioeconomic systems shaped by human mobility, social interactions, infrastructure, and economic activities, emerging computational methods and nontraditional data sources have created new opportunities for poverty estimation and mapping. At the intersection of statistical physics, complex systems science, and data science, these approaches enable poverty estimation at finer spatial and temporal resolutions. This review summarizes the main concepts of poverty and the principal frameworks used to measure it, and examines recent advances in poverty estimation and mapping using satellite imagery, mobile phone data, social media data, and multisource data fusion. The review also discusses persistent challenges related to representativeness, transferability across regions, interpretability, and uncertainty quantification. Finally, the review clarifies both the analytical promise and the practical limits of contemporary poverty mapping. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: A reinforcement learning-guided hyper-heuristic algorithm for cold chain distribution planning
abstract: Cold chain distribution requires routing decisions that meet service requirements while accounting for operating costs and environmental performance. Because routing choices directly affect travel cost, refrigeration energy use, and carbon emissions, effective planning is essential for sustainable cold chain operations. To address this routing problem, this study proposes a hybrid reinforcement learning-guided hyper-heuristic algorithm (HRL-HHA) that adaptively selects and combines search operators to improve search performance and reduce premature convergence. The proposed dual-layer framework enhances solution quality by coordinating intra- and inter-route search, while the parallel batch Tabu search procedure improves computational efficiency. In addition, we compare six RL-guided HHA variants, including five single-RL variants and a hybrid RL variant. This comparison allows us to examine how different RL-based heuristic selection strategies influence HHA performance. Across the benchmark instances, the proposed method achieves better results than the best solutions reported in the literature. In a real-world case study, it reduces travel distance by approximately 30% and total cost by more than 35%. Further analyses examine fleet selection and carbon pricing sensitivity to provide practical insights for sustainable and efficient cold chain distribution planning. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Corruption and capital investment: Worldwide evidence
abstract: Can international anti-corruption monitoring stimulate private investment? We examine staggered reviews across jurisdictions under the United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC), using firm-year observations from 84 economies over 2003–2023. We document that reviews are followed by improvements in economy-level corruption-control indicators. Local-projections difference-in-differences estimates indicate that reviews raise firms' capital expenditure relative to assets by 1.2126 percentage points, equivalent to 20% of the sample mean. Dynamic estimates show no systematic pre-review adjustment, and the result is robust to influential-economy exclusions, economy-level reweighting, alternative sample restrictions, lagged-outcome controls, and alternative staggered-adoption estimators. Investment responses are stronger in high-corruption economies and developing economies and among firms that are more financially constrained, government dependent, domestically concentrated, or reliant on irreversible capital. These patterns are consistent with international oversight reducing corruption-related institutional risk, financing frictions, and the value of delaying investment. UNCAC reviews are also followed by increases in employment, R&D investment, and leverage. Additional analyses provide no evidence that the increase in investment is accompanied by a systematic decline in investment efficiency. Overall, the findings show that a non-punitive international peer-review mechanism can affect firms’ real activity, particularly where initial institutional frictions are greater. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Diffusion-augmented adversarial poisoning in QoS-aware cloud API recommender systems
abstract: Data poisoning attacks pose a serious security threat to QoS-aware cloud API recommender systems by injecting carefully crafted fake user profiles into training data, thereby manipulating recommendation outcomes and compromising prediction reliability. Existing GAN-based poisoning methods often suffer from discriminator overfitting under limited interaction data, leading to pronounced distributional discrepancies between generated and real users, which significantly degrades both attack effectiveness and stealthiness. To address this limitation, we propose DA-GAN, a Diffusion-Augmented Generative Adversarial Network for poisoning attacks against QoS-aware cloud API recommendation systems. DA-GAN integrates diffusion probabilistic modeling into the adversarial training by constructing multi-step noise-augmented real users through a diffusion forward process, and generating fake users via noise-aligned posterior sampling in the reverse process. To further stabilize training, we design a multi-step noise-aligned discriminator that performs joint discrimination across multiple diffusion levels, providing reliable gradient supervision and effectively mitigating discriminator overfitting in small-sample settings. Extensive experiments on real-world cloud API QoS datasets demonstrate that DA-GAN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art poisoning baselines in both attack effectiveness and stealthiness across multiple mainstream QoS-aware recommender systems. Our findings reveal previously underestimated vulnerabilities in existing cloud API recommender systems and underscore the urgent need for diffusion-aware and attack-resilient defense mechanisms. Our code is available at https://github.com/Ethereal-Fairy/DAGANcode. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: Behavioural leakage and the illusion of actionability: A deployment-honest evaluation framework for educational early warning systems
abstract: Educational Early Warning Systems (EWS) rely on feature-selection components that systematically conflate retrospective accuracy with operational utility. We formalise two deployment failure modes: Behavioural Leakage, an EWS-specific subclass of temporal leakage in which selectors draw signal from pedagogically actionable student behaviours that are unobservable at the prediction horizon, and the Illusion of Actionability, the limiting case in which the entire nominal actionability of a selection is illusory. To detect and prevent these failures, we contribute a machine-checkable no-leakage certificate, kept deliberately separate from an intervention-utility score and connected to it by a continuous actionability-dilution coefficient; a two-protocol evaluation design whose primary deployment estimate retrains on horizon-available features only, while a Deployment-Realistic Evaluation (DRE) audit quantifies the degradation of an already-deployed model under missing late features; and a reference selector, Intervention-Constrained Feature Selection (IC-FS), that satisfies the certificate by construction. Experiments on three public benchmarks and a real secondary-school cohort in Vietnam show that standard selectors can exhibit the strict Illusion of Actionability at course start, and that under a corrected, group-aware evaluation protocol IC-FS trades a small, explicitly quantified amount of at-risk predictive performance for substantially higher available actionability, with the certificate satisfied in every fold. A fairness audit across sensitive attributes and an exploratory single-school operational case study complete the deployment-honest evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: HReMatch: HVI enhancement and robust refinement for semi-dense feature matching
abstract: Reliable feature matching is crucial for SLAM and 3D reconstruction, yet it often fails under extreme illumination changes and geometric ambiguity, leading to unstable correspondences. This paper proposes HReMatch, a lightweight semi-dense matcher that stabilizes fine correspondences with two core pillars. First, a Horizontal/Vertical-Intensity (HVI)-enhanced backbone improves illumination robustness by decoupling illumination from color using polarized chroma mapping and learnable intensity compression. Second, a robust refinement protocol with the Hierarchical Overlapping Context Aggregator (HOCA) and the Progressive Correspondence-aware Encoder (PCE) addresses geometric ambiguities in a coarse-to-fine manner: HOCA strengthens hierarchical overlapping context aggregation, while PCE combines spatial inductive bias and local cross-view attention for accurate sub-pixel localization. On MegaDepth, HReMatch achieves 78.3% AUC@10∘, improving over the lightweight JamMa baseline by 0.9%, while using only 5.8M parameters and 192.1G FLOPs; the best overall ranking (Avg. Rank (Formula presented)) further indicates a favorable balance between accuracy and efficiency. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: How market volatility shapes algorithmic collusion: A comparative analysis of learning-based pricing algorithms
abstract: The proliferation of autonomous pricing algorithms in digital markets has sparked intense debate regarding their potential to facilitate collusive outcomes, yet their behavior under realistic demand uncertainty remains underexplored. This study comprehensively analyzes four pricing algorithms-Q-Learning, Particle Swarm Optimization, Double Deep Q-Network, and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient-across three canonical duopoly market structures (Logit, Hotelling, Linear) under autoregressive demand shocks. Through profit- and price-based collusion indices, we systematically disentangle the interactive effects of algorithmic architecture, market structure, and demand uncertainty. Our findings reveal that supra-competitive pricing emerges as a joint property of algorithm-market pairings rather than algorithm class alone, with DDPG exhibiting the most pronounced collusive tendencies. Critically, none of the algorithms meaningfully adapt to unobservable persistent shocks; observed changes in collusion indices under volatility primarily reflect benchmark displacement rather than altered pricing conduct. Demand shocks produce divergent market-level responses: Logit markets experience significant performance deterioration, Hotelling markets remain resilient, and Linear markets exhibit shock-induced profit inflation without corresponding price changes. Heterogeneous competition reveals persistent asymmetries that widen under volatility. These results underscore the primacy of market structure in governing algorithmic competition under uncertainty within the calibrated settings examined in this study, and carry important implications for the regulation of autonomous pricing systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Integrated optimization for open-field layout and scheduling in flexible job shop systems
abstract: In modern flexible job shops, integrating open-field layout with scheduling is crucial for improving operational efficiency and reducing energy consumption. However, it is difficult to obtain satisfactory solutions owing to the high-dimensional continuous solution space and the spatiotemporal coupling between layout and scheduling. To address this challenge, this paper develops a three-population collaborative framework to coordinate global exploration and specialized local exploitation. Building on this framework, a collaborative learning memetic algorithm (CLMA) is proposed to solve the integrated optimization problem with the objectives of minimizing makespan and total energy consumption. In the global exploration phase, boundary annealing and phased mutation are employed to navigate the expansive layout space and expedite convergence. By constructing problem-specific search operators and adopting a dueling double deep Q-network for adaptive selection, the rationality of the search direction during the local optimization phase is maintained. Furthermore, geometric optimization rules are embedded to correct suboptimal spatial structures and ensure physical feasibility. Through 40 benchmark instances and a real-world case, our approach outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms, demonstrating its effectiveness in solving the coupled layout and scheduling problem. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: A diagnostic framework for auditing decision logic in transformer-based portfolio allocation
abstract: Robust portfolio management requires risk-adjusted performance and auditable decision logic under changing market conditions. This paper examines Decision Transformer policies for sequential portfolio allocation and proposes a diagnostic protocol organized around contribution, necessity, and representation structure. It combines feature attribution, temporal occlusion, controlled perturbations, latent-representation analysis, and regime-conditioned portfolio behaviour.The study covers eighteen trained model families differing in lookback horizon, training rebalancing frequency, information set, trajectory objective, and inference-time conditioning. Each family has 96 correlated ex post evaluation variants applied without retraining. Diagnostic definitions, aggregation rules, thresholds, performance bands, and original recommendations were frozen before temporal-holdout inspection; a benchmark-relative economic-admissibility gate is reported separately as a post-hoc amendment. A secondary comparison with DDPG, DQN, and PPO assesses technical portability within the same setting.Complete-family screening indicates that performance and diagnostic evidence capture distinct properties. Across seventeen families with complete records, the frozen aggregate score has a moderately positive but uncertain association with holdout Sharpe. Retrospective higher- versus lower-Sharpe comparisons reveal differences in volatility-sensitive feature use, temporal dependence, regime-conditioned allocation, and latent organization, without establishing deterministic performance rules.Explanation-validity evidence is heterogeneous and method dependent. Feature-family rankings are more stable in magnitude than sign; parameter randomization, deletion, insertion, and input permutation support action dependence only for subsets of policies. Notably, benchmark outperformance during validation does not imply uniformly supported explanations. The protocol therefore supports staged model comparison and controlled validation, not future-return prediction, causal certification of explanations, or deployment authorization. © 2026 The Author(s). title: RIOT: a Riemannian–optimal transport ensemble for robust supply chain delay prediction
abstract: Accurate supply chain delay prediction is critical for enhancing operational efficiency and mitigating supply chain risks, yet existing machine learning models often struggle with class imbalance, noisy labels, distribution shifts, and feature perturbations in real-world logistics scenarios. We present RIOT (Riemannian–Optimal Transport), a geometry-aware fusion framework that integrates Riemannian geometry with optimal transport for stable and probability-aware multi-class delay prediction. Unlike conventional ensemble methods that rely on arithmetic averaging or fixed voting rules, RIOT treats base-learner probability outputs as structured distributions and performs probability aggregation on non-Euclidean geometric spaces. Specifically, Fisher–Rao intrinsic averaging preserves the local statistical geometry of class-probability vectors, whereas entropy-regularized Wasserstein barycentric alignment captures class-mass discrepancies under an ordinal delay-cost structure. RIOT combines these two summaries through a dual-geometric fusion mechanism with validation-based adaptive weighting and a selected mixing coefficient, thereby balancing local probabilistic consistency and transport-based class-mass alignment.Experiments on the INCOM2024 open dataset demonstrate that RIOT achieves the strongest aggregate performance under a leakage-controlled prediction protocol. Across five random seeds, RIOT attains an AUC-ROC of 0.887 ± 0.0064, exceeding XGBoost-v2 and LightGBM by 0.013 and 0.019 AUC-ROC points, respectively. It also achieves the highest Macro-F1 of 0.718 ± 0.0075 and the lowest ECE, Brier score, and NLL values of 0.032, 0.160, and 0.481, respectively, indicating that the benefit of geometric fusion extends beyond discrimination to class-balanced prediction and probability-quality assessment. Under stress conditions, RIOT remains top-ranked across increasing label corruption, covariate shift, concept drift, and surrogate-generated continuous-feature FGSM perturbation stress tests. At 30% label corruption, its AUC-ROC remains 0.853; under FGSM perturbation at ε = 0.20, it retains an AUC-ROC of 0.864.Ablation and ensemble-comparison analyses further show that the full RIOT model achieves higher mean AUC-ROC than its Fisher–Rao-only, OT-only, adaptive-weight-only, arithmetic-averaging, and standard ensemble-fusion variants. Pairwise DeLong tests provide statistical support for the gains over the two single-geometry variants and stacking, whereas the smaller improvement over adaptive-weight-only remains modest and does not reach the conventional significance threshold. The best mean AUC-ROC is observed at α = 0.6, while performance remains stable for α values between 0.5 and 0.8. Leakage-controlled attribution analysis identifies pre-event calendar variables, customer-region attributes, product information, payment-related variables, and order-quantity features as the main predictive factors. Complementary validation on the public Airlines delay benchmark further shows that RIOT remains top-ranked on a related binary delay-prediction task, although this independently retrained setting should not be interpreted as direct cross-dataset transfer. These gains are accompanied by higher training time, inference latency, and memory usage than strong single-model baselines, but post-hoc sparsification reduces the active model count and latency while preserving most of the predictive performance. Overall, RIOT provides an empirically supported geometric fusion strategy for stable and probability-aware supply-chain delay prediction in risk-sensitive operational settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: An adaptive real-time decision-support framework for dynamic school transportation reoptimization
abstract: This paper addresses real-time school transportation reoptimization under evolving operational conditions. It formulates the Dynamic School Transportation Reoptimization Problem (DSTRP), which extends classical school bus routing by incorporating time-dependent travel times, rolling-horizon decisions, hard-committed route segments, configurable transportation policies, and operational modification costs.An adaptive decision-support framework, denoted ARTHGS, combines Hybrid Genetic Search and ALNS-based improvement. Two complementary strategies are evaluated: localized rolling-horizon repair (ARTHGS), which restricts reoptimization to impacted route neighborhoods, and global reconstruction (ARTHGS-GR), which reoptimizes the remaining active non-committed plan.Computational experiments cover three transportation-policy families, three instance-size categories, and five operational scenarios. Relative to No-Reopt-HGS, RH-ACS, ARTHGS, and ARTHGS-GR reduce cumulative lateness by 55.9%, 59.0%, and 68.7%, respectively. The corresponding on-time stop ratios increase from 28.06% with No-Reopt-HGS to 55.40%, 62.31%, and 64.31%. ARTHGS introduces fewer operational changes than ARTHGS-GR.Nonparametric tests, an ablation study, and RH-CPLEX validation support these findings. On tractable subproblems for which RH-CPLEX proves epoch-level optimality, ARTHGS-GR, ARTHGS, and RH-ACS obtain average local objective gaps of 0.20%, 0.85%, and 1.65%, respectively. The results show that localized repair provides greater plan stability, whereas global reconstruction achieves stronger punctuality recovery under severe or cascading disruptions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: The generalization and diversity of global urban regularities
abstract: The simple but appealing regularities have been observed in the complex urban systems, yet their applicability to contemporary global urbanization remains controversial. Here we conducted a global synthesis of urban regularities, including Zipf's law, Gibrat's law, and scaling law, through multiple urbanity dimensions across 9,014 consistently defined urban areas from 1985 to 2020. We found that general urban regularities governed global urban evolution, as evidenced by the enduring power distributions and common spatial scaling relationships, but with localized diversity reflecting urban development. Globally, Zipfian α moved toward 1, declining from 1.12 to 1.00 for urban area, increasing from 0.91 to 0.97 for population, and declining from 1.34 to 1.17 for GDP during the past decades. These changes were associated with the persistent deviations from Gibrat's law, linking size-dependent growth to the evolution of urban size distributions. Urban rank changes illustrated urban economic transformations and spatial realignments, particularly in Asia and Africa. Population scaled sublinearly with urban area, whereas GDP, nighttime light intensity, and CO2 emissions scaled superlinearly, revealing paradoxes in urban prosperity and environmental impact and prompting a reconsideration of sustainability paradigms, especially in less-developed regions. Together, these findings reveal common urban regularities alongside localized diversity, emphasizing the imperative for tailored governance insights in reshaping a livable, equitable, and sustainable urban future. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Ecosystem services of perennial grain crops
abstract: Agriculture faces mounting pressure to produce food, feed, and renewable biomass from a finite land base while safeguarding soil and environmental quality for future generations. Perennial grain crops have emerged as a promising strategy to address these challenges by producing edible grain alongside substantial vegetative biomass, maintaining continuous soil cover, and developing deep, persistent root systems. A key strength of perennial grains is the provision of multiple ecosystem services. Evidence to date indicates that perennial grain systems can reduce nitrate leaching, lower nitrous oxide (N₂O) emissions, increase carbon sequestration, improve soil structure and nutrient retention, enhance on-farm forage value, and promote biodiversity. Reduced reliance on tillage and external inputs may further decrease fossil fuel use and environmental externalities. In addition to these, perennial grains may provide cultural and aesthetic benefits, such as improving landscape aesthetics, and supporting local traditions and practices related to agriculture. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the ecosystem services provided by perennial grain crops and identifies critical research gaps related to their quantification, trade-offs, and scalability. Robust quantification can support economic valuation, providing a foundation for policy and market incentives that favor the adoption of perennial grain systems and add valuable biomass material to support the green transition. © 2026 The Authors. title: Family ownership, performance below aspiration levels and signaling strategies in emerging markets
abstract: Advertising and CSR constitute the two key signaling strategies for family firms in emerging markets to attract new stakeholders and investors and to retain existing ones. However, the preference of family owners for these strategies may shift based on firm performance. We combine Signaling Theory with the Behavioral Theory of the Firm to examine how family ownership influences these strategies and whether these preferences shift when firms perform below aspiration levels. On a sample of Indian firms over the 2006–2019 period, we find that family ownership is positively related to signaling through both advertising and CSR investments. However, when the performance of the firm falls below aspiration levels, family owners invest more in CSR and less in advertising. These findings contribute to literature on family firm signaling and the shifting preferences of family owners during performance fluctuations, in emerging markets. © 2026 The Authors. title: Global research trends in nuclear forensic: A bibliometric review
abstract: Nuclear forensic science is essential for global nuclear security, supporting the identification and attribution of nuclear materials outside regulatory control. Despite its strategic importance, a systematic understanding of the evolution, thematic structure, and key contributors shaping nuclear forensic research remains limited. This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of global nuclear forensic publication trends from 1973 to 2024 using peer-reviewed records from the Scopus database as of October 2025. Bibliometric indicators and network analyses were applied to examine temporal publication patterns, source journals, research themes, and authorship characteristics. Findings show that nuclear forensic research has transitioned from an emergent activity to a maturing and structured scientific discipline, mainly driven by international nuclear security priorities. The journal landscape is dominated by analytical chemistry, radiochemistry, and nuclear measurement science. Thematic analysis reveals a consolidated focus on uranium-based materials and attribution-oriented analytical techniques, whereas emerging approaches, such as microstructural analysis and computational methods, remain peripheral. Authorship and country-level analyses demonstrate a high concentration of research output within a limited number of nuclear-capable states and government-affiliated institutions. The results reveal methodological maturity yet highlight structural constraints, emphasizing the need for thematic diversification, interdisciplinary collaboration, and international capacity building to enhance nuclear forensic science globally. © 2026 Korean Nuclear Society, Published by Elsevier Korea LLC. title: Re-envisioning home healthcare planning through sustainability: An operations research review
abstract: Ageing populations, shrinking family structures, and economic considerations are accelerating the global need for effective home healthcare (HHC) systems. Realising the full benefits of HHC requires careful attention to sustainability considerations. Consequently, sustainable HHC planning has gained increasing prominence within the operations research literature. This review provides a structured, sustainability-oriented synthesis of HHC planning models. The literature is analysed across three dimensions: (i) resource limitations, service design complexity, uncertainty and disruptions as barriers to sustainability; (ii) enablers of sustainability proposed to address these challenges; and (iii) the sustainability aspects influenced by the enablers’ implementation. The enablers and dimensions are examined to determine how they have been incorporated into mathematical formulations in previous studies. Based on this analysis, a general modelling framework is developed that links decision variables, objective functions, and constraints to corresponding sustainability outcomes. By introducing a unifying terminology and modelling structure, the review facilitates systematic comparison across diverse approaches and uncovers gaps in the explicit integration of sustainability into HHC planning. The insights gathered offer a foundation for operations research scholars to identify emerging trends and promising directions for future research, ultimately supporting more effective progress towards sustainability goals in HHC systems. © 2026 The Authors

title: A Fiat-Anchored Dual-Rail Triple-Entry Architecture for SSC-Based K-12 Financial Systems
abstract: School Services Center (SSC) platforms increasingly support tuition and fee collection across multiple educational institutions, yet they often face a persistent separation between fiat settlement and cross-party payment-state visibility, leading to reconciliation delays and weak shared auditability. This paper is grounded in an existing SSC business system and proposes a fiat-anchored dual-rail architecture in which regulated fiat settlement remains off-chain, while payment evidence is normalized, batched into Merkle commitments, and anchored on Cardano as a tamper-evident third entry. In this design, blockchain is not used as the payment rail; instead, it functions as a public evidentiary layer that supports independent verification without exposing raw financial payloads. We evaluate a full-stack prototype using 10,000 synthetic payment events and report a maximum batch size of 1,681 events per anchoring transaction, 609 ms submission-to-receipt latency, 0.0735 ms local proof verification, and an estimated monthly anchoring cost of approximately $4.28 USD under the evaluated workload assumptions. These results indicate promising operational feasibility for extending real SSC deployments with publicly verifiable reconciliation evidence while preserving fiat-native compliance. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: From natural-extract variability to reproducible nanomaterials: AI-QbD strategies for green synthesis from agro-food waste
abstract: Green synthesis of metal nanoparticles from agro-food waste extracts offers environmental and economic advantages over conventional chemical methods, using natural phytochemicals as reducing and stabilizing agents. However, inherent variability in botanical feedstocks, arising from seasonal fluctuation, geographic origin, and extraction protocols, poses significant challenges to reproducibility and standardization. Current literature documents fewer than 300 systematically characterized synthesis studies using non-harmonized protocols, and botanical extract composition inherently varies 15–30 % seasonally and geographically, limiting the generalization of process parameters across waste sources. This review critically examines the materials science foundations of phytochemical-mediated nanoparticle formation, including the mechanistic roles of phenolic compounds, flavonoids, and terpenoids in metal-ion reduction, nucleation kinetics, and surface capping. We analyze how feedstock composition and extraction conditions influence particle size distribution, morphology, crystallinity, and surface chemistry properties, which ultimately determine biological identity and functional performance. We then evaluate the potential of Quality-by-Design (QbD) frameworks and artificial intelligence (AI) approaches to address these reproducibility challenges. However, we emphasize that significant prerequisites remain before AI deployment is viable: AI model performance reported in the literature ranges from 65 to 85 % accuracy across heterogeneous botanical waste sources, substantially lower than idealized estimates, and current models suffer from dataset-size limitations and the risk of overfitting. We propose a phased implementation roadmap: Phase 1 (18–24 months) requires establishing harmonized botanical characterization protocols and controlled extraction procedures; Phase 2 requires 300–500 documented synthesis experiments across multiple waste sources; Phase 3 can then build predictive AI models on this standardized foundation. Throughout, we distinguish between demonstrated evidence, emerging proof-of-concept results, and areas requiring substantial further validation before clinical or industrial translation becomes feasible. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: An adaptive defense generation method for mimic honeypots based on Minimax-Q game theory
abstract: Honeypots serve as powerful tools for protecting critical internal assets by deploying resources without real value as decoys to attract, capture, and analyze attacker behaviors, and have been widely applied in enterprise-level advanced network defense systems. However, as the cybersecurity landscape evolves, attackers are increasingly developing anti-honeypot techniques that can identify and bypass deception mechanisms, or even exploit honeypots as stepping stones to compromise other hosts, thus escalating overall network risks. Consequently, maintaining both strong deception capability and intrinsic security has become a key challenge in network defense. To address this issue, we propose an adaptive defense generation method for mimic honeypots based on Minimax-Q game theory, which effectively enhances both deception and security in honeypot defense systems. Specifically, building upon the multi-level adjudication mechanism, we design mimic honeypots composed of multiple business executors and further define the reward evaluation function of each executor to quantify its defensive effectiveness. Subsequently, an attack–defense game model for mimic honeypots is constructed, and the Minimax-Q reinforcement learning algorithm is employed to solve for the Bayesian Nash equilibrium, enabling the adaptive generation of optimal defense strategies. Furthermore, a dynamic scheduling mechanism is integrated to replace suspicious executors in real time, thereby preventing attackers from further compromising other hosts. Finally, experimental results show that compared with existing methods, the proposed mimic honeypot demonstrates significant advantages in both deception capability and intrinsic security, offering new insights for building more robust network defense systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Identification with the Avatar and Flow as Factors Influencing the Intention to Purchase Virtual Items in Video Games
abstract: Despite the growth of microtransactions as the predominant business model in video games, there is still a need to understand what factors motivate the purchase of virtual items. This study aims to explain the influence of avatar identification on flow and how, together with perceived value and satisfaction, they influence purchase intention. The research used a quantitative approach with surveys of 412 Peruvian players of legal age who purchase virtual items, maintaining the gender proportion of the market. The analysis was performed using the PLS-SEM technique. Among the main findings was that flow not only influences purchase intention, but also on the path leading to it. The study broadens the understanding of the factors that motivate purchase, following the gender proportion of the Latin American market, so that developers can improve the gaming experience. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The relevance of traditional postal services in a diversifying last-mile delivery landscape: The role of human to human (H2H) interactions
abstract: Last-mile delivery research increasingly focuses on business-to-consumer (B2C) automation to satisfy consumers with an ‘I want it now’ mentality, reduce firms’ carbon footprints, and improve cost efficiency. Much less attention has been given to the possibility that there might be differences across consumer segments in their preferences for technology‑enabled or more traditional, human-mediated delivery modes. Building on random utility theory, we developed a hybrid choice model with a latent class kernel and applied it to stated choice data on delivery service preferences collected from 1,007 customers across metropolitan and regional areas of Australia. Our results reveal two latent classes of consumers with distinctly different preferences. The largest group, which we label techies , value speed and low cost last-mile delivery and prefer traditional postal services, followed by aerial drones and parcel lockers, with the effect moderated by parcel value and the availability of a safe place for unattended delivery. The second group, relational, trusting people , place a stronger emphasis on trust and interpersonal aspects of service and substantially prefer traditional postal services (assuming a safe place for delivery is available) and lockers while showing a strong dislike of aerial drones. To interpret these patterns, we draw on social exchange theory and the human-to-human (H2H) relationship model to explain how relational considerations may influence delivery mode preferences. H2H interactions matter for a subset of consumers. Importantly, our broader findings highlight the continued relevance of traditional postal services in a diversifying delivery landscape. Although no direct spatial effect emerges in the class allocation model, our results suggest that residential location (metropolitan versus regional) has a structural effect by influencing consumers’ underlying latent attitudes. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: “We apologise for any inconvenience”: A local grammar of apology in corporate apology letters
abstract: Corporate apologies serve as strategic responses to organisational crises, balancing expressions of regret with reputational, legal, and stakeholder management concerns. This study analyses 389 apology letters issued by Fortune 500 companies between 2014 and 2023, with a focus on the recurrent lexico-grammatical patterning of apology expressions. Through a local grammar approach to mapping recurring form–meaning regularities in the corpus, 25 patterns were identified and grouped into six sets, revealing a preference for specification-rich, structurally explicit, and emotionally moderated apology constructions. The findings show that corporate apologies are typically elaborated through contextual specification, while intensification and direct reference to the offended remain comparatively limited. Implicit realisations, such as acknowledgements of harm or responsibility, were identified, although less frequent, through a model-assisted prompting procedure using ChatGPT. To situate the linguistic findings, the study also considers the crisis contexts in which the letters were produced, including service failures, product issues, reputational controversies, and regulatory or community-facing incidents. The study contributes to ESP and business discourse research by offering a systematic account of how apology is conventionally realised in corporate letters and by providing a descriptive framework that can support genre awareness in professional communication pedagogy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Prices and prevention: decomposing the Norwegian salmon cost explosion, 2016–2024
abstract: Production cost in Norwegian salmon farming roughly doubled between 2016 and 2024, reversing two decades of decline, and the standard explanation is a “biological treadmill” of sea lice and disease. Using firm-level data from the Norwegian Directorate of Fisheries' profitability survey, I decompose the increase and ask whether biology raises cost through damage or through prevention. Two engines dominate. Global feed-price inflation accounts for about a third of the rise, with the feed-conversion ratio almost unchanged. At least a fifth is associated with the cost of managing biological risk, which surfaces as prevention rather than damage: a shift to post-smolt—juveniles reared nearly twice as large on land, at roughly triple the cost per fish, to shorten the lice-exposed sea phase—while feed conversion and harvest weight change little. A stochastic cost frontier provides a complementary check: returns to scale are mild, technical regress is modest, and firm-level inefficiency is small and stable. The cost of biological risk in the accounts is preventive investment, visible in the smolt line rather than in fish-health costs or a collapse in productivity. © 2026

title: Online multi-view streaming feature selection: A dynamic framework for real-time feature data processing
abstract: In the era of big data, multi-source streaming data often exhibit multi-view heterogeneity and continuous feature arrival, posing a novel challenge to existing feature selection methodologies. To address this issue, this paper proposes an Online Multi-View Streaming Feature Selection (OMVSFS) method based on mutual information theory. Upon receiving new features from diverse views in each iteration, OMVSFS sequentially executes four core steps: 1) Online correlation analysis, where relevant features are identified by computing the mutual information between features and labels; 2) Intra-view online redundancy analysis, where redundant features within a single view are eliminated via a pairwise comparison strategy; 3) Cross-view online complementarity analysis, which retains discriminative features through the comprehensive consideration of feature interactions and inter-feature redundancy; 4) Online view weight update, where the view weights are dynamically adjusted based on the average discriminant scores of the selected features in each view. Extensive experiments on 16 real-world multi-view datasets, together with supplementary analyses of scalability, stability, ablation, and robustness, show that OMVSFS provides competitive results and maintains a favorable balance among classification accuracy, feature compactness, and computational efficiency. The source code of OMVSFS is publicly accessible at https://github.com/zhaocx-lc/OMVSFS. © 2026

title: Bringing arts integration to universal pre-K: Variation in impact of New York City’s Create
abstract: Professional learning with training and coaching has been shown to improve preschool classroom quality and strengthen children’s school readiness skills. Even so, training in the arts has rarely been studied in early childhood education, even though this approach is aligned with teachers’ interests and has been shown to support children’s learning and engagement. We examine heterogeneity in the impacts of Create, an arts-integrated professional learning program developed by NYC Public Schools for Pre-K for All. We analyzed 437 pre-K students in 47 sites randomized to Create or business-as-usual as part of a research-practice partnership. We estimate variation in impacts of Create on children’s assessed skills in reading, math, executive function, and self-regulation by children’s neighborhood income, gender, and whether the child is a Dual Language Learner (DLL). This exploratory study is the first to examine impact heterogeneity of arts integration professional learning on children’s school readiness. Create appears to be broadly effective across neighborhood subgroups; there were no statistically significant differences in the strength of impacts across lower vs. higher income neighborhood groups. Impacts of Create differed by child gender on language and literacy, favoring boys. Finally, impacts of Create were far stronger for a small sample of DLLs on literacy, math, executive function, and attention regulation scores. This suggests that Create may be an effective professional learning series for teachers to engage diverse groups of children through the arts, even while further research is needed to confirm these promising findings. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Starting with Operations Management in Software Startups. Motivations and Initial Activities
abstract: A software startup is an emerging company focused on creating and developing an innovative software-intensive product or service as a basis for creating business value. Operations management is usually not a priority in the early stages of this type of venture, but the need to establish it arises due to specific events or circumstances. Through semi-structured interviews and focus group sessions with experienced founding partners and representatives of software startups, we identified four key reasons or circumstances that lead to the initiation of operations management in these new ventures. Additionally, we identified the twelve most suitable operations management activities to implement in response to these events or circumstances. These activities extend beyond those typically associated with the DevOps approach. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Political career incentives and the environmental costs: Evidence from China's promotion tournaments
abstract: This paper shows that promotion incentives for county-level cadres in China are an important driver of air pollution deterioration. Building on the multi-winner tournament model proposed by Clark and Riis (1998), we predict an inverted-U-shaped relationship between the number of counties within a prefecture and the promotion incentives for county-level cadres. Using the length of small rivers as an instrumental variable for the number of counties within a prefecture, our empirical analysis identifies a robust inverted-U-shaped relationship between the number of counties and air pollution levels, suggesting that promotion incentives significantly exacerbate air pollution. Further analysis reveals that, in pursuit of economic growth, local cadres tend to relax environmental regulations and attract more pollution-intensive firms. In regions where cadres’ performance evaluation places less emphasis on economic growth, the inverted-U-shaped relationship does not exist. These findings suggest that local cadres’ career incentives stimulate economic growth at the expense of the environment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Nonlinear river distance effects on housing prices: Integrating XGBoost and GeoShapley for spatially explicit valuation
abstract: Urban river landscapes not only provide recreational and aesthetic benefits but also generate tangible market value. Quantifying the externalities of such amenities on housing prices is critical for evidence-based policy making and spatial planning. Focusing on Tianjin's six central districts, this study integrates conventional spatial models with interpretable machine learning, to identify the nonlinear influence of river water systems on housing prices in Tianjin and the threshold effect. Using 2020 data from the early pandemic period captures pre-regulation market conditions while avoiding structural distortions from post-pandemic policy interventions during 2021–2022. We have compared OLS, GWR and XGBoost; the latter increased R2 by 10.4 % (CV-R2 = 0.712). The winning XGBoost model is subsequently combined with GeoShapley to visualize local marginal effects. Results reveal a three-regime, non-linear distance–price gradient for proximity to the Haihe River and its tributaries, emergent transition zones approximately within 1.0–1.5 km, with suggestive inflection points around 1.0 km and 1.3 km: within 1 km, a 1 % reduction in distance raises prices by 0.155 %; with a 0.074 % increase per 1 % additional distance in the 1–1.3 km sub-zone. These findings provide quantitative benchmarks for tiered river buffer management in Tianjin's Territorial Spatial Master Plan (2021–2035): intensive amenity investment within 1 km, standard regulations for transitional zones (1–1.5 km), and accessibility-focused planning beyond 1.5 km. Spatial heterogeneity across river segments further indicates that uniform zoning is suboptimal, with eastern and northern corridors warranting targeted investment and western and southern segments requiring functional repositioning. Future work will incorporate resident surveys and temporal variation through XGBoost-STSHAP to enable dynamic, space-time analysis. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Ballistic transport in nanoscale devices
abstract: Ballistic transport refers to the condition where charge carriers traverse a conductor without scattering, where conduction is governed not by bulk properties but by how electrons are injected, transmitted, and collected at the boundaries. This review gives a unified and critical overview of ballistic transport in a wide range of nanoscale systems such as 1D/2D heterostructures, topological insulators, inorganic heterostructures, molecular junctions (MJs), perovskites, nanowire, nanosheet transistors etc. In these systems, charge carriers move over nanoscale length with near-zero momentum and phase-randomizing scattering. Starting with a historical and conceptual overview of ballistic transport, the conversation explains how the gradual reduction of device sizes below the elastic and inelastic mean free paths fundamentally invalidates diffusive transport models and requires a quantum-coherent description based on transmission eigenchannels, contact-limited resistance, and nonlocal electrostatics. We also discuss the key experimental signatures and theoretical ideas used to identify ballistic behavior, including conductance quantization, length-independent resistance, and nonlocal transport features. Finally, we critically evaluate the significant challenges that hinder the clear identification and technological utilization of ballistic transport and also outline future perspectives that are anticipated to convert ballistic transport from a mesoscopic phenomenon into a foundational principle for next-generation nanoelectronics and quantum devices. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Cloud continuum node evaluation and selection via mathematical programming
abstract: Selecting appropriate compute resources in dynamic cloud–fog–edge environments is challenging due to diverse node capabilities, costs and fluctuating workloads. We introduce the Cloud Fog Service Broker (CFSB), implemented within the NebulOuS cloud-continuum platform, as a decision-support tool for resource selection. CFSB formulates node evaluation and selection as a multi-objective optimization problem that maximizes the performance score for each node across multiple criteria to derive a common weighting scheme and obtain their ranking. The model integrates quantitative criteria (e.g., CPU performance and proximity to data sources) and qualitative criteria (e.g., provider's reputation), while user-defined preferences are incorporated into the optimization through explicit constraints. CFSB retrieves dynamic measurements from the NebulOuS platform, e.g., data proximity, to support real-time evaluation under varying conditions. The proposed methodology is illustrated using a dataset comprising cloud, cluster and edge nodes. The obtained rankings are compared with those derived from Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). Also, robustness is examined through sensitivity analysis of the ordinal-category discrimination parameter and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis under perturbed data values. The results demonstrate ranking agreement among the compared approaches. CFSB provides a novel and flexible decision support framework for cloud continuum resource selection and deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Footwear waste recycling: material complexity, technological barriers, and pathways to circularity
abstract: The global footwear industry produces >20 billion pairs annually, yet post-consumer recovery rates remain below 5%, with the vast majority landfilled or incinerated. This review focuses on non-leather footwear, the dominant category in mass-market production. Unlike packaging plastics or single-polymer waste streams, non-leather footwear is an engineered multi-material composite that incorporates crosslinked polyurethane foams, ethylene-vinyl acetate, vulcanised rubber, thermoplastic polyurethane, polyester textiles, and permanent adhesive systems, whose structural complexity places it beyond the reach of conventional recycling strategies. This review critically examines footwear as a polymer waste stream from a materials, processing, and resource-systems perspective. Pre-consumer and post-consumer waste generation pathways are analysed, and the technical feasibility and economic viability of mechanical, chemical, and hybrid recycling routes are evaluated against the key barriers of multi-material integration, crosslinking, adhesive bonding, and additive contamination. Footwear recycling initiatives such as large-scale mechanical programs, automated sorting, and chemical pretreatment-led delamination are critically assessed. The review finds that no single recycling route adequately addresses the structural complexity of footwear, and that the most promising pathway lies in integrated frameworks that combine selective chemical pretreatment with polymer-specific downstream valorisation. Pre-consumer manufacturing waste is identified as the most immediately actionable entry point for circularity, offering compositionally defined, minimally contaminated feedstocks with substantially lower technical and economic barriers than post-consumer streams. Policy enablers, including Extended Producer Responsibility and design-for-disassembly, are discussed as necessary complements to technological advancement. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Green power markets in selected Latin American countries: Experiences and trends
abstract: Latin America is undergoing a significant transformation of its electricity systems as countries strive to advance their energy transitions through cleaner technologies, new business models, and strengthened policy frameworks. Despite long-standing reliance on hydropower, the region has experienced both a rapid expansion of non-hydro renewable capacity and, unexpectedly, a parallel growth in thermal generation. However, comparative understanding of how renewable energy policies and emerging green power markets have evolved across the region remains limited. This paper addresses this gap by analyzing the emergence and evolution of green power markets across twelve Latin American countries, examining renewable energy policies, green electricity products, and the mechanisms that shape market development. We compare policy design, investment incentives, and the deployment of wind, solar, biomass, and geothermal technologies, as well as the role of auctions, fiscal measures, grid-access regulations, and energy attribute certificates (EACs). Our findings reveal convergence in the types of policy instruments adopted, but substantial differences in their implementation and green power market development. Overall, market development remains limited and fragmented. The analysis suggests that deeper renewable integration will require clearer long-term policy signals, stronger regulatory coordination, and incentives that mobilize both public and private actors. EAC systems present an opportunity to complement this transition, but their effectiveness depends on regulatory stability, transparency, and market participation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Homogeneous and heterogeneous three-way granular approximations of fuzzy sets
abstract: This paper introduces the notions of homogeneous and heterogeneous three-way granular approximations of fuzzy sets by combining and extending existing studies on rough sets and fuzzy sets. For homogeneous approximations, we take advantage of the idea of the scores of hesitant fuzzy elements, from both a direct perspective and a similarity-inspired construction. For heterogeneous approximations, we use a complete preorder on the elements of a granule determined by their membership degrees. We investigate the concept of the retrieval rate of heterogeneous three-way granular approximations of a fuzzy set in a Pawlak approximation space. We give examples to illustrate the use of these general notions. The notions of homogeneous and heterogeneous approximations of a fuzzy set provide a deeper understanding of current research and offer new directions for further exploration. © 2026 The Authors
