title: Rheo-tribological measurements and trained sensory panel texture perception across size-controllable whey protein microgels
abstract: Protein microgels have gained attention as potential fat replacers and texture modifiers due to their ability to modulate viscosity and lubrication. In this study, whey protein microgels with controlled particle sizes (6 and 20 μm) were incorporated at different inclusion levels (15-45%) into fat-free dairy milk to evaluate their effects on rheological behaviour, tribological performance, and trained sensory texture perception. A combined instrumental-sensory approach was used to establish relationships between microgel structure, lubrication mechanisms, and perceived texture attributes. Sensory evaluation was conducted using a trained panel (n = 13), assessing thickness, smoothness, graininess, creaminess, and astringency. Viscosity and coefficient of friction were measured using a tribo-rheometer with stainless steel and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) geometries. Viscosity measured at oral-relevant shear rates showed a strong positive correlation with perceived thickness (r = 0.959), confirming bulk shear viscosity as a key determinant of thickness perception. Tribological-sensory relationships varied with surface geometry. Stainless steel measurements showed correlations with smoothness (r = - 0.798) and graininess (r = 0.789), while creaminess correlated with friction at intermediate sliding speeds (r = - 0.856). In contrast, PDMS tribology showed the strongest relationship with thickness perception (r = - 0.953) and greater sensitivity to particle size. Larger microgels (20 μm) promoted smoother and less grainy textures, whereas smaller microgels (6 μm) increased graininess, likely due to aggregation within the dairy matrix. Overall, rheological and tribological measurements provided mechanistic and predictive insight into how microgel size and concentration influence perceived texture, supporting the rational design of fat-reduced and healthier products. © 2026 The Authors. title: From tabbing to talking: LLM-driven conversational agents for web form interaction
abstract: Web forms are a critical gateway to online services, yet they remain challenging for blind and visually impaired (BVI) users. Despite accessibility standards, screen reader workflows often prove frustrating and error-prone. This paper investigates how conversational agents (CAs) powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) can enable more accessible, voice-based interaction with online forms. Through a human-centered process involving guidelines analysis, stakeholder consultations, prototyping and a study with 18 BVI participants, we explored how LLM-driven CAs can support data entry, navigation, and input verification. Findings show that participants valued the system’s intuitiveness and reliability but highlighted tensions around verbosity, pacing, and control. From these insights, we derive design patterns that translate abstract voice interaction guidelines into concrete strategies for conversational form filling, contributing to more inclusive digital services for BVI users and beyond. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Cost-Predictable Web3 for Public Asset Auctions: An Industry Case Study of Deterministic-Fee B2G Infrastructure
abstract: Blockchain can improve transparency and auditability in public services, but its adoption in Business-to-Government (B2G) settings is constrained by a practical cost problem. Auction Organizers (AOs) are typically paid through fixed-price, fiat-denominated contracts, while blockchain execution costs are paid in native tokens and may vary sharply under congestion. This paper presents an industry case study of a Cost-Predictable Web3 Infrastructure (CPWI) for public asset auctions. The design combines three elements: deterministic-fee execution, compliance-preserving hybridization, and a treasury policy for planned token procurement. We instantiate the design on Algorand, where bidder onboarding, KYC, fiat deposits, and regulatory coordination remain off-chain, while critical auction state transitions are anchored on-chain. Under an asynchronous bid-sniping workload of 50 requests per second over 2,500 transactions, the deployed MainNet system maintained a constant per-bid protocol fee of 0.003 ALGO and a median time-to-finality of 7.49 s (p95 16.70 s). To assess financial operability under a fixed-price contract, we evaluate a treasury policy based on Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA) and a 50% reserve through a 10,000-path Monte Carlo simulation. In the evaluated setting, this policy reduces the simulated probability of cost overruns above 20% from 25.23% to 13.75%, while reducing Cost Overrun VaR from $36.18 to $9.05 at 95% confidence and from $84.84 to $21.21 at 99% confidence. The case suggests that cost predictability is a practical design requirement for blockchain-based B2G services, not a secondary implementation detail. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Fed-AFD-GAN: A federated generative adversarial network framework based on adaptive feature distillation
abstract: Federated Generative Adversarial Networks (FedGANs) enable distributed generative modeling without sharing raw data, thereby preserving data locality while jointly learning and generating multi-class data distributions across clients. However, under non-IID settings (e.g., label-partitioned data), global generators based solely on parameter aggregation suffer from distribution shift and mode collapse, leading to degraded generation quality. To address this, we propose Fed-AFD-GAN, a federated GAN framework with adaptive feature distillation. Beyond conventional parameter aggregation, Fed-AFD-GAN incorporates a multi-teacher feature distillation mechanism to transfer and fuse distribution knowledge from client generators in feature space, improving the global generator's ability to model heterogeneous data. Furthermore, an adaptive distillation strategy based on feature discrepancy dynamically controls distillation triggering and teacher selection, reducing training overhead in the early stages while improving generation quality in the later stages. Experiments on label-partitioned CIFAR-10 and MNIST demonstrate that Fed-AFD-GAN consistently outperforms the FedGAN baseline in generation quality, achieving FID improvements of 13.17% and 16.69% on CIFAR-10 and MNIST, respectively, while reducing the number of distillation updates by 55.1% and 59.46%, respectively, compared with static distillation, thereby yielding a more favorable trade-off between generation quality and computational efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: A rapid on-site visual detection strategy for vanillic acid based on the specific diazo coupling principle
abstract: The accurate determination of vanillic acid (VA) is essential for quality control and authenticity verification in food and pharmaceutical products. The reliance on instruments hinders on-site VA detection, and existing colorimetric probes, though visually intuitive, remain limited in specificity and signal intensity. In this work, a novel bis-diazonium probe, 1,5-bis(diazonium tetrafluoroborate)naphthalene (NADBF), was designed and synthesized for the rapid and specific colorimetric detection of VA. NADBF features a naphthalene backbone as the π-conjugated chromogenic scaffold, with two diazonium groups introduced to enable diazo coupling with VA. This probe enables direct detection of VA in deep eutectic solvent (DES) extracts without requiring solvent exchange or additional sample processing steps. The method exhibited a linear detection range of 0.75–45 μM, with a detection limit of 0.698 μM and a reaction time within 6 min. It was successfully applied to the determination of VA in corn flour, yielding recoveries of 97.30%–105.90% (RSD < 2.32%). This work provides a new molecular tool for the on-site screening of VA and offers valuable insights for the design of targeted colorimetric probes for phenolic compounds. © 2026

title: Towards a Mental Model-Driven Approach for User Interface Development: Evolving DataForm
abstract: User interface development often faces usability challenges due to discrepancies between developers’ conceptual models and users’ mental models. This paper introduces an enhanced model-driven approach centered on DataForm, a formal language designed to capture, structure, and operationalize users’ mental models in UI design. We extend DataForm to support visual customization, rendering flexibility, and real-time propagation through a modular architecture that separates business logic from interface representation. Integrated into the Task and Data Model-Based User Interface Development (TD-MBUID) framework, DataForm enables model-driven prototyping and dynamic updates. Its abstract syntax is formalized to allow hierarchical structuring of data and interface elements, while propagation mechanisms ensure synchronization between the back-end and the front-end. A case study in a virtual learning environment demonstrates the approach’s potential to enhance interface adaptability, streamline UI evolution, and improve alignment between system behavior and user cognition. While preliminary results are promising, they are based on a structured implementation scenario. Further experimental validation with end users is necessary to empirically assess the extent to which DataForm supports cognitive alignment and usability improvements across diverse interaction contexts. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Historical document restoration via an Adversarial Frequency-aware Guidance Network
abstract: Historical document restoration aims to recover clean and readable document images from complex degradations such as stains, ink corrosion, background noise, and missing strokes. Existing methods mainly improve restoration backbones, but often overlook how to expose the model to challenging yet residual-bounded degradations during training. To address this issue, we propose AFG-Net, a frequency-domain hard-sample learning framework for robust historical document restoration. The key idea is to use input-restoration residuals as online degradation cues, enabling the model to focus on degradation components that remain difficult to recover. Specifically, an adaptive frequency mask generation module constructs hard samples by selectively recombining residual degradations in the Fourier domain, while a complementary-mask objective regularizes frequency selection and improves degradation diversity during training. In addition, we design the restoration branch with a text-structure-aware restoration backbone to better preserve character strokes, text lines, and layout structures. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show that AFG-Net achieves superior restoration performance in terms of image fidelity, OCR-oriented readability, and computational efficiency. © 2026

title: From black carbon reduction to coordinated fuel adoption on a trans-Arctic shipping corridor
abstract: Arctic sea ice loss is opening trans-Arctic routes, but black carbon (BC) from conventional marine fuels amplifies climate risks in ice covered environments. This study evaluates whether lower BC fuel pathways can move from environmental advantage to coordinated deployment on a representative 14,000 km Murmansk-Shanghai corridor. The analysis integrates life cycle assessment (LCA), BC emission inventories, life cycle cost analysis (LCC), a resource–environment–economy (REE) evaluation, and a tripartite evolutionary game involving governments, ports, and shipping enterprises. Relative to heavy fuel oil (HFO) and very-low sulfur fuel oil (VLSFO), LNG and methanol reduce modeled onboard BC mass by 93.9% and 79.0%, respectively. Standard 100-year Global Warming Potential (GWP100) values are 64.68 kg CO2-eq per functional unit (FU) for LNG and 70.53 kg for CO2-methanol, compared with 81.61 kg for HFO/VLSFO. Liquefied natural gas (LNG) ranks first under Climate Priority and Balanced Development, but its Balanced Development advantage over HFO/VLSFO is only 0.0001 in closeness, with similar first-rank probabilities across 20,000 Monte Carlo draws. None of the 60 baseline scenarios or 12,960 bounded policy combinations achieves high tripartite adoption within 25 years; even ambitious LNG cases with positive payoff gaps fall below the 0.8 adoption threshold. Thus, BC is a useful screening signal, but lower BC alone cannot ensure deployment. Coordinated adoption requires simultaneous cost feasibility, port service returns, and sustained enterprise demand. The framework identifies the conditions under which environmental advantage can or cannot translate into implementation, offering a staged evidence base for Arctic shipping decarbonization policy. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Online operating of photovoltaic–energy storage-charging and swapping stations in coordinated energy and regulation markets
abstract: With the rapid and sustained growth of electric vehicles (EVs), integrated photovoltaic-energy storage-charging and swapping stations (PV-ES-CSSs) are emerging as a new business model that enhances station profitability while providing flexible resources for mitigating EV-induced grid impacts and promoting renewable energy accommodation. However, uncertainties in PV generation and EV charging/swapping demand, along with volatile real-time electricity prices, challenge the reliable and economic operation of PV-ES-CSSs. This paper proposes an online operation strategy for PV-ES-CSSs in a multi-market environment to maximize station revenue while ensuring operational feasibility under uncertainty. First, a state of charge (SOC)-consistency-based flexibility aggregation model is developed to quantify heterogeneous regulation capability and reduce station-level flexibility overestimation, providing a unified scheduling basis for coordinated participation in energy and regulation markets. Then, an opportunity value function model integrating supervised learning and dynamic programming is proposed to map the residual energy states of ES, charging EVs, and swapping batteries into future revenue, enabling coordinated optimization of immediate profits and future regulation potential. Furthermore, a geometric-water-filling-based power allocation strategy with urgency indicators is designed to decompose station-level dispatch commands online under different market conditions while ensuring service demand fulfillment and regulation response accuracy. Simulation results show that the proposed strategy satisfies real-time response requirements, and reduces flexibility overestimation by 4.81%. Compared with coordinated multi-market operation without considering future opportunity values, the proposed strategy increases the total revenue by 2.98%. Moreover, compared with the cases involving participation only in the energy market and only in the regulation market, the total revenue is increased by 176.84% and 2.37%, respectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Thermo-reversible bigels stabilized by soluble dietary fiber extracted from microwave-treated okara: Molecular interactions, network rearrangement, and application in mayonnaise
abstract: This study investigates the preparation and structural regulation of thermo-reversible bigels composed of soluble dietary fiber from microwave-treated okara (M-SDF) hydrogels and carnauba wax/sunflower seed oil oleogels, evaluating their application in low-fat mayonnaise. Carnauba wax was introduced as the oleogelator to structure the oil phase, with its crystalline matrix largely determining the mechanical properties and thermal reversibility of the bigels, while M-SDF served as a macromolecular stabilizer to structure the hydrogel phase and enhance interfacial stability. Microwave pre-treatment altered the molecular characteristics of okara SDF, leading to altered monosaccharide composition, enhanced thermal stability and increased crystallinity, driven by strengthened hydrogen bonding and a more ordered network arrangement. Using variable-temperature FTIR and rheological temperature sweeps, the microstructure and phase transition of the bigels were systematically characterized. The spectral and structural responses were highly dependent on the oleogel-to-hydrogel ratio, with the 7:3 bigel exhibiting pronounced thermal reversibility. Temperature elevation intensified bands at 3677 and 1041 cm−1, indicating the progressive weakening of intermolecular interactions and interfacial rearrangement. Rheological measurements confirmed that the optimized bigels possessed elevated storage modulus (G′ up to 4.65 × 103 Pa) and high phase transition temperature (Tgel of 85.87 °C), supporting a mechanically robust matrix. Incorporating these bigels into mayonnaise significantly improved textural properties and viscoelastic behaviors, demonstrating their effectiveness as a clean-label structuring and stabilizing agent. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: The impact of CSR contracting on reputational risk: An expectancy violation theory perspective
abstract: We focus on a fast-growing phenomenon in which firms link top executive compensation to corporate social responsibility (CSR) criteria, commonly referred to as CSR contracting. Drawing on expectancy violation theory (EVT), we examine whether and how CSR contracting influences firms’ reputational risk. Using panel data on S&P 1500 firms from 2010 to 2021, we find that CSR contracting is negatively associated with reputational risk. CSR contracting signals a firm’s social commitment and raises stakeholder expectations that the firm will act responsibly. Firms tend to avoid violating stakeholder expectations by reducing their irresponsible behavior, thus lowering reputational risk. We further demonstrate that this relationship is partially mediated by reduced stakeholder pressure. Additionally, while a firm’s experience in using CSR contracting strengthens the negative relationship between CSR contracting and reputational risk, CEO duality weakens it. The contributions of these findings are discussed. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: Integrated scheduling of single-track channels, tugboats, continuous berths and quay cranes via learning-driven multi-objective artificial bee colony algorithms
abstract: Container terminals, pivotal hubs for modern maritime logistics, underpin economic development and environmental protection. The diversity of resources in port operations makes holistic optimization a vital research focus for both scholars and practitioners. This work proposes a multi-objective integrated scheduling problem of a single-track channel, tugboats, continuous berths and quay cranes in consideration of economic and environmental sustainability. Firstly, a mixed integer programming model is formulated to minimize total dwelling time of vessels and energy consumption of quay cranes. Secondly, an artificial bee colony algorithm with a deep Q-network is developed. Therein, problem-specific encoding and decoding strategies are incorporated, and the deep Q-network is used to intelligently select effective crossover methods. Furthermore, a learning-based local refinement strategy with adaptive neighborhood selection methods is designed. Finally, extensive experiments are conducted to verify the developed model and algorithm against an exact solver and three state-of-the-art meta-heuristics. The results show their stronger competitiveness in solving the considered problems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Food hypersensitivity communication across physical and online foodservice menus in Brazil: fragmented regulation and consumer experiences in a mixed-methods study
abstract: Inadequate communication of food hypersensitivity in foodservice settings is a recognised risk to consumer safety, yet in Brazil no national regulation governs disclosure in non-prepackaged foods. This study characterises how food hypersensitivity is communicated through physical and online foodservice menus across Brazilian cities, and whether communication differs by the presence of local legislation. A convergent mixed-methods study assessed food hypersensitivity communication in 1034 menus (323 physical; 711 online) from 18 Brazilian cities (seven with specific legislation, 11 comparators). Menus were classified by format: no information; ingredient-only; emphasised (typographic highlighting); or symbol/code-based (icons, codes or matrices). Four focus groups with 18 participants explored experiences of adults with food allergy, intolerance or coeliac disease, and parents of children with food allergy or coeliac disease. Most menus provided some information, predominantly ingredient-only (physical: 76.2%; online: 88.0%); few provided none (6.5%; 1.0%). Warning messages were uncommon (physical: 11.1%; online: 0.1%). Explicit food hypersensitivity information was more frequent in regulated than unregulated physical menus (regulated: 24.5%; unregulated: 12.7%; p < 0.001). Higher average customer expenditure predicted explicit information (OR = 3.46), and the effect of local regulation depended on establishment type (interaction p < 0.001). Regulation was associated with explicit information among independent establishments (OR = 8.29) but not among chains (OR = 0.55), which provided it at comparable levels regardless of regulatory context. No regulatory effect was observed online, where local laws rarely apply. Consumers valued clear, visually salient formats — icons and complete ingredient descriptions — and identified hidden hypersensitivity-relevant ingredients in composite dishes and inconsistent staff guidance as key barriers, particularly on delivery platforms. This is the first assessment of food hypersensitivity communication in Brazilian foodservice, showing that subnational regulation is associated with more explicit physical-menu communication among independent establishments. Establishments require structured communication and staff training; delivery platforms need mandatory disclosure fields and standardised warnings; policymakers should prioritise structured allergen fields on delivery platforms, with a national framework as a longer-term objective. © 2026 The Authors

title: Deep contrastive multi-view spatio-temporal clustering for stock volatility prediction
abstract: Forecasting extreme stock volatility from candlestick patterns, investor commentary, and macroeconomic indicators requires reconciling views with different noise levels, temporal scales, and statistical distributions. We formulate this problem as cluster-guided multi-view forecasting: the representation and clustering modules learn latent market regimes from historical input windows, while a cluster-to-class mapping calibrated only on the training period assigns the regimes to future-return classes. We propose DCMVC-TRANS, which couples domain-adversarial low-level alignment with instance- and cluster-level contrastive objectives, Transformer-based cross-view interaction, quality-aware view weighting, and local–global assignment alignment. This coupling is designed to preserve complementary view information while preventing a noisy or dominant view from determining the consensus representation. Experiments on 238 small- and mid-cap stocks show that DCMVC-TRANS obtains the best three metrics at the 5-day horizon, the best accuracy at the 20-day horizon, and the best recall and F1-score at the 60-day horizon among the compared methods. Long-only backtests further show the highest Sharpe ratio at all three horizons. These results support the use of cluster-guided heterogeneous representation learning for robust stock volatility prediction. © 2026

title: Enhanced dissipation and global well-posedness for a three-dimensional flame propagation model with couette flow
abstract: We study a three-dimensional gravity-induced flame front model under a Couette flow. By exploiting the enhanced dissipation induced by the Couette flow, we prove global-in-time well-posedness of the Cauchy problem in R3 and derive decay estimates for the solution and its spatial derivatives in Lp norms for all p > 1. The analysis is based on a Green’s function approach for the associated variable-coefficient linearized operator. Since an explicit representation of the Green’s function is unavailable, we first establish decay estimates in the spectral domain and then transfer them to physical space. These results show that enhanced dissipation induced by the Couette flow is the key mechanism leading to global existence in the whole space, in the large initial data regime. Copyright © 2026. title: A RAG-Based Pipeline for Automated COSMIC Functional Size Measurement
abstract: Functional size measurement is essential for reliable software project management. While automation of the COSMIC method (ISO 19761) has long enabled large-scale application in industry, the rise of Large Language Models combined with Retrieval-Augmented Generation offers new opportunities for further advancement. This paper presents CosmoScope, a RAG-based pipeline for automating COSMIC functional size measurement that builds a structured knowledge base from five richly annotated official COSMIC case studies, applies domain-aware contextual prefixing based on Anthropic’s Contextual Retrieval technique, and dynamically retrieves relevant examples during inference. A system prompt refined through iterative development encodes the complete COSMIC rule set using chain-of-thought reasoning. Evaluated on 47 held-out functional user requirements across business, real-time, and embedded domains, CosmoScope achieves 97.9% measurement accuracy in Direct Mode and 100% in Guided Mode. A three-condition ablation study further decomposed these contributions: retrieval alone adds 4.3% points beyond prompt engineering, and contextual prefix enrichment adds a further 4.3% points on top of raw retrieval—establishing that knowledge base representation quality matters as much as retrieval itself. To handle inherent requirement ambiguity, the paper introduces a novel dual-mode assumption-resolution mechanism: Direct Mode for fully automated measurement and Guided Mode that surfaces ambiguous decisions with recommended resolutions for human confirmation, supporting transparent and auditable industrial workflows. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Decision-boundary aware undersampling via Adversarial Influence for imbalanced software defect prediction
abstract: Class imbalance severely impairs the capacity of software defect prediction (SDP) models to distinguish between defective (minority class) and non-defective (majority class) software instances. Conventional undersampling methods alleviate this problem by reducing the number of non-defective instances. However, they frequently eliminate informative non-defective instances essential for constructing reliable decision boundary, thereby compromising prediction performance. The key challenge lies in determining which non-defective instances should be retained to preserve effective decision boundary while balancing class distributions. To address this challenge, we propose Adversarial Influence-Based Intelligent Undersampling (AIIUS), a decision-boundary-aware undersampling for imbalanced SDP. In AIIUS, we introduce the Adversarial Influence metric to quantify the importance of non-defective instances to the model's decision boundary and formulate non-defective instance selection as an Adversarial Influence-based ranking problem. Specifically, we compute Adversarial Influence scores via adversarial perturbations on a surrogate model to rank non-defective instances and select the top-ranked ones most critical to decision boundary for constructing a balanced training dataset. Experiments on 18 public defect datasets and five commonly used classifiers show that AIIUS consistently improves imbalance-robust performance, achieving average gains of 9.50% in Balance, 3.43% in Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC), and 17.02% in Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) over representative resampling baselines, with statistically significant improvements in most settings (Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Cliff's δ). These results suggest that decision-boundary-aware instance selection is an effective and practical strategy for handling class imbalance in software defect prediction. © 2026

title: Resilience enhancement of multi-carrier microgrids under extreme weather: A distributionally robust operational strategy with actuarial risk
abstract: Extreme weather can simultaneously perturb energy supply, demand, and infrastructure availability in multi-carrier microgrids (MCMGs), while physical service loss and its monetary consequence may differ across load classes. This paper develops a two-stage data-driven Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization (WDRO) framework that separates physical service adequacy, actuarial valuation, tail-risk preference, and meteorological distributional ambiguity. Regional vulnerability is represented by an externally calibrated actuarial spatial vulnerability factor (ASVF), and a two-tail mean–GlueVaR functional characterizes multi-level upper-tail monetary exposure. The Wasserstein radius is calibrated exclusively from meteorological training data, with validation and holdout samples kept separate. For a fixed finite candidate support, the model admits an exact mixed-integer linear programming reformulation and a finite-candidate column-and-constraint generation (CCG) scheme with an explicit no-violation termination certificate. In the industrial-park case study, Glue-ASVF-WDRO yields zero held-out critical-service expected energy not supplied (EENS) and 21.339 kWh of general-service EENS, whereas risk-neutral WDRO gives nearly identical total EENS but 20.571 kWh of critical-service EENS. Matched-risk conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) and two-tail GlueVaR produce the same reported held-out outcomes, and the CCG and monolithic formulations attain the same objective value to numerical precision. Sensitivity analyses show stable held-out service outcomes across most tested perturbations, whereas stronger external distribution shifts cause marked deterioration. The results underscore the importance of separating physical service adequacy from actuarial valuation when evaluating resilient MCMG operation under extreme-weather uncertainty. Copyright © 2026. title: Circular bioeconomy pathways for converting seafood processing wastes into low-emission marine fuels: Waste management, technologies, life-cycle impacts and policy enablers
abstract: Seafood processing industries generate substantial quantities of organic residues, including fish heads, frames, skins, scales, viscera, crustacean and molluscan shells, sludge and wastewater solids, many of which remain underutilized. Converting marine processing wastes into renewable marine fuels presents a promising circular bioeconomy strategy that addresses both waste management challenges and maritime decarbonization goals. This review examines the potential of marine processing residues as feedstocks for low emission marine fuels by synthesizing knowledge across feedstock characteristics and waste management practices, conversion technologies, life cycle environmental performance and policy and market frameworks. Marine by-products can support multiple fuel pathways. The suitability of each pathway depends strongly on feedstock composition, moisture content, nitrogen levels, and system integration. Life cycle assessment studies indicate that marine waste derived fuels can reduce environmental impacts compared with conventional disposal and fossil marine fuels, although performance depends on factors such as feedstock logistics, upgrading requirements, methane leakage control and energy inputs. The review highlights the role of emerging regulatory frameworks such as the IMO greenhouse gas strategy and FuelEU Maritime regulation in shaping future fuel adoption. Marine waste to fuel systems can contribute to maritime decarbonization when implemented within cascading circular bioeconomy models that prioritize high value compound recovery before energy conversion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Bridging the privacy gap: Developers’ practices and the missing role of privacy engineers
abstract: Context: Privacy has become a first order concern in software engineering, yet organizations still struggle to translate legal mandates into actionable engineering practices. Goal: This study investigates how Brazilian software practitioners perceive and operationalize privacy standards/practices. Methods: We conduct a conceptual replication of prior work via survey (N = 31). The instrument maps privacy-related perceptions/practices, use of standards/frameworks/techniques, organizational responsibility allocation, perceived challenges, and improvement opportunities. Results: Practitioners report distinguishing privacy from security, but formalization is limited. Although 60.7% report considering privacy across the software development, half do not use privacy-focused methods, and a substantial portion (46.4%) report being unaware of such approaches. Practices skew toward classic security controls (e.g., access control, 85.7%) rather than dedicated privacy engineering artifacts. The Brazilian General Data Protection Law (LGPD) is the dominant compliance driver (82.1%), with low uptake of ISO 27701/NIST. Key barriers include unclear legal guidance (53.6%), insufficient training (42.9%), and late integration of privacy (39.3%). Automation remains incipient (14.3% fully automated; 42.9% manual). Organizational support is uneven (39.3% sufficient; 39.3% partial; 21.4% insufficient). Applying the Spearman correlation test revealed strong relationships (ρ up to 0.63) between experience, training, and integration practices, indicating that professional maturity and capacity building are strongly associated with privacy-by-design adoption. Conclusion: Results indicate a persistent gap between awareness and effective governance. We recommend (i) targeted training and curricular inclusion, (ii) clearer role/accountability assignments, and (iii) investment in tooling/automation to operationalize privacy-by-design. These actions can help shift privacy from reactive compliance to a sustained dimension in Brazilian organizations. title: Analysis on dynamics and tipping points for a stochastic SIM model involving media influence
abstract: In this paper, a stochastic SIM epidemic model involving media influences is proposed and the dynamical behavior of its solutions and the problem of tipping points are investigated. The stochastic epidemic model is first established by taking into account the media influence. The existence, extinction and persistence of this stochastic model are then discussed respectively by applying Lyapunov functions method and strong law of large numbers for martingales. Existence of steady-state distribution of this system is studied as well by the method of Lyapunov exponents. Finally, to show the effects of the stochastic noise-induced transient dynamics, the problems of tipping probability, tipping time and the confidence ellipse function of this stochastic model are discussed, and the related numerical simulations are also conducted to illustrate the obtained results. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: A multi-product operations-emission cost optimization model with stochastic demand
abstract: Production of multiple products sequentially is widely practiced in industries. Their unpredictable demands and lead times generate inefficient supply chain flow in meeting demands. Besides, production-based business activities emit carbon. However, researchers developed conventional inventory models with deterministic/stochastic demand, ignoring environmental impact. Here we present a model assuming stochastic demands of products processed sequentially by incorporating the costs of operations and multi-source carbon emissions. A lot of a product is assumed to be multiple of its demand plus approximated safety stock. Usually, larger production in lesser setups minimizes setup and processing costs imposing higher holding and carbon emission costs (due to warehousing and temperature control), and vice versa. Consolidated shipments with fuel-efficient slower transportation decrease transportation cost and carbon emission, requiring higher lot sizes and safety stocks, increasing inventory-related carbon emission. This operations-emission cost trade-off encompasses balancing these conflicting objectives. We minimize this total cost via calculus method of differentiation, synchronizing the production flow of satisfying demand of a product during production of other products. The model is illustrated with an example problem and applied to a local Coca-Cola production plant of bottling five types of this beverage. Minimum total carbon emission cost is found to be about 30-32% of the minimum total cost for the former, and 12-13% for the latter. When standard deviation of demands and lead times are jointly increased by 30%, the minimum total cost increases by 5.44%. Finally, results of sensitivity analyses on various parameters and managerial implication of the optimal solution policy are highlighted. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: From what to how and when: Implementing an enhanced MLOps framework for a structured AI development lifecycle
abstract: Currently, AI-enabled solutions in the public sector are often developed in a fragmented manner, limiting their transferability across organizations and highlighting the need for methodologies that streamline the AI development process. In response, regulatory bodies have introduced standards defining the required characteristics of AI systems, while recent research has called for comprehensive methods to guide the integration of these requirements throughout the AI lifecycle. However, existing approaches tend to remain at a high level, overlooking the challenges of translating principles into low-level implementations and bridging procedural and technical perspectives. Moreover, the level of granularity of AI lifecycle stages does not facilitate the modularity of AI systems, which would enable the easy integration of new implementation to meet system requirements. To address these challenges, this paper enhances the AI lifecycle by introducing explicit operations that support the modular development and reuse of AI products. We propose a structured framework that operationalizes system-level objectives across the different phases of the AI lifecycle while systematically leveraging existing toolkits. In particular, the framework operationalizes cross-cutting requirements by bridging the gap between regulatory objectives and technical implementation, making explicit what requirements an AI product satisfies, how they are implemented, and when they should be addressed throughout the lifecycle. By promoting modularity and reusability, the framework facilitates the systematic development and adaptation of AI products, thereby supporting their scalability and cost-effective adoption across public sector organizations. An exploratory study conducted with ten AI researchers and engineers provides initial feedback on the framework. Finally, two proofs-of-concept use cases demonstrate its practical applicability. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier B.V. title: Unveiling the dynamics of data driven innovation in human resource analytics: A grounded theory of strategic approach to HRM
abstract: Data-driven innovation (DDI) in Human Resource Analytics (HR Analytics) presents a significant potential for strategic organizational change. A persistent gap exists between the theoretical promises of HR Analytics and its practical, value-generating implementation within organizations. This study aims to develop a conceptual model for the effective implementation of HR Analytics within private-sector organizations in a developing economy (Iran), framed through the lens of DDI. Employing a Grounded Theory (GT) approach, specifically the systematic coding methodology of Strauss and Corbin, this research gathered rich qualitative data through in-depth, semi-structured interviews with HR Analytics and Business Analytics experts operating within the Iranian organizational context. Data analysis, facilitated by MAXQDA, involved rigorous open, axial, and selective coding until theoretical saturation was achieved, with study rigor confirmed via Lincoln and Guba's criteria. The resulting conceptual model elucidates the complex interplay of causal conditions (e.g., transformation in human resource management, data-driven approach), context (e.g., technology adoption, cultural contexts), strategies (pre-adoption, decision-making, adoption phases), intervening obstacles, and possible outcomes. By highlighting the contextual features of the Iranian economic environment, this model offers a coherent framework to assist private enterprises in comparable settings to more effectively navigate their transition toward data-driven HR management, offering insights for organizations aiming to leverage HR Analytics as a driver for strategic innovation and business value enhancement. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Hub-centric heterogeneous graph reinforcement learning for integrated automated guided vehicle dispatching and unrelated parallel machine scheduling with finite-buffer constraints
abstract: The integration of automated guided vehicle (AGV) dispatching and unrelated parallel machine scheduling constitutes a challenging problem in flexible manufacturing systems, particularly when finite output buffers cause blocking effects and potential deadlocks. This paper investigates an integrated event-driven AGV dispatching and unrelated parallel machine scheduling problem with finite-buffer constraints, aiming to minimize the makespan. In this study, dispatching refers to the real-time assignment of AGVs to transportation tasks, whereas scheduling refers to assigning workpieces to parallel machines and determining processing sequences. These two decision processes are strongly coupled through transportation, processing, and buffer interactions. To address the strong coupling among transportation, processing, and buffering decisions, this paper proposes a framework that integrates a hub-centric heterogeneous graph neural network (HCHGNN) with proximal policy optimization (PPO), termed HCHGNN-PPO. The manufacturing system is modeled as a hub-centric heterogeneous graph comprising four node types: orders, AGVs, waiting areas, and buffer areas. In this structure, AGVs serve as hub nodes that bridge task sources and processing resources. To leverage this, an HCHGNN encoder is developed to extract structured state representations via AGV-mediated message passing and learnable feature standardization. To improve training stability, a decoupled actor–critic architecture is introduced, in which the policy and value networks use independent graph encoders and optimizers. Moreover, a priority-based action-masking mechanism reduces the risk of buffer-induced blocking by prioritizing buffer-clearance operations, while an incremental reward based on minimum idle-time progression provides denser feedback for makespan-oriented learning. Extensive experiments on various benchmark instances demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms conventional dispatching rules and representative deep reinforcement learning baselines. These results demonstrate the capability of the proposed framework to generate effective scheduling decisions for complex integrated manufacturing systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: From standards to patent pools: SEP-owner heterogeneity and the staged formation of collective licensing
abstract: Patent pools enable owners of standard-essential patents (SEPs) to coordinate licensing for standards-based technologies, but doing so requires agreement among firms with divergent competitive positions, technological capabilities, and commercialization interests. We develop a staged governance framework in which SEP-owner composition is associated with patent pool formation through theorized stage-contingent mechanisms. The conditions that increase the governance necessity and coalition feasibility of collective licensing in Stage 1 need not be the same conditions that enable rapid agreement in Stage 2; in some cases, the same compositional feature can operate in opposite directions across the two stages. Using a new dataset covering nearly 1000 ICT standards, of which 57 became viable pool candidates, we estimate a two-stage survival-selection model that jointly examines whether a standard enters the pool-formation process and, conditional on entry, the time required to launch a pool. We find that greater heterogeneity in SEP owners' knowledge domains increases the likelihood of pool candidacy but slows formation, suggesting that fragmented technological ownership raises governance necessity while impeding execution. Business-domain heterogeneity is associated with slower formation but has no detectable association with candidacy, a pattern consistent with an execution-stage friction. SEP-quality dispersion is associated with lower candidacy and slower formation, a pattern consistent with asymmetric outside options weakening coalition feasibility and bargaining efficiency. The findings provide ex ante observable indicators of licensing-coordination delay risk and suggest that standard establishment alone is insufficient for timely commercialization when IP ownership is fragmented across heterogeneous SEP owners. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: RARSGAN: An End-to-End Intelligent Generative Framework for Regime-Faithful and Risk-Aware Electricity-Market Scenario Generation
abstract: Electricity-market scenario generation is most difficult when synthetic paths must preserve not only marginal price behavior but also regime shifts, state-dependent risk, tail pressure, and heterogeneous hub conditions. This paper develops RARSGAN, an integrated end-to-end regime-faithful and risk-aware framework for forward hub-level electricity-market scenario generation. The framework transforms trading records into structured market states, dynamically validates latent regimes through a Student-t Markov layer, constructs a multi-component risk state, recursively simulates future regime-risk conditioning sequences using only information available at the simulation origin, and generates synthetic market-state paths through a conditional TimeGAN-based architecture. The method provides finite-sample structural-error bounds linking fitted risk, regime-occupancy, and transition discrepancies to the structures it is designed to preserve. Evaluation follows a locked chronological train-validation-test protocol with repeated runs and compares the generated paths with held-out observations through mechanism-aligned structural metrics, independent path-level diagnostics, synchronized cross-hub dependence tests, and downstream procurement-risk measures. The results show that joint regime-risk conditioning provides the most balanced mean preservation across the model’s primary structural objectives, while the supplementary tests identify important remaining limitations in real-synthetic distinguishability, simultaneous multi-hub stress, and tail-loss calibration. RARSGAN therefore offers a transparent framework for generating, stress-testing, and evaluating forward electricity-market scenarios without conflating improved structural balance with universal statistical or economic dominance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Production Capacity Forecasting Model: A Data Approach in the Apparel Industry
abstract: In the clothing industry, a sector facing increasingly stringent demands regarding productivity, costs, and delivery schedules, the application of machine learning to forecast production capacity has become an essential management requirement. This study focuses on developing a production capacity forecasting model by analyzing the interplay between clothing order characteristics and sewing line parameters. The Naive Bayes model provides a probabilistic framework for classifying expected production capacity into distinct levels; consequently, the model’s output offers a clear basis for planners to assess capacity-related risks and make informed decisions regarding resource allocation and line balancing. Specifically, the forecasting results can support decisions concerning workforce requirements, production scheduling, sewing line assignments, and delivery planning. The research also demonstrates the potential of machine learning as a decision-support tool, transforming historical production data into actionable insights to inform practical plans. These findings will enable fashion enterprises to optimize resources, meet rigorous customer demands, and mitigate risks throughout the production process. © 2027, Semarak Ilmu Publishing. .

title: Selective etching of atomically flat diamond (111) surfaces using H2+N2 plasma etching
abstract: In this study, atomically flat (111) diamond surfaces fabricated by lateral homoepitaxial growth were employed as a platform for H2 + N2 plasma etching. Atomically flat (111) diamond surfaces have been reported to exhibit high performance in inversion-mode diamond MOSFETs, making them a promising platform for advanced diamond devices. While lateral etching is dominant in conventional hydrogen plasma etching, the introduction of nitrogen into hydrogen plasma promotes vertical etching. The etching rate was approximately 1 nm/min, and the root-mean-square (RMS) roughness ( S q) of the etched trench bottom was less than 0.25 nm. Anisotropic trenches were successfully formed, and the atomically flat surface was preserved after metal-mask removal. In contrast, previous studies using commercially available mechanically polished HPHT diamond substrates have had difficulty distinguishing the effects of surface defects and polishing-induced damage on etching behavior and surface roughness. By employing atomically flat (111) surfaces, we clearly identified N2-induced etch pits that were not observed in conventional hydrogen plasma etching, demonstrating that N2 addition promotes vertical etching on the (111) surface. Furthermore, an etching depth on the order of 100 nm was achieved while maintaining a flat surface, demonstrating the potential of the proposed process for high-precision diamond device fabrication. The influence of boron incorporated in the diamond substrate was beyond the scope of this study. The findings provide valuable insights toward the realization of diamond devices with atomically flat surfaces and are expected to contribute to further advances in device design and fabrication for diamond power electronics and quantum technologies. © 2026 The Authors.

title: D4RNet: A lightweight distracted driver detection network with knowledge distillation and gradient reversal layer
abstract: Distracted Driver Detection (DDD) is critical for intelligent transportation systems, yet existing methods often incur high computational costs, leading to non-real-time detection on terminals and/or limited generalization across different camera views. In this work, we propose D4RNet, a lightweight Distracted Driver Detection network that integrates knowledge Distillation with a gradient Reversal layer (GRL) for the first time in this domain. We employ a Swin-B as a teacher guide a MobileNetV2 student for training, in addition to predicting the type of distraction, the forward path extracts multi-scale, low-semantic features to predict the auxiliary tags, while during backpropagation the GRL reverses the gradient to adversarially suppress the auxiliary label, thereby enforcing the model to learn domain-invariant representations of the distraction behaviors, rather than noise such as image modality, camera angle, or vehicle scenes. Experimental results show improvements of 3.4% on D-all and 4.3% on N-all over the baseline, attains 81.32% average accuracy over eight subsets, surpassing the previous SOTA by 3.36%, while achieving 52 FPS on a real edge device, Jetson Nano via ONNX Runtime. Qualitative tests on real driving videos also demonstrate strong performance and robustness. Moreover, we introduce five new temporal–spatial combined splits for the 100-Driver dataset along with corresponding baselines, to provide a more comprehensive evaluation of model performance. We also indicate, based on numerous experiments, that future work should prioritize annotation quality and image diversity rather than architectural over-engineering. In summary, D4RNet offers a fast, accurate, and open-source solution for real-time DDD at the edge. Code, data, and models are available at https://github.com/jerodzhao/D4RNet. © 2026 The Author(s). title: The functional Choquet integral
abstract: We introduce the notion of functional Choquet integral (FCI), a new family of fusion operators that are aggregation functions in many cases, obtained by replacing the capacity values in the discrete Choquet integral with data-dependent fusion functions applied to the ordered tail of the input vector. Unlike previous extensions, different functions are allowed at each summation term, providing additional modeling flexibility while preserving the ordered-difference structure of the Choquet integral. We provide a detailed mathematical analysis of the main structural properties of the FCI. Necessary and sufficient conditions are established for idempotency, homogeneity, monotonicity, and shift-invariance. In particular, we prove that monotonicity of the FCI is guaranteed under a double-increasing condition on the generating vector of functions, and a sufficient condition is given for comonotone additivity. These results clarify both the expressive power and the structural limitations of the proposed framework. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Biomass and MOF-derived FeCo/C aerogels with tailorable electromagnetic wave absorption performance
abstract: The synergistic regulation of impedance matching and attenuation capability provides an effective strategy for achieving efficient electromagnetic wave absorption (EWA). However, challenges in cost and process remain for large-scale industrial applications. Herein, a facile one-step method is designed to synthesize a sugarcane-derived carbon aerogel loaded with FeCo bimetallic nanoparticle heterostructures (FeCo/C@SCA). It is revealed that the sugarcane-derived carbon aerogel retains its original pore structure without collapse after high-temperature carbonization with FeCo bimetallic nanoparticles uniformly distributed across the material surface. Its unique three-dimensional (3D) porous structure optimizes the impedance matching of the material, promoting multiple reflections and scattering of electromagnetic wave (EMW) within the material. The synergistic effect of dielectric loss and magnetic loss enhances the performance of the material in terms of EWA. Among these, FeCo/C@SCA achieves an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB, RL < −10 dB) of 7.2 GHz at a thickness of 1.7 mm when the Fe/Co ratio is 1:2; FeCo/C@SCA with an Fe/Co ratio of 1:1 achieves a minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of −52.60 dB at a thickness of 3.6 mm. This study proposes a new method for creating high-performance EMW absorbers in addition to achieving high-value exploitation of waste biomass. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Shaping sustainable investment through digital technologies: Strategic perspectives for the transformation era
abstract: This paper examines the importance of technological infrastructure in influencing sustainable investment, with particular reference to gross fixed capital formation (GFCF) and foreign direct investment (FDI). We use principal component analysis (PCA) and data envelopment analysis (DEA) to uncover the structural interdependences among digital readiness, innovation capacity and macroeconomic stability. Countries that are identified as DEA-efficient, with high internet penetration, extensive mobile uptake and strong high-tech exports, are consistently receiving greater investment. Inflation impacts economies in different ways, it prevents capital accumulation in less efficient economies and it helps promote investment in more efficient economies. This highlights the importance of context sensitive macroeconomic strategies. Unemployment is still a big hurdle to sustainable investment, limiting GFCF and FDI especially in economies with structural rigidities. The outlier analysis identifies Vietnam, China and Malta as examples of ICT-driven investment resilience, while Sudan illustrates how structural and labor-market constraints can impede capital accumulation despite moderate digital progress. A robust digital infrastructure, innovation capacity and a stable macroeconomic and labor-market are essential to sustain competitive investment strategies. This alignment of factors strategically promotes inclusive growth and long-term investment resilience in countries. It provides actionable guidance to policy makers and business leaders to advance sustainable economic development. © 2026

title: Increasing the Efficiency of Using the Energy Potential of Wood: Solutions for Ukraine
abstract: The aim of the research is to develop directions for increasing the efficiency of using wood as an energy source in Ukraine. The state of global forestry and the use of the energy potential of fuel wood from 2013 to 2023 is assessed on the basis of data from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). The analysis of global trends in logging, wood processing, and the use of wood as fuel revealed discrepancies in global trends regarding the rates of change in the share of fuel wood production, wood pellets, and briquettes. Significant growth rates in the production of wood agglomerates worldwide indicate an intensification of the use of energy potential of wood driven by ecological and economic factors. With one of the highest shares of fuel wood in total wood volume, Ukraine produces nearly 7 times less wood pellets than Germany. Based on the developed regression models, a scenario has been elaborated to enhance the efficiency of utilizing the fuel potential of wood in Ukraine. It has been demonstrated that there are reserves in Ukraine for processing fuel wood and waste from both wood processing and saw-milling industries into more efficient products in terms of energy production and compliance with environmental conditions, namely pellets, briquettes, and so on. It is concluded about advisability to process wood waste directly at the sites of logging or wood processing, using technologies and equipment for collecting and sorting the waste from saw-milling and woodworking production and by-products. The interest of local communities, the availability of labor, and support for small businesses will contribute to the implementation of the proposed scenario, which will improve the fuel and energy security of the country. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Corporate venturing in the digital era
abstract: Rapid technological advances in artificial intelligence and other digital technologies play a critical role in enabling established organizations to venture into new entrepreneurial opportunities. These advances present new challenges for corporate venturing (CV): how to organize, transfer information, and execute venturing activities as existing organizational structures and competencies become obsolete. This article introduces a framework for understanding how digital technologies reshape knowledge search in CV contexts under varying levels of environmental complexity, and proposes a typology of human-machine configurations that serves as a diagnostic tool for assessing the degree of machine autonomy in CV decisions. It further explores the opportunities and unintended consequences of these evolving digital venturing practices. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: Predictive maintenance for aero-engine fleets integrating uncertainty-aware remaining useful life estimation and maintenance decisions
abstract: Prognostics and health management plays a critical role in improving flight safety and reducing lifecycle costs in aero-engine systems. However, existing predictive maintenance studies generally focus on individual engines or treat remaining useful life (RUL) estimation and maintenance scheduling as separate processes, limiting their applicability to fleet-level operations under uncertain degradation conditions. To address this limitation, this study develops an end-to-end predictive maintenance framework that couples uncertainty-aware RUL estimation with multi-objective maintenance optimization for aero-engine fleets. First, an integrated deep learning model based on Transformer and Monte Carlo dropout is constructed to estimate the RUL and quantify its predictive uncertainty. The resulting uncertainty information is subsequently propagated into a multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming model through risk-related constraints, thereby establishing a closed-loop connection between the prediction and scheduling layers. The model simultaneously minimizes the total maintenance completion time and operating cost under maintenance-resource and sequencing constraints. An iterative ϵ-constraint method is employed to obtain exact Pareto solutions for small-scale fleet instances. For large-scale instances, a tailored multi-objective artificial bee colony algorithm integrated with Q-learning, termed MOABC-QL, is developed by redesigning the search operators, constraint-handling mechanism, and learning-based strategy selection. Unlike iterative methods that repeatedly invoke commercial solvers, MOABC-QL directly approximates the Pareto front with reduced computational overhead. Experimental results based on aero-engine datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework can effectively propagate RUL uncertainty into fleet maintenance decisions and generate high-quality maintenance plans for both small- and large-scale scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: VPP-Based Park-Level Integrated Energy Scheduling System with Carbon Emission and Integrated Demand Response Mechanism Using Data-Driven Distributionally Robust Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the effective management of distributed Renewable Energy (RE) sources in multi-user Park-level Integrated Energy Systems (PIESs), aiming to coordinate power supply, cooling, and other forms of energy through a Virtual Power Plant (VPP) while enhancing environmental and economic benefits in regulation markets. Beyond the uncertain influence of solar PhotoVoltaic (PV) power on VPP operation, the challenge exists in establishing carbon trading and Integrated Demand Response (IDR) mechanisms to enable internal regulation of VPP. To address the above problem, a data-driven two-stage Distributed Robust Optimization (2-DRO) model is proposed. The overall goal is to minimize the operating costs of VPP by maintaining a supply-demand balance in PIESs along with protecting the electricity for production tasks. A case study of an actual PIES in eastern China reveals that our model is more practical and cost-effective. It integrates the deployment of both electricity and cooling energy under the mechanism of IDR and carbon emissions, realising flexible scheduling for multi-scenario operation of PIES. © The author(s) 2027.

title: Bridging criticality assessment and supply chain resilience: a structured framework for operationalizing mitigation actions
abstract: Critical raw materials underpin the energy transition, defense, and digitalization, yet criticality assessments remain diagnostic: they quantify supply risk and vulnerability without prescribing how to act. This gap is addressed through a structured review, from which 139 mitigation actions across mechanisms, capability types, and disruption pathway categories were compiled, harmonized, and classified. A dependency matrix encodes 278 relationships between actions. To operationalize the resulting catalog, a five-stage decision funnel is introduced to filter it by actor-specific structural boundaries and operational readiness. The illustrative application to vehicle electronics shows that no single action is universally applicable, and the set of suitable actions varies with the actor, temporal horizon, degree of control, and disruption profile. By making actor-specific feasibility and inter-action dependencies explicit, the framework enables companies and countries to assemble coherent mitigation portfolios rather than deploying isolated actions whose prerequisites, amplifications, or contradictions remain unexamined. © 2026 The Authors. title: pH-dependent foam stability of egg white protein-sodium alginate-eggshell powder systems: Roles of soluble calcium availability, bulk structuring, and interfacial behaviour
abstract: Egg white protein (EWP)-based foams are widely used in aerated foods, and their stability depends on bulk-phase structure and air-water interfacial behaviour. This study investigated how initial pH conditions regulate soluble calcium availability, structural assembly, interfacial behaviour, and foam stability in EWP-sodium alginate (SA)-eggshell powder (EP) systems. EWP-SA dispersions were initially adjusted to pH 5.0, 7.0, or 9.0 before EP incorporation. Wet ball milling reduced EP to a submicron particle size of 0.41 μm while preserving the calcite CaCO3 crystalline structure. The pH 5.0 group showed the greatest pH increase after EP addition and the highest SWeibull plateau values for soluble calcium measured colorimetrically (21.52-24.22 mM), consistent with enhanced CaCO3 dissolution under the initially acidic condition. This group also exhibited enhanced EWP-SA association, possible Ca2+-mediated alginate crosslinking, broader particle-size distributions, higher β-Sheet contents, stronger bulk viscoelasticity, greater aggregation, and improved long-term foam retention during standing. Although the pH 7.0 and 9.0 groups generally exhibited higher dilatational moduli under the applied oscillatory conditions, the pH 5.0 group showed a faster initial adsorption response, with a maximum Kdiff of 2.359 mN m−1·s−1/2. Moreover, the 1.5% SA-1% EP and 1.5% SA-2% EP systems in the pH 5.0 group retained 100% and 95.63% of their foam volumes after 12 h, respectively. Foam stability was associated with changes in soluble calcium availability, bulk viscoelasticity, and interfacial behaviour. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for constructing stable EWP-SA-EP foams by regulating initial pH to coordinate bulk-interfacial coupling processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Optimal Pricing Strategies and Channel Modes Selection for A Fresh Agricultural Product Supply Chain with Blockchain Traceability
abstract: The traceability system supported by blockchain technology (BCT) provides consumers with authentic information, triggering the premium effect in the fresh agricultural product supply chain (FASC). This paper introduces BCT to the FASC, which consists of a powerful manufacturer and a retailer. We consider two channel modes: The dual-channel (DC) mode, in which the retailer sells products through an offline channel and the manufacturer sells through an online channel, and the buy-online-pickup-in-store (BOPS) mode, in which the manufacturer adds BOPS options to consumers. We analyse the optimal pricing strategies in scenarios with and without BCT and discuss the channel mode selection between DC and BOPS modes for the manufacturer and retailer with BCT. The results show that when the label cost is below the threshold, the manufacturer may adopt BCT, and the retailer is incentivised to join BCT when the premium effect is high. Furthermore, the channel mode selection of the manufacturer and retailer depends mainly on the demand for the BOPS channel. When the demand for the BOPS channel is low (high), both the manufacturer and retailer prefer the DC (BOPS) mode; when the demand for the BOPS channel is moderate, the manufacturer prefers the DC mode, and the retailer prefers the BOPS mode. To resolve the conflict of channel mode preference, we design a set of fixed transfer payment contracts to ensure the uniformity of channel mode preference between the manufacturer and retailer. The adoption of BCT may improve the consumer surplus when the premium effect is high, and the consumer surplus in BOPS mode is higher than that in DC mode when the demand of the BOPS channel exceeds the threshold. © The author(s) 2027.

title: Decarbonization pathways for the dust-proof nets industry
abstract: Plastic dust-proof nets (DPNs) are widely used for mitigating construction fugitive dust to safeguard urban air quality. However, the DPN life cycle entails energy consumption and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from production and plastic pollution from end-of-life disposal. This study develops an integrated framework combining Material Flow Analysis (MFA) and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) to evaluate the resource and environmental impacts of the DPN industry across its entire life cycle under four scenarios. A roadmap for decarbonization by 2060 is also developed. The results indicate that by 2060, under a business-as-usual scenario, GHG emissions from China’s DPN industry could reach 6.14 Mt CO2e, representing increases of 5.9% in GHG emissions and 7.5% in economic costs compared to 2021 levels. Scenario analysis highlights the importance of enhancing recycling rates to reduce energy use, GHG emissions, and plastic pollution. These measures are critical for establishing a closed-loop supply system in this industry, which is key to synergizing GHG emission reduction, pollution control, and economic development. Compared to the baseline scenario, the optimal scenario achieves a 14.0% increase in economic cost while concurrently reducing GHG emissions by 47.3% and plastic pollution by 28.2%. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: MOOC Dropout Prediction with Machine Learning Techniques: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) have gained popularity as an accessible form of education, attracting a diverse and widespread student base. Despite their potential, MOOCs face a significant challenge: high dropout rates, which undermine their effectiveness and impact. The increasing interest in addressing this problem led to numerous studies developing new models to predict dropouts early and automatically, many of which use Machine Learning (ML) approaches. This research performs a quantitative synthesis of the performance of ML techniques for early dropout prediction in MOOCs. Following PRISMA guidelines, we perform a systematic review and meta-analysis. To analyze the overall performance, we use a random-effects model for a meta-analysis of proportions, analyzing two metrics: sensitivity and specificity. We have also studied the relationship between some of the studies’ characteristics and the performance obtained by means of subgroup analysis. The results indicate that ML systems are capable of accurately detecting a significant percentage of potential dropouts. However, the performance of these systems varies depending on the dataset and the definition of dropout used in each study. Despite the promising findings, the high heterogeneity observed across studies suggests that these results should be interpreted with caution. © The author(s) 2027.

title: FDI spillovers in history: Interwar Japanese “Zaikabo” investment in China's cotton spinning industry
abstract: We estimate productivity spillovers from Japanese cotton-spinning firms in China (known as Zaikabo,"在華紡") to local Chinese cotton-spinning mills based on plant-level data for 1925 to 1938. In order to capture the important role of distance in facilitating such spillovers we geo-localised the plants. Our results provide clear evidence for positive spillovers from Zaikabo to local Chinese mills, which go hand-in-hand with an upgrade in production technology towards greater use of capital. Spillovers are very localised, being strongest within a radius of up to 10 km around the Zaikabo and particularly strong for mills in Shanghai. Exploiting information on the workforce composition of the Japanese affiliates, we find suggestive evidence of a skilled-labour channel: spillovers tend to be larger from Zaikabo employing higher shares of skilled labour. We also find some evidence in line with the idea that these gains are larger for Chinese mills with higher initial productivity, consistent with a role for absorptive capacity. Our paper is the first to document FDI productivity spillovers in a historical context and to characterise the channels through which they operate. © 2026 The Authors

title: Conceptualising a scale to measure customers’ off-premise dining experience (OPDineX) with third-party food delivery services
abstract: Third-party food delivery services (TPFDs) have reshaped how consumers experience restaurant meals. Although a substantial body of research on TPFDs exists, measurement of the Off‑Premise Dining Experience (OPDineX) remains fragmented across levels of abstraction in variables measured (high-order vs attribute-based), discrete journey stages, and measures from other contexts. Addressing this gap, this study develops and validates the OPDineX scale as a unified, journey‑based measure capturing customers’ holistic experience with salient attributes across pre‑meal, in‑meal, and post‑meal phases. The study followed a four-stage scale development process, and qualitative item generation and refinement were combined with four quantitative studies conducted in Australia and Singapore. The resulting OPDineX scale comprises eight dimensions and demonstrates strong reliability, convergent, discriminant, and predictive validity, as well as measurement invariance across contexts. By operationalising customer experience at the attribute level while preserving a coherent journey structure, OPDineX advances the measurement of customer experience and provides a robust diagnostic tool for TPFD research and managerial decision‑making. © 2026 The Authors

title: Examining the evolutionary patterns of open-source software projects
abstract: Open-Source Software (OSS) is a cornerstone of modern software development, yet evaluating the trajectory of individual projects throughout their development lifecycle remains a challenge. This paper develops an exploratory classification framework for examining how OSS projects evolve along two interrelated dimensions: innovation intensity and contribution sustainability. Building on contemporary OSS research on governance and contributor dynamics, we analyze 1785 OSS projects initiated by Microsoft, Google, and Apache on GitHub. Our findings reveal that contribution sustainability is primarily driven by the resilience and engagement of the contributor base, rather than innovation alone. We further highlight the nuanced role of the first release in shaping early project dynamics, the evolutionary patterns observed in OSS projects, and the contrasting associations of for-profit and non-profit sponsorship with contribution sustainability and contributor retention. By synthesizing insights from OSS literature, this research seeks to offer theoretical contributions and practical strategies for project owners seeking to sustain innovation in OSS communities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Environmental Literacy for Managerial and Economic Professions in Slovakia
abstract: The aim of the paper is to identify employer-driven professional requirements for managerial and economic positions in Slovakia, with a focus on environmental literacy as a key competence defined in the National Classification of Occupations, and to propose a precise set of job-relevant competences to be integrated into higher-education programmes. The methodology combines a content analysis of qualification standards with a review of employer expectations for sustainability skills and an examination of selected study programmes in economics and management using the Delphi method. The findings show that environmental literacy is consistently required across managerial professions, yet its integration into university curricula is still limited. Embedding this competence into subjects such as financial analysis and financial planning, strategic management, tax systems, intra-corporate controlling, behavioural economics and internet communication can enhance graduate readiness for labour markets shaped by sustainability transitions. The originality of the study lies in linking national qualification standards, employer expectations and higher education practice. The implications highlight the importance of aligning curricula with sustainability demands to foster graduates who actively support the green transition. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Talent, Compensation and Productivity: Workforce Dynamics in Shared Service Centres in Slovakia
abstract: We examine how compensation relates to productivity in Shared Services Centres (SSCs) amid digital transformation and COVID-19. Using FinStat database for 32 Slovak SSCs (2013–2022), we calculate compensation per employee, value-added productivity per employee, and revenue-based productivity per employee. SSCs are classified as per their current hiring strategy as Hiring, Stable, or Downsizing via three-year average headcount change (±8%). We compare pre-COVID (2013–2019) and post-COVID (2020–2022) periods. Three results emerge: (1) Hiring SSCs start with lower employee compensation, accelerate wages after 2016, and show a sustained rise in revenue-based productivity up to 2022; post-COVID dispersion roughly doubles, implying uneven returns to digital investment. (2) Stable SSCs pay the most and sustain high value-added productivity but show muted growth in revenue-based productivity, consistent with centralisation and capability-driven efficiency rather than revenue intensity. (3) Downsizing SSCs pay lowest compensation yet record high revenue per head at the median and upper quartile, consistent with portfolio pruning and a retained high-performing core; a post-2020 rise in value-added productivity suggests restructuring/selection effects. Divergences between value-added and revenue-based measures underscore pricing and client-mix influences versus internal process efficiency. We provide time-varying evidence from Slovak setting on when higher pay aligns with higher productivity. Limitations include a single-country perspective, descriptive design and no parent-company benchmarks. Future work could therefore add parent company comparisons, broader coverage, stronger identification, and additional performance metrics. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.
