title: Knowledge Management Strategies in the Era of Algorithms and Data
abstract: The study explores the integration of Knowledge Management (KM) and Human Resource Management (HRM) in the academic preparation of future managers in the digital era. The research was conducted among 126 students of the Staropolska Academy of Applied Sciences (StANS), representing three programs: Finance and Accounting, Marketing and E-Business, and Business Economics. A mixed-methods approach, based on methodological triangulation, was applied—combining quantitative analysis (survey, SPSS) and qualitative exploration (FGI, NVivo 14). The results demonstrate that awareness of KM–HRM integration varies by field of study. Marketing students display the highest knowledge orientation and digital awareness, Finance students show strong analytical skills but lower social understanding, while Economics students present a balanced, T-shaped profile. The chi-square test (χ2 = 7.82; p < 0.05) confirmed significant differences between groups, and a strong correlation (r = 0.64; p < 0.01) was found between digital competence and readiness to assume the role of a knowledge manager. Qualitative findings emphasized the importance of creativity, collaboration, and technology—particularly artificial intelligence—in effective knowledge management. The study confirms that KM is a strategic component of modern HRM systems and that future managers must integrate analytical, technological, and interpersonal skills to manage knowledge effectively. It recommends introducing interdisciplinary, project-based modules that combine HRM, KM, and digital transformation in higher education. Developing T-shaped competencies—analytical, communicative, and systemic—is identified as the key direction for managerial education in the knowledge-based economy. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Sustainable Leadership and Digital Transformation in SMEs: A Literature Review
abstract: This paper explores the relationship between sustainable leadership and digital transformation in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Although leadership has been widely studied, its role in navigating digitalization and sustainability transitions within SMEs remains underexplored. Using a systematic literature review inspired by the PRISMA-P guidelines, the study synthesizes recent empirical findings on leadership styles in SMEs, emphasizing the emerging relevance of sustainable leadership and digitalization. The analysis highlights that sustainable leadership fosters innovation, collaboration, and ethical decision-making, which are critical enablers of successful digital transformation. SMEs, constrained by limited resources and informal structures, rely heavily on leaders’ vision and adaptability to align digital initiatives with long-term organizational and societal goals. Based on the synthesis of the reviewed literature, the authors suggest that sustainable leadership could represent a promising framework for supporting digital transformation in SMEs, warranting further empirical investigation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Filling in the gaps: Digital platform economies and the agglomeration of urban consumption amenities
abstract: The spatial agglomeration of restaurants and retail establishments provides a physical platform for consumers searching for differentiated local goods and services. However, the rapid penetration of digital platforms, such as Yelp and Meituan, has substantially lowered search frictions and fundamentally changed the search behavior of consumers. This paper establishes a directed consumer search model to investigate the impact of the introduction and merger of digital platforms on urban agglomeration and provides empirical evidence with novel datasets on merchant relocation, platform registration, and consumer reviews. It is found that (1) digital platforms drive merchants to locate in cluster locations with lower horizontal and vertical accessibility; (2) digital platforms complement urban agglomerations regarding business density, diversity, and clustering patterns. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Artificial intelligence and corporate environmental performance: The mediating role of green AI practices and green intellectual capital
abstract: Despite widespread artificial intelligence (AI) adoption in corporate settings, mechanisms through which this technology translates into environmental performance remain unclear. This study examines how AI impacts corporate environmental performance through green AI practices and green intellectual capital dimensions. Integrating Resource-Based View, Knowledge-Based View, and Natural Resource-Based View, we develop and test a serial mediation model using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Data were collected from 265 key informants, including Chief Digital Officers, Chief Sustainability Officers and Corporate Social Responsibility Directors, in SBF 120 companies. Results reveal that AI operates primarily through serial mediation rather than direct effects, with 67.8% of the total effect transmitted through the serial mediators. AI adoption positively impacts green AI practices, which develop three green intellectual capital dimensions: human, relational, and structural capital. These dimensions contribute positively to environmental performance, with comparable magnitudes across the three dimensions. The model explains 60.1% of environmental performance variance. This research challenges the assumption that technology adoption alone drives environmental performance. By demonstrating serial mediation and revealing the theoretically consistent ordering of green intellectual capital dimensions, we show that organisations cannot purchase environmental performance through AI investments but must deliberately transform technology adoption into green practices and organisational capabilities. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Integration of Digital Technology RPA as a Tool for Business Process Transformation in the Context of Industry 4.0
abstract: Robotic Process Automation (RPA) is a digital technology of Industry 4.0 that functions as a reconfigured software instance that mimics human behaviour when interacting with digital systems for the purpose of performing repetitive and algorithmic controlled activities. The main goal of the scientific article is to map the integration of robotic automation in business processes. RPA is revolutionizing business information systems, making them more efficient and cost-effective. The scientific article provides a more comprehensive theoretical and practical view of the integration of RPA in business processes, including specific examples from practice in terms of business sectors and use in real companies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Reframing destination stability: how scale reshapes tourism volatility in the Balearic Islands
abstract: Tourism destinations are often described as spatially differentiated systems, with coastal areas portrayed as more stable and inland areas as more volatile. Yet, it remains unclear whether these differences arise from location per se or from underlying structural properties of destinations. This paper develops a structural perspective on destination stability by examining the association between tourism-system scale and supply-side accommodation-capacity volatility at the municipal level in the Balearic Islands. Using annual data on regulated accommodation capacity for 62 municipalities over 2004–2024, supply-side accommodation-capacity volatility is measured as the standard deviation of growth rates in accommodation places and proxy system scale by average capacity. A log–log model, estimated with robust and bootstrap procedures and complemented by spatial diagnostics, reveals a strong negative elasticity between scale and volatility: larger destinations exhibit systematically lower fluctuations, while smaller systems are more unstable. Once scale is controlled for, the widely assumed coastal-inland divide in volatility largely disappears, and the independent contribution of spatial location becomes negligible. These findings indicate that structural stability in regulated accommodation capacity is strongly associated with tourism-system scale rather than being solely attributable to geographical location. The paper contributes to destination marketing and management by: (i) using supply-side accommodation-capacity volatility as an indicator of structural destination stability, (ii) providing evidence of a negative association between municipal tourism-system size and supply-side accommodation-capacity volatility, and (iii) qualifying spatially grounded interpretations of coastal stability. Policy implications are discussed for the design of capacity, diversification and redistribution strategies in mature sun-and-sand destinations. © 2026 The Author

title: Implementation of Corporate Strategy in Era of Industry 4.0: A Comparative Study of Slovak and Georgian Manufacturing Firms
abstract: Corporate strategy follows the vision and sets actions that guide the organization’s direction, resource allocation, and long-term competitiveness. In the era of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (Industry 4.0), this role has become more critical as technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), robotics, and big data transform not only production systems, but also organizational structures, business processes and business models. Existing research has focused mainly on technological and operational dimensions, while the strategic perspective remains less examined. The purpose of this study was to analyze how manufacturing firms in Slovakia and Georgia formulate and implement corporate strategies in Industry 4.0. A structured questionnaire survey was conducted with 300 firms, and the analysis focused on three areas: (1) the existence and centrality of corporate strategy, (2) implementation practices and mechanisms, and (3) managerial perceptions of opportunities and barriers. The results indicate two main patterns. First, although many firms report having a corporate strategy, it is often treated as one of several priorities rather than the central framework for decision-making. Second, implementation practices differ: Slovak firms employ more formalized mechanisms, while Georgian firms rely on informal approaches and show less systematic integration of Industry 4.0 into their corporate strategy. Across both contexts, barriers are perceived mainly in technical and resource terms, and the lack of a clearly defined strategy is seldom acknowledged. The study extends existing research by linking Industry 4.0 adoption with corporate strategy in a comparative context. It concludes that a structured strategic framework is required to ensure that technological adoption supports long-term competitiveness. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The Readiness Level of Quality 4.0 Among German Medium-Sized Companies in the Sensor Industry
abstract: The transformation of manufacturing under Industry 4.0 has introduced the concept of Quality 4.0, which integrates advanced digital technologies—such as data analytics, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things (IoT)—into modern quality management systems. This study investigates the readiness level of German medium-sized enterprises operating in the sensor industry to adopt Quality 4.0 principles. The findings indicate that while most companies have adopted automation and digital monitoring systems, the broader application of data-driven decision-making and predictive quality analytics remains limited. Key barriers include insufficient digital competencies, fragmented data infrastructures, and a lack of strategic integration between quality and IT departments. Conversely, companies with a clear digital strategy and leadership commitment demonstrate higher readiness and stronger innovation capabilities. The study contributes to both academic and managerial understanding by presenting a Quality 4.0 readiness framework tailored to the sensor industry. This framework outlines maturity levels, critical success factors, and practical recommendations for advancing toward a fully digitalized and resilient quality management environment. The results emphasize the importance of developing digital skills, fostering cross-functional collaboration, and leveraging real-time data analytics to enhance competitiveness in an increasingly dynamic manufacturing landscape. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Bridging Strategy and Practice of Performance Management in Industrial Enterprise
abstract: Employee performance management is an important part of business management. However, for effective performance management, it is important not only to have a unified performance management system in place, but also to ensure that the performance management process enables the organizational strategic goals to be met. The study focuses on analyzing the employee performance management system in an industrial enterprise operating in the railway industry. The aim was to evaluate its current settings, identify its strengths and weaknesses, and propose recommendations for its improvement in line with modern trends in human resource management. The research was based on an analysis of professional literature, internal documentation, and interviews with managers. The findings showed that the enterprise has a functional performance management system that is linked to strategic goals and supports process efficiency. Its weaknesses include the absence of a unified Document Management System (DMS) and limited linkage between performance and employee compensation and development. The recommendations resulting from the study are implementing a unified digital performance management system, expanding the set of indicators to include time and personnel parameters, and strengthening the link between performance and motivational and development tools. These measures could contribute to increasing the organizational efficiency, engagement, and competitiveness. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: From symbolic gestures to substantive reform: how ethics shape the diffusion of gender quota responses
abstract: Drawing on institutional theory and behavioral ethics, we investigate how firms interpret, enact, and respond to gender quota mandates within organizational networks. Based on 6038 firm-year observations from listed firms in France, Germany, and Italy, we find that symbolic compliance is widespread and positively associated with exposure to symbolic peer behavior. We further find that firms with stronger ethics-oriented compliance tendencies are less susceptible to symbolic peer influence and exhibit greater substantive compliance. Exploratory analyses indicate that this moderating effect is most pronounced in France and among larger firms. By integrating institutional diffusion with internal interpretive orientation, this study extends research on symbolic compliance and heterogeneous organizational responses to gender quota policies. The findings suggest that the effectiveness of institutional reforms depends not only on formal regulatory requirements but also on how organizations interpret and enact them within their governance practices. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: From Digitization to Transformation: Business Process Reengineering and AI-Orchestrated Governance in Public Administration
abstract: This paper examines the strategic, organizational, and technological determinants shaping the digital transformation of public services in Slovakia, with an in-depth case study of a large public institution engaged in Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP)—funded modernization projects. Using qualitative triangulation that integrates process mapping, governance documentation, and semi-structured interviews, the study identifies key systemic barriers limiting transformation effectiveness. These include fragmented process governance, the absence of architectural and data management frameworks, and weak impact measurement mechanisms. The findings demonstrate that the institution’s approach to digitalization remains predominantly evolutionary, focused on isolated technological upgrades rather than systemic reengineering. To address these structural limitations, the paper proposes a process-driven, orchestrated, data-connected, and partially autonomous digital ecosystem leveraging AI agents. Conceptually anchored in Business Process Reengineering (BPR), this model provides a framework for achieving end-to-end service integration, evidence-based performance monitoring, and adaptive institutional learning. The study contributes to the literature on digital governance by linking traditional reengineering principles with AI-enabled orchestration in the public sector, offering practical implications for achieving the EU Digital Decade 2030 objectives. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Fashion Second-Hand Market and Re-Branding of Humana Portugal: One Strategy for Sustainability and Circular Economy
abstract: The transformation of the fashion ecosystem from a linear to a circular economy model is driving the development of innovative business models. One way to contribute to the circular economy is by extending the lifecycle of products, either through the purchase of higher-quality items or by enabling these items to have a second life through resale in second-hand clothing stores. This business model, already established in the market, particularly resonates with younger generations, such as Generation Z, both in online and offline retail environments. However, how can the value of second-hand fashion products and brands be effectively enhanced? One approach lies in the implementation of a branding strategy aligned with the values the brand seeks to communicate, supported by a coherent visual identity. This project aims to develop a re-branding strategy for a prominent second-hand fashion brand with national and international relevance: Humana. Based on established branding principles, the objective is to reposition the brand in a way that appeals more strongly to Generation Z consumers—thereby investing in the future while simultaneously fostering awareness of circular economy practices. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Process Management in the Adoption of Digital Solutions: Lessons from Healthcare for Industry 4.0
abstract: Digital transformation is redefining how organisations structure and manage their processes, creating new paradigms of efficiency and adaptability under Industry 4.0. This paper examines the role of process management in facilitating the adoption of digital solutions, using healthcare as an illustrative sector where reliability, regulation, and technological innovation converge. Based on quantitative research conducted among 100 healthcare providers in Slovakia, the article analyses the relationships between leadership characteristics, workplace type, experience, and the degree of digital tool adoption. While no statistically significant differences were found between provider groups, a positive correlation emerged between the intensity of digital adoption and the perceived benefits of the process. The findings demonstrate that effective process management and transformational leadership are critical enablers of digital transformation. Lessons drawn from healthcare extend beyond the sector itself, providing insights into how organisations can strengthen their readiness for Industry 4.0 through adaptive process structures, leadership support, and data-driven decision-making. The article contributes to the broader discussion on how digital transformation shapes new organisational paradigms. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Graduate Unemployment by Field of Study in the Košice Region, Slovakia
abstract: The transition of young people from higher education to the labour market represents a crucial stage characterised by significant uncertainty, increasing competition, and high demands for practical skills. The aim of this paper is to analyse the development of the unemployment of university graduates in the Košice region, Slovakia between 2015 and 2024 and to assess the structural imbalances in their employment according to individual groups of fields of study. The analysis confirms that unemployment is highly concentrated in the fields of social sciences, business and services, and technical sciences, which together account for more than 70% all unemployed graduates. The findings indicate a problem of structural mismatch, with labour market demand in the Košice region insufficient to absorb the supply of graduates in these key segments, while graduates of more specialised fields exhibit higher stability and lower unemployment. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Driving Sustainability in Fashion E-Commerce: Mitigating Returns Through Digital Visual Merchandising and Emerging Technologies
abstract: This paper investigates how Digital Visual Merchandising (DVM) and new technologies improve sustainability within digital fashion platforms. This industry pass through challenges from high return rates related to poor product visualization. This study investigates how DVM technologies can help solving product experience issues, decreasing returns and encouraging consumers to shop responsibly. A mixed-method approach combined literature review with case studies and a survey design. The DVM strategies of six major brands were valued through its AI and AR implementation to determine their effects on sustainability and return rate management. The findings show that brands can reduce returns through AI-driven personalization and AR-based virtual try-ons which also helps to align consumer expectations and to implement circular fashion models. Despite these technologies proved to have potential for improving sustainability in fashion e-commerce, the current analysis relies on secondary data and survey design; consumer insights will be delivered on Phase 2. Future work will investigate how different consumer groups are affected by the tools, explore why small businesses face challenges when implementing these technologies and develop standard methods to track environmental performance. This research contributes to sustainable fashion studies by demonstrating how innovative technologies can merge digital and physical experiences. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: What are the Challenges in High Maturity Organizations
abstract: This paper revisits a widely held assumption in the process improvement and maturity model literature: that high maturity organizations face a consistent set of persistent challenges. However, this study tests that assumption empirically through a survey of high maturity organizations, and contrary to expectations, the findings show that ten commonly cited challenges are largely absent in practice. Rather than struggling with rigidity, excessive bureaucracy, or diminishing returns, high maturity organizations report the opposite conditions: increased adaptability, stronger alignment with business goals, more effective use of data, and sustained capability for continuous improvement. These organizations appear to have resolved or transcended the issues highlighted in prior research. For academics, the results call into question the validity and continued relevance of challenges often mentioned in literature. For practitioners, the findings offer a more optimistic and actionable perspective: achieving high maturity may not introduce new systemic barriers, but instead enables more resilient, efficient and responsive ways of working. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Quantifying transfer coefficients in battery recycling routes for material flow analysis: current state and future scenarios
abstract: The growing volume of end-of-life batteries in the European Union necessitates robust quantification of secondary raw material recovery potential to support material flow analysis and policy evaluation. However, empirical data on recycling process performance remain limited. Transfer coefficients (TCs) quantify the fraction of a material transferred from input into a specific output stream at each process step. The product of step-wise TCs along a route determines recovery for each element and links process-level performance to system-level recovery outcomes. This study compiles route-specific TCs for five lithium-ion battery recycling routes encompassing pyrometallurgical, hydrometallurgical, mechanical, and direct recycling, alongside established processes for zinc-based, nickel-based, and lead-acid batteries. TCs compiled from patents, peer-reviewed literature, and industry data were integrated into a Python-based recovery model, generating 36,358 scenario-ready values from 2010 to 2050. Two scenarios are analysed: business-as-usual, with technological stagnation and continued black mass export, and recovery scenario aligned with EU Battery Regulation targets. A gap analysis reveals highly element-specific challenges. While TCs for cobalt, nickel, and copper already approach regulatory thresholds, lithium recovery from pyrometallurgy-based routes are far below the regulatory target. Non-regulated materials such as graphite, manganese, and phosphorus show zero or marginal recovery, a structural blind spot in the regulatory framework. A structural decomposition shows that process-level efficiency is the dominant driver of system-wide recovery for most elements, whereas route composition acts as a secondary and often counteractive effect. The publicly available TC dataset provides a transparent basis for secondary supply estimation while highlighting uncertainties requiring industrial-scale validation and chemistry-differentiated parameterisation. © 2026 The Authors

title: Behavioral involvement and structural influence in negative word-of-mouth diffusion: Exploring online firestorms during service crises
abstract: Online firestorms arise when service failures aggregate individual grievances into collective criticism on social media. This study investigates how user behavioral involvement and structural influence shape negative word-of-mouth (NWOM) dissemination in corporate crises, and the contingent roles of firm-initiated and peer-driven interactions. Based on regulatory focus theory and social motive perspectives, we analyze 33 official crisis announcements and 26,449 user records from Sina Weibo amid the 2023 Typhoon Doksuri refund crisis. Results indicate a behavioral asymmetry: highly involved users spread more NWOM, whereas influential users disseminate less. Proactive corporate responses mitigate NWOM for both user groups. Peer social support amplifies NWOM only among highly involved users, with no significant effect on influential users. These findings enrich research on online firestorms and social media crisis communication and provide actionable strategies for service crisis management. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Grain refinement mechanism of ultrasonic application stage in wire arc additive manufacturing of alloy steel
abstract: Ultrasound-assisted wire arc additive manufacturing (UA-WAAM) offers a promising route to refine the coarse columnar grains found in as-deposited components. However, the effects of ultrasound applied at different stages during the rapid solidification of the molten pool remain insufficiently understood, and the grain refinement mechanism requires clarification. A novel stage–specific ultrasonic application strategy was designed based on the phase transformation temperatures and thermal history of molten pool. Five discrete ultrasound intervention stages were investigated, before arc extinction, at arc extinction, during solidification, after solidification and continuous application. Microstructural evolution was characterized using optical microscopy and EBSD, while the cavitation dynamics and mechanical response of columnar grains were theoretically modeled to establish a quantitative fragmentation criterion. Results reveal that effective grain refinement occurs exclusively when ultrasound is applied during cooling and solidification stage, transforming coarse columnar grains into fine equiaxed and refined columnar grains. Ultrasound applied before arc extinction or after complete solidification produces negligible microstructural modification due to the absence of surviving nuclei or a liquid medium. Theoretical analysis reveals cavitation-induced grain fragmentation as a key mechanism, with predicted critical fragmentation lengths (15.3–25.8 μm) aligning quantitatively with the measured mean grain size (20.9 ± 3.7 μm). Acoustic streaming plays a supporting role by dispersing fragments as heterogeneous nucleation sites. The critical window for effective ultrasonic application is limited to the sub‑second interval from arc extinction to complete solidification. These findings establish a quantitative relationship between cavitation shock wave pressure and grain fragmentation behavior, providing a scientific foundation for optimizing energy-efficient ultrasonic strategies in WAAM. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: SmartSPI - Smart Data Analysis and Trusted GenAI Results - Experiences of the Automotive Skills Alliance Innovation Agent Working Group
abstract: The innovation agent working group represents one of the active initiatives of the ASA (Automotive Skills Alliance). In the EU project TRIREME this WG continues to develop the innovation capability assessment model (ISO 560xx practical implementation in automotive), as well as it contributes to the development of new paradigms and tools required for innovation in the European industry. While in the year 2025 the working group elaborated methods to use prompting with different GenAIs for ideation (ISO 56007) and for strategic intelligence (ISO 56006) and how to validate the results using data validation criteria, in Q4/2025 and 2026 a research team of EuroSPI, ISCN and TU Graz implemented a new concept and tool which integrates a large research network with 3 GenAI tools, such as MISTRAL, ChatGPT and Gemini. This method was then applied for 3 different case studies: Analysis of cybersecurity test cases for vehicle servers in the EU project Cybertester, analysis of the use of new drone technologies in the agriculture sector, and strategic analysis for the innovation agent WG for the impact of the CRA Cybersecurity Resilience Act on European Union businesses. This paper explains the method, the tool, and selected results of case studies. This method became in 2026 a standard training module of the EuroSPI/ASA certified innovation agent and assessor training and certificate for the automotive (and connected) industry domains. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: A pragmatic, demand-driven framework to prioritise critical raw material recycling
abstract: Every three years, the European Commission publishes a list of critical raw materials (CRMs) based on economic importance and supply risk. Boosting recovery rates is a strategy for criticality mitigation, but not equally relevant for all CRMs. This study develops a pragmatic, demand-driven framework to prioritise CRMs for recycling. The approach integrates four dimensions: criticality, relative availability, industrial demand, and recovery systems effectiveness. Industrial demand introduces a market-pull perspective, linking recycling to existing value chains and economic viability. The framework relies on publicly available data and avoids product-level modelling. Applied at the EU level and for Belgium and Germany, it demonstrates varying priorities across geographic contexts. Results position materials within a two-dimensional matrix that enables a structured diagnosis of where policy intervention is most likely to generate systemic impact. This approach translates criticality assessments into actionable recycling priorities for policymakers, aligned with industrial demand and regional specificities. © 2026 The Authors. title: Dynamic hierarchical population-based differential evolution with parameter control and hypervolume diversity for numerical optimization
abstract: A hierarchical differential evolution algorithm with individualized restart is proposed. In each generation, the population is split into an elite layer and an ordinary layer by an adaptive, progress-dependent threshold derived from normalized fitness deviations, and the two layers are evolved by different mutation operators and parameter-generation rules. Scaling factors and crossover rates are adapted from a success-history memory weighted by successful difference-vector magnitudes, supported by an archive whose members are aged out over time. A volume-based diversity indicator, combined with per-individual stagnation counters, triggers dimension-wise reinitialization of unproductive individuals, while a piecewise-decreasing population size concentrates the remaining budget on refinement. To validate the optimization performance of the proposed HPHD-DE algorithm, we selected six high-performing DE variants as competitors, including two champion algorithms L-SRTDE and RDEx, and conducted comparative experiments on 88 test functions from three well-known testbeds. The experimental results show that although the overall performance of HPHD-DE is inferior to L-SRTDE and RDEx, it significantly outperforms the other five competitors. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Rewarding leadership: CEO compensation and growth outcomes in agricultural industry
abstract: Performance-based CEO pay is becoming more popular as a way to align executive incentives with business growth. However, the research results are still not consistent, especially in emerging markets such as Malaysia. In some cases, CEOs continue to receive high compensation even when companies perform poorly, and many companies provide limited disclosure of executive pay. This raises concerns about whether CEO compensation truly supports sustainable company growth. The objective of this study is to examine the relationship between chief executive officer (CEO) compensation and company growth among Malaysian public listed companies. A sample of 25 companies in the agricultural industry from 2021–2023 was selected. All financial data were collected from Orblis and companies' annual reports. Fixed effects panel regression analysis was used to determine the relationship between the dependent and independent variables and control variables. The results reveal a significant positive relationship between CEO compensation and company growth. Well-structured and performance-based CEO compensation aligns management and shareholder interests, supporting both agency theory and human capabilities theory by enhancing leadership effectiveness and company growth. It further underscores the need for strong governance, transparent disclosure, and independent compensation committees while also signaling to shareholders and investors that executive pay design reflects governance quality and long-term value creation. All the control variables, such as company size, liquidity and company age, are positively related to company growth, whereas leverage is negatively related to company growth. Future research should involve a larger sample across different industries and longer time periods while also considering CEO compensation components, executive characteristics, governance factors, and external conditions to better explain company growth. title: MLOps for enterprise AI: A systematic literature review of frameworks, interpretability practices, and organisational readiness
abstract: The rapid industrialisation of artificial intelligence has elevated Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) into a foundational discipline for organisations seeking to deploy, monitor, and sustain machine learning models in production. Despite a growing body of literature on technical pipeline orchestration and continuous delivery for ML, significant gaps persist in how enterprises-particularly within the financial services and FinTech sectors-integrate interpretability requirements, address organisational readiness, and govern data-driven decision-making at scale. This paper presents a systematic literature review (SLR) following the PRISMA protocol, synthesising findings from 170 peer-reviewed publications spanning 2015 to 2025. We examine three interconnected themes: (i) MLOps frameworks, maturity models, and pipeline orchestration practices; (ii) explainability and interpretability integration within MLOps lifecycles; and (iii) organisational, team-level, and governance factors that determine successful enterprise MLOps adoption. Drawing on the SPACE and DORA frameworks for developer productivity analogy, we further contextualise these findings within large-scale FinTech settings, highlighting the particular pressures of regulatory compliance (SR 11–7, GDPR, EU AI Act), model risk management, and real-time fraud detection pipelines. We propose a four-tier integrative MLOps Maturity and Interpretability Framework (MMIF) and identify eight priority research gaps requiring empirical investigation. Our findings offer actionable guidance for practitioners, engineering leads, and product managers responsible for operationalising AI within enterprise environments. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: PIM.3: A Hidden Accelerator Behind ASPICE Level 3 Success
abstract: The indispensable role of the Process Improvement Process (PIM.3) in developing and maintaining organizational standard processes—and thereby enabling smoother deployment of these processes into projects—has become a key focus area across the automotive industry. Increasingly, car manufacturers expect projects to achieve ASPICE Level 3, which requires teams to begin with mature, ready-to-use process artifacts that accelerate product development and reduce time-to-market pressure. Despite this, many organizations still struggle to establish a managed, closed-loop feedback system that connects process improvement activities with the realities of product development teams. In this paper, members of the SoQrates initiative, representing major automotive organizations, present the relationship between ASPICE Level 3 and PIM.3, citing practical examples and best practices for aligning process improvements with business goals. Some of these insights are drawn from assessments and process improvement initiatives, offering a practical guide for organizations aiming to strengthen process maturity and improve development performance. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Readiness of the taxonomy used by ECCAIRS 2 for Causal Analysis based on Systems Theory
abstract: This paper examines whether the taxonomy used by the European Co-ordination Centre for Accident and Incident Reporting Systems (ECCAIRS 2) can provide suitable inputs for Causal Analysis based on Systems Theory (CAST), a method grounded in the System-Theoretic Accident Model and Processes (STAMP). The methodology combines analysis of CAST inputs and outputs with Semantic Web technologies, Unified Modeling Language (UML) and Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) diagrams to map ECCAIRS 2 entities, attributes, and values to individual CAST steps. A representation of the ECCAIRS 2 taxonomy and an ontology implemented in Protégé were developed to support querying and traceability, and the approach was validated using four real aviation occurrences recorded in ECCAIRS 2 for which CAST analyses were available. The results show that key ECCAIRS 2 attributes can systematically support CAST activities such as defining system boundaries, identifying losses and system-level hazards, identifying controllers of the safety control structure, and formulating Unsafe Control Actions and systemic causal factors. The findings confirm that the ECCAIRS 2 taxonomy can be used as a structured input source for CAST, while highlighting limitations related to incomplete coverage of CAST activities, constrained representation of system context and interactions, and dependence on the quality of occurrence reports. The proposed methodology offers a decision-support framework that enhances consistency, transparency, and efficiency of STAMP-based accident and incident investigations and provides a basis for further tool development and partial automation. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Digitalising the intensive care unit diary: mapping users' perceptions in healthcare settings – a scoping review
abstract: Aim: To map literature on perceptions of patients, relatives, and healthcare professionals regarding the use of digital diaries in healthcare, to inform pre-implementation of an ICU diary by identifying factors relevant to feasibility, acceptability, and integration into ICU workflows. Methods: The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines. Studies including patients, relatives, and healthcare professionals with experience of digital diary use in healthcare settings were eligible. Included studies reported perceptions of digital diaries. Data were synthesised using inductive content analysis. Findings: From 679 identified records, 13 studies (2014–2025) were included, covering symptom diaries (n = 7) and ICU diaries (n = 6). The synthesis generated three overarching categories across user groups: relational connectedness and person-centred care; empowerment and meaning-making; and implementation and technological readiness. Across contexts, digital diaries were described as shaping communication, participation, and continuity of care, while also enabling reflection and meaning-making during illness and recovery. However, their perceived value was highly context-dependent and shaped by implementation conditions. Conclusions: Digital diaries were perceived by patients, relatives, and healthcare professionals as influencing communication, continuity, and engagement in care. Patients highlighted reflection, increased awareness, and participation, while relatives emphasised connection and involvement. Healthcare professionals focused on usability, workflow integration, and organisational conditions shaping use. They were perceived as valuable when they supported communication and made patients' experiences more visible, but as less useful when poorly integrated into clinical routines. Their perceived value depended on how they were embedded in practice and shaped by interactions between users, technology, and organisational context. Implications for Clinical Practice: Digital diaries have the potential to support communication, involvement, and continuity of care. However, realising this potential requires deliberate integration into clinical workflows, role definition, and user-centred design. Ongoing evaluation is essential, particularly in ICU contexts where experiential and person-centred outcomes remain underexplored. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: From Scrum to DevOps education: A review of Agile and Lean software development methods and teaching approaches
abstract: Context: Teaching agile and lean concepts is vital for software engineering students, as the software industry increasingly adopts methods such as Scrum, Extreme Programming, Kanban, and DevOps, equipping students with essential skills for real-world software development. However, despite the importance of software process education, a gap remains in understanding the most effective pedagogical strategies for teaching these methods. Objective: This study aims to address the gap in understanding by identifying the most widely taught software development methods and effective pedagogical strategies for teaching them in higher education. Method: This study addresses the existing gap through a literature survey of 50 primary studies. Results: The literature survey analyzed diverse teaching approaches and learning environments, while the experience report provided insights into how these approaches perform in practice. Combining traditional teaching methods, such as project-based learning and lectures, with innovative approaches like gamification, role-playing, simulations, and industry visits enhances both student engagement and skill development. Conclusion: The study concludes that engaging learning environments, utilizing appropriate teaching methods, and using a combination of software development methods topics in a course can equip students with the necessary skills to meet the demands of the software development industry. © 2026 The Author

title: A hybrid fuzzy-LLM decision support system for lifecycle-oriented supply-chain strategy
abstract: Supply-chain DSSs must translate objectives into lifecycle- and configuration-specific priorities while retaining traceable decision authority. Fuzzy models provide structured prioritisation, but generative explanations may weaken grounding and reproducibility. We developed a hybrid DSS in which a zero-order Sugeno engine combines configuration baselines, Industry 5.0 5S alignment, and lifecycle relevance through 27 rules, while an optional LLM renders frozen evidence under output validation and deterministic fallback. Five controlled scenarios varied lifecycle stage and configuration under a fixed 5S profile. Evaluation comprised 1000 ± 20% perturbations, three MCDA comparators, and a single-round elicitation with 15 experts conducted 10–25 July 2026. Mean Kendall τb under perturbation was 0.898–0.938; alignment with TOPSIS, weighted sum, and PROMETHEE was (Formula presented) –0.897 (all p < 0.001). Expert agreement on rule consequents was strong (Fleiss’ (Formula presented)); 25 of 27 cases achieved at least 80% majority agreement and 21 matched the engine. Membership anchors supported overlapping fuzzy regions, but baseline exact matches were 18.2–25.0% and elicited weights did not justify recalibration. The system provides reproducible, model-agnostic prioritisation and failure-tolerant explanation with external support for its rule structure. Evidence supports an auditable prototype, not industrial, outcome, or user validation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Co-creating responsible AI for public safety: A mixed-method approach toward understanding stakeholder perceptions
abstract: Responsible deployment of AI-assisted video surveillance (A2VS) for public safety requires input from community members and frontline users like security personnel, law enforcement, and small business owners. This study explores their perceptions of A2VS through three in-person focus groups (n = 21) held in June 2025 and a public survey (n = 410) conducted in Charlotte, NC from August to September 2023. Findings show broad support: over 63% of focus group participants expressed positive views, and 85% of survey respondents saw the technology as at least somewhat beneficial. Key concerns included real-time anomaly detection, scalability, and system learning. Random forest analysis of the survey showed education and ethnicity as the top predictors, with white, more educated individuals showing greater support. To synthesize insights, we introduced the Alignment–Tension–Gap (ATG) quadrant map by quantifying cross-group attention and within-group agreement. Alignment topics like notification features were discussed in 100% of groups with 100% agreement. Tension topics like real-time detection appeared in 55% of groups but had only 10% agreement. Emerging gaps like business insights were raised in 25% of groups and showed 70% agreement, pointing to opportunities for innovation. © 2026 The Authors

title: Mathematical and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) investigation of thermo-hydraulic behaviour and cooling performance of an air-cooled server rack under steady information technology (IT) loads
abstract: This study presents mathematical and three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) assessments of an operational 42U air-cooled server rack under five steady information technology (IT) loads from 10 to 20 kW. The principal contribution is not a new CFD algorithm, but a load-dependent integration of rack-scale thermal, hydraulic, turbulence, convective heat-transfer and facility-energy indicators within a single validated framework. The realizable k–ε model reproduced the measured thermal and hydraulic responses with R2 = 0.985–0.993 and a maximum Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) below 3.61%. Increasing IT load raised the maximum rack temperature from 307.6 to 328.8 K and the pressure drop from 35.2 to 68.1 Pa, while rack-average cooling effectiveness decreased from approximately 0.91 to 0.74, corresponding to an 18.7% reduction. Although the inlet condition remained unchanged, the Reynolds number remained approximately 1.92 × 105, whereas the Grashof number increased from 1.64 × 1010 to 3.76 × 1010 and the Richardson number from 0.45 to 1.02, demonstrating a progressive shift from predominantly forced convection toward mixed-convection behaviour. The resulting buoyancy-assisted redistribution promoted upper-rack recirculation, hotspot expansion and increasingly localized turbulence and convective cooling. Numerical energy closure remained above 97% for all cases. In contrast to the deteriorating rack-level thermal performance, facility Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) improved from 1.61 to 1.42 as IT utilization increased. This divergence shows that minimum PUE does not necessarily correspond to the thermally preferable operating state. For the investigated configuration, 15–17.5 kW is therefore identified as a practical compromise operating range between facility energy utilization and rack-level thermal reliability, rather than a universal optimum. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

title: Integrating Frugal Innovation into the Value Stream: An Approach to Continuous Innovation Capability
abstract: Many companies and business units find it challenging to maintain a continuous flow of innovation. Organizational units like competence centers or centers of expertise must consistently offer state-of-the-art solutions. While establishing dedicated innovations organizations such as labs can promote ongoing innovations, this approach requires significant resources, making it impractical for a lot of organizations. An effective alternative is to embed an innovation process within the value stream of an organizational unit, business unit, or the entire company, fostering a culture of inherent innovation. This paper introduces a novel, integrated innovation flow that organizational units can adopt. The approach, implemented in the Volkswagen Group IT Test & Quality Assurance organizational unit and presented as a case study, is built upon frugal innovation principles. A key advantage of this integrated approach is the broad engagement of employees in innovation activities, positively influencing the overall innovation culture and the products and services of the organizational unit—not just those working in dedicated labs. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Which smartphone reuse interventions actually reduce new device production? A stated-preference market-level analysis
abstract: Manufacturing dominates the environmental impact of smartphones, and reuse is widely promoted to reduce production, yet not all reuse interventions achieve this. We integrated stated-preference data from 441 German consumers with a calibrated market model to quantify how four interventions affect smartphone lifetimes and production: new batteries, extended warranties, free data transfer and erasure services, and trade-in programs. The battery intervention produced the largest modelled reduction in manufacturing (32%), followed by warranties (18%). Supply-side interventions increased recirculation but did not reduce production. Combining all four reduced production by 35%, barely exceeding battery alone owing to overlapping segments and rebound effects. Risk perception was the dominant predictor of consumer response. Production reduction in mature reuse markets thus appears gated by demand-side risk mitigation rather than supply-side facilitation. Voluntary interventions alone may be insufficient for sector-level targets and likely require regulatory complements; field-based evidence is needed to confirm these patterns. © 2026 The Authors. title: Framing hotel strategies for demand uncertainty: The asymmetric effects of cancellation policies and F&B incentives
abstract: This study examines how hotels manage demand uncertainty through two contrasting strategies: cancellation policies as loss-framed uncertainty reduction tools and food and beverage incentives as gain-framed coping mechanisms. Drawing on prospect theory, we argue that these approaches generate asymmetric behavioral responses with distinct temporal and revenue implications. The findings show that loss-framed uncertainty reduction initially suppresses demand by discouraging price-sensitive and uncertain customers; however, this negative effect is largely confined to the rooms department and diminishes over time. In contrast, gain-framed coping strategies stimulate in-stay consumption, encouraging guests to engage with additional hotel services and generating positive spillover effects that enhance revenue and profitability across other departments, including in subsequent periods. Overall, uncertainty reduction filters out volatile demand, whereas uncertainty coping enhances perceived value and stimulates consumption. These results underscore the importance of considering both temporal dynamics and cross-departmental effects when designing strategies to manage demand uncertainty. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: From snow to rain: Spatiotemporal transitions and sensitivity patterns in the Amu Darya Basin, Central Asia
abstract: Climate warming is altering precipitation phase with major implications for snow-dependent water resources. However, the nonlinear thresholds and elevation-modulated sensitivity governing snowfall-to-rainfall transitions remain poorly quantified. This study focuses on the Amu Darya Basin, a key water source in Central Asia, and addresses this scientific gap by quantifying transition sensitivity, identifying critical snowfall-fraction thresholds, and projecting future snow–rain dynamics. The analysis spans 1979–2100, using ERA5-Land reanalysis for 1979–2014 as the historical reference and bias-corrected CMIP6 projections for 2015–2100. A threshold-sensitivity-velocity framework is applied to characterize snow-rain phase transition behavior. The framework integrates piecewise regression, clustering analysis, and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to identify dominant drivers. Two robust snowfall-fraction thresholds (0.15 and 0.88) are identified, delineating four precipitation regimes. Projections indicate that snowfall-dominated areas will shrink by 20–25% by 2100, with the maximum snowfall elevation rising by 500–2500 m under SSP585. The transition accelerates after the 2040s, especially in the middle and lower reaches. Sensitivity analysis reveals rapid responses at low (<1000 m) and high (>4000 m) elevations, while mid-elevation zones (1000–4000 m) delay regime shifts by 20–30 years under moderate scenarios. Under the SSP585 scenario, high-elevation regions exhibit a sensitivity rebound. PLS-SEM results show temperature as the dominant suppressive driver of snowfall, with circulation effects acting indirectly. These findings advance understanding of nonlinear precipitation-phase transitions and provide a transferable framework for assessing hydro-climatic vulnerability in other snow-influenced arid and semi-arid regions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Exploring the Role of Artificial Intelligence on Marketing: Key Applications, Industry Transformations, and Emerging Trends Shaping the Future
abstract: AI is most beneficial in marketing, impacting how brands interact with customers. It increases data management capabilities, can create complex algorithms, and expand the information and data sources available. There are differences in AI applications as websites and business models differ. AI is bringing in a paradigm shift for consumers and businesses interacting with brands. Marketers can use AI to do everything from instantaneously delivering content to serve the right consumers over the correct channels in real-time as they evaluate their customer’s needs and paths at each point based on data shared with them from AI algorithms. This will help to ease the customer and boost their chances of purchasing in an eCommerce platform. AI tools can also determine client expectations and evaluate the effectiveness of competitors’ campaigns. Machine learning (ML), allows computers to evaluate and comprehend data independently, providing effective problem-solving skills. Performance and accuracy continuously improve as more data is fed into ML algorithms. Relevant articles on AI in marketing are found and examined in this study using resources including Web of Science, ScienceDirect, ProQuest, Google Scholar., Scopus. This paper highlights the role of AI in marketing, the changes it has brought about and its specialized applications across different industries. This article has made a modest attempt to provide an overview of AI, highlighting its importance and impact in the field of marketing. It examines AI's applications across various marketing domains, identifies key use cases, and explores the transformative changes driven by AI in the sector. Additionally, the article includes a research-based discussion and provides a summary of key insights. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: An exact criterion for a local-time-weighted first-passage identity
abstract: We study first passage for a drifted linear combination of independent Brownian and reflected Brownian motions. We determine exactly when a local-time-weighted expectation equals an explicit exponential expression. This expectation is finite for every positive discount rate. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Extracellular vesicles in neurodegenerative diseases: A new frontier in diagnosis and therapy
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and Huntington's disease are among the progressive disorders of the nervous system that are characterized by the gradual destruction of neurons, the accumulation of misfolded proteins, and the limited effective therapeutic options. In recent years, numerous lines of evidence have emphasized the important role of extracellular vesicles (EVs) in the formation and progression of these diseases. These vesicles are membrane-bound nanoscale structures that are secreted by almost all cell types and play a role in cell-cell communication through the transfer of molecules such as proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids. In neurodegenerative disorders, EVs can facilitate the transport and dissemination of disease-related proteins, including amyloid-β, tau, α-synuclein, mutant huntingtin, SOD1, and TDP-43, thus contributing to the spread of pathological processes in different parts of the nervous system. On the other hand, the ability of these vesicles to cross the blood–brain barrier and reflect molecular changes occurring in the central nervous system makes them valuable candidates for the development of minimally invasive biomarkers. This review reviews the biogenesis, classification, isolation methods, and molecular content of EVs, and analyzes their role in the pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment of the most important neurodegenerative diseases. Also, the importance of EV-associated proteins, RNAs, and lipids as emerging diagnostic biomarkers, as well as the therapeutic potential of natural and engineered vesicles as drug delivery systems and regulators of neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative processes, is discussed. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: CO₂ emission modeling and synthetic fuel energy recovery for hydrogen-integrated sustainable fuel systems
abstract: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions pose a major challenge to sustainable fuel and energy transitions; however, when accurately predicted and reutilized, CO₂ can become a viable feedstock for synthetic and hydrogen-compatible fuels. This study presents an AI-driven framework for predictive CO₂ emission modeling, explainable decision support, and synthetic fuel energy recovery tailored to sustainable fuel infrastructures. A Random Forest Regressor, configured as reported in Section 3 and trained on an agri-food environmental dataset, achieved R2 = 0.9808, RMSE = 33,023.39, and MAPE = 0.1883 on the held-out test partition. LIME and SHAP provide local and global explanations of the model predictions. Beyond forecasting, the framework comprises three coordinated modules: (i) a CO₂ Utilization Energy Management Hub that translates predicted emissions into theoretical synthetic-fuel energy potentials (MWh); (ii) a DiCE-based counterfactual module that identifies model-consistent emission-reduction scenarios; and (iii) a rule-based decision module that maps sensor readings and predicted emissions to IoT-enabled mitigation actions. The case studies illustrate forecasting, counterfactual analysis, and standardized fuel-energy recovery estimates. The resulting architecture links CO₂ analytics with synthetic-fuel and hydrogen-system planning while clearly distinguishing model outputs from plant-level validation. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Commercial or relational cues: how information salience in project titles affects crowdfunding performance
abstract: Scholars have paid considerable attention to factors that could influence crowdfunding performance. However, whether or how the salience of information in project titles may affect crowdfunding performance remains unknown. To address this research gap, we examine 2,064 startups that sought funding on the Kaishiba crowdfunding platform. We find that market validation information in a project title is positively correlated with crowdfunding performance, whereas low psychological distance information is negatively associated with crowdfunding performance. We reveal that the influence of project title information on crowdfunding performance is moderated by the gender of entrepreneurs. Specifically, projects will more (less) likely be funded when entrepreneurs provide information that is congruent (incongruent) with stereotypes associated with their gender. Our findings contribute to the crowdfunding literature by introducing the salience of project title information as a factor that can influence crowdfunding performance while providing practical insights for entrepreneurs, policymakers, and investors. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: A Balanced Scorecard-Based Comparative Analysis of Performance Metrics in Indian Public and Private Sector Banks with Regression Insights on Return on Assets
abstract: The performance of selected Indian private sector and public sector banks is compared in this study. The top three private sector banks (PVSBs) and public sector banks (PSBs) based on total assets were chosen for the study. The authors designed a comprehensive performance measurement framework based on the balanced scorecard approach of Kaplan and Norton. According to the study, the performance of PSBs and PVSBs differs significantly. From the regression analysis, it can be concluded that the selected variables significantly impact return on assets (ROA). This study offers observations for policymakers that might result in more successful strategies for improving the efficiency and performance of the banking sector. The significant antecedents related to banks’ ROI have been identified via research. This research contributes significantly to investigating the antecedents of ROA and provides insights regarding factors influencing the ROA. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Discrete Gauss linking integral representations of correlation trajectories for market stress diagnosis
abstract: Market stress is commonly characterized using contemporaneous correlation levels or other low-dimensional summaries of market dependence, potentially discarding information contained in the ordered evolution of correlation states. We develop a discrete Gauss linking integral (dGLI) representation that retains pairwise contributions between nonadjacent segments of rolling market-correlation trajectories. Our primary representation, dGLI-Reorganization, aligns the same underlying segment pairs across consecutive trajectory windows and measures changes in the organization of their pairwise contribution map.Using S&P 500 constituent data and stress targets constructed from the S&P 500 benchmark index, we evaluate the representation through chronological expanding-window out-of-sample testing and compare it with conventional correlation summaries, trajectory kinematics, market-state transition measures, and persistent-homology features. Relative to the five-variable correlation-state (CorrState) baseline, dGLI-Reorganization increases the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of the random-forest classifier from 0.719 to 0.785 for the Composite stress target, from 0.755 to 0.806 for the 10% drawdown target, and from 0.767 to 0.849 for the 15% drawdown target. The paired improvements in AUC and average precision have 95% confidence intervals entirely above zero for all three targets. MeanCorr and alternative representations nevertheless remain competitive under some target–metric combinations.Across five additional equity markets, Reorganization has a higher pooled AUC than CorrState under market-specific refitting, although the magnitude of the increment varies across markets. Sensitivity analyses show that the magnitude of the increment depends on temporal scale. A separate prospective analysis does not establish a reliable short-horizon drawdown-prediction advantage over CorrState.Overall, the results support aligned-pair dGLI-Reorganization as an incremental representation of dependence-path restructuring for contemporaneous market-stress diagnosis. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: The Role of Smart Technologies in Sustainable Logistics: A Good Practice of Lithuanian Logistics Companies
abstract: The implementation of smart technologies, including advanced robotics, artificial intelligence, autonomous vehicles, blockchain, drones, internet of things, etc., plays a crucial role in fostering sustainability within the field of logistics. These technologies enable cost reduction, enhanced productivity, increased adaptability, improved quality, reduced environmental impact, energy consumption mitigation, carbon emission reduction, and waste minimization. The purpose of the paper is to examine the factors determining the implementation of smart technologies toward sustainability in logistics companies from a theoretical and practical point of view. Systematic literature analysis and case study methods were used. Through analysis of 115 papers from 2011 to 2022, the factors determining the application of smart technologies toward sustainability in logistics companies were identified. Fifth case studies were used to investigate good practice implementing smart technologies. Analysis showed that implementation of smart technologies depends on internal factors, such as the size of the logistics company, business growth potential, organizational structure, culture, and complexity of internal processes. External factors such as the quality and price of smart technologies in market, user-friendliness, complexity, popularity and security, environmental competitiveness, legal regulation, availability and support of external expertise and services, and others also have a significant influence. Case analysis showed that business technology platforms were used, big data analysis and artificial intelligence solutions were actively applied, investments were made in warehouse technologies, and various robotic solutions were used. By managing information and data flows, companies not only create a better network between logistics companies, but also get an effective instrument that allows timely monitoring and control of all-important processes in the supply chain. Quick identification of problems and their solution allows us to avoid losses, reduce service costs, and increase customer satisfaction. At the same time, it indirectly contributes to reducing the negative impact on the environment. Despite the obvious benefits of smart technologies, their implementation is associated with challenges, such as high implementation costs, limited financial resources of companies, lack of qualified employees, employee resistance to digitization. To ensure the implementation of smart technologies in logistics companies toward sustainability, it is important to identify the factors hindering their application and to eliminate them. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Enhanced Document Clustering Using Residue Modulo Partitioner in Map-Reduce Framework
abstract: Information Retrieval (IR) is a domain within computer science focused on the efficient retrieval of text documents based on user queries containing specific keywords. The demand for automated IR systems has grown significantly to meet business requirements based on user inquiries. Recent techniques have proposed various IR frameworks utilizing different data mining algorithms, as well as novel map and reduce approaches, while leveraging default partitioners. However, none of these methods have effectively utilized custom partitioners. The primary goal of this paper is to implement a custom partitioner, Residue Modulo-K, where K denotes the number of reducers used in the process. Map Reduce framework utilizing proposed custom partitioner to the default partitioner is executed and the results were tabulated. Based on the experimental analysis the proposed custom partitioner outperformed the default one. The performance metrics utilized for this study are job execution time, data transfer time, CPU utilization, and F-score. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Assessing drone freight demand in intercity mountainous corridors: A discrete choice modeling approach with capacity-constrained simulations
abstract: The low-altitude economy, as an innovative economic model utilizing low-altitude airspace resources, is reshaping traditional transportation systems through applications like drone logistics, demonstrating pronounced advantages in complex terrains. While existing research predominantly focuses on macro-level airspace deployment, meso-level demand analysis, and micro-level route optimization of drones in passenger transportation, the meso-level demand analysis lacks consideration of drone capacity constraints and the impact of drone allocation across different modes and regions on service levels and traffic volume in freight transportation. This study adapts established discrete choice models to a novel and complex context by explicitly integrating strict capacity constraints into the demand simulation—an aspect largely overlooked in existing applications. Based on stated preference data from four typical mountainous intercity freight corridors in Fujian Province, China, market shares of pure-drone, pure-road, and drone-road intermodal modes are simulated under varying service attributes. Key findings reveal: (1) Shippers across different corridors exhibit significant variations in their preference for drone modes, which correlate with cargo attributes and drone capacity; (2) Competitiveness enhancement requires prioritizing capacity reallocation to corridors with higher cargo unit value and total cargo value (such as the Fuqing-Fuzhou corridor) and reducing waiting time. In particular, the value of cargo transported by drones (including pure-drone and drone-road intermodal modes) increases from 7.87 million Chinese Yuan in the current scenario to 44.57 million Chinese Yuan in the multi-factor optimization scenario (capacity reallocation + waiting time reduction + freight subsidies). This study theoretically offers a quantitative method to understand the relationship between drone service levels and modal share under capacity constraints, and practically provides decision-making support for developing strategies to enhance the competitiveness of drone transportation in various freight corridor scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Highly inclusive teachers’ practices in responding to all students’ learning characteristics
abstract: Background: Although inclusive education places strong emphasis on addressing all students’ strengths and needs, the understanding of student diversity in its broadest sense remains limited. Studies exploring how inclusion is implemented tend to focus on specific groups of learners (e.g., students with SEN or those from socio-culturally disadvantaged backgrounds). However, this methodological shortcut has been repeatedly highlighted in review studies as a limitation that distorts the findings of research on inclusive education for all. To successfully address the learning characteristics of all students in heterogeneous classrooms, teachers must use inclusive practices. Aims: The aim of this research was to explore how the practices of highly inclusive teachers address all students’ learning characteristics, enabling them to learn successfully in a heterogeneous classroom. Sample: The study involved six teachers, forty-two students, and two teaching assistants. Methods: Triangulation of hundreds of hours of ethnographic observation, contextualised through various types of interviews and complemented by products written by students, allowed us to identify diverse types of student learning characteristics and teachers’ inclusive practices. Results: Our findings indicate that teachers' inclusive practices aimed at supporting student engagement, as well as determining and facilitating students' learning progress, were among the most extensively employed and addressed a wide spectrum of students’ learning characteristics. Conclusions: The study unravels the complexity of highly inclusive teachers’ practices and proposes several implications for inclusive education. © 2026 The Authors

title: Global stochastic maximum principle of regime-switching systems with time-varying delay under non-convex control domains
abstract: This paper establishes a global stochastic maximum principle for regime-switching systems with time-varying delays under non-convex control domains. The proposed approach relies on the spike variation and duality methods. One contribution of this paper is the establishment of the well-posedness of anticipated backward stochastic differential equations featuring both time-varying delays and regime-switching, which arise as the first- and the second-order adjoint equations required to handle the non-convexity of the control domain. Additionally, the classical duality relation is extended to accommodate the time-varying delay. Finally, a linear–quadratic problem is presented as an example to demonstrate the applicability of the theoretical results. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: The joint effects of organisational learning and CEO cognition on cross-border acquisition pace
abstract: Organisational learning is a double-edged sword because it is contextual and subject to interpretation by the top managers. Top managers’ cognitions influence how they interpret and process organisational learning, and how they deploy resources. Drawing on organisational learning and upper-echelon theories, we argue for the joint, complementary effects of a firm’s cross-border acquisition (CBA) experience and the chief executive officer’s (CEO) cognitive orientation, measured by their international experience and tenure at the firm, on the pace of CBAs. The results from analyses of an unbalanced panel of 1583 observations across 369 CBAs from 205 Indian MNEs support our hypothesis. Interestingly, we find negative effects of the firm’s CBA experience and mixed effects of the CEO’s cognitions. However, the joint effect is positive and stronger, as hypothesised. We mainly contribute to the CBA literature by demonstrating the role of ‘experience cognition complementarity’ on the CBA pace. © 2026 The Authors.
