title: Improving Environmental Quality in the Mediterranean: The Impact of Financialization, Human Capital, and Energy Efficiency
abstract: Context/Purpose: Environmental quality is one of the cardinal goals of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) of the United Nations. However, prior research has overlooked the necessity of energy efficiency, knowledge economy, and financial resources in achieving environmental quality. Thus, by capturing the contributions of financialization measured in terms of financial development, human capital in terms of returns on education, and energy efficiency in evaluating the environmental quality impact in the Mediterranean, this study offers a fresh perspective. The Mediterranean area is experiencing significant stability problems as a result of its higher rate of warming than the world’s average. Methods: Depending on the availability of data, the study makes use of a panel data covering ten Mediterranean countries between 1990 and 2018 on five variables, namely, ecological footprint, financial development, human capital, energy efficiency and economic growth. The sources of the data include Global Footprint Network (GFN), International Monetary Fund (IMF), Penn World Table (PWT), and World Development Indicators (WDI), respectively. The research utilizes the Cross-Sectional Autoregressive Distributed Lag (CS-ARDL) model. Results: The results showed that financial development and economic growth exert a decreasing impact on environmental quality by incrasing ecological footprint, while human capital and energy efficiency enhance environmental quality in the Mediterranean region by decreasing ecological footprint. Interpretation: The results imply that, in spite of their advantages, financialization and economic expansion contribute to environmental deterioration in the region. This is because growing economies frequently need more raw materials, which deepens extraction and the depletion of natural resources. Furthermore, increased production and consumption usually lead to increased waste and pollution, which degrades the quality of the air, water, and land. Financialization can also push companies to put short-term earnings ahead of long-term sustainability, which can result in environmentally harmful business practices. Conclusion: The findings suggest that financialization, human capital, and energy efficiency are significant factors that influence environmental quality in the Mediterranean region and ought to be taken into consideration when formulating policy decisions. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Hallucinations in organization-backed AI advisors: Evidence about skepticism, verification, and reliance in goal-directed use
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) systems are increasingly used by organizations to deliver information to consumers, patients, students, employees, and citizens. These systems can hallucinate, producing plausible but inaccurate responses. A central question for AI-advised decisions is therefore not only whether users rely on inaccurate information, but whether they recognize that a response may require verification. To answer this question, we review emerging empirical evidence relevant to hallucination detection in goal-directed interactions, with a focus on organization-backed AI advisors. We distinguish three constructs that existing studies often conflate: whether users are skeptical of information presented, whether they verify it (distinguishing attempted from successful verification), and whether the result of verification affects reliance on the information. Across studies examining product search, medical decision-making, content generation, and chatbot-assisted tasks, several patterns emerge. Nearly all studies measure reliance, while variables such as user skepticism and verification of the information are more often targeted by an intervention than measured directly. The cues used to prompt scrutiny of the AI response are predominantly related to the AI output, such as source citations. Whereas general warnings about the risk of hallucinations are among the most deployable interventions for organizations, they show the weakest and most mixed effects in the studies reviewed. More targeted cues about where AI systems tend to fail appear promising, however evidence remains limited. Although the existing literature posits that users may be more likely to scrutinize responses related to particular areas of content, no studies varied the content category, leaving this question open for further research. In future research, measuring skepticism and verification separately from reliance may clarify what current evidence shows, what it only implies, and which questions require further exploration. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Assessing Technological Barriers of Blockchain Adoption in the Energy Sector Using AHP for Group Decision-Making
abstract: After its implementation in cryptocurrencies, blockchain, a Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT), has attracted the attention of researchers in various sectors, while its potential use cases have been explored in a number of fields. As far as the energy sector is concerned, blockchain could enable decentralised electricity and carbon trading, effective energy management of complex systems with high penetration of renewables, coordination of energy storage units and electric vehicle charging, and secure data storage of energy-related data generated by metering infrastructure, among other applications. However, several technical issues hinder the wide-spread adoption of DLT in the energy field, such as scalability and speed constraints, poor performance, as well as security threats. In this paper, the most prominent technological barriers of blockchain adoption in energy services are recognised and assessed. The barriers are ranked, using a Multicriteria Decision Analysis method, the Analytical Hierarchy Process for Group Decision-Making. The findings of the research provide useful insight in the EU funded project InEExS (Innovative Energy (Efficiency) Service Models for Sector Integration via Blockchain), which is going to apply blockchain technology in specific energy-related business cases. The final ranked list of technical constraints could be a useful guide for any market actors interested in overcoming barriers to integrate blockchain technology in energy applications. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Pharmaceutical Import Forecasting for Supply-Chain Decision Support: A Comparative Evaluation of Fuzzy, Statistical, and Machine-Learning Models
abstract: Purpose: Pharmaceutical supply-chain planning in import-dependent economies is sensitive to macroeconomic shocks, currency volatility, and global supply disruptions. This study evaluates a Dynamic Fuzzy Time Series (DFTS) candidate together with statistical and machine-learning benchmarks for annual pharmaceutical-import forecasting. Methods: Azerbaijan’s annual pharmaceutical-import observations for 2012–2023 are used for model development; the 2024 observation (USD 507.50 million) is reserved as an untouched external holdout. Model comparison uses a common rolling-origin/expanding-window protocol beginning with a 2012–2017 initial training window. RMSE is pre-specified as the primary loss, with MAE and sMAPE as complementary measures. The DFTS recency parameter rho is selected from {0.70, 0.80, 0.90, 1.00}, and an optional log-space long-term blending weight alpha is selected from {0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00}, using pre-2024 rolling-origin RMSE only. Results: Among the reproduced benchmarks, the naive forecast achieved the lowest rolling-origin RMSE (95.84 million USD). The best DFTS setting was rho = 0.70 with RMSE = 120.17 million USD; adding the long-term log-trend component did not reduce RMSE, so the selected alpha was 0 and the hybrid candidate collapsed to the DFTS component. Its frozen 2024 forecast was USD 591.91 million, corresponding to a 16.63% absolute percentage error, compared with 10.51% for the naive benchmark. Conclusion: The revised evidence does not support a claim that the hybrid/DFTS candidate outperforms simple benchmarks on this short annual series. Its value is instead methodological and scenario-oriented: the framework provides a transparent shock-aware evaluation structure, while the empirical results show the importance of benchmark discipline, leakage-free validation, and cautious operational interpretation. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Energy Efficiency Implementation: Driver–Barrier Analysis of the Macedonian Legislation
abstract: As one of the energy transition pillars, energy efficiency (EE) holds significant untapped potential, not only via facilitating responsible energy use, but concomitantly, for achieving climate targets and environmental protection obligations. Unfortunately, in the Western Balkan countries, the game-changing power of EE is particularly underestimated due to the discrepancy between the by-instalments harmonization with the acquis communautaire of the corresponding country-specific legislation, on one side, and its actual implementation lagging behind, on the other. Though, in the latest Energy Community (EnC) Annual Implementation Report (EnC 2022), EnC notes Macedonian average annual progress of 67% in terms of EE, significant differences across sectors are evident. The lowest progress is achieved in buildings (52%) and in heating and cooling (54%), whereby the latter, is mainly because only the Macedonian capitol has a developed district heating system, while the majority of households across country use inefficient electrical heating appliances or firing wood. The European Commission (EC) annual accession progress report (EC 2022, Ch. 15) is significantly stricter in assessing country progress as ‘limited’. Considering the above, this study focuses on identifying and quantifying barriers and drivers relevant for implementing EE legislation in Macedonia (As of Feb 2019, the official name of R. Macedonia, has been changed to R. North Macedonia). Though the Law on Energy Efficiency (aligned with the acquis) is in force since 2020, its implementation—as per EC (2022), as well as the EnC (2022) is at a very early stage, while adoption of related by-laws is still pending. Numerous barriers and obstacles—e.g. institutional weakness at national and local level, lack of incentives and/or subsidies among business community, lack of cooperation between stakeholders in promoting innovative solutions, state intervention during crisis, bad governance and corruption, protectionism, etc.—contribute to this. Weighted driver-barrier analysis (DBA) is utilized to categorize and prioritize identified drivers and barriers in accordance to the adopted EE implementation categories—targets/policy measures, buildings, financing, product labelling, heating/cooling, industry—Further, possibilities for transforming certain barriers into drivers, based on country-specific aspects are elaborated and examined. The obtained results are categorized to enable effective assistance for decision-makers in fostering and improved implementation of the Macedonian EE legislation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Analyzing the Contributions of Artificial Intelligence to Enhancing Business Intelligence Capabilities Within E-Commerce Platforms
abstract: This research investigates the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in augmenting Business Intelligence (BI) capabilities within e-commerce platforms. AI-driven BI systems have transformed traditional BI methodologies through automation of data processing, provision of real-time insights, and enhancement of decision-making processes. The study emphasizes the influence of AI technologies, including machine learning (ML), natural language processing (NLP), and predictive analytics, on critical e-commerce functions such as demand forecasting, customer segmentation, inventory management, and dynamic pricing. Through secondary data analysis and case studies from prominent e-commerce platforms like Amazon and Alibaba, the research illustrates the substantial business value created by AI-powered BI systems. Notable improvements include enhanced accuracy in sales predictions, minimized stockouts, and improved operational efficiency. Additionally, AI’s capacity to personalize customer experiences through predictive analytics has led to increased customer retention and conversion rates. The study finds AI integrated platform consistently outperforms traditional business approach relating to sales growth, customer satisfaction, and cost reduction. Direction for future research include exploring AI ethics, data privacy emerging technologies such as blockchain and IoT. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Stationary distribution and extinction of a stochastic HIV infection model including quiescent cells
abstract: In this paper, we study a stochastic within-host HIV infection model including quiescent cells. With the aid of suitably constructed stochastic Lyapunov functions, we obtain sufficient conditions for the model to admit an ergodic stationary distribution. Additionally, we provide sufficient conditions for the extinction of the disease. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Consumer complaints as regulatory signals: Evidence from water services in Metropolitan Lima
abstract: In regulated monopoly services, consumers lack effective exit options, making complaint systems a central mechanism for expressing dissatisfaction and generating regulatory information about service performance. However, complaint rates are not direct or unbiased indicators of service failures, as the decision to complain involves informational, procedural, and behavioral costs, reflecting both service problems and heterogeneous access barriers. Because administrative data record filed complaints rather than adjudicated outcomes, complaint rates are interpreted as noisy signals of perceived billing anomalies rather than direct measures of confirmed service failures, firm misconduct, or regulatory noncompliance. This paper reinterprets billing-related complaints as endogenous regulatory signals in essential public services. We develop a microeconomic framework in which households decide whether to complain when facing an atypical bill under uncertainty about its origin—whether it reflects a firm billing error or household-specific factors. The model’s predictions are tested using sector-month administrative data from Sedapal, the public water utility serving Metropolitan Lima (Peru), covering January 2022–June 2023. We estimate a dynamic panel model (System GMM) to identify persistence in complaint behavior and its response to unanticipated tariff shocks. We find strong persistence in complaint rates and a significant response to unexpected tariff increases. These patterns suggest structural frictions in service provision or communication and a critical role for tariff transparency. Overall, the results imply that regulators should strengthen tariff communication and incorporate complaint data into monitoring systems as screening and triage indicators, rather than as mechanical evidence of confirmed billing errors or firm misconduct. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Deception and detection: The impact of artificial intelligence (AI)-based resume screening on entry-level job seekers’ deceptive behaviors
abstract: Recognizing the unintended consequences of artificial intelligence (AI) in resume screening, this research investigated whether AI-based resume screening increases deceptive behaviors among entry-level job seekers. Across four experiments involving common forms of resume deception, we demonstrated that AI is perceived as less effective at detecting deception, resulting in increased deceptive behaviors, compared with human resume screening. We also identified two theoretically and practically relevant interventions—AI learning-capability and human input—that mitigate AI’s backfire effects on job seekers’ unethical behaviors. These interventions significantly improved AI’s perceived detectability, making AI-based resume screening more effective at discouraging deceptive intentions and experience inflation in resume reporting. Our findings suggest that organizations should consider the negative outcomes of AI-based resume screening, balance AI’s efficiency with human insight and/or improve AI’s ability through learning-capability, ultimately enhancing hiring outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Voluntary sustainability standards and industrial fisheries: Roles of friend of the sea certification on occupational safety and working conditions in Nigeria, Gulf of Guinea
abstract: Fishing, especially within industrial sectors, is widely recognized as one of the most dangerous occupations in the world, as fishers are exposed to adverse physical and environmental risks. While legal frameworks in Nigeria provide occupational safety and labor protections for industrial fishers, inconsistencies in enforcement and compliance persist. Voluntary sustainability standards (VSS) have been promoted as market-based mechanisms to reduce risks, increase safety compliance, and improve working conditions. Despite their relevance, evidence of their impacts on industrial fisheries remains unclear. This study examines the effects of the Friend of the Sea (FOS) certification program on the occupational safety and working conditions of industrial fishers in Nigeria's Gulf of Guinea, Atlantic Ocean. A mixed methods approach was employed, integrating quantitative surveys with semi-structured interviews with key informant to facilitate triangulation among participants recruited from FOS-certified and Business as Usual (BAU) fishing companies. Bivariate analyses revealed that FOS-certified fishers were significantly more likely to have adequate safety equipment (98.0% vs. 74.8%), access to health personnel and emergency services (100% vs. 17.4%), and training opportunities (98.5% vs. 46.8%). Multivariate logistic regression confirmed these associations such that absence of safety equipment was associated with a 0.364 decrease in the probability of FOS certification; no injury history with a 0.291 increase; no exposure to unsafe conditions with a 0.400 increase; and lack of training access with a 0.535 decrease (all p ' 0.001). These findings suggest that, despite statutory legal protections in Nigeria, participation of fishing companies in the FOS certification programme may enhance the implementation of safety standards and improve occupational health outcomes among industrial fishers. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Farmers’ perceptions of conflict-prone neighborhoods – Insights from a choice experiment
abstract: Recent research documents the growing frequency of land-use conflicts in rural areas. As conflicts between farmers and other stakeholders intensify while farmland resources continue to decline, spatial planning and the legal protection of agricultural land have become key policy priorities. This makes understanding farmers’ preferences regarding neighboring land uses particularly important. However, quantitative evidence remains limited. To address this gap, we used a discrete choice experiment to examine farmers’ perceptions of potentially conflict-generating neighboring land uses in a sample of 960 farmers from the Warmińsko-Mazurskie voivodeship, Poland. The results show that residential and business activities, especially when conducted at a large scale, are perceived as the most conflict-generating types of neighboring land uses. However, farmers’ perceptions vary across farm characteristics and locations. Residential neighborhoods are perceived as particularly conflict-generating by livestock farmers and farmers in highly urbanized municipalities, while patterns by farm size and nature-protection status are less consistent. © 2026 The Authors

title: Design, dynamic analysis, and optimization of a hybrid nuclear-storage power system for mobile applications
abstract: With the rapid advancement of heat pipe-cooled reactor (HPR) technology, the integration of mobile nuclear power with energy storage offers a promising solution for energy supply in remote and off-grid scenarios. However, existing research predominantly focuses on stationary systems, lacking comprehensive investigation into the dynamic coupling of HPRs and hybrid storage in mobile environments. To address this gap, this paper proposes a novel hybrid nuclear-storage power system (HNSPS) integrating an HPR with a lithium-ion battery and supercapacitor for mobile applications. A high-fidelity system model is developed in MATLAB/Simulink, incorporating a nuclear power generation system, hybrid energy storage, and control models. A fully active parallel topology is employed for the storage subsystem, utilizing lithium-ion batteries for baseload and supercapacitors for transient power fluctuation mitigation. Simulation results demonstrate robust synergistic operation, characterized by excellent dynamic response and energy management performance. Parameter optimization indicates that the lithium battery rated voltage (determined by series configuration) should balance cycle life and manufacturing cost, while its response time should be extended for high-frequency operation and shortened for high-power-demand scenarios. For the supercapacitor, an initial voltage of 100–200 V and a series number of approximately 200 are recommended to balance transient power capability, safety, and cost. This work validates the feasibility and reliability of the proposed HNSPS for mobile scenarios, providing a theoretical reference for the deployment of mobile nuclear energy applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Modularization Barriers and Barrier Breakers in Capital Projects
abstract: Modularization is an execution strategy that transfers work from the project site to an offsite location for improved project performance. It is expected to have significant growth and wide acceptance, leading to enhanced productivity and competitiveness of capital projects. However, many practitioners in capital projects are still unfamiliar with modularization and resist changing from a traditional approach. The implementations have been limited to lower levels of modularization (e.g., prefabs or pipe racks) and lower extents of modularization. Although previous research has investigated barriers to modular/offsite construction in residential and commercial sectors, there is a lack of studies identifying barriers specific to capital projects (including but not limited to petrochemical plants, manufacturing plants, power generation facilities, and mining operations). Thus, this study focuses on identifying barriers to modularization implementation and proposing solutions to break these barriers in capital projects. First, 33 barriers were identified through iterative sessions with the Construction Industry Institute (CII) Research Team (RT-396), a panel of 15 subject matter experts averaging more than 15 years of modularization experience and 28 executed modular studies/projects. Subsequently, a survey based on these barriers was distributed to CII member companies, gathering data from experts affiliated with globally leading owner and contractor organizations, who possess an average of 23 years of industry experience and 11 years of specific modular expertise. The results identified nine top-rated barriers: (1) requirement of early scope/design freeze; (2) unavailability of vendor data; (3) noncompelling business cases; (4) exclusion of modularization from initial design; (5) incompatible project delivery methods; (6) owner reluctance; (7) lack of final drivers; (8) insufficient early fabricator involvement; and (9) lack of project standardization. These findings contribute to the management-in-engineering body of knowledge by showing that modularization adoption in capital projects is constrained primarily by front-end managerial and organizational conditions rather than by technical concerns alone. The comparative analyses and expert-derived specific "Barrier Breakers"strategic solutions developed to overcome each of these nine top-ranked barriers provide actionable guidance for diverse practitioners regarding early decision making, project delivery alignment, and supply-chain integration. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Environmental performance feedback and green innovation: The moderating role of organizational slack
abstract: Prior research has highlighted a variety of external and internal drivers of green innovation (GI), yet much less is known about how firms interpret their own environmental performance and adjust GI strategies accordingly. Drawing on the behavioral theory of the firm, this study investigates how environmental performance feedback is associated with firms’ GI decisions. Using panel data from Chinese publicly listed firms, the results reveal a U-shaped relationship between performance below aspirations and GI, and an inverted U-shaped relationship when performance exceeds aspirations. Organizational slack weakens both patterns, reducing firms’ responsiveness to both negative and positive environmental performance feedback. These findings provide new insight into how firms adapt their GI strategies in response to environmental performance feedback signals. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Earthen Building – Contribution of RILEM Technical Committees for Terminology
abstract: Earth-based construction involves diverse techniques (e.g. rammed earth, cob, adobe, compressed earth blocks) and regional practices. Without common terminology, misunderstandings arise between designers, engineers, contractors, and regulators. A shared language ensures that experimental results and case studies are comparable globally, accelerating innovation and adoption. This paper reviews existing glossaries and multilingual term lists developed by RILEM, ICOMOS, PROTERRA, TerraBrasil, business companies, researchers and other organisations. It proposes initial definitions for key terms to foster consistency in research, professional practice, and dissemination. The ultimate goal is to establish a standardised terminology framework that supports clarity and promotes wider adoption of earthen building techniques. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Entropy as a diagnostic for time-related constraints on circular transition: Evidence from plastic waste management in the OECD–EU countries
abstract: This study examines time-related constraints on circularity by applying Shannon entropy to measure distributional dispersion across end-of-life fates in plastic waste management. Using OECD data for 1990–2018, end-of-life shares for recycling, incineration, landfill, mismanaged, and littered waste are combined with entropy to assess structural change over time. Entropy makes that structural shift visible and comparable across time. During the early 1990s, plastic waste management was highly predictable due to landfill dominance. From the mid-2010s onward, entropy stabilized at a high level despite continued growth in recycling. That plateau is consistent with persistent dispersion across competing end-of-life routes rather than convergence toward recycling dominance. © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier B.V. title: Tell me about yourself and I might recommend you: a motivation-based explanation of crowdlending investors’ customer citizenship behavior☆
abstract: Competition among entrepreneurial funding platforms has made it more important than ever to attract and retain investors to ensure the sustainability of entrepreneurial ecosystems. In this context, investor recommendations are a key mechanism to generate trust in crowdlending platforms. This paper investigates the existence of necessary and sufficient conditions that explain investor recommendations of crowdlending platforms and explores how the motivations behind investor behavior are linked to investor recommendations of these platforms. Necessary condition analysis (NCA) and qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) were performed using data on 83 investors. Of the intrinsic/self-oriented motivations considered in the analysis, only satisfaction emerged as an individual in-degree necessary condition from the NCA. The analysis also confirmed the synergistic effects of intrinsic/self-oriented and extrinsic/other-oriented motivations as sufficient conditions for explaining investor behavior. Nonetheless, such behavior can still be explained exclusively by intrinsic/self-oriented conditions. The study enriches the knowledge of how investor motivations explain the sustainability of platforms that provide alternative forms of financing for entrepreneurs. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Institutionalization in Consumption Meets Improvisation: A Case Exemplar Approach
abstract: Consumption does not arise from a single cause (e.g., a campaign), but rather from an interplay of multiple internal and external drivers, including psychological, social, cultural, affective, and cognitive factors. These factors are embedded in consumers’ personalities, immediate surroundings, and situational contexts. Their relationship makes consumers’ lives and decision-making a complex matter that even the most comprehensive marketing guidance can only partially anticipate. Although firms provide product guidance and brand narratives to help consumers navigate this complexity, it is during the usage episode that consumers improvise their practices. While improvisation is typical in consumption episodes, it is usually inadequately acknowledged. Using an interpretive paradigm, the paper employs case studies to elucidate how consumption practices lead to improvisations. We examine how consumer-led improvisation thrives outside the institutionalized consumption norms. We note that consumers oscillate between following and bending institutional guidance, and the previously untapped “value pockets” become available. A conceptual framework is proposed to illustrate the interconnectedness of institutionalized and improvised consumption. Thus, the framework sheds light on their mechanisms and outcomes. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Beyond tool adoption: designing cognitive scaffolds in individual preparation to support critical thinking in generative AI integrated learning
abstract: The integration of GenAI into higher education risks promoting passive information acceptance over critical thinking (CT), a challenge that is acutely felt in ill-structured problem-solving contexts such as engineering design. While cognitive scaffolds are recognized as a solution, limited research provides process-oriented evidence on how they mediate student engagement with GenAI. Currently, typical GenAI integration often leads to cognitive offloading where students bypass critical evaluation. To counter this automation bias, this study introduced a novel instructional framework that integrated the Preparation for Future Collaboration (PFC) paradigm with the Target-Criteria-Source-Analogy (TCSA) cognitive strategy to structure GenAI-supported learning. By analyzing the critical thinking patterns of 77 engineering undergraduates across high-, medium-, and low-performing groups, Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA) identified distinct cognitive co-occurrence patterns across GenAI-supported preparation and subsequent AI-free collaboration. High-performing students showed stronger connections among Analysis, Evaluation, and Self-regulation, a pattern we interpretively describe as a “Triangulation Loop,” whereas low-performing students showed stronger connections between Interpretation and Analysis, described as a “Descriptive Loop.” The latter pattern was consistent with greater reliance on AI-generated information. Within the integrated PFC-TCSA instructional design, these observed patterns were characterized by stronger evaluative and self-regulatory co-occurrences, providing practical implications for designing human–AI collaboration. title: Climate-Informed Nonstationary Multihazard Design Load Characterization for Performance-Based Evaluation of Coastal Structures
abstract: Current structural design guidelines face increasing challenges from interacting natural hazards in coastal regions. Climate-driven shifts in hazard intensity, frequency, and interaction add further complexity. Traditional multihazard design approaches often neglect hazard nonstationarity or treat hazards independently, resulting in inaccurate structural demands. This paper presents a probabilistic framework for simulating future multihazard scenarios under changing climate conditions. The nonstationary trends in hazard intensities and frequencies are characterized by probability distributions and regression models with time- and climate-informed parameters, respectively. Interhazard dependence is captured using multivariate copulas on the detrended hazard intensities. The framework supports two approaches: historical data-driven (suitable for regions with sufficient observations) and hybrid simulation-based (leveraging physics-based models to supplement limited observations). The framework's application is demonstrated on coastal wind and flood hazards for San Francisco (historical data-driven) and Miami (hybrid simulation-based), producing joint hazard curves (wind speed versus water level at a target return period) under multiple shared socioeconomic pathway scenarios through 2100. The resulting joint hazard curves provide a risk-consistent basis to select wind-flood intensity pairs for adaptive performance-based evaluation of coastal structures under future climate conditions. At the 100-year return period, ASCE 7 wind speeds are lower by about 21% and 17% in 2050 and 2100 for San Francisco, respectively, and by 6% and 9% for Miami, reinforcing the need to assess structural performance over the full joint hazard curve to capture compound loading scenarios and preserve reliability under nonstationary conditions. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Detection of spatial change boundaries in linear regression models
abstract: Detecting spatial change boundaries that separate regions with different regression relationships is important for the analysis of spatially heterogeneous data. We develop three residual-based procedures for detecting spatial change boundaries in linear regression models: a spatial path scanning procedure, a local block discrepancy procedure, and an integrated strip scanning procedure. The first and third procedures apply cumulative sum (CUSUM) statistics to one-dimensional sequences induced by spatial orderings, whereas the second procedure compares residual averages over neighboring local blocks. The asymptotic properties of the proposed procedures are established under a regular-lattice framework, while irregularly sampled designs are treated as computational extensions and evaluated through simulation. Simulation studies under different boundary configurations, sampling designs, and spatial dependence structures reveal complementary strengths and limitations of the proposed procedures in detecting and localizing spatial change boundaries. Comparisons with residual-based Point Wombling and the spatially clustered coefficient regression method based on a minimum spanning tree (SCC-MST) further illustrate the relative strengths and limitations of the proposed procedures. A Boston Housing application provides a real-data illustration of the spatial boundary patterns produced by the proposed methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Behavioral nudges and feedback lead to improved pre-primary teacher practices in Kenya
abstract: Many national pre-primary curricula call for classroom practices that support children’s autonomy and teacher-child dialogue, but these practices are observed inconsistently. Teachers in low-resource settings often lack affordable, scalable support and professional development to adopt these practices. This four-month, blinded, incomplete factorial randomized controlled trial evaluated whether low-cost, tech-enabled feedback and behavioral nudges can improve pre-primary teachers’ adoption of seven target practices in Mombasa, Kenya. Teachers (n= 129) were randomized into one of three intervention arms: (1) business as usual (control); (2) observation feedback and weekly WhatsApp nudges (feedback and nudge); or (3) observation feedback, weekly WhatsApp nudges, and two in-person meetings facilitated by early childhood trainers (feedback and nudge + cluster). The primary outcome was the number of target practices observed at endline, adjusting for baseline. Relative to control, teachers in the feedback and nudge arm implemented 0.92 additional practices (d = 0.45), and those in the feedback and nudge + cluster arm 0.94 (d = 0.45). The similar effects across arms suggest no statistically detectable incremental benefit of adding cluster meetings in this sample; the design does not permit conclusions about cluster meetings as a standalone component. Seventy-five percent of teachers reported that the nudges were helpful in improving their understanding of target practices and that they would recommend them to fellow teachers. Attrition was under 1%. Embedding feedback and behavioral nudges within existing early childhood quality assurance and professional development systems may therefore offer a scalable approach to strengthening classroom practice in low- and middle-income contexts. title: Commons without borders: How entrepreneurs can engage local actors into collective action for the governance of supra-local common-pool resources
abstract: Based on 41 interviews across three UK-based commons enterprises, this study addresses one of the most pressing challenges of our time: encouraging local actors to contribute to the sustainable governance of supra-local common-pool resources (CPRs)—shared resources whose use and impacts extend beyond community boundaries. While existing research has focused on locally bound natural CPRs, we lack understanding of how entrepreneurial ventures can mobilize the members of local communities to govern resources that span multiple jurisdictions. Our findings reveal a two-step process through which entrepreneurs first embed their commons enterprises in the local community, using asset locks and diversified engagement strategies to involve citizens, local businesses, and public authorities. Building on this embedding, three commoning practices emerge: collective learning about the CPR, collective action and capacity building for CPR stewardship, and collective institutionalization of CPR governance. Around these practices, a community of commoners emerges that is nested within the local community and increasingly sustains collective action independently of the entrepreneur. These practices anchor the supra-local CPR within the local community through three mechanisms: resource proximization, local conditionality, and bonding as a selective incentive, thereby overcoming the collective action barriers arising from lacking resource proximity and perceived responsibility. Our study contributes to research at the intersection of entrepreneurship and the commons by demonstrating the strategic role of common property regimes, shifting attention from the resource to the commoning practices and communities that form around it, and specifying the mechanisms that enable local collective action for supra-local CPR governance. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Information technology as a critical success factor for halal logistics: A bibliometric and innovation systems perspective
abstract: Technology has influenced all aspects of human life, and the Halal industry, especially Halal logistics, is not an exception. This study aims to examine the role of Information Technology as a critical success factor in Halal logistics and its contribution to fostering innovation and value creation from 2010 to 2024 by providing a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of existing research. A total of 60 articles were systematically collected from Scopus and Google Scholar databases, with 57 articles retained after screening. Data obtained were analysed utilizing Microsoft Excel for descriptive analysis and VoSViewer for visualization of research trends, citation patterns, and keyword networks. Thus, the paper represents new development as scholars increasingly investigate critical success factors of Halal logistics by outlining enablers and barriers of information technology adoption in Halal logistics, supported by contemporary supply chain theories. The findings reveal that Information Technology enhances Halal logistics performance through multiple dimensions, particularly by fostering innovation and creativity, improving service quality, strengthening customer satisfaction, and enabling traceability and transparency systems. However, barriers such as limited digital understanding, high implementation costs, and inadequate infrastructure remain significant constraints to adoption. In conclusion, this study reveals the strategic importance of Information Technology in advancing Halal logistics performance and competitiveness. The results provide valuable insights for Halal Logistics Service Providers (HLSP), policymakers, and academicians to enhance service improvement, integration, and niche identification. Furthermore, the study contributes to the advancement of the Halal logistics research cluster by mapping current trends and identifying future research directions. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Net Zero, Full Strategy: Integrating Environmental Goals with Business Strategy as Growth Engines
abstract: Sustainability is not optional for businesses anymore, considering the growing constraints and challenges posed by climate change, environmental degradation, and stakeholder demands. In order to make environmental stewardship a driver of innovation, resilience, and competitive advantage, this chapter discusses how environmental goals can be effectively incorporated into business strategy. The chapter charts the evolution of business cases for sustainability, beginning with cost cutting and legal obligations and ending with increased investor appeal and brand value. It also provides helpful advice on incorporating sustainability into operations, product design, marketing, supply chain, and corporate governance through strategic models, namely the Triple Bottom Line, Shared Value Model, and the circular economy principles. Successful integration and the lessons learned are of actual business practices of powerhouses such as Patagonia, Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL), and Tech Mahindra. This chapter also discusses practical issues such as balancing short-term profitability with long-term sustainability and the dangers of greenwashing. Ecological goals are now an element of company growth and have grown synonymous with it as the environment changes. It also presents responsible environmental integration as a basic necessity for companies which are value-driven and future-ready, apart from being legal requirements. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Innovating for a Sustainable Future: The Interplay of Green, Socially Responsible, and Sustainable HRM Practices
abstract: Organizations, in their efforts to meet the sustainability goals set worldwide, have no option but to adopt the environment and society-friendly practices while at the same time getting pressure. Nevertheless, businesses are not fully unlocking their ability to innovate and perform through the integration of green HRM (GHRM), socially responsible HRM (SRHRM), and sustainable HRM (SHRM) that are very poorly connected and implemented at times. Moreover, one of the key motivations behind the present research is to study the overlapping areas and integration of these three variables and to uncover their potential in terms of sustainability and innovation. Utilizing a PRISMA method, this research has analyzed 179 research articles dating from 2008 to 2025 to discover the trends, theme clusters, and their contributions to sustainability. According to the results, one of the most efficient methods to foster innovation is through GHRM, and at the same time, SRHRM and SHRM are becoming very popular due to the no-brainer of their practices being close to GHRM. The implications of this research are significant for both theorists and practitioners who need to consider the areas of innovation, green creativity, sustainability, and digital transformation as main drivers. The findings will be very useful for the HR practitioners, organizational leaders, and policymakers as well as the researchers who are trying to come up with the integrated, innovation-based HRM strategies that cover environmental, social, and economic sustainability issues. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Authoritarian capitalism and foreign investment
abstract: A core determinant of firms’ international investment decisions is the ability of host-country political institutions to reduce policy uncertainty. While prior research has focused largely on formal constraints within democracies, this paper introduces a novel theoretical framework that reclassifies all political regimes −- democratic and authoritarian −-based on the protections they provide to private capital. This approach allows us to differentiate countries that appear similar under existing measures of executive constraint but vary widely in their institutional treatment of investors. Using firm-level foreign direct investment data, we show that this regime classification significantly improves predictions of investment patterns. Our results reveal that semi-competitive authoritarian regimes attract more investment than their non-competitive authoritarian counterparts, underscoring the importance of moving beyond democracy-centric frameworks when assessing political risk. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: Clause-level structural alignment between ASME Section III and Czech NTD A.S.I. Section III: Domain- and component-resolved assessment
abstract: Comparative studies of nuclear pressure-boundary component design codes have focused mainly on selected provisions and governing equations, but domain- and component-resolved clause-level quantification between ASME Section III and NTD A.S.I. Section III has not been systematically reported. This study applies a Clause Harmonization Index (CHI) to compare the two codes for piping, vessels, and pumps across nine technical domains. The overall clause-level structural alignment was CHI = 0.724, with piping showing the highest overall correspondence and pumps the lowest. A bounded numerical illustration for piping, vessel, and equivalent pump pressure-boundary cases showed only limited deviations in representative analytical quantities, with the largest difference not exceeding 5.5% in simplified fatigue usage, under the yield-governed pressure–temperature condition representative of primary system operation. These patterns are traced to two structural features of NTD A.S.I.: an explicit ASME-NC alternative for piping and qualification-related provisions distributed across multiple NTD Sections. The CHI-based comparison provides a reproducible basis for identifying where additional cross-code mapping is required in national adaptations of ASME Section III. © 2026 Korean Nuclear Society, Published by Elsevier Korea LLC. title: Degradation of Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast integrity: Temporal clustering and anomaly persistence
abstract: As safety systems like the Airborne Collision Avoidance System X (ACAS X) increasingly depend on Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B), the structural reliability of these data streams is critical. Traditional monitors assume independent, stochastic failures. This study challenges that assumption by building a global baseline of longitudinal degradation from 229.0 billion state vectors. The framework integrates multiscale permutation testing with day-resolution, exposure-adjusted survival analysis. Significant temporal clustering appears in 98.9% of the high-utilization commercial cohort (≥20 flight-hours/month; N=30,716) and in 67.2% of the sparser remainder under the uniform null; 81.3% of sparse-cohort detections survive a stricter block-preserving null. Clustering peaks at a 3-second characteristic scale, and the mean sustained duration of 28.83 s exceeds the 5-second fault tolerance of decentralized fusion trackers. Across the fleet, 58.4% of aircraft record clustered anomalies on two or more distinct observation days, and 55.5% across two or more calendar months. With follow-up censored at the first >30-day observation gap, 56.0% of aircraft experience a first clustered anomaly, with a median of 9 observed days. A recurrent-event hazard model links recurrence to recent utilization (hazard ratio 1.19 per standard deviation) and, more strongly, to network observability coverage (hazard ratio 1.52). The negative time-to-first exposure coefficient is largely an artifact of onset timing. These results shift integrity monitoring from point-in-time anomaly detection to predictive system health management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Strategic leadership in cross-border mergers and acquisitions: a unified CEO advice-seeking framework
abstract: Cross-border mergers and acquisitions (CBMAs) require executives to coordinate decisions across resource, institutional, organizational, and stakeholder domains. Yet CBMA literature largely examines these challenges separately, offering limited explanations of how executives mobilize expertise across them. This study synthesizes the intellectual structure of CBMA research using bibliometric and thematic analysis of 1,833 articles published between 1970 and 2023. Emergent themes included value creation through resource alignment, emerging economy contexts, cultural integration and governance, sociocultural complexity and innovation, heterogeneity of CBMA outcomes, and CBMA decision appraisal. Viewed through the lens of the CEO advice-seeking framework, the themes translate into several executive challenges. We propose a unified framework that specifies the expertise required for each challenge, relevant sources of advice, and how advice can be evaluated and translated into strategic action. The framework conceptualizes CBMAs as leadership-driven, knowledge-mobilization processes that involve coordination of expertise distributed across transaction and integration. Further, this study outlines multi-level managerial implications and directions for future research. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Beyond Today: Strategic Foresight in AI-Powered Circular Economies for Environmental Sustainability
abstract: This chapter is investigating how AI could assist in strategic management and strategic foresight in this fast-changing business environment. Conventional strategic planning approaches are usually too rigid or slow to address the multifaceted circumstances. This chapter explores ways in which AI can enhance foresight and support better long-term decision-making. The chapter reviewed the primary strategic foresight tools, horizon scanning, scenario planning, Delphi studies and trend analysis explaining the potential of AI to support each approach. AI solutions like machine learning, big data analytics and natural language processing allow companies to sort through vast amounts of information and spot trends early on, identifying the smallest signs of change. These features facilitates the creation of stronger and evidence-based future scenarios. Above all, the chapter emphasizes that AI integrated with strategic foresight has potential to make organizations more adaptive, robust and ready for future ambiguity. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Media representations of corporate sustainability communication: German news coverage of lithium mining in Chile
abstract: Introduction: The global shift toward e-mobility has intensified scrutiny of raw material procurement, particularly lithium mining in Chile–essential for the automotive industry. However, less is known about how German news media portray and evaluate the sustainability of lithium mining and how corporate messages by the automotive sector are represented in this debate. Methodology: This study analyzes how German news media frame the sustainability of lithium extraction in Chile, focusing on ideological differences across outlets, representations of automotive companies in news coverage, and their implications for industrial and environmental priorities surrounding the debate. A qualitative content analysis of 192 articles from five major outlets (2009-2024) reveals distinct narratives. Results: The left-leaning news outlet Zeit Online and the tabloid Bild emphasize socio-ecological consequences, while the financial newspaper Handelsblatt and liberal outlet FAZ foreground economic risks; the conservative newspaper Welt combines environmental and geopolitical concerns. Findings highlight temporal shifts whereby articles after 2020 reflect global awareness of geopolitical issues. Discussion: The findings suggest that German news coverage increasingly frames lithium mining through interconnected environmental, industrial, and geopolitical concerns, while automotive companies occupy uneven positions of visibility within these mediated sustainability debates. Conclusions: By identifying how automotive companies are represented in news coverage, the study highlights patterns that are consistent with agenda-building dynamics in the interaction between automotive companies and news media. © 2027, HISIN (History of Information Systems). .

title: Model-aware counterfactual explanations for transformer-based sequence prediction via attention-guided semantic search
abstract: Counterfactual explanations for Transformer-based sequence prediction models should change model predictions while remaining semantically plausible and consistent with the underlying data manifold. Existing methods often rely on input-level distance metrics, externally specified constraints, or weakly guided perturbations, limiting their ability to exploit semantic dependencies encoded in neural representations. We propose SAGE, a Semantic Attention-Guided Explanations framework for model-aware counterfactual generation. SAGE formulates counterfactual generation as a constrained semantic optimization problem and transforms the predictive model's attention distribution into a structured probabilistic prior for guiding the search. The framework integrates three components: semantic-aware population initialization in the contextual embedding space, a confidence-aware hybrid fitness function that jointly optimizes target prediction confidence and semantic proximity, and an attention-guided evolutionary operator that perturbs model-relevant sequence elements under feasibility constraints. SAGE is evaluated in predictive business process monitoring, a representative heterogeneous sequence prediction setting involving static attributes and dynamic event sequences. Experiments on BPIC 2017, BPIC 2012, Helpdesk, and Sepsis show that SAGE maintains competitive prediction validity and achieves substantially higher manifold plausibility than most representative baselines. Ablation and controlled comparisons further demonstrate that semantic initialization and attention-guided mutation improve counterfactual quality and search convergence. Under the same evolutionary budget, attention-guided mutation discovers the first valid counterfactual 36.4% earlier in terms of generations than random mutation, although the complete framework remains more computationally expensive than simpler baselines. These results support model-internal attention as an operational search prior for reliable, feasible, and semantically plausible counterfactual explanations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A bibliometric analysis of primary science education in scopus database
abstract: The current bibliometric analysis investigates the evolution of research on primary science education, emphasising on author contributions, country-based production, institutional engagement, and co-occurrence analysis. abstract: Artificial intelligenceArtificial Intelligence (AI) (AI) technologies strive to transform the landscape of human evolution. title: From LinkedIn to labor statistics: Using Revelio microdata for labor market research in developing economies
abstract: We explore the use of Revelio data—obtained primarily from LinkedIn profiles—as a source of labor force microdata in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where large-sample, high-frequency, employer-linked alternatives are largely unavailable. To address the selection inherent to LinkedIn usership, we employ ILO labor statistics to construct five sets of country-year-specific weights that alleviate non-representativeness across occupation, industry, occupation × education, industry × education, and industry × firm-size cells. We further validate these weights using national census data where they are available and not used for ILO labor statistics. The weighted dataset provides a balanced monthly panel with coverage across most LMICs. We also discuss remaining limitations of the dataset, including within-cell selection and self-reporting errors, and suggest techniques to alleviate them. Despite imperfect coverage, Revelio offers improved temporal and geographical resolution as well as cross-country comparability and is especially useful for studying the role of firms in economic development. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Layered lanthanum hydroxycarbonate turns phosphate pollution into slow-release fertilizer
abstract: Mismanagement of Phosphorus (P) depletes phosphate finite rock reserves and exacerbates widespread aquatic eutrophication, driving an urgent demand for integrated strategies that simultaneously remove and recover phosphate (PO43−). Herein, we show that rough-surfaced oblate La(OH)CO3 particles capture PO43− with exceptional efficiency, and the spent one can serve as a slow-release P fertilizer, enabling full pollutant-to-resource conversion. The material achieves a maximum adsorption capacity of 211.59 mgP g−1, rapid chemisorption-dominated kinetics, a broad pH window (3–7), and strong selectivity against competing anions and natural organic matters. In fixed-bed column tests, effluent P concentrations stayed below 0.2 mg L−1 discharge threshold for a breakthrough time of 84 h and > 90% P recovery was achieved. When evaluated as a fertilizer in hydroponic cultivation of Pisum sativum, the spent adsorbent produced plant height and biomass that matched or exceeded those from a conventional soluble P source at the optimal dosage. Mechanistic and comparative studies with La(OH)3 and La2(CO3)3 reveal that the superior performance originates from the synergy of electrostatic attraction, surface OH− ligand exchange, interlayer CO32− anion exchange (facilitated by favorable size matching), and inner-sphere complexation, all enabled by the unique layered structure of La(OH)CO3 ([La(OH)]2+ framework layers and interlayer CO32−). This work reports a high-performance La-based adsorbent for efficient P control and establishes a broadly applicable pollutant-to-resource paradigm that bridges environmental remediation with circular nutrient economies. © 2026

title: Does concentrated ownership structure affect ESG disclosure? Role of corporate life cycle and market competition
abstract: Using a sample of Indian listed firms, this study examines the role of concentrated ownership structure in shaping firms' environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure. We find concentrated ownership has a significant negative impact on ESG disclosure, and the result is more prominent in the case of domestic, family, and state ownership. ESG disclosure is considered to enhance information symmetry and transparency, and the results reveal the role of concentrated ownership, including domestic, family, and state ownership, in limiting transparency. In contrast, foreign and institutional ownership positively impact ESG disclosure, indicating their monitoring role and preference for transparency. Next, we highlight the mediating role of audit quality between concentrated ownership types and ESG disclosure. We also find concentrated ownership negatively impacts ESG disclosure in low market competition and mature product life cycle stages but positively impacts when it interacts with business group affiliation. We also show that ESG disclosure reduces the cost of debt and financing constraints to firms, but concentrated ownership reduces ESG disclosure, highlighting the trade-off preference for concentrated owners between short-term control benefits and long-term value losses. Finally, we show that the results are robust at various robustness checks, including alternative variables, instrumental variables, entropy balancing and propensity score matching. Showing the varying opacity and transparency preferences among different concentrated owner types, the study offers valuable insights to investors, regulators and broader stakeholders. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Contrasting responses of above- and belowground multifunctionality to increasing soil salinealkaline conditions in a semi-arid grassland in Northern China
abstract: Salinealkaline conditions in soils represent a critical environmental stressor that threatens the sustainability of semi-arid grassland ecosystems. However, a systematic understanding how salinization affects ecosystem multifunctionality (EMF), particularly the coupled above- and belowground responses, is currently lacking. This study investigated a semi-arid salinealkaline grassland using 37 quadrats along a natural salinealkaline gradient spanning low, moderate, and high salinealkaline levels. By measuring key indicators of plant community biomass, dominant species, and soil nutrient content, we quantified the aboveground multifunctionality (AGMF) and belowground (soil chemical) multifunctionality (BGMF) as component indices of EMF. Along the gradient, EMF showed no significant overall difference, resulting from offsetting asymmetric responses of AGMF and BGMF. AGMF exhibited a unimodal pattern, driven by dominant species functional traits such as Ca²⁺ accumulation, whereas BGMF declined linearly with increasing pH and salinity, mainly due to reductions in soil organic carbon and suppression of the available nitrogen (NH₄⁺-N) pool. Soil pH acted as a bidirectional regulator, indirectly promoting AGMF by increasing dominant species Ca²⁺ content while directly inhibiting BGMF by decreasing soil NH₄⁺-N. Salinity exerted direct or indirect negative associations with both AGMF and BGMF. Although EMF did not differ significantly along the gradient, it showed a declining trend with increasing pH, suggesting that the sustained negative effects on belowground functions may dominate the long-term trajectory of ecosystem multifunctionality. This study emphasizes that coordinated above- and belowground strategies should be adopted in the management and restoration of semi-arid salinealkaline grasslands. The physiological characteristics of salt-tolerant dominant species can support aboveground productivity in the short term, but maintaining soil organic carbon pools and belowground ecological processes must be regarded as the core goal in curbing habitat degradation and achieving sustainable restoration. By systematically revealing the asymmetric response mechanisms of AGMF and BGMF, this study provides a scientific basis for shifting restoration practices from single vegetation targets to integrated plantsoil system strategies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Exploring the determinants of student loyalty in islamic higher education: An empirical study from Indonesia
abstract: This study investigates the determinants of student loyalty in the context of Islamic higher education in Indonesia, focusing on the role of religiosity and student satisfaction. As competition among higher education institutions intensifies, particularly in Yogyakarta, understanding the drivers of student loyalty becomes essential for institutional sustainability. Drawing upon relationship marketing theory and the service-dominant logic perspective, this research examines whether religiosity directly influences student loyalty and whether student satisfaction mediates this relationship. A quantitative approach was employed via a structured questionnaire distributed to 190 respondents, consisting of final-year students and alumni from private Islamic universities in Yogyakarta. The data were via structural equation modelling-partial least squares (SEM-PLS). The findings reveal that religiosity significantly influences student satisfaction, which in turn positively affects student loyalty. However, religiosity does not directly influence loyalty, indicating that satisfaction plays a critical mediating role. These results underscore the importance of cultivating religiosity-based values in higher education service delivery, as well as ensuring continuous improvement in student satisfaction to strengthen loyalty. The study contributes to the literature by integrating religiosity into the service quality and loyalty framework, offering both theoretical insights and managerial implications for Islamic universities in Indonesia. Despite its notable contributions, this study is constrained by its focus on private Islamic universities within a single regional context, which may limit the generalizability of the findings. Future investigations are encouraged to employ longitudinal designs or comparative analyses encompassing diverse types of higher education institutions and broader geographical areas to enhance the external validity of the proposed model. Additionally, incorporating complementary constructs such as institutional trust, perceived value, and university reputation could provide a more comprehensive understanding of the multifaceted processes underlying student loyalty within faith-based higher education environments. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Temporal trends across diagnostic subgroups of Dutch ICU patients over a decade; a nationwide cohort study
abstract: Background The demand for intensive care in the Netherlands is influenced by evolving treatments, external factors such as pandemics, and policy decisions. Concerns have grown about Intensive Care Units (ICU) capacity, nurse shortages, and changing patient populations. Understanding temporal trends in ICU admissions and case-mix is essential for resource allocation and preparedness. Methods This descriptive study analyzed data from 2014 to 2023 from the National Intensive Care Evaluation registry. Patients were categorized using predefined diagnostic categories and age subgroups, alongside data-driven patient clusters identified through latent class analysis. Trends were analyzed in annual ICU admissions and average daily number of concurrent ICU patients. Results A total of 640,465 ICU admissions from 59 Dutch hospitals were included. Between 2014 and 2023, ICU admissions decreased by 15%. This decline was not linear: a modest downward trend before the pandemic followed by a more pronounced reduction during the pandemic period. The largest decrease was observed among patients aged ≥80 years (40%). In contrast, admissions for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest increased by 13%. Differing trends across diagnostic subgroups drove shifts in ICU case-mix, with an increasing relative contribution of younger and less severely ill patients, reflecting a changing ICU population. Conclusion Changes in ICU case-mix occurred alongside declining admissions and occupancy between 2014 and 2023. These temporal patterns likely reflect both an underlying secular decline and additional pandemic-related effects. Ongoing monitoring of ICU population dynamics is essential for guiding capacity planning, optimizing workforce allocation, and strengthening preparedness for future public health challenges. title: Group zero-norm regularized robust loss minimization: Proximal MM method and statistical error bound
abstract: This paper concerns the group zero-norm regularized robust loss minimization problems. We propose a proximal majorization-minimization (PMM) algorithm to tackle a class of equivalent difference-of-convex (DC) surrogate optimization problems. Under the Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz (KL) property, we establish the global convergence of the proposed algorithm and characterize its local (sub)linear convergence rate. Furthermore, for linear observation models with design matrices satisfying restricted eigenvalue conditions, we derive statistical estimation error bounds between the PMM-generated iterates (including their limit points) and the ground truth solution. To efficiently implement the PMM framework, we develop a proximal dual semismooth Newton method for solving the subproblems. Numerical experiments on both synthetic data and the UCI benchmark demonstrate the efficiency of our PMM method. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Hidden Markov Model variants for prognostics: A comprehensive review and model selection framework
abstract: This paper reviews and systematizes the use of Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) and their semi-Markov extensions for prognostics within Prognostics and Health Management (PHM). It argues that prognostic models should be evaluated not only by prediction error but also by four key characteristics: uncertainty quantification, robustness, interpretability, and feasibility. The review organizes HMM-based methods into three groups: standard HMMs, Hidden Semi-Markov Models (HSMMs), and non-homogeneous HSMMs. Each group is assessed based on how it contributes to the four characteristics. Building on this analysis, the paper formalizes four representative models under a common notation for prognostics: HMM, HSMM, Adaptive HSMM (AHSMM), and Similarity Learning HSMM (SLHSMM). These models are benchmarked on the C-MAPSS turbofan dataset and on impacted open-hole composite specimens to evaluate both controlled and out-of-distribution scenarios. Results show that SLHSMM achieves the highest accuracy and provides sharper, well-calibrated uncertainty when test trajectories resemble training patterns. In contrast, AHSMM shows greater robustness to unexpected shifts and impact-induced behaviors. HMM and HSMM remain attractive choices when simplicity and computational efficiency are most important. The study concludes with practical guidance for selecting among HMM-based approaches based on the four key characteristics required for real-world PHM applications. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Digital and AI-enabled support for HACCP-based dairy food safety management: Functions, evidence, and implementation boundaries
abstract: Dairy food-safety management spans primary production, purchasing, processing, packaging, storage, transport, and distribution. Biological, chemical, physical, and allergenic hazards vary with the product and process. Digital and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled tools can extend how data are collected, interpreted, and connected to Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) and food safety management system (FSMS) activities. Their value depends on the function supported and the evidence for the intended use. This narrative, function-oriented review examines sensors, Internet of Things systems, traceability platforms, machine learning, predictive microbiology, rapid detection, knowledge graphs, retrieval-augmented generation, and large language models. The comparison covers five functions: hazard analysis and risk prioritization; monitoring and deviation detection; verification and the screening–confirmatory interface; documentation, traceability, and plan review; and decision support at the corrective-action interface. The analytical framework records dairy relevance, deployment stage, and validation scope. It also distinguishes analytical outputs and alerts from verified deviations, confirmatory evidence, and site-specific actions. The reviewed tools are best established for data capture, monitoring, and verification inputs. Evidence is thinner for hazard prioritization, digital plan review, and AI-assisted decision support. Food-safety use requires dairy product and process context, fit-for-purpose evidence, approved procedures, auditable records, and review by responsible personnel. Important constraints include interoperability, real-world dairy validation, model and sensor lifecycle control, organizational capacity, and food-safety culture. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Artificial intelligence-supported learning and academic performance: Evidence from Chinese universities
abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence tools into university learning environments has generated urgent but as yet inadequately answered empirical questions about the direction, magnitude, and mechanisms of their effects on student academic performance. This paper provides a comprehensive empirical analysis of AI-supported learning and academic performance in Chinese higher education, drawing on a large-scale survey-administrative data linkage of 1080 undergraduate students across 12 universities spanning five academic disciplines in the 2021-2022 academic year. The study integrates technology acceptance theory, self-regulated learning frameworks, and human capital theory within a unified analytical design employing structural equation modelling, hierarchical regression with moderation testing, mediation analysis with bootstrapped confidence intervals, and a quasi-experimental difference-in-differences specification exploiting staggered institutional AI policy adoption. Core findings establish that AI usage intensity exerts a positive and statistically robust effect on cumulative GPA (standardised beta: 0.284, p < 0.001), mediated primarily through self-regulated learning enhancement (indirect effect: 0.138, 95% CI: 0.094-0.182) and cognitive engagement (0.121, 0.081-0.161). A statistically significant positive interaction between AI usage and prior academic achievement reveals that above-average students benefit more from AI tool adoption than below-average students, raising equity concerns that are empirically corroborated by significant disparities in digital literacy and AI access across socioeconomic subgroups. The difference-in-differences analysis, exploiting staggered university-level AI policy rollout, yields an intent-to-treat GPA effect of 0.18 grade points (p < 0.01), consistent with the primary regression findings. Subgroup analyses document significant effect heterogeneity by discipline, gender, institution type, and first-generation student status, with STEM and business students showing larger effects and first-generation students showing the largest absolute AI benefit but remaining the most digitally underserved group. A GPA trajectory analysis using six-semester longitudinal data confirms that early AI adopters achieved significantly steeper positive GPA trends following AI tool introduction compared with non-adopters. These findings collectively call for policy frameworks that integrate active AI literacy development, equitable access provision, and academic integrity governance into a coherent institutional AI-in-education strategy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Comparison of staff-deployed and patient-directed electronic meal ordering systems: Patient experiences and food intake in an Australian acute care hospital
abstract: Hospital foodservice plays a critical role in patient satisfaction, nutritional intake, and recovery; however, evidence comparing electronic meal ordering systems (eMOSs) remains limited. This study assessed differences in patient satisfaction, self-reported food intake, and reasons for incomplete meal consumption between staff-deployed and patient-directed eMOSs in an Australian acute care hospital. A survey comprising quantitative items and optional free-text comments was distributed via lunch trays across the same participating wards during the staff-deployed eMOS period and repeated following implementation of the patient-directed eMOS. Fifty-one and sixty-one patients completed the survey during the respective study periods. No significant differences in patient satisfaction across foodservice domains or self-reported food intake were observed between systems. Across both groups, food quality was rated lowest, while the dining environment received the highest ratings. Incomplete meal consumption was primarily attributed to dissatisfaction with food quality, including unappealing presentation, disliked taste, and unsuitable food types, as well as reduced appetite and illness-related factors. Thematic analysis identified food quality (flavour, temperature, presentation, and menu variety), and the meal ordering process as central to patient experience. While overall satisfaction did not differ between systems, the nature of negative experiences varied: the staff-deployed eMOS was limited by staffing capacity, whereas the patient-directed eMOS was constrained by usability challenges with television-based interfaces. These findings indicate that eMOS implementation alone is unlikely to improve patient outcomes. Optimising hospital foodservice requires integrating high-quality food provision with accessible, user-centred meal ordering systems to enhance patient satisfaction, support dietary intake, and potentially reduce food waste. © 2026 The Authors

title: Self-adaptive Bregman projection method based on the golden ratio technique for variational inequalities
abstract: This paper studies a golden ratio subgradient extragradient method with multiple sequences of parameters for solving variational inequalities in reflexive Banach spaces. By introducing an improved self-adaptive rule, not only does it avoid prior knowledge of Lipschitz constant of underlying operator, but it also accelerates the convergence rate of the algorithm. Under suitable assumptions and appropriate parameter choices, we obtain weak convergence and R-linear convergence results. In addition, we conduct numerical experiments in both Hilbert and non-Hilbert spaces, demonstrating that the proposed algorithm outperforms some existing ones in the literature. Finally, the proposed algorithm and the weak convergence result are applied to an image restoration problem, verifying the effectiveness and applicability of the algorithms. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
