title: Electron-deficient boron-containing additive induced Lewis acid interface with O–S/B–S chemical adsorption of polysulfides for durable sodium–sulfur batteries
abstract: Room-temperature sodium‑sulfur (RT Na-S) batteries hold great promise for large-scale energy storage, yet they face severe challenges from polysulfide shuttling and sodium dendrite growth. To address these challenges, this study proposes an innovative strategy by introducing a boron-based additive, 2,4,6-trimethoxyboroxine (TMBX), into the propylene carbonate (PC)/NaClO₄ electrolyte to in-situ construct a boron-rich interphase. On the cathode side, the cathode electrolyte interface (CEI) layer is enriched with electron-deficient Lewis acidic B₂O₃, which chemisorbs soluble sodium polysulfides via B-S and O-S bonds. Simultaneously, this interphase forms a physical barrier due to its high mechanical strength and favorable structural properties, and the two effects work synergistically to suppress the shuttle effect. On the anode side, the inner solid electrolyte interface (SEI) layer that rich in boron-containing inorganic components can effectively inhibits sodium dendrite nucleation. Benefiting from the synergistic regulation of the boron-containing interphase, the TMBX-modified electrolyte endows Na-S cells with excellent performance. This work establishes a rational electrolyte design principle of leveraging boron-centered Lewis acidity for targeted polysulfide anchoring, coupled with a high-modulus interphase, offers a scalable and efficient strategy toward durable RT Na-S batteries. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Bridging the pitch and the canvas: Synergistic insights for advancing empirical research a pre-registered report
abstract: High-quality empirical research depends on guidance tools that are structured, coherent, and lifecycle-spanning. Yet researchers across business disciplines continue to draw on fragmented, piecemeal advice that was never designed to integrate into a single system. Two independent responses to this challenge have emerged from within the business academic community over the past decade: the Pitching Research Framework (PRF; Faff, 2015, 2024) and the AMJ Management Research Canvas (MRC; Dorobantu et al., 2024). Developed independently and in different disciplinary communities, they have never been systematically compared, and the prospect of their integration has not previously been explored. This paper presents the protocol for a conceptual study that addresses this gap. We advance the conceptual proposition that integrating the PRF and the MRC produces a unified, end-to-end research guidance pathway that is meaningfully greater than either framework alone in advancing research clarity, rigour, and transparency across the full research lifecycle (from embryonic ideation through to manuscript completion). The research design involves systematic comparative analysis of the components of each framework, leading to the development of an integrated synergistic model grounded in Responsible Science principles (cRRBM, 2017; Faff, 2021; Tsui, 2021, 2022). As a pre-registered report for the Pacific-Basin Finance Journal, details of the analytical design are presented in full, with findings to follow in the Phase 4 paper. © 2026 The Authors. title: Bargaining never stops: Post-entry bargaining in decentralized emerging markets
abstract: This study examines how multinational enterprises (MNEs) bargain with host-country stakeholders after market entry as they expand their operations across decentralized emerging markets characterized by multiple layers of government and influential non-state actors. Drawing on a longitudinal case study of a global MNE with 24 extractive sites across Indonesia, we show that post-entry bargaining requires continuous engagement with multiple layers of government over permits and regulations, as well as with local communities over employment, land and environmental impacts to avoid social unrest. In one region, community opposition forced the MNE to exit, despite substantial sunk costs, demonstrating that formal permits and government support cannot substitute for a social license to operate. We find that post-entry bargaining under institutional complexity requires cross-level strategies that address tensions across government and community levels. These strategies generate spillovers, allowing MNEs to alleviate tensions beyond their intended target. We thus demonstrate that foreign investment is shaped not only by national governments, but also by subnational authorities and communities who play a direct and often decisive role in shaping the terms and success of investments. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Tailoring zeolite-based catalysts for mild, methane-selective VOC combustion in stack emission monitoring systems
abstract: Accurate methane quantification in industrial emissions is frequently hindered by the presence of non-methane hydrocarbons and volatile organic compounds, which can interfere with conventional analytical methods. Commercial oxidation catalysts can remove these compounds, but their relatively high operating temperatures increase energy consumption and may also promote undesired methane oxidation. Here, we report a catalytic gas-conditioning strategy based on Cu- and Co-containing MFI, BEA, and FAU zeolites for the preferential oxidation of interfering hydrocarbons while preserving methane. The effects of zeolite topology, Si/Al ratio, metal loading, dispersion, and redox speciation on catalytic activity and selectivity were systematically investigated. Catalysts prepared from cobalt acetate showed superior performance, with activity increasing sharply above ~5 wt% Co. Structural characterization revealed that cobalt is initially present as highly dispersed Co2⁺ species that transform into mixed-valence cobalt oxides during reaction. Although cobalt migration and sintering occur under reaction conditions, the zeolite frameworks remain structurally stable and maintain high CO₂ selectivities (>90%). Compared with the commercial Carulite® catalyst, Co/MFI displayed superior atom efficiency and enhanced ethane-over-methane selectivity, attributed to the confinement of isolated cobalt species within the zeolite pore network. The combination of molecular confinement and highly dispersed metal sites was identified as the key factor governing low-temperature activity and methane selectivity. By integrating heterogeneous catalysis with energy-efficient, solvent-free gas-phase operation and real-time emission monitoring, this approach supports the green chemistry principles of pollution prevention, catalysis, energy efficiency, and real-time analysis. These results identify cobalt-loaded MFI zeolites as promising catalysts for selective VOC removal in methane-monitoring and air purification applications. © 2026 The Authors. title: PSG-Net: Physical saliency guided adaptive fusion network for infrared and visible image fusion
abstract: The core challenge in infrared and visible image fusion lies in achieving a seamless integration where thermal saliency does not overshadow critical texture details. Existing deep learning frameworks, however, often struggle with a fundamental disconnect, the inability to explicitly translate the inherent physical priors of thermal targets into learnable spatial guidance. This frequently leads to saliency-texture trade-offs, where fine visible textures are suppressed within high-thermal regions, compromising image fidelity. To address this challenge, we propose a novel Physical Saliency Guided Adaptive Fusion Network. Our approach begins by systematically analyzing the physical characteristics of high temperature IR targets and translating these properties into network design principles. By effectively coupling the physical saliency prior with learnable feature representations, PSG-Net achieves the synergistic enhancement of salient objects and background details, significantly improving the visual quality, detail fidelity, and application robustness of the fused images, demonstrating excellent performance on the MSRS, M3FD and LLVIP datasets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: The impact of platform verification badges on social media influencer engagement
abstract: Verification badges play an important role in signaling authenticity and influence for social media contributors. However, recent platform shifts have turned badges from merit-based indicators into purchasable commodities, raising questions about their effectiveness. Drawing on signaling theory, this research examines how verification impacts engagement under three conditions: merit-based, hybrid, and non-merit-based. Using a multimethod design that combines influencer interviews, consumer discussions on Reddit, an experiment, and an empirical analysis of over 8 million daily observations from X, we found verification increases perceived authenticity, which in turn enhances perceived influence, thereby driving higher engagement. This value is not uniform across the mediation, as we find that when verification becomes easier to obtain, the badge continues to raise perceived authenticity, but its effect on perceived influence is reduced and reversed under fully paid verification, weakening its effect on engagement. These findings advance literature and offer actionable insights for influencers, marketers, and platforms. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Divalent cation-mediated regulation of the hierarchical structure and rheological properties of ovalbumin fibrils
abstract: Metal ions can regulate the structural organization and macroscopic properties of protein fibrillar assemblies. Although previous studies have extensively examined ion-mediated regulation of protein fibrillation, the effects of divalent cations on the hierarchical organization of preformed egg-protein fibrils remain poorly understood. In this study, OVA fibrils were prepared by heating the protein at pH 2.0 and 90 °C for 8 h, after which Mg2+, Zn2+, Ca2+, or Fe2+ was added to evaluate the effect of each ion on the post-formation organization and properties of the preformed fibrils. Divalent-cation treatment caused ion-dependent changes in the secondary-structure distribution, colloidal properties, microscopic morphology, and rheological behavior of the preformed OVA fibrils. These changes were attributed to post-formation interfibrillar association, aggregation, and structural reorganization rather than enhanced fibril formation. All OVA fibril systems showed partial precipitation at 500 mM, indicating loss of colloidal stability rather than homogeneous hydrogel formation. ICP-MS revealed ion-dependent differences in apparent metal retention. Collectively, these findings demonstrated that divalent cations regulated the hierarchical organization and rheological properties of preformed OVA fibrils through ion-dependent post-formation structural reorganization, providing a basis for controlling the functionality of egg-protein fibrillar materials. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Maintenance optimization in dynamic environment considering environment-induced maintenance delay
abstract: Most maintenance optimization studies for production systems assume stationary environmental states. In practice, however, the operating environments vary over time, changing both degradation dynamics and production reward of the system. Moreover, under certain harsh environmental states, maintenance actions cannot be executed and must be postponed. These factors impact the production reward, degradation penalty, and maintenance cost in a coupled manner, posing challenges for making optimal maintenance decisions. In this paper, we develop a maintenance optimization framework for minimizing the operational cost of a production system operating in dynamic environments with environment-induced maintenance delay. The optimization problem is formulated as a Markov decision process (MDP) over an infinite horizon, including the quantification of the threefold impact of the environment on maintenance. We establish key structural properties and prove that the optimal maintenance policy has a control limit structure. Based on these properties, we develop an improved value iteration algorithm, exploiting the monotone threshold characterization of the optimal policy and avoiding redundant action comparisons, to obtain the optimal solution efficiently. A numerical study of offshore wind turbines illustrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework and algorithm. Managerial insights are provided through sensitivity analysis. Copyright © 2026. title: Paving the Way toward Sustainability and Improving Performance in Renewable Power Projects Through Risk Management Practices
abstract: Risk management (RM) is an integral and essential component of project management. Addressing two vital aspects is critical: improving project performance and enhancing sustainability. Past studies have illustrated several RM practices without revealing their actual impact on these aspects, especially in addressing the unique characteristics of renewable power project development. This study fills the gaps and aims to explore critical RM practices and examine their influence on project performance and sustainability in developing renewable power projects. The present study identified 25 risk management practices from the existing literature and publicly available documents of 32 leading enterprises in the renewable sector in India. Furthermore, data were collected through a questionnaire survey from 104 renewable sector experts. An underlying structure of these practices was established, and factors were extracted using exploratory factor analysis (EFA). A partial least squares structural equation model (PLS-SEM) was then developed to evaluate their influence on the project's performance and sustainability parameters. The analysis revealed that RM practices such as systematic risk assessment, recording, and training (F1), inclusive and long-term planning (F2), engaging dedicated risk officers (F3), and identifying, documenting, and updating RM policy (F4) significantly and positively influence the performance and sustainability of renewable power projects. Moreover, the study provides a comprehensive insight into the current RM practices in the renewable power sector. The study enhances the body of knowledge by identifying critical RM practices and quantifying their impact on improving the performance and sustainability of renewable power projects. Adopting these crucial practices would help practitioners enhance the success of the power project, paving the way for achieving the sustainable development goals (SDGs). © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Adaptive auxiliary task generation and reinforcement learning-enhanced multi-task multi-population evolutionary offloading in IIoT
abstract: Workflow-based computation offloading has become a fundamental technique for improving execution efficiency in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems. However, heterogeneous workflow structures, complex task dependencies, and dynamic resource conditions make multi-workflow offloading a challenging multi-objective optimization problem. Existing evolutionary offloading methods generally optimize workflows independently and lack effective knowledge sharing mechanisms, resulting in limited search efficiency and potential negative transfer across heterogeneous tasks. To address these issues, this paper formulates multi-workflow computation offloading as a multitask multi-objective optimization problem and proposes an adaptive auxiliary task generation and reinforcement learning-enhanced multi-population MOEA/D (ATRL-MT-MOEAD). The proposed framework assigns each workflow to an independent subpopulation for collaborative evolution, introduces adaptive auxiliary tasks to accelerate convergence, and employs a reinforcement learning-based knowledge transfer mechanism to dynamically regulate inter-task information sharing while suppressing negative transfer. Experimental results on representative IIoT workflow benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method consistently achieves the best optimization performance. Compared with the strongest baseline for each metric, the proposed method reduces the average IGD by 72.0%, GD by 80.4%, ACT by 16.8%, and AEC by 14.5%, while consistently achieving superior Pareto-front quality. These results verify that the proposed framework provides superior convergence, solution diversity, and optimization effectiveness for complex multi-workflow computation offloading in dynamic IIoT environments. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Application of Process Mapping to Identify Nonvalue-Added Activities Associated with Formwork Labor in Reinforced Concrete Foundation Construction: A Lean Construction Study from India
abstract: Formwork handling and assembly significantly contribute to the time and cost of reinforced cement concrete. The performance of construction workers associated with formwork impacts the overall time-cost-quality performance of formwork activity. The application of process mapping (PM) tools helps identify and eliminate nonproductive tasks associated with formwork activity. A site observation-based study is conducted along with interviews with workmen and site engineers who supervised the work. The use of the PM tool helps to identify and categorize the different tasks undertaken by workers. This study observes that many nonproductive activities were undertaken by workers. Through a consultative process with concerned site officials, improvements in activities are identified and mapped using a PM tool. The elimination of nonproductive tasks leads to improved overall progress in the activity. This study is limited to formwork activities. The formwork material considered is plywood. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Identifying knowledge gaps in the assessment of biochar's carbon dioxide removal potential: A Canadian case study
abstract: Achieving carbon neutrality by 2050, as targeted under the Paris Agreement, requires the deployment of carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategies such as biochar production (BC), especially in biomass-rich regions. However, its effectiveness as a negative-emission technology depends strongly on process conditions and the sustainability of biomass feedstocks, requiring robust scientific evidence to confirm its CDR potential. Canada, which is well positioned to develop an industrial BC sector and is projected to rely on it for its net-zero strategy on it, was used as a case study to assess the alignment between BC-related scientific literature and its technical CDR potential derived from exploitable organic resources.Results show that Canada has a sustainably exploitable resource of 165,771 kt C under a conservative baseline scenario, dominated by fire-killed trees (73%), followed by crop residues (14%) and harvest residues (5%). According to Puro.earth's protocol, this resource represents a CDR potential of up to 348,146 kt CO2-equivalent by BC production, excluding upstream and downstream life cycle emissions. The systematic literature review, based on 150 Scopus-indexed publications, shows that Canadian BC research focuses mainly on secondary forestry residues feedstock and agricultural soil amendment applications. However, only 13 studies address BC production's environmental impacts in Canada.Significant knowledge gaps remain in Canadian literature, including insufficient data on alternative feedstocks (e.g., disturbed forest biomass, crop residues, manure), underexplored applications with market potential (e.g., fossil fuel substitution, materials), and limited environmental assessments across provinces and territories. Despite BC being among the most studied CDR options in Canada, current scientific literature does not adequately support large-scale deployment, highlighting the need for targeted research to inform policy and investment. © 2026 The Authors. title: From inclusive innovation to inclusive research: A reflexive journey toward transforming academia Editorial for the Special Issue “Advancing empirics and theory on inclusive innovation and research”
abstract: Inclusive innovation and research involves mechanisms by which marginalized consumers, users, and scholars are involved in producing innovation and research outcomes. In this special issue, we collect empirical studies that (1) shed light on the benefits of inclusion of marginalized groups in innovation and research and (2) propose renewed vocabulary, bold policies, and specific interventions to eradicate systemic biases and inequalities in innovation and research. From these contributions, we outline an agenda for future research on inclusive innovation centered on interdisciplinarity, theory building by conceiving of inclusive innovation as a mechanism, and adopting intersectional perspectives. We also reflect on the editorial journey of the initiative that was to promote inclusive scholarship in business and management. Here, we offer numerous recommendations for transformation to a more inclusive management scholarship, including those to create welcoming spaces for epistemologically diverse and geographically dispersed scholarship, and we outline development paths for inclusion. © 2026 The Authors. title: TEMPO-DQ framework: A Temporal-Ensemble, multi-phase operational data quality approach for early multi-class prediction under heterogeneous big data
abstract: Early multi-class prediction under heterogeneous big data requires data-quality (DQ) assessment that can determine whether partially observed, multi-source and temporally evolving inputs are genuinely fit for downstream deep-learning (DL) inference. Conventional DQ measures and existing DQ frameworks provide static, surface-level evidence, offering limited support for early-stage discrimination, temporal stability analysis and root-cause diagnosis. This study proposes TEMPO-DQ, a Temporal–Ensemble, multi-phase operational DQ framework for deployment-oriented early multi-class DL prediction. Its core contribution is the Temporal–Ensemble principle, which aggregates DQ evidence across observation phases and recurrent model families to reduce single-model bias and capture the stability of data fitness over time. The principle is operationalized by AccTEMPO, a three-level diagnostic mechanism providing a global monitoring indicator, phase-specific intervention summaries and fine-grained variant–model–phase evaluation. Validation uses two XuetangX-derived MOOC datasets of 3,297,128 and 2,324,524 instances under seven data variants, four cumulative phases and four recurrent architectures. Completeness and Consistency saturate at 1.000 for every processed variant, yielding no post-preprocessing discrimination, whereas AccTEMPOM1 still separates operational fitness across ranges of 0.1081 and 0.3370 in the two tasks. Ablating the aggregation mechanism shows that pooling the model committee alone reduces the spread of the DQ verdict for a data version by 54.6% and 65.8%, pooling phases alone by 45.2% and 27.5%, and only their combination yields a single-valued verdict, whereas a published performance-linked baseline recomputed on the same data returns mutually inconsistent per-configuration scores. © 2026 The Authors. title: Alleviating user anxiety towards AI health assistant platforms: integrating HAII-TIME and perceived control perspectives
abstract: This study addresses the critical yet under-researched area of user anxiety alleviation in artificial intelligence (AI) healthcare services. Drawing on the Human-AI Interaction model based on the Theory of Interactive Media Effects (HAII-TIME) and perceived control theory, we develop and test a framework that matches specific design interventions—message interactivity (action route) and visual nonverbal cues (cue route)—to distinct user anxiety types: technology use anxiety, privacy leakage anxiety, and individualized service anxiety. We conducted two cross-cultural online experiments (Study 1A: N = 540 Chinese users; Study 1B: N = 360 Spanish users) with a 3 (anxiety type) × 3 (interaction route) between-subjects design. The findings were consistent across both studies: (1) technology use anxiety was most effectively mitigated by high message interactivity (action route), which restores users’ sense of behavioral control; (2) privacy leakage anxiety was best alleviated by strong visual nonverbal cues (cue route), which restore cognitive control; and (3) individualized service anxiety, which involves a dual deficit in both behavioral and cognitive control, required the synergistic combination of both routes for effective mitigation. Utilizing data from a nationwide company’s AI healthcare mobile app, a field survey yielded 880 valid responses (Study 2), corroborating the findings of Study 1. This research contributes by integrating technology and service perspectives on user anxiety, advancing the HAII-TIME model through the identification of message interactivity and visual cues as crucial moderators, and pioneering perceived control theory in AI healthcare platforms. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Multinational dynamic capabilities: How multinational, how dynamic, how capable?
abstract: The dynamic capabilities perspective is a central framework used to explain how firms adapt, sustain competitive advantages, and/or create new competitive advantages in changing environments. Despite more than three decades of research, important questions remain about the nature, development, deployment, modification, and effectiveness of dynamic capabilities, particularly in multinational contexts. These questions are increasingly salient as multinational enterprises confront technological disruption, geopolitical fragmentation, institutional volatility, and other manifestations of an expanding global polycrisis. Drawing on our review of the evolution of the dynamic capabilities perspective and its extension into international business research, we argue that future research can advance our understanding of the dynamic capabilities construct by addressing three fundamental questions: How multinational are multinational dynamic capabilities? How dynamic are dynamic capabilities? And how capable are dynamic capabilities? Answering these questions requires greater attention to capability configurations and hierarchies, managerial and organizational microfoundations, heterogeneous multinational contexts, capability evolution, and capability measurement. The articles in this special issue advance our understanding of capability development, deployment, orchestration, and reconfiguration across a variety of international settings. They also highlight the importance of context-dependent capability systems and multilevel adaptation. Integrating these insights, we develop a framework for understanding multinational dynamic capabilities and identify directions for future research. We conclude that future progress will depend on developing more precise theories of multinationality, richer explanations of capability evolution, and more rigorous approaches to measure and evaluate multinational dynamic capabilities across contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Risk-Aware MIS Frameworks and Advanced Cybersecurity Solutions
abstract: The problem of phishing attack is among the most widespread cybercrimes that impact the information system of the organisation offering the lack of trust and endangering sensitive data. Such threats should be monitored and controlled via developed analytics to be embedded in the risk conscious Management Information System (MIS). Within the scope of this paper, it is proposed to implement a data analytics structure to combine machine learning with MIS reporting to deliver actionable intelligence with phishing attacks. Using Kaggle Phishing Detection Dataset that had 662 591 records and 11 attributes, a Random Forest classifier was used to classify the URLs as a phishing or a legitimate site. The model was found to have a 94% accuracy, 92% precision, 91% recall, and ROC-AUC of 0.96, which can be seen as evidence of an improved performance as opposed to the baseline classifiers whose typical accuracy is and usually falls below 85% in the framework of the model created. The framework provides risk scores, confusion matrices, precision and recall curves, which are displayed in MIS dashboards and are used by managers to assist them in deciding. It is shown in the use case that it is critical how organisations can target the high-risk entries, deal with the false positives and false negatives, and make organisations more resilient towards phishing attacks. It may be applied to prevent cybersecurity of enterprises monitoring, risk-aware decision-supporting, and embedded to sophisticated MIS infrastructures. Numerical comparisons can prove the soundness of the given solution, as it positions it as a scalable and explainable operational tool of cybersecurity in a business setting of the modern era. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: FracBiNet: Fractional bilateral decomposition with heterogeneous dual-path modeling for cross-market stock index prediction
abstract: Stock index levels are hard to predict one day ahead: daily series are noisy and near-integrated, with only a few thousand observations per market. We propose FracBiNet, a lightweight decomposition model with 4, 612 trainable parameters. Its core is a causal fractional bilateral kernel coupling a power-law temporal decay with an edge-preserving range gate. An innovation-whitening criterion on a dedicated learning-rate clock calibrates the kernel’s two parameters. Its latest level is the trend anchor, and a small additive-attention network models the residual. We evaluate under a leakage-free walk-forward protocol with eleven test folds (2014–2024) across CSI 300, S&P 500, and Dow Jones. Every baseline is tuned per fold under identical grids, with five seeds and Diebold–Mariano tests against persistence. First, FracBiNet is Pareto-efficient among learned models. It is the only one never significantly worse than persistence on any market; all eleven baselines are significantly worse on at least two of three. It never fails catastrophically, and its seed-level variance is negligible relative to market-regime variation. Second, deep forecasters fail at level extrapolation on trending indices. The failure is only partly attributable to the target formulation: retrained to predict next-day changes, some architectures recover toward persistence while others collapse. Third, no model, including ours, demonstrates value beyond naive references (persistence, buy-and-hold) under two strict, complementary evaluations (moving-block bootstrap and Holm-corrected multiplicity). The contrast between point estimates and corrected readings suggests that economic-value claims based on uncorrected Sharpe ratios, common in the stock-index forecasting literature, may overstate what the forecasts support. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Supporting the resolution of microservice security smells
abstract: Microservice-based applications offer scalability and flexibility but introduce security challenges, including security smells, i.e., possible symptoms of poor security decisions. The occurrence of these smells can be resolved via known refactorings, which, however, impact not only security but also other quality attributes, such as maintainability and performance. Deciding which refactoring to implement first is complex due to service interdependencies and varying business priorities. In this paper, to support practitioners in deciding under these complex and dynamic conditions, we introduce a decision support method designed to account for these multifaceted constraints. The proposed approach offers a holistic perspective that considers the urgency of each security smell instance alongside the effort needed to concretely implement the refactoring and cross-team dependencies, ultimately enabling context-aware decisions. We also present a prototype tool implementing the proposed method and assess the perceived usefulness of our method through a preliminary empirical study following a one-group pretest-posttest design. After being introduced to the method, participants perceived the decision process as easier and reported greater confidence in their selected refactorings. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: “To be a personal trainer, you have to look like 4% body fat”: How online personal trainers negotiate social media and body image
abstract: The online personal training industry is continuing to increase in popularity. Sociocultural pressures for personal trainers to maintain a certain physique to be deemed credible and marketable to consumers are well-documented, however no studies have qualitatively explored this in online personal trainers. Whilst previous research has highlighted that consuming certain types of fitness content may negatively impact body image, there is a paucity of research exploring the relationship between content creators and body image.This study aimed to examine how online trainers navigate social media as a digital workplace and their perceptions of its influence on their body image. 17 online coaches (Mage = 33.5; S.D. = 7.4 years), 58.8% female, participated in semi-structured interviews in which they discussed social media, body image and self-selected online content. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Overall, trainers viewed maintaining a social media presence as non-negotiable for business. However, participants also experienced pressure to uphold unrealistic standards online, including showcasing a lean physique and presenting an image of authenticity online whilst concealing body image struggles from consumers. Whilst some trainers rejected these industry standards, other trainers leveraged these norms by utilising their physique to gain traction on social media and enhance perceived desirability and competence to consumers. Findings contribute to improved understanding of appearance-pressures and highlight the need for greater education and support around body image within the online fitness industry. © 2026 The Authors. title: Barriers to Blockchain Implementation: A Multidimensional Analysis of Technological, Organizational, and Regulatory Challenges
abstract: The reason for the great interest in blockchain technology is its potential to make many industries, such as banking, logistics, healthcare, and governance, transparent, secure, and optimized. Whereas blockchain technology may be very instrumental in effecting wide changes in the world, its usage has been limited so far. The purpose of this research paper is to identify and discuss some of the main technological, business-related, and regulatory barriers that impede the full-scale implementation of blockchain technology. The report uses a qualitative approach that is guided by Technology Adoption Theory, Institutional Theory, and Innovation Diffusion in Literature. This study adopts a qualitative systematic literature review approach, synthesizing evidence from 44 peer-reviewed articles selected through a PRISMA-guided screening process shows that the issues surrounding the implementation of blockchain technology can be broadly classified into three different sections: issues revolving around technology, factors related to the readymade nature of the organization, and regulatory/legally related issues. The paper shows that scalability, power consumption, compatibility, and cybersecurity act as factors that may hinder the adoption due to their complexities in implementing novel technologies themselves. Other factors that may hamper adoption include lack of knowledge, lack of recognition, increased cost of implementation, and lack of values themselves. In addition, the lack of standardized legal practices surrounding the absence of the technology affects organizations that plan to implement blockchain technology in their firms. This research refines the existing literature on blockchain and innovation by providing an elaborated framework that can be used to address the issue of the implications of the mentioned barriers to the results of the adoption of blockchain technology. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Data-Centric Architectures for Digital Business and Marketing Technologies
abstract: The rocketing multi-channel customer data, real-time engagement spaces and AI-assisted marketing automation have presented the greatest problems ever in the quest to attain unified customer intelligence in fragmented digital environments. Conventional marketing technology (MarTech) architectures based on silos databases and batch-centric attribution pipeline analytics are challenging to provide real-time personalization, cross-channel attribution accuracy and scale-based adaptive campaign optimization. Although cloud-based solutions have enhanced scalability, they often do not provide the data-centric coherence that is essential to provide consistent customer perceptions, data lineage transparency and predictive optimization in the dynamic business environments. In this paper, we have suggested DataSphere, a data-oriented architecture model that incorporates federated data management, a real-time customer graph model, and artificial intelligence-based decision-making processes into a single Mar-Tech coordination system. The graph architecture uses cross-channel behavior prediction and next-best-action optimization based on transformers and verifiable attribution tracking based on distributed ledger technology. A simulation-based assessment is the comparison of DataSphere with conventional rule-based marketing automation systems and hybrid cloud-data-warehouse systems within the synthetic and real-world e-commerce data. These quantitative findings of three comparative models rule-based automation (Model A), ML-enhanced Customer Data Platform (Model B) and DataSphere (Model C) indicate that DataSphere performs better in converting its campaigns more accurately (42.3 rate better than Model A and 18.0 rate better than Model B), helps minimize errors in cross-channel attribution (58.7 rate better than Model A and B) and incurs less operational latency (36.4 rate better than Model A and B) without compromising GDPR/CCPA compliance through naturally implemented data These results confirm the fact that data centric architecture is a sustainable underpinning to adaptive, transparent and scalable digital business intelligence in the age of privacy consciousness marketing. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Evaluate the Effectiveness of an Open Source Solutions for Protecting Small Business Organization (SB) from DDoS Attacks
abstract: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) Attack become a concern for any organization who adopt online services [1]. It threatens the services availability by overloading its resources by illegitimate traffic. Such attack often result to services unavailability which lead to financial losses and destruction of customer trust [1]. Small Business (SB) organizations are particularly vulnerable to such attack due to the limitation security budgets and resources. The objective of this research is to assess the effectiveness of adapting open-source firewall as mitigation solutions against common DDoS attacks, the study focuses on the pfSense firewall integrated with Suricata as Intru-sion Detection and Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS) [8]. The methodology adapting experimental research design by analyzing and simulating multiple DDoS attack scenarios. It will include HTTP Flood, TCP SYN Flood and UDP Flood attacks. The system’s mitigation capabilities are assessed by monitoring service availability during attack conditions. The results demon-strate pfSense as firewall combined with IDS/IPS, can detect and mitigate common DDoS attack types. It also can maintain acceptable service availa-bility under the attack. This research highlights the impact of using open-source security tools for DDoS defense mechanisms in small businesses, providing practical insight into their performance. The findings aim to sup-port SBs in adopting efficient and affordable cybersecurity measures to pro-tect their online services. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: On the interplay between multi-instance BPMN collaborations and the environment
abstract: Nowadays, business processes are increasingly influenced by information from the surrounding physical environment and vice versa. This is especially evident in the presence of multi-instance participants able to move in and interact within a physical environment. In this regard, BPMN is a widely accepted standard for representing multi-party business processes in terms of collaboration diagrams, offering an expressive and understandable notation. However, BPMN, as well as its extensions, overlooks the support for the physical environment. In this paper, we describe the interplay between BPMN collaborations, including multiple instances of the same participant, and the physical environment. Specifically, we extend the BPMN meta-model with environmental concepts, defining environmental BPMN collaboration models. To facilitate a deeper understanding of the dynamics of these models, we provide a formal account of their semantics, addressing the handling of multiple instances of the same participant and incorporating time as a factor influencing process execution during interplay with the environment. Beyond defining a novel formalization, we propose BEAR, a tool that implements the formal semantics and supports modeling, animation, and debugging of environmental BPMN collaborations, extended to support multi-instance participants and time progression. We illustrate our findings through a fire-extinguishing multi-instance collaborative scenario. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Customer Churn Prediction: From Data to Decision
abstract: Restaurant customer churn is an increasing concern due to the growing use of online food delivery systems, loyalty programs, and other forms of e-commerce. When restaurants lose repeat customers it has a negative impact on the restaurant’s long-term revenue, as well as on their brand reputation and overall viability as a business. By being able to identify which customers are at risk of stopping or reducing their ordering activity, restaurants can develop the necessary retention strategies (e.g., personalized offers, loyalty incentives, targeted marketing campaigns) to keep those customers engaged. The traditional methods of performing churn analysis are often manual and based upon simple statistical reports and therefore, have limitations in terms of their predictive accuracy and scalability. In this paper, we propose a machine learning-based predictive framework to identify restaurant customer churn based upon historical order data, transaction records, customer behavior patterns, frequency of visits, feedback ratings, and spending trends. The methodology proposed combines the use of various ensemble learning algorithms (i.e., XGBoost, LightGBM) with preprocessing techniques (e.g., feature scaling, SMOTE) to address the issue of class imbalance within the dataset. The use of feature engineering will also provide the opportunity to derive additional behavioral characteristics (e.g., frequency of visits, average order size, time since last order, etc.) that will enhance the overall ability to predict customer-churn. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Artificial Intelligence for the Sustainable Development Goals: Corporate Opportunities and Ethical Dilemmas a Qualitative Meta-Analysis
abstract: In the current landscape, artificial intelligence (AI) is no longer an option but a necessity for businesses. These organizations emerge as key players in the deployment of AI to support the achievement of the sustainable development goals (SDGs). Thus, their capacity to design, finance, and disseminate digital solutions positions them as pivotal agents in accelerating both digital and ecological transitions. This paper aims to provide a structured and practice-oriented synthesis of the literature on the role of AI in supporting corporate contributions to the SDGs by identifying the key opportunities and ethical dilemmas discussed in peer-reviewed research. To this end, a qualitative meta-analysis was conducted on articles indexed in the Scopus database between 2015 and 2025 by mobilizing IRAMUTEQ 0.7 Alpha2, NVivo 12 and Rayyan, we performed text mining and qualitative content analysis to extract and classify relevant contributions. Our findings suggest that corporate AI-related opportunities are mainly associated with operational efficiency, innovation, sustainability performance measurement, and data-driven decision-making, yet they remain marginal compared to broader sustainability discussions. However, AI adoption raises notable challenges, such as data governance issues, organizational resistance, risks of greenwashing and skills constraints. In this regard, our analysis reveals a real empirical gap and lack of field-based studies focusing on how companies operationalize AI to support the SDGs. This gap invites future research to explore these opportunities and challenges through empirical, corporate-level studies that demonstrate how AI can effectively help companies in achieving the SDGs. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Linking multiple sources of performance feedback to firm behavior: the combined effect of technological and financial performance on innovation
abstract: The behavioral theory of the firm proposes that performance feedback based on aspiration gaps influences search behavior. Prior research has focused on testing this proposition predominantly using financial performance, with less consideration of other critical sources of feedback, such as technological performance. We argue that both types of performance feedback jointly influence subsequent innovative activities by providing distinct information regarding how firms should balance their degree of exploration and exploitation. We provide evidence that while financial performance feedback impacts the scope and nature of firms’ exploratory search across technological domains, technological performance feedback influences the types of knowledge leveraged and utilized in the search. In doing so, we contribute by developing theory and evidence for why multiple sources of performance feedback matter in decision making amid uncertain exploratory and exploitation processes and how these sources together affect the behavioral states and the innovation strategy of the firm. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Inside-out and outside-in: How digital capabilities and environmental dynamism shape AI adoption in SMEs
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming the competitive landscape, yet small and medium enterprises (SMEs) vary considerably in whether and how they adopt AI technologies. While prior research has focused on the drivers of AI adoption, it has largely overlooked the interplay between internal capabilities and external pressures and has treated adoption behavior as homogeneous across firms. Addressing this gap, we develop and test a model that explains both the level and heterogeneity of AI adoption through the lenses of dynamic capabilities and strategic fit. Using survey data from 616 Russian SMEs across sectors, we find that digital capabilities and environmental dynamism independently promote AI adoption, but their interaction produces a stronger and more consistent response. Our heteroskedasticity-based analysis shows that each factor independently increases variability in adoption behavior. We also find tentative evidence that the alignment of digital capabilities and environmental dynamism is associated with lower heterogeneity in AI adoption, suggesting that capability–context congruence may promote more consistent adoption behavior. By showing that capability-context alignment may shape both the average level and the dispersion of AI adoption, this study moves AI adoption and digital transformation research beyond mean-centric explanations and clarifies when firms converge on similar AI responses versus diverge in how intensively they adopt AI. We also offer guidance for SME leaders on when to invest in digital capabilities, how to prioritize AI projects, and align AI initiatives under turbulent conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Interfacial charge redistribution regulates surface hydroxyl dynamics during photocatalytic nitric oxide oxidation
abstract: Water can replenish reactive surface hydroxyls during photocatalytic nitric oxide (NO) oxidation, yet excessive hydration blocks adsorption sites. Here, Ag2O was deposited on hydroxyl-rich zinc hydroxystannate (ZnSn(OH)6, ZSOH) to couple interfacial charge transfer with dynamic surface-hydroxyl evolution under visible light. The optimized sample removed 69.8% of NO after 30 min and exhibited repeatable activity over five light-on/off cycles. At relative humidities of 5%, 50%, and 95%, NO removal reached 74.3%, 61.8%, and 51.3%, respectively. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, work-function calculations, and differential charge density revealed electron redistribution from ZSOH to Ag2O, while time-resolved photoluminescence, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and photocurrent measurements demonstrated improved carrier separation and transport. Electron spin resonance detected enhanced formation of photogenerated electrons, •O2−, and •OH. Density functional theory further showed that Ag2O coupling strengthened H2O adsorption and elongated the average adsorbed O-H bond. In-situ infrared spectroscopy revealed irradiation-induced redistribution and depletion of surface hydroxyls, followed by water-driven partial restoration of the O-H environment. These results support an interfacially mediated hydroxyl consumption–regeneration cycle in which charge redistribution promotes carrier utilization and reactive oxygen species generation, whereas adsorbed water restores reactive hydroxyl environments. At high humidity, competitive water adsorption increasingly restricts NO and O2 access. This work identifies interfacial electronic regulation of dynamic surface hydroxyls as a strategy for photocatalytic NO oxidation under variable humidity. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Crowding-in pathways in inclusive agribusiness partnerships: Towards a heuristic for responsible scaling
abstract: CONTEXT: Inclusive agribusiness partnerships (IABs) are widely promoted as vehicles for agricultural transformation yet achieving scale while maintaining inclusion remains a persistent challenge. These challenges highlight the need to understand how inclusive outcomes become embedded and sustained at scale in wider institutional environments. OBJECTIVE: This article develops and empirically grounds a theory-informed typology of ‘crowding-in’ pathways through which external actors adapt their practices in response to partnership-induced innovations. The typology aims to help partnerships recognize and proactively engage with different pathways through which surrounding actors may contribute to their inclusive objectives. We examine how these pathways can contribute to responsible scaling and the conditions under which they are more likely to do so. METHODS: The study follows an abductive action research approach combining a narrative literature review with empirical action research and practitioner engagement. The research was embedded within the 2SCALE program, an agribusiness incubator initiative operating in Sub-Saharan Africa and funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The literature review led to a draft conceptual typology of crowding in pathways, which was empirically validated and refined through analysis of five purposively selected 2SCALE partnerships in Ghana, Kenya, and Nigeria. Data was collected through literature study, interviews, participatory workshops, program document analysis, and longitudinal engagement with partnership actors. RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: We distinguish, for each actor type, between an organizational advantage–driven pathway—where actors crowd in to gain capabilities or capital—and an issue-informed pathway—where actors engage to advance inclusive outcomes. This results in the identification of six crowding-in pathways across business, state, and civil society spheres: competitive, normative, facilitative, dependence, credibility, and re-institutionalization crowding-in. The cases illustrate how external actors from government, business, and civil society adapt business models, infrastructure and extension services, and coordination support, extending inclusive outcomes beyond partnership boundaries. However, crowding-in also introduces risks, including corporate market capture, unequal allocation of public resources, and increased farmer dependence on tightly coupled market actors. We conclude that responsible scaling requires continuous attention to power asymmetries, inclusion criteria, and institutional pluralism. The typology offers both an analytical lens and a practical heuristic to anticipate and steer systemic responses in agricultural systems. SIGNIFICANCE: This study advances understanding of responsible outcome-oriented scaling by shifting attention from the performance of individual partnerships to the wider actor networks and institutional environments through which inclusive outcomes become embedded and sustained at scale. Introducing crowding-in as an analytical heuristic, it provides a heuristic for examining how private, public, and civil society actors contribute to scaling processes beyond project boundaries. The typology supports more anticipatory and strategic engagement with external actors while acknowledging the uncertainty and trade-offs inherent in scaling inclusive agribusiness outcomes. © 2026 The Authors. title: Digital Transformation: Setting the Scene for the Emergence of Service-Dominant Logic (SDL) in the Moroccan Telecommunication Sector
abstract: The advent of digital transformation (DT) has significantly increased the need to adopt new business models that prioritize the generation of collective value for all stakeholders involved. Consequently, Service-Dominant Logic (SDL) has emerged as a cornerstone for understanding and driving DT initiatives, ensuring that technological advancements are effectively utilized to enhance service quality, innovation, and overall organizational performance. Therefore, this study aims to explore how DT can pave the way for the emergence of SDL logic. To achieve this goal, we conducted a qualitative analysis of 12 managers within the Moroccan telecommunication sector. The results indicated that core concepts such as customer centricity, resource integration, value creation, and intangibility are key enablers of DT. However, our study revealed new factors that can promote the DT process through an SDL lens, primarily competitiveness and cost reduction. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Understanding Digital Accounting Adoption in SMEs: A Systematic Literature Review of Influencing Factors, Implementation Challenges, and Research Gaps
abstract: The main objective of this study is to provide a comprehensive overview of the key variables influencing adoption decisions, difficulties encountered during implementation, and important information gaps that need to be filled to guide future research. To guarantee rigor and transparency, the study used a systematic literature review (SLR) methodology in accordance with PRISMA criteria. Between 2012 and 2025, there are 315 peer-reviewed journal publications were found, examined, and condensed into 43 thorough and pertinent articles. The results were categorized and assessed using thematic analysis, with an emphasis on three main themes: gaps in research methodology, implementation difficulties, and influencing factors. The results of this literature study unequivocally show that the human factor and implementation gap must be addressed if SMEs are to fully benefit from accounting digitization. This study has significant limitations because it is a systematic literature review that depends on the availability and scope of published literature. Therefore, it is highly advised that future research directions include conducting longitudinal empirical studies to examine how the implementation of digital accounting systems affects the performance of SME businesses, using a mixed-methods approach to better understand the complexity of implementation challenges. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Risk propagation and vulnerability in the global industrial robot trade network: A cascading failure model with adaptive resilience
abstract: Industrial robots underpin intelligent manufacturing and high-end equipment systems, and the stability of their global trade network is directly related to the continuity of international manufacturing specialization. Existing studies mainly focus on structural evolution and centrality features, while offering insufficient explanation of how risk shocks diffuse along trade relations, why core-node failure triggers cascading effects, and whether adaptive buffering mechanisms exist. This study examines the global industrial robot trade network from 2000 to 2023 and develops an adaptive cascading failure model integrating local buffering, global risk-control potential, technological-industrial support, trade-relationship stability, and supply reallocation. Because trade data cannot separate domestic production, processing trade, and re-exports, the propagation results describe network vulnerability and scenario-based trade vulnerability. The results show that network expansion and densification have generated more complex risk transmission paths; simulated risk diffusion is not determined solely by trade scale but by structural position, accumulated import gaps, and substitution absorption capacity; and adaptive supply reallocation can reduce simulated infection scale in some scenarios but cannot fully eliminate cascading risks caused by core-hub failures. This study provides a new analytical framework for identifying critical risk sources, propagation paths, and resilience enhancement directions. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: A multi-similarity matching framework for remaining useful life prediction based on spatiotemporal health indicators
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is a critical task in prognostics and health management (PHM) of industrial equipment. Health indicator (HI) based RUL prediction methods have attracted increasing attention because they represent equipment degradation using low-dimensional and interpretable trajectories. However, most existing similarity-based methods assess degradation similarity primarily through health indicators, without adequately exploiting temporal degradation characteristics and spatial dependencies among sensor data. Moreover, most methods provide only point estimates, limiting the characterization of prediction uncertainty and prediction reliability. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel RUL prediction framework that performs multi-similarity matching based on spatiotemporal feature representations and HIs. The proposed framework consists of three modules: a degradation trajectory module, a health indicator construction module, and a multi-similarity prediction module. Specifically, the degradation trajectory module utilizes sensor data to construct degradation trajectories and extract temporal and spatial features. Based on the learned degradation trajectories, the health indicator construction module employs a change-point detection method to identify the onset of degradation and generate health indicators, while an offline HI library is established by constructing health indicators from multiple equipments. A multi-similarity matching strategy is developed to estimate the RUL of target equipment, and prediction intervals are constructed to quantify prediction uncertainty. Experimental results on publicly available datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves improved prediction accuracy and robustness compared with existing approaches. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Unpleasant moral memory and the formation of inclusive orientation under incomplete institutional guidance
abstract: Leaders increasingly face decisions about what inclusion requires in settings where formal guidance is incomplete or unevenly applied, a situation this study conceptualizes as institutional ambiguity. While prior research has advanced understanding of inclusive leadership by examining observable behaviors, less is known about how leaders develop the internal orientation that guides judgment under such conditions. Drawing on interviews with senior leaders, this study uses the stimulus–organism–response framework to examine how leaders’ interpretations of past morally unpleasant experiences, in part, shape professional responses to inclusion dilemmas. Our findings show that formative experiences do not directly produce inclusive action. Instead, through reflective interpretation and moral re-encoding, they contribute to the development of an inclusive orientation: an internal moral stance that informs judgment when such guidance is incomplete. This orientation is expressed in practice through a context-sensitive set of interpretive lenses: political sensitivity, moral reasoning, cultural respect, authenticity, and practical feasibility. © 2026 The Authors. title: Evolution and Trends: An Exploratory Review of Business Intelligence Migration to Cloud Computing
abstract: The migration of Business Intelligence (BI) systems to cloud computing is a transformative trend shaping the landscape of information technology. During the period (2014–2025), this transition has resulted in important discoveries in the methodologies and constraints suffered by this area. Our paper examines the existing methodologies guiding BI cloud migration and identifies the key obstacles encountered during the process. By analyzing publications retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, the study explores temporal and geographical trends, synthesizes the most frequently adopted migration approaches, and highlights the most prominent challenges that pose a gap in this area and scientific research is still trying to fill them. The results provide an overview for researchers and practitioners researching the field or seeking to embrace cloud migration, while providing a basis for future research aimed at developing models or strategies for business intelligence migration towards the cloud. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Mapping and mitigating greenhouse gas emissions from urban sewer networks in China
abstract: Urban underground sewer network is the backbone of modern cities, yet its role in global urban carbon metabolism remains a critical blind spot. Here, we establish a bottom-up, province-level accounting framework integrating multi-source socio-environmental datasets to quantify sewer-related greenhouse gas emissions across China's 30 provinces from 2010 to 2023, with projections to 2060 under five mitigation scenarios. The framework disaggregates emissions into five categories, namely leakage, in-sewer CH4 from gravity sewers and rising mains, N2O generation, and electricity consumption for pumping, each estimated using source-specific emission factors derived from the SeweX model and IPCC guidelines. A profound structural transition is revealed: driven by improved sewage collection, leakage-related emissions dropped from 90.3% to 58.3%; however, the expanding and maturing pipe networks inadvertently functioned as vast bioreactors, driving in-sewer process emissions from 9.3% to 38.8%. Spatially, this evolution follows an urban-development gradient, with eastern coastal agglomerations peaking earlier than rapidly developing inland regions. Sensitivity analysis identifies sewage collection rate as the most influential parameter. Emissions intensity strongly correlates with economic development, sewage volume, and pipeline length. Scenario analysis demonstrates that integrating end-of-pipe methane recovery with targeted leakage control offers the highest mitigation potential, reducing emissions by up to 79.2% by 2060 relative to business-as-usual. We further propose a regionally adaptive mitigation portfolio that prioritizes methane recovery in eastern coastal provinces with extensive rising mains and improves sewage collection in northwestern regions with low collection coverage, offering a transferable blueprint for decarbonizing underground infrastructure in rapidly urbanizing regions worldwide. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Processes of multi-system co-evolution: Insights from carbon capture and storage in Norway
abstract: Net-zero solutions such as carbon capture and storage (CCS) require the creation of whole new clusters of innovations rather than “merely” a transition in existing systems or the diffusion of single technologies. While prior work highlights negative cross-system interdependencies (e.g., chicken and egg problems), this paper presents a theorization and an empirical study of the processes of multi-system co-evolution that contribute to the formation and development of multi-system complexes. To do this, a framework that integrates the concepts of a meta-rule, structural couplings (institutional, technological, organizational) and complementarity formation mechanisms — synchronization, amplification, and integration — is developed. The framework is illustrated through a qualitative case study of two Norwegian carbon capture and storage projects, Mongstad (2006–2013) and Longship (2016–), drawing on a broad range of media and documentary sources, including policy documents and funding agreements, and 20 interviews. The analysis shows how, in Longship, actors have sought to realize CCS by, for example, (i) fostering coordination and simultaneous co-development between CCS systems via contracts and standards, (ii) enabling CCS systems to expand and diffuse via a scalable ship-to-terminal transport design; and (iii) creating robustness in CCS multi-system complex by involving multiple actors, user sectors and business cases. This differed from Mongstad, where actors failed to prioritize the management of CCS system couplings and related uncertainties. The paper proposes how the processes of multi-system co-evolution can be conceptualized, and explores how actors may seek to deal with the issue of system interdependencies in sustainability transitions. © 2026 The Authors. title: Perspectives on scaling up clean energy technologies in the energy transition
abstract: Carbon neutrality requires massive, rapid scaling up of clean energy technologies, with economic factors playing a central role in market uptake. We investigate how economic drivers and investment behaviors affect technology growth using a novel, multi-model analytical framework. By combining macro-level cost-driven technology diffusion with micro-level business profitability modeling, this framework captures realistic, investment-centric decision-making. Cost-competitiveness-dependent, varying technology adoption rates realistically reflect market growth and saturation, indicating a declining adoption rate as market share increases. Growth is initially influenced by technical and technoeconomic factors, but shifts toward complex systemic, social, and socioeconomic factors around the inflection point (halfway to saturation). This transition triggers, for instance, when solar PV share reaches around 20% of global electricity. At higher market shares, cost-competitiveness encompasses both basic technology costs and system-level limitations, better captured by the value-adjusted levelized cost of electricity than pure cost. Furthermore, micro-level profitability analysis underlines that sustained scaling up requires adequate business margins and profits. Growth can be accelerated through higher sales margins, reinvesting more profits into investments, reducing the time cash is tied up in sales, etc. Public support speeds up market entry but risks creating unhealthy competition and oversupply if sustained too long. Future technologies benefit from policies supporting a shorter development phase followed by rapid adoption. Finally, insights for future scaling up emphasize low costs, profitability, granularity, modularity, system flexibility, learning and scale effects, and technology-push versus market-pull trade-off. This multitude of factors stresses an integrated, multidisciplinary systems view to accelerate scaling up of clean energy. © 2026 The Author

title: Robust fractional-order automatic differentiation and its applications in neural networks
abstract: Fractional-order automatic differentiation (FAutograd) naturally extends fractional-order gradient descent (FGD) for neural network optimization. It builds on the standard automatic differentiation framework and uses fractional-order matrix differentiation theory. This allows symbolic differentiation based on the Riemann-Liouville derivative to be embedded into computational graphs. It thus fully realizes the potential of FAutograd in neural networks. FGD applies fractional-order differentiation only at the root node. In contrast, FAutograd extends it to intermediate and leaf nodes. This extension amplifies the instability caused by the fractional-order term. This often degrades performance in practice. To address this issue, we introduce an element-wise gradient clipping strategy for the fractional-order term. This strategy directly suppresses the source of instability in fractional-order gradient matrices. As a result, we propose a robust FAutograd method for neural network training. In this paper, we first provide a qualitative analysis of the method at the scalar level. Based on this strategy, we then develop the fractional-order Linear (FLinear) layer, a fundamental building block of FAutograd. We conduct empirical evaluations with this layer on various time series datasets. Experimental results show that FLinear improves both training robustness and evaluation performance. The results also confirm its effectiveness on SOTA baselines. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Fully discrete follow-the-leader approximation of one-dimensional scalar conservation laws with vacuum
abstract: We present a fully discrete particle approximation for one-dimensional scalar conservation laws. Under suitable monotonicity assumptions on the macroscopic velocity, we construct a vacuum-compatible family of time-discrete particle equations and show that an appropriate piecewise-constant density reconstruction from the particle setting converges to the unique entropy weak solution of the macroscopic scalar conservation law. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Mitigating cognitive workload in automated driving takeovers: Effects of non-driving-related tasks, takeover request modalities, and lead times
abstract: In Level 3 conditional automated driving, non-driving-related tasks (NDRTs) may reduce drivers’ readiness to resume control, while behavioral indicators alone may not fully capture concurrent changes in workload and psychophysiological stress. This study examined the effects of NDRT packages, takeover request (TOR) modalities, and TOR lead time (TORlt) on cognitive workload, cardiac responses, gaze behavior, and vehicle-control performance. A within-subject experiment used EEG, eye movements, cardiac interval measures, NASA-TLX, and post-TOR driving indicators. News reading and video watching produced larger post-TOR changes in selected physiological indicators and greater vehicle-control effort than the phone call task, while video watching also resulted in higher subjective workload. Visual TORs were associated with higher subjective workload, altered cardiac interval responses in the primary analysis, and greater control fluctuation than auditory and auditory-visual TORs. Shorter TORlt was associated with greater changes in cardiac interval measures, whereas its relationship with steering corrections was less robust across sensitivity analyses. Physiological and behavioral responses were not always aligned, as drivers sometimes maintained relatively stable vehicle control despite elevated workload or psychophysiological stress. These findings support the value of multimodal driver-state monitoring during takeover transitions. Under the present simulator conditions, auditory and auditory-visual TORs may warrant further evaluation when drivers are engaged in screen-based NDRTs or when lead time is limited. Overall, the results provide preliminary evidence for condition-specific adaptive warning design and suggest that combining physiological, visual-attention, subjective, and vehicle-control indicators may improve the characterization of driver state during automated driving takeovers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Guilt by association: Interpretable multiplex graph learning of accounting-risk contagion
abstract: Severe accounting failures—material internal-control weaknesses, fraudulent restatements, and enforcement actions—are rare, costly, and relational: they cluster along the networks binding firms to common auditors, directors, and owners. We recast next-year failure prediction as node classification on a temporal multiplex firm graph whose layers encode a nested auditor hierarchy, board interlocks, and common ownership, and ask when the graph adds to the node-attribute signal. Methodologically, the usual graph-versus-tabular comparison is unfair: graph models receive node features that the tabular baselines are denied; once equalised, every standard graph network falls behind gradient-boosted trees. Architecturally, we introduce ACE-GNN, a pure multiplex network whose strength comes not from a richer operator—ruled out by a deliberate negative result—but from quantile encoding of node attributes and zero-inflated neighbour-exposure signals. ACE-GNN matches the strongest tabular learner, and a tree handed the same exposures attains near-identical accuracy, so the graph's advantage lies in faithful relation-level explanation, not accuracy. For interpretability, silent failures—firms whose warnings arrive only through their ties—are traced by edge-removal counterfactuals to specific auditor peers. These results delineate when graph-based AI earns its place on relational-but-tabular problems—and when it does not. © 2026

title: From segmentation to simulation: Joint lumbar vertebra-disc segmentation in 3D CT enabling finite element modeling
abstract: Segmentation of lumbar vertebrae and intervertebral discs from three-dimensional computed tomography (CT) is essential for patient-specific reconstruction and downstream finite element analysis (FEA), yet remains challenging because of low soft-tissue contrast, ambiguous vertebra-disc interfaces, and the lack of joint annotations within the same volumes. We propose GSC-DPM, a three-dimensional segmentation framework that combines gated skip connections with a DualPathMamba encoder to jointly capture long-range anatomical context and preserve local boundary details. To enable supervised joint learning, we constructed VID-80 through model-assisted annotation initialization and expert consolidation. The same architecture was first trained separately for vertebra segmentation on CTSpine1K and for disc segmentation on the in-house Shanxi Bethune Hospital Lumbar Disc CT dataset (SBH-LD100; unrelated to LIDC-IDRI), and the resulting candidate masks on independent lumbar CT volumes were subsequently reviewed, merged, corrected, and refined by clinical experts to obtain final joint labels. On VID-80, the final joint model achieved Dice scores of 0.963 ± 0.013 for vertebrae and 0.903 ± 0.011 for discs, with an average Dice of 0.933 ± 0.011 and an average IoU of 0.881 ± 0.021. It also achieved the lowest average HD95 and ASSD of 1.243 ± 0.387 mm and 1.114 ± 0.285 mm, respectively, indicating improved boundary accuracy. Controlled ablation experiments further demonstrated the relative influence of gated fusion, dual-path feature mixing, and encoder depth. In addition, we performed a representative-case segmentation-to-FEA feasibility demonstration using a selected GSC-DPMJ-derived vertebra–disc prediction as the geometric basis for FE preprocessing. The remaining anatomical and mechanical components were introduced during FE construction rather than directly predicted by the network. The representative model produced a converged solution under standard lumbar loading conditions, suggesting preliminary feasibility for downstream FE preprocessing. Code is available at https://github.com/Marcusmakusi0612/medical-images. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: From nature-inspired innovation to nature conservation and restoration financing
abstract: Biomimicry—the practice of emulating nature's time-tested patterns and strategies—has generated transformative innovations across multiple sectors, while the biodiversity crisis is accelerating. This paradox reveals an innovation debt to nature: humanity increasingly benefits from ecosystems’ intellectual capital, while ongoing ecological degradation erodes the very knowledge base upon which future innovations depend. Grounded in the semiconducting principle—which permits environmental value to generate monetary gains while rejecting the use of monetary gains to offset or compensate for environmental degradation—this perspective proposes a profit-sharing mechanism designed to redirect socio-economic systems toward activities aligned with ecological thresholds and long-term sustainability. Specifically, the proposed mechanism channels a portion of revenues or profits derived from biomimicry-based innovations toward conservation and restoration activities, thereby helping address the biodiversity finance gap and fostering an eco-surplus culture in which business success and ecological regeneration mutually reinforce one another. In doing so, it creates a positive feedback loop: the more humanity innovates through nature, the more it contributes to sustaining and regenerating it. © 2026 Elsevier GmbH
