title: Integrated energy recovery assessment from municipal wastewater treatment plants: a comparative techno-economic and risk study of activated sludge and UASB systems for electricity, biomethane, and hydrogen using the SIAELA and SIATER software
abstract: Municipal wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) hold substantial untapped energy-recovery potential through biogas valorization into electricity, biomethane, or hydrogen. This study presents the first systematic, integrated techno-economic and probabilistic risk assessment comparing two dominant treatment technologies, the Upflow Anaerobic Sludge Blanket (UASB) reactor and the Activated Sludge System (ALS) with anaerobic sludge digestion, applied to Itajubá, Minas Gerais, Brazil (93,073 inhabitants). Two purpose-built, INPI-registered platforms were used: SIATER v2.0 (BR512026004510-0) for UASB and SIAELA v2.0 (BR512026004511-8) for ALS, each integrating eight modules from population projection to Monte Carlo risk analysis (5,000 simulations) and financial-leverage optimization. The ALS generates 3.9 times more methane (1,410 vs. 362 m3CH4/d) and 2.4 times more electricity, with an LCOE of US$0.276/kWh (UASB) vs. US$0.223/kWh (ALS). SMR hydrogen costs US$8.96–9.56/kg, above fossil parity (US$1.91/kg). Even with voluntary carbon credits (VCS AMS-I.D), neither route reaches a positive NPV: the best SIATER case (grid metering plus carbon) gives NPV = −US$210,720 (IRR = 6.82%; PB = 10.7 yr). CAPEX dominates risk in both systems (Spearman ρ = −0.94 for SIATER; −0.80 for SIAELA). Scale-sensitivity analysis (20,000–1,000,000 inhabitants) shows that neither route reaches a positive NPV at any scale under the Fisher hurdle rate; the UASB route's IRR rises with scale but never reaches the 24.71% MARR, whereas the ALS approaches grid-parity LCOE only at large scale. Results guide utility planners pursuing energy self-sufficiency in mid-sized Brazilian municipalities. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Diffusion-based cross-modal generation for audio-driven facial expression and emotion recognition
abstract: The combination of speech signals and facial expressions can be very useful for the research. If facial expressions can be developed using speech signals, then it will be very easy to recognize the state of human. Generation of facial expressions from audio signals required a cross model correlation. There are some predefined methods which are not very robust as represented in existing results. This paper proposes a framework based on Diffusion-based Contrastive Learning with Multimodal Fusion (DCL-MF). The framework can generate facial expressions as well as emotion recognition. In order to enable robust and discriminative cross-modal feature learning, the suggested framework uses different learning to align audio and visual representations within a shared emotion-aware latent space. A diffusion-based generative model gradually synthesizes high-fidelity and temporally coherent facial expressions driven by speech signals, trained on these aligned embeddings. To further improve emotion recognition performance, a multimodal fusion module combines audio messages with the generated facial features. Benchmark audio-visual emotion datasets such as CREMA-D, RAVDESS, and IEMOCAP are used to assess the efficacy of the suggested DCL-MF framework. Through typical emotion recognition accuracies of 82.6% on CREMA-D, 85.1% on RAVDESS, and 78.4% on IEMOCAP an improvement of 3%–6% over current baselines—experimental results show that DCL-MF consistently outperforms state-of-the-art techniques. Additionally, better Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) scores, which show more realistic and emotionally consistent facial dynamics, demonstrate that the suggested model achieves superior facial expression generation quality. These findings demonstrate that the suggested DCL-MF framework is efficient and scalable for audio-driven affective computing applications by combining diffusion-based generation with contrastive cross-modal alignment, which greatly improves both facial expression synthesis and emotion recognition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Harnessing Big Data for Sustainable Global Supply Chains: Challenges and Opportunities in Indonesia’s Export-Oriented Sectors
abstract: Using big data is essential to increasing the global supply chain’s sustainability and efficiency in the digital age. However, adopting big data technology in sustainable supply chains is hampered by the limitations of technological infrastructure and a lack of workforce expertise in data analytics. The purpose of this study is to identify factors that influence big data adoption and analyze its impact on supply chain sustainability. This study uses a mixed method with the population made up of businesses that have implemented big data in their supply chain management through the use of the Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) technique. Data were collected through a survey of 400 respondents with a purposive sampling technique, and analyzed using thematic analysis and SWOT through in-depth inter-views with 20 agricultural production managers. The results of the study show that technological readiness and policy support from the government have a significant influence on big data adoption, while budget constraints and lack of digital skills are the main obstacles. Strategies that can be implemented include improving digital infrastructure, HR training, and cross-sector collaboration. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Sustainability and Emerging Issues in the Cooperative Sector: Evidence from Iloilo, Philippines
abstract: This study investigates the sustainability challenges and emerging trends influencing the cooperative sector in Iloilo Province and City, Philippines, over the past 5 years, situating local experiences within global cooperative discourse. Using a qualitative case study design, data were gathered from 25 purposively selected key informants, including cooperative development specialists, managers, officers, and members, through in-depth interviews and focus group discussions. Thematic analysis revealed four persistent issues that constrain cooperative sustainability: taxation, governance, membership engagement, and technological adaptation. Taxation concerns revolve around inconsistent regulatory requirements and threats to long-standing privileges under the TRAIN Law, while governance issues highlight leadership monopolies and weak succession planning. Membership apathy and limited participation undermine accountability, and technological gaps limit efficiency and transparency. At the same time, four notable trends were identified: a growing recognition of cooperatives as economic contributors, diversification into innovative and nontraditional businesses, increased adoption of insurance and risk management mechanisms, and strengthened gender and development initiatives that enhance inclusivity. The findings underscore the dual reality of cooperatives as both challenged and resilient institutions that continue to advance equity, social justice, and inclusive economic development. The Iloilo experience offers valuable lessons for policy reform, governance innovation, and sustainability strategies applicable to cooperatives globally. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: LLM-Assisted Logic Rule Learning: Scaling Human Expertise for Time Series Anomaly Detection in Supply Chain Management
abstract: Time series anomaly detection is critical for supply chain management to take proactive operations, but faces challenges: classical unsupervised anomaly detection based on exploiting data patterns often yields results misaligned with business requirements and domain knowledge, while manual expert analysis cannot scale. We propose a framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to systematically encode human expertise into interpretable, logic-based rules for detecting anomalies in supply chain time series data. Distinct from direct LLM deployment, our approach utilizes LLMs to generate and iteratively optimize deterministic rules offline. Deployed at Amazon for monitoring millions of individual products, our approach achieves detection accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art multimodal LLMs while delivering 1) orders of magnitude faster execution with 2) zero inference API costs in production. This establishes a scalable paradigm for bridging expert-driven decision-making with automated production systems, eliminating the latency and stochasticity barriers of direct LLM deployment. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The Influence of Social Capital on the Performance of Women Entrepreneurs Through the Mediating Role of Innovation and Knowledge Sharing in Special Region of Yogyakarta
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of social capital on the entrepreneurial performance of women in the Special Region of Yogyakarta Province, with innovation and knowledge sharing as mediators. A quantitative approach was applied using a cross-sectional survey of 422 women entrepreneurs through non-probability sampling. The results show that social capital has a positive and significant effect on entrepreneurial performance, both directly and indirectly through innovation and knowledge sharing. Regression analysis reveals that social networks, trust, and shared norms open up access to resources and opportunities, as well as encourage the exchange of knowledge and innovative practices that strengthen business competitiveness. The Sobel test confirms the significant role of innovation and knowledge sharing as mediators. These findings emphasize the importance of social capital in supporting the sustainability of women’s entrepreneurial performance and provide theoretical contributions by integrating the perspectives of social capital, innovation, and knowledge sharing, as well as practical implications for policymakers and the business community in strengthening an equitable entrepreneurial ecosystem. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Evaluation of Prompt Engineering for LLM-Based Construction Contract Risk Analysis
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show increasing potential for complex analytical tasks; however, their reliability in high-stakes domains such as construction contract interpretation remains insufficiently understood. This study presents a controlled, human-in-the-loop evaluation of how prompt-engineering strategies influence the quality and perceived reliability of LLM-generated risk analyses for New Engineering Contract (NEC4)-style clauses. Generative pretrained transformer GPT-4.1 was applied in a deterministic configuration to identify contractor risks across six synthetic NEC4-style Z-clauses using five prompt strategies: baseline, direct, role based, chain of thought, and guided prompting. Thirty outputs were evaluated under a blinded protocol against expert-derived reference risk lists by a mixed-expertise cohort, supporting exploratory comparison. Assessment combined descriptive quantitative analysis of Likert-scale ratings of accuracy, completeness, clarity, legal salience, and hallucination risk with qualitative thematic analysis. Results indicate that guided, clause-anchored prompting produced more structured, legally grounded, and traceable outputs, whereas less constrained strategies exhibited narrative drift and weaker clause linkage. These findings suggest that structured prompting may support more consistent clause-level interpretation under controlled conditions, although conclusions remain bounded by the exploratory design, limited sample, and synthetic dataset. The study contributes to understanding how prompt design shapes interpretability and verifiability in contract analysis. The clause-guided human-in-the-loop (CG-HITL) framework is presented as a conceptual approach to support structured use of LLMs in preaward contract risk assessment. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Decoding Netflix: An Explainable AI Approach to Analyze Customer Churn and Content Preferences
abstract: Due to the wide range of services provided by Over-The-Top (OTT) platforms, they are becoming a popular choice among customers. Some of the popular OTT platforms include Netflix, Amazon Prime, Hotstar, Hulu, JioCinema, Zee5, and SonyLiv, to name a few. In this paper, we perform Customer Churn and Content Strategy Analysis for Netflix by leveraging data analytics, machine learning, and business intelligence to enhance customer retention and optimize content strategy. By analyzing user behavior, subscription trends, and engagement metrics, this paper aims to develop a predictive churn model that identifies customer retention strategies. Additionally, the study evaluates content performance, genre preferences, and regional trends to suggest data-driven decisions for content acquisition and production. Further analysis using ensemble Machine Learning models, including XGBoost, CatBoost, Random Forest, and AdaBoost, has also been done. SHAP analysis indicates that Average watch time per day and watch hours contribute the most to the Netflix customer churn. The insights derived will enable Netflix and other OTT service providers to improve user engagement, reduce churn rates, and maximize revenue through a more targeted and efficient content strategy. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Association of observed ramp-electrification status with APU runtime and turnaround performance: A staggered difference-in-differences analysis at a tropical ASEAN hub
abstract: Ramp electrification can reduce aircraft auxiliary power unit (APU) use during turnaround, but operational evidence from tropical airports remains limited and sensitive to treatment-timing and implementation definitions. This study presents a replacement reanalysis of 7122 de-identified turnarounds across 20 stands at a tropical ASEAN hub from 1 March to 28 June 2025. Fourteen stands exhibited an observed transition to active treatment status, six remained never observed treated, and five first-observed treatment-date groups were identified. Because official commissioning records were unavailable, treatment timing was defined by the first observed active-treatment timestamp rather than independently certified go-live dates. A cohort-by-event interaction regression incorporated stand and calendar-date fixed effects and adjusted for aircraft body class, carrier, time of day, wet-day status, temperature, relative humidity, and rainfall. Supported post-treatment cohort-event coefficients were aggregated using cell-count weights, yielding a turnaround-weighted post-treatment estimand across the realized distribution of observed post-treatment turnarounds. Inference used CR1 stand-clustered covariance and a 9999-replication restricted-residual wild-cluster bootstrap- t . Observed treatment status was associated with a 5.874 min/turn reduction in APU runtime (95% CI −6.586 to −5.162; p < 0.001; wild-bootstrap p = 0.0001), approximately 32.0% of the eventually treated pretreatment mean. At 6.5 kg CO2e/min, this corresponds to 38.18 kg/turn of gross avoided APU-related CO2e, a deterministic transformation rather than a net-emissions estimate. Average turnaround time was +0.657 min/turn (95% CI −0.539 to 1.853; p = 0.281; wild-bootstrap p = 0.353), with variation across group-specific estimates, including +6.15 min/turn for the single-stand second treatment group; these differences are interpreted cautiously because post-treatment support and follow-up varied across groups. Joint pretreatment tests were not statistically significant for APU runtime ( p = 0.157) or turnaround time ( p = 0.528), although the earliest pooled APU lead was individually positive. The findings support a consistent association between observed electrification status and lower APU runtime while requiring caution regarding counterfactual comparability, causal interpretation, operational variation, and net-carbon interpretation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Who will I be? Refugee entrepreneurship and founder identity
abstract: We conducted a 27-month field study of 23 North Korean Defector (NKD) founders. Founders responded in three different ways to the disparaging default social identities they encountered by self-categorizing into three “avowed” social identities, which served as aspirations for how they would build their ventures. Founders generated sensemaking narratives that explained their behavior – to themselves and to others – by anchoring on the past, present, or future circumstances and claiming individual capabilities to build their ventures. The resulting ventures were characterized by distinctive missions, branding, and hiring preferences and therefore by patterned differences in the roles founders played. We contribute to scholarly understanding of refugee entrepreneurship by showing that the ways in which refugee founders respond to being in a new country and constructing new identities is more varied – because it is embedded in their responses to local social evaluations – than prior research has portrayed. We contribute to the development of founder identity theory (FIDT) by expanding prior understanding of how social identities drive founder role creation. Overall, we show the extension of refugee founder agency as they move from self-categorizing into avowed social identities to embedding themselves in the concrete social relations required to perform a role. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Anchored FLoE: A Business-Guardrailed Ensemble Framework of Foundation and Local-Trained Models for Demand Forecasting
abstract: Accurate demand forecasting is vital for retail supply chain efficiency, yet a persistent trust-capacity gap limits industrial production to low-capacity interpretable models that fail to capture complex market dynamics. We propose Anchored FLoE, a dual-model framework that bridges this gap by fusing high-capacity deep learning with rigorous business guardrails. The framework integrates: (1) FLoE, an ensemble merging a frozen Time Series Foundation Model (Chronos-2) for global generalization with a Local Specialist (TFT) for domain-specific patterns; and (2) a model-agnostic Anchor Layer that enforces economic monotonicity and business-logic consistency through discount-segmented confidence bands. Validated across 524 product-market segments, Anchored FLoE achieves an 11-percentage-point improvement in sales-weighted MAPE over production baselines, translating to a multi-million dollar impact on free cash flow. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The Art of Data: A Bibliometric Analysis on Digital Accounting, Big Data Analytics, and Digital Literacy for Sustainability Performance (2015–2025)
abstract: This study examines research trends, publications and citation patterns, country contributions, research themes, keywords, and emerging research related to digital accounting, big data analytics, and digital literacy to support sustainability performance, and what gaps can be identified for future research toward sustainability performance, through a bibliometric analysis approach utilizing the Biblioshiny tool. This study used 280 Scopus-indexed articles published from 2015 to 26 June 2025. The findings show an increasing research trend, with the highest number of publications in 2024 (90 articles). The most cited article was titled “Smart Circular Economy: A Digital-Enabled Circular Strategies Framework for Manufacturing” with 510 citations. Researcher Kumar A has the highest productivity (six publications). Moreover, India and China were the leading contributors with 104 and 81 articles. Finally, the thematic map shows that big data analytics, digital literacy, and sustainability performance are basic themes, whereas digital accounting is an emerging theme. Further research suggests exploring digital accounting, especially its integration with digital literacy, big data analytics, and sustainability performance. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Synthetic Scenario Methodology (SSM): An AI-Driven Approach for Strategic Business Insights
abstract: Data functions as a strategic business resource while simultaneously creating operational limitations in the current business world. The traditional collection process faces delays because of regulatory restrictions, high costs, privacy issues and insufficient insurance coverage for unusual yet essential occurrences. The paper presents the Synthetic Scenario Methodology (SSM) as an AI-based approach which studies synthetic datasets by applying structured artefact analysis instead of using them as brief replacements. The Business Context Blueprints (BCB) and Strategic Rules Matrices (SRM) enable SSM to produce synthetic scenarios which maintain transparency and auditability and allow for calibration adjustments. The process consists of four stages which include blueprinting followed by rules specification and then iterative generation and testing. The Human–AI Hypothetical Data Comparison Instrument (H-AI HDCI) achieves calibration through a dual approach that merges expert assessments with divergence mapping to validate findings. The worked example shows how SSM enables business risk planning through its structured outcome ranges which replace traditional single-point forecasts for leaders. The SSM method enables organizations to detect potential disruptions through assumption documentation and future scenario development which leads to shock anticipation strategy development and decision-making improvement. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Hybrid Leadership in the Age of the Metaverse: Navigating Between Physical and Virtual Workplaces
abstract: The swift advancement of digital technologies, propelled by worldwide disruptions including the COVID-19 pandemic, has transformed organizational operations and the dynamics of leader-team interactions. With businesses’ growing adoption of hybrid work models, a novel leadership paradigm is taking shape, necessitating the capacity to lead effectively in both physical and virtual environments. The emergence of the Metaverse introduces significant potential for enhancing workplace interaction, providing immersive and persistent digital environments that fundamentally alter collaboration, communication, and organizational culture. This study investigates the notion of hybrid leadership within the framework of the Metaverse, analyzing the strategies leaders can employ to adeptly manage the convergence of physical office environments and virtual work settings. This study synthesizes current literature, industry practices, and theoretical frameworks to delineate the essential competencies for effective hybrid leadership in an evolving context. The identified competencies encompass digital fluency, emotional intelligence, inclusivity, and sustaining trust and engagement within decentralized, technology-driven contexts. This study further examines the challenges leaders encounter, including digital fatigue, ethical considerations, and technological disparities, while emphasizing opportunities such as the integration of global talent, gamified learning approaches, and data-driven decision-making processes. This study presents strategic recommendations to equip current and future leaders to navigate immersive hybrid work environments. It underscores the significance of adaptability, ongoing learning, and ethical digital leadership. This paper posits that successful hybrid leadership in the context of the Metaverse transcends the mere management of tools; it necessitates a redefinition of leadership paradigms to align with a digitally integrated future. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: From Prediction to Actionable Insight: A Hybrid Machine Learning Framework with Explainable AI for Proactive Customer Churn Management
abstract: In the competitive telecommunications industry, customer churn is an area that requires proactive daily management as it has the highest impact on profitability. While predictive machine learning has dominantly achieved high predictive capability, the “black box” nature of such models has historically hampered the generation of actionable insights, thus resulting in a disconnect between predictions and resultant business activities. This research attempts to bridge this gap by developing and operationalizing a unique integrative paradigm that combines high-performance predictive models with cutting-edge explanatory AI (XAI) methods. We conduct an extensive model evaluation and comparison of four machine learning models (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and CatBoost) on the publicly available Telco Customer Churn dataset. Our proposed methodology relies on extensive hyperparameter tuning and class imbalance handling, as well as post-hoc model interpretation methods such as SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) which helps in globally and locally attributing features to model outputs. Our findings suggest that the CatBoost model post hyperparameter tuning exhibited the greatest predictive power (AUC = 0.839). Most importantly, SHAP analysis provides actionable insights by uncovering intricate and nonlinear drivers of customer churn that can assist in designing targeted customer retention strategies. Finally, we introduce a cost-benefit simulation model that monetizes the economic impact of using the framework, with up to 5 times ROI versus untargeted campaigns. This paper contributes a novel, end-to-end method for translating predictive models into interpretable, actionable, and financially viable business assets. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Harnessing AI for Real-Time Financial Data Analysis and Automated Decision-Making
abstract: The concept of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing the paradigm of the financial sphere because it is engaged in the analysis of real-time data and in automated decision-making. The article addresses the ways in which AI technologies, such as machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, big data analytics, etc., may revolutionize financial forecasting, fraud detection, algorithmic trading, risk management, and strategic planning. The research refines the fact through the analysis of the existing methodologies and practice of the implementation of AI that increases the speed, accuracy, and size of financial insights. It also evaluates the quality of data, explicability and ethical concerns of AI-driven financial systems. The paper provides an overview of how AI can be utilized to create intelligent, adaptable, and sustainable financial systems by adjusting dynamically in response to market shifts and customer needs through the thorough analysis of the existing literature and frameworks. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The Path to Venture Creation: A Moderated Mediation Model of Entrepreneurial Alertness, Intention, and Education on Entrepreneurial Behavior
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between entrepreneurial alertness, intention, behavior, and education directly and indirectly. Also, how these variables may influence the actions and behaviors of aspiring entrepreneurs in Saudi Arabia as an emerging economy. Based on multiple theoretical views involves the Theory of Planned Behavior, Human Capital Theory, and Alertness Theory. The total participants are 405 aspiring entrepreneurs. We performed Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling using Smart PLS 4. The results discovered that entrepreneurial alertness has a positive and significant correlation with individual entrepreneurial intention and behavior. Also, the mediation role of Entrepreneurial intention was confirmed in this model. Likewise, this paper validated Entrepreneurial education as significant moderating construct on the impact of Entrepreneurial alertness on the proposed outcomes. This paper adds to the lack but increasing studies on entrepreneurial actions of aspiring entrepreneurs in an emerging country by providing context-specific understandings into the role of number individual level variables in linking cognitive and behavioral shortcomings in entrepreneurship. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: International Investment in the Age of Sustainability: ESG Drivers, Challenges, and Future Research Agenda
abstract: Given the increasing importance of sustainable development considerations, the success of foreign direct investments FDIs is largely linked to other factors beyond value creation and project potential, namely ESG compliance. The literature addressing the intersection of corporate foreign investment and ESG remains very limited, necessitating more scholarly attention to unveil how ESG factors advance foreign direct investments FDI. This paper aims, therefore, to provide a comprehensive overview of the ESG–FDI nexus by examining existing insights, identifying key challenges, and defining promising avenues for future research. We provide policymakers, investors, and managers with important implications to focus on sustainability-driven investments and ESG disclosure frameworks, as these are transforming the current global investment landscape. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The Landscape of Eco-Tourism in Rajasthan: Challenges and Prospects
abstract: Eco-tourism is a type of tourism which has emerged out of a desire to move toward more sustainable forms. While combining economic and cultural development, at the same time caring for the environment. In Rajasthan, a state renowned for its culture and multi-locational landscapes, eco-tourism could very well lead to sustainable growth. The aim is to relieve over-tourism and environmental degradation. This paper provides an overview on contemporary trends in eco-tourism in Rajasthan, listing majors destinations such as Sariska Tiger Reserve, Keoladeo National Park and desert eco-camps. It discusses activities by local communities, government agencies and private companies in green tourism. Eco-tourism in Rajasthan has developed greatly, as the report shows. This was done despite a poor transport infrastructure, an unfuzzy attitude on the part of both townies and tourists, achieving a balance of environmental sustainability with the growth and use of eco-tourism and so forth other challenges. But there are also some fairly positive gaps that need to be filled. These gaps revolve around technological improvement for marketing purposes, local community participation in eco-tourism programs, a mechanism which gets revenue back into the hands of poor people and assistance provided to individual households in the marketing of handmade items. Potential trends like community-based tourism and digital marketing could further underpin eco-tourism in Rajasthan. Finally, the study ends and offers some attitudes with respect to how to promote eco-tourism in Rajasthan. Ways sit astride capacity building, awareness raising through education and social media and getting involved in businesses never before ventured into. It makes the point very clearly that in order to make eco-tourism happen for Rajasthan, one needs to bring in business people, planners and local people together. This way everyone benefits and the air remains fresh. It is also important to consider future researching routes, which can determine how unsustainable eco-tourism is for the surrounding environment and economy. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Reducing the weighted tool replacement problem to min-cost flow on a linear-size graph
abstract: We study the Weighted Tool Replacement Problem (WTRP), where a fixed sequence of n jobs must be processed using a tool magazine of capacity C, and each tool is associated with insertion and deletion costs. Our main contribution is a new exact reduction of WTRP to a min-cost flow problem that avoids the quadratic-size network of the classical Privault-Finke construction (with running time O(C3n2)). Starting from a packing formulation of WTRP, we build a flow network with O(n) nodes and O(Cn) arcs, yielding a polynomial-time algorithm with running time O(C2n+Cnlogn). Computational experiments show speedups of at least one order of magnitude over established exact approaches for WTRP, including the Privault-Finke method and the algorithm of Crama. Finally, we embed the proposed flow-based routine into a state-of-the-art heuristic for the Job Sequencing and Tool Switching Problem (SSP), thereby extending it to weighted replacement costs. Compared to natural Integer Linear Programming (ILP) formulation adapted to the weighted setting, the resulting method achieves substantially improved objective values on large instances, with improvements of up to 4.2× under identical time limits. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: The Role of Explainable AI in Enhancing Investment Decisions and Risk Management in Financial Markets
abstract: Financial markets are becoming increasingly complex, creating an urgent demand for transparent and reliable decision-support systems. This study investigates the role of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in enhancing investment decision-making and risk management between 2020 and 2025. The analysis focuses on four dimensions: reducing decision-making time, mitigating financial risks, improving the quality of investment choices, and strengthening investor confidence. Secondary data from official reports and industry case studies were analyzed using paired T-tests, Value at Risk (VaR) comparisons, Sharpe and Sortino ratios, and regression models. The results demonstrate that decision-making time was significantly reduced after the adoption of XAI, showing its capacity to accelerate execution without compromising accuracy. Portfolio stability improved as indicated by lower VaR levels, while risk-adjusted returns, measured by Sharpe and Sortino ratios, showed significant gains, confirming better investment outcomes. Investor confidence was also positively linked to interpretability, underscoring the importance of transparency in fostering trust. Collectively, these findings position XAI as a catalyst for efficiency, stability, and trust in financial markets, while future research should extend the analysis to emerging markets and explore alternative interpretability methods. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Human-Centered Pedagogies in the Business Management Curriculum of State Universities and Colleges (SUCs)
abstract: This study analyzed the role of AI in the curriculum of Philippine State Universities and Colleges (SUCs) business management through a qualitative Delphi approach. As AI takes hold in higher education, technology must be balanced with empathy to benefit public universities. Academics specializing in curriculum, education, and AI responded to three rounds of Delphi surveys to achieve a commonality in integrating AI. Themes of convergence were faculty development, the need for infrastructure, and ethics. Consensus was reached regarding modular design and participatory planning, but views were divided around institutional autonomy and faculty decision-making roles. Based on the study, AI must augment values-driven education rather than replace it, through the development of specific policies, stakeholder participation, and targeted capacity development. These results form the basis of curriculum innovation in SUCs and inform the discourse around responsible AI in education. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The Impact of Big Data Analysis on Claims Management in Jordanian Insurance Companies
abstract: The aim of the research is to demonstrate the impact of big data analytics (quantitative analysis, qualitative analysis) on claims management in Jordanian insurance companies. To achieve the research objectives, the descriptive analytical approach was used. The study population consisted of (20) insurance companies. (240) electronic questionnaires were distributed to the targeted companies, and (229) questionnaires were collected. (3) questionnaires were excluded due to similarity in answers, so the number of questionnaires became (226). These questionnaires were analyzed on the (SPSS) software. The research summarized a number of results, the most important of which was the presence of a positive and significant impact of big data analytics (quantitative analysis, qualitative analysis) on claims management in Jordanian insurance companies. The study recommended enhancing the role of big data analysis to improve performance and expedite the claims process. This goal aims to achieve customer satisfaction, which contributes to improving the company’s public image and enhancing its competitiveness in local and global markets through the adoption of modern and advanced technologies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Fecal Immunochemical Test-based Versus Total Colonoscopy-Based Colorectal Cancer Screening in Japan: A Microsimulation Study
abstract: Objectives Colorectal cancer is a major public health concern with a high mortality rate. Fecal immunochemical tests (FIT) and total colonoscopy (TCS) are recommended screening methods; however, their cost-effectiveness varies by country. This study addressed the lack of comprehensive cost-effectiveness analyses comparing TCS with the current FIT-based screening in Japan. Methods We developed a microsimulation-based decision analytic model to compare FIT-based screening (current practice) with TCS-based screening (alternative) in a hypothetical cohort of 10 000 Japanese adults over a 60-year period. The analysis was conducted from the healthcare payer perspective, with both costs and health outcomes discounted annually by 2%. We adhered to the 2022 Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards reporting guidelines and incorporated Japan-specific data on costs, participation rates, and disease progression. Results In the base-case analysis, FIT-based screening was more cost-effective than TCS-based screening. TCS-based screening also yielded fewer quality-adjusted life-years, making it the less favorable approach. Sensitivity analyses showed that FIT remained the dominant screening across most parameter variations. Conclusions In Japan, the current FIT-based colorectal cancer screening is more cost-effective than TCS-based screening. Efforts should focus on improving FIT program participation to achieve greater public health benefits, rather than transitioning to a costlier and less effective alternative. © 2026 The Authors.

title: An LLM-Based Agentic Framework for Industrial Forecasting Workflows
abstract: Demand forecasting at Amazon Devices requires predicting demand for hundreds of ASINs (Amazon Standard Identification Numbers) across regions and channels to support inventory, supply chain, and pricing decisions under strong business pressure to reduce cost, increase sales, and react quickly to changes in consumer behavior. Existing workflows rely on manual, bespoke pipelines for data exploration, feature engineering, model selection, and evaluation, which limits experiment throughput and reuse. We present an agentic framework for forecasting workflows, built on an internal machine learning platform that exposes tools via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and is accessed through Kiro CLI. A central LLM-based orchestrator plans and executes end-to-end workflows by invoking MCP tools for profiling, EDA, feature engineering, model training, and evaluation, including specialized agent skills that compute the M5 competition metric and internal business metrics such as wMAPE and bias. On the M5 benchmark and analogous internal workloads, the agentic pipeline achieves forecast quality close to strong manual baselines while substantially outperforming an AutoML baseline, at a fraction of the expert effort required for manual pipelines. We describe how this changes experimentation and review practices in production settings, and where human domain expertise remains essential. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Distributed gradient descent algorithm for robust kernel-based regression
abstract: In this paper, we study the theoretical underpinning of a gradient descent algorithm with a robust loss function in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) framework. We introduce a novel auxiliary sequence for the error analysis and improve the previous convergence results when the regression function does not lie in the RKHS. Under the universal assumptions, we establish the optimal rates of convergence for distributed robust gradient descent algorithm in both cases where the regression function is inside and outside the RKHS, provided the number of partition is not too large. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Liouville-type theorem for the stationary generalized SQG system
abstract: In this note, we study the stationary generalized SQG system in R2 with α∈[1/2,1) and β∈[1/2,1). We prove a Liouville theorem under the finite fractional energy condition θ∈Ḣα(R2). When the parameters satisfy 3α+2β<3 the energy alone forces θ≡0; otherwise a supplementary Lq condition with 2≤q<1/(α+β−1) is sufficient. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: MambaFusion: Registration-assisted lumbar CT-MRI image fusion via Mamba and dynamic feature modeling
abstract: Medical images play a pivotal role in clinical diagnosis, yet a single imaging modality often fails to provide complete anatomical and pathological information. Multimodal image fusion addresses this limitation by integrating complementary information from different modalities. In this study, a CT-MRI registration and preprocessing procedure was first introduced to reduce spatial mismatch between lumbar CT and MRI images. The MRI volume was registered and resampled into the CT coordinate space, ensuring spatial consistency before image fusion. Landmark-based registration evaluation across 30 patients showed that the mean target registration error (TRE) decreased from 26.725 ± 0.847 mm after geometry-based initialization to 2.808 ± 0.983 mm after final rigid registration, corresponding to an 89.49% reduction. Based on the registered CT-MRI image pairs, this study proposes MambaFusion, a novel multimodal medical image fusion model that integrates Mamba sequence modeling with dynamic convolution for enhanced feature extraction and reconstruction. In addition, a Dynamic Feature Fusion Module (DFFM) is designed to improve cross-modal representation learning by enhancing texture details and cross-modal correlations. Experiments on registered lumbar CT-MRI images demonstrate that MambaFusion achieves competitive visual quality and quantitative fusion performance compared with existing methods. The fused images preserve CT-derived vertebral bone structures while retaining MRI-derived soft-tissue information, providing a complementary multimodal representation for lumbar spine imaging. The code is available at https://github.com/Marcusmakusi0612/MambaMIF. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Business Intelligence as a Strategic Tool for Enhancing Employee Engagement and Organizational Efficiency
abstract: This study quantitatively examined the strategic impact of Business Intelligence (BI) adoption on employee engagement and organizational efficiency with Gender as a potential moderating factor. To test the hypotheses, regression analysis showed that BI adoption had a significant effect on employee engagement (R =.585) and organizational efficiency (R =.558). The findings indicate that making informed decisions based on data, and having the relevant information available, such as real-time data from BI dashboards, facilitates employee empowerment and simplifies processes, resulting in enhanced engagement and productivity. While the original hypotheses were intended to include Gender as a moderator, moderation analyses were provided for H3 and H4. There’s a contradiction: the gender has a positive interaction with the main BI impact on engagement effect, but when it comes to organizational efficiency as a whole, it shows a negative effect, so gender does not moderate the relationship between BI adoption and organizational efficiency. Clarify the coding (e.g., Female = 0, Male = 1 if you claim a stronger effect for females) and report the simple slopes with their standard errors and p-values (Female β = 1.3288; Male β = 0.7222) so the interpretation is verifiable. However, gender was determined not to be an important moderator for the BI adoption-organizational efficiency relationship. The study suggests that larger firms, with their increased resources and formalized processes, are likely to derive more value from BI, which contributes to the justification for a size-specific BI strategy. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Tensor-TimesFM: High-Dimensional Sparse Time Series Forecasting with Tensor Decoders and Latent Dynamics Prediction
abstract: Time-series forecasting in business domains—such as markets, finance, and the broader economy—is challenging due to sparsity, high cross-sectional dimensionality, and temporal skewness with short or irregular histories. These issues cause standard forecasting algorithms to perform poorly. We address these challenges with two key innovations: tensor reconstruction and forecasting in a latent factor space. Tensor-TimesFM couples low-rank tensor completion with a pretrained foundation model applied to latent factors. The tensor component leverages low-rank techniques to denoise and impute at scale, while the foundation model utilizes its strong generalization and zero-shot capabilities to model temporal dynamics. Together, they transform the cross-sectional prediction task into a standard tensor reconstruction problem. We further introduce a regularizer that promotes decorrelation among the generated latent factors and aligns with current foundation models designed for univariate time series. On sparse EPS data, Tensor-TimesFM improves over Tensor-GRU, reducing up to 35.2% forecast error and improving out-of-sample R2 by 39.8%. Code is available at https://github.com/LarryC01/Tensor-TimesFM-ECML-2026. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: When Data Science Optimizes Email Marketing: Financial Impacts of More Targeted and Effective Strategies
abstract: Big Data is transforming the way businesses make decisions and operate. The ability to analyze large amounts of data can reveal trends and patterns that were previously undetectable, leading to new business opportunities and improved decision making. Data analysis allows email marketers to create more targeted and relevant campaigns, which can lead to better overall campaign performance. Specifically, it has been reported that companies spend a significant amount Companies often dedicate significant time to organizing, cleaning, and structuring their user and customer databases (Kelleher and Tierney 2018). To enhance the efficiency of these efforts, the use of appropriate performance indicators can support professionals in marketing, especially those without technical backgrounds in conducting more robust analyses and accurately assessing the time invested in managing data systems. This study explores how Big Data influences email marketing practices, using case studies and Python-based tools to illustrate key findings. We will identify trends for implementing effective Email Marketing campaigns, data sources, methods, and applications related to the perspectives of email marketing. We will then discuss future research directions in the field of Big Data and email marketing. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: ESG Investing: A Bibliometric Study
abstract: Global interest in ESG investments has increased since the COVID-19 pandemic. ESG stands for Environmental, Social, and Governance. The potential of investing in ESG to support sustainable development is enormous. The 2020 coronavirus outbreak, which sparked the greatest social upheaval of the century, brought the ESG considerations to sharp relief. This study offers a detailed understanding of ESG Investing using bibliometric analysis and content analysis. 1,136 relevant documents are evaluated from the Scopus database. VOS viewer and Biblioshiny are applied to analyze the facts and visualize the outcome. In addition to influential keywords, the study identifies countries, institutions, and numerous authors. The study identifies six research clusters, such as (i)Introduction to Sustainable Investments, (ii) Relationship between ESG performance and firm performance, (iii) Highlighting the connection between ESG stocks and ESG ratings, (iv) The emerging theme is ESG Investment, (v) ESG helps to increase the stock prices of the companies, and (vi) Role of SDG and CSR. The study offers fresh insights on previous research, uncovers emerging research themes, and provides directions for future research in the expanding discipline of ESG investing. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Assessment of the Impact of Competition on Financial Security and Business Efficiency
abstract: This study investigates the impact of competition on firm performance and financial security in post-socialist economies. Using a panel data econometric approach with firm-level and macroeconomic data from 2010 to 2024, we assess how geopolitical tensions, political instability, and economic uncertainty influence business outcomes. Our findings suggest that businesses in post-socialist countries need robust institutional frameworks and strong economic integration to withstand geopolitical risks. These results provide valuable insights for policymakers seeking to improve the resilience of firms in transition economies and offer a basis for further research into sector-specific vulnerabilities. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: AI-Driven Retail Recommendation System: Enhancing Transparency and Trust in Customer-Centric Decision-Making
abstract: In rapid retail environments personalized recommendation systems are plays a very important to draw customers attention to increase sales. On the contrary, most of the models are based on sophisticated machine learning are described as “black boxes” due to the non-transparency reason. This fact is a barrier for both users and decision-makers to build up their confidence in the system’s outputs, hence the lack of transparency, no business insights, and in some cases, even the threat of non-compliance with regulations. In light of this, we suggest a XAI-based retail recommendation model that integrates interpretability directly into the recommendation process. The system employs both predictive accuracy and explainability by merging traditional recommendation algorithms with XAI techniques followed by SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations). The framework was tested and validated via Online Retail dataset with a particular emphasis on recommendation accuracy, interpretability, and impact on customer trust and business decision-making. The findings confirm that our XAI-based model not only has predictive accuracy as well as provides localized justifications that are of substantial value. This allows for both consumers and retailers to understand and validate the recommendations with reducing the gap between performance and trust. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Legal Challenges and Technical Solutions for Data Spaces in Complex Value Chains
abstract: The European regulatory framework for data spaces, established by the Data Governance Act (DGA) and the Data Act (DA), introduces various legal requirements surrounding the development of the data economy across different sectors. Complying with these legal requirements while also ensuring an economically sustainable business model is particularly challenging in sectors such as the electronics and the textile industries, which often involve complex international value chains including several participants of different sizes and market power, many of which may not widely employ technological solutions from the digital age. Focussing on the electronics and textile industries as general examples, the paper at hand analyses the European regulatory framework for data spaces and investigates how state-of-the-art data space technology can provide (at least partial) solutions to emerging legal challenges. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: AI-Driven E-Commerce in the Era of 5G and Edge Computing: Opportunities and Challenges
abstract: The three technologies of Artificial Intelligence (AI), 5G networks, and Edge Computing will alter the face of e-commerce as the three technologies develop ultra-fast, personalized, and smart digital experiences. The current article presents the details of the transformation of online retailing, logistics, customer behavior analytics, recommendation engines, and supply chain optimization through the prism of the AI-based solutions, as well as the edge processing capabilities of large amounts of data in real-time. Through the assistance of the low-latency and high-bandwidth nature of 5G communications, and by applying Edge Computing with decentralized data, businesses can now deliver responsive, secure, and seamless services. This study provides summaries of recent research developments, applications, and systems, and exposes the major opportunities and challenges, which include data privacy, latency reduction, resource management, and interoperability. The contribution makes recommendations on the future of the AI-powered solutions in e-commerce in the next-generation digital environment by comparing and contrasting it with the existing literature and existing examples in the industry. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Digital Financial Literacy as a Mediator of Fintech Use and Financial Inclusion in SMEs: Evidence from West Sumatera Indonesia
abstract: Financial inclusion enhances SME sustainability and growth by expanding access to formal financial services, expanding opportunities for capital acquisition, and supporting business stability. This study empirically investigates the effect of FinTech adoption on financial inclusion, with digital financial literacy serving as a mediating variable among SMEs in West Sumatra, Indonesia. Using purposive sampling, data were collected from 253 SMEs through both direct on-site surveys and online questionnaires via Google Forms for geographically inaccessible areas. Path analysis with Smart PLS 3 was employed to test the hypothesized relationships. The findings reveal that FinTech use and digital financial literacy significantly enhance financial inclusion, FinTech use significantly affects SME financial inclusion mediated by digital financial literacy. Results indicate that both FinTech use and digital financial literacy are central to promoting SME financial inclusion. The research provides actionable implications for policymakers and stakeholders when designing effective strategies to foster inclusive finance through the reinforcement of digital financial literacy and FinTech use. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Impact of wind-assistance on the efficiency of a tramp fleet
abstract: Wind assisted ship propulsion (WASP) is expected to be an important element for the decarbonization of the shipping industry. However, studying WASP for a single vessel may neglect the full potential compared to planning a whole fleet of vessels as a unity. This lack of integration constitutes a substantial methodological and practical gap, given the strong inter-dependencies between wind propulsion performance, route selection, and economic–environmental trade-offs at the fleet level. We therefore extend a rich model for Tramp Ship Routing and Scheduling Problem (TSRSP) with weather-dependent routing to study the synergies. The TSRSP model includes speed optimization, bunkering, charter costs, and spot market, hence making it possible to optimize the full set of operational decisions to get the largest benefits of WASP. Historical freight rates and bunker prices supplied by a collaborating shipping company are used in the experiments, covering 9 to 20 vessels, operating in 35 predefined regions. When profit only is maximized, the results show that 5% higher profits and 8% lower emission can be obtained using WASP compared to the business-as-usual scenario. Moreover, using a multi-criteria setting, it is seen that at least 30–40% reductions in emissions can be reached while maintaining the same overall profit. Finally, we assess the impact of optimizing the entire fleet simultaneously compared to considering each vessel individually, showing that the fleet-oriented approach can achieve twice the emission reduction achieved by the vessel-oriented approach. These results show that WASP is an important measure for reaching IMO’s emission goals. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: Flexible computational loads as demand-side resources for surplus renewable energy: A review of siting criteria, thermal management, and operational strategies
abstract: Renewable curtailment often occurs behind local transmission constraints, yet studies rarely examine whether flexible loads are located where surplus arises. This review assesses when Bitcoin mining, deferrable artificial-intelligence and machine-learning (AI/ML), and high-performance-computing (HPC) workloads can use otherwise-curtailed electricity. A PRISMA-informed search, citation tracking, targeted searches, and institutional records produced a 99-record source set. The synthesis follows five steps: verify surplus, match workload flexibility, screen site and thermal feasibility, select an operating pathway, and bound claims. The positive-part Normalized Surplus Index is proposed as a screening concept. A California Independent System Operator audit shows that balancing-area records cannot support nodal NSI without pre-curtailment availability and boundary-consistent absorption and export allocations. Siting criteria include electrical access, communications, cooling and water, land and environmental constraints, and heat sinks; local stakeholder elicitation is required for weighting. Reviewed models support rapid downward interruption of controllable Bitcoin-mining loads, whereas AI/ML and HPC flexibility is slower and schedule-dependent. Surplus absorption requires separately verified upward activation in the same location and time window. No operator-grade nodal validation, site ranking, field deployment, or grid-service qualification is demonstrated. Flexible compute is therefore a conditional demand-side resource, not a general curtailment solution. © 2026

title: Calcium-modulated double emulsion for co-delivery of Monascus pigment and calcium
abstract: Monascus pigments are susceptible to environmental and processing conditions, leading to degradation and reduced functionality, while calcium bioaccessibility remains limited due to interactions within complex food matrices that can restrict its release and uptake during digestion. In this study, a gel-in-oil-in-water (G/O/W) double emulsion with a gelled internal phase was engineered for the co-delivery of Monascus pigments and calcium, enabling systematic investigation of the role of calcium in modulating emulsion structure, stability, and digestion behavior. Physicochemical characterization, including droplet size, ζ-potential, rheology, and SEM, indicated that a gel-like internal network strengthened droplet interfaces, minimized coalescence, and enabled high encapsulation efficiency (92.94 ± 0.35%). In vitro digestion studies showed that the emulsion underwent clear structural evolution from intact droplets in the oral phase, to controlled aggregation in the gastric phase, and partial breakdown in the intestinal phase. This progressive structural change directly influenced the release kinetics of both Monascus pigments and calcium ions, resulting in enhanced bioaccessibility (64.94 ± 1.7% for pigments; 60 ± 2.7% for calcium). The formulation containing 5 mM calcium showed the most favorable stability and structural integrity. These findings demonstrate that calcium-mediated ionic interactions, together with the internal gel network, can regulate emulsion structure, stability, and simultaneous delivery performance, providing mechanistic insight into the stabilization and release of functional ingredients during digestion. The study offers a versatile platform for designing functional food and nutraceutical delivery systems based on double emulsions. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: A gas sensing domain adaptation method for electronic nose systems based on subdomain adaptation with active learning
abstract: In practical deployment, electronic nose (E-nose) systems often encounter distribution shifts arising from long-term sensor drift, storage-temperature-induced changes in volatile profiles, or their coexistence, which can substantially degrade target-domain recognition. Although domain adaptation (DA) can reduce source-target distribution discrepancies, unsupervised class-conditional alignment remains vulnerable to unreliable target-domain pseudo-labels. Meanwhile, active learning (AL) can acquire limited target-domain labels, but existing E-nose studies mainly use them to update classifiers rather than further guide class-conditional cross-domain alignment. We therefore propose Subdomain Adaptation with Active Learning (SAAL), a semi-supervised active DA framework for reliable E-nose recognition with limited target-domain annotation. SAAL integrates prototype contrastive learning, which promotes intra-class compactness and inter-class separation within each domain, with Local Maximum Mean Discrepancy (LMMD), which aligns corresponding source and target subdomains at the class-conditional level. Its active learning module combines entropy–margin uncertainty estimation with K-means clustering to select informative and representative target-domain samples for annotation. The queried samples and their ground-truth labels act as local class anchors to improve pseudo-label reliability and support subsequent semi-supervised subdomain adaptation. On the Vergara gas sensor drift dataset, SAAL achieved an average accuracy of 94.08% using 162 labeled target samples. On the self-collected oyster freshness dataset, it achieved an average accuracy of 95.25% using 90 labeled target samples under compound-shift conditions related to storage-temperature variation. These results demonstrate that SAAL improves E-nose recognition under long-term sensor drift and storage-temperature-related distribution shifts with limited target-domain annotation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Beyond sales: Seller explanation, product availability, and returns in livestream commerce
abstract: Livestream commerce combines seller explanation with continued product availability in a shopping cart. Our data separately record seller explanation duration and cart availability duration; these measures do not isolate informational content or establish actual consumer exposure. Sales alone may miss differences in the postpurchase outcomes associated with these durations. We therefore examine product returns as an indicator of postpurchase outcomes, estimating associations with streamer–product and broadcast fixed effects on a panel of nearly 190,000 livestream product listings. The two durations diverge sharply: longer explanation is associated with a lower return rate and longer cart availability with a higher one, even though both are associated with higher sales. The divergence widens with the scope for uncertainty about whether a product suits a particular buyer, while the price–discount pattern does not match the specific impulse-purchasing prediction examined here. The pattern is consistent with a buyer-screening interpretation, but the data do not observe purchasers’ exposure to explanation or distinguish screening from alternatives such as telepresence. Since only one of the two is scarce, the margin a seller controls is the allocation of the host's attention rather than the length of a product's stay in the cart. © 2026

title: A signaling-cognitive architecture for product rating as quality inference
abstract: Current product rating prediction methods generally rely on algorithmic construction and data-driven approaches, often overlooking the nature of rating generation as a result of quality inference from observable signals. To bridge this gap, we propose ScoRE (Signaling theory-guided and COgnitive-driven Rating prEdiction), an architecture that reframes rating prediction as a quality inference task. This framework integrates signaling theory with a four-stage cognitive process, incorporating a product quality signal strength index to weigh the importance of product-side signals based on their credibility. Extensive experiments show that ScoRE significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Specifically, compared with the strongest baseline on each dataset, ScoRE reduces RMSE by 14.85%, 7.17%, and 16.71% on the Clothing, Electronics, and Home datasets, respectively. Moreover, it surpasses the strongest LLM-based models by 34.25% on Clothing and 7.31% on Music. These results underscore the discrepancy between the generative objectives of LLMs and the requirements of numerical prediction, highlighting the necessity of task-specific and theory-informed designs. Beyond performance gains, this study offers context-dependent strategies for seller signal management on mature, review-rich digital platforms, and advances the paradigm of theory-guided deep learning in predictive analytics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Impulsive synchronization of chaotic neural networks involving unknown states and disturbances
abstract: This article investigates the synchronization of master-slave neural networks (NNs) via observer-based impulsive control, where the slave system contains unmeasurable states and external disturbances. Two types of external disturbances are considered, i.e., vanishing disturbances and harmonic disturbances. Moreover, to deal with the unmeasurable states, a state observer is designed without imposing any restrictive prerequisites on the external disturbances. Then, an impulsive controller based on observer state is designed to achieve synchronization of master-slave NNs. Specifically, a disturbance observer utilizing state estimation is developed to estimate harmonic disturbances, and these estimates are used to compensate for the effects of harmonic disturbances on the synchronization goal. With the aid of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), the state observer gain, disturbance observer gain, and impulsive control gain are obtained. Finally, a simulation result is presented to verify the validity of the designed control strategies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Finding green start-ups at scale: Automating selection through Natural Language Processing algorithms
abstract: Research and policy interest in green entrepreneurship is growing, but identifying green start-ups remains a major challenge because the concept of “green” is inconsistently defined across studies, and existing identification strategies often rely on costly, non-scalable, or discretionary procedures. This paper develops an automated procedure to identify start-ups with an explicit environmental orientation using Natural Language Processing (NLP) with minimal human intervention. To ground the approach conceptually, we derive a green classification framework from Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) targets specifically related to environmental sustainability and use it to map start-up activities into a common set of green topics. We then apply the framework to the websites of more than 10,000 Italian innovative start-ups founded between 2009 and 2023, implementing three complementary NLP pipelines based on an ML dictionary, LDA, and BERTopic approach, to detect firms with environmentally oriented products, services, or processes. The results show that automated text-based identification can capture a broad and policy-relevant landscape of green start-ups while preserving thematic heterogeneity across environmental domains. To illustrate the analytical value of the framework, we compare the resulting distribution of these green start-ups across topics with Italy's National Recovery and Resilience Plan investments and with SDG performance indicators. This application reveals both areas of alignment and mismatch between entrepreneurial emergence, policy priorities, and environmental sustainability challenges. By offering a transparent, scalable, and SDG-grounded procedure for identifying green start-ups, the paper contributes to the measurement of green entrepreneurship and provides a useful tool for technological forecasting and policy planning. © 2026 The Authors

title: Factors associated with casualty injury severity in e-scooter crashes: A machine-learning approach with SHAP explainability
abstract: The rapid adoption of electric scooters (e-scooters) as a micro-mobility mode has been accompanied by rising crash-related injuries, yet the factors associated with severe outcomes remain poorly understood. Because the released dataset is organised at the casualty level, the outcome analysed here is the injury severity of an individual casualty involved in an e-scooter crash, classified as slight versus serious/fatal ; the unit of analysis is the casualty record, not the collision. Using 5166 police-reported casualty records from Great Britain between January 2020 and November 2024, we examine 25 crash-scene, rider, casualty, and environmental features. Five supervised classifiers are compared via randomised hyperparameter search with stratified five-fold cross-validation, with all oversampling confined to the training folds; an integer-encoded SMOTE specification is held fixed as a common reference for comparison rather than as a preferred model. The three gradient-boosted tree models have similar aggregate performance: LightGBM attains a weighted F1 of 0.660 (AUC-ROC 0.624), while paired McNemar tests and bootstrap intervals show that LightGBM, XGBoost, and Gradient Boosting each outperform the fitted Logistic Regression baseline; the LightGBM–Random Forest comparison is not robust across the two inferential checks. Cost-sensitive learning raises serious-class recall to 0.536, and a native-categorical CatBoost pipeline raises it to 0.559. Although weighted F1 remains between 0.653 and 0.661 across the four encoding pipelines, minority-class detection and SHAP rankings are encoding-sensitive. SHAP identifies number of vehicles, latitude, casualty sex, time-of-day band, and rider age as the leading predictors in the common reference model, although encoding sensitivity shows that only NumVehicles and DayTime occur in every encoding-specific top five, and the cost-sensitive ranking agrees only moderately with the SMOTE model (ρ=0.6662). Casualties recorded in single-vehicle incident configurations had higher descriptive serious/fatal injury rates than those recorded in two-vehicle configurations (38.6% versus 26.6%), and a refit restricted to the driver/rider-casualty subset used as a proxy for e-scooter riders — in which NumVehicles remains the top predictor with a stronger single-vehicle effect — indicates the pattern persists within that subset rather than arising solely from mixing riders with pedestrians. A fall or head-impact mechanism is plausible but unmeasured: helmet use, fall occurrence, and head impact are absent from the data, and the subset used to test the pattern is defined by a driver/rider role code that proxies for, rather than verifies, e-scooter rider status. Records involving older riders had higher serious/fatal injury rates (28.8% below age 50 versus 42.7% at or above 50), without establishing age 50 as a policy threshold. DayTime band 0 had the highest observed serious/fatal rate, but the four-band rates are not strictly monotonic and their clock-time meanings are undocumented. Discrimination is moderate and the predicted probabilities are poorly calibrated (Brier 0.219 against a 0.208 prevalence baseline), so these results support cautious, locally evaluated hypotheses rather than causal, operational, or universally transferable prescriptions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Lifecycle costs of safety instrumented systems in process industries: a systematic literature review
abstract: A safety instrumented system (SIS) is an automated system designed to detect and mitigate potential risk of hazardous conditions in industrial processes by taking actions to prevent or mitigate incidents. It is essential because it helps protect people, equipment, and the environment by reducing the risk of accidents in hazardous operations, such as in chemical plants, oil refineries, or power stations. While the primary objective of SIS design is safety, economic considerations, particularly lifecycle cost, play a pivotal role in decision-making during the design phase. Although research efforts exist to incorporate lifecycle cost with safety, the literature is fragmented and lacks a comprehensive lifecycle cost framework. Therefore, a systematic literature review is conducted to uncover safety instrumented systems’ lifecycle cost elements and the decision variables that impact them. The review results lead to a comprehensive and structured cost calculation framework to assess SIS designed to protect a process unit economically. Finally, this study provides perspectives on potential research directions relevant to SIS lifecycle cost, including the impact of systematic failures, cybersecurity integration, the relative weighting of different cost elements, inclusion of risk costs, and various SIS application types. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Lead and succeed: R&D executives and bank digital transformation
abstract: Digital transformation (DT) is reshaping the business of banks in the age of big data, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence. We explore how executives with research and development (R&D) experience shape banks' DT. Based on a sample covering 110 Chinese banks from 2012 to 2023, we empirically confirm that increasing R&D executives significantly enhances banks' technology transformation when banks face low competition or have low risk-taking. We further identify that stronger public digital attention attenuates such a transformation effect. The impacts exhibit heterogeneity, varying across different dimensions of transformation and bank characteristics. These findings remain robust after controlling for endogeneity in various robustness tests. Supplementary analyses show a crowding-out effect as R&D executives hinder banks' cooperation with technology companies, reducing the efficiency of banks. The evidence suggests the challenges of DT for banks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: De-risking equity investment for productive use integration in mini-grids: Designing a first-loss demand-risk guarantee for e-mobility in Kakuma refugee camp, Kenya
abstract: Achieving commercially viable mini-grid operations in remote areas of sub-Saharan Africa remains constrained by uncertain electricity demand, contributing to investor hesitancy, particularly among equity investors. Productive use of electricity can improve asset utilisation and strengthen revenue generation, but its integration requires additional investment that remains exposed to revenue risk when early-stage demand uptake is uncertain. This paper designs and evaluates a first-loss demand-risk guarantee for electric two-wheeler battery-swapping integration into the solar mini-grid of Kakuma refugee camp, Kenya. Methodologically, the case study is grounded in design science research and combines system sizing, financial modelling, scenario analysis, and guarantee stress testing. The system analysis identifies a technically feasible configuration of 200 electric two-wheelers and 140 spare batteries without additional generation or storage capacity, which is used as input for the financial model. The financial model shows that the business case reaches the equity investor threshold, defined as a 15% equity internal rate of return, only under high vehicle utilisation and with a 25% capital subsidy on charging and swapping infrastructure. The proposed guarantee addresses the resulting utilisation-driven revenue risk through partial first-loss coverage, a utilisation-based activation window, annual payout caps, and a cumulative exposure cap. Scenario results show that the guarantee improves equity returns across all eligible utilisation-shortfall scenarios. It raises the base- and best-case scenarios above the investor threshold and substantially reduces the return gap in the worst-case scenario. The study contributes a project-level design framework for developing demand-risk guarantees as development-finance de-risking instruments for productive-use integration, while highlighting the need for case-specific calibration, robust verification, and further testing across additional mini-grid contexts. © 2026 The Authors
