title: Precise integration of attack path and syntax logic analysis for vulnerability severity assessment
abstract: Accurate assessment of vulnerability severity at the source code level is essential for anticipating potential risks and prioritizing remediation efforts. However, current approaches face two key challenges: (i) analyzing exploitability at the basic block level fragments syntactic and semantic logic, causing critical exploitation conditions to be overlooked and leading to severity misjudgments; and (ii) inferring attack paths from inter-block relationships often fails to distinguish benign control flows from exploit chains, polluting attack graphs with false paths and resulting in inaccurate exploitability assessment, especially for access-complexity-related evidence. To address these issues, we propose ASVA (Attack path and Syntax logic analysis for Vulnerability severity Assessment), a novel patch-aware source-code framework that integrates multi-scale syntactic logic extraction with attack path modeling. ASVA employs convolutional kernels with varying receptive fields to capture multi-scale syntactic patterns and leverages an attention mechanism to highlight exploitation logic, reducing misclassification. Furthermore, it utilizes CodeBERT to encode code lines and compute inter-line semantic relationships, enabling the construction of robust attack path representations that effectively distinguish genuine attack flows from normal control transitions. Experiments on two public datasets demonstrate that ASVA outperforms selected state-of-the-art baselines, improving accuracy and robustness over existing methods. This work underscores the importance of fine-grained logic modeling and attack path correlation in advancing automated vulnerability severity assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Matching-game-based beam scheduling for spectrum sharing in massive LEO constellations
abstract: This paper develops an on-board, knowledge-driven decision system for autonomous beam management in massive LEO constellations, in which a bounded local knowledge base and a provably objective-aligned inference rule replace the ground-side optimization loop that current constellations depend on. Massive low-Earth-orbit (LEO) constellations have made orbital spectrum a principal bottleneck on the capacity and service quality of next-generation satellite networks. Letting LEO satellites reuse the pre-assigned geostationary-orbit (GEO) downlink spectrum relieves this scarcity but introduces co-channel interference that must be suppressed. Since a ground user is visible to several LEO satellites and its choice of serving satellite reshapes the beam-pointing geometry, interference can be regulated through beam matching alone once beam power and channel are fixed. On this basis, a spatial-adaptive matching learning (SAML) method is proposed. The user–satellite association is cast as a many-to-one matching game whose exact potential function guarantees that distributed local matching converges to a stable association equivalent to a Nash equilibrium. A quasi-static slot upper bound is then derived in closed form from a joint visibility–Doppler criterion and coupled with the beam-relay overlap window, fixing the hard time budget for service continuity. SAML itself uses only O(1) local interaction and O(N) per-slot computation; its asymptotic optimality is proved by Gibbs-measure concentration and refined by a finite-temperature convergence-rate bound tied to the single-slot budget. Simulations show that SAML attains satisfaction within a few percent of a full-information best-response reference, itself a heuristic rather than the exact optimum, sustains stable link-establishment time across relayed slots, meets an end-to-end on-board time budget within the relay overlap window, and allocates resources more fairly than throughput-oriented baselines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: Uncertainty-aware nodal carbon intensity based on sliced Latin hypercube sampling
abstract: The variability of climate conditions leads to significant renewable uncertainty. With the large-scale integration of renewable energy, it becomes necessary to consider uncertainties in the nodal carbon intensity (NCI) of power systems. However, the renewable uncertainty though the power flow propagates to the carbon emission flow, making an unclear relationship between the renewable uncertainty and the carbon emission flow. In this paper, an uncertainty-aware nodal Carbon intensity method is proposed to handle this issue. An explicit matrix-form relationship linking renewable forecast errors, AGC-based generation dispatch, branch power flow variations, and NCI is established. In addition, a Jacobian-based local sensitivity expression is derived to characterize the local response of NCI to renewable forecast errors. Then, sliced Latin hypercube sampling (SLHS) is employed to estimate the statistical characteristics and probability distribution of NCI. Case studies performed on the PJM 5-bus and IEEE 300-bus systems demonstrate that the proposed method is capable of accurately accounting for the uncertainty in the nodal carbon intensity. © 2026

title: AI-Assisted Seminar Planning Using Personas
abstract: Since the launch of ChatGPT in 2022, artificial intelligence (AI) and user experience (UX) have become increasingly important in business. This study explores how AI can support UX-oriented seminar planning. The Software Association of Japan established a special interest group on AI and UX, which conducted workshops to identify practical applications of AI. The group focused on seminar planning, a task that involved challenges such as selecting themes, promoting the seminar, and engaging participants. The proposed method uses AI-generated personas and simulated interviews to refine seminar ideas and develop attractive seminar designs for target audiences. In a workshop with 13 participants, AI-assisted interviews helped generate and improve seminar proposals. Two highly rated seminar themes emerged: “Designing Winning UX Strategies That Drive ROI” and “Practical UX Quality Control for Evaluating AI-Generated Outputs.” The results suggest that AI-supported persona interviews can effectively enhance seminar planning and UX-oriented idea development. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Upcycling traditional Chinese medicine residue into Fe/Zr bimetallic biochar for synergistic PMS activation: A superoxide-driven route for levofloxacin degradation and toxicity mitigation
abstract: The practical application of biochar (BC) for peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation is hindered by its limited surface area, paucity of active sites, and poor electron transfer. To address these challenges, we synthesized an iron-zirconium bimetallic-modified BC (Fe/Zr0.8-BC) from traditional Chinese medicine residue via impregnation-pyrolysis. Comprehensive characterization confirmed the successful loading of Fe (Fe3O4/metallic Fe) and Zr (ZrO2), which dramatically increased the specific surface area from 4.10 to 269.59 m2/g and created a mesoporous architecture conducive to both PMS activation and pollutant adsorption. The Fe/Zr0.8-BC/PMS system achieved 89.54% levofloxacin (LVF) removal and 42.31% total organic carbon mineralization within 90 min under optimized conditions (catalyst 0.6 g/L, PMS 1 mM, LVF 10 mg/L, pH 7). The catalyst exhibited robust reusability, with only ∼19% activity loss after four cycles and leached Fe/Zr concentrations (0.10 and 0.02 mg/L) below regulatory limits. Mechanistic investigations, combining radical quenching and electron paramagnetic resonance, revealed synergistic contributions from O2•-, SO4•-, •OH, and 1O2, with O2•- playing the dominant role, suggesting a hybrid radical/non-radical pathway. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy further elucidated the interfacial catalytic mechanism driven by reversible Fe2+/Fe3+ and Zr4+/Zr3+ redox cycles. Ten degradation intermediates were identified via high-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, enabling the proposal of three primary pathways: decarboxylation, defluorination, and piperazine ring opening. Toxicity assessment using the T.E.S.T software indicated that most intermediates possessed lower acute toxicity, bioaccumulation potential, developmental toxicity, and mutagenicity than the parent compound. This work not only provides a sustainable strategy for upcycling traditional Chinese medicine residue into high-performance catalytic materials but also offers mechanistic insights into bimetallic synergistic PMS activation, presenting a promising and environmentally benign solution for antibiotic-contaminated water remediation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: A flow shop scheduling problem incorporating a reconfigurable material handling Robot: A constraint programming approach
abstract: A reconfigurable manufacturing system (RMS) is a new paradigm for the manufacturing environment to respond to unpredictable market change and frequent new product introduction. One of the components of an RMS is a reconfigurable material handling system (RMHS). This paper investigates the permutation flow shop scheduling problem in a manufacturing system with RMHS. Hence, first, a novel Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model is developed. Then, to tackle the inherent complexity of the problem, an efficient constraint programming (CP) approach is devised. Finally, comprehensive computational experiments are conducted to evaluate the performance of both models, followed by a sensitivity analysis on three key performance indicators to further assess the CP model and extract the managerial insights. Results show that the CP model has better performance than the MILP model for solving large-scale problem instances and achieves a high-quality solution in a reasonable time. Moreover, the flexibility of eligibility restrictions can significantly affect the Makespan and solution time. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Reliability evaluation of multi-state logistics networks with weibull-based capacities under time-dependent spoilage
abstract: This paper investigates the reliability evaluation for a multi-state logistics network with time-dependent spoilage (MLN-TDS). In the MLN-TDS, arc capacities represent the number of available logistics vehicles, whose time-dependent availability is characterized by a Weibull distribution. Unlike conventional models that assume a constant spoilage rate, this paper evaluates the time-dependent spoilage (TDS) rate of each minimal path according to its delivery time. To account for the resulting discrepancy between dispatched and delivered quantities, intact flow vectors are constructed to determine the required dispatched quantities before deriving the corresponding capacity vectors. The MLN-TDS reliability is defined as the probability that demand can be fulfilled while simultaneously satisfying both loss cost and time constraints. Based on minimal paths and minimal capacity vectors, an algorithm is proposed to evaluate the MLN-TDS reliability, and the recursive sum of disjoint products method is used to compute its value. An illustrative example and a real-world fruit delivery case study are provided to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed evaluation procedure. The results identify critical demand thresholds and show how changes in TDS rates affect MLN-TDS reliability under high-demand conditions. These findings provide quantitative support for reliability-oriented logistics planning and operational decision making. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Communication-efficient distributed quantile regression neural networks via convolution smoothing and poisson sampling
abstract: Quantile regression neural networks (QRNNs) provide flexible nonlinear conditional quantile estimation, but training is hindered by the non-differentiability of the check-loss, and existing methods do not scale to large datasets stored non-randomly across distributed machines. We propose a convolution-smoothed QRNN (CS-QRNN) that replaces the check-loss with a twice-differentiable kernel-convolved surrogate, and a distributed extension (DCS-QRNN) that combines Poisson pilot sampling with a gradient-corrected surrogate loss. After a one-time pilot-sample collection and pilot-estimator broadcast, DCS-QRNN requires only a single round of gradient aggregation, with no further communication during optimization. Under mild regularity conditions, we establish consistency, asymptotic normality, and first-order equivalence to the centralized full-data estimator. In simulations across three nonlinear regression surfaces and three error distributions, DCS-QRNN achieves 80–100 × speedup at a 1% pilot ratio while preserving centralized accuracy: on a challenging multi-peak surface with t(3) errors, DCS-QRNN attains a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.3176 versus 0.3097 for the full-data estimator. Counting all three DCS-QRNN communication stages, the simulated wall-clock time at a network bandwidth of 100 Mbit/s and a latency of 100 ms per one-way stage is 38.0 seconds, versus 140.3 seconds for the fixed-budget FedAvg-QRNN protocol with (Formula presented). On the Household Electric Power Consumption and Beijing Multi-Site Air Quality datasets, DCS-QRNN preserves near-centralized accuracy while reducing running time by roughly an order of magnitude, confirming that its primary practical advantage is computational efficiency together with a substantially smaller number of synchronization stages. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: How do UAVs govern data sovereignty in decentralized federated sensing networks? Tokenized access control via policy-driven smart contracts
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become pivotal in a wide range of applications due to their high mobility, broad coverage, and multi-sensor integration. Advances in wireless networks have further spurred interest in cross-domain collaboration among UAVs from diverse institutions, platforms, and control domains, giving rise to decentralized federated sensing as an emerging research direction. However, the absence of trusted intermediaries, dynamic network topologies, and heterogeneous data ownership make it challenging to achieve ownership-controllable and fine-grained data protection in such decentralized UAV networks. To tackle these challenges, we propose a blockchain-based decentralized access control framework integrating three novel mechanisms. First, a Hybrid Data Token Model (HDTM) unifies composable, fine-grained data permissions that distinguish fungible (replicable) from non-fungible (data-modifying) rights, and anchors them to data provenance via a cryptographic Data Ownership Signature. Second, an Unspent Fungible Token Outputs (UFTO) mechanism enforces attribute-level transfer constraints and discrepancy detection to govern permission lifecycle with full traceability. Third, a Smart contract-driven Attribute-Based Access Control (ScaBAC) algorithm distributes the ABAC decision pipeline across four modular, independently verifiable smart contracts, coupling access decisions to on-chain token state for auditable, verifiable authorization. An implementation implemented on Hyperledger Fabric achieves a throughput of 128–160 tx/s across the ScaBAC contract suite, a 32% reduction in average latency compared to the PpBAC baseline, and sub-10 ms read-query response. These results demonstrate that fine-grained, decentralized access control is feasible under the resource and topology constraints of UAV federated sensing networks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Supply chain digitalization and ESG greenwashing: A signal reliability perspective
abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) greenwashing is often attributed to firm-level opportunism, yet less is understood about how the broader information environment systematically shapes the reliability of ESG signals. We address this gap by examining how supply chain digitalization (SCD) curbs greenwashing by reducing two distinct information asymmetries and enhancing signal reliability. We argue that digitalization enhances supply chain transparency, thereby improving signal fit by reducing supply chain vertical information asymmetry, and strengthening signal honesty by reducing ESG disclosure information asymmetry. Leveraging China's supply chain innovation and application pilot policy as a quasi-natural experiment and analyzing data from Chinese A-share listed firms, we find that digitalization significantly reduces ESG greenwashing, particularly in firms with higher supply chain complexity and higher analyst forecast dispersion. Our study contributes to research on ESG greenwashing, the digital governance of sustainability, and signaling theory by reframing greenwashing as a problem of signal unreliability shaped by the supply chain information environment, and by showing how supply chain digitalization improves both the accuracy and credibility of corporate signals. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Mindfulness in organizations: how and when mindfulness shapes perceptions of distributive justice in society
abstract: Although social inequality is widespread, managers do not necessarily perceive it as unfair. Across four field studies involving European managers, we investigate how mindfulness influences managers’ perceptions of distributive justice in society (PDJS). Three results emerge. First, mindfulness leads managers to perceive societal inequalities as more unfair. Second, social-justice awareness mediates this relationship. Third, organizational context conditions these effects: workplace ostracism weakens the positive influence of mindfulness on social-justice awareness and PDJS, whereas organizational justice buffers this detrimental effect. These results make three contributions. First, we extend mindfulness research by demonstrating its relevance to managers’ perceptions of societal outcomes. Second, we empirically support the mindfulness capability for social justice theory by identifying social-justice awareness as the key mechanism linking mindfulness to PDJS. Third, we establish organizational context as an important boundary condition, showing when the societal benefits of mindfulness are weakened or preserved. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Licochalcone D accelerates cutaneous wound healing with improved perfusion and antioxidant responses
abstract: Impaired local perfusion, excessive oxidative stress, persistent inflammation, and apoptosis can compromise cutaneous wound healing. Licochalcone D (LCD), a licorice-derived flavonoid, has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, but its effects on cutaneous repair remain incompletely characterized. This study evaluated LCD in a rat full-thickness excisional wound model. Thirty-two male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to vehicle control or LCD treatment at 5, 25, or 50 mg/kg/day by oral gavage. Wound closure, local perfusion, histological repair, oxidative stress, inflammatory mediators, apoptosis-related proteins, antioxidant signaling-related proteins, and selected mitochondrial protein markers were evaluated. LCD accelerated wound closure, enhanced perfusion, increased VEGF expression, reduced inflammatory-cell infiltration, and improved collagen organization. LCD also increased SOD activity, reduced MDA and 4-HNE levels, and decreased TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6. Nrf2, HO-1, and NQO1 expression increased after LCD treatment, supporting an association with enhanced antioxidant responses. Apoptosis-related proteins shifted toward an anti-apoptotic pattern. LCD treatment was additionally accompanied by changes in PINK1, Parkin, LC3B, SQSTM1/p62, and COX IV expression; however, these single-time-point measurements do not establish altered mitophagic flux or a causal mitochondrial mechanism. Overall, orally administered LCD improved multiple wound-healing-related outcomes, with more pronounced effects in the medium- and high-dose groups. © 2026

title: Inside out: cutting-edge methods to decode external opportunities for startup growth
abstract: We examine how both internal resources and the external environment influence startup growth, addressing the challenge of measuring the knowledge structure in which the startup operates. We introduce, in relation to firm growth, two indicators belonging to the economic complexity paradigm, complexity and relatedness, to respectively assess the economic sophisticatedness and connectedness of the local area. Using a longitudinal analysis over three-, four-, and five-year growth windows, as well as sustained growth patterns, we investigate the early growth of 902 innovative startups in Italy. Our results confirm previous findings, identifying a positive association between effective organizations, managers’ external relationships, and initial R&D investments and startup growth. Among the external factors, we find a supportive role for relatedness, but not complexity. All variables remain stable and consistent over the period examined. © 2026 The Author(s). title: The impact of artificial intelligence on improving the quality of internal auditing in commercial banks: The moderating role of accounting information systems
abstract: This study investigates the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on enhancing the quality of internal auditing in commercial banks, with a particular focus on the moderating role of accounting information systems (AIS). By employing a descriptive and analytical approach, this research aims to examine the relationship between these variables and their influence on the effectiveness of internal auditing practices. Data was collected through a questionnaire administered to a random sample of administrative workers in Jordanian commercial banks. The statistical package for the social sciences (SPSS) was used to analyze the data collected. The findings of this study demonstrate a statistically significant impact of AI on improving the quality of internal auditing, with AIS acting as a moderating factor in this relationship. © 2026 The Authors

title: Microbial functional differentiation and flavor formation across layer exchange in cereal vinegar fermentation: Multi-omics insights and targeted bioaugmentation
abstract: Spatial heterogeneity is common in cereal vinegar fermentation, but microbial and metabolic changes across the layer-exchange process remain unclear. We combined metagenomics and metatranscriptomics with physicochemical, organic-acid, and volatile profiling to investigate layer-associated changes during Tianjin Duliu mature vinegar (TDMV) fermentation and guide bioaugmentation. Before exchange, the frequently turned upper layer consumed ethanol at 1.14 times the lower-layer rate, rapidly accumulated acetic acid, and was enriched in Acetobacter and Komagataeibacter . The lower layer retained more ethanol and lactic acid, was enriched in lactic acid bacteria and yeasts, and contained more ethyl esters. After upward transfer, the original lower-layer Cupei rapidly accumulated acetic acid as several ethyl esters decreased; after downward transfer, the original upper-layer Cupei acidified more slowly while phenethyl alcohol, phenethyl acetate, ethyl lactate, and 2,3-butanediol increased. Genus-level transcript profiles showed that Acetobacter -affiliated transcripts related to acetaldehyde oxidation and the acetolactate/acetoin branch were more pronounced in upper-positioned Cupei , whereas LAB-affiliated lactate-forming transcripts were prominent in the lower layer. At the 100-kg scale, a targeted two-strain treatment using Lactobacillus helveticus and Acetobacter pasteurianus increased substrate conversion efficiency from 47.35 ± 1.36% to 51.19 ± 0.32% and final total acid by approximately 9.7% in both portions. In a → A, day-17 acetic acid was 43.8% higher than in the control, but the difference was not significant at the endpoint. The bioaugmentation samples showed changes in aroma-related volatile composition. These findings support complementary microbial functional differentiation across Cupei positions and inform position-targeted regulation of TDMV fermentation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: From breakdown to breakthrough: How entrepreneurs craft vulnerability narratives on social media
abstract: Entrepreneurial narratives are widely understood as strategic tools for building legitimacy and mobilizing resources. Yet we observed that some entrepreneurs openly share stories of fear, doubt, and struggle on social media - foregrounding emotional exposure rather than demonstrating strategic purpose. We conceptualize these as entrepreneurial vulnerability narratives: a distinct narrative form through which the lived consequences of entrepreneurial uncertainty are publicly shared and opened to social negotiation. These disclosures expose entrepreneurs to interpersonal risks, heightened for women entrepreneurs who contend with gendered biases and less supportive social contexts. To examine this phenomenon, we conducted interviews with 33 women entrepreneurs and a 21-month observation of their Instagram activity. Our analysis reveals that women entrepreneurs hold multiple and coexisting motivations for disclosure - self-oriented, relational, and normative - oscillating between them as needed, while developing narrative-crafting tactics that sustain the benefits of sharing while managing interpersonal risks. Our study contributes by theorizing entrepreneurial vulnerability narratives as a distinct narrative form; by challenging the view that entrepreneurial narratives serve primarily persuasive functions; and by showing how entrepreneurs actively construct precarious holding environments in fragmented digital contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Guest-origin and temporal heterogeneity in online hotel reviews: A structural topic modeling analysis
abstract: This study examines whether the relative salience of hotel-review themes varies across guest-origin groups and review years. Structural Topic Modeling was applied to 29,304 Booking.com reviews from 144 hotels in Vietnam collected between 2022 and 2025. A seven-topic solution captured staff/location/breakfast satisfaction, room cleanliness and comfort, amenities and food, walkability, personalized hospitality, leisure settings, and booking/travel logistics. Probability-scale contrasts were standardized over the complementary metadata distribution, with hotel-clustered CR2 inference accounting for within-hotel dependence. Guest-origin heterogeneity was markedly more stable than temporal heterogeneity. Under hotel-clustered inference, 15 of 21 guest-origin contrasts met the within-family false-discovery-rate threshold, compared with 1 of 21 2022-referenced temporal contrasts; 11 guest-origin contrasts showed strong multi-specification evidence. The largest difference was a 27.6-percentage-point higher expected prevalence of the Room cleanliness and comfort topic in Domestic than Western reviews; Domestic reviews also showed an 18.4-percentage-point lower expected prevalence of Staff, location, and breakfast satisfaction. Asian reviews exhibited a distinct profile spanning amenities, walkability, personalized hospitality, travel logistics, and leisure-related content. Temporal evidence was less stable: the 2025–2022 increase in Personalized hospitality and attentive service attenuated after hotel fixed effects, although a separate 2023-referenced analysis identified six supported temporal contrasts. The findings show that guest-origin context is associated with persistent differences in what consumers discuss, whereas annual differences are more dependent on hotel composition and temporal reference. The study advances hotel-review analytics by integrating metadata-conditioned topic prevalence with dependence-aware inference and provides context-specific diagnostic signals beyond aggregate ratings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Allocation of foreign aid in emerging economies: Investment in new vs maintenance of old infrastructure
abstract: This paper analyzes the growth and welfare effects of allocating public resources — both domestic tax revenues and foreign aid — between investment in new public capital and the maintenance of existing public capital in emerging economies. We show that moderate increases in maintenance enhance growth and welfare by improving capital efficiency and longevity, while excessive maintenance crowds out consumption and productive investment and has adverse effects. Foreign aid, by easing domestic fiscal constraints, enables lower distortionary taxation, but its effectiveness depends on both its composition and interaction with domestic fiscal policies. Our study emphasizes the importance of a balanced allocation. Numerical simulations suggest that for a plausible calibration an approximate 80-20 split allocation between new investment and maintenance is desirable, but it is sensitive to the quality of the public capital. For the calibrated benchmark model donor-imposed co-financing requirements have conflicting effects on growth and welfare, although these are highly sensitive to the productivity of public capital, but less so to the allocation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Survival analysis of U.S. regional airline routes during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Since the COVID-19 pandemic, U.S. regional airlines have faced substantial operational challenges, including reduced flight activity, fleet restructuring, rising labor costs, and persistent pilot shortage. Between 2019 and 2024, domestic departures by regional airlines declined by nearly 24% from 3.81 million to 2.92 million, while passenger enplanements fell by 19% from 165.2 million to 133.7 million. Mainline carriers temporarily increased their reliance on regional partners during the pandemic but subsequently reduced regional operations during the post-pandemic recovery. Against this backdrop, we examine the determinants of route survival in U.S. regional airline markets during and after the pandemic. Using airline-route panel data for 2017–2024, we estimate Cox proportional hazards models with time-varying route-performance covariates. The results show that routes operated by independent regional airlines face significantly higher discontinuation hazards than those operated by wholly-owned subsidiaries of mainline carriers. Routes serving large hub airports exhibit higher survival probabilities, underscoring the importance of network connectivity beyond local market size. Support through the U.S. Essential Air Service (EAS) program is also associated with greater route survival, while larger aircraft are linked to improved route persistence, consistent with post-pandemic upgauging and capacity consolidation. The analysis also accounts for market demand conditions and operational characteristics, including population, per capita income, unit cost, stage length, and aircraft size. This study extends the literature by examining how ownership structure, network position, route performance, and EAS support jointly relate to regional route survival following the COVID-19 pandemic. The findings also inform EAS program design by highlighting the importance of risk-based route monitoring and service-continuity assessments that consider carrier structure, hub connectivity, market conditions, and fleet availability. title: Turán extremal graphs vs. signless Laplacian spectral Turán extremal graphs
abstract: Let F be a graph with chromatic number χ(F)=r+1. Denote by ex(n,F) and Ex(n,F) the Turán number and the set of all extremal graphs for F, respectively. In addition, exssp(n,F) and Exssp(n,F) are the maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of all n-vertex F-free graphs and the set of all n-vertex F-free graphs with signless Laplacian spectral radius exssp(n,F), respectively. It is known that Exssp(n,F)⊃Ex(n,F) if F is a triangle. In this paper, employing the regularity method and Füredi's stability theorem, we prove that for a given graph F and r⩾3, if ex(n,F)=tr(n)+O(1), then Exssp(n,F)⊆Ex(n,F) for sufficiently large n, where tr(n) is the number of edges in the Turán graph Tr(n). © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Bridging the AI Adoption Gap: A Practitioner Framework for Non-technical Decision Makers: The CREATE Framework for Strategic AI Implementation
abstract: Despite significant advances in artificial intelligence capabilities, organizational AI adoption remains considerably slower than technological readiness would predict. This study addresses the adoption gap—the disconnect between AI’s technical potential and its practical deployment in non-technical organizational contexts—and frames it as a problem of organizational change, decision-making support, and responsible AI governance rather than one of algorithmic performance. Drawing on a structured retrospective analysis of 214 AI implementation engagements documented over four years (2021–2025) with business leaders, nonprofit executives, and other organizational decision-makers, we present the CREATE Framework: a systematic, six-stage decision-making methodology designed to enable non-technical leadership to evaluate, select, and deploy AI solutions strategically. The framework comprises six stages: Customer (problem-first orientation), Research (structured landscape assessment), Expand/Narrow (divergent–convergent ideation), Assemble (strategic technology portfolio construction), Test (rapid validation protocols), and Expand (scalable deployment strategies). The study’s contribution is integrative rather than algorithmic: (1) an explicit data-readiness gate sequenced before technology selection, (2) operational accessibility criteria that keep each stage executable by leaders without data-science training, and (3) a responsible-AI overlay embedding ethics, fairness, and governance checkpoints within every stage rather than treating them as a separate workstream. We validate the framework through three pilot case studies with matched baseline conditions and operationally defined outcome metrics: adoption time, a seven-item stakeholder alignment index, and a four-criterion implementation success rubric. Across the pilots, framework-guided projects reached sustained deployment at the six-month mark, with a mean adoption time 55% shorter than matched baselines. We argue that the primary bottleneck to AI value realization is not algorithmic performance but organizational readiness, leadership capability, and the integration of responsible-AI practice into everyday technology adoption decisions. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Financial profitability of commercial solar on-grid PV in Colombia: A case study on the impact of fiscal incentives
abstract: As part of Colombia's energy-transition framework, Law 1715 of 2014 established fiscal incentives to promote solar photovoltaic (PV) deployment. However, their project-level profitability and interaction with the surplus-remuneration structure established by CREG Resolution 174 of 2021 remain insufficiently quantified. This study develops an integrated deterministic techno-economic framework combining PVsyst energy-production simulations, a 30-year discounted cash-flow model, a Design of Computational Experiments (DoCE), and Sobol Global Sensitivity Analysis (GSA). Three load profiles, two architectures (PV and PV+BESS), 15 installed capacities (10–150 kWp), and eight incentive configurations were evaluated, yielding 720 deterministic physical-policy combinations, while the GSA considered nine technical, economic, and policy inputs. Fiscal incentives consistently improved project profitability, although their effectiveness depended on the broader project configuration. Accelerated depreciation and VAT and tariff exemptions were the strongest individual mechanisms, increasing median NPV by 38.9 and 33.1 MCOP, respectively. Combining all incentives increased median NPV by 76.1 MCOP (54.7%), IRR by 8.71 percentage points (25.0%), reduced LCOE by 429.6 COP/kWh (24.3%), and shortened discounted payback by 2.59 years (39.0%). The GSA identified installed capacity (ST=0.355), capital costs (ST=0.349), and financing conditions (ST=0.349) as the dominant sources of profitability variability. These results demonstrate that fiscal policy, system sizing, financing, load-generation correspondence, storage, and surplus-remuneration rules should be evaluated as interconnected determinants of distributed PV profitability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: BaCu₃ScSe₄ and BaCu₃YSe₄ quaternary selenides: a first-principles exploration of mechanical, optical, and energy-conversion properties
abstract: An emerging platform for energy-conversion and optoelectronic devices is quaternary chalcogenides. Here, using FP-APW + lo density-functional theory in conjunction with TB-mBJ band calculations, we conducted a thorough first-principles evaluation of BaCu₃ScSe₄ and BaCu₃YSe₄. From Voigt–Reuss–Hill and Pugh metrics, both compounds are ductile and meet the Born mechanical-stability requirements. Energy gaps of 1.84 eV (Sc) and 1.72 eV (Y) are shown by electronic structures. Around Ba and the trivalent cations, DOS and charge-density maps reveal a mixed ionic nature with dominating Cu-Se covalency. Optical spectra derived from complex dielectric function yield prominent optical response. Photocatalytic water splitting potential of compounds shows efficient water splitting. BaCu₃ScSe₄ exhibits higher electrical and thermal conductivities temperature-dependent transport, while BaCu₃YSe₄ yields a higher Seebeck coefficient and figure of merit. The results show that BaCu₃ScSe₄ is a mechanically robust candidate and that BaCu₃YSe₄ is an attractive p-type high-temperature thermoelectric with a notable visible-light response. Together with the interband transitions and appreciable optical absorption predicted within the visible-energy range, makes the compounds potential candidate for high-temperature thermoelectric and visible-light optoelectronic applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: FedVRU: Variational representation decomposition with uncertainty-aware refinement
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving collaborative training. However, data heterogeneity across clients degrades the performance of a single global model. Existing Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) methods partially mitigate this issue via client-specific modeling. However, most rely on deterministic point estimation, ignoring the implicit uncertainty within personalized features and leaving the joint representation space vulnerable to local noise. We propose FedVRU, a unified framework for Federated Variational Representation Decomposition with Uncertainty-aware Refinement. Specifically, FedVRU models client-specific representations probabilistically through variational learning to characterize feature uncertainty. An Uncertainty-Aware Gating (UAG) mechanism then adaptively regulates personalized features according to the estimated uncertainty. Concurrently, a Multi-Contrastive Distillation (MCD) objective promotes temporal consistency of global representations and separation between global and personalized representations. Extensive experiments on multiple heterogeneous benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of FedVRU across diverse federated settings without additional communication overhead. The code is available at https://github.com/Baohua-Judy/FedVRU. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: Co-founder selection from a marriage market perspective: How the dark triad shapes judgments of interpersonal attraction, resources, and equity demand
abstract: Co-founder selection is a pivotal decision in new venture formation, yet how lead founders evaluate potential partners remains underexplored. Drawing on insights from marriage market theory, we conceptualize co-founder selection as an act of individuated judgment guided by cooperative logic and associated joint utility projection, wherein lead founders assess co-founder candidates based on social-emotional, instrumental, and distributive considerations reflected in interpersonal attraction, resource contributions, and equity demand. We further propose that lead founders' dark triad shifts this judgmental process from joint utility logic to personal utility maximization. Using a conjoint experiment with 206 entrepreneurs making 3296 co-founder selection decisions, we find that interpersonal attraction and resource contributions positively influence willingness to select a co-founder candidate, whereas higher equity demand reduces candidate attractiveness. Critically, lead founders higher in the dark triad display distinct patterns: they discount interpersonal attraction and display heightened sensitivity to equity dilution—assessments that indicate their prioritization of personal over joint value creation. Taken together, these findings reveal how dispositional tendencies influence the judgments underlying co-founder selection, indicating a shift away from the cooperative logic assumed in marriage market theory and co-founder selection toward greater emphasis on personal utility considerations. We discuss theoretical implications of these findings and offer practical guidance for navigating the complexities of co-founder selection. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Non-market strategies and environmental management: Framework for effective sustainable transformation
abstract: As environmental concerns intensify, businesses are increasingly adopting non-market strategies (NMS) to navigate regulatory pressures and improve environmental performance (EP). However, there has been no systematic effort to synthesise existing studies on the environmental benefits of NMS and to provide an integrated conceptual understanding of the field. As a result, there remains limited understanding of how these strategies influence firms’ EP and the boundary conditions under which they are effective. To address this gap, this study conducts a systematic review of 151 peer-reviewed articles and develops a comprehensive integrative framework linking NMS to firm-level EP. The framework highlights the effectiveness of combined NMS in comparison to single strategies, emphasising the role of dual legitimacy activation. This synthesis provides a foundation for more nuanced future research and offers practical guidance on aligning political engagement, governance capacity, and innovation investment to enhance sustained EP across varying institutional contexts. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Navigating the paradox: Empowerment and power dynamics in international social entrepreneurship
abstract: Social entrepreneurship (SE) often seeks to empower marginalized beneficiaries by reshaping unequal power relations and promoting more enduring forms of social change. Yet efforts to empower others inherently involve the exercise of power and may therefore reproduce the very asymmetries they seek to overcome. While this “empowerment paradox” has primarily been conceptualized through discrete empowerer-empoweree relationships, considerably less is known about how it unfolds across broader relational systems, particularly in international social entrepreneurship (ISE), where organizations operate across institutional contexts characterized by Global South-North asymmetries. Drawing on a qualitative multi-case study of six ISE ventures, informed by 45 interviews and extensive archival data, we develop an integrative model explaining how the empowerment paradox is structured, experienced, and navigated in these settings. We show that empowerment is organized through multilevel relational chains spanning ecosystem, organizational, and operational levels, that the paradox is experienced differently depending on actors’ positions within these chains, and that organizations navigate persistent tensions through the recursive interplay of relational and structural mechanisms. Building on these findings, we introduce ethical ambidexterity, the capacity to integrate pragmatic and critical orientations toward the use of power, as a means of engaging with rather than resolving the empowerment paradox. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Compact broadband low-frequency sound absorption using coupled folded side-slit Helmholtz resonators with dual-peak multimodal resonances
abstract: In order to achieve efficient broadband low-frequency sound absorption within strict volume constraints, a compact absorber based on a two-cavity folded side-slit Helmholtz resonator (FSHR-2C) is proposed. The dual-cavity architecture, integrated with two independently tunable perforations, enables staggered resonances that anchor the low-frequency absorption edge and provides an additional tunable high-frequency response associated with the folded side-slit branch. Additionally, Helmholtz resonators with side slits (HRSS) are introduced as valley-filling elements to improve the continuity of the absorption spectrum through coupling with the FSHR-2C. A transfer matrix model incorporating thermoviscous losses in both slits and perforations is established, and its accuracy is validated by finite-element simulations. Furthermore, a coupled optimization framework based on sequential quadratic programming (SQP) is developed. By exploiting the high tunability of the unit cells and incorporating geometric feasibility constraints through piecewise penalty functions, the optimized theoretical absorber achieves an absorption coefficient above 0.8 in the frequency range from 250 Hz to 600 Hz and also exhibits a secondary high-frequency absorption region around 830 Hz to 970 Hz. Impedance-tube measurements further confirm the main two-region absorption behavior, showing good agreement with the theoretical prediction in the main absorption bands. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Justifying membership fees through quality and pricing in a competitive supply chain
abstract: While membership-based retail has experienced substantial growth, how membership stores can justify membership fees through product quality remains underexplored from a supply chain perspective. This study examines a supply chain consisting of a manufacturer, a membership store, and a traditional retailer, where consumers differ in their perceived value of exclusive membership services and may exhibit the sunk cost effect generated by the prepaid membership fees. We investigate how this behavioural mechanism affects retail pricing and the manufacturer's quality investment. The results show that the sunk cost effect not only reshapes the membership store's pricing strategy but also affects the manufacturer's quality investment decision, thereby enabling the membership store to justify its membership fee. The equilibrium outcomes are jointly determined by the membership store's competitive advantage and the perceived membership fee. Based on these two dimensions, we derive a strategic decision matrix comprising four equilibrium regimes. We use several business cases to help understand how membership stores can adjust their quality and pricing decisions according to their specific characteristics to justify membership fees. This study thus translates analytical results into a managerial framework and provides managerial insights for membership stores’ strategic decision-making. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A Socio-Technical Lens on AI Adoption: Role Conflict and Ambiguity in Large Organizations
abstract: Although AI adoption in private, daily use is accelerating, many initiatives in large organizations stall at the pilot stage and fail to reach production at scale, despite technical optimization. This study examines how heterogeneous organizational roles across business, technical, and functional domains experience role conflict and role ambiguity during AI adoption, and how these role tensions shape adoption outcomes. Based on semi-structured interviews with twelve professionals representing business, technical, and functional organizational roles involved in AI adoption, the Gioia methodology is applied to surface recurrent role conflicts (e.g., business expectations versus technical feasibility; novelty vs. business value) and role ambiguities (e.g., unclear stakeholder responsibilities, risk ownership, and decision-making authority). Substantial inter-coder reliability (κ = 0.74) supports the consistency of the analysis. By integrating Socio-Technical Systems Theory and Role Conflict Theory, a role-based socio-technical lens is proposed that explains why technically sound AI projects stall when role tensions remain unresolved during the simultaneous engagement of heterogeneous organizational roles. The study contributes a typology of role conflicts and role ambiguities, and discusses their implications for role clarity, decision rights, and cross-functional collaboration. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: To Twin or Not to Twin? A Digital Twin Readiness Framework for SMEs
abstract: Digital twin (DT) technology has rapidly matured into a cornerstone of Industry 4.0 and cyber-physical systems. Yet many small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and research laboratories struggle with when, not how, to adopt digital twins. The challenge extends beyond technology to encompass business necessity, data readiness, predictive requirements, organisational decision structures, and cost-value considerations. This study introduces the Effective Digital Twin Readiness (EDTR) framework, a structured decision instrument that integrates measurable variables across four dimensions (Business necessity, Data readiness, Model & prediction requirements, and Organisational readiness) to determine whether a digital twin should be pursued, deferred, or approached through a pilot implementation. To operationalise EDTR, a decision-support chatbot will be developed to guide stakeholders through structured input, scoring, and tailored recommendations. The study further provides historical context, a literature review, case archetypes, prototype conversation flow, and a critical evaluation of limitations and future research directions, offering a comprehensive reference for both researchers and practitioners. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Neuroprotective, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuromodulatory effects of Calliandra portoricensis root bark ethanol extract against carbon tetrachloride-induced neurotoxicity in male Wistar rats
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Calliandra portoricensis (Jacq.) Benth. is used in the ethnomedicine of southwestern Nigeria in treating epilepsy, convulsion, pain, inflammatory disorders, fever and other neurological conditions. However, its neuroprotective potential has not been adequately investigated. Aim of the study: This study evaluated the neuroprotective, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuromodulatory effects of Calliandra portoricensis root bark ethanol extract (CPRBEE) against carbon tetrachloride (CCl4)-induced neurotoxicity in male Wistar rats. Materials and methods: CPRBEE was characterized using phytochemical screening and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS). Thirty-five male Wistar rats were randomly allotted to seven groups (n = 5). Neurotoxicity was induced with CCl4 (1.3 mL/kg; 3:10 v/v in olive oil). Following induction, rats received vitamin C (200 mg/kg) or CPRBEE (10, 20, 30, and 40 mg/kg). Neurobehavioral performance, oxidative stress biomarkers, acetylcholinesterase activity, inflammatory cytokines, neuronal injury markers, trace metal concentrations, Nrf2, HO-1, NF-κB, BDNF concentrations, and histopathological changes were evaluated. Results: GC–MS analysis tentatively annotated several phytochemicals, including phytol, β-sitosterol, stigmasterol, squalene, and a vitamin E (tocopherol derivative) peak consistent with α-tocopherol. CCl4 exposure significantly increased lipid peroxidation, acetylcholinesterase activity, pro-inflammatory cytokines, NSE, GFAP, and NF-κB concentrations, while reducing antioxidant defenses, Nrf2, HO-1, and BDNF concentrations (p < 0.05). CPRBEE attenuated these alterations, improved behavioural performance, partially restored trace-element profiles, and reduced histopathological alterations, with the magnitude of effects varying across biomarkers and treatment levels. Conclusion: CPRBEE demonstrated neuroprotective activity against CCl4-induced neurotoxicity, potentially through attenuation of oxidative stress and inflammation while preserving antioxidant and neurotrophic defenses, supporting its traditional applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: WGLE: Backdoor-free and multi-bit black-box watermarking for graph neural networks
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are increasingly deployed, making ownership verification critical for protecting their intellectual property against model theft. Fingerprinting and black-box watermarking are two main methods. However, the former relies on determining model similarity, which is computationally expensive and prone to ownership collisions after model post-processing. The latter embeds backdoors, exposing watermarked models to the risk of backdoor attacks. Moreover, both previous methods enable ownership verification but do not convey additional information, limiting verification efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes WGLE, a novel black-box watermarking paradigm for GNNs that enables embedding the multi-bit string in GNN models without using backdoors. WGLE builds on a key insight we term Layer-wise Distance Difference on an Edge (LDDE), which quantifies the difference between the feature distance and the prediction distance of two connected nodes in a graph. By assigning unique LDDE values to the edges and employing the LDDE sequence as the watermark, WGLE supports multi-bit capacity without relying on backdoor mechanisms. We evaluated WGLE on six public datasets across six mainstream GNN architectures. Compared to state-of-the-art GNN watermarking and fingerprinting methods, WGLE achieves perfect ownership verification accuracy with marginal fidelity degradation and exhibits robust resilience against potential ownership attacks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Comparative Analysis of Classical and Large-Scale Multilingual Speech Synthesis Models for Saudi Arabic Dialect
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have been recently integrated with the speech modality for enhancing the naturalness and expressiveness of generated speech. Nevertheless, the performance of these LLM-based Text-To-Speech (TTS) models in morphologically rich, dialectally diverse languages such as Arabic has not been extensively discussed yet. In this work, we compare the conventional and LLM approaches for speech synthesis in Saudi Arabia. The fine-tuning set, a proprietary 43-hour single-speaker dataset drawn from Intellas’ internal business recordings and not made publicly available, is used to fine-tune four Text-To-Speech models: the classical Tacotron 2 and three LLM-based architectures, Sesame_CSM_1B, Orpheus_3B, and Spark_TTS_0.5B, which are trained under the same fine-tuning framework for methodological consistency. Evaluation included automatic metrics such as Word Error Rate (WER), Character Error Rate (CER), and accuracy, along with similarity scores, which are calculated based on Intella Voice Speech-To-Text (STT) model, and the agreement by native Saudi speakers through perceptual listening tests. Moreover, Statistical analysis via paired t-tests (N = 3322 utterances) revealed highly significant performance differences (p< 0.001) between LLM-based models and classical architectures across all automatic evaluation metrics. Experiments showed that LLM-based models (Spark_TTS_0.5B & Orpheus_3B) performed better in terms of intelligibility and prosody, with a WER of 23.4% ± 0.19 (t = – 39.51, p< 0.001) *** & 28.1% ± 0.21 (t = – 29.14, p< 0.001) *** and hence a CER of 11% ± 0.12 (t = – 33.15, p< 0.001) *** & 14.3% ± 0.14 (t = – 24.52, p< 0.001) ***, than the fine-tuned Tacotron 2 (baseline), which achieved a WER of 44.3% ± 0.24 and a CER of 25% ± 0.20. They showed that dialectal fine-tuning of language models substantially improves Saudi Arabic synthesis quality across naturalness, intelligibility, and prosodic dimensions, with task-specific dialectal adaptation appearing as a critical success factor alongside pretraining foundations and architectural design. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The effectiveness of industrial gamma and e-beam sources, to inactivate B. pumilus spores in the presence of liquid water and considerations for validation of sterilization dose in accordance with ISO 11137
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of industrial electron beam (e-beam) and gamma irradiators in inactivating Bacillus pumilus spores at varying levels of water availability. Commercially available B. pumilus spore strips were exposed to three hydration conditions: dry, immersed in saturated NaCl solution, or immersed in purified water, and subsequently irradiated. Gamma operated at a dose rate of 1 kGy/h, while the dose rate of e-beam was 1800 kGy/h. The results showed that gamma and e-beam irradiation were equally effective ( p = 0.111) in inactivating dry B. pumilus spores. These findings suggest that, provided the validated minimum dose is delivered, the dose may be transferred between industrial radiation sources without compromising product sterility, assuming no liquid water is present. In contrast, e-beam was more efficient than gamma in inactivating spores in saturated NaCl solution ( p = 0.007) and spores in water ( p = 0.009). It was observed that spore resistance increased with increasing water availability. The protective effect of water may have important implications for dose qualification strategies in sterilization processes. In the industrial sterilization of medical devices, the dose is often qualified by using Method 1/VDmax25, defined in ISO 11137. Method 1/VDmaxdose setting relies on the assumption that the product bioburden exhibits resistance to ionizing radiation that is consistent with the Standard Distribution of Resistance (SDR). If due to the presence of water, the resistance of the bioburden exceeds that of the SDR, Method 2 of ISO 11137-2:2013 should be used instead. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Leadership succession and corporate social responsibility in family firms
abstract: This study investigates the impact of CEO succession on corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance in family firms. Drawing on socioemotional wealth perspective, we argue that CEO succession creates tension between financial accountability and non-financial objectives as successors seek to establish legitimacy and maintain organizational stability. During this period, successors are likely to prioritize financial accountability, organizational continuity, and family control, reducing attention to reputational objectives maintained through CSR. We further propose that external pressures, including peer firms’ CSR practices and media attention, moderate this relationship by increasing the legitimacy costs of reducing CSR engagement. Using data from Chinese family firms, we find that CSR performance declines significantly one to two years after succession. This negative relationship is stronger when external pressure is weak but is mitigated, and may even reverse, under stronger peer and media pressures. Our findings demonstrate how family firms balance financial and non-financial objectives during leadership transitions. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: A data-informed scaling parameterization for non-Fickian retention in atmospheric boundary-layer dispersion
abstract: Pollutant dispersion in the planetary boundary layer is usually simulated with the advection–diffusion equation closed by the gradient-diffusion hypothesis, in which the turbulent flux follows the local concentration gradient. In the convective boundary layer it cannot represent transport driven by thermals spanning the full depth of the layer. The Bevilacqua–Galeão bi-flux model separates the material into a fraction that diffuses classically and a retained fraction that does not follow the local gradient, introducing a fourth-order term governed by a retention coefficient Kz2. In previous applications Kz2 was treated as a constant, with no means of relating it to the state of the boundary layer. Here the equation is solved by a high-order implicit finite-difference scheme, and a constrained Bayesian optimization identifies the parameters best reproducing the Copenhagen and Prairie Grass tracer experiments. Dimensional analysis of these optima yields Kz2(x) in terms of the friction velocity, boundary-layer depth, source height and downwind distance, so that the coefficient is specified in advance from routine meteorological data and grows as the plume travels downwind. The same expression covers the 115 m elevated release at Copenhagen and the near-surface release at Prairie Grass with no constant adjusted to either. When it is prescribed, the absolute fractional bias falls by 57% and 27% respectively, and the normalized mean square error by 12.7% and 17.3%, while other performance measures are preserved. The scaling was determined based on the optimization results, and the validated range is limited to the source heights considered in the tests. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Implementation of Clean Architecture to Reduce Coupling in an Accessible Intelligent Robotics Programming Assistant
abstract: The lack of clear standards for designing software architectures in intelligent assistants geared toward accessible robotics programming has led to solutions with high coupling, limited scalability, and poor adaptability to accessibility requirements, directly affecting people with visual impairments, who face significant barriers in environments traditionally reliant on graphical interfaces. In this context, we propose an architecture based on Clean Architecture, complemented by the Observer pattern, which organizes the system into layers with dependencies on the domain core, decoupling business logic through the Dependency Inversion Principle. The proposal is conceptually validated through an analysis of its structural properties, demonstrating reduced coupling, improved modularity, and ease of integrating alternative interfaces such as voice assistants, contributing to the development of inclusive, maintainable, and adaptable solutions. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Cross-Channel effects of online reputation and offline event participation in B2B Platforms: Synergy or Attenuation?
abstract: This study examines how online reputation and offline event participation jointly relate to seller performance on B2B platforms. Although omnichannel research often predicts online–offline synergy, the interaction between these channels remains underexplored in B2B platform settings. Drawing on media richness theory and anchoring logic, we view both channels as distinct yet potentially overlapping credibility cues. Using 30 months of operational data from sellers on a leading Chinese B2B platform, we find that both are positively associated with seller performance, but their interaction is negative: the conditional association of each mechanism weakens as the other strengthens. Online reputation also has a stronger average association with performance. These findings identify cross-channel attenuation as a boundary condition of omnichannel complementarity, suggesting that one salient credibility cue may reduce the other’s incremental informational value. The study contributes to B2B omnichannel research and informs online–offline investment allocation. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: From academic integrity to credential integrity: What does management education certify once artificial intelligence can produce the work?
abstract: The debate on generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) in management education has centered on whether students may use AI, yet the larger question is what student work can still prove. Once AI can draft and polish a case analysis, an essay, or slides, polished work stops being strong evidence of what a student can do. This article calls the resulting problem credential integrity (i.e., whether a business school can defend what its degree certifies when AI may have produced the graded work). Policies on detection, disclosure, and originality cannot solve this problem, given that all three ask who produced the work and leave intact the assumption that good work proves a capable student. In response, this article draws on assessment scholarship, policy research, and validity theory to propose a verified-judgment architecture in which high-stakes certification rests on unaided command of core concepts and methods, reasoning defended when questioned, positions reconsidered when challenged, learning transferred to changed conditions, and accountable decision making. The architecture is translated into program-level responsibilities for school leaders and redesigned assessments for teachers, neither of which requires a ban on AI or the false belief that an AI-free submission proves learning. A reality check of 84 business schools shows how far practice is from this standard, given that schools describe AI access, curriculum integration, and faculty development more fully than any proof of what the degree certifies and only one school in seven reports a safeguard (e.g., a defended capstone or work kept free of AI). © 2026 The Author

title: Benzylbiphenyl-regulated poly(aromatic ethylimidazole)s toward high-performance high temperature proton exchange membranes in fuel cells
abstract: The development of high temperature proton exchange membranes (HT-PEMs) with simultaneously enhanced proton transport and mechanical robustness remains a major challenge for HT-PEM fuel cells. Herein, we report a molecular backbone engineering strategy based on the incorporation of 4-benzylbiphenyl (BBP) units into poly(p-terphenyl ethylimidazole) frameworks to regulate chain conformation and membrane properties. A series of BBP-containing P(TPx%-BBPy%-EIm) copolymers with systematically varied compositions are synthesized via a superacid-catalyzed Friedel-Crafts polymerization, enabling an in-depth investigation of the relationship between backbone architecture and membrane performance. Experimental characterization and theoretical calculations reveal that the sp3-hybridized methylene bridge in BBP disrupts continuous π-conjugation and induces a twisted, flexible polymer configuration, which enhances phosphoric acid (PA) affinity, promotes microphase separation, and facilitates proton conduction. Among the resulting membranes, P(TP70%-BBP30%-EIm)/214%PA achieves an optimized balance between conductivity and mechanical integrity, exhibiting a tensile strength of 15.7 MPa and a proton conductivity of 104 mS cm−1 at 180 °C under anhydrous conditions. When integrated into an H2/O2 membrane electrode assembly, this membrane delivers a peak power density of 783 mW cm−2 at 180 °C under non-humidified and zero-backpressure conditions, which also display a 144-h durability under 200 mA cm−2 at 160 °C. This work establishes flexible benzylbiphenyl-containing poly(aromatic ethylimidazole) polymers as a promising platform for HT-PEMs in fuel cells and also provides a molecular design strategy for developing advanced membrane materials for other new energy devices. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Who are my people and what can I do? Community remapping for entrepreneurial venturing after forced migration
abstract: Scholarship on post-disruption adaptation largely assumes conditions of partial disruption—situations where despite losing access to one or multiple domains, other important domains remain intact. Yet wholesale disruptions pose a qualitatively different challenge for entrepreneurship. We explore how experiences of wholesale disruption shape actors' reconstruction of their contextual structure, perceived scope of their entrepreneurial possibility space, and the long-term trajectory of their ventures. We conduct an inductive study of the venturing efforts of refugees following their wholesale disruption caused by forced migration to the USA. We develop a grounded theoretical model of community remapping for venturing after wholesale disruption that explains why some refugees enact dynamic, growing ventures while others enact more stable, static ventures and eschew growth aspirations. Our findings and theorizing contribute to literatures on venturing in response to wholesale disruptions and on refugee entrepreneurship. © 2026 The Authors.

title: CGMR-DSR: Cross-graph multi-relational dynamic social recommendation
abstract: Classical recommendation approaches, including matrix factorization and conventional graph-based social recommendation models, mainly rely on historical user-item interactions or a single social-link view. As a result, they often fail to jointly exploit interaction and social graphs, combine direct social links with behavior-derived similarity links, and capture the temporal evolution of user preferences. To address these limitations, this paper proposes CGMR-DSR, a cross-graph multi-relational dynamic social recommendation model. The main contributions are threefold. First, CGMR-DSR models two complementary social relation types and employs basis decomposition-enhanced R-GCN to learn relation-aware social representations with controlled parameter complexity. Second, it performs direct bidirectional feature exchange between shared user nodes in the interaction and social graphs, followed by user-item graph propagation that transfers the social-enhanced user signals to items. Third, it integrates LSTM-based temporal modeling and adaptive alignment loss to capture dynamic preference evolution and suppress noisy social influence. Experiments on seven benchmark datasets evaluate the competitiveness of CGMR-DSR against representative and recent baselines on HR@10 and NDCG@10, together with ablation analyses of its major components. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Water rights allocation in water-receiving districts of the central line project of the south-to-north water diversion, China: a hybrid multi-criteria decision framework
abstract: Water competition in the Water-Receiving Districts (WRDs) of the Central Line Project of the South-to-North Water Diversion (CLP-SNWD) has intensified, highlighting the urgent need for a new water rights (WR) allocation scheme. This study proposes a hybrid multi-criteria decision framework that integrates triangular fuzzy numbers (TrFNs) to improve linguistic-to-numerical conversion, with expert weights to distinguish heterogeneous expertise. In addition, time weights are introduced to capture the dynamic impacts of regional development on WR allocation. Finally, the MARCOS method is employed using data from 2010 to 2022 to generate allocation results. The findings show that: (1) the new scheme prioritizes strategic cities such as Beijing, Tianjin, Zhengzhou, and Shijiazhuang, while assigning fewer WR to cities such as Pingdingshan, Hebi, Nanyang, Zhoukou, Luohe, and Hengshui; (2) compared to the current plan, the new allocation decreases WR for Beijing and Tianjin, while increasing those for Henan Province, thereby better reflecting the practical needs and improving acceptance across regions; (3) by incorporating the principle of government macro-control, the new framework balances the needs of both strategic and economically disadvantaged areas, enhancing fairness and feasibility. Overall, the proposed framework contributes to methodological innovation by combining fuzzy logic, expert systems, and time-sensitive weighting, and provides practical insights for conflict mitigation and sustainable water resources management in large-scale inter-basin diversion projects. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: A novel Index-Organized storage model for modern in-memory database systems
abstract: Large-scale data-intensive applications require high-throughput real-time data processing. Modern in-memory database systems maintain the primary data copy in main memory and support fast concurrent transactions and analytics on recent data. However, under hybrid workloads with long-running queries, pointer-chasing overhead becomes a major bottleneck that prevents these systems from sustaining high performance.In this work, we investigate the pointer-chasing bottleneck in modern in-memory database systems and propose a novel Index-Organized storage model for efficient reads and writes. Its key innovation is storing the latest versions within the leaf nodes of the tree index, combined with a cacheline-aligned node layout and cache-prefetching-assisted version chains, improving pointer chasing performance. We present three optimizations, i.e., pending version table, fine-grained memory management, and Index-SSN algorithm for supporting efficient transaction processing. We implement Index-Organized on an open-source in-memory database system. Experimental results show that Index-Organized achieves up to a 3× speedup over conventional row-store, column-store, and hybrid row-column storage models. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Enhancing the social innovation ecosystem: university-led incubation pathways for rural sustainability
abstract: Universities are increasingly called upon to contribute to sustainability transitions, yet their roles as active intermediaries within social innovation ecosystems remain under-theorised. This study examines how universities can incubate social innovations that advance rural sustainability. Using an exploratory, theory-building case study, we draw on interviews, documents and observational materials from multiple rural revitalisation initiatives led by The University of Hong Kong to identify how incubation processes configure relationships, mobilise resources and reshape institutional environments. Our analysis reveals three distinct incubation pathways, stewardship, platforms and communities, which differ in their locus of intervention, the types of social capital they generate and the institutional roles the university performs. Stewardship initiatives cultivate bonding capital by transforming individuals into rural change agents through experiential learning and place-based engagement. Platform initiatives build bridging capital by providing shared infrastructures that connect rural and urban actors, lowering market and regulatory barriers. Community-focused initiatives mobilise linking capital, enabling collective governance arrangements and facilitating negotiation across local and institutional boundaries. Synthesising these findings, we develop a configurational framework of university supported social innovation incubation that elucidates how these pathways operate through different forms of institutional work across community and institutional boundaries. The framework demonstrates how universities, when locally embedded and institutionally trusted, can orchestrate multiple, complementary pathways that cumulatively reshape social innovation ecosystems. We discuss implications for sustainability transitions scholarship and for designing context-sensitive incubation strategies in underserved or peripheral regions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: A knowledge graph and hierarchical learning framework for food safety risk identification and traceability: A case study on meat products
abstract: Food safety risk analysis is challenged by fragmented information among regulatory standards, production processes, and inspection data, which limits the integrated understanding of risk characteristics and potential origins. This study proposes an integrated framework for food safety risk identification and traceability by integrating knowledge representation and data-driven inference. A dual-layer knowledge graph (DLKG) was constructed to bridge food safety standards (as constraint knowledge) with Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP)-based process knowledge (as a mechanism layer), enabling cross-layer reasoning from detection indicators to Critical Control Points (CCPs). To address imbalanced and long-tail distributions in inspection data, a Hierarchical Cascade Ensemble Learning (HCEL) model was developed to perform hierarchical risk identification, including category recognition and fine-grained indicator inference, with attention-based feature representation and a Top-k constraint strategy. A large language model was further employed to organize model outputs and retrieved knowledge into coherent textual outputs, without contributing to decision-making. Using 5995 non-compliant meat-product records, HCEL achieved 91.99% Top-1 and 98.42% Top-2 accuracy for risk-category identification, with Macro-F1 and Macro-Recall exceeding 85%. Hit@3 and MRR for specific risk indicators reached 83.82% and 73.51%, respectively. Temporal out-of-sample validation showed some performance degradation when 2024 inspection data were used for testing, but HCEL generally maintained better performance than the comparative models. The proposed framework enhances the identification and interpretation of non-compliance patterns and may support risk-oriented inspection prioritization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Cross-Boundary Practices within the Construction Industry: The Case of the Quantity Surveyors
abstract: The evolving dynamics of the construction industry have sharpened the need for quantity surveyors (QSs) to reinterpret their role, expanding beyond traditional commercial management practices to encompass broader strategic functions such as value optimization and interdisciplinary collaboration. At the same time, professional overlaps and cross-boundary practices have become an increasing challenge to the quantity surveying profession, leading to potential conflicts and quality compromises in construction projects. However, there is markedly less research on the negative effects of cross-boundary practices for the quantity surveying profession, particularly regarding professional identity and long-term industry implications. Therefore, this study aims to recognize the challenges posed to the quantity surveying profession by cross-boundary practices and to examine the underlying reasons for these challenges. A comprehensive literature review and 25 semistructured interviews were conducted with two samples: QS professionals and non-QS professionals, to collect data. The content analysis method was used to analyze the gathered data. The core quantity surveying functions, such as taking off quantities, preparing bills of quantities, and contract administration, are increasingly performed by non-QS professionals in the construction industry. Even if there are positive effects, including knowledge transfer and reducing the scarcity of QSs through cross-boundary practices, the negative consequences, such as lowering project quality and harming the professional image of QSs, were found to be more significant. By empirically investigating the causes and effects of cross-boundary practices in quantity surveying, this study addresses an overlooked vulnerability in the construction industry and fills a critical gap in the literature on professional role integrity and industry standards. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.
