title: CSR focus under competitive pressure: The role of national institutions
abstract: How does competitive pressure shape CSR strategy, and does this relationship vary across national institutional contexts? We challenge the prevailing binary framing that competitive pressure either promotes or suppresses CSR by arguing that competition reshapes how firms configure their CSR portfolios, not merely how much they engage. We introduce CSR focus strategy: a firm's selective emphasis on specific CSR dimensions while deliberately de-emphasizing others, allowing simultaneous differentiation and cost-economization through CSR under some conditions. Employing multilevel linear modeling (MLM) on a global dataset of 41 countries comprising 2294 firms from 2002 to 2020, we demonstrate that competitive intensity drives adoption of CSR focus strategy. Critically, this effect is contingent on national market-supporting institutions and firm size, where CSR focus strategies are most pronounced in institutionally weaker environments characterized by limited property rights protection and among smaller firms with limited stakeholder relational capital and opportunities. Further analyses reveal two subtypes, namely CSR excellence and CSR distinction , reflecting different portfolio configurations under competition. By establishing that institutional context shapes firms' CSR portfolio configuration under competition, our study advances international business research and reconciles opposing theoretical positions in the competition-CSR debate. Collectively, these findings extend the emerging portfolio-based view of CSR into the cross-country competitive domain. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: The Type III realisation conjecture of Kirkland and Šmigoc
abstract: Kirkland and Šmigoc constructed a family of stochastic matrices realising the Type III boundary polynomials of the Karpelevič region and conjectured that, conversely, every stochastic realisation of such a polynomial must come from their construction. We prove this conjecture for the full nonzero parameter range 0<α≤1, for the reduced Ito polynomials fα(x)=xy(xq−(1−α))d−αd,n=qd+y, associated with Type III Farey-neighbour arcs of order n. For 0<α<1, the boundary theorem of Dmitriev and Dynkin restricts the possible nonzero entries of a realising matrix. After relabelling the vertices, its directed graph consists of the edges i→i+n1 and a selection of edges i→i+n(n+1−q), with indices taken modulo n. Coates' coefficient formula and a weighted form of Turán's theorem then show that the directed cycles of length q fall into d classes. Any two cycles in the same class share a vertex, while cycles in different classes have no vertices in common. Each class has the same sum of cycle weights, where the weight of a cycle is the product of its edge weights. The positions of these cycles along the n-cycle then yield the product condition required by Kirkland and Šmigoc. The case α=1 is treated separately, and an explanation is provided for the failure when α=0. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Beyond psychology and environment explanations: a linguistic microfoundation approach to entrepreneurs’ anxiety
abstract: We offer a novel theoretical account of why entrepreneurs experience anxiety and how entrepreneurs cope with anxiety. We integrate insights from linguistic theories into entrepreneurship literature to propose that entrepreneurs’ linguistic architecture—particularly the vocabulary their language provides for identifying and describing emotions (i.e., its emotion lexicon)—is an essential linguistic microfoundation that systematically shapes how entrepreneurs process and experience anxiety. As moderators, we examine how bilingualism and entrepreneurial experience can systematically alter how entrepreneurs’ linguistic architecture influences their anxiety. Our final sample was 1,251 entrepreneurs speaking 14 different languages, supplemented by an experimental study with 202 bilingual entrepreneurs in Hong Kong. We find that entrepreneurs with a richer vocabulary for identifying and describing emotions (i.e., a richer emotion lexicon) heighten anxiety due to more precise and vivid emotional processing, and bilingualism weakens, yet prior entrepreneurial experience strengthens the positive effect of emotion lexicon on anxiety. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Experimental impact study on a micro-grid project in rural Madagascar: The Café Lumière project
abstract: This paper evaluates the impact of a pilot innovative project aiming at promoting a replicable model to create access to distributed electricity in rural areas where grid extension is economically infeasible. The project proposes building solar-powered micro-grids to provide affordable electricity and basic electricity services to households, businesses, and public services. The pilot nature of the project was conceived to facilitate a rigorous testing of its developmental impacts, contrasting with the existing evaluation literature, which provides at best descriptive conclusions. The evaluation methodology is based on a randomized control trial (RCT) design, with data collected before and after project implementation through two waves of household surveys in 2017–2018 and 2023, complemented by locality data. The experimental dimension of the paper is based on a treatment implemented at the locality level. A dozen of comparable localities had been initially selected after a common pre-feasibility study as suitable for the project, and the project has been randomly implemented in only half of them. Findings reveal notable improvements in household access to electricity, particularly in the use of modern energy services like lighting and phone charging. The project has also triggered nascent new economic activities, especially secondary income-generating occupations, though the overall impact on household wealth remains limited. Social outcomes have seen mixed results, with only significant improvements in health and none in education. Complementary actions mentioned in the project's theory of change but not fully implemented may be needed to achieve the broader economic and social transformation initially anticipated. © 2026 International Energy Initiative

title: MCA-SSL: A synergistic fusion-optimization-alignment loop for incomplete multi-view clustering
abstract: The missing of views in multi-view data brings challenges to multi-view clustering, such as how to deal with missing views, how to fuse cross-view information, and how to learn clustering-oriented representation. To address these, we propose MCA-SSL, a free-imputation model for incomplete multi-view clustering (IMVC). MCA-SSL integrates mutual cross-attention mechanism (MCA), self-supervised learning (SSL), and global representation and label learning (GRLL), where MCA aims to fuse view-specific representations in a two-way mode for extracting cross-view complementary information in more detail, SSL focuses on optimizing the fused representation by combing contrastive and predictive learning for improving the quality of the view-specific representations, and GRLL is responsible for unifying the feature learning with the clustering task in a framework though contrasting the global representation and pseudo-label with view-specific representations and pseudo-labels for promoting clustering-oriented representations and improving clustering performance. The missing values of samples are initialized by random values, and their representations are iteratively optimized by SSL, which alleviates the difficulty of directly filling the missing values in original data space and enhances the robustness to view incompleteness. The entire process forms a “fusion-optimization-alignment” synergistic loop, providing an integrated learning framework and end-to-end trainable paradigm for IMVC. Extensive experiments on seven benchmark datasets demonstrate that MCA-SSL significantly outperforms baselines. More importantly, ablation studies confirm that the performance gain stems from the effective collaboration, not merely the juxtaposition of its key components. The source code is available at https://github.com/Yuanjing-03/MCA-SSL.git . © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Integrable elasticity via neural demand potentials
abstract: We propose the Integrable Context-Dependent Demand Network (ICDN), a demand-first neural model for multiproduct retail demand. ICDN learns log-demand as a smooth, context-conditioned function of log-prices, allowing elasticities to be derived exactly from the learned demand surface. Across three retail datasets, the model achieves competitive out-of-sample prediction while producing analytically tractable, and economically regularized own- and cross-price responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Driving low-carbon technology diffusion in heterogeneous steel enterprises through carbon emissions trading: An evolutionary game analysis
abstract: Subjected to the carbon neutrality goal, the carbon emissions trading scheme (CETS) has become an essential market-oriented tool for carbon emission reduction in high-emission sectors like the steel industry through the diffusion of low-carbon technologies. However, the heterogeneous responses to CETS across enterprises of different scales remain unclear, limiting the differentiated policy design. This study presents a tripartite evolutionary game model involving the government, large-scale steel enterprise (LSE), and small-scale steel enterprise (SSE) to investigate the low-carbon technology diffusion driven by CETS. By incorporating enterprise-scale heterogeneity like innovation capacity, financing constraints, risk preferences, and policy responsiveness, the model examines the evolutionary pathways of technology adoption under various policy and market conditions. The results show that the evolutionary trajectory of low-carbon technology adoption follows a staged framework but a non-sequential progression, encompassing four distinct scenarios including low-incentive, government-driven promotion, multi-stakeholder collaborative adoption, and industry self-regulation. Shifts between these scenarios are contingent on the interplay of carbon price, quota allocation and other policies considering scale heterogeneity. LSE is highly sensitive to carbon price, while SSE requires relatively light quota constraints combined with sufficiently high carbon price to overcome the barriers for technology diffusion. Furthermore, when collaboration costs fall below a certain threshold, it can effectively shorten the cycle of corporate strategic adjustments, prompting businesses to swiftly transition from partial adoption to comprehensive implementation of low-carbon technologies. This study provides the theoretical understanding of CETS-induced technology diffusion and targeted policy insights for advancing the low-carbon transformation of the steel industry. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Incomplete markets, crop portfolios, and agricultural productivity
abstract: Using the Uganda National Panel Survey, I document that farmers face a trade-off between crop yields and risk, that most grow both high- and low-yield crops, and that poorer farmers concentrate on the low-yield, low-risk ones. I then develop an incomplete-markets model with a crop-portfolio choice, in which households trade off income returns against consumption smoothing. Wealth-poor households optimally under-invest in intermediates and shift toward safer crops. Crop portfolios, intermediate input use, and the wealth distribution are jointly determined in equilibrium. The model also reproduces the low pass-through of both income inequality and income volatility into consumption. Calibrated to rural Uganda, it implies that completing markets raises agricultural productivity by 12.8%, with 15.8% of the gain coming from eliminating the misallocation of inputs across farmers and crops. Consumption rises by 17.6% and welfare by 17.4%, with income inequality rising slightly and consumption inequality unchanged. © 2026 The Author

title: Stochastic inversion of multivariate uniform-distribution-preserving transformations
abstract: A multivariate transformation of the unit cube with component transformations that are piecewise continuously differentiable and uniform distribution preserving (udp) is considered. A stochastic inverse transformation is defined using randomization to overcome the non-injective nature of the udp transformations. The inverse transformation preserves the uniform margins of a random vector distributed according to a copula and yields different copulas for different randomizations. A copula density transformation result for the multivariate stochastic inverse is proved and illustrated in the bivariate case. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: From search results to generative answers: A mixed-methods study of credibility assessment and trust formation in AI Overviews
abstract: Generative search shifts information evaluation from comparing ranked documents to assessing synthesised answers. This study examines how users’ perceptions of answer quality are associated with trust and credibility in Google AI Overviews and explores whether visible interface cues may foster trust without systematic source verification. Study 1 analysed survey data from 510 Spanish users using a consistent partial least squares structural equation modelling approach. Study 2 combined eye tracking and interviews with 20 Spanish users. The model explained 75.7% of the variance in trust and 91.0% of the variance in credibility. Clarity and context (β = .419, p < .001) and access to additional information and supporting sources (β = .335, p = .002) showed the strongest observed associations with trust, whereas response immediacy was not significant (β = .008, p = .874). Trust (β = .834) and perceived usefulness (β = .229) were positively associated with credibility (both p < .001), which, in turn, was associated with recommendation following (β = .877) and intention to use (β = .553; both p < .001). Eye tracking recorded no analysable fixations on the AI-error warning, while the interviews indicated that participants in this subsample did not routinely verify the displayed sources and often interpreted visible references as indicators of reliability. Taken together, Study 1 identifies associations between perceived answer-quality cues, trust, and credibility, whereas Study 2 suggests that visual prominence and visible references appeared to operate as authority cues for some participants and may encourage reliance without active source verification. © 2026 The Authors. title: Large language models in Scrum management: A practitioner survey of use, perceived benefits, risks, and human–AI collaboration
abstract: Context: Scrum management includes knowledge-intensive activities such as backlog refinement, event preparation, and stakeholder alignment. Large language model (LLM) chat assistants may support these activities, but empirical evidence remains limited. Objective: This study investigates practitioners’ self-reported LLM use in Scrum management, perceived benefits and risks, and expectations for human–AI collaboration. Methods: We conducted a practitioner survey, and the results are based on a final analytic sample of 79 respondents who reported using LLM chat assistants in Scrum management. Closed-ended items were analyzed descriptively; open-ended responses underwent thematic coding. Results: In this sample, 48.1% reported daily or almost daily use, and 79.7% rated their LLM knowledge as at least qualified. Reported use centered on backlog refinement, event summarization, and Scrum-practice exploration. Perceived benefits included productivity (77.2%), reduced repetitive-task time (75.9%), and artifact quality (74.7%). Reported problems included almost-correct outputs (65.8%), hallucinations (54.4%), privacy concerns (50.6%), and content-validation difficulty (46.8%). Most respondents envisioned human-led or balanced human–AI collaboration (81.0%); 65.8% selected the no-role-replacement option. Conclusion: Respondents describe LLM chat assistants as complementary tools in Scrum management, particularly for text-intensive and analytical tasks, while emphasizing the continued need for human judgment, validation, and oversight. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: From institutional pressures to employee involvement in organizational sustainability: The role of common good HRM
abstract: Employee involvement in organizational sustainability is critical to achieving long-term environmental, social, and economic goals, yet the drivers of such involvement remain underexplored. Drawing on institutional theory and social exchange theory, this study develops a cross-level serial mediation model to explain how institutional sustainability pressures may become associated with employee involvement in organizational sustainability. We propose that institutional pressures, as perceived by senior executives, are associated with employee-experienced common good human resource management (CG-HRM), which in turn relates to perceived organizational support and, subsequently, employee involvement in organizational sustainability. Using time-lagged, multisource survey data from 96 firms in China, we find support for the proposed model. The findings contribute a more micro-foundational account of how institutional sustainability pressures, as perceived by senior executives, may become meaningful at the employee level through organizational and psychological processes, and clarify the role of employee-experienced CG-HRM in explaining employee sustainability-related behavior. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: Design Strategies and Solutions for Circularity Across the Building Lifecycle
abstract: The built environment is one of the most resource-intensive sectors globally, yet progress towards circularity remains constrained by fragmented implementation, limited lifecycle integration, and insufficient governance frameworks. This chapter examines design strategies and solutions for circularity across the entire building lifecycle, drawing on a systematic comparative analysis of 45 international case studies. Using a matrix-based analytical framework, circular strategies are mapped across six dimensions: design for circularity, materials and products, construction practices, building operations and maintenance, end-of-life and deconstruction, and business models and policy support, and aligned with the 10R circular economy hierarchy. The findings reveal a clear concentration of circular maturity at the design and material levels, with strategies such as adaptability, flexibility, design for disassembly, and low-carbon material selection widely present across the dataset. In contrast, operational circularity, advanced end-of-life planning, digital traceability, and enabling business models remain significantly underdeveloped in mainstream practice. Cross-case analysis identifies five building clusters and six transferable circular design patterns, ranging from reuse-first approaches and design for disassembly as a system, to procurement-driven circularity and use-based strategies. The evidence consistently demonstrates that high circular performance is achieved through integrated, multi-lifecycle-stage approaches rather than isolated interventions. Policy and practice recommendations are derived directly from the pattern analysis, targeting design regulation, public procurement, operational management, and end-of-life governance. The chapter concludes that scaling circularity requires moving beyond project-based experimentation toward systemic frameworks that connect design intent, supply chain mechanisms, and institutional conditions across the full building lifecycle. © The Author(s) 2027.

title: EXPSO: A PSO-based ensemble gene expression classifier for plant species using histone and chromatin accessiblity data
abstract: Gene expression in plants is regulated by complex interactions among chromatin features, including histone modifications and chromatin accessibility. Accurate prediction of gene-expression states from epigenomic information can provide insights into transcriptional regulation and facilitate functional genomic studies. However, the nonlinear and high-dimensional nature of epigenomic data presents challenges for conventional statistical approaches. Here, we developed EXPSO, a PSO-assisted ensemble learning framework for classifying plant genes into high- and low-expression states using integrated histone modification and chromatin accessibility data. The framework uses Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to optimize Random Forest hyperparameters within an ensemble comprising Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and XGBoost classifiers. The framework was developed and evaluated independently across five plant species, including Arabidopsis thaliana, Hordeum vulgare, Phaseolus vulgaris, Setaria viridis, and Sorghum bicolor. EXPSO achieved an AUROC of 0.904 for Arabidopsis thaliana and demonstrated competitive predictive performance across the independently evaluated species. Model benchmarking against DeepChrome, ShallowChrome, and PatternChrome was performed using stratified five-fold cross-validation, with performance reported as mean ± standard deviation and 95% confidence intervals. Paired two-sided t-tests were used to assess fold-wise differences between EXPSO and the benchmark models. Comparative benchmarking included DeepChrome, ShallowChrome, and PatternChrome under the evaluation framework used in this study. Feature-attribution analyses using SHAP, LIME, and PDP consistently identified H3K36me3 and H3K56ac as important predictive features, consistent with their reported associations with transcription-associated chromatin states. To facilitate practical application, we developed the freely accessible EXPSO web server, which enables users to submit gene IDs together with histone modification and chromatin accessibility data as individual entries or CSV files and obtain gene-expression predictions with associated prediction probabilities and downloadable results. EXPSO provides an accessible and interpretable computational framework for plant gene-expression prediction from epigenomic features and a practical web-based implementation for supported plant datasets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Banks and informality: Two perspectives of microenterprises’ balance sheets
abstract: Our paper studies how the nationwide expansion of bank branches affects the performance of informal microenterprises. We exploit the Branch Authorization Policy (BAP) in India, which directed banks to open branches in “underbanked” districts. Using a regression discontinuity design, we find that microenterprises in underbanked districts report higher value-addition, revenues, and productive assets, but no increase in local registration. However, borrowings on the enterprise balance sheet do not increase. The household balance sheet offers a second perspective that reconciles these findings: households in underbanked districts increased their bank borrowings for non-farm business by an amount comparable to the increase in microenterprise productive assets. Micro-entrepreneurs thus accessed bank credit as households rather than as enterprises, weakening a key incentive to formalize and helping explain how expanded access to finance can coexist with persistent informality. © 2026

title: A novel hierarchical optimal control strategy for hybrid energy storage considering smoothing wind power fluctuations and compensating prediction errors
abstract: With the increasing penetration of wind power, its inherent intermittency and prediction errors pose significant challenges to the stable operation of power systems. To fully leverage the rapid dynamic response of supercapacitors and the high energy density of lithium-ion batteries, this paper proposes a novel hierarchical optimal control strategy for a hybrid energy storage system (HESS) to smooth wind power fluctuations and compensate prediction errors. The upper layer model introduces the concept of virtual energy storage (VES) and proposes a novel power extraction strategy based on model predictive control to obtain the total VES power, which is considered as the HESS power. The middle layer model establishes a novel power optimal allocation strategy based on the improved complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise and the grey relational analysis. The strategy realizes the decomposition, reconstruction and correction of li-ion battery (LB) and supercapacitor (SC) power. It avoids the problem of LB and SC power in the opposite direction at the same moment. The lower layer model builds a multi-objective optimal configuration model considering the life loss of HESS, which is solved by the improved multi-objective slime mould algorithm based on generalized opposition-based learning. Finally, some indicators are proposed to assess the effects of smoothing and compensation, simulations are conducted using actual data from western China. Results indicate that, compared with Case 1 using the conventional HESS power allocation strategy, the proposed strategy increases the modeled HESS lifetime from 4.54 years to 14.39 years, corresponding to an improvement of 216.96%, while the configuration satisfaction degree reaches 0.6941. © 2026

title: Early-life adversity and long-term outcomes: evidence from the cocoa swollen shoot virus outbreak in the Gold Coast
abstract: How do early-life economic shocks that do not directly affect human biology shape long-term development outcomes? While a large body of work documents persistent effects of early-life exposure to health crises, famines, and natural disasters, much less is known about shocks that operate through economic disruption. This study addresses this gap by examining the long-term effects of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease (CSSVD), an agricultural epidemic that devastated cocoa production in the Gold Coast (now Ghana) during the 1940s. Combining historical data on climatically suitable cocoa-growing areas with georeferenced household survey data, I exploit variation in exposure across birth timing and space to estimate the epidemic's long-term effects. The results show that exposure during early childhood and school-going years led to substantial and persistent human capital deficits. Individuals exposed during early childhood lost about one year of schooling and were 8.5 percentage points (pp) less likely to obtain formal education, while those exposed during school-going years lost about 0.8 years of schooling and were 7.0 pp less likely to obtain formal education. Exposure is also associated with worse health outcomes, increasing morbidity by 6.2–8.5 pp and disability by 5–7.5 pp. In contrast, there is no systematic evidence of long-term effects on employment type or labor supply. Evidence on potential mechanisms points to both educational and occupational channels. Conditional on ever attending school, exposed individuals completed fewer years of schooling and were more likely to have incomplete primary education, indicating disruptions to both school progression and initial access to schooling. In addition, exposed individuals are more likely to work in the agricultural sector in adulthood, consistent with reduced educational attainment having narrowed their occupational options. These findings demonstrate that industry-specific economic shocks can generate long-term human capital deficits, even in the absence of direct biological exposure. © 2026 The Author

title: Harvesting trade partners online with AI: A joint learning method for predicting the business role of massive web pages
abstract: In small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), users often perform tedious and complex human–computer interactions between search engine data ((Formula presented) ) and webpage data ((Formula presented) ) when seeking potential business partners online via search engines (SEs). While artificial intelligence (AI) has been shown to improve search efficiency, conventional machine learning methods still face challenges in retrieval accuracy and efficiency, particularly in complex big-data environments. To address these limitations, this study proposes an AI module termed the Multi-source Data Joint Learning (MDJL) model, designed to assist SME users in efficiently retrieving online business partners. The MDJL model employs a multimodal information fusion approach to separately represent unstructured data elements in (Formula presented) and (Formula presented) as vectors. An encoder-decoder architecture then jointly learns the associations between (Formula presented) and (Formula presented). Based on these learned joint representations, MDJL incorporates a multi-label attention mechanism to train a classifier that accurately predicts the business roles of companies associated with webpages. The model’s effectiveness is validated using real business datasets annotated by domain experts. Experimental results show that MDJL can effectively learn joint information from any two cross-correlated datasets. The resulting classifier exhibits high efficiency and robustness, especially when data from certain sources are partially missing or unknown. From a managerial standpoint, a trained MDJL model can further help SMEs digitize and consolidate the business knowledge of highly skilled employees, supporting more informed and efficient decision-making in partner search activities. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: More than regulation: How policy mixes shape innovation ecosystems in digital transformation
abstract: The era of digital transformation drives the continuous restructuring of innovation ecosystems, challenging regulators to move beyond conventional regulations to address market and system failures. Although policy mixes are essential to address these challenges and promote innovation ecosystems, the efficacy of specific policy mix characteristics remains underexplored. This study develops a conceptual model to explore the mechanisms through which policy mix characteristics affect firm innovation in the digital transformation era. Specifically, we conceptualize policy mix coordination across three dimensions: temporal (policy stability over time), horizontal (policy similarity across regions), and vertical (policy coherence and complementarity between central and local governments). Firm innovation is examined through firms' technological and business positions within the innovation ecosystem. We conduct an empirical study of Chinese listed companies (2001-2021), employing machine learning techniques to identify policy themes, multi-source heterogeneous network analysis to measure firm innovation, and panel regression to test hypotheses. Results show that temporal and horizontal coordination stimulate firms' technological positions but inhibit business positions, whereas vertical coordination significantly enhances firms' technological positions within innovation ecosystems. These findings contribute to policy mix theory by incorporating a thematic lens and offer insights into recasting regulators' role as strategic coordinators in cultivating innovation ecosystems during digital transformation. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Hydrogen-bonded assisted network of alkali lignin nanoparticles in starch/gelatin films: Concentration-dependent enhancement of UV-shielding, antioxidant activity, and oxygen barrier
abstract: To address the limitations of conventional petroleum-based packaging, this study developed biodegradable composite films by incorporating alkali lignin nanoparticles (LNPs) into a corn starch (CS) and gelatin (GEL) matrix. The findings demonstrated that the LNPs were highly compatible with the CS/GEL matrix. The FTIR and XRD analyses offer indirect evidence suggesting the creation of hydrogen-bonded networks between LNPs and CS/GEL matrix. This structural integration was accompanied by simultaneous enhancement of multiple functional properties that are usually incompatible in biopolymer films. In particular, the LNPs contributed to high hydrophobicity and outstanding UV-blocking ability (over 99.9% in the UVC region) due to phenolic chromophores, while also greatly enhancing thermal stability (Tg > 120 °C) and oxygen barrier properties. Notably, antioxidant activity increased proportionally with concentration, achieving about 40–60% improvement in radical scavenging and more than 200% increase in reducing power, due to the exposed phenolic hydroxyl groups of LNPs. However, loading LNPs beyond 3% caused particle aggregation, which weakened the mechanical strength. These findings indicate that LNPs act not just as fillers but as multifunctional crosslinkers that enhance CS/GEL films into high-performance, sustainable packaging materials. This study offers an environmentally friendly approach to valorize industrial alkali lignin and address the limitation of single functionality in biodegradable food packaging. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Balancing risk and opportunity: Digital transformation, cybersecurity investments, and export performance in low-tech firms
abstract: This study examines whether investments in digital technologies raise export sales among low-tech firms, and whether cybersecurity spending conditions these returns. Reading the Resource-Based View through resource orchestration, we frame digital technologies as enabling resources and cybersecurity as a protective commitment securing their value but competing for the investment budget under scarcity. This competition is sharper in low-tech firms, with thinner slack. Using Bank of Italy data (2016–2023), we find digital investment positively associated with export sales where cybersecurity spending is absent. This association is negative in the highest protective-spending brackets, and a specification imposing no functional form locates the reversal at the top of the distribution. The pattern is clearer among SMEs and manufacturing firms; among larger firms, digital investment shows no association with exports, while protective spending is associated with higher export volume. This is a cyber-risk paradox: under scarcity, protection substitutes for, rather than complements, digital expansion. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Inc. title: Discount display in tiered pricing: Nudging subscriptions in online healthcare services
abstract: Discounts are increasingly embedded within tiered pricing to encourage larger purchases or longer service commitments. However, such discounts are often implicit and embedded across the price options, heightening consumers’ cognitive burden of cross-tier comparisons. How platforms display these discounts and whether salient discount display in tiered pricing can drive consumer demand remain largely unclear. Drawing on nudge theory, we conceptualize discount display as a digital salience nudge and examine its effect on consumer subscription demand in online healthcare settings. We leverage a quasi-natural experiment on a leading Chinese online healthcare platform, which redesigned its subscription interface to render implicit savings across tiers salient to patients. Using an intensity-based difference-in-differences approach, we find that discount display significantly increases patient subscriptions. Further analyses suggest that this effect is unlikely to stem from physician-side price reductions or concurrent platform-side changes and is instead consistent with the informational effect of discount display. Moderation results further show that the promotional effect of discount display strengthens for physicians treating a higher share of chronic conditions and becomes statistically insignificant in predominantly episodic care. This study contributes to discount promotion literature by offering robust empirical evidence on the positive effect of salient discount display in tiered pricing contexts and provides managerial implications for interface design and promotion management in digital retailing markets. © 2026

title: SHG wave propagation in functionally graded piezomagnetic sandwich plates with imperfect interfaces: Analytical modeling and machine learning prediction
abstract: Shear horizontal guided (SHG) waves in functionally graded piezomagnetic structures are highly sensitive to material gradation, interfacial imperfections, and magnetic boundary conditions, making them attractive for smart sensing and structural monitoring applications. This study develops an integrated analytical and physics-informed learning framework for SHG-wave propagation in a composite sandwich structure comprising two dissimilar functionally graded piezomagnetic layers coupled through a spring-membrane imperfect interface and subjected to surface mass loading. Analytical dispersion relations are derived for two distinct velocity regimes under magnetically open-circuit (MOC) and magnetically short-circuit (MSC) conditions. The effects of magneto-mechanical coupling, material gradation, interface characteristics, membrane inertial density, and normalized density on the dispersion response are systematically examined. The results reveal pronounced dispersive behavior and demonstrate that magneto-mechanical coupling, functional gradation, interface stiffness, membrane inertia, and magnetic boundary conditions provide effective mechanisms for controlling SHG-wave propagation. The analytical formulation is further integrated with an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and a physics-informed Deep Operator Network (PI-DeepONet) for rapid prediction of the dispersion response. PI-DeepONet achieves R2=0.99970, compared with 0.99811 for ANN, and reduces RMSE, MAE, and MAPE by approximately 69.6%, 73.1%, and 73.5%, respectively. The physics residual also falls below 10−3 over a substantial portion of the investigated wave-number range, while tests on unseen physical configurations demonstrate improved generalization. The proposed analytical–physics-informed framework provides an accurate and computationally efficient approach for SHG-wave analysis and offers potential for smart piezomagnetic sensors, acoustic-wave devices, and guided-wave-based structural monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

title: Prioritising seafood diversification in Sweden: Integrating biological screening with stakeholder constraints
abstract: Diversifying seafood production and consumption has been proposed as a strategy for improving the sustainability and resilience of food systems. Along the Swedish west coast, numerous low-trophic marine species remain underutilised despite growing interest in sustainable seafood diversification. However, biological suitability alone does not determine whether such species become viable food resources. This study combines biological screening of 38 underutilised marine invertebrate and macroalgal taxa with stakeholder evidence generated through interviews, workshops, and surveys conducted between 2018 and 2024. Species were assessed using a scoring framework, while stakeholder evidence was analysed to identify opportunities and constraints across the seafood value chain. The biological screening identified several promising candidates for diversification, including macroalgae, cephalopods, tunicates, sea urchins, and species of crabs. Stakeholder evidence revealed strong interest in these and other underutilised species but also highlighted recurring barriers related to supply reliability, processing capacity, market access, food-safety requirements, and regulatory uncertainty. The findings demonstrate that the principal constraints to seafood diversification are not primarily biological but organisational and institutional. Diversification opportunities appear strongest where biological feasibility aligns with enabling conditions across production, processing, markets, and governance. In particular, reducing regulatory uncertainty, strengthening value-chain coordination, and creating confidence for investment and market development emerged as important prerequisites for translating biological opportunities into viable seafood products and businesses. By integrating biological and stakeholder perspectives, the study provides a practical framework for identifying priority species and guiding policy and industry efforts to support seafood diversification. title: Optimization of Home-to-Home Energy Trading Using Multi-agent Deep Reinforcement Learning in a Smart Community
abstract: In recent years, home energy management systems (HEMS) have become increasingly popular as part of efforts to achieve a decarbonized society. HEMS can efficiently use electricity generated from renewable energy sources by managing a household's electricity consumption on a schedule. However, in the previous model, HEMS managed only the electricity consumption of individual households and did not consider interactions between households. Also, battery life depletion due to battery charging and discharging was not taken into account. Therefore, we created an environmental model that enables electricity trading among households and takes battery health into account. Simulations were conducted using this environmental model and a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning algorithm. The simulation results showed that the total energy consumption and electricity prices of all cooperating households could be reduced based on the status and electricity prices of each household. Future developments include consideration of rate regimes for household-business and household-to-household electricity trading. © ICST Institute for Computer Sciences, Social Informatics and Telecommunications Engineering 2027.

title: m-QIEA: A modified quantum-inspired evolutionary algorithm for feature selection in code smell detection
abstract: Code smells, indicative of structural defects in software, signify sub-optimal design practices that impede software maintainability. Detecting and mitigating code smells is essential for improving software quality, particularly in both classical and quantum systems. However, conventional machine learning (ML) approaches for code smell detection often suffer from feature redundancy, increased computational cost, and suboptimal model performance. Feature selection (FS) plays a pivotal role in enhancing code smell detection by improving classification accuracy while reducing model complexity. This research aims to improve code smell detection by introducing an FS-driven approach that optimizes feature selection to enhance classification accuracy. The proposed approach leverages deep learning (DL) models for feature extraction, followed by a modified Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithm (m-QIEA) to refine the feature subset for classification. Compared with standard QIEA, m-QIEA incorporates a time-decaying rotation schedule and Gaussian mutation, which are intended to mitigate premature stagnation during the feature-selection search. Experimental evaluations are conducted on a comprehensive suite of six datasets. For classical systems, the primary MLCQ benchmark is used and further the work is extended to SmellyCode++, and a multi-language corpus (Python, Java, and C++). For quantum systems, the primary QNet benchmark is used, extended to a derived large-scale LintQ corpus, and tested on the independent Smelly Eight benchmark. Across all settings, the results demonstrate that m-QIEA achieves superior accuracy and generalization. The study establishes the critical role of FS in optimizing code smell detection accuracy. By integrating DL for feature extraction and m-QIEA for FS, the proposed approach enhances the classification of code smells across multiple programming paradigms and dataset scales. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Artificial intelligence in sales (2017-early 2026): field consolidation and the rise of human-AI collaboration
abstract: This study examines the consolidation phase of artificial intelligence (AI) research in sales between 2017 and early 2026. Using a bibliometric analysis of Scopus data, with robustness checks across Web of Science, we identify the field’s intellectual and thematic structure during its rapid expansion.Contrary to the assumption that AI in sales primarily reflects a technological efficiency paradigm, we find three structural shifts. First, predictive analytics remains foundational but is increasingly embedded in human-AI collaboration. Second, interactional and trust-related themes move from peripheral to central, indicating a shift from performance optimization toward socio-technical integration. Third, legitimacy pressures such as transparency and corporate digital responsibility emerge as organizing dimensions rather than auxiliary concerns.Applying the TOE framework to explain these shifts across technological, organizational, and environmental dimensions, this study clarifies how AI in sales evolves through layering rather than replacement. The findings provide a research agenda for AI-enabled selling’s next phase. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Inc. title: Potato LAI estimation by enhancing spectral features of reflectance and fluorescence to improve application potential among different varieties
abstract: Accurate leaf area index (LAI) estimation of potato crops is of great importance for precision management in potato cultivation. Vegetation indices (VIs) derived from spectral reflectance are widely used for LAI estimation but suffer from saturation under high LAI conditions, limiting accuracy and robustness across varieties. Solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence in the near-infrared region (SIFNIR), closely linked to canopy photosynthetic activity and light absorption, provides complementary information for LAI estimation. However, heterogeneous light radiation and structural differences among canopies interfere with SIFNIR extraction. To address these challenges, we propose an approach that enhances and integrates spectral reflectance and fluorescence features to improve LAI estimation across 40 potato varieties. Seven VIs were calculated and their saturation effects were discussed. SIFNIR was extracted based on Three-band Fraunhofer line discriminator (3FLD) method and normalized by absorbed photosynthetically active radiation (APAR) and canopy coverage (Cov) to reduce radiative and structural effects. Potato LAI estimation models of different varieties were constructed using the Random Forest (RF) method. The results showed that (1) NLI and MSAVI were reliable VIs for assessing potato canopy growth. (2) APAR and Cov showed stronger relationships with LAI, and SIFNIR normalized by these factors could reduce interference from canopy structure. (3) The RF model of reflectance and fluorescence feature fusion achieved the best performance, with prediction set Rp2 of 0.68, 0.70, 0.68, 0.70, and RMSEp of 0.50, 0.45, 0.50, 0.45 for all varieties, early season, mid-season and late season varieties, respectively. These results demonstrate the application potential of reflectance and fluorescence fusion to improve potato LAI estimation, and provide support for precise management in potato cultivation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Navigating the in-between: Contradictions in transitioning service ecosystems
abstract: While research on change in service ecosystems has expanded considerably, one specific type of process—transitions—has received comparatively limited attention. This gap is consequential, as transitions are critical for addressing systemic problems, including sustainability challenges. More specifically, little is known about the nature of contradictions—coexisting yet opposing elements—within these processes. Addressing this gap, we conduct an abductive qualitative study of a transitioning energy service ecosystem, which surrounds a European utility firm. Our findings reveal the individual-level struggles that actors experience amid service ecosystem transitions, especially when the contradictions within transitions go unrecognized or unmanaged. We extend prior research on service ecosystem change in two ways: by conceptualizing contradictions as inherent to transition processes emerging from interactions between coexisting prevailing and emerging service ecosystem states, and by identifying four types of contradictions that further detail the systemic conditions actors must navigate amid transition processes. © 2026 The Authors. title: Large language models in software project management: A two-phase systematic literature review
abstract: Background: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into Software Engineering (SE) processes and practices. However, their application within Software Project Management (SPM) remains fragmented and insufficiently synthesized. This absence of systematic evidence prevents both researchers and practitioners from understanding where LLMs can meaningfully contribute to project management processes in relation to established standards such as the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK). Objectives: This study aims to systematically synthesize existing evidence on the application and integration of LLMs in SPM by means of a two-phase method where Phase I systematically searches for existing secondary studies in the topic of interest, and Phase II (whenever applicable) carries out an SLR in the topic of interest. Method: We conducted a two-phase method: Phase I is a tertiary study that used 14 research questions to assess the existence, coverage, and quality of prior secondary studies in LLMs applied to SPM. As no suitable SLR was identified from Phase I, we also conducted Phase II, which employed the SEGRESS guidelines to analyze primary studies that empirically evaluated the use of LLMs in SPM via five research questions. Phase II also assessed coverage across PMBOK processes and synthesized reported mechanisms, outcomes, research designs and evaluation approaches. Results: The SLR (Phase II) shows that studies employ encoder-only and decoder-only LLM architectures in equal proportion (17 studies each). Their applications focus on a narrow set of SPM tasks, including effort estimation, project planning, and requirements-related activities. Coverage across PMBOK processes is uneven, with limited attention to areas such as procurement, stakeholder, quality, and cost management. Most studies rely on proof-of-concept evaluations, with scarce industrial validation and heterogeneous evaluation metrics. Conclusion: The results indicate that current research on LLMs in SPM provides limited guidance for systematic adoption. One of the main drawbacks for such lack of guidance is the weak empirical validation in many of the included primary studies, limited PMBOK coverage, and lack of context-aware integration of LLMs in SPM.1 © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Source code vulnerability detection with LLMs: A systematic evaluation of fine-tuning and multimodal fusion of code text and software metrics
abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) present new opportunities for automated software vulnerability detection, yet their comparative behavior across models, fine-tuning conditions, imbalance strategies, and input modalities remains insufficiently characterized. We systematically evaluate 23 publicly available general-purpose, code-oriented, and security-related LLMs for binary vulnerability detection on SySeVR and Devign, comparing frozen-backbone head training with full fine-tuning. We examine data imbalance through dataset-level and training-time strategies and evaluate three input settings: software metrics only, source code only, and multimodal fusion of code and metrics. Performance is assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, ROC AUC, execution time, and peak GPU memory usage. Fine-tuning generally improves performance, although the effects vary across datasets and metrics. Metrics-only experiments show a meaningful standalone signal on SySeVR but near-random discrimination on Devign; natural-text metric representations generally outperform structured metric embeddings. The code-only setting achieves the strongest overall performance on SySeVR, whereas multimodal gains are dataset-dependent and most evident on Devign, particularly with mid-level attention-based fusion. Artifact analysis reveals substantial overlap and template repetition in SySeVR, whereas Devign shows considerably lower overlap and repetition under the same criteria; cross-dataset experiments show weak transfer between the benchmarks. Overall, the results demonstrate that both fine-tuning gains and the usefulness of software metrics are strongly benchmark-dependent. Software metrics can complement code-text representations, but their effectiveness as standalone LLM inputs should not be generalized beyond the evaluated datasets. These findings provide a broad empirical benchmark and motivate more robust cross-dataset evaluation and multimodal vulnerability detection. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Personalized assignment of UAV rescue tasks: an integrated framework of content-based filtering and two-stage robust optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel integrated framework approach of content-based filtering and two-stage robust optimization for personalized assignment of UAV rescue tasks. Our approach differs from traditional UAV task assignment method in that (1) The personalized assignment of UAV task is established on the mining of “fine-grained” attributes such as hovering capability, payload capacity, wind resistance, and rainproof capability, etc; rather than simply considering “coarse-grained” attributes like cost, time, and capacity. (2) Pre-disaster airport positioning and UAV allocation are integrated with post-disaster task assignment into a single model, accounting for the uncertainty of disaster scenarios. In our approach: Text mining techniques are first employed to identify the “fine-grained” attributes of UAVs and rescue tasks. Subsequently, content-based filtering method is utilized to calculate the matching degree between UAVs and rescue tasks. Finally, a two-stage robust optimization model, incorporating constraints based on the matching degree parameters, is applied to optimize both pre-disaster UAV deployment and post-disaster task assignment plans. Our approach is applied in a real-world earthquake case study. The results verify the correctness and efficiency of the method. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Preliminary Research and Verification of an Algorithm for an Expert Recommendation System for Assessing the Readiness of Airlines to Implement Artificial Intelligence Technologies
abstract: This paper presents preliminary research and validation of an algorithm for an expert recommendation system that assesses airline readiness to adopt artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. The approach includes an information model that fuzzifies survey data—covering implementation possibilities and managerial understanding of AI—and a hybrid fuzzy model that combines multidimensional assessments into a single readiness indicator and offers targeted recommendations. The proposed solution integrates organizational and data-driven factors, reduces the subjectivity of expert judgments, and directly supports management decisions to enhance business process efficiency and flight safety. The experimental application involving five aviation companies confirms the consistency of the proposed methodology and demonstrates the interpretability and managerial relevance of the readiness indicators obtained. The results provide a structured basis for comparative assessment of AI readiness, enabling the formulation of targeted strategic recommendations for aviation companies. In practical terms, the developed system may support strategic planning, prioritization of AI investments, and risk-informed decision-making in airline management. The proposed approach can also serve as a methodological foundation for further digital transformation initiatives in the aviation sector. © European Alliance for Innovation 2027.

title: Enhancing Decision-Making Through BI Automation
abstract: Every second, large volumes of data are generated which, if not properly interpreted, can lead to wrong decisions and undesirable consequences. Automating and optimising information processing enables faster handling and supports timely, informed decision-making. With the evolution of Business Intelligence tools, adopting data-driven solutions is essential for organisational competitiveness. This work tackles real-time management and analysis of strategic and operational industrial data through the design and development of the Unified Performance Metrics dashboard, which consolidates strategic information of internal business units via key metrics, and the improvement of the existing human resources dashboard. The system integrates a Power BI frontend with a Python-and SQL-based back-end for automation and the extract, transform, and load process. The dashboards were successfully evaluated, approved, and deployed. By automating strategic and operational analyses, the dashboards effectively replaced inefficient manual error-prone procedures, demonstrating clear operational advantages. © 2026, Springer Science and Business Media Deutschland GmbH. .

title: Predictive Dropout Research Through a Data-Based Value-Creation Taxonomy: Patterns and Blind Spots
abstract: Predictive dropout research uses data-based, individual-level predictions for the early identification of at-risk students with the general aim of improving student retention. Yet it lacks a systematic understanding of the specific types of value that its data-driven approaches are expected to create. This study addresses this gap by applying Baecker et al.’s data-based value-creation taxonomy to a purposive sample of 23 predictive dropout studies in higher education contexts. Using the taxonomy as an analytical lens, this study examines how existing research conceptualizes institution-level value-creation through its data foundations, proposed value-creation approaches, and proposed business value. The findings reveal strong convergence, characterized by recurring data foundations and a dominant focus on targeted interventions. In contrast, financial value and institution-level strategic value are rarely articulated. The study contributes a precise conceptual vocabulary for analyzing prediction-based value-creation and clarifies structural patterns and blind spots within predictive dropout research, thereby supporting future empirical work beyond predictive accuracy. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Sustainable production and export performance of globe artichoke in Egypt: evidence from 2000 to 2023
abstract: The globe artichoke is one of the major vegetable crops cultivated in the Mediterranean Basin, with global production reaching nearly 1.6 million tons in 2023. Egypt is among the world’s leading producers, contributing almost one-fifth of global production; however, its export performance remains relatively limited compared with its production potential. This study examines the production dynamics, geographical distribution, and export competitiveness of globe artichoke in Egypt during 2000–2023 within the framework of sustainable agricultural development. Both quantitative and qualitative approaches were used to analyze trends in cultivated areas, productivity, and exports, in addition to major competitiveness indicators in international markets. The results indicate that production growth was driven mainly by horizontal expansion rather than improvements in yield. The cultivated area increased to 50.4 thousand fed in 2023, with an average annual growth rate of about 8%, whereas yield increased only marginally during the study period. Expansion was more pronounced in new lands than in old lands, reflecting the crop’s adaptability to new production areas but also indicating limited progress in productivity efficiency. Despite the increase in production, globe artichoke exports declined by approximately 1.4%, largely due to rising competition from Mediterranean countries, export market concentration, and price fluctuations. Italy, France, and Spain remained the main importers of Egyptian artichokes while simultaneously representing major competitors in international markets. The findings suggest that improving productivity efficiency, promoting value-added products, and diversifying export markets may contribute to strengthening export competitiveness and enhancing the long-term sustainability of globe artichoke production in Egypt. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Deconstructing Digital Transformation in Global Construction Firms
abstract: Digital transformation has become a strategic concern for large contractors, yet it remains difficult to assess systematically because transformation unfolds unevenly across different organisational domains and dimensions. This paper presents a new analytical framework for assessing digital transformation, developed from literature, and applies it to examine how digital transformation unfolds in large contractor firms. The study employs a structured literature review and a qualitative multiple-case study. The framework structures transformation through five domains and three dimensions, enabling a more fine-grained analysis of how digital initiatives are expressed in practice. The analysis demonstrates the value of the framework by revealing systematic variation in digital transformation across firms, as well as across domains and dimensions within the same firm. Empirically, the findings show that digital transformation is not a uniform or linear process, but varies in how firms create value, manage change, scale pilot outcomes, renew business models, and engage at the corporate level. The findings further reveal three distinct strategic profiles: advanced transformation, internally orchestrated, and operational oriented digitalisation. Based on these findings, the paper contributes an analytical approach for identifying and comparing transformation patterns across large contractors. It also offers practical value by helping managers assess digital transformation more systematically and identify areas where development remains fragmented or weak. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: RAG Automation of COSMIC Functional Size Measurement Using Large Language Models
abstract: Functional Size Measurement (FSM) methods, such as COSMIC (Common Software Measurement International Consortium), provide standardized techniques for software effort estimation and efficient project management. However, manual measurement of Natural Language (NL) requirements remains time-consuming, prone to human error, and subject to human interpretation biases. Existing hybrid approach that combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with a rule-based system has demonstrated promising results in automating COSMIC measurement. Yet, its performance varies across domains, with high accuracy in business applications and lower accuracy in real-time systems due to domain-specific terminology and contextual differences. This study enhances the existing LLM-based COSMIC measurement framework by integrating a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) system, which dynamically injects domain-specific COSMIC knowledge into the reasoning process. A rule-based validation layer ensures adherence to COSMIC movement rules and rectifies incorrect classifications. Experimental results indicate that the primary contribution of the proposed approach lies in reducing the performance disparity between application domains. Without RAG, the framework exhibits a noticeable gap between business and real-time systems, with a domain-wise F1-score difference of 0.05. By injecting domain-specific COSMIC knowledge at inference time, the RAG-enhanced framework reduces this gap to 0.01, yielding more balanced performance across domains. These results validate that the com-bination of retrieval and reasoning mechanisms significantly improves the cross-domain robustness and measurement reliability of automated COSMIC sizing. © 2026, Springer Science and Business Media Deutschland GmbH. .

title: Do macro-financial variables improve short-horizon forecasts of U.S. business bankruptcy filings?
abstract: This paper evaluates whether macro-financial variables improve short-horizon forecasts of U.S. business bankruptcy filings beyond a strong univariate benchmark. Using monthly data, we compare seasonal ARIMA models with macro-augmented ARIMA and SARIMA specifications incorporating indicators of credit conditions, real activity, labor-market slack, and financial market performance. Forecasts are generated using expanding estimation windows at one-, three-, and six-month horizons under realistic information constraints and assessed using out-of-sample loss measures and formal predictive accuracy tests. Although several macro variables are statistically significant in sample, they do not deliver robust out-of-sample forecast improvements once persistence and seasonality are properly modeled. Across the three forecast horizons, the univariate SARIMA benchmark performs similarly to or better than the macro-augmented alternative. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Translating Strategic AI Use into Business Value in Organizations: A Qualitative Study
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly regarded as a transformative technology with the potential to unlock significant business value for organizations. However, many organizations are struggling to generate real business value from AI adoption. This study therefore investigates how organizations translate AI’s potential into meaningful business value from a strategic use perspective. We conducted a qualitative study based on 11 interviews from European companies engaged in AI initiatives. We find that AI initiation should be problem-driven rather than technology-driven, and organizations can develop AI-enabled exploitative and exploratory capabilities to gain business value. We propose a conceptual framework to structure how organizations initiate, apply, and scale AI for business value realization. This study contributes to our understanding of the mechanisms of AI value translation and offers practical guidance for organizations seeking to produce meaningful business value from AI use. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Short-Term Financial Management Tool Applied in Administrative-Financial Management for Sustainability in the Small Shrimp Industry
abstract: Global trade is undergoing constant change, and digital transformation is key to the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). In Ecuador, SMEs represent more than 80% of the business fabric, generating jobs, and local economic development. Ecuador is one of the world's leading shrimp exporters, accounting for approximately 20% of non-oil exports. Many SMEs are at an initial level of digitalisation, where administrative financial management is one of the main problems for a company's growth. This research focuses on analysing a proposed Short-Term Financial Management tool (STFM) through its application in a case study for administrative-financial decision-making in SMEs in the shrimp industry, with a view to their sustainability. The method compares financial management models, considering key input factors, to obtain better performance indices. The STFM tool allowed the digitisation of financial statements, optimising 50% of staff time and obtaining a projected annual growth of 2% for the company. Thus, there is great potential for SMEs in the shrimp industry to integrate more efficiently into global value chains by adopting modern technologies (progressive digital transformation). This is within the context of modernising aquaculture production and strengthening the local economy. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Multi AI Agents for Solving Complex Business Tasks: A Case Study
abstract: This work introduces a novel approach to intelligent automation based on multi-agent systems composed of autonomous agents powered by large language models (LLMs). Departing from the conventional use of LLMs merely as query tools, we propose the construction of an autonomous and collaborative ecosystem capable of sophisticated, adaptive decision-making for complex task resolution. As a case study, we present the implementation of a team of artificial intelligence agents designed for automation within the financial domain. CrewAI serves as the foundational framework to orchestrate collaboration among agents powered by two cutting-edge LLMs: DeepSeek-V3 and GPT-4.1-mini. Experimental results demonstrate that while GPT-4.1-mini generally outperforms its counterpart, DeepSeek-V3 delivers highly competitive performance at a significantly lower cost, highlighting the potential of cost-efficient, LLM-driven multi-agent systems. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Proprietary Software Licensing Models: History, Evolution and Trends
abstract: Proprietary software licensing models have undergone significant transformations over the years, driven by technological advances and changing market demands. This article reviews this evolution using narrative review methodology, highlighting the key developments and comparing different models. Initially, software was bundled with hardware under simple licensing agreements. As the software industry expanded, companies unbundled their software from hardware, growing their market and enforcing stricter terms of use and redistribution. The rise of the Internet in the 1990s led to the development of new licensing models, including subscription-based licensing and software as a service-models. Nowadays licensing models offer greater flexibility and scalability, addressing the diverse needs of businesses and customers. The growing adoption of subscription-based and usage-based licensing reflects an industry-wide shift toward recurring revenue streams and fostering long-term sticky customer relationships. Therefore, developing effective licensing strategies will be critical to shaping the future of the software industry. © 2026, Springer Science and Business Media Deutschland GmbH. .

title: Bridging game-theoretic modeling and Artificial Intelligence for fast policy recommendations in multi-channel retail
abstract: Emerging-market milk retail is increasingly split across General Trade, Modern Trade, and E-commerce, where pricing and advertising are strategically interdependent through cross-channel substitution, advertising spillovers, and trust-sensitive demand. Yet decision support is challenging: game-theoretic models capture these interactions but are costly to solve repeatedly, while standard machine learning approaches typically require rich quantitative data, often unavailable in fragmented markets where key drivers (e.g., “low trust”) are qualitative. This paper bridges this gap by proposing a hybrid simulation–surrogate decision-support framework that operationalizes omnichannel theory into rapid decision support. First, a tri-channel game-theoretic simulator incorporating trust, advertising spillovers, and cost heterogeneity generates constrained solver benchmark pricing and advertising decisions. Second, to reduce repeated equilibrium-solving costs during scenario evaluation, a lightweight policy network is trained to approximate this structural mapping, providing feasible scenario-based recommendations at low computational cost. A rule-based natural-language descriptor layer operationalizes qualitative managerial inputs by mapping predefined cues into parameterized intervals. Across 10,000 simulated market states, the trained surrogate policy closely approximates the solver-generated benchmark decisions, with evaluation on the held-out test set yielding a mean profit ratio of 1.001, a trimmed profit ratio of 0.999, and mean economic regret of 0.40%. Stress tests under alternative parameter distributions and comparative evaluations against linear, tree-based, and heuristic baselines indicate the network's stable economic performance across regular simulated market states; while batched evaluations accelerate interactive scenario analysis by up to 14.8 times. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Research on the Current Development Status and Application Schemes of Low-Altitude Economy During the Construction Period of Railway Engineering
abstract: As a strategic emerging industry, the low-altitude economy has demonstrated enormous application potential in the railway sector of railway- developed countries worldwide. By systematically sorting out the current development status and typical application cases of the railway low-altitude economy at home and abroad, this paper further puts forward the application demands in such business scenarios as survey and design, construction and building, environmental and water conservation management, and emergency management during the construction period of railway engineering, aiming at the pain points of traditional survey and design, construction process control and other work, such as low manual efficiency, insufficient precision and high safety risks. On this basis, it designs and constructs the application architecture of the low-altitude economy during the railway engineering construction period, proposes the engineering UAV adaptation schemes as well as data acquisition and transmission schemes for eight typical application scenarios including route survey and design and terrain modeling, points out the challenges faced by the development of the low-altitude economy during the railway engineering construction period and puts forward development suggestions, providing technical guidance for the high-quality development and transformation of railway engineering construction. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Can FinTech mitigate systemic risk? Evidence from macroprudential policies and bank business diversification
abstract: Using Chinese commercial banks as the sample and drawing on panel data from both listed and unlisted banks, this paper systematically examines the mechanism through which financial technology (FinTech) influences bank systemic risk from 2007 to 2023. The results indicate that the development of FinTech significantly reduces systemic risk in the banking sector. Moreover, business diversification serves as an important mediating channel. Further analysis reveals that macroprudential policies strengthen the risk-mitigating impact of FinTech on bank systemic risk, with stronger statistical evidence for price-based policies. Heterogeneity tests show that the risk-mitigating effect of FinTech is stronger among banks with greater homogeneity in their asset and liability structures. Among FinTech's functional dimensions, payment and settlement and resource allocation show the strongest risk-mitigating effects. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Security Engineering in Product-Line Development: Concept and Practitioner Evaluation
abstract: As modern software systems grow in complexity and configurability, organizations increasingly rely on Product-Line Engineering (PLE) to manage variability and reuse. Yet, security remains insufficiently integrated into these processes and is often treated as an afterthought rather than a core design concern. To address this gap, we propose a dedicated security-engineering extension that systematically embeds security in the PLE framework. The extension was developed through a structured framework development process and synthesizes insights from 52 existing publications. It aligns with ISO/IEC 27000 to ensure compliance and practical relevance. The resulting framework comprises six processes and twelve activities situated between domain engineering and application engineering, addressing topics such as business processes, incident management, source-code testing, and third-party services. An initial survey with 36 security practitioners confirmed the framework’s necessity, clarity, and usefulness, with over 90% positive responses. However, the feedback indicated a need for finer-grained methodological guidance and more explicit operationalization of activities. Future work will therefore focus on deepening these aspects through case studies and practical evaluation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Board gender diversity, cultural logics, and corporate tax behaviour
abstract: Corporate tax aggressiveness tests corporate accountability, yet less is known about when board gender diversity translates into more restrained tax behaviour across institutional settings. Using 27,275 firm-year observations from 29 countries across Europe, Asia, and Australasia during 2013–2023, we examine whether board gender diversity is associated with lower tax aggressiveness and whether national culture conditions this association. Board gender diversity is negatively associated with tax aggressiveness: greater female board representation is associated with higher cash effective tax rates and more restrained tax behaviour. This association is stronger in high masculinity, uncertainty avoidance, and long-term orientation settings, but weaker in high power distance, individualism, and indulgence settings. Results are robust to an alternative sign-reversed accrual-based tax proxy, lagged board gender diversity, placebo randomisation, entropy balancing, and two-step difference GMM. The findings contribute to business ethics, governance, and tax research by showing that culture shapes how female board representation translates into accountability-relevant tax outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: State ownership, media sentiment, and the completion of cross-border acquisitions
abstract: Media sentiment plays an important but underexamined role in shaping the completion of cross-border acquisitions (CBAs) by state-owned enterprise (SOE) acquirers. While SOE-led CBAs face a baseline completion disadvantage relative to non-SOE deals due to host-country concerns over political motives, government influence, and national security, we argue that this disadvantage is not static but is actively shaped by how the deal is portrayed in the media. Drawing on agenda-setting and legitimacy theories, we show that positive media sentiment attenuates the legitimacy concerns attached to state ownership, while negative sentiment reinforces them. The effect is amplified when the sentiment is conveyed by prestigious outlets with greater agenda-setting influence. This study contributes to SOE internationalization and CBAs research by showing that legitimacy is not static but socially constructed through deal-level media evaluations. © 2026 The Authors.
