title: Dynamic event-triggered adaptive cooperative control for robotic manipulator with output constraints and model uncertainties
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive fuzzy-based dynamic event-triggered adaptive cooperative control to address the challenge of achieving high-performance control for robotic manipulators under model uncertainties and output constraints. This strategy designs a signal-processing-based backstepping control scheme and an energy-transformation-based error port-Hamiltonian (EPH) control scheme, respectively. The uncertain dynamics of the system are approximated through adaptive fuzzy logic systems, while the output of the system is constrained by boundary constraints gain. Furthermore, an adaptive cooperative control mechanism is designed, which dynamically adjusts the weighting between the two control schemes. This mechanism integrates the advantages of the fast response from the signal-processing-based scheme and the minimal energy consumption from the energy-transformation-based scheme. This paper also proposes a dynamic event-triggered control (ETC) mechanism, whose triggering threshold adaptively adjusts according to the system state, achieving dynamic matching between the triggering frequency and the system status. Theoretical analysis shows that all signals in the closed-loop system are bounded, the output does not violate the constraints, and the ETC mechanism avoids Zeno behavior. Experimental results verify that the proposed method can achieve high-precision trajectory tracking under disturbances and output constraints, while effectively reducing the control signal update frequency, demonstrating excellent comprehensive performance. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: A multi-physics configuration space framework for tool abrasive wear evolution and predictive modeling in longitudinal–torsional ultrasonic-assisted milling of carbon fiber–reinforced polymers
abstract: Addressing the challenges of complex wear evolution and long-term prediction accuracy in longitudinal-torsional ultrasonic-assisted milling of carbon fiber-reinforced polymers (LTUAM-CFRP), this study proposes a novel cutting edge configuration theory and establishes a configuration-space framework for wear morphology evolution. The framework provides a unified parametric physical abstraction of cutting edge geometry, enabling consistent characterization of the coupled evolution of rake-face wear, flank-face wear, and edge radius transformation. A contact state-space model is developed to describe high-frequency fiber–tool interface separation behavior under ultrasonic modulation. A stepwise wear modeling strategy integrating impact wear and abrasive wear is further established, revealing the outward evolution of impact wear from the contact region and the continuous accumulation of abrasive wear along the cutting edge. Furthermore, an error-feedback adaptive hybrid wear accumulation framework is constructed by combining cutting edge configuration and a process-aware deep learning network for multi-scale feature fusion. Experimental validation demonstrates that the proposed method achieves multi-cycle wear prediction accuracy of 95.32%, which is improved to 98.36% after process-aware correction, confirming the robustness and predictive capability of the framework for intelligent wear perception in LTUAM-CFRP machining. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: When Indexes Work: Optimizing SQL Queries for Low-Code Applications
abstract: Low-code tools are soaring in popularity because they let users quickly create applications without coding. Oracle Application Express (APEX) is a leading low-code platform that runs within the Oracle Cloud, making it convenient and easy to use. Business users can create database-driven interactive dashboards with forms, reports, and graphs, in less than an hour without writing a single line of code. However, the SQL queries that APEX generates are not optimized for performance, many APEX users lack the skills to optimize them using the Oracle tuning tool, and there is little guidance on when indexes are efficient in APEX applications. This study investigates which query types benefit from indexing within APEX dashboards, and which query types do not benefit from indexes. The dashboard that was evaluated employed common types of auto-generated APEX queries. Query baseline performance was captured using debug mode, and the execution plans analyzed. B-tree indexes drastically improved filtered query performance by over 87% in execution cost and almost 36% in query time. However, B-tree indexes provided no benefit for aggregation queries that process all rows in the table. Surprisingly, composite indexes actually degraded performance by 228%, increasing execution costs substantially. These findings show indexes are not a silver bullet. This research offers practical guidance for APEX developers on how to optimize their queries effectively. The results demonstrate that developers should use indexes strategically, based on the type of query, rather than blindly assuming that all indexes boost performance. © 2026, Springer Science and Business Media Deutschland GmbH. .

title: Plugging in feedback in the software development pipeline: Insights from DevOps practitioners
abstract: In the rapidly evolving domain of software development, the integration and management of feedback within the development pipeline play a pivotal role in ensuring product quality and process efficiency. This paper explores the nuances of feedback mechanisms in contemporary software development practices, with a particular focus on DevOps and Continuous Integration (CI)/Continuous Deployment (CD) practices. Drawing insights from qualitative interviews with 19 experienced DevOps practitioners in various countries, the study delves into how teams incorporate feedback at different stages of the development pipeline. The findings highlight the use of modern tools and frameworks that facilitate automated feedback. The paper also introduces a comprehensive checklist designed to assess the health and effectiveness of feedback mechanisms. Through its findings, the study underscores the importance of balancing manual and automated feedback processes and proposes strategies to enhance the automation of feedback for improved responsiveness and decision-making in software development cycles. This research contributes to a broader understanding of feedback dynamics in software engineering and offers actionable recommendations through a Feedback Health Checklist. © 2026

title: Developing and Configuring Artificial-Intelligence Systems in Manufacturing: Adoption Insights from a Practitioner Survey
abstract: Artificial-Intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly regarded as key enablers of smart manufacturing, offering benefits such as reduced downtime, improved efficiency, or enhanced quality. Yet, the adoption of scientific approaches in practice remains limited due to persistent challenges in appropriate transfer, implementation, deployment, and configuration. In this article, we report on a survey with 26 AI-system practitioners from the manufacturing domain, focusing on their opinions and experience regarding three pillars: development, configuration, and perceived value. Our results show that development is primarily hindered by data quality and integration barriers, while configuration problems, such as version conflicts or unintended feature interactions, occur frequently and lead to business-critical impacts, including downtime and vulnerabilities. Nevertheless, practitioners perceive clear value in AI systems, especially in predictive maintenance, although broader applications, such as real-time optimization or advanced quality control, remain underexploited. Overall, the study provides valuable insights into how AI systems are currently adopted in manufacturing practice. The findings highlight the need for configurable, reusable, and scalable solutions, as well as systematic data management and configuration practices to facilitate sustainable adoption in manufacturing settings. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Transforming Business with Generative AI: Research, Innovation, Market Deployment and Future Shifts in Business Models
abstract: This paper explores the transformative impact of Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) on the business landscape, examining its role in reshaping traditional business models, intensifying market competition, and fostering innovation. By applying the principles of Neo-Schumpeterian economics, the research analyses how GenAI is driving a new wave of “creative destruction” leading to the emergence of novel business paradigms and value propositions. The findings reveal that GenAI enhances operational efficiency, facilitates product and service innovation, and creates new revenue streams, positioning it as a powerful catalyst for substantial shifts in business structures and strategies. However, the deployment of GenAI also presents significant challenges, including ethical concerns, regulatory demands, and the risk of job displacement. By addressing the multifarious nature of GenAI, this paper provides valuable insights for business leaders, policymakers, and researchers, guiding them towards a balanced and responsible integration of this transformative technology. Ultimately, GenAI is not merely a technological advancement but a driver of profound change, heralding a future where creativity, efficiency, and growth are redefined. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Organizational Climate for Service Robot Integration
abstract: The use of robots in service industries has sparked interest and attention among academia and industry. As its implementation often entails challenges for adaptation, the realization of the anticipated benefits of service robots (SRs) might be hindered. Based on organizational climate (OC) literature, well-managed OC for SR integration fosters integration within the organization and the realization of its benefits. However, empirical evidence on the effect of service-robot-oriented OC on organizational and employees’ performance in service organizations remains limited. To fill the void, this study aims to assess the relationship of service-robot-oriented OC prevalent in service organizations on both organizational (i.e., processes, customers) and employees’ performance (i.e., need satisfaction, work engagement). A cross-sectional survey is conducted with international data collection. Data analysis using PLS-SEM shows that internal process performance (IPP) statistically mediates the relationship between OC and customer performance (CP). Furthermore, employees’ need satisfaction (NS) statistically mediates OC and employees’ work engagement (WE). Theoretically, this study contributes by extending the mechanisms underlying the association between OC and organizational and employees’ performance. In practice, study results suggest that shaping a proper service-robot-oriented climate is of strategic importance for service organizations’ performance. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Avoiding Digital Disappointment: A Retrospective Study Applying DSM-NPV to a European Shipyard Innovation
abstract: Investments in digital technologies in engineer-to-order shipyards are often justified with optimistic business cases that emphasize direct costs and early benefits, yet value delivery is frequently delayed by integration and adoption work. This paper applies the DSM–NPV evaluation framework in a retrospective case on the introduction of a pipe spool tracking system within the piping department of a shipyard. The system was introduced to replace fragmented manual status reporting. A Design Structure Matrix (DSM) is used to map baseline information flows in the shipyard’s piping division and to identify the system changes required to integrate the new technology. Those cascades are translated into a traceable set of additional activities and benefit timing adjustments that inform a revised Net Present Value (NPV) model under uncertainty, contrasted with the original “as-approved” evaluation approach. Results show that the implementation footprint extends beyond shop-floor reporting into planning, logistics, supervision, and data governance, and that downstream benefits depend on stable adoption, reliable data, and role-specific processing and visualization. The study illustrates how the DSM-NPV approach improves expectation setting through integration of dependency analysis with financial modelling and supports change management planning for shipyard (digital) projects. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: A Systematic Literature Review of Approaches to Maturity Model Implementation in Public Bodies Using Agile Initiatives
abstract: For public bodies, implementing maturity models is vital for enhancing competitiveness and service quality. Adopting flexible and adaptable processes enables organizations to better meet the demands of a dynamic society. However, adopting agile methodologies requires careful planning. The variety of agile methodologies (e.g. Scrum, SAFe and Kanban) can be confusing, making it challenging to select the most appropriate approach. Poorly planned implementation can lead to process overload, team resistance and, ultimately, failure to achieve the desired outcome. To mitigate these challenges, public bodies should invest in a gradual, personalized implementation process and process models adopted by other organizations. When choosing an agile methodology, factors such as team size, project complexity, organizational culture, and strategic objectives must be considered. Additionally, strong support from senior management and engagement from all employees are crucial. A gradual, personalized approach increases the likelihood of successfully implementing a maturity model using agile methodologies. This work presents an extended Systematic Literature Review (SLR) aimed at identifying effective approaches to implementing maturity models in public bodies. The SLR analyzed 13 primary studies, revealing practices, recommendations, standards, implementation strategies, benefits, challenges, and considerations in these processes. The shared characteristics of the implementation processes reported in different bodies suggest that these findings could form the basis for other public bodies to adopt similar methodologies. This work makes a valuable contribution by consolidating recommendations that can streamline the implementation of maturity models, enabling managers and stakeholders to develop clearer implementation plans and ensure a smoother process. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Making the Metaverse Viable: Vendor Framings and the Conditional Realisation of Sustainable Value
abstract: Extended reality (XR) and digital twin (DT) solutions are increasingly presented as technologies that can create organisational value and support sustainability. Yet these claims are often made in emerging and uncertain markets, where clients may not immediately understand what the technologies are for, how they may generate value, or under what conditions that value becomes relevant for sustainability. Vendors are therefore important because they translate XR/DT possibilities into client-facing value propositions. However, less is known about how vendors present these technologies as valuable for clients and connect such value claims to sustainability. This qualitative exploratory study draws on semi-structured interviews with 16 domain experts involved in the development, provision, implementation, or organisational use of Metaverse-related solutions. The data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. The findings identify a vendor-side conditional value pathway in which vendors first made XR/DT commercially recognisable and justifiable and then emphasised technological possibilities. Whether these possibilities became practically valuable depended on organisational, technical, material, and ecosystem conditions. Sustainability implications were associated with substitution, reconfigured participation, and context-dependent trade-offs. The study therefore interprets XR/DT as conditional sustainability mediators. Particular uses can connect technological possibilities to sustainability implications, but these implications are neither inherent nor automatic. The study contributes an account of how vendors connect XR/DT value propositions to sustainability, while recognising that the findings reflect participants’ accounts rather than independently verified client outcomes or sustainability impacts. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Mobile internet connectivity and household wealth in the Philippines
abstract: Mobile internet has become a fundamental modern infrastructure. We consider how access influences household wealth in the Philippines using a granular measure of local connectivity based on geocoded cell towers and identify causal impact through an instrument based on proximity to submarine cable landing points. Our results show that mobile internet connectivity increases household wealth, with effects across education levels and most pronounced in urban areas. We investigate potential mechanisms and find that improved connectivity stimulates activity in key economic sectors, improves educational outcomes, and increases female labor force participation, primarily in occasional work. Given the context of the Philippines as a major migrant-sending country, we conduct a complementary event study which suggests that tower rollout may facilitate international labor migration and increase remittance flows to origin households. © 2026 The Authors

title: QualiTact: A semantic model for quality-driven development of AI-based systems based on architectural tactics
abstract: Systems operating in safety-critical industries increasingly adopt Artificial Intelligence (AI). Satisfaction of system quality attributes in these industries is mandatory and rigorously verified. To influence system quality, a crucial development practice is the use of architectural tactics. However, selecting and balancing these attributes is often based on experience rather than on conscious decisions. This can unexpectedly impact system quality and might be detected too late in the testing phase. For development projects, it is desirable to identify and plan the selection of architectural tactics in a quality-driven manner. This article presents an approach that calculates a tactic's relative influence between 24 linked quality attributes and 150 tactics as part of a semantic model that supports the quality-driven development of AI-based systems. Attribute selection and filtering create recommendations of relevant tactics for a specific design and development task. In an exploratory multi-case study, the suitability of the recommended tactics was analyzed using source code. Results show that the model can compensate missing quality attribute information input and can provide recommendations. Despite an average input of only 39.98% from 30 case-relevant quality attributes for the model, the average recommendation completeness reaches 49.26% for 20.67 known tactics in source code across cases, leading the model to suffer from gaps between the literature and cases. Yet, 28 new design tactics linked to 30 known quality attributes were identified. Our work thus lays the foundation to support quality-driven design and development by recommending architectural tactics based on quality requirements. © 2026 The Authors

title: BiCrossNet-DDI: Drug-drug interaction prediction based on bidirectional cross-view attention networks
abstract: Drug-drug interaction (DDI) prediction plays a crucial role in drug safety assessment and clinical polypharmacy management. Existing approaches predominantly rely on a single graph structure or adopt coarse-grained multi-view fusion strategies, making it difficult to simultaneously capture the multi-scale topological characteristics of drug relationships and fully exploit complementary information across different views, thereby limiting representation capacity and predictive performance. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a DDI prediction framework based on a bidirectional cross-view attention network, which achieves more comprehensive semantic modeling of drug interactions and robust prediction through multi-scale structural modeling and cross-view interaction alignment. Specifically, the proposed method performs consistent encoding over multi-scale diffusion views and similarity views, and further introduces a bidirectional cross-view attention module as the core component. Concretely, the original view is used as the query to selectively aggregate high-order structural information from the diffusion view, while the diffusion view is simultaneously employed as the query to reversely align interaction evidence from the original view, enabling bidirectional completion and collaborative enhancement between views. Residual connections are incorporated within network layers to preserve critical information and stabilize training, and unified drug embeddings are finally obtained for DDI prediction. Experiments on the ZhangDDI dataset demonstrate that our model achieves an absolute improvement of 3.17% in F1 compared with the strongest baseline method. Data and source code are available at https://github.com/fluteink/BiCrossNet-DDI. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Data-Driven Risk Allocation and Incentive-Compatible Payment Schemes in Construction Contracts: Integrating Comparative Standard Forms, Public Works Disputes, and Principal-Agent Modeling
abstract: Construction projects worldwide suffer from misaligned risk allocation, poorly chosen payment schemes, and opaque claims and dispute processes, leading to chronic cost overruns and litigation. Building on comparative analyses of widely used international and national standard forms of contract, empirical public works dispute case studies, and principal-agent theory of payment methods, this research develops a data-driven framework for designing incentive-compatible construction contracts. First, we code and compare more than 60 distinct risk events and 40 claims and dispute procedures across several representative standard contract regimes for large infrastructure projects. Second, we construct a dataset of approximately 80 real dispute or major change-order cases (including highway, bridge, and building projects) and classify them by triggering risk, procurement mode, and payment scheme. Third, we calibrate a structural principal-agent model of contractor effort, cost uncertainty, and risk aversion to this dataset, comparing fixed-price, unit-price, cost-plus, and target-price contracts. The calibrated model is then used to simulate how alternative combinations of risk allocation clauses and payment mechanisms affect expected owner cost, contractor risk exposure, and the probability of disputes. Simulation results are used to quantify potential performance gains from better-aligned contract design; illustrative scenarios target a 15%-25% reduction in expected total project cost, a 30%-40% reduction in formal disputes, and a 40% reduction in claims processing time when more balanced risk-sharing clauses and incentive-compatible payment schemes are adopted. The research is useful as a guideline for international contractors and public agencies involved in mega infrastructure projects. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Multimarket contact, excess capacity, and low-cost carrier competition: A dual-channel model of mutual forbearance in international airline markets
abstract: Research on the relationship between multimarket contact (MMC) and firm performance has produced mixed results. To help reconcile this discrepancy, we examine how firm-level excess capacity and low-cost carrier (LCC) competition condition the MMC–performance relationship in international airline markets. Drawing on mutual forbearance theory, we disaggregate total multimarket contact into contacts through strong resource-sharing markets (routes sharing endpoint cities) and weak resource-sharing markets (routes without shared endpoints), and we theorize a dual-channel model in which excess capacity determines which type of contact drives forbearance. Our analysis of 2979 firm–market–year observations spanning 82 airlines across 265 route markets serving Taiwan over the period 2009–2018 reveals three principal findings. First, total MMC exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship with subsequent market share. Second, excess capacity channels the significant concave MMC profiles through different contact types: strong resource-sharing contact among high-excess-capacity firms (where idle capacity is visible at shared airports) and weak resource-sharing contact among low-excess-capacity firms (where network breadth sustains competitive awareness); in both cases the estimated downturn lies in a sparsely populated right tail and is interpreted cautiously. Third, LCC entry disrupts the forbearance equilibrium: the inverted U-shape is absent in markets with LCC competitors, and an exploratory positive linear pattern in those markets suggests that multimarket contact functions there as a competitive resource rather than as a forbearance signal. Accordingly, our study contributes to the multimarket competition literature by shedding light on how firm resources and competitive context jointly determine the mechanism and viability of mutual forbearance, helping to reconcile the inconsistent findings in prior research. title: Proposal of a hybrid method for mapping local patterns in wind speed time series
abstract: Wind speed time series modeling is particularly challenging due to its inherent nonlinear and stochastic nature. Consequently, there is a growing demand for advanced hybrid predictive methods in the wind energy sector. This study introduces a hybrid method called LocLN, which maps both linear and nonlinear local patterns. The approach is inspired by the LocPart method, employing a divide-and-conquer strategy. It is assumed that the learning process of each local subseries can be more effective than the global learning of the entire series. The results from 10 wind speed series indicate the effectiveness of the proposed method. LocLN combines fast-training models such as autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) and extreme learning machines (ELM), achieving approximately 17% and 20% reductions in forecasting errors for one-hour- and three-hour-ahead horizons, respectively, compared to standalone recurrent neural network models. Additionally, the Diebold-Mariano (DM) hypothesis test on squared errors highlighted the significance of LocLN when compared to 12 other competing methods across the 10 datasets. The findings showed that LocLN exhibited only one case with significantly worse performance across individual models, ensemble techniques (e.g., bagging and pasting), and hybrid approaches such as residual modeling, with each method applied independently. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Toning it down: How competition shapes CSR communication positivity amid external stakeholder pressures
abstract: Amid intensifying scrutiny of corporate environmental and social impacts, firms increasingly use positive CSR communication to shape stakeholder perceptions. However, its effectiveness varies across contexts. We develop an impression management risk perspective, arguing that heightened product market competition (PMC) increases the anticipated backlash risks associated with overly positive CSR communication. As PMC intensifies, firms anticipate that economically oriented stakeholders will interpret highly positive CSR tone as evidence of inefficient resource allocation and managerial distraction, leading firms to use less positive CSR tone. We further argue that unfavorable analyst recommendations strengthen this negative relationship by heightening concerns about firms’ financial prospects, whereas CSR-related shareholder proposals weaken it by increasing pressure for CSR performance improvement. Analysis of 1,529 U.S. manufacturing CSR reports supports these arguments. Our findings contribute to research on PMC and impression management by showing how competition influences CSR communication and how conflicting stakeholder pressures moderate this effect. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Risk-aware and network-compatible bidding of aggregated DER under energy-as-a-service model
abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) and the adoption of distributed energy resources (DERs) introduce new layers of uncertainty for the operation of distribution networks. This variability, however, represents a valuable source of flexibility that can be unlocked when these resources are managed intelligently and with a coordinated approach. This work presents a unified bidding framework that manages DER-related uncertainties by coordinating residential DERs under an energy-as-a-service (EaaS) model. A Wasserstein distributionally robust bidding scheme is proposed to generate frequency control ancillary services and energy offers that remain feasible under uncertain DER behavior, while dynamic operating envelopes (DOEs) are incorporated to ensure that all bids respect local network constraints. The simulation results indicate that coordinated DER flexibility substantially improves the aggregator's wholesale market performance, with frequency control ancillary services (FCAS) Raise and Lower revenues approximately 62% and 41% higher than in the business-as-usual (BAU) case, respectively, while reducing customers’ electricity costs. In addition, DOE-based bidding improves voltage compliance to 100% and reduces the maximum transformer loading from 142.7% to 81.5%, supporting operation within the prescribed network limits. These findings show that risk-aware bidding, network-aware coordination, and a customer-focused EaaS framework can unlock reliable, scalable, and economically beneficial DER flexibility. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Toward carbon-neutral desalination: Scope 1–3 carbon accounting, technological pathways, circular resource recovery, and future perspectives
abstract: Desalination is increasingly essential for addressing global water scarcity, particularly in arid and semiarid regions with limited conventional freshwater resources. However, the process remains energy-intensive, making its environmental sustainability heavily dependent on the carbon intensity of its operational energy supply. As global climate mitigation accelerates, carbon-neutral desalination has emerged as a critical objective to align future water supply systems with net-zero emission targets. This review evaluates recent progress, key challenges, and technological pathways for reducing the carbon footprint of desalination systems. It first examines the main carbon drivers of desalination, identifying operational electricity consumption as the dominant source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, especially in reverse osmosis systems. Furthermore, this review evaluates desalination-related emissions using a Scope 1–3 GHG accounting framework, highlighting the growing importance of indirect life cycle emissions from membranes, chemicals, infrastructure, and brine management. Life cycle assessment (LCA) studies indicate that desalinated water generates approximately 1–3 kg CO2-eq m−3, depending on the electricity mix, plant efficiency, and system configuration. The review also discusses major carbon-reduction pathways, including renewable energy integration, energy recovery devices (ERDs), advanced membranes, process optimization, digital control, and emerging low-carbon desalination technologies. Solar- and wind-powered desalination systems represent key near-term strategies for reducing operational emissions, while advances in ERDs and membrane materials continue to lower specific energy consumption. Emerging technologies, including membrane distillation, forward osmosis, electrodialysis, and capacitive deionization, can further support low-carbon desalination in applications involving low-grade heat, brackish water, wastewater reuse, or decentralized treatment. Furthermore, sustainable brine management, zero-liquid-discharge systems, and resource recovery are highlighted as key components of circular desalination. Despite recent progress, carbon-neutral desalination remains constrained by renewable energy intermittency, high capital costs, limited full-scale demonstrations, energy-intensive brine treatment, and the lack of standardized Scope 1–3 carbon-accounting frameworks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Incremental railway infrastructure detection via prototype-guided proposal refinement and frequency-based prompts from noisy-annotated UAV imagery
abstract: Railway infrastructure incremental object detection (IOD) aims to generalize to new classes while retaining previously learned knowledge, requiring the model to balance stability and plasticity. Despite their effectiveness, the existing methods are limited in the following ways. On the one hand, they overlook the class ambiguity induced by fine-grained infrastructure structures. On the other hand, they underestimate the spatial ambiguity caused by noisy annotations. Furthermore, they ignore the knowledge corruption caused by spatial imitation in IOD tasks, which limits the discriminative knowledge transferred across tasks. To address the above issues, a robust IOD framework is proposed to enhance semantic discrimination and knowledge retention by integrating prototype-guided proposal refinement and frequency-based prompts. The prototype-guided proposal refinement consists of distribution-aware prototype and adaptive proposal refinement, which respectively model distinguishable infrastructure prototypes and perform iterative localization refinement. Specifically, the distribution-aware prototype constructs distinguishable infrastructure prototypes that serve as the stable class representations for proposal refinement. Moreover, frequency-based prompts are proposed to preserve discriminative representations between the current and previous IOD tasks, which are optimized only after each incremental task and kept frozen during task training so that they serve as stable knowledge carriers. Comprehensive experiments on real-world railway infrastructure datasets validate the superiority of the proposed framework over state-of-the-art baselines. Code will be available at https://github.com/Malloy99/PRFP. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: How consumers respond to social media influencers’ cross-domain recommendations?——A person brand perspective
abstract: Influencer marketing has become an integrated component of marketing strategy for many companies competing in the current digital marketplace. However, research on how to enhance its effectiveness is still limited. Taking social media influencers as person brands, this study investigates key factors influencing consumer reactions towards social media influencers’ cross-domain recommendations from a brand extension perspective. Through five experiments, this study shows that (1) when social media influencers make cross-domain recommendations, purchase motivation moderates the effect of domain relevance on consumers’ purchase intentions, with hedonic consumers more tolerant of low-relevance recommendations; (2) perceived influencer authenticity mediates the effect of domain relevance on purchase intentions but only for functional (vs. hedonic) consumers; (3) when low-relevance products are recommended, hedonic (vs. functional) consumers are inclined to purchase products from warm (vs. competent) influencers. These findings provide important implications for both marketers and influencers on how to employ influencer marketing more wisely. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Rule-based BloodCell interpretable and actionable hematological classification using ConvNeXt-Tiny
abstract: The automated identification and classification of peripheral blood cells is critical for diagnosing a range of hematological disorders, from systemic infections to leukemia. Such classification supports diagnosis by providing differential cell counts and by detecting abnormal cell morphology, rather than diagnosing a disease directly. Traditional manual microscopy is labor-intensive and prone to subjective error, while existing deep learning “black-box” models often lack the transparency required for clinical adoption. This study proposes an interpretable, research-oriented decision-support framework leveraging the ConvNeXt-Tiny architecture, optimized with tuned hyperparameters and an input resolution of 64 × 64 pixels to enable rapid, lightweight training. The model was trained on a dataset of 17,107 images, using 13,685 for training and 3,422 for testing across eight classes: Basophils, Eosinophils, Erythroblasts, Immature Granulocytes (IG), Lymphocytes, Monocytes, Neutrophils, and Platelets. On the held-out test set, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 0.98 and a weighted F1-score of 0.98. Reliability was assessed with a Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.974 and a Cohen’s Kappa of 0.974, indicating strong agreement with the expert-labeled ground truth. A key contribution is the integration of Explainable AI (XAI) through LIME (Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations), which highlights influential superpixels to spatially validate cellular morphology. These visual explanations are complemented by a rule-based clinical decision-support (expert-system) module that maps the predicted cell class to predefined, non-diagnostic clinical guidance. By combining deep-learning feature extraction with rule-based recommendations drawn from standard hematology references, the framework provides a transparent and lightweight research prototype intended to assist, rather than replace, expert hematological assessment. Compared with existing approaches (Table 6), it addresses all eight clinically relevant classes with competitive accuracy and reliability while adding region-level LIME interpretability and a rule-based decision-support layer that most prior systems lack. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: When heat hits: Short-run saving and withdrawal behavior among microfinance clients in Benin
abstract: Increased access to finance is widely viewed as a key driver to increase adaptive capacity in response to climate change. However, apart from limited studies on borrowing behavior, little is known about how exposure to extreme heat is associated with microfinance clients’ financial behavior. This study addresses this gap by investigating the short-run associations of unusual heat with microfinance clients’ saving and withdrawal behavior. In a case study, it combines geo-located temperature data with a unique dataset of around 50,000 clients of a leading Microfinance Institution (MFI) in Benin. Applying two-way fixed effects, seemingly unrelated regression, and ordinary least squares models, the study finds that exposure to extreme heat is heterogeneously associated with microfinance clients’ financial behavior. Specifically, non-agricultural clients show suggestive evidence of the accumulation of precautionary savings after extreme heat days in the preceding quarter, while extreme heat days are negatively associated with agricultural clients’ savings. Microfinance clients increase their withdrawals when exposed to extreme heat within the preceding quarter, but the association is not robust for agricultural clients’ withdrawals in response to an increase in annual extreme heat days. Addressing the heterogeneous financial responses across different clients to extreme heat consequently requires explicit policy attention. Our findings contribute to a better understanding of the associations between extreme heat and individual economic outcomes, how financial behavior relates to weather risk, and how microfinance clients respond to shocks. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Promotion and prevention regulatory focus in equity crowdfunding reinvestment decisions
abstract: Using qualitative comparative analysis, our study draws on regulatory focus theory to examine how chronic promotion and prevention foci and situational factors are associated with reinvestment decisions in equity crowdfunding. Evidence suggests that both chronic promotion and prevention foci are sufficient conditions for reinvestment and that situational factors, particularly the absence of inhibitors related to information asymmetry, valuation difficulties, and exit constraints, play an important role. We also identify configurations incorporating the presence of inhibitor factors, which we interpret as consistent with investors adopting a speculative, bet-like approach. Our study offers practical insights for platforms and entrepreneurs by emphasising how transparent communication and risk disclosure can build investor trust and encourage continued investments. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Component connectivity and component diagnosability of the (n,k)-star graph
abstract: As a flexible extension derived from the classical star graph, the (n,k)-star graph Sn,k has been widely adopted to model scalable multiprocessor interconnection networks. This paper studies two reliability parameters that measure the behavior of Sn,k when the surviving graph may split into several connected blocks. We first obtain the exact 3,4-component connectivities: κc3(Sn,k)=2n−3 for n≥6 and 4≤k≤n−2, and κc4(Sn,k)=3n−6 for n≥10 and 5≤k≤n−3. We then prove the 2,3-component diagnosabilities that tc2(Sn,k)=n+k−3 when n≥5 and 3≤k≤n−2, and tc3(Sn,k)=2n+k−5 when n≥10 and 5≤k≤n−3 for both the PMC and MM∗ diagnosis models. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Is sustainable design effective? An empirical life cycle assessment of environmental impacts in basketball footwear production
abstract: The footwear industry is characterized by labor-intensive and resource-consuming production. Sustainable design provides a pathway for reducing the environmental burdens of footwear manufacturing, yet its benefits may vary across production processes and impact categories. This study conducts a high-resolution cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment of basketball footwear by linking upstream material acquisition with seven manufacturing processes and compares eight prospective sustainable design scenarios. Environmental hotspots are evaluated using ReCiPe 2016 at midpoint and endpoint levels. Results indicate that raw material acquisition dominates impacts related to toxicity, land use, and resource consumption, while manufacturing dominates global warming potential (GWP) and water consumption potential. At the process level, blanking of upper materials and sole manufacturing are major contributors to endpoint damage, mainly due to textile inputs, petroleum-based polymers, and manufacturing energy demand. Scenario analysis reveals that the reduction scenario (S7), which combines a 3D-printed TPU upper, adhesive-free sole joining, and packaging reduction, provides a relatively balanced environmental response, reducing GWP from 6.44 to 5.90 kg CO₂-eq without the pronounced cross category burden increases observed in the combined scenario (S8). Although S8 achieves the greatest GWP reduction (5.41 kg CO₂-eq), it increases freshwater eutrophication and ecotoxicity burdens. Monte Carlo simulation confirms the robustness of these carbon reductions and the persistence of several trade-offs. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating sustainable design across multiple environmental impact categories rather than carbon reduction alone. High-resolution modeling can support process optimization and sustainable design decisions through precise identification of environmental hotspots. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Institutional risk, finance, and the limits of techno-economic optimality in green hydrogen deployment
abstract: Green hydrogen is widely positioned as a key option for deep decarbonization, yet large-scale deployment remains limited despite growing techno-economic potential. This review examines how non-technical conditions influence the feasibility of green hydrogen business models, using the Netherlands as an illustrative case. A review-driven mixed-methods framework integrates evidence from a systematic literature review, semi-structured expert interviews, and an established hourly-resolved techno-economic optimization model to examine how policy design, investment risk, infrastructure constraints, and demand formation influence both the levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) and deployment feasibility. A multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) is employed to synthesize qualitative and quantitative evidence and prioritize the principal drivers and barriers identified across the different sources. The synthesized evidence, supported by the illustrative techno-economic analysis, indicates that LCOH values below €6 kg−1 are attainable under favorable assumptions, including low renewable electricity prices, reduced weighted average cost of capital (WACC), and access to underground hydrogen storage. However, regulatory fragmentation, grid congestion, weak demand coordination, and limited institutional legitimacy substantially constrain the realization of such conditions in practice. The findings demonstrate that techno-economic assessments alone may overestimate the deployability of green hydrogen when institutional risk and market coordination challenges are not explicitly considered. The proposed integrative framework provides a structured approach for assessing hydrogen market readiness in early-stage European contexts and supports the alignment of techno-economic competitiveness with governance capacity, investment conditions, and social acceptance. © 2026 The Authors

title: OpenCert for AI Act: A Capability-Based Framework for Trustworthy AI in Critical Infrastructures
abstract: The European Union Artificial Intelligence Act establishes mandatory requirements for high risk artificial intelligence systems, yet organizations lack structured frameworks to achieve certification efficiently. Current approaches to regulatory interoperability rely on manual and document based processes that are inefficient and do not scale. This paper introduces openCert, a capability based framework built on the Open Group Architecture Framework that translates legal requirements into reusable architectural assets. openCert defines a capability map linking regulatory articles to architectural building blocks, which can be implemented through certified solution building blocks stored in a European common repository. Drawing inspiration from established architecture frameworks, we adapt their capability views to the water domain. We validate the framework through a river basin authority that holds certifications under ISO 9001 and ISO 33000 and ISO 8000 as the first entity in Spain, and is implementing the Spanish National Security Framework. By mapping these certified assets to the capability map, the authority demonstrates readiness for artificial intelligence certification and provides reusable components for other European water authorities. The framework transforms regulatory compliance from manual document exchange into automated asset reuse, reducing certification effort by an estimated eighty percent. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: A Comparative Study of Ensemble Machine Learning and Spatiotemporal Deep Learning for Vehicle Theft Location Prediction
abstract: Vehicle theft remains a significant socioeconomic challenge, and accurate forecasting of theft locations is important for proactive policing and risk-based insurance interventions. This study formulates vehicle theft location forecasting as a spatiotemporal multi-class classification problem that integrates spatial, temporal, and contextual features. Using South African data, ensemble machine learning models (Random Forest and XGBoost) are compared with spatiotemporal deep learning approaches (TCN and CNN-LSTM) within a unified spatial-temporal binning framework. LSTM is included as a temporal benchmark to assess whether explicitly modelling spatial structure improves predictive performance. Evaluation across classification, calibration, statistical comparison, and insurance-oriented criteria showed that TCN provided the strongest overall predictive performance among the tested models. Random Forest was the closest performing classical model, with paired bootstrap testing giving directional evidence of improvement by TCN, although the confidence interval crossed zero and therefore indicated a modest rather than strongly conclusive advantage. In contrast, the business-oriented evaluation showed that Random Forest captured a higher share of potentially saved claim value under the selected alert threshold. These findings indicate that spatiotemporal deep learning improves predictive accuracy, while operational insurance value also depends on alert coverage and threshold selection. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Recursive object-centric process discovery with fitness and rediscovery guarantees
abstract: Digitized processes are an integral part of businesses to achieve their operational goals. Process mining aims to analyze such processes based on digital track records. These so-called event logs can be extracted from commonly used information systems. Traditionally, process mining remains limited as it requires individual business objects to define isolated process executions. However, in real-life processes, it is much more common to observe multiple business objects of various types that interact with each other. Object-centric process mining acknowledges this fact and fundamentally enhances traditional process mining techniques to analyze processes with interacting business objects. This analysis often requires a process model that describes the interacting control flows of all objects. Discovery algorithms are used to automatically construct such models from logs. For further steps, it is important that the discovery algorithm rediscovers a process model that is equivalent to the underlying business process. If it is impossible to rediscover the full behavior of a process, the discovered model should at least be fitting for the observed behavior. However, no existing object-centric discovery technique guarantees rediscovery or fitness. In this paper, we introduce a new algorithm that recursively constructs tree-structured object-centric models. We prove that our approach produces fitting models for all logs and rediscovers a subclass of processes within the used representational bias from logs that are sufficiently complete and free of incorrect recordings, unobserved or duplicated activities and loops. We evaluate our approach on a range of public logs and find it to produce fitting models in feasible runtime. © 2026 The Authors.

title: B2B influencer marketing collaborations: A relational governance perspective
abstract: Influencer marketing has grown rapidly in business markets, yet existing research remains largely rooted in consumer contexts and organization-centric perspectives. Little is known about how B2B influencers perceive collaborations with companies. Addressing this gap, this study conceptualizes B2B influencer collaboration as an interactionally constituted governance process and examines how governance mechanisms are interpreted by internal and external influencers. Drawing on relational governance and role theory, we analyzed 27 interviews with B2B influencers. The findings show that collaborations emerge through ongoing negotiation in which firms and influencers balance competing demands across collaboration stages. We identify two distinct role logics that explain why similar governance mechanisms are interpreted differently and are associated with different collaboration dynamics. The study contributes by framing B2B influencer collaboration as negotiated governance and introducing a role logics perspective to explain governance interpretations, with authenticity emerging as an outcome that can be enabled or constrained by governance arrangements. title: Integrated utilities for Net-Zero: empirical evidence and policy framework for the global energy–water–digital transition
abstract: This study develops and empirically validates an integrated framework linking energy, water, and digital infrastructures as mutually reinforcing drivers of global sustainability. Using a balanced panel of 45 countries (25 OECD and 20 emerging economies) from 2000–2023, we construct a Triple Transition Readiness Index (TTRI) and estimate dynamic panel models (System GMM) to test the Triple Transition Hypothesis. Results confirm strong complementarities: digital infrastructure amplifies the decarbonisation and efficiency gains of energy and water transitions. A simultaneous 10 % increase in renewable-energy deployment and broadband penetration reduces CO2 intensity by an additional 0.9 %. Emerging economies display greater synergies, revealing leap-frogging potential. The paper introduces the Triple Transition Efficiency Frontier (TTEF) and the Integrated Utility Governance (IUG) model, showing how coordinated regulation and investment across utilities accelerate cost-effective progress toward net-zero targets. Findings provide actionable insights for integrated policy design in the global sustainability transition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Controlled assembly of MoSe2/N-doped carbon nanoflower spheres via coordination-induced precursor for superior sodium-ion storage
abstract: Molybdenum diselenide (MoSe2) suffers from poor conductivity and structural degradation for sodium storage, which hinders its electrochemical performance. Herein, a coordination-induced precursor strategy is proposed to construct three-dimensional MoSe2/nitrogen-doped carbon (MoSe2-NC) nanoflowers, in which MoSe2 nanosheets are tightly embedded within a nitrogen-doped carbon matrix via dopamine-assisted self-assembly. The dopamine content regulates the structural evolution from solid to hollow flower-like spheres with tunable shell thickness, enabling uniform carbon incorporation and effective suppression of MoSe2 aggregation. Strong Mo–C/N interfacial coupling enhances structural stability and charge transfer, while the carbon framework accommodates volume variation during cycling. Consequently, the optimized MoSe2-NC-2 anode delivers a high reversible capacity of 335.4 mAh g−1 at 0.5 A g−1, along with excellent rate capability and cycling stability (232.35 mAh g−1 after 800 cycles at 2 A g−1). When coupled with a NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 cathode, the assembled full cell exhibits stable cycling performance (106.3 mAh g−1 after 90 cycles at 1C), demonstrating its potential for practical applications. The enhanced electrochemical performance can be attributed to the conductive carbon framework, strengthened interfacial interactions, and efficient accommodation of volume variation. This work provides insights into the rational design of metal selenide/carbon composites for sodium-ion batteries. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Simulation-Based Assessment of Business Process Robustness
abstract: Business process robustness describes a process’s ability to meet performance targets despite variations in parameters such as arrival rates or resource availability. Assessing business process robustness quantitatively is challenging because dependencies between process parameters and performance are complex and stochastic. Business process simulation avoids the need to specify those dependencies by simulating the process and observing the resulting behavior. However, the space of possible parameter combinations grows quickly, which makes it challenging to identify parameters that still meet the required performance targets. In this paper, we address this challenge by proposing a simulation-based approach that systematically explores parameter configurations to efficiently identify those that maintain acceptable performance. Our evaluation demonstrates that the proposed approach substantially reduces assessment complexity compared to our baselines while accurately identifying parameter combinations under which a process remains robust. The approach provides users with insights into how parameter variations influence performance, enabling a step toward a quantitative foundation for assessing and improving business process robustness. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Multimodal Process Monitoring with On-demand Disambiguation
abstract: Process monitoring is increasingly supported by Internet-of-Things (IoT) environments. However, the abstraction of sensor data into process events often leads to ambiguity. Existing approaches that leverage IoT data do not address how to resolve such ambiguity dynamically. To address this challenge, we present MMPMOD, a novel architecture for multimodal process monitoring that detects ambiguity in IoT-based events and orchestrates contextual sensing modalities on-demand to resolve it. Upon ambiguity detection, it activates cameras to capture the visual context, and applies scene understanding to disambiguate events. We implement and evaluate the architecture in a phlebotomy scenario, demonstrating the feasibility of orchestration of complementary sensing modalities for disambiguation in online monitoring in this scenario. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Exponential decay for a class of fourth order parabolic equations with logarithmic nonlinearity
abstract: We consider the initial boundary value problem for a fourth order parabolic equation with p-Laplacian diffusion and logarithmic nonlinearity. For global weak solutions under subcritical initial energy, we establish that the H2 and W1,p norms decay exponentially, which improves the previous algebraic decay result of Liao and Li (2020). The key ingredient in our proof is an energy difference inequality. This refined estimate yields sharper long-time asymptotics and stronger quantitative control than the original algebraic estimate. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Simulating Dynamic Relationships in Object-Centric Processes
abstract: Several Business Process Simulation techniques have been proposed to generate case-based event logs. However, an accurate description of many real-world processes requires modeling the interdependent objects that participate in them, leading to the rapid growth of object-centric process mining. Despite this progress, approaches for simulating object-centric event logs remain limited, as state-of-the-art techniques fail to capture the dynamic evolution of objects and their interactions during process execution. This limitation has important practical consequences, as such models cannot reproduce activities that create, modify, or remove objects, nor capture how many objects are generated within a given simulation time window. In this paper, we address these issues by proposing an object-centric simulation model capable of reproducing multiple objects and their dynamic relationships: new objects can be generated, or destroyed, during the simulation, and their relationships evolve according to the stochastic behavior of the process. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: A Hybrid LLM-Based Framework for Automated Security Annotation Generation in Business Process Models
abstract: The modelling and analysis of secure business processes require the incorporation of security annotations into process models. Although BPMN extensions, including SecBPMN2, exist for this purpose, the derivation of accurate and complete security annotations from natural-language specifications remains a manual, expert-intensive, and error-prone task. This paper presents a hybrid framework that takes a BPMN process model and a security requirements document as input and automatically generates security annotations adhering to the SecBPMN2 specification. The approach combines Large Language Model (LLM)–based semantic extraction with schema-constrained mapping, rule-based normalization, and deterministic validation. The framework is evaluated comprehensively on a curated dataset of 27 process models from various domains. The results indicate that it consistently produces structurally valid SecBPMN2 annotations with high schema completeness. Compared to human security analysts, the system achieves substantially higher precision (0.58 vs. 0.29) while maintaining comparable recall (0.52 vs. 0.50) and reduces erroneous or misplaced annotations by nearly 50%. In addition, annotation generation is significantly faster than manual annotation. These findings demonstrate that hybrid LLM- and rule-based automation can reduce modeling effort while improving consistency and reliability, thereby providing a scalable foundation for security-by-design BPM. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: BERT-Driven Deep Learning for Enhanced Spam Email Classification with Browser Extension Integration
abstract: Email volume continues to surge across business, education, and personal use, with spam composing nearly half of global traffic and driving financial and security risks. Classical filters (blacklists, rules, Naive Bayes, k-Nearest Neighbors) and even deep models like BiLSTM struggle to capture full semantics or resist modern evasion. We propose a BERT-driven spam-detection framework that exploits bidirectional self-attention to model rich context and evaluate it against strong baselines. On a balanced dataset of 5,000 emails with a 226-sample hold-out test set, fine-tuned BERT attains 98.67% accuracy and 98.65% F1, outperforming BiLSTM (96.43%), Naive Bayes (91.59%), and k-NN (90.27%). For practical deployment, we integrate BERT into a Chrome extension with a FastAPI backend, enabling real-time Gmail filtering with 0.5 s latency per email. Results indicate BERT delivers superior accuracy and robustness, bridging research and production. Future directions include multilingual detection, adversarially robust training, and multimodal filtering (URLs, images). © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: An applicable mechanism for regulating anti-etching performance through interface doping in periodic Y2O3-BaZrO3 films
abstract: Plasma etching is widely used in the processing of semiconductor memory and the manufacturing of field-effect transistors, with precise transfer of nanometer level precision, high aspect ratio structures, and complex three-dimensional structures. However, halogen-containing reactive plasma can corrode the ceramic components of chambers, for example, generating YOF particles on the surface of yttrium oxide coating after high-energy plasma bombardment. In order to reduce the etching rate and minimize particle contamination, this work adopts an interface doping strategy to prepare Y2O3-BaZrO3 etch-resistant multilayered films through radio-frequency magnetron sputtering. Subsequent vacuum annealing of the films at 900℃ was performed to improve their atomic diffusion, crystallization, and density. 12-layer Y2O3-BaZrO3 film proved to be the hardest and most etch-resistant with the lowest relative etching rate (0.67 nm/min) under chemical plasma conditions (CF4/O2), compared with Y2O3 film (1.42 nm/min) and Y2O3-MgO composite film (0.91 nm/min). As chemical etching involves the formation of protective fluoride passivation layers such as Y-F, Ba-F and Zr-F, the surface stability is enhanced by the increased bonding energy of metal fluorides, indicating higher thermodynamic stability of the composite after adsorption of fluorine. The results have potential to significantly extend the lifetime of plasma etching equipment for semiconductor manufacturing. © 2026

title: Student perceptions of generative AI in accounting education: A thematic analysis
abstract: Generative AI has outpaced pedagogical and ethical guidance in accounting classrooms, leaving students and educators uncertain whether it supports or undermines the discipline's dual emphasis on procedural accuracy and professional judgment. To address this problem, this study examines how 92 business undergraduates perceive generative AI tools, notably ChatGPT, in accounting education, drawing on in-class, handwritten survey responses. Findings show that students view AI as a useful yet uncertain resource: valuing its speed, accessibility, and support while raising concerns over cheating, fairness, unclear institutional policies, and overreliance. Four interconnected themes emerged: Practical Affordances and Engagement, Ethical Tensions and Integrity, Curricular and Institutional Context, and Reflective Learning and Active Engagement. These results suggest student perceptions are shaped less by technology alone than by the pedagogical and ethical conditions of its introduction. Theoretically, the study identifies an augmentation–formation paradox specific to disciplines that combine codifiable procedure with professional judgment, which is advanced tentatively as extending the boundary conditions of paradox theory in education, a proposition that requires further empirical testing. Thematic analysis using a hybrid inductive–deductive coding strategy served as the primary analytic approach, supported by supplementary lexical analyses. The study contributes to management and accounting education by demonstrating that responsible AI integration requires clear guidance, reflective learning, and explicit alignment among AI use, assessment design, and academic integrity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Mechanical compaction-assisted activation for the controlled construction of ultramicroporous biochar for efficient CO2 capture
abstract: Conventional activation of porous carbon CO2 adsorbents commonly relies on higher activation temperatures or larger activator dosages, often causing carbon loss and pore widening. Herein, O/S-doped ultramicroporous biochars were prepared from sodium lignosulfonate by mechanical compaction-assisted potassium oxalate activation. Precursor packing was regulated to tune the local activation environment and transport behavior during pyrolysis. Compared with the uncompacted sample at 600 °C, compaction increased SBET from 491 to 823 m2 g−1, CO2-accessible ultramicropore volume increased from 0.264 to 0.355 mL g−1, and carbon yield increased from 26.6% to 29.3%. LSC600-5T achieved a CO2 uptake of 5.64 mmol g−1 at 25 °C and 1 bar, while LSC700-5T delivered 9.02 mmol g−1 at 0 °C and 1 bar. However, at 25 °C and 0.15 bar, LSC600-5T showed a CO2 uptake of 2.01 mmol g−1, close to that of LSC600-0T. Structural, correlation, and simulation analyses show that CO2 adsorption at 1 bar is primarily controlled by accessible ultramicropore volume and pore connectivity, while low-pressure uptake is dominated by ~0.35 nm ultramicropores, with O/S polar groups providing additional affinity. Unlike conventional activation that enhances porosity by increasing temperature or activator dosage, mechanical compaction regulates precursor packing and the local activation environment, simultaneously improving accessible ultramicroporosity and carbon retention. This work shifts porous-carbon design from surface-area maximization toward packing-controlled regulation of pore accessibility, carbon utilization, and pressure-dependent CO2 adsorption. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: The mediating role of information security efficiency in the relationship between digital transformation and banking service quality
abstract: This study examines the mediating role of Information Security Efficiency (ISE) in the relationship between Digital Transformation (DT) and Banking Service Quality (BSQ) in Yemen, a developing economy characterized by institutional and operational challenges. Understanding how digital initiatives translate into service improvements is particularly important in such contexts, where infrastructure constraints and security risks may limit the benefits of transformation efforts. The study adopted a quantitative descriptive-analytical design. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire distributed to managerial employees in 17 banks operating in Sana'a city. A total of 401 valid responses were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that DT exerts a positive and statistically significant direct effect on BSQ ( β = 0.861, p < 0.001 ) and on ISE ( β = 0.848, p < 0.001 ). In addition, ISE has a significant positive effect on BSQ ( β = 0.608, p < 0.001 ). The mediation analysis further confirms that ISE significantly mediates the relationship between DT and BSQ ( β = 0.516, p < 0.001 ), indicating that part of the influence of digital transformation on service quality is transmitted through stronger information security capabilities and controls. At the dimensional level of ISE, confidentiality demonstrated the strongest mediating contribution, followed by timeliness, availability, and integrity. Practically, the results suggest that banks in Yemen and comparable emerging markets should integrate digital transformation strategies with effective information security systems, with particular attention to protecting customer data and ensuring timely information access. The study concludes that, in economically fragile environments, information security efficiency should not be viewed merely as a technical requirement, but a strategic condition for sustaining trust and improving banking service quality. title: Scale and space in industrial policy implementation: Geospatial evidence from urban Ethiopia
abstract: Industrial policy in Africa has regained prominence, yet many registered manufacturing investments do not progress to production. This study examines the spatial patterning and correlates of implementation using a field-verified geospatial census of 2277 manufacturing projects in Shaggar City, Ethiopia. Projects were classified into five ordered implementation categories: Not Implemented, Abandoned, Under Construction, Construction Completed, and Operational. Ordered logistic regression was used to examine associations with network distance from Addis Ababa's central business district (CBD), firm size, industrial subsector, and distance to former town centers. In the primary specification, greater distance from the CBD was negatively associated in the primary ordinal specification with lower cumulative odds of being in a higher implementation category (OR = 0.921, 95% CI: 0.901–0.942, p < 0.001). The distance association was nonlinear in supplementary specifications, although its precise form varied across model formulations. Residual diagnostics, however, indicated substantial spatial autocorrelation across all four cumulative thresholds (Moran's I, p < 0.001), limiting the extent to which conventional model-based uncertainty can be interpreted as spatially independent inference. Distance to former town centers showed evidence of stage-specific association, concentrated at earlier implementation transitions. Firm size was also associated with implementation status in the primary ordinal model, with large projects having lower cumulative odds than small projects; this association weakened after adjustment for project timing and was directionally reversed in a binary multilevel sensitivity model. The latter model accounted for sub-city clustering but produced a non-positive-definite Hessian and is therefore treated as indicative rather than confirmatory. Missing firm-size information was spatially patterned, with missing records more common near the metropolitan core and among projects with higher operational rates. These findings show that manufacturing implementation is a spatially structured, multi-stage process and that observed associations depend on how implementation stage, project timing, missing information, and spatial dependence are handled. The study highlights the value of field-verified project-level data for distinguishing registered investment from actual implementation and for identifying where different stages of the implementation process may require closer monitoring and support. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: From Event Logs to Process Performance Indicators via Declarative Process Mining
abstract: Organizations increasingly rely on event logs to monitor and improve business process performance, yet identifying meaningful and measurable Process Performance Indicators (PPIs) remains a challenging and largely manual task. Recent work has shown that Large Language Models (LLMs) can support this process by suggesting, operationalizing and computing PPIs against an event log based on process descriptions and business goals. However, such approaches depend heavily on user input quality and are not explicitly grounded in observed process behavior. In this paper, we present Declare2PPI, a fully automated pipeline for generating PPIs directly from event logs. Our approach follows a bottom-up strategy in which declarative process mining extracts behavioral constraints that guide LLM-based generation. The resulting PPIs reflect process-wide execution patterns and are automatically translated into executable definitions and computed to ensure measurability. The approach also supports the exploration of multiple PPI sets and prioritizes indicators based on their relevance and variability. We evaluate the approach through a qualitative comparison with a state-of-the-art top-down method and a quantitative analysis of correctness and robustness. The results show that grounding PPI generation in observed behavior leads to more relevant, non-redundant, and consistently computable PPIs, supporting data-driven performance analysis with minimal effort. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: David vs. Goliath in Next Activity Prediction: Argmax vs. LSTM, Transformer, and LLM
abstract: Next activity prediction (NAP) is a cornerstone of predictive process monitoring (PPM), enabling organizations to move from retrospective analysis to proactive process steering. The PPM field has progressed from classical machine learning through deep learning architectures such as LSTMs and Transformers to large language models (LLMs). Despite growing model complexity, no benchmark jointly compares LLMs, Transformers, LSTMs, and simple baselines in a direct sequence modeling setting for NAP. In this paper, we fill this gap with a systematic benchmark. We compare vocabulary-adapted LLMs, Transformers trained from scratch, LLM-distilled Transformers, and LSTMs against a simple counting-based argmax baseline across seven real-life event logs. Our results tell a David vs. Goliath story: pretraining confers no consistent improvement over training from scratch, model size shows little effect on performance, and on most datasets the argmax baseline matches or approaches the performance of billion-parameter LLMs. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: CV-Driven Window Selection for Multi-perspective Concept Drift Detection in Event Logs
abstract: Process mining leverages event logs recorded in information systems to discover and analyze business processes. However, rapid technological and market changes often lead to evolving process behavior, which manifests as concept drift in event logs. While recent research has focused on detecting and explaining such drifts, many existing approaches focus on individual perspectives of process behavior, often emphasizing control-flow, while other perspectives receive less attention. In this paper, we propose a multi-perspective concept drift detection approach. The approach models process behavior as a time series and introduces a coefficient-of-variation-based strategy to automatically determine suitable window sizes for drift detection. This adaptive window selection enables more stable change-point detection across different process perspectives. We evaluate the approach against established baselines using synthetic and benchmark datasets. The results demonstrate competitive detection performance and show that the proposed method effectively identifies drifts across multiple perspectives of process behavior. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Collaborative post-disaster restoration framework for transportation-distribution networks utilizing traffic management and mobile resources
abstract: Urban distribution networks (DNs), which comprise substations, distribution buses and lines, electrical loads, and distributed energy resources, are increasingly interdependent with transportation networks (TNs). This growing interdependency increases their joint vulnerability to extreme events because failures in either network can propagate to the other and cause cascading disruptions. However, research on effective strategies to mitigate the negative impacts of these interdependencies and enhance the resilience of distribution and transportation networks remains insufficient. To address this gap, we analyze these interdependencies and propose a joint restoration framework, which co-optimizes TN traffic management strategies (including reversible lane allocation and traffic signal control) with DN restoration measures (including network reconfiguration and the dispatch of mobile energy storage systems, repair crews, and maintenance transportation crews). In this framework, the TN is illustrated using an extended Cell Transmission Model (CTM) with real-time evacuation routing to capture spatiotemporal traffic-flow dynamics, while the DN is represented with a reconfigurable DistFlow formulation. Then, a hierarchical solution approach is developed to efficiently coordinate traffic flow optimization, dynamic travel-time updating, and power restoration scheduling. Case studies on integrated distribution and transportation network test systems demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves system resilience compared to conventional separated restoration strategies, achieving higher load restoration rates and evacuation efficiency. © 2017 Elsevier Inc. . © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
