title: Enhancing Transparency and Operational Security in FinTech Transaction Systems Through the Use of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Modern financial institutions, particularly digital banks, fintech companies, and Banking-as-a-Service providers, operate in a highly dynamic environment where millions of transactions and business events are processed every day. Therefore, ensuring an adequate level of operational security, as well as compliance with regulations (DORA, EU AI Act, MRM)—i.e., ensuring the transparency of algorithmic decisions—and, consequently, the use of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods, becomes a critical characteristic of their operations. This article presents selected critical components of an operational security platform for financial institutions, implemented in a Fintech-as-a-Service (FaaS) architecture, that meet the above requirements. They are based on advanced machine learning algorithms and XAI methods. The proposed solution integrates transactional layers with external services for anti-money laundering (AML), know-your-customer (KYC), and fraud detection, enabling real-time anomaly detection. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: GNN4PPM: Multi-Target Predictive Process Monitoring with Relational Graph Convolutional Networks
abstract: Predictive Process Monitoring (PPM) aims at predicting at runtime and as early as possible the future states of a process execution. Common tasks include predicting the next event, the time to completion of a trace, and outcomes. Existing approaches typically consider an event from the perspective of the executed activities along with their timestamps and case identifiers. This leads to the disadvantage that in real-life settings, there is much more information recorded in the event log that is not captured or completely ignored when performing prediction tasks. We introduce GNN4PPM, an approach that predicts all next events along with their complete data payload at once. We represent event information in a heterogeneous knowledge graph that captures the event log as an RDF semantics, and train the embeddings with a Relational Graph Convolutional Network (R-GCN). Our approach is promising in comparison to existing solutions, and experiments with state-of-the-art solutions prove the accuracy and applicability of GNN4PPM in complex settings. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Modelling barriers to green entrepreneurship in traditional MSMEs: Evidence from the Batik industry in Madura, Indonesia
abstract: The global transition toward sustainable development has increased pressure on micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to adopt environmentally responsible business practices. Although green entrepreneurship is widely promoted as a pathway to sustainability, its implementation remains challenging for traditional and culture-based enterprises. Existing studies largely emphasize performance outcomes, while empirical evidence on implementation barriers remains limited. This study examines the key barriers to green entrepreneurship implementation among batik MSMEs in Madura, Indonesia. A quantitative approach was employed using survey data collected from 200 respondents across four regencies. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS to assess the relationships between government policy, technology adoption, environmental education, and implementation barriers. The findings reveal that technology-related constraints constitute the most significant barrier, followed by weak regulatory support and limited environmental knowledge. High costs of green technology adoption and insufficient access to education, information, and sustainable production inputs further constrain MSMEs' readiness to transition toward sustainable practices. This study contributes to the green entrepreneurship literature by shifting the analytical focus from sustainability outcomes to implementation barriers in traditional MSMEs and by providing a more robust empirical model using PLS-SEM. The findings offer policy-relevant insights for developing targeted regulatory frameworks, environmental education programs, and technological support mechanisms to facilitate sustainability transitions in heritage-based industries. Moreover, the results provide implications that may be applicable to traditional MSMEs in other developing economies. title: Feature Attribution-Based Explainability Analysis of Deep Learning Models in Predictive Process Monitoring
abstract: Predictive process monitoring supports the optimization and control of operational business processes by forecasting the future state or outcome of ongoing cases. While deep neural networks have achieved strong performance for these tasks by modeling sequential dependencies in event logs, their black-box nature limits trust and practical adoption. Feature attribution methods are often used to address this, but applying them directly poses a dilemma: event-level attributions impose high computational complexity for long traces, while explanations based on aggregated trace representations often fail to capture the underlying control-flow dynamics. To address this issue, we propose a local post-hoc explainability method for deep neural networks in outcome prediction. The method relies on a control-flow-aware segmentation algorithm that partitions a trace into meaningful segments and supports the computation of segment-level SHAP explanations. This makes it possible to identify which parts of a trace influence a prediction and which change points steer the case toward the predicted outcome. We assess the proposed segmentation method on a synthetic dataset with known process logic, where meaningful change points can be explicitly verified, and we demonstrate its usefulness on real-world event logs from a loan application process and an administrative process of a Dutch municipality. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Visual Comparative Analysis of Process Variants
abstract: Data visualization plays a central role in process mining, particularly when analysts need to compare multiple process models, often representing different process variants, to assess changes, detect deviations, or benchmark performance. However, effectively supporting such comparative analysis remains challenging. To investigate this problem, we combine three perspectives: interviews with nine process mining analysts, established visual analytics principles, and an analysis of existing process mining visualizations. Based on this analysis, we identify key challenges for comparative analysis, including weak support for goal-driven analysis, insufficient scalability, and limited flexibility. Based on these insights, we propose an interactive approach for the flexible, scalable, and goal-driven comparison of multiple process models. The approach enables dynamic, goal-driven highlighting of differences and similarities, allowing analysts to tailor comparison based on specific analysis objectives. We developed a prototype implementing the main concepts and interaction mechanisms, and evaluated its perceived usefulness and usability through two workshops with a total of ten participants (students and experts). The results provide initial design insights for visual analytics techniques supporting process variant comparison and highlight directions for future research. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Semantically-Guided LLM Pipeline for Business Architecture Modelling with Incremental Knowledge Acquisition
abstract: Business Architecture (BA) modelling is a resource-intensive exercise, particularly for abstract concepts such as business capabilities that typically requires iterative workshops that are time-consuming and cognitively demanding for experts. Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as a promising solution for automating BA modelling. However, current methods often fail to capture task context, producing semantically invalid models. Although LLMs can be pre-trained or fine-tuned to encode such context, it is costly and difficult to sustain. This paper proposes an LLM pipeline for business capability modeling that integrates rich contextual knowledge by combining a BA semantic model with organisational insights extracted from unstructured business documents and incrementally acquired expert knowledge. We evaluate the approach on three state-of-the-art LLMs by processing 495 statements extracted from business documents, and compare its performance against the baselines combine standard definitions and in-context learning. Our method reports an average performance gain of 65.2% on a commercial LLM and 58.9%–63.8% on two open-source LLMs over the baselines. This work advances the automation of LLM based BA modelling by providing an effective and efficient mechanism for incorporating existing documents and expert feedback into the automation process with minimal expert involvement. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Circular economy practices and clean energy transition performance: the moderating role of critical mineral circularity and policy stringency among EU energy-intensive firms
abstract: The clean energy transition demands unprecedented quantities of critical minerals — lithium, cobalt, copper, and rare earth elements — with demand projected to rise six-fold by 2030, far beyond what primary mining alone can supply. Circular economy (CE) practices offer a strategic pathway to close this mineral gap while simultaneously reducing the carbon intensity of energy production. Yet despite growing scholarly interest, the empirical relationship between firm-level CE adoption and energy transition performance (ETP) remains fragmented across disciplines, with no unified framework linking these constructs at scale. This study addresses that gap through a two-phase mixed-methods design. Phase 1 delivers a PRISMA-compliant systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis of 405 synthesised articles, confirming the absence of firm-level empirical models in this nexus. Phase 2 develops and tests multi-level conceptual model grounded in Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the Natural Resource-Based View, and Institutional Theory, using structural equation modelling–partial least squares (SEM-PLS) on survey data from 318 EU energy-intensive firms, complemented by fixed-effects panel regression merging Eurostat and IEA databases. CE practices significantly predict ETP (β = 0.312, p < 0.001). This study makes three contributions: an empirically validated firm-level framework linking CE practices to ETP, which to our knowledge is the first of its kind at this scale; the introduction of critical mineral circularity as novel strategic moderator; and cross-national evidence on how policy environments condition the CE–energy transition nexus. Findings carry direct implications for corporate supply chain strategy, EU regulatory design, and achievement of SDG 7, SDG 12, and SDG 13. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Systematic and Automated Diagnosis of Process Models Using Reference Frameworks
abstract: Reference frameworks in Business Process Management (BPM) are generic best-practice templates used to design, analyze, benchmark, and improve business processes (BPs). They promote consistency in BP structure and terminology and support BP model diagnosis by revealing gaps and weaknesses through comparison with a reference structure. Despite extensive research on the development and adaptation of reference frameworks, the BPM literature offers limited methodological support for their systematic application to existing BP models, leaving much of the analysis to manual work by domain experts. However, this analysis typically demands significant time, human, and financial resources and does not scale well to enterprise-wide BP sets, limiting its practical use for BP diagnosis. In this paper, following a Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, we analyze existing approaches that leverage reference frameworks for BP diagnosis to identify their key characteristics, and propose a maturity model to systematically guide their application to existing BP models. To demonstrate feasibility, we use a Large Language Model (LLM) to automate the application of the maturity model, generating suggestions across all diagnostic levels. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Bridging Accuracy and Interpretability in Business Process Simulation via Knowledge Distillation
abstract: Business Process Simulation (BPS) is widely used to analyze and optimize processes in a controlled environment. Recent advances integrate AI models to improve the simulation accuracy of process perspectives such as control-flow and time. However, BPS-based improvement requires testing alternative what-if analyses. This can only be achieved through white-box models, where analysts can inspect and modify the underlying decision logic. Purely black-box models, although often highly accurate, lack transparency and limit configurability. However, traditional white-box models (e.g. decision trees) provide explicit and interpretable rules but may struggle to capture complex dependencies, leading to lower predictive accuracy, hampering the BPS realism. This paper proposes a distillation-based approach to bridge the gap between predictive accuracy and interpretability in BPS. We first train black-box predictive models (referred to as teacher models) to learn complex temporal and behavioral patterns from event logs. We then extract the knowledge captured by the teacher models and transfer it into probabilistic decision trees, obtaining interpretable surrogate white-box models (referred to as student models). The distilled models approximate the learned behavior of the teacher while offering a white-box representation and maintaining competitive predictive performance. Experimental results in four case studies, using four alternative teacher models, demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach. The findings show that distillation is able to improve the accuracy of simulation models, compared to standard decision trees without distillation, while maintaining interpretability and supporting reliable what-if analyses. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: How Organizations Use Process Mining to Enable Automations: Evidence from Qualitative Interviews in Canada
abstract: Robotic Process Automation (RPA) and Agentic AI (AAI) are increasingly positioned as central enablers of digital transformation, supporting organizations in automating repetitive, rule-based tasks as well as more dynamic and decision-intensive processes. However, organizations often face challenges in systematically identifying, prioritizing, and planning automation initiatives that align with strategic goals and deliver measurable value. This study investigates how industry practitioners plan and prioritize automation initiatives and how Process Mining (PM) can be leveraged to identify suitable candidates for RPA or AAI deployment. The research examines practitioners’ approaches to selecting automation opportunities, identifying technical feasibility with business impact, and measuring the automation impact on the improved business processes. The study’s qualitative research design involves semi-structured interviews with fifteen industry experts in Canada, including process analysts, automation leads, consultants, and technology specialists. Using Nvivo and concept coding, the analysis identified recurring patterns for each of the interview themes (6) and subthemes (19). The findings indicate that organizations strongly recognize the value of PM in accelerating the identification of RPA/AAI automation opportunities. However, maximizing its adoption and impact requires addressing several challenges, including data availability, budget constraints, limited technology awareness, and insufficient collaboration among teams. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Automatic AI-Based Extraction of Processes from Administrative Texts: The Case of Waste Management
abstract: Public administrations produce large volumes of unstructured administrative documents that regulate operational procedures, responsibilities, and regulatory constraints. These documents are characterized by high information density and fragmented procedural knowledge, making both human interpretation and automated extraction challenging. This issue is particularly critical in the waste management domain, where regulatory complexity and local variability significantly impact operational processes. This paper presents a hybrid pipeline for the automatic extraction and structuring of operational procedures from unstructured administrative texts. The proposed approach combines LLMs with RAG to ensure faithful, traceable extraction constrained to the source document. The pipeline identifies procedural sections, extracts relevant information from each section, and generates visual workflows. The system is evaluated on real-world administrative documents for waste management. Results show that the integration of generative AI within a structured pipeline improves the accuracy and reliability of procedural knowledge extraction, while mitigating hallucination risks. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: AI-Driven Automation in Knowledge-Intensive License Management: An Empirical Analysis of Enterprise Constraints and Automation Potential
abstract: Software License Management (SLM) is a complex, Knowledge-Intensive Process (KiP) in which fragmented data, heterogeneous IT landscapes, and frequent vendor audits contribute to significant process governance gaps, reducing organizational agility and increasing contractual and financial risk exposure. This study investigates the relationship between operational burden and contractual risk by examining SLM in the context of the Agentic Business Process Management (Agentic BPM) framework and the design–emergence gap. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was used, starting with a quantitative survey (N = 60) to establish three novel metrics: the Cost and Risk Exposure Index (CREI), the Operational Burden and Visibility Index (OBVI), and the Automation Readiness and Demand Index (ARDI). These quantitative findings were refined through twelve semi-structured interviews with senior IT and license managers. The findings reveal that traditional rule-based systems fail to address the dynamic nature of license governance, leaving the SLM undermanaged despite growing financial exposure. To bridge the design–emergence gap, this study presents three process governance-oriented design principles for Agentic BPM: lifecycle visibility, cross-functional coordination, and human-in-the-loop oversight. The study concludes with a proposal for a cross-functional process governance framework that shifts the focus from rigid task automation to a lifecycle-oriented agentic oversight model, thus enhancing audit readiness and supporting the development of process-oriented governance capabilities. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Cognitive framing and affective expressions of green economic growth: Evidence from social media analytics
abstract: Green growth has become an important pathway for reconciling economic development with environmental sustainability, increasing the need to understand how it is discussed and evaluated across digital communication environments. This study examines the cognitive and affective dimensions of stakeholder-related online discourse on green growth using social media analytics. The final analytical dataset comprises 1799 English-language posts collected from LinkedIn, Reddit, TikTok, Twitter/X, and YouTube. The methodological framework integrates lexicon-based sentiment and emotion analysis, Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modelling, correspondence analysis, and non-parametric statistical testing. The sentiment analysis indicates a predominantly positive lexical orientation, although validation results suggest that individual-level sentiment classifications should be interpreted cautiously. LDA topic modelling, conducted on 1792 posts retained after vocabulary filtering, identifies three principal thematic domains interpreted as textual proxies for cognitive framing: Sustainable Development and ESG Transition (29.97%), Climate, Energy and Net-Zero Transition (44.64%), and Circular Economy and Sustainable Business Practices (25.39%). Emotion profiles differ significantly across thematic domains, while cross-platform analysis reveals systematic variation in sentiment, emotional expression, and thematic composition. Correspondence analysis further indicates platform-specific associations between social media environments and thematic domains. Overall, the findings demonstrate systematic associations between thematic framing and affective expression in green growth-related online discourse, while avoiding causal interpretation of these relationships. The study contributes to sustainability communication research by integrating cognitive and affective dimensions within a multi-platform analytical framework and provides practical insights for designing context-sensitive green communication strategies. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Advancing AI Integration: Exploring Business Process Management Capabilities for AI-Driven Processes
abstract: The increased integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into business processes challenges established business process management (BPM) assumptions. AI-driven processes are shaped by autonomy, opacity, and high data dependency. This paper examines the BPM capabilities organizations need to establish when integrating AI into business processes. Drawing on an exploratory qualitative study based on 18 semi-structured interviews, we reveal that existing BPM capabilities must be enhanced to account for autonomy shifts toward AI actors that are characterized by non-deterministic behavior, opacity, and dependence on reliable data. Building on the interview data, we identify AI-specific capability demands and derive three cross-cutting capability shifts that organizations need to establish to successfully and sustainably integrate AI into their business processes. We contribute by showing that effective AI integration requires coordinated attention to process selection, data readiness, governance mechanisms, role development, and organizational conditions enabling effective oversight and continuous adaptation of processes. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: WARP: Worktime-Aware Representation for Predictive Process Monitoring
abstract: Predictive Process Monitoring leverages historical event logs to generate data-driven forecasts about the future development of ongoing process instances, such as the time until the completion of the next event. Recent research has focused on enhancing predictive performance through advanced deep-learning architectures and feature engineering. In this context, existing approaches typically model time as a continuous calendar-based feature. This design choice overlooks an important characteristic of real-world business processes: process execution is often constrained by organizational working patterns, including business hours, shift schedules, and weekends. In this paper, we investigate the integration of organizational working constraints into the predictive pipeline through a worktime-based transformation of the temporal axis. We propose a methodology that maps event timestamps from a conventional clocktime axis to a worktime-based axis, effectively excluding periods of scheduled resource unavailability. This transformation allows predictive models to learn temporal patterns based on active process execution rather than elapsed calendar time. We evaluate the approach using both synthetic and real-world event log data. The results show that the worktime-based transformation improves prediction accuracy, particularly in scenarios characterized by temporal gaps between discrete working intervals. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The judgment-based approach to entrepreneurship: The uncertainty–heterogeneity nexus
abstract: The judgment-based approach (JBA) has emerged as an important contemporary perspective in management and entrepreneurship research. The JBA offers a distinctive theoretical account of entrepreneurship, centered on the formation and implementation of subjective theories of value creation under conditions of Knightian uncertainty, which highlights resource ownership, heterogeneous capital structure, organization and the firm, institutions, uncertainty, and the overarching need to appraise and coordinate all these factors using judgment. We present and develop the JBA by articulating the uncertainty–heterogeneity nexus, in which the joint presence of fundamental uncertainty and heterogeneous resources gives rise to the need for entrepreneurial judgment and makes its exercise economically consequential. Because judgment is subjective, tacit, and difficult to communicate or contract upon, entrepreneurs must rely on ownership and residual control rights to create value, linking judgment to the combination and deployment of resources, profit and loss, and organizational structure. The purpose of this article is threefold. First, we provide a systematic statement of the JBA as a theoretical framework, clarifying its core constructs, causal mechanisms, and domain of application. Second, we engage with key critiques and distinguish the JBA from related approaches, including opportunity-based, effectuation, and bricolage perspectives. Third, we outline directions for future research that build on the JBA's emphasis on judgment, ownership, and the organization and deployment of heterogeneous resources under uncertainty. By integrating these elements, we position the JBA as a coherent and distinctive theory of entrepreneurship with broad implications for research in management, organization, and strategy. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Making Sense of Continuous Process Dynamics
abstract: Operating in dynamic and often unpredictable environments, business processes are exposed to changes that cause their execution to fluctuate over time. Since changes are inseparable parts of process execution, capturing them is crucial for gaining reliable insights into how they behave during their execution. Although prior research has studied continuous fluctuations of processes, most studies have focused primarily on visual representations of such changes. However, drawing more actionable insights requires a structured analysis approach that goes beyond visualization. To this end, this paper explores the potential of leveraging established time series analysis techniques—such as decomposition and correlation analysis—to derive meaningful insights into such changes. We evaluate our approach through backward-looking and forward-looking analysis: the former demonstrates the type of insights it can provide into continuous process dynamics by applying it to multiple event logs, while the latter examines whether the approach is beneficial for a downstream process mining task, the prediction of future process behavior. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Microbial succession and genome-resolved metabolic functions shape flavor evolution during sauce-flavor Baijiu fermentation
abstract: Sauce-flavor Baijiu (SFB) fermentation is characterized by a unique multi-round solid-state process, during which complex microbial succession drives flavor formation. However, the functional differentiation and metabolic mechanisms of microbial communities across successive fermentation rounds remain poorly understood. In this study, the physicochemical properties, microbial assembly, and metabolic profiles of fermented grains (FG) were investigated across seven production rounds (R1-R7). The results revealed that as fermentation rounds progressed, the FG environment evolved toward elevated acidity and reduced pH, driving a directional shift in the microbial community from an initially diverse assemblage to a structure dominated by acid-tolerant Acetilactobacillus, which established pronounced ecological dominance in later rounds. Metabolomic analysis further indicated that this dynamic adjustment of microbial structure drove the evolution of the flavor profile, specifically manifesting as differential accumulation of compounds such as esters, alcohols, and pyrazines across the various rounds. Co-occurrence network analysis demonstrated that positive microbial interactions significantly predominated within the fermentation system, and that community function exhibited a convergent trend as the rounds increased. Furthermore, 158 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) were recovered, and metabolic reconstruction elucidated the potential contributions of genera such as Pediococcus, Bacillus, and Oceanobacillus to key metabolic pathways, including glycolysis, phenylalanine metabolism, and pyrazine biosynthesis. This work provides important insights into microbial regulation and quality improvement in SFB fermentation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Process Binoculars: Resilient Log Generation from Multi-video Sources
abstract: Process mining links event data to process models, typically assuming structured logs. However, many actual processes do not leave digital traces and need to be discovered in the field. Existing approaches mitigate this by integrating logs with multiple sources, including observations of actual processes. Recent works have pioneered process discovery methods from video sources, but these methods often require manual labeling and produce brittle logs dependent on a single viewpoint, risking incomplete capture of activities. We introduce the Process Binoculars, a technique for generating event logs from multiple video sources that provides 360-degree coverage of activities. The approach automates activity identification using representation learning and semantic abstraction. Micro-actions are first extracted from video streams, enabling generalization across processes. Learned representations over event windows improve robustness to camera errors, while clustering and abstraction yield human-readable activities. Evaluation on a large-scale assembly dataset shows that Process Binoculars produces accurate process models and remains resilient under controlled noise. Our code and benchmarks are publicly released (See https://github.com/JulianNeuberger/pm-binoculars). © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Artificial Intelligence for After-Sales Services: A Case of Luxury Fashion Industry
abstract: The paper explores how AI can handle the main challenges in managing after-sales of luxury fashion products. Two most prominent AI solutions were identified: automated image analysis for defect detection and text elaboration for sentiment analysis. Their significance lies in their ability to streamline customer interactions and product evaluations, particularly using computer vision for defect identification and categorization for returned items and leveraging LLMs to assess repair feasibility, estimate service times, and improve communication between in-store assistants and customers. These technologies offer tangible improvements in service efficiency and quality control, reinforcing their strategic importance in after-sales processes in the luxury fashion industry. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Simulation of Circular Product Management Based on a Blockchain Platform
abstract: Circular product management plays a crucial role in establishing circular production systems based on the stock of artefacts distributed in society. The cyber-physical lifecycle system (CPLS) is a digital platform that supports decision-making through material flow analysis for circular product management based on product lifecycle models. This paper proposes a matching function between suppliers and demanders of end-of-use products that is implemented in a blockchain-based CPLS. In a case study focusing on the circular business of refurbished industrial motors, a CPLS prototype was created, and conditions for successful transactions were identified through economic experiments. Subsequently, a lifecycle simulation was performed using the experimental data as input, which demonstrated the effectiveness of the circular management approach based on demand–supply matching within a CPLS. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Mapping the Maturity of Servitization and PSS Research: Evidence from an International Scientific Panel
abstract: Over the past three decades, research on servitization and Product-Service Systems (PSS) has evolved into a consolidated and multidisciplinary field. While numerous literature reviews have mapped dominant themes and theoretical foundations, limited attention has been devoted to assessing the maturity stage of different research streams and identifying their evolutionary trajectories. This study proposes a maturity assessment of servitization and PSS research based on a literature-informed expert panel involving the international Scientific Advisory Board of the ASAP Interuniversity Research Centre on Servitization. The study adopts a lifecycle positioning lens to assess five thematic areas. Through pre-meeting structured inputs, collective discussion, and post-meeting synthesis, the panel evaluated the research streams by positioning them across emergent, maturity, and relaunch stages. Findings reveal heterogeneous maturity levels within the field. Domains such as IoT-enabled service and subscription-based business models achieved conceptual maturity. In contrast, ecosystem governance, customer adoption dynamics, digital regulation remain in the emergent stage. Structural tensions, including organizational capability gaps, scalability challenges, and methodological limitations, suggest that theoretical consolidation has not yet translated into systemic implementation, acting instead as relaunch triggers for the field. By introducing a lifecycle-based perspective and integrating expert-based field evaluation, this study contributes a reflexive assessment of where servitization research currently stands and identifies the emergent challenges and relaunch dynamics. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Development and Validation of a Roadmapping Methodology for Servitization
abstract: Servitization, the transition from product—towards service-centric offerings, offers manufacturers an opportunity to achieve relevant strategic advantage, sustainable impact and increased efficiency, while tackling encompassing challenges and global trends. This transition, enhanced by the combined adoption of digital technologies, requires a significant company transformation, which implies challenges related to the creation and deployment of new activities, resources mindset and partnerships. To manage the transformation and the related challenges, roadmapping can support companies in planning strategic and operational activities and effectively steer efforts. Nonetheless, current literature offers limited approaches for roadmapping in servitization. This paper proposes and validates, through the application in two manufacturing companies, a multi-step roadmapping methodology, leveraging the Business Model Canvas framework. This tool, intended for the application during the initial new business model definition phase, supports companies in building roadmaps to guide and structure strategic and operational activities for servitization, harmonizing efforts across extended timeframes. The paper complements the current research on Product Service System (PSS) design considering the extended transformational process required to sustain the new offerings, while proposing a structured tool to guide manufacturers’ efforts in deploying servitization strategies. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: How Servitization Enables—And Constrains—Sustainable Value Creation: An Empirical Analysis Among Manufacturing Firms
abstract: In recent years, manufacturing companies have been operating in an increasingly complex environment shaped by two concurrent drivers: the evolution of business models and the ecological transition. The diffusion of servitization and Product–Service Systems (PSS), has been accompanied by growing pressure to reduce environmental impacts throughout the entire product life cycle. The relationship between servitization and sustainability has attracted increasing attention in the literature, leading to the emergence of concepts such as sustainable servitization and sustainable PSS. While prior studies highlight the potential sustainability benefits of servitized business models, they also reveal ambiguities and inconsistent evidence, suggesting that servitization cannot be considered inherently sustainable. Building on this literature, this study explores how the barriers hindering the practical implementation of sustainable servitization manifest in practice through qualitative evidence from nine manufacturing companies characterized by different levels of servitization maturity. The findings identify key challenges faced by firms when integrating sustainability into PSS and highlight practices that can help address them. The study contributes to the literature by providing empirical insights into sustainable value creation in manufacturing and by identifying best practices that can support companies in advancing their sustainable servitization strategies. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Sorption enhanced co-gasification of pine wood and waste PET plastic with membrane assisted hydrogen separation for gasifier effluent valorisation and CO2 mitigation
abstract: The use of gasifier effluent streams through integrated gas separation and purification technologies is important for clean H2 production and carbon emission reduction. This study develops an integrated Aspen Plus model that combines sorption enhanced co-gasification of pine wood and waste polyethene terephthalate (PET) with membrane assisted H2 separation to maximise H2 recovery while mitigating CO2 emissions. The effects of gasification temperature, steam-to-feed ratio, feedstock blending, and CaO sorbent addition on syngas composition, gasifier performance, and membrane separation efficiency were systematically investigated. Increasing the gasification temperature initially enhanced H2 production, but a slight decline was observed at higher temperatures. At 750 °C, H2 concentrations reached approximately 62 vol% for pine wood and 58 vol% for PET. CO2 concentration decreased from 26.97 to 18.95 vol% for pine wood and from 25.18 to 13.07 vol% for PET as the temperature increased. Higher steam-to-feed ratios further promoted H2 formation through steam reforming; however, excessive steam slightly reduced carbon conversion efficiency (CCE) and heating value of syngas. The addition of CaO significantly upgraded the gasifier effluent by increasing H2 concentration from 62 to 79 vol% for pine wood and from 58 to 70 vol% for PET, while decreasing CO2 from 22 to 11 vol% and from 16 to 9 vol%, respectively. Net CO2 emissions were reduced from approximately 95 to 40 kg/h, and CCE was reduced from 61.19 to 33.67% and 67.41 to 47.81% for wood and PET plastic, respectively. During co-gasification, PET enrich blends produced syngas with higher calorific value, while CaO maintained H2 concentrations of 72–76 vol% and CO2 below 12 vol%. Integration with a H2 selective membrane separated the gasifier effluent, producing high purity H2 and a CO2 enriched retentate stream for subsequent carbon capture. The integrated process offers an efficient pathway for biomass plastic waste valorisation and low carbon H2 production. © 2026 The Authors

title: Ownership structure and the international expansion of German firms
abstract: Despite decades of falling trade barriers and advancing globalization, most multinational enterprises (MNEs) never venture beyond their home region. We argue that part of the explanation lies in ownership structure: who ultimately controls the firm determines how broadly it operates and how freely its geographic scope can be adjusted. Drawing on the attention-based view, we derive eight hypotheses about how ownership origin, international experience, and concentration shape the breadth of geographic scope and the direction of its adjustment over time. Using a large panel of German MNEs, we show that domestic ownership is associated with broader scope and greater propensity for upward adjustment, with the advantage strongest for internationally experienced owners. Ownership concentration constrains the level of geographic scope but not whether it expands or contracts. These findings provide the first evidence on ownership and geographic scope for developed-country MNEs and reorient theoretical debate from resource transfer to organizational authorization. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: Adoption of Battery Electric Trucks: A Review on Transport Companies’ Perspectives
abstract: The transition to battery electric trucks is widely recognized as a promising step toward decarbonizing road freight, yet adoption remains limited outside a few leading markets. While considerable attention has been devoted to modeling the performance of battery electric trucks, much less is known about how electrification is experienced by transport-owning logistics operators. This review addresses that gap by focusing on studies that provide insight into the implications of adopting battery electric trucks with stationary charging for transport owners. The results show that the literature continues to pay limited attention to the motivations and pressures shaping adoption, as well as to the organizational and business-model changes required to integrate battery electric trucks into logistics operations. In addition, there is a clear opportunity for further research on how these pressures evolve in response to changing and often inconsistent policy signals. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Navigating Complexity in the Circular Economy: A Systems Perspective on Scotch Whisky
abstract: Despite ambitious circular economy (CE) policies in Scotland, translating national commitments into effective industrial implementation remains a critical challenge. This study examines how Scotland’s emerging CE policies enable or constrain CE adoption within Scotch whisky - an industry characterized by export orientation, premium packaging, and untapped potential to valorize by-products. Drawing on systems thinking, we apply causal loop diagrams (CLDs) to analyze qualitative data from semi-structured interviews with stakeholders, using a four-step coding process to translate interview data into feedback structures. Our analysis reveals twelve interconnected feedback loops across three thematic domains: bio-based distilling resource circularity, product packaging circularity, and industry-wide knowledge-sharing dynamics. The findings demonstrate how operational priorities, brand heritage, and export-oriented business models create distinct barriers for the CE transition of Scotch whisky. This research contributes an empirical systems analysis of CE adoption in Scotch whisky and a methodological pathway for systems-based CE research applicable to other industrial sectors. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Path-reliability analysis for perishable goods delivery in urban multigraph networks: Integrating non-instantaneous deterioration and failed-delivery risks
abstract: With the rapid development of the instant retail business model, consumers have placed increasingly stringent demands on delivery speed and service quality in perishable goods distribution. In instant retail contexts, hot-chain delivery involves managing perishable goods characterized by non-instantaneous deterioration, where quality degradation progresses over delivery time in urban multigraph networks, thereby posing distinctive operational challenges. To address these issues, this paper defines path-reliability, denoting the reliability of a specific path between two customer nodes, to summarize path operating conditions, including congestion, reachability, and connectivity, and establishes a functional relationship between path-reliability and delivery delay time. On this basis, a perishable goods delivery (PGD) network model is developed under customer availability profiles, and a hybrid tabu search algorithm equipped with neighbourhood operators tailored to multigraph structures is proposed for its solution. The model is then validated on randomly generated benchmark instances as well as real-world operational data from a prefabricated-food distribution enterprise in Xi'an. The results indicate that in regions with dispersed customer distribution, multi-path planning combined with reliability assessment yields significant cost savings and risk reduction, whereas in highly clustered regions single-path planning is sufficient to achieve efficient resource allocation while simplifying computation and implementation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: The IFIP WG5.7 Service Systems Special Interest Group Renewed Research Framework and Agenda on Product-Service Systems and Digital Servitization
abstract: Product-Service Systems (PSSs) and Digital Servitization are increasingly recognized as key enablers for sustainable and data-driven industrial transformation. However, the rapid evolution of digital technologies, circular economy principles, and service ecosystems is reshaping the PSS research landscape, calling for updated and integrated research frameworks. This paper proposes a Research Framework and Agenda developed within the IFIP WG5.7 Special Interest Group (SIG) on Service Systems Design, Engineering and Management (SSDE&M). The Research Framework and Agenda are grounded in a two-step methodology combining an online brainstorming workshop and a structured survey involving the SIG members. The results identify and structure current research priorities across five core research areas, while also revealing emerging research themes related to ecosystem integration, data-driven value creation, and lifecycle management. Building on these insights, the proposed Research Framework and Agenda organise PSS research into three interconnected levels: (i) Design and Methods, (ii) Business and Organizational Transformation, and (iii) Ecosystem and Governance Context, complemented by four cross-cutting analytical dimensions: (i) Circular Economy and Rebound Effects, (ii) Digital Technologies and Artificial Intelligence, (iii) Service Ecosystems and Governance, and (iv) Responsible and Socially Sustainable Service Systems. The proposed Research Framework and Agenda contribute to consolidating fragmented research streams and provide a structured basis for future research work within the IFIP WG5.7 SSDE&M SIG and broader PSS research community, supporting both academic research and industrial practice. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Mapping Rebound Mechanisms in Circular Manufacturing: A Causal Loop Diagram Approach
abstract: The manufacturing industry is undergoing a strategic transition toward a circular economy to mitigate its substantial environmental footprint. Although circular strategies such as remanufacturing, recycling, and servitization aim to decouple value creation from resource consumption, their implementation often triggers unintended rebound effects. These effects arise when efficiency gains stimulate systemic responses that partially or fully offset the expected environmental benefits. Although these offsets are well documented, research on rebound mechanisms (RMs) in business-to-business (B2B) contexts remains fragmented and largely exploratory. This paper addresses this gap by adopting a system dynamics perspective to map the RMs activated by circular strategies in B2B settings through a Causal Loop Diagram (CLD). The analysis identifies the key variables and feedback structures that shape these mechanisms, providing a qualitative framework for understanding how sustainability gains can be eroded across core business processes (i.e., business model, production, product design, and procurement). The resulting CLD provides a clear and comprehensive view of how circular strategies, despite being designed for environmental improvement, can inadvertently trigger systemic rebound effects. This work contributes to advancing a more nuanced and system-oriented understanding of circular economy implementation in manufacturing. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: What, how, and where: the effects of multidimensional CSR communication strategies focusing on content, framing, and target
abstract: As corporate social responsibility (CSR) becomes important, so does consumer skepticism, making it difficult for firms to communicate CSR as intended. Integrating the Tri-dimensional CSR Model with Activating Events-Beliefs-Consequences (ABC) cognitive theory, this study exploratorily examined the differential effects of what firms communicate (content domain), how they frame and deliver CSR messages (strategic orientation and operational perspective), and where these messages are received (U.S. and China) on consumers’ CSR motivation perceptions and behavioral intentions. To examine these multi-faceted CSR communication effects, a 3x2x2 experiment was conducted with U.S. and Chinese samples. Three-way MANCOVA revealed that consumers’ CSR motivation perceptions differ by the what, how, and where aspects of CSR communications. PLS-SEM analysis further explored the patterns of these effects within each national context. These findings offer exploratory references for understanding the contextual factors that may influence CSR content, framing, and messaging, suggesting potential avenues for future CSR communication strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: The Role of Serious Games for Boundary-Object Negotiation in Innovation Projects
abstract: Innovation projects that span multiple disciplines and organizations depend on cross-functional collaboration and knowledge integration to succeed. Boundary objects—shared artifacts, models, or methods that enable coordination across different social and knowledge domains—are key means for realizing such collaboration and integration. However, boundary objects are rarely self-explanatory or automatically accepted. To become effective, they must undergo negotiation cycles through the active participation of the actors involved in the collaboration. This negotiation process is difficult to achieve, yet essential for developing shared understanding, fostering collective sensemaking, and enabling the effective use of boundary objects. To facilitate this process, this paper explores Serious Games (SGs)—structured, goal-oriented games designed for purposes beyond entertainment—as potential mechanisms for boundary-object negotiation. Guided by a Research through Design perspective—where knowledge emerges through the design and application of artifacts—an SG workshop was developed and implemented within a European rail innovation project, where a Business Case methodology acted as a boundary object for integrating domain-specific knowledge. Drawing on design-thinking principles, the SG enabled participants to understand, analyze, and negotiate the selected boundary object. The study demonstrates how the SG acted as a catalyst for cross-functional dialogue, facilitating shared understanding and collective sensemaking around the boundary object. The findings highlight how playful, participatory, and human-centered interventions can enhance boundary-object negotiation and strengthen methodological alignment, especially in complex innovation environments. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Vibe Coding: An experiment with test-driven development
abstract: Context: Conversational Large Language Models (CLLMs) can automatically generate code by collaborating with users through natural language. However, poor collaboration can lead to poor quality output. Objective: This exploratory study aims to investigate how humans and CLLMs can collaborate as peers through vibe coding, an approach that integrates principles from prompt engineering, agile design, and human-AI co-creation to enhance collaboration. Method: We designed four interaction models representing different collaboration patterns in the software development process: the solo model (human-only development), the collaborative model (human–CLLM collaboration), the fully automated model (development autonomously performed by a CLLM), and the agentic model (development autonomously performed by the MetaGPT X platform). Based on these models, we implemented corresponding Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflows using structured prompts and Python scripts. We then conducted a controlled pre-experimental study with TDD professionals to compare the solo and collaborative workflows. In addition, we performed repeated exploratory executions of fully automated and agentic workflows on the same development tasks to obtain complementary evidence. Results: Our findings suggest that the choice of interaction model should depend on the development objective. Agentic workflows are best suited for rapid development and functionally correct production code but may introduce additional implementation complexity. However, they may also introduce additional implementation decisions that are not explicitly required by the functional specifications, resulting in untested decision points. In contrast, collaborative workflows produce higher-quality, better-organized test suites. Conclusions: Our work explored how humans can collaborate with CLLMs in generating code in highly intensive and demanding development process. Our results also show that accurately reproducing development process workflows is yet an open problem, also in the new agentic technologies. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Livelihood and production stabilization following state land recovery in Vietnam: A qualitative legal study of Thanh Hoa Province
abstract: This study examined the legal framework and documented implementation of support for livelihood and production stabilization following State land recovery in Thanh Hoa Province, Vietnam. It aimed to clarify national eligibility rules, forms and levels of support, provincial implementation arrangements, and the main legal and administrative gaps. A qualitative legal research design was used, combining doctrinal legal analysis, documentary analysis, and descriptive analysis of secondary administrative data. The materials included the Constitution of 2013, the Land Law 2024, relevant national decrees and resolutions, provincial legal instruments, published studies, and three unpublished internal administrative reports covering 2023-2025. The findings show that Vietnamese law distinguishes support from compensation and resettlement and provides measures for livelihood stabilization, production and business stabilization, vocational training, occupational transition, job-search assistance, and resettlement-related needs. Thanh Hoa has specified several support levels and procedures through provincial instruments. However, the framework is more explicit about eligibility, calculation rules, payment levels, and administrative procedures than about longer-term livelihood outcomes. The administrative reports document a substantial site-clearance workload, but they do not provide sufficient information on payment timeliness, employment after training, income restoration, production continuity, or support-related complaints. The study therefore cannot determine the substantive effectiveness of the support measures. Clearer criteria are needed for special cases, together with reasoned decision-making, meaningful participation, livelihood and vocational assistance that extends beyond cash-based support and is linked to local labor demand, and reporting indicators that distinguish administrative progress from sustainable livelihood restoration. Because the study relied on legal and documentary materials from one province and did not collect primary data from affected persons, its findings should be interpreted cautiously. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Access Rights Management and Digital Identity for Digital Product Passports
abstract: The Digital Product Passport (DPP), established by the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR, EU 2024/1781), is a regulated multi-actor digital infrastructure in which economic operators, market surveillance authorities, recyclers, repairers, and consumers each require access to different subsets of product data under different conditions. Managing these access rights correctly constitutes a legal compliance requirement, a governance challenge, and a systems engineering problem simultaneously. This paper makes four integrated contributions. First, a cross-regulation taxonomy is developed that classifies DPP data along three axes: data sensitivity tier, lifecycle mutability, and entitlement source. Second, the three generations of EU digital identity regulation eIDAS (2014), eIDAS 2.0 (2024), and the European Business Wallet (EBW) systematically analysed against the seven core DPP identity requirements, showing that eIDAS meets none, eIDAS 2.0 meets some, and the EBW is near-complete. Third, an updated hybrid authentication architecture is proposed that integrates three pathways: OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect for operator-delegated business actors, the EU Digital Identity Wallet (eIDAS 2.0) for individual authority and base-role actors, and the EBW for organisational and automated flows. Fourth, the taxonomy and architecture are evaluated against the battery passport the first mandatory DPP under EU law confirming full coverage and alignment with EN 18239 and the JTC 24 standard family. The EBW’s credential ecosystem gap and the unspecified presentation protocol layer (OID4VP, W3C VC 2.0) are identified as the critical near-term implementation risks for systems that must be operational before the February 2027 battery passport mandate. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Beyond technological readiness: How financial benefit and top management support drive public electric vehicle charging station investment in Indonesia
abstract: This study investigates what drives potential business partners in Indonesia to invest in public electric vehicle charging stations (PEVCS). Using the TOE framework and TPB, this study examines key determinants of investment decisions in a B2B context. Survey data from 242 organizational respondents were analyzed using PLS-SEM. Results indicate that Perceived Financial Benefit (PFB) is the strongest driver of investment intention, consistent with the economic logic that business decision-makers prioritize profitability and anticipated returns over other considerations. Top Management Support (TMS) also emerges as influential, directly affecting investment intention and reinforcing financial confidence among organizational stakeholders. A notable characteristic of the sample dominated by national private firms with highly centralized structures appears to meaningfully shape how decisions are made within organizations. One of the more striking outcomes of this study is that Government Support (GSP) showed no direct bearing on investment intention. Government incentives only drive investment when perceived as tangible financial gains via cost reduction or revenue growth confirming that policy instruments must translate into firm-level economic value to influence decisions. Perceived complexity, meanwhile, did not register as a meaningful obstacle within this sample, suggesting that surveyed organizations possess formalized capabilities to manage technical and integration challenges. On the other hand, perceived compatibility proved consistently relevant, particularly when the technology slots naturally into pre-existing systems such as parking facilities or customer loyalty programs, thereby amplifying perceived financial returns. From a practical standpoint, these findings carry important implications for policymakers, specifically the need to sharpen messaging on return on investment when engaging top management and to design incentive structures that speak directly to financial attractiveness. While contributing to the sustainable energy infrastructure literature, the cross-sectional design limits causal inference; future studies should examine how ownership type and competitive dynamics moderate investment decisions. title: A Multi-Layered and Conceptual Framework for the Digital Product Service System Passport
abstract: The transition toward Product-Service Systems (PSS) requires continuous and seamless data exchange across the value chain. However, fragmented data silos and stakeholder reluctance often hinder this process. While the emerging Digital Product Passport (DPP) offers a structured approach to data sharing, current literature predominantly views it as a static regulatory compliance tool, lacking a cohesive framework to support dynamic PSS provision. To address this gap, this study proposes a comprehensive and multi-layered framework for the Digital Product Service System Passport (DPSSP). Grounded in Design Research Methodology (DRM), the framework was developed by synthesizing current academic literature and EU-funded projects and subsequently validated through cross-sectoral expert focus groups spanning the machinery, manufacturing, and textile industries. The proposed framework shifts the passport’s paradigm from compliance to a dynamic PSS enabler. Specifically, this paper details the Conceptual Layer of the DPSSP, mapping the interactions among lifecycle phases, a criticality-driven hierarchical data structure (product vs. component levels), multi-level decision-making processes, acquisition and analysis technologies and multi-actor ecosystem. The findings demonstrate that the DPSSP can act as a strategic facilitator for servitization, providing practitioners with a modular blueprint to improve PSS business models. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Bridging Metadata Gaps in Service APIs via Generative AI-Based Inference
abstract: API flexibility is a key enabler of Service-based Architectures, yet achieving it comes with pitfalls. Metadata is a well-established mechanism for increasing system reusability due to the flexibility it provides. Still, service APIs require their clients to adhere to the metadata in the communication, which comes as a challenge. This work proposes an architecture model consisting of a communication interceptor that leverages Generative AI to infer missing metadata. It prompts a Large Language Model (LLM) with the payload as the inference object and the service capabilities’ descriptions as context, acting as a dynamic adapter. This model also addresses the arguably long response times of LLMs using structural hashing caches. Preliminary empirical validation shows the artifact correctly deduces business intent with zero latency overhead on subsequent requests. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Battery Swapping Business Models for Heavy-Duty Machines in Road Construction and Quarry Operations
abstract: Battery swapping has been discussed as a potential approach to support the electrification of heavy-duty machines in road construction and quarry operations. These applications require high energy use, continuous operation, and reliable uptime, which can make conventional charging challenging to implement. At the same time, battery swapping is not widely adopted in these sectors, and there is limited understanding of suitable business models across different operational scenarios. The purpose of this paper is to examine battery swapping business models for heavy-duty machines in road construction and quarry operations under different operational conditions. The study considers five operational scenarios, ranging from single-machine use to multi-machine and high-intensity operations, including synchronized fleets, off-grid construction sites, and large quarry environments. The analysis focuses on four main criteria: machine utilization, project duration, energy infrastructure, and number of subcontractors. These criteria influence the design of battery swapping systems and the corresponding business models. Based on this analysis, the paper proposes a continuum framework of business models, ranging from simple battery rental solutions to more integrated energy-as-a-service approaches. The results show how different operational conditions may require different configurations, from flexible and low-investment solutions to more advanced and service-based models. The findings provide a structured way to explore how battery swapping could be implemented in different construction and quarry settings. The paper contributes to the literature on battery-based business model innovation and servitization, with a specific focus on heavy-duty machine industry. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: From perception to feasibility: Explaining AI adoption in SMEs through the TOE framework
abstract: This study aims to examine the determinants of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Central Java, Indonesia, by applying the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework with a focus on organizational readiness, financial capability, and perceived usefulness. Despite the growing availability of affordable AI-based applications, AI adoption among SMEs remains relatively limited, particularly in developing regions where resource constraints and uneven levels of digital readiness continue to hinder digital transformation. This study employs a quantitative approach using survey data collected from 117 SME owners and managers in Central Java. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to test the proposed relationships among the constructs. The findings reveal that financial capability, organizational readiness, and perceived usefulness all exert positive and significant effects on AI adoption. Among these determinants, perceived usefulness demonstrates the strongest influence, followed by organizational readiness and financial capability. These results indicate that both technological perceptions and organizational capabilities are important drivers of AI adoption decisions among SMEs, with perceived usefulness emerging as the most influential determinant. The study contributes to the literature by extending the application of the TOE framework to the context of AI adoption among SMEs in a developing economy and by providing empirical evidence from SMEs in Central Java, a regional context that remains underexplored in prior AI adoption research. The findings also offer practical implications for policymakers and SME owners in designing strategies that simultaneously strengthen organizational capabilities and enhance awareness of the benefits of AI technologies to accelerate digital transformation among SMEs. title: Decision-Making Within a Leasing Business Model: Enabling Refurbishment of Products at the End-of-Lease Under Stochastics Condition
abstract: Leasing is one approach towards a circular business strategy to enable the transition to CE. At the end of a lease, products are either purchased by the customer or returned to an OEM to be refurbished and resold to a new customer. Leasing contracts outline the rights, conditions, and responsibilities of both the customers and the OEM, including return or purchase conditions and penalties. However, defining these terms poses a challenge to OEMs especially under stochastic conditions. These challenges arise because the customers’ decisions influence the decision of an OEM and vice versa. Furthermore, different decision paths lead the OEM to adopt different refurbishment strategies. To enhance circularity, the life cycle of returned products can be extended through R-strategies such as refurbishment. This study develops a stochastic Stackelberg game-theoretic model in which an OEM acts as the leader and customers as followers. The game evaluates the interplay between initial pricing, leasing revenue, customer segmentation, and residual value. The findings demonstrate that customers’ decisions to return products are driven by the OEM’s upfront pricing decisions. Additionally, the study identifies a parabolic relationship between leasing revenue and NPV. Finally, results reveal that the optimal refurbishment strategy is dynamic: in-house operations are economically justified for high-value products that can amortize fixed costs. These insights provide actionable guidelines to balance secondary market supply, ensuring the long-term profitability of leasing and refurbishment in support of circularity. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Multi-task end-to-end portfolio optimization with self-supervised graph attention network
abstract: End-to-end portfolio methods have attracted considerable attention owing to their capacity to simultaneously optimize the prediction and decision-making processes. However, existing methods mostly rely on single-task learning, which is insufficient to accommodate multi-dimensional investment objectives. In addition, the capture of correlations among stocks and sectors typically relies on static prior knowledge, failing to adequately incorporate their dynamic evolution. Therefore, this paper proposes a portfolio optimization model based on self-supervised graph attention network within a multi-task end-to-end framework. By integrating dynamic correlation capturing, multi-task prediction, and portfolio optimization, this model enables the dynamic and adaptive adjustment of return and risk weighting parameters, thereby automatically optimizing investment allocation in response to varying market conditions. Empirical results on the S&P 500 stocks and the robustness test on the CSI 300 stocks demonstrate that the proposed model achieves improved portfolio performance relative to existing representative models across key evaluation metrics, including cumulative return, Sharpe ratio, and maximum drawdown. These results are essential for enhancing decision-making efficiency and facilitating the development of adaptive quantitative investment strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Designing Sustainable BMs for Testbeds in Industry 4.0: An Empirical 5G Testbed Study
abstract: Testbeds play a critical role in supporting the experimentation, validation, and diffusion of emerging technologies within Industry 4.0. Despite their growing importance, existing research remains predominantly technical and offers limited insight into how sustainable testbed business models can be designed. This study addresses this gap by analysing how testbed characteristics, service offerings, value creation and capture mechanisms can be integrated into a coherent BM, with a particular focus on 5G-enabled environments. Supported by a mixed interpretivist–pragmatic philosophy, the study adopts a qualitative exploratory approach, combining a systematic literature review with semi-structured interviews involving 16 stakeholders from Portuguese and international testbed initiatives. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to identify key patterns, supported by triangulation with literature and secondary sources. Findings show that sustainable testbed BMs rely on three interconnected dimensions: (1) the role of testbeds as controlled experimentation environments that reduce uncertainty and enable technology validation; (2) an extended service portfolio including consulting, training, networking, and matchmaking; and (3) hybrid BM configurations based on strong partnerships, diversified revenue streams, and flexible pricing mechanisms. Trust, transparency, and long-term collaboration emerge as critical enablers across these dimensions. The study proposes a BM framework that integrates these elements, offering theoretical insights and practical guidance for the design and positioning of testbeds in Industry 4.0 contexts. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Was I scammed? Understanding consumer scam reporting behavior through cognitive appraisal
abstract: Underreporting has been hampering regulatory efforts due to consumers’ hesitance to report ambiguous unsatisfactory transactions, particularly in online marketplaces or consumer services where deceptive business practices are uncertain or difficult to prove. This study examines how consumers appraise harm, effort, and resolution uncertainty when deciding whether to respond to potential scams. Drawing on Cognitive Appraisal Theory and Consumer Complaint Behavior, we develop and test a dual-pathway model that explains when victims pursue private action (e.g., contacting the seller) or public action (e.g., filing a complaint). Using nationally representative data from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission's 2017 fraud survey, we show that financial loss, perceived effort, outcome uncertainty, and their interactions jointly shape complaint behavior. We find that private action is driven by restitution motives and is amplified in high-loss or online scenarios, where it is perceived as a low-cost first step. Public action, by contrast, is less influenced by financial stakes and more by confidence in evidence, reflecting a justice-seeking mindset. This research contributes to the theoretical understanding of consumer behavior after perceived scam experiences by adopting long-standing marketing and consumer behavior theories and offers practical managerial insights by shifting the focus from victim profiling to behavioral process modeling. Our findings highlight the need for system-level interventions such as standardized dispute mechanisms, centralized complaint portals, and structured evidence logs to reduce harm and improve reporting confidence in scam-prone “gray areas.” © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: What do cross-lingual clone detectors really learn? A protocol and semantic counterfactual study
abstract: Cross-lingual code clone detection aims to identify functionally equivalent code fragments written in different programming languages. Existing detectors often achieve high F1 scores on standard benchmarks, but these scores may be inflated by code or problem overlap and shallow lexical or structural cues. It is therefore unclear whether the detectors compare the semantics of two code fragments or exploit regularities in benchmark construction. To investigate this issue, we conduct a behavioral audit of six representative clone detectors on Java-to-X pairs from Project CodeNet. The audit combines protocols with increasingly strong isolation controls, shortcut controls, partner shuffling, and meaning-preserving and behavior-changing edits. Our results show that measured performance depends strongly on the evaluation protocol. GraphCodeBERT and UniXcoder fall from F1 scores of 0.9848 and 0.9916 under pair-random evaluation to 0.6588 and 0.6970 under problem-disjoint evaluation. Shallow Control achieves an F1 of 0.6889, showing that even problem-disjoint splits retain exploitable non-semantic cues. Partner shuffling further reveals that detectors differ in their reliance on the original cross-lingual pairing. Semantic counterfactuals show that GraphCodeBERT is stable under meaning-preserving edits but insensitive to behavioral changes, while DeepSeek-v4-flash exhibits the reverse pattern. No evaluated detector achieved both high preservation stability and high breaking rejection on this counterfactual set. Thus, neither high F1 nor clean splitting alone demonstrates cross-lingual semantic understanding. Evaluations should also test shortcut reliance, use of both code snippets, and responses to semantics-preserving and semantics-breaking edits. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: The impact of pilot inland free trade zones on household income: Evidence from China
abstract: Using data from the China Household Finance Survey (CHFS), we employ a staggered difference-in-differences design to examine the effect of the establishment of inland pilot Free Trade Zones (FTZs) on household income. We find that inland FTZs significantly increase household income through increases in wage income, business income, and property income. The income gains are larger for households engaged in leading industries and their supporting sectors, as well as for those with higher human capital and stronger risk tolerance. In addition, inland FTZs reduce both within-city income inequality and the development gap between inland regions and the economic frontier. These findings provide micro-level evidence on the household welfare effects of institutional opening and offer policy implications for promoting high-standard institutional opening-up and more balanced regional development. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
