title: Molecular background of elicitor-induced crop protection: A translational agronomic review
abstract: Crop production is increasingly challenged by interacting biotic and abiotic stresses, highlighting the need for sustainable alternatives to conventional crop protection. Plant defense elicitors have emerged as promising tools for enhancing crop resilience by activating inducible resistance and immune priming. This review provides a critical translational overview of the molecular mechanisms underlying systemic acquired resistance (SAR), induced systemic resistance (ISR), and priming, while evaluating their practical relevance for agriculture. Beyond summarizing current knowledge, we assess the variability, reproducibility, and field performance of major elicitor classes, emphasizing the influence of crop genotype, environmental conditions, microbiome composition, formulation, and management practices on their effectiveness. Commercial and near-commercial elicitors are critically compared according to their biological mechanisms, agronomic validation, and practical limitations. To facilitate objective evaluation of elicitor technologies, we propose an evidence-based translational framework incorporating standardized evidence descriptors, the Overall Evidence Index, the Normalized Translation Index (NTI), the Translation Gap Index (TGI), and a practical decision framework for elicitor deployment. Rather than focusing solely on molecular mechanisms, this review emphasizes the translation of plant immunity research into reliable crop protection strategies. Future progress will depend on standardized field validation, improved formulations, microbiome-informed approaches, and integration with precision agriculture and integrated pest management to maximize the agronomic potential of elicitor-based technologies. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Toward sustainable oceans: Redirecting fisheries subsidies through cleaner production in Chile
abstract: Fisheries subsidies are often linked to overcapacity, overfishing, and environmental harm. As a result, global efforts have increasingly focused on eliminating harmful subsidies, while paying less attention to how public support can be designed to promote positive environmental outcomes. This study analyzes an alternative paradigm from Chile’s industrial shrimp (Heterocarpus reedi) and prawn (Cervimunida johni and Pleuroncodes monodon) fisheries, where a government-supported Clean Production Agreement (CPA) incentivized the adoption of cleaner production methods. Using a mixed-methods approach that combines qualitative documentary analysis with quantitative evaluation of environmental and economic indicators, we assessed the design, implementation, and outcomes of the CPA. Our findings reveal that the scheme enhanced environmental performance by reducing fuel consumption, bycatch, freshwater use, waste, and air emissions, while simultaneously delivering tangible economic benefits for participating companies. The initiative’s success was driven by four key design features: conditional funding tied to environmental goals, mandatory private co-financing, independent auditing and certification, and collaborative governance involving both public and private sectors. Importantly, subsidies did not cover fuel, fleet expansion, or other activities that could increase fishing capacity, thereby mitigating the risks of overcapacity and greenwashing. The Chilean case demonstrates that well-designed environmental subsidies can effectively support sustainability transitions in fisheries and offers valuable policy lessons for differentiating beneficial subsidies from those that threaten marine sustainability. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Competitive anion precipitation governs corrosion product film evolution on corrosion-resistant magnesium alloys in physiological solutions
abstract: In solutions containing Cl− as the base electrolyte, adding either H2PO4−/HPO42− or HCO3− markedly lowers the corrosion rates of Mg-Al-Y alloy wires, suppresses severe localized corrosion and promotes more uniform degradation. When both anions are present, their competitive interactions alter early corrosion product evolution and lead to a less continuous and less protective corrosion product film. Thermodynamic calculations indicate that phase accessibility depends on local pH and ion activities, while quasi-in situ FTIR reveals distinct early interfacial evolution of P- and C-containing species. Subsequent product retention may additionally depend on dissolution tendency and interfacial bonding. First-principles calculations further show that, in the selected idealized models, the carbonate-containing interface exhibits a higher Cl− migration barrier, whereas the phosphate-containing interface exhibits stronger interfacial adhesion. title: MANET cybersecurity: A systematic review of OSI attacks, AI-based detection, and adaptive security gaps (2020–2025)
abstract: – Mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs) rely on the direct participation of network nodes, infrastructure-independent operation, and dynamically changing topologies, making their routing protocols particularly vulnerable to cyberattacks. Routing attacks, including black hole, gray hole, wormhole, Sybil, and routing table poisoning, remain significant threats because they can disrupt packet forwarding, reduce network reliability, and compromise service continuity. Recent research has investigated artificial intelligence, machine learning, trust management, blockchain, and edge/fog computing to improve MANET security. However, limitations concerning scalability, energy efficiency, realistic datasets, and validation under representative operating conditions continue to constrain the practical applicability of many proposed approaches. This paper presents a systematic literature review of 116 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2025, conducted according to the PRISMA methodology. The review examines routing attack models, protocol vulnerabilities, defense mechanisms, and emerging research trends, while also identifying unresolved research challenges. Unlike previous surveys that address these aspects separately, this study proposes an integrated methodological framework that combines an OSI-based attack taxonomy with a four-stage security lifecycle encompassing prevention, detection, mitigation, and adaptive response. The reviewed literature is predominantly focused on intrusion detection, while limited evidence was identified of integrated security architectures capable of supporting the complete security lifecycle across multiple network layers. These findings highlight persistent methodological gaps and provide a structured analytical basis for future research on adaptive, distributed, and resource-efficient security architectures for MANETs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: The potential for coordination between air and ocean transport in advancing Net Zero policies
abstract: This study explores ways to achieve a modal shift in cargo transport markets for high-value commodities, with particular emphasis on shippers' awareness of climate change. Specifically, it aims to (i) provide insights for carriers in designing efficient cargo transport networks aligned with Net Zero policies; (ii) examine the robustness of the results by discussing the feasibility of sea-and-air services for high-value commodities while accounting for heterogeneity in shippers’ behavior; and (iii) inform policymakers in their efforts to support and facilitate such modal shifts. We apply a bi-level model to a simple four-node network and examine several scenarios by explicitly incorporating heterogeneity among shippers. The main findings are as follows. First, as shippers’ awareness of climate change increases, the share of all-air services declines in each market; notably, this decline is much larger in long-haul markets than in short-haul markets. Second, when the level of awareness among time-sensitive shippers is relatively low, the resulting reduction in GHG emissions in both markets remains quite limited. Third, if time-sensitive shippers with a high level of awareness of climate change occupy the major part of the market, ocean transport can become a feasible option for carrying high-value commodities. Under this condition, short-haul markets may become more competitive, whereas long-haul markets may exhibit greater cooperation between air and ocean transport. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Intergenerational eco-craft, women's agency, and climate adaptation in Telaga Biru Coastal Village, Madura, Indonesia
abstract: This study examines how coastal women in Telaga Biru Village, Madura, Indonesia, use natural-dye batik as an everyday practice of livelihood adaptation, ecological knowledge transmission, and community sustainability. Rather than treating women only as vulnerable subjects of climate and coastal change, the article asks how women's craft labour enables them to negotiate socio-ecological uncertainty within unequal gender relations, unstable markets, and limited institutional support. Based on feminist ethnography, the study draws on participant observation, in-depth interviews with 15 women batik artisans, and supplementary interviews with the village head and a local batik business owner. The findings show that women's natural-dye batik work operates as intergenerational eco-craft: it sustains household livelihoods, preserves coastal motifs and natural-dye knowledge, supports small-scale waste management, enables limited digital marketing, and anchors community-based environmental care through women's informal and organisational networks. At the same time, the article cautions against romanticising women's resilience, as their adaptive labour remains under-recognised, poorly supported, and shaped by patriarchal household and community structures. By conceptualising natural-dye batik as intergenerational eco-craft, this study contributes to feminist climate scholarship by showing how women's craft labour connects ecological knowledge, livelihood adaptation, cultural continuity, and coastal sustainability in the Global South. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Turning rivals into partners? emission reduction technology licensing strategies under market encroachment and Cap-and-Trade regulation
abstract: This study examines the optimal licensing strategy for an emission reduction technology (ERT) innovator under Cap-and-Trade (C&T) regulation and the threat of market encroachment by a new entrant. We develop a game-theoretic model involving an innovator, an ordinary incumbent, and a potential entrant, and extend the framework to analyze entrant cost heterogeneity, Two-Part Tariff (TPT) contracts, and endogenous green marketing. Our analysis yields three main insights: (i) the threat of encroachment fundamentally reshapes the strategic landscape by catalyzing cooperation between incumbents through relaxed conditions for fixed-fee licensing, and can paradoxically benefit the innovator when ERL is high; (ii) the optimal contract exhibits a structural reversal contingent on emission reduction efficiency, where royalty-based contracts soften competition for incremental innovations, whereas fixed-fee contracts maximize surplus extraction for high-efficiency technologies—a transition accelerated by endogenous green marketing; and (iii) the innovator exhibits a robust preference for licensing to the incumbent rather than the entrant, which remains structurally robust across all model extensions. Furthermore, under entrant cost heterogeneity, licensing to the incumbent establishes an effective entry barrier to lock out the entrant, whereas royalty-licensing to the entrant serves as a flexible co-optation tool when entry is inevitable. These findings offer strategic guidance for firms managing coopetition and entry threats in carbon-constrained markets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: A context-aware dynamic ensemble interval-valued crude oil price forecasting system
abstract: Crude oil price forecasting is crucial for economic stability and strategic planning; however, traditional point-value and static models fail to capture the market’s volatility and complexity. Existing approaches often rely on simple data processing, limited frequency models, and static ensembles; moreover, these methods typically lack interpretability. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an interval-valued ensemble forecasting system that effectively leverages multi-source mixed-frequency interval-valued information. The proposed system introduces three key innovations: a multi-stage feature engineering process that enriches information from diverse sources and overcomes the limitations of individual feature-processing algorithms; a multi-source mixed-frequency model that enables the joint processing of multiple high-frequency data streams; and a context-aware dynamic ensemble module powered by a dual-attention mechanism, which adaptively adjusts base model contributions according to prevailing market conditions while enhancing the interpretability of the developed system. Experimental evaluations show that the proposed system outperforms several advanced ensemble and state-of-the-art models, achieving Interval Root Mean Squared Errors (IRMSE) of 4.1763 and 4.5703 on West Texas Intermediate (WTI) and Brent crude oil datasets, respectively. Compared with the state of the art models, it delivers improvements ranging from 23.6% to 81.2% on the WTI dataset and from 14.2% to 76.8% on the Brent dataset. Interpretability analysis reveals the dynamic ensemble adapts its strategy intelligently, favoring different models during high volatility and strong market trends. This study thus offers a robust, transparent forecasting system for more informed and reliable decision-making. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Asymptotic analysis of tail moment in a dependent risk model
abstract: In this paper, we discuss a risk model with multiple business lines, where the log-discount process is a combination of a general adapted process with continuous paths and a compound stochastic jump process. We propose a dependence structure under the framework of multivariate regular variation, which not only captures the dependence among the insurance losses but also the one between the insurance losses and the financial jump sizes. We study a novel tail moment risk measure defined as the conditional moment of the present value of an individual business line's aggregate losses, given that the present value of aggregate losses of all business lines exceeds its Value-at-Risk. With the help of Extreme Value Theory, we derive asymptotic expansion of the tail moment. We illustrate the main results with some numerical studies which reveal that while the tail moment is notably impacted by the dependence structure, the heavy-tailedness plays a comparatively more significant role. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: From cox to DeepHit: A comprehensive analysis of aircraft longevity using time-varying and machine learning models
abstract: Estimating the economic useful life (EUL) of commercial aircraft is governed by extreme right-censoring: with over 70% of 35,212 aircraft still in service, retired-only analysis underestimates longevity through exclusion bias, while full-fleet analysis must work from relatively few observed retirements. We argue that this censoring, rather than the choice of model, sets the limit of what can be estimated, and we address it with a staged strategy comprising nonparametric Kaplan-Meier estimation, Cox models with time-varying coefficients, and a DeepHit neural survival network, each introduced to overcome a specific limitation of the previous stage. In individual aircraft-model × usage cells, estimated median EULs range from roughly 25–30 years for passenger jets to 29–42 years for their cargo counterparts, and cargo aircraft outlive passenger aircraft within every estimable model pair (87.7% vs. 33.2% 30-year survival across the pooled fleet). Leasing is associated with later retirement (24.2% lower estimated hazards for passenger aircraft and 42.6% lower estimated hazards for cargo aircraft), and, in pooled passenger-aircraft models, the estimated Airbus–Boeing contrast reverses over the lifecycle, with Airbus aircraft facing higher early but lower late retirement risk; this contrast may partly reflect differences in the manufacturers’ model composition. The censoring constraint becomes especially apparent at the finest resolution: many recently introduced types and modern freighter cells have too few retirements for reliable model-level estimation, motivating a pooled model that shares information across aircraft types. DeepHit, using a learned type embedding and lagged oil prices as leading predictors, attains the strongest predictive accuracy (C-index 0.89 vs. 0.64–0.77 for the Cox-family models), an indicative gain rather than a strict like-for-like ranking because the models are scored on different samples and representations. Reliable EUL estimation thus depends less on any single method than on matching the method to what extreme censoring leaves observable. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Wind farm resilience to tornado strikes: A coupled probabilistic damage and system dynamics framework
abstract: This study develops a coupled probabilistic damage and system dynamics framework for quantifying wind farm resilience to tornado strikes. The loss of resilience, defined as the time-integrated performance deficit, serves as the primary metric, complemented by four shape descriptors (robustness, redundancy, resourcefulness, rapidity) characterizing system performance under disturbance, with and without adaptation measures. Monte Carlo simulations on template wind farms yield mean losses of 62 ± 15 and 116 ± 18 days for EF1 and EF2 tornadoes. The EF1 rapidity distribution is bimodal, reflecting whether large components must be procured, with implications for spare parts inventory decisions. The framework is extended to model suboptimal turbine performance from undetected damage, coupling a stochastic capacity factor with a detection-time model, and to evaluate repowering of collapsed turbines with higher-capacity units. Comprehensive inspections reduce mean recovery time by one week and halve its variability relative to expedited inspections; repowering at a 1.3 capacity ratio reduces L by 7%. A regional-scale application to the Roscoe Wind Farm uses real turbine coordinates and Texas tornado climatology, yielding return periods near 45 and 57 years for EF1 and EF2 strikes and a 100-year resilience loss of 524 turbine ⋅ days. The resulting quantitative resilience value provides an additional decision-making criterion for inspection prioritization, spare parts logistics, and long-term risk management. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Assessing Perceived Construction Risk Allocation and Agreement under Design-Bid-Build Contracts: Evidence from a Developing Country
abstract: This paper examines perceived construction risk allocation under design-bid-build contracts and evaluates the degree of agreement between clients and contractors regarding which party should bear specific risks in the Indonesian construction context. Data were collected through a questionnaire survey of 53 respondents, who evaluated the allocation of 73 construction risks. Descriptive analysis based on median values was used to identify general patterns of risk allocation, while inferential analysis examined differences in perception and associations between allocation and agreement. Agreement was assessed at both the aggregate and individual risk item levels. The results indicate that contractors are perceived as bearing the majority of construction risks, and no statistically significant differences are observed between client and contractor respondents in risk allocation. Overall, allocation patterns are broadly consistent with expectations. However, several deviations are observed in which risks are partially shifted to other parties, even though they are largely within a single party's control. At the aggregate level, agreement is found to be unacceptable, with nearly half of the risks exhibiting a lack of or weak agreement, particularly for client-related and shared risks. Contractor respondents display higher levels of agreement, and risks allocated more heavily to contractors are associated with stronger agreement. These findings highlight the potential for conflict arising from disagreement in risk allocation and offer theoretical and practical implications. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Alternative Dispute Resolution in Construction Projects in the Middle East: A Systematic and Bibliometric Review
abstract: The construction industry in the Middle East is undergoing unprecedented growth driven by megaprojects, strategic national visions, and large-scale infrastructure development. This expansion has intensified the complexity of contractual relationships, leading to frequent disputes that challenge project performance, cost control, and timely delivery. While litigation has traditionally dominated dispute resolution, alternative dispute resolution (ADR) methods such as arbitration, mediation, negotiation, and dispute review boards (DRBs) have gained prominence as more efficient and relationship-preserving mechanisms. This study provides an integrated systematic and bibliometric review of ADR in Middle Eastern construction projects, synthesizing findings from 77 peer-reviewed studies retrieved from Scopus and screened through a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-based process. Employing PRISMA guidelines and VOSviewer mapping, the research analyzes publication trends, thematic clusters, authorship networks, and country-specific practices. The results reveal the dominance of arbitration and litigation, the underutilization of mediation and DRBs, and significant legal variations across jurisdictions. The study highlights cultural factors such as hierarchy, honor, and relational norms as critical mediators of ADR effectiveness. Emerging innovations [including digital platforms, building information modeling (BIM), and expert systems] illustrate a shift toward technology-enabled dispute management. By bridging bibliometric evidence with thematic synthesis, this review contributes a comprehensive overview of ADR practices in the region, identifies gaps in enforcement and institutionalization, and proposes a holistic improvement agenda that balances legal reform, dispute avoidance, and sustainability. Findings provide actionable insights for policymakers, industry professionals, and international investors seeking to strengthen dispute resolution frameworks and enhance project outcomes across the Middle East. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Exploring the platformization dilemma: How manufacturers leverage digital platforms for service business model innovation
abstract: Recent research has highlighted the growing significance of digital platforms in manufacturing, particularly in driving service business model innovation (BMI). However, research gaps persist in understanding how a manufacturer's platform business configuration as well as its platform experience influence its service BMI capability. This paper addresses these gaps by using the digital platform capability approach as a theoretical framework and introducing the concept of digital platform experience. To conduct our study, we first derive hypotheses from literature and test them in a cross-sectional, three-stage empirical analysis using descriptive, bivariate and multivariate regression analysis. For this purpose, we use the German Manufacturing Survey, a representative, large-scale firm-level database, which encompasses 1334 firms from the German manufacturing sector. Our findings reveal that digital platforms play a central yet ambivalent role – depending on experience and configuration – in manufacturers' service BMI. Overall, moving into the platform business generally triggers service BMI. However, these effects are mostly confined to product-related BMI, while customer-oriented models are only enabled through more complex platform configurations. Notably, these positive innovation effects tend to be short-lived: in the long run, innovation dynamics slow down considerably, and manufacturers may face what we refer to as the “platformization dilemma.” © 2026 The Authors

title: Improving spectral reproducibility in SERS analysis of exosomes via surface charge-modulated and biofunctionalized gold nanoparticles
abstract: This study introduces an improved SERS platform for analyzing exosome heterogeneity. We compared three gold nanoparticle substrates: negatively charged citrate-Au NPs (cit-Au NPs), positively charged cysteamine-Au NPs (cyst-Au NPs), and anti-CD63-functionalized cyst-Au NPs. Conventional cit-/cyst-Au NPs yielded fluctuating SERS signals due to random exosome localization, limiting accurate heterogeneity assessment. In contrast, anti-CD63-functionalized cyst-Au NPs specifically anchored exosomes via CD63 targeting, producing highly reproducible spectra. Principal component analysis (PCA) confirmed significantly reduced spectral variance with the antibody-based approach, with 95% confidence ellipses showing substantially tighter clustering compared to charge-based substrates. Theoretical simulations and sensitivity tests further showed the cyst-Au NPs strategy achieved a detection limit of approximately 1.3 × 103 particles/μL, while cit-Au NPs and anti-CD63-functionalized cyst-Au NPs exhibited LODs of 7.9 × 103 and 8.1 × 104 particles/μL, respectively. Notably, the PCA plot for the biofunctionalized strategy revealed two distinguishable circles, potentially indicating the presence of exosome subpopulations or distinct CD63 epitope distributions. By integrating surface charge control with biofunctionalization, this work enables reproducible, sensitive SERS detection, offering a reliable platform for exosome heterogeneity analysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: SemanticSync-BI: A Framework for Multi-cloud Business Intelligence Metadata Harmonization
abstract: Organizations increasingly adopt multi-cloud solutions for Business Intelligence (BI), benefiting from enhanced scalability, flexibility, and cost efficiency. Yet this trend introduces complex metadata management challenges, especially when maintaining semantic consistency across heterogeneous platforms. Current approaches, including technical catalogs, ontological standards, and cloud-native governance tools, face important limitations. These solutions often emphasize structural aspects, lack flexibility, or require extensive manual configuration, which restricts their capacity to adapt to changing business contexts. We present SemanticSync-BI to address these constraints, a conceptual framework for semantic harmonization of BI metadata in multi-cloud environments. Our framework operates through three integrated layers. First, the Context Extractor derives business meaning from diverse metadata sources. Second, Dynamic Mapping builds adaptive semantic similarity graphs. Third, the Multi-Cloud Synchronizer maintains semantic alignment in real time. Through conceptual evaluation using representative scenarios such as migration, enterprise merger, and SaaS integration, SemanticSync-BI shows promise for reducing inconsistencies, accelerating harmonization, and enhancing inter-cloud BI coherence. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Noncovalent interaction-driven self-assembly endows interfacial β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrils with inhibitory activities against lipid-hydrolyzing enzymes
abstract: Pancreatic lipase (PL) and cholesterol esterase (CE) are dominant lipid-hydrolyzing enzymes involved in the digestion and absorption of lipids, making them attractive targets for obesity prevention. β-lactoglobulin (β-LG) can transform into amyloid fibrils with potential inhibitory activity against PL and CE because of its amphiphilic and self-assembling properties. In this study, Dielectric Barrier Discharge atmospheric cold plasma treatment was employed to regulate the fibrillation process of β-LG (P-β-LGF) at three stages of fibril growth, namely, the initial stage (t0), the end of the lag phase (t0.1), and the exponential phase (t0.9). P-β-LGF exhibited enhanced β-sheet content, increased surface hydrophobicity, enhanced colloidal stability, and superior emulsifying and foaming properties. Furthermore, the elongated fibrillar morphology of P-β-LGF with a high aspect ratio and large specific surface area facilitated multivalent binding to the surface of enzymes, which resembled a “grape-on-a-vine” arrangement with enhanced inhibition at the oil/water interface. P-β-LGF exhibited competitive inhibition towards PL and mixed-type inhibition towards CE, indicating structure-specific enzyme inhibition mechanisms that collectively reduced lipid hydrolysis by interfacial behavior. Results demonstrated that P-β-LGF delayed in vitro lipid digestion by modulating enzyme activity effectively, indicating its potential as a functional ingredient for obesity management and lipid-lowering food applications. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Classification of motor imagery EEG signals using CNN–Transformer hybrid models
abstract: Motor imagery-based brain–computer interfaces aim to translate electroencephalographic activity into control commands without requiring overt movement. However, strong inter-subject variability, exacerbated by the limited spatial resolution of compact electrode montages, makes subject-independent decoding particularly challenging. This work presents a compact hybrid convolutional neural network–Transformer architecture designed for stable binary left/right motor imagery decoding using a low-density eight-channel sensorimotor montage. The model integrates convolutional feature extraction with a parameter-efficient temporal self-attention mechanism to capture both localized spatiotemporal patterns and long-range temporal dependencies in the electroencephalographic signal. Under strict subject-wise five-fold cross-validation on the PhysioNet EEG Motor Movement/Imagery dataset, the proposed convolutional neural network–Transformer achieved a mean macro F1-score of 0.816. Moreover, the statistical analysis revealed no significant performance difference (p>0.05) relative to larger architectural variants, thus justifying the selection of the proposed compact model for its computational efficiency and scalability. With only 0.232 million parameters and approximately 0.034 giga-floating-point operations per forward pass, the proposed convolutional neural network–Transformer constitutes a compact and resource-efficient backbone that supports low-latency subject-independent motor imagery decoding under low-density EEG. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Pet-friendliness in hospitality and tourism: Definition, scope, and governance
abstract: Pet-friendliness is a widely used hospitality label, yet it remains poorly defined and inconsistently specified. This paper clarifies what pet-friendly tourism means and how its scope is delimited within hospitality and tourism. Drawing on a systematic literature review and evidence from a global mixed-method survey, it shows that pet-friendliness extends beyond unrestricted pet access or isolated amenities and operates as a governance-mediated form of conditional inclusion supported by clear rules, appropriate infrastructure, staff practices, welfare, hygiene, safety, and coexistence management. Respondents converge on a stable core meaning, with variation arising primarily around tolerance for partial or restrictive arrangements. The findings provide an operational definition that can guide more comparable hospitality research, policy development, and managerial decision-making. © 2026 The Authors

title: How does China's unilateral visa-free policy affect its international aviation market? empirical evidence on passenger volume, flight frequency, and airfare
abstract: China introduced a unilateral visa-free policy in late 2023 as part of its broader effort to restore international mobility and support post-pandemic economic reopening. The policy grants ordinary passport holders from selected countries visa-free entry to China for short stays, thereby reducing travel frictions and potentially stimulating inbound tourism and business travel. Against this background, this study examines how China's unilateral visa-free policy has shaped the recovery and structural evolution of its international aviation market. Using route-level data from January 2023 to March 2025, we apply a staggered difference-in-differences (DID) framework to identify policy-induced changes in passenger volume, flight frequency, and airfare. The empirical results show that the policy substantially increases international passenger volume and flight frequencies. Airfares rise in the short term following the policy change, but this increase fades over time. Heterogeneity analyses further uncover substantial variation across regional markets and routes departing from Chinese airports with different levels of slot constraints. Specifically, on European routes, capacity expansion is driven primarily by the deployment of larger aircraft, whereas on Asian routes it is achieved mainly through increased flight frequency. Moreover, estimated airfare effects are positive on routes serving more slot-constrained airports and negative on routes serving less constrained airports, consistent with differences in the flexibility of capacity adjustment. These findings offer nuanced insights into the joint responses of passenger traffic, airline capacity, and airfares to visa facilitation, providing actionable guidance for airline capacity optimization and strategic aviation policy design. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Deep Learning Driven Multimodal Digital Twin Framework for Risk Prediction and Decision Intelligence in Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Systems
abstract: The need to facilitate enterprise risk prediction and decision intelligence is essential, operational resilience, financial losses mitigation and proactive mitigation of the potential threats in Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems. In this paper, a Multimodal Foundation Model Driven Digital Twin approach of enterprise risk prediction and decision intelligence is presented, which incorporates the ERP data for enterprise operations. The proposed system integrates heterogeneous data on a Transformer-based foundation model, and is supported by a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, and enables the processing of heterogeneous features in a modal fashion and cross-modal representation learning. The joint embeddings are then fed into a simulated digital twin that runs the enterprise until it executes the operations in a virtual world to perform predictive analytics and risk assessment. Finally, a decision intelligence system converts the forecasted risks into the recommendations to be followed on and graphical knowledge via a business dashboard. The proposed framework is experimentally proven to reach performance that is significantly higher than six benchmark CNN, LSTM, BERT, Transformer-XL, BioBERT, and SciBert- on a range of different metrics. The model is accurate with 0.99, it is precise with 0.98, recall is 0.97 and F1-score is 0.985 and the context sensitivity score is 0.95 and indicates that the model has the ability to reason strongly across-modes and predictive ability is sensitive to context. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Tree-based versus neural surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithms for multi-objective optimization of DR-PSA biogas upgrading using MOEA/D, NSGA-III, and AGE-MOEA2
abstract: This study presents a systematic, surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization (MOO) framework for dual-reflux pressure swing adsorption (DR-PSA) biogas upgrading, designed to overcome the computational burden of high-fidelity cyclic simulations. Machine learning surrogates were trained on 125 first-principles simulations to predict key performance indicators, including CH4 purity, recovery, bed productivity, and cycle work. To ensure statistical robustness, three established MOO algorithms were evaluated across multiple runs under bi-objective (purity versus productivity) and tri-objective (incorporating energy minimization) scenarios. The study establishes two transferable design principles: (1) surrogate selection must prioritize functional smoothness alongside accuracy, as piecewise-constant surfaces inherently mislead evolutionary search; and (2) algorithm selection should align with Pareto front geometry, with reference-point methods excelling for mildly curved fronts and geometry-adaptive methods required for curved, tri-objective manifolds. Applying this framework, the optimal DR-PSA design achieves >90% CH4 purity and ~ 90% recovery, representing improvements of approximately 18% and 16%, respectively over the unoptimized base case while reducing cycle work by up to ~50%. First-principles validation confirms that these optimal conditions are physically robust, suggesting a potentially promising, energy-efficient pathway toward high-grade biogas upgrading. This study advances DR-PSA process intensification and provides methodological insights into surrogate selection and algorithm suitability for MOO of cyclic separation processes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Consumer Behavior Analytics Using Deep Learning for Personalized Marketing Strategies in Online Commerce
abstract: The study sets the hypothesis of a personalized marketing of online shopping sites based on a consumer behavior analytics framework of the deep learning. Engagement Features They browse behavior and transactional history of the user are anonymized, sessionized, normalized, and structured in a sequence feature, which makes the model suitable to privacy and efficient learning. The multifaceted behavioral patterns and time-dependent aspect are represented in extensive user interaction data in a hybrid structure of Transformer and LSTM networks and self-attention mechanism of the Transformer that enable the possibility to accurately determine the purchase possibility. It can be seen that through experimental analysis, the classification accuracy of 97.4% and ROC-AUC of about 0.97, with a high and stable precision when recalling levels are Precision-Recall analysis. The confusion matrix also demonstrates that there have been low misclassification error and equal performance. These results show that the framework is effective in integrating latent consumer intent and enabling the personalized recommendations and customized marketing strategies of business online. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Machine Learning Parameters Identification for a New Unit Power-Logistic Quadratic Lindley Model
abstract: This paper introduces a new two-parameter distribution for modelling unit interval data. It is named the Unit Power-Logistic Quadratic Lindley (UPLQL) model. It is constructed by applying a power-logistic transformation to a flexible baseline distribution known as the quadratic Lindley. The resulting density can take several shapes; decreasing, unimodal, right skewed, or left skewed making it suitable for a wide variety of proportional data. Closed-form expressions for the cumulative distribution function (CDF), probability density function (PDF), and hazard rate function are formulated, while the quantile function (QF) is derived in a semi-closed-form. Mathematical properties including moments, Lorenz and Bonferroni curves, order statistics, stress-strength reliability, and stochastic order are derived. Eight frequentist estimation methods are compared through an extensive Monte Carlo simulation (MCS), and a Bayesian analysis using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) is also carried out. An amortised tree-based estimator (ATE) that predicts the parameters directly from a set of features is developed. It can be turned into a fast Bayesian tool using a parametric bootstrap. The performance of the UPLQL model is evaluated on two data sets, the flood-level proportions and petroleum reservoir measurements. In both applications, the new distribution performs competitively with established unit distributions and offers a good combination of flexibility, interpretability, and computational efficiency. © Grace Scientific Publishing 2026.

title: Sensory and consumer research with children and adolescents: A review
abstract: Over the past decade, significant advances have been made in sensory and consumer methods tailored to children, with a growing focus on approaches that capture their perspectives more accurately. This review provides an updated overview of developments in sensory and consumer research with children and adolescents aged 4–17 years. Both classical methods (e.g., hedonic scales, paired comparison, ranking, A-Not-A tests) and innovative approaches (e.g., co-creation, projective mapping, CATA, emoji-based tools, implicit and physiological measures, temporal methods) are critically examined, highlighting their strengths, limitations, and age-appropriateness. Particular attention is given to contextual and cognitive factors that influence children's ability to engage with different methods. The review emphasizes the importance of selecting child-specific approaches to generate reliable insights, encourages the standardization of methods across studies, and identifies research gaps for future investigation. © 2026 The Authors

title: M2VGF: A memory-augmented multi-view gated fusion framework for multimodal sarcasm detection
abstract: With the rapid growth of social media content, multimodal sarcasm detection has become an important task for understanding complex cross-modal semantics. Multimodal sarcasm often involves subtle local contradictions, contextual semantics, and heterogeneous cues whose importance varies across samples. To this end, this paper proposes M2VGF, a Memory-Augmented Multi-View Gated Fusion framework. The proposed model highlights informative local contradictions through saliency-aware fine-grained alignment, enriches current representations with OCR-enhanced context and historical memory, and adaptively combines complementary semantic views through gated fusion. Experiments on the MMSD and MMSD2.0 benchmarks demonstrate that M2VGF achieves competitive and stable performance, with accuracies of 93.37% and 89.45%, and F1-scores of 93.11% and 89.36%, respectively, across five random seeds. Multi-run evaluations further demonstrate the robustness of the proposed model, while routing diagnostics show high retained-memory purity in the evaluated setting. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Assessing industrial land-use efficiency at parcel scale: Actual vs. expected economic outputs across diverse parcel types and spatial conditions
abstract: As urban development shifts toward the optimization of existing built-up areas, identifying inefficient industrial land is increasingly important for targeted land renewal and stock-oriented land governance. Although industrial land-use efficiency (ILUE) has been widely assessed at industrial-park and administrative scales, large-area parcel-scale evaluation remains constrained by limited fine-grained land use information and parcel-scale economic data. To address these limitations, this study develops a parcel-scale ILUE evaluation method by comparing actual economic output (AEO) with expected economic output (EEO), which refers to the reasonably expected output of a parcel given its functional type and spatial conditions. Firstly, using multisource spatiotemporal data, 13,510 industrial parcels in Beijing are classified into four functional types, i.e., technology office, commercial service, manufacturing, and warehouse & logistics, and characterized by built, socio-economic, and ecological conditions. Then, parcel-scale AEO is estimated by integrating gridded economic information with administrative industrial statistics, while EEO is estimated using cyclic random forest regression (CRF-R) to capture nonlinear spatial condition–output relationships. Our results reveal 3684 inefficient parcels, primarily concentrated in southern and eastern peri-urban districts. Compared with observed business revenue and documented renewal projects, the downscaled AEO better captures parcel-scale economic variation, while the inefficient parcels identified using CRF-R achieved a 76.7% project-level spatial correspondence rate. Based on feature importance analysis, the study gives type-specific governance recommendations, including improving transit accessibility for office and commercial land, supplementing residential and public service for manufacturing land, and increasing development intensity and road accessibility for logistics-oriented parcels, thereby providing a practical diagnostic tool for differentiated industrial land renewal. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Fracture mechanical properties and mechanism analysis of structural fiber recycled coarse aggregate concrete
abstract: To investigate the influence of structural fibers (STF) on the fracture mechanical properties of recycled concrete, three-point bending tests were conducted to study the effects of STF type, STF content, and recycled aggregates (RA) substitution rate on the fracture failure mode, load displacement curve, load CMOD (crack mouth opening displacement) curve, residual bending strength, fracture energy, and fracture toughness of concrete. Finally, a bilinear softening constitutive curve for structural fiber-reinforced recycled concrete (STFRRC) was established based on the double-K fracture model. The results indicate that STF can change the failure mode of concrete and significantly improve its fracture performance; The fracture performance (residual bending strength, fracture energy, and fracture toughness) of STFRRC is positively correlated with STF content and negatively correlated with RA substitution rate. Among the STF types, ESF (End-hooked steel fiber) has the greatest effect on the fracture performance of STFRRC, followed by CSF (Corrugated steel fiber) and, finally, SCSF (Shear corrugated steel fiber). Compared with the non-fiber specimens, STFRRC exhibited improved fracture performance and post-cracking toughness. The bilinear σ−w relationship provides a model-derived representation of the post-cracking tensile softening behavior of STFRRC based on the measured ft, Gf, and CTODc, rather than an independently validated constitutive response. Calibration against the experimental fracture-toughness results yielded λ=6, for which the calculated cohesive toughness showed reasonable agreement with the experimental results, with an RMSE of 0.134 MPa⋅m0.5and a mean relative error of 11.82%. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Constitutive metabolic signatures associated with partial resistance to fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) in tropical maize inbred lines
abstract: Fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) poses a major threat to maize production in sub-Saharan Africa, underscoring the importance of identifying durable sources and biochemical markers of host-plant resistance. This study investigated the constitutive metabolic basis of partial FAW resistance in tropical maize by integrating insect bioassays with complementary GC–MS and LC–Q-TOF–MS profiling. Whole-leaf tissues collected before infestation from three resistant (Mp716, CML71, and CKSBL10008) and three susceptible (CML370, CKSBL10025, and CML444) inbred lines were analyzed, and the same tissues were incorporated into artificial diets to evaluate larval growth and feeding preference. Diets derived from resistant genotypes consistently reduced larval relative growth rates and were less preferred by neonates than diets derived from susceptible lines, providing evidence that pre-existing leaf chemistry contributes to both antibiosis- and antixenosis-associated resistance. GC–MS detected approximately 800 analytical features and highlighted resistance-associated trends in amino-acid, nitrogen, and central-carbon metabolism. LC–Q-TOF–MS detected approximately 1,700 features, with 384 differing significantly between resistance classes after false-discovery-rate correction, revealing extensive remodeling of specialized metabolism. Resistant lines were characterized by higher relative abundances of several putative amino acids, purine-related metabolites, phytosterols, and putative defense-associated compounds, including a DIMBOA-hexoside-related feature. In contrast, susceptible lines generally contained higher levels of putative soluble sugars, central-carbon metabolites, and several flavonoid- and phenylpropanoid-related features. Pathway analysis identified 28 differentially abundant consolidated metabolites and significant enrichment of phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, indicating selective metabolic reconfiguration rather than generalized accumulation of secondary metabolites. Together, these findings demonstrate that partial FAW resistance is associated with a coordinated constitutive metabolic signature integrating nutritional composition and specialized defense chemistry. Although targeted and spatially resolved validation is required to establish the functions of individual metabolites, the identified signatures provide promising biochemical candidates for resistance screening and metabolomics-assisted breeding of FAW-resistant maize. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature B.V. 2026.

title: AI-Enhanced Data-Driven Approach to Model the Mechanical Behavior of Sustainable Geopolymer Concrete
abstract: The growing environmental burden of ordinary portland cement has accelerated the search for sustainable alternatives. Geopolymer concrete (GPC), synthesized from industrial byproducts such as fly ash and slag, is a promising candidate. However, its compressive strength is difficult to predict because numerous mix and curing variables interact in complex, nonlinear ways. This study develops and validates an interpretable machine learning framework for forecasting GPC compressive strength. A curated data set of 350 samples was used, containing eight independent variables, i.e., fly ash, ground granulated blast-furnace slag, NaOH molarity, coarse aggregate, recycled aggregate, curing temperature, curing time, and age of testing, and one dependent variable, i.e., compressive strength. Six models (linear regression, decision tree, gradient boosting, support vector regression, artificial neural networks, and random forest) were trained and optimized. Their outputs were integrated into a stacking ensemble, i.e., the super learner (SL) model, with random forest as the metalearner. Performance was evaluated using R2, root mean square error (RMSE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) under 10-fold cross-validation and a held-out test set. The SL achieved R2 = 0.994, RMSE = 0.90 MPa, and MAPE = 1.4 %, consistently outperforming all base learners and surpassing results reported in recent studies when benchmarked under comparable variable ranges. Model interpretability was ensured through Shapley Additive exPlanations and permutation sensitivity analyses, which identified curing time, NaOH concentration, test age, and curing temperature as dominant predictors. The novelty of this work lies in demonstrating that a stacking ensemble with transparent feature attribution can markedly improve accuracy and trustworthiness in predicting GPC strength, offering a rapid and nondestructive tool for sustainable mix design optimization. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Can digital-real integration effectively curb urban sprawl? Evidence from China using double/debiased machine learning
abstract: Urban sprawl (URS) has become a major challenge to China's sustainable development under the backdrop of rapid urbanization. Digital-real integration (DRI) provides a new pathway for urban spatial governance, yet its concrete impacts and mechanisms remain insufficiently tested. Based on panel data from 280 prefecture-level Chinese cities between 2013 and 2023, this study constructs a multidimensional DRI index and employs a partially linear double/debiased machine learning (DML) framework to estimate the effect of DRI on URS. Multiple robustness checks, including complementary instrumental-variable analyses, yield results consistent with the baseline finding. The findings show that a one-unit increase in DRI is associated with a 0.06-unit reduction in the URS index, and this conclusion holds under various robustness tests. The mechanism analysis provides evidence consistent with three potential transmission pathways: industrial structure upgrading, stronger aggregate city-level correspondence between employment opportunities and resident population, and reduced dependence on highway commuting. Further heterogeneity analysis reveals that the restraining effect of DRI is more pronounced in eastern regions, major national urban agglomerations, and cities at more advanced stages of urban development. This study not only provides empirical evidence on how digital technologies reshape urban spatial structures but also offers policy implications for implementing differentiated digital governance strategies and enhancing the effectiveness of spatial planning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Development of a Competency Model for Executives of the Carbon Credit Trading Industry to Mitigate the Impacts of Global Warming in the Digital Era
abstract: Global warming and climate change severely impact ecosystems and human safety, positioning the carbon credit market as a vital tool for emission reduction. This study aimed to identify necessary skills, develop a strategic plan, and construct a handbook for digital-age leaders in industrial carbon credit trading. Utilizing the Delphi method and a focus group discussion, data were gathered from 19 experts and stakeholders. Analysis combined qualitative thematic sorting with quantitative median and interquartile range (IQR) metrics. The findings revealed five core management skills (planning, organizing, commanding, coordinating, controlling), detailed into 25 sub-parts and 125 minor parts. This model integrates environmental knowledge with digital technology to enhance measurement, reporting, and verification efficiency. Experts verified the model's appropriateness, resulting in a two-part handbook outlining 12 execution pathways. Specialists confirmed the handbook is highly suitable for leadership development. © 2027, World Scientific and Engineering Academy and Society. .

title: Business strategy and director compensation in liberal versus coordinated markets
abstract: In this study, we examined the association between business strategy and director compensation and whether this relationship differed between liberal market economies (LMEs) and coordinated market economies (CMEs). Using 27,309 firm-year observations from 16 countries for the 2002–2021 period, we found that differentiation was associated with higher director compensation, whereas cost leadership was associated with lower compensation. These relationships varied across institutional environments. Differentiation was positively associated with director compensation in LMEs but not in CMEs. Cost leadership was negatively associated with compensation in LMEs, but it was weakly and positively associated with compensation in CMEs. Additional analysis indicated that firms in LMEs are more likely to pursue differentiation and less likely to pursue cost leadership than firms in CMEs. The findings demonstrated that compensation arrangements are institutionally contingent and have implications for remuneration committees designing compensation policies to align with firms’ strategic orientations and national institutional environments. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: Mechanisms and spatial effects of digital-financial co-agglomeration on urban digital entrepreneurial vitality
abstract: Based on the panel data of 236 Chinese cities from 2005 to 2022, this study examines the impact of digital-financial co-agglomeration on urban digital entrepreneurial vitality. We measure digital-financial co-agglomeration with a modified E-G index and measure urban digital entrepreneurial vitality with a labor-market approach based on firm registration data. The results show that co-agglomeration significantly increases urban digital entrepreneurial vitality. The findings remain robust after addressing endogeneity and conducting multiple robustness checks. Mechanism tests indicate that venture capital activity and technological innovation mediate the effect. Spatial econometric results further show significant spillovers, and the indirect effect exceeds the direct effect. Threshold estimates reveal a non-linear effect that becomes stronger after the threshold is crossed. © 2026 The Authors

title: Enhancing Business Efficiency Through Strategic AI Adoption in Operations
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has improved business productivity, efficiency, and decision-making across all industries. Strategic application of AI in supply chain management, manufacturing, customer service, human resource management, and financial operations is investigated in this research. Machine learning, natural language processing, and computer vision allow organizations to automate, improve predictive analysis, and optimize resource utilization. AI can lower operational costs, improve consumer experience, and provide businesses with a competitive edge in data-driven market dominance. Adoption of AI has drawbacks including data security, system integration, and accommodating employees. The discussion emphasizes the need for a structured plan of implementation of AI that is commercially oriented and has ethical and legal considerations. Increased accessible AI models and digital economy collaboration should be the center of future studies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Mechanochemical activation of recycled glass–biogenic CaO composites: Structural evolution, hydration behavior, and silicate-network modification
abstract: Mechanochemistry has emerged as a sustainable strategy for producing advanced materials from industrial and biogenic wastes. In this study, mechanochemically activated composites were synthesized using post-consumer recycled soda–lime glass as an amorphous support and biogenic calcium oxide (BCO) derived from waste eggshells as the active phase. Composites containing 5–95 wt% BCO were prepared by high-energy ball milling and characterized by X-ray fluorescence (XRF), X-ray diffraction (XRD) coupled with Rietveld refinement, Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The results revealed that mechanochemical activation significantly reduced the CaO crystallite size from 148.5 to 25.4 nm, while preserving the amorphous nature of the recycled glass matrix. The degree of crystallinity increased progressively with increasing BCO content, reaching 66.2% for the composite containing 95 wt% BCO; however, a substantial amorphous fraction persisted in all compositions, suggesting the formation of highly disordered crystal–amorphous interfacial regions. FTIR and Raman analyses indicated progressive modifications of the silicate network, evidenced by the formation of non-bridging oxygens and Ca–O–Si interfacial species. The Raman intensity ratio (I356/I1084) exhibited segmented behavior, revealing a critical composition of approximately 75 wt% BCO, corresponding to the transition from a glass-dominated to a CaO-dominated structural regime. These findings demonstrate that mechanochemical activation not only promotes efficient dispersion and fragmentation of CaO but also engineers crystal–amorphous interfaces in waste-derived composites, providing new insights into the structural evolution of CaO–silicate systems and highlighting their potential for the development of sustainable functional materials. © 2026

title: How Does Artificial Intelligence (AI) Adoption Affect Occupational Stress Among Workers? A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: The purpose of this study is to systematically review previous articles highlighting the influence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption on occupational stress among workers. A systematic review was conducted based on Scopus and Web of Science databases. Five articles belonging to the management and business fields were included. The results show that the first work addressing this topic was published in 2023. Since then, the literature reveals heterogeneous results, suggesting that the impact can be either positive or negative. Most existing studies have concentrated on two types of business namely the tourism and hospitality sectors. These findings underscore the necessity of conducting further research on this topic, particularly by examining different occupational categories such as managers and executives. Such investigations would enhance our understanding of the phenomenon and provide a foundation for future comparative studies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Cu redistribution layers on permanent glass-core substrates for advanced packaging: Direct-on-glass and polymer build-up architectures
abstract: Glass-core substrates are attracting increasing interest for advanced packaging because of their dimensional stability, high electrical resistivity, smooth surfaces, and compatibility with fine-pitch interconnect processing. This review compares Cu redistribution-layer (RDL) technologies implemented on permanent glass-core substrates through two principal architectures: direct-on-glass RDLs and polymer build-up RDLs. Direct-on-glass approaches reduce dielectric-stack complexity and can support low-loss lateral routing, but their scalability depends strongly on glass–Cu adhesion, seed-layer control, conductor dimensional fidelity, and stress transferred to brittle glass. Polymer build-up approaches enable multilayer routing and microvia-based redistribution while introducing additional constraints associated with dielectric properties, cure-induced dimensional change, moisture response, interfacial integrity, and multilayer registration. Reported studies demonstrate micrometer-scale wiring and vias, broadband signal transmission, multilayer integration, accelerated reliability testing, and large-area glass processing. However, the most aggressive dimensions, highest integration levels, and strongest electrical or reliability results have generally been demonstrated in different material stacks and test vehicles rather than concurrently within a single permanent glass-core platform. Accordingly, minimum feature size alone should not be interpreted as a manufacturing design rule. Future progress will require coordinated design of interfaces, dielectric materials, metallization, and routing architecture, together with statistically meaningful qualification of dimensional control, electrical performance, environmental reliability, and panel-scale manufacturability. © 2026

title: Stakeholder attention to advanced air mobility reveals worldwide disparities
abstract: Advanced air mobility (AAM) has garnered escalating attention from academia, government, business, and the general public. Previous studies tended to investigate these main stakeholders separately, failing to identify their various attentions, attitudes and focus areas. This research employs bibliometric and social media large language model (LLM) text mining methods to explore the perspectives of main stakeholders on AAM for a decade (2015-2024), with approximately 300,000 texts in total. Our findings show a consistent rise in text volume across all key stakeholders, with government stakeholders demonstrating the fastest growth rate. Globally, the text sentiment is predominantly either positive or neutral, with negative sentiment being the least prevalent. The topic analysis reveals stakeholders have heterogeneous priorities, with businesses and governments tending to emphasize AAM-related infrastructure, the general public focusing more on end-user experiences and air mobility infrastructure and integration, while academia concentrating on aerodynamics and safety concerns. This research seeks to inform actionable policy formulation and air-transport planning, thereby facilitating AAM integration into urban and regional transportation systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: From quality to value: linking product and system perspectives in the plastic packaging ecosystem
abstract: This study investigates value in the plastic packaging ecosystem. Previously, we identified the quality perceptions of technical actors, such as polymer producers, converters and recyclers. Using semi-structured interviews, we now extend this by focusing on value for broader ecosystem actors which influence and are influenced by technical actors, such as governments, investors, and academics. Two broad themes emerged from the data analysis which combined lead to the notion of value: quality and system performance. Quality is identified at the product level and consists of the nine previously identified categories: purity, uniformity, mechanical properties, physical properties, processability, functionality, regulations & safety, substitutability and circularity. System performance is defined at the system level and consists of four categories: sustainability, technology fit, multi-criteria performance, and market acceptance. While system performance categories are separate concepts, they do interconnect. This new understanding of value facilitates better alignment in the plastic packaging ecosystem and initiatives. © 2026 The Authors

title: Contextualized learning theory in practice: An assessment study of cultivating procedural vis-à-vis conceptual fluencies in operations management fundamentals through simulations
abstract: Contextualized learning theory promotes effective learning by placing new information in meaningful contexts; however, despite its desirability among educators, identifying practical ways to apply this theory in specific classroom teaching remains an ongoing challenge. To that end, undergraduate business students often find operations management topics challenging to contextualize because of the inherently complex integration of theoretical concepts and methodical procedures that characterize the subject. Accordingly, instructors strive to identify viable instructional tools to help students overcome this challenge and achieve parallel mastery of the intertwined quantitative and qualitative aspects of operations management fundamentals. This paper presents the results of a comparative experimental study examining the effectiveness of simulation-assisted instruction in promoting contextualized learning in an introductory operations management course. The empirical results based on a quasi-experimental design showed that computer simulations enable students to experience contextualized learning, thereby enhancing their performance and fluency in understanding and applying OM concepts and techniques. On that note, performance-based assessment of learning outcomes revealed that students' conceptual fluency, as a reflection of their contextual efficacy, improved the most when simulations were used. Moreover, students' procedural fluency, as evidenced by their technical efficacy, was simultaneously improved, albeit to a lesser extent, when simulations were employed. Perception-based assessment of learning outcomes showed similar improvement patterns; however, unlike the performance-based results, these improvements did not reach statistical significance. The findings provide valuable insights into the utility of such instructional tools through a methodical inquiry into the objective and subjective assessments of polydimensional learning outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A meta integral reinforcement learning-based cooperative guidance evasion scheme against noncooperative spacecraft
abstract: The increasing congestion of space orbits has led to a growing number of close-proximity encounters between operational satellites and noncooperative spacecraft. To achieve online autonomous evasion from noncooperative spacecraft, this paper proposes a Meta Integral Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MI-MARL)-based cooperative guidance scheme. Firstly, the multi-agent orbital encounter is formulated as a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process (Dec-POMDP), where the interaction among spacecraft is modeled as an orbital pursuit-evasion process under incomplete information. Then, a meta multi-actor-critic architecture incorporating a convolutional recurrent inference network is developed to infer high-dimensional spatiotemporal features directly from stacked angle-only observations of noncooperative spacecraft. The proposed meta-network architecture enhances situational awareness and enables online policy retraining within a Dec-POMDP. Furthermore, by theoretical analysis in the Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs framework, we formulate the rational decision-making and Nash equilibrium stability conditions of a perfect Bayes-Nash equilibrium, thereby guaranteeing the convergence and optimality of the MI-MARL. Finally, numerical simulations and computational efficiency evaluations are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness, robustness, superior performance, and real-time onboard feasibility of the proposed method in highly dynamic close-proximity encounter scenarios. © 2026 IAA. title: Petroleum fiscal regimes and contractor returns: empirical analysis of the North Sea and Gulf of Guinea
abstract: Petroleum fiscal regimes are institutions through which resource rents, investment risks, public revenues, and domestic economic opportunities are allocated among states, firms, and producing societies. Yet they are often assessed primarily through tax burdens and contractor returns. This study develops a mechanism-based framework that distinguishes direct production-cost effects, cash-flow redistribution, timing-related liquidity effects, and their wider governance and development implications. A structured comparative analysis of legal, contractual, administrative, and regulatory documents from the United Kingdom, Norway, Ghana, and Nigeria is combined with a normalised cash-flow illustration. The findings show that royalties primarily secure early public revenue while reducing pre-payout contractor cash flow; cost-recovery ceilings mainly defer reimbursement and place particular demands on audit capacity; and profit-based taxes track profitability more closely but depend on transparent bases, loss rules, and predictable administration. State participation and local-content requirements can strengthen domestic capability and value retention, although poorly calibrated obligations may increase financing, procurement, compliance, and delivery pressures. Regulatory complexity and fiscal instability further shape administrative discretion, credibility, and investment risk. The comparison demonstrates that petroleum fiscal design is not only an economic allocation problem but also a resource-governance challenge. Effective regimes therefore require progressivity, credible cost verification, accountable state participation, capacity-sensitive local-content policy, transparent administration, and rules that align public revenue mobilisation with commercially viable investment and domestic development objectives. © 2026 .

title: Aviation Workforce 4.0: Competences for a Sustainable and Digitalized Sector
abstract: The transition toward a sustainable and digital economy requires new workforce models that combine technical, digital, and transversal competences. This paper examines how aviation, as a strategic global industry, illustrates the broader challenges of Workforce 4.0. Drawing on data collected within the AVIONIC project, the study analyzes the effectiveness of training systems, the alignment of higher education with labor market demands, and the emerging need for green and digital skills. Findings reveal a strong demand for programming, managerial, and transversal competences, a continued preference for face-to-face and experiential training formats, and a limited emphasis on environmental sustainability skills. While the case of aviation highlights sector-specific dynamics, the implications extend to other industries undergoing similar twin transitions of digitalization and decarbonization. The paper argues that education systems and business organizations must adopt modular and work-integrated approaches to skill development in order to enhance competitiveness and resilience in a sustainable global economy. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Platform governance and value co-creation in online food delivery ecosystems: capacity allocation and commission strategies
abstract: Online food delivery (OFD) platforms represent a prominent class of service digital ecosystems in which platform governance mechanisms shape multi-sided value co-creation among platforms, restaurant partners, and consumers, the joint gain from coordinating rather than deciding independently. This study examines how OFD platforms strategically govern restaurant networks through incentive-based contracts, specifically, minimum business guarantees (MBGs), and how these governance choices interact with restaurant capacity allocation decisions and pricing strategies across online and offline channels. We develop a Stackelberg game model embedded in a Hotelling-Bertrand competition framework to capture the hierarchical decision-making structure of this ecosystem. The model yields closed-form equilibrium outcomes for the restaurant's optimal capacity allocation between dine-in and online channels, the platform's commission fee, and pricing strategies for both ecosystem participants. Our results reveal that a restaurant's capacity allocation is significantly influenced by the relative share of offline dine-in demand within a fixed total market, and that price mimicking by restaurants is profitable under low dine-in demand but erodes platform value when offline demand is high. Numerical analysis further demonstrates that increasing consumer disutility costs prompt both platforms and restaurants to raise prices across channels, highlighting critical trade-offs in ecosystem optimization. These findings provide actionable governance insights for OFD platforms designing incentive structures and for restaurant partners navigating channel trade-offs. The study contributes to the growing literature on data-driven platform governance and ecosystem optimization in service digital ecosystems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A feature selection layer approach for multi-class classification on neural networks
abstract: In the age of data-driven decision-making, deep learning models have become powerful tools for uncovering patterns and making predictions that influence many aspects of society. However, their broader adoption in scientific and business applications is often limited by a lack of interpretability. Feature weighting methods, which assess the relevance of individual features, are among the most widely studied approaches for improving interpretability. While post hoc techniques have advanced significantly, especially in modeling nuanced relationships between features and labels in multiclass problems, embedded methods typically fall short in this regard. Embedded techniques integrate feature relevance learning directly into the model training process, but they are often unable to capture label-specific relationships. To address the limitation, we propose multiple extensions to this Feature Selection Layer, an embedded feature weighting mechanism for neural networks. Through extensive experimentation, we identify the most effective extension and benchmark it against established feature weighting methods. Our results show that the proposed method matches existing techniques in identifying globally relevant features and outperforms them in capturing label-specific relevance. By leveraging the internal dynamics of the trained neural network, the method reveals how individual features contribute to the prediction of specific labels, requiring no post-processing beyond the training process. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Constrained occupational pathways: Historical ethnic penalties in career mobility among Japanese immigrants in the United States, 1920–1940
abstract: Racial and ethnic stratification was a persistent feature of the early 20th-century U.S. labor market. While acknowledging structural barriers such as organized exclusion, studies of Japanese immigrants have typically emphasized their upward mobility from laborers to independent farmers or small-business owners before World War II. Yet, few studies have examined how such barriers shaped Japanese mobility relative to that of contemporaneous immigrants from Europe, as well as Canada and Mexico. Using linked 1920–1940 U.S. census panel data, this study compares occupational mobility between first-generation Japanese immigrant men (born 1881–1900) and other immigrants by educational attainment. Findings indicate substantial ethnic occupational penalties for Japanese immigrants, particularly pronounced at higher levels of education, where they ranked below even their similarly educated Mexican counterparts. Whereas European and Canadian immigrants frequently ascended into managerial, professional, and skilled or semi-skilled blue-collar occupations, upward mobility among Japanese immigrants remained largely confined to small-business ownership and farming. Such an absence from mid-tier occupations is consistent with historically documented patterns of organized exclusion from labor unions and labor market discrimination. Additional analyses align with constrained occupational pathways as a major channel of the Japanese immigrants' economic disadvantage: within the same detailed occupations, salaried Japanese immigrants faced only modest observed wage penalties relative to U.S.-born Whites. Overall, my findings qualify optimistic narratives about first-generation Japanese immigrants by foregrounding the institutional constraints that structured their career mobility. © 2026 The Author
