title: Advances in enrichment pretreatment for enhanced laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy detection of trace heavy metals
abstract: Heavy metal contamination is a global challenge driven by industrialization and human activities. Conventional detection methods, while accurate, are hindered by high costs, labor demands, and limited speed, restricting large-scale use. Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS), with its rapid, multi-element capability and minimal sample preparation, offers a promising alternative. When coupled with enrichment pretreatment strategies, LIBS achieves improved sensitivity and reduced matrix interference. This review summarizes recent applications of LIBS for heavy metal detection in soils, water, food, and agricultural products, highlighting the limitations of direct analysis. Enrichment approaches such as electrochemical methods, ion exchange, membrane separation, and adsorption are discussed in terms of their underlying mechanisms and effectiveness. Recent advances integrating these strategies with LIBS for trace heavy metal analysis are critically evaluated, alongside challenges of sensitivity, reproducibility, and field applicability. Future directions include developing advanced enrichment materials (e.g., covalent and metal-organic frameworks), integrating with enhanced LIBS platforms, and applying artificial intelligence (AI)-driven data analysis. This review provides perspectives to guide LIBS toward reliable and efficient monitoring of trace heavy metals in environmental systems. This review aims to present a broad overview to support the continued development of LIBS as an efficient and versatile tool for trace heavy metal monitoring in evironmental and food matrices. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Environmental Mandated Delay: A Source-Based Classification Framework for Compliance-Driven Time Impacts in Construction Contracts
abstract: This article examines whether prevailing delay classifications in construction contracts adequately address time risk arising from mandatory environmental compliance obligations. It identifies a structural doctrinal gap in existing categories and proposes a distinct classification framework, environmental mandated delay (EMD), supported by a five-element cumulative test. A normative-comparative doctrinal methodology is employed, comprising (1) systematic analysis of delay provisions in major standard form construction contracts [the Fédération Internationale des Ingénieurs-Conseils (FIDIC) forms, the New Engineering Contract (NEC), and the Joint Contracts Tribunal (JCT) forms]; (2) comparative review of environmental regulatory frameworks in four jurisdictions (the UK, Australia, Indonesia, and the UAE); (3) a systematic review of published arbitral awards rendered under the auspices of the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID) and judicial decisions demonstrating recurring classification ambiguity; and (4) application of the proposed framework to documented infrastructure project contexts. None of the major standard form contracts articulates a delay category grounded in mandatory public law compliance. A structured content analysis of seven publicly available ICSID awards (2014-2022) confirms that compliance-based temporal disruption is recurrent across infrastructure disputes but no tribunal applied a structured delay classification framework in any case. Analysis of published arbitral decisions further identifies five recurring patterns that confirm the structural nature of the gap. EMD directly addresses each pattern by grounding entitlement in the public law source of the delaying obligation. The framework offers a structured analytical tool for extension-of-time (EOT) assessment, aligning delay classification with critical path-based scheduling analysis and improving consistency in contract administration and dispute resolution. The article makes three original contributions: (1) identification of a structural doctrinal gap supported by empirical arbitral evidence; (2) development of a source-based approach reorienting delay analysis from event- and actor-based models toward public law obligations; and (3) provision of an operational test applicable in engineering practice, enhancing predictability in the treatment of compliance-driven delay in climate-transition infrastructure projects. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Designing a Process-Oriented Performance Measurement System for R&D Activities in Manufacturing SME
abstract: Research and development (R&D) fuels innovation and competitiveness but remains hard to evaluate due to uncertainty, intangible outputs, and complex activity-outcome links. While literature identifies performance indicators, few address systematic PMS design based on R&D structure. This study proposes a process-oriented framework grounded in business process management. Through a qualitative case study, a four-phase model is developed: strategic alignment, process structuring, KPI development, and implementation. Key contributions include: (1) bridging the gap in PMS design for R&D, (2) introducing a four-phase model, and (3) demonstrating that aligning measurement with process, linking activities to purpose, and embedding measurement in routines are crucial. This shifts the focus from indicator selection to integrated PMS design and offers a scalable, practical approach for resource-constrained R&D settings. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Maximum-entropy minimal model for gas–liquid two-phase flow liquid holdup prediction across full pipe inclination angles
abstract: Liquid holdup governs pressure drop, flow-pattern transitions, and separation efficiency in gas–liquid pipe flow, but accurate and interpretable prediction across operating conditions remains difficult. In this paper, a maximum-entropy minimal model is extended to continuous multiphase flow to seek a minimal set of dimensionless variables using a linear combination of transformed predictors and a residual-correlation stopping criterion with all excluded candidates. From 35 candidate features constructed from nine physical parameters, greedy forward selection yields a closed-form model containing six selected predictors: no-slip liquid fraction, gas superficial velocity, gas–liquid density ratio, momentum ratio, mixture Froude number, and cosine of inclination. Evaluated on 746 experimental points covering four fluid pairs, seven pipe diameters, and inclinations from − 90° to + 90°, the model attains R2 = 0.9822 and a root-mean-square error of 0.0377. Five-fold cross-validation (R2 = 0.9820 ± 0.0026), holdout data (R2 = 0.9837), and out-of-distribution tests withholding a data source, horizontal flow, or a pipe diameter (R2 = 0.924 ∼ 0.975) confirm robust generalization. However, uneven coverage of inclinations and fluid properties, together with dependence on the compiled experimental sources, constrains the demonstrated scope of generalization. Within the selected six-predictor representation, quadratic and three-way interaction extensions increased mean cross-validated R2 by less than 0.002 under the evaluated settings. Inclination-resolved analysis reveals a complexity hierarchy: downward, upward, and horizontal flows require 1, 3, and 12 features, respectively, describing differences in the selected model sizes across inclination subsets. The unified expression approaches the accuracy of a tuned neural-network benchmark with only seven fitted parameters, a 6034-fold reduction relative to the benchmark. These results provide a data-determined measure of the physical complexity required to describe gas–liquid phase distribution and yield a transparent relation for engineering deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Integrated Payroll Management System Based on Cloud Computing and Microservice Architecture
abstract: Issues associated with the current enterprise payroll management are fragmentation of data, lengthy processing time, and the ability to handle multi-departmental cooperation and dynamic human resource scheduling, and these issues make it challenging to meet the requirements of multi-departmental cooperation and dynamic human resource scheduling. In order to resolve these issues, this paper renders and installs an integrated payroll management system under the basis of cloud computing and microservice architecture. The system uses a containerized deployment, where functional modules like the calculation of salaries, verification of salaries, files of employees and performance evaluation are split into various microservices; This article uses the dynamic scheduling of components between components by using the service registration and load balancing between components. It employs cloud database clusters to ensure that there is consistency of data and real time backup with high concurrency accesses and provides a Role Based Access Control (RBAC) model to provide security of data. The experiment was deployed and verified in an actual enterprise environment, and the results showed that the system reduced response time by an average of 47.5% compared to traditional standalone systems, with a maximum processing rate of 2893 records per second and system availability maintained at 99.98–99.99% when the number of concurrent users reached 2000. The research results demonstrate that the proposed system has significant advantages in performance, reliability, and maintainability, which can provide reference for the digital transformation of enterprise salary business. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Serendipity and innovation in new ventures: The moderating role of primary investor type
abstract: Rather than pure luck or a fully planned search, opportunities in new ventures frequently emerge from serendipitous discoveries. While research has emphasized the antecedents of serendipity, empirical evidence on its innovation outcomes remains scarce. Drawing on social cognitive theory, we argue that serendipity’s value depends on environmental conditions, which shape whether unexpected discoveries are recognized and translated into venture-level action. Analyzing survey data from 386 founders and CXOs of new ventures in Western and Northern Europe, we find that serendipity is positively associated with innovation radicalness and speed. These relationships are contingent on investor type: Compared with bootstrapped ventures, the positive associations are weaker in ventures backed by venture capitalists, business angels, or family and friends. These findings advance our understanding of serendipity’s contingent value in early-stage entrepreneurship and highlight investor dynamics as a boundary condition shaping innovation trajectories. title: Cloud Computing Solutions for Industry-Specific Digitalization in Morocco: Challenges, Opportunities, and Future Trends
abstract: Cloud-based technology has dramatically changed how many businesses operate globally; it also represents one of the most affordable and scalable types of technology available today. Cloud technology is now being utilized by many public and private companies across Morocco, which is attempting to develop what will be known as a “Digital Morocco” through government initiatives. The areas where these companies are using cloud technology include healthcare, agriculture, manufacturing, and finance. The lack of clearly defined rules for the utilization of cloud-based technologies as well as concerns related to cybersecurity and infrastructure issues have limited the wide-scale adoption of cloud-based technologies. Using both qualitative and quantitative methodologies, this research will examine the cloud environment in Morocco and will assess and describe the trends and drivers of cloud adoption within the Moroccan cloud market. The study also determines the economic impact of cloud-based technologies on Morocco and will identify potential sector-specific limitations to future adoption of cloud-based technologies in Morocco. The results demonstrate significant opportunities for increased efficiency of services but also require government agencies to develop and implement clearer regulations regarding cloud technology; and development of locally based cloud architectures and improved security to ensure a sustainable digital future. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Self-built or retailer-based? Online direct-to-consumer channel introduction strategies for the fresh producer under retailer competition and disruption risk
abstract: The sharing of logistics resources among competing retailers provides a new avenue for fresh producers to introduce online direct-to-consumer (OD) channels. However, differences in operational cost and stability create a strategic trade-off between two approaches. Producers may either build the OD channels by themselves, accepting exposure to disruption risk, or rely on retailers, which ensures consistent operational stability. This study develops game-theoretic models of a fresh supply chain comprising one producer and two competing retailers across three scenarios: no OD channel, a self-built OD channel, and a retailer-based OD channel. The results show that, once an OD channel is introduced, higher operational costs lead the producer to reduce direct-sales quantities and lower wholesale prices to stimulate retailer orders. In the self-built OD channel model, the producer must adopt a “conservative,” “aggressive,” or “balanced” operational strategy, depending on the delivery cost, to mitigate profit losses from rising disruption risk. The retailer-based OD channel model becomes the producer's equilibrium strategy only when the logistics service fee falls below a threshold. This threshold increases when the delivery cost is low and exhibits a U-shaped pattern when it is high, as disruption risk rises. Additionally, the retailer-based OD channel model expands the range of equilibrium strategies as disruption risk increases and weakens the moderating effect of wholesale prices on retailers' order quantities. This leads to an asymmetric competitive landscape in which the producer is constrained, the logistics-sharing retailer benefits, and the non-sharing retailer is disadvantaged. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Techno-economic optimization of onboard carbon capture systems under escalating emission penalties using surrogate models
abstract: Onboard carbon capture systems (OCCSs) are emerging as a medium-term response to progressively tightening greenhouse-gas fuel-intensity (GFI) requirements, motivating assessment of appropriate capacity and operation. This study develops a hierarchical multi-period framework that jointly determines one-time OCCS design and annual operation. Gaussian-process-regression surrogates efficiently replace rate-based process simulations, and the framework is applied to a liquefied-natural-gas-fueled very large crude carrier with a 30 wt% monoethanolamine process. On independent test sets, the surrogates achieved coefficients of determination of at least 0.9992 and mean absolute percentage errors of at most 2.01 %. Without surplus-unit trading, the optimum treats 30.0 % of the highest-load main-engine exhaust and matches capture heat demand primarily to recovered waste heat, reducing life cycle cost by 7.9 % relative to compliance without capture. Tightening the GFI trajectory alone does not necessarily increase capture because capture energy also affects attained GFI. When surplus units are traded, their price determines adoption and scale: installation is economical at 304 USD/tonCO2eq and above but not at 266 USD/tonCO2eq and below, while 342 USD/tonCO2eq drives the designs in all three regulatory scenarios to the maximum available main-engine exhaust flow. At 380 USD/tonCO2eq, gross lifetime capture increases from 199 to 634 kton relative to no trading, but net greenhouse gas avoidance increases only from 147 to 325 kton as parasitic emissions rise. Under the assumed immediate-sale surplus-unit market, the prescribed surplus-unit price and net emissions strongly influence OCCS value alongside the target trajectory. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Supporting strategic decisions for coastal watersheds in crisis: A system dynamics model for socio-ecological sustainability
abstract: Sustainable development of coastal lagoons facing complex socio-ecological crises requires quantification of impacts of solutions on all sectors involved. We present a System Dynamics Model (SDM) representing interactions between agriculture, livestock, tourism, and nutrient stocks (aquifer, soils, wastewaters) of the Mar Menor socio-ecological system (SE-Spain), following a participatory process. We applied the SDM to evaluate 22 individual solutions and 3 adaptation scenarios based on contrasting Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1, SSP2, SSP5) and stakeholder inputs. Results show that agriculture drives degradation while recycling nutrients from livestock and urban wastewater, and that legacy Nitrogen and Phosphorus in soils and groundwater limits lagoon recovery. Business-as-usual (SSP2) and agricultural intensification (SSP5) scenarios reduce water security due to climate change and groundwater contamination. End-of-pipe interventions do not provide long-term solutions, whereas source-oriented interventions lower nutrient inputs, providing socioeconomic benefits. A sustainability-focused scenario (SSP1) results in moderate economic growth, environmental improvements, and highest Total Economic Value. © 2026 The Authors

title: ChatGPT as a Tool for Business Insight: A Case Study in Mentorship Data Analysis
abstract: The rapid expansion of data in the business environment created the demand for tools that can transform unstructured data into actionable insights. This case study examines the possibility of using ChatGPT as an effective tool to lower analytical barriers for small organizations, which often lack specialized technical skills and significant staffing resources. By leveraging ChatGPT’s natural-language interface and prompt-engineering techniques, this study demonstrates how Big Brothers Big Sisters’ unstructured case notes, survey responses, and program metrics can be transformed into strategic recommendations without advanced analytical skills. Through exploratory queries and GenAI-driven recommendations, ChatGPT identified key predictors of relationship length and proposed practical strategies to improve mento-mentee relationships. Findings suggest that GenAI can complement traditional analytical techniques, offering rapid, interpretable insights to unlock the full potential of unstructured data. This study concludes by discussing both implications for decision-making in the business context and directions for future research on human-AI collaboration. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Transforming Emerging Markets: Digital Economy as a Driver of Sustainability
abstract: The digital economy is significantly altering global economic environments, particularly in emerging markets through technological adoption, mobile connectivity, and novel business models. This paper reviews literature on the digital economy in these markets, emphasizing key drivers, challenges, and opportunities. A PRISMA-guided literature selection process identified 85 peer-reviewed studies published from 2010 to 2025. Findings indicate that mobile banking, e-commerce, digital entrepreneurship, and government-led digital initiatives serve as the primary catalysts for growth in the digital economy. However, this growth faces significant challenges, including infrastructure gaps, cybersecurity risks, a lack of digital literacy, and various regulatory barriers that need to be addressed to ensure sustained progress. This review emphasizes the capacity of the digital economy to facilitate progress towards Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), notably SDG 8, which focuses on Decent Work and Economic Growth; SDG 9, which pertains to Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure; and SDG 10, which aims to reduce inequalities. Additionally, it provides a thorough discussion on policy recommendations, identifies research gaps, and suggests future directions intended to assist academics, practitioners, and policymakers in harnessing the digital economy’s potential for sustainable development. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: An ABI Architecture for Hospital Appointment Duration Prediction
abstract: Hospitals face the ongoing challenge of managing limited resources in dynamic environments, where variability in appointment duration hinders scheduling efficiency, increases waiting times, and affects the utilization of healthcare professionals. Within the Hospital 4.0 paradigm, traditional Business Intelligence (BI) systems prove inadequate for supporting adaptive and data-driven decision-making. This paper presents an Adaptive Business Intelligence (ABI) architecture that integrates data ingestion, predictive modeling, appointment schedule optimization, and dashboard-based visualization, all orchestrated through containerized services. Each predictive model is encapsulated within Docker containers and exposed via FastAPI microservices, enabling scalability and modular deployment. The main contribution of this work is to demonstrate how real-time predictive insights can effectively support the optimization of hospital appointment scheduling and resource allocation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Robust traffic sign detection in diverse environments: A comprehensive review of methods and trends
abstract: Robust traffic sign detection (TSD) is essential for autonomous driving and advanced driver-assistance systems. Despite significant advances in object detection, modern detectors still suffer performance degradation under adverse conditions such as fog, rain, snow, and low-light environments, compared with clear-weather scenarios. This review highlights a critical finding: architectural evolution alone, from YOLOv1 to YOLOv12, has not resolved the challenge of adverse-weather robustness. No reviewed study reports mean average precision for the same trained YOLO model on paired clear- and adverse-condition data, so the magnitude of the loss cannot be established for this family from the published record; the only paired detection result in the corpus, an enhanced Faster R-CNN evaluated on TT100K, loses 5.7 mAP points in rain, a retention ratio of 93.8%. The 15–20% figure widely quoted for adverse-condition degradation originates in top-1 classification accuracy on pre-cropped CURE-TSR imagery and is therefore not commensurable with detection mAP, and no study evaluates a single model across all four conditions on a common protocol. To address this gap, we present one of the first comprehensive reviews to jointly examine three previously fragmented research areas: the evolution of YOLO alongside Faster R-CNN, SSD, transformer-based detectors, and vision-language models; traffic sign detection under fog, rain, snow, and nighttime conditions; and a critical analysis of nineteen benchmark datasets, which exposes limitations in geographic diversity, weather coverage, and illumination representation. Using a PRISMA-guided methodology, 246 studies were systematically reviewed, and four key contributions were made. First, we introduce the mAP Retention Ratio (adverse-weather mAP divided by clear-weather mAP) as a practical measure of robustness and apply it to the corpus in a retention audit, which finds the ratio computable for only one reviewed study; on the available evidence, no current detector has been demonstrated to achieve strong adverse-weather performance, real-time speed, and deployment efficiency simultaneously. Second, we synthesize adverse-condition detection strategies and isolate image restoration as an experimental variable: relative to an unmodified detector on the same benchmark, decoupled restore-then-detect cascades recover approximately +5 mAP points, whereas restoration jointly optimized with the detection objective recovers up to +18 mAP@0.5 points, with both incurring additional latency, and no reviewed study compares these two strategies under a common detector, dataset, and hardware configuration. Third, we identify the primary causes of poor model generalization, including biases in traffic sign categories, environmental conditions, illumination settings, and regional distributions. Fourth, we propose a focused research agenda centered on transformer optimization for edge devices, LiDAR–camera fusion for occluded signs, generative augmentation for improved cross-domain generalization, and few-shot and zero-shot detection of rare and region-specific signs. Our findings demonstrate that robust traffic sign detection requires more than incremental architectural improvements, because progress will depend on the integration of multimodal sensing, representative datasets, efficient deployment strategies, and weather-aware learning frameworks. By consolidating fragmented literature and providing quantitative insights, this review offers a comprehensive reference for developing traffic sign detection systems that are accurate, reliable, and deployable in real-world autonomous driving environments. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Gas flaring, agricultural productivity and labor reallocation: Evidence from Nigeria
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of natural gas flaring—a byproduct of oil production—on agricultural productivity in Nigeria. Using a panel dataset of Nigerian households from the Living Standards Measurement Study (LSMS) spanning 2012–2018, combined with geocoded data on monthly gas flaring volumes from oil fields, the study employs variation in the timing of interview surveys to assess effects of gas flaring during harvest and planting seasons. The analysis focuses on southern Nigeria, where oil production is concentrated, and leverages a 2010 policy reform (Local Content Act) that increased local onshore oil activities and thus gas flaring. The empirical strategy includes fixed effects (household, and region-by-month-by-year) to control for unobserved heterogeneity, weather variables (precipitation and temperature), and an instrumental variable approach using global oil price changes interacted with pre-sample flaring intensity to address endogeneity. Key outcomes measured are real crop yield per hectare and labor productivity (real agricultural output divided by worker-days). The findings reveal significant negative effects during the harvest season, particularly in rainy periods, but minimal impacts during planting. Mechanisms are explored through satellite data on air pollutants, showing elevated levels of black carbon, sulfur dioxide, and nitrogen dioxide in flaring areas. Robustness checks confirm the results against various confounders like conflicts, oil spills, and placebo tests. The paper contributes to literature on the impact of air pollution on worker productivity and crop yields and climate change impacts on agriculture, highlighting policy needs to mitigate environmental costs from extractive industries in developing countries. © 2026 The Author

title: Why this AI app? The impact of generative artificial intelligence on educators’ choices in educational apps
abstract: In elementary education, generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is being incorporated into educational applications, despite still-emerging evidence of its effects on children's learning and development. Educators, who are already overwhelmed with choice in the commercial app space, may increasincly have to decide whether to incorporate GenAI-enabled apps for their classrooms. Thus, the present study investigates how mentioning GenAI in app store descriptions impacts K-6 educators' selection of educational apps. Over two studies, K-6 educators (each n = 101) from Canada, the US, and the UK viewed and evaluated eight researcher-created educational math apps with and without GenAI. Study 1 tested whether mentioning GenAI in app descriptions affected educators' app evaluations but found no effect. In Study 2, results from a repeated measures MANOVA revealed that educators rated apps without AI higher than those mentioning GenAI, but there were no significant effects of GenAI on likelihood to download or willingness to pay for apps. A hierarchical cluster analysis identified three distinct groups of educators: 1) selectors (n = 28), who exhibited a preference for downloading, rating, and paying for apps including GenAI; 2) agnostics (n = 59), who exhibit minimal preferences; and 3) avoiders (n = 14), who prefer apps without AI. Most educators were agnostic to the use of GenAI in educational apps, highlighting the need to support educators' informed decisions about when to adopt GenAI tools and encourage critical evaluation of GenAI's role in education. More research is needed to understand how educators' GenAI preferences relate to their attitudes, knowledge, and use of GenAI. © 2026

title: Copy That? The Influence of Process Model Representation Format on LLM Comprehension
abstract: LLMs are increasingly applied across the business process management (BPM) lifecycle, e.g., for analyzing or documenting processes. How reliably they support these applications depends on how well they comprehend the underlying process model. In practice, the same process model may be provided to an LLM in different ways, e.g., as a structured serialization or a rendered diagram. However, it is unclear whether and to what extent the choice of representation format affects comprehension. We address this gap with a systematic study that assesses comprehension through interpretation quality, i.e., the graded correctness of task responses. We compare the representation formats of the same process model in three categories: natural-language text, rendered diagrams, and structured serializations. This yields four isolated formats (textual narrative, PNG, BPMN-XML, Mermaid) and selected hybrid combinations, all derived from a common set of BPMN models. We evaluate these format configurations across six LLMs, eight processes, and eleven task types. An LLM-as-a-judge scores responses against reference answers using a graded metric and an error taxonomy. The results show that the representation format substantially affects interpretation quality, with no single format being best across all LLMs. The isolated PNG is consistently the weakest, while hybrid combinations of natural-language text with BPMN-XML or Mermaid emerge as the strongest formats overall. These findings establish the representation format as a design variable for LLM-supported BPM tasks and yield implications for its selection. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The Hack4CBL Framework: A Challenge-Based Learning Approach for Multidisciplinary Hackathons in Higher Education
abstract: This paper introduces the Hack4CBL framework, integrating Challenge-Based Learning (CBL) principles into hackathon design for multidisciplinary higher education. By aligning hackathon stages with CBL domains (engage, investigate, act, transfer), it fosters collaboration and diverse learning outcomes. We illustrate Hack4CBL’s effectiveness through the “Second International Hackathon of Intelligent Solutions for the Promotion of Agribusiness 4.0,” involving 142 undergraduate students from Colombia and Costa Rica across Systems Engineering, Business Administration, and Agronomic Engineering. Its application in a formal undergraduate course is also discussed. Over 16 weeks, interdisciplinary teams tackled real-world agribusiness challenges, developing minimum viable products. Results show that CBL integration enhances collaboration, deepens domain knowledge, and accelerates professional skill development. The framework offers a replicable model for educational hackathons aligned with professional realities. Emotional challenges were identified, suggesting a need for explicit guidance. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Implementation of a Scrum-Based Digital Coupon Web Application in the Retail Sector
abstract: This study presents the implementation of a Scrum-based web application for managing digital coupons in a retail company, addressing the need for agile, scalable, and cloud-oriented promotional systems. The application was developed through five iterative sprints following the Scrum framework and deployed on the Amazon Web Services (AWS) platform using services such as Elastic Beanstalk, S3, CloudFront, Route 53, and Cognito to ensure scalability, security, and operational efficiency. The instrument used to evaluate the system’s commercial effects demonstrated high internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.945), and the Shapiro–Wilk test confirmed the normality of the data. Pearson’s correlation analysis revealed positive and statistically significant associations between the use of the web application and key business indicators, including sales performance (r = 0.557, p = 0.001), new product promotion (r = 0.511, p = 0.004), and private-label product promotion (r = 0.565, p = 0.001). These findings indicate that the implemented solution not only meets technical and operational requirements but also contributes to measurable improvements in promotional effectiveness and commercial visibility. The study provides a foundation for future research integrating artificial intelligence and predictive analytics into digital coupon management systems. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Joint fulfillment and consolidation of multi-item orders in e-commerce: A two-phase heuristic
abstract: In today's business-to-consumer (B2C) e-commerce, high order volumes, multi-item orders and shipments, split deliveries, and escalating transportation costs, pose significant operational challenges. In this environment, jointly optimizing order fulfillment and consolidation is crucial to achieving economies of scale and ensuring cost-effective delivery. This study addresses the Multi-Item Orders Fulfillment and Consolidation Problem (MOFCP) faced by e-commerce retailers that manage both online channels and physical warehouse networks. We develop a model that identifies the optimal set of warehouses to fulfill orders and their corresponding consolidation points to minimize transportation costs. We formulate the problem as a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model with a piecewise linear cost function and propose a two-phase heuristic to solve MOFCP efficiently: in the first phase, we find an initial solution by LP-rounding; in the second phase, we employ a General Variable Neighborhood Search (GVNS) algorithm to improve the initial solution. In addition, we design two benchmark instances based on item coverage in the network and the inventory-to-demand ratio. Extensive computational experiments show that the two-phase heuristic yields solutions close to the ones found by Gurobi, within significantly lower computation time (up to 30 times faster). The experimental results indicate that the heuristic scales well with large problem instances and remains robust across changes in problem parameters. Finally, we demonstrate that consolidation can lead to significant savings, especially in networks with low item coverage and a low inventory-to-demand ratio. © 2026 The Authors

title: From BPMN to TLAQ: A Privacy-Preserving Framework for Executable Clinical Pathway Analytics in Federated Big Data Healthcare Systems
abstract: This paper introduces BPMN-to-TLAQ wrapping methodology that enables the transformation of formal Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) clinical pathway models into executable Tree-Like Analytical Queries (TLAQ) within the QFLS Federated Analytics Framework. Our approach leverages the innovative Lazy Aggregation paradigm of TLAQ, where parent-child query nodes do not adhere to strict containment relations, thereby supporting granular, step-wise medical investigation processes. This methodology bridges declarative process modelling with privacy-preserving distributed data analytics, which allows healthcare institutions to quantitatively evaluate guideline-based clinical workflows across fragmented, sensitive datasets without raw data centralization. We demonstrate the practical utility and scalability of the approach through a comprehensive case study based on a real-life clinical scenario within the context of the EU H2020 QUALITOP Research Project. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Impact of Agile and Hybrid Methodologies on Fintech Software Project Outcomes
abstract: Burnt by the lightning-fast pace of the digital transformation of the global fintech industry, the need to establish software development practices that can deliver all three, i.e., speed, quality, and regulatory compliance, has become more urgent. Although the method of Agile and hybrid project management is quite popular in fintech software development, the literature is dispersed and focused mainly on the qualitative study, and there is little empirical validation at the industry-specific level. Specifically, both large-scale quantitative comparisons between pure Agile and hybrid approaches to development in the context of a regulated fintech space and longitudinal information on its long-term effectiveness in terms of project outcomes are wanting. The study will be a systematic effort to study how agile and hybrid approaches affect the performance of software projects in the world fintech sector. By concentrating on such key performance indicators as delivery efficiency, software quality, stakeholder satisfaction, risk management, and alignment, the study considers the critical enablers with the usage of a structured empirical approach. The research design will be a combination of cross-organizational information of the fintech projects implemented over the past years and will allow drawing comparisons based on the methodological paradigm and organizational dimensions. This study aims to achieve this by providing evidence-based observation to the academic and business communities by setting quantifiable links between the development methodologies and project performance measurements. It is anticipated that the findings will assist in making informed decisions because fintech organizations under regulatory pressure will be faced with methodological choices, and also, the findings will enhance the theoretical conception towards hybrid agility in the complex and compliance-driven software ecosystems. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: What you see is (not) what you got: The human factor in PDF signature verification
abstract: Signed PDF documents have legally binding value under frameworks such as the EU's eIDAS regulation. In this work, we present Genuine PDF Forgeries, a novel attack class that focuses on human factors in signature validation. Our attacks target the disconnect between cryptographically verifiable signer certificates and human-visible signature blocks embedded in documents. We analyze our attacks against 23 PDF viewers and validation tools across desktop platforms and the web. We find that nine of the 13 viewers that automatically report signature validity hide authenticated signer information behind additional user interaction. We then evaluate the attack in twin deception-based online studies with 584 EU-based participants. To further validate the impact, we perform a highly tailored real-world attack study with six trials within two privacy-sensitive organizations. Five of six organizational trials accepted requests authenticated using the forged visual identity. In the online studies (total n=584), the most effective attack variant deceives 71.9% of eligible participants on first impression, and 57.3% continue to be deceived even after we prompt for additional introspection. We derive viewer-side countermeasures and prototype a safeguard that overlays the untrusted signature block with signer information obtained from the validated certificate. Our results show that boolean validity indicators, not associated with the authenticated signer identity, are insufficient in practice. © 2026 The Authors

title: SLM-Driven Schema Evolution for IoT Data Streams
abstract: Data schemas in Internet of Things (IoT) environments change constantly as devices are updated, vendors migrate APIs, and business requirements shift, yet downstream pipelines are expected to keep running without interruption. Manual schema maintenance does not scale in such environments, and existing automated approaches rely heavily on static rules or cloud-based services unsuitable for edge deployment. This paper outlines a vision for edge-based automated schema evolution. It proposes a structure where Small Language Models (SLMs), installed on edge devices, identify structural differences in real-time data streaming and create modification rules. The proposed five-layer architecture includes schema fingerprinting, change classification, rule generation, stream modification, and validation. Key challenges are discussed, including semantic ambiguity and edge resource constraints. Directions for future research include domain-specific fine-tuning, federated schema learning, and explainable adaptation methods. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Terrorism and altruistic giving: Evidence from child sponsorship
abstract: We study how terrorist attacks targeting educational institutions affect private development aid through child sponsorship. Conceptually, terrorist events may increase sponsorship by signaling greater need or reduce it if affected communities are seen as less effective destinations to support. We combine global administrative data from Plan International on child sponsorship across 50 countries over the 2008-2018 period, aggregated at the Primary Sampling Unit (PSU) level, with geocoded terrorism events from the Global Terrorism Database. Our core specification focuses on attacks against educational institutions within 20 km of each PSU. We estimate the causal effect using a heterogeneity-robust difference-in-differences approach suited to staggered, non-absorbing treatments. We find that attacks on educational institutions reduce the share of sponsored children by about 3 percentage points, a 4 percent decline relative to the mean. Back-of-the-envelope calculations suggest this corresponds to funding losses of approximately US$615,000 across affected communities over the study period. Since sponsorship is geographically targeted, these losses fall on the specific communities, underscoring the need to buffer local development funding against security shocks. © 2026 The Authors

title: Object-Centric Process Querying in SQL: Translation Rules and In-Database Execution
abstract: Object-Centric Process Querying (OCPQ) is a visual query language and accompanying tool for expressing queries and constraints over Object-Centric Event Data (OCED). Such queries span multiple object and event types that case-centric query languages cannot natively address. Its existing execution engine processes data in memory: Dataset size is capped by host memory, and the relational database systems that organizations already operate cannot serve as backends, forcing data export or migration. In this paper, we present a translation from OCPQ to SQL, defined as a recursive mapping over the OCPQ query tree with a rule per construct, emitting SQL for SQLite, DuckDB, and PostgreSQL. An OCEL 2.0 Virtualization Layer accommodates source schemas that diverge from the OCEL 2.0 layout via direct rewrite or VIEW generation, so the translation can target them without data migration. We evaluate using three types of workloads: Seven queries from prior work, an automatically generated corpus of 6919 OCPQ trees, and a non-OCEL Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) database schema queried through the virtualization layer. The resulting query outputs match the in-memory engine across all queries, demonstrating that the translation preserves its semantics. Our evaluation also shows the memory decoupling enabled by the translation: SQL backends scale to support large datasets on which the native OCPQ engine runs out of memory. When data fits in memory, the in-memory OCPQ engine remains fastest, with DuckDB roughly 3–12× slower and PostgreSQL 14–71× slower as drop-in replacements. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Process Externalities: A Missing Construct for Responsible BPM
abstract: Responsible Business Process Management (RBPM) asks the discipline to account for the effects of processes on stakeholders, society, and the environment. Yet BPM’s models are scoped within the process boundary and assessed against internal objectives, so they often fail to capture broader societal or environmental effects. Existing approaches – stakeholder analysis, risk management, sustainable BPM, value-sensitive design – each addresses a particular category of such effects; what they lack is a first-class lifecycle construct that treats them as a single class through a shared generative mechanism, complementing rather than replacing them. We propose the construct of Process Externalities (PEs) to capture consequences borne by parties other than a process’s intended beneficiary, or that affect values absent from its objective function, which are generated systematically by optimisation under an incomplete objective. Understood in this way, PEs will be defined by this mechanism rather than merely by the stakeholders they affect, and ultimately, after standardisation, they may be subject to externalities accounting following the direction already set by impact-weighted accounting initiatives in management. This paper shows that PEs are elicitable through a design-fiction method aimed at effects not yet visible in process data, and actionable through an externality register attached to the lifecycle, for which we give a graduated, three-level operationalisation and a sketch of externality accounting. We illustrate it in one ordinary process (loan approval) and two speculative ones. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Participatory Process Mining: A Framework and Call for Research
abstract: Process mining is used to create transparency about organizational work by analyzing event data from business processes. Although such transparency is often assumed to be inherently beneficial, the dominant strand is that transparency is imposed “top-down”. Decision-makers and developers initiate and direct process mining initiatives, while those performing the work have hardly any say. This can be problematic, not least because transparency can lead to perceived surveillance, misrepresentation, and resistance on the side of workers. This paper foregrounds the role of transparency as a socio-technical phenomenon constructed through a series of decisions made at different stages of the process mining lifecycle. To proactively consider and involve the voices of those whose activities are mined and analyzed –who we refer to as the process minees– we introduce the concept of Participatory Process Mining, an approach in which the process minees are recognized as key stakeholders in shaping the conditions under which transparency about their work is produced and used. We propose a conceptual framework that distinguishes the levels (data, tool, organizational) at which participation can be enabled across the process mining lifecycle, and the degrees of participation that can be realized at each level. Moreover, we outline directions for future research to examine how these forms of participation shape process minee perceptions of transparency and empowerment. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Teaching Declarative BPM: Where, When and to Whom it Matters
abstract: The theory of BPM has, for a long time, discussed the interaction between flows and business rules, in what some call the declarative vs imperative business process spectrum. While imperative models constitute the standard in the curricula, with standards such as BPMN being imparted in most educations, declarative BPM has received a much more specialized scope. This paper collects and discusses insights coming from experiences teaching declarative process models in academia, in courses ranging from computer science to business informatics across universities in Austria, Belgium, Denmark, and the Netherlands, with languages such as Declare, DCR graphs, and DMN. We report considerations in curriculum development, considerations for diverse backgrounds, accessibility of tools and materials, and overall student perceptions of declarative modelling. Moreover, it reports some of the challenges of teaching declarative models in the classroom and outlines possible mitigation aspects that could support an easier adoption by the students. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: From Principles to Practice: Embedding GEDSI in Process Design
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of Gender, Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) principles into process design, highlighting their significance in promoting equitable processes. GEDSI has garnered attention among international development agencies, NGOs, and corporations as a framework to enhance organisational effectiveness and social responsibility. Utilising experiences from public sector organisations in the Philippines, which participated in process driven transformation programmes, this study examines the incorporation of GEDSI into process design. It synthesises current research and practice, analysing theoretical frameworks, methodologies, case studies, and challenges, while identifying gaps in the literature. A GEDSI-Process Maturity Framework is introduced to assess process alignment with GEDSI dimensions, although further development is required. The paper emphasises the importance of prioritising GEDSI in process design to ensure ethical and efficient outcomes, offering insights for practitioners and researchers. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Instructional Design in Process Modelling: Surveying Educators’ Perspectives
abstract: Process modelling (PM) education has gained prominence as organizations need professionals who can translate business logic into formal models. While prior work has examined model comprehension, modelling guidelines, flipped classrooms, gamification, and animations, less is known about how educators combine these elements into instructional design (ID) decisions. This study investigates PM educators’ perspectives (N = 13) through an exploratory qualitative survey structured around a five-stage ID framework. Results indicate that educators commonly adopt constructivist, active, and project-based approaches, emphasizing practical engagement and real-world relevance. However, gaps remain in prerequisite support, metacognitive reflection, higher-order Create-level activities, assessment alignment, and the systematic use of animations for comprehension. The contribution is a structured educator-perspective account of current PM instructional design practices, identifying opportunities for course redesign through better alignment of learner needs, learning objectives, assessment, reflective tasks, and dynamic visualization support. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Local Brands, Digital Shelves: Brand Authenticity and E-commerce Consumer Behavior in Vietnam’s Fashion Industry
abstract: Brands significantly influence customers’ identity goals, as they rely on brands for self-expression, self-promotion, or affirmation of their values. Consequently, consumers are predisposed to alter their purchasing behaviors, and their demand for authenticity is pushing Vietnamese local fashion producers to reconsider their branding. Nonetheless, there is a scarcity of research on the influence of the authenticity of Vietnamese domestic fashion brands on consumer behavior in the contemporary era of e-commerce growth. This article introduces a theoretical framework that integrates the S-O-R theory with the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) to analyze the impact of local fashion brand authenticity on consumer behavior in e-commerce. This research specifically focuses on product quality, brand reputation and online shopping experience as cues of authenticity that are used by consumers to evaluate the authenticity of local brands when shopping online. The results offer a more comprehensive understanding of the effect that brand authenticity has on consumers’ behavior in online buying environments. This is done by studying the relationship among brand authenticity, perceived usefulness, and personal attitude in the context of E-commerce consumer behavior. The conceptual framework of the research was checked using the data gathered from an online questionnaire specifically targeting 221 consumers in Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC). The data were then analyzed by employing the PLS-SEM method. The findings can guide local fashion businesses in Vietnam to develop in the future, particularly in terms of publicity and marketing. The constraints, theoretical implications and potential further research topics are also discussed. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: AI-Decision Checkpoints for AI-Augmented Business Process Management: Framework and Educational Instantiation
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and AI agents are increasingly embedded in operational business processes. Yet Business Process Management (BPM) curricula and frameworks still largely treat artificial intelligence (AI) as an add-on technology, leaving graduates (as potential future process developers) unprepared to reason about AI as a first-class design element of end-to-end processes. This paper addresses that gap by proposing AI-decision checkpoints: explicit moments in a process development trajectory where process developers identify AI-candidate sub-processes, assess expected effects on time, cost, quality, and flexibility, consider legal and organisational constraints, and document a reasoned decision to adopt, constrain, or reject specific AI components. The checkpoints are instantiated through a fictitious customer onboarding process as a BPM Teaching Case, embedded in a lifecycle-driven framework spanning six modules that combine process modeling, simulation, workflow execution with AI agents, and process mining, with each module’s output serving as the next module’s input. A preliminary formative reflection draws on instructor observations, submitted artifacts, and discovered process maps from learning-management-system logs. These exploratory observations suggest that the approach supported clearer distinctions between task-level automation and process-level value. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Unlocking Hidden Expertise: How AI Transforms Tacit Knowledge Into Competitive Advantage
abstract: Knowledge in organizations often remains undocumented, residing tacitly in employees’ heads. Amid demographic shifts and rising career mobility, preserving implicit knowledge is increasingly critical for organizational continuity and competitiveness. We present the development, implementation, and evaluation of an AI assistant designed for semi-structured extraction and documentation of tacit workforce knowledge. We propose a multi-stage approach that generates individualized, semi-structured interview guides by integrating feedback about interviewees. We implemented this approach in a practical case study and established a feedback loop to capture interviewees’ and interviewer’s impressions for iterative improvement. We also analyze integration pathways for deploying these tools within corporate IT landscapes. Implementation in the case study demonstrated the feasibility of AI-supported capture and documentation workflows, while the feedback loop enabled rapid refinement of prompts and interaction design. AI-assisted, semi-structured interviewing that leverages multi-source feedback is a promising approach to preserving organizational tacit knowledge. Future work should evaluate long-term knowledge retention, measurable impact on business continuity, and enterprise-grade deployment in diverse IT environments. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

title: Diagnosing and remedying oiling out in an industrial reactive crystallization through coupled reaction, thermodynamic, and population balance modeling
abstract: This work examines a reactive crystallization of an agrochemical intermediate in a solvent–antisolvent system prone to liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS). The initial process encountered oiling-out, yielding a product with a bimodal particle-size distribution and poor bulk-flow properties. To enhance process understanding, we developed an integrated reactor model combining thermodynamics, reaction kinetics, and crystallization dynamics. NRTL parameters fitted to measured solid–liquid equilibrium data were used to calculate solubility and the metastable liquid–liquid binodal in the ternary product–solvent–antisolvent system. We coupled reaction kinetics with a moment-based population balance to describe crystallization and predict the composition trajectory. Projecting this trajectory onto the ternary phase diagram revealed the mechanistic origin of oiling-out, clarified the role of the initial solvent pre-charge, and explained the apparent irreproducibility of empirical seeding events. In silico screening of several process schemes identified viable alternatives. Experimental implementation of one such scheme supported the predicted regime change – a shift from a bimodal to a substantially unimodal particle-size distribution and a less acicular crystal habit. The trajectory-aware analysis subsequently guided scale-up to commercial manufacture of the intermediate at multi-hundred-kilogram scale. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Representing BPMN Choreographies in OCEL 2.0
abstract: Inter-organizational business processes describe the interaction between distributed parties. BPMN choreographies offer a modeling notation for business interactions between participants, setting aside their internal behaviors. In process mining, existing literature views choreographies through a single-case notion lens, attempting to fit interaction data involving several business entities into a flat event log format. In this paper, we investigate how the object-centric event log format OCEL 2.0 can be used to express choreography data. To that end, we present a mapping between the BPMN choreography metamodel and OCEL 2.0 elements. The mapping enforces BPMN choreography semantics by defining data constraints. We demonstrate and evaluate the approach with 19 datasets from different domains. We provide implementations to extract choreography data, validate choreography event logs, and convert them to BPMN choreography diagrams. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: From Classroom to Practice: Bridging BPM Education and Industry Expectations Through a Process Mining Tool Comparison Project
abstract: This paper presents an innovative assignment approach implemented in the Business Process Modelling, Mining, and Automation course for Master’s students at theUniversity of Ottawa. The course integrates Active Learning principles to train industry-ready business analysts, capable of supporting modern business process management, mining, optimization, and automation initiatives. The assignment approach involves a project-based process mining tool comparison project, where students evaluate industry-relevant tools using real event logs to address a concrete business problem. The assignment design integrates experiential learning, formative feedback, and peer review activities to support both technical and professional skill development. The assignment is structured around a set of guiding principles. First, it emphasizes the development of real-world skills aligned with the evolving demands of digital business processes. Second, it encourages students to critically challenge their assumptions, tool limitations, and existing practices through a data-driven, evidence-based mindset. Finally, it promotes continuous self-reflection and the active exchange of constructive feedback among peers to reinforce deeper learning and professional growth. These guiding principles offer a practical framework that can support other educators in the BPM community in designing effective and practical assignment strategies that help bridge the gap between academic learning and industry expectations. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Upper credal Wasserstein envelopes for belief models: Choquet–Kantorovich duality and non-representability of universal rectangle lifts
abstract: A basic probability assignment (BPA) on a finite ground space determines a credal set of compatible additive refinements. When only the BPA is observed, the classical optimal-transport value is therefore partially identified. We study its upper endpoint, the upper credal Wasserstein envelope Wc↑. Finite Kantorovich duality and credal support functions yield a Choquet–Kantorovich representation: the feasible geometry remains the ground-space Kantorovich dual polyhedron, while epistemic imprecision enters through upper Choquet expectations over focal supports. This representation separates Wc↑ from the maximum-lift Dempster–Shafer optimal-transport rectangle surrogate DSOT+. The former optimizes over the focal-max image of ground-feasible potentials; the latter optimizes over the full rectangle-dual region. On any class containing all categorical BPA pairs over the prescribed focal families, an exact BPA-independent linear rectangle representation must consequently use the maximum rectangle lift. On finite spaces, equality Wc↑=DSOT+ is equivalent to feasibility of at least one linear system indexed by a global focal-max pattern. Explicit examples show both equality and strict inequality. An unbounded line family has BPAs supported on non-singleton intervals and a unique maximizing pair of nondegenerate two-atom refinements. The minimum-lift rectangle program equals the lower credal endpoint for every finite cost; a cross-separable regime additionally gives upper exactness. These results identify the global realizability condition omitted by rectangle-wise surrogates and clarify when such surrogates are exact or only upper bounds. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Fine-Grained Control of Blockchain-Based Business Process Instance Deployment
abstract: The integration of blockchain technology into Business Process Management (BPM) has attracted significant attention due to the transparency and immutability offered by distributed ledger technologies. Numerous studies have proposed blockchain-based workflow engine architectures to execute business processes directly on-chain. These adopt distinct design decisions for process instance deployment, resulting in a diverse architectural variants with significantly different gas cost. In this paper we propose to give fine-grained control to process modelers regarding how the control flow logic and process data are distributed across one or multiple smart contracts. To demonstrate the practical applicability of the approach, we compare two deployment configurations of the same blockchain-based crowdfunding process and examine the resulting deployment and execution costs. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Does AI Improve BPMN Modelling? Evidence from Iterative Assignments and Critical Verification Practice
abstract: This paper investigates whether and under what conditions AI assistance improves BPMN modelling in higher education. Building on research in BPM education, active learning, and LLM-assisted modelling, authors designed an iterative two-stage assignment in which students first submitted an initial BPMN model (V1) and then refined it using a rubric-aligned verification checklist, scenario-based test cases, and a shortchange log (V2). A volunteer subgroup additionally produced an AI-assisted alternative final model (V2–AI), accompanied by an AI Usage Statement capturing intentions, verification behaviors, and reasons for accepting or rejecting AI suggestions. Results show substantial learning gains between V1 and V2, particularly in logic-intensive areas such as gateways and events. Error frequencies decreased across most categories, demonstrating the effectiveness of structured scaffolding for guiding iterative improvement. The comparison of V2 and V2–AI reveals heterogeneous outcomes: while some students benefited from AI support, others introduced new inconsistencies when relying uncritically on AI-generated suggestions. Qualitative analysis of AI Usage Statements indicates that critical verification, rather than intensity of AI use, is the key determinant of high-quality AI-assisted modelling. The primary contribution is empirical evidence on learning gains through iterative revision and structured verification. As secondary, exploratory contributions, the study provides: (2) a fine-grained error taxonomy for analysing student process models, and (3) the first paired comparison of human-refined and AI-assisted BPMN models in higher education. The proposed instructional design offers a scalable, responsible approach for integrating critical AI use into BPM education. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Fungal frontiers for sustainability: unlocking the hidden kingdom
abstract: Fungi have repeatedly delivered transformative advances across industries, from medicine to food to materials, yet these breakthroughs have emerged from a narrow base of organisms and well-studied systems. Although mycology has taken a big leap forward in the past decades because of advances in genomics, multi-omics, engineering, phenotyping and environmental monitoring, much fungal diversity remains taxonomically and functionally under-characterised, and many sustainability-relevant innovations remain limited by lack of investment, sparse infrastructure, and fragmented governance. We now have technologies that make previously inaccessible fungal questions tractable, which can help unlock the next generation of fungal breakthroughs. Informed by a workshop held in December 2025 that convened 20 leading experts across fungal disciplines, here we lay out key bottlenecks to fungal research and innovation through three lenses: functional mycology, human and institutional capacity, and governance. We identify selected sustainability-relevant fungal frontiers and use these to surface the recurrent gaps that cut across domains. We propose four elements of coordinated action across research and development, governance, and advocacy that could contribute to unlocking the full potential of fungi for sustainability transitions. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Research on the Application Scenarios and Implementation Strategies of all-Round Digital
abstract: The growing digitalization trend in the industries compels business organizations to put in place holistic strategies that may be in the form of integrating technology, optimization of operations, and long-term value generation. The paper presents the uses cases and implementation strategy of all-round digital transformation with particular emphasis on its application to various business and service scenarios. A new approach, Intelligent Multi-Layer Orchestration Model (IMLOM), is introduced to the successful planning and implementation. MLOM comprises three layers architecture: Perception Layer collects and reconciles data across sources in the environment and market systems context; Cognition Layer makes use of advanced analytics and machine learning to identify trends, predict problems and generate scenario-specific intelligence; and Execution Layer implements ideal strategies automatically by using rule-based and AI-driven decision engines. This architecture has the benefit of organizations responding easily to increased requisitions because resources are synchronized effectively and there is also consistency in service delivery. The following paper will cover some of the spheres of implementation, such as intelligent manufacturing, smart grid operations, digital financial services, and modernization of public services, and will present plans to implement it in stages, taking both the cost of technology and the prospect of successful performance into consideration. This would provide a cross-sector framework that is scalable and can enjoy the benefits of holistic digital capability to ensure flexibility in reacting to the hidden innovations of the future. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Natural Language Querying for Large Declarative Rule Repositories
abstract: In organizations, business processes are constrained by a large number of business rules that can, for example, be represented as process models, declarative constraints, or textual descriptions. When executing, auditing, or managing these processes, users may face specific questions that can only be answered by the declarative business rules that apply in this exact scenario. Non-technical users may only be able to specify their requirements in natural language queries, which need to be answered by specific business rules. However, the efficient matching between the natural language user query and the appropriate declarative business rules is not trivial because rules should be identified based on semantic similarity to the query, which may include synonyms and domain-specific technical terms. In this paper, we propose a system design that combines state-of-the-art technologies, namely Large Language Models, Vector Databases, and Retrieval Augmented Generation, to support cost-efficient natural language querying on large declarative rule repositories to identify appropriate rules. We provide a prototypical implementation of the system design and evaluate it on a large real-world declarative rule repository, showing the technical feasibility of the approach. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Organizational Memory for Agentic Business Process Execution
abstract: LLM-based agents offer new opportunities for automating business process execution beyond the limits of rule-based systems. However, general-purpose LLMs lack the organization-specific knowledge required for reliable execution, which is typically fragmented across human-oriented artifacts such as policies, process models, and standard operating procedures. While such knowledge can technically be encoded in individual prompts or agent-specific retrieval setups, this approach does not scale in enterprises, as it gives rise to knowledge silos and rule duplicates, and makes consistent updates and learning across agents difficult. We argue that this calls for an organizational memory for agentic business process execution: a shared, governed, and agent-consumable reference layer of evolving organization-specific procedural knowledge about how work should be executed. We derive requirements for such a memory, propose an architecture for its curation and consumption, and demonstrate its effectiveness in a proof-of-concept based on a procurement scenario. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Fuel blending impact on decarbonizing cold energy for district cooling and data centers
abstract: Fuel blends are seen as a transitional strategy for decarbonising combustion-based energy conversion processes while retaining dispatchable service for electricity-critical cooling loads. This paper presents a 0-dimensional model for fuel-mixing integrated into a mixed-integer linear optimisation framework for both designing and operating a district cooling plant to meet a data center load. The model considers the Lower Heating Value, delivered cost and comprehensively the upstream carbon intensity of methane-hydrogen blends. It covers the on-site cogeneration, electrically and thermally driven types of chillers, photovoltaic generation and thermal storage. The hypothesis is that the system-level decarbonization performance is affected more by hydrogen production cost and carbon intensity than by the volumetric blend share. A 20 % hydrogen volumetric part is equal to only 7 % chemical-energy substitution. Therefore, it limits the direct point-of-use carbon-dioxide reduction to the same magnitude. As a matter of fact, a full substitution by green hydrogen reduces specific emissions by 46.4 % while it increases the levelised cold energy cost by 37.1 % due its high production cost shifts operation towards grid electricity. Yet, biomass-derived hydrogen reduces specific emissions by 96.5 % under the assumption of biomass carbon neutrality and lowers the levelised cold energy cost by 8.5 %. Moreover, in the case of brown hydrogen specific emissions increase by 124.4 %. The results show demonstrate that volumetric blending targets alone do not guarantee decarbonisation within the considered deterministic prices and emission factors. Certification of upstream hydrogen is crucial for a comprehensive carbon avoidance cost assessment for fuel-specific economic screening. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Silent Responsibility Voids: Evidence for Process Twins in Clinical Trials
abstract: Responsible Business Process Management (RBPM) and process mining have matured as independent research streams, yet their integration on real operational data remains rare, particularly in clinical research, where responsibility obligations are most consequential. This study investigates the protocol deviation management process of Clinical Research Centers (CRCs) using an event log of 13,331 deviation cases from an operational clinical trial management system, complemented by a formative expert evaluation with specialists from contrasting roles and regulatory contexts. Applying process discovery, conformance, and performance analysis, it finds that the most critical responsibility tensions surface less in what the process records than in what it fails to record. We introduce the concept of Silent Responsibility Voids (SRVs): points where the operationalization of an RBPM principle leaves no auditable trace, manifesting as absence, systematic incompleteness, or ceremonial recording. In the studied data, corrective action is documented in 0.1% of cases, regulatory notifications are largely absent, and the typical deviation is registered a median of 153 days after it occurred. We argue that such voids are detectable only by a technology that carries the normative expectation of the process, and use them to specify the monitoring functions a Responsible Digital Process Twin would require. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: OpenGATE-based gamma response mapping of a lead-collimated multi-range GM detector array for nuclear technical waste screening
abstract: Rapid screening of mixed nuclear technical waste requires a radiation measurement layer that can provide both conservative risk estimation and region-level spatial information. This study proposes an OpenGATE/Geant4-based gamma response mapping framework for a 10 × 10 planar multi-range Geiger–Mueller detector array with a lead-grid coarse collimation structure. The simulated photon-transport response is converted into a simulation-normalized dose-rate score map through a statistical multi-range GM fusion model considering dead-time correction, valid-range weighting, and counting uncertainty. The framework was evaluated using particle-number convergence, lead-grid parameter analysis, measurement-time assessment, source-position and shielding response tests, known-level screening validation, independent randomized validation, and robotic sorting priority experiments. The lead grid reduced the neighbor-8/peak crosstalk ratio from 1.905 without lead to 1.075 for the 10 mm/40 mm configuration, with a 57.4% reduction in total counts. A 5 s acquisition achieved a repeated-postprocessing coefficient of variation of approximately 1.85%. The independent randomized validation achieved 96.0% accuracy with no dangerous underestimation. In 50 randomized waste-bag scenarios, the first selected item was an L3 or L4 source in 49/50 cases, with an average top-3 high-risk recall of 0.940. The reported values are simulation-normalized screening scores rather than calibrated ambient dose-equivalent rates; standard-source calibration and prototype validation are required before absolute dose-rate interpretation. title: Simulating the Domain Expert: An Empirical Evaluation of LLM-Based Interview Training for Business Process Modeling
abstract: Business process discovery relies heavily on stakeholder interviews, yet practicing this skill in educational settings is constrained by limited access to domain experts. This paper empirically evaluates whether LLM-based conversational agents, configured to simulate non-technical domain experts, can effectively support the training of business process elicitation and BPMN modeling skills by providing opportunities for structured practice before engaging with human experts. We conducted a counterbalanced within-subjects pilot experiment with eight Computer Science students, who each interviewed both an LLM-based domain expert and a human expert on two different business process scenarios and subsequently produced a BPMN model. Results show that LLM-based sessions were substantially faster (mean 33.4 vs. 59.5 min), perceived as equally informative, and produced models of comparable quality. Both conditions generated distinct but condition-specific error patterns, which varied across process complexity and gateway type. These findings suggest that LLM-simulated domain experts are a useful training tool for BPM education, supporting repeated practice where expert availability is limited. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.
