title: “The System Did It”: Bias, Opacity, and the Misalignment of Ethical Mitigations in (Robotic) Process Automation
abstract: Robotic Process Automation (RPA) and Agentic AI are reshaping business processes, but their ethical governance lags behind deployment. Based on a scoping review of 29 papers that establishes the general, cross-sector landscape of ethical issues and mitigation strategies, and a municipal focus group that serves as an example case why these generally proposed mitigations fail in practice, we identify five recurring ethical issues (loss of autonomy, opacity, bias, responsibility diffusion, privacy) and four mitigation strategies (human-in-the-loop, audit logs, explainable interfaces, impact assessments). Loss of autonomy is the most-cited concern (62%), yet it attracts the least targeted mitigation, while algorithmic bias (14%) commands the most. The focus group confirms this asymmetry and reveals that even well-understood mitigations depend on organizational resources, governance maturity, and cross-departmental collaboration, factors that the literature fails to explore. The result is a framework of socio-technical governance mechanisms that translates abstract ethical principles into actionable guidance for responsible process automation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Business model, pricing, and transparency in neurosurgery and neurology journals
abstract: The business model of scientific journals — gold open access (OA), hybrid, or subscription — creates different financial incentives for publishers, since in the author-pays OA model publication fees (Article Processing Charges, APCs) are collected upon acceptance. This descriptive audit surveys 109 neurosurgery and neurology journals from six major publishing groups (Elsevier, Springer Nature/Wolters Kluwer, Wiley, SAGE, Taylor & Francis, Thieme) and verifies, journal by journal, business model, notoriety indicator (Journal Impact Factor or Scimago SJR), publication fee, and, where publicly available, acceptance rate. Every data point was individually re-verified against official publisher pages and Scimago Journal Rank, correcting a JIF/SJR confusion, several unrecorded transitions to full OA, and one misclassified business model present in the initial collection. After verification, 83 journals (76.1%) are hybrid and 26 (23.9%) are full OA, including 5 diamond (no-APC) journals; no journal is subscription-only. Mean notoriety was similar between hybrid and full-OA journals on both indicators tested separately (JIF: 3.51 vs 3.61; SJR: 0.87 vs 0.89), but full-OA journals excluding the five diamond titles showed higher and more dispersed SJR values (mean 1.24, SD 0.93) than the diamond subset (mean 0.20, SD 0.09). Publication fees were, on average, higher for the OA option of hybrid journals ($4,279, SD $755) than for full-OA journals ($3,415, SD $845). Acceptance rate was the least transparent variable: only 6 of 109 journals (5.5%) publish an identifiable rate, all hybrid; no full-OA or diamond journal discloses this figure. This sample is too small, and too skewed toward hybrid disclosure, to support any inference about whether business model influences acceptance decisions; it instead documents a broad lack of acceptance-rate transparency across neurosurgery and neurology journals and identifies pricing, not acceptance behavior, as the dimension on which a verified between-model difference could be established. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: “Are BPM Graduates Future-Ready?” Reframing BPM Competencies for the Future-of-Work
abstract: Business Process Management (BPM) is at the forefront of digital transformation, yet it remains an open question whether BPM graduates are equipped for this role. This study conducts a thematic discourse analysis to examine how BPM competencies are discursively constructed in academic literature and how they align with emerging skill demands in the World Economic Forum (WEF)’s Future of Jobs reports published between 2016 and 2025. The analysis shows that BPM competency is progressively framed as a hybrid profile spanning process, digital, analytical, social, and adaptive domains, with process and analytical capabilities dominating. This profile is broadly congruent with future-of-work skill projections. In contrast, social, adaptive, and sustainability-related competencies are less strongly foregrounded, despite their growing importance in future-of-work narratives. The study contributes a competency-skill alignment matrix and argues that BPM’s challenge is not a lack of relevant competencies, but uneven emphasis on how they are taught, assessed, or resourced. For educators, the key task is to identify ways to orchestrate BPM curricula that integrate process foundations with digital fluency, learning agility, social capability, and transformational leadership competencies, which are increasingly central to the digital transformation of work environments. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Learning Process Modelling in BPMN Through Real-Life Process Observation
abstract: Process modelling education increasingly emphasizes authentic practice, yet limited research examines how students themselves describe moving from observed business reality to formal BPMN models. This paper analyzes semi-structured learning diaries from three course implementations at two universities, covering 94 diaries from 108 enrolled students. Across the implementations, students completed observation-grounded group modelling assignments and reflective diaries; the first implementation also included AS-IS to TO-BE redesign, while the third explicitly asked about Generative AI. Using a researcher-led qualitative thematic analysis supported by iterative cross-cohort comparison, the study identifies recurring themes in process identification, BPMN learning, collaboration, presentation, transfer, and bounded AI use. The findings show that students experienced process modelling as an interpretive, socially negotiated, and increasingly transferable competence rather than as diagram drawing alone. The paper contributes an observation-to-model instructional case and demonstrates the value of learning diaries as both pedagogical and research instruments for BPM education research and practice. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The duty to rescue at sea and Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS): Implementation under the IMO MASS code
abstract: Under the international legal framework governing Search and Rescue (SAR) at sea, flag states are required to ensure that ships flying their flag render assistance to persons in distress, while coastal states must establish and coordinate adequate SAR services within their areas of responsibility. Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) pose challenges for ensuring compliance with rescue obligations due to difficulties in designating a master and limited embarkation and accommodation capabilities. This paper argues that autonomy does not justify an exemption from, or relief from, the duty to rescue. Against this background, the article examines how Chapter 21 (SAR) of the International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS Code) translates the duty to rescue for MASS into a goal-based structure comprising goals, functional requirements, and expected performance, aligned with SOLAS. It further delineates the respective implementation responsibilities of flag states and coastal states, with a view to ensuring that MASS can render effective assistance to persons in distress at sea. On the one hand, flag states should implement Chapter 21 by survey, certification, and approval processes and oversee compliance through classification societies. On the other hand, coastal states must integrate MASS into SAR coordination arrangements and fulfil their obligation to coordinate the disembarkation of survivors to a “place of safety,” thereby completing the ship-side rescue duty upon delivery. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Theoretical Foundations of Developing a «Qoloner» Handicraft Website
abstract: This study examines the theoretical and practical foundations of developing a handicraft-oriented web platform using the QolOner project as a case study. The research analyzes modern web development technologies and presents a comparative evaluation of traditional web technologies, content management systems, JavaScript frameworks, and cross-platform solutions. A survey involving 40 respondents, including university students and young IT specialists, was conducted to identify preferences and key factors influencing technology selection for web development. The findings indicate that Flutter and Firebase are perceived as reliable and contemporary technologies for developing and maintaining multifunctional web platforms. The use of Firebase eliminates the need for a dedicated server, reduces infrastructure costs, and enables rapid content updates, while built-in analytics support data-driven improvements. Flutter’s Hot Reload functionality significantly accelerates the development process and enhances interface quality across devices. The proposed system architecture is modular and scalable, ensuring clear separation of user and administrative roles and secure content management. The results demonstrate that the proposed technological stack is effective not only for mobile applications but also for fully functional, interactive web platforms. The study confirms that handicraft-oriented web systems can contribute to cultural heritage preservation, digital promotion, and small business development. #CSOC1120 © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Industrial Digital Twin-driven generation of blockchain-based Digital Product Passports for trustworthy product lifecycle management
abstract: The integration of Digital Twins (DTs), blockchain, and Digital Product Passports (DPPs) is emerging as a promising direction for trustworthy, auditable, and interoperable industrial lifecycle management. However, an open issue is how heterogeneous lifecycle evidence generated by DTs from physical and industrial-system observations can be transformed into DPP-consumable claims while preserving provenance, integrity, temporal validity, and manageable certification costs. This paper proposes a framework for DPP-oriented dynamic certification of industrial DTs in distributed industrial environments. The proposed architecture connects physical assets, DT instances, off-chain evidence repositories, permissioned blockchain anchoring, and DPP interfaces. DTs derive structured lifecycle evidence from physical and industrial-system observations concerning products, components, materials, processes, and facilities; blockchain mechanisms provide tamper-evident anchoring through hashes, timestamps, signatures, and Merkle roots; and DPPs expose selected certified claims to authorized stakeholders. A parameterized discrete-event simulation evaluates DPP update policies, certification granularity, blockchain anchoring strategies, hierarchical lifecycle aggregation, and networked certification under heterogeneous IIoT and edge–cloud conditions. The results show that technical blockchain commit success alone is not sufficient to assess DPP feasibility: freshness lag, lifecycle coverage, on-chain payload, and energy cost must also be considered. Overall, the evaluation confirms that hybrid certification strategies can support scalable DT–Blockchain–DPP infrastructures by combining direct compact anchoring for critical lifecycle evidence with periodic, hierarchical, or Merkle-based aggregation for routine updates. title: AI Work Under Guardrails: Task Framing for Responsible Delegation in BPM
abstract: Enterprise AI governance can define principles for accountability, transparency, human oversight, and auditability, but organizations still need to translate these principles into concrete decisions about whether and under what constraints a specific unit of process work may be delegated to artificial intelligence (AI). This research-in-progress paper introduces the Responsibility-Gated Task Frame as a design science artifact for this translation. The artifact extends a descriptive Task Frame with responsibility conditions and supports a task-level decision on the form and constraints of AI-supported delegation. Following a design science research approach, the paper presents the artifact as part of an early design cycle and demonstrates its use through a vignette on AI-assisted compliance assessment based on International Organization for Standardization (ISO) management-system standards. The contribution is a task-level mechanism for operationalizing Responsible Business Process Management (RBPM) and AI governance before AI implementation begins. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Data-driven construction of asymmetric fuzzy numbers via entropy-based shape calibration
abstract: In most fuzzy number families the membership-function shape is selected a priori by the decision maker, and the learned or adaptive approaches that infer it from data do so by optimising a task loss rather than through a closed-form link to the information content of the evidence. This arbitrariness distorts uncertainty representation and precludes principled comparison across families. This paper addresses this shape-selection problem by introducing the data-driven Entropy Calibrated Asymmetric Fuzzy Number (ECAFN), which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first fuzzy number whose left and right transition functions are calibrated in closed form from the Shannon entropies of the supporting evidence within a power-law L-R framework, and which can replace manual membership specification in Mamdani or Takagi Sugeno Kang (TSK) inference systems. Two theoretical results are established within the power-law family: an entropy-matching constraint uniquely determines the shape exponent for the admissible entropy range, and a uniqueness characterisation of the entropy-to-shape calibration map satisfying parabolic and triangular limit conditions and a constant proportional decay rate property. Generalization of standard families (triangular, trapezoidal, exponential, and parabolic) arise as special or limiting cases, the Gaussian is subsumed in a curvature-magnitude sense. A scalar Fuzzy Information Number (FIN) is proposed for cross-family comparison of informativeness, and an ablation study confirms robustness to the method’s hyperparameters. The framework is validated on three benchmarks structural health monitoring, multi-sensor altitude fusion and Basel-III credit-risk modelling. An extended comparative analysis positions ECAFN against recent (2020–2026) families including Fermatean, T-spherical, probabilistic linguistic fuzzy numbers, and Z-numbers. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Enhancing IT Incident Management Through BPM and ITIL V4 Integration: A Case Study in the Automotive Sector
abstract: In the context of Industry 4.0, the automotive sector faces significant challenges in maintaining service continuity due to the increasing volume of IT incidents and the lack of formalized management processes. This study aims to optimize incident management in a Peruvian automotive dealership by proposing and validating an integrated model that combines Business Process Management (BPM) with ITIL V4 practices. A pre-experimental design was applied following a structured approach based on the five phases of the ITIL service value chain: Engage, Improve, Design and Transition, Obtain/Build, and Deliver and Support. The intervention involved deploying workflows redesigned using BPMN 2.0 and a dynamic prioritization matrix. Effectiveness was evaluated through a quantitative analysis of 22 daily observations, validated using Student’s t-test. The implementation yielded highly statistically significant improvements. The daily average of incidents exceeding the Service Level Agreement (SLA) decreased drastically from 6.22 to 1.72 (t = 5.790, p < 0.001), and the timely attention compliance rate increased from 74.73% to 92.14% (t = − 5.950, p < 0.001). Likewise, the load of open incidents (backlog) was significantly reduced from 29.73% to 18.82% (p < 0.05). The integration of formal diagnostic subprocesses and automated prioritization strategies proves to be an effective mechanism to reduce response times and ensure business value in automotive sector operational environments. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Digital Transformation for Sustainable Business
abstract: Digital transformation has become a key enabler of sustainable business by integrating advanced technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), Big Data Analytics (BDA), and Cloud Computing (CC) into organizational processes. These technologies improve operational efficiency while supporting environmental sustainability through enhanced Resource Optimization (RO), Energy Efficiency (EE), and data-driven decision-making. Despite significant progress in this area, existing studies primarily focus on individual technological or sustainability aspects and often lack a unified framework for jointly evaluating digital maturity and sustainability performance. To address this gap, this paper proposes an integrated quantitative framework that combines the Digital Transformation Index (DTI), Sustainability Performance (SP), and an optimization-based performance function within a single analytical model. The proposed framework enables the simultaneous assessment of digital capability and sustainability outcomes while incorporating environmental constraints into the evaluation process. Simulation-based analysis demonstrates that organizations with higher DTI values consistently achieve improved SP and Overall Performance (OP). Moreover, the optimization mechanism effectively satisfies carbon emission constraints while maintaining high organizational performance, confirming the robustness and applicability of the proposed framework. The results highlight the positive relationship between digital transformation and sustainable business performance, demonstrating that strategic adoption of digital technologies enhances operational efficiency, strengthens competitiveness, improves stakeholder engagement, and supports responsible production and consumption practices. Overall, the proposed framework provides a scalable and systematic approach for evaluating sustainable digital transformation and offers practical guidance for organizations seeking to align technological innovation with long-term sustainability objectives. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Designing stateful enterprise control for budget commitments: Identity continuity, context-bound transitions, and controlled execution
abstract: Enterprise information systems manage business objects with persistent control states across transactions and changing organizations, posing a stateful enterprise control problem that requires consistent alignment of object identity, valid state transitions, execution authority, and audit evidence over time. This study establishes design knowledge for such scenarios, focusing on budget commitments. Using design science research, it proposes three technology-independent principles: Commitment Identity Binding, Context-Bound State Transition, and Controlled Execution Boundary and Evidence. These principles are implemented in a three-layer artifact combining a Knowledge Graph (KG), a state-transition module (SAI), and an audit evidence generation module (AIG) for context representation, state control, and structured evidence generation. Evaluated on 18 months of enterprise data, expert cases, ablation tests, historical replay, safety checks, and experiments with 30 practitioners, the artifact yields key findings: state consistency does not guarantee evidential completeness, and accurate rule identification cannot ensure valid transitions without temporal context. Historical Replay successfully replicated all 90 test cases under original contexts. When substantive information was held comparable, structured evidence improved final-state and rule-basis judgments and reduced review time. This work provides integrated design knowledge for stateful enterprise control over persistent business objects. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Adaptive BPM Learning Journeys: An AI-Powered Platform for Personalized Assessment and Multimodal Content Generation
abstract: BPM is taught across heterogeneous audiences ranging from university students to working professionals, who differ substantially in prior knowledge, learning pace, and goals. Traditional one-size-fits-all instructional approaches struggle to accommodate this diversity, often resulting in disengagement and uneven skill acquisition. We present an AI-powered platform for adaptive BPM learning journeys that relocates instructional effort from authoring fixed training modules to curating a shared knowledge base, from which personalized multimodal content and assessments are generated on demand. The platform integrates three pillars: personalization to each learner’s prior knowledge and preferred representations of information, automation of instructional design through an LLM-driven generation pipeline, and gamification elements that sustain long-term engagement. Together, these pillars constitute a five-phase adaptive learning journey. We describe the platform’s architecture, the pedagogical rationale behind the shift from authoring to curating, and its implications for developing the People capability of BPM at scale. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: AI and the Evolving BPM Practitioner Skill Set. Initial Implications for Curriculum Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly reshaping the Business Process Management (BPM) practice, generating new requirements for BPM education and curriculum design. This study examines how AI-driven transformation affects BPM curricula by identifying which competencies remain adequate, which require reinterpretation in an AI-in-the-loop context, and which represent entirely new skill demands. The study applies a three-step structured mapping approach. First, the AI capabilities of 17 established BPM platforms are coded through structured feature analysis across 30 BPM capability areas. Second, these codings are aggregated to characterize how AI tools collectively support each capability area. Third, the analysis evaluates practitioner implications by distinguishing direct AI impacts, indirect effects emerging from related capability areas, and sub-tasks that may no longer require manual training. Results indicate that AI reshapes competency requirements across all BPM capability areas and introduces six new competency demands not captured in existing BPM frameworks. These findings reveal a module-level curriculum gap and provide a foundation for updating existing BPM curricula as well as informing the design of new programs. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Simple repair policies and decompositions for semi-coherent systems with simultaneous failures
abstract: We consider semi-coherent binary systems that are subject to simultaneous failures of its components. These are systems whose components can be either working or failed; the system can also be working or failed depending on the state of the components; and repairing a component cannot cause the system to fail. We consider that one or more components can fail simultaneously, allowing us to model external shocks and disasters. For this, we use the Lévy-frailty Marshall–Olkin (LFMO) multivariate distribution to model the failure times of the components. We aim to answer in which states of the system we should repair the components. This is a challenging question, as the number of repair policies grows super-exponentially in the number of components. To tackle this, we propose a simple family of repair policies, which we call r- out-of- n repair policies , where one repairs all failed components when the system fails or when there are r or more failed components. Our main contribution is that we derive exact and simple expressions for key performance-evaluation quantities of the system operating under our proposed repair policies. That is, we give explicit expressions for the mean time-to-failure of the system, mean time-to-repair, probability of system-failure before repair, and component- and system-repair rate. We also give expressions for the expected cost and long-term average cost, when there are components’ and system repair cost. The only relevant parameters involved in the derived expressions are the structural signature of the system, and the Laplace exponent associated to the LFMO distribution. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Entropy-guided circuit breakers for LLM-augmented intrusion detection: An empirical evaluation of uncertainty-routed cascades in LLMOps
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in security pipelines, but calling them on every input is costly and their reasoning can fail silently. We study an uncertainty-routed cascade for intrusion detection: a Random Forest (RF) classifies each network flow and forwards only low-confidence flows to an LLM, while an entropy-guided circuit breaker monitors token entropy during generation and falls back to the RF when entropy is high. We evaluate it on CIC-IDS2017, CICIoT2023 and NSL-KDD with four instruction-tuned models (Qwen2.5, 0.5B to 14B parameters), using 1200 test flows per model. The RF routes only 0.28%–9.48% of flows to the LLM. On routed flows, LLM accuracy rises with model size from 52.3% to 71.3%, against 56.5% for the RF, and the 14B cascade raises NSL-KDD accuracy from 78.7% to 81.1%. Token entropy, however, is a weak signal of wrong answers: its area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) is 0.51–0.56 early in generation. A threshold calibrated on training flows tripped on every routed flow, saving 88%–95% of the generated tokens, but only 5%–10% once prompt tokens are counted, and discarding the accuracy gains of the larger models. Thresholds tuned on the test set gained at most 2.7 points over a random breaker. Self-consistency with five sampled answers did not help either. Retrieval-only baselines show that the LLM’s advantage is largest where the test distribution has shifted. Routing by classifier confidence is effective; token entropy alone is not a reliable runtime control signal in LLMOps pipelines. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: LLM-Based Orchestration of Business Process Management Toolchains
abstract: There is a tradition in business process management research not only to develop theoretical concepts and powerful algorithms, but also to engineer research prototypes to showcase the contributions. These tools are typically developed in isolation and are rarely designed to interoperate. As a result, researchers and practitioners need to manually combine multiple tools to construct toolchains that address their specific needs, limiting the practical usability and reuse of existing prototypes. In this paper, we propose the PRAXIS (Process Research Artifact eXecution and Integration System) framework that leverages large language models as a natural language interface for practitioners to compose and execute process management toolchains. For a specific user question, the system automatically orchestrates and executes the respective BPM research tools. The framework is prototypically implemented based on state-of-the-art techniques to integrate several existing BPM research tools. We provide an evaluation methodology that generates test cases for a given set of tools to test the framework. The application of the evaluation methodology shows the usefulness of our framework. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Deployment-Sovereign AI Infrastructure for BPM Education: An Open-Source Stack from Document Analysis to Process Execution
abstract: This paper investigates whether deployment-sovereign AI infrastructure can support BPM education without dependence on commercial LLM APIs. We assembled an open-source teaching stack combining PCSS-hosted open-weight models, Flowise/Qdrant retrieval-augmented generation, n8n workflow orchestration, and the CIB Seven BPMN engine. We evaluated 68 BPM prompts across 13 models and three deployment classes, logging 2,248 model calls including a dedicated reliability re-run. The stack was piloted with about 110 participants across three university programmes. Commercial endpoints exhibited provider-specific availability failures and content-policy refusals, most visibly Claude 3.5 Haiku on selected healthcare, chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN), substance-destruction, and self-harm documentation prompts. In the tested PCSS deployment, all five open-weight models completed the high-sensitivity corpus without API errors or policy refusals. A preliminary, non-blinded expert assessment found no obvious quality deficit for routine BPM documentation tasks, but does not establish statistical equivalence to commercial models. We refine pedagogical sovereignty as institutional control over AI cost, availability, content policy, and data jurisdiction. The architecture is replicable at zero marginal licensing cost via national or EuroHPC resources, subject to allocation, configuration effort, and governance requirements. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Differentially Private HeuristicsMiner
abstract: Process discovery aims at extracting process models from prior recordings of process executions stored in information systems, called event logs. These process models may reveal sensitive information about unique traces and about the process stakeholders. Although a differentially private process discovery algorithm exists, it does not lend itself well to handling noisy event logs. This paper proposes the Differentially Private Heuristics Miner (DPHM), an algorithm that considers Differential Privacy at the discovery step while handling noise efficiently. We provide proof of the property of Differential Privacy and evaluated our approach on four real-world event logs against three other process discovery algorithms. The evaluation results indicate that unique traces can be protected with a slight loss of utility. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Towards Ethics into BPM Research Through Ethical Dilemmas Assessment
abstract: Business Process Management (BPM) research increasingly influences organizational decision-making, automation, and human work practices, raising important ethical concerns about fairness, transparency, privacy, accountability, and societal impact. Despite their growing importance, ethical aspects are often addressed only implicitly or considered in isolated stages of BPM research projects. In this paper, we argue that ethics should be integrated throughout the BPM research lifecycle. To support this goal, we propose a framework that identifies potential ethical dilemmas at different research stages, and outlines possible strategies to address them. The framework is grounded in perspectives from Philosophy and Information Systems ethics, emphasizing the socio-technical implications of BPM technologies and methods. We demonstrate its applicability through an analysis of three papers published at the BPM 2025 conference, selected as representative cases of BPM research projects. The analysis illustrates recurring ethical gaps and highlights the need for more structured ethical reflection during the design, development, evaluation, and deployment of BPM solutions. The paper contributes a practical and reflective instrument for supporting ethically aware BPM research and provides initial directions for strengthening the role of ethics within the BPM community. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Ferric iron availability and species identity jointly shape the metabolic profiles and spoilage potentials of grass carp spoilage bacteria: A combined metabolomic and physicochemical evaluation
abstract: Ferric iron is essential for bacterial growth and spoilage-associated phenotypes, yet its specific influences on the metabolism and spoilage potential of fish spoilage bacteria remain unclear. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the metabolic and spoilage potential changes of grass carp spoilage bacteria under varying ferric iron accessibilities, using combined metabolomic and physicochemical detection. The results showed that high ferric iron accessibility stimulated bacterial carbohydrate metabolism (glycolysis and tricarboxylic acid cycle) and fatty acid β-oxidation. Conversely, the low-ferric-mimicking condition partly hindered carbohydrate degradation and enhanced amino acid catabolism, evidenced by the increase in ammonia and a significant 29% decrease in glutamate level. As for spoilage potential, bacteria increased the accumulation of trichloroacetic acid (TCA)-soluble peptides (up to 2.17 μmol tyrosine/g) and biogenic amines (with histamine contents up to 19.32–30.04 mg/kg) under the low-ferric-mimicking condition, owing to possibly increased protease secretion, elevated siderophore synthesis, and decreased amine oxidase activity. Besides, the tested bacteria exhibited different characteristics, such as the potent activity of Pseudomonas putida in utilizing amino acids and carbohydrates, the high capacity of Shewanella putrefaciens in producing putrescine, cadaverine, and histamine, and the strong potential of Shewanella putrefaciens in degrading purine-related compounds. Taken together, this study revealed ferric-dependent metabolic and spoilage potential changes of grass carp bacteria, indicated the potential risk of ferric iron depletion on fish quality preservation, and thereby inspired the development of iron-based preservation strategies for aquatic products. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Agent Behavior Mining: Generative AI Agent Governance in Business Processes
abstract: As organizations increasingly deploy generative AI agents to automate business processes, they face a governance dilemma: although these agents can increase operational flexibility, their non-deterministic nature challenges the control and standardization that Business Process Management seeks to enforce. This paper addresses this invisible autonomy risk by introducing Agent Behavior Mining, a governance capability that enables the application of process mining techniques to render generative AI agent decision-making observable and traceable. We (1) improve the understanding of generative AI agent behavior through an event data model that translates granular agent activities–including reasoning traces, tool usage, and token costs–into standardized process logs; (2) instantiate the data model in a multi-agent order-to-cash implementation, demonstrating how process managers can leverage agent logs to detect policy deviations and quantify operational variability; and (3) evaluate the perceived practical utility of the approach in an exploratory study with 18 industry practitioners. The results indicate that practitioners view behavioral transparency as a prerequisite for trust and consider the ability to examine agent reasoning as an important governance requirement for the next generation of AI-driven business processes. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Beyond landlockedness: transit structure, infrastructure, and the geography of trade costs
abstract: This paper examines how geographic disadvantage and infrastructure shape bilateral trade flows, with a particular focus on landlocked countries. Using a global panel dataset covering 2007–2019, the paper moves beyond the conventional binary classification of landlockedness by decomposing the geographic disadvantage into coastal accessibility and transit structure. The empirical strategy combines an augmented gravity model with the Hausman–Taylor estimator to address endogeneity while retaining time-invariant geographic variables, and is complemented by Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood (PPML) estimation and extensive-margin analysis to account for zero trade flows, heteroskedasticity, and trade participation. The results yield three main findings. First, infrastructure plays a central role in facilitating trade, with improvements in logistics performance significantly increasing bilateral trade flows. Second, the negative effect of landlockedness is largely driven by coastal accessibility: once distance to the nearest coast is accounted for, the estimated penalty of being landlocked declines substantially. Third, and most importantly, the structure of transit access matters. Landlocked countries that depend on a single coastal neighbor experience significantly lower trade, highlighting the importance of competition among transit routes. The findings are robust across alternative estimators, including fixed effects, Hausman–Taylor, PPML, and extensive-margin models. These findings suggest that the disadvantages faced by landlocked countries are multidimensional, reflecting not only geography and infrastructure but also regional political economy. Policies aimed at improving trade integration should therefore focus on enhancing infrastructure, strengthening regional cooperation, and alleviating the trade costs associated with limited transit options © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Temporal organization of negative affect shapes reciprocal feedback with psychotic-like experiences in daily life
abstract: Background Negative affect and psychotic-like experiences (PLEs) reinforce each other in daily life, but which temporal properties of negative affect differ between individuals with PLEs and controls and shape this coupling is unknown. Methods 201 adults (99 with PLEs, 102 controls) completed 7-day experience sampling. Person-level mean negative affect, variability (SD), lability (RMSSD, MASD), and inertia were compared between groups, adjusting for mean negative affect. In participants with PLEs, lagged multilevel models tested whether these indices moderated reciprocal negative affect–PLEs associations, joint models separated amplitude from temporal dependency, and a continuous-time simulation quantified the moderation expected from persistence alone. Results Participants with PLEs showed larger fluctuations of negative affect beyond its higher mean level (adjusted d = 0.63–0.80), whereas their higher inertia depended on mean negative affect. Within participants with PLEs, only inertia moderated the lagged associations: coupling was absent at low and substantial at high inertia. Lability effects reflected its inverse relation to inertia and vanished once inertia was accounted for. Persistence alone accounted for the moderation of the PLEs-to-negative-affect effect and about half of the reverse effect, which operated through carry-over. Limitations Observational design; young, predominantly female, non-clinical sample; inertia estimated from one week with low split-half reliability. Conclusion Between persons, PLEs are associated mainly with the amplitude of negative affect fluctuations; within persons, the persistence of negative affect, not its intensity or amplitude, tracks the strength of its coupling with PLEs. Studies of affective dynamics along the psychosis continuum should therefore distinguish amplitude from persistence. © 2026 The Authors.

title: The Process Canvas
abstract: Business processes as organisational assets need to be evaluated from integrated viewpoints that go far beyond the common operational view of being an executable, efficient process. Established BPM artefacts, however, do not support a comprehensive, multi-dimensional process description on a strategic level. This disconnect motivated the development of the Process Canvas, which allows describing the feasibility, viability, desirability and responsibility of a business process. Developed using Design Science Research, the Process Canvas integrates these four views in a new artefact and, with this, facilitates a previously not supported comprehensive assessment and contextualisation of a process. Its application in three semi-naturalistic and two naturalistic cases exemplifies its applicability and utility, and demonstrates its analytical and explanatory capability. This is further confirmed by a survey with 32 process experts. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: An EOQ model with green degree and population size sensitive demand under pentagonal intuitionistic cloudy fuzzy environment
abstract: This proposed study represents an EOQ (economic order quantity) model concerning the population size, which is an important factor in any inventory management system. Here, demand is assumed to be dependent on the selling price, the green level, and the size of the population. The holding cost is a time-dependent quadratic function. At the start of the cycle, the customers buy the items according to their choice. After a certain time, the deteriorated and overall less preferred items are sold to customers at a discount. In this period, demand may increase, decrease or remain unchanged. Some people will buy the items because of their low prices. However, some customers may not be interested in buying them, thinking that the items are very low-quality products. As a consequence, a study is proposed, developed and solved in a crisp environment. Then, the model is transformed into a fuzzy model by using a pentagonal intuitionistic cloudy fuzzy number. The carbon tax is included, and the development cost is used for preservation technologies for storing decaying items like vegetables, fruits, etc. The computer-based algorithm is used for the solution of the proposed study. At the end, graphical representation and sensitivity analysis are provided to check the applicability of the study. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: A mixed-integer linear programming approach to container terminal layout optimization: application to the port of Piraeus
abstract: This study addresses the issue of designing a container terminal layout by developing a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) mathematical model. The methodology is applied to Pier II of the Piraeus Container Terminal. The mathematical formulation of the problem systematically incorporates real-world spatial constraints and operational factors related to container storage areas, while evaluating alternative scenarios to identify optimal layouts. The methodology considers the geometric and functional characteristics of the terminal, including data related to container handling equipment and the movement of conventional trucks and Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs). The objective function aims to minimize the total operational distance from the berthing positions to the container stacking blocks, thereby enhancing terminal performance. The optimized truck-based configuration reduced the total internal transport distance by 23.1%, while the AGV-based configuration also reduced total internal transport distance by approximately 23% in relation to the existing layout, but it resulted in higher absolute travel distances compared to the truck-based optimal solution. Applying the proposed methodology to real data from the Port of Piraeus shows how alternative layouts can reduce internal transportation distances and enhance operational efficiency. A comparative analysis of alternative scenarios confirms the effectiveness of the proposed solutions, highlighting their potential to significantly improve operational efficiency, while also offering prospects for future research and practical applications. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Intelligent account takeover detection in single sign-on systems using behavioral and device login analytics
abstract: With changing times and digitalization in the field of information technology, Single Sign-On (SSO) mechanisms have become an important feature of identity management systems. SSO enables users to access numerous services with one set of login credentials, but it can increase risks like account takeover (ATO), affecting security and privacy. The research aims to use advanced statistical analysis and Machine Learning (ML) to improve authentication mechanisms and identify predictive features for risk-based authentication. The behavioral changes demonstrated by users after account takeover (ATO) incidents are also examined to design risk indicators. To achieve these objectives, this research utilized a large dataset of 33 million login attempts from 3.3 million users in Norway from February 2020 to February 2021. Using machine learning models evaluated with an 80:20 train-test validation strategy and complementary performance metrics, we observed that ASN, city, Round-trip time (RTT), device type, and login success were the key features for accurately identifying attackers, achieving 93% prediction accuracy. In addition, the login attempts were found to be maximum during typical office hours (9 AM, 12 PM, 3 PM, and 6 PM), where attackers may be trying to imitate themselves as normal users. The research findings will aid in the implementation of secure, user-friendly, and dependable authentication schemes that strengthen all aspects of digital identity management. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: A Case Study Into Factors of Intelligent Process Automation in Audit
abstract: Artificial Intelligence is changing the way process automation is implemented in practice. Intelligent Process Automation (IPA) integrates new AI capabilities, offering efficient mechanisms to automate tasks and overarching processes. Despite research on this topic, little is known about how organizations decide where to use which IPA capabilities and to what extent in order to mitigate potential negative effects. In this paper, we address this knowledge gap by conducting a case study with the FAA and their currently developed IPA for financial audit processes. We identify three major groups of factors and inductively derive corresponding propositions. Our research contributes empirical knowledge on design considerations organizations make to optimize the impact of AI and IPA. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Counterfactual Invariant Market Learning for Provincial Potato Price Forecasting in Agricultural Management
abstract: Potato prices are influenced by recurrent production cycles, storage behaviour, regional circulation, and short-term market disturbances, making their future movements difficult to infer from isolated historical trajectories. This paper develops the Counterfactual Invariant Market Forecaster (CIMF), a forecasting framework that formulates provincial potato price prediction as a mechanism-aware forecasting and model-based counterfactual analysis problem rather than a purely supervised temporal extrapolation task. CIMF first decomposes historical price windows into seasonal anchors and residual shocks, allowing the model to distinguish recurrent potato price rhythms from local abnormal fluctuations. It then learns invariant mechanism representations across heterogeneous environments, including years, seasonal phases, volatility regimes, and regional partitions. Based on these representations, a learned response operator is constructed to describe model-implied cross-provincial associations between residual shocks and future prices. A differentiable counterfactual intervention layer further enables shock removal, amplification, and delay analysis, so that the model can simulate how its forecasts for the future potato price panel change under different local disturbance scenarios. Experiments on weekly potato prices from 25 Chinese provinces during 2012 to 2018 show that CIMF achieves lower MAE, RMSE, and MAPE than CNN, LSTM, N-BEATS, Autoformer, and Informer at both one-step and four-step horizons. Ablation results confirm the contribution of seasonal residualization, invariant mechanism learning, and structural response modelling. These findings suggest that combining invariant mechanism learning with qualified, model-based counterfactual analysis provides a robust and interpretable route for potato price forecasting under heterogeneous market conditions. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to European Association for Potato Research 2026.

title: HyProTwin: Hybrid Digital Process Twins for Predictive Simulation of Continuous Processes
abstract: Business process management has mostly studied discrete processes with clearly identifiable process outcomes, e.g., the package delivery by an online shop. In contrast, continuous processes are characterized by real-time, discrete control of complex, continuous physical dynamics to maintain stable operating conditions, e.g., a sewage water treatment process with constant desirable chemical composition. Digital twins (DTs) of continuous processes provide simulation and prediction capabilities to enable real-time decision making that is key for efficient, proactive operations. However, implementation of DTs is greatly hindered by interoperability, communication, orchestration, and modeling challenges. Moreover, real-time decision making could be enhanced by predictive simulation, i.e., the ability to simulate future what-if scenarios to consider future changes and their impact on predictions. To realize DTs of continuous processes and enable predictive simulation, we propose hybrid digital process twins (HyProTwin) with their architecture and predictive simulation techniques. We demonstrate the feasibility and performance of HyProTwin on three real-world continuous processes. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Fairness in Prescriptive Process Analytics: Integrating Fairness Constraints into the Learning Phase
abstract: Prescriptive Process Analytics is a core field in business process management that provides automated activity recommendations to improve Key Performance Indicators in business processes. Because such recommendations can directly affect individuals involved in the process, ensuring fairness is essential. Recent work has begun to address fairness in process monitoring by enforcing group-level parity across demographic groups at the predictive stage. However, these approaches leave the prescriptive phase entirely unexamined and rely solely on group fairness notions, failing to account for individual-level counterfactual fairness (i.e., the requirement that a recommendation should not change when sensitive attributes are altered). To address this gap, we propose to enforce counterfactual fairness directly in prescriptive process monitoring. We develop a novel neuro-symbolic framework based on Logic Tensor Networks that encodes counterfactual fairness as a logical axiom over predictions, seamlessly integrated into the learning process. We evaluate our approach on real-world event logs and find that it enforces counterfactual fairness at the prediction level and improves recommendation-level counterfactual consistency under the considered policy, while maintaining competitive predictive and prescriptive performance, establishing the first fairness-aware framework for Prescriptive Process Analytics. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Towards Agent-Based Automation beyond RPA: An Exploratory Design Science Study in the Public Sector
abstract: Large organizations increasingly explore large language models (LLMs) to support knowledge-intensive process work. While Robotic Process Automation (RPA) has proven effective for rule-based and structured activities, many process improvement opportunities remain inaccessible due to unstructured natural-language artifacts that require human interpretation. This paper investigates how agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems can support process improvement by transforming interpretative work rather than merely automating execution tasks. Following a Design Science Research (DSR) approach, we study an exploratory prototype implemented in collaboration with a large public-sector organization responsible for nationwide social benefits administration. The artifact integrates LLM-based agents into a software development business process by transforming unstructured user interface (UI) specification documents into structured JSON-based UI representations, executable code components, and automatically generated test cases. The study explores how agentic capabilities affect process structures, handover artifacts, and human roles within an existing workflow. The artifact is evaluated in a real-world setting using a mixed-method approach combining quantitative efficiency measurements and qualitative expert assessments. Results indicate significant reductions in manual transformation effort as well as improved standardization and reduced interpretative ambiguity. At the same time, the findings highlight the need for structured specification practices and human validation mechanisms. The paper provides empirically grounded design insights into how agentic AI can support business process improvement beyond traditional RPA in public-sector contexts. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Entrepreneurial bankruptcy as a career-sorting event: income trajectories, re-entry, and risk-taking
abstract: Entrepreneurial bankruptcy is a salient failure event, yet little is known about its association with subsequent income trajectories and career paths. Using matched employer–employee data, we examine the income consequences of entrepreneurial bankruptcy and heterogeneity in post-bankruptcy careers among entrepreneurs operating incorporated firms. Bankruptcy is associated with persistent income losses on average, though this conceals pronounced heterogeneity. Entrepreneurs who do not re-enter experience significant income declines, whereas those who re-enter earn higher post-bankruptcy incomes. Re-entry is associated with higher revealed risk preferences, along with descriptively higher human capital and financial resources. Entrepreneurs who re-enter tend to operate ventures that grow faster but are more leveraged, less profitable, and more likely to fail again, consistent with higher-variance strategies. Overall, the findings show that entrepreneurial bankruptcy functions as a career-sorting mechanism in which post-failure outcomes reflect both selection into distinct career paths and systematic differences in subsequent strategic behavior. title: Modeling internalizing symptoms and substance use comorbidity using causal network methodology
abstract: The cooccurrence of internalizing and substance use disorders can be explained from several perspectives, yet most are modeled in isolation and limited to correlational evidence. Advancements on two common etiological perspectives – i) internalizing symptoms predisposing toward substance use disorder symptoms, ii) transdiagnostic factors predisposing toward both symptom domains – are therefore hampered by scarce multivariate and causal evidence. The present study addressed this gap by modeling direct (causal) links from internalizing symptoms to substance use behaviors and (causal) links from the transdiagnostic factors cognitive control, locus of control (LOC), and meaning in life. We analyzed data from wave 7 (2019–2023; N = 1725), the 15-year follow-up of the ongoing longitudinal cohort study the Netherlands Study of Depression and Anxiety, using a correlational network and a causal network based on the fast causal inference algorithm. The correlational network showed that depression and social anxiety symptoms were positively related to alcohol-related problems and negatively related to alcohol consumption. Cognitive control and external LOC correlated positively with alcohol consumption. Meaning in life was negatively associated with depression and social anxiety symptoms, alcohol consumption, alcohol problems, and drug use. The causal network showed causal relations of external LOC with depression and social anxiety symptoms. Although our correlational findings gave some support to both perspectives on internalizing and substance use comorbidity, the present findings do not support a causal, etiological interpretation of these perspectives. © 2026 The Authors.

title: BRIDGE: A Bayes-Risk-Informed Process Decoder for Suffix Prediction
abstract: In Predictive Process Monitoring, activity suffix prediction predicts the remaining sequence of activities given a prefix. As a multi-step sequence prediction task with many plausible suffixes, decoding is critical to predictive accuracy. However, the performance of existing decoding strategies is highly dataset-dependent, and no method is consistently reliable. A key limitation is a recurring mismatch between how suffixes are selected during decoding and how prediction quality is evaluated: current approaches typically rely on likelihood to guide decoding, without explicitly accounting for sequence-level prediction error. In this work, we characterize this mismatch and propose BRIDGE, a Bayes-risk-informed decoding framework that samples candidate suffixes and ranks them by expected quality under the evaluation metric, thereby aligning decoding more closely with the task objective. As a post-training inference-time method, it can be applied across predictive models without retraining. We evaluate BRIDGE on eight real-life event logs against multiple decoding strategies and established suffix prediction models. BRIDGE is consistently competitive and often best-performing, with particularly strong gains on logs with long traces and for simple statistical models. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Multi-objective optimization for emergency primary logistics of refined products under pipeline disruption condition: a case study in China
abstract: The primary logistics of refined products plays a critical role in ensuring regional oil supply security and supporting efficient oil allocation. As the dominant transportation mode in primary logistics systems, pipelines are critical for refined products transportation, and pipeline disruptions may significantly affect logistics performance and supply continuity. To address this issue, a multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model is proposed for emergency primary logistics planning of refined products under pipeline disruption condition. The model considers logistics cost and supply shortage as conflicting objectives while integrating multiple transportation modes, lateral transportation, temporary procurement, and temporary vehicle rental decisions within a unified optimization framework. The augmented ε-constraint method is employed to obtain Pareto optimal solutions and analyze the trade-off between economic efficiency and supply security. A real-world large-scale refined products primary logistics system in China is used as a case study. The results show that pipeline disruptions substantially alter transportation patterns, increasing the share of rail transportation from over 20% to more than 30%, while road transportation is generally between 3 and 5%. The analyses further illustrate the impact of pipeline disruption on logistics planning and show the effectiveness of the proposed multi-objective methodology in balancing logistics cost and supply shortage. The obtained Pareto optimal solutions provide flexible decision support for emergency primary logistics planning under different disruption scenarios. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Respecting Object Relationships: An Object-Centric Sampling Algorithm
abstract: Recently, object-centric process mining has emerged as a new process mining direction that places the relationships among multiple data objects at the center, with the Object-Centric Event Log (OCEL) serving as the standard exchange format. OCEL can contain a high volume of events and complex object relationships. Particularly, the size of real-life OCELs presents a challenge for conformance checking, hindering the scalability. This makes it necessary to extract representative subsets of the log for analysis purposes, thereby calling for appropriate sampling algorithms. Currently, only random sampling exists to allow for scalability. However, it disregards dependencies between multiple objects and therefore does not produce reliable conformance checking results. Thus, it cannot be considered as an appropriate sampling strategy. To overcome this, we propose the sampling algorithm RP-OCEL that incorporates object relationships, while reducing the size of the OCEL. RP-OCEL applies weighting according to the connectivity of object types and selects only object types that exhibit below a connectivity score, while the final sample still contains all object types. We applied our approach on a well-known OCEL dataset and compared it to random sampling. The results show that, in contrast to random sampling, RP-OCEL is suited for conformance checking, can perform sampling without altering the objects associated with an event and can significantly reduce processing time. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Trust No Pool: Formal Security Analysis of BPMN Collaborations
abstract: Cross-organizational collaborations face inherent trust challenges: any participant may want to deviate from the agreed-upon process model, trying to deceive others about the shared state. Traditional verification approaches over collaborations – e.g., over BPMN collaboration models – verify correctness properties under the assumption that all participants faithfully execute their roles. They do not consider what a strategically dishonest participant can achieve, and to our knowledge, no formal framework exists for doing so. We introduce potentially adversarial participants for BPMN collaborations as a first-class concept, analyze them as security protocols, and demonstrate that this framing is both formally precise and directly actionable. We utilize a structural correspondence between BPMN’s token-based collaboration semantics and the multiset rewriting formalism of the Tamarin security protocol verifier. This correspondence allows us to define a formal, epistemically grounded threat model and to encode a core subset of collaboration semantics as Tamarin theories, enabling the formal verification of collaboration security: the automated discovery of successful attack strategies or proving of their absence. We introduce a composable attacker model whose elements reflect the underlying platform’s security guarantees – from loosely coupled integrations through smart contract orchestration to Verifiable Credential-based protocols. We demonstrate the approach on an example, examining how the attack surface shifts across the three execution platforms and revealing platform-specific attacks that arise from the interplay of business logic and platform semantics. These attacks are undetectable by standard correctness verification and sophisticated enough to warrant systematic analysis in business-critical settings. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Mind the Long Tail: Understanding the Difficulty of Delay Detection in Business Processes
abstract: The early detection of delayed cases in business processes is a critical capability for organizations. Predictive process monitoring (PPM) supports this task by using historical event logs to predict the remaining time of ongoing cases, enabling timely interventions to avoid missed deadlines and service level violations. Although remaining time prediction has advanced considerably through sophisticated deep learning architectures, little is known about the intrinsic difficulty of delay detection itself. Since performance is typically assessed using aggregate metrics, prior work provides limited insight into how models perform across the target distribution, especially on the operationally most critical cases with large delays. In this paper, we address this gap by analyzing the difficulty of delay detection. Across 14 event logs, we show that remaining times are typically strongly right-skewed, with only a small fraction of cases exhibiting large delays. Existing models capture the mode of this distribution well but perform poorly on high-delay cases. We further uncover pronounced heteroscedasticity, showing that predictive uncertainty increases with delay magnitude. Based on these findings, we evaluate approaches to mitigate the imbalance problem, but find only limited benefits, suggesting that the key underlying problem may not be imbalance but higher uncertainty associated with delayed cases. We show that this correlation can be exploited to substantially improve the identification of delayed cases. Overall, our work provides new insights into the sources of difficulty in delay detection and identifies uncertainty-aware modeling as a promising direction for future PPM research. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Mode of construction of oncoids containing early diversified calcimicrobes from the lower Cambrian Bayan Gol Formation, western Mongolia
abstract: Oncoids, which are a type of microbialite, are widely known from the Precambrian to the present. However, the types of earliest Palaeozoic calcimicrobes within oncoids and their roles in oncoid construction are poorly understood. This study focuses on the construction of Cambrian oncoids from western Mongolia, based on microstructural types (i.e., types A–D), the variety of calcimicrobes and the abundance of fenestral fabrics. Type A microstructure is characterized by well-developed laminae and is dominated by Girvanella. Type B is similar to type A, but with an increased abundance of Kordephyton and Botomaella and with some fenestral fabrics. Type C is dominated by fenestral fabrics. Type D is markedly different from the other types, being characterized by irregular growth forms. Microstructures of types A–C exhibit gradational transitions in their laminae, calcimicrobes and fenestral fabrics, representing a continuous series that formed under changing hydrodynamic conditions. Type A was periodically overturned, forming laminated microstructures. Type C experienced episodic overturning that facilitated the development of Kordephyton and Botomaella, which contributed to the formation of fenestral fabrics and hindered the development of concentric laminae. Type B reflects conditions intermediate between those of types A and C. In contrast, type D was formed during long periods of quiescence with episodic overturning, resulting in highly irregular forms. These early Cambrian oncoids of western Mongolia are recording various microstructures with diverse calcimicrobial communities. The studied oncoids thus provide new information on how the early diversified calcimicrobes contributed to the construction of oncoids in the unique marine environment of the early Cambrian. © Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Predictive basket steering and shopper choice sovereignty in AI-enabled retailing: A self-determination theory perspective
abstract: As artificial intelligence becomes embedded in online retailing, personalization systems increasingly shape consumers’ shopping baskets rather than merely recommend products. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory, this study examines how predictive basket steering is associated with shopper choice sovereignty and retailer reliance comfort among Chinese online grocery shoppers. Predictive steering is conceptualized through three mechanisms: option pruning convenience, preference reflection accuracy, and commercial intent transparency. Survey data from 483 shoppers were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling, with post-stratification calibration to national demographic benchmarks. The results indicate that predictive steering is positively associated with all three mechanisms, and each mechanism is positively associated with shopper choice sovereignty. Preference reflection accuracy and transparency are also directly associated with retailer reliance comfort, whereas option pruning convenience has no direct association with reliance comfort. Shopper choice sovereignty, in turn, is strongly associated with retailer reliance comfort. The study contributes to AI-enabled retailing research by highlighting that convenience alone is insufficient for comfortable reliance; rather, perceived decision authorship (sovereignty) is the central mechanism. It suggests that effective basket steering should combine convenience and personalized relevance with transparent, revisable, and consumer-controlled choice architecture. © 2026

title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of 2-aminopyrimidine-5-carboxamide derivatives as potent selective Wee1 inhibitors
abstract: Wee1 is a serine/threonine kinase that plays an important role in regulating DNA damage response and cell cycle checkpoints. Inhibition of Wee1 could abrogate cell cycle arrest, exacerbate DNA damage, and induce mitotic catastrophe and apoptosis. Herein, a novel series of 2-aminopyrimidine-5-carboxamide derivatives were designed, synthesized, and evaluated as Wee1 inhibitors. Among them, compound WC-27 exhibited excellent inhibitory activity against Wee1 (IC50 = 2.11 nM) and high selectivity over PLK1 (IC50 > 1000 nM), suggesting that it may reduce off-target effects on PLK1 and thereby potentially mitigate the myelosuppression associated with Wee1 inhibitors. Meanwhile, it displayed acceptable antiproliferative activity against NCI-H1299 cell line with an IC50 value of 1.05 μM. Further investigation showed that compound WC-27 could arrest NCI-H1299 cells in S phase and induce apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner. Moreover, compound WC-27 displayed moderate liver microsomal stability and an excellent pharmacokinetic profile (AUC0-t = 2370 ng h mL−1, oral bioavailability of 49.5%) in Sprague-Dawley rats, acceptable PPB, low risk of drug-drug interactions and no apparent toxicity was observed in the acute toxicity assay. Overall, compound WC-27 exhibited high selectivity over PLK1. This favorable profile may mitigate the risk of PLK1-related off-target toxicities such as myelosuppression, a well-recognized safety liability for reported Wee1 inhibitors. Collectively, these results indicate that compound WC-27 is a promising Wee1 inhibitor. © 2026

title: Perceived business value of digital freight platforms: Evidence from small and medium-sized enterprises in Poland
abstract: Purpose: This study examines how SMEs operating in the Polish transport, shipping and logistics (TSL) sector perceive the business value of digital freight exchanges, and how they associate platform use with operational efficiency, empty vehicle movements, transport resource utilization and competitive positioning. The study investigates whether the functionalities offered by digital freight platforms constitute distinct value dimensions or a single integrated platform value dimension. Methodology: Empirical data were collected in 2025 through a questionnaire survey of 65 purposively selected Polish SMEs actively using digital freight exchanges. The sample is therefore not representative of the broader Polish SME road-freight population. The analysis included descriptive and reliability statistics, Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) (Principal Axis Factoring), Spearman's correlation, multiple linear regression, and Kruskal–Wallis tests with Dunn–Bonferroni post hoc comparisons. Factor stability was assessed using bootstrap analysis. Findings: Respondents primarily used digital freight exchanges to obtain transport orders, improve fleet utilization, monitor shipments and maintain operational continuity during periods of lower demand. The most valued functionalities were contractor credibility assessment, freight search, fleet utilization, transaction security and responsiveness to demand fluctuations. Exploratory Factor Analysis identified a provisional one-factor solution explaining 50.67% of the total variance, interpreted as a Perceived Integrated Platform Value dimension, and suggesting that these SMEs evaluate platform functionalities as complementary elements of an integrated business-support system, because the items measure perceived importance. This dimension is interpreted as a proxy for perceived platform value rather than as a measure of realized benefits rather than as separate capabilities. Perceived platform value was positively associated with competitive advantage (ρ = 0.411, p < 0.001). While overall platform value did not differ significantly by enterprise size, micro-enterprises reported greater competitive benefits and more frequent platform use than medium-sized enterprises. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Clarifying environmental responsibility for consistent absolute environmental sustainability assessment: A global sector-level analysis
abstract: Absolute Environmental Sustainability Assessment (AESA) aims to determine whether a system operates within its allocated share of Carrying Capacities (CCs). Initial guidelines have been proposed to establish a methodological framework. This paper proposes methodological recommendations to address three key requirements for a consistent implementation of AESA, i.e., i) additivity in the CCs downscaling, ii) no double-counting issues in environmental assessment, and iii) consistency of system boundaries between environmental assessment and downscaling steps. Proposals are based on the concept of environmental responsibility. Three environmental accounting approaches, which consider different types of actors responsible for a system's environmental impacts, are employed. These are the production-based approach (PBA), the consumption-based approach (CBA) and the income-based approach (IBA). Furthermore, identifying the responsible actor makes the CCs allocation step more transparent. The adapted AESA method is implemented across country-level economic sectors using Exiobase, an input-output database. Results obtained using the three accounting approaches and two theories of distributive justice are then compared. Similar to the choice of theory of distributive justice, AESA results are sensitive to the chosen accounting approach. Both are normative choices. Based on these preliminary findings, recommendations and further research perspectives are proposed for the AESA community. Finally, a focus on a single sector makes it possible to explore in further detail the relevance of the proposed recommendations for decision-making. © 2026 The Authors

title: Continuity Matters: Improving Predictive Process Monitoring Based on Path Coherence
abstract: Predictive Process Monitoring aims to forecast the future behavior of ongoing cases based on historical event log data. It is well established that predictive performance suffers when models treat cases and events as strictly isolated entities. While various approaches have attempted to integrate operational context to mitigate this limitation, the social dynamics in and around organizational processes have not been addressed in depth. We address this gap by drawing on research from the organizational science, specifically on research around organizational routines and operational friction. Specifically, we focus on the coordination friction and delays introduced when the execution context–such as the assigned resource or physical location–changes between consecutive events. This paper incorporates the concept of path coherence to explicitly quantify this situational continuity, as well as the friction that occurs when continuity breaks. We adapt this concept to event logs by engineering path coherence as an event-level feature and integrating it into a prediction pipeline based on Long Short-Term Memory models. Two variants are proposed: a resource-based coherence feature capturing responsibility handoffs and an all-attribute variant reflecting broader situational change. Using eight real-world event logs, we compare coherence-based feature sets with benchmark feature sets. The results show that coherence-based feature sets consistently reduce Mean Absolute Error, yielding statistically significant, mostly medium effect sizes, and that resource-based coherence explains the majority of the predictive performance gains. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: SCOPE: Sequential Causal Optimization of Process Interventions
abstract: Prescriptive Process Monitoring (PresPM) recommends interventions during running business processes to optimize key performance indicators (KPIs). In realistic settings, interventions are rarely isolated: organizations need to align sequences of interventions to jointly steer the outcome of a case. Existing PresPM approaches only partially address this challenge. Many focus on a single intervention decision, while others treat multiple interventions independently, ignoring how they interact over time. Methods that do address these dependencies depend either on simulation or data augmentation to approximate the process to train a Reinforcement Learning (RL) agent, which may create a reality gap and introduce bias. We introduce SCOPE (Sequential Causal Optimization of Process Interventions), a PresPM approach that learns aligned sequential intervention recommendations. SCOPE employs backward induction to estimate the effect of each candidate intervention action, propagating its impact from the final decision point back to the first. By leveraging causal learners, our method can utilize observational data directly, unlike methods that require constructing process approximations for RL. Experiments on both an existing synthetic dataset and a new semi-synthetic dataset show that SCOPE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art PresPM techniques in optimizing the KPI. The novel semi-synthetic setup, based on a real-life event log, is provided as a reusable benchmark for future work on sequential PresPM. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.
