title: Guiding Process Harmonization: A Classification Scheme for Differences Between BPMN Models
abstract: When transforming their IT systems, organizations must harmonize their existing business processes with vendor-provided reference models. This harmonization requires a detailed comparison of underlying BPMN models to identify differences between them. However, existing research provides limited support for identifying concrete, business-interpretable process differences, which means that organizations have little guidance in their process harmonization efforts. To bridge the gap, we propose a novel classification scheme that is tailored to guide process harmonization in workshop settings. Our scheme lifts the representation of process differences from atomic, element-level mismatches to practitioner-oriented change types. It was developed through an iterative approach based on real-world model pairs and validated via expert interviews from both practice and academia. By offering a shared vocabulary and conceptual foundation, the classification scheme facilitates communication across technical and business stakeholders and provides a basis for conducting efficient and effective harmonization workshops. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Automating execution and verification of BPMN+DMN business processes
abstract: The increasing and widespread use of Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) business processes, which also incorporate Decision Model and Notation (DMN) tables, necessitates tools and methodologies to verify their correctness. However, most commonly used frameworks to build BPMN + DMN models only allow designers to detect syntactical errors, thus ignoring semantic (behavioral) faults. This forces business processes designers to manually run single executions of their BPMN + DMN processes using proprietary tools in order to detect failures. Furthermore, how proprietary tools translate a BPMN + DMN process to a computer simulation is left unspecified. In this paper, we advance this state of the art by designing a tool, named BDTransTest, providing: (i) a translation from a BPMN + DMN process (B,D) to a Java program P; ii) the synthesis and execution of a verification plan for (B,D); iii) the analysis of the coverage achieved by the verification plan in terms of nodes and edges of B, as well as of rows in the DMN tables D. Finally, we evaluate our methodology on BPMN + DMN processes from the literature, obtaining over 60% coverage with more than 2000 test cases and negligible resource requirements. © 2026 The Authors

title: Validity Criteria for Explaining Variation in Process Complexity
abstract: Business process complexity is frequently used to assess behavioral change. It is measured repeatedly over consecutive trace windows, resulting in a time series of complexity scores. When analyzing this data, it is a problem that complexity measures can fluctuate even when the underlying process remains stable. So far, business process management research lacks a formal observation model to distinguish process change from measurement-induced variation. In this paper, we build upon signal processing theory to develop an observation model for process complexity. The model decomposes observed complexity scores into a process complexity signal and measurement noise component. The measurement noise component consists of systematic measurement bias and stochastic measurement error. We derive three validity criteria to analyze signal-and-noise characteristics of complexity measures: (1) reliability, reflecting sensitivity to stochastic measurement error when process and observation setting do not change, (2) robustness, reflecting sensitivity to observation setting change, and (3) responsiveness, reflecting sensitivity to process change. We operationalize these criteria and apply them in a large-scale simulation study. The results reveal systematic differences in the signal-and-noise behavior of complexity measures. Our work contributes a measurement-theoretic foundation for interpreting changes in process complexity and for validating complexity measures. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: A physical model approach to order lot sizing
abstract: Abstract: The increasing pressure to reduce operational costs and enhance supply chain efficiency has made inventory management a key area of optimization. In this context, the lot-sizing problem remains a fundamental challenge due to its direct impact on ordering and holding costs. We propose an analytical approach to the lot-sizing problem based on an analogy with a one-dimensional mechanical system of particles connected by elastic elements. This interpretation allows the cost minimization conditions to be derived naturally and leads to an exact solution without resorting to heuristic or computationally intensive methods. The model characterizes the optimal policy through a single dimensionless parameter,, which governs the system behavior: when, the optimal strategy is to place one order per period, whereas for, the optimal number of orders N is smaller than the planning horizon M (). By expressing the total cost in terms of the intensive variable N/M, the problem can be formulated as a single function of. This reduces the need for complex iterative optimization algorithms, requiring only simple adjustments (integer feasibility, rounding, and discrete order composition) to obtain a direct determination of optimal order frequencies and lot sizes. The relevance of this work lies in providing both a novel theoretical perspective and a practical tool for inventory control, allowing faster and more transparent decision-making, particularly in real-time and large-scale planning environments. The applicability of the framework is illustrated through a real-world case study involving a concentrated pulp processing plant, as well as a representative example drawn from the literature, allowing for comparison with classical EOQ-based policies. In addition, a sensitivity analysis with respect to the model parameters is conducted, demonstrating the robustness of the proposed approach. Managerial implications are also discussed, highlighting the interpretability and operational applicability of the model. title: Characterizing Process Variants with Natural Examples
abstract: To improve business processes, it is crucial to analyze why processes differ across process variants. To support this analysis, prior research has often relied on machine learning models trained to classify process variants and used model explanations to distinguish them. User studies in explainable artificial intelligence show that these explanations can be expanded through the inclusion of examples. To this end, we introduce an approach that uses declarative behavioural constraints to support variant classification tasks. Building on these constraints, we perform a post-hoc probability analysis and derive a set of multi-feature measures to characterize cases that are representative of each process variant (prototypes) alongside cases that are close to the classification boundaries between process variants (boundary cases). We assess the explanatory power of those natural examples with two real-world event logs. The results demonstrate that our approach shows the distinctive behavioural traits of variants effectively and intuitively. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: LLM-based multi-agent systems for code generation: A multi-vocal literature review
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have enabled multi-agent systems to perform autonomous code generation for complex tasks. Despite the recent growth in research and industrial applications in this area, there is little work on synthesizing evidence from both academic and industrial sources to capture the current state of research on LLM-based multi-agent systems for code generation. To this end, we conducted a Multi-Vocal Literature Review (MLR), combining insights from both academia and industry, including peer-reviewed studies and grey literature. The aim of this study is to systematically synthesize and analyze existing knowledge on LLM-based multi-agent systems for code generation. Specifically, the review examines the motivations for their use, employed benchmarks and models, key challenges, proposed solutions, and potential directions for future research. We selected and reviewed 114 studies, and the key findings are: (1) the identified reasons for adopting multi-agent systems for code generation were classified into nine categories; (2) the models and evaluation benchmarks utilized across the studies were systematically analyzed to provide a structured overview of commonly adopted LLM configurations and assessment practices; (3) the reported challenges and corresponding solutions were synthesized into seven main categories and 26 subcategories; and (4) future research directions were identified and organized into six main categories and 18 subcategories. The results of this MLR will assist researchers and practitioners in pursuing further studies and supporting the real-world adoption of multi-agent systems in industrial settings. © 2026 The Authors

title: The impact of decision-making sequences on national and store brand competition: a game theoretic approach
abstract: This paper examines how decision-making sequences influence pricing and advertising strategies in a dual-brand supply chain consisting of a national brand (NB) manufacturer and a retailer offering a competing store brand (SB). The manufacturer engages in national advertising, while the retailer conducts local advertising, creating asymmetric promotional effects. We develop a game-theoretic model under a Stackelberg structure to analyze three strategic scenarios: simultaneous decision-making, advertising-first, and pricing-first sequences. The results show that the decision timing significantly influences equilibrium outcomes, profit distribution, and market competition intensity. In particular, simultaneous decision-making maximizes the manufacturer’s profit and overall system performance, whereas pricing-first strategies provide greater stability for the retailer under strong advertising spillover effects. Sensitivity analyses further demonstrate that advertising effectiveness plays a critical role in shaping optimal strategies and profit trade-offs. These findings offer both theoretical insights and practical implications for firms managing national and store brand competition under advertising interactions. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: All Eyes on the Workflow: Automated and Efficient Event Discovery from Video Streams
abstract: Disciplines such as business process management and process mining aid organizations by discovering insights about processes on the basis of recorded event data. However, an obstacle to process analysis is data multi-modality: for instance, data in video form are not directly interpretable as events. Existing approaches rely on a dictionary of activity label as input, cannot provide frame-by-frame labeling explanations, or rely on superseded computer vision techniques. In this work, we present SnapLog, an approach to extract event data from videos by converting frames to feature vectors using image embeddings and performing temporal segmentation through frame-wise similarity matrices. A generalized few-shot classification is then used to assign labels to the video segments, yielding labeled, timestamped sub-sequences of frames that are interpretable as events. Conventional process mining techniques can be used to analyze the resulting data. We show that our approach produces logs that accurately reflect the process in the videos. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Why Behavioral Representations Matter: A Framework for Comparing Their Expressiveness in Business Process Analysis
abstract: Behavioral representations are a fundamental abstraction mechanism in process mining, where an event log is abstracted into a set of behaviors in preparation for a subsequent analysis task, such as process discovery, log-delta analysis or concept drift. However, the choice of representation directly determines which behavioral distinctions remain observable in downstream analysis, yet no formal framework exists to compare representations with respect to this criterion. Consequently, the expressive capabilities and limitations of behavioral representations are undefined, impeding assessment of the quality and completeness of downstream analysis results. In this paper, we propose a framework for formally comparing the expressiveness and information preservation of behavioral representations. We introduce losslessness as a criterion for information preservation, refinement to capture when one representation subsumes the discriminative power of another, and incomparability when neither subsumes the other. We apply the framework to five representations commonly used in process mining. Our results show that representations differ not only in granularity but also in the behavioral dimensions they capture. In addition, commonly used representations are often orthogonal in their expressivity, showing the importance of selecting the most suitable representation for a particular task, as there is currently no single best representation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Towards an OR-Join Semantics that Meets Expectations
abstract: The OR-join is an essential but semantically complex construct in process modeling that has challenged process modelers and analysts for decades. Because it possesses non-local semantics – an OR-join may need to wait for tokens to arrive from “further away” – making it difficult to determine when it is enabled or not. The BPMN specification provides “official” semantics, but despite its complexity, these semantics lead to “surprising” behavior in certain scenarios. This paper investigates the complexities of the BPMN OR-join specification and explores whether alternative semantics better align with the expectations of modeling experts. To assess different OR-join policies, a questionnaire featuring 14 example models was distributed among a large group of process experts. Analysis of the responses shows a significant lack of consensus among experts regarding the expected behavior of OR-joins. None of the experts gave answers fully consistent with the official BPMN standard. We propose a new policy that aligns more closely with expert expectations and is also able to determine ambiguous situations. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Implications of drone delivery: Strategic interaction and competitive equilibrium
abstract: Logistics capability has emerged as a critical strategic asset that shapes business models and competitive landscapes. Within this context, drone delivery represents a disruptive technology that is redefining the nature of interfirm competition and cooperation. This study explores the strategic interactions between a smart retailer that uses drones for delivery and a traditional retailer that relies on conventional methods only, utilizing both Stackelberg and Nash games to analyze drone adoption and pricing decisions. The effective delivery capability of drones and consumer preferences for delivery efficiency are critical factors in this study. The findings suggest that drones enable retailers to increase prices while expanding their market share, thereby creating a competitive advantage for smart retailers when drones are used exclusively. Traditional retailers are more inclined to adopt drones when effective delivery capabilities are high, whereas smart retailers may focus on using drones to optimize efficiency under varying delivery conditions, depending on consumer preferences. Finally, drone-enabled delivery can generate multi-win outcomes under certain conditions, where retailer profits, consumer surplus, and social welfare are simultaneously improved compared with the truck-only benchmark. Moreover, higher operational availability strengthens the economic viability of drone deployment. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Agentic Business Process Modeling: Co-creating Business Processes with Human-Centric AI Agents
abstract: Business process modeling is a highly complex, cognitively demanding task requiring deep domain understanding. While large language models make transforming natural language descriptions into formal models increasingly achievable, conventional single-prompt approaches often yield structural inconsistencies and computational inefficiency. To overcome these limitations, integrating agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems offers promising capabilities. Deploying these autonomous systems can significantly enhance execution. Such architectures iteratively construct, control, and improve models by validating logic, resolving ambiguities, and inferring implicit requirements from unstructured tasks. Yet, integrating such proactive agents into organizational workflows introduces novel socio-technical risks. When deployed with a task-centric design, these applications often impose excessive cognitive load on human modelers, negatively affecting the psychological work experience and task performance, as autonomous execution inherently limits human agency. To address these challenges, we introduce an interactive AI system for agentic process modeling, developed and evaluated through an iterative design science approach. Shifting from monolithic generation to structured collaboration, we propose a self-reflective agent architecture. The system continuously validates internal logic and actively integrates human feedback to resolve structural discrepancies. By prioritizing human-centric design, this approach mitigates risks discovered in exploratory research, including agent-induced cognitive load and the complacent acceptance of AI-generated models. Our findings offer theoretical insights and practical guidelines for configuring human-AI collaborations that ensure efficiency without compromising human agency or cognitive well-being. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Tobacco Retailer Perspectives on Potential Phase Out of Tobacco Sales in South Australia: An Exploratory Survey
abstract: Issue Addressed: To examine tobacco retailers' perspectives on the potential phase out of tobacco sales in South Australia, a retail-based tobacco endgame strategy that directly targets product availability. Methods: A cross-sectional mixed-methods survey of licensed tobacco retailers conducted in South Australia in April 2025. The survey included 70 licensed tobacco retailers and assessed anticipated impacts of a retail phase out, strategies they might adopt in response and the support they would seek. Both quantitative ratings and open-text qualitative responses were analysed using descriptive statistics and inductive thematic analysis. Results: Retailers rated legal requirements, declining profitability and reduced consumer demand as the most important drivers for them to cease tobacco sales, while few highlighted public or community health considerations. One-third reported needing lead-in time to transition, citing financial compensation, business planning support and opportunities for product substitution as priorities. Concerns about illicit tobacco trade featured prominently, with many describing reduced legal sales, financial loss and security risks. Retailers held mixed views on phased transition to ending tobacco sales. Conclusions: Some retailers view tobacco as increasingly unprofitable, yet business sustainability concerns and illicit trade complicate retailer support for mandated phase out. Clear timelines and targeted transition support are critical to increasing retailer confidence and policy feasibility. So What?: By aligning tobacco retail phase-out policies with retailer support, governments may be able to reduce tobacco availability while limiting impacts on retailers' livelihoods; further research is needed to confirm how this approach would affect policy acceptability and business transitions at scale. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Heuristic Work Crafting: A BPM-Inspired Approach to Individual Process Redesign
abstract: Knowledge workers have considerable autonomy in how they structure their daily tasks, yet systematic guidance for improving individual work practices remains scarce. This paper introduces CRAFT@work, an approach that bridges job crafting theory from Work & Organisational Psychology with process redesign heuristics from the BPM field to support self-directed work improvement. We developed a catalogue of 29 individual work redesign heuristics, adapted from established process redesign heuristics, and evaluated them through an intervention study with 12 knowledge workers across diverse occupational contexts. The intervention consisted of individualised coaching sessions in which participants reflected on their current work, created a Personal Crafting Plan, and subsequently enacted and reflected on their chosen heuristics over a four-week period. Results show that the heuristics are broadly applicable across the occupational contexts included in this study, with every heuristic considered relevant by at least five participants. Almost all participants were able to enact meaningful changes to their work, with several reporting concrete improvements. The most impactful heuristics specifically target the ambiguities and information bottlenecks that slow down or complicate work, making BPM a uniquely situated discipline for addressing the friction that knowledge workers experience. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: The punctuality stability of the Nash equilibrium: the advantage of a late player in potential and aggregative games
abstract: In a Nash equilibrium, no player can gain by unilaterally deviating. In many practical settings, however, players can also choose when to act, and delaying may be profitable because it allows a player to move last and respond to others (for example, waiting for competitors to announce prices before setting one’s own). We ask whether one can select a Nash equilibrium in which no player has an incentive to delay intentionally. To address this, we introduce punctually stable Nash-equilibrium, that is, a Nash equilibrium with the additional property that intentional tardiness is not advantageous. We study existence of punctually stable Nash-equilibria in potential games and aggregative games. Remarkably, in some environments, all-player punctuality can be achieved without explicitly penalizing late arrivals. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: AI-Assisted Event Log Generation for Process Mining in Healthcare
abstract: Process mining in healthcare requires structured event logs, yet extracting such logs from complex clinical databases remains a manual, error-prone task requiring substantial SQL skills and domain expertise. This paper investigates the use of large language models to generate SQL queries for event log generation from healthcare data structured according to OMOP, a common data model in healthcare. We develop an artifact to evaluate four prompting strategies across three state-of-the-art LLMs using real-world healthcare data and six clinical treatment processes of varying schema complexity. Generated queries are compared against expert-written ground truth using five metrics: executability, schema conformance, event log completeness, process fidelity, and prompt sensitivity. Results show that prompting strategy has a stronger impact on performance than model choice, while schema complexity is the primary driver of task difficulty. This paper provides a framework as well as practical guidance for LLM-assisted event log generation for process mining from clinical relational data using SQL, further enabling process mining on healthcare data. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Toward Automated Ticket Escalation in Customer Support Processes: From Emails to Explainable Predictions
abstract: Business processes in customer support often remain undocumented, with critical decisions such as ticket escalation relying on tacit knowledge rather than explicit process models. Automating such process decisions is challenging because the underlying data is unstructured email text, not structured event logs assumed by existing process mining and predictive monitoring approaches. We present a novel pipeline artifact that addresses this gap: a semi-automated four-stage pipeline that extracts structured features from customer support emails using large language models (LLMs) together with lightweight domain-expert validation, and employs explainable machine learning to predict the optimal timing of ticket creation, a key decision point in the support process. Our pipeline generates an initial feature schema from sample threads, consolidates semantically similar features through embedding-based clustering under domain-expert review, extracts cumulative feature values at each email point, and constructs a structured dataset ready for machine learning. We introduce a SHAP-based active feature learning strategy that identifies which missing features, when acquired, would most improve prediction confidence, enabling principled decisions about when to request additional information versus making immediate predictions. We evaluate our approach in two stages: first, on a reproducible synthetic dataset where comparison against six baselines demonstrates that LLM-extracted features provide complementary semantic information, with combined features achieving the best overall performance (ROC-AUC 0.90) while end-to-end LLM classification performs worst (ROC-AUC 0.46), validating our design of using LLMs as feature extractors rather than decision makers; second, on 1,500 email instances from 800 real-world email threads from Nosco, a commercial CRM platform, where we demonstrate effective feature extraction, predictive performance, and active feature learning for practical deployment. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Integrated optimization for fleet sequencing, deploying, and scheduling based on carbon intensity management
abstract: The mandatory Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) regulations, enforced by the IMO since 2023, create significant operational challenges for shipping lines. Existing studies mostly treat carbon intensity as a compliance constraint and lack an integrated optimization framework that jointly optimizes route planning, fleet deployment, and scheduling. To fill this gap, we propose a bi-objective mixed-integer nonlinear programming model that minimizes both total fleet operating cost and total fleet carbon intensity, thereby promoting active carbon intensity management. The model incorporates realistic operational features, including partial port call adjustments, heterogeneous vessel fleets, fuel switching inside and outside Emission Control Areas, and speed limits imposed by the Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index. A customized hybrid solution algorithm, combining the ε-constraint method, rule-based heuristics, linearization techniques, and the CPLEX solver, is designed to solve the model efficiently. A case study on the COSCO container network reveals that conventional measures such as speed reduction, port call cuts, and vessel downsizing can reduce short-term costs but may increase vessel carbon intensity, underscoring the necessity of carbon-related objectives. Furthermore, speed optimization serves as an effective short-term strategy to improve both cost and carbon performance. Notably, raising vessel capacity utilization yields greater carbon intensity reduction than extending sailing distances, indicating that route planning should prioritize matching cargo demand with appropriate vessel types. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Aligning Out-of-Plane Polarization in 2D Ferroelectric Perovskite Wafer Boosts Interlayer Carrier Transport for Efficient X-Ray Detection
abstract: High-quality, centimeter-sized polycrystalline wafers of a 2D ferroelectric perovskite are fabricated via a facile hot-pressing method, circumventing the challenge of growing large, thick single crystals of 2D perovskites. The preferred horizontal orientation of grains, combined with electric poling, creates macroscopic out-of-plane polarization, generating a strong built-in electric field that boosts interlayer carrier transport. The poled wafer not only enables self-powered X-ray detection but also achieves a high sensitivity (2285 μC Gy−1 cm−2) and an ultralow detection limit (7.2 nGy s−1) under a small bias, along with exceptional operational stability and high-contrast X-ray imaging. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Identifying Order Processing Types for Circular Production
abstract: The successful establishment of circular production offers significant potential for companies, including reduced material costs, increased supply chain resilience, access to new business opportunities, and compliance with increasingly stringent sustainability regulations. In circular production, material loops are closed through the take-back of used products and their value-preserving recovery, refurbishment, or remanufacturing. However, the required order processing differs substantially from the order processing logic of conventional linear value creation. These differences arise from new sub-processes such as reverse logistics and reprocessing, necessary adaptations of established order processing activities, and possible changes to the underlying business model. To support companies in addressing these challenges, this paper identifies and characterizes order processing types for circular production. Similar to established types in linear production, such as make-to-stock or engineer-to-order, a typology of order processing for circular production can provide a structured understanding of different order processing logics. A combined research design integrating a systematic literature review of 17 typological approaches with an empirical analysis of 65 industrial case studies and twelve expert interviews is applied. The result is a set of eleven order processing types, characterized along four dimensions: return initiation, Re-X concept, Re-X order type, and replacement condition. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Start with the end in mind: An interview-based survey and gap analysis of biochar production and selected industrial applications in Europe
abstract: Biochar occupies a distinctive position among carbon dioxide removal approaches, offering potential carbon storage and functional materials for several industrial sectors. However, technical potential does not by itself establish market integration. We combined two semi-structured interview studies comprising 13 supply-side interviews across nine European countries and 22 application-side interview sessions involving 23 participants. The main analysis covers asphalt, insulation materials, animal feed, biogas and packaging; one additional biofuel-sector interview is retained as contextual evidence. We examined production economics, application requirements and the gaps between them. Supply-side accounts identified feedstock costs, product specifications, energy offtake and carbon-credit revenue as important but configuration-dependent economic factors. Application professionals described barriers involving price–performance relationships, qualification and regulatory requirements, process compatibility and quality variability. These barriers differed within as well as between sectors, and reported trials and finished-product sales qualified a uniformly negative assessment. The findings suggest that production, processing and delivery need to be adapted to the intended end application. Exploratory gap scores and market calculations are reported separately as assumption-dependent tools, not validated rankings or adoption forecasts. Functional benefits may support particular applications, but cannot be assumed to resolve other integration requirements. Carbon-removal demand is likely to remain important for scaling several business models, although the interviews do not establish universal dependence on credits. The study identifies application-specific development priorities and policy options requiring further quantitative evaluation. title: Cognitive Effects of Using LLMs for Process Modeling: An EEG Study
abstract: We investigate the cognitive effects of using large language models (LLMs) for BPMN process modeling. To this aim, we conducted electroencephalographic (EEG) experiments to measure brain activity during AI-assisted vs. non-assisted modeling. Participants were divided into two groups – a group with AI assistance (“LLM group”) and a group that had to model manually (“brain-only group”) – and were then asked to create a BPMN process model in the respective setting. Our results indicate significant differences in brain activities for the two groups, in particular, LLM users exhibited strongly reduced active cognitive engagement across multiple EEG measures such as theta power, alpha power and frontal alpha asymmetry. Furthermore, a post-experiment survey one week after the laboratory session also revealed that participants who used the LLM showed significantly lower memory and ownership of the model they had created. Combined with the EEG results, our findings raise concerns regarding the use of LLMs for process modeling, in particular, in regard to reduced cognitive engagement, weaker recall, and reduced ownership. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: From Global Policies to Local Strategies: Multi-objective Optimization of Resource-Specific Handover Policies
abstract: Efficient resource allocation is a key challenge in business process management, with direct implications for cost, throughput time, and utilization. While recent Reinforcement Learning (RL) approaches have shown promise in deriving adaptive allocation policies, they typically neglect inter-resource collaboration patterns that can strongly influence real-world task handovers. Recognizing this, this paper introduces the first approach for multi-objective optimization of resource-level decision-making, enabling the recommendation of person-specific handover policies. To achieve this, our work combines an existing Multi-Agent System-based process simulator with a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm. The resulting approach produces Pareto-optimal, resource-specific policies that optimize the process across multiple objectives. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets show that our approach reduces costs by an average of 37% and waiting time by 58%, consistently outperforming heuristic baselines and demonstrating the potential of leveraging collaboration-aware optimization to improve process performance. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Semi-automated vs. Manual Process Model Generation: A Comparative Study of the Process of Process Modeling
abstract: Due to recent advances in large language models (LLMs), semi-automated approaches to business process modeling have emerged. These fundamentally shift the modeling task from manual model creation to prompt-based model generation and refinement. Prior research has focused on the capability of LLMs to generate (BPMN 2.0) process models, but little evidence exists on the way the involvement of an LLM affects the process of process modeling itself. This paper investigates how semi-automated process modeling with the assistance of an LLM-based chatbot differs from manual process modeling (i.e., with the use of a common modeling tool) with respect to efficiency, cognitive load, and process model quality. A controlled eye-tracking study was conducted with 24 participants, with each participant creating process models manually as well as semi-automatically with an LLM-based chatbot. Efficiency was measured through task completion time, cognitive load was assessed through eye-tracking metrics and NASA-TLX scores, and process model quality was evaluated with respect to syntactic and semantic correctness. Our results show that semi-automated model creation significantly increases efficiency and reduces both objective and subjective cognitive load. Notably, these advantages do not come at the expense of process model quality. The LLM-generated process models exhibited only moderate syntactic errors and achieved very high semantic accuracy. Overall, the findings highlight the potential of LLM-based semi-automated process modeling to improve the process of process modeling. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: What Do Process Embeddings Learn? A Probing Investigation
abstract: Process representation learning transforms event data into numeric vectors, called embeddings, that machine learning models can use for downstream tasks like prediction, clustering, or anomaly detection. To support these tasks, the goal is to create general-purpose embeddings that encode all relevant data properties. However, embeddings are typically evaluated by downstream task performance, assessing only task-specific quality. Thus, it remains unclear which properties of the event data are encoded in the embeddings and how accessible they are, making it difficult to design, improve or compare task-agnostic general-purpose embeddings. To address this issue, we present a probing evaluation framework that investigates embeddings of process instances by training small classifiers, called probes, to recover predefined process properties. We define seven probing tasks, each dedicated to one property, ranging from simple ones, like duration, to more complex ones, like order relations. We apply the framework to embeddings from three existing representation learning approaches on synthetic and real-life event data. The results show that the embeddings reliably encode simple properties, but have difficulties with more complex ones. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Trend-risk vs trend-of-risk in portfolio optimization context
abstract: This paper examines two highly relevant, distinct perspectives on trend-depending risk in portfolio decision-making, building on Neděla et al. (2024). In particular, trend-risk, which incorporates trend information extracted from asset cumulative returns, and the newly proposed trend-of-risk (ToR), which focuses on the temporal trend of the risk measure itself. We study and propose portfolio optimization frameworks that explicitly differentiate between these approaches. Additionally, we demonstrate how they lead to fundamentally different allocation outcomes despite identical instantaneous risk levels. By embedding the ToR as a dynamic penalization term, the framework captures the direction and persistence of risk evolution and enables a more forward-looking risk-aware allocation. The empirical findings highlight the conceptual and practical implications of treating risk trends as an intrinsic optimization input rather than a by-product of return dynamics on different markets. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Towards better long-range time series forecasting using generative forecasting
abstract: Long-range time series forecasting is usually based on one of two existing forecasting strategies: Direct Forecasting and Iterative Forecasting, where the former provides low bias, high variance forecasts and the latter leads to low variance, high bias forecasts. In this paper, we propose a new forecasting strategy called Generative Forecasting (GenF), which generates synthetic data for the next few time steps and then makes long-range forecasts based on generated and observed data. We theoretically prove that under certain conditions, GenF can better balance the forecasting variance and bias, leading to a much smaller forecasting error. We implement GenF via three components: (i) a novel conditional Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) based generator for synthetic time series data generation, called CWGAN-TS. (ii) a transformer based predictor, which makes long-range predictions using both generated and observed data. (iii) an information theoretic clustering algorithm to improve the training of both CWGAN-TS and the transformer based predictor. The experimental results on five public datasets demonstrate that GenF significantly outperforms a diverse range of popular benchmarks and classical approaches. Specifically, we find a 5%–11% improvement in predictive performance (i.e., mean absolute error) while having a 15%–50% reduction in parameters compared to the benchmarks. Lastly, we conduct an ablation study to further explore and demonstrate the effectiveness of components comprising GenF. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Inter-class co-movement of retail electricity tariffs and the residential adjustment gradient: evidence from a new Latin American panel
abstract: How do the published retail electricity tariffs of different consumer classes move together, and do the schedules of captive residential users adjust more slowly than those of large consumers? This paper assembles a new harmonised panel of tariff schedules for fourteen Latin American countries, covering 91 per cent of regional consumption, annually (2011–2024) and quarterly (2013–2025). Estimated by a mean-group error-correction model, the three schedules move together in the long run, each correcting a quarter to a third of any disequilibrium per quarter. Error correction is bidirectional, so neither class is weakly exogenous: the estimates identify long-run co-movement between published schedules rather than structural pass-through of wholesale, network or policy costs. The long-run co-movement elasticity declines along the industrial–commercial–residential gradient, from 0.88 between the two large-consumer segments to 0.73 and 0.70 for the residential schedule; no relation reaches one-for-one movement, and the residential shortfall is significant when economies are paired (0.21, p = 0.021, against the industrial schedule). Within the residential class the rate of error correction rises with the consumption block, the least-subsidised block adjusting twice as fast as the lifeline block (−0.21; p = 0.024), a gradient consistent with cross-subsidy design though not evidence of it. Splitting the panel by revision frequency shows the calendar governs the pace of convergence, not its long-run extent. The inter-class differential arises not from residential schedules being revised less often but from each revision moving them less far. The results inform cross-subsidy reform, lifeline design and affordability policy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Queueing modeling and cost analysis of M/G/1/K fault-tolerance machining system with general vacation under N-policy for industrial applications
abstract: This investigation focuses on modeling the performance of an M/G/1/K fault-tolerance machining system (FTMS) that incorporates the general vacation feature under threshold N-policy, along with handling failure recovery and reboot processes. In the system design, the repairman has the flexibility to take a vacation only when no failed machines are present in the system. The repairman returns from vacation and resumes repair operations when the number of failed machines reaches the specified threshold value N. In cases where faults in the system are not successfully detected, the system reconfigures itself by initiating a reboot process. To develop the mathematical model, supplementary variables representing the remaining repair and vacation times are employed to formulate the steady-state Chapman–Kolmogorov equations. These equations are the foundation for deriving explicit formulae for the probability distributions using the Laplace-Stieltjes transform (LST) and the recursive method. The resulting system state probabilities are then utilized to establish various performance measures. The study conducts a sensitivity analysis to explore the influence of different parameters on performance measures. Furthermore, we construct the expected cost function and formulate an optimization problem to determine the minimum cost. The particle swarm optimization (PSO) is employed to solve the optimization problem, and the results are compared with those obtained by implementing a sine cosine algorithm (SCA) to find the optimum cost. The proposed model demonstrates its practical usefulness in industrial settings, especially in the electrical sector for the power supply system (PSS) and the production sector for the plastic bottle processing hub (PBPH). © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: No Species Is an Island, Entire of Itself: Genetic Speciation Algorithm with Interplay among Species
abstract: This paper, with a particular emphasis on Genetic Algorithm (GA), proposes a novel approach that integrates clustering mechanisms, predator-prey dynamics, and a distinctive selection strategy for generating subsequent populations. The proposed evolutionary algorithm, referred to as Genetic Speciation Algorithm with Interplay Among Species (GSAIS), is comprehensively evaluated against several variants of GAs as well as a set of widely adopted state-of-the-art optimization algorithms, recognized among the top-performing winners of recent Congress on Evolutionary Computation (CEC) competitions. This thorough comparative study is performed using the most well-established benchmark functions, covering unimodal, multimodal, hybrid, and composition optimization landscapes. The experiments are conducted on medium-, and large-scale problem instances to evaluate the robustness, scalability, convergence behavior, and solution quality of GSAIS across diverse optimization scenarios. The GSAIS achieved rank 2^nd, and 1^st against the competitors in medium- and large-scale benchmark problems, respectively based on the Friedman Test with receiving 40.3 of top ranking along all instances based on best found and standard deviation rankings. Extensive statistical and computational results demonstrate the effectiveness of GSAIS, highlighting its superior performance in achieving global optimization. The ablation study and sensitivity analysis reveals the positive effect of the incorporated mechanisms in GSAIS in finding global optimization, especially in large scale problems. The findings establish GSAIS as a potential candidate method for addressing optimization problems and underscore its potential to advance the design of next-generation evolutionary algorithms. ©2027 The author(s). title: Debonding-on-demand adhesives for circular automotive manufacturing: Triggering mechanisms, joint performance, and process integration - A systematic review
abstract: Adhesive bonding is a critical enabling technology for lightweight multi-material automotive structures combining steel, aluminium, carbon fibre reinforced polymers (CFRP), and thermoplastics. However, conventional structural adhesives are permanent by design, creating a fundamental conflict with end-of-life recyclability targets that require vehicles to achieve 85% recyclability and 95% recoverability by mass and EV battery packs to use joining methods compatible with disassembly. Debonding-on-demand (DoD) adhesives—systems that maintain structural performance in service but release controllably upon application of an external stimulus— represent a promising reso-lution to this conflict. This paper presents a systematic review of the DoD adhesive literature. Although the literature search spanned 2000–2025 to capture foundational work, the field is recent and the majority of quantitative studies benchmarked here were published between 2019 and 2025; the review therefore emphasises this period while retaining seminal earlier references. Four stimulus categories are covered: thermal (Diels–Alder reversible networks, thermally expandable particles, and vitrimer/covalent adaptable networks), electrical, photothermal/UV, and magnetic/hybrid. Quantitative performance data from over 40 primary studies are benchmarked against automotive lap-shear, fatigue, and crash-stability requirements. Process integration challenges—including paint-shop cure compatibility, trigger de-livery in assembled structures, surface preparation, scalability, and supply-chain incentive alignment—are critically assessed. Key findings are: (i) TEP-modified structural adhesives achieve debonding at 120–175 °C via electromagnetic induction while maintaining 20–25 MPa pre-debond lap-shear strength on CFRP/Al/steel substrates; (ii) Diels–Alder epoxy systems now reach competitive lap-shear strengths of 12–16 MPa with debonding at 140 °C, whilst vitrimer adhesives provide an emerging route to recyclable structural bonding; (iii) the split-incentive problem is the dominant systemic barrier to adoption; and (iv) no standardised DoD test protocol, long-term durability data, or comprehensive life-cycle assessment currently exists. Five research gaps define the agenda for future work. © 2026 The Author

title: Customizable Declarative Process Specification Scenarios via Automated Planning
abstract: Declarative specifications define the behaviour of processes by means of temporal rules exerting dependencies between the occurrence of activities. Those rules can constitute the system requirements and normative boundaries within which the workflow is framed. The multitude of rules and their interrelations, though, make it reportedly difficult for users to linearly figure out unfoldings that depict the admitted behaviour in the form of explicative scenarios. While simulation engines can produce example traces of customizable length and in varying numerosity, these state-of-the-art tools adopt random approaches that do not permit the selection of a subset of runs exhibiting characteristic traits. In other words, simulations could produce traces that show common behavior, leaving out significant parts of the possible execution paths, and thus substantially hindering a proper validation of specifications. To mitigate this issue, we propose a principled solution that leverages automated planning to produce execution scenarios depicting the specified behavior according to desirable execution costs, diversifying the enacted behavior, or matching a given subsequence of steps. We demonstrate its efficiency and efficacy through experiments demonstrating its scalability and superiority in terms of behavioral coverage with respect to the state-of-the-art simulation tool for declarative process specifications. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Online Resource-Aware Process Configuration with Uncertain Arrivals and Stochastic Resource Consumption
abstract: Business processes are often executed in multiple variants, which affect operational costs and the consumption of shared resource capacities. We study an online planning problem in which process instances arrive sequentially and must be configured irrevocably upon arrival under horizon-wide resource capacity constraints. For example, in a hospital, an unknown number of patients arrive sequentially during a shift. The patient’s diagnosis consumes capacity of available resources and the resources then chosen for allocation, in turn, affect the resulting control flow configuration for this patient. We formulate the problem as an online integer program (IP) with a fixed configuration space and model uncertainty through (i) a random number of arrivals and (ii) stochastic, positive resource consumptions revealed upon arrival; costs are modeled as a weighted sum of consumed workload, reflecting processing time, and thus are also stochastic. We assess rolling-horizon and resource-pricing (primal-dual) approaches and compare them with simple heuristics and the optimal ex post solution. We instantiate the framework for a hospital diagnostics data set. Using distribution estimates based on this data, we evaluate online decision policies under robustness perturbations. The findings show that optimization-based policies that account for remaining capacities and expected demand substantially improve throughput and resource utilization under uncertain arrivals. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Neuro-symbolic AI for BPM: A Tutorial on Predictive and Prescriptive Process Analytics
abstract: Process analytics has become predominantly data-driven: deep sequence models such as LSTMs and Transformers now dominate predictive and prescriptive process monitoring and deliver strong average-case accuracy. These models are, however, opaque, require large amounts of data, and do not incorporate the process knowledge that organizations already hold in the form of regulations, declarative constraints, and reference process models. The symbolic side of Business Process Management (BPM) carries exactly this knowledge but is brittle on noisy, real-world event data. Neuro-symbolic AI (NeSy) aims to bridge these two traditions, and a growing body of BPM work has begun to use it. This tutorial gives the BPM community an accessible overview of the relationship between BPM and NeSy. It introduces Kautz’s architectural taxonomy of NeSy and the Learning from Logical Constraints paradigm together with its main implementation, Logic Tensor Networks. It then traces how NeSy attaches to concrete BPM analytics tasks through a sequence of case studies spanning compliance-aware prediction, robust rule injection, healthcare outcome prediction, and prescriptive analytics. The tutorial highlights the failure modes that practitioners must avoid when injecting domain knowledge into deep process models, examines how to evaluate whether injected knowledge actually helps, and closes with open problems and a practical decision aid for when NeSy is worth adopting. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: From Descriptive to Predictive Analytics in Healthcare Service Operations: A Strategic Analysis of AI-Driven Digital Twins for Emergency Department Capacity Management
abstract: Many modern business processes operate under congestion: stochastic demand, shared and limited resources, complex routing, and tight service-level constraints. From healthcare and public services to logistics, financial operations, and large-scale customer support, these systems exhibit nonlinear behavior where small disruptions propagate quickly and performance deteriorates sharply. This paper examines how Business Process Management (BPM) can evolve to address congestion-driven environments by integrating process mining, queueing theory, simulation, and machine learning and artificial intelligence (ML&AI) into digital twins. We discuss how descriptive analytics must move beyond static dashboards toward data-driven process models that reveal how processes actually unfold in practice—capturing routing variability, rework loops, synchronization delays, and resource contention. Process mining provides structural visibility; queueing-aware modeling explains performance; ML&AI supports prediction under uncertainty. Building on these foundations, predictive and comparative analytics enable counterfactual “what-if” evaluation of staffing, routing, prioritization, and scheduling policies before implementation. Finally, prescriptive analytics embedded within real-time digital twins allow organizations to intervene proactively—anticipating congestion, reallocating capacity, and mitigating cascading delays. Drawing on industrial deployments through SiMLQ, we demonstrate how combining process intelligence with congestion-aware operational modeling transforms BPM from retrospective analysis into continuous, real-time decision support. The implications extend across service industries where variability and resource contention define performance, resilience, and competitiveness. Emergency departments are not failing because clinicians lack commitment; they are failing because the operating system that coordinates demand, staffing, beds, diagnostics, specialist consultation, and inpatient transfers remains largely reactive. Digital twins that are based on extensive descriptive analytics can transform fragmented event data into a safe, continuously updated environment for prediction, counterfactual evaluation, and prescriptive action. The managerial implication is blunt: modern businesses, such as hospitals that rely only on after-the-fact statistics will remain trapped in decision blind spots. Businesses that build validated digital twins would move capacity management upstream, detect failure before it occurs, and redirect scarce resources to the highest-leverage bottlenecks in real time. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Energy service companies as transition intermediaries: Functions, business models, and prospects for demand-side decarbonization
abstract: Energy service companies (ESCOs) are established delivery vehicles for energy efficiency, but the literature remains fragmented across contract studies, country surveys, financing analyses and emerging digital-service research. This fragmentation leaves a specific knowledge gap: how ESCOs combine technical, financial, contractual, data and institutional functions to act as transition intermediaries, and under what conditions those functions generate additional, persistent and scalable demand-side decarbonization. This structured narrative review synthesizes 129 peer-reviewed and institutional sources published mainly between 2010 and 2026. It develops a transition-intermediary framework, compares contractual and organizational models, proposes a common quantitative performance scorecard, and links ESCO market development to policy, finance, technology, risk allocation and client capability. The evidence indicates that ESCO projects reported average energy savings of about 25% in 2024, while U.S. federal projects delivered reported cost savings equal to 101.0% of estimates and 108.5% of guarantees. These benchmarks demonstrate performance potential but do not support a universal ranking of shared savings, guaranteed savings, Super ESCO and energy-as-a-service models because contract choice is endogenous to client credit, technology mix, project depth and market maturity. The review further shows that ESCO opportunities extend to electrification, distributed energy resources, storage, demand response, flexibility, digital twins, artificial intelligence and carbon MRV. However, transaction costs, baseline disputes, shallow-retrofit incentives, long-term lock-in, data dependence and exclusion of less creditworthy clients can weaken outcomes. We conclude that ESCOs should be evaluated as institutional infrastructure for demand-side implementation rather than as a narrow retrofit industry. A future agenda is organized into five macro-areas and nine linked priorities spanning evidence, market design, contracts, digitalization, system integration and justice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Cost sharing in joint resource purchasing: balancing efficiency improvements and cost savings
abstract: Joint resource purchasing by a subset of decision-making units (DMUs) may offer cost savings, such as bulk discounts, group buying deals, and lower shipping costs; however, determining an appropriate allocation of the resulting discounted total procurement cost becomes a key challenge. Existing studies largely focus on fixed cost allocation, where all DMUs participate in and allocated cost is treated as a new or complementary input of DMUs. However, these approaches fail to address a scenario where only a subset of DMUs jointly procures resources, and the cost to be allocated is the discounted total procurement cost that remains attributable to the input consumption of the participating DMUs. To address this limitation, we develop a novel data envelopment analysis (DEA)-based approach for the issue of cost sharing in joint resource purchasing. First, a traditional DEA model is used to evaluate DMUs’ efficiencies by treating the original procurement cost as an input. We then formulate a multi-objective programming model based on DEA to allocate the discounted total procurement cost among the participating DMUs to optimize their efficiencies. The proposed model ensures group, individual, and coalitional rationality, and incorporates a decision rule to select a unique allocation that balances efficiency improvements with cost savings. We illustrate the approach with an application to 34 hotels, in which 10 hotels located in the same city jointly purchase resources and share the discounted cost. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Impact of substitution on product families’ competition in networked markets
abstract: The competition among product families supplied by different firms in networked markets is constructed as a bipartite graph model. Based on matrix analysis, the Cournot equilibrium of the product families’ competition is derived. Then, the impact of substitution between product varieties on product families’ competition is analyzed. The results show that when the networked markets were symmetric, the firms’ profits and total consumer surplus all decreased in substitution. But when networked markets are asymmetric, the profits increased in substitution for the firms with a smaller total commonality index or few product varieties, or supplying a segmented market with a larger demand intercept. Even in the asymmetric networked markets, the consumer surplus also decreases in substitution. Furthermore, in the networked markets with asymmetric total commonality index, firms exhibit a stronger inclination to form alliances at moderate substitution levels, and a weaker willingness when the substitution was on both sides. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Green Business Process Management: Approaches, Challenges, and Ways Forward
abstract: In light of increasing environmental concerns faced by organizations and society, the Business Process Management (BPM) community has developed the Green BPM sub-field. With a wide array of approaches and capabilities, environmental impacts of business processes can be assessed and reduced, allowing organizations to establish environmentally sustainable practices. While receiving significant research interest over the last fifteen years, Green BPM is still a marginal topic at the BPM conference, as well as in BPM practice. In this tutorial, we provide a general introduction into Green BPM, and present two alternative approaches for integrating notions of environmental sustainability into Green BPM. We discuss challenges associated with the “process lens” of Green BPM, both from a theoretical and practical angle. With our tutorial, we aim to create awareness for the rich stream of existing Green BPM research and ultimately for the potential for further relevant and valuable contributions to be made by BPM researchers. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: SCREEN-LCA: Ex-ante prioritization of bio-based pathways for chemicals and plastics under a climate-mitigation objective
abstract: Life cycle assessment (LCA) is a key tool for guiding circular bioeconomy strategies, including the substitution of fossil carbon with bioresources. However, its data- and time-intensive nature can hinder its use when there are numerous candidate pathways, particularly in the chemical sector. Here, we developed SCREEN-LCA, a stepwise ex-ante framework designed to prioritize case studies before conducting full LCA. The framework combines: (i) sector-level impact estimation; (ii) identification of hotspot products within targeted sectors; (iii) mapping of corresponding alternative bio-based pathways; and (iv) pathway prioritization based on multiple criteria. We applied SCREEN-LCA in a France-oriented demonstration to prioritize residual-biomass-based pathways for subsequent LCA. The greenhouse gas footprint of incumbent petrochemicals and plastics, feedstock compatibility, and technological maturity were used as screening criteria. An extensive graph database covering 50 hotspot products and their alternative bio-based routes was assembled. Ethylene, propylene, methanol, and PET emerged as priorities with promising bio-based alternatives. title: Greener Urban Environments, Greater Climate Anxiety? Pro-Environmental Behavior and Well-Being Across Levels of Green-Space Provision
abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that urban green space may alleviate climate anxiety, reinforcing its conventional role as a psychologically restorative environment. Yet this relationship may be more complex than a uniformly protective effect. This study examines whether perceived green built environments are associated with climate risk perception and climate anxiety, and whether climate anxiety, pro-environmental behavior, and well-being are differently associated across levels of neighborhood green-space provision. We analyzed survey data from 434 residents across four Taipei districts using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and multi-group analysis (PLS-MGA). Contrary to a purely protective interpretation, perceived green built environments were positively associated with both climate risk perception and climate anxiety. Climate anxiety was positively associated with pro-environmental behavior but showed no significant direct association with well-being, whereas pro-environmental behavior was strongly associated with greater well-being. This latter association was significantly stronger in high-green than in low-green districts. These findings highlight the complexity of human–environment relationships under climate change, showing that urban greenness may coexist with greater climate-related awareness and anxiety and that the psychological relevance of pro-environmental behavior varies across green-space conditions. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Eutectic solvent platform for the selective isolation and one-year stabilisation of astaxanthin from crustacean shell waste
abstract: Astaxanthin is a high-value natural carotenoid with strong antioxidant activity, attractive colour properties, and broad potential for use in food, cosmetics, nutraceuticals, and pharmaceutical formulations. However, its practical application is limited by its low stability and the need for sustainable and selective extraction strategies from renewable feedstocks. In this work, crustacean shell waste was explored as a circular source of astaxanthin, using (deep) eutectic solvents (DES) as alternative extraction media. A series of DES based on choline chloride or tetrabutylammonium bromide combined with different hydrogen bond donors was screened for the selective solid-liquid extraction of astaxanthin from shrimp shell waste. Tetrabutylammonium bromide-based DES outperformed choline chloride-based systems, particularly [N4,4,4,4]Br:hexanol and [N4,4,4,4]Br:octanoic acid. Response surface methodology was then used to optimise the solid-liquid ratio (SLR) and extraction time. [N4,4,4,4]Br:hexanol achieved an astaxanthin mass balance of ~80% with minimal co-extraction of proteins (~20%) and no extraction of minerals or chitin, with a SLR of 0.4 g mL-1 and 10 min of extraction time. The long-term stability of astaxanthin in the selected DES was also evaluated for one year under different temperature and light conditions. Astaxanthin showed remarkable stability in [N4,4,4,4]Br:hexanol, retaining approximately 44% of its initial content after 365 days at 25 °C in the dark while maintaining a visible orange-red colour. Kinetic modelling further confirmed this stability, estimating a half-life (t1/2) of 265 and 282 days based on first- and second-order kinetic models, respectively. These results demonstrate that [N4,4,4,4]Br:hexanol can act simultaneously as an efficient extraction solvent and a stabilising medium, reducing downstream processing while enabling the sustainable valorisation of crustacean shell waste into stable natural colourants. © 2026 The Authors

title: A LLM-Powered Multi-agent System for Cross-View Integration in Digital Government Systems
abstract: Improving digital government performance requires the coherent integration of performance (indicator), business, and data views, yet supporting materials are typically expressed in unstructured, inconsistent natural language, making manual consolidation inefficient and unsustainable. To address this cross-view integration challenge, we propose an LLM-powered multi-agent system that automatically (i) extracts performance indicators, business processes, and data associated with business activities (ii) establishes mappings across them, and (iii) generates optimization recommendations to refine both views and mappings. A case study on a smart court project demonstrates the system’s effectiveness in producing accurate, explainable, and actionable cross-view integration. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Port coordination dilemmas in green shipping corridors under unilateral carbon policies
abstract: Under unilateral carbon regulation, including the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS), green shipping corridors (GSCs) face asymmetric coordination challenges among ports and shipping companies (SCs). We develop a tripartite evolutionary game incorporating reduced-form SC heterogeneity, carbon-price feedback, an attractiveness-based green-capacity allocation rule, and stochastic disturbances. A real-world-informed synthetic Europe–Southern Africa container-shipping scenario supports the analysis. Results show that the EU ETS strengthens SC cooperation incentives, but full cooperation requires sustainable port payoffs. The developing-country port lies near its cooperation threshold and is sensitive to incremental green-business revenue, subsidies, and green operational capability. Under the specified rule, improvements in this port’s attractiveness increase its modeled share of configurable green-service demand and can support cooperation without undermining the developed-country port’s cooperation incentive. Stochastic disturbances amplify differences across evolutionary paths for the weaker port. Green-capacity allocation thus links port heterogeneity, competition, and cooperation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Exploring the Impact of Soft Preventive Judicial Measures on Business Resilience and Performance Under Organised Crime Infiltration: Evidence from a Multi-Case Analysis
abstract: Organised crime infiltration in legitimate businesses threatens market functioning, firm governance and local economic development. In Italy, alongside seizure and confiscation, the Anti-Mafia Code introduced continuity-preserving “soft” preventive measures—judicial administration (Art. 34) and judicial control (Art. 34-bis)—aimed at interrupting criminal influence while keeping firms operating. Yet, firm-level evidence on their economic and organisational consequences remains limited. This study adopts an organisational resilience perspective and investigates how firms’ operating and financial conditions evolve around these interventions. We conduct a comparative multi-case analysis of 11 firms subjected to Arts. 34/34-bis, identified through judicial records and matched with peer groups by sector, size and geography using AIDA data. We reconstruct trajectories across pre-intervention, intervention, and post-intervention phases using four indicators: value of production, current ratio, net income and debt-to-equity. Findings suggest that soft preventive measures mainly operate as contingent stabilisers: they support operational continuity, but liquidity, profitability and capital structure remain fragile, especially after the judicial phase. The study contributes by opening the firm-level process between preventive judicial intervention and economic outcomes, offering mechanism-oriented evidence that complements existing research on anti-mafia policies. © The Author(s) 2027.

title: Semantic similarity score: A new method for mapping intellectual structures in business research
abstract: The rapid growth of scientific knowledge makes traditional science mapping increasingly challenging. Existing methods (e.g., citations, co-citation, and bibliographic coupling) rely heavily on lagging citation data. Consequently, they often fail to construct a comprehensive structural image of scientific fields and are ineffective at tracking novel publications and identifying emerging research. To address these limitations, we propose the Semantic Similarity Score (S3), which leverages transformer models to assess the semantic and conceptual similarity of titles and abstracts. We applied this method across two broad domains, ‘Innovation and Diversity’ and ‘Ecosystems in Business’, and evaluated its performance using three performance metrics: Topic Coherence, Silhouette Index, and Quality Index. The results demonstrate that our content-based approach significantly outperforms both established citation-based techniques and standard transformer-based topic modeling methods, offering a more precise approach to mapping both established and emerging intellectual structures. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: First report of the nesting whitefly, Paraleyrodes pseudonaranjae Martin (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae) on coconut in Bangladesh and its co-occurrence with other invasive whitefly species
abstract: The nesting whitefly (NW), Paraleyrodes pseudonaranjae Martin (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae), is an invasive and highly polyphagous species originating from the Neotropics that has recently expanded into Asia. Here, we report the first confirmed occurrence of P. pseudonaranjae in Bangladesh, detected on coconut palm (Cocos nucifera L.) in Mymensingh, a north-central district of the country. Species identity was confirmed based on morphological characteristics and DNA barcoding of the mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (mtCOI) gene. Morphological examination confirmed key diagnostic features of P. pseudonaranjae, including “modified X-shaped” grey bands on the forewings and distinct male genitalia, clearly distinguishing it from the morphologically similar species, Paraleyrodes bondari. Molecular analysis of the mtCOI gene revealed 99–100% nucleotide identity with reference sequences from India and China. Phylogenetic analysis using the Maximum Likelihood method placed the Bangladeshi isolates firmly within the P. pseudonaranjae clade, with strong bootstrap support, clustering closely with invasive lineages reported from India and China. Field surveys conducted across five locations revealed consistent co-occurrence of P. pseudonaranjae, P. bondari, and Aleurodicus rugioperculatus on coconut palm. Notably, the relative abundance of P. pseudonaranjae increased markedly from 6.40–14.60% in June (2025) to 27.40–36.40% in December 2025, accompanied by a substantial decline in A. rugioperculatus (90.20–81.40% to 67.90–58.10%), while P. bondari remained at low abundance. This consistent pattern across locations suggests rapid establishment of P. pseudonaranjae and potential competitive interactions with co-occurring whitefly species, A. rugioperculatus and P. bondari. This study provides the first confirmed record of P. pseudonaranjae in Bangladesh and highlights its rapid establishment on coconut palm. Given its broad host range and increasing abundance, this species poses a potential threat to tropical agroecosystems, underscoring the need for urgent surveillance and development of effective management strategies. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature B.V. 2026.

title: Disulfide bond cleavage in lentil legumin enhances interfacial properties at liquid interfaces
abstract: Plant proteins often have inferior functional properties compared to animal-based proteins with respect to emulsion and foam stabilization because their larger and more rigid complex structures affect their ability to form a cohesive and stiff interfacial layer. To enhance film formation at liquid interfaces, molecular properties can be changed by using reducing agents such as dithiothreitol (DTT) to cleave disulfide bonds. Here, we explore this strategy for lentil legumin, one of the main proteins in lentils for which its structure is held together by covalent and noncovalent bonds, particularly disulfide bonds, giving it a rigid structure. Legumin was modified with different DTT concentrations (5, 50, and 100 mM) to obtain different degrees of modification. Disulfide bond cleavage in legumin led to increased surface hydrophobicity, resulting in enhanced adsorption kinetics, while particle size and surface charge remained similar to those of native legumin. Native and modified legumin were studied for their interfacial rheology at both oil-water and air-water interfaces. The interface formed by the modified legumin was stiffer than that of native legumin at both interfaces. The increased stiffness of the oil-water interface was attributed to the formation of denser interfacial layers rather than to stronger in-plane protein-protein interactions. In contrast, the stiffer air-water interface was associated with both stronger in-plane protein interactions and formation of denser interfaces. This was also confirmed by visualization of the interfacial film at the air-water interface, where the modified legumin formed denser and more cohesive networks than native legumin. Lastly, emulsion formation and stability were studied to assess whether structural changes following legumin modification affect stability on the macroscopic scale. Both native and modified legumin displayed stable emulsions against droplet flocculation and coalescence for 14 days, owing to the droplets having sufficient surface charge. The increased interfacial stiffness did not have a significant effect on stability. The Authors This is an open access article under the CC BY license. http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
