title: Genome-Wide Identification and Expression Profiles of NAT Gene Family in Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) and Their Potential Roles during Stolon-to-Tuber Development
abstract: N-terminal acetyltransferases (NATs) catalyze protein N-terminal acetylation, which is crucial for plant growth, development, stress responses, and metabolic regulation. This study identified 40 StNAT members (StNAT1-StNAT40) in potato. Most were predicted to be hydrophilic cytoplasmic proteins, whereas only StNAT10 and StNAT36 were hydrophobic proteins localized to chloroplast and cytoplasm, respectively, suggesting possible functional divergence. Tandem repeats appeared to play a dominant role in StNAT family expansion. StNAT promoters contained cis-elements associated with hormone response, growth and development, circadian regulation, stress response, and transcriptional regulation. Based on conserved motif and gene structure, the 40 StNATs were divided into three subgroups. Within each subgroup, motif composition and distribution were relatively consistent, whereas significant differences were observed among subgroups. Ten representatives of StNATs were selected from the three subgroups for qRT-PCR analysis. The results showed that the representatives of subgroup I were ubiquitously expressed in various tissues, whereas all the representatives of subgroup II and III exhibited high expression in tubers and stolons, suggesting possible involvement in stolon-to-tuber development. Among these members, the majority exhibited a “V”-shaped expression pattern during stolon-to-tuber transition, peaking at stolon initiation and swelling stages but declining at stolon elongation stage. Some members showed stage-specific high expression at stolon initiation stage (StNAT22 and StNAT32) or swelling stage (StNAT4). Additionally, most members were induced by low GA₃ in stolons, whereas StNAT38 was down-regulated and StNAT2/29 were up-regulated with increasing GA₃, suggesting possible roles in GA-mediated stolon-to-tuber development. These findings suggested that StNATs might play important roles in stolon-to-tuber development, warranting further functional verification. This study provides new insights into the genetic improvement of potato tuber yield and quality. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to European Association for Potato Research 2026.

title: Triboelectric E-Skin Patch Decoding Silent Speech for Advanced Human–Machine Interaction and Augmented Virtual Communication
abstract: Silent speech decoding (lip reading) represents an innovative hands-free communication method for individuals with laryngeal and lingual impairments, addressing critical daily communication challenges. Herein, a novel silent speech decoding system is proposed, which employs a self-powered, low-cost, and conformable triboelectric-based E‑skin patch and a well-trained multi-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) model. We systematically characterize the structural principles and electrical performance of the E-skin patch. A comparative analysis of labial kinematics during vocalized and silent speech is also conducted, which demonstrates strong consistency in time–frequency domain characteristics. The utilized CNN model is trained across 15 lexical categories (200 samples per category), achieving a high accuracy of 98.75% and demonstrating excellent recognition performance. Furthermore, by integrating human–machine interaction (HMI) and virtual reality (VR) technologies, we develop three representative applications, including a real-time lip language visualization system, an orofacial-controlled “Feeding Frenzy” interactive game, and a VR communication platform with avatar dialogue. This technology enables barrier-free communication for voiceless populations, demonstrating significant potential in HMI, augmentative communication systems, virtual reality integration, and biomedical rehabilitation. title: Foreign Entrepreneurship in the District of Municipalities of Catania and Messina: Preliminary Findings
abstract: This chapter examines immigrant entrepreneurship in the metropolitan areas of Catania and Messina in Sicily, focusing on foreign-born business owners holding an Italian VAT number. Based on a quantitative survey of 83 cases, the study analyses entrepreneurial trajectories, business characteristics, startup resources, support networks, and relations with the institutional system. The findings show that migrant businesses are concentrated in retail trade, food services, and personal care and are mainly organized as microenterprises and sole proprietorships. Startup capital derives mostly from personal and family savings, while access to formal credit remains limited. Family and community networks play a crucial role in both business creation and daily management, whereas relations with formal support systems remain weak. Overall, immigrant entrepreneurship emerges as both a strategy of socio-economic stabilization and a resource for local development and social cohesion. © The Author(s) 2027.

title: Mapping Migrant Entrepreneurship and Integration in Italy: A Descriptive Analysis
abstract: This chapter analyses migrant entrepreneurship and migrant integration in Italy, examining their interaction across provinces between 2013 and 2022. Using an original dataset covering 102 provinces and 24 economic sectors, the study reconstructs the evolution, sectoral structure, and territorial distribution of foreign individual-owned firms (self-employment), alongside two composite integration indicators: the Social Integration Index and the Occupational Integration Index. Results show a steady growth of migrant entrepreneurship. Moreover, while integration indicators generally improve, particularly in labour market participation, structural differences persist across provinces. Multivariate analyses indicate that higher entrepreneurial intensity and sectoral diversification tend to be associated with stronger local integration outcomes. © The Author(s) 2027.

title: A skew generalization of the Amitsur–Small Theorem
abstract: We introduce the notion of rigid extensions to generalize a key lemma underlying the Amitsur–Small Theorem to the skew setting. Building on this framework, we establish a skew version of the Amitsur–Small Theorem. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Built-in electric field-driven charge separation in an MXene@TiO2/PdTCPP-HOF S-scheme heterojunction for photocatalytic hydrogen evolution
abstract: Hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) have recently emerged as promising photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen evolution; however, their practical efficiency is severely constrained by rapid charge-carrier recombination and inefficient charge transport. Herein, we hypothesize that constructing an intimate S-scheme heterojunction between MXene-derived TiO2 and PdTCPP-based HOFs can induce interfacial charge redistribution and generate a built-in electric field (IEF), thereby enabling directional carrier migration and enhanced photocatalytic activity. Based on this concept, an MXene@TiO2/PdTCPP-HOFs heterojunction was fabricated via an in-situ self-assembly strategy. As a result, the optimized MXene@TiO2/PdTCPP-HOF photocatalyst achieves a high hydrogen evolution rate of 3412 μmol g−1 h−1, which is approximately 20.3 and 2.7 times higher than those of MXene@TiO2 and PdTCPP-HOFs, respectively. Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM), in-situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy ( in-situ XPS), and density functional theory calculations (DFT) collectively reveal the interfacial charge-transfer behavior and S-scheme photocatalytic mechanism. This work offers a promising strategy for modulating interfacial electric fields and charge-carrier dynamics in HOF-based heterojunctions toward efficient photocatalytic hydrogen production. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: COD-ssi: Enforcing Mutual Privacy for Credential Oblivious Disclosure in Self Sovereign Identity
abstract: The Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI) paradigm is instrumental for decentralised identity management, allowing an entity to create, manage, and present their digital credentials without relying on centralised authorities. Credential Selective Disclosure (SD) is one of the most attractive privacy-preserving features of SSI, allowing users to partially reveal information from their credentials. However, current SD mechanisms primarily focus on protecting Holders’ privacy, while credential Verifiers. Indeed, the specific information requested by a Verifier can inadvertently reveal sensitive information, including internal decision-making criteria, business rules, or strategic plans. In this work, we address this threat by proposing, to the best of our knowledge, the first approach enforcing mutual privacy in credential exchanges. To this end, we introduce COD-ssi (Credential Oblivious Disclosure for SSI), a novel framework that leverages Oblivious Pseudorandom Functions to allow credential selective access without revealing to the credential Holder which specific claims were requested. The security of our solution is formally verified and its feasibility is assessed through the experimental evaluation of our open-source prototype implementation, showing that provable mutual privacy in the context of SSI can be achieved with just moderate computational and communication overhead. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: “Made in heaven, matched by parents”: Can arranged marriage restrict labour market autonomy and participation of women?
abstract: This paper investigates whether parent-arranged marriage causally reduces women's post-marriage labour market autonomy and participation. We conceptualize and separately estimate two distinct dimensions of women's labour market engagement: autonomy (the power to decide whether to work) and participation (the actual decision to work), a distinction overlooked in the existing literature. Using a nationally representative sample of approximately 30,000 currently married women from the India Human Development Survey (2011–12), we estimate causal effects using an instrumental variable strategy that exploits the intergenerational persistence of community marriage norms. Our primary instrument uses lagged marriage-type prevalence within state-caste cells; a second, Leave-One-Out instrument—constructed from other-caste groups’ historical patterns—serves simultaneously as a robustness check and a falsification test, with both instruments yielding statistically indistinguishable estimates. Relative to parent-arranged marriages, self-matched marriages causally increase labour market autonomy by 30 percentage points and participation by 14–16 percentage points; jointly-arranged marriages yield gains of 22 and 10–11 percentage points, respectively. These effects are large, given that only 42% of women in our sample report autonomy over work decisions. Heterogeneity analysis suggests that the pronounced asymmetry between autonomy and participation arises from structural barriers rather than women's preferences. Our findings imply that policies targeting marriage norms must be complemented by supply-side labour market interventions to achieve commensurate gains in women's economic participation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Paradoxical Psychology in disability entrepreneurship
abstract: Social exclusion and constraint shape how individuals with disabilities mobilize psychological dispositions and resources, calling for a perspective on disability entrepreneurship that departs from mainstream entrepreneurship research. This study compares entrepreneurs and non-entrepreneurs with disabilities to examine these distinct motivational dynamics. The findings reveal a paradoxical structure: entrepreneurial self-efficacy is negatively associated with entrepreneurial motivation, whereas self-stigma and resilience are negatively associated with self-efficacy yet positively associated with motivation. These dynamics also differ by entrepreneurial status. These patterns may be interpreted in terms of constraint-induced and adaptive motivational pathways. The findings suggest that disability entrepreneurship may constitute a contextual boundary condition for prevailing theories of entrepreneurial motivation and position resilience as a context-dependent rather than uniformly beneficial resource. Support programs should be tailored to the distinct motivational processes of entrepreneurs and non-entrepreneurs with disabilities. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: What determines the adoption of space cooling technology in households? Evidence from regions in Belgium and Poland
abstract: Frequent heatwaves are common, especially during the climate crisis. Hence, the topic of mitigating the impact of hot summer days is attracting increasing attention, and the demand for cooling solutions is rising. This research aims to identify and assess the factors that individuals in the Antwerp Province of Belgium and the Kuyavian-Pomeranian Voivodeship of Poland might consider when adopting a cooling solution. These regions are experiencing heatwaves during the summer, which are becoming more frequent, intense, and prolonged due to climate change. These two regions are characterized by similar population sizes (∼2 million) but differ in climate, urbanization, and economic roles, making them suitable for comparative analysis. This study employs a discrete choice experiment to examine households' preferences for cooling options, considering the following characteristics: thermal comfort, air quality, sound level, environmental impact, lifespan, and cost. The results indicate that in the Polish region, which is in a more extreme climate zone, households are much more willing to invest in cooling technology than those living in Antwerp Province, which has a milder climate. The Willingness-to-Pay analysis revealed that reduced noise is the most valuable feature of household cooling solutions in the Belgium region, which is much more densely populated. The air quality improvement feature is most valued in areas where people perceive poor air quality. The study suggests that the business sector should design cooling devices to be silent and more environmentally friendly, and that policymakers should make cooling systems more affordable and accessible. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: The dynamic interplay between subjective and objective cognitive performance and their impact on the prognosis of major depressive disorder: A cross-lagged panel network analysis
abstract: Background Subjective cognitive impairments are highly prevalent in patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) and, consistent with objective cognitive impairments, are associated with greater symptom severity and poorer treatment outcomes. However, their interactions and shared and distinct contributions to depressive symptoms and acute-phase clinical course remain poorly understood. Methods We analyzed 621 patients with MDD at baseline and 373 at Week 8. Treatment comprised usual care in a real-world cohort and antidepressant therapy with perospirone or placebo augmentation in a randomized, double-blind trial. Cross-sectional and cross-lagged networks integrated subjective cognition, objective cognition, and three selected depressive symptom domains. Remission-stratified and sensitivity analyses were conducted. Results Subjective cognition, objective cognition, and depressive symptoms formed distinct interacting modules at both assessments, with global network strength increasing from baseline to Week 8 (ΔS = 0.65, Holm-adjusted p = 0.01). Subjective executive function was most central in non-remitters and objective processing speed in remitters. Accounting for baseline network variables, better baseline subjective executive function was associated with greater Week 8 energy ( β = 0.11), and better baseline subjective memory with greater energy and general interest (both β = 0.06). In contrast, better baseline objective immediate verbal memory was prospectively associated with worse Week 8 levels for sad mood, energy/fatigability, and general interest ( β = −0.12, −0.07, and − 0.05, respectively). Conclusions Subjective and objective cognition showed distinct associations with symptom course, supporting their combined assessment. Better baseline objective memory did not necessarily indicate fewer residual symptoms, but this association does not establish reduced treatment efficacy. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Structural Changes and Supply Elasticity of Potato Production: The Case of Slovenia
abstract: This study investigates the long-term structural transformation and supply responsiveness of potato production in Slovenia, a sector that has experienced a substantial and sustained contraction (more than 90% of total potato area in comparison to 1961) over the past several decades. Drawing on official statistical datasets covering the period from 1961 to 2024, we analyze trends in cultivated area, yields, price dynamics, and regional production patterns. Descriptive statistics, ANOVA, and spatial analyses reveal a marked decline of more than 90% in potato-growing area, contrasted by significant yield improvements attributable to technological progress and farm consolidation. Kernel density analysis of GERK parcel data confirms a highly fragmented production structure, with the vast majority of holdings cultivating less than one hectare and only a small proportion engaging in commercially meaningful production. To evaluate supply elasticity, we estimate a log–log regression model and a Nerlovian partial-adjustment model. The empirical results indicate negligible short-run price elasticity and strong path dependence, with lagged area emerging as the dominant predictor of current production. Long-run elasticity estimates remain weak, underscoring the limited capacity of Slovenian potato producers to adjust to market signals due to structural constraints, including small farm size, perishability of the product, and limited integration into commercial supply chains. The findings highlight a sector characterized by persistent contraction and low supply responsiveness. This evidence contributes to the understanding of supply behavior in structurally constrained agricultural systems and provides an analytical basis for future research and policy interventions targeting farm structure, market development, and regional production potential. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Natural disasters and political beliefs
abstract: This paper examines whether local exposure to extreme weather affects support for national climate and energy policies in Switzerland. We construct a municipality-referendum panel linking high-resolution MeteoSwiss data on extreme heat and intense precipitation to municipal voting outcomes in federal referenda. Using a staggered difference-in-differences design and Callaway–Sant’Anna event-study estimators, we compare municipalities first exposed to extreme weather shocks with not-yet-treated municipalities. The results provide little evidence that extreme weather increases support for environmental policy. If anything, the estimates point in the opposite direction: in selected rainfall specifications, environmental yes-shares decline by around 2.7–2.8 percentage points after extreme shocks. These estimates are based on small, geographically concentrated treated cohorts and should therefore be interpreted as cohort-specific. The findings are consistent with the view that salient local shocks may reduce willingness to support costly environmental policies, rather than producing experience-based updating in favor of climate action. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: A graph-theory-based order batching method for pharmaceutical warehouse with tail-bin coupling avoidance
abstract: As pharmaceutical fulfilment rapidly shifts toward split-case picking, warehouses require order batching methods that balance aggregation efficiency with tail-bin coupling risk. Existing studies rarely consider tail-bin coupling in pharmaceutical split-case picking, which can reduce batching effectiveness and prolong completion time. To address this gap, this study proposes a graph-theoretic order batching model incorporating a master–slave association set mechanism that limits excessive concentration of related orders and mitigates tail-bin coupling risk. A Stock Keeping Units (SKU)-association graph is constructed from SKU-sharing relationships among orders to decompose the order set into independent connected subgraphs. The model minimizes the total number of bin presentations. To solve the model efficiently, we develop a memorized branch-and-bound backtracking algorithm that combines graph decomposition, branch-and-bound pruning, and state memorization, followed by a constrained re-binning merging strategy for global batch reorganization. Numerical experiments show that, compared with GUROBI and ALNS, the proposed algorithm delivers the best overall performance, producing solutions close to the GUROBI optimum with an average deviation below 3 % while greatly improving computational efficiency to satisfy real-time engineering requirements. Tests on different order structures and real business data further confirm the algorithm's applicability and convergence stability in pharmaceutical split-case picking. Wilcoxon and Friedman tests confirm that it significantly outperforms ALNS and other methods. Sensitivity analysis indicates that increasing the order limit of the master correlation set T reduces bin presentations but increases tail-bin coupling risk; thus, setting T to 6–8 is recommended for typical pharmaceutical split-case picking scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Reproducing and benchmarking behavioral similarity methods for business process models
abstract: In our primary work, we presented a comparative evaluation of behavioral similarity methods for business process models, assessing Prime Event Structures (PES), Transition Adjacency Relations (TAR) and trace alignment computed with PM4Py on the Process Model Matching Contest 2015 benchmark, where PES achieved the highest effectiveness. In this companion paper, we describe how to reproduce the entire experimental study through a Docker-based pipeline, with step-by-step instructions that regenerate every reported result, including the statistical analyses. While making the experiments reproducible, we identified and removed a source of non-determinism in the trace simulation of PM4Py: repeated executions now yield identical values, and the ranking of the three methods reported in the primary work is preserved. We also assess the stability of the findings on systematically generated process model variants with controlled structural and behavioral perturbations, and we explain how the experiments can be extended to new process models, parameters and similarity methods. All materials, including source code, datasets and protocols, are publicly available, enabling exact replication and extension by other researchers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Sensitive Data Protection for Text-to-SQL Tasks in Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) dominate Text-to-SQL tasks thanks to strong language comprehension. Yet domain adaptation demands knowledge distillation and supervised fine-tuning, which usually rely on real business queries full of sensitive information. Direct training on such data brings severe privacy leakage risks. We design a privacy-preserving framework combining data desensitization and knowledge distillation, working in two stages. First, a desensitization pipeline builds rule sets from security standards, uses an LLM to detect sensitive content, and runs context-aware desensitization that retains business logic while wiping private details. Second, a teacher model generates SQL from desensitized text to build high-quality training samples, which fine-tunes a lightweight student model to inherit domain skills without privacy hazards. Experiments show that our pipeline achieves 92.5% sensitive data processing accuracy and cuts costs by 83% over baselines; the student model reaches 91.5% Text-to-SQL accuracy. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

title: Life Cycle Assessment of open single-shield Tunnel Boring Machine Tunnelling: An Integrated Parametric Exploration Framework
abstract: A large-scale parametric Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) approach for TBM tunnelling was developed based on a database of 525 tunnels excavated with Tunnel Boring Machines (TBMs). This framework is intended as an early-stage environmental decision-support tool. System boundaries encompass the TBM life cycle, from manufacturing to End-of-Life, including the operational phase. Two existing parametric models, both dependent on TBM control parameters and geotechnical conditions, were integrated: one estimating excavation electricity consumption and the other assessing disc cutter wear. Parameters were sampled using Sobol’ sequences across 525 TBM-specific experimental designs of 41,984 runs each, yielding approximately 22 million tunnelling configurations and ensuring quasi-uniform coverage of the parameter space. A Sobol’ sensitivity analysis quantified each parameter's contribution to the variance of environmental indicators. Regarding climate change, results show that environmental impacts range from 2.8 to 29.7 tCO2eq per linear metre of tunnel. A Global Sensitivity Analysis (GSA) using Sobol’ indices identified 12 to 16 parameters explaining from 84% to 96% of the variance across the four most impactful normalised indicators: the abiotic depletion potential of fossil resources (ADP fossils), the freshwater eutrophication potential (FEP), the global warming potential (GWP), and the abiotic depletion potential of metals and minerals (ADP metals/minerals). The most influential parameters fell into four categories: construction material-related parameters (cement content of segments and two-component grout, reinforcement ratio of segments); TBM manufacturing recycling-related parameters (reuse rates of valuable components and metallic structures); TBM control parameters (penetration rate and utilisation rate) and abrasivity-related geological parameters (Cutter Life Index and quartz content). Results also demonstrate that TBM manufacturing – often overlooked in TBM tunnelling LCAs – represents a significant contributor to environmental impacts. © 2026

title: Grassland soil quality in a changing world
abstract: A quantitative assessment of grassland soil quality (GSQ), including its spatiotemporal variability and underlying driving factors, is pivotal for the adaptive management of grassland ecosystems. Despite extensive studies on GSQ, a systematic synthesis of research achievements, gaps and future perspectives remains underdeveloped. This study systematically reviewed literature published between 1990 and 2024 to achieve three primary objectives: (i) evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of different methods for assessing GSQ, (ii) analyze the frequency and application of physical, chemical, and biological indicators in GSQ assessments, and (iii) examine the effects of natural factors and anthropogenic activities on GSQ. The analysis highlights three critical research priorities: (i) developing a standard index system of GSQ and a method of assessment suitable for various environmental conditions and objectives of evaluation, (ii) identifying the primary socio-ecological drivers that govern the spatial heterogeneity and temporal trends of GSQ, and (iii) elucidating the global distribution, dominant controls, and effective restoration strategies for degraded grassland soil. Addressing these priorities requires innovative techniques and global networks for long-term grassland soil monitoring, standardized procedures for assessing GSQ, more effective collaboration between individuals, organizations, and governments, and an enhanced transfer of knowledge and data for combating the ongoing degradation of grassland soil. Incorporating these actions into a policy of sustainability will aid in conserving multiple services, functions and benefits that grassland soil provides in an era of rapid environmental change. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Hydrological restoration in arid wetlands promotes vegetation recovery by alleviating antagonistic interactions between salinity and soil properties
abstract: The antagonistic interaction between salt stress and soil properties in arid-zone wetlands is a core issue affecting vegetation growth; whether degraded wetlands in these regions can be restored under limited water availability is a current challenge, and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. To reveal the mechanisms and effects of hydrological restoration, we investigated a representative wetland restoration project in an arid region of China and integrated soil properties, microbial activity, and plant functional traits to reveal how the restoration approach alleviated the antagonistic interaction between salt stress and soil properties. The results indicate that salt stress is a primary constraint on vegetation recovery in arid wetlands. Hydrological restoration effectively reduced salinity, leading to significant increases in vegetation height and biomass. In addition, soil properties improved, thereby promoting vegetation recovery, with soil organic carbon (SOC) showing the most pronounced increase (53.2%) under long-term flooding. Vegetation responds to environmental stress by adjusting its resource acquisition strategies: under drought conditions, plants exhibit an acquisition-oriented strategy, preferentially allocating nutrients to stems, whereas under stable flooding conditions, vegetation functional traits shift toward a more conservative strategy. Structural equation modeling (SEM) further confirmed that hydrological restoration positively affected vegetation AGB and PH. Ecological water supplementation not only significantly alleviated the direct stress of salinity on plant growth but also promoted SOC accumulation, while improvements in hydrological and soil conditions indirectly enhanced vegetation recovery by altering plant resource-acquisition strategies. Overall, these findings demonstrate the coupled interactions between salinity, soil properties, and vegetation during hydrological restoration, providing a scientific reference for formulating wetland restoration strategies based on water availability in arid regions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Practices and Social Relations in Foreign Entrepreneurship in Catania and Messina
abstract: This chapter investigates migrant entrepreneurship in the metropolitan contexts of Catania and Messina. Building on the growing economic and social relevance of migrant-owned businesses, the study explores their characteristics, relational dynamics, and key challenges, with particular attention to territorial embeddedness and interactions with the local ecosystem. The research adopts an integrated methodological approach combining quantitative and qualitative tools, with a primary focus on semi-structured interviews conducted with migrant entrepreneurs and key actors such as accountants, Chambers of Commerce, and trade associations. Findings show that migrant entrepreneurship is often a pathway to autonomy, evolving from necessity into a life project, with social networks playing a key role in business creation and consolidation. At the same time, significant challenges persist, including limited access to credit, language barriers, bureaucratic complexity, and weak institutional engagement. The study highlights implications for training interventions aimed at strengthening access to financial, informational, and relational resources. © The Author(s) 2027.

title: The invisible architect: Fiscal incentives and floor area ratio growth in China
abstract: This study examines how local fiscal incentives shape the regulation of residential floor area ratio (FAR). We exploit China's intergovernmental land transfer revenue sharing reform as a quasi-natural experiment and implement a continuous-treatment DID using spatially matched land parcel data. We find that when local governments face declines in their share of land transfer revenues, they reallocate land supply toward commercial uses to broaden business tax bases, with stronger responses in cities where business tax potential is higher. This reallocation is accompanied by higher residential FAR, especially in cities with stronger business-tax potential. The floor-space results suggest that higher FAR partially offsets the contraction in residential land area. These findings provide evidence from China that fiscal institutions can shape building-intensity regulation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Does Fraud Risk Affect Legality Ratings? Evidence from Italian Listed Firms
abstract: Within the framework of the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, Goal 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions) aims to combat all forms of organized crime and significantly reduce corruption and illegality. In this context, Law No. 190 of November 6, 2012, introduced the Legality rating, which serves as an institutional mechanism designed to promote ethical behavior and integrity among Italian firms. This study examines whether the elements considered in the attribution of the legality rating can indirectly capture factors associated with financial statement manipulation. Results reveal no significant relationship between the legality rating and the likelihood of fraudulent reporting, suggesting that the rating captures formal compliance rather than substantive financial integrity. The findings highlight the need to enrich the legality rating framework with quantitative indicators of financial misconduct to enhance its role as a comprehensive integrity metric. © The Author(s) 2027.

title: Gender Equality in Governance and Social Topics of Italian Sustainability Reports. First Evidence Under the CSRD
abstract: Gender equality is a key driver in addressing inequalities in business and society while creating value for the broader ecosystem. In governance and management literature, gender diversity is widely recognized as a mechanism that positively affects economic performance, earnings quality and disclosure transparency. However, research on gender equality disclosure within ESG reporting remains limited, despite its growing relevance for competitiveness and sustainability performance. Drawing on legitimacy theory, this study explores how gender equality is disclosed within governance and social topics of sustainability reports and examines whether increased disclosure reflects a genuine commitment to gender-related policies. The analysis is based on content analysis of hand-collected data from 420 nonfinancial reports issued by 105 Italian firms during the transition to the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRSs). The findings reveal an overall improvement in gender equality disclosure related to both sustainable governance and social inclusion. Moreover, recent legislation appears to have enhanced the standardization and comparability of reporting and to have supported women’s participation in governance and social areas. Nonetheless, evidence of the effective implementation of gender equality programs remains limited. The study provides theoretical and practical insights into corporate approaches to gender equality and its integration into sustainability reporting, contributing to the debate on the role of gender equality in strengthening ESG performance in the post-ESRS context. © The Author(s) 2027.

title: Assessing and refining user stories using large language models: a replication study in a real-world organizational software-development setting
abstract: Specifying and maintaining high-quality user stories is challenging because project contexts evolve, natural-language artifacts are ambiguous, and manual assessment requires substantial effort. The INVEST criteria provide a structured framework for evaluating whether user stories are Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, and Testable. This study examines run-to-run variability and model–expert alignment through a two-phase design. The first phase comprised a dependent replication in which 60 original Spanish-language user stories were evaluated by three experts, GPT-5.1 Thinking (ChatGPT interface), and GPT-5.1 (API-based). The second phase extended the design through structured refinement of the original stories followed by reevaluation of the refined versions under the same Likert (1–5) scale and INVEST rubric. Results were criterion- and execution-condition-specific. Evaluator-related differences in the initial evaluation were detected in a limited subset of comparisons. Across all criterion–condition combinations, paired analyses generally indicated smaller absolute expert–model discrepancies after refinement and reevaluation, although magnitudes were heterogeneous and zero changes were frequent. In the initial evaluation, model ratings more often fell below the expert median when ratings differed; this pattern persisted less uniformly after refinement. Agreement for the average of the three expert ratings was high under ICC(2,3), while ordinal agreement varied by criterion in one refined condition. Overall, the findings are consistent with a potential complementary role for large language models in INVEST-based evaluation and structured refinement, but they do not establish causal improvement, model superiority, or equivalence with expert judgment. However, human oversight remains essential for contextual validation, interpretation, and backlog prioritization. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Efficient drift detection and model adaptation for edge MLOps leveraging class separability in the latent space
abstract: When machine learning (ML) applications are deployed in real-world settings, the dynamic nature of these environments often leads to a gradual degradation in model performance over time. This is called drift, which is one of the challenges the Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) paradigm tries to solve using drift detection techniques. At the same time, there is an ongoing trend of moving ML models onto edge devices, closer to the source of the data, avoiding latency issues of inference on the cloud. However, these devices have limited resources making it challenging to employ MLOps techniques like drift detection, which often require large amount of data and processing power. This paper introduces LSDD+ as a robust and efficient drift detection technique with an incorporated model adaptation strategy. This strategy makes it possible to implement new concepts whilst also recognizing previously known concepts. LSDD+ is evaluated against several other state-of-the-art drift detectors on three semi-synthetic datasets. It shows a significant increase in efficiency compared to the most accurate drift detectors whilst still being on par with these detectors in the ability to detect drift. This proves the method’s suitability for MLOps on the edge. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: Protection by Entanglement: Inseparable Design-Embedded Watermarks for Manufacturing-as-a-Service (MaaS)
abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) is a technology that uses 3D printers to manufacture parts based on their digital design without the need for retooling. Thus, it is well suited for the scalable Manufacturing-as-a-Service (MaaS) business model. However, a more flexible but often short-term low-volume manufacturing relationship between customers and providers of this service raises security concerns on both sides. The customer is concerned with the misuse of shared design: Theft, illegal distribution, or infringement of parts are real security threats. The manufacturer, on the other hand, is concerned with a possible bait-and-switch of designs between the quote request and the agreed upon contract. We propose a watermarking solution that addresses this complex threat and mutually protects the parties involved. Watermarking is a technique of embedding information in a defended object, e.g., to assert intellectual property (IP) rights. We exploit the inherent causation between the digital design that defines a part and the physical qualities of the manufactured part to propose a novel method that ensures the robustness of the watermark. While in other domains watermark robustness is commonly achieved through hidden redundancies, our proposal ensures that its removal or manipulation will make the high-quality design unattainable (thus, noticeable in the parts produced: an issue external of the file system!). Note that robustness is a hard-to-achieve property in general because quantifying hidden redundancies is fundamentally difficult. This work achieves this by binding a digital file property to the necessary aspects of the output domain. More generally, our approach is a blueprint for entangling the integrity of the watermark with the utility of the asset. We release the source code developed for this approach under GPL. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Fast aircraft turnarounds via rule-based passenger-flow control: A 48-stratum field study of real-time boarding route management systems
abstract: Gate turnaround performance shapes on-time operations and stand utilisation, yet remains exposed to architectural complexity, shared-area gate corridors and peak passenger loads. This paper reports a field study of a Real-Time Boarding Route Management System (rtBRMS) that introduces an algorithmic, rule-based flow-control engine coordinating door actuation, terminal access points and passenger routing, in real time using live gate-area conditions. To determine whether such automation produces measurable improvements under live operational constraints, a 48-stratum field study of 171 flights was conducted at the field-study airport, aggregating event-level sensor traces into flight-level performance indicators and analysing them with Welch t-tests, Type-III General Linear Models, Estimated Marginal Means contrasts and Firth-penalised logistic regression. The system reduced average passenger-flow gate occupation time, defined here as the span between the start of deboarding and the end of boarding, a measure that is distinct from the wider ICAO Doc 10121 turnaround Gate Occupation Time. It also compressed boarding and deboarding windows, increased passenger throughput across all load levels and gate configurations and raised the probability of meeting the IATA AHM-aligned high-performance boarding (≤13 min) and deboarding (≤11 min) indicators. These findings show that rtBRMS delivers a scalable, architecture-agnostic, real-time flow-control framework that stabilises gate-area queues, harmonises multi-terminal passenger routing, removes critical human-error pathways in shared-corridor door handling, and improves operational resilience under peak-load and high-complexity conditions. The paper provides field-based evidence that rule-based passenger-flow automation is a deployable lever for reliable and scalable turnarounds while regulatory pathways for security-critical autonomous systems continue to evolve. © 2026 The Authors.

title: FOCUS: hybrid secretary bird super fairy optimized customer segmentation in omni-channel environment
abstract: In this paper, a novel hybrid secretary bird super Fairy Optimized CUstomer Segmentation (FOCUS) approach has been proposed for accurate clustering and meaningful customer groups. Textual data is analyzed to extract lexical and keyword-based features, whereas transactional behaviors are captured through RFM scoring. The features are clustered using the hybrid Secretary Bird Super Fairy (SBSFO) optimization, in which Secretary Bird Optimization (SBO) uses global exploration and Super Fairy Wren Optimization (SFWO) uses local exploitation. This model segments customers into meaningful groups, including top customers, loyal buyers, and occasional or lost customers. This approach provides businesses with deeper behavioral insights and enhances targeted marketing strategies. The proposed approach achieves an SI of 0.77, whereas existing RFM-FCA, RFM-K-Medoids, and SONN achieve 0.61, 0.65, and 0.58, respectively. The proposed FOCUS method achieves a minimum DBI of 0.34, outperforming RFM-FCA at 0.57, RFM-K-Medoids at 0.51, and SONN at 0.60. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Coordination-state regulation of aqueous negolytes: electronic structure, degradation, and high-voltage flow-battery performance
abstract: Aqueous redox flow batteries are promising for long-duration energy storage, but their cell voltage is limited by the instability of highly reducing species in water. This review establishes a coordination-chemistry framework for low-potential aqueous negolytes, focusing on strong-field hexacyanometallates, multidentate metal chelates, and polyoxometalate-based clusters. The key premise is that negolyte performance depends not on formal potential alone, but on a reversible coordination trajectory that preserves solubility, kinetic accessibility, and chemical integrity throughout cycling and ageing. Ligand-field strength, spin state, Jahn–Teller distortion, denticity, coordinated water, free-ligand activity, protonation, counterion association, and membrane transport are therefore considered as coupled design variables. Chromium and manganese hexacyanides demonstrate how strong-field ligation stabilizes low-valent states and enables multielectron storage, whereas Fe–DTPA/Ce–DTPA and Fe(TPEN) systems highlight the roles of chelation, shared-ligand design, and ligand-exchange resistance. Polyoxometalates further show how proton-coupled electron transfer, reversible structural adaptation, and solvent-network regulation can expand the practical aqueous voltage window while maintaining low-temperature conductivity. Operando spectroscopy, electrochemical mass spectrometry, and molecular simulation are critically assessed as tools for resolving coordination-state evolution and degradation. Finally, evidence-based design principles and standardized reporting criteria are proposed to guide the development of durable, high-voltage aqueous negolytes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Entrepreneurship Education in Action: Preventing the NEET Phenomenon. Lessons from La Paranza Case Study
abstract: The rise of young people not in employment, education, or training (NEET) is a major concern in Europe, particularly in disadvantaged areas. Entrepreneurship education is seen as a strategy to enhance inclusion and employability, though it remains underexplored outside formal schooling. This study examines La Paranza cooperative in Naples and identifies key drivers, including experiential learning, place-based approaches, mentorship, active participation, and stakeholder networks. These factors foster skills, self-esteem, and local identity, supporting pathways into employment. The findings show that entrepreneurship education can develop beyond schools, contributing to inclusive policies that address youth marginalization and reduce NEET conditions. © The Author(s) 2027.

title: Growth Stage and Cultivar Influence the Interpretation of UAV-Derived NDVI for Potato Yield Assessment
abstract: Single-date UAV vegetation indices are widely used to assess potato crop performance and estimate yield. However, whether their biological interpretation remains consistent across cultivars and growth stages is rarely examined. This study investigated how the relationships between UAV-derived multispectral and thermal canopy indicators and potato yield changed during crop development under contrasting irrigation in two cultivars with contrasting maturity classes (Anouk and Celandine). UAV surveys were conducted in July and August, and canopy metrics were related to final yield and tuber traits. The relationship between NDVI and yield differed markedly between cultivars and growth stages. In the early-maturing cultivar Anouk, July NDVI showed a strong positive correlation with yield (r = 0.87, p = 0.002), whereas August NDVI was not informative. In the late-maturing cultivar Celandine, the relationship reversed from a positive correlation in July (r = 0.56) to a strong negative correlation in August (r = −0.80, p = 0.009), indicating that greater late-season canopy greenness was associated with lower yield. Exploratory LOOCV Random Forest models achieved the highest yield prediction accuracy using July features for Anouk (R2 = 0.72) and August features for Celandine (R2 = 0.47), while multi-temporal features provided similar predictive performance. Greater temporal declines in NDVI were associated with higher yield in both cultivars, consistent with the change in canopy greenness acting as a phenological indicator of the transition from vegetative growth to tuber bulking. These results demonstrate that the interpretation of UAV-derived vegetation indices is strongly dependent on cultivar maturity and growth stage. A single UAV acquisition may therefore provide misleading assessments of crop performance when canopy phenology is not considered. Rather than serving as fixed proxies for yield, canopy vegetation indices should be interpreted within cultivar-specific and temporal contexts when used for potato monitoring and agronomic decision-making. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Beyond Correlation: Integrating Process Mining and Causal Inference for Root Cause Analysis
abstract: The increasing digitalization of business processes has made Root Cause Analysis (RCA) essential for diagnosing Service Level Agreement (SLA) violations. While recent process mining and machine learning techniques automate the extraction of actionable features from event logs, they predominantly frame RCA as a predictive classification task. However, predictive classification is insufficient for identifying root causes because it merely highlights variables that frequently co-occur with anomalies, failing to distinguish between a harmless symptom and an actionable driver. This approach inherently conflates correlation with causation, leaving decision-makers without rigorous proof that intervening on identified bottlenecks will actually mitigate process deviations. To address this gap, this paper proposes a novel, automated framework that bridges predictive process mining with the formal Potential Outcomes framework. Our methodology utilizes global and contextual decision trees to automatically discover candidate treatments and specific operational sub-populations from enriched event logs. Subsequently, we deploy the X-Learner, an advanced causal meta-learning architecture, to rigorously estimate the Conditional Average Treatment Effect (CATE) of these process behaviors. Evaluated on a real-world telecommunications event log, the framework successfully moves beyond correlational analysis to explicitly quantify cause-and-effect relationships. It successfully pinpointed both causal drivers of SLA breaches, such as specific high-risk activities under high workloads, and critical operational mitigators. By providing a scalable and mathematically robust mechanism to rigorously estimate the impact of process attributes, this approach empowers organizations to deploy highly targeted interventions and optimize resource allocation for continuous process improvement. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Machine Learning Models for Customers Contact Channel Recommendation
abstract: The intense competition in all business sectors has raised the need to effectively attract customers, highlighting the importance of interaction through social media, which has been shown to provide significant benefits. This study proposes three models to recommend the most effective communication media for product acquisition or sales, aiming to optimize the customer attraction process by identifying the channels through which companies should promote their products to reach the most interested users. Clustering techniques were applied to analyze customer contact channels and support decision-making in marketing strategies. The methodological approach includes data collection, data preparation, the development of hybrid clustering methods, model testing, and results analysis, using a 70/30 split for training and testing data. Results show that the most frequently used media are Instagram, Pinterest, and Telegram. The hybrid approach used in this paper demonstrated that social media holds more influence over female users. Furthermore, social media appears to influence students more than professionals. Moreover, we found that the most used social media varies among clusters. Overall, our findings reveal that higher education institutions should incorporate different communication strategies rather than a “universal solution” for all their customers. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Main characteristics of quartz-feldspar sands from the Khiva deposit, and the physico-chemical and technological fundamentals of obtaining an enriched concentrate
abstract: This research presents studies on the beneficiation and application of quartz-feldspar sands from the “Khiva deposit” located in the Khorezm region of the Republic of Uzbekistan for the silicate industry. The composition of raw material samples was analysed using modern X-ray diffraction and IR spectroscopic methods. Based on the results, the quantitative mineralogical composition of the samples was determined using the BGMN/Profex Rietveld software package. According to the obtained data, the average chemical composition of the raw material (in wt.%) was determined as follows: SiO₂ – 86.06; Al₂O₃ – 2.64; Fe₂O₃ – 1.37; CaO – 1.37; MgO – 0.22; K₂O – 1.30; Na₂O – 1.85; TiO₂ – 0.04; SO₃ – 0.4, with a loss on ignition of 4.93. The beneficiation processes of the raw material were studied. Based on the specific characteristics of the composition, it was found appropriate in subsequent studies to apply combinations of beneficiation methods such as washing, gravity separation, classification, attrition scrubbing, electromagnetic separation, and flotation. As a result, it was determined that the SiO₂ content in the beneficiated concentrate increased from 86.06% to 97.07%, while Al₂O₃ decreased from 2.64% to 1.06%, and Fe₂O₃ from 1.37% to 0.05%. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Innovative technologies for paraffin deposit removal in oil tubing to enhance oil recovery: a mechanical approach; [Мұнай өндіруді арттыру үшін мұнай құбырларын парафиндік шөгінділерден тазалаудың инновациялық технологиялары: механикалық әдіс]; [Инновационные технологии очистки нефтяных труб от парафиновых отложений для повышения нефтеотдачи: механический подход]
abstract: Asphaltene-resin-paraffin deposits (ARPD) on the inner wall of production tubing shorten service intervals, elevate operating expenditures, and frequently induce downtime at mature fields. This paper presents the design and field performance of a rod-driven in-well scraper that provides continuous tubing cleaning during routine sucker-rod operation without chemical dosing or surface interventions. The scraper sub is inserted into the rod string and is compatible with Ø73-89 mm tubing and Ø19-22 mm rods. Performance was evaluated on a before/after basis using the inter-cleaning period (ICP), downtime, and annual cleaning costs, with extrapolation to multi-well programs. Field deployments of model CP TP ST 01KZ achieved an ICP of 144-280 days with zero cleaning-induced downtime (0 days yr⁻¹). Annual cleaning costs were ~0.265 million KZT per well (scheduled service only), which is ≈31× lower than hot-wash budgets on the same asset. The implied per-well saving is ≈7.94 million KZT yr⁻¹; for a 50-well program, this corresponds to ≥397 million KZT yr⁻¹ in avoided expenditure. Continuous in-well action of the reciprocating toothed head on each rod stroke disrupts the boundary wax layer and limits deposit regrowth between services, eliminating periodic thermal/chemical treatments and their logistics. The subassembly mass (≈30 kg) permits installation with standard handling; the pump string configuration is unchanged apart from the insertion of the scraper section. Compared with thermal, chemical, and batch mechanical methods, the technology extends service intervals, removes cleaning-related shut-ins, and compresses the cleaning budget to a predictable, low annual service cost. The results support routine use of rod-driven scraping for ARPD control in wax-prone wells and provide quantitative guidance for field-scale rollout and further optimization (wear resistance, centralization tolerances, and application in deviated completions). © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Technological and operational properties of composite magnesia binders; [Композициялық магнезиялық тұтқыр заттардың технологиялық және пайдалану қасиеттері]; [Технологические и эксплуатационные свойства композиционных магнезиальных вяжущих]
abstract: The article presents the results of studies of magnesia binders of various material compositions. The purpose of the work is to study the technological and operational properties of composite magnesia binders containing metallurgical slag and magnetite ore. Solutions of magnesium chloride and magnesium sulfate, as well as a mixture of them, were used to seal magnesia binders. The technological properties of magnesia binders were evaluated by the consumption of saline solution, consistency, and viscosity changes of the suspensions. To determine the operational quality of composite binders, indicators of density, strength, water absorption and water resistance were used. The dependences of the rheological properties of suspensions on the composition of the dispersed phase and the type of saline solution are revealed. The operational advantages of composite magnesia binders have been established and substantiated: increased density, lower water absorption, increased water resistance and comparable strength compared with caustic magnesite. The directions of using the developed magnesia-slag and magnesia-magnetite binders are proposed. The research results are aimed at developing resource-saving technologies for magnesia binders and concretes. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Development of technology for obtaining high-purity sodium chloride with induced impurity removal and process modeling; [Қоспаларды кетіруді индукциялау арқылы жоғары тазалықтағы натрий хлоридін алу технологиясын әзірлеу және процесті модельдеу]; [Разработка технологии получения хлорида натрия высокой чистоты с индуцированием удаления примесей и моделирование процесса]
abstract: High-purity NaCl is required for chemical processes. Halite from the South Kazakhstan Bakhyt Tany deposit contains CaSO₄ and Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ that degrade quality and operability. The article presents statistical processing and modeling of impurity deposition with phosphate ions using an automated calculation process. A stoichiometric amount of Na₃PO₄ was added to the NaCl 315 mol/dm3 brine, stirred for 25-30 minutes, precipitated for 30 minutes, and filtered. Sulfate was quantified by barium-sulfate turbidimetry; residual Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ in the filtrate was measured titrimetrically. The Excel 2000 workbook performs coefficient estimation, significance testing, model adequacy testing, and error analysis. Response optimisation is also carried out through protected input fields. The resulting second-order models are adequate within the studied range of factors, reflect significant main effects and interactions, and predict optimal process modes, which have been confirmed experimentally. Under optimized conditions, removal reached 99.9% for Ca²⁺ and 99.8% for Mg²⁺. Sulfate ions remained at trace levels in the NaCl product. The framework enables reproducible parameter selection and provides a basis for integrating near-zero-waste handling of co-products in subsequent process design. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Flowsheet Design and Modelling for High Purity Praseodymium and Neodymium by Solvent Extraction; [Еріткішпен экстракциялау арқылы жоғары тазалықтағы празеодим мен неодимді алудың технологиялық схемасын әзірлеу және модельдеу]; [Разработка и моделирование технологической схемы получения высокочистого празеодима и неодима методом экстракции растворителем]
abstract: Purifying rare earth elements (REEs) from ion-adsorbed clay (IAC) deposits demands complex solvent extraction (SX) setups to achieve commercial-grade purity. This study presents the design and validation of a four-train counter-current SX flowsheet for processing a pre-treated REE chloride liquor sourced from Malaysia’s Jeli deposit. Using an iterative steady-state mass-balance simulation in Microsoft Excel, the research determines the operational parameters needed to achieve a 4N (99.99%) terminal purity target for each REE stream. The methodology involved pinpointing critical A/B separation cuts and optimising the organic-to-aqueous (O/A) ratios across the cascade. The results show that the flowsheet effectively fractionates the feedstock, starting with a bulk LREE/HREE separation (Train 1) and culminating in the challenging separation of praseodymium (Pr) and neodymium (Nd) (Train 4). The simulation identified Pr/Nd separation as the primary technical bottleneck, requiring 62 equilibrium stages (NE) due to a low separation factor (β) of 1.70. In contrast, simpler bulk splits needed as few as 16 stages. These findings confirm the theoretical minimum stage requirements (Nmin) and provide a detailed stage-wise concentration profile for each train. The study concludes that the Pr/Nd circuit dictates the overall plant footprint and capital intensity. The developed flowsheet offers a solid technical blueprint for commercialising Malaysian IAC resources, ensuring high-purity REE recovery through optimised metallurgical design. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Sigmoid Neutralization Response of Acidic Soapstock Waste by Mineralized Phosphorite Residues: A 4-Parameter Logistic Approach; [Қышқыл сабын қалдықтарының сигмоидты бейтараптандыру реакциясында минералданған фосфорит қалдықтарын пайдалану: 4 параметрлі логистикалық тәсіл]; [Сигмоидная нейтрализационная реакция кислых отходов соапстока с использованием минерализованных остатков фосфоритов: 4-параметрический логистический подход]
abstract: This study investigates the neutralization behavior of an acidic wastewater (AWW)–mineralized mass (MM) system at mass ratios ranging from 100:10 to 100:40, processed at 333 K for 30 min. The evolution of pH as a function of MM dosage and the corresponding CaO content (%) in the solid phase were quantitatively evaluated. The solution pH increased sigmoidally from 4.10 to 7.30, while the CaO content rose from 23.92% to 36.96%, approaching a saturation plateau at higher MM dosages. The pH–dose relationship was described using four-parameter logistic (4PL), Gompertz, and Weibull models, all showing a high goodness of fit (R² ≥ 0.97). Model comparison based on AICc and BIC criteria indicated that the Gompertz model provided the best statistical performance, whereas the 4PL model ensured clearer physicochemical interpretability. A strong positive correlation between pH and CaO content was established (Pearson r = 0.9649, n = 7, p < 0.001), enabling estimation of CaO content from pH values. Numerical inversion of the 4PL model combined with a multi-model ensemble approach was used to determine optimal MM dosages for target pH levels. The recommended operating conditions were identified as 100:32 for pH 6.5, 100:36 for pH 6.8, and 100:38 for pH 7.0, with a stabilization zone observed at 100:37–100:40. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Mathematical analysis of the linear increase in SiO2 content during the activation of Navbakhor alkaline bentonite with hydrochloric acid; [Навабахор сілтілі бентонитін тұз қышқылымен белсендендіру кезінде SiO₂ мөлшерінің сызықтық артуын математикалық талдау]; [Математический анализ линейного увеличения содержания SiO₂ при активации навбахорского щелочного бентонита соляной кислотой]
abstract: In this study, the acid activation process of the bentonite clay, which was conducted for producing a bleaching sorbent for the oil and fat industry, was mathematically analyzed. Increase in SiO₂ content under different concentrations of HCl was analyzed using the different mathematical models. During acid activation, increasing the acid concentration from 5% to 20% resulted in an increase in the SiO₂ content from 61.94% to 65.12%. During the activation process, a moderate increase in HCl concentration caused the improvement of the sorption properties of the clay by dissolving some components and restructuring the active sites. An excessive increase in the concentration of HCl leads to degradation of the mineral structure and partial breakdown of the silica framework, which negatively influences sorption performance. Analysis of the obtained results using the different mathematical approaches showed that an increase in SiO₂ content during activation corresponds fully to a linear model. According to this, a linear model was described by the equation y = 60.785 + 0.2088·X. Accuracy of the results obtained from the linear equation was confirmed by a coefficient of determination, R² = 0.9845, indicating a high accordance with the experimental data. This model mathematically predicts the increase in SiO₂ content and proves that the activation process proceeds as a linear function. A mathematical approach to the activation process enables one to calculate in advance the properties of sorption of the clay, to reduce the consumption of acid and water, and to calculate the eventual demands of other reagents. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Mineralogical features and optimization of combined beneficiation flowsheets for refractory gold-bearing ores of the Pakrut deposit (Central Tajikistan); [Пакрут кенорнының (Орталық Тәжікстан) қиын өңделетін алтынқұрамды кендерінің минералогиялық ерекшеліктері және оларды байытудың құрамдастырылған технологиялық сұлбаларын оңтайландыру]; [Минералогические особенности и оптимизация комбинированных схем обогащения упорных золотосодержащих руд месторождения Пакрут (Центральный Таджикистан)]
abstract: Against the backdrop of depleted rich deposits and the increasing proportion of refractory gold-bearing ores, improving their processing methods has become an urgent task. This work presents the results of a comprehensive study of gold-bearing ores from the Pakrut deposit, located in Central Tajikistan's Zeravshan–Gissar zone. Mineralogical analysis established that the principal gold carriers are pyrite and arsenopyrite, with the metal predominantly localized as fine inclusions and fracture-related accumulations. A notable fraction of gold occurs as free particles (17.03%); however, the dominant share is fracture-bound (62.41%) and is predominantly associated with arsenopyrite. This distribution explains the limited efficiency of single-stage treatment and substantiates the need for combined unlocking and recovery routes. Physicochemical studies confirmed the ores' refractory nature, attributed to the fine dissemination of gold within the sulfide matrix, combined with high hardness and abrasiveness. At the laboratory scale, various beneficiation flowsheets were tested, including direct cyanidation; flotation combined with additional leaching of tailings; and variants incorporating gravity separation. A comparative analysis showed that the highest gold recovery rate (92.23%) was achieved by the flowsheet involving cyanidation, followed by tailings leaching and flotation. Although direct cyanidation also demonstrated a high recovery rate (90.05%), it was less effective. The flotation–cyanidation and gravity–flotation schemes yielded comparatively lower performance. The obtained data confirm the effectiveness of an integrated approach to processing the refractory ores from the Pakrut deposit. Optimizing the beneficiation flowsheet enables a significant increase in precious metal recovery, reduces technological losses, and minimizes environmental risks associated with the accumulation of arsenic-bearing waste. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Prospects for Industrial Extraction of Methane from Coal Seams in the Karaganda Basin: Results of Experimental-Industrial Studies at the Taldykuduk Site; [Қарағанды көмір бассейнінің көмір қабаттарынан метанды өнеркәсіптік өндірудің перспективалары: Талдықұдық учаскесіндегі тәжірибелік-өндірістік зерттеулер нәтижелері]; [Перспективы промышленной добычи метана из угольных пластов Карагандинского бассейна: результаты экспериментально-промышленных исследований на Талдыкудукском участке]
abstract: The study focuses on assessing the industrial potential of coalbed methane production in the Karaganda Basin based on drilling and testing data from wells T7 and T8 at the Taldykuduk site. The goal is to develop and verify engineering solutions, ensuring efficient methane extraction from unstressed seams under real geological and technical conditions. The research object is the coal seams of the Karaganda suite, characterized by high gas content, developed fracturing, and heterogeneous reservoir structure. Vertical wells were drilled with local enlargement of productive intervals, zone isolation using packers, and controlled hydraulic stimulation. A set of geophysical surveys was conducted, including gamma, density, and neutron logs, caliper logging, inclinometry, gas-geochemical monitoring, and flow tests, to determine reservoir pressure and permeability. Laboratory analyses of core and coal samples examined adsorption–desorption properties, elemental composition, and formation water characteristics, enabling the selection of optimal reagents and gas treatment schemes. Stable methane inflows up to 30 m³/day were obtained under steady depression without water inflow, confirming readiness for pilot-industrial operation. After hydraulic stimulation and optimization of well regimes, an increase in gas flow rate was recorded, confirming the efficiency of reservoir stimulation. Based on pressure and flow curves, technological parameters were defined — perforation intervals, hydraulic treatment conditions, and requirements for gas collection, dehydration, and compression systems. The practical significance of the study lies in substantiating a technological scheme for industrial methane extraction and reducing methane hazards during mining. Implementation of the proposed approach will enable integration of extracted gas into the regional energy balance and reduce uncontrolled methane emissions, providing environmental and economic benefits. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Evaluation of the Effect of Additives on the Workability of Concrete Mix as Part of a Study of a Modified Wall Block; [Модификацияланған қабырға блогын зерттеу аясында бетон қоспасының қозғалғыштығына қоспалардың әсерін бағалау]; [Оценка влияния добавок на подвижность бетонной смеси в рамках исследования модифицированного стенового блока]
abstract: The article presents the results of an experimental investigation into the effect of modifying additives on the workability and setting times of a concrete mix used in the production of a two-component wall block. The block structure consists of an external façade layer and an internal structural–thermal insulation layer, which requires precise control of the rheological and technological parameters of the concrete mix during sequential casting. Lignin and soapstock, which are by-products of the wood-processing and fat-processing industries, were used as modifying components. The experimental program included the determination of concrete mix flowability and cement paste setting times at various additive dosages. The results showed that the incorporation of lignin and soapstock increased the workability of the concrete mix compared to the reference composition: the maximum increase in flowability reached up to 6.4% for lignin and up to 9.5% for soapstock. Their combined application produced a pronounced synergistic effect, resulting in an increase in workability of up to 16% in linear terms and up to 35% in terms of spread area, as well as a reduction in data dispersion. The setting time tests revealed opposite effects of the additives: lignin contributed to a reduction in both initial and final setting times, whereas soapstock, due to its hydrophobic properties, led to their extension. The obtained results can be used to optimize the technological regulations for manufacturing two-component wall blocks and to improve the quality and stability of the final products. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Mathematical Model of the Dynamics of the Armament of the Tricone Drill Bit; [Үш қашау тісті бұрғыларды жабдықтау динамикасының математикалық моделі]; [Математическая модель динамики вооружения трехшариковых долот]
abstract: This study presents a mathematical model of the dynamics of tricone drill bits, which remain widely used in open-pit mining due to their reliability and versatility. Despite their extensive application, improving their efficiency and durability remains a relevant issue. The main operational challenges are identified, including insufficient knowledge of the stress–strain state of rocks in the contact zone and the effect of tooth geometry on kinematics and rock-breaking efficiency. Analytical dependencies are proposed to account for bit geometry, trajectory motion, transmission ratios, and tooth–rock interaction. Based on the principles of theoretical mechanics, performance criteria are formulated through specific contact and volumetric work of rock destruction, enabling an objective assessment of energy consumption. The model demonstrates the potential of analytical methods for optimizing drill bit design and kinematics, reducing energy consumption, increasing productivity, and extending tool life. The results can be applied in the design of next-generation drill bits and in engineering software for selecting rational drilling parameters under specific geological conditions. The proposed approach provides a foundation for further studies in mathematical modeling of rock destruction dynamics and the advancement of open-pit mining technologies. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: A Review of Constitutive Modeling of Unsaturated Soils
abstract: The mechanics of unsaturated soils are integral to understanding and predicting the behavior of diverse geotechnical and geo-environmental systems, including natural slopes, engineered embankments, landfill covers, and agricultural fields. Unlike saturated soils, unsaturated soils exhibit a complex interplay among air, water, and solid phases, in which suction and partial saturation are pivotal in governing stress-strain responses, volume changes, and fluid flow processes. Over the past several decades, extensive theoretical, experimental, and computational efforts have culminated in sophisticated constitutive models, reflecting the need to include moisture content and suction as additional state variables. This article comprehensively reviews these modeling endeavors, tracing historical developments from empirical extensions of saturated soil models to contemporary elastoplastic, multi-scale, and data-driven frameworks. Emphasis is placed on the evolution of stress state variables, the role of hydraulic hysteresis, and the bidirectional coupling between mechanical and water retention behavior. Special attention is given to recent models that incorporate bound water structure and dehydration mechanisms in expansive clays, highlighting their influence on retention properties, suction, and thermomechanical responses. The paper also explores advances in small-strain stiffness modeling (which is crucial for predicting seismic behavior of unsaturated soils), machine learning integration, and coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical-chemical (THMC) processes. Practical challenges, including parameter calibration, are examined. The paper also offers examples of prominent constitutive models, detailing their mathematical formulations and underlying assumptions. Current trends, including the integration of machine learning, are evaluated, and future research directions are proposed, underscoring the importance of interdisciplinary collaborations and long-term monitoring to refine and validate constitutive models for unsaturated soils. © 2026, Iranian Geophyisical Society. .
