title: Uncertainty estimation in earthquake magnitude determination using high-rate GPS data with Bootstrap method
abstract: Accurate analysis of earthquake magnitude and evaluation of its associated uncertainty are fundamental topics in seismology and disaster management. In this study, the earthquake magnitudes were estimated using high-rate GPS data for three major events: the 2011 Tohoku earthquake (Mw 9.1), the 2021 Chignik earthquake (Mw 8.2), and the 2018 Anchorage earthquake (Mw 7.1). The final estimated magnitudes using the proposed method were approximately Mw 9.25 for Tohoku, Mw 8.27 for Chignik, and Mw 7.08 for Anchorage, closely aligning with official reports. High-rate GPS data, due to their ability to precisely capture real-time crustal displacements, were utilized as the primary data source. These data provided valuable information on maximum displacement, dominant period, and epicentral distance, and were employed for estimating earthquake magnitude and analyzing uncertainty. To analyze the data, combinations of different GPS stations were used to minimize the impact of noisy data and achieve more stable results. The application of the Bootstrap statistical method reduced uncertainty values significantly from approximately 0.0039 to 0.0011 for Tohoku, 0.0031 to 0.0019 for Chignik, and 0.004 to 0.0015 for Anchorage. These results demonstrate the statistical robustness and effectiveness of the proposed approach. Compared to conventional seismic methods, which suffer from data clipping and saturation for large magnitudes, the high-rate GPS method provided stable and unbiased magnitude estimates without signal saturation issues. The findings underscore the importance of expanding GPS networks in tectonically active regions, integrating seismic and GPS data, and employing advanced algorithms for data processing. Furthermore, the research emphasizes the role of comprehensive data analysis in improving early earthquake warning systems. By incorporating high-rate GPS data with traditional seismic data, the precision and reliability of early warning systems can be significantly enhanced, ultimately reducing the potential for loss of life and property. Additionally, this study highlights the necessity of strengthening infrastructure resilience and investing in advanced monitoring technologies. In conclusion, this research successfully demonstrates that high-rate GPS data, combined with the Bootstrap method, can accurately estimate earthquake magnitudes, reduce uncertainty, and enhance the reliability of seismic assessments. These findings contribute to the development of more effective earthquake early warning systems and risk mitigation strategies. © 2026, Iranian Geophyisical Society. .

title: Regionalization, temporal-spatial characteristics, and trend of changes in precipitation and drought in Iran
abstract: This study regionalizes Iran's precipitation and analyzes the temporal-spatial behavior of precipitation and drought in Iran. It used two sets of precipitation data. The first data set is the monthly precipitation data of 63 synoptic stations and the second data set is the Gridded precipitation data of three databases: Global Precipitation Climatology Center (GPCC), Climatic Research Unit (CRU) of the University of East Anglia (UEA) of England and University of Delaware (UDel) of the United States. As the results showed, the GPCC Gridded precipitation data set with a very high correlation (R^2 = 0.97) with Iranian station data was recognized as the most suitable Gridded precipitation data set for Iran. Cluster analysis on this precipitation dataset showed Iran can fall under seven different precipitation regions. Various characteristics of droughts, such as intensity, duration, and frequency of each precipitation region, were extracted and analyzed through four standardized precipitation indices (SPI), percentage of normal precipitation (PNPI), precipitation variability (RVI), and deciles (DI). The results disclosed that the three precipitation regions of Southwest (SW), Central Iran (CI), and Northwest-Northeast (NW-NE), among the seven precipitation regions of Iran, are the most vulnerable precipitation regions to drought. © 2026, Iranian Geophyisical Society. .

title: 3D modeling of electro-facies using a geostatistical algorithm
abstract: Facies analysis is a critical component of reservoir characterization studies. This study employs several clustering methods to generate reservoir electro-facies (EFs) from well logs. The clustering results were then distributed using geostatistical algorithms to create a reservoir facies model within a geometrical structure interpreted from seismic data. Well logs were classified into facies using multi-resolution graph-based clustering (MRGC) and self-organizing map (SOM) methods. Once distributed spatially with geostatistical techniques, the log-derived facies supported the conditional distribution of petrophysical properties by facies. A geostatistical approach, specifically sequential indicator simulation (SIS), was used to integrate well logs and interpreted seismic data, resulting in an accurate 3D facies model. This model was generated for the depth interval spanning the Frontier (Second Wall Creek) to the Crow Mountain horizons in the Teapot Dome. The 3D facies model aids in developing the field plan and identifying potential new well locations for drilling. © 2026, Iranian Geophyisical Society. .

title: AN ACCELERATED MODULUS-BASED MATRIX SPLITTING ITERATION METHOD FOR SOLVING A CLASS OF HORIZONTAL NONLINEAR COMPLEMENTARITY PROBLEMS
abstract: This paper focuses on an accelerated modulus-based matrix splitting iteration method for solving a class of horizontal nonlinear complementarity problems. First, by introducing a secondary matrix splitting based on the principles of stepwise updates and immediate utilization of the latest computational information, the equivalent modulus equation of the horizontal nonlinear complementarity problem is reformulated and thereby the accelerated modulus-based matrix splitting iteration scheme is constructed. Subsequently, under the assumption that the system matrices are H+-matrices, the convergence conditions for the proposed method are established. Finally, the computational efficiency of the new method is demonstrated by numerical experiments. © 2027 American Institute of Mathematical Sciences. .

title: Polymer-bitumen compositions for improving the energy efficiency of road construction; [Жол құрылысының энергия тиімділігін арттыруға арналған полимер-битум қоспалары]; [Полимер-битумные композиции для повышения энергоэффективности дорожного строительства]
abstract: This article examines the effect of two types of polypropylene (H030 and H350) and petroleum residue on the bitumen modification process. Bitumen modification is one of the key methods for improving its physical and mechanical properties and enhancing the quality of road pavement. Currently, bitumen modification is widely used in road construction, playing a crucial role in improving its quality and energy efficiency. Studying the effect of polymers on the mechanical stability of bitumen is a relevant issue in increasing the durability of road surfaces. During the study, six different concentrations of polypropylene H030 and H350 were introduced into bitumen samples, and their main characteristics were compared. The obtained results demonstrated that polypropylene significantly alters the properties of bitumen, contributing to increased strength and durability of road pavements. Furthermore, the addition of petroleum residue enhances the rheological properties of the bitumen mixture, improving its adhesion. These studies provide essential data for improving bitumen used in road construction. The research results indicate that the use of polymer-modified bitumen increases the wear resistance of road surfaces, reduces crack formation, and enhances resistance to climatic factors. This, in turn, extends the service life of road pavements and reduces road maintenance costs. Long-lasting pavements help decrease energy consumption for bitumen production and road construction. The obtained data expand the possibilities for the effective use of polymer-modified bitumen mixtures in asphalt concrete production. Thus, the compatibility of bitumen and polypropylene has been studied, and their optimal compositions have been determined. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Comparative Analysis of Mathematical Models of Drilling in Heterogeneous Geological Sections; [Біртекті емес геологиялық учаскелерде бұрғылаудың математикалық модельдерін салыстырмалы талдау]
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of four main types of well drilling models in heterogeneous geological sections: mechanical-mathematical, energy, kinematic, and empirical. It is shown that each group of models focuses on different aspects of the process: the physics of bitrock interaction (mechanical-mathematical approach), the energy efficiency of rock mass destruction (energy), the trajectory and movement of the tool (kinematic), as well as statistical patterns and the prediction of complications (empirical). The interaction between the bit and the rock is considered depending on their physical and mechanical properties. A comparison of the rotation speed of the rotor and bit is provided depending on the rock hardness. Based on a review of modern publications and the practical experience of leading service companies (Equinor, Schlumberger, Halliburton), the strengths and weaknesses of each approach are identified, and the need for their integration is substantiated. It is established that the integrated use of models of different classes allows not only to describe and explain phenomena but also to manage the drilling process in conditions of high geological variability. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Extraction of P2O5 from the mineralized mass of the Central Kyzylkum using acidic wastewater generated from cotton soapstock processing: scientific analysis based on equilibrium principles; [Мақта майының сабын фракциясын өңдеу кезінде түзілетін қышқыл ағынды суларды (ҚҚС) пайдаланып, Орталық Қызылқұм шөлінің минералданған массасынан фосфор пентоксидін (P₂O₅) алу: тепе-теңдік принциптеріне негізделген ғылыми талдау]; [Извлечения пятиокиси фосфора (P₂O₅) из минерализованной массы Центрального Кызылкума с использованием кислотных сточных вод (КСВ), образующихся при переработке мыльной фракции хлопкового масла: научный анализ на основе принципов равновесия]
abstract: This study explores the prospects of extracting phosphorus pentoxide (P2O5) from the mineralized mass of the Central Kyzylkum region using acidic wastewater (AWW) derived from cottonseed soapstock processing. The acidic components within the AWW were found to facilitate the decomposition of solid-phase phosphorite material. Experiments were conducted at 333 K under varying AWW-to-mineralized mass (AWW:MM) ratios ranging from 100:10 to 100:40. The concentration of P2O5 was determined using a photometric method at a wavelength of 440 nm. The research was based exclusively on the analysis of the solid phase, where the extent of the reaction was assessed through the quantity of precipitate formed. It was demonstrated that an increase in pH had a direct effect on P2O5 extraction. The reduction in CaO content followed an exponential trend, while the P2O5 release exhibited a logarithmic relationship with pH. The equilibrium reactions between ions were interpreted within the framework of chemical mechanisms. Experimental results were expressed through graphical analysis and regression modeling using OriginPro 2021. The obtained data were mathematically modeled with high reliability, as indicated by coefficients of determination (R²) exceeding 0.95. This approach offers a cost-effective, waste-based alternative technological method for phosphorus extraction, utilizing industrial by-products while maintaining environmental and economic feasibility. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Study of the suitability of industrial raw material resources as additives for Portland cement; [Портландцементке қоспа ретінде өнеркәсіптік шикізаттың жарамдылығын зерттеу]; [Изучение пригодности промышленных сырьевых ресурсов в качестве добавок к портландцементу]
abstract: This research investigates the potential of utilizing industrial technogenic waste materials as hybrid mineral additives in the production of composite Portland cement (CPC), aiming to reduce clinker consumption and promote environmentally friendly construction practices. The studied materials include active ash and slag (AAS) from the Angren thermal power plant, microsilica (MS), and processed steelmaking wastes such as ladle slag (LS), furnace slag (FS), and recycled steel slag (RSS) from Uzmetkombinat JSC. The chemical, mineralogical, and mechanical properties of these materials were characterized in accordance with national and international standards. Compressive strength tests and lime absorption measurements evaluated their pozzolanic and hydraulic activities. Experimental results demonstrated that AAS exhibited the highest activity, capable of replacing up to 45% of clinker without compromising mechanical strength. When combined with less active components (MS, RSS, FS, and LS), hybrid additives showed synergistic effects. Among these, the AAS+MS blend had the most significant pozzolanic effect, evidenced by reduced calcium oxide (CaO) concentration in the surrounding liquid and lower solution alkalinity. The statistical validation using the Student’s t-test confirmed the effectiveness of each additive, with t-values significantly exceeding the threshold required to classify them as active mineral additives. The findings support the development of “green” CPCs using hybrid additives derived from local industrial waste, offering a sustainable alternative to traditional raw materials. These formulations can significantly reduce carbon dioxide emissions, energy consumption, and natural resource depletion while maintaining cement performance, thus aligning with global trends toward low-clinker and low-carbon construction materials. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Investigation of the effect of a modified additive on the strength characteristics of foam concrete; [Модификацияланған қоспаның көбікті бетонның беріктік сипаттамаларына әсерін зерттеу]; [Исследование влияния модифицированной добавки на прочностные характеристики пенобетона]
abstract: The article presents the second stage of the investigate the effect of the modified additive on the strength characteristics of foam concrete. This work describes a method for manufacturing foam concrete samples, selects a modifying additive composition with different percentages of components, and analyzes their strength characteristics. The purpose of introducing plasticizing additives (post-alcohol bard) in foam concrete D600 to reduce water consumption and the expected increase in strength. To evaluate the changes in strength, samples were made and tested in compression at the age of 3, 7, 14, and 28 days of normal moisture curing. According to research results, the use of such additives can significantly reduce formwork removal times, increase the load-bearing capacity of structures, and expand the scope of application of foam concrete—even to structural and thermal insulation products. Additives improve not only strength but also structural uniformity, reducing the number of macropores and increasing the density of the material. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Redistribution of rock pressure and deformation of the rock mass in the Karaganda coal basin; [Қарағанды көмір бассейніндегі тау жыныстары қысымының және тау жыныстарының сілемінің деформациясының қайта таралуы]
abstract: The study examines the redistribution of rock pressure and associated deformation processes in the Karaganda Coal Basin. It focuses on the geometry and parameters of the abutment, unloading, and disintegration zones around underground workings, and on their influence on gas-dynamic phenomena. The methodological basis combines a critical review of current geomechanical models, calculation–graphic nomograms for estimating zone width as a function of mining depth and seam thickness, and schematic construction of high-stress regions from the boundaries of the goaf at limiting angles of 75–90°. It is shown that, with increasing depth up to about 500 m, the zone configuration becomes wedge-shaped with a tendency to narrow downward, while increasing seam thickness expands the affected areas. Lithology controls the localization of hazardous zones: weakly bedded argillites and siltstones accelerate loosening and loss of stiffness, whereas stronger sandstones form dome-like stress concentrations with elevated likelihood of sudden outbursts and rockbursts. As a verification case, an episode of a sudden coal-and-gas outburst was analyzed. The observed failure boundaries are consistent with the calculated wedgeshaped high-stress zone, supporting the validity of the chosen approach within the stated assumptions. The practical significance lies in refining threshold conditions that trigger mandatory comprehensive forecasting at depths exceeding ~400 m, justifying regular instrumental monitoring to validate calculations, and adjusting barrier-pillar parameters about seam thickness and depth. The findings can be applied to the planning and safe execution of longwall and development operations under outburst-prone conditions. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Innovative Adsorbent Materials for Efficient Silicon Extraction from Industrial Waters: A review; [Өнеркәсіптік ағынды сулардан кремнийді тиімді бөліп алу үшін инновациялық адсорбент материалдары: Шолу]; [Инновационные адсорбирующие материалы для эффективного извлечения кремния из промышленных вод: Обзор]
abstract: Silica fouling reduces the effectiveness and durability of membrane-based treatment systems, and silicon contamination in industrial water streams poses ongoing operational issues. With an emphasis on their processes, drawbacks, and applicability for various silica species, this article provides a comparative examination of the main silica removal technologies: ion exchange, reverse osmosis (RO), ultrafiltration (UF), electrocoagulation (EC), adsorption, and lime softening. Although they need a significant amount of chemical input and pH control, lime softening and ion exchange are efficient for dissolved silica. RO requires thorough preparation and offers broad-spectrum separation, although it is susceptible to silica scaling. While UF works well with colloidal and particulate silica, it is unsuccessful with monomeric forms. EC achieves excellent removal rates with less sludge by combining electrochemical destabilisation and crystallisation. Adsorption provides variable selectivity, low energy consumption, and compatibility with membrane systems, especially when employing tailored materials like activated alumina, iron oxide-coated media, and functionalised hybrids. In addition to outlining important techno-economic considerations for scaling up silica extraction methods in intricate industrial water matrices, the paper highlights new developments in adsorbent design, such as surface modification, hierarchical porosity, and regeneration techniques. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Predicting Copper Production Cycles in Hydrometallurgy with Interpretable Machine Learning; [Прогнозирование циклов производства меди в гидрометаллургии с помощью интерпретируемого машинного обучения]
abstract: Accurate production forecasting in industrial hydrometallurgy is essential for process optimization yet is often hindered by the scarcity of extensive historical data. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of classical machine learning models as a data-efficient and interpretable alternative to complex deep learning methods for predicting total copper mass. We evaluated four models— Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Decision Tree, and Linear Regression—using a methodology centered on two key strategies: synthetically expanding a limited 150-day dataset into 10,000 simulated cycles (approximately 1.5 million data points) via data augmentation, and engineering 10-day lag features to provide the models with a temporal perspective for a 10-step-ahead forecasting task. The results revealed exceptional predictive accuracy, with ensemble techniques proving superior. The Random Forest model emerged as the top performer, achieving an R² of 0.974, an MAE of 0.088, and an RMSE of 0.111, closely followed by Gradient Boosting (R² of 0.971). All models successfully captured the distinct 150-day cyclical dynamics of the production process, showing a near-zero phase lag (0.00 ± ≤0.05 days). While performance on new, independent data requires further validation, this work establishes a robust and transparent framework for developing reliable forecasting tools in data-limited industrial environments. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Use of Industrial By-products from Metallurgical Production for the Development of Heat-Resistant Building Mixes and their Molding in an Improved Device; [Металлургиялық өндірістіңөнерк әсіптікқосалқыөні мдерінпайдалану рқылыжылуғатөзі мдіқұрылысқоспалар ынәзірлеужәнеоларды жетілдірілг енқұрылғыдақалыптау]
abstract: In the context of the increasing volume of industrial waste and stricter environmental requirements, the urgent task is to efficiently process them to produce products with high added value. In this work, the composition of industrial products of vanadium production formed during the hydrometallurgical processing of rare metals is investigated, and the possibility of their use for the production of heat-resistant building mixes is substantiated. A comprehensive analysis, including X-ray, X-ray fluorescence, and scanning electron microscopic methods, revealed a high content of silica, aluminum oxides, and refractory minerals that determine the heat resistance of the material. Optimal compositions of building mixes based on Portland cement, liquid glass, and chamotte have been developed, providing compressive strength up to 45 MPa and resistance to thermal cycling at temperatures up to 1800 ° C. The design of a device for forming building blocks based on industrial waste from metallurgical production by vibration pressing is proposed, designed to ensure high density and geometric stability of products. The results obtained confirm the possibility of complex industrial waste disposal with the simultaneous creation of environmentally safe, durable, and heat-resistant building materials used in energy, metallurgy, the chemical industry, and civil engineering. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Physicochemical Analysis of Water-Soluble Sodium Silicate Obtained from Modified Raw Materials; [Модификацияланған шикізаттан алынған суда еритін натрий силикатының физика-химиялық талдауы]; [Физико-химический анализ водорастворимого силиката натрия, полученного из модификационного сырья]
abstract: This article investigates the physicochemical properties of water-soluble sodium silicate synthesized from modified raw materials. During the research process, several compositions of soluble glass samples were prepared, and their structural characteristics were analyzed using infrared (IR) spectroscopy. In addition, X-ray fluorescence (XRF) analysis was employed to determine the chemical composition of the products and the distribution of their components. The results demonstrated that two of the studied compositions are considered promising in terms of technological and physicochemical parameters. In particular, the third composition provided the most optimal outcome, exhibiting superior stability, structural homogeneity, and practical applicability of the soluble glass. The findings of this study highlight the potential for developing energy-efficient technologies for the production of water-soluble sodium silicate based on local and modified raw materials. The results of infrared spectroscopic analysis showed that the BMK-3 sample exhibited significantly more stable and intense Si–O–Na bonds compared to other analyzed samples and compositions. This phenomenon is explained by the structural uniformity of the composition, the balance of cation–anion interactions, and the strength of the glass network structure. Therefore, the third composition is recommended as the most promising sample. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Characterization of shale gas adsorption behavior based on the gravimetric method
abstract: Based on gravimetric isothermal adsorption experiments, methane adsorption isotherms were obtained under different temperature and pressure conditions. High-pressure adsorption models were used to investigate methane adsorption behavior and its controlling factors in shale, and machine-learning methods were further introduced to predict adsorption capacity and quantify the influence of different parameters. The dual-site Langmuir model, supercritical Dubinin-Radushkevich model, and Ono-Kondo lattice model were employed to fit and compare high-pressure adsorption behavior over the full pressure range. For machine-learning prediction, temperature, pressure, total organic carbon, and vitrinite reflectance were selected as input variables, and excess adsorption capacity was used as the output variable. The results show that the absolute methane adsorption capacity of shale generally increases rapidly with pressure at the initial stage and then gradually approaches a plateau, while it decreases significantly with increasing temperature. The Ono-Kondo lattice model exhibits the best fitting stability and physical interpretability across different pressure ranges, effectively characterizing adsorption behavior under supercritical conditions. Factor analysis indicates that total organic carbon is positively correlated with methane adsorption capacity, whereas temperature shows a negative correlation. Thermal maturity, as represented by vitrinite reflectance, also affects methane adsorption capacity; however, its apparent influence is nonlinear and coupled with total organic carbon content. Among the machine-learning models, CatBoost achieves the highest prediction accuracy, with a coefficient of determination of 0.9528, indicating strong nonlinear fitting capability. SHAP-based interpretability analysis shows that the importance of different parameters controlling methane adsorption capacity follows the order: pressure > total organic carbon > temperature > vitrinite reflectance. This study provides experimental evidence and methodological support for understanding high-pressure shale gas adsorption mechanisms, accurately characterizing adsorption capacity, and evaluating geological gas-in-place in the Xujiahe Formation of the Sichuan Basin. © 2026 The Authors. title: Inflammation-driven multiorgan Dysfunction: Biomarker-Guided diagnosis, mechanistic insights and emerging precision therapeutic strategies
abstract: Inflammation-driven multiorgan dysfunction syndrome (MODS) represents a major cause of morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients and arises from a complex interplay of dysregulated immune responses, endothelial injury, microvascular dysfunction, metabolic disturbances, and maladaptive organ crosstalk. Although traditionally associated with sepsis, similar inflammatory pathways contribute to organ dysfunction in trauma, pancreatitis, severe viral infections, autoimmune disorders, and other critical illnesses. This review synthesizes current evidence regarding the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying inflammation-driven MODS, with particular emphasis on cytokine amplification, innate and adaptive immune dysregulation, immunothrombosis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and barrier failure across multiple organ systems. Emerging biomarkers, including inflammatory cytokines, endothelial injury markers, damage-associated molecular patterns, and organ-specific indicators, are discussed for their diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance. However, significant challenges remain, including biomarker variability, lack of standardized thresholds, and the absence of universally accepted diagnostic panels for routine clinical use. The review further examines organ-specific manifestations and evolving therapeutic strategies, including anti-cytokine therapies, immunomodulation, endothelial protection, extracorporeal blood purification, and metabolic-targeted interventions. Importantly, many promising anti-inflammatory therapies have demonstrated limited success in clinical translation due to patient heterogeneity, inappropriate timing of intervention, and the dynamic transition between hyperinflammatory and immunosuppressed states. Advances in precision medicine and artificial intelligence offer opportunities for individualized risk stratification and biomarker-guided treatment selection, supporting improved health outcomes, quality of life, healthcare innovation, and sustainable healthcare systems. Integrating biomarker-driven insights with mechanistic understanding may improve clinical outcomes, reduce mortality, and facilitate the development of targeted therapies for this complex syndrome. Addressing these challenges will be essential for developing phenotype-driven therapeutic approaches and improving outcomes in patients with inflammation-driven multiorgan dysfunction. © 2026 The Authors. title: Transcriptomic biomarker analysis of micro- and nanoplastic induced cardiovascular toxicity reveals perturbations in mitochondrial and ribosomal networks
abstract: Environmental pollutants are increasingly recognized as major threats to human health worldwide with micro and nanoplastics (MNPs) outstanding on top, yet their contribution to cardiovascular disease (CVD) at the molecular level remains underexplored. In our study, we conducted an integrative bioinformatics analysis of human transcriptomic datasets to investigate the transcriptional alterations induced by MNP exposure. Differentially expressed genes revealed pervasive perturbations in pathways central to cardiovascular pathology, including oxidative stress, lipid metabolism, immune activation and mitochondrial functions. Protein-protein interaction networks and hub gene analysis identified mitochondrial genes such as MT-ND1 and COX5A, which were upregulated and linked to a potential mitochondrial stress signature requiring functional validation due to enhanced oxidative phosphorylation. On the other hand, ribosomal genes such as RPL5 were downregulated, suggesting impaired translational capacity and protein synthesis. This dual molecular mark, mitochondrial transcriptional regulation alongside ribosomal suppression highlights a coordinated cellular stress mechanism that could contribute to inflammation, remodeling, and energy imbalance in cardiovascular tissues. By mapping these signatures against cardiovascular associated gene sets, we demonstrated the MNP exposure converges molecular pathways already implicated in atherogenesis, cardiac remodeling, and vascular dysfunction. Importantly, transcription factor enrichment suggested upstream regulation by stress responsive factors, providing new insights into how plastic exposure may alter cellular homeostasis. Collectively, this work presents an integrative analysis linking transcriptomic signatures of human MNP exposed lung and intestinal cell models to curated cardiovascular disease gene sets. Our findings propose candidate hub genes and regulatory pathways for experimental validation and underscores the urgency of considering environmental plastic pollution into cardiovascular risk assessment, prevention, and therapeutic development. © 2026 The Authors. title: Axially symmetric Réthy flows in a finite nozzle with an obstacle inside
abstract: In this study, we show that there exists a unique solution to the axially symmetric incompressible Réthy flow for the steady three-dimensional Euler system, and that the free boundaries converge to a certain direction as the flow goes to infinity. This flow pattern was first proposed by Réthy in 1895. The crucial step in our analysis is to overcome the lack of smoothness near the corners at the nozzle inlet. Furthermore, we establish the smooth fit condition of the free boundaries, the positivity of the radial velocity and the asymptotic behavior of the flow far downstream. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Sedimentary facies modeling driven by morphodynamic sedimentary simulation under sparse-well conditions
abstract: Offshore oil and gas fields have become an increasingly important domain for reserve additions and production growth. However, sparse well control and limited-quality seismic data impose significant challenges to constructing high-resolution, depositionally consistent 3D geological models. Multiple-point geostatistics (MPS) can preserve complex spatial structures through training images and maintain geological realism under sparse constraints, yet the construction of representative training images is often difficult and subject to analog-based uncertainties. To address this issue, we propose a sedimentary facies modeling workflow tailored for sparse-well offshore settings. This method employs morphodynamic sedimentary modeling, in which paleo-geomorphic and hydrodynamic conditions are explicitly constrained to generate simulation outputs that honor the geological context of the target system. Based on these simulation results, more objective training images that better reflect depositional dynamics and sedimentary patterns are constructed to constrain facies modeling. By reproducing depositional mechanisms and providing geologically consistent spatial patterns, the approach significantly enhances facies prediction under limited well control and offers a new pathway for fine-scale reservoir modeling in offshore fields. © 2026 The Authors. title: Numerical investigation on percussive cutting of Hubei hot dry rock using conical cutter under varying impact parameters
abstract: As the development of geothermal resources in medium to deep dry hot rock formations progresses, traditional drilling technologies face numerous challenges posed by high-strength hard rocks. These challenges, including inadequate bit penetration capacity and low rotational cutting efficiency, severely constrain drilling performance. In this context, hydraulic impact hammer drilling technology has demonstrated significant advantages in enhancing drilling speed. To investigate the rock-breaking mechanisms under the coupled effects of impact load magnitude and frequency, deep granite was selected as the research object. Based on dynamic mechanical experimental data obtained under high-temperature and high-pressure conditions (200 °C, 40 MPa), a two-dimensional dynamic numerical model for cone-shaped tooth impact cutting of dry hot rock has been developed by incorporating cohesive elements. This model systematically analyzes the effects of varying impact loads (9 to 12 kN) and impact frequencies (30 to 60 Hz) on rock fragmentation patterns, dynamic response characteristics, and impact energy. The results indicate that the cone-shaped tooth impact cutting exhibits a pronounced “dynamic crushing-shear coupling” feature, with the rock-breaking process undergoing dynamic evolution from local crushing initiation to volume fracturing, eventually leading to shear-mixed destruction. An increase in impact load significantly enhances the system's dynamic response amplitude, leading to a transition in the rock-breaking mode from shallow local crushing to extensive shear-mixed failure, accompanied by a notable increase in the fractured area. Additionally, increasing the impact frequency reinforces the superposition effect of stress waves within the rock and ensures continuous energy input, resulting in a denser dynamic response and further expanding the wedge-shaped fracture zone in front of the tooth tip. Moreover, as both load and frequency increase, the impact damaged area and energy increases significantly, allowing the system's energy to be more efficiently converted into rock damage and fracture energy. This study reveals the mechanisms by which high-frequency and high-energy parameters influence the efficiency of impact rock breaking, providing important theoretical support for the optimization of hydraulic impact hammers and the design of drill bit structures. © 2026 The Authors. title: New pulse sequence for improving cardiac black-blood and PSIR MRI quality in cases of arrhythmia
abstract: Most conventional cardiac MRI scans, which rely on electrocardiogram (ECG)-triggered segmented acquisition for k-space data, are highly sensitive to arrhythmia—a vulnerability that can induce severe motion artifacts, thereby degrading image quality and diagnostic accuracy. This study developed a novel pulse sequence: an MRI-independent thread continuously records and analyzes the subject's heart rhythm throughout the entire scan, calculates key temporal parameters in real time, feeds them back to update the sequence dynamically based on actual rhythm, thereby reducing k-space data misalignment and eliminating motion artifacts. Experimental results showed that the new pulse sequence effectively improved cardiac black-blood T2-weighted and phase-sensitive inversion recovery (PSIR) image quality in cases of arrhythmia, and with broad application prospects for cardiac MRI in arrhythmic subjects. This “prevention-first” approach (rather than “repair-after”) makes it highly clinically translatable, as it can be deployed on standard equipment without additional costs. © 2026 The Authors.

title: MXene-based biosensors for biomedical diagnostics: From molecular recognition to wearable systems
abstract: Two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) have emerged as a versatile class of electroactive nanomaterials for next-generation biomedical diagnostics. Their metallic conductivity, tunable surface terminations (–O, –OH, –F), hydrophilicity, and compatibility with nanocomposite engineering enable efficient biomolecule immobilization and high-fidelity signal transduction across electrochemical, plasmonic, wearable, and implantable platforms. This review critically examines recent advances in MXene-enabled biosensors for oncology diagnostics, metabolic monitoring, neurotransmitter detection, and continuous physiological analysis. In cancer diagnostics, MXene-based immunosensors have achieved ultralow detection limits, including 0.0036 pg mL−1 for squamous cell carcinoma antigen and 1 nU mL−1 for CA15-3 and CA-19-9, while exosome detection has reached sensitivities of 19 particles μL−1. In metabolic applications, MXene systems demonstrate nanomolar detection capability, rapid response times (as low as 2 s), and stable performance in whole blood and sweat matrices. Engineering strategies including noble metal hybridization, polymer stabilization, dendrimer functionalization, ratiometric sensing, and microfluidic integration are analyzed to elucidate structure–property–performance relationships. Wearable and implantable architectures further extend MXene functionality toward real-time health monitoring. Despite their promising analytical performance, important translational challenges remain, including oxidation susceptibility, biofouling, enzyme fragility, batch-to-batch reproducibility, large-scale manufacturing standardization, and limited long-term clinical validation. By integrating materials engineering with mechanistic insight, comparative analysis, and translational benchmarking, this review provides a strategic roadmap for advancing MXene biosensors from laboratory prototypes toward clinically viable and commercially translatable diagnostic technologies. © 2026 The Authors. title: Where does the exergy go? Risk-aware irreversibility mapping of a PCM-buffered solar photovoltaic-thermal/geothermal ventilation system
abstract: This study answers a practical question in renewable ventilation design: where does the exergy go when solar–geothermal preconditioning is combined with latent thermal buffering? A hybrid ventilation system coupling an earth–air heat exchanger (EAHE) with an air-based photovoltaic–thermal (PVT) unit is investigated, where phase change material (PCM) is embedded around the buried duct to act as a thermal buffer. Rather than reporting only annual energy savings, the work provides a risk-aware irreversibility breakdown that tracks exergy destruction across preconditioning, mixing, humidity control, and final conditioning. Several scenario analyses are conducted using hourly meteorological records collected over the 2019–2024 period. A bi-level optimization strategy is employed to simultaneously refine the system configuration and time-dependent operating conditions, including ventilation intensity and fresh-air intake ratio. To reduce occupant discomfort under critical conditions, a conditional value-at-risk criterion is incorporated to account for extreme thermo-hygrometric situations. The results indicate that PCM integration lowers system irreversibility. This behavior is mainly attributed to decreased ventilation demand and lower fresh-air intake. As a result, exergy destruction caused by air mixing and dehumidification is reduced. Although CVaR slightly increases during limited hot periods, overall discomfort risk remains about 50–60% below the baseline. © 2026 The Authors. title: Liquid-Core Long Period Grating Temperature Sensor Fabricated by Femtosecond Laser Line Scanning
abstract: We propose a novel liquid-core long-period fiber grating (LPFG) based on a hollow-core fiber (HCF). The grating is fabricated using a femtosecond laser line-scanning technique to periodically induce refractive index modulation in the silica region adjacent to the air core. By infiltrating a high-refractive-index liquid into the HCF, a liquid-core waveguide is formed, enabling resonant coupling between the fundamental core mode and cladding modes, which gives rise to distinct resonant dips. The dispersion characteristics of the liquid-filled fiber can be tailored through the refractive index of the infiltrated liquid. By optimizing this parameter, enhanced temperature sensitivity is achieved. Experimental results demonstrate that the temperature response of the LPFG strongly depends on the refractive index of the filling liquid. In particular, when a liquid with a refractive index of 1.476 is used, a high temperature sensitivity of approximately −3.34 nm/°C is obtained over the range of 25–40 °C. The proposed device provides a proof-of-concept platform for high-sensitivity liquid-core LPFG temperature sensing. © 1995-2012 IEEE.

title: miRNA-mRNA multi-omics integration in breast cancer staging
abstract: The tumor-node-metastasis (TNM) anatomic system is the current clinical standard for breast cancer staging, yet it inadequately captures the molecular heterogeneity that drives disease progression, motivating the development of expression-based biomarker classifiers. We integrated microRNA (miRNA) and messenger RNA (mRNA) expression profiles from 1081 primary TCGA-BRCA tumors (early-stage, Stages I–II, n = 822; late-stage, Stages III–IV, n = 259) and benchmarked nine machine learning algorithms using a stratified 70/15/15 train–validation–test split with class-imbalance weighting. On the held-out test set, XGBoost, selected after Bayesian hyperparameter optimization on the validation set, achieved AUC = 0.687 (95% CI: 0.622–0.748), accuracy = 79.8%, and good model calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.31), significantly outperforming mRNA-only (AUC = 0.654; p = 0.028) and miRNA-only (AUC = 0.612; p = 0.007) models. Differential expression analysis identified 15 significant miRNAs and 194 significant mRNAs (FDR <0.05), and regulatory network analysis revealed three co-expression modules governing epithelial-mesenchymal transition, metabolic reprogramming, and immune evasion, with 15 hub miRNAs regulating 97–516 predicted targets. Multi-omics integration captures progression-associated molecular signatures beyond anatomic staging and could, pending external validation, complement conventional TNM staging by providing a molecularly informed risk-stratification layer; the framework provides a reproducible basis for exploratory translational biomarker discovery. © 2026 The Authors. title: Source term identification for a class of history-dependent quasi variational-hemivariational inequalities
abstract: This article is devoted to the study of inverse problems related to the identification of the source term in a class of evolutionary history-dependent quasi-variational–hemivariational inequalities with constraints introduced in [S. Migórski, Y. Bai, S. Zeng, A new class of history-dependent quasi–variational–hemivariational inequalities with constraints, Commun. Nonlinear Sci. Numer. Simul. 114 (2022), 106686]. We establish the existence of solutions to the considered inverse problem. Furthermore, we illustrate the theoretical results by investigating a quasistatic frictional contact problem. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately recovering the unknown source term. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Prediction and optimization of drill string torque and drag in horizontal wells based on dynamic friction coefficient testing
abstract: With the large-scale development of unconventional oil and gas resources, extended-reach horizontal wells have been increasingly utilized in shale reservoirs. However, excessive torque and drag caused by drillstring–wellbore contact can reduce weight-on-bit transfer efficiency, limit horizontal-section extension, and increase the risk of drilling complications. A major source of uncertainty in conventional torque-and-drag prediction is the use of a constant friction coefficient, which cannot adequately represent the dynamic friction behavior under different drilling modes and water-based drilling fluid lubrication. In this study, dynamic friction coefficient tests were conducted for steel–shale, steel–sandstone, and steel–steel contact pairs under water-based drilling fluid lubrication. The effects of lithology, sliding velocity, rotational speed, and normal load on the friction coefficient were investigated. Based on the experimental results, a velocity-dependent dynamic friction coefficient model was established and incorporated into a three-dimensional stiff-string torque-and-drag prediction model. The additional contact force induced by drillstring buckling was also considered to improve the calculation of normal contact force in highly deviated and horizontal sections. Field verification was performed using the J-H1 Well in the Ordos Basin and ZH-5 Well in the Sichuan Basin. For the J-H1 Well, the proposed model reduced the hook-load prediction error to 6.5% under sliding drilling and 5.9% under composite drilling, and reduced the wellhead torque prediction error to 8.5%. For the ZH-5 Well, the relative errors of hook-load and wellhead torque prediction were 5.0% and 8.2%, respectively, which were significantly lower than those obtained using the conventional constant-friction-coefficient model. The model was further applied to the J-H2 Well to evaluate the effects of trajectory control tools, weight on bit, rotational speed, lubricants, and drilling modes on torque and drag, drillstring buckling, and horizontal-section extension capability. The results show that the proposed dynamic-friction-coefficient model provides more reliable friction inputs for torque-and-drag prediction under water-based drilling fluid lubrication and can support drilling-parameter optimization in extended-reach horizontal wells. © 2026 The Authors. title: EVALUATION OF UAV-ADMINISTERED INSECTICIDES AT DIFFERENT DOSES AGAINST BROWN PLANTHOPPER NILAPARVATA LUGENS (STAL)
abstract: The study aimed to evaluate the bioefficacy of triflumezopyrim 10 SC and pymetrozine 50 WG applied through an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) for managing brown planthopper (Nilaparvata lugens) in rice, and to assess their effect on its key predator, the mirid bug (Cyrtorhinus lividipennis). A field experiment was conducted during kharif 2024 at ICAR-IARI, New Delhi, using rice variety Pusa Basmati 1885 under natural pest infestation. Each insecticide was applied at different rates, i.e., 0.75x, 1x and 1.5x concentrations of the recommended dose using a calibrated Marut 365S multi-rotor UAV. Population counts of BPH and mirid bugs were recorded on tagged hills before spraying and at 5 and 10 days after spraying (DAS). Both insecticides significantly reduced BPH populations at 10 DAS compared to the untreated control, with hopper counts declining to below two insects/ hill across all treated plots. No statistically significant differences were observed among the three dose levels of either insecticide, indicating that even the reduced dose (0.75x) was equally effective under UAV application. Mirid bug populations showed a moderate decline in treated plots but remained comparatively higher in reduced-dose treatments, suggesting lower non-target impact. The findings demonstrate that UAV-based application of triflumezopyrim and pymetrozine is effective for BPH suppression even at reduced doses, while causing comparatively less disruption to the predator community. Reduced-dose UAV application therefore offers potential advantages for resistance management, environmental safety, and integration within rice IPM programs, while reducing pesticide input and application costs. © 2027, The Entomological Society of India. .

title: Numerical Investigation of the Reverse Diffusion in Binary Hydrocarbon Systems at Equilibrium States
abstract: Molecular diffusion is a ubiquitous phenomenon in nature, where the diffusive flux typically aligns with the concentration gradient of species. However, this conventional relationship between diffusive flux and concentration gradient does not always hold, as seen in reverse diffusion, where the flux and concentration gradient are oriented in opposite directions. An important cause of reverse diffusion is the inverse relationship between species concentration and chemical potential, which can be attributed to the non-ideality of the species involved. This study investigates the conditions for reverse diffusion in binary hydrocarbon systems by calculating the derivatives of chemical potential with respect to molar concentration. The Peng-Robinson Equation of State (PR-EoS) is employed to describe the fluid thermodynamics. Additionally, the derivatives of chemical potential with respect to molar fraction, as well as the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Jacobian matrix of chemical potentials with respect to molar concentrations, are calculated. The complete results include binary normal alkane systems ranging from C1 to C10, and CO2-normal alkane systems at temperatures ranging from 200K to 600K, with molar concentrations between 0 and 20,000 mol/m3. The main conclusions are as follows: (1) Ideal gases and ideal solutions exhibit no reverse diffusion theoretically; (2) Reverse diffusion is strongly temperaturedependent, with a higher likelihood at lower temperatures; (3) Binary mixtures with a near-zero molar concentration of one species are more prone to reverse diffusion than those where both species are present in appreciable molar concentrations; (4) The reverse diffusion phenomenon is most pronounced near phase interfaces. © 2027 Global Science Press.

title: High-Precision Calculation of Wave-Current Forces on Offshore Wind Turbines Based on the Regularized Singular Boundary Method
abstract: The main purpose of this article is to develop a regularized singular boundary method for high-precision simulation of wave-current forces on offshore wind turbines. The engineering bottlenecks encountered in the construction of offshore wind turbines are discussed, i.e., how to effectively deal with the singularity of the Green’s function at the origin, and how to accurately calculate wave forces on offshore wind turbines. An origin intensity factor technique for marine dynamic environment simulation is proposed. Based on the origin intensity factor and the Green’s function, a regularized singular boundary method is constructed, which only requires placing source points on the wet surface of offshore wind turbines. Wave load is calculated by substituting wave parameters affected by wave-current interaction into the linear diffraction model. The wave-current force on offshore wind turbines is finally obtained by superimposing the current load and the wave load. Numerical experiments show that the regularized singular boundary method can accurately analyze the Bragg resonance of offshore wind turbines caused by wave-current force. © 2027 Global Science Press.

title: On the Stability and Differentiability of Nonlocal Strain Gradient Porous Thermoelasticity Under (Coleman or Pipkin)–Gurtin’s Law
abstract: A nonlocal theory for porous thermoelasticity based on strain gradient approach where the heat conduction follows the (Coleman or Pipkin)-Gurtin’s law is deduced from [3] with some qualitative properties. The new aspect we propose here is to introduce the Coleman-Gurtin’s law in the temperatures, which depends essentially on past history, representing an improvement of Fourier’s, Cattaneo’s and Gurtin-Pipkin’s models. The case of Fourier’s law or Gurtin-Pipkin’s law can be recovered from the derived system. The obtained system is a coupling of three equations with memory term and higher gradients terms due to the length scale parameters ϖ and l. Based on semigroups theory, we establish existence and uniqueness of weak and strong solutions to the one dimensional problem. By an approach based on the Gearhart-Herbst-Prüss-Huang theorem, we prove that the associated semigroup is exponentially stable, but not differentiable for either Coleman-Gurtin’s law or PipkinGurtin’s law. The lack of analyticity and the impossibility to localise the solutions in time are direct consequences of the lack of differentiability. ©2027 Global Science Press.

title: A Mixed Finite Element Method for Elliptic Interface Problems on Local Anisotropic Hybrid Meshes
abstract: We propose a mixed finite element method for solving second-order elliptic interface problems. The method is based on a fitted hybrid mesh, constructed by connecting the intersection points of the interface with an underlying unfitted triangulation. The resulting mesh consists of anisotropic triangles and quadrilaterals aligned with the interface. On this mesh, we define a pair of finite element spaces of type RT0–P0, designed to preserve the commutativity between the interpolation operator and the divergence operator. This structure ensures that the discrete inf-sup condition is satisfied without the need for additional stabilization. We establish optimal convergence rates in the L2-norm for both the velocity and pressure approximations. Numerical experiments are presented to confirm the theoretical results. © 2027 Global Science Press.

title: Buckling Analysis of Functionally Graded Beams under Combined Loadings
abstract: This paper investigates the buckling behavior of axially functionally graded (FG) material beams subjected to combined loads with various boundary conditions. The classical beam theory is employed for the analysis, and material properties are described using power law equations. The governing equation for buckling of FG beams was derived using the energy method and solved by using the generalized differential quadrature (DQ) method. The current study explores the buckling problem of FG beam under combined loadings, focusing on the interplay of gradient index, parameter np and boundary conditions. The results demonstrate that the buckling resistance of functionally graded beams is enhanced with an increase in the gradient index. For functionally graded beams with a fixed parameter np, the critical buckling load exhibits a nonlinear increase with the gradient index. On the other hand, for functionally graded beams with a fixed material distribution, the critical buckling load decreases almost linearly with the parameter np, and the slope of this linear relationship is determined by the gradient index and the boundary conditions. This study provides valuable insights into the buckling behavior of functionally graded beams under combined loads, offering guidance for the design and optimization of such beams in engineering applications. © 2027 Global Science Press.

title: Numerical Investigation of Flow Control Around Three Cylinders using a Passive Method
abstract: This study investigates the flow behavior around three cylinders with attached splitter plates arranged in an equilateral triangular configuration using the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) at low Reynolds numbers (Re). Although previous research has focused on flow around bluff bodies without splitter plates, this study examines the effects of splitter plates on flow control. The primary objective is to explore passive flow control methods-those requiring no external energy-around the cylinders. Key parameters analyzed include Reynolds number (Re), gap ratio (g∗ ), and splitter plate length (L∗). The investigation considers three different Re values, five g∗ values, and five L∗ values for each g∗ . Drag coefficients (CD), lift coefficients (CL ), and Strouhal numbers (St ) are computed to elucidate the relationships between vortex shedding characteristics, g∗, L∗, and Re. The results demonstrate that wake flow patterns, flow characteristics, and force coefficients are strongly influenced by g∗, L∗ and Re. Distinct flow regimes emerge: at low g∗ and L∗, the three cylinders behave as a single bluff body (SBB), whereas at large g∗ and L∗, the flow transitions to a continuous pattern, diminishing the interaction effects among the cylinders. For small L∗, vortices form near the cylinders, while larger L∗ results in streamlined flow. Additionally, at low Re, vortex shedding remains consistent, but as Re increases, the vortices become irregular. © 2027 Global Science Press.

title: Evaluating structural controls as seismic hazard potential through joint mapping and kinematic analysis: West Rand Gold Mine, South Africa
abstract: This study investigates the structural characteristics of joint sets and their potential influence on seismic hazard at the West Rand Gold Mine, South Africa. A total of 144 systematic 2 m × 2 m window-mapping stations were established across the Eastern and Western sections of the mine to provide representative coverage of recognised geotechnical domains. Joint orientation, persistence, and infill characteristics were recorded and analysed using stereographic projection techniques to identify dominant joint sets and assess their potential influence on shear behaviour. The results identified three major joint sets that are persistent throughout the mine, with Joint Set 1 being the most prominent overall, while Joint Set 3 is more dominant in the Western section. Approximately 45% of the mapped discontinuities were classified as random joints and were predominantly steeply dipping. Calcite was identified as the dominant infill material, indicating reduced joint shear strength and an increased susceptibility to slip. Analysis of joint orientations relative to mining face configurations suggests that mining advances parallel or semi-parallel to persistent, weakly infilled discontinuities may increase the potential for shear reactivation and mining-induced seismicity. The findings demonstrate the importance of detailed structural characterization in seismic hazard assessment, mine planning, and ground control in deep-level gold mining operations. © 2026 The Authors. title: The Band Structure of In-Plane Elastic Cracked Phononic Crystals Based on the Local RBF Collocation Method
abstract: In this paper, the 2D cracked phononic crystals of in-plane elastic waves are studied based on the local radial basis function collocation method (LRBFCM). The direct method is used to solve the instability caused by the derivative calculation of the LRBFCM in the crack. The band structure of the cracked phononic crystals according to the wave vectors in the first Brillouin Zone are presented. The relationship between the band structure and the cracks with different lengths and positions are fully studied. Different acoustic impedance ratios, filling rates, and lattice forms are considered. The numerical results are validated by the band structures obtained from the FEM, which also show interesting phenomenon of the cracked phononic crystals. © 2027 Global Science Press.

title: Nonlinear Vibration Analysis of Fractional Viscoelastic Timoshenko Nanobeams Considering Nonlocal and Surface Effects
abstract: This study proposes a non-classical Timoshenko beam model that incorporates von-Kármán geometric nonlinearity and a fractional Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic model, based on nonlocal strain gradient theory and surface elasticity theory. The model captures the effects of microstructure, surface energy, and nonlocality, with governing equations and boundary conditions derived using Hamilton’s principle to describe fractional viscoelastic nanobeams under transverse harmonic excitation. The Galerkin method and a predictor-corrector algorithm solve the resulting fractionalorder equations, revealing how key parameters influence nonlinear free and forced vibrations. Numerical simulations reveal that fractional order significantly modifies the nonlinear vibration characteristics of structures and enhances damping as the fractional order increases. Furthermore, due to the correlation between fractional order and excitation frequency, the effects of fractional order on nonlinear time responses differ between free and forced vibrations. These findings highlight the crucial role of fractional viscoelasticity in influencing the dynamic behavior of nanostructures, providing valuable insights for the design of advanced nanoscale systems. © 2027 Global Science Press.

title: Error Analysis of the Stabilized Finite Volume Method for Time-Dependent Incompressible MHD Equations with Rotational Velocity Correction
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a fully decoupled numerical method for solving the time-dependent incompressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations. The method features a rotational velocity correction technique, which is combined with the finite volume method to ensure both the local conservation of physical quantities. Using the lowest equal-order mixed finite element pair (P1 −P1 −P1 ) to approximate the velocity, magnetic field, and pressure, we address the inf-sup condition through pressure projection stabilization. A semi-implicit method is used to handle the nonlinear terms, and the rotational velocity correction method decouples the MHD system into three subsystems, thereby simplifying the computation and solution process. By selecting appropriate test functions and applying the Gronwall inequality, the stability of the numerical solution and optimal error estimates for velocity, magnetic field, and pressure are established. Finally, numerical results are presented to validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the performance of the proposed method. © 2027 Global Science Press.

title: Quantification to Symmetry-Breaking of Rotation Invariance for Attractors in Perturbed Lorenz System
abstract: For the existence of the external perturbation on the atmospheric system, the idealized Lorenz system cannot be used to describe the local characteristics of the atmospheric system accurately. From the opinion of mathematical physics, the failure of the description for local characteristics of the perturbed atmospheric system by the idealized Lorenz system is resulted from the symmetry-breaking effects on the local structure the solutions for the system, including the Lorenz attractor. This study aims to precisely quantify the symmetry-breaking degree of the rotation invariant law for the attractors in a perturbed Lorenz system to permit the reproduction on its local characteristics accurately. The attractors of the perturbed Lorenz system are reproduced employing the second-level fourth-order symplectic Runge-Kutta scheme firstly. The structure-preserving properties of the scheme are illustrated by the tiny relative energy error in the conservative field of the Lorenz system, which verifies the validity of the simulation results indirectly. The symmetry-breaking degree for the rotation invariant law of the attractors in the system is characterized by the quantized error defined as the Euclidean distance between the points on the trajectories of the rotated part and of the unrotated part at the same moment. The symmetry-breaking phenomenon characterized by the quantized error goes through three stages in sequence, including the slow growth stage, the quick growth stage, and the oscillation stage. In addition, a pair of Lorenz attractors with the approximate rotation invariant property are observed when the quantized error is in the slow growth stage or in the quick growth stage. From the numerical results, it can be found that, the perturbation may cause the periodic step increase (the amplitudes of steps are doubling increase approximately) of the error with the time elapse even if the perturbation is tiny, which leads to more serious damage to the stability of the system. The main contribution of this work is providing an approach to predict the local stability of the Lorenz system, which may benefit for the accuracy of meteorological forecast or the simulation of specific atmospheric phenomena. © 2027 Global Science Press.

title: Theoretical Analysis of Liquid Lens Evaporation on Immiscible Liquid Surface
abstract: The evaporation of liquid lens widely occurs in various scientific and industrial applications. In this study, a theoretical model is set up for liquid lens evaporation under the axisymmetric toroidal coordinate, with coupled internal heat conduction and external vapor diffusion. The effect of evaporative cooling number, liquid lens shape and volume on evaporation performance is quantitatively analyzed. It is found that overall evaporation rate is determined by the competing effect of evaporation flux and area of upper surface. With the increasing ratios of upper and lower tangential angles, at high evaporative cooling numbers or large liquid volumes, overall evaporation rates decrease firstly, after reaching the minimum value, they start to increase until the asymptotic value. The ”2/3 power law” holds for transient volume variation of liquid lens over time, independent of evaporative cooling and liquid lens shape. These findings may help get insight into the liquid lens evaporation on immiscible liquid. © 2027 Global Science Press.

title: The impact of ideality assumption on biomethane upgrading model
abstract: While most research rely on ideal-gas assumptions without ensuring their accuracy, simulation of adsorption-based biomethane upgrading can lower experimental costs and enhance process analysis. In the current age of decarbonization and clean energy, biomethane has gained attention as a promising renewable energy source. Biomethane is a reliable and sustainable fuel source. This work focuses on biomethane upgrading by the adsorption process. Effect of pressure, temperature on adsorbent breakthrough and saturation time were examined. Four different adsorbents silica gel, activated carbon, carbon molecular sieve, and 13X zeolite were investigated. The effects of model assumptions in regard to adsorbate ideality was also investigated. The results show that adsorption pressure is the main factor influencing the responses coinciding with the process being pressure dominated. Breakthrough time increased by up to 58% when pressure was increased from 2 to 15 bar, but it fell by around 10% when temperature was raised from 25 to 45 °C. The design models for breakthrough and saturation time obtained R2 values of 0.986 to 1, and simulated breakthrough curves corresponded with data from the literature, with R2 values ranging from 0.95 to 0.99. The ideal equation of state assumptions were reliable up to 20 bars. Beyond this point the model is more sensitive to assumptions as the adsorbate reacts non-ideally. This research helps shed light on underreported aspects of biomethane modelling and help provides more reliable frameworks for process assumptions. © 2026 The Authors. title: KINETIC MODELING OF CHLORANTRANILIPROLE AND LAMBDA-CYHALOTHRIN IN NON-FLOODED SOIL SYSTEMS USING GC-MS/ MS
abstract: A pot culture experiment evaluated the dissipation kinetics and ecological risk of a ready-mix formulation of chlorantraniliprole (9.30%) + lambda-cyhalothrin (4.60%) ZC in sandy loam soil under controlled non-flooded conditions. Soil residues (0-10 cm) were monitored up to 90 days using GC-MS/ MS. QuEChERS outperformed MSPD, giving >85% recoveries. Both pesticides dissipated via first-order kinetics (R2 >0.97), with half-lives of 1.65-2.84 days (chlorantraniliprole) and 2.47-4.52 days (lambda-cyhalothrin). Residues persisted up to 60 and 45 days, respectively, depending on dose levels. Initial RQ values for Eisenia fetida (>1) indicated high risk but decreased to <0.1 as residues degraded. Overall, the study reveals rapid dissipation, short-lived ecological risk, and provides essential data for environmental safety evaluation and optimized pesticide application strategies. © 2027, The Entomological Society of India. .

title: SPATIAL MODELLING OF DENGUE OUTBREAK RISK BY INTEGRATING LARVAL DENSITY AND SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS IN AN URBAN AREA
abstract: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) remains a significant public health challenge in Indonesia. Effective prevention requires moving beyond reactive case-based responses to proactive, spatially-targeted interventions based on comprehensive risk factors. This study explores a spatial model to assess DHF outbreak risk in the working area of the Somba Opu Health Center, Gowa Regency, Indonesia. Primary and secondary data were integrated through GIS overlay analysis. Key parameters included larval density (House Index, Container Index, Breteau Index), microclimate (temperature, humidity), socio-environmental vulnerability (population and building density), and community capacity (implementation of the PSN 3M program). Results: Spatial analysis revealed significant heterogeneity in dengue hemorrhagic fever risk across the study area. High-risk clusters were identified in Katangka, Tompobalang, and Tombolo villages, associated with high larval indices, optimal microclimates, and high population density. Larval density showed a significant positive correlation with these optimal temperature and humidity ranges. In contrast, villages with consistent Mosquito Nest Eradication implementation, such as Kalegowa and Bonto-Bontoa, exhibited higher larva-free rates and lower overall risk. The integrated spatial model, incorporating entomological, climatic, and socio-environmental data, successfully categorized the region into low, medium, and high-risk zones. This precise mapping enables targeted, cost-effective vector control and allows health authorities to prioritize interventions in high-risk areas for sustainable dengue prevention. © 2027, The Entomological Society of India. .

title: Electric current generation in bacterial isolates from river sediments using microbial fuel cell
abstract: Microbial fuel cell (MFC) represents a total approach to converting organic matter to sustainable and clean energy. This study investigated the electricity production potentials of bacteria isolated from the sediment of some Rivers at various depths using microbial fuel cells. Samples were taken from River Ala, Ogbese, and Owena at surface water, sediment surface, 50 cm, 100 cm, and 150 cm (depths) using a soil auger. Bacterial population, isolation, and identification of sediments at various depths were determined using microbiological techniques. Pure cultured, Co-cultured, and mixed bacterial isolates of some bacteria isolated from the sediment were used in the current generation. A double-chamber microbial fuel cell was constructed for these bacterial isolates and current, voltage, and resistance readings were taken for 12 days. The current and voltage generated increased in the earlier days of the experiment and decreased in the latter days while the resistance readings were high throughout the experiment. Bacillus pumilus generated the highest current of 0.47 mA and Pseudomonas aeruginosa generated the highest voltage of 1.85V for the pure cultured MFC chamber. In the co-isolated and mixed cultured MFC chamber, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Bacillus pumilus generated the highest current of 1.18 mA and the highest voltage of 1.16 V. Therefore, it is shown that bacteria isolate from river can be used to generate microbial fuel cell which could be a promising technologies to generate electric power in a large scale electric power generation. © 2026 The Authors. title: Prediction of shale brittleness index by genetic algorithm optimization random forest algorithm
abstract: The brittleness index (BI) is a key parameter for determining whether shale is compressible. Accurately predicting BI during CO2 storage is beneficial for evaluating shale's reservoir and cap rock properties and selecting favorable CO2 geological reservoirs. This study uses six logging parameters, including acoustic log (AC), gamma ray log (GR), density log (DEN), neutron porosity (CNL), array induction resistivity (AT120), and potassium log (K), as input variables to develop a traditional multiple linear regressionmodel and four machine learning models for predicting BI. The machine learning models include backpropagation neural network (BP), random forest (RF), genetic algorithm optimized backpropagation neural network (GA-BP), and genetic algorithm optimized random forest (GA-RF). The interpretability of the model is analyzed with Shapley Additive explanations (SHAP). The results indicate that: (1) The coefficient of determination (R2) of the multiple linear regression model is 0.78. For the machine learning models, the R2 values between predicted and ture value are 0.83 (BP), 0.9336 (RF), 0.84 (GA-BP), and 0.96 (GA-RF). The GA-RF model exhibits the highest accuracy. In cross-basin validation, the GA-RF model achieves an R2 of 0.84. (2) In the GA-RF model, the parameter contributions in the importance voting are ranked in descending order as AC > K > CNL > AT120 > GR > DEN. The results indicate that mechanical and petrophysical properties, especially formation hardness, density, and shale-related indicators, are strongly correlated with BI, highlighting their key role in its prediction. (3) The SHAP analysis of the GA-RF model reveals that AC, K, CNL, and GR are strongly negatively correlated with their SHAP values, while AT120 exhibits a weak positive correlation. In contrast, DEN shows SHAP values concentrated around zero with limited variation. The SHAP results are consistent with the feature importance ranking. Accurate prediction of shale BI not only facilitates the identification of optimal fracturing pathways and development sweet spots, but also provides an important theoretical basis for CO2 sequestration site selection. © 2026 The Authors. title: Adaptive trajectory unified framework for stressed AC optimal power flow
abstract: Stressed AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) often exposes a difficult start bottleneck in which, from poor starts, the algorithm must reduce large power balance residuals and active operating limit violations before cost optimization becomes meaningful. This paper proposes the Adaptive Trajectory Unified Framework (ATJU), a residual shaped trajectory homotopy for stressed ACOPF. ATJU keeps the ACOPF model, hard bound projection, and projected first order kernel fixed, and uses a scalar continuation coordinate s to move from squared residual correction to cost oriented linear refinement. A lightweight BD–PTC branch supplies diagonal scaling and damping for the early stiff regime. On a controlled WB3 stressed protocol with shared starts and matched budgets, ATJU-full reaches 40/40 strict feasibility successes; ATJU-fixed-s0, ATJU-fixed-s1, and ATJU-hard-switch reach 0/40; and ATJU-no-BD–PTC gives 39/40. A structured advanced solver comparison shows that ATJU and CasADi+IPOPT both reach 30/30 successes on flat/adversarial stressed starts and 32/32 in the structured stress sweep, while scipy trust-constr is less reliable under the same screen. Case300 and case2736sp anytime curves further show that the same trajectory can continue improving qualified feasible objectives after feasibility is obtained. These results support ATJU as a complementary trajectory mechanism for stressed ACOPF under matched interfaces. © 2026

title: Electromagnetic state prediction in large PMSGs using a physics-informed KAN surrogate model
abstract: To address the challenge of rapid and accurate electromagnetic state prediction for large-scale permanent magnet synchronous generators (PMSGs), this paper proposes a multi-task learning (MTL) surrogate model integrating principal component analysis (PCA), physics-informed constraints, and Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs). The model accepts rotor speed, rotor position, and three-phase currents as inputs. It employs PCA for dimensionality reduction of the spatial magnetic flux density and utilizes a KAN-based multi-task prediction framework to simultaneously output both the magnetic field distribution and scalar quantities, including electromagnetic torque magnitude, iron loss, and eddy current loss. To enhance physical consistency, boundary conditions, divergence constraints, and torque calculation constraints are explicitly embedded into the loss function. Validation using finite element simulation data demonstrates that the model achieves a mean absolute error below 0.01 T for magnetic field reconstruction and a coefficient of determination exceeding 0.99 for electromagnetic torque magnitude prediction. A single inference requires approximately 0.3 seconds, representing a computational speedup exceeding 540 times compared to the finite element method. This work provides a methodological basis for digital twin applications of large-scale PMSGs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
