title: Fault recovery analysis and damping control for global stability of grid-forming energy storage based on Lyapunov's direct method
abstract: With the continuous integration of large-scale new energy into the power system, grid-forming energy storage plays a crucial role in maintaining system stability. However, the current research on the transient stability of grid-forming energy storage is still not comprehensive. The energy function method, as an important tool for power system stability analysis, still does not fully describe the voltage dynamic response of grid-forming energy storage when constructing the energy function. To address these issues, this paper comprehensively considers the dynamic characteristics of the reactive power control loop of grid-forming energy storage, derives an improved Lyapunov energy function considering voltage dynamic changes, thereby improving the accuracy of transient stability judgment. Meanwhile, a global stability damping control strategy based on the second stable equilibrium point is proposed.By analyzing the correlation between the upper limit of frequency variation and virtual damping, it is pointed out that there exists a minimum damping such that the phase trajectory does not exceed the second unstable equilibrium point.This control strategy enables the system to recover stability within the region of attraction corresponding to the second stable equilibrium point under severe post-fault conditions, and improves the transient stability margin of the power grid under large disturbances. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Optimal dispatch strategy for V2G-enabled community microgrids considering uncertain electricity price
abstract: To address the untapped dispatch potential of electric vehicles (EVs), the high complexity of multi-resource coordination, and the volatility of electricity prices, this paper proposes a robust optimal scheduling strategy for EV-integrated community microgrids considering price uncertainty. Specifically, a discharge margin coefficient is introduced to assess the discharging capability of EVs, classifying EVs into two categories based on their parking characteristics. Based on this classification, a differentiated scheduling mechanism is designed. For EV1, a price-based demand response program guides its charging/discharging behavior, while a dynamic charging/discharging subsidy mechanism with SOC-dependent modulation is developed for EV2. Meanwhile, to address the impact of price volatility on the economic operation of the microgrid, a bilateral decoupled trading strategy based on preset price benchmarks is formulated and combined with a robust optimization method to achieve coordinated scheduling under uncertain price environments. In this study, three coordinated scheduling schemes with varying combinations of flexible resources are comparatively evaluated under worst-case price fluctuation scenarios. Simulation results indicate the feasibility and robustness of the proposed multi-resource coordinated strategy and show improved economic performance under the tested scenarios. Furthermore, the differentiated EV scheduling strategy helps facilitate peak shaving and valley filling while improving the local accommodation of renewable energy. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A physics-informed multi-source signal fusion method for excitation transformer fault diagnosis
abstract: Excitation transformers are key components of generator excitation systems in power plants and operate under heavy loads, strong electromagnetic interference, and coupled thermal-mechanical stresses, making reliable diagnosis of mechanical loosening, partial discharge, and DC bias faults challenging. To overcome the limitations of conventional single-signal methods in noisy and non-stationary environments, this paper proposes a physics-informed multi-source signal fusion method for excitation transformer fault diagnosis, termed EM-APMSF. The proposed method integrates enhanced Mel-frequency cepstral coefficient features, temperature information, and mechanism-guided relevance information within a unified diagnostic framework. A weighting strategy combining mechanism-guided relevance and entropy-based confidence is introduced to coordinate the relative contributions of acoustic and temperature features during cross-modal fusion. The method was validated using field monitoring data and historical fault records from excitation transformers in a power plant. Comparative and ablation results show that EM-APMSF achieves a diagnostic accuracy of over 95% with an average F1-score of 0.954, outperforming conventional methods by >8% in accuracy. These results support the feasibility of EM-APMSF as an effective framework for excitation-transformer condition monitoring and fault diagnosis under the field conditions represented in the current dataset. © 2026

title: SISO equivalent impedance modeling with mirror frequency effect and mitigation of sub-synchronous resonance for single-phase grid-forming converters
abstract: Grid-forming converters have gradually become critical equipment for supporting modern power systems. With the rapid development of distributed generation, single-phase grid-forming converters (SGFMCs) have attracted extensive attention. However, SGFMCs face the challenge of impedance modeling, which affects the stability analysis and controller design. This paper investigates the impedance modeling, interaction mechanisms, and sub-synchronous resonance (SSR) mitigation methods. Regarding the impedance modeling, SGFMCs have more complex internal relationships than three-phase grid-forming converters owning to their orthogonal signal generation unit. Existing impedance models for double-power loops SGFMCs rarely account for the mirror frequency effect (MFE), resulting in inaccurate impedance characterization. To fill this research gap, this paper adopts the harmonic linearization method to derive two single-input single-output impedance models that fully capture the MFE for two typical SGFMCs. Furthermore, the interaction mechanism between SGFMCs and grid is explicitly elucidated. Analytical results demonstrate that both SGFMCs are susceptible to SSR under strong grid conditions. To improve the system stability, an impedance shaping method is proposed to mitigate SSR for SGFMCs under strong grid conditions. Finally, experimental results verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: An embedded uncertainty quantification architecture for fuel cell degradation prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction and credible reliability evaluation of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFC) performance degradation are critical for ensuring the safe and reliable operation of their integrated energy system. To address the limitations of existing methods, which often employ tightly coupled architectures with poor flexibility and inadequate uncertainty quantification, this study proposes an Embedded Uncertainty-quantification Architecture (EUA). With a modular design, the EUA serves as a plug-and-play module that can be integrated into deep learning time-series models (as baselines) without structural modifications, thereby enhancing local feature extraction and enabling uncertainty quantification. Specifically, the front end of the EUA incorporates a Multi-scale Temporal Convolutional Network (MSTCN) module to extract multi-granularity local features, while the back end employs a Sparse Gaussian Process Regression (SGPR) module to perform efficient probabilistic modeling of the baseline model outputs, thereby generating well-calibrated predictive confidence intervals. An experimental assessment of dynamic PEMFC datasets demonstrated that integrating the EUA with various baseline models not only significantly improved point prediction accuracy (reducing the RMSE by 28 %-49 %) but also provided reliable and tight confidence intervals. The strong generalization and robustness of the EUA were further validated through experiments under multiple load conditions, cross-condition scenarios, and unseen noisy environments. This study provides a plug-and-play prediction framework with built-in uncertainty quantification for PEMFC health management, effectively bridging the uncertainty quantification gap inherent in high-performance point prediction models. © 2026

title: Voltage sag support strategy based on cooperative optimization control of photovoltaic inverter currents
abstract: Conventional local Low Voltage Ride-Through (LVRT) strategies for photovoltaic (PV) inverters in high-penetration distribution networks lack global coordination and struggle to balance optimal voltage support with real-time responsiveness. To address this, a voltage sag support strategy based on cooperative PV inverter current control is proposed. First, a multi-inverter cooperative voltage-sag support model is established using the nodal impedance matrix and the superposition theorem, quantifying the cross-node voltage-support potential enabled by mutual impedance coupling. Second, targeted global optimization models are developed for symmetrical and asymmetrical faults, aiming to maximize positive-sequence voltage recovery and coordinate positive- and negative-sequence suppression, respectively, to achieve system-level optimal voltage support. Finally, to overcome the computational latency of online optimization, a Deep Neural Network (DNN)-based quasi-static control strategy is proposed. By learning the mapping between grid states and optimal current setpoints offline, this strategy ensures real-time cooperative voltage-sag support while retaining near-optimal performance. Simulations on a 6-node feeder and the IEEE 33-bus system demonstrate that the proposed strategy increases the minimum residual voltage by up to 10.84% under symmetrical faults, while the quasi-static strategy compresses control delays from 106.34 ms to 4.85 ms, providing an effective, hardware-free solution for voltage sag support. © 2026

title: Research on Bi-level cooperative optimization algorithm of wind turbine layout and cable topology in floating offshore wind farm
abstract: A bi-level cooperative optimization strategy is proposed in order to optimize the location layout of floating offshore wind turbines(FOWT) and the topology of cable path, while considering the system's power generation efficiency and investment costs in this paper. The framework dynamically couples turbine siting and cable routing through iterative feedback, enabling the two subsystems to co-evolve toward a global optimum. Its upper level model constructs a 3D engineering wake model of FOWT considering pitch and surge motions to quantify wake effect, and utilizes the improved Whale Algorithm to optimize the layout of wind turbines, aiming to maximize total power output. While its lower level model targets to minimize the Levelized Cost of Energy(LCOE) over the entire life cycle, which employs the DBSCAN clustering algorithm to partition the wind turbine clusters and optimize the cable path through a Ring Topology-based Multiple Traveling Salesmen Problem(RT-MTSP). A classic 25 km × 25 km offshore wind farm is taken as a case study to verify the correctness and feasibility of the proposed model. Results show that the optimal number of wind turbines is 150, which achieves the best economic performance. Under the proposed collaborative optimization framework, the GA algorithm achieves the lowest LCOE value(0.311451 kW*h) with 23.85% reduction, which exhibits better stability compared with SA and PSO. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Two-level stochastic programming for optimal operation of wind-thermal-hydropower systems in day-ahead and balancing markets
abstract: Renewable-rich power systems require flexible scheduling strategies that can coordinate energy, reserve, and storage operation under uncertainty. This study develops a two-level stochastic scheduling framework for a wind–thermal–hydropower–pumped-storage system operating in day-ahead and balancing markets. The framework links day-ahead commitments with scenario-dependent balancing actions to manage uncertainty in wind power, load demand, and hydrological inflow. An initial set of 100 uncertainty scenarios is generated and reduced to 10 representative scenarios, achieving a 90% reduction in scenario count while preserving the system's main stochastic characteristics. The model is validated on a modified IEEE 14-bus system integrating 145 MW of wind generation, 150 MW of thermal generation, a 30 MW hydropower unit, and a 30 MW pumped-storage unit. The optimized daily operating cost is $22,104.52, demonstrating that coordinated hydropower and pumped-storage operation can support renewable integration while maintaining system reliability. Comparative optimization results show that Harris Hawks Optimization achieves a lower best objective value than Particle Swarm Optimization, Genetic Algorithm, and Grey Wolf Optimizer, with improvements of 1.39%, 2.58%, and 1.14%, respectively. Sensitivity analyses further show that reducing thermal ramping capability increases the operating cost to $23,542.49; increasing minimum up- and down-time limits raises it to $23,724.91; and reducing transmission capacity raises it to $24,263.91. These results confirm that hydro-storage flexibility, transmission availability, and thermal-unit responsiveness are key factors in reducing balancing pressure and improving the economic performance of renewable-integrated power systems. © 2026

title: Cross-month reliability-oriented capacity planning and grid integration validation of battery-hydrogen hybrid storage for a PV microgrid
abstract: Grid-connected photovoltaic microgrids face intraday power fluctuations and cross-month source-load mismatch. Long-duration supply risk becomes more pronounced, especially when low winter irradiance coincides with high load demand. This paper proposes a cross-month reliability-oriented capacity planning and grid-integration validation method for battery-hydrogen hybrid storage. The planning stage uses the point of common coupling as the exchange boundary with the external distribution network and formulates a two-stage risk-averse mixed-integer linear programming model for 12 monthly representative days, 24 hourly time steps, and seven seasonal risk scenarios. The model considers mutually exclusive operating states, expected and scenario-level energy-not-served constraints, a low-hydrogen security margin, conditional value-at-risk, and a battery-degradation model segmented by depth of discharge. After capacity planning, the fixed capacity is validated through an 8760 h operational simulation and mapped to the IEEE 33-bus system for LinDistFlow post-checking, network-constrained correction, and sensitivity analysis across multiple connection schemes. The selected capacity achieves a probability-weighted expected energy not served of 0.646 MWh/a in the 8760 h validation. Additional robustness checks show that the selected capacity remains within the reliability limit under scenario-weight perturbations and tested cloudy-window stresses. The network correction results further show that energy adequacy at the point of common coupling and feeder-level voltage feasibility are interconnected but distinct assessment layers. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Enhanced loss of circulation prediction using Sea Lion-optimized machine learning models
abstract: Lost circulation is a major drilling challenge that increases cost and non-productive time and is influenced by different parameters. This study develops and evaluates machine learning models for predicting lost circulation severity during drilling operations. Three machine learning algorithms, Decision Tree, K-Nearest Neighbors (K-NN), and Random Forest, were optimized using the Sea Lion Optimization algorithm to enhance prediction accuracy. Feature importance analysis identified azimuth as the most significant predictor, followed by measure depth, average bit RPM, hook load, and torque, indicating that directional and mechanical drilling parameters outweigh mud properties and formation data in predicting fluid loss. Correlation analysis further confirmed strong relationships among these key parameters. The results indicate that azimuth and depth have a stronger correlation with the target parameters. All optimized models demonstrated good performance in classifying fluid loss severity. The Random Forest model achieved the best performance among the evaluated models. The K-NN and Decision Tree models also showed strong performance. Confusion matrix analysis validated all models' capability to reliably distinguish between different fluid loss severity categories (Seepage, Partial, Severe, and Total Loss) on both training and testing datasets. The findings of this study can help to provide an effective approach for predicting lost circulation severity, offering potential for reducing non-productive time, cost, and improving drilling safety. © 2026 The Authors. title: Prescribed-Time voltage synchronization and reactive power sharing for multi-agent AC microgrids with time-varying cooperative gains
abstract: Although voltage synchronization and reactive power sharing in AC microgrids have been extensively investigated, nonlinear Q-V coupling and mismatched feeder impedances can still induce power sharing imbalances. Fixed-gain droop control exhibits difficulties in simultaneously balancing transient response and steady-state accuracy, whereas conventional finite-time control may be sensitive to initial voltage deviations. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-agent prescribed-time control strategy for voltage synchronization and reactive power sharing in AC microgrids, incorporating nonlinear coupling and time-varying cooperative characteristics. Firstly, a DG state-space model is transformed into a linear canonical form via feedback linearization, which provides a tractable basis for coordinated voltage regulation under nonlinear Q-V coupling. A capacity weighted virtual impedance compensation is incorporated into the voltage consensus variable to enhance capacity based reactive power sharing under nonidentical feeder impedances. Meanwhile, a piecewise-smooth time-varying cooperative gain is designed to improve the initial disturbance response while moderating the control effort. Secondly, a time scale transformation converts the prescribed-time convergence objective into an asymptotic stabilization problem, and Lyapunov analysis is used to establish prescribed-time convergence under the stated assumptions. Finally, MATLAB/Simulink simulations are conducted under load disturbances, reactive load steps, DG plug-and-play events, unequal capacity conditions, practical parameter perturbations, measurement noise, and fixed communication delays. Comparative and sensitivity results with conventional droop control, fixed-gain consensus control, and fixed-time secondary control indicate improved voltage recovery, reduced reactive power sharing error, and finite virtual-input magnitude within the tested operating range. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: CFD analysis of thermophysical characterization & performance optimization of a solar updraft tower utilising multi-composition gas mixtures
abstract: The thermophysical behaviour of the solar working fluid plays an important role on the performance of the solar chimney. This work presents the results of a systematic Reynolds-averaged computational fluid dynamics (CFD) study, with turbulence closed by the shear-stress-transport (SST) k–ω model, of the buoyancy-driven flow in an axisymmetric solar chimney with six industrially relevant binary gas mixtures namely Air–CO, Air–CO2, CO–CO2, CO2–SO2, Air–SO2 and CO–SO2. Uniform wall heat flux of 1000 W/m2 is applied and mole fractions are taken between 0 and 1 with an interval of 0.1, and inlet temperatures are taken between 300K and 900K which results in a total of 462 simulations performed in ANSYS Fluent 2023 R1. The specific heat (Cp), density (ρ), thermal conductivity (k) and dynamic viscosity (μ) are obtained directly from the ANSYS Fluent property database and depend on the composition and temperature. Eight performance measures are reported: Pr, Nu, Re, Gr, Ra, draft pressure ΔP, mass flux G, and a conductivity-bias-corrected Thermal Performance Index TPI = Nu/Pr1/3. Two salient trends found in the data during analysis and retained unchanged in the results are worth noting: the non-physical decrease of Cp with inlet temperature for several pure-component points, and the molar-mass label anomaly in the CO2–SO2 sheet, which raises the value of Pr toward unity at 300 K. The highest centre-line velocity (60.1 m s−1 at 900 K) is reached for the air–CO mixtures while the SO2-rich mixtures produce up to 45 % higher ΔP at 300 K. This pressure gain is overcome at higher temperatures (≈650 K), where the effect of the greater temperature rise of Air–CO outweighs its lower density. The apparent Nu superiority of SO2 systems is shown to be a low-k normalisation artefact. The results are used for quantitative working fluid selection guidelines for industrial solar chimney, passive ventilation systems and flue gas stacks. © 2026 The Authors. title: From centralized monitoring to cooperative aerial intelligence: A MARL–FANET approach for smart microgrid monitoring and defect analysis
abstract: A key requirement of smart microgrids is the need for rapid and reliable monitoring that adapts to changing circumstances to ensure system stability, security, and efficiency. Traditional monitoring techniques using fixed sensor networks and centralized supervision methods can face issues such as low spatiotemporal density, slow response times to faults, and susceptibility to single point failures. To overcome these drawbacks, a UAV-based cooperative monitoring technique for inspection and defect detection of smart microgrids is presented in this paper. These UAVs act like a Flying Ad Hoc Network (FANET), which helps share local observations with each other. A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) algorithm, which includes centralised training with decentralised execution, is used for cooperative monitoring. Defect detection is achieved by using a multimodal input of various modalities for each individual UAV. The proposed framework is evaluated in a simulation environment involving representative smart microgrid assets, including transmission lines, photovoltaic panels, and transformers. Experimental results demonstrate an average fault detection accuracy of 95.3%, an average detection latency of 7.9 s, and an average UAV energy consumption of 14.2 Wh while maintaining 91.4% coverage efficiency. In addition, the FANET communication network achieves a packet delivery ratio of 97.6% with an average communication latency of 112 ms. To ensure fair performance evaluation, the proposed MARL–FANET framework is compared against multiple baseline approaches, including fixed sensor-based monitoring systems, centralized UAV coordination, and non-cooperative UAV deployment strategies. This comparative evaluation provides a consistent benchmark for assessing improvements in detection accuracy, latency reduction, and energy efficiency achieved through cooperative multi-agent learning and decentralized execution. The results indicate that cooperative UAV-based monitoring can significantly enhance microgrid situational awareness, distributed fault response capability, and operational resilience. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Power quality–driven electromagnetic risk amplification in co-located critical energy infrastructures
abstract: The increasing integration of power electronic converters, renewable energy interfaces, and nonlinear industrial loads has significantly degraded power quality in modern transmission networks, leading to elevated total harmonic distortion (THD) and reduced power factor (PF). While the impact of these phenomena on energy efficiency is well documented, their influence on electromagnetic interference (EMI) and AC-induced corrosion of co-located buried pipelines remains insufficiently quantified. This study investigates the coupled effects of power quality degradation on electromagnetic induction and corrosion risk in shared transmission line–pipeline corridors. A multi-frequency extension of the classical Carson–Clem formulation is developed to incorporate harmonic-specific current spectra and frequency-dependent mutual impedance. The induced current density at pipeline coating defects is evaluated for THD levels ranging from 0% to 20% and for PF variations between 0.8 and 0.99. To account for electrochemical behavior, a frequency-dependent corrosion efficiency model is integrated, enabling computation of an effective corrosion-driving current density. Results demonstrate that power quality degradation amplifies corrosion risk through two concurrent mechanisms: (i) reduction of THD leading to increased RMS current and enhanced electromagnetic coupling, and (ii) harmonic redistribution of spectral components that modifies corrosion efficiency at the steel–soil interface. Low-order harmonics are found to dominate corrosion risk, and conventional fundamental-frequency assessments may significantly underestimate the spatial extent of corrosion-critical zones under harmonic-rich conditions. The proposed framework establishes a direct link between power quality metrics and infrastructure integrity, providing a quantitative basis for incorporating harmonic considerations into pipeline interference assessment and critical energy infrastructure protection strategies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Current amplitude and phase-based adaptive differential protection for distribution networks with unmeasured T-taps
abstract: The integration of distributed energy resources via T-taps introduces strong source-load fluctuations that often cause maloperations in conventional two-terminal current differential protection. To address this issue, this paper proposes an adaptive current differential protection scheme utilizing inverse amplitude cross-restraint and phase angle adaptation. An inverse cross-restraint mechanism based on two-terminal current amplitude ratios is introduced to prevent maloperations from internal T-tap fluctuations. Meanwhile, a phase-angle-evolution algorithm rapidly reduces restraint quantities during internal faults, and phase-to-phase differential characteristics are incorporated to further enhance sensitivity to single-phase short-circuits. Simulations confirm reliable operation under heavy T-tap loading, inverter-based resource integrations with diverse control strategies, and single-phase faults at the hundred-ohm level. The proposed method requires no additional voltage-measurement hardware effectively mitigates unmeasured T-tap interference and improves protection sensitivity in active distribution networks. © 2026

title: SPMask: Sparse convolution-based 3D instance segmentation network for key targets in overhead transmission line scenes
abstract: Accurately identifying key targets such as transmission lines (TLs) and Towers in overhead transmission line scenes from point cloud data is a critical task in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based power inspection. However, existing methods perform poorly at identifying TLs and Towers from large-scale power inspection scenes. This paper introduces SPMask, a Sparse Convolution-based 3D Instance Segmentation Network designed to identify individual TLs and Towers. Firstly, the Sparse Convolution Feature Chain Extraction Module (SPC) is designed to enhance the ability of the network to extract features from power inspection scenes. Then the Instance Mask Direct Generation Module (Qmask module) is designed to achieve point-level instance prediction, endowing the network with strong robustness. Finally, we validate SPMask using the Power Inspection Dataset (PID) collected via small UAV-mounted LiDAR and the large-scale outdoor public dataset STPLS3D. The results demonstrate that compared to several existing methods, SPMask performs the best on the PID, with an AP of 93.6% for Towers and an AP of 98.3% for TLs. Additionally, SPMask sets a new state-of-the-art on the STPLS3D validation set, with gains of +2.6 AP, +2.9 AP50, and +3.0 AP25. Moreover, through ablation experiments, we further demonstrate the effectiveness of the SPC and Qmask for instance segmentation in PID. © 2026

title: Structural and causal knowledge-guided defect detection for transmission-line suspension clamps and anti-vibration dampers
abstract: To address small inter-class differences, large intra-class variations, and co-occurring defects in UAV inspection images of transmission-line suspension clamps and anti-vibration dampers, this paper proposes a defect detection framework guided by structural and causal knowledge. The framework features three core components. First, a Structural Knowledge Module (SKM) combines deformable convolution and symmetry-aware feature modeling to enhance structure-sensitive feature representation of geometric variations and structural anomalies. Second, a Causal Knowledge Loss (CKL) incorporates a causal matrix constructed from fitting-instance-level defect co-occurrence statistics into the classification loss. Third, an Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) mechanism performs channel-wise feature recalibration to emphasize defect-related features and suppress background interference. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves the highest detection accuracy among the compared detectors, with an mAP50 of 81.7%, representing a 6.0-percentage-point improvement over the YOLOv11 baseline. The model contains 10.8M parameters, has a computational complexity of 37.2 GFLOPs, and achieves an inference speed of 73.1 FPS. These results indicate that the proposed framework achieves a favorable balance between detection accuracy and inference efficiency for suspension-clamp and anti-vibration-damper defect detection. © 2026

title: Economic optimization dispatch of microgrids based on finite-time dynamic event-triggered algorithms
abstract: To alleviate the excessive communication burden in economic dispatch (ED) of microgrids and the lack of convergence rate guarantees in existing event-triggered control (ETC), a finite-time dynamic event-triggered algorithm is proposed. This algorithm is constructed by integrating dynamic event-triggered control (DETC) with a finite-time consensus algorithm. A triggering condition embedding internal dynamic variables is established, and information exchange among distributed units is executed exclusively when the event-triggered conditions are satisfied. This approach achieves power balance between supply and demand in microgrids at the lowest cost and reduces communication overhead, while ensuring system stability. The stability of the algorithm is verified via the Lyapunov stability theorem, and thus, the avoidance of Zeno behavior is guaranteed. Simulations conducted in the MATLAB environment verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Data-Driven harmonic forecasting in wave energy conversion systems using machine and deep learning
abstract: This study proposes a data-driven harmonic forecasting framework for a power take-off (PTO) and permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) based wave energy conversion system (WECS). A detailed Simulink model represents the end-to-end wave-to-electrical chain, including PTO conversion, generator-side power conversion, grid interfacing, and harmonic monitoring at the 575 V bus. The dataset is constructed from real NOAA/NDBC station 46042 metocean records spanning 2020–2023. After quality filtering (203,380 raw observations reduced to 38,744 valid records) and Simulink-based simulation with transient removal, the final learning-ready dataset contains 8,751 synchronized wave–electrical snapshots. Wave, wind, and electrical state variables are used as multivariate predictors, and voltage total harmonic distortion (THDV) at the 575 V bus is forecast one step ahead. The benchmark includes Random Forest and XGBoost as machine-learning baselines, together with LSTM, GRU, and a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) as sequence-based deep-learning models. Performance is evaluated using RMSE, MAE, normalized RMSE (nRMSE), and R2, with additional trajectory and residual analyses. Over the available Q4 2023 evaluation window ending on 2023-11-25, GRU achieves the best performance, with nRMSE = 11.99% and R2 = 0.611. LSTM follows closely, GRU slightly outperforms the naive persistence baseline, and both recurrent models outperform the tree-based baselines and TCN. The framework supports proactive harmonic supervision for offshore and subsea-connected WECS architectures. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: OptiRT-DETR: A lightweight transformer-based framework for real-time insulator defect detection in power transmission systems
abstract: Insulator defect detection is a critical task in ensuring the safety and stability of power transmission systems. However, existing methods often suffer from high computational complexity and limited robustness under complex environmental conditions, particularly for small and ambiguous defects. To address these challenges, this paper proposes OptiRT-DETR, a lightweight Transformer-based detection framework. The model integrates a ConvNeXtV2 backbone for efficient feature extraction, an enhanced adaptive sparse Transformer encoder for global context modeling, a multi-scale feature fusion network for robust representation, and a quality-aware dynamic sample assignment loss to improve optimization stability. These components are jointly designed to balance detection accuracy and computational efficiency. Extensive experiments on three insulator defect detection datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance while significantly reducing model complexity. Specifically, OptiRT-DETR achieves up to 0.988 mAP@0.5, with only 14.45M parameters and 28.4 GFLOPs. In addition, ONNX-based inference evaluation shows that the model reaches 132.94 FPS on GPU with approximately 70 × acceleration compared with CPU execution, demonstrating strong real-time inference capability and deployment feasibility. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Controller hardware-in-the-loop (C-HIL) testing of a hybrid control architecture for multi-feeder microgrids with heterogeneous generation
abstract: This paper designs and validates a control architecture for multi-feeder heterogeneous microgrids that supports seamless transitions across various topologically distinct modes. The validation process is carried out in a controller hardware-in-the-loop (C-HIL) testbed that integrates a real-time high-fidelity emulation of the microgrid power generation assets, the network, and the loads, and commercially available industrial-grade control hardware to implement the suite of controls. As the test system, we adopt the Banshee system, which is a radial three-feeder microgrid comprising heterogeneous resources including two synchronous generators (SGs), a grid following (GFL) inverter and a droop-based grid forming (GFM) inverter. The control architecture is hybrid in the sense that it implements both logic controls and continuous controls. The continuous controls ensure stability is maintained and include tie-line power controls, synchronization controls, secondary frequency control, and secondary voltage control, while the logic controls facilitate topology (mode) changes by opening and closing circuit breakers. Specifically, the logic controls enable: feeder islanding and re-connection, networking of multiple microgrids, and backfeeding power to islanded feeders through other grid-connected feeders for the 38 modes of the Banshee system. © 2026 The Authors

title: Non-iterative coordinated robust scheduling method for virtual power plant-distribution network system based on feasible region projection
abstract: To address the problems of low computational efficiency and high complexity of information exchange in the iterative solution methods for collaborative scheduling between virtual power plants (VPPs) and the distribution network (DN), this study proposes a non-iterative cooperative robust optimal scheduling strategy for VPP and the DN based on equivalent projection feasible region (EPFR). First, a two-layer collaborative scheduling framework for VPP and DN based on EPFR is constructed. Combined with two types of market clearing strategies, namely the DN price quota curve and the VPP distribution locational marginal price (DLMP), scheduling models for the DN and VPP are established respectively. Then, the improved Fourier-Motzkin elimination (IFME) method is proposed to compute the EPFR of the VPP, under the premise that the internal devices within VPPs are linearly modeled. On this basis, the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence is employed to construct the probabilistic set of scenarios for source-load uncertainty, and a collaborative robust optimal scheduling model for VPP and DN is constructed, which is resolved via the column and constraint generation (C&CG) algorithm. Finally, case simulations are performed on the modified 52-bus-based and 123-bus-based distribution systems so as to validate the effectiveness of the non-iterative collaborative robust scheduling strategy between VPP and DN. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
label: Science (including Engineering)

title: Lightning impulse discharge characteristics and insulation coordination failure mechanisms of insulator strings and surge arresters on distribution lines under wet pollution conditions
abstract: Based on-site investigations of 35 kV transmission lines in Kumishi Town, 1080 artificial lightning pollution flashover tests were conducted on commonly used insulator strings and surge arresters. By evaluating the insulation coordination margin and observing the entire arc development process were analyzed in depth through statistical analysis of the flashover probability of the insulation sections. The results show that under low contamination conditions, when the discharge path remains the grading ring air gap, the lightning pollution flashover voltage of the surge arrester remains nearly unchanged but increases approximately linearly with the gap distance. The lightning pollution flashover voltage of the insulation sections of insulator strings and surge arresters decreases following a negative power exponential relationship as the ESDD increases. The arc development velocity of the insulation sections of insulator strings and surge arresters is positively correlated with ESDD. The arc development velocity of the gap section can reach 52.5 mm/μs, while that of the insulation section of surge arresters is only 31.9 mm/μs, representing a decrease of 39.23%, which hinders the fast operation of surge arresters. The flashover probability of the insulation section shows a positive correlation with both gap distance and ESDD, and a negative correlation with lightning amplitude. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Wind–photovoltaic joint power modeling based on a two-stage optimal selection of marginal distributions and dependence structure
abstract: To address uncertainty challenges caused by high renewable energy penetration, generating joint distribution scenarios that accurately reflect the dependence structure of wind–PV joint output is essential for planning and operating modern power systems with high renewable penetration. Traditional methods often rely on fixed distributional assumptions, limiting their adaptability to different data characteristics. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a wind–PV joint output scenario generation method based on an integrated two-stage adaptive marginal distribution and dependence structure selection and validation framework. First, root mean square error, Kullback–Leibler divergence, Jensen–Shannon divergence, and Wasserstein distance are used as evaluation criteria to adaptively select marginal distributions with the best goodness of fit to historical wind and photovoltaic power output data. Second, log-likelihood, Akaike information criterion, and Bayesian information criterion are used as evaluation criteria to select the Copula function that best captures the dependence structure and tail dependence of historical wind–PV joint output. Finally, we develop a scenario quality evaluation framework including Kendall's tau coefficient, Spearman's rho coefficient, tail dependence coefficients, and energy distance. Time-block cross-validation and mean-rank-based comprehensive ranking are introduced to verify the effectiveness and stability of the two-stage selection and validation results. A case study using measured wind and photovoltaic power output data from Henan Province shows that the selected combination outperforms other candidates in accurately reproducing dependence and tail joint-output characteristics. The generated scenarios reproduce the 24-h hourly mean output profiles and cover seasonal fluctuation scenarios and high- and low-output wind–PV scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: System frequency response modeling and frequency control parameters tuning for hybrid wind generation integrating GFL and GFM doubly-fed wind turbines
abstract: Transforming existing grid-following (GFL) doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) wind farms into grid-forming (GFM) DFIG ones is essential for enhancing system frequency support. Studying frequency response and parameters tuning in hybrid wind farms with both unit types establishes a foundation for frequency control. Frequency response modeling for GFL units is well established, small-signal models of GFM DFIG units fail to capture frequency-active power dynamics due to multi-variable coupling, hindering unified hybrid wind farm modeling. Furthermore, frequency control parameters tuning relies on inefficient trial-and-error methods. These defects limit the application of hybrid wind farms. This paper proposes a comprehensive frequency response model for hybrid wind farms and an efficient parameter tuning method. By analyzing the frequency support process in GFM DFIG turbines, a frequency-active power response model is derived. Considering system inertia sources, wind farm outputs are transformed and aggregated to build a system frequency response model that includes hybrid DFIG wind farms. A multi-objective function based on this model integrates the maximum frequency variation rate, deviation, and steady-state deviation. The improved genetic particle swarm optimization (GPSO) algorithm is applied for parameters tuning under generator output and stability constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed model accurately captures frequency and turbine output dynamics, and the tuning method improves system frequency response and stability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Research on the superhydrophobic surface of silicone rubber induced by femtosecond laser
abstract: Superhydrophobic surfaces have become an important research area for enhancing material surface performance due to their excellent water-repellency and self-cleaning properties. In this work, we propose a method to fabricate superhydrophobic silicone rubber surfaces by femtosecond laser-induced micro-nano hierarchical structures. The effects of laser fluence, scanning speed and filling spacing on the surface morphology and wetting performance were systematically studied. Through single-factor experiments, a superhydrophobic surface with a contact angle of 157.7° and a rolling angle of 4.6° was prepared under the conditions of a fluence of 26 J·cm−2, a scanning speed of 50 mm·s−1, and a filling spacing of 15 μm. Scanning electron microscopy analysis indicated that the superhydrophobicity originated from the micro-nano hierarchical structures induced by the laser, which effectively promoted the droplets to maintain the Cassie-Baxter wetting state. Energy spectrum analysis further revealed that the main elemental compositions remained largely unchanged after laser treatment, while XPS analysis indicated the cleavage of C–Si bonds and the formation of non‑polar C–C(H) bonds, which are beneficial for surface hydrophobicity. Combined with the changes in the microscopic morphology, it indicates that the improvement in surface wettability is mainly attributed to the change in morphology. In addition, droplet impact tests showed that the superhydrophobic surface induced by laser could make the droplets rebound rapidly and completely detach, with a contact time of only about 13 ms. © 2026

title: Physics-enhanced dynamic graph network for wind power forecasting with directional delays and aerodynamic interference
abstract: Multi-turbine wind power forecasting is challenging because of the complex, time-varying aerodynamic interactions among turbines. Existing graph-based methods introduce physical knowledge but treat these interactions as instantaneous, ignoring the finite time required for wind to propagate across a farm. To address this gap, we propose DPGNet, a physics-enhanced dynamic graph network that explicitly models directional propagation delays and wake-induced aerodynamic interactions. At each time step, the optimal inter-turbine delay is identified by maximizing the Maximal Information Coefficient (MIC), and a dynamic directed graph is constructed whose edge weights learnably combine spatial distance, MIC-based dependence, and Gaussian-wake aerodynamic coupling; a delay-aware spatio-temporal network then learns turbine dependencies for multi-step forecasting. On real wind farm data over a 1–10 h horizon, DPGNet reduces the average Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by about 9% over the strongest physics-enhanced baseline, and under 30% missing data its MAE increases only from about 243 to 248 kW, confirming its robustness and generalizability. © 2026

title: Localization challenges and technological gaps in cleaning robots for fixed-tilt coplanar photovoltaic arrays: A review and perspective
abstract: Accurate and reliable localization is crucial for autonomous mobile robots performing cleaning operations on coplanar photovoltaic arrays at fixed tilt angles, where smooth glass surfaces, repetitive textures, and narrow passageways frequently degrade localization accuracy. This paper provides a structured review of localization strategies relevant to photovoltaic panel cleaning. It establishes the fundamentals of ground robot localization and reviews both conventional and AI-enhanced techniques, from odometry and global positioning to deep visual perception and learning-based state estimation. The operational, environmental, perceptual, and computational constraints specific to coplanar photovoltaic arrays are analysed, together with the localization strategies adopted in existing photovoltaic cleaning robots. The review finds that current systems rely almost exclusively on short-range relative localization and lack mechanisms for globally consistent positioning across multi-row cleaning runs. Closing this gap will require localization architectures that bound drift through external geometric references and adapt to slip and illumination variation through learning-based estimation, with active tracking of passive landmarks via pan–tilt–zoom cameras combined with AI-enhanced sensor fusion offering one promising direction. © 2026 The Authors. title: A parallel ensemble framework with multiscale convolution and validation-optimized weighting for wind power forecasting
abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting remains difficult because wind-related variables are nonlinear, non-stationary, and strongly multi-scale. To address this problem, this paper proposes a parallel ensemble framework that combines multiscale feature extraction with validation-optimized output fusion. A refined Tetragonula carbonaria optimization algorithm (RTGCOA) is firstly developed for feature selection and parameter optimization. Using a random forest (RF) based importance analysis, four dominant meteorological variables are retained: 30 m, 50 m, 70 m and hub-height wind speed. Secondly, a multiscale feature fusion convolution module (MSFCM) is designed to capture temporal patterns at different resolutions from the historical power series. Then, an improved bidirectional long short-term memory network (IBiLSTM) with coupled input-forget gates, peephole connections, and gated residual links is run in parallel with an enhanced Patch-based time series transformer (EPatchTST) that incorporates adaptive patch division and a hybrid enhanced attention mechanism. Finally, an RTGCOA-based validation-optimized ensemble strategy is introduced to determine the optimal global weights of the two branches, thereby improving overall forecasting robustness. Experiments conducted on real-world wind farm datasets covering different seasonal and perturbation conditions demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms the comparison models in terms of forecasting accuracy and error stability, confirming the effectiveness of the coordinated multiscale representation, heterogeneous parallel prediction, and validation-optimized output fusion. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Voltage stability in a high renewable distribution system via safety-guided deep reinforcement learning and MACPO
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources within distribution networks necessitates sophisticated coordinated Volt-VAR Control (VVC). This paper presents a safe multi-agent reinforcement learning framework grounded in Multi-Agent Constrained Policy Optimization (MACPO). The proposed methodology employs a centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE) paradigm, integrating a voltage-barrier reward mechanism and a projection-based safety layer utilizing a Straight-Through Estimator (STE). Validated on a modified IEEE 33-bus system equipped with photovoltaic installations and battery energy storage, the MACPO framework effectively maintains voltage profiles within the 0.95–1.05 p.u. range while simultaneously minimizing reactive power losses. Ablation studies demonstrate that the framework exhibits robustness toward parameter variations and different gradient estimation techniques. Although the offline training phase is computationally demanding, the online execution time is in the sub-millisecond range, thereby facilitating decentralized control applications. Future research will focus on extending this framework to larger-scale power systems. © 2026

title: Adaptive physics-constrained ultra-short-term photovoltaic power forecasting based on deep spatio-temporal fusion of multimodal data
abstract: With the increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) generation, ultra-short-term power forecasting is crucial for grid dispatch and renewable energy integration. However, the high uncertainty of cloud motion makes conventional data-driven methods with single-source inputs and limited spatio-temporal modeling inadequate for minute-level prediction. This paper proposes a multimodal fusion model with adaptive physical constraints for ultra-short-term PV power forecasting. The model employs a Vision Transformer (ViT) to extract spatial features from ground-based all-sky images, a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) to capture multi-scale temporal dependencies in historical power, and the Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms (RAFT) optical flow algorithm to compute optical flow between two adjacent cloud frames for extracting motion features; a cross-attention module achieves deep fusion of the three modalities. Based on the optical flow field, divergence, acceleration, and boundary constraints are embedded into the loss function, and their weights are adaptively adjusted according to cloud physical indicators, dynamically balancing numerical accuracy and physical consistency. Experiments on a public dataset show that, compared with the best dual-modality model, the proposed method reduces MAE, RMSE, and MAPE by 56.8%, 63.4%, and 30.4%, respectively; relative to models without physical constraints, the reductions are 47.9%, 54.9%, and 22.1%. The framework significantly improves forecasting accuracy, while reducing dependence on large historical datasets and enhancing adherence to physical laws. © 2026

title: Bioinspired lightweight para-aramid/SiO2 aerogel thermal insulation materials for firefighting protection
abstract: Protective materials used in high-temperature environments often suffer from reduced thermal insulation performance under open-flame exposure, sustained heating and repeated compression, increasing the risk of thermal injury. In this study, a feather-inspired lightweight para-aramid/SiO2 aerogel thermal insulation composite with a fluffy porous structure was developed for firefighting thermal protection. Poly(p-phenylene terephthalamide) (PPTA) fibers were used as a heat-resistant fibrous skeleton to construct a porous insulation network through fiber carding, impregnation and aerogel compounding processes. Among the tested samples, the composite prepared with a nominal SiO2 aerogel addition of 1.5 g has exhibited the lowest surface temperature under a thermal load of 100 °C. Repeated-heating and cyclic-compression tests were conducted separately. The composite exhibited a relatively stable thermal response during repeated heating and a repeatable mechanical response during cyclic compression under the applied test conditions. At the fabric-assembly level, the limiting oxygen index (LOI) increased from 29% for the PPTA fabric-only reference to 35% for the PPTA + PPTA/SiO2-1.5 assembly, indicating improved flame resistance. A simplified PPTA-based protective assembly containing the composite filling has demonstrated a remarkable thermal-barrier behavior under direct-flame conditions with a flame temperature of ∼600 °C. The feather-inspired porous structure provides lightweight, fluffy and deformable filling characteristics while improving the thermal-protection performance of the composite. This work provides a potential structural design strategy for lightweight thermal insulation materials used in firefighting protective equipment. © 2026 Publishing services by Elsevier B.V. on behalf of KeAi Communications Co. title: Integrated wind uncertainty and incentive-based demand response framework for electricity market operation using probabilistic, robust, and fuzzy optimisation
abstract: The greater the integration of wind energy, the more uncertainty is introduced into electricity markets, affecting dispatch decisions, price formation, and system reliability. At the same time, incentive-based demand response provides a flexible means of dealing with imbalances between supply and demand. Yet, most of the studies currently available examine uncertainty modelling and demand response in isolation, leading to only a limited understanding of how different ways of representing uncertainty influence market results when combined with demand-side participation. This study proposes a hierarchical, multi-stage optimisation framework that includes wind generation uncertainty in the energy market and involves independent system operators, load-serving entities, and consumers. Probabilistic, robust, and fuzzy wind uncertainty models are incorporated into a multilevel modelling structure to allow for consistent comparison. The proposed method is solved using a hybrid technique that combines linear programming with Stackelberg particle swarm optimisation and is tested on the PJM 5-Bus and IEEE 118-Bus systems to examine both operational performance and scalability. The results show that combining uncertainty modelling with demand response results in significant improvements in several key market indicators. For the PJM 5-Bus system, the probabilistic approach reduces generation cost by 9.6%, increases demand reduction by 21.2%, and boosts LSE revenue by 9.5%. In the IEEE 118-Bus system, generation cost is reduced by 12.1%, total demand is decreased by 18.3%, and LSE revenue rises by 9.6%. The results demonstrated that the probabilistic model achieves lower locational marginal prices and higher demand flexibility by effectively using forecast information. The robust model produces more conservative but stable results under adverse wind conditions, while the fuzzy approach shows intermediate performance in situations where data are constrained. © 2026 The Authors. title: Multispectral correlation of infrared, ultraviolet, and leakage current attributes in a 500 kV substation under coastal environmental stress
abstract: This study investigates the relationship between infrared (IR), ultraviolet (UV), leakage current, and meteorological parameters for assessing saline contamination in high-voltage insulation systems operating in a coastal environment. A multispectral monitoring methodology was applied to seven 500 kV disconnect switches installed at a coastal substation located approximately 1.5 km from the sea. Infrared thermal attributes, ultraviolet partial discharge indicators, RMS leakage current measurements, and a precipitation-based drought index (derived from rainfall data) were collected and analyzed over several months under real operating conditions. Thermal monitoring was performed using region-based maximum threshold temperature variation (ΔTthreshold), while ultraviolet analysis employed maximum persistence (Pma´x) and corona discharge area (aF) as condition indicators. The monitored parameters exhibited similar temporal behavior, with reductions following significant rainfall events and progressive increases during extended dry periods, indicating the cumulative influence of saline contamination. Correlation analyses indicated strong and statistically significant associations between the monitored attributes and the number of days elapsed since precipitation events ≥ 5 mm. Pearson correlation coefficients ranged from 0.890 to 0.970, while Spearman coefficients reached 0.976 (p ≤ 0.01). Strong associations were also observed among thermal, ultraviolet, and leakage current indicators, suggesting consistency within the proposed multispectral framework. The results suggest that the integrated analysis of IR, UV, leakage current, and precipitation history may provide useful condition indicators for tracking contamination severity and supporting condition-based maintenance of high-voltage assets operating in coastal environments. © 2026 The Authors

title: Unveiling the thermodynamic performance of nano-enhanced bio-PCM for improved efficiency in solar cooling systems
abstract: Nano-enhanced bio-based phase change materials have emerged as promising thermal management materials for solar cooling applications because of their ability to improve heat transfer and thermal energy storage performance. This study presents a systematic review and quantitative synthesis of 50 peer-reviewed studies published between 2019 and 2025, focusing on thermodynamic mechanisms, thermophysical characterization, and cooling applications in photovoltaic and photovoltaic/thermal systems. The results demonstrate that nanoparticle incorporation significantly enhances thermal conductivity by approximately 15–400%, particularly with carbon-based nanofillers such as graphene and multi-walled carbon nanotubes, whereas latent heat retention generally decreases by 5–15% due to nanoparticle volume displacement and molecular interactions. The synthesized datasets indicate that an optimal nanoparticle loading of 2–4 weight percent provides a balanced enhancement of thermal conductivity and latent heat storage capacity. The correlation analysis reveals a minimal linear relationship between dispersion quality and latent heat retention, with a coefficient of r = 0.0935. This indicates that dispersion quality alone does not adequately account for the variations in latent heat retention observed across the reviewed studies. Instead, it suggests that factors such as nanoparticle morphology and interfacial compatibility are likely to have a more significant impact on thermodynamic behavior. The synthesis further shows that photovoltaic operating temperature can be reduced by up to 11°C under peak solar irradiance, resulting in an approximately 7.2% improvement in electrical efficiency. Exergy evaluation indicates that the latent phase contributes the highest useful exergy, approximately 42%, while demonstrating lower thermal irreversibility. Despite substantial material-level improvements, the aggregated system-level performance remains constrained by thermal resistance, methodological inconsistencies, and integration challenges in practical PV and PV/T configurations. © 2026 The Authors. title: Dynamic performance improvement in photovoltaic systems for hybrid renewable energy systems using enhanced optimized RNN approach
abstract: Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems (HRES), which combine Photovoltaic (PV) and Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) for grid-connected power networks, present a viable solution to the growing need for clean and dependable energy. System efficiency and dependability are constrained by issues including variable solar irradiation, conversion losses, and intricate control dynamics. Therefore, High-Resolution Pulse Width Modulation (HRPWM) Resonant DC-DC converter with Improved Reptile Optimization Algorithm (Improved ROA)-Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) based Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) technique is presented in this paper. By reducing component stress and preserving a common ground interface, a new HRPWM Resonant DC-DC converter is deployed to maximize voltage gain and efficiency.Moreover, to control battery storage and maintain energy balance under changing generation and load situations, a bidirectional isolated converter is used. On the inverter side, a Decoupled Radial Basis Function Neural Network (RBFNN) controller is used to achieve grid synchronisation and stable active/reactive power management. With an enhanced tracking efficiency 99.63%, less steady-state oscillation and increased converter efficiency97.56%, the proposed integrated design is ideal for distributed renewable energy and contemporary grid applications, which is proven by MATLAB/Simulink and experimental outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Experimental realization and nonlinear modelling of ferroresonance in a transformer–capacitor circuit
abstract: Ferroresonance is a nonlinear phenomenon capable of producing sustained overvoltages in power systems due to the interaction between system capacitance and the nonlinear magnetizing characteristics of transformers. This paper presents the development of a controlled laboratory platform for the experimental realization and analysis of ferroresonance in a transformer–capacitor circuit. The required series capacitance was determined using Rudenberg's graphical method, and protective arrangements are incorporated to ensure safe operation during high-voltage conditions. Experimental results confirm the successful initiation of ferroresonance and reveal a distinct jump phenomenon at a particular voltage. Bistable behavior is observed near the transition region, where ferroresonant and non-ferroresonant responses coexist under identical supply conditions. It is further found that the time required to reach steady-state ferroresonance decreases with increasing supply voltage. To support the experimental findings, the transformer's nonlinear magnetization characteristic is derived from open-circuit test data and used to formulate the governing nonlinear differential equations of the system. A numerical simulation predicts the ferroresonance transition at a voltage, in close agreement with the experimental observation. The minor deviation is attributed to practical non-idealities that the model does not fully capture. The strong correlation validates the proposed nonlinear framework and provides deeper insight into ferroresonance dynamics. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Effect of Aspect Ratio on the Workability of AA6082/Metakaolin/Nano Silicon Nitride Composites: An Experimental Investigation and Predictive Modeling using RSM and ANN
abstract: Understanding the impact of aspect ratio on the deformation and load-bearing capacity of aluminium matrix composites is crucial in tailoring their forming performance. In this study, aluminium alloy (AA) 6082/Metakaolin (MK)/nano silicon nitride (Si₃N₄) composites containing 7.5 wt.% MK and 1.5 wt.% Si₃N₄ were fabricated using ultrasonic cavitation-assisted stir casting and tested under quasi-static compression with cylindrical specimens of aspect ratios 0.5, 1, and 1.5 in both as-cast and T6 heat-treated conditions. The results showed that lower aspect ratios significantly enhanced workability. The as-cast composite at aspect ratio 0.5 sustained compressive deformation up to a 50% reduction in height without visible cracks, achieving a maximum axial stress of 573.25 MPa. The T6 heat-treated samples exhibited a maximum compressive strength of 543.31 MPa and fractured at lower strain due to embrittlement caused by eutectic Si and Mg₂Si phases. Microstructural analysis indicated pore closure as the governing deformation mechanism in as-cast specimens, while brittle fracture dominated the T6 samples. Instantaneous strain hardening exponent (nᵢ) and strength coefficient (kᵢ) trends confirmed contributions from both matrix and geometric work hardening during deformation. In order to predict the workability parameters for different aspect ratios and loadings, response surface methodology (RSM) and artificial neural network (ANN) were employed. ANN yielded superior prediction accuracy for the workability parameters compared to RSM. These findings confirm that aspect ratio strongly controls the deformation mechanisms, with shorter cylindrical specimens offering optimum workability for practical forming operations. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Analyticity and asymptotic behavior of solutions to the compressible Navier-Stokes-Korteweg equations with the zero sound speed in scaling critical spaces
abstract: We consider the initial-value problem in the d -dimensional Euclidean space Rd ( d ≥ 3) for the compressible Navier-Stokes-Korteweg equations under the zero sound speed case (namely, P′(ρ*)=0, where P=P(ρ) stands for the pressure). The system is well-known as the Diffuse Interface model describing the motion of a vaper-liquid mixture in a compressible viscous fluid. The purposes of this paper are to obtain the global-in-time solution around the constant equilibrium states ( ρ *, 0) ( ρ * > 0) satisfying the estimate on the analyticity as established by Foias-Temam (1989), and investigate the Lp−L1 type time-decay estimates in scaling critical settings based on Fourier-Herz spaces. In addition, we also derive the first order asymptotic formula with higher derivatives for solutions as the application of the analyticity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Discrete energy consistency for dynamic finite-strain frictional contact models with inelastic transformation
abstract: This paper presents a thermodynamically consistent framework for the numerical treatment of finite-strain contact problems involving frictional interaction and inelastic material transformations, with particular reference to plastic or superelastic materials. The formulation combines large-deformation continuum mechanics with dissipative constitutive behavior, including viscoelasticity, and unilateral contact constraints. We devise a time-integration scheme based on the midpoint rule, combined with a semi-smooth Newton strategy for the spatial discretization of frictional contact and inelastic transformation, in such a way that continuous energy balance is reproduced at the discrete level. We carry out a theoretical analysis of the discrete energy balance based on the numerical scheme, and verify the obtained estimates by means of a numerical simulation of two nearly-rigid bars compressing a hyper-visco-elasto-plastic ball. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach accurately captures complex nonlinear phenomena while maintaining robust energy behavior over long-term simulations. The study highlights the importance of discrete energy consistency for reliable and physically meaningful simulations of strongly coupled contact and inelastic processes at finite strain. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: A voltage imbalance prediction technology for wind turbine generator sets with DFIG
abstract: Grid voltage imbalance degrades wind turbine performance and injects distorted currents, significantly reducing power quality and conversion efficiency. This paper first analyzes the underlying causes of voltage imbalance in Doubly-fed induction generators (DFIG). Subsequently, the three-phase unbalance calculation for wind turbine voltage data is implemented to establish a standardized dataset for imbalance analysis. This paper proposes a forecasting model based on the gated recurrent unit–multi-head attention (GRU-MHA) architecture. By combining recurrent temporal modeling with attention-based feature enhancement, the proposed model predicts the positive voltage unbalance rate (PVUR) using historical voltage data and external meteorological data. By learning the variation trend and local fluctuation characteristics of PVUR, the model can provide data support for voltage-unbalance risk early warning in wind farms. Meanwhile, Optuna is employed for an automatic optimizer and hyperparameter tuning, enabling the training process to better adapt to complex temporal dynamics and thereby improving forecasting accuracy and robustness under different operating conditions. Real measured data from two wind farms, four WT units, and three representative months are used to construct 12 datasets. Comparative and ablation results show that GRU-MHA-O achieves superior overall PVUR forecasting accuracy and stability while maintaining acceptable computational efficiency, supporting its application in short-term monitoring and early warning. © 2026

title: A novel start-up control method for a bipolar hybrid cascaded MTDC system considering the DC current limiting capability of LCC
abstract: A bipolar hybrid cascaded multi-terminal high-voltage direct current (MTDC) system is being implemented in the Baihetan–Jiangsu HVDC project in China, where line-commutated converters (LCCs) and modular multilevel converters (MMCs) are integrated in a hybrid DC transmission structure. The uncontrolled charging of MMC submodules can generate large inrush currents, DC voltage fluctuations, and stress on the converter devices for such a hybrid MTDC system during its start-up. To solve these problems, a novel fast and smooth start-up control method of the bipolar hybrid cascaded MTDC system is proposed which makes full use of the DC current limiting capability of LCCs. The proposed method removes the traditional charging stage which is uncontrollable, and directly charges the MMC submodules under a controlled charging process. 1) A current limiting control strategy is designed for the LCC to limit the charging current of the DC side current to a safe range. 2) MMC submodule charging control strategy is proposed to maintain DC voltage stability and minimize inrush current during the controlled charging process. 3) The smooth transition strategy from start-up control strategy to normal operating control strategy is used to avoid the sudden change of DC voltage, DC current and converter power during the start-up process. The proposed start-up control method has been verified to be able to suppress the inrush current of the charging system, stabilize the DC voltage, and realize fast start-up and smooth start-up of the bipolar hybrid cascaded MTDC system through PSCAD/EMTDC simulation results. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Dynamic event-triggered hierarchical coordination for TSO-DSO systems: Communication-efficient optimization under practical constraints
abstract: The proliferation of distributed energy resources (DERs) demands scalable, communication-efficient coordination between transmission and distribution system operators (TSOs and DSOs). Existing hierarchical methods rely on periodic or iterative exchange, inducing excessive overhead and failing to accommodate network imperfections such as heterogeneous delays and packet dropouts. This paper proposes a three-layer dynamic event-triggered hierarchical coordination (DETHC) framework that transforms TSO-DSO interaction from time-driven to event-driven. An ordinary differential equation (ODE)-governed saturated dynamic threshold determines when DSOs transmit flexibility information, provably eliminating Zeno behavior; flexibility envelopes become event-driven objects refreshed upon state-, prediction-error-, and constraint-proximity triggers; and an event-triggered analytical target cascading (ATC) algorithm with distributed nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) solves the coordination asynchronously within a user-specified iteration bound. Under the assumptions of Section 6 (Lipschitz-bounded flexibility variation, second-order-cone-convexified subproblems, bounded delays, and bounded independent dropouts), Lyapunov analysis establishes practical bounded-error stability for communication delays up to 500 ms and stochastic dropouts. The analysis isolates two findings: a saturated threshold bounds worst-case staleness and the minimum inter-event time by design constants regardless of gain ordering—decoupling suppression aggressiveness from closed-loop stability—and the event-triggering protocol hard-limits the signal exchanged between the communication and optimization layers, so that input-to-state stability certifies the coupled scheme without any small-gain condition. Evaluated on a modified IEEE 30-bus system interconnected with five distribution feeders, DETHC achieves 73.3% communication reduction with only 0.06% optimality gap versus the SOCP-convexified centralized benchmark at the nominal five-DSO operating point, while remaining stable and—under this fixed five-DSO-tuned policy—scalable to 20 DSOs, for which the optimality gap remains below 3.2%. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Two-pattern cascading failure modeling with high renewable energy penetration considering the cascading protection characteristics
abstract: Cascading events such as the Spain “4.28” blackout were mostly triggered by protection misoperation and aggravated by the successive off-grid of renewable energy. The evolution characteristic of cascading failure (CF) with high renewable energy penetration shows profound changes compared with traditional power grids. The existing CF models still need improvement in depicting the CF dynamics with high renewable energy penetration. This paper proposes a two-pattern CF dynamic modeling method for power systems with high renewable energy penetration. Integrating the influence of random variation in external environmental factors and hidden faults in relay protection, the two-pattern representation models for renewable energy voltage/frequency protection and line overload protection are established. Considering the multi-time sequence response characteristics of cascading protection, a multi-time sequence dynamic model for CF with high renewable energy penetration is established. The risk analysis indices are further designed for CF risk evaluation. The simulation results on the IEEE 39-bus system and IEEE 300-bus power system show that the CFs with high renewable energy penetration exhibit multi-time-scale cascading characteristics. The method proposed in this paper can effectively distinguish the different evolution stages of CF and better align with the actual evolution process of CF with high renewable energy penetration. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
label: Science (including Engineering)

title: Dynamic Analysis of Functionally Graded Nanobeams Using Various Shear Deformation Theories Based on Doublet Mechanics
abstract: This study investigates the vibrational behavior of a functionally graded beam using the doublet mechanics theory. This theory accounts for interactions between constituent atoms within a structure, enabling consideration of atomic-scale structure and orientation relative to the beam axis. While classical Euler–Bernoulli and Timoshenko beam theories are commonly used within the framework of doublet mechanics, they typically neglect key terms associated with shear deformation effects. To overcome this limitation, the present research introduces the novel application of higher-order shear deformation theories (HSDTs) within the doublet mechanics framework. This approach, not previously explored in the literature, provides more accurate predictions of vibrational characteristics. The results reveal that employing doublet mechanics can significantly influence natural frequencies, with deviations of up to 5%. © 2026 The Author(s).
label: Science (including Engineering)

title: 2D Bond-Based Peridynamic Simulation of Phase Transformation in 3Y-TZP Dental Ceramics Using ABAQUS
abstract: In this research, the fracture behavior of 3 mol% yttria-stabilized tetragonal zirconia polycrystals (3Y-TZP) dental ceramics is investigated. The focus is on the tetragonal (t) to monoclinic (m) phase transformation using ABAQUS and bond-based peridynamics. We conducted two-dimensional simulations of a single grain undergoing uniform dilational expansion within a homogeneous m-phase environment. The effects of transformation time, biaxial stress, and strains on fracture were analyzed. It was found that increasing stress in the surrounding t-phase elevated the elastic strain energy associated with the transformation. By varying stress from-1.1 GPa to 400 MPa, elastic strain energy started to decrease from 3.41, 3.32, 3.11, and 2.85 pJ at fracture strain values of S0= 0.00711, 0.00553, 0.00395, and 0.00237, respectively. These correspond to reductions of 83%, 87%, 90%, and 96%. In addition, damage fractions increased from 0.001, 0.002, 0.003, and 0.004 to 0.005, 0.011, 0.022, and 0.058, respectively. This demonstrates the significant impact of applied stress on the fracture mechanics of 3Y-TZP. Moreover, increasing the elemental parameter S0 from 0.00237 to 0.00711 in the simulations corresponds to a considerable decrease in defect density, resulting in a substantial increase in the total energy required for material division from 0.25 to 2.2 J/m2. © 2026 The Author(s).
