title: Comparative Investigation of Deflection in a Bi-directional Curved Functionally Graded Porous Beam Using Unified Shear Deformation Theory
abstract: The present study investigates the bending characteristics of a two-dimensional functionally graded curved porous beam using unified shear deformation theory (USDT), incorporating shear functions and a modified power law. This approach integrates potential energy, the neutral surface concept, and equilibrium equations to enhance accuracy. Various boundary conditions, such as simply supported (SS), clamped-supported (CS), clamped-clamped (CC), and clamped-free (CF), are employed in the analysis. A metal-ceramic functionally graded beam with both even and uneven porosity is modelled. The symmetrical material gradation ensures that the physical neutral surface aligns with the geometrical neutral surface, which is considered in the formulation. A displacement-based formulation and energy principles are adopted, providing a more comprehensive and precise analysis of the beams. This method accounts for higher-order shear deformation effects, eliminates the need for shear correction factors, and effectively manages the continuous variation of material properties in FGMs. Consequently, it leads to improved predictions of structural behavior, making USDT particularly valuable for advanced material applications. The Hamilton method is employed to derive equilibrium equations for the beams, which are subsequently solved using the Kuhn-Tucker conditions. © 2025 The Author(s).

title: Experimental Investigation and RSM-Based Optimization of Phenolic/PTFE/SiC Composites
abstract: Resole phenolic resin, valued for its excellent heat resistance, strong adhesion, and chemical stability, has long been utilized in aerospace, automotive, and protective material applications. However, its relatively low toughness and brittleness limit broader use. In this study, the thermal and mechanical characteristics of phenolic composites were improved by incorporating Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) powder, Silicon carbide (SiC) particles, carbon, and high-silica fibers. A D-optimal response surface methodology (RSM) design was employed to evaluate the effects of fiber type, curing temperature, and particle loading. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis revealed that the addition of reinforcing particles altered fracture morphology by promoting crack deflection and improving resin–fiber interaction. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) results confirmed a 7% increase in glass transition temperature (Tg) with 10% particle loading, indicating enhanced thermal stability. Mechanical testing demonstrated that the addition of 10 wt% reinforcing particles enhanced both tensile and flexural properties, regardless of the fiber type; however, the fiber type itself had a significant influence on performance. Carbon fiber composites achieved the highest tensile strength (264.8 MPa), which was 13% above hybrid laminates (235.2 MPa) and 185% above high-silica composites (93.0 MPa). Conversely, hybrid laminates exhibited the best flexural strength (219.9 MPa), exceeding carbon by 72% and high-silica by 150%. Quantitative ANOVA validation confirmed the reliability of the developed models for both tensile and flexural strength. Optimal parameters—10% particle loading, 180°C curing with carbon fibers for tensile strength, and hybrid fibers for flexural strength—offer clear, actionable guidance for industrial applications. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Investigation of the Mechanical and Tribological Behaviour of Al Alloy and Al/ZrO2Ex-Situ Nano Composites
abstract: The present study investigates the mechanical and tribological behaviour of Al alloys and Al/ZrO2 ex-situ composites, focusing on their microstructural evolution and property enhancement. Al/ZrO2 composites were synthesised using stir casting, incorporating 1, 3, and 5 wt.% ZrO2 particles. Alloys and composites were characterizedusing X-ray diffraction (XRD), optical microscope (OM), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM)to analyse phase formation, particle distribution. Microstructural analysis revealed homogeneous dispersion of ZrO2 particles, promoting load transfer and matrix strengthening. Mechanical properties were analysed using Vickers microhardness and uniaxial tensile tests, demonstrating substantial increases in hardness and tensile strength with increasing ZrO2 content due to grain refinement, dislocation strengthening, and Orowan strengthening mechanisms. Tribological performance was evaluated using a pin-on-disc apparatus under varying loads (10N-30N) and sliding speeds (1 m/sec-3 m/sec). The Al/ZrO2 composites exhibited a significant reduction in the wear (up to 50%) compared to the unreinforced alloy, attributed to the load-bearing capacity of ZrO2 particles and the formation of a protective tribolayer. Surface morphology of the worn samples, analysed using SEM, indicated a transition from abrasive to mild adhesive wear with the addition of ZrO2. Further topographical parameters were studied using atomic force microscopy (AFM), which suggests a decrease in surface roughness from 0.87 µm to 0.70 µm at3wt. % of ZrO2 compared to the base alloy. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Interlaminar shear behaviour of additively manufactured continuous fibre-reinforced composites using MWCNT-coated filaments
abstract: The unsatisfactory interlaminar performance in additively manufactured continuous fibre-reinforced composites (CFRCs) remains a major challenge inherent to the printing process. Incorporating multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) has improved interlaminar performance in traditionally manufactured laminates. However, the use of MWCNTs in additively manufactured CFRCs has received little attention to date. This study investigates the interlaminar shear behaviour of additively manufactured CFRCs enhanced via coating MWCNTs on the surface of continuous fibre filaments. An automatic layer-by-layer process was developed to coat two types of fibre filament materials: glass fibre filaments (GFF) and carbon fibre filaments (CFF). Multilayer MWCNTs were deposited onto the filaments by sequentially adsorbing positively charged polyethyleneimine (PEI) and negatively charged MWCNTs via an electrostatic self-assembly process. The automated process promoted relatively uniform MWCNT coating through precise control of the filament speed. The updated coating baths allowed the filament to pass over a thin layer of solution without contacting rollers, thereby avoiding mechanical damage associated with the previous roller-based system. MWCNTs were successfully deposited on both GFF and CFF. The contribution of MWCNTs to the interlaminar shear properties differed between CFF and GFF in terms of tangent modulus, maximum load and ultimately the interlaminar shear strength. With a single layer of MWCNTs, the maximum short beam shear load improved by 4% and 14% for CFF and GFF composites, respectively. The addition of 1–5 MWCNT layers enhanced the tangent modulus across all tested configurations, ranging 12–20% for CFF and 32–96% for GFF. The effects of MWCNTs on the stiffness were more pronounced for GFF samples than stiffer CFF samples. The integration of MWCNTs into additively manufactured CFRCs would facilitate the production of customised lightweight components with improved interlaminar performance. © 2026 The Authors. title: Ni-Pi-Ni Based Asterisk Shaped Highly Efficient Solar Energy Harvester
abstract: This article presents an asterisk shaped ultra-wideband absorber designed with nickel (Ni) as conducting layers and polyimide substrate to form a three-layered structure. Its unit cell volume is 45 × 45 × 9 nm3 (0.00000267 λ3 L at 158.174 THz) while operating across the frequency spectrum of 158.174 THz (1896.645 nm)- ≥ 4500 THz (≤66.67 nm) which covers infrared, visible, and ultraviolet spectra for absorption (A) ≥ 90% with an average (Aavg) of 96.35%. It has absorption > 95% across 191.31-388.98 THz and 773.3-3876.75 THz while simulating using CST Microwave Studio Suite (v. 2021). Symmetricity of asterisk’s geometry leads to polarization insensitivity while having Aavg > 90% for 0°≤incident angle(θ) ≤ 60°. The solar absorber efficiency (ȠA) achieved for the proposed absorber is 94.66% with thermal emission efficiency (ȠE) of 91.69%, 93.8%, 94.51%, 94.61% and 94.53% at 1500K, 2000K, 2500K, 3000K, and 3500K, respectively. The range of the proposed absorber, with all its operating frequency bands, makes it a suitable model for uses like solar energy harvesting, solar detectors, sensors, and so on. © 1995-2012 IEEE.

title: Effect of Delamination on the Natural Frequency of Fiber Metal Laminate under Various Conditions
abstract: Multi-layered composite materials with improved capabilities are fiber metal laminates (FMLs). Damage to the composites, such as delamination, decreases their stiffness and modifies the dynamic behaviour of the structures. Vibration analysis can be a good way to forecast delamination since the loss of stiffness affects the natural frequencies, mode shapes, and other structural features. In this research, vibrational analysis of aluminum and mild steel-based carbon fiber metal laminates is considered with delamination. A total of thirty-six fiber metal laminate specimens of 3/2 configuration with various delamination areas and situated at various interfaces were considered for vibrational analysis, which was carried out experimentally and by FEA software. The analysis is done on healthy and delaminated specimens under clamped-free and clamped-clamped conditions. The results demonstrate that the proposed method indicates that delamination reduces the natural frequency of the FML. The decrease in natural frequency can be used for damage detection, which will act as a base for an inverse problem. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Temperature gradient-dependent space charge accumulation and electric field distribution in bi-layer cable-accessory insulation
abstract: Space charge preferentially accumulates at bi-layer insulation interface in high-voltage direct-current (HVDC) cable accessories, rendering this region particularly susceptible to insulation degradation. During cable operation, the bi-layer cable-accessory insulation is inevitably subjected to a temperature gradient (TG) superimposed on DC voltage, yet how TG affects space charge dynamics in the cable-accessory insulation remains insufficiently elucidated. Space charge distributions in cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE)/silicone rubber (SR) bi-layer dielectrics subjected to TG are characterized via the pulsed electroacoustic (PEA) technique. An expanded charge transport model incorporating surface states, impurity ions, and field- and temperature-dependent conductivity is proposed to simulate the charge behavior in the bi-layer dielectrics under TG. The simulations reproduce the principal characteristics of the measured distributions and their variation trends with increasing TG. The results demonstrate that homocharge emerges and progressively intensifies in the vicinity of the high-temperature anode, while heterocharge in the vicinity of the low-temperature cathode continuously accumulates as TG is elevated. The XLPE/SR interface charge density initially increases and subsequently decreases as TG increases. The maximum electric field invariably resides within the high-temperature XLPE adjacent to the XLPE/SR interface. The field distortion is further intensified as TG rises, with the maximum field strength increasing by 20.2% and 28.6% at TG of 15 °C and 35 °C, respectively, and the position of the maximum field strength shifting progressively towards the XLPE/SR interface. These findings provide practical guidance for space charge regulation and insulation design optimization of HVDC cable accessories. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: FCGNet: A fractional- condition-aware gated network for wind power forecasting
abstract: Wind power forecasting is challenging due to the pronounced nonstationarity, multi-scale coupling, and abrupt fluctuations of wind power time series under complex meteorological conditions. Existing forecasting methods either lack explicit modeling of temporal structures or have limited ability to adaptively integrate heterogeneous dynamic features. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a Fractional-Condition-Aware Gated Network (FCGNet) for wind power forecasting. The framework consists of three stages: adaptive input reconstruction, heterogeneous temporal modeling, and collaborative feature fusion. First, an Adaptive Feature Gating module is employed to enhance multivariate input representations through global importance recalibration and local perturbation correction. Then, a Fractional-Order BiGRU branch is introduced to model long-range dependencies via power-law memory accumulation, while a condition-aware PatchTST branch captures operating-condition-dependent multi-scale patterns through physically guided scale weighting. Finally, a cross-branch attention fusion module is designed to achieve dynamic interaction and adaptive integration of the two heterogeneous representations. For a 12 h-ahead forecasting task, Experimental results on two real-world wind power datasets show that FCGNet achieves superior forecasting performance compared with representative baseline models and exhibits strong robustness across different data distributions and wind conditions. The proposed method provides an effective and interpretable solution for high-precision wind power forecasting in renewable energy systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Numerical analysis of elastic elliptic membrane shells in frictional contact with wear
abstract: We consider a family of linearly elastic and elliptic membrane shells, all sharing the same middle surface, with thickness 2ε, clamped along their entire lateral face, which upon deformation may enter in frictional contact with a moving foundation along its lower face. As a result of friction, material might be removed from the interface, thus causing wear. In this paper, we focus in the numerical analysis of our model and provide a priori error estimates for displacements, stress and wear fields. We have implemented the fully discrete scheme with the FreeFEM++ programming environment, by using an intrinsic (basis free) formulation, reduction of order, penalization and Newton method. We carried on a series of numerical simulations to demonstrate the capabilities of our code, providing experimental evidence of our theoretical results regarding the convergence with respect to the thickness parameter ε and mesh size h . As a practical application, we have also included the results of a simulation of the wear that undergoes the tyre of a vehicle braking on a road. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Combinatorial metabolic engineering of Mycobacterium neoaurum LY-2 for efficient androstenedione production from phytosterols
abstract: Androstenedione (AD) is an important precursor for the synthesis of corticosteroids, sex hormones, and other high-value steroid pharmaceuticals. Microbial conversion of phytosterols provides a sustainable route for AD production, but current production levels remain insufficient for practical industrial application. In this study, a modular metabolic engineering strategy was developed to improve AD biosynthesis from phytosterols in Mycobacterium neoaurum LY-2. Competing C19 and C22 steroid pathways were first blocked to attenuate AD degradation, generating the AD-accumulating strain Mbn12 with a titer of 5.14 g/L. Sterol catabolic flux was then enhanced by relieving transcriptional repression and improving acetyl-CoA and propionyl-CoA utilization, which increased AD production to 6.08 g/L. To support high-flux sterol oxidation, cofactor regeneration and oxidative stress resistance were further strengthened, raising AD production to 6.67 g/L. Finally, moderate cell envelope remodeling improved substrate transport and increased AD production to 6.98 g/L. The final engineered strain Mbn30 produced 20.55 g/L AD from 30 g/L phytosterols in a 5 L fermenter, representing a 48.6% improvement over Mbn12. This work provides a scalable engineering framework for AD production and offers guidance for the microbial manufacture of other steroid intermediates. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Experimental Study of Woven Glass, Bamboo, and Jute Fibre Reinforced in Epoxy Composites
abstract: Industries like aerospace, automotive, marine, and transportation require materials that are lightweight yet strong, durable, and impact-resistant. To meet these demands, advanced composite materials are being developed using natural fibres such as bamboo and jute, which are eco-friendly, abundant, and cost-effective. When combined with synthetic fibres like glass, known for its heat resistance and interfacial strength, the mechanical properties of these composites improve significantly. Fabricated using the hand lay-up method with a 70% epoxy and 30% fibre ratio, these materials were tested per ASTM standards. Studies have shown that hybrid composites reinforced with bamboo, jute, and glass fibres offer enhanced tensile, flexural, hardness, and impact strength. The S1 stacking sequence performed best, with a tensile strength of 95 MPa, modulus of 1028MPa, flexural strength of 195 MPa and modulus 54 GPa, impact toughness of 12 J/mm, hardness of 87 RHN, and thermal conductivity of 0.26 W/m·K. These composites are lightweight, strong, and thermally efficient, making them ideal for rail, power, automotive, marine, and aerospace applications. © 2025 The Author(s).

title: Interlaminar Shear Failure Monitoring in GFRPs Using Graphene Nanoplatelets
abstract: Components made of glass fiber reinforced polymers often fail under interlaminar shear loading conditions, which can significantly compromise their structural performance. To solve this problem, the piezoresistive effect of graphene nanoplatelets integrated into the glass fiber reinforced polymers is proposed as a technique to monitor and detect interlaminar shear failure. For that, short beam shear specimens were prepared from glass fiber reinforced polymers modified with graphene nanoplatelets, and changes in electrical resistance caused by quasi-static bending forces were recorded to monitor the electromechanical behavior and failure mode. The interlaminar shear strength was obtained at around 30 MPa for both composites (0.75 and 1 wt.% graphene nanoplatelets). Results indicate that the incorporation of graphene nanoplatelets has a minimal effect on the electromechanical behavior curves, and both concentrations (0.75 and 1 wt.%) provide good electrical sensing capability for interlaminar shear failure in glass fiber reinforced polymers, which can be used as an active tool for health monitoring applications across a wide variety of industrial applications, especially where this failure mode may occur. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Genome-integrated engineering of Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 enables sustained gut-local biosynthesis of 5-hydroxytryptophan
abstract: 5-Hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP) is a functional precursor of serotonin; however, achieving sustained 5-HTP production in vivo by engineered microbes remains challenging. To address this, we developed a genome-integrated engineered probiotic system enabling gut-local biosynthesis of 5-HTP. Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN), a clinically validated probiotic with an established safety profile for intestinal application, was selected as the chassis. Constitutive expression was employed to eliminate inducer dependence, while genomic integration was used to enhance genetic stability and avoid reliance on antibiotic selection for pathway maintenance. In addition, BH4 biosynthesis and regeneration modules were incorporated to address the limited endogenous BH4 availability in the gut environment. Different administration strategies were systematically evaluated to characterize in vivo performance. Notably, our results showed that the hTPH2 hydroxylation module, together with the BH4 biosynthesis and regeneration system, supported 5-HTP biosynthesis in EcN. The engineered EcN strain achieved a 5-HTP titer of 863.2 mg/L, the highest level reported in EcN-based systems. Under non-selective conditions, EcNPconst−5−HTP carrying the chromosomally integrated pathway maintained stable 5-HTP production in vitro and retained 5-HTP-producing capacity after intestinal passage, whereas plasmid loss in non-integrated constructs resulted in a pronounced decrease in production. In vivo analysis showed that single-dose administration induced a transient elevation in plasma 5-HTP, whereas repeated dosing generated reproducible, time-dependent fluctuations in fecal bacterial abundance and gut-local biosynthetic activity. Treatment with the engineered probiotic further improved behavioral phenotypes and modulated brain 5-HT-related metabolites in a reserpine-induced mouse model. Together, these findings provide a translational framework linking in vitro 5-HTP production by engineered probiotics to their in vivo functional performance. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Machining Behavior of Al-MMC Reinforced with Hybrid Additives: Effects of Cutting Parameters – A Taguchi Approach
abstract: Aluminum-based composites reinforced with Mg₂Si particles are valued for their engineering properties. This study examines how cutting parameters and Ag, Bi, and Sr additives affect tool wear and surface roughness during both dry and wet turning of Al–Mg₂Si composites. Using a Taguchi design, we varied spindle speed, feed rate, depth of cut, and lubrication to determine their relative impacts on tool wear area and surface roughness. Composites were fabricated through casting and examined using SEM–EDS techniques to assess microstructural characteristics and wear morphology. Feed rate emerged as the most critical factor, while wet machining with a biodegradable fluid markedly improved both tool life and finish. Among the materials tested, the composite containing all three additives delivered the lowest wear and finest surface. Specifically, the 14.47% improvement in dispersion uniformity was observed when all additives were used, while tool wear was reduced by 24.04%, and surface roughness improved by 18.94% under optimized machining conditions (spindle speed of 1000 rpm, feed rate of 0.12 mm/rev, and depth of cut of 1 mm). Regression modeling supported the experimental findings and demonstrated strong predictive accuracy. Confirmation trials under optimized conditions verified these trends. These results highlight the role of additive elements not only in modifying microstructure but also in enhancing machinability. The findings provide clear guidance on selecting additive combinations and machining settings to maximize productivity, extend tool life, and achieve superior surface integrity in Al–Mg₂Si composite turning. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Strategies and applications for alleviating carbon catabolite repression
abstract: Carbon catabolite repression (CCR) is a widespread regulatory strategy across diverse microorganisms that prioritises the utilisation of preferred carbon sources. In industrial bioprocesses, however, CCR-mediated substrate hierarchy can delay the utilisation of secondary carbon sources in mixed feedstock, thereby extending fermentation time and limiting carbon conversion efficiency toward target products. Existing reviews have largely addressed CCR in a microorganism-specific manner, potentially obscuring conserved principles, limiting cross-species comparisons, and constraining generalisable engineering; computational modelling and engineering applications also remain underrepresented. This review therefore first summarises CCR mechanisms across diverse microorganisms through a common systems-level framework, in which transport-linked sensing converts carbon flux into intracellular signals, transcriptional regulators reprogramme genome-wide expression, RNA-based mechanisms fine-tune the timing and magnitude of responses, and protein stability shapes their persistence. Multi-omics approaches, particularly interactomics and single-cell omics, are then highlighted for revealing CCR as a dynamic and multilayered regulatory system by resolving interaction networks, temporal changes, and cell-to-cell heterogeneity beyond bulk measurements. Quantitative computational modelling is also discussed, with emphasis on kinetic and constraint-based frameworks that connect regulatory mechanisms to metabolic flux and predict system behaviour under changing carbon substrates. Engineering strategies, including adaptive laboratory evolution, transcription factor engineering, transporter and promoter engineering, and pathway rewiring, are further compared for the relief of CCR and improvement of substrate co-utilisation and production performance. Finally, these advances are presented within a Design-Build-Test-Learn framework, through which mechanistic discovery and omics-scale analysis are used to inform model development, and modelling and engineering are iteratively coupled to improve microbial performance. We propose that such an integrative paradigm is emerging as a unifying direction for CCR research, and provides a foundation for rational strain design and more efficient, sustainable biomanufacturing. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Fast frequency parameter adaptive optimization strategy for TD3 wind turbines guided by frequency response mechanism
abstract: With growing wind penetration, reduced inertia raises frequency instability risks. To fully exploit wind frequency regulation capability, this paper proposes a Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3)-based adaptive optimization strategy for wind turbine (WTG) fast frequency parameters guided by frequency response mechanisms. First, a time-domain analytical model of WTG frequency response with deadband is established, revealing coupled effects of deadband threshold, regulation coefficient, and wind penetration on system frequency dynamics. On this basis, a deep reinforcement learning framework is developed: the frequency response model is embedded into a three-stage mechanism-guided reward function, where physical safety boundaries constrain the minimum regulation coefficient in the linear penalty region, and unsafe actions are penalized quadratically proportional to deviation. Meanwhile, dual experience replay buffers with linearly decaying sampling are constructed, enabling smooth transition from a safe baseline to autonomous exploration via knowledge pre-filling. Finally, simulations under varying wind speeds, multiple disturbances, and complex conditions are conducted in MATLAB/Simulink. Results demonstrate the proposed strategy adaptively tunes the primary frequency regulation coefficient, effectively reduces maximum frequency deviation, and improves frequency recovery speed and training stability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Area-based SEL–Π control for voltage safety under disturbances and topology changes
abstract: Maintaining voltage safety in DER-rich distribution feeders is essential for reliable operation, equipment protection, and renewable-energy integration. This paper proposes an online robust voltage-control framework that separates sensitivity/uncertainty adaptation from real-time constraint enforcement. The main novelty is an area-based SEL–Π realization, where Structured Error Learning (SEL) updates within-area voltage–reactive sensitivity blocks and disturbance bounds from closed-loop measurements, while projected control (Π) solves local robust quadratic programs (QPs) with tightened voltage limits, inverter constraints, and slack-assisted feasibility. Centralized operation is recovered as the special case K=1. On the Southern California Edison 56-bus feeder over a 24 h real-data-driven stress study with 14 controlled buses, decentralized SEL–Π eliminates severe open-loop violations, maintains the prescribed voltage band in the tested topology-change case, and achieves centralized-reference-level voltage safety. Additional diagnostics show substantial cross-area coupling and 96.7–98.8% realized residual-envelope coverage, with QP slack numerically zero at a 10−4 tolerance. Compared with tuned local PI feedback, SEL–Π achieves voltage safety with substantially lower actuation, while Π-QP computation remains well below the 6-s control interval and SEL is executed only intermittently. © 2026

title: Nonlinear Behavior of Honeycomb Structure Under Large Deformations Using Absolute Nodal Coordinate Formulation and Periodic Homogenization
abstract: This study determines the elastic constants and evaluates the in-plane mechanical behavior of hexagonal and re-entrant (auxetic) honeycomb structures under large deformations by utilizing the Absolute Nodal Coordinate Formulation (ANCF) for modeling elastic forces and applying periodic boundary conditions (PBCs) to precisely control deformations at the boundaries. A representative volume element (RVE) was selected, and static equations were derived by modeling cell walls as beam elements using the ANCF based on the finite element method (FEM) and the periodic boundary conditions were subsequently implemented. After solving the static equations, analytical validation was performed for small deformations. The results demonstrate that honeycomb structures exhibit nonlinear behavior under large deformations, which is crucial to determine for dynamic applications. In addition, the proposed model provides an effective technique for determining elastic constants and evaluating the mechanical behavior of honeycomb structures under large deformations, with applicability to various cellular geometries and piezoelectric cell structures. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Mechanical Properties of Sandwich Composite with Polyurethane Core Reinforced by Biaxial Geogrid and Carbon-Glass Fiber/Polyester as Skin
abstract: The development of sandwich panels as structural materials is increasingly driven by the diversification of constituent materials. In this study, carbon-glass/polyester fibers were selected for the outer skins due to their high strength-to-density ratio, while polyurethane foam was used as the core for its lightweight characteristics despite its relatively low mechanical strength. To enhance the core’s performance, two-way geogrid reinforcement was incorporated. The primary objective of this research is to investigate the effect of geogrid reinforcement and the influence of core thickness on the mechanical properties of the resulting sandwich composite, with particular emphasis on identifying the optimal geogrid configuration and core thickness that yield the highest structural performance. The novelty of this research is the addition of a geogrid used as a sandwich composite reinforcement. Variations in the number of geogrid layers and core thickness were examined. The composite sandwich panels undergo flexural and compressive tests. The results indicated that the composite with a core thickness of 50 mm and five layers of geogrid reinforcement exhibited the highest performance, achieving a flexural strength of 47.59 MPa and a shear stress of 1856.68 MPa. In contrast, one layer of geogrid achieved a flexural strength of 45.46 MPa and a shear stress of 1768.60 MPa. Similar results were observed in the composite compression tests, where the composite with five geogrid layers achieved a compressive strength of 0.18 MPa, significantly higher than the 0.12 MPa achieved with a single layer of geogrid. The decreasing distance between geogrid layers increases the core density, thus enhancing resistance to compressive loads. This material can be used as a structural material to withstand vibrations such as earthquakes. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Biomimetic interface-regulated composite coatings on flexible fabrics for microwave absorption, flame retardancy, and ultraviolet shielding
abstract: Multifunctional coatings combining electromagnetic protection, fire safety, and environmental durability are attractive for flexible protective textiles. Here, an interface-regulated coating was fabricated by embedding Fe3O4@TiO2@polyaniline (FTP) core-shell fillers in an ivy-inspired poly(vinyl phosphonic acid-co-hydroxyethyl acrylate-co-styrene) (PVHS) matrix and depositing it on polyester fabric. The Fe3O4 core provides magnetic loss, the TiO2 interlayer promotes interfacial polarization and ultraviolet attenuation, and the polyaniline shell contributes dielectric loss and conductive pathways. Meanwhile, phosphonic acid groups in PVHS act as proton donors to regulate polyaniline doping, thereby strengthening polarization loss and improving impedance matching at low filler loading. The optimized FTP@PVHS-4 achieved a minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of −37.25 dB and an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 6.27 GHz, while the coated fabric retained strong absorption with −32.74 dB and 6.73 GHz, respectively. PVHS also promoted condensed-phase charring, reducing the peak heat release rate by 91.2% relative to pristine polyester. In addition, the fabric exhibited excellent ultraviolet shielding, with a protection factor of 1993.21 and average ultraviolet‑A transmittance of 0.05%, while maintaining coating integrity and textile flexibility. This study demonstrates that interfacial electronic regulation and biomimetic polymer design provide an effective strategy for lightweight, durable, and multifunctional electromagnetic protective fabrics. © 2026

title: Interfacial engineering of MOF-on-MOF heterostructure for efficient charge separation and photoelectrochemical water splitting
abstract: Hematite (α-Fe2O3) is a promising photoelectrode material for photoelectrochemical water splitting (PEC-WS). Practical application remains limited by low photogenerated carrier separation efficiency and sluggish surface reaction kinetics. Surface engineering and heterojunction construction offer effective routes to address these limitations. In this study, a dual metal-organic framework (MOF) heterostructure is constructed by introducing MIL-125(NH2) and UiO-66 onto the surface of an α-Fe2O3 photoanode to enhance carrier separation and transport. The resulting α-Fe2O3/MIL-125(NH2)/UiO-66 photoanode delivers a photocurrent density of 1.93 mA cm−2 at 1.23 V versus RHE (VRHE), corresponding to a 1.19-fold increase relative to pristine α-Fe2O3. Mechanistic analysis shows that interfacial interactions and the formation of Fe-Ti and Fe-O-Ti bonds between α-Fe2O3 and MIL-125(NH2) facilitate charge transfer and improve photoelectrochemical water splitting (PEC-WS) stability. Dual-MOF modification lowers the work function of α-Fe2O3 and establishes favorable band alignment, generating an enhanced built-in electric field that drives photogenerated holes toward the MIL-125(NH2)/UiO-66 cocatalyst and accelerates water oxidation kinetics. The dual-MOF heterojunction further prolongs the photogenerated hole lifetime, increasing charge transfer efficiency. These synergistic effects enrich surface active sites, suppress charge recombination, and promote carrier separation and transport, resulting in improved PEC-WS performance of the α-Fe2O3 photoanode. © 2026

title: Structural engineering of carbon-based nanofibers via electrospinning for enhanced electromagnetic functionality
abstract: Carbon-based nanofibers (CNFs) have attracted considerable attention owing to their high electrical conductivity, large specific surface area, superior mechanical strength, and excellent thermal stability, making them promising for applications in energy storage, sensing, catalysis, and environmental remediation. Electrospinning, one of the most effective techniques for CNF fabrication, enables the continuous production of high-performance carbon nanofibers with operational simplicity and excellent controllability. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in electrospinning-derived CNFs. First, the fundamentals of electrospinning and the structural characteristics of CNFs are introduced. The microwave absorption mechanisms of CNFs are then comprehensively discussed. Subsequently, the structural design strategies of electrospun CNF microwave absorbers and the corresponding performance enhancement mechanisms are systematically reviewed. Finally, future research directions are highlighted, focusing on multispectral response, advanced structural design, scalable electrospinning technologies, and integrated device design. This review provides theoretical guidance and technical insights for the fabrication of high-performance electrospun CNFs and offers perspectives for the design and practical application of CNF electromagnetic functional materials. © 2026

title: Post-combustion carbon capture in the cement industry: A critical review of its decarbonization potential
abstract: The cement industry is a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions, accounting for nearly 7% of global anthropogenic CO2 emissions. As cement demand continues to rise, rapid and substantial emission reductions are imperative to keep global warming close to 2 °C by the end of the century. Extensive research over the past decade has explored multiple decarbonization pathways—including alternative low-carbon clinkers, process optimization, and the increased use of supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs). Although such strategies offer meaningful reductions, their overall impact is constrained by limited material availability, performance challenges, slow commercialization rates, and the difficulties of scaling manufacturing solutions within established production pipelines. In this context, post-combustion carbon capture (PCC) has emerged as a particularly versatile and high-impact pathway for mitigating CO2 emissions from both existing and new cement plants, offering a scalable and technologically compatible route to rapid emissions reduction. This review critically examines the CO2 challenge in the cement sector and evaluates currently available mitigation strategies. The review subsequently elaborates on PCC as one of the fastest and most practical solutions by presenting its key technologies, contemporary applications, and associated limitations. Overall, the literature indicates that while PCC is considered among the more viable options, it still faces significant challenges that limit its large-scale deployment. © 2026 The Authors. title: Harnessing Schottky heterointerfaces in thermally activated high-entropy perovskite ceramics toward wide-temperature absorption-dominated electromagnetic wave protection
abstract: To surmount severe high-temperature failure in electromagnetic media, HE-RE1−xSrxCoO3−δ/CC-RE2​O3​ composite ceramics were engineered via a one-step solid reaction. Sr doping provokes lattice distortions and a dynamic Jahn-Teller effect, establishing nanoscale Schottky heterointerfaces and a well-regulated conductor-like electronic state. The synergy between high-entropy configuration and thermally triggered Co3+ spin-state transitions accelerates carrier mobility, overcoming phonon-scattering barriers. Consequently, the optimized S20 composite manifests a profile governed by semiconductor-like transport, where Schottky interface-mediated carrier dynamics stabilize impedance matching while maximizing internal volumetric dissipation. Remarkably, S20 achieves superior dual-mode protection: a minimum reflection loss of −48.64 dB at 200 °C (retaining a −5 dB bandwidth across the X-band up to 600 °C) and an absorption-dominated electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness exceeding 20 dB (peak 31.92 dB) at 600 °C with A > 50%. This establishes a new material-design paradigm for all-temperature, high-efficiency, and absorption-dominated electromagnetic absorbing and shielding systems. © 2026

title: Enhanced dynamic control of multi-area interconnected microgrids using virtual inertia and improved gazelle-optimized TPIDD2 controller
abstract: Low system inertia in renewable-rich microgrids (μGs) makes frequency and voltage stability highly vulnerable to disturbances and non-nominal operating conditions. To address this challenge, this work proposes an enhanced control strategy for two-area interconnected μGs using an improved Gazelle optimization algorithm (IGOA) tuned tilt-proportional-integral-derivative second-order derivative (TPIDD2) controller integrated with virtual inertia control (VIC). The approach simultaneously targets improvements across load frequency control (LFC) and automatic voltage regulation (AVR). Its robustness is evaluated against variations in load demand, renewable generation uncertainty, changes in inertia levels, and communication time delays (CTDs). Performance is benchmarked against controllers optimized with grey wolf, whale, and arithmetic optimization algorithms, as well as a conventional PID controller. Sensitivity analysis is included to ensure reliability under diverse operating scenarios, and practical validation is demonstrated using a real-time experimental OPAL-RT platform. The results confirm that the offered approach substantially enhances the dynamic performance and resilience of interconnected μGs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Mitigation of dynamic coupling and sub-synchronous oscillations in AC–DC coupled multi-terminal MMC–HVDC networks
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic coupling mechanisms and sub-synchronous oscillation (SSO) phenomena in multi-terminal modular multilevel converter–based high-voltage direct current (MMC–HVDC) networks and proposes an effective mitigation strategy. A detailed small-signal model is developed to capture internal MMC dynamics, converter control interactions, and the dynamic coupling between offshore and onshore converters through the common DC link. Eigenvalue- and impedance-based analyses reveal that arm capacitor voltages, zero-sequence component of the circulating current, and DC-voltage controller collectively shape the oscillatory behavior and inter-converter coupling within the 0–50 Hz range. Mode sensitivity analysis further demonstrates that droop gain, DC-voltage PI parameters, and damping coefficients significantly affect modal damping. To mitigate coupling-induced instabilities, a modified circulating current controller is introduced to regulate the zero-sequence current component and suppress its participation in SSO modes. Frequency- and time-domain simulations confirm that the proposed controller effectively mitigates oscillations at SSO range, and 150 Hz, limits disturbance propagation through the DC link, and improves both transient and steady-state damping. The frequency-domain responses analysis establishes a comprehensive framework for understanding and mitigating dynamic coupling in MMC–HVDC networks, supporting the stable integration of large-scale offshore renewable energy systems. © 2026 The Authors

title: Strength-plasticity synergic and low-thermal-resistance sapphire/Cu joints via ultrafast laser micro-welding with intermediate Cu2O nanolayer
abstract: High-quality interfacial bonding between sapphire and Cu is crucial for effective thermal management in power electronic modules. In this work, ultrafast laser micro-welded sapphire/Cu heterostructures with synergetic strength-plasticity and low thermal resistance have been achieved by introducing an intermediate Cu2O nanolayer. The spatially confined ultrafast laser-ablated plasma is strategically regulated by this nanolayer, which activates the inert sapphire surface and tailors a multi-mechanism interfacial micro-nano architecture. The resulting joint features an interlayer composed of amorphous Al2O3, CuAlO2, and embedded Cu nanocrystals, effectively mitigating residual stress and material incompatibility. Concurrently, Al2O3 nano-anchors extending from the base material provide abundant binding sites, facilitating robust mechanical interlocking between sapphire and Cu. The shear strength of the joint with the Cu2O nanolayer reaches 121.1 ± 3.3 MPa, representing an 11.1% improvement over joints welded without the oxide layer. A remarkable 270.1% increase in shear displacement is also achieved, accompanied by ductile fracture on the Cu side, indicating superior room-temperature plasticity. The welded heterojunction shows robustness against thermal cycling with strength deterioration below 21.6% after 500 cycles from −40 to 120 °C. Additionally, the interface exhibits good resistance to dye penetration and excellent interfacial thermal conductance, with a remarkably low thermal resistance of 1.89 ± 0.24 K mm2 W−1 at room temperature. This work demonstrates the feasibility of integrating metal-oxide heterostructures with superior mechanical and thermal properties via ultrafast laser micro-welding, showing great potential for application in advanced thermal management substrates. © 2026

title: Lightweight broadband transition-metal microwave absorbers synergistic engineering of multi-interfacial polarization and hollow conductive networks
abstract: Collaboratively constructing a three-dimensional hollow conductive network and multiple interface polarizations can simultaneously enhance the conductive loss and polarization relaxation efficiency, which is an important direction for the research and development of lightweight, wide-band, and high-performance electromagnetic wave absorption materials. Transition metal sulfides have attracted much attention due to their adjustable electronic structure and excellent intrinsic conductivity. However, single-component materials have shortcomings such as a lack of polarization sites and insufficient continuity of the conductive network, making them difficult to meet the requirements of practical applications. This study proposes a stepwise preparation strategy of etching, modification and sulfidation, using cobalt-nickel Prussian blue-like analogues (CoNi-PBA) cubes as the precursor, and preparing morphologically controllable hollow CoNi-PBA cubes by regulating the ammonia water etching time; subsequently, in situ growing NiFe layered double hydroxide (NiFe-LDH) nanosheets on the surface to construct a CoNi-PBA@NiFe-LDH core-shell structure; finally, using thiourea as the sulfur source, through hydrothermal sulfidation treatment, obtaining the CoNi-PBA@NiFe-LDH/FeNiS4 composite material. The final test results show that the prepared CoNi-PBA@NiFe-LDH/FeNiS4 series composite materials have a minimum reflection loss of −56.6 dB and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 7.04 GHz, demonstrating excellent microwave absorbing performance. This study provides a new strategy for constructing high-performance microwave absorbing materials with multiple interface polarizations and hollow conductive networks, further deepening the understanding of the structure-performance relationship, and has very important significance for promoting the practical engineering application of transition metal-based absorbing materials. © 2026

title: Risk governed early warning prognostics for high-voltage substations: calibration and alarm burden aware validation on field telemetry (Badra Oil Field)
abstract: High-voltage substations in oil-and-gas facilities experience high-impact degradation processes whose weak supervisory signatures can evade conventional threshold alarms while amplifying operator workload. Although physical failure events are rare, the supervised target in this study is an actionable horizon-based degradation label rather than an instantaneous rare-failure indicator. This paper presents a decision-grade, horizon-aware prognostics framework for the Badra Oil Field 120 MW GTPP network using 1-min SCADA/IED telemetry. A leakage-safe protocol applies causal windowing (W=48min), horizon labeling (H=24min), and boundary decontamination via a purge gap G≥W+H=72min, followed by probabilistic calibration and governed alarming (τ*=0.05, cooldown=6h). Models spanning RF/GB/SVM/DNN/LSTM and a stacked ensemble are assessed jointly in discrimination, calibration (ECE/Brier), and alarm-burden sustainability (false alarms/day, event recall, and lead-time). The resulting risk trajectories support auditable escalation under drift and operational label imbalance. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Convolutional tensor completion-based DSSE under high DER penetration and abnormal measurements
abstract: Unlike transmission systems with sufficient observability and complete network information, distribution networks face persistent challenges such as noisy measurements, limited observability, and incomplete or uncertain topology. Traditional distribution system state estimation (DSSE) methods rely heavily on explicit network models (that is, feeder connectivity and line parameters), whereas existing canonical polyadic (CP)-based tensor completion approaches are limited by purely multilinear representations under distributed energy resource (DER)-related operating variability and measurement anomalies. To address these challenges, this paper proposes ConvCP, a self-supervised tensor completion framework for DSSE in which convolutional learning is embedded within the CP decomposition structure and operates without explicit network models. The method captures nonlinear dependencies through refined factor matrices and improves DSSE accuracy and robustness under diverse missing data scenarios, high levels of DER penetration, abnormal measurements, and suboptimal choices of tensor rank. Furthermore, given the high cost and limited deployment of phasor measurement units (PMUs) in distribution networks, the proposed approach is evaluated under limited-observability conditions with sparse voltage phasor measurements and less stringent phase-angle accuracy requirements than PMU-class measurements. Extensive studies are conducted on an IEEE 123-bus system and a realistic low-voltage distribution network to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. © 2026 The Authors

title: Similarity-based strategic data allocation for robust PD defect identification in MV cable terminations
abstract: This paper investigates overfitting caused by overly idealized datasets that fail to capture real-world variability. Four common installation defects in underground cable terminations—improper overlapping of the stress control tube, voids within the insulation layer, carbon tracking on the insulation surface, and irregular edges of the outer semiconductive layer—were physically simulated. Three samples of each defect were fabricated to preserve inherent physical variations. Partial discharge (PD) signals were acquired and transformed into unipolar and bipolar phase-resolved PD (PRPD) patterns. A Residual Neural Network (ResNet-18) was employed for feature extraction and classification. By performing image similarity analysis to strategically allocate training datasets, the model effectively overcomes high intra-class variability, particularly in irregular edge defects. The results demonstrate that bipolar PRPD patterns provide superior diagnostic features compared to unipolar patterns, enabling the optimized ResNet model to improve classification accuracy from 69.81% to 96.50%. This study validates a highly robust, non-intrusive diagnostic framework suitable for practical condition monitoring of field-installed cable terminations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Multi-energy load forecasting based on dynamic relationship awareness and spatio-temporal graph neural networks
abstract: Accurate integrated energy load forecasting plays a critical role for the efficient power consumption and market transaction execution for nowadays power systems; Yet the field suffers from 2 critical drawbacks, (1) non-sufficient consideration of complex spatio-temporal dynamic correlation between load and meteorological information; (2) non-consideration of anomalies itself of the given data. In order to tackle the above shortcomings, in this paper we put forward a dynamic relation perception based load forecasting model with spatio-temporal graph neural networks, where the developed dynamical low-rank multi-head attention mechanism for complex load dynamics can specifically focus on the most vital information for different time-step nodes and spatial nodes accordingly, leading the model to a strong prediction performance. Moreover, to enhance robustness and stability, this work proposes a learnable anomaly feature process module which can detect anomalous data and use learnable weights for processing it, as a result, it can effectively reduce information loss. The comprehensive experiments of the DLR-DHC model on the Arizona State University Tempe Campus Integrated Energy System data shows that prediction accuracy of the proposed model surpasses most existing models across most metrics and prediction time frames. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Deep reinforcement learning-based model-free voltage regulation in an active distribution network using demand-side flexibility aggregation
abstract: The integration of distributed energy resources is challenging the operational stability of low-voltage distribution networks, leading to frequent voltage fluctuations that conventional devices, such as on-load tap changers (OLTCs) and capacitor banks, struggle to manage under dynamic and varied operating conditions. Voltage regulation in active distribution networks typically relies on accurate network models for optimization or on reactive-power support from inverter-based resources, which can be difficult to deploy in community-scale settings with limited observability. This paper presents a real-time, model-free voltage regulation framework that uses only residential active-power demand-side flexibility and a single-point voltage measurement at the point of common coupling, without requiring the network topology, line parameters, or reactive-power actuation for online execution. The proposed adaptive droop learning framework follows a centralized-training distributed-execution architecture: a Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) coordinator maps PCC voltage deviations to aggregate flexibility requests and learns to dynamically allocate them across load buses by learning implicit voltage–power sensitivity structure from data without explicit sensitivity calculations. Distributed SAC bus-agents disaggregate allocated requests into appliance-level setpoints using XGBoost-based flexibility bounds and a quadratic-programming feasibility layer to enforce device constraints and satisfy dynamic grid response requirements. Experimental validation on an RTDS with an IEEE 13-bus radial distribution system demonstrates 88.5% voltage compliance within a ± 10 V band, a 73% reduction in OLTC operations, and 96.9% flexibility-tracking accuracy, outperforming TD3, DDPG, and PPO baselines. The results indicate that low-observability, model-free voltage regulation is feasible for practical distribution feeders. © 2026 The Authors

title: Spatiotemporal distribution and statistical characteristics of lightning activity before and after the construction of 345 m UHV large-span transmission towers based on LLS Data
abstract: Ultra-high-voltage (UHV) large-span transmission towers are characterized by large structural height, long span length, and complex overhead ground-wire systems. Their construction may affect the local distribution of lightning flash locations and the statistical characteristics of lightning current parameters. In this study, two UHV large-span towers, N6750 and N6751, in the Chizhou–Tongling section were selected as the case study. Based on Lightning Location System (LLS) data from 2004 to 2025, a statistical framework including spatial filtering, kernel density estimation, trend testing, and distribution difference testing was established. The lightning stroke distribution, lightning frequency, current amplitude, and polarity before and after tower construction were compared. The results show that lightning flash density was redistributed after tower construction, with a decrease in the middle region of the crossing span and an increase near the two tower bodies. This suggests that the ultra-tall towers and their overhead ground-wire system may have modified the local lightning attachment pattern. The LLS-estimated current distribution also shifted toward higher amplitudes: the mean current amplitude of negative cloud-to-ground flashes increased from 20.4 kA to 38.0 kA, and the proportion of high-current events increased. In addition, more positive lightning records were observed after tower construction. These findings provide observational support for lightning performance assessment, grounding-system thermal stability evaluation, and differentiated operation and maintenance of UHV large-span transmission lines. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Computationally efficient oscillation stability analysis of large-scale renewable power systems via partitioning
abstract: With the increasing penetration of large-scale renewable generation, inverter-induced oscillations pose significant threats to the secure operation of modern power systems, creating an urgent need for efficient oscillation stability analysis. However, conventional analysis methods become computationally expensive for large-scale systems due to the large number of connected devices and the complex network topology, which together result in high-order system models. To address this issue, this paper proposes a partition-based oscillation stability analysis method. A fast partitioning algorithm is developed to decompose the original system into smaller subsystems, thereby reducing computational complexity. A dynamic equivalent method is further introduced to represent the external areas of each subsystem. The consistency between the oscillation modes of the partitioned subsystems and those of the whole system can be maintained. Case studies on practical systems verify that the proposed method achieves agreement with whole-system analysis results while significantly improving computational efficiency, demonstrating its feasibility for extremely large-scale power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Short-term load forecasting using an improved PatchTST model with time–frequency feature fusion
abstract: To address the challenges of strong nonlinearity, non-stationary fluctuations, and multi-scale coupling in short-term power load forecasting, this paper proposes MSTF-PatchTST, a novel time–frequency feature fusion model built on the PatchTST framework. The model consists of a wavelet transform convolution (WTConv) frequency branch, a multi-scale temporal convolution (MSTCN) time branch, an improved PatchTST-based encoder, and a feature fusion prediction module. Specifically, the frequency branch captures periodic and multi-scale spectral characteristics through discrete wavelet decomposition and convolutional feature extraction, while the time branch learns local fluctuations and long-term trends via multi-scale temporal convolutions and patch-based global dependency modeling. Subsequently, the representations from both branches are adaptively fused and mapped to the forecasting targets through the TCFNN-based prediction head, enabling effective complementarity between time-domain dynamics and frequency-domain periodicity. Experiments on the Tetouan City power consumption dataset across 1–3 day rolling forecasting horizons demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms GRU, LSTM, TCN, Transformer, Informer, TimesNet, Autoformer, FEDformer, and iTransformer in terms of MAE, RMSE, MAPE, and R2. The predicted load trajectories closely follow the ground-truth series across all tested horizons, demonstrating both high accuracy and robust generalization as the forecasting horizon extends. © 2026

title: Diffusion characteristics of SF6 decomposition products in typical structural units of 500 kV GIL equipment
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) induced by insulation defects in gas-insulated transmission lines (GILs) during operation can lead to SF6 decomposition and generate a series of characteristic gases, whose diffusion behavior directly affects the effectiveness of equipment fault detection and early warning. This paper investigates the diffusion characteristics of H2S, SO2, and CF4 in linear GILs under continuous and transient fault conditions. The results indicate that H2S diffuses the fastest and provides the most sensitive warning response. Under continuous fault conditions, the diffusion effect is mainly manifested as an increased warning delay, whereas under transient fault conditions, it is mainly reflected in enhanced concentration attenuation. Compared with the point at x = 1 m, the maximum SO2 concentration at x = 49 m decreases by approximately 99.4%. The initial inlet concentration not only affects the fault warning delay but also determines the spatial range over which an alarm can be triggered. Larger equipment configurations increase the risk that characteristic gases may fail to trigger alarms effectively in the later stage of a fault. In practical detection, concentration thresholds should be dynamically optimized according to equipment dimensions. Gases with larger diffusion coefficients and higher concentrations, such as SO2, should be utilized as early warning gases, while incorporating other characteristic fault gases to improve fault discrimination accuracy. The results provide a theoretical reference for optimizing characteristic gas detection and fault early-warning strategies in GILs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Subsynchronous resonance analysis in large wind farms: a probabilistic approach incorporating wake effects and wind uncertainty
abstract: Subsynchronous resonance (SSR) in large wind farms is strongly influenced by aerodynamic uncertainty and wake-induced flow distortions—two factors that conventional deterministic studies often neglect. This paper introduces a probabilistic SSR assessment framework for a doubly-cage induction generator (DCIG)-based wind farm connected to a series-compensated transmission line. The proposed approach explicitly incorporates wind speed uncertainty modeled via a joint Weibull–von Mises distribution, multiple wake interactions captured through a multi-wake aerodynamic model, a six-mass drivetrain, and equivalent collector cable impedance. New probabilistic SSR indices are defined to quantify damping degradation, resonance amplification probability, and the likelihood of critical SSR modes under stochastic conditions. Small-signal eigenvalue analysis, participation factors, frequency scanning, and electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations validate that SSR risk is a probabilistic outcome governed by wind variability, wake topology, and network characteristics. Incorporating wake interaction and collector cable impedance increases the SSR instability risk index by 22–29% and the severity index by 57–62% compared with idealized no-wake, no-cable conditions for regular and irregular wind farm layouts. The collector cable X/R ratio is identified as a key determinant: a higher ratio reduces effective damping and shifts the critical series compensation threshold lower, amplifying both instability probability and severity. Moreover, the proposed probabilistic method substantially outperforms deterministic approaches, closely matching actual-value post-analysis with markedly lower error. A fuzzy C-means clustering-based approach reduces computational burden by over 85% compared with full Monte Carlo simulation while preserving accuracy, making large-scale or real-time probabilistic SSR assessment practical for wind farm planning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Constructing In–O bond charge transfer channels in defective In2S3 via CQDs derived from waste biomass for enhanced photocatalytic antibiotic removal
abstract: Rational design of interfacial chemical bonds is crucial for reducing charge transfer barriers in heterojunction photocatalytic materials, yet this remains a challenge. Herein, we report a novel CQD/In2S3 heterojunction with interfacial In–O bonds, fabricated via an in-situ reaction between biomass-derived carbon quantum dots (CQDs) and sulfur-vacancy-rich In2S3 nanosheets. Experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm the formation of In–O bonds between oxygen atoms on the CQD surface and coordinatively unsaturated indium sites in In2S3, which provide fast channels for interfacial electron transfer. In addition, an ohmic contact is formed between CQDs and In2S3, and the resulting internal electric field drives the transfer of photogenerated electrons toward CQDs. As a result, the optimized catalyst exhibits a prolonged carrier lifetime of 1627.0 ps, as revealed by femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TA) spectroscopy, thereby promoting the efficient generation of superoxide radicals and holes. Consequently, the catalyst achieves a tetracycline (TC) removal efficiency of 81.5% within 60 min, with a kinetic rate constant of 0.107 L mg−1 min−1, outperforming defective In2S3 by a factor of 2.1. Based on theoretical and experimental findings, three possible TC removal pathways are proposed. This work provides an effective interface engineering strategy for the design of metal sulfide-based heterojunctions and enables the high-value utilization of waste biomass in photocatalytic materials. © 2026

title: Impulse transient characteristics of a long vertical grounding conductor under various triggered-lightning discharge processes
abstract: Lightning grounding performance depends strongly on the temporal characteristics of the injected current, yet field evidence comparing different lightning discharge processes remains limited. This study examines the impulse transient behavior of a 24-m-long vertical grounding electrode during artificially triggered lightning, with particular focus on initial continuous current pulses and return strokes. Synchronously measured lightning current and ground potential rise from two triggered-lightning events were analyzed, including five initial continuous current pulses and ten return strokes. Impulse grounding resistance was evaluated from the corresponding peak voltage and current values and compared with the measured power-frequency grounding resistance. Results show that, during the initial continuous current pulses, the mean impulse grounding resistance represented an average reduction of 29.45% from the power-frequency value. In contrast, the return strokes produced an average increase of 26.76% relative to the power-frequency one. Although impulse grounding resistance generally decreased with increasing peak current for both discharge processes, the two groups remained clearly separated. The contrasting behavior is attributed to competition between the inductive response of the long electrode under steep current fronts and the resistance-reducing effect of soil ionization during slower, broader pulses. Findings here demonstrate that transient grounding performance should account for the complete lightning-current waveform. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Elastic PBO nanofiber/rGO aerogels with MPa-strength for infrared-radar compatible stealth
abstract: Mechanical robustness is essential for the long-term service of infrared-radar compatible stealth aerogels. Reduced graphene oxide (rGO) aerogels possess excellent electrical properties, yet their practical application is constrained by insufficient mechanical strength. In this work, we fabricated a poly-p-phenylene benzobisoxazole (PBO) nanofiber/rGO aerogel with an ultralow density of 18.15 mg cm–3 via supercritical drying. The incorporation of rGO significantly enhances the compressive resilience of the aerogel. The resulting aerogel exhibits a compressive strength of 1.28 MPa at 90% strain and retains 97.8% of its original strength after 1000 compression cycles, thereby overcoming the conventional trade-off between high strength and elasticity. Furthermore, the aerogel also demonstrates outstanding thermal insulation performance with a low thermal conductivity of 20.5 mW m–1 K–1, as well as promising electromagnetic wave absorption (EMA) properties, delivering a minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of –41.57 dB at a thickness of 2.4 mm and an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 6.29 GHz. © 2026

title: Quantifying hydrophobicity migration threshold time of composite insulators based on dynamic contact angles under coupled temperature and humidity
abstract: In this paper, a novel hydrophobicity migration threshold time characterization method is proposed on the basis of dynamic contact angle time series analysis, which aims to evaluate the performance of composite insulators after contamination and moisture absorption. Corresponding tests under six combined temperature-humidity environments were performed on artificially contaminated specimens, and a double-exponential empirical model was adopted for quantitative kinetic fitting. Coupled with molecular dynamics (MD) simulation results, the microscopic action mechanisms underlying temperature and humidity influences on hydrophobicity migration through contamination layers were systematically revealed. Furthermore, a continuous threshold time prediction model was constructed, which lays a reliable quantitative foundation for scientific decision-making in power system operation and maintenance in heavily polluted areas. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Hierarchically porous silicon oxide ceramic coatings for synergistic thermal insulation and radiative heat dissipation
abstract: Efficient thermal management under extreme heat flux remains a challenge in aerospace, electronics, and energy systems, requiring materials that maximize radiative heat dissipation while minimizing thermal conduction. Here, inspired by the hierarchical hair structure of camels, we develop a 575 μm-thick amorphous porous SiO2-based coating on the aluminum alloy substrate via an ultrafast (180 s) plasma-assisted oxidation strategy to achieve radiative heat dissipation and thermal insulation. The coating exhibits a high broadband infrared emissivity of 0.95 and an ultralow thermal conductivity of 0.23 W m−1 K−1. The exceptional combination of radiative heat dissipation, thermal insulation, and superior ablation resistance arises from the hierarchical and multiscale design. At the macroscale, a roughened SiO2 outer layer with elevated specific surface area enhances infrared radiation. At the microscale, the porous amorphous SiO2 network effectively suppresses thermal conduction, while Si-O vibrational modes enhance radiation. Meanwhile, the Al2O3/mullite inner layer ensures thermal expansion compatibility and mechanical integrity. Under a 1373 K propane flame, the coating limits the backside temperature to 706 K after 60 s, demonstrating outstanding thermal insulation performance. Furthermore, it maintains structural integrity after 9000 W/cm2 laser irradiation for 60 s, exhibiting robust resistance to extreme thermal and laser environments. This work provides a strategy for synergistic improvement of radiative and conductive thermal management in extreme environments, which can be applied in fields such as aerospace, space exploration, electronics, and sensing. © 2026

title: Chemical doping and crystal-facet engineering synergistically enhanced resistivity and piezoelectricity in Bi4Ti3O12 high-temperature ceramics
abstract: The low resistivity (ρ) and inferior piezoelectricity of bismuth layer-structured Bi4Ti3O12 (BIT) ferroelectrics hinder their application in high-temperature electromechanical coupling. To address this challenge, a synergistic strategy combining W6+/Nb5+/Zr4+ heterovalent co-doping with crystal-facet engineering is proposed. This dual modification elevates the high-temperature resistivity by nearly an order of magnitude (∼106 Ω cm at 540 °C) and yields a large piezoelectric coefficient (d33 = 40.8 pC N−1) together with a considerable Curie temperature (TC = 653 °C). Furthermore, the modified ceramic exhibits excellent thermal stability, maintaining a low d33 fluctuation (∼16%) at RT-540 °C alongside high ρ (>106 Ω cm). The enhanced resistivity is attributed to the widened bandgap and suppressed oxygen vacancies brought by W6+/Nb5+/Zr4+ co-doping. The improved d33 originates from the fine domains with flexible polarization caused by the local structural heterogeneity. Crucially, the crystal-facet engineering approach exposes the highly active polar pseudo-perovskite (a-axis) facets of the ceramic grains. This exposure effectively releases the clamping effect from the insulating (Bi2O2)2⁺ layers, dramatically facilitating domain switching and further amplifying the piezoelectric contribution of the fine domains. This work establishes a broad applicability for unlocking the full potential of bismuth layer-structured piezoceramics. © 2026

title: Synergistic heterointerface engineering and atomic Co-Nx coordination doping in carbon-intercalated MXene for enhanced electromagnetic wave absorption
abstract: Heterointerface engineering and atomic doping are recognized as core strategies for the development of high-performance electromagnetic wave-absorbing (EMA) materials. However, traditional heterostructures frequently exhibit deficiencies in interface continuity and inadequate polarization. Herein, a Co-Nx coordination-doped carbon-intercalated MXene composite (CoSA@MX/C) was successfully fabricated via a coordination anchoring-pyrolysis strategy. The carbon-intercalated heterointerface provides abundant Co anchoring sites, while Co-Nx coordination configurations introduce numerous dipolar polarization centers. Co-Nx atomic coordination and interfacial charge redistribution synergistically enhance interfacial polarization, dipole polarization, and defect-induced polarization, and effectively balance the dielectric and magnetic responses of the composite, further optimizing its impedance matching. The CoSA@MX/C composite achieves an outstanding minimum reflection loss of −54.42 dB at only 1.72 mm. Density functional theory calculations show that uniformly dispersed Co-Nx doping disrupts the local symmetry of the electronic structure, thereby increasing the electrical conductivity loss and enhancing electromagnetic wave absorption performance. This work establishes a novel paradigm for synergistic regulation of heterointerface engineering and atomic coordination doping, thus providing a critical reference point for the design of novel EMA materials. © 2026

title: Effect of additive diffusion on radial differences in thermal aging characteristics of XLPE in high-voltage AC cables
abstract: Thermal aging of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) in high-voltage cables threatens its operational reliability, and the increase in insulation thickness leads to radial non-uniform degradation. In this regard, this paper investigates the effect of additive diffusion on radial performance degradation during thermal aging at 135 °C. The results show that both types of cables exhibit obvious radial non-uniform degradation. The outer layer, with a high initial cross-linking density and good insulation performance, is preferentially affected by thermal-oxidative aging, undergoing post-crosslinking followed by thermal scission. The middle and inner layers have slightly lower initial performance than the outer layer, and their degradation phenomenon lags behind that of the outer layer during thermal exposure. The diffusion of antioxidants and DCP, as well as its correlation with XLPE performance degradation, was revealed through molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and microstructural characterization. It is found that the migration ability of antioxidant in XLPE is restricted as the cross-linking degree increases, and they tend to combine with oxygen. Antioxidants in the middle layer diffuse outward, compensating for the rapid oxidation effect in the outer layer. The diffusion behavior of DCP is weakly dependent on the cross-linking degree, and it induces post-crosslinking reactions. The non-uniform diffusion of additive molecules leads to a time lag in post-crosslinking and thermal scission reactions among different layers, thereby causing a multi-level effective threshold decrease and nonlinear changes in breakdown strength. The above findings provide a basis for revealing the radial degradation mechanism of XLPE in coaxial-structure cables under thermal-oxidative aging. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Mn powder-assisted interfacial reaction engineering for high-performance FeCoNiCrMn HEA-SiC brazed joints: Microstructure, properties and mechanism
abstract: Reliable joining of SiC ceramics to metals is a critical technical approach to expand the engineering applications of SiC. However, the brazing of SiC and metals has long been plagued by three fundamental challenges: poor wettability of liquid metals on SiC, uncontrolled formation of brittle intermetallic compounds, and large residual stresses induced by thermal mismatch. In recent years, face-centered cubic (FCC) structured high-entropy alloys (HEAs) such as FeCoNiCrMn have exhibited exceptional high-temperature mechanical properties, good ductility, and a thermal expansion coefficient well-matched to SiC due to their unique “cocktail effect”, making them ideal structural materials for joining with SiC ceramics. The multiple active elements dissolved from the HEA can promote the wetting of SiC, but uncontrolled dissolution of the HEA will lead to more complex interfacial reaction issues. To address the above problems, this study proposes a novel strategy for indirectly controlling the interfacial reaction on the ceramic side by pre-placing homologous elements to regulate the dissolution of the base metal. The results show that the addition of Mn powder alters the dissolution mode of the HEA, enabling precise regulation of the active elements dissolved into the filler metal. An ordered gradient compound layer with the sequence of Ni2Si/Mn3Ni2Si/Ni16Cr6Si7 from the SiC side to the brazing seam is formed on the SiC interface. This multilayer structure transforms the crack propagation from straight propagation along the Ni2Si layer to tortuous propagation across multiple compound layers, and the fracture mode changes from pure brittle fracture to ductile-brittle mixed fracture, significantly increasing the shear strength of the joint. This study provides a new idea and feasible technical strategy for the reliable joining of ceramics and high-entropy alloys. © 2026
