title: Enhanced prediction of reservoir porosity and permeability via a Second Spectrum-inspired hybrid framework integrating LSTM, Random Forest, and SHAP
abstract: Accurate prediction of reservoir porosity and permeability from wireline well logs remain a central challenge in subsurface characterization, owing to the nonlinear, non-stationary, and spatially autocorrelated nature of petrophysical data. This study presents the Second Spectrum Dual-Pathway Framework, a novel hybrid machine learning architecture conceptually adapted from the NBA Second Spectrum spatiotemporal player-tracking system, which separates macro-level spatial patterns from micro-level sequential dynamics. Applied to 12,101 well-log samples from the Southeastern Sichuan Basin (8 input features: GR, AC, CAL, CNL, DEN, SP, RXO, PE), the framework integrates two complementary learning pathways: Pathway 1 deploys a Random Forest (RF) regressor (n = 200 trees, max_features = √p, min_samples_leaf = 4) as a macro-level, point-wise nonlinear mapper, achieving R2 = 0.8619, MAE = 0.1772, and RMSE = 0.3003 for porosity, and R2 = 0.8357, MAE = 0.0728 (log10 scale) for permeability. Pathway 2 employs a two-layer Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM; 64 and 32 units, dropout = 0.25, L2 = 10−4, Layer Normalization) trained on RF residuals to model depth-axis sequential autocorrelation — a mechanism physically justified by Durbin–Watson statistics < 1.5 across all logs, confirming strong positive stratigraphic continuity. The hybrid combination (ŷ_hybrid = ŷ_RF + ε_BiLSTM) yields R2 = 0.8620, MAE = 0.1773, and RMSE = 0.3002 for porosity, demonstrating that the BiLSTM residual pathway captures depth-trending prediction errors unresolved by the spatial model alone. Five-fold cross-validation confirms stable generalization across geological intervals (porosity: mean R2 = 0.8696 ± 0.0116; permeability: mean R2 = 0.8440 ± 0.0246). Ensemble-based prediction intervals (RF tree variance) achieve a 90 % PI empirical coverage of 98.97 %, with higher predictive uncertainty localized in high-permeability zones (mean σ = 0.1103 log10 mD) relative to tight matrix intervals (mean σ = 0.1857 log10 mD), consistent with heterogeneous pore network structures beyond wireline log resolution. Explainability is provided via Tree SHAP (RF) and GradientSHAP (BiLSTM): for porosity, the acoustic log (AC; mean |SHAP| = 0.1979) ranks first, followed by GR (0.0985), SP (0.0919), and DEN (0.0909), consistent with established density-porosity and sonic transit time transforms. For permeability, DEN and CNL retain dominance while RXO gains relative importance, reflecting pore connectivity encoded in flushed-zone invasion. Critically, the BiLSTM SHAP profile diverges from the RF profile depth-sensitive logs gain relative attribution in the sequential pathway confirming that the two pathways model complementary and physically distinct geological signals. The total training pipeline executes in approximately 149 s (RF: 18 s; BiLSTM: 131 s), with sub-second inference at deployment. The framework is directly integratable into petrophysical evaluation platforms (Techlog, Interactive Petrophysics) and supports uncertainty-aware population of 3D geomodels via P10–P90 permeability realizations. © 2026 The Authors. title: In‑situ synthesis of Ti2AlC MAX phase via laser-directed energy deposition for tailoring microstructures and mechanical properties of TiAl composites
abstract: The in-situ formation of the Ti2AlC MAX phase during laser-directed energy deposition (LDED) has attracted considerable interest for TiAl-based composites used in aero-engine components. However, the phase evolution induced by TiC precursor addition and its effects on microstructure and properties remain unclear. Herein, TiAl-xTiC (x = 0–30 wt.%) composites were fabricated by LDED. The initial addition of TiC promoted the in-situ formation of Ti2AlC, which accounted for 30.14 wt.%. Ti2AlC suppresses columnar grain growth, promotes equiaxed grains, refines microstructure, and reconstructs grain boundaries. The <001> texture is weakened, and local orientation gradients increase. Transmission electron microscopy reveals compatible Ti2AlC/TiAl interfaces and network‑like dislocation accumulation. Mechanical behavior is loading-mode dependent: Compressive strengthening is dominated by interface-induced dislocation strengthening, whereas flexural resistance is governed by crack deflection, bridging, and pinning by the Ti2AlC network, with the T3 (30 wt.% TiC) sample exhibiting the highest flexural strength (≈ 977 MPa). This work establishes a mechanistic framework linking (TiC precursor addition → Ti2AlC formation → microstructure/defect reconstruction → mechanical response) for designing MAX‑phase‑reinforced TiAl composites. © 2026

title: Development of a new recombineering system for Edwardsiella species
abstract: Edwardsiella species are important aquaculture pathogens that also cause opportunistic infections in humans, necessitating efficient genome editing tools to study their pathogenesis and develop control strategies. In this study, we identified and characterized six endogenous recombinases pairs from Edwardsiella and its phages. Among these, the BAS_MS17 system exhibited the highest recombination efficiency in E. piscicida EIB202Δp. Extending homology arms from 150 bp to 200 bp improved editing efficiency by 2-fold, while the addition of Redg or Plug further enhanced recombination by 3-fold and 2.5-fold, respectively, without compromising accuracy (100%). More importantly, when applied to E. piscicida sdu12S, Redg or Plug improved the editing efficiency by 8-fold and 7-fold, respectively. Deletion of the phage-derived single-strand binding protein (SSB) reduced efficiency to 25% of the BAS_MS17 level, whereas expression of the endogenous RecA-family SSB (rSSB) increased recombinant yield by 5-fold, highlighting functional conservation. Furthermore, SSB proteins from heterologous hosts failed to enhance recombination efficiency. Using the optimized system, we successfully knocked out ten distinct genes, including virulence-associated loci, with editing accuracy exceeding 85%. Phenotypic analysis revealed that luxR , but not the other tested genes, contributes to biofilm formation. Virulence evaluation results showed that aroA , fur , and hfq are critical virulence-associated factors. Collectively, this streamlined recombineering system provides a simple, rapid, and efficient genetic tool for Edwardsiella , supporting mechanistic studies of virulence and the development of live attenuated vaccine candidates. title: Heterogeneity, petro-fabric and petrophysical subdivision of the El Garia Formation (Ypresian, Tunisia): Implications for CO2 storage
abstract: Assessing and evaluating each reservoir suitability for carbon dioxide storage (CCS) prior to injection is crucial to ensure safe and long-term geologic carbon storage. Rock physics is a key technique in determining the CO2 storage potential of rock formations. Each assessment should start by understanding the microstructural heterogeneity of each reservoir. Microstructural and petrophysical studies of El Garia nummulitic limestone reservoir were carried out in order to: a) understand the heterogeneity of this complex reservoir and b) subdivide this formation into petrophysical levels in order to define the suitable levels for CO2 storage and c) define factors controlling the heterogeneity of microstructural and petrophysical properties and determine its interrelation as a neecessary step to assess suitability of the formation to host CO2. Microstructural observations, made on 24 thin sections under optical and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), identifies seven deposit facies. Porosity has been measured on seven samples by the triple weight method and estimated from the optical microscopy and SEM observations using JMicrovision software. After microstructural and reservoir characterization studies focusing on sedimentology, diagenesis, types of cement and porosity values and types, a petro-fabric zonation of El Garia reservoir was carried out identifying around four distinct levels based on these cited parameters. In the light of these results, a rock physics study was established. Electrical conductivity, P wave velocities, and anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility have been measured in five samples corresponding to these different levels of El Garia reservoir in order to delves into the microstructural and petrophysical subdivision, to determine the factor controlling the formation heterogeneity and its interrelation. Four parameters have been determined when studying the electrical conductivity (surface conductivity, formation factor, tortuosity and cementation exponent). Petrographical characteristics and petrophysical properties of the sample plugs indicate a correlation between these parameters, showing a microstructural and petrophysical heterogeneity of this reservoir. The results obtained for these electrical parameters show heterogeneity in the pore connectivity and in the arrangement of mineral crystals, particles and pores from one facies to another. The acoustic measurement results show that the vertical evolution of the acoustic velocity varies as a function of the diagenetic evolution and the internal microstructure of each facies of the El Garia Formation. The anisotropy study allows the definition of four acoustic fabric levels into the formation. © 2026 The Authors. Publishing services by Elsevier B.V. on behalf of KeAi Communications Co. Ltd. title: Strategy for enhanced production of A40926B0 in Nonomuraea gerenzanensis using an efficient CRISPR/AsCas12f1 system
abstract: The global emergence of vancomycin-resistant Gram-positive pathogens underscores the urgent need for efficient production of novel lipoglycopeptide antibiotics. Dalbavancin, a last-resort therapeutic agent, relies on its key biosynthetic precursor A40926B0, whose industrial manufacture is severely limited by the low yield of wild-type Nonomuraea gerenzanensis and inefficient genetic tools for this rare actinomycete. Here, we developed a high-efficiency CRISPR/AsCas12f1 genome editing system and applied systematic metabolic engineering to boost A40926B0 biosynthesis. First, conjugation conditions were optimized to elevate the transfer efficiency in N. gerenzanensis D11. The hypercompact AsCas12f1 nuclease showed markedly lower cytotoxicity than SpCas9 and enabled 100% gene deletion efficiency with preferred PAMs (TTTG, CTTG, GTTG). Second, we strengthened the shikimate pathway via multiple genetic strategies: overexpressing feedback-resistant DAHP synthase (aroG fbr ) and chorismate mutase/prephenate dehydrogenase (tyrA fbr ), as well as knocking out pheA . This manipulation blocks the phenylalanine synthetic branch and redirects metabolic flux toward the l -tyrosine branch. Third, we engineered the branched-chain fatty acid (BCFA) pathway via promoter replacement of bkdA2B2C2 , LipAB , fabF and deletion of acdH to enhance isododecanoyl side-chain supply. The combinatorial engineering yielded strain B-13, which produced 1740 mg/L A40926B0 in shake flasks. Finally, 50-L fed-batch fermentation with continuous maltodextrin feeding further increased the titer to 1817 mg/L, the highest reported titer to date. This work establishes a robust CRISPR editing tool for N. gerenzanensis and provides valuable engineering references for precursor-oriented strain improvement targeting lipoglycopeptide antibiotics, offering insights for the industrial scale production of A40926B0. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Transient three-phase short-circuit current calculation based on the dynamic phasor model for grids with high-penetration inverter-based resources
abstract: Due to the complex topological and control structures of inverter-based resources (IBRs), transient short-circuit current calculation of grids with IBRs currently relies mainly on electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation. However, EMT simulation usually requires detailed modeling and a small simulation step, which limits its application in rapid transient-current feature extraction. In this paper, a transient short-circuit current calculation method for three-phase faults in grids with high penetration of IBRs is proposed based on the dynamic phasor (DP) model. The IBR is represented as a stage-separated nonlinear time-varying current source, in which low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) strategy, current limitation, voltage outer-loop saturation, PLL dynamics, current-loop dynamic response, and staged LVRT activation are considered. DP models of IBRs and conventional grid components are then established and solved using the weighted trapezoidal method. The proposed method is intended to extract system-level transient current features, including the current envelope, peak value, peak time, and DC component, rather than switching-frequency electromagnetic transients. Validated by numerical examples, the proposed method achieves satisfactory accuracy compared with EMT simulation while significantly reducing the computation time. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Dual-seed induction of cross-linked reinforced corncob enables graphite-like subcrystalline carbon for high-performance sodium storage
abstract: Graphite-like subcrystalline carbon (GLSC) is a promising anode material for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), featuring nearly parallel carbon sheets with expanded interlayer spacing and few defects, in contrast to the disordered structure of hard carbon. However, converting low-grade biomass like corncob into GLSC is hindered by the structural collapse of the precursor during pyrolysis. Herein, we overcome this limitation by engineering an epoxy resin-reinforced corncob powder composite, where hemicellulose-derived voids are in situ infiltrated and cross-linked by epoxy network during curing. The composite is then processed in a dual-seed graphite induction: the graphite crucible acts as a macro-seed to confine the precursor, while surface-loaded graphite powder serves as a micro-seed to ensure conformal top-surface coverage, collectively establishing a continuous topological pathway from surface to interior and yielding GLSC. The resultant GLSC features an expanded (002) spacing of 3.70−3.96 Å and minimal defects, enabling reversible Na+ intercalation. Consequently, it delivers a high initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.8%, a reversible capacity of 305.6 mAh g−1, and a long low-potential plateau in a half-cell at 20 mA g−1, which translates to full-cell metrics, delivering an ICE of 86.5%, a discharge capacity of 273.5 mAh g−1, a high-potential plateau ratio of 77.3%, and an energy density of 227.6 Wh kg−1 at 50 mA g−1. © 2026

title: Amorphous zirconia supported on nickel foam for efficient catalytic oxidation of ventilation air methane
abstract: Ventilation air methane (VAM) is the largest source of coal mine methane emissions, and its efficient catalytic oxidation requires low-cost catalysts with high sulfur tolerance. Herein, an amorphous zirconia catalyst in-situ grown on nickel foam (a-ZrO2/NF) was developed, exhibiting exceptional activity, robust hydrothermal stability, and excellent resistance to sulfur poisoning. The a-ZrO2/NF catalyst achieves a T90 of 398 °C and maintains robust activity with only 3% loss of methane conversion in 50 h. The catalyst also presents superior sulfur tolerance and water resistance under simulated VAM conditions. The excellent catalytic performance stems from the unique structural characteristics of a-ZrO2, such as optimal mesoporous structure, high specific surface area, increased surface oxygen vacancies, and high oxygen mobility. Synchrotron-based spectroscopy further reveals strong interfacial electronic interaction between amorphous ZrO2 and NiO, facilitating lattice oxygen activation. DFT calculations further confirm that the disordered amorphous surface of a-ZrO2 provides significantly stronger methane adsorption sites compared to the crystalline phase, effectively polarizing C–H bonds for easier activation. This work provides valuable insights into the design of low-cost, sulfur-resistant catalysts for VAM mitigation and other industrial applications. © 2026

title: Generalized error bounds in the recovery of solitary wave profiles
abstract: We investigate the robustness of Constantin’s explicit reconstruction formula for two-dimensional irrotational solitary water waves. This formula recovers the free-surface profile from the dynamic pressure trace at the bed and depends on both the wave speed and the undisturbed depth. We consider simultaneous perturbations in these three quantities and derive an L 2 error estimate for the reconstructed profile. The proof uses the hodograph transform, holomorphic extension arguments, and Paley–Wiener Fourier-decay estimates, yielding stability estimates with sublinear dependence on the perturbation size. We include numerical computations to illustrate the effects of specifically designed perturbations. © 2026 The Author.

title: Electromagnetic and temperature field analysis of a 20 MW-class wind turbine generator with slot-opening internal evaporative cooling
abstract: To address the stator-winding heat-dissipation bottleneck in high-power offshore wind turbine generators, this study proposes a slot-opening internal evaporative cooling scheme for a 19 MW permanent-magnet synchronous generator. A hollow 316 stainless-steel heat-conducting tube is embedded near each stator slot opening, enabling near-source heat removal through the phase-change latent heat of a low-boiling insulating working fluid. Electromagnetic analysis shows that the 240 tubes introduce only 6.2 kW of additional eddy-current loss, while the air-gap flux-density waveform and harmonic spectrum remain essentially unchanged. A quarter-unit multi-parallel-branch evaporative cooling test platform was then constructed with 1:1 fidelity in single-tube geometry and thermal boundary conditions, reproducing the heat-input and flow-distribution characteristics of the prototype. Experiments over heat loads of 500–700 W confirmed stable heat-transport capability, and an equivalent evaporative heat-transfer coefficient of approximately 4901 W/(m²·K) was derived at the 600 W design condition. Three-dimensional thermal simulations show that, under air and water cooling alone, the maximum winding temperature reaches 142.23 °C, corresponding to a temperature rise of 117.23 K. After evaporative cooling is introduced, the maximum temperature decreases to 122.17 °C and the temperature rise to 97.17 K, representing a relative reduction of 17.1%. Meanwhile, the hotspot shifts from the axial mid-section to the winding ends, indicating a redistribution of the dominant thermal resistance. These results demonstrate that the proposed scheme effectively strengthens near-source heat removal, alleviates the winding thermal bottleneck, and improves overall thermal performance while exerting negligible influence on the generator's electromagnetic characteristics. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Spray-assisted evaporative crystallization of conformal drug-encapsulated MOF coatings on macroporous substrates for infected wound healing
abstract: Constructing metal-organic framework (MOF) coatings on macroporous substrates is important for translating MOF functions into practical biomedical materials, but nonuniform crystal growth and pore narrowing remain common challenges. Herein, we developed a sequential spray-assisted evaporative crystallization strategy to prepare MOF coatings on selected macroporous substrates. ZIF-8 and CuBDC were grown on filter paper, nonwoven fabric, and chitosan quaternary ammonium salt/polyvinyl alcohol (HP) aerogel, and the HP-based aerogels retained highly accessible scaffold macroporosity under the selected conditions. ZIF-8/HP was further used as a drug-loading platform for in situ curcumin (CUR) incorporation, yielding CUR-ZIF-8/HP with a CUR loading content of (4.3 ± 0.2)wt.% and an encapsulation efficiency of (68.5 ± 2.1)%. Structural characterization supported retained ZIF-8 crystallinity and successful CUR incorporation. CUR-ZIF-8/HP exhibited pH-responsive CUR release, antioxidant activity mainly associated with CUR incorporation, antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, low hemolysis, acceptable cytocompatibility, and enhanced HaCaT cell migration. In an infected murine wound model, CUR-ZIF-8/HP promoted bacterial reduction and wound repair. This work provides a complementary strategy for constructing drug-loaded MOF coatings on macroporous biomedical substrates. © 2026

title: Tailoring strength-ductility synergy in Mg alloy thin sheets via asymmetric extrusion and two-stage cross rolling: The effect of hot rolling temperature
abstract: Mg alloy thin sheets have broad application prospects, but conventional rolling processes often fail to achieve both high strength and ductility, and the scope for property optimization is limited. In this work, ZE21B Mg alloy thin sheets with a thickness of 0.2 mm were fabricated by asymmetric extrusion combined with two-stage cross rolling. The effect of hot rolling temperature (350, 400, and 450 °C) on the final microstructure and mechanical properties was investigated. The results show that the asymmetrically extruded sheet exhibits fine equiaxed grains and a weak basal texture, providing a favorable microstructure for subsequent rolling. As the hot rolling temperature increases, the grain size of the hot rolled sheets grows from 7.75 to 48.76 μm. Under the same subsequent warm rolling and annealing conditions, the sheet hot rolled at 350 °C undergoes pronounced recrystallization, forming a mixed structure of recrystallized and deformed grains with high dislocation density, achieving an elongation of 28.03% ± 2.1% and an ultimate tensile strength of 356.7 ± 5.3 MPa. In contrast, recrystallization is strongly suppressed in the sheets hot rolled at 400 and 450 °C, and the microstructures are dominated by irregular dislocation walls and regular sub-grains, respectively, resulting in the ultimate tensile strength increasing to 387.6 ± 4.3 and 405.3 ± 6.9 MPa, respectively, but the elongation dropping to 18.60% ± 1.3% and 6.50% ± 2.6%. Simply by adjusting the hot rolling temperature, the strength and ductility can be continuously adjusted, enabling on-demand tailoring of mechanical properties within a certain range. © 2026

title: Periodic cavity-induced dielectric response enhancement enabling magnetic metal alloy@N-doped bamboo-like carbon nanotubes with broadband absorption and corrosion protection
abstract: Effective modulation of dielectric response serves as the key to enhancing electromagnetic wave absorption performances (EMWAPs), while a periodical hollow cavities (PHCs) structure provides an ideal material platform to achieve this goal. This study leverages metal (Fe/Co/Ni)-nitrilotriacetic acid chelate precursors and dicyandiamide (DCD) as a bifunctional carbon/nitrogen source to propose a simple synthesis strategy for preparing metal alloy@N-doped bamboo-like carbon nanotubes (N-BLCNTs) featuring PHCs magnetic/dielectric composites (MDCs). Simultaneously, adjusting the pyrolysis temperature, categories of initial reactants, and DCD content allows the precise regulation of graphitization degree, kind, and electromagnetic parameters for the resulting MDCs. Benefiting from the optimized dielectric response and magnetic/dielectric synergy regulated by the PHCs, together with the interfacial polarization, the CoNi@N-BLCNTs exhibit outstanding corrosion resistance and EMWAPs with an effective absorption bandwidth of 7.80 GHz and a minimum reflection loss of −58.62 dB. In summary, this work provides a scalable and versatile platform to develop the desirable novel microwave absorbers featuring broad bandwidth, strong absorption, and environmental adaptability. © 2026

title: Degradable PLA/PBAT/ZnO@SiO2 composite film with micro/nanostructures for breathable, antibacterial, and thermally regulated medical protection
abstract: Medical protective films are crucial for public health, yet traditional materials often compromise wearer comfort and pose significant environmental challenges due to their non-degradable nature. Herein, a biodegradable and multifunctional composite film is fabricated via micro-extrusion roll forming, composed of a polylactic acid (PLA)/poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) matrix featuring surface and interface micro/nanostructures. The surface micro/nanostructures and interconnected microporous interface endow the medical protective film with a water vapor transmission rate of 203.47 g m−2 h−1, ensuring excellent breathability and wearing comfort. The synergistic effect of uniformly dispersed ZnO@SiO2 nanoparticles and the surface micro/nanostructures achieves an antibacterial rate of 97.69% and effectively inhibits contaminant adhesion. Furthermore, the micro/nano structures and micropores are engineered to manipulate radiative properties, resulting in a passive cooling effect with a surface temperature approximately 10 °C lower than that of commercial fabrics. Crucially, addressing the critical issue of plastic pollution, the film exhibits excellent biodegradability through enzymatic, composting, and alkaline pathways, offering a sustainable solution that mitigates the secondary environmental pollution caused by conventional medical films. This work provides a feasible strategy for the scalable production of next-generation medical protective materials that seamlessly integrate wearable comfort, high performance, and environmental sustainability. © 2026

title: DSCR-mediated recrystallization pathway control enabling strength-ductility-conductivity balance in a heterostructured Cu-Sn alloy
abstract: Balancing strength, ductility, and electrical conductivity remains challenging in Cu alloys because conventional strengthening approaches often increase electron scattering and compromise ductility. Here, a Cu-0.1Sn alloy was subjected to dynamic offsets and shear force adjustment cryorolling (DSCR) followed by annealing to regulate recrystallization and heterostructure formation. Compared with the symmetrically rolled and annealed sample, the DSCR-annealed (DSCRA) sample exhibits an earlier recrystallization onset and faster apparent recrystallization kinetics. This behavior is reflected in its lower softening temperature (594 versus 610 K) and apparent activation energy for recrystallization (113.1 versus 126.4 kJ/mol). After annealing at 598 K, DSCRA develops a partially recrystallized heterostructure comprising recrystallized soft domains and retained hard lamellar domains, some of which contain locally preserved deformation nanotwins. DSCRA also exhibits weaker rolling-texture inheritance and greater orientation dispersion, consistent with a recrystallization pathway involving competition among multiple orientations. DSCRA achieves an ultimate tensile strength of 401 MPa and a uniform elongation of 11.1% while maintaining an electrical conductivity of 87.6% IACS. The favorable property balance is associated with plastic accommodation by the soft domains and strength retention by the hard lamellar domains. Locally retained deformation nanotwins provide additional strengthening, while interactions between the soft and hard domains promote strain partitioning and hetero-deformation-induced hardening. Recovery and partial recrystallization concurrently help reduce defect-induced electron scattering. These findings indicate that regulating the initial deformation state and subsequent recrystallization pathway offers a route to tailoring the strength-ductility-conductivity balance of dilute Cu-Sn alloys. © 2026

title: A TeLU-enhanced deep learning approach for state-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Accurate estimation of the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries is critical for ensuring the safety and reliability of electric vehicles (EVs). However, existing methods often face challenges in real-world applications, particularly in accurate capacity calibration, robust feature extraction, and effective modeling of complex degradation patterns. To address these issues, this study proposes a comprehensive SOH estimation framework based on real-world operational data collected from EVs across diverse geographical regions. First, reliable SOH pseudo-labels are generated by coupling the reverse ampere-hour counting technique with the forgetting factor recursive least squares (FFRLS) algorithm to mitigate the interference of real-world data fluctuations. Second, both time-domain and time-frequency domain features are extracted, with the latter derived through the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to fully leverage complementary degradation information. The core innovation of this paper lies in the comprehensive framework integration of dual-domain feature engineering and deep network design. Within this framework, the pioneering application of the Tangent Exponential Linear Unit (TeLU) activation function serves as a critical enabling component, which significantly improves the nonlinear representation capability and effectively resolves the gradient oscillation problems of conventional activations. Furthermore, a deterministic perturbation-based analysis method is introduced to quantitatively evaluate feature importance, thereby improving model interpretability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively handles real-world data challenges, achieving a MAE below 1.43% and a RMSE under 1.80%, demonstrating superior accuracy and stability compared to the implemented baseline models in strict cross-vehicle generalization tests. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) and Research Skill Development (RSD) in Science Education in Higher Education: A Delphi-Based Model
abstract: This study developed and validated a science learning model integrating Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) with the Research Skill Development (RSD) framework to strengthen students’ research skills. A two-round Delphi study was conducted with experts to establish consensus on the model. The first round generated a conceptual synthesis through qualitative thematic analysis, while the second evaluated expert agreement using Aiken’s V. Experts reached strong consensus on the model structure, the central role of science, integration of the engineering design process, contextual problem-based learning, and progressive research stages. The proposed model has high content validity and provides a systematic framework for developing research skills, supporting student independence, and strengthening research-oriented science learning across higher education contexts. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

title: Digital Renewal of University Education: Barriers, Opportunities, and Contributions to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
abstract: The digital transformation of higher education creates opportunities and challenges, particularly in crisis-affected countries such as Ukraine. This study examines the effectiveness of digital educational technologies and their contribution to sustainable higher education. The study combined a literature-based analysis with a three-month pedagogical experiment involving 64 university students. The findings highlight the potential of online platforms, blended learning, artificial intelligence, gamification, and immersive technologies to support motivation, learning outcomes, personalization, and inclusiveness in higher education. However, limited digital competence, unequal infrastructure, insufficient funding, cybersecurity risks, and fragmented strategies remain barriers. The study proposes an integrated digital renewal framework combining technological, organizational, and pedagogical dimensions. This framework primarily supports sustainable development goals through innovation, inclusion, resilience, and partnerships. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

title: Characterization of two key cytochrome P450 enzymes in Isodon amethystoides and de novo production of 3α,15β-dihydroxy-ent-kaurene in yeast
abstract: Glaucocalyxin A (GLA), a well-known ent- kaurene diterpenoid, has emerged as a high-value bioactive natural product in pharmaceutical research owing to its potent and broad-spectrum activities. To date, its total synthesis has proven extremely challenging due to poor yield and intricate routes, and the biosynthetic pathway of GLA remains poorly understood. Herein, we identified two enzymes, IamCYP71D761 and IamCYP706V18, in Isodon amethystoides , which specifically mediate the C3α- and C15β-hydroxylation of ent- kaurene with high stereoselectivity and regioselectivity, respectively, generating 3α,15β-dihydroxy- ent- kaurene ( 3 ), a key precursor in the biosynthesis of GLA. In addition, we established an efficient de novo biosynthesis platform for 3 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae . Briefly, high-efficiency isozyme screening, protein engineering, increased acetyl-CoA synthesis, and copy number enhancement were applied to the ent- kaurene biosynthesis module. Subsequently, promoter optimization, competitive pathway knockout, and electron transfer optimization were introduced, resulting in production of 3 to 24.0 ± 0.2 mg/L in shake flask. In summary, this work highlights the pivotal roles of IamCYP71D761 and IamCYP706V18 in the heterologous biosynthesis of 3 , offering valuable insights for the further pathway reconstruction and de novo production of GLA, GLB, and other ent- kaurene diterpenoids. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Autocorrelation-based protection for active distribution networks using current direction and magnitude change detection
abstract: This paper presents a current-based protection method applicable to various operating conditions of distribution networks, including radial and meshed topologies, as well as scenarios with penetration of distributed generation. The proposed approach is based on two key criteria: changes in current direction and current magnitude. These criteria are extracted solely from instantaneous current measurements by calculating the autocorrelation between each current cycle and its preceding cycle using a sliding window. In lines where bidirectional current flow is possible, a change in current direction at one end of the line serves as a criterion for faulted area identification. Conversely, in line with unidirectional current flow, changes in the average absolute value of the current magnitude act as an effective criterion for identifying the faulted area. The method was validated through two case studies: a simple ring network and a complex radial-meshed distribution network representing a portion of Sirjan city's distribution system in Iran. Simulations were performed in MATLAB/Simulink environment. The results confirm the accuracy and robustness of the proposed method across different operating scenarios. The method successfully identifies the faulted area with high precision, requiring at most one‑quarter cycle of newly acquired current data. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Cross-attention augmented U-Net for surrogate prediction of inter-electrode magnetic field distribution in vacuum circuit breaker
abstract: To address the high computational cost of magnetic field simulation in vacuum circuit breakers, a cross-attention augmented U-Net (UCA-Net) for fast and accurate prediction of inter-electrode magnetic field distributions is proposed in this paper. First, a dataset for a representative 27.5 kV class vacuum interrupter is generated using finite element method, including structural geometric parameters, spatial coordinates, and the corresponding magnetic field distributions in the target region. Then, these two types of features are encoded separately and fused through a cross-attention mechanism, enabling effective interaction between structural information and field-domain coordinates. And the fused features are subsequently fed into an improved U-Net backbone to predict the magnetic field distribution in the inter-electrode region. In addition, the key training settings, including batch size, loss function and optimizer, are investigated to determine the model configuration. Comparative results show that the proposed UCA-Net outperforms the conventional U-Net in prediction accuracy, while reducing the computation time for a single case from 165.0 s with finite element simulation to 86.0 ms, corresponding to acceleration of approximately 1900 times. Moreover, the maximum prediction error is maintained within 10.0 mT, and the average relative error in the inter-electrode region is below 3.0%. The proposed method provides an efficient data-driven tool for the rapid design and performance evaluation of the investigated 27.5 kV level vacuum circuit breaker. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Toughening strategies for additively manufactured ceramics: A multiscale review of mechanisms and process-structure-property relationships
abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) enables the fabrication of complex ceramic components unachievable by traditional methods. However, AM process-induced defects aggravate ceramic brittleness, the core bottleneck restricting its industrial application. Existing reviews on AM ceramic toughening have three critical unaddressed gaps, including no quantitative criterion to distinguish synergistic toughening from linear additive effects, no clear mapping between AM process constraints and multi-mechanism synergy compatibility, and no systematic summary of synergy failure mechanisms, negative cases, and research pitfalls. To fill these gaps, this review establishes a unified academic definition and quantitative evaluation system for multiscale synergistic toughening of AM ceramics, assesses the compatibility between toughening mechanisms and mainstream AM processes, dissects core synergy coupling mechanisms and quantifies their efficiency, analyzes synergy failure boundaries and industrialization bottlenecks, and proposes a phased, industry-aligned technical roadmap with quantifiable milestones to guide full-cycle engineering application of high-toughness AM ceramics. © 2026

title: Influence and modeling of transmission line construction on ground flash density
abstract: Previous studies of lightning attraction have mainly focused on isolated tall structures, which can be approximated as point-like objects. Ultra-high-voltage (UHV) transmission lines form continuous elevated corridors, for which conventional point-source models are inadequate. Using 14 years of Lightning Location System (LLS) observations, this study examines changes in local lightning activity associated with the ±800 kV BJ UHV direct-current transmission line. A grid-based normalization method and a line-source lightning-attraction model were developed to compare lightning parameters before and after commissioning.Within 3 km of the line, cloud-to-ground (CG) flash density increased by 6.5%, with the increase decaying nonlinearly with horizontal distance. Return-stroke multiplicity and mean peak current increased by 6.8% and 7.3%, respectively, while the proportion of return strokes exceeding 40 kA increased by 11%. These current-related changes also weakened with distance from the line.Three spatial patterns of CG flash-density change were identified: rise–slow decay, rise–rapid decay, and rise–polarity reversal. Their differences were associated with aerosol concentration, topographic position index, large-scale terrain, and LLS location uncertainty. By extending lightning-attraction analysis from isolated point structures to a linear UHV corridor, this study introduces a line-source lightning-attraction model for transmission lines and links distinct lightning-density responses to environmental and observational factors. The results provide a basis for spatially differentiated lightning-protection design for UHV transmission systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Electronic and interfacial water regulation in Ti-modulated NiFe oxide for industrial current density bifunctional water splitting
abstract: Developing efficient and durable bifunctional electrocatalysts is of great importance for large-scale green hydrogen production via anion exchange membrane (AEM) water electrolysis. Herein, a Ti-regulated NiFe-based oxide catalyst (NiFeTiOX) is constructed on nickel foam through an impregnation-assisted in situ precursor growth and annealing strategy. Owing to Ti incorporation, NiFeTiOX exhibits an optimized local electronic structure, abundant oxygen vacancies, a reduced work function, and a reconstructed interfacial water microenvironment. Atomic-scale characterizations and spectroscopic analyses reveal that Ti incorporation induces local lattice distortion, regulates the electronic states of Ni/Fe sites, and enriches defect-related oxygen species on the surface. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations further demonstrate that Ti promotes a more ordered interfacial water arrangement and a stronger hydrogen-bond network, thereby facilitating interfacial charge transfer as well as OH− adsorption and migration. NiFeTiOX has excellent bifunctional hydrogen evolution reaction/oxygen evolution reaction performance, requiring only 328 and 384 mV overpotentials at 1000 mA cm−2, respectively, while operating stably for 500 h. In addition, when this bifunctional catalyst is assembled into an AEM electrolytic cell, only 1.6 V is required to maintain a current density of 1000 mA cm−2 at 80 °C. This work offers a promising strategy for designing transition-metal-regulated NiFe-based oxide electrocatalysts with high current capability, excellent stability, and high efficiency. © 2026

title: Distributed adaptive event-triggered secondary control for electricity-hydrogen coupled microgrid
abstract: The integration of a high proportion of renewable energy sources and electricity-hydrogen coupling units significantly increases the dynamic complexity of islanded microgrids. Traditional centralized secondary control suffers from issues such as single-point failures and heavy communication burdens, while existing distributed cooperative control strategies commonly rely on continuous communication, leading to inefficient resource utilization. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a distributed cooperative secondary control method for electricity-hydrogen microgrids based on an adaptive event-triggered mechanism. First, a nonlinear large-signal model is established for each inverter-based distributed generator and its coupled electricity–hydrogen interface. Then, input–output feedback linearization is applied to the fast electrical subsystem of each DG, while the hydrogen-side dynamics are retained as bounded slow-varying perturbations. Subsequently, an adaptive event-triggering scheme is introduced for each unit, in which the triggering threshold is dynamically adjusted according to the system state. Communication with neighboring units and control updates occur only when local state variations exceed the triggering condition. The asymptotic stability of the overall system is rigorously proven using Lyapunov theory, and Zeno behavior is excluded. Simulation studies conducted on a four-node islanded microgrid with electricity-hydrogen coupling units demonstrate that the proposed method achieves dynamic and steady-state performance comparable to periodic sampling control, while reducing communication events by >88.1%, thereby significantly alleviating communication and computational burdens. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Photovoltaic generation forecasting for newly-built sites based on transfer learning with global adversarial and local contrast learning
abstract: Accurate photovoltaic (PV) generation forecasting is vital for efficient renewable energy integration and operation. However, the newly-built PV sites are constrained by insufficient training data. To overcome the above limitation, a global adversarial and local contrastive learning-based spatial-temporal forecasting algorithm (GL-STNet) is proposed in this paper. First, ST-Net is constructed for both source and target domains to comprehensively model the spatial-temporal characteristics of PV generation. Then, the global adversarial network is designed to learn domain-invariant feature representations through discriminator, and to effectively alleviate the issue of domain shift. Moreover, the local contrast learning is devised to effectively capture local key features by optimizing sample similarity relationships, and compensate for potential local information loss caused by global alignment. Finally, experimental results demonstrate that the proposed GL-STNet algorithm significantly improves forecasting accuracy for newly-built PV sites with scarce data. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Cellular-reaction pretreatment enabled 950 °C rolling of TiAl alloy sheet: Achieving exceptional strength-ductility synergy
abstract: In this work, we report a cellular-reaction-assisted strategy that enables successful rolling of a Ti-44Al-1.5Cr-0.5Re (at.%) alloy sheet at 950 °C while achieving an exceptional strength-ductility synergy. The cellular-reaction-derived pearlite-like microstructure contains discontinuously dispersed β0 phase, abundant phase interfaces, and pre-existing planar defects. During rolling, these microstructural features promote lamellar bending, interfacial separation, defect accumulation, and particle-stimulated nucleation-assisted recrystallization, leading to an ultrafine near-γ microstructure with an average γ grain size of 0.84 μm after 80% reduction. The rolled sheet exhibits a room-temperature tensile strength of 1378 MPa with 1.42% elongation, mainly owing to ultrafine-grain strengthening and deformation-induced stacking faults, twins, and 9R/long‑period stacking‑ordered-related structures. At 800 °C, the alloy shows a tensile strength of 476 MPa and an exceptional elongation of 283%. This superior high-temperature ductility originates from the cooperative deformation of the heterogeneous microstructure, where coarse γ grains provide strain hardening, fine γ grains accommodate deformation through grain-boundary-mediated processes, and boundary discontinuous dynamic recrystallization governs flow softening. These results highlight cellular reaction as an effective route to reconcile low-temperature rollability with strength-ductility synergy in TiAl alloy sheets. © 2026

title: Interfacial charge-driven hydrogel enables self-sustained Fe redox cycling for synergistic therapy of infected wounds
abstract: Chronic wound infections by drug-resistant bacteria remain challenging due to biofilms, oxidative stress, and impaired immunity. Here, we report an interfacial charge-driven hydrogel that enables a light-assisted self-sustained redox cycling for the efficient therapy of infected wounds. By integrating MXene/FeCu-MOFs heterojunctions into the sulfonated chitosan hydrogel (M/M-SCS@Gel), a built-in electric field induces directional charge redistribution and continuous interfacial electron transport across the heterojunction. This process continuously regenerates catalytically active Fe2+ from Fe3+, thereby overcoming the kinetic limitations of Fe2+ depletion and sustaining Fenton-like reactions for persistent reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Notably, MXene-mediated photothermal conversion accelerates electron transfer and redox kinetics, amplifying ROS under NIR irradiation. This synergistic effect enables efficient eradication of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) through ROS generation and Fe2+-mediated catalytic effects, while simultaneously promoting M2 macrophage polarization, angiogenesis, and collagen deposition. These findings demonstrate that the antibacterial mechanism of M/M-SCS@Gel is associated with transcriptomic signatures of translational stress and proteostasis imbalance, including inhibition of ribosome assembly and disruption of translation initiation, which ultimately leads to a translational-metabolic imbalance between amino acid biosynthesis and protein synthesis. This work establishes an interfacial charge-driven therapeutic strategy that integrates self-sustained redox catalysis with immune modulation, providing a broadly applicable strategy for treating pathogen-infected wounds. © 2026

title: In-situ SEM/DIC analysis of crack propagation path selection in TiAl/Ti2AlNb laminated composites: Pre-notch positioning dictates the fracture toughness in three-point bending tests
abstract: TiAl/Ti2AlNb laminated composites were fabricated by vacuum hot-pack rolling, forming three distinct interfacial regions: brittle regions I (βo + α2 + γ + ω) and II (βo/B2 + α2 + ω), and ductile region III (O). Multiscale characterization combining digital image correlation and in-situ three-point bending tests revealed that the laminated composites exhibit a 2.0–2.5-fold improvement in fracture toughness compared with monolithic TiAl alloy. This enhancement arises from the synergy between intrinsic and extrinsic toughening mechanisms. The intrinsic toughening is associated with slip deformation of B2 grains in the Ti2AlNb layer and grain-boundary obstruction to crack propagation, whereas the extrinsic toughening originates from interfacial crack branching in regions I and II, together with crack deflection and blunting in region III. Furthermore, the critical role of the pre-notch position was emphasized. When the notch terminates in the Ti2AlNb layer, interfacial crack branching effectively alleviates stress concentration, increasing KQ to 40.2 MPa m1/2. Conversely, when the notch terminates in the TiAl layer, rapid crack initiation caused by the low damage tolerance of TiAl triggers premature structural instability, reducing KQ to 29.5 MPa m1/2. These findings provide guidance for interfacial design and toughening optimization of TiAl-based laminated composites. © 2026

title: Gradient nanostructure promoting protective oxidation and suppressing dissolution corrosion of 9Cr ODS steel in oxygen-saturated LBE
abstract: Oxide dispersion-strengthened (ODS) steels are promising structural materials for lead-cooled fast reactors, but their corrosion resistance in liquid lead-bismuth eutectic (LBE) is governed by the competition between protective oxide-scale formation and metal dissolution. Here, a gradient nanostructure (GNS) surface layer was introduced on 9Cr ODS steel by ultrasonic surface rolling processing (USRP) to regulate this competition. Corrosion tests were conducted in oxygen-saturated LBE at 650 °C for up to 500 h. The GNS layer, characterized by gradients in grain-boundary density and geometrically necessary dislocation density, facilitated the rapid formation of a protective oxide layer at the early stage of corrosion, with a formation rate markedly higher than that of the untreated sample. After 500 h, the USRP-treated sample developed a compact multilayer scale consisting of Fe3O4, Fe3−xCrxO4, and Cr2O3, with a dispersed Si-O-rich amorphous phase, with a total thickness of 8.90 ± 1.23 μm. By contrast, the untreated sample exhibited pronounced dissolution attack, with a Cr-depleted zone of 9.80 ± 1.40 μm. The enhanced corrosion resistance is attributed to the defect-assisted short-circuit diffusion of Cr and Si in the GNS layer, which promotes rapid oxide nucleation and the formation of a Si-O-rich amorphous phase/Cr2O3 composite barrier at the oxide/substrate interface. This barrier may contribute to the integrity of the inner oxide scale and the stability of the oxide/substrate interface, thereby shifting the corrosion mode from dissolution-dominated degradation to protective oxidation. These results demonstrate that GNS provides an effective surface-design strategy for improving the LBE corrosion resistance of ODS steels. © 2026

title: In-situ photo-patternable ZnO via dual-functional surface engineering strategy for high-resolution QLED devices
abstract: Benefiting from the adjustable emission spectrum, high color purity, wide gamut, and solution-processability, quantum dot light-emitting diode (QLED) is considered one of the most promising next-generation display technologies. As a prevalent electron transport material, ZnO plays a crucial role in enhancing the efficiency and long-term stability of QLED devices. To promote the development of high-resolution QLED displays, this study proposes a dual-functional surface engineering strategy for achieving in-situ photo-patternable ZnO with enhanced electrical properties. Physicochemical characterization revealed that surface defects of ZnO were significantly reduced via direct photolithography, thereby decreasing non-radiative exciton recombination at the QD/ZnO interface. Particularly, the red QLED devices based on photolithographic ZnO exhibited remarkable performance, achieving a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 23.5%, a brightness of over 140,000 cd m−2 at 5 V, and an alleviated positive-aging effect (i.e., anomalous brightness increase). Concurrently, the operational lifetime T95 (the time for the device luminance to drop to 95% of its initial value) was also improved from 1,036 h to 2,084 h. Furthermore, by modulating the morphology of ZnO films, we successfully fabricated pixelated QLED devices, laying the technical foundation for commercializing high-resolution QLED displays. © 2026 Chinese Society of Metals

title: Real-time pricing strategy for photovoltaic prosumer communities based on a bi-level optimization in coupled electricity and carbon markets
abstract: The coordinated operation of electricity and carbon markets is crucial for low-carbon power system transition. This paper proposes a bilevel real-time pricing framework for photovoltaic (PV) prosumer communities in coupled electricity-carbon markets. The upper-level Electricity-Carbon Regulation platform determines internal electricity and carbon prices to minimize its net settlement and residual balancing cost, considering internal settlement with prosumers and external balancing transactions. The lower-level prosumers maximize welfare by optimizing electricity consumption under logarithmic utility, subject to PV generation and carbon-allowance/emission constraints. The bilevel model is transformed into a single-level nonlinear program using Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions and solved by the augmented Lagrangian method. Numerical results show that the proposed strategy achieves the highest prosumer welfare among all considered pricing schemes, while maintaining a relatively low level of carbon emissions, thereby demonstrating the superior economic–low-carbon performance of coordinated electricity–carbon pricing. Cluster-level applicability analysis, Monte Carlo perturbation tests, and sensitivity analyses further verify the computational tractability and robustness of the proposed mechanism. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Fast phase selection method for low frequency transmission system of offshore wind power
abstract: Traditional phase selection method is influenced by control strategy of double-side converters in Low-Frequency Transmission System of Offshore Wind Power, resulting in reduced reliability and difficulty in adaptation. Aiming at to the above issues, proposes a transient fault phase selection method suitable for LFTSOWP. Then, a reasonable frequency range for traveling wave analysis is selected, and a phase-selection method based on the Generalized S-Transform using the energy ratio of line voltage traveling waves is proposed. In addition, the positive and negative energy ratios of phase voltages are adopted as auxiliary criteria to solve the problem of identifying the faulty phase in phase-to-phase ground faults under a certain fault startup Angle. Finally, a typical LFTSOWP model is built in PSCAD/EMTDC. The verification results indicate that the proposed method can rapidly identify the fault phase, has good robustness. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Optimization of train operation for electrified railway considering source-load matching
abstract: To address the low local consumption and high operating costs caused by temporal mismatch between traction load and photovoltaic (PV) generation in electrified railways with distributed PV, this paper proposes a train operation optimization method considering source–load matching. The train operation process is simplified into a two-stage model (constant-speed traction and constant braking), and a multi-train power model incorporating regenerative braking energy balance is established based on average inter-station speeds. After analyzing the conflict between regenerative braking and source–load matching, a multi-objective optimization model is formulated with three objectives: source–load matching degree, total operation time, and system economy. Decision variables include departure time offsets, inter-station running time adjustment coefficients, and braking intensity adjustment coefficients. A differentiated braking intensity strategy is introduced to resolve the identified conflict. The NSGA-II algorithm is applied to obtain the Pareto-optimal timetable. Case studies using operational data show that the optimized timetable improves the local PV consumption rate by 20.5% over the baseline, and the variable braking intensity further reduces the traction system operating cost by 4.6% compared with the constant braking intensity under the same optimized timetable. These results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method in enhancing PV utilization and the coordinated use of regenerative braking energy. © 2026

title: Forecast-free coordinated TSO–DSO framework for day-ahead flexibility exchange
abstract: This paper presents a coordinated approach to provide power grid flexibility in cooperation with transmission system operator (TSO) and distribution system operator (DSO) in the context of day ahead (DA) electricity market. Considering the constraints of distribution network, the DSO submits an aggregated power–cost function using a non-iterative approach that substantially reduces the computational burden of the upstream market clearing, while preserving the essential economic characteristics of the distribution system. In this function, the costs of generations connected to distribution network are obtained by considering the uncertainties of renewable resources using a robust budget approach. This function, in fact, provides the TSO market operator with a range of active power along with their related costs. After the energy market clearing, the amount of power exchanged at the TSO-DSO connection point is notified to the DSO. Since the power-cost functions announced by the DSO are carried out taking into account the constraints of the DSO network, the market clearing results are always feasible, and the market no longer encounters the problem of infeasibility. The framework of the proposed coordinated market is such that the DSO does not need to forecast the upstream market price. The simplicity of the proposed market implementation increases the speed of market clearing and high adaptability to existing markets. The results from the simulation of the Nordic-60 Bus test network demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method well. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Vision-based monitoring of transmission line icing via generative augmentation and improved RF-DETR
abstract: Severe transmission line icing threatens power grid safety by causing conductor breakage and tower collapse. We propose an integrated deep learning-based monitoring framework. An ice coverage image generative adversarial network (IceGAN) is developed to synthesize high-quality samples, effectively mitigating data scarcity. Concurrently, an improved Roboflow Detection Transformer (RF-DETR) model, integrating Icing Feature Enhanced Attention (IFEA) and a Mixed-scale Feature Pyramid (Mix-FPN), is introduced to accurately detect slender lines and preserve topological continuity. Furthermore, an Inverse Perspective Mapping (IPM) algorithm is applied to correct geometric distortions. Experimental results over five repeated scene-level splits demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently and statistically significantly improves detection, segmentation, and thickness-estimation performance. The improved RF-DETR trained with the final augmentation strategy achieves 69.6 ± 0.8 % mAP50:95 and 85.5 ± 0.6 % Dice, significantly outperforming the RF-DETR baseline. The IPM-based calculation reduces the mean absolute thickness error from 3.42 ± 0.36 mm to 0.87 ± 0.11 mm and keeps the angular sensitivity error below 11.5 %. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Curvature-engineered dome-shaped TMD monolayers for tunable near-infrared photoluminescence
abstract: Strain engineering has emerged as a powerful approach to modulate the electronic and optical properties of two-dimensional materials without altering their chemical composition. Among these materials, transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have attracted significant attention due to their strong light-matter interactions and highly tunable band structures. Various strain-induced morphologies, including domes, grooves, and roll-ups, have been widely explored to achieve localized carrier confinement and exciton modulation. In particular, dome-like geometries formed in nanopillar-based architectures provide a versatile platform for engineering strain distributions and position-dependent optical responses. However, the electronic and excitonic properties of dome structures with large height-to-radius ratios and flattened apex geometries remain poorly understood. To address this limitation, we investigate dome-shaped TMD monolayers using a geometry-controlled model based on a Woods-Saxon-type height profile. We show that curvature engineering induces a transition between distinct carrier confinement regimes, leading to strong modulation of electronic states and excitonic transitions. This enables continuous tuning of photoluminescence across the near-infrared (NIR) spectrum, extending into the long-wavelength NIR region that is difficult to access using conventional material or compositional approaches. These findings demonstrate strong potential for broadband NIR technologies, particularly in the long-wavelength regime, establishing a tunable NIR emitter platform for deep-tissue imaging and optical communications. © 2026

title: AI-Driven Surrogate Modeling and Inverse Design of Type-II Superlattice Infrared Detectors
abstract: The conventional design of Type-II superlattice (T2SL) infrared detectors relies on iterative physics-based simulations, which can make broad exploration computationally costly. Here, we develop an AI-driven surrogate workflow for InAs/GaSb T2SL detectors. Two separately trained Transformer regressors with the same layer-token architecture predict dark-current-density curves and quantum-efficiency (QE) spectra from layer thicknesses, doping concentrations, and operating temperature. On fixed held-out test sets, the dark-current model achieved a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.7332 A/cm2, mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 2.7913%, and coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.998103, while the QE model achieved an RMSE of 0.005104, MAPE of 1.6417%, and R2 of 0.999231. Controlled comparisons on identical data splits showed that the Transformer obtained the lowest RMSE and MAPE and the highest R2 for both targets relative to multilayer-perceptron and Random-Forest baselines. Using the two surrogates, we evaluated one million uniformly sampled candidates at 77 K and identified 83 structures meeting the target requirements: dark-current density below 5 × 10-6 A/cm2 at -1 V and mean QE above 56% over wavelengths from 3.03 to 3.42 μm. Six selected candidates were subsequently compared with Crosslight simulations. By combining surrogate prediction, high-throughput target-driven screening, and Crosslight simulation verification, this framework shifts T2SL detector design from repeated trial-and-error simulation toward intelligent prediction and verification, offering a practical route to accelerate the exploration of high-performance infrared detector structures. © 1995-2012 IEEE.

title: Ribosome engineering enhances genetic code expansion in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
abstract: Genetic code expansion enables the site-specific installation of noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) into proteins, but its limited efficiency in eukaryotes remains a major barrier to broader application. Here we establish a visual, plug-and-play screening platform to evolve 18S ribosomal DNA in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and identify ribosomal variants that improve ncAA incorporation. The best-performing strain, designated ribo-hyper, increased ncAA-dependent GFP production by 2.9-fold relative to the wild-type rDNA strain and enhanced incorporation across distinct orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs. Characterization of ribo-hyper showed that global translation activity and cellular growth were moderately reduced. Proteomic analysis further revealed changes in amino acid biosynthesis, translation-related proteins and stress-response pathways, indicating that the engineered ribosome reshapes cellular translation homeostasis. Perturbation of translation quality-control pathways, including the ribosome-rescue factors Dom34 and Hbs1 and the core mRNA exosome component Ski6, reduced ncAA-containing protein output, whereas disruption of ribosome quality-control factor Rqc2 had little effect. These findings support a role for ribosome rescue and associated mRNA turnover in efficient ncAA incorporation in the ribo-hyper strain. Together, our results establish eukaryotic ribosome engineering as a viable strategy for improving genetic code expansion in yeast. Copyright © 2026. Publishing services by Elsevier B.V.

title: Grain boundary segregation engineering via in-situ TiB2 formation for enhanced mechanical properties in additively manufactured AA2024 alloys
abstract: The non-equilibrium solidification that occurs during additive manufacturing (AM) of Al-Cu-Mg alloys typically results in hot cracking and compromised mechanical properties due to their wide solidification range. Here, a grain boundary segregation engineering (GBSE) strategy is developed through the in-situ formation of TiB2 nanoparticles during laser-powder bed fusion, effectively enhancing both printability and mechanical performance of AA2024. The in-situ TiB2 nanoparticles not only promote the formation of a refined equiaxed grain structure with a high density of high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs), but also induce a semi-coherent interface between TiB2 particles and the Al matrix. These microstructural evolutions facilitate segregation of Cu and Mg atoms towards grain boundaries (GBs), which contribute to the development of a continuous intermetallic network composed primarily of θ-Al2Cu and S-Al2CuMg phases. Such a network strengthens GB cohesion and suppresses the formation of intergranular liquid films, thereby mitigating hot cracking. Additionally, it serves as a barrier to GB sliding and dislocation propagation, enhancing microstructural stability and deformation compatibility. Consequently, the as-built TiB2/AA2024 composite achieves an ultimate tensile strength of ∼502 MPa and fracture elongation of ∼9.9%. This work offers new insights into microstructure engineering in AM, demonstrating the synergistic effects of in-situ nanoparticle formation and GBSE in achieving high-performance Al alloys. © 2026 Chinese Society of Metals

title: Critical review on hybrid models for state-of-charge estimation of lithium-ion batteries in wide temperatures
abstract: This paper systematically reviews state of charge (SOC) estimation methods for lithium-ion batteries, with a focus on wide-temperature-range and low-temperature applications. It analyzes the adaptability and limitations of various techniques, including direct measurement, model-based, data-driven, and hybrid strategies. The review shows that hybrid estimators can combine data-driven nonlinear representation with model-based state correction, thereby improving adaptability under low-temperature and dynamic conditions. In the focused temperature-compensated Radial Basis Function Neural Network-Unscented Kalman Filter (RBFNN-UKF) study, the maximum SOC error remained within 6.5% at -20 °C, while the low-temperature estimation error was reduced to about 17% of the conventional equivalent circuit model-Unscented Kalman Filter (ECM-UKF) baseline under the same test protocol. These results highlight the potential of temperature-aware hybrid estimation for battery management in cold environments. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Sustainable Dyeing of Cotton Fabrics with Papaver Rhoeas-Derived Anthocyanins: Impact of Mordant and Acid Types
abstract: T his study explored the eco-friendly application of natural dyes extracted from Papaver rhoeas petals for cotton fabric coloration. Due to growing environmental concerns, natural dyes are being considered as alternatives to synthetic dyes; however, they often suffer from low color strength and poor fastness. To overcome these challenges, this study examined how different mordanting methods, including pre-, meta-, and post-mordanting, a range of metallic and plant-based mordants, and various acid types influence dyeing performance. The petals of Papaver rhoeas contain anthocyanins, especially cyanidin-3-O-glucoside, which provide bright red to purple shades. The results showed that the mordanting method, acid type, and mordant type significantly affected color strength, shade, and fastness properties. Among the tested acids, citric and oxalic acids provided the most favorable dyeing performance, while meta-mordanting was the most effective method overall. Furthermore, natural mordants such as pomegranate rind, oak bark, and Juglans regia performed as well as or better than traditional metal mordants such as tin and iron. Pomegranate rind produced the highest color strength, while these bio-mordants improved color depth and durability. Overall, the study demonstrates that when appropriate mordanting methods, mordant types, and acid types are selected, Papaver rhoeas can be used as an effective and sustainable natural dye for cotton fabrics. © Institute for Color Science and Technology.

title: A Low Voltage Ride-Through control strategy for cascaded H-bridge photovoltaic grid-connected inverters considering asymmetric current injection under phase-to-phase short-circuit fault conditions
abstract: Cascaded H-bridge (CHB) photovoltaic (PV) grid-connected inverters offer strong application potential due to their modular design, multilevel output capability, and independent maximum power point tracking (MPPT) for each module. However, during three-phase operation, asymmetric grid voltage sags may induce real power reversal, resulting in energy accumulation in the DC-link capacitors, continuous voltage rise, and eventual overvoltage protection trips that force the inverter offline. Additionally, the current Low Voltage Ride Through (LVRT) standard requires inverters to inject unbalanced currents during grid faults to maintain voltage, which further exacerbates the real power reversal issue in CHB topologies. Accordingly, this paper takes a three-phase non-isolated CHB PV grid-connected inverter with independently controlled DC buses as an example and first examines the current LVRT requirements. Based on this analysis, a typical phase-to-phase short-circuit fault is selected to evaluate several control strategies for suppressing real power reversal. By integrating different control methods, the proposed approach effectively narrows the range of real power reversal during asymmetric faults. Experimental results validate that the proposed control strategy achieves excellent suppression performance and strong adaptability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Experimental Evaluation of the Effect of Combining a Two-Phase Nano-Composite Containing Al2O3 and NbC in a Surface-Coated Resin Matrix: a Study Based on Dielectric Losses and Radar Reflectance
abstract: Electromagnetic wave-absorbing polymer nano-coatings are recognized as important for advanced electromagnetic shielding and wave management applications. In this study, a novel two-phase Al2O3/NbC polymer nano-composite within an epoxy resin matrix is introduced, incorporating dual silane surface treatments (APTMS and GPTMS) to enhance interfacial bonding and ensure uniform dispersion of the reinforcing materials. A designed experimental (DOE) plan was implemented before the fabrication process to determine the optimal weight fractions of aluminum oxide (Al2O3) and niobium carbide (NbC). Subsequently, chemical bonding, particle surface modification, and matrix homogenization were performed, and the samples were prepared in rectangular molds suitable for electromagnetic rectangular wave guide measurements in the 8.2–12.5 GHz range. The structural and chemical characteristics were analyzed using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The results obtained from electromagnetic absorption and reflection measurements within the 8.2–12.5 GHz frequency range show that sample No.1, with a higher NbC content, demonstrates stronger absorption near 9.5 GHz but reduced performance at higher frequencies. Sample No.2, containing a balanced ratio of Al2O3 and NbC, exhibits a more uniform response across the frequency range, while sample No.3, with a higher Al2O3 fraction, presents improved impedance matching, enhanced dielectric loss, and absorption exceeding 80% throughout 8.2–12.5 GHz, accompanied by a reflection reduction of approximately 6%. These results indicate that tuning the weight fraction of the two phases allows optimization of broadband absorption performance. Overall, the dual-phase Al2O3/NbC system with surface-modified particles can achieve efficient, broadband electromagnetic absorption, offering potential for advanced shielding and wave control applications for aerospace industries. © 2026 Semnan University Faculty of Mechanical Engineering. .

title: Numerical Estimation of the Effective Mechanical Properties (EMP) of Steel AISI 4340 Fiber-Reinforced Concrete
abstract: This study aims to estimate the effective mechanical properties (EMP) of a composite material consisting of two phases: a concrete matrix and randomly distributed cylindrical fiber reinforcements. To determine the composite's effective mechanical properties, several key parameters are considered, including the fiber volume fraction, fiber geometry (expressed as the length-to-diameter ratio), and the void volume fraction. The voids are modeled as spherical inclusions, randomly dispersed within the matrix phase only, with strict non-intersection constraints, ensuring they do not overlap or touch the fibers. This configuration reflects realistic entrapped air porosity while preserving the integrity of the fiber-matrix interface. The effective elastic properties are estimated using a numerical homogenization procedure based on the finite element method (FEM) and the representative volume element (RVE) concept. Periodic boundary conditions (PBC) are applied to ensure representativeness, and a progressive mesh refinement strategy is employed, with a finer mesh around the inclusions, to balance accuracy and computational efficiency. The 3D fiber distributions are generated using a custom Python 3.9 script that enforces non-overlapping conditions between fibers, thereby preventing interpenetration during RVE construction. © 2026 Semnan University Faculty of Mechanical Engineering. .

title: Distance protection scheme for low frequency transmission system with offshore wind power: problems and solutions
abstract: Apparent impedances of conventional distance relays cannot reflect the fault distance correctly in low frequency transmission system (LFTS) since the uncertain phase relationship between local and remote currents makes the voltage drop across fault resistance unpredictable. This paper reveals the mechanism by which a widely used phase selectors based on sequence voltage angles mis-operates in LFTS and indicates that negative-sequence current is the sufficient condition to ensure selectors reliable. Then a distance protection is proposed to eliminate the effect of fault resistance. By means of zero-sequence network, distance protection for single-line-to-ground and line-to-line-to-ground faults can be designed as a source-agnostic scheme. As for line-to-line faults, a uniform calculation expression for fault distance is derived to cope with various control operations. A control-based distance protection for a symmetrical fault is proposed to make the angle of local current be consistent with that of remote current. Simulation tests prove the effectiveness and precision of the proposed distance protection. The above solutions are also applicable to systems consisting of 100% converter-based sources. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Optimal scheduling of droop-controlled islanded microgrid with mixed DERs considering voltage/frequency-dependent load models using fuzzy-grey wolf optimization
abstract: In an islanded microgrid (IMG), dispatchable distributed energy resources (DERs) are typically operated in droop control mode to satisfy real and reactive power demand, which results in permissible deviations in frequency and voltage from their nominal values. The actual power consumption of loads varies with voltage and frequency; however, the voltage- and/or frequency-dependent nature of loads have been neglected in most existing studies. In this work, droop-regulated combined heat and power (CHP) units, along with a solar photovoltaic (PV) system, wind turbine (WT) generator, battery energy storage system (BESS), and shunt capacitors, are optimally integrated into a 33-bus IMG to supply voltage and/or frequency-dependent loads. A multi-objective cost-emission optimization is formulated and analyzed for constant impedance (CZ), constant current (CI), constant power (CP), and composite (CZIP) load models under voltage- and/or frequency-dependent operating conditions. The uncertainties associated with PV and WT generation are modeled using probabilistic techniques, and a novel coordinated BESS charging-discharging strategy is implemented to compensate for PV power fluctuations. The proposed fuzzified grey wolf optimization (Fuzzy-GWO) technique is employed to solve the multi-objective problem, and its performance is benchmarked against Fuzzy-PSO and non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) methods. The results indicate that the system with frequency-dependent loads achieves lower cost and emission values compared to systems with frequency-independent loads. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
