title: Eliminating abnormal grain growth enabled by in-situ micro-alloying in friction stir welding of ultra-high Zn-containing Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloys
abstract: Abnormal grain growth (AGG) has long plagued Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloys produced by friction stir welding (FSW), making them unsuitable for post-welding heat treatment. Here, we propose an innovative wire-arc assisted FSW (WA-FSW) approach to realize in-situ Sc/Mn micro-alloying in 700 MPa-grade Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloys. Primary Al3(Sc, Zr) and Al6(Fe, Mn) particles are successfully introduced into the nugget zone of WA-FSW joints. These thermally stable particles exert strong Zener pinning pressure against grain boundary migration, thereby effectively suppressing AGG during subsequent heat treatment. After heat treatment, the nugget zone consists of submicron Al6(Fe, Mn) particles distributed along grain boundaries and high-density L12-ordered Al3(Sc, Zr) and η/η'-MgZn2 nanoprecipitates formed within fine recrystallized grains. The dense weld formation and homogeneous microstructures contribute to an excellent tensile strength of 640 MPa together with a favorable elongation of 8% in the heat-treated WA-FSW joint. Compared with existing solutions for AGG suppression, our strategy exhibits superiorities in terms of grain refinement, microstructural homogeneity, and mechanical property improvement. These insights provide new theoretical support for the controllable fabrication of high-performance welded joints through weld composition design, elevating the microstructure regulation of FSW joints from “passive adaptation” to “active design”. © 2026

title: In-situ nanowhiskers/cellular interpenetrating networks synergistic enhancing 2024 Al matrix composites achieving ultra-high thermal stability via additive manufacturing
abstract: Conventional high-strength aluminium alloys are generally susceptible to hot cracking during laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) and often suffer from grain coarsening and thermal instability of strengthening phases at elevated temperatures, which restricts their application in aerospace thermal-resistant components. To address these issues, an in-situ strategy combining nanowhiskers with three-dimensional cellular networks is proposed to develop a new 2024 Al alloy (AA2024)-based composite tailored for L-PBF. In-situ formation of nano-sized MgAlB4 whiskers and continuous Al3(Cu,Ni)2 cellular networks constructs an interpenetrating architecture, with whiskers inside cells or in walls, refining α-Al grains and blocking dislocation motion. These quasi-continuous MgAlB4 whiskers effectively mitigate performance degradation caused by the decomposition of Al3(Cu,Ni)2 cellular networks and grain coarsening at high temperatures, maintaining the synergistic enhancement effects of the interpenetrating architecture. Consequently, the as-built composite achieves a high ultimate tensile strength of ∼630 MPa at room temperature, ∼496 MPa at 200 °C, and ∼408 MPa (65% retention) after exposure at 300 °C for 1000 h. With extended thermal exposure, the adaptive strengthening mechanism, namely the evolution from a continuous interpenetrating network to synergistic strengthening by quasi-continuous whiskers and dispersed particles, can hinder dislocation motion, facilitate load transfer, and enhance thermal resistance. This work would provide a new approach to the development of high-thermal-stability high-strength aluminium matrix composites for additive manufacturing in aerospace applications. © 2026

title: Comparative Investigation of Epoxy-terminated and Carboxyl-terminated Butadiene Nitrile Rubber for Toughened Epoxy Resins
abstract: The research presents how Carboxyl Terminated Butadiene Nitrile (CTBN) and Epoxy Terminated Butadiene Nitrile (ETBN) types of Reactive Liquid Rubber (RLR) influence epoxy resins through rheological, thermal, and mechanical property assessments. The use of recycled waste rubber creates sustainable high-performance additives through waste material transformation. Various mechanical, thermal, and rheological tests assessed the effects of CTBN and ETBN concentrations on their viscosity behaviour, mechanical properties, and curing process of the epoxy system used. The thermal stability of the ETBN and CTBN systems was analyzed by using Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) to determine decomposition temperatures and stability measurements. A complete set of mechanical tests measured tensile strength, flexural strength, and impact strength. Toughness improvements reached their peak with 2.5 wt.% ETBN addition resulting in a 42.2% increase in ultimate tensile strength, a 103.8% increase in tensile modulus, a 26.9% improvement in toughness, and a 67.65% increase in impact strength while maintaining all other properties. Also, 5 wt.% CTBN incorporation into the epoxy polymer leads to 30% increment in ultimate tensile strength, 49.5% increase in ultimate flexural strength, 68% increase in tensile modulus, and 300% increase in impact strength. So, both CTBN and ETBN are said to be effective tougheners that can be used to enhance the toughness of the overall matrix system while balancing other mechanical properties. The investigation highlights how the termination chemistry affects phase separation and interfacial adhesion, ultimately leading to improved performance for its applications in automotive and aerospace industries. The innovative use of recycled ETBN and CTBN thus creates a way for the development of sustainable solutions that deliver economic benefits and environmental advantages. © 2026 Semnan University Faculty of Mechanical Engineering. .

title: Electrohydrodynamic inkjet printing of porous perovskite color-conversion layers via evaporation-induced phase separation for high-efficiency micro-LED displays
abstract: Perovskite nanocrystal color-conversion layers (PeNC-CCLs) are highly promising for full-color micro-sized light-emitting diode (micro-LED) displays; however, inefficient photon harvesting and emission extraction in printed thin films remain major barriers to achieving high color-conversion efficiency. Herein, we develop a porous-structure engineering strategy for PeNC-CCLs based on evaporation-induced phase separation in a ternary ink system composed of polymethyl methacrylate, polyethylene glycol, and xylene. During solvent evaporation, the polymer blend undergoes phase separation to form a porous framework containing micro-/nanoscale scattering centers. These embedded pores extend the optical path of excitation photons and mitigate waveguided emission losses, thereby substantially improving photon utilization within the CCLs. To suppress nonradiative recombination and preserve the structural integrity of PeNCs during polymer incorporation, the nanocrystal surfaces are pre-stabilized through sequential ligand exchange using a quaternary ammonium bromide and a sulfonic-acid-based zwitterionic ligand. The resulting CsPbBr3 porous films achieve a photoluminescence quantum yield of 89.54%, placing them among the highest-performing polymer-encapsulated PeNC films reported to date. The strategy is fully compatible with electrohydrodynamic inkjet printing, enabling porous fluorescent arrays with a twofold enhancement in photoluminescence intensity and subpixels as small as 10 μm (1270 ppi). Printed dual-color PeNC-CCLs integrated with a blue micro-LED array further yield a full-color display prototype with a resolution of 520 ppi and a color gamut of 143% NTSC. These results establish porous-structure engineering as a scalable and effective route toward high-efficiency, stable, and high-resolution PeNC-based micro-LED displays. © 2026

title: Hybrid DOE-RSM Modeling of Antibacterial and Mechanical Performance of ZnO-CMC Paper Coatings
abstract: In this study, zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles were synthesized using the glycine-nitrate combustion method and structurally and morphologically characterized X-ray diffraction (XRD) results confirmed the formation of pure ZnO phase with wurtzite structure and nano-crystalline nature of particles, average crystallite size was calculated at 37 nm. Electron microscopy SEM-TEM images confirmed the quasi-spherical morphology of nanoparticles. In order to evaluate the bio-efficacy of the synthesized nanoparticles, minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) tests of the synthesized ZnO nanoparticles against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli bacteria were performed and biologically effective concentration range was selected for use in coating suspension. ZnO nanoparticles were added to carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) base coatings at selected concentrations and applied to paper. Using a full factorial design of experiments (DOE), the simultaneous effect of ZnO concentration and coating thickness on the antibacterial index (R), tensile strength, and burst strength of the coated paper was investigated. Statistical analysis and response surface methodology (RSM) were used to model the main and interaction effects of parameters and develop predictive models. The results showed that ZnO concentration and coating thickness play a decisive role in the antibacterial performance and mechanical properties. Multi-response optimization was performed considering the maximization of antibacterial property and mechanical properties of the paper. The proposed DOE–RSM hybrid framework provides an effective and reliable approach for the design and optimization of antibacterial paper coatings, what the optimize results are related to ZnO (wt. %); 7.55 %, and Thickness 120 (µm). © 2026, Institute for Color Science and Technology. .

title: Finite Element Analysis and Optimization of the Composite Plate Subjected to Close-Range Explosion
abstract: Composite materials, particularly glass and carbon fibre composites, are widely used in aerospace, automotive, and defence applications because of their excellent strength-to-weight ratio and superior mechanical performance. However, their structural integrity can be severely compromised when subjected to high-intensity dynamic loads such as close-range explosions. His study presents a comprehensive finite element analysis (FEA) and optimization methodology to evaluate and improve the blast resistance of these composite plates under surface contact explosive loading. The numerical model was developed in LS-DYNA, where the laminates were modeled with 3D solid elements and governed by the Tsai–Wu failure criterion to predict ply failure behaviour. Model validation was carried out by comparing numerical predictions with experimental data from the literature, showing good agreement in terms of delamination area, perforation, and damage distribution. Following validation, a Genetic Algorithm (GA) implemented through LS-OPT was employed to optimize the laminate lay-up sequence, aiming to maximize the safety factor. The optimization yielded significant performance improvements—raising the safety factor by up to 63% and reducing delamination damage by up to 33%. Furthermore, the effect of explosive stand-off distance was analyzed, revealing its critical role in mitigating structural damage. The proposed framework provides a reliable and practical numerical tool for designing and optimizing blast-resistant composite structures, offering valuable guidance for aerospace, defence, and automotive engineers to develop lighter and safer structural components capable of withstanding severe explosion environments. © 2026 Semnan University Faculty of Mechanical Engineering. .

title: A Neuro-Symbolic Diffusion Hypergraph Framework for Real-Time Power Quality Assessment in Grid-Connected and Islanded Microgrid Clusters
abstract: The growing importance of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) has dramatically transformed the modern power system, leading to the development of microgrids with dynamic, complex operating conditions. Nevertheless, the intermittent nature of renewable production and presence of nonlinear loads lead to severe Power Quality (PQ) disturbances, including voltage sags, swells, harmonics, and discontinuities. Proper detection, prediction, and interpretation of these disturbances remain a major challenge, especially in real-time grid-connected and islanded microgrid systems. To address these issues, the present research introduces a new Neuro-Symbolic Hypergraph (NSDH) model for real-time PQ evaluation. The proposed model combines hypergraph-based spatial modeling to learn higher-order relationships among sensor nodes, a neuro-symbolic reasoning layer to increase interpretability and adherence to domain-specific rules. Also, the Brownian Black Kite Optimizer (BBKO) is used to optimize parameters and enhance convergence efficiently. Benchmark datasets are used to evaluate the model, such as SEED and IEEE 1159 PQ disturbance datasets. Experimental findings indicate the model proposed in the article has a higher performance of 98.6% accuracy, 97.9% Positive Predictive Value (PPV), 98.1% recall, and 98.0% F1-score than the current Deep Learning (DL) and graph-based frameworks. Moreover, the model has a high level of robustness, scalability, and a low level of computational latency; hence, it is applicable in real-time applications. In general, the suggested NSDH models are able to offer a highly efficient, scalable, and interpretable approach to advanced PQ monitoring of contemporary microgrid systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Synthesis of Copper Oxide Nano Powders: Effect of Surface Modifier Type
abstract: particles even in quantum region. CuO nano particles were synthesized via precipitation route in the presence of various surface modifiers (SMs) including Sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) and Polyethylene glycol (PEG), (3-Glycidoxypropyl) trimethoxysilane (3-GPTMS), Triton X-100, Ethylene glycol (C₂H₆O₂) and Oleic Acid. The effects of the SMs type on the structure, microstructure and band gap of samples were studied. Results generally showed that the SMs type led to formation of nanostructured monoclinic CuO phase with no considerable change in the structure and with crystallite size of ≤10nm. Furthermore, Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectra represented corresponding bands of Cu-O bonds in all samples. Moreover, scanning electron micrographs showed that highly agglomerated semispherical nano particles were obtained. Moreover, transmission electron micrographs showed synthesis in the presence of SDS and 3-GPTMS led to smallest and largest nano particles. Furthermore, considerable band gap broadening of powders up to 4 eV confirms the nano nature of synthesized particles even in quantum region. © Institute for Color Science and Technology.

title: Bioinspired photothermal self-healing anti-fouling coating with continuously enhanced slipperiness through dynamic release of lubricant and antibacterial filler
abstract: Marine bio-fouling severely threatens the safety and efficiency of marine equipment. Slippery liquid-infused porous surface (SLIPS) is a promising approach for solving bio-fouling. However, poor durability limits its application due to the loss of the lubricant. Inspired by the morphology and function of toad subcutaneous glands and mucus secretion, a photothermal self-healing and slippery anti-fouling coating was developed by incorporating graphene oxide-based covalent organic framework loaded with carvacrol (GO/COF-Car) as antibacterial filler and butyl stearate (BS) as lubricant in degradable polyurethane. Covalent organic framework (COF) achieves the loading of carvacrol through π–π interaction and hydrogen bonding. In addition, it was verified that there are three types of hydrogen bonds in polyurethane chain through experimental characterization and theoretical calculation, thereby enabling the coating with rapid photothermal self-healing performance (397 s). The degradable coating achieves continuously release of filler and BS, endowing the coating with enhanced slippery surface and antibacterial performance during degradation. The antibacterial rate of the coating after 120 days of degradation remained as high as 93.9% against Escherichia coli. Meanwhile, the coating exhibited an extremely low coverage of algae (0.165%). This strategy provides a new approach to address the problem of insufficient anti-fouling performance caused by the decline in slippery property of SLIPS. © 2026

title: Multi-objective placement of EV charging stations integrating distribution network constraints and traffic demand using hybrid TLBO–PSO
abstract: The increasing penetration of electric vehicles (EVs) has accelerated the need for strategically planned charging infrastructure capable of supporting both transportation demand and distribution network operation. Inappropriate placement of electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) may increase network power losses, degrade voltage performance, and influence distribution system reliability. This study presents an integrated multi-objective planning framework for optimal EVCS placement that simultaneously considers electrical network performance, reliability assessment, and transportation demand characteristics. The optimization model incorporates real power loss, voltage deviation index (VDI), system average interruption duration index (SAIDI), system average interruption frequency index (SAIFI), customer average interruption duration index (CAIDI), EV traffic flow, and accessibility within a unified objective formulation. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Teaching–Learning-Based Optimization (TLBO), and a hybrid TLBO–PSO optimization strategy are employed to solve the proposed planning problem, while Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Simulated Annealing (SA) are additionally included as conventional benchmark methods. The proposed framework is evaluated on the IEEE 33-bus radial distribution system using MATLAB, with algorithmic performance assessed through 30 independent simulation runs to examine convergence behaviour and solution consistency. The results demonstrate that the integrated planning framework effectively balances electrical and transportation-related objectives while achieving consistent optimization performance. The compared optimization methods produce similar network operating characteristics, while the hybrid TLBO–PSO approach exhibits a low mean power loss and the smallest standard deviation across repeated runs, indicating consistent solution behaviour. Furthermore, the optimized EVCS deployment enhances distribution system reliability while maintaining satisfactory voltage performance under the considered operating conditions. The proposed framework provides a comprehensive decision-support methodology for coordinated EV charging infrastructure planning and offers a flexible foundation for future extensions involving uncertainty modelling, large-scale distribution networks, and advanced transportation network representations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Topology-Aware IoT-Enabled online grounding safety-State estimation for converter-Rich Data-Center power networks
abstract: Grounding in converter-rich data-center power networks is still assessed mainly through standards-based design and periodic inspection, although return-path redistribution, extensive bonding, and operating-state variation can affect Earth Potential Rise (EPR), step voltage, and touch voltage. This paper proposes a standards-traceable cyber-physical framework that converts sparse synchronized measurements into online grounding safety-state estimates. The framework combines distributed IoT sensing, a grounding-aware model, constrained sequential measurement fusion, reduced-order surface-potential reconstruction, and standards-based step- and touch-voltage assessment. It is evaluated as a bounded proof-of-concept numerical study on a compact seven-node topology with partially unmonitored return paths. Results show that the main value is not universal reduction in average EPR error over all strong baselines, but a more safety-favorable operating point with stronger unsafe-state detection, lower missed-unsafe burden, improved step-voltage interpretation, and localized safety-margin visibility. Ablation results indicate that topology-aware grounding and auxiliary-path representation provide the dominant gain, while prior-regularized sensor-set analysis shows that reduced sensor configurations retain comparable estimation performance but with reduced information margin within the compact topology. The study supports grounding safety-state estimation as a candidate cyber-physical framework for further validation in converter-rich data-center environments. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Relaxation crossover under stress annealing governing non-monotonic coercivity evolution in Fe-based metallic glass
abstract: AI megasystems and 5G/6G technologies demand advanced soft magnetic materials for high-frequency, high-power-density conversion, for which Fe-based amorphous soft magnets are attractive owing to their low-coercivity potential. This potential can be fully realized only when rapid-quenching-induced frozen-in stresses are relieved, commonly by stress annealing. Yet how stress-coupled glassy relaxation modifies magnetic reversal remains unresolved. Here we address this issue using tensile stress relaxation in Fe82Si4B14 metallic-glass ribbons, where coercivity shows a non-monotonic time dependence that cannot be understood as simple stress relief. Time-resolved activation-energy analysis and strain recovery reveal a transition from reversible γ-like relaxation to cooperative β-related relaxation with irreversible strain accumulation. Magneto-optical Kerr imaging shows that this transition is accompanied by more uniform reversal at the coercivity minimum and renewed heterogeneous reversal after prolonged relaxation. A three-channel kinetic framework captures these signatures through random-pinning decay, stress-written anisotropy, and delayed plasticity-induced pinning, identifying the coercivity minimum as a transient kinetic window rather than the endpoint of simple stress relief. © 2026

title: Lightning geolocation accuracy as the dominant error source in evaluating strike-prediction models for transmission lines
abstract: This study evaluates ten Electro-Geometric Models (EGMs) and one Leader Progression Model (LPM) for predicting lightning strikes to a 220 kV transmission line. Using 15 years of EUCLID lightning-location data (2011–2025) processed through IEC 62858 flash grouping and polarity-specific IC current filtering, we identified 7577 flash events from 18,333 stroke records along an 83.9 km line with eight confirmed fault-causing attachments. Our central finding comes from a one-factor-at-a-time Monte-Carlo analysis (200 realizations per error source): among lightning location, peak current, and stroke-type/amplitude classification, only location error materially changes whether individual confirmed events are detected—for both the geometric (EGM_Young) and physics-based (LPM) models—while peak-current and classification error change it for neither. Because the median location error (89 m) is comparable to or larger than the 43–88 m EGM attractive radii, event-level detection is bounded by geolocation accuracy rather than model choice, and 7 of 10 EGMs detect none of the confirmed attachments. We propose detection ratio and predicted attachment rate as metrics better suited to limited confirmed events with undefined true negatives. The LPM and EGM_Young attain the highest detection ratio (2/8); the LPM predicts 39% fewer total attachments (249 versus 411) at 4.8 × higher computational cost, reported as a model property rather than evidence that either is more accurate. This count ordering is invariant across all three error sources, whereas the detection result, resting on only two detected events, is reported as a sensitivity analysis rather than a full variance decomposition. These models can also screen candidate high-risk segments for maintenance prioritization, subject to the stated limitations. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Bioinspired flexible materials with Lactuca indica leaf-mimicked structures for radar-infrared compatible stealth
abstract: Developing radar-infrared compatible stealth materials is fundamentally challenged by the conflict between efficient microwave absorption and low infrared emissivity. Herein, to break through this bottleneck, we propose a cross-scale reconstruction strategy inspired by the antireflective microstructures of the Lactuca indica leaf and fabricate a multilayer flexible radar-infrared compatible stealth material by precise laser etching. The fabricated biomimetic architectures effectively tune the surface electromagnetic impedance matching performance. Crucially, a multi-period coupled infrared structure was introduced to construct a multidimensional conductive network, effectively mitigating the electromagnetic shielding effect of conventional metallic layers. Experimental and simulation results demonstrate that the biomimetic radar stealth layer achieves a reflection loss (RL) of −47.95 dB at 12.82 GHz with an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB, RL ≤ −10 dB) of 9.05 GHz, driven by synergistic multiple scattering, magnetic resonance, and interfacial polarization. With the infrared stealth layer integrated, the material maintains a low emissivity of 0.12 while restoring broadband, isotropic microwave attenuation, delivering a RL of −31.70 dB at 6.57 GHz and an EAB of 3.76 GHz. Furthermore, its exceptional mechanical flexibility ensures seamless conformance to complex geometries. The present study offers an innovative design route toward flexible materials with radar-infrared bi-compatible stealth performance. © 2026

title: A gated risk assessment and alarm-screening framework for wildfire monitoring in transmission-line corridors
abstract: Wildfires near transmission-line corridors threaten secure power-system operation, while early flames and thin smoke are small, low-contrast, and readily confused with haze, steam, reflection, lighting artifacts, and other corridor interference. This paper develops Vision-Language Power-line Screening (VLPS), a gated alarm-screening framework for utility-operated monitoring images. A recall-oriented High-Recall Visual Gating Module (VGM) controls invocation, and the full Vision-Language Corridor model (VLC-Full) performs fire/smoke localization, interference discrimination, and low/medium/high operational-risk assessment. On real monitoring images from 800 kV and above transmission-line corridors in China, always-on VLC-Full achieves 92.5% mAP@0.5, 96.5% Risk Accuracy, and 0.987 AUROC at 238.0 ms model-side latency. At τvgm = 0.15, VGM passes 599 of 600 risk-positive test images (99.8% Recall), with one medium-risk thin-smoke false negative and no observed high-risk gate failure. Under a 5% risk-positive workload composition, VLPS has an expected average model-side latency of 30.3 ms/image and 97.2% Risk-positive Recall; a gate-passed suspicious image still follows the 246.0 ms serial VGM-plus-VLC-Full model path. The intended deployment target is a dedicated GPU server deployed at the utility monitoring terminal, and complete acquisition-to-alarm engineering latency was not measured. VLPS supports operator-facing alarm prioritization and review rather than automatic protection decisions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Tuning nanomaterial facets with light: A laser-enabled strategy for surface control
abstract: High-index facets play an important role in regulating the surface reactivity of functional nanomaterials. Here, we present a femtosecond (fs) laser-enabled strategy for post-synthesis facet engineering by fabricating laser-induced periodic surface structures (LIPSS) on CoFe2O4/Co3O4 (CFO/CO) epitaxial films. By controlling the laser polarization relative to the crystal orientation, LIPSS sidewalls with different exposed facets are selectively generated. Among them, the {510}LIPSS exhibits the best ethanol-sensing performance, with a high response (1.5 at 5 ppm) and rapid response/recovery times (7/9 s). Under simulated breath conditions, it exhibits good humidity tolerance and stable operation, with responses of 2.1 and 2.9 to 50 and 190 ppm ethanol, respectively, demonstrating its potential as a proof-of-concept breath alcohol sensor. Combined experimental characterization and DFT calculations suggest that the enhanced performance arises from the synergistic effects of facet-dependent surface chemistry, heterointerfaces, and surface-active species. This laser-polarization-directed strategy provides a versatile route for tailoring surface reactivity through crystallographic control beyond conventional synthesis methods. © 2026

title: A hybrid framework for short-term load forecasting via frequency-domain decoupling and spatio-temporal graph fusion
abstract: Load forecasting, as a crucial component of the electricity market, plays a significant role in ensuring the secure operation and rational planning of the power grid. However, accurate short-term load forecasting (STLF) remains challenging due to strong non-stationarity caused by complex meteorological conditions and abrupt load fluctuations. To mitigate these prediction errors and enhance load feature extraction, this paper proposes a hybrid forecasting framework combining frequency-domain decoupling with a spatio-temporal graph neural network. Specifically, a secondary decomposition strategy based on secondary variational mode decomposition (SVMD) and wavelet packet threshold denoising (WPTD) is employed to refine multi-scale modal representations by attenuating weak noise-like wavelet-packet coefficients while retaining meaningful high-frequency load variations. An Energy-Driven Reconstruction (EDR) mechanism is then introduced to reorganize the decomposed modes into dominant low-frequency and high-frequency fluctuation components according to their energy distribution. Subsequently, a heterogeneous dual-branch architecture is deployed: the low-frequency branch employs a multi-basis trend modeling module to track long-term patterns, while a wide-receptive-field temporal convolutional network (TCN) captures transient high-frequency fluctuations. Furthermore, a Weather-GAT module is integrated to aggregate multi-site meteorological features. Employing real-world load data from the Panama National Grid, the proposed framework achieves a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 2.6837% in 24-hour-ahead forecasting. Experimental results demonstrate that the model exhibits strong robustness across regular workdays, holidays, and meteorological disturbance scenarios. © 2026

title: A green molecular gel nanocomposite: Structure, rheological properties and tribological performance
abstract: Molecular gels are a new class of lubricants that offer many advantages over traditional lubricants. However, developing molecular gels that combine environmental sustainability with high lubrication performance remains a significant challenge. In this work, a green molecular gel lubricant using cottonseed oil as a low-cost and sustainable solvent and N-lauroyl-L-glutamic acid di-n-butylamide (GP-1) as a green gelator has been developed. The thermal stability, rheological properties and lubrication performance of the gel are further enhanced by reduced graphene oxide (rGO) nanosheets. At 1.0 wt% of rGO, the onset decomposition temperature is increased from 335 °C to 365 °C, and the storage modulus (G′) from ∼4.05 × 10 ³ Pa to ∼9.35 × 103 Pa. Correspondingly, the coefficient of friction is reduced by approximately 4.62-fold. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations in combination with Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy indicate that the reinforcing effects of rGO are attributable to its physical interactions with GP-1. The interactions also promote the primary nucleation of GP-1, leading to the formation of smaller GP-1 fiber network domains that help distribute GP-1 nanofibers more homogeneously in the gel. The gel network restructuring and reinforcement by rGO may work together to contribute to the high lubrication performance of the gel nanocomposite. Apart from the sustainability design of this molecular gel, the mechanistic insights provide guidance on the selection of nano-additives for designing a high-performance molecular gel lubricant. © 2026 The Authors. title: Cyclic melting of Ni-Nb-Y alloy under space and ground conditions: A comparative study of phase separation and solidification behavior
abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation enables the in situ construction of composite architectures and phase-separation recycling, but droplet coalescence under conventional gravity obscures its intrinsic behavior. Here, electrostatic levitation experiments were conducted on a high-viscosity Ni59Nb20Y21 alloy in space with cyclic melting and compared with ground references. Microgravity and cyclic melting increased undercooling, reduced secondary-droplet size, and produced a regular radial size distribution. Nanoindentation showed higher hardness and modulus of Ni6Nb7 in space-processed samples than in ground-processed counterparts. Cyclic melting also changed some Ni6Nb7 grains from dendritic to near-equiaxed morphology, and only {0001}-type twins were observed in the examined Ni6Nb7 regions. These results clarify phase separation and solidification in phase-separated alloys and provide guidance for fabricating dispersion-type microstructures. © 2026

title: Sensitivity-factor-based local flexibility market clearing for mixed P-Q services
abstract: The rapid expansion of distributed photovoltaic generation in low and medium voltage networks is causing increasing voltage limit violations and congestion problems, which distribution system operators must handle. This paper presents a simulation framework for locationally differentiated procurement of flexibility services at distribution level. We demonstrate how controllable active devices connected to low-voltage networks (residential photovoltaic systems, distributed energy storage, flexible consumers) can support voltage control through combined active and reactive power services, and how the bid prices and activation of such flexibility services can be determined by combining bid prices assumed equal to the marginal costs of flexibility assets with network sensitivity factors in a pay-as-bid local flexibility market clearing algorithm. The results demonstrate how the success of market participants in distribution-level clearing depends on their location relative to the network constraints. By embedding sensitivity factors into mathematical optimization, bids are evaluated not only by price but also by their network impact, producing location-dependent bid selection outcomes that reflect physical contribution. This paper highlights how the proposed sensitivity factor framework can provide a computationally efficient mechanism for locational flexibility procurement within the validity range of the applied sensitivity factors, without requiring centralized optimal power flow computations during market clearing. © 2026 The Authors

title: Structured-DGA transformer for power transformer fault diagnosis under missing-gas setting
abstract: Dissolved gas analysis (DGA) is widely used for power transformer fault diagnosis, yet practical DGA records can be incomplete and fault types are long-tailed. To address these issues, we propose a Structured-DGA Transformer (SDGA-Transformer) for fault diagnosis under complete-gas and missing-gas settings. The proposed method represents each DGA record as a structural ratio matrix that encodes pairwise ratios among the five gases, and places concentration-level information on the diagonal. To support missing-gas diagnosis, SDGA-Transformer introduces a missing-indicator matrix and adopts masked self-attention so that the prediction relies only on observed gas-related entries. To mitigate long-tailed data, we adopt inverse-frequency sampling during training. Moreover, we incorporate IEC 60599, Rogers ratios, and the Duval triangle as a rule-guided teacher prior, and use a reliability-aware gating mechanism to activate rule guidance only when it is applicable and consistent. The revised evaluation uses repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation with fold-specific preprocessing, training-time Missing-{0, 1, 2} augmentation, and identical missing masks for all learning-based baselines. Under this protocol, complete-gas accuracy and macro-F1 are 86.66 ± 5.06% and 85.83 ± 5.67%, respectively. The corresponding values are 79.58 ± 3.93% and 78.80 ± 4.09% under Missing-1, and 67.91 ± 3.33% and 67.02 ± 3.33% under Missing-2. Finally, decision matrices of SDGA-Transformer aligned with the structural ratio matrix provide decision-faithful explanations and fault-type gas-importance for diagnosis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Towards global location of inter-turn short-circuit faults in transformer homogeneous windings via double-end excitation and admittance response subtraction
abstract: The frequency response analysis (FRA) is considered the common method for diagnosing transformer winding deformations, including short circuit (SC) faults. However, for a transformer with a homogeneous winding, it exhibits symmetry and uniform characteristics; each equivalent electrical circuit unit of the winding is almost identical. Consequently, SC faults in symmetrical positions cannot be located by traditional FRA. Besides, the health history FRA curve, namely the fingerprint, is overly dependent on the traditional FRA method. In this article, an improved transformer inter-turn short circuit fault method, namely, combination method of the double-end excitation and admittance response subtraction, is proposed. It breaks the symmetry of the transformer and makes “global” location within the entire winding, from top to bottom, possible. Firstly, the principle of the introduced method is presented. Criteria for establishing the external circuit and sensitivity analysis is studied. The method is then verified on three different transformers, including simulations and experimental tests. Finally, machine learning is used for localization analysis. The results show that the proposed method has “global” diagnosis ability for SC faults and does not rely on complex neural networks, which can achieve satisfactory performance. © 2026

title: Designing a heterogeneous dual-phase Ti-6Al-3Nb-2Zr-1Mo alloy with enhanced strength-impact-toughness synergy
abstract: Developing high-strength titanium alloys with high toughness under varying strain rate loading has been a long-standing pursuit in the development of advanced structural materials. In this study, we report a hierarchical multiscale heterogeneous microstructure (HS) in the Ti-6Al-3Nb-2Zr-1Mo (Ti80) alloy, comprising fine equiaxed α grains, discontinuous lamellar α phase, and transformed β (βt) phase with strong nanoscale α′ precipitates. The HS-Ti80 exhibits an unprecedented synergy of yield strength (860 MPa), uniform elongation (11.2%), and impact toughness (KV2, 104 J). The superior strain hardening capacity of the HS arises from the heterogeneous deformation induced by the coexistence of multiscale domains. The fine equiaxed α grains promote uniform stress distribution and delay strain localization, while the βt phase with nano‑α′ precipitates serves as a hard domain that accommodates strain compatibility with the α matrix. Consequently, multiple types of dislocations and deformation twins are activated, and their intricate interactions sustain plastic deformation over a wide strain range. Simultaneously, the discontinuous lamellar α grains act as effective crack buffers, deflecting propagating cracks, generating a high density of secondary cracks, and forcing a tortuous crack path, thereby substantially dissipating strain energy and enhancing impact resistance. These findings establish that architecting hierarchical HSs provides a promising strategy for developing high‑performance titanium alloys capable of withstanding both quasi‑static and impact loading. © 2026

title: Fault recovery strategy for active distribution networks with high penetration of DGs considering island merging and sequential repair
abstract: The integration of high-proportioned DGs into distributed networks has had a profound impact on improving energy utilization efficiency, promoting the utilization of renewable energy, and offering the potential to enhance power grid resilience. However, the strong randomness and volatility characteristics of DGs introduce significant complexity and uncertainty into the fault recovery process for active distribution networks (ADNs). To address this problem, this paper proposes a novel fault recovery strategy that simultaneously integrates island merging and sequential repair. First, a new island merging model is developed based on a virtual power flow formulation inspired by single-commodity flow theory, thus enabling coordinated optimization of power sharing and topology reconfiguration. Second, by introducing a set of linkage constraints between sequential repair and island power supply capability into the model obtained above, a co-optimization mechanism that integrates fault repair with dynamic island merging is established. After that, a unified fault recovery model is presented by using the mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) model. Validations on the modified IEEE 33-node system demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed strategy. Compared to mainstream benchmark methods, the proposed strategy reduces the total recovery cost by 34.9% to 51.1%, and guarantees a 100% load recovery rate within four repair periods. Finally, extensive tests on the larger modified IEEE 69-node system further confirm the strategy's excellent scalability, computational reliability, and robust engineering applicability under severe multi-fault contingencies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: An efficient cooperative optimization reconfiguration scheme using joint integer coding and hybrid sparrow search algorithm for active distribution networks
abstract: The increasing penetration of distributed generations (DGs) brings both opportunities and challenges to the operation of active distribution networks (ADNs). Conventional distribution network reconfiguration (DNR) approaches often struggle to achieve global optimality and maintain stable operation under DGs-rich conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid sparrow search algorithm (HSSA) based on an integer coding method for the multi-objective reconfiguration of ADNs. The DNR problem is formulated as a multi-objective optimization model that simultaneously minimizes power loss, voltage deviation index (VDI), and load balancing index (LBI), while satisfying radial network topology and operational constraints. To effectively eliminate infeasible solutions and reduce the search space, the ordered loop matrix is constructed based on evaluating a specific electrical metric. To obtain reconfiguration schemes, the HSSA is employed, incorporating the particle swarm optimization (PSO) search strategy and the Metropolis criterion to maintain a dynamic balance between exploration and exploitation. Numerical simulations on IEEE 33-bus and 118-bus distribution networks validate the effectiveness of the proposed HSSA, demonstrating its superiority over existing algorithms in terms of convergence rate and accuracy. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Edge-weight coupled Gaussian masking for resilient operation optimization of multi-energy virtual power plants under eavesdropping-injection attacks
abstract: Multi-energy virtual power plants (VPPs) coordinate distributed electricity and heat resources through communication links that may expose incremental-cost data and permit false-data injection. This paper develops an edge-weight coupled Gaussian masking (EW-CGM) method for resilient VPP operation under eavesdropping-injection attacks. The operation layer embeds electrical and thermal loss sensitivities in the incremental-cost conditions. An attacker model uses intercepted historical data to estimate private cost coefficients and construct ramp-type false commands. EW-CGM applies antisymmetric, time-decaying Gaussian masks to individual links, preserving global aggregation while increasing parameter-estimation uncertainty. Residual detection and predicted-state recovery address the resulting deviations. The analysis and case studies evaluate parameter inference, convergence, detection, recovery, and sensitivity to load volatility and repeated sub-threshold attacks, while retaining the loss-aware operating reference under the nominal tested attack, outage, and recovery conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Price-based centralized coordination of grid-edge resources for residential community energy flexibility assessment
abstract: The growing use of distributed energy resources and flexible loads has transformed residential communities into active participants in distribution system operations. This shift creates opportunities for demand-side flexibility while introducing new operational challenges. This paper presents a price-based, centralized coordination framework to quantify and schedule community energy flexibility from grid-edge resources, including HVAC systems, electric vehicles (EVs), photovoltaic (PV) systems, and battery energy storage systems (BESSs). The framework incorporates customer comfort constraints, fairness considerations for shared EV charging, distribution network operating limits, and battery degradation costs to achieve economically efficient and technically feasible operation under time-of-use and dynamic electricity pricing. The framework is validated on a modified IEEE 123-bus distribution system using retail electricity prices from the Salt River Project (SRP) and Commonwealth Edison (ComEd). Sensitivity analyses assess the impact of battery degradation costs and operational uncertainties, including variations in PV generation and initial EV state-of-charge. A scalability analysis further examines computational performance as the number of participating households increases. Results show that coordinated PV and BESS operation improves flexibility by enabling the temporal shifting of renewable generation. However, fairness constraints and EV charging penalties can reduce available flexibility, while higher battery degradation costs discourage frequent battery cycling and reduce flexibility value. Overall, coordinated scheduling reduces community operating costs and maintains distribution system operating limits when network constraints are considered. These findings underscore the importance of coordinated grid-edge resource management and appropriate pricing strategies for secure and cost-effective residential energy flexibility. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Unlocking proton delivery-conversion-spillover via integrated single-atom and cluster synergy on rich oxygen-vacancy TiO2 for robust H2 production
abstract: We develop a highly active and durable electrocatalyst with low noble-metal use by simultaneously incorporating Pt single atoms and nanoclusters (∼1.3 nm) into rich-oxygen-vacancy TiO2 hollow nanotubes (PtSA-NCs/Oν-TiO2) to upgrade active sites and mass activity for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). The designed catalyst, with a unique dual-active-site architecture, provides distinctive control over the kinetics of active H* formation, migration, and recombination. In addition, introducing significant oxygen vacancies at the TiO2 surface leads to strong interactions with PtSA-NCs, resulting in interfacial charge redistribution and a regulated work function of the active Pt, thereby endorsing H2 production kinetics. The PtSA-NCs/Oν-TiO2 requires a small overpotential of only 26 and 39 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in 0.5 M H2SO4 and 1.0 M KOH media, respectively, along with a superior recorded mass activity of 14/11.89 A mg−1 at 0.2 V, beyond Pt/C by 51.09/59.45-fold. The PEMWE cell with a PtSA-NCs/Oν-TiO2-based cathode requires a small cell voltage of 1.695 V at 1.0 A cm−2 and demonstrates exceptional stability, with 50.17 μV/h degradation over 1000 h of continuous operation. Our research presents a novel concept for rational catalyst design, establishing an essential role in improving water-splitting efficiency for green hydrogen production. © 2026

title: Tailoring precipitation and thermal stability through pre-forging: High-density T-phase precipitation in a heat-resistant Al-Cu-Mg-Mn alloy
abstract: Pre-forging before homogenization was applied to an Al-Cu-Mg-Mn-based heat-resistant alloy to improve elevated-temperature strength and post-exposure stability. XRD shows similar overall diffraction features in the two samples, whereas SEM and TEM reveal that pre-forging fragments coarse intermetallic compounds (IMCs) and promotes a finer, denser T-phase dispersion retained through extrusion, solution treatment, and T6 aging. The average T-phase size decreases from 233 to 148 nm, and the particle count in the same observation area increases from 444 to 851. Accordingly, ultimate tensile strength (UTS) increases from 229.4 to 272.9 MPa at 290 °C and residual UTS from 237.3 to 277.2 MPa after 290 °C/100 h exposure, while T6 room-temperature UTS decreases from 544.5 to 521.9 MPa. The improved stability is associated with suppressed Cu-rich grain-boundary precipitate coarsening and retained fine, dense intragranular T-phase dispersion. Defect-energy calculations and diffusion simulations indicate that T-Al20Cu2Mn3 is more stable and coarsens more slowly than Al2Cu and Al2CuMg, supporting its contribution to 290 °C strength and post-exposure retention. © 2026

title: Electric pulse-induced inversion of asymmetric tension-compression creep in an Al-Cu-Li alloy
abstract: Experiments confirm that incorporating electroplasticity into creep aging facilitates dislocation motion and accelerates creep deformation. While tension-compression creep asymmetry is well-documented under normal thermo-mechanical coupling, its electro-thermo-mechanical counterpart remains rarely investigated. Herein, we studied the asymmetric creep response of an Al-Cu-Li alloy under tensile and compressive stress during electro-assisted creep. We found that electric pulses reverse the conventional tension-compression creep asymmetry. Contrary to the ordinary pattern where tensile creep rate exceeds compressive creep rate, the electroplastic compressive creep rate surpasses its tensile counterpart. Microstructural data show that at the creep onset, the dislocation loop density in compressive specimens is nearly three times that in tensile counterparts. Further analyses indicate that electric pulses promote the evolution of those extra dislocation loops into short dislocation lines, thereby increasing the number density of mobile dislocations and compressive creep rate. In short, electric pulses transform creep-restricting extra dislocation loops into highly mobile short dislocation lines within compressive specimens, resulting in a higher electroplastic compressive creep rate. This work advances the understanding of tension-compression asymmetric creep of aluminum alloys under electro-thermo-mechanical coupling. © 2026

title: TriPort X-gain boost converter integrated with PV and battery sources using optimized PI controller for improved energy management
abstract: High-efficiency, multi-source DC converters that integrate Renewable Energy Systems (RES) with dynamic load flexibility are in high demand. This work proposes a novel TriPort X-Gain Boost Converter (TXGBC) for efficient energy integration of Photovoltaic (PV) and battery sources that feed a common Direct Current (DC)-load. The proposed converter offers higher voltage conversion ratio, less current ripple and better dynamic stability. By simultaneously utilizing boost, switched-capacitor and reboost actions across the ports, the X-Gain arrangement improves the power transmission capacity and permits wide voltage adaptability under changing irradiance and state-of-charge conditions. To achieve precise regulation and low output voltage overshoot, an Animated Oat Optimization (AOO) based PI controller is introduced. In contrast to classical and swarm-based approaches, the proposed OAT algorithm ensures quick convergence and reliable global optimization of PI gains by dynamically stimulating the search trajectory in multidimensional parameter space. Through error minimization and load-demand prediction, the control technique adaptively balances the PV and battery power flow, ensuring stable operation during sudden transients. The proposed system is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink, simulation results demonstrate that TXGBC performs better than conventional converters due to its substantial static voltage gain, low ripple content, and high efficiency of 97.24%. The proposed controller exhibits a settling time of 0.08 s and overshoot of 0.06%. Additionally, a hardware prototype is developed, and the experimental results are validated with comparison analysis, demonstrating the converter's higher performance and practical viability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Construction of a corrosion signal network based on ultra-sensitive near-infrared fillers for rapid diagnosis of early corrosion of magnesium alloy
abstract: Magnesium alloys, possessing excellent mechanical properties and low density, have attracted considerable interest in engineering applications. However, they possess poor corrosion resistance, limiting their implementation. The early detection and imaging of corrosion in coated magnesium alloys, as well as the construction of an integrated early-corrosion signal network, are highly sought after but remain challenging in practice. Herein, we report the synthesis of a novel core-shell near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent filler by coating ZnGa2O4:Cr3+ (ZGOC, NIR signal source) with H3PW12O40 (HPW, ultraviolet-shielding shell). The NIR emission and afterglow of ZGOC are completely quenched upon HPW coating. However, the alkaline environment (pH ≈ 8) generated during early-stage corrosion of magnesium alloys can dissolve the HPW shell, thereby restoring the NIR afterglow of ZGOC. This recovery enables precise localization of corrosion sites and reliable quantitative evaluation of corrosion severity. The corrosion indication capability was evaluated using laser confocal microscope (LCM) and scanning electron microscope (SEM). The results show that after 50 days of salt spray testing, the optical imaging system detects fluorescence signals at the corrosion sites, and the afterglow intensity increases by 3.3 times compared to that at the initial stage, which is consistent with the SEM and LCM results. This work enables detection of corrosion, precise localization of corroded sites, and visualization of corrosion severity, thus enabling the construction of a spatial corrosion signal distribution network and achieving ultra-sensitive detection of early-stage corrosion in magnesium alloys. © 2026

title: Interfacial charge redistribution in Au/TiN Schottky photocatalysts enabling efficient full-spectrum CO2 reduction with H2O
abstract: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction using H2O as the electron donor is limited by rapid charge-carrier recombination and insufficient CO2 adsorption and activation, resulting in low solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency. Herein, we demonstrate that Schottky interface engineering upon metallic photocatalysts offers an effective strategy to optimize charge-carrier dynamics and surface reaction kinetics concurrently. Au nanoparticle-decorated TiN (Au/TiN) photocatalysts were fabricated via a facile impregnation-reduction method, in which uniformly dispersed Au nanoparticles are anchored onto metallic TiN to construct well-defined Schottky heterointerfaces. Spectroscopic studies combined with theoretical calculations reveal spontaneous interfacial charge redistribution driven by the Fermi-level mismatch between Au and TiN, rendering the formation of a built-in electric field that promotes directional electron transfer from TiN to Au. Consequently, the Au-TiN Schottky junction effectively suppresses charge-carrier recombination and accelerates interfacial charge transport. Meanwhile, the deposited Au nanoparticles also serve as active centers for CO2 adsorption and activation, facilitating the reduction reaction. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, the optimized Au/TiN photocatalyst affords CO and H2 evolution rates of 23.04 and 27.69 μmol g−1 h−1, respectively, with the CO production rate being nearly three times that of pristine TiN. In situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy identifies a *COOH-mediated proton-coupled electron transfer pathway for CO2-to-CO conversion. This work establishes Schottky interface engineering as an effective approach for metallic photocatalysts to regulate charge-transfer behavior and catalytic reaction pathways, providing a reliable strategy for efficient solar-to-fuel conversion. © 2026

title: Improving closing stability of high-voltage SF₆ circuit breakers via multi-physics modeling and genetic algorithm
abstract: For 550 kV and above SF₆ circuit breakers, phase-selective closing requires high repeatability of the mechanical closing process to ensure the accuracy of the target closing phase. In this study, the working principle and buffering characteristics of a hydraulic operating mechanism are analyzed, and an electromagnetic–hydraulic–mechanical co-simulation model is established to describe the closing dynamics under different operating conditions. The effects of oil pressure, driving voltage, ambient temperature, buffer gap height, and buffer step length on closing performance are investigated. A buffer-parameter optimization procedure combining a genetic algorithm and a neural-network surrogate model is then developed. The optimized buffer design reduces the terminal piston velocity from 2.30 m/s to 1.27 m/s, corresponding to a reduction of approximately 44.8%, while satisfying the full-stroke closing-time requirement. Prototype tests on a 550 kV SF₆ circuit breaker show that the simulated and measured motion characteristics agree well, with the maximum time deviation within 2 ms and the relative error below 5%. The results demonstrate that the proposed multiphysics-based optimization method can effectively improve the buffering performance and closing stability of high-voltage SF₆ circuit breakers under phase-selective closing conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Inherent physical feature extraction and fault cause identification for HVDC transmission systems
abstract: The accurate identification of line fault causes of LCC-HVDC directly determines the formulation of differentiated operation and maintenance decisions and the reduction of system outage time. However, DC line fault transients are not only driven by physical mechanisms such as lightning strikes and wildfires, but also deeply coupled with the nonlinear reshaping effect of converter station control on transient electrical quantities, which causes DC line faults to be difficult to accurately identify using traditional data-driven models. Therefore, by establishing an analytical model considering the closed-loop control response of the converter station, an analytical extraction method for the fault inherent components of DC electrical quantities is proposed, and the true restoration from controlled waveforms to physical essential characteristics is realized; subsequently, starting from the physical evolution mechanism, the essential differences of lightning strikes, wildfires, wind deviations, and foreign object bridging in electromagnetic characteristics are analyzed; furthermore, a fault cause identification model integrating the multi-branch residual network (MResNet) and gated recurrent unit (GRU) is constructed to extract the local spatial distortion and global temporal evolution features of fault inherent components from multiple dimensions. Based on control response decoupling and inherent physical feature extraction, an identification method for LCC-HVDC fault causes is proposed. Case study results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves effective identification of recorded waveform samples, providing theoretical foundations and engineering references for targeted maintenance and rapid recovery of DC lines under controlled environments. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: FDDNet: Frequency decomposition and dynamic deformable attention for insulator defect detection in complex backgrounds
abstract: Insulator defect detection is a critical task in power system inspection, as it ensures the safe and reliable operation of electrical equipment. However, in real-world inspection scenarios, insulator defects typically appear as small-scale targets with irregular geometries, often amid complex background interference such as vegetation occlusion and illumination variations. Existing object detection methods based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) rely on feature modeling with fixed receptive fields, which can cause entanglement of redundant information within the feature extraction network. This limitation reduces feature discriminability and leads to suboptimal detection performance. To address these challenges, we propose FDDNet, an improved Frequency Decomposition Dynamic Network based on YOLO11. Specifically, we introduce a C3k2_WT module that enhances feature representation via multi-frequency decomposition, effectively suppressing background interference. In addition, we redesign the C2PSA_DLKA module with deformable large-kernel attention, which dynamically adjusts the receptive field. This design effectively overcomes the constraints of fixed receptive fields in traditional CNNs, mitigates feature redundancy, and improves the attention mechanism's ability to capture irregular edge contours. On the IDID dataset, FDDNet achieves 94.7% precision, outperforming the baseline by 4.0%, while requiring only 6.9 GFLOPs. On the CPLID dataset, FDDNet achieves 96.6% precision and 97.9% mAP@50, confirming its generalization capability. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, FDDNet achieves competitive detection performance with substantially lower computational complexity, demonstrating its potential for lightweight deployment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Brazing of Y2O3−MgO and TC4 via Al2O3-mediated in-situ reaction: Interfacial evolution and strengthening mechanism
abstract: To address the issue of the facile formation of a brittle Cu2Y2O5 interfacial layer during traditional active brazing of Y2O3−MgO nanocomposite ceramic and TC4 alloy, a strategy for reconstructing the ceramic surface via Al2O3-mediated in-situ reaction was proposed. A dense Al2O3 coating was fabricated on the Y2O3−MgO ceramic through magnetron sputtering followed by air oxidation, and its influence on interfacial evolution and mechanical properties was systematically investigated. The reconstruction mechanism is revealed: The solid-state pre-reaction prior to filler melting converts the Y2O3 phase into a stable Y3Al5O12 precursor by Al2O3-mediated in-situ reaction, effectively achieving physical isolation from the free Cu atoms in the molten filler and suppressing the deleterious phase from the source. The results demonstrate that the ceramic surface reconstruction via Al2O3 coating effectively suppresses the detectable formation of the brittle Cu2Y2O5 phase, establishing a multi-layered gradient architecture consisting of a Y3Al5O12 + MgO internal reaction layer and a (Cu, Al)3Ti3O + Y2O3 external reaction layer. Under the optimal brazing condition of 880 °C/10 min, the maximum shear strength reached 70 MPa, which represents a significant 84% increase compared to direct brazing. Fracture analysis confirms a transition in the failure path from the brittle interfacial reaction layer to the ceramic matrix, indicating that the reconstructed interface is no longer the weakness of the joint. © 2026

title: In situ TEM evidence for the role of large helium bubbles in the irradiation hardening and embrittlement of SIMP steel
abstract: Helium-induced irradiation hardening and embrittlement are critical issues that restrict the application of ferritic/martensitic steels in advanced nuclear energy systems. In this study, a candidate low-activation martensitic structural material, SIMP steel, was irradiated with 540 keV He2+ at 600 °C to a fluence of 1 × 1017 ions/cm2. By combining in situ transmission electron microscope (TEM)-tensile testing with nanoindentation techniques, this study investigated the dynamic interactions between large helium bubbles and dislocations and their impact on mechanical degradation. Microstructural characterization revealed that irradiation induced the formation of large, irregularly shaped bubbles with an average size of 17.85 ± 6.25 nm. Nanoindentation testing confirmed a localized hardness increase of 0.20 ± 0.01 GPa associated with the He-enriched region. Calculation based on the dispersed barrier hardening model yielded an obstacle strength α of 0.16 ± 0.03. In situ TEM experiments captured the dynamic interaction between gliding dislocations and large helium bubbles, with the observed pinning, bowing, and bypass behavior being consistent with an Orowan-type bypass process under the present experimental condition. The study also revealed crack propagation and fracture behavior highly correlated with the spatial distribution of the helium bubbles. © 2026

title: Ultrabroadband microwave absorption via Co2+ site-occupancy-driven ligand-field reconstruction and spin-orbit coupling synergy
abstract: Despite its promise, ZnFe2O4 spinel is fundamentally limited by weak magnetic anisotropy and poor dielectric loss. Here, we overcome these barriers via a site-occupancy-driven ligand-field reconstruction and spin-orbit coupling (SOC) synergy strategy. By engineering the Co2+ distribution between tetrahedral and octahedral sites, we concurrently achieve two complementary functions: (i) the unquenched orbital angular momentum of high-spin Co2+ in the reconstructed crystal field intensifies SOC, significantly enhancing magnetic anisotropy and low-frequency magnetic loss; and (ii) the charge compensation triggered by Co2+ substitution generates oxygen vacancies and mixed-valence Fe3+/Fe2+ pairs, boosting dielectric loss via defect-induced polarization relaxation. Consequently, the optimized absorber delivers a 9.1 GHz effective bandwidth at 1.9 mm thickness and a −57.8 dB minimum reflection loss at 5.0 GHz. This work establishes ligand-field reconstruction and SOC synergy as a versatile atomic-scale design platform for high-performance microwave absorbers. © 2026

title: Adaptive cyber-resilient frequency regulation in isolated interconnected microgrids under false data injection attacks using empirical distribution-based statistical analysis
abstract: Frequency regulation of isolated interconnected microgrids (InMGs) relies on continuous exchange of measurement signals among control areas via communication channels, making the system vulnerable to cyberattacks, particularly false data injection (FDI) attacks. This paper proposes a model-free cyber-resilient framework for detecting and mitigating FDI attacks in isolated InMGs. A nonlinear autoregressive with exogenous inputs (NARX) neural network-based estimator is trained exclusively on local measurements to reconstruct the nominal frequency deviation without reliance on an explicit system model. The estimation residual is then analyzed using a non-parametric statistical method based on the empirical cumulative distribution function (ECDF), from which an online probabilistic score is derived for attack detection and compromised-area localization. Upon detection, an artificial neural network-based adaptive mitigation controller dynamically reconstructs the injected attack signal from the residual and subtracts it from the compromised frequency measurement, thereby mitigating the attack impact without requiring manual retuning under varying attack conditions. The proposed framework is validated on a two-area InMG under constant, incremental, bounded, and unbounded time-varying FDI attack profiles, and its scalability is demonstrated on an eight-area network. Simulation results confirm reliable attack detection and localization across all scenarios, with frequency recovery achieved within approximately 3 s following mitigation activation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Physics-inspired Bayesian estimation of multilayer soil resistivity incorporating thermo-hydro-groundwater effects for grounding design
abstract: Soil resistivity estimation plays a critical role in the development of grounding systems, affecting the earth potential rise (EPR) and touch and step voltages. Traditional multilayer inversion techniques estimate soil properties based on the fit of observed apparent resistivity curves, assuming soil resistivity parameters to be static and dependent only on depth. Nevertheless, in reality, soil resistivity is characterized by high levels of temporal variability influenced by changes in temperature, moisture content, precipitation, and groundwater. These dynamic factors are seldom considered in the inversion process. This paper presents a Bayesian multilayer inversion and uncertainty-quantification framework integrated with a physics-inspired phenomenological environmental model. The environmental model uses simplified and bounded correction functions motivated by established temperature, moisture, rainfall, and groundwater effects rather than directly solving the coupled governing equations of heat transfer, unsaturated flow, and groundwater movement. A fast Sum-of-Exponentials (SoE) forward model is used to achieve computationally efficient responses in multilayer soils. The inverse problem is solved using bounded stochastic optimization with a regularized log-domain misfit, followed by Bayesian uncertainty quantification using Metropolis-Hastings sampling. A penalty-based model-complexity criterion is applied to avoid unnecessary layers. The proposed approach provides physically plausible seasonal soil-resistivity scenario estimates together with Bayesian parameter and predictive uncertainty measures conditional on the adopted phenomenological model structure, thereby supporting conservative grounding-system design assessment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Hierarchical polyimide-based composite with compatible radar/dynamic infrared stealth performance
abstract: Intelligent camouflage materials with compatible radar/dynamic infrared stealth performance have become a significant and urgent concern in modern military technology. However, the fundamental contradiction between radar and infrared stealth in mechanism seriously hinders the achievement of compatibility. In this paper, a compatible radar/dynamic infrared stealth composite is successfully fabricated by combining the dynamic infrared-modulated frequency-selective surface with hierarchical polyimide-based microwave-absorbing nonwoven fabric. The formation of a sandwich-structured composite assembled from carbon nanotube and polyimide membranes promotes the realization of outstanding modulation in infrared emissivity from 0.87 to 0.34 without any deformation at 150 °C. An excellent stability of infrared modulation between 0.82 and 0.32 is maintained over 5000 cycles with a 95% modulation retention. Therefore, a dynamic infrared-modulated frequency-selective surface can be simulated and subsequently prepared by laser ablation, allowing more radar waves to enter/transmit the high-conductive composite. Meanwhile, the rational construction of hierarchical metallized polyimide-based nonwoven fabric with impedance gradient efficiently facilitates the introduction/dissipation of transmitted radar waves. It exhibits a remarkable effective absorption bandwidth of 29.9 GHz even at 250 °C. As a result, such excellent compatible radar/dynamic infrared stealth performance makes it possible to become a promising smart multi-band camouflage material. © 2026

title: Oxygen–vacancy-assisted S-scheme interface engineering toward efficient and stable solar hydrogen generation
abstract: Although the conduction band position of ZnCdS is thermodynamically favorable for proton reduction, its photocatalytic performance is limited by the rapid recombination of charge carriers and the low efficiency of charge separation. To address this issue, a ZnCdS/OV–CoCeOX heterojunction was constructed. The energy level difference between ZnCdS and CoCeOX drives the formation of an S-scheme heterojunction, promoting directional electron transfer and selective recombination of low-energy holes, and improving the efficiency of electron–hole separation. The oxygen vacancies in CoCeOX capture electrons by creating trap states, delaying recombination and providing unsaturated sites to promote the adsorption and activation of reactants. The synergistic effect of the S-scheme band alignment and the oxygen vacancies enables the effective accumulation of electrons at the active sites, promoting hydrogen production. DFT calculations and experiments confirmed that the redistribution of interface charges dominates the separation of charge carriers and the catalytic performance. After optimization, the composite material containing 20% OV–CoCeOX has an activity 5 times higher than that of a single component. This work reveals the synergistic enhancement mechanism of band matching in S-scheme heterojunctions and oxygen vacancy defects, providing new ideas for the design of efficient heterojunction catalysts. © 2026

title: System-level assessment of operational transients in PV-integrated distribution networks
abstract: The large-scale integration of photovoltaic generation introduces new electromagnetic transient challenges to distribution networks. This paper focuses on capacitor energization as a representative operational transient scenario in PV-integrated distribution networks and investigates its formation mechanism, system response, and assessment method. First, a dynamic equivalent model of capacitive operational transients is developed, revealing a dominant high-frequency damped oscillatory mode jointly determined by the grid equivalent impedance and the capacitor operating conditions. Then, based on a detailed electromagnetic transient model, the transient responses of key nodes on both the distribution network side and within the PV system are analyzed. To distinguish these transients from conventional fault ride-through scenarios, the engineering requirement of operational transient ride-through (OTRT) is introduced, and a minimal yet complete set of system-level assessment indices is established to quantitatively characterize the instantaneous electrical stress imposed by operational transients. The results provide a quantitative basis for transient safety assessment and engineering design of PV-integrated distribution networks under routine operational transients. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Influence of natural ester insulating oil on water molecules migration and aggregation behavior in oil-paper insulation systems
abstract: The hydrophilicity of natural ester insulating oil can maintain the moisture content in transformer insulating pressboard at a relatively low level. To reveal the regulatory mechanism of natural ester insulating oil on the diffusion and aggregation behavior of water molecules. This article conducted Frequency Domain Spectroscopy (FDS) tests on mineral oil and natural ester oil-paper insulation systems with varying moisture content levels. Molecular dynamics simulations were employed to analyze the diffusion behavior of water molecules in both composite systems, while quantum chemical methods were used to calculate and analyze the electrostatic potential interactions between the two types of insulating oils and water dimers. The experimental and simulation results corroborate each other, collectively revealing that the electrostatic attraction interactions, primarily driven by hydrogen bonds, between natural ester insulating oil and water molecules are stronger than the forces required for water molecules to detach from cellulose paper. The hydrophilic characteristics of natural ester insulating oil help mitigate the effects of moisture-induced aging in insulating paper and prevent the accumulation of water molecules at the oil-paper interface, thereby avoiding the formation of high-moisture zones. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Layer-by-layer assembled flexible phase-change/photothermal composite films for dual-mode thermal management
abstract: Developing phase change composite films with high thermal conductivity and robust mechanical flexibility is crucial for preventing thermal failure in electronic devices. Herein, we prepared a flexible multilayer phase change composite film (APM) with a layer-by-layer (LBL) structure to create an anisotropically thermally conductive dual-mode thermal management system by integrating reversible phase transitions with sustainable solar heating. Firstly, the microencapsulated phase change material (MPCM) and Ag-modified MPCM (Ag@MPCM) were prepared by in-situ polymerization and modification. Subsequently, the APM composite materials were fabricated via the LBL assembly technique, comprising alternating layers of MXene-poly(vinyl alcohol) (denoted as the P layer) and Ag@MPCM-MXene-sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (denoted as the N layer). Specifically, the continuous P layers govern ultra-fast in-plane thermal conduction (1.7447 W m−1 K−1) to rapidly eliminate localized hotspots, while the N layers achieve remarkable heat storage ability (104.91 J g−1). This unique decoupled synergy empowers the APM to effectively manage and buffer transient thermal shocks in electronic devices. The resulting APM exhibited excellent thermal durability, remarkable tensile strength (10.82 MPa), and achieved a favorable photothermal conversion efficiency (96%). Overall, the developed APM demonstrated considerable potential for highly efficient solar energy utilization and advanced electronic thermal management. © 2026

title: Lightweight Ti-matrix composites reinforced by graphene-derived TiCx showing superior strain-hardening capacity and strength-ductility synergy
abstract: Lightweight Ti-matrix composites (Ti-MCs) have long exhibited strain softening and low ductility due to localized deformation, which has limited their application in the aerospace industry. In this study, a graphene-derived TiCx-mediated microstructural design strategy is developed for Ti-6Al-4V matrix composites. During processing, graphene is converted in-situ into uniformly dispersed and fragmentable TiCx. Hot rolling induces nanoscale amorphous bands at fragmented TiCx contacts, while subsequent water quenching promotes a refined hierarchical α′-Ti martensitic network. During deformation, TiCx can effectively transfer load and, as a strong obstacle phase, promotes the activation of multiple slip systems in the matrix. Meanwhile, the hierarchical α′-Ti evolves from a dislocation source into an effective barrier, markedly enhancing the deformation resistance of the Ti-MCs. In addition, the amorphous bands mitigate stress concentration, and the widespread activation of <c+a> dislocations delays strain localization, which is beneficial for plastic deformation of the Ti-MCs. The proposed processing route and synergistic deformation mechanism provide practical pathways for designing damage-tolerant, lightweight Ti-MCs. © 2026
