title: Automated Indentation Geometry Detection for Hardness Measurement: A Vision-Based Nondestructive Evaluation Approach
abstract: Hardness testing is one of the most widely applied methods for evaluating the mechanical properties of metallic materials in manufacturing and quality control. Among standardized techniques, Brinell, Vickers, and Rockwell are most commonly used, all relying on precise measurement of indentation geometry. However, conventional evaluation methods still depend on manual or semi-automated readings, which are prone to operator error and unsuitable for industrial automation. This study introduces an automated framework for indentation geometry detection and measurement using two complementary strategies: a classical image processing pipeline based on OpenCV and a YOLOv10n deep learning model. To replicate realistic industrial conditions, St37 steel blocks with unpolished, roughly machined surfaces and random markings were tested under Brinell, Vickers, and Rockwell A hardness standards. A batch of microscope images was gathered, manually annotated, and subsequently expanded via data augmentation to obtain a diverse and reliable labeled image set. The classical pipeline employed brightness enhancement, thresholding, morphological filtering, and contour-based geometry extraction, while YOLOv10n was trained on the augmented dataset and refined using geometry-based post-processing. The YOLOv10n model achieved a mean average precision (detection accuracy) of 94% and reduced mean absolute error by 42–51% compared with classical image processing (p < 0.05). Furthermore, it maintained 96–97% accuracy under brightness variation, rotation, and mirroring, whereas the classical approach deteriorated to 79–84%. YOLOv10n provides a robust, precise, and scalable solution for automated hardness testing, supporting the advancement of automation in industrial quality control. ©2027 The author(s). title: Research on multi-time scale optimal scheduling of virtual power plants based on improved HHO-CVaR
abstract: To address issues such as the intermittency of renewable energy, heat-power coupling, and low-temperature degradation of energy storage in virtual power plants, this study proposes a multi-timescale optimization scheduling strategy that integrates the Improved Harris-Hawke Optimization (IHHO) with Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR). First, a refined energy storage and combined heat-power demand response framework incorporating low-temperature correction is established; second, wind and solar scenarios are generated using Latin hypercube sampling combined with synchronous back-propagation pruning, and economic risk is quantified using CVaR; Finally, To address the high-dimensionality, multi-modality, and strong constraints inherent in VPP scheduling, a triple-mechanism IHHO algorithm—coordinated across the iteration, population, and individual dimensions—is proposed for the day-ahead and short-term dual-scale scheduling model. Its statistical reliability and the generalization robustness of the resulting scheduling scheme were verified through multiple repeated experiments, out-of-sample testing, and extreme scenario validation. The results of the case studies demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms traditional models in reducing curtailment rates and improving economic efficiency and robustness. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Atomistic origins of the sluggish cathodic reduction of α-FeOOH in atmospheric rust layers: A first-principles study
abstract: α-FeOOH is the predominant protective phase in atmospheric rust layers, yet the atomistic origins of its sluggish cathodic reduction remain unclear. Here, first-principles calculations elucidate its preferred surface state, electron-accepting ability, and reduction pathway. Dissociative water adsorption is favored over [H+/Cl–] and [H+/HSO3–] adsorption on α-FeOOH(110), yielding the lowest surface energy among the examined states (0.602 J/m2). The resulting hydroxylated surface has an electron affinity of 3.928 eV, lower than those of representative β-FeOOH·[H+/Cl–]0.167 (4.886 eV) and [H+/HSO3–]-modified γ-FeOOH (5.228 eV), indicating weaker electron uptake. Upon electron injection, charge localizes on Fe sites, causing Fe(III)-to-Fe(II) reduction, FeO6 expansion, and Fe-OH weakening. OH− removal, adjacent-OH condensation, and lattice rearrangement then drive transformation toward inverse-spinel Fe3O4. Adjacent-OH condensation to form H2O* is the rate-determining step, with a barrier of 1.227 eV. Thus, the stable hydroxylated surface, weak electron uptake, and hindered dehydration explain the sluggish reduction of α-FeOOH. © 2026

title: Porphyrin-based covalent organic frameworks with tunable conductivity for intelligent multi-signal formaldehyde monitoring
abstract: The development of intelligent multi-signal gas monitoring systems requires the synergistic integration of high-performance sensing materials and advanced signal-processing architectures. Herein, porphyrin-based covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with dimension-regulated conductivity were developed as electroactive materials for room-temperature formaldehyde (HCHO) detection and integrated into a multi-signal monitoring platform for environmental surveillance. Specifically, three porphyrin-based COFs (3D-MnPor-COF, 2D-MnPor-COF, and 1D-MnPor-COF) with tunable conductivity and controllable dimensionality were synthesized through rational precursor engineering. Compared with the 1D and 2D counterparts, which mainly provide directional diffusion pathways and molecular selectivity, the 3D COF features an ordered isotropic network of interconnected cage-like nanochannels, thereby exposing more Mn−N4 sites. Consequently, when integrated with pencil-drawn paper-based interdigitated electrodes, three flexible gas sensors exhibited sensitive responses toward HCHO, featuring wide detection ranges (0.05−100 ppm), low detection limits (13, 28, and 22 ppb), and excellent mechanical flexibility. Furthermore, theoretical and experimental analyses clarified the relationship between framework dimensionality and sensing performance. Inspired by the human central nervous system, a homo-spatiotemporal multi-signal intelligent monitoring system integrated with “AND” molecular logic-gate operations was further developed to enable self-correction of sensing signals, as well as remote real-time HCHO monitoring and intelligent warning in household environments. This work not only provides an effective strategy for modulating COF conductivity through dimensional engineering, but also establishes a versatile platform for next-generation intelligent Internet of Things-based multi-signal monitoring systems. © 2026

title: Cr/Eu dual doping synergistically promotes reconstruction: Polymetallic MOFs-derived highly active oxyhydroxide for efficient oxygen evolution reaction
abstract: Exploring the design and synthesis strategies of high‑performance MOF catalysts is of great significance for energy conversion technologies. Herein, bimetallic to pentametallic MOF arrays grown on iron foam were synthesized at room temperature using 1,3,5‑benzenetricarboxylic acid as the ligand via a sacrificial pre‑programmed template method. The optimized pentametallic CoNiFeCrEu‑MOF exhibits a low overpotential of 197 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm−2, along with stability exceeding 240 h at 100 mA cm−2. Through a combination of multiple characterizations and theoretical calculations, we reveal that Cr doping, together with its vigorous dissolution during activation, promotes the conversion of Co(II) in the MOFs to Co(III), whereas Eu accelerates the oxidation of Ni(II) and Fe(II) by facilitating electron transfer from Fe and Ni to Co. The dual‑doping engineering significantly promotes the formation of amorphous M(III)OOH, while optimizing the adsorption energies of *OH and *OOH intermediates, thereby accounting for the enhanced OER performance. These findings provide insights into the formation of active oxyhydroxide phases and the synergistic effects of multi‑metal components in MOFs during the OER, offering a viable strategy to enhance water splitting efficiency. © 2026

title: Evaluation of voltage sag tolerance capability for sensitive equipment based on hybrid density method
abstract: Evaluating the voltage-sag ride-through capability of sensitive equipment is important for voltage-sag mitigation. To address the issues of insufficient accuracy and cumbersome solving processes in existing evaluation methods, an evaluation method for assessing the voltage sag tolerance capability of sensitive equipment based on Hybrid Density is proposed in this paper. First, the fuzzy characteristics of the ride-through capability of sensitive equipment are analyzed, and fuzzy variables are transformed into random variables using the Hybrid Density method, with their distribution functions being obtained. Second, failure probabilities of the random variables are evaluated by combining the total probability integral and the Gauss–Hermite method. Finally, based on the IEEE 30-bus system, the failure probability of sensitive equipment is evaluated. The results show that the proposed evaluation method balances computational efficiency and accuracy, enabling a fast and accurate assessment of the ride-through capability of sensitive equipment. © 2026

title: A novel fast and secure detection algorithm for loss of excitation (LOE) protection in synchronous generators
abstract: Loss of excitation (LOE) events have the potential to seriously harm the generator and the power system. The impedance trajectory seen by the generator terminal was mostly used in the first applicable LOE detection systems, which had many disadvantages such as slow performance and mal-operation during SPS. Thus, this work presents a new setting-free LOE detection method that is quick and secure. For this aim, three distinct novel indices are created by applying the derivative of various values, seen from the generator terminal, including: resistance (R), reactance (X), reactive power (Q), and flux (φ). In order to achieve the most suitable index, the operation of them have been evaluated through the simulation of multiple situations, taking into account all of the suggested indices. It is important to note that, MATLAB software has been employed for all the simulations that were conducted. According to the final results, the third suggested index, which is based on applying the derivative of R, Q, and φ, operates the best. When compared to conventional impedance-based and also other methods, the aforementioned index exhibits significantly greater speed and accuracy in detecting LOE and also reliable discrimination of LOE with stable power swing (SPS). © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Simultaneous fault classification and location estimation in transmission lines using wavelet-based features and a MTL-LSTM network
abstract: Accurate fault classification and location in transmission lines are essential for improving the reliability and protection performance of modern power systems. Conventional fault location techniques based on impedance or traveling waves often suffer from reduced accuracy under varying operating conditions and fault scenarios. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid intelligent framework based on a Multitask Learning Long Short-Term Memory (MTL-LSTM) neural network for simultaneous fault classification and fault location estimation in transmission lines. First, power system is modeled in PSCAD/EMTDC to generate a comprehensive dataset of fault conditions. Different types of faults conditions including single-line-to-ground (SLG), line-to-line (LL), double-line-to-ground (LLG), three-phase (LLL), and three-phase-to-ground (LLLG) faults with different fault impedances are simulated at multiple locations along the transmission lines. Three-phase voltage and current signals are recorded and processed in MATLAB. To capture transient characteristics of fault signals, the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) is applied to extract informative features from voltage and current waveforms. These features are then used as inputs to a MTL-LSTM network designed to perform both fault type classification and fault location estimation simultaneously. In addition to wavelet-based transient features, physics-based indicators derived from conventional fault analysis are incorporated as auxiliary inputs, enabling the network to learn nonlinear relationships between multiple fault-related features and the actual fault characteristics. The proposed method achieves about 89% fault classification accuracy while maintaining the fault location error below 1% of the transmission line length. Furthermore, comprehensive performance evaluations, including robustness analysis under noisy conditions, sensitivity analysis under high-resistance faults, and potential generalization to diverse power system configurations, demonstrate the method's effectiveness and reliability for real-world intelligent transmission line protection. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Envelope-like structured TiAl alloy with deformation-induced γ nano-grids for high-temperature strength-ductility synergy
abstract: Coarse lamellae are unable to generate sufficient dislocations and nanotwins, leading to reduced strength and ductility. In this study, a novel multiphase envelope-like microstructure, consisting of γE phases surrounding fine lamellar colonies, was obtained through heat treatment, providing favorable multiphase interfaces for dynamic nano-defect formation. The high-temperature deformation mechanisms of the TiAl alloy were investigated by in-situ experiments. Results show that γ shear bands form through Al/Ti interdiffusion-assisted multicomponent redistribution, while γ nanotwins nucleate and propagate via (1¯11)<11¯2] twinning dislocations slipping. First-principles calculations reveal that coherent twin boundaries correspond to a local energy minimum on the γ-surface, confirming twinning as a stable deformation mode. The dynamically formed γ nano-grids effectively hinder crack propagation, whereas the 60° interlocking dislocation structure within the γE phase promotes coordinated plastic deformation. Owing to the synergistic effects of γ nano-grids, dislocation activity, and lamellar interfaces, the alloy exhibits excellent high-temperature mechanical properties, with tensile strength increasing to 624 MPa at 850 °C and maintaining 527 MPa at 900 °C, and elongation improving from 2.13% to 12.54%. © 2026

title: Diffusion kinetics and atomistic migration mechanisms of order transition driven by third-element dopants in L10-FePt alloys
abstract: Third-element doping is an effective strategy for promoting low-temperature L10 ordering in FePt nanoparticles, but the underlying dopant-regulated diffusion kinetics and atomic migration mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. In this work, density functional theory (DFT) calculations and experiments are combined to elucidate these processes. The calculations reveal distinct defect-mediated diffusion mechanisms. Fe preferentially migrates through nearest-neighbor vacancy jumping, whereas Pt favours a lower-energy antisite-assisted pathway. A five-step strategy integrating thermodynamic, structural, magnetic, and ordering-transition screening with DFT prediction and experimental verification is established to identify promising dopants. Large-radius dopants reduce migration barriers by more than 20% and enhance low-temperature diffusion coefficients by over three orders of magnitude. Atomic radius is identified as the dominant geometric descriptor of migration barriers, while electronegativity and valence electron number provide secondary electronic contributions. Experimental results further support the predicted trends. Large-radius elements, such as Bi and Pb, can promote L10 ordering at low temperatures and achieve a high ordering degree and coercivity. In contrast, Mn shows limited ordering, whereas Co-, Ni-, and Cu-doped systems retain the disordered fcc phase, which is broadly consistent with the calculated trends. This work provides a framework for dopant selection and low-temperature synthesis of ordered intermetallic nanoparticles. © 2026

title: Thermally driven oxygen-vacancy localization at step edges for nanoscale vertical transport in epitaxial oxide thin films
abstract: Vertical charge transport is a key functionality in atomically thin oxide films for nanoscale electronic devices, but it is highly sensitive to local potential variations induced by oxygen vacancy defects. In epitaxial oxide thin films, intrinsic step-and-terrace structures can disrupt the uniformity of oxygen-vacancy distributions, yet how such non-uniformity emerges and affects local vertical transport remains unclear. Herein, we demonstrate that oxygen vacancies spontaneously localize at step edges, leading to edge-enhanced vertical transport. Using single-crystalline non-polar SrTiO3 thin films as a model system, we spatially resolve vacancy-associated vertical transport at step edges using light-assisted conducting atomic force microscopy. At vacancy-enriched step edges, vertical transport is enhanced through a defect-mediated conduction mechanism distinct from direct tunneling. Our density functional theory calculations and diffusion-trapping modeling reveal that step edges are energetically favorable sites for oxygen vacancies, accounting for their accumulation during post-growth cooling. These results show that thermally driven defect redistribution governs spatially confined vertical transport, offering a strategy for harnessing edge-localized conduction channels in ultrathin electronic and quantum devices. © 2026

title: Faulty feeder selection for high impedance faults in resonant grounding systems via physics-guided neural networks with physical posterior verification
abstract: To address noise susceptibility and the lack of physical interpretability in detecting high impedance faults (HIFs) in resonant grounding systems, this paper proposes a novel fault feeder selection method combining Physics-Guided Neural Networks (PGNNs) and posterior verification. First, a PGNN-based framework performs unsupervised parameter identification using the healthy feeders’ zero-sequence current analytical solution. The faulty feeder exhibits physical model mismatch, identified via parameter drift and quantified by a Cumulative Absolute Distance Difference (CADD) metric. Subsequently, a posterior verification mechanism based on Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) synthesizes the theoretical fault current, strictly validating the selection via waveform reconstruction error. Extensive validations on 10 kV substation simulations and field data demonstrate that this approach achieves robust, physically interpretable fault diagnosis, accurately identifying faulty feeders even under severe 5 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) or worse conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Co-condensation engineering of hydrophobic and mechanically robust alumina aerogels for thermal protection under extreme conditions
abstract: Alumina aerogels have emerged as promising candidates for high-temperature thermal protection but suffer from mechanical fragility and hydrophilicity. Herein, we report a co-condensation strategy involving an inorganic aluminum precursor, methyltriethoxysilane (MTES), and polyvinyltrimethoxysilane (PVTMS) to fabricate alumina-based aerogels with a network of hydrocarbon chains and methyl-functionalized aluminosiloxanes. PVTMS provides multiple hydrolyzable silane sites and a polymeric backbone that enhance skeleton connectivity and stress redistribution, while MTES-derived methyl groups reduce surface polarity. At an intermediate PVTMS content, Al-SiMPV0.25 achieves the best balance of compressive robustness, thermal stability, and superhydrophobicity. Under hygrothermal exposure, its reinforced skeleton resists structural degradation, while the low-polarity surface limits moisture uptake and water-assisted thermal coupling, thereby preserving structural integrity and low thermal conductivity. The retained nanoporous framework suppresses gas-phase and solid-phase heat transport, while the aluminosilicate network attenuates radiative penetration through infrared extinction at elevated temperatures. Ultimately, under one-sided heating, Al-SiMPV0.25 maintains an approximately 731 °C temperature difference between the hot (∼980 °C) and cold (∼249 °C) faces. This work provides a route to durable oxide aerogels for humid and high-temperature environments. © 2026

title: Unlocking high work-hardening in multilayered bimodal ZnCu/ZnMg biodegradable composites for bone implants
abstract: Zinc (Zn) and its alloys are considered promising biodegradable metallic implant materials due to their moderate degradation rate, excellent biocompatibility, and multiple biofunctional properties. However, Zn alloys produced through conventional alloying and thermoplastic-deformation processes typically exhibit limited work-hardening capability, which constrains their clinical applicability. Heterostructure materials, characterized by unique microstructural architectures and strengthening mechanisms, provide a promising strategy to concurrently improve the strength and work-hardening capability of Zn-based materials. In this study, a series of multilayered Zn-4Cu (ZC)/Zn-0.5Mg (ZM) composite samples with bimodal grain size and varied layer thickness were successfully prepared using accumulative roll bonding (ARB) followed by annealing at 280 °C for 5 min. The grains in the ZM layer grew up to 3.7 ± 1.9 µm, whereas the ZC layer retained fine grains (∼1 μm) in the annealed ZC/ZM composites. This multilayered bimodal structure, consisting of regions with distinct grain sizes and hardness, caused additional hetero-deformation-induced strengthening during tensile deformation, contributing ∼60% of the flow stress. Notably, the ZC1/ZM2 composite sample subjected to 4 ARB cycles after annealing showed a marked increase in uniform elongation from 6.5% ± 0.4% to 15.6% ± 0.3%, while the ZC2/ZM1 composite sample subjected to 8 ARB cycles after annealing achieved the highest yield stress of 343.5 ± 1.1 MPa. Furthermore, these composites exhibited good biocompatibility and antibacterial properties. © 2026

title: An explainable quantum neural network framework for reservoir permeability prediction from conventional well logs
abstract: Accurate prediction of reservoir permeability is essential for reservoir characterization, production forecasting, and hydrocarbon recovery optimization. Conventional empirical and machine learning approaches often struggle to capture the complex nonlinear relationships between petrophysical variables while providing limited model interpretability. This study presents an explainable permeability prediction framework based on a variational Quantum Neural Network (QNN) simulated on classical hardware using the PennyLane quantum machine learning platform. The proposed framework integrates Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) to improve model transparency and facilitate geological interpretation of the learned relationships. A total of 3213 depth-matched samples acquired from three wells in the Mpyo Field, Albertine Graben, Uganda, were used to develop and evaluate the model using five conventional well-log measurements: thermal neutron porosity (TNPH), effective porosity (PHIE), formation density (RHOZ), spectral gamma ray (SGR), and shale volume (VSH). Hyperparameters of the QNN were optimized through systematic grid search and compared with a classical Group Method of Data Handling (GMDH), Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Regression (SVR) models under identical experimental conditions. The simulated QNN achieved superior predictive accuracy, yielding training RMSE and MAE values of 0.019 and 0.0105, respectively, while demonstrating improved generalization on a blind test well compared with the benchmark model. SHAP analysis identified effective porosity as the dominant predictor of permeability, followed by thermal neutron porosity and spectral gamma ray, with feature contributions remaining consistent with established petrophysical principles. Bootstrap-based uncertainty analysis further demonstrated reliable prediction intervals across different reservoir intervals. Although implemented on a classical simulator rather than physical quantum hardware, the proposed framework illustrates the potential of quantum-inspired learning architectures for nonlinear permeability prediction while maintaining model interpretability for practical reservoir characterization. © 2026 The Authors. title: Fracture propagation law of shale rocks using pre-fracturing technology with supercritical CO2 fluids of different volumes
abstract: Shale reservoirs are intrinsically tight, and conventional fracturing generally induces substantial reservoir damage while only simple fracture geometries are generated. This study investigated the effects of supercritical CO2 (Sc-CO2) volumes on artificial fracture morphology and propagation law during Sc-CO2 pre-injection gel fracturing. A true triaxial fracturing apparatus, combined with micro-CT and coupled thermal-hydraulic-mechanical-damage (THMD) numerical model were applied to elaborate characters of fracture initiation pressures and geometries after using different volumes of Sc-CO2 during pre-injection gel fracturing. The physical and numerical simulation analyses revealed the fracture propagation law that is associated with Sc-CO2 pre-fracturing. The results are as follows: (1) Sc-CO2 pre-injection effectively reduced the fracture initiation pressure by 12.7% as the pre-injection volume increased from 0 to 88.61 mL; (2) greater pre-injection volumes of Sc-CO2 enhanced fracture complexity degree, reflected by that the indexes of fractal dimension, tortuosity, and volume of the induced artificial fractures; (3) the THMD model was successfully validated, which can accurately predict fracture propagation morphology, fracture area ratio, and fractal dimension; (4) both the physical and numerical simulations indicated that, the fracture apertures increased from 0.09 mm to 0.15 mm, as the pre-injection volumes of Sc-CO2 increased from 14.53 to 88.61 mL; (5) fracture propagation exhibits a nonlinear dependence on Sc-CO2 pre-injection volume, characterized by weakly activated, effectively activated, and saturation-activated patterns. These findings provide systematic guidance for optimizing the process parameters of Sc-CO2 pre-fracturing in shale reservoirs. © 2026 The Authors. title: Directed biosynthesis of the designer peptidyl nucleoside antibiotics featuring a simplified azetidine-containing moiety
abstract: Fungal and fungal-like pathogen infections pose escalating threats to the global one-health, thus underscoring the urgent need to reverse this trend by accelerating the development of novel antifungal drugs. Polyoxin (POL), a group of structurally related nucleoside antibiotics, is an eco-friendly fungicide targeting fungal cell wall biosynthesis. However, the chemical diversity and therapeutic potential of this antibiotic has remained underexplored. Here, we report the rational design of a series of POL analogs that feature a simplified azetidine-containing moiety, and we have further realized the directed biosynthesis of them using an industrial POL producer as cell factory. Notably, three analogs (POL-AX, POL-HX, and POL-KX), featuring a l -A2CA ( l -azetidine-2-carboxylic acid) moiety, exhibit enhanced inhibitory activity against Candida albicans and even the oomycete plant pathogen Phytophthora sojae . Moreover, systematic molecular docking analyses reveal that the three POL analogs can be better accommodated to the active pocket of the chitin synthases, directly contributing to the improved inhibitory activity of the designer POL analogs. The study provides the basis for the rational access of next-generation agents targeting chitin biosynthesis. © 2026 The Authors.

title: High internal phase Pickering emulsions stabilized by plant protein and polysaccharide composite particles: Construction, stability, application, and research advance
abstract: High internal phase Pickering emulsions (HIPPEs) stabilized by plant protein-polysaccharide composite particles represent a core innovation direction in the field of plant-based foods. Physicochemical structures of composite particles can be directionally regulated via molecular modification, covalent/non-covalent crosslinking, and physical modification methods including ultrasonication and high-pressure homogenization, thereby compensating the functional defects of single protein or polysaccharide. Formed by a dual-network composed of particulate interfacial film and continuous phase gel, HIPPEs possess prominent storage stability, antioxidant capacity, digestive stability and sustained release capacity of bioactive substances. Benefiting from solid-like rheological properties and high encapsulation loading capacity, HIPPEs can be applied to artificial plant-based fats, delivery carriers for functional factors and 3D-printable edible materials, facilitating the industrialization of healthy plant-based foods. There are still bottlenecks restricting the industrial application of this system at present: inherent off-flavors of raw materials impair product sensory quality, in vitro digestion models fail to reproduce real in vivo digestive behaviors, and large-scale production is limited by process scaling, batch variations of raw materials and high production costs. Subsequent research should be guided by green sustainability. Low-cost raw materials such as grain-oil processing by-products need to be developed, and the technical challenges of deodorization and decolorization should be addressed. Integrating soft matter physics, artificial intelligence and molecular simulation technologies can precisely match raw materials, preparation processes and emulsion performances. Relying on its edible and biodegradable structural merits, HIPPEs can break the limitations of food applications and expand to biomedicine and eco-friendly materials, broadening its industrial application scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: ‘Rigid-flexible hybrid’ epoxy resin with superior curing performance, fire safety, and toughness
abstract: The rapid advancement of aerospace, electronics, and electrical industries has imposed increasingly stringent requirements on the fire safety and mechanical properties of epoxy (EP) resins. However, traditional additive flame retardants suffer from low efficiency, and their excessive incorporation often leads to deterioration in the mechanical properties of EP. Therefore, the development of intrinsically flame-retardant EP has emerged as an important research direction. Herein, a flame-retardant co-curing agent, N-(2-(bis(2-aminoethyl)amino)ethyl)-P, P-diphenylphosphinic amide (BADP), was synthesized and introduced into the EP matrix to construct a ‘rigid-flexible hybrid’ crosslinking network. When the phosphorus content was only 0.6 wt.%, the resultant EP sample (EPBP4) achieved a vertical burning (UL-94) V-0 rating with a limiting oxygen index of 36.3%. Compared with pure EP, the peak heat release rate and total heat release of EPBP4 declined by 43.3% and 24.9%, respectively. These results demonstrate a significant enhancement in fire safety performance, which can be attributed to the char‑forming promotion effect of BADP. In addition, EPBP4 exhibited 113.0% and 34.7% improvements in impact strength and flexural strength, owing to the construction of a ‘rigid-flexible hybrid’ network. Overall, EPBP4 achieved an excellent balance between flame retardancy and mechanical properties, demonstrating strong potential for applications in electrical and electronic, aerospace, and other emerging advanced industries. © 2026

title: Joint clearing strategy for power-carbon-frequency regulation markets considering dynamic carbon pricing and green certificate mechanisms
abstract: To promote multi-market integration and drive the low-carbon transformation of the energy system, this paper focuses on the coordinated operation of the electricity-carbon-ancillary service market. It introduces a dynamic carbon pricing mechanism to reflect real-time carbon cost signals and incorporates a green certificate trading mechanism to incentivize clean energy consumption. A bi-level joint market clearing model considering the dynamic carbon pricing mechanism and the green certificate mechanism is established. The upper-level model aims to maximize energy system profits, obtaining optimal bidding strategies by incorporating declared capacity and price constraints. The lower-level model seeks to minimize system operating costs, determining the optimal clearing prices and winning quantities for each market based on constraints such as power balance, carbon balance, frequency regulation balance, and market clearing rules. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed joint clearing mechanism effectively increases clean energy consumption by 73.90%, reduces carbon emissions by 26.88%, and enhances total profits by 10.22%. Additionally, it guides flexible resources to participate in frequency regulation ancillary services through electricity-carbon price signals, promoting the synergistic achievement of economic and environmental objectives. This research provides theoretical support for the collaborative design and policy formulation of multi-markets under the new power system. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Numerical investigations of electromagnetic time reversal for locating partial discharge in power transformers using a stable discontinuous Galerkin time-domain method
abstract: The localization of partial discharge (PD) inducing ultra-high frequency (UHF) electromagnetic radiation is crucial for the safety of power transformers. Compared with conventional localization techniques based on the time difference of arrival (TDOA) of UHF signals, the emerging electromagnetic time reversal (EMTR) methods are less sensitive to noise and more accurate under the complex geometry of transformers, hence are promising alternatives. However, the postprocessing of UHF signals in TDOA-based methods is straightforward, yet in EMTR framework, the counterpart is transient electromagnetic analysis with heavy computational overheads. In this paper, a discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) solver with novel time integration schemes is proposed to overcome the efficiency bottleneck. The essence is that the lossy terms in governing equations are discretized via implicit Crank–Nicolson (CN) method, while the remaining terms are integrated by explicit Runge–Kutta (RK) methods, so that the impact of the conductive media in transformers on the time-step size vanishes without spoiling the favorable explicit nature of the classic DGTD method. The performance of the EMTR method using the proposed CN–RK-DGTD solver is demonstrated in the PD localization in a three-phase transformer, and the influences of the position and number of UHF sensors, PD locations, noise, etc., are further investigated numerically. Subsequently, the feasibility of the proposed EMTR-based method for locating PD in an actual complex transformer is verified experimentally. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A functionally synergistic sequential-response bilayer coating strategy for enhanced thermal protection of epoxy-based carbon fiber composites
abstract: Carbon fiber-reinforced epoxy composites (CFEP) possess excellent lightweight and high-strength properties; however, their resin matrix is flammable and lacks sufficient fire protection capabilities. To improve the fire safety and post-combustion structural integrity of CFEP, a bilayer protective system consisting of an intumescent flame-retardant coating (IFC) and a ceramicizable thermal-insulation coating (CTIC) was constructed in this work. Compared to single-layer coatings, the Bi-IFC/CTIC system exhibits superior comprehensive flame-retardant performance, with its LOI increased to 32.4% and achieving UL-94 V-0 rating. The bilayer coating also effectively reduces the CFEP's PHRR (69.4%), THR (47.4%), and TSR (20.7%), demonstrating optimal flame-retardant and smoke-suppressing effects. Direct flame impact tests indicate that the bilayer coating's char layer can stably support an applied weight, demonstrating greater char layer strength. Furthermore, Bi-IFC/CTIC can control the back-surface temperature of the CFEP at 201 °C and maintain a post-combustion flexural strength retention rate of 88.7%. Overall, the Bi-IFC/CTIC system constructs an efficient and stable composite thermal-protection barrier through a sequential-response mechanism of outer-layer charring via expansion and inner-layer ceramic reinforcement, thereby significantly improving the fire safety and structural reliability of CFEP under fire exposure. © 2026

title: System-level frequency stability enhancement in solar PV-dominated low-inertia power systems using robust nonlinear control
abstract: The rapid integration of inverter-based resources (IBRs) is changing the dynamic behaviour of modern power systems. As synchronous generators are replaced by photovoltaic (PV) inverters, system inertia decreases and frequency stability becomes more difficult to maintain. This paper compares proportional-integral (PI) control and sliding mode control (SMC) for PV inverter regulation in an IEEE 9-bus test system. Synchronous generators are progressively replaced by PV inverters to represent low and high IBR penetration levels. In both cases, active power sharing is provided through frequency-based droop control. Four MATLAB/Simulink scenarios are studied under 10% and 15% load disturbances. The results show that PI control provides smoother and better-damped responses under low IBR penetration. However, its performance deteriorates when penetration level and disturbance magnitude increase. In contrast, SMC improves the frequency nadir and shortens the recovery time under high-penetration and large-disturbance conditions. These findings show that PI and SMC have complementary operating characteristics. PI is more suitable for moderate operating conditions, while SMC provides stronger robustness in low-inertia scenarios. The results provide practical guidance for controller selection in renewable-dominated power systems. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: A one-end current-based method for single line to ground fault location in the stitched transmission lines
abstract: Due to economic constraints and the limited availability of bays in high-voltage substations, some transmission and sub-transmission networks employ stitched lines—a special configuration of double-circuit lines connected to a single bay at both ends. Although these lines offer cost and space advantages, they present significant challenges for fault location because the currents of the two circuits cannot be measured separately. So far, no one-end fault location method has been proposed for fault location in stitched lines. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel impedance-based fault location method that utilizes negative- and zero-sequence networks and relies solely on current measurements from one end of the line to locate single-line-to-ground faults. The method's performance is evaluated for single-line-to-ground faults in different phases, locations, and fault resistances, while considering uncertainties in Thevenin and line impedances, as well as the effects of noise, variations in sampling frequency, fault inception angle, and fault clearing time. Simulation results demonstrate that the method achieves high accuracy, with an average error below 1% in most cases, confirming its effectiveness and reliability for fault location in stitched transmission lines. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Achieving thermally stable subgrain microstructures with superior strength-ductility synergy in dilute Al-Mn alloys via a low-temperature homogenization strategy
abstract: To address challenges associated with coarse-grained microstructures and inadequate mechanical properties in conventional dilute Al-Mn alloys, the present study has designed a low-temperature homogenization strategy aimed at generating a higher volume fraction of α-Al(Mn, Fe)Si dispersoids within the Al matrix. Owing to the strong Zener pinning pressure exerted by these dense dispersoids, long-range grain boundary migration is effectively suppressed during extrusion, thereby promoting the formation of a fine subgrain structure. Remarkably, this subgrain structure demonstrates exceptional thermal stability even after exposure to elevated temperatures as high as 500 °C. During plastic deformation, the abundant low-angle grain boundaries continuously emit dislocations, while the α-Al(Mn, Fe)Si dispersoids pin dislocations and hinder dynamic recovery, thereby enhancing both dislocation multiplication and storage. Compared with its conventional coarse-grained counterpart, dilute Al-Mn alloy fabricated via the novel low-temperature homogenization strategy exhibits an excellent synergy of strength, ductility, and thermal stability. This study offers an innovative perspective for the advancement of dilute Al alloys with superior comprehensive performance. © 2026

title: Advanced AI and deep learning enabled techniques for anomaly detection in EV charging behavior using real-time household smart meter data
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EV) are critical for monitoring and maintaining the health, performance, and safety of electric vehicle batteries. However, these systems often face challenges due to unexpected faults, irregular battery behaviour, and noisy sensor data, which lead to inaccurate monitoring or potential system failures. In this manuscript, Advanced AI and Deep Learning Enabled Techniques for Anomaly Detection in EV Charging Behavior Using Real-Time Household Smart Meter Data (AD-DBMS-EV-SIGNN) is proposed. Initially, real-time electricity consumption data collected from smart meters installed in 900 households is utilized to detect anomalies in EV charging behavior by capturing grid-level voltage, current, and power fluctuation patterns, reflecting the impact of EV charging load on the home grid. Under Robust Consensus Tobit Kalman Filtering (RCTKF), then the input data is pre-processing for cleaning, normalization and denoising. The pre-processed data is given to the Spike Induced Graph Neural Network (SIGNN) to accurately detect anomalies in EV Charging Behavior. Generally speaking, SIGNN does not include any adaptation of optimization techniques for identifying the best parameters to guarantee precise anomaly detection in EV systems. Therefore, SIGNN is optimized under the House Swallow Optimizer (HSO) to accurately identify anomalies in EV Charging Behavior. The performance of the proposed AD-DBMS-EV-SIGNN method is 99.43% for accuracy, 98.14% for precision, and 98.37% for recall when compared to other existing methods. © 2026

title: Fermentation-driven remodeling of whey macromolecules: Mechanisms, functional outcomes, and industrial implications
abstract: Whey, a protein- and carbohydrate-rich dairy byproduct, presents significant valorization potential yet remains largely underutilized due to the high cost and energy intensity of conventional fractionation technologies. Fermentation offers a biologically driven, scalable alternative that fundamentally remodels whey macromolecules through microbially mediated enzymatic and metabolic cascades. This review critically examines fermentation-induced structural, conformational, and interactional modifications of whey proteins, glycoproteins, and associated carbohydrate fractions. We delineate how strain-specific proteolytic systems, pH-dependent conformational unfolding, and non-proteolytic transformations (e.g., glycation, phenolic–protein complexation, and microbial transglycosylation) govern macromolecular hydration, interfacial behavior, and network assembly. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic evidence demonstrates that optimal bioactivity and matrix stability emerge at a substrate-dependent degree of hydrolysis: 8–12% for sweet whey (native protein conformation), 6–10% for acid whey (partially denatured proteins), and 10–15% for pre-heat-treated whey (exposed hydrophobic domains). Beyond these thresholds, excessive cleavage compromises functional epitopes, triggers bitterness via hydrophobic 3–8 residue peptides, or exposes neo-allergens. By establishing a structure–function framework for fermentation-mediated whey remodeling, this work positions microbial bioprocessing as a precision tool for engineering next-generation hydrocolloid-functionalized dairy matrices, aligning with circular bioeconomy and sustainable food system objectives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Interface-stabilized MXene/nanofiber film for integrated thermoelectric sensing and electromagnetic interference shielding
abstract: The rapid proliferation of wearable electronics demands materials that enable simultaneous physiological monitoring and protection against electromagnetic interference (EMI), yet these functions are typically decoupled into separate components. Here, we report an interface-stabilized thermoplastic polyurethane/pluronic F127/MXene/poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) nanofiber film treated with dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), denoted TFMPD, for thermoelectric sensing, EMI shielding, and shielding-state feedback. F127-mediated surface hydrophilization and polyethyleneimine activation promote MXene deposition on the nanofiber film, while DMSO treatment reorganizes PEDOT:PSS and consolidates the conductive coating through solvent-assisted fiber welding. The film shows thermoelectric voltage responses to small temperature differences, with a temperature resolution of 0.07 K and a response time of ∼410 ms, enabling self-powered respiration and body-temperature monitoring. The same conductive network achieves an X-band EMI shielding effectiveness of ∼44 dB with reflection-dominated attenuation and retains stable shielding performance after 5000 bending cycles and three months of ambient exposure. By correlating sheet resistance with EMI shielding degradation, the film further enables resistance-based evaluation of healthy, warning, and failure-risk states. This work provides a flexible conductive-interface strategy for wearable systems requiring thermal-signal monitoring, EMI protection, and service-state feedback. © 2026

title: A data-driven framework based on signal processing and transformer model for fault detection, classification, and localization in microgrids
abstract: This paper proposes an integrated machine learning framework for fault detection, classification, and localization in microgrids, utilizing a hybrid Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Transformer architecture. To eliminate the need for complex voltage sensing equipment (i.e., potential transformers), the framework relies on current measurements, thereby reducing both data acquisition costs and computational complexity during training. In the proposed scheme, transient features are extracted from current signals via VMD and fed into a Transformer model to identify patterns associated with various states. The framework is evaluated under diverse operating conditions, including different fault types, load variations, changes in the generation level of distributed sources, and noisy environments. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a fault localization accuracy of 99.57% and a detection and classification accuracy of 99.13%, maintaining a high accuracy of 98.08% even under a Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of 10 dB. Furthermore, the model issues tripping commands in <25 ms (under 1.5 cycles), outperforming conventional models that require >30–35 ms. These findings confirm the framework's reliability, speed, and robustness for microgrid protection and monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Sample-preserving evaluation and frozen rank consensus for UAV transmission-line anomaly detection under detector uncertainty
abstract: Unsupervised anomaly detection for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) power-line inspection aims to identify defective assets using models trained only on normal data. In detector-derived region-of-interest (ROI) pipelines, however, upstream localization errors can silently remove difficult samples, alter crop geometry, and make retained-subset metrics overstate full-population performance. This study presents FRC-KARP (Frozen Rank Consensus with Keep-All Region Priors), a reliability-oriented evaluation and consensus framework rather than a new anomaly-feature extractor. FRC-KARP combines three elements: a strict sample-preserving full-population protocol, frozen percentile-rank consensus over raw-image and region-prior score streams using fixed equal weights, and a separate detector-conditioned reliability audit for retained-subset bias, aggregation-rule sensitivity, and crop completeness. The audit reads frozen scores and ROI metadata after score export; it neither feeds back to nor changes the final FRC-KARP score. No fitted fusion weights, anomalous training samples, or test-label-tuned stream selections are used. On the primary InsPLAD object-centric glass-insulator/missingcap task, FRC-KARP achieves AUROC 0.8870, AP 0.4893, and Max F1 0.6058 over all 671 test images. On two additional InsPLAD asset tasks, it gives the highest AUROC among the three reported outputs and raises the three-task macro AUROC to 0.8519. Under controlled image shifts and 10–30% proposal dropout, performance degrades measurably, but FRC-KARP loses less AUROC than the Padded-ROI stream. The evidence supports sample-preserving reliability analysis within InsPLAD; external-domain and genuine full-frame UAV generalization remain unverified. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Biosynthesis of vanillin glucoside in Escherichia coli
abstract: Vanillin is a widely used flavor compound in the food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical industries. Although microbial biosynthesis offers a green alternative to conventional chemical synthesis, challenges such as unstable heterologous enzyme expression, insufficient methyl donor supply, and product cytotoxicity limit de novo production. Here, we engineered Escherichia coli to produce vanillyl alcohol, vanillin, and vanillin glucoside directly from glycerol. Genomic integration of the alcohol dehydrogenase ADH6 and multi-copy of the caffeic acid O -methyltransferase COMT gene eliminated the need for plasmid-based expression, yielding 1.09 g/L vanillyl alcohol in shake flasks. To overcome methylation bottlenecks, we reinforced the S -adenosyl- l -methionine (SAM) cycle by enhancing SAM biosynthesis, accelerating S -adenosyl- l -homocysteine (SAH) hydrolysis, and establishing methionine regeneration, which increased vanillyl alcohol production to 1.95 g/L. Subsequent deletion of four endogenous aldehyde-reduction genes together with removal of heterologous ADH6 enabled vanillin accumulation at 551.6 mg/L. Introduction of the glucosyltransferase UGT72E3/2 converted vanillin into vanillin glucoside, reaching 1.37 g/L in shake flasks and 2.12 g/L in a 3-L fed-batch fermenter. This work establishes a modular platform for efficient production of vanillin and its derivatives in E. coli . © 2026 The Authors.

title: An ensemble mean Q-networks algorithm with prioritized sampling for automatic generation control of multi-area power systems
abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy has intensified stochastic disturbances in power grids. This poses significant challenges to Automatic Generation Control (AGC), which is responsible for maintaining frequency stability and scheduled tie-line power exchange in multi-area power systems. Under highly stochastic operating conditions, conventional PID-based controllers have limited adaptability. Existing RL-based AGC strategies may also suffer from high value-estimation variance and overestimation, which can impair learning stability and control performance. To overcome these limitations, this paper develops an EMQN-based AGC framework for multi-area power systems under strong stochastic disturbances. The proposed framework introduces two main design enhancements: first, multiple Q-networks are integrated through ensemble learning to reduce estimation variance and alleviate overestimation; second, a network-specific prioritized sampling scheme is designed to weaken the correlation among ensemble members and further improve learning stability and sample efficiency. In addition, delay-free target updating is adopted in the AGC framework and further validated through sensitivity analysis. Case studies on the IEEE two-area system and the Guangdong power grid show that the proposed method consistently outperforms the compared methods in terms of frequency deviation, ACE, and CPS1 under both step and stochastic disturbances. In the IEEE two-area system under step load disturbance, EMQN achieves an average frequency deviation of 0.0150 Hz, a CPS1 of 199.8441%, and an average ACE of 40.5155 MW. In the Guangdong power grid case, it reduces the average frequency deviation by 20.72%–57.08% and the average absolute ACE by 19.86%–62.7% compared with benchmark methods, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed EMQN-based AGC framework. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Short-term variability in sediment carbon sequestration in tropical Indian Wetlands: Physicochemical controls and policy relevance
abstract: Wetlands are critical components of the global carbon cycle, functioning as both carbon sinks and sources depending on environmental conditions. This study assessed short-term variability in sediment carbon storage and its physicochemical controls across five tropical wetlands in southern India. Sediment samples collected in March 2024 and March 2025 were analyzed for pH, macronutrients (N, P, K), bulk density (BD), organic carbon (OC), total organic carbon (TOC), and derived carbon indices, including carbon mass (CM), total mass carbon (TMC), and carbon density (CD). Results indicated consistent increases in OC (0.6–2.4% to 0.7–2.65%) and TOC (1.2–6.2% to 1.5–7.1%), accompanied by increases in CD (1.71–10.69–2.18–12.57 kgm⁻²), suggesting enhanced short-term carbon accumulation. Correlation and principal component analyses revealed strong associations among carbon-related variables, while BD and pH contributed to secondary gradients. However, these relationships partly reflect mathematical dependencies among derived indices and should be interpreted with caution. Effect size analysis (Cohen's d) indicated substantial short-term differences for carbon-related variables (d = 2.04–2.46), along with strong effects for OC and BD, reflecting consistent directional changes across sites. Nitrogen showed a supportive role in organic matter accumulation, whereas phosphorus exhibited limited short-term influence. Slightly acidic conditions (pH 4.2–6.0) were associated with reduced decomposition and enhanced carbon preservation. Despite these findings, the study is constrained by its short temporal scope and the absence of key biogeochemical parameters such as redox potential and greenhouse gas fluxes. Overall, the results provide baseline insights into sediment carbon dynamics and inform future wetland carbon monitoring and management strategies. © 2026 The Authors

title: Experimental Evaluation of Low-Velocity Impact Performance of Glass–Basalt Hybrid Composites: Influence of Fiber Weight Fraction and Impact Energy Levels
abstract: The growing demand for lightweight structural materials with high impact resistance and energy absorption has driven research into hybrid composites. This study aims to develop a hybrid composite by combining natural basalt fiber with synthetic glass fiber and evaluating the effect of basalt fiber weight fraction on low-velocity impact performance. Composite laminates were fabricated using the hand lay-up technique with epoxy as the thermosetting matrix and reinforced with glass and basalt fibers at varying basalt contents: 0%, 18%, 36%, 52%, 72%, and 100%. Low-velocity impact tests were carried out as per the ASTM D7136 guidelines at three distinct energy levels: 20 J, 40 J, and 80 J. Internal damage was assessed using visual inspection and C-scan imaging, while ANOVA was used to statistically analyze the influence of fiber weight fraction on impact force, energy absorption, and damage area. Pure basalt laminates demonstrated high stiffness but brittle failure, while pure glass laminates absorbed more energy due to their higher ductility. The results revealed that among the hybrid laminates, the laminate with 52% basalt fiber demonstrated the most balanced combination of stiffness, energy absorption, and damage area, exhibiting strong hybrid synergy across all energy levels. These findings demonstrate the potential of basalt-glass hybrid composites as sustainable, lightweight, and impact-resistant materials. © 2026, Semnan University, Faculty of Mechanical Engineering. .

title: Image-based fault diagnosis for reliable operation of photovoltaic generation plants using a modified ConvNeXt model
abstract: Image-based fault classification is a bottleneck for the operation and maintenance (O&M) of utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) plants, where unflagged soiling, snow burial, electrical damage and physical defects translate directly into lost generation. Existing deep-learning approaches either rely on very large backbones whose training cost is incompatible with frequent site-specific retraining and whose inference precludes on-board deployment, or on lightweight networks that are fast but unreliable on the small, imbalanced field datasets typical of real plants. This work proposes a Modified ConvNeXt-Tiny that augments an ImageNet-pretrained trunk with multi-scale Convolutional Block Attention Module taps at stages 2–4 of the feature pyramid, a Global Response Normalization block before the deepest attention stage, and a parallel five-convolution texture branch that processes a Jet-recolored rendering of the input image, specialized to fine-grained surface textures. The four descriptors are fused and classified by a three-layer multilayer-perceptron head, giving a 30.6-million-parameter model. Under 5-fold stratified cross-validation on the public Faulty Solar Panel dataset (885 images, six classes), benchmarked against seventeen deep-learning baselines under a common training protocol, the proposed model attains 91.30 ± 0.86 % accuracy and 91.62 ± 1.48 % macro-F1, matching the ConvNeXt-Large baseline within 0.13 percentage points while using 6.4 × fewer parameters, training about 19 × faster per fold, and showing the lowest fold-to-fold variance in the leaderboard. A coupled Grad-CAM analysis confirms that attention concentrates on the actual fault region in every class, supporting a human-in-the-loop O&M workflow that improves the availability of renewable generation assets. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Faulted phase selection using paraconsistent annotated logic
abstract: Accurate faulted phase selection is an essential function in the protection of long transmission lines. However, conventional schemes based on deterministic thresholds or impedance estimation may fail under remote and high-resistance fault conditions, where fault indicators often provide contradictory information. This paper proposes a robust decision-level framework based on paraconsistent annotated logic for faulted phase selection in long transmission lines. The proposed approach fuses multiple fault indicators, including voltage magnitude variations, phase angle relationships, and symmetrical component ratios, while explicitly handling inconsistent and uncertain evidence. Extensive simulation studies were conducted considering different line lengths. The proposed method correctly identified the faulted phases, demonstrating superior performance compared to a conventional selection scheme for lines longer than 320 km under weak-infeed conditions, as well as in high-resistance fault scenarios. Misoperations of the conventional algorithm occurred in 189 out of 9156 fault cases. A real fault case is also analyzed to illustrate the practical applicability of the proposed algorithm. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Bulk stacking fault probability as a diffraction-derived metric for quantitative planar defect kinetics
abstract: Quantitative descriptions of defect-accumulation kinetics require a physically meaningful defect metric that can be continuously measured and compared across different deformation states. Such a metric remains unavailable for many diffraction-derived defect descriptors because existing quantities are either model-dependent or lack a rigorous bulk-scale interpretation. Here, an orientation-corrected bulk stacking fault probability (SFP), reconstructed through orientation-weighted integration of in situ synchrotron high-energy X-ray diffraction measurements during tensile deformation of a stainless steel, is proposed as a diffraction-derived planar defect metric. The measured SFP exhibits pronounced orientation dependence and is therefore better interpreted as a directional defect descriptor than as an intrinsic scalar quantity. By correcting the directional faulting field for texture-induced orientation bias through pole-density-weighted integration, a bulk measure of the overall degree of faulting is obtained, enabling the transformation of a directional faulting field into a physically interpretable defect metric. The resulting bulk SFP enables direct quantification of stacking fault accumulation kinetics, revealing rapid initial fault generation followed by progressive deceleration at larger strains. A strong linear correlation between SFP and diffraction peak broadening further indicates concurrent evolution of stacking faults and defect-induced lattice distortions during deformation. Unlike peak-width-based quantities, which generally lack a rigorous averaging property and contain contributions from both Type II and Type III stress fields, the proposed bulk SFP retains both a rigorous averaging property and a direct crystallographic interpretation. The resulting framework enables quantitative characterization of planar defect accumulation kinetics using experimentally measurable diffraction data. © 2026

title: Anisotropic orthogonal random feature-based ridge regression for data-scarce short-term load forecasting
abstract: Accurate day-ahead short-term load forecasting is essential for the operation of microgrids, yet many practical scenarios involve limited historical data, short input sequences, and strict computational constraints. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an anisotropic orthogonal random feature-based ridge regression (AORF-RR) framework with a transfer-learning strategy. By embedding group-wise anisotropic scaling into finite-dimensional orthogonal random Fourier features, the proposed anisotropic orthogonal random feature (AORF) mapping preserves the small-sample generalization capability of kernel learning while substantially reducing the computational cost of model training. The resulting primal-space ridge-regression model improves expressiveness for heterogeneous feature groups without introducing scenario-dependent kernel weights or the high computational burden associated with exact kernel learning. The developed transfer-learning scheme further enables effective adaptation from data-rich source domains to data-scarce target domains within a shared AORF feature space. Numerical studies on benchmark datasets show that AORF-RR consistently outperforms representative neural-network-based baselines and achieves competitive or superior accuracy relative to kernel-based baselines, particularly under short-input and data-scarce settings. Paired statistical significance analysis confirms that the observed error reductions are stable across testing tasks. Large-scale forecasting experiments further demonstrate substantially reduced training cost, supporting scalable and cost-effective deployment in modern power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Anomalous strength inversion in multiphase ceramic joining: When the joint outperforms the base ceramic
abstract: In the field of ceramic/metal brazing, the joint strength is conventionally regarded as limited by the strength of the ceramic base material. However, an anomalous phenomenon challenging this perception was observed in the brazing of Y2O3−MgO multiphase ceramic to TC4 alloy. After undergoing the same heat treatment, the strength of the Y2O3−MgO ceramic was found to be lower than that of the Y2O3−MgO/TC4 brazed joint within a certain temperature range. This study investigated the joining of Y2O3−MgO/TC4 using various fillers and elucidated the intrinsic mechanism of this phenomenon through systematic microstructural characterization. Results show that this “strength inversion” phenomenon is attributed to the Ag-based plastic phase induced by the substitutional solid solution of In at the brazing interface. Geometric phase analysis (GPA) and transmission Kikuchi diffraction (TKD) confirm that the rigid constraints of MgO within the ceramic trigger significant stress concentration, while the Ag plastic phase at the interface can alleviate residual stress through plastic deformation, thereby enhancing the joint strength. Consequently, this work reveals the anomalous mechanism where the base material strength is not the upper limit in multiphase ceramic brazing, providing novel strategies and insights for breaking through the strength limits of multiphase ceramic joints. © 2026

title: Advancing urban solar integration: Performance and policy analysis of BIPV systems in India
abstract: Sustainable urban energy generation is an attractive goal with a growing solution: building integrated photovoltaic system. By combining the functions of a building envelope with those of a photovoltaic system in a single construction, building integrated photovoltaic systems simultaneously serve as a building component and an energy generation system. India has a high potential for building integrated photovoltaic applications in massive scales due to the extensive urbanization and ambitious targets set by the Indian government for renewable energy. This analysis offers a thorough evaluation of building integrated photovoltaic performance, architectural integration, and policy aspects in India through a systematic review approach, drawing on the PRISMA framework. The studies and projects related to the scope of the research were found by searching through databases such as Scopus, Web of Science, Science Direct, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, and technical reports through predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The novelty of this study is that it has an analytical framework is India-specific, and merges the aspects of architectural design, technical performance, operational challenges, policy analysis, and comparative evaluation of real-world case studies of building integrated photovoltaic systems. The study clearly differentiates building integrated photovoltaic systems from building applied photovoltaic systems to avoid conceptual ambiguity, unlike previous studies. The case studies analyzed in this study showed that annual energy production of over 89,000 kWh/year and average annual energy yields of nearly 1460 kWh/kWp could be achieved. Semitransparent glazing solutions, bifacial modules, roof mounted photovoltaic tiles and façade mounted solutions were proposed as the solutions for urban application. The study also addresses some challenges such as partial shading, thermal degradation, complexity, maintenance requirements, and lack of policies for building integrated photovoltaic in India. © 2026 The Authors. title: A Parameter-Efficient Entropy-Guided feature suppression framework for accurate insulator fault detection in edge-Compatible drone inspection
abstract: This paper presents a lightweight and computationally efficient deep learning system for real-time detection of insulator defects. It was made to work on edge platforms that don't have a lot of resources. Starting with a basic You Only Look Once 11 Nano (YOLOv11n) detector, the proposed method uses a Transfer Learning architectural optimisation strategy that combines depth-width scaling, entropy-guided feature suppression, and lightweight convolutional blocks to make a hybrid architecture called Entropy-guided Lightweight Transfer-learning Architecture (ELTA)-YOLOv11. The model keeps good detection accuracy through this hybridisation, and it also reduces the number of parameters by a significant and clear 40.70%, from 2.56M to 1.53M. Even though architectural compression lowers accuracy at first, adding our proposed technique makes it possible to recover performance very well. This results in a final mAP@0.5 of 96.4%. Through extensive inference benchmarking, it has been shown that the model is suitable for edge deployment. The proposed model was deployed in real-time on a Raspberry Pi 5, with an inference time of about 54.48 ms. The inference latency is much lower on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano with TensorRT optimisation, at about 48 ms. The suggested framework's efficiency is also shown by the lower computational complexity ( ∼ 5.6 Giga Floating-Point Operations Per Second (GFLOPs)). The results show that ELTA-YOLOv11 strikes a good balance between deployability, accuracy, and efficiency. This makes it a good choice for real-world edge-based power infrastructure inspection systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Effect of ECAP on the microstructure and mechanical properties of titanium fabricated by thermomechanical particle consolidation
abstract: In this work, fully dense titanium fabricated by thermomechanical consolidation of titanium sponge particles was processed by equal-channel angular pressing (ECAP) to refine its microstructure and improve its mechanical properties. It was found that 4 passes of ECAP carried out at 400 °C with a channel angle of 120° caused a significant change in the microstructure and mechanical properties of the titanium: an ultrafine-grained structure consisting of equiaxed grains in the range of 0.2–20 µm and with a high density of dislocations (4.36 × 1013 m−2) was formed, the yield strength increased from 186 to 380 MPa, the ultimate tensile strength increased from 293 to 418 MPa, but the elongation to fracture decreased from 45% to 22% which shows that the ECAP processed titanium still exhibits an excellent ductility. The strength increase can be attributed to the combined effect of grain refinement (Hall–Petch strengthening) and dislocation hardening (Taylor strengthening), while the ductility decrease is associated with the drastic flow stress increase and the decrease of the strain hardening rate resulting from strain hardening. The obtained results demonstrate a promising potential of combining thermomechanical consolidation and ECAP to produce titanium billets with enhanced mechanical properties, making them suitable for a wider range of practical applications. © 2026

title: An adaptive multi synchrosqueezing transform driven deep network for partial discharge defects discrimination
abstract: Accurate localisation and categorisation of partial discharge (PD) defects are very important to analyse insulation degradation in high-voltage equipment. However, due to the transient discharge characteristic of PD signals, feature representation quality and classification accuracy often degrade. To solve these problems, this paper proposes an advanced time-frequency representation (TFR) in combination with a deep learning (DL) framework for PD defects classification. This article presents an adaptive multi-synchrosqueezing transform (AMSST) driven customized ConvNeXt framework for automatic PD defect discrimination. Proposed AMSST applies Rényi entropy guided iterative TF representation for PD signals. These TFRs are subsequently fed to a customised ConvNeXt architecture, which incorporates adaptive multi-kernel depth-wise convolution for feature extraction and classification. Experimental verification was executed using three independent PD datasets, consisting of 2 laboratory-acquired datasets and an openly available IEEE data port benchmark dataset. A comparative study against conventional TF plots and other conventional classifier models has also been done. This highlights the capability of the proposed framework in improving PD feature extraction and classification performance. Cross-dataset assessment further demonstrated flexibility across independently acquired PD datasets. The results demonstrate that the implementation of adaptive TF enhancement and lightweight multiscale feature learning delivers an effective framework for intelligent PD diagnosis while maintaining moderate computational complexity. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed framework, gaining 100% accuracy during classification on the laboratory-acquired dataset, and portraying strong generalisation capability on the IEEE benchmark dataset. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: State-enhanced surrogate environment and multi-time-scale deep reinforcement learning for robotic grinding optimisation
abstract: Robotic grinding parameter optimisation requires reliable evaluation of how candidate parameter actions affect grinding performance. Experimental construction of the evaluation relationship is costly, as each candidate parameter combination must be physically executed and measured. Surrogate environments can support virtual performance evaluation and reinforcement-learning-based optimisation. However, most existing approaches directly map pre-processing variables to final indicators, neglecting informative but difficult-to-measure intermediate process responses. This study proposes a state-enhanced surrogate environment and a multi-time-scale deep reinforcement learning (MTS-DRL) framework for robotic grinding optimisation. The surrogate environment estimates intermediate process responses to enrich the grinding-state representation and then evaluates action-conditioned grinding indicators through a multi-objective performance-estimation component. On this basis, the proposed MTS-DRL framework assigns temporal information according to the different roles of parameter generation, value feedback and environment-side performance evaluation, rather than using a single shared temporal horizon. The functional allocation enables parameter decisions to respond to recent process variations while incorporating longer-context effects on multiple grinding indicators. Robotic grinding experiments show that the proposed surrogate environment improves indicator-estimation reliability, and the MTS-DRL strategy achieves a better balance between surface quality and processing efficiency than representative baselines. Physical grinding trials further confirm the effectiveness of the learned policy for robotic grinding parameter recommendation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Step-level screening-driven reasoning enhancement for large language models in prefabricated substation fault diagnosis
abstract: Prefabricated substations are core components of novel power systems, yet inter-compartment coupling triggers cascading faults, while high-dimensional asynchronous multi-source monitoring data severely reduces manual fault diagnosis efficiency. Vanilla large language models (LLMs) produce opaque single-path inference lacking traceability. Chain-of-Thought (CoT) improves reasoning transparency but suffers from single-trajectory bias. Self-Consistency (SC) adopts multi-trajectory voting, yet it fails on open-ended fault diagnosis when outputs differ drastically in semantics and format. This study proposes a Step-level Screening-driven Reasoning Enhancement Method (SS-REM) to select optimal reasoning trajectories for substation fault diagnosis. SS-REM generates diverse reasoning paths via temperature sampling, decomposes them into atomic steps, and integrates TF-IDF semantic consistency scoring and length regularization for fine-grained step-level screening. We construct PMEESET—the first multi-compartment prefabricated equipment fault dataset—and propose a three-dimensional DDM quantitative evaluation principle tailored to power engineering. Experiments on PMEESET show SS-REM lifts average reasoning scores by 35.9% and 27.9% compared with vanilla LLMs and CoT, respectively. As a lightweight inference-stage post-processing module without model fine-tuning, SS-REM delivers remarkable improvements in diagnostic reliability and logical traceability, supporting edge intelligent maintenance of prefabricated substations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Operation-oriented dependency-aware joint probabilistic forecasting of load and renewable generation for microgrid dispatch
abstract: This paper presents a forecasting–scenario–dispatch framework for day-ahead microgrid operation. Its forecasting component, termed the Dependency-Aware Fusion Quantile Network (DAFQ-Net), jointly trains three marginal quantile forecasts for electricity load, wind power, and photovoltaic (PV) generation. The main architectural design is an adaptive gate that balances shared historical context and cross-task attended future context for each target. The network uses learned associations to control information exchange, but it does not directly estimate the full joint probability distribution. A Gaussian copula subsequently combines the marginal quantiles and reconstructs cross-variable and 24-hour temporal dependence from training-period forecast errors. The resulting scenarios are evaluated in a proof-of-concept stochastic dispatch model. Tests on two hourly microgrid datasets show improved marginal scores and, for the complete DAFQ-Net–copula pipeline, improved scenario and dispatch metrics against the implemented baselines. The results are case-study evidence under the stated data, copula, and dispatch assumptions, rather than evidence of a general joint-density model or universal operating-cost reduction. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
