title: Risk assessment of voltage violations during unintentional islanding events
abstract: The increasing penetration of distributed generators (DGs) has led to the proposal of fault ride-through (RT) requirements. These requirements enhance the reliability of the electrical system; however, reduce the sensitivity of anti-islanding protections, potentially exposing sensitive equipment to severe overvoltages before DG disconnection when an unintentional islanding occurs. To assess the extent of these events, also reported as load rejection overvoltage, this paper introduces the Voltage Violation Region (VVR) concept, i.e., an area in the ΔP × ΔQ plane given by the operating points in which anti-islanding protections fail to rapidly disconnect DGs before violating sensitive load tolerance limits. Based on dynamic simulations and the VVR, a risk assessment method is proposed to quantify the probability of post-islanding voltages violating the tolerance limit of voltage-sensitive loads. Our analysis of practical passive and active islanding detection methods (IDMs) reveals that RT requirements may significantly delay the activation of anti-islanding protections, resulting in high risks of voltage violations, depending on the tolerance curve and power imbalance measurements. When active IDMs are enabled, these violations may occur even in scenarios with deficit of active power imbalance within the islanded grid. The results support distribution engineers in identifying high-risk feeders, requesting end-users to apply additional protection for sensitive loads, or re-setting the DG's anti-islanding protections. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Evaluating the Durability and Aesthetic Stability of Three Vaccumm-Formed Retainer Materials: An In Vitro Comparative Study
abstract: Objective: To evaluate and compare the mechanical properties and color stability of three types of commercially available thermoplastic retainer materials in a simulated oral environment. Material and Methods: Ten thermoformed samples of retainer materials from three manufacturers (Leone; Duran; Essix ACE) were selected. Samples were subjected to three different testing solutions: artificial saliva at room temperature; artificial saliva supplemented with hot tea at 55º C to 60º C temperature (15 minutes each day); artificial saliva augmented with a cold carbonated drink at 3.5º C to 5.5º C temperature (15 minutes each day), all for 2 weeks. The mechanical properties were characterized using a universal testing machine (MultiTest 10-i) and colour stability was evaluated using a Bio-Rad Smart Spec Analyser Statistical analysis comparing results between retainer groups and testing solutions was carried out using the Kruskal-Wallis test, followed by Dunn's post hoc test. Results: Samples tested in the Hot Tea group showed statistically significant (p<0.05) differences in modulus of elasticity, yield strength, and ultimate tensile strength compared with the other groups. Samples tested in the Hot Tea group and the Cold Carbonated drink group showed a statistically significant (p<0.05) colour change. Among the thermoplastic sample groups, Duran showed significantly better mechanical performance, and Leone showed the least colour change. Conclusion: Duran showed exceptional mechanical performance, whereas Leone showed greater stain resistance. © 2027, Association of Support to Oral Health Research (APESB). .

title: Thermal Behaviour and Coupling Effects in Laminated Composite Beam Structures Using Refined Shear Deformation Theory
abstract: This study investigates the thermoelastic behaviour of laminated composite beams with symmetric (0/90/0) and asymmetric (0/90) layer-ups subjected to sinusoidally distributed thermal line loads. A quasi-3D shear deformation theory incorporating parabolic and trigonometric through-thickness functions based on Reddy’s refined model forms the core analytical framework. The governing equations are derived from the principle of virtual work and solved in closed form via a Navier-type series. The classical beam theory and first-order shear deformation theory are employed solely for comparative analysis. The thermal line load model, representing realistic non-uniform heating scenarios, enables assessments of coupling effects due to laminate asymmetry. Results reveal that asymmetric configurations exhibit significant thermal coupling leading to higher displacements and stress concentrations, while symmetric laminated beams offer improved thermal stability. A MATLAB-based computational tool supports the analysis. The findings underscore the critical role of stacking symmetry in mitigating thermal deformations, guiding the design of reliable composite structures for thermally demanding environments. © 2026, Semnan University, Faculty of Mechanical Engineering. .

title: Similarity solution and asymptotic analysis of a multi-phase Stefan problem with a convective boundary condition at the fixed face
abstract: In a one-dimensional multi-phase Stefan problem occurring within a semi-infinite, homogeneous material, a convective (Robin-type) boundary condition is applied at the fixed boundary x=0. The evolution of the problem is governed by heat diffusion equations that are connected through Stefan conditions at the free boundaries, describing a phase-change process involving n distinct phases separated by moving boundaries. Under appropriate assumptions about the physical parameters and the heat transfer coefficient the existence and uniqueness of a similarity-type solution are established. The locations of the free boundaries and the temperature profiles in each phase are explicitly identified. It is shown that the nonlinear system of equations used to determine the free boundary coefficients has a unique solution. Additionally, the asymptotic behavior as the heat transfer coefficient approaches infinity is analyzed. The similarity-type solution of this Stefan problem with a convective boundary condition approaches the similarity-type solution of the multi-phase Stefan problem with a fixed-temperature boundary condition in this limit. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: The existence and instability of blowing-up steady states for the Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto competition model with cross-diffusion
abstract: This paper is concerned with the existence and stability of a type of blowing-up positive steady states for a shadow system of the Shigesada–Kawasaki–Teramoto (SKT) two-species competition model and for the perturbed SKT system with a sufficiently large cross-diffusion parameter and bounded random diffusion parameters. The asymptotic behavior of coexistence steady states of the SKT model as one of the cross-diffusion parameters tends to infinity was studied by Lou and Ni [1], who showed that almost all coexistence states can be characterized by one of three shadow systems. In [2], the first author of the present paper studied one of these shadow systems with one cross-diffusion term in one space dimension and proved that one component along a bifurcation branch blows up as the bifurcation parameter approaches the least positive eigenvalue of −Δ under the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. Using a different approach from that in [2] , based on suitable transformations and the Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction, we establish the existence and detailed asymptotic structure of several branches of positive steady states near the blow-up points for shadow systems with one or two cross-diffusion terms in one- and multi-dimensional domains. We further prove that all the large steady states obtained near the blow-up points are spectrally unstable. Finally, by perturbation arguments, we establish the existence and instability of corresponding branches of positive steady states for the original SKT system when one of the cross-diffusion parameters is sufficiently large. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Shape optimization for the Stokes hemivariational inequality with slip boundary condition
abstract: In this paper we study a shape optimization problem for a variational-hemivariational inequality describing the steady-state Navier-Stokes model of an incompressible fluid of the Bingham type in a bounded domain with a nonmonotone slip boundary condition. First, we provide results on the stability of solutions to the variational-hemivariational inequality on variations of the domain. Then, an existence result is proved for an optimal shape design problem for the variational-hemivariational inequality. Finally, we discuss the convergence of shape optimization problems for the regularized variational-hemivariational inequality when the regularization parameter tends to zero. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
label: Science (including Engineering)

title: Elliptic quasivariational-hemivariational inequalities in the Beppo-Levi space
abstract: In this paper, we study elliptic quasivariational-hemivariational inequalities in the Beppo–Levi space D1,p(RN), where both the constraint set and the associated energy functional depend on the unknown solution. Owing to the lack of compactness of the embedding of D1,p(RN) into the standard Lebesgue spaces, we work within an appropriate weighted Lebesgue space framework. To overcome the difficulties arising from the solution-dependent constraints, we introduce an auxiliary penalized problem, whose solvability is established by combining a surjectivity theorem, Minty’s lemma, and Kluge’s fixed-point theorem. Finally, we establish the convergence of penalized solutions and recover a solution of the original quasivariational-hemivariational inequality. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Exact solutions with haptotaxis effect and conserved quantities of an avascular cancer model
abstract: In this paper, we perform a classification of Lie point symmetries of a (3+1)-dimensional model describing tumour cells, extracellular matrix (ECM), and matrix-degrading enzymes (MDEs). From the symmetries, we were able to find new exact solutions for the model. One of the solutions we found has haptotaxis effect. We explore these solutions, analysing the invasion of tumour cells, the evolution of the ECM degradation by MDEs and the diffusion of the MDEs. We also obtain three conserved currents and from them we explore the time variation of certain biological quantities. © 2026 The Author(s).
label: Science (including Engineering)

title: Optimization of cultivated-wasteland ratio and crop irrigation quota in the Hetao Irrigation District based on long-term soil salinity simulation
abstract: The Hetao Irrigation District serves as a vital grain production base in China. To enhance the allocation of water and soil resources within this district, this study conducted field experiments specifically in the Hetao Irrigation District. Utilizing long-term soil salinity simulations, various scenario schemes were established to optimize the cultivated-wasteland ratio and crop irrigation quotas in the area under investigation. The results indicate that over the next decade, soil salinity levels in wasteland, cultivated land, and the transition zone above the drain level are expected to decrease, whereas soil salinity in the transition zone below the drain level is projected to increase. The optimal cultivated-wasteland ratio identified for the study area is 12:1, with a suitable sunflower-maize planting ratio threshold of 4:1. The optimal irrigation quotas for maize and sunflower are determined to be 286 and 175 mm, respectively, which represent water savings of 15% and 5% compared to the existing irrigation quotas, thereby effectively controlling soil salinization. Additionally, the suitable threshold for irrigation water salinity in this area is established at 1.0 dS·m⁻¹. This study provides a scientific foundation for the prevention and control of soil salinization, as well as the efficient utilization of water and soil resources within the irrigation district. © The Author(s) 2027. title: A review of Nb-Si-based ultra-high temperature alloys on oxidation resistance
abstract: Nb-Si-based ultra-high-temperature alloys are promising candidate materials for next-generation aerospace engine blades, recognized for their excellent high-temperature mechanical properties and low density. Research on these alloys primarily focuses on fracture resistance and oxidation resistance. Through compositional and processing optimizations, the room temperature fracture toughness of these alloys has reached levels suitable for engineering applications. However, significant breakthroughs in oxidation resistance remain elusive. This article reviews recent progress in the oxidation resistance of Nb-Si-based alloys, with a specific focus on three key aspects: alloying, processing routes, and coating technologies. It summarizes studies on the effects of various alloying elements on oxidation behavior, examines the oxidation performance of alloys produced by different processing methods, and compares the protective efficacy of various coating systems fabricated through different techniques. Finally, the paper outlines future research directions in this field. © 2026

title: A dispatch strategy for islanded multi-energy microgrid incorporating gravity-based energy storage based on an IGWO algorithm
abstract: Addressing the challenges of abundant yet highly fluctuating wind and solar resources in mountainous regions, high costs of power and heat supply, and difficulties in matching supply and demand alongside carbon emission issues within the coordinated dispatch of “electricity-gas-heat-carbon” multi-energy systems, this paper proposes a dispatch scheme for mountainous islanded multi‑energy microgrid incorporating gravity storage, based on an improved grey wolf optimization algorithm. First, integrating mountainous terrain characteristics with the “electricity-gas-heat-carbon” coordination framework, the scheme leverages the topographical adaptability of gravity storage and the resource recycling advantages of carbon-closed-loop technology to overcome traditional system limitations. Second, considering the fluctuation characteristics of wind and solar predicted output and time-series differences in multi-energy loads under a typical daily deterministic scenario, and carbon emission constraints, an optimization dispatch model is established with the objective of minimizing overall system costs, clarifying the coordinated operation mechanism for multiple devices. Finally, an improved Grey Wolf Optimization algorithm—combining Latin Hypercube Sampling for initialization with particle swarm optimization for local search—solves the model. Simulation results demonstrate that this approach can enhance renewable energy integration rates, reduce system carbon emissions and operational costs. Further comparative simulations under summer and winter typical-day conditions verify the good robustness and engineering applicability of the proposed dispatch strategy under distinct mountain climatic conditions, providing theoretical support and practical guidance for low-carbon, stable, and economical operation of multi-energy systems in mountainous regions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Constructing a cross-scale structure via self-doping for high-performance n-type PbTe thermoelectrics
abstract: Decoupling electron and phonon transport is a central challenge in thermoelectrics. Here, we demonstrate that self-doping in PbTe enables a cross-scale structural strategy to achieve this goal and enhance thermoelectric performance. The introduction of excess Pb into Pb0.993Bi0.007Te triggers the formation of Pb interstitials, which promotes carrier density by donating electrons into the conduction band and provides impurity levels near the conduction band minimum to enlarge effective mass. Meanwhile, a nanoscale porous structure at grain boundaries is generated during cooling of the sintering process by the thermal expansion mismatch between the PbTe matrix and Pb-rich precipitate phases. The cross-scale structure, comprising interstitial defects and nanopores, significantly enhances phonon scattering. Therefore, a high peak ZT of about 1.7 at 773 K is achieved by adding 1% Pb excess to Pb0.993Bi0.007Te, contributing to an experimental conversion efficiency of 3.3% under a small temperature difference of 370 K in the single-leg module. This work highlights that constructing a cross-scale structure by simple self-doping is an effective pathway for high-performance thermoelectrics. © 2026

title: Multiphase synergistic strategy enabling flexible ceramic fibers with electromagnetic stealth capability for thermal protection up to 2000 °C
abstract: Next-generation aerospace vehicles demand thermal protection materials that can withstand aerodynamic heating achieving 2000 °C, while concurrently maintaining structural flexibility and electromagnetic stealth capabilities—a synergistic performance portfolio that remains largely unattainable with conventional ceramic materials. To address this exigent requirement, flexible multiphase SiC-ZrC-C fibers are designed and fabricated in this work. In situ-formed ZrC nanoparticles preferentially nucleate at SiC grain boundaries and act as pinning phases, suppressing SiC grain coarsening at ultrahigh temperature, while the continuous porous carbon scaffold accommodates mechanical deformation. The resultant fibers demonstrate exceptional thermal stability, characterized by phase stability following exposure at 1600 °C for 50 h, as well as retained flexibility even after annealing at 2000 °C for 1 h in an Ar atmosphere. Concurrently, the fibers exhibit potent electromagnetic wave absorption capabilities, achieving a minimum reflection loss of −52.60 dB and an effective absorption bandwidth of 5.56 GHz. Besides, continuous fabrication yields large-area fibrous membranes, highlighting the feasibility of large-scale production. The results of this work provide new insights into the design and development of structure-function-integrated thermal protection materials for extreme environments. © 2026

title: Strong electron coupling effect of Cd0.5Zn0.5S nanoparticles anchored on NiCo2S4 nanoflowers: Ohmic junction formation for boosted photocatalytic hydrogen production
abstract: Optimized interfacial charge transport and reinforced interfacial bonding are indispensable for achieving efficient carrier separation and constructing advanced heterogeneous systems toward photocatalytic hydrogen evolution. In this work, a NiCo2S4/Cd0.5Zn0.5S (NCS/CZS) Ohmic junction was rationally designed and constructed to modify semiconductor-based photocatalysts. The synthetic strategy ensures the uniform dispersion of CZS nanoparticles on NCS nanoflowers with intimate interfacial contact. The introduction of NCS nanoflowers significantly enhances the photocatalytic hydrogen evolution performance of CZS. Impressively, the optimized NCS-0.04/CZS heterojunction reaches an optimal hydrogen production activity of 92.62 mmol h−1 g−1, showing a 20-fold enhancement relative to pure CZS. Efficient charge separation triggered by the intrinsic electric field formed at the NCS/CZS Ohmic junction interface accounts for the remarkable improvement in photocatalytic performance. Specifically, the Ohmic junction efficiently facilitates the directional migration of photogenerated electrons from CZS to NCS and effectively suppresses their backflow. Through a combination of experimental studies and theoretical simulations, the fundamental mechanism underlying photocatalytic hydrogen evolution was elucidated. This research is expected to provide a novel perspective and pathway for the design and fabrication of high-performance photocatalysts. © 2026

title: Hierarchical reinforcement learning for load restoration of distribution networks under typhoon disasters
abstract: Under typhoon disasters, distribution-network faults evolve over time and progressively alter the feasible topology and available supply regions, making load restoration a sequential problem that couples discrete network reconfiguration with continuous resource dispatch. This paper proposes a restoration-specific hierarchical deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for automated load restoration during fault evolution. A dynamic environment incorporates the time-varying typhoon wind field, line-failure probability, fault latching, and load scaling. The high-level agent uses a deep Q-network (DQN) to select tie-line command templates, while the low-level Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) agent dispatches distributed generation (DG) and interruptible loads (ILs) within the resulting topology. An AC-power-flow-based safety layer screens bounded continuous actions, applies deterministic backtracking correction when necessary, and invokes a conservative fallback if correction fails; only reverified feasible states are executed. A critical-load-first allocation rule and a marginal-gain high-level reward are further incorporated and separately evaluated by ablation. Tests on the IEEE 33-bus system over 30 Monte Carlo typhoon scenarios show that the proposed method reduces weighted unserved power by 63.43% relative to fixed-topology dispatch. It achieves a 95.54% restoration rate and 98.64% critical-load restoration, close to the MISOCP benchmark (96.08% and 98.91%), while reducing mean online decision time from 0.548 s to 0.019 s. These results demonstrate a favorable restoration-quality-latency tradeoff for rolling load-restoration decisions under evolving typhoon faults. © 2026

title: Optimal G2V/V2G fleet scheduling under uncertainty using a quadratic interpolation supercell thunderstorm algorithm
abstract: This paper develops and applies a Quadratic Interpolation Supercell Thunderstorm Algorithm to electric vehicle fleet charging scheduling optimization under uncertainties over a 24-h horizon, through smart coordination between grid-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-grid operations. Validated on the Congress on Evolutionary Computation 2022 benchmark, Quadratic Interpolation Supercell Thunderstorm balances global exploration and local exploitation through a supercell-inspired population structure combined with quadratic interpolation, navigating multi-modal solution spaces and accelerating convergence toward locally smooth cost regions without requiring gradient information. The addressed electric vehicle scheduling problem is an inherently non-convex, high-dimensional, due to coupled fleet constraints, stochastic operating conditions, and battery degradation dynamics, which limits the applicability of classical deterministic optimization methods. In addition, a state of health based adaptive C-rate control mechanism is introduced, in which charging and discharging rates dynamically adjust according to battery health and state of charge conditions, keeping the operation electrochemically safe and limiting accelerated wear. Five case studies are investigated, including a deterministic baseline, thermal excursion battery degradation uncertainty, day-ahead price uncertainty, arrival/departure uncertainty, and scalability testing. The Quadratic Interpolation Supercell Thunderstorm Algorithm is benchmarked against five competing metaheuristic and two deterministic approaches under equal computational budgets across 30 independent runs. Comparative results show that the improved approach achieves up to 20% lower operational cost compared with the baseline approach, while also obtaining the lowest cumulative cost across all scalability scenarios. Statistical validation further confirms its superiority, with significant differences in 50 out of 56 Wilcoxon pairwise comparisons and the lowest average Friedman rank (1.71). In addition, the Quadratic Interpolation Supercell Thunderstorm Algorithm consistently satisfies target state of charge constraints with zero violations and demonstrates strong scheduling robustness across all investigated scenarios. © 2026 The Authors. title: High-temperature degradation mechanisms of SiC whiskers reinforcement driven by thermo-mechanical coupling effects during sintering processes
abstract: The sintering of SiC whiskers (SiCw)-reinforced ceramic matrix composites typically requires the combined application of high temperature and pressure to achieve densification. However, at elevated temperatures, the degradation of SiCw (i.e., a transition from rod-like to equiaxed morphology) prevents the anticipated reinforcing effect from being realized. How this thermo-mechanical coupling governs whisker degradation remains a critical gap in current understanding. To address this, this study investigates the degradation behaviors of SiCw under both pressure-assisted and pressureless conditions over a temperature range of 1700–1900 °C. The analysis covers SiCw as a reinforcement in two different ceramics: SiAlON (liquid-rich) and SiC (liquid-poor), along with a comparison of SiCw powders. The results demonstrate that the degradation of SiCw is primarily driven by the minimization of surface energy, proceeds in close conjunction with the annihilation of intrinsic stacking faults, and is significantly accelerated by the applied pressure and temperature. Under pressureless conditions, surface diffusion dominates mass transport, resulting in a bimodal microstructure consisting of residual rod-like whiskers and equiaxed grains. The application of pressure dramatically accelerates degradation kinetics by enhancing inter-whisker contact, inducing plastic deformation, and promoting grain-boundary diffusion, leading to complete conversion of SiCw into particles at 1800 °C. Further investigations using SiCw/SiC and SiCw/α-SiAlON composite systems revealed that the pressure-induced accelerating effect of whisker degradation is significantly suppressed in a liquid-rich sintering environment. This study provides a direct theoretical basis for tailoring the microstructure and optimizing the sintering process of SiCw-reinforced composites. © 2026

title: Enhanced power quality using wind energy based DSTATCOM with decoupled neural network control
abstract: Modern energy infrastructure is swiftly progressing with increased integration of Renewable Energy Sources (RESs), deregulation of power sector, growing energy demands and advancements in technology. However, these developments present significant obstacles in sustaining Power Quality (PQ) in energy system. Therefore, an innovative PQ enhancement approach, using Wind Energy-based Distribution Static Compensator (DSTATCOM) with a Novel Decoupled Neural Network (DNN) based control strategy, is introduced in this work. The proposed system integrates DSTATCOM powered by wind energy to compensate PQ issues. A key feature of the control strategy is the implementation of Decoupled Neural Network (DNN), which includes reactive power compensation and harmonic mitigation sub-networks. The system also features a DC-link voltage control mechanism employing Class Topper Optimized (CTO)-PI controller, which optimizes the DSTATCOM operation by maintaining a stable DC-link voltage. The system is evaluated using MATLAB/Simulink, which demonstrate its ability to curtail PQ disturbances. Additionally, the practical applicability of the proposed DSTATCOM with DNN control, is validated through the development and testing of a laboratory prototype. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Existence and necessary optimality conditions for nonlinear inverse problems governed by quasi-hemivariational inequalities with parameter-dependent constraints
abstract: This paper investigates nonlinear inverse problems governed by a class of evolutionary quasi-hemivariational inequalities featuring constraints that depend simultaneously on parameters and unknowns. We begin by establishing the well-posedness of the parametric forward problem within the framework of evolution triples, providing existence, uniqueness, and a priori estimates for the state system. The associated inverse problem is subsequently formulated as a Tikhonov-regularized output-least-squares optimization problem, where the existence of at least one optimal parameter is proved utilizing the direct method of the calculus of variations. A primary analytical contribution of this work is the derivation of necessary optimality conditions in the presence of both nonsmoothness and state constraints with potentially empty interiors. To overcome these inherent challenges, we employ a rigorous double-approximation strategy combining smoothing and penalization techniques. This methodology leads to the derivation of an adjoint system and a first-order variational inequality associated with a singular Lagrange multiplier. Finally, to demonstrate the utility and applicability of our abstract theoretical framework, we apply our results to a nonlinear parabolic quasi-obstacle problem. Within this context, the abstract framework is verified in appropriate Sobolev spaces, and explicit optimality conditions are successfully derived. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Hierarchical and regional coordination strategy for optimal operation of shore power systems based on energy routers
abstract: Energy routers act as the energy transmission hubs of shore power system and play a crucial role in achieving the reliable and efficient utilization of renewable energy. To improve the safe and economical operation of shore power systems, this paper proposes a hierarchical and regional coordination strategy for energy-router-based shore power systems. Firstly, a shore power network incorporating energy routers is introduced and divided into a regional layer and a global layer. Secondly, power allocation and loss optimization are implemented separately at the regional and global layers, enabling the shore power system to prioritize renewable energy consumption and minimize the system's active power loss under normal operating conditions. Case studies are conducted on a three-substation shore power system under both normal and faulty operating conditions. When the power supply of a substation is disconnected from operation due to a fault, the optimal fault transfer power supply scheme is determined by analyzing and comparing the hierarchical and regional optimal operation results under various fault transfer alternatives. Case study results indicate that the proposed strategy can minimize the active power loss of the shore power system under various operating conditions, thereby enhancing the safety and economy of the shore power system. © 2026

title: Facet-directed multiphase TiO2–BiVO4 heterojunction for directional charge transport and photoelectrochemical cathodic protection
abstract: Regulating charge transport across semiconductor heterojunctions is critical for photoelectrochemical (PEC) energy conversion and photoelectrochemical cathodic protection (PECP). Herein, we report a facet-directed multiphase and defect-regulated strategy to tailor interfacial energetics and carrier dynamics in TiO2–BiVO4 heterostructured photoanodes. By introducing Bi-containing domains onto TiO2 nanosheets with co-exposed {001}/{101} facets, the optimized TiO2–BiVO4-T forms a spatially heterogeneous multiphase architecture consisting of residual α-Bi2O3, tetragonal BiVO4, and monoclinic BiVO4. TiO2 facet configuration, multiphase BiVO4 domains, and defect-associated electronic modulation are proposed to regulate local band alignment, facilitate charge separation, and favor electron extraction. Spectroscopic characterization, electrochemical analysis, density functional theory calculations, and light-assisted Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) show modified interfacial energetics, photoinduced surface-potential response, and improved carrier-transfer behavior. Accordingly, TiO2–BiVO4-T exhibits higher charge-separation efficiency, stronger PEC activity, and stable solar-driven cathodic protection for stainless steel and copper. The relationship between structure, electronic modulation, and PECP response identifies facet-selective formation of multiphase domains as a practical route for photoelectrodes used in corrosion protection and solar-energy conversion. © 2026

title: Spongiatia-inspired pore engineering strategy for phase change material encapsulation and all-day freshwater-electricity co-generation
abstract: Integrating interfacial solar steam generation with phase change materials (PCM) has emerged as an efficient approach for all-day solar-driven freshwater-electricity co-generation. However, building those multi-functional evaporators requires complex materials design and leakage-free PCM encapsulation. Herein, we develop a simple, one-step pore engineering strategy to synthesize carbon nanotube microspheres (CNM) with rich nano-/micro-scale pores using waste polypropylene as raw materials and subsequently construct persistent PCM@CNM composite-based multi-functional evaporators. The synergistic effect of multi-level pores significantly promotes PCM encapsulation, realizing an extremely low PCM leakage of < 0.4%. The high thermal conductivity of PCM@CNM (0.547 W m−1 K−1) enables fast thermal energy transfer and utilization for improving water evaporation and thermoelectricity generation. Under 1 sun irradiation, the evaporator delivers an evaporation rate of 2.7 kg m−2 h−1 and a voltage output of 217 mV, surpassing the state-of-the-art PCM-containing evaporators. During outdoor tests, a voltage output of 3 V is achieved, which can charge a mobile phone. Technoeconomic analysis results indicate that the cost-effectiveness of PCM@CNM stands at 209.30 g h−1 $−1. This work offers a cost-effective, sustainable platform to produce multi-functional evaporators for all-day freshwater-electricity co-generation. © 2026

title: Self-rotating wood sphere evaporator enabled by flame-induced carbonization for high-efficiency solar desalination
abstract: Self-desalting solar evaporators have exhibited remarkable potential in enhancing interfacial evaporation stability and mitigating salt accumulation, although most existing systems rely on chemical modifications to optimize photothermal performance or surface wettability, which leads to intricate fabrication procedures and additional environmental burdens. In this work, a flame-carbonized wood sphere (CWS)-based self-rotating floating evaporator was developed to overcome these limitations by employing natural wood as a renewable substrate and fabricating it through a facile, chemical-free flame treatment process that simultaneously enhanced light absorption and surface hydrophilicity while preserving the intrinsic longitudinal vessels and multiscale porous architecture. Such structural integrity enables a synergistic regulation between efficient water transport and localized heat confinement, ensuring stable and continuous evaporation. Experimental evaluations revealed that the optimally carbonized sample, CWS-2, achieved an evaporation rate of 2.05 kg m−2 h−1 under one-sun illumination in 3.5 wt.% saline solution and maintained a high rate of 1.20 kg m−2 h−1 even in 20 wt.% salinity, displaying exceptional long-term operational stability over 8 h of continuous testing. Centered on natural, eco-benign materials and featuring a chemical-free, low-energy fabrication route, this self-rotating evaporator demonstrates superior environmental adaptability and scalability, offering a high-performance and sustainable strategy for solar-driven desalination and water purification applications. © 2026

title: A study on hotspot temperature prediction in dry-type transformers based on multiphysics and field synergy analysis
abstract: Transformers are the primary energy-consuming devices in substations. Accurate loss calculation and hotspot temperature prediction are vital for grid stability. This study focuses on a 5250 kVA dual-winding dry-type transformer. We established a magnetic-thermal-fluid multi-physics coupling model. This model considers non-uniform current density in low-voltage windings caused by magnetic leakage. Through field synergy analysis, we explained the relationship between fluid vortices and local hotspots. Furthermore, we proposed a prediction model using the Grey Wolf Optimizer and Kernel Extreme Learning Machine (GWO-KELM). This model uses load rate, ambient temperature, and fan position as inputs. A digital-twin-oriented prototype platform was also developed to support online monitoring. Temperature rise tests show that the simulation error is within 4%. Compared with the backpropagation neural network (BP) and the standard KELM model, the proposed GWO-KELM model tracks hot-spot temperature variations more accurately and achieves lower prediction errors. This research provides a reliable basis for the status monitoring and predictive maintenance of dry-type transformers. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Maximizing photovoltaic efficiency using dual core boost converter and artificial intelligence-based MPPT
abstract: The growing adoption of Photovoltaic (PV) systems for renewable energy requires advanced techniques to manage their efficiency under fluctuating environmental conditions. Henceforth, this work proposes an advanced PV energy conversion system incorporating a Dual Core Active Boost Converter and an Artificial Rabbit Optimized (ARO) Radial Basis Function Neural Network (RBFNN) Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm. The system is designed to maximize energy extraction from solar module and distribute a DC output for various applications. Dual Core Active Boost Converter employs a high-step-up design with active clamping to diminish switching losses and raises power conversion efficiency. The Artificial Rabbit Optimized RBFNN MPPT algorithm dynamically tracks PV system's MPP under changing circumstances such as irradiance and temperature, ensuring optimal energy harvesting. The validation of proposed model is done over MATLAB, which evaluates the performance of converter and MPPT algorithm. The outcomes attained demonstrate faster convergence to MPP with 99.76%, improved energy efficiency (93%) and greater stability under dynamic operating conditions with a response time of 0.0125s. This advanced PV energy conversion system showcases its effectiveness in increasing solar power conversion and highlights its potential for practical deployment in renewable energy technologies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Rapid identification of Sub-/Super-Synchronous oscillations by interpolated Zero-padding DFT
abstract: Sub-/super-synchronous oscillations pose significant threats to the safety and stability of the smart grid. Fast and accurate parameter estimation is essential for identifying sub-/super-synchronous oscillations, providing a foundation for addressing this challenge. However, with a short window length, frequency resolution is limited, making it difficult for existing interpolated-DFT-based methods to accurately estimate the parameters of closely spaced sub-/super-synchronous components near the fundamental frequency. To enhance real-time and precise identification, an interpolated zero-padding DFT method is proposed for estimating parameters of these oscillations from time-domain waveform data. This method accounts for the influence of multiple frequency components and uses spectral leakage as useful information. By examining the relationship between signal parameters and DFT bins, a linear equation system is constructed and solved to accurately determine the frequencies, amplitudes, and phases of the sub-/super-synchronous oscillations. Test results indicate that, compared to existing methods, the proposed method (i) reduces latency by a factor of 7.8 and (ii) offers a wider estimation range for the damping factor of sub-/super-synchronous components. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Dislocation defects in 4H‑SiC crystals grown by physical vapor transport: Evolution, origins, and control strategies
abstract: Silicon carbide (4H-SiC), a key wide-bandgap semiconductor material commonly grown by the physical vapor transport (PVT) method, holds great promise for high-power electronics, quantum photonics, and advanced optoelectronics. However, dislocation defects severely limit the performance and reliability of SiC-based devices, especially in large-diameter crystals. This review systematically outlines the evolution behavior and distribution characteristics of dislocations in PVT-grown 4H-SiC, and examines the underlying mechanisms driving dislocation multiplication across different growth stages. Key influencing factors-including seed crystal quality, source powder properties, growth interface morphology, and cooling protocols-are analyzed in detail. Effective strategies for suppressing dislocations, such as controlling carbon inclusions and eliminating edge polycrystals, are summarized. Finally, perspectives are provided toward achieving low-dislocation-density, large-size SiC crystals, offering both theoretical guidance and practical insights for further research and industrial development. © 2026

title: Deep Bi-LSTM-based intelligent detection of loss-of-excitation faults in STATCOM-integrated power system
abstract: Loss of excitation (LOE) and partial loss of excitation (PLOE) are critical faults in synchronous generators that can compromise system stability and lead to severe equipment damage if not identified promptly. Conventional impedance-based protection techniques often experience degraded performance under dynamic conditions and in the presence of power electronic compensation. This work proposes a data-driven framework for excitation fault diagnosis using multivariate time series analysis of generator signals. A synchronous generator model integrated with a Static Synchronous Compensator (STATCOM) is used to generate simulation data for six operating conditions, including normal operation, full LOE and partial LOE under both compensated and uncompensated scenarios. A set of electromechanical and electrical variables, including electromagnetic torque (Te), active power (Pe), reactive power (Qe), q-axis voltage (Vq), stator current (Is), rotor speed deviation (Δω), rotor speed (Wm), voltage deviation (Dv), torque-speed interaction (Te*Δω), field voltage (Vf), field current (If) and q-axis current (Iq) is extracted within a fault-centered time window. To enhance fault discriminability, first-order temporal derivatives and RMS-based envelope features are incorporated, resulting in a 26-dimensional feature representation for each sequence. Two sequence learning models are evaluated: a baseline recurrent neural network (RNN) and a deep bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) network. The results demonstrate that while the baseline RNN achieved a classification accuracy of 91.0%, the Deep Bi-LSTM significantly improved performance, attaining an accuracy of 99.58%, F1-score of 99.6%, and an MCC of 0.995. These results confirm the effectiveness of deep bidirectional temporal learning for accurate and reliable LOE and PLOE detection. The proposed approach demonstrates strong potential for development of reliable, data-driven protection schemes for synchronous generators in modern power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Dielectric properties of synthetic ester-based nanofluid under various electrode configuration, cellulose contamination, and circulation velocity
abstract: This study systematically investigates the influence of electrode tip geometry (needle, sharp, and blunt), cellulose particle contamination (0, 0.5, and 1 g/L), and circulation velocity (0, 0.3, and 0.5 m/s) on the dielectric performance of synthetic ester-based nanofluids. The methodology integrates experimental breakdown voltage tests with Finite Element Method (FEM) simulations to analyze the electric field distribution and particle accumulation. Dielectric failure is characterized using Weibull analysis of the breakdown data, while the FEM results support the interpretation of the experimental findings. The results indicate that the electrode geometry significantly affects the dielectric strength of insulating oil, with the performance decreasing in the order of blunt, square, and needle electrodes. This behavior is closely linked to the electric-field distribution and breakdown voltage characteristics. Furthermore, cellulose contamination significantly weakens the dielectric strength through conductive bridges, leading to local breakdown along the gap, but increasing the circulation speed effectively mitigates this effect by reducing cellulose accumulation via drag force, thereby improving the dielectric properties and enhancing the breakdown voltage. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Using selected flexibility resources in the power system to eliminate overloads on high-voltage lines
abstract: With the growing share of distributed energy sources and energy storage, the problem of high-voltage line overloads is becoming one of the key challenges of modern power systems. This paper proposes a method to eliminate transmission line overloads by coordinating power changes among selected generation units, loads, and energy storage units, with network reconfiguration as needed. A key element of the proposed approach is identifying the controllable elements most strongly associated with overload patterns in post-contingency scenarios. These elements were identified using statistical correlation coefficients describing the relationship between line loading levels and the power generated, consumed, or stored at individual buses. Correlation analysis was used to determine a subset of candidate elements most relevant to the observed overload patterns, thereby reducing the dimension of the control problem. The proposed approach enables effective overload reduction while simultaneously reducing the problem's dimensionality. The results indicate that it can be a useful tool supporting network management under conditions of high generation and load variability. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Thermal stress mitigation via synergistic dual-interface reconstruction in Si3N4/Cu joints
abstract: Severe thermal expansion coefficient (CTE) mismatch in brazed Si3N4/Cu joints frequently induces interfacial stress concentration and ceramic cracking. Herein, a (Cu20Sn)100−xTix/Nb/Ti multilayer composite filler is proposed to achieve dual-interface reconstruction by simultaneously tailoring the Si3N4 and Nb interfaces, thereby synergistically regulating residual stress distribution within the joint. At the Si3N4 interface, the filler constructs a Si3N4/TiN/Cu6−xTixO+(Nb, Ti)5Si3 architecture, establishing a smoothed CTE gradient and relieving interfacial stress. At the Nb interface, Nb-Sn interactions generate a hierarchical architecture comprising a continuous basal layer and micron-submicron (Nb, Ti)3Sn particle band. Thermodynamic and kinetic analyses reveal that restricted Ti activity allows Nb-Sn/Nb-Si reactions to dominate, wherein (Nb, Ti)3Sn growth obeys a parabolic law governed by a transition from reaction-diffusion to dissolution-precipitation mechanism. First-principles calculations demonstrate that strong Cu-3d/Nb-4d orbital hybridization endows the Cu(111)/(Nb)Nb3Sn(111) interface with excellent interfacial adhesion to establish reliable metallurgical bonding. The in-situ (Nb, Ti)3Sn/Nb composite serves as a stress buffer to mitigate the von Mises equivalent stress near the Si3N4 interface. Driven by the dual-interfacial strategy, the joint achieves a maximum shear strength of 163.2 MPa under optimal brazing conditions (930 °C, 5wt.% Ti). The fracture path migrates from the Si3N4 interface to the (Nb, Ti)3Sn particle band, which confirms effective stress redistribution and improved joint reliability. This dual-interface reconstruction strategy may provide a general approach to residual-stress mitigation in ceramic/metal joints with severe thermophysical mismatches. © 2026

title: Mixed-Discrete optimization of spacer configuration for Short-Circuit force reduction in EHV bundled conductors
abstract: Short-circuit events in extra-high-voltage (EHV) air-insulated substations produce strong electrodynamic forces on flexible bundled conductors, resulting in high tensile stress, pinch interaction between sub-conductors, conductor swing, and possible reduction in phase-to-phase clearance. In such cases, the system's reaction depends on spacer span, spacer mass, and bundle spacing, determining the system's equivalent mass and dynamic behavior. In this study, the governing force is defined as the maximum value among the tensile, drop, and pinch forces, which must be minimized while satisfying mechanical and clearance constraints. Given the discrete nature of design variables, this is a nonlinear and mixed-discrete optimization problem. The resulting problem is formulated as a nonlinear, constrained, mixed-discrete optimization problem in which spacer span, spacer mass, and bundle spacing are optimized simultaneously. A hybrid CSS-EM solver is adopted as the computational optimizer for the proposed mixed-discrete formulation. The main novelty of the work lies in the spacer-configuration optimization formulation rather than in the development of a new metaheuristic algorithm. A practical 220 kV case study shows the existence of a complex and nonlinear design space with transition zones where the governing force mechanism changes. Existing standards such as IEC 60865 and IEEE Std. 605 provide procedures for short-circuit-force calculation; however, they do not explicitly consider spacer-configuration optimization. The proposed methodology addresses this design gap. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Fault detection methods for medium-voltage flexible DC power supply systems under active current limiting control at MMC converter stations
abstract: In medium-voltage flexible DC power supply systems, conventional protection of Modular Multilevel Converters (MMC) typically relies on MMC blocking, which may result in converter station shutdown. Under active current-limiting control, the fault current is suppressed by reducing the number of inserted submodules during a fault. This strategy enables DC-side faults to be detected before the MMC converter station is blocked or shut down, thereby providing sufficient transient time for subsequent fault detection and selective isolation. However, the suppression of fault currents via active current-limiting control may reduce the accuracy of conventional. protection methods in fault detection. To address this issue, this paper proposes an Logistic-Gauss Circle- Feature Mode Decomposition(LGC-FMD)-based fault detection method for medium-voltage flexible DC power supply systems that incorporates converter-station current-limiting control. By combining this method with a Joint Judgment Criteria of IMF based on Approximate Entropy(AE) and the Maximal Information Coefficient(MIC), Despite the fault current suppression provided by active current-limiting control at the converter station, faults can still be accurately detected. This method is of practical importance for improving the stability and reliability of medium-voltage flexible DC power supply systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Competition and interaction between shear-banding and cleavage-cracking in an Fe-based metallic glass
abstract: High-strength Fe-based metallic glasses (Fe-MGs) are prone to catastrophic fracture under external loading, and clarifying their ductile-to-brittle transition (DBT) mechanism and realizing brittleness modulation is of significance. The competition between shear-band-dominated plastic deformation and cleavage-crack-dominated fracture is the key to determining the failure mode transition of Fe-MGs. However, the interaction mechanism between shear-banding and cleavage-cracking remains unclear. In this work, we performed a systematic investigation on a high-strength and relatively tough Fe-MG using two different sample sizes and quasi-in situ compression tests to vividly show the size-dependent failure behavior, damage evolution, competition and interaction between shear bands and cleavage cracks. We found that the stress concentrators due to the pre-existing external defects and the interaction of shear bands promote the initiation of cleavage-cracking, while the stable crack propagation depends on sample size. This study deepens the current understanding of the failure mechanisms in high-strength MGs and also provides a new insight into the sample size effect in brittle MGs. The fact that the smaller MG sample deforms more plastically rather than brittle fracture is not only because it contains smaller and fewer external defects but also due to the more stable crack propagation. © 2026

title: Functional protein extracts and colouring co-products from Chlorella fusca: Towards integrated microalgal bioprocessing
abstract: The rising demand for sustainable, high-quality protein sources has sparked interest in microalgae as an alternative to conventional proteins. This study aimed to identify the most suitable Chlorella strain for protein extraction and utilisation and to optimise the cell disruption and extraction conditions to maximise protein recovery and functionality. Among the five strains evaluated, Chlorella fusca exhibited the highest growth rate (0.16 d−1) and biomass productivity (83.55 mg⸱L−1⸱d−1) and was therefore selected for further experiments. The optimisation of cell wall disruption revealed the highest efficiency at 100 g⸱L−1, although 10 g⸱L−1 was adopted for practicality. Protein extraction was optimised at pH 11.90 for solubilisation and pH 3.40 for precipitation, yielding a protein content of 44.63 g⸱100 g−1 of biomass. The extracted proteins exhibited good emulsifying (up to 66.1 ± 0.2% at pH 10) and foaming capacities (78.6 ± 0.1% at pH 2), as well as relevant water- and oil-holding capacities (2.5 ± 0.2 and 3.3 ± 0.3 g⸱g−1, respectively). Gel formation occurred only at 20% protein concentration under alkaline pH. The amino acid profile revealed that essential amino acids represented 45.7% of the total amino acids, comparable to those reported for common food protein-rich extracts. Furthermore, the protein extraction leftovers demonstrated strong colouring potential in food matrices, particularly for green tonalities in fondant and pasta products. Overall, these findings highlight C. fusca as a promising, sustainable microalgal source of functional proteins and natural pigments for food and nutraceutical applications. Moreover, the valorisation of extraction residues as natural colourants reinforces the circular and zero-waste potential of microalgal biorefineries. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: Unveiling the impact of mixed-strain solid-state fermentation on wheat bran dietary fiber: gluten protein structure evolution, dough rheological modulation and steamed bread quality enhancement
abstract: Wheat bran dietary fiber (WBDF) helps enhance the nutrition of dough products, but its direct incorporation triggers quality deterioration. In this study, a mixed-strain solid-state fermentation strategy involving Basidiomycetes, Candida utilis, and Lactobacillus plantarum was employed to modify WBDF. The underlying mechanisms by which modified WBDF affects dough and steamed bread quality were systematically investigated across a range of addition levels (0, 3, 6, 9, 12, and 15 %). Results showed that unfermented WBDF (UWBDF) disrupted the gluten network, reducing dough and steamed bread quality. In contrast, fermented WBDF (FWBDF) effectively mitigated these adverse effects. At the gluten protein level, FWBDF promoted disulfide bond cross-linking (free sulfhydryl groups content decreased from 8.16 to 7.36 μmol/g), and increased the glutenin macropolymer content from 0.47 to 1.92 g/100 g. Besides, FWBDF optimized water distribution within the dough, improving water availability for starch and gluten proteins. These changes enhanced the pasting, extension, and dynamic rheological properties of dough, ultimately improving steamed bread quality-characterized by increased specific volume (from 1.71 to 2.30 mL/g), texture (hardness from 3209 to 2670 g; springiness from 0.81 to 0.84), and antioxidant capacity. Notably, the beneficial effects of FWBDF were closely dependent on its addition level. At 3-6 % addition, the modifying advantages of WBDF were fully realized; however, at 12-15 %, excessive FWBDF exacerbated gluten network disruption, leading to quality deterioration of dough and steamed bread. This study provides a theoretical foundation for the fermentation modification of WBDF and its application in steamed bread production. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Stabilization of sesame paste via a capillary bridge-driven oleogel strategy
abstract: Sesame paste is susceptible to phase separation during storage, which results in the formation of an upper oil layer and a lower solid sediment, which impairs product consistency and consumer acceptability. This study systematically investigated a simple strategy without additional chemical additives that leverages capillary bridge-mediated particle assembly to stabilize sesame paste. By controllably introducing water as the secondary fluid, a three-dimensional particulate network was formed, transforming the paste into a self-supporting oleogel. The stabilization effect was critically dependent on the secondary fluid saturation (S). At S = 35%, the system reached an optimal water-in-oil microstructure (funicular state), exhibiting maximum rheological moduli and texture parameters, and zero oil leakage during 90-day storage. Nevertheless, this enhanced physical stability was accompanied by accelerated oil oxidation at higher water content and a significant deterioration in sensory quality when S exceeds 10%. In contrast, at a lower saturation (S = 4%), the paste retained sensory attributes indistinguishable to the control while substantially enhancing physical stability, presenting a promising balance for practical application. Moreover, at S = 35%, the mechanical strength of the gel network was highly sensitive to environmental conditions: strongly acidic pH (2) reinforced the network, whereas increasing ionic strength weakened it. Collectively, this research established capillary bridges regulation as a scalable, clean-label approach to enhance the physical stability of sesame paste, offering fundamental insights into the structure-performance relationship of oil-continuous systems in food matrices. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Comparative study of curcumin- and limonene oil-encapsulated Pickering emulsions stabilized by pH-Responsive chitosan nanoparticles: Structural, rheological, and controlled release properties
abstract: Curcumin and limonene oil, bioactive compounds with therapeutic potential, are vital for human health but face limitations due to poor solubility, stability, and bioavailability. Chitosan (CS), a pH-responsive natural polysaccharide, serves as an effective stabilizer in Pickering emulsions (PEs), thereby enhancing their delivery. This study focuses on preparing stable CS nanoparticles (CSNPs) via a pH-responsive self-assembly method for encapsulating bioactive compounds. Optimal stability of CSNPs was observed at pH 6, as indicated by a higher contact angle reflecting enhanced hydrophobicity. At pH 6.5, the contact angle decreased due to the formation of large, unstable aggregates that settled out, resulting in a reduced hydrophobicity of CS. Curcumin-loaded PEs prepared at pH 6 exhibited uniform droplet size and distribution, which can be attributed to the strong hydrophobic interactions of the CSNPs. Below pH 6, the CSNPs became hydrophilic, resulting in the phase separation of the PEs. Increasing the concentration of CSNPs and oil content promoted the formation of interconnected networks, resulting in elastic gels that are stable at 35°C. At elevated temperatures (70°C), the enhanced kinetic energy of CSNPs induced a gel-to-semi-gel transition, while elevated ionic strength further liquefied PEs. Limonene oil-encapsulated PEs were stable at pH 5.5 and 6.0, differing from curcumin systems due to limonene's lower viscosity and the pH-sensitive behavior of CSNPs. This study demonstrates that slight pH variations in CSNPs have a significant impact on bioactive encapsulation and stability. Curcumin- and limonene-loaded PEs achieve high efficiency, capacity, and controlled release, providing a versatile method to improve bioactive delivery in food and pharmaceutical systems. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Fibrillation-induced compositional remodeling of egg white protein: Differential glycerol regulation of cryogel networks and thermomechanical performance
abstract: Cryogels constructed from food proteins derive their macroscopic properties from the structural organization and intermolecular interactions established in the precursor gel network. This study investigated the structural and compositional changes in egg white protein (EWP) during acid–heat-induced fibrillation and how these changes influence the subsequent effects of glycerol (Gly) on the protein network. Acid-heat treatment converted native globular EWP into β-sheet-rich fibrillar assemblies while simultaneously inducing protein hydrolysis, redistribution of protein components, and reorganization of surface interaction sites. These changes resulted in a heterogeneous composite gel network containing native proteins, fibrils, and remodeled protein components rather than a network dominated by globular protein aggregates, thereby modifying the available intermolecular contacts and load-bearing junctions. Gly consequently exhibited distinct concentration-dependent effects in the two networks. In native EWP cryogels, a relatively low Gly level was sufficient to maximize network stiffness, whereas the EWPF-containing system required a higher Gly level to achieve its maximum Young's modulus and bending load-bearing capacity. This shift in the optimal Gly concentration was associated with the greater heterogeneity of the hydrogen-bonding environment and the stronger structural constraints imposed by fibrillar and protein interfaces. Excessive Gly increased molecular mobility and heat transfer, ultimately reducing network stiffness and thermal-insulation performance. These findings show that fibrillation regulates EWP cryogels not only through fibrillar reinforcement but also through compositional and interaction-site remodeling, which in turn redefines the way Gly interacts with and regulates the resulting protein network. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Development of hydrocolloid-structured choline chloride–lactic acid eutectogels enriched with Terminalia catappa extract through intermolecular hydrogen bonding for active fruit coating and postharvest quality preservation
abstract: Eutectogels have gained attention as soft structured materials due to their ability to form stable, biocompatible, and viscoelastic networks suitable for edible and active coating systems. In this study, hydrocolloid-based eutectogels were developed using choline chloride–lactic acid (ChCl: LA) as the eutectic solvent system and xanthan gum as the structuring agent at concentrations of 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, and 1.25% (w/w). Rheological analysis showed that all eutectogels exhibited non-Newtonian flow behavior with weak gel-like characteristics. Textural evaluation demonstrated desirable gel strength, adhesiveness, springiness, cohesiveness, and resilience. Increasing xanthan gum concentration progressively improved the rheological and textural attributes. Among the formulations, DESG-0.5 was selected as the most suitable coating matrix based on its visual appearance, flow behavior, and texture. To obtain a bioactive coating, Terminalia catappa extract was incorporated into DESG-0.5, forming DESGE. FTIR analysis indicated enhanced functional group expression, confirming extract integration within the eutectogel matrix. DESG-0.5 and DESGE showed transmittance of 63.24–87.30%, absorbance of 0.06–3.67 a.u., effective gas and water vapor barrier properties, and high weight-holding capacity of 98.22–99.03%. Coating application improved cherry tomato preservation for 36 days at 4 °C and 15 days at 25 °C, with DESGE showing potential as a coating material for retention of physicochemical and color quality. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: A pre-deployment framework for simulation-driven optimization of robotized manufacturing tasks
abstract: The pre-deployment configuration of robotic workcells encompasses layout design, task allocation, motion planning, and safety assessment. Despite their strong interdependence, these aspects are still largely addressed through expert knowledge and empirical rules, often in a sequential manner and without a formal optimization framework. This paper proposes a simulation-driven optimization framework that jointly optimizes these interdependent domains during the early design stages. To ensure general applicability, we formulate the overall problem as a hierarchy of nested optimization layers, each dedicated to a specific domain of the robotic task, while accounting for the coupling between them. The overall problem is treated as a black-box iterative optimization, where the unknown underlying function is replaced by a high-fidelity digital model, allowing to evaluate system performance through simulation rather than analytical cost functions. By decoupling domain-specific decisions while preserving their inter-dependencies, the proposed approach can be flexibly applied to heterogeneous scenarios, ranging from fully autonomous robotic operations to human–robot collaborative assemblies within the same manufacturing cell. The framework is evaluated on representative robotic tasks, including both collaborative and human-free scenarios, and its performance is compared against experience-based design solutions. The results show that the proposed method consistently attains better performances than the benchmark strategies enforced as a baseline, demonstrating its effectiveness as a systematic alternative to traditional heuristic-driven design practices. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Heterolayered gradient photonic textile harmonizing scattering coloration and continuous microclimate comfort
abstract: Personal thermal management (PTM) enables on-body microclimate modulation independent of external environments, regarded as a revolutionary avenue unifying comfort, health, and energy efficiency. Inadequate adaptability, limited stability, and restricted coloration hinder existing PTM materials, stemming from intrinsic structural contradictions among competing functional requirements. This study presents a hierarchical design with interlayer complementarity, rationally integrating a photonic crystal layer, a porous layer, and a heating layer to realize a continuous microclimate comfort PTM textile (PTMT) with tunable coloration. The photonic crystal layer imparts structural color through interference and coherent scattering without perturbing mid-infrared (MIR) spectral modulation. Together with the porous layer, it provides low solar absorptance (∼10.3%) and high MIR emissivity (∼88.1%) for radiative cooling. The heating layer exhibits a high solar absorptance of approximately 90.2% and a low MIR emissivity of approximately 5.6%. Asymmetric interfacial wettability drives unidirectional moisture transport and improves moisture management. In outdoor tests, the PTMT reduced the surface temperature by approximately 18.9 °C (cooling) and increased it by approximately 25.5 °C (heating). This complementary hierarchical strategy may provide insight into overcoming inherent structural contradictions in PTMT and facilitate broad commercialization. © 2026

title: Harnessing metal-polyphenol networks (MPNs) to regulate the digestive kinetics and enhance gel properties of whey protein gel: The influence on intermolecular interaction force and microstructure
abstract: Whey protein (WP) has significant applications in the fields of food and nutrition. However, WP has the characteristics of fast digestion rate and a wide range of different gel properties depending on processing history, which limits its application in industrial production. Therefore, in this study, proanthocyanidins and calcium ions were introduced as model polyphenols and metal ions to form a versatile novel material, metal-polyphenol networks (MPNs). MPNs with strong adhesive properties were added to whey protein isolate gel (GWPI) to form MPNs-enhanced GWPI (GWPI@MPNs). This experiment first elucidated the mechanisms by which proanthocyanidins and calcium ions form MPNs and the molecular interactions between MPNs and WP. Then, the effects of adding different proportions of MPNs on the digestion kinetics and gel properties of GWPI@MPNs were determined. The indicators of digestion rate included degree of hydrolysis, digital image of the digestion process, SDS-page, and distribution of polypeptide molecular weight. Gel properties encompassed texture properties, rheological properties, denaturation behaviours, low-field nuclear magnetic resonance, and water-holding capacity. It was found that adding an appropriate amount of MPNs was an effective method to control the digestion rate and enhance the gel properties of GWPI. The mechanism might be that MPNs could enhance the intermolecular forces of WP and make the GWPI form a dense and uniform microstructure. The novel method developed in this research has the potential to contribute to overcoming the inherent limitations of WP and adding a new digestion related functional value for its application in the food industry. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Breathing in harm: current insights into the effects of air pollution on cardiorespiratory health
abstract: Air pollution significantly contributes to cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, leading to increased morbidity and mortality. This review critically examines the mechanisms linking air pollution to higher cardiometabolic risk and cardiovascular death. It examines the impact of air pollution on respiratory health, specifically its role in exacerbating conditions such as heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and asthma. Special attention is given to vulnerable groups, including pregnant individuals, neonates, children, and patients with pre-existing cardiovascular or respiratory conditions, who are particularly susceptible and experience more severe health effects. Emerging evidence regarding the interactions between air pollution and coronavirus disease 2019 is also presented, showing how reductions in pollution levels during pandemic lockdowns were associated with improved cardiopulmonary health. Furthermore, the review discusses international differences in air quality standards and recent updates to exposure limits for air pollutants, as well as their implications for public health. It evaluates various mitigation strategies, including policy interventions, technological solutions, and approaches to reduce risk-based exposure. Lastly, the review emphasizes the need for comprehensive, evidence-based frameworks to minimize exposure and prevent diseases associated with pollution. Strengthening air quality management is essential for reducing the global burden of cardiovascular and respiratory diseases. © 2026 Medical Gas Research

title: Segmented variable impedance controller with trajectory adaptive adjustment for robotic polishing tasks
abstract: In robot contact force control, adaptive variable impedance control reduces force tracking error compared to constant impedance control, but there is a collision between the end effector and the environment, resulting in overshoot of the contact force. To reduce contact-force overshoot and further improve force-tracking accuracy, an adaptive reference trajectory-based adaptive variable impedance control (ART-AVIC) method is proposed. The controller’s reference trajectory is adjusted in real time based on the magnitude of the force error. Meanwhile, the damping parameters are updated in a segmented manner according to the contact force error in contact stage. This approach effectively reduces the system’s steady-state error and significantly reduces overshoot and settling time during robotic polishing. In the simulations that account for environmental changes, desired force variations, and practical factors, the ART-AVIC method exhibits better overall performance. In curved surface polishing experiments, compared with other control methods, ART-AVIC reduces the contact-force overshoot by 13.61%-54.93% and the steady-state contact-force RMSE by 11.11%-61.90%. In addition, polishing experiments on blade and cage have demonstrated the potential of the ART-AVIC method for industrial applications. Simulations and experiments validate that the ART-AVIC method performs better and is suitable for robotic polishing tasks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Time series power load forecasting based on PCC-MIC hybrid feature selection and differential attention improved PatchTST
abstract: Accurate power load forecasting is essential for the secure and stable operation of power systems. Nevertheless, the inherent complexity and stochasticity of load time series pose great challenges to precise prediction. In this paper, we propose a novel forecasting framework integrated with hybrid feature selection and Differential Attention mechanism, namely Seasonal and Trend decomposition using Loess (STL) enhanced Patch Time Series Transformer (PatchTST), abbreviated as STL-PatchTDT. First, key features are selected using Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC) and Maximum Information Coefficient (MIC). Next, the STL technique decomposes load series into trend, seasonal, and residual components. Taking the decomposition and feature selection results as input to the model, the forecasting model enhances the foundational PatchTST model by incorporating a “Differential Attention” mechanism, thereby boosting its ability to model complex patterns. Using multi-load data from Arizona State University's Tempe Campus, experiments show the proposed method improves R2 by 2.7%, and reduces MAE and RMSE by 21.7% and 15.5%, respectively, outperforming baseline models and achieving high-precision forecasting in complex scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Rationally designing cluster-based MOF catalysts to achieve high-efficiency CS2 green conversion via quadruple synergistic effect
abstract: Green conversion of carbon disulfide (CS2) waste into high-value products under mild conditions is a highly significant and challenging strategy. Herein, three novel cerium-based copper-iodine cluster metal-organic frameworks (MOF-a, MOF-b, and MOF-c) have been harvested by simple acid-base regulation and characterized structurally. Notably, these MOFs, featuring different densities of [CuxIy] clusters and pore characteristics, can catalyze the CS2 cycloaddition reaction with aziridine into high-value-added thiazolidine-2-thione, with increasing catalytic efficiency from MOF-c to MOF-a. Especially, the recyclable catalyst MOF-a demonstrates the highest yield of 99% for 4 h at ambient temperature and pressure without a co-catalyst, and Submicron-MOF-a further shortens the reaction time to only 2.5 h with excellent performance, realizing a breakthrough in the mildest catalyst for the CS2 green transformation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations combined with experimental analyses further elucidate that the exceptional catalytic efficiency is governed by a quadruple synergy of Cu(I) Lewis acid sites, nucleophilic I– species, stable cerium‑oxygen clusters, and appropriately sized pore architecture. This work provides an ultra-efficient and environmentally friendly CS2 conversion catalyst, conforming to the green chemistry concept. © 2026

title: Experimental harmonic characterization of grid–connected PV inverters using FFT, time–frequency analysis, and VMD–HHT
abstract: This paper presents an experimental framework for the characterization of harmonic distortion and transient phenomena in grid–connected photovoltaic (PV) inverters operating under non–stationary conditions. In PV–based smart grids, harmonic behavior is influenced by solar irradiance variability, inverter control dynamics, and inverter–grid interactions, which challenge classical stationarity assumptions. Although classical and advanced signal–processing techniques are widely used, their independent application often provides limited insight into time–varying inverter–associated disturbances. To address this limitation, a hybrid and sequential signal–processing framework is proposed, integrating frequency–domain analysis, time–frequency representations, and adaptive signal decomposition to identify stationary, non–stationary, and transient harmonic components. The methodology is experimentally validated using real measurements from a grid–connected PV inverter operating under variable irradiance and dynamic load conditions. The campaign–level average current THD increased from approximately 1.5% under baseline conditions to approximately 7.8% during PV–inverter operation, with peak values exceeding 8%. Dominant low–order harmonics and short–duration current distortions were also observed. The novelty of the proposed framework lies in the hierarchical assignment of complementary diagnostic roles to each method and in the quantitative evaluation of the VMD–HHT stage using experimental measurements. The framework provides a practical methodology for advanced power quality assessment and monitoring in inverter–dominated distribution networks. © 2026

title: Transient stability enhancement for grid-forming DFIGs under symmetrical grid faults: Seamless mode-switching control based on active-flux decoupling
abstract: Grid-forming doubly fed induction generators (GFM-DFIGs) are key enablers for voltage and frequency support in high-renewable-penetration power systems. However, deep symmetrical grid faults lead to transient instability, overcurrent, and insufficient reactive power. This paper reveals that coupling between the natural and forced components of the stator flux is the root cause of these problems. To address them, seamless mode-switching control based on active-flux decoupling is proposed. The method includes (i) an active-flux decoupling algorithm that separately regulates natural and forced flux via feedforward compensation to accelerate transient energy dissipation and (ii) a seamless switching logic that eliminates transient shocks during fault transitions. Theoretical analysis using the equal-area criterion yielded the critical clearing time (CCT). Verification on a low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) platform under deep symmetrical faults revealed that under an 80% voltage sag, the proposed method accelerated flux attenuation by 73.7% and reduced the peak rotor current by 52.3% compared with conventional VSG-based GFM-DFIGs. Under a 50% sag, the CCT was extended by 68.8%, and no switching oscillations occurred. The experimental results confirmed the effectiveness of the method. The strategy achieved coordinated optimization of the fault current limitation, transient stability, and reactive power support. © 2026
