title: Non-covalent interactions between Lycium barbarum polysaccharides and goat whey protein isolate: Structural changes, odor mitigation and application in yogurt
abstract: This study investigated the non-covalent interactions between Lycium barbarum polysaccharide (LBP) and goat whey protein isolate (GWPI), as well as the structural modifications of LBP-GWPI complexes, their effects on volatile release associated with goaty flavor, and their application performance in yogurt. The results demonstrated that LBP bound to GWPI via hydrogen bonding, electrostatic interactions, and hydrophobic interactions, inducing conformational rearrangement and a more compact microstructure of GWPI. The complexation process disrupted the ordered secondary structure of GWPI without altering its primary structure, with the complexes formed at pH 3 exhibiting stronger intermolecular binding and more compact microstructures. Electronic nose analysis indicated that the complexes modulated the release of volatile compounds associated with goaty flavor, with a greater effect observed at pH 3 than at pH 7. Furthermore, application of the optimized LBP-GWPI complex in goat milk yogurt revealed that it effectively maintained structural stability while significantly improving product quality; the optimal ratio was LBP-GWPI = 1:1, which increased yogurt viscosity by 424% at a shear rate of 0.01 s−1 and water-holding capacity by 18.57% relative to the control group. This study elucidates the structure-function relationships of LBP-GWPI complexes in modulating volatile release, providing a feasible green modification strategy and robust theoretical support for quality enhancement and high-value utilization of goat dairy products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Wholesale electricity market pricing model design: Layering the transparency
abstract: The energy transition is challenging traditional wholesale electricity market pricing models. Divergences in modelling outcomes hinder comparisons across regional studies, often attributed to variations in model designs and data availability. This is further complicated by theoretical model designs that are insufficiently aligned with real-world constraints, such as limited access to market data, confidential information, or high-quality datasets.Rather than building a market model and then rummaging for suitable datasets, this study inverts the approach and layers data into the model design.The framework was applied in a longitudinal study across three study regions, Alberta (AESO), California (CAISO), and Western Australia (WEM), which have experienced high growth in renewable generation. The technical implementation employed a broad range of established machine learning methods (OLS, MARS, ANN, GAMLSS, XGBoost) alongside a structured probabilistic approach (Bayesian Belief Networks). The approach was found to be feasible as several models consistently provided the optimal design across regions and configurations implemented, as such supporting the assertion that models could be designed, configured and compared using this layered approach.Matching model complexity to all available data should serve as a guide, since higher-performing models do not necessarily require access to extensive datasets. Finally, cross-market comparisons showed that different market characteristics had a greater influence on model accuracy, illustrating that real-world data constraints need to guide model development. © 2026 The Authors. title: Impact of nanoemulsion-Filled algal hydrogels structure on the in vitro digestibility and β-carotene bioaccessibility
abstract: Bioactive compounds encapsulated in nanoemulsions (NEs) can gain additional protection when the NEs are incorporated into hydrogels and forming NE-filled hydrogel. In this regard, algal-derived hydrocolloids are attractive gel-forming materials, but it remains unclear how their gelation mechanisms influence lipid digestion and the bioaccessibility (BA) of bioactive component under gastrointestinal (GI) conditions. In this work, β-carotene-loaded NE was incorporated into agar, alginate, or κ-carrageenan hydrogels (0.5% and 1.0% w/w) and subjected to a semi-dynamic in vitro digestion. Particle size analysis and confocal microscopy showed that NE-filled hydrogels limited droplet aggregation, whereas the unencapsulated NE exhibited coalescence during late gastric emptying (GE). During intestinal phase, NE showed the highest total free fatty acid (FFA) release (92.45 ± 0.72%), whereas NE-filled hydrogels reduced lipolysis depending on hydrocolloid gelation mechanism and concentration. Alginate exhibited the most concentration-dependent effect, with FFA release decreasing from 79.43 ± 0.90% at 0.5% (w/w) to 67.06 ± 3.11% at 1.0% (w/w) consistent with formation ‘egg-box’ structures via cross-linking with Ca2+.In contrast, agar and κ-carrageenan, showed weaker concentration-dependent effects, attributed to differences in network architecture and permeability. NE-filled hydrogels maintained higher β-carotene BA across the GE stages than the unencapsulated NE. While the BA of the NE was 14.77 ± 1.01% at GE5, all NE-filled hydrogels retained substantially higher BA values, remaining above 35% at GE5. These findings show that polysaccharide gelation mechanism and concentration can be tuned to modulate lipolysis and enhance β-carotene delivery. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: Effects of dislocation-twin interactions on twin evolution and dislocation transformation in AZ31 magnesium alloy
abstract: The interaction between dislocations and deformation twins strongly influences microstructural evolution and deformation behavior in Mg alloys. In this work, the effects of dislocation-twin interactions on twinning and slip behavior in AZ31 magnesium (Mg) alloy were investigated using a two-step quasi-in-situ compression approach. The results show that during the initial deformation stage, basal-prismatic/prismatic-basal (BP/PB) interfaces generated by dislocation-twin interactions suppress twin growth while promoting new twin nucleation and non-basal dislocation transformation, with the strongest pinning effect occurring at an intermediate interface density. During subsequent deformation, twin growth continues, while dislocation slip gradually becomes the predominant deformation mode. Basal ⟨a⟩ dislocations transform into non-basal dislocation types through distinct pathways governed by geometric compatibility. Direct transformation is favored at high geometric compatibility factor (m′), whereas indirect transformation predominates at low m′ values. These findings reveal how BP/PB interfaces influence twin evolution and dislocation transformation in Mg alloys. © 2026

title: Coordinated current-limiting and transient stability control of grid-forming VSGs under grid-voltage sags
abstract: When power systems experience large disturbances such as grid-voltage sags, virtual synchronous generators (VSGs) can suffer from power-angle instability and output overcurrent. Existing current-limiting strategies often cannot restrict fault currents while preserving converter transient stability and grid-forming support capability. To address this challenge, this paper analyzes the transient instability mechanism and current-limiting characteristics of VSGs and proposes a transient stability control strategy that coordinates steady-state current regulation and instantaneous-overcurrent suppression. The proposed strategy maintains power-angle stability by improving the active-power loop; reconstructs the reactive-power loop through output-current closed-loop integral control to achieve accurate steady-state fault-current limiting while preserving voltage-source characteristics; and uses adaptive virtual impedance to suppress instantaneous overcurrent at fault inception and clearance. The proposed control scheme is validated comprehensively through simulations and hardware-in-the-loop verification. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Photovoltaic maximum power extraction and delivery based on adaptive PSO-neural network-fuzzy algorithms implemented using an experimental test bench
abstract: This paper reports the hardware implementation of two novel Maximum Power Point Tracking strategies for photovoltaic systems. To maximize harvested energy, the photovoltaic source must be regulated for high efficiency while keeping the controller low-cost, computationally light, and easy to implement. It is proposed that two Maximum Power Point Tracking algorithms that use Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization to train a neural network. The first, based on Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization, enhances the classic fixed-step Perturb-and-Observe method; the second integrates a fuzzy-logic regulator. Both approaches are designed to overcome the limitations of conventional Maximum Power Point Tracking techniques. The controllers drive a non-isolated, high-gain DC/DC boost converter used as an impedance adapter to optimize power transfer from photovoltaic modules to the load. Simulink models were developed and benchmarked against standard Perturb-and-Observe and fuzzy-logic methods, with simulations indicating clear benefits for the Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization-based neural network with fuzzy-logic regulation. A hardware test bench—comprising a solar emulator and a dSPACE 1104 board—was then built to validate performance. Experiments confirm that the Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization-based neural network with fuzzy-logic regulation achieves fast execution (0.03 s), high robustness, no steady-state oscillations (steady-state error <10−5), and no measurable energy loss, with a measured overshoot of 19.5% across diverse environmental and load conditions. © 2026 The Authors. title: Ultrasound pretreatment of Acacia seyal gum arabic before spray drying: effects on interfacial behavior and avocado oil emulsion stability
abstract: High-intensity ultrasound can modify hydrocolloid functionality, but the processing conditions that improve gum arabic performance without impairing stabilization remain uncertain. This study evaluated a structured screening matrix in which gum arabic dispersions at 20–30% (w/w) were treated at nominal powers of 255–765 W for 0–15 min, spray dried, reconstituted to 20% solids, and used to stabilize avocado oil-in-water emulsions. Intrinsic viscosity, Cross-model rheology, time-resolved interfacial tension, gum-dispersion zeta potential, droplet-size evolution, and Turbiscan stability were evaluated. The intrinsic-viscosity-derived apparent hydrodynamic-size estimate decreased from 0.760 MDa in untreated gum to 0.663 MDa after 10 min, with little further average change after 15 min. Across the tested branches, 10 min gave the most favorable average interfacial and physical-stability response: mean interfacial tension at 1800 s decreased from 15.04 to 11.25 mN/m, the pre-drying gum-dispersion zeta potential shifted from −23.69 to −29.32 mV, and mean day-21 Turbiscan Stability Index decreased from 2.834 to 1.987. A branch-adjusted repeated-measures analysis supported an exploratory association between interfacial-tension reduction and increased zeta-potential magnitude (coefficient 0.938; 9 degrees of freedom; probability below 0.001). The endpoint-specific rankings were not identical: E−10 had the lowest day-21 Turbiscan Stability Index, whereas C-15 had the smallest final droplets. Thus, 10 min is interpreted as an operationally favorable average duration within the tested concentration–nominal-power matrix, not as a universal optimum or direct evidence of a molecular mechanism. The observed differences reflect the complete processing history, including ultrasound pretreatment, heating, spray drying, and reconstitution. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: Enhancing robotic interoperability: An approach for ROS 2-driven system integration
abstract: Reconfigurable manufacturing requires robotic workcells that can adapt to changing products, processes, and equipment without extensive redesign or manual reprogramming. This paper presents the R3M framework, a ROS 2 driven integration architecture that connects model based manufacturing knowledge with execution level robotic control. Product, process, and equipment information is formalised through UML domain models and serialised in AutomationML(AML), enabling automated correspondence between assembly requirements, available skills, and executable recipes. The framework integrates automated programme generation, reinforcement learning based recipe optimisation, and a modular CAD informed six degree of freedom perception layer to support both technical and semantic interoperability across simulated and physical workcells. The approach is evaluated through Cube Kitting and Cylinder Stacking use cases implemented on distinct robotic platforms, including ABB and Universal Robots systems. Experimental results show high reliability, with environment launch performance reaching up to 99.93%, standard skill sequences achieving 100% execution success, and full use case trials exceeding 97% success in simulation and reaching 100% on physical hardware. These findings demonstrate that R3M provides a scalable foundation for adaptive robotic manufacturing, reducing programming effort while supporting modular substitution, robust perception, and simulation to real deployment. © 2026 The Authors. title: Robotic learning from demonstration enabled by improved gaussian mixture model and gaussian mixture regression
abstract: Robotic learning from demonstration (LfD) can significantly minimize robotic programming difficulties due to its intuitiveness and efficiency. Gaussian mixture model (GMM)/Gaussian mixture regression (GMR) is an effective method to implement LfD. However, there are limitations in GMM/GMR, such as the requirement of creating multiple demonstrations, sensitivity to demonstration defects, and underfitting/overfitting generalization in industrial tasks. To tackle the issues, in this study, an improved GMM/GMR approach with three improvements is proposed. Firstly, a Gaussian noise scattering strategy is designed to minimize the required number of multiple demonstrations and eliminate unsmooth turning areas/jitters defects in the demonstration. Secondly, based on a new evaluation criterion of incorporating the Gaussian cluster number, Bayesian information criterion, and dynamic time warping, the particle swarm optimization algorithm is introduced to achieve an optimal balance between feature preservation and smoothness for a regression solution, thereby effectively mitigating the overfitting/underfitting issues. Thirdly, the B-spline curve-based reconstruction of the regression solution is devised to enhance the adaptability of GMM/GMR to the changes in target positions. Experiments on retired product recycling are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the approach presented in this study, providing a reliable solution to facilitate LfD in industrial environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: A coordinated reclosing strategy for active distribution networks based on fault type discrimination and sectionalized coordination
abstract: A coordinated reclosing strategy based on fault type discrimination and sectionalized coordination is proposed for active distribution networks with high inverter-based resource penetration, tackling the issues of sustained inverter feeding during faults, complex reverse power flow paths, and complicated coordination among multiple circuit breakers. By analyzing the influence mechanism of time-varying arc resistance during the processes of arc burning, current zero-crossing, extinction, and reignition on Fourier-based impedance calculation, a criterion based on the fluctuation area of mean-removed equivalent reactance is established to achieve rapid discrimination between transient and permanent faults. A sectionalized reclosing strategy is developed among the main circuit breaker, the inverter-side disconnecting breaker, and the downstream sectionalizing breaker, by integrating the faulted section identification, power direction, and breaker functional configurations. The corresponding operation sequences including tripping, blocking, dead-line reclosing, and synchro-check reclosing are specified for various fault sections. For transient faults, the proposed strategy enables sequential reclosing between the inverter-side breaker and the main breaker, restoring supply to healthy sections. For permanent faults, it inhibits the reclosing of the responsible breaker and prevents re-energization of the permanent fault. Dynamic physical testing and PSCAD/EMTDC simulations demonstrate that the proposed fault type discrimination method effectively discriminates between transient and permanent faults, and that the sectionalized reclosing coordination strategy achieves selective fault isolation and orderly service restoration for upstream, midstream, and downstream fault sections, enhancing the security and reliability of the reclosing process in inverter-rich distribution networks. © 2026

title: Scalable microfluidic blow spinning for in situ synthesis of A-site engineered perovskite nanocrystals in nanofibers with enhanced stability and outdoor functionality
abstract: Scalable fabrication of perovskite nanocrystals (PNCs) with both exceptional fluorescence stability and tunable blue-to-red emission remains a key challenge in perovskite research. In this study, we develop a room-temperature microfluidic blow spinning (MBS) strategy that enables in situ growth and encapsulation of PNCs within polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofibers, together with simultaneous modulation via A-site and ligand engineering. Starting from a green-emitting γ-phase Rb0.5Cs0.5PbBr3/PAN nanofiber film, achieved through partial substitution of Cs with Rb at the A-site, a series of γ-phase Rb0.5Cs0.5PbX3/PAN (X=Br, I) nanofiber films are fabricated at scale. By tuning the halide composition and the type and concentration of ligands, including oleylamine (OAm) and octylamine (OTAm), blue-to-red emission spanning 476‒600 nm is achieved. The resulting nanofiber films exhibit excellent stability under harsh conditions, including long-term storage, thermal cycling, water immersion, and ultraviolet irradiation. Furthermore, the Rb0.5Cs0.5PbX3/PAN nanofiber films demonstrate multifunctional performance, enabling fluorescent patterning for wearable devices and efficient photocatalytic CO2-to-CO conversion under natural sunlight, with a maximum production rate of 83.6 μmol g−1 h−1. This work provides a scalable approach for fabricating high-performance PNCs and offers new insights into their practical application. © 2026

title: An advanced deep learning framework for scalable smart grid intrusion detection
abstract: The smart grid is a critical component of modern energy distribution system; however, it faces several cybersecurity challenges, including firmware exploitation, data leakage, unauthorized access, and data manipulation. To overcome these challenges, a deep learning-based intrusion detection system (IDS) for the IEEE-39 and 118 bus smart grid framework is proposed in this research. First, communication traffic is collected, interpreted, and processed to obtain meaningful features for intrusion detection. The proposed model combines three novel techniques: transductive few-shot learning enhanced by spectral-spatial embedding for sequential pattern recognition and temporal heterogeneous graph contrastive learning for static relationship learning. Furthermore, a graph convolution network with a self-attention mechanism is optimized by the spotted deer optimization algorithm for efficient learning. This hybrid approach is effective for both temporal and spatial dependencies in network data. The experimental findings represent the suggested IDS detecting the attack with high accuracy of 98.6% and a lower false alarm rate. The proposed methodology is validated via MATLAB simulations on IEEE-39 and 118 bus systems and is superior to existing methods in the smart grid environment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Finite-Element Assessment of Concrete Mine-Shaft Lining: Lamé Validation and Groove Effects
abstract: This paper presents a Lamé-verified finite-element workflow for assessing the stress–strain state and residual load-bearing capacity of concrete linings in vertical mine shafts with local technological grooves. A full three-dimensional 1 m high lining ring with an internal diameter of 6 m was modeled in Abaqus and verified against the analytical Lamé solution for a thick-walled cylinder under external pressure. Four scenarios were analyzed: an elastic intact reference model, an elastic model with an inner technological recess, a zonal concrete damage-plasticity model (CDPM2) without groove, and a zonal CDPM2 model with groove. The radial and hoop stress profiles closely matched the analytical solution. The groove caused pronounced stress redistribution, including a tensile hoop-stress concentration of approximately 24 MPa on the outer side of the lining opposite the groove and inner-contour ovalization with radial displacement from −9.0 to +7.4 mm. A parametric post-processing campaign evaluated groove depth, groove radius/opening, mesh density, concrete class, and zonal material assumptions using the normalized residual-capacity indicator R_FE. Groove depth governed the global residual-capacity trend, whereas groove radius/opening acted as a secondary geometric modifier. The Abaqus internal energy output (ALLIE) and dissipated/stabilization energy output (ALLSD) are interpreted as comparative energy indicators, not standalone failure criteria. The workflow connects finite-element assessment with field diagnostics while acknowledging limitations related to local peak-stress convergence, low-pressure proxy interpretation, and the adopted CDPM2 parameterization. ©2027 The author(s). title: A Game-Theoretic Approach for Probabilistic Reactive Power Management with Flexibility and Stability Assessment
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources and the inherent uncertainties in power systems have made reactive power management a critical challenge for maintaining voltage stability and system flexibility. This study proposes an innovative probabilistic reactive power optimization method based on game theory for the IEEE 57-bus system. This approach considers uncertainties in both load demand and wind power generation while modeling interactions among network players, including generators, transformers, and reactive power compensators. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method significantly reduces network losses (∼65 MW), efficiently allocates reactive power from compensators, and improves voltage stability and flexibility indices. Furthermore, the approach enables multi-objective analysis by evaluating the impact of wind power variability on network losses and the probability of constraint violations. These findings demonstrate that the proposed framework provides a robust and effective tool for intelligent reactive power management in modern power networks with high renewable penetration. ©2027 The author(s). title: Existence of variational solutions to the problem of contact of a beam with a DNC obstacle
abstract: This work establishes the existence of weak solutions to a mathematical model for the vibrations of an Euler-Bernoulli beam that may come in contact with a reactive obstacle situated below it. The obstacle reaction is described by the Damped Normal Compliance (DNC) contact condition, which extends both the normal compliance and the damped normal response contact conditions. The model consists of the Euler-Bernoulli beam, clamped at the left end and free at the right and, with the added DNC contact resistance. The classical and variational formulations of the model are presented. A Galerkin method is applied to the version of the beam with added viscosity. Then, the necessary estimates derived, and the existence of the unique solution to the problem with viscosity proved. Then, passing to the limit of vanishing viscosity, a solution to the problem without viscosity is obtained and its uniqueness is established. This work is an addition to the currently expanding Mathematical Theory of Contact Mechanics (MTCM). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Weather-guided decomposition and hard-routing expert modeling for short-term photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: Solar energy has become a pivotal renewable resource in modern power systems; however, the stochastic and weather-dependent variability of photovoltaic (PV) generation continues to challenge accurate power forecasting and grid operation. This study proposes a weather-adaptive forecasting framework that integrates meteorological classification, signal decomposition, and hybrid deep learning for short-term PV power prediction. Specifically, a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) partitions historical samples into homogeneous weather subsets, after which Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN) is applied to each subset to extract intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). A weather-guided hard-routing expert framework is then employed. Three long short-term memory network-Transformer(LSTM–Transformer) experts with identical architectures but independent parameters are trained separately using the sunny, cloudy, and rainy subsets. For each forecasting day, a rule-based weather router activates the expert associated with the dominant weather category. The activated expert jointly models meteorological variables and IMF components to represent weather-induced temporal variations and cross-time dependencies. Experimental results on a two-year PV dataset demonstrate that, compared with the baseline models, the proposed method reduces the average mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE) by 33.7% and 30.2%, respectively, while achieving an average coefficient of determination (R²) of 98.69%.These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in the evaluated PV power forecasting task. © 2026

title: Testing of Multi-Section Deep Well Sampler and Fluid Sampling from Borehole 5G at Vostok Station, Antarctica
abstract: Testing of the Multi-section Deep Well Sampler (MDWS) was conducted during the 70th Russian Antarctic Expedition at Vostok Station in 2024/25. The MDWS is a non-circulating piston sampler designed to collect borehole fluid samples from multiple depths in a single round trip. Surface tests verified the operational integrity of the electromechanical system and identified optimal performance parameters. The MDWS was then tested in Borehole 5G-5 at depths from 1,250 m to 3,597.4 m across six round trips, collecting 18 samples under extreme conditions (temperatures down to −60°C and pressures up to 350 atm). The device successfully passed all tests, proving its efficiency for Arctic and Antarctic applications and confirming its manufacturability at the Empress Catherine II Saint Petersburg Mining University, Russian Federation. ©2027 The author(s). title: Numerical and Experimental investigation on a new tube design featuring micro-finned tubes with broken double V-cut twisted tapes
abstract: Achieving high thermal efficiency remains a key challenge in the design of absorber tubes. As a result, the thermohydraulic performance of a newly proposed absorber tube, featuring finned tubes with broken double-V-cut twisted tapes, was investigated using Thermohydraulic performance factor analysis. The numerical and experimental study evaluated five key parameters: the number of V-cuts (2, 4, 6), the number of twisted tapes (2, 5, 8), the thickness of twisted tapes (0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5 mm), the width of the twisted tape (6, 6.5, 7, 7.5, 8 mm), and the twist ratio in the twisted tapes (0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1). This research was conducted under a constant heat flux of 1000 W/m2 and a Reynolds number range between 800 and 6000. Out of 95 simulation cases, the optimal tube design achieved a 1.221 THPF at a Reynolds number of 800, with a 0.5 twisted-tape twist ratio, a width of 7 mm, a thickness of 1 mm, 4 V-cuts, and 2 twisted tapes. Finally, changing the working fluid from water to 0.4% CuO and then to 0.8% CuO nanofluids resulted in Thermohydraulic performance factor values of 1.369 and 1.407, respectively. © 2026 The Authors. title: Deep Learning-Based Multimodal Fusion of Wavelet-Decomposed MRI and PET for Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis
abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is crucial for timely clinical intervention and treatment planning. Recent advances in deep learning have facilitated the automatic extraction of informative biomarkers from neuroimaging data. In this study, we proposed a multimodal framework that integrates structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and functional positron emission tomography (PET) using three-dimensional convolutional neural networks (3D-CNNs) with wavelet-domain feature extraction (CO.2). First, MRI and PET volumes are decomposed into multiple sub-bands via discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to capture complementary frequency-domain patterns. Next, a custom 3D-CNN extracts multi-scale hierarchical features from each modality (CO.3,4). The resulting modality-specific embeddings are fused at the decision level through a stacked one-dimensional CNN (1D-CNN) ensemble to classify subjects into AD, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and normal control (NC) groups. Experiments on the ADNI dataset show strong performance across three binary tasks, achieving 97.9% (AD vs. NC), 97.5% (MCI vs. NC), and 99.6% (AD vs. MCI, AUC ≈ 0.997). These results demonstrate that the proposed wavelet-enhanced stacked multimodal model provides a robust and generalizable tool for early-stage AD detection, particularly in distinguishing subtle transitions between MCI and AD (CO.2). ©2027 The author(s). title: Grid-connected performance optimization control strategy of DFIG with coaxial high-inertia flywheel system
abstract: The high penetration of grid-connected renewable energy has significantly reduced power system inertia, bringing critical challenges to frequency stability and voltage support. To improve the operation resilience of low-inertia systems, this paper presents a grid-connected performance optimization control strategy for the combined topology of a doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) and a coaxial high-inertia flywheel. The DFIG stator is directly connected to the grid, and the flywheel provides fast kinetic energy support through mechanical coupling. The grid-side converter maintains stable DC voltage and unity power factor, while the rotor-side converter realizes decoupled control of stator active and reactive power. To enhance frequency stability, a system frequency response model is established, and real-time active power compensation is generated via droop and inertia control. A variable-parameter optimization strategy is further proposed to adjust droop and inertia coefficients dynamically. For grid voltage sag conditions, an optimized feed-forward transient current control scheme is adopted to enhance low-voltage ride-through capability. Both theoretical analysis and results verify that the proposed topology and control strategy can effectively improve the frequency and voltage stability of low-inertia power systems, providing technical support for the reliable operation of high-renewable power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Optimal pricing and charging design of the EVCS-EVs network based on a Stackelberg mean field game approach
abstract: With the rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) and charging networks, the design of dynamic pricing (DP) and dynamic charging (DC) strategies has become critical for maintaining grid stability and improving economic efficiency. However, traditional DP methods often fail to capture strategic interactions between electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) and large-scale EVs. This paper proposes a Stackelberg mean field game (SMFG) framework for the joint optimization of EVCS's DP and EVs’ DC. The framework models the EVCS as the leader, optimizing DP via Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP), while EVs act as followers whose DC is described by an N-player differential game (DG) and approximated by a MFG. The mean field equilibrium is obtained by solving the coupled Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman and Fokker–Planck–Kolmogorov equations. A hierarchical DP–DC algorithm is developed and proven to converge to a SMF εN-Nash equilibrium (NE). Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves efficient and scalable coordination between DP and DC decisions, while improving computational efficiency and maintaining stable system performance. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Simultaneous enhancement of hardness and corrosion resistance in liquid-metal-dealloyed Mg–Ti composites via short-time Al-melt treatment
abstract: This study presents a short-time reactive Al-melt treatment that simultaneously enhances hardness and corrosion resistance in liquid-metal-dealloyed Mg–Ti composites. A three-dimensional bicontinuous Mg–Ti composite is first fabricated by immersing a Ti30Cu70 precursor in a pure Mg melt, followed by immersion in a pure Al melt at 750 °C for 10 s. The initial Mg–Ti composite consists of a co-continuous α -Mg/ α -Ti matrix–matrix structure. After Al-melt treatment, the interconnected morphology is preserved, while the phase constitution is reconstructed into a multiphase α -Ti/TiAl3/Al3Mg2 structure. TiAl3 forms along the residual α -Ti ligaments, whereas the original Mg-rich regions transform into Al3Mg2. The average effective grain size of the residual α -Ti decreases from 3.7 to 0.8 µm, accompanied by increased local misorientation and a higher density of {11–22} compression twin boundaries. As a result, the surface hardness increases from 106 to 378 HV, while remaining above 260 HV at a depth of 260 µm. The Al-treated Mg–Ti composite also exhibits a markedly reduced corrosion rate in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution, decreasing from 13.2 to 0.5 mm/year based on hydrogen evolution measurements and from 17.2 to 0.7 mm/year based on weight-loss measurements. Scanning Kelvin probe force microscopy reveals that the initial direct α -Mg/ α -Ti interface, with a Volta potential difference of approximately 635 mV, is replaced by α -Ti/TiAl3 and TiAl3/Al3Mg2 interfaces with lower potential differences of approximately 271 and 285 mV, respectively. Overall, the short-time Al-melt treatment enables simultaneous hardness increase and corrosion mitigation through rapid interfacial reconstruction and phase transformation while preserving the bicontinuous structure. title: A Machine Learning Approach for Cassava Leaf Disease Identification Using Constraint-Regularized Neural Networks and AJFO Meta-Optimization
abstract: Early diagnosis of cassava leaf diseases is paramount to enhance the productivity of cassava and to support sustainable agriculture. Traditional deep learning methods, however, are not very robust in complex field conditions, suffer from manual hyperparameter tuning, and are not fully leveraging the structural information from the disease, which leads to poor classification accuracy and poor generalization. To cope with these challenges, this paper proposes a unified machine learning framework for cassava leaf disease identification, which combines with enhanced image preprocessing, Residual Multi-scale U-Net (RMUNet) segmentation, Multi-Level Feature Extraction (MLFE), Constraint-Regularized Neural Network (CRNN), and Artificial Jellyfish Optimization (AJFO). The proposed approach is different from the conventional RMUNet-based disease detection techniques, which involve disease-oriented multiscale segmentation along with structural regularization in feature space to enhance the classification resilience in the presence of illumination variations, background clutter, and noisy farming ground. Moreover, AJFO uses to tune the learning rate, batch size, dropout rate, training epochs, and regularization coefficient in an automatic way, which removes the manual tuning of these parameters and increases the stability of convergence. A computational complexity analysis also shows that the extra cost of optimization is only during offline training, and inference complexity is comparable to the conventional deep learning models. Experimental results on the Cassava Leaf Disease dataset show the effectiveness of the proposed framework with 99% classification accuracy for healthy leaves, 97% classification accuracy for Cassava Mosaic Disease (CMD), 95% classification accuracy for Cassava Green Mite (CGM), and 93% classification accuracy for Cassava Brown Streak Disease (CBSD) and consistently better precision, recall, and F1-score than CNN-PLDD, SVM-PLDD, and DENN-PLDD. Overall, the proposed integrated framework demonstrates its capability of achieving effective convergence, better generalization performance, and effective disease classification performance under different imaging conditions, which is considered as a strong solution for intelligent precision agriculture and automated crop health monitoring. ©2027 The author(s). title: Water as a dual-function modulator: From defect passivation to energy-transfer control for color-tunable lead-free perovskite white LEDs
abstract: This work demonstrates a humidity-responsive, single-component white-light-emitting device based on Cs3CeCl6:Sb3+ nanocrystals. Under controlled humid conditions, the device exhibits continuously tunable white-light emission, with the correlated color temperature varying from 4400 to 5600 K while maintaining a color rendering index above 95%. Controlled H2O adsorption not only passivates surface defects in Cs3CeCl6 nanocrystals, increasing the photoluminescence quantum yield from 75% to 98%, but also regulates the Ce3+ → Sb3+ energy-transfer process in the Sb3+-doped system. Spectroscopic analysis, carrier-dynamics measurements, and surface-slab calculations show that adsorbed H2O interacts with the Cs3CeCl6 surface and perturbs the local electronic environment of Ce3+ sites near the nanocrystal surface, leading to a blue shift of the Ce3+ 5d-related energy levels and reduced spectral overlap with the Sb3+ absorption band. This suppresses the Ce3+ → Sb3+ Förster resonance energy-transfer process and enables dynamic tuning of the emission color and color temperature. These results reveal the dual role of surface-adsorbed H2O in defect passivation and energy-transfer regulation, providing a new strategy for developing efficient, color-tunable, lead-free metal-halide luminescent materials. © 2026

title: Programming-Based Computational Modelling for Freight Distribution Using Clarke-Wright Savings Method for Route Optimization: A Case Study in Surabaya, Indonesia
abstract: Urban freight pickup in dense metropolitan areas is constrained by short service windows, congestion, and limited vehicle capacity. This study evaluates a practical hybrid heuristic—Clarke-Wright Savings for clustering and Nearest Neighbor for sequencing—for evening pickup operations at a major Indonesian postal logistics hub in Surabaya. Using 46 pickup locations, the MATLAB implementation assesses service coverage, route-time feasibility, fleet requirement, distance efficiency, and capacity utilization under a 500-unit vehicle capacity and a 150-minute maximum route duration. The optimized plan serves all 46 pickup locations with five vehicles, compared with 22 locations served by seven vehicles in the existing operation, and reduces distance per served point from 14.57 to 4.08 km/point while keeping the longest route at 144 minutes. The case also reveals a transferable operational pattern: early routes tend to be filled efficiently in demand-concentrated areas, whereas residual spatially dispersed demand tends to create lower-utilization tail routes. A fixed-seed Genetic Algorithm benchmark further reduced total distance to 152.79 km under the same constraints, but required a longer average runtime of 60.52 seconds compared with 1.13 seconds for the proposed MATLAB-based heuristic. These findings show that transparent classical heuristics can still deliver implementable gains in urban pickup logistics when capacity and time feasibility are evaluated jointly. ©2027 The author(s). title: The complex Ginzburg-Landau equation on a finite interval and chaos suppression via a finite-dimensional boundary feedback stabilizer
abstract: In this paper, we study the well-posedness and boundary stabilization of the initial-boundary value problem for the complex Ginzburg-Landau (CGL) equation on a finite interval. First, we establish a local well-posedness theory for the open-loop model in L 2-based fractional Sobolev spaces in the case of Dirichlet-Neumann type inhomogeneous mixed boundary conditions. This local well-posedness result is based on linear estimates derived by using the weak solution formula obtained via the unified transform (also known as the Fokas method). Next, we study the global well-posedness properties of the open-loop model in presence of inhomogeneous boundary conditions. Then, we turn our attention to the rapid boundary feedback stabilization problem and design a nonlocal controller which uses a finite number of Fourier modes of the state of solution. This design relies on the fact that solutions of the CGL equation can be separated into a slow, finite-dimensional component and a rapidly decaying tail, with the former primarily governing long-term behavior. We determine the necessary number of modes required to stabilize the system at a specified rate. Additionally, we identify the minimum number of modes that ensure stabilization at an unspecified decay rate. These theoretical results are validated by numerical simulations. The spatiotemporal estimates established in the first part of the paper are also employed to obtain local solutions of the controlled system. The existence of global energy solutions follows from stabilization estimates, while uniqueness follows from the uniqueness of an associated initial-boundary value problem with homogeneous boundary conditions whose solutions are in correspondence with the solutions of the original system through a bounded invertible Volterra-type integral transform on Sobolev spaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Purification of lanthanum chloride solution through tertiary amine extraction: thermodynamic and graded assessment; [Лантан хлориді ерітінділерін үшінші деңгейлі амин экстракциясы арқылы тазарту: термодинамикалық және кезеңдік бағалау]; [Очистка растворов хлорида посредством третичной аминной экстракции: термодинамическая и этапная оценка]
abstract: Purification of lanthanum chloride from high-load zinc contaminants remains a major challenge in producing grade 5N lanthanum oxides. This study investigates the process of matrix-driven solvent extraction using tertiary amine N235 to treat a 1.41 M rare earth oxides (REO) industrial lanthanum chloride feed containing 3000 mg/L zinc. Thermodynamic modelling with Medusa Hydra and Langmuir isotherms revealed that the high chloride activity (> 4 M) of the matrix induced significant changes in coordination towards the extractable [ZnCl4]2- complex. This transition has a spontaneous Gibbs free energy of-14.68 kJ/mol. While the two-stage counter-current flow sheet meets the industry target of less than 50 mg/L zinc, the five-stage configuration achieves a four-log reduction to 0.23 mg/L, effectively achieving 99.999% purity. This reagent's lean approach, using water-induced stripping, offers a sustainable and mathematically validated framework for ultra-high purity rare earth finishes. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Contrastive self-supervised temporal transformers with physics-guided regularisation for low-label photovoltaic array fault diagnosis
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) arrays under variable irradiance and temperature are susceptible to incipient line-to-line faults (LLF), open-circuit faults (OCF), partial shading faults (PSF), and high-impedance LLF (HILL), whose fault currents fall below the protection threshold at the maximum power point, where the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) controller masks the fault signature. Data-driven diagnosis achieves high accuracy but typically requires large labeled fault datasets that are difficult to obtain in operational plants. This paper proposes a three-stage self-supervised learning (SSL) framework for PV array fault diagnosis operating exclusively on sequential voltage, current, and power measurements. A temporal encoder (1-D convolutional neural network front end + four-layer Transformer) is pretrained on unlabeled monitoring sequences via NT-Xent contrastive learning with PV-safe augmentations, then fine-tuned with limited labels using a physics-guided regularizer that penalizes violations of the P=VI relation in the embedding space. An evidential Dirichlet-output uncertainty head enables calibrated selective decision-making, achieving an expected calibration error (ECE) of 0.0214 and out-of-distribution flagging rates of 41–87% under unseen operating conditions. On a simulated 10 × 3 grid-connected PV array, the framework attains 98.26 ± 0.20% overall accuracy with only 50 labeled samples per class, outperforming the semisupervised ladder network by 1.38 percentage points (pp) and SSL time-series baselines (TS-TCC, TFPred) by 1.90–2.52 pp. Validation on the real experimental GPVS-Faults dataset yields 98.14 ± 0.18% accuracy (AUROC 0.996, ECE 0.012), a sim-to-real gap of only 0.12 pp, and a macro-F1 of 0.961 under realistic class imbalance. The physics loss improves accuracy by +1.65 pp at 10 dB SNR, confirmed significant by McNemar's test (p < .01). © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Gallic acid modulates the balance among network structure, water stability, and antioxidant function in corn peptide-konjac glucomannan gels
abstract: Plant-based gels increasingly need to reconcile mechanical integrity, water stability and bioactivity, yet most designs still rely on intact proteins whose folded or aggregated structures limit molecular accessibility. Corn peptide (CP) offers a distinct but underused route: a short-chain, mobile and chemically exposed plant-peptide fraction with intrinsic antioxidant potential, but limited ability to form self-supporting networks. This study treated CP as an interaction-active, network-modulating component within a konjac glucomannan (KGM) scaffold and examined how gallic acid (GA) concentration translated peptide-associated reactivity into macroscopic gel performance. GA regulated the CP-KGM matrix in a concentration-dependent manner. At 0.3% GA, the gel combined low syneresis and freeze-thaw water loss, shorter water-relaxation times, high cohesiveness, rapid stress relaxation, and greater microstructural continuity. Higher GA levels further enhanced ABTS and T-AOC responses but were associated with larger operational hydrophobic-association indices and reduced network uniformity. Operational extraction indices and FTIR changes were consistent with concentration-dependent reorganization of non-covalent association. In simplified docking models, the two representative CP fragments yielded scores of −4.3 and −3.7 kcal/mol, whereas the KGM oligomer yielded −2.9 kcal/mol under the respective docking setups. This descriptive pattern suggests a possible peptide-biased interaction tendency. Accordingly, peptide-biased association is proposed as a working model for interpreting how GA may couple peptide-rich domains with the KGM-rich environment. These findings identify CP as a reactive plant-peptide component and establish a property-dependent formulation map: 0.3% GA favors an integrated combination of water stability, cohesion, stress dissipation, and microstructural continuity, whereas higher GA levels favor in vitro antioxidant output. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Mineralogical characteristics of oxidized copper-porphyry ores at the Koktaszhal deposit; [Көктасжал кен орнының тотыққан мыс-порфирлі кендерінің минералогиялық ерекшеліктері]; [Минералогические особенности окисленных медно-порфировых руд месторождения Коктасжал]
abstract: This paper presents the results of a comprehensive mineralogical study of oxidized copper-porphyry ore from the Koktashal deposit. Optical microscopy, silicate analysis, and quantitative phase analysis were used to characterize the mineral composition and forms of copper occurrence in the oxidation zone. The ore contains 0.735% total copper, of which 89.8% occurs in oxidized form, 6.39% in primary sulfides, 2.72% in secondary sulfides, and 1.09% in water-soluble form. The principal ore minerals are malachite (1.5–2.0%) and azurite (0.3–0.4%), accompanied by hematite with magnetite (0.5%), goethite (0.2%), and pyrite (0.2%), whereas copper sulfides and native copper occur only in trace amounts. The integration of classical mineralogical methods with quantitative phase analysis provides new insights into the distribution of copper occurrence forms and their relationship to oxidation processes. Malachite and azurite occur as well-crystallized vein and nest aggregates as well as colloform earthy masses developed along microcracks in association with iron hydroxides. Their close association with iron hydroxides and the near absence of copper sulfides represent a diagnostic feature of the oxidation zone in copper-porphyry systems. These findings improve the assessment of supergene alteration during exploration and support the classification of oxidation-zone ores as a distinct geological and industrial type for reserve estimation, ore body delineation, and processing scheme selection. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Soybean protein-stabilized O/W emulsion coagulant for controlled Mg2+ release: A novel green strategy for high-quality tofu production
abstract: Conventional brine coagulant, mainly Magnesium chloride (MgCl2), tends to cause rapid solidification and result in uneven gel structure in tofu. The development and application of controlled release coagulants provide an effective solution to this problem. In this study, soybean protein was used as the natural emulsifier to construct oil-in-water (O/W) emulsion coagulants to achieve effective loading and controlled release of Mg2+. The preparation process, physical properties, Mg2+release of the emulsions, and the effect of temperatures on the quality of the tofu were investigated. The emulsion prepared under optimized conditions achieved a loading rate of MgCl2 to 57.39%, with an average particle size of 47.73 μm, exhibiting excellent physical stability, rheological property and long-term storage stability. Simulated release tests showed that the initial and equilibrium conductivity of Mg2+ in the emulsion coagulants was lower than that of the brine control, indicating that the emulsion had a good controlled release performance for Mg2+. This is mainly attributed to the high viscosity and the tight droplet network structure of the emulsion. Compared with traditional brine tofu, the moisture content of the emulsion coagulated tofu decreased lightly, but the water holding capacity increased significantly. Scanning electron microscopy analysis confirmed that a uniform and dense protein network was formed inside the emulsion coagulated tofu, and there were numerous microporous structures, which could effectively capture and bind more water molecules. The color and texture analysis of the tofu revealed that the introduction of oil phase markedly enhanced the brightness of tofu. The color parameters of the tofu prepared at high temperature were very similar to those of traditional brine tofu. The texture analysis showed that the hardness of the tofu was significantly reduced, while its springiness and cohesiveness were greatly improved, resulting in a softer texture and enhanced resistance to deformation. The emulsion coagulants developed in this study based on the natural components of soybean seed without any chemical emulsifier, providing a novel approach to produce green or organic tofu. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Nonlinear mechanical characteristics of high-voltage circuit breaker based on rigid-body dynamic model with clearance joint
abstract: The manufacturing and assembly technology of the operating mechanism of the high-voltage circuit breaker leads to clearance joints between components, which significantly affect the mechanical characteristics of the operating mechanism. Based on Lagrangian theory, the mathematical rigid-body dynamic model of the operating mechanism is constructed by integrating the optimized Lankarani-Nikravesh normal contact force model and the optimized tangential friction force model. Essential nonlinear factors, such as cam-roller contact, spring force, buffer force, and mass parameter of components, are considered. The established model possesses the advantages of modularity and parameterization. The nonlinear dynamic behaviors of the operating mechanism are examined under diverse conditions, including the position, size, friction coefficient, and quantity of the clearance joints. The clearance joint results in an increase in instantaneous impact and fluctuations of acceleration. The clearance position with the most pronounced effect causes the peak acceleration to exceed twice that under the ideal operating condition. The simulation results offer essential data foundation for the structural optimization and durability analysis of the operating mechanism. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Integrity-Constrained Laboratory Screening of EOR Methods for Heavy-Oil Carbonate Reservoirs; [Ауыр мұнайлы карбонатты коллекторлар үшін пайдалану сенімділігі шектеулерін ескеретін EOR әдістерінің зертханалық скринингі]; [Лабораторный скрининг методов увеличения нефтеотдачи с учетом ограничений эксплуатационной надежности для тяжелонефтяных карбонатных коллекторов]
abstract: Enhanced oil recovery (EOR) screening is commonly initiated from reservoir and fluid properties, displacement mechanisms, and expected recovery potential. In technically complex offshore systems, however, a candidate method may be unsuitable for further development if the associated fluids and operating conditions intensify corrosion, inorganic scaling, organic deposition, emulsion persistence, phase instability, or near-wellbore damage. This study develops an integrity-constrained pre-pilot laboratory screening workflow for the integrated Field X-Field Y system. The workflow integrates brine chemistry and water-compatibility calculations, corrosion and inhibitor tests, wax-appearance-temperature (WAT) and viscosity data, emulsion stability, PVT recombination, and filtration compatibility. Untreated corrosion rates reached 11.586 mm/year at the electrical submersible pump outlet and 2.942 mm/year at the wellhead. Field X-Field Y formation-water mixing was compatible at 60 °C, whereas cooling to 30–50 °C increased predicted BaSO4-dominated precipitation, with 18.849 mg/L at 30 °C for the 75/25 mixture; the broader marine-water case reached 58.79 mg/L under the evaluated low-temperature/low-pressure condition. Field Y DST-1 was the most restrictive oil in the organic-deposition screen, with 10.6 wt.% paraffin and WAT evidence spanning 17.4–22.4 °C. Artificial emulsions retained up to 70% water for Field X DST-3 and 80% for Field Y DST-1. For the selected associated-gas analogue, a gas-oil ratio not above 90 m³/t at 18 MPa and 60.5 °C was used as the single-phase recombination boundary. The six-domain matrix was reformulated as an equal-weight ordinal qualification-burden index rather than a recovery-ranking tool; WAG had the highest burden (S=15; R=2.50), and this position remained unchanged under ±25% one-at-a-time criterion-weight perturbations. The framework therefore identifies operational-integrity constraints and the laboratory qualification required before direct displacement corefloods, compositional simulation, and pilot validation; it does not quantify incremental oil recovery. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: An embedded fault detection method for wind farm collector lines using adaptive statistical thresholding
abstract: In recent years, energy transition has boosted the expansion of new electrical generation sources, most of which are inverter-based, significantly altering the behavior of voltage and current signals. Thus, fault diagnosis methods should be validated and adapted to operate in this new scenario. This paper evaluates the performance of five classic fault detection methods and, addressing their identified limitations, proposes a fault detection algorithm based on ATs combined with a rule-based internal and external fault discriminator for medium-voltage collector networks in onshore wind farms. The method is robust, eliminating the need for prior parameterization in the primary detection stage. The proposed methodology was validated on an actual system located in Northeast Brazil, modeled in PSCAD/EMTDC and through hardware-in-the-loop tests using the RTDS interfaced with a Texas Instruments F28379D development board. The performance was tested under diverse operating conditions, including variations in fault resistance, different circuit topologies, and event types, while also considering wind turbine shutdowns and fluctuations in wind penetration levels. The results are highly promising and compatible with modern protection requirements, demonstrating an average primary pickup of under 1.36 ms, confirmed within 18 ms, and an accuracy rate exceeding 99.8%, even in the presence of noisy signal conditions. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Industrial robot fault detection and diagnosis for intelligent maintenance: A review of data, methods, and emerging trends
abstract: Industrial robots are widely used in intelligent manufacturing due to their high efficiency, flexibility, and repeatability. However, long-term operation under complex working conditions inevitably leads to performance degradation and various faults across mechanical, transmission, and electrical subsystems. Owing to the structural complexity of industrial robots, strong coupling among subsystems, and heterogeneous monitoring data, fault detection and diagnosis has become a challenging yet crucial task for ensuring system reliability and enabling intelligent maintenance. Despite considerable progress, existing studies remain fragmented across different robot subsystems, data modalities, and diagnostic paradigms, and a systematic review dedicated to industrial robot fault detection and diagnosis is still lacking. To address this gap, this paper presents a comprehensive and structured review from three complementary perspectives: fault characteristics and data resources, diagnostic methodologies, and emerging trends. Specifically, the review summarizes typical fault types and data acquisition strategies, organizes existing diagnostic methods into a structured taxonomy, and discusses key challenges and emerging directions such as multimodal fusion, trustworthy deployment, and digital-twin-driven diagnosis. This review provides a structured reference for advancing both theoretical research and engineering applications of industrial robot fault detection and diagnosis in intelligent manufacturing systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Substituent effects of thiourea derivatives on steel corrosion inhibition in 1.0 M HCl: An experimental and theoretical study
abstract: Carbon steel corrosion in acidic pickling media remains a critical industrial challenge. Herein, thiourea (TU) and three substituted thiourea derivatives, including phenylthiourea (PTU), allylthiourea (ATU), and methylthiourea (MTU), were investigated to clarify substituent-regulated corrosion inhibition and adsorption behavior in 1.0 M HCl. Weight loss, electrochemical tests, SEM, AFM, XPS, and TOF-SIMS analyses were integrated with quantum chemical calculations, first-principles calculations, and molecular dynamics simulations to establish the relationship among inhibition efficiency, interfacial film structure, and molecular adsorption mechanism. The results show that all four thiourea derivatives effectively suppress the corrosion of carbon steel in 1.0 M HCl and behave as mixed-type inhibitors. At 20 °C and 100 mg L−1, the inhibition efficiencies of TU, PTU, ATU, and MTU reach 88.1%, 87.8%, 89.1%, and 89.8%, respectively. Surface analyses reveal that MTU forms a more continuous, homogeneous, and compact adsorption film on the steel surface. First-principles calculations demonstrate pronounced coupling between molecular orbitals and Fe surface states after adsorption, with evident hybridization of S 3p and N 2p orbitals with Fe 3d orbitals. In particular, Fe-S interactions dominate interfacial bonding and charge transfer. These results show that inhibition performance depends not only on single-molecule adsorption strength, but also on orbital coupling, film coverage, interfacial homogeneity, and thermal stability, providing molecular-level guidance for designing efficient thiourea-based inhibitors for acidic media. © 2026

title: Physicochemical and commercial properties of a microelement-containing nitrogen fertilizer based on ammonium nitrate and spent lithium-ion batteries; [Аммоний нитраты мен пайдаланылған литий-ионды батареялар негізіндегі микроэлементтермен байытылған азотты тыңайтқыштың физика-химиялық және тауарлық қасиеттері]; [Физико-химические и товарные свойства микроэлементсодержащего азотного удобрения на основе нитрата аммония и отработанных литий-ионных батарей]
abstract: The results of a comprehensive study of the physicochemical and commercial properties (hygroscopic point, sorption kinetics, sorption moisture capacity) of trace-containing nitrogen fertilizers based on ammonium nitrate (AN) melt and cathode powder from used lithium-ion batteries are presented. The use of cathode powder as a polymicroelement additive (PMА) is shown, and they were introduced into the saltpeter melt at various mass ratios of NА: PMА from 100 (0.5-3.0). The prepared samples of fertilizers with a granule size of 2-3 mm were tested to determine the hygroscopic point, sorption kinetics, and sorption moisture capacity at relative air humidity of 60, 70, 85, and 100%. The samples of fertilizers were studied at a relative humidity of 60%, and it was proved that at such a relative humidity, the samples do not get moistened, but rather dry out. The results of the study of samples with a 4-hour exposure are given and it is found that fertilizer granules have a low hygroscopic point from 50 to 60% and a high moisture absorption rate in the order of 1.860; 5.920 and 6.710; 2.052; 6.790 and 9.451, as well as 3.481; 6.954 and 9.906 mg/(g min) at relative air humidity of 70, 85 and 100%, respectively. Due to the fact that the process of sorption of the investigated granules of products lasts up to 30 days (or 720 hours), they have a hygroscopic point of 60 to 70%, related to hygroscopic substances. Appropriate conclusions are drawn due to the properties of the studied fertilizers: they have a low moisture capacity, and their physical properties begin to deteriorate sharply only at a moisture content of about 2%. The resulting fertilizers are not inferior to known fertilizers in their characteristics. Recommendations are given for packaging the finished product in plastic bags for storage and transportation over long distances. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Influence of structure and non-Newtonian rheology on the lubrication of emulsion gels in soft contacts
abstract: The microstructural complexity and rheology of emulsion gels significantly influences their lubrication behaviour in soft contact tribology, resulting in experimental observations that are difficult to interpret. To investigate this, model emulsion gels (acidified milk gels) were prepared with systematic variations in protein to fat ratio, total solid content, and fat particle size. The lubrication of these multiphasic gels with semi-solid rheology deviates notably from the typical Stribeck “master curve” by showing the existence of a secondary transition in mixed lubrication (ML) regime. This behaviour generally occurs for shear-thinning lubricants, and we show how this secondary transition in ML relates to the presence of a yield stress, which relates to the strength and integrity of gels’ microstructure and the fat content. This distinct tribological behaviour of emulsion gels diminishes as the system enters the elasto-hydrodynamic lubrication (EHL) regime due to the enlarged interfacial separation so that the response depends on high-shear viscosity. For systems where there is a significant amount of free fat (i.e. the fat is not strongly associated with the protein network), local phase separation can occur whereby the fat phase dominates tribological response at low entrainment speeds (narrow gaps). By systematically decoupling the effects of composition, rheology, and microstructural integrity within a common emulsion-gel platform, this study establishes a mechanistic framework for interpreting the lubrication behaviour of complex multiphasic food gels. The findings demonstrate how structural evolution during oral processing influences tribological response in complex foods. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: Research on the integration method of power transfer and data communication based on LCL resonant topology
abstract: To address the limitations of traditional Power Line Carrier (PLC) communication, which can only transmit weak signals and struggles to balance high-power supply in strong interference environments, this paper proposes a power and signal integration method based on an LCL resonant topology. Unlike conventional PLC that superimposes communication signals onto the power-frequency grid, this scheme utilizes the LCL resonant network to construct a physical channel characterized by "isolation at power frequency and conduction at high frequency." This enables efficient transmission of hundred-watt-level high-frequency power while simultaneously performing narrowband data communication. By establishing a fundamental equivalent model of the system, the dual mechanisms of impedance matching and bandpass filtering of the LCL topology near the resonant frequency are revealed. This demonstrates its feasibility in ensuring power transfer efficiency while naturally suppressing power-frequency and broadband noise through frequency selectivity. Simulation and experimental results show that the system can stably deliver hundred-watt-level power at a resonant frequency of 20 kHz. It exhibits excellent robustness in noisy environments, achieving a Bit Error Rate (BER) of 0.0649 even with a Gaussian white noise Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) as low as 5 dB. This research achieves the integrated "power supply and communication" functionality over power lines, offering a highly reliable and high-power-density transmission solution for local energy internet applications in complex electromagnetic environments. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Nanoscale surface of a blade induced by novel immersed polishing assisted by ultrasonic and photocatalysis and elastic abrasive polishing
abstract: Titanium (Ti) alloy has extremely low thermal conductivity, low elastic modulus, and high chemical activity, making it prone to deformation, scratches, and abrasive embedding on Ti alloy during traditional polishing. Therefore, surface roughness (Sa) of Ti alloy is usually > 0.2 μm after polishing. To solve this challenge, novel combined polishing is proposed by immersed polishing assisted by ultrasonic and photocatalysis and elastic abrasive air jet polishing (EAAJP). The immersed polishing was performed using a developed setup, under irradiation of ultraviolet ultrasonically in a new environmentally-friendly slurry. The slurry consisted of ceria, nicotinic acid, and deionized water. After immersed polishing, hardness, Sa, and tensile strength on specimens of Ti alloy decreased from 392.23 HV, 532.18 nm, and 1080.01 MPa to 280.44 HV, 402.27 nm, and 1022.41 MPa, respectively, reducing 29%, 24%, and 5%, correspondingly. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy show that hydroxyl radicals were generated during photocatalysis, oxidizing the surface of the Ti alloy and forming a titania layer. Nicotinic acid dissolved the titania layer and complexed Ti ions with carboxyl and pyridyl groups. This is in good agreement with the calculations of density functional theory that the electrostatic potential of nicotinic acid is distributed in the range from −39.4 to 54.76 kcal/mol, and the complex occurred on the oxygen and nitrogen atoms derived from carboxyl groups and pyridine rings, respectively. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that tangential force, normal force, transmitted depth of von Mises stress, and thickness of damaged layer on pristine Ti alloy are 207.34 nN, 143.92 nN, 41.33 Å, and 39.62 Å at a scratching depth of 15 Å, while those with titania layer are 166.76 nN, 85.41 nN, 18.14 Å, and 30.71 Å, respectively, decreasing 20%, 41%, 56%, and 22%, correspondingly. Core-shell structured elastic abrasives of ethylene-vinyl acetate copolymers@silicon carbide (EVA@SiC) were prepared using a custom-made stirrer with controlled temperatures. EAAJP was conducted on a self-made four-axis polisher. EVA@SiC abrasives have a lower Young's modulus, varying from 0.2 to 1.0 GPa, measured by atomic force microscopy. After EAAJP, Sa, tensile strength, and hardness reached 12.57 nm, 1231.56 MPa, and 426.33 HV, respectively, improving 98%, 14%, and 9%, correspondingly, compared with those prior to polishing. Transmission electron spectroscopy confirms that the thickness of the damaged layer decreased from 723.91 nm prior to polishing to 9.59 nm after EAAJP, reducing 99%. Sa on a blade with a complex surface decreased from 569.87 nm before polishing to 13.96 nm after EAAJP, improving by 98%. Our outcomes provide new insights to get nanoscale surface on a blade of Ti alloy with a complex surface using both immersed polishing ultrasonically under irradiation of ultraviolet and EAAJP. © 2026

title: Simulation-based multi-objective optimization of reliability-centered maintenance in power distribution networks considering mode-dependent failure behavior
abstract: An efficient power distribution system must provide reliable power delivery and maintain voltage levels with minimal fluctuations. To achieve these objectives, regulatory organizations implement preventive maintenance programs to enhance system reliability and extend equipment lifespan. The reliability of a distribution system is one of the key indicators used to evaluate the service quality of electric distribution utilities. Considering the critical importance of reducing operational and capital expenditures, optimizing preventive maintenance programs is essential for minimizing costs while improving reliability. This study proposes a multi-objective model for optimizing the reliability of electrical power distribution systems. The primary objective is to minimize system maintenance costs while simultaneously maximizing the overall system reliability index. The NSGA-II algorithm is employed to solve the multi-objective optimization model, and the resulting Pareto front is presented. A key innovation of this study is the explicit modeling of mode-dependent failure behavior, where each maintenance action selectively restores only the targeted failure modes to their as-new condition. This approach allows for a more realistic representation of component degradation, improves the fidelity of reliability estimation, and enables more precise and cost-effective maintenance scheduling compared with traditional aggregated failure-rate models. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Radioactivity as a prospecting indicator of rare earth, gold and polymetal deposits in eastern Kazakhstan and an indicator of increased radioecological hazard during their development; [Шығыс Қазақстандағы сирек жер элементтері, алтын және полиметалл кен орындарын іздеудің белгісі ретінде радиоактивтілік және осы кен орындарын игеру кезінде радиациялық-экологиялық қауіптің жоғары деңгейінің индикаторы]; [Радиоактивность как поисковый признак месторождений редких земель, золота и полиметаллов Восточного Казахстана и индикатор повышенного уровня радиоэкологической опасности при разработке этих месторождений]
abstract: This study evaluates the role of natural radioactivity as an exploration indicator for rare-metal, gold, and polymetallic mineralization in Eastern Kazakhstan, as well as its significance as a factor of radioecological hazard. The analysis is based on the results of regional radiohydrolithochemical surveys conducted at a scale of 1:1,000,000, including bottom sediment sampling within microbasins. The study focuses on key natural radionuclides (U-238, Ra-226, Th-232, Ra-228, K-40) and their spatial distribution. Factor analysis was applied to identify anomalous geochemical associations and to assess their relationship with metallogenic structures. As a result, 80 potentially radioecologically hazardous zones were identified across Kazakhstan, including 5 zones within Eastern Kazakhstan. Within the study area, 12 anomalous sites were distinguished, characterized by 3–5 factors with cumulative explained variance ranging from 62.8% to 83.6%. The identified anomalies show spatial correspondence with major metallogenic zones, particularly the Rudny Altai and Kalba-Narym regions, which are associated with polymetallic and rare-metal mineralization. The results demonstrate that natural radioactivity can serve both as an effective exploration indicator and as an important factor of environmental risk. The study highlights the potential of integrating radioactivity parameters into exploration criteria and emphasizes the need to consider radiation safety in geological exploration and mining activities. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Termination-dependent interfacial interactions of ionic-liquid-modified Ti3C2Tx for boundary lubrication
abstract: The effectiveness of two-dimensional additives in boundary lubrication is often limited by poor dispersion stability and unstable low-shear interfaces in polar lubricants. Here, we report an ionic liquid (IL)-enabled interfacial-engineering strategy that couples surface anchoring with shear regulation at Ti3C2Tx MXene interfaces. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggest that the imidazolium cation acts as the primary anchoring motif, showing strong, termination-sensitive binding to Ti3C2Tx surface terminations, while the alkyl chain extends toward the counterface and may provide a molecular basis for an organic shear-accommodating overlayer. First-principles calculations further indicate a termination-dependent interfacial interaction trend, in which the calculated stability of the composite layer on steel is more closely associated with Ti3C2Tx-Fe electronic coupling than with cation-Ti3C2Tx anchoring. This trend provides a possible mechanistic basis for reconciling interfacial persistence with low shear resistance. Accordingly, IL-modified Ti3C2Tx reduces wear by up to 61% at an ultralow concentration of 0.05wt.%. Tribochemical and cross-sectional TEM analyses support the formation of an 8.5 nm continuous composite tribofilm enriched with IL- and Ti3C2Tx-derived species, consistent with reduced direct steel exposure during sliding. These findings offer design concepts for two-dimensional additives in polar lubricants. © 2026

title: A temperature-coupled Cahn-Hilliard-Stokes-heat model for thermally driven phase separation
abstract: We study a diffuse-interface model for thermally driven phase separation in viscous incompressible mixtures. The system couples a convective Cahn-Hilliard equation for the order parameter with a Stokes subsystem for the velocity-pressure field and a heat equation for the temperature. Temperature enters the bulk free energy through a Landau-type coefficient, while the phase field feeds back on the flow through concentration-dependent density and viscosity, yielding a phenomenological temperature-coupled Cahn–Hilliard–Stokes–heat system. The model serves as a proxy for temperature-triggered condensation-like phase separation and does not include humidity, latent heat, vapor pressure, or capillary forcing; these effects are absorbed into the choice of the threshold temperature Θ S . We motivate the chemical potential by a temperature-dependent Landau free energy and derive a priori estimates for the regularized subproblems. On the analytical side, we prove local-in-time existence of weak solutions for a regularized auxiliary model of the coupled system. This regularized formulation serves as an auxiliary analytical model for establishing local existence. On the numerical side, we use a first-order sequential finite-element discretization of a simplified quasi-static formulation. The heat equation is advanced by an implicit diffusion step, the variable-coefficient Stokes problem by a Taylor–Hood discretization, and the Cahn–Hilliard bulk derivative is evaluated at the previous time level, so every algebraic subproblem is linear. An isothermal diffusive test confirms mass conservation to roundoff and exhibits monotone discrete-energy decay for the tested parameter set. Time-step and mesh-refinement studies show first-order temporal and approximately second-order spatial behavior. The remaining computations are qualitative, parameter-specific illustrations, and no global discrete energy law is claimed for the non-isothermal sequential scheme. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Open-circuit fault diagnosis method for grid-connected inverters based on endogenous disturbance
abstract: To address the issues of indistinct residual signal features and detection speeds that are susceptible to load fluctuations in the open-circuit fault diagnosis of grid-connected inverter power switches, this paper proposes an open-circuit fault diagnosis method based on endogenous disturbance observation. First, an improved observer is constructed by introducing the Super-Twisting Algorithm (STA) combined with a hyperbolic tangent function. Through the design of a smooth control law, traditional sliding mode chattering is eliminated, and state tracking accuracy is enhanced. Second, an endogenous disturbance feature extraction method centered on endogenous control gains is proposed. By capturing the compensation amount generated within the observer to bridge the "energy gap" caused by the fault, the fault features are sensitively reinforced. This effectively resolves the problem of indistinct mutations in traditional current residuals. Finally, by utilizing the spatial distribution characteristics of fault vectors in the complex plane, a highly robust fault localization criterion is established using vector dot product operations and adaptive threshold logic. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively suppresses interference caused by grid power fluctuations. It achieves accurate identification of switch open-circuit faults under various operating conditions, offering the advantages of rapid diagnosis speed, low computational overhead, and no requirement for additional sensors. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
