title: Fabrication of a large-area, uniformly fine-grained high-entropy alloy with excellent mechanical properties and corrosion resistance by collaborative friction stir welding and processing
abstract: Fabricating large-area, uniformly fine-grained high-entropy alloy (HEA) remains challenging because welding can introduce microstructural heterogeneity and degrade material performance. Here, a new approach, termed collaborative friction stir welding and processing (C-FSW/P), was developed by integrating FSW and FSP, which share the same basic principle. The approach eliminated weld-induced microstructural heterogeneity during the fabrication of large-area fine-grained sheets and transformed cast-alloy slices into a large-area CoCrFeNiMn sheet with a uniform equiaxed fine-grained microstructure (∼2 μm). The resulting fine-grained HEA exhibited an excellent strength-ductility synergy, achieving tensile strengths of 724 and 1150 MPa at 293 and 77 K, with elongations of 34% and 45%, respectively. The critical twinning stress in the fine-grained processing zone (PZ) was determined experimentally and theoretically to be 957 ± 27 MPa. Deformation twins were first observed at true strains of ∼8.4% at 77 K and ∼27% at 293 K. At 293 K, the work-hardening rate (WHR) decreased continuously with increasing strain because deformation twinning was activated only at a late stage. By contrast, the higher WHR at 77 K resulted from the earlier activation of deformation twins, which acted together with stacking faults and secondary twins to provide additional work hardening. Relative to the values at 293 K, the tensile strength and elongation of the PZ at 77 K increased by 37% and 24%, respectively, owing to twin-boundary strengthening. The PZ also exhibited superior corrosion resistance in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution, as evidenced by its higher corrosion potential (−0.225 V) and lower corrosion current density (0.084 μA/cm2) relative to the base material. This improvement arose from the formation of a stable, dense Cr2O3-rich passive film. This study establishes an efficient short-process route for fabricating large-area, structurally uniform ultrafine- and fine-grained materials without size constraints. © 2026

title: Single-ended fault location method for multi-terminal overhead-cable hybrid transmission line using alternating search algorithm
abstract: With rapid urbanization and power grid expansion, multi-terminal overhead-cable hybrid transmission lines have been increasingly utilized. However, the significant differences between overhead lines and cables, combined with the complexity of multi-terminal structures, lead to complicated refraction and reflection of travelling waves (TWs). Therefore, conventional single-ended TW-based fault location methods, which rely on accurate identification of reflected waves and a high sampling frequency in the MHz range, are not suitable. To address this issue, the paper proposes an enhanced TW-based fault location method based on waveform similarity. First, this method incorporates a frequency-dependent multi-terminal hybrid transmission line analytical model to reproduce fault transient voltage waveforms. On this basis, dynamic time warping and normalized mean square error collaborative similarity metrics are established to evaluate calculated and actual fault transient waveform characteristics, and the sensitivity analysis of the similarity metrics shows that there is a coupling relationship among the fault variables. Then, a variable-step, dual-metric alternating search algorithm is proposed to accurately identify fault variables (e.g., fault inception angle, fault resistance, and fault distance). Finally, simulation results using PSCAD/EMTDC demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately locate the fault at a sampling frequency of 200 kHz, is less affected by fault resistance, and does not require data synchronization. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Surrogate-Assisted Deep Reinforcement Learning for Bi-Level Multi-Objective Capacity Sizing of Railway Collaborative Power Supply System
abstract: The Grid-Source-Storage-Vehicle collaborative power supply system (GSSV-CPSS) enables railway power supply to evolve from a grid-only supply to coordinated multi-source supply with flexible regulation, thereby improving renewable energy (RE) utilization and source-load matching under high renewable penetration. However, short-term source-load fluctuations, long-horizon temporal variability, and strong planning-operation coupling make capacity sizing computationally expensive, because candidate schemes must be repeatedly evaluated through fine-resolution, long-horizon chronological dispatch. To address this issue, a planning-operation coordinated capacity sizing framework is developed. The planning-layer targets annual economic performance and RE utilization, and formulates capacity sizing of photovoltaic (PV), energy storage systems (ESS), and power converters as a single-step continuous decision problem. The operation-layer evaluates candidate schemes through year-long chronological rolling-horizon optimization and feeds the annual return back to the planning-layer. Building on this framework, Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) is adopted as the policy-optimization backbone to realize unified policy optimization across different objective-weight preferences. Furthermore, a surrogate-assisted (SA) mechanism is introduced, in which a learned reward surrogate predicts the expected return and uncertainty of candidate capacity schemes. The predictive mean and uncertainty are then used for candidate-scheme scoring and screening, so as to reduce unpromising real operation-layer evaluations. The resulting method is termed SA-SAC-Select. Case studies show that the proposed method makes more effective use of costly annual operation-layer evaluations and supports efficient capacity sizing across different objective-weight preferences. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Vulnerable node identification in active distribution networks under multi-scenario quasi-static time-series operation: A CVaR-based conditional-consequence screening framework
abstract: Expected-loss and composite-score rankings can underrepresent active distribution network (ADN) nodes whose severe consequences concentrate in stressed operating states. This paper develops a CVaR-based conditional-consequence screening framework for standardized node removals over weighted year-round quasi-static time-series (QSTS) operation. Each candidate is represented by a post-removal consequence distribution that combines energy not supplied, incremental voltage-violation severity, and relative branch-loading stress. CVaR, tail amplification, and resampling-based selection probability distinguish mean-driven from tail-dominated consequence profiles. In the modified IEEE 33-node feeder, nodes 29 and 28 rise from expected-loss ranks 8 and 9 to CVaR ranks 1 and 2 under the main grid-forming (GFM)-enabled scenario; the ordered Top-2 is preserved in the independent 2024 test with 90% Top-10 overlap. The 85-node feeder gives an 8/10 expected-loss/CVaR Top-10 overlap and promotes two strongly tail-amplified nodes into the CVaR Top-10. A current-domain diagnostic using a literature-based 255-A surrogate and ± 20% sensitivity further separates baseline-relative branch-loading stress from absolute current utilization: observed exceedances occur on solved main-grid branches, whereas the terminal GFM-supported-island pattern is associated with departures from branch-specific daily baselines. The resulting ranking is conditional on the standardized contingency, with event likelihood retained as a separate layer for downstream risk-aware applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Biogenic Amine Determination by High-Performance Liquid Chromatography Using a Sol-Gel-Immobilized 2-Hydroxy-5-nitrobenzaldehyde-2,4-dinitro phenyl hydrazone Solid-Phase Extractant; [Определение биогенных аминов методом высокоэффективной жидкостной хроматографии с использованием твердофазного экстрагента на основе золь-геля, иммобилизованного на 2-гидрокси-5-нитробензальдегиде и 2,4-динитрофенилгидразоне]
abstract: This study focuses on the solid phase extraction of biogenic amines (BAs) using a sol-gel adsorbent immobilized with a hydrazone ligand, named 2-hydroxy-5-nitrobenzaldehyde-2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone. The hydrazone compound was synthesized and characterized through Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FT-IR) and Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy. The efficiency of the sorbent material for extracting BAs was evaluated using the solid phase extraction (SPE) method. Key experimental parameters affecting BA extraction, including pH, equilibrium time, ligand concentration, and biogenic amine (BA) concentration, were systematically investigated. The results indicated a strong recovery of BAs from aqueous samples, demonstrating a significant affinity between the sol-gel matrix containing the hydrazone ligand and the target analytes. The findings demonstrate that incorporating the hydrazone ligand resulted in a marked enhancement of extraction efficiency at a concentation of 17 × 10-3 M. Notably, the method exhibited high selectivity for aliphatic biogenic amines such as putrescine (PUT), cadaverine (CAD), and spermidine (SPD). This extraction method was successfully applied to food samples, yielding good recovery rates. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Structural-function relationship of β-cyclodextrin derivatives in regulating encapsulation and humidity-triggered release of essential oils
abstract: Understanding how cyclodextrin cavity microenvironment and key physicochemical properties of guest molecules govern the encapsulation and release behaviors of essential oils is critical for designing efficient delivery systems, yet the relevant mechanisms remain unclear. In this work, we systematically investigated this structure-function relationship using three β-cyclodextrin variants (native, methyl-β-cyclodextrin and hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin) and four representative essential oil molecules (cinnamaldehyde, carvacrol, eugenol and terpinyl acetate). We find that the relative contributions of guest hydrophobicity and molecular size to encapsulation efficiency are not intrinsic, but are dictated by the substituents on the cyclodextrin rim. Multiscale characterizations including XRD, FTIR and 1H NMR verified stable 1:1 inclusion complexes across all systems. Release kinetics exhibited a pronounced humidity-triggered pattern, governed by a balance between cyclodextrin hydrophilicity and crystallinity that linked water-mediated cavity hydration and diffusional resistance. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that hydrophobic interactions dominate host–guest binding, while substitution enhances cavity flexibility and alters guest embedding depth, thereby modulating the encapsulation and release of essential oils. This work establishes a structure, microenvironment and release framework for cyclodextrin-based delivery systems, providing mechanistic insights for rational design of controlled release carriers in food preservation applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Effects of calcium hydroxide on the physicochemical and digestive properties of Tartary buckwheat starch: the role of calcium ions and hydroxide ions
abstract: This study investigated the effects of Ca(OH)2, CaCl2, NaOH, and NaOH + CaCl2 at different addition levels (0%-1.0%) on the structure, physicochemical properties, and in vitro digestibility of Tartary buckwheat starch (TBS) to elucidate the mechanism by which Ca(OH)2 modifies TBS properties. Bound calcium content was higher in the Ca(OH)2 and NaOH + CaCl2 groups than in the CaCl2 group, suggesting that OH− may promote the association between Ca2+ and TBS. The solubility and swelling power of Ca(OH)2 group moderately increased. Rheological results and SEM images revealed that Ca(OH)2 induced TBS to form a gel network with higher elasticity, as well as more uniform and compact microstructures. An appropriate concentration of Ca(OH)2 decreased the relative crystallinity (0.2%-0.6%) and degree of order (0.2%-0.8%), reduced gelatinization enthalpy, increased gelatinization temperatures (To, Tp, Tc) and double helix content, delaying in vitro digestion of TBS. The differences in properties and structures among the four treatment groups suggest that the modification of TBS by Ca(OH)2 may be attributed to the combined action of Ca2+ and OH−. These findings provide insights into the distinct contributions of Ca2+ and OH− in modifying properties and structure of TBS. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Phenolic acid-grafted high-amylose maize starch as a multifunctional emulsifier in agarose-based emulsion gels for thymol loading and release: Application in active coatings for strawberry preservation
abstract: Three benzoic-type phenolic acids with progressively increasing hydroxyl substitution (p-hydroxybenzoic acid, 3,4-dihydroxybenzoic acid, and gallic acid) were covalently grafted onto native high-amylose maize starch (Na-HAMS) via EDC·HCl/DMAP-mediated esterification, yielding Ph-HAMS, Da-HAMS, and Ga-HAMS at a grafting ratio of approximately 12%. Successful esterification at the C-6 primary hydroxyl groups was confirmed by FTIR, UV-Vis, XPS, and NMR analyses. Phenolic acid grafting significantly enhanced surface hydrophobicity and conferred marked antioxidant and antimicrobial activities, both following a consistent structure-dependent ranking of Ga-HAMS > Da-HAMS > Ph-HAMS, reflecting differences in phenolic hydroxyl number and ortho-cooperative configuration. Thymol-loaded emulsion gels were subsequently constructed using each modified starch as an emulsifier combined with an agarose network. Compared with Na-HAMS, modified starch-based emulsion gels exhibited substantially improved emulsifying activity, reduced droplet size, and enhanced thymol loading efficiency (∼30% to 92%), along with superior physical stability. Rheological analysis confirmed elasticity-dominated viscoelastic behavior (G′ > G″) stable across 20-90 °C, while LF-NMR and MRI revealed more homogeneous internal water distribution within the modified gel matrices. Based on a comprehensive performance evaluation, Ga-HAMS emulsion gel was applied as an active coating for strawberry preservation at 25 °C. Compared with control and Na-HAMS groups, Ga-HAMS coating effectively suppressed microbial growth, reduced decay and weight loss, and better maintained firmness, color, and soluble solids. LF-NMR and MRI further confirmed the preservation of cellular water compartmentalization. This work systematically elucidates the structure-activity relationships of benzoic-type phenolic acid-grafted HAMS and provides a theoretical basis for polysaccharide-based active emulsion gels in postharvest fruit preservation. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Starvation trap strategy: An amylase-responsive potato starch-based Pickering emulsion for inhibiting foodborne microorganisms and preserving starchy foods
abstract: Inspired by microbial carbon-source uptake, we developed polysaccharide-based intelligent responsive cinnamaldehyde (CIN) nanoemulsions (NEs) stabilized by the metal–phenolic network (MPN)-modified potato starch particles (PSEF). This system achieved amylase-responsive CIN release and inhibition of Bacillus cereus in starchy foods, while continuously releasing CIN to control other foodborne microorganisms. The results confirmed that the prepared 5% CIN NEs showed high encapsulation efficiency (98.66%), sustained release, and reliable biosafety (relative hemolysis rate <5%), effectively inhibiting Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, Listeria monocytogenes, Bacillus cereus, Burkholderia gladioli, and Aspergillus niger. Co-incubation with Bacillus cereus further supported the amylase-responsive release behavior of the system. Finally, the 5% CIN NE coating extended the shelf life of fresh-cut kiwifruit, lotus root, and rice noodles by 1.5–2.0-fold, showing better preservation performance than the commercial preservative ε-polylysine hydrochloride (ε-PLH). This safe and intelligent responsive coating may provide a sustainable solution for extending the shelf life of starchy foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Mitigation and adaptation strategies for mass removals in arid zones: A theoretical model based on urban architecture projects in Antofagasta; [Estrategias de mitigación y adaptación para remociones en masa en zonas áridas: Modelo teórico basado en proyectos de arquitectura urbana en Antofagasta]
abstract: The Atacama Desert, particularly in the Antofagasta region, faces increasing risks of mass movement exacerbated by climate change. This article proposes a theoretical model that integrates mitigation and adaptation strategies within urban architecture projects at the neighbourhood scale, focusing on sloped desert areas. The methodological process includes an initial deductive classification stage followed by an inductive qualitative analysis. Within 13 academic projects from the School of Architecture at the Universidad Católica del Norte in the city of Antofagasta, two typologies are identified: one oriented toward mitigation through flood-control basins and retaining walls, and another mixed type that incorporates terrain adaptation, green barriers, floodable areas, ramps, and underground channelling. The model helps fill a gap in the literature on risk management in arid contexts, aligning with SDG 11 and SDG 13. It also offers a practical guide for architects and urban planners, promoting more resilient, sustainable, and safe urban policies and projects. © of the edition: Estoa, 2027.

title: Exploring 2D Isotope Heterostructures for Atomic-Scale Control of Thermal Radiation
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) materials with their characteristic layered structures and weak van der Waals interlayer interactions provide a versatile platform for manipulating emergent phenomena and engineering novel functionalities in the thermal near field. Recently, it has been revealed that the energy-momentum dispersions and photonic density of states of 2D materials can be effectively modulated by isotope engineering. Here, we explore the impact of isotope composition on thermal radiation for 2D heterostructures based on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). By systematically varying the number of layers, we discover that few-layer hBN amplifies the isotope-induced spectral match and mismatch between the hyperbolic phonon polaritons. The largest isotope effect is observed in monolayer hBN, where the ratio of the heat transfer coefficient between isotopically identical and maximally distinct hBN pairs reaches approximately 300. Interestingly, for emitters and receivers of different layer counts, the heat flux between isotopically distinct hBN pairs can surpass that for identical pairs. Furthermore, we reveal that thermal transport is highly sensitive to the stacking order at sub-10 nm gap sizes, as demonstrated by bilayer isotope heterostructures. Finally, to facilitate experimental study, the substrate and temperature dependence of the isotope effect are investigated. Our findings highlight the unique potential of 2D materials for isotopically engineering near-field thermal radiation with single-atomic-layer precision. © 1995-2012 IEEE.

title: Discrete-time capability-aware multi-rate frequency control of fast and slow distributed energy resources in microgrids
abstract: This paper presents a discrete-time multi-rate frequency control scheme for a single-bus system comprising a synchronous generator (SG) and an inverter-based resource (IBR). The proposed method coordinates the fast IBR response with the slower SG dynamics using a discrete-time signal derived from the frequency evolution, which captures the required rate of active power variation for frequency regulation. The IBR reference is defined as a combination of frequency-deviation feedback and a rate-dependent term modulated by a smooth activation function, while the SG is governed by a ramp-limited integral control law updated at a slower sampling rate. The resulting control architecture is implemented in a multi-rate framework with distinct fast and slow update loops. A discrete-time model of the closed-loop system is derived and formulated as a singularly perturbed system, in which the IBR tracking dynamics form a contractive fast subsystem and the SG–frequency dynamics evolve on the slow time scale. Practical stability is established by combining a contraction property of the fast subsystem with an input-to-state stability characterization of the slow sampled dynamics. The analysis characterizes the influence of IBR tracking bandwidth, sampling-rate separation, and SG ramp-rate constraints on the closed-loop frequency response. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: An optimized single-machine equivalent model for doubly-fed wind farms based on controller aggregation
abstract: Due to the influence of the voltage distribution (VD) and power distribution (PD) within the WF, the traditional single-machine equivalent model (SMEM) and feature-based clustering methods may introduce large errors in characterizing the whole WF. The PD causes errors in active power during the quasi-steady-state and fault-recovery periods, and the VD causes errors in reactive power during faults, as shown in the authors’ earlier work. In this paper, based on detailed fault-stage division, the causes of control errors in each stage, and the mutual influence between PD and VD, the optimizations and principles for instruction aggregation are presented. An optimized single-machine aggregation model of the WF is developed through mathematical analysis and controllability considerations, and this model features mechanistic interpretability. The structure and parameter-acquisition principles of the single-machine aggregated equivalent model are presented. Based on the structured single wind turbine (WT) model and the aggregated control of the WF equivalent model presented herein, a structured WF equivalent model suitable for different WFs and different internal unit types of WFs is proposed. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the constructed model are confirmed across varying wind speeds, voltage dip depths, WFs and short-circuit ratios (SCRs). Simulation results show that, for the scenarios considered herein, the proposed model improves simulation efficiency by approximately 30 while maintaining the highest accuracy, with a maximum deviation of no more than 1.5 % across the relevant indicators. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Artificial-intelligence-driven wide-area fault location for transmission systems: A traveling wave-based approach
abstract: Accurate and timely fault location (FL) is essential for improving grid resilience, minimizing service interruptions, and accelerating system recovery in power transmission networks. Among the various approaches, traveling wave (TW)-based methods-particularly wide-area TW-based techniques-offer high speed and accuracy, making them attractive for modern grids. However, existing TW-based methods often rely on ideal assumptions such as uniform propagation velocities, perfect sensor coverage, and noise-free measurements. These limitations hinder their performance in realistic settings, where line parameters vary, sensors may fail, and data may be incomplete or distorted. This paper presents a novel approach that leverages TW arrival times and a multi-task artificial neural network (ANN) architecture to jointly identify the faulty line and the FL. By formulating sensor placement as an optimization problem and solving it via Integer Linear Programming (ILP), the method significantly reduces hardware requirements while preserving high accuracy. Extensive simulations on a modified IEEE 39-bus system—featuring realistic grid conditions including underground cables, overhead lines, hybrid lines, and substation impedance—show that, for the final enhanced configuration, the proposed method achieves a classification accuracy of 99.62% and a mean absolute fault-location error (MAE) of 166.16 m. © 2026

title: A post-fault island partitioning method for distribution networks considering overall frequency security and spatial nodal RoCoF constraints
abstract: For distribution networks with distributed generators, post-fault island partitioning can restore local power supply, whereas limited island inertia and frequency support may cause frequency security violations during load restoration. To address the limitations of conventional methods in simultaneously capturing the center-of-inertia frequency response and the spatial heterogeneity of nodal rate of change of frequency (RoCoF), this paper proposes a post-fault island partitioning method considering overall frequency security and spatial nodal RoCoF constraints. An island-level frequency response model is first established, in which the center-of-inertia RoCoF, frequency nadir, and quasi-steady-state frequency deviation are embedded into the stepwise load restoration process. A spatial nodal RoCoF model is then developed to identify local dynamic security risks that may be overlooked by center-of-inertia frequency indicators. Furthermore, nodal RoCoF checking is incorporated into the feasibility assessment of load restoration, and load blocks associated with RoCoF violations are adjusted to determine load block energization, partial load restoration, and final island partitioning results. Case studies on the IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 69-bus systems show that a restoration scheme satisfying center-of-inertia frequency constraints may still experience local nodal RoCoF violations. The proposed method can eliminate such local violations by adjusting selected load blocks, thereby improving the dynamic security of post-fault island partitioning schemes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Learning Deliverable Wind-Power Capability from Censored SCADA Records for Curtailment-Aware Energy Management
abstract: Accurate reconstruction of turbine-level available power is essential for active-power dispatch in curtailed wind farms because turbine commands must remain physically deliverable. However, SCADA active power during command-tracking curtailment is constrained by turbine-level set-points and is therefore not an exact observation of available power. This paper formulates reconstruction as a mixed-observation learning problem in which turbine-interval records provide point, lower-bound, interval, or unavailable capability information according to operating state. A wake-coupled spatio-temporal quantile model reconstructs the conditional distribution of latent available power, while local observational support regulates its admission into turbine-level dispatch. The framework is evaluated using 12 months of SCADA, command, status, and event data from three utility-scale wind farms in China. Under 80% controlled censoring, the proposed method achieves an absolute bias of 0.33% and a CRPS of 1.19% of capacity, compared with 0.79% and 1.63% for standard quantile learning. In real curtailed replay, the infeasible-command rate decreases from 7.8% to 4.2% and the non-deliverable ratio from 0.72% to 0.46%. This corresponds to approximately 260 MWh of avoided non-delivered energy per 100 GWh requested and a scenario-based value of CNY 52,000–130,000 (USD 7,700–19,200) under assumed energy values of CNY 200–500/MWh (USD 29.5–73.7/MWh), based on the official RMB central parity rate on 28 August 2026. Release-event, high-curtailment, ablation, and cross-farm experiments further confirm robustness and transferability. The results show that information-consistent treatment of censored SCADA improves capability reconstruction, dispatch reliability, renewable-energy utilization, and operational economic value. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Constitutive modeling of the BCC-FCC transformation-affected powder densification controlled by diffusion and creep of the Al0.7CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys during spark plasma sintering
abstract: The precise construction of the densification model of spark plasma sintering (SPS) is the theoretical basis for the preparation of high-performance materials and guidance of process parameters. Diffusion and creep are the two dominant mechanisms responsible for powder densification during SPS. High-entropy alloys (HEAs) prefer sintering temperatures in the ranges accompanying the beneficial phase transformation to obtain satisfying structural properties. However, it brings difficulty in the study of densification kinetics as none of the current models consider the phase transformation and, as a result, reduces the accuracy in describing both diffusion- and creep-dominant densification of HEAs in SPS. Thus, a new constitutive model considering the effect of phase transformation on densification is proposed in this study. The transformed phase volume fraction is determined according to the nucleation and growth model, and Taylor expansion is introduced in the calculation of the convolution integral in the model during the heating period. After the transformed fraction is obtained, the chemical compositions in the retained parent phase are computed based on the conservation of matter. Subsequently, the contribution of atomic diffusion to densification as a function of the transformed fraction under the electromigration effect is obtained. Furthermore, the grain size of the parent and daughter phases as a function of the transformed fraction is determined utilizing the grain growth model. The final model is obtained by substituting the functional relations between atomic diffusion, grain growth, and phase transformation into the densification model framework consisting of diffusion and creep. © 2026

title: Kinetic modulation via trace cationic surfactant additive enabling dense Zn deposition for ultra-stable aqueous batteries
abstract: Aqueous Zn metal batteries are promising for grid-scale energy storage but suffer from severe anode instability. While electrolyte additives are widely explored, achieving effective stabilization at an ultralow dosage remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report that a trace amount of a non-sacrificial additive, 2-methacryloyloxyethyltrimethylammonium chloride (METAC), fundamentally stabilizes the Zn interface. METAC preferentially adsorbs on Zn via its quaternary ammonium center, forming a persistent protective layer that displaces water and suppresses corrosion. Crucially, this adsorption is facet-selective, raising the Zn2+ migration barrier on the (100) and (101) facets while lowering it on the (002) facet, thereby redirecting the deposition orientation toward dendrite-free, horizontal growth. This dual mechanism enables the batteries with exceptional cyclability: The Zn//Zn cell exceeds 8000 cycles at a high current density of 20 mA cm−2, and the Zn//NaV3O8 full cell retains a remarkable capacity retention of 85.3% at 5 A g−1 after 3000 cycles. This work demonstrates that precise interfacial molecular engineering with trace, non-sacrificial additives is a viable path to practical aqueous batteries. © 2026

title: Dual built-in electric fields enabled by S-scheme/high-low dual-heterojunction engineering in CoSx@ZnIn2S4@O, K-co-doped g-C3N4 for efficient photocatalytic H2 evolution
abstract: Constructing dual built-in electric fields and multiple charge-transfer pathways is an effective approach to improving solar H2 production. Herein, a ternary CoSx@ZnIn2S4@O, K-co-doped g-C3N4 (OKCN) photocatalyst was prepared by pyrolysis/in situ precipitation. In this architecture, ultrathin ZnIn2S4 nanosheets were anchored on OKCN to form an S-scheme heterojunction, while in situ introduced CoSx coupled with ZnIn2S4 to construct a reduction-state high-low heterojunction. This dual-heterojunction structure generated dual built-in electric fields, promoting carrier separation, migration, and interfacial reactions. The optimized 3% CoSx@ZnIn2S4@OKCN with an OKCN/ZnIn2S4 mass ratio of 2:20 achieved a H2 evolution rate of 317.6 μmol h−1 under visible light, which was 1.75, 20.76 and 3.14 times those of CoSx@ZnIn2S4, CoSx@OKCN, and ZnIn2S4@OKCN, respectively, with an apparent quantum efficiency of 12.2% at 420 nm and good stability over five cycles. Photoelectrochemical measurements, photoluminescence (PL)/time‑resolved PL, density functional theory calculations, in situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, Kelvin‑probe force microscope and Mott-Schottky analyses confirmed that the dual built-in electric fields accelerated interfacial charge transfer and optimized H2 evolution. This work provides guidance for designing efficient multi-interface photocatalysts through S-scheme/high-low dual-heterojunction engineering. © 2026

title: Fully distributed security control for wind farms subject to hybrid cyberattacks
abstract: Modern wind farms (WFs) increasingly integrate information technologies with wind power generation, which introduces new cyber-physical vulnerabilities. As the penetration of wind power in power systems continues to increase, secure communication and stable operation of WFs become increasingly important. However, coordinated control of WFs under hybrid false data injection (FDI) and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks remains insufficiently addressed. To fill this gap, this paper develops a fully distributed security control strategy for cyber-physical WFs under hybrid cyberattacks. A six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) wind turbine (WT) model is integrated with a WF communication network model to characterize the effects of FDI and DoS attacks on active power tracking and fair load sharing. A distributed security control strategy based on an auxiliary layer is then designed to track grid-side active power demand while preserving fair load sharing. Lyapunov stability analysis establishes closed-loop convergence under nominal and admissible DoS conditions and characterizes the recovery error under FDI attacks, thereby clarifying how control gains and network structure affect resilience. Case studies on a grid-connected WF demonstrate that the proposed strategy maintains active power tracking and fair load sharing under FDI, DoS, and hybrid attack scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Transient phase-based faulty feeder identification for high-impedance faults via autocorrelation entropy difference
abstract: In resonant grounding distribution systems (RGDSs), high-impedance faults (HIFs) generate severely attenuated currents and complex arcing behaviors, making faulty feeder identification particularly challenging. Existing magnitude-based methods suffer from significant performance degradation, while conventional phase-extraction techniques are vulnerable to noise and intermittent arcing. To address these limitations, a robust feeder identification method utilizing a novel autocorrelation entropy difference (ACED) index is proposed. First, based on equivalent models for both fixed-resistance and arcing HIFs, the initial phase disparity of zero-sequence transient currents inherently persists, remaining structurally decoupled from the extreme attenuation caused by HIFs. To circumvent the unreliability of direct phase estimation under low signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), the ACED index is formulated to characterize the structural correlation discrepancies of transient signals, achieving robust feature extraction without relying on explicit phase calculation. Simulation and field-test results demonstrate that the proposed method maintains satisfactory performance under extreme fault resistances, nonlinear arcing, and diverse operating conditions. Specifically, under a SNR of 10 dB, the proposed method achieves an identification accuracy of 84.4%, outperforming existing methods, and reliably identifies HIFs with fault resistances up to 3000 Ω, demonstrating enhanced noise robustness and practical potential. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Near-optimal loop opening with a rotary power flow controller: Global-optimality conditions, certified domains, and practical-band fragmentation
abstract: Opening an RPFC-supported loop without a fresh voltage disturbance hinges on how the controller withdraws to zero injection. Field practice uses a two-step rule—suppress the injection magnitude, then reset the residual angle—yet no path-level theory explains when this rule is optimal or how it fails. This paper casts the exit stage as a continuous path problem on the control plane with voltage excursion as cost. An exact identity equates the two-step excess above the endpoint lower bound to the sum of two endpoint-envelope violations; when both vanish, the path is globally optimal. A counterexample rules out any unconditional theorem; implicit-function arguments then yield checkable pointwise and domain certificates. On the IEEE 69-bus feeder, a 625-point operating rectangle is certified with zero excess and a monitored, nonsingular load-flow Jacobian; certification persists out to ± 30% load, carries over to a meshed variant, a non-ideal excitation-branch model, and a 118-bus feeder, and survives 500 paired Monte Carlo draws on two topologies with heterogeneous load and photovoltaic uncertainty. On the reduced plane, 78.1% of feasible points are safely near-optimal at the 0.01 kV threshold, with the worst path-induced gap at 0.0063 kV. Execution stress contracts the practical band from 1.389 to 0.906 kV and fragments it into up to four islands; sensitivity sweeps expose a sharp bias-driven collapse between 0.75∘ and 1.25∘, whereas ± 20% load shifts barely matter. External reactive support of up to 1 Mvar widens the band edges yet heals none of the bypass-limited gaps, confirming where the remediation budget belongs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Remaining electrical life prediction of AC contactors based on PA-OT-PSM stage transfer
abstract: To address the complex degradation process of AC contactors, large cross-device lifetime data discrepancies, and limited generalization of traditional data-driven prediction models, this paper proposes a remaining electrical life prediction method based on physics-guided stage manifold-constrained transfer learning, namely Prototype Alignment–Optimal Transport–Physics-guided Stage Manifold (PA-OT-PSM). First, feature parameters are extracted from full-life tests, and degradation feature sequences are constructed using Euclidean distance. A change-point detection algorithm is then used to divide the degradation process into multiple stages. Based on this, a stage prototype alignment mechanism is introduced to align feature centers of corresponding degradation stages in the source and target domains, preserving stage structural consistency. Furthermore, an optimal transport mechanism is embedded within each stage to achieve sample-level relational transfer, while source-domain lifetime labels are used to generate soft supervision for target-domain samples. To ensure physical consistency, degradation monotonicity and remaining-life monotonicity constraints are incorporated into model training. In addition, a few labeled target-domain samples are used for lightweight fine-tuning of the prediction layer and key alignment parameters, enabling target-domain distribution calibration and lifetime mapping correction. Finally, the model is optimized through a joint loss function to obtain target-domain remaining useful life predictions. Experimental results show that, after few-shot target-domain fine-tuning, the proposed method achieves high prediction accuracy and strong cross-device generalization in both same-type and cross-type transfer scenarios, providing a useful reference for condition assessment and predictive maintenance of electrical equipment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Rapid globularization of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V alloy via ordered dislocation structures induced by pulsed current
abstract: Transforming lamellar grains/phases to globular can improve the ductility of metallic materials. However, this process always relies on time-consuming, complex heat treatments (HTs) to regulate dislocations. This work introduces a current-driven strategy that “guides” dislocation motion to bypass this complexity, enabling rapid globularization. A prior electropulsing treatment (EPT) rapidly reorganizes the initially high-density dislocations into ordered intra-lamellar structures and promotes their accumulation near pre-existing twin boundaries under transient electro-thermal conditions. These preconditioned dislocation structures facilitate boundary splitting during a subsequent short HT, eliminating the need for cyclic or multistep processing. The resulting EPT+HT process achieves rapid globularization and a favorable strength–ductility balance. This work not only delivers an efficient strategy for microstructure regulation in additive manufacturing but also provides fundamental insights into defect dynamics under electro-thermal coupling. © 2026

title: Engineering rare-earth and amorphous/crystalline interfaces for efficient H2O2 photosynthesis
abstract: Photocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) for hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production is an environmentally friendly and safe method. However, its widespread application is hindered by challenges such as a high recombination rate of photogenerated charge carriers. In this study, we propose a strategy that combines crystalline-amorphous interface engineering with rare earth atom doping to accelerate carrier dynamics, thereby significantly enhancing ORR performance. By strategically doping Er atoms into the CdIn2S4 lattice and subsequently loading amorphous CoS onto the prepared catalyst, the resulting catalyst exhibits a significant increase in photocatalytic H2O2 activity in pure water, approximately 9.8 times higher than that of undoped CdIn2S4. The in-situ photo-Fenton effect of CS/Er-CIS achieved a degradation efficiency of up to 85%. Experimental and theoretical calculations reveal that the Er atom acts as act as centers for electron capture, facilitating rapid electron transfer from the bulk to the surface. Meanwhile, the crystalline-amorphous interface formed by hybridizing with amorphous CoS creates a strong built-in electric field, enhances electron conductivity, and significantly improves the adsorption/desorption kinetics of reaction intermediates. This study presents a novel strategy for improving charge carrier kinetics and highlights the promising potential of metal sulfides for future development through rational electronic structure engineering. © 2026

title: Plasticized eutectic electrolytes for safe 4.7 V lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Raising the charge cutoff voltage enhances the energy density of lithium-ion batteries but imposes stringent requirements on electrolyte stability and safety. Nonflammable eutectic electrolytes are promising candidates; however, strong hydrogen-bond (H-bond) networks and cation-solvent coordination often limit room-temperature ion transport and high-voltage interfacial stability. Although fluorinated ether additives can enhance ionic conductivity and oxidative stability, the underlying structure-property relationships remain unclear. Here, we investigate the effects of different fluorinated ether molecules in an amide-based eutectic electrolyte. Three solvation configurations are identified: non-bridging, micelle-like, and plasticized. Among them, the plasticized solvation structure provides the most effective regulation of both bulk transport and interfacial chemistry. Particularly, fluorinated ether molecules penetrate the H-bond network via multisite interactions, weakening intermolecular H-bonding and promoting cathode-electrolyte interfacial reconstruction. This behavior is analogous to plasticizers in polymer systems, which enhance segmental mobility by reducing intermolecular interactions. As a result, the plasticized eutectic electrolyte markedly improves rate capability and cycling stability in 4.7 V Graphite||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 full cells and enables the 1.6 Ah pouch cell to pass a nail penetration test without thermal runaway. This work clarifies the relationship among fluorinated ether molecular structure, eutectic solvation networks, and interfacial reconstruction, providing guidance for designing eutectic electrolytes for high-voltage, safe lithium-ion batteries. © 2026

title: Tailoring strain delocalization in particle-reinforced metal matrix composites toward strength-ductility synergy through core-shell heterostructured metallic building blocks
abstract: Particle-reinforced metal matrix composites (PRMMCs) suffer from severe strain localization stemming from the mechanical incompatibility between hard reinforcements and soft metallic matrices. To overcome this challenge, SiC-nanoparticle-decorated aluminum powder was subjected to low-energy ball milling to produce core-shell heterostructured building blocks composed of ultrafine-grained (UFG) shells surrounding coarse-grained (CG) cores. Upon consolidation with micro-SiC particles, these building blocks induce a bulk composite featuring a dual core-shell architecture of CG-UFG matrix and SiC-UFG particles. Mechanistically, the UFG shells served distinct and complementary functions: Those around the CG in the matrix provided a hetero-deformation-induced strengthening contribution of ∼68 MPa (∼14% of yield strength) via long-range back stresses arising from hetero-interfaces; concurrently, those around micro-SiC particles suppressed strain localization at particle-matrix interfaces and promoted macroscale uniform deformation. As a result, an exceptional tensile strength of ∼685 ± 26 MPa combined with > 8% elongation was achieved. Therefore, the featured dual core-shell architecture induced by CG-UFG metallic building blocks offers a robust design route for achieving strength-ductility synergy in PRMMCs. © 2026

title: Protonated COF/g-C3N4 S-scheme heterojunction for photocatalytic H2O2 production
abstract: Regulating the electronic structure and interfacial charge transfer of metal-free photocatalysts is essential for efficient solar-driven hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production. Herein, an all-organic S-scheme heterostructure (HCOF-CN) was fabricated by in-situ growth of an imine-linked covalent organic framework (COF) on graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4), followed by mild sulfuric acid protonation. Protonation converted neutral CdbndN groups into positively charged CdbndNH+ sites, thereby extending visible-light absorption, promoting charge separation, and lowering the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) barrier. Under simulated light irradiation, optimized HCOF-CN achieved an H2O2 production rate of 4393 μmol g−1 h−1, 2.4 and 3.3 times those of pristine g-C3N4 and COF, respectively. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and in-situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) confirmed that H2O2 was mainly produced through an indirect two-electron ORR pathway. Kelvin probe force microscope, in-situ irradiated X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations confirmed the S-scheme interfacial charge-transfer mechanism. Protonation further reduced the formation energy of the key *OOH intermediate from 1.61 to 0.97 eV. This work provides a simple protonation-assisted heterojunction strategy for designing efficient metal-free photocatalysts for sustainable H2O2 production. © 2026 Chinese Society of Metals

title: Localized corrosion and oxidation-assisted crack filling and bridging in cracked Cr coatings on Zr alloy cladding
abstract: Through-thickness cracking can compromise the barrier function of Cr coatings on Zr-alloy fuel cladding, yet the defect response depends strongly on environment and crack geometry. Here, 15 ± 2 μm Cr coatings containing narrow cracks generated by 2% tensile strain and wide cracks generated by 20% strain were exposed, respectively, to low-dissolved-oxygen water at 360 °C and 20 MPa for 6000 and 10,000 h and to steam at 1100 °C for 600–3000 s. In pressurized water, coolant reached the substrate through the narrow cracks and produced isolated ZrO2 pockets whose depths increased from approximately 2.1 to 3.6 μm. The surrounding Cr remained adherent, and no continuous interfacial oxide or underfilm propagation was detected, in contrast to the continuous 4.4–5.5 μm oxide on the uncoated inner surface. In steam, the initially 4.7 ± 1.3 μm-wide cracks progressively narrowed and became bridged by 3000 s. Multiscale characterization resolved sequential sidewall Cr2O3 growth, Cr–Zr interdiffusion, ZrCr2 formation, and grain-boundary transport of Zr; the observed phase distributions were also consistent with a possible local reduction of Cr2O3 by transported Zr. These coupled processes generated a multiphase Cr2O3/Cr/ZrO2/ZrCr2 filling zone. The two investigated defect–environment combinations exhibited distinct condition-specific responses: Transport-limited localized corrosion around narrow cracks in hydrogenated water and oxidation-assisted crack filling and bridging of wide cracks in high-temperature steam. The latter produced geometric bridging in the examined sections but did not establish complete three-dimensional closure, recovered mechanical integrity, or gas tightness. © 2026

title: Effect of grain size and thermal annealing on the mechanical and superconducting properties of nanograined Nb-47wt.%Ti alloy
abstract: To investigate the effects of grain refinement on the superconducting properties (critical temperature (Tc), critical current density (Jc), and upper critical field (Hc2)) and mechanical properties of Nb-47wt.%Ti superconducting alloys, bulk samples with grain sizes from micrometers down to 19 nm were fabricated via high-pressure torsion. Microstructural refinement led to a continuous increase in hardness, while the superconducting properties exhibited a non-monotonic dependence on grain size. An optimal grain size of ∼55 nm exhibited a high Jc of ∼30.9 kA/cm2 (4.2 K, 5 T), a hardness of 2.9 GPa, and a well-retained Tc of 8.63 K. For the 55-nm-grained sample, subsequent annealing at 400 °C resulted in slight grain coarsening to ∼85 nm and simultaneous precipitation of nano-sized α-Ti precipitates. This composite structure endows the samples with better matching of strength and superconducting properties: a hardness of 3 GPa, a Tc of 9.19 K, and a Jc of ∼32 kA/cm2 (4.2 K, 5 T). This work provides insights into designing high-strength superconducting metallic materials. © 2026

title: Surface-metallized microvia arrays empower omnidirectional conductive films with exceptional electromagnetic interference shielding and heat dissipation
abstract: Against the ongoing trend toward lightweight electronic packaging, conventional electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials, typically based on bulk metals or highly filled composites, struggle to simultaneously achieve low density, mechanical compliance, and structural resilience. Here, we develop a microvia-engineered metallization strategy to enable efficient EMI shielding at low metal loading. Specifically, a styrene-butadiene-styrene (SBS) film is patterned with a controlled array of microvias, followed by in situ silver deposition on both the surface and microvia walls to construct a continuous 3D conductive network (denoted as TSV-Ag). Notably, the metallized microvia array does not deteriorate shielding in the X-band; instead, it produces a net increase in EMI shielding performance, delivering a shielding effectiveness of 66.35 dB in the X-band at an Ag volume fraction of only 0.58 vol.%. Moreover, the flexible SBS matrix suggests potential utility for gasket applications, and the microvia structure also provides additional pathways for heat transfer across the film thickness. These results indicate that microvia-enabled 3D conductive networks provide a viable route to decouple metal loading from shielding performance, offering a scalable design strategy for mechanically adaptive and thermally functional EMI shielding materials. © 2026 Chinese Society of Metals

title: Latency-robust corridor supervisory control for hybrid nuclear–HVDC–renewable power systems under communication-constrained low-inertia operation
abstract: Hybrid nuclear–HVDC–renewable transmission corridors introduce new supervisory coordination challenges due to reduced inertia, heterogeneous asset dynamics, and non-negligible bounded communication delay. Conventional coordination approaches typically assume ideal communication or treat latency as a secondary implementation issue, limiting robustness under wide-area supervisory operation. This paper proposes Latency-Robust Corridor Supervisory Control (LR-CSC), a reproducible engineering framework for delay-robust supervisory coordination under bounded communication delay. The methodology integrates a compact corridor-level state-space representation, a delay-embedded min–max supervisory formulation, and a digital-twin-based feasibility screening engine. Rather than relying on continuous online optimisation or centralised control authority, LR-CSC evaluates candidate supervisory actions over an admissible state envelope and enforces constraint satisfaction for all delays within a specified design bound. Validation is conducted using a fully specified synthetic nuclear–HVDC–renewable corridor benchmark under disturbance variation, stochastic bounded communication delay, and inertia degradation. Results demonstrate three principal outcomes. First, embedding bounded communication delay directly within supervisory feasibility expands the stable inertia–delay operating region relative to delay-blind coordination strategies. Second, delay-embedded feasibility screening suppresses oscillatory interaction between fast converter dynamics and slower synchronous response, yielding improved frequency nadir, reduced peak RoCoF, and faster settling behaviour. Third, robustness improvements persist across Monte-Carlo disturbance and communication uncertainty scenarios, indicating that performance gains arise from structural delay-embedded supervisory coordination rather than scenario-specific tuning. The proposed framework is intentionally positioned as a supervisory feasibility layer for low-inertia corridor coordination and provides a transparent balance between bounded computation, reproducibility, and practical implementability under communication-constrained operation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Real-time environmental understanding through active classification using tactile sensing in robotic disassembly
abstract: This paper proposes a generalized active classification framework designed to classify the environment of a robot through controlled tactile interaction, with direct application to robotic disassembly of Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE). In this domain, purely vision-based systems frequently fail due to occlusions, dust, and reflective surfaces, making haptic identification an operational necessity. By formulating environment identification as an active sensing problem, we utilize the entropy of learned interaction models and a receding-horizon optimization to select control inputs that maximize information gain from force–torque feedback. Our approach transitions from a passive classifier to an active framework that dynamically probes the environment to resolve belief uncertainty across six distinct tactile classes, demonstrated through the high-precision detection and unfastening of screws using an industrial 6-DOF robotic arm. Experimental results on a consumer microwave demonstrate that the active framework achieves a 51% reduction in detection latency for screws compared to passive baselines and consistently outperforms expert-designed heuristics. Furthermore, the system exhibits robust zero-shot generalization to novel industrial objects, indicating that learned tactile signatures are invariant to the global object context. These results provide a scalable foundation for autonomous disassembly in high-variance environments like electronic waste recycling, while offering a broader methodology for any robotic classification task where control can be leveraged to accelerate information gain. © 2026 The Authors. title: Research on rapid diagnosis of transmission tower abnormal state under subsidence condition based on 3D laser point cloud scanning
abstract: Traditional methods for inspecting the status of power transmission towers are inefficient and labor-intensive, while existing remote sensing techniques primarily assess overall geometric tilt, lacking the ability to diagnose localized structural anomalies. This paper proposed a rapid diagnosis technique based on 3D laser point cloud scanning and finite element method for abnormal state of transmission tower under ground settlement condition. The stress and displacement distribution of the tower under different foundation settlement conditions have been analyzed. With the first diaphragm plane of the tower as the reference plane, the multi-phase point cloud registration based on Super4PCS and ICP algorithm are proposed. The displacements of key nodes have been extracted to realize the rapid diagnosis of the abnormal state of the transmission tower. Application results show that displacement-to-height ratios of all key nodes exceed 16.69‰, and the tower is in a state of structural anomaly, which is consistent with detailed field investigation and quantitatively validated against independent total station measurements. The research results will help to quickly detect abnormal transmission towers and reduce the losses. © 2026 The Authors

title: LiMn2O4-centered manganese-based cathodes in aqueous lithium-ion batteries: Material genealogies, degradation mechanisms, and design strategies
abstract: Aqueous lithium-ion batteries (ALIBs) represent highly promising candidates for grid-scale energy storage due to their intrinsic safety, low cost, and environmental benignity. Concurrently, manganese-based (Mn-based) cathode materials align exceptionally well with these natures and the electrochemical stability window of aqueous electrolytes, which makes them the most extensively studied cathode materials. However, the underlying degradation mechanisms of Mn-based cathodes in aqueous systems remain to be fully elucidated. Focusing on spinel LiMn2O4 (LMO) as a quintessential model material, this review summarizes the development and material genealogies of Mn-based cathodes in ALIBs. Furthermore, both classical and emerging degradation mechanisms are scrutinized in depth, as these insights guide both contemporary and future design strategies. Under specific conditions, LMO can exhibit a kinetically maintained, metastable interfacial buffering regime in which compensating processes temporarily reduce the net degradation rate. However, continued species accumulation and interfacial heterogeneity eventually destabilize this regime, highlighting the need for precise interfacial regulation. Ultimately, this review bridges the degradation mechanisms of aqueous Mn-based cathodes with targeted modulation strategies, enabling high-voltage and long-life Mn-based cathodes for advanced ALIBs. © 2026

title: Experimentally validated ANN-based sustainable fault diagnosis framework for solar PV systems
abstract: Faults in solar photovoltaic (PV) arrays significantly degrade energy yield, reliability, and operational safety, particularly on the DC side where continuous energization increases fault severity. This paper presents an integrated Artificial Neural Network (ANN)-based framework for fault detection, classification, and location (FDCL) in grid-connected solar PV systems. An ANN model is trained using irradiance and ambient temperature to predict the expected array current and voltage under normal operating conditions. Fault detection is achieved by comparing ANN-predicted and measured power, enabling robust identification of abnormal operating states under varying environmental conditions. Following detection, a rule-based classification algorithm distinguishes among major DC-side faults, including open-circuit, short-circuit, degradation, and partial shading faults, using normalized electrical indices and adaptive threshold parameters. A low-complexity voltage-sensor-based fault localization strategy is further developed to accurately identify the faulty module or string with minimal sensing requirements. The proposed FDCL framework is validated through detailed MATLAB/Simulink simulations and extensive experimental testing on a real grid-connected solar PV plant under field operating conditions. Experimental results confirm high fault detection accuracy, reliable fault classification, and precise fault localization, demonstrating the practical applicability of the proposed approach for real-time monitoring and maintenance of solar PV systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Image-Based FEM Modeling of the Stress State in Hypereutectic High-Chromium Cast Irons; [Жоғары хромды гиперэвтектикалық шойындардағы кернеу күйін Image-based FEM-модельдеуі]; [Image-based FEM-моделирование напряжённого состояния в высокохромистых заэвтектических чугунах]
abstract: We developed an approach to analyze local thermal stresses in hypereutectic high-chromium cast irons using image-based finite element modeling (FEM) based on real metallographic images. Model preparation included Otsu thresholding of the microstructure, filtering noise objects, and directly assigning the spatial phase distribution from the binarized image without intermediate geometry construction in computer-aided design (CAD) systems. To verify the proposed approach, Drawing Exchange Format (DXF)-based and image-based FEM models constructed from the same microstructural data were compared, and the influence of finite element size on the calculated stress state was investigated. The results showed that, with a progressive reduction in finite element size, the image-based simulation results approached those obtained using the DXF-based models despite the discrete pixel-based representation of the phase boundaries. The image-based approach reproduces the main features of the local stress distributions obtained using the DXF-based models while eliminating the need for image vectorization and intermediate CAD/DXF geometry construction, thereby substantially simplifying the preparation of computational models of real microstructures. The obtained results confirm the applicability of image-based FEM for comparative analysis of local thermal stress distributions in complex multiphase microstructures of high-chromium cast irons. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Critical review of tools and techniques for predicting microplastics pollution in watershed runoff
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) pollution, especially, stormwater runoff from non-point sources is a major source of MPs into surrounding soils and aquatic environment. Numerous studies have investigated MPs occurrence, distribution, sources, morphology, environmental impact, and fate and transport (F&T) modeling, particularly in marine and freshwater ecosystems. However, models for MPs F&T, especially in the surface runoff context, are limited in scope or underexplored. This critical evaluation of hydrodynamic, process-based, mass-balance based, statistical, artificial intelligence (AI) based and hybrid approaches, alongside dedicated watershed hydrological models, including their input data requirements, spatial and temporal resolution, land-use classification, MPs typology, and software accessibility, to underscore influence on the model predictive reliability. Key findings reveal that existing models lack the representation of MPs as a discrete pollutant entity with density-dependent, and morphology-driven transport behavior. Hydrodynamic models excel in mechanistic fidelity but limit their scope with urban watershed runoff, while hydrological models provide an appropriate framework for watershed dynamics but lack MPs specific parameterization. AI and hybrid models show promising options for MPs predictive modeling but require robust calibration and validation datasets. Interconnected components of conceptual, structural, and empirical models are linked but constrained by barriers, hence it continues to limit MPs F&T model development and application. Addressing these challenges require standardized protocols, benchmark datasets, and integrated modeling frameworks. The synthesized information presented in this paper will not only assist in developing future MPs F&T models but also guide urban planners, environmental scientists, and water resource managers in selecting appropriate predictive tools for managing watershed MPs pollution. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: A composition generation framework embedded with domain knowledge for chemically disordered inorganic compounds
abstract: Generative models are increasingly attracting attention due to their ability to navigate the chemical space for inverse design of materials. However, generating valid compositions for chemically disordered crystals remains challenging, as inherent model noise makes it difficult to map continuous outputs onto precise, discrete stoichiometric coefficients. Here, we propose Tri-Control-MatVAE, a domain knowledge-embedded Variational Autoencoder (VAE) for triple-objective controllable generation over element selection, target properties, and ordered/disordered regimes. By decoupling the integer and fractional states of elements through autoregressive prediction, the framework captures the hybrid stoichiometric distribution of chemically disordered compositions. We further propose a reliability metric termed Stoichiometric Fidelity to quantify the alignment between authentic and generated compositions, under which our framework achieves an improvement from 59.55% to 97.87% compared to conventional generative models. Such fidelity and controllability enable the direct exploration of complex chemical spaces without requiring model retraining. By steering the generation toward targeted lithium-containing compositional regimes, it generates 1229 candidate compositions, including 349 stoichiometric variants of established database entries, providing a narrowed compositional starting point for downstream structural validation. Our work establishes a domain knowledge-embedded framework that extends controllable compositional inverse design to chemically disordered materials. © 2026

title: Design of strong anti-corrosion and high electrical conductivity protective bilayer coatings on bipolar plates in PEMWE cells by machine learning
abstract: Bipolar plates (BPs) are crucial components in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis cells, demanding protective coatings that simultaneously possess strong anti-corrosion and high electrical conductivity to ensure long-life durability. In this work, a machine learning (ML) method is established to accelerate the design and development of protective bilayer coatings on Ti BPs. Firstly, comprehensive datasets on corrosion resistance and electrical conductivity of metal/metallic carbide (nitride) bilayer coatings are compiled from published articles. Based on the optimized subset and regression algorithms, ML models for coating performance are trained and validated. The ML screening identifies TaC/Ta and TaN/Ta bilayer coatings as primary candidates, which exhibit strong anti-corrosion properties and good electrical conductivities. To experimentally validate the ML predictions, TaC/Ta, TaN/Ta, and NbN/Nb bilayer coatings are deposited on Ti BPs. The measured Icorr values are in the sequence of TaN/Ta < NbN/Nb < TaC/Ta, while the measured interfacial contact resistance (ICR) values are in the order of TaC/Ta < NbN/Nb < TaN/Ta, consistent with ML prediction trends. Furthermore, 3-h potentiostatic polarization at 2 V vs. saturated calomel electrode reveals that the formation of metallic oxides could enhance their corrosion resistance and long-term stability, but reduces their electrical conductivity. Notably, the TaC/Ta bilayer coating demonstrates exceptional comprehensive performance, maintaining good anti-corrosion stability and the lowest ICR value, highlighting its immense potential for next-generation BPs. © 2026

title: Day-ahead energy and ancillary services joint decision of hybrid energy storage with aging-aware frequency response simulation
abstract: The hybrid energy storage system (HESS), which integrates a battery and a supercapacitor, offers high flexibility and efficiency for peak shaving, frequency regulation (FR), and inertia support. To fully exploit the complementary characteristics of the HESS and support effective decision-making across multiple markets, this paper proposes a day-ahead joint decision model for HESS participation in energy, FR, and inertia services. To account for performance-based settlement in the FR market, FR simulation is integrated into the day-ahead scheduling model. To address the computational burden associated with the second-level time resolution of FR simulation, a rolling optimization framework is developed. In each rolling step, the first scheduling interval is represented at a fine time resolution, within which FR simulation is embedded. In the FR simulation, an HESS power allocation strategy is proposed to quantify the expected FR revenue and the battery marginal aging cost when energy arbitrage and FR provision are performed jointly. Accordingly, the profit-optimal FR power thresholds are derived to maximize HESS profit. Case studies demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the proposed framework. The inclusion of virtual inertia increases the expected HESS revenue by 25%, with inertia revenue accounting for 29% of the total revenue. Embedding FR simulation into day-ahead scheduling improves the average FR performance pass rate from 67.6% to 94.7%, while reducing the number of intervals failing to meet the requirement from 31 to 5. Compared with existing power allocation strategies, the proposed aging-aware FR allocation strategy reduces daily battery aging costs by 43% and increases total daily profit by 9.47%. © 2026

title: High creep resistance in a dilute Mg-Al-Mn-Sm cast alloy at elevated temperature
abstract: This study achieved significant enhancement in creep resistance in a dilute Mg-Al-Mn-Sm alloy by forming a thermally stable eutectic network through optimizing the Al to Sm ratio. It was found that at 200 °C and 50 MPa, the steady-state creep rate of the Mg-0.8Al-0.7Mn-0.9Sm alloy was 1.10 × 10−9 s−1, nearly two orders of magnitude lower than that of the Sm-free alloy, and no fracture occurred after 500 h of creep testing. With the increase in Al content to 2.5%, despite the suppression of Mg17Al12 formation, the creep resistance deteriorated to 2.75 × 10−8 s−1. Microstructural observations showed that the Mg-0.8Al-0.7Mn-0.9Sm alloy contained a homogeneous distribution of Al2Sm-rich eutectic network throughout the matrix. They effectively pinned dislocations, suppressed twin growth and coalescence as a manifestation of enhanced microstructural stability, and reduced damage accumulation along grain boundaries during creep. In contrast, even with a higher alloy concentration, the fraction of eutectic particles was much lower. Solidification simulations revealed that a low Al/Sm ratio led to a wide Al2Sm formation window of approximately 84 °C and a final eutectic fraction of 7.5%, whereas a high Al/Sm ratio narrowed the window to approximately 20 °C and produced only discrete Al-Sm compounds with a final eutectic fraction of only 1.3%. Consequently, the effective creep driving force in the Mg-0.8Al-0.7Mn-0.9Sm alloy is only about 2% of that in the Mg-2.5Al-0.8Mn-0.9Sm alloy, leading to a much lower creep deformation. © 2026

title: Ferroresonance overvoltage identification in distribution networks based on Markov transition field and GNN–Dual-ViT: A Markov–graph co-design framework
abstract: Ferroresonance is a typical abnormal operating condition in distribution networks. The overvoltages it produces can damage potential transformers (PTs) and, in extreme cases, cause switchgear explosions and electrical fires. The wide spectrum and strong nonlinearity of ferroresonance signals render conventional time–frequency methods inadequate. This paper proposes a Markov–graph co-design framework that tightly couples a theoretically grounded encoding stage with a structure-aware classifier. First, the first-order Markov approximation for quantised ferroresonance sequences is assessed using conditional mutual information and a conditional-independence test, with partial autocorrelation and Ljung–Box residual diagnostics used as supporting evidence. The combined results provide an empirical basis for Markov Transition Field (MTF) encoding without imposing an ordinal interpretation on the categorical states. Second, MTF converts one-dimensional voltage signals into weighted directed graphs whose edge weights encode state-transition probabilities. Third, a GNN–Dual-ViT architecture with progressive multimodal fusion exploits the resulting graph topology. The framework is evaluated against seven representative baselines reimplemented on a common ATP–EMTP dataset under identical protocols with multiple random seeds, and is further stress-tested under low SNR and load fluctuation. A cross-voltage study distinguishes same-mechanism transfer to a 35 kV PT system from adaptation to a physically different 110 kV CCVT regime. The results indicate that transfer is feasible with lightweight domain adaptation and limited labelled target data, while regime-specific calibration remains necessary for deployment. A branchwise qualitative analysis, a failure-case taxonomy, and a maximum-mean-discrepancy audit of the sim-to-field domain gap characterise both the mechanism and the boundary of applicability of the proposed framework. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Novel QUASC–CI converter with HEO-PI controller for hybrid renewable microgrid application
abstract: The changeover towards resilient and sustainable energy infrastructures has emphasized the integration of Renewable Energy Sources (RESs) into the hybrid microgrids. Still, the non-linear and intermittent behavior of RESs poses issues, in maintaining a stabilized DC bus voltage and grid support. In this research, a hybrid microgrid system is proposed with a novel Quadratic Ultra-Gain Switched-Capacitor Coupled Inductor (QUASC-CI) and an optimized controller to address the instabilities. The Photovoltaic (PV) system is incorporated with a QUASC-CI converter, offering extended gain in voltage at reduced duty ratios, with minimized stress and losses. On the other hand, for regulation of converter, Hare Escape Optimized Proportional Integral (HEO-PI) controller is introduced. The microgrid system, also incorporates Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG), battery and grid interface, guaranteeing that the developed hybrid system effectively manages fluctuating renewable generation, delivering smoother power to load and supporting grid compliance. MATLAB studies prove that the QUASC-CI converter in combination with HEO-PI controller offers superior converter efficiency of 96.49%, improved voltage gain, faster response of 0.15 s and reduced harmonic distortion, while confirming continuous grid integration. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Effect of laser shock peening on the corrosion resistance of additively manufactured AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy
abstract: Here, laser shock peening (LSP) was employed to tailor the near-surface microstructure and corrosion behavior of laser-directed energy-deposited AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) in 0.6 M NaCl solution. The LSP process preserved the face-centered cubic (FCC)/body-centered cubic (BCC) dual-phase constitution, and markedly modified the deformation microstructure. Within the FCC phase, the deformation microstructure evolved progressively with increasing laser impacts from dislocations to stacking faults, Lomer-Cottrell locks, nanotwins, and ultimately a 9R structure. However, the BCC phase primarily accommodated dislocation tangling, localized stacking faults, and heterogeneous lattice strain. All LSP-treated samples showed improved passivation relative to the as-built sample. Among the investigated conditions, twice LSP impacts (LSP-2) showed the most favorable overall passivation response, with the widest passive range (565.27 mV), the lowest passive current density (5.52 × 10−7 A cm−2), and the highest polarization resistance (24.24 × 105 Ω cm2). However, four LSP impacts (LSP-4) led to a deterioration in corrosion resistance relative to LSP-2 despite producing the highest compressive residual stress. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, Mott-Schottky, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analyses consistently revealed that the improved corrosion resistance was governed by passive film quality rather than film thickness. Specifically, LSP-2 exhibited the largest model-derived effective thickness of the highly resistive inner region (δi, PLM = 0.85 nm), the lowest apparent donor and acceptor densities, and the most favorable oxide/hydroxide ratios. By contrast, the deterioration in LSP-4 coincided with increased surface roughness, greater deformation complexity, and enhanced interphase electrochemical heterogeneity. These results demonstrate that LSP can optimize the corrosion resistance of additively manufactured EHEAs by regulating defect-mediated passivation mechanisms. © 2026

title: Artificial gene clusters designed for simultaneous multi-gene expression enable reconstruction of metabolite biosynthesis pathways in Trichoderma reesei
abstract: The filamentous fungus Trichoderma reesei represents a highly promising chassis cell for the efficient synthesis of both protein and non-protein metabolites. Despite the availability of diverse genetic manipulation tools for T. reesei , the engineering of chassis cells frequently requires coordinated regulation of multiple genes, a process that remains laborious and time-consuming with current methods. Here, we designed a modular and inducible artificial gene cluster (AGC) by repurposing functional DNA elements from the quinic acid (QA)-responsive gene cluster in T. reesei . This AGC is capable of expressing up to six functional genes for the assembly of genetic circuits. Under culture conditions utilizing a mixed carbon source of glycerol and QA, both robust cellular vegetative growth and activation of the gene cluster are compatible. Moreover, we identified qai1 as a gene encoding a putative transcriptional activator that governs the expression of the qai gene cluster. Notably, its overexpression alone is sufficient to bypass QA-sensing induction. Leveraging this insight, we engineered a QA-independent, constitutively expressed version of the AGC. As a proof of concept, we reconstructed the biosynthetic pathways for ilicicolin H and erythritol in T. reesei using the above QA-dependent and QA-independent AGCs, successfully achieving the synthesis of ilicicolin H and enhanced erythritol production in the T. reesei chassis cells. In summary, our study establishes novel genetic manipulation tools for engineering T. reesei chassis cells, allowing for rapid, multiplexed gene expression regulation to facilitate metabolite biosynthesis. © 2026 The Authors.
