title: Ultra-strong carbon fibers via atomic layer deposition-induced dual-scale defect regulation
abstract: Carbon fibers (CFs) with high tensile strength are highly desirable as reinforcement materials in advanced composites. However, their theoretical tensile strength (∼180 GPa), estimated from sp2 C–C bond strength in defect-free structures, remains unattainable because of intrinsic surface and internal defects. Here, we demonstrate an atomic layer deposition (ALD)-based strategy enabling dual-scale defect mitigation in commercial polyacrylonitrile-based CFs through simultaneous surface passivation and internal structural reinforcement. Conformal Al2O3 layers reduced surface irregularities and stress concentration sites, while infiltrated Al-containing species promoted interfacial bonding and cross-linking within the carbon microstructure. Consequently, the tensile strength of commercial CFs was significantly enhanced after ALD treatment, with T1000G fibers exhibiting a ∼41% increase in tensile strength and reaching 8.45 ± 1.35 GPa. Structural analyses using X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, small-angle X-ray scattering, field‑emission transmission electron microscopy, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping revealed reduced microvoid dimensions without significant alteration of the graphitic microstructure. These findings establish ALD-induced dual-scale defect mitigation as an effective and potentially industrially applicable approach for producing next-generation ultra-strong CFs. © 2026

title: Calculation of the local ground-level total electric field near a tower in a multi-circuit AC-to-DC conversion project based on an improved upwind finite element method
abstract: To address the problems of complex ion-flow space-charge distribution in AC-to-DC converted transmission lines under wind action, and the tendency of the conventional upwind finite element method to suffer from iterative oscillations and convergence difficulties, this paper proposes an improved upwind finite element method that enhances the stability of ground-level total electric field calculation under complex wind conditions. Taking a typical multi-circuit project where 750-kV AC cup-shaped towers are converted for 500-kV DC transmission as the engineering background, the local ground-level total electric field near one converted tower is investigated under different wind speeds and three-conductor polarity arrangements. The results show that the proposed method exhibits better convergence performance than the conventional upwind finite element method. An increase in wind speed promotes the wind-driven transport and redistribution of space charge, thereby affecting the peak magnitude and location of the local ground-level total electric field. The conductor polarity arrangement significantly influences the local field distribution, with the positive-positive-negative arrangement yielding a higher field magnitude among the investigated local configurations. The findings can provide a reference for local electromagnetic-environment assessment near towers in similar AC-to-DC conversion projects. © 2026

title: Superior interface thermal conductance via chemical bonding between diamond and carbon nanotubes
abstract: Facing growing thermal challenges in electronics, diamond/carbon nanotube (CNT) composites offer a breakthrough heat-dissipation solution, yet the phonon transport across covalently bonded diamond/CNT interfaces remains poorly understood at the atomic scale. Based on our experimental synthesis results, we build the interfacial bonding structure model of the diamond/CNT composite materials for the first time and demonstrate the effects of covalent bonding and atomic interfacial structure on interfacial thermal conductance (ITC). The interfacial chemical bonding can significantly enhance ITC (by 4 to 73 times compared to unbonded interfaces, depending on the temperature and the number of bonds per unit diameter), with the most pronounced enhancement observed at 700 K. Increasing the number of bonds further improves ITC by exciting more delocalized phonons to participate in transport. Structural analysis reveals that the combination of diamond with the (111) crystal plane and zigzag CNTs yields the optimal thermal conductance, while phonon analysis shows that delocalized phonons in CNTs contribute more prominently to thermal transport. We design several diamond/CNT array structures, including aligned and crossed arrangements, and achieve ITC on the order of ∼100 GW/(m2 K), which is the highest value reported in the literature. Our research not only demonstrates a method for fabricating high-performance diamond/CNT composites with excellent heat-dissipation properties, but also paves the way for the design and preparation of novel carbon‑based materials. © 2026 Chinese Society of Metals

title: Demand-side regulation potential enabled by user-point voltage control
abstract: Demand-Side Response (DSR) could play a significant role in balancing power supply and demand. This paper exploits the correlation between load voltage and power consumption, whereby load power can be regulated by adjusting supply voltages. A User-Point Voltage Control (UPVC) DSR mechanism is proposed. Compared with the existing approaches, UPVC enables a more flexible way for load regulation as it regulates the voltage supplied to each load, and is able to facilitate full utilisation of load regulation potential and enhanced implementation flexibility. The paper presents a quantitative analysis of the load regulation capacity enabled by UPVC to understand its DSR potential and benefits. The analysis applies initially to a generic Great Britain (GB) medium voltage/low voltage distribution network, with reference to high resolution daily load profiles, and is then extended to urban areas across GB and the entire United States (U.S.). The results are very encouraging as up to 2.4 GW in GB and 30.5 GW in U.S. load power regulation could be achieved for DSR, which indicates that the proposed scheme could serve as a new source of load flexibility in both countries. An economic feasibility analysis further confirms that large-scale deployment of UPVC is economically attractive. © 2026

title: Deep learning architectures for fault analysis in power system protection: A reproducible evaluation on public waveform data
abstract: The increasing operational variability of power systems motivates data-driven methods for fault analysis in protection applications. This paper presents a systematic evaluation of deep learning models for fault detection, classification, line identification, and localization. Models are trained on EMT-simulated voltage and current waveforms from the public PROTECT-90 dataset, a 90 kV double-line benchmark. Recurrent, convolutional, hybrid, and transformer-based architectures are compared under shared data splits, temporal decision horizons, and leakage-aware validation protocols to assess predictive performance, inference latency, and model complexity. The results reveal distinct task characteristics. Detection, classification, and line identification reach near-saturated performance once short post-fault transients are available, whereas localization depends strongly on temporal context and improves with longer observation windows. Additional sensitivity analyses contextualize localization under reduced relay observability, test-time communication perturbations, and impedance-based reference methods. Across tasks, compact recurrent and hybrid architectures nearly match the predictive performance of larger architectures while maintaining shorter inference times, indicating diminishing returns from increased capacity under centralized EMT-based measurements. The findings provide guidance for architectural selection in learning-based protection and post-fault analysis under controlled, reproducible EMT sensing assumptions. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: GridSage: A Skill-grounded LLM platform for scenario-oriented reinforcement learning evaluation in distribution networks
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) research in distribution networks continues to face challenges associated with complex scenario construction, high configuration overhead, and limited experimental reproducibility. Although existing RL platforms such as PowerGym and PowerGridworld provide standardized simulation and interaction interfaces, translating research intent into executable scenario configurations still relies heavily on manual effort. To address this issue, this paper proposes GridSage, an integrated platform that combines large language models (LLMs) with physics-aware power system simulation. GridSage adopts a Scenario Skill retrieval and incremental semantic editing framework, enabling users to construct customized scenarios through natural-language instructions. All generated scenarios are further subjected to safety validation to verify their physical validity and operational consistency. The validated scenarios are subsequently deployed into a Gymnasium-compatible RL environment incorporating photovoltaic generation, wind power, energy storage systems, electric vehicles, and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) interaction, supporting the training and evaluation of mainstream RL algorithms. On an independently prepared 600-instruction benchmark, incorporating Scenario Skill retrieval increased semantic success from 36.50% to 80.33%. The layered safety validator achieves a classification accuracy of 89.52% on 210 test cases. In a comparison involving four participants, GridSage reduces the average scenario-configuration time by 43.58%. Cross-LLM experiments further demonstrate that the proposed configuration workflow can operate effectively across different LLM backends. These results show that GridSage provides an effective and auditable approach for translating natural-language research intent into reproducible RL scenarios for active distribution networks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: An Experimental Vision-Based Predictive Framework for Lane Detection and Vehicle Localization Under Low Visibility Conditions During Driving
abstract: Reliable lane detection and vehicle localization are essential for advanced driver assistance systems, particularly under low-visibility conditions such as fog, shadows, low illumination, and degraded lane markings. This paper presents a vision-based predictive framework integrating deep convolutional neural networks, classical image processing, and Kalman filter-based state estimation supported by inertial measurement unit (IMU) data. Lane geometry is estimated from monocular camera images using a CNN-based regression model, while a confidence-adaptive predictive filter exploits vehicle motion to compensate for temporary visual degradation. The system is implemented on low-cost onboard hardware consisting of a forward-facing monocular camera, an IMU, a GPS module, and an embedded processing unit installed on a passenger vehicle. Experimental evaluation is conducted through simulation and real-world driving tests on urban highways using approximately 277000 image frames collected under diverse traffic and visibility conditions. Results demonstrate an average lane detection accuracy of 86.0%, improving to 92.7% with image enhancement. Vehicle localization achieves average lateral errors of 0.24-0.31 m and remains stable for up to 3 s during short-term loss of visual information. Real-time performance is achieved at 30 FPS with an average processing time of 26 ms per frame, confirming suitability for practical ITS deployment. © 2027 The author(s). title: Hijacking host RNA polymerase for processive in situ mutagenesis
abstract: Targeted mutagenesis is a crucial tool for in vivo continuous evolution. However, existing methods for long-range targeted mutagenesis in vivo often face limitations such as low efficiency, poor host compatibility, operational complexity, and uneven distribution of mutations across these windows. In this study, we developed a novel in vivo T argeted A ssisted M utagenesis via E ndogenous R NAP tool (TAMER) by functionally fusing the endogenous ω subunit of RNAP with a deaminase and dCas9. This tool achieved a mutagenesis efficiency of 1.28 × 10−3 substitutions per base (s.p.b.), which represents a 4.2 × 105-fold increase over the natural mutation rate. Additionally, this method enables uniform mutation distribution, an even mutation rate, a broad mutagenesis window, low off-target effects, and cross-host portability. Overall, TAMER offers a simple, efficient, and broadly applicable strategy for in vivo targeted long-range mutagenesis. © 2026 The Authors.

title: A new power transformer risk modelling considering cumulative surge effects in insulation coordination studies
abstract: Accurate insulation risk assessment plays a critical role in ensuring the reliability of power transformers, given the significant technical complexities involved in their design. Back flashover failure (BF) caused by lightning overvoltages on incoming substation lines must be considered as an effective stress component in transformer insulation design. These transient surges impose electrical stress on the paper-based insulation system of the transformer. Since such insulation materials are non-self-restoring, the analysis of the voltage–time (V-T) withstand characteristic is essential for insulation risk evaluation. These characteristics are typically derived from laboratory tests on power transformers; however, insulation aging occurring during the testing process may influence the accuracy of the extracted data. In real operating conditions, neglecting aging effects can lead to inconsistencies in insulation coordination. This paper proposes a novel model for correcting aging- deviations in voltage-time (V-T) characteristic curve, enabling a more accurate evaluation of insulation risk. Furthermore, the proposed framework incorporates the cumulative impact of aging in order to estimate the overall insulation risk of the transformer throughout its service life. The findings of this study contribute to safer and more optimized design of power transformers and support improved insulation coordination under realistic operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Micropore confinement engineering of porous carbon for efficient two-electron oxygen reduction to hydrogen peroxide
abstract: Two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e- ORR) for H2O2 synthesis offers a sustainable alternative to the traditional anthraquinone process. In this study, porous carbon (PC) with abundant micro-mesoporous structures and a large specific surface area of 2319.3 m2 g−1 was synthesized through a one-step calcination process with citrates as precursors. A natural air diffusion electrode (NADE) was subsequently fabricated based on PC, enabling efficient H2O2 production via the 2e- ORR. H2O2 yields of 5669.9 ± 95.5 and 5319.3 ± 186.6 mmol gcat−1 h−1 were achieved under alkaline and neutral conditions, respectively, with ~90% Faradaic efficiency at 100 mA cm−2. The structure-activity relationship between PC and ORR performance demonstrates that the micropore volume is positively correlated with the ORR onset potential. Molecular dynamics simulations confirm that the mean square displacement (MSD) of reactant molecules decreases with decreasing channel size, verifying the confinement effect of micropores. Additionally, theoretical calculations indicate that microporous structures can modulate the electronic properties of oxygen functional groups in carbon materials, optimize the adsorption energy of *OOH, and enhance 2e- ORR selectivity and activity. Therefore, rational regulation of the micro-mesoporous architecture represents an effective strategy for boosting 2e- ORR activity of carbon materials, providing a practical pathway toward large-scale electrosynthesis of H2O2. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Influence mechanism of electro-thermal coupling effect on inter-turn insulation damage of high-frequency transformer
abstract: Existing studies have demonstrated that high-frequency discharge, thermal effect, and charge transport mechanism are the primary causes of high-frequency insulation failure, yet it remains unclear which mechanism plays the dominant role. Therefore, this paper establishes an experimental and simulation platform for partial discharge (PD) in inter-turn insulation under high-frequency (HF) square-wave voltage to investigate the damage mechanism of inter-turn insulation induced by high-frequency electro-thermal coupling. Experimental results show that a transition region exists around 10 kHz. Below 10 kHz, the PD amplitude changes significantly while the temperature rise is relatively gentle, and the failure of HF transformer inter-turn insulation is mainly attributed to the coupling effect of HF PD and thermal effects. Above 10 kHz, the PD amplitude exhibits negligible variation whereas the temperature rises sharply. Notably, the inter-turn insulation breaks down rapidly with an extremely short time to breakdown at 30 kHz, indicating that high-frequency thermal effect becomes the dominant factor. The electric field acts in synergy with the thermal effect to accelerate the degradation of Nomex paper, thereby further promoting the thermal degradation and premature breakdown of the insulation. The findings of this study provide a solid theoretical basis for the life assessment and multi-physics modeling of HF transformer inter-turn insulation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Promoting effects of Cr2O3 Lewis acid on the multi-component metal glass for seawater electrolysis
abstract: Current direct seawater electrolysis faces major challenges, including insufficient catalytic activity and stability of electrode. To address these issues, a multi-component metal glass (FeCoNiMoLaWCr) is synthesized via a facile electrodeposition followed by Zn dealloying strategy, during which trace amounts of Cr2O3 Lewis acid are formed on its surface. The resulting FeCoNiMoLaWCr metal glass exhibits remarkable multifunctional electrocatalytic performances, delivering potentials of 1.46, 0.095, and 1.37 V for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), and methanol oxidation reaction (MOR), respectively, at a current density of 100 mA cm−2. When employed as both anode and cathode, FeCoNiMoLaWCr enables alkaline water electrolysis and methanol-assisted water electrolysis with low cell voltages of 1.56 V and 1.49 V at 100 mA cm−2, respectively. Moreover, the Cr2O3 Lewis acidic sites effectively repel Cl- ions in seawater, thereby greatly enhancing both activity and stability of FeCoNiMoLaWCr during seawater electrolysis. When used as both electrodes in seawater electrolysis, the FeCoNiMoLaWCr-based cell achieves a voltage of 1.58 V at 100 mA cm−2 and maintains negligible performance degradation during 3800 h of operation at 200 mA cm−2. This work provides a new strategy for designing highly active and durable electrodes for efficient seawater electrolysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Hydroxyl reinforcement effect on the heterointerfaced Rh/CoP remarkably accelerates hydrogen evolution reaction in alkaline media
abstract: The heterointerfaced Rh-CoP/C was designed and evaluated as a robust electrocatalyst towards the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), offering an immense playground for an anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE). Notably, Rh-CoP/C spontaneously converses to OH-Rh-CoP/C during alkaline HER via hydroxyl (OH) adsorption and its OH reinforcement effect on the alkaline HER performance was deeply explored by density functional theory (DFT) calculations coupled with experimental measurements. The results demonstrate that OH adsorption at the heterointerface not only promotes water dissociation but also creates a pathway for efficient hydrogen spillover to boost hydrogen (H2) release, thereby obviously enhancing alkaline HER. Moreover, OH adsorption stabilizes the heterointerface by suppressing P atom migration, ensuring long-term structural integrity. In addition, the optimized heterointerfaced OH-Rh/CoP catalyst exhibits excellent alkaline HER activity, achieving an ultralow overpotential of 10 and 186 mV at 20 and 500 mA cm−2, respectively, even surpassing commercial 20 wt% JM-Pt/C catalyst and most of previously reported noble metal-based catalysts. When deployed in an anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE), it requires a low cell voltage of 1.731 V to reach 1 A cm−2, along with outstanding operational stability over 2100 h with a minimal degradation rate of 61 µV h−1. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Optimizing Cooling Mode Switchovers in Green Data Centers via a SC Metric and TRNSYS-PSO Simulation
abstract: Driven by the demand for green and efficient data center cooling, this study develops a rack-level rear-door heat pipe (RDHP) cooling system and proposes a comprehensive metric SC by integrating Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE), Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE), Carbon Usage Effectiveness (CUE), and scoring components from the Chinese green data center standard GB/T 44989-2024. Optimizing the switchover between free, hybrid, and mechanical cooling modes is critical for improving the energy efficiency and reducing the carbon footprint of data centers. A delimiting temperature (T_delimit) of 17°C was established to optimally balance enhanced free cooling utilization with operational safety, ensuring server inlet temperatures remained within the limits. The switchover temperatures were optimized for four climatically diverse Chinese cities using TRNSYS simulations coupled with the GenOpt tool and a Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm. Results show that SC-oriented optimization effectively prolongs free cooling duration, reduces PUE, WUE, and CUE simultaneously, and outperforms empirical temperature settings. Also, the SC metric presents higher sensitivity than single indicators, while its optimization remains stable under varying grid carbon emission factors. This work provides a valuable methodology and a practical tool for advancing the green and low-carbon transformation of data centers, offering significant implications for policy-making and sustainable infrastructure planning. © 2027 The author(s). title: Adsorption Performance of Cationic and Anionic Dyes Using a UiO-66COOH@GO Composite: Synergistic and Competing Effects in Multicomponent Adsorption
abstract: The discharge of dye-contaminated wastewater poses a serious environmental challenge because of the persistence and toxicity of synthetic dyes. A UiO-66COOH@GO composite was synthesized by grafting graphene oxide onto solvothermally prepared UiO-66COOH at an optimized ratio and characterized by FESEM, BET, FTIR, TGA, and elemental analyses. The optimized composite was used to remove methyl orange (MO), an anionic dye, methylene blue (MB), a cationic dye, and their binary mixture. Solution pH was the key factor governing adsorption, with maximum capacities of 98.9 mg/g for MB at pH 8 and 57.4 mg/g for MO at pH 3. Equilibrium analysis revealed that the Langmuir–Freundlich and BET isotherms provided the best interpretation for MB and MO adsorption, respectively. The Avrami model well described the adsorption kinetics for both dyes. In binary MB/MO systems, synergistic effects enhanced MB adsorption, whereas competitive effects led to a reduction in MO uptake. These findings demonstrate that the UiO-66COOH@GO composite is an effective adsorbent for the simultaneous removal of cationic and anionic dyes, benefiting from the high aspect ratio of GO and the abundant functional groups of UiO-66COOH. ©2027 The author(s). title: A hierarchical hybrid control framework for networked microgrids: Integrating primary droop, distributed consensus, and economic dispatch
abstract: The integration of multiple interconnected microgrids presents significant challenges in maintaining stability, ensuring power quality, and optimizing economic operation. This paper presents a comprehensive hierarchical hybrid control framework that coordinates primary, secondary, and tertiary control layers to address these challenges systematically. The proposed architecture employs decentralized droop control for immediate power sharing, distributed consensus algorithms for voltage and frequency restoration, and economic dispatch optimization for cost-effective operation. This study developed a complete mathematical formulation and implemented a detailed simulation environment in Python to validate the framework's performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach maintains frequency within ±0.5 Hz of nominal values during steady-state operation and within ±0.5 Hz during islanding transitions, achieves proportional power sharing with less than 5% deviation from ideal ratios, and reduces operational costs by 23.7% compared to conventional decentralized control strategies. The framework's scalability is verified through small-signal stability analysis, showing all non-zero eigenvalues with negative real parts and a minimum damping ratio of 0.12 across various network configurations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Ligand-based intelligent modification of β-lactoglobulin: multi-target virtual screening, interaction mechanism elucidation, and functional validation
abstract: Phenolic acids offer a natural strategy for modulating the structural and functional properties of dairy proteins. Bovine β-lactoglobulin (β-LG) is a protein with structural plasticity, multiple ligand-binding cavities for bioactive molecules but is limited by its antigenicity and intrinsic antioxidant activity. Phenolic modification is a targeted means to modulate function of β-LG. Phenolic acids were selected based on docking performance, followed by residue-level prediction using a previously developed deep-learning model, and four target phenolic acids were ultimately identified: punicalagin (PG), 3,4-dicaffeoylquinic acid (DCQ), chicoric acid (CCA), and gallic acid (GA). Hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic associations are the dominant stabilizing forces identified from molecular docking results in binding to phenolic acids to β-LG residues. The model can estimate the interaction probabilities of novel uncharacterized binding sites on β-LG. This research focuses on evaluating how non-covalent β-LG-phenolic acid complexation can improve the protein's structural and functional properties. Multiscale multi-spectroscopic (UV-Vis, fluorescence, FTIR, CD) analysis clarified interactions and conformational changes. UV-Vis and fluorescence characterization confirmed the association of the β-LG-phenolic acid complex via elevated UV absorption peak intensity and obvious fluorescence quenching. FTIR and CD further revealed transformation of protein secondary structure after complexation. The antigenicity inhibition rates of β-LG-PG, β-LG-DCQ, β-LG-CCA, and β-LG-GA were 41.26%, 12.22%, 20.73%, and 42.36%, respectively. The complex's antioxidant potential was also enhanced before and after in vitro digestion. This study provides a strategy for screening phenolic acids and developing β-LG complexes with reduced antigenicity and enhanced antioxidant capacity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Steering CO2 electroreduction selectivity: Pulse-induced switching between C2H4 and CH4 over Cu4(NO3)2(OH)6 pre-catalyst
abstract: Manipulating competitive reaction pathways to obtain target hydrocarbons from electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) holds promise yet is still challenging. While pulsed electrolysis has been widely employed to tune CO2RR selectivity on Cu catalysts, the role of the pre‑catalyst structure in pulsed CO2RR has remained largely unexplored. Herein, we achieve switchable CO2 electroreduction between C2H4 and CH4 by coupling a customized pulsed potential protocol with a rose‑like Cu4(NO3)2(OH)6 pre‑catalyst. Its distinctive layered structure enables a rapid reconstruction within the first pulse cycle, generating a defect‑rich, derived Cu active phase that is highly responsive to pulsed potential tuning. Pulse parameter screening reveals that the anodic potential is the primary factor governing the selectivity switch for Cu4(NO3)2(OH)6-derived Cu. The two optimized pulsed protocols, differing primarily in the anodic potential, establish two distinct near‑surface oxidation states on the derived Cu: a Cu0/Cu+‑enriched region that favors C–C coupling to C2H4, and a Cu+/Cu2+‑enriched region that promotes *CO hydrogenation to CH4. This strategy thus delivers a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 52.5% for C2H4 and 43.05% for CH4. In situ spectroscopy and DFT calculations further elucidate that the near-surface oxidation state determines *CO coverage and the subsequent reaction pathway branching. Our work highlights that the ability to achieve pulse‑tunable selectivity depends critically on the pre‑catalyst architecture, establishing a coupled catalyst‑pulse design principle for steering CO2 electroreduction toward desired products. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Barrier-Function-Constrained Residual RL-Based Current Control for LCL-Filtered NPC Inverters under Weak-Grid Operation
abstract: As renewable energy penetration continues to grow, grid-connected inverters are increasingly required to operate reliably under weak-grid conditions, where low short-circuit ratios, changing grid impedances, and rapid disturbances reveal the limitations of conventional fixed-gain PI current controllers. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a more adaptive control approach; however, its application to fast inner current loops remains limited by stringent safety requirements and practical rediness challenges. This paper presents a control framework that combines a model-free Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based residual reinforcement learning controller with a model-based Control Lyapunov Function–Control Barrier Function (CLF–CBF) quadratic-program (QP) safety filter for an LCL-filtered three-phase neutral-point-clamped (NPC) grid-connected inverter. Although residual RL and CLF–CBF safety methods have been explored independently, this work integrates a model-free PPO-based residual controller with a model-based CLF–CBF safety filter within a unified architecture for fast inner-loop current control under varying grid-strength and operating conditions. Instead of replacing the conventional PI controller, the residual policy generates bounded corrective voltage commands that complement a fixed PI baseline, while the CLF–CBF–QP safety filter provides analytical enforcement of stability and operational constraints independently of the learned policy. A two-stage training strategy, consisting of unconstrained warm-start followed by safety-constrained fine-tuning, enables efficient policy learning while maintaining safe operation. Evaluated across eight representative operating scenarios with five independent trials per condition, the proposed framework achieves a maximum total harmonic distortion (THD) reduction of 49.7% under extreme thermal stress and 44.2% under nominal operation, with an average THD reduction of 25.7% across all scenarios. The framework also reduces aggregate constraint violations by 35.7% across the evaluated conditions, indicating that the integration of model-free residual reinforcement learning with a model-based CLF–CBF safety layer can improve harmonic performance while providing model-based supervision of current and voltage operating constraints. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Heavy-atom node engineering in perylene diimide-based MOFs for efficient singlet-oxygen-mediated aerobic oxidation
abstract: Efficient singlet oxygen (1O2)-mediated selective oxidation requires photocatalysts capable of promoting intersystem crossing and enriching triplet states. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) provide a multifunctional platform for photocatalytic detoxification, yet how metal nodes regulate excited-state dynamics and triplet exciton formation remains insufficiently understood. Herein, we construct two isostructural perylene diimide (PDI)-based MOFs to systematically elucidate node-dependent spin-orbit coupling effects. The Hf nodes promote spin-related excited-state evolution through a heavy-atom effect, favoring triplet-state formation and 1O2 generation. As a result, the Hf-based MOF PDI-MOF(Hf) exhibits outstanding performance in mustard gas simulant detoxification, achieving a half-life of ∼ 4 min while maintaining high selectivity, and exhibits wide-ranging applications in the selective oxidation of aromatic sulfides into sulfoxides. Phosphorescence and in-situ electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy measurements corroborate the enhanced triplet-state processes and dominant 1O2-mediated pathway. This work establishes a clear correlation between heavy-atom node engineering and spin-dependent photophysics, providing a general strategy to overcome intersystem crossing limitations in organic chromophores and advancing the rational design of MOF photocatalysts for detoxification and selective oxidation. © 2026

title: Mixed double-hemivariational analysis of piezoelectric contact with multiplier-coupled nonmonotone friction
abstract: We introduce and analyze a static piezoelectric contact model for Hencky-type materials in which the nonsmooth interface response depends on the tangential displacement, the electric potential jump, and a regularized representation of the normal contact reaction through the Lagrange multiplier. This yields a genuinely multiplier-dependent double nonsmooth coupling on the contact boundary. The model is formulated as a mixed problem in which a Lagrange multiplier is associated with the unilateral Signorini-type contact constraint and, through its regularized representation, also enters the nonsmooth interface response. The resulting boundary functional is expressed in hemivariational form through Clarke’s generalized directional derivative with respect to both the primal interface variables and the regularized multiplier variable. Under standard assumptions on the constitutive operators and suitable growth, compactness, and upper semicontinuity conditions on the coupled superpotential, we prove the existence of weak solutions. The proof combines a truncation procedure, a Fan–KKM argument with a Minty-type reformulation, a uniform multiplier estimate based on an inf–sup property for the normal trace, and a weak compactness argument. We also establish a sequential stability result showing the robustness of weak solutions under perturbations of the loadings and of the foundation data. Finally, a numerical illustration is provided to highlight the influence of the regularized normal reaction on the effective frictional and electrical interface responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: HPC-accelerated parallel algorithms for large-scale power system contingency analysis
abstract: The extension of static security assessment from N-1 to N-2 contingency analysis poses significant computational challenges because of the combinatorial growth in outage scenarios and the repeated execution of AC load-flow solutions. This paper proposes a high-performance computing (HPC) framework for efficient N-1 and N-2 contingency ranking using the fast decoupled load flow (FDLF) method on heterogeneous CPU-GPU platforms. Contingency severity is evaluated using a composite performance index based on line overloads and bus voltage deviations. The framework incorporates MPI-based CPU parallelization, CUDA-based GPU acceleration, and hybrid CPU-GPU execution, with cuBLAS-assisted LU factorization to accelerate the dominant FDLF linear solves. The proposed framework is validated on the IEEE 118-bus, Indian Northern Regional Power Grid (246-bus), and Polish 2383-bus systems under extensive N-1 and N-2 contingency sets. The MPI implementation achieves speedups of up to 19 × over the sequential implementation, while the hybrid implementation provides superior performance for GPU-enabled systems with limited CPU resources. Overall, the proposed framework significantly reduces the computational burden of large-scale AC-based contingency analysis and provides practical guidance for selecting suitable HPC architectures for modern power system security assessment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Engineering hollow-strut lattices for low-density, high-strength metal mechanical metamaterials
abstract: Hollow-strut lattice metamaterials enable lightweight metallic materials by placing material away from the neutral axis, thereby enhancing bending stiffness and buckling resistance. Their design has been largely limited to circular hollow struts. Here, strut cross-sectional geometry is introduced as a new design lever for high-performance hollow-strut lattices. Hollow square-strut body-centered cubic lattices are designed, fabricated in Ti-6Al-4V by laser powder bed fusion, and rationalized using a geometry-dependent analytical model. The square hollow geometry provides a higher second moment of area than circular hollow strut, enabling stronger resistance to deformation. Consequently, Ti-6Al-4V hollow square-strut lattice designs with three densities in the range of 1.4–2.3 g/cm3 achieve yield strengths of 103–328 MPa, compressive strengths of 132–448 MPa, and elastic moduli of 5.0–7.5 GPa, outperforming circular counterparts across all densities. Their yield strength increases by up to 27%, accompanied by more uniform strain distribution, delayed strain localization, and improved deformation stability. At comparable densities, their absolute yield strength exceeds that of high-strength magnesium alloys while retaining the corrosion resistance, biocompatibility, and other intrinsic advantages of Ti-6Al-4V. This work establishes cross-sectional geometry as a powerful design dimension for lightweight, high-strength metallic mechanical metamaterials. © 2026

title: Capillary-suspension-structured cellulose/fish oil oleogel-based bigels: Ratio-driven phase organization and swallowing performance
abstract: Dysphagia-friendly foods require tunable texture, structural stability, and controlled oral deformation. In this study, cellulose/fish oil oleogels were constructed through capillary suspension structuring, and further combined with fish gelatin hydrogels to produce bigels with adjustable swallowing properties. Oleogel formation was jointly regulated by cellulose and water contents. The oleogel containing 25 wt% cellulose and 5 wt% water formed a stable bridged network with improved oil-holding capacity, reaching 73.32 ± 0.45%, and its structural recovery increased from 11.85% to 66.00% with increasing cellulose content. The oleogel/hydrogel ratio markedly affected bigel phase organization, rheology, texture, stability, and IDDSI performance. Increasing oleogel fraction induced a structure transition from hydrogel-continuous phase structure to semi-bicontinuous transitional structure and finally to an oleogel-rich structure. BG50 exhibited favorable structural and mechanical performance, with compact network, enhanced gel strength, and stable deformation resistance. IDDSI tests showed that bigels containing 10∼50% oleogel corresponded to Level 6, whereas those containing 70∼90% oleogel shifted to Level 5. Additionally, bigels with an oleogel content below 50% exhibited higher centrifugal stability, supporting their potential for processing, storage, and transport. Overall, this study provides new insights and methods for the design of dysphagia-friendly foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Twin-boundary-rich PtPd metallene suppresses CO poisoning for efficient methanol electrooxidation
abstract: Direct methanol fuel cells (DMFCs) are regarded as a highly promising clean-energy technology. Herein, an ultrathin two-dimensional twin-boundary-rich PtPd metallene (TB-PtPdene) is successfully synthesized using a salt-templating method. Structural analyses confirm a homogeneous metallic alloy configuration with reduced coordination environments and optimized electronic structure induced by twin interfaces. Electrochemical evaluations show that TB-PtPdene delivers a mass activity of 1.99 A mgPGM−1, outperforming commercial Pt black, Pd black, and TB-Ptene for methanol oxidation reaction (MOR). Mechanistic studies reveal suppressed accumulation of poisoning CO intermediates and altered behavior of oxygenated intermediates on TB-PtPdene. Density functional theory calculations further reveal that the twin-boundary-rich PtPd structure modulates the adsorption energetics of MOR intermediates and reduces the uphill free-energy change of the *CHO-to-*HCOO step. TB-PtPdene also maintains substantial catalytic activity during prolonged electrochemical operation, with its structural integrity well preserved after stability testing. When TB-PtPdene is implemented in DMFCs, the assembled device achieves a peak power density of 14.2 mW cm−2, significantly exceeding that of Pt black-based devices. This work offers an innovative strategy for designing MOR electrocatalysts with both high activity and stability, and deepens the mechanistic understanding of the role of twin defects in catalytic processes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Unique polarization configuration and enhanced anhysteretic electrostrictive strain in PMN-PZN crystal via antiferroelectric PMW modification
abstract: High-precision actuators serve as critical components in precision measurement, control, and drive. Ferroelectric materials with large electrostrain are constrained from application in precision actuators due to their severe hysteresis. In this work, two relaxor systems, Pb(Mg1/3Nb2/3)O3-Pb(Zn1/3Nb2/3)O3 (PMN-PZN) and Pb(Mg1/3Nb2/3)O3-Pb(Zn1/3Nb2/3)O3-Pb(Mg1/2W1/2)O3 (PMN-PZN-PMW), were designed and grown into single crystals. The obtained PMN-PZN-PMW crystal demonstrated significant improvements in breakdown field and electrostrictive strain level compared with that of the PMN-PZN crystal: PMN-PZN gets an anhysteretic electrostrictive strain of 0.107% at 25 kV cm−1, while PMN-PZN-PMW achieves an anhysteretic electrostrictive strain of 0.17% at 50 kV cm−1. The enhancement in electrostrictive strain and the absence of hysteresis are attributed to the morphotropic relaxor boundary-like structure induced by the incorporation of antiferroelectric PMW. In this structure, multiple polar nanoregions coexist and are interconnected through continuously rotating polarization vectors. This unique polarization configuration not only suppresses leakage current but also lowers the energy barrier for polarization switching. This demonstrates an innovative approach to improving electrostrictive strain performance by constructing a multi-relaxor structure. The developed single crystals are highly suitable for precision actuators and hold broad application prospects. © 2026

title: Kinetic matching of desorption and oxidation through functional decoupling in tandem catalysis
abstract: The simultaneous removal of multicomponent aromatic volatile organic compounds (VOCs), such as benzene and toluene mixtures widely encountered in industrial exhaust streams, is severely hindered by competitive adsorption, intermediate accumulation, and the kinetic mismatch between desorption and catalytic oxidation. Herein, we propose a kinetic decoupling-matching strategy, in which adsorption and oxidation are spatially decoupled in a tandem catalytic system (5Ag/Beta-300‖MnO2), while ultrafast infrared (IR) heating enables rapid kinetic matching between VOCs desorption and catalytic oxidation for achieving one-stage “adsorption-degradation” elimination of multicomponent VOCs. By identifying the critical heating rate (≥1500 °C/min), we successfully synchronize VOCs desorption with the active oxidation window of the catalyst, achieving spatiotemporal matching and ensuring complete degradation without “low-temperature release” during oxidation. In-situ DRIFTS and DFT analyses demonstrate that Ag modified zeolites facilitate the formation of intermediates such as diphenylmethane, elevating desorption temperature and widening the operational margin. Compared to traditional thermal catalysis, the IR-driven process reduces degradation time from hours to seconds and reduces energy consumption by 65%, establishing a highly efficient and low-carbon route for complex VOCs mixture. © 2026

title: The environmental efficiency of the combined combustion of low-grade Ekibastuz coal and plant biomass; [Төмен сұрыпты Екібастұз көмірі мен өсімдік биомассасының аралас жануының экологиялық тиімділігі]; [Экологическая эффективность совместного сжигания низкосортного Экибастузского угля и растительной биомассы]
abstract: This article presents the results of a study on the layered combustion of low-grade Ekibastuz coal blended with biomass additives aimed at improving the energy efficiency and environmental sustainability of small-and medium-scale energy systems. Corn waste, which is a by-product of agro-industrial production, was used as a bio-additive. Comprehensive physico-chemical analysis of the original components was carried out, including determination of their calorific value. Based on the obtained data, fuel mixtures with different biomass contents were prepared, which allowed an in-depth analysis of co-combustion processes and the relationship between the proportion of biomass, the calorific value of the mixture, the combustion efficiency, and the level of pollutant emissions to be determined. The results showed that the most optimal composition is a fuel mixture with a biomass content in the range of 20-30% and coal in the range of 70-80%, providing the best combination of energy and environmental performance. Calculations and experimental studies of layered combustion parameters in installations with a fixed layer have been performed. It was demonstrated that the addition of 20–30% biomass intensifies the combustion process, increases the overall calorific value of the fuel blend, and reduces the concentration of harmful substances in flue gases compared to the combustion of pure coal. Rational process conditions have been defined, including the optimal height of the fuel layer, temperature regimes, and combustion duration. The results confirm the high prospects of using fuel mixtures based on low-grade coal and biomass as a cleaner and more sustainable solution for heat supply of small and medium-sized energy systems in Kazakhstan. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: In situ observation and dynamic evolution of 9R structures enabled by Mg/Ag alloying for exceptional strength-conductivity synergy in a Cu alloy wire
abstract: Achieving high strength while retaining high electrical conductivity remains a central challenge in precipitation-strengthened copper alloys. Here, a Cu-Ni-Co-Si-Mg-Ag alloy wire was developed through multi-step cold drawing and intermediate aging, and the strain-dependent role of localized 9R structures during plastic deformation was investigated. At a true strain of 3.79 after peak aging, the alloy exhibits an ultimate tensile strength of 1055 MPa, a yield strength of 955 MPa, an elongation of 5.9%, and an electrical conductivity of 48.2% IACS. Multiscale characterization and atomistic calculations reveal that Mg and Ag preferentially segregate at Cu/δ-(Ni, Co)2Si interfaces, thereby reducing interfacial energy and stacking fault energy, stabilizing nanoscale precipitates, and creating favorable conditions for localized 9R formation. Meanwhile, severe drawing develops a strong 〈111〉 fiber texture, which shifts the Schmid factor distribution toward lower values, thereby promoting localized partial-dislocation-mediated deformation. In situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction and in situ transmission electron microscope further reveal that the 9R structures are not only retained after cold drawing but also evolve dynamically during tensile deformation, with their local fraction initially increasing and subsequently decreasing before fracture. This dynamic evolution intensifies the interactions among 9R structures, precipitates, and dislocations, thereby enhancing dislocation storage and resistance to plastic flow. In parallel, solute depletion and limited electronic perturbation by Ag preserve the electrical conductivity. These findings establish a mechanistic link among Mg/Ag segregation, dynamic 9R evolution, hierarchical defect interactions, and the high strength-conductivity performance of highly drawn Cu alloy wires. © 2026

title: AVT: Adhesive visual tactile sensor for anthropomorphic and precise manipulation of tiny mechanical components
abstract: Grasping and manipulation of tiny objects have always been a significant challenge in manufacturing and industrial automation, especially in tasks such as small-part sorting, kitting, and assembly preparation. The tiny size makes it hard for vision systems to detect and locate small pieces with high accuracy. And they offer only limited contact regions for robotic hands to pick. Thus, this study proposes a non-prehensile manipulation method for tiny components based on a developed adhesive visual tactile sensor. This sensor incorporates a transparent adhesive layer with a visual tactile sensor, enabling the picking of multiple pieces using adhesive force while detecting the object types and locating the positions. We developed a two-fingered dexterous robotic hand that mimics intuitive human behavior, utilizing one finger to adhere a tiny component and another finger nail to detach it. The proposed sensor is equipped on the sensor finger, while the other fingertip features a nail structure. Inspired by human behavior, the hand can stick and detect objects using the sensor finger, and detach the picked objects from the adhesive surface to the target positions using the nail finger. We also propose the associated planning methods for finger and robot motions. Experimental results show that the method can effectively classify and organize various scattered tiny components with a classification accuracy of 96.4% and an average positioning error of 0.51 mm, validating the proposed method for manipulating tiny mechanical components in manufacturing applications. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Cinnamaldehyde-lactic acid deep eutectic solvent modified chitosan composite film and its application in grape preservation
abstract: To address the issues of non-degradability in traditional petroleum-based packaging materials and the limitations of chitosan (CS) films (e.g., poor mechanical properties, insufficient water resistance, and single functionality), this study incorporated a deep eutectic solvent (DES) composed of cinnamaldehyde (CIN) and DL-lactic acid (LA) into the CS matrix to fabricate high-performance composite films. The effect of DES content on the structure and properties of the composite films was investigated. FTIR and XPS analyses suggested that a fraction of the aldehyde groups of CIN participated in Schiff base formation with the amino groups of CS. Together with hydrogen-bond reorganization and LA induced protonation of CS amino groups, these interactions contributed to the regulation of the CS network. When the DES content was 60% of the dry weight of CS, the resulting CS(CIN:LA)60 film exhibited the optimal comprehensive performance: its tensile strength (TS) reached as high as 41.57 MPa; the water contact angle (WCA) was approximately 100°, indicating good hydrophobicity; the water vapor transmission rate (WVTR) was reduced to 560.2 g/(m2·24h); meanwhile, it possessed excellent ultraviolet (UV) shielding ability, remarkable anti-fogging performance, and good antibacterial activity. Grape preservation experiments demonstrated that the CS(CIN:LA)60 film could effectively inhibit microbial growth, reduce water loss, and delay fruit softening and the degradation of nutritional components. Compared with commercial polyethylene (PE) cling film, the composite film showed advantages in antibacterial activity, anti-fogging performance, and the maintenance of several grape quality attributes. This study provides a new strategy for the development of green food packaging materials. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Boron doping manipulated local coordination environment of atomically dispersed nickel sites for efficient CO2 electroreduction and Zn-CO2 batteries
abstract: Atomically dispersed transition metal-nitrogen-carbon catalysts are emerged as promising electrocatalysts for CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). However, it remains challenging to precisely modulate the coordination configuration of atomically dispersed metal sites and elucidate the correlations between their geometric/electronic structures and CO2RR catalytic performance. Herein, we report a co-doping strategy to synthesize carbon-supported single-atom nickel catalysts with boron and nitrogen dual coordination environments (NiBNC). The NiBNC exhibits superior performance in the electroreduction of CO2 to CO, achieving an ultrahigh Faradaic efficiency of 99.8% and a high current density of –200 mA cm–2 in a flow cell. The hard X-ray absorption analysis reveals atomically dispersed Ni sites are coordinated with one B atom and three N atoms in the first shell, namely Ni-N3B1. Theoretical calculations suggest that the asymmetric Ni-N3B1 coordination enhances the electron density around Ni sites compared with the symmetric Ni-N4 configuration, facilitating the formation of *COOH intermediates and improving CO2RR kinetics. Furthermore, aqueous Zn-CO2 battery with NiBNC cathode delivers a high CO Faradaic efficiency (~ 99%) at 7 mA cm–2 and long-term stability over 100 h. This work opens up a new route to simultaneously modulate the geometric and electronic structure of single-atom catalysts toward efficient CO2 conversion. © 2026

title: Harnessing synthetic microbial communities for desert vegetation restoration
abstract: The core bottleneck for desert vegetation restoration is extreme water stress during early seedling establishment, with hydraulic failure as the primary lethal mechanism. Traditional engineering measures (e.g., irrigation) and single-strain inoculation cannot adequately address these challenges due to high cost, weak sustainability, or limited functionality. Synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) offer a new approach to synergistically regulate plant water use and soil microenvironment by integrating functionally complementary taxa. This review discusses the soil water characteristics of deserts and the bottlenecks in seedling water use, indigenous microbial resources and their adaptive mechanisms, principles and design strategies for constructing SynComs, as well as the mechanisms by which SynComs improve seedling water use efficiency and survival. We also analyze key challenges and future research directions. Although SynComs have been extensively studied for enhancing plant stress resistance, their application in desert vegetation restoration is still in its infancy. Future research needs to clarify how to design SynComs to ensure their ecological compatibility, persistence, and functionality in the highly variable and extreme environments of desertified landscapes. This review provides a theoretical basis for advancing SynComs application in arid land ecological restoration. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Selective ROS generation via engineered electron donor/acceptor sites: Switching photocatalytic oxidation from toxic intermediate to complete mineralization
abstract: Catalytic oxidation technologies face the challenge of incomplete oxidation, which generates secondary pollutants and undermines environmental benefits. Achieving complete mineralization requires precise steering of reaction pathways, a process fundamentally governed by reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated on the catalyst surface. Herein, we demonstrate that creating localized sites with defined electron-donating or electron-accepting character regulates interfacial charge transfer, thereby directing ROS evolution and final reaction pathway. Using photocatalytic NO oxidation as a model reaction, we engineered ZnO surfaces selectively enriched with donor-type oxygen vacancies (VO) or acceptor-type zinc vacancies (VZn). While both achieved high NO removal efficiency, VZn-rich ZnO produced substantial toxic intermediate NO2 (106.3 ppb), whereas VO-rich ZnO suppressed NO2 to 20.4 ppb. In-situ characterization and theoretical calculations reveal that VZn sites stabilize photogenerated holes, promoting •OH formation and incomplete NO oxidation to NO2. In contrast, VO sites localize electrons, driving O2 activation to •O2− and a deep oxidation pathway to nitrate. The VO-rich catalyst was further immobilized on a porous Al2O3 support, retaining high activity and selectivity with excellent operational stability. This work establishes a fundamental principle for precisely controlling ROS-based reaction pathways, offering a strategy to advance environmental catalytic technologies that maximize conversion efficiency while minimize secondary pollution. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Water-assisted *CO protonation decouples C2+ formation from carbon loss in acidic CO2 electroreduction
abstract: Electroreduction of CO2 to multicarbon (C2+) products in acidic electrolytes offers a carbon-efficient route for producing value-added fuels and chemicals. However, high C2+ selectivity in acidic media typically relies on concentrated alkali-metal cations, which stabilize *CO and promote C-C coupling but reinduce (bi)carbonate formation and salt precipitation. Reducing cation concentration alleviates (bi)carbonate-derived carbon loss, but weakens cation-mediated interfacial regulation, causing adsorbed *CO to favor desorption over C-C coupling toward C2+ products. Here, we develop a water-assisted protonation layer (WAPL) on Cu to decouple C2+ formation from (bi)carbonate-derived carbon loss under low-cation acidic conditions. WAPL regulates the Cu-water interface through interfacial charge redistribution induced by electron-accepting interactions, promoting water-assisted *CO protonation and *CO-*CHO coupling. In 0.5 M K+ acidic electrolyte, a total C2+ FE of 63.0% was achieved at 150 mA cm−2, while limiting CO2-to-(bi)carbonate conversion to 2.8%, a 5.5-fold decrease compared with concentrated-K+operation. In situ fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy and Raman spectroscopy combined with theoretical calculations reveal that WAPL restructures interfacial water and facilitates *CO protonation to *CHO, enabling asymmetric C-C coupling. This work provides an interfacial proton-transfer strategy for achieving high C2+ selectivity in acidic media while suppressing the (bi)carbonate-derived carbon loss associated with concentrated-cation operation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: From industrial electrowinning to reversible aqueous manganese metal batteries
abstract: Aqueous manganese metal batteries (MnMBs) hold great promise for grid‑scale energy storage, owing to their low redox potential (–1.18 V vs. SHE), high volumetric capacity (7250 mAh cm–3), and vast crustal abundance. However, the severe thermodynamic mismatch between Mn and water induces concurrent hydrogen evolution, spontaneous corrosion, and interfacial passivation, which critically undermine Coulombic efficiency and cycle life. This review bridges the century‑old empirical knowledge of industrial electrolytic manganese metal (EMM) production with modern battery science. It shows that interfacial kinetic shielding, historically achieved by additives such as SeO2, provides a translatable blueprint for stabilizing Mn anodes. We systematically deconvolute the coupled failure mechanisms and assess state‑of‑the‑art modification strategies for the anode, electrolyte, and cathode. More importantly, we emphasize the need to translate macroscopic metallurgical principles into nanoscale reversible electrochemical loops and outline a holistic roadmap toward practical MnMBs. Key future directions are identified, including operando interfacial characterization, decoupling of competitive reaction pathways, development of low‑toxicity additives, pH mismatch management, self‑discharge mitigation, and impurity‑tolerance guidelines. By integrating fundamental chemistry and industrial metallurgical wisdom, this review aims to accelerate the development of highly reversible and cost‑effective aqueous MnMBs for next‑generation storage. © 2026

title: Unlocking high-performance manganese-based layered oxide cathodes for sodium-ion batteries
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), characterized by energy-storage mechanisms similar to those of lithium-ion batteries and offering substantial resource and cost advantages, are regarded as highly promising candidates for next-generation energy storage systems. Given that cathode materials are crucial in determining electrochemical performance, their rational design and optimization are essential for accelerating the commercialization of SIBs. Among various cathode candidates, manganese (Mn)-based layered oxide materials have attracted particular interest owing to their low cost, high specific capacity, and environmental benignity. However, their practical application is hindered by the intrinsic Jahn-Teller effect and complex phase transitions, which lead to structural and electrochemical degradation during cycling. In this review, we comprehensively summarize the key challenges encountered by Mn-based layered oxides during charge/discharge processes and delve into the fundamental mechanisms governing their electrochemical performance. We further discuss representative modification strategies designed to enhance cycling stability and rate capability, mainly including local-environment regulation, phase-structure tailoring, morphology engineering, and surface customization. These approaches can effectively suppress lattice distortion and parasitic side reactions, stabilize the structural framework, and thereby enhance the electrochemical performance. Finally, we outline the remaining challenges and future prospects for Mn-based layered oxide cathodes, with the goal of facilitating their practical application in SIBs. © 2026

title: Machine learning-driven electromagnetic wave absorbing: Prediction and its applications
abstract: With the rapid development of electronic information technology and increasingly complex electromagnetic environments, electromagnetic wave absorbing materials are essential for electromagnetic compatibility, stealth, packaging, and anti-interference applications. Modern absorbers require lightweight, thin, broadband, efficient, and multifunctional designs, yet their performance is governed by strongly nonlinear interactions among composition, phases, defects, interfaces, thickness, processing, dielectric/magnetic losses, impedance matching, interfacial polarization, and multiple scattering. Traditional trial-and-error approaches are inefficient for such high-dimensional design spaces, whereas machine learning provides data-driven tools for nonlinear modelling and multi-objective optimization. This review summarizes machin- learning applications in absorption performance prediction, structure-activity relationship mining, key variable identification, parameter optimization, high-throughput screening, and inverse design. Current challenges include limited and inconsistent data, insufficient feature representation, weak generalization and interpretability, and incomplete experimental validation. Future efforts should focus on high-quality databases, mechanism-constrained models, few-shot learning, multi-objective optimization, and automated closed-loop platforms to enable intelligent design and rapid engineering application of high-performance absorbing materials. © 2026

title: Online state estimation based on forecasting-correction-refinement framework for active distribution systems
abstract: The increasing penetration of distributed energy resources and new types of loads introduces rapid power fluctuations and uncertainties into active distribution systems (ADSs), posing challenges to online distribution system state estimation (DSSE) under sudden power changes. This paper develops a functionally decoupled forecasting-correction-refinement framework for online forecasting-aided DSSE. First, recursive least squares (RLS) generates one-step-ahead forecasts of the system states. The resulting forecasts are then rapidly corrected by a covariance-informed linear least-squares estimation (LLSE) stage using fixed and continuously available micro-phasor measurement unit (μPMU) voltage measurements. Subsequently, weighted least squares (WLS) uses the corrected forecasts as prior information and incorporates the remaining heterogeneous measurements to obtain the final current-slot estimates. To maintain stable recursive updating, the LLSE-corrected forecasts, rather than the final WLS estimates, are fed back to update the RLS model. Case studies on modified IEEE 34-bus and IEEE 123-bus systems demonstrate that the proposed method consistently improves state-estimation accuracy over the benchmark methods. It effectively suppresses large forecasting deviations while maintaining stable recursive operation, and exhibits satisfactory scalability and computational efficiency for online applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Ultrasonically textured engineering of protein amyloid fibrils-tannic acid composite hydrogels for dysphagia management
abstract: Dysphagia severely affects the quality of life in elderly and neurological patients. Conventional carbohydrate-based dysphagia-oriented foods, which have insufficient nutritional richness, tend to fragment during oral processing, increasing aspiration risk. Protein amyloid fibrils offer high protein supplement and robust mechanical properties, which can form stable hydrogels with polyphenols, suggesting potential for dysphagia-oriented foods. However, the effect of the protein amyloid fibril structure on related hydrogel properties and its International Dysphagia Diet Standardization Initiative (IDDSI) classification remain unclear. In this case, we used ultrasonic pretreatment to modulate the β-lactoglobulin fibril structure, and then induced fibril-tannic acid (TA) interactions to form composite hydrogels. Transmission electron microscopy showed that ultrasound accelerated fibrillation kinetics and induced fibril shortening, and excessive treatment (U50-10, 4.80 W/mL, 10 min) resulted in predominantly short fibrillar species. Ultrasonic pretreatment significantly increased the surface hydrophobicity and free sulfhydryl content of the resulting fibrils. These morphological and physicochemical changes markedly enhanced hydrogel network stability, as confirmed by rheology and texture analysis. Among all groups, U50-6 (4.80 W/mL, 6 min) improved elasticity and creep recovery the most, while also showing the highest water-holding capacity and hardness, attributed to a denser crosslinked network formed by moderately shortened fibrils. Notably, hydrogels precisely covered IDDSI levels from 3 to 5, allowing tailored design for patients with varying swallowing abilities. This study establishes a structure-assembly-function relationship for protein fibril–polyphenol systems and offers a rational strategy for developing personalized dysphagia-oriented foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Around-the-clock intelligent sensing transportation systems based on vdWs n-p-n heterostructure memristive arrays
abstract: The detection of near-infrared light is of great importance in fields such as traffic monitoring, medical imaging, and security monitoring. However, conventional sensing systems based on the von Neumann architecture face fundamental challenges in terms of integration and performance due to their sensing-computing separation model. In this study, we present a van der Waals n-p-n Bi2Te3/SnSe/Nb:SrTiO3 hetero-memristor. This device combines the advantages of two-dimensional (2D) topological insulators and 2D ferroelectric materials. Modulating the ferroelectric polarization effectively adjusts the device performance, achieving a 75% yield, an optical on/off ratio of approximately 104, and a pulse cycle lifetime of over 108 cycles. Furthermore, the device exhibits stable 32 resistance states and a pronounced wavelength-dependent optical response, demonstrating exceptional stability over 31,000 optical switching cycles under 808 nm illumination. By integrating optical measurement precision with infrared spectral robustness, a near-infrared sensing system based on memristor sensing arrays has been realized. Incorporating the memristive sensing characteristics into the YOLOv11-based recognition framework, the proposed system achieves accuracy rates of 83% and 93% for pedestrian and vehicle recognition, respectively. These recognition outcomes demonstrate the potential of intelligent near-infrared sensing systems for neuromorphic perception applications. © 2026

title: Stress interference and propagation uniformity in multi cluster hydraulic fracturing using a coupled XFEM based CZM model
abstract: The uniform propagation of multiple hydraulic fractures is crucial to maximize the volume of stimulated reservoirs and improve the recovery of hydrocarbons in unconventional reservoirs. However, simultaneous fluid injections often result in non-uniform fracture growth due to strong stress interference between adjacent clusters. The unresolved issue is a quantitative ranking of how the spacing of the clusters, the count of the clusters, the injection rate and the viscosity of the fluid control the uniformity of propagation under matched geomechanical conditions. This study addresses that gap using a two-dimensional plane strain coupled XFEM based CZM model for simultaneous multi-cluster fracture propagation from a horizontal wellbore in a tight and low-permeability reservoir. The model is verified against the analytical solution dominated by toughness of KGD and applied to fourteen parametric cases covering cluster spacing of 20 to 35 m, injection rate of 0.001 to 0.005 m3/s per cluster, fluid viscosity of 10−3 to 10−1 Pa s, and two to five clusters. Results show that coalescence of individual stress shadows into a continuous compressive stress umbrella is the main cause of non-uniform growth, with interior clusters confined while exterior fractures propagate more freely. Fracture spacing is the dominant control and increasing spacing from 20 to 30 m raises the uniformity index from 0.42 to 0.94 and supports uniform growth to 88 to 95 m. Cluster count is the second strongest control, injection rate has a secondary non-monotonic effect, and fluid viscosity has negligible influence on uniformity. The sensitivity ranking is first the fracture spacing, followed by the group count, the injection rate, and the viscosity of the fluid. For the modeled formation, 30 m spacing favors uniform simultaneous propagation, whereas spacing below 25 m may require sequential or zipper initiation. © 2026 The Authors. title: A hybrid GRA-D-PRGO-BP model incorporating dynamic decay strategy to enhance ultra-short-term photovoltaic power forecasting accuracy
abstract: Photovoltaic power generation is characterized by significant intermittency and stochasticity, making accurate ultra-short-term PV power forecasting essential for ensuring secure and stable grid operation and improving renewable energy accommodation. However, in ultra-short-term forecasting scenarios, existing BP-based forecasting methods still suffer from input redundancy, parameter sensitivity, and insufficient optimization stability. To address these issues, this study proposes a hybrid GRA-D-PRGO-BP model for ultra-short-term PV power forecasting. First, Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) is employed to evaluate the relevance of candidate input features with lag information, so as to identify key input variables and reduce feature redundancy. Second, a dynamic plant root growth optimizer (D-PRGO) is proposed. By introducing nonlinear dynamic decay weights into the dual-root growth mechanisms, the proposed algorithm enhances the coordination between global exploration and local exploitation. Finally, D-PRGO is used to optimize the initial weights and biases of the BP neural network, thereby improving forecasting accuracy and stability. Experimental results show that the proposed GRA-D-PRGO-BP model achieves an MAE of 9.9179 ± 0.5092 kW, an RMSE of 23.6070 ± 1.0767 kW, and an R² of 0.8924 ± 0.0099. It outperforms BP-based benchmark models in forecasting accuracy and run-to-run stability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Learning fuzzy normal-operation regimes for interpretable power system anomaly detection
abstract: This paper presents an interpretable one-class anomaly detection framework for power systems based on adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference systems (ANFIS). The proposed method is trained exclusively on benign operational data and learns a compact set of fuzzy regimes describing normal cyber-physical behavior. The learned regimes are used to define rule-local invariant bounds and regularized Gaussian compatibility models. A fuzzy rule-weighted Mahalanobis score then measures the compatibility of each new observation with the activated benign regimes. Unlike supervised detectors, the proposed method requires no fault or attack samples during training and evaluates anomalous observations through deviations from learned normal operation. The framework is evaluated on the Mississippi State University and Oak Ridge National Laboratory Power System Attack Dataset, which contains benign operation, natural faults, and cyberattacks. The proposed detector achieves a ROC-AUC of 0.9773, a PR-AUC of 0.9998, precision of 0.9994, recall of 0.9265, specificity of 0.9138, and an F1-score of 0.9616. In addition to anomaly detection, the framework provides rule and feature-level explanations by identifying the activated fuzzy regime, the measurements contributing most strongly to the anomaly score, and any violated invariant conditions. The learned rules also capture distinct physical measurement profiles, supporting interpretable analysis of detected faults and attacks. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Zonal allocation and pricing of power system inertia considering frequency spatio-temporal characteristics
abstract: In high‑ratio power electronic systems, the uneven distribution and diversity of generation sources lead to significant spatio-temporal characteristics in frequency response, complicating inertia configuration. Most power markets with frequency security constraints clear at the system level, which cannot capture the dynamic process. This paper aims to address the issue of improper inertia allocation in power systems with a high penetration of renewable energy. It proposes a zoning method that accounts for system topology and congestion risks to allocate inertia and establish zonal inertia prices, thereby implementing a zone-based framework for inertia dispatch and pricing. Firstly, the system topology and the line congestion characteristics under uncertain scenarios are analyzed, and the real-time zoning results under different scenarios are obtained by combining the cosine similarity and clustering algorithm. Secondly, the inertia market clearing model is constructed, and a continuous security constrained unit commitment (SCUC) model is proposed to accurately quantify the price of inertia in each zone. The final case study shows that, compared with overall dispatching, zonal dispatching of inertia effectively alleviates the inertia deficit in certain areas, leading to more accurate allocation and a 20% reduction in total cost, making this approach more economical. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Temperature-dependent interfacial degradation and premature oxide spallation of a Y-Hf co-doped AlCrFeNi multi-principal element alloy
abstract: The high-temperature oxidation resistance of multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) is influenced by the adhesion and stability of the oxide scale. In this study, the oxidation behavior and failure mechanism of the Y-Hf co-doped AlCrFeNi MPEA at 1100 and 1200 °C in static air are studied. After oxidation for 500 h at 1100 °C, a continuous, adherent α-Al2O3 scale consisting of inner columnar grains and outer equiaxed grains is formed. In contrast, severe spallation and interfacial rumpling are observed after oxidation for 50 h at 1200 °C, despite the formation of a similar α-Al2O3 scale. The premature spallation is attributed to the degradation of the oxide-scale/alloy interface. Accelerated Al consumption and phase-dependent Al/Ni mobility mismatch promote interfacial pore formation, reducing the effective contact area between the scale and substrate. The sulfur enrichment detected at the spalled interface suppresses pore healing and converts interfacial pores into effective decohesion sites. Furthermore, the reduced high-temperature strength of the alloy enhances oxide rumpling, facilitating stress localization and accelerating scale spallation. These results indicate that the beneficial Y-Hf reactive-element effect in stabilizing the oxide scale becomes insufficient at 1200 °C under severe interfacial degradation conditions, providing scientific guidance for developing MPEAs with enhanced oxidation resistance. © 2026

title: Core-shell supported NiCo bimetallic catalysts with alloying synergy for oleic acid hydrogenation to bio‑jet fuel
abstract: Reducing carbon emissions from the aviation sector represented a pressing environmental challenge, and the hydrogenation of vegetable oils to produce high‑value bio-jet fuel offered one of the most promising and economically viable pathways. Herein, we reported a novel bimetallic alloy catalyst with a tunable Ni/Co ratio, specifically designed for the selective hydrogenation of oleic acid to bio-jet fuel. This system delivered 100% conversion of oleic acid and a higher bio-jet fuel yield of 57.2%, while maintaining high iso-alkanes selectivity, which demonstrated superior performance compared to previously reported dazzling heterogeneous catalysts. The introduction of Co promoted the formation of a NiCo alloy phase and facilitated electron transfer from Co to Ni species. The resulting electronic and geometric synergies collectively enhance the dissociation and activation of H2, as well as the hydrogenation activity of substrates. Moreover, the Ni/Co ratio directly modulated the catalyst acidity, and the optimized acid properties played a critical role in the subsequent cracking and isomerization of deoxygenated intermediates. Collectively, these findings established a foundation for the rational design of efficient catalysts for bio-jet fuel production derived from oils. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
