title: Thickness-tailored FeB/Fe2B diffusion barriers on Q345R steel for long-term corrosion protection in molten solar salt
abstract: Q345R steel is an economically attractive structural material for molten-nitrate thermal-storage systems, but its corrosion resistance in molten solar salt is limited. In this study, FeB/Fe2B diffusion layers were produced on Q345R steel by pack boriding at 850 and 900 °C for 2 h, and their corrosion behavior was evaluated in molten solar salt at 450 °C for 500 and 1000 h. Mass-loss measurements, surface and cross-sectional SEM/EDS, EBSD, and XRD were used to characterize material loss, near-surface microstructure, corrosion-product morphology, and phase constitution. After 1000 h, the annualized corrosion rate decreased from 0.060 mm/year for untreated Q345R steel to 0.020 mm/year for B-850 and 0.012 mm/year for B-900. Cross-sectional SEM observations showed that the boride-layer thickness increased from approximately 10 μm for B-850 to approximately 20 μm for B-900. Owing to the effective inhibition of ionic diffusion by the borided layer, the corrosion rate of the borided specimens was merely one-fifth that of the untreated steel, accompanied by a notably retarded oxide-scale growth. Among all the conditions investigated, the B-900 specimen exhibited the most pronounced protective effect, achieving the lowest values in both mass loss and annualized corrosion rate. These results indicate that pack boriding can improve the corrosion resistance of Q345R steel during prolonged static exposure to laboratory-grade solar salt. © 2026

title: Bioactive nanocomposite-reinforced biopolymer films for multifunctional food packaging
abstract: Developing sustainable food packaging materials with mechanical strength, antibacterial activity, and biodegradability remains challenging. In this study, a multifunctional konjac glucomannan (KGM)/quaternized nanocellulose (QNC)-zinc oxide (ZnO) composite film was fabricated through a triple interfacial synergistic reinforcement strategy using KGM, QNC, and ZnO nanoparticles. The incorporation of QNC and ZnO enhanced film performance via strong interfacial interactions. The optimized film exhibited a tensile strength of 139.6 MPa and elongation at break of 21.7%. Moisture resistance improved, with a water vapor transmission rate of 78.2 g m−2·day−1 and a water contact angle of 88.6°. The composite exhibited strong antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus with antibacterial rates of 99.75% and 99.99%. The composite also showed good biodegradability and excellent cytocompatibility. Grape preservation tests indicated a weight loss of only 15.49% after 18 days. This study provides a green and feasible strategy for constructing biodegradable multifunctional packaging films with enhanced mechanical properties, antibacterial activity, and preservation functionality. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Tuning the molecular characteristics and functionality of wheat bran arabinoxylans via controlled alkaline extraction conditions
abstract: A comparative assessment of alkaline extractions of wheat bran (WB) arabinoxylans (AX) with NH4OH and NaOH solutions (pH 8.5-11.5, 2-4 h, 60 °C) was made, focusing on their molecular characteristics and rheological/gelling behavior. NMR and FTIR spectroscopies showed that under mild alkaline conditions (NaOH or NH4OH, pH 8.5/2h), extracted AX had lower A/X ratios (0.34), while at higher pH (NaOH, pH 11.5/2 h) the A/X reached up to 0.69. The apparent peak molecular size (Mp; based on size exclusion chromatography data) of NH4OH-extracted AX showed an increase up to pH 11.5 (∼248 kDa), whereas the NaOH-AX showed increased Mp up to pH 9.5 (∼276 kDa) and declined values thereafter. Extracted AX at moderate pH (8.5, 9.5) exhibited high contents of esterified ferulates (∼325-515 mg/100g AX extract); with increased alkalinity (pH 10.5, 11.5), partial or extensive de-esterification was noted in both NH4OH- and NaOH-concentrates. Strong gels were made by oxidative cross-linking (peroxidase/H2O2) using aqueous dispersions of AX extracted at pH 8.5 and 9.5, whereas for those obtained at pH 10.5 and 11.5, the gelation capacity was retained only for NH4OH-AX concentrates. Viscosity of aqueous AX dispersions increased with their molecular size. An array of 2D NMR experiments, including DOSY (Diffusion-Ordered Spectroscopy), revealed the typical AX features, showing structural complexity-microheterogeneity among samples and molecular populations with discrete diffusional characteristics. Araf–Araf side chains were also identified, with notably higher abundance in the NaOH-concentrates (pH 10.5–11.5). The findings highlighted the significant impact of both type and pH of alkaline medium on the diversity of molecular characteristics and functionality of alkali-extractable WB AX. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Credible flexibility envelope learning for renewable curtailment reduction in export-constrained power systems
abstract: Renewable-rich areas often experience curtailment because local demand and export capacity cannot absorb short-duration surpluses. Flexible loads and storage can help, but nameplate capability does not necessarily represent reliable market capacity when availability, internal state, rebound, telemetry quality, and baseline error vary between events. This paper develops a credible flexibility envelope by eroding a multi-period physical feasible set with a calibrated trajectory-error set. A class-conditioned recurrent state captures recent operation, a hierarchical Bayesian decoder updates uncertain physical parameters, and weighted block-conformal calibration adjusts residual margins under temporal dependence and drift. Offers, cleared capacity, dispatch instructions, and verified delivery are modeled separately, and the resulting envelopes are embedded in a loss-aware, multi-corridor network clearing model with voltage, thermal, feeder, settlement, and credit constraints. A controlled three-year synthetic benchmark uses a modified IEEE RTS-24 system, three radial feeder equivalents, seven resource classes, 20 random seeds, and 540 stress-test combinations. At a 95% coverage target, the proposed method achieves 95.0% empirical coverage, reduces non-delivery from 10.1% to 4.6%, increases curtailment reduction from 22.6% to 40.0%, and raises mean net surplus from 62.7 × 103 to 193.0 × 103 USD. Ablation and stress tests further examine drift, forecast error, telemetry loss, baseline bias, correlation, network changes, and extreme renewable conditions. The results are specific to the modified RTS-24 benchmark and motivate further evaluation on other networks and measured data. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Carrageenan based hydrogel systems with artificial compartment for probiotics microcapsules and tannic acid to preserve perishable food
abstract: In this study, microcapsules of Lactococcus lactis in whey protein isolated/sodium alginate was co-encapsulated with tannic acid in the carrageenan hydrogel. This design created compartments via the microcapsules and prevented the activity loss with direct contact of the components. The structural analysis results indicated that tannic acid and microcapsules strengthened the network structure through hydrogen bonding. The incorporation of microcapsules into the hydrogel provided physical support, improving the mechanical properties of the carrageenan-based composite hydrogel by 36.5%. Furthermore, the acidic microenvironment created by Lactococcus lactis and the protective network formed by tannic acid mutually enhanced stability and demonstrated synergistic effects. The composite hydrogel exhibited excellent antioxidant activity with scavenging rates exceeding 80% for ABTS, DPPH and superoxide anion radicals. Meanwhile, it significantly inhibited the growth of bacteria and fungi, including Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, Salmonella enteritidis, Aspergillus niger and Botrytis cinerea. Biocompatibility assessment showed that the composite hydrogel exhibited virtually no cytotoxicity or hemolytic activity, and could promote plant growth after degradation in water. Practical storage tests confirmed that composite hydrogel significantly delayed browning of fresh-cut apples and potatoes, maintaining acceptability after 1 and 8 h storage. Besides, it slowed the accumulation of total volatile basic nitrogen and deterioration of sensory quality in refrigerated chicken, extending shelf life by 2 days. In summary, the composite hydrogel possessed outstanding functionality and practicality, providing a promising strategy for the design of highly efficient and safe active food packaging. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Line outage impact factor (LOIF): A new sensitivity factor for enhanced transmission observability
abstract: Undetected transmission line outages degrade operator situational awareness and can increase the risk of incorrect control actions and escalating system stress. To improve transmission observability for outage detection under limited monitoring, this paper introduces the Line Outage Impact Factor (LOIF), a new sensitivity indicator that quantifies the relative change in power flow experienced by an observed line following an outage elsewhere. Unlike the conventional Line Outage Distribution Factor (LODF), which normalizes by the pre-outage flow on the disconnected line, LOIF normalizes by the pre-outage flow on the observed line, offering a better indicator for the sensitivity of the observed line to another line's outage and, thus, facilitating the selection of monitored lines that enhance system observability. Building on LOIF, we propose two observed transmission line (OTL) selection strategies to maximize outage coverage with a small number of monitoring locations. With OTLs selected in the IEEE 30-bus, 118-bus, and the Wisconsin 1664-bus systems, we performed outage detection using different machine learning classifiers. Results show that, for the same number of OTLs, LOIF-based selections generally achieve higher F1-scores than LODF-based selections, with the most consistent gains observed in the large 1664-bus system, demonstrating LOIF's potential for scalable transmission monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Active harmonic filters: Evolution from classical to advanced engineering practices - A comprehensive review
abstract: The rapid growth of power-electronic converters has elevated harmonic mitigation from a secondary power-quality concern to a core requirement for grid compliance, reliable operation, and stability. Passive filters remain attractive for their simplicity and low cost, but suffer from detuning, resonance, and poor adaptability under varying conditions. Active harmonic filters (AHFs) use controlled converters to deliver adaptive, broadband compensation suited to converter-dominated grids. This paper reviews active harmonic filtering from a system-level perspective, covering shunt, series, hybrid, and unified configurations; two-level, multilevel, and modular converters; and resonant, predictive, nonlinear, and data-driven control. It treats DC-link energy, thermal stress, grid interaction, and component aging as first-order constraints rather than secondary concerns. Particular attention is given to high-power applications—most notably fast electric-vehicle (EV) charging— where compensation capability may be constrained by thermal and energy headroom, semiconductor current rating, modulation-voltage margin, DC-link ripple, and other operating limits. Performance metrics, benchmarking, and validation practices are consolidated into an AHF Minimum Reporting Set that extends comparison beyond total harmonic distortion (THD) alone; the limits of simulation-only studies are highlighted. Open challenges include weak-grid operation, wide-bandgap reliability, coordinated multi-converter control, and intelligent reliability-aware AHFs. © 2026

title: AI-enabled multi-class visual fault diagnosis for large-scale solar photovoltaic systems supporting energy transition and net-zero operations
abstract: Large-scale solar photovoltaic installations are required to have reliable inspection methodologies in order to detect surface conditions or degradation states which could negatively affect their operational efficiencies. In this paper, we develop a visual condition classification system for large-scale photovoltaic (PV) modules based on an AI technique capable of identifying six PV module surface conditions classified into six different classes: physically damaged, visually apparent electrical degraded, dirty/dusty, snow-covered, bird-drop impacted, and clean. Using transfer learning techniques, four different architectures were tested as classifiers under the same balanced classification protocol. EfficientNet-B0 produced the highest average results among all tested architectures with an average overall classification accuracy score of 94.3% for all tests. Additionally, the average Macro-Precision, Macro-Recall and Macro F1 scores for EfficientNet-B0 were 93.2%, 92.8%, and 93.0%. Furthermore, EfficientNet-B0 exhibited a variability in its Macro-Precision and Macro F1 scores of no greater than 1.6% between the best and worst test result of any individual run, thus demonstrating consistent performance across multiple runs. Lastly, the maximum processing time (inference time) for EfficientNet-B0 was less than 18 ms per image in the current reporting. The results demonstrated herein represent a proof-of-concept for a scalable methodology for visually inspecting PV surfaces, but additional testing at multiple sites along with the collection of additional data regarding operational status will be necessary before validation can be conducted. © 2026 The Authors. title: Wind power prediction based on a deeply coupled IT2FNN-attentional GRU network
abstract: The prediction of wind power output is crucial for the safe and stable operation of power grids with a high proportion of renewable energy. This paper addresses the nonlinear, non-stationary, and uncertain characteristics of wind power sequences by proposing a novel forecasting framework that integrates interval type-2 fuzzy logic with deep learning. We establish a deeply coupled architecture of interval type-2 fuzzy neural networks and gated recurrent units, which combines uncertainty quantification capabilities with time-series feature extraction abilities. Furthermore, we introduce an attention mechanism to achieve adaptive focusing on key historical information, enhancing the model's perception and expression capabilities. The proposed Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Neural Network-Attentional Gated Recurrent Unit (IT2FNN-AGRU) network effectively addresses the high volatility and complex uncertainties of wind power output. To evaluate its practical performance, the proposed model was empirically validated using operational data collected from two wind farms located in Turkey (3.6 MW) and France (1.85 MW). Experimental results on both datasets show that the proposed model consistently achieves low MAPE values, significantly outperforming all benchmark methods. This demonstrates its accuracy, stability, and practical value across diverse wind power generation scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Advances and perspectives in genetically encoded biosensors for biomarker detection and theranostic circuits
abstract: Effective biomarker detection is critical for timely and accurate clinical disease diagnosis. However, conventional analytical methodologies are often constrained by laborious procedures, reliance on specialized equipment, and an inherent inability to perform continuous in situ monitoring. To circumvent these limitations, synthetic biology has pioneered the development of genetically encoded biosensors as a rapid, highly sensitive, and cost-effective alternative. This review specifically focuses on transcriptional regulation-based biosensors, primarily those utilizing allosteric transcription factors (aTFs) and two-component systems (TCSs). By integrating these regulatory sensing modules into engineered microbial chassis, researchers can achieve continuous, real-time biomarker monitoring even within complex and otherwise inaccessible physiological environments. This review particularly focuses on microbial chassis rather than mammalian systems due to their highly tractable genetics, rapid response kinetics, and their unique potential to be deployed as autonomous living probiotics for in situ theranostics. Furthermore, coupling these sensors with engineered actuator genes enables the construction of intelligent therapeutic genetic circuits. This closed-loop theranostic paradigm facilitates simultaneous, real-time diagnosis and autonomous, localized therapeutic interventions, paving the way for personalized and dose-adaptive precision medicine. Finally, we summarize recent advancements in these biosensor platforms, explore their applications in targeted disease interventions, and discuss the contemporary challenges alongside future perspectives for their clinical translation. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Grid-strength mirroring-driven seamless adaptive evolution control for PMSG wind turbines in ultra-weak grids: achieving phase-impedance-energy synergy
abstract: To address the transient impact issues caused by the lack of synchronous torque in direct-drive wind turbines under ultra-weak grids and the switching between grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM) control modes, an adaptive evolutionary control strategy based on real-time mirroring-driven grid strength is proposed. First, a frequency-adaptive improved recursive discrete Fourier transform (IRDFT) and a recursive least squares (RLS) algorithm are introduced to achieve millisecond-level simultaneous identification of grid impedance and inertia characteristics, thereby constructing a two-dimensional digital mirror of the grid in time and space. Second, an evaluation model of grid state of health (SOH) is established based on this mirror, generating a continuously differentiable nonlinear evolution factor to guide the grid connection characteristics from conventional passive phase-locked synchronization to flexible voltage-source synchronous evolution with active support capability. Meanwhile, the virtual reactance is dynamically reshaped using weighting factors to expand the system stability boundary, and combined with the feedforward compensation mechanism on the DC side to achieve adaptive allocation of reserve capacity, effectively balancing the power support strength under ultra-weak grids and the economic efficiency of power generation under strong-grid conditions. Simulation results show that under the extreme condition of a short-circuit ratio of 1.1, this strategy reduces the transient current impact during mode switching by 42.5%; compared with conventional grid-connection control, the 10-year net profit increases by 96.5%, achieving Pareto optimality in terms of safety and economy. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Controllable product selectivity in electrochemical nitrate reduction over CuCo2S4 catalyst
abstract: Electrochemical nitrate reduction (eNO3RR) offers a promising route for nitrate removal and conversion into value-added nitrogen products such as nitrite, hydroxylamine, ammonia, and dinitrogen. However, controlling product selectivity remains a major challenge, as the reaction pathway is highly sensitive to catalyst surface properties and operating conditions. Here, we address this challenge by demonstrating that selectivity can be systematically tuned through electronic structure of catalyst, applied potential and electrolyte-controlled reaction environments. In particular, the thiospinel CuCo2S4 catalyst exhibits unique active sites that regulate the adsorption and reduction of nitrate-derived intermediates, enabling selective ammonia formation. Comparative studies on respective monometallic sulfides reveal that CuS favors nitrite production, whereas CoS and CuCo2S4 show enhanced ammonia selectivity, highlighting the critical role of catalyst structure in directing reaction pathways. Beyond catalytic structure, applied potential and nitrate concentration further modulate selectivity. On CuS, ammonia selectivity increases from 44% to 88% as the potential shifts from 0.0 to −0.5 V vs. RHE. More importantly, nitrate concentration governs surface intermediate coverage, driving a transition in product distribution from hydroxylamine (47%) at ultra-low concentrations to ammonia (96%) at moderate concentrations (>0.05 M), and to N2 formation (64%) at high concentrations, reflecting a shift between hydrogenation and N–N coupling pathways. Within this framework, as synthesized CuCo2S4 catalyst coated electrode delivers outstanding performance, achieving 96.4 ± 1.8% ammonia selectivity, 83.6 ± 5.6% Faradaic efficiency, and an ammonia yield rate of 11.6 ± 1.0 mg h−1 cm−2 at −0.4 V vs. RHE. A sulfur re-enrichment strategy substantially restores catalytic activity by surface reconstruction. Overall, this work establishes catalyst design, reaction-condition engineering and surface reconstruction as key principles for tuning eNO3RR selectivity. © 2026

title: Uniform CO2-enriched microenvironment enabled by sequentially functionalized hollow double-shell structure for maximal active site utilization in CO2 electroreduction
abstract: Sequentially functionalized hollow multishell architectures typically boost catalysis via enhanced site exposure and reactant enrichment; however, their potential to modulate intrinsic activity through spatiotemporal ordering remains elusive and underexplored. Here, we demonstrate that the sequentially functionalized double-shell architecture homogenizes mass transport to establish a uniform microenvironment, which synchronizes the electronic structures of active sites for equivalent excitation and maximized collective utilization, thereby enhancing catalytic activity and selectivity. A double-shell nanotube catalyst was developed, in which the pyridinic-N-doped defective carbon inner shell enables efficient CO2 enrichment and supply within catalytic microenvironment, while the outer carbon shell hybridized with Ni single atoms and nanoparticles facilitates electrocatalytic CO2 reduction. COMSOL simulations reveal that temporal-spatial ordering enhances both the magnitude and spatial uniformity of local CO2 concentration at the active sites. This catalyst delivers enhanced CO2-to-CO activity and selectivity, achieving a CO partial current density of 496.5 mA cm–2 with Faradaic efficiency above 97.5% over 100–500 mA cm–2 in flow-cell, along with 145 h of stable operation at 100 mA cm−2 with FECO > 94% in an MEA. The mechanistic analyses reveal that the uniform CO2-enriched microenvironment homogenizes and optimizes the electronic structure of all active sites, lowering the *COOH formation barrier and promoting *CO desorption to enhance catalytic performance. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized role of temporal‑spatial ordering, offering a powerful design principle for advanced catalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Research on the fuzzy adaptive VSG-MPC coordinated control strategy considering regenerative braking
abstract: In urban rail transit AC/DC microgrids, the injection of regenerative braking energy from trains and power absorption by traction loads can cause severe fluctuations in DC-bus power. During bidirectional power-flow transitions, conventional virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control may exhibit delayed active-power response, pronounced DC-bus voltage fluctuations, and frequency deviations.To address these limitations, this paper proposes a coordinated control strategy integrating fuzzy adaptive parameter regulation with model predictive control. First, grid-forming VSG control is employed as the fundamental control scheme for the converter. The angular frequency deviation and its rate of change are used as inputs to a fuzzy controller, which regulates the virtual inertia and damping online. This improves the dynamic frequency support capability of the VSG under power disturbances.Second, an MPC prediction model is constructed based on the DC-bus energy state, and the equivalent VSG power-response time constant is updated online according to the adaptive inertia and damping coefficients to match the current VSG dynamics. Receding-horizon optimization of the active-power reference then stabilizes the DC-bus voltage and smooths bidirectional power regulation. MATLAB/Simulink simulations and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experiments demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively suppresses DC-bus voltage fluctuations and frequency deviations under inverter feedback, rectification-based energy absorption, and mode-transition conditions, while improving the dynamic active-power response of the VSG. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: IoT enabled deep learning and multi objective optimization of nanoPCM solar thermal energy storage for intelligent charging discharging control
abstract: Temporal differences between the availability of solar thermal energy and thermal requirements limit the effective utilization of solar thermal power, necessitating advanced thermal energy storage solutions. This study complemented the working performance of phase change material (PCM) based thermal energy storage system with the assistance of graphene nanoparticle and intelligent optimization approach.An experimentally studied PCM storage unit based on paraffin was embedded with a helical heat exchanger and tested under real outdoor conditions with graphene nanoparticle loadings of 0, 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5 wt%. The methodology is the combination of the experimental study and the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) surrogate modelling and multi-objective optimization with the assistance of NSGA-II in order to find Pareto-optimal operating conditions.Experimental evidence shows that the addition of graphene increases the charging rate of PCM by 30–35%, enhances stored energy by 10–18%, and extends useful discharge time by 25–30% compared to pure PCM. Improved performance of the energy storage is demonstrated by a drastic increase in cycle thermal efficiency (up to approximately 74%) and exergy efficiency and both quantitative and qualitative. The novelty of the work is that it integrates Nano-enhanced PCM and AI-controlled prediction and optimization of adaptive solar thermal energy systems.The combined forecasting–optimization approach improves discharge stability and energy recovery under varying solar conditions, highlighting the potential of smart Nano-PCM storage systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Interfacial layer-driven sliding ferroelectricity in MoS2
abstract: Two-dimensional sliding ferroelectricity offers a promising route toward ultrathin nonvolatile memory devices by enabling polarization control via interlayer sliding. However, scalable integration of interface-engineered structures remains challenging due to complex stacking and fabrication limitations. Here, we develop a controllable thermal-gradient chemical vapor deposition strategy for the one-step synthesis of homo-structured ABB- and AAB-MoS2 with integrated interfacial and ferroelectric layers. Hybrid 2H/3R-stacked MoS2 exhibits pronounced out-of-plane ferroelectricity governed by interlayer symmetry breaking and interfacial charge redistribution. Notably, the ferroelectric response is dictated by the position of the interfacial layer. AAB-MoS2 enables nonlocal propagation of the interfacial electric field, giving rise to proximity ferroelectricity across the entire trilayer, whereas ABB-MoS2 results in a spatially confined interfacial field and layer-confined polarization. Vertical Au/MoS2/Co devices exhibit a switchable diode effect, in which interfacial layer positioning governs the Schottky barrier height via polarization switching. This work establishes stacking-engineered MoS2 as a platform for uncovering ferroelectric mechanisms and advancing ultrathin nonvolatile memory devices. © 2026

title: Vanishing viscosity method for a class of second order Clarke subdifferential inclusions
abstract: We study a coupled system consisting of a second-order subdifferential inclusion, in which the multivalued term is given by the Clarke subdifferential of a locally Lipschitz function and an ordinary differential equation (ODE). The studied system arises from a contact problem involving a viscoelastic body and involves two operators related to viscosity and elasticity effects. The coercivity of the viscosity operator plays a crucial role in establishing the existence result for the viscoelastic problem. In addition, we consider an elastic case in which the viscosity operator is absent, leading to a loss of coercivity. To address this difficulty, we introduce a vanishing viscosity regularization and analyze the associated approximating problem. Using known results in the coercive setting, we establish existence for the regularized system, derive uniform a priori estimates, and pass to the limit to obtain a solution to the noncoercive problem. The approach extends previous results on hemivariational inequalities (HVIs) to a coupled HVI–ODE system and provides an alternative to discretization methods, with applications in contact mechanics and systems with evolving internal state variables describing adhesion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Surrogate-model-assisted optimization of centrifugal pump-as-turbine impellers: A systematic review and structured evidence synthesis
abstract: Impeller redesign can improve the turbine-mode performance of centrifugal pumps, but direct optimization with high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics is expensive. This review critically evaluates the evidence for surrogate-model-assisted optimization of centrifugal pump-as-turbine impellers. The revision followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for literature searches in systematic reviews reporting principles and used Synthesis Without Meta-analysis because the available studies did not report commensurate study-level uncertainty estimates. A reproducibility audit verified nine eligible studies published from 2015 to 2024. Artificial neural network families were most common; single studies used Kriging and support vector machine high-dimensional model representation, and one study used response surface methodology. Reported efficiency improvements from baseline to optimized designs were generally specific to the operating point. Directly comparable principal-point gains were generally about 2–6%, including 2.28–2.91% for genetic algorithm–backpropagation neural-network workflows, 3.8% for Kriging at the best-efficiency flow, 5.74% for a radial basis function neural-network and nondominated sorting genetic algorithm II workflow, and a 3.4% experimentally measured gain for support vector machine high-dimensional model representation; one multi-condition artificial neural network study reported larger point-specific gains of 8.67–13.1%. These results support a typical design-point improvement on the order of 4%, but they do not support a universal pooled effect or a model ranking. Computational savings were consistently attributed to replacing repeated computational fluid dynamics calls with surrogate evaluations, yet the reporting was insufficient to justify the previously claimed 45:1 ratio or a universal cost reduction. The evidence, therefore, supports surrogate assistance as a sample-efficient design strategy, while model choice should be based on dimensionality, data volume, validation rigor, and the need for uncertainty quantification. © 2026 The Authors. title: Electronegativity drives charge polarization in indium single-atom catalysts for low-overpotential CO2 electroreduction
abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction to formate is limited by high overpotentials and competing reactions. Herein, we report an indium single-atom catalyst that modulates the adsorption geometry of CO2 by engineering the charge state of the active site. The optimized catalyst achieves a Faradaic efficiency (FE) for formate of 93.5% at −0.6 V vs. RHE in a flow cell with 400 mV overpotential and maintains high selectivity across a wide potential window (-0.6 to −0.9 V). The overpotential of formate is highly sensitive to the initial dispersion of In atoms causing optimal CO2 adsorption and fast electron transfer, and increases significantly when In clusters/particles become predominant species. In situ characterizations and theoretical calculations indicate that oxygen-coordinated isolated In sites induce significant interfacial charge polarization, which preferentially stabilizes a bidentate O-bound adsorption configuration of CO2-derived intermediates through strong In-O interactions and thereby enables highly selective conversion to formate. This work identifies electronegativity as a key descriptor for controlling intermediate adsorption on p-block single-atom catalysts and provides insights into the rational design of selective CO2RR electrocatalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Qualitative Analysis of the Circuits of Au-Tonomous Inverters with Shut-off Valves; [Сөндіру клапандары бар автономды инверторлық схемасының сапалық талдауы]; [Качественный анализ схем автономных инверторов с запорными клапанами]
abstract: The article presents the results of a qualitative analysis of circuits of autonomous current and voltage inverters with cut-off valves. The influence of the charge on the switching capacitor in parallel and series equivalent circuits on the restoration of the switching properties of the thyristors in the inverter power circuit is studied. It is shown that, due to the energy periodically accumulated in the inductive elements of the load, the voltage across the switching capacitor in the cut-off state is higher than in a conventional parallel autonomous current inverter. This ensures increased switching stability of the inverter. Consequently, the circuit of an autonomous current inverter with cut-off valves remains operational in valve converters for variable-frequency electric drives and maintains performance during sudden load surges and short circuits, since the voltage on the switching capacitor does not depend on the load voltage. Thus, the charge on the switching capacitor is preserved even when the load voltage drops sharply between thyristor commutations. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Digital modeling for rapid prediction and multi-objective optimization of the entire microstructure and property fields of complex components in die forging
abstract: Die forging components used in high-end manufacturing have complex geometries and many interacting process variables, complicating accurate prediction and control of the entire microstructure and properties. This work proposes a method integrating finite element simulations, a limited number of forging experiments, and machine learning to enable rapid and precise prediction and optimization of die forging component's entire microstructure and property. First, finite element simulations were conducted under 114 different sets of process parameters. The deformation physical quantities (mean deformation temperature, mean strain rate, mean equivalent stress, and equivalent strain throughout the forging process) were obtained at 100 feature points on the forgings. Using forging process parameters and feature point coordinates as inputs, deformation physical quantity prediction models (DPQ models) were established employing the gradient boosting algorithm. Next, forging experiments were conducted under 16 different sets of process parameters. The microstructure and properties were measured at six sampling points in forging samples, including grain size, recrystallization volume fraction, grain aspect ratio, and hardness. Using deformation physical quantities as inputs, microstructure and property prediction models (MP models) were developed employing the random forest algorithm. The DPQ and MP models were then connected in series and combined with thin plate spline interpolation to enable rapid prediction of forging's entire microstructure and property fields. Prediction time is on the order of seconds, with errors below 10%. For forging process parameters optimization, a multi-objective optimization method based on a genetic algorithm was developed to achieve grain refinement, hardness improvement, and homogenization of grain size and hardness. This work offers valuable insights and methodological references for real-time prediction and intelligent control of the microstructure and properties of die forgings. © 2026

title: Laser slicing of 4H-SiC wafers with different doping types: Multiscale mechanism investigation and deep learning-based processing strategy
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) is the core substrate material for next-generation high-voltage power devices and high-frequency radio-frequency electronics, while wafer slicing remains a critical bottleneck constraining its low-cost, high-yield manufacturing. Conventional diamond wire sawing suffers from severe kerf loss and serious subsurface damage; ultrafast laser slicing technology represents a revolutionary alternative to traditional wire sawing, yet the pivotal regulatory effect of doping type on optical absorption and energy deposition remains unrevealed. This study comprehensively employs experimental characterization, first-principles calculations, and the two-temperature model to systematically investigate the multiscale mechanisms of ultrafast laser slicing of 4H-SiC wafers with different doping types, elucidating the regulatory laws of dopant elements on laser energy absorption, free-carrier excitation, carrier-lattice coupling, and crack propagation behavior. A deep learning-based process optimization framework is proposed, and a conditional neural network model based on feature-wise linear modulation is constructed, taking material resistivity, focal depth, and doping type as inputs to accurately predict critical process parameters including laser power, scanning speed, and hatch spacing. With model-optimized parameters, the exfoliated surface roughness of samples is significantly reduced to below 0.4 μm. The coefficient of determination (R2) on the test set exceeds 0.97, achieving adaptive optimization of process parameters for wafers with different doping types. This study provides systematic theoretical interpretation and intelligent process solutions for low-damage, high-precision laser slicing of 4H-SiC wafers. © 2026

title: Thermomechanical and functional performance of fully bio-based formulations from lentil flour and aquafaba
abstract: Developing sustainable bioplastics from whole pulse flours presents a complex macromolecular challenge due to the interpenetrating networks of starch and proteins, which differ significantly from isolated protein matrices. This study investigates whole lentil flour and its spray-dried cooking water (aquafaba) as renewable feedstocks, for injection-moulded bioplastics, addressing the valorisation of food industry by-products. Thus, prexisting structural alterations in aquafaba (induced by its hydrothermal extraction) could synergistically modulate starch gelatinization and protein cross-linking during subsequent thermomechanical processing. Formulations with varying lentil flour:glycerol ratios (85:15 to 70:30) and aquafaba replacements (0–20 g/100g, at constant 20% glycerol) were processed via thermomechanical mixing and injection moulding. DSC confirmed thermal stability above 150°C, guiding moulding at 120°C. Specific mechanical energy (SME) significantly decreased with both higher glycerol and aquafaba addition, as aquafaba acted as an internal lubricant that improved processability without sacrificing mechanical performance. While water uptake increased with lentil flour, 20% aquafaba replacement yielded water uptake comparable to the 85:15 formulation while providing substantially higher strain at break (from 2.1 to 3.7%). DMA showed that aquafaba reduced the elastic modulus (from 184.9 to 96.5 Pa) and increased frequency dependence (n′ from 0.11 to 0.165), consistent with a plasticizing effect. FTIR revealed a decreased amide I/amide II ratio, indicating greater protein denaturation, and an increased 1025/990 cm−1 ratio, reflecting reduced carbohydrate crystallinity due to the interactions between native flour starch and aquafaba co-solutes. These findings provide a novel pathway for utilizing whole pulse flours and industrial by-products to manufacture stable, high-performance biodegradable thermoplastics for active food packaging. © 2026 The Authors. title: Accelerated reaction dynamics in engineered multifunctional nanodomains for efficient photothermal ammonia synthesis
abstract: Prospects for a sustainable economic and ecological growth identify the ammonia economy as a pivotal facilitator for future energy transition. Herein, we demonstrate that FeCo co-doped N,S-modified Ti3C2 MXene with in-situ derived TiO2-x nanoparticles (or FeCo-CNS-TM) achieves efficient photothermal catalytic ammonia synthesis from nitrogen and water vapor (100 mW cm–2, 350 °C), yielding a production rate of 1769.8 μmol g–1 h–1. In this catalyst, FeCo bimetallic nanoclusters enrich energetic photoelectrons from both TiO2-x and Ti3C2 MXene, and then bimetallic synergy promotes N2 side-on adsorption and electron donation, enabling effective N2 activation and reduction. Meanwhile, TiO2-x and hydrophilic groups on MXene preferentially interact with water molecules and produce protons, preventing the competitive water adsorption and poisoning of FeCo active sites, thereby ensuring high efficiency and selectivity of ammonia synthesis reaction. Such multifunctional nanodomains provide a viable approach for designing highly active and stable photothermal catalysts for green NH3 synthesis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Hardness convergence enables ductilization of flash-heated high-carbon martensitic steel via two-stage tempering
abstract: Flash quench-tempering is an efficient route for producing ultrahigh-strength high-carbon martensitic steels by refining the martensitic framework and retaining a high defect density. However, further improving ductility without sacrificing ultrahigh strength remains challenging because non-equilibrium carbon distribution generates microscale mechanical heterogeneity and promotes strain localization. Here, we propose a two-stage tempering strategy to ductilize a flash-heated high-carbon low-alloy martensitic steel without sacrificing strength. Compared with the flash quench-tempered (QT) steel, which exhibited a yield strength of ∼2067 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength of ∼2254 MPa, and a total elongation of ∼7.5%, the secondary-tempered steel, hereafter referred to as QTT steel, maintained comparable strength while increasing the total elongation to ∼11.1%. Microstructural characterization revealed continued carbide evolution from η-Fe2C to θ-Fe3C, while the martensitic block size and dislocation density were both largely retained. Nanoindentation mapping demonstrated a clear convergence of local hardness after secondary tempering, as evidenced by the decrease in the fraction of high-hardness indents above 12 GPa from 19% to 3.5% and the reduction in hardness standard deviation from 3.1 to 1.8 GPa. High-resolution micro-digital image correlation (μ-DIC) further revealed reduced microscale strain heterogeneity after secondary tempering, indicating improved deformation compatibility. This enhanced ductility is attributed to hardness convergence and improved deformation compatibility rather than global martensite softening. These findings establish two-stage tempering as a practical strategy for ductilizing flash-heated ultrahigh-strength martensitic steels by tailoring local mechanical gradients. © 2026

title: Analytical Review of the Methods of Studying Open Pit Slope Stability Under the Conditions of Mining Operations Digitalization; [Тау-кен жұмыстарын цифрландыру жағдайында карьерлік беткейлердің тұрақтылығын зерттеу әдістеріне аналитикалық шолу]; [Аналитический обзор методов исследования устойчивости карьерных откосов в условиях цифровизации горных работ]
abstract: Open-pit slope stability is one of the key factors determining the safety and efficiency of open-pit mining operations. With increasing pit depth, growing complexity of rock mass structure, and intensification of mining activities, the need for advanced methods for studying slope stability based on digital technologies is steadily increasing. The aim of this study is to systematize and comparatively analyze modern methods for investigating open-pit slope stability, taking into account their capabilities and limitations under mining conditions. The paper presents an analytical review of computational geomechanical approaches, geodetic instrumental methods, terrestrial laser scanning, UAV-based photogrammetry, and satellite radar interferometry (InSAR). A comparative analysis of these methods is performed based on key parameters, including data type, spatial coverage, and capabilities for deformation analysis. The results show that each method has specific advantages and limitations related to data characteristics, observation conditions, and analytical potential. It is established that none of the methods, when used individually, provides a complete and reliable description of slope stability. The highest level of informativeness is achieved through the integration of different methods within comprehensive analytical approaches. The results of this study provide a systematic understanding of the role of modern digital methods in slope stability research and confirm the перспективность of developing integrated digital systems for monitoring and assessing open-pit slope stability. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Modeling the impact of diffusion, Non-Darcy flow, and solubility on core-scale CO2 injection
abstract: Reliable forecasting of CO2 injection behavior demands an accurate description of the fundamental transport and flow mechanisms active within porous media. This work examines how molecular diffusion, non-Darcy flow effects, and CO2 solubility in the aqueous phase collectively shape oil displacement efficiency and flow characteristics at the core scale. To achieve high-fidelity predictive capability, Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM) were integrated with advanced hyperparameter-optimization strategies. Model robustness was assessed through K-fold cross-validation, while SHAP revealed CO2 solubility as the most influential factor governing the recovery factor. Among all tested configurations, the GBM-GPO model delivered the strongest performance, achieving an R2 of 0.9951 and an AARE% of 0.5952, surpassing other machine-learning pipelines. The results demonstrate that hybrid optimization–enhanced ML frameworks not only provide prediction exactness but also yield physically meaningful insights. © 2026 The Authors. title: Engineering W/Mo-modified Ni3S2 with local crystalline/disordered interfacial domains for efficient alkaline hydrogen evolution
abstract: The rational engineering of crystalline/disordered interfacial domains with tailored electronic properties represents a promising strategy for developing high-performance electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, a three-dimensional self-supported W/Mo-modified Ni3S2-based electrocatalyst with local crystalline/disordered interfacial domains (Ni3S2@W:Mo-0.2:0.2) is fabricated through a facile hydrothermal strategy. Structural characterizations support the coexistence of crystalline Ni3S2 domains and adjacent Ni-containing W/Mo/O-associated disordered regions, while the combined experimental and theoretical results suggest interfacial electronic regulation and enhanced alkaline HER kinetics. The local interfacial structure is associated with interfacial charge-transfer behavior. Consequently, the electrode requires an average overpotential of 101.00 ± 1.73 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH, together with improved apparent kinetics, reduced charge-transfer resistance, and stable operation at 100 mA cm−2 for 100 h. The enhanced activity arises from the combined contributions of accessible surface area, ECSA-normalized apparent specific activity, and charge-transfer kinetics. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggest modulated H* adsorption energetics and a lower water dissociation barrier. Gas chromatography (GC) analysis quantitatively confirms sustained H2 generation. This work provides insights into interfacial engineering and electronic structure regulation for advanced electrocatalyst design. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Purification of metallic ions from technological solutions before sorption recovery of rhenium under JSC Almalyk MMC; [Алмалық ТКМК АҚ жағдайында ренийді сорбциялық жолмен бөліп алу алдында технологиялық ерітінділерді металл иондарынан тазарту]; [Очистка технологических растворов от ионов металлов перед сорбционным извлечением рения в АО Алмалыкский ГМК]
abstract: In this article, rhenium’s distinct physicochemical characteristics, which make it essential for petrochemistry, electrical technology, rocket and aviation engineering, and the manufacturing of catalysts and high-precision tools, account for the metal's rising demand. The main source of rhenium at JSC "Almalyk MMC" is the off-gases produced when molybdenum concentrates are roasted, where rhenium is mostly found as Re2O7. High selectivity and overall efficiency are ensured by optimizing the process parameters at each of the multiple subsequent technical phases involved in rhenium recovery. Perrhenate sorption is less efficient when organic molecules and Mn²⁺ and Cu²⁺ ions are present in the process fluids. Oxidative-precipitation techniques were used for the first purification: Mn ions were oxidized and precipitated using potassium permanganate, and Cu2+ ions were selectively precipitated using an ammonium sulfide solution (NH4)2S. ICP-OES was used to assess the composition of the solutions, while SEM and EDS were used to examine the roasting gas-dust products. Using contemporary analytical methods, a thorough investigation of the relevant phases of selective purification was conducted for the first time at JSC "Almalyk MMC." It was shown that treating the solutions with KMnO4 and (NH4)2S efficiently eliminates interfering elements without causing rhenium or molybdenum losses, thereby creating ideal conditions for the sorption of perrhenate ions later on. Manganese and copper concentrations dropped from 1.44 to 0.0039 and 2.68 to 0.0036 g/l, respectively, demonstrating the great purification process efficiency. Rhenium and molybdenum concentrations did not alter during these phases, suggesting that they were fully preserved. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Synergistic bulk-gradient and surface-dual-doping design for Co-free Li-rich cathodes
abstract: Cobalt-free lithium-rich layered oxides (LLOs) are critical enablers for next-generation lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) with high energy density, low cost, and environmental sustainability. However, cobalt elimination retards oxygen activation and reaction kinetics, while triggering severe structural and surficial degradation. Herein, a versatile design of Co-free LLOs combining bulk gradient and surface Al/Mg dual-doping is proposed. While the bulk gradient affords an active core and robust shell, surface dual-doping not only adjusts atomic structures but also regulates the in situ constructions of a Ni-rich spinel-like layer and disordered nanodomains. This integrated design simultaneously boosts mechanical integrity by approximately 33% and suppresses oxygen release. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers a high initial discharge capacity of ∼283.5 mAh g−1 and retains a remarkable capacity retention of 86.8% alongside minor voltage fade of ∼0.26 mV/cycle over 500 cycles, which facilitates the fabrication of high-performance pouch cells. This study offers a viable route toward high-energy, low-cost, and eco-sustainable Co-free LLOs cathodes for next-generation LIBs. © 2026 Chinese Society of Metals

title: Development of a methodology for microstructural and thermal verification of the quality of an industrial Ti-10V-2Fe-3Al triple vacuum arc remelted ingot; [Ti-10V-2Fe-3Al титан қорытпасының үш мәрте вакуумды-доғалық қайта балқыту арқылы алынған өнеркәсіптік құймасының сапасын микрокұрылымдық және термиялық верификациялау әдістемесін әзірлеу]; [Разработка методики микроструктурной и термической верификации качества промышленного слитка Ti-10V-2Fe-3Al тройного вакуумно-дугового переплава]
abstract: The article is devoted to the development of a methodology for microstructural and thermal verification of the quality of an industrial Ti-10V-2Fe-3Al triple vacuum arc remelted ingot produced by UK TMP JSC. It was established that all zones of the ingot demonstrate a two-stage thermal evolution characteristic of the β-metastable Ti-10V-2Fe-3Al alloy: decomposition of the metastable β phase (≈520–570 °C) and an endothermic α→β phase transformation (≈950–1120 °C). It was found that the enthalpy of the exothermic decomposition of the β matrix increases by approximately 60–80% in the lower zone of the ingot. The width of the phase transition (ΔT) correlates with an increase in microsegregation. It was also determined that the enthalpy of the endothermic α→β transformation decreases from the bottom part of the ingot toward the steady-state crystallization zone (Middle-1), which correlates with a reduction in the microsegregation parameters obtained from SEM–EDS profiles (ΔC_max, σC, Lcorr). Thus, thermal analysis confirms the absence of a pronounced vertical gradient of structural stability and can be used as a validating criterion for the integral electrode quality index. For the first time, a quantitative correlation between SEM–EDS profiles and DSC–DTG characteristics has been proposed. Thermal analysis is suggested as an independent validator of microsegregation. An approach to the quantitative evaluation of microsegregation based on SEM–EDS profiles using the parameters ΔC_max, σC, Lcorr, and ΔCO(local) has been developed. Additionally, the use of an integral chemical index Ichem, and a critical threshold Icritchem is proposed for electrode quality control using thermal analysis results. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Investigation of the Structure and Composition of TiN and CrN Coatings as a Function of Deposition Parameters; [TiN және CrN жабындарының құрылымы мен құрамын тұндыру параметрлеріне байланысты зерттеу]; [Исследование структуры и состава покрытий TiN и CrN в зависимости от параметров осаждения]
abstract: Addressing corrosion and wear in assemblies, components, machine parts, and equipment operating in aggressive environments under severe wear conditions remains a pressing challenge and continues to draw focused scientific attention. This work aimed to investigate how the key magnetron sputtering parameters (working pressure, plasma current, and process-gas flow rates) affect the surface morphology, microstructure, and composition of TiN and CrN films deposited under different conditions. Microstructural analysis revealed that, across the investigated parameter window, the films exhibit a columnar cross-sectional architecture and a smooth surface morphology with no visible defects, showing no pronounced differences between the deposition regimes. After 30 min of deposition, the film thickness ranged from 0.17 to 0.46 μm for TiN and from 0.59 to 3.46 μm for CrN, depending on the sputtering conditions. The results demonstrate that plasma current and working pressure have a strong effect on film thickness and chemical composition, whereas variations in the working-gas flow rate exert a coupled influence on thickness, microstructure, and the stoichiometry of TiN and CrN layers. Elemental analysis further indicates that increasing the pressure to 0.65 Pa increases oxygen incorporation in the films. During chromium sputtering, raising the plasma current to 1.5 A leads to film delamination. For TiN, a balanced regime with a moderate N2 flow is preferable, providing a reasonable growth rate and a composition close to stoichiometric. For CrN, the range of stable operating conditions is substantially broader, and the process parameters have a more pronounced impact on its structure and composition. These findings can support the design of TiN/CrN wear-resistant multilayer coatings produced by magnetron sputtering for protecting machine parts and equipment against wear and corrosion. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Recent advances in covalent organic frameworks-based S-scheme photocatalysts
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have drawn considerable interest in photocatalysis owing to their π‑conjugated networks, large specific surface areas, and adjustable pore structures. However, single‑component COFs are constrained by rapid photo-generated charge recombination and insufficient redox driving forces, which hamper their catalytic efficiency. Constructing S‑scheme heterostructures by coupling COFs with suitable semiconductors can facilitate charge separation and boost both oxidation and reduction capacities. This review first outlines the evolution of S‑scheme heterojunctions and the regulation principles of interfacial charge carrier migration. Subsequently, COFs are categorized according to their linkages and building blocks. Then, the synthesis strategies and characterization approaches of COF‑based S‑scheme heterostructures, along with the applications in photocatalytic H2 production, H2O2 synthesis, CO2 reduction, organic conversion, and pollutant degradation, are reviewed. Lastly, to address the remaining challenges, we propose several recommendations, including strengthening interfacial bonding, enhancing durability, lowering costs, and incorporating multiple advanced characterization techniques, to facilitate the fabrication of high-efficiency photocatalytic systems. © 2026

title: Transformer partial discharge identification via supervised contrastive learning and Multi-scale perceptual networks
abstract: Accurate partial discharge (PD) identification is essential for the operational integrity of traction transformers in electrified railways, yet intense electromagnetic interference and similar discharge patterns often diminish diagnostic robustness. This study proposes a framework integrating supervised contrastive learning with a Multi-scale Perceptual Network (MSDP-Net) to enhance diagnostic reliability. A dual-view adaptive augmentation strategy, involving Gaussian noise injection and temporal shuffling, is first applied to improve invariant representation learning. The physics-informed MSDP-Net utilizes a morphological branch with dilated convolutions for long-range envelopes and an instantaneous branch with singularity-aware operators for energy mutation detection. Supervised contrastive learning is then employed to optimize the latent feature space, strengthening intra-class compactness. Additionally, a new electromagnetic pulse amplitude sequence dataset is established and publicly released to address the scarcity of PD benchmarks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 98.42% identification accuracy across four typical defects, surpassing both general-purpose deep architectures and re-implemented PD-specific strategies. To exclude session-level information leakage, run-wise group-wise and leave-one-run-out cross-validation, in which all pulses of a given experimental run are confined to either the training or the test partition, are additionally conducted and retain 97.29% and 96.88% accuracy respectively. The framework exhibits exceptional robustness in high-noise environments, significantly outperforming current state-of-the-art models and offering a more reliable solution for railway power supply monitoring. Finally, a complexity analysis shows that the framework requires only 0.0882 GFLOPs and 0.94 ms per-pulse inference latency, and that the contrastive projection head is discarded at inference and therefore adds no deployment cost. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Research and Improvement of Methods for Predicting Hidden Fracturing in a Rock Mass at a Polymetallic Mine; [Полиметалл кенішінде тау жыныстары массивінің жасырын жарықшақтылығын болжау әдістерін зерттеу және жетілдіру]; [Исследование и совершенствование методов прогноза скрытой трещиноватости горного массива на полиметаллическом руднике]
abstract: This paper presents the results of a study aimed at improving the reliability of predicting hidden fracturing in the near-contour rock mass adjacent to underground mine workings at a polymetallic mine. The relevance of the study is associated with the fact that hidden discontinuities are not always identified during conventional visual inspection of the rock mass, which increases the risk of local collapses and complicates the selection of support parameters. The work aimed to improve methods for predicting hidden fracturing through the integrated application of ground-penetrating radar profiling, three-dimensional surveying, spatial fracture mapping, and geomechanical modeling. The study included analysis of the mining and geological conditions of the deposit, laser scanning of mine working sections, spatial fracture analysis in ShapeMetriX, numerical modeling in RocTunnel3, and GPR profiling using the GROT 12N system. It was established that the highest reliability of hidden fracturing prediction is achieved through the sequential integration of 3D survey data, spatial fracture analysis, and GPR investigation. The practical effect of the proposed approach lies in improving the validity of selecting existing support schemes rather than introducing new support types. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: A unified Cu-solvation and redox model for standard SCR on Cu-CHA: Explaining seagull-shaped light-off and driving-cycle performance
abstract: NH3-assisted Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) over Cu-Chabazite (CHA) proceeds via redox cycling of NH3-solvated Cu(I)/Cu(II) ions, with the Cu solvation state governing the shift between low- and high-temperature mechanisms. Despite considerable progress, existing dual-cycle models do not fully reconcile NH3 solvation effects, in-situ spectroscopic data, and real-world catalyst behaviour. This work introduces a triple-cycle SCR model featuring three parallel redox cycles involving highly-solvated, partly-solvated, and bare Cu ions, whose relative distribution is determined by an experiment-derived NH3 solvation model. For the calibration of redox kinetics, we then propose a novel method which combines steady-state conversion and Cu oxidation-state quantification during SCR, aligned with industrial practice. The model accurately reproduces the characteristic “seagull” NO conversion profile under various experimental conditions. We report the experimental observation of a similar seagull profile also in the Cu oxidation state during SCR, as confirmed by UV-Vis spectroscopy. The model correctly reproduces this trend as well, confirming proper repartition between reduction and oxidation paths, as validated with half-cycle transient experiments. Finally, to the best of the author's knowledge, this work presents the first application of a redox-based SCR model to the simulation of driving cycles, marking a significant advance toward chemically-consistent reactor models for real-world after treatment applications. © 2026

title: Effect of κ-carrageenan and chitosan modification on curcumin-perilla seed oil composite liposomes
abstract: To address the issues of poor stability and low bioavailability of curcumin and perilla seed oil, this study employed the ethanol injection method to prepare composite liposomes. These liposomes were sequentially modified with a single layer of chitosan (0.2%) and a double layer of κ-carrageenan (0.04%). The physicochemical properties, membrane characteristics, environmental tolerance, and in vitro digestibility of the liposomes before and after modification were systematically evaluated. The results showed that after double-layer modification, the liposomes achieved an encapsulation efficiency of 95.27%, with a particle size of 318.5 nm and a zeta potential of +36.92 mV, exhibiting a distinct core-shell structure. FTIR and Raman spectroscopy confirmed that the polysaccharides interacted with the liposomes via electrostatic forces and hydrogen bonding without disrupting the ordered arrangement of the phospholipid bilayer. The double-layer modification significantly increased the phase transition temperature (75.18 °C) and colloidal stability of the liposomes. In vitro digestion experiments showed that, at the end of intestinal digestion, the cumulative release rate of curcumin from the double-layer-modified liposomes was 59.84%, and the release of free fatty acids was 44.58%; both values were significantly lower than those of the unmodified liposomes, demonstrating excellent sustained-release performance. In this study, using curcumin-perilla seed oil composite liposomes as a model system, the feasibility of the κ-carrageenan-chitosan double-layer modification strategy in enhancing liposome stability and controlled-release performance was validated, providing new insights into the co-delivery of hydrophobic bioactive compounds and functional oils. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Synthesis Process of Silica–Activated Carbon Composite Ceramic Membranes for Integrated Filtration and Adsorption in Acid Mine Drainage; [Қышқыл шахта ағындыларын кешенді сүзу және адсорбциялау үшін кремний диоксиді мен белсендірілген көмірден композиттік керамикалық мембраналарды синтездеу процесі]; [Процесс синтеза композитных керамических мембран из диоксида кремния и активированного угля для комплексной фильтрации и адсорбции кислых шахтных стоков]
abstract: Acid Mine Drainage (AMD) is a liquid waste from coal mining by-products. AMD is a highly corrosive liquid (pH 1.5 – 4.0) and contains heavy metals, which is one of the problems in coal mining. Filtration technology using ceramic membranes can offer greater corrosion resistance than other membranes. Therefore, the study aims to fabricate and characterize composite ceramic membranes made from silica extracted from rice husk ash (RHA) and modified with high-performance activated carbon (Maxsorb III) to boost heavy metal adsorption capacity. The membranes are produced through extrusion molding and stepwise sintering processes. The results were analyzed using SEM-EDS, XRF, XRD, and BET. XRF analysis showed that the silica purity increased from 88.42 to 98.62 wt%, while XRD confirmed a predominantly amorphous structure with a broad peak centered at approximately 22° (2θ). SEM-EDS revealed the formation and distribution of pores, with Si, O, and C as the main elements. Increasing the activated carbon content from 10 to 20 wt% increased the BET specific surface area from 238 to 412 m²/g and the average pore diameter from 16 to 25 nm, indicating increased pore development and surface area. These results indicate that activated carbon effectively modifies the porous structure and textural properties of the ceramic membrane. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Proton-rich interfacial microenvironment engineering enables efficient and durable hydrogen evolution over Ru/metal (hydr)oxide catalysts
abstract: The intrinsically sluggish kinetics of the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) are largely associated with limited proton availability in alkaline media. To accelerate the Volmer kinetic step and alleviate pH dependence, we report a Ru3 + hydrolysis-driven impregnation strategy for constructing localized acidic and proton-enriched interfaces. Using Ru@Ni(OH)2 as a model catalyst, Ru species are anchored onto oxygen-vacancy-rich Ni(OH)2 nanosheets. Operando Raman spectroscopy combined with theoretical calculations reveals that Ru sites promote water dissociation process and act as proton capture centers, thereby facilitating the formation of hydronium ions (H3O+) species. The resulting interfacial microenvironment balances hydrogen adsorption strength and accelerates HER kinetics. As a result, the Ru@Ni(OH)2 catalyst delivers ultralow overpotentials of 50 mV at -10 mA cm-2 and 364 mV at -2800 mA cm-2, together with sustained operation over 1200 h at -100 mA cm-2. This synthesis approach can be readily applied to a wide range of transition-metal and rare-earth (hydro)oxide systems. This work establishes interfacial proton regulation as an effective strategy and provides a broadly applicable framework for designing high-performance electrocatalysts with accelerated reaction kinetics. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Interface engineering: Enhanced oxidation resistance of Cr/CrTaAl multilayered coating exposed to 1000 °C steam
abstract: In this study, a crystalline/amorphous Cr/CrTaAl multilayered coating with equal layer thickness of 50 nm, as well as the amorphous CrTaAl and pure Cr coatings, were deposited on zircaloy substrates via magnetron sputtering, subsequently exposed to 1000 °C steam to investigate their oxidation behavior and the structural evolution of oxide scales. The amorphous CrTaAl coating exhibited limited oxidation resistance comparable to that of the Cr coating, while its degradation was mainly driven by the extensive phase separation within the amorphous coating upon O penetration and the insufficient retardation of O diffusion by the thin Cr2O3 layer and adjacent Ta2O5 layer. In contrast, the heterogeneous interfaces and tailored elemental diffusion kinetics synergistically dominate the oxidation process in Cr/CrTaAl multilayered coating, resulting in a gradually thickened Cr2O3 outer oxide layer with multilayered Al2O3 formed at the interfaces. This hierarchical oxide structure functions as an effective diffusion barrier for impeding O penetration and confers superior oxidation resistance on the Cr/CrTaAl multilayered coating than single layer coatings. Moreover, the detailed microstructure evolution during oxidation and the underlying failure mechanisms were unraveled. These findings provide critical insights into the microstructural design of advanced multilayered coatings for enhanced oxidation resistance in nuclear fuel cladding applications. © 2026

title: Stepwise identification method for SVG fault ride-through control parameters in multiple solution spaces
abstract: Accurately obtaining the controller parameters of the Static Var Generator (SVG) is crucial for modeling new energy stations and analyzing grid-connected characteristics. However, due to the lack of observation characteristics and the coupling between the control loop parameters, all the parameters that are identified together in the entire solution space easily cause large errors. Given this, a stepwise identification method for SVG fault ride-through control parameters in multiple solution spaces is proposed. First, the maximum information coefficient is used to analyze the correlation between the control parameters and observations. The control parameters are divided into multiple solution spaces for decoupling, and the stepwise identification order is determined according to the difference in parameter sensitivity in each solution space. Second, in multiple solution spaces, the observed features are used to train the XGBoost algorithm to optimize the initial values of the control parameters. The IHHO algorithm is employed for the precise identification of the SVG fault ride-through control parameters. Finally, through hardware-in-the-loop testing, the effectiveness and adaptability of the proposed method were verified under various operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Application of bank protection structures for regulation of channel processes in the lower reaches of the Shu River; [Шу өзенінің төменгі ағысындағы арналық процестерді реттеу үшін жағалауды қорғау құрылымдарын қолдану]; [Применение берегозащитных сооружений для регулирования русловых процессов реки Шу в нижнем течении]
abstract: The article presents the application of bank protection structures for regulating channel processes in the lower reaches of the Shu River under conditions of high hydrological variability. The analysis is based on long-term hydrological observations conducted at the Tashutkul (Tasotkel) hydrological station over the period 1967–2022. A statistical assessment of annual maximum and mean discharges, including measures of variability, skewness, and exceedance probability, revealed the occurrence of rare but extreme flood events that significantly influence channel deformation and bank erosion in reaches composed of sandy–gravel alluvial deposits. A probabilistic hydrological analysis was applied to justify the design hydraulic loads acting on river training structures. Based on the identified hydrological and morphological risks, an improved prefabricated modular floating bank protection spur was developed for river engineering and channel regulation. The proposed structure provides adjustable permeability, promotes flow energy dissipation, and reduces local scour intensity under different flow conditions. The obtained results may be applied in the design and operation of adaptive bank protection structures for the lower reaches of the Shu River and other rivers characterized by pronounced channel instability and hydrological variability. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Self-sacrificial in-situ carboxylation for dynamic donor-acceptor optimization in metal-free photothermal catalytic H2O2 synthesis
abstract: The static donor-acceptor (D-A) architectures of conventional organic photocatalysts are poorly adapted to the dynamically evolving redox environment of photoelectrochemical interfaces, leading to exciton trapping and progressive catalytic site deactivation. While pre-synthetic functionalization can tune frontier orbital levels, it produces fixed configurations that cannot adapt to operational degradation or fluctuating interfacial potentials during catalysis. Here we report a self-sacrificial dynamic optimization strategy, in which hydroxymethyl groups undergo photothermal oxidative dehydrogenation to form electron-withdrawing carboxyl functionalities in-situ, enabling operando reconfiguration of D-A push-pull structures for enhanced catalytic function. This in-situ carboxylation scavenges photogenerated holes, suppresses early-stage recombination, and promotes exciton dissociation by withdrawing electron density from acceptor units. Critically, it optimizes the catalytic carbon active sites, lowering the O2 activation barrier from 0.80 to 0.29 eV. As a result, the charge-separated state lifetime increases from 454 to 988 ps, and the reconstructed catalyst delivers a H2O2 production rate of 3216 μmol g⁻1 h⁻1, a solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency of 4.03% (optimized high-loading condition), and catalytic stability exceeding 50 h with negligible activity loss. Outdoor tests under natural sunlight further demonstrate scalable H2O2 production from both freshwater and seawater, establishing an adaptive design principle for robust metal-free photocatalysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Optimization of Aluminum Casting Process Using PLA-Based Casting Patterns and Analysis of their Thermal Behavior; [Оптимизация процесса литья алюминия с использованием литьевых схем на основе PLA-материалов и анализа их термического поведения]
abstract: This paper presents the results of experimental and numerical studies of the casting process of 99.85% pure aluminum using investment-casting technologies with patterns produced by additive manufacturing. The influence of pouring temperature, mold-filling time, and gating-system design on porosity formation and casting quality was analyzed. It was established that increasing the pouring temperature within the range of 700–800°C leads to increased porosity due to higher gas solubility and intensified turbulence of the melt flow. It was shown that the separating gating system ensures a minimum number of defects compared to top and bottom metal-feeding systems. In addition, thermal analysis of PLA and a glass-fiber-reinforced PLA composite was carried out. Pure PLA was found to burn out almost completely (residue about 2.4%), whereas the composite was characterized by a high residual content (~43.6%), which may negatively affect mold quality. The simulation results obtained using the AutoCAST software package showed good agreement with the experimental data and confirmed the effectiveness of numerical modeling for optimization of casting processes. It was established that the optimal pouring-temperature range for aluminum is 720–760°C. The obtained results confirm the potential of using PLA in investment casting technology and make it possible to improve the quality of aluminum castings under industrial production conditions. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Unlocking robust antibiotics oxidation in nanosphere-confined Fe2O3 via size-exclusion effect and inner-surface-bound radicals
abstract: Nanoconfined peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation provides a promising strategy for the robust degradation of emerging organics in complex water matrices. However, the resistance to size-dependent natural organic matter (NOM) and the behavior of confined oxidative radicals remain unclear. Herein, we precisely confine Fe2O3 nanoparticles within the mesoporous hollow carbon nanospheres (MHCN) via an encapsulation strategy, constructing a nanoreactor (Fe2O3-in-MHCN) for PMS activation. This unique size-exclusion and electrostatic repulsion architecture effectively blocks diverse macromolecular NOM and inorganic anions from entering the cavity, while allowing the small-molecule antibiotic levofloxacin (LVFX) to freely diffuse and enrich inward, achieving 99.5% degradation within 10 min, with a 6.3-fold higher kobs than the non-confined system. Finite element analysis reveals that the shorter pore channels (20 ± 2 nm) accelerate the mass transfer of LVFX molecules toward the inner nanosphere. Moreover, the confined microenvironment shifts the dominant reaction pathway from free radicals to surface-bound radicals (SO4•−* and •OH*), significantly improving reactive species utilization. Fe2O3-in-MHCN gel beads further exhibit excellent long-term stability and environmental safety over 100 h of continuous operation. This study offers a new strategy for designing confined PMS activation systems that synergize pollutant enrichment, enhanced radical utilization, and strong anti-interference capability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
