title: Plasmonic heterojunction on dental implant abutments for enhanced antibacterial activity and soft tissue integration
abstract: Peri-implantitis, a leading cause of dental implant failure, is characterized by bacterial infection, immune dysregulation and inadequate soft tissue integration. To address those challenges, this study proposes a novel plasmonic heterojunction coating on titanium-based abutments. The introduction of tungsten doping and lattice defects significantly increases the free electron density, thereby inducing a strong LSPR effect in the titanium oxide matrix within the near-infrared region. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, the coating demonstrates good antibacterial activity through a dual-mode mechanism: it generates energetic “hot holes” that participate in the “electron hijacking” process, which disrupts bacterial energy metabolism and redox balance; concurrently, the non-radiative relaxation of surface plasmons produces a controlled and mild photothermal effect, which induces bacterial thermal stress and increases bacterial membrane permeability. The plasmonic heterojunction also promotes the adhesion, proliferation, and collagen secretion of human gingival fibroblasts and modulates the immune microenvironment, thereby facilitating the formation of a stable biological seal. In vivo experiments in rats and beagle dogs confirm its good antibacterial activity and biocompatibility, as well as its therapeutic potential in treating peri-implantitis. This work presents a promising potential of plasmonic heterojunction coatings in developing next-generation smart, multifunctional implants to improve long-term clinical success. © 2026

title: Recent Advances in Polymeric Nanocomposite Carriers of Various Active Ingredients for Controlled and Sustained Drug Release: A Review; [Бақыланатын және ұзақ мерзімді дәрілік заттардың шығарылуына арналған әртүрлі белсенді ингредиенттердің полимерлі нанокомпозиттік тасымалдаушыларындағы соңғы жетістіктер: шолу]; [Последние достижения в области полимерных нанокомпозитных носителей различных активных ингредиентов для контролируемого и пролонгированного высвобождения лекарственных средств: обзор]
abstract: Controlled and sustained drug delivery has emerged as a transformative strategy for overcoming the limitations of conventional pharmaceutical formulations, including poor bioavailability, rapid drug clearance, systemic toxicity, and non-specific distribution. Among the numerous delivery platforms investigated, polymeric nanocomposite carriers have attracted considerable attention because they integrate the excellent biocompatibility, biodegradability, and processability of polymers with the unique physicochemical, mechanical, optical, magnetic, and therapeutic properties of inorganic nanomaterials. This review provides a comprehensive and critical evaluation of recent advances in polymeric nanocomposite-based drug delivery systems, highlighting the synergistic interactions between natural and synthetic polymers and a broad spectrum of nanofillers, including metal and metal oxide nanoparticles, carbon-based nanomaterials, nanoclays, mesoporous materials, and electrospun nanofibers. The influence of nanocomposite composition, fabrication strategies, and physicochemical characteristics on drug loading, encapsulation efficiency, release kinetics, targeting capability, and biological performance is systematically discussed. Furthermore, representative therapeutic applications in cancer therapy, wound healing, antimicrobial treatment, tissue engineering, neurological disorders, and regenerative medicine are critically compared to establish structure–property– performance relationships. This review primarily summarizes individual carrier systems, preparation methods, release mechanisms, and biomedical applications into a unified framework while identifying current limitations related to nanoparticle aggregation, long-term biocompatibility, biodegradation, large-scale manufacturing, regulatory approval, and clinical translation. This review provides valuable insights for researchers working on the rational design of advanced polymeric nanocomposites with enhanced therapeutic efficacy, improved safety, and accelerated clinical applicability. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Temperature-dependent island size-morphology correlation in Smoluchowski ripening from machine-learning molecular dynamics
abstract: Precise fabrication of nanostructures on surfaces requires an atomic-level understanding of surface ripening. Although Smoluchowski ripening (SR) describes the phenomenon where nanostructures migrate, collide, and coalesce, resolving the coupled temperature-dependent evolution of island size and morphology in a many-island ensemble remains challenging. Here, we develop a high-accuracy machine-learning potential (MLP) combined with large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to examine nanosecond-scale, early-stage nonequilibrium SR-like coarsening of Zn adatoms on the Zn(0001) basal surface over 100–500 K at 12.5% coverage, using three independent 4 ns trajectories at each temperature. We identify a reproducible three-stage evolution: initial clustering and early aggregation, active coalescence, and quasi-steady ripening. Temperature strongly regulates island size and morphology, with higher temperatures yielding larger, less morphologically anisotropic islands. Crucially, we uncover a consistent temperature-dependent island size-morphology correlation and trace it to the coupling between size-dependent thermodynamic preference for higher-coordination compact structures and temperature-enhanced kinetic relaxation through edge diffusion and post-coalescence rearrangement. These results demonstrate the capability of MLP-MD and provide an atomistic framework for understanding the coupled evolution of island size and morphology during early-stage surface coarsening, with significant implications for fields such as catalysis and electronic devices. © 2026

title: Engineering dual asymmetry: Directed magnetic and random conductive bilayer aerogels for absorption‑dominated EMI shielding
abstract: The rapid advancement of 5G communications and wearable electronics has intensified the demand for high-performance electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials with low-reflection characteristics. Herein, we propose a dual-asymmetric design strategy that synergistically integrates compositional asymmetry (magnetic/conductive) and structural asymmetry (directed/random pores) within a bilayer aerogel architecture. Specifically, a magnetic/conductive bilayer aerogel (MCBA) comprising a directed magnetic top layer (ML) and a random conductive bottom layer (CL) was fabricated using a blended matrix of waterborne polyurethane (WPU) and bacterial cellulose (BC). The ML incorporates MXene@hollow Fe3O4 (MXene@HFO) heterostructures and directionally freeze-cast vertically aligned microchannels that facilitate maximal entry of incident electromagnetic waves (EMWs); the CL employs MXene nanosheets bridged by carbon nanotubes (CNTs) within a randomly freeze-cast, isotropic three‑dimensional (3D) conductive network that ensures highly efficient EMW attenuation. The HFO loading was systematically tuned to optimize the electromagnetic parameters and impedance matching of the MXene@HFO fillers, while the filler contents, pore orientations, and layer thicknesses of both layers were co‑designed to maximize absorption‑dominated shielding performance. This spatial decoupling of wave entry and energy dissipation enables a synergistic “absorption–reflection–reabsorption” pathway, yielding an outstanding EMI shielding effectiveness (SE) of 83.02 dB and an exceptionally low reflection coefficient (R) of 0.151. Furthermore, the MCBA delivers a low density (∼0.269 g cm−3), robust compressive resilience, low through‑plane thermal conductivity (∼0.149 W m−1 K−1), and favorable infrared camouflage. This work presents an ingenious dual‑asymmetric design strategy for developing lightweight, resilient, absorption‑dominated, and multifunctional EMI shielding materials tailored for complex operational environments. © 2026

title: Phase-engineered manganese dioxide for decoupling oxygen reduction and ammonia poisoning in direct ammonia fuel cells
abstract: The inevitable crossover of ammonia from the anode to the cathode in direct ammonia fuel cells (DAFCs) severely poisons conventional platinum cathodes, fundamentally necessitating the development of resilient alternatives. Herein, a phase-engineering strategy is developed to regulate the crystalline evolution of manganese dioxide, driving a simultaneous transition from amorphous aggregates to highly crystalline α-MnO2 nanorods to explicitly decouple the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) from parasitic ammonia poisoning. Serving as an exceptionally resilient ORR center, the phase-optimized MnO2-400 catalyst effectively suppresses undesired ammonia oxidation, yielding a negligible half-wave potential decay of merely 7 mV alongside outstanding long-term durability. Benefiting from this strict reaction decoupling, the assembled DAFC delivers an open-circuit voltage of 0.70 V and a peak power density of 238.8 mW cm−2, demonstrating a highly competitive performance among reported non-precious-metal cathodes. Combined in situ spectroscopic measurements and density functional theory calculations confirm that unlike the Pt baseline, MnO2 surfaces display an intrinsic thermodynamic preference for oxygen capture over ammonia, thereby effectively suppressing adverse ammonia accumulation on the electrocatalytic active sites. This work provides mechanistic insights and fundamental design principles for developing ammonia-tolerant transition-metal-oxide cathodes for DAFCs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Turning coal into gold: Earth-abundant calcined coal as a facile photocatalyst for efficient photopolymerization
abstract: The exploitation of earth-abundant and inexpensive carbonaceous materials as high-performance photocatalysts for controlled radical polymerization remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a serendipitous yet transformative discovery that naturally abundant coal, after a simple calcination treatment in air, can serve as an efficient heterogeneous photocatalyst for PET-RAFT polymerization. Through systematic optimization of the calcination temperature, the catalyst designated as NCC250–2, exhibits an optimal balance of surface functional groups, photogenerated charge-carrier transport kinetics, and lifetime, as well as favorable oxygen adsorption and depletion capacity. This delicate equilibrium endows NCC250–2 with exceptional photocatalytic activity, enabling well-controlled PET-RAFT polymerizations with narrow molecular weight distributions and high chain-end fidelity under visible-NIR light irradiation. Remarkably, compared with previously reported photocatalysts in this field, NCC250–2 not only offers compelling advantages of ready availability, straightforward preparation, and ultralow cost, but also demonstrates superior or comparable catalytic performance. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of utilizing raw coal in PET-RAFT polymerization, turning this low-grade fossil fuel into a functional catalytic material a true “stone-into-gold” transformation. This work not only expands the palette of photocatalysts for precision polymerization but also opens a new avenue for valorizing abundant natural resources into high value materials for sustainable polymer chemistry. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Electrochemical reconstruction-confinement coupling of defect-rich V2O5 nanowires enables ultralong-life zinc-ion storage
abstract: Vanadium-based oxides with multiple redox states are promising cathodes for aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs), yet their practical application is hindered by sluggish Zn2+ transport, structural degradation, and vanadium dissolution during prolonged cycling. Herein, we report a confinement-engineered and electrochemically reconstructed vanadium-oxide cathode, in which V2O5 nanowires are spatially embedded within a conductive carbon nanofiber network and subsequently transformed into a defect-rich hydrated vanadium-oxide framework through electrochemical induction. The carbon nanofiber matrix not only establishes continuous electron-transport pathways but also effectively suppresses active-material dissolution through spatial confinement. Moreover, electrochemical reconstruction generates abundant oxygen vacancies and structural water, leading to a highly active yet structurally resilient Zn-storage framework. Comprehensive experimental investigations combined with density functional theory calculations reveal that the reconstructed architecture simultaneously optimizes the electronic structure, strengthens Zn2+ adsorption, lowers the Zn2+ migration barrier, and promotes pseudocapacitive-dominated reaction kinetics. Consequently, the optimized V2O5-NWS@CNFs cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 463.1 mAh g−1 at 1.0 A g−1 and retains 96% of its capacity after an ultralong lifespan of 16 000 cycles at an ultrahigh current density of 20 A g−1. This work demonstrates electrochemical reconstruction-confinement coupling as an effective strategy for constructing high-rate and ultralong-life cathodes for advanced aqueous energy-storage systems. © 2026

title: AI-assisted design of low-modulus and high-strength Ti-Zr-Hf-Nb-Ta multi-principal element alloys
abstract: Stress shielding caused by the high stiffness of conventional metallic implants creates a demand for low-modulus and high-strength orthopedic materials. Here, an AI-assisted alloy design strategy combining WGAN-GP and NSGA-II was used to explore Ti-Zr-Hf-Nb-Ta multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs). Three representative compositions, Ti42Zr44Hf3Nb8Ta3, Ti35Zr43Hf6Nb10Ta6, and Ti36Zr37Hf9Nb9Ta9 (A1–A3), were experimentally validated. All three alloys exhibited chemically uniform single-phase BCC structures. A1 showed the lowest Young's modulus of 54.3 GPa, with a yield strength of 599 MPa and an elongation of 14.8%, whereas A3 achieved the highest yield strength of 780 MPa with a modulus of 65.5 GPa. The elastic admissible strain values ranged from 1.10% to 1.19%. These results suggest that AI-assisted alloy design provides an efficient route for exploring compositionally complex alloys with a favorable modulus-strength balance. © 2026

title: Dual-branch network for threat analysis of external-force hazards on power transmission lines
abstract: External-force hazards have become a major cause of faults in overhead transmission lines. Existing studies focus on hazard detection, but do not localize the transmission-line safety region or analyze whether a detected target is threatening the line. To address this issue, we propose a dual-branch network that integrates hazard detection, transmission-line segmentation, and pixel-level spatial discrimination for line-aware threat analysis. In the detection branch, a multiscale multihead convolutional gated attention mechanism and a multiscale adaptive spatial attention gate are introduced to enhance multiscale hazard perception, and suppress corridor background interference while maintaining a lightweight design. In the segmentation branch, context anchor attention is embedded into TransUNet to improve the extraction of elongated transmission-line structures and generate reliable line masks. The pixel-level positioning and discrimination module fuses the outputs of the two branches and performs line-aware threat screening. Experimental results show that the detection model improves mAP50 by 5.5 percentage points over the baseline model, while the segmentation branch improves IoU by 1.16 percentage points over the baseline TransUNet. More importantly, after pixel-level screening, only 2.08% of the images require further manual verification, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving warning precision in practical transmission-line inspection. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Carbon nitride enhanced with carbon dots in PDMS coatings: A synergistic approach for elevating corrosion resistance and photothermal self-healing activity
abstract: Multifunctional photothermal self-healing anticorrosion coatings have attracted increasing attention for practical applications. Herein, CDs were loaded onto carbon nitride nanosheets (g-C3N4 (CN)) and incorporated into polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) to prepare carbon dots-decorated carbon nitride (CCN)/PDMS coatings with photothermal self-healing, antimicrobial, and anti-biofouling functions. As verified by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy tests, the impedance modulus of CCN/PDMS coatings after 28 days of immersion is still 1.837 × 109 Ω cm2, which is higher than that of pure PDMS coatings (1.072 × 108 Ω cm2) and CN/PDMS coatings (1.224 × 108 Ω cm2). In addition, the coating scratches were able to be photothermally self-healed within 120 min, while exhibiting a certain degree of anti-biofouling properties with inhibition and suppression of Chlorella and Escherichia coli. This work serves as a reference framework for the design of multifunctional smart anti-corrosion coatings. © 2026

title: Functionalized Chitosan-Modified PVDF-co-HFP Polymer Inclusion Membrane for Enhanced Au(III) Extraction; [Функционалдандырылған хитозан-модификацияланған PVDF-co-HFP полимерлі инклюзивті мембрана Au(III) экстракциясын күшейту үшін]; [Функционализированная хитозан-модифицированная полимерная мембрана на основе PVDF-co-HFP для повышения эффективности извлечения Au(III)]
abstract: Gold recovery from aqueous solutions requires environmentally sustainable alternatives to conventional cyanide-based extraction processes. This study aimed to develop the polymer inclusion membrane (PIM) by incorporating functionalized chitosan into a poly (vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-co-HFP) membrane to enhance the transport and extraction efficiency of Au(III). The membrane consisted of PVDF-co-HFP as the base polymer, Aliquat-336 as the carrier, and dioctyl phthalate (DOP) as the plasticizer, while functionalized chitosan was incorporated at concentrations ranging from 0.5 to 2.5 wt.%. The fabricated membranes were prepared using the solvent-casting techniques and characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), contact angle, and ion exchange capacity (IEC). The membrane containing 2.0 wt.% functionalized chitosan (M5) exhibited the highest Au(III) extraction efficiency of 98.19%.The improved extraction performance was attributed to enhanced membrane hydrophilicity, increased ion exchange capacity, and more efficient carrier-mediated transport. These findings demonstrate that the developed PIM system is a promising and sustainable membrane-based technology for high-efficiency gold recovery. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Acid and Thermal Activation of Clay Separated from Kaoline for Uranium Purification; [Уранды тазарту үшін каолиннен бөлінген саздың қышқылды және термиялық активтенуі]; [Кислотная и термическая активация глины, выделенной из каолина, для очистки урана]
abstract: Clay minerals are commonly used as adsorbents due to their wide availability, large specific surface area, and cation exchange capabilities, making them suitable for removing heavy metal ions from wastewater. This study investigated the activation of clay by acid and thermal treatment to obtain an adsorbent for the purification of uranium from impurities such as iron and magnesium. Acid modification of clay samples was carried out with sulfuric acid (15%) at a temperature of 80–90 °C for 3 hours. While the activation of the clay using the thermal process was performed at 600–650 °C for 12–24 hours. X-Ray Diffraction, Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR), and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) were used to analyse the clay's chemical composition and structural changes before and after activation. FTIR identified free OH groups and hydrated SiO2. EPR showed a high level of paramagnetic centers linked to structural defects and oxygen vacancies, which contribute to the material's strong adsorption and catalytic activity. After acid treatment, the clay particles exhibited a notable rise in specific surface area, expanding from 35.2 m²/g to 342.5 m²/g. Additionally, the specific pore volume grew substantially, increasing from 0.024 cm³/g to 0.30 cm³/g. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Engineering asymmetric energy pathways using Janus gel heteroarchitectures for electromagnetic radiation absorption and directional radiative‑evaporative thermal management
abstract: Modern electronic devices are increasingly affected by coupled electromagnetic and thermal disturbances. Existing multifunctional materials often combined shielding, absorption, insulation, or cooling functions, but clear pathways for electromagnetic and thermal energy transport were rarely established. In this work, a bio-inspired Janus aerogel hydrogel composite was developed for coordinated electromagnetic attenuation and directional thermal regulation. The porous reduced graphene oxide aerogel was used as an impedance-matched gateway for wave entry and external heat blocking. The liquid metal nanoparticles-modified polyvinyl alcohol hydrogel was used as a conductive and hydratable sink for electromagnetic dissipation and heat release. The composite achieved an electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness above 50 dB, a reflection coefficient of 8.87 × 10−4, and an effective absorption bandwidth of about 7.5 GHz. It also reduced CPU hotspot temperature by 5 °C and achieved 7 °C sub-ambient cooling under outdoor conditions. Building simulations further indicated seasonal energy saving potential. These results showed that asymmetric energy pathway design was effective for integrated electromagnetic thermal protection and low-carbon thermal management. © 2026

title: Adaptive power quality control with forecast-driven parameter optimization for reduced harmonic distortion in grid systems
abstract: The increasing integration of distributed renewable energy sources (RES) into modern utility grids has intensified power quality (PQ) challenges, particularly under nonlinear and dynamically varying operating conditions. To overcome these challenges, this paper presents an intelligent method for developing PQ in grid-connected systems with a Tilted Integral Fractional Derivative with Filter plus Fractional Derivative (TIFDNFD) controller. The proposed method combines the Humboldt Squid Optimization Algorithm (HSOA) and Temporal Inductive Path Neural Network (TIPNN), which is termed the HSOA-TIPNN technique. The main objective of the proposed method is to minimize Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), thereby enhancing PQ. The HSOA is utilized to optimize the gain parameters of the TIFDNFD controller, while TIPNN is used to predict the performance of the controller. The proposed technique is tested in MATLAB and compared with Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Deep Recurrent Neural Network (DRNN). The proposed HSOA-TIPNN is able to get the THD of 0.8% while ANN, CNN, and DRNN are 0.9%, 1.0%, and 1.1%, respectively. It also achieves a prediction accuracy of 99.90%, an MSE of 0.0032, and a settling time of 0.15 s, demonstrating improved harmonic suppression, faster dynamic response, and enhanced PQ under nonlinear and disturbed grid conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Mechanisms and suppression methods of interaction oscillations in complex inverter networks under weak grid conditions
abstract: Under weak-grid conditions, coupling between grid-connected inverters and grid impedance can excite high-frequency oscillations. This paper develops a modular small-signal model that maps local VSC state-space models to a global dq-domain nodal-admittance matrix. Modal sensitivity and participation factors are used to identify the dominant resonant mode and its contributing components. Based on this diagnosis, a participation-factor-guided HPF active-damping strategy is designed, with an analytical nominal gain and a full-order robust correction accounting for digital delay and grid-impedance uncertainty. Simulations of a three-VSC ring network, including comparisons with CCF-AD and GCF-AD over SCR=1.2–2.5, demonstrate improved high-frequency damping with limited fundamental-frequency error and control effort. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Geochemical Partitioning and Correlation of Rare Earth Elements, Thorium, and Uranium in Ion-Adsorption Clays from the Gemang Area, West Kelantan, Malaysia; [Геманг аймағы, Батыс Келантан, Малайзиядағы ион-адсорбциялық саздардағы сирек жер элементтерінің, торий мен уранның геохимиялық бөлінуі және корреляциясы]; [Геохимическое распределение и корреляция редкоземельных элементов, тория и урана в ионно-адсорбционных глинах района Геманг, Западный Келантан, Малайзия]
abstract: This study aimed to determine the geochemical partitioning of total rare earth elements (ΣREE), thorium (Th), and uranium (U) in ion-adsorption clays (IACs) from the Gemang area, West Kelantan, Malaysia, and to evaluate how this partitioning may influence selective REE recovery with limited radionuclide mobilisation. An eight-step sequential extraction procedure was applied to representative saprolitic IAC samples, and the extracted fractions were analysed by ICP-OES. Pearson correlation analysis and principal component analysis (PCA) were further used to examine associations among ΣREE, Th, U, and selected major elements. The sequential extraction results showed that ΣREE were concentrated mainly in the ion-exchangeable fraction (average 22.0%), with additional contributions from the residual fraction (15.3%) and a notably high proportion in the primary sulphide step (53.4%). In contrast, Th and U were concentrated mainly in the primary sulphide fraction (54.4% and 41.3%, respectively) and the residual fraction (26.2% and 45.0%, respectively). Major elements such as Al, Fe, Mn, Ca, and Na showed distributions consistent with clay, oxide, and refractory mineral hosts. Statistical analysis indicated a positive association between ΣREE and Ca-Na, whereas Th and U were more closely associated with Fe-Mn-bearing fractions, indicating different host controls and different mobilisation behaviour. These results suggest that a recoverable REE pool is present in the exchangeable fraction, while most Th and U remain in less labile phases under the tested operational scheme. The study therefore provides geochemical evidence that mild ammonium-salt leaching may favour selective REE recovery from Gemang IACs while limiting the release of naturally occurring radioactive materials, although further mineralogical validation and dynamic leaching tests are still required. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: An incipient fault diagnosis method for substation equipment based on multidimensional temperature gradient features
abstract: Infrared thermography is widely used for fault diagnosis of substation equipment. However, existing temperature-based methods mainly rely on absolute temperature information and are highly sensitive to environmental disturbances, such as ambient heat sources and wind speed, which limits the reliable identification of incipient faults. To address this issue, this paper proposes an incipient fault diagnosis method for substation equipment based on multidimensional temperature gradient features. The key innovation is to shift the diagnostic basis from absolute temperature analysis to multidimensional thermal variation analysis by introducing temperature gradient as a more robust indicator of local thermal state changes. First, the physical significance of temperature gradient for condition characterization under environmental interference is analysed based on Fourier's law. Second, a YOLOX based detection method is developed to automatically localize substation equipment from infrared images and extract the corresponding diagnostic regions. Third, a multidimensional diagnosis strategy is established by jointly using the hotspot temperature gradient M∇T and the relative temperature gradient difference R∇T, enabling incipient faults to be characterized from both local thermal intensity and spatial thermal variation. By integrating automatic equipment detection with multidimensional temperature gradient analysis, an automatic diagnosis framework for incipient faults is established. Experimental results show that the proposed detection method attains a mean average precision of 97.76%. The diagnosis thresholds derived for incipient faults are 0.88 °C/m for M∇T and 33.00% for R∇T. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Rare earth-dependent modulation of Cu for C2+ selective CO2 reduction: Correlation with the Cu d-band centre
abstract: Rare earth (RE)-modified Cu-based catalysts have shown enhanced C2+ selectivity in CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR), but the role of different RE elements in regulating the electronic structure and catalytic behaviour of Cu remains insufficiently understood. Herein, five RE-modified Cu catalysts (RE = La, Ce, Pr, Sm, and Eu) were synthesized to investigate the relationship between RE modification and C2+ product selectivity. Theoretical calculations and experimental results revealed an empirical correlation between the Cu D-band centre and C2+ selectivity within the investigated RECu catalysts. Specifically, Eu and Sm shifted the Cu D-band centre upward and exhibited enhanced C2+ selectivity, whereas La, Ce, and Pr showed the opposite trend. Further mechanistic investigations of EuCu indicated that the Eu-containing surface structure modified the thermodynamics of key CO2RR intermediates and promoted water adsorption and dissociation. For the calculated EuCu model, the maximum uphill free-energy difference along the C2H4 formation pathway was lower than that of calculated for the Cu model. EuCu catalyst exhibited a C2+ Faradaic efficiency of 70.9% at a current density of −1 A cm−2 in flow cell, surpassing most reported Cu-based catalysts. These results empirically correlate the Cu D-band centre with C2+ selectivity within the present RECu series. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: End-to-end pseudo-measurement learning for state estimation under limited observability
abstract: Distribution System State Estimation (DSSE) is becoming increasingly important with the integration of Distributed Energy Resources and the active operation of distribution networks (DNs), but it remains challenging due to the limited and heterogeneous monitoring infrastructure available in these networks. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel DSSE framework that restores observability through data-driven pseudo-measurements generated by a Neural Network (NN), while preserving the exact non-linear AC power flow model within a classical Weighted Least Squares (WLS) estimator. Unlike conventional approaches that generate pseudo-measurements independently of the downstream state estimation, the proposed method explicitly couples both components through an end-to-end learning formulation. Specifically, the WLS estimator is embedded as a layer within the NN architecture, enabling implicit differentiation to propagate the impact of pseudo-measurements on the final estimation error back to the NN parameters. Extensive numerical experiments on the IEEE 30-bus and IEEE 33-bus systems demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in state estimation (SE) accuracy under a wide range of loading conditions and measurement configurations. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Rethinking transmission line health indices under rising lightning activity
abstract: Health and condition indices (HI and CI), based primarily on physical inspections, are fundamental in asset management but show severe limitations in regions with high lightning activity. In a 230 kV transmission line (TL) in Colombia, failure rates vastly exceeded design Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) despite assets being classified in "good condition", evidencing the inadequacy of static evaluations. To bridge this gap, this study integrated the traditional HI with a multidimensional framework combining a ten-year spatiotemporal characterization of lightning strikes (2015–2024), physical insulation modeling, and induced overvoltage estimation. Results demonstrate that KPI deviations align with pronounced interannual increases in lightning activity strongly correlated with the positive phase of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), confirming the breakdown of climate stationarity and the emergence of localized exposure hot spots. Furthermore, induced overvoltages—amplified by high local grounding parameters—can exceed 50% of the Critical Flashover Voltage (CFO) even under moderate currents, explaining failures in assets lacking visible defects. Based on these empirical findings, a methodological roadmap is proposed to evolve toward a Dynamic Health Risk Index. © 2026 The Authors

title: Thermodynamic-guided design of cost-effective ultrahigh-strength carbide-free bainitic steel
abstract: Carbide-free bainitic (CFB) steels offer an attractive combination of strength, ductility, and toughness but generally rely on complex alloy chemistries and prolonged isothermal treatments to achieve bainite formation and retained-austenite stabilisation. Here, a new air-cooled CFB steel with simplified chemistry was developed using a thermodynamics-guided alloy design framework. By analysing the effects of common alloying elements on the bainite start temperature, T0′ locus, and bainite hardenability, the carbon partitioning window is introduced as a thermodynamic descriptor to assess the compatibility of bainite formation under continuous cooling. Using this framework, it is shown that combined additions of cost-effective Mn, Al, and Si are sufficient to promote carbide-free bainite without relying on conventional heavy alloying with Ni, Cr, or Mo. Based on this design strategy, a Fe-0.4C-3.5Mn-2Si-0.5Al steel was selected and experimentally validated. The alloy formed a fully CFB microstructure directly after forging and air cooling, eliminating the need for prolonged isothermal treatment. The as-forged steel exhibits a yield strength of ∼1650 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength exceeding 2300 MPa, an elongation greater than 8%, and a Charpy impact toughness of 14 J. These properties are comparable to those of heavily alloyed CFB and martensitic steels while requiring substantially simpler chemistry and processing. The proposed design framework provides a practical pathway for developing cost-effective, sustainable ultrahigh-strength bainitic steels. © 2026

title: Translating alcohol dehydrogenation into H2O2 photosynthesis through proton-coupled electron transfer
abstract: Photocatalytic H2O2 synthesis coupled with selective alcohol oxidation offers a promising route for solar-driven chemical manufacturing, yet the disconnected transfer of protons and electrons between alcohol dehydrogenation and O2 reduction remains a fundamental bottleneck that limits H2O2 selectivity and redox efficiency. To address this challenge, here we describe a Ce-mediated proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET)-bridged photocatalysis strategy by incorporating buried Ce into zinc indium sulfide (ZIS) to form ZIS-Ce, where the local Ce-S coordination environment functions as a cooperative PCET bridge connecting benzyl alcohol dehydrogenation with O2 hydroperoxidation. The optimized ZIS-Ce photocatalyst achieves an H2O2 mass activity of 1.6 mmol g−1 h−1 together with 100% selectivity toward benzaldehyde, outperforming pristine ZIS and conventional redox-decoupled photocatalytic systems. Rather than accelerating isolated half-reactions, the buried Ce site couples a reversible Ce3+/Ce4+ 4 f electron mediator with a polarized Ce-S proton relay, thereby translating benzyl alcohol dehydrogenation into selective O2 hydroperoxidation through synchronized H+/e- delivery. This work redefines alcohol oxidation from a sacrificial hole-consuming reaction into a chemically coupled hydrogen-equivalent donor process, providing a PCET-guided design principle for selective H2O2 photosynthesis and value-added organic oxidation. © 2026

title: Real-time adaptive DC bus voltage control using Jellyfish search algorithm for SAPFs under dynamic operating conditions
abstract: Electrical networks are often subjected to various operational disturbances, among which load variation plays a major role in increasing harmonic distortion and current waveform deformation. Conventional power quality improvement techniques generally depend on simplified mathematical models and fixed parameters, which makes them less effective when the system operates under dynamic conditions. In this work, a real-time control strategy is developed to determine an optimal reference DC bus voltage (Vdc*) for a Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF). Unlike conventional methods that propose a constant Vdc*, Jellyfish Search Algorithm (JSA) looks for an optimal Vdc* in real time whatever external and internal disturbances are detected. In the proposed framework, the active power tracking error (ep) is used as the objective criterion for determining the optimal Vdc*. The proposed control strategy was implemented and experimentally tested against several conventional methods under both steady and dynamic operation conditions using a dedicated test bench. The experimental results demonstrated a noticeable improvement in harmonics mitigation. The proposed control achieved a Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of 2.7 % in steady state. Even applying high load variation, the THD keeps low values with acceptable transients whereas the traditional methods lead to poor power quality. Such experimental evidence demonstrates the capability of the JSA-based approach to adaptively regulate the Vdc* in real time while ensuring that the SAPF performance remains within the harmonic distortion limits defined by IEEE Standard 519–2022. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A haptic feedback architecture for bionic teleoperation blade cleaning tasks
abstract: Hazardous environment operations cannot eliminate the need for human intervention. Teleoperated robots can prevent operators from being exposed to danger. However, a lack of highly immersive tactile feedback hinders safe and efficient teleoperation. To address this issue, a nonlinear tactile feedback method based on a bionic shared-control architecture is proposed in this paper, which can achieve real-time tactile perception and force correction for remote bionic hand. A "Modular Pneumatic Tactile Soft Actuation system (MTSA)" was designed to replicate the bionic tactile sensation. The tactile feedback method is constructed based on the Hunt-Crossley (HC) nonlinear contact model, to ensure it aligns with the dynamic characteristics of human skin contact. Six groups of experiments were conducted under the proposed architecture. The results demonstrated that the bionic teleoperation system, with the integrated tactile feedback, produced effects that better matched human perceptual characteristics. This match effectively reduced the operator's cognitive load while enhancing both the tactile realism and the operational precision of the teleoperated robot. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Thermo-energetic parametric assessment of PV/T cooling technologies: Implications for energy yield, economic savings and CO2 reduction
abstract: Growing societal energy demand has increased the consumption of non-renewable resources, causing resource depletion as well as environmental, economic, and human health concerns. In this context, the transition to renewable energy systems has become essential. Photovoltaic panels integrated with electrical energy storage are among the most promising alternatives to fossil-fuel-based power generation. However, the rise in the photovoltaic panel temperature significantly reduces their efficiency, which remains a major limitation. This study addresses this issue through a theoretical parametric analysis of four photovoltaic-thermal cooling methods: water-based photovoltaic-thermal system, nanofluid-based photovoltaic-thermal system, phase change material photovoltaic-thermal system, and nano-phase change material photovoltaic-thermal system. Minimum and maximum interval boundaries of relative efficiency enhancement values collected from the literature were used to estimate the potential energy gains, economic savings, and carbon dioxide emission reductions under the climatic conditions of Tyre and Baalbek, Lebanon. The results revealed a strong influence of climate, with Baalbek consistently outperforming coastal Tyre because of its higher solar irradiation. Among all systems, nano-phase change material photovoltaic-thermal system achieved the best energetic, economic, and environmental performance. In July, under Baalbek conditions, it reached 100.06 kWh/m2 energy enhancement, 43.86 USD/m2 savings, and 55.61 kg/m2 carbon dioxide reduction. Normalizing the results per unit photovoltaic panel area also provided a scalable assessment tool for stakeholders. © 2026 The Authors. title: Hybrid Deep Learning Finite Difference Time Domain Modeling via Surface Equivalence Theorem for Accelerating Electromagnetic Simulations
abstract: This work presents a hybrid, deep learning-assisted electromagnetic (EM) solver that accelerates time-domain simulations by integrating neural modeling with the Surface Equivalence Theorem (SET). A deep neural network (DNN), composed of long short-term memory (LSTM) and fully connected layers, is trained to reproduce the scattering behavior of a predefined object enclosed by Huygens' surfaces. Once trained, the DNN is embedded into a Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) solver to replace the corresponding subregion, generating equivalent surface fields in real time while preserving multiple-scattering interactions with the surrounding environment. This hybrid approach substantially reduces the computational cost of repeated forward simulations typically required in optimization-driven analyses, such as inverse design, microwave imaging, and parameter estimation. The proposed network, trained using data generated at a central frequency of 9 GHz, accurately predicts broadband EM responses across the 8-12 GHz range. The training procedure and hyperparameter optimization of the network are presented, and various numerical examples are provided. Numerical experiments demonstrate an acceleration of up to 86.7 compared to conventional FDTD and 85.5 relative to the Huygens Sub-Gridding (HSG) technique, with negligible loss in accuracy. The method provides a physics-consistent framework for fast, reusable forward solvers and offers a promising path toward efficient large-scale EM modeling. ©2027 The author(s). title: Intertwined escort dynamics: A dynamical framework for constrained optimization
abstract: Feasibility-preserving algorithms with guaranteed convergence continue to pose challenges for constrained optimization, especially on larger scales or in distributed settings. Toward solving this problem, a well-founded mathematical framework named Intertwined Escort Dynamics (IED) is introduced, in which optimization takes the form of an interacting dynamical system described by escort maps. The framework ensures feasibility inherently at all stages of the process. With fixed-point analysis, it is proven that the resulting dynamics have equilibria that satisfy the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) optimality conditions under general conditions. The proposed framework provides a clear bridge between evolutionary dynamics and constrained optimization, offering an algorithmic approach to obtaining an optimum without resorting to the traditional Lagrange multiplier-based approach. This capability has been verified using a number of optimization benchmarks and economic load dispatch in a large-scale scenario. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Residual nitrogen aggravating hydrogen embrittlement via boron grain-boundary depletion in press-hardened martensitic steel
abstract: The increasing use of scrap-based electric arc furnace routes inevitably introduces elevated residual nitrogen into press-hardened steels, raising concerns regarding their reliability in hydrogen-containing environments. In this work, the effect of residual nitrogen on hydrogen embrittlement (HE) in press-hardened martensitic steel was systematically investigated using steels with controlled nitrogen levels. Slow strain rate tensile tests after hydrogen pre-charging reveal that increasing nitrogen content markedly aggravates HE susceptibility, with the HE index rising from ∼43% to ∼61%, accompanied by a transition toward intergranular-dominated fracture. Microstructural characterization confirms that both steels exhibit fully martensitic structures after hot stamping; however, higher nitrogen deteriorates hardenability and promotes the formation of coarser and more numerous TiN particles. Thermodynamic calculations and inclusion analyses demonstrate that elevated nitrogen enhances TiN precipitation, which modifies boron partitioning. Atom probe tomography provides direct atomic-scale evidence that boron segregates to prior-austenite grain boundaries in the low-nitrogen steel, whereas such segregation is absent in the high-nitrogen counterpart, indicating nitrogen-induced boron depletion at grain boundaries. First-principles calculations show that boron segregation strengthens grain-boundary cohesion (Estr ≈ −0.3 eV), suggesting that the loss of boundary boron reduces interfacial stability and facilitates hydrogen-enhanced decohesion. The combined results establish a mechanistic framework in which residual nitrogen aggravates HE primarily by suppressing boron grain-boundary segregation rather than by altering the martensitic matrix itself. These findings provide critical guidance for nitrogen control in sustainable electric-arc-furnace-produced press-hardened steels. © 2026

title: Experimental evaluation of ensemble learning models for partial discharges detection in transformer insulation mediums
abstract: The reliability and stability of power systems largely depend on the integrity of power transformer insulation systems. Early detection of partial discharge (PD) activity plays a crucial role in preventing catastrophic failures, as PDs are localized dielectric breakdowns that indicate insulation degradation and may develop into severe faults if left undetected. Most conventional diagnostic techniques rely on single-sensor measurements, which may not fully capture the characteristics of PD events under varying operating conditions. This paper proposes a multi-signal ensemble learning framework for the accurate detection, identification, and classification of PDs in transformer insulation systems. Current, voltage, and acoustic PD signals were collected, filtered, and analyzed using time-domain feature extraction. Two ensemble classifiers, Random Forest (RF) and Gradient Boosting (GB), were employed to classify PD patterns occurring in air, mineral oil, and kraft insulation paper. The results show that RF achieved the highest classification accuracy of 96.51% using acoustic signals, outperforming GB, which achieved 95.87%. Compared with the best directly comparable previously published acoustic-sensor-based method, which reported an accuracy of 93%, the proposed RF approach achieved an improvement of 3.51 percentage points, equivalent to a relative improvement of 3.77%. Under the experimental conditions investigated in this study, these findings demonstrate the strong diagnostic capability of acoustic sensing combined with ensemble learning and highlight its potential for reliable and high-precision monitoring of transformer insulation health. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Gluconic acid-driven thermodynamic and kinetic synergy for efficient alkaline seawater oxidation
abstract: Interface engineering constitutes a promising strategy for enhancing catalytic performance. However, the synergistic kinetic-thermodynamic mechanisms induced by interface engineering are yet to be elucidated. Herein, a feasible ligand-modification strategy is proposed to tailor the catalyst-electrolyte interface, aiming to achieve cooperative kinetic and thermodynamic improvements in alkaline seawater oxidation. Thermodynamically, the intrinsic reducibility and the alkaline deprotonation of gluconic acid (GA) ligands render an electron-rich surface of the reconstructed NiFeGA-MoOx (R-NiFeGA-MoOx), elevating the Cl– adsorption barrier to suppress chlorine evolution reaction (ClER). Kinetically, GA destabilizes the hydrated K+ layer and reconstructs the H-bonds in the Helmholtz layer, facilitating the access of free OH– to the catalytic sites. The rapid OH– mass transport provides a kinetically driving force for the alkaline seawater oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Besides, GA-induced hydrophilicity mitigates O2 bubble adhesion, further accelerating mass transfer of the whole reaction system. Based on the synergistic effects of kinetics and thermodynamics driven by GA, the R-NiFeGA-MoOx achieves a favorable OER performance with a low overpotential of 220 mV at 10 mA cm–2 in alkaline seawater. The synergistic ligand engineering drives the trade-off between selectivity and activity, establishing a versatile paradigm for high-performance electrocatalytic systems. © 2026 The Authors

title: Mung bean protein fibrils reinforce whey protein gels at neutral pH: Effects of fibril maturity, concentration, and microstructure
abstract: The effect of mung bean protein fibrils (MF) as active nanoscale scaffolds on the heat-induced gelation of whey protein isolate (WPI) at pH 7 was studied. The microstructural features, intermolecular interactions, and rheological properties of WPI-MF composite hydrogels formulated with MF induced from different heating times (4 h, 8 h, and 12 h) and MF concentrations (0.1 wt%, 0.3 wt%, and 0.5 wt%) were investigated compared to pure WPI gels (Control). After heating at 90 °C for 30 min, WPI formed weak amorphous particulate networks, and the incorporation of β-sheet-rich MF promoted co-assembled into highly interconnected networks as revealed by X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM). The CLSM images of gelled samples were analysed by a novel ResNet-34 transfer learning framework coupled with principal component analysis (PCA) to obtain the microstructural differences, indicating that 0.3 wt% MF was a critical concentration for structural reinforcement. The WPI-MF composite gels demonstrated significant rheological reinforcement, leading to an exceptional growth in the storage modulus (G′). This might be because MF efficiently recruited WPI molecules, resulting in the non-network protein fraction dramatical decrease of more than 30%. Furthermore, the solvent-extraction results suggest that hydrophobic associations made the largest operational contribution to maintaining the WPI–MF gel network. This finding demonstrates that utilising plant-derived fibrils as active scaffolds is an effective strategy for fabricating plant-dairy hybrid gels, reducing the overall concentration of WPI usage with excellent viscoelastic properties. © 2026 The Authors. title: Deep Copper Recovery from Autogenous Smelting Slags under Strongly Reducing Conditions; [Жоғары тотықсыздандыру жағдайында автогенді балқыту қождарынан мысты терең бөліп алу]; [Глубокое извлечение меди из шлаков автогенной плавки в условиях интенсивного восстановления]
abstract: Deep reduction of copper smelting slags is a promising route to recover entrained non-ferrous metals and to generate slags suitable for further processing. This work investigates the depletion of fayalite–magnetite slags formed during autogenous smelting of copper concentrates in conditions simulating the oxidation and reduction zones of a two-zone Vanyukov furnace. Laboratory charges of 100 g, containing 14.63–16.82 wt.% Cu, 25.6–27.6 wt.% Fe, 30 wt.% S and 15 wt.% SiO₂, were smelted at 1350 °C with controlled oxygen injection to produce slags containing 0.93–1.54 wt.% Cu, 30.05–32.30 wt.% SiO₂ and 7.8–9.8 wt.% Fe₃O₄. Subsequent reduction at 1300 °C was carried out with activated carbon in a fivefold stoichiometric excess relative to magnetite, at an oxygen-containing blast flow rate of 5 L/h and a 1 h holding time. Chemical analysis shows that Fe₃O₄ in slag decreases from 7.8–7.95 wt.% to 2.5–2.6 wt.%, while copper content drops from 0.93–1.033 wt.% to 0.43–0.50 wt.% under oxygen partial pressures of 10⁻¹²–10⁻¹¹ atm. X-ray diffraction and electron microscopic studies reveal a transition from fayalite–magnetite slags with dispersed metallic copper and sulfides to fayalite-dominated matrices containing ferruginous sphalerite, copper minerals of the bornite–chalcopyrite type, iron oxides and glassy phases. Simultaneous thermal analysis demonstrates that all major endothermic and exothermic events are completed by 1300 °C, supporting this as an optimal temperature for deep slag depletion. The results define an operating window—slag composition, temperature, reductant dosage and pO₂— under which copper losses to slag can be reduced to about 0.5 wt.% in industrially relevant fayalite slags. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Analysis of the electro-thermal characteristics of MOA with average power equivalent method by incorporating stray capacitance
abstract: The voltage distribution across the varistor blocks of metal oxide arrester (MOA) becomes non-uniform due to stray capacitance which imposes greater electrical stress on varistor block located near the high-voltage electrode. Consequently, the upper varistor blocks undergoes greater thermal stress during operation, resulting in accelerated aging. An enhanced wide-range MOA model incorporating stray capacitance is proposed in this paper to accurately characterize the electrical behavior of the arrester. By integrating the circuit model with the electro-thermal model through the average power equivalent method (APEM), APEM effectively solves the challenge of computational resources due to time-varying excitations. Experiment is conducted to validate the accuracy of APEM and both models. This paper systematically examines the effects of stray capacitance and harmonics on the electro-thermal behavior of MOA. It is found that stray capacitance causes higher voltage on the top varistor block while also causing an overall increase in temperature and thermal non-uniformity. These effects are further significantly amplified in the presence of odd-order harmonics. The conclusions provide a theoretic reference for optimizing the durability and heat dissipation performance of MOA. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Top-down systems engineering of manganese-based lithium-ion batteries for practical deployment
abstract: Uniting economic viability, environmental benignity, highly tunable electrochemical attributes, and paramount safety, manganese (Mn)-based batteries stand as the most formidable contenders to define the state-of-the-art in the upcoming next-generation energy landscape. However, their intrinsic structural and interfacial instabilities are aggressively exacerbated by scenario-specific operational stressors, cascading across multiple engineering echelons in Mn-based batteries. Adopting a forward-looking, Mn-centric perspective, this review uniquely and systematically deconstructs the distinct challenges of Mn-based batteries across three echelons—material, device, and scenario—thereby exposing their cross-layer mismatches and subsequently mapping out targeted technological trajectories. Transcending conventional material-centric summaries of recent advances, the proposed paradigm treats real-world application requirements as top-down design inputs that coordinate material chemistry, device engineering, and system-level integration, thereby breaking the siloed research mode prevalent in traditional Mn-based battery reviews. Addressing these intertwined, dynamic multi-scale impediments, we delineate a scenario-driven, cross-layer co-design paradigm for the broader Mn-based battery ecosystem, championing the integration of frontier characterization and digital intelligence as the twin engines to catalyze the journey of Mn-based technologies from laboratory curiosity to industrial and commercial maturity. © 2026

title: Regulating high-sodium P2 layered oxides through rational lattice modulation for fast kinetics and superior structural stability
abstract: Layered Na-based oxides with the general formula of NaxTMO2 (TM: transition metal) have attracted significant attention due to their high compositional diversity, which enables tunable electrochemical performance as cathodes for sodium-ion batteries. However, their practical applications are often hindered by the irreversible structural transitions leading to capacity fading during cycling. Herein, we synthesize a high-sodium-content layered oxide Na34/48Ni17/48Mn24/48Ti7/48O2 (NNMTO) via the precise substitution of manganese with titanium, thereby realizing enhanced structural stability. The increased sodium content lowers the average oxidation state of the TMs, reduces the O(2p)-TM(3d-eg*) band gap, and thereby enhances O(2p)-TM(3d-eg*) orbital hybridization. The introduction of Ti4+ ions disrupts the Na+/vacancy ordering and effectively mitigates the detrimental P2-O2 phase transition during prolonged cycling. Consequently, the NNMTO cathode exhibits exceptional Na+ mobility and superior electrochemical stability, maintaining 94.8% of its initial capacity after 600 cycles under high-rate 5 C cycling within the voltage window of 2.2–4.2 V. All in all, this study provides critical insights into the rational design of high-performance P2-type layered cathode materials for sodium-ion batteries. © 2026

title: Spatially separated redox reactions over a floatable Fe–Co MOF/S-doped carbon nitride heterojunction for in situ H2O2 generation and ciprofloxacin oxidation
abstract: Photocatalytic H2O2 generation coupled with contaminant oxidation offers a promising route for solar-driven water treatment. However, the efficiency is often hindered by charge recombination, competing redox pathways, and poor catalyst recovery. Here, we report a floatable cobalt-doped MIL-101(Fe)-NH2, (MNH(FeCo)) and sulfur-doped porous tubular carbon nitride (PTCN) heterojunction on expanded perlite (EP), MNH(FeCo)/PTCN@EP, enabling spatially separated redox reactions under visible light. The chemically integrated interface promotes directional charge migration, enabling photogenerated electrons to accumulate on PTCN for the selective reduction of two-electron oxygen to H2O2, while holes remain on MNH(FeCo) to drive ciprofloxacin oxidation. The optimized catalyst achieved a H2O2 production of 1037.8 µM with the rate of 5.35 mmol g−1 h−1 within 2 h, and removed 90.1% of ciprofloxacin within 50 min. Ciprofloxacin-assisted hole consumption further enhanced H2O2 yield. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and in-situ electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) reveal that Fe-Co sites promote O2 activation and decreases energy barrier for formation of •OOH. The expanded perlite support provides buoyancy and enables facile catalyst recovery with stable long-term performance during repeated cycles. Overall, this study provides a recoverable photocatalytic platform that couples in situ H2O2 generation with antibiotic degradation, offering a low-carbon, resource-efficient water treatment technology. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Host-guest interaction and π–π stacking-directed construction of three-dimensional monolithic precursors for molecular-level N/O/S co-doped porous carbon in supercapacitors
abstract: Heteroatom doping is an effective strategy for enhancing the electrochemical performance of porous carbon for supercapacitors. However, inhomogeneous dopant distribution within carbon frameworks presents challenges in enhancing specific capacitance. Herein, a molecular-level heteroatom doping strategy was proposed for constructing N/O/S co-doped porous carbon (DPC) through synergistic integration of chemically induced phase separation (CIPS), host-guest inclusion, and π–π stacking interactions. Monochlorotriazinyl-β-cyclodextrin was synthesized as a host molecule and oxygen source to encapsulate sulfur-containing guest molecules, and the aromaticity of triazine moieties and guest molecules further promoted π–π stacking-assisted assembly. Meanwhile, branched polyethylenimine (b-PEI) served as both nitrogen source and crosslinker to construct a three-dimensional interconnected monolithic precursor via CIPS. The resulting monolithic precursor enabled homogeneous heteroatom incorporation to enhance pseudocapacitance and facilitated the formation of hierarchically porous carbon with abundant accessible active sites after carbonization and activation. Benefiting from uniform N/O/S co-doping, high specific surface area, and hierarchical porosity, the obtained DPC delivered a high specific capacitance of 642 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 and maintained 99% capacitance retention after 20,000 cycles in a three-electrode system. Furthermore, the assembled symmetric supercapacitor achieved an energy density of 19.78 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 299.95 W kg−1, with 96% capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles. Notably, the assembled asymmetric supercapacitor delivered an energy density of 40.2 Wh kg−1. This work provides an effective strategy for achieving uniform heteroatom doping in porous carbon materials toward high-performance supercapacitors. © 2026

title: Elucidating the contributions of alginate and fucoidan to algal cell wall structure and rheology using bacterial cellulose gels
abstract: Bacterial cellulose gels (BC) containing alginate or fucoidan were developed to investigate cellulose-algal polysaccharide interactions and, their impact on gel structure, mechanics, rheology and processing stability. Alginate, a well-established thickening polysaccharide in the food industry, and fucoidan, a sulphated polysaccharide with emerging applications due to its bioactive potential, were incorporated into the incubation medium during cellulose synthesis. A multiscale characterisation approach combining solid-state 13C NMR, X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), rheological and mechanical analyses was employed to elucidate the organisation and interactions within the gel network. The presence of either polysaccharide led to a reduced elastic modulus G′ of the gels, likely reflecting a reduction in cellulose fibril entanglement density, and was associated with lower compressive stress values. BC gels containing alginate exhibited complete stress relaxation following compression, whereas BC gels retained residual compressive stress, indicating a reduced capacity for stress dissipation in BC networks. Both alginate and fucoidan were located in close proximity to cellulose fibres, with fucoidan appearing to coat the fibre surfaces. Neither polysaccharide altered cellulose crystallinity, and both behaved as mobile components within the gels. After dehydration, the gels did not fully rehydrate, regardless of the presence of non-cellulosic polysaccharides. Following thermal treatment in water, alginate was solubilised from the gels, whereas fucoidan remained within the gel network. The results revealed distinct roles of alginate and fucoidan in modulating bacterial cellulose network assembly, viscoelasticity, and mechanical performance. This study provides new insights into cellulose-marine polysaccharide interactions relevant to better understanding algal cell walls and demonstrates the potential of bacterial cellulose gels as tuneable biomaterials for technological applications. © 2026 The Authors. title: Electrostatic and Radio Frequency Performance Optimization of a Triple Metal Gate Hybrid Nanowire Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor
abstract: This paper presents a simulated study on a 2D Asymmetric Gate Stack-Triple Metal Gate-All-Around (AGS-TM-GAA) Nanowire MOSFET with a SiGe-Ge-InGaAs hybrid channel, multi-work function metal gates, and optimally structured high-k dielectric stack (TiO₂/Hf O₂/Si₃N₄). The device has lightly p-doped source/drain, the highly n-doped channel and gate work functions 4.0 eV, 3.9 eV, 4.4 eV to have a greater threshold voltage stability, to lower the potential barriers and to have a better carrier injection. This has been demonstrated to be excellent electrostatic integrity, with steep conduction-band bending ≈-1.5 eV, uniform distribution of fields in the mid-channel ≈1.3-1.5×10⁶ V/m and constant electron mobility ≈8-10 cm2/Vs with ATLAS simulator. The proposed device has the following highest gate-to-drain and gate-coupling capacitances Cgd ≈ 7.5×10-18-2.4×10-19 fF/μm and Cgg ≈ 4.8×10-19 fF/μm, maximum drive current Ids ≈ 5×10-3 A, subthreshold slope 2.2×10-8-1.45×10-9 mV/dec and drain conductance 1×10-9 μS/nm. Short-channel effects, including the variation in threshold-voltage, and degradation of mobility and enhancement of leakage, are substantially reduced due to the GAA, asymmetric gate stack and enhanced quantum confinement. Cut-off frequency (ft), robust FTP behaviour and peak current density are high-frequency metrics that verify the suitability of the architecture to high-speed and Radio Frequency applications. ©2027 The author(s). title: Fast and Accurate Time-Domain simulation of Lightning Response in Grounding systems Considering Frequency-Dependent Soil parameters and Ionization
abstract: It has been demonstrated that most pole-residue sets proposed in the literature to represent the Alipio–Visacro (AV) model—which accounts for the frequency dependence of soil parameters using rational functions—result in high computational cost, making time-domain simulations inefficient for larger or more complex grounding systems. This inefficiency arises from the need for an extremely small time step in such simulations. Furthermore, it has been shown that an unnecessarily high precision requirement during wide-bandwidth curve fitting contributes significantly to the small time-step size. Since the ionization behavior must be updated at each time step, the computational burden becomes even more severe. To address this issue, a new set of poles and residues has been introduced for the AV model to represent the frequency dependence of soil parameters in time-domain simulations. This new parameter set significantly reduces computational costs while maintaining a level of accuracy comparable to that of previous models. Additionally, handling certain ionization-related calculations through lookup tables or predefined curves further reduces simulation runtime when soil ionization is considered. The effectiveness of this method has been validated through comparisons with the reliable frequency-domain Hybrid Electromagnetic Model (HEM). © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: High-entropy ferrite with ultrafine heterostructured nanoclusters for broadband and intelligent switchable microwave absorption
abstract: High-entropy (HE) ferrites with multi-element substitution emerge as promising candidates for microwave absorption (MA) due to their adjustable structure and unique HE effects. However, the effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) and the absorption strength of conventional kinetically random-mixing single-phase HE ferrites are limited. Herein, we report the synthesis of HE ferrite with the formation of ultrafine nanoclusters within the matrix anchored on carbon aerogel (CA) through rapid microwave heating. Benefiting from the binary formation energy differences among the constituent elements (Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Mn, Ce, O), CeO2 nanoclusters are formed within the HE ferrite matrix. The CeO2/HE ferrite-decorated CA (CH/CA) exhibits polarization-enhanced electromagnetic attenuation, which substantially widens the EAB. At 4.0 mm thickness, CH/CA achieves a minimum reflection loss of −69.14 dB at 5.21 GHz, with EAB covering 92.9% of C-band. Notably, the EAB reaches 8.94 GHz at a thickness of 2.5 mm, covering 89.4% of the combined X- and Ku-bands. The integrated EAB of CH/CA at a thickness ranging from 1.5 to 5.0 mm reaches 14.82 GHz, which is comparable to the reported highest values. Furthermore, the CH/CA exhibits compressive strain-driven intelligent on/off switchable and frequency-tunable MA performance. This work proposes a phase-separated HE composite for broadband and smart MA applications. © 2026

title: Regulating nitrogen distribution in covalent organic frameworks for dual-pathway photocatalytic H2O2 production
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising photocatalysts for H2O2 production, yet the charge separation and transport remain a major bottleneck restricting their photocatalytic efficiency. Herein, we proposed a strategy for regulating nitrogen sites to construct a delocalized electronic structure across the COF framework, which facilitates intramolecular charge transfer and suppresses charge recombination. Three COF materials with distinct nitrogen sites were designed and synthesized, namely PDE-PB (nitrogen-free), PDE-PA (pyridine nitrogen), and PDE-PT (triazine nitrogen). Concentrated triazine nitrogen sites in PDE-PT induced donor-acceptor (D-A) separation and charge migration, enhancing optical absorption and photocurrent response. Consequently, PDE-PT delivered a H2O2 production of 5015 µmol·g−1·h−1 under pure water and air conditions, markedly surpassing PDE-PA and PDE-PB. Notably, PDE-PT maintained a high H2O2 yield of over 3600 µmol·g−1·h−1 in real water matrices, highlighting robust adaptability. Additionally, EPR/scavenger experiments confirmed that PDE-PT utilized both ORR and WOR pathways, with the ORR pathway being the dominant contributor (> 97%) and the WOR pathway contributing approximately 2.6%. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further revealed that the outstanding performance of PDE-PT stemmed from both the intrinsic electronic structure of triazine and its concentrated configuration, which induced a typical charge-transfer (CT) state. This work provides insights into the influence of nitrogen sites on H2O2 photosynthesis and offers perspectives for catalyst design. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Effect of atmospheric cold plasma treatment on the structural characteristics and gel properties of hemp protein isolate
abstract: Hemp protein isolate (HPI) is a promising plant protein source owing to its balanced amino acid composition and low allergenicity; however, its propensity for aggregation severely limits its functional and gel properties. This study investigated the effects of atmospheric cold plasma (ACP) treatment on the structural characteristics and heat-induced gel behaviour of HPI. ACP treatment induced structural modifications in HPI, resulting in increased carbonyl content, enhanced exposure of sulfhydryl and hydrophobic groups, reduced particle size, and improved solubility, which increased from 19.6% to 40.9%. Under optimal conditions (350 W, 5 min), ACP treatment promoted protein unfolding, which increased the accessibility of sulfhydryl groups and hydrophobic regions involved in subsequent intermolecular interactions during gel formation. Consequently, ACP-treated HPI exhibited improved gel hardness, viscoelasticity, and water holding capacity (WHC), with the maximum WHC reaching 78.11% at a protein concentration of 12%. Microstructural observations and low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) revealed that these structural modifications facilitated the formation of a more continuous and compact gel matrix with restricted water mobility. Overall, moderate ACP treatment effectively improved the structural and gel properties of HPI and enhanced the stability of the heat induced gel system. These findings provided a basis for improving HPI gel properties and expanding its application in food products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Reducing Hydrogen Diffusion Losses by Modification of Fluoroplastic Barrier Coatings for Increasing Efficiency and Safety of Hydrogen Transportation
abstract: High-pressure hydrogen transport can cause hydrogen embrittlement of steel pipelines, leading to loss of mechanical integrity and failures. Therefore, protective internal coatings are required to reduce hydrogen permeability. In this work, the effect of composite fluoropolymer coatings modified with carbon nanotubes (CNTs), silicon carbide (SiC), and hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) on the hydrogen permeability of 1020 steel was studied using the Devanathan-Stachurski electrochemical method. The effective diffusion coefficient, steady-state diffusion flux, and hydrogen concentration in the near-surface layer were determined for uncoated steel, steel with a graphite layer, and various nanomodified PTFE coatings. Applying fluoropolymer coatings containing CNTs significantly reduced the effective diffusion coefficient and hydrogen flux compared to uncoated steel. Additional incorporation of SiC and h-BN particles enabled further tailoring of the barrier properties. The PTFE-based composition filled with CNTs and SiC provided the lowest effective diffusion coefficient and diffusion flux, which is attributed to the formation of a dense, low-defect polymer structure with an elongated diffusion path. To evaluate the influence of the nanofiller composition on agglomeration and coating defectiveness, the ratio of reduction coefficients ηJ / ηD is proposed as an additional performance indicator. Diffusion loss calculations for a model pipeline section showed that the developed coatings substantially reduce hydrogen permeation through the steel wall, confirming their potential for internal pipeline protection in hydrogen transport and storage systems. © 2027 The author(s). title: Stability of new X-site MAX phases by high-throughput DFT simulations and machine learning with experimental assessment
abstract: The MAX phases have attracted significant attention due to their structural diversity and potential applications. However, they were previously restricted to a very limited set of X-site elements, primarily B, C, and N. This work systematically investigates the synthetic potential of novel X-site MAX phases through first-principles calculations, machine-learning screening, and experimental validation. By selecting thermodynamically and intrinsically stable MAX phases, 206 stable phases (109 211-type and 97 312-type) were identified from a pool of 1980 candidate phases. The stability trends reveal that X-site elements with moderate atomic radii and electronegativity favor phase stability. Further, machine learning models, particularly an artificial neural network with eight key elemental descriptors, achieved an overall accuracy of 86.74%, with 83% accuracy for stable phases. Experimentally, Ti2SeP was obtained as the dominant phase via self-propagating high-temperature synthesis, with lattice parameters matching theoretical predictions, providing preliminary experimental support for its predicted accessibility. © 2026

title: Finite element approximation of a hemivariational inequality for steady-state heat conduction: double-limit convergence of penalization and discretization
abstract: In this paper we study the numerical approximation and convergence analysis of a steady-state heat conduction problem with mixed boundary conditions. The physical model is governed by a hemivariational inequality depending on a heat transfer parameter α > 0. We consider the finite element approximation of this penalized problem, as well as its corresponding limit problem with a prescribed constant temperature on a part of the boundary. The main theoretical result establishes the strong convergence of the discrete solutions. Specifically, we prove the double-limit convergence of the finite element approximations to the limit solution as the mesh size h tends to zero and the penalization parameter α tends to infinity, independently and simultaneously. We further complement the convergence analysis with an error estimate of optimal order for the discrete limit problem, and we explain why an estimate uniform in the penalization parameter cannot be expected. The theoretical results are illustrated by numerical simulations on four examples verified by the method of manufactured solutions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Regulating Fe3O4-to-FeO ratio by Co3O4 pre-deposition to enhance oxidation resistance of pure iron
abstract: Oxidation of iron-based alloys above 600 °C produces a Fe2O3/Fe3O4/FeO trilayer scale, in which the porous, rapidly growing FeO layer is detrimental, whereas Fe3O4 is desirable owing to its high compactness and lower growth rate. Yet the vastly different growth kinetics of the two oxides make FeO suppression challenging. Here, we demonstrate that pre-depositing a layer of Co3O4 nanoparticles on pure iron can effectively regulate the growth kinetics and structure of the oxide scale at 700 °C, reducing the oxidation rate constant by one order of magnitude and increasing the Fe3O4/FeO thickness ratio from 0.06 to 1.36. Density functional theory calculations reveal that these changes originate from Co2+ doping, which increases the diffusion barrier for cation vacancies while lowering that for anion vacancies in both Fe3O4 and FeO. As a result, FeO growth is strongly suppressed, and Fe3O4 growth shifts toward inward O2− diffusion, promoting competitive growth at the Fe3O4/FeO interface and further hindering FeO thickening. This work provides theoretical guidance for rational regulation of oxide-scale phase structure and oxidation-protection strategies in iron. © 2026

title: Synthesis of highly active R‑ZIF-67 from spent lithium‑ion batteries for peroxymonosulfate activation: Distinct roles of Ni and Li impurities
abstract: The distinct roles of framework-doped Ni and free Li+ in R‑ZIF‑67 catalysts derived from spent LiCoO2 were investigated for peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation toward metronidazole (MNZ) degradation. The catalysts were prepared via acid dissolution–coprecipitation, with Li content tuned by vacuum extraction, and their structural and electronic properties were probed by a combination of experimental characterizations and DFT calculations. The resulting R‑ZIF‑67 achieved complete MNZ removal within 25 min (k = 0.0835 min−1), outperforming pristine ZIF‑67 (50 min, k = 0.0221 min−1). For the enhanced performance, Ni as framework active sites enhanced PMS chemisorption and shortened the O–O bond, while free Li+ as an electron buffer reduced the charge‑transfer resistance from PMS to the catalyst. Owing to the synergistic effect of Ni and Li, the energy barrier for PMS conversion via terminal O2 atoms was lowered, thereby promoting PMS conversion to active species (1O2) over SO4·⁻/·OH. This work offers a sustainable route for upcycling spent LIBs into high‑performance catalysts and decouples the roles of framework metals and free ions in catalysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
