title: Kinetics of starch digestion in Australian pigeonpea [Cajanus cajan (L.) Millsp.] genotypes and consequences for nutrient asynchrony
abstract: In view of pigeonpea global food importance, the in-vitro starch digestibility of Australian genotypes ICPLs 14425, 86022, 88039, 90048, 91039, and 98011 was investigated, objectively revealing monophasic and biphasic digestograms. The digestograms were adequately modelled (r2 > 0.89, p < 0.001) by the 1- and 2-term exponential and non-exponential plus the recommended sequential modified first-order kinetic model. Genotypes ICPLs 86022, 88039, and 91039 were monophasic with digestion rates (KST x 10−3 min−1) 6.9-11.3. The biphasic genotypes ICPLs 14425, 90048, and 98011 exhibited a rapid-slow digestion phenomenon with KST 13.8–30.8 for the rapid first phase and 0.5–5.2 for the slow second phase. The maximum digestible starch (D∞, g/100g dry starch) ranged from 8.4 to 100.0, indicating remarkable genotypic differences (heterogeneous amylolysis), also revealed in the very rapidly (2.7–4.2), rapidly (3.9-9.8), and slowly (2.0–4.9) digestible and resistant (85.4–92.7) starches. Moreover, the genotypes significantly (p ≤ 0.05) differed in their low glycaemic indices (eGIAVG, 22.1–38.9%) and loads (eGL, 6.7–11.8%) relative to white wheat bread. The relative release (nutrient asynchrony) of amino acids and glucose during digestion was examined by comparing the starch hydrolysis index (HISTARCH) and eGIAVG (current study) with their protein parameters (HIPROTEIN, in-vitro protein digestibility [IVPDAVG], Malau & Sopade [2026]. Food Science and Processing 2 {2}: 8). The nutrients could be comparably released in ICPL 90048, but amino acids could be released slower in ICPL 14425 and faster in ICPLs 86022, 88039, 91039, and 98011. These results, hereby first reported, are valuable for global uses of pigeonpea. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Gelatin-based hydrogels modified by transglutaminase and acid-heated ovalbumin aggregates: Experimental characterization
abstract: Conventional cold-set gelatin hydrogels have limited mechanical strength and thermal stability. This study examined gelatin (GEL)-based formulations modified with transglutaminase (TGase) and acid-heated ovalbumin aggregates (AHOA). Short-time characterization of acid-heated ovalbumin showed spectroscopic changes consistent with amyloid-like aggregation and an increased elastic response. AHOA prepared by an 8-h acidic heat treatment was incorporated into gelatin formulations. At a common TGase reaction time of 6 h, the GEL:AHOA volume ratio of 6:4 gave the highest hardness and springiness among the tested formulations. Because changing this ratio also changes protein concentrations, the maximum describes a formulation-dependent response. TGase-treated gelatin hydrogels exhibited higher moduli and altered hydration behavior than the untreated control. In the extended in vitro digestion test, treated groups showed lower early but higher final cumulative betacyanin release, and a higher fraction of endpoint-recovered betacyanin in the liquid phase. The storage tests showed higher betacyanin retention at 8 days and lower loss at 28 days for the TGase-treated groups than for GH in the respective series. These results distinguish the mechanical response to AHOA incorporation from the hydration and pigment-release properties measured for gelatin hydrogels with and without TGase. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Cross-graph learning based mating interface identification for CAD-assisted assembly design
abstract: During CAD model exchange and reuse, explicit assembly metadata may be incomplete even when the geometries of candidate parts remain available. For a predefined pair of B-rep parts, an upstream task is to rank the face pairs most likely to constitute a mating interface before constraint type inference or pose estimation. However, existing methods pay insufficient attention to the interaction between faces across different parts. To address these issues, this paper proposes MFPNet, a lightweight cross-graph learning method for mating interface identification between B-rep part pairs. The proposed method constructs face representations by integrating geometric and shape information, while a topology-aware graph encoder captures intra-part contextual dependencies among B-rep faces. A matcher integrating cross-graph attention and bilinear feature interaction is subsequently employed to rank the candidate face pairs. Experiments on the Fusion 360 Gallery Assembly Dataset demonstrate that the proposed network achieves competitive recognition accuracy with reduced parameter overhead. Moreover, zero-shot tests are performed on the self-built aerospace part mating surface dataset, named Aero-MF. A prototype system further demonstrates how the ranked mating interface candidates can be presented to engineers as upstream decision support for CAD-assisted assembly design. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Photovoltaic tilt optimization using physics-informed machine learning methods
abstract: Photovoltaic arrays are typically installed at a tilt angle, measured from the horizontal plane, close to the site latitude; however, this approach can underperform relative to the physics- or data-driven optimum tilt, resulting in suboptimal energy yields. In this work, we introduce a physics-informed machine learning framework to determine the annual fixed tilt that maximizes energy yield for Antalya, Turkiye. To this end, we process daily irradiance records to derive the diffuse fraction and seasonal harmonics. We use the Liu-Jordan isotropic model to generate a physics-based reference curve and obtain an annual optimum array tilt of 34.75∘. Afterward, we apply machine learning algorithms to a tilt-augmented dataset (0-60∘, in steps of 0.25∘). The best-performing machine learning model yields an incident irradiation of 1,850kWhm−2year−1, which corresponds to an electrical specific yield of 1.57MWhkWp−1year−1 (assuming a performance ratio of 0.85). Finally, all the results provide a robust way to select the tilt angle for optimal system design and to compare data-driven with physics-based models. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Numerical and Experimental Investigation of Thermo-Hydraulic Performance Enhancement of Water-Cooled Photovoltaic Modules Using a Helical Pipe Network with Twisted Tape Inserts
abstract: High and spatially non-uniform temperatures reduce the electrical output of photovoltaic (PV) modules and accelerate hotspot-related degradation. While previous research has looked into water-cooled PV/T systems and the use of twisted-tape inserts as separate solutions, there's a noticeable absence of studies that combine these approaches. Specifically, there is a lack of investigation into optimizing the arrangement of cooling pipes before incorporating internal flow enhancements. Moreover, experimental evidence is essential to confirm if such a dual strategy can genuinely improve the performance without imposing significant hydraulic disadvantages. This research directly tackles these issues by introducing and validating a two-step optimization strategy for water-cooled PV/T modules. Our work commenced with a computational assessment of four different helical pipe arrangements (100 × 150, 100 × 100, 100 × 50, and 80 × 80 mm). After this initial evaluation, the most promising configuration was further refined by adding either four or ten twisted-tape inserts. The best-performing layout was then enhanced using four and ten twisted-tape inserts. Simulations in three dimensions, investigating conjugate heat transfer, were performed using ANSYS Fluent. These simulations were carried out under a heat flux load of 800 W/m², with incoming water at a temperature of 25 °C, and across a range of Reynolds numbers from 5,000 to 11,000. The configuration featuring an 80 × 80 mm layout emerged as the optimal baseline. This setup successfully lowered the average temperature of the PV surface to 45.62 °C when the Reynolds number was 11,000. Concurrently, it achieved an electrical efficiency of 16.05% and an electrical power output of 205.49 W. The subsequent introduction of ten twisted-tape inserts led to a further reduction in temperature, bringing it down to 42.30 °C. This enhancement also boosted the electrical efficiency to 16.44% and the power output to 210.48 W. To confirm these findings, experimental validation was conducted. The results from these experiments showed mean absolute percentage errors of 1.46% for the baseline setup and a slightly lower 1.23% for the configuration enhanced with inserts. An important consideration, the pumping power required for these systems remained below 3 W across all tested conditions. The distinct contribution of this research lies in its comprehensive approach, which unifies several key aspects within a single design framework. This includes optimizing the helical pipe layout, harnessing the flow enhancement provided by twisted tapes, evaluating the uniformity of temperature, and undertaking experimental validation of the thermohydraulic performance. This integrated methodology effectively demonstrates that improvements in hotspot management and overall electrical performance can be realized without incurring substantial demands on hydraulic energy. © 2027 The author(s). title: Artificial intelligence for stability assessment and early-warning in converter-dominated power systems: A unified review and risk-envelope framework
abstract: Converter-dominated power systems with high penetration of inverter-based resources exhibit fast, nonlinear, and multi-timescale dynamics that introduce new stability modes and operational risks beyond the scope of traditional assessment techniques. In recent years, artificial intelligence and machine learning methods have been widely applied to small-signal, transient, voltage, and frequency stability prediction using simulation data and wide-area measurements. Although many studies report high predictive accuracy, the literature remains fragmented across stability categories, data regimes, and model classes, and typically emphasizes point prediction rather than uncertainty, regime transitions, and control-oriented early-warning. This review presents a systematic and literature-rich synthesis of AI-driven stability assessment approaches for converter-dominated power systems, covering learning architectures, feature representations, graph-based methods, and real-time monitoring integration. Key gaps are identified in uncertainty-aware prediction, cross-timescale stability coupling, interpretability for control action, and operational risk quantification. To address these limitations, a novel AI-Based Stability Risk Envelope Framework is proposed, linking predictive models with uncertainty bounds, operating-region tracking, and decision-triggered early-warning mechanisms for dynamics-informed grid operation. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Electronegativity-guided construction of bimetallic centers on black phosphorus for CO2-to-C2 electroreduction: A DFT study
abstract: Dual-atom catalysts (DACs) hold great promise for the CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) owing to their synergistic effects and full atom utilization efficiency. However, a general strategy for precise structural control remains lacking, which limits the activation of key intermediates and the selectivity toward C2 products. Herein, we propose an electronegativity-difference strategy to construct black phosphorus (BP)-supported heteronuclear DACs. Co and Pd, with electronegativity lower and higher than P, respectively, form a stable Co-Pd@BP structure. Electronic structure calculations reveal that the electronegativity difference between the bimetallic sites and BP induces directional charge redistribution and creates efficient electron transfer pathways. Such characteristics promote electron injection into adsorbed CO2, activate the inert CO2 molecules, and lower the formation energy of the key *COOH intermediate. Gibbs free energy calculations confirm that Co-Pd synergism optimizes the *CO-*CHO coupling step both thermodynamically and kinetically, overcoming the limited C2 production capability. The acetaldehyde evolution pathway exhibits the lowest energy of 0.36 eV. Moreover, this electronegativity modulation strategy is extendable to Ru-Co and Rh-Co heteronuclear systems with comparable CO2RR activity, showing preliminary extendability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Fe7Se8/Cu3Se2 heterostructure regulates active hydrogen generation for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia
abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) has emerged as a promising strategy for coupling nitrate removal with value-added ammonia synthesis. However, the multistep proton-electron transfer process and complicated evolution of nitrogen-containing intermediates impose stringent requirements on the electronic structure and active-site configuration of catalysts. Herein, an integrated synthetic strategy of in situ growth, Fe3 + selective etching, and annealing-selenization is developed to construct self-supported Fe7Se8/Cu3Se2 heterostructured nanotube arrays on Cu foam. In neutral 0.5 M Na2SO4 electrolyte containing 50 ppm NO3--N, the Fe7Se8/Cu3Se2 electrode delivers a nitrate conversion of 92.56%, NH3 selectivity of 97.91%, Faradaic efficiency of 85.23%, and NH3 yield rate of 1.93 mg h−1 cm−2 at −0.5 V vs. RHE. Single-component control experiments indicate that Cu3Se2 is more favorable for nitrate conversion, whereas heterointerface construction facilitates the further conversion of NO2- and downstream intermediates. XPS and XANES analyses indicate interfacial electron redistribution toward Cu sites, while H* scavenging and EPR measurements support H*-related responses and active-hydrogen involvement on Fe7Se8/Cu3Se2. Potential-dependent in situ Raman measurements provide additional spectroscopic evidence consistent with the evolution of nitrate-derived intermediates. DFT calculations further indicate that heterointerface formation thermodynamically favors H* formation and lowers the Gibbs free-energy change (ΔG) of the potential-determining step (PDS) for continuous nitrate reduction. Moreover, the catalyst enables a Zn-NO3- battery system with a maximum power density of 1.577 mW cm−2 and continuous discharge operation for 12 h. These results support a cooperative role of Fe7Se8/Cu3Se2 heterointerfacial synergy in regulating the electronic structure and facilitating active-hydrogen involvement, thereby promoting selective nitrate-to-ammonia conversion. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Marrying PDI with cyano-oxygen co-doped carbon nitride for efficient self-powered H2O2 photoelectrochemical cells
abstract: A novel heterojunction photocatalyst is crafted by strategically marrying perylene diimide (PDI) with cyano-oxygen co-doped carbon nitride (COCN). This union creates a synergistic interface that not only extends visible-light absorption but also profoundly boosts the separation and migration of photogenerated charge carriers. When deployed as a photoanode in a self-powered H2O2 photoelectrochemical cell, the optimal PDI/COCN-10 composite achieves a remarkable maximum power density of 1.62 mW cm−2 with a solar-to-electrical conversion efficiency of 1.28%, a performance that stands out among contemporary systems. This configuration demonstrates a 2.5-fold and 4.2-fold enhancement in power density over cells based on pristine PDI and graphitic carbon nitride, respectively. Moreover, the cell exhibits superior energy storage capability, retaining 58.9% of its specific capacitance after 12 h of operation in the dark. This work exemplifies a successful marriage of molecular and polymeric semiconductors to create efficient, multifunctional devices for solar energy conversion and storage. © 2026

title: Coordinating the multi-sites synergistic adsorptions by heterogenizing Ru nanoclusters onto NiCoP nanoarrays for concurrent highly-selective biomass upgrading and efficient hydrogen evolution at large current densities
abstract: Electrooxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) offers an attractive route for the concurrent production of 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) and hydrogen, yet insufficient coordination among multiple adsorption sites limits its high selectivity at large current densities. Herein, Ru nanoclusters are heterogenized onto NiCoP nanoarrays to construct Ru–P–(Ni/Co) heterointerfaces, which coordinate the multi-site synergistic adsorption for highly selective HMFOR coupled with efficient HER. Operando and theoretical studies reveal that differentiated adsorption synchronizes HMF activation and hydroxyl supply, thereby lowering key oxidation barriers and promoting FDCA formation. Meanwhile, the Ru–P–(Ni/Co) interfacial ensembles also facilitate H2O activation and H* conversion for alkaline HER. Benefiting from this mechanism, the catalyst exhibits 1000 mA cm−2 at 1.6 V, achieving 93.1% selectivity and 99.4% Faradaic efficiency of FDCA, with excellent stability for HMFOR. It also exhibits outstanding HER activity, delivering 1265 mA cm−2 at −0.7 V and sustained durability for over 100 h. Eventually, the bifunctional catalyst enables simultaneous FDCA and H2 generation at 138 mA cm−2 at 2.0 V in a membrane electrode assembly electrolyzer. This work provides a mechanistic framework for site-specific co-adsorption and cross-interfacial reactant coupling, offering a promising strategy for highly selective biomass upgrading and efficient hydrogen evolution at large current densities. © 2026

title: Knowledge-grounded multimodal cognitive decision-making for aerospace machining: A physics-aware reasoning framework for generative process planning of special-shaped features
abstract: Complex aerospace products encompass numerous special-shaped features (SSFs), whose machining processes rely on highly customized process planning. Traditional data-driven discriminative models predominantly operate as physics-agnostic "black boxes." Moreover, applying general-purpose Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to manufacturing often causes "physical hallucinations", generating linguistically plausible but mechanically infeasible process plans. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a Knowledge-Grounded Multimodal Cognitive Framework (KGMCF), which extends discriminative feature recognition with physics-aware generative reasoning for machining decision-making. First, an Aerospace Multimodal Process Knowledge Graph (Aero-MPKG) is constructed to formalize manufacturing constraints. A cross-modal visual anchoring mechanism is introduced, enabling the MLLM to precisely map unstructured engineering drawings to discrete symbolic nodes via topological embedding retrieval. Second, a KG-guided Symbolic-Neural Synthesis (SNS) strategy is developed to construct a multimodal instruction-tuning dataset, thereby driving a multi-stage physics-aware Chain-of-Thought (CoT). Finally, a symbolic verification loop with semantic traceback detects constraint-violating parameters and triggers self-correction through natural language feedback. Extensive experiments on an aerospace vortex shell benchmark demonstrate that the KGMCF effectively suppresses the Graph-based Physics Violation Rate (G-PvR) from 24.52% (vanilla MLLM) to 9.62%, while simultaneously achieving a Tool Selection Accuracy (TSA) of 93.12% and a Machining Parameter Selection Accuracy (MPSA) of 91.44%. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Synergistic modification of okara insoluble dietary fiber by hydrothermal alkaline treatment and ball milling reinforces casein gel properties
abstract: This study investigated how hydrothermal alkaline treatment, ball milling, and their combination modified the structural and physicochemical properties of okara insoluble dietary fiber (OIDF) and influenced the properties of acid-induced casein gels. Hydrothermal alkaline treatment (105 or 121 °C, pH 11.0) loosened the compact fiber structure, generated a porous network, and shifted the hydrogen-bonding pattern from intra- to intermolecular associations. These changes markedly enhanced water-holding capacity (WHC) and elasticity, supporting the formation of a gel-like fiber network. Ball milling (300 rpm, 1 or 3 h) preferentially disrupted amorphous regions, reduced particle size, and increased specific surface area and pore volume by 10- and 22-fold, respectively. In casein gels, the increased negative surface charge and altered hydrogen bonding may facilitate OIDF-casein interactions, while fiber structure further influenced its incorporation into the gel network. Hydrothermally alkali-treated OIDF may contribute to gel reinforcement through its network-like structure, whereas ball-milled OIDF primarily favored filling and surface interactions. The combined treatment, particularly hydrothermal alkaline treatment followed by 1 h of ball milling (105-BM-1 or 121-BM-1), combined the complementary effects of the two treatments, resulting in a link density of 90.0%, a WHC of 795 g/kg, and a storage modulus of 900 Pa. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Ni-Co bimetallic sulfide-derived catalysts for efficient electrooxidation of xylose to formate
abstract: Abundant xylose from agroforestry residues can be electrocatalytically oxidized to formate, offering a promising green biomass valorization strategy for carbon neutrality. Herein, a novel post-activated (PA) Ni-Co bimetallic sulfide-derived electrocatalyst supported on a nickel foam substrate for the xylose oxidation reaction (XOR), denoted as PA-NiCoS@NF, was fabricated via a facile one-step electrodeposition method. Co doping induces the formation of an ultrathin nanosheet array structure. Furthermore, it enables precise modulation of the electronic structure of the Ni centers, and the strong electronic interaction between Co and Ni bimetallic sites facilitates the oxidation of Ni2+ to Ni3+. The PA-NiCoS@NF catalyst exhibits outstanding electrocatalytic performance for XOR, delivering a xylose conversion of 99.9%, a formate yield as high as 80.1% with a formate selectivity of 81.0%, a corresponding Faradaic efficiency of 80.9% at a low potential of 1.45 V vs. RHE. Additionally, the XOR delivers a current density of 50 mA·cm⁻² at only 1.39 V vs. RHE. Density functional theory calculations reveal that Co doping optimizes the adsorption behaviors of xylose and adsorbed hydroxyl species on the active sites. Furthermore, the PA-NiCoS@NF catalyst exhibits excellent cycling stability for XOR and increased anodic current responses in a preliminary LSV screening of five biomass-derived substrates. This work provides a novel and feasible strategy for the electronic structure modulation and nanostructure engineering of high-efficiency catalysts in the field of electroconversion of aldose biomass platform molecules. © 2026

title: Techno-economic assessment of a solar-powered absorption air-conditioning system for a commercial building in Sudan
abstract: This study evaluates the technical, environmental, and economic feasibility of solar-powered air conditioning (AC) systems in Sudanese buildings. Sudan’s high ambient temperatures make AC a major contributor to electricity demand. The Bank of Khartoum is selected as a case study, with an 83.4 TR solar cooling system modeled in TRNSYS (latitude 15.6°N, longitude 32.6°E). The system comprises a lithium–bromide absorption chiller, evacuated tube collectors (ETCs), and thermal energy storage (TES). Iterative simulations identify optimal operating conditions: 400 m2 collector area, 53,280 kg/h ETC flow rate, and 15 m3 TES. The system achieves a coefficient of performance (COP) of 0.7, primary energy savings (Formula presented) of 212 MWh, and a payback period (PBP) of 13.2 years—strongly influenced by local electricity tariffs. The study uniquely evaluates ETCs for medium-temperature (90–110 °C) solar thermal applications in Sudan’s climate, optimizing system parameters for commercial buildings. © 2026 The Authors. title: Sulfur-vacancy modified hierarchical hollow Ni2CoS4 nanospheres boosting electrochemical kinetics and stability for high-performance asymmetric supercapacitors
abstract: The sluggish reaction kinetics of positive electrode materials limit the rate performance of supercapacitors, which has become a bottleneck restricting their large-scale energy storage applications. Herein, hierarchical hollow nanosphere H-Ni2CoS4 with sulfur vacancies was prepared via hydrothermal synthesis and calcination using nickel-cobalt glycerate as the template. The H-Ni2CoS4 material exhibits an exceptional specific capacitance (Cs) of 2162 F g−1 at a current density of 1 A g−1. The as-fabricated asymmetric supercapacitor (H-Ni2CoS4||activated carbon) delivers an energy density of 63.5 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 384.1 W kg−1 within a voltage window of 0–1.6 V. After 18,000 cycles at 10 A g−1 in 1 M KOH, its capacitance retention reaches 80.71%. Experimental investigations in conjunction with density functional theory calculations uncover that the integration of sulfur vacancies and a hierarchical hollow structure can expose richer active sites and sustain effective redox processes. Compared with single Ni- or Co-based sulfides, the d-band center of nickel-cobalt composite sulfides is effectively regulated, which optimizes the adsorption of hydroxyl ions on metallic active centers, improves electronic conductivity, accelerates ionic mobility, and enhances interfacial charge accumulation. The present work simultaneously boosts the electrochemical reversible capacitance and structural stability, demonstrating great application potential as state-of-the-art electrode materials toward supercapacitor applications. © 2026

title: Dynamic Load Recovery in Hydraulic Force Sensors via Frequency-Domain Signal Separation and Inertia-Damping Correction
abstract: This study presents an analysis of existing solutions for measuring dynamic loads and introduces an approach for reconstructing dynamic loads from hydraulic force sensor data, that accounts for the sensor's physical and structural characteristics. A mathematical model is proposed that relates the applied force to the measured fluid pressure while incorporating damping and inertia effects. It is demonstrated that parasitic high-frequency waves caused by resonant processes in the fluid column and forced oscillations of the piston and fluid can be separated from the desired signal through spectral analysis. To isolate the mechanical component of pressure, frequency-domain harmonic selection is employed, followed by signal decomposition into Gaussian functions and envelope-based correction, accounting for inertia and damping. The validity of the approach is confirmed by numerical simulation of wave processes in the sensor chamber and laboratory experiments involving impact loads generated by a conical striker in free fall from various heights. A comparison of the reconstructed signals with reference signals obtained using a grapho-analytical method shows excellent agreement. Pearson's correlation coefficient was 0.951 and mean squared error was 0.0107. The relative deviation of the total transmitted impulse from the theoretical value is less than 0.02%. © 2027 The author(s). title: Ultrafast synthesis of two-dimensional rare-earth oxychlorides enables dual-site synergy for efficient nitrate to ammonia electrosynthesis
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) rare-earth oxychlorides (REOCls), with their unique structural and electronic properties, offer exciting opportunities for applications in catalysis. However, conventional synthesis routes for REOCls generally involve prolonged (≥1 h) and energy-intensive high-temperature pyrolysis, which often lead to surface coking and formation of large particle sizes. In this work, we develop a Joule heating (JH) technique for ultrafast synthesis of 2D REOCls (RE=La, Tb, Nd, and Sm) within an exceptionally short time of only 15 s. As a representative, the as-prepared 2D LaOCl exhibits outstanding electrocatalytic performance toward nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR), achieving an NH3 yield of up to 426 μmol·h−1 cm−2 and a Faradaic efficiency of 95.88% at a low potential of −1.2 V vs. RHE. Furthermore, in situ Raman spectroscopy, operando attenuated total reflection Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations collectively unveil that 2D LaOCl nanosheets not only enhance the affinity of rare-earth sites for NOx- species but also regulate hydrogen adsorption on chlorine sites, thereby accelerating the hydrogenation steps and sustaining a steady *H generation-consumption cycle. This work demonstrates a highly efficient strategy for the ultrafast synthesis of 2D REOCl materials and highlights their promising potential in catalytic applications and beyond. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Ce/La-induced formation of Al2RE/Al2Ca composite phases and enhancement of mechanical properties and ignition resistance in Mg-Al-Mn-Ca alloy
abstract: Mg-Al-Mn-Ca (AMX) alloys are promising candidates for next-generation lightweight structural materials owing to their attractive combination of mechanical properties and ignition resistance. In this study, the effects of Ce/La co-addition on the second-phase evolution, mechanical properties, and ignition resistance of an AMX402 alloy were systematically investigated. The results show that Ce/La co-addition induces the formation of micron-scale Al2 rare earth (RE)/Al2Ca composite phases, which is governed by preferential Al2RE precipitation, low lattice mismatch between Al2RE and Al2Ca, and favorable adsorption of Ca atoms at Ce-enriched sites. Meanwhile, the tensile yield strength and ultimate tensile strength increased from 270 ± 4 and 316 ± 5 to 293 ± 6 and 326 ± 6 MPa, respectively, mainly owing to precipitation strengthening by the rod-like Al2Ca phase, grain boundary strengthening, and residual dislocation strengthening. The ignition temperature also increased from 897 ± 15 to 971 ± 6 °C. This improvement is attributed to Ce/La-induced redistribution of Ca, which increases dissolved Ca in the α-Mg matrix and promotes the formation of a compact MgO-CaO protective oxide film. These findings provide insight into rare-earth-mediated second-phase regulation for developing high-strength ignition-resistant Mg alloys. © 2026

title: Zr-regulated discontinuous precipitation suppressing intermediate-temperature embrittlement in L12-strengthened HEAs
abstract: Intermediate-temperature embrittlement (ITE) limits the structural reliability of L12-strengthened high-entropy alloys (HEAs). However, the microstructural origin of preferential grain-boundary damage during ITE, particularly the role of discontinuous precipitation (DP), remains unclear. In the heat-treated Al0.5Cr0.9FeNi2.5V0.2 HEA, ITE is closely associated with preferential damage along DP-affected grain boundaries. Here, we reveal that trace Zr microalloying mitigates ITE by regulating this damage process. Zr addition increases the elongation at 700 °C from ∼2.5% to ∼23.4% while retaining comparable strength. Multiscale characterization reveals that Zr substantially reduces the DP area fraction, refines DP colonies, and modifies the body-centered cubic morphology within the DP regions by decreasing the proportion of lamellar constituents. The refined DP structure disrupts continuous brittle damage pathways and delays grain-boundary crack initiation. In addition, serrated grain boundaries may further impede crack propagation. Consequently, the dominant failure mode shifts from intergranular fracture to ductile fracture. These findings indicate that Zr-induced DP refinement mitigates grain-boundary damage and improves ductility in the studied alloy at 700 °C, suggesting a potential microstructural design route for alleviating ITE in L12-strengthened HEAs. © 2026

title: A critical review on the formability and improvement strategies of wrought magnesium alloys
abstract: Wrought magnesium (Mg) alloys offer exceptional lightweighting potential for transportation vehicles, yet their limited formability, especially at room temperature, remains a major barrier to broader applications. This review systematically summarizes recent progress in technological development for improving the formability of wrought Mg alloys, focusing on the mechanistic origins of poor formability, assessment methodologies, alloy‑ and process‑specific improvement strategies, and the engineering validations and gaps for secondary-formed Mg sheet components. The limited formability of Mg alloys is primarily attributed to the intrinsically low number of readily activated independent slip systems in hexagonal close‑packed Mg, coupled with the propensity to develop strong basal textures during thermomechanical processing. For coarse‑grained Mg alloys, introducing pre‑existing twinning via pre‑compression can enhance subsequent formability by facilitating detwinning‑dominated deformation. For fine‑grained alloys, weakening basal texture and promoting non‑basal slip via targeted alloying and optimized processing routes are central to achieving higher ductility and stretch formability. Additional approaches, including engineered heterogeneous grain structures and the introduction of deformable second phases, primarily aim to increase work‑hardening capacity and uniform elongation by stimulating geometrically necessary dislocations and improving strain accommodation. These potential strategies are often applied across different grain-size regimes, depending on the specific alloy and processing conditions, rather than being strictly limited to a particular grain-size range. Finally, Mg alloy sheets have certain weight reduction potential under the condition of meeting specific stiffness requirements, but their widespread application in automobile body structures still needs to undergo rigorous multi-constraint verification. © 2026

title: Making large time series models work for urban load forecasting: A dual-stream large-lightweight hybrid framework with trend–fluctuation decomposition
abstract: Accurate short-term urban aggregate load forecasting (SULF) supports power system operation. At 15-minute resolution, urban load combines lower-variation temporal structure with rapid fluctuations associated with weather, calendar effects, and recurring operating schedules. Large time-series models (LTMs) provide reusable long-context representations. However, their rigid architectures make it difficult to model the joint effects of exogenous covariates and load composition heterogeneity in SULF, limiting cross-regional deployment. We propose CRD-DLF, a dual-stream framework that combines an LTM with a lightweight multivariate MLP-Mixer through trend–fluctuation decomposition. The LTM forecasts the lower-variation stream, while the MLP-Mixer models the rapidly varying stream. Within the latter, the Industrial Load Separator (IndSep) extracts a schedule-dependent, covariate-insensitive forecasting component associated with recurring industrial operating patterns in aggregate observations. The remaining fluctuations are modeled using meteorological and calendar covariates. Adaptive fusion combines the branch forecasts, and the Patch Structural Loss encourages structural consistency during training. Tests on the Lishui citywide and county-level datasets show that CRD-DLF improves forecasting accuracy and stability relative to the plain LTM and other state-of-the-art methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Orientation-geometry correction for quantitative radial Raman analysis of carbon fiber based on the G-band tensor
abstract: Radial Raman spectroscopy is widely utilized to probe the skin-core architecture of carbon fibers. However, the continuous variation in spatial orientation of graphitic crystallites across the cross-section heavily modulates the Raman scattering intensity under a fixed polarized laser. Consequently, the conventionally measured Raman intensity ratio (AD1/AG) manifests as a convoluted apparent signal, where intrinsic microstructural gradients are severely distorted by geometric optical artifacts. To address this fundamental challenge, we established a rigorous orientation-geometry decoupling framework grounded in Raman tensor physics. Utilizing highly oriented pyrolytic graphite as a macroscopic, structurally uniform model, the exact E2g G-band tensor response was experimentally isolated to purely formulate the geometric modulation mechanism. To systematically evaluate this methodology, this framework was applied to a comprehensive library of polyacrylonitrile-based carbon fibers with customized structural states. By correlating the recovered intrinsic Raman responses (R′) with the reciprocal in-plane crystallite size of graphene (1/La) independently derived from micro-beam wide-angle X-ray scattering—a bulk technique fundamentally immune to optical polarization interferences—we confirm the accuracy and reliability of the proposed decoupling process. The tensor-based decoupling effectively strips away optical measurement artifacts and substantially strengthens the linear correlation between R′ and 1/La. More importantly, the post-decoupling slopes move closer to the theoretical expectation of the Tuinstra-Koenig relation. This work provides a universal physical paradigm for the authentic quantitative profiling of highly anisotropic carbon materials. © 2026

title: Taming the boundary effect: Femtosecond laser slicing of 4H-SiC enabled by side scribing for improved processability
abstract: The 4H polytype of silicon carbide (4H-SiC) has excellent properties such as high electron mobility and high saturation electron velocity; ithas therefore become an important material for high-power and high-frequency devices. In the slicing step of wafer fabrication, however,conventional wire-saw cutting is constrained by the inherent high hardness and brittleness of 4H-SiC, causing excessive material removal andsurface and subsurface damage. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a femtosecond laser slicing technology combined with sidescribing. A simulation model of the boundary effect in internal laser processing was established to analyze the optical energy distribution underspherical aberration. The simulations revealed boundary regions that resist laser modification because of the coupling between asymmetricfocusing and spherical aberration, which degrades the slicing quality of conventional laser processing. Systematic parametric experimentswere then used to investigate the influence of the laser processing parameters on the formation of the modified layer. Targeted experimentsperformed using the optimized processing parameters provided a quantitative characterization of the hard-to-modify regions and guided theapplication of the side-scribing process. The peeling results demonstrate that the proposed side-scribing-assisted femtosecond laser slicingprocess effectively reduces the peeling stress and the cracking that occurs during slicing, achieving a 68% reduction in peeling stress and a 27%reduction in the arithmetic mean roughness Sa of the peeled surface, together with the formation of laser-induced periodic surface structuresthat are better suited to subsequent processing, compared with conventional laser slicing. This study improves the processability of 4H-SiCwafer slicing and provides a new approach to substrate preparation for wide-bandgap semiconductor materials. © 2026 Author(s).

title: A four-shank 32-channel microelectrode array integrated with FPGA-based online processing for multichannel neural recording
abstract: Multichannel neuralrecording requires not only microelectrode arrays(MEAs) with sufficientspatial coverage but also stable front-end acquisition and online signal processing hardware. In this work, a four-shank 32-channel MEA and a field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-basedonline processing module are developed for multichannel neural recording. The four-shank structure is designed to provide broader spatialcoverage while maintaining a compact probe footprint. Platinum nanoparticles (PtNPs) are modified on the electrode surfaces to improvethe electrical interface of the recording sites. Electrochemical measurements demonstrate that PtNPs modification significantly improves theinterfacial properties of the electrodes. An FPGA-based module is employed to enable communication with the front-end chip and performonline signal processing. Post-implementation verification further demonstrates that the FPGA design satisfies the timing constraints whilemaintaining acceptable power consumption. The end-to-end performance of the electrophysiological recording chain is evaluated throughgain/bandwidth testing and simulated neural signal detection. The system exhibits an average gain of 45.57 dB within the main passband, witha bandwidth ranging from 4.28 to 2.36 kHz. In addition, simulated spike tests demonstrate stable online detection and waveform extraction.In addition, in vivo recordings from the hippocampal CA1 region demonstrate that the proposed system simultaneously acquires clear spikeand local field potential signals from multiple channels, with representative spike waveforms exhibiting good consistency. The combinationof a four-shank MEA with PtNPs-modified recording sites and FPGA-based online processing supports stable neural signal acquisition bothin vitro and in vivo and provides a useful foundation for future neural interface applications. © 2026 Author(s).

title: Correlation study of vortices and pressure pulsations in multistage centrifugal pump as turbine
abstract: Multistage centrifugal pumps operating as turbines (PATs) are important devices for hydraulic energy recovery. However, vortex-induced flow instabilities cause pressure pulsations and efficiency losses, especially in configurations with complex interstage interactions. In offshore oil and gas field systems—such as platform seawater systems, produced-water treatment systems, and subsea energy recovery—stable PAT operation is essential for reliability and continuous energy utilization. This study investigates the correlation between vortex evolution and pressure pulsation across different stages of a multistage PAT. Numerical simulations and Pearson correlation analysis reveal that in the first three stages, vorticity and pressure pulsation distributions exhibit strong spatial consistency. From the second to the last stage, both vorticity intensity and pressure pulsation amplitude increase markedly compared with the first stage. The first stage maintains a stable flow with weak dynamic–static effects, while downstream stages show less stability, dominated by dynamic interactions. In high-vorticity regions, vortex evolution is the primary cause of pressure fluctuation, and its correlation with pulsation intensity is strongest. In later stages, the vortex–pressure correlation weakens as complex interstage dynamics prevail. Overall, the results confirm a positive correlation between vorticity and pressure pulsation intensity at various locations within the multistage PAT. These findings provide theoretical insight and practical guidance for optimizing impeller–diffuser matching and stage configuration, enabling improved hydraulic stability and enhanced energy recovery efficiency, particularly under offshore and subsea operating conditions. © 2026 Author(s).

title: Synergistic Effect of Dual Ionic Liquid PVDF-HFP Polymer Inclusion Membranes: Linking Mechanical, Chemical, Microstructural and Gold Recovery Performance; [PVDF-HFP полимеріне екі иондық сұйықтықты қосу арқылы мембраналардың синергетикалық әсері: механикалық, химиялық, микроқұрылымдық қасиеттер мен алтынды алу тиімділігі арасындағы байланыс]; [Синергетический эффект мембран с включением двух ионных жидкостей в полимер PVDF-HFP: связь между механическими, химическими, микроструктурными свойствами и эффективностью извлечения золота]
abstract: Poly (vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP) polymer inclusion membranes (PIMs) are widely used across separation industries because of their ability to selectively separate ions or molecules, their chemical stability, and their mechanical flexibility. Still, improving how the membrane performs without making the membrane material properties deteriorate remains a challenge. In this study, Aliquat 336 and Cyphos IL 104 were blended with PVDF-HFP and fabricated through the solvent casting method. The main objective of this study is to understand how the ionic liquids can affect the membrane’s chemical properties, physical properties, mechanical stability, and its ability to recover gold through an H-cell setup. FTIR analysis confirmed the presence of Aliquat 336, showing bands associated with quaternary ammonium groups, while Cyphos IL 104 displayed vibrations related to phosphonium-related P–C. SEM images further revealed clear differences in how the membrane morphology looked. Pure PVDF-HFP alone had compact surfaces; Aliquat 336 membranes appeared to have smoother features, and Cyphos IL 104 membranes developed rougher surfaces with micro-voids. The addition of ionic liquids also increased membrane porosity from 25 % in the pure membrane to 45 % with the addition of ionic liquids. At the same time, the contact angle dropped from 90° to 58°, indicating improved hydrophilicity. Mechanical testing showed that pure PVDF-HFP had the highest tensile strength (30 MPa), modulus (450 MPa), and tear resistance (2.5 N/mm). Membranes with higher Aliquat 336 content retained better tear resistance, close to 2.0 N/mm, while maintaining smoother membrane surfaces. In comparison, the addition of Cyphos IL 104 adversely impacts the mechanical properties. Gold extraction experiments showed promising performance. The PVDF-HFP/A15C20 membrane achieved 76 % recovery within 12 h. The combination of both Aliquat 336 and Cyphos IL 104 improved ion transport while maintaining acceptable membrane stability properties. Overall, the results showed that the ionic liquid composition has a strong influence on both the membrane’s durability properties and separation performance. These findings provide a useful approach for developing membranes in precious metal recovery applications. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Unlocking cooperative geometries in inverse spinel CuCo2O4 for superior catalytic oxidation of chlorinated VOCs
abstract: The low-temperature catalytic oxidation of chlorinated volatile organic compounds (CVOCs) is challenged by chlorine poisoning and toxic byproducts, while the correlation between tetrahedral(Td)/octahedral(Oh) cation geometric configurations and dechlorination pathways remains unclear. Herein, a series of cation-regulated spinel catalysts were constructed to unlock cooperative geometric sites for dichloromethane (DCM) oxidation. Structural characterizations verified that Cu2 + preferentially occupies Oh sites, inducing an inverse spinel (CoTd3+[CuOh2+CoOh3+]O4) that triggers Jahn–Teller lattice distortion, enhances oxygen vacancy and optimizes Co electronic structure. Consequently, CuCo2O4 achieves 91% DCM conversion and 94.1% CO2 selectivity at 200 °C, with excellent stability and negligible polychlorinated byproducts. Integrated in-situ spectroscopies and DFT calculations unravel a triple‑site anti-chlorination mechanism, in which CoOh3+ sites polarize and cleave C–Cl bonds to form *O-CH2Cl, adjacent CuOh2+-OH donate protons to promote HCl desorption, and CoTd3+ sites activate O2 to sustain deep oxidation. This synergy reduces the rate-determining rearrangement barrier from 0.27 eV on Co3O4 to 0.13 eV on CuCo2O4. The balanced Cl⁻ affinity of CuOh2+ (−3.16 eV) and Cu–O–Co orbital hybridization further enhance charge transfer and redox cycling, avoiding irreversible chlorination. This work unravels the geometric configuration-dependent anti-chlorination mechanism and provides a cationic site modulation strategy for robust spinel catalysts toward CVOCs oxidation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Mathematical modeling and ecological assessment of fluoride release in a mixture of mineralized phosphorite waste and wastewater from the fat and oil industry; [Минералданған фосфорит қалдықтары мен май-май өнеркәсібінің ақаба сулары қоспасындағы фтордың бөлінуін математикалық модельдеу және экологиялық бағалау]; [Математическое моделирование и экологическая оценка высвобождения фтора в смеси минерализованных фосфоритных отходов и сточных вод масложировой промышленности]
abstract: This study investigates fluoride loss in a mixture of mineralized mass (MM) extracted from the Central Kyzylkum phosphorite deposits and acidic wastewater (AWW) generated by the fat-and-oil industry. The research aimed to evaluate fluoride release and its retention stability under various conditions. Experimental trials were conducted using AWW:MM mass ratios ranging from 100:10 to 100:40. The experiments were carried out at 333 K for 30 minutes, employing ionometric analysis. The theoretical fluoride content varied from 1.23 g to 4.90 g, while the experimental values ranged from 0.88 g to 3.68 g. The lowest fluoride loss was observed at the 100:20 ratio, amounting to 0.34 g. The highest loss, 1.22 g, was recorded at the 100:40 ratio. The 100:25 ratio (pH 5.90), with a fluoride loss of 0.40 g and an experimental retention of 2.66 g, was identified as optimal. At pH values between 6.33 and 7.30, fluoride levels stabilized between 3.08 g and 3.68 g. An exponential regression model demonstrated a high degree of correlation (R² = 0.9767). The standard deviation ranged from ±0.002 g to ±0.008 g. Ions in AWW (SO₄²⁻: 48,145 mg/L and Cl⁻: 38,116 mg/L) significantly accelerated fluoride volatilization. The emission of HF gas contributed to atmospheric pollution; however, the 100:25 ratio minimized environmental impact. The results aligned with literature-reported fluoride loss ranges of 0.3–1.5 g. This research contributes to the development of effective and environmentally safe approaches to waste reutilization. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Tandem catalysis of Al-rich Cu/FAU-EMT intergrowth zeolites for boosting the selective catalytic reduction of NOx with ammonia
abstract: Different topological ratios of Al-rich FAU-EMT intergrowth zeolites were synthesized via one-pot hydrothermal method with double templates. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Cs-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) coupled with an annular dark field (ADF) images jointly confirmed the presence of twinned FAU-EMT interfaces. 29Si magic angle spinning (MAS) nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) revealed the FAU-EMT zeolites have excellent skeleton crystallinity, along with more pronounced SBET compared to sole-phase zeolites. In particular, the Cu/FAU-EMT-50% showed the surprising low-temperature activity, achieving nearly complete NO conversion across wide-temperature window (150–550 °C). Series of copper species characterization demonstrated the highly active [Cu(OH)]+ ions are primarily active sites over Cu/FAU-EMT, and no significant distribution of less active copper species has been detected. In addition, the [Cu(OH)]+ ions on FAU-EMT interface have an appropriate d-band center, which are conducive to both ammonia adsorption and intermediate species activation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations indicated that the EMT phase is more conducive to the adsorption of sufficient NH3, which then carries the reactive [Cu(OH)(NH3)3]+ species to migrate locally to the FAU phase, where SCR reactions are favored, thereby achieving synergistic effects at twinned FAU-EMT interfaces. Hence, the Cu/FAU-EMT intergrowth zeolitic catalysts exhibit an extraordinary performance for NOx removal. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Optimal evaporation regime of alkaline solution obtained from cotton stalk ash and chemical analysis of precipitation process; [Мақта сабағы күлінен алынған сілтілі ерітіндінің оңтайлы буландыру режимі және тұнба түзілу процесінің химиялық талдауы]; [Оптимальный режим выпаривания щелочного раствора, полученного из золы стеблей хлопчатника, и химический анализ процесса образования осадка]
abstract: This article describes a comprehensive analysis of the optimal evaporation method for an alkaline solution that is prepared using the aqueous extract of cotton stalk ash, along with the investigation of the chemical composition of the precipitation that appears during evaporation of the solution. Cotton stalk ash is regarded as a secondary product from burning biomass in household appliances, specifically in tandir ovens used to bake bread and somsa, and is currently being discarded into the environment. In the presented research, the procedure for preparation of the alkaline solution was conducted under optimal conditions, when the mixture of ash and water with the weight ratio of 1:5 was boiled. Then, filtration and evaporation of the obtained suspension were performed. From the results obtained, the optimal evaporation regime was identified as 75%, as during this regime no precipitation occurs. Nevertheless, at an evaporation level of 80%, precipitation was observed in the solution due to the disturbance of the solubility equilibrium. The content of the precipitated components in relation to cations was estimated using flame photometry, and the phase composition was evaluated with FTIR spectroscopy. Thus, the precipitate was found to contain mainly carbonate-like compounds. It was proved that potassium ions prevailed in the solution, and their molar concentration is much greater than that of other cations. Moreover, when the concentration is high, a certain share of potassium ions is transferred from the solution into the precipitate phase. As calculated, the total alkalinity of the prepared solution equals 3.41 N and constitutes about half of the alkalinity of the 6 N NaOH solution employed in the vegetable oils purification process. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: NPR-NLMMI hybrid mode-locked fiber laser with an SMF-PCF-GIMF-SMF saturable absorber
abstract: This study demonstrates a hybrid mode-locked fiber laser by incorporating a single-mode fiber-photonic crystal fiber-graded-index multimode fiber-single-mode fiber (SMF-PCF-GIMF-SMF) structure as a saturable absorber (SA) into a nonlinear polarization rotation cavity.The SA exhibits a modulation depth of 5.8% and a saturation intensity of 59.8 μJ/cm2. Stable fundamental mode-locking is achieved at acenter wavelength of 1555 nm with a 3 dB spectral width of 7.2 nm. Compared to the hybrid mode-locked laser employing a conventionalSMF-GIMF-SMF SA, the proposed SA reduces the fundamental-frequency mode-locking threshold from 120 to 50 mW, improves the signalto-noise ratio of the RF spectrum from 35 to 48 dB, and decreases the pulse width from 580 to 493 fs. Harmonic mode-locking up to the eighthorder is achieved by adjusting the pump power and polarization controllers. The long-term stability of the laser is confirmed by the powerfluctuation of the fundamental-frequency pulse train over an 8-h period. This compact, low-cost laser exhibits a high damage threshold andgood stability, highlighting its significant potential for both fundamental ultrafast photonics research and industrial applications. © 2026 Author(s).

title: Identification of Methane-Bearing Coal Seams in Borehole Sections of the Karaganda Basin Using Geophysical Logging Data; [Қарағанды бассейні ұңғымалары кесіндісінде метаны мол көмір қабаттарын геофизикалық каротаж деректері бойынша бөліп шығару]; [Выделение метаноносных угольных пластов в разрезе скважин Карагандинского бассейна по данным геофизического каротажа]
abstract: The Karaganda coal basin is one of the most gas-bearing in the world. Its feature is that there are no large accumulations of free gas in it, while the natural gas content reaches up to 25-30 m³/t; this is confirmed by a large volume of gas sampling, gas logging data, and gas survey data in operating mines. Methane from coal seams enters the atmosphere through natural migration through overlying rocks, as well as at the places where seams outcrop under overburden and through the shafts of closed mines. During degassing of coal seams in the Karaganda basin during the opening of seams by mine workings, including during open-pit mining, seam outcrops to the surface, degassing of the worked-out space of closed mines, part of the extracted methane is used at the mines for obtaining thermal and electrical energy, and the larger part enters the atmosphere during degassing of coal seams. It is known that methane entering the atmosphere retains the Earth's heat significantly higher, by 25-30 times, than carbon dioxide. The extraction of methane from unloaded coal seams for its industrial use in obtaining thermal and electrical energy is an important task in the development of technologies for the integrated development of coal-methane deposits, as well as for reducing the environmental load on the regions where they are located. The purpose of the research is the identification in the section of gas-bearing coal seams for assessing the potential of methane extraction from unloaded seams for its industrial use and reducing emissions into the atmosphere. Methods. A complex of geophysical methods for studying exploration wells to investigate the physico-mechanical and filtration-capacity properties of coal seams and host rocks, sampling and analysis of coal seam samples in mine workings. Results. Patterns of changes in the complex of physical properties of coal seams determining their gas content have been established, geological justification for these changes and changes in the physico-mechanical properties of host rocks has been given. Application. The gas-bearing coal seams identified in the section can be used in planning methane extraction from all gas-bearing seams of the geological section, including coal seams being developed by mines, and the patterns of changes in physico-mechanical and filtration-capacity properties of coal seams prepared for development or being developed can be used in geomechanical calculations. The factual materials for conducting the research were obtained from the results of laboratory and geophysical studies of exploration wells, materials from geological and production reports. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Biomass-derived amorphous carbon-modified NiFe-LDH for efficient urea electrooxidation: Electron-deficient Ni3+ sites induced by interfacial electron transfer
abstract: Replacing the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) with the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) offers a promising route for energy-efficient hydrogen production and the electrochemical treatment of urea-containing wastewater. However, the practical application of UOR is still hindered by insufficient anode durability and sluggish UOR kinetics. Herein, biomass chitosan was employed as the carbon precursor to fabricate amorphous carbon-modified coral-like NiFe layered double hydroxide (NiFe-LDH), which was in-situ anchored on nickel foam via a facile one-step hydrothermal strategy. The optimized catalyst achieved remarkable UOR electrocatalysis, requiring only 0.94 V and 0.96 V overpotential to reach 50 mA·cm−2 and 100 mA·cm−2, respectively, accompanied by a small Tafel slope of 22 mV·dec−1 and outstanding long-term stability exceeding 1000 h at 100 mA·cm−2. Operando spectroscopic characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations indicated that electron-withdrawing functional groups on chitosan-derived amorphous carbon induced interfacial electron transfer, which stabilized electron-deficient Ni3+ sites. This pre-stabilized Ni3+ facilitated the in-situ generation of active γ-NiOOH at low potential, while γ-NiOOH served as the catalytic phase to drive the UOR; the complementary synergy between the two significantly enhanced the overall catalytic performance. This study affords a versatile interfacial modulation protocol for designing high-performance crystalline/amorphous hybrid electrocatalysts, which may offer a promising route for sustainable energy conversion and the electrochemical treatment of urea-containing wastewater. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Influence of gas flow parameters on the velocity of bulk materials; [Газ ағыны параметрлерінің сусымалы материалдардың ағу жылдамдығына әсері]; [Влияние параметров газового потока на скорость истечения сыпучих материалов]
abstract: This article examines the flow patterns and kinetics of granular media interacting with ascending and descending gas flows. Bulk material release control is a critical aspect of shaft furnace and hopper operation Experimental studies were conducted on a flat transparent model and a close-up "hot" model using high-speed video recording (SK-16). With an error in the calculated values of the critical speed, amounting from to-30.0 to +28.8%, the main parameters varied within the following limits: specific gravity and viscosity of the gas, respectively, from 11.97 to 1.16 N/m3; from 8,9 ⋅ 10−6 to 1.81 ⋅ 10−5 Pa ⋅ s; diameter, specific gravity and coefficient of internal friction of bulk material from 4,0 ⋅ 10−4 to 15.0 ⋅ 10−3 m; from 14.3 to 39.2 kN/m3; from 0.55 to 0.95; coefficient taking into account the shape of the particles, from 6.0 to 7.8; outlet diameter from0.01 to 0.06 m; attitude equals 0,02 − 0,4. The materials studied were agglomerate, lime, millet, and coke; the gas phases were air, helium, and hydrogen. It was established that the outflow mechanism is staged and determined by the frequency of destruction of dynamically unstable vaults. It was found that gas density is the key factor influencing the outflow rate, while the effect of viscosity is secondary. An analytical relationship was formulated for calculating the critical gas velocity that causes layer suspension. The obtained data make it possible to optimize the design parameters of outlet openings and blast supply modes in metallurgical units. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Stability of the critical constant steady state of a Keller–Segel model
abstract: In this paper, we prove the asymptotic stability of the critical constant steady state for a simplified parabolic–elliptic Keller–Segel system in RN ( N ≥ 3), which admits a one-parameter family of constant steady states. Although the stability threshold for constant steady states is known, the critical case has remained open. We also show that the convergence rate in the critical case differs from the rates obtained for previously studied subcritical constant steady states. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Comparative analysis of loss-aware optimal power flow considering droop-controlled inverters
abstract: The rapid integration of renewable energy sources into distribution networks necessitates advanced voltage regulation strategies, such as smart inverter Volt-VAR droop control with dead-bands. However, conventional linearized optimal power flow (OPF) models frequently overlook network losses, resulting in suboptimal reactive power allocation. This study presents a comparative analysis of three loss-aware OPF formulations tailored for inverter-dominated grids employing piecewise linear droop control. The iterative mixed-integer linear program (MILP) linearizes quadratic loss terms using successive Taylor expansions within a trust-region framework. The mixed-integer quadratically constrained quadratic program (MIQCQP) relaxes nonconvex loss equalities into convex quadratic inequalities, incorporating a reactive loss penalty. The two-stage MILP + AC-OPF enforces the full nonlinear AC power flow equations as optimization constraints. These formulations are evaluated on a combined IEEE 30-bus and 33-bus transmission–distribution system under four scenarios that vary photovoltaic (PV) capacity, flexible AC transmission system (FACTS) device availability, and inverter reactive power limits, and on a modified 250-bus T118D4 system with 40 PV inverters. The iterative MILP and MIQCQP converge to nearly identical generation costs. The AC-OPF achieves 1.0–2.3% lower generation costs and 5–20% lower reactive power losses through different reactive power allocations. All three formulations yield AC-feasible dispatches, but their reactive power allocations differ substantially, highlighting that AC feasibility alone does not ensure dispatch optimality. On T118D4, the MIQCQP more closely reproduces the AC-OPF voltage and reactive power dispatch, whereas the iterative MILP solves faster, revealing a tradeoff between agreement with the AC-OPF benchmark and computational efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Phase-stability engineering of oxide scales in multicomponent (Hf,Zr,Sc)B2 coatings for durable cyclic ablation resistance
abstract: The growing demand for reusable thermal protection systems calls for ceramic coatings that can retain protective oxide scales under repeated ultra-high-temperature ablation. However, conventional ultra-high-temperature ceramic (UHTC) coatings often fail under thermal cycling because their HfO2/ZrO2-dominated oxide scales suffer phase-transformation-induced cracking and delamination. Here, we address this limitation by incorporating Sc into multicomponent (Hf,Zr,Sc)B2 solid-solution coatings to engineer oxide-scale phase stability. The optimized coating containing 10 mol% Sc maintains scale integrity after 6 × 120 s exposures at temperatures above 2300 °C and exhibits a negative linear recession rate of −0.11 μm s−1. Multiscale characterization of the resulting oxide scale reveals partial tetragonal-to-monoclinic martensitic transformation within parent tetragonal grains, producing monoclinic laths while retaining Sc-stabilized metastable tetragonal domains and thereby limiting the overall transformation-induced volumetric strain. These tetragonal domains are preferentially retained at grain boundaries and triple junctions along intergranular crack paths, a spatial distribution consistent with transformation-associated crack tolerance. These findings establish phase-stability engineering of oxide scales as an effective strategy for maintaining scale integrity and protecting high-temperature structural materials under repeated extreme thermal exposure. © 2026

title: Sulfur-vacancy-regulated adjacent Cu-Bi sites enable cooperative CO2 and nitrate adsorption for efficient urea electrosynthesis
abstract: Electrochemical urea synthesis by coupling CO2 reduction with nitrate reduction provides a new route to convert carbon- and nitrogen-containing feedstocks into value-added chemicals. Its efficiency, however, is limited by sluggish C-N coupling and competing side reactions. Here, sulfur-vacancy-rich Cu/Bi co-doped NiS2 hierarchical microspheres were prepared through a MOF-derived strategy to construct adjacent Cu-Bi dual sites for urea electrosynthesis. The Cu/Bi co-doping with sulfur vacancies regulates the local coordination and electronic structure of active sites. Particularly, the Cu sites preferentially stabilize *CO intermediates, whereas neighboring Bi sites facilitate NO3⁻ adsorption and activation, thereby favoring the subsequent C-N coupling. Additionally, the sulfur vacancies further reconstruct the local Cu-Bi environment, enhance H2O adsorption and activation, and regulate the utilization of active hydrogen intermediate (*H) while suppressing the competing hydrogen evolution reaction. Operando ATR-IR, in situ Raman spectroscopy, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal the evolution of carbon- and nitrogen-containing intermediates and support the *CO-*NO coupling pathway toward urea formation. As a result, the CuBi-NiS2 delivers a urea yield rate of 912.41 μgurea h⁻1 mgcat.⁻1 with a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 30.8% at −0.6 V (vs. RHE), with stable electrocatalytic performance. This work offers a defect-engineered dual-site approach to promote selective electrochemical C-N bond formation. © 2026 The Authors

title: Placer formation processes in the cenozoic of Northern and Eastern Kazakhstan; [Солтүстік және Шығыс Қазақстан Кайнозойындағы шашылымдардың түзілу процестері]; [Процессы Россыпеобразования в Кайнозое Северного и Восточного Казахстана]
abstract: The article is devoted to the generalization of data on the entire geological and genetic range of placers in Eastern and Northern Kazakhstan: from the weathering of the kaolin profile at the root sources of ore minerals Au, Ni, Co, RM, Ti, Zr, Nb, TR, through polyfacial and alluvial placers of the near demolition of the Zaisan depression to coastal-marine titanium-zirconium placers Northern Kazakhstan and Pavlodar Irtysh region. The sections and patterns of ore localization for gold-and nickel-bearing weathering crusts of the Rudny Altai are considered in more detail. An idea is given of the different conditions of formation of the Paleocene-Miocene ilmenite placers of the Zaisan Depression, depending on the tectonic regime – rifting in the Paleocene-Eocene and orogeny in the Lower Miocene. The dating of titanium-zirconium placers of the Pavlodar Irtysh region has been clarified due to the large-scale removal of silicon from the eluvium of the Kazakh shield. The relationship of the processes of coastal-marine placer formation with regional paleogeographic changes in Central Eurasia, starting with the collision of Hindustan and Eurasia and the Paleocene-Lower Eocene temperature maximum, is shown. The role of the completion of water exchange between the Tethys and Arctic shelf seas in the occurrence of constant westerly winds from the Tarim and Gobi, which played a major role in the formation of placers in the northern border of the Kazakh Shield, is shown. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Systems metabolic engineering of a plasmid-free Escherichia coli cell factory for high-level cytidine production
abstract: Cytidine is an important precursor for nucleoside pharmaceuticals, but its fermentative production is constrained by competing degradation, poor selectivity of pyrimidine flux, insufficient precursor supply, and energy-redox imbalance. In this study, a plasmid-free E. coli cell factory was constructed through systems metabolic engineering. Sequential deletion of cytidine degradation, salvage, and precursor-consuming pathways enabled initial cytidine accumulation. The conversion from UMP to CMP was strengthened by introducing feedback-deregulated pyrH D93A and pyrG D160E, E162A, E168Kcgl mutants and nudG , while the heterologous expression of PHM8 sce improved CMP-to-cytidine conversion selectivity. Scaffold-based assembly of PyrF, PyrHD93A, NudG, and PHM8sce using CipA/CipB further improved local pathway channeling and reduced uridine formation by 98.70%. To reinforce upstream flux, de novo UMP biosynthesis was reconstructed with the B. subtilis pyr operon, PRPP synthesis was enhanced, and nitrogen-donor and pyrimidine-ring precursor supply was improved through glnA , ppc , and aspC expression. Finally, an ATP-responsive ydaO motif regulatory module was used to dynamically control respiratory-chain and oxygen-utilization modules, coordinating ATP supply with NAD+ regeneration. The final strain cyt 23 produced 96.20 g/L cytidine in 50 h in a 5 L fed-batch bioreactor, with a glucose conversion yield of 0.38 g/g and productivity of 1.92 g/(L·h), representing the highest reported titer, yield and productivity for microbial cytidine production to date. This work provides an integrated strategy for high-level microbial cytidine production and nucleoside cell-factory development. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Hydrodynamic characteristics of a pump as turbine under periodic inflow fluctuations
abstract: In seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) systems, the pump as turbine (PAT) recovers energy of high-pressure brine by coupling with high-pressure pumps. This can significantly reduce the system’s specific energy consumption. However, the upstream flow rate to the PAT is not constant during operation. It typically fluctuates within a certain range, thus affecting the stability of the PAT during actual operation. Therefore, this study uses computational fluid dynamics to investigate the transient flow behavior of a PAT with a fixed-axis and constant-torque connected load pump under periodic fluctuations in the incoming flow. To simulate the fluctuating flow process, user-defined functions are implemented to describe the instantaneous flow variations and capture the transient hydrodynamic characteristics at various fluctuation frequencies. The numerical simulation results are validated against experimental data. The results indicate that when the PAT is subjected to periodic inflow fluctuations, the rotational speed, torque, and internal flow field of the impeller vary significantly with the flow rate. This will exert a significant impact on the efficiency and stability of PAT operation. Meanwhile, the external characteristic parameters (head, power, and efficiency) and stability of the PAT are also affected by the inflow fluctuation frequency. At higher inflow fluctuation frequency, the PAT system exhibits higher average efficiency and a small axial force fluctuation in the impeller, but the radial force fluctuation is more intense. The results obtained in this study can provide theoretical support for the anti-interference design and operational optimization of PAT energy recovery systems in SWRO systems. © 2026 Author(s).

title: An AFM DNA image-segmentation method based on random height mapping and a Sobel-guided attention module
abstract: DNA conformational analysis requires accurate molecule-level delineation, meaning that segmentation is a prerequisite for quantitative analysis of atomic force microscopy (AFM) height maps. Although AFM provides direct height imaging, in grayscale renderings, DNA boundariesare often obscured by limited contrast. Salt deposits and scanning artifacts can produce fragmented traces and cause DNA to be merged spuriously with nearby salt deposits in the segmentation results. AFM images acquired under different scanning conditions often vary in contrastand sharpness, and the resulting degraded appearance challenges the robustness of segmentation. We propose a framework that integrates (i)quantile-bounded RGB mapping, (ii) Sobel-guided attention in UNet skip connections, and (iii) random-mapping training for robustness.With all components enabled (quantile-bounded RGB mapping, Sobel-guided attention at Skip1, and random-mapping training), the finalmodel achieves an intersection over union (IoU) of 0.74 and a Dice score of 0.85 on the AFM test set. To assess robustness to boundarysmoothing, we further applied post hoc Gaussian blur to the test inputs. At a Gaussian blur standard deviation of 3 pixels, the model trainedwith random mapping retains an IoU of 0.46, whereas the counterpart trained with fixed mapping drops to 0.26, an absolute gain of 0.20.Additional Gaussian-noise experiments on raw AFM height maps confirm that random-mapping training improves robustness to stochasticheight-domain perturbations. Together, these results indicate that combining imaging-aware height-to-color encoding with training-timerandomized mapping and lightweight, gradient-guided reweighting of skip features offers a practical route to robust and stable AFM–DNAsegmentation, with potential transferability to other AFM image-analysis tasks. © 2026 Author(s).

title: Study of the mechanism and efficiency of using mineral-organic bleaching-filtering agents in polishing refining; [Минералды-органикалық ағартқыш-сүзгілеуіш агенттерді жылтырату рафинациясында қолдану механизмі мен тиімділігін зерттеу]; [Исследование механизма и эффективности применения минерально-органических отбеливающе-фильтрующих агентов при полировочной рафинации]
abstract: In this scientific study, the main objective is to purify vegetable oils stored in the state reserve for an extended period to reach consumable quality based on their physicochemical parameters. In the experiments, polishing refining of cottonseed oils stored for 6 months or longer was carried out. By analyzing the physicochemical parameters of polishing-refined vegetable oils, selective bleaching-filtering agents (BFAs) with various pore structures were obtained for use in the bleaching-filtration stage. The BFAs were obtained through acid activation of bentonitic and opoka-type clays, as well as pyrolysis of sunflower husk. The filtration capacities of each activated BFA toward polishing-refined oils were investigated. The findings show that the highest efficiency was achieved when a composite BFA of the BK grade-prepared at a 1:1 mass ratio of acid-activated Navbahor alkali bentonite (ANAB) and pyrolyzed sunflower husk (P-SH) was added at 1.5-2.0% relative to the oil mass. The research results demonstrate that a composition consisting of polar organic and non-polar inorganic components was successfully obtained, capable of filtering fine soapstock particles while not resisting pressure buildup during the filtration process. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Beyond a sintering aid: Dual-function Li2CO3 enabling low-temperature co-firing and ultrahigh piezoelectricity in PNN-PZT- LiNbO3 relaxor ferroelectrics
abstract: Reconciling low-temperature co-firing compatibility with ultrahigh piezoelectricity remains a longstanding challenge for advanced multilayer piezoelectric devices. Here, a Li2CO3-enabled low-temperature lattice-regulation strategy is developed to simultaneously reduce the sintering temperature and enhance the piezoelectric performance of Pb(Ni1/3Nb2/3)O3-Pb(Zr, Ti)O3-LiNbO3 (PNN-PZT-LN) relaxor ferroelectrics. The introduction of Li2CO3 lowers the sintering temperature from 1250 to 980 °C, while the optimized ceramic exhibits an ultrahigh d33 of 1027 pC N−1, exceeding that of the conventionally sintered counterpart (905 pC N−1 at 1250 °C). This unusual combination of low-temperature processing and enhanced piezoelectricity indicates that Li2CO3 contributes beyond conventional sintering promotion. Structural and spectroscopic characterizations reveal a shifted morphotropic phase boundary, reconstructed local Pb-O and oxygen coordination environments, and softened BO6 octahedral dynamics after Li2CO3 modification. These changes are accompanied by enhanced local piezoresponse and more ordered ferroelectric domains, providing a multiscale structure-property correlation for the enhanced piezoelectric response. The Curie temperature is also increased from 106 to 118 °C. Taking advantage of the reduced firing temperature, multilayer piezoelectric ceramics and multilayer macro-fiber composite strain sensors are successfully fabricated, with the latter exhibiting a strain sensitivity of 2 mV με−1. This work demonstrates that Li2CO3 can simultaneously facilitate low-temperature densification and induce local structural regulation in PNN-PZT-LN ceramics, offering a practical route toward high-performance multilayer piezoelectric devices. © 2026
