title: Elemental Assessment of Lead–Bismuth Sludge from Copper Smelting with Emphasis on Tellurium Recovery; [Теллурды мыс балқыту арқылы алуда қорғасын-висмут шламының қарапайым бағалауы]; [Элементарная оценка свинцово-висмутового шлама при выплавке меди с акцентом на извлечение теллура]
abstract: Industrial by-products generated during copper smelting are increasingly regarded as promising secondary sources of strategically important and critical elements. Among such technogenic materials, lead–bismuth sludge formed during wet gas cleaning of sulfur-bearing gases represents a potentially valuable reservoir of selenium and tellurium. The present study provides a comprehensive elemental assessment of lead–bismuth sludge obtained from the Almalyk Mining and Metallurgical Complex (Uzbekistan). Prior to analysis, representative sludge samples were subjected to acid digestion using freshly prepared aqua regia, followed by elemental determination using inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES). Particular attention was devoted to the distribution behavior of selenium and tellurium due to their technological importance as critical raw materials. The analytical results demonstrated that the investigated sludge is characterized by a pronounced polymetallic composition dominated by lead (20.0%), together with significant concentrations of iron (6.76%), copper (5.34%), and zinc (4.40%). Tellurium was detected at a concentration of 0.33%, indicating its selective accumulation in the lead–bismuth residue, whereas selenium was not detected under the selected analytical conditions. Based on elemental composition data and thermodynamic considerations, the investigated sludge may be considered a promising secondary source for tellurium recovery. The obtained results contribute to understanding the physicochemical behavior of chalcogen elements during copper smelting and wet gas-cleaning processes and may serve as a basis for the development of integrated recycling approaches for technogenic metallurgical waste. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Sulfate-Resistant Portland Cement Clinker Based on the Raw Material Base of Karakalpakstan: Technology, Economics and Ecology; [Қарақалпақстанның шикізат базасына негізделген сульфатқа төзімді портландцемент клинкері: технологиясы, экономикасы және экология]; [Сульфатостойкий портландцементный клинкер на основе сырьевой базы Каракалпакстана: технология, экономика и экология]
abstract: This study is devoted to the production of sulfate-resistant Portland cement clinker based on local raw materials found in the Aral Sea region of the Republic of Uzbekistan and the study of its properties. The results obtained highlight technological, economic, and environmental advantages. The raw material mixtures consisted of limestone, barren sand, kaolin, and iron-rich industrial waste, resulting in a clinker with an optimized oxide composition (LSF = 0.82, SR = 2.15, AR = 0.94). X-ray phase analysis shows a high content of alite (C3S ≈ 38.6%) and belite (C2S ≈ 41.0%) phases, which provides high mechanical strength. The low content of tricalcium aluminate (tricalcium aluminate < 5%) and the sufficient content of ferrite (C₄AF ≈ 16.2%) increased sulfate resistance and phase dominance. Sulfate resistance tests performed in accordance with ASTM C1012/C1012M showed that sulfate-resistant Portland cement had the lowest swelling index among samples placed in a 5% Na2SO4 solution, proving its high resistance compared to ordinary Portland cement and mixed cement types. The results of the experiments prove the feasibility of producing high-quality sulfate-resistant Portland cement clinker based on local raw materials and demonstrate its potential for use in the sulfate-rich conditions of the Aral Sea region. Economically, the use of local raw materials reduces production costs, the need for imports, and increases the competitiveness of the cement industry in our region. Ecologically, the long service life of sulfate-resistant Portland cement and the possibility of using industrial waste are consistent with the principles of the "green economy" and contribute to waste reduction and sustainable growth. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: A Dual-capacitor converter-type hybrid DC circuit breaker with adaptive reclosing capability
abstract: DC circuit breakers are critical equipment for fault clearance in DC power systems. Existing circuit breakers suffer from high costs, limited current-limiting capabilities, and insufficient reliability. This paper proposes a dual-capacitor converter-based hybrid DC circuit breaker topology with adaptive reclosing capability. This topology incorporates current-limiting branches to suppress the rise of fault currents. Its adaptive reclosing capability enhances circuit breaker reliability, preventing erroneous reclosing. The proposed topology primarily employs thyristors, diodes, and conventional mechanical switches for transitions during fault clearance at various stages, eliminating the need for separate capacitor charging equipment or fully controllable devices, thus offering significant economic benefits. A single-terminal equivalent DC system and a four-terminal flexible DC transmission system model are established based on the PSCAD/EMTDC simulation software. Simulations are carried out in both the single-terminal equivalent DC system and the four-terminal flexible DC transmission system. The results demonstrate that the proposed circuit breaker exhibits certain advantages in terms of reliability and economy. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Improved response of grid forming doubly fed induction generator under grid disturbances
abstract: The response of grid-forming (GFM) doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) is influenced by its power synchronization control loop (PSCL) as it establishes frequency and synchronizes the DFIG in network. A large deviation in the phase and frequency of GFM DFIG during fault may cause it to become unstable. Additionally, the response of the DC-link following a disturbance may cause the DFIG to be unstable. Addressing these challenges, an analogy is established between DC-link dynamics and swing equation through detailed modeling of DC-link, which incorporates dynamics of PSCL. This model is subsequently utilized to design proposed synchronizing and damping control. In proposed synchronizing control, a power-based synchronizing multiplier term is integrated into PSCL to minimize frequency and phase deviations of DFIG's terminal voltage, resulting in a stable response of DFIG. In the proposed damping control strategy, the current compensation term is integrated into the active current loop of the GSC. This integration minimizes variations in the DC-link voltage, resulting in a stable response of DFIG. Along with proposed control, the active and reactive currents of DFIG are controlled to meet the reactive current criterion as per the grid code. Control hardware-in-loop validation further supports the practical applicability of the proposed control. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Multiscale-engineered monolithic single-atom cobalt catalysts with micro-channels for self-driven water purification
abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer high atom utilization and tunable active sites, making them promising for Fenton-like water purification. However, integrating powder-form SACs into monolithic structures while preserving atomic-scale sites and efficient mass transfer remains challenging. Here, Co single atoms were anchored on ordered anodic aluminum oxide micro-channels to construct a multiscale-engineered monolithic catalyst (Co-N4O2-C@AAO) for mass-transfer-enhanced peroxymonosulfate activation and self-driven water purification. At the atomic scale, the heterointerfacial coordination of Co atoms with axial O and in-plane N supported coexisting nonradical and radical pathways, enhancing both versatile degradation performance and environmental stability. At the microscale, the AAO micro-channels significantly reduced dead volume and accelerated mass transfer. The system achieved nearly complete propranolol removal within 10 min, exhibiting a rate constant 14.3-fold higher than that of granular catalysts and exceeding most reported alumina-based monolithic catalysts in both active-site utilization and geometric efficiency. At the macroscale, the monolithic Co-N4O2-C@AAO was integrated into a self-driven reactor powered by capillary action and a mild hydraulic gradient, maintaining > 96% pollutant removal over 100 h without external electrical power input. This work demonstrates a feasible route for monolithic catalytic systems towards efficient and stable advanced wastewater treatment with potential sustainability benefits. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Coordinatively unsaturated Cu/Cu2O enables coupled hydrogen delivery and carbonyl activation for HMF electrohydrogenation
abstract: Electrocatalytic hydrogenation of biomass platform molecule offers a promising route for sustainable chemical synthesis, yet its practical application suffers from suboptimal product productivity and insufficient catalytic efficiency under high substrate concentration conditions. The fundamental challenge lies in the rational design of catalysts capable of simultaneously facilitating efficient hydrogen species (H*) delivery and effective substrate activation, wherein tuning active-site coordination and interface structure serves as the key solution. Here, we develop a facile synergistic strategy to construct dual Cu active sites in Cu2O-derived electrocatalysts. Specifically, the Cu+ species serve as the active sites for HMF hydrogenation, while the Cu0 centers are responsible for the generation of active H* radicals. By adjusting anions during microwave hydrothermal synthesis, we precisely regulate Cu coordination from low to high states. The low-coordinated LC-Cu/Cu2O exhibits exceptional activity for 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) hydrogenation to 2,5-bis(hydroxymethyl)furan (BHMF), with high BHMF Faraday efficiency (FE) of 91.21% and 89.05% at ultrahigh HMF concentrations of 0.15 M and 0.5 M, respectively. XAS and DFT results confirm its favorable structure enhances CdbndO activation, reduces reaction barriers, promotes H* production and suppresses competing hydrogen evolution, while optimized charge distribution further improves catalytic efficiency and selectivity. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Enhanced DC link voltage control in grid connected PV systems using WSOA tuned PI and HG-SEPIC converter
abstract: Grid-connected Renewable Energy Source (RES), mostly those incorporating photovoltaic (PV) panels, meets challenges comprising voltage boosting for effective power transfer and ensuring even DC link voltage. Traditional control schemes frequently face challenges in accommodating varying conditions, ensuing in shortcomings such as overshooting and sluggish response times, which eventually hinder the system's performance. This research aims to address these challenges by proposing advanced control strategy to enhance system performance and reliability. Specifically, a High-Gain Single-Ended Primary Inductor Converter (HG-SEPIC) combined with White Shark Optimization Algorithm assisted Proportional-Integral (WSOA-PI) controller is employed to efficiently manage voltage levels and improve power transfer efficiency. The proposed controller aims to improve settling time and dynamic response outputs, thereby enhancing the overall system performance. MATLAB validation extensively tests the proposed system model to determine its efficiency and performance under varied conditions. Comprehensive evaluations against existing techniques demonstrate superiority of proposed approach, highlighting its potential for practical implementation of grid system connected PV. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Proton-assisted topotactic transformation tailored tunnel-structured (Na, K)-OMS-2 oxides: Synergistic Mn4+ and oxygen vacancies for efficient soot combustion
abstract: The overcoming of performance bottlenecks in manganese oxide octahedral molecular sieve (OMS-2) remains a critical challenge for catalytic oxidation reactions. Herein, we report the rational fabrication of 2 × 2 tunnel-structured (Na, K)-OMS-2 via a proton-assisted topotactic transformation strategy, enabling the controllable incorporation of multiple cations within the tunnel framework. Catalytic performance evaluations show that (Na, K0.1)-OMS-2 achieves a significant breakthrough in the long-standing performance limitations of OMS-2 materials, exhibiting a remarkably low ignition temperature of soot particles of 267 ℃, with an apparent activation energy of 61.7 kJ/mol. Systematic characterizations reveal that the introduction of K+ into Na-OMS-2 induces synergistic regulation arising from the distinct characteristics of Na+ and K+, thereby significantly increasing the surface concentrations of Mn4+ species and oxygen vacancies while enhancing lattice-oxygen reactivity. These structural and compositional features enrich the catalyst surface with abundant nitrogen oxide and gaseous oxygen anchoring sites, thereby enabling the construction of a dual-functional surface that achieves efficient activation of NO and O2 molecules. Moreover, the catalyst maintains high catalytic stability along with prominent water and sulfur resistance, highlighting its great potential for practical applications in soot elimination. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A Node voltage violation risk based adaptive partitioning and distributed voltage control method of ADN
abstract: High penetration of distributed photovoltaics (PV) aggravates voltage violations in active distribution networks (ADNs). This paper proposes a risk-adaptive partitioning and distributed voltage control method. A risk-adaptive partitioning index is defined for network clustering incorporating a comprehensive performance index combining the regional voltage regulation capability for both overvoltage and undervoltage cases and an improved modularity index. A risk-adaptive double-layer distributed voltage control method with a risk-adaptive penalty mechanism is developed. The risk-adaptive penalty mechanism is introduced into the upper-layer objective function by updating the penalty coefficients of on-load tap changer (OLTC) and capacitor banks (CBs) operations. In the upper layer, the OLTC and CBs are coordinated on an hourly timescale to suppress the voltage violations and minimize active power losses while reducing the mechanical equipment actions. In the lower layer, the controller provides fast intra-partition voltage support and reduces power losses with a control period of 15 min. Simulations on an improved IEEE 123-bus system under different scenarios verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Self-driven bidirectional redistribution of Zr species constructing a dual oxidation barrier in SiC-ZrC ultrafine fibers
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) ultrafine fibers hold great promise for flexible thermal protection systems, yet their service temperature is severely limited by oxidative degradation above 1300 °C. Herein, SiC-ZrC ultrafine fibers (SZF) with linearly tunable Zr content are fabricated by electrospinning, electron-beam curing, and carbothermal pyrolysis. The optimal SZF-20 maintains structural integrity after oxidation at 1600 °C for 30 min and at 1300 °C for 30 h in air. Focused ion beam sectioning and transmission electron microscope reveal temperature-dependent spatial redistribution of Zr species across the oxide scale. During high-temperature oxidation, nonstoichiometric ZrOxCy intermediates redistribute inward along the advancing oxidation front and accumulate at the oxide-matrix interface, forming a linear, high-melting-point inner ZrO2 barrier. Meanwhile, some ZrO2 grains segregate outward as the SiO2 matrix crystallizes into cristobalite, pinning grain boundaries to create an outer passivation layer. This dual-barrier architecture synergistically suppresses oxygen ingress and microcrack formation, thereby enabling reliable short-term high-temperature oxidation tolerance up to 1600 °C. The assembled fiber aerogels demonstrate nearly full shape recovery with residual strain below 1% following 80% compression, good thermal shock stability over repeated rapid cycles between 1600 and 25 °C, and low thermal conductivity, highlighting their great potential as reusable high-temperature thermal protection materials. © 2026

title: Beyond passive mixing: Geometric evolution and multifunctional applications of staggered herringbone microfluidic devices
abstract: Staggered herringbone microfluidic chips are widely used passive systems for enhancing transport and interaction under laminar flow conditions, and have been extensively applied in chemical synthesis, biosensing, and cell-related studies. The performance of these systems is fundamentally governed by their geometric design, which determines mixing efficiency, mass transfer, and flow-induced stimulation. Despite their widespread adoption, the design logic connecting geometric parameters, fabrication constraints, and functional applications has not been systematically clarified. In this review, we summarize and organize the key geometric features of herringbone microstructures and their influence on fluid behavior, fabrication feasibility, and application performance. Representative design strategies are discussed across different application scenarios, ranging from homogeneous reactions and nanoparticle synthesis to surface-interaction enhancement and cell functional regulation. By integrating design principles with practical implementation and application-driven requirements, this review aims to provide a critical overview of the design logic and application-dependent optimization strategies of staggered herringbone microfluidic chips. HIGHLIGHTS • Staggered herringbone structures enhance fluid mixing and particle transport in microchannels. Geometric design directly impacts chip performance across synthesis and sensing. Passive microfluidics can be tuned for bioanalysis, cell manipulation, and material production. © 2026 Author(s).

title: Mitigation of wind-induced deflection of oversized composite-insulator sheds using a −1° lower-surface inclination and disk-type rib structures
abstract: Silicone rubber composite insulators with oversized sheds can effectively reduce the risk of external insulation flashover caused by bird-dropping bridging. However, the wind-induced deflection of oversized sheds under strong-wind conditions and the effects of their lower-surface geometry on the deflection response have not been sufficiently investigated. In this study, a typical silicone rubber composite insulator with an oversized shed was investigated. The deflection characteristics of the oversized shed at an airflow velocity of 30 m/s were experimentally determined using an open-circuit wind tunnel. A fluid–structure interaction model benchmarked against the wind tunnel measurement was subsequently established to systematically investigate the effects of airflow velocity, lower-surface inclination, and disk-type rib-reinforced structures on shed deflection, surface pressure, and shed-root stress. The results show that changing the lower-surface inclination from 6° to −1° reduces the maximum deflection from 71.3 mm to 1.7 mm, corresponding to a reduction of 97.6%. At the original inclination of 6°, the addition of straight-rib and curved-rib disk-type structures reduces the maximum deflection to 45.0% and 35.9% of that of the original structure, respectively. In addition, a low-cost deflection measurement method based on suspended mass loading is proposed for the preliminary comparison of different anti-deflection structures when wind tunnel facilities are unavailable. The findings provide a reference for the anti-deflection design and field retrofitting of oversized-shed composite insulators in strong-wind regions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Role of deformation heterogeneity in the superplasticity of Ti6321 titanium alloy with a bimodal microstructure
abstract: Superplastic forming offers a promising approach for producing critical ultra-thick titanium alloy components for marine applications. Near-α Ti6321 titanium alloy with a bimodal microstructure provides excellent mechanical performance and is therefore widely used in marine engineering. However, the influence of microstructural heterogeneity on its superplastic behavior and the underlying deformation mechanisms remains insufficiently understood. In this work, interrupted high-temperature tensile tests combined with systematic microstructural characterization were performed. The results reveal that deformation is accommodated by distinct yet coupled mechanisms in equiaxed α and lamellar α regions. In equiaxed α, plastic flow is predominantly governed by strong dynamic recovery and continuous dynamic recrystallization (DRX), with discontinuous DRX activated at intermediate strains. In contrast, lamellar α undergoes pronounced strain- and orientation-dependent dynamic globularization and more extensive DRX, particularly in Type II/III colonies. A distinct DRX mechanism, epitaxial recrystallization, is identified in lamellar α at low strains, where newly formed α grains preserve the local Burgers orientation relationship with adjacent β and form semi-coherent, low-misfit α/β interfaces. Two-beam TEM observations reveal extensive <a> and <c+a> dislocation activity, consistent with the in-grain misorientation axes results showing that the preferred Taylor axes progressively shift from <0001> toward <01¯12> and <uvt0> with increasing strain. The co-activation of multiple slip variants gradually alters the local misorientation axes away from those established by preceding slip, thereby modifying local grain orientations through slip-induced lattice rotation and promoting increasingly dispersed slip activity. The synergistic interplay of heterogeneous slip and multiple DRX mechanisms promotes the transformation of hard-slip-dominated lamellar α into a fine-grained equiaxed microstructure. This microstructural homogenization facilitates multidirectional soft slip and grain boundary sliding, thereby underpinning the superior superplastic response of the alloy. © 2026

title: Strain-engineered FeNi@SDC heterointerfaces for durable high-temperature seawater electrolysis
abstract: Hydrogen production from seawater using solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) offers a promising pathway towards a sustainable energy future. However, severe Ni catalyst coarsening and chloride-induced surface poisoning under high-temperature steam conditions still limit long-term operation. Herein, we develop a reduction-driven strategy to construct strain-engineered FeNi@SDC heterointerfaces by infiltrating an FeSDC (Sm0.2Ce0.7Fe0.1O2-δ) precursor into a commercial nickel-yttria-stabilized zirconia (Ni-YSZ) fuel electrode. Partial Fe diffusion into the Ni lattice during reduction drives the in-situ formation of FeNi alloy nanoparticles, simultaneously generating lattice strain and a robust metal-oxide heterointerface. Theoretical calculations show that these coupled structural features regulate the electronic structure of Ni, thereby promoting water activation, optimizing hydrogen adsorption and suppressing chloride adsorption. As a result, the modified electrolysis cell achieves an electrolysis current of 52.7 A at 1.5 V, while maintaining stable operation for 645 h with an ultralow degradation rate of 8.4 × 10−4% h−1. This work establishes a general strategy that integrates alloy-induced lattice strain with heterointerface engineering for the development of durable fuel electrodes for high-temperature seawater electrolysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: An improved isolation forest based on kernel principal component analysis for anomaly detection in helicopter-based power-line inspection data
abstract: For helicopter inspection data, including flight trajectories, task status, and equipment operating status, conventional anomaly detection methods still suffer from difficulties in separating high-dimensional nonlinear data, insufficient anomaly isolation capability, and low anomaly discrimination. To address these problems, this paper proposes an improved isolation forest anomaly detection method based on kernel principal component analysis (KPCA). The proposed method extracts five categories of features from inspection data, including standard deviation, coefficient of variation, centroid, resilience, and scale features, and constructs a fused feature matrix through sliding windows. KPCA is then used to perform nonlinear reconstruction and dimensionality reduction on the feature matrix to obtain a low-dimensional subspace. In this subspace, the single axis-aligned splitting strategy of the conventional isolation forest is improved into multi-directional splitting along principal-component directions and their combined directions. In addition, the path length is corrected according to the distance between each sample and the normal center. Experimental results based on 7027 real records from a helicopter inspection platform show that the proposed method outperforms conventional methods in terms of Precision, Recall, F1-score, FAR, and PR-AUC. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively identify flight-trajectory deviations, equipment operation anomalies, and task-execution anomalies, providing a feasible data-driven technical approach for improving the intelligence and reliability of power-line inspection. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Enhancing the foaming properties of spirulina biomass via microfluidization and enzymatic polysaccharide hydrolysis for egg white substitution in cakes
abstract: This study utilized high-pressure microfluidization (HPM) coupled with enzymatic polysaccharide hydrolysis to enhance the foaming properties of spirulina biomass for partial egg white replacement in cakes. HPM disrupted cell walls, releasing intracellular proteins that promote the formation of fine, uniform bubbles. Compared with untreated spirulina, HPM treatment reduced surface tension and contact angle by 6.46% and 13.86%, respectively, and increased foaming capacity by 42.86%. Proteins were identified as the key foaming-active substances in the HPM-treated spirulina supernatant, and low polysaccharide concentrations (≤30%) facilitated foam stability. However, the polysaccharide components in HPM-treated spirulina suppressed foaming through a viscosity-enhancing effect, limiting the egg white substitution ratio to ≤25%. Pectinase (PE) treatment reduced the viscosity from 10.20 to 3.65 mPa s and increased the substitution ratio to 50%. Compared with HPM alone, the HPM-PE treatment further enhanced foaming capacity by 41.24%, decreased batter specific gravity by 26.15%, and improved cake specific volume by 24.71%. The spirulina-substituted cake possessed superior nutritional value and a distinctive aroma contributed to 11 key volatiles, including (E)-β-ionone, nonanal, (E, E)-2,4-nonadienal, 1-octen-3-ol, and 2-pentylfuran. These results suggest that HPM-PE treatment markedly enhances the egg-white replacement capacity of spirulina biomass-derived fraction, providing a scientific basis for sustainable plant-based food development. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Topologically crosslinked molecular intercalation enabling strain-resilient EMI shielding in an n-type conducting polymer
abstract: Maintaining stable electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding performance under large deformation remains a major challenge. The n-type conducting polymer poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) exhibits excellent electrical conductivity. However, strong π-π interactions lead to severe intrinsic brittleness. The incorporation of flexible polymers can alleviate brittleness, yet the resulting improvement in deformability is still limited. This work, by grafting 3-isocyanatopropyltriethoxysilane (IPTS) onto both ends of polyethylene glycol (PEG) to synthesize a flexible, both-end IPTS-grafted PEG (BIP), proposes a strategy based on molecular-level intercalation and dense hydrogen-bonding interactions. BIP is intercalated into the interlayers of PBFDO, increasing the free volume of the system and forming a high-density hydrogen-bonding network with PBFDO. The resulting increase in deformation freedom enables the composite film to achieve an elongation at break of 580%. Under strains of 100% and 500%, the EMI shielding effectiveness retention of the composite film reaches 93% and 65%, respectively. Moreover, a fully connected neural network is constructed to predict EMI shielding performance, achieving an external-validation root mean square error of 2.429. This work provides an effective strategy for alleviating the brittleness of n-type conducting polymers and achieving stable EMI shielding performance under large deformation, demonstrating great application potential in flexible electronics. © 2026

title: Coupling Ti-assisted secondary-hydroxyl activation with H-regulated radical overoxidation control on WO3 photoanodes for highly selective glycerol to dihydroxyacetone conversion
abstract: Selective photoelectrochemical oxidation of glycerol to dihydroxyacetone (DHA) offers a compelling strategy for integrating solar energy conversion with biomass valorization. However, efficient DHA accumulation remains challenging because two key issues are often underemphasized: the atomic level control of glycerol adsorption geometry for secondary-hydroxyl oxidation, and the suppression of radical mediated overoxidation of the formed DHA. Herein, we report a H, Ti-dual-modified WO3 photoanode (H,Ti)/WO3 that enables highly selective glycerol oxidation to DHA via cooperative interfacial pathway regulation. The (H,Ti)/WO3 photoanode achieves a DHA selectivity of 71.9%—a sharp rise from 35.7% for WO3, and a DHA production rate of 264.5 mmol m−2 h−1, roughly 5 times that of the unmodified counterpart. Mechanistically, highly dispersed Ti sites enhance adsorption of the secondary hydroxyl group of glycerol, directing the pathway toward DHA via two‑electron transfer. H‑insertion, in contrast, shifting hydroxyl chemistry away from free •OH mediated deep oxidation toward more surface-bound hydroxyl species and thereby suppressing DHA overoxidation. With this dual-pronged strategy, our work provides new insights into the selective formation and stable accumulation of DHA in biomass photoelectrochemical systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: From catalyst functional zoning to air oxidation–nitrogen oxide reduction cascade: An effective pathway for ammonia synthesis from air
abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction to ammonia, centered on nitrate reduction, faces challenges including insufficient catalyst activity and stability, along with difficulties in integrated application. Using Salen (N-N′-bis (salicylidene)-1,3-propanediamine) as ligand, this work uniformly introduces multi-dimensional iron species onto carbon fibers surface (named FeSCN/CF) via complexation confinement and hard template confinement. FeSCN/CF efficiently promotes nearly 100% electroreduction of nitrate-to-ammonia under various complex conditions, and the Zn-nitrate battery constructed with FeSCN/CF as the core enables self-driven ammonia synthesis alongside stable energy supply. Driven by intermittent electrical energy, a low-temperature plasma air oxidation process cascaded with an electrocatalytic unit enables direct air-to-ammonia conversion, successfully demonstrated in a distributed agricultural ammonia fertilizer supply scenario. Experimental and theoretical calculations confirm that multiscale/multitype sites synergistically promote highly selective electroreduction of nitrogen oxides to ammonia, while a self-driven plasma-air-oxidation cascade electroreduction system powered by green electricity effectively addresses nitrogen source shortages and adapts to distributed ammonia synthesis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Diverse oxidosqualene cyclases for triterpenoid biosynthesis
abstract: Triterpenoids, a significant group of secondary metabolites, possess diverse skeletons and excellent pharmacological activities and are widely applied in cosmetics, medicine, and biopesticides. Traditional plant extraction and chemical synthesis cannot meet the needs of commercial production, and heterologous biosynthesis of triterpenoids has become a promising strategy. Oxidosqualene cyclases (OSCs) are the key enzymes that determine triterpenoid biosynthesis. However, most OSCs exhibit low heterologous expression, low catalytic activity, and promiscuous catalytic products, which impedes the heterologous biosynthesis of triterpenoids. In this study, we constructed a dataset of 348 OSCs with known functions, which is the largest centralized resource of characterized OSCs to date. The 88 triterpenoid skeletons produced by these OSCs are classified based on their structural features, 49 of which have been experimentally characterized as the main products of OSCs, and the formation mechanisms of the common skeletons are summarized. Phylogenetic analysis and motif analysis elucidated the relationships among the sequences, structures, and products of plant-derived OSCs. Phylogenetic analysis showed that plant-derived OSCs were divided into two major clades, which corresponded to the biosynthetic mechanisms of the "protosteryl/dammarenyl" dichotomy. Motif analysis showed that 5 motifs are present in plant-derived OSCs, including 3 related to the catalytic activity of the OSCs and 2 related to product specificity. Finally, we summarized the common strategies for mining OSCs to provide directions for the discovery of novel OSCs and new triterpenoid skeletons. Our study will help discover or design OSCs with specific product profiles as functional elements for applications in synthetic biology. © 2026 The Authors.

title: K+-driven interfacial water reconstruction via charge-enriched heterointerfaces for accelerated alkaline hydrogen evolution
abstract: The sluggish water dissociation kinetics in alkaline media remains a major bottleneck for efficient hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Beyond intrinsic active sites, the interfacial microenvironment, particularly local charge distribution and water structure, plays a decisive role in governing reaction pathways. Herein, we report a two-dimensional Cu-modified RuOx catalyst containing carbonaceous components (denoted as Cu-RuOx/C), featuring crystalline-amorphous heterointerfaces that create charge-enriched interfacial regions for regulating the interfacial water network. Cu incorporation generates a charge-enriched surface that promotes the accumulation of K+ near the catalyst interface, thereby reconstructing the interfacial hydrogen-bond network. This regulation shortens the K+-surface distance and weakens hydrogen-bond connectivity within interfacial water, leading to a decreased fraction of tetracoordinate hydrogen-bonded water and an increased proportion of free water. Such an optimized interfacial water structure ensures sufficient proton supply during the HER process. As a result, Cu-RuOx/C delivers an ultralow overpotential of 13 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH and sustains 800 h of operation at 1000 mA cm−2 in an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer. This work demonstrates highly dispersed Cu modulation as an effective strategy for engineering catalytic microenvironments to enhance alkaline HER. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Soy protein isolate composite gels fabrication via short-term high-intensity ultrasound
abstract: Dual-protein systems offer advantages for improving soy protein isolate (SPI) gelation. However, conventional gelation approaches still rely on complex procedures and prolonged heating, resulting in high energy consumption. Herein, short-time high-intensity ultrasound (HIU; 20 kHz, 400 W, 4-6 min) was used to directly fabricate SPI composite gel without additional heating, with ovalbumin (OVA), peanut protein isolate (PPI), and pea protein isolate (PAPI) serving as added proteins. The results indicated that SPI-OVA gel at a mass ratio of 2:4 exhibited the highest gel strength (183.02 g), the strongest viscoelasticity, and the greatest water immobilization (T22 = 54.789 ms), corresponding to a highly compact and dense network. Importantly, intermolecular force analysis revealed that OVA promoted the formation of a highly compact network dominated by hydrophobic interactions and disulfide bonds. The SPI-PPI composite gel network was mainly maintained by ionic bonds, while the dominant forces in the SPI-PAPI composite gel network shifted from ionic bonds to hydrophobic interactions and disulfide bonds as PAPI concentration increased. Furthermore, free sulfhydryl and surface hydrophobicity results indicated that HIU thermal effects facilitated protein unfolding and sulfhydryl exposure, while excessive hydrophobic aggregation in SPI-PPI and SPI-PAPI gels partially buried hydrophobic groups and weakened network formation. This study reveals mechanistic insights into HIU-induced fabrication of SPI composite gels and supports the rational design of high-performance dual-protein gel systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Genetic algorithm-supervised graph shadow estimation for low-observability distribution feeders: calibrated validation on a real feeder
abstract: Real distribution feeders often operate under partial observability, while physics-based state estimators can be too slow for frequent digital-twin updates. This paper proposes a Genetic Algorithm (GA)-supervised graph surrogate for shadow state estimation using feeder topology, sparse measurements, and physics-constrained GA pseudo-states. The model is trained with reliability-aware corrupted measurement views and deployed non-intrusively beside the operational GA estimator. Over an approximately eleven-day Terni feeder deployment, the mean estimation-call time decreased from 13.11 s to 0.655 s. At Fontana di Polo, the only hidden medium-voltage point with an independent active/reactive-power reference, the calibrated graph surrogate achieved weighted mean absolute percentage error (wMAPE) values of 12.64% and 12.80%, respectively, on the held-out test interval. Sensitivity tests showed progressive degradation as voltage-measurement availability decreased and negligible change under additive zero-mean noise within the trained corruption range. Controlled hidden-photovoltaic scenarios showed stable calibrated performance within the generated model-based operating groups. The results demonstrate short-term shadow-mode feasibility for the investigated Terni feeder; long-term robustness and cross-feeder transfer remain unverified. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Rainfall flashover characteristics of high-speed train roof insulators in a static environment
abstract: Roof insulators are critical components of high-speed railway traction power supply systems. When trains are stationary at stations under heavy rainfall, rainwater tends to accumulate on the shed surfaces and form water films and inter-shed rain columns, thereby reducing creepage-distance utilization and increasing the risk of flashover. To investigate the rain-flashover characteristics of roof insulators under such conditions, three post insulators with different shed configurations were subjected to artificial-rain flashover tests. The effects of rainfall intensity and rainwater conductivity on flashover voltage were investigated, and finite-element simulations were performed to evaluate the influence of rain-column evolution on the local electric-field distribution. The results show that the flashover voltages of all three insulators decrease with increasing rainfall intensity and rainwater conductivity, following negative pow-er-law relationships. The relative rain-column elongation ratios are 0.39, 0.48, and 0.66, with corresponding bridging proportions of 5.5%, 11.0%, and 12.5%, respectively. As the droplet length increases from 10 mm to 30 mm and subsequently develops into a bridging state, the local peak electric-field strength increases from 6.77 kV/mm to 17.10 and 61.14 kV/mm, respectively. Rain-column elongation shortens the residual air gap and intensifies the electric field at the rain-column tip, thereby increasing the likelihood of local discharge. Based on leakage-current characteristics, flashover-arc behavior, and electric-field simulations, a physical discharge mechanism for roof insulators under static heavy-rain conditions is proposed. The findings provide a basis for roof-insulator selection and rain-flashover mitigation design for high-speed trains. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Engineering regulation of free radicals by Cu-Ni bimetallic synergistic effect for low-temperature catalytic hydrolysis of carbonyl sulfide
abstract: Carbonyl sulfide (COS) is a stubborn organic sulfur contaminant hindering natural gas deep desulfurization. Traditional hydrolysis catalysts face short service life and severe overoxidation of byproduct H2S. Herein, Cu-Ni bimetallic modified CeAlOx composite oxide was synthesized via ammonia precipitation for low-temperature COS catalytic hydrolysis. Multiple material characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations were adopted to uncover bimetallic synergistic regulation on oxygen vacancies and reactive free radicals. The Cu-Ni co-modified CeAlOx catalyst exhibited optimal desulfurization performance, prominent anti-interference ability against H2O and CH4. Cu-Ni/CeAlOx maintained full COS removal for 570 min and achieved 209 h long-term stable operation. Cu promoted water dissociation and superoxide radical (·O2-) generation to accelerate COS hydrolysis, while Ni suppressed excessive ·O2- production to avoid deep oxidation of H2S. Oxygen vacancies and triply bridged hydroxyl groups acted as core active sites. Atomic-scale DFT confirmed CuO oxygen vacancies dominated COS hydrolysis, and NiO oxygen vacancies realized selective oxidation of H2S to elemental sulfur. The formation and the decomposition of HSCO2- are the rate-determining step for COS hydrolysis. This work provides theoretical guidance for developing high-efficiency desulfurization catalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Morphology-tunable ZrO2@SiC@NiCo2O4/NiO composite fibers for integrated high-temperature electromagnetic wave absorption and multifunctional performance
abstract: The development of high-performance electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorption materials with high-temperature tolerance is urgently required for applications in extreme environments, including stealth aircraft and aeroengine heating components. Traditional EMW absorption materials primarily exhibit outstanding EMW absorption performance at room temperature. However, maintaining long-term performance in extreme environments remains challenging. To address this challenge, morphology-tunable ZrO2@ silicon carbide (SiC)@NiCo2O4/NiO composite fibers were constructed through electrospinning and hydrothermal reactions to integrate room-temperature and high-temperature EMW absorption. SiC fibers, renowned for their high-temperature stability and oxidation resistance, served as thermally robust frameworks for the controlled growth and spatial dispersion of NiCo2O4/NiO nanostructures. The results show that the sheet-like NiCo2O4/NiO-decorated ZrO2@SiC fibers achieve an effective absorption bandwidth of 7.4 GHz and maintain 7.3 GHz after heat treatment at 450 °C. Interfacial polarization at the heterogeneous interfaces between components significantly enhances EMW absorption. Furthermore, the fibers exhibit outstanding thermal insulation, flame retardancy, and infrared stealth properties. This material is a promising candidate for structural-functional integration in extreme environments and is suitable for demanding aerospace and military applications. © 2026

title: Electro-assembly of soy protein and konjac glucomannan into biomimetic scaffolds for cultured meat: Structural and biological performance
abstract: Anisotropic porous scaffolds for cultured meat were fabricated by freeze-dried soy protein isolate (SPI) and konjac glucomannan (KGM) hybrid hydrogels aligned under a low-voltage electric field. The scaffolds exhibited well-defined oriented pore structures with porosity exceeding 80%, where freezing temperature governed pore architecture: scaffolds prepared at −20 °C produced pores of 50–200 μm, while −80 °C generated finer pores (0–100 μm). SEM analysis revealed an ordered lamellar structure, and mechanical testing further demonstrated higher transverse strength than longitudinal strength. Optimal KGM content (1.0–1.5 wt%) enhanced stiffness (up to 160 kPa), whereas excessive KGM (2.0–2.5 wt%) reduced mechanical strength to 40-80 kPa. The scaffolds displayed excellent water absorption (800%–1147%) and maintained structural integrity after swelling (KGM concentrations: 1.0–2.5 wt%). C2C12 myoblasts showed high seeding efficiency (up to 90%) with enhanced robust adhesion, proliferation, and differentiation. Scaffolds prepared at −20 °C, with pore sizes of 50–200 μm, provided a more favorable microenvironment for cell growth, whereas the overly dense structure formed at −80 °C likely limited cell proliferation and nutrient diffusion. Notably, constructs fabricated at −80 °C with 1.5 wt% KGM achieved excellent mechanical properties (∼56 kPa). This study established an in-house, laboratory-scale, low-voltage direct-current electric-field system and provides a potential sustainable strategy for designing anisotropic scaffolds for cultured meat and highlights the potential of hydrogels in next-generation food and biomedical applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Self-adaptive phase transition precipitates enabled superior strength of additively manufactured (Nb15Ta10W75)98.5C1.5 refractory multi-principal element alloys at ultra-high temperatures
abstract: Refractory multi-principal element alloys (RMPEAs), particularly those of the Nb-Ta-W system, are promising candidates for structural applications under ultra-high temperature (UHT) conditions of ≥ 1500 °C. However, their softening temperatures (Tc ≈ 1600–2000 °C) coincide with the operational range required for the heat-resistant components in aerospace and energy systems, leading to severe strength degradation. Here, we propose an in-situ nano-precipitation strategy mediated by adaptive phase transformations to overcome this limitation. The required C content of 1.5 at.% was estimated using Thermo-Calc software. We designed a novel (Nb15Ta10W75)98.5C1.5 (NTWC) RMPEA that enables in-situ (Nb,Ta)C precipitation during laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). Isothermal kinetic calculations show that the in-situ precipitates have excellent thermal stability. These nano-precipitates undergo a three-stage evolution successively from metastable (Nb,Ta)C to equilibrium TaC at 1600, 1800 and 2000 °C, enabling NTWC to achieve yield strengths of 634, 328 and 126 MPa respectively, surpassing most LPBF-fabricated refractory alloys. The effect of microstructure characteristics and phase transition behavior of nano-precipitates on the UHT strength was evaluated in detail. Beyond demonstrating a pathway for unprecedented UHT strength retention, this work establishes a general principle of coupling thermodynamic stability and kinetic adaptability for precipitates in complex concentrated systems via molecular dynamics. © 2026

title: Fast extremum values calculation of electro‑thermal fields for ±800 kV valve‑side resin-impregnated paper bushing under multiple factors
abstract: Valve-side resin-impregnated paper (RIP) bushings are key insulation components of HVDC converter transformers. Combined AC–DC voltage, high current, and varying thermal boundaries produce non-uniform electro-thermal fields, potentially causing local overheating and electric-field concentration. A three-dimensional electro-thermal finite-element model was developed for a full-scale ±800 kV valve-side RIP bushing and its temperature-field calculation was validated through temperature-rise tests, yielding an MAE of 2.301 °C and an RMSE of 2.467 °C. Single- and multi-factor effects of load rate, ambient air temperature, and transformer oil temperature were investigated. The factors create different temperature and conductivity gradients, producing non-equivalent electric-field responses and non-monotonic variations with thermal boundaries. Temperature-dependent field distortion is dominated by DC redistribution, and electric-field concentration does not necessarily coincide with the thermal hot spot. Contribution analysis assigns 46.10%, 41.57%, and 5.94% of hot-spot-temperature variation to load rate, oil temperature, and air temperature, respectively, while load rate accounts for 88.76% of electric-field-extremum variation, showing joint load–oil control of the thermal response but predominant load control of electrical stress. An interpretable fast-prediction model combining a sparse high-order response surface with Kriging residual correction was developed. For 25 independent numerical test conditions, its MAE/RMSE values were 1.437/1.743 °C for hot-spot temperature and 0.060/0.076 kV/mm for electric-field extremum. Compared with conventional Kriging, BP, and LSTM, the proposed model achieved the lowest five-fold validation and independent-test RMSE values for electric-field-extremum calculation while retaining an explicit mathematical form. The model provides a rapid quantitative approach for condition evaluation and identification of potentially unfavorable RIP-bushing operating conditions. © 2026

title: The diffusion characteristics and mechanism of O3 caused by corona discharge under the coupling of temperature and humidity conditions
abstract: High-voltage switchgear is an indispensable core equipment in power distribution networks. Its interior is susceptible to corona discharge, which inevitably leads to substantial energy loss and degradation of equipment insulation performance. In this paper, experimental verification and simulation modeling methods were employed to investigate the generation, diffusion patterns of O3 caused by corona discharge within the high-voltage box under various temperature and humidity conditions, as well as the correlation characteristics between O3 production and the degree of discharge. By establishing an O3 diffusion simulation model, the evolution characteristics of O3 over time and space under the influence of different temperature and humidity were calculated and analyzed, and the influence mechanism of multiple factors on O3 diffusion was revealed. The results show that for the actual process of O3 generation, the concentration of O3 shows a saturation trend in the later stage of discharge. An increase of 20 °C in ambient temperature leads to an approximate 60% rise in O3 content, while a 20% rise in relative humidity results in an around 80% reduction in O3 content. With the increase of applied voltage, the concentration of O3 generated by discharge rises significantly. Under the same temperature and humidity conditions, the O3 concentration at an applied voltage of 15 kV is approximately three times that at 10 kV. During the process of ozone diffusion and decomposition. The concentration of O3 declines significantly as temperature rises and shows a decreasing trend with increasing humidity. The O3 concentration at 40 °C is 50% lower than that at 20 °C, and the concentration at 80%RH is about 20% lower than that at 40%RH. The research can provide theoretical and experimental references for the monitoring of corona discharge O3 and the status assessment of high-voltage switchgear cabinet type box-type equipment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A non-standard protection scheme for coordinated and stable SDGs operation
abstract: The integration of distributed generation, especially synchronous distributed generators, into power distribution networks has introduced new protection and stability challenges. One critical issue is that the coordination of protection devices could be disrupted because of the fault current provided by distributed generations. Another problem is the transient instability of synchronous distributed generators due to their low inertia during fault events. This paper presents a novel protection strategy that simultaneously addresses both problems. A customized non-standard time-current-voltage characteristic is proposed for overcurrent relays where the adaptive coordination is obtained. It also improves stability while satisfying both Coordination Time Interval and Critical Clearing Time constraints. This approach includes an offline phase involving power flow, fault, and protection coordination studies. If transient stability constraints are violated, an online adaptive phase is activated by using local voltage measurements at the synchronous distributed generator buses. The proposed method is implemented and validated on the IEEE 33-bus distribution system by using ETAP software. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the method to maintain coordination time intervals and ensuring synchronous distributed generators stability, even under severe fault conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Multi-stage siting and sizing of PV stations under long-term carbon price: a branch-and-bound embedded progressive hedging approach
abstract: Reasonable programming of photovoltaic (PV) site selection and sizing is essential for boosting renewable energy penetration and power system carbon emission reduction, thereby mitigating future electricity procurement cost risks under dynamic carbon pricing. However, the problem of optimal PV siting and sizing with integer decision variables is complicated by the long-term uncertainty of carbon prices. To address the above issue, this paper proposes a PV site selection and capacity determination mixed integer multi-stage stochastic programming model considering the long-term uncertainty of carbon prices, and designs a collaborative solution framework of the Progressive Hedging (PH) algorithm and Branch-and-Bound (BB) to optimize the low-carbon and economic performance of the system. Firstly, a multi-stage stochastic programming model for PV siting and sizing is constructed, employing scenario trees based on an enhanced binomial tree model to depict the stochastic evolution of carbon prices over the long term. Secondly, the PH algorithm solves the subproblems for individual scenarios and refines the solutions through interaction to meet the nonanticipativity constraints in carbon prices. Finally, the PH algorithm is embedded within the BB framework to optimize the integer decisions related to PV siting locations. Case studies on the IEEE 33-bus system demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in identifying adaptive PV deployment strategies under long-term carbon price uncertainty. A 10% decrease or increase in carbon prices changes the expected final-stage PV capacity by approximately -11.2% and +10.7%. These results highlight the capability of the framework to capture the impacts of carbon price uncertainty on PV investment decisions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Evaluating the safety impacts of three-dimensional alignments of mountainous freeways using an interpretable machine learning approach
abstract: The safety of mountainous freeways remains a critical concern in road infrastructure planning, especially for routes characterized by intricate geometric alignments. The roadway is essentially a ribbon-shaped structure in three-dimensional (3D) space, and using 3D spatial parameters allows for a more accurate representation of its true geometric characteristics. However, quantifying the impact of 3D alignment features on crash occurrence remains challenging. To this end, this study investigates the nonlinear relationship between crash rate and 3D alignments using 4 neural network models: multilayer perceptron (MLP), Wide & Deep, residual network (ResNet), and graph neural network (GNN). The crash dataset was collected from two mountainous freeways in Guangdong Province, including crash records, traffic volumes, and road geometry over a 3-year period (2021–2023). According to model evaluation metrics, the Wide & Deep model achieved the best predictive performance. To enhance model interpretability, the SHapley additive exPlanations (SHAP) method and partial dependence plot (PDP) method were applied, enabling insights into the global importance of each feature and their interaction effects. SHAP results indicate that three geometric attributes, namely vertical curve length (VC_length), horizontal curve length (HC_length), and grade, have a significant influence on crash rate. Notably, 3D curvature-related features emerged as key predictors. As shown in the SHAP analysis, both excessively high and low curvature values, as well as a pronounced drop in curvature between consecutive segments, exhibit negative SHAP contributions, implying a mitigating influence on the predicted crash risk and underscoring the significance of curvature consistency. By contrast, torsion-related variables show limited impact. Additionally, key interaction effects were identified among several variable pairs, particularly between VC_length and HC_length, VC_length and back curvature difference, and HC_length and back curvature difference. These findings provide practical guidance for optimizing geometric design on mountainous freeways, supporting safer and more informed infrastructure planning. © 2026 Tongji University and Tongji University Press.

title: Thermal atomic migration for contact doping in scaled carbon nanotube transistors
abstract: Single‑walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) are considered promising candidates for next‑generation transistors owing to their atomic thickness, high carrier mobility, and dangling‑bond‑free surfaces. However, as technology nodes continue to scale down, achieving reliable electrical contacts between SWCNTs and metal electrodes at the sub‑nanometer scale remains a critical challenge. Here, we report a strategy based on localized thermally driven migration of physically encapsulated iodine inside SWCNTs to improve the contact performance and overall device characteristics of individual SWCNT transistors. Spectroscopic characterization combined with theoretical calculations confirms that the strong charge transfer between the iodine crystal and the SWCNT transforms the nanotube in the contact regions into a degenerate semiconductor, thereby significantly reducing the contact resistance at the metal electrode interface. By applying Joule heating to drive the migration of iodine atoms, in situ dedoping of the channel region is achieved. The contact resistance of film‑based devices is reduced to 1.7 kΩ μm. For individual SWCNT devices, the on‑state current increases approximately 40 times, the on/off ratio increases 37 times, and the contact resistance decreases by a factor of 5. This work presents a proof-of-concept contact engineering strategy for high-performance SWCNT transistors. © 2026

title: Melt-spinning-enabled microstructure engineering toward high thermoelectric and mechanical properties in Ag2Se-based composites
abstract: Tailoring the microstructures is essential for simultaneously enhancing the thermoelectric and mechanical properties of Ag2Se‑based materials, while effective processing strategies for realising such rational microstructural design are still required. Herein, Ag2−xSe1+xSbx (x = 0.02, 0.04, and 0.06) pellets were fabricated via a sequential process of melt spinning followed by hot pressing. The resulting Ag2Se‑based composites contain uniformly dispersed AgSbSe2 inclusions and exhibit substantially refined grains compared to single-phase Ag2Se material. These tailored microstructures effectively promote phonon scattering, impede crack propagation, and modulate deformation behaviour, leading to reduced lattice thermal conductivity, enhanced compressive strength, and increased maximum compressive strain. Notably, the Ag2−xSe1+xSbx (x = 0.04) sample attains a compressive strength of 247.9 MPa, which is superior to previously reported values, along with a dimensionless figure of merit of 0.90 at 368 K. This study highlights melt spinning combined with rapid sintering as an effective strategy for fabricating Ag2Se-based composites with multiscale microstructures and balanced thermoelectric properties and mechanical robustness. © 2026

title: Solving multi-objective optimal power flow with renewable energy sources using an improved non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm
abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy sources (RESs) into power systems poses challenges to multi-objective optimal power flow (MOOPF) problems, including uncertainties and complex constraints. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an improved NSGA-II algorithm based on an adaptive geometric crowding distance (AGCD) strategy, referred to as AGCD-NSGA-II. The proposed algorithm inherits the nondominated sorting and genetic evolutionary mechanisms of NSGA-II and introduces an adaptive geometric crowding distance strategy, which dynamically captures the distribution characteristics of nondominated solutions in the objective space and incorporates a nearest-neighbor density evaluation mechanism to achieve an effective balance between convergence performance and solution diversity. To address the uncertainties of wind speed and photovoltaic (PV) generation, Weibull and lognormal probability distributions are employed to model the uncertainties of wind power and PV outputs, respectively. First, the proposed algorithm is compared with several multi-objective optimization algorithms on the Viennet (VNT) benchmark functions using the inverted generational distance (IGD) and hypervolume (HV) metrics. The experimental results demonstrate that AGCD-NSGA-II exhibits competitive performance in terms of convergence and solution distribution. Subsequently, eight case studies are conducted on the modified IEEE 30-bus and IEEE 57-bus systems considering renewable energy integration. The objectives include generation cost, pollutant emissions, active power loss, and voltage deviation. In addition, the Wilcoxon rank-sum test is performed to further verify the statistical significance of the performance differences among the algorithms. The results indicate that the proposed algorithm can effectively solve MOOPF problems considering renewable energy uncertainties and exhibits excellent optimization performance and robustness. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Technological Assurance of the Quality of Slide Bearing Shells Based on Two-Stage Magnetic Abrasive Finishing
abstract: The article describes the methodology of a two-stage finishing process for slide bearing shells made of bronze. The goal of the first finishing stage was to form a base roughness profile with uniform values of the controlled parameters. Based on the results of the first stage, regression equations were derived. These equations make it possible to evaluate the effectiveness of the influence of the process variable factors (tool rotational speed, feed rate, processing time, and workpiece diameter values) of magnetic abrasive finishing on the value of the controlled parameters. The results showed that the parameters of tool rotational speed and processing time have the greatest influence. In the second stage of the experimental research, a two-factor experiment (varying the time and abrasive grain sizes) was conducted. The aim of this stage was to test the possibility of applying oil-retaining grooves onto the formed profile. The results showed that the most noticeable grooves are formed at a processing time of 6 minutes and an abrasive grain size of 350 µm. The roughness parameters did not increase significantly compared to the values after the first processing stage. The need for further research to evaluate the operational characteristics of the machined workpieces during wear testing is established. © 2027 The author(s). title: Tunable oxygen vacancy engineering via electron beam irradiation in TiO2/MXene: A combined experimental and DFT study on photocatalytic performance and hydrogen adsorption energetics
abstract: Defect engineering is a powerful strategy for enhancing catalytic activity, charge-carrier mobility, and structural stability through the controlled introduction of defects such as oxygen vacancies (Ov). Electron beam (EB) irradiation offers a precise route for generating vacancies and lattice disorders, enabling tailored modulation of electronic and surface states for photocatalytic applications. In this work, a 1D/2D TiO2/MXene (TMX) was synthesized via electrostatic self-assembly method, where TiO2 serves as the primary light-absorbing semiconductor and MXene acts as a co-catalyst to promote charge separation and surface redox reactions. High-energy EB irradiation was employed to induce Ov and Ti3+ species within TiO2, markedly improving the photocatalytic hydrogen production of TMX. The optimally irradiated sample (TMX3–500) achieved a hydrogen evolution rate of 691 ± 9.54 μmol g−1 h−1, 5.25 times higher compared to sample before irradiation. Such enhancement was ascribed to improved light absorption, efficient charge carrier separation by the generation of Ov, confirmed by different spectroscopic characterizations. DFT calculations further showed that Ov generate defect states within TiO2 bandgap that interact with adsorbed hydrogen, while interfacial charge transfer from TiO2 to MXene optimizes ΔGH* towards thermoneutrality. The findings highlight the role of EB-induced defect engineering in designing efficient photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen production. © 2026 The Authors

title: Polyvinyl alcohol/gelatin/carboxymethyl chitosan hydrogels with improved mechanical strength and fatigue resistance for artificial heart valves
abstract: Hydrogels are promising materials for heart valve tissue engineering; however, their translation into medical devices remains limited by post-processing steps that can introduce defects and weaken mechanical performance. Recent advances in mechanically robust hydrogels with nanoscale fibrous architectures have renewed interest in post-processing strategies for hydrogel devices. Here, polyvinyl alcohol/gelatin/carboxymethyl chitosan hydrogels (PVA/gelatin/CMCS, denoted as PGC) were fabricated by directional freeze-casting and further reinforced by Fe3+ cross-linking and heat treatment to obtain aPGC/Fe hydrogels. The resulting aPGC/Fe hydrogels exhibited an elastic modulus of up to 8.16 MPa, toughness of 6.45 MJ m−3, and a fatigue threshold of 275.31 J m−2, close to those of native heart valve leaflets. The aPGC/Fe hydrogels showed good hemocompatibility and cytocompatibility. Furthermore, interlayer assembly was employed to mimic the native trilayer architecture of human heart valve leaflets, while microgrooves were patterned on the hydrogel surfaces to regulate near-wall fluid behavior. Artificial heart valves fabricated from the post-processed aPGC/Fe hydrogels reproduced physiologic hydrodynamic performance with effective orifice area (EOA) and regurgitant fraction (RF) values satisfying the requirements of the ISO 5840-2 standard. Collectively, these results establish a reinforcement and post-processing strategy for translating fibrous hydrogels into biomedical devices. © 2026

title: Defect-driven construction of fully exposed Ru clusters on CeO2 for efficient low-temperature CO2 methanation
abstract: High-density oxygen vacancies were constructed on the CeO2 support via H2 prereduction, and the loading of Ru in the form of two-dimensional fully exposed clusters was successfully induced thereby, rather than conventional three-dimensional nanoparticles. The directional injection of charge into Ru clusters was driven by oxygen vacancies, resulting in an upward shift of the D-band center and an increase in electron cloud density, and the activation of CO2 molecules was significantly enhanced. In addition to the direct CO* dissociation pathway, the presence of a parallel HCOO* pathway on the catalyst was revealed by in-situ characterizations and calculations. The energy barrier of the rate-determining step was reduced from 0.75 eV to 0.56–0.65 eV by the synergy of the two pathways. Consequently, a CO2 conversion of 32.3% was achieved by Ru/CeO2-Ov at 150 °C, and the TOFs value was enhanced by nearly two orders of magnitude compared with the reference sample. No deactivation was observed during 400 h of stability testing. This work provides a new strategy for constructing efficient methanation catalysts through defect engineering. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Design principles of metallophthalocyanine-based ORR catalysts: Coordination environment and spin-state engineering
abstract: Metallophthalocyanine (MPc) complexes with well-defined M-N4 coordination sites are promising non‑precious metal catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet their rational design is limited by incomplete mechanistic understanding and computational challenges. This review establishes actionable design principles by examining how coordination geometry, ligand substitution, and spin configuration collectively govern O2 adsorption, O–O bond activation, and reaction pathway selectivity. Spin state is highlighted as a tunable catalytic degree of freedom, particularly for modulating intermediate binding and 4e−/2e− selectivity. We discuss the electronic origins of activity trends across 3d transition metal MPcs, the modulating effects of electron‑donating and electron‑withdrawing substituents, and the synergistic roles of carbon supports in enhancing conductivity and active‑site utilization. Current limitations in density functional theory calculations, including functional dependence, van der Waals interactions, and spin‑crossover modeling, are comprehensively assessed alongside the persistent theory‑experiment gap. By bridging coordination chemistry and theoretical modeling, this review offers an open framework for the rational development of efficient, stable, and earth‑abundant MPc‑based ORR catalysts. © 2026

title: Synergistic enhancement of actuation performance through crystallographic texturing and configuration optimization
abstract: Piezoelectric actuators must simultaneously achieve large stroke, good linearity, and high precision. Piezoelectric property enhancement plays a critical role in improving actuation performance. In this study, [001]c textured 0.73Pb(Mg1/3Nb2/3)O3-0.27PbTiO3-Gd2O3 (PMN-PT-Gd) ceramics with F001 = 98% were fabricated via the templated grain growth method. The textured ceramics exhibit excellent piezoelectric properties, including d33 = 1300 pC/N, d31 = −417 pC/N, k31 = 45%, kp = 70%, d33* = 1460 pm/V, and a low Hs = 5.6% under 20 kV/cm. Finite element analysis demonstrated that a square-tube configuration actuator yielded a significant increase in the output displacement, compared with that of the conventional cylindrical-tube structure, along with a more uniform stress distribution and lower energy dissipation. The actuator achieves remarkable performance improvement through the synergistic effect of enhanced piezoelectric properties and configuration optimization. The piezoelectric scanners based on textured PMN-PT-Gd ceramics exhibited an emitted spot displacement range 83.2% larger than that of the PZT-5H based counterparts, and also showed excellent linearity with respect to the driving voltage. These results demonstrate that the textured piezoceramic scanner with a square-tube configuration features strong potential for application in high-precision laser-modulation systems and miniature insertable medical endoscopes. © 2026

title: Permanent magnet synchronous motor parameter identification considering nonlinearities based on harmonic suppression and an improved black-winged kite algorithm
abstract: Aiming at the loss of accuracy and stability in permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) parameter identification under voltage source inverter (VSI) nonlinearities, this study develops an improved black-winged kite algorithm with PIR harmonic suppression. First, a PIR controller is used to suppress the sixth-order harmonics of the d-q axis currents. This reduces the adverse effect of VSI nonlinearities on the quality of identification data. Second, a snowmelt factor is introduced to adaptively adjust the position update step in the attack phase, which improves both exploration and exploitation. Finally, a cooperative migration strategy based on Bezier curves is designed to enhance convergence stability and speed. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method maintains reliable identification performance under the tested operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Noise-resilient meta-learning on the Grassmann manifold for few-shot fault diagnosis of industrial robots
abstract: Fault diagnosis for industrial robots is critically challenged by the limited labeled data and noise. Conventional meta-learning methods assume Euclidean data structures and lack adaptive mechanisms to cope with noise. Thus, they are highly vulnerable to noisy perturbations, resulting in suboptimal discriminative power and unstable prototype estimation. To address these challenges, we propose a noise-resilient meta-learning (NRML) framework on the Grassmann manifold. Specifically, a noise-aware damped distance (NADD) is developed to provide a robust similarity measure under varying noise levels. NADD employs a task-adaptive damping mechanism that dynamically balances the discriminative sensitivity and noise robustness, and it is formally proven to be a valid distance. Furthermore, an energy-thresholded subspace prototype (ETSP) is designed for adaptive and compact class representation on this manifold under extremely limited and noisy support samples. Comprehensive experiments on a public bearing dataset and a homemade industrial robot dataset demonstrate that NRML consistently outperforms multiple classical and state-of-the-art few-shot diagnosis methods. The experimental results indicate that the proposed manifold-based adaptive framework offers a practical and effective solution for robust few-shot fault diagnosis of industrial robots. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: 4d orbital mediated adaptive spin-electronic regulation steering non-radical oxidation
abstract: The ability to selectively direct reactive oxygen species evolution is emerging as a prerequisite for developing efficient and sustainable peroxymonosulfate (PMS)-based advanced oxidation processes, yet the catalytic principles governing reaction-pathway selectivity remain poorly understood. Here we demonstrate that introducing spatially extended Mo 4d orbitals into inverse spinel CoFe2-xMoxO4 establishes a reaction-responsive spin-electronic regulation of octahedral Co active sites. Unlike conventional electronic modifications, Mo dynamically interacts with neighboring Co 3d states, continuously modulating interfacial electron redistribution and stabilizing an intermediate-spin configuration (t2 g6eg1) throughout the catalytic cycle. This adaptive spin-electronic state strengthens Co-PMS orbital coupling, facilitates proton-coupled electron transfer, and lowers the energy barrier for Co (IV)=O formation, thereby redirecting PMS activation toward a selective non-radical 1O2 pathway. Consequently, CoFe1.7Mo0.3O4 delivers an 11-fold enhancement in reaction rate compared with pristine CoFe2O4, together with superior stability and environmental compatibility. Integrated spectroscopic analyses, electrochemical measurements, and density functional theory calculations consistently confirm that the enhanced catalytic performance originates from orbital-driven spin-electronic adaptation rather than static electronic modulation, establishing a general framework for steering reaction-pathway in advanced oxidation processes and provides mechanistic insights for designing high-performance environmental catalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Reconstruction-driven bifunctional electrocatalysis over CeO2@Ni3S2 heterostructures: Boosting biomass and OH– adsorption for efficient HMFOR
abstract: Anodic value-added chemical production paired with cathodic H2 evolution is highly practically valuable. In this work, a heterojunction Ni3S2@CeO2 was grown on nickel foam (NF) via a hydrothermal–impregnating method, which could act as highly efficient bifunctional electrocatalysts for both electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and electrocatalytic oxidation reaction of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMFOR). The electronic structure of Ni3S2 was effectively regulated due to the excellent electron-absorbing ability of CeO2. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and multiple characterization tests revealed that the Ni3S2@CeO2 heterointerface promotes the adsorption of HMF and OH– as well as accelerate the reconstruction of NiOOH from Ni3S2, which greatly improved the electrochemical ability. The optimal CeO2@Ni3S2/NF-2h exhibited much better excellent HER and HMFOR performances. The overpotential of CeO2@Ni3S2/NF-2h was only 304 mV to reach 100 mA cm–2 for HER. For HMFOR, the yield and Faraday efficiency of FDCA reached 97.89% and 98.97% respectively. The stability test of the anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) demonstrates that the catalyst can operate stably at an industrial current density of 500 mA cm–2. This work provides novel theoretical insights and material design guiddlines for subsequent industrial applications of Ce-modulated bifunctional catalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Sulfur-driven in situ oxygen vacancy engineering in TiO2 enables efficient photocatalytic transfer hydrogenation of furfural
abstract: Photocatalytic transfer hydrogenation (PTH) of biomass-derived furfural (FF) to furfuryl alcohol (FA) using methanol as a green hydrogen donor represents a sustainable route for producing value-added chemicals, yet developing robust noble-metal-free catalysts remains challenging. Herein, we present a sulfur-doped TiO2 photocatalyst exhibiting exceptional activity and selectivity for FF hydrogenation. The optimized catalyst delivers an impressive space-time FA yield of 44.0 mmolFA·gcat.−1·h−1 with 99.5% selectivity under 500 mW·cm−2 irradiation, surpassing most state-of-the-art systems. Comprehensive characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that lattice-substituted sulfur atoms form surface S–O species, driving oxygen vacancy formation and modulating the electronic structure of TiO2. The synergistic interaction between S species and VO sites regulates the electron density at active sites, thereby markedly promoting FF adsorption/activation, charge separation, and targeted hydrogenation. This work establishes a strategy for constructing high-efficiency, non-precious photocatalysts through sulfur-mediated oxygen-vacancy engineering. © 2026
