title: A pseudo-labeling approach for automated assignment of unlabeled proteins exceeding 100 amino acid residues
abstract: In the era of AI-driven protein structure prediction, there is an urgent demand for rapid, accessible experimental approaches to validate computationally predicted structural models or to improve the accuracy of AI-based structure determination. As a key experimental technique for determining protein structures in solution, conventional biomolecular NMR spectroscopy relies heavily on proteins labeled with 13C and 15N isotopes, a requirement that entails high experimental costs, lengthy sample preparation times, and steep technical barriers, thereby limiting its broader application. Building on our previous work, we have developed a pseudo-labeling strategy for the automated resonance assignment of unlabeled proteins. Using high-field NMR spectrometers equipped with cryoprobes, we acquired natural-abundance 1H–13C and 1H–15N heteronuclear correlation spectra directly from unlabeled samples. By integrating predicted chemical shifts of HN, Hα, 13Cα, and 15N from three complementary AI tools into an iterative simulated annealing framework with an alternating scoring scheme, our method effectively resolves severe cross-peak overlap during the automated assignment process by introducing heteronuclear dimensional constraints. This approach enables reliable automated backbone resonance assignment for unlabeled proteins exceeding 100 amino acid residues. We anticipate that this labeling-free strategy will lower the technical barrier to biomolecular NMR, enabling researchers without specialized NMR expertise to employ NMR spectroscopy in fundamental life science research and drug development. © 2026 The Authors.

title: A new partial differential system involving evolutionary variational-hemivariational inequalities arising in contact mechanics
abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of a new partial differential system involving an evolutionary variational inequality, a history-dependent hemivariational inequality and a partial differential equation in Banach spaces. Under mild conditions, by applying Banach’s fixed point theorem, we prove a unique solvability result for the problem. Furthermore, the main results are applied to obtain the unique solvability of a long-memory viscoelastic frictional contact problem that incorporates wear, damage, and a curved contact surface. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
label: Science (including Engineering)

title: Engineering high coordination shell of single-atom Fe-N-C to enhance electronic push-pull and oxygen reduction performance
abstract: The development of iron single-atom catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is hindered by the strong adsorption of oxygenated intermediates on the Fe-Nx active sites and the sluggish kinetics of ORR. In general, the intrinsic ORR activity of Fe-N4 sites is constrained by their plane-symmetric D4 h coordination environment. Herein, an exceptional Fe-N4OP configuration is proposed by constructing an outer coordination sphere consisting of Fe atom coordinated with four in-plane N atoms and one axially oriented O atom in the first shell, together with the simultaneously incorporated P in the second coordination shell. Benefiting from the coordination shell engineering, the ORR activity and stability of Fe-N4OP/NPCS catalyst are significantly improved compared to other Fe-N-C counterparts and approximate to Pt/C. Experimental results and theoretical calculations reveal that the electron-donating P species and electron-withdrawing O species triggered a synergistic push-pull electronic effect. As a consequence, the Fe-N4OP sites with suitable electron density and D-band center can effectively regulate the intermediate adsorption and alleviate the energy barrier of the rate-determining step. This work expounds the significance of push-pull electronic effect on electronic structure and the local environment in high-coordination single-atom electrocatalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
label: Science (including Engineering)

title: A real time simulation of rule-based energy management system for PV array and battery bank using OPAL-RT with ARTEMIS technique
abstract: A nano-grid is a power distribution system comprising several energy sources. However, the intermittent nature of photovoltaic energy sources and the uncertainty of load demands are major challenges in efficient and reliable nano-grid operations. As such, this study addresses gaps in real-time energy management for nano-grid system based on short-term dynamic validation by proposing a rule-based energy management system for real-time power flow control to maintain the stability and power balance of nano-grid system. Real-time simulations, via the OPAL-RT platform, specifically the OP5700 test bench, was used to validate the performance of the proposed rule-based energy management system. Furthermore, the researchers used the ARTEMiS optimization technique to carry out real-time activities in a multi-converter framework. This technique categorises the nano-grid system into four independent subsystems and pre-calculates the state-space matrices for the different switching topologies, thereby eliminating the computationally expensive matrix processes, which lead to execution overruns. The proposed rule-based energy management system was utilized to manage local controllers, namely, converters and inverters. The rule-based energy management system was responsible for making critical decisions regarding real-time power distribution, load balancing, and system stability, while the local controllers implemented the directives. This technique was used for testing the four operating scenarios, which included dynamic load requirements, variable photovoltaic generation, and grid interaction modes. The results of all the experiments indicated that the rule-based energy management system displayed a zero computational overrun, with a primary computation time of 8.84 μs, 48.48% CPU utilization, and communication latency less than 1 s. This study has addressed the crucial gap between theoretical energy management system designs and fully operational control systems by conducting a real-time validation of a rule-based energy management system technique specifically designed for nano-grid system based on the OPAL-RT platform with ARTEMiS optimization. The results provide reference real-time performance benchmarks relevant to short-term feasibility evaluation of energy management strategies for small-scale renewable energy systems. © 2026 The Authors. title: Inhibiting strength degradation through delayed recrystallization: A texture-controlled heterogeneous recrystallization mechanism in Ni-Cr-Mo-W superalloy foil
abstract: Ni-Cr-Mo-W superalloy foil serves as a key substrate for second-generation high-temperature superconducting tapes, but its strength degradation during high-temperature coating limits performance. This study demonstrated that the dynamic competition of deformation mechanisms during cold rolling produced specific crystallographic textures, which governed stored energy distribution and subsequently suppressed strength loss during recrystallization. Within the investigated range, an apparent transition from slip-twinning synergy to pronounced shear band formation and twinning-dominated texture transformation occurred around 60% reduction. Quantitative analysis revealed a stored energy sequence of γ-fiber > <112>-fiber > S texture > α-fiber. Focused ion beam transmission electron microscopy (FIB-TEM) observations showed that shear bands formed mainly in γ/<112>-fiber regions contained high-density nanotwins and stacking faults, providing additional interfacial energy. Consequently, recrystallized grains preferentially nucleated at or near these high stored energy regions, while low stored energy α-fiber regions exhibited delayed recrystallization and retained work hardening, alleviating strength loss. Under the present 900 °C for 5 min annealing condition, the 50% cold-rolled sample provided the best strength-retention window. These findings provide a basis for mitigating annealing softening in metal foils. © 2026

title: Variable reactive power compensators versus fixed and switchable capacitor banks in providing ancillary services considering voltage fluctuations
abstract: Voltage fluctuations across distribution network buses can significantly influence both load consumption patterns and the reactive power output of compensation devices. To address these effects, strategic placement of reactive power support equipment is essential. While prior research has extensively examined the positioning of capacitors for loss minimization and voltage enhancement, limited attention has been given to the economic implications of deploying variable reactive power compensators—such as thyristor-switched capacitors (TSCs) or static VAR and static synchronous compensators (SVCs and STATCOMs)—for ancillary service provision under dynamic voltage conditions. Moreover, representative analytical approaches may rely on nonlinear optimization techniques or simplified linear models, creating a tradeoff between model fidelity and computational effort when the sensitivity of reactive power output to voltage variations. Nonlinear approaches can be computationally intensive and difficult to implement. In this paper, a computationally efficient mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) framework is proposed to incorporate voltage fluctuations into the economic evaluation of fixed and switchable capacitors, and variable reactive power devices. The model is solved using commercial linear solvers and enables effective planning of reactive power resources while maintaining computational tractability. Case studies on standard 33- and 69-bus distribution systems declare that the proposed approach improves technical and economic indicators in the investigated cases. In the 33-bus system, variable reactive power compensators reduced total annual cost by 76.3% compared with fixed capacitors while improving the minimum voltage from 0.93 to 0.981 pu and generating annual ancillary service revenues of up to 13,578$. In the 69-bus system, variable reactive sources achieved up to 13.2% greater cost savings and 11.7% higher loss reduction than fixed capacitors. The results further show that voltage-dependent load modeling significantly affects the optimal allocation and sizing of reactive compensation devices, with constant-impedance loading conditions generally yielding the lowest losses and best voltage profiles. Furthermore, the proposed framework obtained high-quality solutions within only a few seconds, demonstrating its computational efficiency. These findings demonstrate, for the investigated systems, the potential technical and economic benefits of integrating voltage-dependent load and reactive power behavior, flexible reactive power resources, and ancillary-service revenues into distribution system planning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Inside the cooling die: prediction of the flow profile of a high-moisture soy protein melt during extrusion
abstract: The fibrous structure of plant protein-based meat analogues, manufactured using high-moisture extrusion, is determined by the flow in the cooling die. However, currently there is little understanding of how the rheological properties influence said flow. In this work, we predict how a soy protein melt flows under changing inlet temperature, cooling temperature, and pH. The model relies on a pH- and temperature-dependent dynamic yield stress and a wall slip equation, parametrised by in situ MRI velocimetry measurements in a circular die. The model predicts that the inlet velocity profile quickly transforms into plug flow for neutral and acidic pH conditions, where the dynamic yield stress is higher. Under alkaline conditions, where the dynamic yield stress is lower, the central core remains flowing, after which it transitions to plug flow. The model was validated by pressure and temperature profiles from a rectangular cooling die, measured along the length of the cooling die. The model provides insight into the link between solidification of the protein melt and the shear stress and the velocity profiles inside the cooling die. Thus, a scalable model was created that can be used to predict the pressure drops and temperature/velocity profiles over different geometries and cooling conditions. This will enable future work to more accurately model flow in the transition zone and cooling die. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: Sustained thermal stability over 1000 h in Cu–15Ni–8Sn alloy by Ti-guided exclusive L12 precipitation
abstract: Long-term precipitate stability at high temperatures remains a key challenge in metallic materials. This study demonstrates a Ti-guided strategy to enhance thermal stability of Cu–15Ni–8Sn alloys by suppressing discontinuous precipitation (DP) while promoting the ordering transformation (OT). The addition of 0.3 wt.% Ti reduces the critical formation concentration of L12 below that of DO22, leading to earlier onset of spinodal decomposition; the resulting Ti partitioning into L12 accelerates OT kinetics, depleting supersaturation and the chemical driving force for DP, which ultimately suppresses DP at grain boundaries and facilitates high-density intragranular L12 precipitation. First-principles calculations confirm that Ti substitution for Sn significantly reduces L12 formation energy. Consequently, the alloy maintains peak hardness even after 1000 h of aging. These findings establish a universal “guided” mechanism for tailoring precipitation pathways toward superior high-temperature performance in spinodal decomposed alloys. © 2026

title: Existence and Hausdorff convergence of sliding phenomena in traveling waves for a fast-slow Keller-Segel equation
abstract: A one-dimensional Keller-Segel equation with a piecewise-defined reaction term depending on the density gradient gives rise to a nonsmooth fast-slow system. Using Filippov convexification and geometric singular perturbation theory, we prove the existence of sliding traveling wave solutions for sufficiently small ε > 0 and characterize the corresponding sliding region. In the singular limit ε=0, we construct a singular sliding heteroclinic orbit on the critical manifold and show that it persists for sufficiently small ε > 0 under appropriate conditions on the wave speed and model parameters. The family of perturbed orbits converges to the singular orbit in the Hausdorff distance as ε → 0. These results provide a rigorous construction of sliding traveling waves for a chemotaxis model with gradient-dependent switching. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A regional partition-aided multi-task prediction framework for substation flooding and secondary disasters based on improved Transformer
abstract: Frequent extreme rainstorms have seriously threatened the safe operation of substations, causing enormous economic losses. Accurate prediction of substation flood depth and the resulting equipment damage and outage risks is crucial for enhancing disaster resilience. Traditional models face great challenges due to strong spatial correlations among substations, multi-scale temporal dependencies, heterogeneous data types, and data imbalance. To address these limitations, the proposed substation multiple flooding risks Transformer (SMFR-Former) adopts an integrated design that simultaneously couples regional spatial partitioning, dynamic-static heterogeneous representation, and train loss-balancing mechanism within a unified architecture for the joint prediction of the three risks.A regional partitioning strategy is introduced to characterize latent spatial correlations among substations, while adaptive temporal encoding strengthens the extraction of complex temporal dependencies. To achieve effective heterogeneous data fusion, distinct encoders are designed for different data modalities, and adaptive weighting is employed to dynamically optimize feature integration. Furthermore, a dynamic train loss-balancing mechanism is developed to alleviate inter-task optimization conflicts during multi-task learning. The experimental results show that each strategy is effective and compatible with each other. SMFR-Former outperforms Transformer model, reducing the RMSE of flood depth and equipment damage degree prediction by 30.00% and 26.94%, respectively, while improving the F1 score of outage probability prediction by 18.31%. Furthermore,cross-regional validation results demonstrate that the proposed SMFR-Former maintains strong generalization capability under different spatial distributions and regional characteristics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Atomic engineering of stability-kinetics Ce-Fe dyads in Ni3S2 for efficient urea-assisted hydrogen production
abstract: Replacing the energy-intensive oxygen evolution reaction (OER) with the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) presents a promising route for energy-saving hydrogen production coupled with wastewater remediation. However, developing electrocatalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and long-term stability remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we propose and validate a novel “kinetic-structural synergy” design principle by constructing atomic-scale Ce-Fe binary catalytic unit within Ni3S2 nanoarrays. Unlike random doping, this defined architecture enables a functional division of labor. The Fe site acts as a kinetic promoter to dramatically lower the potential for active NiOOH phase formation, while the adjacent Ce site functions as a structural and electronic stabilizer, securing the high-valent Ni intermediates. The resulting catalyst achieves an ultra-low UOR potential. When configured in a two-electrode urea electrolyzer, it requires only 1.37 V to deliver 100 mA·cm−2 current density and maintains remarkable stability for over 510 h. In situ Raman spectroscopy directly evidences the earliest formation and exceptional persistence of the NiOOH phase on this catalyst. Combined X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) analysis and density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate from the atomic-level principle that the Fe-Ce unit cooperatively tunes the local coordination and electronic structure of Ni, leading to an optimal Ni-S bond length and a favorable D-band center of Ni site, collectively facilitating the reaction pathway. This work demonstrates that targeted lanthanide-transition metal pairing can create integrated catalytic units where activity and stability are inherently coupled, providing a new design strategy for advanced energy conversion systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Comparative optimization of biohydrogen production and purification using pressure swing adsorption
abstract: Biohydrogen production has emerged as a promising alternative for the development of sustainable energy systems due to its high calorific value and potential to reduce polluting emissions. Among the most efficient purification technologies, pressure swing adsorption stands out for its ability to increase hydrogen purity through selective separation processes. The objective of this article is to perform a sensitivity analysis and parametric study, which allows for the identification of the most influential operating variables on the performance of the rigorous pressure swing adsorption process. Therefore, the evaluation of a two-bed pressure swing adsorption plant is fundamental to optimizing key indicators such as energy efficiency, productivity, and biohydrogen recovery. Significant results were achieved, as the sensitivity analysis showed that the best breakthrough curve was obtained by using the temperature variable, which adsorbed a greater amount of the compounds CO2, CO, and CH4 in a shorter time (300 s[jls-end-space/]) compared to the other variables. The results obtained from the parametric study after achieving a biohydrogen purity of 99.9% were outstanding, as it was determined that the composition variable resulted in a greater retention of CO2 along the column. However, with the temperature variable, the purity of the biohydrogen was 99.1% compared to the other purities obtained (production and purge pressure variables). A recovery of 60.24% was achieved, with a productivity of 0.0021 (Formula presented) and an energy efficiency that ranged between 0.89% and 2.10%. © 2026 The Authors. title: Incremental resistance MPPT algorithm with proportional integral compensator for extended DC-DC buck-boost converter in PV systems
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power output is significantly influenced by environmental and climatic variables, such as the sun's irradiance, air humidity, and ambient temperature. In addition, most PV power sources have relatively small output voltages not suited for direct utilization by common loads. Additionally, PV power output depends also on the PV operating voltage and current. In this sense, a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithm is required to achieve maximum power output and improved efficiency in PV systems. Due to shadowing or fast irradiance changes, MPPT algorithms must operate at high speed and accuracy. Thus, this paper proposes a MPPT control strategy based on incremental resistance (INR) combined with a proportional-integral (PI) compensator (INR-PI). This approach modifies the seldom used INR MPPT algorithm to set the current and combines it with a proportional-integral compensator to regulate the I-V operating point of the PV panel. This reformulates the INR principle as a PV panel voltage regulation problem ensuring closed-loop stability and disturbance rejection. The theoretical analysis considers the dynamics of the input current in a quadratic Buck-Boost converter with an extended duty-cycle range in the Buck voltage region, connected to a DC microgrid. The proposed MPPT technique is designed to ensure fast and efficient operation of PV systems under rapidly changing environmental conditions. To validate this control system, initial simulations were conducted using MATLAB/Simulink, followed by experimental testing with a laboratory prototype setup. Both numerical and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the feedback-based incremental resistance algorithm in tracking the maximum power point (MPP) of PV systems when irradiance fluctuates quickly. © 2026 The Authors

title: Parameter determination method for model of ZnO varistors based on dynamic V-I characteristics
abstract: This study investigates the dynamic volt-ampere characteristics and residual voltage responses of ZnO varistor of five different sizes under various impulse waveforms, including 8/20 μs lightning current, 30/80 μs operating wave, 1/5 μs steep wave, and 2 ms square wave impulses. The experimental results demonstrate that larger ZnO varistor exhibit a downward shift in the dynamic volt-ampere characteristic curve. The IEEE frequency-dependent model was used in simulations to evaluate its applicability to different waveforms. For 8/20 μs and 30/80 μs impulses, the model yielded simulation errors within 5 %, while for 1/5 μs and square wave impulses, the errors were approximately 10 %. Significant discrepancies were observed between the experimentally measured and simulated energy absorption values, indicating the IEEE model's limitations in accurately representing such waveforms. To address this, the circuit structure and nonlinear resistance parameters in the IEEE model were revised based on experimental dynamic volt-ampere data. The resulting improved simulation model reduced the average simulation errors for residual voltage to within 4 % for the four waveforms especially for the three waveforms of 8/20 μs, 30/80 μs and 1/5 μs, the errors are within 2 % and for energy absorption to within 4 % across all tested varistor sizes and waveforms. These results confirm the enhanced accuracy and applicability of the improved model for simulating both residual voltage and energy absorption. The value of nonlinear resistance in the model has been clearly defined and can be obtained from experimental results. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A novel approach to optimal PMU placement for state estimation in electric power systems
abstract: This paper proposes a new method for the optimal placement of phasor measurement units (PMUs) in power systems. The proposed method minimizes the number of PMUs to be embedded in the network by leveraging virtual current injection measurements at zero-injection buses. This approach guarantees full system observability under normal and N-1 operating states without requiring conventional post-placement observability propagation rules. Unlike other approaches, the proposed optimization model uses equality constraints to account for the virtual measurements, thereby avoiding the need to change the network topology or use merging techniques to eliminate nodes with virtual measurements during the PMU placement process. The proposal's effectiveness is demonstrated on several benchmark IEEE power systems and the Polish 2383-bus large-scale system, considering base topology cases and N-1 contingency scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Valorization of camel milk whey into a synbiotic fermented sports beverage enriched with Guddaim fruit extract (Grewia tenax) and coconut milk: Phenolic profile, antioxidant activity, microbiological viability, and storage stability
abstract: This study investigates the structural, rheological, and functional properties of a synbiotic fermented beverage formulated from camel milk whey and coconut milk, enriched with Guddaim (Grewia tenax) polysaccharides. Camel whey serves as a protein-rich hydrocolloid matrix, while Guddaim polysaccharides and phenolic compounds interact with dairy proteins, modifying the beverage microstructure and viscosity. Fermentation with Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis and Lactobacillus plantarum produced a stable matrix with a final pH of 4.6. The incorporation of Guddaim extract significantly enhanced viscoelastic properties, gelation behavior, and microstructural stability, while also improving antioxidant activity and color. Probiotic viability remained above 106 CFU/mL during 30 days of refrigerated storage. These findings demonstrate that interactions between camel whey proteins and plant polysaccharides can effectively modulate structure–function relationships in fermented beverages, providing a strategy for valorization of camel whey and development of functional hydrocolloid-rich products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Lattice tensile strain restructures interfacial hydrogen‑bond network for boosted alkaline hydrogen evolution
abstract: The sluggish kinetics of alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), governed by water dissociation, remains a critical challenge for efficient hydrogen production. Here, we demonstrate that lattice tensile strain can regulate interfacial water structure and thereby accelerate HER kinetics. Density functional theory calculations identify an optimal tensile strain (~+2%) that maximizes p-d orbital hybridization and induces a favorable downshift of the D-band center, optimizing adsorption energetics. Meanwhile, the strain-enhanced built-in electric field promotes charge transfer to interfacial water, facilitating its activation. Guided by this principle, a Mo/W-CoP catalyst supported on etched NiCu1-x@Ni foam with a tensile strain of ~ + 1.9% is constructed. An operando Raman imaging approach is developed to spatially resolve lattice strain and interfacial water configurations, revealing that tensile-strain-rich domains serve as preferential sites for the enrichment of coordinated water, thereby reconstructing the hydrogen-bond network. Consequently, the catalyst delivers an overpotential of 133 mV at −50 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH. This work establishes a direct link between lattice strain and interfacial hydrogen-bond network, offering a general strategy for engineering electrocatalytic interfaces. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A geology-guided GBDT–BiSSM framework for carbonate reservoir classification from well logs
abstract: Accurate reservoir classification is essential for the efficient development of carbonate hydrocarbon reservoirs. Strong heterogeneity, complex diagenetic alteration, and overlapping well-log responses make this task difficult in the low-porosity and low-permeability Jialingjiang Formation of the central Sichuan Basin. To address this challenge, a GBDT-BiSSM fusion framework is proposed by integrating gradient boosting decision trees with a multiscale bidirectional state-space model. GBDT extracts static discriminative information from multivariate logging responses, whereas BiSSM learns depth-dependent contextual representations from ordered well-log sequences to characterize vertical variations and boundary-related transitions. Geological information is not embedded as an explicit constraint in the model-training process; instead, the fused predictions are refined during inference using geological-consistency decoding based on reservoir thickness, evaporite-related responses, and vertical reservoir continuity. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an overall classification accuracy of 92.9% and effectively reduces isolated label fluctuations and the misclassification of thin reservoirs. The method provides an effective approach for the detailed delineation of low-porosity and low-permeability carbonate reservoirs and the prediction of high-quality reservoir intervals. © 2026 The Authors. title: s-orbital modulated d-band center of Cu1−δ active site via interfacial electron spillover effect for nitrate reduction to ammonia
abstract: Photoelectrochemical nitrate reduction to ammonia offers a promising route for sustainable closure of the nutrient loop and auxiliary renewable energy storage. However, the currently reported electrodes are still limited by sluggish kinetics and poor ammonia selectivity. Herein, a strategy based on the interfacial electron spillover effect is proposed to modulate the d‐band center of materials with fully occupied d‐orbitals, such as copper-based catalysts. By engineering the Cu/Cu2O interfacial site, the 4s-electron-shielded interfacial cuprous sites (Cu1−δ) exhibit an elevated d‐band center with enhanced adsorption of *NO2 intermediate, thereby achieving a current of 20.8 mA cm−2, NH3 yield rate of 92.1 ± 0.7 μmol h−1 cm−2, and NH3 selectivity of 88.3 ± 0.5% at −0.4 V vs. RHE. This work provides a pragmatic strategy for d‐band center modulation to overcome adsorption limitations of crucial intermediates in materials with fully occupied d‐orbitals. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Quantitative decoding of Fe(IV)=O and Co(IV)=O in nonradical peroxymonosulfate activation over waste PET-derived FeCo-N-C
abstract: This study quantitatively decodes the individual contributions of Fe(IV)=O and Co(IV)=O in nonradical peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation over a waste PET-derived FeCo dual-site catalyst (FeCo-N-C). The catalyst, featuring atomically dispersed FeN4-CoN3 heteronuclear pairs, was prepared via a facile one-step pyrolysis. It achieved 99.78% tetracycline (TC) removal within 30 min, significantly outperforming its single-metal counterparts. Quantitative ROS analysis revealed that nonradical oxidation dominated the degradation process (96.11%), in which Fe(IV)=O and Co(IV)=O contributed 20.92% and 71.05%, while radicals and singlet oxygen (1O2) accounted for only 3.89% and 4.14%. Quenching, EPR, steady-state concentration measurements, and PMSO probing verified the dominant high-valent metal-oxo (HVMO) pathway. DFT calculations revealed that Fe-Co electronic coupling lowers the O-O bond cleavage barrier, steering PMS toward selective HVMO formation. This work quantitatively deciphers the contributions of individual HVMO species in a Fe-Co dual-site catalyst system and provides new insights into the rational design of selective PMS activation catalysts for environmental remediation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Ionizing irradiation induced non-equilibrium cation vacancies switching peroxymonosulfate activation pathways
abstract: Ionizing irradiation was investigated as a non-equilibrium defect-engineering strategy to generate Fe-vacancy-associated environments in spinel ferrites and thereby regulate peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation pathways. Using CoFe2O4 as a model catalyst, irradiation conditions were tuned to control Fe deficiency, while X-ray absorption spectroscopy, in situ Raman spectroscopy, electrochemical analyses, reactive-species quantification, and density functional theory calculations were integrated to resolve the resulting structure–activity relationship. The optimized catalyst exhibited a pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.285 min−1 for sulfamethoxazole degradation and 99.7% PMS utilization, with •OH and SO4•- accounting for 83.4% of degradation; Fe-vacancy-associated environments promoted cooperative Fe–Co electronic coupling, PMS adsorption, and O–O bond cleavage, while maintaining efficient oxidation across pH 5–9 and for diverse contaminants. These results establish that irradiation-induced Fe deficiency redirects PMS activation toward radical-dominated oxidation through local coordination and electronic-structure regulation. The extension to NiFe2O4 and MnFe2O4 and stable 168-h continuous-flow wastewater treatment further demonstrate the potential of non-equilibrium irradiation engineering as a general route for tuning reactive-species pathways in Fenton-like catalysis. © 2026

title: Fourier neural operators with least-squares readout refit for learning random obstacle-to-solution maps
abstract: We study operator learning for random obstacle-to-solution maps arising from elliptic variational inequalities with finite-band self-affine random obstacle fields. Instead of introducing an explicit truncated stochastic parametrization of the random input, we learn the map directly from sampled obstacle realizations on a fixed grid. This problem is challenging because the solution is governed not only by the obstacle field itself, but also by the induced contact set and free-boundary geometry. We introduce a post-training least-squares readout refit for the Fourier neural operator (FNO). After the FNO is trained end-to-end, its nonlinear backbone is frozen and the final affine readout is recomputed by solving the induced linear least-squares problem over all training samples and grid points. The refit yields the empirical squared-error optimal readout for the learned frozen features while leaving the nonlinear representation unchanged. We compare vanilla DeepONet, POD-DeepONet, a two-stage DeepONet baseline, FNO, and FNO with least-squares readout refit (FNO-LS) on two obstacle ensembles with different amplitude levels. Numerical results show that FNO-LS achieves the best average field accuracy and the strongest structure-sensitive performance among the tested models, particularly in the higher-amplitude regime. The least-squares refit further improves contact-set recovery and obstacle-violation metrics at low additional cost, especially when the FNO backbone is informative but not fully converged. These results suggest that least-squares readout refit is a simple and effective post-training enhancement for learning random obstacle-to-solution maps. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Impact of gamma irradiation as a non-thermal technology on the structural, digestive, and rheological properties of rice bean (Vigna umbellata) protein isolate and its application in the development of 3D printable food ink
abstract: This study aimed to analyze the effect of gamma modification on the functional properties of rice bean protein isolate (RBPI) at doses of 3, 5, and 10 kGy. Both native and gamma-irradiated RBPI were characterized through structural, molecular, functional, rheological, and digestive analyses to evaluate the influence of different irradiation doses and identify a suitable dose for 3D food ink formulation. Gamma irradiation induced dose-dependent structural modifications, as evidenced by FTIR and UV–visible spectroscopy, particle size analysis, SDS–PAGE, and SEM, suggesting irradiation-induced structural modifications, alteration in particle organization, and microstructural changes without evidence of extensive protein degradation under the studied conditions. These structural modifications significantly (p < 0.05) improved solubility and water-binding capacity, particularly at moderate irradiation doses (3-5 kGy), whereas the highest in vitro protein digestibility was observed at 10 kGy. Rheological evaluation revealed enhanced shear-thinning behaviour, elastic dominance (G′ > G″), and improved viscoelastic stability in gamma-irradiated RBPI, reflecting stronger protein–protein interaction networks. Based on its favourable functional and rheological characteristics relevant to 3D printing, the modified RBPI was further applied to develop a fruit-based 3D-printable ink formulated with agar and guar gum. The rheological behaviour of native and gamma-irradiated RBPI-based inks was characterized, revealing enhanced shear-thinning, elastic dominance, and viscoelastic stability, which are considered favourable for extrusion-based 3D food printing. Textural analysis further indicated higher mechanical strength, cohesiveness, and structural integrity of the gamma-irradiated RBPI food ink, suggesting its potential as a component of a composite formulation for extrusion-based 3D food printing. Representative self-supporting printed structures were obtained under the selected printing conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Curvature-induced electronic asymmetry in hollow nanoreactors dictates pathway-selective radical chemistry for rapid water decontamination
abstract: This work unveils the pivotal role of curvature-induced electronic asymmetry of the carbon shell in governing radical chemistry during peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation within hollow nanoreactors. By selectively anchoring Co3O4 nanoparticles on the inner or outer surface of mesoporous hollow carbon nanospheres (Co3O4-in/out-MHCN), we isolate two chemically equivalent but electronically distinct catalytic interfaces. Spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal that curvature-induced lattice strain redistributes π-electron density outward, producing an electron-rich exterior that favors free radicals and singlet oxygen, while an electron-deficient interior stabilizes long-lived surface-bound radicals. This inward-directed asymmetry, synergizing with confinement-enhanced reactant enrichment, yields a 13.7-fold higher degradation rate constant for Co3O4-in-MHCN/PMS than for Co3O4-out-MHCN/PMS, and granular Co3O4-in-MHCN sustains continuous and biocompatible operation in a fluidized-bed reactor for 240 h. Curvature-induced electronic asymmetry thus emerges as a general design principle for steering reactive-species generation in hollow catalysts, advancing nanoconfined catalysis with high efficiency and more selective water purification. © 2026 The Authors

title: Integrated probabilistic framework for long-term solar resource reliability assessment for photovoltaic planning at provincial capitals in Sumatra
abstract: Reliable solar resource assessment requires consideration of both expected performance and associated uncertainty, particularly under heterogeneous climatic conditions. This study develops an integrated probabilistic framework for evaluating long-term solar resource reliability at ten provincial-capital reference locations across Sumatra, Indonesia. Satellite-derived hourly global horizontal irradiance data from 2015 to 2024 were temporally integrated to obtain daily global horizontal irradiation and analysed through climatological characterisation, probabilistic photovoltaic yield estimation, composite reliability assessment, multidimensional pattern recognition, and Bayesian hierarchical inference. Because the hourly observations were integrated into daily totals, the analysis characterises variability among daily irradiation values over the 2015–2024 period and does not resolve intraday fluctuations. Mean daily irradiation varied only moderately among the analysed locations, whereas temporal variability and photovoltaic yield uncertainty differed substantially. Median annual photovoltaic yield ranged from approximately 1330 to 1474 kWh/kWp/year, showing that locations with similar mean irradiation can exhibit markedly different long-term reliability characteristics. A composite reliability index combining normalised scores derived from temporal variability, annual photovoltaic yield spread, and resource magnitude ranged from approximately 0.15 to 0.80. The Bengkulu and Lampung reference locations obtained the two highest index values, whereas the Riau Islands reference location obtained the lowest. Bayesian hierarchical modelling quantified uncertainty in the location-level reliability estimates and generated partially pooled posterior estimates, thereby supporting more cautious interpretation of extreme deterministic scores. The framework provides a transparent and reproducible basis for preliminary comparative screening and for prioritising locations for detailed ground measurements and techno-economic assessment. The empirical findings are specific to the analysed locations in Sumatra; application to other tropical regions requires independent validation using locally representative and spatially distributed data. © 2026 The Authors. title: Dynamic modeling, grid synchronization, and power quality analysis of a geothermal ORC power plant using a coupled thermodynamic–Simulink framework
abstract: This study presents a site-specific coupled thermodynamic–electrical simulation framework for evaluating the grid-integration performance of the Afyon Geothermal Power Plant, a low-temperature geothermal Organic Rankine Cycle facility. The proposed approach combines EES-based thermodynamic property calculations with a dynamic MATLAB/Simulink electrical model, enabling simultaneous assessment of ORC performance, grid synchronization, transient voltage–frequency response, and power-quality behavior. The grid interface is represented by a synchronous generator, transformer, transmission line, RLC load, circuit breaker, measurement blocks, and a Phase-Locked Loop based synchronization unit. The model was parameterized using published operating data from the Afyon plant, including a geothermal fluid temperature of 110 °C, a mass flow rate of 150 kg/s, R134a as the working fluid, and a reported plant capacity of approximately 3 MW. Simulation results show that the system achieves stable synchronization within approximately 0.5 s after breaker closure, with the frequency converging to the nominal 50 Hz value and the voltage/current responses reaching steady-state without sustained oscillations. FFT-based harmonic analysis was performed for both grid-connected and standalone operating conditions. The calculated THD values were 0.49% for grid-connected current, 0.02% for grid-connected voltage, 0.01% for standalone current, and 0.02% for standalone voltage, remaining well below the IEEE 519-based 5% reference limit. The validation and sensitivity results indicate that the net-equivalent power output approaches the reported 3 MW plant capacity, while geothermal temperature and brine-flow variations mainly affect the ORC power output without destabilizing PLL-based synchronization. A simplified techno-economic assessment further shows a unit electricity cost of approximately 0.0233 $/kWh and a simple payback period of about 3.2 years under base Afyon operating conditions. The developed framework provides a reproducible benchmark model for assessing thermodynamic performance, grid compatibility, and power quality in low-temperature geothermal ORC power plants. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Hierarchically confined electrode enabling surface-enhanced atomic hydrogen concentration for advanced electrocatalytic hydrodehalogenation
abstract: Electrocatalytic hydrodehalogenation (ECH) is a promising strategy for detoxifying chlorinated organic pollutants; however, its efficiency is often limited by the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), resulting in low electron utilization efficiency. Because both ECH and HER share atomic hydrogen (H*) as a common intermediate, regulating the fate of H* is critical for improving reaction selectivity and energy efficiency. Here, we propose a hierarchically confined electrode design by embedding a core–shell confined architecture into a sandwich-type electrocatalytic membrane. The core-shell structure acts as a local reservoir to enhance the surface concentration of H* in the cavity, while the hierarchically confined graphene oxide (GO) layers is engineered to improve mass transport. By prolonging the residence time of H* and suppressing its recombination into molecular hydrogen, the confined membrane preferentially promotes H*-mediated hydrodehalogenation. Using 2,4,6-trichlorophenol (2,4,6-TCP) as a model pollutant, the freestanding electrocatalytic electrode achieved 91.5% degradation within 120 min. Scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) and COMSOL verified the H* confinement capability within the core–shell structure, while electrochemical characterizations and scanning electrochemical microscopy (SECM) revealed effective suppression of HER and regulation of current density distribution by GO layers. This study elucidates how hierarchically confined, diffusion-limited electrocatalytic electrode govern the fate of H* and provides a structure-based strategy for enhancing electron utilization efficiency and energy efficiency in ECH. Synopsis: A flow-through GO sandwich electrode embedding Pd@Co–N/C nanocatalysts created H*-rich microenvironment that markedly enhanced electro-hydrodechlorination of chlorinated organic pollutants. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Neutral current redistribution and differentiated dc bias protection of multiple main transformers in one substation via a refined metro–grid coupling model
abstract: Significant differences in neutral currents exist among different grounded main transformers within the same substation. Simplifying the substation as a single conductor fails to resolve the internal distribution of metro-induced stray current, thereby masking potential DC bias risks. To prevent such failures, a refined metro–power system coupling model that considers multiple main transformers is established using actual parameters of the metro system, power grid, and local soil. The model accurately calculates neutral current of different interconnected transformers, enabling early identification of uneven current distribution that may lead to DC bias. Results show that the maximum ratio of absolute neutral currents among transformers reaches 2.76, while the minimum mean absolute current error against field measurements is 3.74%. A reduced-scale physical analogue provides supplementary validation of the model's ability to reproduce current redistribution among multiple transformer grounding branches. Based on this model, the influence of various metro operating conditions on stray current is analyzed to identify failure-prone scenarios. A neutral-point resistance model, combined with global optimization algorithms with verified stability, designs three-level differentiated protection schemes. The resulting schemes keep all transformer neutral currents within specified limits under the actual topology—unlike traditional-model-based schemes—thereby preventing DC bias-induced failures in multiple main transformers within the same substation. © 2026

title: Geometry-agnostic reinforcement learning for toolpath-dependent residual stress mitigation in metallic component manufacturing
abstract: Residual stress (RS) remains a critical bottleneck in toolpath-dependent metal fabrication processes such as additive manufacturing, machining, and welding, because toolpath‑induced thermal non-uniformity drives distortion, cracking, and premature failure. Existing RS optimization methods necessitate either computationally intensive, geometry-specific simulation searches or extensive data requirements for machine learning models that require retraining upon changes in part geometry. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel reinforcement learning (RL) framework that facilitates geometry-aware, layer-wise toolpath planning for unseen 3D geometries within the trained computational domain without the need for part-specific retraining. The target 3D geometry is voxelized, and the RL state integrates the current layer design with the accumulated 3D temperature field predicted by a finite difference method simulation that incorporates the heat source, heat transfer, and dwell time. The RL agent learns to select from 30 distinct toolpath patterns per layer to maximize thermal uniformity and mitigate RS. Consequently, the model reduces per-part optimization time by approximately three orders of magnitude compared with the evaluated search-based optimization baselines, demonstrating superior computational efficiency. Experimental validation demonstrates that the optimized toolpaths reduce warpage by up to 27.5% and mitigate the average RS within critical high-stress regions by up to 25.5%, while microstructural analysis reveals more uniform thermal histories. By integrating physics-based thermal modeling with RL, this framework demonstrates potential for extensibility to various manufacturing processes where the toolpath governs thermal quality. © 2026

title: Atomic-scale interfacial welding unlocks the electrochemical potential of chemically robust proton-conducting electrolytes
abstract: Solid-state electrochemical devices face a fundamental trade-off: chemical stability for durable operation often comes with surface inertness that passivates the electrode−electrolyte interface. This challenge is especially acute in proton-conducting ceramics like BaZr0.8Y0.2O3−δ (BZY), where chemical inertness suppresses interfacial kinetics, limiting conductivity to nearly two orders of magnitude below theoretical values. Here, we report an atomic-scale interfacial welding strategy that leverages the superior sintering activity of nanoparticles. Taking CuO as a model system, this welding agent drives bidirectional elemental interdiffusion between inert electrolyte and porous air electrode, transforming initially void-containing and discontinuous junctions into a continuous chemical continuum. Time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry and aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy confirm overlapping elemental gradients and intimate interfacial contact across the reconstructed junction. By eliminating interfacial discontinuities, the welded interface achieves a 2.85-fold increase in adhesion strength while establishing more continuous charge/ion-transfer pathways. The resulting BZY cell delivers a 3.94-fold enhancement in peak power density over the pristine counterpart, together with an apparent conductivity of 0.015 S cm−1 at 700 °C. By validating the feasibility across different material systems, this work establishes a transferable paradigm for unlocking the full potential of robust electrochemical devices. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A study on the mechanism of arc fault branch localization based on load response characteristics
abstract: Accurate localization of arc fault is a prerequisite for effective mitigation of electrical fire hazards; however, the underlying physical mechanisms that affect precise localization remain unclear. This paper systematically investigates the influence of load type, power level, and arc fault incandescence intensity on the intrinsic electrical and physical processes, by integrating experimental data with a mathematical model of arc fault current. First, empirical measurements are used to identify both commonalities and differences in arc fault responses across various load types. Subsequently, a coupling model—termed the dispersion relation—is established between load current loss ratio and arc fault characteristics based on the mathematical representation of fault current signals. This model systematically characterizes the interrelationship between arc fault features and load properties under varying degrees of incandescence, thereby revealing the fundamental mechanism of arc fault branch localization. Furthermore, it elucidates the root causes of response ambiguity under interference from homogeneous loads and proposes a technical pathway for resolution. The findings of this study provide theoretical foundations and directional guidance for developing future branch localization models for arc faults based on load response characteristics. © 2026

title: EXTENSION OF THE BERIT SUTURE ZONE TO EASTERNMOST TÜRKIYE (EAST OF LAKE VAN): EVIDENCE FROM AN UPPER CRETACEOUS INTRA-OCEANIC ARC, SUPRA-SUBDUCTION ZONE OPHIOLITES, AND PALAEOZOIC-CENOZOIC SEDIMENTARY SUCCESSIONS
abstract: This paper discusses and interprets the important but little studied eastward extension of the regionally important Berit Suture Zone that extends across eastern Türkiye into Iran (>500km). Fragmentary Upper Cretaceous ophiolites, oceanic island arc units and accretionary melange, east of Lake Van, are keys to an understanding of the Berit Suture Zone in this area. Field and geochemical evidence suggest that a dismembered ophiolite (Mehmetalan ophiolite) in the study area, mainly depleted mantle harzburgite, dunite and cumulate gabbro, formed in an Upper Cretaceous fore-arc setting. Cross-cutting alkaline diabase dykes in one of the ophiolite fragments hints at plume involvement. The volcanic arc, part of the regional Yüksekova Complex, is dominated by variably evolved tholeiitic, calc-alkaline and alkaline volcanics that erupted in an open-ocean setting, together with minor granodioritic intrusives. Intercalated pelagic carbonates are dated here as Campanian-Maastrichtian (locally late Maastrichtian) based on planktic foraminifera. The arc-related volcanics display two geochemical trends: one is typical of variably evolved basic-felsic oceanic arc volcanism; the other is alkaline and could represent escape of relatively enriched upper mantle through a slab rupture or alternatively plume involvement in the SSZ magmatism. A dismembered Palaeozoic-Mesozoic platform succession in the area can be correlated with the Malatya-Keban (Tauride) platform >300 km to the west. The deposition and deformation of the sedimentary cover units, of Late Palaeocene-Middle Eocene and also of Oligocene-Early Miocene age, help to constrain the timing of deformation. Three main phases of southward-directed compression, thrusting and consequent subaerial erosion are recognised: latest Cretaceous, Late Eocene and Mid-Late Miocene. This was followed by plateau uplift, strike-slip/transpression and westward ‘tectonic escape’. The proposed tectonic model correlates the various units east of Lake Van with the development of the Berit Ocean between the Malatya-Keban platform to the north and the Pütürge and Bitlis metamorphic units generally to the south. Differences, however, include the absence of exposed Bitlis continental crust to the south, the lack of significant Eocene volcanism, thrust emplacement farther south, and a more complex and variable deformation history. © 2027, Edizioni ETS. .

title: Role of a Pd cocatalyst on cuprite dendrites in selective electrochemical nitrate reduction to dinitrogen in a flow-through reactor
abstract: Electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO3RR) offers a promising route for removing nitrate from wastewater while controlling the distribution of nitrogen-containing products. Here, Pd-decorated cuprite dendrites were prepared by sequential electrodeposition and thermal annealing to promote selective nitrate conversion to N2. The dendritic Cu2O framework provided a high-surface-area support for Pd dispersion and abundant Pd-Cu interfacial sites. Among the compositions evaluated, Pd25Cu75 exhibited the best performance, achieving 96% N2 selectivity, 93% Faradaic efficiency, and 94% nitrate removal at −1.0 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) from an initial nitrate concentration of 100 mg-N L−1. Density functional theory calculations indicated that Pd substitution rendered the NO2-to-NO step less endergonic and stabilized adsorbed NOx intermediates through Pd-N interactions. A steady-state kinetic model further showed that Pd loading governs the competition between N-N coupling and sequential hydrogenation by regulating the conversion of surface intermediates. The Pd25Cu75 cathode also sustained nitrate removal from industrial wastewater in a flow-through electrolyzer while maintaining low metal leaching and stable N2 selectivity. These findings clarify the composition-dependent role of Pd in Cu2O-based NO3RR catalysts and demonstrate a practical electrode architecture for nitrate remediation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Ultrasonically modified coconut protein hydrogel-sunflower seed oil oleogel bigels: Effects of hydrogel/oleogel ratios on physicochemical properties and freeze-thaw stability
abstract: Bigels, integrating protein hydrogels and oleogels, have emerged as promising solid fat substitutes due to their tunable texture and nutritional profiles. However, their practical application in frozen foods is critically limited by structural degradation caused by ice crystallization and repeated freeze-thaw cycles. The central scientific question of this study is how the hydrogel-to-oleogel ratio modulates the interpenetrating network architecture and freeze-thaw resilience. To address this, we fabricated bigels using ultrasonically modified coconut protein isolate hydrogel (HG) and beeswax-structured sunflower seed oil oleogel (OG) at varying ratios, and benchmarked their performance against neat HG and neat OG. The optimal formulation H1O3 exhibited a 77.73% increase in hardness compared with either single component, alongside a superior water-holding capacity of 98.13% and enhanced rheological moduli. Crucially, after three freeze-thaw cycles, H1O3 retained approximately 50% of its initial hardness, whereas neat HG and neat OG suffered severe textural collapse. Microstructural (CLSM) and spectroscopic (XRD, FTIR) analyses confirmed that the H1O3 ratio fosters a densely entangled bicontinuous interpenetrating network without new chemical bonds, while differential scanning calorimetry revealed a melting peak at 30.37°C and an onset temperature of 63.72°C. Collectively, these results demonstrate that the synergistic interplay between ultrasonication-induced protein conformational flexibility and oleogel network density, governed by the Hydrogel and Oleogel ratio, dynamically redistributes water and oil phases to buffer freeze-thaw stress. Therefore, this study established a rational ratio-based design strategy for developing plant-based fat substitutes with strong structural integrity that can withstand freezing, which are expected to find applications in frozen desserts, plant-based meat products, and other frozen convenience foods that require stable texture during freeze-thaw cycles. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Weakly-C1 solutions to the biharmonic problem on multi-patch domains
abstract: Solving fourth-order problems typically requires C1-smooth splines. While straightforward on cuboidal patches, constructing these spaces on complex multi-patch geometries is challenging, often leading to complex and restrictive implementations, limitations on spline degrees, or reliance on constrained non-conforming approaches. This paper proposes an alternative method generalising Ainsworth and Parker (2024a). We decompose the biharmonic problem into three equivalent second-order problems, enabling a conforming discretisation using standard, easily constructed C0-smooth multi-patch splines. The discrete solution pair (wh, θh) directly approximates both the primary solution and its gradient. This approach provides several key advantages: • It accommodates curvilinear multi-patch geometries and allows spline spaces with degrees bi-quadratic or higher. • Standard C0 spaces allow for straightforward imposition of essential boundary conditions and even support local refinement for adaptivity. • It explicitly computes a C0-smooth, weakly curl-free gradient (θh), thus producing what we denote a “weakly-C1” solution. • The formulation avoids arbitrary tuning or penalty parameters while maintaining computational complexity comparable to the method from Ainsworth and Parker (2024a). • It permits general choices of inf-sup stable discrete spaces, but recovers exactly H2-conforming solutions if spaces forming a discrete Stokes’ complex are utilised. We establish the well-posedness of the discrete method and derive error estimates that demonstrate its optimal approximation properties. Numerical tests using multi-patch Taylor–Hood spline spaces confirm these advantages, comparing favourably against established H2-conforming and non-conforming constructions. © 2026 The Authors

title: Valley polarization boost enabled by interfacial exciton-magnon interaction in TMD/CrSBr antiferromagnetic heterostructures
abstract: Manipulating valley pseudospin in two-dimensional materials using antiferromagnetic proximity remains a significant challenge, as the zero net magnetization invalidates conventional magnetic proximity based on spin-polarized carrier hopping or effective magnetic field. Here, we overcome this limitation by harnessing a distinct mechanism, strong magnonic excitations in antiferromagnets, to achieve valley control without relying on net magnetization. We demonstrate a boost of valley polarization in MoSe2/CrSBr antiferromagnetic heterostructures enabled by the interfacial exciton-magnon interaction. This boost appears exclusively below the Néel temperature of CrSBr, directly correlating with antiferromagnetic order. Optical excitation and magnetic field dependence exclude the conventional mechanism of the magnetic proximity effect. We attribute this antiferromagnet-driven valley polarization boost to the interfacial scattering between photoexcited magnons in CrSBr and excitons in MoSe2, which effectively suppresses the exciton spin precession, thereby reducing the intrinsic electron-hole exchange interaction that dominates valley depolarization. Our work demonstrates interfacial exciton-magnon interaction as an effective approach for valley manipulation and bridges the gap in antiferromagnet-controlled valley degree of freedom. © 2026

title: A novel edible, all-biomass Pickering emulsion coating based on Lys/Alg composite nanoparticles for curcumin delivery and active fruit preservation
abstract: The integration of nano-encapsulation with edible coatings holds great potential for active fruit preservation. However, conventional emulsions often rely on chemical surfactants, posing safety risks and limited functionality. Here, we developed an edible, all-biomass-derived Pickering emulsion (CLAPE) coating stabilized by amphiphilic lysozyme/alginate composite nanoparticles (Lys/Alg). The Lys/Alg were fabricated through electrostatic self-assembly followed by Ca2+ cross-linking, forming a robust interfacial layer that effectively encapsulates curcumin (Cur). Molecular docking simulations revealed a strong binding affinity between Lys and Cur (binding energy: −87.2 kcal/mol), which significantly enhances the aqueous dispersibility and stability of Cur. The resulting Pickering emulsion enables sustained release of curcumin over 60 h, with a peak cumulative release of 94.0%, approximately twice that of the unencapsulated control. This release profile follows Fickian diffusion, extending the bioactive duration and increasing the total released amount, thereby enhancing curcumin's bioavailability. Moreover, CLAPE exhibits excellent thermal stability, maintaining high stability indices under varied accelerated storage conditions. It also exhibited high antioxidant (99.02%) and broad-spectrum antibacterial activity. Additionally, the application of CLAPE on strawberries, bananas and grapes has led to a doubling of their shelf life while maintaining the freshness and nutrient content of the fruits. The edible active preservative material, based entirely on biomass, not only forms a multifunctional protective coating that prevents spoilage but can also be easily washed off. This study presents an innovative strategy for the designs of active preservation materials utilizing all-natural plant-derived components. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Online transient stability assessment for AC/DC power systems based on clustering BCU and hybrid neural networks
abstract: The widespread integration of power electronic devices including renewable energy sources and Line Commutated converter (LCC)-based High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) poses significant challenges to the transient stability of AC/DC power grids. To realize the accurate and fast online transient stability assessment of AC/DC power systems, this paper firstly constructs terminal potential energy expressions through the integration of active power with respect to voltage phase angle and reactive power with respect to voltage magnitude. Subsequently, this paper proposes an online transient stability assessment method based on clustering Boundary of stability based Controlling Unstable-equilibrium-point (BCU) and hybrid neural networks to address the computational inefficiency issue of pure mechanism analytical approaches in critical energy determination. The clustering BCU method significantly reduces computational complexity when generating offline critical energy datasets by eliminating redundant calculations for different fault scenarios within the same coherent fault cluster. Besides, the convolutional neural networks-gate recurrent unit (CNN-GRU) based hybrid neural network is presented for real-time online transient stability assessment, which can quickly and accurately require the critical energy during system faults and compare it with the transient energy at fault clearing time to determine system stability. Compared with the multiple parallel CNN-GRU model, the proposed approach further provides physically interpretable indicators, including critical energy, critical clearing time, and stability margin, enabling more reliable evaluation of system stability boundaries. Finally, simulation results under different renewable penetration levels, transmission conditions, and fault scenarios demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high assessment accuracy, strong robustness, and improved computational efficiency for online transient stability assessment of renewable-integrated AC/DC hybrid power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Tight sandstone gas exploration potential of the Upper Triassic Baiguowan Formation in the Xichang Basin, SW China
abstract: The Xichang Basin, excluding the Sichuan Basin areas, is an important strategic replacement zone in Sichuan Province. Given the variability of continental oil and gas exploration conditions, the entire basin must be considered as the study area. The geological conditions of tight gas in the Baiguowan Formation were systematically analyzed using extensive core, logging, and field outcrop data to assess the exploration and development potential of continental Baiguowan Formation tight sandstone gas (hereafter referred to as tight gas) in the Xichang Basin. The results indicate that the Baiguowan Formation in the Xichang Basin can be vertically divided into three complete third-order sequences. (1) The channel sandstones deposited in low-stand system tracts of the first and second third-order sequences contain thick, laterally continuous sand bodies with well-developed joints and fissures, forming excellent reservoirs for tight gas accumulation. (2) The tight gas of the Baiguowan Formation in the Xichang Basin is mainly concentrated in the Bai 1 and Bai 2 Members, which exhibit favorable hydrocarbon source conditions, moderate thermal evolution, high hydrocarbon generation intensity, broad reservoir distribution, excellent reservoir properties, favorable early structural settings, and vertically stacked multilayer gas storage. (3) The Baiguowan Formation experienced rapid burial and subsequent denudation, and the tight gas reservoirs underwent two hydrocarbon charging events followed by two accumulation periods, showing a characteristic pattern of accumulation controlled by source, structure, and sedimentary facies. (4) Based on the source rock quality, reservoir type, and hydrocarbon generation intensity, the Jiatie–Sikai zone is identified as the most favorable exploration area, covering 1860 km2 with a tight gas resource of 6756 × 108 m3. Further investigations should focus on five promising tight gas sweet spot areas: Southern Zhaojue, Northern Zhaojue, Lieridi, Tiejia, and Sikai. © 2026 The Authors. title: Comparative structuring of goat, yak, and camel casein isolates in moldable emulsions via calcium-mediated association, TGase crosslinking, and ultrasound-assisted emulsification
abstract: Acid-isolated caseins from goat, yak, and camel milk were compared within a common processing framework to evaluate differences in the structuring of moldable oil-in-water emulsions among the three casein sources. Casein preparations were subjected to sequential calcium-mediated association and microbial transglutaminase (TGase) crosslinking, followed by ultrasound-assisted emulsification at an oil-to-aqueous-phase volume ratio of 2:1. Calcium source, Ca2+ concentration, TGase activity, redispersed casein concentration, sonication duration, and ultrasound set power were screened in independent one-factor series. Processing responses were generally nonlinear and differed markedly among the three casein sources. Within the tested formulation space, CaCl2 supplying 5 mmol/L Ca2+, 3% (w/v) redispersed treated casein, and an ultrasound set power of 2.0 kW provided the most consistent overall balance of oil incorporation, macroscopic homogeneity, physical stability, low apparent flowability, and moldability. The selected TGase activities were 4, 8, and 4 U/g casein for goat, yak, and camel caseins, respectively, with corresponding sonication durations of 15, 15, and 10 s. Maximum apparent viscosity did not consistently predict the selected formulation: low-shear viscosity reached approximately 240 Pa s for goat casein and approximately 300 Pa s for camel casein under intermediate treatment conditions, whereas higher treatment levels could markedly increase instability, with TSI values exceeding 20 in the camel system. Confocal microscopy further showed a comparatively fine and densely interspersed goat emulsion, large incompletely dispersed casein-rich aqueous domains in the shape-retaining yak emulsion, and a broader heterogeneous domain-size distribution in the camel emulsion. These findings demonstrate that macroscopic moldability can emerge through different multiscale structural pathways and does not necessarily imply microscopically uniform emulsification or elastic gel formation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Sulfone-bridged connectivity modulation induces favorable spatial configuration and electronic structure in polymer photocatalysts for enhanced overall H2O2 production
abstract: Insufficient charge separation efficiency and sluggish two-electron water oxidation kinetics are the primary limitations for photocatalytic H2O2 production over polymer photocatalysts. Herein, we proposed an innovative connectivity engineering approach for functional groups to tackle these drawbacks. Specially, we developed two polymer photocatalysts with distinct sulfone group connectivity configurations, namely sulfone-bridged Tp-DASO-B and sulfone-fused Tp-DPSO-F. In situ characterizations and theoretical calculations revealed that the sulfone-bridged configuration in Tp-DASO-B introduced a non-coplanar twist and modulated the electron delocalization. This structural feature enhanced exciton dissociation and increased the spatial distance between holes and electrons, thereby promoting charge separation and transfer. Meanwhile, the strong electron-withdrawing effect of the sulfone group in Tp-DASO-B activated the water oxidation sites on adjacent benzene rings, enhancing the adsorption and activation of water molecules and significantly promoting two-electron water oxidation. Consequently, Tp-DASO-B achieved a markedly improved photocatalytic H2O2 production rate of 9.36 mmol g−1 h−1 in pure water, which was 3.84 times higher than that of Tp-DPSO-F and exceeded the performance of most reported photocatalysts. Furthermore, multiple evaluations including long-term accumulation, cyclic stability, complex water systems, outdoor scale-up experiments and continuous-flow measurements, further verified the excellent activity, stability and durability of Tp-DASO-B. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Photoswitchable pollutant adsorption regulates spin electron transport channels to reversibly switch radical and nonradical peroxymonosulfate oxidation pathways
abstract: Heterogeneous photo-Fenton-like systems for oxidative degradation of organic pollutants represent a promising sustainable technology for wastewater remediation. However, precisely regulating oxidation pathways to tolerate complex water matrices while maintaining high-efficiency treatment performance remains a critical challenge. Herein, a confined heterojunction was developed to achieve light-responsive switching between radical and electron transfer pathway (ETP)-dominated nonradical PMS activation through reversible control of pollutant adsorption and desorption. Integrated experimental investigations and in situ characterizations revealed that spatial confinement promoted pollutant enrichment and interfacial electron transfer, facilitating the formation of ETP-dominated oxidation under dark conditions. Upon visible-light irradiation, photoinduced electronic redistribution weakened pollutant–catalyst interactions and triggered pollutant desorption, thereby disrupting the ETP route and promoting PMS activation through photoinduced metal redox cycling toward O2•―-mediated radical oxidation. The resulting system exhibited robust degradation performance and operational stability, maintaining over 90% pollutant removal after 900 min of continuous-flow treatment in practical water matrices. This study provides a photo-responsive strategy for dynamically regulating PMS oxidation pathways and reveals the critical role of interfacial adsorption and electron-transfer regulation in selective nonradical oxidation. © 2026

title: Vulnerability-aware reinforcement learning scheduling of AI data centers under typhoon-induced thermal coupling
abstract: The rapid growth of AI data-center loads, amplified by typhoon-induced thermal coupling between workloads and cooling systems, poses new challenges to transmission grid vulnerability assessment and scheduling. This paper develops a vulnerability-aware reinforcement-learning (RL) scheduling framework that integrates a measured-data-driven AI load model, a typhoon-day temperature–PUE–cooling model, a seven-indicator vulnerability assessment covering physical, structural, and AI-specific dimensions, and RL scheduling via PPO, SAC, and TD3 with a PTDF-based top-K branch-selection mechanism that confines control to AI-responsive branches. Validation on the IEEE 39-bus and 118-bus systems shows that all three RL algorithms achieve statistically significant VDC reductions of 6.9–9.3% (p < .001), with PPO outperforming an LP comparator by 3.4–8.4% on the 118- and 1354-bus systems. The reduction magnitude correlates with the vulnerability-gradient signal—the product of mean PTDF sensitivity and baseline vulnerability—rather than with system size per se: on the PEGASE 1354-bus system, where the AI load represents only 0.016% of total system demand and the transmission network is highly robust, no scheduling strategy produces a meaningful VDC response, confirming a physical optimization ceiling governed by AI load penetration rather than network size. Under extreme stress at 3.0 × AI load, TD3 reduces EENS by 44%, confirming VDC as a proactive leading indicator of curtailment risk. An ablation study identifies topological sensitivity as the most influential indicator. The proposed framework provides grid operators with ex-ante guidance on when vulnerability-aware scheduling becomes effective, based on the relationship between AI load penetration, vulnerability gradients, and system controllability. © 2026

title: The π-orbital axis vector-gated peroxymonosulfate activation: Switching from O-O bond cleavage to nonradical pathway
abstract: Although peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation is commonly divided into radical and nonradical routes, controllably switching between these pathways by catalyst design remains challenging. Here, we show that surface curvature, quantified by π-orbital axis vector (POAV) analysis, can regulate PMS activation in a Co-cluster/Mn-N₄ porous carbon catalyst. With polystyrene spheres as sacrificial templates, Co clusters and Mn-N₄ single-atom sites are anchored on a curved N-doped carbon framework. POAV analysis shows that increasing curvature enhances local carbon pyramidalization and π-σ rehybridization, which in turn modulates the local ligand field and d-orbital splitting of the metal sites during the PMS adsorption and activation. This geometry-driven electronic regulation changes the role of the two metal centers: planar carbon favors PMS adsorption and O-O bond cleavage at Co-clusters, leading to radical generation, whereas curved carbon shifts PMS activation to Mn-N₄ sites as PMS*, and promotes nonradical electron transfer. Beyond pathway control, the 3D curved porous framework also improves solar absorption and heat confinement, enabling photo-accelerated oxidation and interfacial evaporation. These findings reveal POAV is a key parameter for realizing tunable catalytic activation in carbon-framework geometry. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
