title: A two-layer degradation-aware energy management framework for renewable power grids with battery and hydrogen storage
abstract: High renewable energy penetration supports sustainable power generation; however, intermittency, component aging, and long-term performance uncertainty may pose operational challenges for power systems. This study proposes a degradation-aware, two-layer framework that jointly evaluates short-term system operation and long-term component performance. In the first layer, the Tunicate Swarm Algorithm (TSA) determines system capacities and energy-sharing parameters for a 24-h period. An objective function includes operating costs, emissions costs, BESS costs, hydrogen system costs, demand response, and renewable energy curtailment. In the second layer, the optimized system and energy management strategy (EMS) parameters are transferred without re-optimization to a 365-day simulation under variable renewable generation and load. BESS energy/SOH, hydrogen inventory, PEM electrolyzer degradation, and PEM fuel-cell efficiency are updated continuously. The novelty lies in directly testing the long-term operational robustness of short-term optimized system and EMS decisions within a continuous annual power-balance model. Selected load and conventional generation data from the IEEE 24-bus RTS are used as reference inputs. At the same time, the RES capacities, BESS configuration, DRP parameters, and P2H–H₂ storage–PEMFC system are defined and adapted specifically for the present study. The results show that the BESS state of health decreases from approximately 1.00 to 0.9785 (yearly), while the average PEM electrolyzer effective conversion coefficient decreases from approximately 0.649 to 0.62. The integrated BESS and hydrogen storage structure also supports renewable power balancing under variable operating conditions. Thus, the proposed framework shows the long-term technical effects of short-term energy-management decisions in renewable power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Simulation-based deep learning for lightning localization using convolutional autoencoder and multilayer perceptron
abstract: Lightning-induced overvoltages are a major cause of faults and outages in overhead transmission systems, significantly affecting the reliability and operational continuity of power networks. Accurate and timely localization of lightning strikes is therefore essential for improving system monitoring, fault diagnosis, and post-event analysis. In this paper, a simulation-based data-driven approach for two-dimensional lightning localization is proposed using voltage signals induced on transmission lines and evaluated at limited sensor locations. The method combines a convolutional autoencoder (CAE) for feature extraction with a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for regression, forming a hybrid deep learning architecture (CAE-MLP) tailored to the nonlinear nature of the localization problem. The framework uses Rusck's analytical formulation to generate waveforms for six line configurations, enabling assessment of topology effects on localization accuracy. No field-measured transmission-line records were used. Compared with CNN, LSTM, and standalone MLP, CAE-MLP achieves the lowest coordinate RMSE in 10 of 12 configuration/axis cases. Across six configurations, its RMSE ranges from 121 to 758 m in the x-coordinate and from 123 to 610 m in the y-coordinate; median two-dimensional error ranges from 150 to 427 m. The results demonstrate in-distribution feasibility using two sensor waveforms under assumptions of an infinite, lossless, single-conductor line above perfectly conducting ground. Archived SNR tests indicate lower sensitivity than comparison models over 5–40 dB. However, because training and testing data were generated by the same idealized model, the results do not establish practical deployment readiness. Validation with measured records or an independent, higher-fidelity electromagnetic model remains necessary. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Convergence analysis of the randomized Kaczmarz method with anchoring hyperplanes
abstract: We propose an improved randomized Kaczmarz method, named the randomized Kaczmarz method with anchoring hyperplanes (RKM-AH), for solving large systems of linear equations. Our method originates from a variance reduction idea: choosing one or several hyperplanes, called anchoring hyperplanes, and forcing the iterative sequence generated by the method to belong to these hyperplanes through projections, thereby reducing the oscillation amplitude of the iterative sequence and accelerating the convergence rate. To the best of our knowledge, the convergence rate estimation of our method is better than those of the randomized Kaczmarz method and existing related methods. In addition, to further reduce the computational workload, we also present a dual version of the randomized Kaczmarz method with anchoring hyperplanes (D-RKM-AH). Numerical experiments are also provided to show advantages and outperformance of our method over the randomized Kaczmarz method and existing related methods. Specifically, D-RKM-AH exhibits more excellent numerical performance in most cases. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Next Generation Intelligent Transportation through Disaster Aware Privacy Preserving Federated Learning
abstract: The growing challenges posed by rapid urbanization and increased vehicle density have highlighted the need for precise and privacy-preserving traffic flow prediction models. Traditional centralized learning methods involve aggregating privacy-sensitive traffic flow data, which poses severe privacy, scalability, and governance issues. To overcome these issues, this paper presents a disaster-aware privacy-preserving federated learning (PP-FL) solution for multi-city traffic flow prediction in heterogeneous and non-IID data settings. Each city separately trains a local deep learning model using local traffic, environmental, and disaster-related data, while only privacy-protected model updates are exchanged with a central aggregator. The proposed solution leverages secure aggregation and differential privacy to ensure data privacy and facilitate efficient cross-city knowledge sharing. Extensive experiments on multi-modal urban traffic datasets, including junction-level surveillance traffic data, highway traffic time-series data, and disaster-influenced traffic data, validate that the proposed solution outperforms state-of-the-art centralized and federated learning baselines by up to 8-12% in RMSE error while substantially mitigating privacy leakage. The results also validate enhanced anomaly detection and disaster-caused traffic disruption prediction performance across cities with limited local traffic data. The obtained results validate the effectiveness of the proposed PP-FL framework as a scalable, secure, and efficient paradigm for next-generation intelligent transportation systems. © 2027 The author(s). title: Amino-vacancy dual-site engineering in Ru-incorporated nickel hydroxide for ampere-level alkaline hydrogen evolution
abstract: The sluggish Volmer step of the Ru-based catalysts remains a persistent major kinetic bottleneck for ampere-level alkaline water electrolysis. To mitigate this limitation, we developed a strategy to regulate both the local electronic structure and the interfacial water microenvironment. A self-supported Ru-incorporated Fe-doped nickel hydroxide skeleton was successfully grown on the nickel foam substrate. Subsequent NH3/Ar plasma treatment introduced NHx-related surface species and oxygen vacancies, creating a highly synergistic dual-site microenvironment on NRNFOH/NF. In situ ATR-FTIR shows that NHx-related species reorganize the interfacial water network to facilitate activation, while complementary evidence from quantitative EPR analysis, O 1 s XPS, and oxidative oxygen-vacancy healing supports vacancy formation; Ni/Fe/Ru core-level XPS shifts combined with DFT calculations reveal vacancy-induced electronic modulation of metal centers that optimizes intermediate adsorption. NRNFOH/NF delivers 1000 mA cm−2 at an iR-corrected overpotential of 124 mV in 1.0 M KOH, maintaining outstanding catalytic stability for 500 h. Integrated into an anion-exchange membrane water electrolyzer, this device achieves 1.81 V at 1000 mA cm−2 while outperforming the commercial Pt/C/CP ||IrO2/CP benchmark and maintaining stable operation for 1000 h at 60 °C. This work presents a dual-site engineering route for durable ampere-level hydrogen production under application-relevant alkaline conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Defect dipole engineering induced by Cobalt(II) doping enables ultralow dielectric loss in Zn2SiO4 ceramics
abstract: Tunnel-structured zinc orthosilicate (Zn2SiO4) is a promising low-loss dielectric ceramic, yet further suppression of dielectric dissipation requires effective regulation of its local defect structure. Herein, pristine Zn2SiO4 and Ni2+, Co2+, and Mn2+ singly doped ceramics are prepared from chemically homogeneous precursors obtained by solvent evaporation. This synthesis route promotes uniform transition-metal incorporation at Zn lattice sites and enables controlled perturbation of the tetrahedral framework. Although Ni, Co, and Mn substitution all induce lattice distortion and defect formation, their dielectric effects are markedly different. In contrast to Ni and Mn, which introduce additional relaxation loss, Co selectively lowers dielectric dissipation. The Co-doped ceramic exhibits an ultralow tanδ of 7.3 × 10−5 at 1 MHz with an εr of 9.2 at room temperature, nearly one order of magnitude lower than that of pristine Zn2SiO4. Electron paramagnetic resonance, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations suggest that tetrahedrally coordinated Co2+ may enhance localized electron trapping and stabilize oxygen-vacancy-related defect complexes. These localized defect centers may suppress long-range carrier migration and weaken Maxwell-Wagner interfacial polarization, thereby reducing dielectric loss while maintaining a relatively high dielectric constant. This work establishes dopant-stabilized defect localization as an effective strategy for designing ultralow-loss silicate dielectric ceramics. © 2026

title: Complex-impedance features for transformer winding-fault diagnosis: Finite-element classification with laboratory frequency-response corroboration
abstract: Automated interpretation of transformer frequency-response analysis (FRA) often retains impedance magnitude but discards signed real and imaginary components. This study evaluates complex (R, X) features for five-class winding-fault classification and fault-specific severity estimation. A finite-element model supplies network parameters for 210 labelled cases, and a state-space solution supplies the complex frequency response. Evaluation uses repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation (20 repeats) with one common healthy reference and fold-local preprocessing. Relative to magnitude-only features, complex frequency-domain features increase LightGBM accuracy from 93.57 % to 94.95 % (+1.38 percentage points, paired p=0.0012). Adding descriptors of the inverse-transformed spectrum changes accuracy to 95.10 % (+0.14 points, p=0.356), confirming that these descriptors are only a re-encoding of the same spectrum. A stacked ensemble reaches 95.45 % accuracy and 94.87 % macro-F1, compared with 95.93 % and 95.52 % for XGBoost; the difference is unresolved (p=0.169), so no superiority is claimed. Laboratory impedance sweeps from one disc-winding specimen corroborate the directions of inductance and anti-resonance changes for controlled axial, disc-space, radial and short-circuit interventions. They also reveal a low-frequency resistance-resolution floor and the absence of decay structure in the inverse-transformed response. A public converter-transformer magnitude–phase record additionally confirms that signed R and X inputs can be reconstructed from an in-service measurement. Because the measured set contains only one healthy sweep and ten retained deformations, it tests physical premises but does not externally validate the classifier. The reported predictive performance therefore remains specific to the simulated dataset. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A multi-branch arc fault detection method based on time-frequency feature fusion and random forest
abstract: With the rising global demand for electrical energy, ensuring power system operational reliability has become critically important. In this background, electrical fire prevention, particularly arc fault detection, has gained significant attention. However, in complex multi-branch load networks, coupling interference between different branches results in unacceptably high false alarm rates in conventional detection methods. To address this problem, this study proposes an arc fault detection method based on multi-branch time-frequency feature fusion and random forest (RF). First, a multi-branch arc simulation experimental platform is designed to acquire original current waveform datasets. Time-frequency features are subsequently extracted and fused of all branches. An RF-based detection framework is then developed to identify the fused feature. On this base, evaluation of different feature fusion strategies is conducted to determine the optimal strategy. Finally, experiments validate that the proposed detection framework achieves a 99.89% detection accuracy and a 0.0106‰ false alarm rate. When deployed on embedded systems, the framework achieves a response latency within 20 ms while maintaining 100% fault detection accuracy within 80 ms, confirming its hardware implementation feasibility. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Effect of Y addition on microstructure, tensile properties, and corrosion behavior of high-speed-extruded Mg–5Bi–3Al alloy
abstract: This study investigates the effect of Y addition on the microstructure, tensile properties, and corrosion behavior of high-speed-extruded Mg–5Bi–3Al (BA53) alloy. Y-free BA53 and Y-containing BAW53 x alloys ( x = 0.2, 0.5, and 1.0 wt.%) are extruded at a die-exit speed of 67 m/min, and the role of Y is examined with emphasis on second-phase evolution and its influence on mechanical and corrosion behavior. Y addition progressively changes the second-phase characteristics from fine intragranular Mg3Bi2 particles to coarse BiY particles concentrated mainly along grain boundaries, while distinct grain refinement appears only at the highest Y content. The tensile yield strength and ultimate tensile strength decrease slightly with increasing Y content, whereas tensile elongation remains comparable and increases slightly at 0.2 wt.% Y. The strength reduction is mainly associated with the reduced strengthening contribution of fine Mg3Bi2 particles. Longitudinal-section observations near the fracture surface show that coarse BiY particles do not act as dominant crack-initiation sites; instead, fracture remains governed mainly by twin-related cracking, which accounts for the limited change in tensile ductility despite the marked change in second-phase characteristics. The corrosion behavior shows a strongly non-monotonic dependence on Y content. A minor addition of 0.2 wt.% Y markedly improves corrosion resistance, whereas larger additions lead to severe deterioration. The Volta potential difference between BiY and the α -Mg matrix is substantially larger than that between Mg3Bi2 and the α -Mg matrix, indicating a stronger local galvanic driving force. Early-stage and cross-sectional corrosion observations further show that BA53 is more susceptible to widespread Mg3Bi2-assisted corrosion initiation, whereas high-Y alloys increasingly develop BiY-assisted localized corrosion, corrosion-front propagation along grain-boundary regions, and corrosion-film instability. These results demonstrate that a minor addition of 0.2 wt.% Y provides a favorable combination of high-speed extrudability, strength–ductility balance, and enhanced corrosion resistance in the present BA53-based alloy system. title: MDG-Mamba: Evolution-aware selective state-space modeling with macro-micro decoupling for non-stationary photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for the reliable integration of solar energy into modern power grids. However, the strong non-stationarity and rapid fluctuations of PV outputs caused by changing weather conditions make it challenging for existing methods to capture abrupt power transitions. To address this challenge, this paper proposes MDG-Mamba, a gradient-enhanced macro-micro decoupled framework built upon the Mamba architecture. The model incorporates gradient-based temporal evolution enhancement to characterize first-order variations in PV generation and employs macro-micro temporal decoupling to separate long-term trends from high-frequency fluctuations. A multi-frequency refinement mechanism is further introduced to preserve local fluctuation characteristics while enabling efficient long-range dependency modeling. Experiments on four heterogeneous real-world PV datasets show that MDG-Mamba consistently outperforms competitive baselines, with an average MAE reduction of approximately 8.5%. In ramp-event evaluations on the LSP-PV dataset, MDG-Mamba achieves an MAE of 0.241 under ramp-only conditions, outperforming representative baselines and demonstrating superior capability in tracking abrupt PV power transitions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Reduction-induced non-monotonic Cu redispersion on hydroxyapatite creates functionally differentiated interfaces for furfural hydrogenation
abstract: Constructing non-noble-metal hydrogenation catalysts with high activity, chemoselectivity, and durability under mild conditions is a key challenge in biomass valorization. While strong metal–support interactions on hydroxyapatite (HAP) typically involve noble metals via oxidative pathways, we report a reduction-induced interfacial reconstruction for Cu-HAP. During temperature-programmed reduction, Cu shows non-monotonic evolution: aggregation then redispersion into an anchored state at 600 °C, bypassing sintering. Spectroscopic and DFT reveal that HAP retains long-range order, while the Cu–HAP boundary stabilizes Cu0/Cu+ and HPO42-, enabling cooperative H2 dissociation and carbonyl polarization. The optimized catalyst achieves quantitative furfural conversion with > 99% furfuryl alcohol selectivity (80 °C, 1.5 MPa H2). Kinetic benefits include decreased Ea (88.1→69.3 kJ/mol) and shifted H2 order (1.20→0.25). The catalyst also maintains stable performance over five cycles with negligible leaching. These findings highlight the distinctive role of HAP's Ca–PO4–OH environment in reduction-induced Cu redistribution and interfacial reconstruction, providing new insights into the design of cooperative metal–support interfaces for selective hydrogenation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A single-ended fault location method based on active boundary control for multi-terminal flexible DC grids
abstract: In modular multilevel converter (MMC)-based multi-terminal flexible DC (MTDC) grids, fault current limiting suppresses post-fault electrical transients and weakens available fault characteristics, thereby reducing the sensitivity and reliability of conventional fault location methods. To address this issue, this paper proposes a single-ended fault location method based on active control and boundary self-validation. First, a coordinated MMC control framework integrating fault current limiting and characteristic-frequency signal injection is developed to construct controllable electrical features after fault occurrence. Then, an active boundary control strategy is proposed at the converter where fault model selection is required. By coordinating with a local directional criterion, different terminal responses are constructed for different fault regions, enabling invalid location results caused by incorrect fault model selection to be rejected. On this basis, frequency-domain fault location models are established for both pole-to-ground (PTG) and pole-to-pole (PTP) faults, with detailed discussion on parameter selection. The fault distance and transition resistance are identified through multi-frequency residual minimization, after which the relative residual variation is used to validate the location result and determine the final fault distance. Simulation results on a three terminal flexible DC system demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately locate PTG and PTP faults on different line sections under various fault distances and transition resistances, with fault location errors below 1%. The proposed method enables single-ended fault location without inter-station communication and can potentially serve as a backup protection function, thereby facilitating faster post-fault restoration in MTDC grids. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Closed-loop robotic polishing cell with toolpath orchestration for mid-spatial frequency error suppression
abstract: Mid-spatial-frequency (MSF) errors induced by repetitive toolpaths remain a major limitation in robotic polishing of precision optical surfaces. This study proposes a closed-loop robotic polishing cell with toolpath orchestration that integrates surface metrology, removal-function management, a parameterized toolpath library, path-based material-removal prediction, and multistage robotic execution. The proposed approach replaces isolated single-path optimization with stage-specific coordination of complementary trajectories. A NURBS-interpolated Gosper path is incorporated as a functional toolpath within the proposed framework, where the space-filling characteristics of the Gosper curve provide multidirectional coverage and NURBS interpolation improves trajectory continuity for MSF-error suppression. Numerical verification and two sets of polishing experiments were conducted on aspheric optical components. In the representative Hilbert–NURBS-interpolated Gosper strategy, the Hilbert path provided efficient baseline correction, whereas the proposed path further suppressed residual periodic textures. Numerical results reduced PV/RMS from 403.216/70.968 nm to 146.891/18.255 nm, corresponding to reductions of 63.6% and 74.3%, respectively. Experimental PSD analysis showed that this coordinated strategy produced the lowest final PSD value among the three tested configurations, with an overall convergence rate of 86.849% at the characteristic MSF wavelength. Additional experiments comparing spiral–NURBS-interpolated Gosper and NURBS-interpolated Gosper–pseudo-random sequences provided further experimental evidence for the effectiveness of toolpath coordination under the tested conditions. The former achieved PSD convergence rates of 99.99%, 99.96%, and 99.02% at characteristic wavelengths of 4, 2.5, and 1.28 mm, respectively, and produced the lowest final spectral levels. These results demonstrate that coordinated use of complementary paths can simultaneously improve form convergence, suppress characteristic MSF peaks, and enhance residual-surface uniformity, providing a framework for integrating metrology, toolpath planning, and robotic precision finishing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Molecular characterization and nonlinear rheology of native and carboxymethylated carrageenans
abstract: Carrageenans are important marine polysaccharides extracted from red algae and are widely used for their ability to form ion-induced hydrogels. In food and pharmaceutical applications, these hydrogels are often subjected to large-amplitude, rapid shear deformations, making the study of their nonlinear rheological responses highly relevant. Herein, carboxymethyl derivatives with varying degrees of substitution (DS) were prepared from κ-, ι-, and λ-carrageenans. Structural characterization using FT-IR, NMR, elemental analysis, and gel permeation chromatography confirmed successful carboxymethylation, accompanied by partial desulfation and changes in molecular weight. Steady and dynamic shear tests revealed shear-thinning behavior in the solutions; carboxymethylation converted the original gel-like response to a more liquid-like viscoelasticity by altering chain conformation and electrostatic interactions. Large amplitude oscillatory shear (LAOS), combined with Fourier-transform and Chebyshev analyses, showed that κ-carrageenan gels exhibit weak strain overshoot and a narrow linear viscoelastic region, whereas ι-carrageenan and most carboxymethylated derivatives display strong strain overshoot and a broader linear region. Notably, increasing DS progressively enhances resistance to nonlinear deformation. These findings elucidate transient network dynamics and establish a structure–rheology relationship for carboxymethylated carrageenans, guiding the design of soft, tough hydrogels for food and biomedical applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Cu/Ni co-doping enhances solar-driven CO2-to-CH4 conversion in M. barkeri-g-C3N4 biohybrids
abstract: The solar-driven conversion of CO2 into CH4 offers an effective route for carbon utilization and production of value-added fuels. Here, a semiconductor-microbe biohybrid was reported for efficient light-driven CO2-to-CH4 conversion. CuNi co-doped graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) was used as semiconductor to construct biohybrids with Methanosarcina barkeri (M. barkeri). The CuNi-g-C3N4 self-assembles with M. barkeri via electrostatic interactions, which enhances visible-light absorption, charge separation, and interfacial electron transfer. This biohybrid achieves a CH4 yield of 957.05 μmol·gcat−1 with nearly 100% CH4 selectivity, a 6.54-fold increase compared to the pristine g-C3N4 counterpart. Density functional theory calculations reveal that CuNi co-doping modulates the electronic structure of g-C3N4 and optimize CO2 activation and reaction selectivity. Transcriptomic analysis confirmed upregulation of methanogenesis genes and electron/proton transfer pathways. This work demonstrates a robust and sustainable approach for solar-driven CO2 utilization, highlighting the critical role of Cu/Ni co-doping in promoting electron utilization in the semiconductor-microbe biohybrid. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Effects of Balangu seed mucilage and plant proteins on the rheological and structural properties of gluten-free bread: A mixture design approach
abstract: The absence of gluten weakens the structure of gluten-free bread systems, resulting in poor batter stability, limited gas retention, and reduced crumb porosity. To overcome these limitations, plant proteins and hydrocolloids are commonly incorporated to restore viscoelastic properties. In this regard, batter rheology plays a critical role in regulating gas-cell stability during fermentation and baking, thereby determining the final crumb structure and bread quality. This study used a mixture design to evaluate the effects of two protein isolates (soy protein isolate, SPI; faba bean protein isolate, FPI) and two hydrocolloids (carboxymethyl cellulose, CMC; Balangu seed mucilage, BSM) on the rheological properties of gluten-free batters and bread quality. The aim was to compare SPI and FPI and assess the performance of BSM relative to CMC, considering both individual and interactive effects. Results showed that batter viscoelastic behavior was strongly affected by both protein source and hydrocolloid type. BSM enhanced structural strength and stability more effectively than CMC, indicating a greater ability to promote network formation in the batter matrix. Appropriate protein–hydrocolloid combinations improved gas-cell stability and crumb porosity, whereas excessive hydrocolloid levels produced overly rigid matrices that restricted expansion. Optimization using a desirability function identified an optimal formulation (SPI 0.897%, FPI 3.60%, CMC 0.00%, BSM 0.498%), yielding bread with a specific volume of 4.37 mL/g and porosity of 31.5%. Overall, the results highlight the potential of BSM as a bio-based alternative to CMC and demonstrate the importance of optimizing protein–hydrocolloid ratios to improve gluten-free bread structure. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: CO2 storage suitability, capacity, and emission-reduction implications of oil and gas reservoirs in the Shaanxi sector of the Ordos Basin, China
abstract: Geological storage of CO2 offers a viable means of reducing large-scale carbon emissions, thereby contributing to the mitigation of global climate and environmental challenges associated with CO2 emissions. This study evaluates candidate oil and gas reservoirs in the Shaanxi sector of the Ordos Basin using an Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation framework and estimates CO2 storage capacity with the US-DOE volumetric method. The results show that Hengshan Oilfield has the highest overall suitability for CO2 sequestration, whereas Jinghe Oilfield has the largest effective storage capacity. The total effective storage capacity of the screened reservoirs is estimated at 1.02 × 109 t CO2, Meanwhile, total CO2 emissions in Shaanxi Province increased from 308.25 Mt in 2010 to 601.25 Mt in 2022, with fossil fuel combustion contributing more than 94% of total emissions and with higher emissions concentrated in northern Shaanxi and Guanzhong region. The CO2 injected into oil and gas reservoirs, if employed for enhanced oil recovery, is projected to produce 1.02∼6.12 × 108 t of crude oil, translating to economic returns of 50 billion USD. This study provides a reference for achieving carbon neutrality in Shaanxi Province and advancing low-carbon development in the Ordos Basin. © 2026 The Authors. title: Enabling metal-free photocatalytic self-Fenton mineralization of refractory pollutants via a quinone/hydroquinone redox cycle
abstract: Photocatalytic self-Fenton catalysts synergistically remove organic pollutants by coupling photosynthesis of H2O2 with the Fenton reaction. However, metal-based self-Fenton systems inevitably generate secondary pollution associated with transition metal sludge disposal. Here, we rationally designed a metal-free graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) catalyst covalently grafted with tetrahydroxy-1,4-benzoquinone (THQ) to construct an efficient, sustainable photocatalytic self-Fenton system. The integrated THQ not only enhances the visible-light harvesting and directional separation of photogenerated carriers of g-C3N4, but also serves as a dual-functional active center. Specifically, THQ is proposed to facilitate the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e- ORR) for in-situ H2O2 generation and subsequently promote the activation of the generated H2O2 into highly reactive hydroxyl radicals (•OH) through its quinone/hydroquinone (Q/QH2) redox cycle. Consequently, the THQ/g-C3N4 composite exhibits exceptional catalytic performance, achieving a 4.98-fold enhancement in the degradation rate constant of ciprofloxacin (CIP) within 2 h compared to pristine g-C3N4. Furthermore, the catalyst demonstrates remarkable practical applicability, achieving a 50 % total organic carbon (TOC) removal efficiency in Chinese Baijiu distillery wastewater within 5 h. This study establishes metal-free, photocatalytic self-Fenton catalysis as a promising strategy for sustainable environmental remediation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Coordination and K-induced electronic effects promote efficient COS hydrolysis over K-Nd/Al2O3 catalysts
abstract: The development of efficient alumina-based catalysts for carbonyl sulfide (COS) hydrolysis remains a significant challenge, as their application in real blast furnace gas is largely hindered by insufficient activity and poor long-term durability. Here, K-Nd/Al2O3 maintains nearly complete COS conversion for 20 h at 120 °C and achieves a cumulative COS conversion capacity of 1.46 g/g under a simplified H2S/O2-containing atmosphere. Comprehensive characterization reveals that K-Nd co-modulation tailors acid-base site distribution, preserving active sites. Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM and XAFS analyses confirm that Nd is predominantly atomically dispersed, existing as isolated, low-coordinated Nd-Ox single-sites. During reaction, the Nd-O coordination number increases from 4.2 to 8.0 without aggregation, demonstrating reaction-induced reconstruction of the first coordination shell. Surface characterization, in-situ DRIFTS, and DFT calculations further show that K enhances surface electron density and fine-tunes Nd Lewis acidity, promoting H2O dissociation and nucleophilic *OH attack on COS, stabilizing *HOCOS and *HSCOO intermediates while facilitating H2S desorption. The synergy between Nd-Ox centers and K-induced electronic regulation reconcile durable COS hydrolysis under harsh conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Facet-dependent cobalt leaching governs structural reconstruction of spinel cobalt oxides in polysulfide electrocatalysis
abstract: Electrocatalysts are pivotal in surmounting the intrinsically sluggish kinetics of sulfur redox reaction (SRR) in lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries. However, improving the electrocatalytic efficiency remains a formidable challenge due to the insufficient understanding of surface dynamics of electrocatalysts, necessitating atomic-scale insights into the structural evolution under working condition. By deciphering the critical interfacial structures and dynamics of Co3O4 across distinct facets, this work demonstrates that the facet-dependent electrocatalytic efficacy of Co3O4 is intrinsically governed by site-specific Co leaching and the consequently reconstructed oxysulfide shell during SRR. Combined with spatiotemporal in-situ characterizations and theoretical calculations, we reveal that the leached Co ions primarily originate from tetrahedral (Td) sites characterized by weaker Co–O covalency, whereas the octahedral (Oh) sites exhibit remarkable stability owing to the robust Co–O bonding strength. Accordingly, the Co3+Oh-terminated (100) facet undergoes a surface-exclusive reconstruction upon cycling, yielding superior electrocatalytic performance and practical potential for Li–S batteries. Conversely, the Co2+Td-terminated (111) facet suffers from rapid deactivation triggered by the excessive bulk-participating reconstruction, accompanied with decayed electrochemical performances. These findings underscore the decisive role of surface configuration in regulating the electrocatalyst reconstruction and associated activity, providing a rational design paradigm for durable Li–S electrocatalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Molecular structure governs intermolecular interactions and rheological properties of three seed mucilage polysaccharides
abstract: Seed mucilage polysaccharides are promising plant-derived hydrocolloids. This study selected three seed mucilage polysaccharides: chia seed gum (CSG), Artemisia sphaerocephala Krasch polysaccharide (ASKP) and Plantago ovata seed mucilage (POSM), and elucidated the relationships between structure, intermolecular interaction and rheological relationship through structural characterization, chain conformational analysis and steady shear/oscillatory rheological measurements. Although all three samples consisted of two molecular fractions, they exhibited significant differences in molecular weight, degree of branching and uronic acid content. POSM has the highest molecular weight, exhibited the highest viscosity and the strongest intermolecular association, which was related to its highly branched structure promoting intermolecular hydrogen bonding. CSG had a lower molecular weight but a high terminal uronic acid content, causing its rheological behavior to be strongly influenced by electrostatic repulsion. ASKP exhibited weaker network formation, linked to weaker intermolecular interactions resulting from differences in its composition. These results indicate that molecular weight, branching structure, uronic acid content and intermolecular interactions collectively govern the rheological behavior of seed mucilage polysaccharides. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Grid-connected solar photovoltaic-supported dynamic voltage restoration for enhanced voltage stability and power quality
abstract: Grid-connected PV systems are important in modern power systems as they enhance voltage stability, improve power quality (PQ), and support renewable energy integration under varying solar generation conditions. However, optimizing voltage restorers remains challenging due to reactive power compensation requirements, system stability issues during PV variations, and diverse grid conditions and load profiles. To overcome this problem, this work proposes a grid-connected solar photovoltaic fed quasi-impedance source driven dynamic voltage restorer employing optimized switching strategy for enhanced voltage gain and power quality. The proposed technique is the joint execution of both House Swallow Optimizer (HSO) and Skeleton guided convolutional neural network (SGCNN) and is commonly referred as HSO- SGCNN method. The main objective of the proposed technique is to reduce the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) and enhance power output quality. The proposed HSO is utilized to optimize THD performance and SGCNN is used for maximizing the power of PV. The proposed technique is simulated in MATLAB and its performance is compared with various existing techniques includes Multi-Objective Bees Algorithm (MOBA), Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Butterfly Optimization Algorithm (BOA). The proposed control and HSO-SGCNN achieve the better performance, with voltage gain exceeding MOBA 16, GA 12, and BOA 9 at modulation index 0.5, reaching over 15 at M = 1, voltage stress reducing to 1.1 pu, and THD minimized to 4 % compared to 8–10 %, ensuring maximum stability analysed to other existing techniques. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Effect of low - methoxy pectin, heat treatment and pH on interfacial properties of purified cricket protein
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of cricket protein isolate at A/W and O/W interfaces on their interfacial rheology. Dilatational and shear rheological analyses were performed to elucidate the emulsifying and foaming properties, as well as the short- and long-term stability, of cricket protein-stabilized emulsions and foams. Additionally, the adsorption kinetics of the proteins at the interfaces were assessed. The results showed a decrease in interfacial tension at both interfaces, with values at saturation (10% w/w protein isolate) of 35 ± 2 mN/m at the A/W interface and 22 ± 2 mN/m at the O/W interface, similar to those of several vegetable proteins. The dilatational results showed that the films exhibited viscoelastic behavior at both interfaces, with the oil interface appearing more structured. On the other hand, shear analysis revealed a weak and non-elastic interfacial layer under shear deformation, suggesting the need for extra stabilizing agents in emulsions and foams. In order to stabilize the interface, a polysaccharide, low-methoxyl pectin, was added. Optimized protein-pectin solutions were produced through thermal treatments and pH variations. The mixtures were produced at two different pH levels (5.5 and 3.5) to investigate repulsive versus attractive electrostatic interactions, both with and without thermal treatment (80 °C). The interfacial rheological properties of low-methoxyl pectin–cricket protein mixtures were studied at the sunflower oil/water interface. In particular, while O/W dilatational rheology at pH 3.5 was constrained by droplet detachment, complexation under these acidic conditions formed a highly effective electrosteric barrier. This was quantitatively validated by a high surface potential (∼- 38 mV) and invariant droplet size distributions over 5 days (p = 0.101), ensuring robust kinetic emulsion stability. Furthermore, thermal processing significantly enhanced emulsion fine structure, yielding a reduced mean droplet size (ds = 3.26 μm, p < 0.001) and lower absolute variance compared to untreated systems. title: Kinetics-driven heterogeneous nucleation of yolk-shell metal sulfides toward tunable microwave absorption
abstract: The regulation of heterogeneous nucleation is considered a promising strategy in constructing multiple hetero-interfaces and simultaneously promoting interfacial polarization. However, the precise control of heterogeneous nucleation during the growth of the crystal nucleus still remains a huge challenge. In this work, a kinetics-driven heterogeneous nucleation strategy via the change of gradient concentration has been proposed to realize the phase evolution for yolk-shell metal sulfides. The results indicate that excessive Zn2+/Co2+species regulate the sulfur liberation and facilitate the formation of multi-phased metal sulfides, thereby generating increased concentration of sulfur vacancies. As expected, benefiting from the cooperative merits of optimized impedance, introduced sulfur vacancies, multiple hetero-interfaces, and yolk-shell architectures, the yolk-shell ZnCo2S4/ZnS composites exhibit a maximum reflection loss of −55.9 dB, an effective absorption bandwidth of 8.6 GHz, and a greatest radar cross section reduction value of 23.9 dB m2. Meanwhile, the as-synthesized composites display superior specific reflection loss and specific effective absorption bandwidth than the vast majority of counterparts. Furthermore, this study inspires a new insight in regulating the phase evolution via a kinetics-driven heterogeneous nucleation strategy. © 2026

title: A perfluorooctanol functionalization strategy boosting CO2 electroreduction to ethylene
abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction to ethylene represents an environmentally friendly and promising technological pathway for achieving a carbon-negative cycle. However, sustaining efficient CO2-to-ethylene conversion under industrially relevant current densities remains a significant challenge. Herein, we propose a perfluorooctanol functionalization strategy that effectively boosts the performance of electrochemical CO2 reduction to ethylene. The functionalized copper-based catalyst achieves a Faradaic efficiency exceeding 50% for ethylene and exhibits robust stability spanning over 100 h at a current density of 0.6 A cm−2. The incorporation of perfluorooctanol significantly alters the surface microenvironment and modulates the electronic structure of the Cu active sites. In situ spectroscopic analysis and theoretical calculations demonstrate that this molecular modulation effectively lowers the energy barriers for key intermediate formation and facilitates asymmetric C–C coupling, thereby promoting ethylene generation. This work presents a promising molecular interface engineering approach to realize efficient CO2-to-ethylene conversion at industrially viable current densities. © 2026

title: Two-stage data-driven distributionally robust optimization for capacity configuration of pumped-storage used to retrofit cascade hydropower stations
abstract: The increasing penetration of wind and photovoltaic power poses significant challenges to power system operation due to their inherent uncertainty and variability. Retrofitting cascade hydropower stations with pumped-storage units offers an effective way to enhance system flexibility; however, the optimal sizing of pumped-storage units under renewable energy uncertainty remains insufficiently explored. This paper proposes a two-stage data-driven distributionally robust optimization framework for the capacity configuration of pumped-storage units in a hybrid wind-photovoltaic-hydro-thermal system. The proposed framework jointly optimizes capacity investment and operational decisions while characterizing renewable energy uncertainty through a data-driven ambiguity set constructed from historical data. Case studies show that the proposed approach significantly improves both economic performance and operational flexibility. Compared with the benchmark case, the total system cost is reduced by 41.12%. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective and robust planning tool for flexible resource deployment in power systems with high renewable energy penetration. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Direct electron transfer-mediated flow-through electrochemical reductive dechlorination over a 3D self-supporting Co-N3O1 single-atom membrane electrode
abstract: Electrochemical reductive dechlorination (ERD) represents a sustainable route for eliminating halogenated pollutants, yet its practical application is fundamentally limited by insufficient intrinsic catalytic activity and sluggish interfacial mass transport. Herein, a three-dimensional (3D) self-supporting flow-through membrane electrode incorporating atomically dispersed Co-N3O1 sites (CoSAC-FEM) was developed to synergistically regulate the electronic structure of catalytic sites and convective mass transport, thereby promoting direct electron transfer (DET)-dominated dechlorination. Under microfiltration-coupled electroreduction, the CoSAC-FEM attained > 95% tris(2-chloroethyl) phosphate (TCEP) removal within 60 min, while membrane-thickness optimization enabled a single-pass dechlorination efficiency of 98.3% and a 77-fold enhancement in the mass-normalized rate constant compared with the conventional flow-by electrodle systems. Mechanistic investigations deried from membrane transport analysis, finite-element simulation and density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that convective flow-through substantially compresses the diffusion boundary layer to maximize single-atom utilization, while the asymmetric Co-N3O1 coordination optimizes the electronic structure to enhance TCEP adsorption affinity (-0.33 eV) and reduce the C-Cl bond cleavage barrier to 0.17 eV, thereby facilitating DET-dominated dechlorination and simultaneously suppressing the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Together with its excellent stability, broad matrix adaptability, negligible Co leaching (0.163 μg L−1) and low operating cost (2.4 CNY t−1), the as-fabricated CoSAC-FEM exhibits a carbon footprint 54.07% lower than that of the flow-by process. This work establishes a general design strategy that integrates electronic-structure engineering with interfacial mass-transfer enhancement for sustainable electrochemical remediation of persistent halogenated micropollutants. © 2026

title: Fault diagnosis of high-voltage transmission lines based on sequence components and multi-scale spatiotemporal awareness
abstract: The transient signals of faults in high-voltage transmission lines usually exhibit strong nonlinearity and inter-phase coupling characteristics. Traditional protection algorithms are prone to false actions or false alarms in conditions with weak characteristics such as high-resistance grounding. Therefore, this paper proposes a fault diagnosis method that integrates physical machine decoupling and multi-scale spatiotemporal perception networks. Firstly, by combining the sliding Fourier transform and the symmetrical component method, independent time-series component features are constructed to eliminate inter-phase electromagnetic coupling. Secondly, a multi-scale one-dimensional CNN network is used to extract transient broadband features, and a BiGRU network with a sliding time-series window is utilized to track the sequence evolution process. The weighted attention mechanism is combined to dynamically focus on the key fault wavefronts. Additionally, the Bayesian algorithm is introduced to achieve global optimization of model hyperparameters. Experimental results based on the 220kV high-voltage three-phase transmission line simulation system show that the model exhibits excellent recognition accuracy in six typical scenarios: no fault, single-phase grounding short circuit, two-phase grounding short circuit, two-phase short circuit, three-phase short circuit, and three-phase grounding short circuit. The model has excellent resistance-to-high-resistance capability and has broad application prospects in smart grid engineering. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Coordination-locked metastable zirconia from MOF pyrolysis drives enhanced metal–support interaction for high-performance formic acid dehydrogenation
abstract: Palladium catalysts for formic acid dehydrogenation (FAD) are profoundly influenced by the crystal phase of the support, yet the phase-dependent electronic metal–support interaction (EMSI) remains mechanistically elusive. Herein, we craft a metastable tetragonal ZrO2 (t-ZrO2) support through the confined pyrolysis of an NH2-UiO-66 metal-organic framework (MOF). The in situ formed O–Zr–N coordination network kinetically locks the t-ZrO2 phase, preserving abundant defects and enabling robust EMSI with Pd nanoparticles. This results in exceptional Pd dispersion and interfacial electron transfer, a remarkably high turnover frequency of 11088 h−1 for FAD at 323 K, surpassing the performance of many recently reported Pd-based catalytic systems. By integrating in situ spectroscopy, synchrotron radiation analysis, and PALLAS machine-learning path searches, we unveil that the O–Zr–N network kinetically stabilizes t-ZrO2 by raising the lattice reconstruction barrier. Furthermore, the gradient acid–base sites on t-ZrO2 synergize with Pd–O–Zr interfacial charge transfer to substantially lower the energy barrier for HCOO− dehydrogenation. This work establishes a new paradigm for engineering metal–support synergy via precise crystal-phase control of oxide supports. © 2026

title: Localized-state sensitization and coordination-environment modulation enhance Tm3+ near-infrared luminescence in a rare-earth double perovskite: Imaging and hierarchical optical encryption
abstract: Lead-free halide double perovskites combine low toxicity, structural tunability, and good dopant compatibility, making them important host materials for rare-earth near-infrared luminescence. However, the weak 4f–4f absorption of rare-earth ions limits near-infrared output under near-ultraviolet excitation. Here, we report a multiband Cs2NaGdCl6 phosphor co-doped with Sb3+ and Tm3+. Under near-ultraviolet excitation, the material simultaneously produces self-trapped exciton emission at 463 nm and characteristic Tm3+ emissions at 808, 1222, and 1432 nm, with the near-infrared internal quantum efficiency reaching 47.41%. Sb3+ increases the internal quantum efficiency of the host from 0.72% to 90.91%. The 1G4 level of Tm3+ serves as an energy bridge, enabling a maximum Sb3+→Tm3+ energy-transfer efficiency of 62.64%. Density functional theory calculations show that Tm3+ doping barely alters the band-edge structure of Cs2NaGdCl6, whereas Sb 5s/5p–Cl 3p hybridization creates localized states within the band gap that account for the enhanced near-ultraviolet absorption. Sb3+ also induces local charge rearrangement and octahedral distortion, reducing the local symmetry of [TmCl6]3− and thereby favoring a higher radiative probability for Tm3+ 4f–4f transitions. The packaged near-infrared phosphor-converted light-emitting diode enables clear night-vision and transmission imaging. By exploiting the similar visible luminescence of the series of samples and their differing responses to excitation wavelength and detection window, we also constructed a dual-gated platform for hierarchical dynamic optical information encryption. These results reveal the dual role of Sb3+ in near-ultraviolet photosensitization and regulation of the local coordination environment of Tm3+, and demonstrate the use of emission spanning the visible, near-infrared-I, and near-infrared-II regions in multi-scenario imaging and hierarchical optical information encryption. © 2026

title: Evaluating the effect of physical work in the heat on cognitive performance of construction workers
abstract: The risk of excessive heat exposure is especially high among outdoor construction workers and can have detrimental effects on their cognitive performance, including impaired attention and reduced memory. Reduced attention might lead to impaired judgement and increased risk of accidents, while reduced memory can diminish workers’ capacity to remember crucial safety procedures, carry out complex tasks correctly, and make wise decisions on the construction site. In this study, the cognitive performance of 20 participants performing manual laboratory-simulated construction work was investigated in a hot environment (36°C, 60% relative humidity) compared to a temperate environment (20°C, 60%). The study also evaluated the effect of physical work in hot and temperate conditions on the mental and physical demands of the performed tasks, as well as the thermal perceptions of participants. There were no significant differences in attention (Go/No-Go test) and memory (simple 2-back test) between hot and temperate conditions. Performance on the more complex memory task (3-back test) was impaired in the hot condition compared with the temperate condition (P < 0.05). Results of the present study revealed that construction workplaces can consider additional safety measures for construction workers performing complex cognitive tasks demanding working memory in hot conditions. © 2026 The Authors.

title: A fault-responsive control strategy for improving superimposed distance protection in mixed GFES–IIDG grids
abstract: In high-penetration inverter-based resources (IBR) system, the widespread deployment of grid-forming energy storage (GFES) and inverter-interfaced distributed generation (IIDG) introduces complex and time-varying behaviors in power frequency fault component (PFFC) networks. These behaviors, shaped by diverse low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) strategies, lead to significant uncertainty in the IBR PFFC impedance, undermining the performance of power frequency superimposed distance protection (PFSDP). This paper first constructs fault sequence component equivalent networks under representative GFES and IIDG control strategies. Impedance-plane analysis is used to characterize the transient evolution of characteristic impedance and identify key contributors to PFSDP performance degradation. To address these challenges, a fault-responsive sequence voltage control (FRSVC) strategy is proposed. This control scheme bypasses the outer-loop controls post-fault and output actively shaped sequence current components to emulate synchronous generator impedance behavior. The proposed strategy stabilizes the PFFC impedance, enables PFSDP to maintain correct operation under mixed-source conditions. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving protection sensitivity in systems with both GFES and IIDG. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Co-optimization of production scheduling and demand response for hydrogen-based steel plants considering hydrogen buffering and liquid-steel thermal constraints
abstract: Hydrogen-based direct reduced iron and electric arc furnace (H2DRI-EAF) technology can support deep decarbonization of steel production and provide demand-response (DR) flexibility to power systems. Realizing this flexibility requires coordination of electrolysis, hydrogen storage, and sequential steelmaking operations. Existing studies rarely represent upstream hydrogen management together with downstream liquid-steel production requirements. This study develops a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) framework for day-ahead co-optimization of hydrogen production, hydrogen storage, and heat-by-heat steelmaking schedules. Maximum waiting time limits preserve temporal coordination between consecutive liquid steel stages. A linear cooling relation verifies thermal feasibility for the final transfer from AOD to CC, while hydrogen storage decouples electrolyzer operation from shaft furnace hydrogen demand. Under matched conditions, coordinated scheduling reduces specific operating-energy cost by 31.14% and increases the DR flexibility index, quantified here as the off-peak electricity-share index, by 14.55 percentage points relative to the controlled baseline. All 27 joint stress-test scenarios combining variations in PV availability, electricity-price profiles, and shaft-furnace hydrogen consumption remained feasible. Relative to the nominal case within this assessment, the change in total operating-energy cost ranged from −6.67% to 16.73%. The off-peak electricity-share index changed by −1.04 to 1.25 percentage points. Sensitivity analysis identifies electrolyzer capacity as a key determinant of this index under the evaluated conditions. © 2026

title: Cross-robot open-set fault detection via normal-only adaptation and residual latent-space alignment
abstract: Reliable fault detection and health monitoring of industrial robots are important for smart manufacturing in Industry 4.0. However, robotic platforms differ in their mechanical design, sensing characteristics, and operating conditions. These differences make it difficult for data-driven models to generalize to unseen robots and working conditions. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a cross-robot framework for open-set fault detection using only normal data from the target robot. The framework uses a condition-normalized residual adaptation mechanism in the latent space. First, a structured representation is learned from the source robot. The learned representation is then adapted to the target robot using only normal samples. Compactness-based constraints and statistical modeling of normal behavior are used to detect unknown faults as deviations from the normal representation. The framework is evaluated on two industrial robots under variations in load, speed, and motion. Two evaluation strategies are also considered: sequential normal-only adaptation to welding motion and direct open-set detection without further adaptation. The results show consistent fault detection across different robots and operating conditions. A comparative benchmarking analysis further demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach and its ability to maintain reliable fault detection performance under different loading and motion conditions. This demonstrates the potential of the framework for practical industrial health monitoring. This is an open access article under the CC BY-NC license. http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/

title: Regulating H2O dissociation on Ni-doped Cu nanowires to promote electrocatalytic nitric oxide reduction to ammonia
abstract: The electrocatalytic nitric oxide reduction reaction (NORR) presents a promising method for simultaneously mitigating nitric oxide (NO) pollution and synthesizing ammonia (NH3). However, its practical application is hindered by sluggish kinetics, primarily due to inefficient water dissociation, which results in an inadequate supply of active hydrogen (*H) and thereby limits the hydrogenation of nitrogen-containing intermediates. Herein, we present Ni-doped Cu nanowires as a high-performance electrocatalyst for the NORR. The optimized catalyst with a Ni/(Ni + Cu) molar ratio of 10% (CuNi10% NWs) delivers an industrial-scale current density exceeding 1000 mA cm−2 in a flow cell, achieving an exceptional Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 90.35% and an NH3 yield rate of 6.84 mmol h−1 cm−2 (17.28 mmol gcat−1 h−1) at −1.0 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode. Furthermore, in a membrane electrode assembly, the CuNi10% NWs achieved an NH3 FE of 82.47% and an NH3 yield rate of 4.44 mmol h−1 cm−2 (8.88 mmol gcat−1 h−1). Remarkably, in situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and Tafel slope analyses reveal that Ni doping reduces the interfacial charge transfer resistance of Cu nanowires, accelerates the rate-determining Volmer step of water dissociation, and facilitates the generation and adsorption of *H intermediates. This study opens a new pathway for the resource utilization of industrial waste gas NO and the direct synthesis of NH3. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Phosphomolybdate-guided synthesis of large-interlayer-spacing phosphate-modified NiOOH array for ampere-level oxygen evolution reaction
abstract: Electrochemical water splitting is a promising route for green hydrogen production, but the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) limits the overall efficiency. Layered NiOOH is a cost-effective OER electrocatalyst, yet its activity and stability—especially at high current densities—remain insufficient. Herein,we propose a novel design strategy that combines phosphate ion (Pi) modification with interlayer spacing enlargement in NiOOH. A large phosphomolybdate (PM) anion serves as an situ self-removable pillaring agents during the reconstruction of nickel molybdate into a Pi-intercalated Ni(OH)2 precatalyst (Ni(OH)2-PM-Pi), which is then electrochemically activated to form NiOOH-PM-Pi. This material features enhanced Ni4+ content, abundant oxygen vacancies (V..o), and expanded interlayer spacing. The elevated Ni4+ and V..o cooperatively accelerate OER via the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), while the expanded interlayer spacing enhances mass transport within the NiOOH interlayers, greatly suppressing interlayer localized acidification and increasing interlayer utilization, thereby improving the catalyst's stability and activity. Consequently, the resulting catalyst exhibits an iR-corrected overpotential of only 324 mV at 1000 mA cm−2 and maintains excellent stable operation for 500 h at ~1000 mA cm−2 in Pi-containing KOH electrolyte, outperforming most reported Ni-based OER electrocatalysts. This work offers a design approach to achieve both high activity and high stability in OER catalysts under ampere-level current densities. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Impact of surface protrusions on negative corona discharge onset voltage for high–voltage stranded conductors
abstract: The onset voltage of negative corona discharge on high-voltage conductors is strongly influenced by surface irregularities and electric field non-uniformity. Previous studies have investigated corona inception on stranded conductors and the effect of conducting protrusions on electric field enhancement; however, their combined influence has not been adequately addressed. In this paper, a three-dimensional numerical model is developed to investigate the onset of negative corona on a stranded conductor with a conducting protrusion in the presence of a grounded plane. The electric field distribution is computed using an extended charge simulation technique, in which the stranded conductor is represented by helical line charges, while the protrusion is modeled using ring and point charges. Image charges are implemented to simulate the grounded plane. To ensure high computational accuracy, the boundary conditions were evaluated, demonstrating that for all investigated protrusion geometries, the maximum percentage potential error remained below 1.06 %. The proposed algorithm is tested against previous experimental work, and excellent agreement is reached. The results show that a conducting protrusion dramatically increases the local electric field compared to a stranded conductor without protrusions, which in turn decreases the corona onset voltage. The proposed method is implemented to study the effect of different dimensions of protrusions on the surface electric field and the corona onset voltage, aiding the performance analysis of irregular practical stranded conductors. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Synergistic surface modification of β titanium alloy by friction stir processing and compressed plasma flow for enhanced osteogenesis and antibacterial performance
abstract: To address the key technical challenges of insufficient bioactivity and poor coating adhesion on the surface of β-titanium alloy biomedical implants, this study employed a synergistic modification technology combining friction stir processing (FSP) and compressed plasma flow (CPF) to prepare a composite functional structure containing ZnO nanoparticles (ZnO-NPs). Utilizing the severe plastic deformation and dynamic recrystallization effects generated during the FSP process, the alloy surface exhibits a fine-grained structure with reduced elastic modulus. The cross-section reveals a gradient grain structure, significantly improving the mechanical compatibility between the implant and bone tissue. Subsequent CPF treatment promotes the uniform dispersion of ZnO-NPs, which is associated with the formation of TiN phases. This treatment further optimized the surface morphology, creating a rough interface at the micron scale and a smooth interface at the nanoscale. In vitro experimental results demonstrate that these improvements significantly enhanced cell adhesion, proliferation, and osteogenic differentiation, while also improving antibacterial properties by reducing bacterial adhesion and disrupting bacterial cell membranes. In vivo experimental results indicate that the implant significantly promoted the growth of bone tissue. The synergistic effect of FSP and CPF technologies provides an innovative strategy for the surface modification of biomedical titanium alloys. © 2026

title: Processing-driven interplay of interfacial asymmetry and microstructure in spin-orbit effects of Pt/Co heterostructures
abstract: Deposition conditions such as Ar pressure and power density are well-known to influence the surface and microstructure of sputtered thin films and multilayers, which in turn affect spin-orbit coupling-related magnetic properties such as interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) and spin-orbit torque (SOT) in nonmagnetic layer (NM)/ferromagnetic layer (FM) heterostructures. Nonetheless, a holistic approach to understanding how processing conditions influence magnetic properties has been understudied. This study investigates how deposition conditions affect the surface roughness and microstructure of the Pt layer, and how these factors impact DMI and SOT in Pt/Co heterostructures. The Pt surface roughness exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on Ar pressure from 1.5 to 20 mTorr, altering the interfacial asymmetry and, consequently, varying the DMI energy density from 0.93 to 1.19 mJ/m2. In contrast, power density shows a weak influence on roughness and DMI within the investigated range from 1.23 to 7.40 W/cm2. Post-deposition annealing promotes interdiffusion at the Pt/Co interface, reducing both the surface anisotropy (Ks) and the absolute value of the DMI (Deff). Increasing Ar pressure also modifies the Pt microstructure, reducing crystallite size from 5.02 to 2.92 nm and increasing microstrain from 0.022 to 0.037. These microstructural changes promote electron scattering and increase electrical resistivity from 27.8 to 92.8 µΩ cm, accompanied by an increase in the damping-like SOT efficiency (ξDL) up to 0.24. Varying the power density also increases crystallite size from 3.33 to 4.76 nm, leading to a rise in the switching current density (Jc) from 48.6 to 69.0 MA/cm2, despite its relatively weak influence on surface roughness and DMI. These results reveal how deposition conditions affect both the interfacial and microstructural characteristics of Pt layers and their associated properties in Pt/Co heterostructures. © 2026

title: Dipole Field Engineering in Ni(II)‐Acetylide Frameworks under Mechanical Activation for Enhanced Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction
abstract: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction offers a promising route for solar-to-chemical energy conversion, yet its efficiency remains limited by inefficient charge transport within two-dimensional organic frameworks due to rapid intralayer recombination. Here, we develop a dipole-field engineering strategy in a nickel(II)-acetylide framework, TP(NH2)-Ni-AF, in which polar –NH2 groups enhance piezoelectric polarization and regulate intralayer charge kinetics. Under visible-light and ultrasonic irradiation, the TP(NH2)-Ni-AF/Na2SO3 system delivers a CO production rate of 125.2 μmol g−1 h−1 with 88.36% selectivity, outperforming the non-aminated analogue. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that TP-Ni-AF exhibits a dipole moment of 175.49 D under 2 GPa, whereas –NH2 increases structural asymmetry and raises the dipole moment to 192.01 D. Consistently, piezoresponse force microscopy confirms a higher piezoelectric response, with a d33 value of 16.56 pm V−1. This internal polarization field promotes charge separation and electron migration from the photoactive ligand to the catalytically active –CtbndC–Ni(PBu3)2–CtbndC– sites. Mechanistic studies further show that polarization-assisted charge migration facilitates CO2 adsorption through a ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) pathway and lowers the energy barrier for *COOH formation. These results establish polar-group-induced internal electric fields as a powerful design principle for controlling photogenerated carrier dynamics and advancing piezo-photocatalytic systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Horizon-adaptive time–frequency fusion for renewable power forecasting: empirical evidence of a consistent horizon–representation relationship across wind and solar systems
abstract: Accurate renewable power forecasting requires extracting information from both temporal dynamics and frequency-domain fluctuations, yet the optimal balance between these representations across forecasting horizons remains unclear. This study proposes a Horizon-Adaptive Time–Frequency Fusion (HATF) framework that learns horizon-dependent weighting between temporal and spectral features through a lightweight fusion module. Experiments on seven years of operational wind farm SCADA data demonstrate that HATF consistently outperforms recurrent, convolutional, and Transformer-based baselines across forecasting horizons from 15 min to 4 h. Cross-dataset validation on an independent wind turbine dataset and a solar photovoltaic dataset further confirms the robustness of the approach; for the solar dataset, the auxiliary input channels of the model carry irradiance and ambient temperature rather than wind speed and wind direction, preserving the three-channel architecture across energy sources. Ablation studies show that adaptive fusion is essential for effectively integrating time-domain and frequency-domain information. A key finding is that the learned fusion coefficient exhibits a highly consistent approximately linear relationship with forecasting horizon across all datasets (R²>0.98). Autocorrelation analysis indicates that this behavior is linked to the substantially different persistence timescales of low-frequency and high-frequency signal components, causing the model to gradually shift from frequency-dominant representations at short horizons to time-dominant representations at longer horizons. In addition, a Gaussian prediction head provides well-calibrated uncertainty estimates with near-nominal 95% prediction interval coverage. The results suggest that horizon-adaptive time–frequency fusion offers both an effective forecasting framework and an interpretable perspective on how predictive information evolves across temporal scales in renewable energy systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Study of optimum photovoltaic energy ingress in conventional grid system without compromising stability margins
abstract: Due to growing energy demand, rising greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, and a rising global average temperature, replacing fossil fuels with sustainable renewable energy sources is the ultimate global target. However, variable renewable energy sources have repercussions for existing grid systems due to their inherent volatility and uncertainty. Such drastic variations can lead to transient stability issues and need to be considered when planning high ingress of renewable energy sources in a conventional grid system. This paper provides an optimization model based on the genetic algorithm technique to allow maximum possible photovoltaic (PV) energy ingress in the system, keeping system parameters within stipulated stability limits. Certain design variables have also been defined and constrained to achieve the optimization objective. The resulting design variables from the optimization model are then plugged into the IEEE 30-bus test system for simulation of transient stability. The system shows complete recovery from the applied transient disturbance from sudden generation and load drop events. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Constructing Lewis acid-base pairs on S-scheme Al-BiOBr/Bi2O3 heterojunctions for highly efficient photocatalytic nitrogen fixation
abstract: Photocatalytic nitrogen fixation has long been constrained by the intrinsic inertness of the N=N bond and the severe recombination of photoexcited electron-hole pairs. Here, we construct an aluminum-doped BiOBr/Bi2O3 S-scheme heterojunction in which Al3 + selectively replaces Bi3+ sites in the BiOBr lattice, while the Bi2O3 phase retains its inherent crystal structure almost entirely. This asymmetric doping configuration strengthens the internal electric field across the S-scheme interface. The strong polarizing ability of Al3+ activates nearby lattice oxygen atoms into Lewis base sites and induces the formation of additional oxygen vacancies (Ov), while simultaneously extracting electron density from adjacent Bi centers via Al-O-Bi bridge bonds, thereby enhancing the Lewis acidity of Bi. The resulting Al/Bi-O Lewis acid-base pair activates N2 through a synergistic push-pull mechanism, in conjunction with the charge modulation induced by the oxygen vacancies. In pure water and in the absence of any sacrificial agent, the optimally designed photocatalyst achieves an NH3 production rate as high as 801.3 μmol g−1 h−1 under simulated sunlight, surpassing transition-metal-doped analogues. This work establishes a lattice-confined Lewis acid-base pair paradigm, opening a new avenue for designing high-efficiency nitrogen-fixing photocatalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Defect-rich PtCo multilayer nanobowls for the efficient glycerol electrooxidation and coupled hydrogen evolution
abstract: The electrocatalytic glycerol oxidation reaction (GOR) is important for turning excess glycerol from biodiesel byproducts into valuable chemicals. However, the process inevitably generates C1-C3 byproducts, resulting in compromised Faradaic efficiency (FE) and poor selectivity toward target compounds. Remarkable electrocatalytic performance in glycerol conversion is achieved using surface-defective PtCo layered metallene nanobowls (PtCo MNs). This novel catalyst facilitates the conversion of glycerol to formate production with an outstanding Faradaic efficiency (FEformate) of 95.89% and a selectivity of 92.36%. The results obtained from density functional theory prove that the addition of Co element can effectively regulate the electronic configuration, promote electron transfer and accelerate the progress of the GOR reaction. This work creates a method for making layered nanobowl structures and enables the design of next-generation electrocatalytic systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Cross-domain attack detection in integrated energy systems based on knowledge-data dual-view collaboration
abstract: To address the challenges of scarce cross‑domain attack samples and strong cooperative stealthiness in Integrated Energy Systems (IES), this paper proposes a detection method based on knowledge–data dual‑view collaboration. First, considering the gas–thermal inertia of IES, a knowledge graph (KG) encoding the spatio‑temporal logic and constraints of Denial‑of‑Service (DoS), False Data Injection (FDI), and Replay attacks is constructed to form the knowledge view. Second, the knowledge view embeds physical constraints via the RotatE embedding model, while the data view employs a Spatio‑Temporal Graph Attention Network (ST‑GAT) to extract dynamic measurement features, thereby establishing a dual‑view collaborative detection framework. Finally, bilinear pooling is applied to fuse heterogeneous features, and anomaly discrimination is performed based on the consistency between domain-knowledge constraints and measurement features. Simulation tests on an IEEE 30‑bus electricity–heat–gas coupled system show that the proposed method attains an F1 score of 0.939 at a 5% attack rate, outperforming the Long Short‑Term Memory Autoencoder (LSTM‑AE), Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), RotatE, and ST‑GAT baselines, with markedly reduced false‑positive and false‑negative rates. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Enhancing Na-ion conduction in Na3Zr2Si2PO12 electrolyte for solid-state sodium batteries via Na/Si/P ratio regulation strategy
abstract: NASICON-type Na3Zr2Si2PO12 (NZSP) has received extensive attention as an electrolyte for solid-state sodium batteries (SSSBs) owing to its good air stability and chemical durability. However, low ionic conductivity and poor interfacial contact are major challenges for the application of NZSP electrolyte in SSSBs. Herein, an intrinsic Na/Si/P ratio regulation strategy is adopted to optimize the crystal structure and Na-ion transport behavior of the NZSP electrolyte, enhancing its ionic conductivity and electrochemical performance. A series of Na3+xZr2Si2+xP1−xO12 (x = 0–0.3) electrolytes are synthesized by a sol-gel method, and the influence of intrinsic Na/Si/P ratio variation on the crystal structure, microstructure, ionic conductivity, and electrochemical performance is systematically investigated. The optimized Na3.1Zr2Si2.1P0.9O12 (NZSP0.1) exhibits effective enhancement of electrical and electrochemical performance, achieving an improved ionic conductivity of 0.26 mS cm−1, which is approximately three times higher than that of NZSP. A Na/NZSP0.1/Na symmetric battery demonstrates reduced interfacial resistance and an elevated critical current density of about 0.42 mA cm−2, enabling stable sodium plating and stripping for 400 h at 0.05 mA cm−2. Moreover, a Na3V2(PO4)3/NZSP0.1/Na full battery delivers favorable rate capability and cycling stability. This work presents a simple and effective strategy to prepare advanced NZSP-based electrolytes for application in SSSBs. © 2026

title: Tailoring ferroelectric phase stability in zirconium-rich hafnia through atomic layer stack engineering
abstract: HfO2-based ferroelectric thin films are attractive for nonvolatile memories due to their scalability and CMOS compatibility. However, ferroelectricity in hafnia is typically constrained by a narrow compositional window, while Zr-rich films are prone to stabilize antiferroelectric tetragonal phases rather than the desired ferroelectric orthorhombic phase, thereby limiting both polarization robustness and device reliability. Here we show that an atomic layer stack strategy offers an effective handle to tailor the strain and further modulate phase evolution in Zr-rich HfO2-ZrO2 films. By constructing solid-solution, periodic multilayer, and bilayer HfO2-ZrO2 films under a comparable Zr-rich nominal design, we observe a clear evolution from antiferroelectricity to stable ferroelectricity with progressive relief of in-plane strain. Structural and electrical characterizations reveal that stack configuration favors the stabilization of the metastable orthorhombic phase in a Zr-rich regime conventionally unfavorable for ferroelectricity. Among the investigated architectures, the bilayer H20Z80 film exhibits a high 2Pr of 52.1 μC/cm2 together with endurance beyond 1011 cycles and a projected retention time of 10 years. These results reveal that ferroic phase evolution is extendable beyond conventional compositional constraints and can be accessed through atomic layer stacking engineering. This work provides a practical materials-design strategy for high-endurance hafnia-based ferroelectric memories. © 2026
