title: MOF-derived Ni-Co bimetallic catalyst enabling photothermal dry reforming of methane at the thermodynamic limit
abstract: Dry reforming of methane (DRM) is an attractive route for CO2 utilization and high-value energy conversion, yet conventional thermal catalysis suffers from high energy consumption and serious catalyst deactivation. To address these challenges, efficient photothermal catalysts were rationally designed through metal-organic framework (MOF) derivation to promote low-carbon DRM and enhance catalytic performance. A series of MOF-derived Ni-based catalysts were synthesized by post-synthesis modification combined with atmosphere-mediated treatment. The optimal NiCo-CeO2-M exhibited full UV-Vis-NIR spectral response and delivered enhanced photothermal synergistic DRM performance. Under the operating conditions of 600 ℃, 72 L·gcat−1·h−1 and 2.55 W·cm−2, it achieved a good balance between reactant conversion and syngas production rate, maintaining 100 h of stable operation without deactivation at the thermodynamic limit level. Characterizations revealed a hierarchical pore structure favorable to mass transfer and light harvesting, while high metal dispersion and abundant interfacial sites facilitated reactant activation and migration. Co doping narrowed the bandgap and constructed Co3O4/CeO2 heterojunction, improving light absorption and carrier separation efficiency. Theoretical calculations and electromagnetic simulations further clarified the synergistic mechanism originating from the precise regulation of the Ni-Co bimetallic system and interfacial structure, which optimized charge transfer, lowered activation barriers and strengthened localized electric fields. In this photothermal system, the synergistic interaction between light-assisted electronic effects, surface-defect-associated CO2 activation, and thermal driving forces contributes to enhanced DRM performance and stability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Precipitation-assisted microstructural stabilization and twin-mediated strength-ductility synergy in EB-PBF TiAl alloys
abstract: Inherent microstructural inhomogeneity and limited ductility remain major obstacles to achieving superior strength-ductility synergy in additively manufactured TiAl alloys. In this study, a TiAl-Si alloy was fabricated by electron beam powder bed fusion and tailored through a two-step heat treatment to control its microstructure and mechanical performance. The resulting alloy exhibits a hierarchical multiscale architecture. Atom probe tomography reveals that nanoscale Ti5Si3 precipitates partially dissolve while submicron particles are retained, stabilizing the lamellar structure through Zener pinning and diffusion inhibition, and effectively suppressing coarsening. Transmission electron microscope observations further identify three twin-twin interaction modes that activate defect-mediated mechanisms triggered by local stress concentrations, thereby accommodating strain and sustaining plastic flow. Consequently, the alloy achieves an ultimate tensile strength of ∼1050 MPa and significantly enhanced elongation relative to the as-built state. This strength-ductility synergy arises from the decoupled yet complementary effects of precipitate-stabilized lamellae and twin-interaction-induced plasticity, establishing a mechanistic framework for designing additively manufactured TiAl alloys. © 2026

title: Mechanistic study on self-healing coating with superior corrosion fatigue performance for Mg alloy
abstract: Although pre-corrosion-induced fatigue crack initiation is a limitation for the engineering application of Mg alloys, the development of protective coatings to address this issue remains unexplored. A self-healing electrophoretic paint (E-paint) coating on Mg-Al-Ca alloy was developed in this study by encapsulating a corrosion inhibitor (barbituric acid, BA) into halloysite nanocontainers (HNT) to fabricate pH-responsive nanocontainers, which were subsequently incorporated into the coating system. The mechanism of the coating on fatigue crack initiation under pre-corrosion conditions was systematically investigated. Results show that after 7 and 14 days of pre-corrosion, the E-paint-HNT-BA specimen achieved fatigue strengths of 112 and 98 MPa at 1 × 106 cycles, representing improvements of 60% and 133%, respectively, compared to the uncoated alloy. Further evidence demonstrates that when the coating is damaged and the Mg substrate begins to corrode, BA is rapidly released from the HNT in response to the local pH increase caused by corrosion, thereby achieving highly efficient self-healing. This mechanism retards corrosion fatigue crack initiation and enhances the fatigue performance of the Mg-Al-Ca alloy, effectively preventing the progression of localized corrosion attack toward fatigue cracking and thereby addressing the critical challenge of pre-corrosion-induced fatigue failure in service components. © 2026 Chinese Society of Metals

title: MS2RSHAT-Net: A hybrid Shoebill optimized deep learning framework for accurate electrical fault prediction
abstract: Electrical faults arise from insulation failure, aging, and disturbances, causing instability, traditional and deep learning methods show limitations in performance. To overcome these boundaries, this paper presents a novel hybrid Multi-Scale Sparse Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) Stack Hierarchical Attention Transformer Network (MS2RSHAT-Net) for precise electrical fault detection and classification. The steps involved data preprocessing using missing value imputation and Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) using distribution charts. For efficiently represent the data, feature engineering techniques applied Min-Max scaling and feature extraction are applied. For capturing both local and global temporal trends in fault behavior, a hybrid MS2RSHAT-Net incorporates a multi-scale sparse recurrent stack for learning fine-grained transient patterns and long-term degradation drifts, while a hierarchical attention transformer for adaptively re-weights temporal contexts across scales, ensuring computational efficiency for embedded or edge deployment and emphasizing diagnostically salient epochs. Additionally, the Shoebill Optimization Algorithm (SOA) is employed to optimize the hyperparameters. The proposed model is executed by Python and evaluated using Electrical Fault Detection and Classification dataset. Experimental results show proposed technique achieves high accuracy of 99.61 %, precision of 99.58 %, recall of 99.53 %, and F1-score of 99.56 %, outperforming existing techniques. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Energy-level engineering of quasi-two-dimensional perovskite for efficient photocatalytic C(sp3)–H bond oxidation
abstract: Photocatalytic selective oxidation of aromatic C(sp3)–H bonds represents an appealing strategy for producing value-added chemicals and enabling solar-to-chemical energy conversion. Despite rapid progress in halide perovskite photocatalysts, their practical performance remains fundamentally limited by inefficient charge separation and rapid photocarrier recombination. Herein, we demonstrate a quasi-two-dimensional perovskite platform, (C4H9NH3)2(CH3NH3)Pb2BrxCl7−x (BMPBC-x, x = 0–7), in which structural anisotropy and electronic structure engineering are synergistically integrated to regulate photocatalytic reactivity. Precise modulation of the Br−/Cl− composition enables continuous tuning of the band structure while simultaneously activating a local polarization-related electromechanical response associated with the quasi-2D framework. This dual regulation established a cooperative mechanism that enhances both light harvesting and charge separation, thereby significantly improving photocarrier utilization efficiency. Hence, the optimized composition delivers up to a 17-fold enhancement in activity relative to the Cl-pure phase and a 1.5-fold increase compared with the Br-pure counterpart. Emphatically, the optimized BMPBC-4.7 nanosheets exhibit a benzaldehyde formation rate of 19.1 mmol·g−1·h−1 under light irradiation, representing one of the highest reported performances for single-component perovskite photocatalysts. This work highlights halide-mediated energy-level engineering coupled with facet junction as an effective strategy for manipulating charge-carrier dynamics in quasi-2D perovskites, offering new opportunities for efficient photocatalytic organic transformations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Integrating distance relay blinding constraints into security-constrained economic dispatch via protection shift factors
abstract: The rapid integration of Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs) is introducing new couplings between market-based dispatch and distance-relay security. In meshed transmission networks, economy-driven dispatch of low-cost IBRs can increase reverse fault-current infeeds and erode Zone 1 security margins. This paper proposes a new preventive dispatch framework that integrates specific distance-relay blinding margins into linear Security-Constrained Economic Dispatch (SCED) constraints through a developed Protection Shift Factor (PSF). The proposed method separates a post-fault network-side transfer factor from an IBR-level fault-current sensitivity using a source-resolved current tracing methodology. This separation reveals whether higher IBR dispatch increases the relay-relevant fault current. Results from Electromagnetic Transient (EMT) simulations of the IEEE 14-bus network using a generic Western Electricity Coordinating Council (WECC)-type IBR control policy show the IBR's fault-current contribution decreases as its pre-fault power dispatch increases. Conversely, under a retained-active-current policy, the IBR's fault-current contribution increases with higher pre-fault dispatch, thereby establishing an operationally meaningful protection constraint for SCED. The study also demonstrates realistic distance-relay underreach scenarios considering a nearby dispatch-boundary case used for SCED. In the SCED example, conventional dispatch exceeds the EMT-identified projected-current limit, while the protection-constrained dispatch curtails the network-sensitive low-cost IBR and produces a protection-induced nodal-price deduction. Furthermore, the scalability of the framework is validated on the WECC 240-bus system, demonstrating that the linear surrogate maintains exceptional accuracy across bulk grids and successfully arbitrates numerous interacting distance-relay constraints. The developed framework provides a practical route for carrying EMT-identified relay-security margins into linear market clearing and helps mitigate pricing protection-security congestion. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Structural evolution and mechanical properties of metallic disordered materials influenced by the Bragg effect of ion irradiation
abstract: Ion irradiation, an established radiation damage technique, exhibits the Bragg peak effect, resulting in uneven energy deposition along the incidence trajectory. This study evaluated proton irradiation on ZrCuNiAl(Nb) metallic glasses (MGs). A SRIM simulation demonstrated decreased displacement damage in the Nb-containing MG in the cascade region (CR). Atomic force microscopy revealed an anomalous increase in energy deposition (Edis) in the CR of the Nb-containing sample, in contrast to the reduced liquid-like character in the Nb-free sample. Combined with synchrotron radiation results, Nb promotes short-range ordered structures with high displacement threshold energy; its doping mainly alters the structural response inside the track region under electronic energy loss, forming a “loose yet stable” latent track structure with enhanced damage buffering capability. The structure can accommodate part of the cascade-induced defects and suppress their long-range migration, thereby maintaining stable hardness and modulus in ZrCuNiAlNb along the irradiation path, whereas ZrCuNiAl exhibits irradiation-induced hardening. These results yield fundamental insights into the role of electronic energy loss and provide important guidelines for elucidating defect-buffering mechanisms in MGs under ion radiation. © 2026

title: Complete selectivity switching between CO and CH4 for CO2 photoreduction on Pd-SrTiO3 nanocrystals
abstract: Carbon dioxide (CO2) photoreduction to methane (CH4) encounters low selectivity. This is mainly attributed to insufficient protons to sustain deep protonation; additionally, linearly adsorbed intermediates on single active sites tend to undergo direct desorption to form carbon monoxide (CO). Herein, we designed Pd nanoparticle-loaded semiconductor oxides nanocrystals, in which Pd not only facilitates water dissociation to generate protons, but also enables the construction of interfacial dual sites for bridge-mode adsorption of reaction intermediates. As a prototype, Pd nanoparticle-loaded SrTiO3 nanocrystals were synthesized. Density functional theory calculations indicate Sr–Pd hetero-sites stabilize *COOH and enhance *CO adsorption; Pd incorporation lowers the water dissociation barrier from 0.97 to 0.79 eV and facilitates sustained hydrogen spillover to generate sufficient active H species. Quasi in situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and charge density difference results confirm the charge redistribution and form electron-rich dual-active sites. Hence, the Pd-SrTiO3 nanocrystals achieved nearly 100% selectivity toward CH4, whereas the SrTiO3 nanocrystals only produced CO. This work establishes a rational principle for designing high-selectivity photocatalysts toward deep CO2 conversion into CH4. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Atomic coordination engineering for overcoming the selectivity-durability tradeoff of carbon-encapsulated metals towards sustainable wastewater purification
abstract: Breaking the selectivity-durability tradeoff of carbon-encapsulated cobalt/peroxymonosulfate (C-Co/PMS) remains challenging. Although singlet oxygen (1O2) derived from C-Co/PMS shows high selectivity toward electron-rich pollutants, it is readily quenched by water, which impairs catalytic durability during repeated operation. Herein, we rationally construct copper single atoms on C-Co (CuSA-C-Co) to trigger the formation of additional high-valent copper-oxo species (Cu(III)-OH) during PMS activation, which compensates for the intrinsic defect of sole 1O2, overcoming this critical tradeoff. On Co sites, adsorbed PMS undergoes O-H dissociation to form peroxomonosulfate radical (*SO5•-), which self-disproportionates into 1O2. Meanwhile, strong orbital hybridization between the Cu 3d orbital of CuSA and the O 2p orbitals of PMS induces heterolytic cleavage of peroxide O-O bonds, facilitating oxygen atom transfer to generate Cu(III)-OH. Benefiting from these complementary oxidation pathways, CuSA-C-Co/PMS retains high selectivity toward electron-rich pollutants while achieving catalytic durability during repeated cycling compared with pristine C-Co/PMS. Beyond the sole 1O2-mediated mineralization of bisphenol A (BPA), Cu(III)-OH converts BPA into oligomers via proton-coupled electron transfer, and these oligomers spontaneously accumulate on the CuSA-C-Co surface, which simplifies subsequent water treatment. Continuous treatment of BPA-containing wastewater over 240 h shows that the CuSA-C-Co/polyvinylidene fluoride/PMS system sustains > 91.4% BPA removal. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Suppression strategy of neutral-point potential fluctuation in VIENNA rectifier based on zero-sequence voltage component injection
abstract: The neutral-point potential fluctuation in the VIENNA rectifier is one of the key factors affecting the charging performance of DC charging systems. To address this issue, the charging and discharging behavior of the DC-link capacitors under different switching states is analyzed, revealing that the neutral-point potential fluctuation mainly consists of an AC fluctuation component and a DC offset component. A time-domain expression for the neutral-point potential fluctuation is derived, showing that its amplitude is proportional to the modulation index and the input current amplitude, and inversely proportional to the grid frequency and the DC-link capacitance. Based on this analysis, a zero-sequence voltage component injection strategy based on neutral-point charge balance is proposed. The strategy regulates the switching-period-averaged neutral-point current, divides the modulation cycle into different intervals according to the polarities of the three-phase input currents, and analytically determines the AC-compensation zero-sequence voltage in each interval. A DC-offset correction component is then superimposed to simultaneously suppress the low-frequency AC fluctuation and DC offset of the neutral-point potential. To verify the proposed strategy, a three-phase VIENNA rectifier experimental platform is built. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy reduces the voltage ripple of each DC-link capacitor from ±2.5% to ±1.0%, thereby confirming its effectiveness. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Template-induced assembly and in situ polymerization for constructing uniformly distributed molybdate-secondary-doped polyaniline toward self-passivating and self-healing epoxy coatings
abstract: Conductive polymer coatings show great promise for the passivation protection of metals. However, the aggregation of conductive polymers and the gradual deterioration of electrochemical activity still limit their long-term protection in harsh marine environments. In this study, plasma-modified basalt (MB) scales were employed as two-dimensional (2D) templates for the induced assembly and in situ polymerization of aniline (ANI), followed by secondary doping with molybdate ions (MoO42−). The resulting P-Mo/MB filler was incorporated into an epoxy (EP) resin to construct a multifunctional coating for Al alloys. The uniformly distributed polyaniline (PANI) improves filler dispersion within the EP resin, increases the accessibility of redox-active sites, and helps alleviate localized electric field concentration. Additionally, MoO42− secondary doping enhances the electrochemical cycling stability of PANI and enables pH-responsive release of the inhibitor. The P-Mo/MB/EP coating maintains a |Z|0.01 Hz value of 2.46 × 1010 Ω cm2 after 150 days of immersion, approximately 10 times that of the MB/EP coating. Surface and cross-sectional analyses reveal the formation of a compact protective film with a thickness of approximately 450 nm on the Al alloy surface. Moreover, no obvious corrosion is observed in the scratched area of the P-Mo/MB/EP coating after 120 h, accompanied by the gradual formation of a continuous protective film. These results demonstrate that the synergistic integration of physical shielding, self-passivation, and self-healing provides an effective strategy for developing long-term multifunctional anti-corrosion coatings. © 2026

title: Strength-ductility synergy of hierarchical porous copper prepared by one-step dealloying of Cu-Mn-Fe alloy
abstract: The practical deployment of dealloyed porous copper for functional applications remains hampered by its inadequate mechanical strength and macroscopic brittleness. A critical challenge in this field lies in fabricating bulk structures with superior mechanical performance via facile synthetic routes. In this work, we prepared hierarchical porous copper with strength-ductility synergy through one-step dealloying of the Cu40Mn50Fe10 alloy. The resulting material exhibits remarkable mechanical properties, achieving an initial peak compressive stress of 58.22 ± 7.08 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength of 17.12 ± 1.32 MPa, and a fracture strain of 5.07% ± 0.44%. Such excellent mechanical performance originates from effective stress redistribution and crack deflection across the microscale ligament network, coupled with intrinsic strain accommodation and dislocation accumulation within the nanoporous structure. Moreover, the deformation resistance provided by retained twin structures inherited from the master alloy also plays a vital role. Furthermore, we anticipate that the tension-compression asymmetry in the mechanical response of the present material will provide new insights into the structural optimization and performance enhancement of hierarchical porous copper. © 2026

title: Enhancement of chitosan coating properties by carrier-free self-assembled coptisine-cinnamic acid nanoparticles and their application in cherry tomato preservation
abstract: Chitosan is an important hydrocolloid for edible films; however, its strong water affinity, swelling tendency, and limited moisture-barrier capacity restrict its application in high-humidity food storage. In this study, we synthesized carrier-free coptisine–cinnamic acid nanoassemblies (COP–CA NPs) and incorporated them as active nanofillers into chitosan coatings. The optimized nanoparticles had an average particle size of 55.09 nm, a PDI of 0.205, and a relatively narrow particle size distribution, while retaining good in vitro free radical scavenging and antibacterial activities. Strong antibacterial functionality was also maintained after incorporation into the CS matrix. The incorporation of COP–CA NPs reduced the water wettability, water solubility, and swelling degree of the chitosan film, while simultaneously enhancing its moisture barrier properties and mechanical strength. The water vapor permeability of the 0.20% composite coating film (0.20% CS@NPs) decreased by 56.1%, while its tensile strength increased by 53.5%, without markedly affecting elongation at break. Physical characterization and multiscale simulations indicate that COP–CA NPs form multisite interfacial associations with chitosan through hydrogen bonding, local electrostatic interactions, aromatic contact, and van der Waals forces, thereby limiting water absorption, swelling, and water migration within the film. After 14 days of storage, the 0.20% CS@NPs coating reduced the weight loss of cherry tomatoes from 14.75% to 6.89%, and better maintained fruit firmness and total soluble solids. The COP–CA carrier-free nanoassemblies can effectively enhance the water resistance, moisture barrier properties, and fruit preservation capacity of the chitosan coating. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Microwave-thermo-electrical energy recycling via thermally conductive absorbing network and entropy-amplified ionic thermoelectrics
abstract: Converting the ubiquitous microwave interference into electrical power allows simultaneous electromagnetic protection and energy harvesting, which is technologically important yet challenging for the ever-compacting electronic devices. Herein, a cascaded microwave-thermo-electric transducer (MW-iTE) has been designed with enhanced electromagnetic attenuation and amplified thermoelectric conversion. A thin and flexible FeCo/CoFe2O4@reduced graphene oxide/waterborne polyurethane sheet combines multiple electromagnetic loss mechanisms for microwave dissipation with a percolated conductive network that contributes to the conductive loss while delivering the generated heat to the thermoelectric layer. A polyethylene glycol (PEG)-regulated poly(vinyl alcohol)/I−/I3− hydrogel strengthens n-type thermopower by enlarging the redox-entropy difference through PEG-I3− coordination and by constructing hydrogen-bonded hydrated ion-transport channels. Series connection with a p-type gelatin hydrogel further amplifies the thermovoltage under a limited temperature gradient. The resulting MW-iTE exhibits an architecture-level thermopower of 77.86 mV K−1 and delivers a reversible voltage of 0.30 V under 17.9 GHz irradiation at 0.625 W cm−2. By converting intercepted microwave radiation into an electrical signal, this work establishes an efficient energy-recycling paradigm for self-powered microwave monitoring and energy harvesting. © 2026

title: Dynamic performance enhancement of a three-phase interleaved resonant boost MMC using adaptive disturbance compensation
abstract: Offshore wind energy is emerging as a critical renewable energy source. For the three-phase interleaved resonant boost MMC considered in this study, load variations, input-voltage fluctuations, and modeling uncertainties may degrade output-voltage regulation performance. To improve the transient response and disturbance-rejection capability of the converter, a backstepping dynamic surface control strategy assisted by a Zernike neural-network-based adaptive compensator is proposed. First, a state-space model of the three-phase interleaved parallel MMC boost converter is established. Then, the Zernike neural network is employed to adaptively approximate the unknown load-dependent term in the output-voltage dynamics and generate an online compensation signal. with a compact basis-function structure compared with the conventional RBF neural network used for comparison. Meanwhile, DSC is incorporated into the backstepping framework to avoid the derivative explosion problem and reduce implementation complexity. Lyapunov analysis proves that all closed-loop signals are bounded and the tracking error is semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded. The inherent low-ripple and self-balancing characteristics of the topology are validated before the dynamic control performance is investigated. The proposed method achieves smaller overshoot and requires less execution time than the RBF-NN-assisted ABDSC under the adopted implementation settings. Therefore, the proposed strategy provides a preliminary methodological reference for improving the dynamic performance of MMC-based converters, with potential relevance to future offshore wind power HVDC applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: SHAPE OPTIMIZATION FOR PIECEWISE PARAMETER IDENTIFICATION IN INVERSE DIFFUSION PROBLEMS WITH A SINGLE BOUNDARY MEASUREMENT
abstract: This paper proposes a unified shape and coefficient optimization approach for inverse problems governed by diffusion equations. The associated forward problem is considered with a Robin boundary condition, physically motivated in diffuse optical tomography to model partial reflection of light at tissue boundaries. The main objective is the recovery of the piecewise-defined absorption coefficient together with its underlying interface from a single boundary measurement. To this end, a shape-based reconstruction approach is formulated in which the interface is introduced as a geometric unknown governing the piecewise structure of the absorption coefficient. While classical approaches rely on the Fréchet derivative with respect to spatially varying parameters, the Eulerian derivative with respect to the interface is additionally exploited. This leads to a unified framework for the simultaneous recovery of the coefficient and the geometry under the single-measurement setting. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, even for complex and non-convex interfaces. © 2026, American Institute of Mathematical Sciences. .

title: Nanoprecipitate assisting HCP→FCC phase transformation in Zircaloy-4 alloy under multiple micro-indentation loading conditions
abstract: Stress-induced HCP→FCC phase transformation in zirconium has been well documented, yet its activation by secondary phase particles (SPPs) remains underexplored. Here, we report that Zr2Fe SPPs can promote this phase transformation in a Zr-4 alloy under micro-indentation loading. Specifically, the applied stress stimulates extensive {101‾0}<12‾10> dislocation slip in the Zr matrix. These dislocations interact with the reinforced Zr2Fe SPPs, which barely deform plastically at room temperature, thereby generating localized stress concentrations at the SPP/matrix interface. Due to specific crystallographic orientation and rod-shaped morphology of the SPPs, the stress concentration is lower along the lateral (long-axis) interfaces but significantly higher at the two ends. This stress disparity accounts for the distinct shell structures around the SPPs: the ends preferentially develop a P-type FCC-Zr phase, whereas the lateral interfaces are dominated by (0001) stacking faults without B-type FCC transformation. Our findings elucidate a novel mechanism by which SPPs assist local phase transformation to accommodate deformation stress. © 2026

title: Dual role of oxygen vacancies in Mn0.3Cd0.7S/WO3−x S-scheme heterojunctions for strengthening internal electric field and extending light harvesting toward efficient H2 evolution
abstract: S-scheme heterojunctions exhibit unique advantages in promoting charge separation while preserving the strong redox capability of photogenerated carriers, and their efficiency is strongly dependent on the interfacial internal electric field (IEF). Herein, we report an oxygen-vacancy engineering Mn0.3Cd0.7S/WO3−x (M/OV) S-scheme heterojunction for efficient photocatalytic H2 evolution. In this system, oxygen vacancies in WO3−x play dual roles. One is to modulate the electronic structure of tungsten oxide, thereby enlarging the Fermi level (EF) difference relative to Mn0.3Cd0.7S, and consequently strengthening the IEF to accelerate directional charge transfer. The other is to induce localized surface plasmon resonance, which broadens the light harvesting range of M/OV photocatalysts into the near-infrared (NIR) region for more efficient solar energy utilization. The synergistic effect endows the M/OV heterojunction with a H2 evolution rate of 1600 μmol g−1 h−1 under visible-NIR irradiation, which is 2.4 times as high as that of the Mn0.3Cd0.7S/WO3 counterpart derived from air-calcined WO3−x. This work provides an effective strategy for boosting photocatalytic H2 evolution through defect-induced EF engineering and IEF regulation toward solar-to-chemical energy conversion. © 2026

title: A SIMPLE RANGE CHARACTERIZATION FOR SPHERICAL MEAN TRANSFORM IN ODD DIMENSIONS AND ITS APPLICATIONS
abstract: This article provides a novel and simple range description for the spherical mean transform of functions supported in the unit ball of an odd dimensional Euclidean space. The new description comprises of a set of symmetry relations between the values of certain differential operators acting on the coefficients of the spherical harmonics expansion of the function in the range of the transform. As a central part of the proof of our main result, we derive a remarkable cross product identity for the spherical Bessel functions of the first and second kind, which may be of independent interest in the theory of special functions. Finally, as one application of the range characterization, we construct an explicit counterexample proving that unique continuation type results cannot hold for the spherical mean transform in odd dimensional spaces. © 2026, American Institute of Mathematical Sciences. .

title: Strain partitioning and recrystallization suppression via intralamellar β0 precipitates in a β-solidified γ-TiAl alloy during hot deformation
abstract: The β0 phase is an important phase in TiAl alloys, and its influence on the hot deformation behavior warrants in-depth investigation. In this study, the hot deformation behavior of a heat-treated (HT) specimen, in which β0 precipitates are formed within the (α2/γ) lamellae, is compared with that of an as-cast specimen free of such intralamellar precipitates. The results show that the HT specimens exhibit a lower peak stress and a slightly decreased work-hardening rate compared to the as-cast specimens, indicating that the intralamellar β0 (IL-β0) precipitates can moderately improve the hot workability of the TiAl alloy. After deformation, a high density of γ twins is formed in the lamellar colonies of both specimens; however, the twin density within the lamellae of HT specimens is distinctly lower than that of the as-cast microstructure. Furthermore, twin pairs are clearly identified in the HT specimen, whose formation arises from the propagation and traversal of twins across γ/γ interfaces generated via the α2 → γ phase transformation. Such effects are proposed to stem from the fact that the IL-β0 precipitates in the HT specimens undergo intrinsic plastic deformation and effectively mediate strain partitioning between adjacent α2 and γ lamellae. This interphase coordination is considered to be responsible for: (i) reduced twin density in the γ lamellae, (ii) the alleviated stress concentration within the α2/γ colonies, and (iii) the delayed recrystallization of the γ lamellae. Collectively, elucidating the role of IL‑β0 precipitates in modulating hot‑deformation behavior and lamellar recrystallization provides valuable insights for the rational optimization of thermomechanical processing of TiAl alloys. © 2026

title: Preference-guided graph reinforcement learning for multi-objective quality-aware hybrid flow shop scheduling with multilevel assembly
abstract: Product quality is crucial to the competitiveness of manufacturing enterprises. However, existing quality-aware scheduling studies mainly approximate product quality evolution using indirect factors such as processing time, making it difficult to characterize the integrated effects of equipment health conditions and operation precedence relationships on product quality. To address this issue, a quality-aware hybrid flow shop scheduling problem with multilevel assembly (QHFSP-MA) is formulated by incorporating multilevel assembly processes and processing-assembly quality propagation mechanisms of complex precision products. Due to the large solution space and multi-objective characteristics of QHFSP-MA, existing multi-objective reinforcement learning methods still struggle to obtain high-quality Pareto fronts. Therefore, a preference-guided graph reinforcement learning framework (PGRL) is proposed. A heterogeneous graph is first constructed to represent the processing-assembly system. Then, a preference-guided meta-relation heterogeneous graph neural network is developed to dynamically adjust the importance of different meta-relations according to objective preferences, enabling generalized policy learning under diverse preferences. Furthermore, an adaptive preference weight mechanism (APWM) is designed to reduce the mismatch between uniform preference sampling and irregular Pareto front distributions, thereby improving Pareto front approximation. Experimental results demonstrate that PGRL outperforms dispatching rules, metaheuristic algorithms, and two advanced multi-objective deep reinforcement learning methods in terms of optimization performance, generalization, and computational efficiency. An automotive engine manufacturing case further validates its practical effectiveness, reducing makespan, quality loss cost, and maintenance cost by 27.3%, 25.7%, and 8.8%, respectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Cooling-controlled microstructure engineering for mechanical–magnetic synergy in high-strength non-oriented silicon steel
abstract: Developing non-oriented silicon steels with both high mechanical strength and low iron loss is critical for high-speed drive motors, yet remains challenging because conventional strengthening strategies often deteriorate magnetic performance. Herein, post-annealing cooling is employed as a kinetic control parameter to regulate the retained Cu precipitation state and magnetic domain structure without introducing a separate aging treatment. Rapid cooling retained a high density of fine, coherent B2-type Cu-rich clusters and BCC Cu nanoprecipitates by suppressing diffusion-mediated coarsening and structural transformation, whereas slower cooling promoted precipitate growth and evolution toward coarse incoherent 9R Cu precipitates. Combined density functional theory calculations and three-dimensional micromagnetic simulations indicate that fine coherent Cu-rich precipitates provide effective precipitation strengthening while causing relatively weak perturbation of local magnetization. Meanwhile, rapid cooling refined the magnetic domain width and reduced iron loss by approximately 24%, although a slight decrease in magnetic induction occurred because of the intensified γ-fiber texture. These results demonstrate that post-annealing cooling provides an effective kinetic pathway for coordinating precipitation strengthening, magnetic domain refinement, and texture evolution in high-strength non-oriented silicon steels. © 2026

title: Engineered pyridinic-N-rich COFs drive an adsorption–reduction cascade for macroscopic gold recovery from e-waste leachates
abstract: Gold recovery from electronic waste (e-waste) offers a sustainable solution to resource scarcity. However, integrating selective Au(III) capture, interfacial reduction, and efficient product recovery within a single functional platform remains challenging. Herein, we report a pyridinic-N-rich covalent organic framework (BTTPA-Bpy-COF) for selective gold recovery from e-waste leachates through an adsorption–reduction cascade. The integrated bipyridine/pyridine–imine motifs enable rapid [AuCl4]− capture through cooperative electrostatic and coordination interactions. Concurrently, the electron-rich π-conjugated COF framework promotes electron transfer to the coordinated Au species, facilitating the reduction of Au(III) to Au(0). The resultant BTTPA-Bpy-COF exhibits rapid Au(III) adsorption kinetics and a maximum experimentally measured extraction capacity of 4655.95 mg g−1 under optimized conditions (1000 mg L−1 Au(III), pH 4, and 65 °C). Under mild thermal and mechanical stimulation, the in situ generated Au nanoparticles undergo aggregation and subsequent liberation from the COF scaffold, enabling physical isolation of an Au-rich fraction, followed by thermal purification to obtain metallic gold. Processing BTTPA-Bpy-COF into membrane and aerogel architectures further improves its processability and recoverability by enabling easier separation and reuse of the material compared with its powder form. This work offers a new strategy for integrating gold capture and recovery in COF platforms. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Impact of Unauthorized Vehicles on Road Safety Using Machine Learning in Bangladesh
abstract: The rising number of unauthorized vehicles in rural Bangladesh has led to an alarming increase in road accidents, particularly on rural highways. Despite a significant body of research on road safety in developed countries, limited studies have focused on road safety in Bangladesh, especially concerning unauthorized vehicles. This study applies machine learning to analyze road traffic accidents involving unauthorized vehicles using data collected between 2018 and June 2023 from high-risk regions in Bangladesh, including Pabna and Sirajganj. A total of 72 accidents were examined and classified into head-on, rear-end, and pedestrian-related collisions. The traffic accident data was categorized into four distinct classes based on their causes: overspeeding, overtaking, reckless driving, and unknown causes. A total of 179 accidents were reported during the study period, with unauthorized vehicles contributing to 41.00% of the total incidents. Among the machine learning models tested, the CatBoost Classifier achieved the highest accuracy of 89%, with strong performance metrics, including an F1-score of 0.8457. The study also incorporated SHAP values to identify key predictors of accident severity, with vehicle type, weather conditions, and driver behavior being the most influential factors. Head-on collisions were the most frequent accident type, with auto vans accounting for 22.2% of cases. Reckless driving was the leading cause, primarily affecting individuals aged 25–44 years. Unauthorized vehicles, particularly auto vans, CNGs, and motorcycles, were involved in most incidents, with the Pabna-Natore corridor accounting for 56.5% of cases. These results highlight the critical role of unauthorized vehicles in traffic-related fatalities and underline the urgent need for stricter enforcement of regulations. This research provides valuable insights into the role of unauthorized vehicles in road safety and offers actionable recommendations for policymakers to reduce accidents and fatalities. The findings emphasize the need for improved legislative frameworks and better road infrastructure to enhance road safety in rural Bangladesh. © 2027 The author(s). title: Integration of the online river water quality monitoring management framework based on inclusive governance
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Online river water quality monitoring systems are increasingly used to support pollution control. Nonetheless, the efficacy of these systems remains constrained by key technical and organizational challenges, namely high data variability, sensor instability, restricted interoperability, and decentralized institutional governance. These challenges reduce the trustworthiness of online data for evidence-based pollution control policy and decision-making. The study objectives were to develop an integrated framework to improve data quality, system performance, and coordination in the governance of online river water quality monitoring river water quality monitoring in watersheds across Indonesia. METHODS: A transdisciplinary methodological approach was applied by combining 1) Integrated data quality management to assess data completeness, accuracy, validity span and stability; 2) Key performance indicators measured by the analytical hierarchy process to evaluate the performance of online river water quality monitoring systems; and 3) Soft systems methodology to build a governance-oriented conceptual model through rich descriptions, root definitions, conceptual models and evaluation of the 3Es (efficacy, efficiency and effectiveness). This study analyzed environmental data collected between 2023 and 2025 from four monitoring stations representing the upstream and downstream reaches of the Ciliwung and Cisadane Rivers. To complement these quantitative findings, semi-structured interviews were conducted with a broad range of stakeholders, including government agencies, vendors, academics, researchers, the media, community-based non-governmental organizations, and local communities residing near the four stations. FINDINGS: An analysis of data quality demonstrated robust completeness (99–100 percent), highly variable non-zero completeness across all stations, high validity across the range for dissolved oxygen, hydrogen potential, and temperature (greater than 95 percent), and large fluctuations in stability at stations affected by tidal and sediment dynamics. The system performance index was 61.18 percent. Synthesizing soft systems methodology highlighted key operational barriers, such as fragmented roles, low trust towards online data, and lack of community participation. Consequently, this study developed an online river water quality monitoring management framework designed to prioritize digital interoperability, transparency, accountability, and multi-stakeholder governance. CONCLUSION: The inclusive governance-based online river water quality monitoring framework provides an empirically informed conceptual framework for organizing data-quality, performance, and governance improvements, improved collaboration among government agencies. Subject to contextual adaptation and prospective validation, this framework offers valuable insights for management design in other watersheds, ultimately contributing to the advancement of digital environmental governance in developing nations. ©2026 The author(s). title: Formation mechanisms of a nanocrystalline-amorphous hybrid interface in Al-Cu impact welding
abstract: This study systematically investigates the interfacial evolution mechanisms of Al-Cu joints fabricated by electromagnetic pulse welding. Transmission electron microscope (TEM) analyses reveal a gradient-refined interface comprising three distinct regions: central impact zone characterized by a nanocrystalline-amorphous structure, impact-affected zone with sub-micron grain refinement, and non-impacted zone showing only minor lattice distortion. The central impact zone contains a ∼1.3 µm transition layer exhibiting an “amorphous sea-nanocrystalline islands” structure composed of amorphous regions, Al2Cu nanocrystals, and residual Al/Cu nanograins. A phenomenological ΔC–Rc framework is proposed to describe the competition among compositional driving force, deformation-induced disordering, and kinetic arrest, in which high compositional gradients favor Al2Cu nucleation while rapid cooling restricts subsequent grain growth. The amorphous phase is attributed predominantly to deformation-induced solid-state amorphization, as supported by its heterogeneous morphology, the limited liquid-state diffusion length, and intense shear-driven atomic mixing. Molecular dynamics simulations further reveal a strong velocity dependence: An intermediate velocity of 500 m/s produces coexisting ordered and disordered structures consistent with experimental observations, whereas 2000 m/s velocity produces predominantly disordered configurations. Semi-quantitative high-resolution TEM/ inverse fast Fourier transform analyses also yield local dislocation-density estimates on the order of 1016 m−2 in highly deformed regions, demonstrating substantial defect accumulation during impact. These findings establish a coupled mechanism linking deformation, atomic mixing, and phase evolution in non-equilibrium Al-Cu interfaces and provide insights into controlling nanocrystalline-amorphous structures in high-velocity impact welding. © 2026

title: Descriptor-based plasma-regulated ultrafine high-entropy alloy supported on vertically aligned carbon nanotubes with enhanced bifunctional catalytic performance for excellent direct methanol fuel cell
abstract: This work proposes an efficient strategy for screening high-entropy-alloy (HEA) dopants using atomic radius and electronegativity as principal criteria. Multi-metal precursors, screened via descriptor-based methods and density-functional-theory calculations, are reduced using low-temperature radio-frequency plasma technology to obtain defect-rich PtFeCoNiCu HEAs anchored on vertically aligned-carbon nanotubes (P-PtFeCoNiCu@VACNTs@CC). The synergistic effects of the ordered HEA structure, plasma defect-engineering, electronic-structure modulation, and the vertically aligned-carbon nanotubes (VACNTs) significantly enhanced the electrocatalytic performance and stability of P-PtFeCoNiCu@VACNTs@CC for both the methanol-oxidation-reaction (MOR) and oxygen-reduction-reaction (ORR). Electrochemical analyses reveal that the P-PtFeCoNiCu@VACNTs@CC delivers outstanding bifunctional activity, attaining a peak-current-density of 2.44 ± 0.067 A mg−1Pt at 0.93 V for MOR (0.5 M H2SO4 + 0.5 M CH3OH) and a half-wave potential (E1/2) of 0.761 ± 0.006 V for ORR (0.5 M H2SO4). The enhanced performance can be attributed to three factors: the high-entropy characteristics, lattice distortion, sluggish diffusion, and cocktail effect inherent to HEAs; the enlarged specific surface area enabled by three-dimensionally oriented CNT architectures; and the optimized D-band center of Pt together with improved intermediate adsorption achieved via plasma defect-engineering coupled with electronic-modulation. This work presents a novel strategy for efficient screening and fabrication of high-performance HEA based electrodes and highlights promising applications in direct methanol fuel cells. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Ergodicity for a Constantin-Lax-Majda-DeGregorio model of turbulent flow at large viscosity
abstract: This paper presents a mathematical analysis of a stochastic generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda-DeGregorio (gCLMG) equation. We focus on the specific case where the nonlinearity in the equation allows an inviscid conserved quantity, i.e., the squared norm of model vorticity. The existence of an invariant measure is proved via the classical Krylov-Bogoliubov argument. The uniqueness of the measure and exponential mixing are proved under a sufficiently large viscosity condition, in which the nonlocal structure of the nonlinear term becomes manifest. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Mg single crystal microscopic fracture mechanism governed by twin-mediated synergistic non-basal slip
abstract: The activation of non-basal slip can retard crack propagation during the fracture process of Mg. As a vital deformation mechanism, twinning reorients crystal lattices into favourable orientations for activating various non-basal slip systems, thereby accommodating abundant c-axis strain. In this work, pre-twins were introduced into pure Mg single crystals via compression perpendicular to the c-axis. Both untwinned and pre-twinned specimens were subjected to uniaxial c-axis compression until fracture, aiming to uncover the microscale fracture mechanism governed by twin-mediated synergistic multi-slip activity. The experimental results reveal that pre-twinning reduces the critical resolved shear stress ratio of non-basal slip to basal slip, simultaneously improving the formability of Mg single crystals. Three dominant slip modes give rise to distinct microstructural morphologies and fracture characteristics: Prismatic 〈a〉 slip generates sparse discrete dislocations and isolated dislocation loops, resulting in severe lattice distortion and localised stress concentration, with only discontinuous dynamic recrystallisation (DDRX) formed near fracture sites. Pyramidal 〈a〉 slip triggers extensive dislocation dissociation and abundant stacking faults, leading to the coexistence of continuous dynamic recrystallisation and DDRX within fractured regions. For pyramidal 〈c+a〉 cross-slip activated concurrently with detwinning, mutual dislocation annihilation eliminates lattice distortion and localised stress peaks, transforming the fracture mode from brittle failure to ductile fracture dominated by uniform equiaxed dimples. This study provides insights into the multi-scale regulation mechanism of various slip systems on c-axis deformability in pre-twinned Mg alloys during fracture, and offers theoretical support for optimising the formability of Mg through pre-twinning. © 2026

title: Satellite-based assessment of high Andean wetlands and carbon sequestration under the influence of climate change
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: High-Andean wetlands play an important role in providing ecosystem services, particularly carbon sequestration. Yet, anthropogenic climate change threatens to restrict their spatial footprint and curtail their overall efficacy as atmospheric carbon sinks. Therefore, the study objectives were to estimate carbon uptake in High-Andean wetlands using satellite imagery and to evaluate its relationship with climatic variables in the Huancané Basin, Peru. METHODS: Google Earth Engine and RStudio integrated development environment (v4.3.1) were used with JavaScript and R programming languages. Wetland extents were delineated across seasonal wet and dry phases via Linear Spectral Unmixing applied to Landsat 5–8 imagery. Subsequent to the conversion of digital numbers to surface reflectance, the wetland index was implemented to estimate carbon uptake using moderate resolution imaging spectroradiometer gross primary productivity and net primary productivity datasets. Climate data were obtained from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration power platform, and the relationships between wetland extent, carbon dioxide sequestration, and climatic variables were analyzed. FINDINGS: Wetland coverage declined across both seasons over the study duration, experiencing contractions of 109.43 square kilometers during the wet season and 85.60 square kilometers during the dry season between 2010 and 2022. Carbon uptake also showed a decreasing trend during both seasons. Values ranged from 9.985 to 28.234 kilograms of carbon per square meter during the wet season and from 7.091 to 19.103 kilograms of carbon per square meter during the dry season. Significant relationships were found between wetland extent, carbon uptake, and climatic variables (p<0.05). Arid climatic trends, characterized by diminished precipitation, elevated temperature ranges, lower relative humidity, and increased wind speeds, corresponded closely with contractions in wetland extent and reduced carbon uptake. CONCLUSION: The results indicate that recent climatic changes have contributed to the degradation of high-Andean wetlands and to a reduction in their carbon uptake capacity in the Huancané Basin. These results provide vital baselines for tracking wetland trajectories, informing climate change mitigation and conservation frameworks to guide future ecosystem management and sustainable planning in fragile mountain regions worldwide. title: Assessment of asphalt pavement segregation under varying construction conditions via multi-scale 3D texture analysis
abstract: Asphalt pavement segregation, characterized by non-uniform aggregate distribution, detrimentally impacts pavement performance and service life. Conventional two-dimensional (2D) image-based approaches are limited in quantifying three-dimensional (3D) texture geometry and multi-scale features, with environmental factors introducing evaluation uncertainties. This study proposes a framework to quantify segregation by decomposing it into two morphological types: surface aggregate clustering (assessed via 2D-entropy coefficient of variation for planar uniformity) and vertical stratification (evaluated using coarse-to-fine aggregate ratio derived from multi-scale relative energy for gradation deviation). By leveraging 3D laser scanning and 2D wavelet decomposition across nine scales, this research investigates five asphalt mixtures (AC-13, AC-16, AC-25, OGFC-13, SMA-13) under varying temperatures (95–165 °C) and compaction passes (12–24). Results reveal that temperature influences fine aggregate surface uniformity in dense-graded mixtures, while compaction enhances uniformity in SMA-13. Vertical segregation in dense-graded mixtures decreases with elevated temperatures, unaffected by compaction intensity. The study provides new perspectives and methods for assessing asphalt pavement segregation in pavement construction quality control scenarios. Copyright © 2026. Publishing services by Elsevier B.V.

title: Modulating excited-state dynamics in RhB@Cd-MOF composites: spectroscopic elucidation of PET-driven quenching and ACQ- suppressed radiative enhancement for differential fluorescence sensing
abstract: Tuning host–guest interactions in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provides a powerful strategy for regulating the photophysical pathways of encapsulated chromophores. Herein, a dual- emissive composite (RhB@ 1 ) was constructed by encapsulating rhodamine B (RhB) within a Cd-MOF ( 1 ). Under 350 nm excitation, RhB@ 1 exhibits two well-resolved emission bands at 433 nm (MOF host) and 585 nm (RhB guest) via efficient host-to-guest energy transfer, enabling a rare differential fluorescence behavior: a selective “turn-off” response to Fe3+ and a distinctive “turn-on” response to o-nitrobenzaldehyde (o-NBA). Time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy reveals that the fluorescence lifetime decreases from 2.22 ns to 1.68 ns upon Fe3+ addition, confirming dynamic quenching through a photoinduced electron transfer (PET) pathway, while Stern-Volmer analysis further supports this mechanism. In stark contrast, the turn-on effect for o- NBA is attributed to the suppression of aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) via supramolecular rigidification of RhB molecules, which restricts intramolecular rotation and enhances radiative decay. The composite also demonstrates outstanding photostability and recyclability, benefiting from efficient host-to-guest energy transfer. The practicality of the method was verified by visual detection of Fe3+ using test strips, Fe3+ recovery by standard addition in Yanhe River water, and o-NBA recovery by standard addition in tap water. Overall, this work not only provides a dual-responsive sensing platform but also offers direct spectroscopic evidence for how MOF nanoconfinement dictates the excited-state dynamics of guest dyes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Steric hindrance engineered through-space conjugation for the emission wavelength control of organic room-temperature phosphorescence
abstract: Owing to the structural diversity and excellent biocompatibility, single component organic room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials have intrigued considerable interest in the past two decades. However, compared with the high quantum yield and ultra long lifetime, which have been consistent focus of attention, the emission wavelength, as an important property of organic RTP, has not received sufficient attention and thus lacks relevant theoretical research, although the application of RTP materials highly depends on their emission wavelength. While the steric hindrance effect is the core theoretical foundations of organic chemistry and is crucial for solving various problems, to the best of our knowledge, there have been no reports on utilizing steric hindrance to regulate the emission wavelength of RTP. In this work, by ingeniously introducing different steric hindrance groups to diphenylmethylamine derivatives which could regulate the degree of through-space conjugation (TSC), the emission wavelength of RTP was engineered. As the steric hindrance increased, the rotation of the two benzene rings was restricted, thereby rigidifying the molecular skeletons and effectively promoting TSC. Efficient TSC not only stabilized the triplets and produced high performance of RTP, but also promoted the gradual redshift of the emission wavelength from blue (463 nm) to green (556 nm). © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Modulating localized microenvironments via construction of CoS/CN heterojunction to strengthen hydroxyl adsorption for efficient 5-hydroxymethylfurfural electrooxidation
abstract: Electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) provides an efficient route for the production of value-added chemicals. However, the slow oxidation of the hydroxyl groups in the HMF molecule limits the reaction rate. Herein, a CoS/CN with a p-n heterojunction structure was designed and successfully synthesized. Among the prepared samples, the optimal current density of CoS/CN-4 is 2.5 times that of CoS at 1.47 V vs. RHE. Machine learning (ML) was used to optimize the experimental parameters (coulombs, potential, and stirring rate) to achieve nearly 100% of 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) yield and Faradaic efficiency (FE), and FDCA yield remained above 95% after 25 cycles. Ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) combined with theoretical calculations indicates that the superior performance is attributed to the redistribution of interface charges, forming positively charged CN centers, which enhance the adsorption ability for electron-withdrawing hydroxyl functional groups. Different from CoS with 5-hydroxymethyl-2-furanic acid (HMFCA) pathway to produce FDCA, CoS/CN with 2,5-diformylfuran (DFF) pathway exhibits a faster HMF oxidation rate. Finally, 72% yield of higher-value product named 5-formyl-2-furancarboxylic acid (FFCA) was achieved by tuning the base concentration, outperforming most previously reported electrocatalysts. This work provides important theoretical and experimental insights for rationally modulating HMF adsorption behavior to alter the reaction pathway and accelerate biomass conversion. © 2026

title: Detection of Unmarked Non-Metallic Underground Pipelines Using Fine-Grained Strontium Ferrite-Based Powders
abstract: An obvious global trend is the spread of plastic pipelines in the construction and repair of underground utilities, including gas distribution pipelines. Despite the advantages of non-metallic pipes, their use is associated with a number of specific problems characteristic of plastic materials. One of such significant problems facing the gas industry is the problem of detecting underground non-metallic utilities and selectively identifying them from adjacent facilities. Pipelines not linked to the global coordinate system in a timely manner can lead to significant economic costs in case of abnormal situations during construction and installation works. The paper investigates an original method of searching for non-metallic utilities associated with the introduction of magnetic powder into the gas flow. It is shown that in the case of the site location in the urban area it is a low-information and ambiguous method. On the contrary, in the open area, in the absence of third-party ferromagnetic interference, this method is not only potentially applicable, but deserves close attention and further research, for which the appropriate design of the test site is proposed. Potential application of the method will increase the informative value of data on the underground location of non-metallic pipelines by 15% for gas distribution pipelines of various diameters, considering the achievement of a magnetic induction level above the pipeline in the range of 60-120 nT. © 2027 The author(s). title: Local ultraconvergence of post-processed finite volume element solutions over quadrilateral meshes for elliptic problems
abstract: This paper establishes, for the first time, the local ultraconvergence properties of post-processed high-order finite volume element methods (FVEM) for second-order elliptic problems with constant coefficients. We introduce two Richardson-type extrapolation operators-originally developed in the finite element context-and apply them to post-process both the FVEM solution and its gradient on quadrilateral meshes of degree k ≥ 1. We rigorously prove that the post-processed solution and gradient attain 2kth order convergence, up to a logarithmic factor, at interior nodes. In particular, this work provides the first theoretical proof that the FVEM gradient exhibits kth order ultraconvergence, up to a logarithmic factor, a phenomenon previously unknown in the FVEM framework. A new analytical approach is developed to overcome the lack of Galerkin orthogonality, and numerical experiments confirm the sharpness and generality of the theoretical results. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Effect of sintering aids on densification and microstructure of pressureless-sintered tantalum carbide coatings
abstract: Tantalum carbide coatings protect graphite during SiC crystal growth, but pressureless sintering often gives poor densification and residual impurities. This work compares cobalt, silicon, and tantalum sintering aids. Cobalt aids enable liquid‑phase sintering but leave Co residues (~350 ppm), yielding moderate hardness and corrosion resistance. Silicon aids form a liquid but react with TaC or carbon, generating carbides or gases that create pores. Among tantalum aids, Ta metal shows limited solid‑state effect, while Ta₂O₅ melts above 1850°C. Via coupled carbothermal reduction‑liquid spreading, pressureless sintering at 2000°C produces a fully dense, pore‑free, coarse‑grained (~22.15 μm) high‑purity TaC coating. Hardness is 10.4 GPa, better acid corrosion resistance than CVD or Co‑aided coatings, no foreign impurities. These results show a liquid phase is necessary but insufficient; dissolution‑precipitation of TaC in the liquid aid is key. This work provides a theoretical basis for preparing dense high‑purity TaC coatings via a simple pressureless route. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Crystallization of lithium aluminosilicate glass into low thermal expansion glass-ceramics by Ultrafast High-temperature Treatment
abstract: We employed an Ultrafast High-temperature Treatment (UHT) to crystallize monolithic lithium aluminosilicate (LAS) glass pieces with variable holding time and electric power level under controlled power ramp. Phase evolution was analyzed by X-ray diffraction, revealing the formation of high-quartz solid solution (HQSS) at lower power levels and an increasing amount of β-spodumene with increasing power. Scanning electron microscopy revealed the development of large crystalline domains and growth-related microstructural features, consistent with extensive crystal growth during processing. Dilatometric measurements of the resulting glass-ceramics show that selected UHT conditions allow them to reach near-zero thermal expansion coefficients, on the order of ±0.1 ppm/°C. These results demonstrate that UHT offers a time- and energy-efficient route to produce low-thermal-expansion LAS glass-ceramics within seconds. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Damage-tolerant Cu/Cu2TiAl heterostructure enabled by Al-modified interlayer design for Ti6Al4V/CoCrFeNi dissimilar metals
abstract: Additive manufacturing of Ti6Al4V/CoCrFeNi dissimilar metals is fundamentally limited by the strong chemical affinity of Ti with Fe, Co, and Ni, which causes brittle intermetallic compounds and severe interfacial cracking. Although ductile Cu interlayers with favorable metallurgical compatibility improve interfacial bonding, the formation of continuous Cu-Ti intermetallic compounds may still degrade interfacial integrity and trigger premature failure. An Al-modified Cu interlayer strategy is developed to regulate interfacial reactions during laser-directed energy deposition. The addition of Al redirects interfacial phase evolution from multiple continuous Cu-Ti binary compounds to a Cu/Cu2TiAl networked heterostructure, reducing lattice mismatch and improving metallurgical bonding with suppressed interfacial cracking. Unexpectedly, the continuous Cu-rich network promotes plastic accommodation and suppresses local stress concentration. Consequently, the interfacial shear strength of the interlayer/CoCrFeNi interface increases from 185.1 to 321.7 MPa, representing a 73.8% improvement. This work establishes a composition-mediated pathway for interfacial compound formation to convert deleterious intermetallic formation into mechanically compatible heterostructures, offering insights into interlayer design for additive joining of Ti-based dissimilar metals with severe metallurgical incompatibility. © 2026

title: Engineering dual-network oleogels based on OSA starch/chitosan complexes for enhanced astaxanthin stability: Effects of beeswax and β-sitosterol crystal networks
abstract: To improve the stability of emulsion-templated oleogels and enhance astaxanthin protection, dual-network oleogels based on OSA starch/chitosan complexes (OS/CS) were fabricated by incorporating crystalline networks formed by beeswax or β-sitosterol. The effects of different crystalline networks on the microstructure, stability, and astaxanthin retention of OS/CS oleogels were systematically investigated. The incorporation of both crystalline networks significantly (p < 0.05) enhanced the oil-binding capacity of OS/CS oleogels under various processing and storage conditions, with beeswax exhibiting the most pronounced improvement. After storage at 25 °C for 56 days, astaxanthin degradation was observed in all oleogel samples; however, the OS/CS oleogels containing 6% beeswax or β-sitosterol showed relatively lower astaxanthin degradation of 19.32% and 21.05%, respectively. In vitro digestion revealed that astaxanthin bioaccessibility in the dual-network oleogels (23.92-43.04%) was higher than that of bulk oil (20.97%). Overall, beeswax exhibited superior synergistic effects in promoting the formation of a dense dual-network structure and enhancing the oil-binding capacity of OS/CS oleogels, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving oleogel stability and astaxanthin retention. title: Pyrolysis/non-thermal plasma/catalysis of waste plastics with bimetallic catalysts: Control of Brønsted and Lewis acid sites to improve production of BTEX aromatic hydrocarbons
abstract: Pyrolysis-catalysis of waste plastics is an endothermic process that suffers trade-offs between diffusion limitations and rapid catalyst deactivation due to catalyst coking. This study investigates a two-stage pyrolysis-plasma catalytic system that couples non-thermal dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) with engineered mono- and bimetallic (Ga, Ti, W) modified β-zeolite catalysts to produce high-value benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylenes (BTEX) from waste plastic (polypropylene). A quantitative reaction engineering framework utilizing the Specific Energy Input (SEI), Hydrogen Index (HI), and Desirability Index (DI) is presented. Characterization techniques, including NH₃-TPD and Py/Lut-TGA, confirm that bimetallic configurations can successfully control the acidity of the catalyst. It is proposed that this creates a synergy between Brønsted sites—which drive the primary cracking of polypropylene pyrolysis products and extra-framework gallium Lewis acid sites, which are suggested to facilitate rapid dehydrogenation and aromatization. Bimetallic Ga-Ti-β-zeolite catalyst, operating at an optimal SEI of 48 kJ/g (40 W), achieves peak dehydrogenation efficiency (high HI) and > 90% selectivity for alkylated aromatic compounds (toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylenes). Furthermore, temperature programmed oxidation (TPO) of the used catalyst to characterize the coke deposition, showed that optimizing the SEI effectively suppresses graphitic carbon coke deposition. © 2026 The Authors

title: Ecological diversity in soil properties and bacterial communities in tropical coastal areas with contrasting electrical conductivity
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Coastal soil salinization is an environmental constraint that alters soil physicochemical conditions and may restructure microbial communities, while field patterns may also reflect land use and co-varying soil properties. The study objectives were to characterize soil physicochemical conditions together with bacterial diversity, composition, community dissimilarity, and predicted ecological functions at three tropical coastal sites in Palang, Tuban, East Java, with contrasting electrical conductivity. METHODS: Electrical conductivity at sampling sites PA8, PA9, and PA10 was 13.68, 3.74, and 0.50 decidiemens per meter, respectively. A single composite soil sample was collected and analyzed from each site and subjected to near full-length bacterial small-subunit ribosomal ribonucleic acid gene amplicon sequencing. Following quality filtering and denoising, amplicon sequence variants were resolved, and taxonomic assignments were performed against a curated ribosomal reference database. Observed richness, Shannon and Gini-Simpson indices, Bray-Curtis and Weighted UniFrac principal coordinate analyses, taxonomic relative abundance, and taxonomy-based predicted functions were summarized descriptively. Site-to-site variations in exchangeable sodium, organic carbon, cation exchange capacity, phosphorus availability, soil texture, and culturable bacterial abundance were also compared among sites. Due to the confounding of site identity, electrical conductivity, land use, and other edaphic properties, replicated inference of salinity effects was not feasible. FINDINGS: PA8 had 2,052 observed sequence variants and a Shannon index of 9.61; PA9 had 5,205 variants and a Shannon index of 11.39; and PA10 had 3,145 variants and a Shannon index of 11.03. Taxonomic profiles differed among sites. PA8 was characterized by Bacillota, Bacillales, and Incertae_Sedis_14; PA9 by Bacillota/Pseudomonadota, Bacillales, and Neobacillus; and PA10 by Chloroflexota, Anaerolineales, and UTCFX1. Weighted UniFrac distances were 0.3266 for PA9-PA10, 0.4850 for PA8-PA9, and 0.5226 for PA8-PA10. Predicted chemoheterotrophy accounted for 20.46 percent, 16.97 percent, and 23.88 percent of post-filter reads at sites PA8, PA9, and PA10, respectively. PA8 also had the highest exchangeable sodium, whereas PA10 had the highest organic carbon, cation exchange capacity, Olsen-available phosphorus, and culturable bacterial abundance. CONCLUSION: While intra-site analyses revealed marked heterogeneity in physicochemical parameters and bacterial community structures, the observational framework of this study limits direct causal attribution to salinity gradients and restricts the extrapolation of findings to wider salinity categories. The findings provide a site-specific environmental baseline and hypotheses for future replicated studies. title: Environmental modeling of yellowfin tuna fishing grounds integrating oceanographic and biological parameters using generalized additive model
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Marine environmental variability influences the distribution, productivity, and habitat suitability of yellowfin tuna (Thunnus albacares). However, fishing-ground assessment based primarily on environmental conditions or production may overlook the biological suitability of harvested fish. The study objectives were to develop an integrated generalized additive model framework for assessing yellowfin tuna fishing grounds. The framework combined oceanographic conditions and fishing operational factors with production potential and fish size through two complementary Generalized additive models. METHODS: The study was conducted in the waters of West Sumatra, eastern Indian Ocean, Indonesia. Fisheries and oceanographic data covered 2019–2024, while biological observations covered 2019, 2020, and 2024. Oceanographic predictors included sea surface temperature, chlorophyll-a concentration, sea surface salinity, and sea surface height. Fisheries predictors included fishing year, month, gear, spatial location, and vessel capacity. A total of 8,771 yellowfin tuna fork-length measurements were analyzed. A fork length of 99 centimeters was used as the maturity-based threshold. Two complementary generalized additive models were developed. The Fishing Ground–Environment, Technology, and Production model used catch as the production response. The Fishing Ground–Environment, Technology, and Size model used fork length as the biological response. FINDINGS: Sea surface temperature ranged from 29.37–30.45 degrees Celsius. Chlorophyll-a concentration ranged from 0.21–0.43 milligrams per cubic meter. Sea surface salinity ranged from 33.29–33.87 practical salinity units. Sea surface height ranged from 0.46–0.59 meters. Overall, 94 percent of fish were harvest-suitable. The production model had an Akaike information criterion of 155,482.9 and cumulative deviance explained of 11.5 percent. The size model had an Akaike information criterion of 77,913.73 and cumulative deviance explained of 28.74 percent. Medium to high fishing-ground potential occurred more frequently around the Mentawai Islands. Temporal integration identified highly potential and potential fishing-period statuses based on relative production potential and the landing-based biological size indicator. CONCLUSION: The integrated generalized additive model framework links environmental conditions, fishing operations, production, and biological size. This approach provides a more selective basis for adaptive and sustainable management of yellowfin tuna fisheries. title: A base-editing and auxotrophic selection platform for linking epigenetic regulators to silent biosynthetic gene clusters in Aspergillus nidulans
abstract: Filamentous fungi harbor numerous silent biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), representing an underexplored reservoir of natural products. Chemical inhibition of epigenetic regulators is an effective strategy for activating silent BGCs, but it often lacks specificity and cannot readily link activated clusters to their cognate regulators. Here, we developed a coupled cytosine base editing and auxotrophic selection platform in Aspergillus nidulans to systematically identify epigenetic regulators of silent gene clusters. An sgRNA library targeting 24 core epigenetic regulators was introduced, together with a cytosine base editor, into 21 pyrG -based PKS reporter strains, enabling growth-based selection and direct sgRNA recovery by Sanger sequencing. This screen identified five regulator-cluster activation pairs, including known interactions and two previously uncharacterized mechanisms. Specifically, KdmB represses the AN7084 gene cluster by erasing promoter H3K4me3, whereas Kmt5 silences the cichorine core pks gene through H4K20me3 deposition. This scalable platform enables rapid matching of silent BGCs with their epigenetic regulators and advances chromatin-guided fungal genome mining. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Identification and characterization of biofilm-degrading aptamers against Escherichia coli by Inhibition-SELEX and analysis of their target proteins and interactions
abstract: Escherichia coli is a common contaminant in food processing environments, and its biofilm formation can greatly enhance its tolerance to disinfectants and antibiotics, thereby posing a serious threat to food safety. In this study, we used Inhibition-Systematic Evolution of Ligands by Exponential Enrichment (SELEX) to screen and obtain three aptamers (D1, D2, and D3) that showed strong degrading effects against preformed E. coli biofilms. At 2 μM for 2 h, D1, D2, and D3 showed degradation rates of 70.80%, 72.40%, and 72.24%, respectively, against E. coli biofilms, whereas their degradation rates against the biofilms of non-target bacteria (Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Pseudomonas plecoglossicida, Vibrio alginolyticus, Vibrio harveyi, Vibrio anguillarum, Aeromonas hydrophila, and Nocardia salmonicida) were all <20%. In combination with tetracycline, the degradation rates against E. coli biofilms increased to 82.66%, 81.83%, and 84.03%, respectively. Structural analysis showed that D2 adopted a flat tertiary structure and exhibited very high flexibility and conformational variability. Through magnetic separation, sodium dodecyl sulfate–polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis, and mass spectrometry, the target proteins of D2 were identified as lysine-tRNA ligase (Lys-tRNAL) and outer membrane protein A (OmpA). Molecular docking analysis revealed that D2 interacted with Lys-tRNAL and OmpA through four binding sites each. At the binding site, D2 is likely to form hydrogen bonds or electrostatic interactions via the O atoms in its bases and the N, C, and S atoms of Leu, Met, Arg, and Met in the target protein, thereby affecting the structure and function of the target protein, disrupting the activity and biosynthesis of proteins involved in maintaining biofilm stability, and ultimately leading to rapid biofilm degradation. This study provides a new strategy for the prevention and control of E. coli biofilm contamination in food processing environments, and has practical guiding significance for ensuring food safety and reducing microbial contamination in food production. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: CEEMDAN-Based hybrid models for short-term power load forecasting
abstract: Short-term load forecasting is critical for maintaining grid stability and ensuring economic operation. Existing methods often struggle to capture both local short-term fluctuations and global trends, and conventional approaches exhibit limited flexibility and generalizability. This study proposes two Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN) based hybrid models: Temporal Convolutional Network–Attention-based Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (TCN-ABiLSTM) and Temporal Convolutional Network–Transformer–Gated Recurrent Unit (TCN-Transformer-GRU). These models integrate Intrinsic Mode Function (IMF) weighted attention and multi-period rolling training. Their performance is evaluated using multiple metrics. Experimental results indicate that CEEMDAN-TCN-Transformer-GRU reduces day-ahead RMSE by 39.37%, while CEEMDAN-TCN-ABiLSTM reduces month-ahead RMSE by 41.81%, significantly outperforming conventional and single-model approaches. © 2026
