title: Multiscale adaptive Kolmogorov-Arnold networks with cross-variable learning for short-term electricity price forecasting
abstract: With the transition of electricity markets toward low-carbon and market-oriented structures, the electricity price time series exhibits strong non-stationarity, multi-scale fluctuations, and complex nonlinear dynamics, which pose significant challenges for Electricity Price Forecasting (EPF). However, existing models often fail to completely capture these complex patterns. To address the limitations of current methods, we propose a Multiscale Adaptive Kolmogorov-Arnold Network with Cross-Variable Learning (MKAN-CL), which is combined with the Adaptive Lemming Algorithm (ALA) for automatic hyperparameter optimization. MKAN-CL integrates spectral decomposition with adaptive modeling to capture complex temporal dynamics in short-term electricity price series. Specifically, the method consists of four key components. First, a multi-lag cross-variable modeling mechanism is designed to capture cross-scale dependencies between electricity prices and exogenous variables. Then, hierarchical spectral decomposition is applied to separate non-stationary sequences into distinct frequency components. Subsequently, Chebyshev-based Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) are employed to perform adaptive nonlinear modeling across frequency bands. Moreover, the Adaptive Lemming Algorithm (ALA) is employed to automatically select key hyperparameters for the proposed model, reducing reliance on manual tuning. Finally, experiments on the Australian and Singapore electricity markets demonstrate the effectiveness of MKAN-CL. On the AEMO dataset, MKAN-CL reduces RMSE, MAE, and MAPE by 4.97%, 13.75%, and 12.95%, respectively, relative to the strongest baseline, CrossLinear. Overall, MKAN-CL provides an effective solution for short-term electricity price forecasting in complex environments and offers data-driven support for price volatility assessment and operational decision-making in renewable-integrated power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Study on the physicochemical properties and biocompatibility of proanthocyanidin cross-linked collagen hydrogels mediated by laccase
abstract: The discarding and low-value utilisation of by-products from silver carp processing caused serious environmental pollution and waste of resources. The study employed silver carp skin as the primary raw material in the fabrication of collagen hydrogels, focusing on the impact of laccase-mediated proanthocyanidin cross-linking on the physicochemical properties and biocompatibility of collagen hydrogels. This investigation is undertaken with a view to promoting the high-value utilisation of silver carp by-products. The results indicated that laccase-mediated proanthocyanidin cross-linking significantly improved the mechanical properties and thermal stability of collagen hydrogels. The maximum cross-linking degree of the laccase-mediated proanthocyanidin cross-linking (PL) group reached 81.26% nearly double that of the proanthocyanidin cross-linking (PA) group, while the maximum hardness was 6.02 N. It was evident that both the heat deflection temperature and the thermal degradation temperature had increased. Furthermore, the study findings demonstrated that proanthocyanidins primarily form hydrogen bonds through their phenolic hydroxyl groups with the carbonyl groups on proline residues in collagen. In contrast, the laccase-mediated cross-linking mechanism of proanthocyanidins involves a Michael addition reaction between the quinone groups and the amino groups in the collagen hydrogel, thereby achieving covalent cross-linking. The biocompatibility assays using NIH3T3 cells revealed that cross-linked hydrogel extracts were highly biocompatible and upgraded the expression of wound healing-related factors in fibroblasts. This study provided novel insights into the application of silver carp skin collagen in bio-based materials, thereby expanding avenues for the comprehensive utilisation of silver carp by-products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Optimization-based dynamic voltage support strategy for inverter-based resources in weak grid conditions: Design, analysis and validation
abstract: The growing penetration of inverter-based resources (IBRs) in modern power systems demands effective dynamic voltage support (DVS) strategies, especially during low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) events. This paper proposes an optimization-based DVS method that coordinates active and reactive power while ensuring synchronization stability and robustness against grid impedance uncertainty. The voltage support problem is formulated as a constrained optimization considering current limits and dc-side power availability. An analytical, real-time solution is derived through Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions applied to the nonconvex voltage maximization problem, yielding closed-form expressions for optimal active and reactive current references across three distinct operating regions determined by active constraint combinations. Simulation results under various balanced and unbalanced fault conditions show up to 95% improvement in voltage recovery and enhanced power delivery compared to droop, PI, MPC, and RL-based methods. The inverter dynamic model incorporates dual-sequence current control in the synchronous dq-reference frame with explicit dc-link voltage regulation, enabling coordinated LVRT response under both symmetrical and asymmetrical grid faults. The proposed strategy achieves near-optimal voltage support with low computational cost, making it suitable for real-time deployment in weak and renewable-rich grids. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Prismatic <c>-type dislocation-induced nanoscale ordered phase boundary engineering enables static–dynamic property synergy in high-oxygen titanium alloys
abstract: Achieving simultaneous static strength–ductility synergy and dynamic deformation stability remains a major challenge for multiphase structural alloys, largely because heterogeneous phase boundaries promote strain incompatibility and localization across loading regimes. Here, we develop chemically ordered phase boundary engineering (COPBE) to reconstruct α/β interfaces in a high-oxygen titanium alloy through dislocation-induced nanoscale oxygen ordering. Prismatic <c>-type dislocations generated at α/β interfaces are stabilized by ordered O configurations, forming a BCC/COPB/HCP interfacial architecture. Under quasi-static tension, COPBs redistribute interfacial stresses and promote coordinated dislocation transmission across α/β interfaces, sustaining work hardening and plastic accommodation while retaining ultrahigh strength. Under dynamic compression, oxygen redistribution from COPBs toward octahedral interstitial sites in the BCC phase provides an additional pathway for thermal and mechanical energy dissipation, thereby suppressing strain softening and delaying adiabatic shear localization. Consequently, Ti-5553-0.43O (wt.%) achieves a tensile strength of 1.9 GPa with 7.0% elongation, together with a dynamic compressive strength of ∼2.9 GPa and a fracture strain of 26.9%. These results demonstrate that COPBE couples interfacial chemical ordering, dislocation transport, and O configurational evolution to regulate deformation across strain rates, providing a general strategy for achieving static–dynamic mechanical synergy in multiphase metallic materials. © 2026

title: Architectural control of high-temperature creep and failure in additively manufactured superalloy metamaterials
abstract: Additively manufactured superalloy-based metamaterials offer a promising route toward lightweight structural components for extreme high-temperature applications, yet the mechanisms governing their creep deformation and failure remain largely unexplored. Traditionally, creep is viewed as an intrinsic material limitation governed by microstructural degradation. Here, we show that creep resistance in superalloy metamaterials is highly governed by architectural topology. By systematically comparing strut-based, plate-based, and TPMS architectures, we reveal pronounced architecture-dependent creep behavior under compressive loading at 650 °C. The plate-based lattice demonstrates the best creep resistance, exhibiting the lowest steady-state rate under identical applied stresses. While all architectures fail by macroscopic shear bands, high-resolution 3D tomography and atom-probe analysis reveal a cross-scale transition where failure initiates at stress-concentrated nodes and propagates via oxygen-assisted intergranular damage, even as the core (γ′/γ″) remains remarkably stable. This work highlights architectural control as an effective design principle for tailoring creep resistance in metallic metamaterials, providing a foundation for designing lightweight and reliable metallic components for high-temperature applications. © 2026

title: Breaking the limitations of ZnSe anodes: Boosting sodium-ion kinetics via electronic structure regulation and morphology design
abstract: Transition metal selenides have garnered considerable attention as promising anodes for sodium-ion batteries, yet their practical application is hindered by intrinsically low conductivity and sluggish conversion kinetics originating from strong metal-selenide bonds. Herein, we propose an innovative electronic structure modulation strategy to overcome these limitations by doping Cu into ZnSe particles anchored within a hierarchical porous N-doped carbon (NC). Experimental results and density functional theory calculations reveal that Cu doping induces charge redistribution, narrows the bandgap, and elongates the Zn-Se bond, thereby lowering the kinetic barrier for the conversion reaction. Moreover, the NC framework and Cu-induced morphological optimization accommodate volume expansion and promote electrolyte penetration, enhancing cycling stability. Kinetic analyses reveal a dominant pseudocapacitive contribution and reduced charge transfer impedance. Hence, the optimized Cu2-ZnSe@NC delivers exceptional rate capability (240.3 mAh g–1 at 30 A g–1) and outstanding cycling stability (389.5 mAh g–1 after 1000 cycles at 2 A g–1 with a capacity retention of 82.9%). In full-cell evaluation, the device maintains stable electrochemical performance across a broad temperature range from −20 to 25 °C, highlighting its potential for practical applications. This work establishes a structure-property paradigm in which heteroatom doping weakens metal-chalcogenide bonds, offering a generalizable design principle for high-performance conversion-type anodes. © 2026

title: Oxygen vacancy-rich Ce-substituted LaCoO3 perovskites for high-efficiency plasma-catalytic ammonia synthesis under ambient conditions
abstract: Ammonia synthesis under mild conditions using non-thermal plasma provides a promising route for decentralized and renewable-driven production. However, the rational design of catalysts that can simultaneously regulate plasma activation and surface reaction pathways remains challenging. Herein, a series of Ce-substituted La1-xCexCoO3 perovskite catalysts were developed for plasma-catalytic ammonia synthesis, and the role of A-site Ce engineering in modulating catalytic structures and plasma-catalyst interactions was systematically investigated. Moderate Ce incorporation reconstructed the surface Co-Ov interfacial sites through lattice distortion, oxygen vacancy generation, and electronic redistribution between Ce and Co species. The optimized Co-Ov sites exhibited enhanced electron-donating capability, promoting N2 adsorption and activation through electron transfer to the antibonding π* orbitals of N2. The increased weak acid sites facilitated NH3 desorption and suppressed plasma-induced NH3 decomposition. Excessive Ce substitution resulted in the segregation of CeO2 and Co3O4 phases, blocking accessible Co-Ov sites and deteriorating catalytic performance. Under an SEI of 40 kJ·L−1, the optimized La0.9Ce0.1 catalyst achieved an NH3 synthesis rate of 19.1 mmol·g−1·h−1 with an energy efficiency of 4.8 g-NH3·kWh−1, representing the most competitive performances reported for plasma-catalytic ammonia synthesis. In-situ DRIFTS, OES, and plasma discharge simulations further revealed that Ce engineering simultaneously regulated surface nitrogen intermediates and plasma-generated reactive species. This work establishes Co-Ov interfacial site engineering as an effective strategy for designing efficient plasma-catalytic ammonia synthesis catalysts. © 2026 The Authors

title: Prediction of lightning flashover on overhead distribution lines from preliminary breakdown voltages based on deep learning
abstract: Lightning strikes represent a major source of risk for power systems, particularly for overhead distribution lines, where indirect events can induce dangerous overvoltages through electromagnetic coupling. This work represents a first step towards the development of a predictive lightning protection system based on the detection of Preliminary Breakdown (PB) pulses, i.e., sequences of lower-intensity atmospheric discharges typically preceding the Return Stroke (RS) by several tens of milliseconds. Synthetic PB- and RS-induced voltage waveforms are generated using a dedicated simulation tool. Time-domain samples of PB-induced voltages from two sensors are used to train a Deep Learning (DL) model to predict the maximum RS-induced voltage and assess whether it may lead to a flashover event. The line Critical FlashOver Voltage (CFO), increased by 50%, is used as a threshold for classification between safe and dangerous conditions. The proposed model achieves promising performance, paving the way for further development of a preventive lightning protection system (to be combined with state-of-the-art methods) exploiting PB-induced voltage measurements. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Incorporating renewable reactive-power capability curves into multi-objective AC optimal power flow: a comparative assessment of cost, voltage performance, and reactive flexibility
abstract: In current power systems, the rising use of inverter-based renewable energy sources (RESs) is altering voltage control and reactive-power management. Although photovoltaic (PV) and wind generation units can provide substantial reactive-power support through their power-electronic interfaces, their actual reactive-power capabilities depend on operating conditions and are frequently overlooked or oversimplified in traditional optimal power flow (OPF) formulations. This paper presents a multi-objective AC-OPF framework that explicitly integrates renewable reactive-power capability curves into power-system operation studies. Seven representative capability-curve models are systematically compared within a common optimization framework. The proposed framework simultaneously minimizes generation operating cost, active-power losses, and voltage deviation while maximizing renewable reactive-power flexibility through a Reactive Flexibility Index (RFI). The approach is validated using a modified IEEE 30-bus system with three RESs. The results reveal that renewable reactive-power capability curves greatly influence operational cost, transmission losses, voltage performance, upward and downward renewable reactive-power reserves, and renewable reactive-power flexibility. The Constant Reactive-Power model attains the lowest operating cost and active-power losses, the Triangular model provides the lowest voltage deviation, and the Oversized-Inverter model offers the highest upward and downward renewable reactive-power reserves, the highest RFI, and the highest TOPSIS score. Parameter-sensitivity analysis further confirms the robustness of the principal capability-curve conclusions and demonstrates increasing reactive flexibility with inverter oversizing. These results highlight the importance of accurately representing renewable reactive-power capability when assessing the operational flexibility and voltage performance of renewable-integrated power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A domain-informed forecasting framework for short-horizon carbon emissions prediction in power plants under reduced-history conditions
abstract: Accurate short-horizon forecasting of CO₂ emissions from thermal power plants is increasingly important for unit-level operational forecasting and emission-aware operation support. In practice, emission forecasting is hindered by limited plant-specific data, operating regime shifts, and the limited interpretability of purely data-driven models. This study proposes a domain-informed predictive framework that uses thermodynamic analysis to construct physically meaningful exogenous variables for a pre-trained time-series forecasting model in combined gas-vapor cycle (CGVC) power plants. By incorporating physically meaningful variables, the framework improves feature relevance and supports stable short-horizon forecasting within the evaluated reduced-history operating conditions. The approach is evaluated on real plant operational data under data-rich, reduced-history, and short-horizon settings. The corresponding observed MAE ranges for TimeGPT and TimeGPT-EF are 2.565–2.584, 2.784–2.792, and 2.115–2.283 t/h, respectively. Lightweight plant-specific fine-tuning further supports rapid adaptation using limited same-day operating data. SHAP-based analysis identifies turbine exhaust duct pressure, steam flow, and temperature-related variables as major contributors to the model predictions. Rolling-origin evaluation provides preliminary within-unit evidence of short-horizon predictive stability, while split-conformal calibration improves the empirical coverage of the original under-calibrated prediction intervals on the May 24 test set. This study provides a practical and interpretable framework for short-horizon carbon emission forecasting in power plants, with potential applicability to emission monitoring after further validation across broader operating conditions. © 2026

title: Cooperative elemental variations: A novel composition control strategy based on the cluster formula approach
abstract: Composition control is primary for alloy production. The present work addresses the long-standing concern in alloy production: precise composition control within the general standard, using the example of popular 316L austenitic stainless steel. By using the cluster formula approach, the ideal composition zone can be identified for any alloy grade, e.g., (Cr,Mo,Si)3.25±0.25-(Ni,Mn)2±0.25-Febal for the substitutional-type austenitic face-centered-cubic solid solution of 316L, where the two elemental groups represent respectively ferrite and austenite stabilizers. The corresponding wt.% elemental ranges are (16.0–17.5)Cr-(2–2.7)Mo-(0.2–0.8)Si-(10.3–12.7)Ni-(1.2–1.9)Mn-Fe-(0–0.03)C. Then, mathematical equations are derived to describe the cooperative elemental variations in wt.% to comply with the specified formula zone. For 316L, the equations lead to cooperative elemental variations 17.6 ≤ Cr+0.63Mo+1.70Si ≤ 20.5, 11.5 ≤ Ni+1.06Mn ≤ 14.7, and 5.8 ≤ (Cr+0.63Mo+1.70Si)-(0.90Ni+0.95Mn) ≤ 8.7, where the element symbol represents the element's wt.%. The formulated composition zone in combination with the cooperative elemental variations provides a general composition control strategy for alloy production. © 2026

title: Charge-carrier-mediated photothermal synergy in Pt/TiO2-{001} catalysts for low-temperature soot oxidation
abstract: Soot, a major constituent of vehicular PM2.5 and black carbon, remains largely unabated during hybrid vehicle cold starts, where exhaust temperatures below 250 °C fall beneath the light off window of conventional oxidation catalysts. Here, Pt nanoparticles (~2.6 nm) grown epitaxially on TiO2-{001} nanosheets are shown to overcome this limitation through photothermal catalysis. Under full-spectrum illumination, the optimized Pt3.0/TiO2 catalyst (3.0 wt% Pt) reduces the soot light-off temperature from 292 to 189 °C and enhances the oxidation rate (39.9 μmol g−1 min−1 at 190 °C, 2 W cm−2) 8-fold compared with thermal catalysis alone. We find that photogenerated charge carriers cooperatively activate molecular O2 and interfacial lattice oxygen, producing reactive oxygen intermediates (·O2-, O-) that accelerate NO-to-NO2 conversion, the kinetically limiting step in the soot oxidation cycle. Density functional theory calculations corroborate this mechanism and show that the fivefold coordinated Ti sites exposed on the {001} surface lower the barrier for electron transfer to adsorbed O2 by 0.32 eV and reduce the oxygen vacancy formation energy at the Pt-O-Ti interface to 1.61 eV. Coupling photogenerated carriers with facet specific surface oxygen on metal oxide catalysts therefore shifts the operating window of soot oxidation into the cold start regime, offering a route to filter regeneration that does not rely on fuel post injection to raise exhaust temperature. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Synergistic electrode/electrolyte optimization enables efficient dissolution-deposition chemistry in Zn-MnO2 batteries
abstract: Electrolytic Zn-MnO2 batteries based on the MnO2/Mn2+ dissolution/deposition reaction have attracted considerable interest due to their high redox potential and exceptionally high theoretical capacity. However, such systems typically require an acidic environment to initiate the one‑step MnO2/Mn2+ conversion. Herein, high-performance cathode-less Zn-MnO2 batteries are designed. Benefiting from its high surface area and manganese affinity, the aminated Prussian blue analogues (MF@NC‑HA) seed layer provides extra active sites, inducing uniform MnO2 deposition and improving its charge structure. Meanwhile, amino‑acid additives with chelating ability toward Mn2+/Zn2+ are introduced to optimize the cationic solvation structure. Asp lowers the Gibbs free energy of the MnO2 dissolution reaction, thereby enhancing reaction efficiency. The MnO2@HA‑Asp delivers a high areal capacity of 0.53 mAh cm−2 after cycling at 0.5 mA cm−2 and maintains nearly 100% CE over 300 stable cycles at 1.0 mA cm−2. Importantly, Asp can preferentially adsorb on the Zn (002) plane, guiding uniform Zn2+ horizontal deposition and effectively suppressing dendrite growth. Ultimately, the Zn//MnO2@HA‑Asp pouch cell exhibits a high discharge plateau of ∼1.5 V and a capacity of 11.7 mAh. This work provides an efficient strategy for realizing the two‑electron transfer process of Zn-Mn systems. © 2026

title: A new Dixon resultant algorithm for solving parametric polynomial systems using sparse multivariate rational function interpolation
abstract: Elimination methods such as Gröbner bases and triangular sets have been employed to address the growing demand for solving parametric polynomial systems in practice. However, experiments have shown that when used in Computer Algebra Systems such as Maple and Magma they often struggle with systems that have many parameters. To address this problem, we present a new interpolation algorithm for solving parametric polynomial systems over Q using the Dixon resultant. The Dixon resultant is a multiple of the unique generator of an elimination ideal of a polynomial system. It can be expressed as the determinant of a matrix of polynomial entries called the Dixon matrix.In practice, the Dixon resultant R often has many repeated factors and a large polynomial content. To avoid computing these unwanted factors of R, our new algorithm interpolates the rational function coefficients in the parameters of the monic square-free factors of R from monic univariate images of R. It does this using our newly developed sparse multivariate rational function interpolation method. By not computing R in expanded form, our approach often dramatically reduces the number of images needed to interpolate the monic square-free factors of R over Q[jls-end-space/].We have implemented our new Dixon resultant algorithm in Maple with many parts of the algorithm coded in C for increased efficiency. Our benchmarks show that our new Dixon resultant algorithm can solve many parametric polynomial systems that other algorithms for computing R are unable to solve. Our new algorithm is probabilistic; it may fail to produce an answer, and even when successful, it may return an incorrect answer, but with provably low probability. In this work we identify and classify all the causes of failure in our new algorithm, and we give a detailed failure probability analysis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Impact of temperature-dependent viscosity and permeable boundaries on thermal instability in a Darcy–Brinkman ferrofluid layer
abstract: This study investigates the onset of thermal instability in a horizontal Darcy–Brinkman ferrofluid layer with temperature-dependent viscosity, bounded by permeable horizontal surfaces. The variation of viscosity with temperature is described using linear, exponential, and inverse-linear relations. The governing equations are nondimensionalized and reduced to an eigenvalue problem, which is solved using the single-term Galerkin method to determine the critical Rayleigh number for the onset of stationary convection. The incorporation of permeable boundaries, together with different viscosity relations in a ferrofluid-saturated Brinkman porous medium, provides a novel extension of the classical framework and broadens its applicability in various scientific and engineering contexts. The results reveal that the viscosity variation parameter stabilizes the system under linear and exponential laws, but has a destabilizing effect in the inverse-linear case across all boundary conditions. A transition in permeable boundaries from free to rigid enhances the stability of the system by delaying the onset of convection. Additionally, the magnetization parameters M 1 and M 3 both promote instability; however, their effects on convection cell size differ: M 1 favors smaller convection cells, while M 3 promotes larger ones. The permeability of the porous medium also supports the development of larger cells and reduces the critical Rayleigh number. Previous results are consistently recovered as limiting cases, confirming the validity of the present analysis. The study provides deeper insight into ferrofluid convection with relevance to aerospace, porous thermal management, and magnetically driven heat transfer applications. © 2026 Author(s).

title: Atomristors: A new memristive paradigm enabled by atomic-scale switching
abstract: Atomristors represent the ultimate thickness limit of memristors by employing monolayer two-dimensional materials as atomically thin switching media. Reducing the switching layer to a single atomic plane fundamentally transforms resistive switching (RS) from the evolution of extended conductive filaments into atomically confined processes governed by point defects, electrode-derived metal species, and van der Waals interfaces. This Review summarizes atomristors from switching mechanisms, device engineering, and emerging applications. We first present the dissociation-diffusion-adsorption mechanism as a conceptual framework for understanding how metal species migrate across monolayer interfaces and are immobilized at atomic defects to generate conductive spots. We then summarize how defect, electrode, and interface engineering govern device performance and reliability. Benefiting from atomic-scale confinement, representative atomristors have demonstrated fA-level leakage currents, switching ratios exceeding 1011, sub-volt operation, and ps-level switching speeds. Finally, we highlight recent advances in nonvolatile in-memory computing, volatile threshold selectors, radio-frequency switches, and stochastic sources. We then discuss the remaining challenges in clarifying atomic-scale switching mechanisms, reducing cycle-to-cycle and device-to-device variability, and achieving wafer-scale integration. By linking atomically confined switching physics with materials and device engineering, atomristors offer a platform for understanding RS at the atomic limit and for developing scalable atomic-scale information hardware. © 2026

title: Surface modification of Inconel 718 superalloy with BaO–Al₂O₃–SiO₂ glass-ceramic coatings for enhanced durability
abstract: A new BAS was synthesized and coated on Inconel 718 superalloy to enhance thermal shock resistance and hardness. Tailoring Al2O3 and BaO/SiO2 raised Tg to 829 °C, exceeding conventional BAS glasses. The Cr₂O₃-containing frit was slurry-sprayed and sintered at 1100 °C for 2 min. The prepared coating was dense, with amorphous BAS and dispersed Cr₂O₃. After 10 thermal cycles to 1000 °C, it remained intact to 800 °C. At 900–1000 °C, microcracks and spallation appeared without delamination. XRD showed Cr₂O₃, TiO₂, and BAS to 800 °C; BaTi₃O₉, celsian at 900 °C; Al3Ti at 1000 °C. Microhardness was 850 ± 24 HV for as-sintered coating, far above uncoated alloy (450 ± 16). Hardness remained stable at 600–800 °C but decreased to 706 at 900 °C and 640 at 1000 °C, still exceeding bare metal. All in all, high Tg delayed flow and suppressed reactions, preserving integrity. Composition-driven tuning yields high-performance gas-turbine coatings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Convergence of substructuring waveform relaxation algorithms for hyperbolic PDEs with time delay
abstract: This article investigates the application and analysis of two substructuring waveform relaxation algorithms namely Dirichlet-Neumann Waveform Relaxation (DNWR) and Neumann-Neumann Waveform Relaxation (NNWR) for solving hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs) with time delay. These equations are relevant in numerous physical and engineering contexts, such as wave propagation, biological processes, and control systems, where the system's dynamics are influenced by past states. The study emphasizes the stability, convergence, and computational efficiency of these non-overlapping domain decomposition methods when applied to such problems. Specifically, the DNWR and NNWR algorithms are analyzed using both Fourier and Laplace transforms in asymmetric domain decomposition to assess their capability to manage delayed terms in hyperbolic systems. Using Fourier analysis, we establish linear convergence estimate for the numerical errors. Laplace transform analysis enables a more in-depth study for characterizing finite-step convergence. Additionally, we derive the optimal parameters required to achieve finite step convergence in presence of heterogeneous spatial domain. Theoretical findings are complemented by numerical experiments, showcasing the methods’ effectiveness in maintaining accuracy while reducing computational complexity. Additionally, the study explores potential extensions to more complex problems and diverse applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Lattice-electron dual regulation enhances oxygen-redox reversibility and structural stability in cobalt-free lithium-rich manganese-based cathodes
abstract: The cobalt-free lithium-rich manganese-based cathode (LMNO) has attracted much attention due to its high specific capacity, low cost, and environmental friendliness. However, irreversible oxygen loss and transition-metal migration hinder their practical deployment. Herein, a lattice–electron dual-regulation strategy based on Na/Y co-doping was introduced to modify LMNO cathode materials. Theoretical and experimental results confirm that Y doping reduces the Mott-Hubbard splitting energy (U) and irreversible oxygen loss. Furthermore, the Na/Y co-doping optimizes the lattice structure, improving the transport kinetics of Li+ while enhancing the stability of the material structure. The modified cathode achieved an excellent capacity of 302 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C and 2–4.8 V (compared to 268 mAh g−1 for pristine). After 200 cycles at 1 C, the modified material retains 90% of its capacity, with a voltage drop of 0.34 V (compared to 55% and 0.50 V for Pristine). This strategy provides a new approach for regulating oxygen redox behavior and enhancing structural stability. © 2026

title: A fast adaptive finite element method for nonlocal diffusion problems on octree-based adaptive Cartesian multilevel mesh formulation
abstract: We propose a novel adaptive finite element method (AFEM) algorithm for nonlocal problems discretized on an n-dimensional Cartesian mesh. Based on the octree data structure, an efficient mesh algorithm on the Cartesian mesh is implemented, improving search efficiency for elements in the nonlocal neighborhood. We prove that when the nonlocal kernel function is radially symmetric, the number of distinct entries in the stiffness matrix on the Cartesian mesh depends only on the mesh depth. Based on this property, a fast assembly algorithm is designed to reduce the computational cost of solving nonlocal problems with AFEM. Numerical experiments successfully implement adaptive solutions for 2D and 3D nonlocal problems, verifying the effectiveness of the new AFEM algorithm. © 2026

title: A robust lowest-order method for the Brinkman equations
abstract: The Brinkman equation couples the Stokes and Darcy equations by varying viscosity and permeability parameters to accommodate broad applications. Developing a numerical solver that remains robust and efficient across all parameter regimes presents significant research challenges. In this paper, we propose a uniform and pressure-robust finite element method of the lowest order to solve the Brinkman equation. In our discretization, the velocity variable is approximated by a linear Lagrange polynomial enriched by the lowest order Raviart-Thomas element, while the pressure variable is approximated by piecewise constant functions. We provide a rigorous theoretical analysis and numerical validation to demonstrate the method's uniform convergence. Furthermore, to address the high computational costs associated with large-scale practical problems, we design an effective preconditioner that ensures high efficiency and scalability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Rational N,O co-coordination of Fe-N2O2 single atoms modulates the electronic structure to facilitate 1O2 generation
abstract: Selective generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) remains a major challenge in single-atom-catalyst-based advanced oxidation systems, especially in complex water matrices. Herein, a Schiff-base ligand was used to regulate the local N,O coordination environment of Fe sites, yielding an N,O-coordinated carbon-supported Fe single-atom catalyst denoted as Fe-N2O2 based on the proposed idealized coordination model. Compared with Fe-N4, Fe-N2O2 exhibited a higher Fe oxidation state, improved electrical conductivity, and enhanced phenol (PN) adsorption (22.3% vs 5.62%). The Fe-N2O2/PMS system also showed enhanced involvement of 1O2 during PMS activation. As a result, PN, a representative electron-rich phenolic pollutant, was completely removed within 5 min. The apparent rate constant reached 2.51 min−1, and total organic carbon removal reached 73.1% within 30 min. Theoretical calculations revealed that N,O co-coordination reduced Fe charge density and lowered the Gibbs free energy change (ΔG) of O* formation, facilitating PMS activation and 1O2 generation. The favorable cycling stability and continuous-flow performance (>94.9% PN removal within 36 h) highlight the practical potential of the Fe-N2O2/PAN membrane. This work demonstrates that Schiff-base-defined N,O coordination is a viable strategy for regulating ROS evolution in PMS-based catalytic oxidation systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Photonic Quantum Gates Using OAM and MPLC
abstract: Quantum computing based on photonic platforms offers a promising route toward scalable quantum information processing due to its low decoherence and access to high-dimensional state spaces. A promising approach for realizing photonic quantum computation is to encode quantum information in the Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) states of light, enabling the realization of high-dimensional quantum gates. Implementing such quantum gates requires programmable unitary transformations between selected computational basis states. The fabrication of integrated multi-plane light conversion (MPLC) structures could provide a pathway toward large-scale programmable quantum processors. In this work, we investigate the implementation of photonic NOT-gate transformations using OAM states and MPLC systems with a limited number of phase planes. Unlike conventional MPLC approaches that optimize phase masks for a fixed modal basis, the proposed framework treats the computational basis itself as the optimization variable. To identify suitable computational basis states, a photonic quantum-gate optimization algorithm was developed to systematically evaluate candidate LG mode pairs. For each computational subspace, the three-plane MPLC phase masks were optimized using the wavefront-matching algorithm, and the corresponding modal and gate fidelities were calculated. The results show that conjugate-OAM mode pairs {LG_{p}^{l},LG_{p}^{-l}} and neighboring-radial mode pairs {LG_{p}^{l},LG_{p+1}^{l}} consistently achieve higher gate fidelity than structurally mismatched mode pairs under identical hardware constraints. These findings establish a direct relationship between computational-basis selection and quantum-gate performance, providing practical guidelines for computational-basis engineering in OAM-based quantum information processing, photonic quantum gates, and programmable quantum photonic processors. © 1995-2012 IEEE.

title: Adaptive accelerated proximal gradient for controlled autoregressive moving average models with outliers in outputs
abstract: This paper develops an efficient approach for parameter estimation in controlled autoregressive moving average models. Outliers are detected by formulating the problem as Robust Principal Component Analysis, after which an adaptive accelerated proximal gradient algorithm is employed to reconstruct the uncontaminated information matrix. To accommodate large-scale data and obtain unbiased estimates, parameter identification is then performed using the recursive extended least squares algorithm. The simulation studies are provided to demonstrate the robustness and favorable performance of the proposed adaptive accelerated proximal gradient recursive extended least squares method. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Multi-type transient voltage instability identification for power systems with high renewable energy penetration
abstract: High renewable energy penetration leads to diversified transient voltage instability patterns and the need for rapid assessment from short post-fault measurement windows. To tackle these critical challenges, this paper presents a transient voltage stability identification method that integrates Koopman operator theory with multidimensional trajectory feature fusion. First, a novel transient voltage stability index is developed, which comprehensively incorporates the voltage sag area and oscillation intensity during the recovery phase to accurately characterize complex instability behaviors. Second, a Koopman-operator-based prediction model is constructed for transient voltage trajectories, which delivers accurate trajectory prediction for diversified instability modes using short post-fault measurement windows from PMU-equipped buses. Specifically, the model lifts the nonlinear dynamics of power systems into a high-dimensional linear space, thereby enabling precise extrapolation of transient voltage trajectories. Finally, simulation tests are carried out on the China Electric Power Research Institute (CEPRI) standard test system to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results demonstrate that the method achieves high-precision trajectory extrapolation with a short observation window, exhibits strong reliability in high renewable-penetration scenarios, and provides reliable technical support for online security early warning of modern power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Ir/IrOx-WO3 nanocomposites with direct catalyst-support junctions for low-iridium proton exchange membrane water electrolysis
abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is considered a promising technology for sustainable green hydrogen production, but it is still limited by the sluggish acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER), which requires scarce Ir-based catalysts. Herein, Ir/IrOx-WO3 nanocomposites were designed to reduce Ir loading in PEMWE anodes. By controlling the Ir/W ratio, the density of direct Ir/IrOx-WO3 junctions was systematically tuned. Ir/IrOx-WO3 nanocomposite with an Ir content of 30 wt% (IW-30) exhibited the highest acidic OER activity, achieving an overpotential of 278.3 mV at 10 mA cm-² and a mass activity of 457 A gIr-¹ (1.55 V vs. RHE). Operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy revealed that residual metallic Ir in IW-30 was oxidized more rapidly during acidic OER than in IW-55, indicating that direct Ir/IrOx-WO3 junctions facilitate the formation of catalytically active oxidized Ir species. In PEMWE tests, IW-30 delivered 3 A cm-² at 1.9 V and maintained stable operation for 450 h at 2 A cm-² with an ultralow Ir loading of 0.25 mgIr cm-². These findings reveal that direct Ir/IrOx-WO₃ junctions accelerate Ir oxidation under OER conditions, providing a viable strategy for developing low-Ir and durable PEMWE anode catalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Spatially encoded broadband all-optical thermoelectric synapses for in-sensor computing
abstract: In-sensor computing integrates the separated sensing, memory, and computing functions of conventional artificial intelligence (AI) systems, enabling low-power and efficient intelligent systems. In this study, we report a self-powered, broadband (from 405 to 1550 nm), spatially encoded all-optical artificial synapse based on screen-printed thermoelectric Ag2Se for in-sensor computing. The excitatory and inhibitory behaviors of biological nervous systems can be emulated by a single Ag2Se device through the generation of continuously tunable spatially dependent positive and negative photo-thermoelectric responses. Under consecutive optical pulses, the device can exhibit typical short-term potentiation (STP) and inhibitory facilitation, demonstrating dynamic synaptic plasticity, with synaptic weight updates regulating the enhancement and attenuation of neural signal transmission. Furthermore, the device enables logic operations including NOT and XOR gates. Using this artificial synapse, we further constructed a convolutional neural network (CNN) model for a multitask computing system, achieving smile detection, gender recognition, and image recognition, with accuracies of 92.2%, 98.6%, and 94.3%, respectively. This facile thermoelectric hardware platform enables integrated broadband photo-thermoelectric sensing and neuromorphic computing, offering a cost-effective solution for artificial intelligence systems. © 2026

title: Rotational twinning endows B2 multi-principal element intermetallic alloys with excellent strength and ductility
abstract: The synergistic enhancement of strength and ductility remains a critical challenge for B2 intermetallic alloys due to their intrinsic room-temperature brittleness. Herein, using the Ni–Ti system with its highly tunable composition and sensitive phase stability as an ideal model, we designed Ni50Ti16.7Zr16.7Hf16.6 and Ni25Co25Ti16.7Zr16.7Hf16.6 alloys via a multi-principal element approach. Multiscale characterization and first-principles calculations show that the Co-free alloy adopts a brittle B19′ martensitic structure at room temperature, with a fracture strain of ∼13%. In contrast, Co-doping induces changes in the structural ground state, which facilitates the stabilization of the monolithic B2 phase. The Ni25Co25Ti16.7Zr16.7Hf16.6 alloy shows an exceptional combination of strength and ductility, with a yield strength of 1527 MPa, an ultimate compressive strength of 3099 MPa, and a compressive strain of ∼40%. This distinctive feature stems from a deformation mechanism in which <110>-oriented rotational twinning mediates strain accommodation, maintains long-range structural order, and facilitates screw dislocations cross-slip. This twinning-induced plasticity within ordered structures provides a generalizable pathway for designing high-performance B2 intermetallic alloys. © 2026

title: Physics-guided multiscale modeling of hydrogen trapping at rhenium-decorated nanovoids in Tungsten
abstract: Understanding hydrogen-isotope trapping and release at irradiation-induced nanovoids decorated by rhenium (Re) is critical for tungsten plasma-facing materials, yet atomistic adsorption descriptions become intractable with increasing nanovoid size and hydrogen (H) loading. We develop a physics-guided multiscale framework linking density functional theory (DFT), high-throughput analysis, the sure independence screening and sparsifying operator (SISSO), and object kinetic Monte Carlo (OKMC) simulations. DFT shows that H trapping is governed mainly by the local coordination environment of surface adsorption sites, while Re generally weakens H binding with little effect on short-range H–H interactions. High-throughput calculations using a DFT-informed local-environment model generate > 6.1 × 105 H-adsorption configurations, whose energetics collapse onto two surface-scaled descriptors for H loading and Re enrichment. SISSO yields a compact analytical expression that reproduces these energetics and extrapolates to larger nanovoids within the model framework. OKMC predicts lower deuterium desorption temperatures with Re decoration when small vacancy clusters dominate, with a weaker effect after cluster coarsening. This work establishes a compact two-descriptor representation of H trapping and provides a general multiscale modeling framework for irradiated materials. © 2026

title: Influences of dissolved organic matter and halide ions on the photodegradation of amitriptyline: Kinetics and characterization of transformation products
abstract: Amitriptyline (AMT), a widely used tricyclic antidepressant, is frequently detected in both freshwater and marine environments, where its photochemical fate may differ. In this study, the photodegradation of AMT was investigated in reservoir water and seawater, and dissolved organic matter (DOM) and halide ions were identified as the key factors controlling its photolysis. The photodegradation behavior of AMT was systematically examined in the presence of humic acid (HA) and halide ions. HA promoted AMT photodegradation, and higher HA concentrations led to more pronounced enhancement. In halide-containing systems, both ionic strength and specific halide effects jointly influenced AMT photodegradation. When HA coexisted with halide ions, the excited triplet state of HA (3DOM) and the resulting reactive halogen species (RHS) were identified as the key drivers promoting AMT photodegradation. In freshwater, AMT was photodegraded mainly through ROS-mediated oxidation and hydroxylation, whereas in saline water it reacted with RHS to form a halogenated intermediate that was further oxidized and hydroxylated into low-toxicity final products. Overall, AMT photodegraded faster under saline than under freshwater conditions, and the toxicity of its major transformation products decreased accordingly. These findings improve our understanding of the photochemical fate of AMT in freshwater and saline waters and provide valuable insights for the ecological risk assessment of AMT and structurally analogous pollutants in estuarine and coastal systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Achieving exceptional superplasticity in Al0.5CoCrFeNiCu high-entropy alloy via partial recrystallization-induced heterostructure
abstract: Heterogeneous microstructures are generally considered detrimental to uniform superplastic deformation. However, a partial recrystallization behavior is observed in the Al0.5CoCrFeNiCu high-entropy alloy, leading to the formation of a heterostructure—comprising both fully recrystallized and retained unrecrystallized regions—following annealing at 800 °C. This heterostructure achieves an exceptional elongation of 1720% under deformation conditions of 1000 °C and 0.005 s−1. In this heterostructure, the recrystallized regions rapidly accommodate superplastic deformation at the initial stage, promoting uniform superplastic flow. Meanwhile, the stored strain energy in the unrecrystallized regions is released during superplastic deformation, activating dynamic recrystallization and further refining the grains. The refined grains, in turn, better accommodate grain boundary sliding. Consequently, the alloy with an initial heterostructure maintains a high strain rate sensitivity (m value) throughout the superplastic deformation process, enabling uniform superplastic deformation and ultimately achieving significantly higher elongation than that of the initial banded-grained structure and the initial equiaxed-grained structure. © 2026

title: Active-site decoupling and reactor-scale thermal coupling for simultaneous NOx and CO removal over Pd/V–Mo/TiO2
abstract: Simultaneous NOx and CO removal from oxygen-rich industrial flue gases is constrained by NH3 nonselective oxidation and deactivation under SO2-containing conditions. Here, a hierarchically organized Pd/V–Mo/TiO2 catalyst was developed by introducing trace PdOx species and high-density Brønsted acid onto industrially relevant V2O5/TiO2 catalysts, and the same loading strategy was subsequently transferred to a V-based honeycomb catalyst. The optimized 0.3 Pd/2V9MoTi powder catalyst achieved CO and NO conversions and N2 selectivity above 90% at 240–300 °C. Dynamic atmosphere-switching experiments and apparent reaction-order analysis showed that CO oxidation and NH3-SCR were functionally separated and exhibited limited kinetic cross-interference. XAFS and XPS indicated that highly dispersed oxidized Pd species, predominantly Pd2 +–O, serve as the major active sites for CO oxidation, whereas preserved V5+–O species were associated with low-temperature NH3-SCR. CO/NH3-TPD and in situ DRIFTS further suggested that a Mo-associated Brønsted acidic environment preferentially retained NH3 and restricted its access to Pd2+–O sites, thereby suppressing competitive adsorption and NH3 nonselective oxidation. A reduced-order CFD model incorporating experimentally derived kinetics predicted favorable operating ranges of 6000–9000 h−1 for GHSV and 0.6–0.7 for bed porosity. Under the simulated conditions, 5,000 ppm CO oxidation increased the catalyst-bed temperature by more than 40 K, and enhanced NOx conversion by over 30% at 30,000 h−1 relative to standalone NH3-SCR. After transfer to an extruded honeycomb catalyst, NO and CO conversions remained at approximately 83% and 75% at 40,000 h−1, respectively, during 100 h of operation at 230 °C in the presence of 10 vol% H2O and 100 ppm SO2. These results demonstrate the preliminary engineering feasibility of combining functional active-site separation with reactor-scale thermal coupling for integrated NOx and CO removal. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: AIE-enhanced mesoporous nanozyme-based multimodal lateral flow assay for trimodal sensing of imidacloprid and Hg2+
abstract: Multimodal lateral flow immunoassay (LFA) strategies have largely relied on the parallel combination of functionally homogeneous signals, leaving the effective dynamic range and gradient complementarity among detection modes unaddressed. Herein, we report a mesopore-confinement co-assembly strategy in which the AIE fluorophore BTPE and AuIr bimetallic nanozymes are simultaneously loaded into the radial channels of dendritic mesoporous silica nanoparticles (DMSNs), yielding a multifunctional nanotag DMSN-BTPE/AuIr with colorimetric, catalytic-enhanced colorimetric, and fluorescent outputs. Channel confinement enriches BTPE to activate AIE emission while sustaining AuIr catalytic loading; optimization of the BTPE-to-AuIr ratio balances the fluorescent and catalytic outputs within a single nanoparticle. The three signals provide complementary readouts across different concentration ranges, extending the effective dynamic range to six orders of magnitude. Applied to simultaneous dual-channel detection of imidacloprid (IMI) and Hg2+ in cucumber and river water, the fluorescent mode achieved LODs of 3.97 and 4.04 pg/mL with recoveries of 81.44%–115.87%, in close agreement with LC-MS/MS and ICP-MS reference methods. This work provides a design strategy for multifunctional nanotags and multimodal lateral flow detection over a wide concentration range. © 2026

title: Multifunctional cation-site doping unlocks high-performance Mg3Bi1.4Sb0.6-based thermoelectrics
abstract: Thermoelectric (TE) materials require both high performance to maximize energy conversion efficiency and favorable mechanical properties to ensure processability and reliable operation. Herein, we propose a synergistic band engineering and defect engineering strategy to simultaneously optimize the TE performance and mechanical strength for Mg3.2−x(EryCu1−y)x(Bi0.7Sb0.3)1.99Te0.01. Er-Cu co-doping effectively modulates the band structure, shifting the Fermi level deep into the conduction band and inducing band flattening, thereby maintaining a significant Seebeck coefficient at high carrier concentrations. Consequently, a remarkable power factor of ∼23.86 μW cm−1 K−2 is attained for Mg3.18(Er0.50Cu0.50)0.02(Bi0.7Sb0.3)1.99Te0.01 at 323 K. Meanwhile, the integration of multi-scale defects, encompassing grain boundaries, precipitates, dislocations, nanoclusters, and interstitial atoms, synergistically enhances phonon scattering and significantly reduces lattice thermal conductivity. Ultimately, the Mg3.18(Er0.75Cu0.25)0.02(Bi0.7Sb0.3)1.99Te0.01 exhibits an excellent zT of ∼1.30 at 573 K and a superior average zT of ∼1.14 from 323 to 573 K. Furthermore, Er-Cu co-doping introduces multiple strengthening mechanisms, resulting in a Vickers hardness of ∼1.63 GPa and compressive strength of ∼422.1 MPa for Mg3.18(Er0.75Cu0.25)0.02(Bi0.7Sb0.3)1.99Te0.01. This work demonstrates that band engineering and defect engineering through Er-Cu co-doping can simultaneously enhance TE and mechanical properties, providing a general paradigm for designing high-performance Mg3Bi2-based alloys. © 2026

title: Salisbury screen structure to enhance the spectral defense performance of cellulose-based composite
abstract: The development of materials that seamlessly integrate electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding and infrared stealth is of vital importance in addressing the challenges of complex electromagnetic environments and advanced multi-spectral detection. However, conventional metallic spectral defense materials suffer from high thermal conductivity and high density, making it difficult to meet the requirements for lightweight, high-performance materials. Herein, we incorporated the classic Salisbury screen structure into cellulose-based composites to overcome this problem. The composite featured a “conductor-insulator-conductor” architecture consisting of a cellulose nanofiber (CNF)/metal carbides/nitrides (MXene) film as the conductive layer and a CNF/gelatin aerogel as the insulating layer. This design exploited high interfacial reflection and phase-delay‑induced destructive interference, achieving an EMI shielding effectiveness of up to 90.8 dB at a thickness of only 1.3 mm. Simultaneously, the Salisbury screen configuration inherited the low infrared emissivity of MXene and the thermal insulation capability of the aerogel, substantially reducing the radiation temperature of the hot target surface and exhibiting outstanding infrared stealth performance. By modulating a sustainable cellulose platform with a classic wave‑interference architecture, this work establishes a new paradigm for next‑generation spectrally compatible defense materials that combine high‑performance EMI shielding and infrared stealth in a lightweight, eco‑friendly composite. © 2026

title: Deformable Ti particles regulating strain partitioning and microstructural evolution in a high-yield-strength Mg-Gd-Y-Zn composite
abstract: A Ti-particle-reinforced Mg-9Gd-4Y-1Zn-0.5Mn (Ti/VW94) composite with excellent yield strength was fabricated via near-recrystallization warm extrusion at 340 °C followed by aging treatment. During warm extrusion, trace Mn atoms dynamically segregated toward the Ti/Mg interfaces, leading to the in-situ formation of a low-mismatch interface layer of MnTi intermetallic compound. This robust metallurgical bonding facilitated coordinated elastoplastic co-deformation between the Ti particles and the Mg matrix, thereby effectively governing local strain partitioning within the composite. Meanwhile, the coarse deformed undynamic recrystallization (unDRX) grains retained extremely high stored strain energy and dense dislocation structures, while the dual-source particle-stimulated nucleation mechanism induced by Ti particles and intrinsic long-period stacking ordered (LPSO) phases promoted the formation of ultrafine DRX grains (∼350 nm). After aging, nanoscale β′ precipitates and lamellar LPSO phases preferentially formed in high-defect-density unDRX grains, while β phases preferentially formed along solute-rich DRX grain boundaries. These precipitates constructed a hierarchical multi-scale obstacle network that effectively impeded dislocation motion. Owing to the combined effects of grain refinement, dislocation strengthening, precipitation strengthening, and load transfer, the composite achieved a high yield strength of 535 MPa and an ultimate tensile strength of 549 MPa. These findings demonstrate that deformable metallic reinforcements can fundamentally regulate strain partitioning and thereby govern recrystallization pathways, dislocation density, and precipitation behavior in Mg-rare earth-Zn alloys, providing a new strategy for designing high-strength magnesium matrix composites. © 2026

title: Asymmetric built-in electric fields in a MoS2/TiO2/CuS S-scheme heterojunction enhance photocatalytic tigecycline degradation and solar-driven interfacial evaporation
abstract: A ternary MoS2/TiO2/CuS S-scheme heterojunction with asymmetric built-in electric fields was constructed for photocatalytic tigecycline (TGC) degradation and solar-driven interfacial evaporation. Combined UPS-derived band alignment, dark-state XPS, in situ XPS, and DFT analyses revealed opposite interfacial charge-redistribution trends before and under illumination, confirming the S-scheme charge-transfer pathway and supporting the formation of asymmetric built-in electric fields. MTC achieved 96.38% TGC removal within 80 min, with an apparent pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.0358 min⁻¹ . Scavenging and EPR experiments identified h+ and 1O2 as the main reactive species. LC-MS and ECOSAR analyses were used to explore possible TGC transformation pathways and toxicity trends. After immobilization on melamine foam, MTC-MF maintained approximately 90% TGC removal during 10 h of illuminated single-pass operation and achieved evaporation rates of 1.80 kg·m−2·h−1 in water and 1.72 kg·m−2·h−1 in a 1 mg·L−1 TGC solution. During simultaneous photocatalytic treatment and interfacial evaporation, the TGC removal efficiencies in the solution and condensate reached approximately 85% and 90%, respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of MTC-MF for integrated photocatalytic treatment and solar-driven interfacial evaporation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Grounding grid state identification method based on the strong coupling effect of the return line
abstract: To address weak corrosion and fracture responses in grounding grids under variable soil conditions, this paper proposes a state identification method combining the strong coupling effect of the return line with multidimensional time-frequency feature fusion. The routed return path increases the contribution of defect-sensitive branches to the measured loop impedance, thereby enlarging defect-induced perturbations. Frequency-domain spectra are reconstructed into time-domain responses; the wavelet power ridge peak, effective pulse width, root-mean-square (RMS) bandwidth curve integral, low- and high-frequency power proportions, and differential local wavelet power map morphology are normalized to the complete grounding grid reference. Over 30–1000 Ω·m, the maximum complete grounding grid ridge and RMS ratios (1.0039 and 1.0030) remain below the minimum fracture ratios (1.0099 and 1.0164). The dataset uses midpoint thresholds of 1.0069 and 1.0097: fracture requires both thresholds plus temporal, spectral, or morphological corroboration, whereas conflicting evidence is reported as indeterminate. Corrosion produces smaller coordinated amplitude and spectral changes, minimal pulse-width change, and localized patterns dependent on severity and position. Simulations reveal two-level location sensitivity: outer frame defects generally produce larger deviations than internal branch defects, and electrically path-weighted locations respond more strongly within each topological category. The intact, corroded, and fractured states exhibit distinct resistivity-dependent map evolution: the complete grounding grid develops a distributed high resistivity negative-left/positive-right band; corrosion shows the opposite low resistivity polarity sequence and a localized high resistivity positive-left/negative-right band; fracture shows broader discontinuity-related patterns with a negative-dominated transition. Field tests reproduce the principal simulated fracture trends and support the method's engineering applicability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
label: Science (including Engineering)

title: Hierarchical heterostructure-driven high-efficiency co-generation of electricity and ethylene
abstract: Steam cracking of alkanes such as ethane accounts for over 90% of global ethylene production, but relies on energy-intensive, high-temperature pyrolysis, leading to significant carbon emissions and complex by-products that require costly purification. Enabling the co-generation of ethylene and electrical energy in oxide-ion-conducting solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs), we design a highly selective anode for the electrochemical oxidative dehydrogenation of ethane (EOD-eth). The anode consists of a hierarchical heterostructure featuring oxygen-vacancy-rich FeCu-FeOx anchored onto a Sr2Fe1.26Cu0.24Mo0.5O6-δ double-perovskite/Ruddlesden-Popper matrix (FeCu-FeOx@SFCu0.24M-DP/RP). The SOFCs demonstrate outstanding performance, maintaining CO2-free operation for over 400 h, while delivering a high-power density of 0.51 W cm−2 with an ethylene selectivity of 81.7% and an ethane conversion rate of 78.4% at 750 °C. Mechanistic investigations reveal that FeOx acts as both an effective oxygen-ion channel and an oxygen storage reservoir, activating ethane C–H bonds and promoting dehydrogenation, while FeCu enhances both ethylene selectivity and electronic conductivity. Beyond this specific reaction, the FeCu–FeOx–SFCu0.24M-DP/RP architecture embodies the essential attributes universally required of fuel electrode—including multivalent redox adaptability, robust structural resilience, and compatibility with diverse hydrocarbon or syngas fuels—thereby representing a broadly applicable catalytic platform for next-generation fuel-flexible SOFCs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A multi-mode active frequency support strategy for a grid-friendly integrated PV-ES system
abstract: The integration of photovoltaic (PV) and energy storage (ES) is an effective solution to mitigate PV output fluctuations and enhance solar energy utilization. However, existing PV-ES coordination schemes are often limited by insufficient consideration of source-side support capability, grid-side frequency demands, and source-grid interaction. These systems typically operate in a passive manner, merely complying with grid codes rather than actively supporting the grid, thereby limiting the development of power systems with high penetration of renewable energy. To address these limitations, this paper makes the following contributions. First, theoretical analysis reveals that the dual-stage PV system possesses inherent advantages in active frequency support due to its wide-range power regulation capability, which provides a topological guideline for designing grid-friendly integrated PV-ES systems. Second, the active frequency support performance of the PV-ES system is enhanced by optimizing the reserved capacity of the energy storage system. It is theoretically proved that state-of-charge (SOC) balancing among ES units can maximize the system's transient frequency support capability. Third, a multi-mode active frequency support strategy that simultaneously considers grid-side and source-side requirements is proposed. It enables a coordinated and flexible interaction between the grid and PV-ES system, achieving a balance between active support and economic operation. Experimental validation confirms that the proposed control strategy is both feasible and effective. © 2026

title: Data-driven design of high-performance Ti-Fe-O alloys via iron oxide doping into titanium
abstract: Conventional biomedical Ti alloys suffer from toxic elements, high cost, and the inability to quantify the nonlinear composition–microstructure–property correlation. Herein, a machine learning-driven strategy was proposed to establish high-precision property prediction models for Ti-Fe-O alloys, and four algorithms were compared to identify the optimal framework. Among them, the coefficient of determination (R2) of the optimal Random Forest (RF) model reached 0.98. Combined with the simulated annealing algorithm, inverse design was performed toward strength–ductility synergy, and the optimal Ti-1.28 wt.% Fe2O3 alloy was successfully developed. This alloy exhibits a thermally stable α+β duplex microstructure, and annealing induces significant coarsening and morphological transformation of secondary α (αs) from acicular to globular, which converts the hard, barely deformable β phase into a plastically deformable domain. O shows a gradient-type heterogeneous distribution across primary α and β phases. The as-annealed alloy achieves an ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of 888 MPa and an excellent elongation (El.) of 25.7%, demonstrating exceptional strength–ductility synergy. The results suggest that O redistribution and preferential accommodation in the αs/β regions, together with O-assisted dislocation pinning, contribute to mitigating local O-induced embrittlement and promoting coordinated plastic deformation. Meanwhile, O-assisted dislocation pinning activates massive 〈c + a〉 dislocations, and deformation twinning together with stacking faults further enhances the strain-hardening capacity. This work provides a reliable data-driven route for the design and engineering application of high-O biomedical Ti alloys. © 2026

title: Research on multi-objective optimization strategy of three-level dual active bridge converter based on model predictive control
abstract: To address the problems of hard turn-on of power switches, poor dynamic performance and large backflow power in the three-level dual active bridge (3L-DAB) DC-DC converter, a multi-objective optimization strategy based on model predictive control (MPC) is proposed in this paper. First, the switching process of power switches under dual phase-shift (DPS) modulation is analyzed, and the mathematical model of power transmission for the three-level dual active bridge (3L-DAB) converter is established. Taking the stable tracking of output voltage as the core objective, the model predictive control (MPC) model of the converter is constructed based on state-space equations, and an error correction method is introduced as the feedback correction link to eliminate the steady-state error caused by parameter mismatch. Second, the power regions are divided by combining the zero-voltage switching (ZVS) turn-on conditions and the backflow power optimization criteria. The optimal phase-shift angles are solved according to the operating characteristics of different regions, and a comprehensive optimization control strategy that takes into account ZVS turn-on, backflow power suppression and dynamic performance improvement is formulated. Finally, the experimental verification results show that the proposed control strategy can achieve ZVS turn-on of power switches, effectively reduce backflow power and improve the dynamic performance of the system. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A novel lattice hydrodynamic model for bidirectional pedestrian flow considering the pedestrians’ anticipation effect of density difference
abstract: Pedestrians’ anticipation effect, which is a conscious or unconscious response to the surrounding environment, plays an important role in pedestrian flow, especially under high-density condition. In order to investigate the pedestrians’ anticipation effect of density difference, an extended lattice hydrodynamic model for bidirectional pedestrian flow is proposed in this paper. The stability condition of the proposed model is deduced using linear stability analysis and the analytical result reveals that the anticipation effect of density difference can significantly enlarge the stability region on the phase diagram. By the use of nonlinear analysis method, the time-dependent Ginzburg Landau (TDGL) equation is derived to describe the evolution of pedestrian flow near the critical point. The modified Korteweg-de Vries (MKdV) equation is also derived to characterize the kink-antikink waves in unstable region. The theoretical results indicate that jams can be effectively mitigated by considering the anticipation effect of density difference. Numerical simulations are conducted to validate the accuracy of the theoretical findings. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

title: A method for predicting essential proteins in heterogeneous networks based on discrete quantum walk
abstract: Essential proteins are an important material basis for life activities, and their accurate identification is crucial for understanding cellular functions and biological mechanisms. Although there are already various experimental and computational methods for detecting essential proteins, most of them are limited to a single network or local features, making it difficult to integrate heterogeneous network information, and they lack accuracy and robustness in complex networks. Therefore, we propose a heterogeneous network essential protein prediction algorithm based on discrete-time quantum walk (HNDQW). This algorithm first constructs a protein–domain heterogeneous network according to the original protein–protein interaction (PPI) network and the known relationships between proteins and domains. Then, it constructs a quantum weighted transition matrix of the heterogeneous network by integrating network topological features and multi-source biological information. Finally, it constructs a discrete-time quantum walk model and performs quantum walks on the heterogeneous network. The average probability of reaching each vertex is selected to represent the essentiality score of the protein node. By ranking the proteins, the top-ranked proteins are selected as candidate essential proteins. In addition, to evaluate the performance of the algorithm, we compare this method with 13 other different methods on three datasets, DIP, Krogan and Gavin. The experimental results show that this method achieves recognition accuracies of 94.12%, 63.35%, 56.82% and 51.26% among the top 1%, 15%, 20% and 25% of candidate proteins, respectively. It also performs well under multiple evaluation metrics, with prediction accuracy exceeding that of the other 13 methods, and can effectively identify essential proteins. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

title: Research on the sensitivity of key factors influencing evacuation in building stairwell based on simulation
abstract: With more people clustering in buildings, evacuation in high-rise buildings has become a challenge in urban safety. Despite the identification of key influencing factors in existing studies, quantitative analyses of their impacts remain inadequate, and there is a lack of a systematic evaluation framework. To address this gap, the present study employs a multi-factor-aware pedestrian evacuation agent model, coupled with parameter sensitivity analysis, to investigate the effects of evacuation parameters on evacuation time. The research proceeds as follows: first, a Perception-Decision-Operation (PDO) framework for occupant movement is proposed and integrated into the pedestrian evacuation model; second, the proposed model is validated by using evacuation experimental data collected from different floors; third, the sensitivity of evacuation time to four critical parameters — pedestrian number, expected speed, step depth, and stair width — is analyzed, and the degree of influence of each parameter is quantified. The results demonstrate that expected speed exerts the most significant impact on pedestrian evacuation time, followed by step depth, while stair width has the least influence. The sensitivity quantification method adopted herein overcomes the limitations of traditional empirical approaches. These findings not only provide a data-driven basis for optimizing key building evacuation parameters but also facilitate a paradigm shift in emergency evacuation design from qualitative assessment to quantitative evaluation. Ultimately, this study offers valuable insights for emergency management in complex built environments. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

title: Influence of threshold-activated linear decay behaviors on information propagation in social networks
abstract: The social propagation of behaviors is influenced not only by interpersonal interactions, but also by individual psychological dynamics. This study presents a threshold-activated linear decay behaviors (TALDB) that incorporates both social and psychological factors to investigate propagation phenomena in social networks. Through edge-based partition theory and numerical simulations, the results demonstrate that TALDB can induce a range of phenomena, including continuous phase transitions, discontinuous phase transitions, and static behaviors. As the values of behavioral parameters increase, the behavioral intensity weakens, leading to a shift from continuous to discontinuous to static phase transitions. The findings reveal a phase transition crossover in how TALDB changes: the high-intensity behaviors promote the propagation of behaviors, while the weak behaviors delay propagation, decreasing gradually and more slowly. These insights extend the theoretical understanding of how individual psychology affects propagation dynamics in social systems, providing a mechanism for targeted interventions in complex networks. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

title: Link prediction in multiplex social networks based on information transmission graph neural networks
abstract: Social networks are omnipresent graph-structured data where entities and interactions between them can be modeled as nodes and edges, respectively. In recent years, graph neural networks (GNNs) have evolved as a mainstream and powerful model for handling graph data. Link prediction, which can foretell missing or potential links, is a crucial task in social network analysis. However, most existing methods focus on monolayer networks and usually ignore that multiplex networks have richer information, which often results in poor performance on link prediction. Therefore, this paper proposes an information transmission-based GNN (IT-GNN) model for link prediction in multiplex social networks. IT-GNN first learns the representation of each node in a multiplex network from itself and its neighborhood. Specifically, the neighborhood information of a node is learned from its 1-, 2- and 3-hop neighbors in combination with the three new ways of information transmission. Then, the embedding of a node pair is obtained based on these representations. In this regard, the final representations of potential links in the target layer, which are used to determine the existence of potential links, are generated by fusing their embeddings from all layers. Extensive experiments on seven real-world networks demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed model. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

title: The effects of risk perception based on local or global information in suppressing the spread of infectious diseases
abstract: This paper aims to investigate the role of individuals’ perceptions of infection risk in suppressing the spread of infectious diseases. It also examines whether global or local information is more effective in preventing infections. We developed an agent-based model in which 100000 individuals are connected in a small-world network. Infection information for the entire population was classified as global information, and infection information for the surroundings of a specific individual was classified as local information. The degree of response to infection risk information was measured using a normalized tunable sigmoid function. Higher sensitivity to infection risk increases the implementation of preventive measures, which reduces the spread of infectious disease. The use of global information on infection risk has been shown to be more useful in suppressing infections in general. However, if infected people around us can be recognized immediately and personal quarantine is quickly followed, the use of local information has been shown to be the most cost-effective way to end infections. Our study emphasizes the importance of individuals recognizing and responding to infected people around them to effectively control the spread of infectious diseases. It demonstrates that higher sensitivity to infection risk leads to better adherence to preventive measures, which in turn reduces disease transmission. These findings suggest that individual awareness and behavior play a critical role in managing infectious diseases. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.
