title: Bi-level optimization of harmonic mitigation and energy trading in distribution networks with connected microgrids using PV-inverters and active power filters
abstract: The widespread deployment of power electronic-based devices in modern distribution networks introduces significant power quality challenges, necessitating effective mitigation strategies at the distribution level. This paper proposes a novel bi-level optimization framework that coordinates a Local Energy Market (LEM) and a Local Harmonic Market (LHM) for interconnected microgrids (MGs), enabling simultaneous energy management and collaborative harmonic mitigation using PV inverters and Active Power Filters (APFs). The proposed framework is validated on modified IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 123-bus distribution systems. Simulation results demonstrate compliance with the IEEE 519 harmonic standard while establishing an incentive-based harmonic market that transfers the economic responsibility for harmonic mitigation to the Distribution System Operator (DSO), increasing its expenditure by 15.3% while creating additional revenues for participating MGs. Moreover, the distributed optimization achieves solutions within 4.86% of the centralized optimum while reducing computational time by approximately 60%, confirming its computational efficiency and scalability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Reconciling rheology, stretchability and thermal conductivity in thermal interface materials through dynamic polymer interactions and multimodal filler networks
abstract: Thermal interface materials (TIMs) used for heat dissipation of high-power electronics must combine good dispensability, high stretchability, and high thermal conductivity to maintain efficient heat dissipation during assembly and thermo-mechanical cycling. However, achieving these properties in one system remains challenging because the high filler loadings needed for efficient heat transport typically increase viscosity and reduce stretchability. Here, we report a polyurethane-siloxane TIM that integrates dynamic polymer interactions with a multimodal aluminum filler network to overcome this trade-off. Disulfide exchange and abundant urethane hydrogen bonding promote rapid stress relaxation and network rearrangement, while ternary particle-size-graded aluminum fillers improve packing efficiency and interparticle contact, forming effective thermal conduction pathways. As a result, the TIM exhibits low viscosity (234.13 Pa s), pronounced thixotropic behavior, high stretchability (elongation at break of 304.58%), and high thermal conductivity (8.13 W m−1 K−1). Integrating the TIM into a chip, we demonstrate the reduced operating temperature and thermo-mechanical reliability of the chip under cyclic and prolonged operation. This design offers a promising strategy for next-generation TIMs requiring both processability and mechanical reliability. © 2026

title: Conductive polymer modified with nematic liquid crystal doped with graphene oxide for highly sensitive acetone sensing
abstract: Acetone has been recognized as a critical biomarker for diagnosing and monitoring blood glucose levels in people having type II diabetes, and its measurement has been considered essential for maintaining human health. In this study, a highly sensitive gas sensor was developed in which a nanostructured polyaniline film was modified with a graphene oxide (GO)-doped nematic liquid crystal (NLC), and this composite layer was employed for acetone detection. The fabrication of the gas sensors was carried out through the electrosynthesis of polyaniline on interdigital electrodes (IDEs) under acidic conditions, after which the resulting films were modified using GO-doped NLC. Detection of chemical vapors was achieved by monitoring variations in the electrical resistance of the sensing layer, which were induced by orientational ordering transitions of GO and NLC, as well as by the absorption of analyte molecules onto LC droplets distributed across the polyaniline surface. The morphology of the polymeric films prior to and following modification was examined using scanning electron microscopy. The sensor responses (SRs) toward acetone were evaluated both in the presence and absence of GO, and enhanced sensitivity and improved selectivity toward acetone were observed when GO was incorporated. A detection limit of 0.27 ppm and a linear dynamic range of 1–10 ppm were obtained for acetone determination. Validating the method was carried out through the comparison of the sensor results with those obtained using gas chromatography. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Do influence tactics matter? investigating prompt framing effects in LLM code generation
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into software engineering workflows, helping developers write, debug, test, and maintain code. While prompt wording and structure are known to influence model performance, the impact of psychologically inspired prompt framings remains unexplored. This study investigates whether different psychology-based communication strategies that humans use to persuade or motivate others can lead to more effective prompt framing, which may, in turn, affect LLM behaviour in coding tasks. Drawing on Yukl & Falbe’s well-known taxonomy, we operationalized eight influence tactics (like rational persuasion, ingratiation, and exchange) into reproducible prompt templates. These prompt templates were evaluated across five leading open-weight LLMs using two widely adopted benchmarks: LiveCodeBench and SWE-bench Verified. We assessed the resulting code output on four key software quality dimensions: functional correctness, quality, maintainability, and security. Our results show that certain influence-induced prompt framings, particularly those emphasizing urgency, were associated with reduced correctness and security. This work presents the first large-scale empirical study of influence-induced prompt framing in software engineering tasks, offering insights into how linguistic cues may shape LLM outputs. We conclude with practical insights for designing transparent and interpretable human-AI interactions in code generation. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: “Whose Death Killed Death, and Took Away His Sting”: Aemilia Lanyer-s Subtle Art of Death in Salve Deus Rex Judaeorum
abstract: Historically grounded approaches to the Renaissance “death arts” can be used to illuminate Lanyer-s mobilizing and transforming of standard rhetorical tropes and poetic conceits—most notably the blazon—to reconceptualize and represent the bliss-imbued chiastic movement from Jesus-s incarnation and death by crucifixion to the resurrected Christ-s making possible the prospect of eternal life. Consonant with Lanyer-s participation in the querelle des femmes (the longstanding controversy over women-s ontological and social status in a patriarchally organized world-system), Salve Deus partakes of earlier traditions of female piety like those popularized in The Golden Legend, and also the Christus Mortuus contemplative technique brought to prominence in Reformation England by Katherine Parr. Lanyer-s poem thus provides a rich case study in the death arts to promote a novel, reconfigured form of female piety predicated on a series of stunning memory images of the grotesquely maimed and blood-drenched male body. title: Aemilia Lanyer and the Body
abstract: Scholars have consistently turned to representations of the body in Salve Deus Rex Judaeorum to consider issues of genre, religion, gender, race, social status, poetics, and poetic authority. Yet, despite scholars- frequent attention to topics of corporeality and embodiment, “the body” has not been recognized in Lanyer studies as a central subject of inquiry. The introduction to this special issue surveys how the corpus naturale has undergirded Lanyer scholarship over the past fifty years. Whereas previous studies have identified the body-s importance at discrete moments or in specific mechanisms in Lanyer-s poetry, this introduction emphasizes how the form and content of Salve Deus is fundamentally rooted in the body and bodily experience. This special issue, thus, reconceptualizes the categories of “women writers” and “women-s writing,” highlighting how we might consider the female body not as a historical identity but rather as a formal model in early modern English literature. title: Grace, the Spirits of the Blood, and Mystical Marriage in Aemilia Lanyer-s Salve Deus Rex Judaeorum
abstract: Aemilia Lanyer-s relationship to the prospective patronesses of her Salve Deus Rex Judaeorum has been the subject of much scholarship. The sheer number of dedicatory verses in Salve Deus have led some to read the volume-s devotional elements as a cynical cover for worldly ambition. At the same time, scholars interested in the potential erotic bonds Lanyer depicts between women have also given the poem-s social ends primacy over its devotional discourses. This essay reevaluates these assumptions by drawing out how Lanyer persistently unifies social and spiritual grace in Salve Deus. Showing how Lanyer draws on spirit-based physiologies to describe the operations of grace in both the patronage poems and in passages on the Passion of Christ, I argue that Lanyer uses physiological beliefs about the spirits of the blood to position divine grace as an embodied force that constitutes the social bonds she creates through her poetry. title: Nanocellulose-reinforced κ-carrageenan/gluten films with Ardisia elliptica anthocyanins: structure-property balance for freshness-related colour response
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable alternatives to petroleum-based packaging has stimulated the development of intelligent materials capable of providing visual information on food quality during storage. In this study, soil-burial-disintegrable biopolymer films based on κ-carrageenan, wheat gluten, cellulose nanofibrils (CNF), and anthocyanin extract from Ardisia elliptica fruits were prepared by the solution-casting method and evaluated for their structural, optical, water-related, mechanical, and colourimetric properties. Anthocyanin incorporation conferred a clear pH-dependent colour response across the tested pH range, while CNF-containing formulations exhibited reduced UV transmittance, increased surface wettability (lower water contact angle), and modulated tensile performance and water-related properties in a formulation-dependent, non-monotonic manner. Among the CNF-containing formulations, the film containing κ-carrageenan, gluten, anthocyanin extract, and 20% CNF (κCG-GL-ANT-CNF20) exhibited the lowest water solubility and swelling, coupled with low UV transmittance, with water vapour permeability remaining a formulation-dependent trade-off rather than the primary selection criterion. Soil burial assays showed progressive disintegration, reaching more than 93% weight loss by day 35. Proof-of-concept applicability was assessed using rose apple, apple, and a sardine-based model system, where visible film colour changes were observed during storage. Within the tested series, κCG-GL-ANT-CNF20 provided the most balanced formulation, combining improved resistance to liquid-water-induced disintegration, low UV transmittance, lower short-term anthocyanin release, and qualitative food-model colour responsiveness. The developed films therefore show potential as colour-responsive hydrocolloid materials for qualitative freshness-related assessment. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: Modelling carbon price dynamics with jump-diffusion and higher-order hidden Markov switching
abstract: This paper proposes a dynamic modelling framework that integrates a jump–diffusion process with a higher-order hidden Markov model, allowing carbon prices to exhibit both short-term volatility spikes and long-run regime memory. Motivated by the rapid expansion of emissions trading markets since the early 2000s, the framework captures the stylized facts of carbon prices, including non-stationary fluctuations, abrupt jump episodes, and discrete transitions across latent regimes. To improve adaptability to daily-frequency data, recursive filters are developed to estimate and update hidden states and model parameters in real time. Monte Carlo experiments confirm the convergence and accuracy of the estimation procedure in offline and online implementations. For empirical validation, daily carbon price data from two representative markets—the European Union Emissions Trading System and China’s carbon market—are analyzed over the period from 2004 to 2024. Both point and interval forecasting performances are evaluated against benchmark models, including the autoregressive integrated moving average model, g eometric Brownian motion, extreme gradient boosting, and long short-term memory networks. The results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves improvements in model fitting and short-term forecasting performance. The findings confirm that our approach based on a higher-order hidden Markov model provides a flexible and robust tool for modelling carbon price dynamics in emission trading systems. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Intra-Matrix Flexible Optical-Electronic Configuration Algorithms for Energy-Efficient Large Language Model Inference
abstract: Low-energy, low-precision inference is an important enabler for scalable deployment of large language models (LLMs). Optical-electronic computing offers high bandwidth, low latency, and potentially high energy efficiency, making it a promising approach for future LLM deployment. However, existing optical and hybrid optical-electronic inference systems typically use uniform hardware configurations, such as fixed optical power or a fixed electronic-photonic partition across layers. Fine-grained allocation of optical power and optical-electronic computation remains underexplored for photonic LLM inference. Here, we propose three flexible configuration algorithms: Flexible Optical Power Allocation (FOPA), Flexible Weak-Column Allocation (FWCA), and Joint Optical Power and Weak-Column Allocation (JOWA). Using a diagonal Hessian estimator without constructing the full Hessian matrix, these methods jointly optimize optical-electronic resources under predefined energy budgets. Evaluations on Llama 2-7B and DeepSeek-LLM-7B-Base show estimated energy savings of 40.11%-60.85% relative to FP16 inference on the NVIDIA H100 and 5.34%-38.12% relative to uniform optical-power and weak-column baselines, while maintaining an acceptable perplexity increase. Evaluations using a Tianshu-hardware-calibrated simulator show corresponding estimated energy savings of 39.91%-53.67% and 5.02%-26.76%, respectively. These results indicate that fine-grained resource allocation can improve the energy-accuracy trade-off of hybrid optical-electronic systems for LLM inference. © 1995-2012 IEEE.

title: Stochastic optimization algorithms for biomedical image classification
abstract: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) remains the primary optimization method for training deep neural networks; however, its performance can deteriorate in the presence of noisy gradients or highly variable curvature. While momentum based and adaptive learning rate methods partially mitigate these challenges, they often rely on accumulated second moment estimates or exhibit sensitivity to hyperparameter choices, particularly when gradient statistics change over time. In this paper, we propose three stochastic optimization algorithms, SGD(New), SGD(We), and SGD(Was), which integrate three complementary mechanisms: Nesterov-type look ahead gradient evaluation, a normalized momentum update constructed from successive gradient differences, and an adaptive stepsize that scales inversely with the variability of gradient changes. By defining momentum in terms of directional consistency rather than gradient magnitude, and by adjusting the learning rate using curvature information implicitly inferred from gradient differences, the proposed methods yield stable and responsive updates under stochastic gradient feedback. Together, these components form a lightweight and principled optimization framework applicable to both standard i.i.d. training and more challenging learning scenarios. We evaluate the proposed algorithms against widely used baselines, including SGD with momentum, Adam, RAdam, and Adagrad, on four MedMNIST biomedical image classification datasets using an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 model. The empirical results demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve improved optimization stability and competitive performance across binary, multi-label, and multi-class medical image classification tasks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Fast and accurate node-level hosting capacity estimation in distribution networks using graph neural networks
abstract: This paper presents a fast and accurate method for estimating node-level hosting capacity in distribution networks using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). A large open dataset of synthetic networks, representative of Italian distribution grids, was created, and hosting capacity values were computed using AC optimal power flow (AC-OPF) simulations, which are computationally expensive. This dataset was used to train a GNN regressor based on the Graph Isomorphism Network architecture, integrating path-based electrical features to capture both local and global grid dependencies. The proposed GNN is compared to a fast physics-based estimation method, showing a reduction in mean absolute error of about 30%, highlighting its ability to capture the spatial and electrical relationships embedded in the network topology and to produce physically consistent estimates. In terms of efficiency, the model achieves an inference speed over 11,000 times faster than AC-OPF, enabling hosting capacity estimation in milliseconds. This significant speed-up allows real-time applications such as interactive hosting capacity maps, large-scale scenario analysis, and decision support for distribution system operators. The model's robustness is also evaluated under out-of-distribution conditions, where some performance degradation is observed, particularly for small networks, emphasizing the importance of representative training data. Importantly, the GNN remains operational even when traditional power flow methods fail to converge, providing stable and reliable estimates without requiring manual intervention. Overall, the approach demonstrates strong potential for scalable, real-time hosting capacity assessment to support the integration of distributed energy resources. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Behavior-aware group target tracking for AAV swarms with dynamic structural evolution
abstract: Most traditional approaches to multiple unresolvable group target tracking simplify the modeling of group evolution, limiting their effectiveness in scenarios with complex group dynamics. In practical applications, dense group targets, such as autonomous aerial vehicle (AAV) swarms, often exhibit dynamic structural changes including merging and splitting, which pose significant challenges for reliable tracking and behavior interpretation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a modular, closed-loop framework for group target tracking and behavior recognition (GTTBR). The proposed framework integrates measurement clustering, cluster-to-group association, behavior recognition, state estimation, and track management within a unified recursive process. Variational Bayesian (VB) inference is employed in key stages, including measurement clustering and group state estimation. Within this framework, a behavior-aware extent prediction mechanism is developed, where group behaviors inferred from association patterns are incorporated into the prediction of spatial extents, enabling adaptive modeling of dynamically evolving group formations. In addition, a robust track management mechanism with track-backward correction is introduced to mitigate clustering errors and improve temporal consistency. Experiments on synthetic simulations and real-data measurements after clutter removal demonstrate that the proposed method effectively tracks evolving group structures and provides interpretable descriptions of group behavior evolution. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: “Looking at artifacts”: The development of visual aesthetic preferences
abstract: Developmental aesthetics is an underexamined yet growing area of aesthetics research. Very few studies have investigated infants’ visual preferences for artifacts. Would a young child have visual preferences for artifacts, given their limited exposure to the world and with a developing brain? Revisiting our framework (Göksun et al., 2014), which was built on the aesthetic triad of Chatterjee and Vartanian (2014), we provide an overview of the current state of the field on early visual aesthetic preferences with a focus on art and architecture. After presenting evidence for perceptual primitives that may guide visual aesthetic preferences, we center on early artifact appreciation with infants and young children. We conclude the paper by charting new research directions required to examine early aesthetic appreciation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Stage-aware deep learning with adversarial data synthesis enables prospective season-scale A/H1N1 influenza forecasting in China
abstract: Accurate influenza forecasting is essential for public health preparedness, yet many models require future covariates, provide limited interpretability, and degrade under post-pandemic regime shifts. We propose a Stage-Aware Multimodal Neural Network (SAMNN) that integrates multimodal temporal features using configurations adapted to heterogeneous transmission regimes and supports season-ahead scenario forecasting using adversarially synthesized covariates. Using 13 years of national A/H1N1 surveillance data from mainland China (2011∼2024), SAMNN was evaluated across three epidemiologically distinct seasons spanning ∼20-fold differences in peak intensity. SAMNN achieved R 2 values of 0.82–0.95, 0.82-0.97, and 0.55-0.97 for 1-week-, 2-week-, and 4-week-ahead forecasting, respectively, and generally maintained competitive performance relative to five baseline models across forecast horizons. SHAP attribution showed that epidemiological signals dominated predictions, with context-dependent contributions from climatic and social-context features. To support prospective scenario forecasting, we used an adversarial synthetic covariate-generation pipeline to produce season-ahead forecasts for 2024/25 using information available at the prespecified forecast origin. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Evaluating land price effects of zoning policy adjustment in Bekasi's TOD area: A regression discontinuity design analysis
abstract: The expansion of Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) and associated zoning adjustments in Bekasi, Indonesia, has reshaped urban land markets, yet their causal effects on land prices and social outcomes remain insufficiently examined in developing-city contexts. This study estimates the impact of zoning regulation changes on land prices around TOD areas using a sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) with dual distance cutoffs at 500 and 750 m. Based on 905 geo-referenced land price transactions from 2017 to 2024, the results reveal a statistically significant discontinuity at the 750-m threshold, corresponding to an average increase in land value of approximately 107 percent. In contrast, no significant effect is detected at the 500-m cutoff, suggesting that land prices in the immediate TOD core had largely internalized accessibility benefits prior to the formal zoning adjustment, resulting in a pre-existing price premium. Covariate balance and robustness tests support the validity of the causal estimates. The findings indicate that zoning-induced land value capitalization is most pronounced in transitional TOD zones rather than in fully matured TOD centers. While the results empirically support the use of a 750-m TOD planning radius, the magnitude of land value appreciation also raises concerns regarding housing affordability and potential gentrification. These outcomes highlight the need for complementary policy instruments to ensure that TOD-driven zoning benefits contribute to inclusive and socially balanced urban development. Copyright © 2026. title: Experiences of after-dark urban forest walks when using head torches: off-the-shelf vs customised
abstract: During the dark season, electric lighting in urban forests can facilitate recreational activities and psychological restoration. However, the permanent presence of electric lighting causes light pollution, with detrimental effects for people and wildlife. This study explored the extent to which head torches could support pedestrian needs in a Nordic context where daylight hours are reduced during the winter season. The aim was to compare the pedestrian appraisal of an urban forest path under different lighting conditions: daylight (DL); regular off-the-shelf head torches (OHT); and customised head torches (CHT), with reduced light distribution and thereby less light pollution. The 75 participants completed structured walks with observer-based environmental assessments on site by means of questionnaires under DL, OHT or CHT light conditions. The results showed that participants experienced (appraised) the urban forest path similarly in the two head torch conditions in terms of visual accessibility, perceived safety, and the restorative potential of the forest setting. The behavioural intention to choose the path did not differ between head torches, but the intention to avoid the path was lower with OHT. No differences in comfort aspects of the light could be identified. As expected, the urban forest was rated higher for the environmental appraisals in DL, but retained its restorative potential even in the two head torch conditions. It is concluded that light sources with less ecological impact could be introduced without influencing pedestrians’ environmental experiences negatively. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Solvent-ion synergistic engineering of hierarchical hydrogels for multifunctional all-weather ionic skins
abstract: Resolving the intrinsic conflict among optical transparency, mechanical robustness, environmental adaptability, and conductivity remains a formidable challenge for hydrogel-based ionotronics. Herein, a novel “Solvent-Ion Synergistic Engineering” strategy is proposed to construct a hierarchical triple-network hydrogel (GAAE-Zr) that successfully overcomes these trade-offs. The design integrates a covalently crosslinked poly(acrylamide-co-2-acrylamido-2-methylpropanesulfonic acid elastic backbone, dynamic Zr4+ coordination bonds for toughening without coloration, and an ethylene glycol/water binary solvent system for anti-freezing and anti-dehydration. Through this architecture, the resulting hydrogel exhibits exceptional toughness (elongation > 1500%, tensile strength 286 kPa) and broad-spectrum adhesion, while maintaining glass-like transparency (> 90%). Simultaneously, the reconfigured hydrogen-bonding network significantly depresses the freezing point to −49.5 °C and locks in moisture for long-term stability. Leveraging these merits, the GAAE-Zr hydrogel is demonstrated as a high-fidelity strain sensor with stable conductivity (up to 0.74 S/m) for thermally stable wireless human-machine interaction, and is further implemented as a fully encapsulated triboelectric nanogenerator delivering an instantaneous power density of 220 mW m−2. This work establishes a versatile material platform and a new design paradigm for next-generation wearable electronics requiring multifunctional integration and all-weather operational reliability. © 2026

title: Multidisciplinary design, analysis, and optimization (MDO) for co-designed transmission & distribution electric grid planning
abstract: This paper describes early experiences and example use cases applying multi-disciplinary design analysis and optimization (MDO) to the integrated design of power grids. Adapted from aerospace, MDO enables combining multiple existing tools into a coordinated optimization. Here we use MDO to simultaneously capture integrated transmission-distribution and investment-engineering trade-offs in an automated framework. Example use cases showcase prototype interactions among existing grid models using MDO and hint at the types of integrated analyses enabled by this approach. In addition, we share experiences and thoughts on grid-specific challenges and opportunities to help advance further work in this area. © 2026

title: From surface coverage to biofilm involvement: Hyaluronic acid influences TiZr alloy corrosion under sterile and Staphylococcus aureus biofilm conditions
abstract: Hyaluronic acid (HA) is widely used for intra-articular injection to improve joint lubrication and mobility, but its influence on microbiologically influenced corrosion of joint implants remains unclear. Here, we investigated how HA affects the corrosion behavior of TiZr alloy in simulated body fluid (SBF) under sterile and Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) biofilm conditions. Surface observations and chemical analysis indicated that HA-related surface coverage was formed on the TiZr surface and reduced surface damage under sterile conditions, suggesting a protective role of HA. However, in the presence of S. aureus biofilm, HA showed contrasting effects at different immersion stages, slightly reducing corrosion at the early stage compared with the S. aureus group but aggravating biofilm-associated localized damage after prolonged exposure. Contact angle analysis showed decreases of 68.1% and 57.1% within 1 min in the S. aureus + HA group on days 7 and 14, respectively, indicating that HA promoted rapid surface wetting and altered the interfacial wetting behavior in the biofilm environment. At these time points, electrochemical tests further confirmed corrosion acceleration, with the S. aureus + HA group showing the highest corrosion current densities among all groups, reaching 7.972 × 10-6 A cm-2 and 2.715 × 10-6 A cm-2, respectively. These results demonstrate that the effect of HA on TiZr alloy corrosion shifts from protection under sterile conditions to corrosion aggravation during prolonged S. aureus biofilm exposure. This finding suggests that HA-related effects on biofilm formation and implant corrosion should be considered when assessing the corrosion risk of TiZr joint implants under infection-related conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Informal urban regeneration through social capital: The Anousheh Street experience in a developing city
abstract: While underprivileged neighborhoods are often seen as obstacles to urban development, their regeneration is essential for achieving sustainable urban development. Understanding the factors that influence successful regeneration experiences can guide action in similar neighborhoods. This study examines how the local community drove the informal regeneration of Anousheh Street in Ahvaz, Iran, transforming an underprivileged neighborhood into a vibrant street food hub. This study employed a Straussian Grounded Theory approach based on 24 in-depth interviews, triangulated with secondary socioeconomic data, to explain how the regeneration of Anousheh Street emerged. The findings show that vendor solidarity, rooted in social capital, acts as the central driving mechanism. This solidarity enabled informal creativity in attracting customers, supported by gradual institutional involvement from local authorities. This sequential process drives social, economic, and physical regeneration, evidenced by a 31-fold increase in commercial units and a halving of the local unemployment rate (from 35.27% to 16.81%) between 2011 and 2016. Unlike top-down models, this informal approach preserves cultural authenticity, fostering local identity and economic opportunities. This study develops a novel empirical model demonstrating how urban regeneration in developing cities can be achieved without reliance on large-scale physical investment, instead leveraging social capital and street food-based economies. The model contributes to theory by addressing a key gap in Middle Eastern urban studies and extends the application of Grounded Theory within urban regeneration research. From a practical perspective, this study proposes a context-sensitive yet scalable and transferable model based on three key conditions: vendor solidarity, vendor informal creative practices, and gradual institutional support. While the model demonstrates potential for application in other developing cities, its success depends on local socio-cultural and institutional contexts. These findings provide new policy-relevant insights for advancing inclusive and low-cost urban regeneration in the Global South. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Physics-informed surrogates for multi-objective optimization of scraped falling-film plastic pyrolysis reactors
abstract: Melt pyrolysis of mixed polyolefin waste is limited by slow, non-uniform heating of viscous, low-conductivity melts and coke formation on overheated or poorly wetted walls. Scraped falling-film reactors can alleviate these limitations by renewing thin melt films, but their design remains challenging because scraping simultaneously enhances heat transfer, alters residence time, and affects film stability. Here, we develop a physics-informed CFD–surrogate–optimization framework for a vertical scraped falling-film pyrolysis reactor. A two-phase volume-of-fluid CFD model, benchmarked against TG and batch pyrolysis data, couples endothermic cracking kinetics with a Danckwerts-type surface-renewal closure using a dimensionless scraping number, avoiding moving-mesh resolution of blade motion. The model reproduces batch oil yields at 440 and 480 °C with absolute deviations within 1.3 wt%. Mechanistic maps show that stronger scraping monotonically increases heat-transfer enhancement, whereas conversion enhancement peaks at intermediate intensity, revealing a non-monotonic balance between surface renewal and effective residence time. To accelerate design-space interrogation, a physics-informed neural-network surrogate constrained by energy and reaction-progress residuals is trained on CFD data; on 60 held-out cases, it achieves R2 = 0.83–0.98 for key scalar and field outputs. Coupling the surrogate with NSGA-III identifies Pareto trade-offs among oil yield, specific energy input, and coking risk. Balanced candidates cluster at 460–471 °C and scraping numbers of 11–14; within this region, B3–B4, corresponding to 466–469 °C and scraping numbers of 13–14, are predicted to deliver 80.9–81.4 wt% oil, defining a prioritized operating window within the design space. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: The benefits of reading narrative fiction
abstract: The benefits of reading are well-known and have been well-established by research. But does it matter what we read? Are there unique benefits to reading narrative fiction: stories about people, their goals, challenges, emotions, and interactions? Focusing on research published in the past few years, we review the empirical evidence of the benefits associated with reading fiction. This includes a wide range of domains, including language abilities, our ability to understand others, early social development, intergroup prejudice, meaning in life, cognition, longevity, and well-being. Several remaining research questions are also presented. In light of the many potential benefits that reading affords, and the few likely harms, promoting narrative fiction among children and adults of all ages should be a high priority. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Engineering hydrophobic membranes with tunable pore accessibility via selective swelling of SDS block copolymers for ethanol concentration
abstract: The separation of ethanol from dilute aqueous solutions, such as fermentation broths, is critically important for biofuel production. Membrane distillation (MD) with porous membranes usually suffers from insufficient selectivity, while pervaporation (PV) with dense films is inadequate in permeability. To overcome this trade-off, we developed a novel hydrophobic membrane via the selective swelling of a polystyrene-b-polydimethylsiloxane-b-polystyrene triblock copolymer (SDS). By precisely controlling the swelling agent and duration, we engineered the optimal membrane with a tailored pore structure featuring interconnected nanopores and partially blind pores, along with a PDMS-enriched pore surface. This unique architecture enables a multipath permeation mechanism combing solution-diffusion and the transport pathway for molecules under vapor–liquid equilibrium within pore channels. The optimized membrane demonstrated an exceptional combination of high permeation flux and separation factor for a 5 wt% ethanol/water mixture at 50 °C, yielding a remarkable pervaporation separation index (PSI) of 38.2 kg·m−2·h−1. This performance surpasses many PDMS-based PV and conventional MD membranes. This work presents a simple and efficient strategy for fabricating high-performance membranes that simultaneously achieve high flux and selectivity, offering significant potential for advancing energy-efficient bioethanol recovery processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Blowing Leaves in Archaeology—The Multidimensionality of Technological Complexity in Human Origins Research
abstract: Technological complexity has been a continuous trope in archaeological research from its beginnings in the nineteenth century. Based on a concept of unidirectional cultural evolution, archaeological material was ordered along a linear progression from simple to complex. While creating hierarchies of extant populations based on the complexity of their tools is not overtly practiced in archaeology anymore, the same is not true for the deep past. The concept of behavioural modernity and research on human cognitive evolution is still partly founded on technological complexity. The turn away from technological complexity to symbolic behaviour in pursuing questions surrounding behavioural modernity and humanness was less a reaction to criticisms of the concept but served to maintain the hierarchical ranking between modern humans and extinct hominins. Here, we propose an alternative view on technological complexity that attempts to overcome linear hierarchies and lingering progressivist notions. By reviewing several measures of complexity alongside their analytical units and underlying definitions, we show that technological complexity is not suitable for creating a single hierarchy of artefacts, assemblages, or hominin species. The multitude of existing definitions, methods, and measures does not imply a fundamental flaw in these approaches but exemplifies the multidimensionality of technological complexity. We propose a new way of understanding multiple, justified measures for technological complexity through a heterarchical structure that allows various kinds of ranking to exist depending on context, need, scale, or function, including the potential for competing or even contradictory hierarchies. A heterarchical perspective on technological complexity asks ‘How were technologies or hominins complex?’ rather than ‘How complex were technologies and hominins relative to another?’ This approach can shed persistent historical bias and overcome simplistic dichotomies such as ‘us’ and ‘them’ in deep-time archaeology that hinder our ability to engage with questions about the becoming of humans in a meaningful way. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: A review on hydrogen energy in the transportation sector: progress, challenges, and prospects in aviation, marine, and land
abstract: The transportation sector emits large amounts of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere, necessitating the adoption of a cleaner energy sources to reduce emissions. Hydrogen energy is considered as a cleaner energy source, offering zero emission during combustion, possessing the highest heating value and energy-to-weight ratio among conventional fuels. Therefore, hydrogen can be a better option for the transportation sector, including aviation, marine, and land transport. A thorough overview of the present status of hydrogen energy in the transportation sectors, assessing progress, challenges, and prospects for its application in different modes of transport considering hydrogen storage system is presented in this paper. Furthermore, the paper provides a full analysis of the current challenges impending the practical application of hydrogen in transportation sector and provides recommendations to overcome the challenges. This study also reviews current and future research on hydrogen fuel by different automakers such as Toyota, Honda, BMW, MAZDA, and Mercedes-Benz, aviation companies like Boeing and Airbus as well as marine vessels developed by China, Japan, France, Norway, and United Kingdom. This paper presents and discusses Commercial Readiness Index (CRI) and the Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of hydrogen production processes, providing valuable insights for researchers, policymakers, and stakeholders. The authors identified key challenges that must be addressed to incorporate hydrogen in transportation sector, including the development of a convenient, safe, and cost-effective storage of hydrogen, reduction of hydrogen production cost, development of infrastructure, and the establishment of the formulation policy and regulatory framework. title: Coupling degree with self-supervised learning for multimodal recommendation
abstract: Multimodal recommendation systems, leveraging multimodal data, demonstrate great potential in modeling user preferences and improving recommendation accuracy. However, due to the issues such as sparse interaction data, their performance typically deteriorates significantly, limiting their applicability. Existing works address this issue by using modality feature enhancement or self-supervised learning signal generation. The fusion features, which are derived from similar nodes with the original features, is suboptimal when enhancing user embedding features. To address these issues, we propose the Coupling Degree with Self-supervised Learning for Multimodal Recommendation (CDSSL). First, a novel concept is proposed named Coupling Degree (CD) in recommendation systems, which is utilized to enhance the representation of users and items by learning the coupling between nodes in the interaction graph. Furthermore, we guide the consistency learning of original interactions and generated interactions by combining modality information, thereby improving self-supervisory signals. The effectiveness of CDSSL was comprehensively assessed using four publicly available datasets, which is on average 6.12% higher than the current optimal baseline, demonstrating the effectiveness of the framework. The source code is available at https://github.com/Loyreem/CDSSL . © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Male DNA on underwear: Can Y- STR results help discriminate activities?
abstract: This research is based on a case in which the complainant alleged that the defendant had removed her underwear, while the defendant claimed they had only danced together. To assist in resolving this issue, DNA was collected from the sides of the complainant’s underwear and Y-chromosome STR (Y-STR) analysis performed using the PowerPlex® Y23 System. As no published research were available on DNA recovered from the sides of underwear given the two alleged activities, 60 experiments were conducted to generate specific data on the expected results given underwear removal and given dancing. The underwear removal was simulated using a dummy, while the dancing experiments involved real participants. The paper discusses a principled approach to representing prior knowledge and combining it with the experimental observations when assigning probabilities to DNA recovery outcomes under the competing activity level propositions. To explore whether our LRs were calibrated, we applied our model to published ground truth studies. For the presence of a full Y-STR profile PP23, we show that our LRs in the order of 50 are robust. The prevalence of DNA from cohabitants was also studied. In our experiments, taking the cohabitant's Y-STR profile into account did not impact the value of the observations given activity level propositions. However, having access to the cohabitant reference sample increases the number of interpretable DNA mixtures and can provide relevant information. We therefore recommend requesting the cohabitant DNA reference samples, particularly in cases involving balanced Y-STR mixtures. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier B.V. title: Pathogen evolution under strategy changes in vaccination campaigns: A game-theoretic framework
abstract: In existing models of pathogen evolution under voluntary vaccination, vaccination behaviour is typically assumed to be static, overlooking the conflicts between individual and collective interests. To address this, we develop a multi-scale model within a game-theoretic framework that couples the dynamic processes of disease transmission, vaccination decision-making, and pathogen evolution. By reformulating vaccine uptake as a time-dependent strategic choice and incorporating a heterogeneous update mechanism, we establish the evolutionary model of vaccination strategies. Numerical results show that heterogeneous updating rules will capture autonomous population decision-making. The co-evolutionary dynamics are highly sensitive to the evolutionary adaptation rates and exhibit an asymmetric relationship between population and evolutionary dynamics. At the early stage of a vaccination scenario, we observe that imitation behaviour dominates due to limited information. Enhancing vaccine uptake is effective in limiting the emergence of detrimental variants, and the long-term evolutionary outcome may favour the emergence of specialist variants. This framework provides quantitative methods and key methodological advancements for multi-scale mathematical modelling in the context of pathogen evolution. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Accumulation and transfer behavior of typical heavy metals in Spirulina products: Implications for risk assessment
abstract: This study investigated the exposure, bioaccumulation, migration, and associated risks of Pb, Cd, Hg and As throughout the Spirulina-based food supply chain. A total of 83 commercial Spirulina powder samples were analyzed by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), followed by dietary risk assessment using Monte Carlo simulation. Controlled exposure system was established to evaluate heavy metal bioaccumulation during cultivation, and metal redistribution was tracked during phycocyanin production. The results showed that all four heavy metals were detected in commercial samples, with total As exhibiting the highest concentration level and exceedance rate, followed by Hg. Under the population-average intake scenario, the combined hazard index (HI) remained below 1. However, scenario-based recalculation using consumer-relevant Spirulina intake levels indicated that the HI could approach or exceed 1 under moderate-to-high and high supplement consumption. Under the controlled single-metal exposure conditions used in this study, Spirulina possessed significantly higher BCFs for Pb and Cd than for As and Hg, and that the soluble fraction served as the principal intracellular storage compartment. During processing, heavy metals were redistributed during crude extraction, ammonium sulfate precipitation, and dialysis, with approximately 30%-40% ultimately retained in the final phycocyanin product. Isothermal titration calorimetry further confirmed that all four metals could spontaneously bind to phycocyanin through exothermic interactions. This study reveals the transfer characteristics of heavy metals along the pathway of “water - algal biomass - algal powder - phycocyanin”, and provides a scientific basis for full-chain safety control and risk assessment of Spirulina-derived products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A multi-scale modeling approach for infectious disease: Integrating within-host dynamics to network-based transmission
abstract: Infectious disease transmission is shaped by tightly coupled biological processes within hosts and social contact patterns between hosts, making cross-scale modeling essential for understanding epidemic dynamics. We develop a data-driven multiscale framework that links within-host viral kinetics to between-host transmission on a dynamic multilayer contact network. Using influenza virus, SARS-CoV-2, and SARS-CoV as representative pathogens, we infer infection-age-dependent infectiousness from longitudinal viral-load data and integrate the resulting profiles into a stochastic individual-based model with contact layers constructed from empirical demographic and contact data. By comparing infectiousness profiles within the same multilayer transmission framework, we show that epidemic trajectories depend not only on overall transmission potential but also on the timing and duration of infectiousness. Early, concentrated infectiousness produces earlier epidemic peaks and shorter outbreaks, whereas later or prolonged infectiousness delays and extends transmission. Layer-resolved analyses show that setting-specific contributions arise from interactions among contact volume, contact intensity, and infectiousness profiles. Intervention simulations highlight the importance of temporal alignment: case isolation and vaccination are most effective when implemented before or during the pathogen-specific period of high infectiousness, whereas physical distancing reduces epidemic burden by lowering contact opportunities. This framework provides a flexible approach for linking viral-load-derived infectiousness with network-mediated transmission and evaluating targeted epidemic control strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: A soft computing-driven modelling approach to investigate Nipah virus transmitted diseases
abstract: In this study, we have developed an integrated scientific machine-learning framework to characterize the hidden drivers of Nipah virus transmission, a zoonotic pathogen with complex multi-host ecology. We construct a deterministic compartmental model that captures the principal infection pathways and rigorously analyze its biological and structural properties. Numerical simulations using Python's odeint solver validate the theoretical results. To quantify the dominant forces shaping disease propagation, we perform a global sensitivity analysis based on partial rank correlation coefficients. We further employ a Multilayer Perceptron Neural Network (MLPNN) that learns the underlying vector field of the ODE system, enabling it to act as a computationally efficient surrogate operator that faithfully reproduces the mechanistic dynamics. This neural surrogate accurately reconstructs trajectories comparable to the classical solver, providing a flexible, data-driven tool for rapid prediction, simulation, and scenario exploration without repeatedly integrating the original ODEs. Augmenting this, a Genetic Algorithm (GA)-based optimization procedure is used to minimize the basic reproduction number (R0) by tuning the dominant parameters, yielding control strategies that remain robust under variation in initial conditions. Collectively, this framework enhances interpretability, improves predictive fidelity, and offers actionable insights for Nipah virus mitigation and preparedness. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Music in early childhood: Perception, action, and social experience
abstract: Research on early musical development has expanded beyond perceptual abilities to encompass movement, social interaction, and broader developmental processes. This Opinion article highlights three themes that illustrate this evolution: the relation between rhythm perception and movement, the role of music in caregiver–child interaction and social communication, and the developmental significance of active musical engagement. Through the lens of these themes, musical development appears as an embodied and socially embedded process in which perception, action, and social interaction are closely intertwined. © 2026 The Author
label: Social Sciences

title: Topology-aware gap analysis for national DC fast-charging networks: The case of Türkiye
abstract: This study evaluates the functional adequacy of DC fast-charging infrastructure using a network-based framework that moves beyond station counts to assess corridor continuity, traffic demand, and targeted expansion strategies. A graph representation of the national intercity highway system integrates public DC fast-charging stations as network seed nodes, and accessibility is quantified through multi-source shortest-path analysis. Minimum Viable Coverage (MVC) criterion and traffic-weighted metrics are used to reflect heterogeneous mobility demand across provinces. The results reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity, highlighting a disconnect between nominal infrastructure availability and functional long-distance mobility. Inequality analysis shows that the top ten provinces account for approximately 72.8% of national traffic-weighted accessibility, while the bottom 40% contribute only about 2.2%. Sensitivity analysis across inter-charger distance thresholds indicates diminishing marginal gains beyond moderate spacing levels. A gap-based DC expansion scenario further demonstrates that a limited number of strategically placed stations can substantially restore consecutive coverage along previously disconnected highway corridors, yielding relative MVC improvements of up to 62% in structurally underserved provinces. At the national level, the targeted deployment raises primary-corridor MVC from 86.72% to 91.22%, recovering approximately 3,400 km of previously disconnected roadway. Overall, the proposed framework provides a transferable planning tool for improving corridor continuity, supporting targeted charging-infrastructure deployment, and informing the integration of growing EV charging demand into power-system investment decisions in emerging EV markets. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Authentication and key agreement mechanisms for internet of drones: A novel taxonomy, critical review, and experimental performance analysis
abstract: The continuous progress and distinct capabilities have led the Internet of Drones (IoD) to be a persuasive paradigm that offers promising advantages across various applications, spanning from defense to civilian uses. Despite its manifold benefits, it is essential to highlight that it also faces several challenges, and security remains a critical concern that can hold back its widespread adoption. Stringent authentication mechanism design has appeared as one of the favorable techniques for tackling distinct security attacks in IoD networks. This survey presents a detailed review of existing literature, focusing on authentication protocols explicitly designed for securing communication in IoD networks. Recognising the growing complexity and diversity of communication, we present a novel multi-layered taxonomy that offers a comprehensive roadmap for classifying authentication mechanisms across the IoD stack. The presented taxonomy interactively maps each authentication technique to its system roles, cryptographic foundations, and operational context within the IoD network to demonstrate a more holistic understanding of prevalent authentication mechanisms. Drawing from our presented taxonomy, we highlight the compelling contributions and acknowledge the potential limitations of the recent literature. We compare the security and resistance to common attacks of prevalent protocols while highlighting their advantages and limitations. Based on the security analysis, we shortlist protocols for full-scale implementation that exhibit the highest security coverage. We then present a detailed experimental analysis of these selected protocols against various metrics (i.e., CPU execution time, memory consumption, etc.) using a Holybro QAV250 quadcopter drone-based testbed setup. Finally, we discuss future challenges that require joint efforts from academia and industry. © 2026 .

title: Synthesis-structure-property-performance economic value creation relationships in biomass-derived carbon materials for hydrogen storage: Implications for green finance and sustainable development
abstract: The transition toward a hydrogen-based economy requires innovative storage materials that simultaneously enhance hydrogen performance, promote resource efficiency, and generate long-term economic value. Biomass-derived porous materials have emerged as a promising solution by transforming abundant agricultural, forestry, and industrial biomass residues into high-value hydrogen storage media, thereby supporting the principles of the circular bioeconomy and sustainable resource management. This study examines the economic value creation potential of biomass-based hydrogen storage technologies and evaluates their implications for green finance, low-carbon investment strategies, and sustainable development. It highlights how biomass valorization reduces dependence on expensive conventional storage materials while creating new revenue streams through waste utilization, carbon reduction, and renewable energy integration. The analysis demonstrates that biomass-derived activated carbons, biochars, carbon aerogels, and hierarchical porous carbon nanostructures possess favorable physicochemical properties, including high specific surface area, tunable pore architectures, lightweight characteristics, and excellent adsorption performance, making them attractive candidates for efficient hydrogen storage systems. From an economic perspective, these technologies improve supply-chain resilience, lower production costs, stimulate rural economic development, and encourage investment in sustainable manufacturing industries. Furthermore, biomass-based hydrogen storage aligns closely with green finance mechanisms by attracting environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investments, facilitating access to green bonds and climate finance, and supporting national decarbonization policies designed to achieve net-zero emissions. The study also discusses the integration of biomass-derived storage materials within emerging hydrogen value chains, emphasizing their contribution to carbon neutrality, renewable energy storage, and energy security. Despite challenges related to commercialization, feedstock standardization, scalability, and investment uncertainty, continued advances in material engineering, policy incentives, and financial innovation are expected to accelerate industrial deployment. Overall, biomass-derived hydrogen storage represents a strategically important intersection between sustainable materials science, green finance, and circular economic development, offering significant opportunities to create environmental, economic, and social value while supporting the global transition toward resilient and sustainable energy systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Politeness negotiation in English refusals: Evidence from Javanese EFL learners and Native Speakers of English
abstract: This study examines how politeness is negotiated in English refusal speech acts produced by Javanese Learners of English (JLEs) and Native Speakers of English (NSEs) across situations characterized by variations in power relations and social distance. Data were collected through a set of written discourse completion tasks (WDCTs) consisting of nine scenarios representing interpersonal, academic, and professional contexts. The study employs a comparative qualitative design, with refusal strategies identified using an established taxonomy and systematically coded using Atlas.ti. The results show that refusal is consistently realized as a sequence of pragmatic moves rather than a single illocutionary act. Among JLEs, the most frequent pattern is layered mitigation, characterized by the combination of apology, appreciation, and indirectness prior to the main refusal. This pattern becomes more prominent in situations involving greater interlocutor power and greater social distance. In contrast, NSEs tend to employ concise mitigation combined with clearer expression intent, often limiting negotiation and reducing ambiguity. Indirectness in JLEs frequently functions to maintain relational harmony and prolong interactional openness, whereas in NSEs, it operates within a more bounded and situationally oriented framework. The study also revealed that direct refusal emerges selectively in equal-power relationships, with differing orientations toward politeness marking between the two groups. Theoretically, this study contributes to the literature on interlanguage pragmatics by positioning politeness in refusal as a dynamic negotiation process shaped by the interaction of cultural orientation, social variables, and sequential organization of speech. These findings highlight the need to conceptualize refusal not as a fixed strategy type but as a context-sensitive pragmatic practice. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Immunohistochemical evidence of glutamatergic modulation of Nesfatin-1 neurons in the rat supraoptic nucleus during inflammatory stress
abstract: Background: Stress triggers a complex network of neuroendocrine, immune, and behavioral responses aimed at maintaining homeostasis. Nesfatin-1, a hypothalamic peptide initially identified for its anorexigenic effects, has also been increasingly implicated in stress-related processes. Methods: This study investigated whether acute inflammatory stress induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) activates Nesfatin-1 neurons in the supraoptic nucleus (SON) and examined the modulatory role of glutamatergic receptor antagonists. Female and male Sprague–Dawley rats were assigned to control, LPS, MK-801 + LPS, and CNQX + LPS groups. Neuronal activation was assessed using dual immunohistochemical staining for c-Fos and Nesfatin-1, followed by quantitative analysis of co-localized neurons in the SON. Results: LPS administration significantly increased the proportion of c-Fos-positive Nesfatin-1 neurons in both female and male rats compared to controls (p = 0.001). Pretreatment with MK-801 and CNQX attenuated this activation (p < 0.01), indicating the involvement of both NMDA and non-NMDA glutamatergic pathways. Conclusion: Acute inflammatory stress activates Nesfatin-1 neurons in the SON, and this response is modulated by glutamatergic signaling. These findings provide new immunohistochemical evidence linking glutamatergic transmission to stress-induced Nesfatin-1 activation, with potential implications for the neurobiological interaction between inflammation, energy homeostasis, and stress-related processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Toward climate-responsive higher education: A HeatReady framework for state universities and colleges in the National Capital Region in the Philippines
abstract: Extreme heat events have increased risks and threats to the education sector in urban areas across the Philippines. This study developed a HeatReady Framework for State Universities and Colleges (SUCs) in the National Capital Region (NCR) of the Philippines for climate-responsive educational management. The method that was employed in this study is the explanatory sequential design with 180 participants from seven SUCs in NCR. Findings revealed that all five HeatReady key action areas must be present in crafting a framework because of the high level of agreement of importance of the stakeholder in these components. Based on the inferential analysis using the Kruskal-Wallis H test revealed significant differences across SUCs (χ2 (6, N = 180) = 15.045, p = .010). The Ordinal logistic regression analysis confirmed that the five domains collectively predicted the importance of these key action areas in building the framework (χ2(11) = 22.265, p = 0.014), indicating the integration rather than isolation of these factors' impact. The goodness of fit is not significant, which indicates that the model fits the data very well (Pearson χ2 (446) = 269.623, p = 1.000; Deviance χ2 (446) = 243.014, p = 1.000). Qualitative findings revealed that the major challenges experienced by stakeholders included inadequate ventilation and cooling facilities, poorly ventilated classrooms, and the absence of formal institutional heat policies during extreme heat events. Stakeholders recommended the development of standardized HeatReady policies, flexible learning modalities during high heat index conditions, and the improvement of campus infrastructure through cooling systems, shaded spaces, and heat-safe areas. The HeatReady framework offered a model to safeguard welfare, ensure academic continuity, and improve the adaptive capacity of SUCs in NCR for climate-responsive educational management. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: The power of noticing the good: The mediating role of reward perception in the effect of mindfulness on depression and suicidal ideation
abstract: Background: Although dispositional mindfulness is inversely associated with mental health problems and suicidal ideation, the behavioral mechanisms underlying this relationship remain unclear. This study investigated whether environmental reward perception mediates this association. Method: In a cross-sectional study of 407 Colombian adults, Kendall’s tau correlations and bootstrapping mediation analysis with 5,000 resamples and bias-corrected 95% confidence intervals were used to estimate indirect effects. Results: Mindfulness positively correlated with reward perception; both inversely correlated with depression and suicidal ideation. The model revealed a significant indirect effect of mindfulness on depression (ab = −0.281, 95% CI [-0.335, −0.226]) and suicidal ideation (ab = −0.367, 95% CI [−0.427, −0.308]) through reward perception. Conclusions: The findings were consistent with an indirect association between dispositional mindfulness and both depression and suicidal ideation through environmental reward perception. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as theoretically consistent associations rather than evidence of a causal mediation process. However, these indirect associations illustrate the value of this analytic approach for identifying candidate mediators such as environmental reward perception, which can subsequently inform the design of future longitudinal and intervention research on mindfulness-based approaches to depression and suicide prevention. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. title: Resilience Optimization Strategy for Cyber-Physical Distribution Systems Under Coordinated Fake-Base-Station and Physical Attacks
abstract: Driven by the deployment of intelligent terminals and advanced communication technologies, modern distribution networks have fundamentally evolved into cyber-physical distribution systems (CPDSs). Consequently, these systems face an escalating exposure to sophisticated, coordinated cyber-physical attacks. To address this critical vulnerability, a tri-level defender-attacker-operator optimization model is proposed in this paper to enhance CPDS resilience against coordinated fake-base-station (FBS) and physical attacks. The coordinated attack process is modeled by jointly considering physical line disruptions, cyber-induced RCS communication failures, and their coupled impact on post-attack self-healing. To render the resulting complex tri-level formulation computationally tractable, a hybrid framework is developed, which integrates an improved column-and-constraint generation method with M²SITRI. Comprehensive simulations conducted on modified IEEE 33-node and IEEE 123-node distribution test systems verify both the effectiveness of the proposed resilience-enhancement model and the computational efficiency of the hybrid solution method. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Deployment conditions for biomass value chains on marginal lands: Evidence from a multi-case stakeholder survey
abstract: Biomass from marginal lands is increasingly considered as a feedstock for European bio-based value chains, particularly where biomaterials, bioenergy, and other bio-based products can support decarbonisation without directly competing with food production. This study examines stakeholder-assessed deployment conditions across seven biomass value-chain cases, with a primary focus on Europe and additional evidence from Argentina and South Africa that broadens the empirical scope. Using a mixed-methods analysis of stakeholder survey data from 133 respondents, the study examines perceived risks, sustainability priorities, implementation challenges, enabling measures, and expectations regarding bio-based products and bioenergy. The findings show that implementation does not follow a single generic pattern. Instead, stakeholders identified different combinations of environmental, regulatory, market, technological, and coordination conditions associated with different biomass value chains. Fibre- and material-oriented pathways were characterized by stakeholder emphasis on product standards, certification, and market development; wetland biomass pathways with ecological compatibility, land-use clarity, and regional logistics; biofuel-oriented pathways with policy stability, quality assurance, and secure demand; biogas- and substrate-related pathways with supply coordination, infrastructure, and predictable incentives; and restoration-linked woody biomass pathways with institutional coordination, land-tenure clarity, and local value creation. Across cases, stakeholders indicate deployment conditions of biomass conversion and utilisation depends not only on feedstock availability or technological potential, but on how environmental safeguards, regulatory conditions, market structures, and coordination arrangements align in practice. The study contributes stakeholder-based evidence on the conditions shaping the deployment of biomass for bioenergy and bio-based products primarily in Europe and highlights why value-chain-specific support conditions matter for implementation. © 2026 The Authors. title: Factors affecting collaborative management among agencies involved in the development of organic rice farmer networks in Thailand
abstract: This study aimed to examine the factors affecting collaborative management among agencies involved in the development of organic rice farmer networks in Thailand and to propose guidelines for enhancing interagency collaboration in this context. The study applied a quantitative research approach using a structured questionnaire as the primary data collection instrument. Data were collected from 261 organic rice farmers who were evaluated under the organic rice production system during the 2023 to 2024 production year in Sisaket Province, Thailand. The sample size was determined using the Taro Yamane formula with a sampling error of 0.05. To ensure representation of different groups of farmers within the organic rice production system, stratified sampling was applied, followed by proportional allocation and accidental sampling to select respondents within each stratum. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, including percentage, mean, and standard deviation, as well as stepwise multiple regression analysis to identify the most significant factors influencing collaborative management. The results indicated that the overall mean scores of the four examined factors were at a high level. Among these factors, the learning process showed the highest mean score, followed by leadership, communication, and policy implementation. The results of the multiple regression analysis revealed that leadership (β = 0.511), policy implementation (β = 0.198), and the learning process (β = 0.170) had a statistically significant influence on collaborative management among agencies involved in the development of organic rice farmer networks in Thailand at the 0.05 significance level. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening learning processes, effective leadership, and consistent policy implementation to support collaborative governance among agencies and farmer networks. Enhancing these factors can improve coordination, knowledge exchange, and resource utilization among stakeholders, thereby contributing to the sustainable development of organic rice farmer networks and improving the livelihoods of farmers in Thailand. title: Differentiated instruction competency development among preservice primary teachers: A descriptive survey
abstract: Differentiated instruction is important in primary teacher education because future teachers need to respond to students' diverse readiness levels, learning needs, interests, and learning pace. This study described differentiated instruction competency development among preservice primary teachers at a Vietnamese university. A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted with 28 lecturers and 250 preservice primary teachers from the Primary Education program at Hung Vuong University. Data were collected using structured online questionnaires. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize lecturer ratings, student self-ratings, perceived goals, perceived pathways, and perceived related factors of differentiated instruction competency development. Lecturer ratings showed that differentiated instruction competency was highest among K19 students, followed by K20 and K21. Students' self-ratings showed a similar pattern, although students generally rated their own competency more positively than lecturers did. Both lecturers and students viewed differentiated instruction competency development as relevant to professional preparation, effective teaching in primary schools, and connecting theory with practice. Courses in the teacher education curriculum were identified by both groups as the main pathway for developing this competency. Lecturers emphasized lecturer competency, class size, and curriculum content as important related factors, whereas students gave the highest rating to their own awareness of the role of differentiated instruction competency. The findings suggest that differentiated instruction competency may be strengthened through an integrated approach that combines coursework, practice-based learning, self-study, student research, and lecturer guidance. title: Racialized psychotherapy: Understudied risks and the case for empirical scrutiny
abstract: Racialized psychotherapy, a cluster of approaches centering race, racial identity, and racism in clinical work, emerged from legitimate concerns about cultural incompetence and minority underservice. The field has not tested the assumption that race-centering benefits racial minority clients. This paper identifies four mechanisms by which racialized therapy may harm clients: therapist-imposed racial salience that overrides client-defined concerns; hypervigilance induction through attributional training toward racial threat; externalized locus of control that undermines agency; and therapeutic deference that reduces the productive challenge clients from stigmatized groups may most need. The validation argument for racialized therapy is partly right but justifies responsive rather than proactive race-framing. The evidence base for culturally adapted interventions is modest, adverse effects go unreported, and the most explicitly race-focused protocols lack randomized trial evidence. Systematic research on conditions under which race-centered approaches benefit or harm clients is overdue. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Social inequalities and occupational disease in Colombia: An ecological analysis of the 2021 ENCSST and associated determinants; [Desigualdades sociales y enfermedad laboral en Colombia: análisis ecológico de la ENCSST 2021 y determinantes asociados]
abstract: Introduction. Occupational disease represents a growing public health challenge in Colombia, characterized by marked territorial inequalities associated with socioeconomic, organizational, and exposure-related factors. Objective. To describe the prevalence of occupational disease in Colombia and to identify the associated socioeconomic, organizational, and exposure-related factors across the country's six regions. Materials and methods. An exploratory ecological study was conducted using regional data from the 2021 National Survey of Working Conditions and Health (ENCSST) and socioeconomic indicators from DANE and DNP. Spearman correlations were estimated between occupational disease prevalence and variables related to exposure, organizational conditions, and structural determinants. A multiple linear regression model was developed to identify factors associated with regional variation. Results. The prevalence of occupational disease showed substantial disparities, ranging from 36 cases per 100,000 workers in the Pacific region to 2,289 per 100,000 in the Amazon region. Implementation of the Occupational Health and Safety Management System (SG-SST) was significantly inversely associated with prevalence ( β = -6.04 ; 95% CI: -7 to -5 ; p = 0.002 ). Exposure to biological hazards ( β = 6.29 ; 95% CI: 5-7.62; p = 0.002 ) and multidimensional poverty ( β = 1.06 ; 95% CI: 0.652-1.47; p = 0.008 ) were positively associated with higher prevalence. The model explained 50 of the regional variation. Conclusions. Occupational disease in Colombia reflects profound territorial inequalities driven by the interaction between social vulnerability, occupational exposure, and organizational capacity. Strengthening the Occupational Health and Safety Management System, implementing differential epidemiological surveillance, and reducing structural gaps are key priorities to decrease the burden of occupational disease in the country. © 2027, Instituto Nacional de Salud. .
