title: Missing in action: unaddressed cost-of-illness studies in Colombia – A 30-year review; [Estudios sobre el costo de la enfermedad no abordados en Colombia: una revisión de 30 años]
abstract: Introduction. Cost studies aim to answer questions about resource use and allocation. They provide information on the magnitude of the resource use of an illness paid for by patients, providers, health insurers or systems. Objective. To systematically review cost-of-illness (COI) studies conducted in Colombia over the past 30 years to identify neglected disease areas using the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) classification. Materials and methods. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in MEDLINE, Scopus, and EMBASE up to February 2025, using standardized search terms related to cost-of-illness and Colombia. Eligible studies reported direct medical costs associated with diseases. Studies focused on cost-effectiveness, caregiver costs, or non-peer-reviewed literature were excluded. Data were extracted using a standardized form and adjusted to 2023 Colombian Pesos (COP) using the national Consumer Price Index. Studies were classified according to GBD Level 1 and 2 categories. Results. Of 257 studies screened, 44 met inclusion criteria. Mostly focused on non-communicable diseases, particularly hemophilia A, which had the highest average annual cost per patient. Rheumatologic and neurological disorders also showed high per-patient costs. Communicable diseases with significant costs included HIV/AIDS and drug-resistant infections. Pediatric studies were limited, with ICU-treated respiratory illnesses being most costly. Mental disorders, maternal and neonatal conditions, and several injury subgroups were largely unaddressed. Only 2 of the top 10 causes of DALYs in Colombia had corresponding COI studies. Conclusions. COI literature in Colombia remains fragmented and limited in scope. Standardized methodologies and targeted research are needed to guide equitable health policy and resource allocation. © 2027, Instituto Nacional de Salud. .

title: Advancing smart school initiatives: A case study of Zahedan city
abstract: This mixed-methods case study evaluates Iran's Smart Schools Project in Zahedan, a socioeconomically heterogeneous city, to identify barriers and scalable interventions for technology-enhanced schooling in resource-constrained contexts. Data comprise structured surveys (n = 150), semi-structured interviews with policymakers (n = 10), and classroom observations across urban, semi-urban and rural schools. Findings reveal stark infrastructure and access gaps (rural device-sharing 1:175; chronic power outages; intermittent urban connectivity). Targeted, low-cost interventions (solar microgrids, offline learning-management systems, and Raspberry Pi deployments) produced measurable gains (rural literacy +25%; STEM engagement +18%). Cultural resistance was substantially reduced through engagement with religious leaders, raising parental approval from 20% to 65%. Analysis is situated within TPACK (Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge) and SAMR (Substitution, Augmentation, Modification, Redefinition) frameworks. Policy implications include tiered funding that prioritizes rural allocation (proposed 60% share), promotion of domestic low-cost device manufacturing, and decentralized, context-sensitive teacher training. The study demonstrates that equity-driven, culturally attuned strategies can align national smart-school ambitions with local realities, offering a replicable model for other resource-limited regions seeking to close the urban–rural digital divide. © 2026 The Author.

title: Ambient-condition photocatalytic conversion of synthetic polymers to methane via a dual-source carbon and hydrogen strategy
abstract: Petrochemical wastes possess significant potential as “urban carbon resources,” and the sustainable production of methane (CH4) from these wastes represents an important strategy for addressing global energy supply challenges. In this study, the photocatalytic conversion of polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), used as a water-soluble model polymer, into CH4 was investigated using TiO2 photocatalysts loaded with PtOx (x = 0, 1) or PdOx (x = 0, 1) co-catalysts under ambient temperature and pressure conditions. Among the prepared photocatalysts, PtOx-TiO2 exhibited the highest CH4 production activity, achieving a CH4 concentration of 9.95 µmol L−1, which was more than ten times higher than that of PdOx-TiO2. Analysis of gaseous reaction products suggested that CH4 formation proceeded via the methanation of CO2 generated during the photocatalytic oxidation of PVA. Furthermore, deuterium-labeling experiments revealed that the hydrogen atoms in CH4 originated from both PVA and water. These findings provide a proof-of-concept for a sustainable reaction design that converts polymer-derived carbon resources into fuel molecules through coupled degradation and hydrogenation reactions within a single photocatalytic system. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Soy protein–maltodextrin conjugates as rheologically tuneable structuring agents for extrusion-based 3D food printing inks
abstract: Soy protein isolate (SPI)-based inks often exhibit a narrow processing window in extrusion-based 3D food printing because it is challenging to achieve both smooth flow under shear and rapid structural recovery after deposition. Protein–carbohydrate conjugation offers a potential means to reconcile these competing requirements. This study investigated whether SPI–maltodextrin (SPI–MD) conjugation can tune the flowability–buildability trade-off in SPI-based printable inks, compared with heat-treated and physically mixed systems. SPI–MD conjugates were prepared at SPI:MD ratios of 10:1–10:4 to systematically vary MD incorporation. The extent of glycation increased with MD content. Conjugation improved protein solubility, while decreasing water absorption capacity and increasing least gelation concentration, indicating improved dispersion but reduced bulk water retention. Rheological analysis showed that all inks exhibited shear-thinning and were predominantly elastic; however, conjugated systems exhibited reduced flow resistance and more favorable post-shear recovery than physically mixed systems. These rheological changes were reflected in printing performance: native SPI produced rough and discontinuous filaments, whereas conjugated inks enabled smoother extrusion and improved shape fidelity. Notably, C-SPI (10:3) provided the most balanced performance, achieving continuous filament formation, stable layer stacking, and sufficient vertical buildability. Conversely, excessive MD incorporation (10:4) facilitated extrusion but compromised three-dimensional stability, indicating that planar printability can be decoupled from vertical structural support. Overall, SPI–MD conjugation represents a practical formulation strategy for tuning the rheological responses and printability of plant protein-based food inks, with the optimal balance achieved at intermediate MD incorporation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Culturally responsive cognitive-behavioral therapy for black populations: a scoping review
abstract: This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize the contributions of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) to culturally responsive clinical practice addressing racial and ethnic issues, with an emphasis on the mental health of Black populations. The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute and PRISMA-ScR guidelines and included systematic searches across multiple databases and complementary sources, resulting in 22 included publications. Findings revealed a predominance of studies conducted in the United States and a notable lack of empirical research in Latin American and African contexts. Conceptual heterogeneity emerged regarding how the cultural contextualization of CBT is defined and implemented, ranging from structured adaptations of standard protocols to culturally responsive therapeutic stances integrated into case conceptualization and clinical interactions. The most frequently reported intervention domains included cognitive restructuring, coping skills training, psychoeducation, and engagement in valued activities, often accompanied by explicit validation of racism-related experiences. The literature emphasized the centrality of culturally responsive therapeutic relationships and identified structural racism and healthcare mistrust as key barriers to access and engagement. Although the field demonstrates growing methodological and clinical maturity, theoretical fragmentation and the absence of integrative conceptual models remain significant gaps, underscoring the need for further empirical research in diverse sociocultural settings. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. title: Elucidating the relationship between fluidization dynamics and reactor performance in CO methanation via weakly-compressible DEM-CFD simulations
abstract: Catalytic CO methanation is vital for synthetic natural gas production, yet its highly exothermic nature poses challenges for reactor design and thermal management. Fluidized-bed reactors offer a solution through enhanced heat transfer; however, the mechanistic relationship between mesoscale hydrodynamic structures and local reaction performance remains insufficiently understood. A coupled weakly-compressible DEM-CFD reaction model was developed and validated, accurately predicting species concentrations across conditions. Macroscopic analyses show that, given sufficient gas–solid contact time, the CH4 production rate scales linearly with gas throughput up to 30umf without compromising the thermodynamic equilibrium yield. Despite substantial heat generation at high flow rates, particle circulation maintains pseudo-isothermal conditions throughout the bed. Mesoscopic analyses reveal a fundamental trade-off: low gas velocities promote premature reactant depletion near the gas inlet, whereas high gas velocities extend the kinetics-governed regime but induce localized convective mass-transfer limitation in the upper bed due to the formation of distinct dense and dilute regions. Consequently, an intermediate solid volume fraction ((Formula presented) –0.35) emerges as the optimal regime balancing catalyst holdup and reactant accessibility. These findings demonstrate that the governing rate-limiting mechanism is determined not only by reactor height but also by the local mesoscale structure. Therefore, disrupting phase separation through reactor internals or secondary gas injection represents a key strategy for improving catalyst utilization and optimizing industrial-scale fluidized-bed methanation reactors. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Depressive symptoms, coping skills, and the perception of barriers to psychological treatment among college students
abstract: College students experience psychological symptoms at a concerning rate but infrequently access psychological treatment. However, research in this context has been incredibly limited, and the psychological factors related to perceptions of barriers to treatment are not well understood. We set out to provide an evaluation of the perceived prevalence of common barriers to psychological care, considering how perceptions of barriers are associated with depression symptoms and coping skills. Our findings were consistent with depressive symptoms being associated with greater perceived subjective and objective barriers. Interpersonal skills demonstrated small negative associations with stigma, treatment concerns, and perceived access barriers, and mindfulness skill was negatively associated with both stigma and perceived access barriers. Emotionally impaired coping was positively related to both stigma and treatment concerns. However, behavioral and cognitive skills were not correlated with any perceived barriers. We also considered how coping skills and depression symptoms interacted to predict perceptions of barriers. We found two significant interactions for perceived access barriers specifically. When cognitive or behavioral skills were greater, psychological symptoms were more strongly related to barrier perceptions. This suggests that those with greater coping skills perceive more barriers to treatment when experiencing elevated depressive symptoms compared to those with more limited coping skills. Findings from this study provide an initial characterization of barrier perceptions among college students and have the potential to inform efforts to increase treatment seeking among college students. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. title: Mapping the Global Technology Landscape and Dynamic Evolution of Artificial Intelligence-assisted Drug R&D Based on Patent Analysis
abstract: Purpose: This study investigates the global development trajectory, thematic evolution, and technological life cycle of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled drug research and development (R&D). It aims to clarify the evolutionary trajectory of the field, the leading countries and technological domains, and the current life cycle stage of the technology. Methods: Drawing on global patent data, the study integrates bibliometric analysis, social network analysis (SNA), technology life cycle (TLC) modeling, and a cross-time Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) model. A Logistic growth model is applied to estimate developmental stages and long-term saturation, while cross-time LDA identifies major technological themes and their temporal evolution. Results: Patent activity has increased sharply since 2013. The United States (40.19%) and China (32.20%) dominate global filings, with China surpassing the U.S. in annual applications by 2022–2023. India has emerged as a rapidly growing contributor. TLC analysis suggests the technology entered the growth stage in 2022 and is projected to mature around 2030, with a projected saturation of approximately 21,875 patents by 2048. Topic modeling identifies 19 themes, with dominant areas including therapeutic use prediction, physicochemical modeling, retrosynthesis prediction, multitarget drug design, and personalized medicine. The technological focus has shifted from early computer-aided design to deep learning and clinical optimization. Conclusion: The findings reflect accelerating technological convergence between AI methods and pharmaceutical innovation, pointing to strong long-term growth potential. The quantitative TLC staging and cross-time LDA provide descriptive insights that may support strategic R&D planning, investment prioritization, and policy formulation. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: MVRFDet: Malicious package detection in PyPI ecosystem using multi-view representation fusion
abstract: The widespread use of the Python Package Index has made it a primary target for malicious package poisoning attacks, seriously threatening software supply chain security. However, existing detection methods often rely on single-view features, making it difficult to cope with increasingly complex and covert attack methods, and it is difficult to achieve an effective balance between detection performance and efficiency. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel malicious package detection method called MVRFDet, based on multi-view representation fusion. Specifically, this method fuses features from three views: package metadata, global API call graph of source code and fine-grained control flow graph, and code semantic features of suspicious API code context snippets. To reduce runtime overhead, a centrality analysis and large language model are used to automatically extract a list of sensitive APIs offline, accurately locating suspicious API code context snippets. Finally, a channel attention module is designed to adaptively fuse representations from three views to achieve accurate classification. Extensive experiments on mixed datasets from multiple sources demonstrate that MVRFDet achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to eight baseline methods, with improvements in precision ranging from 2.5% to 24.8% and recall from 4% to 18.3%. Ablation studies and parameter sensitivity analyses validate the effectiveness of the model’s component design and the optimal selection of hyperparameters. Furthermore, detection efficiency evaluations show that it achieves a better trade-off between runtime overhead and detection performance. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: ST-JSCC: Synergizing structural and textural dependencies for robust and efficient image transmission
abstract: Semantic communication has emerged as a promising paradigm for next-generation intelligent communications by prioritizing semantic fidelity over conventional bit-level accuracy. Although deep joint source-channel coding (JSCC) has demonstrated strong robustness under varying channel conditions, existing methods still face a trade-off between structural preservation and textural reconstruction. Most existing approaches rely on either convolutional neural networks (CNNs) or Transformers. CNN-based methods are effective at capturing local textures but struggle to model long-range structural dependencies, while Transformer-based methods capture global information yet often fail to preserve fine-grained textures under aggressive compression. To address these limitations, we propose Structural-Textural JSCC (ST-JSCC), a novel framework that jointly exploits structural and textural representations for robust image transmission. Specifically, a parallel architecture is designed, consisting of a linear attention branch for efficient global structure modeling and a CNN branch for local texture preservation. Furthermore, a Gated Fusion Module (GFM) is introduced to adaptively integrate complementary features from both branches. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that ST-JSCC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, especially under low-SNR conditions. The source code will be made publicly available upon publication. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: Attention-based convolutional architecture for aspect-based sentiment analysis: training with text-based feature set
abstract: Sentiment analysis is the technique used to find, extract, and examine sentiments in textual data using Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) models. It is facing the challenges of accurately interpreting offensive or sarcastic language, as well as understanding cultural and context-specific expressions. To overcome this limitation, a novel Attention-Based Convolutional Architecture is implemented for an effective Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis. Initially, preprocessing takes place for cleaning the raw data for further analysis. Along with conventional techniques such as N-grams, Bag of Units, Count Vectorization, TF-IDF, a new Semantic Similarity measure and an improved Aspect Term Feature extraction technique is proposed. The enhanced Semantic Similarity is developed by combining improved Lin similarity and Wu & Palmer similarity, enabling more accurate contextual understanding. Finally for sentiment classification, an Optimization-Based Hybrid IACSNet model is designed which is an integration of Improved Attention-based Convolutional Neural Network (IACNN) and SqueezeNet to enhance learning efficiency and performance. Furthermore, to boost the classification accuracy, a novel Coati-Tuna Swarm optimization (COTS) is introduced which fine-tunes the weights of the model. The experimental studies are evaluated over three datasets, namely the Amazon product review dataset, Twitter Sentiment Analysis dataset and the Multilingual-sentiment-datasets with respect to various performance measures. The results demonstrated that the proposed model achieved an accuracy of 0.986 on the Amazon Product Review dataset, 0.963 on the Twitter Sentiment Analysis dataset, and 0.950 on the Multilingual Sentiment dataset, indicating that it outperforms the existing approaches. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Corruption via mean field games
abstract: A new mathematical model governing the development of a corrupted hierarchy is derived. This model is based on the Mean Field Games theory. A retrospective problem for that model is considered. From the applied standpoint, this problem amounts to figuring out the past activity of the corrupted hierarchy using the present data for this community. Three new Carleman estimates are derived. These estimates lead to Hölder stability estimates and uniqueness results for both that retrospective problem and its generalized version. Hölder stability estimates characterize the dependence of the error in the solution of the retrospective problem from the error in the input data. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Closed-loop versus conventional synchronization in spontaneously breathing adult patients– a randomized controlled study
abstract: Background The IntelliSync+ [IS+] algorithm provides closed-loop synchronization by continuously analyzing airway pressure and flow waveforms in real time to optimize inspiratory and expiratory cycling. This study evaluated the efficacy of IS+ compared with conventional physician-tailored synchronization during noninvasive ventilation [NIV] in spontaneously breathing adult patients with ARF. Methods This multicenter, prospective, randomized controlled, single-blind crossover trial was conducted between March 2024 and May 2025 in two tertiary hospitals. Adult patients receiving NIV for ARF were randomized to start with either conventional synchronization or IS+. Each mode was applied for 30 min, separated by a 15-min washout period. The primary outcome was the Asynchrony Index [AI], defined as the number of asynchronous events per 100 breaths. Results Compared with conventional synchronization, IS+ significantly reduced the total AI [11.8 (7.9–22.4) vs. 25.5 (12.1–35.3) events/100 breaths, p < 0.001], as well as both major and minor asynchrony indices [8.3 (4.5–16.4) vs. 17.6 (7.5–25.6), p < 0.001; 3.4 (1.5–5.4) vs. 7.6 (3.4–13.6), p < 0.001, respectively]. Dyspnea scores were significantly reduced during IS+ [3 ± 1 vs. 5 ± 1, p = 0.0001], indicating improved comfort. Conclusions Closed-loop synchronization using IS+ significantly improved patient–ventilator interaction and comfort during NIV in adults with acute respiratory failure with no adverse events observed during the study period. This study demonstrates that synchrony during NIV can be enhanced using a closed-loop algorithm alone, solely through real-time waveform analysis, without the need for additional invasive monitoring. title: Reconstructing the Life History of Double Perforated Ivory Beads from the Swabian Aurignacian: A Combined Traceological and Experimental Approach
abstract: Aurignacian ivory beads provide valuable insights into ivory-working techniques, labour investment, production organisation, and the symbolic behaviour of Early Upper Palaeolithic people. Although decades of research have led to a detailed understanding of the chaîne opératoire of these iconic beads, systematic approaches for identifying and interpreting manufacturing- and use-related traces remain limited. Using 74 double perforated ivory beads (DPIBs) from Archaeological Horizon IV at Hohle Fels Cave as a case study, we integrate taphonomic, typological, morphometric, and traceological analyses with experimental replication to develop an analytical framework for reconstructing the manufacture and use of archaeological ivory beads. Our results suggest that DPIB production followed a broadly shared production sequence while allowing flexibility in the order and execution of individual manufacturing steps. The archaeological evidence indicates that the beads were produced, used, and discarded on site. Experimental replication further provides a basis for evaluating labour investment and identifying surface modifications associated with manufacture and use. The observed morphological variability may reflect differences in production practices related to variation in skill, individual behaviour, and the involvement of multiple craftspeople. The analytical approach presented here is transferable and can be applied to other archaeological ivory bead assemblages. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Energy-efficient beamforming design for sub-connected active RIS-assisted ISAC systems
abstract: Active reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) can mitigate severe multiplicative fading through signal amplification, but fully-connected architectures consume substantial hardware power because each reflecting element requires a dedicated power amplifier (PA). This paper investigates a sub-connected active RIS (SC-ARIS)-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where multiple reflecting elements share one PA, reducing active-hardware power consumption at the cost of lower amplification-control flexibility. We formulate a highly non-convex energy efficiency (EE) maximization problem by jointly optimizing the base station transmit beamforming, radar receive filter, and SC-ARIS reflection coefficients, subject to a minimum radar signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) requirement, power budgets, and hardware constraints. To solve it, we develop an alternating optimization framework combining Dinkelbach’s method and fractional programming. By exploiting the phase freedom of the radar receive filter, the non-convex radar SNR constraint is transformed into a linear constraint on the transmit beamformer for a fixed receive filter, while projection-based recovery yields hardware-feasible SC-ARIS coefficients. Simulations show that the proposed design achieves higher EE than fully-connected and random-phase baselines, although the fully-connected benchmark attains a higher communication sum-rate. These results demonstrate a favorable trade-off among EE, ISAC performance, and active-hardware complexity. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Structure-dependent transport in ordered packed beds: pore-scale CFD analysis and Nusselt-number correlations
abstract: Ordered packed beds can enhance particle-to-fluid heat transfer while reducing hydraulic resistance, but their thermo-hydraulic behavior depends on both porosity and packing architecture. This study investigates flow reorganization, pressure gradient, and convective heat transfer in cubic, orthorhombic, and rhombohedral ordered packed beds using pore-scale CFD. A particle-layer stacking model is introduced to quantify transverse packing and axial overlap, and 27 configurations with different normalized inter-particle spacings are analyzed. Results show that packing structure governs pore connectivity and flow pathways, producing distinct thermo-hydraulic responses among bed families. In cubic beds, decreasing transverse packing weakens particle-induced flow disturbance, reducing heat-transfer coefficients by up to 51.37 % while the pressure gradient decreases substantially (maximum 362.14 %). Orthorhombic beds exhibit weak thermal sensitivity, with heat-transfer variations of 0.42–6.75 % due to compensating flow accessibility. Rhombohedral beds show the strongest structure-induced transitions: connected axial passages cause abrupt flow redistribution, heat-transfer variations of 0.84–64.81 %, and pressure-gradient variations up to 48-fold. Although local heat transfer may decrease, the larger reduction in hydraulic resistance improves overall performance, with rhombohedral beds achieving the most favorable heat-transfer-to-pressure-drop trade-off. Structure-dependent Nusselt-number correlations are developed, incorporating packing-architecture effects, with maximum deviations of 14.49 %, 3.26 %, and 9.92 % for cubic, orthorhombic, and rhombohedral beds. These results highlight the limitations of porosity-based characterization and provide a structure-aware framework for predicting and optimizing ordered packed-bed performance in chemical and thermal processes. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Quasi-real-time degradation-aware energy management for standalone PV-battery microgrids under uncertainty
abstract: Energy management in standalone photovoltaic-battery microgrids requires balancing supply reliability, forecast uncertainty, and battery degradation within tight computational budgets. This paper proposes an integrated, quasi-real-time energy management framework that couples nonlinear rolling-horizon model predictive control with three complementary mechanisms: (i) a variable-resolution dispatch layer that adapts the optimization granularity to system dynamics, (ii) an operating reserve formulation based on short-term energy-mismatch forecasts produced by dedicated Long Short-Term Memory recurrent neural networks (LSTM-RNN) for load, photovoltaic generation, and reserve estimation, and (iii) an online battery degradation assessment algorithm compatible with the optimization layer. The framework is evaluated on a standalone microgrid in Ouarzazate, Morocco, using one-second-resolution data over three representative weeks. The results reveal that the integrated degradation-aware framework does not uniformly improve dispatch performance, but rather establishes an explicit trade-off between supply reliability and battery lifetime. Under the tested configuration, the joint framework extends expected battery lifetime by approximately 218% compared to the uncertainty-only strategy (from 4.51 to 14.36 years averaged across three weeks), at the cost of a 50% relative increase in unmet load (from 19.22% to 28.78%), providing microgrid operators with a quantifiable, tunable mechanism to prioritize battery preservation when operationally justified. The proposed online cycle detection algorithm is cross-verified against pyLife's rainflow-based reference implementation across all 30 evaluated dispatch cases, showing a mean absolute cycle-count deviation of 2.68%, confirming its consistency with reference rainflow methods and its suitability for real-time embedded deployment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A three-stage interpretable linguistic group decision-making model: A perspective of combining concept lattice and adversarial interpretive structure modeling
abstract: In complex decision-making environments, linguistic group decision-making (GDM) often faces the challenge of high decision complexity as well as ensuring transparency and interpretability of decision results. To address the above challenges, this paper proposes an interpretable linguistic GDM model based on formal concept analysis (FCA) and adversarial interpretive structure modeling (AISM), which provides a three-stage framework for revealing the hierarchical relationships and directed dependencies among alternatives. Linguistic truth-valued lattice implication algebra is first utilized to represent the decision-maker’s linguistic evaluation information, which can handle both comparable and incomparable linguistic information. Second, the incorporation of Pareto frontier facilitates the identification and filtering of lower-ranked alternatives, reducing computational complexity and improving scalability in large-scale GDM scenarios. In addition, the integration of FCA and AISM enhances the interpretability of the decision-making process. Finally, a case study and experiments demonstrate the advantages of the proposed model in reducing decision complexity and improving decision interpretability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Trends in molecular gastronomy
abstract: Molecular gastronomy, a fusion of food science and culinary art, applies scientific principles to modify and transform ingredients and culinary techniques. By understanding the physical and chemical mechanisms and properties of food, scientists and researchers create various innovative foods with different, unique textures, flavors, and appearances. Recent trends in molecular gastronomy highlight the importance of eco-conscious practices by incorporating plant-based ingredients, microbes, and novel techniques to generate novel foods. Additionally, advancements in food technology, such as 3D printing, allow customization of food products with novel ingredients and complex geometric structures with personalized nutritional food products, have also evolved and developed. This paper mainly aims to focus on the recent advancements in molecular gastronomy and the recent trends in foods, with different technologies also being discussed. Different methodologies, which include foam and emulsion, gelation, smoke infusion, specification techniques, and methodologies, have been implemented in food products to improve product sustainability, product consistency, and public acceptance toward the product. Various products, such as encapsulated products, nano products, 3D printed products, functional foods, and novel foods, have also been developed with the emerging molecular gastronomy techniques. The benefits and challenges of molecular gastronomy foods and the new culinary future trends have been discussed with molecular gastronomy. © 2026

title: Survey on associative aggregation functions continuous around diagonal
abstract: This paper is the final step in the characterization of associative aggregation functions continuous around the diagonal. First, we survey all previous results concerning both commutative and non-commutative associative aggregation functions. Then we extend the result which shows that all commutative associative aggregation functions continuous around the diagonal can be expressed as a z-ordinal sum of semigroups with continuous additive generators, and show that also without commutativity, all non-commutative associative aggregation functions continuous around the diagonal can be expressed as a non-commutative ordinal sum of semigroups with continuous additive generators. Therefore, all associative aggregation functions continuous around the diagonal are characterized by inter and intra aggregation with respect to the corresponding summands. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Optimal resource control of a food chain with weak Allee effect and antipredator behaviour
abstract: The aim of this paper is to study a nonautomonous food chain model with three trophic levels: producers (plants), primary consumers (herbivores) and secondary consumers (carnivores). The model includes some realistic biological assumptions such as carrying capacity, seasonal reproduction, rigid social structure and the inclusion of antipredatory behaviour. Results concerning existence, uniqueness, positivity, uniform boundedness of the solution and local stability analysis of the (uncontrolled) model are presented. An optimal control problem related to primary consumer’s biomass is formulated. Existence and uniqueness of the optimal control is proved. Numerical simulation of both uncontrolled and controlled cases is presented. A study on the control efficiency is also presented. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: GRL-DDC: A data-driven paradigm for sustainable governance of online information propagation
abstract: Online information governance is not merely a problem of predicting diffusion outcomes, but an information-fusion-driven dynamic decision problem that requires balancing credible-information promotion, risk-oriented suppression, and benign-discussion preservation under limited resources. This paper proposes Graph Reinforcement Learning for Dual-Track Diffusion Control (GRL-DDC), a graph reinforcement learning framework for dual-track diffusion control on dynamic graphs. The core innovation of GRL-DDC lies in integrating temporal graph learning, model-based reinforcement learning, constrained intervention, influence maximization/minimization, and misinformation suppression into a unified two-stage framework for online information governance. In the first stage, a temporal graph state-transition predictor fuses observable network structure, node-level semantic states, and user behavioral features to learn short-horizon propagation-state transitions from observational graph snapshots. In the second stage, the trained transition predictor remains fixed and supports a constrained reinforcement learning policy learner that evaluates model-based counterfactual estimates and allocates promotion or suppression actions under explicit budget and action constraints. Experiments on real-world social media data show that GRL-DDC learns an interpretable asymmetric resource-allocation pattern: it prioritizes nodes that contribute to credible or constructive information diffusion while selectively suppressing negative-risk propagation at relatively low cost. These results demonstrate that GRL-DDC provides a feasible data-driven decision-support approach for resource-constrained intervention in dynamic online information diffusion. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Novel starch/agar smart bioplastic incorporated with dual-encapsulated anthocyanin for shrimp freshness monitoring
abstract: A dual-encapsulation strategy for anthocyanins (as the active core) was proposed, using chitosan hydrochloride and carboxymethyl chitosan (90, 160, and 240 kDa) as the external shell and β-cyclodextrin as the internal shell. The highest encapsulation efficiency (63.65%) was achieved in the complex constructed with carboxymethyl chitosan of 240 kDa, while that of 160 kDa enabled the complexes with superior stability against light, heat, and oxidation. Furthermore, smart bioplastics were constructed, where starch/agar networks well-entrapped the complexes by establishing new intermolecular interactions. Although the molecular weight of carboxymethyl chitosan insignificantly affected the bioplastics’ capacity to indicate shrimp freshness, all obtained bioplastics showed good color response to different pH conditions, excellent color stability at 25°C for 21 days, and reversibility. Color difference values of the bioplastics were confirmed as a reliable indicator of the edible quality of shrimp, and an artificial neural network model was successfully established between the color information (L*, a*, b*, color difference) and the related quality parameters (total volatile basic nitrogen content, pH) of shrimp. Findings support the application of such bioresource-based smart bioplastics in the seafood packaging field. © 2026

title: Collective Action and Efficiency Loss? The Role of Kinship in Multi-Household Grassland Management on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau
abstract: By facilitating cooperation, the multi-household management pattern (MHMP) enables some household members to engage in non-agricultural employment and is often assumed to enhance production efficiency. However, empirical evidence on its actual efficiency effects remains limited. Drawing on survey data from 156 herder households in Maqu County on the QTP collected between November 2021 and March 2022, this study applies an output-oriented Data Envelopment Analysis combined with Tobit regression to examine the impact of MHMP on production efficiency. The results show that participation in MHMP is associated with lower production efficiency. Labor reallocation from animal husbandry to non-agricultural activities explains this negative relationship. Moreover, strong kinship ties intensify the efficiency loss, as households embedded in close kinship networks tend to adopt more lenient norms regarding effort. While kinship-based cooperation facilitates collective action, it simultaneously reinforces relational norms that weaken performance-oriented incentives. These findings highlight a critical trade-off between social cohesion and production efficiency in collective pasture management. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Enhancing Agricultural Extension Access: The Role of Different Extension Media in Climate-Vulnerable Areas of Bangladesh
abstract: Enhancing rural productivity and resilience depends heavily on agricultural extension services, which support farmers in climate-vulnerable regions. This research examines how different farmer characteristics affect access to agricultural information through three channels: individual, group, and mass media. A cross-sectional survey of 820 farm households across the High Barind Tract and the southwest coastal and southeastern hilly regions of Bangladesh used random sampling for data collection. Researchers then analyzed the data with descriptive statistics and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial (ZINB) and Tobit regression models to identify determinants across the three communication channels. According to the results, human capital (education, experience) and social capital (organizational participation) remain the strongest and most consistent drivers of farmers’ multi-channel access to agricultural extension services. Age negatively influenced engagement, while farming experience enhanced contact. The majority of farmers relied on informal networks, including progressive farmers and neighbors, but showed minimal interaction with official extension agents and digital resources. Older and less-educated participants displayed restricted use of mass media. The study establishes that effective extension strategies require educational development, organizational engagement, and demographic adjustments. The successful delivery of agricultural information requires both formal service expansion and digital literacy education, as well as reinforcement of community-based learning platforms in climate-vulnerable regions. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Traditional Ecological Knowledge in Sustaining Mobile Pastoralism of Türkiye
abstract: Traditional ecological knowledge (TEK) underpins sustainable pastoralism by guiding livestock mobility, resource management, and climate adaptation. However, in Eastern Anatolia, Türkiye, TEK is increasingly marginalized by socio-economic change and restrictive land-use policies. This study documents the TEK held by mobile pastoralists in Eastern Anatolia, Türkiye, and examines how it informs herd mobility, pasture use, and weather-related decision-making. Ethnographic fieldwork was conducted between February and April 2024 across Diyarbakır and neighboring provinces, involving structured interviews, participatory observations, and focus group discussions with 20 mobile pastoralists. Qualitative and descriptive statistical analyses were used to identify patterns in decision-making related to migration, pasture selection, and weather forecasting. Within this small, purposive sample, pastoralists reported weighing pasture condition (75%), weather conditions (55%), and water availability (15%) when planning migration and grazing. Traditional forecasting relied on ecological indicators, including star density (65%), cloud formations around the moon (60%), and animal behavior (20%). These practices reveal an embedded ecological literacy that integrates environmental perception with kin-based decision-making. Yet declining interest in pastoralism among younger community members, land privatization, conservation restrictions, and other socio-economic constraints threaten TEK continuity. TEK functions not merely as inherited knowledge but as a living body of practice that supports pastoral communities within their own socio-ecological systems. Integrating TEK into contemporary rangeland management could enhance sustainability, climate preparedness, and the long-term viability of pastoral livelihoods in semi-arid environments. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Contesting Interests Between Institutional Pluralism and People-Centred Development in Natural Resource Management: Lessons from Selous Niassa Wildlife Corridor in Tanzania
abstract: The debate on institutional pluralism (IP) in relation to natural resources management and people-centred development has become significant in Tanzania and many other developing countries. Mostly, the debates are related to the challenges of balancing conservation goals with people-centred development pathways in natural resources management. The theory of Self-Governance explains how the central government manages resources in community-owned areas. Data were gathered from national- and local-level government, non-governmental, and private-sector institutions relevant to the study, particularly those predominantly involved in natural resources management. The study utilized key informant interviews (KIIs), focus group discussions (FGDs), and household surveys in villages within the Selous-Niassa wildlife corridor (SNWC). The KII and FGD data were analysed using content analysis, and descriptive statistics were computed for the household interview data using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS). The results indicate that the evolution of institutional pluralism progressed through distinct stages, both before and after independence. During the pre-independence period, indigenous knowledge and practices for managing natural resources were destroyed, giving the colonial government power, even though it did not ensure sustainable management. This remained the same until the 1990s, when decentralization and Community-Based Resource Management were established (1990s - present). Tanzania saw increased recognition of the role of institutional pluralism in natural resource management. However, the increased recognition did not align with the current management status of natural resources in the SNWC, where degradation is accelerating due to increased human development. This paper concludes that natural resource management under institutional pluralism is influenced by communities’ development ambitions. This paper calls for strategies that balance the goals of natural resource management and development and recommends natural recovery measures. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.
label: Social Sciences

title: The Influence of Tswana Cosmological worldview and Sacred Beliefs on the Spatial Organization of Traditional Settlements: A Study of the Setswana Traditional Space kgotla
abstract: This study examines how Tswana cosmology and sacred beliefs shaped the spatial organization, social structure, and geography of traditional settlements, focusing on the Setswana kgotla as the central sociopolitical, ritual, and spiritual space. Although the kgotla has undergone substantial functional and physical transformation through colonization, modernization, and contemporary planning, its historical development provides important insight into the principles underlying Tswana settlement planning. Using an interpretive qualitative approach based on historical documents, classic ethnographic literature, comparative spatial analysis, field observations, and oral accounts from six historically significant Tswana villages in Botswana—Kanye, Mochudi, Molepolole, Maun, Serowe, and Ramotswa—this study investigates the sacred and social principles governing settlement organization, including the location of the kgosi’s ward, the centrality of the kgotla, geographic setting, cardinal orientation, hierarchical ward structure, spatial configuration, and threshold treatments. The findings show that traditional Tswana settlements were shaped not only by practical and defensive needs but also by a cosmological order in which authority, ancestry, community, environmental relationships, and protection were expressed through space. Rather than serving solely as a traditional court, the kgotla functioned as the symbolic center where the moral, political, and sacred dimensions of Tswana society converged. The study argues that Tswana spatial organization is best understood as a dynamic system shaped by cosmology, environmental knowledge, and historical change rather than as a fixed symbolic structure. It further demonstrates that precolonial Tswana settlement planning embodied an Indigenous system of spatial knowledge rooted in concepts of hierarchy, enclosure, ecology, and social affiliation. Reconsidering the cosmological foundations of the kgotla therefore provides valuable insights into Indigenous settlement planning and contributes to broader discussions of culturally grounded, context-responsive approaches to spatial organization. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Livelihood Diversification and Migration Amid Climatic Risk Perception in Slash-and-Burn Agroecology in Northeast India: A Case Study
abstract: Slash-and-burn agriculture in tropical forests is widely debated in the context of net-zero carbon emissions and global warming. In India, approximately two million hill tribes practice slash-and-burn agriculture, locally called jhumming, across 11 million hectares, with a high concentration in Northeast India. The present study aims to assess climatic risk perception in jhumming in Northeast India, examine livelihood diversification and labor migration as part of livelihood strategies, and finally propose policy measures to address the crisis. This is a case study based on a field investigation of 352 tribal households in Manipur, one of the Northeast Indian states where jhumming is predominant. The study finds that soil erosion, declining soil fertility, monsoon vagaries, and summer temperatures are the predominant perceived risks in cultivation. There are also non-ecological issues, such as market inaccessibility and infrastructure deficits. Approximately 72% of households have ‘zero’ income diversification, specializing in a single activity—farming. Rural non-farm diversification is very challenging here; customary land rights and physiography are key bottlenecks. Labor migration—accounting for around 36% of households—to urban centers contributes substantially to non-farm income diversification. Vertical crop diversification—value addition to existing crops and market linkage—would be a policy suggestion. It will enhance farmers’ income and make farming sedentary, resulting in a longer fallow period and a well-developed secondary forest. Meanwhile, organized labor migration can be placed in the policy arena, which has double benefits—minimizing livelihood crises and reducing pressure on forest resources. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Preserving Sacred Forests and Rivers in Abanyom, Cross River State, Nigeria: Is the Environmental Worldview Eco-Centric, Anthropocentric or Relational?
abstract: The debate surrounding the ethical nature of the African environmental worldview remains inconclusive, with some scholars arguing that it is primarily eco-centric, while others claim that it is largely anthropocentric. Using the case study of Abanyom’s preservation of sacred forests and rivers, we revisited this debate by exploring the taboos and rituals associated with these sacred sites as well as the motivations for their preservation. The study conducted in-depth interviews with 15 community members (comprising traditional leaders, clan heads and chief priests) and analysed the data thematically. The findings reveal that the Abanyom community’s environmental worldview cannot be strictly classified as either eco-centric or anthropocentric. Instead, the worldview is best categorised under the relational value framework, an “in-between” category that incorporates elements from both perspectives. The study recommends utilising the relational value framework in future research on African relationships with nature and in formulating environmental sustainability policies on the continent. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: The Resource, Users’ Socio-economic Status, and Governance in Coastal Marine Benthic Mollusk fisheries in Costa Grande, Guerrero, Mexico
abstract: The mollusks caught by coastal fishing were analyzed as a resource, as well as the socioeconomic condition of the fishermen involved in this activity, who are members of the fishing cooperatives of the Costa Grande of the state of Guerrero. The objectives were to be acquainted with the list of species fished for human consumption, determine those of greatest economic importance, analyze the socioeconomic characteristics of the fishermen, and determine the current state of the mollusk resource based on the fishermen’s perception. The specimens were acquired from landing zones and restaurants, and a total of 27 surveys were conducted with fishermen, members of fishing cooperatives in the region. A total of 24 species of mollusks were identified; 10 were the target species for fishing, and seven species were not economically profitable for fishermen. Striostrea prismatica, Trochita trochiformis, and Hexaplex princeps generate more income annually. Five species have been excluded from the list of catches: Megapitaria squalida, Periglypta multicostata, Pinctada mazatlanica, Malea ringens, and the giant limpet Scutellastra mexicana. There was no evidence of generational replacement in the fishing activity. The fishermen’s income is sufficient to cover their basic needs and those of their families. The current regulations are insufficient. There is an urgent need to carry out technical-scientific and biological research to provide relevant information that can be used to implement measures for the appropriate use and regulation of mollusk fisheries in the region. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Revisiting the Agropastoral Landscape of Çatalhöyük East Through Agent-Based Modeling (9100–8100 BP)
abstract: Understanding the complex interplay between external climatic forcing and internal socioecological dynamics remains a major challenge in the study of early sedentary societies. While unilinear frameworks frequently link systemic shifts to external climate triggers, these perspectives tend to neglect the internal dynamics and non-linear feedback loops of complex socioecological systems (SES). This research sheds new light on established narratives by investigating the 1000-year coevolution of agropastoral practices and landscape dynamics at Çatalhöyük East (ca. 9100–8100 BP). We employ a high-resolution agent-based model (ABM), integrating the MedLanD (MML) platform with the Macrophysical Climate Model (MCM) via an original sequential simulation design. This methodological novelty allows us to quantify how cumulative land-use legacies and their environmental costs shaped the community’s later options. Our results indicate that while the agricultural strategy effectively sustained high population density, it simultaneously pushed the system toward a rigidity trap. The model demonstrates how short-term adaptive successes generate structural limits in landscape capacity. These findings suggest that the settlement’s eventual reorganization was not a simple response to external climatic forcing but rather an emergent outcome of internal socioecological stress. By reframing the trajectory of Çatalhöyük through a complex systems lens, this study emphasizes that resilience must be understood as a dynamic process shaped by the long-term interaction of human agency and landscape evolution. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Gut-joint axis mediates susceptibility to osteoarthritis in female adult offspring rats with prenatal caffeine exposure
abstract: Prenatal caffeine exposure (PCE) is closely associated with the susceptibility to adult osteoarthritis, but the mechanisms underlying the gut microbiota remain unclear. In this study, the postnatal weeks (PW) 12 and 36 PCE female offspring rats showed decreased articular cartilage mass, increased modified Mankin's score, decreased matrix synthesis, elevated local inflammatory factors in articular cartilage, and increased matrix degradation. Furthermore, the gut microbiota of PCE female offspring rats was disturbed, which was primarily characterized by decreased butyric acid-producing bacteria (such as Butyricimonas and Romboutsia). The short-chain fatty acid metabolic profile also confirmed that decreased serum butyric acid levels in the PCE group were significantly correlated with the expression of essential genes of the osteoarthritis phenotype. The fecal microbiota transplantation experiment confirmed that the altered gut microbiota in PCE offspring rats induced osteoarthritis phenotype. Supplementation with sodium butyrate can alleviate the osteoarthritis phenotype caused by PCE in female adult offspring rats. © 2026

title: Transforming noncooperative behavior with dynamic trust and weight incentives mechanism in social network group emergency decision making
abstract: In emergency disaster response, resource allocation conflicts stemming from functional specialization often trigger noncooperative behaviors that severely compromise group decision-making efficiency. Existing social network group decision-making methods face two critical limitations: static trust models fail to capture the dynamic evolution of decision-makers’ credibility, and penalty mechanisms tend to provoke psychological resistance in high-pressure environments. To address these issues, this study develops an incentive-driven consensus framework. The approach integrates subjective trust relationships with objective behavioral similarity to construct a dynamically updated composite trust scoring mechanism, which enables adaptive allocation of decision makers’ weights. Furthermore, it introduces a harmony degree-based feedback mechanism incorporating a maximum individual cooperation willingness detection model to accurately identify noncooperative decision-makers. The core contribution lies in its weight incentive mechanism, which stimulates cooperation by increasing the decision weights of noncooperators, thereby transforming the traditional penalty paradigm into a reputation-based incentive paradigm. Case studies and comparative analyses demonstrate that the framework not only achieves consensus at lower adjustment but also effectively transforms noncooperative behavior into proactive collaboration while ensuring fairness. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Multi-source observational data fusion for imputing missing confounders in debiased recommendation
abstract: In recommender systems, selective interactions between users and items introduce selection bias. This leads to distributional shifts between training and test data, hindering the learning of users’ true preferences. When features that influence both the user selection mechanism and the feedback, referred to as confounders, are unobserved, hidden confounding arises and further complicates debiasing. In this study, we first highlight that unobserved confounders introduce errors in both outcome modeling and propensity estimation. Existing solutions primarily neglect the former issue, address the latter topic, and thus lead to inaccurate recommendations. Moreover, current methods often rely on untestable assumptions about hidden confounding or require costly auxiliary data, which limits their practical applicability. To address these challenges, we propose a two-stage debiasing framework leveraging multiple observational datasets. These datasets contain both shared confounders (e.g., mandatory information) and source-specific confounders (e.g., optional inputs). In the first stage, we identify each sample’s adaptive neighborhood to impute missing confounders. We aggregate these confounders using weights that incorporate spatial structure and neighbor reliability. In the second stage, we enhance the classical IPS debiasing method with a differentiable expected calibration error (DECE) loss. This loss mitigates potential imputation errors from the first stage. Experiments on public datasets demonstrate that our framework effectively alleviates selection bias under hidden confounding and consistently outperforms existing approaches. Copyright © 2026. title: Exploring the Dissolution-enhancement Functionality of Poloxamer 407 in Cilostazol Tablets Prepared by Different Manufacturing Techniques
abstract: Purpose: Investigating the impact of different manufacturing techniques on the dissolution-enhancement functionality of poloxamer 407 for the improvement of the release of the poorly water-soluble model drug Cilostazol. Methods: Formulations containing increasing levels of poloxamer 407 (0%, 5.0%, 10%, and 20% w/w) were prepared using direct compression (DC), wet granulation (WG), and hot-melt extrusion (HME). Powder blends were assessed for their compressibility and flowability. Additionally, particle size distribution (PSD) was determined by the laser diffraction technique. Compressed tablets from various powder blends were evaluated for hardness, weight, thickness, disintegration, and dissolution. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) was performed for identification of the drug’s solid state. Results: DC trials yielded no appreciable improvement in dissolution. Whereas the WG trials had an improved performance at 5.0% w/w of poloxamer 407. Dissolution results with further enhancement were achieved with 10% of poloxamer 407 in both WG and HME trials. At higher levels of the polymer, WG tablets exhibited a slower dissolution rate compared with those produced by HME. Both WG and HME methods improved the physical properties of the drug blends with a slight advantage for HME. DSC analysis of the different blends showed no detected changes in the crystalline solid state of the drug. Conclusion: Findings highlight the necessity of optimizing the levels of poloxamer 407 during different manufacturing methods to enhance polymer wettability, thereby improving the dissolution of poorly soluble drugs. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Academic self-handicapping in education: reconceptualizing it as a central psychological mechanism through a systematic review
abstract: This study synthesizes empirical findings on academic self-handicapping (ASH) in educational contexts using a systematic literature review (SLR) of 30 articles retrieved from major international databases. The review aims to identify antecedent factors, examine the role of ASH as a psychological mechanism, and analyze its impact on academic and psychological outcomes. The findings indicate that ASH is a complex and multidimensional phenomenon shaped by the interaction of psychological, motivational, and contextual factors, including academic anxiety, low self-control, performance-avoidance orientation, weak self-regulation, and social pressure. More importantly, ASH operates as a core psychological mechanism that links antecedent variables to outcomes, functioning as a psychological bottleneck that constrains positive resources and as a risk-amplifying mechanism that intensifies negative academic and psychological consequences. Although intervention-based research remains limited, preliminary intervention evidence suggests that cognitive- and emotion-focused approaches, including CBT, REBT, and ACT, may help reduce academic self-handicapping; however, the limited number of intervention studies precludes firm comparative conclusions. This study contributes by shifting the understanding of ASH from a variable-based construct toward a process-oriented psychological mechanism within the academic system. The findings highlight the need for future research to develop contextually grounded and intervention-focused approaches that explicitly target ASH to improve students’ academic success and psychological well-being. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive

title: Optimizing melt–stretch properties in yeast protein vegan mozzarella analogues through protein–starch interactions
abstract: The role of yeast protein (YP) in structuring Mozzarella-type vegan cheese analogues was investigated through its interactions with tapioca starch in composite gel systems. YP exhibited a lower water-holding capacity and smaller particle size (measured in 1%, w/w protein dispersions) than conventional plant proteins, which significantly influenced subsequent gel formation and functionality. Cheese analogues were formulated at varying YP:starch ratios (9:12, 12:9, 15:6, and 18:3), and their physicochemical rheological, microstructural, and functional properties were systematically evaluated. The YP:starch ratio critically governed the network structure, water distribution, lipid organization, and phase stability. At low YP levels, a starch-dominated matrix containing a high proportion of loosely held water lacked a continuous protein network, resulting in limited meltability and stretchability. An intermediate YP:starch ratio (15:6) produced a homogeneous co-continuous protein–starch network with balanced water immobilization and controlled lipid distribution, resulting in the greatest meltability and stretchability. At the highest ratio (18:3), elevated intermolecular β-sheet content was associated with protein aggregation, structural heterogeneity, water over-immobilization, and enlarged lipid domains. These findings demonstrate that the thermo-mechanical functionality of vegan cheese analogues is governed primarily by the structural integration of protein, starch, water, and lipid phases, rather than by protein content alone, providing mechanistic insights for the rational design of high-protein vegan cheese analogues. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Topological signal processing over product cell complexes
abstract: Topological signal processing (TSP) is a framework that leverages algebraic topology to model and analyze signals on complex networks. Recently, TSP has been successfully applied to the analysis of signals in cell complexes, providing an effective approach for processing signals in complex networks. In numerous practical scenarios, it is common to handle multidimensional signals with spatiotemporal characteristics, particularly when these signals are represented using product structures. To facilitate effective modeling of spatiotemporal signals in cell complexes, we propose a novel framework based on product cell complexes to extend the TSP to higher-dimensional structures. We first formalize the definition of product cell complexes and derive their boundary operators, Hodge Laplacians, and Fourier transforms of product cell complexes. Additionally, we present an algorithm for inferring the structure of product cell complexes from data, achieving a trade-off between sparsity and accuracy. Leveraging the Hodge decomposition, the edge signal reconstruction problem is transformed into constrained optimization, and we further design an FIR filter targeting the solenoidal component of edge signals by leveraging the properties of the product cell complex Laplacian. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms approaches based on product simplicial complexes, product graphs, and non-product structures, thereby validating its effectiveness. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Transformation–conditioning Heckman-type selection models with extended skew-elliptical errors: mathematical characterization, computational aspects, and applications
abstract: In bivariate sample-selection problems, the outcome is observed only for selected units, so misspecification of the joint selection–outcome error distribution can affect estimation and inference. Classical Heckman-type specifications are often based on Gaussian or symmetric error structures, which limits their ability to represent skewness, tail behavior, and support restrictions. We develop a transformation–conditioning, or hidden-truncation, construction for bivariate models that yields a unified extended skew-elliptical class, including skew-normal, skew-Student–t, log-skew-elliptical, Birnbaum–Saunders–elliptical, sinh-type, unit-type, and related distributions. The approach combines strictly monotone componentwise transformations, including support-changing cases, with hidden truncation in a single likelihood-based framework, and evaluates the hidden-truncation factor through the conditional distribution induced by the chosen elliptical generator rather than through a universal Gaussian-type standardization. This generator-aware formulation separates raw latent hidden-truncation quantities from the normalized effective parameters that enter the observed density, clarifying identifiability and the Gaussian-alignment case. We embed the resulting distribution in a Heckman-type threshold-selection model, derive the observed-data likelihood, and establish maximum-likelihood consistency and asymptotic normality under explicit regularity and population identification conditions. The reported implementation uses smooth reparameterizations, data-based multi-start optimization, and low-dimensional Gaussian or Student–t probability evaluations for the extended skew-normal (ESN) and extended skew-Student–t (EST) cases considered. Monte Carlo recovery experiments and synthetic benchmark comparisons with normal, symmetric Student–t, contaminated-normal, ESN, and EST Heckman specifications show a regime-dependent likelihood–penalty tradeoff. The results position the proposed class as an expanded modeling toolkit to be used alongside simpler benchmarks, with model choice guided by likelihood, information criteria, parsimony, convergence, and boundary diagnostics. An application to the Mroz87 dataset illustrates nesting, interpretation, and model comparison on a common likelihood scale. The computational workflows are implemented in reproducible R code. © The Author(s) under exclusive licence to Sociedade Brasileira de Matemática Aplicada e Computacional 2026.

title: Translation and Transcultural Adaptation of the Monitor-Blunter Dental Scale (MBDS) into Brazilian Portuguese
abstract: Objective: To translate and culturally adapt The Monitor Blunter Dental Scale (MBDS) into Brazilian Portuguese. Material and Methods: The MBDS assesses the extent to which children report using monitoring and blunting strategies and whether dental-specific coping styles can be identified. It consists of four scenarios. Children are asked to imagine each situation and tick all strategies that would apply to them. For each item, there are equal numbers of monitoring and inattention strategies (three each). Results: Most children interviewed in the pre-test were boys (65%), with ages equally divided between 8-9 and 10-12 years. In the application, five questions were marked as “I didn’t understand” by at least one participant, but no item exceeded the 15% misunderstanding limit. Only boys reported doubts, and most children who indicated difficulty in at least one item were aged 8–9. In the pre-test, all items were understood by at least 85% of the children. Conclusion: The MBDS was well understood by children treated at a university dental clinic and was considered properly translated into Brazilian Portuguese and culturally adapted to the evaluated population. © 2027, Association of Support to Oral Health Research (APESB). .

title: Enhanced adaptive SRF-PLL-based robust synchronization and control of grid-integrated PV-battery systems for seamless mode transition under distorted grid conditions
abstract: Synchronization problems, harmonic distortion, and power regulation problems are likely to occur in grid-integrated SPVA-BES microgrids serving nonlinear loads due to changing grid conditions. A dual-mode approach, EAFF-SRF-PLL, has been introduced for the grid-integrated SPVA-BES microgrid, which operates in both grid-connected and standalone modes. In the synchronization loop, adaptive gain scheduling, along with a frequency feed-forward estimation technique, has been used to maintain phase-locking capability under distorted, unbalanced, and nonlinear grid conditions. A supervisory energy management strategy controls the BDDC and grid-connected VSC based on the battery SOC status and BES availability. The performance of the controller is tested under harmonic distortion, varying loads, irradiation, unbalanced voltages, frequency deviations, PV unavailability, and mode transitions. The results of CHIL experiments employing an STM32F407G-DISC1 controller with an OPAL-RT OP4512 real-time simulator include the following: a synchronization time of 5 ms, a phase ripple of 0.78%, and a grid current total harmonic distortion of 2.7%. Compared with traditional SRF-PLL and DDSRF-PLL, the proposed algorithm achieves better synchronization accuracy and transient response. Harmonic voltage and current obtained from the test results meet the criteria of IEEE Std. 519. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Mechanistic insights into tandem reaction kinetics in PMS activation by manganese-based poly(ionic liquid) for oxidative removal of dibenzothiophene
abstract: A manganese-based polymeric ionic liquid catalyst, P[BVIM]MnCl3, was synthesized for PMS activation toward the deep oxidative removal of dibenzothiophene (DBT) under mild conditions. Unlike conventional endpoint evaluations, this study established a time-resolved GC–MS sampling strategy combined with consecutive first-order kinetic modeling, enabling the simultaneous determination of apparent rate constants, steady-state radical concentrations, and radical lifetimes from a single experiment. A global kinetic model incorporating radical consumption by the intermediate DBTO was further developed, revealing that intermediate accumulation-induced feedback inhibition is the key rate-limiting factor for overall desulfurization. Selective quenching experiments coupled with kinetic analysis demonstrated the differentiated roles of SO4•− and •OH: SO4•− dominated the initial DBT oxidation, contributing over 95%, whereas •OH mainly promoted DBTO oxidation to DBTO2. A radical generation efficiency parameter and multi-index evaluation system were established to elucidate the diminishing benefits and trade-offs associated with catalyst and PMS dosages. Under optimized conditions (30℃, 35 mg catalyst, and 0.5 g PMS), 97.3% desulfurization was achieved with an apparent activation energy of 17.1 kJ·mol−1. This work provides mechanistic insights into the Mn-based polymeric ionic liquid/PMS system and methodological guidance for the design and kinetic evaluation of oxidative desulfurization catalysts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Kronecker product overdetermined independent vector analysis for online blind source separation
abstract: Online blind source separation is essential for real-time speech communication and human-machine interaction. Among existing solutions, overdetermined independent vector analysis (OverIVA) has demonstrated superior separation performance by jointly exploiting source independence and the orthogonal constraint between the source and noise subspaces. However, when employed with large microphone arrays, the dimensionality of the separation filters grows rapidly, which poses significant challenges for reliable parameter estimation in online implementations. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a generalized Kronecker product decomposition for online OverIVA, in which each source extraction filter is represented as a sum of multiple Kronecker products of shorter sub-filters. The proposed formulation introduces an explicit Kronecker order that flexibly controls the model rank, enabling a smooth trade-off between representation capability and parameter efficiency. An efficient alternating optimization algorithm based on iterative projection is derived to estimate the structured extraction filters in an online manner. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves improved separation performance and enhanced robustness. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Inhibition of histone deacetylases accelerates wound healing in diabetic skin and is associated with vascularization and epidermal tight junction protein expression
abstract: Background: Chronic wounds in diabetic patients, represent a significant clinical challenge due to impaired epidermal barrier function and deficient wound healing. The development of novel therapeutic strategies aimed at enhancing both barrier integrity and wound healing is therefore critical. Recent evidence suggests that histone deacetylase inhibitors (iHDACs) may modulate wound healing. Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of iHDACs, 1,3-Diphenylurea (DiPU), 2′-Aminoacetanilide (Ace), and Tert-butyl (2-aminophenyl) carbamate (N-boc), on epidermal barrier integrity and tight junction (TJ) protein expression, as well as their ability to promote wound healing and vascularization under diabetes conditions. Methods: Diabetes was induced in mice by streptozotocin (STZ) administration. Full-thickness excisional wounds were created, and wound closure was quantified by digital planimetry. Tissue samples were analyzed by H&E and Masson's trichrome staining to assess histological changes and collagen deposition. claudin-1, ZO-1, and occludin were evaluated by immunohistochemistry. Vascularization was quantified by measuring microvessel density. Results: Treatment with iHDACs improved re-epithelialization and increased the expression of tight junction proteins, suggesting restoration of molecular components associated with epidermal barrier integrity. Moreover, all treatments promoted wound closure. Macroscopic observations and quantitative analyses further demonstrated that N-boc and Ace significantly enhanced the formation of denser and more organized vascular networks in both healthy and diabetic mice, whereas DiPU produced a more moderate pro-angiogenic response in diabetic wounds. Conclusion: These findings indicate that iHDACs may offer therapeutic benefit by reinforcing epidermal barrier function and stimulating wound healing and vascularization, supporting their potential use as treatments for chronic wounds. © 2026
