title: Universal speech steganalysis via coupled-domain progressive fusion
abstract: Existing universal speech steganalysis methods are generally constrained by an inherent trade-off between detection generalization across multiple steganographic encoding domains and domain-specific discriminative performance. This limitation is particularly pronounced in scenarios where heterogeneous encoding domains and diverse embedding strategies coexist. To address this, we propose a novel universal speech steganalysis scheme based on Coupled-Domain Progressive Fusion (CDPF), which constructs a correlation-aware, multi-level fusion strategy to alleviate information drift while preserving domain-specific cues. The scheme is inspired by the biological perfusion process, in which beneficial substances are progressively transmitted through microcirculatory pathways in an adaptive manner. First, to determine an optimal propagation order of informative patterns across domains, inter-domain associations are quantitatively characterized using the maximal information coefficient and cosine correlation coefficient, providing guidance for CDPF’s progressive fusion. Second, to extract domain-specific representations, CDPF incorporates encoding-domain decoupling blocks built on liquid neural networks with closed-form dynamics, enabling effective modeling of temporal dependencies in speech signals. Third, to achieve fine-grained inter-domain coupling, extracted features are adaptively fused via perfusion blocks leveraging deformable convolutional networks, facilitating flexible feature alignment. Fourth, to enhance discriminative capability for hard-to-distinguish samples, a heavy-tail expansion and projection block is introduced. Finally, a domain-consistent classifier is employed to jointly optimize and unify cross-domain representations. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that CDPF achieves consistently superior performance in both multi-domain and specific-domain detection scenarios, confirming its effectiveness and robustness for universal speech steganalysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Development and test-retest reliability of a laboratory-based shipboard firefighting simulation for controlled performance testing
abstract: Understanding shipboard firefighting performance is critical for improving crew safety and vessel preservation during damage control events. While prior research has been conducted in naval spaces, controlled simulations that assess performance without requiring naval vessels, personnel or specialised equipment are lacking. This study was designed to both develop and test a laboratory-based shipboard firefighting simulation. Consistent with shipboard firefighting activities, the simulation included walking, stair climbing, hose dragging, simulated boundary cooling, extinguisher carrying and casualty dragging tasks, completed within 8 min. Twenty-seven participants (22 males, 5 females) performed the simulation twice, with good test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.78; SEM = 17.6 s). Compared to Session 1, time-to-completion was 2.6% faster, RPE was 12.2% higher, HR was 5% lower, and core temperature estimate was 0.8% lower in Session 2 (all p < 0.05). This simulation provides a practical, low-cost solution for conducting shipboard firefighting research using minimal space, equipment, and untrained subjects. Copyright © 2026. title: Biofeedback in musicians: A systematic review and meta-analysis of its effects on muscle activity, musculoskeletal health, and performance
abstract: Musicians are at high risk for playing-related musculoskeletal disorders (PRMD) and playing- or performance-related pain (PRP), which can severely interfere with their practice routine, rehearsals, and performance. Although biofeedback offers a promising approach to address these problems, it has not been widely implemented into music education or practice, underscoring the need for a comprehensive assessment of its efficacy for physiological, health, and performance outcomes. We conducted a pre-registered systematic search of 9 electronic databases, yielding 3041 published works, and included 49 studies on biofeedback in musicians that reported outcomes related to muscle activity, musculoskeletal health, or performance. After extracting relevant data, we performed a meta-analysis of 36 studies using Bayesian mixed-effects models to evaluate effects across time (pre- vs. post), condition (biofeedback vs. comparator conditions, including traditional practice), and type of outcome. Across the selected studies, we found compelling evidence that biofeedback improves muscle activity (primarily reflected as reductions in activation), performance, and musculoskeletal health, indicating its potential to address PRMD and PRP symptoms, while also targeting relevant risk factors and supporting overall performance quality. These findings suggest that biofeedback-driven body awareness and physiological regulation can form the foundation for effective and sustainable performance. Successful implementation, however, will require collaboration between scientists, educators, and musicians to integrate biofeedback into pedagogical practice, supporting both performance and physical wellbeing. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Effectiveness of mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for individuals with premenstrual syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a common condition affecting women of reproductive age, characterized by a variety of physical, emotional, and behavioral symptoms that can significantly disrupt daily life and overall well-being. Given the limitations of traditional pharmacological treatments, there is a growing interest in exploring non-pharmacological interventions. Objective: The present systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to assess the effectiveness of mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) in reducing PMS symptoms and enhancing psychological health. Methods: The review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was performed across eight academic databases to identify studies evaluating the impact of MBCT on PMS-related outcomes. The eligibility criteria were developed based on the PICOS framework, focusing on women diagnosed with PMS who underwent MBCT. Of the 1,213 papers initially identified, five randomized controlled trials and one before-after feasibility study met the inclusion criteria, involving a total of 384 participants. Meta-analyses were performed using a random-effects model, and effect sizes were reported as standardized mean differences (SMD) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: Meta-analysis of three randomized controlled trials showed a significant reduction in PMS symptoms (SMD = -1.74, 95% CI: −2.13 to −1.35; I2 = 0%). Meta-analysis of two randomized controlled trials showed significant improvement in health-related quality of life (SMD = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.51 to 1.27; I2 = 29.96%). Narrative synthesis of secondary outcomes (depression, anxiety, health-promoting behaviors, work-related quality of life, PMS impact in daily life, and mindfulness) also suggested potential benefits of MBCT. Conclusion: Preliminary evidence suggests that MBCT may alleviate PMS symptoms and improve psychological well-being. However, the limited number of studies, methodological limitations (particularly lack of blinding and inadequate randomization procedures), and restricted geographical representation (five of the six studies were conducted in Iran) warrant cautious interpretation. Larger, methodologically rigorous, and geographically diverse randomized controlled trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive

title: Performing Power and Transitional Space: the Use of Acoustics and Multimodal AI in Etruscan Painted Tombs
abstract: This article presents a new multimodal AI and acoustic methodology using two 5th c. BCE Etruscan painted tombs at Tarquinia, Italy, the Tomba del Gallo and the Tomba dei Demoni Azzurri as case studies. Via the integration of AI computer vision–based visual saliency analysis, architectural affordance modelling, acoustic data, and agent-based perceptual trajectories, the study suggests that each tomb affords distinct experiential strategies. The Tomba del Gallo privileges visual sequencing, threshold control, and gaze discipline, whereas the Tomba dei Demoni Azzurri potentially induces perceptual disorientation and immerses the visitor into a sensory and spatial environment that has the possibility of inducing trance-like experiences. A central contribution of the study is the reinterpretation of subterranean funerary spaces as possible transitional spaces, where architectural and symbolic devices mediate between life and death, order and chaos, memory and transformation, and sensory manipulation operate as core ritual technologies. Ultimately, we argue that when combined with scientifically documented acoustic data, AI enables archaeology to move beyond representational interpretation toward the experimental modelling of ritualised experiences in the ancient Mediterranean. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Algorithms-Based Monitoring of Vaccine Coverage in Chronic-Disease Cohorts: A Population-Based Evaluation of Regional Immunization Policy in Emilia-Romagna, Italy
abstract: Objectives This study aims at estimating uptake of risk-based recommended adult vaccinations among major chronic-condition subgroups in Emilia-Romagna Region (Italy) and at quantifying sociodemographic and territorial determinants of vaccine uptake. Methods Retrospective, population-based record-linkage study including all residents aged ≥18 years registered on December 31, 2023 ( N = 3 793 475). Chronic conditions (nonmutually exclusive: diabetes, cardiopathies, heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease [COPD], chronic kidney disease, cancer, and anatomical asplenia) were identified through multisource algorithms applied to regional administrative databases (2020-2024). Vaccination histories were retrieved from the Regional Vaccination Registry-Real Time (2000-2024); uptake was defined as ≥1 recorded dose. Uptake was modeled via subgroup-specific multivariable logistic regression (sex, age group, citizenship, Local Health Authority). Results Pneumococcal uptake ranged from 28.4% in cancer to 40.7% in COPD and was markedly higher in anatomical asplenia (85.1%). Composite uptake mirrored these patterns (32.6% cancer; 42.0% COPD; 85.5% asplenia). Uptake of other risk-indicated vaccines was low in large subgroups, whereas asplenia showed high meningococcal uptake (MenACWY 67.5%; MenB 65.8%). In multivariable models, Italian citizenship was consistently associated with statistically significant higher odds of composite uptake (OR 1.348-2.527), and male sex increased odds in all subgroups ( P < .001) except for asplenia. Age effects were substantial but condition specific. Residual territorial heterogeneity persisted after adjustment. Conclusions Algorithm-based identification of chronic-disease populations linked to immunization registries enables scalable, risk-stratified monitoring applicable to any chronic-condition subgroup definable through administrative codes. This approach detects strong equity gradients and persistent between-Local-Health-Authority variation, supporting regression-based indicators for subregional benchmarking and targeted strengthening of integrated multivaccine delivery pathways. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Crossing margins: Intersectional users’ ethical concerns about software
abstract: Many modern software applications present numerous ethical concerns due to conflicts between users’ values and companies’ priorities. Intersectional communities, those with multiple marginalized identities, are disproportionately affected by these ethical issues, leading to legal, financial, and reputational consequences for software companies, as well as real-world harm for intersectional users. Historically, the voices of intersectional communities have been systematically marginalized and excluded from contributing their unique perspectives to software design, perpetuating software-related ethical concerns. This work aims to fill the gap in research on intersectional users’ software-related perspectives and provide software practitioners with a methodology for analyzing intersectional voices in software ethics discourse. We collected 36,777 posts from over 700 intersectional subreddits discussing software applications and utilized large language models to identify ethical concerns in these posts. We then applied regression models with counterfactual analysis to examine how intersectional identity dimensions shape the amplification or suppression of ethical concern expression across software genres, and conducted a time-series analysis to examine how concern expression varies over time in relation to real-world events. As a case study in the social media domain, we further demonstrate how identified ethical concerns can be prioritized to surface issues warranting timely developer attention, validated against survey-derived ground truth. Together, these analyses form the basis of a nascent feedback-driven framework for assessing whether software systems are meeting the needs of intersectional users. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Property-based testing in Python: empirical insights
abstract: Property-Based Testing (PBT) automatically generates test inputs to validate properties of programs, shifting developers’ effort from writing examples to specifying invariants. While the technique has gained popularity in Python through the Hypothesis framework, little is known about how developers adopt and use it in practice. This paper reports on three empirical studies. First, we analyzed 367 PBTs from 244 Python projects, classifying them into nine property categories and quantifying their use of Hypothesis constructs. We found that Test Oracle properties dominate (29.97%), and that PBTs are generally concise (median 14 LOC), relying heavily on built-in strategies (75.20%), but also on external (22.62%) and internal (17.17%) ones. Second, we studied 213 Stack Overflow posts tagged with PBT, revealing that the main challenges developers face concern data generation strategies (36.62%), especially for composite and tabular data (24.36%). Finally, we evaluated Ghostwriter, Hypothesis’s automated test generator, against 203 tests from our dataset; only 18.23% were fully automatable, while most required partial adaptation (30.05%) or were incompatible (51.72%). Together, our findings provide the largest empirical characterization of PBT in Python to date, highlight developers’ difficulties in adopting the technique, and expose limitations of current tool support. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Influence of temperature on the bio-oil production from biomass pyrolysis in a solar hybrid drop-tube/fixed-bed reactor
abstract: Aviation remains a critical climate challenge in Europe, with emissions stubbornly high due to fossil fuel dependence, rising demand, and the slow adoption of low-carbon alternatives. SAFs, currently under 1% of fuel use, face barriers like high costs and limited feedstocks. The EU's Fit for 55 package mandates SAF blending targets of 2% by 2025, scaling to 70% by 2050, including e-fuels. To address these challenges, CNRS-PROMES (France) developed a solar-assisted quartz hybrid drop-tube/fixed-bed reactor (DTR), optimized for low-temperature pyrolysis (500 - 700 °C) and bio-oil production from the pyrolysis of demolition wood. The aim was to evaluate and optimize bio-oil yields, analyze products distribution (bio-oil, char, and gases) and elemental composition, and identify potential improvements to the solar reactor. The results showed that the bio-oil yield peaked at 500 °C, reaching 56 wt% when accounting for the “mass lost” required to close the mass balance, assuming that the missing mass consisted exclusively of liquid products. When considering only the measured mass, the bio-oil yield peaked at 600 °C, at 50 wt%. It declined at higher temperatures due to secondary cracking, while gas yield increased (12.5 - 20.4 wt%) and char yield remained stable (∼32 wt%) before slightly dropping at 700 °C. Compared to a Bubbling Fluidized Bed (BFB) reactor, the DTR produced less bio-oil (43 wt% for DTR vs. 62 wt% for BFB) and less gas (12 wt% for DTR vs. 17 wt% for BFB), but more char (32 wt% for DTR vs. 15 wt% for BFB), highlighting trade-offs tied to heat transfer and residence time. The study concludes that moderate temperatures (500 - 600 °C) favor bio-oil and char, while higher temperatures promote gasification, demonstrating the potential of solar-driven pyrolysis for scalable, carbon-neutral SAF production and circular biomass valorization. © 2026 The Authors. title: Categorical exclusion: Speciesism as a neglected dimension of prejudice in cognitive behavioral therapy
abstract: While CBT and ABA have recently begun to grapple with their own internal biases, the field's ethical framework remains stubbornly anthropocentric. Scholarship increasingly addresses systemic prejudice in research, yet speciesism—the hierarchical valuation of life based on biological category—is still largely ignored as a socio-political ideology. This is a significant oversight: psychometric evidence suggests that speciesism is not a fringe belief, but is cognitively rooted in Social Dominance Orientation (SDO), much like racism and sexism. Consequently, the discipline's human-centricity should not be viewed as a neutral default, but as an active ideological framework that prioritizes control over clinical insight. This is visible in the pathologization of vystopia. By framing the profound distress caused by industrialized animal exploitation as a cognitive distortion, clinicians commit a form of microaggression that can fundamentally weaken the therapeutic alliance. Furthermore, the behavioral emphasis on mastery and compliance uncomfortably echoes colonial power structures, treating sentient beings as mere variables rather than autonomous agents. To evolve, the field must adopt a socio-ecological model that recognizes the agency of both non-human animals and neurodivergent individuals alike. Decolonizing these frameworks does not dilute the efficacy of CBT; rather, it allows the discipline to function more fully as a science of liberation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Data-driven modeling of toxic dyes adsorption onto human hair-activated carbon using artificial neural networks and Box–Behnken response surface methodology: mechanistic insights and cost evaluation
abstract: This study examined the effectiveness of human hair activated carbon (HHAC) in removing Methylene Blue (MB) and Eriochrome Black T (EBT) from aqueous solutions using an integrated approach combining experimental analyses with kinetic, thermodynamic, and chemometric modeling. Parametric tests indicated that equilibrium was reached in 40 min, highlighting particularly rapid kinetics. MB adsorption was maximized in a basic environment, whereas EBT adsorption was favored in an acidic environment, confirming the decisive importance of electrostatic interactions. The Langmuir model provided the best fit among the tested isotherm models, particularly for MB, although the fit for EBT was comparatively weaker than that for MB. The pseudo-second-order kinetic models provided the best fits (R2 = 0.87–0.92 for EBT and 0.98 for MB), indicating a mechanism controlled by adsorbent–adsorbate interactions. Box–Behnken response surface modeling showed remarkable robustness (R2 = 0.998 and 0.996, p < 0.0001), identifying optimal conditions at pH 8.7, 65.45 mg L−1 of dye, and 0.25 g L−1 of adsorbent. Meanwhile, artificial neural networks showed slightly lower performance (R2 = 0.9868 for MB and 0.9938 for EBT), while confirming the intrinsic non-linearity of the system and revealing maximum capacities of 365.61 mg g−1 (MB) and 158.63 mg g−1 (EBT). The material retained its effectiveness after five thermal regeneration cycles, demonstrating its stability and potential for the sustainable treatment of colored effluents. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Using physiological measures to assess and diagnose team performance: An interrogative approach
abstract: Physiological measures have the potential to capture the dynamic nature of teamwork as it unfolds. Despite this potential, relatively few studies have applied physiological data in team contexts, leaving a gap in theory and practice. To address this gap, this work examines the following question: What are the emerging principles for using physiological measures to assess and diagnose team performance? To explore this question, we present an interrogative approach that structures the key considerations for applying physiological measures in team research. Specifically, this approach organizes considerations related to the purpose, context, personnel, timing, measurement selection, and implementation of using physiological measures to assess team performance. Building on prior guidance, we propose a set of emerging principles that synthesize best practices while introducing new considerations specific to the use of physiological data in team contexts. These principles provide practical guidance for researchers and practitioners seeking to leverage physiological measures, while emphasizing that their effective use depends on rigorous methodology, ethical safeguards, and integration with other validated assessment approaches. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: From distraction to engagement: An applied examination of the IMPACT framework in technology-rich management education
abstract: Student perceptions of instructional effectiveness in technology-rich management education remain actively studied amid concerns about classroom distraction in digitally mediated environments. This study introduces IMPACT—an integrative pedagogical framework composed of Incentive, Measurement, Project-based Learning, Accountability, Critical Reflection, and Technology. It presents an exploratory, multi-course demonstration across four management courses spanning the MBA, Executive MBA (EMBA), and Executive Postgraduate Diploma in Management (EPGDM–VIL) programs, delivered in face-to-face and synchronous online modes. Implementation was examined using institutional course-evaluation data (N = 202 of 203 enrolled students), and a thematic close reading of open-ended comments informed by reflexive thematic analysis. Across all four courses, student perceptions of instructional effectiveness were uniformly high on standardized nine-item instrument (weighted averages ≥ 6.0 on a seven-point scale). Qualitative themes aligned with the framework's design intent: practical relevance, structured project workflows, visible progress indicators, and technology-mediated tools, alongside integrative configuration as a framework-level property. Findings support consistent implementation across heterogeneous settings and association with positive student perceptions, but do not support causal claims about engagement. The study contributes design-oriented vocabulary identifying integrative configuration, operational workflow, and multi-mode portability as the framework's primary contributions. Limitations include single-institution, single-instructor, construct–measurement mismatch, and the absence of comparative or pre/post designs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Steering the oxygen reduction pathway from 4e⁻ to 2e⁻ in surface-dominant CoNi/NC alloys for efficient H2O2 electrosynthesis
abstract: Balancing the activity–selectivity trade-off in the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e⁻ ORR) is essential for efficient electrochemical hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production. Herein, constant-potential density functional theory calculations combined with experiments demonstrate that CoNi alloying regulates ORR branching through composition-dependent electronic interactions. Calculations on Co(111), CoNi(111), CoNi3(111), and Ni(111) show that Co(111) favors *OOH dissociation and thus the four-electron (4e⁻) pathway, whereas Ni(111) preferentially promotes H2O2 formation via the 2e⁻ pathway. In CoNi alloys, charge transfer from Co to Ni tunes the D-band center of Ni sites, which kinetically lowers the barrier for *OOH conversion to H2O2 while maintaining a comparatively high barrier for O–O bond cleavage. These effects kinetically favor the 2e⁻ branch over the competing 4e⁻ pathway. Guided by these insights, surface-dominant CoNi alloy nanoparticles with varying Ni contents were synthesized on N-doped carbon using a molten-salt-mediated method. Comprehensive characterizations support a surface-dominant CoNi alloy structure and electronic interactions between Co and Ni. Electrochemical measurements reveal a volcano-shaped dependence of H2O2 selectivity on alloy composition, with an optimized CoNi/NC catalyst achieving ~97% selectivity in 0.1 M HClO4. The catalyst also shows efficient and stable H2O2 electrosynthesis in flow cells, sustaining ~300 mA cm⁻2 for 100 h with 83–95% Faradaic efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A comprehensive survey on robust federated learning: From threat models to defense mechanisms
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without centralizing raw data and has become an important paradigm for privacy-sensitive intelligent systems. Nevertheless, its distributed architecture, heterogeneous data, and unreliable participants introduce substantial robustness and security challenges, ranging from communication noise and system failures to poisoning, privacy inference, and Byzantine attacks. In this paper, we present a structured survey of robust federated learning. We first organize the literature through a threat-oriented taxonomy that covers poisoning attacks, privacy leakage risks, Byzantine behavior, and scenario-specific robustness challenges. We explicitly analyze stronger adversaries that collude, coordinate poisoning campaigns, replace models behind secure aggregation, and adapt their optimization to defense-specific weaknesses. We then review representative defense mechanisms, including robust aggregation, backdoor defense, privacy-preserving training, secure aggregation, and personalized robustness enhancement. Particular attention is given to three recurring tensions in the literature: robustness under Non-IID data, robustness-efficiency trade-offs, and robustness-privacy trade-offs. We further discuss robust federated learning in wireless and IoT environments, where communication uncertainty and resource constraints become first-order concerns. We examine how existing robustness mechanisms translate, or fail to translate, to foundation-model-based FL, federated fine-tuning of large language models, federated reinforcement learning, agentic federated systems, and federated retrieval-augmented generation. Finally, we summarize open challenges and outline future research directions for building more reliable, efficient, and deployable federated learning systems. Copyright © 2026. title: Structural parameters for dense temporal graphs
abstract: Temporal graphs provide a useful model for many real-world networks. Unfortunately the majority of algorithmic problems we might consider on such graphs are intractable. There has been recent progress in defining structural parameters which describe tractable cases by simultaneously restricting the underlying structure and the times at which edges appear in the graph. These all rely on the temporal graph being sparse in some sense. We introduce temporal analogues of three increasingly restrictive static graph parameters – cliquewidth, modular-width and neighbourhood diversity – which take small values for highly structured temporal graphs, even if a large number of edges are active at each timestep. The computational problems solvable efficiently when the temporal cliquewidth of the input graph is bounded form a subset of those solvable efficiently when the temporal modular-width is bounded, which is in turn a subset of problems efficiently solvable when the temporal neighbourhood diversity is bounded. By considering specific temporal graph problems, we demonstrate that (up to standard complexity theoretic assumptions) these inclusions are strict. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Alignments and Trade-Offs in Multidimensional Household Diversification: A Pseudo-Panel Analysis of Standard Practices and Public Programs in Rural Ethiopia
abstract: In rural Ethiopia, multidimensional household diversification (MDHD) has become a vital element in strengthening livelihood resilience. While earlier research addressed how household-level standard practices (HLSPs) and public income-generating initiatives (PIGIs) influence diversification, their direct impact on resilience was not fully understood. This study analyzed data from five waves of the Ethiopian Living Standards Measurement Study from 2011 to 2021 to clarify these relationships. Households were classified into 15,191 cohorts based on birth year, location, and household head gender. Using a weighted Herfindahl-based method, the analysis found that 51.33% of households were highly diversified. The results indicated that public income-generating initiatives significantly enhanced diversification, increasing it by 6.88 points on a 0-100 scale. Other important factors included land tenure arrangements, gender dynamics, access to extension services, and participation in nonfarm enterprises. A key insight was that public income-generating programs are most effective when aligned with existing household strategies. Among households already engaged in traditional livelihood practices, involvement in government initiatives led to the greatest improvements, adding 6.88 points to diversification levels. For policymakers, the study suggests that the Ministry of Agriculture should require regional offices to evaluate household practices before implementing income-generating programs. Additionally, District Rural Development Offices should supplement these efforts with agricultural training and enhanced extension services. Such an integrated approach would enable rural households to develop more diverse income sources and better withstand economic shocks. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis unravels the molecular basis of conspecific aggression in Pelodiscus sinensis
abstract: Aggressive behavior is a critical issue affecting health and survival in aquaculture animals; however, the molecular mechanism of aggression in reptiles has not been fully understood. Using the Chinese softshell turtle (Pelodiscus sinensis) as a model, we established a turtle model of reactive aggression using the intruder experiment to compare aggressive and non-aggressive individuals. Integrated brain transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis revealed enrichment in glutamatergic and GABAergic pathways between aggressive and non-aggressive individuals. Aggressive individuals showed upregulated glutamate receptor genes (GRIA2, GRIA3, GRIK3) and an altered GABAergic system. Correlation networks confirmed coordinated gene-metabolite covariation in these pathways. Drug injection tests demonstrated that NMDA receptor antagonist MK-801 significantly reduced attacks, indicating that glutamatergic signaling is a primary driver of aggressive behavior. These findings highlight conserved excitatory mechanisms in vertebrate aggression with reptile-specific characteristics and offer targets for low aggressiveness breeding in aquaculture. © 2026

title: Development, Optimization, and Evaluation of Chitosan Nanoparticles for Co-Delivery of Rivastigmine and Harmaline via Intranasal Route for Brain Targeting
abstract: Purpose: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) remains difficult to manage due to the lack of disease-modifying therapies and poor brain bioavailability of existing drugs. This study aimed to develop an intranasal nanocarrier system capable of simultaneously targeting cholinergic dysfunction and tau pathology using rivastigmine (RIV) and harmaline (HAL). Methods: RIV and HAL were co-loaded into chitosan nanoparticles (RHLCNPs) prepared by ionic gelation. Nanoparticles were evaluated for particle size, polydispersity index (PDI), drug release kinetics, nasal mucosal penetration, stability, and histopathological safety. Nasal transport was assessed using ex vivo permeation and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM). Results: Optimized RHLCNPs showed a mean particle size of 148.9 ± 4.0 nm with a PDI of 0.3037 ± 0.0345, indicating uniform nanoscale dispersion. Sustained drug release followed the Higuchi model (R² = 0.9773) with a non-Fickian diffusion mechanism. Ex vivo and CLSM investigations show increased nasal penetration up to 30 μm compared to dual-drug suspension (20 μm). The formulation remained stable for six months with minimal changes in % EE and particle size, while histopathology confirmed the absence of mucosal damage. Conclusions: Intranasal RHLCNPs represent a safe and effective strategy for the targeted delivery of a dual drug-loaded nanoformulation in AD. However, further in vivo investigations are required to validate its clinical efficacy. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Optimizing Semaglutide Therapy in Type 2 Diabetes: Pharmacokinetic Limitations, Nanoemulsion-Based Delivery Strategies and Translational Potential
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) continues to be one of the important global public health problems, and semaglutide is an efficient agonist of the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor that could provide beneficial outcomes for glycaemic regulation and weight loss. Nevertheless, its oral delivery is limited due to a high extent of degradation in the gastrointestinal tract, poor epithelial permeability, low bioavailability, and the need for using the drug transport enhancer sodium N-(8-[2-hydroxybenzoyl]amino) caprylate (SNAC). This structured narrative review of the literature critically examines the possibility of using delivery systems based on nanoemulsions to circumvent the pharmacokinetic challenges of oral semaglutide. For that purpose, a thorough literature search in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar was performed for articles published from 2020 to 2025, where topics included the following: semaglutide pharmacokinetics, oral peptide delivery, nanoemulsion formulation, mechanistic transport pathways, and translational research. This review focuses on contrasting the advantages of the use of nanoemulsion-based delivery systems with the clinically approved method of SNAC-mediated oral semaglutide, based on different absorption mechanisms, formulation methods, and pharmacokinetic profiles. Formulation issues, scalability, regulations, and knowledge gaps are among the factors that impede the implementation of these methods in the clinic. While these systems show good preclinical results, a lack of evidence from the clinical point of view prevents their superiority in relation to currently used oral systems from being proven. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Design of piezoelectric energy harvester with low frequency vibration via multiscale topology optimization
abstract: Vibration energy harvester with piezoelectric material is expected as maintenance free power source for small electronic devices taking the advantages of compactness and high power density. Power generation capacity of the harvesters is not sufficient for applications especially at low frequency range. The basic strategy to improve the output power is matching the natural frequency of the harvester to the outer vibrations. However, change of the shape of the harvester to match the natural frequency to low frequency detract compactness of the piezoelectric harvesters. To address this trade-off, we consider a lattice-structured energy harvester and develop a multiscale topology optimization framework. The proposed method concurrently optimizes the macroscale structure and the microscale unit-cell structure by using the homogenization method to estimate the effective properties of the lattice. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Associations between teaching approaches, epistemological beliefs, utility value, and science-related career choice: A study across different metacognitive levels
abstract: This study utilized survey data from 1,257 Chinese eighth-grade students to examine the associations among teaching approaches (i.e., inquiry-based teaching and teacher-directed instruction), epistemological beliefs, utility value, and science-related career choice. Crucially, these relational patterns were analyzed within different levels of metacognitive ability (high, medium, and low). Specifically, the present study employed multi-group structural equation modeling to examine group-specific patterns of associations among variables across students with different levels of metacognitive ability. Results indicated that positive associations between inquiry-based teaching and the examined variables were mainly observed within the high-metacognitive group, whereas teacher-directed instruction demonstrated positive associations with certain variables across groups. In addition, indirect associations involving utility value in the relationship between teaching approaches and science-related career choice were identified in the high-metacognitive group, while comparable patterns were not observed in the other groups. These findings suggest that the association patterns involving teaching approaches, epistemological beliefs, utility value, and science-related career choice may differ across metacognitive groups. title: Existence of ground state solutions for a class of fractional Kirchhoff equations with Hartree-type nonlinearity
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence of ground state solutions for a class of Kirchhoff equation involving the fractional Laplacian and Hartree-type nonlinearity {(a+b∫R3|(−Δ)s2u|2dx)(−Δ)su+V(x)u=(Iμ⁎|u|p)|u|p−2uin R3,u∈Hs(R3), where a,b>0 are constants, μ∈(4s−3,3), s∈(34,1), p∈(3+μ3,3+μ3−2s), Iμ denotes the Riesz potential, and (−Δ)s stands for the fractional Laplacian. Firstly, we establish the existence of Pohozaev-type ground state solutions for the equation with the constant potential V(x). Building upon this result, we further apply appropriate analytical techniques to prove the existence of such ground state solutions for the equation with a general potential V(x). © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: A comprehensive survey of federated learning for intrusion detection systems in Internet of Things environments
abstract: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into Internet of Things (IoT) is bringing unprecedented conveniences to daily life, but it also introduces severe cybersecurity challenges due to the widespread deployment of IoT devices. Federated learning, with its distributed nature and privacy-preserving characteristics, has emerged as a powerful framework for building Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) in IoT environments. It enables collaborative model training across distributed devices without centralizing sensitive data. In this paper, we systematically present typical federated learning-based IDS architectures in IoT environments, along with optimization algorithms that enhance their performance and robustness. We explicitly define a threat model that distinguishes two fundamentally different security layers. The first layer consists of external network intrusions that federated learning-based IDSs aim to detect. The second layer comprises internal model-layer attacks, such as poisoning, backdoors, and gradient leakage, which target the federated learning training process itself. Our review methodology involves retrieving literature from major academic databases (Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, Springer Link, and ScienceDirect) and Google Scholar, with selection based on strict criteria. This survey contributes a structured synthesis and taxonomy of existing federated learning-based IDS literature, a comparative experimental analysis of datasets, and a detailed discussion of optimization strategies organized around the defined threat model. We conclude by discussing current challenges and outlining future research directions, including the critical need for lightweight model design and robust defenses against adversarial attacks on the federated learning. title: Moderator analysis for single-case experimental design meta-analysis
abstract: Moderator analysis in single-experimental design (SCED) meta-analysis allows for fine-grained analysis allowing explanation of variability in intervention effectiveness between studies in addition to between participants. This is desirable for the field of cognitive therapy as individual SCED study participant characteristics might explain participant's responsiveness to interventions. This stands in contrast to traditional group design meta-analysis in which moderator analysis is limited to exploring study level characteristics. If traditional meta-analytic techniques were to be used, as in group design studies (i.e., using study average moderators), then the unique benefits of synthesizing SCED studies are missed. In this manuscript, three-level meta-analysis for synthesis of SCED effect sizes with inclusion of moderators is introduced and an empirical demonstration using SCED studies focusing on cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is provided. The goal is to provide applied SCED meta-analysis with appropriate methodology to conduct moderator analysis which can result in more fine-grained evidence. This approach can support a more comprehensive understanding of the conditions under which, and the participants for whom, interventions may be recommended. © 2026

title: Design principles for advanced hydrides: A DFT and molecular dynamics study of tetragonal silicon-based A₂SiH₄ frameworks combining structural stability, ductility, and superior hydrogen storage metrics
abstract: This work presents a comprehensive first-principles investigation of tetragonal A₂SiH₄ (A = Li, Na, Be, Mg) hydrides as promising solid-state hydrogen storage materials. Structural optimization, phonon dispersion, and ab initio molecular dynamics confirm their thermodynamic, mechanical, and thermal stability. All compounds exhibit near-isotropic elastic behavior, positive Cauchy pressures, and high Pugh ratios, indicating dominant ionic bonding and intrinsic ductility, which are critical for resisting mechanical degradation during hydrogen cycling. Hydrogen storage analysis reveals gravimetric capacities ranging from 4.99 to 8.76 wt% and volumetric densities up to 76.08 kg H₂/m³, exceeding DOE targets. Li₂SiH₄ delivers the highest gravimetric performance, while Be₂SiH₄ achieves maximum volumetric density. Formation enthalpies (–42 to –48 kJ/mol·H₂) indicate stronger hydrogen binding than previously estimated, placing these materials near the upper limit of the optimal thermodynamic window. Corresponding desorption temperatures (315–355 K) remain within practical ranges, although higher thermal input may be required, particularly for Li-based compounds. The observed trends highlight the key role of cation mass, ionic radius, and charge density in tuning structural compactness and hydrogen thermodynamics. Overall, A₂SiH₄ hydrides offer a versatile platform combining high storage capacity and mechanical resilience, while further optimization of thermodynamics and kinetics is necessary for practical deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS): From technology advances to carbon neutrality pathways in energy and industrial sectors
abstract: Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is critical for hard-to-abate sectors including steel, cement, chemicals, and power generation. This review systematically synthesizes recent advances across the full CCUS chain, covering emerging electrochemical and membrane-based direct air capture (DAC), AI-enhanced monitoring, verification, and risk management with digital twins, and synergistic coupling with green hydrogen and power-to-liquid synthetic fuels. Mature capture technologies and utilization pathways are assessed alongside geological storage in saline aquifers, depleted oil and gas reservoirs, and coal seams. Operational data from million-tonne demonstration projects are distilled to bridge the gap between laboratory innovation and industrial implementation. The International Energy Agency (IEA) projects CCUS playing a key role in global emissions reductions by 2050, while the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) emphasizes its critical role in ambitious climate stabilization pathways. A conceptual system integration framework is proposed to clarify the distinct roles of CCUS in energy conversion versus industrial production. Despite persistent challenges, including high costs, energy penalties, infrastructure deficits, and regulatory gaps, future directions prioritize low-energy materials, AI-driven optimization, industrial clustering, cross-border networks, and policy incentives. Through innovation and cooperation, CCUS is transitioning from demonstration to commercial-scale deployment to support global climate goals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Consumer egg washing and handling practices in Southeast Asia: a mixed-method study
abstract: Egg washing at home is generally discouraged in some regions because it can damage the egg's natural protective cuticle and increase the risk of bacterial penetration. However, little is known about how consumers in Southeast Asia wash and handle eggs in domestic settings. This study aims to investigate egg washing and handling practices among consumers using a mixed-method approach. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with consumers from Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Thailand, and Vietnam. This was followed by 24 domestic kitchen observations and semi-structured interviews in Malaysia, Indonesia, and Thailand. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, Kruskal-Wallis tests, and logistic regression. Qualitative data were analysed thematically. The majority of participants reported washing eggs before cooking. More than half of those who washed eggs indicated that they would still wash eggs even when they appeared visually clean. Eggs were commonly rinsed under tap water, often to remove dirt, faeces, slime, or feathers. Respondents from Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines and those with greater perceived risk of Salmonella contamination in eggs were more confident in following the message. Observations revealed appropriate handwashing after handling or cracking eggs was rare and cross-contact opportunities were frequently observed. Semi-structured interview findings showed that egg washing was closely linked to perceived beliefs about cleanliness and safety, habitual practice, and uncertainty about how eggs had been handled before purchase. Some participants also described wiping as an alternative cleaning strategy, while informal information sources appeared to influence views on egg washing. Practical guidance should emphasise washing only visibly dirty eggs, cooking them immediately after washing, handwashing hands with soap and water after handling or cracking eggs and preventing cross-contamination during preparation. © 2026 The Authors

title: AI-assisted analysis of creative thinking opportunities in new Chinese elementary mathematics textbooks
abstract: Developing students’ mathematical creative thinking has become a central goal of mathematics curriculum reform worldwide. This study examines opportunities for mathematical creative thinking in the three Grade 1 Chinese mathematics textbook editions first implemented under the Compulsory Education Mathematics Curriculum Standards (2022 Edition). Drawing on the Opportunities-to-Learn framework, the study localizes Hadar and Tirosh’s (2019) analytical framework by refining the operational indicators of divergent, convergent, and lateral thinking and extending the framework through the incorporation of cognitive complexity. A human–AI collaborative coding approach was used to analyze 1,473 mathematical tasks. The findings indicate that approximately half of all textbook tasks provide opportunities for mathematical creative thinking, with convergent thinking emerging as the dominant dimension across all three editions, although each edition places emphasis on different indicators of mathematical creative thinking. This study contributes a localized analytical framework for evaluating mathematical creative thinking in curriculum materials and provides implications for textbook design, curriculum reform, and future research on mathematical creative thinking. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Introducing a Conditional Support Framework: How young residents view the Olympic games
abstract: While cost-benefit frameworks have dominated resident support research, they struggle to explain why governance quality increasingly shapes acceptance. This Research Note introduces the conditional support framework (CSF), which treats resident support as a contingent, revisable stance: granted, withheld, or withdrawn depending on perceived governance quality. Drawing on 74 semi-structured interviews and 14 focus groups (N = 146) with young residents aged 18 to 30 years in Lombardy, Italy, this study examines perceptions of the Milano–Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games. Findings reveal that support is contingent on four governance-related conditions: (a) transport readiness, (b) housing fairness, (c) sustainability credibility, and (d) local inclusion. Economic and reputational benefits were widely acknowledged, yet proved insufficient to secure endorsement when governance performance was questioned. By reframing resident support as governance-dependent rather than purely impact-driven, the CSF extends resident attitude research and offers a transferable lens for future research on tourism legitimacy. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Long-term impact of ChatGPT-4 on music students' creative and analytical skills: A follow-up study
abstract: The rapid integration of generative AI into education has raised important questions about its long-term influence on higher-order thinking. Building on our earlier study that examined the one-off impact of ChatGPT-4, the present follow-up study investigated its sustained effects on music students’ creative and analytical skills. A quasi-experimental design was employed with 74 undergraduate music students assigned to an experimental group ( n = 36) and a control group ( n = 38). Across a 24-week intervention, creativity and analytical skills were assessed at 12 repeated measurement points. Data were analyzed using latent growth modeling, multivariate analysis of covariance, cross-lagged panel modeling, epistemic network analysis, and a first-order Markov chain model. Results indicated that the experimental group began with higher initial levels and demonstrated steeper growth trajectories, reflecting a Matthew effect, while the control group displayed compensatory tendencies. Cross-lagged analyses revealed that analytical reasoning strongly predicted subsequent creativity in the experimental group, and network analysis confirmed stable co-occurrences between creative and analytical moves. Transition modeling further showed recursive cycles of idea generation, revision, evaluation, and structural reasoning. These findings suggest that ChatGPT-4 fosters an integrated interplay of creativity and analysis, offering music educators worldwide practical strategies for designing AI-mediated learning that balances innovation with critical rigor. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Examining primary students’ mathematical communication through the lens of de Bono’s practical thinking processes
abstract: Mathematical thinking is a complex, multi-faceted process that typically involves both intra-personal and interpersonal communication. While it has been described as messy and difficult, it can also show growth and insight into conceptual understanding and knowing. This paper explores the application of Edward de Bono's practical thinking processes to examine the mathematical thinking processes that primary school students use. de Bono’s perspective is relevant as it foregrounds thinking as an active developmental process, providing the metalanguage to describe children’s communication of their mathematical thinking. The research was conducted in a small regional South Australian school where the entire school population (n = 36) was divided into two classes. The two-phase research first used participant (n = 23) drawings, written descriptions, and interviews about their drawings to document retrospective accounts of the processes students used to engage and to communicate their mathematical thinking. Analysis of the data from this phase was then used to inform subsequent class observations (n = 20) conducted to identify the processes of practical thinking used in-the-moment during mathematical learning experiences. By applying the foundations of de Bono's practical thinking, this paper offers insights into the potential benefits of integrating the tenets of practical thinking into mathematics education. The analysis identifies how primary students engage and use connect-up thinking, carry-on thinking, and porridge words as core processes which facilitate the communication and development of their mathematical understanding. Of note is the emergence of different forms of connect-up thinking, and students’ creative use of porridge words. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: A quantitative heuristic process predictive model based on relative volatility for screening green entrainer
abstract: Screening the green economic and sustainable entrainer is the key to extractive distillation (ED). This quantitative heuristic process screening predictive (HPSP) model has formed the functional system of model equations, achieving the improvement of screening green entrainers from qualitative analysis of monotonically positive correlation to function-equationalized quantitative evaluation of TAC and LCA impacts, which could construct the more efficient auxiliary algorithm to promote the ηcd for screening entrainers of ED separating azeotropes, and would become the process theoretical principles to accurately and efficiently predict and screen the green entrainers. PECI and ηcd could evaluate the green efforts of screening entrainers schemes. As the number N of entrainers increases, the ηcd decreases, and the greater the workload M of process simulation and optimization, the smaller the ηcd, the better the process model screening effect in the ED separation azeotropes. title: Efficient stability-preserving model order reduction for vibro-acoustic systems with complex configuration of porous and poro-elastic materials
abstract: Recent developments in digital twins have led to a renewed interest in efficient transient vibro-acoustic finite element simulations, which can be combined with limited measurements to bridge the gap between the model and the physical world. To this end, stability-preserving model order reduction (spMOR) is a rapidly emerging topic to enable large-scale finite element models, which can reduce the size of these models but preserve their high fidelity and stability. Notably, the spMOR for vibro-acoustic systems with different porous materials was recently addressed by introducing additional variables. The trade-off is that the size of the resulting full-order models increases significantly with the complexity of porous materials, such as the frequency range and dimensions. Consequently, substantial computational resources are required for the offline generation of the reduction basis. Hence, an efficient approach is proposed in this paper to improve the offline stage efficiency of the spMOR for vibro-acoustics with a complex configuration of porous and poro-elastic materials, which adopts a two-step strategy to generate stable reduced-order models. Firstly, a higher-order Krylov subspace method based on Taylor’s theorem is applied to the frequency-domain model, leading to an intermediate reduced-order model. This process ensures the preservation of system matrix properties and positive realness of the frequency-dependent parameters. Secondly, leveraging these key properties, the spMOR for vibro-acoustics with porous and poro-elastic materials is applied to the intermediate reduced-order model to give a compact time-domain model. The proposed method is demonstrated on a simple cubic cavity and a more involved sedan car cabin. The proposed method significantly accelerates the calculation of the reduction basis and reduces memory usage. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Shiny by Design: Establishing Diagnostic Criteria for Intentional Burnishing on Prehistoric Bone Artifacts
abstract: The identification of intentional burnishing on prehistoric osseous artifacts remains a persistent methodological challenge. Bone surfaces are highly reactive and readily record microwear traces but are susceptible to taphonomic alteration. This study investigates how the use of different burnishing materials affects the morphology of bone surfaces and the formation of diagnostic microwear traces to develop a methodologically grounded classification for identifying intentionally burnished surfaces on archeological osseous artifacts. Experimental observations are evaluated in relation to existing knowledge of use-related, manufacturing, and postdepositional surface modifications. The analysis is based on a microwear framework that integrates multiscalar observations (low- and high-magnification microscopy and scanning electron microscopy) with quantitative three-dimensional surface texture analysis. Both microscopy and quantitative data derived from confocal microscopy reveal clear differences among bones burnished with different agents, highlighting agent-specific topographic patterns. The experimentally derived reference dataset was subsequently applied during microwear analysis of selected prehistoric bone points from Lake Lubāns (Latvia) and the Wiele 33 site (Poland) to assess the analytical applicability of the proposed protocol. The results of our study demonstrate the diagnostic potential of the created classification of wear traces to distinguish intentional burnishing on archaeological osseous artifacts and to discriminate between intentional, use-related, and taphonomic surface modifications. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Assessment of biomass resource utilization and greenhouse gas mitigation potential in Xinjiang
abstract: Biomass energy offers a renewable pathway to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions while supporting energy security. This study assesses the collectable, utilizable, and GHG mitigation potentials of five biomass resource categories (crop residues, forest residues, animal manure, municipal solid waste, and sewage sludge) in Xinjiang, China, from 2003 to 2050. Historical trends (2003–2020) were analyzed, and an ARIMA time-series model was developed to forecast collectable potential through 2050. Four scenarios combining planned/maximum utilization with/without carbon capture and storage (CCS) were designed, and life-cycle assessment (LCA) was applied to quantify GHG mitigation. Results show that Xinjiang's total collectable biomass potential will reach 1839.7 PJ by 2050, with crop residues accounting for 62.8%–74.6%. Under the maximum-potential-with-CCS scenario, the GHG mitigation potential reaches 298.90 Mt CO2e in 2050, with bio-liquid fuels and bio-electricity as the dominant contributors. These findings provide a dynamic, high-resolution basis for optimizing bioenergy deployment and supporting Xinjiang's dual-carbon transition and provides certain guidance for the development and utilization of biomass resources in Xinjiang and for mitigating global climate change. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: BBZS glass-ceramics for sealing to 4J33 Kovar alloy: crystallization behavior and sealing mechanism
abstract: To resolve the trade-off between low sealing temperature and high-temperature insulation in lead-free sealants, a novel Bi2O3–B2O3–ZnO–SiO2 (BBZS) glass-ceramic system was developed for sealing to 4J33 Kovar alloy. The influence of the Si/B mass ratio on the network structure and crystallization of the parent glasses was systematically investigated. The resulting BBZS glass-ceramics exhibited coefficients of thermal expansion (CTEs) tailored from 7.01 to 7.37 × 10−6 K⁻¹ , closely matching that of the Kovar substrate. An optimal joint was achieved at a moderate sealing temperature of 750 °C for 30 min, yielding an average shear strength of 4.70 MPa. Notably, the sealant retained an outstanding bulk resistivity of 107.99 Ω⋅cm at 500 °C. Interfacial analysis revealed that the bonding is driven by elemental interdiffusion, forming a stable transition layer. This work presents a promising strategy for designing environmentally friendly, highly insulating heterogeneous packaging sealants operable at moderate temperatures. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Breaking selectivity-conversion trade-off for CO2-glycerol carbonylation via constructing ternary active-sites in zeolite-based catalyst
abstract: Directly converting glycerol (GL) and CO2 into glycerol carbonate (GC) offers a pivotal solution to valorize biodiesel by-products while mitigate greenhouse gas emmissions. However, the chemical inertness of CO2 and the inherent complexity of GL molecular structure pose a significant challenge in balancing activity and selectivity for this reaction. Herein, Lewis and Brønsted acid sites were constructed on the inherent Lewis basic sites within ETS-10 zeolite, leading to the formation of a ternary-active-sites Zn(Otf)x/ETS-10 catalyst for overcoming the long-standing trade-off between activity and selectivity in CO2-GL carbonylation. The tailored Lewis and Brønsted acid sites synergistically anchor GL molecules and provide a novel mode for their targeted activation, resulting in an intriguing 11-membered ring-shaped Zn-GL* intermediate. Subsequently, the direct cyclization with the adjacent bi-COO* species formed by CO2 activation on Lewis basic sites promotes GC production while suppressing the side reactions that consume both GL and GC. Ultimately, by using CaC2 as a solid dehydrating agent, a 95.2% of GC selectivity and 40.9% of GL conversion were achieved within the regular and enlarged 12-membered ring (12-RS) of the ETS-10 framework. This work offers valuable insights into the rational design of active sites for highly active and selective carbonylation catalysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Multi-period interval optimization of a renewable steam-methanol system for uncertainty-aware industrial decarbonization
abstract: Deep decarbonization of industrial steam systems is fundamentally constrained by renewable intermittency, fluctuating steam demand, and tightly coupled interactions among energy, hydrogen, and carbon-management processes. This work presents a representative-month-based interval MINLP framework for uncertainty-aware planning and operation of a renewable-integrated steam–methanol co-production (RE-ISMP) system. The framework integrates wind power, solar steam generation, water electrolysis, CO2 capture and utilization (CCU), and methanol synthesis within a multi-pressure steam network. Interval parameter programming is employed to address uncertainties in renewable resources and steam demand without requiring probability distributions. An interval mixed-integer nonlinear optimization framework solved through an interactive boundary decomposition strategy is developed to coordinate equipment configuration and representative-period operation, while the ε-constraint method is used to quantify the economic–environmental trade-off. Application to a practical refinery case demonstrates favorable economic and plant-gate carbon performance, reveals a transition toward intensified CCU deployment, and highlights methanol valorization as an economic compensation pathway under uncertainty. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: A multi-actor multi-criteria decision analysis framework for siting a biomass pyrolysis facility in Trabzon
abstract: Selecting a biomass pyrolysis facility location requires reconciling site conditions with the priorities of affected stakeholders. This study develops an integrated Multi-Actor Multi-Criteria Analysis (MAMCA) framework combining the Pivot-Linked Elicitation Best-Worst Method (PILE-BWM) and Multi-Attribute Value Theory (MAVT) to evaluate four organized industrial zones for a tea- and hazelnut-residue bioenergy and biochar hub in Trabzon, Türkiye. A common nine-criterion performance matrix was constructed from documented regional sources, historical district-level information, and transparent screening assumptions, while separate consensus weights were elicited for farmers, residents, public-sector representatives, and private-sector actors. Farmers and the private sector assigned the greatest importance to resource and supply, whereas residents and the public sector emphasized environmental and accessibility considerations. Arsin ranked first for farmers and the private sector, while Akçaabat-Şinik ranked first for residents and the public sector. Although biomass-weighted inbound haul distance received the public sector's largest criterion weight, it favoured Arsin; Akçaabat-Şinik's narrow public-sector lead was driven by its settlement-separation advantage. The four rankings showed relatively high descriptive concordance (Kendall's W = 0.78), and minimax regret identified Akçaabat-Şinik as the compromise alternative (maximum regret = 0.47). Extended sensitivity analyses showed stable winners for farmers, residents, and the private sector, whereas the public-sector winner changed under selected circuity-factor and reference-anchor scenarios. The findings show that preserving stakeholder-specific preferences reveals trade-offs that would be obscured by aggregated weighting. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Multi-technology synergic mechanism and integration pathways for regional organic waste-to-energy manufacturing utilization: A case study of China
abstract: China generates more than 300 million tonnes of municipal solid waste annually, with organic fractions representing over 50 percent of this volume. The conversion of organic waste to energy (OWtE) has emerged as a central pillar of China's circular economy strategy and its dual-carbon targets of peak emissions by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060. This paper examines the multi-technology synergic mechanisms underpinning regional OWtE systems in China, analyzing the technical, economic, environmental, and policy dimensions of four primary conversion pathways: anaerobic digestion (AD), incineration with energy recovery, pyrolysis, and gasification. Drawing on provincial data, life cycle assessment outcomes, and techno-economic evaluations, the study proposes an integrated framework for regional OWtE manufacturing utilization. The findings demonstrate that hybrid systems combining AD with thermal treatment can reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 58 to 68 percent relative to landfilling while achieving levelized energy costs of 42 to 82 USD per MWh. Regional differentiation in technology deployment is driven by waste composition, economic development level, and feedstock availability. Policy coherence under the 14th Five-Year Plan and subsequent instruments has accelerated capacity development, though technology-region mismatches and digestate management gaps remain persistent barriers. This study provides an evidence-based roadmap for optimizing OWtE integration pathways across China's diverse regional contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Cost-Utility Analysis of Sentinel Node Biopsy Versus Selective Neck Dissection for Node-Negative Early-Stage Oral Cancers: A Health Economic Evaluation from the Indian Healthcare System Perspective
abstract: Objectives To conduct a cost-utility analysis comparing sentinel node biopsy (SNB) with selective neck dissection (SND) for clinically node-negative early-stage oral cancer from the Indian healthcare system perspective. Methods A hybrid decision-tree-Markov model compared SNB with SND over a 10-year horizon, incorporating 18 clinical pathways, time-trade-off utilities from an Indian population, and costs from Indian settings. Model and R code construction were assisted by a large language model (Claude-3.5-Sonnet) with author verification. Effectiveness was measured in quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs). Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted. The primary outcome was net monetary benefit at the India-specific willingness-to-pay threshold of INR 212 307/QALY. Results SNB yielded 6.145 QALYs versus 6.032 for SND (incremental 0.114) at INR 332 865 versus INR 336 433 (incremental −INR 3568). SNB dominated SND in the deterministic base case. Under probabilistic sensitivity analysis, SNB was cost-effective in 78.5% of iterations at the India-specific threshold (mean incremental net monetary benefit INR 15 944; 95% CrI −INR 22 141 to INR 54 287) and 81.8% at 1× gross domestic product per capita (INR 245 000/QALY). A lifetime-horizon scenario (cohort age 55-100; 45 cycles) confirmed SNB dominance with incremental cost −INR 5466 and incremental QALYs 0.1767. Results were robust across deterministic and scenario analyses. Conclusions SNB is a cost-effective alternative to SND for clinically node-negative early-stage oral cancer in Indian tertiary cancer centers with appropriate technical expertise, dominating in the deterministic base case and remaining cost-effective in 78.5% of probabilistic iterations at the India-specific threshold. These findings support adoption of SNB as the preferred staging strategy at such centers. © 2026 The Authors.

title: A pilot randomized controlled trial of the feasibility and acceptability of a school-based intervention to reduce student anxiety during the transition to middle school
abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of a school-based intervention to reduce anxiety and related impairment during the transition to middle school. Thirty-eight students were randomly assigned to receive the Transitioning Emotionally and Academically to Middle School Successfully (TEAMSS, n = 20) program, a group cognitive behavioral intervention, or Enhanced Usual Care (EUC, n = 18), a study generated resource list and usual school counseling. Students (mean age 10.4; 85.7% White; 50% female) had elevated anxiety symptoms and/or a primary anxiety disorder. Feasibility and acceptability were assessed via recruitment, retention, attendance, intervention satisfaction, and intervention adherence. Exploratory student outcomes of anxiety and constructs targeted in TEAMSS (e.g., behavioral avoidance, academic organizational and social skills) were assessed at post intervention (10 weeks after the initiation of treatment) and at the end of the academic year (follow-up). Results revealed student recruitment challenges; enrolled participants found the intervention acceptable and helpful. Student attendance at the group meetings was high. Clinician adherence to the intervention indicated room for improvement. At post and follow-up assessments, students in both groups showed significant reductions in anxiety and improvements in functioning, but there were few statistically significant between-group differences. Within group effect sizes were medium to large and favored TEAMSS on several measures assessing changes in areas targeted in TEAMSS (e.g., maladaptive cognitions, social skills); however, these findings should be interpreted with caution given the overall absence of group differences on most measures. Implementation challenges and future directions are discussed. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. Published by Elsevier Masson SAS. title: Human-Elephant Conflict and its Impact on the Social Vulnerability of Subsistence Farmers in the Chure Terai Madhesh Landscape, Nepal
abstract: Asian elephants (Elephas maximus) mainly inhabit fragmented landscapes within their range and frequently clash with humans, rendering subsistence farmers socially vulnerable. However, the extent of this vulnerability in Nepal is not well understood. In this study, we explored the social aspects of human–elephant conflict (HEC) and its impact on subsistence farmers by interviewing 1,060 affected households in Nepal’s Chure Terai Madhesh Landscape. Data were analyzed using the Social Vulnerability Index based on the five capitals of the Sustainable Livelihood Framework. 60% of respondents perceived an increase in HEC. The most common impacts reported were crop damage (47%), property losses (38%), and human casualties (15%). Among the 19 districts studied, Bardia and Jhapa showed the highest exposure and sensitivity to HEC. Farming households faced moderate to high vulnerability to crop loss caused by elephants. Of the five livelihood capitals, physical capital was the most vulnerable, followed by financial capital; social and human capitals showed the lowest vulnerability. The greater vulnerability of financial and physical capital indicates a reduced adaptive capacity among subsistence farmers. We recommend implementing tailored mitigation strategies, such as physical barriers for protecting crops and property, improving financial support systems, and promoting community-based adaptation measures to diminish the vulnerability of affected subsistence farmers. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Art as a scaffold for social cognition
abstract: The idea that art connects us to others is culturally compelling, yet empirical evidence linking art engagement to social cognition remains mixed across paradigms, methods, and timescales. We develop the thesis that art functions as a scaffold for social cognition, rather than a direct intervention on social-cognitive abilities. From this perspective, art structures the conditions under which social cognition unfolds by shaping whether individuals engage with socially meaningful content, how deeply they become involved, and whether they return to similar experiences over time. The scaffold model identifies three interrelated components: a motivational gate, qualities of engagement, and reinforcement and habit formation. By integrating previously disconnected literature, the scaffold model reframes art's social-cognitive impact as a recursive process that creates repeated opportunities for social-cognitive practice across contexts, media, and timescales. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Topology design of a 3D-printed reactor for CO elimination based on multi-objective optimization and its experimental evaluation
abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) can accumulate rapidly in confined spaces during fires, fuel leaks, internal-combustion-engine emissions, and post-blasting operations, creating severe exposure risks. For independent CO purification devices, the reactor flow-channel structure directly affects CO transport, gas-catalyst contact, and flow resistance. This study develops a variable-density-based multi-objective topology optimization method for the internal flow-channel design of a CO elimination reactor. The CRITIC method is used to determine the weights of the domain-averaged reaction-rate objective and total power-dissipation objective, avoiding subjective weighting. Topology evolution and performance trade-offs are analyzed under different inlet flow conditions, and the selected topology-optimized structure is converted into a 3D-printed reactor prototype. Hopcalite is coated on the inner channel walls for experimental evaluation. Compared with a conventional parallel-channel reactor, Structure 2 increases the CO elimination efficiency by 54.1%, while the pressure drop increases by only 14.0%, resulting in a PECexp value of 1.35. The results demonstrate that topology optimization can improve CO elimination while controlling the flow-energy penalty, and that 3D printing provides a feasible route for fabricating complex optimized reactor channels. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: A comprehensive review on ammonia-hydrogen synergistic combustion technology for engine applications: a utopia or still a challenge?
abstract: Amid the global pursuit of carbon neutrality and energy transition, the decarbonization of engines has become an inevitable trend. Ammonia, featuring zero-carbon content and high hydrogen density, offers advantages such as easy storage and transport, a mature industrial chain and low cost, making it a promising alternative fuel for carbon–neutral energy systems. However, the inert combustion of pure ammonia severely limits its direct application in engines. Given the physicochemical differences between hydrogen and ammonia, blending highly reactive hydrogen can create novel combustion schemes for ammonia-hydrogen synergistic fuels. Notably, a critical gap remains between current fundamental reaction kinetics of ammonia-hydrogen systems and their engineering application in macro-scale engines. Therefore, this paper systemically reviews the latest technological advancements in ammonia-hydrogen synergistic fuels for internal combustion power systems, focusing on reaction kinetic mechanisms, mixture formation, advanced combustion mode adaptability, and emission generation and control strategies. In engineering applications, the realization of online hydrogen production through vehicle-mounted catalytic cracking is essential for establishing a single-fuel ammonia power system. New combustion methods, such as jet ignition and spark-assisted compression ignition, show great promise in improving the efficiency of ammonia-hydrogen combustion and reducing nitrogen-based emissions. However, ammonia-hydrogen combustion systems still face several challenges, including incomplete combustion mechanisms, unreliable materials in the injection and cracking systems, low catalytic cracking efficiency and the difficulty of controlling nitrogen-based emissions. In summary, ammonia-hydrogen synergistic combustion is a vital technical approach to achieving zero-carbon combustion in engines, but its commercial application necessitates continuous technological innovation and development. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
