title: Foraging Theory and the Colonization of Unfamiliar Landscapes: Assessing Late Pleistocene Projectile Point Reduction Strategies
abstract: How humans perceive risk has long been of interest to the social sciences. The colonization of unfamiliar landscapes by Late Pleistocene hunter-gatherers is a valuable case study that required novel strategies of risk management, technological organization, and ecological knowledge acquisition. Here, we apply evolutionary theory to projectile point reduction in the Tennessee River Valley to model utility thresholds and assess resharpening versus replacement decisions. We evaluate attributes of Clovis and Cumberland points to quantify artifact use-lives and curation intensity using a dataset drawn from the Paleoindian Database of the Americas. Results indicate that Clovis groups practiced a more conservative lithic resource management strategy by resharpening points further to extract greater utility. By contrast, subsequent Cumberland groups more frequently discarded points with variable amounts of utility remaining, suggesting reduced emphasis on resource conservation. We interpret this difference as reflecting the resolution of landscape knowledge barriers. Clovis groups confronted higher search costs in raw material acquisition, whereas Cumberland groups inherited generational knowledge of local lithic resources and became more familiar with known resource distributions. More broadly, our study demonstrates that lithic artifacts, when modeled as patches of utility, provide archaeologists with rare opportunities to test predictions of optimal foraging theory and risk management. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: PLRA-KG: Pattern-derived latent relation augmentation for knowledge graph-based recommendations
abstract: Knowledge graph (KG)-based recommendation has emerged as an effective solution to data sparsity by incorporating structured semantic information into user and item representations. However, existing KG-based recommendation approaches still face two core challenges: (i) over-reliance on explicit relations while insufficiently capturing latent connections between items, and (ii) feature degradation during high-order propagation, which leads to the dilution of informative signals in learned representations. To this end, we propose PLRA-KG, a pattern-derived latent relation augmentation framework for KG-based recommendation. PLRA-KG uncovers implicit item associations by generating syn-relations and syn-entities from global user preference patterns and relational structures. Specifically, PLRA-KG first performs relation-aware clustering via self-training to group items with strong association patterns. It then introduces a discernment-aware relation-pair selection mechanism to identify relation combinations that significantly influence user decisions. Based on the selected relation-pairs, a pattern-derived syn-relation generation strategy is designed to construct latent relations by jointly modeling global user preferences and relational value interactions. These generated syn-relations and syn-entities are subsequently integrated into the original KG, resulting in an augmented graph that better captures hidden semantic connectivity. Finally, PLRA-KG is optimized in a unified framework that jointly considers recommendation learning, KG embedding, and clustering objectives, enabling seamless integration with various KG-based recommendation models. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that PLRA-KG consistently improves both recommendation accuracy and diversity, achieving average improvements of approximately 6.64% in Recall, 7.83% in AD, 5.56% in Coverage, and 6.20% reduction in ARP. The source code is accessible at https://github.com/ZZP-RS/PLRA-KG. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: An AI-driven clinical decision support system for coronary artery disease prediction in T2DM patients using clinical laboratory parameters and deep fusion learning
abstract: This article presents an intelligent clinical decision support system that integrates graph-based modelling and deep fusion learning for coronary artery disease (CAD) risk prediction using a clinical Laboratory and validated dataset. A Graph-Based Multivariate Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) imputation approach is proposed to handle the missing values, while latent class analysis (LCA) is applied for outlier detection. The framework further incorporates with the graph-based directional risk scoring and the comorbidity network analysis to identify significant clinical attributes and capture complex relationships among risk factors. For prediction, the Enhanced TabNet and Enhanced Residual MLP (ResNet) architectures are then combined through the probabilistic fusion with XGBoost as a meta-learner. The proposed system achieves 96.77% accuracy, demonstrating improved robustness and predictive performance. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: The role of attention and norm perception in online comments’ impact on attitudes toward sunscreen: An eye-tracking approach
abstract: Social media platforms have become a major source of health information, where user-generated comments often shape attitudes toward health behaviors. Yet, the mechanisms underlying these effects remain unclear. This study examines the role of selective attention and perceived norms in the influence of online comments on attitudes toward sunscreen use. Using a between-subject eye-tracking experiment (N = 177), participants viewed a simulated YouTube live-stream video promoting sunscreen misinformation accompanied by either pro- or anti-sunscreen comments. Attention to comments was measured objectively (time viewed, fixation counts) and subjectively (self-reported attention). Results reveal that prior attitudes and behaviors predict selective attention in distinct ways: individuals with more positive attitudes attended more to pro-sunscreen comments, whereas more frequent sunscreen use was associated with more attention to anti-sunscreen comments. Mediation analyses indicate that attention to comments influences perceived norms differently across conditions. In the pro-sunscreen condition, greater attention predicted stronger perceived proximal network norms, which were strongly associated with attitude change. In contrast, in the anti-sunscreen condition, attention predicted weaker perceived social media norms but did not alter proximal norms. Across models, changes in proximal network norms were the most robust predictor of attitude change. Findings highlight the importance of examining selective attention to better understand online comment effects and reveal nuanced normative pathways. The study advances selective exposure and social norm literature in online comment contexts and underscores the value of eye-tracking for objectively measuring visual attention to online comments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Bioprinted core-shell living material platform for spatially controlled encapsulation of Bacillus subtilis and sustained metabolite exchange
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents an escalating global health crisis, demanding alternative strategies to reduce resistant pathogen burden across environments. Microbe-based biocontrol is promising, yet effectively deploying it in practical settings remains challenging. In this study, we present a 3D bioprinted core-shell construct featuring a polyethylene glycol diacrylate (PEGDA) shell with tunable nanoscale porosity, encapsulating germinable spores of the biocontrol agent Bacillus subtilis TH035. This configuration supports long-term spore viability while providing protection from common environmental stressors including UV-C irradiation, ethanol exposure, and desiccation over 4 weeks. The nanoporous PEGDA shell enables effective bacterial confinement while facilitating sufficient metabolite exchange for B. subtilis germination and growth, as well as suppression of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) growth by approximately one order of magnitude. This approach demonstrates the feasibility of embedding B. subtilis spores within engineered scaffolds for extended competitive functionality. The versatility and scalability of digital light processing (DLP) based bioprinting offers significant potential for tailored designs and high-throughput manufacturing. This proof-of-concept platform may find future applications in areas such as biomedical packaging, environmental sanitation, and built environment surface coatings, particularly in settings where intermittent moisture or nutrient availability can support spore germination and biocontrol activity. © 2026 The Authors. title: Transparent and mechanically robust fish gelatin hydrogels through covalent–noncovalent interfacial regulation by dialdehyde carboxymethyl chitin nanofibers
abstract: Polysaccharide reinforcement enhances the mechanical strength of fish gelatin (FG), narrowing its performance gap with mammalian gelatins (bovine and porcine gelatins). However, the improved mechanical strength is often accompanied by reduced optical transparency due to interfacial incompatibility-induced aggregation, phase separation, and light scattering. Herein, a covalent–noncovalent interfacial regulation strategy based on dialdehyde carboxymethyl chitin nanofibers (dCMCh-NF) was developed to optimize protein–polysaccharide interactions in FG hydrogels. At a low loading of 0.1 wt%, dCMCh-NF effectively reinforced the FG network. The FG/dCMCh8-NF hydrogel exhibited a hardness of 695.52 ± 4.51 g, significantly higher than that of pure FG (497.30 ± 19.19 g) and comparable to that of mammalian gelatin. Meanwhile, its light transmittance reached 85.70 ± 1.32%, markedly exceeding that of FG/CMCh-NF (71.37 ± 0.47%). Structural characterization and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that aldehyde groups on dCMCh-NF formed Schiff-base linkages with FG as the primary interaction, while hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions served as secondary stabilizing forces. This dual crosslinking suppressed local aggregation, reduced phase separation, and facilitated the formation of a homogeneous and compact network, thereby minimizing light scattering. This work establishes covalent–noncovalent interfacial regulation as an effective strategy for overcoming the inherent transparency-strength trade-off in polysaccharide-reinforced FG hydrogels. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Semiparametric Bayesian network classifiers
abstract: Continuous Bayesian network classifiers are attractive because they provide probabilistic interpretability, but they face a trade-off between the computational efficiency of parametric modeling and the flexibility and computational cost of nonparametric density estimation. This paper studies whether semiparametric modeling can provide a better solution for continuous classification than purely Gaussian or kernel-based approaches. Therefore, we define a family of semiparametric Bayesian network classifiers in which each continuous node is modeled either parametrically or nonparametrically, and we instantiate this framework across seven established classifier structures. We propose efficient learning algorithms that automatically determine the best structure and distribution type (parametric or nonparametric) from data. Experiments on 25 UCI benchmark datasets using multiple predictive metrics, runtime analysis, and statistical significance testing show that the proposed models generally achieve better classification performance than their parametric counterparts, while incurring lower prediction-time costs than fully nonparametric alternatives. These results are relevant for researchers and practitioners who require interpretable probabilistic classifiers in settings where Gaussian assumptions may be too restrictive and uniformly nonparametric modeling may be computationally burdensome. More broadly, the findings suggest that adaptive node-wise distribution selection is a promising framework for probabilistic classification and motivate future work on mixed-type variables and alternative learning strategies. © 2026 The Authors

title: Socio-ecological Landscape Contexts and Ecosystem Services in the Argentine Dry Chaco: From Agroexpansion to Inhabited Forests (2000–2020)
abstract: Landscape transformation driven by agribusiness expansion in the Dry Chaco is among the most pressing socio-ecological challenges globally, yet biophysical, ecosystem-service (ES), and sociodemographic dynamics are typically analyzed separately, obscuring how territorial configurations shape landscape change. To address this gap, this study proposes the Socio-Ecological Landscape Context (SELC) framework — a spatially explicit approach that integrates biophysical metrics with sociodemographic variables to define territorial units and interpret how they mediate ES supply over time. We applied it to Santiago del Estero Province in the Argentine Dry Chaco, analyzing landscape transformation (patch count and edge density) and ES supply (a rapid multicriteria assessment assigning potential supply values to land-cover types) over two decades (2000–2020), using satellite imagery (MapBiomas Chaco Collection 4), deforestation records, and census data. Cluster analysis identified six SELCs: First Wave Agroexpansion, Second Wave Agroexpansion, Concentrated Population, Inhabited Dry Forest, Hilly Arid, and Alluvial Plain. Closed woody vegetation declined by 12.6% points (from 66.6% to 54.0%), while the number of forest patches rose by 44%, indicating progressive fragmentation. Two contrasting patterns emerge: dynamic SELCs (First and Second Wave Agroexpansion, Concentrated Population) show marked declines in key ES, whereas persistent SELCs maintain higher ES levels over time. A sparse rural population shows a modest but consistent positive association with ES supply. These findings suggest that similar land-cover compositions can yield divergent socio-ecological outcomes depending on landscape configuration and modes of inhabitation, supporting biocultural conservation approaches that recognize peasant and Indigenous communities as active contributors to landscape multifunctionality. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Resurgence of large-scale influenza A (H1N1) outbreaks: Modeling the interplay of transmission, loss of immunity, and vaccination
abstract: Influenza is a highly transmissible respiratory virus that can cause devastating pandemics. The 2009 influenza pandemic, caused by a strain of A(H1N1) virus, resulted in millions of cases and hundreds of thousands of deaths worldwide. In the following years, many regions experienced waves driven by environmental conditions, waning immunity, and other factors. More dramatically, several locations saw unpredicted large resurgent outbreaks, yet the mechanisms behind these severe resurgences remain poorly understood. Despite an extensive literature of epidemic models aimed at explaining and predicting H1N1 dynamics, mathematical frameworks specifically designed to address why these large outbreaks recur years after an initial epidemic are still lacking. Here we address this gap by proposing a mechanistic model with time-varying rates of infection, loss of immunity, and vaccination. In particular, we explore two mathematical functions to model dynamic loss of immunity, capturing how viral evolution may reduce the duration of immune protection. Numerical simulations show that the model reproduces key features of H1N1 case data, and that delayed resurgence is associated with longer immunity periods and higher vaccine efficacy. We also fit the model to data from Brazil, Turkey, Iran, New Zealand, the United States, Colombia, South Africa, and Croatia, demonstrating its ability to capture resurgence patterns. Fitted infection rates exhibited a wide range of temporal profiles, from regular annual cycles to higher-frequency oscillations and gradual changes, suggesting that transmission is driven by factors beyond seasonal influences. The model also inferred dynamic loss-of-immunity rates, representing different effects of antigenic drift. To our knowledge, this is the first mechanistic modeling study specifically aimed at investigating large resurgent H1N1 epidemics across multiple locations. Our findings highlight the need for context-specific models and surveillance systems that account for the complex interplay among environmental drivers, population immunity, and viral mutation driving H1N1 dynamics. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Data centres and the new strategic infrastructure governance: From cloud ESG to compute sovereignty
abstract: Data centres have moved from the background of the digital economy to the foreground of energy, climate, industrial and national-security politics. Artificial intelligence is intensifying this shift through growing demand for compute, electricity, cooling, land, hardware and critical materials. Yet governance remains largely organised around facility-level metrics that treat data centres as bounded technical assets rather than strategic infrastructure embedded in grids, water systems, supply chains, communities and security architectures. This article develops the CLOUDS framework—Coherence, Lifecycle materiality, Operational locality, Utility burden, Digital sovereignty, and Social licence and public purpose—as a diagnostic architecture for evaluating data centres as system-shaping infrastructure. It also develops capacity extraction: the process through which heterogeneous inputs such as electricity, water, land, permits, institutional trust and community tolerance are rendered as a single quantity called capacity and converted into compute whose higher-value layers may remain controlled elsewhere. The framework is developed through an integrative review and tiered empirical design spanning Chile, Australia, Querétaro, Ireland and Singapore. It is proposed for testing rather than presented as validated. Two findings are central. First, instrument incoherence can arise without regulatory capture when no institution can govern trade-offs across electricity, water, planning and public value. Second, hosting is not sovereignty: physical location alone creates no assured claim on compute access, workload priority, crisis continuity or higher-value layers. The policy implication is strategic infrastructure bargaining over both system capacity and the institutions governing its conversion into compute. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Mechanization, gender, and livelihoods in artisanal and small-scale mining: a technofeminist political ecology perspective
abstract: This study examines the gendered impacts of mechanization in artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM), a sector increasingly shaped by excavators, washing plants, motorized pumps, trommels, and leaching techniques. Drawing on field investigations in mining communities in southwestern Ghana, the study shows that technological adoption in ASM is not gender neutral. While mechanization has improved efficiency and productivity, it has simultaneously displaced women from core mining activities where they historically played essential economic roles. As a result, women are increasingly relegated to ancillary and informal tasks that generate lower and often unsustainable incomes while exposing them to heightened environmental and health risks. These intersecting experiences show how mechanization can simultaneously produce economic displacement and continued environmental vulnerability for women in ASM. To explain these dynamics, the study develops and applies a Technofeminist Political Ecology (TPE) framework as an original analytical lens. Integrating insights from technofeminism and feminist political ecology, TPE conceptualizes technology not as a neutral tool of progress but as a social and political force that restructures labor, redistributes environmental risk, and reconfigures gendered vulnerabilities within extractive economies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Sustainable epoxy–polyurethane adhesives based on ionic liquids with high adhesion strength, low-temperature resistance, and direct adhesion on cold surfaces
abstract: The exploration of the trade-off between adhesion performance and low-temperature resistance is essential for enabling the application of adhesive materials in cryogenic environments. However, simultaneously achieving strong adhesion, cryogenic tolerance, reusability, and stable adhesion directly on cold Surfaces remains a major challenge. Herein, we report a series of epoxy polyurethane adhesives regulated by ionic liquids (ILs), in which excellent low-temperature resistance and high adhesion are achieved through a crystallization-delayed self-reinforcement mechanism. The results demonstrate that the PU–E44 adhesive achieves an adhesion strength of 5.7 MPa at –40 ℃ and maintains a strength of 1.18 MPa even under liquid nitrogen conditions. Furthermore, this adhesive not only exhibits good adhesion properties at low temperatures and reusability, but also enables stable adhesion directly on cold surfaces. Such an adhesive, combining low-temperature durability, reusability, and direct adhesion to cold surfaces, offers new insights into the design and application of sustainable and recyclable adhesive systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Deep sea mining, think tanks, and the politics of expertise
abstract: Deep sea mining (DSM) is being contemplated in an environment of heightened geopolitical tensions. A confluence of factors has led to securitised framings of DSM, including the centrality of the Pacific as both a potential mining location and a perceived frontline of strategic competition, and the desire of western states to “derisk” from China when it comes to critical minerals. One of the factors shaping how strategic competition is understood and responded to is the role of experts. Within western states such as the US and Australia, think tanks play an important role in shaping narratives, perceptions, and policies relating to defence and foreign affairs. In this paper I will investigate how western security-related think tanks are approaching DSM.I will argue that think tanks are playing a significant role in contributing to narratives of necessity regarding DSM, and that security and strategic competition are the dominant framing of these narratives of necessity. title: Learning from incomplete signals: Multi-view knowledge distillation for robust harmful micro-Video detection
abstract: As hateful and misleading content continues to proliferate on social media platforms, detecting multimodal harmful content in micro-videos has become increasingly important. While recent advances in this area have shown promise, existing methods often assume complete access to all modalities, including video, audio, and textual descriptions. This assumption fundamentally limits their robustness in real-world settings, where micro-videos are frequently modality- and segment-incomplete due to upload artifacts, platform-level compression, or missing metadata. To bridge this gap, we introduce three real-world benchmarks that systematically capture varying degrees of incompleteness at both the modality and segment levels. We further propose MVKD , a multi-view knowledge distillation framework tailored for robust harmful micro-video detection under incomplete and uncertain conditions. MVKD (1) adaptively distills modality-specific knowledge through confidence-aware guidance, (2) enhances sample- and domain-level representations via contrastive alignment, and (3) integrates complementary cues using a multi-view mixture-of-experts strategy. Extensive experiments show that MVKD consistently outperforms strong baselines in both accuracy and robustness across diverse missingness patterns, and generalizes effectively to previously unseen domains. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Scaffold-shift uncertainty calibration in molecular activity prediction: A multi-target benchmark of coverage, efficiency, and risk-aware selection
abstract: Uncertainty estimates are increasingly used to prioritize molecules, yet their reliability under chemical scaffold shift is poorly characterized. We benchmarked prediction intervals and downstream selection policies across six human protein targets using 20,327 target-specific ChEMBL 37 compound records (19,972 globally unique ChEMBL molecule identifiers) and 7731 target-specific Bemis–Murcko scaffold instances, two model classes, and 20 scaffold-disjoint train/calibration/test partitions per target. We compared raw random-forest ensemble intervals, standard split conformal intervals, similarity-normalized conformal intervals, and similarity-binned local conformal intervals. Raw nominal 90% ensemble intervals achieved only 9.5%–11.4% molecule-weighted coverage. Conformal methods generally restored average coverage toward 90%, but results depended on target, partition, model, and whether molecules or scaffolds received equal weight. Conditional coverage averaged 82.3% in the least training-similar quartile and 78.7% in the highest-activity quartile. Similarity-adaptive methods did not uniformly improve the coverage–width trade-off. Across 240 matched target–partition–model comparisons, lower-confidence-bound selection reduced mean observed activity by 0.107 pActivity units, reduced top-decile hit rate by 0.063, and increased false optimism by 0.012, while selecting 2.16 additional scaffolds on average. Marginal calibration, conditional reliability, and decision utility are therefore distinct properties. Conformal calibration can repair severe interval undercoverage, but it does not automatically provide reliable extrapolation or a superior molecular-ranking policy. © 2026 The Authors

title: Revisiting topological bias in imbalanced graph learning: A Dual-Balanced Graph Neural Network approach
abstract: Class imbalance in node classification can impair the discriminative capability of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) partly by limiting class-wise topological supervision reachability. While existing methods primarily focus on balancing sample quantities, we theoretically characterize, under a mean-field neighborhood-growth model and an exponential attenuation assumption for long-range message passing, how the effective supervision intensity of minority-class nodes can exhibit a power-law decay as the imbalance ratio increases. This conditional scaling result provides a theoretical explanation for how limited supervision reachability can constrain minority-class learning. To address this, we propose the Dual-Balanced Graph Neural Network (DB-GNN), which introduces a supervision-reshaping graph augmentation strategy. By constructing class-balanced supervision anchors, DB-GNN equalizes anchor-level supervision quantity and narrows relative class-wise disparities in topological supervision distance. Furthermore, we devise an anchor-guided alignment mechanism to transfer balanced anchor-level constraints to the corresponding original training nodes. We also introduce a stability-aware regularization strategy that uses cross-view prediction consistency to apply pseudo-supervision to stable unlabeled nodes and negative learning to prediction-inconsistent nodes. Experiments on six benchmark datasets show that DB-GNN achieves competitive performance against strong imbalance-aware baselines, attaining accuracy gains of up to 3.4 percentage points on CiteSeer and 3.6 percentage points on Computers over the second-best methods in the corresponding settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Equilibrium of inorganic carbon species during photocatalytic CO2 reduction in TiO2 slurries: effect on the product yields and on the process kinetics
abstract: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction is a promising route for renewable fuel production, yet its efficiency remains limited by complex interactions between reaction conditions and carbon speciation. In aqueous systems, CO2 is in equilibrium with bicarbonate and carbonate species, with their distribution governed by pH, while only molecular CO2 is directly involved in photoreduction. This study systematically investigates the influence of carbon speciation on photocatalytic performance in TiO2 suspensions under UV-C irradiation. Experiments were performed in a stirred batch photoreactor using different loadings of Aeroxide P25 TiO2 in NaOH or NaHCO3 solutions saturated with either CO2 or He. Gas-phase product formation, pH and total dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) were monitored. The highest yields of CO, CH4, and H2 were obtained in CO2-saturated NaHCO3 solution, which stabilized at about pH 6.7 and exhibited higher DIC and increased availability of dissolved CO2. In contrast, He-saturated NaHCO3 solution exhibited higher pH, significantly lower fractions of molecular CO2, and reduced product yields despite comparable DIC. A comprehensive reactor-scale kinetic model explicitly coupling inorganic carbon equilibrium with heterogeneous photocatalytic kinetics, radiation transport, and gas–liquid mass transfer showed good agreement with experimental data. This work demonstrates that photocatalytic performance is governed by the equilibrium concentration of molecular CO2 rather than the total carbon content, revealing a trade-off between CO2 capture capacity and reactive availability of CO2. These findings provide new insight into the role of carbon speciation in aqueous photocatalytic systems and offer a quantitative reactor–scale framework for process optimization and photoreactor simulation and design. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Students’ engagement with statements and their understanding of corresponding proofs by contradiction and contraposition
abstract: Engagement has been shown to influence students’ understanding and achievement, yet little is known about how engagement with statements relates to students’ understanding of corresponding proofs. In this paper, we take a step towards addressing this gap by investigating whether engaging with statements is associated with better understanding of proofs by contradiction and contraposition. Eighty-seven Indonesian undergraduate mathematics education students, organized in four groups, participated in the study. Two groups (n = 43) were randomly selected to first engage with the statements—reflecting on their meaning, judging their truth, and attempting to prove or disprove them—before responding to an instrument designed to measure their understanding of given proofs for the same statements; the other two groups (n = 44) proceeded directly to the instrument. There were six statements overall, three proved by contradiction and three by contraposition. We found that students who engaged with the statements achieved significantly higher mean scores on measures of proof understanding than those who did not, with a medium effect size. Regression analyses confirmed engagement as a significant predictor of students’ understanding for both proof methods, and individual semi-structured interviews with 12 participants provided qualitative support for these findings. Overall, our findings identify engagement with statements as a meaningful factor in students’ proof understanding and suggests that selectively incorporating an engagement stage before introducing key proofs may enhance undergraduate mathematics instruction beyond the typical Definition-Theorem-Proof (DTP) approach. title: A SIQOR dynamical model for rumor propagation in online social networks with coupled banning and debunking
abstract: Online social networks (OSNs) often face a counterintuitive challenge during rumor outbreaks: regulatory suppression, such as node-level banning, can paradoxically amplify dissemination. Existing models largely neglect these cascading behavioral responses. To accurately simulate this dynamic and provide a mechanistic interpretation of the Streisand effect, the SIQOR rumor propagation model is proposed in this paper. Moving beyond traditional frameworks, the SIQOR model captures the interaction between platform-level intervention and user behavioral responses, specifically emphasizing how banning stimulates a state of heightened willingness to disseminate the rumor and curiosity among neighboring users. Following theoretical analysis of the system’s dynamic behavior, the model is validated through numerical experiments on synthetic scale-free networks and empirically verified using four real-world Twitter datasets. The results faithfully reproduce the peak scale and long-tail decay of actual rumor outbreaks. Crucially, while raising the baseline banning rate monotonically suppresses the peak scale of active spreaders, aggressive early-stage interventions subject to capacity limits conditionally trigger a non-monotonic surge in propagation desire among neighboring users, demonstrating that raising the banning probability mechanically triggers a non-linear surge in propagation desire, thereby proving that the Streisand effect is a predictable dynamical outcome rather than a mere behavioral anomaly. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Translanguaging as an epistemic mechanism in Korean immigrant parents’ mediation of mathematical meaning
abstract: This study investigates how Korean immigrant parents draw on translanguaging practices to mediate mathematical meaning with their elementary-aged children during home mathematics interaction. Using video-based, ethnographically informed observations of six sessions across three parent-child dyads, the analysis examines how parents coordinated Korean and English alongside gesture, diagrams, and tools to make mathematical relationships more visible, interpretable, and open to negotiation in real time. In this study, translanguaging is conceptualized as the epistemic mechanism through which mathematical meaning is mediated. The findings suggest that parents used translanguaging to diagnose procedural and structural mismatches, make unfamiliar terminology more accessible, bridge semantic and structural relationships across concepts, reorganize algebraic representations, and coordinate geometric action through multimodal guidance. The most salient form of this mechanism appeared in diagnostic interactions, where bilingual contrast and multimodal coordination made otherwise implicit mismatches visible and available for repair. The study contributes to translanguaging research in mathematics by respecifying translanguaging not only as a resource for participation but as an epistemic mechanism through which mathematical structure is made visible and available for reorganization. The study also suggests that Korean-English interaction provides an analytically productive context for examining how typologically associated linguistic resources become interactionally available in mathematical activity. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Green hydrogen-enhanced coal-based methanol-to-aromatics and olefins system: SHAP-coupled entropy-energy-economic analysis and ANN-assisted multi-objective optimization
abstract: A green hydrogen-enhanced coal-based methanol-to-aromatics and olefins (MTA/MTO) system offers a promising route to improve carbon utilization and reduce emissions in coal-based chemical production. However, the key variables and subsystem-level contributions affecting overall performance are not fully understood, and achieving efficient, feasible multi-objective optimization is challenging. This study develops an artificial neural network (ANN)-assisted multi-objective optimization approach based on SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-coupled entropy-energy-economic (3E) analysis. The approach integrates ANN-based Pareto region identification with hierarchical Aspen Plus re-evaluation and repair to improve both optimization efficiency and solution feasibility. SHAP-coupled 3E analysis clarifies the roles of decision variables and subsystems in thermodynamic, economic, and energy performance, and highlights trade-offs among entropy generation rate, annual energy cost, and net present value. Results indicate that methanol-related and proton exchange membrane electrolyzer operations primarily influence overall 3E performance, while electrolyzer operation and methanol separation variables are most significant for objective trade-offs. Utilizing an ANN-assisted parallel NSGA-II, a promising Pareto region is identified in surrogate space within 132 s. Following rigorous re-evaluation and SHAP-coupled 3E-informed repair, all ANN-guided solutions converge in the rigorous model, with the relative errors between rigorous objective values and ANN predictions below 1.00 %. Compared to the baseline, the selected compromise solution increases the net present value by 28.48 %, while reducing the overall entropy generation rate by 1.52 % and the annual energy cost by 0.13 %. This study provides an interpretable, efficient, and reliable optimization framework for the low-carbon upgrading of highly integrated coal-based chemical processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Overcoming the sensitivity–selectivity trade-off in laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) for uranium isotope analysis via joint spectral decomposition of single- and double-pulse spectra
abstract: Reliable analysis of uranium isotopes (235U and 238U) is essential throughout the nuclear fuel cycle. Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) has emerged as a promising technique for rapid detection of uranium. However, its application to isotope analysis is hindered by a fundamental sensitivity-selectivity trade-off: High-energy laser pulses, while essential for enhancing sensitivity, exacerbate the overlap between closely spaced spectral features, thereby reducing isotope selectivity. To circumvent this dilemma, the present study proposes a joint spectral decomposition framework that integrates two complementary spectra obtained using single-pulse (SP) and double-pulse (DP) LIBS. SP spectra preserve the narrow spectral features required for isotope discrimination, whereas DP spectra provide enhanced emission intensity and detection sensitivity. By simultaneously fitting the SP and DP spectra under a shared isotope-ratio constraint, the proposed framework combines DP-enhanced sensitivity with SP-derived isotope selectivity, achieving a uranium limit of detection (LOD) of 0.008% in a soil matrix while keeping the isotope-quantification bias within approximately 1 percentage point. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed framework for improving the analytical performance of LIBS-based uranium isotope analysis and provide a basis for further validation toward rapid uranium isotope screening. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: HGMG: Enhancing heterogeneous graph embedding by meta-graph learning
abstract: Due to the ability of heterogeneous graph in modeling different types of objects and relationships in the real world, and the capability of graph embedding in extracting the effective features from graphs, heterogeneous graph embedding has received extensive attention in recent years. Heterogeneous graph embedding aims to learn low-dimensional node representations by capturing attribute information, structural information and semantic information of heterogeneous graph, facilitating downstream tasks, such as node classification, node clustering and link prediction. Meta-graphs, the powerful tool for expressing the complex composite semantic relationships between nodes, are widely combined with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and the attention mechanism to explore rich and meaningful semantic information hidden in heterogeneous graphs. Although existing meta-graph-based methods have achieved success, there remains considerable room for comprehensively exploring semantics in heterogeneous graphs, including selecting meta-graphs with rich semantics, learning meta-graph semantics, utilizing diverse node semantics. To address the above challenges, we propose a novel model for enhancing Heterogeneous Graph embedding by Meta-Graph learning (HGMG). Firstly, we propose a structure-aware meta-graph selection strategy for capturing rich semantics. Secondly, we design a meta-graph semantic learning mechanism for enhancing node embeddings. Finally, we present a semantic incorporating method for fusing the structural semantics and inherent semantics of nodes. Experimental results on real datasets demonstrate the proposed HGMG model outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on three downstream tasks including node classification, node clustering and link prediction. The source code and implementation details of HGMG are available at https://github.com/kkkkajwjds/HGMG. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A review of tandem matching for chemical reactor design
abstract: Reactor design is fundamental to chemical engineering, supporting controllable, efficient, and safe unit operations and chemical conversions. Tandem architecture can address inherent trade-offs among reaction stages in conventional reactors. Tandem matching, the core of its performance, governs the synergy between sequential processes across spatial and temporal domains. We review recent advances, current challenges, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled future directions of tandem matching for reactor design. We propose a unified hierarchical theoretical framework for tandem matching spanning molecular, catalyst, reactor, and system scales. It integrates transport-reaction matching that couples transport rates with reaction kinetics, and tandem thermodynamics-kinetics matching that coordinates thermodynamics and reaction kinetics as a novel conceptual insight. Together, they determine the efficiency, selectivity, and stability of tandem reactor systems, either in a zoned single reactor or cascaded multiple reactors. This framework offers a unified rationale for developing next-generation chemical reactors toward sustainable and intensified processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Phase-resilient in situ exsolution via thermal pre-stabilization of a double perovskite for high-efficiency solid oxide CO2 electrolysis
abstract: Metal in situ exsolution endows perovskites with highly active and strongly anchored catalytic sites for high-temperature CO2 electrolysis. However, the concomitant lattice oxygen loss and B-site cation reduction often trigger detrimental phase transitions that compromise long-term durability. Here we demonstrate a chemically non-invasive thermal pre-stabilization strategy that fundamentally resolves this activity-stability trade-off. By elevating the calcination temperature of the double perovskite (DP) Sr1.95Ce0.05Fe1.3Ni0.2Mo0.5O6−δ (SCFNM) from 1100 to 1250 °C, we induce lattice contraction and enhanced BO6 octahedral ordering, which increase B-site cation oxidation states and metal-oxygen bond strength. This robust structure effectively suppresses the DP phase of perovskite transitioning to Ruddlesden-Popper phase during in situ exsolution, while preserving uniformly exsolved NiFe nanoalloys and retaining a higher oxygen vacancy concentration and a stronger CO2 adsorption capacity. As a result, the phase-pre-stabilized NiFe@SCFNM-1250 achieved a current density of 1.72 A cm-2, a maximum CO Faraday efficiency of 98.63% at 1.5 V and 850 °C and a markedly reduced degradation rate of 2.06 mA cm–2 h–1 over 100 h, which outperforming its non-stabilized counterpart by nearly twofold in durability. This work establishes thermal pre-stabilization as a universally applicable paradigm for balancing catalytic activity with structural stability in perovskite-based electrodes, offering a chemical-doping-free route toward durable CO2 electrolysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: From half-cell to heavy-duty: a critical review of MXene catalysts for PEMFC cathodes
abstract: MXenes have emerged as promising cathode catalyst supports for proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) due to their high conductivity and tunable surface chemistry. However, despite numerous reports of exceptional half-cell oxygen reduction reaction activity, MXene-based catalysts have not yet been demonstrated to translate into practical membrane electrode assembly (MEA) performance, especially under combined heavy-duty automotive conditions. This review critically evaluates the gap between the rotating disk electrode and single-cell performance of Pt/MXene, MXene-carbon, non-precious, and single-atom catalysts. We systematically benchmark MEA-level metrics, peak power density under H2/air, high-current–density polarization, electrochemical surface area retention under accelerated stress tests, and Pt utilization against commercial Pt/C and heavy-duty targets. We identify key unresolved barriers: MXene oxidation under acidic and oxidative cathode conditions, nanosheet restacking-induced oxygen transport resistance, and the lack of standardized MEA validation. Finally, we provide an engineering-oriented roadmap that integrates termination engineering, hybrid architectures, and AI-assisted design to bridge the half-cell-to-heavy-duty gap. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: STR-LBSN: Spatio-temporal Role-based Heterogeneous Hypergraph Embedding for location-based social networks
abstract: Location-based social networks (LBSNs) contain rich social, spatial, and temporal information. However, most existing embedding methods overly simplify the underlying hypergraph structure, represent each user with a single static embedding, and fail to model the coupling between social relationships and mobility behaviors. To address these limitations, we propose STR-LBSN, a Spatio-temporal Role-based Heterogeneous Hypergraph Embedding framework for Location-Based Social Networks. STR-LBSN models users’ temporally evolving behavioral roles as hidden states in a Hidden Markov Model and constructs a role-centric hypergraph from the decoded role assignments. Based on this structure, STR-LBSN learns multi-role representations through biased random walks and heterogeneous sampling in cosine space, while balancing social contexts and spatio-temporal mobility patterns. Extensive experiments on seven real-world LBSN datasets demonstrate that STR-LBSN achieves the highest mean performance among twelve state-of-the-art baselines in nearly all settings. Specifically, for friend recommendation, STR-LBSN achieves substantial relative improvements across four evaluation metrics, including Precision, Recall, F1-score, and NDCG, with particularly large gains on sparse datasets. For POI recommendation and activity recommendation, it delivers average performance gains of about 5% to 30% in terms of Hit@5, Hit@10, and Hit@20. Furthermore, comprehensive ablation studies and parameter sensitivity analyses support the effectiveness of the main modeling components and examine the robustness of STR-LBSN to key hyperparameters. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Interface-tuned Janus-type high-entropy heterostructures for cascade electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural
abstract: High-entropy materials (HEMs) hold great promise for electrocatalytic applications owing to their tunable electronic structures, particularly in complex reactions involving multiple intermediates. However, HEMs prepared by conventional methods often suffer from a trade-off between site diversity and reaction specificity, resulting in limited catalytic efficiency. In this study, we address this challenge by developing a Janus-type high-entropy alloy/high-entropy layered hydroxide (HEA/HELH) heterostructure with synthetically controllable interfaces via Fe3 +-mediated topochemical reconstruction with precisely controlled reconstruction times of 30–120 min. Leveraging the Fe3+/Fe2+ redox-driven carbon-confined galvanic replacement reaction, we achieved epitaxial interfacial growth and formed a built-in electric field (BIEF) with a work-function difference of 0.54 eV, which lowered the potential required to reach 10 mA cm⁻² by 240 mV. The optimized HEA/HELH heterostructure delivers a Faradaic efficiency of 93.5% for FDCA at 1.55 V vs. RHE and retains more than 90% of its current response over 100 h, comparing favorably with recently reported HMFOR electrocatalysts. Mechanistic studies suggest that interfacial charge redistribution associated with the BIEF facilitates the formation and utilization of high-valence Co/Ni/Fe species, thereby promoting cascade oxidation from HMF to FDCA. Furthermore, the controllable HEA/HELH demonstrates significant potential for broader adaptability in multistep electrocatalytic oxidation. This work provides an interfacial engineering strategy for designing high-entropy catalysts for electrocatalytic biomass valorization. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
label: Social Sciences

title: IBCL: Information Bottleneck Contrastive Learning with minimum sufficient augmentation and generalized representations
abstract: Contrastive Learning (CL) has established itself as a dominant paradigm in self-supervised representation learning. However, its efficacy can be limited by discriminative information overfitting, where models learn overly specialized features for instance discrimination while insufficiently preserving semantic and structural information needed for downstream generalization. In this work, we re-examine CL through the lens of the Information Bottleneck (IB) principle and propose Information Bottleneck Contrastive Learning (IBCL), an IB-inspired framework that characterizes contrastive representation learning as a compression–preservation trade-off. Specifically, IBCL introduces two conceptual criteria: minimum sufficient augmentation, which encourages compact contrastive views by reducing redundant input information, and information-generalized representations, which aim to preserve useful semantic and structural information beyond pretext discrimination. Guided by this perspective, we propose Masked Reconstruction Contrastive Learning (MRCL), a plug-and-play instantiation of IBCL for classical contrastive learning frameworks. MRCL uses random patch masking as a controllable view-level compression mechanism and incorporates a lightweight reconstruction objective as an auxiliary semantic-structural regularizer to mitigate excessive information loss caused by masking. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MRCL consistently improves conventional CL baselines across ImageNet classification, ADE20K semantic segmentation, and COCO detection/instance segmentation. Notably, MRCL shows favorable scalability on large Vision Transformers and achieves competitive transfer performance on dense prediction benchmarks. These results suggest that the proposed compression–preservation design provides a practical and effective way to improve the generalization ability of contrastive representations. © 2026
label: Social Sciences

title: On the role of perception in the psychology of art: More than meets the eye of the beholder
abstract: Perception is a cornerstone of aesthetic experience and the psychology of art, providing the primary means through which people engage with artworks and generate emotional and cognitive responses. Across theories of aesthetics, perception is the key process connecting the classic psychological triad of stimulus, person, and context, by integrating sensory information with situational influences. It encompasses factors ranging from low-level visual features, such as natural image statistics with broad appeal, to high-level influences related to familiarity with particular contents and artistic styles shaped by individual experience and sociocultural background. Crucially, mid-level perceptual processes are where perceptual, cognitive, emotional, and contextual factors interact most strongly, playing a central role in aesthetic appreciation and in explaining individual differences in artistic preferences. © 2026 The Author
label: Social Sciences

title: Optimization of process variables for CO2/CH4 and CO2/N2 binary gas separation using dual-layer hollow fiber mixed-matrix membrane
abstract: Membrane based carbon dioxide removal from methane, biogas, and process modified streams, such as flue gas recycling, oxy-fuel combustion with air ingress, and industrial exhausts remained a pivotal strategy to curb greenhouse gas emissions and support sustainable energy development. Dual-layer hollow fiber mixed-matrix membranes (DLHFMMMs) have recently garnered substantial attention for CO2 separation, however, optimization of separation variables for such process is still imperative. In this study, design of experiment framework was adopted to perform process optimization of binary gas separation involving CO2/CH4 and CO2/N2 via DLHFMMM. The influences of feed pressure (2–10 bar for CO2/CH4; 5–10 bar for CO2/N2), temperature (30–50 °C), and CO2 feed composition (30–70 vol.% for CO2/CH4; 10–50 vol.% for CO2/N2) on DLHFMMM performance were evaluated. A response surface methodology (RSM) coupled with central composite design (CCD) was utilized to develop predictive models correlating these variables with CO2, CH4 and N2 permeances, along with the corresponding CO2/CH4 and CO2/N2 separation factors. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) identified the most influential factors governing each response, while three-dimensional response surfaces elucidated variable interactions. The optimized conditions for the CO2/CH4 separation (50 °C, 4.420 bar, 70 vol.% CO2) yielded a 22.76 GPU for CO2 permeance together with a CO2/CH4 separation factor of 27.59. For the CO2/N2 binary gas separation, optimal performance (50 °C, 10.000 bar, 50 vol.% CO2) resulted a 14.52 GPU of CO2 permeance and a CO2/N2 separation factor of 46.36. The close agreement between experimental measurements and model predictions confirms the validity of the developed models. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Mapping the science of aesthetic emotions
abstract: In this review, we trace the current state of research on aesthetic emotion in empirical aesthetics. Taking several theoretical contributions as a starting point, we highlight empirical studies that recently added to our knowledge in the field. Furthermore, we also highlight where the majority of recent work has been done, and which questions remain open. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: A solution approach for sustainable uncertain multi-objective 5D shortest path problem involving fixed-charge: Application to fish transport system
abstract: Sustainability encompasses the interplay between environmental, economic, and social systems at multiple levels. Vehicles rely on various fuels to meet their energy needs in transportation systems. However, these fuels emit greenhouse gases, leading to environmental pollution. Considering this context, this study investigates a sustainable fixed-charge multi-objective multi-route multi-conveyance multi-driver shortest path problem. The main goal is to identify the most efficient route that minimizes costs, time, risk, carbon emissions, and distance for travel between sources and destinations. In practical scenarios, the parameters of fixed-charge multi-objective multi-route multi-conveyance multi-driver shortest path problems often involve uncertainties, which can be anticipated based on human judgment. Liu's uncertainty theory is widely accepted as a legitimate tool for handling such uncertainties. Therefore, zigzag uncertain variables are incorporated into the proposed model to represent uncertain parameters. The study develops the expected and optimistic value models of the fixed-charge uncertain multi-objective multi-route multi-conveyance multi-driver shortest path problem and provides their corresponding deterministic transformations. Moreover, two multi-objective genetic algorithms namely, aspiration level - based non-dominated sorting genetic algorithms -II and III are used to address the deterministic model. An application of the proposed model is demonstrated through a fish transport system problem. A comparison of the compromise solutions obtained from the mentioned techniques is presented with hybrid genetic algorithm, non-dominated sorting genetic algorithms-II, and III, along with a sensitivity analysis of the objective functions concerning the shape parameter and aspiration level. Finally, the coverage performance measure is calculated to showcase the effectiveness of the proposed methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Gender differences in early semantic trajectories and academic career persistence
abstract: Gender disparities in academia are well documented in publication output, citations, and career attrition, yet relatively little is known about whether male and female scholars differ in the semantic development of their research. Using SPECTER2 embeddings derived from 67 million publications in OpenAlex, we characterize the semantic trajectories of 2.76 million scholars using three measures: semantic expansion (divergence from prior work), research coherence (consistency of prior research), and semantic alignment (continuity with prior research direction). On average, male scholars exhibit greater semantic expansion, whereas female scholars show higher research coherence and semantic alignment. These differences persist across career stages and productivity levels. Discrete-time hazard models further indicate that early semantic trajectories are associated with subsequent publication-based career persistence. Greater early semantic expansion is associated with a lower risk of dropout for both genders, whereas greater research coherence and semantic alignment are associated with a higher dropout risk, with stronger associations among female scholars. These patterns are consistently observed across major scientific disciplines. Together, our findings suggest that gender differences in academia are reflected not only in research productivity and career outcomes but also in the semantic organization of research development, and that early semantic trajectories are associated with subsequent patterns of career persistence. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Adaptive shuffle-boosting federated learning for imbalanced medical image analysis
abstract: Medical image analysis is critical for clinical diagnosis, yet its application in federated learning remains constrained by class imbalance and inter-institutional heterogeneity. To address these challenges, we propose FedASB, a novel federated learning framework for imbalanced medical image analysis. This framework integrates two complementary modules: Adaptive Head Shuffle (AdaShuffle) and Dynamic Head Ensemble (DynEns) to enhance generalization capability and decision reliability in the presence of imbalanced and heterogeneous medical data. Specifically, we propose AdaShuffle, a dynamic head redistribution mechanism that assigns diversity classifier heads to different clients based on cross-client validation performance stored in a memory bank. By selectively excluding overfitted heads, AdaShuffle achieves an effective trade-off between global representation learning and client-specific adaptation. During inference, we propose DynEns to adaptively integrate predictions from multiple client-specific classifier heads via entropy-based confidence weighting, allowing reliable classifier heads to dominate the prediction while suppressing uncertain or overconfident outputs. Extensive experiments on multiple medical image benchmarks demonstrate that FedASB consistently outperforms existing federated learning methods under both imbalanced and heterogeneous conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Out of the picture: A multilevel framework of gender disparities in art
abstract: Why do women artists remain a minority in museum collections and art markets, decades after becoming the majority in art schools? Talent does not explain it, since creative ability shows no meaningful gender differences, and audiences cannot tell an artist's gender from the work itself. The gap persists, we argue, because it is produced by a system rather than at any single stage of artwork production, selection, and reception. We therefore introduce a multilevel framework that treats the art world as an ecosystem. Artists, gatekeepers, and audiences act on artworks within three embedded levels of analysis (individual, institutional, and societal), and gender enters the ecosystem not only through these actors but also through the gendered content of artworks and the norms of the wider society. Actors, artworks, and norms interact across levels and over time. Societal beliefs in male artistic genius are internalized by artists and audiences and enacted by gatekeeping institutions; biased selections accumulate into a male canon; and the canon feeds that belief back to the next generation. The ecosystem is thus recursive, reproducing inequality without requiring discriminatory intent. Yet the same loop invites contestation, and excluded artists have answered with concealment, counter-institutions, and activism. Integrating evidence scattered across disciplines, this review derives a research agenda that treats the feedback loop, rather than any single stage, as the unit of analysis and as the lever of change. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: BadLingual: Language-Triggered Anomalous Behavior in Multilingual Foundation Large Language Models
abstract: Multilingual foundation Large Language Models (LLMs) have greatly improved accessibility for users across different regions, but they also introduce new surfaces for anomalous behavior. In this paper, we identify a new form of anomalous behavior in multilingual foundation LLMs, termed lingual-backdoor attack, in which the input language itself acts as the trigger and selectively induces attacker-desired abnormal outputs. Because language is naturally associated with specific speaker populations, lingual-backdoor enables precise targeting and may amplify social bias or misinformation risks. To study this threat, we first implement a task-specific baseline that injects the anomaly through conventional data poisoning on downstream tasks. Although effective in controlled settings, it generalizes poorly to realistic task-agnostic scenarios on instruction-tuned foundation LLMs. We therefore propose BadLingual, a task-agnostic lingual-backdoor that improves trigger robustness and cross-task generalization through PPL-constrained Greedy Coordinate Gradient-based Search (PGCG) and adversarial training. Extensive experiments across multiple models, languages, and downstream tasks show that BadLingual improves attack success rate by up to 37.35% over the baseline while preserving utility on clean inputs. Furthermore, widely used anomaly detection and recovery methods are largely ineffective against this language-triggered anomalous behavior. These findings reveal multilinguality as a previously underexplored source of anomalous behavior in foundation LLMs and highlight the urgent need for more effective anomaly-aware defenses. © 2026
label: Social Sciences

title: “Can talking like you make it work?”: The role of linguistic convergence and maintenance in human–robot interaction
abstract: As domestic robots become more integrated into everyday life, effective and socially attuned communication strategies are essential for enabling meaningful human–robot collaboration. Prior work has addressed robot errors, but less is known about handling user errors. This study investigates how domestic robots’ verbal coordination strategies shape user experiences when handling human speech errors. To establish the experimental framework, Communication Accommodation Theory (CAT) was applied to define two linguistic strategies (convergence vs. maintenance), and McGrath's Group Task Circumplex Model was utilized to establish four task types (Generate, Choose, Execute, and Negotiate). We conducted a video-based experiment using a 2 × 4 × 2 mixed factorial design, varying CAT strategy, task type, and age group. Results revealed that while convergence was generally perceived more positively, its advantage was task-dependent. In Generate and Choose tasks, convergence was associated with greater trust, while maintenance was comparably effective in Execute and Negotiate tasks. Participants’ evaluations varied by both task type and age, suggesting that communication strategies should be tailored to context and user characteristics. This study contributes design insights for adaptive, socially responsive domestic robots. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Spatial wildfire risk assessment for Oahu, Hawaii, using swarm-intelligence-optimized CatBoost and the analytic network process
abstract: Wildfires in the Hawaiian Islands are an increasing concern due to climate change and the spread of invasive species. This study thus assessed the wildfire risk on Oahu, Hawaii. Wildfire susceptibility was modeled using the categorical boosting (CatBoost) algorithm. To improve model performance, its hyperparameters were optimized through a comparative analysis of two swarm-intelligence (SI) metaheuristics: the pathfinder algorithm (PFA) and the sparrow search algorithm (SSA). These SI approaches automatically explored the hyperparameter space and maximized the prediction accuracy for the validation set, resulting in two optimized models (PFA-CatBoost and SSA-CatBoost). Socioeconomic vulnerability was then quantified using the analytic network process (ANP), based on eight socioeconomic and demographic indicators that were weighted, fuzzified, and integrated into a composite index. The wildfire susceptibility results showed that the hybrid PFA-CatBoost and SSA-CatBoost models outperformed the baseline CatBoost model, with SSA-CatBoost achieving the best performance, reaching an accuracy of 0.984 on the testing set. The ANP analysis identified annual household income, population density, and education level as the primary socioeconomic indicators associated with wildfire vulnerability. According to the resulting wildfire risk map, 11.7% of Oahu fell within the high or very-high risk categories. The high-risk areas were primarily concentrated in densely populated corridors such as Makaha, Waianae, Maili, Nanakuli, Ewa Gentry, Waipahu, and the Honolulu–Waialae-Kahala corridor. Overall, the proposed framework provides a robust approach to spatial wildfire risk assessment, supporting risk-informed decision-making for wildfire mitigation, land-use planning, and emergency management on Oahu Island. © 2026

title: Integrated assessment of the environmental and social impacts of bauxite mining in the Boké Prefecture
abstract: Since the 2011 mining reforms, Guinea has experienced a rapid increase in bauxite extraction, particularly in the Boké Prefecture. While this growth has significantly stimulated the nation's economy, the aggregated socio-environmental and territorial consequences of bauxite extraction at the local level remain insufficiently documented in peer-reviewed literature, especially through comprehensive, community-level empirical analyses that links spatial transformations to residents’ experiences of displacement. This study argues that existing compensation and governance frameworks do not match the territorial extent of bauxite mining impacts, resulting in ongoing livelihood insecurity even in cases of formal resettlement. The research employs a mixed-methods approach, integrating field surveys, direct observations, interviews, and focus group discussions with 83 participants from four impacted communities. It also incorporates a diachronic analysis of land use and land cover (LULC) derived from Landsat imagery spanning 1973 to 2024. The study follows Cernea’s Impoverishment Risks and Reconstruction framework. Findings indicate a marked increase in mining areas (from 0 to 68 km²) and exposed soils near Sangarédi, accompanied by a substantial decline in vegetation cover (–28%). These spatial changes align with local perceptions of deteriorating air and water quality, farmland loss, and heightened livelihood insecurity, despite observable investments in social infrastructure. In Kanfarandé, the expansion of port infrastructure has precipitated significant territorial changes, even absent direct mining activities. Overall, the research shows that current compensation and governance mechanisms remain inadequate to address the cumulative and indirect impacts of bauxite exploitation, underscoring the need for integrated, participatory, and territorially informed governance frameworks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Fear of missing out, entertainment, and social presence: A stimulus-organism-response model of impulse buying in Chinese live-stream commerce
abstract: This study examines the drivers of impulse buying behavior in China's rapidly expanding live-stream e-commerce environment. Building on a Stimulus-Organism-Response framework, it investigates how key live-stream features — including entertainment value, host interactivity, perceived scarcity of product offers, and social presence — influence consumers’ internal reactions (emotional arousal and fear of missing out) and ultimately their impulse purchase intentions. Survey data were collected from a representative sample of 580 Chinese consumers with recent live-stream shopping experience. Using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA), the results show that entertainment and scarcity stimuli significantly increase arousal and FOMO, both of which in turn are associated with higher impulse purchase intention, while social presence relates directly to impulsive buying. Multi-group analyses indicate significant demographic differences in some pathways. The fsQCA reveals distinct configurations of conditions associated with high impulse purchase intention, highlighting the crucial roles of scarcity cues and community engagement. The findings offer new theoretical insights into digital retailing and practical guidance for designing engaging live-stream shopping experiences that balance consumer excitement with brand objectives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
source_title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services

title: A stock-and-flow perspective on destination brand equity across the PyeongChang Olympic period: Evidence from a two-wave panel
abstract: This study examines how destination brand equity was distributed across the PyeongChang 2018 Olympic period. A matched panel of 502 U.S.-based target-market respondents evaluated South Korea approximately three months before and three months after the Games. The post-event measure intentionally captured evaluations attributed by respondents to hosting the Games and is therefore interpreted as an early event-attributed response rather than a causal Olympic effect. Separate-wave latent profile analyses, supported by focused four-versus-five-state validation, retained five ordered destination-brand-equity states. Average destination brand equity was higher at the post-event observation (mean difference = .340), but this positive net difference coexisted with substantial between-person heterogeneity. A fixed-criterion regression-to-the-mean benchmark reproduced the small residual net direction but not the observed volume of gross bidirectional redistribution, while reliable-change analysis indicated that most respondents did not exceed a conservative change threshold. After baseline adjustment, media consumption and hosting appraisal were positively associated with the post-event score, whereas their interaction was not significant. The findings show why aggregate brand tracking and individual-level diagnostics should be interpreted jointly and distinguish early event-attributed responses from durable mega-event legacy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: When tourism competitiveness becomes human development: The conditioning role of institutional quality in Central and Eastern Europe
abstract: Why do destinations with similar levels of tourism competitiveness experience different human development outcomes? Integrating Sen's Capability Approach with the Tourism Competitiveness Theory Hypothesis, this study examines the institutional conditions under which tourism competitiveness becomes meaningful for human development. Tourism competitiveness is conceptualized as a resource-generating capacity, while institutional quality represents a macro-level condition shaping its conversion into human development. Using annual data for eleven Central and Eastern European countries (2000–2023), we estimate heterogeneous panel autoregressive distributed lag models, error-correction dynamics, and Granger-type causality tests. Results show a positive long-run relationship between tourism competitiveness and human development, with stronger institutional quality associated with larger developmental returns. A trajectory analysis identifies four tourism–development pathways and interprets their differences through institutional quality. The study extends tourism competitiveness theory beyond destination performance by explaining why comparable competitive capacities can generate different human development outcomes across institutional contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Biomass densification-assisted pyrolysis for bio-oil production: structural regulation, product distribution, and fuel-quality trade-offs
abstract: Biomass pyrolysis is a promising route for producing bio-oil and value-added chemicals, but its practical application is limited by the low bulk density, unstable storage and transportation, poor feeding behavior, and structural recalcitrance of lignocellulosic feedstocks. Biomass densification provides an effective strategy to overcome these supply-chain constraints while also functioning as a structure-regulating pretreatment for subsequent pyrolysis. This review summarizes how compression-induced particle rearrangement, lignin softening and redistribution, pore reconstruction, hemicellulose disruption, and cellulose crystallinity variation affect heat transfer, volatile release, product distribution, and bio-oil quality. The synergistic roles of torrefaction, hydrothermal carbonization, steam explosion, biological and chemical pretreatments, and reactive co-densification are further discussed. These coupled strategies can improve feedstock uniformity and alter product distribution and bio-oil characteristics during subsequent pyrolysis. Their performance varies with feedstock properties, treatment intensity, densification conditions, and reactor operation, so the preferred route also depends on the desired product. Route selection must balance gains in liquid yield, bio-oil quality, or phenolic enrichment against the additional energy input and chemical or solvent recovery required by the process. This review highlights densification-assisted pyrolysis as an integrated pathway linking biomass supply, structural regulation, product-oriented conversion, and sustainable system design. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Policy relay in low-carbon transition: A double machine learning analysis of coal power retirement and renewable energy development on economic growth and environmental pollution
abstract: The global energy transition requires policymakers to phase out coal-fired power plants (CPPs) while expanding renewable energy. However, existing studies mainly examine these policies separately and provide limited evidence on their joint economic and environmental effects. This study investigates the interaction between China's CPP retirement policy and the new energy demonstration city (NEDC) policy. Using panel data from 284 prefecture-level cities from 2011 to 2023, we apply double machine learning (DML) to estimate their synergistic effects. The results show that joint implementation reduces NO2 emissions by about 12% and increases economic growth by approximately 6.4%. Government attention to green development and green finance serve as important transmission channels for both pollution reduction and economic growth. The joint policy effects are stronger in eastern regions and in cities with higher levels of industrial upgrading and technological progress. The single-policy analysis shows that the NEDC policy promotes economic growth, whereas CPP retirement reduces economic growth by about 3.1% in the short term. Both policies reduce NO2 emissions by approximately 5.0% and 6.8%, respectively. By integrating satellite-derived pollution data with DML, this study provides causal evidence on how coordinated coal retirement and renewable energy policies can jointly support economic growth and environmental improvement during the energy transition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Upward movement of pedestrian groups on stairways under different urgency levels
abstract: Efficient vertical evacuation through stairways has become a challenge for underground and high-rise buildings. The patterns and behavioral mechanisms of upward movement of pedestrian groups on staircases remains unrevealed, particularly under emergency conditions. In this paper, upward movement characteristics of pedestrians including monads, dyads, triads, and tetrads on a double-turn staircase with a divergent platform are investigated under normal and emergency conditions. A self-organized two-lane pattern is formed during turning, while the stair–platform transition induces rapid configuration reorganization. Dyads increasingly adopt chain configurations near the junction, whereas triads and tetrads shift toward triangle and quadrangle configurations. Moreover, emergency conditions enlarge interpersonal spacing and walking dissimilarity. The splitting probabilities of dyads, triads, and tetrads increase from 23%, 41% and 62% under normal conditions to 50%, 53% and 100% under emergency conditions respectively. Average speed decreases with group size and increases by 0.25–0.38 m/s under emergency conditions. At the individual level, monads generally maintain higher average speed, whereas group members tend to exhibit a larger increase under emergency conditions. These findings clarify the combined effects of stair–platform geometry, group size, and urgency level on group behavior and evacuation dynamics, providing empirical evidence for group evacuation modelling and stairway design. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: International supply chain drivers of forage-livestock conflicts in pastoral China
abstract: China aims to eliminate forage-livestock conflicts (FLCs) in pastoral areas by 2035 to restore degraded grasslands and address related environmental, social, and economic issues. International trade affects grazing-induced FLCs in pastoral China through global economic supply chains. Here, we examine the crucial foreign consumption drivers, international supply chain paths, and global socioeconomic factors influencing FLCs in pastoral China from 2010 to 2020. The results show that foreign consumption caused two million tons of FLCs in pastoral China in 2020. During 2010–2020, foreign consumption contributed 0.1%–10.4% of FLCs in each pastoral province of China. Inner Mongolia, one of the vital ecological barriers against sandstorms in Asia, underwent a significant increase (92.0%) in its FLCs caused by foreign consumption over the decade. The final production sectors in critical international supply chain paths moved from non-pastoral provinces to foreign economies during 2010–2020. In addition, foreign economic structure transitions led to 660 kt of FLC increments during the decade, where foreign production structure transitions contributed 66.8%. Our findings highlight the importance of optimizing foreign production structures and fostering international cooperation to realize China's goal of FLC elimination. © 2026
