title: Spectral energy modeling for weighted graph anomaly detection
abstract: Graph anomaly detection is critical for high-risk applications such as cancer gene identification and telecom fraud detection. However, traditional graph neural networks (GNNs) mainly focus on unweighted topology, while ignoring weight heterogeneity, i.e., differences in the strength of edge connections between nodes. Weight heterogeneity manifests as irregular interaction strengths between genes in biological networks and fraudulent behavior patterns in communication systems, both of which play a key role in graph anomaly detection. This study establishes a fundamental theoretical connection between weight heterogeneity and the spectral energy distribution of graphs. We theoretically show under a stylized random-weight model that weight heterogeneity induces the “flattening out” of spectral energy, in which energy shifts from the middle region and accumulates more prominently at the upper and lower bounds. This phenomenon is empirically validated on both synthetic graphs (Barabasi–Albert and Erdős–Renyi) and real-world datasets, including two protein–protein interaction networks (STRINGdb and CPDB) with cancer genes and two telecom graphs (Tele-Max and Tele-Min) with fraudsters. Motivated by this finding, we propose a Hierarchical-Perspective Graph Neural Network (HIPGNN), a novel framework that integrates spectral and spatial perspectives. HIPGNN not only captures variation in spectral energy distribution to mitigate the “flattening out” phenomenon, but also captures the detailed interaction strengths between nodes from a spatial perspective to address weight heterogeneity. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets show that HIPGNN significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, validating the importance of modeling weight heterogeneity and spectral energy distribution for effective weighted graph anomaly detection. © 2026

title: Exploring the influence of experiential learning on IA practice: Understanding IA professionals' views about the objectives and utility of strategic and regional assessments in subsequent project IAs
abstract: Strategic and regional assessments (SAs/RAs) can inform and influence subsequent impact assessments (IAs) in various ways. In Canada, IA systems that include SA/RA provisions often require their downstream consideration, but leave it to IA professionals to determine how, and to what extent, they should be used in that context. While previous research has investigated perspectives about the goals and utility of SAs/RAs in project IAs, there has been no investigation of the basis for, and origins of, these views. Drawing on experiential learning theory, this study undertook statistical analyses of data from recent surveys of IA regulators and practitioners in Canada to investigate whether different forms of IA experience and knowledge help explain these perspectives. Its findings indicate that amount (years) of IA experience was primarily associated with the view that SAs/RAs should improve project IA efficiency through government scoping decisions. Respondents' self-rated knowledge of SAs/RAs was often associated with perspectives regarding their broader role in improving the quality, effectiveness and efficiency of subsequent project IA scoping and conduct. These findings provide initial evidence that experiential learning can represent one mechanism through which IA professionals develop perspectives on the downstream role of these assessments in practice, while also highlighting that broader SA/RA knowledge may be especially influential in that regard. © 2026 The Authors

title: Motivational Aspects of Teacher Feedback Practices: Development and Validation of a Questionnaire Based on Students’ Perceptions
abstract: This study developed the Motivational Aspects of Teacher Feedback Practices Questionnaire (MATFP-Q), designed to examine students’ perceptions on six key types of teacher feedback—task-focused, specific, self-referenced, normative, next-step, and person-focused—from a motivational perspective. The instrument’s theoretical foundation integrates Hattie and Timperley’s (2007) feedback model with Koenka and Anderman’s (2019) principles for motivation-supportive feedback. Validation was conducted with a sample of 1,079 Chinese secondary school students. Student workshops were conducted to ensure ecological and cognitive validation, and expert reviews were used to establish content validation. Exploratory factor analysis was conducted to identify the underlying factor structure, and confirmatory factor analysis provided evidence for the structural validity of the proposed six-factor model (χ² = 902.49, df = 309, p < .001, CFI = .920, TLI = .909, SRMR = .059, and RMSEA = .042 [90% CI = .039, .045]). The internal consistency of the subscales (Cronbach’s α = .69–.86) ranged from acceptable to excellent. Furthermore, correlations among the MATFP-Q subscales indicated that the instrument captures related but distinguishable aspects of teacher feedback. In addition, the expected pattern of correlations with students’ perceptions of teachers’ goals and mindset belief provided evidence for convergent and divergent validity. The MATFP-Q is a reliable, theory-based tool for examining teacher feedback from a student motivation perspective. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Oxygen recovery in a long channel PEM fuel cell using side injection: Balancing uniformity, power density, and pressure drop
abstract: Increasing the length of proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cell channels attracts a lot of attention due to benefits such as enhanced reactant residence time, increased contact area and mass transfer path, and reduced edge effects. However, increasing the channel length may lead to a non-uniform distribution of the reactant along the flow path, which can result in performance degradation in the downstream regions. To compensate for this defect, the effect of side air injection into the cathode channel on the performance and oxygen concentration uniformity in a long PEM fuel cell is numerically investigated. A parametric study evaluating the impacts of the number and arrangement of injection ports on reactant distribution and overall cell efficiency of PEMFC was conducted and compared with case of without injection to finding the optimal configuration from point of view of power density and performance index. Results demonstrate that side injection effectively compensates for the oxygen concentration decline resulting from increased PEMFC channel length. Depending on the injection port arrangement, the power density enhancement relative to the no-injection case ranges from 27% to 158.96%. The highest power density was achieved with the eight-injection configuration (ports 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9), corresponding to a 158.96% increase. Furthermore, the six‑injection configuration (ports 1, 4, 5, 7, 8, and 9) emerges as the global optimum based on the performance index, which accounts for the trade‑off between hydrodynamic resistance and electrochemical performance, thus maximizing efficiency while avoiding excessive pressure drops. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Large language model-assisted modeling and optimization of high-purity Li2CO3 recovery from LFP recycling streams
abstract: The downstream recovery of high-purity Li2CO3 from Li/K-rich solutions generated in Fe3+-based LFP recycling involves a strong trade-off between product purity (>99.5 %) and lithium recovery (>90 %). In this work, we develop a Large Language Model-Driven Multi-Agent Platform (LLM-MAP) based on GPT to guide the optimization of this method. LLM-MAP decomposes a complex task among role-defined agents and records intermediate outputs as structured summaries, thereby improving constraint retention and consistency during multi-stage, multi-objective process development. Using LLM-MAP, we jointly modeled the key precipitation and purification operations involved in Li2CO3 production via Fe3+ leaching, thereby accounting for the recovery losses that can arise when interdependent operations are optimized separately. Multi-objective optimization strategies implemented through the platform identified operating conditions that simultaneously achieved a product purity of 99.72 % and a recovery efficiency of 93.62 %. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Memory-augmented dual-pathway model for temporal speech emotion recognition
abstract: Speech emotion recognition requires not only identifying salient local emotional cues, but also incorporating broader temporal context to better interpret the overall emotion of an utterance. To address this issue, we propose Dynamic-MEM, a dual-pathway framework that jointly models short-term contextual information and long-term accumulated emotional context. Specifically, the short-term pathway focuses on capturing emotionally informative local patterns and sequential context from speech representations, while the long-term pathway employs a dynamically updated external memory to progressively retain historical emotional information across an utterance. In addition, a multi-scale classification module is introduced to integrate temporal features at different receptive fields and enhance emotion discrimination. By explicitly coordinating immediate emotional evidence with accumulated contextual information, the proposed framework provides a more effective way to model temporally informative cues than conventional sequential encoding alone. Experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of Dynamic-MEM for speech emotion recognition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Integrating human–stream interactions into ecological stream assessment: A novel rural–urban socioecological sustainability framework
abstract: Current assessment tools for streams and rivers focus on ecological functioning while ignoring the social dimension, which varies across rural and urban ecosystems. This study presents the rural–urban socioecological stream sustainability index (hereinafter, RU-SESSI) for assessing stream function across the rural–urban continuum. This index is based on the stream ecosystem services (ES) and biodiversity index (SESBI), which was developed in our previous study to assess stream health. The SESBI was extended into a sustainability subindex by adding two economic indicators, and the framework was complemented by a stream–society interaction subindex comprising accessibility, public safety, and community involvement. Together, these subindices capture stream function through both sustainability performance and human–stream interaction patterns. The framework was refined and validated using the Delphi method, revealing significant differences in the relative importance of most RU-SESSI indicators between rural and urban segments. Applied to the Yarkon Stream in central Israel, the index revealed higher biodiversity and regulating services scores in the rural reach, whereas economic, recreation, and accessibility scores were higher in the urban reach, while public safety and community involvement were comparable between reaches. The urban reach achieved a slightly higher RU-SEES score than the rural reach (6.22 vs. 5.76), with no significant difference in the distribution of weighted indicator scores. The RU-SESSI offers a context-sensitive framework that accounts for unique socioecological dynamics, providing policymakers with valuable insights for tailoring stream management to rural–urban settings and contributing to global water security and sustainability. © 2026 The Author(s)
label: Social Sciences

title: Lexicon-guided representation learning with self-attentive transformer models: Enhancing offensive language detection in low-resourced languages
abstract: Detecting offensive language in online social platforms is essential yet challenging in low-resourced, morphologically rich languages such as Turkish. This study presents an engineering-driven and innovative approach for offensive language detection in Turkish. The proposed method directly injects offensive lexicons collected from local sources by domain experts into transformer self-attention mechanisms. In particular, it leverages lexicon-guided representation learning within Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) variations to enhance attention toward offensive linguistic cues. DistilBERT and XLM-RoBERTa are enhanced with a lexicon mask that reweights attention toward lexicon-matched tokens by a factor of five, while maintaining end-to-end fine-tuning without architectural modifications. Using the OffensEval Turkish dataset (35,284 annotated tweets), the proposed method is evaluated against traditional baselines (MLP, CNN, SVM, LSTM, BiLSTM, and GRU) as well as vanilla transformer models. The proposed Lexicon-Guided XLM-RoBERTa achieves an F1-score of 0.87, while Lexicon-Guided DistilBERT attains 0.85, outperforming vanilla XLM-RoBERTa (0.78), DistilBERT (0.76), and non-transformer baselines (0.66–0.72). Additionally, LIME is employed to provide local and model-agnostic explanations for both offensive and non-offensive predictions, demonstrating that lexicon-guided attention enhances the detection of morphologically complex and implicit offensive cues while reducing false positives in neutral contexts. The proposed method offers practical and multidisciplinary contributions through a lightweight plug-in attention mechanism based on linguistic resources, achieving state-of-the-art performance in Turkish offensive language detection while providing interpretable outputs beneficial for content moderation, human-centered AI, and computational social science. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: Efficient on-site treatment of kitchen waste using a microbial consortium: scale-up validation from laboratory to pilot system and mechanistic insights
abstract: Exogenous microbial inoculation is widely regarded as an effective strategy for enhancing the treatment efficiency of kitchen waste (KW). This study systematically evaluated the performance of a laboratory-prepared composite microbial inoculant (LCI) in KW treatment through a stepwise scale-up strategy. In an 18 L laboratory-scale reactor, LCI achieved efficient liquefaction of KW, with removal efficiencies of 62.7% for COD, 50.7% for TP, 61.5% for TN, and 64.7% for NH4+-N, alongside substantial reduction in weight and volume by 88.3% and 86.5%, respectively. Upon scaling up to a 300 L pilot-scale system with the addition of fruitwood chips (FW) as a reinforcing agent, the LCI-FW configuration maintained stable and high treatment performance. No scale-up attenuation was observed compared with the laboratory-scale results, and the overall performance was superior to that of the commercial microbial inoculant (CI). High-throughput sequencing analysis revealed that LCI-FW significantly enriched dominant microbial taxa represented by Lactobacillus, forming a community structure more conducive to KW degradation. Functional prediction further indicated that, beyond enzymes associated with carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus metabolism, those linked to substrate uptake and environmental adaptation also showed higher predicted abundances, providing mechanistic insights into the enhanced treatment efficiency. Economic assessment demonstrated that LCI-FW achieved a 56.5% cost reduction compared with commercial products, indicating substantial economic advantages. Overall, this study demonstrates the feasibility of the LCI-FW synergistic reinforcement system for practical KW treatment. It also provides experimental evidence supporting the engineering application of microorganism–immobilized carrier strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Gaze aversion and emotional mimicry deficits in individuals with schizophrenia during naturalistic interaction
abstract: Individuals with schizophrenia exhibit a range of verbal and nonverbal impairments during social interaction, which contribute to reduced interaction quality and broader social dysfunction. To optimize clinical interventions, it is essential to identify the mechanisms underlying these deficits. Building on previous findings demonstrating reduced emotional mimicry in schizophrenia, the present study examined whether gaze aversion is associated with instances of failed mimicry during naturalistic conversation. In a within-partner design, interacting partners (n = 20) each engaged in one conversation with an individual with schizophrenia (n = 20) and one with a matched healthy control (n = 20). Prior analyses using OpenFace-based video coding revealed diminished emotional mimicry in the schizophrenia group. In the present study, the same video recordings were reanalyzed using FaceReader to extract gaze direction. We specifically examined gaze aversion during the interaction and, more critically, during episodes of failed mimicry, defined as instances in which participants did not reciprocate their partner's smile. Results indicated that although individuals with schizophrenia did not display significantly greater overall gaze aversion across the entire interaction, they exhibited significantly greater gaze aversion when their partner was smiling. This pattern was associated with a higher proportion of failed mimicry accompanied by gaze aversion in the schizophrenia group compared to controls. These findings suggest that reduced visual attention may represent one mechanism contributing to emotional mimicry deficits in schizophrenia. Clinical implications are discussed, along with the potential role of stigma in exacerbating these processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Efficacy of group-based acceptance and commitment therapy in reducing anxiety and improving mental health among adults recovering from COVID-19: a quasi-experimental interventional study
abstract: Background: Survivors of COVID-19 frequently encounter persistent psychological distress. While Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) aims to enhance psychological flexibility, its clinical utility and underlying mechanisms in post-pandemic recovery within diverse cultural contexts require further empirical investigation. Objective: This study evaluated the efficacy of a group-based ACT intervention in alleviating anxiety and promoting psychological well-being and mental health among COVID-19 survivors in Iran. Methods: This study employed a quasi-experimental interventional design with a pretest–posttest and 6-week follow-up assessment, including a control group. Individuals meeting the preliminary eligibility criteria were screened using the Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) and the General Health Questionnaire-28 (GHQ-28). A total of 40 adults who had recovered from COVID-19 and exhibited clinically significant anxiety and reduced general mental health were enrolled and randomly assigned to either the ACT intervention group (n = 20) or the control group (n = 20). The intervention consisted of eight weekly 90-minute sessions focusing on the core processes of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT). Outcomes were assessed using the BAI and GHQ-28 at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and at a 6-week follow-up. Results: Analysis of the 36 participants who completed the protocol revealed that the ACT group demonstrated significant and sustained reductions in anxiety and somatic symptoms, alongside marked improvements in social functioning and overall mental health compared to the control group (p < 0.001). These gains were maintained at the 6-week follow-up. High intervention fidelity (90%) and attendance (87%) suggest the feasibility and acceptability of this approach in a post-viral clinical context. Conclusions: Group-based ACT is an efficacious and feasible intervention for addressing the long-term psychological sequelae of COVID-19. The findings support the integration of ACT into rehabilitation programs to enhance resilience and quality of life in survivors. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive

title: Characterizing Core Morphology and Scar Patterning Within a Unified Spherical Harmonic Framework
abstract: Lithic cores preserve the most direct evidence of past reduction strategies, yet their analysis still relies largely on typological classifications that are subjective and difficult to reproduce. Recent 3D methods quantify core attributes more precisely, but morphology and scar organization are handled in separate mathematical frameworks, precluding joint analysis of how the two relate. Here we present a unified framework based on spherical harmonics that encodes both core morphology (M-SPHARM) and scar patterning (SP-SPHARM) within a single rotation-invariant, landmark-free space, the latter being the first application of spherical harmonics to scar orientation data. Co-inertia analysis examines their covariation, and harmonic reconstruction renders statistical axes back into interpretable three-dimensional forms. While the methods are complementary, validation on ideal models and experimental cores shows that the scar pattern descriptor resolves finer distinctions among core types than existing metrics, most clearly the radial subtypes others cannot separate. The exploratory analysis on experimental and archaeological assemblages reveals no detectable covariation between morphology and scar organization. We identify core type as the principal factor structuring variation at Sandinggai (Hunan, China). The methods are released as an open-source R package (spharmlithic) with a fully reproducible workflow. More broadly, the framework supports understanding core variability as a continuous techno-morphological space rather than a set of discrete types. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Feasibility of an internet-based cognitive behavioral treatment for university students with depression and/or anxiety: A mixed-methods single arm repeated measures study
abstract: Mental health problems are prevalent among university students, with anxiety and depression being the most common conditions. Despite available campus services, barriers to access persist, creating a substantial treatment gap. Internet-based cognitive behavioral therapy (iCBT) offers a scalable alternative, although evidence in university settings remains limited.This study assessed the feasibility and preliminary effects of VIVIM, an adapted iCBT program delivered through interactive eBooks for Spanish- and Catalan-speaking university students with anxiety and/or depression. It also evaluated the feasibility of conducting a future randomized controlled trial (RCT).Feasibility was evaluated through recruitment, retention, adherence, engagement, and acceptability. Thirty-three students from Rovira i Virgili University accessed the intervention over eight weeks.Recruitment targets were achieved within the planned timeframe, whereas retention was limited, with 45.45% and 39.39% of participants completing post-treatment and follow-up assessments, respectively. Adherence was low: only 12.12% of participants accessed all six predefined core eBooks, and 6.1% remained engaged throughout the intervention period. Nevertheless, participants who completed post-treatment assessments reported moderate-to-high levels of engagement and satisfaction.Completers and intention-to-treat sensitivity analyses showed significant improvements in depression and anxiety, although the uncontrolled single-arm design does not permit attribution of these changes to the intervention. Exploratory analyses suggested a possible association between greater eBooks use and larger symptom improvements, although findings were based on small subgroups and partly LOCF −imputed data.The findings suggest that both the intervention and study procedures require further optimization before progression to a full-scale RCT, despite encouraging preliminary evidence of improved mental health outcomes. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Masson SAS on behalf of Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive.

title: What motivates landowners to use prescribed fire in a wildfire prone landscape? Evidence from California, USA
abstract: The use of prescribed fires on private lands is important to achieving landscape and community resilience goals, yet private landowner adoption remains low. This study examines the factors shaping non-industrial private forest and rangeland owner intentions to use prescribed fire in California. Using the Theory of Planned Behavior framework and Likert scale questions, we administered a survey to 4000 landowners, yielding 509 usable responses. We used multinomial logistic regression to model adoption intention (yes, maybe, and no) and binary logistic regression to examine preferred implementation approaches among landowners open to burning. Results indicate that 27% of respondents were willing to burn, 42% remained uncertain, and 31% were unwilling. Social norms were the strongest predictor of adoption intention. Past wildfire exposure, perceived wildfire risk, landholding size, perceived benefits of prescribed fire, and attitudes toward cultural burning positively impact adoption likelihood. Capacity to conduct burns strongly differentiated the willing adopters from uncertain ones, while prohibitive cost was the most consistent barrier across groups. Among landowners open to burning, community cooperative burning was the most preferred implementation approach, followed by agency-assisted burning, with preferences shaped by trust, liability concerns, and landholding size. Findings suggest that in California, making prescribed fire more visible may matter as much as making it feasible. Effective outreach should prioritize peer-based demonstration strategies, reduce cost and liability barriers, and build local burning capacity to bridge the gap between interest and action. Policy interventions supporting community burn networks and technical assistance could accelerate prescribed fire adoption on private lands. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Modelling Local Strontium Isotope Baselines from Human Isotopic Data Using Machine Learning: Implications for Past Mobility Studies
abstract: Estimating bioavailable strontium isotope baselines is a critical step in archaeological mobility studies. Conventional proxy-based approaches, which rely on environmental samples, such as soils, fauna, plants, or waters, are not always feasible and may be affected by environmental, taphonomic, or sampling-related biases. Here, we introduce MobSr, a machine-learning-based model designed to estimate probable local 87Sr/86Sr baselines directly from human enamel isotope data. The model combines four first-layer classifiers—Naïve Bayes, k-nearest neighbours, support vector machine, and Random Forest—with a Bayesian ensemble layer that integrates classifier outputs and refines local/non-local probability estimates. MobSr was trained on a dataset of approximately 3000 human enamel samples from 86 archaeological sites, using published expert-derived local/non-local classifications. Local isotopic ranges are estimated by analysing posterior probabilities assigned to individual observations. Model performance was evaluated through general cross-validation and through site-specific case studies, including a La Tène period cemetery from the Czech Republic, an Early Medieval cemetery from Finland, and multi-period burial assemblages from Bahrain in the Arabian Peninsula. The results show 87–95% agreement with published local/non-local classifications, depending on the evaluation strategy and treatment of atypical cases. These values quantify concordance with the source-study labels. These findings demonstrate that MobSr can replicate and refine local baseline estimates without requiring additional environmental sampling. The model offers an efficient tool for preliminary mobility assessment and provides a complementary strategy to traditional baseline construction in bioarchaeological research. In addition, the use of a large training dataset enables broader exploration of expert-derived locality assignments across predominantly sedentary populations from different regions and periods. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Factors associated with installed photovoltaic capacity in Australia across small, medium, and large-scale systems
abstract: Australia, as a global leader in photovoltaic deployment, has attracted significant research attention, has attracted significant research attention into factors associated with PV installation patterns. Previous studies have highlighted the role of early adopters, family wealth, and education, and have identified financial parameters (such as investment cost, internal rate of return, and net present value), social parameters (including household income and demographics), and environmental factors as relevant correlates of PV adoption. However, how these correlations vary across different system sizes, small, medium, and large, has not been systematically examined using historical data. In this study, historical time-series data on installed PV capacity in Australia, categorized by system-size groups across five states from 2013/14 to 2024/25 are collected, and the correlation of 4 groups of economic, market, financial, and affordability variables with PV installed patterns is examined. The results indicate that different system-size categories exhibit distinct association patterns. Small-scale adoption shows higher correlations with electricity prices and unit costs, medium-scale systems are more correlated with income and affordability indicators, and large-scale systems are more correlated with long-term financial returns and market incentives. The main contribution of this study is a systematic comparison of association patterns across PV system-size categories, highlighting how selected parameters are differently correlated with Installed PV capacity across system sizes and states. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: The influential first offer: How to advance a negotiation classic by integrating features, mechanisms, and outcomes
abstract: Six decades of research and hundreds of effects have identified robust first-offer advantages and disadvantages. Too assertive an offer can alienate the opposing negotiator, elevate the impasse risk, as well as impair the relationship and outcome satisfaction. In contrast, first offers can also beneficially anchor negotiation outcomes in the first mover's favor. This advantage is particularly strong when first movers effectively apply the first offer's moderating features precision, framing, ranges, and rationales. Despite more than six decades of research, existing studies on first-offer effects tend to isolate specific mechanisms or outcomes, thereby capturing a comparably narrow slice of the underlying complexity. We argue that future research can (and should) advance this field by further integrating first-offer features, psychological mechanisms, and separate measures of negotiation outcomes. © 2026 The Authors

title: Water footprint of low-tech digesters for bioenergy recovery from waste
abstract: This study aimed to assess the water footprint of plastic tubular digesters to treat organic waste and recover bioenergy. Different scenarios in a small-scale dairy farm in Colombia were considered: i) scenario without the digester in which cow manure is piled up, and dairy wastewater is directly discharged into the environment, ii) scenario with a plastic tubular digester treating cow manure, and iii) scenario with a plastic tubular digester co-digesting cow manure with dairy wastewater. The ReCiPe 2016 – midpoint (H) method was used to assess the degradation of water bodies (i.e. eutrophication and ecotoxicity impact categories), while the AWARE 2.0 method was applied to evaluate the water scarcity impact category. Results showed that, in terms of water quality degradation, the co-digestion scenario exhibited impacts 10% to 45% lower than those of the other scenarios, depending on the impact category. In terms of water scarcity, the co-digestion scenario exhibited approximately 10% lower water scarcity than the other scenarios, which showed a similar water scarcity footprint. This indicates that implementing plastic tubular digesters, even under mono-digestion conditions, does not worsen water availability. These benefits are greater if co-digestion of different agri-food waste is applied, since it helps preserve water quality by valorising the intrinsic water content of food wastewater. It also decreases environmental impacts by reducing synthetic fertiliser use through the production of a higher-quality digestate. Overall, plastic tubular digesters provide a low-water footprint alternative to the direct discharge and uncontrolled storage of livestock waste and food-production wastewater in small-scale farms. © 2026 The Authors

title: Psychological perspectives on acting, redux
abstract: Acting is everywhere - film, television, theatre, and everyday performances such as work presentations, leisure activities, and pretend play with children. Yet psychology has historically paid very little attention to what skills, physiological states, and psychological mindsets are needed to act, as noted in Goldstein, 2009. Happily, over the last two decades multiple studies on the major psychological components of acting have produced exciting discoveries, and new questions have arisen. For such a commonly watched activity that involves all the components of human behavior and emotion, it remains strange that acting as an empirical area of study continues to be underdeveloped. Nonetheless, the field is now ripe for nuanced work and interdisciplinary questions from multiple perspectives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: 'In Every River, in Every Lake': Impacts of Beaver Population Change on Indigenous Livelihoods and Wellbeing in the Inuvialuit Settlement Region, Western Canadian Arctic
abstract: Ecosystem transformation driven by climatic, environmental and societal factors poses interlinked ecological and social challenges for many Indigenous communities. For Inuvialuit communities in and around the lower Mackenzie Delta, in the western Canadian Arctic, recent changes in the population of beavers (Castor canadensis) have disrupted subsistence harvesting activities and travelling routes, exacerbating stresses linked to the cost of living and increasing the exposure of active harvesters to risk. Drawing on interviews with 25 Inuvialuit knowledge holders from the three communities of Inuvik, Tuktoyaktuk, and Aklavik, we investigated concerns around beaver population change in the western Arctic and the impact of this change on Inuvialuit livelihoods and wellbeing. Beyond the direct impact of beavers, the issues associated with ecosystem transformation pose challenges for Inuvialuit collective identity, the continuity of knowledge and connections to the land. While beaver population change was widely attributed to the local effects of a warming climate, participants also pointed to the effects of social transformations over recent decades. Ecological changes interact with social factors to produce complex and wide-ranging consequences for Indigenous communities. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Aesthetic experience: Foundations, tensions, and new directions
abstract: Neuroaesthetics is a young subdiscipline of cognitive neuroscience that investigates the psychological and biological bases of diverse aesthetic experiences. Emerging from the iterative interaction of perceptual, affective, and cognitive processes, aesthetic experiences are complex, dynamic, subjective states with considerable individual variability. Three decades of behavioral and neuroimaging investigation supports varied and robust theoretical accounts, with key points of debate including whether aesthetic experience constitutes a distinct psychological and neural phenomena or is sufficiently explained in entirely domain general terms. Foundational research conducted in lab settings has established general principles of experience, especially with respect to the engagements with visual art and architecture. Studies with culturally diverse stimuli and populations, and in ecologically valid contexts are growing, and important for testing the generalizability of such patterns. Moving beyond beauty and pleasure, characterizing the diverse and nuanced emotional dimensions of aesthetic experience is a major area of development. Promising applied approaches in neuroaesthetics include the health and wellbeing impact of aesthetic experiences, and how people respond aesthetically to nature and the built environment. Research in these areas has the potential to inform policy and practice in healthcare, architectural design, and urban planning. Contemplative neuroaesthetics has emerged as a new subdiscipline, expanding the interdisciplinary nature of the field. Immersive aesthetic experiences that encourage receptive, non-evaluative attention can expand our understanding of the transformative potentials of aesthetic engagement. © 2026

title: Numerical investigation of interfacial stability and crack-induced cohesive degradation in Cr-coated zircaloy-4 cladding under LOCA conditions
abstract: The interfacial integrity of chromium (Cr)-coated Zircaloy-4 (Zry-4) cladding under Loss-of-Coolant Accident (LOCA) conditions is critical to maintaining its protective function. A coupled thermo-mechanical and cohesive-zone framework was developed within MOOSE to investigate substrate burst behavior and coating–substrate interfacial degradation. The baseline model was benchmarked against a selected uncoated Zry-4 Severe Accident Test Station (SATS) experiment, reproducing the burst time of approximately 437 s. Cohesive zone modeling (CZM) was subsequently introduced together with prescribed through-thickness transverse coating cracks. The continuous coating remained interfacially stable before substrate burst, whereas a baseline crack with a 1 μm initial opening width generated highly localized mixed-mode loading, with tangential and tensile-normal tractions of approximately 97 and 49 MPa, respectively, and a maximum cohesive damage of approximately 0.55 without complete separation. Parametric analyses showed that the crack-induced response was substantially more sensitive to interfacial strength than to the critical energy release rate, while varying the initial crack opening from 1 to 20 μm produced only minor changes in the local response. Increasing crack number did not proportionally increase the maximum damage, and the average damaged-interface length per crack decreased with increasing segmentation. Increasing the Cr coating thickness from 5 to 20 μm delayed the predicted substrate burst from 439.6 to 444.8 s but increased the maximum cohesive damage from approximately 0.41 to 0.84. These results identify coating cracks as local sources of interfacial degradation and reveal a trade-off between improved burst resistance and increased demand on interfacial integrity. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: LMC-DETR: A lightweight detection model for foreign object detection on power lines
abstract: To address the dual requirements of model lightweighting and detection accuracy in foreign object detection for drone-based power-line inspection, this paper proposes a lightweight multi-scale context-aware detection model, termed LMC-DETR. Specifically, a Context-aware Global Block (CGB) is introduced into the backbone network, which integrates multi-scale receptive field fusion with global context recalibration, thereby achieving significant reduction in parameters while enhancing feature extraction capabilities. In the neck network, a Multi-scale Context Fusion Framework (MCFF) is designed to construct an intelligent feature pyramid, wherein two cooperative submodules, Fusion-U and Fusion-D, collaborate. Attention-guided upsampling and downsampling mechanisms are employed to substantially improve the quality of multi-scale feature fusion. Furthermore, a Squeeze-and-Excitation Channel (SEC) module incorporates a lightweight Efficient Squeeze-and-Excitation (ESE) attention mechanism for adaptive channel-wise feature recalibration, effectively suppressing background noise while accentuating critical feature representations. Experimental evaluations on a public power line foreign object dataset demonstrate that the proposed LMC-DETR achieves a detection accuracy of 85.0% APIOU=50. Compared to the baseline, LMC-DETR reduces the number of parameters (15.1M) and computational cost (44.1 GFLOPs) by 23.7% and 22.5%, respectively, striking a favorable trade-off between accuracy and efficiency. Consequently, the model shows promise for real-time drone inspection scenarios, pending further validation on edge hardware. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Examining the Prevalence and Impact of Sleep Disorders among Dental Interns, Postgraduates and Dental Staff
abstract: Objective: To assess the prevalence of sleep disorders among dentists in private and public tertiary care hospitals in Peshawar, Pakistan. Materials and Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted in four major hospitals, including two private and two government institutions. Dentists, including dental interns, postgraduates, and staff, participated in the study. Data were collected using the Epworth Daytime Sleepiness Scale (ESS) and analyzed in SPSS. This study used descriptive statistics, t-tests, multivariate regression, and chi-square tests to examine associations between sleep disorders and sociodemographic factors. Results: Among the 570 participants, the mean age was 27.67 ± 2.67 years. The prevalence of sleep disorders was 65%, with a mean ESS score of 11.80 ± 3.64. Dental postgraduates exhibited the highest levels of moderate to severe sleep disorders. No significant association was found between sleep disorders and gender or workplace. However, job designation was significantly associated with sleep disturbances (p = 0.007). Work output and efficacy, personal changes, workplace environment, and gender were significant predictors of sleep disorders. Conclusion: Addressing sleep disorders among dentists requires comprehensive strategies, including organizational changes, stress management support, and workload reduction. Future research should explore interventions to enhance sleep quality and assess the long-term impacts on dentists' well-being and patient care outcomes. © 2027, Association of Support to Oral Health Research (APESB). .

title: Client selection of multi-criteria and adaptive deadline in federated learning
abstract: Edge computing-enabled federated learning (FL) is pivotal for privacy-preserving data-intensive applications, but data and system heterogeneity severely degrade global model performance, slow convergence, and induce fairness issues. Existing single-criterion client selection methods fail to handle strong data heterogeneity, while static timing controls exacerbate the dropout effect in heterogeneous environments. To address these critical challenges, we propose FedMA, a novel FL framework integrating Multi-Criteria Client Selection (MCCS) and Adaptive Deadline Determination (ADD). MCCS synthesizes three key metrics—data volume, data distribution (measured via Earth Mover’s Distance, EMD), and participation frequency—to ensure data quality and selection fairness, avoiding high-resource client dominance. ADD dynamically adjusts round deadlines using Deadline Efficiency (DDLE) and Round Utility, adapting to device computing/communication capabilities and training progress. Extensive experiments on FEMNIST, CIFAR-10, and GoogleSpeech datasets demonstrate FedMA’s effectiveness. On FEMNIST, FedMA attains the highest accuracy among all compared methods (81.45%); on CIFAR-10 (70.95%) and GoogleSpeech (71.51%) its accuracy is on par with the strongest baseline (Oort). Crucially, FedMA reduces end-to-end latency by 28.02%–85.67% compared to state-of-the-art methods, yielding a superior trade-off between accuracy and training efficiency without compromising fairness. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: What are we measuring when we measure attractiveness?
abstract: Facial attractiveness ratings are widely used as indicators of mate value and sexual preference in evolutionary aesthetics. Yet recent large-scale evidence reveals a robust Gender Attractiveness Gap (GAP): female faces are rated as more attractive than male faces across cultures, sexual orientations, age groups, and methodological contexts. This structural asymmetry has remained largely invisible despite being embedded in facial-attractiveness datasets for decades. It challenges the assumption that explicit attractiveness ratings map straightforwardly onto sexual desire. Rather, the GAP suggests that attractiveness judgments are outputs of a broader evaluative system in which female appearance occupies a privileged position. This article discusses the conceptual and methodological implications of this finding for measurement, theory construction, and future research on human aesthetic cognition. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Modeling the Relationship Between Physical Activity, Mental Health, and Cognitive Abilities with the Mediating Role of Perceived Social Support in Older Adults
abstract: Objectives: Aging is one of the most significant demographic phenomena of the twenty-first century, and identifying factors affecting the physical and mental health of older adults is crucial. This study aimed to examine the relationship between physical activity, mental health, and cognitive abilities with the mediating role of perceived social support in older adults. Materials and Methods: This correlational descriptive study with path analysis was conducted among older adults aged 60 years and above (Mean = 67.63, SD = 6.02) in Sanandaj, Iran, in 2024. Using a convenience sampling method, 280 participants were recruited. Data were collected using the Physical Activity Questionnaire, the Quality of Life Questionnaire (mental health domain), the Cognitive Abilities Questionnaire, and the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support. Data analysis was performed using SPSS-24 and AMOS-24. Results: Path analysis indicated that physical activity (Mean = 10.32, SD = 5.26) had significant direct effects on perceived social support (Mean = 40.87, SD = 11.33; β = 0.378, P < 0.001), cognitive abilities (Mean = 69.09, SD = 15.34; β = 0.351, P < 0.001), and mental health (Mean = 18.86, SD = 5.53; β = 0.189, P = 0.002). Cognitive abilities and mental health also had significant direct effects on perceived social support. Mediation analysis confirmed the significant mediating role of perceived social support in the relationships of cognitive abilities (β range = 0.061-0.453, 95% CI range [0.022- 0.573], P < 0.001) and mental health (β range = 0.054-0.153, 95% CI range [0.010-0.224], P < 0.001) with physical activity. Conclusions: These findings confirm that strengthening perceived social support can serve as a key mediating pathway that enhances the impact of mental health and cognitive abilities on physical activity among older adults. Perceived social support plays an important mediating role in amplifying the effects of physical activity on mental health and cognitive functioning in this population. Accordingly, health-promotion programs and public health policies should simultaneously focus on fostering supportive social interactions and encouraging regular physical activity in order to improve the psychological well-being and cognitive performance of older adults. © (2027), (Negah Institute for Social Research and Scientific Communication). title: Residency-Aware Rewriting for self-referenced chunks in deduplicated backup systems
abstract: Data deduplication is a highly effective redundancy-elimination technique that operates at the chunk level by replacing duplicate chunks with references to their previously stored copies. In backup systems, only unique chunks are physically stored and packed into fixed-size containers, each holding hundreds or thousands of chunks. Despite its storage efficiency, deduplication introduces chunk fragmentation, which significantly degrades restore performance. Rewriting techniques mitigate this problem by avoiding references to sparse containers, i.e., containers with few useful references. Among them, History-Aware Rewriting (HAR) achieves a favorable trade-off by exploiting the temporal stability of sparse containers across backup versions. However, HAR identifies sparse containers over the entire backup stream and overlooks the impact of self-referenced chunks, i.e., duplicate chunks within the same backup, which can cause restore-cache thrashing. This results in some containers being loaded multiple times during restoration, each time with varying useful ratios, making them appear sparse during some loads and non-sparse during others, a complexity HAR fails to address. We observe that, in the presence of self-referenced chunks, sparse containers must be identified within the scope of the restore cache to achieve accurate classification. We further observe strong temporal stability: for containers that are loaded multiple times during restoration due to cache thrashing, the numbers of times they are classified as sparse or non-sparse remain highly consistent across consecutive backups. Based on these insights, we propose Residency-Aware Rewriting (RAR), a novel rewriting framework that explicitly accounts for the impact of self-referenced chunks on restore performance. RAR emulates restore-time cache dynamics during backup ingestion and identifies sparse containers within the restore-cache scope. For containers that may be loaded multiple times during restoration, RAR tracks, for each container, the number of times it was classified as sparse and non-sparse in the previous backup and uses this information to determine its final classification. Experimental results show that RAR improves restore performance by up to 2.39× compared with existing rewriting schemes including HAR, while incurring only modest redundancy-elimination loss and maintaining comparable backup throughput. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Explaining Strategies to Reduce the Occurrence of Medication Errors at Older Adults with Polypharmacy
abstract: Objective: Age-related changes make the older susceptible to multiple chronic diseases and, consequently, an increase in the number of medications consumed. The present study aimed toexplain strategies to reduce the incidence of medication errors at illiterate and low-literate older adults with polypharmacy from the perspectives of the older, caregivers, and pharmacists. Method: The present study is a qualitative study that was conducted with 23 semi-structured interviews with three different groups of participants including illiterate and low-literate older adults with polypharmacy, caregivers of the older (informal caregivers of the older such as family members), and pharmacists from August 2022 to Murch 2024 in Tabriz, Iran. Participants were selected using purposive sampling method and interviews were conducted based on a designed interview guide. Conventional content analysis method was used to analyze the data. Findings: The inductive content analysis process extracted 6 main categories from 32 subcategories. The average age of the older participants in the study was 67.53 years. From the perspective of the study participants, strengthening self-care and health-oriented behaviors and beliefs, using techniques to optimize medication management, caregiver responsibility and support, effective education, effective interaction between the older and the physician-pharmacist, and an efficient healthcare system can be effective in reducing the incidence of medication errors in the older. Conclusion:Due to the multifactorial nature of medication errors, it is not the sole responsibility of health professionals to contribute to the reduction of medication errors, and integrated actions must be taken by health care providers, the pharmaceutical industry, insurers, educational providers, legislators, caregivers, and ultimately the elderly themselves. © (2027), (Negah Institute for Scientific Communication), .

title: Correlations between cerebrospinal fluid and plasma levels of GABA, glutamate, dopamine, and related metabolites, and their concentrations across neurological disorders
abstract: Background Neurotransmitters play critical roles in both central and peripheral nervous system function. However, the correlation between cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and plasma levels of neurotransmitters remains incompletely understood, limiting the interpretation of peripheral measurements as surrogates for central neurochemical changes. This study aimed to investigate the correlations between CSF and plasma levels of GABA, glutamate, dopamine, and related metabolites, and to explore their expressions across common neurological disorders in a real-world clinical setting. Methods A total of 181 paired CSF and plasma samples from patients with neurological disorders and 67 plasma samples from healthy controls were analyzed. Concentrations of GABA, betaine, L-DOPA, histamine, glutamine, glutamate, dopamine, and choline were quantified using LC–MS/MS. Correlations between CSF and plasma concentrations were assessed using Pearson correlation analysis. Age- and sex-related effects were evaluated in healthy controls, and differences among disease groups were analyzed after classifying patients into neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs), CNS demyelinating diseases (CNS DDs), CNS tumors, and CNS infections. Results GABA, histamine, betaine, glutamate, and choline exhibited higher concentrations in plasma than in CSF, whereas glutamine concentrations were higher in CSF. Except for betaine and glutamate, all other neurotransmitters showed statistically significant but weak CSF–plasma correlations ( r = 0.15–0.7, p < 0.05). In healthy controls, plasma histamine, betaine, glutamate, and choline levels were higher in males. Plasma GABA levels in all disease groups were consistently lower than controls, and plasma glutamine levels in NDDs, CNS DDs, and CNS tumors were significantly higher than those in controls. By contrast, there were no significant differences in CSF levels among different disease groups, except that glutamate was higher in the CNS tumor group than in the other disease groups. Conclusions Most plasma neurotransmitters and their metabolites do not reliably reflect their CSF levels, which may provide important context for interpreting peripheral neurotransmitter biomarkers in CNS diseases. title: Wuwei Huanglian Wan inhibits Helicobacter pylori and alleviates associated gastritis: host metabolic remodeling and altered IL-6/STAT3 signaling
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Wuwei Huanglian Wan (WWHLW) is a traditional Tibetan medicine formula developed by Tibetan physician Takpe Pingcuo and officially documented in the Ministry of Health Drug Standards for Tibetan Medicines (Volume I, 1995). It has long been used for the treatment of gastrointestinal disorders, particularly conditions associated with gastrointestinal discomfort and inflammation. Given the overlap between its traditional indications and the clinical manifestations of H. pylori-associated gastritis (HAG), WWHLW represents a promising candidate for the management of H. pylori infection and related gastric inflammation. In addition, several constituent herbs of WWHLW have demonstrated anti-H. pylori and anti-inflammatory activities, providing a pharmacological basis for further investigating its therapeutic effects. Aim of the study: This study aimed to systematically evaluate the therapeutic effects of WWHLW against H. pylori infection and HAG, and to explore the biological processes associated with these effects through integrated multi-omics and experimental validation. Materials and methods: The therapeutic effects of WWHLW were evaluated through in vitro antibacterial assays and an H. pylori-infected mouse model. UHPLC-HRMS/MS was employed for chemical profiling and identification of serum-absorbed constituents. Serum metabolomics, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, network pharmacology analysis, molecular docking analysis, and molecular biological analyses were integrated to investigate the metabolic, microbial, and signaling changes associated with its therapeutic activity. Results: WWHLW exhibited anti-H. pylori activity, with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of 0.2-0.5 mg/mL against both standard strains and multidrug-resistant clinical isolates. At MIC concentrations, WWHLW treatment altered the expression of multiple virulence-associated genes and reduced gastric H. pylori colonization by 93.8% in infected mice. UHPLC-HRMS/MS analysis putatively annotated 121 compounds in the WWHLW extracts, of which 10 prototype constituents were detected in serum after oral administration. Integrated metabolomics and network pharmacology analyses revealed alterations in lipid and amino acid-related metabolic pathways following WWHLW treatment. Gut microbiota analysis showed that WWHLW was associated with less pronounced alterations in microbial diversity and composition than antibiotic treatment. Correlation analysis further revealed statistical associations between microbial taxa and lipid and amino acid-related features. Experimental validation showed that WWHLW reduced inflammatory cytokine expression and suppressed STAT3 phosphorylation, consistent with altered IL-6/STAT3-related molecular changes. Conclusions: WWHLW exhibits therapeutic potential against H. pylori infection and HAG through combined antibacterial, anti-inflammatory and metabolic regulatory effects. The protective activity of WWHLW was associated with reduced IL-6/STAT3 signaling, providing pharmacological evidence supporting its traditional use in gastrointestinal disorders. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: A hybrid deterministic-stochastic method for extreme sea level prediction incorporating tide-surge interaction
abstract: Extreme sea levels driven by storm surges and high tides can have devastating impacts on coastal communities. Reliable prediction of these extremes is challenging due to site-specific nonlinear interactions between tide and surge, in addition to other complexities. Existing methods have drawbacks; for example block maxima suffers from data wastage, peaks-over-threshold introduces practitioner subjectivity, while joint probability methods rely on assumptions that are not always valid. To address these gaps, this paper develops a broadly applicable method for predicting extreme sea levels based on the crossing rate approach, by treating tide as deterministic and modeling surge as a tide-dependent stochastic process. The formulation makes minimal assumptions and rigorously models the salient problem characteristics including tide-surge interaction, non-Gaussian behavior, serial correlation and seasonality. Moreover, the method fully exploits the information embedded in the entire time series record, not only the peaks or maxima. The proposed method is demonstrated at three tide-gauge sites: Tanjong Pagar, San Franciso and Quarry Bay. The predicted upcrossing rates are in excellent agreement with observations. Cross-validation analysis by data splitting reveals that the proposed method is accurate for out-of-sample forecasting, with small predictive uncertainty and good statistical extrapolation. Overall, the proposed method is shown to be a powerful practical tool for reliable prediction of extreme sea levels. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Social consequences of emotional expressions in negotiation
abstract: Negotiation is integral to social life. Whether we focus on exchanges between individuals, groups, organizations, or nations, negotiation is the most common and constructive way of making deals and solving disputes. Negotiations can spark intense emotions, which in turn shape negotiation processes and outcomes. Here, we review research on the social consequences of emotional expressions in negotiation. We summarize evidence regarding specific single emotions (e.g., anger, happiness, disappointment, sadness, fear, guilt, shame, pride, hope) as well as alternative (patterns of) emotional responses (e.g., empathy, emotional ambivalence, mixed emotions, alternating emotions, indifference) across levels of analysis (interpersonal, intragroup, intergroup). Our review indicates that emotions can have both favorable and unfavorable consequences, depending on critical moderators (e.g., information processing, perceived appropriateness) and the focal criterion (e.g., monetary gains, social outcomes). The richness of the empirical record underlines the importance of investigating discrete emotions (rather than positive vs. negative affect) and defies simple conclusions about the (dys)functionality of emotions. Emotional expressions can help or hurt negotiators’ outcomes depending on goal prioritization (e.g., maximizing individual outcomes vs. maintaining positive relations) and the social context. We call for research outside the lab to gain insight into real-world consequences of emotional dynamics in (intergroup) negotiation, mediation, and diplomacy. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Modelling, intelligent optimisation and techno-economic analysis of post-combustion carbon capture for ethylene production under variable loads
abstract: Thermal cracking furnaces in ethylene plants are the dominant source of CO2 emissions in the petrochemical industry, making the integration of carbon capture plants critical for decarbonization. However, the coupling behaviours between the thermal cracking furnace and the capture plants, particularly under different operating conditions, pose significant challenges to system optimization. To address this, this study proposes a comprehensive integrated simulation and intelligent optimization framework for a 60 kt/yr industrial thermal cracking furnace coupled with a Monoethanolamine (MEA)-based carbon capture process. Firstly, a high-fidelity coupled thermal cracking furnace model (based on Zone Method and COILSIM1D) is established to accurately predict flue gas characteristics under varying fuel gas flowrates. Secondly, a rate-based post-combustion carbon capture plant model is developed in Aspen Plus®, validated against pilot scale experimental data from the Technology Centre Mongstad (TCM), and scaled up to match the flue gas from the industrial scale thermal cracking furnace. Genetic Algorithm (GA) is implemented in MATLAB to interact with process simulations, enabling the global optimization of energy consumption and carbon capture costs. Optimization results reveal a previously unidentified divergence between technical and economic performance: the lowest specific reboiler duty occurs at 82–84% capture level, whereas the lowest cost consistently lies at 86–90%. We demonstrate quantitatively that this 4–6 percentage point gap arises from the trade-off between the change of capital cost caused by economies of scale and the exponential rise in regeneration energy, which is established for the first time for low carbon ethylene plants—— the optimal capture level shifts towards higher values as fuel gas flowrate decreases. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Political Ideology Shifts in Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in politically sensitive contexts, raising concerns about their susceptibility to ideological biases. In this work, we examine how synthetic persona conditioning shapes ideological expression across seven open-weight instruction-tuned models (7B–72B parameters) using the Political Compass Test (62 statements) as a standardized behavioral probe. Across three studies involving 200,000 synthetic personas and more than 260 million model responses, we analyze implicit and explicit malleability, as well as theme-associated variation. We find that: (i) larger models exhibit broader implicit ideological coverage, increasing from 14%–35% for 7–8B models to up to 49% for 70B+ models; (ii) explicit ideological priming induces large and statistically significant shifts, with right-authoritarian cues moving all models in the intended direction and generally producing larger shifts than left-libertarian cues across model-axis comparisons; (iii) left-libertarian priming produces more heterogeneous responses, with counter-directional economic shifts in three of four 7–8B models and intended-direction shifts across all 70B+ models; and (iv) theme-associated semantic content in persona descriptions is linked to systematic and interpretable directional shifts in ideological space. While our results identify an upstream mechanism through which persona conditioning can alter model responses under a standardized ideological probe, we do not test whether such shifts affect users’ beliefs, decisions, or political behavior. Our findings are best understood as evidence of ideological malleability at the generation layer, highlighting the need to account for interactional factors when evaluating political neutrality, fairness, and safety in English-prompted, persona-conditioned language models. © 2026 The Authors. title: Power quality performance assessment of stand-alone minigrids in Kenya
abstract: Global rural electrification initiatives have accelerated the deployment of renewable energy-based minigrids. However, their performance is highly susceptible to weather dynamics, which adversely affect power quality and service delivery. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of power quality in autonomous minigrids. The assessment was conducted on eleven autonomous minigrids in remote regions of Kenya. Structured questionnaires were administered across all sites, while detailed power quality logging was performed at six selected sites using a Fluke 1777 power quality analyzer for one week per site. Novel integrated fuzzy framework was developed using Weighted Sum Method (WSM), Fuzzy AHP, and AHP + CRITIC to compare overall minigrid performance. Robustness of the final ranking was tested via one-at-a-time sensitivity analysis (±20% weight perturbation) and Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 iterations, 95% CI). Results revealed significant variations, the highest average power factor was recorded at Ndeda Island (0.89), while Illaut (0.61) and Remba Island (0.51) exhibited very poor power factors. Frequency variations at Locheromoit (0.52), Ndeda (0.59), and Remba (1.2) exceeded EN 50160:2010 and IEEE 519-2022 thresholds. Substantial prolonged interruptions were observed at Hadado (1.2 hrs/week) and Illaut (2.59 hrs/week). Unlike Wasini that achieved the highest FTPQI (0.93), Illaut registered the lowest FTPQI (0.29). Wasini and Illaut demonstrated 100% rank stability under ±20% perturbation. Spearman correlations between WSM vs. AHP+CRITIC and FAHP vs. AHP+CRITIC were 0.89 and 0.94, respectively. The findings demonstrate that fuzzy power quality indices are critical for diagnosing specific failures, particularly poor power factor, frequency instability, and prolonged interruptions in autonomous minigrids. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Graphene and MXenes: performance–scalability trade-offs and application-driven materials selection in two-dimensional technologies
abstract: Graphene and MXenes are leading two-dimensional (2D) materials, yet their selection for emerging technologies remains limited by the lack of quantitative comparison between intrinsic performance, scalability, and cost. This review introduces a practical performance–scalability assessment framework based on a multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) approach. In this regard, material-performance, synthesis-scalability, and techno-economic indicators were normalized and integrated to calculate the final material-selection score. The evaluated criteria include electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, mechanical strength, electrochemical capacitance, synthesis yield percentage, maturity status, price per unit mass of precursors, specific energy utilization, and oxidation resistance capability. Graphene exhibits higher thermal conductivity (2000–4000 W m⁻1 K⁻1), mechanical strength (∼130 GPa), and oxidation stability, supporting its use in performance-critical electronics and structural applications. MXenes provide higher electrochemical capacitance ( 300–1500 F g⁻¹), higher reported synthesis yields (80–99%), tunable surface chemistry, and lower estimated laboratory-scale cost (US$10–50 g⁻1), favoring energy storage, sensing, electromagnetic interference shielding, and water-related applications. The novelty of this review lies in combining property-level performance, synthesis maturity, scalability indicators and cost-performance mapping, into a single comparative framework, enabling rational, application-specific selection of graphene, MXenes, and their hybrid systems. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Multiple pathways to social bonding through music
abstract: Music is widely recognized for its ability to foster social bonding. Yet, while research has largely focused on interpersonal movement coordination, other ways in which music can connect people have received comparatively less attention. We argue that music-related social bonding extends beyond coordinated movement and emerges through multiple forms of imagined and shared social experience. We propose a conceptual framework comprising three interrelated pathways: interpersonal coordination, shared social experience without explicit behavioral coordination, and imagined social experience during solitary listening. Across these pathways, music recruits interacting mechanisms of temporal prediction, self-other integration, reward processing, and social-cognitive alignment that together promote social closeness, affiliation, and prosocial orientation. We further highlight how musical features and individual differences shape these processes. By integrating evidence from music psychology, cognitive neuroscience, and social psychology, this framework broadens current perspectives on how music promotes social bonding and identifies conceptual and methodological directions for future research. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: A diffusion-based framework for probabilistic communication performance degradation prediction in train control systems
abstract: Train-ground data communication is the only channel for safety-critical information exchange in train control systems, and its degradation can directly threaten operational reliability. However, degradation prediction is challenging due to cross-layer coupled indicators, strong uncertainty, and partial observability caused by missing monitoring data. To address these issues, this paper proposes a diffusion-based framework for probabilistic communication performance degradation prediction. The framework reformulates degradation prediction as a two-stage task consisting of probabilistic forecasting of degradation-sensitive indicators under incomplete observations and degradation risk probability prediction through degradation-index-based mapping. In Stage-I, a Multi-Granularity Token Conditional Diffusion Model (MTCDM) sequentially reconstructs incomplete multivariate historical observations and forecasts the probabilistic future trajectories of three degradation-sensitive indicators. In Stage-II, a Degradation Risk Probability Prediction (DRPP) module maps forecasts into interpretable degradation states and risk probabilities. Three degradation-sensitive indicators are selected to characterize degradation at the physical, service, and application levels. Experiments on a real-world railway communication dataset and a public benchmark demonstrate superior reconstruction, forecasting, and degradation-aware risk prediction performance compared with baselines. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective solution for risk-aware communication degradation monitoring and proactive warning in safety-critical train control systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Resilience assessment and enhancement of critical infrastructure under natural hazards with case studies in Nordic power grid
abstract: Maintaining the operational continuity of critical infrastructures during natural hazards is essential for supporting societal well-being and economic development. This paper introduces the RECINAT framework, as a proactive approach for assessing and enhancing the technical and economic infrastructure resilience against natural hazard-triggered technological events. The study specifically focuses on distribution power systems in the Nordic region, which face significant vulnerabilities from rainfall-induced landslides. This study utilizes an indicator-based methodology to quantify resilience through a hazard-preventive pathway with metrics such as normalized electrical energy not supplied (NEENS), interruption of nodes (ION), and the cost of energy not supplied (CENS). Integration of distributed energy resources configured as virtual power plants (VPPs) is proposed for system resilience enhancement. An enhanced IEEE 33-bus distribution test system is adapted to represent a regional grid in Southwest Norway as the case study. The strategic deployment of these VPPs is formulated as a multi-objective optimization problem and solved using the nondominated sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) as the targets of simultaneous minimization of NEENS, CENS, total VPP capacity, and active power losses. Numerical results demonstrate that optimized VPP deployment reduces economic losses from service interruptions and improves the overall redundancy resilience index. The proposed framework can support resilience-oriented operational planning and long-term investment decision-making for distribution networks exposed to increasing climate-related hazards. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Highly active Ni-Co catalyst on hybrid MWCNT-Graphene nanoplatelet catalysts for ammonia decomposition
abstract: Ammonia decomposition offers a promising route for on-demand hydrogen production. However, the large-scale use of non-noble metal catalysts is limited by their low activity and poor stability at low temperatures. In this study, a series of monometallic Ni, Co and bimetallic Ni-Co catalysts supported on a hybrid multi-walled carbon nanotube-graphene nanoplatelet were synthesised via impregnation. This study examined how changes in the Ni-Co ratio affect the properties and performance of the catalysts. The catalysts were carefully analysed using XRD, N2 physisorption, CO chemisorption, H2-TPR, H2-TPD, N2-TPD, NH3-TPD, SEM, and TEM. They were then tested for NH3 decomposition at a weight hourly space velocity of 12,000 mL/gcat.h. The results showed that increasing Co content increased the surface area, metal dispersion, and reducibility, while lowering the adsorption and desorption energies for H2, N2, and NH3. The 2.5Ni-7.5Co catalyst had the highest surface area (166.8 m2/g), the best metal dispersion (8.39%), the smallest crystallite size (7.27 nm), and the lowest desorption temperatures and energies for H2, N2, and NH3. It reached 78% NH3 conversion at 500°C and 99% at 550°C, and remained stable for 24h. These findings show that the combination of Ni and Co, along with conductive carbon supports, is important for making efficient, long-lasting, non-noble-metal catalysts for low-temperature NH3 decomposition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Children’s vocabulary predicts their math abilities: The mediating role of verbal and visuospatial short-term memory
abstract: This study recruited 131 Chinese children aged 4 to 6 years and measured their forward counting, symbolic and nonsymbolic magnitude comparison, arithmetic problems, shape naming, vocabulary, and verbal and visuospatial short-term memory to explore the relationship between vocabulary, short-term memory, and mathematical ability. The results showed that verbal short-term memory fully mediated the relationship between vocabulary and symbolic magnitude comparison, as well as between vocabulary and arithmetic problems However, no mediating effect of visuospatial short-term memory was found between vocabulary and current mathematical ability. In addition, for nonsymbolic magnitude comparison and shape naming, only the direct effect of vocabulary was significant. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: Risk-informed design of integrated nuclear-hydrogen production facilities using probabilistic consequence modeling
abstract: The U.S. Department of Energy estimates that one 1000 MW nuclear power plant integrated with a hydrogen electrolysis facility can produce 150,000 tons of hydrogen annually [ 1 ]. To ensure the safety of both facilities through risk-informed design and mitigation measures, we characterized the effects of hydrogen explosions and jet fires on plant infrastructure and integrated the results into a quantitative risk assessment (QRA). We leveraged Kingery-Bulmash, Baker, and TNO models to evaluate overpressure at different distances and hydrogen accumulation times, informing critical structure vulnerabilities. The models showed hydrogen piping from each electrolyzer unit experiences high overpressure if an explosion occurs. Therefore, we conducted finite element analysis on that area and determined the fixed ends experience the highest stress. Simulations of jet fires show they are of little concern in design decisions due to short flame duration, assuming proper safety component placement. Finally, we integrated the overpressure models into our QRA framework to calculate location-specific individual and site risk (LSIR and LSSR) to inform setback distance and safety decisions, probabilistically. Our results show the benefits of using analytical models for overpressure calculations in QRAs. We conclude with risk-informed design and safety distance recommendations to ensure safety of nuclear-hydrogen production facilities. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.
