title: How do children intervene in transgressions? The influence of apology and intervention costs
abstract: When norms for maintaining cooperative networks are violated, humans try to cope in various ways. However, knowledge is limited regarding how children respond to transgressions. Across two experiments, we examined how 82 six-year-olds, predominantly of Japanese ethnicity (97.6%), choose among punishment, forgiveness, and non-intervention when addressing transgressions from a third-party perspective using a novel paradigm. In addition, we examined how an apology from the transgressor and intervention costs influence children’s moral intervention behaviors. In Experiment 1, Japanese children (N = 41) were presented with a transgressor who either did or did not apologize. Contrary to the previous assumption that children are highly inclined to moral intervention even when it is costly, punishment was the least selected option and non-intervention was the most selected. Children who initially showed reluctance to intervene in transgressions then flexibly adjusted their choice to show forgiveness in response to the transgressor’s apology. In Experiment 2, as in Experiment 1, Japanese children (N = 41) avoided costly punishment and predominantly chose non-intervention. However, when punishment involved no personal cost, children were more likely to choose punishment and less likely to choose no intervention. These findings demonstrate that, when presented with multiple options, 6-year-olds engage less actively in punishment or forgiveness than previous work has suggested, and their intervention strategies are sensitive to social cues and personal costs. This research provides novel insights into the development of moral decision-making in early childhood. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: CL3E-GNN: Three-phase attention with feature fusion based on curriculum implementation strategy for class imbalanced node classification
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) often struggle with node classification under class imbalance because standard methods fail to adequately leverage graph topology. Specifically, majority nodes dominate message passing, causing the aggregated information from minority nodes to become statistically diluted, which masks relational signals associated with under-represented classes. Traditional techniques such as oversampling and cost-sensitive learning mitigate data skew but typically neglect structural dependencies, leading to under-representation of minority classes or overfitting to local graph substructures. We propose CL3E-GNN , a novel curriculum learning framework that addresses class imbalance through three synergistic phases: Engage, Enact , and Embed . The Engage phase employs multi-head attention to identify critical node and edge connections, generating enhanced feature representations via dual graph convolution network (GCN) and graph attention network (GAT) aggregation. The Enact phase refines minority class representations through three complementary mechanisms, each targeting a distinct source of imbalance: importance sampling for active feature learning, metapath propagation for knowledge transfer across heterogeneous relations, and anomaly detection for identifying structural irregularities. The Embed phase introduces a memory-augmented reinforcement learning mechanism that progressively refines node embeddings via reward-modulated updates. A dual-loss optimisation strategy combining cross-entropy with adaptive curriculum loss ensures gradual difficulty progression, offering a principled alternative to simple loss functions or data augmentation alone. Extensive evaluations on eight benchmark datasets, with results averaged over five independent runs, demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods. These results establish CL3E-GNN as a new benchmark for imbalanced node classification, effectively preserving topological integrity while mitigating class distribution skew. The implementation code is available at https://github.com/afofanah/CL3E-GNN . © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Mission reliability assessment and optimization of offshore wind farm inspection unmanned aerial vehicle swarm with coupled physical and data layers under multi-source uncertainties
abstract: Mission reliability assessment and dynamic optimization are essential to ensure safe and efficient operation of offshore wind farm inspection unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms under multi-source uncertainties. However, existing methods remain limited in characterizing cross-layer coupling effects, including interactions between physical-layer energy consumption and data-layer transmission, and dependencies among environmental disturbances, equipment degradation, and communication channel variations. This paper proposes a mission reliability assessment and optimization method for offshore wind farm inspection UAV swarms under multi-source uncertainties, based on C-vine copula modeling and graph reinforcement learning. The method develops a coupled physical-data layer modeling framework incorporating battery degradation, offshore wind disturbance, and line-of-sight/non-line-of-sight (LoS/NLoS) channel variation to characterize swarm behavior in complex offshore inspection scenarios. Furthermore, a C-vine copula-based joint uncertainty model is established to capture nonlinear dependencies among key variables, supporting a dynamic reliability assessment framework that links battery capacity fade and hovering energy constraints to mission feasibility probability. A graph attention network-proximal policy optimization (GAT-PPO) algorithm is then proposed for dynamic task reassignment. Simulation results show that the proposed method reduces the reliability estimation deviation from 7.87% under the independence assumption to 0.82%. It further improves reliability by 3.1% and 3.5% over the best baseline under the most severe UAV failure and task revisit scenarios, respectively, demonstrating improvements in mission reliability and operational efficiency. title: Effects of orifice diameter and initial state on flashing, depressurization and cooling during liquid CO2 pipeline leakage
abstract: High-pressure liquid CO2 pipelines are integral to carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS), but accidental leakage can cause rapid depressurization, intense flashing and severe cooling. Such cooling may increase the risk of fracture and crack propagation, with implications for pipeline integrity. We investigated how phase-transition evolution and these transients vary with orifice diameter in a fully liquid-filled horizontal pipeline. Releases through 1, 2 and 3 mm circular orifices were tested under different initial pressures and temperatures, with synchronized pressure, temperature and high-speed imaging. Larger orifices were associated with greater resolved discharge capacity and faster depressurization. As diameter increased from 1 to 3 mm, release duration decreased from approximately 70 to 13 s. The maximum resolved depressurization rate increased from 16.9 to 45.7 MPa/s. The maximum measured degree of superheat ranged from 0.4 to 4.9 °C. Faster depressurization coincided with deeper pressure–temperature excursions into the metastable region, stronger visible flashing and larger in-pipe fluid-temperature drops. Within the observation window, the first persistent visible bubbles occurred in the bulk liquid for the 1 mm case and earlier in the upper visible region for the larger orifices. Higher initial pressure was associated with a longer single-phase stage for the smaller orifice, whereas higher initial temperature was accompanied by later persistent bubble onset. These results characterize associations among orifice diameter, initial state, flashing and cooling, and provide data relevant to safety assessment of liquid CO2 pipelines. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

title: Mechanism-guided soft sensing of NOx emissions in CFB boilers under heterogeneous noise and multiscale dynamics
abstract: Accurate soft sensing of NOx emission concentration in coal-fired boilers is important for clean combustion control. However, real CFB operating data contain heterogeneous noise, multiscale dynamic responses, and stage-dependent dominant variables, which hinder extraction of NOx-formation dynamics and degrade soft-sensing accuracy. To address these issues, a NOx emission soft sensing method is proposed. First, training samples consistent with practical disturbances are constructed from differences in the statistical distributions of process variables. Representation consistency between noisy and original data is then constrained in the latent space to reduce abnormal-disturbance effects on basic features. After obtaining basic representations, a variable-scale prior weight matrix is designed using data characteristics and CFB combustion mechanisms. This matrix is combined with data-driven scale weights to fuse multiscale features and extract dynamic information better matched to the actual combustion process. To capture dynamic changes in variable effects, learnable proxy vectors aggregate NOx-related key segments with reduced sequence interaction cost. Variable gating then generates variable weights from proxy temporal representations, dynamically identifying dominant process variables across operating stages. Experiments on practical operating data from a 350 MW CFB unit show that the proposed method achieves an R2 of 0.953 on the test set. Under compound disturbances comprising random, abnormal, and drift noise, the R2 remains 0.896, indicating strong noise robustness. SHAP analysis and internal-weight visualization show that the identified key variables and their time-varying effects are generally consistent with CFB combustion mechanisms. Overall, the proposed method improves the accuracy, robustness, and interpretability of NOx emission soft sensing, and provides a practical auxiliary tool for NOx emission monitoring in CFB boilers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: The development of children’s mathematics achievement in primary school: the early and longitudinal links with perceived teacher support and mathematics anxiety
abstract: This longitudinal study investigated developmental trajectories of children’s mathematics achievement, especially the early and longitudinal effects of perceived teacher support and mathematics anxiety. The participants included 1231 Chinese children (M T1age = 8.49, SD = 0.59; 40.29% female) assessed annually across four waves from Grade 3 through Grade 6. Latent class growth models identified three trajectories of children’s mathematics achievement: a low stable group (9.3%), a medium fast rising group (81.4%), and a high stable rising group (9.3%). Relative to the low stable group, early higher levels of mathematics anxiety were associated with lower odds of membership in the latter two groups both. In terms of the developmental trajectory of perceived teacher support, a higher initial level, a smaller early decline, and faster growth during the middle-to-late period were associated with a greater likelihood of membership in the high stable rising group. In contrast, the developmental trajectory of mathematics anxiety indicated that a higher initial level of as well as a slower subsequent decline were associated with a greater likelihood of membership in the low stable group. These findings highlight the distinct predictive roles of perceived teacher support and mathematics anxiety across diverse trajectories of mathematics achievement. Practically speaking, the present study emphasizes the need for differentiated instructional interventions tailored to children’s achievement levels, with attention to both environmental support and individual academic emotions. title: Thermal-hydraulic performance and multi-objective optimization of a V-shaped bifurcated honeycomb-fin cooling plate for large-format lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Localized heat accumulation, non-uniform temperature distribution, and the trade-off between thermal performance and hydraulic penalty remain major challenges in large-capacity lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) battery modules. This study proposes a liquid cooling plate integrating dendritic hierarchical flow channels with honeycomb-inspired hexagonal fins for an eight-cell 280 Ah prismatic LiFePO4 module. A three-dimensional transient fluid–solid conjugate heat transfer model was established and experimentally validated, with maximum relative deviations below 3% for temperature and 4.79% for pressure drop. Comparative analyses identified the hexagonal-fin structure with the SIDO arrangement as the preferred configuration, followed by investigation of the nonlinear effects of porosity, fin arrangement, fin spacing, and Reynolds number on maximum temperature, maximum temperature difference, and pressure drop. A Kriging surrogate model based on 60 LHS–CFD samples was validated using five-fold cross-validation and 12 independent CFD points. Multiple NSGA-II runs and TOPSIS weight sensitivity analysis were then employed to identify the Pareto compromise region, followed by high-fidelity CFD screening. The recommended design (φ = 0.405, S = 5.48 mm, Re = 308) achieved Tmax = 34.336 °C, ΔTmax = 4.671 °C, and ΔP = 255.22 Pa. Compared with the baseline, Tmax and ΔTmax decreased by 0.699 °C and 0.441 °C, respectively, while ΔP increased from 143.29 to 255.22 Pa. Off-design simulations confirmed a stable thermal advantage across the investigated operating conditions. The results reveal a synergistic interaction between macroscopic flow redistribution and periodic regeneration of local thermal boundary layers, providing guidance for thermal–hydraulic trade-off design of large-capacity LiFePO4 liquid cooling systems. title: Unveiling the role of nanocrystallization in acousto-optic properties of Ge-Sb-S chalcogenide glasses
abstract: Acousto-optic (AO) devices are essential in modern photonic systems and support applications such as optical communication and laser processing. Chalcogenide glasses (ChGs) have attracted considerable attention as promising AO materials, yet their AO performance optimization remains hindered by intrinsic trade-offs among key parameters. Herein, a controlled crystallization strategy is developed to regulate the AO performance of GeS2-Sb2S3 ChGs by introducing two representative crystalline phases, In2S3 and PbCl2. The results reveal that distinct crystallization mechanisms exert different influences on AO performance. Compared with In2S3, which participates in glass network formation, PbCl2 largely preserves the intrinsic glass network structure after crystallization, allowing the advantageous properties of the crystalline phase to more effectively optimize refractive index and acoustic response and thereby facilitate the decoupling among key AO parameters. This work provides a feasible route for overcoming intrinsic property coupling in ChGs and offers a viable strategy for designing high-performance AO materials. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Crops in Motion: Strontium Isotope Analysis of Cereal Provenance in a Foraging-Oriented Neolithic Economy
abstract: Strontium isotope analysis offers a powerful tool for investigating mobility and provenance in prehistoric contexts, yet its application to archaeobotanical finds remains limited. This study applies ⁸⁷Sr/⁸⁶Sr analysis to charred cereal grains from Molino Casarotto, an Italian Middle Neolithic wetland site characterised by a foraging-oriented subsistence strategy and unusually limited cereal use compared to contemporary Neolithic farming sites. A locally defined bioavailable ⁸⁷Sr/⁸⁶Sr baseline was established through systematic sampling of modern plants across distinct lithological units surrounding the site. The isotope ratios of the archaeological cereals reveal a non-local and heterogeneous supply pattern, with values consistent with both regional fluvial units and more radiogenic extra-regional sources. These results provide direct evidence for a spatial decoupling between crop production and consumption and demonstrate the methodological viability of strontium isotopes for tracing cereal provenance. By extending isotopic provenancing to plant remains, this study contributes a new analytical framework for investigating crop circulation and provisioning systems in prehistoric societies. More broadly, it highlights the potential of archaeobotanical isotopic data to address fundamental questions concerning surplus, exchange, and the organisation of economic networks in non-state contexts. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Sequential patterns in turn durations of dynamic speech interaction
abstract: People’s conversations follow distinct interaction patterns. We examine the role of time in these patterns by visualizing, analyzing, and identifying patterns in transitions between speakers using tools from dynamical systems theory. We map spontaneous conversational activities as paths in state space, calculate the likelihood of state transitions, and evaluate the correlation between the durations of subsequent turns. Our measurements demonstrate that the duration of consecutive turns follows a structured pattern: consecutive turns are highly correlated in length, except for pairs involving at least one short turn. These results advance descriptive knowledge of turn-taking dynamics and may help inform the design and evaluation of conversational systems. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Pastoral Nomads at a Crossroads: Investigating the Resilience of the Bakarwal Community to Climate and Socio-Ecological Challenges
abstract: Environmental shifts influence the livelihoods of Bakarwal pastoral nomads as they traverse the varied terrains of the Western Himalayas. Climate fluctuations and socio-ecological stressors markedly affect their resilience. Using a mixed-methods approach, the study examines how environmental factors and livelihood pressures interact among these nomads. By integrating scientific analysis of long-term climate patterns with qualitative data from 239 Bakarwal families, the research investigates their adaptive strategies and internal capacity. Results show that a 1 °C rise in winter and early summer temperatures, coupled with decreased rainfall in winter and transit habitats, affects mobility and resource availability, including fodder and water. The study highlights the importance of traditional knowledge, flexible transhumance practices, and eco-friendly methods in enhancing resilience. However, socio-ecological challenges, including limited institutional support and marginalization, threaten the sustainability of their pastoral lifestyle. The research situates livelihood resilience within the dynamic interactions of environmental and cultural systems. By simultaneously evaluating climate and socio-ecological factors, it affirms the enduring value of traditional wisdom and the resilience of pastoral systems in preserving ecological integrity and fostering sustainable development. It underscores the need for inclusive, community-driven policies and adaptive strategies to strengthen resilience and sustain pastoral livelihoods. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Polyethylene gasification in a bubbling fluidized bed: Operating-parameter effects on syngas, tar and soot formation
abstract: Plastic gasification offers a route to recover polymer carbon as synthesis gas; changes in operating conditions affect both syngas properties and the partitioning of carbon among gaseous, condensable, and solid products. This study investigates these effects during polyethylene gasification in an electrically heated lab-scale bubbling fluidized bed. Experimental series varied temperature (750–850 °C), equivalence ratio (ER; 0.20–0.30), and steam-to-carbon ratio (S/C; 0.25–0.75), with additional tests assessing the influence of feed rate and oxygen enrichment. Raising temperature increased H2 and CO yields, doubled gas yield from 0.90 to 1.74 Nm3/kgdaf, and raised carbon conversion efficiency to 93%, while shifting condensables from aliphatics toward aromatics/PAHs. Increasing ER to 0.30 lowered condenser-collected tar but increased soot sixfold and produced less favourable methanol-relevant stoichiometry, showing a trade-off between tar reduction, soot formation, and syngas quality. Steam addition suppressed soot by almost one order of magnitude, but H2, CO, and gas yields peaked at S/C = 0.50, with limited further conversion benefit at higher S/C. Oxygen enrichment from 30% to 72%, with additional steam moderating bed temperature, maintained gas-phase carbon conversion with only a minor reduction in cold-gas efficiency. Paired in-reactor and downstream sampling tracked gas evolution through the freeboard, showing continued olefin conversion and H2 formation consistent with kinetic-model predictions at an imposed 850 °C. C2H4 in the product gas accounted for 25–35% of feed carbon under all conditions. Further hydrocarbon conversion, contaminant removal, and H2 adjustment would therefore be required before the syngas could be used for methanol synthesis. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Health-promoting effects of sky gardens in high-density cities: Evidence from subjective restorative evaluation, eye tracking, and machine learning
abstract: Sky gardens are increasingly recognized as health-promoting potential strategies in high-density urban environments, yet how specific spatial elements contribute to restorative benefits remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates the relationships between spatial composition, visual attention, and psychological restoration by integrating subjective assessments, eye-tracking data, and machine learning analysis across nine sky gardens in Singapore. The results reveal that restorative effects are primarily driven by natural landscapes, public facilities, and waterscapes, while urban landscapes and high-rise elements tend to undermine restoration. Different spatial elements exhibit distinct restorative roles: natural landscapes support both immediate visual attraction and sustained engagement, whereas waterscapes and people presence mainly enhance short-term attention, and public facilities contribute to longer-term restorative experiences. Importantly, these effects are nonlinear, with identifiable threshold ranges beyond which restorative benefits may diminish. These findings provide evidence-based insights for designing health-promoting sky gardens, emphasizing the need to balance natural landscapes, functional facilities, and visual openness to optimize restorative effects. This study deepens understanding of restorative mechanisms in vertical urban spaces and offers practical guidance for improving environmental quality in dense cities. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Automatic design of flow channel for PEMFC based on space-weighted topology and multi-objective optimization
abstract: To address the severe concentration polarization in Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC) under high current density, caused by oxygen transport limitation and water management imbalance, this study proposes a three-dimensional automatic flow channel design framework integrating topology optimization and Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). A multi-physics coupled model is established, with average current density, current density variance, and pressure drop selected as optimization objectives. The weight space is systematically explored through Latin hypercube sampling combined with simplex mapping, and a BP neural network surrogate model is trained based on COMSOL-MATLAB high-fidelity simulation data to enable efficient global optimization. The results reveal a pronounced nonlinear trade-off among the three objectives. Single-objective optimization improves current density but significantly increases pressure drop, while conventional empirical weighting schemes fail to achieve balanced performance. The optimal compromise solution (w1 = 0.571, w2 = 0.286, w3 = 0.143), identified using the TOPSIS decision-making method, achieves a 5.04 % increase in peak power density compared to the conventional structure, while significantly enhancing oxygen distribution uniformity and water management capability. Furthermore, the lateral flow intensity ratio demonstrates a fundamental transition of oxygen transport from diffusion-dominated to convection–diffusion coupled mechanisms. This study provides a systematic and data-driven optimization framework that eliminates empirical bias in weight selection, enables automatic generation of complex flow channel structures, and the optimal structure’s discovery mechanistically reveals the embryonic form of single-channel optima, offering new insights for designing high-performance PEMFC flow fields. title: AI-assisted interactive narrative as an integrative-learning design task: Student appraisal in preservice teacher education
abstract: Research on generative AI in education often asks whether these tools improve learning outcomes. Collaborative design raises a prior question: how should teaching organize AI-supported work so that disciplinary knowledge, creativity, collaboration, and human judgment come together? Integrative learning names that aim: connecting disciplinary knowledge with situated experience and synthesizing insights across cases. Integration matters in teacher education, where preservice teachers must apply principles to ambiguous professional situations. We examined an AI-assisted interactive-narrative (AI-IN) assignment in which preservice teachers designed branching professional-ethics games through a whole-part-whole sequence: course-wide orientation, collaborative development of a focal case with AI-supported possibility generation, and cross-case reintegration. We used self-reports from a 480-person primary cohort and an independent 257-person same-course cohort to ask how students appraised the design, whether the learning ratings shared residual covariance in a one-factor model, and which conditions accompanied appraisal. Allowing residual covariance between the two perceived-learning ratings improved the one-factor model in both cohorts (scaled Δχ²(1) = 11.99 and 14.20, respectively; both p < .001); the localized association was stable across sensitivity analyses. This localized covariance may reflect perceived-learning content or shared-method influences, including wording and placement; it establishes neither learning gains nor a distinct latent domain. In the primary cohort, favorable appraisal accompanied clearer roles, efficient collaboration, greater contribution, better challenge-engagement balance, and positive AI attitudes. Students reported challenges in translating ethics into plots, selecting platforms, and managing workload. AI-IN offers a testable design proposition for integrative learning: AI supports possibility generation while students retain responsibility for selection, verification, ethical judgment, and synthesis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Development and experimental analysis of a novel impulse turbine compounded naturally aspirated High-Speed diesel engine
abstract: Despite decades of research and development proving the technical advantages of turbocharging, several gasoline and diesel engines, especially the single-cylinder engines, remain naturally aspirated. Commercially available single-cylinder engines are rarely turbocharged due to inherent technical challenges and cost-to-performance trade-offs. The pulsating exhaust flow typical of single-cylinder engines causes efficiency losses in conventional turbocharger reaction turbines, which are designed for steady or near-continuous exhaust flow. Thus, the benefits of charging and exhaust energy recovery are not realised in many engines, especially single-cylinder engines. Even in the case of two-cylinder and three-cylinder engines, the benefit of charging is not fully realised, as adapting a turbocharger to these engines involves several compromises in energy extraction by the turbine due to the pulsated exhaust flow, in matching the turbine and the compressor, and in matching the turbine and the engine. Consequently, the best-suited compressor or the most effective turbine is not designed individually for these engines, since matching both to the engine compromises the system’s effectiveness. Thus, commercially available single-cylinder engines are rarely turbocharged, supercharged, or turbo-compounded. Therefore, neither the advantage of charging is realised nor the potential for exhaust energy recovery is capitalised, leaving these engines underutilised and underperforming despite their potential. In this work, a novel impulse turbine capable of extracting work from the pulsating exhaust flow typical of a single-cylinder engine was designed and developed for a commercially available single-cylinder diesel engine, based on simulations and theoretical calculations. Furthermore, a turbocompounding layout was developed to adapt the novel impulse turbine for the single-cylinder engine. Subsequently, an experimental analysis was conducted to evaluate the performance of the impulse turbine. Experimental results showed that the impulse turbine delivered 1.2 kW of power at 3000 rpm, increasing the naturally aspirated (NA) engine brake power output by 12 %. The turbine efficiency was about 80 %, and the net brake power output of the NA engine with the impulse turbine was 11.5 kW at 3000 rpm. The present study demonstrates the potential to improve the performance of single-cylinder engines by effectively extracting thermal energy from exhaust gas through impulse turbo-compounding. title: Experimental investigation of different CO2 injection schemes to enhance oil recovery in sandstone reservoir
abstract: Application of carbon dioxide injection to enhance oil recovery is one of the best strategies to achieve a balance between energy security and reduced atmospheric emissions. Several injection schemes can be adopted to implement carbon dioxide-enhanced oil recovery. Injected CO2 mobilizes trapped oil by developing partial or full miscibility through diffusion, oil swelling, and viscosity reduction, but mechanisms such as viscous fingering, gravity override, and early gas breakthrough limit recovery efficiency. This study presents an experimental investigation of four different CO2 injection schemes, including continuous gas injection (CGI), cyclic injection (huff-n-puff), water-alternating-gas (WAG), and polymer-assisted WAG (PWAG) for enhancing oil recovery. Core was characterized for mineralogy, porosity, permeability, and wettability, while density, API gravity, rheology, and safety–critical properties of crude oil were evaluated. Core-flooding experiments were conducted at 70 °C and 800 psi overburden pressure, beginning with secondary waterflooding followed by tertiary CO2-EOR. Waterflooding recovered 47.47 % of the original oil in place (OOIP), leaving 52.53 % OOIP as the target for EOR method. CGI, cyclic, WAG, and PWAG injection schemes using CO2 resulted in significant incremental recovery. The results highlighted the critical role of mobility control in improving sweep efficiency, incremental oil recovery, and effective CO2 utilization by establishing a clear performance hierarchy: PWAG ' WAG ' CGI ' cyclic injection. title: The blind spots of in-situ upgrading: Rethinking social infrastructure
abstract: In-situ upgrading has become a preferred strategy for improving informal settlements worldwide, yet its focus on physical infrastructure often obscures the social infrastructures that sustain everyday life. This study examines how communal spaces—alleyways, rooftops, and other informally produced environments—function as urban commons and how they become vulnerable during upgrading processes. Drawing on Schlager and Ostrom’s bundles-of-rights framework, document analysis, field observations, and 105 interviews, the research traces changes in access, use, management, and ownership of communal spaces during a comprehensive in-situ upgrading project in Nantou, Shenzhen. The findings show that social infrastructure in informal settlements is constituted through shared routines, tacit norms, and collective practices rather than formal design, making it particularly susceptible to enclosure when upgrading prioritizes aesthetic, commercial, or heritage objectives. The study identifies governance displacement as a mechanism through which upgrading reconfigures rights and responsibilities, producing non-physical forms of dispossession even without relocation. By conceptualising social infrastructure as urban commons, the paper advances a framework for recognizing and protecting these often-invisible systems. The findings offer transferable insights for upgrading practices globally, highlighting the need for governance-sensitive, participatory approaches that safeguard the social foundations of community life. © 2026 The Authors.

title: CROWN: Contract-theoretic resource optimization for welfare maximization in heterogeneous edge networks
abstract: Efficient edge-assisted video streaming requires the synergistic orchestration of caching, computing, and transmission resources. However, this potential is practically impeded by the complex coupling of these heterogeneous resources and the information asymmetry regarding nodes’ private marginal operating-cost types. To address these challenges, we propose CROWN, a contract-theoretic incentive mechanism designed to support welfare-oriented resource coordination between the Content Provider and Content Delivery Network nodes A core modeling contribution of CROWN is a window-level multi-resource accounting formulation that translates the disparate constraints of storage, bandwidth, and computing into a tractable optimization framework while retaining their respective physical meanings. Building on this model and established discrete-screening results, we analytically derive a monotone contract menu that guarantees Individual Rationality and Incentive Compatibility under the stated static-screening and observability assumptions, thereby achieving a second-best welfare-maximizing solution under adverse selection. To ensure scalability in dense networks, we further develop a polynomial-time Primal–Dual Ironing procedure, implemented through scalar bisection and generalized PAVA ironing, to efficiently enforce allocation monotonicity. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of CROWN in balancing economic efficiency and service quality. Compared with the Stackelberg baseline at the representative network scale, CROWN yields a 9.31% improvement in total social welfare and sustains a 92.1% hit rate for long-tail content, demonstrating its effectiveness within the evaluated settings. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Distributed maximum clique computation via clique-preserving partitioning and vertex replication
abstract: The maximum clique problem is a fundamental NP-hard problem in graph theory. Despite advances in exact and heuristic solvers, their performance on large graphs is limited by irregular search spaces, strong sequential dependencies in pruning, and pronounced load imbalance. Parallel execution is therefore necessary to address these challenges, but achieving high performance without degrading solution quality is nontrivial. In this work, we propose a distributed-memory framework for the maximum clique problem based on structure-aware graph decomposition that preserves clique structure. The framework integrates controlled boundary vertex replication to maintain global clique integrity while enabling efficient parallel execution. Experimental results on large real-world and benchmark graphs demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves substantial parallel speedups on an HPC cluster while maintaining high solution quality. With 16 processors and a replication ratio of 1%, the framework preserves the maximum clique on the majority of real-world graph instances, achieving an average speedup of approximately (Formula presented) and peak speedups of up to (Formula presented). Additional experiments with a fundamentally different maximum clique solver indicate that the framework is largely independent of the underlying clique-search strategy. We further provide theoretical guarantees that characterize when graph partitioning preserves the maximum clique and quantify the replication required to recover cliques fragmented by partitioning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Underground movements: Zama Zama Mobility, Precarity, and community resilience in South Africa’s Platinum Belt
abstract: This article examines the lived experiences of unregulated artisanal miners, locally known as Zama Zamas, who mine within and around abandoned platinum mines in South Africa’s North West province, a region rich in critical minerals. While artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) in abandoned gold mines has been the subject of considerable academic inquiry, similar activities in platinum mining areas remain understudied. This study seeks to address this gap by situating ASM within the broader discourse on Africa’s critical minerals agenda and contributing to both academic and policy debates on its strategic role. Drawing on a mixed-methods approach, the paper investigates how Zama Zamas navigate precarious and often dangerous working conditions, patterns of circular and transnational migration, and exclusion from formal mining economies. It further reveals the social and economic networks and adaptive local strategies that foster resilience and community cohesion amid institutional abandonment and uncertain regulation within the critical mineral extraction sector of derelict mines. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Pastoral Belonging and Educational Opportunity for Mongolian Herder Women
abstract: As part of the UN’s International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralism (2026) the Gender Working Group stresses the importance of equality in pastoralism. For herder women themes of family, work, schooling and marginality resonate across African and Asian drylands. As environmental, economic and development pressures impact herding women are essential to its continuity. In Mongolia, a prominent pastoralist nation, the role of rural women in household decision-making, livelihood production and community contributions has received little study. In a series of interviews in two rural districts this study explores the practice and knowledge of female herders with a focus on their daily lives. Findings reflect pastoralism in a time of social and livelihood transition. Nature, livestock and tradition were valued whilst family and work responsibilities were arduous. Reflecting perceived challenges and opportunities, experienced herders encouraged daughters to pursue education. Whether growing up in the socialist era or appreciating today’s conveniences, women’s commitment to herding is a vital part of the country’s past nomadic heritage and future direction. As social roles and environmental uncertainty reconfigure pastoralism, female herders are at the forefront of changing rural communities in Mongolia. The next evolution may ask ‘is there a role for educated female herders?’ © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Urban transformation in heritage cities through the perceptions of experts- A case of Varanasi, India
abstract: This study presents responses to questionnaires submitted to 30 experts from diverse professional backgrounds about one of the oldest settlements in India, i.e., Varanasi. Expert interviews provided diverse perspectives on the challenges of urban settings and their transformation. To decipher the subjective responses, this data was analysed using MAXQDA24, a data analysis tool that facilitates quick analysis, coding, and presentation of large qualitative datasets. The expert highlights that the visual representation of the city, including its religious, educational, and historical significance, is highly prominent. Additionally, the study suggests the establishment of a city-level heritage body to a) maintain heritage properties, b) plan different neighborhoods for different perceptual experiences to segregate the footfall, and c) involve the local community. Overall, this study offers a unique expert-driven perspective on the current conditions and the transforming fabric of Varanasi. © 2026 The Authors.

title: The effects of resilience-oriented workspace interventions: combining social network analysis and organizational quality indicators
abstract: Although it is known that workspace influences the performance of healthcare teams, there is scarce evidence regarding how to evaluate its implications for resilient performance. This study demonstrates an integrated approach for evaluating the effects of relocating three acute response teams responsible for the same patients – the rapid response team (RRT), medical on-call team (MOC), and nursing supervision (NS) – from separate rooms to a shared workspace. The intervention was evaluated using two complementary sources of evidence. First, social network analysis surveys were conducted before and after the intervention with the same 30 participants. The surveys mapped advice-seeking relationships from which 22 social network metrics were derived. Second, seven organizational quality indicators were analyzed before and after the intervention. Five quality and 12 network indicators showed statistically significant improvements; except for two social network metrics, all 27 indicators changed in the expected direction for improvement. Notably, reciprocity between teams, which is crucial for resilience, increased substantially – e.g., RRT↔MOC increased from 57.5% to 80.0%. Changes in collaboration patterns and quality indicators provided complementary evidence that the conditions supporting resilient performance were enhanced. The evaluation approach can be adapted to other resilience-oriented interventions in which relational dynamics and patient safety are crucial. © 2026 The Authors.

title: From control to authorship: Exploring how user agency relates to generative presence and therapeutic self-attribution in AI-driven VR mindfulness
abstract: AI-driven interactivity is expanding the design space of virtual reality mindfulness-based interventions (VR-MBIs), but the experiential value of semantic co-creation remains unclear. We propose an agency-centered framework in which Generative Presence (GP) and Therapeutic Self-Attribution (TSA) represent potentially coupled experience- and belief-level pathways, with Emotional Resonance (ER) reflecting affective fit and responsiveness. In a mixed-methods pilot randomized controlled trial (N = 48), participants completed a 10-minute breath-focused session in either the generative condition (GEN) or a matched static active-control condition (STA). Semantic co-creation yielded higher covariate-adjusted post-session state mindfulness than pre-authored scene selection, whereas anxiety decreased in both conditions without a detectable between-condition difference. Exploratory differences were largest for the study-specific indicators of expressive control and authorship, while ER, therapeutic attribution, and spatial presence also favored GEN; broader established agency and attribution measures showed limited differentiation. Within GEN, authorship correlated with ER, and ER with post-session mindfulness—a pattern anticipated by the framework, although mediation and temporal ordering were not tested. Interviews (n = 12) identified two regulation modes: expressive control through attentional anchoring and meaning construction, and low-effort exposure through restorative absorption. The interviews further suggested that added agency could support engagement but also introduce evaluative pressure, whereas static exposure could reduce effort but was sometimes accompanied by boredom and rumination. These preliminary findings position semantic authorship as a conditional design resource that may support mindfulness by making the attentional object more personally meaningful and intention-linked, while its implications for immediate state anxiety regulation may vary with user–task fit. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Intervening Impersistence on the St. Johns River, Florida
abstract: Across 9000 years, shells were a common medium of terraforming along the St. Johns River in northeast Florida. In this regard, shell mounds nicely match definitions of persistent place. However, close attention paid to shells and their itineraries highlights how impersistent these places were. Shell, as a construction medium and an index of history, provided opportunities for re-establishing place in the context of change, even when used by settler colonists to build out Florida’s road networks in the twentieth century. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Populist urbanism and the speculation network: Discourse, conflict, and planning monopoly in Hamadan
abstract: This article explores how populist discourse reshapes urban planning conflicts and legitimizes speculative development in Hamadan, Iran. Using post-structuralist discourse theory and qualitative analysis of 1248 local media texts (2017–2024), it shows how signifiers like “the people” and “justice” construct antagonistic narratives that erode planning authority. The study introduces the concept of a “speculation network” involving political, commercial, and media actors that exploit participatory rhetoric for elite gain. It finds that populism marginalizes expertise and reinforces monopolies, with media as a key discursive arena. The article advances agonistic planning theory and advocates media-aware, conflict-sensitive planning approaches. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Recognition of individual angry versus happy faces in 6- and 9-month-old infants
abstract: With mixed evidence from adults, children, and infants suggesting either anger or happiness superiority in emotion detection, emotion recognition, and recognition of individual faces posing emotional expressions, the current research was undertaken to determine if one or the other emotion would result in higher recognition of individual faces by 6-month-old and 9-month-old infants. The infants were familiarized with an angry or happy face and then given a novelty preference test pairing the familiarized face with a novel face posing the same emotion. Recognition performance of both age groups in each emotion condition was above chance; however, recognition of angry faces was reliably higher than for happy faces. A simple exposure-frequency account of the findings is unlikely because infants experience more happy than angry faces. In addition, lower-level interpretations based on differences in salience, complexity, and discriminability were not supported by image analyses, infant looking times during familiarization, or adult ratings. An account based on the processing of facial expressions as social or communicative signals by infants is discussed, with a possible role for an early negativity bias. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Re-imagining visions as shared societal statements– empirical insights from Indian cities
abstract: Visions in Indian cities lack commitment from actors and possess low normative power. To address these concerns, we take up the task of examining vision-making with a focus on institutional settings across 31 million-plus populated cities. Ostrom's Institutional Analysis and Development (IAD) framework and ADICO grammar tool are used for analysis. We ask how rules-in-use within the vision-making settings are organized and geared towards collective action, and how they affect outcomes, i.e., visions. The analysis underscores three commonalities that hinder collective action, i.e., bureaucratic hegemony and allegiance to sectoral mandates, fragmented actor constellation and weak regulatory power of visions. Within visioning settings, facilitators serve as key agents for ensuring a level playing field. We found that when facilitators are external (i.e., consultants), stakeholder coverage is wider and documentation is exhaustive. In large metropolises and megacities, the visioning process acknowledges stakeholder consultation responsibly. Perhaps fair information exchange and informal monitoring of visions by civil society actors contribute to the politicisation of vision-making. In institutional terms, visions are closer to being a strategy and less to norm-setting. The paper argues that participatory discussions in diverse and heterogeneous settings with the scope of repeat interactions will build homophily and address concerns of structural fragmentation. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Effect of pastoral management and climate change on Alpine pasture vegetation: An assessment over two decades
abstract: Alpine pasture vegetation is jointly shaped by climate and grazing, yet long-term studies addressing the drivers of vegetation change have rarely accounted for the spatial and temporal variability of grazing intensity. This study resurveyed 51 GPS-referenced vegetation plots in five actively grazed pastures of the Western Italian Alps after 19 years (2003–2022). Vegetation surveys and weather-station records were integrated with two complementary grazing metrics: official annual stocking-rate trajectories at the pasture scale and a slope-derived Site-Use Intensity (SUI) index representing potential livestock use at the plot scale. Changes in six dominant Social Behaviour Types (SBTs), plant diversity, and pastoral value were related to climatic and management predictors using machine-learning models. All pastures experienced warming, whereas precipitation and stocking-rate trends varied among sites. Only species typical of meso-eutrophic grasslands and oligotrophic acidophile montane swards increased significantly in cover. Both SBTs showed their largest increases at intermediate SUI, but their climatic and grazing responses diverged. The increase in species associated to meso-eutrophic grasslands was linked with faster increases in mean annual temperature and precipitation and was weakly related to stocking-rate trends. Oligotrophic montane acidophile species increased mainly under moderate warming and greater water availability, but declined with rapid warming, longer dry spells, and sharp stocking-rate increases. Climate and management had comparable and mainly additive importance, while SUI was the most influential individual predictor of both SBT cover changes and community evenness. Species richness and pastoral value remained stable, whereas the Effective Number of Species increased by 11.8%, indicating a redistribution of relative cover rather than net species accumulation. By separating pasture-scale livestock pressure from plot-scale potential use, this study showed that local grazing distribution may be more informative than livestock numbers alone for explaining long-term vegetation change. Adaptive management should therefore align stocking rates with pasture-specific vegetation carrying capacity, manage livestock distribution within pastures, and adjust occupation and recovery periods to interannual variation in vegetation growth and water availability. © 2026 The Authors. title: Design-based estimation and central limit theorems for local average treatment effects for RCTs
abstract: There is a growing literature on design-based methods to estimate average treatment effects for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) using the underpinnings of experiments. This article builds on these methods to consider design-based regression estimators for the local average treatment effect (LATE) estimand for RCTs with treatment noncompliance. New finite-population central limit theorems are proved for a range of designs, including blocked and clustered RCTs, allowing for baseline covariates to improve precision. Consistent, conservative variance estimators based on model residuals are provided, and simulations show that the estimators yield confidence interval coverage near nominal levels. The methods are demonstrated using data from a private school voucher experiment conducted in the United States. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Multi-objective multi-task optimization using decomposition collaboration mechanism and adaptive differential evolution
abstract: Multi-objective multi-task optimization (MOMTO) is a key research direction in evolutionary computation, widely used to address complex trade-offs among multiple objectives and tasks. In recent years, numerous algorithms have been proposed and demonstrated promising performance. However, with the increasing scale and complexity of real-world problems, especially in high-dimensional settings, existing methods face major challenges such as slow convergence, high computational cost, and loss of population diversity. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an innovative many-objective and multi-task optimization algorithm (MaMTO/D-ADE). The algorithm incorporates an efficient neighborhood cooperation mechanism based on a decomposition strategy to mitigate the high complexity and inefficiency of solving large-scale optimization problems. Furthermore, an enhanced differential evolution approach is developed, which integrates adaptive parameter control with hybrid mutation operators to effectively balance global exploration and local exploitation. A flexible offspring updating mechanism is also introduced to accelerate convergence while maintaining population diversity. Extensive experiments conducted on several well-established benchmark problems demonstrate that MaMTO/D-ADE achieves significant improvements in both convergence speed and solution quality, exhibiting superior competitiveness compared to existing state-of-the-art algorithms. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: A novel tetrafluoroborate with giant birefringence assembled from biocompatible adenine
abstract: Birefringent crystals with large optical anisotropy are indispensable for the achievement of optical devices miniaturization. Due to structural diversity, organic-inorganic hybrid crystals have emerged as promising platforms for modulating birefringence. However, achieving ultraviolet (UV) transparency and large birefringence simultaneously still remains a challenge due to intrinsic trade-off. Herein, a strategy that combines a biocompatible planar π-conjugated cation with non π-conjugated anion is proposed. Adenine (ADE, C5H5N5) is employed as a new birefringence-active unit and assembled with tetrafluoroborate [BF4]− anions, yielding a new fluoroborate crystal (C5H6N5)BF4 (ADE-BF4). The anhydrous two-dimensional structure, sustained by intermolecular hydrogen bonding and π-π interactions, endows ADE-BF4 with high thermal stability up to 213 °C. It features a giant birefringence of 0.439@546 nm, and the limited electron delocalization of ADE and [BF4]− endows it with a wide transparency range extending into the UV region (cutoff edge at 289 nm). Theoretical calculations disclose that the coplanarity of the planar ADE moieties contribute to the significantly enhanced birefringence. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Using substances while playing: Players’ motivations, perceptions, and experiences with psychoactive drugs during recreational gaming
abstract: Research on psychoactive substance use during video game play has traditionally adopted a medical lens, focusing on the addictive potential of licit and illicit drugs and their pathological impacts on players. This framing highlights negative outcomes of the co-occurrence between excessive gaming and substance use, leaving the motivations, meanings, and perceptions that players themselves attach to substance use during recreational play under-examined. In this article, we explore a first-person perspective on substance-involved play through a qualitative study with 24 participants (11 Italians and 13 Americans) who reported using psychoactive substances during gameplay. Semi-structured interviews were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis, which led us to develop three themes: first, adult players describe a “lost immersion”, an effortless absorption they remember from youth and no longer attain spontaneously, which leads them to deploy a repertoire of strategies, including substance use, to re-enter it; second, participants engage in “situated modulation”: they use substances as precise, context-sensitive levers for shaping experience, emotion, and cognition, aligning substance choice with game genre, in-game task, and the stakes of the session; third, participants perform legitimacy work around fairness, treating the same substance as benign in casual play and suspect in competitive play, and practicing situational rather than categorical self-restraint. Substance use also produced unintended effects that sometimes diminished, rather than enhanced, players’ agency over play and over their internal states. By foregrounding first-person accounts, this article contributes to HCI scholarship on digital games, altered states, and player agency in ways that complement the medical lens. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Urea revisited: Isopropyl substitution for a balanced nonlinear optical performance
abstract: Organic nonlinear optical (NLO) materials represent a promising class of NLO crystals. Compared with inorganic NLO crystalline materials, they often exhibit stronger second-harmonic generation (SHG) responses. However, many organic NLO crystals suffer from excessively large birefringence, and there is an inherent trade-off between achieving a large SHG coefficient and maintaining a moderate birefringence. In this work, by substituting some of the hydrogen atoms in urea with isopropyl groups, we obtained the compound N,N’-diisopropylurea (DIU), which exhibits a strong SHG effect (∼0.9 × urea) and a large optical bandgap (5.91 eV), while achieving a dramatic reduction in birefringence (a 60% decrease compared to urea). The resulting birefringence is very close to that of the most classic inorganic NLO crystal, KH2PO4 (KDP), which is of great importance for the application of NLO crystals. Furthermore, using the atomic space tessellating (AST) method, we explored, at the atomic and electronic levels, the evolution pattern of the contributions of different structural motifs to the SHG coefficient and birefringence induced by the structural changes in this series. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Hydrazo Bridging Combined with Multiple Hydrogen-Bonding Network: A Strategy for Regulating Energy and Safety in Pyrazinyl Energetic Molecules
abstract: Hydrogen bonding plays a pivotal role in the crystal engineering of energetic materials and provides an effective strategy for the synergistic regulation of structural stability and energetic properties. In this work, we used polysubstituted pyrazine as the parent skeleton, other six-membered aromatic rings as building blocks, and a hydrazo group as a bridging module to construct a series of symmetric and asymmetric hydrazo-bridged bicyclic pyrazinyl energetic molecules. A systematic evaluation of their geometric structures, electronic properties, detonation performance and safety was conducted by integrating theoretical calculations with experiments. Experimental and theoretical calculations have revealed a clear structure-property rule: as the number of ortho-NH2/NO2 modules increases, the hydrogen bond network gradually becomes more continuous and abundant, leading to improved detonation performance (Dv: 8023∼8414 m·s⁻¹), reduced mechanical sensitivity (IS: 8∼20 J) and improved thermal stability (Td: 223∼283 °C). It is worth noting that the enhancement of hydrogen bonding networks effectively eliminates the long-standing trade-off between energy and safety, while additional conjugation enhancement helps to improve thermal stability. This work establishes hydrazo-mediated multiple hydrogen bond network engineering as a universal and scalable strategy for achieving triple synergistic optimization, providing clear design principles for the next generation of high-performance, insensitive and thermally stable energetic materials. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Cooperative operation of networked virtual power plants in low-carbon distribution systems
abstract: Networked virtual power plants can create coordination gains while their emission and participation outcomes depend on the governing carbon and settlement rules. This study develops a DSO-coordinated mechanism that couples feeder-constrained two-stage stochastic dispatch, carbon-policy accounting, and coalition-stable settlement. The dispatch model coordinates renewable output, dispatchable generation, stationary storage, mobility-coupled electric vehicles, reserve, and scenario recourse. Risk is represented by six clustered empirical scenarios and one explicit tail scenario, with a 95% conditional value-at-risk term. The policy layer separates physical operational emissions, allocated allowances, carbon-valued accounting cost, and internal settlement. The settlement layer uses standard Shapley values to calibrate weighted-Nash gains and evaluates every coalition through core and least-core diagnostics. In a 168 h CAISO-eGRID case, cooperation under the same tiered carbon rule reduced total accounting cost from 52,566.65 to 50,349.19 USD and created 2217.47 USD of surplus. Physical emissions changed from 141.3554 to 144.5849 t CO2, an increase of 3.2294 t CO2 under the matched policy. Carbon prices produced a non-uniform physical response, whereas renewable expansion changed the feasible operating set directly. The integrated results identify the operating and governance conditions that support cost efficiency, carbon accountability, and stable participation. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Collective communication behavior driven by emotion: A systematic meta-analysis of the relationship between emotional arousal and rumor spreading
abstract: This meta-analysis aimed to quantify the relationship between emotional arousal and rumor spreading. To this end, it integrated 30 empirical studies (55 effect sizes, N = 32,082) and employed a three-level meta-analytic model. Meta-regression examined the moderating effects of emotional valence, rumor-spreading channel, measurement dimension, and participants’ country, gender, and educational background. Results indicated a significant positive correlation between emotional arousal and rumor spreading (r =.294, p <.001). Moderation analysis further revealed that emotional valence significantly moderated this relationship (QM (1) = 4.20, p <.05), and positive emotional arousal showed a stronger correlation with rumor spreading. Additionally, participants’ country significantly moderated the relationship between emotional arousal and rumor spreading (QM (1) = 5.453, p <.05). The correlation between emotional arousal and rumor spreading was stronger among samples from developing countries relative to those from developed countries. Participants’ gender, educational background, rumor-spreading channel, and measurement dimension did not exert significant moderating effects. This indicates that rumor spreading is a collective social behavior, and its variation is significantly contingent on macro-level factors. Consequently, rumor governance represents a collective social endeavor. Theoretically, this meta-analysis identified emotion as a core construct correlated with rumor spreading, validating and expanding upon the existing theoretical framework. The findings also offer novel perspectives for rumor governance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: The role of mnemonic discrimination in symptom severity and treatment response of obsessive-compulsive disorder
abstract: Mnemonic discrimination, the ability to differentiate novel stimuli from highly similar past ones, has been evidenced as a compelling factor for fear overgeneralization in anxiety disorders. However, very limited research has examined mnemonic discrimination in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). The current study provided an initial examination of the relationship between mnemonic discrimination to OCD symptoms and treatment response. Patients (N = 48) in an intensive partial hospital/residential treatment program for OCD completed the Mnemonic Similarity Task at admission and discharge, along with self-report measures of OCD severity, trait worry, intolerance of uncertainty, and threat estimation. Results showed no significant relationship between mnemonic discrimination and baseline OCD symptom severity. Over the course of treatment, mnemonic discrimination did not change significantly, nor was it associated with OCD symptom reduction. Notably, however, there was a significant interaction between poor mnemonic discrimination and high trait worry to predict more severe OCD symptoms at baseline. Findings suggested that while mnemonic discrimination alone might not be a risk factor for OCD severity or impact treatment response, it could be a potential transdiagnostic risk factor that exacerbates internalizing symptoms when co-present with other cognitive vulnerabilities. Future studies should continue investigating the mechanistic link behind these relationships in larger, more representative samples. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Streaming algorithm for supply chain inventory optimization on the integer lattice
abstract: In a multi-echelon supply chain, to mitigate stockout risks and holding costs, the optimal inventory strategy can be transformed into an optimization problem that maximizes the difference between two DR-submodular functions. Specifically, let x denote the inventory level at each node (an integer variable), where g(x) represents the revenue from inventory meeting demand (DR-submodular, i.e., the marginal revenue of inventory diminishes as the inventory level increases), and h(x) denotes inventory holding costs (also DR-submodular). Maximizing g−h thus effectively mitigates stockout risks and cuts down inventory holding costs. In this paper, we design two algorithms for the problem of maximizing the difference of two DR-submodular function g−h (DDRS) on the integer lattice, where g(x) is monotone and non-negative DR-submodular, and h(x) is monotone and non-negative submodular with curvature ch. We first propose a one-pass streaming algorithm for the unconstrained problem. On this basis, we analyze the algorithm's performance and prove that it provides verifiable approximation guarantees. Second, we design a threshold streaming algorithm for the cardinality-constrained problem. Finally, numerical experiments are conducted to verify the superiority of the proposed algorithms in terms of solution efficiency and approximation accuracy, further corroborating the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis and the practical application value of the algorithms. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Symptom network structures of social media addiction and internet gaming addiction among school-aged youth: Undirected and Bayesian directed graph analyses
abstract: Social media addiction (SMA) and internet gaming addiction (IGA) are increasingly recognized as important behavioral concerns among children and adolescents. However, little is known about whether their symptoms occupy similar structural positions across digital behavior contexts. This study compared the symptom structures of SMA and IGA among school-aged children and adolescents using network and Bayesian graph analyses. A school-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among 11,638 students aged 10–18 years from six public schools in Chongqing, China. SMA was assessed using the Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale, and IGA was measured using the Game Addiction Scale. Regularized partial correlation networks, Network Comparison Tests, and Bayesian Directed Acyclic Graphs were estimated to examine symptom associations, gender differences, and probable directional pathways. Both networks were densely connected but organized around different hubs. Tolerance emerged as the most central symptom in SMA, whereas Withdrawal occupied the central position in IGA. No significant gender differences were observed in the SMA network. In contrast, the IGA network showed significantly greater global strength among females, although no individual edge difference survived correction for multiple comparisons. Bayesian analyses yielded no directionally interpretable pathways for SMA, whereas the IGA network showed a small number of interpretable pathways, with Tolerance and Withdrawal both pointing toward Mood Modification. These findings revealed the different symptom structures of SMA and IGA, with implications for more targeted school-based assessment and intervention. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Explaining the relationship between urban land use per capita and residents’ perceived accessibility using a spatial justice approach: A case study of Tehran metropolis
abstract: Land use per capita remains one of the most widely used quantitative indicators in urban planning for evaluating the provision of urban services. Despite its normative significance, its validity as a proxy for accessibility has received limited empirical examination. This study investigates the extent to which land use per capita provision corresponds to accessibility outcomes across seven neighborhoods in District 20 of Tehran. Using a spatial evaluation model, spatial equity is evaluated through observed service distributions and survey-based accessibility data. Accessibility is operationalized as a measurable variable derived from standardized survey responses. Statistical analyses and spatial diagnostics, including Global Moran’s I, are employed to explain the relationship between six categories of service-related land uses and reported accessibility levels. The findings reveal that higher land use per capita provision does not consistently translate into improved accessibility. The relationship is weak and spatially unstable, while service distribution exhibits a fragmented and non-clustered pattern across neighborhoods. These results suggest that land use per capita standards provide only a partial representation of accessibility outcomes. Spatial configuration and distributional structure emerge as key dimensions influencing the effectiveness of service provision. The study highlights the need for more robust, evidence-based evaluation models that integrate spatial and behavioral dimensions of accessibility. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Do you need to add (con)text to the equation? Subject-related, linguistic, and contextual factors in competence-oriented assessment
abstract: Background: The growing emphasis on competence-oriented school assessments requires tests with more complex descriptions of real-life situations. However, few studies have systematically examined the associated changes in performance requirements, therefore, it is unclear how subject-specific and linguistic task characteristics (interacting) determine the level of difficulty of such tasks and the role of real-life context. Aims: This study examines how linguistic, subject-related, and contextual task characteristics influence the empirical difficulty of reality-based assessment tasks. Sample: The participants were 786 lower secondary school pupils from three comprehensive schools in a federal state in Germany. Methods: In the experiment, three different language versions and three mathematical tasks were developed for 15 German-language factual texts and used in paper-and-pencil tests with a rotational design. Results: The results of the generalized linear mixed models showed that mathematical and linguistic task factors significantly affect empirical task difficulty, although no interactions were found. The real-life context of the tasks proved to be relevant, as students' interest in respective contexts significantly influenced task success. Conclusions: The findings highlight the need to differentiate specific linguistic features in task construction and acknowledge the previously neglected but critical role of real-life contexts in competence-oriented assessments. © 2026 The Authors

title: Impact of heritage status on market prices of townhouses in Central Rio de Janeiro
abstract: This study investigates the effects of differentiated heritage protection regimes on townhouse property values in central Rio de Janeiro, contributing original evidence to a largely unexplored field in Brazil. Based on a sample of 86 townhouses, it applies a traditional hedonic pricing model (OLS), a Geographically Weighted Regression (GWR), and a Multiscale Geographically Weighted Regression with Spatial Autoregressive Error (MGWRSAR), which account for spatial heterogeneity and residual autocorrelation. To overcome data limitations, the analysis employs a bootstrap procedure to improve the robustness of inference. Results indicate that only properties under the least restrictive protection (“monitored”) display statistically significant price premiums. However, rather than reflecting a simple inverse relationship between restrictions and market value, this finding points to the importance of regulatory legibility, enforcement consistency, and perceived investment risks. The discussion highlights how flexible and intelligible protection regimes may foster market confidence, while ambiguous or overly rigid frameworks can undermine the effectiveness of heritage policy. The study also underscores a structural barrier to evidence-based policymaking: the lack of public access to transaction-level data in Brazil. This constraint limits empirical evaluation and transparency, both in academic research and in public administration. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Multi-granularity fusion network with mixed multi-hop graph convolution for hyperspectral image classification
abstract: Effectively integrating spectral–spatial features under limited labeled samples remains a core challenge in hyperspectral image (HSI) classification. Existing hybrid CNN–GCN methods often struggle to balance fine-grained local detail extraction and coarse-grained global relational modeling, frequently suffering from over-smoothing and inefficient cross-modal fusion. To address these issues, we propose a Multi-Granularity Fusion Network (MGF-Net) that systematically bridges coarse-grained structural contexts and fine-grained spatial details. Specifically, at the coarse granularity, a Mixed Multi-hop Graph Convolutional Network (MMGCN) operates on superpixel graphs, where the core Mixed k-hop blocks explicitly incorporate a parallel 0-hop branch to mitigate over-smoothing while capturing long-range dependencies. Concurrently, at the fine granularity, a Convolutional Feature Pyramid Network (CFPN) employs atrous blueprint separable convolutions to extract multi-scale pixel-level details with minimal parameter overhead. To seamlessly integrate these heterogeneous representations, a lightweight Hybrid Feature Fusion Module (HFFM) enforces early cross-granularity alignment via channel shuffle and group convolutions, offering an efficient alternative to heavy attention mechanisms. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that MGF-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance with statistical significance. Notably, the framework exhibits superior robustness under limited training samples and maintains the lowest theoretical computational complexity, offering a compelling accuracy–efficiency trade-off for practical HSI analysis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Why conversations constitute neighbourhood cohesion: A mixed-methods approach to substantiating cause and effect
abstract: Communicating is a meaningful practice for building neighbourhood cohesion by fostering a sense of connection, mutual support and belonging among residents of a geographically defined neighbourhood. In our paper, we highlight the role of regular contact and conversations with neighbours for generating neighbourhood cohesion. Following a mixed-methods approach, we combine qualitative instruments from two case studies focusing on neighbourhoods in Hanover with quantitative data from a panel survey conducted in Hanover and Magdeburg, Germany. The residents’ statements clearly show that talking to each other influences their socio-spatial orientation towards the neighbourhood as a point of reference, thus promoting attitudes and practices to strengthen neighbourhood cohesion. Based on these results, the causal model confirms the effect of conversations on neighbourhood cohesion, which is mediated by the factor of trust. Combining the two types of data helps to understand and explain why neighbourhoods are relevant for peaceful coexistence: they enable low-threshold interaction and thus the experience of belonging and integration. It remains open whether and to what extent neighbourhood cohesion can be scaled up, which requires comparisons with other cities and city types as well as different neighbourhoods to identify regional and international differences. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of rural human settlement quality in China: Based on a Kernel-Driver analytical framework
abstract: Improving rural human settlements is essential for enhancing rural residents' well-being and achieving SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities). This study develops a Kernel-Driver analytical framework to investigate the spatiotemporal evolution, driving mechanisms, and future trajectories of rural human settlement quality (RHSQ) in China from 2005 to 2024. Results show that: First, RHSQ improved substantially, with an average annual growth rate of 6.10%, exhibiting a stable east-central-west gradient and gradually narrowing regional disparities. Second, rural development investment, farmers' income, rural industrial upgrading, urbanization, and rural digitalization promoted RHSQ improvement, although their marginal effects weakened over time. Rural hollowing and terrain slope constrained RHSQ, while rural population aging showed a weak positive effect overall, with declining intensity and negative effects in some regions. These drivers exhibited pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity. Third, RHSQ is projected to improve under all scenarios, with the enhanced rural revitalization scenario generating the greatest improvement. However, spatial equity remains challenging, as policy strengthening has limited capacity to reshape long-standing regional disparities. By revealing the dynamic mechanisms underlying RHSQ evolution, this study provides insights for developing more targeted and adaptive rural governance strategies to promote equitable and sustainable rural development. © 2026 The Authors
