title: The therapy room is not a classroom: Why emotional safety in therapy belongs to the client
abstract: Emotional safety in the therapy room is a clinical resource that belongs to the client. A growing number of clinicians, particularly those trained in social justice frameworks, feel empowered or obligated to correct clients' use of language deemed offensive. This paper argues that such practices are ethically indefensible and clinically counterproductive. Drawing on meta-analytic evidence on the therapeutic alliance, countertransference management, and core conditions of change, the evidence indicates that corrective responses to client language damage the alliance quality, increase the risk of premature termination, and suppress the very kind of honest disclosure that therapy requires. This paper further examines structural ideological bias in the profession, the contradictions between activist training frameworks and foundational ethics codes, and the misapplication of harm-speech theory to the clinical context. The fiduciary obligation of the therapist, the clinical evidence base, and every major professional ethics code converge on the same conclusion: the counseling room is not a classroom, and the client's psychological safety is not the therapist's to withdraw. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: CrackLite: lightweight concrete crack segmentation with direction-guided topology aggregation and local geometry refinement
abstract: Concrete crack segmentation in field inspection images remains challenging due to thin structures, weak contrast, irregular morphology, and confusing background patterns. This paper presents CrackLite, a lightweight topology-aware segmentation network for thin-crack pattern recognition. CrackLite introduces a Direction-Guided Topology Aggregation module to capture crack-oriented contextual dependencies and a Normal-Calibrated Local Geometry Refinement module to enhance local structural discrimination. A training-only auxiliary supervision scheme provides structural regularization without increasing inference-time complexity. Experiments on a self-collected Bridge Crack dataset and two public benchmarks show competitive segmentation accuracy with structure-sensitive behavior. Paired image-level analysis on Bridge Crack, zero-shot evaluation on PCHUN, and Jetson Orin NX profiling provide complementary evidence on performance differences, cross-domain transfer, and deployment efficiency under the evaluated protocols. Overall, CrackLite offers an accuracy–topology–efficiency trade-off for resource-constrained infrastructure crack segmentation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: RealTalk: Real-time audio-driven face generation with 3D prior-guided identity alignment
abstract: Person-generic audio-driven face generation remains a formidable challenge in multimedia and computer vision, primarily due to the trade-off between high-fidelity lip synchronization and real-time inference speed. Existing methods often struggle to preserve unique individual traits or suffer from high computational latency. To bridge this gap, we propose RealTalk, a novel generalized framework composed of an Audio-to-Expression Transformer and a high-fidelity Expression-to-Face Renderer. In the first stage, we introduce an improved facial prior mechanism that incorporates both 3D facial shape and historical expression data. By leveraging cross-modal attention, our model effectively captures intra-personal motion variations, ensuring precise alignment between lip movements and audio signals. In the second stage, we design a lightweight Facial Identity Alignment (FIA) module equipped with a learnable facial mask. This module achieves high-quality texture generation and identity preservation using a single reference image, bypassing the computational bottleneck of complex feature warping used in prior arts. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate that RealTalkoutperforms state-of-the-art methods in both lip-sync accuracy and visual quality while maintaining real-time efficiency (e.g., 30 FPS on a V100 GPU), making it highly suitable for practical applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Asciminib in Patients With Chronic Phase Chronic Myeloid Leukemia Previously Treated With 2 or More Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors in Colombia
abstract: Objectives To assess the cost-effectiveness of asciminib in adult patients with chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia who have been treated with 2 or more tyrosine kinase inhibitors, from a third-party payer perspective in Colombia. Methods A nonhomogeneous partitioned survival model was developed using ASCEMBL trial and matching-adjusted indirect comparisons. Outcomes included overall survival, progression-free survival, and safety. Overall survival was modeled using exponential functions based on 6-month major molecular response rates. Quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) were estimated using phase-specific utilities. Direct medical costs were obtained from national public databases (2024-2025) and expressed in 2025 USD (USD 1 = COP 4053). A 30-year time horizon was applied. Base case compared asciminib with bosutinib and ponatinib. Scenario analyses included nilotinib and dasatinib because they are rarely used in third line in Colombia. Sensitivity analyses explored ponatinib dose deescalation, generic drug pricing, asciminib price thresholds, relative dose intensity, and alternative overall survival assumptions. Probabilistic sensitivity analyses were performed. Results Asciminib was dominant compared with bosutinib and ponatinib, yielding more QALYs (0.41 and 0.20) and lower costs (−USD 47 334 and −USD 88 554). Scenario analyses including nilotinib and dasatinib favored asciminib, with higher QALYs (0.32 and 0.25) and lower costs (−USD 43 785 and −USD 6400). Results remained robust across analyses, including ponatinib dose deescalation, generic pricing, relative dose intensity, and alternative overall survival assumptions. Conclusions Asciminib was a dominant treatment option for patients with chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia who have been treated with 2 or more tyrosine kinase inhibitors, offering clinical and economic advantages over other pharmacological treatments. © 2026 The Authors.

title: A transferable methodological framework for using EIA documentation as a data source for sector-level environmental footprinting
abstract: Sector-level environmental assessment of mining is frequently constrained by the limited availability of consistent and publicly accessible operational inventory data. Although Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) documentation contains detailed engineering information on mining projects, its potential as a source of life cycle inventory (LCI) data has received little attention. This study develops and demonstrates a transferable bottom-up methodological framework that uses EIA documentation as a source of operational inventory data for sector-level environmental footprinting. The framework integrates project-level information extracted from publicly available EIA studies with official national mining statistics to estimate extraction-stage greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, land-use intensity, and water use. Croatia was selected as the demonstration case because publicly available EIA documentation can be systematically linked with official production and concession data. A total of 68 EIA studies describing 75 mining operations prepared between 2015 and 2024 were analysed. The estimated extraction-stage GHG emissions of the Croatian mining sector amount to 0.164 Mt. CO₂-eq, corresponding to approximately 2–3% of industrial GHG emissions. Construction stone and aggregates dominate total emissions because of their production volume, whereas dimension stone quarrying exhibits the highest specific GHG emissions and land-use intensity. The results further demonstrate that production scale primarily determines total environmental burdens, while extraction technology exerts a stronger influence on specific environmental intensities. Beyond the presented case study, the principal contribution of this research lies in demonstrating how publicly available regulatory documentation can be systematically transformed into operational inventory data suitable for sector-level environmental assessment. The proposed framework complements conventional LCA and national environmental inventories by improving the visibility of extraction-stage impacts and provides a transferable methodological approach for jurisdictions where comparable regulatory and statistical data are available. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Object identity in preschoolers: constraints in avoiding misidentification
abstract: This study investigated whether preschool children act on the understanding that identical-looking objects can no longer be re-identified once their positions change unnoticed, using an everyday task assessing the ability to avoid misidentification and comparing their performance with that of adults. Although children aged 4 to 7 years (N = 66) reliably and repeatedly identified which of five identical-looking nuggets was a Playmobil figure’s “favorite”, the majority (56 %) nevertheless failed to separate it when tidying up the five nuggets into two opaque bags. In contrast, all adults (N = 66) did so. The fact that the majority of children failed to separate the verbally marked nugget, despite knowing “which one it was”, indicates that they struggle to anticipate that the identity of very similar objects can be maintained only as long as identity-relevant spatial information is available, pointing to a still-developing concept of object identity. Older preschoolers tended to be more successful in separating the figure’s favorite nugget than younger ones, suggesting a developmental progression in how spatial identity criteria for objects are conceptualized. In a condition in which the figure’s favorite nugget was perceptually distinct (different color), 64 % of another group of children (N = 66) packed it separately, even though this was not necessary, indicating that their behavior was strongly driven by perceptual salience. Taken together, these findings suggest that many preschool children still struggle to use spatial criteria of identity to guide their behavior, even in a context that minimizes memory, attentional, and linguistic demands. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Physics-informed neural network for predicting high-temperature flow stress of 3Cr-1Si-1Ni ultra-high-strength steel
abstract: In this work, a first application of physics-informed neural network (PINN) to predict the high-temperature flow stress of an ultra-high strength steel is proposed, in which the accuracy, robustness and data efficiency are enhanced. Physical embedding and physical constraints are incorporated into the PINN as guiding physical principles, enabling superior generalisation ability and accuracy compared with the conventional artificial neural network (ANN) and the Johnson–Cook (J–C) model. The PINN also demonstrates significantly improved data efficiency when only small amounts of training data are available, requiring only three datasets for training. In terms of robustness, the PINN is shown to tolerate higher levels of random noise than the ANN. When the standard deviation of added random noise increases from 0 % to 10 %, the absolute prediction error of the PINN rises by only 5.5 MPa, compared with a 30.0 MPa increase for the ANN. These results demonstrate that PINNs provide a powerful framework for the development of constitutive models for metals with improved accuracy, data efficiency, and robustness. Furthermore, the proposed PINN can be extended by incorporating additional deformation-related physical constraints, offering a promising direction for constitutive modelling of metals. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

title: “How can I help you learn?” Incorporating emotions into parents' support of young children's self-regulated learning at home and school during prolonged crisis
abstract: Background: Parents apply their knowledge of cognition, emotion, and behavior (metacognition, metaemotion, and metabehavior) to provide children external regulation to achieve learning goals. Aims: Two studies examined how parents' metaprocesses shape children's self-regulated learning (SRL) strategies through external regulation (other-regulation and co-regulation) in distance and in-school learning. Study 1 Method: Mothers (N = 357) were surveyed regarding their own and their 1st–3rd graders’ SRL in three cohorts: Cohort 1 (in-school learning; pre-COVID-19); Cohort 2 (distance learning; COVID-19 first lockdown); and Cohort 3 (in-school learning; post-lockdown). Results: Mediation coefficients were estimated for parent metaprocesses associated with their children's SRL, mediated through external regulation. In distance learning, parental metaemotion, metabehavior, and co-regulation were positively associated with their children's SRL. Co-regulation was positively associated with emotion SRL-reappraisal for Cohort 2 and Cohort 3. Study 2 Method: Parents (n = 311; 49% fathers) were surveyed while their 1st-3rd grade children were in distance learning (Time 1: COVID-19 third lockdown) and in routine in-school learning (Time 2) in a repeated-measures design. Their children (n = 143) reported on social, math, and language abilities at Time 2. Results: Cross-lagged models investigated Time 1 and Time 2 associations within- and across-time effects using complex mediation models. Metaprocesses were linked to SRL, math, and language skills through other-regulation, whereas metaprocesses were associated with SRL strategies and social skills through co-regulation. Conclusion: Parent metaprocesses were positively associated with prompts guiding their children's SRL strategies and learning outcomes. Findings highlight links between metaprocesses and child emotion SRL-reappraisal through co-regulation. © 2026

title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based predictive model for prognosis in cerebral hemorrhage patients after hyperbaric oxygen therapy
abstract: (Figure presented.) Intracerebral hemorrhage is a common and critical neurological emergency, and the inconsistent results of hyperbaric oxygen therapy make predicting outcomes challenging. Therefore, a reliable predictive model for outcomes is needed to improve treatment plans. This study used interpretable machine learning to determine key risk factors linked to adverse outcomes in cerebral hemorrhage patient post-hyperbaric oxygen therapy. To improve prognostic accuracy and support clinical decision-making, we analyzed the data from 401 patients with intracerebral hemorrhage who received hyperbaric oxygen therapy at the First Affiliated Hospital of Jiaxing, China, using multivariate logistic regression and machine learning to develop predictive models, with model performance assessed via 10-fold cross-validation. SHapley Additive exPlanations values aided in model interpretation and in the development of a logistic regression-based nomogram. Based on the modified Rankin scale, patients were stratified into two prognostic groups: a good prognosis group (modified Rankin scale < 3, n = 265) and a poor prognosis group (modified Rankin scale ≥ 3, n = 136). Significant differences in various factors were observed between the groups. Independent risk factors identified included the Glasgow coma scale score, computed tomography hemorrhage volume, activities of daily living score, treatment modality, intraventricular bleeding, and rebleeding. Among the models tested, the random forest algorithm yielded the highest predictive performance (the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve = 0.99). The study identified key predictors, including activities of daily living score, computed tomography hemorrhage volume, and Glasgow coma scale score, as factors influencing hyperbaric oxygen therapy outcomes in intracerebral hemorrhage patients. Random Forest model demonstrated strong predictive capability, with SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis providing insights into individual risk factors. Overall, these findings are crucial for improving clinical decision-making and personalized treatment. © 2026 Medical Gas Research

title: Progressive resource allocation outperforms uniform strategies in enhancing urban vegetation growth offset: Evidence from DSTFormer-SHAP modeling across China's 19 urban agglomerations
abstract: Urbanization degrades vegetation through direct land conversion while simultaneously stimulating residual vegetation growth through indirect environmental modifications. The growth offset coefficient (GO), measuring the degree to which indirect enhancement compensates for direct loss, serves as a key indicator of vegetation-growth compensation capacity; however, the nonlinear response, temporal lag structures, and optimal management strategies governing GO remain poorly understood. This study develops DSTFormer, a spatiotemporal Transformer integrated with SHAP analysis, and applies it to panel data from 227 cities across China's 19 major urban agglomerations from 2001 to 2022. Results indicate that GO increased at 0.0043 yr−1, with indirect enhancement (Ind) strengthening (0.0065 yr−1) faster than direct loss (DI) deepening (−0.0021 yr−1), although the net urbanization effect on vegetation remained negative throughout the study period. SHAP attribution identified forest landscape cohesion (FLCOHESION) as the leading positive predictive factor and impervious patch number (IMNP) as the main fragmentation-related constraint associated with GO variation. Temporal lag structures differed systematically across agglomeration types: the full sample and Optimization-Upgrading Agglomerations showed stronger recent contributions, whereas Cultivation-Development Agglomerations retained stronger historical contributions. Under identical total adjustment budgets, progressive temporal allocation was associated with larger predicted GO gains than uniform allocation. Spatial clustering further identified three regulatory regimes requiring differentiated interventions: a landscape-composition and infrastructure-environment mixed regime, a connectivity-fragmentation constraint regime, and a built-environment morphology and management-environment coupling regime. These findings suggest that improving GO is associated with harnessing nonlinear leverage effects, pursuing synergistic co-optimization, and adopting temporally progressive, agglomeration-specific greening strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: HyFora: Hyperspherical representation and frustration quantification for community structure discovery in complex information networks
abstract: Complex information networks encode rich associative structural information about group organization, cross-group interactions, and information diffusion, making community structure discovery an important task in information science. However, existing methods mostly rely on Euclidean proximity or local structural features, making it difficult to balance global community separation with local relational consistency measurement. To address this issue, this paper proposes HyFora, a hyperspherical frustration-aware framework for community structure discovery in complex information networks. HyFora first constructs a background-corrected relation operator to distinguish community-relevant structural deviations from degree-driven connectivity patterns. Based on this operator, node relations are represented on the unit hypersphere, where directional consistency and angular separation jointly characterize intra-community cohesion and inter-community distinction. HyFora further quantifies the mismatch between local relations and global community organization as structural frustration, providing an interpretable consistency measure for community readout and boundary-node analysis. Experimental results show that HyFora achieves maximum relative improvements of approximately 21.2%, 27.3%, 15.4%, and 14.0% in terms of NMI, ARI, ACC, and modularity Q[jls-end-space/], respectively, while ablation, sensitivity, and node-ranking analyses verify the effectiveness and interpretability of the proposed components. The source code is publicly available at . © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: The underestimated role of effort in ability self-concept formation: Preliminary evidence for another major comparison process
abstract: Background: Early studies found that, among individuals with equal achievement, those perceived to exert less effort were rated as having greater ability (i.e. there was a negative relationship between effort and ability), leading to proposals that effort-achievement comparisons are highly influential in forming ability self-concepts. We argue that effort-achievement comparisons have been neglected in recent research due to large-scale studies failing to confirm the early findings. However, this may be because these studies have shifted their focus to a different type of effort: goal-driven effort, meaning perceived effort an individual actively chooses to invest. Aims: This study examines whether the negative relationship between effort and ability self-concepts among individuals with equal achievement can be confirmed when effort is operationalized more similarly to the earlier studies, as so-called data-driven effort, meaning perceived effort resulting from task requirements. Sample: Participants were 448 ninth-grade students from Germany. Method: Data-driven effort, achievements (school grades) and ability self-concepts in the domains of STEM and languages were assessed. We used structural equation modeling to test our hypotheses. Results: There was a strong negative relationship between data-driven effort and ability self-concepts in the two domains when controlling for achievements in the domains. Conclusions: In line with older self-concept research, these findings suggest that there is another influential comparison process, in which data-driven effort is compared with achievements, a topic that merits further investigation in future research. © 2026 The Authors

title: Mirror-Smoothing: Leveraging historical data for enhanced utility in differentially private data stream release
abstract: Data stream release enables real-time analysis across various applications but raises significant privacy concerns due to the risk of exposing sensitive user information. Although several studies leverage Differential Privacy (DP) to add noise to released statistics and protect privacy, existing methods face critical challenges, including sampling myopia, budget misallocation, and noise volatility, which degrade the utility of the released data. To address these challenges, we propose Mirror-Smoothing, a novel framework that incorporates three coordinated mechanisms: Sample-Mirror, Budget-Mirror, and Noise-Mirror. Sample-Mirror adjusts the sampling rate based on historical data, Budget-Mirror optimizes privacy budget allocation by learning from historical consumption, and Noise-Mirror generates temporally correlated noise by combining fresh and historical noise to mitigate volatility. By utilizing historical data to guide decisions on sampling, budget allocation, and noise generation, Mirror-Smoothing significantly improves data utility while ensuring rigorous privacy guarantees. Extensive experiments on both real-world and synthetic datasets show that Mirror-Smoothing achieves the best overall average performance among the compared methods across various utility metrics and privacy budgets, particularly under complex data stream patterns. These results suggest that Mirror-Smoothing is a promising solution for real-time streaming applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Barriers and innovation pathways for Europe's circular bioeconomy: grassroots stakeholder insights from 43 multi-actor workshops
abstract: The bioeconomy is a key pillar of the European Green Deal, yet its implementation remains constrained by entrenched linear value chains, fragmented logistics systems, and regulatory uncertainty. This paper examines how practitioners across Europe envision circular bioeconomy transitions, drawing on 43 harmonised multi-actor workshops conducted in 14 countries with 1078 participants from primary production, processing industries, technology provision, public authorities, and civil society. Using a structured participatory canvas and comparative thematic analysis, we analyse how stakeholders redesign existing value chains, which innovation pathways they prioritise, and which barriers they encounter in practice. Across agriculture, forestry, aquatic systems and bio-based industries, stakeholders consistently shift the focus from expanding biomass production toward better use of residues and side-streams. Dominant innovation pathways include residue valorisation, nutrient and water recycling, integrated bioenergy systems, and emerging biomaterials. Four interlinked barrier domains recur across countries and sectors: economic barriers, technological limitations, feedstock logistics and infrastructure constraints, and policy and regulatory challenges. The findings suggest that circular bioeconomy transitions are constrained less by a lack of innovation opportunities than by recurring economic, technological, infrastructural, regulatory, and knowledge-related barriers across countries and sectors. Providing one of the most extensive cross-country, practitioner-led analyses of circular bioeconomy transitions to date, the study offers insight into the conditions shaping circular bioeconomy development across Europe. The findings point to a policy agenda focused on regulatory clarification, coordinated investment in residue aggregation and pre-treatment infrastructure, while highlighting the need for complementary sustainability assessments to evaluate ecological effectiveness and broader socio-ecological implications. © 2026 The Authors. title: Complementary recommendation with abductive correction in incremental development
abstract: Complementary cloud API recommendation, which suggests APIs frequently co-invoked with a given set of APIs, plays a crucial role in enabling efficient incremental development. Existing approaches primarily model API complementarity from co-invocation behaviors but often overlook weak complementary relationships revealed through functional co-occurrence. Moreover, most methods follow a one-step paradigm, directly generating recommendations from learned relationships without further abductive refinement, thereby limiting accuracy. To address these issues, we propose a Complementary Recommendation method with Abductive Correction, named CRAC. CRAC is built on three key ideas: (1) developing a path-based modeling approach that unifies both strong complementary (from co-invocation) and weak complementary (from functional co-occurrence) relations into a unified framework; (2) introducing complementary projection and higher-order reasoning modules that capture complementary and non-substitutable relationships while enforcing complementary-but-not-substitutable constraints; (3) designing an abductive correction mechanism that refines recommendation results through abductive tasks and losses, with an over-correction strategy to ensure effective correction. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that CRAC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Further ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of weak complementarity modeling and abductive correction in enhancing complementary recommendation performance. The implementation of CRAC is publicly available on: https://github.com/lhnngp/CR_AC. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Biogas-fueled oxy-fuel power system integrated with desalination and CO2 liquefaction: 4E analysis and multi-objective optimization
abstract: This study proposes an integrated multi-generation system in which a multi-effect distillation (MED) unit is thermally coupled with a biogas-fueled oxy-fuel power plant, a transcritical CO2 cycle, and a CO2 capture and liquefaction subsystem. The system is comprehensively evaluated using thermodynamic (energy and exergy), economic (exergo-economic and net present value), and environmental (life cycle assessment-based exergo-environmental) analyses. An artificial neural network (ANNs) integrated with the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) are subsequently employed for multi-objective optimization under four scenarios: exergy–cost, exergy–environment, cost–environment, and exergy–cost–environment. The three-objective optimization yields an exergy efficiency of 50.63%, a unit product cost of 29.73 $/GJ, and a specific exergo-environmental impact of 4309 mPts/GJ. At the optimized operating conditions, the system simultaneously produces 6939 m3/h of freshwater, 21,005 kW of net electricity, and 12,327 m3/h of liquefied CO2. In addition, optimum state indicates a net present value of 265.2 M$ with a payback period of 3.4 years. The results demonstrate that integrating biogas-based energy conversion with MED desalination and CO2 capture enhances resource utilization while reducing the environmental burden of energy and freshwater production. The proposed system therefore offers a promising pathway toward low-carbon and resource-efficient multi-generation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Oxidative stress, aging, metabolism, SIRT1, and the gut microbiota: the neurocardiac basis of cognitive loss
abstract: Cardiovascular disease and cognitive loss have a neurocardiac basis. Poor vascular perfusion can impair cognitive function in both Alzheimer’s disease and multiple sclerosis. However, a treatment gap exists because current approaches do not adequately address the shared underlying cellular mechanisms responsible for cognitive dysfunction in these conditions. Current treatments for cognitive impairment in diseases such as cardiovascular disease, Alzheimer’s disease, multiple sclerosis, and diabetes often fail to fully address the shared underlying cellular mechanisms. Consequently, the prevailing precision treatment strategy, which focuses on managing symptoms and preventing disease progression, is insufficient. This highlights the urgent need for innovative approaches capable of targeting these common cellular pathways across these diverse conditions. Novel investigations into oxidative stress, cellular senescence, programmed cell death with apoptosis, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, and autophagy, cellular metabolism with apolipoprotein E and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonism, silent mating type information regulation 2 homolog 1 (Saccharomyces cerevisiae), mitochondrial dynamics, and the gut microbiome offer the potential to address the risk factors and clinical treatments for cardiovascular disease and cognitive loss. These pathways are exquisitely dependent upon one another and require in-depth knowledge of the modulatory cellular mechanisms for effective translation to clinical care. © 2026 Medical Gas Research

title: Hydrogen from pine wood waste via pyrolysis and autothermal steam reforming: technoeconomic and environmental performance of single and co-production pathways
abstract: Biomass-based hydrogen production represents a promising pathway to reduce the environmental impacts associated with fossil-based hydrogen. In thermochemical pathways, biomass is typically converted into intermediate streams such as bio-oil prior to hydrogen production. However, in bio-oil reforming processes, a key unresolved question is whether hydrogen production should prioritize complete conversion of the pyrolysis liquid or selective upgrading of its aqueous fraction, recovering the organic fraction as a fuel co-product.In this work, the implications of both alternatives at industrial scale are systematically evaluated through an integrated techno-economic and environmental assessment, comparing two process configurations for hydrogen production from pine wood waste via fast pyrolysis coupled with autothermal reforming, and benchmarking them against conventional steam methane reforming.The results show that both biomass-based scenarios can reduce climate change impacts by approximately 80% compared to steam methane reforming. However, this benefit is accompanied by higher impacts in categories such as acidification and resource use (minerals and metals) due to electricity consumption and forest management. From an economic perspective, the configuration based on complete conversion of bio-oil leads to a levelized cost of hydrogen of 5.2 €2025/kg H2, which decreases to 2.8 €2025/kg H2 when the organic fraction is co-produced as fuel for industrial heat boilers.Overall, the results demonstrate that the choice of bio-oil valorization strategy for hydrogen production constitutes a critical design variable, introducing a trade-off between hydrogen yield, economic performance and environmental impacts. The co-production strategy enhances economic robustness, while environmental differences between the two scenarios remain minor, and depend on the allocation approach and the impact category considered. © 2026 The Authors. title: Intelligent molecular design of working fluid and multi-objective optimization of system for ocean thermal energy conversion
abstract: To address the critical challenges of working fluid selection and low efficiency in ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) systems, a phased collaborative framework is proposed in this paper, integrating working fluid inverse design, intelligent variable screening, and multi-objective system optimization. First, computer-aided molecular design (CAMD) is employed to inversely identify high-efficiency, environmentally acceptable working fluids, balancing thermodynamic performance and basic safety considerations. Second, convergent cross mapping (CCM) combined with a knowledge graph is used to identify the key system variables that most significantly influence turbine power, reducing the dimensionality of the optimization problem from eight variables to four critical decision variables: evaporation temperature (Te), condensation temperature (Tc), superheat degree (Ts), and pump outlet pressure (Pp). Finally, the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) is applied to perform multi-objective optimization of exergy efficiency and levelized cost of electricity (LCOE). The results indicate that propane is the optimal working fluid, and the optimal solution achieves an exergy efficiency of 41.0% and LCOE of 0.146 $/(kWh). This framework effectively addresses the bottlenecks associated with low-temperature working fluids and high-dimensional optimization, offering a practical and efficient paradigm for the intelligent design and optimization of OTEC systems. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Hamiltonian dynamics of Boolean networks
abstract: This article examines the impact of Hamiltonian dynamics on the interaction graph of Boolean networks. Three types of dynamics are considered: maximum height, Hamiltonian cycle, and an intermediate dynamic between these two. The study addresses how these dynamics influence the connectivity of the graph and the existence of variables that depend on all other variables in the system. Additionally, a family of unate Boolean networks capable of describing these three Hamiltonian behaviors is introduced, highlighting their specific properties and limitations. The results provide theoretical tools for modeling complex systems and contribute to the understanding of dynamic interactions in Boolean networks. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: X-MCB-Net: Explainable multimodal Cyberbullying Detection Network using Swin Transformer
abstract: Cyberbullying on social media represents a persistent digital safety concern, often conveyed through the interplay of offensive text and images. Existing detection systems largely treat visual and textual modalities independently and offer limited interpretability, hindering deployment in accountable content-moderation workflows. This study presents X-MCB-Net, an explainable multimodal cyberbullying detection framework that integrates the Swin Transformer for visual feature extraction with XLM-RoBERTa and a bidirectional GRU for textual analysis. A dynamic intermodal attention mechanism fuses visual and linguistic representations to capture implicit and context-dependent cues for abuse. The core novelty lies in the joint design of adaptive cross-modal fusion and explainability-aware attribution, enabling both high detection performance and transparent decision support for human moderators. Evaluated on 5790 annotated image–text pairs from the Multimodal Cyberbullying Detection Dataset, X-MCB-Net achieved 98.8% accuracy and 96.6% F1-score under stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Explainable AI (XAI) visualizations identify the image regions and text tokens that drive each classification decision, supporting auditability and moderator trust in automated online safety systems. Future work will extend the evaluation to additional multimodal benchmarks and multilingual corpora to establish the framework’s generalizability across diverse platforms and cultural contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Performance evaluation of an ORC-based combined cooling system for data center waste heat recovery
abstract: The rapid growth of data centers has produced large amounts of low-grade waste heat, but its efficient use remains difficult. To address this problem, an HPA-ORC-VCR system was proposed to convert data center waste heat directly into useful cooling. A comprehensive framework was developed to evaluate thermodynamic, economic, and environmental performance under three server utilization conditions and 17 working fluid combinations. The results showed that lower condensing temperature, lower compressor outlet temperature, smaller intermediate heat exchanger pinch temperature difference, and higher micro-channel evaporation temperature improved overall performance. Increasing evaporation temperature increased COP all but reduced exergy efficiency. Among all working fluid combinations, R161-pentane consistently gave the best overall performance. Under low server utilization, this combination achieved the highest COP all of 1.618 at T eva = 288 K and the maximum exergy efficiency of 26.04% at T cond = 298 K, T 3 = 363 K, T mic = 358 K, and T pinch-i = 5 K. Under high utilization, it also gave the best economic and environmental performance, with a minimum payback period of 0.7118 years, a maximum annual emissions reduction of 24.720 × 105 kg, and a maximum annual fossil fuel savings of 22.038 × 104 L. These results show that the proposed HPA-ORC-VCR system has strong potential for recovering low-grade waste heat from data centers and converting it into useful cooling. The low-GWP working fluid pair R161-pentane is a promising option for sustainable waste-heat-driven cooling in data center applications. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Masson SAS.

title: Finding common and different factors in the motives underlying food choices across African and European countries
abstract: Food Choice Questionnaires (FCQs) are widely used to assess consumers' food choice motives. Most validated versions originate from WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, Democratic) countries and may not fully capture food environments in developing regions. This study applied a 39-item FCQ to urban consumers in four African countries (South Africa, Kenya, Uganda, Ethiopia) and three European countries (Norway, Finland, France) (N = 500 per country). Urban populations were targeted because they are often early adopters of dietary trends. The assumed FCQ factor structure showed low reliability across countries. To identify shared food choice motives, a two-step approach was applied. First, Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) was conducted separately in each country. Second, factor loadings were compared and clustered using the Tucker Incongruency Coefficient (TIC), enabling identification of factors with similar loading patterns across countries. Convenience and sustainability emerged as highly similar motives in all countries. Meat-related motives were also present across countries but showed greater heterogeneity in their factor structures. Emotional eating factors were identified in most countries. Gender differences were observed, with men placing greater emphasis on meat-related motives and women scoring higher on emotional eating. Despite substantial cultural and economic differences, the findings indicate the existence of shared food choice motives across low-, middle-, and high-income settings, although these motives appear to be expressed differently depending on context. The study introduces a novel methodological approach for comparing factor structures across cultures and may support the development of more context-sensitive measurement instruments, nutrition policies, and interventions tailored to diverse food environments. © 2026

title: Unequal sanitation in the Global South: infrastructure and governance shortfalls in northern Minas Gerais, Brazil
abstract: The universal provision of public utilities, such as basic sanitation, remains a critical challenge in the Global South, where infrastructure disparities and governance failures perpetuate the exclusion of vulnerable populations. This article analyses the disparities in the provision and management of water, sewerage, solid waste and drainage services in the Brazilian semi-arid region, comparing a regional hub (Montes Claros) with 19 peripheral municipalities in northern Minas Gerais. Using microdata from the National Sanitation Information System (SINISA – 2024), the study develops a matrix of institutional compliance and integrated indicators of coverage and inefficiency. The results confirm the persistence of a deep centre-periphery infrastructure divide and identify severe ‘statistical invisibility’ — characterised by an absence of official data — in localities with lower governance capacity. Furthermore, the study highlights the lack of coordination between sanitation policy areas, with a serious historical neglect of stormwater drainage and solid waste management. It is concluded that current funding metrics and the expansion of privatisation in the sector are insufficient without a regulatory framework that addresses territorial inequalities. The study provides recommendations for improving public policies, highlighting the need to review federal coordination mechanisms and subsidies to ensure water and sanitation security in peripheral regions. © 2026 The Authors. title: SR-MCUR: A scalable and robust CUR decomposition method for large-scale matrix approximation
abstract: Matrix decompositions are powerful tools for analyzing and processing large-scale data in computer vision and pattern recognition applications. In particular, CUR decompositions offer several advantages over other factorizations, such as interpretability and computational efficiency. This paper proposes a robust and scalable CUR matrix decomposition, called SR-MCUR, based on deterministic sampling of rows and columns. It addresses the main limitations of a recently developed deterministic CUR method based on the discrete empirical interpolation method (DEIM), as it does not require seeing the whole data matrix and only requires computing the singular vectors of a few observed data samples. Two versions of SR-MCUR, SR-MCUR(1) and SR-MCUR(2), are proposed based on selecting the rows and columns simultaneously and sequentially, respectively. We demonstrate that SR-MCUR(2) provides a more stable performance than the existing deterministic CUR methods and is less subject to ill-conditioning. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets are conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed methods. SR-MCUR methods dramatically outperform the existing deterministic CUR methods in terms of computational efficiency, enabling the handling of large-scale datasets on a single machine with limited computing and storage resources. Moreover, it provides a near-optimal approximation accuracy compared to deterministic CUR methods. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: A self-supervised approach to malware classification using hybrid VAE-Swin Transformer models
abstract: Malware detection and classification are critical in cybersecurity, where accurate identification of malware families enhances threat response and mitigation. Despite significant advances in malware image-based classification, challenges such as limited capture of local and global contextual dependencies, loss of spatial information, and high computational complexity continue to hinder robust malware family classification, particularly for diverse and imbalanced datasets. This paper introduces MalVEIT, a hybrid deep Variational Autoencoder (VAE) using an attention mechanism in the bottleneck of the model for malware classification under a self-supervised learning paradigm. Malware binaries are transformed into image representations, where the selected RGB formulation is adopted based on comparative evaluation against grayscale and other channel-construction alternatives. The VAE encoder then compresses these patches into a compact latent representation parameterized by learned mean and variance. Within the bottleneck layer of the VAE, shifted-window based self-attention mechanism is implemented using Swin Transformers for hierarchical feature extraction, enabling effective capture of both local structural patterns and global contextual dependencies. The refined features are sampled and reconstructed through a VAE decoder enforcing Kullback–Leibler divergence regularization to maintain a smooth distribution. The aggregated feature maps are then passed to a fully connected layer for malware family classification. The proposed model is evaluated on six benchmarked datasets, viz., Malimg, Malevis, Big-2015, Blended, Packed PE, and Obfuscation. It consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating robust multi-family malware classification across diverse datasets with data imbalance and outliers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of an age-space structured epidemic model with partial immunity, nonlinear infection rate, and combined transmission pathways from hosts and environment
abstract: To account for the complex challenges of spatial heterogeneity, inevitable human mobility, and dual transmission pathways (human-to-human and environment-to-human) in epidemic dynamics, we propose a novel age-space structured model incorporating partial immunity and nonlinear incidence. The model explicitly includes the infection age structure of both infected individuals and environmental pathogens to capture variations in infectivity during the transmission process. First, the well-posedness of the model solution is rigorously established using the Banach fixed-point theorem. Next, by applying the Laplace transform, we derive the next-generation operator L, then the basic reproduction number is defined as its spectral radius. Furthermore, under a spatially homogeneous scenario, R0 is obtained in exact analytical form. The global asymptotic stability of the disease-free and endemic steady states is then established by analyzing the distribution of the roots of the characteristic equations and constructing appropriate Lyapunov functionals. Numerical simulations visually elucidate complex spatio-temporal-age dynamics and quantify the effectiveness of interventions. In particular, restricting the mobility of infected individuals and improving vaccine efficacy significantly curb transmission. Fitting to cholera case data from Somalia, we find that neglecting either age structure or spatial heterogeneity leads to significant biases in case number estimates, underscoring their indispensable role in accurate forecasting. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Towards effective multimodal emotion recognition in conversations via joint multi-graph learning and self-distillation
abstract: Emotion Recognition in Conversation (ERC) is a crucial component of empathetic dialogue systems, enabling conversational agents to comprehend users’ expressed emotions and respond appropriately. In recent years, ERC has increasingly evolved toward multimodal approaches, particularly graph-based ones, that leverage complementary signals to enhance effectiveness. Although these approaches show promise, they face challenges in effectively modeling relational structures, computing the contribution of each modality during fusion, and regularizing unimodal representations to prevent modality bias. In this study, we propose DiGemo, a novel multimodal ERC framework that employs Transformer-based contextual modeling and graph-based learning to jointly capture both sequential dependencies within conversations and complex inter-utterance relational structures across modalities. To effectively balance and exploit multimodal information, we employ an adaptive fusion approach based on the Gated Multimodal Unit to estimate the contributions of each modality. In addition, we integrate a self-distillation training strategy to regularize unimodal representations, allowing each modality to learn from the fused multimodal representation and achieve more stable learning. DiGemo achieves Weighted F1-scores of 74.44% and 65.92% on the IEMOCAP and MELD datasets, respectively. These results validate the effectiveness of jointly modeling conversational context, cross-modal interactions, the adaptive contributions of modalities, and self-distillation for multimodal ERC. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Supply-chain transmission and shared responsibility for multi-gas footprints across Chinese urban agglomerations
abstract: Urban agglomerations connect the production, consumption, and governance of greenhouse gas emissions through interregional supply chains, yet existing studies often separate footprint accounting, emission drivers, supply-chain transmission, and responsibility sharing. This study examines 18 Chinese urban agglomerations comprising 204 cities using an integrated framework of environmentally extended multiregional input–output analysis (EE-MRIO), exact structural decomposition across all 120 factor-order permutations (SDA), structural path analysis (SPA), multi-gas emission-state diagnostics and a Shapley cooperative game. Consumption-based footprints of carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and aggregate greenhouse gases were assessed for 2012, 2015 and 2017. Per capita final demand increased emissions across all gases and periods, while the main mitigation source shifted from improvements in resource and emission intensity in 2012–2015 to changes in production structure in 2015–2017. For nitrous oxide, the −51.98% intensity effect in the earlier period was substantially offset by production restructuring and an expansion in final demand. Supply-chain pathways were gas-specific: carbon dioxide and aggregate greenhouse gases were transmitted mainly through electricity–industry–investment chains, whereas methane and nitrous oxide were more closely associated with agriculture, fuel exploitation and waste treatment. In 2017, eastern final demand induced 22.7–36.6% of the corresponding source-side footprints in western China, with the highest share for methane. Strong inter-gas coupling did not necessarily imply coordinated mitigation. Under the baseline Shapley allocation, five leading agglomerations accounted for 50.66% of total responsibility, while cross-scenario tests identified a stable four-agglomeration core and a policy-sensitive boundary. These findings support a differentiated, gas-specific and adaptive framework for shared supply-chain responsibility. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Does prediction error explain referential adaptation?
abstract: Pronoun resolution is guided by various discourse cues. For instance, ambiguous pronouns are often assigned to the subject of the preceding sentence (e.g., Ana went shopping with Liz. She bought a hat). Studies have found that these discourse biases can be learned through exposure by tracking frequent pronoun-reference patterns (e.g., pronouns often refer to subjects), a process known as referential adaptation (e.g., Johnson and Arnold, 2023 ; Kaiser, 2009 ; Ye and Arnold, 2023b). Yet, the mechanisms underlying this learning remain unclear. Two experiments examined whether referential adaptation is driven by prediction error, which has been suggested to explain syntactic adaptation (e.g., Chang et al., 2012). This account predicts that learning depends on how surprising the input is, with more unexpected input leading to stronger adaptation. We tested this prediction by exposing people to discourse patterns within both contexts where the reference was highly expected (Exp. 1) and equi-biased (Exp. 2). Robust referential adaptation occurred in both experiments. These findings show that strong expectation violations are not necessary for referential adaptation and suggest that adaptation is not straightforwardly determined by the strength or consistency of prediction error. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.
label: Social Sciences

title: EPIPTrack: Rethinking prompt modeling with explicit and implicit prompts for multi-object tracking
abstract: Multimodal semantic cues, such as textual descriptions, have shown strong potential in enhancing target perception for tracking. However, existing methods rely on static textual descriptions from large language models, which lack adaptability to real-time target state changes and prone to hallucinations. To address these challenges, we propose a unified multimodal vision-language tracking framework, which leverages explicit and implicit prompts for dynamic target modeling and semantic alignment. Specifically, explicit prompts transform spatial motion information into natural language descriptions to provide spatiotemporal guidance. Implicit prompts combine pseudo-words with learnable descriptors to construct individualized knowledge representations capturing identity-related semantic attributes. Both prompts are dynamically adjusted through a pretrained vision-language text encoder to respond to changes in target states. Furthermore, we design a Discriminative Feature Augmentor to enhance visual and cross-modal representations. Extensive experiments on three public multi-object tracking benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms existing trackers across diverse scenarios, exhibiting robust adaptability and superior performance. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Stage-specific expression and localization of ETRAMP4 during gametocyte development in the malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum
abstract: The early transcribed membrane protein 4 (ETRAMP4) is one of 14 predicted members of the ETRAMP family in the malaria parasite Plasmodium . All characterized ETRAMP proteins localize to the parasitophorous vacuole membrane (PVM) and associated membranous structures during the early stages of parasite infection of erythrocytes; and are thought to participate in host-parasite material transport, which is critical for parasite development. In this study, we investigated the stage-specific expression and subcellular localization of ETRAMP4 during the asexual and gametocyte intraerythrocytic stages. Indirect immunofluorescence assays revealed that ETRAMP4 is prominently detected in immature stage I and II gametocytes; whereas no detectable signal was observed in stage III to V gametocytes or in asexual blood-stage parasites under our experimental conditions. Immunoelectron microscopy demonstrated that ETRAMP4 predominantly localizes to the PVM and PVM-derived membranous structures extending into the host erythrocyte cytoplasm, suggesting a potential role in membrane dynamics during early gametocyte development. title: Impact of distributor zone design on flow uniformity in metal foam cooling flow fields of PEMFC
abstract: In a proton exchange membrane fuel cell, the distributor zone of a metal foam cooling flow field directly affects coolant distribution among the cooling branches and the resulting temperature uniformity. Based on the optimized structural parameters of the main metal foam cooling flow field, a three-dimensional numerical model incorporating the core components of a single cell and the distributor zone was developed. This study systematically investigated how three key design parameters, namely distributor zone shape, circular hole diameter, and number of circular holes, regulate coolant flow uniformity. The circular structure was retained as the baseline configuration because of its favorable thermal characteristics and geometric adjustability. The results showed that the optimal circular hole diameter was 1.5 mm, yielding an average mass flow deviation of 26.05 %. With this diameter fixed, the configuration with 14 circular holes exhibited the lowest average mass flow deviation and coefficient of variation among the examined cases, at 17.93 % and 27.26 %, respectively, thereby achieving the best trade-off between flow uniformity and hydraulic resistance. This study clarifies how the structural parameters of the distributor zone regulate coolant distribution and provides key technical support for the integrated design and performance optimization of cooling systems at the stack level. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: The social implications of classroom seats: replicating and extending previous findings on seating arrangements and peer status
abstract: This preregistered replication study examined how physical proximity in the classroom is associated with peer perceptions of social status, specifically likeability and popularity. We aimed to replicate and extend the study by van den Berg and Cillessen (2015) using data from 719 students across 33 elementary classrooms (grades 4–6; Mage = 10.27; 51.6% boys). We applied the Social Relations Model and mixed-effects modeling to examine (1) whether proximity between classmates is concurrently associated with likeability and popularity, (2) whether longitudinal changes in proximity lead to changes in likeability and popularity, (3) whether these findings differ for friends versus non-friends, and (4) whether they depend on how proximity is operationalized. We replicated previous findings by showing that classmates seated closer together concurrently rated each other as more popular and likeable. Furthermore, when given the opportunity to create their own seating arrangements, students placed classmates they found likeable and popular closer to themselves. We extended previous findings by showing that increased proximity between two classmates over time led to an increase in mutual liking, but not perceived popularity. Further, findings did not differ significantly between friends and non-friends. Finally, because extant studies differ in how proximity is measured, we tested an operationalization of proximity in terms of desk clusters. This alternative operationalization produced similar results to its continuous counterpart, highlighting the conceptual and practical value of the current operationalization for future research. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Translating human values into requirements
abstract: Values influence the needs of stakeholders, they can directly affect requirements or can be unconscious desires for system behavior. Stakeholders have individual conceptions of values such as sustainability, fairness, or privacy. This clash leads to misunderstandings. In this paper, we explore the practical application of a recently published software process for eliciting human values from stakeholders and translating them into requirements. To avoid misunderstandings regarding the definition of values, this process uses Schwartz's theory of basic human values. However, this value-based process had not been practically applied. We applied this process to the development of a group allocation system for capstone projects. We used surveys, interviews, and a workshop to elicit the relevant human values from two stakeholder groups: students and project organizers. Sets of human values were bundled into personas and prioritized by stakeholders of both groups in a follow-up workshop. Our own experience during the process and statistical analyses of the results revealed that not all elicitation techniques are equally suitable for determining the human values of end-users. The participants’ feedback was mostly positive. Based on our experience, we provide multiple recommendations regarding aspects that should be considered during the value-based requirements elicitation process. We explored the process's applicability in practice and refined the value-based software development process. © 2026

title: GLAM: Unifying global–local graph geometry via asymmetric mutual learning
abstract: Real-world graphs exhibit both global homogeneity and rich local heterogeneity. Existing graph neural networks (GNNs) typically embed nodes into a single constant-curvature space, such as Euclidean or hyperbolic, ignoring geometric diversity and lacking sufficient modeling capacity for mixed structures. Although some works employ product or pseudo-Riemannian manifolds, these spaces remain homogeneous and cannot adapt to local geometric variations. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel Global–Local Asymmetric Mutual Learning Graph Neural Network (GLAM), comprising a local heterogeneous model (LeGNN), a global homogeneous model (GoGNN), and an asymmetric mutual learning module (AMLM). At the local level, LeGNN dynamically assigns each node a learnable constant-curvature Riemannian manifold via inter-layer smoothing constraints and achieves personalized modeling of microscopic topological patterns. At the global level, GoGNN efficiently utilizes a homogeneous manifold to characterize macroscopic structural patterns, providing a consistent topological view for the overall framework. Finally, AMLM performs a complementary fusion of geometric representations across multiple scales. Experiments on multiple benchmarks for node classification and link prediction show that GLAM performs competitively across both tasks, while exhibiting more pronounced advantages on link prediction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Multimodal fusion for precision livestock behavior monitoring: A systematic review of deep learning, pose estimation, and sensor integration strategies
abstract: Animal behavior analysis is a cornerstone of precision livestock farming, providing non-invasive insights into health, welfare, and productivity through continuous behavioral monitoring. Traditional approaches, including manual observation, sensor-based systems, and rule-based modeling, are limited by labor intensity, observer subjectivity, and low temporal resolution. This systematic review (PRISMA 2020; 2020-2026 literature) presents a comprehensive synthesis of deep learning and multimodal artificial intelligence approaches for animal behavior recognition in precision agriculture. Deep learning architectures, including convolutional, recurrent, and transformer-based models, achieve reported accuracies of 85-99% across livestock species, with transformer-based models reaching a mean of 94.4% (95% CI: 91.96-96.76%). Critically, multimodal fusion systems demonstrate a mean accuracy gain of 10.3 percentage points over single-modality baselines in an exploratory analysis of four independent source-level comparisons (95% CI: 4.9-15.8%; paired t(3) = 6.01, p = 0.009, Cohen’s d = 3.01), with peak detection sensitivities exceeding 90% for health-critical conditions, including lameness and metabolic disorders. This review evaluates early, late, and hybrid fusion strategies; the role of pose estimation in fine-grained movement analysis (with 94-100% accuracy in lameness detection); and the contribution of wearable and environmental sensors to continuous monitoring. Explainable AI methods are assessed for their role in improving model transparency and stakeholder trust. Key challenges, including data scarcity, annotation heterogeneity, multimodal synchronization, and limited cross-domain generalization, are critically discussed, along with six directions for future research. This review uniquely positions adaptive multimodal fusion as the central paradigm for next-generation, deployable precision livestock behavior monitoring systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: ACOPI-QGen: Implicitness-aware joint quintuple extraction for aspect-based sentiment analysis via contrastive and graph-based modeling
abstract: In social media and online reviews, sentiments are often expressed implicitly through contextual, figurative, or indirect language, making them difficult to capture using traditional Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) techniques. Many prior studies on ABSA treat implicit aspects and opinions as auxiliary cases or evaluation subsets, limiting their role during learning. To address this limitation, we propose ACOPI-QGen, a joint structured framework that extracts a five-element sentiment quintuple (Aspect Term, Aspect Category, Opinion Term, Polarity, Implicitness). Rather than treating implicitness as a post-hoc attribute, we model it as a supervised four-class variable: EAEO, EAIO, IAEO, and IAIO, where A/O denote aspect/opinion and E/I denote explicit/implicit realization. The proposed framework combines BERT-based contextual encoding, Supervised Contrastive Implicit Learning, and a Relational Graph Attention Network guided by a Surrogate Aspect-Opinion Dependency Tree to support implicit sentiment modeling when aspect or opinion spans are missing. A non-autoregressive set decoder uses parallel tuple queries to predict multiple candidate sentiment quintuples while preserving aspect-opinion alignment. We curate three datasets for quintuple extraction (Restaurant-ACOPI: 2584; Laptop-ACOPI: 4376; and Shoes-ACOPI: 3896 instances). ACOPI-QGen achieves Exact Match F1 scores of 55.68, 48.43, and 60.49 on Restaurant-ACOPI, Laptop-ACOPI, and Shoes-ACOPI, respectively, with corresponding improvements of 2.92, 2.53, and 5.45 absolute F1 points over the best-performing state-of-the-art models across the three domains. These results show that explicit modeling of implicitness improves joint quintuple extraction in implicit sentiment settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Multi-Level collaborative optimization for Multi-Modal media manipulation detection and grounding
abstract: The proliferation of manipulated multi-modal content threatens the credibility of social media. Although existing detecting and grounding multi-modal media manipulation (DGM4) methods exploit image-text complementarity, they optimize classification and localization largely independently, overlooking structured collaboration between the two tasks. To address this limitation, we propose a multi-level task collaboration (MLTC) framework that progressively promotes detection and grounding interaction at the feature, semantic, and decision levels. At the feature level, cross-modal alignment and interaction construct modality-specific bridge representations, enabling classification and grounding within each modality to reason over a shared multi-modal evidence space. At the semantic level, the proposed cross-granularity semantic fusion (CGSF) module learns shared semantic importance weights to coordinate global classification semantics and local grounding evidence, encouraging consistent manipulation-aware evidence selection across different granularities. At the decision level, focusing on the dense spatial nature of visual grounding, we introduce cross-granularity decision fusion (CGDF), which integrates image-level manipulation confidence and patch-level localization responses to produce a manipulation probability map (MPM). The manipulation-aware grounding refinement (MAGR) module further introduces the MPM as a bounded soft prior during query-based evidence aggregation, strengthening manipulation-relevant patch contributions while preserving the baseline visual evidence for robust bounding-box prediction. On the entire DGM4 test set, MLTC achieves an AUC of 94.94%, a multi-label mAP of 90.72%, an image-grounding IoUmean of 79.63%, and a token-grounding F1 score of 76.85%. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Study on the effects of ditching behavior on emergency evacuation behavior in large civil aircraft
abstract: Large civil aircraft ditching evacuations face operational uncertainties driven by unquantified interactions between dynamic fluid environments and passenger behaviors. To investigate these mechanisms, an extended cellular automata model was developed using an A320neocase study, integrating aircraft floating attitude, leakage, passenger dimensions, anxiety, and overtaking behaviors. Simulations evaluated varying wave conditions, pitch angles, and passenger compliance. Results indicate high-frequency, short waves amplify pitch disturbances, increasing evacuation time to calm water. Initial fuselage pitch angle exerts a non-linear effect on efficiency, as large angles induce aisle congestion due to gravity and friction. Additionally, non-compliant behaviors (luggage retrieval, premature life jacket inflation) generate negative synergistic effects: at a 50% overlap probability, the model yields a 47.3% reduction in average cabin movement speed. Under leakage scenarios, an improved Tanimoto-EW-TOPSIS model demonstrates that a door selection strategy, reconfiguring routes only upon substantial exit failure, optimizes system adaptability by controlling evacuation time, exit density, stagnation frequency, and water-exposure time. This research provides quantitative references regarding multidimensional environmental constraints and human factors for aircraft airworthiness verification. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: On flat production surfaces associated with Cobb-Douglas-type production models exhibiting variable returns to scale
abstract: We prove that the flatness of the production surface associated with a Cobb–Douglas-type production model exhibiting variable returns to scale forces the local return-to-scale index to be constant, thereby establishing a rigidity result for this class of production functions. Consequently, every flat production model in this class is homogeneous, and its local classification follows directly from the classification theorem established in [8] . This demonstrates a remarkable phenomenon: the flatness condition completely suppresses the variability of the local return-to-scale index. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: A bladder microenvironment-adaptive ceria nanozyme hydrogel enables urea-responsive intravesical chemo-immunotherapy
abstract: Bladder cancer intravesical therapy remains limited by rapid urinary washout, insufficient penetration across the bladder mucosal barrier, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Here, we developed a bladder microenvironment-adaptive chemo-immunotherapy system, Gel/UCeNZ/Gem/CpG, to improve local bladder cancer treatment. In this system, urease-modified CeO2 nanozymes (UCeNZ), gemcitabine (Gem), and CpG oligodeoxynucleotide (CpG ODN) were incorporated into an injectable thermosensitive adhesive hydrogel. After intravesical administration, the hydrogel rapidly formed a mucosa-adherent depot, thereby prolonging bladder residence and enabling sustained therapeutic release. Meanwhile, UCeNZ responded to endogenous urinary urea to enhance particle transport and mucosal penetration, improving local drug exposure beyond passive instillation. Functionally, CeO2-mediated redox regulation amplified Gem-induced oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, apoptosis, and immunogenic cell death-associated signaling, as evidenced by HMGB1 translocation/release, calreticulin exposure, and intracellular ATP dysregulation. CpG ODN further promoted dendritic cell maturation and strengthened T cell-mediated antitumor immunity. In an orthotopic bladder cancer model, Gel/UCeNZ/Gem/CpG significantly suppressed tumor progression, prolonged survival, increased CD8+ T cell infiltration, reduced regulatory T cells and M2-like macrophages, and enhanced memory/effector-like T cell activation without obvious systemic toxicity. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed coordinated regulation of oxidative stress, apoptosis, antigen presentation, cytokine signaling, T cell activation, PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint signaling, and p53-related tumor-suppressive pathways. Overall, this study presents a bladder-adaptive intravesical chemo-immunotherapy strategy that integrates mucosal retention, urea-responsive penetration, redox-amplified immunogenic chemotherapy, and immune microenvironment remodeling for bladder cancer treatment. © 2026 The Authors. title: Robust optimization of emergency evacuation and supply allocation considering personnel demand heterogeneity and temporary shelters
abstract: In emergency management, it is crucial to promptly evacuate affected people to shelters and allocate medical supply efficiently. Typically, these people have heterogeneous medical supply needs, with injured people requiring more medical supplies than uninjured ones. Additionally, their demand for medical supplies increases with evacuation time, which presents a significant challenge in emergency management. To address this, this paper proposes the novel idea of establishing temporary shelters to ensure the rapid evacuation of injured people and alleviate the resource burden. Considering the uncertainty in the proportion of injured people, we employ a robust optimization approach to jointly optimize emergency evacuation, supply allocation, and the establishment of temporary shelters. We then formulate a robust counterpart model and design a customized Benders decomposition algorithm to efficiently solve the model. For large-scale instances, we further incorporate a Branch-and-Cut procedure into the Benders decomposition framework to accelerate the solution process. Finally, we test our methodology using both a virtual example experiment and a Houston-based case, demonstrating the high performance of the designed algorithm and the advantages of establishing temporary shelters in reducing overall evacuation time and mitigating medical supply shortages. Based on these numerical results, we provide several valuable managerial insights for real-world applications. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: A systematic method for designing aging-resilient nuclear balance-of-plant systems: Theoretical foundations
abstract: Maintaining service continuity is a fundamental requirement for nuclear plants, especially when supplying industrial heat users without access to a buffering thermal network. In such settings, gradual performance losses in balance-of-plant components can translate directly into curtailed thermal and electric delivery. This paper introduces PRIORITY (Probabilistic Ranking for Improving Operational Reliability through degradatIon-aware miTigation strategY selection), a computationally lightweight, design-stage framework that (i) identifies which component degradations most strongly limit productive capacity and (ii) ranks candidate mitigation portfolios (e.g., redundancy, oversizing, bypasses, dedicated control schemes). Long-horizon degradation trajectories are replaced by an ergodic Monte Carlo formulation in which multi-component health states are sampled from bounded distributions informed by Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), defined over the admissible range between nominal performance and the maintenance threshold. For each sampled state, a steady-state performance model evaluates a degraded power-capacity metric combining delivered process heat and net electric output expressed in thermal-equivalent units. Because all design variants are evaluated on the same set of sampled states, their performance distributions can be compared using probability of outperformance and synthesized into a global ranking (Bradley–Terry). The framework makes modeling assumptions explicit (stationarity, approximate independence, exclusion of common-cause effects) and outlines extensions to dependent degradations and cost-aware selection. A companion paper applies PRIORITY to a representative cogeneration configuration and quantifies the value of specific mitigation portfolios. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Design, development, and evaluation of STI Shield: A multi-chatbot mobile application for sexual health education and behavior change in African young adults
abstract: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) remain a significant public health concern among African young adults, driven by limited knowledge, high-risk behaviors, stigma, and inadequate access to care. While mobile health (mHealth) interventions offer potential, many existing tools lack cultural relevance, theoretical grounding, and adaptability. This study presents STI Shield, a multi-chatbot mobile application designed to enhance STI awareness and encourage safer sexual behaviors. The app integrates rule-based and large language model (LLM)-based chatbots to deliver structured education and personalized counseling, drawing on the Health Belief Model and Persuasive System Design principles. A two-phase evaluation involving African participants living both in Africa and outside Africa, comprising pilot and in-the-wild studies, demonstrated high usability and acceptability, strong educational impact, high persuasiveness, and positive shifts in key behavior change determinants. This work contributes to the fields of mHealth, conversational artificial intelligence, and human-computer interaction by offering a novel chatbot-based system model for delivering personalized, culturally relevant, and theory-driven digital health support in under-resourced settings. © 2026 The Author(s).
