title: Strict phonics instruction outperforms mixed phonics: Evidence from a large-scale study
abstract: Background: Learning to read is a foundational milestone in formal education, and a large body of research supports the effectiveness of systematic phonics instruction in early literacy development. However, much less is known about whether different implementations of phonics instruction influence children's reading outcomes. This study investigates whether variation within phonics-based instruction—specifically, strict versus mixed phonics approaches—is associated with differences in early reading development. Methods: We combine survey data from more than 9000 first-grade teachers with longitudinal assessment data for over 139,000 pupils in France. Teachers were classified according to the instructional approaches they reported using and the characteristics of the reading materials employed in their classrooms. Pupils’ reading fluency and reading comprehension were measured using nationally administered standardized assessments conducted during Grade 1 and at the beginning of Grade 2. Results: Multilevel analyses showed that pupils taught using strict phonics approaches achieved higher reading fluency and reading comprehension than those taught with mixed phonics approaches, with differences corresponding to approximately 0.11–0.16 standard deviations. These effects were substantially larger among pupils with weaker pre-reading skills and those attending socioeconomically disadvantaged schools. The findings remained robust across multiple complementary analyses designed to address potential selection effects and omitted-variable bias. Conclusion: The findings demonstrate that meaningful differences in reading outcomes may arise not only from whether systematic phonics instruction is provided, but also from how it is implemented. They further suggest that optimizing the coherence of early phonics instruction may be particularly beneficial for pupils most at risk of reading difficulties. © 2026 The Authors

title: Dependence of high-temperature plastic deformation of fine-grained Y2O3 on the electric power density
abstract: High-temperature plastic deformation behavior of two-step sintered, fine-grained Y2O3 polycrystals was examined under various direct current (DC) electric fields/currents. High-temperature flexural tests in the fine-grained Y2O3 body with an average grain size of 0.47 µm were conducted under DC electric fields of 0–1000 V·cm−1 and current density of 0–15 mA·mm−2 at 1000℃–1400℃ and strain rates of 2.4 × 10−5–1.0 × 10−4 s−1. Flash events, characterized by a rapid increase in specimen temperature and electric conductivity, were triggered by initial power inputs greater than ~30 mW·mm−3. Deformation of Y2O3 was athermally promoted by DC electric fields, with a maximum stress reduction of 36%, even when subtracting the thermal effect caused by Joule heating. In particular, the activation energy of the high-temperature plastic flow gradually decreased with increasing steady-state power density, which was amplified under a flash event and reached up to 225 mW·mm−3. Thus, the electric power density is likely a key factor in determining the plastic flow behavior in fine-grained Y2O3 assisted by electric field/currents. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Digital echoes of death and dying distress among family members of intensive care unit patients: A qualitative study
abstract: Objectives: To explore how ICU family members experience and articulate death and dying distress through social media narratives. Methods: This study employed a qualitative design informed by the socioecological model and a constructivist epistemological perspective. Data were drawn from publicly available posts on REDnote (also known as Xiaohongshu), a popular Chinese social media platform, using a keyword-based search targeting ICU-related experiences. After screening for relevance, 317 posts comprising 124,906 Chinese characters were retained for analysis. Reflexive thematic analysis was conducted following Braun and Clarke's six-phase approach, emphasizing researchers' active role in co-constructing themes through iterative engagement with the data. Results: Eight themes were identified across three socioecological levels: at the microsystem, emotional volatility and multi-dimensional distress reflected intense emotional experiences and endurance; at the mesosystem, shared burdens, concentrated family responsibilities, and support beyond blood ties captured family dynamics under strain; at the macrosystem, digital spaces, institutional barriers, and financial pressures shaped broader sociocultural experiences of death and dying distress. Conclusion: This study provides new insights into the distress of ICU family members facing death and dying. It highlights that such distress is not solely an individual psychological reaction, but an experience of endurance shaped by family relationships and broader social and institutional contexts. Implications for clinical practice: These findings suggest that nursing interventions could adopt a systems-oriented approach to support family functioning, address relational and institutional challenges, and extend support beyond the bedside to include digital spaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Training emotion regulation in Preschoolers: Preliminary evaluation of a Researcher–Teacher co-constructed program aligned with usual classroom practices
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of a research-based, innovative training program targeting emotion regulation in preschool children. The program was co-constructed with teachers to ensure its integration into everyday classroom practices. Its effectiveness was evaluated using tasks assessing emotion comprehension, recognition, and identification, as well as Theory of Mind and emotion regulation (ERC-vf checklist; Nader-Grosbois, 2014, completed by teachers). The results indicated improvements in teacher-rated emotion regulation and reductions in teacher-rated emotion dysregulation associated with the intervention, as well as gains in the identification of emotional intensity (particularly at the highest levels). Across these domains, pre- to posttest gains were greater in the Intervention group than in the Non-Intervention group, with differences in emotion regulation and dysregulation between groups emerging only among older children (5–6 years) in the classroom-adjusted analysis, although the effect for emotion regulation was at the threshold of statistical significance. The potential role of emotion regulation in supporting emotional and non-emotional competencies is discussed. These findings might prompt new ideas and initiatives in the design of future educational programs. © 2026 .

title: Neural-network learning and identifiability for mobility-based SEAIR epidemic models
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a mobility-based SEAIR epidemic model that addresses two limitations of existing heterogeneous compartmental models: the neglect of pre-symptomatic transmission, and the absence of symptom-driven mobility reduction. Classical models assume homogeneous mixing and a single infectious stage, which ignores individual heterogeneity in contact behavior and causes systematic overestimation of outbreak size; both shortcomings were consequential during COVID-19. Each individual carries a fixed mobility trait governing their contact rate; the infectious period is split into an asymptomatic stage and a symptomatic stage with reduced mobility. We establish four main results: a closed-form basic reproduction number whose entire stage structure collapses into a single effective infectiousness parameter (with latency dropping out entirely); strict selective depletion of high-mobility susceptibles and stage-dependent differences in infected mobility distributions; a scalar final-size equation together with a unique seed-selected branch that satisfies the shielding inequality of [1]; and unique identifiability of the mobility distribution from the aggregate symptomatic time series, with a length-two Taylor delay relative to the SIR case reflecting the additional latent and asymptomatic stages. Numerical experiments illustrate the analytic results and show how pre-symptomatic transmission, isolation, and mobility heterogeneity affect synthetic epidemic trajectories. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Molecular detection of Paenibacillus larvae, Melissococcus plutonius and Vairimorpha spp., in historical honey samples from South Brazil
abstract: Honey bee colonies are threatened by several pathogens, including Paenibacillus larvae , Melissococcus plutonius , Vairimorpha apis , and Vairimorpha ceranae . Those infections affect bee health, survival, and productivity. The social behavior of the bees facilitates the spread of these pathogens, making disease management a significant challenge in apiculture. This study aimed to assess the historical presence of Paenibacillus larvae , Melissococcus plutonius , Vairimorpha apis , and Vairimorpha ceranae in honey samples from Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. A total of 125 archival honey samples collected from 2011 to 2022 were retrospectively evaluated. The samples had previously been analyzed for physicochemical and botanical origins. DNA was extracted from honey and spores, followed by PCR assays targeting the four pathogens. Sequencing was performed to confirm the results. M. plutonius was the most frequently detected pathogen, identified in 112 samples (89.6%), followed by V. ceranae , which was present in 67 samples (53.6%). In contrast, P. larvae were identified in only six samples (8.8%), and V . apis was absent. The high detection rate of M. plutonius suggests its widespread distribution in South Brazilian apiaries. The absence of V . apis suggests that V . ceranae has displaced this specie in the region. The presence of P. larvae spores emphasizes its resilience through the ability to persist for extended periods in the environment. Additionally, the simultaneous detection of multiple pathogens raises the concern for synergic effects or interactions, which could further increase colony losses. Finally, these findings highlight the importance of continuous surveillance and enhanced biosecurity and prophylactic strategies, altogether essential for honey bee health and productivity. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Multi-behavior popularity-aware recommendation
abstract: Recommender systems (RSs) face a persistent challenge known as popularity bias, which is characterized by the systematic over-recommendation of popular items and under-recommendation of long-tail or new items. This issue has been addressed in existing single-behavior recommendations, which mainly focus on mitigating popularity bias in the final interaction (such as purchasing). Multiple behaviors of users typically exhibit sequential dependencies across multiple stages (e.g., browsing → adding to cart → purchasing). However, existing multi-behavior recommendations fail to sufficiently leverage these relationships to effectively address popularity bias. In this paper, we propose a multi-behavior popularity-aware recommendation to alleviate the above problem. We explore the role of user sequential behavioral relationships in alleviating popularity bias from two perspectives: items and users. From the perspective of items, we redefine popularity under multi-behavior. We calculate the item popularity by counting the number of user-item interactions, such as browsing, adding to cart, and purchasing. From the user’s perspective, we calculate the user’s attention to the item popularity and divide all users into conservatives and trend-followers by their attention. Subsequently, we design a popularity-matching loss to influence the recommendation probability. It represents the matching degree between the two kinds of followers’ preferences and the popularity of the target item. Finally, we rank the probabilities of all target items and provide a recommendation list for the user. Experimental results on five well-known datasets indicate that compared with twenty-four state-of-the-art models, the proposed model is superior in terms of NDCG, Recall, and APT. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: The health effects of genetically modified crops
abstract: Public debates on genetically modified (GM) crops center on environmental and health risks, yet evidence remains limited and focuses largely on herbicide-tolerant varieties or on local exposure, leaving the broad consequences of insect-resistant crops unclear. Insect-resistant crops can reduce pesticide use and generate health effects beyond directly exposed farmers. Yet their net effects are ambiguous, as any environmental gains may be offset by crop substitution, pest resistance, industrial expansion, and land-use change. We exploit the staggered approval of Bt cotton across China, combined with river networks that link cotton-growing areas to downstream residents. Bt cotton approval leads to significant downstream reductions in under-five mortality by 4.2%, driven by reduced pesticide use and improved water quality. In aggregate, Bt cotton approval reduces national pesticide use by 3.2%. The findings show that the social value of insect-resistant GM crops can be significantly underestimated, as they generate positive health externalities through environmental spillovers. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: “Triggering autonomy, not just automation”: Design implications for LLM-based home automation assistants for people with intellectual disability
abstract: Smart home technologies offer considerable potential to enhance autonomy, safety, and quality of life for individuals with intellectual disabilities (ID). Yet, configuring and personalizing such systems remain challenging due to complex interfaces and the technical expertise required. Traditionally, End-User Development (EUD) is often proposed as a way for non-experts to autonomously configure home devices. This work investigates the extent to which Large Language Models (LLMs) can provide effective support to people with ID in applying EUD. It explores whether an LLM-powered conversational interface can support individuals with ID in shaping smart home behaviors through natural conversations. Insights from exploratory sessions involving users with ID, caregivers, and stakeholders demonstrate a positive attitude towards this approach and suggest that conversational interaction can foster accessibility of automation programming through iterative clarifications. We conclude by outlining design opportunities and broader implications that can inform future research towards LLM-based EUD interfaces for people with ID. © 2026 The Author(s). title: A system dynamics model for sugarcane-based alcohol-to-jet sustainable aviation fuel supply chains
abstract: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is a key pathway for decarbonizing aviation, but its deployment depends on integrating supply-chain, economic, and policy conditions. This study develops a generalized system dynamics model of a sugarcane alcohol-to-jet (ATJ) supply chain and demonstrates its application using Ecuador as a case study. The model integrates four subsystems: upstream (land allocation, sugar and ethanol production), midstream (ethanol allocation and ATJ conversion), downstream (SAF blending with fossil jet fuel and use), and finance (economic viability). Under baseline conditions, SAF production reaches 50 million liters, corresponding to a blend ratio of 9.7% at a minimum selling price (SAF MSP) of 1.8 USD/L. Sensitivity analysis identified sugarcane yield as the main production driver, while uncertainty analysis also identified ethanol price as the dominant driver of SAF MSP. Policy scenarios showed that stacked interventions, including ethanol price support and an incentive for SAF producers, improved financial viability. Monetizing the avoided emissions from SAF use could accelerate plant deployment, but only at carbon prices well above current levels. Alternative construction paradigms mainly reduced fixed capital investment (FCI), with limited direct effect on SAF MSP, although combining co-location with policy support increased the number of SAF plants that could potentially be deployed and reduced the time required to reach a positive net present value (NPV). The Ecuadorian case study results show that feedstock availability alone is insufficient to enable SAF industry growth, and project economics remain the main limiting factor. The model provides a dynamic framework for evaluating how ATJ industries may evolve under different structural and policy conditions. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Event-centric human value understanding in news-domain texts: An actor-conditioned benchmark across multi-scope event contexts
abstract: This work presents NEVU, a benchmark for actor-conditioned, event-centric, and direction-aware human value recognition in news-domain texts. NEVU evaluates whether models can infer values from event-structured evidence, attribute them to the correct social actors, and determine their aligned or contradictory direction. Built from 2865 English news articles, NEVU represents news at four semantic levels, from subevents to composite events and full articles. Using a hierarchical taxonomy of 54 fine-grained and 20 coarse-grained values, the benchmark contains 46,589 semantic units, 72,905 annotated unit–actor pairs, and 168,061 directed value instances. NEVU is constructed through a staged LLM-assisted annotation and verification pipeline, with targeted human verification for unresolved cases. Candidate-level acceptance and agreement are further examined through a multi-group assessment. The experiments show that prompting-only models remain limited, whereas LoRA-tuned open-weight models substantially improve performance, with overall Micro-F1 gains of 29.77 and 8.21 percentage points over the strongest prompting-only open-weight and proprietary baselines, respectively. These gains primarily reflect learnability under the NEVU reference-label setting. NEVU provides a structured benchmark for systematic evaluation and supervised adaptation of actor-conditioned human value recognition in English news. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: Decentralized anaerobic digestion in emerging Indian cities: A systems perspective on urban waste management, bioenergy recovery, and circular economy transitions
abstract: Rapid urbanization in emerging Indian urban cities is increasing the pressure on municipal solid waste management. This review evaluates anaerobic digestion as an integrated option for urban organic waste management, renewable energy recovery, and circular economy development. A structured narrative review was used to assess feedstock characteristics, digester configurations, operating conditions, and biogas uses. Policy support and reforms are discussed, followed by techno-economic evaluation of decentralized anaerobic digestion, along with opportunities to diversify income through bio-CNG, electricity, and bio-fertilizer production. Life cycle studies indicate a potential to reduce greenhouse gas through methane capture, fossil fuel substitution, and comparison with conventional methods. The reviewed evidence indicates that decentralized anaerobic digestion is most suitable if the waste is source-separated, moisture-rich, and available within a short distance. These work best if the local demand for energy and digestate exists. The economic performance of this technology depends substantially on digester scale, capacity utilization, feedstock availability, capital and operating and maintenance costs, etc. Direct thermal use may require lower treatment and conversion. At the same time, electricity generation and biomethane upgrading provide higher-value energy products, but the latter involves greater capital cost, operational complexity, and energy demand. Environmental benefits are higher when methane leakage is controlled, energy recovered replaces conventional energy resources, and digestate is used safely as a nutrient source. From a circular economy perspective, decentralized anaerobic digestion can reduce the disposal of biodegradable waste, promote energy and resource recovery, and support localized waste-to-resource systems. However, poor waste segregation, inconsistent feeding, limited capacity utilization, poor maintenance, and inadequate digestate management remain major barriers. This review article concludes that decentralized anaerobic digestion can support sustainable urban waste management in India only if technology selection, feedstock management, energy utilization, financing, policy support, and community participation are integrated. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Spatio-temporal cross attention involved dual graph convolution network for traffic flow prediction
abstract: Traffic flow prediction is a critical task in intelligent transportation systems. The main challenge lies in the existence of complex, intertwined and dynamically evolving spatio-temporal dependencies in real-world traffic networks. Existing methods often rely on inherent static road network graph structures, lacking focus on the key time nodes and effective interaction mechanisms of spatio-temporal dimension information. To address this limitation, we propose a traffic flow prediction model named spatio-temporal cross attention involved dual graph convolution network. Our method adopts a parallel framework to synchronously extract features from both spatial and temporal dimensions. It spatially achieves enhanced learning of global and local dynamic dependencies through a dual graph convolution module, and temporally, it combines a long short-term memory network with a temporal attention module to capture continuous temporal correlations. Then through a cross attention fusion module, it dynamically integrates spatio-temporal information and establishes an interaction mechanism between them. Extensive experiments on four real-world traffic datasets from the Caltrans performance measurement system (PeMS03, PeMS04, PeMS07 and PeMS08) demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an average performance improvement of 2% to 15% compared with existing baseline models. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Continuity and Discontinuity in Artefact Distributions from Multi-Period Archaeological Sites
abstract: Artefact finds recovered by metal detecting and reported by members of the public are a growing source of archaeological information, with over 1.2 million finds recorded to date by the Portable Antiquities Scheme in England and Wales. Heritage schemes in many other European countries where hobby detecting for archaeology is legal likewise report growing numbers of finds. Using point pattern analysis, this paper presents a worked-out set of computational methods to study diachronic processes within artefact assemblages at field or local (e.g. parish) levels. We present a simulated ‘toy’ example to illustrate the methodology and test it with two large artefact assemblages from the counties of North Yorkshire and Norfolk that differ in terms of finds record quality and known contextual archaeological landscape information. The proposed approach and example code can be reapplied to other archaeological point patterns. It formalises a spatial statistical workflow that produces an assessment regarding landscape persistence and reuse, and which can be used, for example, to assist fieldwork or planning decisions by identifying areas for further research. The case studies highlight the considerable need for formal analytical workflows in public finds research, which can be easily deployed at different sites and local assemblages. Moreover, while the proposed workflow has been designed with public finds scatters in mind, it is scale-agnostic and can be reapplied to investigate a range of archaeological phenomena from monument distributions across a larger region to investigating artefact scatters within an excavated area. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Risk-based collaborative planning for cyber–physical–social distribution systems against extreme weather
abstract: Extreme weather can simultaneously damage distribution lines and communication facilities, weakening coordinated resource operation and increasing load-shedding risk. Such disruptions are particularly consequential in cyber–physical–social systems (CPSS) supporting distribution system operation, where power delivery depends on cyber connectivity and prosumer participation. To address this interdependence, a risk-based collaborative planning framework traces fragility-based failures through communication service to prosumer market access and adaptive post-event operation. Within this framework, peer-to-peer (P2P) trading serves as a communication-dependent mechanism for energy exchange among accessible prosumers rather than as an independent planning objective. A two-stage mean–CVaR model coordinates the distribution system operator’s (DSO) investment in communication backup and active-power transfer capacity with prosumer investment in renewable generation and energy storage. As cyber–physical conditions deteriorate, the model shifts from grid-connected coordination to communication-supported island operation and ultimately to local self-supply. A nested progressive hedging and alternating direction method of multipliers (PH-ADMM) algorithm coordinates scenario decisions and the interfaces between the DSO and prosumers. Studies on modified IEEE 33-node and 123-node systems show that communication survivability materially affects investment decisions and feasible post-event energy coordination. The framework provides a scalable basis for resilience-oriented collaborative planning in communication-dependent distribution systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Bridging governance and sustainability in the Global South: NGO-led urban transition pathways in Mashhad, Iran
abstract: Urban areas in the Global South face growing challenges of centralized governance, rapid urbanization and environmental degradation, which demand more inclusive and sustainable planning approaches. This article investigates how civil society organizations, particularly professionally oriented NGOs, can influence urban governance and contribute to sustainability-oriented transitions. The study examines the case of CharTabaqeh, a non-governmental organization in Mashhad, Iran, that contested the construction of the Southern Beltway and played an important role in the policy process that ultimately contributed to the project's transformation into the Mountain Park. Drawing on document analysis and observation, the research adopts a qualitative case study approach. The findings reveal that CharTabaqeh acted as a transition intermediary by creating participatory spaces, mobilizing citizens, and connecting community concerns with formal decision-making processes. The organization also promoted a shift toward more sustainable and resilient urban development by advocating for the preservation of ecological assets and the development of public green space in place of a car-oriented infrastructure project. Moreover, the NGO's strategic use of digital platforms during the COVID-19 pandemic facilitated civic mobilization, strengthened coalitions and amplified advocacy efforts at local and national scales. These results demonstrate that NGOs can act as catalysts of sustainable urban transitions by bridging community interests with policy processes, reframing development trajectories and leveraging digital technologies within centralized governance contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Enhancing fog performance through content replacement and caching strategies using Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has resulted in a significant increase in traffic sent to cloud data centers for processing. This event poses significant challenges, including network congestion, increased latency, and higher costs, which are particularly detrimental to real-time applications. Fog computing is a decentralized environment that utilizes Fog Nodes (FN) that are closer to users to process user requests, thereby improving latency, optimizing bandwidth utilization, and reducing costs. By implementing caching strategies within these FNs, we can further reduce response times, particularly for real-time applications. This paper presents a cooperative caching strategy with considering replacement for FNs and uses a Deep Learning (DL) method to predict popular content. Our goals include increasing the Cache Hit Ratio (CHR) while minimizing total delay and total cost to increase user satisfaction, and also answering all user requests by considering content replacement and distributing popular content among FNs to avoid duplication and improve resource usage. Since movie content has a significant contribution to the fronthaul load in fog computing networks, we utilize a real MovieLens dataset to evaluate our proposed method. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method has higher CHR, lower total delay, and lower total cost, while answering all requested content compared to traditional methods. Overall, this significantly improves the performance of fog computing. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Complex post-traumatic stress disorder in patients initially diagnosed with idiopathic hypersomnia: a case series
abstract: Objectives: The etiology of hypersomnia remains largely unknown, while the concept of complex post-traumatic stress disorder has recently emerged in the field of psychotraumatology. This case series report aims at highlighting a possible association between hypersomnia and trauma-related disorders. Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of medical records conducted as part of routine clinical practice. This case series comprises 17 consecutive patients previously diagnosed with idiopathic hypersomnia based on clinical and neurophysiological evaluations, all of whom underwent psychological and psychometric evaluations. Results: Eleven of 17 patients (64.7%) met ICD-11 criteria for CPTSD. Inferential comparisons between the CPTSD and non-CPTSD groups were exploratory and did not reach statistical significance after correction for multiple comparisons. Descriptively, patients with CPTSD showed higher trauma-related and anger-related symptom scores. Dissociative symptoms also showed a descriptive difference, although interpretation was substantially limited by missing data in the non-CPTSD group. Conclusions: This case series suggests that some cases of pathological hypersomnolence might be associated with traumatic disorders. Hypersomnolence may represent a response to traumatic memories, particularly in patients with complex traumatic histories, such as childhood abuse. The small sample size limits the generalizability of the findings. The small sample size limits generalizability of our findings and warrants confirmation in larger studies, while opening a potentially relevant avenue for hypersomnia research. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. title: Modeling the historical relationship between waterfront development and transport infrastructure: Evidence from Jeddah’s coastal transformation
abstract: The redevelopment of waterfronts is increasingly perceived as a transport-mediated spatial process as opposed to a design or land-use process. Nevertheless, limited information exists on the impacts of transportation infrastructure on waterfront integration over time, nonlinear dynamics and temporal lag effects, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions. This paper examines the history of the relationship between the evolution of transport infrastructure and waterfront spatial integration along the Jeddah coastline in a longitudinal, GIS-based study. The analysis combines network accessibility, pedestrian permeability, land-use intensity gradients, and a composite Waterfront Mobility Integration Index (WMII) across three historical development phases. Normalized indicator trajectories, sensitivity tests, and counterfactual situations are used to analyze the concepts of threshold behavior and time lag. It has been found that accessibility to transport grows more rapidly than other spatial dimensions, and that substantial growth in pedestrian permeability and the continuity of public space is achieved only after accessibility becomes critical, with a time lag. The findings reveal that accessibility is sufficient, though not necessary in waterfront integration, and that pedestrian infrastructure is the mediating variable in the transformation of transport investment into continuous, publicly accessible waterfront environments. The research adds to the transport-waterfront literature by offering a replicable analytical framework on evaluating waterfront change in fast growing coastal metropolitan areas and providing longitudinal evidence of threshold effects and lagged spatial response. © 2026 The Authors.

title: From maritime near misses to recovery mechanisms: A Safety-II event-chain graph approach
abstract: Maritime near misses are not only precursors of accidents, but also empirical traces of how hazardous situations are detected, coordinated, and controlled before escalation. However, existing near-miss studies have largely focused on risk identification and accident prediction, leaving limited quantitative evidence on the Safety-II-informed recovery patterns embedded in near-miss narratives. A Safety-II-informed event-chain graph framework is proposed to learn recovery-oriented patterns from maritime near-miss reports. A concept-level event-chain graph is constructed to represent links among antecedent contexts, hazardous situations, protective interventions, process mechanisms, and resilience outcomes. To capture response structures beyond ordinary pairwise relations, a stage-informed hypergraph is developed to preserve higher-order co-activation among protective functions. Time-to-clearance and restricted mean risk exposure time are examined as exploratory indicators of reported risk-exposure duration, while unadjusted (Raw), inverse probability weighting (IPW), and augmented inverse probability weighting (AIPW) are compared to assess adjusted observational associations under comparable hazardous contexts. Cross-actor coordination showed the most stable adjusted association with risk removal/mitigation, whereas associations with high-quality recovery were more sensitive to narrative completeness. The proposed framework provides an interpretable approach for Safety-II learning from near-miss reports and supports maritime traffic governance, emergency response planning, and proactive safety management. title: CloudTrip: Exploring physiological data-enabled multisensory metaphorical narratives for everyday stress management
abstract: In modern society, an increasing number of people are suffering from the harmful effects of chronic stress, while data-enabled reflection has been shown to be an effective approach to stress management. However, most existing human–data interaction designs primarily focus on retrospective data review, often failing to foster engaging and meaningful reflection. In this paper, we present CloudTrip, an immersive application that represents the users’ data throughout a day as an experiential and interactive digital story for mental health self-reflection. Specifically, CloudTrip metaphorically conveys users’ daily stress-related physiological data into narrative experiences by dynamically mapping the data onto changes in visual and auditory elements of characters and virtual environments. Users can record reflective content during the experience and receive responsive feedback generated by a large language model, thereby forming an interactive narrative loop that further deepens reflective engagement. We conducted a 14-day within-subject study with 20 participants, comparing CloudTrip with a traditional line-chart visualization using a mixed-methods evaluation to assess its impact on the reflection experience and reflection support. Results show that CloudTrip was associated with a cardiac autonomic pattern compatible with higher arousal, increases in self-reported valence, arousal, and dominance, more favorable motivational ratings for the experience, stronger perceived support for reflection, and promise for repeated use. Finally, we discuss design implications for integrating data-enabled multisensory storytelling techniques into human–data interaction systems to promote everyday reflective behavior for mental health management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: TiDISC: A titans-inspired disentangled spectral memory-augmented contrastive model for dynamic graphs
abstract: Dynamic graph representation learning is essential for modeling evolving dependencies in complex networks. Existing methods commonly encode temporal interactions as a unified sequence, which makes it difficult to distinguish slowly varying trends from rapidly varying event dynamics and increases vulnerability to shortcut patterns induced by repetitive interactions. To address these limitations, TiDISC, a Titans-inspired Disentangled Spectral Memory-augmented Contrastive model, is proposed. TiDISC first constructs adaptive leakage-safe historical contexts. Temporal Scaling Co-occurrence Attention (TSCA) then encodes recurrence-aware structural priors while discouraging excessive reliance on direct counting cues. The resulting tokens are organized into patches, and a Trend–Event Disentangled Filter (TEDF) constructs complementary trend-oriented and event-oriented representations through energy-guided spectral routing. A heterogeneous dual-stream encoder uses Titans-inspired implicit MLP attention to model long-range trends without reproducing the complete Titans memory system. A strictly causal convolutional branch captures short-term event bursts. A Trend–Event Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) decoder performs pair-specific routing between trend and event evidence for link prediction. Spectral-Augmented Contrastive Learning (SACL) further improves robustness through complementary structural perturbations and branch-specific spectral jitter. Experiments on eight benchmark datasets demonstrate that TiDISC achieves the strongest overall ranking under transductive evaluation and remains competitive across diverse inductive link prediction settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Lithium extraction and developmental embeddedness in Zimbabwe: Chinese-led investment and local development outcomes
abstract: Zimbabwe’s rapidly expanding lithium mining sector, dominated by Chinese investment and integrated into global battery and electric vehicle value chains, presents significant opportunities for economic transformation. However, whether this investment generates development benefits for mining-affected communities remains uncertain. This paper examines the extent to which Chinese-led investment contributes to locally experienced development outcomes in Zimbabwe. Drawing on survey data from 230 respondents across six lithium mining sites complemented by stakeholder interviews, field observations, and documentary sources, this study assesses economic outcomes, social responsibility, environmental stewardship, governance and public participation, and physical infrastructure. The findings reveal limited local economic integration and infrastructure development, weak community participation, and significant environmental and social costs. These outcomes are shaped not simply by investor nationality, but by the interaction between corporate practices, globally integrated transition mineral value chains, and fragmented and weakly enforced governance frameworks. The article argues that Zimbabwe’s lithium sector remains weakly developmentally embedded despite rapid production and export growth. It advances the Community-Centered Developmental Embeddedness Framework as an analytical framework for assessing whether transition mineral extraction becomes developmentally embedded through inclusive governance and participation, local economic integration, and environmental and social accountability, supported by coordinated government action. The framework contributes to existing scholarship on transition mineral governance and resource-based development by placing community-level development outcomes at the center of assessing the developmental impacts of extraction. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Michelin Key recognition and hotel evaluation: The roles of perceived transferred essence and travel distance
abstract: This research investigates how Michelin Key recognition shapes consumer judgment in the hotel context. Across five experiments, participants evaluated fictitious hotels that either received or did not receive Michelin Key recognition, with variations in signal strength and travel distance. The results show that Michelin Key recognition increases attitude toward the hotel. This effect is consistently mediated by perceived transferred essence, defined as the belief that a hotel experience embodies a coherent and intentionally designed identity. This mediating role persists when perceived prestige and expected service quality are modeled as competing mediators. The mechanism emerges even in a mid-range hotel context designed to minimize explicit luxury cues, indicating that Michelin Key recognition operates beyond luxury-based inferences. The effect is further amplified when the hotel is framed as geographically distant, consistent with Construal Level Theory, through strengthened perceived transferred essence. Overall, Michelin Key functions as a meaning-oriented signal in pre travel hotel evaluation, shaping how consumers interpret the identity and coherence of the stay experience. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Assessment of horizontal ecological compensation in China based on ecosystem service flows
abstract: Ecological compensation has been regarded as a key mechanism for promoting the coordinated development of regional social-ecological systems and addressing environmental justice. The scientific identification of compensation priorities and amounts is recognized as fundamental for the effective implementation of horizontal compensation schemes. The spatiotemporal dynamics of supply and demand for water, grain, and carbon ecosystem service values were assessed, together with coupling coordination and supply-demand balance. A national horizontal compensation framework for China integrated flow models for individual services, network topology analysis, and compensation accounting to link providers and beneficiaries across cities and estimate reference amounts. Supply generally increased, whereas demand rose for water and carbon but remained relatively stable for grain. Across 2000, 2010, and 2020, the average proportions of cities where local supply exceeded local demand were 80%, 86%, and 22% for water yield, grain production, and carbon sequestration, respectively. Substantial variations in network structure and node characteristics were observed among the compensation networks, with the number of modeled flow paths increasing for water and decreasing for grain and carbon. The numbers of ecological-provision and ecological-beneficiary cities decreased, while their respective average modeled net ecological benefits and net compensation payments were higher in 2020 than in 2000. Meanwhile, the number of cities with unresolved service deficits and no modeled compensation inflows or outflows increased. By linking supply-demand imbalances with flows of individual services, the framework provides a quantitative basis for identifying compensation partners and negotiating differentiated payment responsibilities using estimated amounts as references. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Unraveling the multi-stage damage evolution in architected SiC/SiC composite claddings via quasi-in-situ X-ray computed tomography
abstract: While multi-layered SiC/SiC composites are essential for accident-tolerant fuels, linking structural architecture to damage evolution remains critical. This study evaluates hoop tensile failure across single-layer, duplex, and triplex claddings using quasi-in-situ XCT, Raman, and EBSD. Results reveal that macroscopic failure is governed by spatial defect distribution, residual stresses, and interlayer. Single-layer claddings exhibit flaw-sensitive failure influenced by the distribution of radially aligned pores. Duplex claddings achieve the highest strength via disrupted defect continuity, favorable compressive residual stresses, and polymorphic (6H/2H-SiC) boundaries that force tortuous crack pathways. Conversely, the triplex architecture exhibits a distinct mechanical trade-off: inner tensile stresses and a thickened PyC interlayer slightly reduce peak strength but trigger extensive interfacial debonding, yielding remarkable pseudo-ductility and damage tolerance. These insights highlight that managing structural architecture and residual stress is critical for optimizing multi-layered SiC/SiC composite claddings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: GLP-1 medication use is associated with stronger implicit preferences for healthy foods based on enjoyment and taste
abstract: The present study examined whether GLP-1 medication use was associated with differences in implicit and explicit evaluations of healthy and junk foods. Implicit preferences were measured using the Implicit Association Test in two separate conditions employing different types of evaluative terms. One condition used evaluation terms related to food enjoyment and taste, whereas the other used terms related to food desirability. Explicit preferences were assessed via ratings of healthiness, tastiness, and irresistibility. The results revealed stronger implicit preferences for healthy foods when evaluations were based on enjoyment and taste among medication users relative to non-users. Further analyses revealed stronger enjoyment-based implicit preferences for healthy foods among semaglutide users than among non-users, whereas no corresponding difference was found between tirzepatide users and non-users. No significant differences were found when evaluations were based on food desirability. Moreover, explicit ratings did not differ by medication status, suggesting that semaglutide users may be unaware of their implicit preference for healthy foods. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Smart city governance and public value creation: an analysis in emerging cities
abstract: Governance is a core component of smart cities, yet further research is needed to understand its internal structure and interactions. This study analyzes how smart city governance (SCG) is configured and the types of public value it generates in two emerging economy cities: Medellín, Colombia, and Buenos Aires, Argentina. Using an exploratory qualitative approach, the research draws on 70 interviews, non-participant observation, and over 40 official documents. It proposes a socio-technical SCG model with four components: strategic management, collective intelligence, technological intelligence, contextual conditions, alongside a public value outcome dimension, 12 subcomponents and 15 types of public value. These values fall into two categories: urban sustainability and internal efficiency and effectiveness. The model offers an integrative framework for understanding SCG and guiding policy and program design. © 2026 The Authors.

title: On-Line Scheduling with A Non-Renewable Resource Under Periodic Supply
abstract: This is the first paper to address an on-line scheduling problem with a non-renewable resource. Resource is supplied with known quantity periodically. The jobs arriving on-line over time have the same basic processing time and the same required quantity of resource. Each job is revealed until its release time, and a scheduler makes decision without the information of future jobs. If the available quantity of the resource satisfies the resource requirement, a job is processed with the basic processing time by consuming the resource requirement. Otherwise, the job can be processed with deterioration under a longer processing time by consuming the insufficient resource quantity. The objective is to minimize the makespan. For this problem on a single machine, we derive a lower bound on the competitive ratio by adversary strategy, and provide a best possible on-line algorithm with a competitive ratio of 1 + α, where α is the positive root of α2 + 3α = 1. © The author(s) 2027.

title: Local Knowledge for Ecological Restoration: Motivations and Barriers in Urban Protected Areas in Mexico
abstract: Local knowledge is recognized as an important part of ecological restoration, and local communities have become more actively involved in recent years. Because participants hold diverse worldviews, their experiences can support ecological restoration. This study explored motivations and barriers to restoration based on the experiences of local participants in urban protected areas in the Valley of Mexico. We collected data through a survey and interviews. Local participants in restoration were mainly motivated by nature conservation and air purification. The main barriers to restoration were drought and fires. Participants’ restoration goals varied and were less aligned with protected-area objectives. Additionally, more experienced participants were more likely to identify restoration goals than less experienced participants. Overall, participants acquired knowledge through experience and undertook diverse efforts to address constraints. This suggests that learning from restoration activities, as a form of local knowledge, is important for identifying context-based barriers. From a socio-ecological perspective, this research discusses the need to establish context-based ecosystem targets and shared goals among stakeholders, as well as the importance of local knowledge for improving ecological restoration. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Sounding different: Exploring attitudes towards digital voice personalization in a conversational setting
abstract: With the rapid advancement of voice generation and conversion technologies, the application of voice personalization in everyday communication is becoming increasingly possible. However, current studies on voice personalization have largely focused on tool design, while relatively little is known about the impact of these technologies on self-presentation and social interaction. To explore this, we conducted a qualitative study with 14 pairs of participants (28 in total, 15 females and 13 males) that integrated a voice personalization tool into natural conversation. In pairs, participants first engaged in a conversation using their original voices, and then reflected on this experience. After that, they personalized their voices using a voice modification tool and took part in a second conversation with the same partner in which they heard each other’s modified voices in real-time. Finally, they participated in follow-up interviews. Our findings show that voice personalization prompted participants to reflect on their original and modified voices, to negotiate between authenticity and desired traits, and to consider both benefits and risks of voice personalization in different contexts. These insights indicate that voice personalization is intricately linked to self-perception while simultaneously functioning as a malleable social signal. Overall, this study contributes empirically grounded findings on how voice modification affects self-perception and impression management, and offers design directions for future personalization tools. © 2026 The Authors. title: When the sea remembers: Ritual, emotion, and identity at the Mazu Festival
abstract: The study examines how ritual participation in religious festivals generates emotional energy and reinforces cultural identity, using the Mazu Festival in China as a case example. Findings reveal that ritual engagement fosters affective synchronization and reactivates collective memory, enabling participants to reconnect with heritage, culture and negotiate evolving identities. Emotional energy emerges as a central process linking symbolic system to identity formation. The research contributes to festival tourism studies by advancing an integrated emotional and symbolic framework and by highlighting the role of festivals as dynamic platforms for cultural continuity and identity renewal. The findings also offer practical insights for destination managers and policymakers seeking to enhance cultural meaningfulness of festival experiences. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Optimizing Federated Incremental Learning: Efficient Malicious Data Removal for Big Data Analytics
abstract: Federated incremental learning facilitates decentralized and continuous model updates across multiple clients, presenting a promising framework for big data analytics in distributed environments. However, the presence of poisoned or malicious data introduces significant challenges, including compromised model performance and system reliability. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes an efficient and resource-aware machine unlearning method tailored for federated incremental learning. The approach utilizes a membership inference attack mechanism to accurately identify poisoned data based on prediction confidence levels. Once detected, a targeted forgetting mechanism is applied, leveraging fine-tuning techniques to erase the influence of the poisoned data while preserving the model’s incremental learning capabilities. By aligning the distributions of poisoned data with third-party datasets, the method achieves reliable unlearning without introducing excessive computational overhead. Extensive experiments conducted on diverse datasets validate the method’s effectiveness, demonstrating a significant reduction in forgetting time (up to 21.05× speedup compared with baseline approaches) while maintaining robust model performance in incremental learning tasks. This work offers a scalable and efficient solution to the data forgetting problem, advancing the reliability and practicality of federated incremental learning in distributed and resource-constrained scenarios. © The author(s) 2027.

title: A structured and gated autoregressive Gaussian process for robust and efficient multi-fidelity learning
abstract: Multi-fidelity learning with Gaussian processes (GPs) has become an effective strategy for improving predictive accuracy by leveraging inexpensive low-fidelity simulations to enhance high-fidelity inference. However, existing multi-fidelity GP methods often lack flexibility in representing heterogeneous cross-fidelity dependencies and remain vulnerable to negative transfer when cross-fidelity correlations become locally unreliable. Moreover, conventional Monte Carlo (MC)-based uncertainty propagation incurs a non-negligible computational cost. To address these limitations, we propose a structured and gated autoregressive GP (SGARGP) framework to improve robustness and computational efficiency in multi-fidelity learning. Specifically, a structured autoregressive kernel that combines linear and nonlinear components is introduced to capture diverse cross-fidelity relationships. A leave-one-out cross-validation–informed gating mechanism is further developed to adaptively downweight unreliable cross-fidelity transfer and mitigate localized negative transfer. In addition, a deterministic uncertainty propagation scheme (DGHUP) based on Gauss–Hermite quadrature is proposed to achieve an improved accuracy–cost trade-off compared with MC sampling. Comprehensive experiments on synthetic examples, benchmarks and two physics-based engineering applications demonstrate that the structured kernel improves robustness across linear-dominant, nonlinear-dominant, and mixed-dominant scenarios; the gating strategy effectively alleviates negative transfer without degrading performance in well-aligned cases; and DGHUP achieves predictive accuracy comparable to MC methods at significantly reduced computational cost. These results demonstrate that SGARGP provides a reliable and efficient probabilistic framework for multi-fidelity learning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Assessment of a Role-Playing Game’s Effectiveness in Identifying Cattle Herding Strategies at a Wildlife-Livestock Interface in Zimbabwe
abstract: Natural resource management at the interface between protected areas and communal lands varies across space and time, affecting wildlife and livestock movement patterns. In southern Africa, many communities bordering protected areas are partly agropastoral and rely on access to these areas to graze their cattle. However, farmers face complex decisions about whether to graze cattle inside protected zones or on communal lands, weighing factors such as increased predation risk or exposure to wildlife-borne diseases within protected areas. Social, economic, cultural, and climatic influences further complicate herding strategies and decision-making. We analysed data from a role-playing game co-designed and played by local farmers living near protected areas and communal lands in Zimbabwe to explore their cattle herding practices and the factors driving grazing choices at this wildlife-livestock interface. Multiple correspondence analysis revealed two primary herding strategies. The most prevalent involved grazing cattle inside protected areas during the farming season. The second was a mixed strategy, with farmers grazing cattle both inside protected areas and on communal lands in similar proportions during the transition between agricultural and dry seasons. Grazing decisions were mainly linked to the presence of crops or stored crop residues on communal lands. We observed variations in strategy use under different rainfall scenarios. Our findings can be integrated into an agent-based model to simulate cattle movements at this wildlife-livestock interface. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Welfare analysis of electricity distribution: The Dignity Tariff in Bolivia
abstract: We conduct an analysis of the demand functions associated with electricity distribution in Bolivia, focusing on the implications of price fluctuations on consumer welfare. This analysis requires the estimation of demand functions, which we achieve through the application of panel data with fixed effects and the use of instrumental variables. Additionally, we apply propensity score matching (PSM) to compare electricity expenditures between beneficiary and comparable non-beneficiary households, providing an independent welfare estimate grounded in observed household behaviour rather than structural demand parameters alone. In 2006, the Bolivian government introduced the Dignity Tariff, aimed at regulating electricity distribution costs for both urban and rural households. This tariff offers a 25% reduction in electricity prices for households that consume up to 70 kWh per month. Our key findings indicate that the Dignity Tariff effectively acts as a subsidy for electricity consumption. Estimates derived from demand functions suggest an average monthly welfare gain ranging from Bs 17.98 to Bs 21.12 (USD 2.58 to USD 3.03), while propensity score matching yields an average monthly saving of approximately Bs 47 (USD 6.75) for beneficiary households, providing significant financial relief to economically vulnerable populations. © 2026 The Authors. title: Beyond copy number: circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA Fragmentomics and structural states in liquid biopsy
abstract: Circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf-mtDNA) is commonly treated as a concentration-based biomarker, yet the measured signal is a composite of biologically distinct molecular states that are differentially affected by blood collection, platelet activation, centrifugation, storage, extraction, amplification, and sequencing. This analytical heterogeneity has become more consequential as cf-mtDNA research moves from copy-number assays toward fragmentomics, topology, heteroplasmy, oxidative lesions, and carrier-resolved measurements. Recent multi-cohort studies indicate that fragment size, 5′-end composition, motif diversity, and regional breakage patterns can support cancer detection and tissue-of-origin inference, while clinical chemistry studies demonstrate that routine preanalytical choices can markedly alter the mitochondrial fraction recovered from plasma. This review develops a laboratory-medicine framework in which cf-mtDNA is considered a multidimensional analyte rather than a single abundance variable. We integrate mitochondrial release biology with the extracellular carrier states of mtDNA; explain how TFAM, membrane pores, mitophagy, extracellular vesicles, platelets, and nucleases shape the observed fragmentome; evaluate preanalytical and analytical sources of bias; and assess translational evidence across oncology, critical illness, cardio-renal disease, metabolic inflammation, transplantation, and neuroinflammatory disorders. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing true biological variation from procedure-induced redistribution of cf-mtDNA between soluble, vesicular, platelet-associated, and cell-free mitochondrial compartments. We propose minimum analytical descriptors, quality-control priorities, and validation steps required before cf-mtDNA fragmentomic signatures can become transportable clinical tests. The central implication is that the next phase of cf-mtDNA diagnostics will depend less on measuring more DNA than on measuring the correct molecular fraction with traceable preanalytics, orthogonal characterization, and clinically locked computational models. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Learning to coordinate: A knowledge-distilled agent for adaptive multi-agent code generation
abstract: Code generation powered by large language models (LLMs) faces substantial challenges due to the variability of task difficulty, ranging from simple string-manipulation tasks to complex algorithmic implementations. Current approaches, including many multi-agent frameworks, typically employ uniform processing strategies across all tasks. This leads to systematic resource misallocation: over-processing simple tasks while providing insufficient reasoning and verification support for complex ones. To address this inefficiency, we propose an adaptive multi-agent framework driven by a knowledge-distilled Coordination Agent. By distilling posterior behavioral signals from a high-capacity teacher model into a specialized dataset, Code-PBD, our lightweight student agent learns to assess task difficulty and route tasks to appropriate execution workflows. Based on the predicted difficulty, the framework dynamically orchestrates specialized agents into three differentiated workflows: streamlined, standard, and enhanced; the enhanced workflow incorporates an Abductive Chain-of-Thought (D-CoT) mechanism for deep logical diagnosis. Empirical evaluations on HumanEval and MBPP demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 73.8 % and 77.3 % Pass@1, respectively. Compared with the Fixed-Enhanced baseline, the proposed approach reduces token consumption by 67.2 % and 70.0 % on HumanEval and MBPP, respectively, while achieving Pass@1 scores that are 2.4 and 3.4 percentage points lower. On HumanEval, the method further improves Pass@1 by 16.6 percentage points over the Fixed-Standard baseline with only a small increase in API calls, demonstrating a more favorable quality–cost trade-off. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Experimental Study on Smart Sloped Rolling-Type Bearings Integrated with Early Prediction of Peak Velocity
abstract: The use of sloped rolling-type bearings (SRBs) to protect critical equipment from seismic damage has been widely adopted. However, maintaining SRB displacement responses within safe limits often requires a large damping force, which results in unacceptable accelerations. This highlights the trade-off in seismic isolation: reducing displacement typically comes at the cost of increased acceleration, and vice versa. Although previous numerical studies have shown that adjusting the SRB damping force based on peak velocity (PV) predictions from an earthquake early warning (EEW) system enables better control over acceleration and displacement responses, experimental validation is necessary. This study employs magnetorheological (MR) dampers to apply the damping force determined by the predicted PV. Performance tests are conducted to characterize the physical properties of the MR dampers and develop their mathematical representation. Numerical simulations incorporating the MR damper and SRB models under seismic conditions are used to establish a control law that correlates PV with the voltage required by the MR dampers. To predict PV, the first few seconds following primary seismic wave (P-wave) detection undergo a multi-scale short-term Fourier transform (STFT) to generate a spectrogram. After feature enhancement, it is fed into a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based model, which predicts the impending earthquake’s PV. This prediction, alongside the established control law, enables rapid adjustment of the SRB damping force shortly after P-wave detection. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is evaluated through shake table testing. Results indicate that the approach significantly mitigates isolation displacement responses under major earthquakes, demonstrating its potential for improving seismic isolation performance. 2026 © The Author(s)

title: Reinforcement learning with experience sharing promotes collective cooperation on higher-order networks
abstract: As a central form of prosocial behavior, collective cooperation is the cornerstone of social prosperity, and elucidating how it emerges among the self-interested population is of significant theoretical and practical importance. However, existing research of cooperative evolution on higher-order networks typically assumes that agents update decisions exclusively based on their own experiences, overlooking the pervasive diffusion of information within groups. In reality, decision-making is shaped not only by individual experience, but also by experiences acquired from neighboring agents. To this end, we develop a hypergraph-based reinforcement learning framework that integrates individual and neighborhood experiences to investigate how information sharing affects cooperation under higher-order interactions. Specifically, we utilize hypergraphs to characterize the interaction topology, within which agents update their strategies according to the Q-learning algorithm. Extending the standard learning paradigm, we introduce an experience sharing mechanism, where neighborhood information is aggregated to form a shared experience and subsequently fused with individual experience to guide decision-making. Through extensive simulations, we demonstrate that an intermediate level of experience sharing can significantly enhance the collective cooperation, particularly under severe social dilemmas, increasing the final cooperation level by up to approximately 0.43. In contrast, excessive experience sharing leads to behavioral homogenization among agents, thereby undermining the relative advantage of cooperation. Moreover, higher learning rates coupled with moderate discount factors are most conducive to cooperation. These findings shed new light on how experience sharing shapes cooperative dynamics in higher-order networks. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Spectral clustering based on neighborhood relationships and the number of nearest neighbors k
abstract: Spectral clustering has become a mainstream method for clustering complex data due to its strong adaptability to non-convex distributions, high-dimensional data, and manifold structures. The performance of spectral clustering is directly determined by the quality of the similarity matrix, yet conventional methods often rely on globally fixed parameters, making it difficult to accommodate local structural variations in the data, which can easily lead to degraded clustering results. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel spectral clustering algorithm based on neighborhood relationships and the number of nearest neighbors k(SC-k). The algorithm constructs an ε-neighborhood graph that integrates mean and variance, uses the average distance between a sample and its k nearest neighbors as a local scaling parameter, and designs a new Gaussian kernel similarity measure. This ensures both sparsity and reasonableness of the similarity matrix while reducing sensitivity to the parameter k. Finally, extensive numerical experiments are conducted to compare the proposed algorithm with existing advanced methods, demonstrating that our approach achieves more efficient clustering performance. © The Author(s) under exclusive licence to Sociedade Brasileira de Matemática Aplicada e Computacional 2026.

title: Making critical-mineral sourcing visible: recorded-origin evidence from U.S. federal procurement
abstract: Critical-mineral security depends not only on extraction and processing capacity but also on state visibility. Governments struggle to govern a mineral dependence they cannot observe in their own records, even when fragments of that information are held privately across agencies. This article asks how far the United States federal government’s recorded sourcing of the critical-mineral commodities it buys can be seen in its own contract data. Using approximately one thousand federal contract awards for selected critical-mineral commodity classes over fiscal years 2018–2026, we measure domestic-versus-foreign sourcing at the contract level in USAspending / Federal Procurement Data System (FPDS) records. Country of product origin is recorded for about 94% of awards and for nearly all obligated dollars, enough to support a bounded sourcing profile in this narrow universe. Among awards with recorded origin, foreign sourcing is a minority, about 9%, but it is policy-relevant: China is the largest foreign source by dollar value, concentrated in two large manganese awards, while Germany is the most frequent by award count. Bullion and coinage flows must be separated from strategic-materials procurement, or they inflate the universe twenty- to forty-fold. Two preliminary findings, a selective-onshoring trend and a defense-logistics sourcing effect, do not survive the complete data. The analysis covers U.S. federal procurement only and measures recorded procurement sourcing rather than upstream mine origin or total national dependence. Its contribution is to make one layer of critical-mineral governance, the state’s own recorded purchasing, observable, and to clarify what that layer can and cannot show for public oversight. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Structure-Aware Representation Enhancement for Incomplete Bundle Recommendation
abstract: Bundle recommendation systems are able to enhance user experience and increase sales profits by offering curated item collections. However, the complexity inherent in bundling items poses significant challenges in accurately collecting user interactions with bundles. This limitation often results in incomplete user-bundle interaction data, making it hard to accurately capture user preferences within the context of bundles. In this work, we propose a framework named Structure-aware representation enhancement for Incomplete Bundle Recommendation (SIBR). Specifically, we first conduct pretraining with user-item interactions and bundle-item affiliations to learn representations of users, bundles, and items, which are consistent with the underlying structure. Furthermore, we introduce a graph-signal enhancement strategy focused on user-bundle interactions. This strategy aims to reveal the distinct relations between user-user and bundle-bundle, enabling the refinement of user and bundle representations. The ultimate goal is to leverage these enhanced representations to improve the accuracy of bundle recommendations. Extensive experiments on three real-world benchmark datasets show that our proposed framwork achieves significant performance gains, which consistently achieves an average of 20.1% improvement over state-of-the-art competitors in both Recall and NDCG metrics. © The author(s) 2027.

title: Multi-scenario CTR prediction with LLM-augmented semantic graphs and anti-polarization experts
abstract: Click-through rate (CTR) prediction is a core task in recommendation systems. However, existing multimodal CTR methods still rely heavily on interaction-driven graphs, which are often too sparse to capture deeper semantic relations between users. To address this limitation, we propose APEX-GraphMoE, a unified framework centered on LLM-enhanced LightGCN (LLN). LLN introduces an LLM-as-graph-builder paradigm, in which fine-tuned large language models aggregate multimodal user behaviors and construct semantic user–user edges to enrich the graph beyond explicit interactions. Building on this core paradigm, we further introduce HUBM and APG to address two additional challenges caused by strong semantic graph signals. HUBM performs task-aware multimodal refinement to preserve the contribution of image and text features during downstream optimization, while APG stabilizes adaptive routing in MMoE and alleviates expert polarization. Experiments on the large-scale AntM2 C dataset, containing approximately 10 million samples across five scenarios, show that APEX-GraphMoE improves AUC by 2.89% and reduces expert-usage variance by 50.21% over strong baselines.We further conduct auxiliary validation on MM-CTR1 M to provide preliminary cross-dataset evidence, while keeping AntM2 C as the primary benchmark. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of LLN as the core source of semantic topology enhancement, with HUBM and APG serving as complementary supporting mechanisms. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: The processing of word order is affected by verb subcategorization frequency: Evidence from electrophysiology
abstract: This study investigated the influence of verb subcategorization preferences on sentence processing in Standard Indonesian. We examined how verb biases affect the processing of active and passive sentences by utilizing event-related potentials. Our findings revealed that passive sentences with active-bias verbs elicited a significant late positive shift (P600) relative to active sentences, which indicated increased processing difficulty. No such effect was detected for passive sentences with passive-bias verbs. The cost was observed only where the verb's preference conflicted with the passive structure, suggesting that verb-specific statistics, rather than word order alone, contribute to the difficulty of passive sentences. We highlight the need for a nuanced understanding of sentence comprehension that incorporates both structural and lexical influences. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Risk perception and preventive control in indoor plant production: food safety practices among Swedish operators of leafy vegetables and microgreens
abstract: Indoor plant production is often promoted as a controlled production system that can reduce some hazards associated with open-field cultivation. However, ready-to-eat leafy vegetables, herbs, microgreens and sprouts remain vulnerable to microbial contamination through seeds, water, nutrient solutions, growing media, surfaces and human handling. This study investigated how Swedish commercial indoor production operators perceive and manage food safety in their urban soilless production systems. A mixed-methods design was used, combining an online survey of 17 respondents with semi-structured interviews with representatives from eight indoor production operations. Fisher's exact tests showed no statistically significant association between awareness of applicable safety requirements and educational level, certification status, or previous safety training. Interview data showed that food safety management was shaped by three interrelated dimensions: risk perception, preventive control practices, and economic, spatial and regulatory constraints. Some operators interpreted controlled indoor production as inherently low risk, whereas others recognized system specific hazards and reported routines for seed treatment, water testing, cleaning, employee hygiene, documentation and certification. Resource limitations, testing costs, limited space, language barriers and unclear regulatory communication constrained implementation. Because the study did not include observation, audit or microbiological sampling, it addresses perceived safety and reported preventive control rather than verified food safety performance. The findings reinforce that indoor plant production modifies, but does not remove, the food safety risk landscape. Strengthening food safety in this sector requires practical, regulation-aligned training, scalable guidance, and verifiable preventive controls adapted to indoor production systems. © 2026

title: An adaptive methodology for determining the optimal transition point and reuse lifespan of photovoltaic panels considering degradation-adjusted energy yield
abstract: End-of-Life (EoL) management of Photovoltaic (PV) panels is an emerging concern for waste managers and policymakers, given the high rates of PV deployment worldwide. Existing studies emphasize the benefits of PV recycling, but there are few assessments of panel reuse. Identification of the appropriate transition point from reuse to recycling that balances economic and environmental trade-offs is much needed. Studies that do engage with this domain fail to account for the operational and maintenance (O&M) and EoL costs incurred during the reuse phase. With the aims of sustainable waste management, the present study develops a dynamic techno-economic and environmental optimization framework for PV reuse, based on a scalarized multi-objective analysis, referred to as the Reuse Time Span Optimization Model (RTOM). RTOM integrates degradation-adjusted energy generation and monetized environmental benefits into an economic optimization model while accounting for O&M and EoL costs. Results indicate that, after a first life of 25 years, PV panels can be optimally reused for up to 13 years, yielding substantial net benefits. It shows that reuse boosts PV panel benefits by eight times (8×) compared to recycling. The study concludes that reuse is beneficial only within an optimal reuse duration; beyond which, it is no longer advantageous. A Monte Carlo-based sensitivity analysis is used to capture parameter uncertainty and evaluate robustness. The developed RTOM is a decision-support framework that is adaptable and transferable by modifying region-specific parameters. Overall, this work advances the discourse on PV waste management by repositioning reuse as a viable and preferable strategy. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.
