title: An integrated framework for total nitrogen load allocation and multidimensional assessment reconciling equity and environmental efficiency in large river basins
abstract: Total nitrogen (TN) load governance is crucial for safeguarding river and nearshore water environments. However, translating basin reduction goals into equitable and efficient spatial targets remains challenging due to socioeconomic, hydrological, and biogeochemical heterogeneities. This study develops an integrated framework coupling process-based water quality modelling (SWAT) with Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) to reconcile environmental efficiency with regional equity. Applying this framework to the Liao River Basin in China, this study generated multiple allocation schemes reflecting different socioeconomic priorities and evaluated their performance across TN compliance, abatement costs, food production, and social equality. Results show that under the 30% reduction target, schemes integrating efficiency reduced total basin abatement costs by 0.1%–6.5% and increased crop yields by 0.4%–2.4% relative to the equity-only scheme, although they widened regional disparities in economic and livelihood burdens. Sensitivity analyses indicate that the economic advantages of efficiency-integrated schemes weaken under the 40% reduction target due to nonlinearly escalating marginal abatement costs, and remain sensitive to source allocation within individual catchments. The scheme performance assessment accounting for multiple uncertainties reveals that the optimal schemes depend on the total reduction target and specific policy priorities, including objective weighting and policy-weighted scenarios prioritizing food security, cost control, or social equality. Ultimately, this framework explicitly quantifies multidimensional tradeoffs and provides a practical basis for formulating load management strategies across varying reduction targets and policy priorities. © 2026

title: FEDS: Feature and Entropy-Based Distillation Strategy for efficient learned image compression
abstract: Learned image compression (LIC) offers strong rate–distortion performance, but many high-performing models remain too heavy for deployment. This paper introduces Feature and Entropy-based Distillation Strategy (FEDS), which transfers knowledge from a strong offline teacher to a lightweight student through output supervision, intermediate feature alignment, and entropy-guided latent supervision. The latent objective ranks teacher channels by entropy and transfers the channels with the largest expected coding cost under the student's limited channel budget. On Kodak, Tecnick, and CLIC, the student stays close to the teacher, with BD-rate gaps of only 1.24%, 1.17%, and 0.55%, while reducing parameters by 63% and decreasing encoding/decoding time by about 73%. Additional channel-selection, alignment, bit-rate robustness, and transformer-family ablations confirm that FEDS provides an effective compression–efficiency trade-off. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Leveraging avatar fingerprinting: A multi-generator photorealistic talking-head public database and benchmark
abstract: Recent advances in photorealistic avatar generation have enabled highly realistic talking-head avatars, raising security concerns regarding identity impersonation in AI-mediated communication. To advance this challenging problem, the task of avatar fingerprinting aims to determine whether two avatar videos are driven by the same human operator. However, current public databases in the literature are scarce and based solely on old-fashioned talking-head avatar generators, not representing realistic scenarios for the current task of avatar fingerprinting. To overcome this situation, the present article introduces AVAPrintDB, a new publicly available multi-generator talking-head avatar database for avatar fingerprinting. AVAPrintDB is constructed from two audiovisual corpora and three state-of-the-art avatar generators (GAGAvatar, LivePortrait, HunyuanPortrait), representing different synthesis paradigms, and includes both self- and cross-reenactments to simulate legitimate usage and impersonation scenarios. Building on this database, we define a standardized and reproducible benchmark for avatar fingerprinting, considering public state-of-the-art avatar fingerprinting systems and exploring novel methods based on Foundation Models (DINOv2 and CLIP). We also conduct a comprehensive analysis under generator and dataset shift. Our results show that, while identity-related motion cues persist across synthetic avatars, current avatar fingerprinting systems remain highly sensitive to changes in the synthesis pipeline and source domain. The AVAPrintDB, benchmark protocols, and avatar fingerprinting systems are publicly available to facilitate reproducible research. © 2026 The Authors

title: Robust incomplete multi-view clustering via adaptive similarity graph completion and dual-tensor decomposition
abstract: Incomplete multi-view clustering (IMC) is crucial for real-world applications such as image retrieval, text classification, and subtype recognition, where multi-modal data frequently suffer from missing values and severe noise due to acquisition limitations or transmission losses. However, most existing methods rely on raw data completion, single-tensor constraints, and isolated multi-step processing paradigms. These approaches not only struggle to simultaneously preserve cross-view consistent principal components and filter out view-specific variations, but their phased nature also introduces irreversible error accumulation. To overcome these bottlenecks, this paper proposes a novel unified framework named Dual-Tensor Graph Completion for Incomplete Multi-View Clustering (DTGC-IMVC). Specifically, to eliminate reconstruction noise at the data feature level, an adaptive similarity graph completion mechanism is introduced to directly recover the similarity graph within the self-representation. Meanwhile, a dual-tensor architecture seamlessly integrating the tensor nuclear norm and the Schatten-p norm is constructed to rigorously capture high-order cross-view consistent features and effectively sparsify noise and view-specific components. Furthermore, a unified multi-source denoising strategy constrained by the L2,1-norm is introduced. Comprehensive experiments on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of clustering performance and robustness. The source code of this work is available at https://github.com/kamenrider-x/DTGC-IMVC. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning-Based Flow Splitting for Combinatorial Network Packet Routing Problem
abstract: Due to the rising demand for Quality of Service (QoS) in the emerging network, this paper considers the routing problem of efficiently planning the transmission path of flow demands to balance the load of the network. Existing classical routing algorithms based on static decision-making are unable to adjust to dynamical scenarios with fluctuating flow. Traditional reinforcement learning-based methods face challenges in large-scale scenarios due to the vast state and action spaces. Besides, the neural networks used for policy generation also suffer from issues like rudimentary feature extraction and limited learning capability. In this paper, we first introduce RequestNet, a novel attention-based model designed to better leverage the information of network topology and feature correlations. We also propose a multi-agent modeling approach for the network packet routing problem, named RequestNet-MA, which treats pairs of edge routers as agents, allowing us to allocate traffic from the perspective of flow demands, thus significantly reducing the dimensions of state and action spaces and enhancing inter-agent communication and cooperation. Extensive experiments and ablation studies demonstrate that the proposed RequestNet-MA can reduce maximum link utilization and scale well to a large-scale network. © The author(s) 2027.

title: Subsample averaging for non-periodic microstructures: Bias reduction, dispersion increase, and practical trade-offs in computational micromechanics
abstract: The computation of effective properties of random microstructured materials via representative volume elements (RVE) is affected by both bias and dispersion. For non-periodic microstructures (snapshots), which naturally arise in experiments and imaging-based studies, the bias decays slowly, rendering standard homogenization approaches inaccurate, significantly biased, and therefore unreliable. Recent theoretical results suggest that subsample averaging – evaluating the apparent properties only on a strictly interior subdomain – can significantly reduce the bias. In this work, we investigate the practical performance of subsample averaging for linear elastic particle-reinforced composites using large-scale numerical experiments and FFT-based computational micromechanics. We first demonstrate that subsample averaging must respect the Hill–Mandel condition to improve the convergence behavior of the bias, i.e., both stress and strain fields must be subsample averaged. In particular, the naive approach of subsample averaging the apparent stress alone may reduce the magnitude of the bias, but does not improve its convergence rate. When applied consistently, subsample averaging reduces the magnitude of the bias and produces a more favorable decay trend for the investigated non-periodic microstructures. However, this bias reduction comes at the cost of an increased dispersion due to the reduced sampling domain, resulting in only marginal improvements of the total error when used in isolation. To overcome this limitation, we combine subsample averaging with variance reduction via optimized volume fraction (OVF), which significantly improves overall accuracy and reliability for matrix-inclusion composites. The presented strategy is straightforward to implement and can be readily applied within existing computational frameworks without modifying the underlying solver. These results reveal a fundamental bias–dispersion trade-off associated with subsample averaging and provide practical guidance for computing the effective properties from non-periodic microstructure samples, including samples obtained experimentally. © 2026

title: Diagnosing ecosystem service mismatches through service flows and explainable AI: evidence from the Weihe River Basin, China
abstract: Ecosystem service flows (ESFs) connect ecological supply with human demand, yet the links among service transmission, supply-demand imbalance, and nonlinear response thresholds remain difficult to diagnose in rapidly urbanizing regions. To provide a transferable diagnostic approach, we developed an explainable AI-assisted supply-demand-flow framework. We tested it in the Weihe River Basin, a representative ecological-economic transition zone of Northwest China, from 2000 to 2020. We quantified the supply, demand, and ecosystem service supply-demand ratios (ESDRs) for water yield, soil conservation, carbon sequestration, and food provision; simulated service-specific flows; and used XGBoost-SHAP-PDP to identify dominant drivers and threshold intervals. Ecological sources in the Qinling, Longshan and loess hilly regions remained separated from demand centers on the Guanzhong urban plain. Water yield supply increased from 9.41 to 11.99 billion m3, and soil conservation supply from 4.36 to 5.93 billion t, while their respective demands declined by 21.5% and 24.1%. Water and soil conservation flows were concentrated along terrain-controlled river corridors, carbon sequestration showed strong outward spillover and weak internal inflow, and food flows shifted toward a multi-center network linking eastern Gansu and the Guanzhong Plain. SHAP identified population density as the leading driver of water and food ESDRs and forestland proportion as the dominant driver of soil and carbon ESDRs. By coupling service-flow mechanisms with interpretable machine learning, the framework offers a reusable basis for environmental impact assessment, ecological compensation, corridor protection, demand-side regulation, and threshold-based territorial planning in comparable urbanizing regions. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Quantifying energy–cost–carbon tradeoffs in China's onshore wind expansion: A life cycle-based turbine design optimization
abstract: China's onshore wind expansion must reconcile electricity generation, life-cycle cost, and life-cycle carbon emissions across heterogeneous wind regimes. We develop a region-specific assessment and turbine-design optimization framework linking rotor diameter and hub height to annual energy production, life-cycle cost, and greenhouse gas emissions from component manufacturing to grid delivery. Spatial screening identifies 2.61 million km2 of eligible land, representing 27.2% of China's land area. Under a uniform-design assessment using the reference wind speed, maximum geometric capacity reaches 10.1 TW, with gross generation of 30 PWh/yr and 10.6 PWh/yr after an idealized infinite-array adjustment. Separate national optimizations select turbine configurations across wind-speed zones under generation, cost, and carbon constraints, assuming full development of eligible land and using gross generation. The minimum-unit-cost solution generates 38.2 PWh/yr at 0.25 CNY/kWh and a carbon intensity of 15.0 g CO₂-eq/kWh. Minimizing carbon intensity lowers it to 13.3 g CO₂-eq/kWh but raises unit cost to 0.75 CNY/kWh, with generation of 40.2 PWh/yr. Selected turbine dimensions and rated powers generally decrease beyond their respective peaks in low-to-intermediate wind-speed zones; the minimum‑carbon-intensity solution generally favors larger rotors and higher-rated turbines. By quantifying energy–cost–carbon trade-offs, the framework supports turbine selection tailored to regional wind conditions and economic or carbon objectives. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: What prevents community gardens from long-term survival? A five-year case study in Suzhou, China
abstract: Community gardens are increasingly recognised as important instruments of urban micro-regeneration, yet their long-term sustainability remains fragile under project-based governance. This study traces the five-year evolution (2021–2025) of maintenance barriers in a government-initiated community garden in Suzhou, China. Using a longitudinal mixed-methods design, this paper tracks the community garden across three stages (inception, growth and struggle) through three phases of Likert-scale surveys and semi-structured interviews, supplemented by Participatory Action Research (PAR). The findings reveal a marked divergence in barrier trajectories. Individual technical constraints declined as residents accumulated horticultural knowledge, with the mean score for ‘lack of gardening knowledge and skills’ falling from 4.00 in 2021 to 1.83 in 2025. By contrast, team and institutional barriers intensified: ‘lack of an internal leader’ rose from 4.07 to 4.83, ‘unclear garden tasks’ from 3.20 to 4.33, and ‘Inadequate support from local authorities’ from 3.53 to 4.83, reaching the ceiling value of 5.0 for several individual respondents in 2025. The withdrawal of external facilitators exposed a governance vacuum that residents themselves labelled the ‘Three-Ignores’ ( san-bu-guan ) condition, in which fragmented responsibilities among Residents’ Committees, Property Management Companies and Homeowners’ Committees, together with unfulfilled budgetary commitments, produced systemic deterioration. At the same time, a significant demographic shift towards a volunteer team composed exclusively of elderly residents weakened the garden’s collective resilience. Sustaining community gardens requires a shift in urban management from temporary ‘project logic’ to more durable ‘governance logic’, including formal exit strategies, clearer responsibility arrangements and the incorporation of community assets into established administrative and budgetary systems. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Motivation for cyberhate among Ukrainian youth
abstract: While research on cyberhate has focused largely on prevalence and exposure, motivation underlying cyberhate perpetration remains under-researched. This study examines revenge and proactive motivations for cyberhate perpetration among Ukrainian youth during the ongoing war. Guided by the general aggression model, social identity theory, and social cognitive theory, we explored the mediating roles of revenge and proactive motivation in the association between cyberbullying victimization and cyberhate perpetration. Using exploratory structural equation modeling on survey data from 4149 youth aged 10–25, we found that victimization was significantly associated with cyberhate perpetration, partly through revenge motivation. Proactive motivation was related to victimization but was not significantly associated with cyberhate perpetration. Findings highlight the role of revenge motivation in cyberhate behaviors. In this war-affected population, the nonsignificant proactive pathway suggests that cyberhate may differ from forms of online aggression driven by entertainment or social reward. © 2026 The Authors

title: Worker-to-ergatoid differentiation is associated with reproductive maturation and DNA repair-related transcriptional remodeling in Reticulitermes chinensis
abstract: Termite reproductives provide a useful system for examining molecular changes associated with reproductive differentiation because secondary reproductives can arise from worker-like individuals. Here, we compared workers and worker-derived ergatoids of Reticulitermes chinensis to characterize transcriptional changes associated with the acquisition of reproductive status. Histological observations revealed developed gonads containing vitellogenic oocytes in female 10-day post-differentiation ergatoids and spermatids and spermatozoa in male 10-day post-differentiation ergatoids. Transcriptome sequencing, targeted gene set enrichment analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and RT-qPCR revealed caste-associated changes in the expression of genes annotated to DNA repair-related pathways. Gene sets associated with homologous recombination, p53/checkpoint signaling and mismatch repair were significantly positively enriched toward the ergatoid-associated end of the ranked gene list, whereas the Fanconi anemia-related repair gene set showed a positive but non-significant enrichment trend. Several mismatch repair genes, including MSH2, MSH6, and MLH1, showed higher transcript abundance in ergatoids, and MLH1 retained conserved sequence and domain features across representative insects. These findings indicate that worker-to-ergatoid differentiation is associated with reproductive maturation and coordinated transcriptional remodeling of DNA repair-related genes. This study identifies candidate genes and pathways for future functional investigations of genome-maintenance-related processes during reproductive differentiation in termites. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Teaching people to draw is teaching people to look
abstract: Artists have long observed that drawing facilitates a way of looking at the world more attentively. Psychological research has sought to evaluate this claim by investigating the association between drawing abilities and training, and performance on visuospatial tasks. This body of research literature has shown that some visuospatial abilities are enhanced in those that have better drawing abilities, specifically those that require integration of stored perceptual and cognitive schemas, and flexible visual attention. Longitudinal research has further shown that learning how to draw leads to changes in the way that visuospatial tasks are approached, suggesting that drawing involves strategies designed to circumvent the limits of perception. Such insights are valuable in the context of an environment that often precludes looking slowly and closely, and suggest that teaching drawing may be an effective way of teaching people how to look. © 2026

title: Computing aesthetic taste
abstract: Recent breakthroughs in computational and experimental techniques have produced major discoveries in the science of aesthetic taste. This paper reviews key findings from two complementary approaches: machine learning and large-scale human experiments. We argue that together these approaches represent a fundamental shift in computing aesthetic taste, from measuring preferences and choices to reconstructing the complex, high-dimensional representations that generate them. Using these representations, which we refer to as ‘taste spaces’, researchers can move beyond asking what people like to explaining why they like it, and how aesthetic taste is learned, structured, and transformed across individuals, cultures, and artificial systems. We conclude by discussing how these advances create new opportunities for addressing some of the defining scientific challenges of the coming decades, such as understanding the rich diversity of aesthetic taste across individuals and cultures, and the ways in which artificial intelligence increasingly distorts human taste. © 2026

title: LMGNN: Long-range graph modeling for recommender systems
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have become a dominant paradigm for collaborative filtering by propagating signals over user–item interaction graphs. Yet, two fundamental issues remain: (i) shallow propagation fails to capture informative long-range collaborative signals, while deep propagation tends to homogenize representations and causes over-smoothing; and (ii) global attention can be computationally expensive and may weaken structural inductive bias. In this work, we propose a depth-adaptive long-range graph collaborative filtering framework that treats multi-hop GNN representations as an ordered sequence along the depth axis and learns node-specific fusion weights via a degree-conditioned Mamba depth-gating network. Moreover, to enhance robustness without perturbing the sparse interaction graph, we construct a contrastive view by perturbing only the depth-fusion gate rather than applying dropout to depth tokens. Concretely, in the common two-depth case, we reformulate depth fusion as a sigmoid gate and perform lightweight stochastic and adversarial perturbations on the gate logits, while reusing the same propagation content. The overall objective combines a pairwise ranking loss with regularization and an importance-sampled InfoNCE regularizer. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that LMGNN significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines (up to 20.82%), validating the effectiveness of our proposed framework. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Computational models of hedonic evaluation: An explanatory–predictive framework
abstract: Hedonic evaluation underlies preferences across domains ranging from food and social stimuli to art. Increasing evidence suggests that these diverse judgements rely on common computational and neurobiological principles, motivating a unified perspective on how hedonic value is constructed. Computational modelling has become central to this endeavour by transforming conceptual theories into quantitative, testable accounts of how sensory information, prior experience, internal states and contextual factors give rise to subjective value. However, the rapid expansion of computational approaches has produced a heterogeneous landscape of models that differ in their assumptions, computational principles, explanatory ambitions and predictive performance. Here, we propose an explanatory–predictive framework for organising, comparing and evaluating computational models of hedonic evaluation. The framework characterises models according to two complementary dimensions: mechanistic explainability and empirical predictive performance. We also organise models into six broad families defined by their dominant computational principles. Finally, we argue that progress will depend less on competing modelling traditions than on integrating complementary computational principles into a general computational theory of hedonic evaluation. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: How AI amplifies, mitigates, and creates social biases: A tripartite framework
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in social life, shaping how individuals perceive themselves and others and influencing social dynamics that bear directly on equality and collective welfare. Yet its relationship to social bias is paradoxical: the very systems that can entrench and amplify long-standing prejudices may also be leveraged to challenge them, and may simultaneously generate entirely novel forms of bias. This review synthesizes recent empirical literature within a tripartite framework organized around the core pathways along which AI shapes social biases: AI design, lay beliefs about how AI operates, and processes of social evaluation and attribution. Drawing on these pathways, I outline three corresponding avenues for intervention: more equitable AI design, targeted adjustment of lay beliefs about AI capabilities, and redesign of social evaluation processes to account for the attribution biases that AI introduces. Together, these findings underscore the urgency of a socially informed approach to AI development and governance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Deep reinforcement learning-driven adaptive search algorithm for emergency rescue routing
abstract: Following natural disasters, emergency rescue route planning becomes substantially more challenging due to damaged transportation networks, urgent rescue demands, and the operational complexity of heterogeneous rescue resources. Efficient rescue decision-making under constraints including time windows, regional accessibility, and casualty survival risk is therefore of considerable practical significance. However, existing studies often suffer from inadequate modeling of casualty survival dynamics, excessive reliance on manually designed operator control strategies, and limited search robustness in highly constrained environments. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a reinforcement learning-assisted iterated greedy algorithm for heterogeneous rescue and route planning, termed Dueling Double Deep Q-Network Iterated Greedy (D3QNIG). First, a disaster rescue routing optimization model integrating casualty evacuation and relief material distribution is developed, where an injury-adaptive survival-risk mechanism is incorporated alongside capacity, time-window, and accessibility constraints. Second, a reinforcement learning-assisted iterated greedy framework is designed to adaptively control operator selection and destruction intensity during the destruction, reconstruction, and local search stages. Third, a state representation approach based on set attention pooling is constructed for variable-length and heterogeneous routing solutions, together with a hierarchical Dueling Double DQN decision architecture to enhance policy-learning stability and search effectiveness. Finally, a two-stage reward–acceptance decoupling strategy is introduced to alleviate the credit assignment issue and improve training stability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed D3QNIG achieves superior solution quality, faster convergence, and stronger robustness than benchmark methods, indicating its effectiveness for heterogeneous rescue route optimization in complex disaster scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Multi-modal knowledge-level representation learning for structure-oriented patent citation prediction
abstract: Patent citation prediction aims to identify prior patents that challenge the novelty of new patent applications. A citation is valid when the technical components in the new application are functionally and structurally similar to those disclosed in the prior patent. This component structure is conveyed through two modalities: the claim text and the patent figures. Existing methods predominantly rely on text and struggle to capture the graph-structured nature of patent components. We propose a Multi-Modal Knowledge-Level Patent Representation Framework. First, we construct a multi-modal component graph that links text-derived triples with figure-derived visual components via reference numerals. Second, we introduce a knowledge-level attention mechanism operating at the triple level, coupled with cross-modal attention that injects figure-grounded structure into token embeddings, jointly aligning the modalities and suppressing noise arising from legal characterizations in patent text. Finally, we introduce a re-ranking module that performs structure-oriented similarity reasoning over the fused representation. We introduce PatCite, the first citation dataset categorizing samples into “tree-structured” and “graph-structured” types. Under the dynamic full-corpus protocol, our method achieves macro Recall@1/Recall@10 of 14.4%/43.8% on PatCite, with a Recall@1 gain of 5.0 percentage points over the strongest fine-tuned baseline. © 2026

title: Assessing the applicability of existing design recommendations to AI companion design: A multi-method study
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of large language model (LLM)-based systems, AI companions have emerged as conversational agents designed to cultivate emotional connection rather than primarily to support humans in instrumental tasks. Because engagement with AI companions involves relational, emotional, and potentially long-term interactions, their design is consequential. Prior work has offered guidance for designing trustworthy and relational AI systems and has begun to examine design for AI companionship. However, while such work provides insights into possible design solutions, less is known about what makes AI companion design difficult as a design problem. To examine this challenge, we assessed the applicability of existing design recommendations from adjacent domains in the context of AI companion design. Our multi-method investigation unfolded across four phases: literature review, practitioner co-analysis, internal heuristic evaluation, and external expert assessment. Throughout this process, we synthesized nine design principle areas that surfaced tensions in the applicability of existing recommendations to AI companion design. Our findings show that ethical and UX-oriented considerations are deeply intertwined and often require context-sensitive application. We document a systematic, multi-method problem analysis that uses these principle areas as an analytic artifact to examine why existing recommendations cannot be directly transferred to AI companion contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Node-to-cluster contrastive learning with modularity maximization for graph clustering
abstract: Attributed graph clustering has advanced significantly through self-supervised graph contrastive learning. However, existing methods often face two key limitations: (1) direct reliance on raw topology and features makes models susceptible to noise and representation collapse; (2) the lack of multi-granularity modeling prevents the effective integration of local node consistency, meso-scale cluster semantics, and macro-level community structures. To address these challenges, we propose Node-to-Cluster Contrastive Learning with Modularity Maximization (NC-MGC). Specifically, our model first executes a graph optimization strategy that reconstructs an attribute-augmented adjacency matrix via KNN refinement and employs a graph Laplacian filter to suppress high-frequency noise. Then, our approach builds upon contrastive learning by introducing a hierarchical structure that simultaneously optimizes node-level and cluster-level representations. While node-level alignment maintains local consistency, the cluster-level contrastive module provides meso-scale semantic guidance by attracting matched cluster prototypes and repelling dissimilar ones, thereby enhancing inter-class discriminability. Finally, a global modularity maximization objective is integrated to capture macro-level community interactions, ensuring the structural cohesiveness of the learned partitions. Extensive empirical evaluations on six benchmark datasets demonstrate that NC-MGC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Robust hybrid graph fusion for multi-modal relation extraction via information bottleneck denoising
abstract: Mainstream Multi-modal Relation Extraction (MRE) methods often suffer from performance degradation. This is due to inherent inconsistencies, or ”modal incongruity, between visual and textual modalities, leading to inaccurate predictions. To address this critical challenge, we propose IBHF, a novel framework that actively denoises multi-modal inputs to purify robust relational signals. The core of IBHF is its pioneering Hybrid Multi-modal Graph (HMG). This structure synergistically fuses a heterogeneous graph, which captures fine-grained pairwise interactions, with a hypergraph that models key high-order group semantics. Critically, we devise an innovative graph denoising framework, IB-GD. It applies the Information Bottleneck (IB) principle to a unique contrastive learning objective. This strategy compels the model to learn a representation that is highly informative for the MRE task but minimally dependent on the noisy input. This process effectively mitigates the negative impact of modal inconsistencies. Our unified framework is applicable to both entity-entity (EE-MRE) and the more challenging entity-object (EO-MRE) extraction tasks. Extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets, MNRE and MORE, demonstrate the superior performance of our IBHF. Notably, on the more challenging MORE dataset, IBHF achieves an F1-score of 72.59%, setting a new state-of-the-art with a significant margin of 2.34%. On the MNRE dataset, IBHF also delivers SOTA-level performance, reaching the highest accuracy and an F1-score of 89.91%. By combining a hybrid graph structure with an IB-based structural denoising strategy, IBHF offers a robust and effective paradigm for handling noisy, real-world multi-modal data. Copyright © 2026. title: Machine learning surrogate models for Thermo-Elastohydrodynamic Lubrication in line contacts: Full-field prediction and reduced-order modelling
abstract: Conventional Thermo-Elastohydrodynamic Lubrication (TEHL) solvers for line contacts require solving coupled Reynolds–elasticity–energy equations, which typically take minutes per operating point. This limits their use in optimisation and system-level simulations. Moreover, accurate prediction of full-field quantities is essential: pressure profiles are required for fatigue analysis, film thickness distributions enable the proper translation of capacitance in measurements, and the heat fluxes are used in thermally coupled multiscale simulations. In this work, we develop and benchmark full-field surrogate models that generate 1D pressure and film thickness profiles and a 2D temperature-rise field using four architectures: MLP, generative CNN, POD-NN (linear reduction), and DLROM (autoencoder-based non-linear reduction). The models are trained on approximately 36,000 converged TEHL solutions spanning a twelve-dimensional input space of operating and material parameters, utilising robust outlier removal. All surrogates achieve a global R2>0.99 on the test set and compress inference times into the microsecond regime, delivering speed-ups of up to O(106) on CPU and O(107) on GPU relative to the numerical solver. Out-of-distribution testing demonstrates robust extrapolation capabilities, with maximum temperature errors below 1 °C and an RMSE below 0.8 °C when predicting beyond the training boundaries. The benchmark highlights clear trade-offs: the MLP and CNN are strong baselines on a fixed spatial grid; the POD-NN is particularly stable and fast for the high-dimensional temperature field but may smooth highly localised extrema; and the DLROM offers compact non-linear representations but exhibits higher extrapolation variance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Evolution and Uses of Rock Art Sites: Contribution of Morphogenic Mapping of Rock Walls
abstract: In this article, we present a new method for investigating rock art within the framework of site morphogenesis. Although numerous surveys of paintings and engravings have been conducted in archaeology since the twentieth century, few have taken into account the geomorphological characteristics of rock surfaces and their morphogenic evolution. Yet the processes responsible for these transformations directly interact with rock art. This approach therefore raises several questions: have the sites and their rock surfaces always been accessible? If not, from when until when were they accessible? Beyond parietal paintings and engravings, are there other traces of human activity? How are these related to the rock art? The method developed, based on the general geomorphological ground mapping’s codes, has been adapted for the analysis of painted and engraved rock walls at different spatial scales. The results demonstrate the relevance of such morphogenetic analysis of rock walls for the understanding of painted and engraved archaeological sites. At Rocher du Château (France, Savoie), phases of the rock wall’s evolution have been identified, which enable discussions about Neolithic and proto-historic frequentations contemporaneity with rock paintings, and their accessibility through time. At Bruguier rock shelter (France, Gard), seven phases of human activity, that are not visible on the ground, and numerous modifications were identified on the rock wall. The methodological and cartographic framework presented in this paper is grounded in an integrative approach to the study of evolving rock walls. Geomorphological analysis sheds light on the physical changes affecting the rock wall before, during, and after (pre)historic human occupation, while the cartographic framework is intended to be further developed through interdisciplinary collaboration. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Cura: The case for institutionalizing health and well-being in the arts & culture sector
abstract: A convergent body of evidence from clinical trials, epidemiological cohort studies, mechanistic science and emerging economic analysis demonstrates that arts and cultural engagement is a meaningful determinant of health. Yet the organisational infrastructure of arts and cultural institutions has not kept up with this science. Drawing on the historical example of how education became a permanent institutional vertical in arts and cultural organisations during the twentieth century, this paper argues that the evidence base for arts and health now meets a reasonable threshold for a parallel structural change: the creation within arts and cultural organisations of a permanent, staffed and resourced health and well-being vertical. The argument is normative in its institutional commitments, but deliberately pluralist in form. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Beyond exposure: familiarity and the ecology of food meaning in hierarchical environments – A military field study
abstract: Familiarity is commonly assumed to enhance food acceptance and reduce waste through repeated exposure. However, in institutional environments shaped by hierarchical norms and operational constraints, repeated contact may influence not only sensory responses but also the meanings and practices associated with food. This study examined how food-related evaluations and practices differed across military career stages characterized by different levels of accumulated institutional experience. A focused ethnographic approach was conducted with 113 Brazilian Army personnel classified as Early-Career (EC), Mid-Career (MC), and Advanced-Career (AC). Contextual observations and semi-structured interviews were analyzed through thematic coding complemented by supervised AI-assisted sentiment classification. Negative sensory and physiological sentiment remained relatively stable across career stages, while patterns of expressing and managing dissatisfaction differed among career-stage groups. In early-career personnel, consumption remained closely shaped by supervision and institutional expectations. Mid-career personnel developed more detailed, peer-supported evaluations and engaged more frequently in selective consumption and food discard. By advanced career, dissatisfaction persisted, but participants routinely modified and combined ration components to make meals more practical and acceptable under field conditions. Career-stage differences were not consistent with progressively greater liking; rather, responses to persistent dissatisfaction differed across groups characterized by different levels of accumulated institutional experience. These findings support a multidimensional and contextual interpretation of familiarity and extend consumer research on food acceptance in constrained, high-demand institutional environments. © 2026 The Authors

title: A flexibility-oriented scheduling framework for steel enterprises: an optimization model integrating onsite flexible loads and captive power plants
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources (RES), particularly wind and solar, has introduced significant variability and uncertainty to modern power systems, posing challenges for operational stability and economic dispatch. Industrial users, especially in the steel sector, are emerging as promising flexibility providers due to their high electricity consumption and growing electrification. This study proposes a source-load coordinated scheduling model for steel enterprises equipped with captive power plants (CPP), aiming to enhance system flexibility and improve renewable energy integration. Flexible operational models are developed for key energy-intensive processes-electric arc furnaces (EAF), air separation units (ASU), and rolling mills, and integrated with internal generation scheduling within a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) framework. The model jointly optimizes grid interaction, production-side load shifting, and captive generation dispatch to minimize total system cost and wind power curtailment. A case study based on a representative steel enterprise is conducted to evaluate the proposed approach. The results show that coordinated scheduling can effectively reduce system operating costs and improve wind power utilization. While relatively large improvements are observed when compared with an inflexible baseline, consistent performance gains are also maintained under more practical scenarios with partial flexibility. The findings indicate that coordinated control of industrial loads and captive generation can provide additional system flexibility and support renewable energy integration. The proposed framework offers a modeling perspective for analyzing the role of large industrial users in future low-carbon power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Data-centric AI in disaster management: Scalable Named Entity Recognition via LLM-based stacking and pseudo-label generation
abstract: This study presents a scalable Teacher–Student architecture for Named Entity Recognition (NER) that enables automatic information extraction from Turkish disaster-related social media texts. To reduce labeling costs, the collective intelligence of three large language models (Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5) is combined through a learnable stacking meta-classifier. On a 500-tweet manually annotated dataset, stacking reached a token-level Macro F1 of 0.9313 (0.9219 under leakage-free tweet-level grouped cross-validation), on par with the strongest individual model (0.9245) and clearly above a BERT baseline trained on the same data (0.8335). It was selected as the Teacher for its learnable per-class weighting, its stability across meta-classifiers and its robustness to single-provider outages. The Teacher’s discrete predictions were transferred to a more efficient BERT Student through hard-label pseudo-labeling, and this Student was then used as a zero-cost proxy labeler to scale the corpus to 17,000 tweets. On a fully isolated 300-tweet blind test set, the final model obtained an entity-level Macro F1 of 0.9160, against 0.8648 for the baseline trained only on manual labels. A size-matched controlled experiment isolates the source of this gain: labeling the same 3000 tweets with the model ensemble instead of a self-training labeler improves entity-level Macro F1 by 0.033 in all five random seeds ((Formula presented) ), whereas scaling from 3000 to 17,000 instances adds only 0.006. Label quality, rather than data volume, drives the improvement, and the approach offers a practical, low-cost route to rapid humanitarian needs mapping when annotated data is scarce. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: The neuroaesthetics of liveness
abstract: Live theatre, dance and music pervade to human culture. Building on a rich theoretical debate within theatre, performance and media studies, this review sketches out a psychological approach to understanding live experiences. It distinguishes physical liveness (presence in a here and now) from social liveness (sharing experiences with others). Recent mobile EEG studies on live dance performances and music concerts demonstrate that audience engagement during live performances is measurable as dynamic brain synchrony between co-present audience members or between audience members, music and movement. Differences in audience engagement between live and recorded performances (physical liveness) are measurable as looser or tighter slow wave neural synchrony. Conversely, social liveness can increase audience arousal, indexed by reduced power in the EEG alpha band during collective viewing of both live and recorded dance. These findings suggest that variable performance content and stable performance context engage dissociable neural mechanisms, attention and arousal respectively. Research on liveness originates in the performing arts but can be extended to the visual arts and to sport events. Physical and social liveness may facilitate those rare, memorable and transformative aesthetic experiences that are difficult to produce in lab-based environments. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: From facial synchronization to social conformity: A computational analysis of emotional contagion in online co-viewing
abstract: This study examines emotional contagion and social conformity in online co-viewing environments, where viewers can observe one another's facial expressions during shared media experiences. Using a 2 (group size: 3 vs. 8) × 3 (emotional valence: happy, neutral, mixed) between-subjects experiment, we applied deep learning–based facial expression analysis (DeepFace) to capture participants' emotional responses on a frame-by-frame basis. Emotional contagion was operationalized as frame-by-frame facial expression synchronization between participants and co-viewers. The results showed that facial expression synchronization was significantly higher in smaller groups and in the happy-valence condition, suggesting that emotional contagion occurred even without direct interpersonal interaction. Contrary to predictions based on classic conformity research, synchronization was stronger in smaller groups, indicating that visual social cues may operate differently in online co-viewing than in face-to-face settings. Time-lag analyses further showed that facial expression synchronization was strongest with no temporal delay and declined as the lag increased, suggesting that emotional contagion emerged rapidly during online co-viewing. These findings extend current understanding of emotional contagion and social conformity in video-mediated communication by showing that visually mediated emotional cues can shape shared affective responses in ways that differ from established patterns of face-to-face social influence. Methodologically, this study illustrated the usefulness of AI-based facial expression analysis for examining dynamic emotional processes during shared media experiences. The findings also provide practical implications for designing online co-viewing platforms that leverage visual social cues to enhance shared viewing experiences. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Behavior of Children with Down Syndrome During Preventive Dental Care: An Observational Study
abstract: Objective: To compare behavior guidance techniques (BGTs) applied to children with and without Down Syndrome (DS) during preventive dental care. Material and Methods: This observational, cross-sectional study included 40 children aged 2-6 years with and without DS. Heart rate and the dentist´s subjective evaluation were assessed in the waiting room, during the anamnesis, during the child's positioning, during the preventive procedure, and at the end of the preventive procedure. The Melamed´s Modified Behavior Scale was evaluated during the preventive procedure and the Frankl's Behavior Rating Scale (FBRS) was classified after dental care. The BGTs applied were evaluated by direct observation. Friedman and Mann-Whitney U tests and Spearman's Correlation Coefficient were applied. Results: A total of 76 attempts were required to perform the dental procedure for children with DS and 42 for children without DS. According to Friedman's test (p = 0.7385), there were no statistically significant differences in heart rate values across all children in the five situations analyzed. In the Mann-Whitney U test, statistically significant differences were found between the following variables: heart rate during anamnesis (p = 0.0166) and during the preventive procedure (p = 0.0009), and the highest values were obtained in children with DS in both cases. In Spearman's post-correlation coefficient, negative and statistically significant correlations were found between the values of the following variables: age, when compared with all heart rate during anamnesis (p = 0.016), in the child’s positioning (p = 0.018), preventive procedure (p = 0.027) and at the end of the procedure (p = 0.017). Conclusion: There was a difference between groups in relation to the behavior evaluated by the physiological method. The behavior guidance techniques applied were similar. © 2027, Association of Support to Oral Health Research (APESB). .

title: Attribution, zonation, and simulation of spatiotemporal distribution of negative oxygen ions in mountainous megacity: A case study of Chongqing, China
abstract: Negative oxygen ions (NOI) are key indicators of urban ecological quality. However, NOI dynamics in mountainous megacities remain poorly understood. A key challenge lies in translating complex environmental observations into interpretable knowledge for environmental planning rather than prediction alone. Therefore, we integrated few-shot learning, explainable AI (e.g., SHapley Additive exPlanations), and causal inference within an explainable GeoAI framework to identify NOI drivers and predict spatial patterns in Chongqing, China. Results revealed pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity, with low concentrations in southwestern urbanized areas and high values in forested mountains and river valleys of northeastern Chongqing. Attribution analysis identified elevation, curvature, relative humidity (RH), NO₂, and aerosol optical depth (AOD) as dominant drivers with model-derived nonlinear response thresholds (AOD > 273.67; NO₂ > 15.42; RH > 90.95%), beyond which predicted NOI responses changed markedly. Additionally, DML-based analysis estimated a positive treatment effect of middle elevations on NOI (+0.179 per unit, p < 0.001). Scenario simulations demonstrated that humidity enhancement and the integrated scenario yielded stronger responses than pollution mitigation or greening alone, and achieved a mean ΔNOI of 130.12 cm−3 with 76.25% of the area displaying gains. However, the integrated scenario increased inequality despite maximizing population-weighted benefits (106.99 cm−3), favoring sparsely populated mountainous regions (Gain = −28.76 cm−3, Gini = 0.0835). These findings underscore the capacity of explainable GeoAI for adaptive urban planning by linking environmental response interpretation, intervention evaluation, and spatial equity assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Different knowledge, different aesthetic experiences (and vice versa)?
abstract: Do different kinds of knowledge lead to different aesthetic experiences (and vice versa)? This paper addresses this question by examining the role of (art) knowledge within an interactionist perspective. Contemporary theories increasingly conceptualize aesthetic experience as emerging from the interaction between perceiver, stimuli, and contexts rather than from isolated properties of artworks or perceivers alone. Despite this theoretical shift, empirical research still often investigates knowledge as a characteristic of perceivers. We argue for a broader and more integrative understanding of knowledge that distinguishes between internal knowledge, residing within the perceiver, and external knowledge, provided by the environment. Internal knowledge encompasses prior experiences, competencies, and beliefs, whereas external knowledge includes information embedded in contextual features such as exhibition settings, curatorial texts, and other environmental cues. Drawing on empirical literature and illustrative findings from museum and laboratory studies, we show that aesthetic experiences are shaped by the continuous interaction between these two forms of knowledge. External knowledge can activate relevant internal knowledge, guide expectations, and support interpretation, while internal knowledge influences how viewers engage with artworks, seek additional information, and construct meaning. This reciprocal process can generate new insights that become incorporated into future knowledge structures, thereby influencing subsequent aesthetic encounters. Our perspective aligns with phenomenological perspectives emphasizing situated and embodied engagement with the world. We conclude that variations in aesthetic experiences give rise to differences in knowledge (and vice versa), and more specifically, that this is due to the interaction between internal and external forms of knowledge during aesthetic experiences. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Emotions in flipped and lecture-based math courses
abstract: Background: Emotions play an important role in learning. Activating teaching methods, such as flipped learning, can provide positive learning experiences but also pose emotional challenges to students. Aims: This intensive longitudinal study investigated 1) how students’ emotional valence before a learning event, learning mode (individual, peer, teacher-led), teaching implementation (lecture-based vs. flipped), and physiological arousal (electrodermal activity, EDA) during the learning event related to emotional valence after a learning event, and 2) how EDA varies across within-event segments and teaching implementations during learning events. Sample: Participants were 69 students enrolled in an engineering mathematics course implemented either as lecture-based (n = 34) or flipped learning (n = 35). Methods: Students reported their emotional states via a smartphone application and wore smart rings to measure EDA. A series of multilevel binomial logistic regression and linear mixed-effects models were analyzed across 546 learning events, totaling 827 h of data. Results: Positive pre-event emotional valence predicted positive post-event emotional valence. Teacher-led events were associated with more positive post-event emotional valence than individual events, particularly in the lecture-based group. The main effect of the teaching implementation was not significant. EDA did not show robust associations with post-event emotional valence; however, lecture-based events showed a clearer decline in EDA across event segments than flipped learning events. Conclusions: The results highlight the importance of supporting social and individual learning processes and examining physiological arousal as a temporal learning-event process rather than a simple proxy for post-event emotional valence. © 2026 The Authors

title: Renewable energy infrastructure in desert-gobi-arid zones: A review of physical-ecological transformations and ecosystem resilience
abstract: Desert-Gobi-Arid (DGA) zones are key regions for large-scale photovoltaic and wind-energy development and represent fragile dryland ecosystems with strong water limitation and slow ecological recovery. This paper critically reviews the ecological impacts of renewable-energy infrastructure in DGA-type landscapes, using China’s DGA bases as the main empirical context and evidence from ecologically comparable drylands for comparison. It examines how photovoltaic and wind facilities affect surface environments, ecological processes, and carbon cycling. Existing studies indicate that these facilities influence local microclimate, soil conditions, vegetation dynamics, and carbon exchange through shading, surface disturbance, airflow alteration, and hydrothermal redistribution. These impacts are site- and scale-dependent and are jointly controlled by facility layout, disturbance intensity, surface substrate, vegetation background, climate conditions, and management practices. Under low-disturbance design and effective management, they may support soil moisture retention, vegetation recovery, soil carbon accumulation, and ecosystem resilience, while higher disturbance may increase ecological risks such as water stress and habitat fragmentation. This review links direct emission reductions with indirect ecological effects and governance considerations and provides a case-based reference for assessing renewable-energy development in fragile dryland environments. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Differentially private encrypted-domain image retrieval with key-rotation robust token learning
abstract: Cloud-based image retrieval should protect visual confidentiality without sacrificing search accuracy over outsourced image collections. Existing encrypted-domain (ED) methods limit direct content exposure, but encrypted descriptors and queries may still reveal statistical information. This paper proposes a differentially private ED image retrieval framework with key-rotation robust token learning. Images are protected on the client side through randomized JPEG-domain encryption, and descriptors are extracted directly from encrypted JPEG bitstreams. The ED descriptor combines variable-length integer (VLI) code-length features, total zero count per block (TZCPB) statistics, and Huffman-symbol frequencies. Before cloud release, the complete descriptor is clipped and perturbed using a calibrated Gaussian mechanism, providing feature-level (ε, δ)-DP for the released descriptor. Query images use the same client-side pipeline, so the cloud receives only privatized ED descriptors. Client-side processing protects the image and privatizes its descriptor. The cloud then performs embedding generation, indexed similarity search, and fixed-size encrypted result delivery. A Vision Transformer learns retrieval embeddings from privatized tokens, while key-rotation training improves robustness to unseen encryption keys and cipher-domain shifts. Repeated-query leakage is reduced through descriptor reuse, privacy-budget tracking, and fixed-size responses. Experiments on Corel10K-a, Corel10K-b, ImageNet100, and MIRFLICKR-25K demonstrate improved performance over reproduced ED baselines, reduced representation-level leakage, strong visual obfuscation, and limited latency under a configurable privacy-utility trade-off. © 2026 The Author(s). title: The inclusion of transaction costs in conservation compensation schemes as illustrated with tigers
abstract: Human expansion into wildlands has intensified human-wildlife conflicts (HWC), resulting in a need for mitigation. Compensation, a mitigation tool, faces challenges due to underestimated costs, including transaction costs. We developed a framework to identify transaction costs based on successful post-conflict compensation scheme elements, focusing on Verification, Process, and Compensation. As part of this framework, we identified key parameters determining transaction costs. We applied this framework to quantify transaction costs in a human-tiger conflict (HTC) compensation scheme near Pilibhit Tiger Reserve, India, by surveying HTC-affected persons or their families in 2022. Most participants were unaware of the compensation process, found it difficult, and expressed dissatisfaction with government agencies. The average waiting cost at the 2022 USD rate was $583 per claimant, with a 101-day delay, and total transaction costs exceeded 40% of the compensation amount received. Because compensation increased with claimant effort rather than need, awareness, or socioeconomic status, the results point to an equity concern: administrative burdens disproportionately reward those able to navigate costly processes. Therefore, reducing procedural barriers is essential to ensure fair and equitable access to compensation schemes. This framework provides a scalable tool to improve conservation compensation programs globally by identifying interventions that reduce transaction costs, thereby alleviating the impacts of HWCs across diverse regions and species. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Unlocking reversible hydrogen storage in penta-hexa-hepta graphene through lithium functionalization
abstract: A newly proposed two-dimensional carbon allotrope, penta–hexa–hepta graphene (PHH-Gr), is systematically investigated as a potential hydrogen storage medium using first-principles calculations. The thermodynamic, dynamical, and thermal robustness of PHH-Gr are verified through cohesive energy evaluation, phonon spectrum analysis, and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. Lithium decoration is found to be energetically favorable, with Li atoms strongly anchored at heptagonal hollow sites and minimal clustering tendency due to large Li–Li separations and high diffusion barriers. Electronic structure analysis demonstrates substantial charge transfer from Li to the PHH-Gr substrate while preserving metallic characteristics. Hydrogen adsorption on pristine PHH-Gr is weak, whereas Li functionalization markedly enhances H2 binding through polarization and charge-transfer effects. Each Li species can adsorb up to four hydrogen molecules, yielding a maximum gravimetric and volumetric hydrogen storage capacities of 10.75 wt% and 91.2 g L−1, respectively. Thermodynamic analysis using differential adsorption energies reveals that while the maximum storage capacity requires cryogenic temperatures or elevated pressures, a practical working capacity of approximately 6–8 wt% is achievable under reversible cycling conditions (298 K, 30 bar for uptake; 373 K, 3 bar for release). AIMD simulations also verify that the weakly bound fourth H2 molecule per Li site desorbs at room temperature under ambient pressure. These results highlight Li-decorated PHH-Gr as a robust and efficient material for reversible hydrogen storage applications with a working capacity exceeding DOE targets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: From rules to reasoning: A systematic review of agent-based and LLM-empowered simulation of public collaboration
abstract: Agent-based simulation of public collaboration is consolidating into a distinct research pathway, with rule-based agent-based modeling (ABM) and large language model (LLM)-empowered simulation emerging as two technological lineages. Whether they are competitive, substitutive, or complementary has not been systematically examined. Drawing on 1,064 public collaboration simulation studies, we apply a “2 × 4” framework to compare the two lineages across research agendas, theory–model relationships, simulation paradigms, and knowledge contributions. The comparison reveals a pronounced divergence: rule-based work concentrates on outcome explanation (79.5%) and policy evaluation (64.4%), whereas LLM-empowered work is overwhelmingly methodological (98.5%) and foregrounds deliberation and consensus building (35.8%), with meta-theoretical inquiry at 38.8% versus 7.5% in rule-based work. These headline differences persist under temporally controlled comparison against same-period, early-stage, and more strictly matched rule-based windows, with support attenuating in the smallest window, and they are consistent with paradigm expansion rather than substitution: simulation instruments not only answer research questions but shape the questions that can be asked. For information processing and management, the review supplies the evidence base and reporting standards needed to evaluate generative simulation as an instrument for studying collective information behavior, and identifies hybrid ABM–LLM architectures, behavioral validation protocols, and dynamic-network modeling as priority agendas. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Velocity-dependent evolution of central wear and lateral third-body retention in a carbide-bonded graphene/steel reciprocating contact
abstract: Although velocity-dependent friction and wear of carbon coatings are widely documented, spatially differentiated third-body evolution remains poorly understood. In this study, interrupted ball-on-disc reciprocating tests were combined with geometrical measurements, friction and wear analysis, and SEM/EDS characterization to investigate the interfacial evolution of a carbide-bonded graphene (CBG) coating sliding against a 304 stainless-steel ball at velocities of 0.5, 2, and 8 mm/s. The results reveal that a dual-zone morphology consistently developed at the sliding interface, comprising a central damage region (Region I) and lateral debris-retention regions (Region II). At a given cycle number, higher velocities were associated with a wider affected region, earlier local coating breakthrough, and greater material removal in Region Ⅰ. In Region II, debris redistribution and broad, flattened, and locally interconnected debris morphologies developed earlier, followed by the formation of a visually more compact surface at later stages. At higher sliding velocities, the friction coefficient transitioned earlier to a lower, relatively stable regime. At 15k cycles, the friction coefficient was approximately 0.21 at 0.5 mm/s and 0.15 at 8 mm/s, while cumulative specimen and ball wear volumes were highest at 8 mm/s. These results show that sliding velocity primarily altered the timing and pathway of dual-zone interfacial evolution. Earlier friction stabilization at higher velocities was accompanied by accelerated coating damage and substrate involvement. Thus, lower friction did not indicate improved wear protection, revealing a trade-off between friction stabilization and coating durability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Uncovering heterogeneity in students’ metacognitive ability within social-emotional learning: A rasch measurement analysis
abstract: This study aims to uncover the heterogeneity of students' metacognitive ability within the framework of Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) using the Rasch measurement model. While previous studies have tended to treat metacognitive ability as a homogeneous construct, limited attention has been given to latent individual variability through modern psychometric approaches. This study employed a descriptive quantitative design involving 536 secondary school students in Bali, Indonesia. Data were collected using a metacognitive ability scale and analyzed using the Rasch Rating Scale Model to estimate individual abilities and item difficulty on a common logit scale. In addition to person and item calibration, the analysis included reliability indices, rating scale diagnostics, principal component analysis of residuals, differential item functioning by gender, and person-item mapping through the Wright Map. The findings indicate that students' metacognitive ability is heterogeneously distributed and forms multiple distinct ability strata. The instrument demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties and was capable of differentiating levels of student ability meaningfully. Visualization through the Wright Map shows that student abilities are continuously distributed from low to high levels, without clustering in a single category. Furthermore, some students exhibited ability levels that exceeded the difficulty of most items, suggesting the need to develop more challenging items to enhance measurement precision. This heterogeneity may reflect variations in self-regulation development, learning experiences, and socio-emotional factors. In addition, some observable gender-related patterns emerged, although these tendencies should be interpreted cautiously and within their sociocultural context. Overall, the findings highlight the contribution of Rasch measurement in revealing latent variations that are often obscured by aggregate scores and provide empirical support for differentiated learning strategies aimed at fostering reflective, autonomous, and adaptive learners. title: PinNet: Edge-optimized skin lesion segmentation
abstract: Accurate skin lesion segmentation is an important prerequisite for computer-assisted dermoscopic image analysis, yet achieving reliable segmentation under stringent computational constraints remains challenging. Dermoscopic images frequently exhibit irregular lesion morphology, weak boundary contrast, heterogeneous pigmentation, and artifacts such as hair and illumination variations, whereas many high-performing segmentation networks incur substantial parameter and computational costs. To address this trade-off, we propose PinNet, a lightweight encoder–decoder network for skin lesion segmentation. PinNet incorporates a Morpho-Spectral Harmonic Layer (MSHL) that combines multi-scale Morphic Convolutions with frequency-domain feature modulation to capture irregular lesion structures while improving robustness to imaging variations. In addition, a Dual-perspective Block Attention Module (DBAM) jointly recalibrates channel-wise and spatial features and performs lightweight local refinement to improve boundary representation. Experiments on the ISIC2017 and ISIC2018 datasets demonstrate that PinNet achieves DSC scores of 88.47% and 90.10%, respectively, with only 0.050 M parameters and 0.068 GFLOPs. Under a unified training protocol, PinNet achieves a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off compared with the evaluated conventional and lightweight segmentation baselines. These results suggest that PinNet provides a compact solution for resource-constrained dermoscopic image segmentation. The implemented code is publicly available at: https://github.com/IMOP-lab/PinNet. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Love, faith, and cognitive dissonance in interfaith relationships: A CBT-informed analysis of Indonesian digital narratives on the song Mangu
abstract: Interfaith relationships in Indonesia involve negotiations among romantic attachment, religious commitment, moral and spiritual identity, family belonging, and sociocultural expectations. Although interfaith relationships have been widely examined from sociological, theological, and legal perspectives, less is known about how these tensions are cognitively, emotionally, and spiritually narrated in naturally occurring digital spaces. This study examined Indonesian YouTube users’ narratives concerning interfaith relationships, religious conversion, hidayah, sociocultural pressure, and separation in comments surrounding the song Mangu by Fourtwnty featuring Charita Utami. An exploratory corpus analysis using Voyant Tools was first conducted on a broader corpus of 16,356 Indonesian-language YouTube comments to identify lexical patterns and support data familiarization. Subsequently, qualitative content analysis was conducted on 51 criterion-selected comments through inductive thematic analysis, followed by a bounded, non-diagnostic CBT-informed interpretation. Five themes were identified: struggles in maintaining interfaith relationships; religious conversion as a pathway to relational and spiritual alignment; sociocultural and familial pressure; hidayah and changes in belief; and firmness of belief followed by relational separation. Across the narratives, similar contexts of religious difference were assigned different meanings and followed by multiple pathways, including continued negotiation, maintenance of separate religious identities, conversion, reconciliation, and separation. A CBT-informed reading suggests that these pathways may be understood through interactions among cognitive appraisal, core and intermediate beliefs, emotional responses, coping processes, and meaning reconstruction. However, conversion, hidayah, and separation were not treated as inherently adaptive, pathological, or clinically verified processes. The study contributes a context-sensitive framework for interpreting digital narratives at the intersection of religion and intimacy and highlights the need for ethically neutral counseling support that addresses intrapersonal, interpersonal, and sociocultural dimensions. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. title: Perceived influence of the principle of confidentiality in extrajudicial conciliation: A quantitative study among conciliators in the Peruvian Amazon
abstract: This study aims to determine the perceived influence of the principle of confidentiality on the practice of extrajudicial conciliation from the perspective of conciliators in a city of the Peruvian Amazon, considering its relevance for effective dispute resolution and the strengthening of trust between parties. Methods: A quantitative approach was adopted, with a nonexperimental cross sectional design; the sample consisted of 80 conciliators selected through nonprobabilistic convenience sampling based on strict active procedural eligibility criteria, and data were collected through a 15 item Likert scale questionnaire assessing relational, institutional, and ethical dimensions, demonstrating high and uniform internal reliability with a total Cronbach's alpha coefficient of 0.75. Furthermore, the instrument allowed for a comprehensive assessment of perceptions associated with procedural integrity and professional conduct. Results: The findings show that 77.5 of participants perceive a high level of influence of confidentiality in conciliation processes; moreover, the relational dimension reached a unanimous 100 high rating, while institutional (65) and ethical (67.5) dimensions also showed elevated levels, although with identifiable margins for improvement. Additionally, the nonparametric Wilcoxon signed rank test evaluated against a theoretical neutral midpoint of 3.0 confirmed statistically significant differences with respect to the baseline (Z = 7.874; p < 0.001), yielding a very large overall effect size (r = 0.88) that reinforces the practical magnitude and robustness of the results. Conclusions: Therefore, confidentiality constitutes a structural pillar in conciliation practice; however, its full consolidation requires institutional strengthening, regulatory clarity, and specialized ethical training, providing empirical evidence from a subnational Latin American context and proposing a replicable three dimensional model for future research in alternative dispute resolution mechanisms and professional practice, as well as informing public policy and institutional decision making processes, particularly in decentralized justice systems and emerging governance frameworks. title: Can a wealth tax reduce CO2 emissions in Europe?
abstract: We analyse the potential of wealth taxes to reduce CO2 emissions through two transmission channels: the inequality channel, which links reductions in wealth inequality to lower emissions, and the consumption channel, which operates through the effect of wealth taxes on consumption by top wealth holders. We simulate the effects of various wealth tax designs over one- and ten-year horizons using harmonized microdata from 22 European countries. Our analysis accounts for survey non-response bias, heterogeneous rates of returns across households, and behavioural responses to taxation. We find that, through the inequality channel, a recurrent annual progressive wealth tax could reduce annual CO2 emissions by 7.5%–14.7% after 10 years relative to a no-tax scenario, depending on tax progressivity. Through the consumption channel, the average reduction is 1.5%–3.6% after 10 years. In addition, we show that the revenues generated cover the entire investment gap identified by the European Commission's ‘Fit for 55’ emissions reduction programme. These findings highlight the potential of wealth taxes to serve a dual purpose: curbing wealth concentration and contributing meaningfully to climate mitigation and justice, by focusing on high-net-worth households that account for a disproportionate share of emissions. © 2026 The Authors. title: Non-progressive influence maximization in temporal social networks
abstract: The influence maximization (IM) problem involves identifying a set of key individuals in a social network who can maximize the spread of influence through their network connections. In this paper, we focus on the temporal non-progressive IM problem, which considers the temporal nature of real-world social networks and the special case where the influence diffusion is non-progressive, i.e., nodes can be activated multiple times. While influence diffusion in many real-world social network scenarios is non-progressive, such as in marketing campaigns promoting updated products and public health campaigns promoting healthier lifestyle choices, this problem has received limited attention in prior research. We first extend an existing diffusion model to capture the non-progressive influence diffusion in temporal social networks. We then propose a method, named TNIMRL, which employs deep reinforcement learning and temporal graph embedding to solve the temporal non-progressive IM problem. In particular, we propose a novel algorithm that effectively leverages temporal graph embedding to capture the changes in temporal social networks and seamlessly integrates with deep reinforcement learning. The extensive experiments on different types of real-world social networks demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier Ltd.
