title: LENS: A graph-based ciphertext semantic retrieval scheme with lightweight representations
abstract: With the rise of cloud outsourcing and pre-trained language model-driven semantic retrieval, high-quality semantic search over encrypted data remains challenging. Existing schemes either depend on keywords or coarse representations that cannot capture complex semantics, or use high-dimensional dense vectors with linear scanning, causing prohibitive computation. Although tree indexes reduce latency, their rigid partitioning may miss neighbors. Meanwhile, encrypted graph indexes still lack explicit leakage characterization and security adaptation. To address these issues, we propose a ciphertext semantic retrieval scheme that jointly integrates robust semantic representation learning, lightweight vector compression, and graph-based navigation. Specifically, we construct low-dimensional compact semantic vectors for encrypted computation through hard-negative-driven sample construction, global-local collaborative optimization, and multi-level self-distillation. We then build an encrypted graph index whose retrieval workflow is isomorphic to hierarchical navigable small world graph (HNSW) search. We further characterize the leakage boundary of graph-based retrieval and prove chosen-keyword attack security under an IND-CPA secure inner-product primitive. Experiments on the TREC corpus demonstrate a better trade-off among query efficiency, retrieval quality, and scalability than scan-based and tree-based baselines. These results suggest that high-performance ciphertext semantic retrieval requires the joint design of representation learning, index topology, and security modeling. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Does fast mapping accelerate lexical integration? Evidence from spoken and written novel words
abstract: Fast mapping (FM) is an encoding paradigm in which a novel label is learned incidentally by inference. Some studies have interpreted FM training as capable of bringing forward the integration of novel words into existing lexical networks relative to typical consolidation timelines, although the evidence is mixed. We conducted three experiments to investigate whether FM promotes faster lexical integration compared to explicit encoding (EE). Experiments 1 and 2 extended prior orthographic fast mapping work, testing whether the rapid lexical integration claim generalises to the auditory (spoken) domain. Participants learned novel spoken words through either FM or EE training. Lexical integration was assessed using a pause detection task immediately after learning, one day later, and one week later (Experiment 1 only). Neither experiment found evidence that FM led to more rapid lexical integration compared to EE. Experiment 3 was a direct replication of previous orthographic fast mapping research ( Coutanche and Thompson-Schill, 2014 ), using a semantic categorisation task to assess integration of visually presented novel words. Again, we found no advantage for FM in promoting rapid lexical integration. Across all experiments, EE consistently produced superior explicit memory for the novel words compared to FM. These findings fail to support claims that FM-based training allows novel words to bypass time-dependent consolidation processes and become rapidly integrated into the mental lexicon. The results are consistent with complementary learning systems accounts positing that lexical integration typically benefits from offline consolidation, regardless of encoding method. title: Politicization of duan lolat culture as an electoral strategy in the 2024 regional elections in Tanimbar Islands Regency, Indonesia
abstract: This study examines how Duan Lolat culture was politicized as an electoral strategy during the 2024 Regional Head Election in the Tanimbar Islands Regency, Maluku, Indonesia. The research employs a qualitative-interpretive case study approach to understand the transformation of customary kinship relations into instruments of political mobilization within the context of local democracy. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with twelve key informants consisting of political actors, customary leaders, election organizers, and community members, supported by limited participant observation and document analysis. The data were analyzed using thematic coding techniques and triangulation procedures to ensure credibility and analytical consistency. The findings reveal that Duan Lolat culture has experienced a functional shift from a form of social capital grounded in solidarity and reciprocity into a political instrument for electoral mobilization. The study identifies three principal mechanisms of politicization: structural informality, relational emotionality, and material-symbolic hybridity. Through these mechanisms, customary kinship networks were strategically utilized by political elites to construct symbolic legitimacy, strengthen emotional loyalty, and mobilize electoral support based on kinship obligations rather than programmatic political preferences. The study also identifies a normative gap referred to as kosong, namely a regulatory space between customary law and formal electoral regulations that enables identity-based political mobilization to operate informally beyond institutional oversight. These findings indicate that while local democracy in Tanimbar procedurally functions in a stable manner with relatively high voter participation, substantively it remains vulnerable to identity polarization, patronage politics, and cultural manipulation. This research contributes to the broader literature on identity politics, social capital, and hybrid governance by demonstrating how indigenous cultural systems can be transformed into symbolic and political resources within local electoral contestation in Indonesia. title: Milking consumers' willingness to pay for greener dairy: Udderly important or a moo-t point?
abstract: In an effort to combat their environmental footprint, leading associations in the United States dairy industry have committed to implementing new technology in manure management and achieving Net Zero production by 2050. These pledges can increase the cost of producing milk, but it is unclear if these production changes can garner price premiums from consumers. This study uses a choice experiment to analyze consumers' preferences for a gallon of milk described by four attributes: organic production, GHG emissions reduction, nutrient runoff reduction, and price. An online survey was administered across four U.S. regions to individuals who regularly purchase milk from grocery stores. We find evidence of heterogeneity in preferences and conduct several market segment analyses. A consumer segment characterized by higher socioeconomic status and environmental attitudes shows substantially higher WTP for organic production and GHG reductions than a lower-socioeconomic-status, less environmentally engaged segment, which actually exhibits disutility from organic production. A secondary analysis suggests that education is the main determinant of increased WTP for organic production, while environmental attitudes likely drive WTP associated with GHG reductions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Social-ecological resilience and environmental justice in Bangladesh: A multi-site analysis of sand mining governance
abstract: As global demand for sand reaches an estimated 50 billion tonnes annually, the pressure on fluvial and coastal ecosystems has created a significant sustainability crisis. This study examines the environmental and socioeconomic impacts of sand mining in Bangladesh, a deltaic country where rapid urbanization has transformed sand into a multi-billion-dollar industry. Combining Social-Ecological Systems (SES) and Environmental Justice (EJ) frameworks, the research uses a qualitative case study approach across three ecologically distinct sites: Chandpur (river confluence), Sandwip (estuarine island), and Cox's Bazar (mainland coast). Data from 39 semi-structured interviews and field observations show that unregulated extraction is reported and observed as coinciding with a self-reinforcing (positive) feedback loop of increased riverbank erosion and habitat loss that respondents associate with harm to the livelihoods of marginalized fishers and farmers. The results reveal a triple failure of justice: distributive (unequal erosion burdens), procedural (exclusion from leasing decisions), and recognitional (marginalization of local ecological knowledge). Additionally, an analysis of the Balumohal and Soil Management Act (2010) uncovers critical institutional issues, including political patronage and poor coordination between the Department of Environment and local authorities. By highlighting community stories of adaptation and displacement, this study contends that sustainable resource management must shift from top-down, revenue-focused models to participatory, justice-driven frameworks that safeguard the resilience of rural social-ecological systems. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Assessment of multi-stage telescopic control rods in a pebble bed reactor, Part I: Mechanical design, neutronic assessment, and economic analysis
abstract: The low power density of Pebble-Bed Reactors (PBRs) results in larger Reactor Pressure Vessels (RPVs) and reactor buildings in comparison to other Generation IV concepts. Multi-stage Telescopic Control Rods (TCRs) have been proposed to reduce both the size and complexity of both the RPV and reactor building to reduce construction costs. This work seeks to explore the neutronic feasibility and economic impact of a three-stage TCR design in the 200 (Formula presented) Generic Pebble Bed Reactor (GPBR-200). Modeling of the reactor from startup to the equilibrium core was conducted using Serpent 2 and kugelpy. A wide range of TCR geometries using fresh boron carbide were found to bring the core to a subcritical state following a steam ingress scenario, assuming a uniform distribution of steam throughout the core and no prompt change in core temperatures. Loss of Boron-10 in the control rods was found to be insignificant up to 20 years but became neutronically significant by the reactor’s 30-year maintenance period. However, the depleted control rods were still capable of bringing the core to a subcritical state following a steam ingress scenario. A top-down economic analysis based on cost estimates from the Modular High Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactor (MHTGR) program was then used to assess the economic impact of TCRs when introduced at various stages of reactor design completion. Subject to underlying assumptions, incorporation of TCRs resulted in an estimated 1.7%–4.3% savings, with earlier adoption of TCRs in the design phase resulting in greater savings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Transformative learning strategies in health education: Health Literacy and Information Discernment among tertiary students
abstract: This study evaluated the impact of transformative learning strategies on the health literacy and information discernment of tertiary students at North Eastern Mindanao State University (NEMSU) – Cantilan Campus. While conventional health education often focuses on the passive transmission of factual knowledge, this research explored the effectiveness of pedagogical strategies grounded in Mezirow's Transformative Learning Theory (TLT), which emphasize critical reflection and the deconstruction of personal health assumptions. A quasi-experimental matching pretest-posttest control group design was implemented, involving 200 participants divided into experimental and control cohorts. The experimental group utilized reflective journals, collaborative case studies, and thematic health modules, while the control group received traditional didactic instruction. Data were gathered through a validated 50-item instrument designed to measure health knowledge and reflective insight. Findings revealed that the experimental group's mean scores improved from 22.10 (SD=4.12) to 37.70 (SD=3.45), whereas the control group's scores increased from 21.50 (SD=4.30) to 32.10 (SD=4.05). Statistical analysis, including an independent samples t-test (p=0.037) and a normalized gain (N-gain) test (t=5.894, p < 0.001), indicated a statistically significant difference in learning outcomes between the two groups with a large effect size (d =1.45). Observations from student journals further suggested an increased capacity for the critical evaluation of health information. These results indicate that integrating reflective teaching practices into the curriculum can significantly enhance health literacy and analytical discernment skills among tertiary students. This study aligns with Sustainable Development Goals 3 (Good Health and Well-Being), 4 (Quality Education), and 10 (Reduced Inequalities), suggesting that transformative pedagogical approaches provide a viable framework for addressing contemporary health literacy challenges in a university setting. title: Enhancing college students’ reflective thinking through online visualized collaborative argumentation: An exploratory study
abstract: In this era of technological advancements, how to better support students in argumentation-based computer-supported collaborative learning using emerging interactive technology to develop their reflective thinking has become an important issue in talent development. This study was embedded in the Cognition of Multimedia Learning course, and involved a pre- and posttest experiment with 56 college students to investigate the effects of visualized collaborative argumentation on their reflective thinking. The relationships between students’ argumentation and changes in their reflective thinking were also examined. Moreover, the differences in cognitive performance in argumentation among students with different levels of change in reflective thinking were explored using epistemic network analysis. The findings revealed that visualized collaborative argumentation significantly enhanced students’ reflective thinking. Especially, the higher the students’ level of engagement in rebuttal, the greater the impact on their reflective thinking. Moreover, according to the changes in reflective thinking behavior scores, K-Means cluster analysis determined a high-level change group (N = 33) and a low-level change group (N = 23). The findings revealed that the high-level change group outperformed the low-level change group in cognitive performance. Students with high-level change in reflective thinking are more adept at illustrating ideas through examples or attributes to avoid unclear understanding by others; they are more able to make direct rebuttals and evaluations, or to ask counter-questions; they show more rigor in deduction, pursuing the sufficiency of evidence; and they are good at using divergent thinking to break through thinking limitations. This exploratory study suggests that online visualized collaborative argumentation may have potential for supporting college students’ reflective thinking. The findings offer preliminary implications for the design of instructional strategies aimed at fostering reflective thinking development. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: RSD-YOLO:A Lightweight Model for Rail Surface Defect Detection
abstract: With the rapid development of the railway industry, ensuring the operational safety of railways places increasingly stringent demands on the efficiency and accuracy of rail surface defect detection. To address the low efficiency of traditional inspection methods and the imbalance between computational complexity, model lightweighting, and detection accuracy in existing deep learning–based approaches, this paper proposes a lightweight rail surface defect detection model termed RSD-YOLO. Built upon YOLO11n, the proposed model introduces the HSFPN module into the neck to enhance multi-scale feature fusion while maintaining a lightweight architecture. In the backbone network, ADown downsampling and the RFE receptive field enhancement module are integrated to improve the detection performance of small-scale rail defects. Furthermore, an Ultra-LSPPF lightweight pooling module and a redesigned detection head based on MBConv convolutions are employed to systematically reduce model complexity while enhancing overall performance. Experimental results on the rail surface defect dataset demonstrate that, Compared with the original YOLO11n, RSD-YOLO reduces the number of parameters, FLOPs, and model size by 62%, 57%, and 58%, respectively. In terms of detection metrics, the proposed model increases Precision from 73.2% to 76.7%, corresponding to an absolute gain of 3.5 percentage points and a relative improvement of 4.8%. Meanwhile, mAP@0.5 changes from 79.9% to 79.2%, showing only a slight decrease of 0.7 percentage points. The proposed model achieves an inference speed of 142 FPS, indicating that RSD-YOLO provides a favorable trade-off among model lightweighting, inference efficiency, Precision, and mAP@0.5, making it suitable for real-time rail surface defect detection with substantial engineering application value. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Domain-specific risk tendencies show little association, directly or indirectly, with domain-specific self-esteem
abstract: Both risk taking and self-esteem have traditionally been considered general traits that apply across domains of behaviors, although each has separately been considered as multidimensional or domain specific at times. The domain specificity of both constructs is debated, though, and the theoretical relationships between self-esteem and risk-taking remain unclear. The present study (N = 191) looked at relationships across both domain specific self-esteem and domain-specific risk taking, as well as a theoretically hypothesized possible moderating variable of relative state (perceived ability/need). General self-esteem and general risk taking were assessed concurrently. Specific domains of self-esteem and risk taking were mostly correlated with, yet distinct from, the general constructs with a few notable exceptions. General self-esteem was not correlated with general risk taking, and—although social and physical appearance self-esteem differentially associated with evaluations of their relative state in those areas—domain specific self-esteem was largely not correlated with specific types of risk taking. Moderation analyses did not support an indirect relationship between self-esteem and risk taking. Better measures for the relative state model of risk and more firmly grounded theoretical models of self-esteem and risk taking may be needed in order to better understand if and how they are related. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Effect of Bi2O3 content on the physical properties and gamma ray shielding performance of Na2O-Bi2O3-B2O3 glasses
abstract: The radiation-shielding properties of 20Na2O-(80-x)B2O3-xBi2O3 glasses (x = 0, 10, 20, and 30 mol%) were investigated using Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations over the photon-energy range of 50-5000 keV. The linear and mass attenuation coefficients (LAC and MAC), mean free path (MFP), half- and tenth-value layers (HVL and TVL), effective atomic number (Zeff), transmission factor (TF), and radiation protection efficiency (RPE) were evaluated. Increasing the Bi2O3 content improved photon attenuation because of the higher density and atomic number introduced by bismuth. NaBiB30 exhibited the best gamma-ray shielding performance, with LAC values of 22.34 cm−1 at 50 keV and 0.150 cm−1 at 5000 keV, together with the lowest HVL, TVL, and MFP values among the investigated compositions. In contrast, the calculated fast-neutron removal cross section decreased from 0.0985 to 0.0820 cm−1 with increasing Bi2O3 content, indicating a trade-off between gamma-ray attenuation and fast-neutron removal. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: GCN-T: A fusion prediction model for GCN-Transformer optimized using an improved sine cosine algorithm
abstract: Air quality forecasting serves as a critical foundation for public health protection and environmental management decisions. Accurate forecasts provide a scientific basis for pollution warnings and effectively mitigate the adverse effects of polluted air. However, traditional models struggle to integrate the temporal and spatial correlations of pollutant data effectively. While standalone graph convolutional networks (GCNs) can capture spatial correlations, they fall short in mining temporal dynamic features. Conversely, Transformer models are adept at capturing temporal dependencies but lack effective modeling of spatial correlations. Furthermore, parameter tuning for both types of models often relies on empirical settings, making them prone to overfitting and stuck in local optima, which results in prediction accuracy and model stability that do not meet practical application requirements. To address these issues, this paper deeply integrates GCN and Transformer to construct a new air quality prediction model. In this model, the Transformer uses a multi-head self-attention mechanism to calculate the dependency weights between the features of various pollutants. After symmetric normalization, these weights directly serve as the adjacency matrix for the GCN. The two components iterate alternately at each layer, with attention guiding graph convolution and the graph convolution output fed back to the attention mechanism at the next layer, thereby achieving cross-layer collaborative modeling of feature relationships and graph structures. To enhance model performance, this paper employs an improved sine cosine algorithm (SCA) for adaptive parameter optimization. First, multiple population mechanisms are introduced to expand the search range of SCA, effectively accelerating the algorithm’s convergence. Second, random parameters are incorporated to ensure that SCA favors global search during the initial iterations, thereby preventing the algorithm from getting trapped in local optima. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed model, experiments were conducted using eight datasets containing air quality data, comparing the proposed model with seven existing mainstream prediction models. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms the comparison models across all evaluation metrics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: EFL teachers’expectation and recommendation: Intercultural curriculum implementation
abstract: This study examines EFL teachers' expectations and recommendations for the intercultural dimension of Emancipated Curriculum, understood as the curriculum's emphasis on linking English language learning with local culture, global communication, respect for diversity, student agency, differentiated learning, and project-based tasks. Responding to concerns about uneven curriculum enactment across Indonesian schools, the study used a convergent mixed-methods design. An online questionnaire generated 172 valid responses from secondary English teachers in 11 provinces, while the regional focus was placed on East Java and West Nusa Tenggara because these two provinces contributed the largest survey clusters and all focus group discussion data. FGDs involved 27 teachers in East Java and 32 teachers in West Nusa Tenggara. Open-ended questionnaire responses and FGD transcripts were coded into meaning units, producing 308 coded items: 178 expectations and 130 recommendations. The findings show that teachers generally supported the reform and associated it with improved educational quality, better student futures, critical thinking, creativity, independence, and more contextual learning. However, their support was conditional on clearer operational guidance, practical and sustained teacher training, improved infrastructure, reduced administrative burden, curriculum evaluation, and stronger stakeholder collaboration. Regional and school-type comparisons indicated similar priorities across contexts, but West Nusa Tenggara teachers more often emphasized detailed training and infrastructure support, while East Java teachers more often highlighted administrative alignment and school-level coordination. The study contributes to curriculum implementation research by showing that teachers' expectations and recommendations provide diagnostic evidence for refining reform. Successful enactment requires not only policy dissemination but also locally responsive professional development, equitable resources, and feedback mechanisms that position teachers as central agents in intercultural EFL curriculum implementation. title: Differences in the orthographic expectation effect during auditory novel pseudo-character learning in Mandarin-speaking prelingually deaf children with cochlear implants
abstract: While the orthographic expectation effect (OEE) is well-documented in alphabetic languages, its manifestation in logographic systems like Chinese, particularly among children with atypical auditory experience such as those with cochlear implants (CIs), remains unexplored. This study investigated whether Mandarin-speaking children can form orthographic expectations for Chinese characters through auditory exposure alone, comparing 36 prelingually deaf children with CIs and 36 age-matched children with normal hearing (NH). Using a novel-word learning paradigm, participants were auditorily exposed to pseudo-characters. Their reaction times in a subsequent lexical decision task were analyzed using Generalized Linear Mixed-Effects Models (GLMM) to compare auditorily learned versus unlearned phonograms and non-phonograms, as well as predictable versus unpredictable phonetic radicals. Results revealed that both groups exhibited significantly faster reaction times for auditorily learned phonograms, and this expectation effect emerged robustly only when the phonetic radicals were highly predictable. However, children with CIs demonstrated markedly slower responses than their NH peers across all conditions. These findings demonstrate that Mandarin-speaking children can form robust orthographic expectations through auditory input regardless of hearing status. Although children with CIs exhibit slower baseline processing speeds due to underlying perceptual constraints, the magnitude of their orthographic expectation effect remains remarkably intact and comparable to their normal-hearing peers. Ultimately, this highlights the resilient nature of cross-modal reading acquisition, offering crucial neurocognitive insights for designing adaptive literacy interventions in clinical and educational settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Tell me what you read, and I will tell you what you remember: Evidence for personalized embeddings in memory modelling
abstract: Computational models of memory have achieved considerable success by formalizing how traces are encoded, cued, and retrieved. However, the role that individual linguistic experience plays in shaping representational structure has been relatively understudied. Where the issue has been examined, most models assume that a common population-level semantic space suffices, effectively treating individual variation in language experience as noise rather than signal. We test the theoretical adequacy of this assumption. In a large-scale experiment ( N = 478), participants completed a cued recall task in which identical target words were paired with cues drawn from eight different genre-specific semantic spaces (mystery, fantasy, horror, literary fiction, romance, science fiction, thriller, and non-fiction). Participants reported their reading habits across the eight genres, and personalized semantic representations were constructed by weighting genre-specific corpora proportionally to each participant's reading profile. Two complementary analyses were conducted. In a model-free analysis, cosine similarity computed within each participant's personalized semantic space predicted recall and omission outcomes more reliably than similarity derived from generic semantic spaces. In a computational analysis, substituting personalized representations into the embedded Computational Framework of Memory improved cue–target-level predictions over generic alternatives, accounting for approximately 4 percentage points more explained variance. These findings provide proof of concept that variation in individual linguistic experience shapes semantic structure in ways that are both behaviourally detectable and computationally tractable. More broadly, they suggest that the predictive limits of memory models may reside not only in their retrieval mechanisms but also in the fidelity of the representations they assume. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Pursuit and burnout: How goal orientation influences academic pressure in students
abstract: This study comprehensively investigated the relationship between students' goal orientation and their corresponding experience of academic pressure, emphasizing how distinct motivational frameworks impact psychological stress within modern academic settings. Recognizing that goal-driven behavior can simultaneously inspire exceptional achievement and inadvertently heighten emotional strain, this research aimed to shed light on how students' varied motivational orientations structurally align with their perceived academic demands. A descriptive-correlational research design was employed to capture these dynamics, involving a sample of 225 college students systematically selected through simple random sampling techniques. Data collection was facilitated using two standardized and highly reliable instruments: the Academic Stress Scale and the Achievement Goal Questionnaire-Revised (AGQ-R). Descriptive statistics were utilized to examine the general baseline trends in students' goal orientation and stress levels, while Spearman's rank-order correlation determined the exact nature, strength, and direction of the relationship between the two primary variables. Findings revealed that students generally demonstrated a high level of goal orientation, with a particularly strong emphasis placed on mastery-oriented goals. Concurrently, participants reported notable academic pressure stemming from intense personal expectations and the perceived social importance of academic success. Crucially, a significant positive correlation emerged between goal orientation and academic pressure, demonstrating that increased achievement motivation is frequently accompanied by heightened student stress. These results clearly indicate that while a strong goal orientation contributes positively to students' engagement and drive, it may also manifest as severe emotional strain if not properly balanced. Understanding this complex psychological dynamic is essential for designing supportive academic environments, offering vital insights for educators, counselors, and institutional policymakers aiming to cultivate a holistic learning climate that encourages high achievement without compromising long-term student health. title: Beyond the final product: AI-Enabled Learner Traces as Assessment Evidence in Project Management Education
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in project management education (PME), especially in digital learning environments where learner activity can be captured as process data. This matters because project management learning involves collaboration, coordination, decision-making, reflection, and professional judgement, which are difficult to assess through final outputs alone. This systematic mapping review examines how AI-generated or AI-mediated learner data are collected, analysed, and used for assessment-related purposes, and identifies the educational implications reported in the literature. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searches were conducted in Web of Science, Scopus, ERIC, and IEEE Xplore for studies published between January 2016 and November 2025. Nineteen studies met the inclusion criteria. The review identified five categories of AI-enabled learner data and assessment-relevant evidence: human–AI dialogue and prompt-based interaction logs, adaptive and personalised learning process data, project artefacts and revision traces, reflective, self-report, and course feedback evidence, and standardised task, output, and scoring data. These categories are treated as different layers in the data-to-evidence process rather than as learner traces in a narrow technical sense. Future-oriented conceptual data systems were identified as an emerging possibility but were treated separately from reported learner data and assessment evidence. Across the included studies, data were analysed using natural language processing, machine learning, rule-based techniques, learning analytics, and generative AI/LLM-based prompting, and were used to generate feedback, indicators, recommendations, and scoring support. Reported benefits mainly relate to formative feedback, improved visibility of learning processes, and more timely instructional support. However, the evidence base remains limited and uneven, with important gaps in validity, fairness, transparency, and longer-term educational effects. Overall, AI in PME is used not simply to automate assessment, but to broaden how learner activity is captured, interpreted, and used to support process-oriented assessment and pedagogical judgement. © 2026 The Authors

title: From disposition to action: The role of trait and state reactance in pro-choice protest participation in Poland
abstract: Governmental restrictions on individual freedoms often elicit heterogeneous public responses. While some individuals mobilize collectively, others remain passive. The present study examines whether stable personality differences in trait reactance explain variability in protest engagement in response to abortion restrictions in Poland. Drawing on psychological reactance theory, we test a mediation model in which trait reactance predicts state reactance, which in turn predicts protest-supportive attitudes and collective action participation. Autonomy orientation and frustration with injustice were included as related dispositional variables to test the specificity of the proposed trait–state relationship. A sample of 586 participants completed measures of trait reactance, autonomy orientation, frustration with injustice, state reactance, and self-reported protest behavior. Structural equation modeling revealed that trait reactance positively predicted state reactance, which was strongly associated with favorable protest attitudes and higher participation. The indirect effect of trait reactance on participation via state reactance and attitudes was significant, whereas the direct effect was not. Autonomy orientation did not predict state reactance when controlling for trait reactance, providing evidence that the trait–state association was not explained by autonomy orientation. These findings suggest that sensitivity to freedom restriction is a key dispositional factor underlying collective action in response to political constraints. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Achieving superior piezoelectric temperature stability in Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3-based piezoceramics via mixed phase boundary engineering
abstract: A long-standing challenge for Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3 (BNT)-based ceramics is that constructing a single morphotropic phase boundary (MPB) makes it difficult to simultaneously achieve high piezoelectric constant d 33 and superior piezoelectric temperature stability, which hinders their industrial applications. Herein, a novel strategy is proposed to mitigate the above trade-off by designing a mixed phase boundary strategy that integrates the multi-MPB components (abbreviated as M-BNT) to construct polymorphic polar domains. By this strategy, the M-BNT ceramic not only possesses a high d 33 of 180pC/N and a large depolarization temperature T d of 145°C, but also exhibits outstanding thermal stability of in-situ d 33. The competitive residual stress related to the mismatch of shrinkage rate and coefficient of thermal expansion during sintering and cooling, provides the driving force for the development of polymorphic polar domains. Our work offers a viable strategy for developing BNT-based piezoceramics that simultaneously exhibit a high d 33 and superior piezoelectric temperature stability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: BCF-CDAN: bidirectional cross-modal fusion and conditional domain adversarial network for multimodal cross-subject emotion recognition with EEG-fNIRS
abstract: Emotion recognition is essential for affective brain-computer interface (BCI), yet poses significant challenges. Specifically, emotion processing involves complex temporal dynamics and spatial brain networks. Therefore, it’s difficult to decode human emotions. Furthermore, individual differences limit the generalizability of cross-subject emotion recognition. In addition, the feasibility of EEG-fNIRS for fine-grained emotion recognition remains underexplored. To address the above issues, this study proposed an interpretable multimodal cross-subject emotion recognition model—the bidirectional cross-modal fusion and conditional domain adversarial network (BCF-CDAN). The proposed framework explicitly exploited the high temporal resolution of EEG and the high spatial resolution of fNIRS. Specifically, modality-specific convolutional neural networks were first employed to emphasize the temporal information of EEG and the spatial information of fNIRS. A multi-stream module and a one-stream module were then designed to achieve cross-modal fusion. The multi-stream module employed bidirectional cross-attention to capture interactive correlations between EEG temporal features and fNIRS spatial features, while the one-stream module used self-attention to learn a global discriminative representation. Subsequently, a conditional domain adversarial network (CDAN) combined with maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss was applied to achieve cross-subject distribution alignment. Results on the two self-collected EEG-fNIRS datasets, TMVED3 (three-class task) and TMVED8 (fine-grained eight-class task), showed that BCF-CDAN achieved cross-subject accuracies of 80.14% and 53.13%, respectively, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, the interpretability analysis revealed cross-modal dependencies between EEG temporal features and fNIRS spatial features. Overall, the approach leveraged modality-specific strengths, offering a generalizable and interpretable strategy for brain signal integration. Our code is available at: https://github.com/ThreePoundUniverse/BCF-CDAN . © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Lean limit extension Aspects of gasoline direct injection (GDI) engine with hydrogen fraction
abstract: An experimental investigation was conducted on a spark-ignition gasoline direct injection (GDI) engine equipped with hydrogen port fuel injection (PFI) to investigate the effects of hydrogen enrichment on combustion characteristics, thermal efficiency, and exhaust emissions under lean-burn operation. Gasoline–hydrogen blends with different hydrogen mass fractions were tested at varying equivalence ratios, while spark timing was adjusted between 14° and 35° bTDC to compensate for hydrogen’s higher flame speed. The results showed that hydrogen addition accelerated combustion, shortened combustion duration, and significantly extended the lean operating limit. However, hydrogen enrichment generally increased nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions because of higher in-cylinder combustion temperatures. Under homogeneous combustion conditions, hydrogen was supplied through port fuel injection (PFI) in the intake manifold with a start of injection (SOI) of 210° during the suction stroke, while the gasoline direct injection (GDI) SOI was set at 330° during the engine suction stroke. With a spark timing of 22° bTDC, 5.17% hydrogen by mass fraction reduced nitric oxide emissions by 0.29 g/kW-h and improved the hydrocarbon–NOx emission trade-off. Stable engine operation was achieved at an equivalence ratio of 0.55. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Narratives of workplace conflict: A mixed-methods analysis of HEXACO and Dark Triad personality predictors
abstract: Workplace conflicts are common, yet most evidence links personality to broad conflict management styles rather than to how concrete episodes unfold. We used a mixed-methods design to examine whether Dark Triad and HEXACO traits predict the content and course of real conflicts. Hungarian employees ( N = 318, 31.1% male, 68.9% female, M age = 35.24, SD = 10.34) completed personality measures and provided written narratives of a workplace conflict in which they were directly involved. Narratives were inductively coded into indicators of conflict context, process, outcomes, and narrative structure, and binary logistic regressions were used to examine associations with personality traits. Personality traits were more strongly related to how conflicts unfolded and were interpreted than to their structural features, such as who was involved or what triggered the conflict. Interpersonal traits from the HEXACO model showed the most consistent associations with conflict dynamics, emotional responses, and relationship outcomes. Dark Triad traits showed selective but limited associations with conflict processes, offering little evidence for broad predictive advantages beyond broader personality dimensions. Overall, the findings suggest that workplace conflict is not only enacted but also interpreted through the lens of personality, highlighting the importance of integrating dispositional and situational perspectives in research on organizational conflict. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: ViLID: Multimodal misinformation detection with complementary input- and rationale-level inconsistency signals
abstract: Multimodal misinformation on social media platforms often exploits subtle inconsistencies between text claims and accompanying images, such as repurposing authentic images out of context. Traditional vision–language models (VLMs) optimized for similarity can overlook these discrepancies. To address this challenge, we introduce ViLID, a vision–language inconsistency detector that combines a raw multimodal pathway with complementary rationale-derived signals rather than relying on rationales alone. ViLID employs two complementary signals: an embedding-level inconsistency score and a rationale-level inconsistency score, derived from structured rationales generated by large language models (LLMs) for both text and images. This approach integrates explicit inconsistency features with fused multimodal representations and incorporates an alignment regularization term that reduces inconsistency on truthful pairs. We evaluate ViLID on Fakeddit and MMFakeBench. The full model achieves the strongest overall performance, while the ablation results indicate that rationale-derived signals primarily improve error balance and the preservation of truthful samples by reducing the over-flagging of benign mismatches. Lastly, we translate our model's scores into practical moderation operating points, illustrating relevant precision/recall/workload trade-offs that inform effective deployment strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Engaging youth in end-of-life care: The 3 Wishes Project experience
abstract: Background Citizen engagement can create a community of compassion for dying hospitalized patients. Objectives To describe a family co-designed end-of-life intervention engaging schoolchildren, and characterize dying hospitalized patients and their terminal wishes. Methods This cohort study partnered a healthcare organization and educational institution to voluntarily engage students attending senior, middle, junior, and Montessori schools in an end-of-life care program. The 3 Wishes Project involved hospital staff and family members eliciting and implementing wishes to honor dying patients. Age-appropriate engagement involved student-led acts of compassion. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Results From June 2024–May 2026, 481 patients were enrolled, aged 65.4 (16.8) [mean (standard deviation)] years. The most common diagnoses were neurologic or neurosurgical (175, 36.4%), cardiovascular or vascular (97, 20.2%) and trauma (59, 12.3%). Of 2305 elicited end-of-life wishes, 2280 (98.9%) were implemented. Personnel eliciting wishes included nurses (169, 35.1%), social workers (152, 31.6%) and the project coordinator (99, 20.6%). Common wishes were tributes and keepsakes (820, 35.6%), acts to humanize the patient (374, 16.2%) and facilitating connections (248, 10.8%). The project coordinator as a child life specialist offered bereavement resources for children with dying hospitalized relatives, coached families and staff on sensitive communication about death and grief, and liased with the school. Students engaged in this end-of-life program for 125 (26.0%) of decedents, participating in 162 (7.1%) wishes by creating compassion cards, lavender sachets, crochet hearts and personalized memory boxes. Conclusions Community engagement in this adaptation of the 3 Wishes Project involved family member co-design and student partnership to help with terminal wishes for dying hospitalized patients. title: Perceived need and measured well-being: How well do subjective rankings capture relative poverty?
abstract: Subjective well-being rankings are widely used to target social protection programs, yet their ability to capture relative welfare and wealth remains debated. This study compares three commonly used subjective ranking methods: self-, peer-, and elite-based poverty rankings, against consumption- and wealth-based measures using a large household survey in Ethiopia, where about 20 households per village were ranked from most to least “needy” by themselves, their peers, and community leaders. We assess concordance between subjective and conventional welfare rankings and explore sources of divergence. Subjective rankings align more with relative wealth than consumption and with total rather than per capita welfare, suggesting they overlook household composition. Among the three subjective ranking methods, elite-based rankings best capture conventional measures, although overall concordance between subjective and welfare-based rankings remains weak. Subjective rankings also better reflect relative deprivation among households exposed to covariate shocks. A composite index combining all three modestly improves concordance with standard metrics. We find suggestive evidence that information asymmetry, favoritism, and welfare dynamics partly explain discrepancies between subjective rankings and conventional welfare measures. These findings offer important insights to improve targeting in data-scarce settings. © 2026 The Authors

title: A hybrid HEART method based on large-scale group decision-making to estimate human error probabilities in the railway driving process
abstract: The hybrid Human Error Assessment and Reduction Technique (HEART) is widely used to estimate the Human Error Probability (HEP). In this technique, the Assessed Proportion Of Affect (APOA) is determined by fusing evaluators’ opinions using the Dempster-Shafer (D-S) evidence theory. However, when evaluators’ opinions diverge significantly, the aggregated results from the D -S evidence theory may fail to align with the views of any individual evaluator. This can undermine the reliability of the outcomes. In cases with a large number of evaluators, this problem is particularly prominent. To address this issue, the large-group HEART (LG-HEART) method is proposed, which first facilitates consensus-building among a large cohort of evaluators, then fuses their opinions using the D -S evidence theory. Specifically, the LG-HEART method incorporates an evidence-similarity-based clustering technique to classify evaluators into several subgroups and a centralized evidence-based feedback consensus model to mitigate divergences among evaluators. By doing so, the LG-HEART method effectively mitigates the adverse impact of unreliable outlier opinions, thereby yielding more accurate HEP estimates in scenarios where critical operations demand the participation of numerous evaluators. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: CCA-ID: Confidence-calibrated adaptive intrusion detection with selective routing for IoT networks
abstract: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) deployments has extended the cyber-attack surface. In resource-constrained IoT monitoring environments, maintaining always-on deep or ensemble-based intrusion detection can be challenging for high-rate, real-time traffic. This study presents CCA-ID, Confidence Calibrated Adaptive Intrusion Detection which integrates calibrated decision confidence with selective, resource-aware inference for IoT intrusion detection. CCA-ID combines an isotonic-calibrated logistic regression gate, heterogeneous heavy learners including DNN, XGBoost, and LightGBM, and a stacking meta-classifier within a class-specific confidence-driven routing mechanism. High-confidence samples are finalized by the lightweight calibrated gate, whereas low-confidence samples are selectively routed to the heavy ensemble for deeper analysis. The proposed CCA-ID is evaluated on the large-scale Gotham Dataset 2025, using a final experimental dataset comprising 7,792,438 packet-level samples across 18 traffic classes. Experimental results indicate that CCA-ID achieves 89.92% accuracy, 61.70% macro F1-score, and 98.93% macro ROC-AUC, while routing only 6.28% of samples to the heavy ensemble. The method also achieves an Expected Calibration Error (ECE) of 7.66%, showing improved confidence reliability for routing decisions. An inference-time analysis further indicates that CCA-ID achieves a 13.94 × speedup over the always-on heavy stack on a fixed stratified subset of the held-out test set. Overall, CCA-ID provides a calibrated trade-off between selective inference and heavy-model invocation for IoT intrusion detection. It reduces unnecessary heavy-model usage while maintaining strong threshold-free discriminative performance under severe class imbalance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: FALSAx-IWS: Framework for accuracy and logic synthesis (LS) estimation of approximate adders on image watermarking systems
abstract: An image watermarking system (IWS) protects digital content by embedding an imperceptible watermark into a host image, thereby supporting copyright enforcement, authenticity verification, and data integrity. This work introduces FALSAx-IWS, a framework for estimating the accuracy and logic-synthesis of approximate adders for Haar-based image watermarking. The objective is to close the gap between watermarking robustness studies, which commonly emphasize only visual quality and attack resistance, and hardware-oriented design exploration, which requires evaluating area, power, and accuracy trade-offs before implementation. FALSAx-IWS explores multiple approximation levels for the approximate discrete Haar Wavelet transform (AxDHWT), its inverse (AxIDHWT), and an optimized transform (AxODHWT), integrating sixteen approximate adder architectures and a Random Forest regressor to estimate the impact of each configuration. The evaluation considers 105 host images and several attack classes, including additive Gaussian noise, JPEG compression, median filtering, speckle noise, and salt-and-pepper noise. The revised statistical analysis shows that the proposed approximation-aware selection preserves the accepted normalized cross-correlation interval of (Formula presented) while reducing synthesis complexity by up to (Formula presented). The best low-power level-3 configuration reaches 0.00364 mW at 65 nm, 1.25 V, and 200 MHz, while maintaining robust watermark recovery. These results indicate that FALSAx-IWS can support real-time and embedded watermarking scenarios by reducing arithmetic complexity while preserving resistance to relevant image-processing attacks. The proposed method is therefore positioned as a generalized AxC-driven design pipeline for secure, resource-constrained, Haar-based image processing systems. © 2026 The Authors. title: Multi-dimensional resilience assessment and spatio-temporal risk transmission in interconnected power grids under high-level renewable penetration
abstract: Decarbonization is reshaping the structure and risk profile of power networks. Using complex network analysis and dynamic simulation, this study assesses the resilience of China’s provincial power grids under uncertainty. It combines historical data for 2005–2023 with scenario simulations for 2030–2060 to examine network evolution, risk propagation, and restoration during the energy transition. The results show that: (1) Interprovincial electricity dependence increases as the network evolves from dispersed connections to coordinated multipath transmission. High renewable-energy penetration strengthens block-structured dependencies and concentrates risk along critical transmission corridors; (2) The low-carbon transition provides only modest gains in initial disturbance resistance but more consistently reduces post-restoration residual and cumulative losses; (3) Resilience outcomes vary across regions and disturbance types because of differences in exposure, cascading propagation, and restoration benefits. Line failures are more recoverable, whereas persistent supply-side shocks cannot be fully mitigated through network reconfiguration alone; and (4) System losses depend on failure locations, cascading pathways, and restoration sequences rather than the scale of initial failures alone. Static topological indicators therefore cannot fully capture systemic risk. These findings support critical-corridor protection, system-wide topology optimization, flexible-resource deployment, and region-specific resilience planning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Approximating highly inapproximable problems on graphs of bounded twin-width
abstract: For any ε>0, we give a polynomial-time nε-approximation algorithm for MAX INDEPENDENT SET in graphs of bounded twin-width given with an O(1)-sequence. This result is derived from the following time-approximation trade-off: We establish an O(1)2-approximation algorithm running in time exp⁡(Oq(n2)), for every integer q⩾0. Guided by the same framework, we obtain similar approximation algorithms for MIN COLORING and MAX INDUCED MATCHING. In general graphs, all these problems are known to be highly inapproximable: for any ε>0, a polynomial-time n1−ε-approximation for any of them would imply that P=NP [Håstad, FOCS '96; Zuckerman, ToC '07; Chalermsook et al., SODA '13]. We generalize the algorithms for MAX INDEPENDENT SET and MAX INDUCED MATCHING to the independent (induced) packing of any fixed connected graph H. In contrast, we show that such approximation guarantees on graphs of bounded twin-width given with an O(1)-sequence are very unlikely for MIN INDEPENDENT DOMINATING SET, and somewhat unlikely for LONGEST PATH and LONGEST INDUCED PATH. Regarding the existence of better approximation algorithms, there is a (very) light evidence that the obtained approximation factor of nε for MAX INDEPENDENT SET may be best possible. This is the first in-depth study of the approximability of problems in graphs of bounded twin-width. Prior to this paper, essentially the only such result was a polynomial-time O(1)-approximation algorithm for MIN DOMINATING SET [Bonnet et al., ICALP '21]. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Experimental study on high-pressure constant-volume combustion of ultra-lean methane-air mixtures under different ignition delay times
abstract: Low-concentration coal mine gas is typically characterized by low combustion rate and significant heat losses. Studies on ultra-lean methane-air combustion under high-pressure constant-volume and turbulent conditions remain limited. This study experimentally investigates turbulent combustion characteristics and heat losses under elevated initial pressures, where turbulence intensity is regulated by adjusting the ignition delay time t d. Results reveal that varying t d non–monotonically affects both flame development and rapid combustion stages. While turbulence plays a primary role in shortening the rapid combustion duration, its intensification does not monotonically reduce heat losses, since the flow field influences both the convective heat transfer coefficient and the temperature difference between combustion products and chamber walls. At t d = 1 s, weak turbulence attenuates the promoting effect of temperature rise on flame development, with the most pronounced effect observed at P 0 = 0.5 MPa and 0.7 MPa. Further turbulence intensification yields a greater reduction in combustion duration than that resulting from the combined effect of temperature rise and weak turbulence. Within initial pressures of 0.3–0.7 MPa, the coupled effects of temperature rise and turbulence reduce the combustion duration by 20.6%–54.0% and increase P max by 10.3%–19.2% relative to quiescent combustion. An initial pressure of 0.6 MPa is found to minimize heat losses for the 6 vol% methane–air mixture. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Urban park biodiversity preferences and trade-offs: A comparison between residents and professionals using Adaptive Choice-Based Conjoint analysis
abstract: Urban parks are important biodiversity hotspots as well as recreational spaces in cities. It is desirable for urban residents to derive pleasure from parks that also embody biodiversity values due to their ecological and health benefits. Despite the evidence that urban residents are happier and healthier when they have access to green spaces of good quality, it remains unclear how residents prioritise biodiversity when considering the joint effects of other green space attributes, and how these priorities differ from those of landscape/ecology professionals. We used Adaptive Choice-Based Conjoint (ACBC) analysis to examine how biodiversity was prioritised in trade-offs with other important park attributes among residents and professionals. The ACBC study was conducted in Hangzhou (N = 187) and Shanghai (N = 194), two cities in eastern China. Utility values and average importances were estimated using Hierarchical Bayes (HB). While both residents and professionals preferred higher biodiversity levels, biodiversity improvements from poor to moderate yielded greater utility gains than from moderate to rich. Residents prioritised facilities over biodiversity when making trade-offs, whereas professionals prioritised biodiversity as the most important park attribute and valued it significantly more than residents. In both groups, preferences for higher biodiversity were associated with preferences for fewer facilities, denser tree cover, and low-maintenance, wild-looking landscapes. Urban park planning may prioritise biodiversity enhancement in biodiversity-poor sites over further enhancement in biodiversity-moderate sites to optimise resource allocation. Professionals should account for differences between their own preferences and those of residents, while recognising the importance of managing biodiversity-amenity trade-offs and supporting the coexistence of both objectives. © 2026

title: Assessing urban carbon emissions from a water-energy-food nexus perspective: An intensity-structure-pressure framework for differentiated management in Chinese cities
abstract: The classic Kaya identity lacks integration of water-energy-food (WEF) nexus elements, and conventional geographical zoning fails to capture the structural heterogeneity of urban carbon emissions. To address these gaps, this study extends the Kaya identity to construct an intensity–structure–pressure chain decomposition equation covering the energy-economy-agriculture-land-water system. A three-stage analytical framework, macro-driving decomposition, structure type identification, and conditional associations analysis, is then applied. Using city-level panel data from China (2000−2020) and integrating Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) decomposition, Partitioning Around Medoids (PAM) clustering, and panel quantile regression, the study decomposes the structural factors of carbon emissions, identifies city clusters with homogeneous resource structures, and reveals heterogeneous factor associations across emission levels. The results indicate that: (1) Economic growth emerges as the dominant positive factor in carbon emission growth, with its decomposed proportion exhibiting significant north–south regional divergence; (2) cities can be classified into six distinct structural typologies in terms of resource use and emissions, high-emission clusters are typically constrained by a dilemma of improving efficiency while still expanding in scale, whereas low-carbon clusters have systematically entered a phase of decoupling economic growth from carbon emissions; and (3) regression analysis further suggests that the direction and magnitude of the conditional association of the same decomposition factor differ significantly between low- and high-carbon cities, with the marginal association of most factors diminishing as emission levels increase. This study provides a basis for transcending the limitations of geographical proximity and establishing intensity-structure-pressure-oriented, precise, and differentiated carbon management strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Hematological and biochemical profiling of iron deficiency anemia among adolescent girls: A cross-sectional study from rural areas of the Jungle Mahal, West Bengal, India
abstract: Background Iron deficiency anemia (IDA) is a major public health concern among adolescents, adversely affecting physical growth, cognitive abilities, and maternal future health. Our study evaluated the incidence of anemia and the hematological and biochemical parameters of iron deficiency among adolescent girls in the Jungle Mahal area of West Bengal, India. Methods A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted between May 2022 and June 2025 among 372 adolescent girls. Blood samples were analyzed for hemoglobin, complete blood count, and iron-status biomarkers, including serum iron (μg/dL), ferritin (μg/dL), TIBC (μg/dL), UIBC (μg/dL), and transferrin saturation (%). Results The overall prevalence of anemia was 52.42%, with rates of 11.3% in early, 34.9% in mid, and 53.8% in late adolescence. Serum iron (28.84 ± 26.29), transferrin saturation (16.88 ± 6.50), and serum ferritin (13.63 ± 0.34) were significantly lower in the severe IDA group compared to the control group. However, TIBC (412.77 ± 197.53) and UIBC (386.95 ± 192.55) were substantially higher. RBC and HCT have a significant positive correlation with Hb ( r = 0.866 and 0.923, respectively). RDW-CV and PWD showed negative correlations ( r = − 0.273 and − 0.508) with Hb. Conclusion The present study reveals that anemia affects a small proportion of adolescent girls in early and mid-adolescence, but is more frequent in late adolescence. The burden of anemia among rural adolescent girls could be reduced by strengthening community-based screening, nutrition education, iron supplementation, and awareness programmes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Hospitality and tourism industry as a primary beneficiary of artificial intelligence: A conditional optimistic scenario
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a disruptive force reshaping the entire economy through automation, productivity gains, and changing labor dynamics. Under supportive labor policies, AI may drive substantial productivity gains across many sectors and generate a “leisure dividend” through increased leisure time and disposable income, driving greater demand for experience-based services central to the hospitality and tourism (HT) industry. This study develops a conditional optimistic scenario in which the HT industry may emerge as a primary beneficiary of this AI-driven shift, with AI serving not as a threat but as a conditional catalyst for the industry's growth and the elevation of human roles. Drawing on socio-technical systems theory and the experience economy framework, a conceptual framework is proposed wherein, under certain conditions, AI may generate a positive cyclical relationship among AI-integration, HT industry expansion, employee wellbeing, and guest satisfaction. The implications of AI-driven transformation in the HT industry are discussed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A novel strategy for high conductivity and dimensional stability sulfonated polyimide proton exchange membranes for direct methanol fuel cells
abstract: The trade-off between proton conductivity and dimensional stability of sulfonated polyimide (SPI) proton exchange membranes (PEMs) greatly limits their practical application in direct methanol fuel cells (DMFCs). Herein, a strategy for regulating the proton conductivity and dimensional stability of copolymer membranes through the coupled regulation of the degree of sulfonation (DS) and fractional free volume (FFV) is proposed. By introducing bulky fluorene groups as side chains to regulate the FFV, a series of SPI PEMs with different DS and FFV were prepared. It is found that an appropriate balance between DS and FFV is critical for achieving high proton conductivity and dimensional stability. In particular, the BSPI-50 membrane achieves a proton conductivity of 113 mS·cm−1 at 80 ℃ while maintaining a low swelling ratio of 35.2 %. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that FFV can be tuned by adjusting the content of fluorene units, as increased side-group content weakens intermolecular interactions between polymer chains. An appropriate balance between DS and FFV facilitates the formation of well-connected hydrophilic nanochannels, thereby promoting proton transport while maintaining dimensional stability. The BSPI-50 membrane delivers a peak power density of 72.97 mW·cm−2 in single cells and exhibits durability over 100 h of continuous operation, with a minimal voltage decay rate of 0.7 mV·h−1. This work demonstrates that the combined regulation of DS and FFV provides an effective approach to balancing proton transport and dimensional stability, enabling the development of SPI PEMs with excellent overall performance for DMFCs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Differentiated impacts of urban expansion patterns on ecosystem services and their socio-ecological drivers: Evidence from the Pearl River Delta urban agglomeration in China
abstract: Urban expansion can alter ecosystem services (ES), yet the effects of different expansion patterns and their socio-ecological drivers remain insufficiently understood. The study focused on the Pearl River Delta urban agglomeration (PRD) to understand how different geometric expansion types influence regional ES. The Landscape Expansion Index (LEI) was used to identify interior-filling, edge-spreading, and leap-frogging expansion, while the InVEST model assessed changes in habitat quality, carbon sequestration, soil retention, water yield, and food production. A Random Forest model was further employed to identify the relative importance of ten socio-ecological drivers under different expansion patterns. The results showed a clear spatial gradient, with interior-filling concentrated in the urban core, edge-spreading dominant in the middle belt, and leap-frogging more common in peripheral areas. Carbon sequestration, habitat quality, and food production declined over 2000–2020, with net changes of −11.86 × 108 gC, −21.67 × 104, and −17.12 × 105 t, respectively, while soil retention decreased by 7.73 × 106 t. Water yield increased by 7.24 × 107 mm despite declines during the early periods. Edge-spreading generated the largest absolute ES losses because of its extensive spatial footprint, whereas interior-filling produced the highest ES loss intensity per unit area. The driving mechanisms also differed among patterns: edge-spreading was more sensitive to topography and precipitation, while interior-filling was more strongly associated with socioeconomic factors. Leap-frogging had smaller regional effects but may increase local risks such as habitat fragmentation, soil erosion, and reduced ecological connectivity. These findings suggest that urban growth should be managed according to expansion patterns, with ecological land around urban fringes protected during edge-spreading, ecological safeguards strengthened during interior development, and green infrastructure improved in areas affected by leap-frogging expansion. title: Semantic drift-resistant learning for robust multimodal sentiment analysis with incomplete information
abstract: With the rapid growth of multimodal user-generated content, multimodal sentiment analysis in real-world applications is increasingly challenged by missing modality information. Existing methods mainly focus on missing information reconstruction or representation completion, while paying less attention to the disruption of cross-modal semantic consistency caused by incomplete information, which leads to latent representation shifts and further induces semantic drift. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Semantic Drift-Resistant Learning framework (SDRL) from the perspective of semantic drift mitigation. Specifically, SDRL models the representation relationship between complete and incomplete states through semantic consistency constraints to restrict the semantic deviation caused by missing information. Meanwhile, a reliability-aware proxy compensation mechanism is introduced to generate proxy semantic representations from non-text modalities and dynamically adjust the contribution of textual and proxy representations, thereby reducing the interference of unreliable information during cross-modal representation learning. Furthermore, a hierarchical consistency optimization strategy is designed to constrain the propagation of semantic drift from multiple perspectives, including local representations, global structures, and task responses. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SDRL consistently outperforms existing methods under different missing rates and various missing modality patterns on the MOSI, MOSEI, and SIMS datasets. The results verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework in mitigating semantic drift and preserving semantic information in incomplete multimodal scenarios. Copyright © 2026. title: Global research mapping of waste oil pyrolysis: Bibliometric analysis of technological trends, environmental impact, and SDG contributions (2015-2025)
abstract: Global waste oil production from the automotive, industrial, and manufacturing sectors creates significant environmental challenges due to its persistent, toxic, and difficult-to-decompose characteristics. This study aims to analyze research trends, collaboration patterns, and global mapping on waste oil pyrolysis to identify technological trends, environmental impacts, and SDG contributions through a bibliometric approach. Bibliometric analysis was conducted on 167 Scopus-indexed publications from 2015 to 2025 using VOSviewer. Data were systematically processed to identify publication trends, author productivity, institutional networks, geographic patterns, subject area distribution, and funding patterns. The results of this study show a significant transformation from a niche topic to a mainstream topic in the global energy transition, marked by a 480% increase in publications (from 5 publications in 2015 to 29 publications in 2025) driven by postpandemic circular economy awareness, SDG commitments, and technological developments. Bibliometric analysis of 164 documents from 687 authors at 312 institutions from 45 countries reveals the structure of global collaboration. The temporal evolution shows progress from an initial exploration phase (2015-2017) focused on the feasibility of the basic process, to a consolidation phase (2018-2020) with systematic scale-up through catalytic pyrolysis, followed by an innovation phase (2021-2023) with the advent of hierarchical catalysts and the integration of machine learning, to a global phase (2024-2025) showing integration with the broader sustainable energy system through the coproduction of green hydrogen, biorefinery integration, and digital twinning, positioning waste oil pyrolysis as an integral component of future sustainable energy systems in the context of Industry 4.0 and the circular economy. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Toward intelligent safety science: a paradigm-oriented framework for AI-enabled reconstruction of safety theories and models
abstract: Modern socio-technical systems are increasingly interconnected, dynamic, and uncertain, which challenges safety research that relies mainly on retrospective accident explanation. Although artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely applied to risk identification, fault diagnosis, early warning, and decision support, its role in safety research is still often fragmented and limited to tool enhancement. This paper proposes Intelligent Safety Science (ISS) as a paradigm-oriented framework for organizing AI-enabled safety research. The framework aims to explain how AI can help extend classical safety theories from post-accident analysis toward earlier understanding and management of evolving risks. To develop this framework, the paper identifies three AI-enabled extension paths for classical safety theories: dynamic upgrading, real-time enhancement, and proactive transformation. It then abstracts a Perception-Reasoning-Decision-Intervention (PRDI) structure as a conceptual-methodological framework for linking risk observation, risk analysis, safety response, and feedback. Based on PRDI, ISS is characterized by four capability dimensions—predictability, holism, adaptability, and generativity—and four supporting elements: data, model, knowledge, and interaction. Scenario-based analyses of complex industrial systems, urban critical infrastructure, and human-machine collaborative environments further illustrate how ISS can be adapted to different sectoral conditions. This study provides a theoretical framework for clarifying the role of AI in safety science and offers a basis for future empirical research on intelligent safety systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: RumorGAL: Graph-anchored LLM for domain-generalized rumor detection
abstract: Rumor detection models must remain robust to breaking events that are unseen during training. Although large language models (LLMs) offer strong generalization potential, their text-centric nature makes them vulnerable to spurious textual patterns in noisy social media discussions and leaves them without explicit awareness of how rumors propagate through conversation threads. To address these limitations, we propose RumorGAL, a graph-anchored LLM framework for domain-generalized rumor detection. The framework first employs a graph neural network (GNN) to derive graph-anchored structural prefixes from the propagation graph, providing structural guidance for the LLM. It then identifies high-quality textual evidence from noisy discussions through an evidence density-guided mining strategy. Finally, a hierarchical reasoning mechanism organizes both the structural prefixes and textual evidence into a unified reasoning process, enabling the LLM to ground its predictions in both propagation patterns and informative content. Across the three transfer settings, RumorGAL achieves robust performance, improving average accuracy over the strongest baseline, zero-shot GPT-4.1, by 5.27 percentage points under the domain generalization setting. When compared with domain adaptation methods, it surpasses the best domain adaptation method in two out of three tasks, with improvements of 3.1 and 0.5 percentage points in F1 score for the rumor class, respectively. These findings suggest that an LLM-as-primary, GNN-as-auxiliary design, which couples structure-aware guidance with evidence-grounded reasoning, is a promising approach to robust and interpretable rumor detection. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: A graph-based friend recommendation system in social networks using Q-Deep Learning Network
abstract: The growth of social networks heavily depends on effective user connectivity. In such networks, users typically establish connections through cascading diffusion models. This allows them to expand both their friend circles and the overall reach and scalability of the network. However, due to the overwhelming number of users, identifying potential friends with similar interests and experiences can be challenging. To address this, friend recommendation systems aim to suggest similar users based on individual features and activities on social platforms. This task becomes even more difficult under the “cold start” condition, where no prior user information is available. Given the dynamic nature of social networks, user preferences are continuously changing. For this reason, using adaptive machine learning models is essential. Reinforcement learning, which adapts through interaction with the environment and user behavior, presents a promising solution for dynamic friend recommendation. In this paper, we propose a Graph-based Friend Recommendation system using a Q-Deep Learning Network (GFRQLN). Our method leverages standard social network datasets stored as adjacency matrices. It uses graph centrality metrics—degree, closeness, and betweenness—as input features. Each state in the proposed model includes a user and their immediate friend circle, while the action corresponds to adding a new user to this circle. The reward mechanism is based on modularity: if the modularity increases, a positive reward is given; otherwise, a penalty is applied. Experimental results demonstrate that GFRQLN outperforms several state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, it shows improvements in accuracy and precision of approximately 12 % and 24 % on the Facebook dataset, 10 % and 13 % on DBLP, 11 % and 10 % on IMDB, and 20 % and 17 % on Yelp. Additionally, our model achieves significant reductions in MAE and RMSE, with improvements of about 43 % and 48 % on the Ciao dataset, and 35 % and 28 % on the Epinions dataset, respectively. © 2026

title: Fast dynamic obstacle avoidance for quadruped robots via privileged state estimation and hierarchical reinforcement learning
abstract: Avoiding fast, dynamic obstacles is a safety-critical capability for legged robots operating near people and in unstructured environments: the robot must infer an incoming object’s motion from brief noisy observations, generate a collision-free body motion, and execute it within tens of milliseconds. We present a hierarchical system for high-speed dynamic obstacle avoidance, instantiated and stress-tested on quadruped projectile evasion. A history-based Ball Estimator encodes short observation windows into an estimate of projectile motion that stays stable under observation noise, where simple differentiation degrades; a privileged High-Level Intention Modeling (HIM) Estimator aligns observation histories with future robot states to produce an intent latent for control. A lightweight planner searches over target body poses on a voxelized trunk model and outputs a collision-aware goal, which is tracked by a low-level policy trained with an asymmetric actor-critic and curriculum learning. In Isaac Gym, the method achieves a 76.3% success rate against 10 m/s projectiles and outperforms all baselines under the same training budget. We further deploy the trained policy on a Unitree Go1 and validate near-real-time execution of the planning and control stack under an external mocap-grade projectile-state input protocol with injected latency and noise; onboard visual perception is not evaluated in these hardware trials. © 2026 The Author(s).
