title: Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) therapy for flashforwards: Randomized multiple baseline single case experimental design in social anxiety disorder
abstract: Background and objectives: Negative mental imagery in social anxiety is common and can involve memories of adverse events or catastrophic future anticipations (i.e., “flashforwards”). Laboratory research has shown that such imagery can be modulated by dual-tasking interventions, which is used in Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) therapy. Methods: Using a replicated sequential single-case experimental design, we examined whether EMDR therapy for flashforwards reduces social anxiety and avoidance of fear-related situations, relative to baseline, in eight individuals with social anxiety disorder. Participants were recruited from a specialized treatment center after unsuccessful CBT or because of treatment complexity (e.g., comorbidity) and were randomly assigned to varying baseline durations before EMDR therapy. Outcome variables were daily social anxiety and avoidance. Randomization tests were conducted for each case separately to test whether EMDR therapy compared to a baseline phase resulted in less daily 1) social anxiety and 2) social avoidance for individual participants and for the total sample. Results: The preregistered randomization tests did not show statistically significant between-phase differences in daily social anxiety, daily social avoidance, or weekly social anxiety severity. Exploratory, unplanned permutation distancing tests, conducted to examine the possible influence of serial dependency, indicated lower scores during the intervention phase across all three outcomes. At the individual level, these exploratory analyses indicated reductions in daily social anxiety for six participants, in daily social avoidance for three participants, and in weekly social anxiety severity for five participants. Aggregated effect-size estimates were medium for daily social anxiety, small for daily social avoidance, and small to medium for weekly social anxiety severity. Limitations: Limitations include modest serial dependency, absence of an active treatment control condition, absence of long-term follow-up measurements, and inclusion of one participant without a clearly identifiable flashforward, although treatment adhered to the prespecified Stage 1 treatment protocol. Conclusions: The preregistered analyses did not provide confirmatory evidence that EMDR therapy for flashforwards reduced social anxiety or avoidance. However, the descriptive findings, effect-size estimates, and exploratory analyses showed a pattern consistent with possible reductions in social anxiety, while findings for avoidance were weaker and less consistent. These results should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered controlled studies. title: Research on multi-objective optimization of hard-rock shield tunnelling parameters for cutterhead performance enhancement
abstract: Hard-rock shield tunnelling involves inherent trade-offs among excavation efficiency, cutterhead loading, and energy consumption, making operational parameter selection a challenging multi-objective problem. This study develops an integrated prediction–interpretation–optimization–decision-making framework for cutterhead performance enhancement using field data from a hard-rock section of the Shenzhen–Shanwei Intercity Railway. Penetration per Revolution (PPR), Cutterhead Wear Pressure (CWP), and Total Cutterhead Power (TCP) are adopted to represent excavation efficiency, wear-related loading, and energy consumption, respectively. Bayesian Optimization-based Random Forest models establish nonlinear mappings between operational parameters and cutterhead responses, achieving testing-set R2 values of 0.9974, 0.9891, and 0.8228 for PPR, CWP, and TCP. SHAP analysis shows that advance rate and cutterhead rotational speed dominate PPR and TCP, whereas thrust-pressure distribution governs CWP. NSGA-II, MOEA/D, and MOPSO are jointly employed, and their Pareto solutions are integrated through non-dominated sorting to improve solution diversity and front coverage. TOPSIS identifies the final compromise solution. Compared with mean field conditions, the optimized scheme increases PPR by 67.1 % while reducing CWP and TCP by 1.56 % and 12.94 %, respectively, demonstrating effective coordinated optimization of cutterhead performance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: AI-supported learning environments in nursing education: A scoping review of accessibility, engagement, and educational inclusion
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence across higher education has significantly reshaped instructional design, learner interaction, and pedagogical infrastructures within professional programs. In nursing education, AI-supported systems have been increasingly adopted to enhance instructional responsiveness, personalize learning experiences, and optimize feedback mechanisms. Despite expanding scholarly interest, existing research remains conceptually dispersed, with limited synthesis examining how AI-mediated environments intersect with accessibility, learner engagement, and broader inclusion-oriented concerns. This study employed a scoping review methodology guided by Arksey and O’Malley’s framework to systematically map and synthesize the evolving body of literature addressing AI-supported learning environments in nursing education. A comprehensive search was conducted across multidisciplinary databases, capturing empirical, conceptual, and review-based studies relevant to AI applications within nursing and health professions education. Extracted data were analyzed using a thematic mapping approach emphasizing conceptual patterns rather than methodological appraisal. Findings reveal that AI-supported learning environments are predominantly framed through three interrelated dimensions: accessibility-enhancing infrastructures, engagement-mediating mechanisms, and inclusion– ethical considerations. The literature suggests that adaptive systems, multimodal delivery, and algorithmically driven personalization may reduce structural learning barriers while supporting learner variability. However, engagement outcomes appear context dependent, influenced by pedagogical design, digital literacy, and learner perceptions of AI credibility. Importantly, the synthesis identifies persistent tensions concerning algorithmic bias, equity implications, governance structures, and ethical safeguards. These patterns informed the development of an emergent conceptual model positioning AI-mediated nursing education as a multidimensional ecosystem rather than a purely technological intervention. The review highlights critical knowledge gaps and underscores the necessity of aligning technological innovation with inclusive pedagogical frameworks and institutional ethical accountability. Collectively, the study contributes to a more coherent understanding of AI’s pedagogical, structural, and equity-related implications within nursing education. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Social media reading engagement and critical reading proficiency among Vietnamese EFL learners: A correlational study
abstract: Social media has become a routine source of English reading for university students, yet its contribution to critical reading proficiency remains empirically under-specified in EFL contexts. This study examines the extent to which social media reading engagement and learners’ critical reading orientation are associated with performance-based critical reading proficiency among Vietnamese undergraduate English majors. Adopting a cross-sectional correlational design, data were collected from 100 third-year English majors at a public university in Vietnam using a questionnaire measuring social media reading engagement and critical reading orientation, alongside a performance-based critical reading test targeting inference making, evaluative judgment, and credibility assessment. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson and Spearman correlations, and hierarchical regression. Results showed a moderate positive association between social media reading engagement and critical reading proficiency (r = 0.42), with engagement alone explaining 17.6% of the variance in test performance. When critical reading orientation was added to the model, the explained variance increased modestly to 20.7%, representing a small incremental gain (ΔR² = 0.031). Regression coefficients indicated that engagement accounted for the larger unique share of variance, whereas the contribution of orientation was statistically weaker and sensitive to threshold criteria. Overall, the findings suggest that social media reading functions as a supportive but conditional literacy environment: engagement with English texts on social media is associated with higher critical reading performance, yet its explanatory power remains bounded and insufficient to account for substantial individual differences. The study underscores the need for restrained pedagogical expectations regarding informal digital reading and highlights the importance of instructional mediation in fostering critical reading development in digitally saturated EFL contexts. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: The Filipino attitudinal framework for academic success and well-being: Exploring the role of attitudes toward lesbians and gay men and social interest on psychological well-being and perceived academic performance
abstract: Extant knowledge has established associations among the psychological constructs attitudes toward lesbians and gay men (ATLG), social interest (SI), psychological well-being (PW), and perceived academic performance (PAP). However, these studies for the most part have been compartmentalized. Very few, if not none, have explored the plausible complexity underlying the interactions among these constructs. Using a correlational cross-sectional research design covering 932 students (between 16 to 26 years old) in a public university, I hypothesized that ATLG, SI, and PW interact to play an enabling role in the pursuit of academic excellence. I likewise hypothesized that sex (SE), sexual orientation (SO), gender identity (GI), and gender expression (GE) as possessing moderating effects on ATLG and SI. A structural equation model (SEM) on the interaction of all of the aforementioned variables was posited. The results of the SEM revealed that ATLG and SI are directly associated to PW and PAP. Moreover, PW mediates the relationship between ATLG and PAP, and that of SI and PAP. However, SE, SO, GI, and GE were found to have no moderating effects on ATLG and SI. Likewise, SI does not mediate the relationship between ATLG and PW, and that of ATLG and PAP. Consequently, a proposed model is derived, referred to as Parreño’s Filipino Attitudinal Framework for Academic Success and Well-being or PAFIFAB, with model fit indices APC = 0.199, P < 0.001 and ARS = 0.136, P < 0.001. The present study contributes to integrative theory building as it underscores the importance of employing a gendered lens and having progressive attitudes and compassion in achieving positive mental and academic outcomes, thus allowing academic institutions to bring to fruition the global mandate of promoting well-being, advocating gender equality, and advancing quality education. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Disability support services in higher education: A systematic review of institutional practices, academic impact, and inclusive strategies
abstract: This article provides a systematic literature review of the role and effectiveness of disability support services in higher education institutions. Employing the PRISMA framework, peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025 were systematically identified, screened, and analyzed to synthesize empirical evidence regarding the types of support services, their academic and psychosocial impacts, implementation barriers, and emerging best practices. The review demonstrates that disability support services typically encompass academic accommodations, including extended examination time, alternative assessments, assistive technologies, tutoring and learning support centers, individualized learning plans (ILPs), disability coordinators, and Universal Design for Learning (UDL) implementation. The findings reveal a consistent positive association between structured support services and student retention, persistence, and psychosocial outcomes, particularly self-efficacy, confidence, and sense of belonging within academic environments. Nevertheless, the influence on academic performance indicators, such as grade point average (GPA) and graduation rates, remains modest and varies across institutional contexts and the specific types of support provided. The review further identifies persistent barriers, such as stigma, limited student awareness of available services, complex administrative procedures, inconsistent implementation across departments, insufficient staff training, and institutional resource constraints. Universal Design for Learning is identified as a proactive, inclusive approach that reduces reliance on individual accommodations and supports broader institutional inclusion. Disability support services should therefore be regarded not only as compliance mechanisms but also as strategic institutional components that advance equitable participation in higher education. These services also contribute to improving student engagement, learning accessibility, and institutional responsiveness toward diverse learner needs. Additional longitudinal and intersectional research is recommended to inform evidence-based inclusive policy development in future higher education systems. However, the findings should be interpreted cautiously due to the limited number of studies and the methodological heterogeneity of the reviewed literature. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Between indeterminacy and intervention: A field-based typology and design framework for interstitial Urban voids
abstract: Urban voids are increasingly discussed as opportunities for urban transformation, yet they are often treated as a homogeneous category despite their diverse spatial, perceptual, and social characteristics. This study adopts a field-based qualitative research design that combines walking-based observation, standardized field coding, photographic documentation, and matrix-based comparative analysis to examine interstitial urban voids as heterogeneous spatial conditions. Using this research design, 61 interstitial micro voids were documented across four dense urban corridors in Istanbul. Data were recorded through a standardized protocol integrating morphological features, visibility and accessibility, informal use traces, sensory conditions, and perceived safety. The coded variables were then comparatively analysed to construct a typology and to support context-sensitive transformation decisions. Based on the combined evaluation of these variables, six void types were identified: circulation leftover, back-of-house void, residual structural gap, visual relief void, unintentional social pocket, and infrastructure-related void. Findings indicate that transformation potential differs across types and cannot be interpreted through a single factor. Unintentional social pockets and selected visual relief voids were associated with observed social or perceptual value, supporting preservation or light-touch intervention as analytically derived options rather than intensive formalization. By contrast, back-of-house voids and infrastructure-related voids combined poorer maintenance, negative sensory conditions, weaker public integration, and lower observer-based perceived safety, indicating a stronger need for safety-oriented redress before public activation. Circulation leftovers and residual structural gaps occupied an intermediate position, where transformation potential depended on access, visibility, ownership, maintenance, and existing use conditions. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Ionized magnesium in serum measured using a blood gas analyser: Agreement with whole blood, short-term stability and preliminary reference interval in healthy adults
abstract: Objectives Ionized magnesium (iMg) is the biologically active fraction of circulating magnesium, yet its use in routine practice remains limited. This study evaluated serum iMg measurement using a blood gas analyser, focusing on agreement with whole blood, short-term pre-analytical stability, and factors associated with iMg concentrations in healthy adults. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 60 healthy individuals were included. iMg was measured in paired whole blood and serum samples using a blood gas analyser. Agreement between matrices was assessed using Spearman correlation, Passing–Bablok regression, and Bland–Altman analysis. Serum stability was evaluated at 4 and 24 h under refrigerated conditions. Multivariable linear regression was used to identify factors associated with iMg concentrations. A preliminary reference interval was estimated according to CLSI EP28-A3c. Results Serum and whole blood iMg showed strong correlation (ρ = 0.727; p < 0.001) with minimal systematic bias, although variability between matrices was observed. Serum iMg remained within acceptable limits at 4 h but exceeded the maximum permissible instability at 24 h. The preliminary reference interval for whole blood iMg was 0.53–0.68 mmol/L, with a corresponding interval in serum of 0.49–0.71 mmol/L. In multivariable analysis, total magnesium was the only variable independently associated with iMg concentrations (β = 0.658; p < 0.001). Conclusions Serum iMg measured using a blood gas analyser may represent a feasible alternative matrix under controlled pre-analytical conditions. However, its limited stability requires timely analysis. These findings support a stepwise approach to magnesium assessment, in which iMg may be considered as a reflex test in patients with low or near-low total magnesium concentrations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Unbowed: Raiding and Hunting with Paracas Spearthrowers and Slings and the Conspicuous Absence of the Bow in Western South America
abstract: New weapons such as the bow and arrow often emerge alongside rising population densities and interpersonal conflict. We test this generalization in southern Peru during the violent Final Formative (400–1 BCE) with measurements of 200 obsidian projectile points anchored to precise Bayesian chronologies from Paracas sites in the Palpa valleys. Based on Bayesian regressions against hafted archaeological projectile points, we conclude all Paracas points were spearthrower darts. This agrees with the lack of bows in Paracas burials and in imagery on ceramics and textiles. Conflict was limited to small-scale raids, based on a compilation of sites with slingstones, mace heads, skeletal trauma, and walls. Hunting and herding were focused in the highlands, mapped with a MaxEnt predictive surface of modern prey location. Based on spatial correlations, conflict did not drive settlement patterns; the key factors were hunting grounds, herding pastures, and agricultural suitability. Pending future research, the notable lack of the bow in the region may include later Nasca, Moche, and Chimú populations. This invites us to rethink the conditions that drive and limit the adoption and invention of bows, a uniquely human and purportedly superior projectile technology that no one bothered with during these violent centuries. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Fabrication and validation of a detailed anthropomorphic oculo-orbital phantom based on novel tissue-equivalent materials for diagnostic radiology
abstract: This study presents the fabrication and validation of an anthropomorphic oculo-orbital phantom incorporating detailed ocular structures based on novel epoxy-based tissue-equivalent materials for diagnostic radiology. Dedicated formulations were developed to simulate orbital bone, extraocular muscle, optic nerve, and crystalline lens, including 65% epoxy–35% CaCO3, pure epoxy resin, 92% epoxy–8% acetone, and 93% epoxy–7% NaHCO3, respectively. The developed materials were evaluated through mass attenuation coefficient, effective atomic number, electron density, and computed tomography (CT) number measurements. The results demonstrated good agreement between the fabricated materials and the corresponding reference tissues over the diagnostic energy range. CT measurements further confirmed the suitability of the proposed materials, with Hounsfield Unit values closely matching those obtained from clinical examinations. These findings support the use of the developed phantom as a realistic and cost-effective tool for CT dosimetry, protocol optimization, and quality assurance applications in diagnostic radiology. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Firefighter turnout gear limits the ability to reach down for an object without flexing the spine
abstract: The restrictive nature of firefighter turnout gear may influence firefighter's ability to lift low-lying objects using strategies aimed at mitigating low back disorder risk. This study examined the influence of each component of firefighter turnout gear on how far they could reach down for an object with their spine physically restricted from forward flexion. Wearing any component of fire gear restricted reach depth ( p < 0.001). The greatest amount of restriction, compared to wearing station fatigues, occurred when firefighters wore full gear with boots (12 cm, 95% confidence interval = [10, 14]). There was no statistical difference in restriction when firefighters wore only fire pants versus wearing only fire jacket and oxygen tank. Wearing boots only had a significant impact when firefighters wore full gear (average difference = 2 cm, 95% confidence interval = [1, 3], p < 0.001). Firefighter turnout gear limits the ability to lift low-lying objects without flexing the lumbar spine. © 2026 The Authors.

title: The rise of religious influencers and their impact on social communication in Asia: A systematic review of Da’wah, preaching, and public discourse
abstract: This systematic review examines how digital platform ecosystems have reshaped Islamic da’wah, contemporary preaching practices, and public-facing religious engagement in Asian contexts through the growing prominence of online faith-based opinion leaders. The review synthesizes studies indexed in Scopus covering the period 2020–2025. Using a qualitative thematic synthesis approach, the article analyzes recurring patterns related to authority transformation, platform-specific communication strategies, credibility and authenticity, youth engagement, religious moderation, gender participation, ethical risks, media literacy, and institutional adaptation. The findings show that religious authority in digital environments is increasingly negotiated through visibility, engagement, relatability, and algorithmic circulation rather than through formal institutional credentials alone. Religious communicators successfully expand access to religious learning by adopting short-form video, live interaction, collaborative content, and personalized storytelling, particularly for younger audiences. At the same time, the review identifies substantial risks, including interpretive oversimplification, misinformation, commercialization pressures, gendered constraints on legitimacy, and the amplification of polarizing content by platform logics. The study further demonstrates that sustainable digital religious communication requires hybrid governance arrangements that combine theological stewardship, operational content standards, media literacy interventions, and strategic collaboration between scholars, institutions, and digital communicators. Overall, the review highlights that the digitization of da’wah is not merely a technological shift, but a structural transformation in how religious authority, trust, and public moral discourse are produced, circulated, and contested across Asian societies. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Mapping Healthy Days Scores to EQ-5D-5L Utilities: Development and Validation of an Algorithm Using Population Survey Data
abstract: Objectives To develop and validate an algorithm for estimating EQ-5D-5L utility scores from the nonpreference-based Healthy Days (HD) instrument using direct and indirect mapping approaches. Methods Data were drawn from the Queensland Preventive Health Survey for 2022 ( N = 12 491) and 2023 ( N = 12 679). Survey-weighted ordinary least squares (OLS), Tobit, beta, majorize-minimize, and ordinal logistic regression models were evaluated. Algorithms were developed using an 80% random training sample from the 2022 data, tested in the remaining 20%, and externally validated using 2023 data. Predictive performance was assessed using root mean square error, mean absolute error, differences between predicted and observed mean utilities, and subgroup analyses by age, sex, body mass index, smoking status, and utility quartile. Results Moderate correlations were observed between unhealthy days measures and EQ-5D-5L utilities (Pearson’s r: −0.53 to −0.56). Predictive accuracy was broadly similar for the OLS, beta, and ordinal logistic models. The OLS model including physically unhealthy days, mentally unhealthy days, activity limitation days, self-rated health, age, and sex was selected as the preferred algorithm. It demonstrated strong and stable predictive performance across samples (root mean square error ≤ 0.117 and mean absolute error ≤ 0.066 in validation samples). All models overestimated utilities in the lowest utility quartile. Conclusions The HD instrument can be mapped to the EQ-5D-5L with favorable predictive accuracy in population survey data. The proposed algorithm provides a pragmatic approach for estimating mean utilities for quality-adjusted life-year calculation when only HD data are available, although caution is warranted in populations with very low baseline health status. © 2026 The Authors.

title: A fuzzy metric approach to composite healthcare-resource indicators
abstract: This paper proposes a fuzzy metric-based framework for the construction of composite indicators that attenuates the reliance on normalization and eliminates the need for exogenous weighting schemes. Instead of transforming the data, the methodology evaluates observations through their proximity to a reference profile within a fuzzy metric space, preserving the intrinsic geometry of the original variables. The approach introduces an endogenous sensitivity mechanism that adjusts the contribution of each dimension according to its effective discriminatory power, providing a structure-consistent alternative to traditional weighting methods. From a theoretical perspective, the framework is formulated in terms of factorisable fuzzy metrics and aggregation functions that preserve the underlying metric structure. In particular, a multiplicative aggregation scheme is shown to yield a coherent representation consistent with distance-based composite indicators, highlighting a structural analogy with distance-based composite indicators such as the Pena Trapero distance. An empirical application to the performance of the health system illustrates the proposed methodology. The results indicate that the fuzzy metric approach produces stable rankings under sample perturbations and reduces the impact of redundant information. Sensitivity analysis further shows that the resulting rankings are less affected by variations in weights, supporting the robustness and structural coherence of the proposed framework. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Technology acceptance and student experience with a web-based school management system in Philippine higher education
abstract: The integration of digital management systems has become a critical strategy for enhancing administrative efficiency and service delivery in higher education institutions. This study aimed to examine students’ perceptions of the usability, functionality, and overall effectiveness of a Web-Based School Administration Management System (WebSAMS) implemented in a public university in the Philippines. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed, combining quantitative and qualitative approaches to provide a comprehensive analysis of user experiences. A total of 408 students were selected using stratified random sampling, and data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, analysis of variance, and correlation techniques, while focus group discussions were conducted to enrich the findings. Results revealed generally positive evaluations of the system, with mean scores of 3.93 for enrollment procedures, 3.88 for system functionality, and 4.00 for data management, indicating moderate to high levels of satisfaction. Significant differences in satisfaction were observed across academic divisions (F(6, 401) = 18.70, p < .01), with variations attributed to differences in system accessibility, technical support, and user training. A strong positive correlation (r = 0.76, p < 0.01) between system accessibility and overall satisfaction further emphasized the importance of usability in shaping user experiences. Qualitative findings supported these results, identifying key challenges such as system downtime, delayed technical support, and limited orientation for new users, alongside positive perceptions of improved enrollment efficiency and accessibility of academic records. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening system reliability, enhancing user support services, and implementing continuous training programs to sustain effective ICT integration. The study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on digital transformation in higher education by providing evidence-based insights that can inform institutional policy, system improvement, and data-driven decision-making in similar contexts. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Interpretable early warning of misinformation cascades via latent-state response dynamics
abstract: Current misinformation studies often optimize retrospective veracity classification, leaving pre-verification monitoring underdeveloped. Using the CHECKED Weibo dataset (2057 events; 3.05 million interactions), we reconstruct cascades into sliding windows and estimate response uncertainty, barrier weakness, and diffusion complexity. Because these distribution-based proxies require minimum within-window activity, latent-state estimation uses a coverage-gated subset of 1669 events, and the early-warning task uses a further nested cohort of 853 events with a fully observed 4-hour window, a subsequent 6-hour horizon, and no regime entry during the observation period. A pooled Gaussian hidden Markov model identifies a shared critical risk regime, and misinformation-linked events in the gated sample enter this regime earlier (median first-entry time 4.15 h vs. 5.37 h for verified events). Transparent regularized linear models forecast future regime entry from the first 4 h of activity, reaching an AUC/PR-AUC of 0.735/0.702 on the reference split and a mean AUC of 0.665 across repeated random splits, which we treat as the primary performance estimate; diagnostic checks rule out classic overfitting and are consistent with split-level variability. These results show that latent-state regime monitoring offers an interpretable complement to end-label classification for proactive platform triage. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Federated knowledge graph-driven multimodal neuroinformatics for early diabetes-related cognitive risk prediction
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is increasingly recognized as a major contributor to cognitive decline and neurodegeneration through intertwined metabolic, vascular, and neuroinflammatory mechanisms. Despite growing clinical evidence, early identification of diabetes-related cognitive risk remains challenging due to the heterogeneous, longitudinal, and distributed nature of healthcare data. Existing predictive models typically rely on centralized, static learning paradigms, which limit scalability, privacy preservation, and adaptability to evolving patient trajectories. In this paper, we propose CNEC, a Continual federated knowledge graph-driven multimodal Neuroinformatics framework for Early diabetes-related Cognitive risk prediction. CNEC integrates heterogeneous multimodal data–including EHRs, metabolic biomarkers, lifestyle factors, and IoMT signals–into a diabetes-aware knowledge graph that explicitly models metabolic, vascular, and neurocognitive interactions. A relation-aware graph neural network is employed to learn interpretable representations, while continual learning mitigates catastrophic forgetting under longitudinal data shifts. Federated learning enables privacy-preserving collaborative training across distributed healthcare institutions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CNEC consistently outperforms various baselines, achieving up to a 6.1% improvement in AUC and significantly enhanced robustness under continual updates, with less than 1.5% performance degradation in federated settings. These results indicate that CNEC provides an effective, scalable, and interpretable solution for proactive cognitive risk assessment in populations with diabetes. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: (Dis)trust in tap water: Consumer perceptions and behavior in California
abstract: Tap water is not universally trusted in high-income countries, leading to tap avoidance and reduced public support for urban water infrastructure. This paper examines trust as a dynamic process that shapes drinking water perceptions and behaviors. We investigate how trust is built, eroded, and rebuilt using narratives from 91 semi-structured interviews in California. Results highlight that trust is built gradually through transparent communication and positive lived experience, yet can be quickly lost with sudden, unexplained changes in perceived quality. Utility compliance with water quality regulations is insufficient on its own to rebuild trust. Residents also value direct and frequent engagement from their utility and improved tap water aesthetics. Findings highlight why technical measures of water quality and public perceptions often diverge and offers actionable insights for urban utilities to enhance public trust by responding to residents’ lived experiences. © 2026 The Author(s). title: The importance of language patterns in the sensory evaluation of chocolates and plant-based drinks
abstract: Language is a central tool through which individuals communicate sensory impressions and emotional reactions to food. Yet, the response modality through which these evaluations are expressed may substantially influence the linguistic patterns that emerge. Using an exploratory approach, this study examined how response modality (written vs. spoken) shapes the characterisation of food products during sensory evaluation. Participants evaluated three chocolates and three plant-based drinks, providing open-ended descriptions that were analysed using LIWC2015. While hedonic mean scores showed a consistent preference for chocolates across modalities, linguistic patterns revealed substantial differences between written and spoken modalities. Written responses contained more affective terms, perceptual descriptors, and lexically complex words, whereas spoken descriptions were longer and relied more on cognitive and function words, typical of spontaneous speech. Across modalities, chocolates elicited more affective and descriptive language, whereas plant-based drinks prompted more analytical and perceptual vocabulary. The findings demonstrate that the written and spoken modalities capture differentially emotional and cognitive aspects of food perception, highlighting the importance of modality choice in sensory and consumer research. © 2026

title: A cross-disciplinary reflection on the role of Indonesian traditional fermented foods in strengthening sustainable science education
abstract: Traditional fermentation practices in Indonesia embody biocultural knowledge by linking food production, microbial processes, ecological adaptation, and community traditions. Nevertheless, industrialization, urbanization, and diminished intergenerational knowledge transfer have increasingly marginalized these practices, resulting in the underutilization of their educational potential for sustainable science learning. This study argues that the deliberate incorporation of Indonesia’s traditional fermentation practices into sustainability-focused STEM education, guided by culturally responsive pedagogy, can directly foster scientific literacy, promote sustainability, and strengthen local cultural connections. Such integration addresses the underutilization of biocultural knowledge in fermentation and underscores its unique potential at the intersection of science and culture. A systematic narrative literature review was conducted utilizing Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar. Publications from 2000 to 2025 were included. Eligible sources comprised peer-reviewed articles or academic works addressing fermentation, science education, sustainability, and indigenous knowledge. Studies were analyzed using thematic content analysis and inductive-deductive coding. The review further assessed conceptual clarity, empirical rigor, contextual depth, and educational relevance. The findings indicate that traditional fermentation serves as a living laboratory, connecting microbiology, biochemistry, ecological knowledge, and sociocultural practice. Five themes emerged: indigenous ecological knowledge; microbiological and nutritional aspects; cultural transmission and identity; food security and sustainability; and STEM pedagogy integration. Although many studies provide strong cultural and conceptual insights, fewer offer robust empirical evidence regarding classroom implementation or measurable outcomes. This study presents a framework for incorporating traditional fermentation into science education. By prioritizing contextual, interdisciplinary, and community-based approaches, the framework demonstrates how local knowledge can enhance scientific literacy, sustainability, and cultural resilience. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Sym-SKAN: Symbolic spiking Kolmogorov–Arnold learning for interpretable hyperspectral land-cover classification
abstract: Accurate hyperspectral land-cover classification is increasingly needed in precision agriculture, urban mapping, wetland monitoring, disaster assessment, and satellite/UAV-based Earth observation. However, many recent deep hyperspectral classifiers improve accuracy by relying on dense spectral–spatial representations whose decision mechanisms are difficult to interpret and whose computational cost limits deployment on resource-constrained remote-sensing platforms. This study proposes Sym-SKAN, a Symbolic Spiking Kolmogorov–Arnold Network for interpretable and energy-aware per-pixel hyperspectral classification. The framework first maps each normalized hyperspectral pixel to a compact scalar representation using a narrow Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) spectral encoder with learnable spline functions. The encoder is explicitly regularized for symbolic distillation, allowing its learned spectral response to be converted after training into closed-form analytic spectral-index expressions that can be inspected by remote-sensing practitioners and evaluated in conventional GIS or band-math workflows. The learned representation is then processed by a Leaky Integrate-and-Fire spiking classifier, providing a sparse inference path suitable for low-power edge, UAV, and on-orbit hardware. Sym-SKAN therefore supports two complementary deployment modes: a full spiking mode for energy-aware classification and a symbolic-only mode that evaluates the discovered analytic index without specialized neural hardware. Experiments on six public hyperspectral benchmarks, Indian Pines, Salinas, Pavia University, Pavia Center, Kennedy Space Center, and Botswana, show consistent performance across vegetation, urban, and wetland scenes, with Mode A overall accuracies of 87.1%, 95.7%, 88.8%, 98.1%, 91.7%, and 92.9%, respectively. The study further reports the discovered symbolic indices, symbolic residuals, decision-threshold ranges, ablation results, and energy estimates. The results indicate that Sym-SKAN provides a practical trade-off between classification accuracy, analytic interpretability, and deployment efficiency, offering a remote-sensing-oriented route toward auditable and hardware-aware hyperspectral inference. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Sequentially coupled numerical modeling of liquid-propellant-induced in-situ pyrolysis of oil shale
abstract: The low thermal conductivity of oil shale restricts heat propagation during in-situ pyrolysis, while reservoir stimulation and heating are commonly treated as separate processes, making it difficult to capture the dynamic alteration of heat-transfer pathways after fracture creation. To address this issue, a sequentially coupled numerical framework integrating liquid-propellant deflagration pressure release, main-fracture propagation, discrete fracture-network construction and mapping, reservoir heat transfer, and kerogen pyrolysis was developed. Deflagration pressure was described using the JWL equation of state, main-fracture growth was driven by net pressure, and the resulting main and statistically generated branch fractures were mapped into a three-dimensional reservoir domain. Subsequent thermal and pyrolysis responses were calculated using Robin-type gas–rock wall heat transfer, bedding-anisotropic heat conduction, and distributed activation energy model (DAEM) kinetics, together with sensitivity analysis of the key thermal-boundary parameters and numerical verification of the heat-transfer implementation. For a single 3 kg charge, the peak gas and net pressures reached 83.78 and 77.73 MPa, respectively, and the main-fracture half-length stabilized at 1.49 m within approximately 0.3 s. The fracture network promoted preferential heat transfer from the hot gas into the reservoir, yielding 138.88 kg of cumulative primary shale-oil generation after 1800 s. Three-stage sequential deflagration substantially increased the axial thermal influence. Increasing the stage spacing from 2 to 8 m expanded the axial extent of the T ≥ 310 °C region from 12.12 to 24.12 m, whereas cumulative primary shale-oil generation decreased from 467.33 to 389.33 kg, demonstrating a trade-off between spatial coverage and inter-stage thermal overlap. These results reveal the sequential mechanism of short-duration fracturing, fracture-enhanced heat transfer, and early-stage pyrolysis, and indicate that liquid-propellant deflagration is better suited as a pre-fracturing and thermal-startup technique coupled with subsequent sustained heating rather than as an independent long-term heat source. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: How is self-defeating humor associated with perceptions of the physical self? A large-sample resting-state fMRI study
abstract: Self-defeating humor (SDH), characterized by self-ridicule to gain social approval, has been consistently linked to the body-image disturbance. However, its neural underpinnings remain poorly understood. The present study investigated the neural mechanisms linking SDH to negative physical self-perceptions in a large sample ( N = 1668). Participants completed measures of humor style and negative physical self, and resting-state functional MRI. Behaviorally, SDH was positively correlated with all dimensions of negative physical self. Whole-brain fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations analyses revealed that SDH was associated with decreased activity in the right parahippocampal gyrus, left caudate, right posterior cingulate cortex (PCC), and right precuneus (PCUN), but increased activity in the right postcentral gyrus (PoCG). Resting-state functional connectivity analyses showed SDH was negatively associated with caudate–occipital and PCC–PCUN connectivity but positively associated with PCC–occipital and PCUN–occipital connectivity. Mediation analyses identified a negative indirect effect through PoCG activity, and a positive indirect effect through PCUN activity in the associations of SDH with negative evaluations of general appearance and fatness, respectively. These findings highlight the role of brain regions involved in self–other information processing in linking SDH to maladaptive self-perceptions, thereby advancing our understanding of the neural pathways through which humor styles influence psychological health. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Semantic comprehensibility modulates the time course of prosody-syntax interactions in poetry: An ERP study
abstract: The present study investigated whether syntactic processing in classical Chinese poetry is modular or interacts with prosodic processing, and whether semantic comprehensibility modulates this effect. Classical Chinese poetry, with its fixed rhythmic framework and flexible syntax, is ideal for examining this issue because it permits a dissociation between syntactic and rhythmic boundaries. Each poetic line had a 4 + 3 or 2 + 5 syntax, read with a conventional 4 + 3 or unconventional 2 + 5 rhythm. Syntactic structure effects were operationalized as differences between the 4 + 3 and 2 + 5 syntax. Participants listened to seven-character quatrains with high or low semantic comprehensibility and completed a word recognition task, with accuracy and reaction times recorded. EEG was recorded during listening, and the 2nd, 4th, and 7th characters of each line served as keywords. Behaviorally, reaction times showed only a Semantic Comprehensibility × Syntactic Structure interaction. Cluster-based permutation tests on EEG data revealed a significant three-way interaction (Semantic Comprehensibility × Rhythmic Pattern × Syntactic Structure) at the 2nd and 4th keywords. Within the conventional 4 + 3 rhythm, syntactic processing varied with semantic comprehensibility. Under high comprehensibility, the 2 + 5 syntax elicited a more negative N100 than the 4 + 3 syntax at the 2nd keyword. Under low comprehensibility, the 2 + 5 syntax elicited a larger P300 at the 2nd keyword, and the 4 + 3 syntax elicited a larger post-CPS negativity at the 4th keyword. These findings indicate that semantic comprehensibility modulates the temporal dynamics of the rhythm-syntax interaction, providing neural evidence from classical Chinese poetry for an interactive, rather than a modular, account of language comprehension. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Neuro-swarm intelligence-based dynamic offloading framework for heterogeneous IoMT in edge–cloud healthcare environments
abstract: The growing need for real-time, energy-efficient processing in intelligent healthcare systems highlights the limitations of traditional medical devices and distributed computing systems. Existing computational offloading methods are often costly or require substantial architectural changes and additional hardware, thereby limiting their scalability and practical deployment in large-scale healthcare environments. To address these challenges, this study proposes a hybrid edge-cloud offloading framework specifically designed for the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT). The proposed framework dynamically adapts to heterogeneous computing environments and execution contexts, thereby improving system responsiveness and reducing energy consumption. Its key contributions include the use of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) for predictive load balancing and task scheduling, the integration of Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) for intelligent path discovery and resource allocation, and the Least Connection Method (LCM) for minimizing latency by assigning tasks to resources with the fewest active connections. By combining these techniques, the proposed framework enables efficient offloading of computation-intensive tasks, supports real-time processing, and optimizes resource utilization across heterogeneous edge-cloud infrastructures. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces latency, improves energy efficiency, and enhances overall system performance for time-sensitive IoMT applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: A criminological mixed-methods analysis of university policies and strategies against AI cheating: A case study of novel deviance and cultural lag
abstract: University policies regarding AI-facilitated cheating are premised on classic criminological notions of rational choice positing that individuals will refrain from actions, such as academic dishonesty, because of the risks of being caught and punished. In the present study, we examine the efficacy of such policies and the applicability of Rational Choice Theory (RCT) to AI-facilitated cheating with a large scale, mixed-methods experiment (N = 3298 college students). In support of RCT, we find that students' perceived likelihood of getting caught and perceived severity of punishment significantly reduced their likelihood of using AI to cheat. However, we do not find that the tested university practices and policies influence students' perceptions of these risks. Our analysis suggests that this is due to the novelty of AI. First, there is a “cultural lag” among AI use and its regulation in society. As such, students’ decisions to use AI to cheat are primarily driven by various personal factors, rather than the situational elements such as school policy. These include their own moral assessments of cheating and their personal definitions of what constitutes cheating with AI. Secondly, as using AI to cheat is a novel form of deviance, there is no consensus on what constitutes a high (low) risk situation. We discuss implications for RCT more broadly and make suggestions for university administrators and instructors for addressing this growing form of academic misconduct. © The Authors

title: Vulnerable narcissism outperforms grandiose narcissism as a predictor of social comparison orientation, motives, and affect
abstract: Narcissism is often characterized by feelings of superiority over others, yet little research has directly tested its relationship with social comparison. Existing work has focused mostly on grandiose narcissism, leaving the role of vulnerable narcissism largely unexplored. Thus, it remains unclear how the two dimensions of narcissism contribute to social comparison processes. Across four correlational studies, we tested how facets of narcissism predict frequency of making social comparisons (Study 1, N = 176; Study 2, N = 217), motives for making comparisons (Study 2), tendencies to make upward and downward comparisons (Studies 3, N = 228; 4 N = 300), and affective responses to upward and downward comparisons (Studies 3 & 4). We also explored whether associations between narcissism and social comparison varied across measurement approaches, using three measures of narcissism. Across studies, vulnerable narcissism consistently predicted greater social comparison orientation, self-enhancement motives, higher directional comparison tendencies, and more negative affect following upward comparisons. In contrast, associations involving grandiose narcissism were weaker, inconsistent, and dependent on measurement approach. These findings indicate that vulnerable narcissism is a more robust predictor of social comparison processes than grandiose narcissism and should be centrally incorporated into future research on narcissism and self-evaluation. title: Psychological control and parent–child attachment in relation to adolescent delinquency and externalizing behaviours: A systematic review
abstract: Adolescent delinquency and externalizing problem behaviors continue to represent major psychosocial concerns affecting adolescents across different cultural contexts. Growing evidence suggests that parenting practices, particularly parental psychological control, together with the quality of parent–child attachment, play important roles in shaping adolescent behavioral outcomes. The present systematic literature review aimed to synthesize recent empirical evidence on the relationships among parental psychological control, parent–child attachment, and adolescent delinquency. This review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was performed using five electronic databases, namely Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO, PubMed, and Embase. Studies published between 2019 and 2025 involving adolescents aged 10–19 years were included. A total of 1,421 records were initially identified, and after screening and eligibility assessment, eight empirical studies met the inclusion criteria and were systematically analyzed. The findings consistently demonstrated that parental psychological control, characterized by intrusive parenting behaviors such as guilt induction, emotional manipulation, and love withdrawal, was positively associated with adolescent delinquency, aggression, rule-breaking behavior, and other externalizing problems. In contrast, secure parent–child attachment was consistently associated with lower levels of delinquency and maladaptive behavior, functioning as a significant protective factor. Several studies further revealed that attachment quality mediated or moderated the relationship between psychological control and adolescent behavioral outcomes, indicating that adolescents exposed to high psychological control were more likely to engage in delinquent behaviors when attachment security was low. Conversely, secure attachment reduced the negative impact of psychologically controlling parenting practices. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of family relational dynamics in understanding adolescent delinquency. This review emphasizes the need for family-based interventions that promote supportive parenting practices, reduce psychological control, and strengthen secure parent–child attachment to prevent maladaptive developmental outcomes and promote healthy adolescent adjustment. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Epistemological bridges: A systematic review of virtual reality for ethnoscience and culturally responsive learning
abstract: This research is motivated by the increasing use of VR media in science learning. Therefore, this literature review aims to identify, collect, and analyze scientific publications on the use of VR in the context of culture-based science learning and ethos to answer questions regarding the state, trends, and potential of research, as well as its implications for science learning. Following the PRISMA protocol, the literature published between 2016 and 2025 was searched across four primary databases: Google Scholar, CrossRef, Scopus, and ERIC. Among the initial 535 identified records, 12 peer-reviewed articles met the rigorous inclusion criteria for qualitative synthesis. The results demonstrate that VR serves as an epistemological bridge, connecting abstract scientific concepts with concrete, indigenous practices. The analysis reveals that the level of VR immersion significantly affects the research methodology: fully immersive VR is predominantly utilized in small-scale qualitative studies focusing on deep experiential learning, whereas semiimmersive and nonimmersive formats offer broader accessibility for larger-scale classroom implementations. Despite persistent technical hurdles and high implementation costs, the findings indicate that VR consistently enhances students' affective and cognitive domains. It fosters heightened cultural awareness, greater appreciation for traditional knowledge, and a sophisticated understanding of the intersection between science and heritage. However, the review highlights a significant geographic concentration of research and a lack of long-term longitudinal data. This study concludes that while the field is currently a specialized niche, there are substantial opportunities for future research to utilize VR as a medium for integrating diverse knowledge systems into science curricula. These findings suggest that integrating ethnoscience through VR can fundamentally improve the quality and inclusivity of global science education. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Identification and causal analysis of human factors in autonomous vessel accidents: An integrated transformer-DEMATEL approach
abstract: This study proposes an integrated Transformer-DEMATEL framework to identify and analyse human factors in Maritime Autonomous Surface Ship (MASS) accidents based on the HFACS taxonomy and accident text mining. A corpus of investigation reports and academic literature is processed through semantic filtering, BERTopic topic modelling, and hierarchical classification to construct structured human-factor representations. A Transformer self-attention mechanism is introduced to extract causal influence matrices from textual data, reducing direct reliance on expert scoring in traditional DEMATEL analysis. Bayesian inference and sensitivity analysis are further applied to quantify causal propagation strength and inter-layer dependencies. Results indicate that organisational-level deficiencies, particularly the governance of system reliability, cybersecurity protocols, and cognitive resource allocation, form the core of the causal network. A clear dual-path mechanism of unsafe acts is revealed: action errors are primarily driven by systemic and environmental degradation, while routine violations are mainly associated with operator states and exhibit strong behavioural autonomy and weak system sensitivity. Moreover, supervisory and organisational failures demonstrate strong asymmetric cascading effects, where upstream deficiencies rapidly amplify downstream risks, while corrective interventions show limited and delayed mitigation effects. This explainable, data-driven framework hierarchically models human-factor causation in MASS accidents, advancing risk evaluation, system resilience, and safety management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Adaptive subsidy implementation for stakeholder-centric biofuel supply chains
abstract: The transition to sustainable energy is hindered by the uncertain dynamics of biofuel supply chains, where traditional constant subsidy schemes frequently create fiscal inefficiencies and misaligned incentives. This work proposes a framework to formulate and implement adaptive subsidy plans for biofuel supply chains by highlighting the critical role of stakeholder engagement throughout the biofuel ecosystem. We introduce an agent-based reinforcement learning (RL) framework that describes stakeholder dynamics and adaptively explores subsidy policies. By simulating dynamic interactions across the biofuel value chain under uncertain transition dynamics, our framework learns policy schedules that dynamically align incentive timing with stakeholder readiness. Computational experiments demonstrate that adaptive RL policies achieve market adoption levels comparable to traditional maximum-stimulus benchmarks while reducing total subsidy expenditure by roughly half (∼[jls-end-space/]50%). Furthermore, stakeholder-targeted policy mitigates early adoption disparities across supply chain tiers without worsening the baseline emissions profile (preserving particulate matter reductions without escalating NOx penalties). These findings show that RL-enabled, agent-based policy design reveals the emergent coordination patterns and provides a systematic mechanism for delivering cost-effective, equitable, and environmentally robust interventions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Herbal medicine among vulnerable populations in Cameroon: a systematic review and meta-analysis with clinical, mechanistic, and global health perspectives
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Herbal medicine (HM) is widely used in Cameroon, yet its prevalence, clinical evidence, and the pharmacological mechanisms supporting its use among vulnerable populations have not been comprehensively synthesised.Aim of the study: To systematically review and meta-analyse HM use among women, adolescents, and children in Cameroon, summarise the available clinical and mechanistic evidence for commonly reported medicinal plants, and identify challenges relevant to policy and global health. Materials and methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, multiple databases were systematically searched. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate the pooled HM proportion. Also, a PubMed search for clinical evidence (randomised controlled trials, RCTs) and bioactive compounds/mechanistic insights was conducted to support the folkloric use of the identified plants. Results: Sixteen studies involving ∼15,000 individuals were included. The pooled proportion of HM use was 46.9% (95% CI 30.7 – 63.4%), with subgroup estimates of 52.1% (95% CI 33.6 – 70.4%) in women and 26.4% (95% CI 0.0 – 85.0%) in children. A total of 93 plant species belonging to 79 genera and 44 families were identified. Anaemia, digestive problems, labour, and cancer were the main reasons for HM. Cordia platythyrsa and Entandrophragma candollei were classified as vulnerable/endangered by the IUCN. RCT evidence was available for only 19 plant species, including 6-shogaol (Zingiber officinale) and annonacin (Annona muricata) for cancer, quercetin-3-rhamnoside (Alchornea cordifolia) for anaemia, and oleic acid (Phoenix dactylifera) for labour. Mechanistic studies indicated that these bioactive compounds act through multiple pathways (e.g., shogaol - upregulated STAT3 pathway, reactive oxygen species generation, and cell cycle arrest in cancer cells). Conclusions: Nearly one in two individuals in these vulnerable populations reported HM use, despite limited high-quality clinical evidence supporting most medicinal plants. Strengthening epidemiological surveillance, clinical research, conservation of threatened medicinal species, and integration of traditional medicine into health systems could improve the safe and evidence-based use of HM in Cameroon and similar settings. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Reframing brain drain in ASEAN: Strategic talent retention and regional governance in emerging economies
abstract: This study examines the phenomenon of brain drain in ASEAN emerging economies and proposes a strategic reframing of talent mobility through the lens of regional governance and talent retention. Drawing on a structured review of 20 peer-reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2025, the analysis reveals that brain drain is not merely an economic outflow of skilled labor but also a multidimensional governance challenge shaped by opportunity gaps, institutional fragmentation, and global competition for talent. The findings identify persistent structural drivers, including limited career progression, inadequate research and innovation ecosystems, weak professional recognition systems, and insufficient reintegration mechanisms for returnees. The review demonstrates that financial incentives alone are insufficient to ensure sustainable talent retention. Instead, effective responses require coordinated and multilevel strategies that integrate national policies with regional cooperation mechanisms. Four strategic pillars emerge from the synthesis: strengthening regional talent governance, institutionalizing brain circulation platforms, implementing comprehensive retention frameworks at the organizational and national levels, and realigning national development strategies with the aspirations of globally mobile professionals. By shifting the narrative from talent loss to strategic talent mobility management, this study highlights the importance of ASEAN-level collaboration, diaspora engagement, and policy harmonization in fostering long-term talent sustainability and knowledge exchange. This paper contributes to multidisciplinary debates on migration, development, and governance by positioning brain drain in ASEAN countries as a regional coordination issue that demands integrated and forward-looking policy solutions. The review is grounded in the PRISMA framework and covers publications from 2010 to 2025 across multiple academic databases, employing a two-stage screening process that combined title and abstract review with full-text eligibility assessment based on predefined inclusion criteria. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: The effect of 3D printing technology in early childhood education: A systematic review
abstract: The current landscape of early childhood education predominantly relies on traditional teaching methods, which may not fully address the diverse learning styles and developmental needs of young children. This systematic literature review examines the role of 3D printing technology as a potential tool to bridge this gap. Utilizing the PICOS framework and PRISMA model, a comprehensive search was conducted across five major databases, EBSCO, Springer, IEEE, ScienceDirect, and Scopus, resulting in the selection of 244 relevant studies based on strict inclusion and exclusion criteria. The findings reveal that 3D printing positively influences various domains of early childhood development, including cognitive growth, motor skills, creativity and design abilities, collaborative learning, educational integration, and foundational knowledge such as shapes, letters, and numbers. Although the current evidence is limited, this review highlights the promising potential of 3D printing to enhance creativity, spatial reasoning, and engagement among young learners. Nonetheless, significant gaps remain in understanding how to effectively integrate 3D printing into early learning environments. These include the need for developmentally appropriate pedagogical strategies, evaluation of long-term educational outcomes, and adequate preparation and training for educators. Addressing these gaps is crucial to fully harness the educational benefits of 3D printing while maintaining a balanced approach that complements traditional play-based learning. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Advancing student mental health through AI-assisted group counseling in smart schools: A literature review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), educational data analytics, and digital mental health technologies are rapidly transforming educational environments and creating new opportunities for student psychological support. Although substantial research has examined AI applications in education and mental health, limited attention has been devoted to the integration of AI-assisted group counseling within smart educational environments. This narrative literature review examines the role of artificial intelligence and educational data ecosystems in enhancing digital psychological support and group counseling in smart schools. Relevant studies were identified through major academic databases and synthesized using a thematic review approach. The analysis revealed three major themes: (1) emerging AI technologies for educational mental health, (2) AI-enhanced school counseling and group counseling, and (3) data-driven psychological support, ethical challenges, and governance considerations. The findings suggest that AI technologies, including machine learning, large language models, conversational AI, and educational analytics, can support psychological assessment, early identification of student needs, intervention planning, psychoeducation, and counseling decision-making. Emerging evidence also indicates that AI-assisted group counseling may enhance peer support, engagement, self-reflection, and student well-being through collaborative and data-informed interventions. Despite these opportunities, important concerns remain regarding privacy, transparency, explainability, algorithmic fairness, accountability, and human oversight. Based on the reviewed literature, this study proposes an Integrated Human-Centered Framework for AI-Assisted Group Counseling in Smart Schools that connects educational data ecosystems, AI-powered support systems, counseling processes, ethical governance, and student well-being outcomes. The review highlights the importance of human–AI collaboration and provides directions for future research and practice in AI-enabled educational mental health services. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Mitigating cascading failures through intentional line removal: A conditional reinforcement learning approach
abstract: Cascading failures in power networks pose critical challenges to system resiliency, as they can trigger widespread blackouts through the uncontrolled propagation of failures. This paper proposes a novel conditional reinforcement learning approach to mitigate cascading failures via strategic transmission line tripping. Our method combines: (1) an interaction learning module that quantifies failure dependencies between network lines, and (2) a deep Q-network (DQN) architecture that integrates real-time failure probabilities as conditional inputs for remedial action selection. This work advances the integration of physics-informed deep reinforcement learning by explicitly modeling inter-component dependencies to derive real-time mitigation strategies that improve power system resilience. We train the framework using a cascading failure simulator built on the IEEE 300-bus, 118-bus, and 57-bus systems, and evaluate line-tripping actions using DC optimal power-flow analysis. The proposed algorithm’s input is the state of the power network, and the output is the transmission line whose tripping mitigates the unfolding cascading failure. Experimental results demonstrate that our conditional reinforcement learning method reduces cascade sizes and failed power compared to no-action baselines, outperforming standard Q-learning in reducing cascade size. Furthermore, experimental evaluations under modified network topologies and AC power flow conditions verify the robustness of the proposed approach. Representative scenarios are also provided to illustrate the step-by-step mitigation process. Finally, an analysis of decision latency highlights the severe impact of delayed line tripping, underscoring the critical necessity for real-time control algorithms. © 2026 The Authors.

title: A study of difficulties in solving real-valued function problems: A systematic review
abstract: The purpose of this study was to analyse and synthesise available scientific evidence regarding the difficulties students face when solving problems involving real-valued functions. Understanding real-valued functions poses a significant challenge in mathematics education due to difficulties interpreting concepts, establishing relationships between variables, coordinating different representations, and selecting appropriate problem-solving strategies. A systematic literature review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines, involving the selection and analysis of 34 studies published between 1965 and 2026 that addressed mathematical problem-solving, the concept of a function, and learning difficulties associated with them. Despite the extensive body of research on the topic, the reviewed studies reveal persistent gaps in understanding how these difficulties manifest across different educational levels and instructional contexts. The results revealed that difficulties in solving problems involving real-valued functions are multidimensional, linked primarily to cognitive, conceptual, semiotic, procedural, didactic, and epistemological factors. Key findings included persistent difficulties in understanding the concept of a function, interpreting variables and dependency relationships, and converting between graphical, algebraic, tabular, and verbal representations; limitations in metacognition and a tendency toward the mechanical application of procedures were also identified. Furthermore, the data indicated that strategies based on contextualised problems, mathematical modelling, meaningful learning, metacognition, and the integrated use of multiple representations foster a deep understanding of functional thinking. Consequently, the study concludes that addressing these difficulties requires a comprehensive approach that goes beyond procedural instruction to promote conceptual understanding, interpretation, and mathematical argumentation; these findings thus offer valuable guidance for designing instructional strategies and conducting future research aimed at strengthening the learning of real-valued functions. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: An interpretable multi-task TabNet framework for predicting multidimensional railway accident severity
abstract: Accurately predicting the multidimensional severity of railway accidents is critical for risk assessment and safety management. Existing studies usually treat fatalities, injuries, and property damage as independent prediction tasks, failing to capture the dependence among these correlated outcomes caused by the same accident. Additionally, railway accident data are heterogeneous tabular data with severe class imbalance, making it difficult to balance prediction accuracy, rare-event learning, and model interpretability. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes an interpretable multi-task learning framework for jointly predicting three severity dimensions using the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) rail equipment accident database. The framework consists of a joint-label-stratified Tabular Variational Autoencoder (TVAE) augmentation strategy for supplementing underrepresented outcome patterns, a Multi-Task TabNet for shared representation learning, and a mask-aware gradient projection (MAGP) strategy to alleviate task-gradient conflicts in the feature-routing process. Model interpretability is achieved by analyzing sequential feature masks combined with SHAP local attributions, which provide complementary evidence from encoder-level feature routing and task-specific prediction attribution. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive overall performance and improves the recall-oriented detection of sparse fatality cases compared with several single-task and multi-task baselines. However, the class-wise evaluation also indicates that minority fatality prediction remains challenging, due to the extreme imbalance of fatal accidents. The interpretable results provide explanatory evidence consistent with engineering knowledge, supporting practical railway risk identification and safety decision-making as a screening-oriented decision-support tool. title: Assessing the techno-economic performance of membrane-based carbon capture and storage in South African coal-fired power plants
abstract: South Africa relies heavily on coal for electricity generation, making its power sector a major contributor to carbon dioxide emissions. Carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies have been proposed as pathways to mitigate carbon dioxide emissions and environmental impacts. This study presents a techno-economic evaluation of a membrane-based carbon dioxide capture system tailored for a South African coal-fired power plant. This study presents a techno-economic evaluation of a membrane-based carbon dioxide capture from a South African coal-fired power plant. The work involves firstly simulating a supercritical coal power plant with a capacity to produce a gross power of 804 MW. Coal characteristics and local ambient conditions in a specified region of South Africa are considered. The resulting flue gas composition and state are determined from the simulation. In a second stage, a membrane system is proposed for carbon capture from the power plant flue gas. To optimise the process, a superstructure-based model is applied. The capture efficiency is set at 90% whilst the product stream consists of 95% carbon dioxide. The cost of the membrane process, transport and storage and ultimately the cost of electricity, is determined. The study shows that an optimal membrane-based carbon capture and storage system in South Africa would result in an additional 10.6% efficiency penalty. The cost of electricity would increase by 131.9% to 152.5 US$/MWh. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Students’ perceptions of learning management systems for academic essay writing and creative expression
abstract: This study investigates students’ perceptions of the use of Moodle-based Learning Management System (LMS) in supporting essay writing skills as a form of creative expression in higher education. The study was conducted at Universitas PGRI Palembang, where the LMS was integrated into academic writing instruction. Although digital learning platforms have increasingly transformed writing pedagogy, empirical studies focusing on students’ perceptions of LMS use for creative academic writing in Indonesian higher education contexts remain limited. Addressing this gap, the study examines how the Moodle-based LMS supports the development of essay structure, language accuracy, and idea expression from the learners’ perspective. A mixed-methods research design was employed. Quantitative data were collected through a questionnaire administered to 50 undergraduate students (n = 50), while qualitative data were obtained from semi-structured interviews with 20 selected participants (n = 20). In this study, Moodle functioned as the primary learning platform for essay writing activities, including the distribution of instructional materials, assignment submission, and instructor feedback. The findings indicate that students generally perceive the use of Moodle positively in supporting their essay writing development. LMS use was associated with perceived improvements in essay organization, grammatical accuracy, and clarity of ideas. Its flexibility and accessibility allowed students to learn at their own pace and revisit learning materials, contributing to deeper understanding and enhanced creative confidence. Additionally, the availability of diverse learning resources supported students’ creativity in developing written ideas. However, challenges such as limited personalized feedback and technical issues were reported, which negatively affected student engagement. Overall, the study concludes that a Moodle-based LMS can effectively support essay writing development and creative expression when pedagogical implementation and technological reliability are optimized. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .
