title: Integrated stockyard allocation and handling scheduling in dry bulk ports with mixed storage
abstract: Efficient dry bulk terminal operations are essential to global supply chains for raw materials such as coal and ores, yet fugitive dust from open storage and handling remains an environmental challenge. Enclosed silos can reduce dust dispersion, yet prolonged silo storage may cause self-heating and spontaneous-combustion risks, requiring preventive silo-to-yard transfers before temperatures exceed safety thresholds. This paper studies an integrated stockyard allocation and handling scheduling problem in dry bulk ports with mixed storage, where open stockyards and a silo complex coexist. The problem jointly determines storage allocation, handling schedules, inventory evolution, silo temperature dynamics, and preventive transfer decisions to minimize total task dwell time and environmental protection costs from open stockyard storage. We propose a novel space–time–state network (STSN)-based mathematical formulation for this problem. By embedding temporal, spatial, and temperature-state transitions into feasible network paths, the formulation reduces reliance on auxiliary logical variables and big-M constraints, thereby improving computational tractability. Numerical experiments show that the proposed model reduces the objective value by 16.5% on average relative to the rule-based benchmark across the instance set. Compared with the MIP formulation, the STSN-based model proves optimality for all tested instances and reduces end-to-end runtime by 70.3% on average for the instances where both models reach optimality. The trade-off and capacity-sizing analyses further show that the model can quantify the balance between operational efficiency and open-storage environmental costs and support case-specific evaluations of open stockyard capacity under specified operational conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Cold plate with orifice-type manifolds and 3-pass channels for high temperature uniformity in battery packs
abstract: Flow maldistribution in liquid-cooled cold plates is often overlooked in battery thermal management system (BTMS) design, despite its critical influence on cell-to-cell temperature uniformity at the pack level. This study proposes a novel bottom-cooled liquid cold plate that integrates orifice-type manifolds with a parallel 3-pass channel configuration to systematically address coolant flow maldistribution and temperature gradients in battery packs. First, the effects of flow maldistribution in parallel-straight-channel cold plates are quantified, revealing a flow maldistribution factor of up to 99.6%, which results in a row-to-row cell temperature difference of 3.03 °C at 2-C discharge. By introducing orifice-type manifolds, the flow maldistribution factor is reduced to 18.8%, leading to a 72.4% reduction in temperature variation across cell rows. A parametric study identifies an optimal manifold-to-port area ratio of approximately unity, providing the best trade-off between flow uniformity improvement and pressure drop penalty. To further mitigate temperature non-uniformity in the battery pack along the overall streamwise direction, a parallel 3-pass channel configuration is introduced, which reduces the temperature variation across cell columns by 67.8%. Furthermore, a parametric study reveals that the spanwise temperature uniformity in the battery pack decreases with the channel pitch for the parallel 3-pass channel configuration and the optimal 3-pass channel pitch is found to be 47.6 mm. Finally. compared with a conventional-serpentine-channel design, the proposed cold plate achieves a 53.3% reduction in overall cell-to-cell temperature difference (from 5.89 °C to 2.75 °C) while simultaneously reducing pressure drop by 75.7% at 2-C discharge and total flow rate of 23 L/min. Comparable improvements in thermal-hydraulic performance are also achieved under higher thermal loads of 3-C discharge and larger total flow rate of 35 L/min. The proposed design is lightweight, scalable, and compatible with conventional manufacturing processes, offering practical design guidelines for high-performance liquid cooling systems in battery packs. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Faunal Evidence and the Duration of Occupation: A Statistical Approach to Neanderthal Archaeological Sites
abstract: The duration of Neanderthal occupations of caves and rock shelters is one of the most debated issues in prehistoric archaeology. Several disciplines, including lithic analysis, micromorphology, zooarchaeology, taphonomy, and spatial archaeology, have proposed criteria to estimate occupation length, but their reliability varies. This study focuses only on indicators derived from faunal assemblages and evaluates their effectiveness through statistical testing. Four features were analysed: number of taxa, hunting spectrum, anthropogenic modifications, and evidence of carnivore activity. These characteristics were applied to a dataset from Late Mousterian sites in Spain and south-eastern France (70–40 ka) that have previously been examined through multidisciplinary approaches. The results indicate that the four features do not provide equally robust signals. Anthropogenic modifications and the number of exploited taxa show the strongest correlation with occupation duration. In contrast, the number of taxa and carnivore activity, when considered alone, are less reliable indicators. Multivariate analyses reveal a clearer structuring of the faunal assemblages. Brief stopping places are consistently distinguished from longer occupations. However, long-term occupations and repeated short-term occupations tend to overlap, largely because of palimpsest effects. Overall, these findings demonstrate both the potential and the limits of faunal criteria. They highlight the need for integrated, high-resolution approaches to reconstruct the duration and intensity of Neanderthal occupations. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Biorefining of whole cotton plant residues for bioethanol production with greenhouse gas emission reduction and social carbon benefits
abstract: This study evaluated the potential of cotton-processing residues, including leaves, bolls, linters, and stalks, as feedstocks for bioethanol production using ethanol-based organosolv pretreatment. Biomass samples were pretreated with 65 % (v/v) ethanol at 120, 150, and 180 °C for 30 and 60 min, followed by enzymatic hydrolysis and fermentation. Organosolv pretreatment altered biomass composition through partial removal of hemicellulose and enrichment of glucan in the recovered solids, which was associated with improved enzymatic digestibility and ethanol production. The highest hydrolysis efficiencies reached 75.4 %, 80.2 %, 83.0 %, and 79.9 % for leaves, bolls, linters, and stalks, respectively. Correspondingly, the highest ethanol yields were obtained from leaves (70.8 %) and stalks (61.1 %) after pretreatment at 180 °C for 30 min, while maximum yields of 42.3 % and 42.6 % were achieved for bolls and linters, respectively. The results demonstrated that pretreatment severity significantly influenced both hydrolysis and fermentation performance, although the optimal conditions varied among biomass fractions. Greenhouse gas reduction calculations estimated that replacing gasoline with E85, E10, and E5 ethanol–gasoline blends could reduce emissions by 55.7 %, 4.9 %, and 2.4 %, respectively. In addition, the social cost of carbon analysis indicated substantial reductions in the social cost of carbon emissions, with the highest benefit obtained from boll-derived bioethanol due to its greater production potential. These findings demonstrate that cotton-processing residues represent a promising lignocellulosic resource for bioethanol production while supporting agricultural waste valorization and greenhouse gas mitigation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Training and Institutional Guidelines in Teachers’ Adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence: Bibliometric Analysis, Empirical Evidence, and Implications for Quality Education and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly shaping educational practice, yet teachers’ professional adoption remains uneven. This study examines the roles of AI-related training and institutional guidelines in teachers’ use of GenAI and situates the findings within the broader context of quality education and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). A cross-sectional survey of 208 Moroccan teachers was analyzed using descriptive statistics, bivariate tests, and binary logistic regression, complemented by a concise bibliometric overview of GenAI research trends. AI-related training was significantly associated with professional GenAI use, whereas institutional guidelines were not significant after adjustment. The findings emphasize the importance of sustained professional development and provide evidence for strengthening responsible GenAI integration in education, particularly in support of SDG 4 on quality education. © 2026, Yayasan Bumi Publikasi Nusantara. .

title: Exposing rumor in online networks: A CP tensor-based detection framework
abstract: With the proliferation of social media, the speed and scope of rumor dissemination have grown exponentially, posing significant challenges to information security and public governance, thus necessitating the development of robust rumor detection methods to address the increasingly complex online environment. Conventional rumor detection approaches, primarily relying on natural language processing or single-modal feature analysis, struggle to capture the complex user interactions and multi-dimensional contextual correlations in social networks, while graph neural network (GNN)-based methods, despite exploiting structural information, remain vulnerable to malicious manipulations and adversarial perturbations, resulting in limited generalization and detection performance. To address these challenges, this study proposes an adversarial training-based rumor detection framework, which integrates posts, authors, users, and comments into a fourth-order rumor feature tensor, leverages a multi-graph regularization joint optimization mechanism within the CP tensor decomposition framework, and incorporates four camouflage strategies under a min-max optimization framework to enhance the model's capability to model heterogeneous relationships and resist adversarial attacks. Experimental results on the PHEME and Weibo datasets show that the proposed framework achieves strong performance and improved robustness compared with the considered baselines. © 2026

title: Teaching methods for civic and moral education in Vietnam: Implications for pre-service teacher education and competence-based pedagogy
abstract: Civic and Moral Education (CME) is important in developing students’ moral judgement, civic responsibility, legal awareness, critical thinking, and the ability to participate in society responsibly. In Vietnam, CME is mainly embodied in the school subject of Giáo dục công dân, which is located at the intersection of moral education, citizenship education, legal education, values education and social responsibility. The competence-based General Education Curriculum of Vietnam has brought new pedagogical expectations to this subject. Instead of mainly focusing on the transmission of moral principles and legal knowledge, CME is increasingly expected to engage students in reasoning, dialogue, reflection, problem-solving and the application of civic-moral knowledge to everyday situations. This narrative literature review synthesises Vietnamese and international scholarship on pedagogical approaches relevant to CME, with particular focus on their implications for pre-service teacher education. Five main pedagogical directions are discussed: discussion-based and critical thinking-oriented learning; case-based and problem-based learning; experiential and service learning; reflective pedagogy and professional ethics education; digital pedagogy for civic participation. The literature reviewed indicates that these approaches may provide students with valuable opportunities to analyse civic-moral dilemmas, take different perspectives, link knowledge with lived experience, and take responsible action in both physical and digital communities. However, their realisation is highly dependent on the pedagogical design, dialogic facilitation, ethical judgement, reflective practice and assessment competence of teachers. In Vietnam, there is a persistent gap between competence-based curriculum expectations and teacher preparation to implement participatory and practice-oriented pedagogy. Hence, this review suggests an integrated framework for pre-service CME teacher education that links civic-moral content knowledge, pedagogical design, dialogic facilitation, experiential practice, ethical reflection, digital responsibility, and competence-based assessment. The review concludes that it is important to strengthen teacher preparation to translate curriculum reform into meaningful civic-moral learning while being sensitive to Vietnam’s cultural, institutional, and educational context. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Modelling the macroeconomic impact of Brazil's ecological transformation plan: a stock-flow consistent approach
abstract: In 2023, the Brazilian government launched the Ecological Transformation Plan (ETP), a new development strategy aimed at promoting environmentally sustainable economic growth while enhancing productivity and social equity. This paper evaluates the macroeconomic impacts of the ETP's financial policy mix, by developing a stock-flow consistent model.The analysis focuses on representing the policy mix embedded in the ETP—particularly its financial instruments—and evaluating its implications for investment, growth, and macroeconomic stability. A key contribution of the paper is the explicit modelling of financing mechanisms designed to mitigate currency risk, a structural constraint that affects many EMDEs and limits the scalability of low-carbon investments. By incorporating these features into an SFC framework, the paper provides new insights into how financial structures and policy interventions interact with real economic dynamics.Simulations through 2030 indicate that the ETP is expansionary, with projected GDP growth rising up to 1.6% and the creation of 360,000 to 900,000 new jobs. While the plan improves the primary fiscal balance by increasing tax revenues, it introduces specific trade-offs: the reduction in unemployment may prompt the Central Bank to raise the Selic rate to curb inflation, and increased demand for capital goods is expected to widen the current account deficit by 0.2–0.4 p.p. of GDP. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Aggregate convergence and constituent divergence in incel-related online communities: A mentalizing-theory lens on cross-platform linguistic patterns
abstract: The “incel” (involuntary celibate) subculture comprises an online ecosystem spanning mainstream-hosted, independent, and recovery-oriented communities. Using Fonagy's mentalizing framework, we derived four community-level Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC-22) patterns: rigidity–flexibility (Psychic Equivalence-inspired), goal–affect balance (Teleological Mode-inspired), cognitive-affective elaboration (Pretend Mode-inspired), and counter-positioning–curiosity (Epistemic Mistrust-inspired). Study 1 compared 2261 incels.is discussion-thread documents with 15 LIWC-22 Test Kitchen reference corpora and the overall benchmark. Incels.is generally showed higher Psychic Equivalence-inspired scores and consistently higher Epistemic Mistrust-inspired scores; Teleological Mode-inspired differences were reference-dependent, whereas Pretend Mode-inspired results were heterogeneous across reference genres. Excluding text from the top 1% of identifiable contributors retained 61 of 64 comparison directions. Study 2 analyzed 28,980 platform-specific user aggregates across five communities. Although platform differences were supported, their magnitude was modest (η2 = 0.037–0.055), with most user-level linguistic variation remaining within platforms. Relative to IncelExit, active-incel platforms generally scored higher on the Psychic Equivalence- and Teleological Mode-inspired patterns and lower on the Pretend Mode-inspired pattern. IncelExit had the highest Epistemic Mistrust-inspired score despite high curiosity, showing that the composite did not isolate epistemic closure from counter-positioning. Across all four patterns, community means showed a consistent ordering, although adjacent contrasts were not uniformly supported. The three-platform portion of the ordering persisted in temporally matched and year-adjusted analyses. Evidential support was clearest for PE, partial for TM, limited for EM and PM. The latent ecological or psychological basis of the ordering remains unresolved, and the linguistic patterns are descriptive rather than validated measures of mentalizing. © 2026

title: DRNet: Parallel two-branch network with fusion-enhancement and channel-pixel attention for color image steganalysis
abstract: Image steganalysis is a hot topic in the field of information security, and researchers have recently proposed a series of methods. However, existing color image steganalysis methods tend to extract features indiscriminately from different channels and regions, which fails to focus on steganographically relevant channels and texture-rich areas where stego signals are concentrated. In addition, most methods lack effective mechanisms to aggregate and amplify steganographic information across the three color channels, leaving weak stego signals dispersed and undetected. To address these issues, we propose a parallel two-branch network with fusion-enhancement and channel-pixel attention for universal color image steganalysis. In the main branch, we design a stego signal fusion-enhancement block that performs multi-channel information fusion and first introduces detail-enhanced convolution to amplify weak stego signals. In the auxiliary branch, we design a channel-pixel attention mechanism that jointly performs attention across channel and pixel dimensions, enabling precise localization of steganographic regions via multiplication-based fusion with main branch features. Experiments on the Alaska II dataset demonstrate that the proposed network achieves superior detection accuracy and generalization over state-of-the-art methods. Ablation studies validate the contribution of each component, and visualizations confirm that the channel-pixel attention mechanism effectively guides the model to focus on steganographic regions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Role-specific household contact patterns in urban and rural China: Implications for influenza household transmission
abstract: Background Household contact patterns significantly influence the household transmission dynamics of respiratory pathogens. Previous studies have shown ignoring the heterogeneity of household contact patterns can lead to an underestimation of the relative susceptibility and infectivity of children to influenza. However, there is a lack of studies on household contact patterns across all age groups and family structures in China. Methods We conducted two cross-sectional studies via face-to-face, paper-based surveys in Anhua County, Hunan Province (June–July and October 2021) and Kunming City, Yunnan Province (February–April 2023). Factors associated with household contact patterns were explored using linear mixed-effects models. Role-specific contact matrices were established, stratified by household structures and crowding levels. Additionally, using influenza as a representative example, we developed a discrete-time, individual-based stochastic model to investigate household transmission dynamics initiated by different index case roles and to evaluate various role-targeted vaccination strategies. Results The mean number of household contacts reported by participants was 2.58 (95% CI, 2.50–2.66) in Anhua County and 2.26 (95% CI, 2.19–2.33) in Kunming City. Household contact patterns were mainly associated with family roles, household structures, and the number of bedrooms. Contact duration was significantly longer between father–mother pairs, between mother–child pairs in two-generation households and mother–grandchild pairs in three-generation households, and among siblings. Mothers as index cases generated the highest number of secondary cases, whereas grandfathers caused the fewest. When grandparents or parents were the index cases, transmission most frequently occurred to children or grandchildren, whereas when children or grandchildren were the index cases, infection most commonly spread among siblings. Crowded living environments increased transmission risk, leading to a higher average number of secondary cases across all index case roles. Prioritizing vaccination of children or grandchildren yielded the greatest reduction in secondary cases, with further improvement when mothers were also vaccinated. Although vaccinating grandparents had minimal impact on reducing household transmission, it remained essential for their personal protection. Notably, vaccinating both grandparents and grandchildren together was the most efficient four-dose strategy for reducing infection risk for grandparents. Conclusions Given the heterogeneity of household contact patterns, to reduce household secondary cases, priority should be given to vaccinating children or grandchildren. However, if the aim is to reduce the infection risk among grandparents, directly vaccinating them is more effective. Unlike traditional age-based vaccination strategies, our findings provide a new perspective to optimize vaccine allocation. © 2026 The Authors.

title: FedLoop: Personalized federated learning with closed-loop feature rectification
abstract: While Personalized Federated Learning (pFL) has emerged as a promising solution to statistical heterogeneity, existing methods predominantly rely on static client-level adaptation. However, uniform adaptation ignores instance-level heterogeneity, inevitably leading to the under-fitting of outliers and the catastrophic forgetting of well-aligned samples. To address this, we introduce FedLoop, a novel paradigm that shifts from static parameter tuning to dynamic, instance-aware feature rectification. FedLoop establishes a closed-loop feedback mechanism that explicitly decouples rectification into direction and magnitude, utilizing prediction uncertainty as a real-time feedback signal to dynamically modulate the rectification intensity. Notably, our method adds personalization through a local rectifier that is excluded from aggregation, so instance-level adaptation does not alter the aggregated global backbone. Extensive experiments across computer vision, time-series, and NLP benchmarks demonstrate that FedLoop significantly outperforms state-of-the-art pFL methods. Crucially, it achieves rapid convergence with negligible computational overhead and maintains superior robustness even under sparse client participation, effectively resolving the long-standing dilemma between local personalization and global utility. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Teachers’ language-promoting questions in primary classroom discourse: Relations with teacher expectations and student learning
abstract: Background: Enhancing student learning with the use of cognitively and linguistically challenging questions is considered key for fostering student learning in classroom discourse. Theoretical models suggest that teachers’ use of questions is related to their achievement expectations for students. However, evidence for the interplay of teacher expectations, teacher questions, and student learning is scarce. Aims: This study (1) describes the use of teacher questions in whole-classroom discourse, (2) examines relations between teacher expectations and teacher questions, (3) and investigates the effects of teacher questions on student achievement in reading, vocabulary, and mathematics. Sample: The sample includes 329 first grade students and 17 teachers (nschools = 13) from 15 German language and 14 mathematics classrooms in Germany. Methods: First, we coded the language-promoting quality of teacher questions based on video recordings of whole-classroom discourse. Second, we employed multilevel modeling to examine links between teachers’ (inaccurate) expectations, teacher questions, and later student achievement. Results: Teacher questions were mostly of low language-promoting quality. Teachers asked significantly more questions in mathematics, including more open-ended questions. For mathematics, (inaccurately) low expectations were linked with higher frequencies of questions that promote elaboration and description. A positive effect on vocabulary emerged from questions that motivate students to hypothesize and conclude. Conclusions: Overall, language-promoting questions occur comparatively rarely in content lessons. Evidence for class-level expectancy effects on teacher behavior was limited. Our findings suggest that the effectiveness of teacher questioning is domain-specific. © 2026 The Authors

title: Two-stage graph estimation for complex motifs
abstract: In this article, I develop an Induced-Sequential-Sampling (ISS) algorithm for subgraph estimation and propose a two-stage graph estimation strategy for verifying complex motifs in large and directed networks. I also derive the asymptotic properties of the estimators for subgraph identification and motif verification, and the simulation results are consistent with expectations. Finally, I provide an example for demonstrating how the proposed framework can be applied to investigate fragmentation in real-world trade networks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: EgoMamba: Fusing hand-guided spatial cues and multi-scale temporal context for efficient egocentric action recognition
abstract: Egocentric action recognition requires modeling hand-object interaction regions and their temporal evolution while maintaining high computational efficiency. Existing methods are mainly based on CNNs or Transformers. CNN-based methods are limited in long-range dependency modeling, whereas Transformer-based methods often incur high computational and memory costs. Recent state space models such as Mamba offer an efficient alternative for sequence modeling, but directly applying them to video understanding remains insufficient for capturing action-critical spatial interactions and non-strictly causal temporal context in egocentric scenes. To address these limitations, we propose EgoMamba, an efficient spatiotemporal modeling framework for egocentric action recognition. EgoMamba adopts a spatiotemporally decoupled architecture and introduces lightweight enhancement branches in both the spatial and temporal stages. In the spatial stage, a hand-guided global and local spatial reweighting module highlights core hand-object interaction regions. In the temporal stage, a multi-scale temporal context convolution branch supplements short-, medium-, and long-range temporal cues. We further incorporate a semantic-prior-guided masked pretraining strategy to improve representation learning for key egocentric regions. Experiments on Something-Something V2 and EPIC-KITCHENS-100 show that EgoMamba achieves a favorable trade-off between recognition accuracy and computational efficiency, outperforming various CNN-based, Transformer-based, and existing Mamba-based methods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Beyond transactions: Cultural role enactment, positive emotional response, and supportive behavioral intention in Northeast China
abstract: Grounded in dramaturgical, performative identity, and cultural memory theories, this study develops and validates a three-dimensional measure of Cultural Role Enactment and examines its associations with emotional and supportive outcomes in rural bazaars (Ganji) in Northeast China. Using scale development and structural equation modeling, the findings show that participants reporting stronger Cultural Role Enactment also report more positive emotional responses and stronger intentions to support Ganji. Positive Emotional Response is associated with stronger Affective Attachment and Supportive Behavioral Intention, while greater attachment is also related to stronger supportive intentions. Bootstrapped indirect effects support the theoretically specified associations, and Ganji Familiarity strengthens the association between Cultural Role Enactment and Positive Emotional Response. The study offers a participant-level framework for understanding how culturally meaningful participation relates to emotion, attachment, and support for cultural continuity, with implications for rural tourism and community-sensitive destination development. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A tax-subsidy scheme for efficient investment in renewable generation capacity
abstract: Electricity markets are central to the energy transition, but current market rules do not always deliver socially desirable outcomes. This paper studies two related inefficiencies in wholesale electricity markets. First, competitive market-clearing based on merit-order dispatch can ignore pollution damages, leading to inefficient spot-market outcomes. We address this distortion by deriving a Pigouvian tax that charges each generator for its marginal contribution to pollution damages. Second, because generation capacity affects future spot prices, producers may strategically distort their long-run investment decisions, particularly in systems with increasingly low-operating-cost renewable generation. To align private investment incentives with social welfare, we derive a generator-specific investment subsidy based on each producer's contribution to aggregate utility. We show that, under the stated behavioral and informational assumptions, the combined tax–subsidy mechanism aligns decentralized dispatch and generation-capacity investment decisions with the social-welfare benchmark while respecting operational constraints. Implementing this mechanism does not require producers to report their complete private cost functions; the tax and subsidy can instead be calculated using existing market submissions and settlement data, verified emission information, and generator-specific counterfactual market re-clearing outcome. An analytical example and numerical experiments illustrate the mechanism and show that strategic capacity investment can exceed the socially optimal level and reduce welfare. © 2026 The Authors

title: Benchmarking operational spatial plausibility and temporal compatibility of EEG inverse solutions in the visual P300 network
abstract: Background: EEG source localization is ill-posed, and competing inverse priors may yield different spatial, temporal, and reliability profiles for visual P300 source estimates. Methods: We benchmarked nine inverse solutions across four families (RAP/TRAP, LCMV/DICS, MNE/dSPM/sLORETA/eLORETA, and Bayesian sparse/hierarchical inference) in 31 participants, 63 sessions, and 2520 trials. Analyses were repeated under an fsaverage template BEM and an alternative spherical conductor model. Outcomes included continuous nearest-ROI distance, 20 mm ROI coverage, 5–40 mm tolerance sensitivity, P3b-window temporal plausibility (300–500 ms with ±25 ms shifts), cross-session reliability, computational cost with setup-versus-inference timing, and source-method×head-model interaction testing. FDR-corrected contrasts, TOST equivalence tests, subject-level bootstrapping, and Aligned-Rank-Transform checks were used. Results: Under fsaverage, LCMV had the highest 20 mm ROI-proximal coverage (21.7%). However, the head-model interaction was significant (p=9.8×10−8), and MNE was the most probable top performer under the spherical model. Cross-session dispersion showed no significant method effect (p=0.866). P3b-timing conclusions were sensitive to the shifted windows, and cross-method agreement was low (mean κ about 0.13). Computational cost ranged from 17.2 to 191.1 s per trial under fsaverage and reached 974.0 s for spherical DICS. Conclusions: The results support uncertainty-aware, multi-constraint method selection rather than a single fixed ranking. © 2026

title: Community resilience: A hybrid framework of multi-agent simulation and spatiotemporal graph learning
abstract: Better forecasts do not necessarily lead to better decisions when intervention exposure is held constant. We examined this question by linking a heterogeneous multi-agent simulation (MAS) of 5000 agents to a spatiotemporal graph convolutional network (ST-GCN) with daily mobility weighting. New York City borough case counts and subway activity provided the observational setting. Across 20 paired seeds, adaptive management reduced the mean peak affected share from 29.95% to 17.05% (p = 5.44 × 10⁻²³). Within the ST-GCN family, mobility weighting reduced borough RMSE by 22.32%, although Persistence remained the strongest baseline in the test period (RMSE 21.99 versus 126.17). An SIR model calibrated on public data in March transferred poorly to April through June (city RMSE 2143.64; R² = -0.660). With action exposure matched, no learned predictor consistently outperformed both reactive and Persistence policies across five training seeds and 20 paired MAS seeds. When contact opportunity was fixed, dynamic edge activation increased the AUC of the affected fraction, while rewiring that preserved node degree increased peak burden. An independent replay used 188,508 proximity events measured by sensors at 20 s intervals. The empirical temporal sequence produced a lower AUC of the simulated infected fraction than a stationary null based on aggregate contact affinity. Rewiring that preserved node degree increased this AUC under the same 15 min contact budgets. The source dataset contained no infection outcomes. These results show why forecast accuracy, action allocation, intervention exposure and simulated outcomes need to be evaluated separately. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Pore-confined synthesis of ultra-small Pt nanozymes on gold nanobipyramids for electrochemical detection of cancer cell-derived H2O2
abstract: Accurate quantification of H2O2 released by tumor cells is important for characterizing cancer-associated oxidative stress, yet conventional biosensors often face an intrinsic trade-off between catalytic activity and structural stability. Herein, we present a rational strategy for real-time electrochemical monitoring of cancer-associated oxidative stress species through the in-situ fabrication of ultrasmall Pt nanozymes confined within the mesoporous silica shell of gold bipyramids (AuPt@SiO2). In this architecture, the Au core provides conductive nucleation and anchoring sites, the mesoporous SiO2 shell regulates Pt growth and affords structural stabilization and molecular-sieving protection, and Pt serves as the catalytic center for H2O2 reduction. The resulting AuPt@SiO2 nanozyme exhibited pronounced peroxidase-like activity with a favorable Michaelis-Menten constant (Km) of 6.08 mM toward H2O2. After integration into a Nafion-based sensing interface, the enzyme-free sensor provided complementary linear ranges of 0.25-60 mM by cyclic voltammetry and 1-2100 μM by amperometry with a detection limit at 0.3 μM of H2O2. The electrochemical sensor based on AuPt@SiO2 also demonstrated excellent repeatability and exceptional stability, retaining over 85% of its initial response after 30 days. Importantly, this platform enabled label-free monitoring of phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)-triggered H2O2 efflux from MGC-803 gastric cancer cells and differentiated their oxidative-stress phenotype from that of normal gastric epithelial cells. The apparent H2O2-equivalent response normalized to cell number was approximately 1.72 × 10−13 M per cell. This work highlights the potential of confined nanozymes for high-performance H2O2 sensing and precise pathological profiling at the single-cell level. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: The relationship between product-based creativity and ADHD traits in children and the associations with later well-being
abstract: Creativity is increasingly recognized as a positive aspect among adults with ADHD and those with high ADHD scores, but evidence in youth is limited, particularly regarding product-based creativity. It also remains unclear whether higher creativity benefits the lower well-being typically associated with ADHD traits. This study investigated associations between ADHD traits and product-based creativity in children, as well as longitudinal associations with well-being. Data were sourced from the Twins Early Development Study, a population-based sample of twins. ADHD traits (age 8), product-based creativity (age 9, writing task), and well-being (age 16) of 1,170 children were assessed. Correlation and regression analyses were used to explore the associations of ADHD trait dimensions (inattentiveness and hyperactivity/impulsivity) with writing-based creativity. Moderation analyses were conducted to examine whether this writing-based creativity moderated the association between childhood ADHD traits and later well-being. Additionally, we conducted exploratory analyses on children meeting screening criteria for suspected ADHD. We observed a small negative correlation between inattentiveness and writing-based creativity, which remained significant after controlling for hyperactivity/impulsivity, sex, IQ, reading, and writing. The writing-based creativity did not moderate the negative association between ADHD traits and well-being, nor did we observe differences in well-being between high-creativity and low-creativity groups among children meeting screening criteria for suspected ADHD. Future research utilizing diverse creativity measures beyond writing tasks is warranted to explore the developmental relationship between ADHD traits, creativity, and well-being. Additionally, our results highlight that taking both a creativity-domain-specific and a lifespan perspective is needed when studying and understanding ADHD-related positive aspects. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: A convolutional low-rank continuous tensor representation for multi-dimensional data recovery
abstract: Convolutional low-rank methods have been widely used in image processing and computer vision due to their ability to capture local spatial structure. However, existing convolutional low-rank methods are limited to rectangular meshgrids at a fixed scale, which restricts their applicability to emerging real-world spatial-irregular data, such as semantic spatial sub-regions and spatial transcriptomics. To overcome this limitation, we propose a convolutional low-rank tensor representation for spatial arbitrary-shape multi-dimensional data. Specifically, by representing the latent tensor through an implicit neural representation, we impose a new tensor nuclear norm (low-rank regularization) on the sampled domain by inferring the inside/outside data entries and develop a new ARbiTrary-shape Convolutional Tensor Nuclear Norm (ART-CTNN). Compared with classic convolutional low-rank tensor representations, ART-CTNN offers two key advantages: it unifies the exploration of the convolutional low-rank prior for spatial arbitrary-shape data, and it can exploit convolutional low-rankness at arbitrary resolutions beyond the original sampling grid, allowing regularization at a suitable scale. Extensive experiments on both regular and irregular datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the recovery performance of complex spatial details and structures, while further enhancing downstream clustering performance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Experimental validation of an E-GOA-Based MPPT for PV-SEPIC systems under challenging irradiance conditions
abstract: In photovoltaic systems, partial shading and rapidly changing irradiance create multiple peaks in the power-voltage (P-V) characteristic, making global maximum power point tracking (GMPPT) challenging. The grasshopper optimization algorithm (GOA) provides a population-based search mechanism for GMPPT but remains sensitive to search boundaries and algorithm parameters. This work establishes, through simulation and hardware experiments, an enhanced GOA (E-GOA) for MPPT of PV-SEPIC systems. In the proposed implementation, the search space is defined directly by the converter duty cycle, with each search agent corresponding to a candidate operating point within the prescribed limits. The search process is reinitialized when the relative variation in PV output power exceeds a predefined threshold. The search dynamics are re-tuned through the social-force parameters and a linearly decreasing control coefficient to balance exploration and exploitation. E-GOA was evaluated in MATLAB/Simulink using a 162 W PV array under ten uniform irradiance levels, ten mismatched patterns and four dynamic scenarios. The methods were benchmarked against PSO, GWO, FA and P&O over 1000 independent runs using tracking efficiency, RMSE, MAE and STD. E-GOA tracked the MPP at 1000 W/m2 in 0.33s, compared with 0.55 s for FA, 0.64 s for PSO and 0.91 s for GWO. Under mismatched irradiance, E-GOA achieved average tracking efficiencies of 94.21-97.25%, compared with 86.65-95.89% for PSO and 53.46-85.21% for P&O. Experimental validation showed that E-GOA achieved tracking efficiencies ranging from 98.99% to 99.95% across the tested scenarios. The measurement uncertainty of the experimental acquisition chain was also quantified. These results confirm the effectiveness of E-GOA for fast and reliable GMPPT. © 2026

title: Choice and goal framing effects in food evaluation: The roles of positive–negative asymmetry and decision sequence
abstract: Food choices in everyday life are typically made as a sequence of repeated decisions rather than as isolated choices. We previously developed a sequential preference-based task and demonstrated consistent effects of choice framing on food choice behavior. Building upon that, the present study investigated two forms of framing: choice framing, by comparing Binary and Defer tasks, and goal framing, by contrasting Positive- and Negative-selection instructions. Participants completed a virtual food-shopping task in which food images were presented sequentially and each item was either accepted (“Take”), rejected (“Leave”), or, in some tasks, temporarily postponed (“Wait”). To characterize stage-specific and temporal dynamics of food choice, both aggregate and sequential analyses were conducted. Aggregate analyses replicated previous findings that “Take” decisions required longer processing times in both image viewing and evaluation stages than “Leave” decisions, whereas the “Wait” decision elicited the longest processing times, reflecting greater decision uncertainty. Furthermore, Negative-selection tasks elicited a reversed trend in different decision stages and higher between-participant variability for “Wait” decisions compared to Positive-selection tasks, despite identical task structures, supporting theories of positive–negative asymmetry. Sequential analyses further showed that response dynamics systematically evolved across Choice Sequences in Positive-selection tasks, whereas such temporal modulation was largely absent under Negative-selection, suggesting sustained cognitive demand throughout the task. These findings demonstrate that food choice is a dynamic, multi-stage process and illustrate how integrating stage-specific and sequential analyses can reveal cognitive mechanisms that remain hidden in conventional aggregate analyses. The present study highlights the value of integrating stage-specific and sequential analyses to advance understanding of consumer food decision-making. © 2026 The Authors

title: Effects of psychosocial interventions on emotional health outcomes in parents within one year after paediatric intensive care: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background: Post-intensive care syndrome in paediatrics affects the physical, cognitive, emotional, and social health of children and their families. Although psychosocial interventions are increasingly advocated, evidence regarding their effects on parental emotional health after paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission remains uncertain. Objectives: To determine the effects of psychosocial interventions on emotional health outcomes in parents of critically ill children within one year after PICU discharge. Research methodology and design: This systematic review and meta-analysis included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating psychosocial interventions for parents of children admitted to a PICU. Five databases were searched from inception to January 2026. Eight RCTs were included, and all eight contributed PICU-specific data to at least one meta-analysis. Outcomes included post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), depression, anxiety, and stress. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Setting: Studies were identified through searches of PubMed, EMBASE, the Cochrane Library, PsycINFO, and CINAHL from database inception to January 2026. Main outcome measures: Parental PTSD, depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms assessed within one year after PICU discharge. Results: Eight RCTs involving 470 participants contributed PICU-specific data to the quantitative synthesis. Psychosocial interventions were associated with small reductions in PTSD symptoms (eight studies, n = 467; SMD = −0.30, 95% CI −0.53 to −0.07, p = 0.017) and depression symptoms (seven studies, n = 448; SMD = −0.13, 95% CI −0.24 to −0.02, p = 0.029). The pooled effect on anxiety was not statistically significant (eight studies, n = 470; SMD = −0.08, 95% CI −0.28 to 0.12, p = 0.380). General stress was reported by one study and was not pooled. Conclusion: Psychosocial interventions may produce small reductions in PTSD and depression symptoms in parents after their child's PICU admission, whereas the anxiety estimate remained compatible with benefit and no effect. Interpretation is limited by the small number and size of trials, variation in intervention characteristics, and risk of bias. Implications for clinical practice: Accessible evidence-based psychoeducational support, distress screening with appropriate referral pathways, and planned follow-up may help address parental emotional distress after PICU admission. title: EIMa: Efficient and robust local feature matching with interleaved Mamba
abstract: The trade-off between accuracy and efficiency remains a fundamental challenge in feature matching. Although recent Mamba-based detector-free matchers such as JamMa achieve remarkable performance in outdoor scenes with low inference latency, their lightweight parameterization and reliance on purely sequential modeling constrain generalization capabilities, leading to significant degradation in complex indoor environments. To address this limitation, we propose EIMa, a novel feature matching framework that effectively balances accuracy and computational efficiency. First, we propose an interleaved scan strategy that spatially interweaves tokens from both views at the feature level to promote high-frequency cross-view interactions. Second, we design a sparse omnidirectional scan scheme coupled with a lightweight global aggregator, which substantially reduces the scan sequence length while preserving a global receptive field. Finally, we introduce an aggregated attention mechanism that synergizes with these scan paradigms to strengthen cross-view global modeling, thereby significantly enhancing generalization in challenging scenarios. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EIMa achieves a superior performance-efficiency trade-off, providing an efficient and robust solution for lightweight local feature matching. Project page: https://github.com/ljxg00dj0b/EIMa. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Crowd evacuation dynamics in a multi-exit room under the presence of simulated attackers: An experimental study
abstract: In recent years, knife and axe violent attacks in crowded public places worldwide have occurred frequently. Such incidents easily trigger large-scale crowd physiological stress and stampede accidents, and have become one of the primary public safety risks threatening urban crowd. To reveal the physical-physiological coupling mechanism of crowd evacuation under knife attack scenarios, this study investigates evacuation dynamics in a multi-exit room under simulated attacker-induced threats through controlled experiments. Sixty-two participants completed 54 repeated runs across 27 experimental combinations, including 3 simulated attacker scenarios (0, 1, 2 simulated attackers) and 3 exit layout configurations (1, 2, 4 exits). High-precision trajectories were extracted using PeTrack software, and continuous physiological data were recorded by Apple Watch S7 devices. Results show that simulated attackers significantly exacerbate exit bottleneck deadlocks and the classic “faster-is-slower” effect with markedly prolonged peak time headway. They significantly increase crowd detour ratio by forcing evacuees to take longer alternative routes, reduce overall mean speed despite initial individual acceleration, elevate flow field turbulence intensity, and cause the fundamental speed-density relationship to deviate substantially from classical pedestrian flow laws. A distinct “physiological lag effect” is quantitatively verified, with peak heart rate consistently occurring after the completion of evacuation in most high-stress trials, and crowd danger increases stepwise with increasing attacker count. The findings of this study reveal the unique evacuation characteristics under dynamic threat conditions, providing critical scientific basis and empirical support for multi-exit architectural layout optimization, targeted emergency evacuation plan formulation, and proactive crowd safety management under violent attack scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: “Feminine” strengths, “masculine” costs: Rethinking gender gaps in negotiation research
abstract: The impact of gender on negotiation outcomes has been an important aspect of the negotiation literature for decades. This literature has primarily focused on “masculine” attributes, such as assertiveness, as ideal negotiator characteristics, manifesting in gender research focused on men's economic advantages in negotiations, to the detriment of both women and men. Yet recent research has begun to examine gender gaps in “feminine” attributes, highlighting women's strengths in negotiations, particularly in relational outcomes. Future work is needed to fully unpack these results, understand the impact of intersecting identities, and explore partner effects. We also emphasize the importance of replication efforts and conducting this research in naturalistic settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: IAEF: Illumination-adaptive event-frame fusion framework for autonomous driving object detection
abstract: Object detection for autonomous driving degrades under varying illumination. Traditional RGB cameras lose information in extreme brightness and darkness, and existing RGB-event fusion methods do not adapt to how information distribution shifts between modalities as lighting changes. We propose the Illumination-Adaptive Event-Frame Fusion Framework (IAEF), which combines RGB frames and event camera streams through three modules: an Adaptive Multi-modal Feature Extraction Network that cross-enhances features between modalities at multiple scales; an Illumination-aware Complementary-Unique Fusion module that separates unique and complementary features and weights them according to local illumination; and an Event-Frame Fusion Dynamic Detection Architecture that routes scenes through a lightweight or heavy detection path based on learned scene difficulty. On the DSEC-Det dataset, IAEF achieves 82.6% mAP50 and 52.3% mAP50:95, outperforming SFNet by 2.6% in mAP50 among RGB-Event methods and TSD-DETR by 4.2% among RGB-only methods. The gain is largest at night, where IAEF exceeds YOLO-FSE by 6.6% in mAP50, confirming that illumination-conditional fusion provides the greatest benefit when RGB features degrade most. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.
label: Social Sciences

title: Generating synthetic citation networks with communities
abstract: Generating realistic synthetic citation, patent, or component dependency networks is essential for benchmarking community detection, graph visualisation, and network data mining algorithms. We present a systematic comparison of generators of directed graphs that are nearly acyclic and have a ground-truth community structure. We evaluate 12 methods across 7 real citation networks and 26 metrics. We propose the practice of reversing the directions of edges in static generators to break cycles and induce a citation-like flow, which markedly improves the performance of a degree-corrected Stochastic Block Model. Our methodological approach to evaluating community detection benchmarks distinguishes between endogenous and exogenous mesoscopic similarities, with the latter proving more important. This distinction reveals that high-parameter models gain much of their advantage by memorising planted community statistics, which limits their fidelity when the evaluation is blind to those labels. Finally, we introduce the Citation Seeder (CS) algorithm, an iterative generator grounded in the Price-Pareto model of citation networks, with interpretable parameters and O(N+E) generation. CS achieves competitive results against the best-performing baselines while using up to four orders of magnitude fewer parameters, providing an interpretable account of a network's structure and, on a temporal hold-out, extrapolating its future in-degree distribution more faithfully than descriptive baselines. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Environmental performance of hydrogen production via eucalyptus biomass gasification and natural gas steam reforming: A life cycle assessment approach
abstract: A life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted to compare hydrogen production via steam methane reforming (SMR) of natural gas and eucalyptus biomass gasification under Brazilian conditions. Three scenarios were evaluated for the production of 1 kg of hydrogen: (i) SMR, (ii) SMR with carbon capture and storage (SMR-CCS), and (iii) Gasification-WGS (eucalyptus gasification with water–gas shift reaction). The ReCiPe 2016 midpoint method was applied, with normalization used to identify the most relevant impact categories. Global warming potential (GWP) was confirmed as the most critical category by both midpoint and endpoint results. SMR generated 10.13 kg CO2-eq, SMR-CCS 6.40 kg CO2-eq, and Gasification–WGS 1.30 kg CO2-eq per kg of hydrogen, corresponding to reductions of 36.8% and 87.2% relative to conventional SMR, respectively. Carbon capture reduced the climate impact of the fossil route but did not result in net-negative emissions. SMR-CCS showed higher burdens than conventional SMR in seventeen of the eighteen impact categories assessed, most markedly in water consumption (14.1-fold) and land use (8.5-fold), the latter arising from the biomass-fired cogeneration supplying MEA regeneration heat. Gasification-WGS achieved the lowest climate impact but did not dominate across all indicators: it outperformed conventional SMR in nine of the eighteen categories and underperformed in the remaining nine, most notably in land use (37-fold), water consumption (3.8-fold), marine eutrophication (2.3-fold) and freshwater ecotoxicity (2.2-fold). The comparison therefore describes a trade-off in which the biomass route exchanges carbon and fossil resources for land, water and nutrient pressure. Overall, the results indicate that the preferred pathway depends on which environmental priority dominates in a given region: eucalyptus gasification offers the largest climate and fossil-resource benefit, while carbon capture on the fossil route delivers a smaller climate gain at the cost of increased impacts in nearly every other category. By addressing both climate mitigation and resource sustainability, this study provides guidance for policymakers and industry in developing low-carbon hydrogen pathways adapted to regional conditions. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Atomic layer deposition of thermally stable conductive MoOx films using a low-valent precursor for ZrO2-based capacitors
abstract: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) of conductive molybdenum oxide is attractive for advanced capacitor electrodes; however, ALD-grown MoOx typically forms in a highly oxidized MoO3-like phase and can undergo degradation during post-deposition annealing, making the stable formation of MoO2 films remain challenging. Here, ALD using a low-valent Mo(II) precursor and O3 yielded as-deposited MoOx films containing Mo4+, Mo5+, and Mo6+ species. After annealing at 500 °C for 1 min in either N2 or H2, the films became Mo4+-dominant and crystallized primarily as monoclinic MoO2 while retaining a continuous surface morphology. Resistivities of 723 μΩ·cm under N2 and 612 μΩ·cm under H2 were obtained for films thicker than approximately 12 nm. In ZrO2/MoOx/TiN capacitors, the MoOx interlayer thickness strongly influenced the overall electrical performance of the capacitor stack, with the most favorable characteristics obtained at ∼ 5.2 nm. Compared with conventional ZrO2/TiN capacitors, the optimized ZrO2/MoOx/TiN structure achieved lower EOT and higher capacitance density with comparable or lower leakage current. These results demonstrate an integrated process–material–device approach in which ALD-grown mixed-valence MoOx is converted into a conductive MoO2-dominant film and employed as a thickness-optimized interlayer on TiN to improve the EOT–leakage trade-off of ZrO2-based capacitors. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Efficient optimal scale combination selection via granular sequential three-way decision
abstract: Optimal scale combination (OSC) selection is crucial for knowledge extraction in multi-scale decision systems (MDSs). However, existing multi-scale rough set models typically represent the three regions as unions of equivalence classes, losing the structural information of equivalence classes and hindering rule extraction. Moreover, most OSC selection algorithms adopt a fine-to-coarse backward search strategy, which not only contradicts the human coarse-to-fine cognitive mode but also is inefficient on large-scale datasets due to scale combination explosion. To address these issues, a granular sequential three-way decision model for MDSs (GrS3WD-M) is developed, and then an efficient forward optimal scale combination selection algorithm (FOSC) is designed. First, a two-step trisecting strategy is proposed to accelerate boundary region reduction, and then GrS3WD-M based on granular rough sets is developed to preserve the structural information of equivalence classes. As a result, rules can be directly extracted from equivalence classes in the positive region, while redundant computation during granulation is avoided. Second, the core scale combination is defined, an equivalent computational formula is derived, and an efficient algorithm based on GrS3WD-M and attribute grouping is proposed for its computation. Finally, the outer significance of attributes in MDSs is defined, and an efficient method for computing it is presented. Furthermore, the FOSC algorithm is proposed, which starts from the core scale combination and uses the outer significance as a heuristic to guide a coarse-to-fine forward search. Experimental results show that, compared with the state-of-the-art OSC selection algorithms, FOSC improves the average computational efficiency by more than 50 times. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Building on sand: state capacity, livelihoods, and the limits of environmental governance in Cabo Verde
abstract: Cabo Verde has built an extensive environmental policy framework, ratifying major multilateral agreements and enacting decree-laws that formally regulate the exploitation of natural resources. Yet on Santiago Island, small-scale illegal extraction of development minerals by low-income households continues to cause severe degradation of beaches, watersheds and hillsides. Drawing on fieldwork in two northern municipalities (São Miguel and Tarrafal) and 25 semi-structured interviews with community leaders and sand and gravel extractors, this article investigates why extraction persists despite a dense regulatory architecture. We find that extraction is a survivalist strategy primarily undertaken by women heads of household, for whom environmental regulation represents a direct threat to precarious livelihoods. Mobilising the "environmental state" framework and feminist political ecology (Nightingale, 2006). We argue that state intervention has tightened coastal enforcement but displaced extraction into riverbeds and hillsides, intensifying rather than reducing aggregate environmental pressure. We characterise this as "governing through precarity", an environmental state present in law and on highly visible beaches, though absent in inland sites where the poorest extractors work. By centring the politics of enforcement and social reproduction, the article contributes to global debates on artisanal extraction, gender, and informality in African Small Island Developing States (SIDS). © 2026 The Authors.

title: The social embeddedness of learning: Social network formation and academic achievement in an undergraduate student community
abstract: Background: Students play an active role in developing their social learning environment and peer relationships. Meanwhile, their academic behaviors are likely to be affected by their integration and individual positions in social networks. Despite the clear importance of social aspects on learning, the mechanisms shaping students’ social networks and the impact of emerging social ties on students’ academic performance remain underexplored. Aims: We investigate (1) the development of undergraduate students’ friendship and co-learning relationships, and (2) the influence of social embeddedness on students’ academic achievement. Sample: The sample consists of first-year students from two large STEM cohorts at a Swiss university: NA=225, NB=625. Methods: With longitudinal network data, we applied stochastic actor-oriented models to simultaneously examine the (co-)evolution of friendship and co-learning networks for each cohort while controlling for other network mechanisms on relationship formation. Furthermore, we implemented network autocorrelation models to examine the influence of social embeddedness on students’ first-year qualification exam GPAs. Results: The results revealed a mutual sustainability of co-learning and friendship ties, which were initially bridged by more generic positive social interactions. Furthermore, we found a significant association between students’ first-year grades and the average grades of their co-learners. This grade interdependency may be a joint outcome of peer selection and peer influence processes. Conclusion: Our study contributes to a deeper understanding of the co-dynamic processes of undergraduate students’ co-learning and friendship networks and highlights the importance of social embeddedness in students’ academic performance. © 2026 The Authors

title: Dynamic sequential recommendation via lag-aware graph learning
abstract: Most existing sequential recommenders implicitly assume that feedback is observed immediately after it occurs. This assumption is often violated in production pipelines, where interaction logs can arrive late due to client buffering or downstream feature computation. As a result, the model input at decision time is frequently a censored and temporally misaligned history. In addition, the delay process is rarely stationary in online services, where it can change across users, items, devices, traffic regimes, and time periods. In this paper, we propose DynaLag, a dynamic framework for sequential recommendation via lag-aware dynamic graph learning. DynaLag represents observed user-item interactions as a time-evolving graph and introduces a learnable time-lag adjacency tensor that explicitly routes information across multiple temporal lags. Our method is designed as a lightweight local architecture: dynamic graphs are updated by event-driven insertion into bounded user and item buffers, and inference uses only adaptive local neighborhoods. Experiments on benchmark sequential recommendation datasets under heavy-tailed simulated logging latency show that DynaLag outperforms strong Transformer and graph-based baselines. Code is available at https://github.com/ChoiYoonHyuk/DynaLag. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: From alignment to decision: Page-matching supervision and consistency-shaped fusion for phishing detection
abstract: With the widespread adoption of online services, phishing detection based on URLs and HTML must handle heterogeneous evidence sources whose representations may be misaligned, incomplete, or dominated by one modality. This paper proposes a URL–HTML multimodal detection framework that connects representation alignment with decision-level stability. First, a page-matching auxiliary task constructs matched and mismatched URL–HTML pairs to strengthen page-level cross-modal correspondence, while a controlled same-domain different-page variant examines whether the learned signal extends beyond coarse domain or topical differences. Second, a class-aware consistency loss imposes a “legit-close/phish-far” constraint on normalized cross-modal similarity, shaping a more discriminative shared space. Third, a sample-adaptive gating network dynamically balances URL, HTML, and fused features to reduce modality dominance and preserve complementary evidence. Experiments on the Mendeley dataset, a CompPhish-derived cross-dataset evaluation set, and a joint URL–HTML obfuscation setting show that the proposed method achieves the best performance among the evaluated reproducible URL/HTML baselines, especially under low-FPR operating points. Ablation studies and diagnostic visualizations further verify the complementary roles of page matching, consistency shaping, and adaptive gating. A sample-level gate analysis demonstrates reliability-aware weight reallocation under joint URL–HTML obfuscation, while a same-domain hard-negative evaluation reveals both improved fine-grained correspondence discrimination and its trade-off with the primary phishing-detection objective. © 2026

title: Structure-aware prompt learning with large language models for drug–drug interaction prediction
abstract: Drug–drug interactions (DDIs) are a major cause of adverse drug reactions and clinical safety risks, highlighting the need for accurate and clinically meaningful prediction methods. While most existing approaches primarily formulate DDI prediction as a binary classification task, systematic exploration of predicting specific interaction types remains limited, despite its higher clinical relevance. Meanwhile, although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong reasoning capabilities, their application to pharmaceutical prediction tasks remains limited and rarely leverages structural drug information. To address these gaps, we propose ProDDI, a structure-aware prompt engineering framework for DDI prediction. Specifically, we design a novel prompt generation module that incorporates multi-path subgraphs from the drug interaction network and molecular structure sequences into prompt templates. This enables the model to capture both high-order relational semantics and fine-grained chemical structures. In addition, a low-rank adaptation strategy is adopted to ensure efficient fine-tuning. Experiments on DrugBank and OGB-biokg datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and versatility of ProDDI. Notably, ProDDI also exhibits strong generalization and robustness under cold-start and noisy conditions, making it a promising paradigm for advancing LLM-based drug knowledge discovery. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Speech-driven dialogic question generation for preschool picture book reading: a cognitive-level-aware spoken interaction system using pre-trained language models
abstract: The quality of preschool children's language development depends largely on the cognitive level of questioning strategies employed during shared reading interactions; however, existing intelligent dialogic reading systems predominantly rely on fixed question scripts and lack the capacity for dynamic adaptation to narrative context and children's cognitive needs. This study proposes a speech-driven, cognitive-level-aware dialogic question generation system targeting preschool picture book reading scenarios. The system maps Bloom's revised taxonomy onto a three-tier cognitive hierarchy comprising memory retrieval, inference, and prediction; uses the FairytaleQA narrative annotation dataset as the primary training corpus; employs a T5 pre-trained language model combined with a cognitive-level prefix control strategy to achieve controllable question generation; and integrates a Whisper automatic speech recognition module to construct a complete speech interaction loop. Experimental results show that the full model achieves a CL-Accuracy of 0.831, outperforming baseline systems across multiple dimensions of both automatic and expert human evaluation. Comparative analysis against the CHILDES parent-child shared reading benchmark further indicates that the generated questions possess preliminary ecological validity. Speech module evaluation shows that Whisper-small achieves a word error rate (WER) of 21.4% under clean children's speech conditions, reduced to 19.8% after language model post-processing; the narrative relevance threshold τ = 0.5 is confirmed as the optimal parameter via sensitivity analysis (F1 = 0.754); and the end-to-end interaction loop simulation achieves a session completion rate of 94.0%. Ablation experiments further validate the core contribution of the cognitive-level prefix control mechanism. This framework provides an explorable methodological pathway for translating dialogic reading theory into scalable intelligent systems. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: A broad learning model with dual-path feature encoding for robust and expedient incremental fault diagnosis
abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis (IFD) models that rely on one-shot learning often struggle in dynamic mechanical systems because they exhibit limited knowledge stability and high computational cost under incremental learning (IL). To address the trade-off between robustness and efficiency, this paper proposes a Multi-Scale High-Resolution and Source-Informed Broad Learning Model (MHRSI-BLM). By leveraging the computational efficiency of broad learning for rapid weight correction and pseudo-inverse updating, the proposed framework achieves efficient incremental updates. In addition, the MHRSI-BLM framework adopts a dual-path feature-encoding strategy to improve robustness: a multi-scale high-resolution pathway enhances feature representation, while a complementary source pathway provides a relatively stable feature anchor for incremental updates. Experiments on two rolling-bearing datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves strong diagnostic accuracy with competitive computational efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Multi-omics profiling of muscle tissue reveals metabolic signatures associated with size variation in redclaw crayfish (Cherax quadricarinatus)
abstract: The rising market demand for large, premium grade redclaw crayfish (Cherax quadricarinatus) highlights the need for improved production efficiency, yet the molecular characteristics associated with body-size variation remain poorly understood. This study employs an integrated multi-omics approach (untargeted metabolomics, targeted taurine analysis, and transcriptomics) to characterize the metabolic signatures associated with crayfish size variation. Untargeted analysis of 18,204 metabolite features identified 229 differentially abundant metabolites, including a 28-fold higher level of sucrose in large individuals (p = 0.025). Targeted analysis confirmed that taurine, a key osmolyte and antioxidant, was significantly elevated in larger crayfish. Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses revealed metabolic features associated with carbohydrate and purine metabolism that correlated with body-size variation. In contrast, smaller crayfish exhibited elevated purine turnover (xanthine/uric acid) and reduced levels of key anabolic metabolites. These findings provide a multi-omics characterization of metabolic states associated with growth phenotypes and identify candidate biomarkers for future studies investigating the potential of nutritional strategies to improve crayfish production. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: PhDGPT: Measuring bias in academic mental health across quantised and uncensored LLMs
abstract: We investigate bias in academic mental health as reflected by Large Language Models (LLMs). To this aim, we introduce PhDGPT, a synthetic dataset encapsulating the machine psychology of Ph.D. researchers and professors as perceived by OpenAI’s GPT-3.5 and GPT-OSS-20b. The dataset consists of 18,000 data points for each model, comprising 300 iterations repeated across 15 academic events, 2 gender personas, 2 career levels and 42 unique items responses of the Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale (DASS-42) across 2 LLMs. The PhDGPT dataset integrates these psychometric scores with their explanations in plain language. This synergy of scores and texts offers a dual, comprehensive perspective on the emotional well-being of simulated academics, e.g. male/female Ph.D. students or professors. We find that both GPT-3.5 and GPT-OSS produce higher levels of mental distress when impersonating Ph.D. students compared to professors, a direction that aligns with humans’ recent results about mental health in academia. Compared against more than 39,000 human psychometric responses, GPT-3.5 reproduces the canonical structure of anxiety, stress and depression, whereas GPT-OSS does so only under vLLM inference and not under the GGUF quantisation analysed here. This specific instance of GPT-OSS, run via LM Studio under GGUF quantisation, also produces markedly fewer linguistic patterns correlating with psychological dimensions of distress than GPT-3.5. A robustness check — encompassing prompt paraphrasing across four alternative formulations and 3 additional open-source models spanning a range of alignment strategies (Mistral Small 24b Instruct, and 2 uncensored variants) — confirms that psycholinguistic signatures are stable across surface-level prompt variation, while revealing that the relationship between safety alignment and psycholinguistic richness is more complex than a simple censorship effect. We treat safety alignment as one of several candidate explanations for the observed degradation, alongside architectural differences and training procedures. © 2026 The Authors. title: Locally constrained optimization of PC-SAFT parameters for reliable restricted group contribution calculations for associating fluids
abstract: Accurate vapor-liquid equilibrium (VLE) prediction for associating fluids is paramount for chemical separation and carbon capture. However, systematic model parameter optimization across diverse equations of state (EoSs) remains limited. A fundamental challenge arises when transitioning from model parameters to a group contribution (GC) framework: the inherent trade-off between correlative accuracy and the linear additivity of groups. In this study, we first construct a high-precision model parameter database for 57 pure associating fluids using global optimization across PC-SAFT, SAFT-VR Mie, and CPA EoSs. SAFT-VR Mie demonstrates superior performance with an average absolute relative deviation (AARD%) below 0.42%. To reconcile the conflict between correlative accuracy and the linear additivity of groups, we propose an optimization strategy. This strategy yields model parameters that preserve both correlative fidelity and the linear additivity of groups. This framework enables the derivation of first- and second-order group parameters capable of resolving isomers, thereby substantially extending the applicability of PC-SAFT to complex associating systems with limited experimental data. Finally, we find that global optimization exhibits parameter compensation behavior, thereby achieving excellent fitting to experimental data. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Modeling pedestrian evacuation in ships: an enhanced heuristic-based approach accounting for oscillation and falling
abstract: Passenger ship motion, characterized by periodic oscillations (pitching and/or rolling) induced by wind, waves, and currents, critically influences pedestrian behavior and crowd dynamics during evacuations. Severe oscillations can significantly impede movement or even cause falls, elevating the risk of stampedes and fatalities. This study examines how ship motion parameters—oscillation direction, amplitude, and period—affect pedestrian evacuation. We first analyze pedestrian desired speed on an inclined ramp by balancing gravitational, frictional, and driving forces. This model is then extended to simulate dynamic shipboard conditions by incorporating the effects of transient weightlessness and overweight accelerations. The analysis reveals that ship motion reduces desired speed. This modified desired speed is subsequently integrated into a heuristic-based pedestrian flow simulation model. Additionally, falling behavior is modeled by comparing real-time speed to the maximum achievable desired speed. Simulation results demonstrate that ship motion reduces evacuation efficiency in both room and corridor. Larger oscillation amplitudes and shorter periods further prolong evacuation times. Shifting the oscillation direction from pitching to rolling can partially mitigate efficiency losses. Critically, excessive oscillations trigger falls, drastically increasing evacuation time. This research enhances understanding of evacuation dynamics under ship motion and supports the development of effective crowd management strategies for large passenger vessels. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
