title: TacFG-9: A tactile-vision-language dataset for factorized fine-grained tactile semantics
abstract: Tactile semantics provide essential physical cues for understanding object properties during robotic interaction. However, existing tactile-language datasets primarily rely on coarse tactile semantics and lack systematic annotations for fine-grained tactile semantics, which makes it difficult to generate semantically faithful descriptions under partial tactile observations. To address this issue, we introduce TacFG-9, a fine-grained tactile-vision-language dataset constructed through a three-level, nine-dimensional annotation framework. Each TacFG-9 sample combines a tactile observation, visual context, a verified caption, and structured tactile semantic labels organized from material identity to local perceptual cues. To scale TacFG-9 while maintaining annotation reliability, we use model-assisted expansion to explicitly identify samples with uncertain or semantically inconsistent predictions and route them to targeted human review. Building on TacFG-9, we further propose TacRAGate, a similarity-gated tactile captioning framework for reliable fine-grained description generation. TacRAGate uses retrieved verified captions and fine-grained tactile attribute labels as evidence, estimates evidence reliability using the top-1 retrieval similarity, and accordingly switches among Direct Retrieval, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Low-Evidence Generation. Experiments demonstrate that the structured tactile-vision-language supervision in TacFG-9 improves tactile representation learning, while TacRAGate produces more semantically faithful tactile descriptions than existing tactile captioning methods under partial observations. title: A multi-objective planning study of distributed photovoltaics based on candidate-node screening and an MO-ISSA method
abstract: Distributed photovoltaic (DPV) siting and sizing in distribution networks is a high-dimensional discrete optimization problem with coupled objectives. Existing studies usually focus on optimizer improvement or full-bus-set planning, while the coordinated improvement of search-space reduction and Pareto-front quality remains insufficient. To address this issue, a DPV planning framework combining topology-aware candidate-node screening and a Multi-Objective Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm (MO-ISSA) is proposed. A Node Comprehensive Importance Index (NCII), integrating inter-community connections, betweenness centrality, and active-power-loss improvement, is constructed to identify candidate nodes before optimization. MO-ISSA is then used to solve a three-objective model considering economic benefit, comprehensive grid vulnerability, and active power loss. Results on the IEEE 33-bus system show that the proposed screening strategy reduces computation time while maintaining planning quality. Compared with NSGA-II, MOPSO, and SSA, MO-ISSA achieves better Pareto-front quality, convergence, and stability. Comparisons with the full-node-space heuristic result, an SOCP-representable deterministic surrogate reference model, and full-node-space standard algorithms further verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The IEEE 69-bus case confirms its applicability to larger distribution networks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Ethical considerations in establishing reference population DNA databases of Indigenous peoples in Southeast Asia
abstract: Reference population DNA databases are essential for accurate forensic statistical calculations, yet Indigenous populations remain significantly underrepresented in most forensic genetic repositories, limiting the scientific accuracy of allele frequency distributions and population genetic parameters in affected countries. This gap is particularly acute in Southeast Asia, where Indigenous peoples comprise substantial populations but are largely absent from forensic databases. This paper reports ethical and governance principles that should be considered in establishing and maintaining Indigenous reference population DNA databases to generate empirically derived allele frequency distributions, characterize population structure, and calculate population-specific theta (θ) values for forensic applications. We propose that such databases should be governed by policies discussed with and approved by authorized Indigenous representatives, with independent academic or government institutions serving as custodians. Effective governance requires culturally informed ethical policies, defined organizational structures, standardized operational procedures, and well-trained staff. Drawing on international precedents from Singapore (Health Science Authority), Malaysia (Jabatan Kimia Malaysia), New Zealand (the New Zealand Institute for Public Health and Forensic Science), and the Philippines (Filipino Genomes Research Program, DNA Analysis Laboratory, Natural Sciences Research Institute, University of the Philippines Diliman), we demonstrate that reference population DNA databases can be successfully managed by universities or government agencies that maintain institutional independence from law enforcement while supporting calculations of random match probabilities and likelihood ratios. We identify critical ethical gaps regarding informed consent, community engagement and/or partnership, data ownership, and restrictions on secondary use. We recommend adopting dynamic consent models consistent with Indigenous data sovereignty and the CARE (Collective Benefit, Authority to Control, Responsibility, Ethics) principles. The Philippines is presented as a case study, demonstrating how free, prior, and informed consent (FPIC) frameworks and stakeholder engagement enable the collection of Indigenous population genetic data while respecting Indigenous rights, albeit with their own challenges. Our findings demonstrate that ethical inclusion of Indigenous peoples in forensic database development is essential for generating accurate, population-specific genetic parameters and advancing forensic science that encompasses both broad general populations and smaller Indigenous communities. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Development and application of HELDA: a multi-criteria decision analysis software tailored for sustainable energy system transitions
abstract: Achieving sustainable energy system transitions necessitates the development of innovative technologies and systems, and their integration into complex and rapidly changing societal frameworks. In such a dynamic context, it is important to have a tool that accelerates decision-making processes, including stakeholder preferences, while maintaining scientific rigor, transparency and inclusiveness. To achieve this objective, sustainability assessments (SA) with multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) methods have been widely used. Despite the development of MCDA software tools to facilitate the implementation of MCDA methods, challenges often arise concerning the selection of a proper MCDA method and the integration of stakeholders, which often requires significant resources. This research presents HELDA, the Helmholtz Decision Analysis Tool developed following the concepts of MCDA for SA including the strong sustainability concept and stakeholders’ integration. To our knowledge, HELDA is the only free MCDA software that integrates binary relations methods (ELECTRE III and PROMETHEE I and II) with online surveys for weights elicitation of stakeholder groups (synchronous and asynchronous). The HELDA software is the result of extending the functionality of an existing MCDA software based on a previous study on the capabilities of MCDA software to conduct SA. HELDA development process was based on theories from agile software development. The functionality of HELDA is illustrated in a case study on the prospective SA of individual motorized mobility options using ELECTRE III method. The preferences of 13 researchers were elicited as individuals and in group settings to reach consensus on criteria weights. © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: Peripheral arylation engineering for high-performance non-doped blue OLEDs based on phenanthroimidazole-anthracene hybrids
abstract: Developing high-performance non-doped blue organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) remains a formidable challenge due to the trade-off among efficiency, color purity, and device stability. Herein, we report a molecular engineering strategy by systematically introducing peripheral phenyl and naphthyl substituents onto phenanthroimidazole-anthracene core (oPAN, oPANPH, and oPANNA). Single-crystal and theoretical analyses reveal that intramolecular through-space n–π interactions and C–H···N hydrogen bonds rigidify the molecular backbone, while the bulky peripheral groups effectively suppress intermolecular aggregation and vibronic coupling. Consequently, the neat films of oPANPH and oPANNA exhibit significantly narrowed emission (FWHM: 65 and 64 nm) with substantially reduced red-shifts (18 and 19 nm) compared to oPAN, along with enhanced photoluminescence quantum yields of up to 86%. Benefiting from the extended π-conjugation that progressively increases oscillator strengths and electron mobilities, the non-doped OLEDs based on oPANNA achieve outstanding performance with maximum luminance of 32840 cd m−2, EQE of 5.22%, and narrow EL spectrum with a FWHM of 53 nm, alongside low turn-on voltage of 2.8 V. This work demonstrates that attaching judicious peripheral aromatic groups is an effective approach to concurrently enhance color purity, efficiency, and carrier balance in blue OLED materials. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Debunking decisions for dynamically emerging topic-associated rumors
abstract: In public emergency events, topic-associated rumors typically erupt in a streaming, multi-wave fashion, requiring authorities to continuously produce debunking decisions as new rumors keep emerging, all under unknown diffusion-model parameters. Inspired by Planck’s blackbody radiation law, we propose the Topic-associated Rumor Dynamic-emergence Competitive Cascade (TRDCC) model with a cognitive-fatigue effect, cast dynamic debunking as an online learning problem under the query–decision regression paradigm, and develop the Topic-associated Rumor Dynamic Control (TRDC) algorithm. Theoretically, we establish the NP-hardness of the problem and the submodularity of the objective, and derive a probabilistic approximation bound for the score function as well as a generalization-error upper bound that accounts for state distribution shift. On four real-world networks, TRDC attains time-averaged Performance Ratio (PR) values of 0.859, 0.891, 0.657 and 0.713 even under fully unknown diffusion parameters. Across all four networks, it outperforms the best-performing heuristic, learn-and-optimize and deep reinforcement learning baseline by margins of at least 0.23, 0.25 and 0.28 in PR, respectively, and remains stable throughout the entire decision stream. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: 2D time-domain SH-wave full-waveform inversion for geotechnical site characterization: a practical comparison of optimization strategies
abstract: Engineering-geological site investigation requires reliable identification of shallow subsurface structures, interfaces, and weak zones, whereas conventional methods such as boreholes and coring remain spatially discrete. Two-dimensional time-domain SH-wave full-waveform inversion (SH-FWI) provides a nondestructive, in situ, and spatially continuous approach for recovering shear-wave velocity (Vs) and density, two parameters directly relevant to engineering-geological interpretation. This study presents a practical evaluation of steepest descent (SD), L-BFGS, and Gauss–Newton (GN) within a unified 2D time-domain SH-FWI framework, focusing on their effects on Vs and density recovery using one synthetic model and two representative engineering-geological field cases with contrasting near-surface conditions. In the field cases, the inversion-derived density results are quantitatively compared with laboratory-measured borehole core densities through depth-dependent and layer-wise statistical analyses, thereby providing practical evidence for assessing the applicability of different optimization strategies in engineering-geological site characterization. The results show that all three methods can recover the main engineering-geological framework, including shallow hard layers, weathered limestone transitions, localized weak intervals, and competent bedrock. GN provides the highest inversion resolution and fastest convergence but at substantially greater computational cost and memory demand. SD serves as a stable first-order baseline but tends to produce smoother models and slower convergence. L-BFGS provides a practical compromise among inversion reliability, borehole-density consistency, and computational affordability under the tested field conditions. Overall, the results demonstrate that SH-FWI can provide useful and spatially continuous information for shallow engineering-geological characterization, and the recovered Vs and density models can further support the derivation of stiffness-related parameters for subsequent engineering-geological analysis and application. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Monophily-aware graph pre-training for heterophilic graphs
abstract: Graph pre-training algorithms aim to learn generic node embeddings without relying on labeled data. These models are typically designed based on the homophily assumption, which posits that connected nodes present similar features and same labels. However, this design limits their expressiveness and generalization ability on heterophilic graphs that exhibit dissimilar features and different labels between connected nodes and are prevalent in real-world scenarios. To address this limitation, we propose MAGNET, a novel Monophily-Aware Graph pre-traiNing for hETerophilic graphs, which unifies feature dimensionality across graphs and exploits latent similarity structures within graphs, enabling effective representation learning and robust cross-dataset generalization under heterophily. Specifically, we introduce a feature alignment mechanism that projects node features from different graphs into a consistent representation space with unified dimensionality, facilitating cross-dataset generalization. Based on the aligned features, we design a monophily-based message-passing mechanism that identifies and aggregates structurally similar two-hop neighbors to extract informative latent similarity information. This mechanism is further integrated into a dual-encoder architecture to capture complementary structural patterns and learn high-quality node representations on heterophilic graphs. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that MAGNET significantly outperforms baselines on heterophilic graphs, achieving improvements of 6.75% on Crocodile and 4.49% on Cornell, while maintaining competitive performance on homophilic graphs. Moreover, it exhibits superior generalization in cross-dataset learning. Our code is available at https://github.com/xusun0111/MAGNET. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Effects of black soldier fly larvae meal on hepatic metabolism and intestinal health in juvenile southern catfish (Silurus meridionalis): Insights from non-targeted metabolomics
abstract: To investigate the effects of replacing fishmeal (FM) with black soldier fly larvae meal (BSFLM) on hepatic metabolism and intestinal health in juvenile southern catfish (Silurus meridionalis), six isonitrogenous and isoenergetic diets were formulated with graded replacement levels of 0%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% and fed to fish for 8 weeks. Intestinal antioxidant parameters, serum immune factors, hepatic free amino acids, and non-targeted hepatic metabolomics were analyzed. No significant differences were observed among groups in intestinal superoxide dismutase (SOD), glutaredoxin (GSH-PX), total antioxidant capacity (T-AOC), or malondialdehyde (MDA) (ANOVA, all P > 0.05). Serum interleukin-10 (IL-10) showed a significant linear increase with increasing BSFLM inclusion (P = 0.021), indicating dose-dependent anti-inflammatory immunomodulation. Hepatic free amino acid profiling revealed that ornithine decreased significantly with increasing replacement (P = 0.012), S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) peaked in the H50 group (36.59 vs. 24.00 in H0, P = 0.006), proline decreased significantly (P = 0.030), taurine and cysteine were significantly elevated in the H50 group (P = 0.007 and 0.022, respectively), and gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) declined significantly (P = 0.004). Non-targeted metabolomics revealed a three-phase metabolic trajectory: 10–20% replacement represented an adaptation phase characterized by decoupling of central nitrogen metabolism from anabolism; 30% constituted a transition phase with synergistic integration of energy metabolism, carbohydrate utilization, and glucuronidation detoxification; 40–50% represented a stress/dysregulation phase, marked by a coordinated stress module containing norepinephrine and pyroglutamic acid, with 2-furoic acid emerging as a potential stress biomarker at 50% inclusion. The number of differentially abundant metabolites increased from 7 in the H10 group to over 60 in the H50 group. KEGG pathway enrichment confirmed activation of amino acid and secondary metabolite biosynthesis at low levels, while high levels enriched oxidative stress-related pathways including glutathione metabolism, ferroptosis, and ABC transporters. Collectively, these findings indicate that BSFLM replacement should not exceed 30% in juvenile southern catfish diets to balance sustainable protein utilization with maintenance of metabolic homeostasis and overall health. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: RoC-GRL: A right-of-way communication graph reinforcement learning multi-agent decision-making method for mixed-traffic unsignalized intersection
abstract: Safe cooperative control of connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs) at unsignalized intersections in mixed traffic is an important foundation for advancing intelligent transportation toward collective intelligence. To address heterogeneous vehicle-interaction modeling and safe continuous-action exploration, we propose RoC-GRL, a graph reinforcement learning decision-making method integrating right-of-way constraints and communication topology. First, potential path conflicts, passing priorities, CAV perception information, and V2V communication topology are explicitly structured to construct a local right-of-way yielding graph and a global CAV communication graph. These graphs represent asymmetric yielding relationships among mixed-traffic participants and communication-based cooperation among CAVs, respectively. Second, a sequential graph representation learning architecture is designed. Multi-head attention extracts right-of-way-sensitive local interaction features, while communication-graph message passing aggregates global cooperative information, producing a high-level state representation for centralized multi-vehicle decision-making. Based on this representation, TD3 generates a centralized cooperative policy for multiple agents. To address high-risk exploration under potential conflicts, a behavioral exploration optimization mechanism jointly considering time-to-collision and yielding priority dynamically adjusts the action boundary of each CAV. The resulting behavioral-boundary deviation is incorporated into the policy loss, allowing execution-level safety constraints to influence policy learning. Risk-prioritized experience replay and a structured reward function considering safety, efficiency, and cooperation further enhance the learning of safety-critical experiences. Comprehensive experiments in a CARLA mixed-traffic environment demonstrate that RoC-GRL achieves stable training convergence and outperforms the baseline methods in traffic efficiency and safe cooperative decision-making. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Cash transfers and social preferences of children
abstract: We study the effects of a large unconditional cash transfer program on social preferences of children in rural Kenya using a randomized controlled trial. We measure the social preferences of 4022 children with survey questions and incentivized behavioral games three years after the cash transfer. First, we find no persistent economic effects of the program. Additionally, we find no consistent evidence that children from the treatment group or that children from the spillover group are more or less prosocial than children from the control group. However, we find some evidence of reduced psychological well-being among adults and children in spillover households. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: From Individual Reasoning to Collaborative Engagement: Continuity of Student Problematic in Grade 1 Mathematical Problem Solving
abstract: This qualitative study examined the continuity of student problematic from individual reasoning to collaborative engagement in a Grade 1 mathematics classroom within the Transformative Lesson Study Incorporating Open Approach (TLSOA) context. Seven Grade 1 students were followed across six lessons on addition and subtraction. Data were collected through video and audio recordings, students’ written work, field notes, and photographs, and analyzed using protocol analysis and analytic description. The findings show that student problematic remained observable when students re-engaged with the same mathematical problem in small groups. Student problematic appeared through proposing, questioning, explaining, checking, reconsidering, and coordinating mathematical ideas. The study contributes to understanding how young learners’ mathematical engagement continues across changing social contexts. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

title: Granular-ball graph coarsening for graph representation learning
abstract: Graph coarsening provides an effective approach for improving the computational efficiency of Graph Neural Networks; however, existing paradigms often suffer from a connectivity-semantics gap, where rigid partitioning leads to a resolution mismatch that compromises structural integrity. To resolve these challenges, we propose GBC-GL, a novel granular-ball-based coarsening framework designed for high-fidelity graph representation learning. GBC-GL initiates with a connectivity-driven decomposition to safeguard the global topological skeleton. Building on this, we develop a structure-aware partitioning strategy that synergistically fuses PageRank-derived centrality with multi-scale features to map nodes into optimal granules. Crucially, a dynamic granularity control mechanism adaptively modulates aggregation scales based on local structural complexity, effectively mitigating information collapse in critical motifs while maximizing redundancy reduction. Extensive experiments across 16 benchmark datasets demonstrate the superiority of GBC-GL: it consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance, yielding a 95.94% accuracy on Physics for node classification, 84.80% on YEAST for graph classification, and a 0.628 mean absolute error on ZINC for graph regression. Notably, GBC-GL delivers a 50-fold to 60-fold acceleration compared to spectral-based methods on representative graph classification benchmarks, effectively bridging the gap between high-efficiency graph compression and high-precision predictive modeling. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/GBC-GL-1DD3/. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Human behaviour in wildfire emergencies: insights from evacuation decision-making and timing across Canada, Australia, and the United States
abstract: Wildfires often require rapid evacuation to save lives, leading residents to make quick and context-specific transportation decisions that may differ across countries and cultures. This study examines intended evacuation behaviours during wildfires, focusing on promptness, departure time, and cross-country differences. Surveys were conducted across Canada, the United States, and Australia (with sample sizes of 1,366, 1,490, and 1,173, respectively), and the data were used to run advanced choice modelling techniques to estimate factors influencing time-related decisions. The findings emphasized the importance of preparedness, reasons for evacuating, and risk perception in shaping responses to emergencies. Moreover, results identified country differences and similarities in evacuation preparedness time. For instance, employment, age, and income were factors relevant only in the U.S. context, while gender was significant exclusively in the Australian context. For all three countries, households with older adults were less likely to evacuate promptly, while households with children were more likely to evacuate promptly. The study also revealed that complex models showed minimal or no improvement in fit relative to simpler models. These insights on evacuation decisions and departure times, especially across jurisdictional boundaries, can assist in improving generalized wildfire evacuation plans and implementing more inclusive emergency communication strategies. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Urban residential cues to care in Detroit neighborhoods: A validated lot level virtual audit tool
abstract: High-quality built environments have potential to improve the mental and physical health of residents. Qualitatively, such environments are characterized by the visible evidence of human intervention and maintenance, including cues to care (CTC). However, to date, there has not been a validated way to quantify CTC that accounts for structure-inclusive lot types (i.e., residential, commercial). We present a validated tool that allows entire urban neighborhoods to be assessed (including occupied properties and vacant lots). We validated lot-scale physical CTC against measures of neighborhood conditions that have been widely associated with residents’ health. These measures include land use amenities and resident perceptions of neighborhood cohesion, attractiveness, and safety. We developed a novel coding tool that expands current geospatial CTC tools to quantitatively assess urban residential CTC. We applied Lot Level Cues to Care (LLCTC) to 781 lots across 245 street segments in Detroit, MI. We then investigated the relationship between LLCTC (where higher values indicate more CTC) and widely used as well as validated measures of neighborhood conditions, in a survey of 214 Detroit residents. We found negative correlations between LLCTC scores and signs of disorder and area deprivation. We also found significant associations between LLCTC scores and perceived neighborhood attractiveness. Although only approaching statistical significance, higher perceived cohesion and greater perceived safety were also associated with higher LLCTC scores. In conclusion, LLCTC is a valid quantitative geospatial measure of CTC in an urban residential environment, as validated by resident perceptions of their neighborhoods. © 2026

title: Valuing the ecosystem service gap in private forestland management: evidence from Texas and Louisiana
abstract: Private forestlands generate substantial ecosystem services that function as positive externalities, often requiring private operations to bear costs. This market failure creates a gap between private incentives and socially optimal forest stewardship, which leads to chronic underinvestment in sustainable forestry management practices. Using the contingent valuation method, we measure the divergence in forest stewardship by evaluating five practices across NIPF operations in Texas and Louisiana. Results show that thinning requires the highest average cost-share at around 53%, while prescribed burning presents the lowest barrier at around 30%. When translated to monetary terms, establishment commands the highest private valuation at around $308 per acre, whereas prescribed burning shows the lowest Implied WTP at around $42 per acre. We find that the willingness to pool management with neighboring operations is associated with lower required cost-share percentages across all practices. Land size is associated with lower required cost-share percentages for establishment, but shows limited evidence of association for the other practices. These findings illuminate the economic mechanisms underlying the market failure in ecosystem service provision and demonstrate how practice-specific incentive design and landscape-scale collaboration can more efficiently align private operation behavior with social objectives for forest-based natural capital stewardship. © 2026 The Authors. title: Determinants of membrane sensitivity to the Mastoparan-1 peptide from Polybia Paulista
abstract: The membrane-disrupting peptide Mastoparan-1 (MP-1), derived from the wasp Polybia paulista is known to possess antimicrobial properties, and exhibits enhanced activity against a number of cancer cell lines relative to healthy cells. Due to the mechanism of action of MP-1 it is likely that differences in plasma membrane lipid composition arising from cancer associated mutations, such as localisation of phosphatidylserine (PS) lipids to the outer leaflet of the plasma membrane, are involved in driving that enhanced activity. Rapid screening of MP-1 mutants in a combined approach using model membrane and cell-based biological assays, has led to the identification of a number of derivative peptides with enhanced selectivity for cancer-like membrane models and breast cancer cell lines and provided insights into the mechanism of membrane disruption and cell death. Notably, the morphology of the membrane perturbations observed by Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) and activity in cell model systems can change considerably in response to single-point mutations in the MP-1 sequence, indicating a complex structure-activity relationship. © 2026 The Authors

title: Psychometric properties and validity of the Family Accommodation Scale–Patient Version (FAS-PV) in adults with obsessive compulsive disorder: A French adaptation
abstract: Background: Family accommodation (FA) is a common phenomenon in obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD) and is associated with greater symptom severity, functional impairment, and poorer treatment outcomes. Assessing FA is therefore clinically relevant, yet no validated French-language instrument is currently available to assess accommodation from the patient’s perspective. Objective: The present study aimed to translate and validate a French version of the Family Accommodation Scale–Patient Version (FAS-PV) and to examine its psychometric properties in adults with OCD. Methods: Eighty-five adults diagnosed with OCD and 68 of their relatives were recruited in a specialized outpatient clinic. Patients completed the French FAS-PV alongside measures of OCD severity (Y-BOCS), relative-reported accommodation (FAS-SR), psychological distress, functional impairment, and family functioning. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses were conducted, and internal consistency, test–retest reliability, and convergent and divergent validity were examined. Results: The French FAS-PV demonstrated excellent internal consistency (McDonald’s ω = 0.89) and strong test–retest reliability (r = 0.89). Exploratory analyses supported a four-factor solution explaining 51.8 % of the variance, although item distribution partially diverged from the original theoretical structure. Confirmatory analyses provided partial support for the four-factor model, with adequate absolute fit but incremental indices slightly below conventional thresholds. Convergent validity was supported by significant associations with OCD severity, family accommodation, distress, and functional impairment, while divergent validity was confirmed by the absence of associations with impulsivity and age. Conclusions: The French FAS-PV demonstrates appreciable psychometric properties as an instrument for assessing family accommodation in adults with OCD and provides a useful tool for clinical practice and research in French-speaking contexts. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. title: A trustworthy evidential transformer with linear fusion and Gram-matrix distillation for efficient optic disc and cup segmentation
abstract: Accurate glaucoma screening relies on the vertical cup-to-disc ratio (VCDR), but automation remains challenging. A critical trade-off between computational efficiency, segmentation accuracy, and model trustworthiness hinders clinical deployment. Vision Transformers offer global context but suffer from quadratic complexity (O(N2)), while standard Convolutional Neural Networks lack explicit mechanisms for uncertainty quantification (UQ). To bridge this gap, we propose EviG-Former (Evidential Gram Transformer), a highly efficient student network trained via Teacher-Student distillation. Our framework combines Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) with Linear Multi-Scale Token Fusion (L-MSTF). We designed an Uncertainty-Gated Feature Fusion (UGF) module that uses epistemic uncertainty to guide gradient flow, focusing on ambiguous regions like faint vessel boundaries. Additionally, Gram-Matrix Consistency Distillation ensures the lightweight student maintains topological integrity. We validated EviG-Former on RIM-ONE-r3, Drishti-GS, ORIGA, and REFUGE datasets. It achieved highly competitive Optic Cup segmentation Dice scores (0.9004, 0.9423, 0.8916, and 0.9005, respectively) when evaluated against thirteen leading baselines. Crucially, this performance requires only 0.69M parameters (up to 178× fewer than recent high-capacity networks) while sustaining real-time processing (≈60.7 FPS). Furthermore, the estimated VCDR mean absolute error falls below the 0.05 clinical threshold on three datasets. By uniting diagnostic precision, edge efficiency, and calibrated uncertainty mapping, EviG-Former effectively addresses the traditional capacity-accuracy-trustworthiness trade-off. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The power of varying more than one thing at a time
abstract: Background: Varying one thing at a time (VOTAT) is considered a universal approach for designing informative experiments. Its core idea is that controlled experiments can be designed by manipulating a single variable. However, we show that this single-manipulation heuristic can produce misleading evidence in contexts involving interrelated variables. We argue that varying more than one thing at a time (MOTAT) can be more informative when learners’ prior beliefs render alternative explanations implausible. Aims: To test these claims, we compared single-manipulation to MOTAT experiments in a Bayesian learning simulation and a pre-registered empirical study on children's learning about water displacement. Sample: Participants in the empirical study were 185 children aged 6–9. Methods: Learners predicted which of two spheres would displace more water and then observed an animation of the spheres being submerged. In the single-manipulation experiments, the spheres differed either only in size or only in material, leading to a confound of these dimensions with mass. In the MOTAT experiments, both size and material were manipulated such that the larger sphere was lighter. We investigated the formal informativeness of single-manipulation and MOTAT experiments (simulation study) and their effect on children's learning, as measured via a post- and transfer test (empirical study). Results: MOTAT experiments were most informative and led to the highest transfer test performance. Conclusion: These findings provide initial evidence that VOTAT's core heuristic has a narrower scope than is commonly assumed. When variables are interrelated, deliberately varying more than one variable may be the better choice. © 2026 The Authors

title: Gendered environmental leadership and the rise of biodiversity finance
abstract: This paper examines whether gender diversity in environmental governance is associated with biodiversity-finance outcomes across the 27 European Union countries between 2012 and 2023. We distinguish between administrative, ministerial, and legislative dimensions of women's representation and evaluate their relationship with biodiversity-finance volume and intensity using fixed-effects Poisson and fractional-response models. The results provide limited evidence that gender representation alone systematically predicts biodiversity-finance outcomes. Female representation in environmental administrations is negatively associated with biodiversity-finance intensity, while female environment ministers are positively associated with intensity. No robust unconditional relationship is observed for biodiversity-finance volume. However, several conditional patterns emerge. In the later years of the sample, higher female representation in environmental administrations, ministerial positions, and parliamentary environmental committees becomes more strongly associated with biodiversity expenditure. Similarly, the positive association between female ministers and biodiversity-finance outcomes is stronger in countries characterized by higher levels of women's political empowerment. By contrast, threshold analyses provide little evidence of critical-mass effects. Overall, the findings suggest that the relationship between gender diversity and biodiversity finance is conditional on institutional and policy context rather than representation alone. These results contribute to the emerging literature on biodiversity finance by highlighting how governance structures may shape biodiversity-related public spending. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: AC-UKAN: An enhanced U-KAN framework integrating modulated deformable convolution and mixed pooling
abstract: Accurate medical image segmentation is pivotal for clinical diagnosis. Segmentation targets in medical images differ in appearance, geometric morphology, and contextual organization, which motivates complementary architectural choices rather than a single universal mechanism. We propose AC-UKAN, a depth-specialized extension of U-KAN that assigns modulated deformable convolution (MDConv) to the shallow encoder for input-conditioned geometric sampling, tokenized Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (Tok-KAN) blocks to the low-resolution semantic stages for an alternative nonlinear parameterization, and a mixed pooling module (MPM) to the bottleneck for combined isotropic and anisotropic context aggregation. AC-UKAN was evaluated on the three heterogeneous two-dimensional binary segmentation benchmarks used by U-KAN: BUSI (breast ultrasound), GlaS (gland histopathology), and CVC-ClinicDB (colonoscopic imaging). For a controlled comparison, eight representative segmentation architectures were trained locally under an identical protocol. AC-UKAN achieved an average IoU of 80.78% and DSC of 88.86% with 6.66 M parameters, improving IoU over the U-KAN baseline by up to 4.04 percentage points on the evaluated splits, with its largest gains on BUSI and CVC. Component ablations showed that MDConv and MPM each provided incremental improvements in overlap-based metrics relative to the baseline and to each other's single-module configuration, whereas their combined effect and boundary-distance behavior varied across datasets. Under the official U-KAN protocol, AC-UKAN therefore offers a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off among the evaluated representative architectures, rather than uniform superiority across all three datasets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Fear of psychosis in an OCD analogue sample: Prevalence and associated factors
abstract: Obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD) includes heterogeneous presentations, despite the disproportionate research and clinical attention on contamination and symmetry symptoms. Colloquially coined “schizophrenia OCD”, obsessional fears of having or developing a psychotic disorder (or “going crazy”) and associated compulsions have received growing recognition within psychoeducational contexts and patient communities. This preliminary study examined the prevalence and associated factors of fears of psychosis among a university student sample (N = 154). Participants completed an online questionnaire that included symptom checklists assessing psychosis-related unwanted intrusive thoughts and compulsive behaviours, alongside a series of validated measures. Fears of psychosis were commonly endorsed: 77.9% endorsed lifetime unwanted intrusive thoughts, 70.1% endorsed associated compulsive behaviours, and 83.1% reported at least one psychosis-related unwanted intrusive thought or compulsive behaviour. Fears of losing control of your thoughts or actions was the most frequently endorsed intrusive thought (50.6%), whereas fear of developing a psychotic illness (18.3%) was rated most distressing. The most frequently endorsed compulsive behavior was replacing “bad thoughts” with better thoughts (53.2%). Supporting our hypothesis, individuals meeting OCD symptom cut-offs were more likely to endorse psychosis-related fears. Finally, hierarchical regression analyses indicated that health anxiety and negative beliefs about losing control predicted psychosis-related unwanted intrusive thoughts, over and above demographic factors, OCD severity, or other clinically relevant variables. Findings underscore the need for recognition of fears of mental health issues in individuals with OCD and suggest that interventions targeting health anxiety and perceptions of loss of control may be particularly relevant. © 2026 The Authors. title: Do digital platforms delocalise consumer activity? Platform services, retail agglomeration and the localisation of neighbourhood dining and shopping
abstract: The platform economy is reshaping the relationship between digital service availability and physical retail activity. Yet how platform-service environments and physical retail provision are jointly associated with the localisation of dining and shopping visits, and whether these relationships vary across socioeconomic contexts, remains poorly understood. Using location-based service data from 6213 residential communities and more than 50 million dining and shopping records in Shenzhen, China, we measure local patronage as the share of each community's dining and shopping visits made to retailers within its proximate walking catchment. We combine income-stratified estimation using a heteroskedasticity-robust generalised method of moments spatial-error model (GMM-SEM) with gradient-boosted machine learning and SHAP interaction analysis to examine average, non-linear and interaction associations. Three findings emerge. First, greater food-delivery and instant-retail availability is consistently associated with lower physical-visit localisation, with the negative association for food delivery generally stronger in lower-income communities. Second, retail attractiveness and format show marked socioeconomic heterogeneity: restaurant ratings are more strongly positively associated with dining localisation in higher-income communities, whereas traditional markets are positively associated with shopping localisation across all income groups but most strongly in lower-income communities. Third, SHAP interaction analyses show that this negative platform–localisation association is conditional on physical retail provision: positive interaction contributions between platform-service availability and retail agglomeration emerge where restaurant and shopping-mall densities are high, consistent with a buffering role of dense local retail clusters. These findings show that relationships between platform-service environments and physical-visit localisation are conditional on retail agglomeration and neighbourhood socioeconomic context, with implications for retail location strategy, commercial real estate and neighbourhood retail planning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Riveted Fe–N5 moieties confined in curved graphitic carbon enable a triple-protection mechanism for robust acidic oxygen reduction electrocatalysis
abstract: Fe–N–C exhibits exceptional catalytic activity and stands as a prominent representative of single-atom catalysts (SACs). However, the activity and, especially, the stability of its active sites pose a formidable challenge for practical applications. Therefore, we first performed DFT predictions on active site structural models featuring curvature and axial coordination, revealing that the curved Fe–N5 configuration simultaneously boosts both the activity and stability. Then we adopt an O-Tolidine molecular-induced strategy to construct the curved graphitic carbon layers, which anchor Fe single atoms in a bent and axial N-coordinated configuration. The molecular-assisted effect facilitates micropore formation, accelerates the graphitization process, and simultaneously provides additional nitrogen coordination sites, ultimately achieving the curved Fe–N5 configuration. The curved Fe–N5 motifs establish a triple protection mechanism: resistance to Fe dissolution, suppression of carbon corrosion and shielding against H⁺ attack, thus alleviating the long-standing activity–stability trade-off in SACs. Benefiting from these structural merits, the as-obtained catalyst delivers outstanding durability in H2-O2 fuel cell, achieving a high peak power density of 1.37 W cm−2 with only 10.2% performance degradation after 10,000 square-wave cycles—far lower than the 29.8% loss of conventional Fe–N–C. Under H2-Air conditions at 0.65 V, it retains 74.3% of its initial current density over 200 h. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Further construction of 8 × 8 bijective S-boxes based on coupled Tent map and permutation particle swarm optimization algorithm
abstract: Aiming at constructing an 8 × 8 substitution box (S-box) with strong resistance against multiple cryptanalytic attacks, this paper proposes a discrete permutation particle swarm optimization (PPSO) scheme integrating a heterogeneous initialization strategy and a local refinement mechanism. This scheme employs a two-dimensional coupled Tent chaotic map and reference anchor synchronization to construct a heterogeneous initial population, thereby achieving synergistic optimization between random search and algebraic priors. A discrete PPSO algorithm based on finite permutation sequences is designed to ensure that the evolutionary process satisfies bijective constraints. A fitness function that balances multiple cryptographic criteria is constructed to guide the search, and a local refinement strategy is incorporated to enhance the ability to direct the search toward high-performance solution neighborhoods. Experiments demonstrate that the overall cryptographic properties of the newly constructed 8×8 S-box are superior to those of similar constructions. While ensuring that the differential uniformity reaches the best known value of 4, its nonlinearity is as high as 110. The S-box not only satisfies bijectivity and achieves the optimal algebraic degree of 7, but also possesses excellent strict avalanche and bit independence properties, thus achieving a good trade-off among various cryptographic criteria. © The Author(s) under exclusive licence to Sociedade Brasileira de Matemática Aplicada e Computacional 2026.

title: High-performance thin film nanocomposite membrane prepared from 2D ZIF-67 nanosheets and Pebax for natural gas dehydration
abstract: Thin film nanocomposites (TFNs) fabricated with metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are considered as promising alternatives for natural gas (NG) dehydration. However, it remains difficult to realize both high water permeance and selectivity at the same time. The ultrathin selective layer of the TFN structure inherently provides higher permeance than traditional membranes. In this research, TFN membranes were fabricated via incorporating ultrathin ZIF-67 nanosheets into a Pebax 1657 polymer matrix with polyacrylonitrile (PAN) porous support. The 2D ZIF-67, characterized by their leaf-like morphology, create well-defined molecular sieving channels while maintaining excellent interfacial compatibility. A key innovation of this work is the achievement of exceptionally high separation performance. The optimized membrane with 12.5 wt% ZIF-67 loading demonstrated exceptional separation capabilities, a remarkable 38,356 GPU in water vapor permeation along with H2O/CH4 separation factor of 18,235 was documented, which surpasses most reported membranes for NG dehydration. The synthesized membranes also exhibited exceptional stability of 10 days. This work demonstrates that 2D MOF nanosheets can overcome the typical permeability-selectivity trade-off, advancing membrane based NG dehydration toward practical applications. Copyright © 2026. title: Approximate minimization of interpretations in fuzzy description logics under the Gödel semantics
abstract: The problem of minimizing fuzzy interpretations in fuzzy description logics (FDLs) is important both theoretically and practically. For instance, fuzzy or weighted social networks can be modeled as fuzzy interpretations, where individuals represent actors and roles capture interactions. Minimizing such interpretations yields more compact representations, which can significantly improve the efficiency of reasoning and analysis tasks in knowledge-based systems. We present the first algorithm that minimizes a finite fuzzy interpretation while preserving fuzzy concept assertions in FDLs without the Baaz projection operator and the universal role, under the Gödel semantics. The considered class of FDLs ranges from the sublogic of fALC without the union operator and the universal restriction to the FDL that extends fALCreg with inverse roles and nominals. Our algorithm is given in an extended form that supports approximate preservation: it minimizes a finite fuzzy interpretation I while preserving fuzzy concept assertions up to a degree γ∈(0,1]. Its time complexity is O((mlogl+n)logn), where n is the size of the domain of I, m is the number of nonzero instances of atomic roles in I, and l is the number of distinct fuzzy values used in such instances plus 2. Methodologically, our approach fundamentally differs from existing ones, as it avoids quotient constructions traditionally employed for minimizing fuzzy interpretations and fuzzy automata. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Routine Distributional Analysis of Health Inequality Impact by Socioeconomic Group: Technical Feasibility Study in Queensland, Australia
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to evaluate the technical feasibility of routine distributional analyses of healthcare interventions in Australia, by adapting a Health Inequality Impact Calculator for Queensland. Building on methods established in a previous study in England, the calculator compares the magnitude of health inequality impact across interventions for different diseases. Methods The calculator was adapted for adults in Queensland using the Index of Relative Socio-economic Advantage and Disadvantage quintiles, Australian Bureau of Statistics population estimates, 2023 hospital admissions (International Classification of Diseases-10th edition 3-digit level) from Queensland Health, and published quality-adjusted life expectancy. It was used to conduct aggregate distributional cost-effectiveness analysis of 5 interventions for diseases with relatively high prevalence in disadvantaged groups, based on existing cost-effectiveness results identified by a targeted review. The health inequality impact was summarized using the slope index of inequality in quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs). Results The selected interventions were 2 screening interventions for diabetes and hypertension, and 3 treatment interventions for chronic kidney disease. The calculator demonstrated that all 5 interventions would reduce health inequality. Population screening for diabetes had the greatest impact on reducing health inequality of 8562 QALYs. Among the 3 treatment interventions, intensive blood pressure control had the greatest impact, with a health inequality benefit of 514 QALYs. Conclusions Routine aggregate distributional cost-effectiveness analysis of interventions in Queensland is feasible, once standard cost-effectiveness estimates are available. The calculator for Queensland enables fast, transparent, and replicable analysis of health inequality impacts using minimal data, with visual outputs to explore trade-offs between health outcomes, inequality, and cost-effectiveness. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Modelling temporal thermal taste responses: Variability, thermal taster subgroups and potential mechanisms
abstract: Thermal taste is a phenomenon where some individuals perceive taste sensations when temperature is applied to the tongue. Reported tastes vary across individuals and temperature ranges, but limitations in earlier phenotyping methods made it difficult to explore underlying mechanisms. The RapCoTT approach addresses this by capturing real-time taste reports at the approximate stimulation temperature. This study analysed data from three RapCoTT studies (including previously published data in Botha et al., 2021) to examine relationships between reported tastes and temperature, using model-based clustering to identify patterns in thermal taster responses. From responses of 230 respondents, three distinct subgroups emerged. Cluster 1 (C1) often reported salty taste, either with any taste except metallic (State 4) or with metallic (State 2). Cluster 2 (C2) showed sour (State 2), savoury (State 4), and metallic (State 3) responses. Cluster 3 (C3) featured bitter taste combined with dominant sweet (State 2), metallic (State 5), or sour (State 3). By identifying critical temperatures where specific tastes or combinations occurred, this study highlighted potential temperature-sensitive receptor mechanisms underlying thermal tastes, in particular TRPA1 and TRPM5, but also TRPM4, TRPV4, TRPV1 and TMC4 and the need for research to understand potential variation in the identified receptors and thermal taste phenotype. © 2026 The Authors

title: Aligning risk frameworks with fieldwork realities: extending Rasmussen’s model to scientific research settings
abstract: Scientific fieldwork is an essential component of research across many academic disciplines. Fieldwork entails numerous risks, ranging from interpersonal to environmental risks, and can often result in physical and mental injury or illness. Despite these potential harms, standardized frameworks for understanding, managing, and responding to incidents in fieldwork remain underdeveloped. A limited understanding of incident causation in fieldwork contexts compounds this gap. In this article we propose that fieldwork, like other workplaces, operates as a complex socio-technical system in which people, cultural beliefs, governance, equipment, and the environment interact to create both safe and unsafe outcomes. To better understand the scientific fieldwork system, we conducted four focus groups to identify the people and institutions that constitute a fieldwork system and to characterize how these actors are organized within hierarchical levels. Through these sessions, we developed a classificatory scheme of variables that together influence safety outcomes. In total, 91 different actors across seven hierarchical levels and a contextual domain were identified. The resulting ActorMap and associated contributory factors offer a foundational framework for operationalizing safety and risk approaches, such as AcciMapping, in fieldwork settings. By incorporating these insights, we can enhance training, policy development, and institutional support structures to better equip researchers for the challenges of fieldwork. © 2026 The Authors.

title: A vacation queueing model for the performance of blockchain systems by different transaction behaviors
abstract: Performance bottlenecks have become a critical constraint hindering the further development of blockchain. Applying queueing theory to model blockchain systems provides an effective approach for performance analysis. As transactions serve as the core entities in blockchain systems, investigating the impact of transaction behaviors on system performance is of great necessity and significance. Firstly, considering the phenomena that transactions may suspend upon arrival or renege during waiting in the system, this study clarifies the transaction confirmation mechanism and constructs a multi-server vacation queueing model. A two-dimensional Markov process is established based on the states of transactions and miners. The steady-state solution is obtained via the successive over-relaxation method, and the key performance metric—transaction latency—is derived. Secondly, the influences of transaction suspension rate and reneging rate on latency are analyzed. Results show that higher suspension and reneging rates contribute to better system performance. Finally, simulation experiments and correlation analysis verify the model reliability, indicating an almost perfect consistency between theoretical and experimental results. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Incentivized sadism: The impact of intrinsic and extrinsic reward on sadistic aggression
abstract: In two studies (one correlational, one experimental; total N = 419), we tested whether dispositional sadism is related to the anticipation of experiencing pleasure (instead of guilt) during and after aggressing, and whether this anticipation motivates aggressive behavior. We also tested whether individuals higher in sadism are less likely to use dissonance reduction strategies for behaving aggressively (and feeling pleasure while doing so). Study 1 looked at how dispositional sadism is related to the anticipation of intrinsic and extrinsic rewards of behaving aggressively. Study 2 looked at whether offering a meager extrinsic reward for behaving aggressively (i.e., financial compensation) increased the experience of pleasure and decreased the experience of guilt during and after aggression – a dissonance reduction strategy – and whether this effect was reduced for people high (vs. low) in sadism. Results revealed that dispositional sadism positively predicts (1) the expectation of reward and lack of guilt after behaving aggressively (Study 1), (2) aggressive behavior in an animal-killing paradigm (Study 2), and (3) hedonic pleasure and lack of guilt while doing so (Study 2). Notably, these affective correlates of sadism were not maintained after aggression, suggesting that hedonic gains are short-lived. The effects of introducing a financial incentive for behaving aggressively were inconsistent across the main studies and a preliminary pilot study (reported in Supplementary Materials), and should be interpreted with caution. Overall, the current studies portray dispositional sadism as a trait primarily associated with intrinsic motivation for aggressive behaviour, driven by its emotional benefits — at least in the moment. © 2026 The Authors. title: Breaking the NOx-soot trade-off in compression ignition engines at mid-load with high-percentage n-Pentanol blends through charge cooling and oxygenation
abstract: The quest for sustainable and environmentally friendly fuel alternatives has significantly increased interest in exploring higher alcohols, particularly n-pentanol, as a promising oxygenated biofuel option for internal combustion engines. This study meticulously analyzed the combustion, performance and emission characteristics of a 60% n-pentanol/40% n-dodecane blend, designated P60D40 , and n-dodecane, D100, utilizing computational fluid dynamics simulations. Here, n-dodecane was used as a surrogate for diesel fuel. The analysis was conducted under a variety of engine operation control parameters to ensure a thorough understanding of their behaviors. The results showed that under identical operating conditions, the indicated thermal efficiency of the P60D40 blend was 47.94%, which is higher than the 44.32% for D100. Furthermore, the equivalent indicated specific fuel consumption for the P60D40 blend was 169.89 g/kWh, in contrast to the 183.77 g/kWh of D100. This represents a 7.55% reduction in fuel consumption, highlighting the efficiency benefits of using n-pentanol as a fuel component. In addition to the performance improvements, the study also found significant reductions in harmful emissions. Specifically, emissions of soot, nitrogen oxides and carbon dioxide were reduced by 91.46%, 86.18% and 12.91%, respectively, compared to D100. The utilization of a 60% n-pentanol blend demonstrates considerable potential, as it not only meets the selected Euro VI reference limits of 0.4 g/kWh and 0.01 g/kWh for NOx and soot, respectively, but also offers excellent performance characteristics. Moreover, it shows the capability to effectively address the common trade-off between NOx and soot emissions, particularly under mid-load operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Multiscale engineering of lignocellulosic materials: from hierarchical deconstruction to genetic reprogramming
abstract: The widespread reliance on fossil-derived materials has enabled modern manufacturing but has also driven plastic pollution, carbon emissions, and end-of-life waste challenges. Lignocellulosic biomass offers a renewable and biodegradable alternative, yet its intrinsic heterogeneity has historically limited precise materials design. In this Review, we present a unified multiscale engineering framework for lignocellulosic materials, using wood as an archetypal system to illustrate how structure–property–function relationships can be deliberately programmed from the molecular to the macroscopic scale. We synthesize recent advances in hierarchical deconstruction (top-down processing of cell-wall polymers into micro-, nano-, and molecular building blocks) alongside emerging hierarchical assembly strategies enabled by genetic reprogramming of cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin biosynthesis. This convergence enables unprecedented control over composition, anisotropy, interfaces, and transport pathways, yielding biomass-derived materials with tailored mechanical, optical, barrier, and electrochemical performance. We further discuss how these approaches reduce feedstock heterogeneity, improve process efficiency, and align materials development with circular-economy principles, carbon sequestration, and low-impact manufacturing. By linking molecular-level design and genetic modification to scalable processing routes and device-level functionality, this review positions engineered lignocellulosic materials as credible, high-performance alternatives to fossil-based plastics and composites, with transformative implications for energy, environmental, and sustainable manufacturing applications. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Towards reliable intelligent decision-making systems: implicit and explicit correlation analysis with hypergraph neural networks
abstract: Intelligent decision-making systems in autonomous operations require reliability analysis approaches capable of representing the complex, high-dimensional correlations among components, failure chains and decision measures. Conventional graph methods remain limited in describing both explicit structural dependencies and implicit influence pathways. This study proposes a Hypergraph Neural Network with Reversed Multi-Head Attention (HGNN-RMHA) that integrates explicit and implicit correlation modelling for interpretable and reliable decision support. The framework employs hyperedges to represent multi-node relations, while the Reversed Multi-Head Attention mechanism enhances sensitivity to low-frequency but crucial implicit features, enabling a unified representation of cross-layer dependencies. The Top-K adaptive association-rule mining approach further extracts semantically interpretable causal patterns, and comprehensive correlation analyses are conducted to reveal the intrinsic relationships between component failures and decision measures. Additionally, the Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA) knowledge-enhancement strategy injects rule-level priors into large language models (LLMs), aligning structural reasoning with natural language inference for rule-driven interpretability. Experimental evaluations on multiple public datasets verify that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing baselines in node classification, link prediction, correlation interpretation, and rule-based reasoning. The integration of explicit and implicit correlation effectively captures the cross-layer failures­ propagation patterns, thereby improving the trustworthiness and interpretability of intelligent decision-making in safety­ critical applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Budget Impact Analysis of System-Level Costs Associated With Topical Janus Kinase Inhibitor Therapies for Moderate Atopic Dermatitis in Germany
abstract: Objectives German statutory health insurance budgets are driven by escalation to advanced systemic therapies for atopic dermatitis (AD). Effective and affordable novel options for adults with AD are needed to reduce the economic burden. Our objective was to estimate the 5-year budget impact of adopting the topical Janus kinase inhibitor, 1.5% ruxolitinib cream, for adults with moderate AD, affected body surface area ≤ 20%, and clinical eligibility for systemic therapy from a German population perspective. Methods We developed a budget impact model that compares the current systemic treatment mix with a forward-looking intervention scenario in which 1.5% ruxolitinib cream is adopted for adult AD from 2026 onward. Uptake increases linearly to 25% by 2030 and proportionally displaces systemic therapies. Ruxolitinib cream costs were modeled based on real-world evidence. Direct costs included drug acquisition and nondrug medical costs; the societal perspective incorporated out-of-pocket costs and productivity losses. Results The systemic-eligible population was estimated at 330 600 patients in 2025, growing to 402 200 by 2030. Among those were 90 000 patients treated with 1.5% ruxolitinib cream in 2030. Over 2026 to 2030, costs were €39.8bn with ruxolitinib cream versus €44.1bn with current systemic treatments, yielding a cumulative budget impact of €4.3bn. Statutory health insurance savings accounted for 80% (€3.4bn) of those savings. Conclusions Under the modeled uptake and displacement assumptions, ruxolitinib cream could represent a cost-mitigating option that could reduce the economic burden of AD. Postlaunch evidence on utilization, persistence, and therapy switching is needed to validate and refine budget impact estimates. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Embedded micro-pin-fin heat sink with 3D manifold for cooling high-power electronics
abstract: The relentless increase in chip power density has driven heat fluxes beyond 1 kW cm−2, urgently demanding effective and efficient thermal management. Although embedded manifold microfluidic cooling with micro-pin-fin (MPF) arrays has emerged as a promising strategy, the cross-scale impacts of the complex three-dimensional (3D) architecture on the thermohydraulic performance remain to be elucidated, together with the underlying physical mechanisms. In this study, we conduct a comprehensive 3D numerical investigation of embedded HU-type manifold MPF heat sinks. Using a hierarchical three-model strategy, we analyze the influence of key MPF geometric parameters and array layouts on the thermohydraulic performance. To begin with, we consider in-line and staggered arrays of circular MPFs and compare against a conventional microchannel (MC) baseline. Systematic analysis shows that increasing MPF diameter reduces the maximum chip temperature rise (ΔTmax) while raising pressure drop (ΔP); conversely, increasing MPF height (Hf) yields the opposite trade-off when the cavity height (Hcav) of the microfluidic layer varies accordingly. With a fixed Hcav, however, increasing Hf reduces the top clearance, which suppresses bypass leakage and significantly enhances heat transfer. Further, transverse and longitudinal spacings highlight asymmetric cross-coupling effects. At large spacings, flow channeling circumvents MPFs through low-resistance pathways and creates wakes that severely degrade heat transfer. Moreover, by evaluating a variety of MPF cross-sections, we reveal that the diamond shape can outperform the MC baseline in both thermal and flow performance. At a heat flux of 2000 W cm−2, diamond-shaped MPFs simultaneously achieve lower ΔTmax (56 K) and ΔP (28 kPa), yielding a coefficient of performance exceeding 2000. These findings establish parametric design maps and mechanistic insights for optimizing manifold MPF heat sinks targeting high-power electronics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Integrating syntactic and semantic features for dual-task extraction in Arabic aspect-based sentiment analysis using graph convolutional networks
abstract: Arabic aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) remains underexplored, particularly end-to-end dual-task learning that jointly performs aspect term extraction (ATE) and aspect sentiment classification (ASC). Most existing Arabic ABSA approaches are pipeline-based or restricted to single-task identification, which weakens task synergy, constrains performance, and rarely leverages explicit syntactic structure. To address this gap, we propose a structure-aware, end-to-end model that integrates contextual semantics with linguistic structure to perform ATE and ASC tasks simultaneously. Our architecture builds on contextual representations from an Arabic BERT, augmented with token-level attention and sequential modeling via a BiLSTM. A gated fusion module then learns adaptive weights to combine these features into a unified representation. To incorporate linguistic relations, we introduce a dual-branch graph convolutional network that captures (i) dependency-based syntactic relations and (ii) part-of-speech relational patterns. Both branches use attention-weighted adjacency matrices to reduce sensitivity to parser noise and to emphasize sentiment-relevant links. The proposed model is evaluated on three Arabic ABSA datasets (Hotel, News, and HAAD). It achieves ATE and ASC accuracies of 95.29% and 90.87% on Hotel, 91.85% and 82.15% on News, and 90.96% and 75.06% on HAAD, respectively. Under strict end-to-end exact-match evaluation of aspect–sentiment pairs, the model achieves F1-scores of 71.12%, 64.98%, and 33.81% on the Hotel, News, and HAAD datasets, respectively. © 2026 The Authors. title: Logit-guided feature denoising distillation for model compression
abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective strategy for compressing deep models by transferring knowledge from a large teacher network to a lightweight student network, which is particularly valuable for reliable deployment in resource-constrained industrial environments. Traditional distillation methods usually align features as a whole, ignoring that they often contain background activations unrelated to the target as well as scattered noisy responses. To address this problem, Logit-Guided Feature Denoising (LGFD) distillation is proposed, which integrates the logit discriminative encoder (LDE) and the feature denoising mask (FDM) into a novel framework to guide the student toward acquiring the truly discriminative feature of the teacher. Specifically, the LDE encodes the teacher’s logit discriminability for feature denoising, thereby aligning features along semantic directions. Based on the LDE, the FDM highlights the attentive regions related to label class, which can help suppress redundant and noisy activations in the feature maps. Comprehensive experiments covering CIFAR-100, ImageNet, MS-COCO, and RTE confirm both the effectiveness and wide applicability of LGFD to classification, detection, and natural language inference. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Positive emotion dispositions and human values in a Brazilian sample: Structural evaluation and exploratory network analysis
abstract: Understanding how positive emotions relate to broader motivational systems across cultural contexts is essential for clarifying their underlying structure. In this study, we examined the organization of positive emotions and their motivational correlates in Brazil, contributing to ongoing debates about the structure and foundations of positive emotions across cultures. Analyzing responses to the Dispositional Positive Emotions Scales (DPES; Shiota et al., 2006 ) in a Brazilian sample ( N = 435), we found mixed fit and reliability across individual scales, but neither the full seven-factor solution nor a previously reported six-factor model adequately fit the data. Following stability-based item pruning, EGA yielded four exploratory communities based on 18 items that cut across the original categories: Social Recognition, Awe & Happiness, Compassionate Caregiving, and Self-Contentment & Growth. We examined how these emergent communities mapped onto values as indicators of motivational goals. Value associations differed across communities, particularly between Compassionate Caregiving and Social Recognition. Overall, the findings identify exploratory item communities showing differentiated associations with several human values in this sample. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Effect of hemp protein isolate on the quality and in vitro digestion of high moisture plant-based meat
abstract: Plant-based meat (PBM) offers high protein, low fat, and cholesterol-free benefits, yet optimizing its nutritional and functional quality remains a challenge. This study incorporated hemp protein isolate (HPI) into soy protein–wheat gluten blends to produce PBM via high-moisture extrusion, examining HPI effects on quality, structure, digestibility, and bioactivity. Results showed that HPI improved mechanical properties, color, and fiber formation; at 40% HPI, disulfide bonds peaked, enhancing water-holding capacity and network density. During in vitro digestion, HPI reduced α-helix/β-sheet ratios and increased random coils, facilitating enzyme access. Protein digestibility peaked at 30% HPI (48.47% gastric, 84.52% intestinal), yielding more small peptides. Although total peptide counts dropped, 28 unique HPI-derived peptides appeared, with six predicted in silico as potential α-glucosidase inhibitors. Moderate HPI addition thus improves PBM quality and digestibility while offering potential bioactivity, providing a theoretical basis for functional PBM development. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Age-related emergence of behavioral deficits and amyloid pathology in the J20 mouse model of Alzheimer's disease
abstract: Transgenic mouse models carrying familial Alzheimer's disease mutations are widely used in preclinical research, yet phenotypic variability across age and sex can complicate experimental design and interpretation. Here, we performed an age-stratified behavioral and pathological phenotyping of the hAPP-J20 mouse model using independent cohorts of female and male mice at 3, 6, and 9 months of age (n = 5–21 per group depending on the assay). Animals underwent a battery of cognitive and non-cognitive assays assessing well-being–related behaviors (nesting, splash test), locomotion and exploration (open field), anxiety-like behavior (elevated O-maze), working memory (Y-maze spontaneous alternation), and spatial learning and memory (Barnes maze). In parallel, amyloid pathology was quantified using ELISA measurements of Aβ1–40 and Aβ1–42 levels and histological assessment of hippocampal plaque burden. J20 mice exhibited early behavioral alterations detectable at 3 months, including impaired working memory, increased locomotor activity, and alterations in self-care behaviors. Spatial learning alterations were detectable from 3 months, whereas robust spatial-memory deficits became more consistently evident at later ages. Soluble and insoluble Aβ species increased progressively with age, whereas hippocampal plaque pathology was minimal at 3 months and rose markedly at 6 and 9 months. Analyses including sex as an independent factor identified endpoint-specific sex-related effects but did not support a consistent sex-specific trajectory. Overall, non-cognitive and working memory deficits emerge early, while spatial memory impairment and amyloid pathology dominate at later stages. This study provides a reference framework to guide age- and sex-appropriate experimental design in preclinical studies using the J20 model. © 2026

title: Performance assessment and multi-objective optimization of a novel vehicular power system integrating a direct borohydride fuel cell with an organic Rankine cycle
abstract: In this study, a novel vehicular direct borohydride fuel cell (DBFC) power system integrated with an organic Rankine cycle (ORC) is proposed. The ORC subsystem recovers the waste heat generated by the onboard DBFC stack to produce additional electrical power. Given the limited engineering maturity of vehicular DBFC systems and low-temperature ORCs, the proposed system is investigated through steady-state theoretical and numerical analyses. The principal contribution of this work is the development of a DBFC-ORC system-level framework for vehicle-oriented power assessment, incorporating comprehensive 4E evaluation and multi-objective trade-off analysis in terms of energy, exergy, economic, and environmental performance.Numerical results show that the integration of the ORC subsystem effectively enhances system performance. At operating temperatures of 70, 75, and 80 °C, the maximum net output power of the integrated system is increased by 9.0%, 8.5%, and 8.0%, respectively, compared with that of the standalone DBFC stack. Moreover, the parametric analysis reveals that the 4E performance indicators cannot be simultaneously optimized through parameter adjustment alone. Therefore, multi-objective optimization is performed to obtain the Pareto-optimal solution set and the corresponding optimal operating parameters. Compared with the baseline case(current density of 10500 A/m2, an operating temperature of 353.15 K, a NaBH4concentration of 1 mol/L, an inlet pressure of 2 atm, anode stoichiometric ratios of 1.2 and cathode stoichiometric ratios of 1.2), the selected Pareto-optimal solution yields an 18.22% increase in net output power, a 14.52% reduction in the levelized cost of energy, and a 97.27% increase in exergy efficiency. These results are instructive for the design and implementation of DBFC as a power source for automotive applications. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.
