title: Birdsong with gentle wind selectively benefits stimulus interference but not response or multisource interference: Evidence from EEG
abstract: Despite the growing threat of urban noise pollution to cognitive health, empirical evidence regarding the cognitive benefits of natural sounds remains mixed. The Specificity Hypothesis addresses this by proposing that such benefits are selective, benefiting only those cognitive functions that are highly matched with directed attention. Interference control is a cognitive function closely linked to directed attention and comprises three types: stimulus interference, response interference, and multisource interference. These types differ in their relationship with directed attention. However, whether natural sounds produce differential effects on distinct types of interference control remains unclear. The present study employed electroencephalography to examine the effects of natural sounds such as birdsong with gentle wind on distinct types of interference control. Thirty-nine participants performed the multi-source interference task while listening to either birdsong with gentle wind or an urban sound dominated by machine noise, with electroencephalography recorded simultaneously. Behavioral results showed no significant differences between the two sound stimuli across any type of interference control. Neurophysiological results revealed that birdsong with gentle wind significantly enhanced alpha oscillations, N200, and N450 amplitudes in the stimulus interference condition, whereas no significant changes in any neural measure were observed in the response interference or multisource interference conditions. Exploratory correlation analyses suggested that the enhancements of N200 and N450 were correlated with behavioral improvement in stimulus interference. These findings indicate that birdsong with gentle wind selectively supports the resolution of stimulus interference, while it does not significantly modulate response interference or multisource interference in the current experimental conditions. This finding suggests that future soundscape design should reconsider the general utility of this type of natural sound and pay more attention to the alignment between the cognitive demands of the task context and its benefits. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Using a UE5 Platform Based on Point Cloud to Develop the Digital Twin System of a Lianziya Scenic Spot in Xilingxia of the Yangtze River in China
abstract: Addressing the challenges of complex terrain modeling and poor real-time interactivity in geologically sensitive areas, this study presents a digital twin system construction method based on the Unreal Engine 5 (UE5) platform. Taking the Lianziya dangerous rock mass in the Three Gorges area as a case study, high-precision terrain data were acquired using an unmanned aerial vehicle equipped with light detection and ranging, fused with oblique photography imagery. A cascade filtering pipeline was implemented to optimize point cloud quality, and the quadric error metrics algorithm was applied for model simplification. The results show that the method reduced the mesh polygon count by 50% while maintaining level of detail 4 accuracy, with a mean geometric error (Hausdorff distance) of only 0.018 m. The resulting system enables dynamic weather simulation and adaptive path planning, maintaining a stable frame rate of over 60 FPS at 4K resolution, effectively resolving rendering stalls in large-scale scenes. This workflow provides a reproducible, high-fidelity technical solution for the digital preservation and intelligent management of geological hazard sites. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Cushioned but hollowed out: coal’s end and the demographic legacy of Spain’s mining communities
abstract: Between 2018 and 2020 Spain closed almost its entire coal sector, abruptly and in a handful of mining districts, under a just-transition agreement that retired displaced miners early. I ask what the closures did to the population of the mining municipalities and whether the cleaner air they left behind drew anyone in Comparing the municipalities that the government classified as most affected by the mine closures with non-mining municipalities on the same pre-closure population path, I find that the two move together until the closures and then diverge: the mining municipalities lose about three percent of their population by 2022. The loss is larger where coal mattered more and survives randomization inference. It did not arrive as unemployment, which fell relative to controls because early retirement converted dismissal into pension, and it was not offset by newcomers: in-migration to the areas whose air improved most does not respond, an improvement that was small in this low-pollution setting. The transition therefore delivered justice to workers without securing the territory. Read through the lens of territorial justice, income protection for the displaced is necessary but not sufficient for the sustainable development of extractive regions, and the social and cultural costs of a hollowing community, together with the lagged effects on services and on the young, lie beyond what the quantitative record yet shows. title: Capitalizing on positive experiences: Receiving affective empathy fosters a better mood and prosocial waiting
abstract: Interpersonal responses to emotional disclosures have potent effects on immediate affective states, yet their capacity to shape subsequent prosocial behavior remains unclear. Across two experiments, we investigated how the perceived empathy conveyed by facial responses influences both emotional outcomes and downstream altruistic choices. In Experiment 1, participants shared imagined positive or negative life events and received either an empathic, nonresponsive, or counter-empathic facial response from ostensible partners. We observed a context-dependent affective modulation: empathic responses maximally enhanced positive affect following positive disclosures, whereas counter-empathic responses most severely worsened mood following negative disclosures. In Experiment 2, we coupled this paradigm with an experiential intertemporal choice task in which participants chose between different waiting durations for rewards benefiting themselves or a charitable cause. Empathic responses to positive disclosures selectively increased charity-benefiting decisions, indicating a greater willingness to incur personal time costs for others. Computational modeling of choice data characterized this prosocial enhancement as being accompanied by a reduction in the weight placed on waiting time relative to reward, that is, a lower subjective cost of waiting. These findings demonstrate that receiving affective empathy, particularly in the context of positive experiences, promotes downstream prosociality by recalibrating the cost–benefit computations underlying altruistic choice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Polycentric risk governance across safety and security risk logics
abstract: The regulatory regime governing the Norwegian petroleum sector changed significantly in response to new geopolitical conditions following the war in Ukraine and the sabotage of the Nord Stream I and II pipelines. New legal security requirements and security risk logics were introduced into a sector whose traditional regulatory regime and risk logic had been intrinsically oriented toward safety. This shift altered the balance between safety and security considerations within the sector. This article explores the implications for regulatory regimes and risk logics when transitioning from safety-oriented to security-oriented regulatory models. Our ambition is primarily conceptual and theoretical, with the Norwegian petroleum industry serving as an illustrative case. The article analyses the emerging interface between safety and security, emphasizing the ontological, epistemological, and procedural divergences that complicate the integration of security concerns − focused on intentional, adversarial threats − into established safety regimes that manage unintentional harm. Anchored in a polycentric governance framework, the article examines how geopolitical developments have created tensions between rule-based and risk-based regulatory models, and the implications for organizational practices, regulatory oversight, and tripartite cooperation. It concludes by proposing a model of enforced self-regulation that reconciles safety and security logics, highlighting the need for adaptive, resilient, and knowledge-driven approaches to risk management in complex and evolving threat landscapes. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: The role of creativity and imagination in scientific endeavour
abstract: Creativity and imagination (C&I) are integral, but often overlooked, aspects of scientific endeavour. If scientists aim to innovate and develop new knowledge about the world around us, C&I are essential, yet how C&I are used in science is poorly understood. This lack of clarity about how C&I are defined, and how they are used, results in uninformed views about the nature of scientific endeavour. Here, we propose a conceptual Framework for an informed view of C&I to support the understanding of science through both research and teaching. We define our understanding of scientific endeavour, then define creativity in science through the generation of new thoughts, processes and products in intentional and unintentional ways which are effective in the context in which the creativity was applied. Imagination complements creativity and is defined as the ability to form mental images in the absence of the senses. During scientific endeavour, C&I work in conjunction with critical thinking and manifest as dispositions and actions when questioning, planning, doing and reflecting in science. Nineteen aspects of scientific endeavour are identified and the roles of C&I for each aspect are illustrated. The result is a characterisation of the role of C&I in scientific endeavour that makes creative and imaginative thoughts and actions explicit. This conceptualisation of an informed view provides a Framework for science educators who are tasked with researching, teaching and assessing, students’ understanding about the role of C&I in scientific endeavour. We close with implications for science education and research. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Disparity Considerations in an Alternative Eligibility Criterion for Medicare Medication Therapy Management Programs With Machine Learning
abstract: Objectives Current eligibility criteria for Medicare Medication Therapy Management (MTM) programs may disadvantage racial and ethnic minorities. As health plans increasingly apply predictive modeling to guide MTM eligibility, these tools risk perpetuating existing disparities. This study examined whether hospitalization and emergency room (ER) costs could serve as an alternative eligibility criterion to improve minority representation in MTM enrollment and whether machine learning models reflect racial and ethnic differences. Methods A 10% random sample of fee-for-service Medicare beneficiaries in 2019 was analyzed. The outcome was inclusion in the top quartile of hospitalization and ER costs. Racial and ethnic differences were assessed using a multivariable logistic regression. Five machine learning algorithms (regularized logistic regression, support vector machines, neural networks, random forest, and gradient boosting trees) were developed, with their predictions combined in a consensus model. A multivariable fractional logistic regression was used to test whether predicted probabilities reproduced observed racial and ethnic differences. Results The analytic sample included 1 848 654 beneficiaries. Black beneficiaries were significantly more likely than non-Hispanic White (White) beneficiaries to be in the top cost quartile (odds ratio [OR] = 1.09, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.07-1.12), whereas Asian (OR = 0.66, 95% CI = 0.63-0.69) and Other racial groups (OR = 0.87, 95% CI = 0.85-0.89) were less likely. No significant Hispanic-White difference was observed. Machine learning models largely reproduced these patterns. Conclusions Hospitalization and ER costs represent a potential alternative MTM eligibility criterion that may enhance inclusion of Black beneficiaries but underrepresent other minority groups. This study highlights the importance of equity-focused design in predictive tools. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Nitrogen-doped graphene composite with optimized pyridinic/pyrrolic configurations for high-performance NH4+ storage
abstract: Graphene has emerged as a crucial class of electrode materials for aqueous ammonium-ion batteries (AAIBs). However, pristine graphene suffers from severe restacking and lacks sufficient redox-active sites, fundamentally limiting its practical application. Herein, we employ a two-step temperature-controlled pyrolysis strategy using melamine as both a nitrogen source and a self-sacrificing template to synthesize a nitrogen-doped graphene/g-C3N4 composite (g–CN@G-700) that features both a high proportion of redox–active pyridinic and pyrrolic nitrogen configurations and an optimal graphitization degree, thereby resolving the trade-off among conductivity, specific surface area, and active nitrogen content. Consequently, the material demonstrates a high reversible NH4+ storage capacity of 202 mAh g−1 at 0.1 A g−1, favorable rate capability, and satisfactory long-term cycling stability with no significant capacity decay after 5,500 cycles at 4 A g−1. By using X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy, we reveal a highly reversible synergistic charge storage process involving the active nitrogen species and carbonyl groups with NH4+. Finally, combined with theoretical calculations, we propose a synergistic NH4+ storage mechanism where pyridinic-N and pyrrolic-N provides primary redox-active sites, and graphitic-N maintains structural integrity. This work provides a pathway to design and synthesize high-performance carbon-based materials for AAIBs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Polycaprolactone diol-mediated interfacial energy modulation for enhancing processability and thermal conductivity of highly filled epoxy/alumina composites
abstract: The application of highly filled ceramic–epoxy composites is often limited by the rapid increase in viscosity at high filler loadings. Here, polycaprolactone diol (PCLD) is shown to function as a combined viscosity and interfacial modifier in alumina-filled epoxy composite systems, enabling effective flow control under high solid loading. PCLD content (0–15 wt%) and molecular weight (Mn = 530 and 2000 g·mol−1) were varied to evaluate rheological behavior and thermal transport. At 30 vol% alumina, 15 wt% PCLD (Mn 530) reduced viscosity from 57.8 to 5.3 Pa·s at 10 s−1, nearly one order of magnitude compared with the composite without PCLD. Under the same condition, thermal conductivity increased by 36%, from 0.60 to 0.82 W·m−1·K−1. PCLD altered the surface free energy of the epoxy matrix and reduced the estimated epoxy–alumina interfacial energy, consistent with improved filler wetting and changes in filler organization. These results indicate that the combined effects of bulk viscosity reduction and interfacial-energy modification can improve processability and heat transport in highly filled epoxy composites. However, the accompanying decreases in glass-transition temperature and tensile strength represent important trade-offs for application at elevated temperatures or under higher mechanical requirements. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A systematic cost-effective assessment of multiple grassland restoration methods in China
abstract: Extensive grassland restoration programs were being expanded nationwide in response to the pervasive and severe degradation of grasslands in China. However, there was a significant dearth of quantitative cost-effective analyses pertaining to grassland ecosystems. The lack hindered the selection of the most cost-effective approaches to achieve restoration goals. After reviewing 214 studies, we comprehensively analyzed the precise restoration costs (distinguishing one-time inputs and ongoing inputs) and effectiveness of 17 diverse grassland restoration methods across China's three most prevalent grassland types. One-time inputs refer to non-recurring expenditures during implementation, including machinery, seeds, fertilizers, fencing, and labor, accounting for over 50% of total costs for most methods. Ongoing inputs are annual recurring costs for maintenance, encompassing ecological compensation for herders, maintenance staff salaries, and opportunity costs. Results showed that: (1) grassland restoration enhanced biodiversity and ecosystem multifunctionality but 17 recovery methods had significant differences in effectiveness; (2) China's grassland restoration methods tended to be costly while grazing management was a low-cost approach; and (3) grazing management could be a viable and cost-effective approach across the main grasslands in China. Our results provided valuable insights for policy-makers aiming to enhance the cost-effectiveness of grassland restoration projects in China, thereby addressing the financial barriers associated with scaling up restoration efforts at a national level. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Distributed neuromorphic computing with temporal co-optimization of spiking dynamics
abstract: Neuromorphic processors and event-based sensors enable always-on perception, yet training their computational building blocks, namely spiking neural networks (SNNs) across heterogeneous edge devices, is constrained by bandwidth, latency, and energy. This paper studies the systems problem of distributing continuous-time SNN training when computation and communication are driven by sparse spike events. Building on a previously developed exact event-driven single-device learner (ExactTrain) as a local training primitive, we develop distributed protocols, an AER communication abstraction, and the associated convergence, traffic, and system analyses. In particular, we formulate: (i) FedSNN, a federated protocol that matches centralized exact-gradient training under full participation and a one-full-local-gradient regime, (ii) SplitSNN, a split protocol that partitions a model across devices and exchanges address-event representation (AER) spike and error packets, and (iii) HybridSNN, a two-tier split/federated hierarchy that exposes an explicit accuracy-communication trade-off.Experiments on the N-MNIST and DVS Gesture benchmarks evaluate centralized equivalence, split and hybrid traffic, matched-configuration and byte-accounted baseline comparisons, scalability, sensitivity to non-IID data and partition location, and trace-driven network emulation with injected bandwidth limits, jitter, and packet loss. The results reveal that the proposed protocols preserve the timing benefits of exact event-driven local learning while replacing dense activation exchange with sparse spike/error traffic whose scaling is predictable from event rates and cut connectivity. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: A hierarchical scheduling strategy for achieving multi-source energy complementarity in self-powered systems
abstract: Ensuring long-term, stable operation of self-powered systems considering the stochastic and fluctuating nature of ambient energy remains a pivotal challenge, as existing multi-source harvesting architectures are confined to static, non-responsive paradigms. This work presents a self-powered wireless sensing system that transitions the field toward automatic, priority-driven management through a hardware-enforced, quadruple-buffered power scheduling strategy. The core of this strategy is a scheduling protocol that orchestrates energy flow in the following order: real-time photovoltaic (PV) energy, PV-stored energy, real-time thermoelectric-vibration hybrid energy, and auxiliary-stored energy. This is implemented via a dedicated circuit that enables automatic stored energy release and seamless source switching (<20 ms). A critical enabling feature is the electrical isolation between the primary and auxiliary power paths, which prevents mutual interference and resolves the impedance mismatch inherent in conventional static topologies. Experimentally, the system achieves 93 min of operation from a 10-min charge under controlled conditions, surpassing standalone PV-only and thermoelectric-only systems by 47.6% and 116.3%, respectively. Its practical viability is demonstrated by 75 min of stable field operation and consistent performance over a 10-day continuous test, with an overall system efficiency of 75%. This work provides a robust, maintenance-free power solution, demonstrating significant potential for sustainable wireless sensing in intelligent transportation and broader Industrial Internet of Things applications. © 2026 Author(s).

title: Res-PGDnet: A time frequency fusion model with physiologically constrained adversarial training for PPG-based valence–arousal state classification
abstract: Accurate valence–arousal assessment is crucial for affective computing applications. Photoplethysmography (PPG) is a promising, practical modality for this task, but it poses challenges: signals are noise-prone, the physiological affect mapping is complex and subject-specific, and models generalize poorly. Existing methods often focus narrowly on temporal features, employ physiologically unconstrained robustness strategies, or suffer from a severe performance–efficiency trade-off. We propose Res-PGDnet to address these issues via synergistic time frequency fusion and physiologically constrained adversarial training. Its core innovations are (i) applying adversarial perturbations constrained by physiological priors to model parameters to ensure robust, plausible learning and (ii) hierarchically integrating DCT attention modules to jointly enhance temporal and spectral feature representations. On the DEAP-PPG dataset, Res-PGDnet achieves 93.47% intra-subject accuracy and 92.46% Macro-F1 score, with strong robustness (metric: 0.920) and 85.1% cross-subject accuracy. The model is efficient (12.5 M parameters, 1250 FPS), demonstrating potential for wearable-based valence–arousal classification in settings like mental health monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Association of Dissociative Symptoms With Non-Suicidal Self-Injury and Repeated Suicide Attempts in Adolescents
abstract: Background: Self-harm and suicidal behaviors are major mental health concerns among adolescents. Dissociative symptoms have recently been recognized as clinically relevant factors linking emotional dysregulation to self-injurious behaviors. However, empirical evidence supporting this association remains limited in Korean adolescent clinical populations. This study examined whether dissociative symptom severity was associated with frequent nonsuicidal self-injury (NSSI) and suicide attempts among adolescents attending a psychiatric outpatient clinic. Methods: This retrospective chart review included 63 adolescents younger than 19 years who visited the Department of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry at Hallym University Sacred Heart Hospital between March 2020 and March 2023 and completed the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL), Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D), and Korean Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children-Fourth Edition. Dissociative symptoms were indexed using a summed score of six dissociation-related CBCL items and categorized as low (≤ 5 points) or high (≥ 6 points). NSSI frequency was classified as 0-5 versus ≥ 6 episodes, and suicide attempts as 0-1 versus ≥ 2 episodes. Sex, age, IQ, and depressive symptoms measured by the CES-D were included as covariates. Group differences were analyzed using independent samples t-tests and associations with high-frequency NSSI and repeated suicide attempts were examined using logistic regression. Results: Among the 63 participants, 26 were male (41.3%) and 37 were female (58.7%); the mean age was 15.4 years and the mean IQ was 88.0. Adolescents with high-frequency NSSI (≥ 6 episodes) had significantly higher CES-D and dissociation scores than those with 0-5 NSSI episodes (P = 0.008 and P = 0.003, respectively). In logistic regression, adolescents in the high-dissociation group had higher odds of high-frequency NSSI than those in the low-dissociation group (odds ratio [OR], 5.02; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.34-18.81; P = 0.017). Similarly, adolescents with repeated suicide attempts (≥ 2 episodes) had higher CES-D and dissociation scores than those with 0-1 attempts (P = 0.006 and P = 0.039, respectively), and high dissociation was associated with higher odds of repeated suicidal attempts (OR, 5.33; 95% CI, 1.54-18.47; P = 0.008). Age, IQ, and sex were not significantly associated with either outcome. Conclusion: Dissociative symptoms were independently associated with both high-frequency NSSI and repeated suicide attempts among Korean adolescents receiving psychiatric outpatient care. Adolescents with elevated dissociation showed approximately five-fold higher odds of high-frequency NSSI and repeated suicide attempts, even after adjustment for depressive symptoms and demographic factors. These findings suggest that dissociation may be a clinically meaningful marker of elevated self-harm and suicide-related risk, supporting the routine assessment of dissociative experiences in adolescent mental health evaluations. © (2027), (Korean Academy of Medical Science). . title: Instance-Prototype Affinity Learning for Non-Exemplar Continual Graph Learning
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNN) endure catastrophic forgetting, undermining their capacity to preserve previously acquired knowledge amid the assimilation of novel information. Rehearsal-based techniques revisit historical examples, adopted as a principal strategy to alleviate this phenomenon. However, memory explosion and privacy infringements impose significant constraints on their utility. Non-Exemplar methods circumvent the prior issues through Prototype Replay (PR), yet feature drift presents new challenges. In this paper, our empirical findings reveal that Prototype Contrastive Learning (PCL) exhibits less pronounced drift than conventional PR. Drawing upon PCL, we propose Instance-Prototype Affinity Learning (IPAL), a novel paradigm for Non-Exemplar Continual Graph Learning (NECGL). Exploiting graph structural information, we formulate Topology-Integrated Gaussian Prototypes (TIGP), guiding feature distributions toward high-impact nodes to augment the model's capacity for assimilating new knowledge. Instance-Prototype Affinity Distillation (IPAD) safeguards task memory by regularizing discontinuities in class relationships. Moreover, we embed a Decision Boundary Perception (DBP) mechanism within PCL, fostering greater inter-class discriminability. Evaluations on four node classification benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, achieving a better trade-off between plasticity and stability. Code is available at https://github.com/SONGLEI-arch/IPAL. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: AWCRL: Adaptive Weakly Supervised Cross-Modal Reliability Learning for resource-constrained proxy-state recognition
abstract: Multimodal pattern recognition can support the characterization of affective and behavioral states by integrating complementary visual and physiological evidence, but real-world deployment is challenged by unreliable modalities, limited annotations, and constrained computation. We propose Adaptive Weakly Supervised Cross-Modal Reliability Learning (AWCRL), a resource-aware framework for recognizing ontology-derived affective proxy states under incomplete or unreliable multimodal evidence. AWCRL estimates modality reliability from unimodal predictions and a lightweight pre-routing pooled consensus, then uses a budget-conditioned router to retain informative tokens before low-rank cross-modal fusion. An explicit weak ontology maps affective and engagement-related cues to four ordinal proxy states — stable, disengaged, cognitive overload, and acute stress — while confidence- and affinity-weighted prototype refinement reduces the influence of uncertain weak labels. Under subject-independent five-fold evaluation on K-EmoCon and AMIGOS, AWCRL achieves 78.6% and 76.2% macro-F1 with mean computation of 0.78 and 0.82 GFLOPs per segment, respectively. Compared with full-token inference at 1.95 GFLOPs, the budgeted setting reduces computation by 60.0% and 57.9%, with macro-F1 decreasing by only 0.8 and 0.7 percentage points. On K-EmoCon, AWCRL also achieves the highest descriptive macro-F1 among the compared methods under complete, missing-modality, and single-modality corruption conditions. These results indicate a favorable recognition–efficiency trade-off under weak supervision and variable multimodal evidence. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Adaptive time-period discretization for multi-period scheduling of gaseous energy systems in steel enterprises
abstract: Multi-period scheduling of gaseous energy systems in steel enterprises commonly relies on Equal Time-Period Discretization (ETPD), which involves an inherent trade-off between discretization accuracy and computational efficiency. Coarse discretization may accumulate storage deviations and cause safety violations, whereas fine discretization significantly increases the computational burden. To address this issue, this study proposes Adaptive Time-Period Discretization (ATPD), a time-representation and inventory-safety enhancement framework that adaptively partitions continuous-time supply–demand parameters based on cumulative storage deviation. Specifically, ATPD decouples the adaptive parameter grid from the uniform decision-variable grid and incorporates the deviation bound as a compensation margin in the storage safety constraints, thereby directly linking discretization accuracy to physical safety. The proposed method is validated through a case study on oxygen and byproduct gas scheduling using real-world data from a steel enterprise. Compared with ETPD, ATPD achieves more accurate parameter fitting, eliminates storage safety violations via deviation-bound compensation, and improves computational efficiency by over tenfold while maintaining a comparable model size. The results demonstrate that ATPD effectively balances discretization accuracy, storage safety, and computational efficiency in gaseous energy scheduling. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Gravity-inspired key node identification in complex networks using entropy-weighted shortest path analysis
abstract: Identifying influential nodes is an important issue in analyzing complex networks. This paper proposes Gravity-Inspired Entropy-Weighted Shortest Path Analysis (GEWSP), a multidimensional strategy for identifying influential nodes in complex networks. GEWSP can consider node interactions as gravitational forces based on the law of gravity, providing a more faithful representation of structural influence. A network weighting strategy is introduced to account for path diversity and structural heterogeneity. Meanwhile, GEWSP integrates multiple weighted shortest-path features to characterize node importance from different structural perspectives. Information entropy is then employed to adaptively determine the weight of each dimension, enabling a more balanced integration of different structural influences. In addition, GEWSP adopts a semi-local perspective by jointly considering the intrinsic properties of each node and the characteristics of its nearby neighborhoods within a predefined range. This configuration enables the model to exploit information from different structural scales without imposing substantial computational overhead. The proposed framework is evaluated on several networks by the Susceptible–Infected–Recovered (SIR) spreading model. Experimental results show that GEWSP consistently outperforms existing methods in epidemic spreading simulations. It achieves higher identification accuracy and stronger discrimination among influential nodes, demonstrating its effectiveness for key node identification in complex networks. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Ensemble of deep architectures for SWARM AI-based decision-making
abstract: This work studies how an artificial agent can participate in swarm-based decision-making alongside human experts by learning collective decision dynamics. We formulate this problem as a multimodal sequential prediction task that combines two complementary sources of information: (i) spatiotemporal interaction traces generated by experts through the HANS web platform and (ii) the corresponding image. We propose a hybrid architecture with an LSTM branch for interaction sequences and a WideResNet branch for image encoding, followed by feature fusion and joint optimisation. The model predicts the evolution of the collective decision at each time step, thereby acting as an autonomous swarm AI agent that receives the same evidence as a human participant. We evaluate the approach on four use cases from environmental microscopy and biomedical imaging: diatoms, cyanobacteria, HER2 and Ki67. The analysis considers interaction-level prediction error, measured by RMSE, and decision-level metrics, including precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score and balanced accuracy under Top-k settings. Across the datasets, the model achieves low interaction error and strong balanced accuracy, while the temporal analysis shows that it captures meaningful convergence patterns in expert consensus. These results support the feasibility of hybrid multimodal models for embedding artificial agents in collaborative decision environments. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: ASD-FCGCN: A biologically interpretable graph convolutional network for ASD diagnosis from rs-fMRI
abstract: Background and Objectives: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition traditionally diagnosed through subjective behavioral assessments. Resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) provides a potential pathway for objective neuroimaging biomarker discovery; however, existing deep learning methods often struggle to integrate neurobiological priors with data-driven representations. This study aimed to address these limitations by developing a biologically interpretable graph-learning framework for rs-fMRI-based ASD classification. Methods: We propose ASD-FCGCN, a biologically informed graph convolutional network validated on 871 subjects from the ABIDE dataset. The method systematically integrates neurobiological priors with graph learning. Specifically, prior-weighted functional connectivity matrices are constructed to generate hemisphere-specific representations. A Pairwise Association Encoder (PAE) is employed to estimate inter-subject phenotypic relationships, transforming similarity weights into channel-wise gating signals to dynamically regulate graph convolution. Furthermore, a corpus callosum-inspired interaction mechanism is introduced to enable bidirectional information exchange between hemispheres, thereby synthesizing whole-brain features for classification. Results: Experimental results demonstrated that ASD-FCGCN achieved strong classification performance under subject-level 10-fold cross-validation, with an accuracy of 94.60% ± 3.04%, an AUC of 97.66% ± 1.82%, a sensitivity of 94.66% ± 3.72%, a specificity of 94.52% ± 4.16%, and an F1-score of 94.96% ± 2.81%. Conclusion: The results indicate that integrating neurobiological priors, phenotype-guided convolution, and cross-hemispheric coordination can improve subject-level rs-fMRI-based ASD classification. The proposed model provides a promising computational framework for ASD auxiliary diagnosis and offers biologically informed model-level interpretability by integrating ASD-related prior ROIs, phenotype-guided graph propagation, and hemisphere-specific interaction modeling. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Dynamic temporal modeling and distribution-calibrated fusion for multimodal sentiment analysis
abstract: Existing multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) methods still lack dynamic modeling of unstable emotional information. Emotional expressions in audio and visual modalities often exhibit different temporal rhythms, while most existing recurrent state update mechanisms propagate hidden states at fixed temporal progression scales. In addition, some cross-modal associations merely reflect statistical co-occurrence patterns, and such incidental correlations do not always correspond to genuine emotional dependencies. Moreover, the reliability and contribution of each modality may dynamically vary across real-world scenarios. To address these issues, this paper proposes a multimodal sentiment analysis framework based on dynamic temporal modeling and distribution-calibrated fusion. Specifically, adaptive temporal modeling is performed on audio and visual sequences through dynamic temporal granularity selection, enabling the model to capture both short-term emotional fluctuations and long-range emotional dependencies while estimating temporal confidence. Furthermore, Gaussian distribution modeling and perturbation consistency constraints are introduced to characterize uncertainty in modality representations, thereby preventing over-reliance on unreliable associations during fusion. Temporal confidence and distributional uncertainty are further combined into a unified modality confidence, which dynamically regulates cross-modal fusion and representation alignment to improve semantic consistency of fused representations. Experimental results on the CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, and CH-SIMS datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Integrated simulation of forest dynamics and bioenergy utilization for GHG mitigation: A case study of Hyogo prefecture, Japan
abstract: This study developed a dynamic simulation framework integrating forest growth, forest management, biomass supply, and energy utilization to jointly assess the supply potential and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions of woody biomass energy, using Hyogo Prefecture, Japan, as a case study. Under conventional carbon-neutral accounting, GHG emissions from forest harvesting and forest residue utilization were 0.168 and 0.094 kg-CO2eq/kWh, respectively. When biogenic CO2 from combustion was included without subsequent forest uptake, these values increased to 2.660 and 2.586 kg-CO2eq/kWh. At the forest-system level, both woody biomass supply and the GHG balance were strongly influenced by forest age structure and harvesting regime. Under the baseline S3-a scenario, annual woody biomass harvest declined from approximately 84,000 BDT/yr in 2020 to 14,000 BDT/yr by 2050 and remained relatively stable thereafter, while cumulative net GHG emissions reached −60.492 million t-CO2eq by 2100. Increasing final felling enhanced woody biomass supply but weakened the long-term GHG balance. Among the scenarios examined, 10 km2/yr represented the highest final-felling level and approached the long-term forest-stock constraint, whereas 5 km2/yr maintained a substantially more favorable cumulative GHG balance than 10 km2/yr. These results demonstrate that maintaining forest growing stock and achieving a favorable GHG balance represent distinct management criteria, highlighting the importance of dynamically considering forest age structure, harvesting, regeneration, and subsequent growth when evaluating woody biomass energy utilization. © 2026 The Authors. title: Development of mental imagery strategy in a recall task as a function of word imageability and grade level in elementary school children
abstract: Objective: This study investigated the development of mental imagery strategy in episodic memory as a function of word imageability and grade level in elementary school children. Method: A total of 62 first-grade children, 61 third-grade children, and 60 fifth-grade children performed a free recall task involving high- and low-imageability words. A test of word memory was conducted using either a mental imagery strategy or a rehearsal strategy. Results: The results showed that the benefit of the mental imagery strategy over the rehearsal condition was lower for first-graders than for third- or fifth-graders. Furthermore, word imageability influenced word recall to a greater extent in the mental imagery condition than in the rehearsal condition. Finally, the effect of word imageability did not interact with the children's age. Conclusion: The findings are discussed in light of theories on the development of mental imagery and the cognitive processes underlying episodic memory. © 2026 The Authors

title: How could redistribution be possible? Effects of national identity and communion among Chinese youth
abstract: Previous studies in Western countries demonstrated that the relationship between national identity and redistribution preferences was inconsistent, and few studies addressed the cross-cultural consistency about this relationship. Based on social identity theory, the present study aimed to explore the relationship between national identity and redistribution preferences and its mechanisms as well as boundaries through three sub-studies in Chinese youth. A cross-sectional study among 1791 young adults, a priming experiment among 182 college students, and integration of experimental manipulation and daily diary study among 51 college students were conducted respectively in study 1–3. We found that national identity of Chinese youth had positive effect on redistribution preferences and communion mediated this effect at the static and dynamic levels (study 1–3). Dark Triad strengthened the direct relationship between national identity and redistribution preferences (study 1), whereas weakened its indirect relationship (study 1 and 3). These findings indicated the positive effect of national identity on redistribution preferences and the mediating role of communion in this effect, and the well-adapted function of Dark Triad to some extent. These findings provided theoretical basis for the initiative for common prosperity from the perspectives of identity and personality in Chinese context. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Deterministic modeling of infection dynamics under Far-UVC irradiation: a cumulative-exposure framework and its mathematical relation to infectious quanta
abstract: Far-UVC irradiation (200–235 nm) is a promising photonic intervention for suppressing the environmental transmission of airborne pathogens in occupied spaces. However, establishing a robust physical and mathematical framework to quantify these dynamic pathogen-host interactions remains challenging, as direct verification using mammalian models is experimentally demanding and cost-prohibitive. Here, we present a controlled in vivo biophysical model system—utilizing zebrafish and Yersinia ruckeri —to quantitatively examine the macroscopic survival dynamics of a host population under varying environmental pathogen loads. We observed a distinct, threshold-like transition in macroscopic host survival near a critical pathogen density (106 CFU/mL for a 0.25-day exposure duration), above which infection-induced mortality sharply increased. Far-UVC irradiation reduced the viable pathogen density as a function of UV dose, systematically driving the system below this critical threshold and demonstrating effective physical pathogen attenuation. To elucidate the underlying dynamics, we introduced a deterministic, multistep Susceptible-Infectious-Removed (SIR) model governed by a system of coupled differential equations. The theoretical model revealed that the final macroscopic state of the system is governed by a cumulative exposure parameter, Λ=β0ρτ, where β0 is the infectivity coefficient, ρ is the bacterial density, and τ is the exposure duration, rather than by instantaneous bacterial density alone. Crucially, the cumulative exposure parameter Λ derived from this aquatic infection model shares the same exponential cumulative form with the infectious quanta in the Wells-Riley model for predicting airborne transmission. Therefore, this in vivo platform validates a quantitative physical framework specifically for evaluating ultraviolet (UV) disinfection dynamics. These findings provide a theoretical basis for designing precise photonic irradiation algorithms that maintain cumulative environmental exposure below critical pathogenic thresholds. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Acceptability-driven adaptive migration promotes cooperation in human–machine hybrid population
abstract: Sustaining cooperation in social systems is persistently challenged by the destabilizing influence of selfish behavior. In human–machine hybrid networks, interactions between artificial agents and human participants introduce both new obstacles and new opportunities for maintaining sustained cooperation. Social interactions are strongly influenced by individuals’ affective assessments of peer strategies. Here, “acceptability”—the degree to which an individual's strategy is supported by neighbors—drives emotion-based migration toward more favorable positions. By contrast, cooperative robots are unaffected by such emotional evaluations and instead base their migration decisions on either success-driven movement or random exploration. Inspired by this notion, the Acceptability-Driven Adaptive Migration (ADAM) model is proposed. Monte Carlo (MC) simulations demonstrate that the proposed ADAM model effectively fosters the emergence of cooperative strategies. In populations where ordinary nodes migrate according to acceptability, increasing the proportion of cooperative robots markedly enhances cooperation, while node density exerts minimal influence except at extremely high or low levels. When a greater share of robots follow the success-driven rule rather than random exploration, cooperation is further reinforced. Network-level average acceptability improves when robots constitute either a minority or a majority of the population. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: JCF-NMF: Automatic hierarchical multi-view clustering via Joint Convex-Fused Non-negative Matrix Factorization
abstract: Multi-view clustering has attracted considerable attention due to its ability to integrate information from multiple sources to uncover the intrinsic structure of data. Among various techniques, Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) has been widely employed in multi-view clustering due to its strong interpretability and effectiveness. However, most existing approaches adopt a two-stage paradigm — first learning a common representation and then performing clustering — which focuses mainly on representation-level alignment but fails to fully exploit the consistent cluster structures shared across views. Moreover, decoupling representation learning from clustering often leads to suboptimal performance, and the requirement of predefining the number of clusters further limits their flexibility. To address these issues, inspired by the idea of convex clustering, we propose JCF-NMF, a novel one-step, joint convex-fused NMF framework for automatic hierarchical multi-view clustering. The key innovation of our work is a joint convex fusion penalty applied to the representation matrices of all views. Specifically, an l2-norm regularization is imposed on inter-sample representation differences, which guides them to converge toward a shared cluster structure. This design enables a joint optimization of representation learning and clustering, allowing dynamically updated representations to iteratively refine clustering assignments. As the fusion penalty strength increases, representations from different views gradually merge, forming a multi-granularity hierarchical clustering structure that progresses from fine to coarse levels. This mechanism contributes to the interpretability of the model. Extensive experiments on five real-world datasets demonstrate that JCF-NMF consistently and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art multi-view clustering methods. © 2026

title: Taylor-sparsified differentially private federated learning with support-consensus robust aggregation
abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative training without sharing raw data, but sparse private updates may still leak information through both support masks and noisy values, while remaining vulnerable to Byzantine attacks. We propose TDP-SRA, a Taylor-sparsified differentially private federated learning framework with support-consensus robust aggregation. Clients select supports using a privatized Taylor utility criterion and release clipped sparse values with Gaussian perturbation, providing client-level privacy accounting for the complete sparse release. The server maintains a temporally smoothed support frequency vector, estimates a consensus support, scores uploads by support agreement and privacy noise normalized residuals, and aggregates server clipped sparse updates via a weighted geometric median in the consensus subspace. We establish client-level Rényi differential privacy and provide sufficient or conditional analyses for support recovery and robust aggregation under explicit support stability, support separation, and effective Byzantine weight assumptions. Experiments on multiple vision datasets under standard, data poisoning, and adaptive support-aware attacks show that TDP-SRA achieves a favorable empirical trade-off among accuracy, privacy, robustness, and uplink communication efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Spectral graph filter bank fusion for multimodal rumor cascade representation and detection
abstract: Rumor detection on social media is inherently a multi-source information fusion problem that involves heterogeneous signals from textual content, user interactions, and temporal dynamics. Existing approaches often underexploit the global structural patterns encoded in rumor propagation graphs. In this work, we propose a unified multimodal fusion framework, termed Rumor Graph Filter Net (RGFN), which integrates multimodal representations with learnable spectral graph filtering. Specifically, post content embeddings derived from a pre-trained language encoder, user social relation representations obtained via self-supervised contrastive learning, and propagation timestamps are jointly transformed into the graph spectral domain using the Graph Fourier Transform (GFT). To adaptively capture discriminative propagation characteristics, we design channel-wise graph filter banks based on Chebyshev polynomial approximations, enabling frequency-selective enhancement and noise suppression. The filtered spectral responses are projected back to the spatial domain through the inverse GFT, followed by a simplified hierarchical multi-view graph pooling mechanism to obtain robust graph-level representations across scales. The final classifier operates on fused multilevel features for rumor identification. Experiments on two real-world rumor datasets, Twitter and Weibo, show that RGFN achieves the highest F1-score among the baselines and performs competitively on other metrics. Specifically, RGFN outperforms the best baselines on Twitter and Weibo by 4.9% and 1.4% on F1-score, respectively. The proposed framework offers a principled integration of graph signal processing and multimodal information fusion for social media credibility assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: How punishment sensitivity affects delay discounting: The mediating role of functional connectivity between the left dorsal medial prefrontal cortex and right postcentral gyrus
abstract: Punishment sensitivity refers to an individual's tendency to perceive and respond to punishment and other negative outcomes. Delay discounting refers to that an individual tends to devalue the subjective worth of future rewards as the waiting time increases. Previous findings suggest that punishment sensitivity may be related to delay discounting, but direct evidence for this association and the neural mechanisms underlying this relationship remain unclear. To address this question, we combined behavioral measurements, voxel-based morphometry (VBM), resting-state fMRI, and mediation analysis to investigate their brain-behavior mechanisms. Behaviorally, punishment sensitivity negatively correlated with delay discounting. Furthermore, VBM analysis found that the gray matter volume (GMV) of the left dorsal medial prefrontal cortex (dmPFC_L) is positively associated with punishment sensitivity, and neuroimaging results revealed that the functional connectivity between the dmPFC_L and the right postcentral gyrus (PCG_R) was positively associated with punishment sensitivity. More critically, mediation analysis showed that this functional connectivity exhibited a partial mediation with a statistical suppressor effect in the association with delay discounting. These results suggest that the functional connectivity between the dmPFC_L and PCG_R may represent a neural correlate of this association, providing new insights and a neurobiological interpretation for this association. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Peripheral Neuropathy Screening in Patients With Thalassemia: A Hybrid Decision-Markov Model
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of a systematic screening program for thalassemia-related peripheral neuropathy (ThalPN) compared with standard care in Malaysia. Methods A hybrid decision-Markov model was developed to simulate the lifetime health outcomes and costs for a hypothetical cohort of adult thalassemia patients (both transfusion-dependent and non-transfusion-dependent). The analysis was conducted from a healthcare provider perspective, utilizing the neuropathy symptomatic score and neuropathy disability score as screening tools. The model was populated with data from the Malaysian Thalassemia Registry, a clinical cohort study for prevalence and utility values, and published literature. Costs and health outcomes were discounted at 3% annually. Results The screening strategy for ThalPN was found to be highly cost-effective across all age cohorts compared with standard care. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was most favorable in the ≥40 age group at USD 2027 per quality-adjusted life-year gained. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratios for the 18 to 29 and 30 to 39 age groups were USD 2951 and USD 3209 per quality-adjusted life-year gained, respectively. Conclusions Incorporating a ThalPN screening program into standard care is a cost-effective strategy. By facilitating early intervention, screening can prevent or slow irreversible disease progression, thereby improving health-related quality of life and potentially reducing long-term costs for this patient population. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Enhancing graph link prediction with sequential latent variable diffusion models
abstract: Predicting interactions between nodes, known as link prediction, is a fundamental task in graph machine learning. This task is critical due to its widespread application in domains such as recommendation engines, social network analysis, drug discovery, and sequential data analysis. Deep generative approaches, such as Graph Auto-Encoders (GAEs) and Variational Graph Auto-Encoders (VGAEs), along with their derivatives, have set benchmarks by addressing challenges related to edge partitioning during training, the complexity of prediction functions for node pairs, and the proficiency in reconstructing data through latent spaces. Despite the prominence of these models in link prediction, in this work, we reveal their limitations through analytically investigations. Specifically, their reliance on a single set of latent variables often fails to capture the full spectrum of complex interactions and potential links between nodes. Moreover, we mathematically demonstrate that integrating multiple latent variables can substantially enhance a model's expressive capacity. To address this, we propose a methodology that enriches model expressiveness by leveraging a sequence of latent variables to perform multi-step latent refinement. Our approach involves constructing a parameterized forward process and a reverse reconstruction model to optimize the probability of accurately reconstructing the adjacency matrix, which follows a diffusion-inspired multi-step refinement scheme. Evaluations on diverse datasets, both homophilic and heterophilic, supported by detailed visualization analyses, confirm that our approach significantly improves the detection of potential links and the handling of complex node features within graph structures. The source code of our model is available at https://github.com/zxj8806/LPDiffusion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Grinding Charcoal for Rock Painting: A Methodological Framework for Particle-Size Analysis in Rock Art Micro-Samples
abstract: Research on the materiality of rock art has shifted attention from images as finished products to the technical and social processes involved in their making. Within this framework, pigment grinding is a crucial but still methodologically elusive aspect of painting production, despite its potential to inform technological choices, labor investment, and variability in painting practices. In this paper, we propose an experimental and archaeometric approach to the study of charcoal grinding in rock art micro-samples. By combining experimental archaeology, optical microscopy, and particle analysis, we develop a model linking charcoal particle area to grinding time. We apply this method to study black rock paintings from the Oyola archaeological site, in northwestern Argentina, where charcoal was identified as the main black pigment. The results show that microscopically measurable differences in particle areas make it possible to distinguish varying degrees of grinding among paintings that are macroscopically and chemically similar. Beyond the local case study, our findings demonstrate that pigment granulometry can provide access to otherwise invisible dimensions of rock art production, complementing the existing knowledge of technical variability, painting events, and the historical processes through which painted surfaces were made and transformed. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: MLLM-based dual-stream synergistic model for multimodal aspect-based sentiment analysis
abstract: Multimodal aspect-based sentiment analysis (MABSA) aims to determine the sentiment polarity associated with specific aspects in image–text content. While various approaches have been proposed to integrate multimodal information, most existing methods face two key challenges: (i) cross-modal interaction modeling may hinder the learning of syntactic structures; and (ii) external knowledge is often underutilized to enrich aspect context. To address these issues, we propose an MLLM-based dual-stream synergistic model (LLM-DSS). Specifically, to balance cross-modal interaction and syntactic structure learning, we adopt a parallel dual-stream architecture. We construct a knowledge-enhanced multimodal stream and a syntax-enhanced text stream and we use a synergistic alignment mechanism to promote cooperative modeling across streams. This design structurally decouples syntactic learning from cross-modal interaction, and we further design a Multi-View Syntactic Fusion (MSF) module to strengthen syntactic modeling. To supplement aspect context, we use an MLLM to generate aspect-related external knowledge and introduce a Context-aware Knowledge Filter (CKF) module to remove redundant knowledge. Experiments on two public MABSA datasets show that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Integrative genetic analyses of circadian chronotype and autism highlight regional co-association at 17q21.31
abstract: Chronotype and sleep problems are common in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but their genetic relationship remains uncertain. We integrated published cross-trait LD score regression (LDSC), brain eQTL-based summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), SNP-based two-sample MR, two-step mediation MR, secondary parallel SMR, and Bayesian colocalization using UK Biobank chronotype GWASs, the iPSYCH/Psychiatric Genomics Consortium ASD GWAS, and GTEx v8 brain eQTLs. The published LDSC estimate was negative for morningness-coded chronotype and ASD (rG = −0.199). Primary ASD-outcome SMR identified 50 gene-tissue pairs representing 24 genes at the exploratory multi-SNP PSMR < 0.001 threshold; none met Bonferroni significance. Fifteen candidates occurred in the LD-rich 17q21.31 inversion and are not independent gene discoveries. Secondary eveningness-outcome SMR tested all 24 candidates in matched tissues; 22 had PSMR < 0.05, but GTEx reuse made this descriptive. At 17q21.31, the prespecified p12 = 1 × 10⁻⁵ favored distinct variants (PP.H3 = 0.785) over one shared variant (PP.H4 = 0.126). H3 dominance strengthened at p12 = 1 × 10⁻⁶ and reversed only at the permissive p12 = 1 × 10⁻⁴, equal to p1 and p2. Eveningness-oriented IVW MR was positive (β = 0.270, P = 0.008), whereas robust estimators were attenuated; no mediation was detected through sleep duration or insomnia complaints. These analyses prioritize exploratory regional associations without proving shared causality or mechanism. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Locus of morphological processing during visual L2 compound recognition: An ERP investigation
abstract: The extent to which second language (L2) speakers process morphologically complex words through morphem-based processes remains debated, with conflicting evidence from behavioral studies suggesting that L2 learners may rely primarily on orthographic overlap rather than morphological structure. The present study employed morpho-semantic priming paradigm and event-related potentials (ERPs) to investigate whether and how Chinese-English bilinguals engage in morphological decomposition and morpho-semantic integration during real-time English compound word recognition. We manipulated two factors: Relatedness (primes semantically related vs. unrelated to the first constituent morpheme of the compound word) and Semantic Transparency (transparent vs. opaque compound words). In the N400 time window, a significant main effect of Relatedness emerged, with both transparent and opaque compound words showing comparable N400 attenuation, indicating early semantically blind morphological decomposition. In the late negativity window (800–1200 ms), a significant main effect of Semantic Transparency emerged, with opaque compounds eliciting greater negativity than transparent compounds, reflecting the late morpho-semantic integration process. These findings demonstrate a biphasic pattern of L2 morphological processing encompassing early obligatory morphological decomposition followed by late morpho-semantic integration. Overall, our findings suggest that Chinese-English bilinguals can engage in native-like morphological processing during recognition of English compound words. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Who fights best? Discovering winning personality pairings for LLM debate agents
abstract: Multi-agent debate (MAD) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). However, most MAD systems employ personality-neutral agents and overlook the role of personality, which has been shown in psychology and behavioral science to influence reasoning styles and collaborative problem-solving. In this study, we introduce MBTI-DB, a debate framework for systematically studying the impact of personality in MAD. We design 16 distinct personality profiles and inject them into debates in a modular manner. Through experiments across four LLM families and 700 factual questions, we demonstrate that incorporating personality induces systematic and measurable accuracy shifts. Further analysis reveals that lexical density, personality-question similarity, and prompt perplexity influence these accuracy variations. We evaluate personality-pair selection strategies and find that retrospectively selecting the best-performing pair for each question yields significant gains as an oracle upper bound. However, automatically identifying the best configuration remains challenging with substantial cross-model variation, suggesting that while personality diversity offers meaningful performance benefits, its effects are complex and context-dependent. Our code and datasets can be found at https://github.com/KJOrigin/WhoFightsBest. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Broken bodies in Domestic Spaces: Direct and Structural Violence in an Atypical Mortuary Dataset from Iron and Viking Age Scandinavia
abstract: A major challenge for the understanding of violence in the past is that our main source of evidence comes from cemeteries, but a significant proportion of the victims of violence are not buried in cemeteries. Iron and Viking Age Scandinavia (c. 500 BCE–1050 CE) is infamous for its emerging warrior ideology and hegemony of violence. Yet, somewhat counter-intuitively, trauma rates have typically been found to be relatively low in cemetery populations. Not everyone was afforded formal burial in cemeteries, however. The BODY-POLITICS project examines a previously neglected mortuary dataset: disarticulated and semi-complete human remains deposited in and around domestic spaces such as longhouses, pits, wells, postholes, and hearths. We report on 12 individuals inscribed with 19 ante- and perimortem traumatic injuries, analysed through osteological, bimolecular and digital imaging methods. The unusual post-mortem history of these individuals, set within a historical context of raiding, enslavement, and ritual violence including potential ‘human sacrifice’, allows us to explore multiple scenarios for inflicted injuries: war-like events (extra-community violence), interpersonal and domestic violence (intra-community violence), and ritual violence. Finally, by integrating trauma patterns, mortuary treatment, and contextual information, we discuss the broader life histories of these individuals and argue that some may have been vulnerable to structural, ‘slow’ violence that compounded over the lifecourse. This study thus contributes to broader discourse on direct and structural violence towards potentially marginalised people, as well as connections between ritualised violence and divergent mortuary pathways. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Extracts of Coriaria nepalensis ameliorate MK-801-induced schizophrenia-like behaviors via regulation of neurotransmitter imbalance and neuroinflammation
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Coriaria nepalensis Wall. is a traditional ethnomedicine used by the Dong ethnic group in Guizhou Province, China, for the treatment of schizophrenia. However, its pharmacological effects and the bioactive constituents responsible for its therapeutic efficacy remain largely unknown. Aim of the study: To evaluate the anti-schizophrenic effects of C. nepalensis extracts and investigate their underlying mechanisms and potential bioactive constituents. Materials and methods: An MK-801-induced schizophrenia-like Sprague–Dawley rat model was established to evaluate the therapeutic effects in the blank control group, model group, positive drug group, and different dose groups of C. nepalensis extracts (EA-H, EA-M, EA-L, SJ-H, SJ-M, and SJ-L). Schizophrenia-like behaviors were assessed using the open-field, Y-maze, three-chamber social interaction, and prepulse inhibition (PPI) tests. Neurotransmitter levels in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex were determined by LC-MS, inflammatory cytokines were quantified by ELISA, and the expression of signaling pathway-related proteins and glutamate decarboxylase 67 (GAD67) was analyzed by Western blotting. Plasma-absorbed constituents of the active extract were characterized using HPLC-MS/MS. Results: C. nepalensis extracts alleviated MK-801-induced schizophrenia-like behavioral abnormalities to different extents, including altered locomotor activity, impaired spatial working memory, and social deficits. Among all treatments, the low-dose ethanol extract (EA-L) produced the most pronounced effects. EA-L significantly improved sensorimotor gating deficits in the PPI test and showed a stronger ameliorative than risperidone under the present experimental conditions. Mechanistically, EA-L restored neurotransmitter homeostasis in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, attenuated neuroinflammatory responses, regulated the abnormal activation of inflammation-related signaling pathways, and normalized GAD67 expression. These changes were associated with improvements in schizophrenia-like negative symptoms, cognitive deficits, and sensorimotor gating impairment. Chemical profiling identified 251 constituents in the ethanol extract, of which 57 were detected in rat serum after oral administration, suggesting that these absorbed compounds may contribute to the observed pharmacological activity. Conclusion: Extracts of C. nepalensis, particularly EA-L, ameliorated MK-801-induced schizophrenia-like behavioral abnormalities by restoring neurotransmitter homeostasis and suppressing the aberrant activation of neuroinflammation-related signaling pathways. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: A non-explosive alpha-series recurrence framework for modelling mortality jump arrivals
abstract: Catastrophic mortality jumps disrupt long-term trends, yet existing jump models assume either constant jump probability or i.i.d. recurrence times, ignoring how jump-timing patterns evolve. The Lee–Carter framework is extended with a non-explosive alpha-series recurrence process, letting inter-jump durations shift with event order, nesting the stationary renewal process as a special case. Jump years are identified from the total-population mortality index and modelled as a common event sequence, with female and male dynamics linked through sex-specific effects and correlated innovations; the discretised likelihood uses exact recurrence-duration probabilities, including right-censoring after the most recent jump. Applied to Denmark, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the UK, and the USA with a 2019 calibration cutoff, the model reveals substantial cross-country heterogeneity in jump recurrence and favourable forecast performance. For a term-life portfolio, alternative arrival mechanisms yield similar expected liabilities, while their relative differences become more visible in tail-capital measures, indicating that recurrence assumptions matter more for tail-risk assessment than for mean liability levels. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Brazilian Expert Consensus on the Use of Equity and Acceptability in Health Technology Assessment: A Delphi Panel
abstract: Objectives To achieve consensus among Brazilian experts on the concepts of equity and acceptability within the context of health technology assessment (HTA) in Brazil and to identify guidance for their practical application across assessment stages, operationalization methods, and strategies for evidence generation and use. Methods A 2-round online Delphi panel with Brazilian HTA experts assessed agreement on predefined literature-based concepts of equity and acceptability and explored perspectives on HTA stages, methods, and evidence generation and retrieval strategies. Reasons for disagreement and recommendations for further incorporating these dimensions were also qualitatively analyzed. Results Participants were experienced HTA professionals, and consensus on the concepts of equity and acceptability was reached in the first round, exceeding the predefined threshold of 80% agreement. These dimensions were considered cross-cutting throughout the HTA process, with priority given to technology assessment, clinical guideline development, and implementation stages. Evidence search methods and cost-effectiveness analyses were prioritized for equity, whereas qualitative evidence and mixed methods were prioritized for acceptability. Strategies including secondary data analysis, primary data collection, and standardized filter use were prioritized for both dimensions. Conclusions This study advances the conceptual understanding of equity and acceptability in HTA and provides methodological guidance across process stages, supporting the development of more comprehensive HTA that is sensitive to inequities and responsive to population needs. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Where biomethane works: Geospatial and technical drivers of cost-effective deployment at municipal scale
abstract: Biomethane produced from agricultural and agro-industrial residues can contribute to replacing fossil natural gas, yet national estimates alone do not reveal where production is technically and economically viable. This study developed a spatially explicit assessment of biomethane production across mainland Portugal, combining feedstocks, anaerobic co-digestion configurations, greenhouse gas accounting, feedstock and grid logistics, and techno-economic analysis at the municipal level. Results were aggregated to quantify national theoretical, technical and implementable potential while retaining the spatial detail needed to identify deployment constraints. Theoretical biomethane potential reached 0.643 bcm·yr−1, declining to a technical potential of 0.225 bcm·yr−1 after accounting for feedstock recovery rates and conversion losses. Once spatial, infrastructural and economic constraints were applied, implementable potential fell to 0.140–0.183 bcm·yr−1 across 81–133 sites, depending on carbon pricing, with resource-rich municipalities failing to qualify due to infrastructure inaccessibility. Transport, grid connection and feedstock logistics determine viability, producing geographically concentrated patterns. Under best available technology, net GHG abatement reached −1211 kt CO2eq·yr−1, while uncontrolled methane leakage more than halved it and left 9 to 12% of sites as net emitters under standard practice. 69% of avoided emissions originate from agricultural co-benefits (manure management and fertiliser displacement) rather than NG substitution, highlighting system boundary relevance. The median levelized cost of the implementable subset (€95 MWh−1 at the €80 PAB reference price) was competitive under current carbon pricing. Biomass availability, infrastructure coverage and carbon pricing shape an economic feasibility outcome that is inherently spatial and policy-sensitive. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Learning aircraft procedures through an immersive virtual reality environment
abstract: Pilot trainees must familiarize themselves with a cockpit and master the associated procedures, i.e. specified sequences of interaction. Usually, this self-regulated learning relies on paper-based procedures and a cockpit poster, which can be monotonous and demotivating for trainees. In this study, N=36 pilot students tested the efficiency of a new Virtual Reality (VR) training tool for learning aircraft procedures. Results were compared with previously collected data from both traditional paper-based training and desktop training software embedded on a tactile screen. Participants were more motivated using the VR tool than with the two other methods. When tested in a realistic flight simulator, training effectiveness was better for VR than the traditional method, but similar to the tactile desktop tool. Moreover, study duration has not been shorten with the VR tool. Finally, open comments by participants provided useful directions on improving user interaction with the VR environment. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Choquet integral and shapley value-based operators for context-aware recommendation
abstract: In modern recommendation scenarios, Context-Aware Recommender Systems (CARS) play a critical role in providing personalized suggestions by leveraging additional contextual information such as user preferences, time, and location. Despite significant advances, two key challenges persist: effectively weighting context features and selecting relevant neighbors to ensure accurate and robust recommendations. In this work, we propose a novel aggregation framework based on Choquet integral and Shapley value operators, capturing both individual feature importance and interactions among features. Simultaneously, we introduce a correlated neighbor selection strategy that identifies and prioritizes the most influential users, improving robustness against irrelevant or malicious neighbors. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach consistently enhances recommendation accuracy and reliability, outperforming classical baselines in terms of RMSE and MAE. These results highlight the potential of combining Choquet- and Shapley-based feature weighting with correlated neighbor selection to advance the effectiveness of context-aware recommender systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Newton-Cotes-based FIR smoothing for robust ECG segmentation: Integration with the Modified Varri method
abstract: Reliable segmentation of electrocardiographic (ECG) signals is often compromised by noise and non-stationary artifacts, which can lead to unstable boundary detection. This study proposes a preprocessing strategy to enhance the robustness of the Modified Varri method using Newton–Cotes Moving Average (NCMA) filters. NCMA filters are symmetric, normalized FIR operators derived from closed Newton–Cotes quadrature rules. Their construction ensures unit DC gain, linear-phase behavior, and exact preservation of low-order polynomial trends in an integral sense. These properties make them suitable as structured smoothing operators for ECG signals, reducing noise variance while maintaining the underlying signal morphology. NCMA filters with 3, 5, and 7 points were evaluated on both synthetic signals and real recordings from the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database using standard denoising metrics (MSE, SNR, and PRD) and a segmentation-specific Boundary Stability Index (BSI). Results show that the 5-point NCMA filter provides the best trade-off between noise reduction and signal fidelity, outperforming Savitzky–Golay smoothing of comparable length on synthetic data. On real recordings, while the 5-point filter balances signal fidelity and noise reduction, the 7-point configuration provides the highest segmentation stability (lowest BSI), despite greater morphological smoothing. Statistical validation across multiple noise realizations confirms the robustness of the proposed approach. These findings demonstrate that NCMA-based preprocessing offers a reliable and lightweight alternative to conventional SG filtering, enhancing ECG segmentation reliability in noisy environments. © 2026 The Authors.
