title: Beyond tasks: Environment and interaction as active components in virtual reality interventions for dementia
abstract: Dementia presents a major global health challenge, and virtual reality (VR) offers an emerging platform that combines therapeutic potential with engaging human-computer interaction. Research has often emphasized task design or exercise-based training, yet the roles of the environment and interaction within VR interventions remain underexplored. This systematic review synthesized 48 empirical studies published between 2010 and 2024, encompassing 1944 participants across 23 countries. Literature was identified through searches in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CNKI, and Elsevier, and study quality was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool. Findings indicate that natural, cultural, and personally meaningful environments were linked to reducing anxiety, depression, and behavioral symptoms in individuals with moderate to severe dementia, while task-oriented and gamified environments enhanced memory, attention, and executive function in those with mild impairment. Modes of engagement also shaped outcomes, with whole-body interaction producing greater improvements in balance, coordination, and daily functioning than passive viewing. Intervention frequency further influenced results as high-frequency short-term programs supported rapid emotional and physical benefits, whereas low-frequency long-term programs promoted sustained cognitive stability. By framing environments, engagement, and frequency as active design variables, this review positions VR dementia interventions within a broader human-computer interaction perspective that can inform future technologies for aging populations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: ECG-based NSR, CHF, and ARR classification: Tradeoff between classical feature engineering and TCN-based deep features
abstract: Accurate and efficient automatic classification of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is essential for scalable cardiac monitoring and timely clinical decision making. Herein, we focus on classifying Arrhythmia (ARR), Congestive Heart Failure (CHF), and Normal Sinus Rhythm (NSR). In particular, this study compares a classical feature-based pipeline that includes time-domain, frequency-domain, and time-scale features with a modern deep feature extractor employing the Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN). For this, MATLAB simulations were conducted on ECG signals from the MIT-BIH database to evaluate the classification performance and quantify practical trade-offs by reporting wall-clock training times, inference latency, and hardware requirements. The results showed that the Support Vector Machine (SVM) achieved classification accuracies of 88%, 91%, and 100% for ARR vs NSR, ARR vs CHF, and NSR vs CHF, respectively, when trained and tested on the classical features. On the other hand, the TCN achieved an overall accuracy of 99.4% to distinguish between the three classes. Furthermore, the TCN yielded superior raw predictive performance but offered reduced interpretability compared with the classical feature-based pipeline, at the expense of requiring substantially greater computational resources. These results demonstrated that well-engineered classical descriptors remain competitive for low-resource deployment, while data-driven TCNs deliver higher accuracy when computational budgets permit. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Integrated Waste-to-Energy Systems: A comprehensive review of Technologies, decision Frameworks, and sustainability metrics
abstract: Rising waste generation and growing energy demand have driven global interest in Waste-to-Energy (WtE) systems as a pathway toward sustainable waste management and resource recovery. However, existing WtE reviews remain fragmented: most are technology-centric, focusing on individual conversion routes, while others address environmental performance, economic feasibility, or decision-making methods in isolation, without linking them to waste characteristics or site-specific conditions. This limits the ability of researchers, policymakers, and stakeholders to systematically select suitable WtE solutions for specific regional contexts. This review addresses this gap by first characterizing major waste streams—municipal solid, industrial, agricultural and forestry, sewage sludge, medical, e-waste, and construction and demolition waste—and evaluating their compatibility with thermal (incineration, gasification, pyrolysis), biological (anaerobic digestion, landfill gas recovery), and emerging hybrid conversion technologies. It then examines site-specific factors governing WtE deployment, including economic conditions, geographic and logistical constraints, regulatory and policy drivers, and social acceptance. Building on these dimensions, the review proposes a novel conceptual 3D matrix framework integrating waste type, technology suitability, and site characteristics into a unified selection platform, and synthesizes multi-criteria decision analysis approaches supported by case study synthesis. Environmental and economic performance is further consolidated through life cycle assessment, levelized cost of energy, and circular economy indicators to establish a holistic sustainability assessment methodology. Finally, the review identifies key challenges in emission control, investment uncertainty, resource recovery, and public acceptance, and outlines future opportunities in AI-assisted optimization, carbon capture integration, and circular economy-driven WtE systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Teacher emotional support, question openness and student oral participation: The role of positive emotion across stages in AI-observed STEM and non-STEM classes
abstract: Background: Student oral participation is essential for engagement and learning, yet participation tends to decline in large-class and STEM contexts where social risk and cognitive demands are higher. Existing studies often relied on self-reported or small-scale observations, which may introduce subjective bias and are labor-intensive, limiting large-scale evidence on how instructional practices influence participation across contexts. Aims: This study examines how teacher emotional support and question openness influence student oral participation through student emotion, and whether these effects vary across educational stages and disciplinary contexts. Sample: Data were collected from 1455 face-to-face classes in China. Methods: Artificial intelligence-based techniques were used to capture fine-grained classroom interactions. Structural equation modeling and multigroup analyses were conducted to examine the mediating role of student positive emotion and to compare pathway patterns across educational stages and disciplinary contexts. Results: Teacher emotional support was primarily associated with student oral participation via student positive emotion, whereas question openness showed a more direct association with participation. The indirect role of emotional support through positive emotion became stronger across educational stages, suggesting a compensatory function in secondary education where baseline participation tends to decline. Students in STEM classes were less emotionally responsive to teacher support but showed a stronger association between positive emotions and oral participation. Conclusions: Emotional support is a context-sensitive intervention rather than a universally effective strategy. By combining large-scale AI-based observation with cross-stage and disciplinary comparisons, this study contributes methodological advances for classroom interaction research, although cross-cultural validation of AI-based measures is needed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Field Assessment of the Safety Action Evaluation Protocol: Construction Safety Climate Focus
abstract: Frontline supervisors play a vital role in shaping the construction safety climate. Critical supervisory safety actions have been developed into the Safety Action Evaluation Protocol (SAEP) and a field assessment undertaken by frontline supervisors to evaluate its effectiveness and potential. A longitudinal field assessment was undertaken involving four stages of mixed-method inquiry to elicit both quantitative and qualitative data in a convergent design. Twelve frontline supervisors implemented the SAEP over a three-month period, embedding it into their daily work practices. Qualitative and quantitative data were collected at key stages and analyzed using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis. The frontline supervisors found the SAEP to be a useful and usable tool in the field that helped them prioritize and enhance safety. Allocation of suitable time to deliver the SAEP, and full organizational support and commitment, were felt to be critical for operational success. The SAEP was also considered a strong and well-balanced safety metric with potential as a safety management and monitoring tool in the future. The SAEP was evaluated as an effective tool to enhance the safety actions of frontline supervisors in the field. Future research will assess its use as a tool for safety monitoring and evaluation, completing the validation of the SAEP in the field. The SAEP is a practical safety management tool, cocreated with industry. It was found to be both useful and usable by frontline supervisors, who felt it enhanced their safety actions in the field. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Preschoolers use exploratory approaches to selective social learning
abstract: Preschoolers evaluate many cues when making inferences about others (Harris et al., 2018). It is unclear whether children’s understanding of inference-making is sophisticated enough that they also seek out the most relevant cues for making specific inferences. Here, we tasked 4- and 5-year-olds and adults with a modified epistemic trust paradigm in which they were told to select one of two informants to help them learn about novel objects. However, before doing so, participants were told that they could learn up to three pieces of information about the informants: what they know (epistemic cue), how they play with their friends (benevolence cue), or what they look like (appearance cue). Of particular interest was which cue participants prioritized (picked first) and what strategies they used for seeking information. In Study 1, adults prioritized learning epistemic information and tended to employ efficient information-seeking strategies (selecting the fewest cues possible to make their inferences). Children, on the other hand, chose each cue first at relatively equal rates and tended to employ exploratory strategies for information-seeking (sampling broadly from the available information). This was even the case in Study 2, in which the informativeness of the appearance and benevolence cues was reduced. These studies raise questions about the way in which children make inferences about others and point to a tendency for children to employ exploratory strategies for learning about others (Gopnik, 2020). © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Reinforcement learning for robust ageing-aware control of Li-ion battery systems with data-driven formal verification
abstract: Rechargeable lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries are a ubiquitous element of modern technology. In the last decades, the production and design of such batteries and their adjacent embedded charging and safety protocols, denoted by Battery Management Systems (BMS), has taken central stage. A fundamental challenge to be addressed is the trade-off between the speed of charging and the ageing behaviour, resulting in the loss of capacity in the battery cell. We rely on a high-fidelity physics-based battery model and propose an approach to data-driven charging and safety protocol design. Following a Counterexample-Guided Inductive Synthesis scheme, we combine Reinforcement Learning (RL) with recent developments in data-driven formal methods to obtain a hybrid control strategy: RL is used to synthesise the individual controllers, and a data-driven abstraction guides their partitioning into a switched structure, depending on the initial output measurements of the battery. The resulting discrete selection among RL-based controllers, coupled with the continuous battery dynamics, realises a hybrid system. When a design meets the desired criteria, the abstraction provides probabilistic guarantees on the closed-loop performance of the cell. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. This is an open access article under the CC BY license. http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Robust subband adaptive filters: A review
abstract: Due to its outstanding decorrelation ability, the normalized subband adaptive filter (NSAF) algorithm has been widely used in scenarios involving highly correlated input signals. Under Gaussian noise, the NSAF algorithm based on the mean square error (MSE) criterion has attracted extensive attention due to its low computational complexity and excellent performance for correlated signals. However, practical environments often contain impulsive noise instead of ideal Gaussian noise. Since the MSE criterion is sensitive to outliers, impulsive noise will seriously deteriorate the convergence and steady-state performance of the NSAF algorithm. To suppress impulsive interference, robust subband adaptive filter (RSAF) algorithms usually adopt nonlinear saturation-based loss functions (e.g., Lp-norm, Huber function, correntropy) to weaken the impact of outliers. Beyond this core anti-impulsive capability, techniques derived from the RSAF framework for fixed step-size implementation, sparse system identification, nonlinear tasks, censored regression (CR) models, errors-in-variables (EIV) models, and distributed network problems have also attracted considerable scholarly interest. Overall, despite the rapid development of RSAF algorithms in recent years, there remains a lack of comprehensive reviews that systematically summarize their design principles, performance characteristics, and application scopes. Addressing this research gap, this paper presents a systematic overview of RSAF algorithms and proposes several promising future research directions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Alexithymia and everyday interpersonal emotion regulation
abstract: Alexithymia, a multifaceted personality trait characterized by difficulties identifying and describing feelings and an externally oriented thinking style, is linked to social difficulties. Drawing on the extended process model of extrinsic interpersonal emotion regulation (IER), we examined whether higher (vs. lower) levels of alexithymia are associated with differences in how people regulate others' emotions, a pathway that may help explain why alexithymia is linked to social dysfunction. Across two ecological momentary assessment studies (Study 1: Germany, n = 129; Study 2: United States, n = 220; 6028 observations), results revealed distinct patterns of association across alexithymia facets. In both studies, the direction of associations suggested that greater difficulties identifying feelings were associated with higher IER strategy use, with this pattern most apparent for more cognitive and problem-focused strategies versus more emotion-oriented IER. In contrast, greater difficulties describing feelings were consistently linked to lower IER strategy use, whereas externally oriented thinking showed no consistent directional pattern. These findings suggest that alexithymia is associated with differential patterns of IER strategy use, underscoring IER difficulties as an interpersonal process that may contribute to links between alexithymia and social dysfunction. Our results emphasize the importance of considering the multifaceted nature of alexithymia in IER. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Ultrasonic vocalizations in mice: Effects of sex, age, and environmental conditions
abstract: Ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) are key communicative signals in rodents, reflecting developmental stage, sex, and social context. Most studies on female mice USVs focus on their effects on male behavior or pup interactions, while few address vocalizations unrelated to reproduction or maternal care. The present study aimed to fill this gap by characterizing USVs in C57BL/6 mice of both sexes at different developmental stages and under distinct contexts. Neonatal (PND 3–4), postnatal (PND 13–14), adolescent (PND 30–45), and adult (PND 90) mice were evaluated in various contexts. Our results reveal a dynamic transitional pattern in USV production. Neonates of both sexes emitted a high number of calls, which markedly declined after the postnatal period, indicating a behavioral shift in communication. Sexual dimorphism emerged in adulthood, as females partially recovered vocalization rates, whereas males maintained low emission levels after adolescence. Although no significant differences in USVs were detected between stressed and non-stressed adolescents, some stressed individuals completely ceased vocalizing, suggesting a strong individual variability in response to acute stress, independently of sex. In adulthood, males and females exhibited distinct vocal strategies depending on the social or non-social context. Overall, these findings highlight the importance of USVs as sensitive markers of developmental, sex-dependent, and context-specific communicative behaviors, providing valuable insights for refining animal models in behavioral neuroscience. © 2026

title: Differential frontostriatal ΔFosB dynamics and behavioral flexibility in autism like VPA-exposed mice
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) involves social impairments, repetitive behaviors, and behavioral inflexibility, defined as an inability to adapt behavior to changing contingencies, and is linked to frontostriatal dysfunction. How behavioral training modulates these circuits is unclear, but ΔFosB, a marker of sustained neural activity, may be useful to establish their relationship. The aim was to evaluate frontostriatal ΔFosB expression following prenatal exposure to valproic acid (VPA) and to determine how experience in the midsession reversal (MSR) task modulates posterior ΔFosB expression. CD-1 mice were prenatally exposed to VPA (500 mg/kg) or vehicle. Brains from postnatal day (PND) 30 mice were analyzed to quantify baseline ΔFosB + cells in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), dorsal striatum (DS), and ventral striatum (VS). In the second experiment, mice performed the MSR task for 13 days. Then, ΔFosB was re-evaluated at PND43 to assess experience-dependent changes. At PND30, VPA-exposed mice showed a significant increase in ΔFosB + cells in mPFC, OFC, DS, and VS, suggesting sustained activity-dependent engagement of the frontostriatal circuit. In the MSR task, mice adapted to contingency shifts using mixed strategies, including win-stay/lose-shift behavior and temporal estimation, whereas VPA mice showed less consistent strategy selection after reversal. After MSR, ΔFosB expression in the OFC and striatum of VPA mice normalized to control levels and remained persistently elevated in the mPFC at PND43. Thus, prenatal VPA induces long-term increases in neuronal transcriptional changes, suggesting activity-dependent plasticity in the frontostriatal circuit. Despite these neural alterations, behavioral flexibility was preserved, suggesting circuit-level adaptations underlying ASD-related strategies. Future studies could broaden these results by examining sex differences and characterizing the cellular and molecular changes dependent on frontostriatal ΔFosB dynamics. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Explaining deceptive language in topical discourse: Integrating transformer models and explainable AI using LIME and SHAP for transparent text-based deception detection
abstract: Detecting deception in textual communication is an important challenge in online environments where misleading information and deceptive narratives are increasingly prevalent. This study investigates the integration of fine-tuned transformer models, prompt-based large language models (LLMs), and explainable AI (XAI) techniques for interpretable deception detection. Its contributions include a statistically validated comparison of six BERT architectures, a factorial prompt ablation across five GPT models, and a quantitative evaluation of LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) explanation quality and stability. Experiments were conducted on two domain-specific datasets totaling 500 statements, with 264 related to climate change and 236 related to COVID-19. The results show that transformer models are effective for deception classification even when trained on relatively small datasets, with DeBERTa achieving 88.87% and 87.92% accuracy on topical datasets. LIME and SHAP were applied to analyze word-level attribution patterns in the best-performing model. The two XAI methods exhibited substantial aggregate-level agreement, converging on similar sets of influential words associated with deception across domains, whereas agreement on individual predictions was more limited. These findings align with prior research on recurring patterns in deceptive language and provide supportive evidence that linguistic patterns identified through explainability techniques remain consistent across topics, even under limited data conditions. Overall, the results demonstrate that combining contemporary language models with XAI techniques can provide both accurate predictions and interpretable insights into the linguistic characteristics of deceptive communication. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Fusion techniques of time frequency-based images to predict the outcome of rTMS depression therapy
abstract: Depression is a mental condition that can lead to suicide and self-harm. Predicting the outcome of depression treatment is one of the most difficult tasks for clinicians. Among various treatment options, repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) is a widely used non-invasive method. Predicting rTMS response using Electroencephalogram (EEG) data is difficult because of high inter-subject variability and limited features from single-domain analysis. We introduce two fusion techniques, montage and blending, to overcome these limitations and extract richer features from EEG-derived Time-Frequency (TF) images. We then propose a lightweight custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on fused TF representations. We use a primary dataset of 15 patients and a secondary dataset of 46 patients. We run two sets of experiments. The first set uses segment-level 10-fold cross-validation. In this setup segments from the same patient can appear in both training and testing. The Montage CWT_ST fusion reaches 99.90% accuracy on the primary dataset and 91.90% on the secondary dataset. The second set uses strict subject-disjoint cross-validation. All segments of a patient stay in one fold and no patient appears in both training and testing. Performance collapses. We test four time–frequency methods, six fusion mechanisms, and fourteen model architectures. With one exception, every configuration on both cohorts falls between AUC 0.31 and 0.54 and every 95% confidence interval contains 0.5. A patient-level permutation test on the best standalone method returns p = 0.703. The best subject-level result is Montage CWT_ST on the primary cohort, which reaches AUC 0.874 ± 0.183 and 82.7% accuracy. The same fusion strategy on the same pair of methods reaches 0.514 on the secondary cohort, so the mechanism behind this difference is not yet established and we identify it as the main target for follow-up work. The gap between the two experimental setups is the main result. Segment-level validation raises accuracy from chance to near-perfect on this data. Similar figures in the EEG literature should therefore be read together with the fold construction used to produce them. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Multi-agent reinforcement learning for energy-efficient cooperative UAV deployment in 5G networks
abstract: The increasing demand for ubiquitous mobile connectivity and the rapid deployment of fifth generation (5G) networks have intensified the need for flexible communication infrastructures that can adapt to highly dynamic user distributions. In this context, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) operating as aerial base stations (BSs) have emerged as a promising solution for extending network coverage and capacity in scenarios where terrestrial infrastructure is unavailable, congested, or insufficient. However, determining efficient UAV deployment strategies remains a challenging optimization problem due to user mobility, network dynamics, and energy constraints. This paper presents a continuous-state multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework for the cooperative deployment of UAV-based aerial BSs. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on grid-based mobility abstractions, the proposed framework incorporates force-based control dynamics to model UAV motion. Two representative MARL algorithms, namely multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) and monotonic value function factorization (QMIX), are evaluated under a centralized training and decentralized execution paradigm. Three independent and unweighted reward formulations are introduced, targeting network capacity maximization, relative capacity improvement, and energy-efficient data delivery, to isolate the impact of the reward structure and ensure that observed performance trade-offs are strictly attributable to the reward design. Bayesian hyperparameter optimization is applied independently to each configuration, while a functional ANOVA analysis demonstrates that hyperparameter sensitivity is inherently dependent on the algorithm and the reward. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed cooperative learning framework enables UAVs to learn coordinated deployment strategies that consistently outperform non-adaptive baseline approaches under diverse user mobility conditions, increased user density, intermittent position-report losses, and variations in action-force magnitude. Measured inference latency remains below one-fifth of the control interval on all evaluated hardware platforms, indicating that decentralized execution is feasible without an onboard accelerator. Among the evaluated configurations, reward shaping plays a critical role in balancing throughput and energy consumption, and MAPPO exhibits the most robust overall performance. These findings highlight the potential of adaptive MARL for efficient and energy-aware UAV-assisted 5G network deployment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Scale-armor-inspired rigid-soft-coupled heterogeneous structures: Additive manufacturing and tribological mechanisms
abstract: Biological scale armor offers a natural strategy for reconciling lightweight design with wear resistance through rigid-soft synergy. However, the pronounced mismatch in composition and mechanical properties between rigid and soft materials often causes interfacial incompatibility and stress concentration, hindering the precise fabrication and tribological optimization of bioinspired rigid-soft coupled structures. Inspired by the wear-resistant and drag-reducing structure of desert lizard scales, we construct a bioinspired rigid-soft coupled structure (BRSCS) by multimaterial additive manufacturing and systematically investigate how structural parameters affect its friction and wear behavior. The results indicate that incorporating a flexible constituent phase promotes deformation accommodation and subsurface loading redistribution, thereby improving the tribological performance of the material under sliding conditions. Compared with pure rigid resin, the BRSCS reduces the coefficient of friction ( COF ) by 25.7% and the wear rate by up to 62.6% under a representative normal load of 20 N and the present dry reciprocating sliding conditions. Combined mechanical, dynamic mechanical, and wear-morphology analyses indicate that the tribological response is associated with the evolution of the interfacial contact states under different rigid-soft configurations. This work provides structural-design guidance for additively manufactured polymer-based bioinspired materials with potential lightweight structural and wear-resistant applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A dual-process motivational approach to understanding antisemitism: The role of authoritarianism, social dominance orientation, and conspiracy mentality
abstract: Antisemitism remains a persistent challenge in contemporary societies, yet its psychological underpinnings are not well understood. Building on the dual-process motivational (DPM) model of ideology and prejudice, this study examined the extent to which antisemitism is rooted in broader ideological dispositions - right-wing authoritarianism (RWA), social dominance orientation (SDO), and conspiracy mentality. Using a nationwide online survey of German adults ( N = 457), bivariate and multivariate analyses indicate that conspiracy mentality is the strongest correlate of antisemitic attitudes, followed by individual differences in SDO. These findings support the view that antisemitism is embedded within a broader ideological belief system characterized by anti-egalitarian and conspiratorial worldviews. The role of conspiratorial worldviews as a potential distinct motivational pathway to prejudice within the DPM model is discussed. © 2026 The Author.

title: Beyond the hotspots: Identifying public opinion blind spots and agenda-setting dynamics in crisis information generation
abstract: During sudden crises, a structural mismatch between social media attention and governance value often marginalizes key crisis issues, creating public opinion blind spots that undermine effective emergency management. Using the 2021 Henan rainstorm as a case study (N = 40,160), this study proposes an integrated framework to identify public opinion blind spots and examine their agenda-setting dynamics. Methodologically, we combine grounded theory with Large Language Model (LLM) analysis for theme classification (92.7% accuracy), apply refined Importance-Performance Analysis (IPA) to identify blind spots, and use Vector Autoregression (VAR) models, Granger causality tests, and impulse response functions (IRFs) to examine agenda-setting dynamics. Bootstrap estimation further assesses the association between blind spots and agenda-setting effects. Results show that blind spots vary dynamically across the 4R phases, with Prevention Education, Disaster Causation, and Review and Improvement recurring most frequently. Bidirectional agenda-setting effects can emerge at a 1-hour resolution, and stronger agenda guidance from authoritative users is associated with blind-spot mitigation. Ultimately, these findings offer practical implications for optimizing crisis information supply and strengthening social resilience. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Parks as behavioral climate adaptation infrastructure: mechanisms and limits under extreme heat
abstract: Urban parks are increasingly positioned as critical nature-based solutions for mitigating extreme heat. However, while their physical cooling capacity is well-documented, their role as infrastructure for behavioral climate adaptation remains underexplored. This study examines urban parks as behavioral climate adaptation infrastructure by integrating event-based mobility analysis, park-level adaptation performance assessment, and neighborhood-scale accessibility analysis in the City of Las Vegas. Using anonymized mobility records, extreme heat episodes were identified and linked to changes in visitation intensity, dwell time, and nighttime use. Event-level behavioral responses were summarized using the Park Behavioral Adaptation Index (PBAI), while longer-term park performance was evaluated using the Park Adaptation Performance Score (PACS). Accessibility to higher-performing parks was subsequently assessed in relation to neighborhood social vulnerability. The results reveal three key findings. First, adaptation occurs primarily through temporal reallocation. Second, adaptation performance varies substantially across parks and cannot be explained by park size, morphology, vegetation greenness, or amenity provision alone. Third, access to higher-performing parks is unevenly distributed across the city. Adaptation deficit zones are concentrated in lower-income, renter-dominated, and minority neighborhoods, indicating that opportunities for park-based adaptation are socially unequal. By linking behavioral responses, park performance, and adaptive accessibility within a unified framework, this study shifts attention from the cooling potential of parks to their role in enabling realized adaptation under extreme heat. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Leveraging concept-cognitive learning to identify maximum s-defective cliques in network systems
abstract: Detecting maximum s-defective cliques and cohesive subgraphs tolerating up to s missing edges is crucial for analyzing noisy and dynamic networks, but due to its NP-hardness, it remains challenging, leading to poor time efficiency and difficulties in dynamic scenarios. To address this problem, this study introduces a novel framework that leverages Formal Concept Analysis (FCA) under the paradigm of Concept-Cognitive Learning (CCL). This paper presents a theoretical proof that any maximum s-defective clique can be derived by expanding an equiconcept, which refers to a clique structure with equal intension and extension, and with at most s vertices, thereby ensuring detection completeness. Based on this, we develop two algorithms: a static method SFDC and an incremental method IFDC. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that our approach typically achieves 10x to 100x speedups over state-of-the-art methods in both static and dynamic settings, with particularly strong performance in high-defect and dynamic environments. A case study further illustrates the practical utility of our method in extracting meaningful cohesive structures from real networks. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: The influence of gender, socioeconomic, and domain competencies on students’ creative thinking across four high-performing educational systems
abstract: This study explores the multidimensional construct of students’ creative thinking by analysing the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking assessment data from four educational systems: Chinese Taipei, Hong Kong, Macao, and the Czech Republic. These jurisdictions are uniquely characterised by high student performance in reading, mathematics, and science, while their average creative thinking scores fall below the OECD benchmark. The study examines the predictive power of gender, socioeconomic status (SES), and academic proficiency in Reading, Mathematics, and Science on students’ performance across four creative thinking (CRT) domain contexts: Written Expression, Visual Expression, Social Creative Problem-Solving, and Scientific Creative Problem-Solving. Evidence shows that female students consistently outperformed male students across all four creative thinking domains, while SES demonstrated a modest but consistently positive association with creative thinking performance. Academic competencies also contributed significantly to CRT but exhibited distinct domain-specific predictive patterns. Reading competence was the strongest and most consistent predictor, particularly for Written and Visual Expression. Science competence showed stable positive associations across domains, whereas Mathematics contributed most strongly to Social and Scientific Creative Problem-Solving but was negatively associated with Visual Expression. These findings indicate that academic competencies contribute differently across creative thinking domains. Representative item-level analyses further illustrated task-specific predictive patterns, while the complete item-level analyses are reported in the Supplementary Material. These findings support a domain-sensitive view of creative thinking, in which academic competencies show differential associations with creative performance depending on the domain and task context, and further offer practical implications for creativity assessment and educational practice. title: UHPLC-HRMS-based untargeted lipidomics for differentiating halal and non-halal meat species in processed sausages
abstract: The integrity of the halal food supply chain is continually challenged by fraudulent adulteration, particularly in processed meat products where visual identification of ingredients is impossible. This study used untargeted lipidomics based on ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC-HRMS) combined with chemometric analysis to differentiate halal and non-halal meat species in processed sausages. Five sausage formulations were prepared: 100% beef, 100% pork, 100% dog meat, and 50:50 mixtures of beef–pork and beef–dog meat. Lipid profiles were acquired in both positive (ESI+) and negative (ESI−) ionization modes. Principal component analysis (PCA) clearly separated the five sausage formulations, indicating distinct lipidomic profiles. Partial least squares-discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) further differentiated the sample groups and identified several putative lipid biomarkers based on variable importance in projection (VIP) scores. Among these, PG(16:0/18:2) and PE(6:0/14:1) + H detected in pork samples were consistent with previous reports and may serve as candidate biomarkers for halal authentication, while PC(18:0p/17:1) + H and PC(13:0/21:2) + H were identified as putative lipid biomarkers characteristic of dog meat sausages. These findings highlight the potential of UHPLC-HRMS-based untargeted lipidomics for differentiating halal and non-halal meat species in processed sausages. However, the proposed biomarkers require further validation by targeted MS/MS analysis and independent sample sets before broader application. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Mitigating feature degradation in deep Forward–Forward networks
abstract: The Forward–Forward (FF) algorithm is a promising alternative to Backpropagation (BP) using layer-wise optimization. However, due to its local learning nature, FF suffers from feature degradation, which can be more severe than in BP for deep networks. To bridge this gap, we propose Sustained Forward (SF), which employs a dual-mechanism approach to achieve sustained feature propagation. Specifically, Cross-layer Gradient Momentum (CGM) propagates cross-layer gradient momentum to enrich the learning signal, and Local Feature Reconstruction (LFR) reconstructs local features to compensate for information loss. Extensive experiments on common benchmarks demonstrate that SF achieves significant performance improvements (e.g., over 6% on CIFAR-100), substantially narrowing the gap to BP. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Current research on catalysts and deactivation mechanisms for methane catalytic oxidation
abstract: Focusing on the complex marine exhaust conditions with high water vapor, trace sulfur compounds and fluctuating operating loads, this work systematically summarizes the structure–activity relationships and anti-deactivation characteristics of mainstream catalysts for marine methane total oxidation. Among noble metal materials, Pd-based catalysts exhibit remarkable low-temperature catalytic activity, while Pt-based catalysts deliver superior sulfur tolerance under harsh flue gas environments. By contrast, the performance advantages of Rh catalysts are mainly effective for partial oxidation of methane. Beyond noble metals, low-cost transition metal oxides, perovskites, zeolites, and metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have also been comprehensively analyzed, with emphasis on their modification strategies tailored to improve low-temperature activity, hydrothermal stability and sulfur resistance. This review highlights the rational design and directional optimization of multifunctional catalysts targeting the actual demanding marine working conditions, providing theoretical guidance for the development of efficient and durable marine methane emission control technologies. title: Fast semi-supervised graph clustering by directly solving pairwise constrained problem
abstract: Pairwise-constrained graph clustering has been widely studied in semi-supervised learning. Most existing methods incorporate pairwise constraints indirectly, either as penalty terms in the objective function or through modifications to the similarity graph, and subsequently obtain cluster results via relaxation strategies. Such approaches may not sufficiently enforce the given constraints and often involve costly eigendecomposition, which limits their efficiency on large datasets or in the presence of numerous constraints. To address these limitations, we propose a novel optimization framework that directly solves the original discrete constrained graph clustering problem. Specifically, a block coordinate descent (CD) method is formulated to exhaustively evaluate all feasible assignments of the two-row associated with each cannot-link pair yielding an exact solution to the corresponding discrete subproblem. Furthermore, connected components induced by must-link constraints are merged during anchor graph construction, effectively shrinking the problem scale. Crucially, a two-row incremental update mechanism is developed to accelerate the joint optimization process. Extensive experiments across twelve benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior clustering performance and exhibits high computational efficiency. © 2026

title: Competition-aware information fusion for cascade popularity prediction
abstract: Estimating the final size of an information cascade from its early prefix is difficult on open social platforms, where concurrent cascades often compete for overlapping user attention. Existing methods have improved prefix-based prediction with structural, temporal, and continuous-time representations, but external diffusion information is still often treated as generic context. The target-specific competitive environment available at prediction time is therefore not explicitly represented. We propose COMPETE, a competition-aware information fusion framework for macroscopic cascade popularity prediction under historical observability. COMPETE constructs a leakage-free local competition field from cascades visible at the prediction time. It combines structural-anchor and dynamic-burst views to represent the target cascade, selects locally relevant competitors by representation similarity, user overlap, and temporal concurrency, and couples the resulting competitive representation with the endogenous state for popularity estimation. In this formulation, surrounding cascade activity is represented as a target-specific field rather than a coarse context vector. Experiments on four public datasets show that COMPETE outperforms representative baselines in most settings. Additional analyses show that local competition is useful mainly when the observable environment contains stable external signals, which makes prediction-time competition a practical information source for cascade popularity prediction. The source code is publicly available on GitHub . © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Synergistic non-thermal plasma-catalytic reforming of toluene over hierarchical Ni/mHZSM-5 catalysts for efficient syngas production
abstract: Biomass tar reforming is generally constrained by the high energy demand of conventional thermal processes because of the chemical stability of aromatic compounds. In this work, dielectric barrier discharge plasma was coupled with hierarchical Ni/mHZSM-5 catalysts for the steam reforming of toluene as a representative biomass tar compound. The effects of Ni loading, reaction temperature, and discharge power on toluene conversion, syngas formation, carbon recovery, and energy efficiency were systematically investigated. Among the catalysts, 15 wt% Ni/mHZSM-5 exhibited the best performance because of its favorable Ni dispersion, high proportion of surface chemisorbed oxygen, enhanced reducibility, and balanced acidity distribution. Among the operating conditions investigated, the best overall reforming performance was obtained at 75 W and 525 °C, achieving a toluene conversion of 99.2%, an H2 yield of 48.3%, a CO selectivity of 36.0%, and a gaseous carbon balance of 60.1%. In comparison, conventional catalytic reforming required substantially higher temperatures to achieve lower conversion and syngas production, demonstrating the promotional effect of plasma excitation on aromatic activation and subsequent surface reforming. The highest toluene conversion energy efficiency of 6.5 g·kWh−1 was obtained at 30 W, indicating a trade-off between conversion performance and energy input. The catalyst also maintained high activity during a 48 h stability test, although gradual deactivation occurred because of carbon deposition. Identification of reactive species and by-products suggests the involvement of plasma-generated species in toluene and steam transformation, while Ni-containing sites may contribute to the subsequent conversion of intermediates toward H2 and CO. These results demonstrate that hierarchical Ni/mHZSM-5 is a promising catalyst for energy-efficient plasma-assisted biomass tar upgrading. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Measuring head motion across deceleration levels in automated driving: Quantifying comfort
abstract: Passenger-centred comfort measures are needed to enable adaptive driving styles in automated vehicles, particularly where comfort begins to decrease. This study examined passengers' head motion during automated braking at a crosswalk. Data from thirty-four participants were analysed, who experienced three deceleration levels (−1.5, −2.5, −3.5 m/s2) and two pedestrian visibility conditions, reflecting how quickly the AV braked after the pedestrian appeared, rating comfort respectively. As expected, head pitch and translational acceleration increased with deceleration intensity, while pedestrian visibility had no effect on head motion, even though faster AV responses were previously found more comfortable, suggesting this reflects passengers' judgement of the AV's response rather than head stability. Head-motion measures did not add predictive value beyond vehicle kinematics, likely because comfort ratings were similar across conditions. In this scenario, head-motion mainly reflected physical response to braking rather than subjective evaluation. Future research should test head-motion measures in more complex driving conditions. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Collective reinforcement learning and human–machine cooperation in multi-state stochastic games
abstract: With the growing deployment of artificial intelligence agents in collaborative systems, understanding how they jointly shape cooperative behavior with humans under dynamic environmental conditions becomes essential. Stochastic games provide a natural framework for capturing how environmental feedback shapes behavioral choices and supports the emergence of cooperation. Building on this framework, we incorporate collective reinforcement learning dynamics (CRLD) into a multi-state stochastic game and develop a mixed human–machine population model to examine the emergence and stability of cooperation. Unlike existing models that mainly consider homogeneous learning populations or externally determined environmental states, this framework explicitly captures the feedback interaction among human behavioral responses, environmental state transitions, and machine learning dynamics. Our results show that environmental vulnerability, public-goods incentives, human cooperative inclination and its population share, as well as machine discounting, jointly determine the evolutionary path of cooperation. Cooperative humans increase the likelihood of favorable environmental states, lowering the threshold for machines to learn cooperative strategies. In contrast, defect-prone humans can disrupt numerically stable cooperative states and induce cooperation collapse. Increasing the proportion of cooperative humans also reduces the critical discount factor required for machines to sustain cooperation. These findings demonstrate that human behavior reshapes environmental state transitions and alters machine value evaluation, exerting essential influence on learning and strategy evolution. Overall, this study reveals the mechanisms that sustain cooperation in human–machine systems with variable environmental states and provides theoretical insights relevant to coordination in mixed-agent systems. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: DMJP: Diffusion and multi-model joint perturbation for enhanced facial privacy
abstract: Face recognition technology has been adopted in public safety, social platforms, and other domains. However, unauthorized identity recognition poses privacy risks, exacerbating concerns about the misuse of personal data and thus calling for robust privacy protection methods. Current face privacy protection techniques often encounter challenges such as limited transferability or noticeable image distortion. To tackle these issues, this paper introduces DMJP, a framework that integrates Latent Diffusion Models with a multi-model joint perturbation optimization mechanism. The method encodes an input image into the latent space, applies gradient-based multi-model perturbations, and generates a protected image via Denoising Diffusion Implicit Model sampling. Gradients from multiple white-box face recognition models are combined to guide common feature manipulation, while different adversarial attack algorithms are merged to form a unified perturbation direction, enhancing transferability against black-box FR models. In addition, an adaptive perturbation strategy dynamically adjusts perturbation strength according to the diffusion timesteps and reconstruction errors, balancing protection effectiveness and image quality. Experiments on CelebA-HQ and FFHQ demonstrate a favorable trade-off between Protection Success Rate and image quality, with competitive PSNR/SSIM and substantially improved Fréchet Inception Distance. Further experiments evaluate computational efficiency through sparse injection and demonstrate target-free anonymization and robustness to preprocessing and DDIM purification. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Mapping the intellectual structure of floating photovoltaics research, trends and emerging frontiers: a hybrid bibliometric review and content analysis
abstract: This study presents a hybrid bibliometric–content analysis integrating scientific publications, patent activity, and deployment statistics to map the evolution, intellectual structure, and emerging research priorities of floating photovoltaic (FPV) systems. A dataset of 1716 publications spanning 2004–2025 was analysed using Bibliometrix, and the resulting thematic structure was used to organize a technical synthesis. Four interconnected domains were identified. Structurally, FPV deployment spans three aquatic environments, three principal floating concepts, and four station-keeping families, confirming that design requirements vary fundamentally with site conditions and environmental loading. Reported FPV energy-yield differences relative to land-based PV range from −3.84% to +19.68%, demonstrating that thermal benefits are strongly dependent on climate, geometry, and ventilation. Environmental studies commonly assess approximately 10% reservoir coverage, while scenarios reaching 25–30% indicate increasing trade-offs between water conservation and ecological uncertainty. Techno-economic evidence reports FPV capital-cost premiums of approximately 25–30%, with operating-cost estimates commonly 2–4% higher than land-based PV, although assumptions vary substantially. These findings demonstrate that FPV is a coupled water–energy–infrastructure system whose reliability, environmental sustainability, and bankability cannot be evaluated independently. Future research should prioritize long-term structural monitoring, transferable performance models, ecosystem-scale assessment, standardized reporting, and uncertainty-aware life-cycle economic frameworks for commercial-scale deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Development and experimental evaluation of common rail direct injection methanol (MD97) fuelled compression ignition engine
abstract: Methanol has emerged as a promising alternative to fossil fuels for powering internal combustion (IC) engines due to its higher fuel-to-oxygen ratio and lower tendency to form soot. Given the widespread use of compression-ignition (CI) engines in heavy-duty applications, there has been significant interest in adapting methanol for their operation. However, methanol’s inferior autoignition characteristics and longer ignition delay (ID) compared to diesel make its direct use in CI engines challenging. To overcome these limitations, engine modifications are essential to optimise the engine performance and ensure stable combustion. In this experimental study, a single-cylinder, four-stroke CI engine was modified by increasing its compression ratio (CR) and by incorporating an intake air preheating system to improve methanol ignition. The engine’s mechanical fuel injection system was replaced with a custom-built common-rail direct-injection (CRDI) system, and an in-house developed controller was utilised to inject methanol supplemented with an ignition improver (MD97: 97 % w/w methanol and 3 % w/w catalyst). The performance, combustion, and emission characteristics of MD97 were analysed and compared with baseline diesel (FIP 600 bar, SoI 14° bTDC). MD97 achieved stable ignition with a minimum ID of 7° CA, compared to the baseline diesel’s 7.5° CA. Injection timing was further optimised to achieve a balanced trade-off between the engine performance, combustion, and emission characteristics. Under optimised conditions (FIP 500 bar, SoI 13° bTDC), MD97 exhibited ∼40 % higher brake thermal efficiency (BTE), ∼88 % reduction in nitrogen oxides (NOx) emissions, and almost negligible exhaust smoke; however, hydrocarbons (HC) and carbon monoxide (CO) emissions increased by ∼23 % and ∼52 %, respectively, compared to baseline diesel. title: Spectral-temporal dual view graph convolutional networks: A deep learning framework for dynamic bipartite graphs
abstract: Dynamic bipartite graphs (DBGs) are widely used in real-world scenarios, where representation learning is particularly challenging due to the heterogeneity of node types and the temporal evolution of interactions. A key difficulty lies in jointly capturing non-stationary micro-level preference dynamics and macro-level stable structural evolution. Existing methods typically focus on either temporal dependency modeling or structural pattern extraction. For instance, recurrent or attention-based temporal models struggle to capture abrupt, short-term preference shifts, while spectral or structure-oriented approaches emphasize long-term regularities but overlook fine-grained dynamic variations. This imbalance becomes especially pronounced in scenarios with sparse interactions or sudden behavioral changes. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a spectral-temporal dual-view framework, ST-DYB, for DBG representation learning. By explicitly decoupling macro-level structural evolution and micro-level preference dynamics, the model captures complementary heterogeneous patterns from two perspectives. A cross-view adaptive fusion mechanism further integrates these representations, enabling effective modeling of both implicit preference dependencies and temporal dynamics. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that ST-DYB consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in dynamic link prediction and node classification tasks, validating the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed dual-view modeling paradigm. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Sleep regulation as a function of boredom proneness
abstract: Boredom proneness has been cast as a challenge of self-regulatory control such that the highly boredom prone struggle to launch into action despite the desire to do so. This has typically been explored in the context of cognitive and affective dysregulation. Here, in two samples ( n = 256 and 309), we explored the relation between trait boredom proneness and sleep regulation. In both samples, higher boredom proneness was associated with poor sleep quality. In step-wise hierarchical regressions, boredom proneness reliably predicted poor sleep quality, but was only a significant predictor of bedtime procrastination in Sample #2. In our second sample, boredom proneness also predicted poor sleep hygiene. In that sample, we used mediation analyses to explore the role of rumination in the relation between both state and trait boredom (as predictors) and sleep quality and hygiene (as outcome variables). Results showed that the tendency to ruminate acted only as a partial mediator in these relations. Results are discussed in the broader context of self-regulatory models of state and trait boredom. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Personality, resilience, and educational recovery after disaster: A 12-month longitudinal analysis of mediation and cross-lagged associations
abstract: Individual differences in personality may shape educational adaptation following natural disasters. This 12-month longitudinal study examined Big Five personality traits, academic resilience, and four adaptation outcomes among 884 Turkish university students following the February 2023 earthquake. Latent growth curve models indicated that conscientiousness (β = 0.34) and emotional stability (β = 0.28) showed the strongest associations with adaptation trajectories. Academic resilience accounted for approximately 32–38% of these associations, although concurrent T1 assessment of personality and resilience precludes causal interpretation of the indirect effects. Confirmatory factor analyses and the Fornell–Larcker criterion supported the empirical distinctiveness of personality and academic resilience. Cross-lagged analyses showed prospective associations between resilience and subsequent adaptation across academic performance, online learning adaptation, psychological well-being, and life satisfaction, with resilience-to-adaptation paths generally stronger and more consistent than reverse paths. These associations should be interpreted cautiously because traditional CLPMs do not separate within- and between-person variance. A robustness analysis using verified pre-earthquake GPA records ( n = 648) indicated that the principal personality associations with academic recovery persisted when performance was modeled relative to pre-earthquake achievement. Person-centered analyses supported three prototypical trajectories: Resilient Adapters (63.7%), Gradual Improvers (26.7%), and Struggling Students (9.6%). The findings are organized using the Dynamic Personality–Resilience–Adaptation framework as a heuristic, educationally specific extension of existing personality-adaptation accounts rather than as an independently validated theory. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: An enquiry into noise-induced reactivity shifts in the point-kinetics equations
abstract: Neutron noise analysis within the point-kinetics model is traditionally formulated using linear response theory under small-amplitude sinusoidal perturbations. Although this approach has proven successful in providing a conceptual foundation for neutron noise measurement and diagnostics, it neglects potential non-linear effects that may, for example, modify the stationary state of the reactor. In particular, effective reactivity shifts can be generated by non-linear interactions, which are not captured by the standard linearized treatment. These effects are nevertheless generally assumed to remain negligible under deterministic forcing. This assumption may break down in the presence of stochastic fluctuations. Multiplicative noise can indeed induce systematic drift terms in the effective dynamics, leading to noise-induced reactivity shifts that drive the mean neutron population away from stationarity.The present work investigates the impact of non-linear neutron noise within the point-kinetics model, considering both deterministic and stochastic excitations. The magnitude of the resulting reactivity shifts is quantified, and the respective roles of stochastic forcing and delayed neutron precursors are analysed, providing an assessment of their potential operational significance. © 2026 The Author(s). title: CAST-DRO: Cognition-aware service triage with configurable risk adjustment for resource-constrained AI information services
abstract: AI information service platforms must allocate heterogeneous requests across models, memory, clarification, and human review under joint resource constraints. We develop CAST, a cognition-aware five-action service-triage framework; CAST-ERM learns group-level empirical allocations, and CAST-DRO adds a configurable mean-plus-variability adjustment. Using sequence-grouped train/evaluation splits for 520 LifeSim-derived evaluation requests across 20 repeated splits, CAST-DRO improves over rule-based CAST in quality (0.679 to 0.743), failure rate (0.617 to 0.350), and final satisfaction (46.35 to 56.51), while reducing normalized high-value resource cost (0.087 to 0.081). CAST-ERM reaches quality 0.738, confirming that cognition-group empirical allocation explains most of the average gain. The risk adjustment changes 12 of 104 eligible group-seed action selections and sharply reduces selected-action loss variability in the medium-risk group. A LinUCB comparison warm-started with full-information simulator outcomes reaches quality 0.744 with high-value cost 0.092. A strict budget audit finds zero human, memory, or total-spend violations for all four hard-budget policies across all 20 splits. Resource-price and capacity tests retain a positive quality advantage over CAST, although high-value resource use depends on the bottleneck. In a two-layer stress test, separate mandatory safety-review capacity of 30% reduces latent-reference high-risk miss from 0.788 to 0.230, with 0.035 overflow and 0.398 total escalation. Real-model evaluation on 100 requests and anonymized 1–5 ratings of 50 request–response pairs provide supporting, not production-level, validation. CAST-DRO is best interpreted as an auditable middle-layer allocator after mandatory safety filtering. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Throughput and energy efficiency optimization in cooperative IoT systems with multi-level adaptive vacation and delay strategies
abstract: This paper addresses the trade-off between throughput and energy efficiency in Internet of Things (IoT) systems. A joint multi-level adaptive vacation and delay strategy is proposed for relay assisted Short Packet Communication (SPC). The relay is modeled as operating in four states: transmission, delay, vacation, and idle. Based on this model, closed-form expressions are derived for steady-state queue length, average durations of different system states, average throughput, and energy efficiency. Numerical results show that the benefit of delay strategy is condition dependent and is jointly affected by transmission reliability, system load, and vacation parameters. Research shows that the delay-assisted vacation strategy exhibits stronger robustness in improving throughput than in enhancing energy efficiency, with its performance gains jointly constrained by system load and link reliability. The strategy is only stably effective under high-load and high-reliability scenarios; thus, it should be deployed differently according to specific system conditions and optimization objectives rather than being enabled globally without distinction. Further comparison with multi-vacation strategies in the literature demonstrates that the proposed approach achieves a better balance between throughput energy efficiency over a broad feasible load–reliability range under the evaluated vacation settings. The results provide theoretical guidance for strategy design and parameter optimization in low-power IoT systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Multi-field coupling mechanism of internal fin radial length on two-phase flow in gravity-assisted heat pipe
abstract: Aiming at the unclear regulatory mechanism of internal fin parameters in the evaporation section of gravity-assisted heat pipes (GAHPs) and the insufficient systematic interpretation of the physical nature behind non-monotonic heat transfer behavior in industrial waste heat recovery, this paper establishes a three-dimensional numerical simulation framework coupled with the VOF-Lee-CSF model. Validated by bench-scale experiments, it quantitatively analyzes how circumferential internal fins with radial lengths of 1–8 mm affect in-tube gas-liquid two-phase flow and phase-change heat transfer. The results show that fin radial length exerts bidirectional nonlinear regulation on heat pipe performance through the synergy of vortex evolution and nucleate boiling modulation, with 6 mm as the optimal radial dimension. Under this condition, the heat transfer coefficients of the evaporation and condensation sections rise by 27.27% and 24.67% respectively compared with the 1 mm baseline, and the relative deviation between simulation and experiment stays within 12%–20%. These findings supplement the mechanistic explanation of fin-enhanced heat transfer in gravity-driven two-phase systems and provide quantitative reference for refined heat pipe structural design. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

title: Emotional Stability and within-person Big Five profile dispersion: Evidence for a U-shaped association in adolescents
abstract: Personality traits are typically studied as independent predictors of behavior and well-being, yet less attention has been paid to their configuration within individuals. One approach to capturing this configuration is through intra-subject variance across traits which could reflect the consistency or divergence across the five traits. We operationalized intra-subject variance (Vi) as the within-person variance of direct Big Five scores. Across N = 3785 adolescents (14–17 years), we observed a robust U-shaped association between Emotional Stability (ES) and Vi: profiles were most homogeneous at moderate–high ES and more dispersed at both low and very high ES. This pattern held in polynomial regression models including a significant quadratic term. A robust non-linear (U-shaped) association was found between Emotional Stability and Vi: both low and very high levels were linked to greater dispersion, whereas moderate-to-high levels showed more homogeneous profiles. Other traits showed weaker nonlinear associations, with substantially lower explanatory capacity than Emotional Stability. Emotional Stability emerged as the strongest predictor. Findings suggest that Emotional Stability plays a distinctive role in the internal organization of personality and highlights the relevance of within-person approaches. However, the cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation, and further longitudinal and multi-method research is needed. © 2026 The Authors.

title: The residential food environment, financial constraints, and dietary behavior in Dutch adults with low socioeconomic position: a test of the EnRG framework
abstract: Socioeconomic disparities in dietary behavior are often partially attributed to differences in the residential food environment, yet evidence linking food outlet availability to diet quality remains inconsistent. The Environmental Research framework for weight Gain prevention (EnRG) proposes that environmental influences operate through both a cognitive pathway, mediated by Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) constructs, and a direct, automatic pathway. In this secondary analysis of cross-sectional data from 1033 adults with oversampling of low socioeconomic position, we tested both pathways while additionally examining the role of food insecurity and financial scarcity. Outlet density and distance to nearest fast-food and fruit and vegetable outlet were measured at the postal code level. Dietary behavior, TPB constructs, food insecurity, and financial scarcity were assessed by self-report. Path analyses tested cognitive mediation; subgroup and moderation analyses examined whether food insecurity altered food environment effects. The residential food environment showed minimal associations with dietary consumption: only one of eight direct associations reached significance (fast-food distance and fast-food consumption), and was attenuated in path analyses. All paths from food environment characteristics to TPB constructs were non-significant, indicating no support for cognitive mediation. Food insecurity did not moderate food environment effects. In contrast, food insecurity and financial scarcity were consistently associated with lower fruit and vegetable consumption and poorer diet quality, but not with fast-food consumption. These findings do not support the hypothesis that the residential food environment plays a large role in shaping dietary behavior in low-SEP populations, while financial constraints were more consistently associated with dietary outcomes supporting evaluation of policies aimed at affordability alongside environmental interventions. © 2026 The Authors. title: Spatio-temporal heterogeneity in the built environment-urban vibrancy nexus of rail transit station areas and its implications for targeted management: Case study of Xi’an, China
abstract: Urban Rail Transit (URT) station areas are pivotal nodes for shaping urban structure and fostering Urban Vibrancy. However, the spatio-temporal heterogeneity of the built environment’s impact on urban vibrancy remains underexplored, as existing research predominantly relies on spatially invariant global models, which overlook how the effects of the built environment vary across geographical locations and temporal contexts. To address this gap, this study uses Xi’an Metro Line 2 in China as a case study. Employing multi-source big data, including Location-Based Service (LBS) population heatmaps and Points of Interest (POIs) at a fine-grained grid scale, we utilize a Geographically Weighted Regression (GWR) model to quantitatively deconstruct the spatially varying interactions between built environment’s variables and urban vibrancy across different time periods (morning, noon, and evening).The results first statistically confirm the significant spatial non-stationarity of the built environment’s impacts. Based on this, the study identifies three distinct vibrancy generation archetypes: (1) "endogenous service-oriented" vibrancy, driven by localized built capacity and public services; (2) "exogenous attraction-based" vibrancy, defined by city-level functional synergies and public space quality; and (3) "nodal absorption-oriented" vibrancy, characterized by the efficient absorption of commuter flows through high-density development and functional diversity.These findings empirically challenge the universal applicability of principles within Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) theory. The core contribution of this study, therefore, is its advocacy for a paradigm shift in planning-from a "prescriptive framework" that applies standardized principles to a "diagnostic framework" predicated on the precise identification of local, dominant driving mechanisms. This conclusion provides a solid scientific basis and theoretical guidance for formulating place-based and time-sensitive strategies to enhance station area vibrancy. © 2026 The Authors.

title: AI-enabled cyberbullying detection from a cyber-physical-social-thinking space integration perspective: Theories, technologies, and challenges
abstract: Cyberbullying has emerged as a pervasive threat to digital well-being, evolving into a multidimensional phenomenon that spans multiple interconnected spaces. Despite significant progress in detection techniques, existing approaches predominantly rely on textual analysis, limiting their ability to capture the full spectrum of cyberbullying behaviors and contextual dependencies. To address this limitation, this study presents a systematic review with qualitative synthesis of AI-enabled cyberbullying detection through the lens of Cyber-Physical-Social-Thinking (CPST) space integration. Based on 120 included studies, the review develops three principal outputs. First, it develops a fusion-mechanism taxonomy of AI-enabled cyberbullying detection research across cyber, physical, social, and thinking dimensions, organizing how content, contextual, relational, behavioral, and cognitive information is combined to support more comprehensive and context-aware detection. Second, it establishes a quantitative and descriptive landscape of the reviewed literature across CPST-space coverage, modalities, model families, publication trends, social media platforms, dataset characteristics, and evaluation metrics. Third, it develops a four-level conceptual taxonomy that organizes cyberbullying-related information into observable evidence, latent states, behaviors, and outcomes. Building on this evidence-based output, the study synthesizes a CPST-based conceptual reference architecture that organizes heterogeneous data sources, feature representations, information-fusion strategies, and decision-making processes, while distinguishing the differing empirical maturity of the four spaces. The review further synthesizes state-of-the-art AI technologies, including natural language processing, computer vision, network analysis, affective computing, and multimodal learning, in relation to their roles in cross-space information integration. The synthesis identifies key challenges, including data privacy, bias, and generalization, and highlights research opportunities involving explainable AI, federated learning, and human-in-the-loop systems. The resulting synthesis provides a structured evidence base for understanding existing fusion approaches and guiding future research on cross-space cyberbullying detection. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Adaptive PSO for consensus optimization oriented to trust-consensus inconsistency correction and personalized guidance
abstract: In social network group decision-making (GDM) based on fuzzy preference relations (FPR), trust among decision-makers (DMs) dominates the efficiency of opinion convergence. Traditional particle swarm optimization (PSO) has inherent drawbacks when applied to the consensus reaching process (CRP), and existing research has three limitations: static trust weights lack quantitative correction methods for trust-consensus inconsistency, unified consensus guidance fails to generate differentiated adjustment targets based on preference similarity and dynamic consensus contributions, the personal historical optimum of classical PSO becomes invalid, and undifferentiated global guidance easily traps the algorithm in local optima. This paper adopts PSO instead of other algorithms because of its one-to-one particle-DM correspondence, interpretable updating rules and good compatibility with multi-round CRP iterations. To retain PSO’s strengths and address the local optimum problem, a three module collaborative optimization framework is proposed, including the trust-consensus inconsistency correction mechanism, consensus-oriented adaptive weighted aggregation mechanism, and reconstructed improved PSO. The first module identifies inconsistent trust via bidirectional ranking of trust degrees and consensus levels to ensure trust weights match the consensus reliability of DMs. The second module constructs a dual aggregation structure driven by similarity and consensus to produce exclusive personalized guiding opinions for each DM. The third module reconstructs the PSO updating paradigm and adopts consensus progress adaptive inertia weights and learning factors to balance global exploration. The three modules operate in closed-loop collaboration: calibrating trust weights, generating customized guidance, and adaptively updating preferences. Experimental results indicate that the proposed framework achieves faster consensus convergence and lower adjustment costs under the tested settings, providing a promising intelligent solution for complex decision-making tasks in social network analysis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Mapping potential recurring risk of wildfire across Canada using artificial intelligence: Implications for human populations and tree species
abstract: In response to the escalating global concern over increasing wildfire events and their extensive socioecological consequences, it is crucial to develop efficient and practical methods for reliably identifying high-risk wildfire zones to guide large-scale environmental management. Wildfire susceptibility assessment is one of the basic critical approaches to wildfire risk management. In the present study, numerous deep learning architectures—including bidirectional recurrent neural network, encoder-decoder bidirectional recurrent neural network, deep neural network, recurrent neural network and long short-term memory—are applied to map wildfire susceptibility across Canada, with performance benchmarked against a comparatively low-complexity categorical boosting. Initially, a spatial database comprising 4,240 historically large wildfire occurrence locations across Canada from 2014 to 2023 was compiled. Next, we calculated the statistical Frequency and Likelihood of occurrence at 10,000 well-distributed points across Canada. Characteristics of 13 candidate wildfire-related hydrogeoclimatic parameters were extracted at the same points; feature selection retained 11 for Frequency and 10 for Likelihood as model inputs. Subsequently, potential recurring hazard and risk indices across Canada were calculated. To identify the effective predictor variables and optimal combinations, Boruta and classification and regression tree algorithms were used. Finally, the performance of models was evaluated using the error metrics including root mean squared error, mean absolute error and coefficient of determination. Results revealed that the bidirectional recurrent neural network gave the best value on five of the six test-set metrics across Frequency and Likelihood, while categorical boosting was weakest on five of six. According to the SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis, wind speed, climatic water deficit, shortwave radiation and potential evapotranspiration were the most influential predictors of large wildfire occurrence; higher climatic water deficit, shortwave radiation and potential evapotranspiration raised model predictions, whereas higher wind speed lowered them, consistent with its negative correlation with both targets. In terms of exposure to human populations, the metropolitan regions of Yellowknife, southwestern British Columbia, Winnipeg and Calgary were identified as facing the highest recurring risk of future wildfire impact. Regarding tree species, black spruce and jack pine were the tree species most frequently occurring in Canada’s high wildfire-risk regions. The study underscores the efficacy of these integrated models in tackling the complexities of wildfire prediction, offering significant potential for enhancing wildfire mapping, prevention and mitigation strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
