title: IGPC: Multi-domain multimodal fake news detection via Info-Gini Weight Adaptation and Prototypical Multi-level Contrastive Learning
abstract: Multi-domain multimodal fake news detection requires models to integrate textual and visual evidence while generalizing across diverse domains. Existing methods still struggle with multi-level data imbalance, weak class geometry in data-scarce domains, and transfer to held-out target domains. We propose Info-Gini Weight Adaptation and Prototypical Multi-level Contrastive Learning (IGPC), a method that decomposes imbalance into inter-domain, intra-domain, and global levels, and converts dataset statistics into stable training weights. It then learns a domain–label prototype space and applies multi-level contrastive learning to enforce compact intra-class clusters and clear inter-class margins. Finally, a prototype-based transfer enhancement, including a global class-prototype bridge and prediction fusion, improves robustness on held-out target domains without introducing extra loss terms. Experiments on Weibo (7723 experimental samples), Weibo-21,(6156 experimental samples), and FineFake (16,796 experimental samples) show that IGPC outperforms the strongest directly reproduced baseline by 1.06%, 1.48%, and 1.01% in overall F1 score, respectively. It also shows consistent gains in held-out target-domain evaluation on Weibo and Weibo-21 and visible class separation in the learned representations These results indicate that explicitly modeling multi-level imbalance and prototype geometry is effective for robust multi-domain multimodal fake news detection under domain shift. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Overcoming Digital Twin Blindness: An event-triggered edge–cloud architecture using quantized TinyML
abstract: Maintaining synchronization between physical assets and their Digital Twin (DT) typically requires continuous data transmission, which becomes challenging in bandwidth- and energy-constrained Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments. Continuous data transfer introduces a trade-off between update frequency, state accuracy, and communication overhead. To address this challenge, an edge–cloud cooperative architecture is proposed for event-triggered DT synchronization using a quantized Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) model. An ultra-lightweight INT8-quantized separable convolutional autoencoder is deployed at the edge. This model performs on-device sensor fusion and triggers synchronization when significant deviations in the physical state are detected. During periods without edge transmissions, a cloud-hosted forecasting model predicts and maintains the DT state. The proposed approach is evaluated using the SKAB, CMAPSS, and MNIST datasets. Micro-benchmark results show that the TinyML gatekeeper is compressed to 10.77 KB and consumes only 0.0058 mJ per inference, resulting in an 11.9 times reduction in memory footprint and a 45 times improvement in Age of Information compared to conventional synchronization methods. Cloud-side experiments further show that predictive state reconstruction preserves DT fidelity while reducing communication overhead by more than 85%. End-to-end evaluations show that the proposed framework significantly extends the Pareto frontier of DT synchronization. The system operates at a low bandwidth utilization of approximately 54.2%, reduces univariate synchronization error by over 71%, and achieves a perfect synchronization for multivariate anomaly tracking with RMSE of zero for 8-dimensional data. Overall, the framework mitigates the Digital Twin Blindness problem inherent in static polling approaches and provides a scalable synchronization strategy for next-generation IIoT systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Community Flood Perceptions in the Context of Flood Risk and Flood Hazard Indicators
abstract: Floods have and continue to cause severe damage to property and loss of life globally and in the US. The perceived risk of flooding, defined as an individual’s subjective assessment of the likelihood and severity of a flood event, can influence their preparedness and response to flooding and proposed mitigation strategies. The current study investigated individuals’ flood risk perception using data from 700 responses to a telephone survey conducted in Harris County, Texas (Houston). Results indicated that individuals lack situational awareness (i.e., ability to perceive, understand, and effectively respond) of their flood risk but are well-informed and have opinions regarding proposed mitigation alternatives. The study correlated flood risk perception to select sociodemographic variables and demonstrated more corresponding perceptions of risk among older White and Asian communities. The study additionally pointed to the complexity of flood risk assessment and the lack of effective communication methods and tools to better inform individuals and communities. The study used data on flood hazard indicators such as past flooding and high-water marks after a flood to assess objective risks; it is proposed that such a framework presents an opportunity for more readily communicating flood risks to individuals and communities. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Causal-inspired knowledge tracing via class-conditioned latent representation learning
abstract: Knowledge Tracing (KT) plays a foundational role in smart education by modeling students’ evolving knowledge states from historical learning interactions. Existing deep KT architectures predominantly mine statistical correlations from individual interaction sequences, neglecting group-level educational contexts (e.g., class). Such contextual heterogeneity forces models to rely on spurious correlations, leading to error next-response predictions. Guided by advanced educational philosophies, causality offers a principled lens to characterize the underlying data-generating process of student learning. Nevertheless, comprehensive contextual signals are inherently complex and largely latent. To bridge this gap, we propose CLR4KT, a causal-inspired plug-in framework for Class-Conditioned Latent Representation Learning in KT. CLR4KT introduces an identifiable Variational Autoencoder (iVAE) style architecture to capture the data-generating mechanism, leveraging class-level contextual information as an observed group-level conditional signal to assist in identifying and resolving the complex, latent context representations. By conditioning both the latent prior and the variational posterior on class labels, CLR4KT learns class-conditioned latent representations. These enhanced latent states are seamlessly integrated into mainstream KT backbones via temporal modeling. Extensive experiments across four benchmark datasets demonstrate that CLR4KT consistently boosts predictive capability. Ablation and visualization analyses confirm the effectiveness of class-conditioned latent representation learning module of our method. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Psy-DMTL: Psychology-guided dynamic multi-task learning for LLM-based personality detection
abstract: Personality detection aims to infer individuals’ psychological traits from user-generated text and has broad applications in user profiling, personalized services, and human–computer interaction. Recent LLM-based methods have shown strong potential for this task by providing rich semantic representations. However, most existing methods still face three limitations: coarse-grained long-history encoding may dilute sparse personality cues, shared user representations may entangle heterogeneous evidence across personality dimensions, and cross-dimension dependencies are often modeled implicitly without psychology-inspired structural guidance. To address these issues, we propose Psy-DMTL, a psychology-guided dynamic multi-task learning framework for LLM-based personality detection. Psy-DMTL first encodes posts independently with a frozen LLM and uses a gated hierarchical context encoder to capture user-level dependencies while preserving fine-grained cues. It then introduces orthogonal dimension-attention pooling to extract dimension-specific representations for different MBTI dimensions. Finally, a psychology-guided dynamic modulation decoder models directional cross-dimension interactions through FiLM-based feature modulation. Experiments on the Kaggle and Pandora benchmarks show that Psy-DMTL achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of average Macro-F1 on both datasets. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for long-history personality detection. Supplementary experiments on the Italian Personal-ITY dataset further support the model's competitive performance. Our model is publicly available at https://github.com/qaswzh/Psy-DMTL. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and nonlinear drivers of MSW carbon emissions from the perspective of consumption and industrial structure upgrading: An explainable machine learning approach
abstract: Municipal solid waste (MSW) carbon emissions pose a major challenge to urban sustainable development, yet nonlinear drivers across different urban development contexts remain insufficiently understood. Based on consumption upgrading and industrial structure upgrading, this study classifies 284 prefecture-level and above cities in China into four development types, estimates MSW carbon emissions from treatment processes during 2010–2023, and constructs an XGBoost–SHAP model to identify key drivers, nonlinear thresholds, and interaction contributions. The results show that MSW carbon emissions followed an overall trajectory of “growth–decline–slight rebound,” with comprehensive upgrading cities, despite being the smallest group, maintaining the highest long-term emission levels. Urban construction scale and population size are identified as core drivers, whereas waste treatment structure upgrading shows a negative contribution. Comprehensive upgrading cities are characterized by joint drivers related to scale agglomeration, economic activity, and governance capacity; household consumption is a more prominent driver in consumption-led upgrading cities; environmental sanitation infrastructure emerges as a more prominent driver in industry-led upgrading cities; and scale-related factors remain the primary drivers in foundational cities. From the combined perspective of demand-side consumption changes and supply-side industrial structure adjustment, this study reveals heterogeneous drivers of MSW carbon emissions and provides insights for city-type-specific low-carbon MSW governance strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Regulating metallurgical continuity and fracture-path selection through interfacial coupling in multi-material additive manufacturing
abstract: The growing demand for multifunctional components requires structural and functional properties to be spatially tailored within a single architecture, a capability difficult to achieve using monolithic materials. Multi-material additive manufacturing offers a promising solution, yet its implementation is constrained by the difficulty of forming reliable interfaces between dissimilar alloys. Here, we reveal how interfacial melt-pool coupling governs interface evolution and fracture-path selection in 316L stainless steel/CuSn10 multi-material architectures fabricated by multi-material laser powder bed fusion. Four programmed coupling conditions were produced by varying the cross-boundary scan extension and were operationally classified as decoupled, partially coupled, stably coupled, and over-coupled according to the resulting interfacial morphologies. Stable coupling transformed the sharp and discontinuous boundary into a continuous, chemically heterogeneous transition zone with broadened Fe/Cu redistribution, refined interfacial grains, and locally identified BCC α-Fe within the Cu-rich matrix. This transition suppressed boundary-dominated failure and redirected fracture across both constituent materials, increasing the ultimate tensile strength by 61.7%, from 161.1 to 260.5 MPa, although the elongation decreased from 8.33% to 5.23%, indicating a strength–ductility trade-off. Insufficient coupling preserved lack-of-fusion defects, whereas over-coupling generated pore-bearing Cu-rich regions and shifted failure to a pore-assisted path. Time-resolved synchrotron X-ray imaging further revealed keyhole fluctuation, partial collapse, and pore retention as a plausible pore-formation pathway. Application-oriented multi-material demonstrators with complex geometries were successfully fabricated, supporting the geometric implementation of interface-controlled MM-LPBF. These findings establish a coupling-dependent interface-control principle for balancing metallurgical continuity against defect-assisted damage in multi-material additive manufacturing. © 2026 The Authors. title: Sociotechnical imaginaries and acceptance of artificial intelligence in education: A longitudinal social media analysis
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a site of public debate on social media concerning the future of education, raising broader societal questions about human behavior, judgment, and accountability. However, how educational AI is publicly interpreted and contested in everyday digital discourse is still underexplored. Addressing this gap, this study examines how AI in education is publicly discoursed through a longitudinal mixed-methods analysis of user comments responding to TED Talk videos on YouTube that circulate influential public narratives about technological and educational futures between December 2022 and November 2025. The study traces changing public orientations towards educational AI and the future visions underpinning them. Multilingual sentiment analysis reveals a fluctuating three-year trajectory, with sentiment becoming more positive in the middle period before negative sentiment rose again in 2025. Thematic analysis of the public discourse further identifies three sociotechnical imaginaries through which commenters articulate competing visions of educational futures: (1) human-centered education in an age of cognitive displacement, where concerns focus on preserving critical thinking and human judgment; (2) educational transformation through literacy, governance, and accountability; and (3) teachers as mediators of competing AI-powered educational futures. The study contributes to existing scholarship by demonstrating how acceptance and resistance toward AI in education are socially and discursively constructed through competing visions of desirable educational futures in digital public spaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Identifying key regions in spatial networks via regular hexagonal grids
abstract: Spatially embedded complex systems are often disrupted at the regional level rather than by isolated node or edge failures, making key region identification a challenging combinatorial problem. Existing partition-based approaches either suffer from overlap and coverage trade-offs with circular regions or rely on square grids that may inadequately capture spatial influence and accessibility in real-world settings. We adopt a non-overlapping regular hexagonal grid and propose Key Region Identification with Graph Neural Networks using Regular Hexagonal Grids (KRIG-H). The framework treats each grid cell as a region node and constructs a region graph through geometric mapping between original edges and grid cells. Trained on synthetic spatial networks, KRIG-H generalizes to unseen real-world networks. Using the fraction of removed regions as a normalized evaluation scale, we compare KRIG-H with six region-centrality baselines under both hexagonal and square decompositions, with random region removal as a control. On real-world networks, KRIG-H reduces AUC by 24.88 % relative to its square counterpart, while hexagonal partitioning lowers the overall average AUC across methods by 21.77 %. Results on synthetic and real infrastructure and road networks show that KRIG-H achieves effective, robust, and transferable region-based vulnerability analysis with limited additional computational cost. © 2026

title: Mass analysis of supercritical nitrous oxide and helium in a recompression Brayton cycle utilizing in-situ resources for lunar base energy system
abstract: The Moon is the only natural satellite of the Earth and also the closest celestial body to the Earth. The Moon is regarded as an outpost of deep space exploration. The construction of lunar base infrastructure, polar exploration, and rovers constitutes the first step for humans to venture into the Moon. In the process of constructing a lunar base, it is essential to establish an energy system that can fully utilize local resources. This system will reduce the weight of materials transported from Earth and ultimately solve the energy shortage problem on the Moon. A recompression Brayton cycle that utilizes in-situ resources, with supercritical nitrous oxide and helium as the working media, and evaluates the mass of the energy system. A small modular reactor is applied to predict the minimum-mass reactor suitable for the given cycle conditions. The system mass and specific mass optimization explored the trade-offs among the reactor, radiation shield, Brayton cycle unit, recuperator, and radiator to obtain the minimum mass of the lunar base energy system. The results indicate that the specific mass of the energy system is 17.37 kg∙kWe−1. In addition, it is found that, by utilizing in-situ lunar base resources, the mass and volume of the radiation shield for the reactor can be reduced by 3.55% and 14.20%, respectively. In conclusion, the proposed energy system scheme offers several advantages, including light weight, high efficiency, and continuous electricity supply, for application in lunar bases. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Collaborative multi-instance feature aggregation for visual privacy protection
abstract: The rapid advancement of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) has dramatically shaped numerous domains of modern society. With the increasing emphasis on high-quality and personalized data, safeguarding visual privacy and preventing information leakage have become urgent research priorities. Traditional privacy-preserving strategies predominantly rely on isolated instance-level manipulations, such as artificial noise injection or pixel-level obfuscation, to achieve de-identification. Yet, these independent sample-level approaches inevitably face an inherent trade-off: slight alterations provide inadequate protection, whereas aggressive modifications severely distort task-relevant semantics and compromise downstream accuracy. To overcome this dilemma, we introduce a novel visual privacy protection framework driven by multi-instance feature-level aggregation. Unlike conventional methods that perturb a single isolated instance, our approach constructs anonymized representations by collaboratively aggregating identity-discriminative feature fragments drawn from multiple data instances. Instead of relying on external noise to conceal identity, this collaborative aggregation synthesizes protected data, effectively weakening the deterministic link between the original identity and the visual representation. Comprehensive experiments on diverse visual identity recognition benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed framework delivers superior results, achieving both robust perceptual anonymization and high downstream task utility compared with prior state-of-the-art techniques. © 2026

title: Aesthetic perception is an embodied experience
abstract: For at least the past century, philosophers have proposed a role for the human body in aesthetic perception. Scholars from experimental psychology, empirical aesthetics and human neuroscience joined in this endeavour in earnest at the start of the 21st century, following on from the establishment of neuroaesthetics as a formal scientific discipline as well as neuroscientific discoveries advancing our understanding of action–perception coupling in the human brain. The expansion of embodied accounts of aesthetic perception was most pronounced following the proliferation of research working directly with the performing arts (specifically dance), as such studies focus on the body as both subject and object, performer and observer. This piece charts the short history of scholarly thinking on aesthetic perception as an embodied experience and speculates on what the future of this line of inquiry might hold, especially given the increased involvement of disembodied AI tools in artistic practices and aesthetic experiences. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Semi-Asynchronous Efficient Hierarchical Federated Learning for heterogeneous resources
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of cloud–edge–device collaborative computing, Hierarchical Federated Learning (HFL) has become a promising paradigm for large-scale distributed model training. However, existing HFL systems still struggle with device heterogeneity, Non-IID data distributions, and substantial communication overhead, leading to inefficient training and unstable convergence. To overcome these limitations, we propose SAEHFL, a Semi-Asynchronous Efficient Hierarchical Federated Learning framework designed for heterogeneous environments. SAEHFL leverages a heterogeneity-aware device grouping strategy that clusters devices based on computational capability and data distribution, reducing intra-group imbalance and mitigating Non-IID-induced bias. A circular ring-sequential aggregation mechanism further restructures device–edge communication, reducing communication overhead and improving bandwidth utilization. At the edge–cloud level, a hybrid synchronization strategy enables synchronous group updates while incorporating semi-asynchronous buffered aggregation, reducing waiting time and reducing global waiting time while maintaining stable convergence behavior. Extensive experiments on MNIST, FEMNIST, and CIFAR10 show that SAEHFL achieves a favorable time–accuracy trade-off. At the target accuracy for each dataset, SAEHFL reduces the average training time by 55.61%, 56.91%, 63.45%, 62.99%, and 61.54% compared with SFedAvg, SAFedAvg, Random, FedProx, and HFLCHFL. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of SAEHFL in enabling efficient and communication-aware hierarchical federated learning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Robust optimization of energy consumption and compliance risk for indirect electric-heating drying of particle-laden water in southern Xinjiang
abstract: For high-sediment agricultural irrigation water-conveyance conditions in southern Xinjiang, the key drying process parameters of oven-drying-based sediment monitoring equipment have not yet been systematically optimized, which has constrained the measurement accuracy and field applicability of such equipment under complex sediment-laden conditions. Here, we develop a multi-objective framework that balances relative specific energy consumption against the probability of meeting a 0.5% residual-moisture criterion. Heating power, heating time, water-sediment mixture mass and sediment concentration were varied using a Box-Behnken design. Both response-surface models achieved R2 > 0.98. Sediment concentration exerted the strongest influence on residual moisture content and emerged as a key factor linking energy consumption with compliance risk. We then coupled support vector regression, calibrated logistic classification and Monte Carlo chance-constrained Pareto analysis to identify minimum-energy, minimum-risk and compromise knee-point regions. Independent validation experiments subsequently evaluated these regions. The minimum-risk region near 1492 W, 50 min and 400 g met the criterion at sediment concentrations of 1.0% and 17.5%. The knee-point region near 1079 W, 50 min and 400 g met the criterion at 15.0% and 16.5%, but marginally exceeded it at 3.5% (0.52489%). By contrast, the minimum-energy region near 1014 W, 50 min and 400 g failed the criterion at both tested concentrations. Thus, low-energy operation cannot be assumed to preserve compliance; operating conditions must instead reflect an explicit trade-off between energy use and compliance risk. This framework provides an experimentally informed basis for selecting operating conditions in automated gravimetric monitoring of high-sediment irrigation water. Copyright © 2026. title: Chemical proximity governs open-world infrared identification of microplastics using dual-evidence calibration
abstract: Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) classifiers can assign familiar polymer labels to spectra outside their training domain. We developed SPARC-FTIR to couple class-conditional conformal prediction with a calibrated distance gate for binary high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and polypropylene (PP) identification with rejection. Five spectral views were combined in a training-derived principal-component representation. The two gates distinguished label-set uncertainty from departure from the known feature domain and produced four evidence states. After auditing sample identifiers, 776 spectra were retained from an open ATR-FTIR collection; 689 HDPE/PP spectra supported training, calibration and testing, while 87 non-target spectra were withheld. On the primary test partition, closed-set balanced accuracy was 100%, 124 of 139 known spectra were accepted correctly, and 37 of 87 unknown spectra were rejected. Rejection was 29.4% for low-density polyethylene, 33.3% for mixtures and 100% for the 14 remaining unknown spectra. Across 30 group-preserving splits, mean known acceptance and unknown rejection were 92.8% and 36.3%, respectively. Matched spectral-library comparisons showed different subgroup trade-offs in acceptance and rejection. Frozen-model evaluation on two additional libraries showed acquisition-dependent acceptance and rejection. The calibrated decision states provide an auditable basis for reviewing spectra within a declared HDPE/PP scope; overlapping polyolefin spectra and cross-library transfer remain the principal constraints. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: STGCM: Sign-aware triple graph collaborative model for recommendation
abstract: Recommendation systems, as a core technology for mitigating information overload, play a crucial role across many fields. In recent years, graph neural networks (GNNs) have significantly improved recommendation performance by modeling user-item interactions as a graph structure. However, most existing sign-aware methods directly partition the user-item interaction graph into separate positive and negative graphs for modeling. While this local modeling approach can distinguish different feedback types, it disrupts the global topology of the original graph. This impairment exacerbates data sparsity and weakens the propagation of signed information. To address this, we propose STGCM, a Sign-aware Triple Graph Collaborative Model for Recommendation. STGCM employs a multi-perspective graph convolution embedding learning framework, which preserves the complete topology of the original graph while thoroughly excavating local preference features from both positive and negative feedback. Building on this, a two-stage hierarchical attention fusion mechanism is designed to achieve a global-information-supplemented, synergistic fusion of multiple perspectives, thereby enhancing the model's information complementarity capability. The experimental results provide compelling evidence that STGCM outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across three real-world datasets. The source code is publicly accessible at https://github.com/Dongqin-Wang/STGCM. © 2026

title: A comprehensive survey on multimodal sentiment analysis: Approaches, challenges and open issues
abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) aims to extract affective knowledge from various types of input media, including image, audio, and text. Given the significant impact of leveraging the vast amount of multimodal data from social networks and of fusing and integrating information extracted from different modalities on enhancing the validity and accuracy of the sentiment analysis process, MSA has become an important, fascinating, and widespread topic. The MSA methods presented in the literature exploit the latest advances in deep learning and transformers for multimodal feature extraction, fusion, classification, and polarity identification to enhance efficiency and performance. Despite various research having been conducted and recent articles presented with diverse approaches for MSA, the lack of a comprehensive study that examines several aspects of the problem addressed in these studies, including approaches, paradigms, methods, tools, and techniques, and evaluates them by considering related issues such as the datasets and benchmarks used, criteria and parameters for measuring results, and the extent to which intermediate and final objectives are addressed and achieved, is noticeable. In this paper, MSA and its various processes and phases are addressed within a comprehensive study framework. In this regard, techniques, tools, and datasets for feature extraction, multimodal fusion, and sentiment classification are thoroughly reviewed, categorized, summarized, compared, and evaluated, and for better comparison, some evaluation factors are proposed at each stage. Furthermore, a comprehensive overview of existing challenges, open research topics, and future research directions is provided along with a set of guidelines for conducting future studies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Early Termination Provisions in Public–Private Partnerships: Synthesizing Institutional Guidance into Process-Based Benchmarks
abstract: Early termination provisions (ETPs) are critical risk management mechanisms in public–private partnership (PPP) contracts, defining the conditions, processes, and consequences under which contracts may be terminated before their expiry. While leading institutional guidance documents provide extensive and authoritative treatment of ETPs, their coverage is dispersed across different mandates, drafting styles, and levels of procedural detail, making it difficult to extract a coherent, operational benchmark directly from the guidance. The objective of this study is to systematically synthesize institutional PPP guidance into a unified, process-based benchmark for early termination. Using inductive qualitative content analysis methodology, the study examines guidance issued by five widely recognized institutions: the World Bank, the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL), the European PPP Expertise Centre (EPEC), the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), and the US Federal Highway Administration (FHWA). The analysis identifies five principal ETP categories—private partner default, contracting authority default, voluntary termination, force majeure (FM), and uninsurability—and, where applicable, drives analytically grounded subcategories. These findings are translated into five benchmark flowcharts that operationalize early termination as a sequenced process structured around circumstances, procedures, and consequences. The results demonstrate that, despite differences in articulation and drafting depth, institutional guidance reflects a shared conceptual framework in which early termination is an exceptional outcome following the failure of cure, adaptation, or policy intervention mechanisms. The resulting benchmarks provide a practical reference for institutions to design, assess, and align ETP regimes in PPP contracts, supporting clearer risk allocation, improved governance, and more defensible termination practices. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Complexity and Economic Value of Care Provided in Humanitarian Relief Clinics for Displaced Persons at the Mexico-US Border, 2020-2022
abstract: Objectives Millions of people rely on humanitarian organizations for medical care. We characterized the complexity and economic value of care provided by a humanitarian relief organization for displaced persons at the Mexico-US border. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study of clinical encounters by a humanitarian relief organization in Tamaulipas, México, near US ports of entry from 2020 to 2022. We used records from a sample of medical encounters to assign ICD-10 and Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) billing codes for each encounter, procedure, or service. We derived an estimate of economic value for these encounters in 2020 US dollars by mapping the CPT billing codes to Medicaid reimbursement rates in Texas, and we compared these with a locally derived estimate using a fee schedule from the Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social. We stratified economic value estimates by demographics, site of care, and type of medical service. Results From 23 339 clinical encounters representing 13 963 unique patients (59.5% female; median age 30 years), the most common codes were office visits: CPT 99202 (“office visit with a history”) comprised 43.9% of all encounters. The most common procedure was obstetric ultrasound, present in 341 (1.5%) of all clinical encounters. The value of care was $39.18 per encounter, which was within 5% of the locally derived estimate. Evaluation and management services accounted for 95.4% of the value. Conclusion This approach of assigning diagnosis and billing codes to clinical encounters provides an estimate for the value and complexity of clinical services provided by humanitarian relief organizations at the México-US border. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Consequence-driven active defense resource allocation for chemical park cyber-physical systems
abstract: With the increasing deployment of Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), the risk landscape in chemical industrial parks has progressively shifted from the physical domain to the cyber domain. This paradigm shift enables cyber adversaries to manipulate physical processes, thereby inducing catastrophic accidents. Traditional Industrial Control Systems (ICS) defense methods often isolate cyber vulnerability analysis from physical consequence analysis, failing to address this cross-domain threat. To bridge this gap, a hierarchical risk transmission model is established based on a three-layer architecture of chemical park CPS, spanning the information, cyber-physical, and physical layers. Attack graphs are utilized to quantify cross-layer attack paths, and Bayesian networks are employed to infer the severity of physical consequences. A coupling index is proposed to prioritize node defense resources under limited budgets. Furthermore, an attack-defense game model solved by a greedy algorithm is developed to realize a honeypot deployment scheme. The framework is validated using both a real cascaded water tank experimental platform and the non-linear Tennessee Eastman Process benchmark. Results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively intercepts unknown attacks originating from the information layer, thereby preventing catastrophic physical intrusions. Copyright © 2026. title: Impact of parvalbumin interneuron inhibition during adolescence on social behaviors
abstract: Adolescence is an important period for the maturation of prefrontal circuits and the complex behaviors it regulates, including social interactions. A major component of this developmental process is the maturation of parvalbumin-expressing (PV) interneurons, which regulate excitation-inhibition balance and contribute to the refinement of cortical networks. Although PV neurons have been implicated in social behaviors, their role during adolescence in shaping social behavior development remains unclear. To address this question, we chemogenetically inhibited prefrontal PV interneurons in male and female mice during either adolescence or adulthood and assessed long-term changes in PV network characteristics and social behavior. Adolescent PV inhibition produced persistent reductions in detectable PV neurons and increased PNN labeling surrounding PV cells, as well as reduced social motivation in males following prolonged food deprivation. In contrast, adult inhibition did not alter detectable PV neurons or PNN association, but reduced cFos expression in PV-targeted cells in the prelimbic cortex in response to a social interaction and produced changes in female social interaction patterns and sex-dependent changes in anxiety-like behavior. These findings suggest that PV interneuron activity contributes to the regulation of prefrontal inhibitory circuitry and social behavior, with disruption during adolescence producing lasting changes in PV network characteristics and social motivation. © 2026 The Authors

title: Do workers value formal jobs? Evidence from Brazil
abstract: Informal employment, and the resulting lack of social insurance coverage, remains widespread in low- and middle-income countries. This paper contributes to the debate on the determinants of informality by estimating workers’ willingness to pay (WTP) for a formal job using a sample of 4997 Brazilian dependent workers. On average, workers are willing to forgo 15.1% of their wages for a signed work card, with higher WTP among formal and highly educated workers. Predicted eligibility for non-contributory social assistance lowers WTP, while predicted eligibility for contributory social insurance increases it. A simple calculation suggests that workers’ WTP may not fully offset employer contributions if passed on through lower wages. Providing additional information on formality raises WTP, but mainly among those already having a higher valuation of formality. © 2026 The Author

title: Benefit-principle accounting of CO₂ emissions in the global textile and clothing value chain
abstract: Existing emission accounting frameworks assign CO₂ responsibility to producers or final consumers but do not identify factor-provider beneficiaries within bilateral trade flows. This study extends benefit-principle emissions (BPE) accounting by introducing a trade-pattern decomposition for the global textile and clothing (T&C) value chain. Using the multi-regional input-output table, the framework distinguishes producers, factor providers, final producers, and consumers, and separates final-goods, intermediate, and global value chain (GVC) trade. Consumer economies retain the largest single shares of their own T&C BPE. Developed-economy providers generally receive BPE above the consumption-based emissions (CBE) in their economies, while production-linked developing providers fall below. Bangladesh, the world's second-largest garment exporter, accounts for only 0.13% of EU-27 consumer T&C BPE despite its assembly role. Foreign factor-provider attribution rises in GVC-related trade, where assembly economies face higher CO₂ per dollar of factor-provider value added than in direct final-goods trade. Although final demand targets T&C products, emitted BPE concentrates in electricity, gas, and water, separating the consumer product from the emitting sector. Aggregate BPE-CBE ratios sit near parity for Bangladesh and selected developing-country pairs, while GVC-specific BPE exceeds CBE in most bilateral pairs. Bangladesh's economy-wide BPE exceeds its territorial emissions by 19%, showing that sectoral value capture and economy-wide balances can classify the same economy differently. Border carbon instruments based only on emission location or final-product origin can place compliance costs on actors capturing limited factor-provider benefit. Benefit-principle metrics give an additional diagnostic for border adjustment design, product-level disclosure, revenue recycling, and climate finance allocation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Effect of walking slope on cognitive performance. Electrophysiological evidence of dual-task interference
abstract: The neural basis of cognitive–motor dual-tasking (CMDT), which involves the simultaneous performance of motor and cognitive tasks, has received increasing attention. However, the electrophysiological impact of walking complexity on concurrent cognitive performance remains unclear. This study examined how walking slope modulates cognitive performance and event-related potentials during a visuomotor discrimination task requiring a simple manual keypress response to target stimuli while walking on a treadmill. Twenty healthy adults (20–36 years) completed the task under three slope conditions (downhill −11%, flat 0%, uphill +11%) while electroencephalogram was recorded. Behavioral results showed preserved accuracy across conditions, with slower response times during downhill walking relative to uphill walking. Early sensory processing was strongly affected by locomotor complexity: both uphill and downhill walking elicited larger P1 amplitudes and reduced N1 amplitudes relative to flat walking. In contrast, late cognitive processing indexed by the P3 was largely preserved, although the differential P3 was selectively reduced during uphill walking, suggesting selective redistribution of resources under the highest energetic and cognitive load, consistent with a possible capacity-sharing account. Uphill walking was perceived as the most physically and cognitively demanding condition, while the lowest mean state-anxiety score was observed after uphill walking. Overall, these findings indicate that locomotor complexity selectively modulates early sensory and attentional processing during CMDT, while higher-order decision processes appear relatively preserved. The results are consistent with models of flexible resource allocation and provide insights relevant to the design of motor–cognitive training and rehabilitation protocols. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Comparing neural signatures of risky decision-making and guaranteed reward processing using a modified Balloon Analogue Risk Task and multi-echo imaging
abstract: Risky decision making is a fundamental human behavior involving multiple cognitive processes. Understanding how these processes are represented in the brain offers critical insights into decision-making, development, and vulnerabilities to psychopathology. However, functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) research of decision-making under risk and reward often does not clearly distinguish between risky decision processes and response to guaranteed reward and has limited sensitivity to deep subcortical regions, constraining our contributions. In this study, we present a modified Balloon Analogue Risk Task completed under a multi-echo fMRI protocol meant to enhance subcortical signal. Forty-eight participants inflated virtual balloons across three conditions: risky reward, guaranteed reward, and neutral. GLM analyses revealed increased signal in orbitofrontal cortex, anterior insula (AI), striatum and a brain stem nuclei, ventral tegmental area (VTA), during risky reward decision versus guaranteed rewards conditions. Multivariate analysis identified the AI as a key predictor of the risky decision condition, outperforming striatal and VTA contributions. These results suggest risky decision-making shows greater recruitment of reward-relevant regions and illuminates putative neurobiological mechanisms associated with risky decision making relative to guaranteed and non-contingent reward. The study also provides a new tool to enhance the resolution of human neuroscience research on risk-taking across the lifespan and vulnerabilities to psychopathology. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: From faux flipped to gamified flipped classrooms: scaffolding and cognitive load management
abstract: Background: Students new to flipped classrooms frequently encounter challenges with motivation and comprehension when engaging with pre-class materials independently, particularly outside scheduled class hours. Aims: This study examined a scaffolded flipped-learning approach that helped students move step by step from a Faux Flipped Classroom (FFC) to a Regular Flipped Classroom (RFC), and then to a Gamified Flipped Classroom (GFC) over one semester. The goal was to support students in adapting to flipped learning, managing their mental workload, and improving their learning performance. Method: Mixed methods were employed in the data collection. For quantitative data, learning achievement was assessed with tests and self-rating scales measured cognitive load, while qualitative interviews provided more detailed feedback. Results: The results revealed that students in the experimental group who learned through the scaffolding strategy performed better than their counterparts in the control group. Meanwhile, both groups demonstrated a small drop in intrinsic cognitive load, likely because they became more familiar with the tasks rather than because the material got easier. However, the scaffolded group showed a larger drop in unnecessary cognitive load and a larger increase in germane cognitive effort, suggesting the intervention helped students focus more on learning and less on confusion or figuring out what to do. Intrinsic and germane cognitive load should be interpreted cautiously because they are closely related. Conclusion: This study contributes to Cognitive Load Theory and scaffolding research by showing that flipped classroom success depends not only on design but also on how students are gradually prepared to use it. © 2026 The Authors

title: Effectiveness of exposure-based therapy through inhibitory learning via virtual reality in electronic gambling machines: Multiple baseline single-case experimental design
abstract: Context: Electronic gambling machines (EGMs) can harm individuals and contribute to gambling disorder (GD). Empirically supported cognitive-behavioral interventions are effective yet associated with high relapse rates. One avenue for improvement is to target the urge to gamble through exposure. In the exposure approach based on the inhibitory learning model, the perceived self-efficacy (PSE) to refrain from gambling despite the urge serves as a proximal factor for change. The goal is to create a new learning association that overrides the pre-established link between gambling stimuli, urge to gamble, and PSE to refrain from gambling. Exposure can be done in virtual reality (VR) to promote self-control and reduce gambling behaviors. VR is a relevant exposure method because it allows reproduction of ecologically valid, realistic environments. Furthermore, researchers have more control over the course of the immersion experience than during exposure in vivo. Objective: This study evaluates the effectiveness of a VR exposure-based intervention for EGM players. Method:. The single-case, multiple-baseline experimental design includes six intervention sessions with VR exposure and daily journaling to measure PSE, urges, and gambling behaviors. This approach emphasizes building PSE to resist from gambling despite the urge. Four adult males who wanted to stop their gambling behavior participated in this study. Results: Statistical analyses demonstrate a significant increase in PSE across participants and a significant reduction in the urge to gamble in three of the four participants. This study highlights the potential benefits of using of such an exposure model. It provides grounds for a large-scale randomized controlled trial where exposure and its underlying clinical rational could be included in more traditional cognitive-behavioral therapy programs. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. title: Redistribution meets decarbonisation: Exploring universal basic income through an ecological macroeconomic integrated assessment model
abstract: The dual challenge of climate change and rising inequality calls for policies capable of delivering both ecological sustainability and social equity. Within the field of Ecological Macroeconomics (EM), integrated assessment models (IAM) with biophysical and socio-economic linkages provide a promising approach to explore policy trade-offs ex ante. This paper contributes to this literature by employing the Within Limits Integrated Assessment Model (WILIAM), an EM-IAM that combines a macroeconomic multi-regional input–output structure with explicit representations of energy and material flows, biophysical constraints, and climate damages. We assess a policy mix designed to support a just low-carbon transition in 21 European countries over the period 2025–2050, including a universal basic income (UBI) financed through a wealth tax, alongside a carbon tax aimed at internalising the external costs of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. We examine the interactions between redistribution and emissions within a unified modelling framework that accounts for household heterogeneity, economic rigidities and ecological limits. Our results show that the policy mix substantially reduces income inequality and improves social outcomes. However, the introduction of UBI generates rebound effects through increased consumption, which can be partially mitigated in the presence of carbon pricing. These findings highlight a potential trade-off between equity and environmental objectives. We discuss the mechanisms driving these dynamics and explore policy design implications, including the role of complementary measures to decouple well-being from material throughput. The paper illustrates the value of EM-IAMs for analysing complex policy interactions and advancing the integration of social and ecological dimensions in macroeconomic modelling. © 2026 The Authors. title: Fat body transcriptomic responses to dietary macronutrient balance and Metarhizium infection in the desert locust, Schistocerca gregaria
abstract: Dietary macronutrient balance influences immunity and disease outcomes in most organisms, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly understood. We investigated how dietary protein-to-carbohydrate ratio shapes the fat body transcriptomic response of an insect, the desert locust (Schistocerca gregaria), following infection with the entomopathogenic fungus Metarhizium robertsii. Our earlier research showed that a carbohydrate-biased diet extends better survival from infection. We hypothesized that this was due to enriched immune functions, potentially due to more readily accessible energy to support immune responses, and/or because the fungal growth was slowed due to reduced availability of protein or other nutrients. RNA sequencing of fat body tissue collected 96 h post-infection followed by differential expression analysis showed that infection elicited a core transcriptional response, whereas direct dietary effects remained limited. Infection substantially enriched all immune pathways (humoral, cellular, and recognition and signaling) regardless of diet. These results provide support against the hypothesis that differences in survival among dietary treatments are due to differences in host immune pathway activation. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Teaching Through Making: |xam and !xun Material Culture of the Bleek and Lloyd Collection
abstract: At Wits Art Museum (University of the Witwatersrand, Johannesburg, South Africa) is a small collection donated to the former Wits Museum of Ethnology by Percival Kirby in 1952. A note in the accession register ties the items into the context of the renowned ‘Bushman researches’ of Wilhelm Bleek and Lucy Lloyd in Cape Town in the 1870s and 1880s, an unusual cross-cultural collaboration with a small group of |xam- and !xun-speaking people against the backdrop of the extreme oppression of San peoples across the southern African region. These objects represent a rare instance of historical material culture of San (‘Bushman’) origin in museum collections being associated with named persons or specific communities of origin. We examine them according to object type—spoon, head ornament, firestick, plaything, arrow and bullroarer—to assess their provenance and approach them ‘biographically’, exploring their community origins and coming into being as specific things, and their being gifted to Kirby by Wilhelm's daughter, Dorothea Bleek. Our ‘relocation’, documentation and contextualization of the Bleek-Kirby collection enables some of the material linkages to be restored, complementing the better-known narratives, making the case for the objects as active participants in the conversations, and enriching understanding of the Bleek and Lloyd Collection as a whole. We examine the significant cultural know-how embedded in these objects and emphasize the creative agency of the |xam and !xun people—|hanǂkass'o, !nanni, Tamme among others—as primary authors and producers of knowledge within the broader intellectual project. The bullroarers in particular reveal some of the affordances of this detailed work, assisted by the ongoing digitization and digital curation of the archive. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Integrating fatty acid signatures through machine learning for traceability and nutritional profiling of wild and farmed gilthead sea bream (Sparus aurata)
abstract: Fatty acid composition of seafood can provide insights into its nutritional value and tools for traceability analysis. In this study, the fillet fatty acid compositions of wild-caught gilthead sea bream and specimens produced under cage-reared and pond-reared aquaculture regimes in Northeast Atlantic waters were evaluated to (i) assess nutritional quality using lipid quality indices and (ii) test the traceability discrimination potential of fatty acids using machine-learning classification (Random Forest) and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis. Distinct fatty acid profiles and total lipid contents were observed between all groups. Although wild-caught fish exhibited higher relative abundance of nutritionally important marine fatty acids EPA and DHA, the greater total lipid content of farmed specimens yielded comparable or higher absolute levels of these omega-3 fatty acids. Mid-Atlantic cage-reared fish contained the highest total fatty acid and EPA + DHA contents, whereas coastal cage-reared specimens displayed favorable cardiovascular health indices. The traceability model achieved high accuracy during the training (100%) and validation phases (99.1%), with higher classification accuracy for wild-caught and pond-reared specimens, followed by coastal and Mid-Atlantic cage-reared specimens. Notably, this methodological approach identified key fatty acids, driving discrimination between groups, providing biologically meaningful markers likely linked to feeding regimes and production practices. Overall, fatty acid profiling coupled with machine learning provides a highly accurate framework for discriminating the production groups examined while delivering consumer-relevant nutritional information and supporting future seafood traceability applications. © 2026 The Authors

title: THDiff: Joint modeling of social and temporal factors in hyperbolic space for time-aware information diffusion prediction
abstract: Information Diffusion Prediction (IDP) aims to forecast how information spreads among users on social platforms at a micro level. Most existing methods emphasize social relations while overlooking fine-grained temporal dynamics, even though both factors are essential to diffusion. Moreover, both social and temporal factors exhibit hierarchical and imbalanced structures, posing challenges for effective modeling via conventional Euclidean methods. In particular, our analysis of real-world diffusion data reveals highly irregular and heavy-tailed time-interval distributions, suggesting the need for refined representations that can accommodate such imbalanced patterns. While hyperbolic geometry has demonstrated strong capability in capturing hierarchical social influence, its potential for modeling temporal imbalances remains largely unexplored. Motivated by these observations, we propose a novel time-aware hyperbolic diffusion prediction model (THDiff) that jointly models social and temporal factors within a unified hyperbolic framework. Specifically, THDiff uses a rotation-assisted hyperbolic embedding to construct user representations that encode global hierarchical social influence. Building on these representations, it leverages hyperbolic attention to construct cascade representations from both social and temporal perspectives and fuses them through a hyperbolic Hawkes process, enabling comprehensive modeling of complex dynamic diffusion dependencies. By jointly modeling social and temporal factors, THDiff effectively predicts not only who will be activated but also when diffusion events are likely to occur. Extensive experiments across four real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms existing methods, achieving up to 8.2% and 10.9% improvements in Hits@1 and MRR, respectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Coupling under-specification in functional resonance analysis method
abstract: A growing body of research has combined the Functional Resonance Analysis Method (FRAM) with network-analytic tools to derive quantitative insights about function importance and variability propagation in socio-technical systems. This article identifies a structural limitation shared by all the FRAM-network representations identified in the present review: the arcs between functions are treated as unspecified conduits through which variability propagates, without declaring the nature of the transmitted object or the mechanism of its distribution. This condition is termed “coupling under-specification”. This omission generates systematic ambiguities. Drawing on Borgatti's theory of network flows, the interpretation of propagation processes and the selection of appropriate network measures require the explicit specification of the nature of the transmitted good, the modality of its distribution, and the trajectory type of transmission processes. The problem is formalised through a PRISMA-compliant review of published studies combining FRAM and network models. An illustrative ontology for FRAM couplings based on three dimensions is proposed: coupling role, output nature, and transmission mechanism. The proposed ontology is illustrated through an industrial dairy packaging plant case study, an inter-rater reliability study examining the reproducibility of its application to a selected set of couplings, and a mapping between coupling classes and appropriate network measures. The results indicate that coupling under-specification is a validity condition of FRAM-derived network analyses rather than a defect of individual models, and that it constrains which network measures can be interpreted at all. The ontology is offered as one candidate means of supplying the missing specification, not as a validated instrument. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Spatial perspective on perceived fairness of climate-related fuel tax increases
abstract: We explore the perceived fairness of fuel tax increases from a spatial perspective. Actions in transport sector are needed to meet climate change mitigation targets, but such policies may disproportionately impact rural and urban residents, leading to spatially varying experiences of injustice. Perceived fairness is the most important determinant of public opinion towards mitigation policies, but perceived fairness of these policies itself has been understudied. We combine our inquiry of perceived fairness regarding fuel tax increases with considerations of spatial justice. We explore, whether residential area type, region, and variables such as climate concern, trust in climate policies, political orientation and use of fossil-fuelled car, are associated with perceived fairness of increasing fuel tax, and whether there are regional differences in these variables. Data were collected via a survey in June 2022 in three regions with different characteristics in Finland: Helsinki, Finland Proper, and Northern Ostrobothnia. Our results reveal that residents in rural areas and sparsely populated regions perceive fuel tax increases as less fair. Climate concern, trust and political orientation were found to influence fairness perceptions. Moreover, climate concern and trust were lower in sparsely populated regions. Considerations of fairness perceptions are important for successful climate mitigation policy. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier B.V. title: Locked in: How formal institutional design sustains extractivism and ecological decline in Ghana’s mining–water sector
abstract: Mining-related water pollution persists despite repeated legislative reforms and regulatory interventions. Yet, existing explanations largely attribute this persistence to weak enforcement, political patronage, or socioeconomic pressures driving artisanal small-scale mining (ASM). We argue instead that the problem is fundamentally one of institutional design. Drawing on institutional theory and institutional grammar analysis, we examine how Ghana's mining-water legislation allocates authority and embeds incentive structures that shape environmental governance. We find that the legislative framework privileges regulative over constitutive institutional elements, producing governance arrangements that are procedurally elaborate yet functionally weak. At the same time, it embeds economic and political incentives that favor extractivism while providing comparatively weak social and regulatory incentives for environmental stewardship, reinforcing fragmented authority, symbolic governance, and executive overreach. These institutional arrangements generate intertwined common-pool resource and public-bad dilemmas that lock Ghana's mining-water sector into a gilded trap, in which short-term extractive gains systematically outweigh long-term socioecological sustainability. The findings suggest that persistent mining-related water pollution is not simply a failure of enforcement but a consequence of institutional architectures that privilege extractivism while weakening environmental governance. In reconceptualizing the gilded trap as an institutionally produced condition, the paper demonstrates how imbalances between constitutive and regulative institutional elements generate symbolic governance and position the state as an active producer, rather than merely a failed regulator, of extractivist outcomes. © 2026 .

title: Gas-solid interfacial photoelectrocatalysis for toluene mineralization with concomitant hydrogen peroxide generation
abstract: The abatement of gaseous volatile organic compounds (VOCs) such as toluene is constrained by sluggish mass transfer and the trade-off between adsorption and oxidation activity in conventional liquid-phase systems. Herein, a solid-state paired photoelectrocatalytic system that operates at the gas-solid interface is proposed for enabling simultaneous anodic toluene mineralization and cathodic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) generation under ambient air feed. Particularly, by using a bifunctional composite electrode, in which ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA)-modified SnO2 (E-SnO2) nanospheres are anchored onto MXene nanosheets, a toluene degradation efficiency of 90.05 ± 3.79% with an exceptional CO2 selectivity of 97.72 ± 3.57% is achieved alongside sustained H2O2 production as a valuable byproduct. Comprehensive analyses reveal that MXene and EDTA synergistically modulate the band structure of SnO2 for promoting ∙OH generation, while MXene further amplifies this through photoelectric synergy and photothermal effects. In situ tests confirm the complete mineralization without accumulation of toxic intermediates, and theoretical calculations elucidate the increased electron density near the Fermi level, which significantly enhances the adsorption of both toluene and O2. Hence, this dual enhancement boosts the anodic oxidation kinetics but also facilitates the cathodic reduction reaction, offering a promising pathway for sustainable environmental remediation. © 2026

title: PG-DCA: prototype-guided knowledge transfer for imbalanced and heterogeneous data collaboration
abstract: Collaborative analysis of distributed data requires fusing information from multiple sources whose raw data cannot be centralized, whose label distributions may be highly skewed, and whose local feature mappings may be incompatible. Data Collaboration Analysis (DCA) can align heterogeneous client representations after local dimensionality reduction, but traditional DCA relies on anchors that often lack task-specific semantic structure and are used only after biased local mappings have already discarded important discriminative components. This paper formulates this limitation as Non-IID component loss and proposes Prototype-Guided Data Collaboration Analysis (PG-DCA), a heterogeneity-robust framework based on prototype-guided knowledge transfer. PG-DCA constructs a task-relevant reference by extracting class-level knowledge from client-side statistics, translating it into the observation space, and rebalancing it without moving raw client data. Crucially, this reference is used as a knowledge carrier to guide local mapping before DCA alignment begins. A local-first guidance interface incorporates prototype knowledge into each client’s mapping while retaining the native objective of its chosen structured linear algorithm. The guided representations are then aligned in a common collaborative space to support server-side model training. Experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 under severe statistical and algorithmic heterogeneity show that PG-DCA reduces component loss and improves collaborative utility, with gains driven by prototype-mediated reference quality and guidance of local mapping. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Can liking be instructed? Evaluations of familiar and unfamiliar food following Go/No-Go instructions and training
abstract: Go/No-Go (GNG) training can influence food evaluations, yet the processes underlying these effects remain debated. Associative accounts propose that evaluative change emerges through repeated stimulus-response learning, whereas inferential accounts emphasise the evaluative meaning individuals derive from stimulus-response relations. This research examined whether instructions about stimulus-response contingencies can influence food evaluations before the corresponding responses are performed. Across two preregistered studies, participants received either detailed contingency instructions or general task instructions. In both conditions, go responses were framed as selecting a food and no-go responses as rejecting a food. The detailed instructions additionally specified which food category was associated with each response. Detailed instructions also framed go responses as selecting a food and no-go responses as rejecting a food. Food evaluations were assessed after instruction but before training (T1), and after GNG training (T2). Study 1 (n = 54) used familiar food stimuli, whereas Study 2 (n = 63) used novel, unfamiliar food stimuli. At T1, evaluations of go- and no-go-associated foods did not differ between instruction conditions in either study. Following GNG training, go-associated stimuli were evaluated more positively in both studies, whereas no-go devaluation was observed for familiar foods in Study 1 but not overall for unfamiliar foods in Study 2. Exploratory analyses in Study 2 indicated stronger no-go devaluation among participants higher in trait impulsivity. These findings suggest that providing information about stimulus-response contingencies before training was not reflected in differences in food evaluations. The observed changes in evaluations following training suggest that the evaluative impact of these stimulus-response assignments may depend in part on how responses are experienced and interpreted during task performance, although this possibility requires further investigation. © 2026 The Author. title: A unified micro–macro stochastic framework for tool wear evolution and lifetime prediction
abstract: Tool wear results from the interaction of numerous micro-scale contact regions subjected to mechanical, thermal and tribological loading. This paper proposes a physics-informed micro–macro stochastic framework linking contact-scale degradation processes with engineering-scale prediction of wear evolution and tool life. At the micro-contact level, tool degradation is represented by a population of interacting contacts undergoing wear, load redistribution and local instability. Model reduction leads to a state-dependent stochastic differential equation whose drift and diffusion terms describe macroscopic flank-wear evolution, while a jump component represents intermittent degradation events. Abrasion/ploughing, adhesion/BUE, thermal–oxidative and diffusion–chemical wear are represented as dominant degradation mechanisms, whereas coating protection and edge instability are treated as latent degradation states. Tool life is formulated as a first-passage problem with respect to a prescribed wear limit. Model parameters are identified from experimentally reconstructed wear increments, with different tribological systems represented using the same stochastic formulation through coefficient calibration. Validation is performed at three complementary levels: predictive assessment of wear evolution, statistical evaluation of degradation dynamics and independent physical validation. The framework reproduces nonlinear wear evolution and increasing degradation variability, while the inferred mechanism hierarchy and latent degradation states are qualitatively supported by independent experimental evidence. The proposed methodology bridges tribological processes at the micro-contact scale and stochastic reliability assessment at the engineering scale, integrating wear evolution, mechanism interpretation and tool-life prediction within a unified physics-informed framework. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Boosting chemical looping hydrogen production over Cu–Al co-doped NiFe2O4: insights into lattice-oxygen activity and structural stability
abstract: NiFe2O4 is a promising oxygen carrier for chemical looping hydrogen production, but its application is limited by the trade-off between lattice-oxygen activity and structural stability. Here, Cu- and Al-doped NiFe2O4 oxygen carriers were prepared to combine enhanced oxygen reactivity with improved cyclic durability. Structural characterization supported the incorporation of Cu and Al into the spinel framework and revealed higher defect-related oxygen fractions in the Cu-containing samples. At 850 °C, Cu0.2Ni0.8Fe1.8Al0.2O4 (CNFAO) achieved an H2 yield of 14.8 mmol·g−1 Fe2O3 and a production rate of 1.48 mmol·g−1 Fe2O3·min−1, while retaining 12.3 mmol·g−1 Fe2O3 after 80 cycles. Mechanistic analysis indicates that Cu doping enhances lattice-oxygen activity by promoting oxygen-vacancy formation and bulk lattice-oxygen diffusion, thereby improving reduction kinetics and hydrogen production. Meanwhile, Al stabilizes the spinel framework and suppresses phase separation, particle coalescence, and pore collapse. Their complementary effects enable CNFAO to balance high reactivity with long-term structural stability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A Land-Sea integrated ecological compensation framework based on carbon sequestration service flows: Evidence from a Coastal City
abstract: Ecological compensation (EC) is an important policy instrument for coordinating ecological conservation and economic development and promoting carbon neutrality. However, existing EC policies in coastal regions remain largely terrestrial-oriented, making it difficult to identify cross-regional dependence on land-sea carbon sequestration services (CSs) and the corresponding compensation responsibilities. Using Qingdao, China, as a case study, this study develops a land-sea integrated EC framework that combines random forest, the IPCC inventory method, and a spatial interaction model to identify land-sea CSs supply-demand patterns and carbon sequestration service flows (CSF), and to allocate EC responsibilities accordingly. The results show that: (1) from 2004 to 2023, the imbalance between CSs supply and demand continuously intensified, with pronounced spatial mismatches; (2) CSF exhibited clear land-sea coupling, with the sea area and coastal mountainous area (Laoshan District) serving as the major CSF sources. CSF outflows from the sea area accounted for 29.02%–47.81% of the total positive regional CSF and primarily flowed to the rapidly urbanizing area of Huangdao District; and (3) actual EC payments differed markedly from ideal responsibilities across county-level administrative units, while the sea area received 78.10% of total inter-county compensation receipts. The Ecological Compensation Priority Index (ECPI) further indicated that the sea area and key terrestrial CSs supply areas should be prioritized for compensation. By integrating land-sea ecological contributions, external CSs dependence, compensation responsibilities, and implementation priorities into a unified analysis, the framework can support more equitable and efficient EC decision-making in coastal regions. © 2026

title: Intellectual overconfidence and susceptibility to anti-science misinformation
abstract: Anti-science misinformation can undermine trust in science, and understanding who is most susceptible is important for combatting its influence. One relevant trait is Intellectual Humility (IH), associated with greater understanding of science and the reasoning skills required to reject misinformation. Three pre-registered experimental studies (total N = 1604) examined IH and susceptibility to anti-science misinformation in the context of consumer genetic testing. A central subscale of IH – Lack of Intellectual Overconfidence – emerged as the strongest predictor, with intellectually overconfident individuals most susceptible to misinformation, though effect sizes were modest. The final study introduced a warning-label intervention that had a small positive effect on reduced susceptibility to misinformation about genetic testing companies, but only for participants with less intellectual overconfidence, suggesting that those who would benefit most from such interventions may be least likely to do so. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Empowering LLMs for biomedical information extraction with RAG-ICL and DFPO
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities for biomedical information extraction (IE), but their application to named entity recognition (NER) and relation extraction (RE) remains limited by prototype selection, preference alignment, and structured-output validity. In this study, we formulate LLM-based biomedical IE as a structure-constrained pattern recognition problem and propose a framework centered on two complementary adaptation mechanisms. Retrieval-Augmented In-Context Learning (RAG-ICL) performs inference-time prototype selection by retrieving and reranking instance-specific demonstrations, enabling LLMs to use more relevant contextual examples without parameter updates. Dual-Phase Fine-tuning with Preference Optimization (DFPO) performs training-time parameter alignment through supervised fine-tuning, MFPEA-based structured preference data, DPO-Positive optimization, and post-finetuning. In addition, Dual-Mode Correction and Review (DMCR) is used as an auxiliary output-side verification module to improve parsability and reduce malformed structured predictions. Experiments across biomedical NER and RE benchmarks show that RAG-ICL improves over zero-shot and random/fixed ICL baselines, while DFPO consistently enhances extraction performance over supervised fine-tuning and representative biomedical IE systems. Further analyses demonstrate the importance of compact, relevant demonstrations, the incremental contribution of DFPO stages, and the practical trade-off between inference-time and training-time adaptation. These results suggest that decomposing LLM-based biomedical IE into prototype selection, preference-aware decision alignment, and structural verification provides an effective and coherent framework for schema-constrained biomedical text recognition. © 2026

title: Beyond taste: how production-system information influences consumer liking of poultry meat from novel organic alternative production system
abstract: Alternative food production systems may be unfamiliar to consumers, making communication of production-related credence attributes important for product understanding and evaluation. This study examined whether information about a novel dual-purpose poultry production system influenced consumer liking and preference when the chicken meat remained identical. In a within-subject repeated-measures design, consumers (n = 657) evaluated two identical chicken meat samples presented with either information about the production system or basic origin information only. Providing production-system information increased overall liking, taste liking, and texture liking, though samples were in fact identical. Preference responses showed that 50% preferred the sample with information, 24% preferred the sample without information, and 26% reported no preference. Across the whole sample, characteristics of the novel production system were generally rated as important, with minimal waste and outdoor access, specifically, receiving the highest importance ratings, while growth rate and price were rated lowest importance. In contrast, when participants selected broader grocery shopping values independent of the specific production system, price was most frequently prioritised, followed by animal welfare and taste. When stratified by preference, participants preferring the sample with information assigned greater importance to the novel production system characteristics compared with those reporting no preference, whereas general shopping values did not differ between groups. Overall, the findings indicate that information about food production systems can influence consumer evaluation of a food product even when sensory input is held constant, highlighting the potential role of communicating relevant credence attributes in supporting consumer acceptance of alternative food production systems. © 2026 The Authors

title: Beyond openness: Mapping need for cognition across Big Five domains and facets in university students
abstract: Need for cognition (NFC) is closely associated with openness-related personality traits, but broad domains may obscure a more selective facet-level pattern. We examined NFC in 1551 university students using the Big Five Inventory–2 and a split-sample discovery–validation design. In discovery, three domains (Open-Mindedness, Conscientiousness, and Extraversion) and four facets (Productiveness, Intellectual Curiosity, Assertiveness, and Creative Imagination) met the selected magnitude threshold. In held-out validation, all three domains remained independently associated with NFC, whereas at the facet level only Assertiveness, Intellectual Curiosity, and Productiveness did so. Complementary latent models indicated positive associations of NFC with both Intellectual Curiosity and Assertiveness, although a bifactor decomposition of Open-Mindedness was inadmissible and correlated-factor model fit was mixed. Overall, the findings support the particular importance of intellectual openness while indicating that NFC is also embedded in a selective cross-domain configuration involving agentic and goal-directed characteristics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
