title: Online collective aggression in algorithmic environments: The roles of algorithm awareness, moral outrage, and negative descriptive norms
abstract: In algorithmic social media environments, filtering, ranking, and recommendation systems shape which online events, comments, and group reactions become visible. However, little is known about whether awareness of these algorithmic processes can reduce online collective aggression. Drawing on a focused application of value-added theory and a multidimensional framework of algorithmic literacy, the present research tested a moderated mediation model in which algorithmic awareness may reduce aggressive participation through attenuated moral outrage, with negative descriptive norms as a boundary condition. Across three experimental studies with emerging adults aged 18–28, participants completed self-developed online collective aggression scenarios. Study 1 (N = 158) showed that experimentally induced algorithmic awareness reduced individuals' tendency toward online collective aggression. Study 2 (N = 306) further found that moral outrage mediated this effect, suggesting that algorithmic awareness may reduce aggressive participation by weakening immediate moralized emotional responses to online events. Study 3 (N = 289) revealed a significant index of moderated mediation: the conditional indirect effect through moral outrage was significant when negative descriptive norms were low but not when they were high. Together, these findings identify algorithmic awareness as a potentially protective cognitive factor whose effects depend on the normative climate inferred from visible cues. They clarify how algorithmic curation, moralized emotion, and normative cues jointly shape aggressive participation. Practically, these findings underscore the need to develop algorithmic literacy education and platform interventions that address both users’ recognition of algorithmic curation and the normative cues conveyed by visible comment environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Life cycle analysis and multi-objective optimization of CCUS-integrated methanol reforming PEMFC-CCHP systems
abstract: Distributed methanol steam reforming (MSR)-proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) systems have attracted attention due to their high efficiency, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness. Coupling these systems with combined cooling, heating, and power (CCHP) configurations further enhances energy utilization. However, their strong reliance on fossil fuels leads to substantial carbon emissions. Although integrating carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) mitigates operational emissions, it introduces additional energy penalties, economic costs, and complexity, while its full life cycle environmental benefits remain insufficiently understood. Moreover, conventional single-objective optimization is inadequate to simultaneously balance energy, economic, and environmental performance. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel distributed MSR-PEMFC-CCHP system integrated with CCUS and develops a comprehensive evaluation framework combining life cycle assessment (LCA) and multi-objective optimization. Three configurations—CCHP-C (without carbon treatment), CCHP-S (with CCS), and CCHP-M (with CCUS)—are systematically analyzed to quantify full life cycle environmental impacts and identify optimal trade-offs. Results show the operation stage dominates life cycle emissions, contributing over 80 % in all configurations. Under the adopted inventory assumptions and system boundary, CCHP-M has the lowest total pollutant emissions and global warming potential, whereas CCHP-C has lower acidification and respiratory effect potentials. For CCHP-M, the selected compromise solution, Point D, achieves an energy efficiency of 85.61 % and an LCOE of 0.2463 $/kWh. Compared with the energy-optimal solution, Point K, Point D reduces the LCOE by 2.84 % and lowers life-cycle CO2-equivalent emissions by 2.816 t, or 4.14 %, to 65.153 t, while decreasing energy efficiency by 1.79 %. These results identify the environmental trade-offs among the three carbon-management configurations and the operating compromise within CCHP-M. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Adsorption performance of radial-flow contactors for direct air capture: A computational study
abstract: The need for efficient direct air capture (DAC) is increasing as the global mean temperature continues to rise and a large fraction of CO2 emissions cannot be addressed by conventional CO2 capture technologies. For adsorption-based DAC, the geometry of the gas-solid contactor is an important design parameter because it determines pressure losses, sorbent utilisation, and the efficiency of the process. This study investigates the adsorption stage in a centripetal Z-type radial-flow adsorber for DAC. A computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model is adopted to simulate the gas flow through the porous bed of adsorbent particles adsorbing CO2 from the gas with the help of the linear driving force model and the Toth isotherms. The material properties are experimentally obtained for a commercial amine-functionalised resin. Twelve different configurations of the contactor are analysed with various bed aspect ratios and radius ratios while keeping the bed volume constant. The simulations indicate that the geometry strongly affects the flow distribution, pressure drop, and adsorption time, which affect the specific energy requirement and productivity of the adsorption stage of the DAC process. Configuration selection represents the trade-off between low energy requirements (at high bed aspect ratio and radius ratio), low space requirements, and construction material costs (at low bed aspect ratio and radius ratio). The intermediate geometries provide the most practical basis for scaling up to a 7-contactor adsorber. © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier Ltd. This is an open access article under the CC BY license. http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Proton-conducting solid oxide fuel cells with La0.5Sr0.5Fe0.75X0.25O3 (X=Co,Ni, Cu) cathodes: a comparative study
abstract: To enhance the cathode performance of La0.5Sr0.5FeO3 (LSF) in proton‑conducting solid oxide fuel cells (H‑SOFCs), different transition metal elements (Co, Ni, Cu) are introduced at the Fe site, forming the composition La0.5Sr0.5Fe0.75X0.25O3 (X = Co, Ni, Cu). Ni doping is the most effective in promoting oxygen vacancy formation, oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity, and proton migration. H-SOFCs employing the Ni-doped LSF cathode achieve higher power output and lower polarization losses than those using Co- or Cu-doped counterparts. Furthermore, the Ni-doped LSF material is evaluated in composite cathodes. A trade-off exists between the ORR activity of the Ni-doped LSF cathode and the proton conduction provided by the proton conductor. The optimal composition was found to contain 10 wt% proton conductor, yielding a peak power density of 1456 mW cm−2 at 700 °C. This result represents a substantial improvement in the performance of LSF-based cathodes for H-SOFCs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Life history strategy and the Dark Triad: A meta-analysis of trait-specific associations
abstract: Life History (LH) Theory has been increasingly employed as an evolutionary framework for understanding individual differences in the Dark Triad. However, findings remain inconsistent regarding trait-specific associations between LH strategy and the Dark Triad. This meta-analysis synthesized 41 effect sizes from 18 independent samples reported in 16 articles. A three-level random-effects model showed a significant positive overall association between faster LH strategy and Dark Triad traits (Pearson's r = 0.26, 95% CI [0.19, 0.33], p < 0.001). Moderator analyses revealed significant differences among the three traits, with psychopathy showing the strongest association ( r = 0.36), followed by Machiavellianism ( r = 0.25), whereas narcissism showed the weakest association ( r = 0.11). The main effects of LH operationalization, gender composition, sample type, and cultural region were not statistically significant. However, the interaction between Dark Triad trait and LH measurement domain was significant ( Q M (4) = 11.90, p = 0.018), indicating that the pattern of associations across LH measurement domains differed among the three traits. By providing a quantitative synthesis of trait-specific associations between life history strategy and the Dark Triad, this study clarifies current evolutionary accounts of dark personality traits and highlights the importance of differentiating among the three traits. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Machine learning algorithms empower traditional Chinese medicine: Breakthrough approaches from chemical component analysis to pharmacological mechanism research
abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine studies are constrained by complex chemical components and multi-target biological interactions, making conventional analytical methods inefficient for mechanism exploration. As a data-driven technique, machine learning has been widely adopted to tackle diverse complex challenges in TCM research. Nevertheless, most existing reviews merely summarize individual algorithms or scattered application cases, lacking systematic task-based classification and unified operational standards. Based on literature published from 2022 to 2026, this review systematically classifies machine learning applications in TCM into four core research tasks. A task-oriented framework is constructed to match different algorithms with appropriate TCM research scenarios. This paper further establishes a complete standardized workflow covering algorithm selection, model construction and model evaluation to standardize ML applications in TCM research. This review also summarizes the applications of machine learning in TCM quality control, bioactive compound identification, processing analysis, and mechanism elucidation. Furthermore, major bottlenecks in current ML-based TCM studies are analyzed, and feasible optimization strategies are proposed. This review aims to provide clear and practical guidelines for the standardized application of machine learning in future TCM research. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Economic consequences of climate change: Evidence from the Philippines
abstract: This paper evaluates the economic implications of climate change in the Philippines. Data spanning two decades reveal that warmer temperatures increase out-migration, yet locations exposed to intense heat send fewer migrants to historically connected destinations. This pattern raises the question of how climate change affects the spatial allocation of economic activity when mobility is constrained. I employ a quantitative spatial equilibrium model in which rising temperatures and sea-level rise depress local amenities and productivity. Taking climate projections for 2100, I estimate aggregate welfare and output to fall by 15% and 12% respectively, with more prominent losses for high-skilled workers. Large-scale coastal protection can offset damages by up to 3 percentage points, but removing migration barriers attenuates welfare losses by as much as 13 percentage points. © 2026

title: Time, cognition, and culture: A three-dimensional self-system model of subjective well-being and interdependent happiness
abstract: This research proposes a “time–cognition–culture” self-system model to examine whether and under what conditions Future Self-Continuity (FSC) is associated with well-being among Chinese undergraduate students across three studies (N = 1010). Study 1 experimentally showed that increasing FSC enhanced both Subjective Well-Being (SWB) and Interdependent Happiness (IH). In Study 2, PROCESS analyses showed that Self-Concept Clarity (SCC) moderated the associations between FSC and both well-being outcomes, such that the positive associations were stronger among individuals with higher SCC; however, the corresponding latent-variable interaction for SWB was positive but did not reach conventional statistical significance. Study 3 showed that self-construal qualified the FSC × SCC interaction. The clearest conditional patterns were observed for independent self-construal in relation to SWB and interdependent self-construal in relation to IH. Overall, these findings suggest that the association between FSC and well-being may vary as a function of SCC, with this moderation pattern further qualified by self-construal. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Systemic approaches in human factors and ergonomics for analysing team dynamics: A systematic review
abstract: Team dynamics in complex sociotechnical systems are critical for safety and organisational effectiveness. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the utility and applicability of systemic Human Factors and Ergonomics(HFE) approaches for analysing team dynamics. Four databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect) were searched for peer-reviewed articles published in English between 2020 and September 2025. Studies were included if they applied systemic HFE methods to analyse team dynamics in organisational settings. Studies focusing solely on individual performance or lacking methodological detail were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data, and methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Data were synthesised using thematic analysis. Seventy-seven studies were included, with healthcare being the most represented domain (n = 39). Most studies (51.9%) used adapted or combined approaches. Communication and coordination were the most frequently analysed dimensions of team dynamics. Established frameworks (e.g., SEIPS, FRAM) supported system-level analysis, while author-developed methods provided greater insight into local interactions. Hybrid approaches enabled integration across levels of analysis. Most studies were of high methodological quality (64.9%). These patterns informed a two-axis model positioning systemic HFE approaches by level of analysis and methodological integration, operationalised as a framework for method selection. Systemic HFE approaches are effective for analysing team dynamics in complex settings; however, no single method is universally optimal. Effectiveness depends on alignment between the analytical approach, context, and research objectives. Hybrid and adapted approaches appearing particularly promising. Further research is needed in underrepresented domains and through comparative methodological studies. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: A perception-oriented framework for assessing wind turbine aerodynamic noise and operating-parameter effects with normal amplitude modulation
abstract: To evaluate the effects of wind turbine operating parameters on residents’ perceived annoyance from aerodynamic noise in open rural areas, this study proposes a perception-oriented engineering framework that explicitly accounts for normal amplitude modulation (NAM). Initially, the ISO 9613–2:2024 propagation model is combined with empirical corrections to characterize attenuation across different azimuthal directions around the turbine. A directionally corrected Quasi-AM factor is then introduced to quantify variations in modulation depth under diverse propagation conditions and turbine operations. To better capture subjective human response, a power-law saturation penalty model is developed to adjust the conventional sound pressure level (SPL) by incorporating the contribution of NAM. The resulting NAM-corrected A-weighted sound level is subsequently employed in an annoyance model to evaluate residents’ perceived disturbance. The framework is validated through representative case studies in open rural areas, examining the effects of yaw angle, pitch angle, and rotational speed on the Quasi-AM factor, NAM-corrected A-weighted sound level, and perceived annoyance. Results demonstrate that the framework accurately captures the principal azimuthal variation of NAM, with a mean absolute error of approximately 0.38 dB, NAM-related corrections reach up to 3.60 dB in the main radiation region, indicating that NAM can substantially amplify perceived annoyance even when overall SPL changes are limited. The power-law saturation penalty model exhibits strong fitting performance (R2 = 0.9461), confirming its ability to represent the nonlinear contribution of NAM to annoyance. Sensitivity analysis further reveals that yaw angle, pitch angle, and rotational speed exert distinct effects on the spatial distribution of perceived annoyance. Overall, this framework provides a robust and practical tool for noise-oriented optimization of wind turbine operation and environmental assessment in rural wind farm settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Hydrogen production from municipal solid waste via oxygen–steam gasification for a Riyadh application: process simulation, sensitivity analysis, and techno-economic screening
abstract: This study develops an Aspen Plus thermodynamic screening framework for hydrogen production from municipal solid waste (MSW) in a Riyadh application through oxygen–steam gasification, staged water–gas shift (WGS), surrogate contaminant removal, and surrogate pressure swing adsorption (PSA). MSW was represented on an as-received basis using literature-derived proximate and ultimate analyses. Gasification was modeled using an equilibrium reactor coupled adiabatically to decomposition, with the industrial-purity oxidant flow solved for the target temperature. The 100 kg h−1 reference case produced 6.775 kg h−1 of product hydrogen (67.75 kg H2 per metric ton of as-received MSW). Hydrogen production decreased across the 10–60 kg h−1 steam sweep at 900 °C. Response-surface analysis of 15 distinct simulations ranked 25 kg h−1 steam, an 800 °C gasifier temperature, and a 180 °C low-temperature WGS temperature highest within the studied domain; two cases excluded from regression showed interpolation errors below 0.074 %. A comparison case at 27 kg h−1 steam, 800 °C and 180 °C (Case A) produced 7.083 kg h−1 hydrogen, with specific compressor work of 5.911 kWh kg-H2−1 and an oxidant demand of 36.841 kg h−1. A 1200 °C refuse-derived fuel benchmark with reconstructed steam input reproduced four major wet-gas fractions within 0.76 percentage points. Two fluidized-bed comparisons at 850 °C showed substantial departures in gas ratios, and hydrogen yields at 800–900 °C remain unvalidated. Under three capital scenarios, the preliminary minimum hydrogen selling price for Case A was US$4.10–5.51 kg-H2−1. The results define conditional operating trade-offs and priorities for local feed characterization, kinetic, separation, heat-integration, and equipment-level studies. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Ultrasonic vocalizations in mice and rats: New applications and recent developments from sender to receiver
abstract: Mice and rats emit ultrasonic vocalizations (USV) above the human hearing range. Such USV are widely regarded as reliable indicators of the animal's affective state. Moreover, USV serve important communicative functions. Given their prominent role in social communication, this review adopts a reciprocal framework that considers both sender and receiver, with particular emphasis on the production and perception of USV. The review focuses on sex differences and subtype variations in the sender, and explores the communicative value of USV through playback studies, revealing their role in regulating social interactions from the receiver's perspective. It also examines recent applications, including the use of isolation-induced USV during the homing test, USV as measures of expectation, and their relevance in modeling mania and emotional contagion. Furthermore, this review takes into account advancements in sender identification and live tracking in semi-natural environments, which have enhanced our understanding of USV. These insights offer valuable perspectives on rodent social communication and emotional processes, with implications for studying human disorders. © 2026 The Authors
label: Social Sciences

title: The dynamics of climate change skepticism sharing on social media: Social identity, partisanship, and the impact of negative public opinion cues
abstract: Social media has facilitated the rapid spread of incorrect information, including climate change skepticism. Drawing on Social Identity Theory, we investigated why individuals adopt skeptical views and disseminate them on social media. Study 1 (N = 316) revealed that Republicans were more likely to endorse climate change skepticism and that those with strong partisan attachments were particularly likely to share these views actively as a manifestation of their social identity. Furthermore, Study 2 (N = 120) designed through the lens of the Spiral of Silence theory revealed that explicit social media cues signaling opposition to climate skepticism (e.g., high number of “dislikes” on posts about climate change skepticism) effectively discouraged climate change skeptics from sharing their skepticism. The findings of the two studies highlight the psychological drivers of climate change skepticism dissemination on social media and demonstrate that explicit cues (e.g., number of “dislikes”) can reduce the spread of climate change skepticism in digital spaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
label: Social Sciences

title: An accelerated recursive decomposition algorithm for dynamic seismic reliability analysis of large-scale networks with complex component dependencies
abstract: Accurate dynamic seismic reliability assessment of lifeline networks is critical for seismic design optimization and post-earthquake emergency response, however it faces challenges from complex internal network dependencies and computational inefficiency for large-scale networks. To calculate the dynamic seismic reliability of large-scale network systems with component dependencies, this paper proposes an accelerated recursive decomposition algorithm (RDA). Through a comparative analysis, a two-level nested joint cumulative distribution function (CDF) is developed and incorporated into the RDA to accurately capture complex dependencies while avoiding the curse of dimensionality. This joint distribution model is constructed by first reducing the dimensionality of high-dimensional variables via grouping based on k -medoids clustering, and then coupling the grouped variables using multiple Gumbel copulas. Based on the joint CDF (jCDF), this paper introduces an improved Dijkstra’s algorithm for the most reliable path search in the RDA to accelerate convergence of system reliability bounds. Moreover, a subgraph decomposition strategy based on real-time updated importance rankings is developed to identify fewer disjoint shortest paths and cuts while satisfying the requirement on system reliability bounds, thereby enabling rapid convergence of reliability bounds. The accuracy, efficiency, and applicability of the proposed accelerated RDA are demonstrated through two numerical examples. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
label: Social Sciences

title: Enhancing combustion in an ethanol rotary engine via turbulent jet ignition: parametric study and mechanism analysis
abstract: Enhancing the combustion of ethanol rotary engine (ERE) is crucial for carbon neutrality. This study systematically compares the effects of conventional spark plug ignition mode (CSPIM) and turbulent jet ignition mode (TJIM) on the performance of an ERE. This investigation employs a combined methodology of experimental validation and numerical simulation, systematically analyzes the combustion characteristics of both ignition modes across multiple equivalence ratio conditions. Furthermore, this research elucidates the effect of jet nozzle diameter (JND) on the combustion behavior of the TJIM. The results reveal that TJIM’s effectiveness is governed by the coupling between the energy of the jet flame and the concentration of the mixture in the pre-combustion chamber. It demonstrates superior flame propagation and combustion at equivalence ratios of 1.0 and 1.2 by generating highly turbulent jet flames, but underperforms CSPIM under an equivalence ratio of 0.8 due to reduced jet flame intensity. Furthermore, the optimal JND shifts with the global equivalence ratio — 3.5 mm for lean and 2.0 mm for stoichiometric combustion. The JND governs a trade-off between the mass of fuel in the pre-combustion chamber and the jet flame velocity. While TJIM significantly reduces CO emissions via more complete combustion, it increases NO formation due to higher temperatures. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Shared regulatory systems in memory suppression and fear extinction: An ALE and MACM meta-analysis
abstract: Memory suppression and fear extinction both reduce the influence of past experiences on current cognition and behavior, but they are typically studied within separate research traditions. The present study examined whether these two processes recruit partially overlapping neural systems involved in the regulation of unwanted memories and previously threat-associated cues. We conducted a preregistered coordinate-based meta-analysis of fMRI studies using activation likelihood estimation (ALE) and meta-analytic connectivity modeling (MACM). The analysis included 63 experiments involving 1452 participants and focused on contrasts commonly used to index retrieval suppression in the Think/No-Think paradigm and threat-cue processing during extinction learning. ALE revealed convergent activation in bilateral inferior frontal gyrus/anterior insula and right inferior parietal lobule. MACM further showed that these regions were embedded within broader executive-control and attention-related coactivation networks. These findings suggest that memory suppression and fear extinction partially converge within broader control- and attention-related systems involved in controlling task-relevant memory and threat representations. At the same time, partly distinct medial temporal and affective-learning patterns point to important domain-specific differences between intentional episodic retrieval suppression and extinction-based threat–safety updating. Overall, the findings help bridge research on memory control and fear extinction by identifying partially overlapping regulatory systems while preserving important theoretical distinctions between the two processes. This framework highlights how control- and attention-related neural systems may contribute to the regulation of unwanted memories and conditioned fear responses through their interactions with memory, threat-learning, and contextual updating processes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Mn-doped polysaccharide-derived calcium-based sorbents with enhanced CO2 capture and cyclic stability
abstract: Rapid CO2 emissions from fossil-fuel combustion have intensified the demand for efficient carbon-capture technologies. Calcium looping (CaL) is considered a promising option because of its high theoretical capacity and low material cost; however, severe sintering of CaO-based sorbents during repeated carbonation–calcination cycles results in rapid performance degradation. Mn-doped polysaccharide-derived CaO-based sorbents (Mn-PDCA) were prepared through a microtitration–wet-impregnation route to improve their cyclic CO2-capture performance. Among the prepared sorbents, 15Mn-PDCA exhibited the best overall performance, achieving an initial CO2 uptake of 0.474 g/g and retaining 0.417 g/g after 15 cycles under mild conditions, corresponding to a capacity retention of approximately 87.97%. Its initial uptake was 65.73% higher than that of Mn-free 0Mn-PDCA. Comprehensive experimental characterization indicated that the enhanced performance originated from the coordinated effects of Mn-associated surface regulation, Ca–Mn mixed-oxide pinning, XG-directed porous-structure formation, and residual-carbon confinement. Mixed Mn valence states and defect-associated oxygen species contributed to favorable surface chemical environments for CO2 adsorption, while thermally stable CaMnO3 and Ca4Mn3O10 phases acted as interfacial or grain-boundary barriers that restrained CaO crystallite migration and coalescence during cycling. Meanwhile, XG directed precursor nucleation and promoted the formation of porous microspheres, with the retained carbonaceous species providing an additional spatial-confinement effect. Excessive Mn loading at 20% caused Mn-rich aggregation, partial pore blockage, and dilution of active CaO, revealing a capacity–stability trade-off. These findings demonstrate a coordinated template–metal regulation strategy for developing sintering-resistant CaO-based sorbents for calcium-looping CO2 capture. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Adaptive Learning-based Semantic Enhancement for Multimodal Dialogue Discourse Parsing
abstract: Dialogue Discourse Parsing (DDP) aims to identify dependency structures and relation types among utterances in conversations. Existing multimodal DDP methods often directly fuse low-level audio-visual features, making it difficult to establish explicit semantic links between nonverbal behaviors and discourse relations and potentially introducing irrelevant modality noise. To address these limitations, we propose ALSE-MDDP, an Adaptive Learning-based Semantic Enhancement framework for Multimodal Dialogue Discourse Parsing. ALSE-MDDP includes three modules: Text Pre-Parsing (TPP), which performs text-only parsing and identifies low-confidence predictions; Explicit Semantic Augmentation (ESA), which converts discourse-relevant audio-visual behaviors into textual cues; and Adaptive Feedback Preference Optimization (AFPO), which uses parser feedback to optimize cue generation. Experiments on DraDDP and MODDP show that ALSE-MDDP achieves 56.79 and 57.50 Link&Rel F1, outperforming the strongest multimodal baseline, LLaMIPa* (Qwen2.5-Omni-7B), by 3.45 and 5.23 points, respectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Decarbonizing dairy processing with grid-connected hybrid renewable energy systems: a surrogate-assisted multi-objective framework
abstract: Industrial decarbonization requires site-specific hybrid renewable energy systems (HRESs) that reduce lifecycle cost, grid dependence, and operational emissions. This study primarily develops and validates a surrogate-assisted optimization method and demonstrates it for an engineering-derived 333 kWh/day dairy-processing load in Colac, Victoria. Four grid-connected architectures were compared: grid only; grid + photovoltaic (PV); grid + PV + battery; and grid + PV + wind + battery. Relative to the grid-only baseline (NPC = USD 852,233; LCOE = USD 0.306/kWh), the best HOMER architecture reduced NPC by 77.09% to USD 195,258 and LCOE by 95.42% to USD 0.014/kWh, while reaching 98.3% renewable fraction. Its annual supply comprised 714,854 kWh wind, 99,792 kWh PV, and 10,075 kWh grid imports; all cases had zero unserved load because the grid supplied residual demand. Under displacement-based accounting, Case 4 exported 457,937 kWh/yr and produced a net CO2 credit of 283,049 kg/yr. Gradient-boosting surrogates trained on 16,000 site-specific HOMER designs achieved held-out R2 values of 0.99999 for LCOE and 0.99985 for NPC. The revalidated MO-FWSC compromise yielded USD 0.01267/kWh and USD 176,762, respectively. Surrogate reuse reduced each optimization campaign from 10.3 to 1.9 h; including one-time data generation, the first complete pipeline required 12.2 h. The contribution is therefore methodological and site-demonstrated rather than a claim of universal dairy-plant performance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Extending the operating range of HCCI engines with the rhombic drive mechanism: A novel concept
abstract: Homogeneous charge compression ignition (HCCI) engines offer high thermal efficiency and very low nitrogen oxides (NOx) and soot emissions, but they have significant challenges such as a limited operating range, knocking at high loads, and misfiring at low loads. In this study, the use of a rhombic drive mechanism as an alternative to the conventional crankshaft mechanism was numerically investigated for the first time to extend the operating range of HCCI engines. A total of 301 computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were performed using CONVERGE CFD, employing an HCCI engine model validated with experimental data. The simulations were conducted at engine speeds of 800–2600 rpm, within a λ range of 1.3–3.4, using fuels with research octane numbers of 20 and 40 (RON20 and RON40). The results showed that the rhombic drive mechanism extended the compression phase, allowing the piston to remain near top dead center (TDC) for a longer duration. This increased the average cylinder temperature, facilitating auto-ignition and enabling stable HCCI combustion near the low-load limit at higher engine speeds. With the rhombic drive mechanism, heat release was more concentrated around TDC, the combustion duration was shortened, and the combustion process approached a constant-volume character. The principal contribution of the rhombic drive mechanism was extending the upper engine-speed limit of naturally aspirated HCCI operation. The low-load improvement was secondary, while higher MPRR under identical engine-speed and lambda conditions showed no direct extension of the high-load limit at a fixed speed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Actionable Weather Communication Recommendations for Hard-to-Reach Populations Using Topic Modeling and Thematic Analysis
abstract: Language barriers, geographic isolation, and limited digital access are some of the obstacles that hard-to-reach populations in the United States face when trying to access weather and climate information. These conditions restrict equitable access to the public benefits mandated by federal weather policy and public warning systems. We identified actionable, evidence-based strategies for strengthening hazard communication for these populations. We conducted topic modeling on 7,705 peer-reviewed article abstracts and an in-depth thematic analysis of 129 peer-reviewed studies documenting effective approaches for engaging groups with differentiated information needs. The thematic analysis produced four integrated recommendations: community-embedded communication, hybrid and redundant communication systems, cross-sector coordination, and inclusive and actionable communication. Across these themes, studies emphasized strategies such as mobile service delivery, low-tech communication channels, culturally specific messages, trusted messengers, and participatory design. The results show how broader federal priorities for improving forecast communication and public response can be advanced and hazard communication improved through practices validated in health and social services. When taken as a whole, these insights provide communicators, emergency managers, and legislators with scalable ways to create more resilient and inclusive hazard information systems. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Green methanol production under carbon constraints: pathways, system integration, and deployment conditions
abstract: Green methanol links low-carbon carbon sources with renewable electricity while retaining liquid-fuel handling advantages. We reviewed 155 publications covering genuinely green routes based on renewable hydrogen and sustainable carbon (CO2 hydrogenation with renewable H2 and biomass- or waste-derived methanol), transitional low-carbon retrofits of fossil-based plants, and less mature electrochemical, photocatalytic, or methane-conversion routes. Retrofits are treated as transitional, not genuinely green, because their carbon remains fossil-derived unless the feedstock is replaced. Authors adopt different system boundaries and functional units, and assumptions about electricity, CO2 supply, plant scale, and cost are rarely identical. Our comparison places each pathway in its operating conditions and avoids ranking isolated performance values. It considers technical maturity, energy demand, life-cycle emissions, levelized methanol cost, feedstock supply, infrastructure, and operating flexibility, and examines when power-hydrogen-carbon integration is justified. The review provides four outputs: a protocol for checking the comparability of techno-economic assessment and life-cycle assessment (TEA/LCA) evidence, conditional rules for evaluating integration, a qualitative regional pathway-selection matrix, and a dynamic-validation gap analysis linking demonstrated performance to availability, load-following, capacity factor, and degradation. No route is universally preferred; a defensible choice depends on consistent accounting and on regional electricity, carbon resources, industrial assets, and end use. The integration comparison distinguishes H2-to-CO2 power-to-methanol (PtM), H2-enhanced biomass/waste conversion, retrofit/carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) in fossil methanol hubs, and multi-source industrial symbiosis, and shows that no archetype is universally superior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Multi-material topology optimization of tunable multifunctional microstructures with nonlinear magnetic and thermal fields
abstract: Multi-material microstructures provide a versatile means for tailoring multiple macroscopic properties beyond those of monolithic materials. Achieving reliable magnetic performance while ensuring efficient heat dissipation is essential for magnetic devices and motivates the concurrent design of magnetic and thermal responses. In this context, multifunctional material systems offer an expanded design space for meeting such combined requirements. However, most existing studies on magnetic fields remain limited to single-material systems. To address this limitation, a novel multi-material inverse homogenization framework is proposed to facilitate microstructure design by considering both magnetic and thermal fields. In this approach, micromechanics-based homogenization is employed to evaluate effective properties. A discrete-material-optimization-based interpolation scheme was adopted to represent the spatial distribution of two-phase ferromagnetic materials with inherent trade-offs between magnetic permeability and thermal conductivity and was further modified using exponential interpolation to improve numerical characteristics. To obtain balanced multifunctional designs, a global criterion method was introduced to integrate multiple physical performance criteria into a unified objective function. Several numerical examples were presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The results showed that multi-material designs under multi-field conditions offer apparent benefits over their single-material or single-field counterparts and that considering magnetic nonlinearity leads to distinct design outcomes. Furthermore, systematic performance tuning was achieved through material volume fraction control, and directional magnetic responses were realized by introducing an additional orthotropy constraint. This study provides insights into the engineering design of hybrid material systems, highlighting the potential of multi-material and multi-field approaches for achieving controllable and application-relevant functional performance. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Compressive payoff-to-signal transduction can separate the start and sustain thresholds of cooperation
abstract: Cooperation is often difficult to start but easier to sustain once established. We ask whether this asymmetry can arise from payoff-to-signal transduction before objective payoffs enter action comparison. In a minimal contribution-sharing game, at a given return factor, cooperation has a net objective disadvantage relative to defection that does not vary with the local cooperative environment. When compressive transduction is applied separately to the two action payoffs, however, the transduced cooperation–defection comparison gap can vary across local environments. Population reweighting aggregates these environment-dependent local gaps into a state-dependent mean comparison signal, whose slope is governed by the environment–gap covariance. In the baseline response map, two branch points satisfy fixed-point self-consistency, tangency, and non-degeneracy, yielding distinct start and sustain thresholds. Analytical derivations, controls, and finite-population tests support this mechanism. The contribution lies in identifying and verifying the conditional cross-level chain linking compressive encoding, population reweighting, and adaptive updating. They also show that whether the deterministic threshold structure is clearly expressed in finite-time trajectories depends on whether the update process reads out the same-environment action gap. These results identify a cross-level mechanism in which payoff-to-signal transduction, population reweighting, and adaptive updating jointly separate the start and sustain thresholds of cooperation. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Mapping distribution system operators for electricity and gas around the world
abstract: This paper presents a global mapping of energy distribution system operators (DSOs). The mapping illustrates the variation in power and gas distribution sector utilities across the world. We analyze information on 194 electricity and 67 gas utilities serving capital cities in 194 countries. The paper compares information on size, ownership, degree of integration, performance and quality of service. We find a large degree of variation across the world with significant differences between continents and economic groupings. Overall, the paper highlights the significant challenges facing many distribution utilities in promoting the energy transition, given their very different starting points. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: Hand-in-river: Design of direction-dependent virtual cues of assistive/resistive force via auditory displacement and pitch variation
abstract: This paper investigates the role of sound-only manipulations in eliciting pseudo-force perception during lateral hand movements within a virtual river environment. Building on prior formative and exploratory studies, a pseudo-force feedback design is refined, leveraging two mechanisms: (i) auditory displacement, a spatial shift in the virtual, binaural position of the hand-in-river sound, creating a conflict between where the hand is felt and where it is heard; and (ii) pitch variation, making the sound splashier or calmer by raising or lowering its pitch, relying on learned touch–sound associations. No physical force is actuated and no haptic or kinesthetic response is measured; the manipulation is entirely auditory and the dependent measure is a forced-choice judgment. A within-subjects psychophysical experiment used a two-interval forced-choice (2IFC) protocol with a 2 × 2 factorial design, evaluating pitch variation and displacement for resistance (leftward movement against the flow) and assistance (rightward movement with the flow). Results showed that both restricting displacement and pitch increase reliably biased participants toward perceiving resistance, with pitch variation being the dominant factor—suggesting that spectral content carries more perceptual weight than localization—and no interaction between cues, indicating an additive effect. Conversely, aiding displacement and pitch decrease did not reliably bias participants toward perceiving assistance—though displacement exhibited a positive trend—revealing a potential direction-dependent asymmetry. These findings refine the design space of sound-based pseudo-force feedback for inclusive immersion among visually impaired users. Resistive cues can be tuned modularly to create pseudo-haptic boundaries for navigation, while assistance likely requires strategies beyond simply inverting resistive cues. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: N-LAS-IAM: Climate change in a balance-of-payments framework
abstract: Climate change is becoming a macro-financial development problem for peripheral economies, yet integrated assessment models remain poorly equipped to analyse climate vulnerability in externally constrained developing countries. Existing heterodox models are mostly closed or global, while balance-of-payments-constrained growth models treat climate in reduced form and incompletely formalise the financial channel. This paper introduces the N-LAS-IAM, a recursive framework coupling a Thirlwall–Hussain growth core with endogenous green structural change, capital flows under financial fragility, sovereign risk, and a climate module mapping global emissions into damages that feed back into profitability and sovereign fragility. Green structural change is endogenised through logistic diffusion equations governing trade income elasticities as functions of green R&D and the real exchange rate. The model is explored via Monte Carlo experiments in which damage intensity and climate-to-risk transmission vary while emissions, policy, and structural-change parameters remain fixed. Three results emerge. First, higher damage produces a more fragile debt regime with elevated spreads, tighter financing, and prolonged deleveraging. Second, damages widen the elasticity gap between exports and imports, slowing green upgrading and locking the economy into lower-sophistication trade patterns. Third, the damage-to-fragility relationship is nonlinear: below a threshold the economy absorbs shocks, but above it a self-reinforcing regime emerges where lower productivity, higher spreads, weaker inflows, and structural regression feed on one another. These findings suggest that physical damages erode policy capabilities by raising external finance costs when green investment is most needed, and that early mitigation may yield convex macroeconomic returns for peripheral economies under balance-of-payments constraints. © 2026 The Author(s). title: The structure and properties of the solid solution of high temperature piezoelectric ceramics: (1-x)Li0.5Bi2.5Nb2O9-xBi3TiNbO9
abstract: Bismuth layer-structured piezoelectric ceramics have long faced an inherent trade-off between piezoelectric performance and Curie temperature. A novel solid solution (1-x)Li0.5Bi2.5Nb2O9-xBi3TiNbO9 (denoted as (1-x)LBN-xBTN) was designed and fabricated via a conventional solid-state reaction method to achieve a synergistic improvement in both properties. With increasing BTN content, the rotation angle of the oxygen octahedra within the a-b plane increased, resulting in a more pronounced orthorhombic distortion. The Curie temperature rose from 833 °C to 896.3 °C. Furthermore, the refined grain size and increased relative density synergistically enhanced the breakdown electric field. The ferroelectric domains were more fully oriented under high electric fields, significantly improving the remnant polarization and piezoelectric response. The (1-x)LBN-xBTN series of ceramics achieved optimal overall performance when x = 0.5: TC = 861 °C, d33 = 13.0 pC/N, ρdc (at 500 °C) = 2.39 × 107 Ω·cm, demonstrating its promise for high-temperature applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Cognitive predictors of narrative retelling in early childhood
abstract: This study examined the associations between inhibitory control, working memory, inductive reasoning, awareness, and children’s narrative retelling abilities in early childhood. A total of 212 children aged 4–7 years participated in the study. Executive functions were assessed through measures of verbal and visuospatial working memory and inhibitory control, inductive reasoning was assessed using a Raven-like matrix task, and awareness was assessed through perceptual and inferential awareness tasks. Narrative retelling was evaluated using a story retelling task that captured multiple aspects of narrative performance. Correlational analyses indicated moderate associations between inhibitory control, working memory, and several narrative retelling indicators. Narrative retelling performance also increased significantly with age, indicating clear developmental gains from the preschool to the early school years. Structural equation modeling further showed that inhibitory control and verbal working memory were significant predictors of the latent narrative retelling construct, whereas visuospatial working memory and inductive reasoning were not significantly associated with narrative retelling. Awareness showed small but significant associations with certain narrative retelling indicators. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Comparative diagnostic utility of cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers in multiple sclerosis
abstract: Background Multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosis depends on clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data; the need for confirmatory cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers for differential diagnosis is a crucial step. Objective We aim to investigate and compare the diagnostic value of CSF markers (e.g., chitinase 3-like 1 (CHI3L1), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP)) compared to the established supportive diagnostic oligoclonal bands test (OCBs) in MS. Methods We collected 62 CSF samples from suspected MS patients with T2-Hyperintense lesions and investigated OCBs and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for NfL, CHI3L1, and GFAP. Results The CSF levels of NfL ( p < 0.001) and CHI3L1 ( p < 0.001) were significantly elevated in the MS group compared to the non-MS group, in contrast to GFAP ( p = 0.17). Diagnostic criteria for MS diagnosis was excellent for OCBs (Area under curve (AUC) = 0.978, p < 0.001; 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 0.929–1.000), good for CHI3L1 (AUC = 0.838, p < 0.001; 95% CI: 0.738–0.939), acceptable for NfL (AUC = 0.729, p = 0.003; 95% CI: 0.602–0.855) and poor for GFAP (AUC = 0.604, p = 0.173; 95% CI: 0.477–0.762). Conclusion Among the studied biomarkers, CHI3L1 showed potential as an adjunctive biomarker for discriminating MS from non-MS patients. Its diagnostic accuracy was higher than that of NfL in our cohort, but GFAP has limited diagnostic accuracy, which could restrict its use in MS diagnosis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Identifying and Mitigating Legal and Contractual Risks in BIM-Enabled Construction Projects: A Conceptual Framework
abstract: Building information modeling (BIM) is accelerating across Saudi Arabia's construction sector in support of Vision 2030, yet its legal and contractual integration lags behind technical adoption. This study investigates the legal and contractual risks associated with BIM-enabled project delivery and proposes a conceptual framework to guide risk mitigation in the Saudi context. A total of 21 BIM-related legal risk factors were identified from a comprehensive literature review and refined through a pilot study. An online questionnaire survey was administered to construction practitioners (consultants and contractors), yielding 87 valid responses for analysis. Principal component analysis revealed two latent dimensions: legal and regulatory ambiguities and BIM model management and technical risks. Mean-rank analysis identified the lack of coordination and control over the BIM model, lack of clarity regarding BIM standards and processes in the contract, and unclear rights and responsibilities related to BIM were ranked as the top risk factors. Synthesizing the empirical findings with mitigation strategies identified through an extensive literature review, the study developed a seven-pillar conceptual framework for risk mitigation: (1) standardization and legal infrastructure; (2) contractual clarity and enforceability; (3) roles, responsibilities, and liability; (4) ownership and intellectual property; (5) confidentiality and security; (6) data integrity and interoperability; and (7) collaboration and dispute resolution. The findings extend the limited scholarship on BIM's legal and contractual risks in Saudi Arabia and offer context-aware guidance for policymakers and practitioners to embed BIM-specific provisions aimed at mitigating dispute propensity in BIM-enabled construction projects. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: HeRaKT: Heterogeneous bidirectional modeling for response-aware knowledge tracing
abstract: Knowledge Tracing (KT) aims to predict future performance of learners by modeling the evolving knowledge states from historical interactions. Existing methods typically do not distinguish the semantic roles of responses and encode them in a unified structure, thereby overlooking the heterogeneous semantics between correct and incorrect interactions. In this paper, we conduct empirical analyses revealing that responses with the same correctness label as the prediction target contribute positively to performance, whereas those of the opposite type introduce semantic noise. Motivated by this finding, we propose a novel Heterogeneous bidirectional modeling framework for Response-aware Knowledge Tracing (HeRaKT). To explore the underutilized semantic heterogeneity of learner responses, we design a path-separated architecture for handling heterogeneous signals with distinct inductive biases. To further enrich each path with broader bidirectional response-level signals, we devise a cloze-style training strategy which aggregates both past and future responses without label leakage. Extensive experiments on multiple public KT benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, validating the importance of explicitly modeling response heterogeneity and leveraging bidirectional response contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Structural integration of inert porous media as a primary mitigation strategy for firewood stoves: Toward decoupling combustion intensification from emissions
abstract: Residential wood combustion in energy-vulnerable contexts creates a critical trade-off between thermal comfort and air quality, while many conventional emission-control technologies require electricity, maintenance, or active control. This study evaluates the structural integration of inert porous media (IPM) within a commercial residential wood stove as a passive primary mitigation strategy. Combustion cycles, conducted following an adapted EPA Method 5G protocol, compared the baseline stove with the IPM-integrated prototype. IPM operation showed a tendency toward a more intensive fuel-conversion regime together with thermal redistribution toward the stove enclosure. Median thermal efficiency was 29.3 % higher, while exhaust-gas temperature decreased by 6.0 % and outer lateral-wall temperature increased by 18.8 %. Despite the higher burning rate, PM2.5 and CO mass emission factors showed directional decreases of 65.5 % and 30.9 %, respectively; HC remained essentially unchanged, whereas NOx increased. Particle-number emission factors were lower across most of the measured 0.253–35.15 µm size range. Useful-energy normalization strengthened the environmental benefit, with PM2.5 and CO decreasing by 76.3 % and 33.4 % per unit of useful heat delivered; HC shifted toward a lower burden, whereas the NOx increase was attenuated but remained. Overall, the findings support a pollutant-specific tendency toward decoupling combustion intensification from incomplete-combustion emissions and identify structural IPM integration as a promising passive strategy for improving residential wood-heating performance without auxiliary energy input, particularly where affordability and operational simplicity constrain advanced emission-control technologies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Do smiling faces change children’s minds? Testing evaluative conditioning in 3–6‑year‑olds
abstract: This study examined whether preschoolers form preferences for shapes paired with happy or sad faces (evaluative conditioning) and whether the effect varies with age or with the number of different faces paired with each shape. Sixty-one children aged 3–6 years viewed four neutral shapes during a brief conditioning movie. Each shape was assigned to one of four conditions, in which it was paired with a single happy face, a single sad face, five different happy faces, or five different sad faces. Shape preferences were measured before and after the movie, along with memory for the pairings. Children showed clear pre-existing preferences for some shapes, and the pattern differed by age. After accounting for these starting preferences, two additive advantages emerged (for positive over negative faces and for multiple over single faces) and their combination in the shape paired with multiple smiling faces was the only condition to produce a reliable shift from zero. The other three conditions did not produce reliable change, and children’s exact age and memory for the pairings did not predict change. These findings suggest that evaluative conditioning in preschoolers is more selective than typically assumed, with the number of different faces paired with a shape emerging as a key factor. The results also highlight the importance of accounting for children’s pre-existing preferences when measuring acquired evaluative learning. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Research on multi-behavior recommendation model via relational graph attention networks based on knowledge graph
abstract: In practical recommendation scenarios such as social media and e-commerce, users engage in diverse interactions with items, including browsing, favoriting, adding to cart, and purchasing. However, traditional recommendation techniques still face limitations: (1) the neglect of differential values across diverse interactions; (2) the persistent challenge of user cold-start problems; and (3) the blurring of individual preference boundaries caused by an over-reliance on group-level characteristics, which leads to inadequate modeling of individualized preferences. To address these challenges, we propose the Multi-behavior Recommendation Model Based on Knowledge Graph and Relationship Graph Attention Network (MBRGAT). First, we construct a dual-layer attention architecture: at the micro level, node-level attention precisely captures the intensity of user preferences for different items; at the macro level, behavior-level attention dynamically learns the contribution weights of diverse behaviors to purchase prediction. This facilitates end-to-end quantification of behavioral significance, resolving the issue of uniform interaction weighting. Second, we design a cold-start preference transfer framework based on Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) clustering. By modeling preference groups through multiple Gaussian distributions, the framework assigns cluster membership probabilities to users, establishing reliable carriers for preference transfer to cold-start users. Finally, we implement a contrastive learning mechanism with a dual-layer intra-group and inter-group architecture. Training is optimized through dynamic sample-weight allocation, enhancing individual expression while accounting for group commonality. Comprehensive experiments across three public datasets–Yelp, Tmall, and Taobao–demonstrate that our framework offers significant advantages over state-of-the-art methods. The code is available at https://github.com/meywi959/MBRGAT.git. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Regional heterogeneity in the relationship between temperature and household electricity consumption across rural South Africa
abstract: In this study we examine the heterogeneous effects of temperature on household electricity consumption using combined hourly electricity consumption and temperature data across several rural areas in South Africa. We apply a panel data regression model controlling for temperature bin dummies to capture nonlinear temperature effects, as well as a set of fixed effects to capture the unobserved heterogeneity across households and over time. We find that the temperature–consumption relationship varies across geographical locations and is characterised predominantly by inverse J-shaped and inverse U-shaped patterns, which differs from the typical U-shaped curve in the literature. This study deepens the understanding of the complex and heterogeneous effect of temperature on household electricity consumption in a developing-country context, highlighting substantial variation across climatic and geographic regions within the same country. © 2026 The Authors. title: Women-Led Wildfire Disaster Adaptations within and from Indigenous Knowledge Perspectives
abstract: This study examines Indigenous women-led wildfire disaster adaptations through traditional environmental knowledge and community-led strategies. Centering Indigenous traditional story sharing, intergenerational learning, and land stewardship, Indigenous women serve as key leaders in wildfire prevention and forest management. The research highlights the role of Indigenous fire governance in sustainable land management and the critical intersection between traditional knowledge and Western scientific tools in Chang Mai, Thailand. Using decolonial methodologies, the study highlights the necessity of Indigenous women leadership in climate-resilience efforts. Findings reveal that Indigenous women's practices contribute significantly to biodiversity conservation, climate adaptation, and community-led disaster response. The study calls for stronger academic engagement with Indigenous knowledge and policy reforms that center Indigenous women's expertise into global forest fire governance. The research provides a foundation for future transdisciplinary collaborations, advocating for Indigenous women's leadership in sustainable wildfire management. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Wedge-index based butterfly counting in bipartite graphs
abstract: Butterfly counting is a key metric in the analysis of bipartite networks. Existing butterfly counting techniques are primarily classified into two categories: layer-priority-based and vertex-priority-based methods. Both approaches compute the number of butterflies in bipartite graphs by enumerating wedges from the neighbor lists of vertices. The state-of-the-art algorithms typically adopt vertex-priority-based techniques, where priorities are assigned to vertices, enabling the enumeration of fewer wedges during the butterfly counting process.In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient wedge-based index for bipartite graphs, referred to as the WB-index (Wedge-based Bipartite Index), designed to accelerate butterfly counting. We introduce two variants of the WB-index based on the two primary butterfly counting principles. By performing a single traversal of the WB-index, we can compute three types of butterfly statistics: the total number of butterflies in the bipartite graph, the number of butterflies for each vertex, and the number of butterflies for each edge. These three computations are implemented by the algorithms BFC-WB, VBFC-WB, and EBFC-WB, respectively. Furthermore, when the bipartite graph undergoes changes, butterfly counting can still be performed efficiently by maintaining the index without the need for reconstruction, especially for medium-scale graphs. Experimental results show that BFC-WB substantially improves butterfly counting efficiency compared with state-of-the-art vertex-priority algorithms, achieving speedups of 66× to 103×. © 2026

title: Conventional salmon or novel salmon alternatives? An evaluation of consumers' perceptions and stated willingness to eat across different salmon concepts in Switzerland
abstract: In response to public concern about human health, fish welfare, and the environment, the salmon industry is seeking alternative ways of producing salmon with novel technologies such as land-based recirculated aquaculture systems, cell cultivation, and 3D printing. We conducted an online study to investigate consumers' attitudes towards different salmon production techniques. A total of 237 participants from Switzerland evaluated five salmon concepts (i.e., wild-caught, ocean-farmed, land-farmed 3D-printed cultured, and 3D-printed plant-based salmon), which were presented together with one of two final salmon product images (i.e., salmon fillet vs. sticks). Both qualitative data (initial association related to concerns and benefits) and quantitative data (evaluation facets) were assessed. The quantitative findings showed that the wild-caught salmon concept was the most favored with ocean- and land-based salmon concepts in second place. For the 3D-printed cultured and 3D-printed plant-based salmon concepts, participants stated the lowest stated willingness to eat. Fish attachment positively predicted stated willingness to eat for the land-based salmon concept. Concern about the environment and climate change positively predicted stated willingness to eat for the 3D-printed plant-based salmon concept. Food technology neophobia negatively predicted stated willingness to eat for the salmon alternative concepts. In addition, age was negatively associated with stated willingness to eat for the 3D-printed cultured and 3D-printed plant-based salmon concepts. Future salmon production and relevant research should therefore not only consider how to meet consumers' expectations on food healthiness, tastiness, and environmental friendliness but also focus on developing strategies for addressing food technology neophobia and building trust among consumers. © 2026

title: Electrospray preparation of Fe-PMMA films for one-drop analysis of thiocyanate a tobacco biomarker as a case study
abstract: In this work, a single-step electrospray strategy for the fabrication of colorimetric films based on FeCl3 immobilized within a poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) matrix was developed. Electrospray parameters were optimized to obtain stable and uniform coatings using sustainable and non-hazardous solvents. The films enable one-drop thiocyanate analysis as a case study, with a rapid response (1 min), monitored by microvolume UV–vis spectrophotometry. The method was successfully applied to saliva samples treated by an optimized in-tip solid-phase extraction procedure. Thiocyanate levels of 0.57 – 0.80 mM and 1.3 – 2.0 mM were found for non-smokers and smokers, respectively, allowing to discriminate between saliva samples from smoker and non-smoker volunteers. In addition, the film exhibited good storage stability at 4 °C for at least one month. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Know its worth? Factors affecting the social acceptability of water reuse: A mixed methods planned behavior model
abstract: Due to strong demographic pressure, rapid urban development, and climate change, water demand is increasing while usable freshwater supplies are being depleted. The reuse of treated wastewater (RTWW) is one of the avenues currently being explored to ensure the quantitative and qualitative security of the water supply. The interests for social acceptability emerged with risk management approaches and the subsequent debates on the role of technical progress, the implementation of major development projects, and their consequences for the environment between the late 1970s and early 1980s. The purpose of this article is to identify the factors that influence the building of RTWW acceptability. This study was carried out in southern France. It combines a quantitative survey on behavior related to engaging in RTWW, based on Ajzen's theory of planned behavior, with a qualitative socioeconomic study aimed at understanding representations and beliefs regarding RTWW. The findings show that a lack of knowledge about RTWW and the implementation of only a few RTWW projects result in a normative gap and a perceived lack of control. In addition, trust in managers and public authorities, the quality of treatments, as well as risks perceptions – particularly those relating to health – significantly influence intentions to engage in RTWW. Lastly, several factors such as emotions, types of uses, and environmental awareness play an underlying role by helping build perceptions of water reuse, trust in relevant stakeholders, and more accurate perceptions of risks. © 2026 The Authors. title: Adaptive loss-based random Fourier filtering with complementary adaptation: Algorithm design and performance analysis
abstract: Random Fourier features (RFF) based adaptive filtering provides an efficient tool for nonlinear modeling by approximating kernel mappings with finite-dimensional feature representations. However, existing RFF-based filters typically rely on quadratic loss functions and fixed adaptation strategies, making them vulnerable to non-Gaussian disturbances and limiting their ability to balance convergence speed and steady-state accuracy. To address these issues, a new adaptive filtering framework in the RFF domain is proposed. The framework incorporates an adaptive loss function with an adjustable shape parameter to improve robustness under non-Gaussian and impulsive noise environments. In addition, two RFF-based filters with complementary adaptation characteristics are combined through a convex combination strategy, providing a favorable trade-off between convergence rate and steady-state performance. The steady-state performance analysis of the proposed filtering framework is presented, which characterizes its steady-state behavior under mild assumptions. Simulation results validate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method under various noise conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Evolution of cooperation in spatial public goods games via Q-learning with random walks
abstract: This study investigates the evolution of cooperation in spatial public goods games with overlapping local groups. Considering that learning outcomes depend not only on the update rule itself but also on the information available to learners, we introduce random walks into Q-learning to incorporate multistep spatial information, and a Random Walk Weighted Q-Learning mechanism is constructed. Secondly, under such a mechanism, we conduct numerical simulations. Simulation results indicate that the RWQ mechanism achieves higher cooperation levels than Self-Q, Direct-Q, and Global-Q, and also shows an advantage over Unweighted k-hop-Q in the low synergy region. Further analyses of social state perception and learned Q-value provide additional insight into the mechanism underlying the promotion of cooperation. Finally, we employ sensitivity analyses with respect to the state resolution, information range, random walk decay factor, exploration rate, learning rate, and discount factor, and the results further confirm the robustness of this cooperative advantage. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Ecological mechanisms and bifurcation dynamics in a mathematical model of African wild dogs
abstract: The African wild dog (Lycaon pictus) is an endangered species, they live in cooperative packs led by alpha males and females, responsible for breeding and hunting. Young members disperse to maintain genetic diversity, while integration from other packs is welcomed. Pack size is crucial for survival: small packs struggle to hunt and face extinction, whereas large packs face challenges in feeding and raising pups. A mathematical model of predator–prey dynamics includes three roles within the predator population: pups and breeding helpers, active hunters, and dispersing individuals. The study demonstrates the fundamental role of social structure and cooperation in predator–prey dynamics. By incorporating Allee effects and dispersal, the model provides a more realistic representation of population viability in social carnivores and offers quantitative guidance for conservation of endangered cooperative species such as African wild dogs. Bifurcation analysis identifies critical thresholds separating steady and oscillatory regimes: Allee effects lower the threshold for oscillatory onset and amplify their intensity. At the same time, dispersal acts as a stabilizing force, delaying oscillatory behavior and enhancing population persistence. Numerical simulations reveal that Allee effects lengthen and amplify population cycles, particularly during socially dependent life stages, thereby increasing vulnerability at low densities. The existence of stable limit cycles confirms the persistence of oscillatory dynamics and enables detailed characterization of their periods. Furthermore, employing bifurcation analysis, which includes both Hopf and transcritical bifurcations, reveals critical transitions in system behavior as key parameters change. This analysis offers insights into the conditions necessary for stability. © 2026 International Association for Mathematics and Computers in Simulation (IMACS).

title: Enhancing computational thinking through unplugged activities in elementary education: A systematic literature review
abstract: This study aims to analyze the role of unplugged activities in enhancing computational thinking (CT) skills among elementary school students through a systematic literature review. Using the systematic literature review design guided by the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses) framework, the study examines 34 relevant empirical studies. Data collection involved literature searches in multiple electronic databases using keywords related to unplugged activities and CT concepts. The data were analyzed using a coding scheme covering methodological characteristics, subject area, types of unplugged activities and tools, contextual factors, challenges and suitability. The findings indicate that unplugged activities can support the development of computational thinking skills, particularly in resource-limited environments. Reported contextual factors associated with variation in outcomes include learner age, year level, curriculum and school support. However, challenges such as inadequate teacher training, difficulties in curriculum integration, and the lack of standardized assessment tools persist. The implications of this study suggest that unplugged activities can serve as an inclusive and cost-effective pedagogical tool for teaching CT skills in elementary education. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Physics-constrained spatiotemporal modeling for temporal localization in structured multichannel acoustic signals
abstract: Temporal localization in structured multichannel acoustic signals, such as first-arrival picking in geophysical logging, is a fundamental yet challenging task. Traditional signal processing methods rely heavily on manual heuristics, while existing data-driven deep learning approaches often overlook the inherent physical priors of multichannel arrays, resulting in a trade-off among accuracy, stability, and real-time performance in field applications. To address these challenges, we propose FA-Picker, a physics-constrained spatiotemporal modeling framework for first-arrival picking. This model explicitly incorporates the depth dimension to construct a three-dimensional input data volume, enabling the capture of joint spatiotemporal features across multiple receivers and consecutive measurements. Moreover, an end-to-end multi-task architecture is designed, where coarse first-arrival segmentation guides continuous arrival-time regression. A dual-constraint mechanism is introduced, combining soft loss-based guidance with hard physical constraints, ensuring that the localized temporal points strictly comply with the underlying wave propagation laws. Furthermore, to alleviate the scarcity of high-quality labeled data, we exploit the highly structured characteristics of multichannel acoustic arrays to develop a comprehensive synthetic data generation workflow that simulates diverse formation variations and acquisition environments. Experimental results on field datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed modeling and data augmentation strategies, showing the superior performance of FA-Picker in practical first-arrival picking tasks. The code is available at: https://github.com/longw0110/Synthetic-workflow-for-FA-Picker. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Rapid inter-individual vocal interactions in freely behaving rats revealed by acoustic source localization
abstract: Ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) in rodents have been widely used as indicators of affective states; however, their role in rapid temporal exchange between individuals remains largely unexplored, primarily due to technical limitations in identifying vocalizing individuals during free social interactions. Here, we combined acoustic source localization (USVCAM) with markerless multi-animal tracking to examine the temporal structure of vocal interactions in freely behaving rat dyads. In three dyads with sufficient vocal output, inter-individual vocalization intervals exhibited a clear peak at approximately 50–250 ms, indicating fast temporal exchanges of vocalizations between individuals. To test whether this pattern could arise from independent vocal production, we performed Monte Carlo randomized simulations based on empirically observed intra-individual intervals. The simulated distributions failed to reproduce the empirical peak and instead showed a concentration at shorter intervals, resulting in a significant distributional difference. These results reject the null hypothesis of independent vocal generation and suggest that the observed temporal structure reflects the influence of one individual's vocalizations on those of the other individual. Together, these findings extend the potential applications of rodent USVs, in addition to their established use as affective indicators, by providing a proof-of-principle demonstration of rapid inter-individual vocal exchanges and a tractable experimental framework for investigating the temporal dynamics of social vocal communication. © 2026 The Authors

title: A dynamic fusion enhanced trajectory distillation framework for multi-view classification
abstract: Multi-view classification incorporates multiple views to improve classification performance. However, in real-world scenarios, different views often exhibit unequal informativeness, which poses challenges to learning discriminative representations. Existing fusion methods mainly rely on weighting or attention mechanisms, which can mitigate redundancy but still lack explicit semantic guidance for discriminative representation learning. To address this issue, we propose a novel dynamic fusion enhanced trajectory distillation method for multi-view classification. Specifically, we develop a dynamic fusion module that enhances discriminative learning and adaptive multi-view fusion by incorporating label embeddings as explicit semantic guidance. Furthermore, we propose a trajectory distillation strategy to prevent the risk of inference-time label leakage while ensuring effective knowledge transfer, thereby enabling the student model to inherit the representation capability of the teacher model without relying on label information during inference. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method consistently achieves superior performance and learns more discriminative representations for multi-view classification. Our code is available at https://github.com/Hige6010/DEFT. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
