title: Rapid microwave-assisted synthesis of ZnMn dual-atom nanozymes for cancer catalytic immunotherapy
abstract: Catalytic nanomedicines face a persistent trade-off between structurally defined active sites and rapid synthesis. A microwave-assisted salt-flux conversion is developed that transforms a bimetallic metal-organic framework precursor within 3 min into nitrogen-doped carbon-supported ZnMn dual-atom nanozymes (ZnMn DAzymes). Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM and dual-edge X-ray absorption fine structure analyses support adjacent Zn-Mn sites with an N-dominated ZnMn-N6-like coordination motif. Steady-state kinetics and density functional theory calculations suggest cooperative catalysis: Zn modulates H2O2 adsorption and O-O bond activation, whereas Mn provides stronger H2O2 chemisorption and redox flexibility, jointly enhancing catalase-, peroxidase-, and oxidase-like activities. The resulting cascade decomposes H2O2, relieves hypoxia, generates reactive oxygen species, and depletes glutathione, inducing mitochondrial dysfunction, immunogenic cell death, cGAS-STING-associated signaling, dendritic-cell maturation, and effector T-cell infiltration. Glutathione-responsive Mn2+ release additionally enables activatable T1-weighted magnetic resonance contrast. Combined with αPD-L1, ZnMn DAzymes suppress primary and distal tumors by approximately 90%, reduce lung metastases by 92%, and prolong survival in 4T1 models. This work provides a rapid route to ZnMn dual-atom nanozymes for catalytic immunotherapy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Evaluating SHAP feature selection guided by a biomechanical prior for offline knee angle estimation from sEMG
abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) supports continuous knee-angle estimation, but predictive feature importance can diverge from expected patterns of muscle activity. This study evaluated a literature-informed biomechanical prior as a guide for feature selection and quantified its relation to predictive performance and agreement between model attribution and the prior. The proposed offline framework combines window-level sEMG descriptors with phase-stratified Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). A muscle-level Bio-Consistency Score (BCS) quantifies prior–attribution agreement, whereas a feature-level Phase-Profile Concordance (PPC) term guides selection alongside global importance and redundancy. Trajectory-cycle bins were assigned retrospectively from synchronised knee-angle records. Evaluation used 15 participants in an outer leave-one-subject-out design, with feature selection confined to an inner training–validation split. Cross-dataset analyses used a common four-channel, 48-feature candidate space and six target participants. The prior-guided selector retained 10.20 of 132 features on average, with a mean root mean squared error of 14.15∘, compared with 13.14∘ for the complete feature set. Selected subsets had a mean pairwise Jaccard similarity of 0.162. Prior guidance produced a less negative mean BCS, but no method-by-fold permutation test provided evidence of a statistically significant departure from the muscle-label reference. In cross-dataset analyses, none of the multiplicity-adjusted paired comparisons was statistically significant for prior-guided selection versus matched controls, warm-start adaptation versus from-scratch fitting, or teacher-target blending versus observed-target training. The results quantify the trade-off among input dimensionality, attribution concordance, and predictive accuracy under the evaluated protocol. This framework provides a reproducible basis for examining these properties of knowledge-guided sEMG feature selection. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Dual-view contrastive learning for heterogeneous graph representation
abstract: Representation learning on heterogeneous graphs relies on exploiting both diverse semantics and intricate structural relations. However, the common approaches struggle to simultaneously account for distant semantic interactions and fine-grained structural patterns. Therefore, we introduce a novel Heterogeneous Graph Representation Learning method via a dual-view contrastive structure (HGRL). Specifically, the Schema-aware Graph Abstraction Module (SGAM) captures relational dependencies using a type-aware graph neural network augmented with adaptive residual pathways to learn structural representations. Moreover, the Mamba-based Semantic Reasoner (MSR) utilizes a globally-enhanced Mamba backbone with multi-scale fusion and directional positional encodings to model high-order semantic dependencies. Furthermore, we design a dynamic bidirectional contrastive learning framework that aligns the semantic and structural views, where each view serves as a form of learnable augmentation and mutual supervision for the other, thereby fostering robust and mutually-enriched representations. Comprehensive experiments on six benchmark datasets show that HGRL achieves competitive or superior performance relative to representative state-of-the-art methods across node classification and clustering tasks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A unified instance selection approach based on distributional similarity for machine learning
abstract: In this study, we propose a unified instance selection approach, applicable to both regression and classification tasks, that selects a reduced dataset whose distribution matches that of the original, thereby preserving its key statistical and structural properties. Our central contribution is to analytically show that the instance selection problem, aiming to ensure distributional similarity measured via the Wasserstein distance, is exactly equivalent to the balanced k-medoid problem when the compression ratio is integer-valued. We further extend this equivalence to arbitrary (non-integer) ratios with explicit bounds on the resulting approximation error. This equivalence allows the instance selection problem to be addressed directly with existing balanced k-medoid solvers. To this end, we employ a Lloyd-style alternating (EM-type) constrained k-medoid algorithm, obtained by extending an existing constrained clustering method. Extensive experiments across binary classification, multi-class classification, and regression tasks confirm the method's effectiveness: it significantly outperforms the task-specific baseline at most reduction ratios on all seven multi-class datasets (Wilcoxon, p<0.05), outperforms the boundary-focused baseline on the majority of binary settings—most clearly on the higher-dimensional datasets—and attains lower error on four of five regression datasets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: SPECTRA: Sequential prismatic ensemble and cross-domain transfer residual alignment for multimodal multi-domain fake news detection
abstract: The task of multimodal multi-domain fake news detection is to identify the fake news from multiple domains with mixed textual and visual contents. Technically, the existing methods face the following problems: domain feature alignment bias, cross-domain negative transfer under long-tail distributions, and modality interaction vulnerability to domain interference. To address these problems, in this paper, we propose an approach with Sequential Prismatic Ensemble and Cross-domain Transfer Residual Alignment Network for this task, which is abbreviated as SPECTRA for clarity. Specifically, a domain-aware alignment mechanism in terms of Gaussian mixture model is built to perform the dynamic distribution alignment in the feature space. A sequential prismatic fusion network based on orthogonal latent variables is designed to capture concealed cross-modal logical misalignments. Moreover, a dynamic domain knowledge transfer strategy by using residual-query pattern is developed to ensure the effective reconstruction of features in sparse long-tail domains and overcome the phenomenon of cross-domain negative transfer. Experimental results on three real-world datasets demonstrate that SPECTRA outperforms the state-of-the-art methods, showing its effectiveness on fake news detection in complex multi-domain scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: RFEP-SI-Fed: Fuzzy risk-entropy prediction safety island with federated reinforcement learning for low-carbon dispatch of nitrogen-hydrogen-ammonia coupled multi-park integrated energy systems
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy requires multi-park integrated energy systems (IESs) to coordinate electricity, heat, cooling, hydrogen, ammonia, and nitrogen while retaining local operational data and screening safety-critical actions before execution. This study proposes RFEP-SI-Fed, which integrates a six-carrier N2-H2-NH3 dispatch model, risk-weighted fuzzy-entropy assessment with Green/Yellow/Red Safety Island control, and FedProx-based PPO coordination. In the original three-park representative-day benchmark, aggregate operating cost decreased from 46,640 to 38,960 CNY/day (16.5%) and aggregate carbon-trading cost decreased from 5460 to 3590 CNY/day (34.2%) relative to the NoMonitor baseline. Warning coverage ranged from 92.1% to 94.7%, the average warning lead time was 22.4 min, and the complete configuration achieved a 96% survival rate in the reported ablation evaluation. The extended evaluation used three independent training seeds, six program-generated out-of-distribution scenarios, 3-, 6-, and 12-park systems, communication-delay and client-dropout tests, optimizer comparisons, and parameter screening. From 3 to 12 parks, mean server-side aggregation latency increased from 11.45 ± 2.92 to 40.79 ± 6.62 ms, while mean cost per park increased by 2.42%. One- to three-round aggregation delays increased paired mean cost by 4.57–5.66%. Across the tests of six limited scenarios, the complete framework is consistently constrained within the predefined risk envelope, which demonstrates that the proposed method realizes a clear trade-off between safety and economic cost. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Full-scale experimental investigation of rockfall impact on EPS geofoam-cushioned composite vertical rigid barriers
abstract: Expanded polystyrene (EPS) geofoam is a promising sacrificial cushioning material for rockfall protection, yet its full-scale performance in composite vertical rigid barriers remains insufficiently quantified. This study investigates the lateral rockfall impact response of an EPS-cushioned composite barrier through a full-scale L9 orthogonal test program. The barrier comprised a 1.8-m-thick EPS cushion, a reinforced-concrete load-distribution slab, force-sensor assemblies, and a rigid supporting wall. Rockfall mass and EPS density were selected as nominal factors. Transmitted force and block acceleration were measured synchronously, while impact velocity, rebound, and translational kinetic-energy change were derived from high-speed video. Results revealed a clear stiffness–deformability trade-off: higher-density EPS resisted local penetration more effectively but generally produced higher peak transmitted forces and lower translational kinetic-energy loss fractions. The measured kinetic-energy loss ranged from 35.92% to 47.56% and decreased consistently with increasing EPS density within each rockfall-mass group. The system response resulted from EPS compression and crushing, lateral load spreading, and subsequent load redistribution through the RC slab. These findings demonstrate the potential of replaceable EPS geofoam as an effective frontal sacrificial layer for improving the impact-mitigation performance of composite vertical rigid rockfall barriers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: Effective algorithms for tensor-train decomposition via the UTV framework
abstract: The tensor-train (TT) decomposition is widely used to compress large tensors into a more compact form by exploiting their inherent data structures. A fundamental approach for constructing the TT format is the well-known TT-SVD method, which performs singular value decompositions (SVDs) on the successive unfolding matrices sequentially. But in practical applications, it is often unnecessary to compute full SVDs. In this article, we propose the TT-UTV method, a general framework that incorporates the family of UTV-type algorithms to compute the TT decomposition. As an extension of TT-SVD, it can choose rank-revealing UTV factorizations for the extraction of core tensors, enabling more efficient handling of large-scale intermediate unfolding matrices. We further analyze the error propagation of each step within the TT-UTV framework, and derive a tight overall error bound. Based on this analysis, we recommend distinct sweep patterns for the ULV and URV cases, and formulate the rank-adaptive algorithms with prescribed accuracy. Numerical experiments on various datasets, including magnetic resonance imaging data completion, demonstrate their good performance in practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
label: Social Sciences

title: Plug-and-play watermarking method for diffusion models via distribution alignment
abstract: Generative models are widely distributed to multiple users, raising significant concerns about tracing malicious content dissemination. While watermarking is a common solution, existing methods struggle to support scalable multi-user scenarios and maintain watermark integrity under adversarial manipulations. To address these issues, we propose a plug-and-play watermarking method for diffusion models based on distribution alignment, enabling effective detection and per-user traceability. Specifically, watermarks are embedded directly into latent representations without altering diffusion model parameters, allowing seamless deployment and replacement across different users. Our method leverages the connection between latent representations and generated images to ensure high watermark accuracy. Furthermore, we enforce distribution constraints to couple watermark integrity with image utility. This mechanism ensures that generated content inherently carries the watermark while neutralizing malicious bypass attempts. Experimental results demonstrate our method’s high effectiveness, achieving average true positive rates exceeding 95% for both detection and traceability under various complex distortions. Crucially, the framework thwarts Quality-Constrained Evasion (QCE) by forcing the semantic quality of tampered images to drop to unusable levels (CLIP score < 0.2). Collectively, our method provides a robust and secure plug-and-play framework for tracing the source of generated content in generative AI deployment scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: Multi-source Heterogeneous Data Fusion with Graph-Aware Dual Contrastive Learning for drug–drug interaction prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of drug–drug interactions (DDIs) is vital for patient safety and therapeutic efficacy. Recently, DDI prediction methods based on graph neural networks and multi-source heterogeneous drug information have made progress. However, most existing multimodal DDI prediction methods still fail to fully integrate multi-source heterogeneous drug information and effectively exploit the complementary information across different modalities, making it difficult to fully capture the sequential, structural, and semantic characteristics of drugs, thereby limiting the quality of drug representations and DDI prediction performance. To address these limitations, we propose MHGCL, a Multi-source Heterogeneous Data Fusion with Graph-Aware Dual Contrastive Learning framework, designed for DDI prediction. Initially, we construct a comprehensive drug representation by integrating four modalities: drug SMILES sequences, protein target sequences, molecular graphs, and a biomedical knowledge graph (KG) to holistically capture and incorporate the sequential, structural, and semantic information of drugs. Next, we design a graph-structure-aware adaptive subgraph extraction strategy that selects the optimal sampling method based on the structural properties of the KG, and propose a dual contrastive learning mechanism to enhance the quality of feature representations for both molecular graphs and KGs. Finally, we construct a cross-modal self-attention fusion module that achieves dynamic interaction and deep integration of heterogeneous modality features. Experimental results on three real-world drug datasets demonstrate that MHGCL significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art methods, validating its effectiveness for DDI prediction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
label: Social Sciences

title: Nursing faculty perspectives on integrating emerging technologies in undergraduate nursing education: A qualitative descriptive study
abstract: Background: Emerging technologies (ET), including virtual, augmented, mixed, and extended reality alongside simulation-based tools, are increasingly available for undergraduate nursing education, yet their institutional and pedagogical integration remains uneven. Nursing faculty are central to this process, but their own experiences and perceptions of adopting ET have received limited empirical attention. Aim: To explore nursing faculty's experiences and perceptions of integrating emerging technologies into undergraduate nursing education. Design: Qualitative descriptive study with a contextual quantitative component. Settings: Three university nursing faculties in Spain. Participants: Twenty-two nursing faculty members. Methods: Three focus groups were conducted and analyzed using template analysis, a form of thematic analysis. An ad hoc questionnaire provided descriptive data on participants' self-reported experience with specific technologies, used to contextualize the qualitative findings. Results: Three themes emerged: Resources and Integration, Teaching and Learning, and Navigating the Digital Divide in Nursing Education. Faculty recognized the pedagogical value of ET, particularly of well-established tools such as high-fidelity simulation, but identified limited institutional support, unequal training opportunities, and concerns about preserving humanistic and relational aspects of care as central barriers. Low-cost technologies already accessible to most institutions were seen as a complement to, rather than a replacement for, theoretical instruction. Conclusions: Nursing faculty view emerging technologies as pedagogically valuable but constrained by institutional support, training, and equity considerations. Because this study captures the perspective of faculty only, future research should examine how nursing students experience these same tensions. © 2026
label: Social Sciences

title: VoXaaS: Safety-governed service orchestration with risk-aware volunteering for vehicular micro-edge computing
abstract: Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC) enables connected vehicles to collaboratively provide sensing and computing services beyond their primary driving functions. However, existing orchestration approaches mostly optimize Quality-of-Service (QoS) metrics and treat vehicles as generic resource providers, without explicitly considering real-time driving safety. This may result in unsafe service participation under demanding traffic or operational conditions. To address this limitation, we propose VoXaaS (Vehicle-oriented eXecution as a Service), a safety-governed vehicular micro-edge computing framework that regulates service participation according to driving risk, resource availability, and provider reliability. The framework introduces Safety-Aware Volunteering (SAV), a continuous risk-driven mechanism for regulating participation in cooperative service execution. SAV determines service eligibility, contribution type, and contribution capacity while ensuring that safety constraints remain dominant over service optimization objectives. VoXaaS further combines risk-aware provider qualification with trust- and QoS-aware orchestration to support dependable cooperative vehicular services. We evaluate the proposed framework through extensive simulations using realistic vehicular mobility traces and increasing service demand levels. Experimental results show that VoXaaS reduces selected-provider risk by more than 80% compared with QoS-based and trust-based orchestration baselines while completely eliminating unsafe volunteering. Unlike conventional safety-preserving approaches that rely on admission throttling, VoXaaS maintains full task admission under increasing service load. As a result, it achieves the highest task success rate and delivers up to 14% higher throughput than competing approaches while incurring only moderate latency overhead. The results demonstrate that explicit safety governance can significantly improve orchestration dependability while maintaining strong service performance under the evaluated service-load conditions. By tightly integrating safety-aware volunteering, elastic trust regulation, and real-time driving risk into service orchestration, VoXaaS provides a step toward dependable and safety-governed vehicular micro-edge ecosystems. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.
label: Social Sciences

title: The role of personal norms in farmers’ safety practices: Protective equipment use in pesticide handling
abstract: Farmers’ use of personal protective equipment (PPE) during pesticide handling has been studied, but factors shaping this behavior can vary considerably. Farmers’ intention to use PPE in pesticide handling and observed protective behavior were studied using the norm activation model (NAM). Data analysis was conducted using descriptive statistics, Spearman’s correlation, multiple linear regression, and binary logistic regression models. Almost fifty-nine (58.9%) of farmers showed unsafe behavior regarding PPE use. Intention to use PPE was low (mean: 2.415 on a 1–5 scale) and positively associated with observed protective behavior. Regarding NAM constructs, farmers showed moderate personal norms (mean: 3.027), slightly lower awareness of the consequences associated with not using PPE (mean: 2.888), and relatively weak ascription of responsibility (mean: 2.741) for reducing those consequences. Personal norms significantly predicted both intention and observed protective behavior (P < 0.01). In turn, awareness of consequences and ascription of responsibility were significant positive predictors of personal norms, supporting the applicability of NAM for understanding PPE-related behavior. Further analysis indicated that personal norms were negatively associated with age and farm size (P < 0.01), suggesting weaker norms among older farmers and those managing larger farms. Conversely, education was positively correlated with personal norms (P < 0.01). Overall, personal norms played a central role in shaping PPE use, with their relationship influenced by recognition of the risks of non-use and acceptance of responsibility for mitigating them. Enhancing communication about pesticide risks and emphasizing the importance of PPE may help strengthen personal norms and promote safer PPE-related practices. © 2026 The Author(s).
label: Social Sciences

title: Genetic inference in social insects: the continued utility of microsatellites in the sociogenomic era
abstract: Social insects differ from many other biological systems because colonies function as integrated reproductive, ecological, and evolutionary units, often conceptualized as superorganisms. This organization makes genetic inference inherently hierarchical, often requiring genotyping across multiple biological levels: the colony, the population, the individual, and, in some cases, the cellular level. Although whole-genome sequencing and single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based approaches are now widely used in population genomics, microsatellites or short tandem repeats remain a useful approach for cost-effective, low-input, and highly replicated genotyping, particularly in the hierarchical sampling designs common in social insect studies. Here, we review the utility and limitations of microsatellites in social insect research using a three-tiered framework spanning colony-, population-, and individual- or cellular-level analyses. Across these scales, microsatellites are especially valuable for colony delimitation, kinship inference, diagnostic screening of known reproductive systems, and low-input genotyping. By comparing the suitability of microsatellites with that of SNP-based and broader genomic approaches across these applications, this review links marker choice to biological scale, sampling design, and inferential goal in studies of social insects. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Distributionally-robust heterogeneous graph neural networks via relation-aware grouping
abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization remains a key challenge for heterogeneous graph neural networks (HGNNs), which often exhibit substantial performance degradation under real-world distribution shifts. While Group Distributionally Robust Optimization (GroupDRO) has proven effective in promoting OOD generalization in various domains, its application to heterogeneous graphs remains largely unexplored. This gap stems from a fundamental obstacle: the complex, multi-relational nature of heterogeneous graphs renders conventional group definitions, which rely on explicit node attributes, inadequate. To bridge this gap, we propose DroHGNN, a GroupDRO-based framework for OOD generalization on heterogeneous graphs. DroHGNN introduces a relation-aware soft grouping mechanism coupled with a two-stage optimization procedure to enhance OOD robustness. Specifically, DroHGNN learns soft group assignments through learnable prototypes over relation-specific node representations. These assignments serve as optimization-oriented group proxies for GroupDRO, which minimizes worst-case group risk. To encourage structural coherence of the inferred assignments, we further introduce a heterogeneous graph structural consistency constraint that regularizes the group assignments of structurally connected target nodes. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world benchmarks show that DroHGNN consistently achieves strong OOD performance compared with competitive baselines. Notably, under degree-distribution shifts on the ArXiv dataset, DroHGNN outperforms NaiveDRO and the leading baseline CaNet by 23.3% and 6.5% in Macro-F1, respectively. Moreover, relative gains of up to 3.2% in average Macro-F1 under the inductive temporal setting further demonstrate its effectiveness under heterogeneous distribution shifts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Development of flood fear scale and investigation of psychometric properties
abstract: This study aimed to develop a flood fear scale. The study was designed as a methodological and cross-sectional study. The study was conducted with 1158 participants aged 18–65 residing in Türkiye’s Black Sea Region between February 15, 2025, and May 15, 2025. SPSS 25 and Amos 21 programs were used to analyze the data. The flood fear scale consists of four dimensions and 26 items. The Cronbach’s alpha coefficient was 0.948, and the scale explained 62.644% of the total variance. The model fit indices were χ2/ df = 3.444, RMSEA = 0.065, SRMR = 0.056, CFI = 0.921, IFI = 0.922, NFI = 0.893, and TLI = 0.912. The findings indicated that the flood fear scale provided valid and reliable for adults aged 18–65 residing in Türkiye’s Black Sea Region. The total scores obtainable from the scale range from 26 to 130, with higher scores indicating an increased level of flood fear. Scale can be used to assess flood fear in community-based disaster risk reduction efforts. It is recommended that validity and reliability studies of the scale be conducted in different cultures and geographical regions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Delay-aware feasibility control for quadrotor path following
abstract: Safe quadrotor path following under input delay is formulated here as a quantitative feasibility problem in which delayed actuation directly reduces the transverse acceleration authority available for path recovery. The proposed framework establishes an explicit chain from bounded thrust-channel delay and rotor-level actuator limits to a recoverability margin, a curvature-aware path-speed law, and a second-order Lyapunov invariant tube. A delay-matched nonlinear disturbance observer is incorporated to reduce the disturbance-related residual, while a command-rate-limited closed-form speed governor regulates path progression only when curvature demand and delay-induced authority loss approach the available recovery budget. The resulting controller requires no online optimization and is implemented through the same full SE(3) plant, rotor allocation, thrust–attitude mapping, and actuator constraints used in the numerical benchmarks. Across four simulation scenarios, including a certification-oriented case and more demanding nominal, stress, and curvature-varying conditions, the proposed method preserves the implemented feasibility margin while avoiding unnecessary uniform speed reduction. In the stress case, with a delay reserve of 0.703 m/s2 and a certified transverse acceleration radius of 5.724 m/s2, the proposed controller maintains zero negative-margin duration, whereas the fixed-speed disturbance-observer controller and the delay-ignorant proportional–derivative controller exhibit negative-margin durations of 12.76% and 20.56%, respectively. The proposed controller attains a root-mean-square transverse error of 0.195 m at a mean path speed of 3.682 m/s, illustrating the intended safety–progression trade-off rather than minimizing tracking error at the expense of recoverability. These results demonstrate that input delay can be treated not merely as a stability perturbation but as a quantifiable loss of rotor-backed recovery authority that can be compensated through explicit feasibility-based progression regulation. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Fast density clustering via layered diffusion
abstract: Density-based clustering algorithms often encounter difficulties when handling datasets with non-uniform density. To address this issue, we propose a novel clustering algorithm, termed Layered Diffusion Density Clustering (LDDC), which performs clustering through a layer-by-layer diffusion process from centroid points to high-density regions and finally to low-density regions. Specifically, LDDC first categorizes data points into centroid points, high-density points, and low-density points. It then propagates labels from centroid points to neighboring high-density points, after which the labeled high-density points continue diffusing labels to their high-density neighbors. During this process, clusters whose centroid points are connected by dense paths are merged, and label propagation continues until all high-density points have been assigned, thereby forming the cluster backbone. Subsequently, low-density points are incorporated into the corresponding clusters through outward diffusion from the cluster backbone, while the remaining low-density points are grouped together according to their neighbor relationships. Through this layered diffusion strategy, LDDC can effectively identify clusters with arbitrary shapes and non-uniform densities. Experiments on 9 synthetic and 10 real-world datasets demonstrate that, relative to the best-performing competing method for each metric, LDDC achieves average improvements of 16.84%, 13.31%, and 9.48% in ARI, NMI, and ACC, respectively, while maintaining high computational efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Semantics-aware truth discovery based on semi-supervised representation refinement
abstract: Data scientists are facing the urgent need to build a robust data integration pipeline for heterogeneous data from multiple sources. Existing truth discovery algorithms consider textual values as categories, ignoring semantic ambiguity. This work seeks to answer the Semantics-aware Truth Discovery problem: How to incorporate semantic information into truth discovery methods? We tailor an off-the-shelf tabular representation method for multi-source observations as a Basic Representation Model (BRM). However, as an unsupervised model, BRM falls short in dealing with inadequate local semantic information in multi-source observations. To mitigate this issue, we construct a semi-supervised hyperparameter search strategy for representation refinement. We also propose warm start and pruning strategies to accelerate hyperparameter search. Empirical evaluation on three real world datasets shows that S3TD outperforms existing truth discovery state-of-the-art algorithms by 3.07% on average, and can enhance the performance of existing truth discovery algorithms by up to 8.17%, both in absolute error rate. Moreover, S3TD can obtain such performance gains using as few as 5% labeled data, and reduce time costs without performance loss. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Comparing Strava and survey-based data for coastal recreation accounting
abstract: Coastal zones provide recreational ecosystem services across land and sea, yet spatial data for ecosystem accounting is limited. We compared Strava activity data with survey-based public participation GIS (PPGIS) data across the Oslofjord, Norway, to assess spatial and sociodemographic biases in crowdsourced recreation accounting. Strava over-represented activities along the coastal belt and across marine areas, while under-representing island visitation and leisure-oriented activities. Spatial bias was partly associated with age, gender, and income. Although Strava underestimated absolute recreation activity levels relative to PPGIS, the datasets showed strong agreement in relative spatial variation among municipalities. Our findings demonstrate that Strava data can support mapping of recreation patterns, but may misrepresent the magnitude and distribution of coastal recreation activity. These biases may influence the identification and prioritization of recreational areas in planning and accounting. Combining Strava data and representative survey-based approaches may improve recreation assessments for coastal planning and accounting for physical and monetary recreation services. © 2026 The Authors

title: Interface-aware adaptive layer-wise physics-informed neural networks for multilayer large-strain consolidation: a benchmark of architectures, training strategies, and trade-offs
abstract: Multilayer large-strain consolidation in stratified soils involves nonlinear pore-pressure dissipation, evolving deformation, and material discontinuities, which pose significant challenges for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). This study develops a layer-wise adaptive PINN framework in which soil layers are represented by neural subnetworks coupled through pore-pressure and Darcy-flux continuity conditions. A controlled three-layer benchmark is used to evaluate MLP and KAN architectures, adaptive activation, adaptive weighting, and parameter sharing over three independent random seeds. The framework is further extended to four- and five-layer profiles using Shared MLP, layer-wise MLP, and KAN. Results demonstrate that no single architecture is optimal across all physical responses: parameter sharing improves mean global and settlement accuracy, KAN-based models better control selected local errors, and adaptive strategies alter pressure, settlement, and interface behavior in a metric-dependent manner. The successful four- and five-layer calculations further support the applicability of the same physical formulation as the number of internal interfaces increases, although the preferred architecture changes with the layer arrangement. Overall, pore-pressure accuracy, settlement prediction, interface consistency, and computational cost involve distinct trade-offs, so model selection should reflect the target physical quantity and profile complexity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Domain-adaptive probabilistic broad learning with evidence fusion for multimodal biomedical vigilance estimation
abstract: In multimodal biomedical data analysis, wearable physiological signals provide complementary neural and oculomotor measurements for safety-critical vigilance monitoring. Joint analysis is complicated by differences between electroencephalography (EEG) and eye-movement (EM) streams in their distributions, dimensionalities, noise characteristics, and informativeness across subjects. Existing single-modal and static fusion methods do not jointly address cross-subject distribution shifts and sample-specific evidence uncertainty. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a domain-adaptive probabilistic broad learning system with pseudo-view enhanced Dempster–Shafer evidence fusion (PBLS-DS) for multimodal biomedical vigilance estimation. PBLS-DS embeds marginal source–target alignment in closed-form BLS output optimization and transforms deterministic scores into normalized evidence assignments for Dempster fusion. In this formulation, the term probabilistic refers to evidence or belief assignments rather than calibrated posterior probabilities. Its fusion mechanism constructs a lightweight joint EEG–EM view and combines evidence through evidence-concentration discounting, sample-dependent subset selection, and Dempster fusion. Experiments on SEED-VIG show that PBLS-DS outperforms representative supervised learning, domain adaptation, and deep transfer learning baselines across multiple evaluation metrics while retaining low measured training and inference costs. Post-hoc contribution analyses further characterize complementary oculomotor and frequency-dependent EEG information. PBLS-DS therefore formulates wearable vigilance estimation as a multimodal biomedical pattern-recognition task under the evaluated cross-subject protocol. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Cognitive flexibility as a bridge between depressive symptoms and problematic smartphone use in adolescents: A two-wave network analysis across depression-severity groups
abstract: The co-occurrence of depressive symptoms and problematic smartphone use (PSU) in adolescents poses a growing public health concern, but its component-level conditional associations, cross-wave patterns, and variation across depression-severity groups remain insufficiently understood. Using a two-wave observational design with a 12-month interval (N = 1200 students from one high school in a county of Gansu Province, China), this study integrated Gaussian graphical modeling (GGM), network comparison testing (NCT), and latent profile analysis (LPA). Cognitive Flexibility showed the largest absolute bridge expected influence at both waves, and the ranking was unchanged when the comparison was restricted to nodes measured at the same level of aggregation. NCT detected no significant global difference between the T1 and T2 contemporaneous networks, although several local cross-community edges differed between the two estimates. LPA retained four nearly parallel, severity-ordered classes at both waves, interpreted as depression-severity groups rather than qualitatively distinct profiles. Subgroup bootstrap analyses showed acceptable edge-weight accuracy; expected-influence CS coefficients ranged from 0.286 to 0.750, whereas all bridge-expected-influence CS coefficients were below 0.25, so the subgroup findings are confined to cross-community connectivity. Between-group differences in cross-community connectivity persisted after equal-n down-sampling. These findings should be interpreted in light of the observational design, single-school convenience sample, and reliance on self-report measures. Cognitive flexibility nevertheless emerged as a consistent cross-community correlate in the overall networks and warrants further longitudinal and intervention evaluation rather than being regarded as an established intervention target. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Enhancing mass transfer and water drainage in proton exchange membrane fuel cells via active-passive synergistic composite flow channels
abstract: Appropriate design and optimization of cathode flow fields are crucial for enhancing the overall performance of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). This study proposes an Active-Passive Synergistic Hybrid Channel (APSHC) to optimize central mass transfer in the channel center and water drainage in the rib regions. The core unit consists of a central teardrop-shaped deflector and wall-mounted semi-teardrop grooves arranged alternately along the flow direction. A 3D multiphysics model is built to evaluate mass transfer and water drainage performance and explore the influence of core unit parameters (height H , radius R , and pitch P) and the number of units (N). Simulation results at 0.45 V show that the APSHC delivers better performance than conventional parallel channels. It yields 18.7% higher net power density and 5.6% higher oxygen concentration, and reduces liquid water saturation by 6.1%. Parametric analysis reveals that H and N require optimal thresholds to mitigate excessive lateral flow and the flow shielding effect. Furthermore, the preferred value of R screened by single-factor analysis yields a favorable trade-off between mass transfer efficiency and pumping losses. In contrast, increasing pitch (P) impairs device performance, thereby demonstrating the superiority of compact structural layouts. By integrating geometry and spatial layout, the proposed APSHC balances trade-offs among mass transfer, water drainage, and flow resistance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: DMoA: Dynamic Mixture of Adapters with Feature-Enhanced Fusion for UAV Visible-Infrared Object Detection
abstract: Visible-infrared (RGB-IR) object detection has attracted significant attention in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based applications, such as disaster search and rescue, intelligent surveillance, and battlefield target tracking. However, the quality of RGB and IR modalities may vary substantially under different environmental conditions, causing one modality to become unreliable and leading to suboptimal feature enhancement and fusion. To address this challenge, we propose the Dynamic Mixture of Adapters (DMoA), a novel modality-aware enhancement framework that dynamically refines multi-modal features before semantic fusion through a Mixture of Experts (MoE) mechanism. Applied across multi-scale feature layers, DMoA consists of three key components. First, a Cross-Modality Feature Pre-Enhancement (CMFPE) block exploits complementary information to compensate for weak modality features. Second, the Dynamic Feature Enhancement (DFE) block employs separate four-expert pools and gating networks for RGB and IR at each scale, with no parameter sharing across modalities or scales. Each gating network sparsely activates the top two lightweight experts for input-adaptive feature refinement, thereby limiting computational overhead. Finally, a Semantic Information Fusion (SIF) block promotes cross-modal semantic consistency through mutual information optimization while suppressing redundant feature responses. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that DMoA consistently achieves competitive detection performance and a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off, highlighting its effectiveness for UAV-based RGB-IR object detection. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Prolonged participation AI-based mindfulness school programme in primary education: Implications for AI practices, schools and developers
abstract: Background: Research on Artificial Intelligence (AI) -supported mindfulness programs in primary education remains limited, particularly in rural contexts where implementation conditions differ from urban settings. Aim: This study examines the effects of an AI-supported mindfulness intervention on rural primary school students' behavioral and socio-emotional outcomes, and on teachers' self-regulation and creativity, measured at pretest (T1), posttest (T2), and follow-up (T3). Method: The study used a quasi-experimental design with a control group across selected classrooms in four rural schools. The sample comprised an intervention group (N = 91) and a control group (N = 54), with 16 teachers participating in the intervention group. The intervention ran for ten weekly sessions across the fall and spring semesters. AI tools (ChatGPT and Gemini) supported teacher candidates in lesson planning and in the inquiry phase that followed each mindfulness practice. Implementation fidelity, assessed through mentor cross-rating, was 88.6% (SD = 9.7), with Cohen's κ = .86 in a sub-sample. Results: Split-plot ANOVAs showed significant Time × Group interactions favouring the intervention group on life skills (LSAS, η2p = .242), behavioural difficulties (SDQ total, η2p = .378), and teacher-student relationship quality (STRS total, η2p = .025). In the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ), all five subscales were significant. The Closeness subscale drove the STRS effect; Conflict did not change. Nested analyses confirmed consistent effects across grade levels. Teachers showed gains on all nine TSRS subscales, and on the Social Value subscale of the TCS. Conclusion: The intervention was associated with improvements in students' life skills, behavioral functioning, and teacher-student closeness, as well as gains in teachers' self-regulation. The findings inform AI-supported mindfulness practice in rural primary education. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Synthesis, physicochemical characterization, and alkyd-enamel performance of cobalt phthalocyanine pigment
abstract: Cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc)-containing pigment was prepared by heating phthalic anhydride, urea, and cobalt(II) chloride with boric acid and magnesium acetate tetrahydrate at 200 °C for 2 h and evaluated in PF-115 alkyd enamel. A 40.000 g portion of the crude product yielded 16.400 g of dry pigment-containing material after acid treatment, neutralization, washing, and drying (41.0% purification mass recovery); the chemical yield and purity of CoPc were not established. Powder X-ray diffraction showed changes after acid treatment but did not permit an unambiguous α/β polymorph assignment. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) bands supported a phthalocyanine-related framework, whereas absorptions at 1772 and 1722 cm−1 indicated possible residual carbonyl-containing compounds. Ultraviolet–visible absorption of a sample prepared in dimethyl sulfoxide showed features in the 600–700 nm region. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) showed an unresolved signal near 337.9 mT (effective g = 1.9996) without uniquely identifying its origin; scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy provided local, semi-quantitative elemental information. Enamels containing 4.5 wt% pigment matched the reported first-grade GOST 6465-76 numerical limits, with gloss values of 54% and 50% and hiding-power values of 60 and 40 g m−2 for light-blue and blue coatings, respectively. The results support use of the recovered pigment fraction as a colorant in the tested alkyd formulations, while its chemical yield, bulk purity, and polymorph identity remain unresolved. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Unified task profiling and performance interference-aware Makespan and energy scheduling for cloud robotics tasks driven by an improved genetic algorithm
abstract: Cloud robotics systems offload heterogeneous, computation- and data-intensive tasks to shared cloud nodes, yet suffer from severe performance interference caused by co-located contention for shared physical resources. Such interference renders idealized execution times unreliable and degrades both Makespan and energy efficiency in conventional schedulers. To enable interference-aware scheduling, it is first necessary to quantitatively characterize the resource demands of diverse tasks and to measure how co-location affects their execution. Therefore, this paper proposes a unified task profiling approach that characterizes CPU, I/O, and memory demands and other key differentiating attributes of eight representative cloud robotics tasks spanning perception, planning, control, and execution. Lightweight, tunable benchmarks are then designed to emulate these resource-access patterns, enabling controlled co-location experiments that construct a quantitative interference-sensitivity matrix. On this foundation, an interference-aware integer programming model is formulated to minimize the weighted sum of Makespan and energy consumption. The main novelty lies in connecting task profiling, benchmark-calibrated interference measurement, and joint Makespan-energy scheduling into a unified interference-aware optimization method. To solve the resulting NP-hard problem, we propose an Improved Genetic Algorithm for Cloud Robotics Task Scheduling (IGA-CTS), which jointly searches task allocation and execution order over the interference-aware scheduling model. In benchmark-calibrated simulation experiments against seven evaluated baselines, no baseline simultaneously achieves lower median Makespan and energy consumption than IGA-CTS at any scale; although some baselines perform better on an individual objective, these advantages are accompanied by inferior performance on the other. An objective-weight sensitivity analysis further shows that this overall trade-off is largely maintained under varying optimization preferences. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Multi-objective optimization of thermo-hydraulic performance for dimpled–protruded tubes of an intermediate heat exchanger in SCO2 gas fast reactor using machine learning and NSGA-II
abstract: The thermo–hydraulic performance of heat exchangers is governed by coupled interactions among geometry, flow conditions, and fluid properties. This study develops a hybrid framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), machine learning (ML) and multi-objective optimization framework to predict and optimize the thermo-hydraulic and exergy performance of supercritical CO2 (SCO2) flowing through dimpled-protruded tubes (DPTs) for intermediate heat exchangers in SCO2 gas-cooled fast reactors. title: Operationalising the arts exposome
abstract: A recent arts exposome framework identified 50 transdiagnostic causal mechanisms (emotional, cognitive, self-referential, arousal–stress, inflammatory–epigenetic, social, and behavioural) by which arts engagement may affect mental health, organised around patterned daily exposure to active ingredients across diverse modes of arts engagement. Translating this structure into testable predictions depends on two operational prerequisites that current research has under-addressed. First, the active ingredients must be decomposed into mechanism-aligned exposure dimensions: aggregating activities as varied as receptive consumption, active participation, and cultural attendance under “arts engagement” averages mechanistically different effects and yields findings that the framework cannot localise to specific processes. Second, mechanism tractability is unevenly distributed across measurement modalities. Stress–HPA–immune mechanisms are well-served by peripheral measurement, including transcriptomic markers such as the Conserved Transcriptional Response to Adversity. Aesthetic and reward mechanisms are tractable through central measurement and autonomic indices of aesthetic emotion, but not through peripheral biomarkers. Affiliative mechanisms face validity challenges in peripheral measurement that may require pharmacological probes or behavioural proxies. Neither prerequisite suffices alone: a valid biomarker linked to a heterogeneous exposure measures something the framework cannot interpret, and a well-specified exposure linked to an inappropriate modality deteriorates evidence quality. These refinements are best understood as minimum conditions for identifying the core ingredients that matter most for each mechanism, since individual and contextual variation continue to moderate activation in real-world settings. Together, they identify where mechanism research can deliver near-term advances, where alternative methods are needed, and how the framework can move from theoretical mapping toward ecologically grounded testable inference. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Breaking the performance trade-offs of nano-metal fuels: ammonium perchlorate-mediated high-performance energetic microspheres
abstract: Simultaneously achieving high energy density, rapid reaction kinetics, and practical processability remains a fundamental challenge for metal fuels in next-generation solid propellants. Here, high-performance energetic microspheres (HPEMs) are established as a particle-level energetic composite by integrating nano-aluminum, nano-boron, and ammonium perchlorate into individual energetic microspheres, enabling intrinsic property complementarity to evolve into combustion synergy. The optimized HPEMs (Al:B = 7:3) simultaneously achieve high energy density, rapid reaction kinetics, and excellent processability. Specifically, the optimized HPEMs deliver a combustion heat of 24.0 kJ g−1, 1.86 and 1.48 times higher than those of the Al@AP and B@AP counterparts, respectively. They exhibit the shortest ignition delay (577.2 ± 31.6 ms), accelerated flame propagation, and a balanced combustion duration (88.3 ± 5.0 ms), demonstrating efficient kinetic coupling between rapid Al oxidation and sustained boron combustion. The particle-level architecture suppresses nanoparticle aggregation, reducing slurry viscosity of propellant from 138.380 to 61.596 Pa·s while maintaining superior combustion performance in propellant formulations. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that rapid Al/AP combustion establishes a self-sustained high-temperature oxidizing environment, which promotes the dynamic evolution of the molten B2O3 layer, facilitates oxygen transport to the boron core, and continuously activates boron oxidation. Consequently, the rapid reaction kinetics of nano-aluminum are effectively transferred into sustained boron oxidation, establishing a synergistic combustion pathway that combines rapid reaction kinetics with continuous high-energy release. More importantly, this work establishes the coordinated integration of complementary energetic constituents as a general design strategy that shifts material optimization from overcoming the limitations of individual components toward synergistic optimization of multicomponent performance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: ICU onboarding, boot camp, and procedural readiness curricula as entry-phase competency development for residents and fellows entering adult critical care: A scoping review
abstract: Introduction Entry into an adult intensive care unit (ICU) requires adaptation to unstable physiology, invasive support, local workflows, team roles, and supervision practices. We mapped onboarding, orientation, boot camp, and procedural-readiness curricula for residents and fellows entering adult critical care. Methods We conducted a prospectively registered scoping review (OSF DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/H2SN4 ). PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, CINAHL Plus with Full Text, and ERIC were searched on April 25, 2026 and updated through September 10, 2026. Embase was searched on September 10, 2026 to address its omission from the initial search. Supplementary citation and gray-literature searches were conducted. Records were independently screened by two reviewers, with third-reviewer adjudication when required. Intervention and landscape/needs studies were synthesized separately. Results Following database updates, the corrective Embase search, and eligibility re-adjudication, 31 reports representing 26 independent studies and five linked reports were included. Twenty-three studies evaluated interventions and three were landscape/needs studies; 20 interventions were entry-window and three were entry-anchored longitudinal. Non-mutually exclusive outcome mapping identified Level 1 outcomes in 14 studies, Level 2a in 15, Level 2b in 14, Level 3 in 2, Level 4a in 1, and Level 4b in 1. Twelve independent studies were conference-abstract-only. Conclusions Adult critical care entry curricula were heterogeneous and predominantly US-based. Technical and respiratory readiness were the largest evidence clusters, although nonprocedural transition domains were also represented. No superior curriculum model was identified; workplace-transfer evidence was uncommon, and patient-level evidence was limited to one uncontrolled airway-program evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Biological effects of ionizing radiation combined with extremely low frequency magnetic fields among occupationally exposed X-ray technicians
abstract: The human body is susceptible to ionizing radiation penetration resulting in cancer and other adverse health outcomes. One potent ionizing radiation source that has uses in medicine is X-rays. Globally, about 2.3 million and in Pakistan about 26,046 registered medical technicians are exposed to X-rays. Along with X-rays, these X-ray technicians are also potentially exposed to extremely low frequency magnetic field (ELF MF) from X-ray machines and other electrical devices. This study investigated the individual and combined effects of X-rays and ELF MF in the form of molecular mechanism including disruption of antioxidant enzyme activities, generation of reactive oxygen species, and the DNA damage. A total of 250 healthy workers were enrolled in this study; divided into ionizing radiation exposed and un-exposed groups. Along with exposure to ionizing radiation and ELF MF, information about exposure to potential confounding factors and effect modifiers was also collected. The results showed a statistically significant increased risk of DNA damage in the X-ray exposed group 20.3 ± 11.2 compared to un-exposed group 10.3 ± 5.85, p < 0.001. Also, antioxidant enzymes activities were statistically significantly higher in the exposed group Vs. un-exposed group for CAT: 12.1 ± 4.53 Vs. 9.67 ± 4.99; p < 0.001 and MDA: 9.36 ± 6.55 Vs. 5.92 ± 4.58; p < 0.001. However, the increase for SOD was not statistically significant (7.75 ± 5.58 Vs. 7.45 ± 4.83; p= 0.648). The combined exposure of ionizing radiation and ELF MF (≥0.4 μT) increased the impact for DNA damage only where changes in all the antioxidant enzymes were not meaningful. The age was statistically significantly associated with DNA damage and SOD activity. Also, the risk increased with dose-response (duration of employment) and highest DNA damage was observed in workers with work experience of ≥10 years. The study findings are useful in reporting the adverse health effects of exposure to occupational X-rays radiation and also in educating the laboratory technicians about the potentially harmful parts of their work. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Optimal planning of rooftop PV systems participating in local energy markets: evidence from Japan's electricity market
abstract: Rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems integrated into community-based local energy markets (CBMs) offer a promising solution for urban energy transitions by enabling local consumption of surplus energy. This study develops a comprehensive modeling framework to investigate (1) the impact of CBM dynamics on the optimal sizing and configuration of rooftop PV systems, and (2) the potential of the proposed system to mitigate feed-in-tariff (FiT)–related challenges, especially renewable energy curtailment due to limited grid capacity. The developed model is formulated as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) framework to identify rooftop PV configurations that maximize total social welfare in residential areas operating and trading within a CBM, distinguishing it from previous studies that primarily focus on technical, spatial, economic, or aesthetic aspects of rooftop PV planning. The developed CBM-based Rooftop PV system optimization model is validated using data from the Japan Electric Power Exchange (JEPX) market, combined with electricity load and meteorological data from Fukuoka City in Kyushu, a major island in Japan, which has frequently experienced challenges associated with FiT-induced renewable energy curtailment. Four market scenarios with varying FiT and CBM fees are considered to assess their impact on rooftop PV spatial deployment and electricity transactions. The results reveal that rooftop PV deployment is highly sensitive to FiT levels and CBM dynamics, and CBM further enhances local utilization. The results highlight that lower FiT levels combined with CBM can reduce subsidy burdens while promoting intra-community energy exchange and more efficient use of rooftop PV systems in urban systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Ultrasonic vocalizations as markers of anxiety and depression in rodent models of neurotrauma
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) and traumatic brain injury (TBI) are severe events that cause lasting sensorimotor and autonomic impairments. Both injuries often also lead to psychological and somatosensory dysfunctions such as anxiety, depression, or pain. Preclinical assessment of anxiety and depression in rodents often relies on locomotion-based behavioural tests confounded by motor deficits and pain-related changes. Because rodents cannot self-report sensory or emotional experiences, behavioural outcomes are limited to observable proxies of anxiety and depression. Ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) offer a complementary, non-locomotor tool that may capture anxiety- and depression-relevant context not detected by behavioural tests. Despite extensive USV research in stress, reward, and social behaviour, applications to neurotrauma remain underexplored, with no studies directly examining USVs in relation to anxiety- or depression-like outcomes after SCI. Even so, evidence from related fields and the limited neurotrauma literature suggests that USVs warrant further exploration as affective readouts after TBI and particularly SCI. USVs may complement behavioural testing by providing socioaffective context without relying on locomotor performance, potentially helping distinguish post-injury anxiety- and depression-like phenotypes from pain-related and other injury-associated changes. By integrating behavioural, neural, and pharmacological evidence, we highlight how USV features may reflect affective dimensions relevant to post-injury anxiety- and depression-like states and outline methodological considerations for validity and specificity. Machine-learning approaches further enable high-throughput, objective detection of subtle affective shifts. With development of collaborative datasets, these methods could reveal consistent affective vocal patterns and lay groundwork for a rudimentary ‘lexicon’ of rodent affect. Integrating USV analysis into neurotrauma and CNS disease research may refine preclinical models of affective dysfunction and improve triangulated evaluation of treatments targeting chronic mental health outcomes. © 2026 The Authors

title: DensePSA: Robust image watermarking framework with cross-scale dense structure and patch-wise self-attention mechanism
abstract: While recent architectural advances in image watermarking have yielded notable performance improvements, they often introduce substantial model complexity and computational overhead, thereby impeding real-world deployment. To address this trade-off, we propose a robust yet lightweight image watermarking framework that integrates cross-scale dense connection with a self-attention mechanism. Specifically, we design a multi-scale dense-connected encoder/decoder architecture that systematically reuses intermediate features across resolutions, enhancing both feature utilization and representational capacity for reliable watermark embedding and extraction. Complementing this design, we incorporate a Patch-wise Self-Attention (PSA) module between convolutional stages. By partitioning high-resolution feature maps into non-overlapping patches and applying an adaptive re-weighting strategy, PSA effectively captures global dependencies with reduced computational cost. This patch-based design preserves global contextual information without incurring the prohibitive complexity associated with conventional attention models on large tensors. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both imperceptibility and robustness against common signal-processing attacks, all while supporting real-time inference. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Governing Indigenous territories: trust, moral economy, and the legitimation of Indigenous territorial authority in the Honduran Moskitia
abstract: Formalizing Indigenous land rights is critical for environmental justice and sustainable development. Yet legal recognition often creates new territorial governing bodies tasked with managing collective lands, whose legitimacy cannot be assumed. This study examines how trust in Indigenous territorial authorities is built, contested, and withdrawn following the formalization of collective land rights in the Honduran Moskitia. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork and household interviews in three villages across diverse socio-ecological settings, the study analyzes how residents assess their territorial authorities. The analysis treats trust as multidimensional and relational. The study examines different forms of trust—dispositional, rational, affinitive, and procedural—to identify the rationales that drive assessments of authority in each village. These rationales are interpreted through the lens of a Miskitu moral economy, framing trust assessments in terms of what residents expect of a territorial authority to be considered legitimate. A moral economy lens contributes analytically to a multidimensional trust framework by explaining why certain forms of trust feel more salient when evaluating authority performance and how they interact with one another. The central finding is that the socio-spatial configuration of land conflicts shapes which evaluative dimensions of trust become most salient. A multidimensional and relational trust analysis contributes a more granular understanding of this process: it shows how different forms of trust interact and shift through everyday encounters with authority, identifying the specific points at which legitimacy is strengthened, strained, or quietly lost. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Empowering adaptive MOOCs: A learning path recommendation model based on multi-level knowledge graphs and rule-guided path constraint optimization
abstract: Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) provide abundant learning resources, yet their fixed instructional structures and limited adaptive support constrain learning effectiveness. Previous path recommendation approaches typically depend on predefined start and target nodes, offer limited dynamic adaptability, and insufficiently consider multi-hop dependencies among learning content. To address these challenges, this study proposes an adaptive learning path recommendation model based on a multi-level knowledge graph and rule-guided path constraint optimization (KGRRec). First, we design a multi-level knowledge graph framework that models course knowledge structures and integrates MOOC resources across three levels: instructional organization, knowledge representation, and resource aggregation. Second, building on this framework, we develop a rule-guided path constraint optimization method, which incorporates dynamic reasoning mechanisms, path constraint modeling, and learning gain simulation to deliver adaptive learning path recommendations. Implemented in a prototype integrating seven database-related MOOCs, KGRRec was evaluated through a one-group pretest-posttest study (34 students) and a randomized controlled study (59 students). Results showed KGRRec significantly outperformed eight baselines on Prerequisite, CogValidity-F, and expert ratings. Furthermore, it showed a trend toward improved learning performance and supported positive learning experiences. These findings provide preliminary evidence of the model’s effectiveness and a methodological reference for the future development of large-scale adaptive MOOCs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Dynamic link prediction with community structure evolution modeling
abstract: In dynamic graphs, future link formation is influenced by both structural evolution and temporal dependency. Many existing methods primarily focus on node-level dynamics or local interaction patterns, while insufficiently exploiting mesoscopic community structure and its evolution. To improve dynamic link prediction by learning mesoscopic evolution patterns of network community structure, a community-evolution-aware framework, termed CoEvoNet, is developed. Specifically, community assignments are explicitly learned from temporally encoded node states to extract mesoscopic organizational information beyond node-level dynamics. A progressive soft-to-hard assignment strategy is then introduced to obtain community representations that preserve gradual affiliation patterns while providing clearer structural boundaries. The learned community signals are used to enhance dynamic link prediction, and a community structure evolution modeling module is further constructed to capture the temporal evolution of mesoscopic organization and to provide auxiliary supervision through reconstruction. Finally, extensive experiments on three real-world dynamic graph datasets show that CoEvoNet consistently outperforms competitive baselines in dynamic link prediction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Handedness, psychological characteristics, and social adaptation among Chinese college students
abstract: Handedness may be associated with individual differences in information processing, but its implications for social adaptation remain unclear. This cross-sectional study examined associations among handedness type, openness, cognitive flexibility, multitasking preference, and social adaptation in 3798 Chinese college students. Mixed-handed students reported higher openness (η2 = 0.013), cognitive flexibility (η2 = 0.030), and multitasking preference (η2 = 0.007) than right- and left-handed students, with the largest group difference observed for cognitive flexibility. Left- and right-handed students showed broadly similar scores across these characteristics. Social adaptation was positively associated with openness ( r = 0.20), cognitive flexibility ( r = 0.32), and multitasking preference ( r = 0.23). Mixed-handedness was positively associated with openness ( r = 0.11), cognitive flexibility ( r = 0.17), and multitasking preference ( r = 0.08), whereas its association with social adaptation was weaker ( r = −0.04). Overall, these findings suggest that mixed-handedness is associated with a differentiated pattern of adaptation-relevant psychological characteristics, particularly cognitive flexibility and openness. The results highlight modest but potentially informative individual differences linked to handedness and indicate that these differences are more evident in specific psychological characteristics than in overall social adaptation. title: Dual roles of higher-order interactions in temporal cooperation dynamics
abstract: Higher-order interactions are ubiquitous in real-world collaborative systems, yet existing studies often consider temporal dynamics and higher-order interactions separately, limiting the understanding of cooperation in realistic group environments. To bridge this gap, we develop an empirical evolutionary game framework based on temporal higher-order networks using two real-world face-to-face interaction datasets: Office 2013 and Office 2015. Specifically, we show that higher-order interactions exhibit a condition-dependent dual role: under a weak dilemma ((Formula presented) ), cooperation frequency fC reaches 0.73 compared with 0.16 in pairwise networks, whereas under a strong dilemma ((Formula presented) ), cooperation collapses to 0 compared with 0.12 in pairwise networks. Randomization experiments further reveal that the association between temporal burstiness and cooperation differs between pairwise and higher-order interaction systems. Finally, we extend the heterogeneous activity-driven model to derive an analytical defection threshold for temporal higher-order networks, providing a theoretical framework for understanding cooperation collapse in evolving group interactions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Marine ecosystem extent accounting in a deep-sea-dominated nation
abstract: The global economy is heavily reliant on healthy ecosystems, which provide humanity’s foundation for prosperity, resilience, and well-being. This interdependence has driven growing international interest in developing frameworks to assess and account for the value of natural capital to humanity, society, and the economy. In response to this need, the United Nations developed the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting - Ecosystem Accounting (SEEA EA), and, in late 2024, the European Parliament adopted Regulation (EU) 2024/3024, which establishes ecosystem accounts as a core component of the European Union’s environmental-economic accounting system. This Regulation mandates Member States to compile data for three key physical accounts: ecosystem extent, ecosystem condition, and ecosystem services flows, covering both their terrestrial and marine territories. It provides a comprehensive framework that allows countries to move beyond GDP, enabling a systematized and coherent assessment of Member States' natural capital. Marine ecosystem accounting represents an innovative and data-driven approach for integrating ecological, economic, and social information into decision-making processes. This paper presents the methodological approach and preliminary results of Portugal’s Marine Ecosystem Extent Account, which showed that 99% of the Portuguese maritime space is deep-sea (' 200 m). Results show that, particularly for deep-sea dominated nations, greater detail is needed, beyond classes defined solely by depth and slope, in order to support useful and actionable ecosystem accounting. The paper also discusses the methodological challenges encountered during the compilation of Portugal’s marine extent account and highlights its policy relevance as a decision-support tool for evidence-based marine management and sustainable ocean governance. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Significantly enhancing the strength of aluminum while preserving excellent electrical conductivity via single-walled carbon nanotubes reinforcement
abstract: The inherent trade-off between the strength and electrical conductivity has long constrained the development of advanced aluminum (Al) conductors, and the potential of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) to break this dilemma remains critically underexplored, largely due to their dispersion difficulties. Herein, SWCNTs reinforced Al matrix nanocomposites are fabricated via friction stir processing (FSP) and followed by hot extrusion, and the strength-electrical properties are systematically evaluated. Microstructural analysis confirmed the well dispersion of SWCNTs without micro-sized aggregations. The smaller diameter and much higher specific surface area of SWCNTs enables the formation of a greater number of clean and strong bonded interfaces with the Al matrix under the thermo-mechanical conditions of FSP, which is the key for enhancing strength and maintaining electrical conductivity of Al. As a result, the ultimate tensile strengths of the SWCNTs/Al nanocomposite reached 201.1 MPa, representing an increase of 113.0% over the unreinforced Al. Remarkably, the SWCNTs/Al nanocomposite retained a high electrical conductivity (∼62.3% IACS) and good elongation (∼12.5%). This combination of more than doubled strength with uncompromised conductivity highlights the advantage of SWCNTs over conventional CNTs reinforcements in achieving strength-electrical conductivity synergy. Our findings establish that SWCNTs, despite their processing challenges, serve as exceptionally efficient reinforcements for overcoming the long-standing strength-conductivity trade-off, positioning them as a highly promising reinforcement for next-generation high-performance Al conductors. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Bubble-cell native fluorescence imaging for high-sensitivity label-free protein quantification
abstract: Quantification of low-abundance proteins is critical for biopharmaceutical development, proteomics, and biochemical research; however, existing methods often require trade-offs among sensitivity, sample consumption, and workflow simplicity. Ultraviolet (UV) absorbance at 280 nm remains the most widely used method for routine protein quantification because it is rapid, label-free, and reproducible, but its intrinsic sensitivity limits the analysis of dilute samples, particularly when only microliter sample volumes are available. Here we present a high-sensitivity, label-free method for protein quantification based on native fluorescence imaging (NFI) using a bubble-cell capillary, in which a short, enlarged section is incorporated into an otherwise uniform capillary to enhance fluorescence detection. The enlarged bubble-cell increases the optical interrogation volume, generating a localized fluorescence peak that enables robust peak-based quantification, signal-to-noise analysis, and direct visualization of proteins near the detection limit. Using only 1–2 μL of sample, the method achieved experimentally validated limits of detection of approximately 0.005 mg/mL for bovine serum albumin (BSA) and 0.0025 mg/mL for monoclonal antibodies, representing detection limits approximately one order of magnitude lower than literature-reported values for NanoDrop UV spectrophotometry, while preserving the simplicity of a rapid, label-free, and reagent-free workflow. Method validation demonstrated good reproducibility, satisfactory spike-and-recovery performance, negligible carryover, and reliable quantification over the validated working range. The method was further applied to monitor low-abundance fractions collected during monoclonal antibody charge-variant fractionation, enabling detection of minor protein populations that were not reliably detected using a conventional fluorescence plate reader. The combination of high sensitivity, validated analytical performance, minimal sample consumption, and simple peak-based detection demonstrates the potential of bubble-cell NFI as a practical platform for routine protein quantification and characterization, particularly when sample availability is limited or low-abundance protein species must be analyzed. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
