title: How information format, climate attitudes, and trust shape consumer response to food carbon emission information
abstract: Consumers often underestimate the carbon emissions associated with their food choices, and carbon-emissions information is increasingly proposed as a way to close this knowledge gap. Yet evidence remains limited regarding how alternative information formats affect intended dietary choices and whether responses vary across consumers. We conduct a randomized online experiment comparing personalized carbon-emissions totals, generic food-category rankings, and their combination. We also examine heterogeneity in treatment effects by climate attitudes and explore whether reported trust and information internalization are associated with these differences. On average, all three formats produce negative estimated effects on projected emissions, with the largest point estimate observed for the ordinal ranking. Effects are highly heterogeneous: individuals with greater concern about climate change reduce projected emissions, whereas those with low concern show little response. Climate-concerned individuals also report greater trust in the personalized information and update their self-assessed emissions more closely toward the displayed estimates. The association between climate attitudes and information internalization is substantially attenuated after accounting for reported trust. Together, our findings demonstrate that responses to carbon-emissions information depend on both the format of the information and consumers' pre-existing climate attitudes, underscoring the importance of clear, credible, and actionable carbon-emissions information and of accounting for heterogeneity in consumer receptiveness when designing information interventions. © 2026 The Authors

title: Solitary ground-nesting bees: opportunities and challenges for crop pollination management
abstract: The majority of bee species worldwide are solitary and nest in soil or earthen substrate (i.e. ground-nesting). Among these, several are effective crop pollinators. Despite their abundance, diversity, and ubiquity, only one species of solitary, ground-nesting bee (Nomia melanderi) has been commercially deployed in the field for crop pollination. Compared with bees that nest aboveground in cavities, ground-nesting bees pose unique challenges to management, but offer several advantages as well. Soil is a relatively cheap and abundant nesting material, but laborious and difficult to move, and the soil preferences of many ground-nesting bee species are unknown. Additionally, farm management, including tillage and pesticide applications, especially when done directly to the soil, can significantly limit the successful establishment and population growth of ground-nesting bees. Despite these challenges, a number of ground-nesting bees show potential to be managed in the field or greenhouse and could be valuable supplements to the current over-reliance on a few social and/or cavity-nesting bees. In this review, we highlight past successes at managing ground-nesting bees for crop pollination and describe the bee traits that have led to success. We also present several species with potential for further development and management on-farm or in greenhouses owing to their ability to persist in or near crop fields, their willingness to use provided nesting substrates such as soil mounds or adobe blocks, and our growing understanding of their nest preferences. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Idiosyncratic influences of hotel occupancy on energy consumption: Moderating effects of service style, hotel size, and hotel class
abstract: With the growing attention to sustainability and energy management, understanding the dynamics of energy consumption in hotels has become increasingly important. We confirm that the utility expenses (e.g., electricity and water expenses) of a hotel generally follow a logarithmic increase with occupancy. A hotel's energy consumption rises rapidly when occupancy is relatively low but increases gradually once occupancy reaches a certain high level. In addition, full-service hotels exhibit a positive moderating effect at low occupancy rate but a negative moderating effect at high occupancy rate. Similar moderating effects are observed in large and high-class hotels. The findings indicate that full-service, large, and high-class hotels have opportunities for energy efficiency improvements when their occupancy rates are lower relative to those of limited-service, smaller, and lower-class hotels. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Spatiotemporal resampling-based dynamic ensemble selection for nonstationary streams
abstract: Classifying imbalanced data streams in nonstationary environments presents a substantial challenge, primarily due to the simultaneous presence of class imbalance and concept drift. Existing ensemble methods often struggle to balance the trade-off between preserving historical minority concepts and adapting to rapid distribution changes, thereby leading to performance degradation. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel framework named the spatiotemporal resampling-based dynamic ensemble selection (STR-DES). First, a spatiotemporal weighted SMOTE (STW-SMOTE) is introduced, which synthesizes high-quality minority class instances by weighting historical neighbors according to both spatial proximity and temporal recency, ensuring alignment with the evolving data concept. Second, a stabilized dynamic ensemble selection strategy is developed, in which the competence region is constructed from multiple historical chunks to improve the robustness of local classifier evaluation under nonstationary environments. Third, a recall-biased ensemble management mechanism is introduced, combining a competence metric with recall emphasis and bounded specificity modulation with an oldest-worst pruning policy to suppress trivial classifiers while preserving discriminative ensemble members. Furthermore, a dual-threshold drift detection mechanism is integrated to adaptively distinguish between minor fluctuations and severe structural changes, triggering proportional model updates to effectively balance stability and plasticity. Evaluated on 10 synthetic and 5 real-world data streams, STR-DES achieves the lowest average rank (1.267) for both G-mean and Recall compared to nine baseline methods, ranking first across 12 and 11 streams, respectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: A network approach to mapping responsibility in wildfire risk mitigation
abstract: As wildfire risk escalates in the wildland urban interface/intermix (WUI), creating defensible space clear of flammable fuels is important for wildfire risk mitigation and management. By definition, defensible space is constrained to the property parcel's boundaries and wildfire risk assessments generally focus on individual parcels, but this overlooks any risk in neighboring properties. If we imagine defensible spaces as buffers that cross property boundaries and overlap, neighboring properties may share wildfire risk in the overlapping spaces. However, homeowners may not recognize these overlapping regions and spillover effects of mitigating risk, jeopardizing their properties and, ultimately, the entire neighborhood. To address this issue, we propose a novel paradigm to rethink defensible space management by mapping the homeowner's responsibility to mitigate wildfire risk in overlapping defensible space buffers with respect to their neighbors who may share or owe responsibility to mitigation. First, we develop three new spatial metrics (Personal Responsibility (PR), Shared Responsibility (SR), and Owed Responsibility (OR)) for each homeowner, computed as the product of wildfire risk and the corresponding area of responsibility. Here, we use a fire behavior model to generate rate of spread (ROS) as a measure of wildfire hazard and compute each responsibility metric. Second, we build the metrics into spatial responsibility networks, modeled using all the houses in a given neighborhood with nodes characterized by average PR and with links weighted by average SR (or OR) that are directed to designate who is responsible between neighboring properties. In our study site, we find that SR and OR networks are composed of multiple sub-networks. This information is important to inform homeowners about their individual responsibilities, identify properties with greater responsibility, and gather neighbors with interconnected responsibility. Subsequently, we simulate different mitigation strategies by iteratively removing network links and monitoring how the total responsibility may change in the neighborhood. We use three strategies (random, localized, and targeted) for link removal. Results demonstrate that the targeted strategy (removing links in descending order of highest responsibility) reduces the total responsibility most rapidly and fragments the network into smaller components, concentrating mitigation on the highest-responsibility links. Through this study, we provide a framework for wildfire risk management, which can be used with different metrics and for various neighborhood layouts. Ultimately, the spatial responsibility metrics and networks provide a scalable and spatially-explicit approach to map complex wildfire risk in the WUI, which can help inform defensible space inspections, guide efficient resource allocation, improve neighborhood-level planning, and empower individual homeowners to make more risk-informed decisions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Debiasing scene graph generation with Context-Aware Peer Networks
abstract: Scene graph generation (SGG) aims to detect objects and infer their pairwise relationships, but long-tailed predicate distributions cause models to over-predict frequent predicates and under-recognize informative tail relations. We propose Context-Aware Peer Networks (CAPN), a plug-and-play framework for unbiased SGG. CAPN replaces a single relation predictor with multiple collaborative peers and introduces a context-aware encoder with Context-to-Peer (CPE) and Context-to-Predicate (CPR) modules. CPE adaptively weights peer contributions according to scene context, while CPR modulates predicate logits to improve context-consistent prediction and alleviate head-predicate dominance. Experiments on Visual Genome and Open Images V6 show that CAPN improves the mR-R trade-off across Motifs, VCTree, and Transformer backbones, achieving a weighted score of 45.1 on OI-V6 and a mean score of 49.0 on VG PredCls. Code is available at CAPN. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Beyond decontamination: Investigating the effect of gamma irradiation on natural dyes in a historical wool carpet
abstract: This study investigates the viability of gamma irradiation as a treatment process for historical textiles, focusing on the dyes of a 19th–century wool carpet. The effect of irradiation doses (1–10 kGy) on blue-, red-, and yellow-dyed fibers was evaluated by multiple techniques, including colorimetric, spectroscopic, chromatographic, thermal, and morphological analyses along with theoretical calculations. Colorimetric measurements showed that color changes were hardly perceptible (ΔE* < 3) for all samples after 10 kGy irradiation. XRF results indicated that the red and yellow fibers were mordanted with aluminum, whereas the blue dye was applied directly. Dye characterization using the LC-PDA-MS method revealed the presence of indigo carmine in the blue fibers, cochineal in the red fibers, and a mixture of weld and cochineal in the yellow fibers. The irradiation at 10 kGy significantly decreased the extractability of red and yellow color components. As no new peaks corresponding to degradation products were detected in the chromatograms, the reduced extractability was attributed to radiation-induced solid-state molecular reorganization, consistent with the Raman and SEM findings. The thermal characteristics of the dyed fibers were almost unaffected by irradiation. Furthermore, theoretical evaluations of the experimental findings were performed using global reactivity descriptors, charge distributions, and local reactivity regions obtained via optimized geometries, MEP mapping, and Fukui functions, respectively. The findings demonstrate that gamma irradiation up to 10 kGy is a safe treatment for historical wool carpets, causing no significant visual or molecular damage to the color components, while even enhancing the stability of certain dyes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Can visibility-based metrics predict soundscape perception in cities?
abstract: Context plays a central role in soundscape perception within the ISO 12913 series framework. However, there is a lack of empirical evidence on how to identify operational, standardised proxy metrics for capturing ‘context’ in soundscape assessment and prediction. The study addresses this gap by deriving a set of visibility-based metrics from Isovist and Visibility Graph Analysis (VGA) and evaluating their effectiveness in a soundscape predictive model. An on-site soundscape data campaign was conducted in Bloomsbury, Central London., Isovist and VGA metrics were computed for each soundscape observation to obtain a high-resolution, geospatial soundscape dataset (N = 787). Key findings stand out: (1) Isovist and VGA metrics correlate strongly with pleasantness (PISO) but weakly with eventfulness (EISO); (2) four ‘visual-spatial’ clusters (ViSpID) are derived from the selected Isovist and VGA metrics: Highly connected streets, Moderately connected streets, Open spaces & poorly connected streets, and Enclosed spaces; and (3) a linear multilevel model predicting PISO that incorporates these clusters (ViSpID) with psychoacoustic predictors (R2 = 0.51) outperforms a psychoacoustics-only baseline model (R2 = 0.15). These findings demonstrate that Isovist and VGA metrics provide practical proxies for the structural visibility and spatial configuration dimensions of physical context and support a systematic and reproducible framework for integrating these effects into predictive modelling. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Blastocystis sp. in human populations: Pooled prevalence and subtype distribution from a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Blastocystis is widely detected in human populations, yet prevalence estimates vary substantially across geographic regions, population settings, and diagnostic approaches. We systematically reviewed cross-sectional surveys published from 2015 to 2025 that investigated non-disease-selected human populations. Across 137 eligible survey units from 47 countries, 562,327 participants and 26,697 positive detections were included. The crude participant-level positivity was 4.7%, whereas the random-effects pooled prevalence across published surveys was 17.9% (95% CI: 13.9%–22.6%; 95% PI: 0.7%–87.5%; I2 = 99.7%). Regional pooled estimates were 44.2% in Africa, 36.7% in the Americas, 8.4% in Asia, and 7.2% in Europe; however, these comparisons should be interpreted descriptively because substantial residual heterogeneity and study-level confounding remained. Population-group differences were not statistically significant ( P = 0.074), while the three broad diagnostic-strategy groups were summarized descriptively because multimodal protocols were heterogeneous. Sensitivity analyses restricted to population-based surveys and community/household surveys yielded pooled estimates of 15.8% and 13.0%, respectively. Among 62 studies reporting molecular subtype information, 5220 isolates were assigned single subtypes, while 658 mixed-subtype detections from 18 studies were summarized separately. ST3, ST1, and ST2 were among the predominant reported subtypes. These findings summarize available published surveillance data rather than a population-weighted global burden estimate and highlight the need for standardized sampling frameworks, harmonized molecular workflows, and integrated One Health investigations to clarify Blastocystis epidemiology and transmission ecology. title: Decoding interfacial differences between regioisomeric organic dyes: The role of alkyl-chain conformational accessibility
abstract: Long alkyl chains in dye-sensitized solar-cell sensitizers are commonly regarded as aggregation-suppressing substituents, although their conformational accessibility may influence interfacial organization. Here, DFT, TD-DFT, CREST/xTB conformational sampling, and projected density-of-states (PDOS) analysis were combined to examine the regioisomeric dyes T5-1 and T5-2, for which IPCE maxima of approximately 60% and 85%, respectively, have been previously reported. The T1–T4 reference series shows that π-extension red-shifts absorption while introducing trade-offs in adsorption and charge-transfer descriptors. For T5-1/T5-2, frontier-orbital energetics and alkyl-free dye–TiO₂ coupling are comparable; however, the low-energy T5-1 ensemble favors syn-type chain dispositions, whereas T5-2 has a thermally accessible anti conformer. Thus, conventional backbone-centered electronic descriptors alone do not fully account for their distinct interfacial behavior. Selected interface models associate the T5-2 motif derived from the anti-conformer with more-upright adsorption, stronger local chain-mediated contacts, and larger LUMO resonance broadening. This organization provides a structural basis for reduced electrolyte accessibility and a lower propensity for interfacial charge recombination, while retaining strong dye–TiO₂ electronic coupling. These findings highlight alkyl-chain conformational accessibility as an important factor linking molecular connectivity to interfacial behavior in the T5-1/T5-2 regioisomeric dye pair. title: The association between maternal acculturation, acculturative stress and factors related to child feeding in the Hispanic community health study/study of Latinos family lifestyle outcomes research (HCHS/SOL FLOR) study
abstract: The acculturation process and its related stress have been associated with health declines among Hispanic/Latino immigrants in the US. However, the impact on caregiver feeding style and the home food environment are unknown. This study aimed to assess the associations between maternal acculturation and acculturation stress with both caregiver feeding style (n = 248) and the home food environment (n = 178) using data from mother-child dyads from the Family Lifestyle Outcomes Research ancillary study of the Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos. Children were aged 3-9 years at the time of the study. Results suggest an association between greater maternal acculturative stress and greater odds of authoritative and authoritarian feeding styles. An association between greater acculturative stress and greater maternal demandingness in feeding was also observed. Additionally, greater language acculturation and greater length of time in the US were associated with more sweetened beverages and fewer fruits and vegetables reported in the home. These results highlight the importance of supporting Hispanic immigrants as they adapt to life in the US and developing culturally appropriate interventions that can address child feeding and food purchasing behaviors among immigrant parents. © 2026 The Authors. title: Extremely lightweight salient object detection in optical remote sensing images
abstract: Existing salient object detection models in optical remote sensing images (ORSI-SOD) struggle to achieve a trade-off between saliency performance and computational efficiency. To address this issue, an extremely lightweight ORSI-SOD model is designed which operates independently of pre-trained weights. The proposed model incorporates an extremely lightweight trainable backbone, i.e. Octconv Backbone Network (OctNet) that is able to capture high-quality features. Different from commonly used lightweight ORSI-SOD models that introduce the MobileNet series as their backbone, the OctNet achieves this without relying on pre-trained weights. The high-quality features are subsequently fed into a multi-scale feature extraction module (MFEM) and a boundary enhancement module (BEM). The MFEM improves the feature extraction capability for multi-scale salient objects by introducing convolutions with diverse receptive fields. The BEM strengthens the capability in capturing intricate object boundaries within a dual-branch structure. The experimental results on three datasets consistently demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms the existing state-of-art salient object detection models in terms of saliency performance and computational efficiency without relying on pre-trained weights. Furthermore, when the input data size is 288 × 288, the proposed model comprises merely 0.93 million parameters and requires only 3.25 billion floating-point operations (FLOPs). The corresponding code for the model proposed in this article can be viewed at https://github.com/blossom-lv/Lightweight_ORSI_SOD_Models/tree/master. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Newcomers help most after being helped, veterans do not: Evidence from Stack Overflow
abstract: Whether people who receive help online go on to help others is an open question. Prior observational studies report mixed results, and designs that ignore prior user activity may overstate reciprocity. We develop a matched difference-in-differences survival analysis of over 21 million Stack Overflow questions, comparing users whose questions were answered with propensity-score-matched users whose questions were not. We don't ask broadly whether reciprocity works in general, but locate the narrow conditions under which it affects user behavior. Users whose questions were answered helped others slightly more often (increment at answer arrival, hazard ratio [HR] = 1.049, 95% CI [1.044, 1.054]). The response depended on tenure: new users responded most (HR = 1.071 in the first week, 95% CI [1.056, 1.086]), while the longest-tenured users did not respond measurably. The tenure gradient is the most robust pattern we find. Timing mattered too, though far more fragilely: users answered within 30 to 60 min responded most strongly, while answers under 30 min show no elevation. Most of our data predate 2020, and the generalized reciprocity effect among new users does not survive a split at 2020, so these estimates largely reflect a pre-generative-AI baseline. We review gratitude, moral obligation, social expectation, and incentive displacement as possible psychological mechanisms but cannot measure them. On Stack Overflow, generalized reciprocity is less a general driver of cooperation than a recruitment channel for contributions from new users: designers gain most by getting newcomers’ questions answered. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Evaluating feasibility of an ACT group telehealth-delivered therapy intervention for adolescents with depression
abstract: Increasing rates of adolescent depression call for efficient and accessible interventions that are well received by adolescents. Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) is a third-wave psychotherapy that has been shown to be effective in treating depression in adolescents, delivered both individually and in group settings. Group therapy can help address service provider shortages by enabling a single provider to treat multiple individuals at once. Additionally, telehealth allows greater access to care for individuals who cannot readily travel to a clinic. Telehealth-delivered group therapy combines these two strategies to facilitate adolescents’ access to mental health treatment. We piloted a 10-week group intervention, adapted from ACT for Adolescents with Depression, and explored its feasibility. Adolescent patients with depression (N = 10) ages 14 to 18 (M = 16; SD = 1.49 years), seeking mental health services, participated in the program and completed pre and post assessments. The majority identified as female (70%) and White (60%). The groups were well attended; only one patient dropped out, and one was discharged. The patients reported overwhelmingly overall positive experiences with the program. Group means for depression and anxiety scores in this sample decreased from baseline to end of treatment, psychological flexibility increased by the end of treatment, and no changes were observed in flourishing scores. Overall, the intervention was well accepted. Well-powered research studies with randomized allocation to telehealth delivered ACT and control groups are needed to test this protocol’s effectiveness in treating depression in adolescents as an independent treatment or as adjunct treatment to individual therapy. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. title: Decoupled semantic alignment and emotion-aware gated fusion for group emotion recognition
abstract: Video-based group emotion recognition must resolve three coupled problems: semantic entanglement among multimodal cues, the loss of transient affective climaxes during temporal aggregation, and the propagation of noisy sensory features during fusion. We propose a Modality-Decoupled Language-Guided Framework that uses a vision-language model as an offline semantic engine to generate independent psychology-informed visual and acoustic narratives. The resulting modality-specific text anchors are aligned with CLIP visual features and CLAP acoustic features through a dual InfoNCE objective. A Soft Emotion-Aware Temporal Attention (SETA) module predicts a continuous emotion distribution and maps it to an affective query for frame-wise temporal weighting. The same distribution is projected into a fusion-specific query for Soft Emotion-Aware Gated Fusion (SEGF), which performs complementary channel-wise routing of the refined visual and acoustic features. The main novelty is the coordinated use of narrative-level modality decoupling and a shared soft affective hypothesis across both temporal localization and multimodal fusion. Across 10 independent runs, the framework achieves 77.69 ± 1.04% mean accuracy on VGAF and 97.87 ± 0.47% on GECV, with best-run accuracies of 80.03% and 98.52%, respectively. Interpretability, corruption, efficiency, narrative-decoupling, and failure-case analyses further characterize the behavior of the proposed modules. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Longitudinal associations between physical exercise and psychological resilience among college students: A random-intercept cross-lagged panel model
abstract: Physical exercise is closely associated with psychological resilience, yet the temporal direction and within-person dynamics of this relationship remain unclear. This study examined the longitudinal association between physical exercise and psychological resilience among Chinese college students and tested whether it differed by sex. A three-wave longitudinal survey was conducted among students from universities in four provincial-level regions of China. Physical exercise and psychological resilience were assessed using the Physical Activity Rating Scale and the Connor–Davidson Resilience Scale, respectively. A total of 1451 valid participants were included at baseline, of whom 913 completed all three waves. At the between-person level, physical exercise was significantly and positively associated with psychological resilience. At the within-person level, physical exercise positively predicted subsequent psychological resilience across both time intervals, whereas the reverse association was small and observed only from T1 to T2. Multi-group analyses showed no significant sex differences in the autoregressive or cross-lagged paths. These findings extend the longitudinal evidence on the relationship between physical exercise and psychological resilience, reveal the dynamic nature of their within-person associations across the two time intervals, and suggest that physical exercise may be an important behavioral factor supporting the maintenance and development of psychological resilience among college students. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A Q-guided offline reinforcement learning framework for incentive mechanism optimization in spatial crowdsourcing
abstract: Spatial crowdsourcing platforms require effective incentive mechanisms to recruit distributed users for location-dependent tasks while jointly considering platform revenue, user participation, and budget constraints. Existing heuristic and game-theoretic approaches often depend on simplified assumptions about user rationality and system information, whereas online reinforcement learning methods require repeated interaction with the environment, making them costly and risky for practical deployment. To overcome these limitations, we propose QG-DiffIRL, a Q-guided diffusion offline reinforcement learning framework for incentive mechanism optimization. Learning from constructed offline interaction records derived from real mobility traces, QG-DiffIRL integrates a diffusion-based policy for complex continuous action generation, critic-guided value refinement for high-quality incentive decisions, and prospect-theory-based user modeling for boundedly rational acceptance behavior. Extensive experiments on multiple spatial crowdsourcing datasets demonstrate that QG-DiffIRL consistently improves platform utility, utility per accepted task, and budget efficiency while achieving competitive or superior social welfare over representative baselines, highlighting its value for robust and data-driven incentive design in spatial crowdsourcing platforms. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Surgical treatment for idiopathic toe walkers gives good biomechanical and patient satisfaction outcomes
abstract: Purpose: To assess the impact of bilateral surgical calf lengthening in patients with idiopathic toe walking (ITW) and calf contracture, including those with an autism diagnosis. Methods: Clinical assessment included passive range of motion and 3D gait analysis to capture kinematic and kinetic data. Temporal spatial parameters were measured. Gait Profile Scores (GPS) were calculated to evaluate gait normalcy, and Gait Variable Scores (GVS) identified the components of any change. Ankle push-off power was analysed. Patient satisfaction was assessed via questionnaires. Statistical analysis included paired t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results: Thirty-eight patients were included; 34 had complete kinematic and 30 had complete kinetic data. Mean age at surgery was 10.3 yrs and mean follow-up was 1.3 ± 0.4 yrs. Ankle dorsiflexion showed a significant improvement. Walking speed increased due to increased step length, while cadence was reduced. GPS improved from 11.4º from the norm preoperatively to 6.2º postoperatively (p < 0.001). GVS improved for ankle dorsiflexion (p < 0.001) and pelvic tilt (p < 0.005). Peak ankle power generation and work done during late stance significantly increased. Pain decreased postoperatively and patient satisfaction was high. There were no adverse biomechanical outcomes such as recurrence or overcorrection. Conclusion: Calf lengthening surgery for ITW has demonstrated improved clinical, kinematic and kinetic outcomes in gait analysis at one-year. High levels of satisfaction, with notable improvements in mobility and pain management postoperatively, were reported. However, longer-term follow-up to evaluate sustained benefits is needed. © 2026

title: EGCG accelerates wound healing in diabetic mice by Notch pathway to enhance epidermis formation
abstract: Keratinocyte proliferation delay was a prominent clinical manifestation of diabetes, significantly impeding the wound healing process in diabetic mice. The potential therapeutic role of (−)-epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) has been recognized due to its ability to enhance wound healing under diabetic conditions, but the underlying mechanism remained unclear. This study elucidates that EGCG expedited wound healing in diabetic mice by accelerating re-epithelialization and collagen deposition. Remarkably, we observed that EGCG promotes epidermal cell proliferation and enhances wound healing process in diabetic mice. We also discovered an overexpression of the Notch pathway in the epidermal cells of diabetic mice. Interestingly, EGCG effectively suppresses this overexpressed Notch pathway, suggesting a targeted mechanism for its therapeutic effects. Furthermore, the experiments with human immortalized keratinocytes (HaCaT) confirmed that high glucose levels activated the Notch signaling pathway, which was subsequently inhibited by EGCG treatment. In conclusion, our study reveals that EGCG improves wound healing in streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic mice by targeting the Notch pathway in epidermal cells. These findings offered novel insights into therapeutic strategies for diabetic wounds and highlight EGCG as a promising candidate for treating chronic wounds. © National R&D Center for Edible Fungus Processing Technology 2026.

title: Informing users about LLMs' environmental costs encourages ethical consumption
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming deeply embedded in everyday human-AI interaction. However, the environmental costs associated with using those tools remain elusive. Here, we address the question of whether providing users with information about the environmental costs of using LLMs tempers their use. Such information highlights an ethical tension: acting pro-environmentally requires people to forgo some of the benefits AI tools provide. We study how people solve this trade-off in tasks that are relatively easy to tackle without using LLMs and further assess if the impact of providing such information has a stronger effect on people who have stronger environmental concerns. In two preregistered experiments (total N = 1200), we studied participants' use of ChatGPT in a text-editing task after they learned about the tool's environmental costs. Results revealed that (i) raising awareness of ChatGPT's environmental costs reduced its use and usage volume; (ii) interacting with a sycophantic model, one that encourages continuous use, did not attenuate the awareness effect, although it led to greater overall use; and (iii) raising awareness was especially effective among people with high environmental concerns. The findings highlight how raising awareness concerning LLM's environmental costs can encourage responsible consumption. © 2026 The Authors

title: Spatial cognitive patterns of underground public spaces from a stimulus-organism-response perspective: evidence from LLM-empowered social media data mining
abstract: Current underground public space (UPS) renewal prioritizes engineering-oriented physical upgrades, neglecting users’ multidimensional cognitive experiences. Existing studies on underground space perceptions rely on small-sample surveys and fail to capture joint co-occurrence patterns among multiple stimuli. This study integrated the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework with large language models to decode spatial cognitive patterns. It drew on 76,078 social media reviews from 64 UPSs in 19 Chinese cities (2005–2024). DeepSeek extracted 27 spatial stimuli and their sentiments, serving as public perceptions. Generalized ordered probit regressions showed that management quality, environmental conditions, and atmospheric experiences exhibited the strongest associations with overall ratings. Negative perceptions showed stronger negative associations with ratings than positive perceptions showed positive associations. Association rule mining uncovered co-occurrence patterns across genders, city clusters, and review periods. Dissatisfaction was associated with shorter, more concentrated patterns of negative stimuli, whereas satisfaction was associated with the co-occurrence of positive functional and experiential perceptions. Co-occurrence patterns varied markedly across organismic attributes. Males showed simpler, function-oriented networks, while females displayed more complex, multi-dimensional ones. Regional expectation thresholds differed across contexts. Temporal patterns shifted from physical defects to operational management. These findings support a cognition-driven renewal paradigm, shifting from engineering-oriented interventions to weakness prioritization, multifunctional experience design, and inclusive context-specific strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: KFS-CT: A physics-constrained hybrid network for broaching tool condition monitoring
abstract: Tool condition monitoring (TCM) in industrial broaching faces significant challenges due to complex progressive multi-tooth geometries and cutting dynamics. To address these bottlenecks, this study proposes a physics-constrained hybrid expert network, termed the KFS-CT (Kalman Filtering Sparse-CNN-Transformer) framework, for multi-task decoupling of continuous full-teeth wear profiling and discrete transient chipping classification. In this framework, a macro-gating pipeline isolates the active cutting segments and partitions them kinematically, forming tooth-index-aligned interval matrices. Subsequently, a Kalman filtering sparse (KFS) separation operator is applied to decouple these segments into periodic degradation trends and transient shock components. Specifically, the framework employs a dual-branch feature fusion strategy: a multi-scale 1D-CNN branch directly processes the raw Spatio-Temporal signals, while a parallel physics-informed branch utilizes the KFS operator to decompose signals into periodic and transient components for extracting 16-dimensional expert physical fingerprints. Subsequently, the representations from both branches are concatenated, integrated with learnable positional encodings, and processed by a dual-layer spatial Transformer. Finally, a homoscedastic uncertainty loss is employed to dynamically balance the multi-task optimization objectives while incorporating physical mechanism constraints. Full-lifecycle industrial experiments demonstrate that KFS-CT achieves favorable diagnostic capabilities, limiting the full-teeth wear regression mean absolute error (MAE) to 0.0117 mm and yielding an 87.56% chipping classification F1-score. Concurrently, the computational latency of 2.84 s satisfies the requirements of quasi-real-time workshop deployment, offering a practical trade-off between diagnostic accuracy and computational efficiency in intelligent manufacturing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Rethinking cultural awareness in think-aloud research
abstract: Background: Think-aloud protocols have long been valued as a window into cognitive processes. However, insufficient attention has been paid to how culture shapes what participants articulate, how they do so, and what remains unspoken during think-aloud tasks. Purpose: This commentary re-examines think-aloud methodology on the basis of established theoretical, philosophical, and micro-linguistic foundations. Building on what has been achieved in this collection of studies, it aims to bolster cultural awareness in think-aloud research by proposing a reflective framework that foregrounds culture as integral to cognition rather than viewing it as methodological noise. Results: The developed reflective framework consists of five core dimensions of cultural awareness: (1) participant and researcher positionality; (2) the situatedness of tasks and materials; (3) cultural considerations in protocols and instructions; (4) cultural sensitivity in data analysis; and (5) the generalizability of research claims. Drawing on the studies in this special issue, each of these dimensions is detailed with an array of concrete, actionable aspects that operationalize cultural awareness across study design, data collection, analysis, and conclusion framing. The empirical practices featured throughout this special issue illuminate transformative horizons for future research, offering operational guidance to help researchers move beyond assumptions of procedural neutrality and treat verbal reports as culturally situated performances. Conclusions: Future think-aloud research should critically interrogate its methodological assumptions, foreground cultural dimensions throughout the analysis process, and ensure that theoretical claims are ecologically grounded in the data from which they are derived. © 2026 The Authors

title: An agenda for plastics crisis research in the synthetic age
abstract: This survey synthesizes insights from environmental social sciences to recast the plastics crisis as a structural feature of growth-dependent economies instead of a problem solvable by consumer choice or incremental technologies. Rather than a within-field review of ecological economics, it maps adjacent literatures to specify what this field could study and how, clarifying researchable questions, suitable methods, and tractable indicators. The synthesis foregrounds connections between expansionary political-economic dynamics, globally uneven socio-ecological burdens across the plastics life cycle, and the power and knowledge relations that shape what is produced, measured, and governed. It calls for comparative, mixed-methods, multi-scalar work and for open, standardized data on plastics flows to strengthen causal inference and comparability. Shifting attention upstream—from end-of-pipe fixes to the transformation of provisioning systems—the paper charts lines of inquiry capable of aligning social metabolism with biophysical limits and human needs, providing a roadmap for ecological economics to organize and accelerate research beyond consumer or techno-managerial framings. © 2026 The Authors. title: An improved algorithm for searching all minimal paths in networks using degree-2 chain compression and boundary-closure pruning
abstract: Minimal paths (MPs) are fundamental to binary and multistate network reliability evaluation, but exhaustive MP search becomes computationally expensive as network size increases. To reduce redundant branch expansion in DFS-based MP search, this study develops an improved algorithm that eliminates redundant branches before and during the search process. First, an s–t core network is extracted by recursively removing source-sink-irrelevant leaf branches, and degree-2 chains are compressed to replace deterministic node-by-node traversal with endpoint jumps. Second, a geometric outer boundary of the core network is constructed, based on which boundary-closure pruning discards candidates that cannot reach the sink in the current residual graph. The local-closure pruning rule is refined using a sink-side criterion, and the inherited first-bifurcation decomposition is implemented with spawn subprocesses. A formal correctness theorem establishes complete and duplicate-free MP enumeration under the combined preprocessing and pruning rules. Computational experiments on the reported benchmark and transportation-network cases show lower wall-clock time than the tested Bai and Zhou baselines where comparable results are available; the magnitude of the gain depends on network topology, terminal placement, and workload. title: Energy, exergy, and direct engine-out emission impact assessment of an ethyl acetate–diesel dual-fuel engine under different EGR rates
abstract: This study experimentally investigates the energy, exergy, and direct engine-out emission impacts of ethyl acetate (EA)–diesel dual-fuel operation under exhaust gas recirculation (EGR). Tests were conducted on a single-cylinder direct-injection diesel engine at 1800 rpm and 25–100% loads. EA injection durations of 1, 2, and 3 ms and EGR rates of 0%, 5%, 10%, and 20% were investigated. Energy and exergy balances were established, and direct emission impact was calculated from CO, CO2, HC, and NOx mass-flow rates derived from the measured exhaust-gas concentrations and intake-air flow. At full load, EA(2 ms) + 20% EGR increased energy and exergy efficiencies by 39.1% and 38.4%, respectively, and reduced exergy destruction by 42.5% relative to diesel operation without EGR, representing the thermodynamically preferred condition. EA(3 ms) without EGR produced the maximum pointwise direct emission-impact reduction of 72.5% at 25% load, whereas EA(3 ms) + 20% EGR provided the greatest average reduction of 35.8%. Condition-mean ANOVA showed that engine load accounted for 84.81%, 84.61%, and 91.70% of the variations in energy efficiency, exergy efficiency, and direct emission impact, respectively. Load-resolved TOPSIS identified EA(2 ms) + 20% EGR as the highest-ranked balanced compromise, with a mean closeness coefficient of 0.7781; however, EA(3 ms) + 20% EGR became preferable when direct emission impact received greater weight. The results demonstrate metric-specific optima and support load-dependent coordination of EA injection and EGR. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Drought, women's time poverty, and the development costs of water collection in Sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Drought can impose development costs that are not fully captured by income, production, or formal water access indicators. This paper examines one such hidden cost in Sub-Saharan Africa by focusing on women's time poverty arising from household water collection. Combining harmonized Demographic and Health Surveys with geocoded drought exposure measured at the survey cluster level, we estimate how local drought conditions are associated with women's annual water collection burden and broader household adjustments. We find that drought exposure is associated with higher water-collection time for women, with larger estimated increases among women living in poor households, women with no formal education, and women living in households without piped-water access. Intermediate-outcome evidence shows that drought is associated with lower local water availability and a higher likelihood of very long collection trips, particularly journeys exceeding 60 minutes. These water-time burdens are also associated with greater engagement in flexible, household-based, family-based, and self-employed forms of work among women rather than with a simple expansion of protected paid employment. In addition, higher community water burdens are associated with poorer schooling outcomes among girls, including a greater likelihood of being out of school and larger grade-for-age gaps. Household-linked evidence further shows that poorer girls’ schooling outcomes are associated with larger household shares of adult women in unpaid or in-kind work, self-employment, and family work. The findings suggest that drought-related water insecurity can redistribute adaptation costs within households, making women's unpaid time a key margin through which climate stress produces hidden development costs. © 2026

title: From revision to learning transfer: Self- and socially shared-regulated pathways in AI-assisted feedback
abstract: Background: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has transformed feedback provision in writing practices. However, little is known about the mechanisms through which AI-mediated engagement and revision contribute to longer-term learning transfer. Research aims: Framed by theories of self-regulated learning (SRL), socially shared regulated learning (SSRL), and cognitive engagement, the study examined the relationship among engagement, immediate revision gains, and longer-term learning transfer in AI-assisted feedback. Methods: This 16-week cluster-randomized experiment involving 108 undergraduates in China compared two feedback modes: AI-assisted self-feedback and AI-assisted peer feedback. Analyses drew on 1100 writing samples (including pretests, four assignments with two drafts each, and posttests), and 432 reflection forms on AI feedback. Findings: Linear mixed models revealed a decoupling of learning and performance: while both conditions produced similarly strong second drafts, AI-assisted peer feedback demonstrated significantly greater learning transfer to subsequent tasks. In AI-assisted self-feedback, learning followed a performance-dependent SRL cycle in which AI engagement and revision improvements independently predicted learning. A threshold-like pattern further showed that benefits emerged only when students engaged constructively, measured by reflection forms, to internalize writing standards. Conversely, AI-assisted peer feedback was associated with stronger learning transfer that was less dependent on revision gains or engagement with AI, a pattern consistent with an SSRL perspective emphasizing interactive engagement and co-constructed understanding. Conclusion: These findings highlight the importance of revision mechanisms and depth of engagement across feedback contexts. The study contributes to theories of regulation and cognitive engagement and offers pedagogical and design implications for fostering meaningful learning through AI-assisted feedback. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A hierarchical federated learning trusted collaboration and auditable mechanism based on DAG–consortium chain hybrid ledger
abstract: Hierarchical federated learning (HFL) reduces wide-area communication by introducing edge aggregation, but it also creates additional trust boundaries: malicious or low-quality client updates may contaminate edge models, edge-side admission and aggregation decisions are difficult to verify, and conventional training logs provide limited support for end-to-end accountability. This paper proposes a trusted coordination and auditing mechanism based on a hybrid directed-acyclic-graph (DAG)–consortium blockchain ledger. Full model updates remain off-chain. At each edge, a bounded client trust score combines historical reputation, exponential timeliness, alignment with a clean root update, and contribution quality. The score drives dynamic admission, median-norm clipping, and a hybrid aggregation rule that combines coordinate-wise trimmed mean with trust–sample weighted averaging. Meanwhile, client-, edge-, and global-level commitments are linked into a cross-layer evidence chain: the DAG layer records high-frequency update metadata, whereas a permissioned consortium blockchain anchors lower-frequency governance and audit records. Experiments with three random seeds on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 cover 20/50/100 clients, multiple robust baselines, label-flipping, backdoor, free-rider, collusion, Sybil, and adaptive attacks. Under 30% label flipping, the proposed method achieves (Formula presented) final accuracy on MNIST and exhibits dataset-dependent trade-offs on Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10. At 100 clients, it reduces accounted cross-layer tensor communication from 127.44 to 95.12 MB/round, at the cost of increasing round time from 7.38 to 10.05 s. A Hyperledger Fabric v2.5.14 prototype further processes 6400 audit-record submission attempts with a 99.734% success rate; with a 256-B payload and concurrency 10, it reaches 32.70 tx/s with 304.25 ms mean commit latency. These results show that the proposed design provides a verifiable cross-layer coordination path while explicitly exposing the robustness, computation, communication, and ledger-overhead trade-offs of trustworthy HFL. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Assessing Urban Flood Resilience through the Lens of a Dynamic Flood Resilience Index: Systematic Review
abstract: Urban flooding is becoming more frequent and damaging due to the combined effects of climate change and rapid urbanization, exposing the limitations of conventional risk-based flood-management approaches. Consequently, resilience-based strategies have gained attention for managing uncertainty, system complexity, and recovery capacity in urban flood contexts. Flood-resilience index (FRI) frameworks are widely used to operationalize resilience by integrating social, economic, infrastructural, institutional, and environmental dimensions into composite indicators. However, many existing FRI frameworks rely on static or snapshot-based assessments that inadequately represent feedback mechanisms, temporal evolution, and nonstationary flood regimes. This study presents a systematic literature review examining how geographic information systems (GIS), multicriteria decision-making (MCDM), and system dynamics modeling (SDM) have been applied individually and in combination to support urban flood-resilience assessment. Seventy-six peer-reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2024 were analyzed using qualitative content analysis and frequency-based quantitative synthesis. The review synthesizes dominant methodological practices and identifies recurring limitations related to indicator aggregation, weighting, spatial representation, uncertainty treatment, and temporal dynamics. The findings show that GIS-MCDM approaches enable spatially explicit and structured resilience assessment but are commonly constrained by static assumptions and criterion independence. SDM applications offer strong potential for capturing feedback-driven system behavior and for the long-term evolution of resilience, yet are rarely integrated with GIS-based MCDM FRIs. The paper proposes a formalized synthesis-based framework that integrates GIS, MCDM, and SDM to support spatially explicit and dynamically informed urban flood-resilience assessment. It highlights key research gaps for future development. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Newly graduated nurses' experiences in internal medicine and surgical clinics after the earthquake
abstract: Aim: To explore the experiences of newly graduated nurses working in internal medicine and surgical units in earthquake-affected regions. Background: The 2023 earthquakes in Türkiye severely disrupted healthcare services and increased the need for healthcare professionals in affected regions. Little is known about the experiences of newly graduated nurses as they begin their careers in disaster-affected settings. Methods: This qualitative descriptive phenomenological study used semi-structured interviews with 10 newly graduated nurses working in internal medicine and surgical units between February and August 2025. The interviews were conducted online, recorded, transcribed, thematically analysed, and reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research guidelines. Results: Six main themes and 14 sub-themes were identified: (1) assignment process and decision-making, involving perceived ease of appointment, obligation, family guidance, and social responsibility; (2) physiological and environmental challenges, including health, housing, basic needs and transportation problems; (3) psychological challenges, including adaptation difficulties, post-traumatic fears, and empathic burden from traumatic narratives; (4) social life challenges, characterised by limited social opportunities and gradual development of a new social life; (5) professional experiences, including inexperience, working with disaster-affected colleagues, and caring for earthquake-affected patients; and (6) recommendations for supporting newly graduated nurses. Conclusions: Beginning professional practice in a disaster-affected region created substantial environmental, psychological, social, and professional challenges for newly graduated nurses. These findings support the need for structured preparation and support to facilitate their adaptation to such settings. Implications for nursing and health policy: Newly graduated nurses assigned to disaster-affected regions should receive disaster preparedness training, structured orientation, and psychological and institutional support. Workforce planning should also ensure access to experienced nurses who can support newly graduated staff in high-risk settings. title: Aesthetic taste in humans and machines
abstract: Aesthetic taste remains an elusive phenomenon that has been comparatively underexplored in psychology. We argue that taste integrates four dimensions: sensitivity to fine-grained differences within a domain; valence, through which these differences come to matter affectively; orientation, the selective tendency to seek encounters that may further transform one's sensibility; and normativity, through which judgments of taste become shareable and contestable. These are not separate dimensions but faces of a single underlying capacity: continuously monitoring one's grip on the world and letting that monitoring modulate what happens next. This makes human engagement non-uniform. Throughout, we use current artificial intelligence as a contrast case, exploring how far it can model or replicate human taste. Machines can be sensitive to fine-grained distinctions, predict human preferences, generate apparently tasteful outputs, and shape the environments in which human taste develops. But they do not yet possess taste in the full human sense, because they lack the stake that makes human processing non-uniform: self-directed exploration, online self-transformation, and genuine normative vulnerability. The upshot is a systematic framework for the study of human taste and for assessing how AI may transform its formation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A semantic-aware dual-stream framework for spatiotemporal trajectory-user linking
abstract: Trajectory-User Linking (TUL) aims to associate mobility trajectories with corresponding users. Current solutions rely heavily on POI identifiers and sequential dynamics, thereby providing narrow spatiotemporal insight. This paradigm yields task-specific representations that lack commonality in human mobility patterns and cross-city transferability. In this work, we propose a Semantic-Aware Trajectory-User Linking framework with city-wise transfer learning, named SATUL. In detail, SATUL leverages pre-trained semantic encoders to embed POI category texts and develops multi-frequency sinusoidal encoding to jointly capture temporal periodicity and spatial continuity. Furthermore, SATUL establishes cross-city transferability through a dual-stream mechanism that pre-trains a shared trajectory encoder across cities via joint domain optimization. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that SATUL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines with superior data efficiency, particularly in data-scarce and cold-start scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Comparative morphology and chemical profile of the metapleural gland in two ants: Paraponera clavata and Pachycondyla crassinoda
abstract: Ants possess a pair of metapleural glands whose secretions are associated with antimicrobial defense and colony hygiene. Despite their importance, comparative studies integrating morphology and chemical characterization of these glands remain limited, particularly among poneromorph ants. This study investigated the hypothesis that species belonging to different ant lineages exhibit differences in the morphology and chemical composition of the metapleural glands. These features were evaluated in workers of Paraponera clavata (Fabricius, 1775) (Paraponerinae) and Pachycondyla crassinoda (Latreille, 1802) (Ponerinae), two phylogenetically distant species with distinct ecological habits. Histological and morphometric analyses were conducted to describe gland structure, including secretory cells, reservoir, and sieve plates, and gland extracts were analyzed by gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS) to identify chemical compounds. The metapleural glands of both species share the same general organization but differ in ostiole morphology, the number of sieve plates, and reservoir size, with the latter being larger in P. clavata. GC–MS analyses revealed both shared and species-specific compounds, with P. clavata exhibiting a greater chemical diversity, including the long-chain alcohols 1-octacosanol and 1,30-triacontanediol. Notably, 1-octacosanol has rarely been reported in ants, whereas 1,30-triacontanediol appears to have not been previously documented in the family Formicidae. These results demonstrate that the metapleural gland shows some morphological and chemical variation between phylogenetically distant species and provide new data that contribute to the understanding of the diversity and evolution of exocrine glands in Formicidae. © 2026 The Authors

title: SafeBound: Safety-aware lower-bound learning for Remaining Useful Life prediction
abstract: Deep learning-based prognostics for Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction have achieved significant accuracy but often lack the reliability required for safety-critical systems. While recent risk-aware approaches employ asymmetric loss functions, they fundamentally treat safety as a soft penalty rather than a constraint-aware optimization, often failing to rule out hazardous overestimation at the instance level. To address this, we propose SafeBound ( Safe ty-Aware Bound ary Learner ), which reformulates RUL prediction from cost minimization to constraint-aware optimization. SafeBound decouples the prediction task into a conservative lower bound estimate and an accuracy-refining slack variable. By incorporating monotonic degradation as a domain-informed safety prior and a boundary-aware stabilization scheme, our method balances boundary tightness with feasibility, mitigating optimization instability. Extensive experiments on C-MAPSS, N-CMAPSS, and NASA Battery datasets demonstrate that SafeBound achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while maintaining low safety bound violation rates — as low as 2.4% on turbofan engines and below 1% on battery degradation — effectively addressing the trade-off between predictive accuracy and operational safety. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Global and Regional Prevalence of Areca Nut Consumption among Children and Adolescents – A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Objective: This systematic review and meta-analysis (SRMA) aimed to pool the estimates of prevalence of areca-nut consumption among children and adolescents. Materials and methods: A comprehensive search was done in “PubMed”, “EMBASE”, “Scopus”, and CINAHL databases till 31st December 2024 using search terms “Areca nut” OR “Betel nut” OR “Areca catechu”, “Arecas” AND “Children” OR “Youth” OR “Juvenile” OR “Child” OR “Minor” OR “Teenagers” OR “Adolescent”. Cross-sectional and cohort studies that reported the prevalence of areca nut consumption among children and adolescents, and studies published in English were included. Variables extracted were year, country, age and sex, sample size, prevalence (maximum recall), sex specific prevalence, and type of population. Results: A total of 1447 publications were identified using a systematic search of various databases. Title and abstract screening were performed for 722 publications after removing duplicates (n = 725). Six publications were identified from other websites. Full text screening was performed for 106 publications, which yielded 66 estimates. Males have a significantly higher prevalence than females (OR: 2.6). The pooled prevalence of areca-nut consumption was 29.1 (95% CI: 23-35.3; n = 66) with high heterogeneity. Multiple meta-regression analyses were done, which showed no significant influence of age, male: female ratio, publication year, and the risk of bias score on the overall estimates. Sensitivity analysis showed that the overall estimates were not changed drastically when one study was eliminated successively. Conclusion: Three out of 10 children and adolescents had the habit of consuming areca nuts. © 2027, Association of Support to Oral Health Research (APESB). .

title: Balancing structural life and digital technologies: global evidence for a preventive policy model
abstract: Objectives: Everyday life is increasingly mediated by digital technologies. These systems improve access and convenience but can also replace movement, sleep-protective routines and in-person participation. We examined whether the activity-cognition index changed gradually or showed a rapid transition as digital mediation expanded, and whether the proposed three-parameter model performed better than simpler alternatives. Methods: We analysed global annual data for 2000–2024. An activity-cognition index combined adult mobility, metabolic integrity (inverse obesity), cognition-related health burden and international learning performance. A digitality index combined Internet and mobile-broadband access, digital payments and remote work/education anchors. We compared the study-specific quartic benchmark with linear, quadratic, spline, segmented, logistic, calendar-time and autoregressive models, and examined annual changes, serial dependence and detrended early-warning indicators. Results: The digitality index increased from 0.060 to 0.680. The benchmark fold was 0.456, first crossed in 2016; observed A first became negative in 2017, and the 2024 benchmark equilibrium was -0.220. A digitality-based logistic transition fitted best (RMSE 0.063; leave-one-year-out RMSE 0.074), but a calendar-time logistic model fitted nearly as well (leave-one-year-out RMSE 0.082), and digitality correlated 0.998 with year. Raw variance and autocorrelation increased around the transition period but weakened after detrending. Conclusions: The series shows a marked nonlinear change in the mid-2010s, but it does not establish a causal or universal digitality threshold. The framework should serve as an exploratory monitoring tool that makes scale, model and temporal uncertainty visible and can be tested with national, local and service-specific data. © 2026

title: Shaping tastes: Context- and task-dependent correspondences between basic tastes and visual forms
abstract: Crossmodal correspondences refer to systematic associations between features across sensory modalities, such as gustatory sensations and visual shapes. The current study examined associations between three basic tastes (sweetness, sourness, and bitterness) and two visual dimensions (angularity and symmetry), focusing on their dependence on taste contrast, mapping direction, and measure explicitness. In Experiments 1–3, separate participant groups were assigned to one of three taste contrasts (sweet–sour, sweet–bitter, sour–bitter) and completed either taste/shape matching tasks or an Implicit Association Test (IAT). Experiment 4 assessed all contrasts within participants using taste/shape rating tasks or the IAT. Across matching and rating tasks, sweetness was associated with rounded and symmetrical shapes, whereas sourness and bitterness were associated with angular and asymmetrical shapes; however, less consistent mappings in the sour–bitter contrast suggest that sweetness served as a key reference. In addition, association tended to be more consistent in the taste-to-shape direction than in the shape-to-taste direction, suggesting that visual features alone may provide limited information for inferring specific tastes. IAT results showed the most consistent evidence for the sweet–sour contrast, with weaker and less consistent effects for the other contrasts. These findings demonstrate that taste–shape correspondences are context-dependent and modulated by the direction of mapping and the explicitness of the measure. The results inform theoretical accounts of taste–shape correspondence formation and have practical implications for product design and marketing, indicating that rounded and symmetrical features may effectively convey sweetness, whereas angularity may better differentiate sourness from bitterness. © 2026 The Authors

title: Co-firing of upgraded biomass towards flexible CO2 reduction for coal-fired power plants in China
abstract: The increasing trend in CO2 emissions from fossil fuels has accelerated the renewable energy development, especially in China, the world's largest CO2 emitter, which targets carbon peaking by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060. Co-firing of raw biomass is a promising carbon–neutral energy option in China, but its application is limited to only 10% incorporation with stable combustion performance. Therefore, in this study comprehensively assessed biomass upgrading methods, including torrefaction, pelletization, pyrolysis, and gasification, demonstrated that upgraded biomass exhibited significant potential as an attractive, feasible, and sustainable alternative fuel for a low-carbon approach to co-firing in existing PC power plants. The existing research work revealed that the recent Chinese energy policies support the co-firing of biomass, while biomass upgrading technologies are under development and need bioenergy-supported policies. The results showed that upgraded biomass enables higher co-firing ratios in PC boilers, achieving up to 50% substitution on an energy basis and reducing net CO2 emissions by up to 50% compared with full coal combustion. Co-firing of the upgraded biomass not only maintains the high efficiency of PC and CFB furnaces, but also has the potential to lower their carbon footprint and NOx emissions. Additionally, the effectiveness of the co-firing strategy for achieving carbon neutrality is evaluated. This review paper can assist in identifying the potential methods that can increase the biomass-to-coal ratio during direct co-firing in existing PC furnaces without requiring large modifications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Neural and endocrine correlates of extinction of conditioned sexual incentive salience in male rats
abstract: Conditioned sexual arousal (CSA) can develop when initially neutral social cues acquire sexual incentive value through associative learning. In male rats, pairing the D2-type receptor agonist quinpirole (QNP) with cohabitation with an almond-scented juvenile male induces a conditioned sexual response toward that stimulus. Here, we examined how this response changes following repeated nonreinforced exposure to the conditioned social cue. Adult male rats underwent three conditioning trials followed, in the extinction-training groups, by three additional drug-free exposures to the almond-scented juvenile male. Conditioned responding was subsequently assessed toward both a receptive female and the juvenile male. QNP-Paired males showed robust juvenile-directed non-contact erections (NCEs), whereas QNP-Extinction males showed markedly reduced NCE responding. Genital investigation also showed a significant Partner × Treatment interaction, while the remaining behavioral measures did not survive correction for multiple comparisons. Free testosterone did not differ significantly among treatments. Exploratory Fos-immunoreactivity (Fos-IR) analyses revealed treatment-related differences in several brain regions; however, no direct QNP-Paired versus QNP-Extinction regional comparison remained significant after correction for multiple testing. Thus, repeated nonreinforced exposure to the conditioned social cue was associated with a marked reduction in conditioned sexual responding. Because the Paired and Extinction conditions differed in elapsed time and additional experience, this reduction is compatible with extinction but cannot be attributed uniquely to extinction learning. The endocrine and Fos-IR findings should be considered exploratory. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: From overloaded to unsatisfied: The short- and long-term effects of online career media exposure
abstract: The contemporary career landscape is increasingly influenced by digital technologies. The widespread availability of online career information and the daily exchange of content via social media not only facilitate autonomous career development but also expose individuals to a vast array of career options. Although this abundance reflects greater self-determination, it may also lead to psychological challenges through choice overload. In this study, the possibility that online exposure to career information and options increases career choice overload, which, over time, may reduce overall career satisfaction, is examined. Using a combined contemporaneous and cross-lagged effects model, we found that greater online exposure to career information was associated with increased career choice overload, which was captured across three dimensions: career choice avoidance, disengagement from one's current career, and impatient career idealism. Longitudinally, elevated career choice overload predicted lower overall career satisfaction, and conversely, lower satisfaction contributed to greater overload, which suggests a potential negative spiral. Our findings provide empirical evidence that routine online media exposure can generate both conscious and unconscious career choice overload, which highlights the occurrence of choice overload in high-stakes career contexts and its multidimensional nature. © 2026

title: Cross-modal vision transformer with energy-system priors for interpretable operational pattern discovery
abstract: The identification of the repeating operating conditions for energy assets — namely, the limited range of states through which any turbine or building passes — forms an essential component of condition monitoring; however, since operating labels are seldom available at scale, the process has to be unsupervised. Progress is hampered by two issues: one-dimensional sequence encoders do not explicitly represent pairwise lag, recurrence, and transition structures that can separate states with similar marginals; moreover, physics-blind clustering can collapse into trivial magnitude groups that lose temporal coherence. We present PRISM, a cross-modal vision transformer that reads the operational segment both as a smoothed picture derived from the signal via the vision transformer branch and as an unprocessed sequence of signals through the selective state-space branch, connecting the two derived perspectives using cross-attention with prior biasing. We present an idealized conditional identifiability result under explicit multi-view and bounded-switching assumptions, while the envelope prior provides only a qualitative complexity rationale. On five public benchmarks involving buildings (the Building Data Genome 2 and REFIT) and wind turbines (Kelmarsh, Penmanshiel, CARE-to-Compare), PRISM brings fault and anomaly detection to a mean AUROC of 0.922 and exceeds the leading contrastive baseline by 0.031 (3.1 percentage points), while improving silhouette from 0.489 to 0.571. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: High-efficiency near-infrared TADF OLEDs with dipole moment selective matching and exciton management strategy for polar hosts
abstract: Near-infrared organic light-emitting diodes (NIR-OLEDs) based on thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) are promising for optical communication, bioimaging, and biomedical sensing, but face a persistent trade-off between long-wavelength emission and device efficiency. Here, the previously reported NIR-TADF emitter APDC-DTPA is used to examine a dipole-moment-selective host-screening strategy together with energy-level matching and device-level exciton/charge management. Changing the host from BCP to PPF and DPEPO shifts the film PL maximum from 690 to 724 and 729 nm, while the corresponding photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQY) are 28.87%, 24.89%, and 15.17%, respectively. These results show that host polarity can stabilize the charge-transfer excited state, whereas HOMO/LUMO alignment, triplet energy, and transport properties jointly determine device suitability. PPF therefore provides the most practical spectral-photophysical compromise and is selected for device optimization. Transient electroluminescence further reveals intermediate carrier-response dynamics for the PPF-based device. Subsequent insertion of CzSi/TSPO1 blocking layers and optimization of the hole-injection/transport architecture improve exciton confinement and charge balance. The optimized MoO3/TAPC:MoO3/TAPC device exhibits EL centered near 730 nm, a maximum luminance of 220 cd/m2, a maximum radiance of 4.86 W/sr/m2, and a measured peak EQE of 5.81%, corresponding to an approximately 175.4% increase relative to the initial PPF-based Pristine device (2.11%). Together, these results establish a host-selection and device-engineering framework for efficient NIR-TADF OLEDs. © 2026

title: Analysis of medical isotope yield based on 232Th(p, x)225Ac reaction
abstract: Actinium-225 (225Ac) has emerged as a premier medical isotope for targeted alpha therapy (TAT), yet its large-scale production remains impeded by multiple technical challenges. This study aims to develop an optimal thick-target scheme for 225Ac production via proton beam irradiation of thorium targets. Specifically, the FLUKA code was employed to quantify and analyze the impacts of thorium target thickness and incident proton energy on both 225Ac production yield and the maximum deposition power density within the target, thereby identifying the optimal proton energy and corresponding target thickness parameters. The results indicate that irradiating an 18-cm-thick thorium target with 500 MeV protons maximizes 225Ac production efficiency under the constraint of constant proton beam power. This work achieves an optimal trade-off among 225Ac yield, proton energy, and target heat load, thereby providing a critical technical reference for the efficient and scalable production of this pivotal medical isotope. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Self-construal and the three flows of compassion: The role of dialectical thinking
abstract: Compassion for self, others, and from others is increasingly understood as culturally embedded. This study examined the relationships between self-construal and the three flows of compassion and explored dialectical thinking as a potential process linking self-construal to compassionate experience. Caregivers of older adults in Hong Kong ( N = 210; 75.2% women) completed an online survey including the Compassionate Engagement and Action Scale, Self-Construal Scale—Short Version, and the attitude toward contradiction subscale of the Analysis–Holism Scale. Mediation analyses were conducted to examine indirect effects. Independent self-construal was positively associated with self-compassion and compassion for others, whereas interdependent self-construal was associated only with compassion for others. Independent self-construal was positively related to dialectical thinking, which was associated with self-compassion and compassion for others, but not compassion from others. A significant indirect effect of independent self-construal on self-compassion via dialectical thinking was observed, with a positive but non-significant indirect effect for compassion for others. Dialectical thinking may link independent self-construal to compassion, particularly self-compassion, while other mechanisms may underlie the association between interdependent self-construal and compassion for others. These findings highlight distinct pathways to compassion across self-construal. © 2026 The Authors.
