title: Understanding preferences for explainable AI: A study on LIME variations
abstract: The current research aims to empirically examine user preferences of four variations of visual explanations from an image classification model. Participants ( N = 23) were recruited from a Midwestern university. The study was a within-subjects design in which participants were asked to rate four local interpretable model-agnostic explanation (LIME) variations from best to worst in an image classification task across 10 trials. A Friedman's test and a Plackett-Luce analysis were conducted to examine participants' rank-order preferences for the variations, and a linear mixed-effects model on eye-tracking data was used to examine on which variations participants expended the most visual effort. Results reveal that, overall, participants preferred images that were non-obfuscated and spent more time fixating on images that highlighted both positive and negative features compared to positive only features. The findings have implications for interface design, particularly for designers aiming to prioritize human-centered preferences. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: When is plant-based meat close enough? A multiplicity- and selection-aware non-inferiority reanalysis of sensory-parity claims
abstract: Claims that a plant-based meat alternative has reached sensory parity can depend on the product designated as the category leader, the endpoint and margin examined, and whether multiple comparisons and product selection are considered. We reanalyzed the public respondent-level exports from a blinded consumer benchmark covering 14 meat categories. Primary products were fixed from the source metadata rather than re-selected from the reanalysis outcomes. We reported paired raw differences, standardized effect sizes, rating-based same-or-better shares, one-sided non-inferiority tests, and an inverted confidence-bound summary termed the minimum data-supported margin. The focal family comprised 14 Overall Liking tests at a 0.5-point margin and was adjusted using Holm's procedure. Chicken Nuggets and Unbreaded Chicken Filets met the nominal criterion, but neither remained non-inferior after familywise adjustment. Across the 70 source-roster contrasts, nine nominal findings were reduced to four after a conservative global Holm adjustment: Texture, Appearance, and Similarity for Chicken Nuggets and Appearance for Meatballs. At 0.5 points, no candidate-product Overall Liking conclusion survived within-category Holm adjustment. Source-designated and export-sample-best leaders differed in two categories, with an additional exact tie in Bacon. The public exports contained no city/site identifier or product-specific purchase, willingness-to-pay, or choice outcome; consequently, the analyzed margins cannot be interpreted as behaviorally validated acceptance thresholds. These findings reposition non-inferiority as one component of a transparent robustness audit: sensory-parity claims require an explicit decision margin, effect-size reporting, multiplicity control, and separation of product screening from confirmation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Intervention scope and crowd evacuation reliability under panic contagion
abstract: Evacuation planning under exit failure is conventionally posed as a routing problem, in which the decision that matters is where each occupant is sent. This paper shows that once panic contagion couples crowd density to its own collapse, a control action becomes a load on the crowd it protects, and its reliability is decided by how many occupants it sets in motion. Three decisions that prior work confounds, the exit assignment, the release schedule and the scope of the repair applied when an exit closes, are varied independently in a validated social-force simulator with SIR-type contagion, across three station geometries with 40 paired seeds per cell. Metering the release into three batches is worth 20 to 36 percentage points. Redirecting only the occupants whose exit closed is worth 7.5 to 9.5 points on a linear-program plan and leaves the number of frozen occupants unchanged, whereas a re-solve that also releases the remaining crowd falls 43.5 to 43.9 points below that targeted repair wherever a cascade can develop. Optimizing the assignment yields no dependable gain. Every occupant ends the run evacuated, stranded or frozen, and the value of an intervention is its balance of stranding recovered against freezing induced. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: A latent counterfactual disentanglement framework for implicit hate speech detection
abstract: Implicit hate speech often conceals hateful intent through semantic camouflage, such as sarcasm and metaphor, causing core toxicity features to remain hidden beneath the surface text. Existing models tend to jointly encode core toxicity and camouflage style during feature extraction, thereby leading to spurious decision shortcuts dominated by camouflage-style cues. To alleviate this problem, this paper approaches implicit hate speech detection from the perspective of camouflage-style removal and proposes a latent counterfactual disentanglement (LCD) framework for implicit hate speech detection. Specifically, LCD decomposes textual latent representations into a core toxicity subspace and a camouflage style subspace through causal feature disentanglement. It further constructs counterfactually augmented representations using a feature-level multiple counterfactual intervention mechanism, thereby reducing the model’s dependence on camouflage style. Meanwhile, a latent semantic reconstruction module is introduced to mitigate the risk of information loss during disentanglement. Experimental results on three challenging public benchmark datasets, namely IHC, SBIC, and DYNA, show that LCD achieves Macro-F1 scores of 79.20%, 91.09%, and 83.43%, respectively. Further experiments and visualization analyses demonstrate that LCD can reduce the leakage of label-related information into the camouflage style branch and improve prediction consistency under style perturbations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: How do I measure emotion regulation repertoire? Let me count the ways: The sum index, distinct index, diversity index, and latent profiles
abstract: Emotion regulation repertoire—the range of strategies used by an individual—is thought to underlie flexible regulation and polyregulation. A larger, diverse repertoire may be more adaptive because it allows for better context-by-strategy fit. However, there is considerable variability in how repertoire diversity is measured and no consensus on the best approach. The present study leveraged seven independent datasets ( N = 3024; M age = 18.96) to examine associations between four different indices of ER repertoire (i.e., sum, distinct, diversity, latent profiles) and test whether employing more complex measures of repertoire provide added value when examining associations with ill-being (i.e., depression, anxiety, stress). Latent profile analysis identified five profiles: “Ruminate & Engage Propensity”, “Reappraise, Engage & Relax Propensity”, “Ruminate & Suppress Propensity”, “Diverse Regulators”, and “Distract & Suppress Propensity”. The sum, distinct, and diversity indices were all positively intercorrelated. Both the distinct and diversity indices showed clear, interpretable associations with each profile. Associations between the sum index and the latent profiles did not follow a theoretically meaningful pattern. Only the sum index and latent profiles were consistently associated with ill-being. Implications of these results are discussed in the context of the indices' conceptual clarity, methodological complexity, and recommendations for the field. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Development and validation of a game-based assessment tool for computational thinking practices in lower primary students
abstract: Computational thinking (CT) is a core problem-solving competence that originated in computer science and now applies across disciplines and to everyday life. It has been widely integrated into K–12 curricula, which creates an urgent need for valid assessments of students’ performance. However, instruments targeting CT practices remain scarce for lower primary learners, and many tools depend on specific programming platforms, capture limited process evidence, or lack adequate psychometric evaluation. This study addresses this gap by developing and validating a game-based assessment tool for CT practices in lower primary students, named CT Practices Quest for Lower Primary (CTPQ-LP). The tool was developed using an Evidence-Centered Game Design (ECGD) framework, with coherent student, task, and evidence models designed to operationalize five practices: pattern recognition, abstraction, problem decomposition, algorithmic thinking, and debugging. The content was validated through expert review and cognitive interviews, followed by a pilot study (n = 74) and a main study (n = 510) administered to students in Grades 1–3 at a Chinese primary school. We examined reliability, item characteristics, and factor structure using classical test theory (CTT) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). We further investigated performance differences across background characteristics and analyzed gameplay records to identify challenges encountered in solving CT problems. The study contributes an assessment tool and a transparent development procedure that can inform CT classroom practice, guide future assessment design, and support evidence-informed improvement of early primary instruction. © 2026

title: Transformations in nursing education: Voices of senior faculty members with decades of experience
abstract: Background: Nursing education in Türkiye has undergone profound structural transformations over the past decades, driven by rapid program expansion, intensifying demands for research productivity, digitalization, and the erosion of academic-clinical continuity. Despite their centrality to educational quality, the lived experiences of senior nursing faculty members navigating these changes remain largely unexplored. Aim: To explore how senior nursing faculty members in Türkiye describe the major transformations in nursing education throughout their careers and how these changes have shaped their professional roles and academic identities. Design: Descriptive qualitative research design using thematic analysis. Settings: Multiple higher education institutions providing nursing education in Türkiye. Participants: Twelve senior nursing faculty members were recruited through purposive sampling with maximum variation, supplemented by snowball sampling to reach participants across diverse institutional contexts; the mean age was 54.67 years, with an average of 29.50 years of academic experience. Methods: Data were collected through semi-structured, in-depth, online individual interviews. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis framework. Rigor was ensured through reflexive researcher positioning, collaborative analytic discussion, and member checking with six participants. Results: Three themes emerged: the transformation of academic nursing identity, characterized by growing distance from clinical practice and competing academic demands; shifting student cultures and the transformation of teaching, reflecting pedagogical alienation and decreased depth of learning; and the transformation of academic production from quality to quantity, characterized by metric-driven academic value, disconnection from nursing practice, and the burden of academic productivity. Conclusions: Senior nursing faculty members in Türkiye are navigating interlocking structural pressures that have destabilized the professional foundations of nursing academia. Urgent institutional responses are needed, including restructuring academic roles to protect clinical engagement, supporting pedagogical adaptation, and reconceptualizing promotion criteria to honor the full breadth of nursing scholarly contribution. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Employment subcenters and polycentric urban development in the Greater Dhaka Region, Bangladesh
abstract: Although a significant number of studies have focused on urban growth patterns in Dhaka, the spatial structure of employment and its roles in shaping polycentric urban development is poorly understood. Specifically, how employment subcenters (ESCs) emerge and organize under conditions of informal and infrastructure-led urban growth typical of Global South megacities remains unclear. Hence, this study poses the question of how ESC formation is related with the construction and development of a polycentric urban employment structure in the city and how their hierarchical spatial organization shapes intra-urban agglomeration. To answer this question, the spatial distribution of employment in the Greater Dhaka Region during the 2011-2013 study period was analyzed based on fine-scale employment data from the 2013 economic census together with Local Moran's I (LMI) within a grid-based framework. An optimal grid size and shape were used to detect ESCs, including their location, hierarchy, spatial extent, geographical distribution, spatial characteristics and processes. The study found 59 ESCs, including one rank 1 center, four rank 2 centers, 18 rank 3 centers, and 36 rank four centers. The findings reveal a core-dominant but dispersed polycentric employment structure, in which high-ranked ESCs concentrated within approximately 20 km of Dhaka's historical core and low-ranked ESCs developed along major transportation corridors in peripheral areas. The findings suggest that the employment structure observed during the study period reflected a hierarchical, corridor-oriented pattern influenced by market forces and infrastructure-led urban processes rather than by planned decentralization, with weak metropolitan coordination strengthening the continued dominance of the historical core. These findings refine polycentricity theory for Global South contexts and provide evidence to support data-driven spatial planning and more balanced urban development in rapidly urbanizing regions. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Rural occupational health in Colombia: policy–practice gaps among agricultural workers in Bolívar, Valle del Cauca
abstract: This study examines policy–practice gaps in occupational safety and health (OSH) protection among agricultural workers in Bolívar, Valle del Cauca, Colombia. A multi-method design combined 14 semi-structured interviews and two focus groups with an adapted ILO Vision Zero Fund survey administered to 200 agricultural workers. Survey data were analyzed descriptively and through exploratory Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA), and qualitative and quantitative findings were integrated during interpretation. Findings showed multidimensional patterns involving occupational protection, working conditions, health-service availability, agricultural practices, and productive autonomy. These patterns coexisted with informal, seasonal, short-term, day-labor, and subsistence work, limited occupational risk coverage, discontinuous prevention and training, and fragmented institutional coordination. Qualitative findings further highlighted women’s combined productive and care roles, local and traditional knowledge, community participation, and heterogeneity across territorial settings and agricultural practices as relevant to prevention and decision-making. Conventional social protection and occupational risk arrangements centered on formal, contributory employment may not fully respond to dispersed and unstable rural work. Strengthening rural OSH requires integrated, territorially adapted, gender-sensitive strategies linking prevention, social protection, sustained training, institutional coordination, community participation, and productive autonomy. The findings support assessing differentiated and progressive protection pathways, including the feasibility of subsidized occupational risk coverage for more vulnerable workers and small productive units, combined with contributory mechanisms where work arrangements are more stable. By linking worker-level realities with institutional and policy-implementation gaps, this study provides evidence to inform more equitable rural OSH policies responsive to diverse territorial realities in Colombia. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Emergent collaborative scheduling in satellite swarms: A distributed multi-agent reinforcement learning approach with adaptive experience evolution
abstract: Autonomous collaboration among multiple Earth observation satellites is essential for improving the performance of satellite swarms. However, this task is challenging because of limited onboard computing resources and unstable inter-satellite links, particularly when global coordination is required under communication constraints. Traditional centralized optimization methods often adapt poorly to dynamic observation requests, whereas existing multi-agent approaches may incur communication overhead that hinders practical deployment. To address this issue, we propose a distributed scheduling framework that enables emergent global coordination through local agent interactions and formulates the problem as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP). Specifically, we develop L-QTRAN, a multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm that enables satellites to coordinate based on local observations with limited communication. To alleviate the non-stationarity inherent in dynamic swarm environments, we introduce an Adaptive Experience Evolution (AEE) mechanism. This mechanism follows the survival-of-the-fittest principle by selectively retaining elite transition experiences, thereby accelerating the development of cooperative strategies. Furthermore, a Random Segment Sampling (RSS) technique is introduced to improve training stability and convergence in high-dimensional solution spaces. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms the baseline methods under weak-communication conditions and achieves sub-second response times, highlighting its potential for autonomous satellite swarms operating in dynamic environments. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.
label: Social Sciences

title: Dynamic engagement patterns during collaborative reasoning discussions and their relations to adolescents’ individual reasoning
abstract: Background: Collaborative Reasoning (CR) is a dialogic, learner-centered instructional approach shown to promote learners’ higher-order thinking. However, existing research has paid less attention to how learners engage in CR processes and how the temporal dynamics of engagement relate to the development of individual reasoning. Aims: To address this gap, this study investigated the temporal development of behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement during CR discussions and examined how evolving engagement patterns were associated with subsequent individual reasoning. Sample: The participants were 29 seventh-graders from a middle school in China. The students formed four discussion groups, and each group participated in seven CR discussions. Methods: The 28 discussions were video-coded for cognitive, emotional, and behavioral interactions (6868 codes). Process mining and epistemic network analysis were used to model shifts in engagement patterns. Individual reasoning was assessed through post-discussion essays. Results: Engagement patterns shifted dynamically over time, moving from socially shared regulation to sustained knowledge co-construction. Groups differed in the timing and trajectory of this transition: some groups shifted earlier, whereas others engaged in prolonged regulatory exchanges. The group characterized by later transitions produced fewer basic argumentative elements but more advanced elements in their individual essays. Conclusions: This study highlights dynamic engagement patterns as an important link between collaborative processes and learning outcomes and underscores the importance of understanding temporal configurations of regulation and knowledge co-construction in collaborative learning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
label: Social Sciences

title: Virtual reality as a catalyst for change: Promoting communication intention, policy support and interaction with migrant workers in Singapore
abstract: Migrant workers are vital to the host country's development, yet they often remain socially invisible and face barriers to social integration. Drawing on narrative persuasion and indirect contact perspectives, this research examines how immersive storytelling relates to empathy and supportive orientations toward migrant workers through two laboratory experiments in Singapore. Study One (N = 125) compared narrative delivery via virtual reality (VR), 360-degree video, and text. VR generated the highest immersion, and a sequential path indicated that greater immersion was associated with stronger identification with the protagonist, followed by greater empathy; empathy was associated with stronger willingness to interact with migrant workers, greater policy support, and higher future supportive behavioral intentions. Study Two (N = 87) focused on a key VR design choice, avatar perspective, by comparing self-versus other-embodiment in the VR experience. Self-embodiment increased self-presence, while greater self-presence was sequentially associated with immersion, identification with the protagonist, and empathy, followed by the same pattern of supportive outcomes. Together, the studies show that both modality and within-VR self-representation shape empathy-based pathways toward supportive orientations, offering actionable guidance for designing immersive interventions that promote understanding and support for marginalized groups. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
label: Social Sciences

title: Unpacking the pathways: Self-regulation’s mediating effect on students’ self-efficacy and mathematics achievement
abstract: This research design aims to investigate the influence of self-regulation as the mediating variable on the relationship between self-efficacy and mathematics achievement of the participants who are Grade Nine students at the selected public high schools in the Philippines for the school year 2024 – 2025. The study seeks to enhance the theoretical and empirical understanding of psychological processes that contribute to effective student performance in mathematics, where planning, monitoring, adjusting, and reflecting are critical for academic success. A quantitative descriptive correlational research design was used to collect the data through two adopted survey questionnaires administered using a simple random sampling technique. The survey measured key constructs, including self-efficacy and self-regulation, while mathematics achievement was evaluated using first quarter mathematics grades. The study included a total of 845 valid responses from Grade Nine students. The data collected were treated using frequency count, percentage, weighted mean, standard deviation, Pearson’s r, and multiple regression analysis. The analysis of the findings revealed moderate levels of students’ self-efficacy and self-regulation in planning and monitoring, while levels of adjusting and reflecting were high. Moreover, there was a significant weak positive correlation between self-efficacy and mathematics achievement, a weak positive for self-efficacy and self-regulation, and a weak positive for self-regulation and mathematics achievement. It is determined that the students’ self-regulation partially mediates the relationship between students’ self-efficacy and mathematics achievement, indicating that self-efficacy enhances mathematics performance not only directly but also indirectly by fostering self-regulatory behaviors. Thus, teaching staff and administrators must put into practice methods that strengthen self-efficacy and self-regulation to boost mathematics achievement. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Regulatory exclusion and occupational health risk in Turkish firefighting: a legal-epidemiological policy analysis
abstract: Article 2(2)(b) of Turkey’s Law No. 6331 on Occupational Safety and Health excludes the intervention activities of disaster and emergency units from that statute’s scope. The exclusion concerns duties performed during response operations; it does not establish that firefighters lack every protection under other legal or administrative instruments. This evidence-informed legal and policy analysis combines a structured, non-systematic occupational-health evidence synthesis, doctrinal analysis, a review of 43 Turkish judicial decisions issued from 1997 to 2024, and a functional comparison with the United Kingdom. International evidence identifies occupational firefighting as carcinogenic to humans (IARC Group 1), links fire suppression with sharply elevated risk of fatal coronary events, and documents substantial psychological and musculoskeletal burdens. In the official sources examined, no nationally binding firefighter-specific instrument was identified that prescribed post-incident decontamination, detailed health-surveillance content, personal protective equipment performance monitoring, or structured psychological support. The judicial corpus was coded across eight analytical categories; its holdings concentrated on pay, personnel status, compensation, procedure, and jurisdiction rather than concrete preventive OSH duties. We interpret these findings through a structural accountability gap model, under which the statutory exclusion may constrain investigation, data generation, standard-setting, and regulatory learning. The model is interpretive, not a tested causal finding. United Kingdom law provides an illustrative comparator because it retains general employer and enforcement duties without a categorical operational exclusion. The article proposes eight evidence-linked policy options. Their effectiveness, feasibility, and cost-effectiveness require prospective evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Exploring the relationships between problem and responsible gambling behaviors across time
abstract: Recent legislative and technological changes have transformed the gambling landscape in the United States, underscoring the need to better understand both problem gambling and responsible gambling behaviors. The Positive Play framework conceptualizes responsible gambling from the player’s perspective, yet little is known about how these behaviors change over time. The present study examined longitudinal changes in Positive Play scores and problem gambling symptoms among a sample of adult gamblers (n = 2,942). Participants completed repeated assessments of the Positive Play Scale and the Problem Gambling Severity Index across five waves over approximately two years. Confirmatory factor analyses supported the original four-factor structure of the Positive Play Scale. Latent growth models indicated that scores across all Positive Play subscales increased over time, while problem gambling symptoms decreased. Notably, increases in gambling literacy scores were associated with greater reductions in problem gambling severity, whereas changes in other Positive Play domains were not. These findings suggest that gambling literacy, in particular, may be associated with reductions in gambling-related harm over time. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Narrative-driven VR exergames for active older adults: Examining the impact of narrative styles and themes on motivation and user experience
abstract: Older adults often face the dual challenge of insufficient physical activity and unmet psychological needs. Although exergames can promote physical activity, they often struggle to sustain motivation or adequately support psychological need satisfaction. This work explores the potential of integrating narrative into a VR cycling exergame, focusing on how narrative design can enhance motivation and fulfill psychological needs. Two experiments examined the impact of narrative styles with varying interactivity demands and different narrative themes (hedonic, eudaimonic, mixed-affective) on user experience. Study 1 (N=15) suggested that interactive narrative styles were associated with enhanced autonomy and relatedness, facilitated attentional dissociation from bodily fatigue, and led to higher psychological need satisfaction and lower perceived exertion, albeit at the cost of increased cognitive demands. Study 2 (N=36) compared hedonic, eudaimonic, and mixed-affective narratives. Hedonic narratives appeared to support flow and motivation with relatively low cognitive demands, whereas eudaimonic narratives were linked to deeper emotional and reflective engagement but imposed higher cognitive and emotional demands, leading to reduced replay intention. Mixed-affective narratives, by contrast, presented a potentially more balanced trade-off between motivational benefits and competence satisfaction. Interpreted through a Self-Determination Theory-informed perspective, these findings provide insights into how narrative styles and affective themes may be leveraged to design VR exergames that better align psychological engagement with older adults’ physical capacities. Overall, these exploratory findings highlight both the promise and the limitations of narrative-driven exergame design, and they offer implications for the development of adaptive, psychologically informed exergames for older adults. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Industrial robotization and provincial green synergy performance in China: Coupling coordination, regional disparities, and dynamic responses
abstract: Rapid industrial automation is becoming an important feature of production systems operating under economic and environmental constraints, while its observed performance implications may emerge with delay and differ across regions. This study examines whether industrial robotization and provincial green synergy performance evolve in tandem, where coordination disparities originate, and how their dynamic relationship unfolds. Using panel data for 30 Chinese provincial-level regions from 2006 to 2023, we employ a shift-share measure of robot installation density and estimate green synergy performance with a super-efficiency slacks-based measure integrating economic output, urban greening, industrial pollution, and carbon emissions. The coupling coordination degree evaluates the alignment of the two systems, the Dagum Gini decomposition identifies the sources of regional disparities, and a panel vector autoregression examines reciprocal temporal predictability and lagged responses. The national coordination degree increased from 0.4810 to 0.7740, while the overall Gini coefficient declined from 0.1685 to 0.1009. Between-region differences remained the largest component of disparity, accounting for 51.14% on average, with the eastern-western gap being the widest. Robotization predicted green synergy performance nationally and in eastern China, with a negative first-lag association followed by a positive second-lag association. By period 10, innovations in robotization accounted for 18.63% of the forecast-error variance in green synergy performance nationally and 34.02% in eastern China. These results reveal a stage-dependent and regionally uneven predictive relationship, although the research design does not identify structural causal effects. The findings highlight the value of coordinating robot deployment with green process redesign, region-specific technical support, and full-cycle performance monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: SGRLCF: Supervision-guided reinforcement learning for rating prediction in collaborative filtering
abstract: Collaborative Filtering (CF) is widely used for rating prediction in Recommender Systems (RSs). Traditional CF methods are highly sensitive to data sparsity, while recent Deep Learning (DL) based CF models enhance representation capacity by capturing complex nonlinear user–item interactions. However, most DL based CF methods rely on standard Supervised Learning (SL) and optimize prediction errors independently for each interaction. With sparse data, gradients estimated from limited observations may exhibit greater stochastic variability, leading to unstable optimization and suboptimal convergence in deep models. To address this issue, we propose a Supervision-Guided Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for rating prediction in CF, termed SGRLCF. Rather than minimizing only per-interaction regression errors, SGRLCF constructs reinforcement rewards from ground-truth labels to guide sequential optimization. Specifically, we design a dual-level reward scheme that jointly considers immediate prediction error and overall training improvement. Then, we introduce a validation-guided fusion strategy that incorporates a collaborative prior derived from the training data into the actor output, with the fusion weight selected on a held-out validation subset. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets show that SGRLCF achieves competitive or superior Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) in both single-domain and cross-domain scenarios. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Combating human trafficking in Vietnam: How does the 3P+P framework influence policies and laws?
abstract: Human trafficking remains among the greatest human rights violations globally, and Vietnam—as both a source country and a transit country—has undergone substantial legal and policy reform over the past fifteen years. This article systematically analyzes the development of Vietnam's legal and policy framework for the prevention and control of human trafficking from 2010 to 2025, applying the 3P+P theoretical framework (Prevention, Protection, Prosecution, and Partnership) as the primary analytical lens. Drawing on doctrinal legal analysis and policy analysis, this study examines domestic legislation, including the 2011 Law on Prevention and Combat of Trafficking in Persons, the 2015 Penal Code (as amended in 2017), and the landmark 2024 Law on Prevention and Combat of Trafficking in Persons, alongside international instruments—notably the Palermo Protocol and the ASEAN Convention Against Trafficking in Persons (ACTIP)—and empirical materials from UNODC, UNDP, and the U.S. Department of State's annual Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Reports. Analysis across three phases (2010–2015, 2016–2020, and 2021–2025) reveals a progressive trajectory from foundational criminalization toward a multisectoral, human rights-centered approach, reflecting both endogenous developmental priorities and exogenous normative pressures. Key findings indicate that while Vietnam has achieved meaningful normative alignment with international standards—particularly in victim protection, legal aid, and regional cooperation—critical implementation gaps persist, including inadequate victim identification, weak interagency coordination, the absence of corporate supply chain accountability, and delayed legal responses to emerging exploitation forms such as online scam operations. This study offers the first longitudinal 3P+P analysis of Vietnam's complete 2010–2025 legal and policy trajectory, including the 2024 Law, highlighting the persistent gap between normative progress and implementation outcomes. Accordingly, the article proposes concrete legal amendments: incorporating “abuse of a position of vulnerability” into Article 150 of the Penal Code, formalizing NGO legal status in specialized law, and establishing a corporate accountability regime for forced labor in supply chains. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Navigating Sustainability of Fisheries in Pulicat Lagoon: An Indicator-Based Multidimensional Assessment
abstract: Sustainable management of lagoon fisheries requires an integrated assessment of ecological and human dimensions. Pulicat Lagoon, India’s second-largest brackishwater lagoon, supports diverse fisheries and livelihoods but faces threats from anthropogenic activities and environmental degradation. This study applied the modified Rapid Appraisal for Fisheries (RAPFISH) framework to evaluate the sustainability status of Pulicat Lagoon fisheries using a multi-dimensional, indicator-based approach. The ten major fisheries were assessed across five dimensions: ecological, economic, social, technological, and governance based on 34 indicators. Sustainability scores were estimated using multi-dimensional scaling, supported by leverage analysis to identify influential indicators. The overall sustainability score of Pulicat Lagoon fisheries was 47.50%, classifying the system as ‘less sustainable’. Ecological (65.81%) and governance (53.35%) dimensions exhibited relatively better performance, while economic (46.39%), social (43.70%), and technological (28.26%) dimensions remained weak. Penaeid shrimp (53.29%) and crab fisheries (52.92%) showed comparatively higher sustainability than other fisheries. Key drivers influencing sustainability included resilience, fishing income, education, handling and processing practices and research and development support. The findings of this study directly contribute to several key Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), namely SDG 14 (Life Below Water), SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 16 (Strong Institutions). Therefore, these findings highlight the importance of implementing targeted, dimension-specific interventions to strengthen adaptive fisheries management and to ensure the long-term sustainability of fisheries in the Pulicat Lagoon. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Coastal and Estuarine Research Federation 2026.

title: Enhancing Empathy and Creativity through Embodied Cognition: The Application of a Hand Pain Intelligent Simulation Glove in Design Education
abstract: Fostering students' empathy and creativity toward marginalized user groups is essential to achieving human-centered design in design education. Although experiential learning has gained increasing attention in recent years, there remains a lack of operable and perceptually engaging tools to support empathy instruction. To this end, this study developed a hand pain simulation glove and incorporated it into design instruction. Two quantitative experiments and one qualitative study were conducted to evaluate the glove's pedagogical potential. In the initial experiment, 30 students were subjected to three distinct pedagogical interventions: textual experience, video experience, and embodied experience, with the objective of comparing their respective impacts on empathy scores. A subsequent experiment engaged another cohort of 30 students in product design tasks under different experiential conditions, and their creative outcomes were evaluated by expert raters. Results showed that embodied simulation produced greater gains in empathy and design performance than text- and video-based instruction, particularly in innovative thinking and technical functionality. By translating otherwise invisible and action-dependent pain-related constraints into first-person sensorimotor experience, the glove supported students in reframing user problems and generating more context-sensitive design responses. These findings position embodied pain simulation as a pedagogical approach for empathy-oriented design education and provide a transferable framework for related learning contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Development and validation of an ICD-11–based problematic social media use scale
abstract: The present study aimed to address conceptual and measurement challenges in assessing problematic social media use by developing a scale grounded in the ICD-11 diagnostic framework for behavioral addictions. Item generation was based on core features including impaired control, prioritization of the behavior, continuation despite negative consequences, and functional impairment. Following expert review and pilot testing, data were collected in multiple phases. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a multidimensional structure consistent with ICD-11 criteria. Measurement invariance was established across gender (female vs. male) and age groups (emerging adults vs. adults) in separate Multigroup Confirmatory Analyses. Item Response Theory analyses showed that the scale demonstrates higher discrimination at low to moderate levels of problematic use, highlighting its sensitivity for early detection. Overall, the findings suggest that the scale is a theoretically grounded and psychometrically sound instrument for assessing problematic social media use, with potential applications in research, screening, and early intervention contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Between criminalization and decriminalization: Homosexuality, gender norms, and sociolegal change in Kosovo
abstract: Since the mid-nineteenth century, Kosovo has undergone significant social transformation and legal reform, particularly in relation to sexuality and state intervention in private life. This study provides a historical analysis of criminal legislation addressing homosexuality, examining both normative legal frameworks and prevailing social attitudes. At first glance, the fact that approximately 95 of the population of Kosovo identifies as Muslim might suggest the existence of a pronounced social resistance towards homosexuals, as seen in certain countries of the Eastern world. However, empirical research reveals a considerably more intricate social reality. While traditional attitudes toward homosexuality persist, there is no proportionally strong political or social mobilization against the rights of homosexual individuals. Indeed, a significant segment of the population endorses the civil rights of LGBT people in general. The main reason for these attitudes is that national identity often carries more social and political weight than religious affiliation. The research employed a mixed-methods design, integrating a literature review, historical and comparative analysis, two personal communications, and a structured questionnaire survey conducted with 1,050 respondents stratified into three age groups. The χ^2 test of independence was used to assess the associations between attitudes, gender, and age, while Cramer's V measured the strength of these relationships. The findings demonstrate that age exerts a statistically significant influence on attitudes, whereas gender differences are relatively small. The majority of the respondents (74.8%) recognize that homosexuals and lesbians often marry heterosexually to conform to tradition, while 77.3% believe imprisonment would not eliminate homosexuality. Furthermore, the results indicated that more than half (53.2%) oppose renewed punishment for homosexuals, and 52% acknowledge its timeless existence. The findings of this study suggest that attitudes toward homosexuality in Kosovo are shaped by a complex interplay of historical experience, legal change, cultural norms, and contemporary human rights discourse. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Work–life conflict and psychological well-being among working women: A qualitative study from counselors’ perspectives
abstract: Women's increasing participation in the workforce has intensified their exposure to multiple and competing role demands arising from work, family, and personal responsibilities. These overlapping demands may generate work-life conflict and affect psychological well-being. Although previous studies have examined these issues, much of the existing literature has relied on quantitative approaches, with limited qualitative evidence drawn from counsellors who work directly with affected women. This study explored counsellors' perspectives on work-life conflict and psychological well-being among working women. A qualitative research design was employed using semi-structured interviews with seven professional counsellors who had experience handling cases involving working women. Participants were selected through purposive sampling, and the interview data were analysed using inductive thematic analysis. The analysis generated six main themes: work-life conflict experienced by working women, psychological and emotional impact of conflict, coping strategies and conflict management, counselling as a safe space and source of emotional support, factors influencing work-life balance and well-being, and challenges faced by counsellors in supporting working women. Three emergent themes were also identified: normalisation of working beyond office hours, the importance of personal boundaries and emotional regulation, and counselling as emotional release rather than problem solving. The findings indicate that working women's psychological well-being is shaped by the interaction of workplace demands, family responsibilities, emotional strain, coping resources, and support systems. This study contributes qualitative insights into counselling practice and highlights the relevance of Role Conflict Theory and Boundary Theory in understanding the psychosocial experiences of working women. The findings offer practical implications for counsellors, organisations, and policymakers in developing more responsive support systems for working women. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Informal elder care in Malaysia: Cultural norms, motivations and family dynamics shaping adult children’s caregiving roles
abstract: This qualitative study explores the cultural norms and motivational factors shaping adult children's involvement in informal elder care for ageing parents in Malaysia from a multidisciplinary perspective. Amid rapid population ageing, growing numbers of working adult children undertake informal caregiving responsibilities while balancing employment and family commitments, often in contexts of limited formal support. Within this setting, caregiving arrangements are largely negotiated within families and shaped by deeply embedded social expectations and moral obligations. Drawing on in-depth interviews with thirteen working adult children from middle- to high-income households, the study examines the motivations underpinning caregiving roles as well as the family dynamics and challenges encountered. Thematic analysis identified nine interrelated factors influencing the assumption of caregiving responsibilities: (1) rejection of institutional care, (2) siblings' inability or unwillingness to provide care, (3) a sense of responsibility and perceived capability, (4) parental selection, (5) caregiving as a natural family role transition, (6) religious motivation, (7) caregiving as an opportunity, (8) personal choice, and (9) intergenerational role modelling. Beyond motivational drivers, participants' narratives reveal the emotional, cultural and moral complexities of informal elder care within a collectivist social context, shaped by familial expectations, religious values and caregiving norms. The findings highlight the need for integrated support systems and responsive social policies to reduce caregiver burden and enhance quality of life among working caregivers. By conceptualising informal elder care as a culturally embedded and multidimensional family practice, this study offers insights relevant to counselling, public health, social policy and family studies, while contributing to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 3: Good Health and Well-being. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Integrating local cultural values into deep learning pedagogy: A framework for teaching science fiction writing in Indonesia
abstract: This study examines the integration of the Deep Learning curriculum with Javanese cultural values in teaching science fiction writing to high school students. The study is motivated by the importance of developing STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) competencies integrated with the strengthening of cultural identity in the era of globalization. A mixed methods research approach was applied involving 30 students and 2 Indonesian language teachers at SMA Negeri 9 Malang. Data were collected through structured observations, semi-structured interviews, and analysis of student work documents using rubrics developed based on the 6C's dimensions of Deep Learning (Critical Thinking, Creativity, Collaboration, Communication, Character, Citizenship). The research results revealed that the integration successfully actualized all dimensions of Deep Learning at a high level (scores of 4.3-4.8 on a 5-point scale), with the highest achievements in the Collaboration (4.8) and Creativity (4.7) dimensions. Qualitative analysis of student work identified five patterns of Javanese cultural integration, namely: (1) integration of technology with Javanese philosophy, (2) technology as an optimizer of local wisdom, (3) mythology as the basis of technology, (4) collaborative resolution of generational conflicts, and (5) culture as a value system regulating technology. As many as 55% of student works reached the very good category, showing a significant improvement in aspects of creativity and cultural integration. The research conclusion states that the integration of the Deep Learning curriculum with Javanese cultural values not only improves technical competence in writing science fiction but also develops contextual scientific literacy and strengthens students' cultural identity. This model represents a transformative synthesis between global education paradigms and local wisdom relevant to the Indonesian educational context. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Mental imagery and visuospatial processing in visual communication design education: Examining relationships with creative performance and academic achievement in university students
abstract: This study investigated the relationships among mental imagery, visuospatial processing, creative performance, and academic achievement in university visual communication design students. A sample of 156 undergraduate students majoring in visual communication design completed the Mental Imagery Test (MIT), Raven's Standard Progressive Matrices (RSPM), and Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking (TTCT), while their academic performance in design studio, typography, digital imaging, and visual theory courses was assessed through course grades. Results indicated significant positive correlations between mental imagery abilities and both creative performance and academic achievement across all design-related courses. Visuospatial processing, operationalized here as figural-inductive visuospatial reasoning, partially mediated the relationship between mental imagery and academic performance in design studio and digital imaging courses, while creative self-efficacy emerged as an additional mediator for typography performance. Gender differences were minimal, with males showing slight advantages only in spatial transformation tasks. These findings underscore the importance of developing mental imagery and visuospatial skills within visual communication curricula and suggest that targeted cognitive training interventions may enhance both creative output and academic success in design education contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Natural capital: the boom and bust of a metaphor? Insights from Scotland
abstract: Despite a fifty-year academic history, the concept of ‘natural capital’ has only been translated into national policy and practice more recently. Since the early 2000s, global initiatives like The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity and the UN System for Environmental Economic Accounts have spurred country-level adoption of natural capital approaches around the world. To examine the implications of this uptake, we traced the concept’s evolution in Scotland through a discourse analysis of 14 interviews, supplemented by key documents and events. Natural capital entered the Scottish context in the early 2010s, intended to make nature visible to decision-makers through economically valuing the environment. By the 2020s, concerns over insufficient public funding for ecological restoration, conceptualised as a nature finance gap, shifted focus to making nature financeable by the private sector. Subsequently, natural capital became emblematic of emergent nature markets, particularly carbon-based mechanisms, precipitating a boom in private sector interest. As the risks of operationalising these markets became apparent to investors, confidence in natural capital faltered by 2023. This prompted the public sector to assume responsibility for de-risking market development. We argue natural capital has facilitated a discursive slide from advocacy for valuation towards commodification practices, framing environmental crises as apolitical market opportunities. This trajectory tends towards privatisation of potential returns while socialising risk through public mechanisms. While natural capital may enhance aspects of nature’s legibility within existing political and economic systems, we caution that its discursive dominance constrains more transformative ambitions to reconfigure the structures that harm nature and its restoration. title: Equity in print: Unveiling GEDSI construction in an Indonesian junior high school english textbook
abstract: This study investigates how Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) are represented in English for Nusantara Grade Seven, an Indonesian government-issued English textbook developed under the Merdeka Curriculum. While previous textbook studies have predominantly focused on binary gender representation, limited research has examined disability and social inclusion through a multimodal critical discourse analysis (MCDA) framework. Addressing this gap, the present study analyzes how verbal and visual elements jointly construct meanings related to gender equality, disability, and inclusion. Using Kress and van Leeuwen's MCDA framework, the study examined the entire 264-page textbook and identified Chapters 1 and 2 as the only sections containing explicit GEDSI-related representations. The analysis focused on ideational, interpersonal, and textual meanings embedded in images, comic strips, and written passages. The findings reveal partial efforts toward inclusive representation. Female and male characters are portrayed in both domestic and public roles, indicating attempts to challenge traditional gender stereotypes. The textbook also includes characters with physical disabilities, particularly wheelchair users, and presents them as socially active participants in school and family life. However, representations remain limited in scope. Physical disabilities dominate the portrayals, while cognitive, sensory, and invisible disabilities are absent. In addition, female characters with disabilities are less visible and less empowered than male characters with disabilities, reflecting intersectional inequality. Although the textbook promotes positive messages of diversity and participation, GEDSI representation appears only in selected chapters and is not consistently integrated throughout the textbook. This study contributes to scholarship on inclusive education, multimodal textbook analysis, and GEDSI representation in English language teaching materials. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Development of an immersion-type hydrogel-integrated microfluidic glass fiber-based analytical device and its application to smartphone-assisted glucose colorimetric assay
abstract: Microfluidic paper-based analytical devices (μPADs) are attractive platforms for on-site analysis; however, quantitative analysis remains challenging because sampling strongly influences analytical performance. Existing sampling methods often require precise volumetric sampling or operator-dependent handling, which involves an inherent trade-off between analytical simplicity and quantitative reliability. To overcome this limitation, herein, we propose the concept of a quantitative assay using an immersion-type hydrogel-integrated microfluidics glass fiber-based analytical device (IHμGFAD). The IHμGFAD consisted of a reagent-encapsulated hydrogel for reaction/detection with a glass fiber channel for sampling. The combination of the hydrogel with the glass fiber channel was realized by exploiting the self-adhesive property of hydrophobic patterns fabricated using a liquid crystal display 3D printer. The immersion-based quantitative assay using the IHμGFAD was demonstrated with a glucose oxidase/horseradish peroxidase-based glucose colorimetric assay as a model system. The limit of glucose detection (3σ) was estimated to be 68 μM. The immersion-based assay was also applied to the quantification of glucose in human serum controls and pooled human serum, demonstrating its potential applicability to real-sample analysis. The immersion-based assay provides a μGFAD-based analytical method that achieves both practical user-friendliness and reliable quantitative performance, and it contributes to the advancement of on-site quantitative analysis in a wide range of fields, including healthcare, environmental monitoring, and food safety. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Think-pair-share strategy integrated with Google Classroom: Investigating its effect on students with different cognitive styles for learning about electrolysis
abstract: While acknowledging that students organise, process and perceive information in different ways, empirical studies report that students perform poorly in chemistry, and the topic of electrolysis, in particular. Some of these studies suggest integrating technology into science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education. A think-pair-share instructional strategy, integrated with Google Classroom (TPSISIGC) was useful for increasing students' achievement and active learning. This study examined the effect of the TPSISIGC on students' achievement in electrolysis for different cognitive styles and the challenges students encounter when electrolysis is taught using the TPSISIGC. The study involved secondary school chemistry students and used a quasi-experimental research design. Students in the experimental group were taught electrolysis utilising TPSISIGC, and the control group was exposed to the lecture method. Data were collected using the Electrolysis Achievement Test (EAT), Group Embedded Figure Test (GEFT), and a questionnaire titled Student Challenges When Taught Electrolysis Using Think-Pair-Share Integrated with Google Classroom (SCETPSIGC). The instruments were validated by three experts, and reliability indices of 0.88, 0.85, and 0.80 were established for EAT, GEFT, and SCETPSIGC, respectively. The data collected were analysed using mean, standard deviations and ANCOVA. The study findings reveal that TPSISIGC, compared to the lecture method, significantly improved students' achievement on the topic of electrolysis. Although no significant difference was found between students with field-dependent and field-independent cognitive styles when they were taught about electrolysis using TPSISIGC, there was a significant interaction effect between cognitive styles and treatment on secondary school students' achievement on the topic of electrolysis. Moreover, inadequate teacher training, too little time, unstable internet connectivity and unstable power supply were some of the challenges students encountered while using TPSISIGC. The researchers concluded that TPSISIGC is an inclusive strategy that enhances the achievement of both field-dependent and field-independent students and that the effectiveness of instructional strategies can vary and depends on students' cognitive styles. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Integrated investment and recovery optimization for power distribution system resilience under hurricane hazards
abstract: Hurricane resilience of a distribution system depends not only on the amount of pre-event investment but also on how a fixed budget is distributed among capabilities that act at different stages of disruption. This study develops a two-stage mixed-integer linear programming framework that jointly allocates investment to three functional resilience capacities: damage resistance through utility-pole upgrades, emergency service continuity through rooftop photovoltaic battery units, and restoration capacity through prepositioned crews, equipment, and spare poles. A parametric hurricane wind-field model and available pole-fragility functions are used to generate scenario-specific damage states. A resource-constrained recovery model then represents localized emergency supply, sequential pole-replacement tasks, switching, and network re-energization. Locally controlled capacities are committed before landfall and dispatched, rather than expanded, during recovery, while external assistance is represented as an exogenous time-dependent input. The objective is to minimize cumulative unmet demand over a 10-day recovery horizon. Application to the IEEE 123-bus system shows that the optimal capacity profile changes nonlinearly with hurricane intensity and budget availability. At the lowest modeled intensities, larger budgets produce mixed portfolios with substantial restoration investment, whereas damage resistance becomes most consistently dominant at intermediate intensities around 48–53 m/s. Around 58–63 m/s, the marginal value of additional hardening declines sharply relative to restoration capacity. At higher intensities, larger-budget portfolios shift toward recovery-oriented resources, whereas rooftop photovoltaic–battery units provide a supplementary localized service buffer under severe budget constraints. At the highest modeled intensity and lowest budget, part of the prescribed budget remains unallocated because no additional improvement is identified within the modeled intervention set and recovery horizon. Directional and Bernoulli damage sensitivities alter the precise allocation and transition location but preserve the intermediate-intensity hardening peak and the subsequent shift toward recovery-oriented investment. The framework provides a transferable method for identifying system-specific resilience-capacity priorities rather than a universal wind speed threshold. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Dual-cycle mechanism of project-based learning in engineering soft skills development
abstract: Given the relatively limited resource conditions and institutional environment of local universities (LUs), how to construct a practical and realistic project-based learning (PBL) implementation framework still requires systematic exploration. This study constructs and verifies a dual-cycle PBL model that integrates institutional context analysis (external cycle) with continuous feedback and reflection (internal cycle). A quasi-experimental sequential mixed-methods design was used. 93 sophomore Chemical Engineering and Technology(CET) students at Chongqing H University were assigned to an experimental group (n=48) and a control group (n=45). The experimental group received a 6-month intervention, using the proposed structured dual-cycle PBL framework. The control group received traditional lecture-based course teaching, with the same project tasks and overall assessment structure. Results showed: (1) The experimental group demonstrated extremely significant improvement in overall soft skills (pre-test M=3.64, post-test M=4.34, Δ =0.70, p<0.001), while the control group showed only a negligible natural growth (Δ≈0.17, p>0.05); (2) Repeated measures analysis of variance confirmed that there were extremely significant Group × Time interaction effects in all four soft skill dimensions (all p<0.001, partial η^2=0.338-0.483, with large effect sizes), which proved that the improvement in skills was associated with PBL intervention measures rather than time factors; (3) Creativity and collaboration skills showed the most significant improvement; (4) Qualitative data indicated that the dual-cycle framework was highly consistent with the application-oriented talent cultivation orientation of the learning unit, and maintained structural stability even under limited resource conditions. The results show that the dual-cycle PBL significantly enhances overall soft skills, with creativity and collaboration improving the most. The proposed dual-cycle framework provides a context-adaptive, structurally stable implementation path for engineering education in LUs. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Sound temporal personality and perceived posttraumatic growth: Positive affect as a prospective indirect pathway in a half-longitudinal design
abstract: Posttraumatic growth (PTG) is crucial for individuals' psychological well-being and development after adversity. While personality traits have been associated with perceived PTG, the processes linking personality to perceived PTG remain poorly understood. This study examined whether positive affect (PA) constitutes a prospective indirect pathway linking Sound Temporal Personality (STP) with perceived PTG. Employing a two-wave longitudinal design over a six-month interval, we assessed 312 college students and tested a half-longitudinal mediation model. The half-longitudinal indirect effect through PA was statistically supported. Specifically, T1 STP was prospectively associated with T2 PA, and T1 PA was prospectively associated with T2 perceived PTG. These findings extend previous work on STP by providing preliminary longitudinal evidence for PA as a potential affective pathway linking STP with perceived PTG. Copyright © 2026. title: From rejection sensitivity to phubbing: Self-compassion and self-uncertainty as serial mediators and a self-compassion writing intervention
abstract: Phubbing—attending to one's smartphone in another person's presence—is widespread, yet its dispositional and intrapersonal correlates remain poorly understood. Drawing on the cognitive-affective model of rejection sensitivity (RS) and a self-regulatory resource framework, we examined whether RS is associated with phubbing through two intrapersonal processes: reduced self-compassion and heightened self-uncertainty, operationalized as low self-concept clarity. Across three studies with Chinese university students, we combined a cross-sectional survey (Study 1, N = 1202), an experiment crossing measured high- versus low-RS groups with a social-context recall manipulation (Study 2, N = 197), and a four-week randomized self-compassion expressive-writing intervention with one-month follow-up (Study 3, N = 87 completers). In Study 1, RS was positively associated with phubbing, with statistical indirect associations via self-compassion, self-uncertainty, and their serial combination. Study 2 replicated these indirect associations and showed that social context moderated the indirect pathway through self-compassion: relative to a neutral condition, it was larger after rejection recall and smaller after acceptance recall. In Study 3, self-compassion writing, relative to neutral writing, produced larger gains in self-compassion and larger reductions in phubbing, sustained at follow-up. The findings identify intrapersonal responses to rejection as correlates of phubbing and provide preliminary evidence for a targeted writing intervention. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Deconstructing oversampling in software defect prediction: Algorithm constraints, trade-offs, and new baselines
abstract: Synthetic oversampling (OVS) is a common approach for addressing class imbalance in software defect prediction (SDP). While foundational SDP studies established rigorous evaluation standards, recent evaluations frequently rely on narrow experimental setups and restricted subsets of OVS techniques. Given the rapid introduction of OVS technique variants, it remains unclear whether the longstanding OVS baselines in SDP are still adequate or require revision. To address this gap, this study benchmarks 89 OVS techniques across eight learning algorithms and 25 imbalanced defect datasets, establishing an experimental space sufficient to determine algorithm-specific responses to these diverse OVS techniques. The evaluation pipeline incorporates Bayesian hyperparameter optimization, 20 independent repetitions, four standard performance metrics, and the Brunner’s test with Cliff’s d effect sizes. Results demonstrate that OVS improves the performance of tree and tree-based ensemble algorithms but offers limited or no gains for distance-based, kernel-based, and neural network algorithms. Furthermore, the conventional probability of detection and false alarm (pd−pf) Pareto analysis is augmented with the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) as a balanced recovery criterion. This augmentation identifies a candidate set of 52 learning algorithm × OVS technique configurations, organized into four operational zones based on explicit pf tolerance. The findings confirm that the current OVS baselines in SDP require revision, with standard SMOTE and widely adopted SDP-specific OVS techniques absent from the recommended configurations capable of maintaining operational false-alarm control. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Extreme weather and human capital formation: evidence from Qing China
abstract: Weather shocks can constrain educational investment and human capital formation. In Qing China, education spending rose and fell with weather-sensitive farm income. Using a two-century panel (1646–1904) covering 234 prefectures, we find that a drought occurring one year before the examinations and additional droughts within the past five years reduce jinshi (the highest degree in the imperial examination system) density by approximately 6 % and 2.6 % per period, respectively. Adaptive measures such as the introduction of sweet potatoes, savings from surplus years, and flexible pricing mechanisms prove effective in mitigating drought effects. For robustness, we proxy regional recording capacity with the word count of meteorological entries and augment the baseline with controls for social unrest and epidemic shocks, with results remaining stable. By bringing long-run historical evidence to bear, this study enriches the literature on how extreme weather affects human capital formation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Narrative identity awareness as a regulatory pathway between rumination and reflection and personality functioning
abstract: Personality functioning reflects individual differences in self and interpersonal capacities. This study examined whether narrative identity awareness mediates the associations of rumination and reflection with personality functioning. In a community sample of 424 adults, participants completed self-report measures of personality functioning, rumination, reflection, and narrative identity awareness. Cross-sectional mediation analyses (complete cases, N = 405) showed that rumination was associated with greater impairment, whereas reflection showed a more selective pattern. Narrative identity awareness was associated with lower impairment, and significant indirect associations were observed for both rumination and reflection in the simultaneous model; sensitivity analyses indicated that the indirect association was more robust for reflection than for rumination. Indirect associations were most evident for identity and self-direction, smaller for intimacy, and not statistically detectable for empathy. Component-level analyses indicated that coherence-related facets, particularly causal coherence, showed the most consistent indirect associations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Dynamic stability and controllability assessment of blood glucose regulatory system in human body using fractional derivatives
abstract: Nonlinear interactions between glucagon, insulin, and glucose are part of the complex process of regulating blood glucose levels. This work proposes a mathematical model of fractional order for the dynamics of diabetes based on the eight-dimensional Liu-Tang system. The Caputo fractional derivative is used to integrate the memory and inherited traits found in biological systems into the model. The existence and uniqueness of solutions are demonstrated using the Banach contraction principle, and the positivity and boundedness of the system are established. Furthermore, the concepts of controllability and observability are evaluated using Kalman-type criteria specific to fractional tempered systems. The first kind of Ulam-Hyers-Mittag-Leffler (U-H-M-L) stability is used to identify equilibrium points and evaluate their global stability. Chaos control techniques based on linear response theory are used to control erratic blood sugar swings. The dynamic behavior and effectiveness of the suggested model are demonstrated by numerical simulations for different fractional orders using Newton polynomial interpolation. The findings show that fractional modeling offers a more accurate and adaptable description of glucose-insulin control than traditional integer-order systems, providing important information for diabetes diagnosis and treatment. © 2026 International Association for Mathematics and Computers in Simulation (IMACS).

title: Archaeologies of Indigenous Foodways and Collective Capacities
abstract: Recent archaeological scholarship has embraced food security and food sovereignty frameworks to connect past foodways to present-day crises. However, these studies require critical examination of the colonial origins and ideological foundations of these frameworks, which emerged from industrialized western economic paradigms that do not align with Indigenous worldviews. Drawing on food studies scholarship, I argue that archaeologists must move beyond the uncritical adoption of food security and sovereignty frameworks to embrace culturally grounded paradigms developed by and for descendant communities. This paper advocates for reframing North American archaeological investigations of foodways through Indigenous philosopher Kyle Powys Whyte’s concept of collective capacities: webs of relationships among humans, non-human beings, and landscapes organized together to support responses to change and continuance. As a linking tool, collective capacities help archaeologists carry out the material and analytical work that Indigenous Food Sovereignty movements call for. An archaeology of collective capacities shifts our focus to understanding how food systems functioned as relational infrastructures of care, responsibility, and reciprocity that sustained communities across millennia. In this contribution I outline an archaeological framework identifying key material signatures of collective capacities. Applying this framework to the Pend Oreille Valley in northeastern Washington State, I demonstrate how paleoethnobotanical and archaeological data from the last 1500 years reveal Indigenous food systems were sustained through active management, coordinated labor, and intergenerational knowledge transmission across climatic and sociopolitical changes. I also consider how contemporary practices of reciprocity and relationality mirror the archaeological record of stability and stewardship. By centering culture-specific terminology and philosophies, an archaeology of collective capacities offers a methodological and theoretical approach that supports, rather than imposes frameworks upon, past societies while documenting the enduring systems that enabled communities to thrive across deep time. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Science takes more than belief: Epistemic and cognitive predictors of scientific reasoning
abstract: Belief in science and scientific reasoning represent related but conceptually distinct aspects of individuals' engagement with science: the former reflects an epistemic orientation toward science, whereas the latter concerns the ability to evaluate evidence, methods, and inferences. We examined actively open-minded thinking (AOT) and cognitive reflection (CRT) as theoretically complementary characteristics, representing an epistemic disposition and a reflective cognitive component, respectively. In a sample of 333 Italian participants, we examined the incremental associations of belief in science, AOT, and CRT with scientific reasoning and whether AOT and CRT showed similar or differentiated associations with belief in science and scientific reasoning. Belief in science was positively but weakly associated with scientific reasoning. AOT and CRT accounted for additional variance in scientific reasoning beyond sociodemographic characteristics and belief in science. AOT was associated with both belief in science and scientific reasoning, whereas CRT was associated with scientific reasoning but not significantly with belief in science. Overall, the findings indicate partly differentiated patterns of association across the two constructs. Given the cross-sectional design, no causal or temporal conclusions can be drawn. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A hybrid framework of LLM-based interaction generation and adaptive sampler for recommendation enhancement
abstract: Data augmentation (DA) is a critical technique for addressing data sparsity. Existing DA methods suffer from several limitations: extensive parameter tuning, dependency on specific types of data, and the tightly coupled DA network in the backbone recommendation model. Consequently, there remains a notable absence of universal data augmentation frameworks capable of adapting to diverse recommendation tasks and backbone models. To address these issues, we propose a hybrid framework to mitigate data sparsity via DA in a more flexible and universal paradigm. Notably, we disentangle the data augmentation process into two modules, data generation and data fusion. Firstly, we prompt LLMs to learn collaborative filtering information from raw user–item interaction data in a CSV format, generating new reliable interactions. Specifically, we devise clustering-based data grouping and multi-round shuffling strategies to enable LLMs to capture comprehensive collaborative filtering information through limited context. Secondly, we design an adaptive sampler to obtain personalized fused data for backbone recommendation models dynamically, making the fused data satisfy the different data demands of diverse downstream recommendation models. Experiments on various recommendation models across distinct datasets demonstrate that our framework can consistently improve vanilla recommendation models and facilitate existing DA methods. Compared with vanilla recommendation models, our framework achieves an average performance gain of 7.10%, 23.54%, and 24.55% on MovieLens-100k, Book-Crossing, and Toys and Games datasets, respectively. These results highlight the effectiveness of our proposed framework in mitigating data sparsity in recommender systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
