title: Why disaster experience does not always improve Preparedness: The role of disaster learning and heterogeneous effects
abstract: The frequency and severity of natural disasters and public emergencies have continued to increase worldwide. Household preparedness plays a vital role in disaster risk reduction, yet the effect of disaster-related experience on preparedness remains inconclusive. Using survey data from 5,862 residents in China, this study separately examines the associations of past disaster experience and disaster learning with household preparedness. Conventional regression models and a causal forest approach are used to estimate average associations and explore heterogeneous effects across individuals. The results show that disaster learning, rather than past disaster experience, is positively associated with preparedness behavior, highlighting the importance of capacity building. In addition, both past disaster experience and disaster learning exhibit heterogeneous effects across individuals. Feature importance analysis further indicates that social capital, emergency awareness, and community infrastructure are important influential factors associated with preparedness behavior. By introducing a causal forest approach to distinguish the differential effects of past disaster experience and disaster learning, this study provides a more nuanced understanding of household preparedness and offers useful insights for developing more targeted household disaster risk reduction strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Beyond financial literacy: The role of trust and neuropsychiatric symptoms in fraud vulnerability in dementia
abstract: Background: Fraud vulnerability is an increasing concern in aging populations, particularly as financial activities shift to digital environments. Individuals with neurocognitive disorders may be especially vulnerable, yet the relative contribution of financial literacy, behavioral functioning, neuropsychiatric symptoms, and interpersonal factors remains poorly understood. This study examined these determinants in individuals with neurocognitive disorders. Methods: 290 individuals with neurocognitive disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, Lewy body dementia, semantic dementia, and mild cognitive impairment, were enrolled. Financial vulnerability was assessed using the Financial Frailty Battery, a caregiver-administered instrument evaluating financial behaviors before and after disease onset. Neuropsychiatric symptoms were assessed with the Neuropsychiatric Inventory. Regression models examined predictors of fraud occurrence, fraud type, and fraud frequency. Results: Behavioral changes in everyday functioning and interpersonal trust emerged as the strongest correlates of fraud vulnerability. Behavioral tendencies (OR = 1.10, 95% CI [1.01, 1.19], p = .030) and trust (OR = 1.11, 95% CI [1.04, 1.18], p < .001) significantly predicted fraud victimization. Higher trust predicted non-digital (OR = 1.12, p = .005) and mixed fraud (OR = 1.19, p < .001), but not digital-only fraud (OR = 1.08, p = .101). Trust was also associated with repeated victimization (χ2(2) = 42.2, p < .001). Conclusions: Fraud vulnerability in neurocognitive disorders appears to be driven primarily by behavioral and interpersonal factors rather than financial knowledge alone. Preliminary evidence suggests partially different vulnerability profiles for digital and non-digital fraud, highlighting the need for prevention strategies tailored to different forms of financial exploitation. © 2026

title: The effect of social robot authority on epistemic vigilance in early childhood
abstract: Social robots are increasingly deployed as tutors and learning partners, yet their authority cues may discourage children from questioning or verifying information. We investigated whether robot authority influences Chinese children’s epistemic vigilance and which source of authority drives this effect. In Study 1 (N = 128, ages 4 and 6, Mage = 5.39 years, SD = 0.92, 66 girls and 62 boys), robots with high and low overall authority asserted that all aliens in a task had three eyes. Children’s verification behaviors were assessed in terms of the number of times they checked the information, the length of time they spent checking, and how much time passed between checks. Results showed that children engaged in significantly less verification in the high-authority condition, and 6-year-olds checked more often than 4-year-olds. Study 2 (N = 200, ages 4 and 6, Mage = 5.19 years, SD = 0.92, 97 girls and 103 boys) built on Study 1 by manipulating two sources of authority: role authority (teacher-like vs. peer-like) and cognitive authority (knowledgeable vs. unknowledgeable). The same task and outcome measures were used as in Study 1. The results showed that cognitive authority significantly decreased children’s verification behavior, but there was no significant effect of role authority or child age. Together, these findings suggest that authority cues can shape how much evidence children seek before accepting robot testimony, particularly when the robot is presented as knowledgeable. title: Multi-objective design and optimization of modular methanol production systems integrated with renewable hydrogen and direct air capture
abstract: A unified multi-objective optimization framework integrating renewable energy generation, electrolyzers, hydrogen-driven electrochemical CO2 capture systems (HECCS), methanol synthesis, and multiple storage technologies is developed to enable joint optimization of capacity configuration, operational scheduling, and flexibility allocation amid coupled electricity-hydrogen-carbon-methanol flows. The evolving roles of HECCS under supply-driven and demand-driven operating modes are evaluated. Under the supply-driven scenario, CO2 storage enables carbon-side buffering and partial temporal decoupling between carbon capture and methanol synthesis. At the minimum-total-annualized-cost Pareto solution, S2 with CO2 storage reduces the total storage requirement by approximately 41.3% relative to S1 without CO2 storage, while maintaining a nearly unchanged total annualized cost. This indicates that CO2 storage primarily restructures the inter-temporal regulation pathway rather than directly reducing system cost. Under the demand-driven scenario, HECCS achieves the lowest total annualized cost relative to conventional thermally regenerated direct air capture (DAC) technologies, demonstrating advantages in energy consumption and system integration. Further analysis shows that the fast response capability of HECCS does not necessarily lead to frequent dynamic operation. Under the economically optimal conditions, the system preferentially employs lower-cost storage to absorb renewable fluctuations and maintain stable operation of capital-intensive process units, whereas HECCS flexibility is activated mainly under storage-constrained conditions. The system-level process flexibility is thus governed by system constraints, economic trade-offs, and coordination among multiple flexibility resources rather than by intrinsic dynamic capability alone. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: CRAFMark: Contrastive-driven robust adaptive frequency-aware video watermarking against H.265/HEVC compression
abstract: Deep learning-based video watermarking has achieved notable progress in robustness and imperceptibility, yet it remains vulnerable to strong video compression such as H.265/HEVC. The main challenges arise from the non-differentiable operations in real encoders, including quantization, mode decision, and in-loop filtering, as well as the simulation-to-real domain gap between differentiable compression proxies and actual encoding pipelines. To address these issues, we propose CRAFMark, a Contrastive-driven Robust Adaptive Frequency-Aware Video Watermarking framework designed for robust watermarking under real-world H.265/HEVC compression. At the embedding stage, a Hierarchical Wavelet Frequency Modulation (HWFM) module guides watermark embedding toward compression-resilient frequency subbands, while a Motion-aware Temporal-Spatial Channel Attention (MTCA) module is introduced as a task-specific temporal-perceptual enhancement component to exploit motion information and spatiotemporal redundancy. To enable end-to-end optimization against real encoders, CRAFMark further incorporates a lightweight SAO-inspired Diff-SAO refinement module into the differentiable compression proxy to improve proxy fidelity. More importantly, CRAFMark introduces a Cross-domain Contrastive Compression Distillation (CCD) mechanism to align the latent features of proxy-decoded and real-decoded videos, thereby mitigating the proxy-to-real domain shift and encouraging compression-invariant decoding representations. Experiments on Kinetics-600 and UCF-101 demonstrate that CRAFMark achieves higher watermark extraction accuracy than existing methods under severe H.264/AVC and H.265/HEVC compression scenarios, while maintaining reasonable visual quality and temporal perceptual consistency. The proposed method also generalizes well across different video resolutions and frame lengths, indicating its applicability to intelligent and robust video watermarking for copyright protection in highly compressed distribution scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Critical assessment of the multifaceted impact of in-situ water removal on CO2 hydrogenation to methanol in membrane reactors
abstract: The thermodynamic limitation of CO2 hydrogenation to methanol remains a bottleneck for intensified e-methanol production. A kinetic–thermodynamic analysis assessed the potential of in-situ water removal for enhancing methanol synthesis and whether the theoretical benefits of selective dehydration can be preserved under realistic membrane-separation conditions. A catalytic packed-bed reactor (PBR) was adopted as a reference system, followed by an idealized point-wise water-removal benchmark and zeolite membrane-assisted reactor configurations with different transport characteristics. The reaction system was described using a one-dimensional pseudo-homogeneous plug-flow coupled with the Vanden Bussche–Froment kinetic model for methanol synthesis over a Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 catalyst. Membrane-assisted configurations combined reaction kinetics on the retentate side with permeance-based membrane transport. A highly water-selective NaA membrane and a steam-selective SOD-type membrane with appreciable reactant co-permeation were considered to evaluate the impact of non-ideal permeation and reactant losses. The reference PBR exhibited the trade-off between increasing CO2 conversion and enhanced CO formation at higher temperatures. The idealized benchmark showed that selective dehydration can relax equilibrium constraints and enhance methanol yield, particularly at high water-removal levels. However, comparison with realistic membrane-assisted systems revealed that these gains depend on the balance between water removal and reactant retention. The NaA membrane provided the best performance, achieving a methanol yield of 23.8% at 250 °C and ΔP = 30 bar, whereas SOD-based configurations suffered from H2 and CO2 co-permeation losses that partially offset benefits of water extraction. Overall, membrane-assisted methanol synthesis is advantageous only when water-removal capacity is balanced by sufficient reactant retention within the catalytic environment. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Probable alcohol use disorder in the U.S. Veteran population: Results from the 2025–2026 National Health and Resilience in Veterans study
abstract: Background Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a pervasive public health problem in the United States, and military veterans are at elevated risk. A prior wave of the National Health and Resilience in Veterans Study (NHRVS) estimated the prevalence of past-year probable AUD at 10.5 % in 2019–2020. Updated national surveillance data are needed given demographic shifts in the veteran population and evolving drinking patterns in the post-pandemic era. Methods Using data from the 2025–2026 NHRVS (N = 2,620), we estimated the weighted prevalence of probable AUD and compared it to that of the prior NHRVS wave. Multivariable analyses examined sociodemographic, military, trauma and mental health characteristics associated with probable AUD. Results The weighted prevalence of probable AUD in 2025–2026 was 12.1 %, compared with 10.5 % in 2019–2020 (difference, 1.6 percentage points; 95 % CI, −0.6 to 3.8), a difference that was not statistically significant. Independent correlates of probable AUD included younger age, unpartnered status, homelessness history, higher household income, and more adverse childhood experiences. When all lifetime psychiatric diagnoses were examined simultaneously, self-reported provider-diagnosed attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) remained significantly associated with probable AUD (OR = 2.40). Veterans with probable AUD also had significantly greater odds of past-year suicidal ideation (OR = 2.02; 31.6 % vs. 11.7 %) and lifetime suicide attempt (OR = 1.67; 11.8 % vs. 4.0 %). Conclusions The prevalence of probable AUD among U.S. veterans remains elevated and is characterized by early adversity, co-occurring psychiatric conditions, and elevated suicide risk. Enhanced screening for social determinants of health and psychiatric concerns, including routine ADHD assessment in AUD treatment settings, alongside targeted outreach and integrated approaches are essential to address this complex and important problem. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Do Hopfield networks dream of stored patterns? A statistical–mechanical theory of dreaming in multidirectional associative memories
abstract: We introduce the Dreaming L-directional Associative Memory (DLAM), a multi-layer Hebbian architecture in which off-line dreaming and supervised heteroassociative coupling coexist within a single cost function, placing our approach within the framework of energy-based models (EBMs). The replica-symmetric free energy, derived via the Guerra interpolation scheme, yields self-consistency equations governing the order parameters across the control-parameter space. The effective local field decomposes into signal, intra-layer dreaming noise, and inter-layer noise. Dreaming improves retrieval by differentially attenuating high-eigenvalue interference modes of the empirical correlation matrix, suppressing inter-pattern crosstalk while preserving the signal. Dreaming and inter-layer coupling prove synergistic, opening retrieval regions unreachable by either mechanism alone, as confirmed by Monte Carlo simulations for (Formula presented). Their interplay is most pronounced on pattern disentanglement: given a mixture state as input, the network splits the constituent patterns one-per-layer, recovering each modality-specific pattern from a common cue that simultaneously blends noisy evidence from all sensory channels. Phase diagrams are planar projections of the hyperspace (α, T, ρ, t)—where α is the storage load, T the fast-noise temperature, ρ the dataset entropy, and t the sleeping time. In the (ρ, t)-plane, the diagrams reveal a data–computation trade-off: off-line consolidation substitutes for additional training data, extending to heteroassociative architectures a phenomenon previously established for autoassociative networks. Enriching the standard Hopfield model with heteroassociativity and dreaming gives rise to EBMs capable of complex tasks beyond classical pattern recognition, contributing to a modern theory of neural information processing. title: Hybrid scheduling for serverless function workflows in edge computing system
abstract: Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) computing paradigm enables fine-grained resource scheduling through decomposing complex workflows into a series of functions deployed in edge computing systems by a containerized manner. The temporal constraints of these workflows are required to be satisfied, where delay-sensitive and delay-tolerant workflows are scheduled through a priority-aware mechanism. We focus on resource-constrained edge nodes which are characterized by limited energy supply and computing capability. It is challenging to achieve the optimal trade-off between response delay and energy consumption through optimally deployed functions on edge nodes for scheduling unpredictable incoming workflows. This issue is formulated as an online deadline-aware function deployment model in terms of the Lyapunov optimization technique with efficient stability queues. A Markov decision process is formulated by continuously updating system states, selecting scheduling actions, and evaluating corresponding rewards. We develop a Deep Q-Learning based Workflow Scheduling (denoted as DQLWS) technique to achieve adaptive hybrid workflow scheduling, while considering long-term response delay and energy efficiency. Extensive experiments are conducted in terms of different proportions between delay-sensitive and delay-tolerant workflows, delay-energy weighting settings, scalability of edge node quantity and long-term scheduling performance. Evaluation results show that our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches in multiple comparison dimensions, including response delay, energy consumption, temporal violation rate, and algorithm stability, and thus achieves near-optimal scheduling solutions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: RAGM-track: Typed graph memory for reliability-conditioned identity reasoning in RGB-T multi-object tracking
abstract: Identity errors in RGB–thermal MOT can persist beyond the degraded frame because unreliable associations committed to memory distort later matching and identity recovery. Existing trackers encode history as homogeneous queues, prototypes, or track queries, limiting control over evidence retrieval and updating. We propose Reliability-Aware Graph Memory Tracking (RAGM-Track), which represents each identity as a persistent typed graph of identity, appearance, motion, reliability, occlusion, and hard-negative evidence. Reliability-derived degradation adapts the candidate-retrieval budget, while modality reliability and cross-modal conflict modulate association scores and protect memory writing, limiting error propagation and supporting re-entry recovery. On VT-MOT, RAGM-Track achieves 41.37 HOTA, 43.19 DetA, 42.76 IDF1, 50.83 MOTA, and 1124 identity switches. Among published results reproduced in our benchmark comparison, it reports the highest HOTA, DetA, and MOTA and the lowest identity-switch count, while its cross-pipeline IDF1 remains below PFTrack (47.25) and ACNTrack (48.04). Memory-slot-controlled ablations support the benefits of typed organization. On UniRTL-MOT, RAGM-Track improves AssA and IDF1 over untyped attention memory by 1.42 and 1.67 points with shared MCTrack detections, and 3.28 and 2.58 points with oracle boxes. These results show that governing memory evolution complements the interpretation of current observations in robust multimodal tracking. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Holding the periphery: Women, territorial holding labour, and the post-extractive labour-sending economy
abstract: Post-extractive scholarship has focused predominantly on mines, mining towns and industrial transition, with limited attention to labour-sending territories historically incorporated into extraction through labour circulation and social reproduction. Drawing on qualitative interviews with 21 participants engaged in informal livelihood activity in Viljoenskroon, South Africa, this paper focuses analytically on nine women to examine how such territories continue to function after extractive employment contracts. The findings identify seven interlocking mechanisms through which women sustain households, livelihoods and community continuity under conditions of constrained accumulation, weakened institutional incorporation and infrastructural decline. The paper conceptualises the territorial condition produced through these relations as the extractive periphery and the feminised work through which its continuity is maintained as territorial holding labour. It argues that as extractive employment contracts, reproductive labour that historically subsidised extraction through the reproduction of labour increasingly subsidises its territorial aftermath through the reproduction of continuity. This extends post-extractive analysis beyond sites of production and social reproduction analysis beyond households and labour power to the reproduction of territorial continuity. The findings also challenge continuity as evidence of successful transition: apparent resilience may conceal the transfer of unresolved adjustment costs into women’s income, time and labour. Transition policy must therefore account for labour-sending territories and for who bears the costs through which their continuity is sustained. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Automated analysis of prosodic and conversational speech markers for autism spectrum disorder screening and severity estimation
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is associated with clinically meaningful differences in speech, prosody, and reciprocal communication; however, these markers are difficult to quantify consistently during routine screening. This study investigates whether automatically extracted acoustic, prosodic, and conversational speech markers can support objective ASD screening and severity estimation. We present SpectrumNet, a speech-marker modeling framework designed to analyze communication-relevant features rather than replacing clinical diagnosis. The framework combines a multi-scale acoustic encoder, a prosody encoder, and a conversational-dynamics encoder to represent voice quality, rhythm, intonation, speech rate, pause behavior, and turn-taking patterns. A cross-domain feature disentanglement module separates ASD-relevant communication markers from speaker identity and emotional variation, while a hierarchical attention mechanism identifies patterns across short-, medium-, and longer-range temporal scales. The model was evaluated using five publicly available datasets, with ASDSpeech serving as the primary clinical benchmark and ADOS-2 scores used for severity estimation. On ASDSpeech, SpectrumNet achieved 93.10% accuracy, 92.80% F1-score, and 95.50% AUC for ASD versus typically developing classification. Severity estimates were strongly associated with ADOS-2 scores, including a Pearson correlation of 0.891 for the total score. Cross-dataset testing on AV-ASD showed 78.43% zero-shot accuracy and 85.20% accuracy after minimal fine-tuning, suggesting partial generalizability across recording settings. These findings support the potential value of speech-based computational markers as an adjunctive screening aid for communication-disorder assessment, while highlighting the need for larger, clinically diverse, and prospectively validated cohorts before diagnostic deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Topology-aware dynamic co-evolution for robust graph learning
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have achieved remarkable success in learning from graph-structured data. However, recent studies have revealed their vulnerability to adversarial attacks, where imperceptible perturbations to the graph structure can easily mislead predictions. Existing defense methods predominantly rely on global heuristic strategies, which often lead to over-smoothing in deep architectures and fail to capture localized, fine-grained structural anomalies. In this paper, we propose Topology-Aware Dynamic Co-evolution (TADC), a novel framework that reformulates graph defense as a closed-loop optimization process. Unlike static purification paradigms, TADC introduces a closed-loop dynamic co-evolution framework, in which graph topology and model parameters are jointly optimized through validation-guided meta-gradients, enabling continuous and adaptive structural refinement during training. To further ensure the reliability of topology updates, we identify the topology-agnostic limitation of conventional meta-gradients and propose a topology-aware gradient calibration mechanism, which incorporates structural priors to guide gradient directions toward more plausible and semantically consistent graph modifications. Concretely, TADC first localizes vulnerable nodes via a structural-semantic consistency probe and constructs an initialized graph through topology-aware refinement. It then performs structure decoupling to disentangle reliable and potentially adversarial edges into distinct channels. Building upon this decomposition, a fully differentiable attention-based architecture DeepGCN enables end-to-end optimization of the co-evolution process. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that TADC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various attack settings, with particularly pronounced advantages under strong adversarial perturbations and high perturbation rates. title: Leveraging Digital Twins for Bridge Maintenance Prioritization following Coastal Flood Events
abstract: Bridges are critical to the US transportation network and are essential components of our infrastructure systems. Coastal floods can disrupt these structures, isolating communities and highlighting the urgent need for effective maintenance and prioritization strategies. This study introduces a digital twin framework that evaluates the impacts of coastal floods on bridge substructures by integrating multisource data and employing spatial algorithms like inverse distance weighting and k-d tree methods to model flood severity. Using a generative adversarial network (GAN) with focal loss, the framework simulates preflood and postflood scenarios, generating synthetic data sets that reflect realistic damage patterns and evolving maintenance priorities. The GAN-enhanced model improved F1 scores (the harmonic mean of precision and recall, providing a balance between the two metrics), particularly for Condition 4 (bridges with advanced section loss, deterioration, spalling, or scour), where the score increased from 0.63 to 0.87 preflood and from 0.63 to 0.88 postflood, effectively addressing class imbalances. It also enhanced macro and weighted average F1 scores, demonstrating robust predictive capabilities. Confusion matrices showed increased identification of bridges in Conditions 4 and 5, consistent with the model's emphasis on vulnerable infrastructure. The study's findings reveal shifts in maintenance priorities when flood severity is incorporated, emphasizing bridges with higher susceptibility to combined flooding and socioeconomic impacts. While the framework primarily focused on physical infrastructure impacts, it also highlighted potential disparities in resource allocation, suggesting the need for further research into equitable distribution strategies. The digital twin provides actionable insights for local and federal agencies, offering a valuable tool for managing and prioritizing infrastructure maintenance in response to extreme weather events while laying the groundwork for more inclusive resource planning. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Graft: Navigable graphs grown on spatial-approximation rootstock
abstract: The best navigable graphs for approximate nearest-neighbor search are built serially: each inserted point searches the partially built graph, and its neighbors are selected from what that search visits — a serial dependency chain in which concurrent insertions contend for shared state and two builds of the same data differ. Graft keeps the search step and removes the mutation: the candidate-producing search needs only some navigable graph, and a much cheaper one suffices. Construction builds a rootstock — a forest of T independently seeded spatial-approximation trees, unioned into a fixed, redundant scaffold — then harvests : every point, in parallel, beam-searches the frozen scaffold with itself as the query, and the expanded vertices are occlusion-pruned into its adjacency list. Both phases are embarrassingly parallel, and the graph is bitwise identical at any thread count. A per-point stopping rule ( patience ) preserves graph quality across a 10× increase in n where a fixed search budget tuned at the smaller scale does not. The build costs 0.5%–5% of n distance computations per point; in paired repeated-build experiments at 106 points its wall-clock time is at parity with tuned Vamana on SIFT, 1.3–3.2× slower on GloVe, and 4–17× slower than the GEMM-based PiPNN. The return is measured in distance evaluations, the hardware-independent cost: at recall 0.95–0.97, Graft is within 5% of Vamana on SIFT, GloVe, and a 1024-dimensional Wikipedia benchmark (1.12× on GIST, 1.3× on Fashion, 14%–20% behind on GloVe’s 0.985–0.99 tail); 20%–22% ahead of PiPNN on GloVe; 9%–39% ahead of HNSW at 107–108 points. A degree-matched random substrate needs 4.7× more distances per query: the scaffold’s routability is necessary. The construction consumes only distance comparisons and applies unchanged to any metric. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Deep spectral unmixing unfolding network for multispectral and hyperspectral image fusion
abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) comprise tens to hundreds of contiguous narrow spectral bands, imposing substantial computational demands on HSI processing. However, the strong similarity between adjacent bands creates considerable redundancy, whose reduction is essential for computationally efficient processing. We propose a multispectral and hyperspectral image fusion (MHIF) framework, termed the Deep Spectral Unmixing Unfolding (DSUU) network, from a matrix factorization perspective. DSUU exploits sparsity priors through a spectral unmixing model to reduce information redundancy. It then applies proximal gradient optimization and unfolds its iterations into a deep network, improving the efficiency of conventional model-driven optimization. The proximal operators for endmembers and abundances use 1D- and 2D-DWT-based blocks to mitigate errors arising from inaccurate initialization. To capture spatial-spectral correlations overlooked by matrix factorization, we introduce a Spatial-Spectral Refinement Block (SSRB) comprising a multiscale spatial module and a spectral attention module. Experiments on three benchmark datasets show that DSUU achieves a more favorable trade-off between fusion quality and computational complexity than state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. By integrating data-driven learning with model-driven optimization, DSUU retains an interpretable algorithmic structure while achieving efficient and high-quality fusion. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Dynamic risk assessment and emergency response effectiveness analysis for hazardous chemicals explosion based on dynamic Bayesian network and cloud model
abstract: Hazardous chemical explosion accidents are characterized by multifactor coupling, time-dependent risk accumulation, and cascading consequence escalation. However, existing studies provide limited quantitative analysis of dynamic accident-risk evolution and the risk-reduction effectiveness of emergency safety barriers. To address these limitations, this study proposes a dynamic risk-assessment and emergency-response effectiveness analysis method for hazardous chemical explosions by integrating a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) with a cloud model (CM). First, a DBN incorporating explosion-related risk events, emergency safety barriers, and accident consequences is constructed based on accident investigation reports, accident evolution mechanisms, and expert knowledge. Second, the CM and an expert confidence index are used to quantify linguistic expert judgments and convert them into the prior and conditional probabilities required by the BN. Finally, Bayesian inference, sensitivity analysis, and safety-barrier scenario simulation are performed to identify the critical causal factors and quantify the risk-reduction effects of emergency measures. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can dynamically predict accident risk, diagnose critical contributing factors, and quantitatively evaluate the effectiveness of emergency safety barriers. It therefore provides quantitative decision support for hazardous chemical safety management and emergency-resource allocation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Landscapes of extraction: Youth, coal and contested livelihoods in Tinsukia, Assam
abstract: The article explores the diverse and intersecting forms through which youth encounter, experience, and respond to coal mining in Tinsukia, Assam’s easternmost resource-rich district. Drawing on qualitative ethnographic fieldwork in the Ledo and Margherita coalfields, it examines how extractive economies reshape youth livelihoods, aspirations and vulnerabilities in a landscape marked by environmental devastation, informalization of labour, and uneven development The article focuses on three connected processes: the erosion of traditional livelihoods and ecological relations; entry into precarious and informal mining-related work; and the emergence of critique and resistance. Rather than treating youth as a homogeneous category, the article analyzes how their positions are not fixed but fluid. It shows how their positions differ according to access to land, labour, networks, and political resources, while also shifting between economic dependence, negotiation, and opposition. The article contributes to political ecology and extractive-frontier scholarship by foregrounding youth perspectives from a Northeast Indian coal belt and by showing how development is experienced simultaneously as livelihood opportunity and socio-environmental harm. title: Coupled design of a bamboo-shaped cathode flow field and hybrid-porosity gas diffusion layer for enhanced performance and multiphysics transport in open-cathode PEMFCs
abstract: The bamboo-shaped cathode flow field can enhance heat-mass transfer and improve the performance of open-cathode proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). However, its further engineering application faces two prominent challenges: 1) the effects of the key design parameters on cell performance and multiphysics transport remain unclear; 2) geometry-induced local convection enhancement may aggravate the inherent spatial nonuniformity of the physical fields within the porous electrode assembly and increase the risk of local degradation. To address these challenges, this study first studies the impacts of two key design parameters, the number of bamboo-joint units ( N ) and bamboo-joint indentation depth ( W ), on PEMFC performance and the associated heat and mass transfer in porous electrodes. Furthermore, the flow field is coupled with a hybrid-porosity GDL to improve physical field uniformity while retaining enhanced transport. The results show that moderate increases in N and W strengthen the periodic contraction–expansion effect of reactants within the bamboo-shaped configuration, thereby enhancing shear disturbance and lateral mixing. This promotes faster renewal of the thermal and concentration boundary layers in the flow field and porous electrode, thereby increasing the net water and oxygen transport fluxes and improving heat dissipation. Adjusting N and W contributes to superior open-cathode PEMFC performance by up to 8.10 % and 18.85 %, respectively. Increasing N and W also increases the ideal cathode air-supply power due to the relatively larger pressure drop under otherwise identical operating conditions, indicating a greater relative air-supply penalty. Accordingly, the flow field design requires a trade-off among performance improvement, ideal air-supply penalty, and the uniformity of key physical fields within the MEA. Guided by these mechanistic insights, a coupled design is developed by integrating the bamboo-shaped flow field with a hybrid-porosity gas diffusion layer (GDL). This novel design retains the transport and performance advantages of the bamboo-shaped flow field while further alleviating the inherent limitation of the non-uniform distribution of key physical fields within the porous electrode. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Coupled convection–radiation heat transfer and optimization in microscale fin structures
abstract: With the increasing power density of electronic devices, effective thermal management is essential for maintaining performance and reliability. Although air-cooled heat sinks have been extensively investigated, studies have primarily focused on structural optimization and convective heat transfer, while the contribution of surface radiation has received comparatively limited attention in microscale thermal management. This study investigates a backside-integrated air-cooled heat sink, with particular emphasis on the coupled effects of forced convection and surface radiation at the microscale. Comparative analysis shows that the parallel plate fin structure provides the best heat dissipation performance, while fin optimization reveals a trade-off between heat transfer enhancement and flow resistance. Furthermore, increasing the inlet velocity effectively enhances convective heat transfer and reduces the chip temperature, but the cooling benefit gradually diminishes beyond approximately 1.2 m/s, whereas flow-related energy consumption continues to increase. Meanwhile, radiative heat transfer is strongly influenced by flow conditions and input power, with surface emissivity playing an increasingly important role under low velocity and high input power conditions. At an inlet velocity of 0.2 m/s, increasing the emissivity from 0.05 to 0.95 reduces the maximum chip temperature by approximately 10.8 °C at 0.1 W and 33.3 °C at 0.3 W. At ε = 0.95 and v = 0.2 m/s, the radiative contribution reaches 32.0%, 34.3%, and 36.4% at input powers of 0.1 W, 0.2 W and 0.3 W, respectively. These results demonstrate that appropriate matching of inlet velocity and surface emissivity can effectively regulate heat dissipation while reducing reliance on excessive airflow. The findings provide a practical basis for the design and optimization of integrated thermal management systems for high power density electronic devices. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

title: A density-aware and overlap-driven framework for task allocation in distributed spatial data processing environments
abstract: The increasing volume of data generated by distributed sensing and Internet of Things (IoT) devices and applications has intensified the need for efficient data and task management in edge and distributed environments. A key challenge in such systems is determining how to allocate tasks that require the processing of multidimensional data across distributed nodes while preserving data locality and limiting communication overhead. In this paper, we propose a density-aware and overlap-driven framework for task allocation in distributed data-processing environments. Tasks and node data regions are represented as multidimensional hyper-rectangles, while each node maintains information about its local data density. The proposed framework employs a scenario-based allocation mechanism based on strict spatial containment, tolerance-based containment, and external execution. Depending on the spatial relationship between a task and the available data regions, as well as the corresponding density conditions, the task can be executed locally, supported through neighboring-node collaboration, offloaded to another node, or reported as unserved when no suitable execution node is available. Candidate nodes for collaboration and offloading are selected using a scoring mechanism that considers spatial overlap and communication latency. To improve adaptability under heterogeneous data distributions, the framework additionally supports adaptive density thresholds and bounded tolerance expansion according to the observed node densities. The proposed approach is evaluated using three heterogeneous real-world datasets: OpenStreetMap (OSM) data from Greece, NYC Yellow Taxi data, and data derived from the National Ambulatory Medical Care Survey (NAMCS). The evaluation examines allocation behavior, execution success, communication requirements, decision overhead, scalability, parameter sensitivity, and deadline-aware admission. The results demonstrate accurate allocation decisions with low decision overhead while highlighting the trade-offs among local execution, neighbor collaboration, and external offloading. The proposed framework provides an interpretable and adaptive approach to multidimensional task allocation and offers a practical basis for distributed data processing in edge and IoT environments. title: Bridging single-species models to ecosystem-based maximum sustainable yield for environmental sustainability in marine fisheries
abstract: Maximum sustainable yield remains a central biological reference concept in fisheries management. Its reliability is shaped by model assumptions, uncertainty, ecological interactions, and environmental change. The study objectives were to reconstruct the mathematical progression of maximum sustainable yield, from single-species deterministic models to ecosystem-based, multispecies formulations. The critical narrative review synthesizes the paradigm shift in ecological modeling, tracing its trajectory from equilibrium-based single-species frameworks to holistic, ecosystem-aware formulations. Classical production models are compared with age-structured, stock-recruitment, bioeconomic, precautionary, and multispecies approaches. The assumptions, data needs, uncertainty, and management implications are evaluated. Eight fisheries cases are used to illustrate contrasts in data availability, assessment methods, harvest rules, ecosystem awareness, and shared-stock governance. These cases are treated as illustrative examples rather than a representative validation sample. Evidence shows that trophic interactions can alter species-specific and system-level reference points. The direction of change depends on food-web structure, selectivity, interaction strength, environmental productivity, and management objectives. Environmental variation can also affect growth, recruitment, natural mortality, habitat capacity, and species interactions. Accordingly, biological reference points require adaptive updating when stock productivity exhibits nonstationarity, precluding their interpretation as rigid constants amidst shifting environmental conditions. Economic objectives, social needs, and conservation goals must also be distinguished from biological yield objectives. A five-dimension readiness framework is proposed as a preliminary hypothesis-generating heuristic. Alternative weighting schemes indicate that some borderline classifications are sensitive to assumptions. Independent validation and inter-rater testing are therefore required before operational use. While substantial data constraints persist across multiple Indonesian fisheries, these limitations must not be regarded as the sole impediment to comprehensive management. Governance, enforcement, fleet structure, socioeconomic incentives, habitat condition, and climate variability can independently affect performance. Greater use of adaptive monitoring, precautionary harvest rules, uncertainty analysis, and ecosystem indicators is therefore recommended. Multispecies assessment should be prioritized where trophic or technical interactions materially influence stock dynamics. Maximum sustainable yield is best retained as an analytical reference point rather than a literal catch target. Environmentally sustainable application requires precautionary, adaptive, and ecosystem-based governance frameworks dynamically aligned with local empirical data quality, ecological conditions, and institutional capabilities. title: Soft-Hard interfacial engineering for optimized mechanical properties of magnesium alloy/polylactic acid films
abstract: The clinical translation of poly (lactic acid) (PLA)-based bioresorbable scaffolds (BRS) is severely hindered by a strength-thickness trade-off and the inevitable physical aging of the matrix. To improve the overall mechanical properties of the PLA matrix, we fabricated magnesium (Mg) alloy/PLA composite structural films via magnetron sputtering. The results demonstrate that, compared with the pristine matrix, the elastic modulus and yield strength of the unaged PLA-based composite films increased by 306% and 363%, respectively. For composite films based on aged PLA, the modulus and strength still increased by 21.2% and 20.1%, respectively, while maintaining favorable ductility. By coupling a time-dependent physical elasto-viscoplastic constitutive model with a finite element cohesive zone model, this study reveals an aging-induced anomalous mechanical transition mechanism driven synergistically by matrix structural relaxation and interfacial mechanical evolution. It is found that in the unaged state, the sputtering energy dissipates deeply into the PLA matrix with high free volume, forming a strongly constrained interfacial transition zone (ITZ) and a robustly anchored interface, triggering premature brittle fracture of the material. In the intermediate aging stage, the intrinsic densification of the matrix shrinks the ITZ and weakens the interfacial bonding strength. This interfacial debonding effect relieves the geometric constraints imposed by the metal layer, thereby releasing the intrinsic ductility of the matrix, enabling the composite structural films to avert brittle failure while simultaneously enhancing their modulus and strength. Furthermore, the quantitative analysis framework for multi-mechanism synergy established herein elucidates the intrinsic coupling correlations among the aforementioned multi-physical mechanisms, which will facilitate the design and development of high-performance biodegradable scaffolds based on polymer/metal composites. title: Singularity avoidance control of independently steerable and driven mobile robots
abstract: This paper develops a coordinated singularity avoidance control framework for independently steerable and driven mobile robots by jointly regulating steering geometry and control allocation. A unified model is established by combining the common instantaneous-center-of-rotation consistency constraint with planar rigid-body dynamics, thereby relating steering configuration, chassis motion, and wheel actuation within a common formulation. In the steering layer, a manipulability-gradient correction is combined with a boundary-localized safeguarding mechanism. Positive invariance of a prescribed safe steering set is established under explicit initialization and guard-region regularity conditions, providing a sufficient condition for operational singularity avoidance under the nominal steering dynamics. In the chassis layer, an adaptive disturbance-compensating controller is integrated with a manipulability-dependent damped least-squares allocator. The resulting allocation mismatch is retained in the closed-loop dynamics, and uniform ultimate boundedness of the chassis tracking errors is established under a bounded total disturbance. Numerical studies on representative four-wheel and six-wheel configurations show that the proposed method preserves a positive manipulability margin and substantially limits singularity-induced actuator amplification while allowing a finite transient deviation from nominal geometric consistency. Under actuator, steering-rate, sensing, and steering-lag nonidealities, the four-wheel configuration maintains a minimum scaled manipulability of 0.1705 with a peak commanded wheel torque of 3.818 Nm, while the six-wheel configuration maintains a minimum value of 0.6326 with a peak commanded torque of 4.339 Nm. A gain-sensitivity study further quantifies the trade-off between manipulability preservation and geometric consistency. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Network-mediated information–behaviour coupling drives collective decision-making in crowd evacuation
abstract: Emergency evacuation in real buildings is governed not only by physical interactions but also by the propagation of warnings, misinformation, and corrective cues through social and local communication channels. Cellular automaton (CA) models are widely used in crowd-evacuation modelling because their discrete transition rules enable computationally efficient simulation and large stochastic ensembles. Conventional CA formulations nevertheless often represent pedestrians as geometry-driven agents, leaving information transmission and route revision exogenous; standalone information-propagation models describe communication pathways but omit embodied route adaptation in space. Here, we develop a network-mediated cellular automaton framework to investigate information–behaviour coupling in crowd evacuation. The model integrates a floor-field CA with a dynamic small-world social network and a questionnaire-informed random utility formulation for local information acceptance, thereby coupling crowd motion, social topology, and heterogeneous behavioural response within one simulation framework. Simulations show that information–behaviour coupling accelerates route correction, weakens congestion near the failed exit, and improves both individual and collective evacuation performance relative to a geometry-driven CA. Systematic analyses further uncover the mechanisms underlying these improvements. Moderate network rewiring accelerates the spread of collective awareness via long-range shortcuts, while increasing local interaction range enhances performance up to a saturation threshold. Notably, increasing the average social degree produces an onset-and-plateau pattern in which fragmented local responses gradually become coordinated global egress. Two-parameter explorations further show that evacuation performance emerges from compensatory interactions among network topology, transmission fidelity, local interaction scale, and initial information composition, rather than from any single parameter in isolation. These findings establish information–behaviour coupling as a fundamental mechanism governing collective evacuation under uncertainty and provide a theoretical foundation for communication-aware evacuation design and management. More broadly, this work highlights the critical role of information-driven interactions in shaping collective dynamics in complex adaptive systems. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Maximizing mutual information in multi-view representation learning for next POI prediction
abstract: Next point-of-interest (POI) prediction is a fundamental task in spatiotemporal data mining, aiming to facilitate personalized location-based services through modeling individual mobility trajectories. Despite recent advances in deep neural networks for capturing human mobility patterns from both short- and long-term trajectories, accurate POI prediction remains challenging due to the fragility of short-term intent representations and user preference drift. These challenges arise from intent inconsistency between stable long-term behavioral patterns and transient short-term contingencies, as well as the inherent stochasticity induced by sparse, noisy, and exploratory human mobility trajectories, ultimately causing biased or unstable future intention predictions. In this study, we propose MVMI, a Multi-View representation learning framework based on Mutual Information for next POI prediction. To improve the robustness of short-term intent representations, MVMI decomposes short-term trajectories into instantaneous and context-dependent intents and employs a Gaussian perturbation–based multi-view augmentation strategy to enhance the robustness of short-term intent representations against trajectory stochasticity. To address user preference drift, MVMI further introduces a mutual information (MI) constraint that aligns integrated user preferences with the ground-truth future intentions, where a dual-task learning paradigm is employed to enforce hierarchical spatial constraints at both the POI and region levels. Finally, experiments on four real-world datasets demonstrate that MVMI significantly outperforms representative baselines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Toward ammonia-to-NOx ratio control in an ammonia/diesel dual direct-injection engine under low-load conditions
abstract: An excessive ammonia-to-NOx ratio (ANR) under low-load operation poses a challenge to the efficient operation of aftertreatment systems in ammonia-fueled engines. In this study, experiments were conducted on a single-cylinder ammonia/diesel dual direct-injection (DDI) engine to investigate the effects of ammonia substitution ratio (ASR), intake pressure, dual-fuel injection pressure, and injection timing (−28 to −12°CA ATDC) on NH3 emissions, NOx emissions, and the ANR under a low-load condition of 4 bar indicated mean effective pressure (IMEP). The results show that increasing ASR is the dominant factor driving the increase in the ANR. When the ASR was maintained below 60%, coordinated optimization of intake pressure, dual-fuel injection pressure, and injection timing under the late diesel injection strategy reduced the ANR to 1.1–1.25 while maintaining a high indicated thermal efficiency (ITE), thereby reducing the ANR to a level compatible with the efficient operating window of the aftertreatment system, and engine-out N2O emissions showed no evident deterioration. Furthermore, by substantially advancing diesel injection timing (−340 to −220°CA ATDC) to establish a thermally favorable in-cylinder environment before ammonia combustion, the ANR could be further reduced to below 1.0. However, a trade-off between ASR and ITE together with a marked increase in engine-out N2O emissions was observed under this strategy. The study systematically elucidates the regulation characteristics of key combustion control parameters on the ANR under low-load conditions and proposes practical ANR control strategies for ammonia/diesel DDI engines. The findings provide new insights into the optimization of ammonia utilization and energy conversion efficiency, and offer useful guidance for in-cylinder combustion control with aftertreatment requirements in ammonia-fueled engines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Hierarchical diagnosis and operating-condition tracing of energy-efficiency abnormalities in crude oil distillation units
abstract: Dynamic energy-efficiency abnormalities in crude oil distillation unit (CDU) are difficult to diagnose because process variables are strongly coupled and abnormal operating conditions may affect multiple process sections. This study develops a hierarchical diagnostic framework that progressively narrows the diagnostic scope from process-level abnormality monitoring to process-section localization and finally to operating-condition tracing. First, slow feature analysis (SFA) is employed to monitor the dynamic energy-efficiency state and detect deviations from normal operation. A convolutional neural network (CNN) is then used for process-section classification to narrow the diagnostic scope to a specific process section. Subsequently, a convolutionally encoded heat-map strategy based on sliding-window feature extraction is applied to characterize temporal deviations among variables within the localized section and trace the associated abnormal operating condition. Eight abnormal operating conditions are simulated for the CDU, with 2400 samples generated for each condition at a 2-min sampling interval. Using 21 selected process variables, the CNN achieves average precision, recall, and F1 scores of 99.84 %, 99.90 %, and 99.87 %, respectively, under the reported experimental setting. SFA achieves an average recall of 99.54 %, a false-positive rate of 0.39 %, and a fault detection delay of 7 min, compared with 98.79 %, 2.26 %, and 15.25 min for PCA. Two industrial operating cases are further analyzed to examine the practical applicability of the proposed diagnostic workflow. The results demonstrate the potential of the framework for hierarchical energy-efficiency abnormality detection and operating-condition tracing in CDU processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Mitochondrial-derived peptides in female reproduction: Emerging regulators of oocyte competence and novel therapeutic opportunities for infertility
abstract: Female infertility affects approximately 17.5% of adults worldwide. Mitochondria are central to oocyte developmental competence, and a novel class of mitochondrial genome-encoded peptides, mitochondrial-derived peptides(MDPs) comprising MOTS-c, Humanin and small Humanin-like peptide2(SHLP2), regulates cellular metabolism, oxidative stress and apoptosis. This hypothesis-driven perspective aims to:(i) synthesize indirect evidence to construct a mechanistic framework for MDP involvement in oocyte physiology and female infertility;(ii) propose prioritized research questions; and(iii) delineate translational paths toward MDP-based biomarkers and therapeutics in assisted reproductive technology(ART). PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched up to May 2025 using terms related to MDPs, oocytes, follicular fluid, ovarian aging and IVF. Bibliographies were hand-searched. The search yielded 312 records, of which 87 were retained. The three principal MDPs decline with age in humans, mirroring the age-related deterioration of oocyte quality. The reduced MOTS-c in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS; formerly polycystic ovary syndrome, PCOS) (a 56% reduction in serum concentration versus controls, P < 0.001), provides preliminary evidence, albeit unreplicated and without ovarian sampling. Mechanistically, MDPs activate AMPK(MOTS-c), sequester pro-apoptotic Bax(Humanin), and reduce mitochondrial ROS while enhancing electron transport chain activity(SHLP2). Humanin is already known to be present in human follicular fluid and to associate with ovarian reserve and PMOS-related insulin resistance; we propose that this extends to MOTS-c and SHLP2, that composite MDP levels correlate with oocyte-specific quality parameters, and that a composite biomarker panel could improve IVF outcome prediction beyond AMH alone. MDPs(MOTS-c,Humanin,SHLP2) decline with age, regulate AMPK, suppress oxidative stress and inhibit apoptosis; processes that drive oocyte quality decline. Reduced MOTS-c in PMOS provides an initial, unreplicated clinical link. Convergent biology positions MDPs as promising candidates to improve IVF outcomes. Direct empirical testing, starting with quantification of MDPs in human follicular fluid and granulosa cells, is now warranted. © 2026

title: HAPO: Hierarchical affinity aware propagation for unsupervised graph anomaly detection
abstract: Graph anomaly detection (GAD) aims to identify nodes that deviate from normal structural or semantic patterns and is critical in security-sensitive applications. Existing unsupervised anomaly detection methods based on anomaly scoring are largely grounded in the local homophily assumption and are limited by feature smoothing to aggregating one-hop neighborhoods. Consequently, they lack a global perspective for detecting globally anomalous nodes and tend to misclassify structurally peripheral yet normal nodes as anomalies. Moreover, most existing approaches are not readily applicable to multi-view settings, limiting their effectiveness in graphs with heterogeneous relational semantics. To address these challenges, we propose Hierarchical Affinity-Aware Propagation (HAPO), a unified framework for single-view and multi-view GAD. HAPO combines multi-hop affinity-aware propagation with affinity-guided residual connections to enlarge the receptive field while mitigating over-smoothing, and a multi-classifier hierarchical affinity module to construct robust global affinity representations. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework. In particular, HAPO outperforms state-of-the-art methods by more than 10.11% on the single-view Amazon dataset and 9.69% on the multi-view IMDB dataset in terms of AUPRC. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Tuning donor–acceptor interactions via electronic modulation in Ga-doped ZnO for carbon chain growth from syngas
abstract: Higher alcohol synthesis from syngas over conventional CuZn catalysts often encounters a trade-off between total alcohol selectivity and C2+ distribution. Here, we show that Ga-doped ZnO enables precise electronic modulation to balance donor and acceptor reactions through controlled Ga doping. Electron-deficient Znδ+ sites serve as key active centers, facilitating non-dissociative CO adsorption and CO insertion for carbon chain growth. At low doping, substitutional Ga acts as a donor, promoting C-O bond activation. At 1 mol% Ga, substitutional Ga and the resulting electron-deficient Znδ+ sites effectively balance the electron donation-acquisition relationship, achieving 63.5% liquid C2+ alcohol content. Excessive doping (13 mol%) causes Ga clustering and electron-rich states, over-dominating acceptor reactions and suppressing CO insertion. This work establishes that balancing donor–acceptor reactions via electronic modulation is key to overcoming this trade-off, offering a design principle extendable to other electronically tunable catalytic systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Isogeometric analysis for explicit wave propagation in poroelastic media
abstract: For higher-order discretizations of explicit dynamics problems, Isogeometric Analysis (IGA) has several favorable properties as compared to classical Finite Element Analysis (FEA). While FEA produces spurious modes at orders beyond linear, this is not the case for IGA. Consequently, fewer degrees of freedom are required for comparable accuracy, larger timesteps can be taken, and the method is more robust for nonlinear problems. After eliminating outlier modes, the timestep even becomes virtually independent of the order. In this paper, we investigate how these advantages apply to the poroelastic continuum model.We consider both a primal formulation, wherein our variables are the displacement of the matrix material, the fluid displacement, and the pressure, as well as a reduced form wherein the pressure is eliminated. For our discretizations, we employ divergence-conforming spline spaces. Employing such spaces for the fluid displacement ensures inf-sup stability for the primal form, and exactly reproduces the kernel of the undamped problem in both forms. Furthermore, we prove and demonstrate that the two formulations coincide when both displacements are discretized with divergence-conforming spline spaces.Through spectral analysis, we find that the aforementioned benefits of IGA do carry over directly to the context of poroelasticity. In 1D, we split the discrete spectrum into fast and slow waves. When normalized against an analytical solution, each of these sub-spectra closely resembles results known in elasticity. Consequently, when poroelasticity is discretized with outlier-free IGA, the timestep is essentially independent of the order. We show this timestep scaling in 2D as well. title: Disengaged conversational behaviors and learning in student-AI dialogues for mathematical problem solving
abstract: As the conversational AI agents become integrated into digital learning environments, students' interaction with these systems can show conversational disengagement, including mocking, misleading, or otherwise diverting the agents. Although task-based disengagement such as gaming the system and off-task actions are well documented, the nature of the consequences of this conversational disengagement in student-AI dialogue remains largely unexplored. This study examined how different types of conversational disengagement relate to middle-school students’ mathematical learning with an AI-powered teachable agent embedded in a large-scale platform. We coded 5522 utterances from 246 students into six conversational disengagement categories (False Answering, Mocking, Ghosting, Mirroring, Withholding, and Random/Noisy) versus engagement. Regression analyses showed that some disengagements (False Answering and Mocking) were positively associated with post-test scores after controlling for pre-test performance, although these associations did not replicate in a sensitivity analysis restricted to human-annotated utterances. To capture process-level dynamics, we modeled how conversational disengagement ends using a competing-risks approach and separately clustered students based on their turn-by-turn transition probabilities. Most conversational disengagement tended to end within the first few turns, whereas Withholding showed a strong tendency to continue. Students in the highest-performing cluster combined a moderate level of conversational disengagement with strong recovery pathways, whereas the lowest-performing cluster exhibited persistent self-loops without recovery. Together, these findings suggest that some apparent disengagement in conversation with AI may occur within interaction trajectories that subsequently return to productive engagement. © 2026 The Authors

title: Beyond topology-driven graph convolution: Node patch convolutional network for node representation learning
abstract: Attributed graph node representation learning is crucial for tasks such as node classification in attributed networks. Conventional GNNs, whether coupled or decoupled, are mainly topology-driven and struggle to capture attribute correlations among non-neighboring nodes. Existing CNN-based graph methods alleviate this limitation by selecting relevant nodes but remain sensitive to node ordering and often fail to integrate attribute and topology views effectively. In this paper, we propose a CNN-based graph representation learning framework namely node patch convolutional network (NPCN) that constructs node-centric patches from both attribute and topology perspectives. Moreover, a tailored patch augmentation and the corresponding readout mechanism are adopted to enhance the node representation learning. A patch consistency constraint further stabilizes the learned representations. Experiments on both homophilic and heterophilic graphs demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms representative approaches. Moreover, computational efficiency analysis shows that NPCN achieves competitive performance with lower training overhead compared with Transformer-based graph representation learning methods, making it a practical solution for attributed graph node classification. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Navigating the unspoken: A qualitative study of how clinical nurse educators transmit tacit knowledge to nursing students
abstract: Background: In nursing education, a significant body of knowledge essential for professional practice is tacit—difficult to articulate, yet crucial for clinical judgment, ethical comportment, and professional identity formation. Understanding how clinical nurse educators perceive and transmit this tacit knowledge is critical for optimizing student preparation. Objective: This study aimed to explore the experiences of clinical nurse educators in identifying, conveying, and cultivating tacit knowledge among nursing students. Design: A descriptive qualitative study. Methods: The study involved in-depth, semi-structured interviews with 20 clinical nurse educators who were purposively sampled from 15 Chinese provinces and possessed ≥5 years of teaching experience. Data were collected from July to October 2025 and analyzed using thematic analysis, from which the key themes and subthemes were derived. Results: Four themes and 12 subthemes were extracted. The themes were The nature and expression of tacit knowledge in clinical nursing education, Strategies for transmitting tacit knowledge, Challenges in tacit knowledge transmission, Organizational support and cultural nurturing. Conclusions: Tacit knowledge is fundamental, not optional, to nursing practice. Its effective transmission hinges on deliberate pedagogy, supportive structures, and a reflective mentoring culture. These findings provide a foundation for developing clinical education frameworks and faculty policies dedicated to cultivating competent, compassionate, and ethically aware nurses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Network science in sports
abstract: Network science has become a central methodological framework for the study of complex systems, with applications across social, biological, and technological domains. Its strength lies in formalizing such systems as collections of interacting units, whose collective behavior depends not only on the properties of the individual components, but also on the structure, dynamics, and evolution of their interactions. In this Review, we analyze how this framework, rooted in statistical physics, is being applied to the study of sports systems. Sports provide a particularly suitable domain for network modeling, as performance emerges from interactions among agents, whose actions are constrained by spatial embedding and temporal ordering, and evolve under competitive, adaptive, and out-of-equilibrium conditions. We review the main network representations used in sports, from classical graph-based descriptions to more general frameworks, including spatial, temporal, multilayer, and higher-order networks. Particular attention is devoted to soccer, where network science has had its deepest methodological impact, while applications to other sports such as basketball, volleyball, American football, or badminton serve to illustrate the generality of the underlying principles. Network science provides sports analytics with a rigorous language for quantifying coordination, emergence, adaptation, and collective performance. At the same time, the availability of high-resolution event, tracking, and pose-estimation data makes sports an ideal testbed for validating and refining network models in realistic settings. As a result, the relationship between network science and sports, currently driven primarily by the application of network methods to sport, has the potential to become genuinely bidirectional. In this Review, we not only organize the literature on network methodologies and their applications to sports, but also discuss complementary concepts needed to capture the full picture, including entropy and complexity measures, as well as key ideas from statistical physics and nonlinear dynamics. Finally, despite the substantial progress made so far, the field remains under active development, and we highlight the main open questions that should be addressed in future research. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Effect of CO2 concentration on carbon sequestration and mechanical strength of coal-based solid waste cemented backfill
abstract: Coal production generates large quantities of coal-based solid wastes (coal gangue, blast furnace slag, and fly ash) and significant CO2 emissions, creating severe ecological challenges in mining regions. This study integrates coal-based solid waste cemented backfilling with CO2 mineral sequestration to manage both solid wastes and CO2. The CO2 uptake and uniaxial compressive strength (UCS) of coal-based solid waste cemented backfill (CSCB) were investigated after 14 days of mineralization curing at CO2 concentrations of 0–10 vol%. Thermogravimetric analysis (TG), scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) were used to examine the sequestration mechanism and the associated strength reduction. CO2 uptake increased with CO2 concentration: raising the concentration from 1.5 to 10 vol% increased the uptake from 2.42 to 4.05 wt% (a 67.4% increase), based on a single TG measurement per group. In contrast, UCS decreased from 6.05 MPa (0 vol%) to 0.72 MPa (10 vol%), an 88.1% reduction. Microstructural and mineralogical analyses indicate that CO2 reacts with alkaline phases and hydration products (CH, MH, C-S(A)-H gel, and AFt) to form calcite, gypsum, and possible Mg-bearing carbonate (XRD peaks tentatively assigned to dolomite). The strength loss is attributed to weakening of the alkaline environment, decalcification of C-S(A)-H gel, and carbonation of AFt to gypsum. A concentration of 1.5 vol% provided a reasonable balance, with 2.42 wt% uptake and a 13.2% strength loss. These results show a clear trade-off between carbon uptake and mechanical performance in CSCB. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Simulating Shape Variation in Material Culture: The Simumorph R-package
abstract: Archaeologists have devoted a significant amount of effort to define their types, or units of analysis. However, strong disagreements persist even after years of debate. This may occur for many reasons, some intrinsic to the archaeological record itself—since different technocomplexes may involve distinct and not always comparable types—and others related to the discipline’s epistemology, where interobserver bias and differences in theoretical schools and training traditions can play a key role. As a result, most archaeological analyses, usually based on type presence/absence or type frequencies, present uncertainty levels from the start, which are not always due to the archaeological record itself, but to how we analyse that record. In this work, we adopt a materialist view to present an alternative approach where we analyse purely artefact shape without the need for previous categorisation. To do this, we resort to Geometric Morphometrics, widely used in archaeology, and we develop a simulation framework for stepwise artefactual change. We provide the software tools to do this, which have been compiled in the R-package Simumorph, and we showcase its performance in four simulated archaeological scenarios. Here, we base our simulations on the geometric microliths found during the Early and Middle Holocene in the Western Mediterranean, but the framework can be applied to any context where shape variation matters. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Text-augmented patch–scene collaborative network for joint hyperspectral and LiDAR classification
abstract: Remote sensing (RS) image classification is an important technique for land-cover understanding and environmental monitoring. Combining hyperspectral imagery (HSI) with light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data has become a promising strategy for improving land-cover recognition. However, most existing approaches still focus on visual representation learning and make limited use of scene-level context and category-related semantic knowledge. Relying only on image features makes it difficult to associate visual patterns with land-cover semantics, especially for categories with similar appearances. Moreover, most methods focus on spectral–spatial feature extraction from local patches while overlooking potential scene dependencies among land-cover types. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Text-Augmented Patch–Scene Collaborative Network (TAPSCN), a multilevel information fusion framework for joint HSI and LiDAR classification. TAPSCN integrates patch-level cross-modal cues, scene-level structural context, and category-level textual priors for scene-aware semantic classification. First, an Interactive Patch Fusion Module (IPFM) employs spectral-channel attention and geometric-spatial attention to accommodate the heterogeneous characteristics of HSI and LiDAR data, respectively. A two-stage asymmetric cross-modal mutual-guidance strategy further enhances collaborative representation learning across modalities, yielding robust local patch representations. Subsequently, a Global Scene Guidance Module (GSGM) models whole-image context through visual state-space modeling. By collaboratively optimizing local patch information and global scene semantics, GSGM improves the discrimination of complex scenes and easily confused classes. Finally, a Text Augmentation Alignment Module (TAAM) constructs semantic priors from class-level textual prompts. Through the joint optimization of strong vision–text alignment and weak semantic reconstruction, TAAM guides visual features to capture high-level semantic knowledge associated with land-cover classes, thereby enhancing their semantic discriminability. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that TAPSCN achieves superior classification accuracy while maintaining moderate parameter complexity. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/RogsXie/TAPSCN . © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Stakeholder acceptance and feasibility of REM, a multi-device medication reminder system for adults with hypertension
abstract: Introduction: Medication non-adherence remains a major challenge in hypertension management among middle-aged and older adults. Reminder systems can support timely medication use, but many existing tools lack usability and healthcare workflow integration. REM, derived from the word ‘reminder’, was developed as an integrated medication adherence support system connecting patients, physicians, and pharmacists through a mobile application, smart pillbox, and wearable device. This study explored stakeholders’ perceived usefulness, ease of use, behavioral intention to use REM, and recommendations for improvement. Methods: This qualitative formative study used semi-structured interviews with hypertensive middle-aged and older adult patients (n = 20), physicians (n = 10), pharmacists (n = 10), and information technology (IT) experts (n = 10). The interview guide was informed by the Technology Acceptance Model and examined perceptions of system usefulness, ease of use, intention to use, feasibility, and recommended refinements. Data were coded and organized using MAXQDA. Results: Participants perceived the REM system as useful and easy to use for supporting medication adherence and patient monitoring. Most participants were willing to use or recommend REM, although acceptance depended on physician endorsement, affordability, insurance coverage, and workflow compatibility. Suggested refinements included secure communication, improved portability, offline functionality, and enhanced data security. Conclusion: REM was perceived as a useful and easy-to-use digital health intervention with potential to support medication adherence among middle-aged and older adults with hypertension. Findings highlight the importance of user-centered design, stakeholder integration, affordability, workflow compatibility, and robust data security in promoting future adoption and implementation. Public interest summary: Middle-aged to older adults with high blood pressure often forget to take their medication on time. To address this, the REM system was developed to improve their medication compliance. REM was derived from the word "reminder". The system consists of a mobile application, a smart pillbox, and a wearable device that work together to help patients remember their medication. Physicians and pharmacists can also access patients’ prescriptions and medication intake schedules to monitor their progress and compliance. In this study, patients, physicians, and pharmacists, including IT experts, were interviewed to express their thoughts about REM. Most participants were also willing to use and recommend REM for its usefulness. Suggested improvements included chat support, offline accessibility, portability, and stronger privacy and security features. In conclusion, the REM system shows potential as a user-friendly tool for improving medication adherence and supporting better health outcomes. © 2026 Fellowship of Postgraduate Medicine
