title: Microbial contamination and hygiene practices in small- and medium-scale pig slaughterhouses in Vietnam: The effects of two interventions
abstract: Foodborne diseases impose major health and economic burdens on low- and middle-income countries. In Vietnam, bacterial contamination is common along pork supply chains, particularly within traditional slaughterhouses. These facilities therefore represent key intervention points for improving food safety. This study evaluated the effects of interventions on microbial contamination and hygiene practices across small- and medium-scale pig slaughterhouses in four provinces of Vietnam. A controlled trial was conducted in 16 small- and medium-scale pig slaughterhouses. Eight slaughterhouses were first randomly assigned to receive a ‘Technique’ intervention (low-cost equipment and training), while the remaining eight served as no ‘Technique’ group. Within both groups, four slaughterhouses additionally received an ‘Incentive’ intervention (practice-rating program with monetary rewards). Microbiological and behavioral data were collected pre- and post-intervention through swabs of workers' hands (n = 128), pig carcasses (n = 192) and structured observation checklists (n = 192). The main effects of the ‘Technique’ and ‘Incentive’ interventions were evaluated using difference-in-differences mixed-effects models. The results revealed that Salmonella prevalence and mean total bacteria count on carcasses did not significantly change (37.5% and 5.4 log10 CFU/cm2 at baseline to 35.4% and 4.7 log10 CFU/cm2 at endline, respectively). Coliforms and Escherichia coli counts decreased across all groups, including the control, a pattern more consistent with seasonal and operational factors than the interventions. Neither intervention was associated with lower carcass contamination, and hygiene practice scores were not associated with contamination. Temperature, slaughtering capacity and workforce size showed mixed associations with microbial indicators. The ‘Technique’ intervention produced measurable improvements in hygiene practices, while the ‘Incentive’ intervention improved practices only in the short-term. While neither intervention reduced contamination, the study documents real-world slaughterhouse conditions and suggests that durable improvement will require sustained, multi-level strategies that combine behavioral change with structural and environmental upgrading. These findings could support interventions in traditional small- and medium-scale slaughter settings in low- and middle-income countries. © 2026 The Authors

title: A comparative investigation of physics-driven machine learning architectures for consolidation analysis
abstract: Physics-driven machine learning has emerged as a powerful framework for forward and inverse modeling of partial differential equations (PDEs), with increasing applications in geotechnical engineering. However, the relative performance of different physics-driven learning strategies remains problem-dependent, and their suitability for typical geotechnical problems has not been systematically established. This study systematically compares four physics-driven machine learning paradigms for consolidation analysis by combining Multi‑Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) and Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) with physics-informed neural networks (PINN) and the discrete-time deep energy method (DTDEM). The paradigms are evaluated for forward and inverse consolidation problems in one and three dimensions, with particular attention to convergence, computational cost, parameter inversion, accuracy, and robustness to noise. For forward problems governed by PDEs, although the energy-form DTDEM converges in fewer epochs than the strong-form PINN under both MLP and KAN architectures, its higher per-epoch cost results in a longer total wall-clock training time. A similar trade-off applies to KAN relative to MLP where the higher per-epoch cost can offset the benefit of faster convergence in terms of epochs. In terms of solution accuracy, replacing MLP with KAN improves both accuracy and training-loss convergence under the strong-form PINN framework, while under the DTDEM framework this advantage is not consistent. For parameter inversion, the DTDEM-based energy formulation is ineffective for parameter inversion because treating material parameters as additional optimization variables make the functional unbounded from below, resulting in divergent training. In contrast, within the strong-form framework, KAN substantially improves parameter-inversion accuracy and robustness to noisy data compared with MLPs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: BMHA-Net: A two-branch multiscale hierarchical attention network for depression severity estimation from facial videos
abstract: Depression is a prevalent mental disorder that imposes a substantial public-health and socioeconomic burden, while conventional assessments based on rating scales and clinical interviews are constrained by subjectivity and limited professional resources, hindering large-scale, low-cost, and consistent assessment. Facial-video-based automated modeling provides a non-invasive alternative for depression severity estimation and has attracted increasing attention because facial dynamics may provide informative behavioral cues associated with depression. However, depression-related visual cues are often subtle, sparsely distributed, and sensitive to head pose, illumination, and inter-subject variability, while existing multi-branch attention designs may introduce additional parameter and computational overhead, making the balance between prediction accuracy and model complexity an important issue. To address these challenges, we propose BMHA-Net, a two-branch multiscale hierarchical attention network that enhances fine-grained facial cues through high-resolution local and shifted-window self-attention, captures global spatial dependencies through low-resolution global attention, and strengthens appearance–geometry complementarity via bidirectional cross-branch interaction and adaptive multi-scale fusion. Experiments on AVEC2014 demonstrate that BMHA-Net reduces MAE from 8.86 to 6.30 (28.9% relative) and RMSE from 10.86 to 8.47 (22.0% relative) compared with the official baseline. Under the same visual-only input setting, BMHA-Net achieves lower FLOPs than several recent vision-based methods with reported computational costs while maintaining competitive regression performance. Additional experiments on DAIC-WOZ further demonstrate its adaptability to pre-extracted visual descriptors under a different depression-score protocol. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Exhaust emission control strategies for lean-burn NH3/H2-fueled spark ignition engines
abstract: Ammonia-fueled engines are attracting increasing interest as a carbon-free energy conversion technology; however, their exhaust typically contains unburned ammonia (NH3), nitrogen oxides (NOx), and nitrous oxide (N2O), and achieving their simultaneous removal under oxygen-rich conditions remains a major challenge. This study investigates emission control strategies using SCR catalyst for a NH3/H2-fueled spark-ignition engine, with emphasis on the linkage between engine-out exhaust characteristics and SCR performance. Engine experiments demonstrate that the engine-out ammonia-to-NOx ratio (ANR) can be systematically controlled through mixture composition, specifically via the equivalence ratio and H2 energy fraction, providing a practical control index for aftertreatment. Using Fe- and Cu-zeolite SCR catalysts, ANR-dependent conversion characteristics are quantified over a wide temperature range. Both catalysts exhibit a temperature-dependent optimal ANR at which near-complete simultaneous removal of NH3 and NOx is achieved, reflecting competition between SCR reactions and NH3 oxidation. To address sensitivity to ANR variability, two complementary and distinct approaches are demonstrated: (i) a control-based strategy employing periodic ANR swing to exploit NH3 storage in zeolite catalysts, and (ii) a catalyst-design-based strategy using a tandem Fe/Cu SCR configuration. Both approaches achieve catalyst-out NH3 and NOx concentrations below 10 ppm. For the tested Fe/Cu tandem system at a nominal catalyst-inlet gas temperature of 450 °C, simultaneous high NH3 and NOx conversions were observed at all tested ANR points between 1.25 and 1.62. In addition, the effects of catalyst configuration and temperature on N2O formation and decomposition are clarified, highlighting trade-offs between operational robustness and greenhouse gas mitigation. The results present proof-of-concept emission-control approaches under the selected steady-state conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Evaluating Mild Cognitive Impairment using large language models: A comparative analysis
abstract: This study evaluates whether fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) can support preliminary screening of Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) from transcribed Chinese speech. Using the Chinese subset of the TAUKADIAL/TalkBank connected-speech dataset, we compared Llama3, Gemma, Qwen, and Qwen1.5 models under supervised fine-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, different quantization settings, automatic speech recognition systems, and prompt styles. The experiments were evaluated with subject-level five-fold cross-validation and reported with mean and standard deviation for accuracy, F1-score, precision, and recall. Among the tested configurations, Llama3-8B with 4-bit QLoRA achieved the strongest performance, with accuracy and F1-score of approximately 0.86. To place these results against transparent alternatives, we added the official TAUKADIAL feature-based benchmarks, which use acoustic eGeMAPS features and interpretable linguistic measures such as token count, type count, type–token ratio, lexical density, and verb and pronoun ratios. Because the official benchmark uses a different multilingual train/test protocol, it is treated as an external reference rather than a head-to-head ranking. The findings suggest that LLM-based transcript analysis may be useful as a low-cost prescreening aid, but the small, language-specific dataset and lack of matched external validation require cautious interpretation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Stepwise salting-out and freeze-thaw strategy enables robust conductive polyvinyl alcohol hydrogels via interfacial synergy for multifunctional wearables
abstract: To address the intrinsic trade-off between mechanical robustness and ionic conductivity in polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogels arising from structural heterogeneity, this work presents a stepwise salting-out and freeze-thaw cycling strategy to fabricate high-performance composite hydrogels with synergistic interfacial interactions. By integrating sodium alginate-dispersed liquid metal with lignosulfonate mediation, we establish a multi-scale crosslinking network governed by hydrogen bonding, metal-coordination, and electrostatic effects. Crucially, the stepwise process mitigates the excessive densification typical of conventional methods, facilitating the homogeneous infiltration of additives and refining PVA microcrystalline domains. The optimized hydrogel achieves a tensile strength of 1.22 ± 0.04 MPa and an ionic conductivity of 1.7 ± 0.05 S·m−1—representing enhancements of 1406% and 765% over pristine PVA, respectively—while exhibiting exceptional fatigue resistance with negligible hysteresis decay over 2000 loading-unloading cycles. Additionally, the hydrogel demonstrates versatile functionality as strain sensors, triboelectric nanogenerators, and bioelectrodes; notably, integration with a one-dimensional convolutional neural network deep learning model enables a self-powered system to achieve 91.76% accuracy in gait pattern recognition. This study provides fundamental understanding of interfacial synergy in physically crosslinked hydrogels, paving the way for durable soft colloidal materials. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Analysis of COVID-19 cases in India through machine learning: A study of intervention in the SIR model
abstract: To analyse and predict COVID-19 cases from the prevalence of reported real COVID-19 cases, we propose a modified SIR (Susceptible-Infectious-Recovered) model that incorporates interventions using machine learning approaches. The SIR model is extended by introducing an intervention parameter, denoted by ρ, which collectively represents intervention measures such as complete lockdowns, partial lockdowns, quarantines, isolations, and social distancing. Further, we analyse the equilibrium points, local and global stability at the disease-free and endemic equilibria of SIR model with intervention. In addition, phase portrait plotting has been employed to visualize the qualitative dynamics of the system. Further, a supervised machine learning approach is used to estimate the transmission rate (β) based on real COVID-19 case data from the entire India and some states. The proposed SIR model with intervention and SIR model implemented and computed the prediction for active and recovered cases for COVID-19 data with computing β from prevalence COVID-19 data for India, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and compared their results with actual reported COVID-19 data. The visual and quantitative results in term of RMSE, MAPE and R2 demonstrate the efficacy of proposed SIR model with intervention in comparison to SIR model. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Understanding human detection of algorithmic bias through drift-diffusion modeling
abstract: Algorithms increasingly make high-risk decisions that impact individuals' lives, from loan approvals to medical diagnoses, but can exhibit problematic biases that require human oversight. Despite regulatory moves toward human-in-the-loop systems, little is known about a person's ability to detect algorithmic bias or how cognitive processes influence detection accuracy. Across two experiments, we show that human detection of algorithmic bias is limited, even when bias is pronounced and participants evaluate decisions across multiple trials. Detection accuracy is shaped by individual differences in gender and moral reasoning, and was not improved by a single warning ahead of time that bias may be present. Participants who are better at detecting bias tend to engage in more deliberative decision-making, taking longer to reach conclusions and requiring more evidence before responding. Modeling detection as a process of evidence accumulation allows us to locate where in the decision oversight may break down rather than only assessing whether it breaks down or not. These findings highlight the potential and limits of human oversight in algorithmic systems, suggesting that effective human-in-the-loop designs must support careful, reflective judgments and account for variability in users' monitoring abilities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Balancing hierarchical representation and quantization: A performance trade-off in text embeddings
abstract: Hierarchical text embedding models offer variable-length representations, while quantization reduces numerical precision; both aim to improve computational efficiency. This work is an empirical benchmark study of how these two orthogonal, already-established techniques interact. We evaluate 38 tasks from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) using four transformer-based embedding models, covering 1D and 2D hierarchical representations combined with 32-bit, 8-bit, and binary quantization, for 168 configurations per task. We report each efficiency dimension separately: theoretical per-vector storage and end-to-end evaluation time. Under a Friedman test with Nemenyi post-hoc analysis, int8 quantization is statistically indistinguishable from float32 for pair classification and re-ranking and costs at most 1.5 percentage points overall, whereas binary quantization is significantly worse across every task category. Halving the embedding dimension once is not statistically detectable above m=16; two successive halvings always are. Combining an 8× dimensionality reduction with int8 yields a 32× reduction in per-vector storage at 94.4% of baseline effectiveness. Because evaluation times were measured once, we treat them as indicative: we find no evidence that quantization speeds up evaluation, whereas sampling from intermediate layers shortens it substantially. Retrieval degrades far faster than every other category, so we report findings per task category. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Structure-aware optimization of recurrence thresholds for multi-sensor kinematic time-series image representations
abstract: Recurrence plots (RPs) provide a nonlinear representation of time-series dynamics, but their structural characteristics are highly sensitive to recurrence-threshold selection. Conventional fixed-threshold and fixed-recurrence-rate strategies prescribe the recurrence condition without explicitly evaluating the structural properties of the resulting representation. To address this limitation, this work proposes a structure-aware recurrence-threshold optimization framework for multi-sensor kinematic time-series image representations. Rather than directly optimizing the absolute threshold ε, the target recurrence rate (RR) is formulated as a representation-design variable and evaluated using a normalized and regularized multi-metric Recurrence Quantification Analysis (RQA) objective. A kinematics-aware recurrence representation is constructed from acceleration magnitude, angular-velocity magnitude, jerk magnitude, and angular-acceleration magnitude to characterize both steady and transient motion dynamics. Experiments on UP-Fall show that the proposed formulation identifies a stable, non-boundary recurrence-density regime around the prior-informed RR≈0.08 region and produces systematic structural differences relative to fixed, nearest-neighbour, and stability-based threshold-selection methods, with large effect sizes for several RQA descriptors. Independent validation on SisFall confirms systematic RR dependence of the evaluated recurrence structures under different sensing and acquisition conditions, while demonstrating that the numerical operating regime is dataset-dependent rather than universally fixed. Downstream fall-versus-ADL validation further shows that the complete kinematics-aware representation achieves 85.58% accuracy, 88.89% recall, and 84.83% F1-score using RQA features, while direct KA-RP image classification achieves 0.9609±0.0089 accuracy and 0.9902±0.0044 AUC. Overall, these results support recurrence-rate selection as a structure-aware representation-design problem and provide a data-dependent framework for constructing density-controlled recurrence representations for wearable kinematic time series. © 2026

title: Navigating blue economy research conflicts for improved societal outcomes
abstract: The Blue Economy aims to balance economic prosperity, environmental stewardship, and social equity through sustainable ocean development. Its rapid expansion—spanning fisheries, aquaculture, maritime transport, and energy—has intensified competition for marine resources and space, often generating conflict and cumulative impacts on ecosystems and communities. These tensions are driven by uncertainty about outcomes, as well as differing stakeholder values and perceptions. To realize the goals of the Blue Economy, robust research is needed. However, research institutions working in contested marine spaces may face reputational, ethical, and strategic risks. These include navigating tensions among ocean users, developers, policymakers, and the public. From an organisational perspective, deciding whether to engage in such research requires balancing potential benefits against risks to integrity, partnerships, and long-term goals. This paper introduces the Conflict Navigation Grid, a decision-support framework that enables research organisations to systematically evaluate the risks and benefits of proposed projects. The Grid helps identify initiatives that provide strong organisational, community, environmental, and policy value while also assessing whether reputational, operational, or personal risks are manageable. It distinguishes projects that align with institutional values and capacities from those where the potential harms outweigh uncertain returns. By adopting this systematic decision framework, organisations can confidently make decisions in the face of conflict, thereby managing risk and achieving improved societal outcomes. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Speed-Resolved experimental and CFD evaluation of a Low-Power Intake-Air ionization retrofit for diesel combustion and emission control
abstract: A low-power intake-air ionization attachment was experimentally and numerically evaluated as a retrofit strategy for diesel-engine performance and emission control without fuel reformulation or engine modification. A single-cylinder compression-ignition engine was tested under baseline and staged ionized-air conditions at 300–1500 rpm, with five repeated measurements at each operating point. Each negative-ion module operated at a fixed 12 V DC input (<1 W per module) with device-rated values of approximately −9.5 kV DC high-voltage output, 1.2 x 1013 ions s−1 negative-ion production, and 1.9 x 1012 ions cm−3 at a 2.9-cm reference distance. The staged strategy activated one to five modules as speed increased. At the fully load-matched 1500-rpm condition, brake power and torque remained 1.94072 kW and 12.35 N m in both modes, while fuel mass-flow rate decreased from 2.34 x 10-4 to 2.25 x 10-4 kg s−1. Using an LHV of 42.5 MJ kg−1, BSFC decreased from 0.4341 to 0.4174 kg kW-1h−1 and brake thermal efficiency increased from 19.51 % to 20.30 %. Across the speed range, mean exhaust-gas temperature decreased by 6.8–19.8 °C and CO, HC, and NOx analyzer concentrations were lower under the staged ionization-ON condition. Crank-angle-resolved in-cylinder pressure and ion-current signals were measured, and apparent net and cumulative heat release were derived from the pressure trace. A steady three-dimensional RANS model used displacement-consistent inlet conditions based on the 0.363-L swept volume and eta_v = 0.82. Grid refinement at 1500 rpm used approximately 1.6, 3.2, 6.3, 12.6, and 25.2 million cells; the 6.3-million-cell grid was selected as the production mesh after the monitored solution changed by less than 1 % with further refinement. Residual reduction, monitored-variable stability, and inlet–outlet mass conservation were verified before post-processing. The CFD results include velocity, pressure, recirculation, residence-time, turbulence/mixing, outlet-flow redistribution, and normalized scalar-transport fields for the solved operating points. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: The regulatory roles of the medial septum and hippocampus in spatial memory impairment of PTSD mice
abstract: This experiment was based on the establishment of an analogue of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in mice, aiming to explore the regulatory effects of the medial septum (MS) and the hippocampus (HIP) on spatial memory impairment in mice, and to establish a theoretical foundation for revealing the pathological basis of PTSD-related spatial memory impairment. The PTSD mouse model was prepared, behavioral testing, FluoroGold (FG) retrograde tracing technique, viral tracing technique, in vivo fiber photometry recording technique, chemogenetic technology and in vivo electrophysiological recording techniques were applied to observe and analyze the changes in spatial memory ability and the central regulatory mechanism. PTSD mice showed heightened anxiety, impaired spatial memory, suppressed Sch-CA1 long-term potentiation, and hyperactivity of MS-CA1 cholinergic neurons; chemogenetic inhibition of this pathway rescued both the behavioral and synaptic plasticity deficits. The regulation of spatial memory impairment in PTSD mice involves MS-resident cholinergic neurons. We found a cholinergic pathway connection between MS and CA1, and this pathway may regulate murine spatial cognition by influencing the synaptic plasticity of Sch-CA1. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Contrastive semi-supervised clustering based on pairwise constraint for identifying influential nodes in complex networks
abstract: Identifying influential nodes is crucial for understanding the functional dynamics of complex networks. However, existing approaches face significant limitations: centrality-based methods capture only specific topological aspects, while supervised techniques require abundant labeled data, hindering their practical applicability. To overcome these issues, we propose PCGCN, a contrastive semi-supervised graph clustering framework that integrates limited node labels with structural information through pairwise constraints. Our method leverages regular equivalence-based (RE) similarity to define pairwise constraints between unlabeled nodes, which are jointly used with labeled data to guide the learning process. By combining a graph convolutional network (GCN) encoder with a pairwise constraint-based contrastive loss, PCGCN learns discriminative node embeddings under limited supervision. Extensive experiments show that PCGCN generally achieves better performance than the centrality-based and unsupervised/semi-supervised methods, while remaining competitive with the supervised methods adopted for comparison. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Tracing locations from pixels: A survey of worldwide image geo-localization
abstract: Worldwide image geo-localization (WIGL) estimates the geographic coordinates of a photograph from its visual content, without metadata on the query image and without a known search area. This capability supports practical applications, including cybercrime source tracing, disaster response, and autonomous navigation. In this manuscript, a comprehensive review of WIGL is presented, in which current methods are systematically organized into four paradigms: classification-based, retrieval-based, generation-based, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). For each paradigm, representative approaches and core design principles are examined, with their strengths and limitations compared. Training, testing, and fine-tuning datasets are also reviewed in depth. A spatial distribution analysis of these datasets reveals notable coverage biases in existing benchmarks. Standard evaluation metrics are consolidated, and the reported results on six test sets are aggregated, providing a common basis for comparison across methods. The comparative analysis of reported results indicates that RAG approaches currently achieve the highest accuracy on major benchmarks, though this advantage is partly confounded by larger backbone models and training data while generation-based approaches offer a promising alternative for zero-shot location inference. Finally, several under-explored research challenges that are rarely discussed in prior surveys are identified and outlined. These include the difficulty of disambiguating visually similar images captured at distant locations, as well as other open problems to guide future work. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Decoupled reverse Kullback–Leibler: Rethinking knowledge distillation loss for bridging GNNs and MLPs
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) excel at handling graph-structured data but are often prohibitively expensive for low-latency applications. Cross-architecture graph knowledge distillation (GKD) addresses this by training efficient Multi-layer Perceptrons (MLPs) to mimic GNN performance. Interestingly, while existing methods predominantly use forward Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence, we find that the two terms of reverse KL exhibit optimization properties that are better matched to the GKD objective. However, its conventional form suffers from tightly coupled fitting and regularization terms with fixed weights, limiting its flexibility. To overcome this, we propose Decoupled Reverse KL (DRKL), which introduces hyperparameters to independently adjust the weight of each term, enabling more effective adaptation to diverse prediction scenarios. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DRKL outperforms both standard forward and reverse KL losses across multiple metrics. Furthermore, DRKL serves as a plug-and-play loss that can enhance the GKD frameworks evaluated in this work without added computational cost, delivering improved performance, robustness, and fast inference. Our code is available at https://github.com/xsk160/DRKL. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Trust fusion: a weighted multi-perspective framework for ECG anomaly detection in IoMT
abstract: Continuous electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring in Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) environments faces a fundamental precision–sensitivity trade–off. Standalone reconstruction–based detectors achieve high specificity but miss subtle anomalies, while geometric detectors capture rare patterns but generate excessive false alarms. This paper presents a hybrid Trust Fusion framework that resolves this trade–off through linearly weighted integration of an LSTM–Autoencoder, a 6–band Isolation Forest, and Z–score statistical validation, augmented by a clinically motivated Label–Free Adaptive Recovery mechanism that reclassifies borderline missed arrhythmias closest to the decision boundary. Evaluated on the MIT–BIH Arrhythmia Database under a strict inter–patient protocol (25 training records, 10 held–out test patients, 406,210 windows), the proposed method achieves 93.56% Accuracy, 86.96% Sensitivity, 96.15% Specificity, 89.86% Precision, 88.39% F1–Score, and an AUC–ROC of 0.9640, reducing missed arrhythmias by 74.5% compared to the standalone LSTM–AE baseline while maintaining a clinically acceptable False Positive Rate of 3.85%. The core detectors are trained without labeled data; only threshold calibration and recovery configuration use a small validation subset offline. Computationally, the framework operates at 7.93 ms per window with a throughput of 3,697 windows/s and a compact 350–400 KB footprint, making it well–suited for real–time, resource–constrained IoMT deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Characterizing the spatial correlation network of cultivated land system resilience: Nonlinear relationships between interregional production factor flows and node centrality
abstract: Against the backdrop of intensifying uncertainty shocks and increasingly frequent cross-regional factor flows, the spatial governance of cultivated land system resilience (CLSR) has become an increasingly important issue. Existing studies have largely treated CLSR as a localized attribute confined to specific administrative units, while paying limited attention to the evolution of its spatial correlation network. To address this gap, the Vertical and Horizontal Scatter Degree Method, Social Network Analysis, and the XGBoost-GeoShapley model were employed to examine the spatiotemporal patterns of CLSR and interregional flows of labor, capital, and technology across Chinese cities, and to identify the nonlinear relationships between interregional production factor flows and node centrality in the CLSR spatial correlation network. The results show that CLSR in China increased steadily and exhibited a clear east-west gradient, with higher levels in the east and lower levels in the west. Interregional flows of labor, capital, and technology continued to intensify, while spatial agglomeration and differentiation coexisted. The CLSR spatial correlation network in China was characterized by overall connectivity but sparse linkages. Network density fluctuated only between 0.10 and 0.14, indicating that substantive intercity linkages in CLSR remained relatively weak. All node centrality measures displayed long-tailed distributions, and cities such as Beijing, Shanghai, Tianjin, Suzhou, Chongqing, and Qingdao occupied advantageous positions in terms of connectivity, accessibility, and bridging functions. Further analysis reveals a significant nonlinear relationship between interregional production factor flows and node centrality in the CLSR spatial correlation network. Overall, low levels of interregional production factor flows were associated with positive contributions to node centrality, whereas high levels were associated with negative contributions, which gradually stabilized at the upper end of the flow distribution. Moreover, fiscal support, geographical location, and their interaction emerged as important factors explaining heterogeneity in node centrality. From the perspective of relational geography, this study extends the analytical framework of CLSR and provides a scientific basis for the cross-regional coordination of CLSR enhancement and the optimization of resource factor allocation. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Navigating public and private funding options for conservation measures: A cross-country comparison of western European farmers' preferences
abstract: Evidence in economics highlights the importance of the design of agri-environmental contracts for farmers' participation. However, there is little evidence on Western European farmers' preferences between alternative public and private contracts and labels, and on their synergies with participation in farmer clusters. In addition, cultural or institutional differences may lead to variation in contract design preferences across countries. Thus, we apply a discrete choice experiment using an online survey to estimate farmers' preferences for the contract organiser (government, retailer, NGO), the payment method (fixed per hectare payment, price premium associated with a label), and participation in a farmer cluster including technical assistance by a facilitator as part of the contractual arrangement (no farmer cluster, optional participation, mandatory participation) in the United Kingdom, France and the Netherlands. Based on a sample of 767 farmers, respondents prefer, on average, government-organised contracts to contracts from retailers or NGOs. Farmers prefer fixed per hectare payments over price premiums associated with a label and contracts granting the option to join a farmer cluster. The results vary between farm types and countries. title: Governance transitions in underground infrastructure: Coordinating resilience enhancement of ageing metro systems
abstract: As critical underground infrastructure, the resilience of ageing metro systems is fundamental to peoples’ safety and urban services. Its resilience failures extend far beyond technical origins; they arise from misaligned incentives, fragmented governance, and inefficient multi-stakeholder decision-making that derail technical implementation in complex urban settings. Here, we reconceptualize metro resilience as a socio-technical coordination problem rather than an exclusively technical one, developing a dynamic evolutionary game framework that reveals how service disruption constraints and stakeholder incentives determine whether cities escape low-resilience lock-in or achieve sustained adaptive capacity. We introduce a novel integration of life-cycle-informed, tripartite evolutionary game framework that integrates expert-based stakeholder salience identification with nonlinear dynamic modelling to capture long-term coordination in resilience enhancement decision-making. The results reveal that metro resilience is governed by sharp evolutionary tipping points: systems either remain trapped in low-resilience lock-in driven by short-term cost aversion or shift abruptly into stable high-resilience cooperation when institutional pressure, public supervision and risk reduction efficacy surpass critical thresholds. Beyond the ageing metro systems, this framework offers a transferable analytical lens for collaborative resilience decision-making in the comparable ageing urban underground infrastructures. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: hnRNPU regulates the sorting of exo-miR-125a-5p in colon epithelial cells and its role in realgar-induced central nervous system toxicity
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Elucidating the mechanisms underlying realgar-induced toxicity is essential for the early prevention and treatment of arsenic-related adverse effects and for reducing the associated healthcare burden. Aim of study: Owing to its poor solubility, realgar preferentially accumulates in the intestine after oral administration. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanism by which realgar regulates exosomal miR-125a-5p (exo-miR-125a-5p) sorting in colonic epithelial cells and to investigate the role of exo-miR-125a-5p in realgar-induced central nervous system (CNS) toxicity. Materials and methods: A chronic realgar-exposed mouse model was established and combined with AAV9-mediated hnRNPU knockdown, miR-125a-5p-enriched exosome administration, and probiotic intervention. Complementary in vitro studies were performed using YAMC cells subjected to hnRNPU silencing or co-treatment with realgar and L-cysteine sulfinic acid (LCSA). Small RNA sequencing, 16S rDNA sequencing, quantitative proteomics, untargeted metabolomics, RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), miRNA pull-down, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), Western blotting, and other molecular biological approaches were integrated to systematically investigate the molecular mechanism underlying realgar-regulated exo-miR-125a-5p sorting in colonic epithelial cells and its contribution to realgar-induced CNS toxicity. Results: Realgar exposure induced dose-dependent colonic injury, altered the exosomal miRNA profile of colonic epithelial cells, and significantly reduced the secretion of exo-miR-125a-5p. Mechanistically, the RNA-binding protein hnRNPU directly bound mature miR-125a-5p, enhanced its post-transcriptional stability, and promoted its nuclear retention, thereby limiting its loading into exosomes. Realgar-induced gut microbiota dysbiosis reduced the abundance of Lactobacillus and the level of its metabolite, LCSA, resulting in aberrant upregulation of hnRNPU. The consequent reduction in circulating exo-miR-125a-5p relieved repression of the STAT1 signaling pathway, leading to activation of the microglial STAT1–NLRP3 inflammasome axis and exacerbation of realgar-induced CNS toxicity. Conclusion: Realgar induces both colonic and central nervous system toxicity. Mechanistically, realgar disrupts gut microbial homeostasis, depleting Lactobacillus-derived LCSA, which promotes hnRNPU expression and enhances the nuclear retention of mature miR-125a-5p. This process suppresses miR-125a-5p sorting into exosomes, reduces circulating exo-miR-125a-5p levels, and consequently activates the microglial STAT1–NLRP3 inflammasome pathway, thereby aggravating CNS toxicity. These findings identify a previously unrecognized gut microbiota–metabolite–RNA-binding protein axis governing exosomal miRNA sorting and establish exo-miR-125a-5p as a critical mediator linking intestinal injury to neuroinflammation. This study provides new mechanistic insights into realgar-induced colonic and CNS toxicity and expands our understanding of gut–brain axis-mediated toxicological mechanisms. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: The emission-inequality nexus across stages of development
abstract: Does a more unequal society emit more CO2? The nexus between carbon emissions and income inequality has been at the core of a vast literature yielding conflicting results. Here, we provide robust evidence of a non-linear relationship that depends on the structural composition of the economy. Specifically, we document a positive association between income inequality—measured using five different indicators, for both pre-tax and post-tax income—and per capita carbon emissions in highly tertiarized countries. By contrast, this relationship turns negative in non-service-intensive economies. We provide evidence for plausible mechanisms mediating this non-linear association. In particular, the investment carbon footprint of the top 1% and the size of the manufacturing sector emerge as key dimensions underlying the observed patterns. Our results point to the structural composition of the economy as a crucial factor shaping the emission-inequality nexus. As such, economic structure helps identify phases of development in which reducing inequality comes with climate-related benefits. © 2026 The Authors

title: Occurrence, distribution and infection of triatomines with Trypanosoma cruzi in the state of Campeche, Mexico: Triatomines in Campeche Mexico; [Presencia, distribución e infección de triatominos con Trypanosoma cruzi en el estado de Campeche, México]
abstract: Campeche is a Mexican state with an ideal habitat for triatomines, the vectors of Trypanosoma cruzi, the parasite that causes Chagas disease. While different entomological indices and the geographic distribution of these triatomines have been reported in the state, data remain limited to a few localities. Objective. Evaluate the occurrence, distribution, and natural infection of triatomines in Campeche, Mexico. Materials and methods. Triatomines were collected from 1996 to 2023 in 32 localities of Campeche within intradomicile, peridomicile, and sylvatic areas. The percentage of natural infections was calculated, and associations between triatomine species and locality, as well as between triatomine instars and infection status, were analyzed. Results. A total of 532 triatomines were collected: Triatoma dimidiata was the most abundant and widely distributed species in the state, whereas only a single specimen each of Triatoma nitida and Eratyrus cuspidatus was found. Across all three collection areas, adults were more frequently found than nymphs. Furthermore, most females were captured in intradomicile areas, and more females exhibited a higher proportion of Trypanosoma cruzi infection compared to males. The overall natural infection rate for the entire region was 18.8%. The only significant statistical association was between triatomine developmental instars and Trypanosoma cruzi infection (χ2 = 80.396, p < 0.0001). Conclusion. This work highlights the importance of continuously monitoring areas around dwellings to prevent potential infestation by non-domiciliated bugs and crucially to reduce the risk of Trypanosoma cruzi infection among the local population. © 2027, Instituto Nacional de Salud. .

title: Affective Dimensions of Spanish as a Foreign Language (SFL) Education: Exploring the Interplay of Anxiety, Motivation, and Self-Esteem among Secondary School Students
abstract: This study probed the associations among Spanish as a foreign language (SFL) students’ anxiety, motivation, and self-esteem. Beyond mapping the connections between these affective factors, the research also examined the extent to which students’ motivation and anxiety predicted their self-esteem. The data were collected from 118 secondary school students through three validated instruments, namely the Foreign Language Classroom Anxiety Scale, Foreign Language Self-Esteem Scale, and Motivation towards Foreign Languages Survey. The analysis indicated clear patterns of association, with higher levels of anxiety linked to lower levels of both motivation and self-esteem. The results highlighted the importance of addressing emotional factors in foreign language education and suggested that interventions targeting anxiety reduction and the enhancement of self-esteem and motivation could foster a more supportive language learning environment. By demonstrating how affective factors shape SFL learning, the study offered practical insights for policymakers and language educators seeking to promote students’ emotional well-being and engagement. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .

title: EWiAR: Enhanced WiFi activity recognition using spectrogram analysis and cross-attention
abstract: Driven by the development of wireless sensing, human activity recognition (HAR) based on WiFi channel state information (CSI) has attracted immense attention owing to its low-cost, device-free, and non-intrusive characteristics. Conventional approaches heavily rely on time-frequency analysis to generate spectrograms. However, fixed-window time-frequency transforms involve an inherent trade-off between temporal and frequency resolution, while residual noise and artifacts may obscure motion-related structures in the spectrograms. To tackle these challenges, we propose EWiAR, a framework designed for high-precision HAR. At its frontend, an Enhanced Spectrogram Analysis Network (ESAN) is introduced to mitigate resolution trade-offs. It leverages a multi-scale feature extraction (MSFE) bank to dynamically capture varying frequency resolutions, followed by a spectrogram refinement module (SRM) that actively purifies the representations from background interference. Rather than using standard classifiers, the backend employs a Time-Frequency Cross-Attention Transformer (TFAiT) to process these spectrograms. TFAiT orchestrates a dual-branch learning mechanism that concurrently models temporal motion dependencies via a bidirectional LSTM and extracts global spectral patterns using a vision transformer. These complementary features are fused through a dedicated Time-Frequency Cross-Attention mechanism. Comprehensive experiments across synthetic signals and three public datasets demonstrate that EWiAR achieves superior overall performance compared to eleven mainstream benchmarks. Specifically, it delivers accuracies of 98.6% on WiAR, 99.1% on UT-HAR and 98.9% on NTU-HAR, firmly validating its exceptional effectiveness for complex indoor environments. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Trade-offs between water storage and transport mediated by three percolating pores in subtropical red soils: X-ray CT evidence from an 11-year tillage experiment
abstract: Red soils in subtropical regions are highly susceptible to structural degradation, resulting in poor water retention and restricted water transport. Although tillage strongly influences soil hydraulic properties, the pore-scale mechanisms governing these responses after long-term management remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how 11 years of no-tillage (NT), rotary tillage (RT), and deep ploughing (DP) reshaped pore architecture and regulated soil hydraulic behavior across a 0–40 cm red soil profile by integrating soil physical measurements, van Genuchten modeling, X-ray computed tomography (CT), and multivariate analyses. Relative to conventional rotary tillage (RT), DP reduced bulk density by 16.8% and increased saturated hydraulic conductivity (Ks) by 138.9–1248.2% and air permeability (Ka) by 25.9–167.0% within the 0–30 cm cultivated layer through enhanced macroporosity and pore connectivity. In contrast, NT maintained higher Ks and Ka in the 20–40 cm subsoil, reflecting the preservation of continuous biopore networks under long-term minimal disturbance. RT preferentially promoted mesopore (200–500 μm) development, resulting in the highest saturated water content, field moisture capacity, and plant-available water. Random forest analysis identified global pore connectivity (Γ), pore anisotropy (An) and pore size distribution, rather than total porosity, as the dominant predictors of hydraulic behavior. Correlation, principal component, and redundancy analyses consistently showed that macropores (>500 μm) primarily controlled water transmission, whereas meso- and micropores (60–200 and 200–500 μm) governed water retention. Structural equation modeling demonstrated that tillage regulated hydraulic function indirectly through pore architecture, with pore conductivity promoting hydraulic conductivity (standardized path coefficient: 0.38) and pore storage enhancing hydraulic storage (0.45), while revealing a strong antagonistic trade-off (-0.93) between conductivity and water storage. These findings establish pore architecture as the mechanistic link between long-term tillage and soil hydraulic function, providing a scientific basis for optimizing tillage strategies to improve water use efficiency and drought resilience in red soil agroecosystems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: The Effect of Mindful Teaching on Job Satisfaction among L2 Instructors: Examining the Mediating Role of Teacher Self-Efficacy
abstract: Teacher well-being has become an important concern in higher education due to increasing levels of occupational stress, burnout, and attrition, which may negatively affect instructional quality and student learning outcomes. These challenges are particularly evident in English as a foreign language teaching, where instructors frequently manage intensive workloads, diverse learner needs, and substantial emotional demands. Although previous research has linked mindfulness and self-efficacy to positive teacher outcomes, limited attention has been given to the psychological mechanisms through which mindful teaching contributes to job satisfaction in EFL contexts. Addressing this gap, the present study examined the direct effect of mindful teaching on job satisfaction and investigated the mediating role of teacher self-efficacy in this relationship. The participants consisted of 321 EFL instructors working in English-language preparatory programs in higher education in Türkiye. Data were collected using the Mindfulness in Teaching Scale, the Teacher Self-Efficacy Scale, and the Job Satisfaction Index. The findings revealed a statistically significant positive relationship between mindful teaching and job satisfaction. Teacher self-efficacy was also found to partially mediate this relationship, indicating that mindful teaching contributes to job satisfaction both directly and indirectly through stronger efficacy beliefs. These findings identify self-efficacy as an important psychological mechanism underlying the relationship between mindful teaching and job satisfaction. The study extends current understanding of teacher well-being in EFL higher education by providing empirical support for a mediation model linking mindful teaching, self-efficacy, and job satisfaction. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .

title: Adaptive fusion heterogeneous graph attention network for detecting review spammer groups
abstract: Detecting review spammer groups is important because coordinated fraudulent reviewers can jointly manipulate product reputation at a scale that single-review spam detectors often miss. In heterogeneous review graphs, the core challenge is to learn node representations that simultaneously characterize individual-level behavioral abnormality and group-level coordination, and then use them to detect review spammer groups. Existing methods often underemphasize spam-indicative embedding dimensions, combine local behavioral and global structural evidence with a fixed fusion rule, or generate candidate groups from topology alone. We therefore propose AFHGAN, which uses FFAA to recalibrate informative dimensions and adaptively combine local and global evidence, and S-Louvain to jointly consider structural cohesion and embedding similarity during candidate-group construction. On three benchmark datasets, AFHGAN achieves the best P@1000, R@1000, and F1@1000 under the adopted protocol. Relative to original Louvain, S-Louvain improves F1@1000 by 10.8 %, 8.5 %, and 40.0 % on Amazon, YelpChi, and Yelp_four, respectively. These results support the value of retaining behavioral semantics in candidate-group construction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Digital Literacy of English Language Teachers in EFL Contexts: The Necessity of Teachers’ Development in the Digital World
abstract: Digital technologies have significantly reshaped the landscape of language education, influencing both pedagogical practices and teacher professional development. This review article investigates the role of English language teachers’ digital literacy in enhancing teaching efficiency by synthesizing findings from recent empirical and theoretical studies. Drawing on a comprehensive analysis of peer-reviewed journal articles, books, and academic reports published over the past decade, the review explores how digital competence contributes to instructional effectiveness, classroom engagement, and ongoing teacher growth. The literature was systematically selected based on relevance, publication quality, and thematic focus on digital literacy and language education. The synthesis reveals that teachers with higher digital literacy are better equipped to integrate educational technologies, adapt to dynamic learning environments, and foster more interactive and learner-centered classrooms. The review highlights the growing importance of digital skills in teacher development and calls for structured digital literacy training in language teacher education programs. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .

title: A sight for restored minds: examining the impact of nature image exposure on perceived restorativeness and healthy food choices
abstract: Nature exposure (including through images) offers physical and psychological benefits, including cognitive restoration. Growing evidence suggests it may also promote healthy food choices, though the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This pre-registered study examined whether perceived restorativeness (the perceived capacity of an environment for cognitive restoration) mediates the effect of nature image exposure on healthy food choices. Fruit and vegetable (FV) desirability was also examined as an alternative outcome. A total of 925 adults (M age = 39.46 y, SD = 15.67, 54.3% female) participated in an online between-subjects experiment and were exposed to a natural or urban image for 30 s. They then completed a food choice task – selecting a main course, side dish and drink (each from four options; two healthy, two unhealthy), followed by perceived restorativeness and FV desirability measures. There was a significant main effect of healthiness on the likelihood of choice (OR = 1.77, p < .001) and a significant healthiness × image exposure interaction (OR = 1.40, p < .001), indicating that healthy food choices were more likely following nature (vs. urban) image exposure. Additionally, nature (vs. urban) image exposure had a significant indirect effect on healthy food choices through perceived restorativeness (ACME = 0.04, p = .022). However, nature (vs. urban) image exposure did not significantly affect FV desirability (p = .087, d = 0.11). These findings suggest that nature image exposure can promote healthy food choices (though not FV desirability), an effect explained by enhanced perceived restorativeness. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: A learning-based robust framework for chest X-ray pneumonia classification: Privacy-preserving deep learning with adversarial training
abstract: Chest X-ray classifiers must protect patient data without sacrificing diagnostic utility or robustness to adversarial perturbations. We propose a multi-objective framework that integrates differential privacy with adversarial training through sample-adaptive gradient clipping, dynamic privacy-budget allocation, and structure-aware adversarial sample generation. Experiments on ChestX-ray14 and the COVID-19 Radiography Database evaluate clean accuracy, adversarial accuracy, and resistance to membership inference attacks. At a privacy budget of ε=1.0, the proposed method achieves 87.3% clean accuracy, 65.1% adversarial accuracy, and a membership inference attack success rate of 54.1%. Ablation results show that each adaptive component contributes to the observed privacy–utility–robustness trade-off. An exploratory diabetic-retinopathy experiment further examines transfer to a different imaging modality. © 2026

title: Why identity matters for development
abstract: This paper argues that while development economics has moved beyond income-based metrics toward a broader capabilities framework, it remains insufficiently attentive to the role of social identity in shaping life chances. Identities such as caste, race, gender, and ethnicity structure access to resources, opportunities, and power in ways that conventional and multidimensional indices fail to capture. Drawing on evidence from global gender disparities and caste-based inequalities in India, the paper demonstrates how identity-blind policies risk reinforcing structural hierarchies. It concludes by advocating an identity-conscious development framework that centres historical injustice, targeted interventions, and inclusive governance to advance equitable development. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Does AI encourage lax thinking, or does the human preference for validation make it that way?
abstract: We offer a different perspective on whether AI encourages lax human thought. Specifically, we propose an “enjoyment-engagement tradeoff”: the type of chatbot that people most enjoy interacting with may be the type that encourages less cognitive engagement. We examined this possibility in the context of chatbot congeniality, expecting that people would prefer interacting with a congenial chatbot (one that consistently validates their views) over an uncongenial chatbot (one that consistently challenges their views); furthermore, we expected that people would show greater signs of enjoyment when interacting with a congenial chatbot but would show greater signs of cognitive engagement when interacting with an uncongenial chatbot. We tested this idea in an experiment wherein participants (N = 438) interacted with either a congenial chatbot, an uncongenial chatbot, or a default-model baseline chatbot that exhibited the default behavior of a popular AI chatbot. Results, based on self-reports and linguistic analyses of conversation transcripts, suggested that participants who interacted with the congenial (vs. uncongenial) chatbot showed greater attraction toward the chatbot (e.g., desire to interact again) along with signs of greater enjoyment (e.g., more positive affect) while participants who interacted with the uncongenial (vs. congenial) chatbot exhibited various signs of greater cognitive engagement (e.g., enhanced perceived learning, higher word counts). The default-model baseline chatbot closely resembled the congenial chatbot in its effects on attraction, enjoyment, and cognitive engagement. Findings suggest a novel perspective on whether AI chatbots encourage lax human thought: People's preference for congenial (vs. uncongenial) chatbots may, ultimately, undermine cognitive engagement. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Multi‑objective optimisation and experimental validation of a compact energy‑efficient active regeneration burner for diesel particulate filter regeneration
abstract: Active regeneration burners are essential for diesel particulate filter (DPF) regeneration. However, they are often constrained by low flow utilisation, excessive gas velocity, and inadequate mixing between combustion products and exhaust gas, leading to poor thermal efficiency and degraded regeneration performance. To tackle these challenges, this study focused on achieving a compact and lightweight burner design via iterative and dimensional optimisation. A multi‑objective optimisation framework incorporating Response Surface Methodology (RSM), Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III), and Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) was then established to enhance the combustion performance. The effectiveness of this optimisation approach was verified through regeneration experiments. The optimised design reduced burner volume and mass by 57.7 % and 39.5 %, respectively, while maintaining outlet velocity uniformity above 97 % across three investigated exhaust-flow conditions. Outlet temperature uniformity increased from 82.8 % to 92.2 %, the maximum measured outlet temperature at the five-point thermocouple plane increased from 865 °C to 970 °C, and thermal efficiency increased from 38.8 % to 51.1 %. The time required for the DPF upstream temperature to reach 600 °C decreased from 200 s to 172 s, while the regeneration efficiency increased from 92 % to 94 %. Smoke opacity, HC, and CO decreased from 3.9 % to 3.1 %, 28 ppm to 8 ppm, and 0.205 vol% to 0.100 vol%, respectively; however, NOx increased from 104.5 ppm to 117.0 ppm, indicating a trade-off between oxidation completeness and NOx formation. These results demonstrate the practical potential of the burner for compact and energy-efficient diesel aftertreatment systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Graphitic-shell-mediated interfacial bonding and MWCNT-enabled electrical percolation in superhard cBN composites
abstract: Conductive superhard cubic boron nitride(cBN)-based composites are difficult to realize because conductive additives often weaken the covalent load-bearing framework. Here, we demonstrate a graphitic-shell-mediated interface/network strategy for integrating electrical transport with superhardness in cBN composites synthesized by high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) sintering at 5 GPa and 1400 °C. Surface-graphitized nanodiamonds and multi-walled carbon nanotubes were incorporated into a polycrystalline cubic boron nitride (PcBN) matrix to couple robust cBN/diamond load bearing with carbon-network conduction. The optimized composite exhibits a Vickers hardness of 40.8 GPa, and an electrical conductivity of 1.33 × 104 S m−1, with rapid net mass loss observed near 1331 °C in air under the present thermogravimetric analysis conditions. Microstructural, Raman, and transport analyses reveal strongly bonded cBN/diamond interfaces and multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)-connected carbon-rich pathways. This interfacial/network architecture partially decouples mechanical and electrical functions, offering a practical route to overcome the hardness–conductivity trade-off in cBN-based superhard ceramic composites. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: From the couch to the arena: Prefrontal cortex network dynamics of reward and loss processing during gameplay across internet gaming disorder symptom severity
abstract: This study employed functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) to investigate how gameplay contexts differing in sense of agency are associated with prefrontal cortex (PFC) network dynamics during reward and loss processing, and how these dynamics relate to Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD) symptom severity. Eighty-four college students participated in the experiment. Data-driven clustering identified three recurrent PFC connectivity states across active gameplay (higher-agency) and passive viewing (lower-agency) conditions. Compared with passive viewing, active gameplay recruited the high connectivity state more frequently during both reward and loss processing. Furthermore, IGD symptom severity was associated with context-dependent changes in the occurrence probability and network topology of PFC network states during reward and loss processing, with differential patterns emerging across gameplay conditions differing in agency. These findings indicate that agency-related gameplay contexts are associated with distinct patterns of PFC network organization during reward and loss processing, whereas IGD symptom severity is associated with context-dependent network organization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Cognitive forecasting: How intuitive theories of attention shape anticipated risk preferences
abstract: How do people forecast their own and others' risk preferences? Although it is well established that affective forecasts shape decision-making, less is known about where these forecasts come from. Five studies demonstrate that people rely on intuitive theories of attention when forecasting future affect—such as dread and savoring while waiting for a risk to be resolved—with these affective forecasts in turn shaping willingness to take such risks. In Study 1, forecasts of the participant's own expectations and attention were systematically related to forecasts of positive and negative affect during a waiting period, which in turn predicted risk preferences. Studies 2a and 2b demonstrate substantial heterogeneity in intuitive attention–affect theories: some participants believed attention amplifies the emotional consequences of expectations, whereas others believed attention is uniformly affectively negative. These differences led to sharply divergent predictions about when attention should increase or decrease risk-taking. Study 3 shows that attention is also informative about expectations: participants differed in whether they believed attention signals optimism or pessimism, producing downstream consequences for affective forecasts and risk-taking. Finally, Study 4 reveals that many people endorse asymmetric causal models, viewing optimism as a cause of risk-taking, but risk-taking as a cause of attention. Together, these findings show that forecasts of risk preferences depend critically on people's intuitive theories about how cognition shapes affect and how affective utility is generated over time. By integrating affective forecasting, attention, and decision-making under uncertainty, this work highlights the role of metacognitive beliefs in shaping economic preferences. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Defisherization: The political ecology of small-scale fisheries decline in Indonesia
abstract: In many coastal areas, the decline of small-scale fisheries is a daily reality for fishers. However, it is still framed as a technical issue, leaving unaddressed the power relations in marine governance that gradually erode fishers' livelihoods. This article develops the concept of defisherization to analyze how conservation-oriented coastal governance and ecological pressures cumulatively erode the livelihoods of small-scale fishers. Based on research in fishing communities along the coast of Buton, Southeast Sulawesi, the study employs observation, in-depth interviews (including a structured household questionnaire), and focus group discussions to examine the dynamics of this transformation. The findings suggest that defisherization occurs through the interplay of four main mechanisms: the narrowing of fishing spaces through permanent conservation zones; ecological pressures that drive household adaptation strategies without fully exiting the fisheries sector; symbolic persistence without adequate material reproduction; and the cumulative interaction between the three that gradually consolidates fisheries as a cultural identity but increasingly marginalizes it as a livelihood. This article offers defisherization as an analytical lens to move beyond explanations that view the decline of small-scale fisheries as an unintended consequence of conservation or environmental crises, demonstrating that environmental governance is vulnerable to undermining the material foundations of livelihoods. In this context, successful ecosystem protection often comes at the cost of compromising the sustainability of small-scale fishers' livelihoods. By offering an analytical lens to understand fisheries decline as a cumulative political-ecological process, this study emphasizes the importance of linking conservation agendas to the sustainable social reproduction of coastal communities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: From clinician to coach: Immediate learning and experiences of mental health nurses following a coaching for clinical nurses (C4CN) workshop
abstract: Background: Coaching is increasingly used to strengthen nursing leadership and reflective practice, yet limited evidence describes how workplace coaches are prepared or how coaching education supports capability and role clarity in healthcare environments. Aim: To explore mental health nurses' experiences of a Coaching for Clinical Nurses (C4CN) workshop and examine immediate learning in developing workplace coaching capability and emerging coach role. Design: Exploratory qualitative analysis of a preparatory workshop within a constructivist embedded case study. Methods: The two-day workshop was delivered to 13 clinical leaders working in a single adult inpatient mental health unit in Queensland, Australia, in preparation for a six-month workplace coaching intervention. Workshop material included written reflections and group discussions, anonymous real-time responses and facilitator reflective session notes. Inductive reflexive thematic analysis was used to examine immediate learning and understandings of workplace coaching. Results: Four themes captured participants' learning: personal and leadership commitment to coaching; integration of coaching into daily routines; practical application of coaching; and self-development and confidence building. Subthemes reflected an emerging coaching mindset, coaching in the moment, structured coaching processes, developing coach identity and role clarity, and self-reflection and self-management. Participants described clearer coaching purpose and boundaries and growing confidence in coaching conversations. Experiential practice, peer dialogue and structured frameworks supported movement from technique towards a developmental leadership approach. Implications for nurse education: Workplace coach preparation should combine experiential skills development, reflective learning, role-boundary clarification and opportunities to practise coaching. Continuing development and organisational support are important for translation into practice. Conclusions: The C4CN workshop showed how experienced mental health nurses began developing workplace coaching capability and making sense of their coach role alongside other nursing and leadership responsibilities. The findings support workplace coach preparation as an experiential, reflective developmental process and provide a foundation for subsequent examination within the broader case study. © 2026 The Authors

title: Toward a greater understanding of profound and complex experiences during engagement with art
abstract: This review focuses on two contemporary trends in the psychology of art. The first is a shift in research focus from hedonically based judgments of art, such as liking, preference, and beauty, toward more complex and profound outcomes of art engagement, such as experiencing self-transcendent emotions, experiencing a greater sense of meaning in life, and sensing personal transformation (awe, absorption, and being inspired and moved). The second trend involves new approaches to characterizing and conceptualizing art engagement. Examples include network analysis and latent profile analysis that help reveal the hidden and multidimensional nature of the aesthetic experience of art. Together, these trends suggest a shift toward understanding of art engagement as a multidimensional experience that can shape cognition, emotions, and the self. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Two automatic motivations, two control systems: A neuroscience framework for negotiation
abstract: Negotiation often involves a recurring tension between self-interest and social preferences such as fairness, trust, honesty, and reciprocity. A central debate concerns which motive, self-interest or social preferences, constitutes the automatic default and which requires cognitive control to be expressed. Understanding these automatic processes is important because negotiations often tax cognitive resources, increasing reliance on automatic responses. Yet, the evidence remains contradictory: in some contexts, self-interest appears spontaneous and social concern effortful, whereas in others the reverse holds. This review argues that the inconsistency stems from a flawed premise. Drawing on converging evidence from social, affective, and decision neuroscience, I propose that both self-interest and social preferences are automatic motivational processes, driven by distinct motivational systems and regulated by separate prefrontal control mechanisms. The right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (rDLPFC) is proposed to regulate reward-seeking motivation, facilitating prosocial behavior such as fairness and reciprocity, whereas the right ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (rVLPFC) is proposed to regulate socio-emotional responses, facilitating self-interested choice, together forming a proposed double dissociation within this motivational conflict. This dual-control framework reframes the central question from which motive is automatic to which automatic motivational system dominates a given context. It reconciles conflicting findings and explains why subtle situational shifts can reverse the apparent automatic response. The review considers emerging hormonal, neuromodulation, and hyperscanning evidence from dynamic interactions and discusses how changing circumstances may alter not only which motivation dominates, but also which form of control is needed to act in accordance with one's goals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Graph-informed learning of interpretable interaction dynamics in collective motion
abstract: Inferring interaction mechanisms from collective-motion trajectories is challenging because effective interaction partners are typically unobserved, and motion updates arise from the coupled effects of neighbor selection and response rules. We propose Graph-informed Learning of Interaction Dynamics (GILD), an interpretable framework for homogeneous collective-motion systems. GILD jointly learns a state-dependent neighbor selector and a physically structured response rule through closed-loop rollout training. We evaluate GILD on six simulated collective-motion systems with diverse neighbor-selection mechanisms, response rules, and motion constraints. Across these systems, GILD achieves strong closed-loop prediction performance and reproduces the main trajectory-level and group-level behaviors of the simulated dynamics. Post-hoc analyses show that the learned selector weights are broadly consistent with rule-defined neighbor-selection mechanisms, and that the learned response modules can be distilled into compact symbolic expressions capturing the dominant functional structures of the underlying dynamics. Ablation experiments support the effectiveness of the main components of GILD. Experiments with response-noise perturbations further reveal model-dependent robustness and sensitivity under noisy trajectory generation. These results suggest that GILD provides a predictive and interpretable route for modeling collective-motion dynamics when interaction mechanisms are not directly observable. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Hierarchical contrastive learning for multi-modal representation in Alzheimer's disease diagnosis
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis increasingly relies on the integration of multi-modal data, including structural magnetic resonance imaging, positron emission tomography and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers. However, existing methods often inadequately explore the discriminative information within each modality and fail to fully capture complementary interactions between modalities. In this paper, we propose a hierarchical contrastive learning method which can fully utilize the intra-modal and inter-modal information, guiding the model to learn a well-structured feature space to improve the performance of diagnosis. Specifically, our method first introduces intra-modal alignment, which enforces supervised contrastive constraints within each modality, thereby effectively exploiting discriminative information between different clinically diagnosed groups. Secondly, we innovatively propose a clinical label-guided inter-modal alignment method to exploit the complementary interactions between modalities, leading to more discriminative and coherent representations. Furthermore, a dynamic learning strategy is employed between the intra-modal and inter-modal alignments to ensure the stability of the training process and achieve the comprehensive hierarchical contrastive learning. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches, validating its efficiency in learning discriminative multi-modal representations for AD related diagnosis. The source code is available at https://github.com/qizhiJing/HSCL. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Maternal diet and offspring ASD and ADHD: A critical narrative review of dietary patterns, choline, and polyphenol-related exposures
abstract: Maternal diet may influence fetal neurodevelopment through nutrient availability, placental function, and maternal–fetal metabolite signaling. This critical narrative review used a structured, purposive search to organize human evidence on prenatal dietary patterns, choline, and polyphenol-related exposures according to outcome directness: diagnosed autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), related dimensional traits, and general neurodevelopment. Whole-diet studies provide the most direct human evidence, but diagnostic findings are cohort-dependent and vulnerable to residual familial and genetic confounding. Choline trials and cohorts mainly address attention-related traits or general cognition; they do not establish prevention of diagnosed ASD or ADHD. Polyphenol evidence is limited to food proxies and one trimester-specific cohort of estimated intake, without diagnostic or biomarker-based studies. Preclinical data support biological plausibility—particularly for choline in BTBR, maternal immune-activation/CHRNA7, and Ts65Dn models and for resveratrol in valproate-exposed rodents—but remain model-specific. The evidence is therefore best treated as an organizing framework rather than a confirmed causal hypothesis. Clinical translation should prioritize achieving recommended dietary adequacy and balanced dietary patterns; evidence does not support high-dose single-nutrient or concentrated-polyphenol supplementation for ASD/ADHD prevention. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
