title: Neuroendocrine and circuit remodeling under chronic social stress
abstract: Social stress has emerged as one of the most impactful environmental risk factors contributing to psychiatric disorders in modern societies. Although acute stress responses are adaptive mechanisms that promote survival and homeostasis, chronic social stress induces maladaptive neurobiological changes that culminate in pathological behavioral phenotypes. Accumulating evidence from rodent studies demonstrates that chronic social stress reshapes neural circuits and disrupts neuroendocrine regulation. In this review, we summarize and compare major rodent models including early life stress, social isolation, chronic social defeat stress, and chronic subordinate colony housing, and synthesize how these paradigms differentially engage the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis and monoaminergic systems, including serotonergic, noradrenergic, and dopaminergic circuits, as well as emerging modulators such as endocannabinoids and neuropeptide Y. Because these paradigms engage distinct developmental windows and have been validated predominantly in males, we explicitly evaluate outcomes as a function of age at exposure and sex. We further integrate these neurochemical alterations into a synaptic and cell-type-specific framework of cortico-limbic circuit remodeling linking excitation/inhibition imbalance and astrocytic dysregulation to the divergence between susceptible and resilient phenotypes. We introduce allostatic load as an integrated framework linking cumulative, paradigm-specific stress burdens to vulnerability and resilience, and highlight active, compensatory neuroendocrine and circuit-level mechanisms that confer resilience. We propose that chronic social stress represents not a simple neurotransmitter deficit, but a dysregulation of neural circuits and neuroendocrine plasticity, providing a systems-level perspective of stress-related mental illness. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: EV-PV-capacitor integration in distribution systems with reliability-cost trade-off: A utility-prosumer perspective
abstract: This paper proposes a generalized framework for the integrated planning of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS), Photovoltaic (PV) systems, and capacitors in distribution networks using a sequential optimization strategy aligned with practical planning dependencies. The three-stage approach addresses multi-stakeholder economics and reliability–cost trade-offs. To establish the planning baseline, Stage-1,determines EVCS locations that minimize total network losses using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Stage-2 employs Multi-Objective PSO (MOPSO) to size PV systems by jointly optimizing conflicting utility and prosumer Net Present Values (NPVs), considering bill savings, export revenue, lifecycle costs, loss reduction, interruption savings, deferral benefits, FiT expenses, and PV degradation, with the optimal solution selected using Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). Stage-3 applies a similar framework to co-optimize capacitor number, size, and placement, balancing investment costs with reliability. Validation on the 33-bus system under probabilistic uncertainties in load, solar irradiance, and EV charging shows reduced losses, improved economic performance, and enhanced stability and reliability. Results demonstrate that the coordinated EV-PV-capacitor solution reduces active power losses by 59.0%, improves minimum voltage by 6.2%, and reduces SAIFI, SAIDI, and AENS by 17.9%, 20.4%, and 30.3%, respectively. Sensitivity analysis of FiT and electricity prices identifies economically favorable tariff combinations for scalable and cost-effective grid integration. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: eHealth literacy levels and associated factors among nursing students: A global systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background: The rapid digital transformation of healthcare highlights the importance of electronic health literacy (eHealth literacy) for nursing students. However, existing global evidence regarding their eHealth literacy levels and associated factors remains fragmented. Objective: To determine the overall level of e-health literacy among nursing students worldwide, analyze its associated factors and associations with health outcomes, and provide evidence-based support for nursing education reform in the digital age. Methods: A systematic search was conducted in eight Chinese and international databases, including PubMed, for cross-sectional studies published from the inception of each database through June 1, 2026. Study quality was assessed using the AHRQ scale, and random-effects meta-analyses and meta-regression analyses were performed using Stata 19.0. This systematic review protocol was registered in advance with PROSPERO (Registration No.: CRD420261418156). Results: A total of 20 cross-sectional studies involving 12,390 nursing students across 11 countries were ultimately included. The pooled eHEALS score for nursing students worldwide was29.51 (95% CI: 28.42–30.61), indicating an overall level slightly above average; however, there was extremely high heterogeneity among studies (I2 = 99.4%, P < 0.001). Senior-year students demonstrated significantly higher levels of literacy than junior-year students (SMD = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.41–0.59, P < 0.001); gender had no significant overall effect on literacy (SMD = −0.04, 95% CI: −0.35–0.27, P = 0.803). Regression analysis showed that living in an urban area (β = 4.24, P < 0.001) and having good economic conditions (β = 0.79, P < 0.001) were exploratory study-level indicators associated with higher literacy. Digital health literacy was moderately positively correlated with health-promoting behaviors (r = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.35–0.49, P < 0.001) and was significantly associated with lower levels of anxiety (OR = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.92–0.99, P = 0.006). Conclusions: Overall, the digital health literacy of nursing students worldwide is acceptable, but regional digital divides remain prominent. Systematic nursing education may help enhance digital health literacy, which is associated with more positive health behaviors and mental health outcomes. Institutions need to refine their digital health curriculum systems, focusing on cultivating students' abilities in information evaluation and AI-assisted decision-making to meet the evolving demands of digital healthcare and artificial intelligence. © 2026 The Authors

title: A multilevel framework for distinguishing psychopathy from related disorders
abstract: Although psychopathy is not a standalone diagnosis in current psychiatric classification systems, it remains widely used in forensic contexts and can have significant consequences for individuals within the legal system. Consequently, it is critical that the field be able to distinguish psychopathy from other mental disorders with over=lapping symptom presentations. This review proposes a multilevel theoretical framework for understanding how psychopathy differs from related disorders when mechanistic and dispositional factors are considered alongside behavioral symptoms. It illustrates how disorders overlapping with psychopathy at one level of analysis (e.g., chronic antisocial behavior and aggression) diverge from it at others, particularly the mechanistic level (e.g., attentional functioning, threat reactivity, empathy processing) and dispositional level (e.g., callous-unemotional traits). It further considers how contextual factors modulate whether psychopathic features are rewarded or criminalized and how this may affect their interpretation. By identifying features that distinguish psychopathy across levels of analysis, the framework clarifies what makes psychopathy a distinct construct, with implications for case formulation, treatment, and forensic assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Comparing direct and indirect measures of attitudes toward health and sustainability in the perception of organic and ancient wheat labels
abstract: Rising interest in organic and sustainable cereal-based foods necessitates clarifying how consumers' health and sustainability attitudes influence product experience. While attitudes are usually assessed through validated scales, such measures may suffer from social desirability bias, underscoring the value of complementary indirect techniques. This study investigates how consumer segmentation influences expectations and perception of organic crackers made from ancient (Verna) and modern (Altavista) wheat based on health and sustainability attitudes. Attitudes were measured through explicit scales and the indirect text highlighting (TH) method. Following a within-subjects design, one hundred and eighteen consumers evaluated the crackers under blind (only tasting), expected (only information: organic label alone vs. organic combined with the ancient wheat label), and informed conditions (tasting+information). Explicit scales identified two clusters, differing in broad general interest (high vs low) for both health and sustainability. Conversely, TH revealed a different context-specific segmentation based on information prioritization, distinguishing two groups, a health-oriented and a sustainability-oriented group. The two methods did not overlap, separating broad attitudinal traits (scales) from context-specific priorities (TH). Combined organic and ancient wheat cues generated higher expectations for liking, healthiness, sustainability, naturalness, and novelty than the organic label alone across consumer prioritizing health (TH) and both sustainability and health (attitudes) information. However, no assimilation toward expectations was found for liking, suggesting a misalignment between expectations and product experience. This research highlights the complementary value of indirect methods (TH) and underscores the need to align extrinsic cues with sensory characteristics to support more sustainable and healthier food choices. © 2026 The Authors

title: The mediating effect of nursing students' academic resilience between the clinical nursing internship environment and patient safety competency: A cross-sectional study
abstract: Background: The clinical internship environment is crucial for developing nursing students' patient safety competency. While existing studies have confirmed their direct correlation, the underlying psychological mechanism remains unclear. Academic resilience, a key psychological resource for coping with clinical challenges, may serve as an important mediator, yet its specific role lacks empirical evidence. This study aims to address this gap. Objective: To examine the mediating role of academic resilience between the clinical nursing internship environment and patient safety competency among nursing students. Methods: From February to March 2025, we used convenience sampling to recruit nursing students from two tertiary grade-A hospitals in Kaifeng, yielding 298 valid questionnaires. We collected data using a general information questionnaire, the Clinical Nursing Internship Environment Evaluation Scale, the Patient Safety Competency Scale, and the Nursing Student Academic Resilience Scale. We performed mediation analysis using the SPSS PROCESS macro. Results: We obtained survey data from 298 nursing students. The total scores for the clinical nursing internship environment evaluation, patient safety competency, and nursing student academic resilience were 94.0 (91.8, 110.0), 117.0 (114.5, 138.0), and 70.0 (68.0, 78.0), respectively, all in the medium-upper range. Correlation analysis revealed significant positive correlations among the total scores of the clinical nursing internship environment, patient safety competency, and academic resilience (r = 0.933–0.960, P < 0.01). Nursing students' clinical internship environment and academic resilience can directly and positively affect their level of patient safety competence; nursing students' academic resilience partially mediates the relationship between clinical nursing internship environment and patient safety competence, with a mediating effect of 0.368 (95% CI: 0.1789–0.5108), accounting for 49.47% of the total effect. Conclusions: Nursing students' academic resilience mediates the relationship between the clinical nursing internship environment and patient safety competence. Nursing managers should focus on improving nursing students' academic resilience and adaptability to the practice environment during clinical practice to optimize the clinical practice environment, improve nursing students' safety competence, and ensure patient safety. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Gaussian Splatting for real-time scene reconstruction: Methods, systems, and trade-offs
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) allows for high-quality real-time novel-view synthesis. Since its inception in 2023, its explicit and highly configurable scene representation has been extended toward sparse-view generation, dynamic reconstruction, efficiency and compression, streaming, and simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). Although Gaussian Splatting can provide real-time rendering, rendering an existing representation is distinct from constructing, updating, or maintaining the scene itself. In this survey, we synthesize current literature, categorize them and provide a connection of current approaches and tools towards an end-to-end pipeline. Explicitly, we categorize GS scene reconstruction into five overlapping families: single-shot generation, dynamic representations, efficiency and compression, streaming and immersive systems, and Gaussian Splatting SLAM. We distinguish render-only throughput from task-specific scene generation, update, tracking, mapping, and optimization costs, and combine controlled sparse-view benchmarking with native evaluations to identify cross-family quality, latency, memory, and update-cost trade-offs. © 2026

title: A production-ready machine learning system for inclusive employment: Requirements engineering and implementation of AI-driven disability job matching platform
abstract: Employment inclusion of people with disabilities remains critically low in Italy, with only 3.5% employed nationally despite mandatory hiring quotas. Traditional manual matching processes require 30–60 min per candidate, creating bottlenecks that limit service capacity. Our goal is to develop and validate a production-ready machine learning system for disability employment matching that integrates social responsibility requirements while maintaining human oversight in decision-making. We employed participatory requirements engineering with Centro per l'Impiego di Villafranca di Verona professionals. The system implements a seven-model ensemble with parallel hyperparameter optimization using Optuna. Multi-dimensional scoring combines semantic compatibility, geographic distance, and employment readiness assessment. The system achieves a 90.1% F1-score and sub-100 ms response times while processing 500,000 candidate–company combinations in under 10 min. Qualitative expert validation with employment center professionals suggests potential for 60%–100% capacity increases for employment centers. The LightGBM ensemble shows optimal performance with 94.6-second training time. Our findings indicate that advanced AI systems can successfully integrate social responsibility requirements without compromising technical performance. The participatory design methodology provides a replicable framework for developing ethical AI applications in sensitive social domains. The complete system, including source code, documentation, and deployment guides, is openly available to facilitate replication and adaptation by other regions and countries facing similar challenges. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Tracking fitness, comparing bodies: Social comparison and exercise activity among college students
abstract: Wearable fitness trackers are widely used by college students to monitor exercise and promote healthy habits. Previous research has predominantly identified the positive role that fitness trackers have in users' exercise behavior. Guided by Bandura's Social Cognitive Theory, this study explored both positive and negative behaviors associated with wearable fitness trackers. A total of 253 college students completed a cross-sectional survey that examined associations among exercise tracking, exercise-related social media use, social comparison, exercise-related outcomes, mental health, and disordered eating. This study found students who tracked exercise behavior reported higher levels of exercise involvement, motivation, and positive exercise outcomes. Tracking was also associated with increased upward and downward social comparison, which can be harmful for some students, particularly for those who have been treated for an eating disorder. How often students share tracked exercise behavior on social media was not significantly related to most outcomes, suggesting frequency alone may not capture its relationship to mental health. Future research should investigate the psychological effects of social comparison, the role of social media in influencing exercise behavior, and strategies to help students resist the harmful consequences of constant comparison. © 2026 The Authors

title: Sex-divergent vulnerability to chronic peripheral LPS challenge in aged ApoE4 mice: Male systemic fragility versus female central neuroinflammation
abstract: Inflammageing links chronic inflammation to biological aging, contributing to senescence and multimorbidity common in the elderly. In neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease, inflammatory processes play a causal role in accelerating neurodegeneration. Interestingly, apolipoprotein E (APOE), particularly the APOEε4 allele, is a major genetic risk factor for neurodegeneration, acting as a key immunomodulator with sex differences. This is especially relevant given the lack of clear prevention strategies for APOEε4 carriers. Therefore, this study characterized the sex-specific neuroinflammatory and cognitive vulnerability of APOE4 genotype under a chronic lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge in senescence-transition stage. Male and female homozygous apoE4 mice (15–16 months old) were administered intraperitoneal doses of 0 or 0.25 mg/kg LPS three times per week for a total of 17 doses. Body weight was monitored, and behavioural assessments were conducted from the 12th injection until the 17th. Serum and tissues were collected to assess hippocampal, cortical and systemic markers of inflammation, antioxidant-related genes, genes implied in myelin dynamics, and neurotrophin-related transcripts. Findings revealed basal sex-dependent divergent phenotypes with specific responses under LPS challenge. Under LPS treatment, males exhibited higher systemic fragility, with significantly increased mortality, which may have conditioned cognitive outcomes. Females showed greater central alterations related to neuroinflammation along with altered expression of myelin-related transcripts. However, the results suggest a stablished tolerance to LPS. These results highlight how chronic systemic inflammation during ageing in an APOE4 genotype background shapes sex-divergent pathological trajectories, underscoring the need to address sex-specific therapeutic strategies. © 2026 The Authors
label: Social Sciences

title: The perceived legitimacy of costly punishment in the evolution of cooperation under private reputation
abstract: Indirect reciprocity promotes cooperation by allowing reputation to serve as a social currency for future benefits. However, the role of costly punishment under private reputation remains less understood. Under private reputation, independent assessments may lead observers and punishers to hold different views about the same recipient. This raises the question of how an observer evaluates punishment when the punished recipient appears to have a good reputation. We introduce the perceived legitimacy of costly punishment into a private-reputation model of indirect reciprocity. We first analyze the core dynamics among unconditional cooperators, unconditional defectors, and discriminating punishers, and then test whether the cooperative state is stable against the full set of action-rule mutants, including antisocial punishers. Our results show that costly punishment promotes cooperation only when its perceived legitimacy lies within an appropriate range. In this regime, discriminating punishers and unconditional cooperators can coexist stably, producing high cooperation and social payoff. However, insufficient legitimacy prevents punishers from disciplining defectors, whereas excessive legitimacy allows strategies that punish high-reputation individuals to invade, linking the model to antisocial punishment. Finite-population Markov analyses further confirm that the main qualitative dynamics are robust to small punishment execution and assessment errors. These findings show that, under private reputation, the perceived legitimacy of costly punishment determines whether punishment sustains cooperation or facilitates antisocial punishment. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.
label: Social Sciences

title: Declining cocoa and intensifying artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM): examining changing labour structures and livelihoods in rural Ghana
abstract: Ghana’s cocoa frontier increasingly overlaps with mechanised artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM), creating competition over land and labour. This article examines how declining cocoa production and intensifying ASGM reorganise a local labour regime and reshape rural livelihood pathways in Juaboso District, Western North Region. It draws on 40 semi-structured interviews with cocoa farmers, ASGM workers and institutional actors, alongside observations at four ASGM sites, conducted in 2024. The analysis combines the Sustainable Livelihoods Framework for the 21st Century (SLF-21) with a labour-regime lens. The findings show that cocoa decline and political arrangements governing access to land, machinery, finance and licences create uneven openings for mining. Landowners and operators can convert cocoa land and capture mining rents, while young, often migrant, workers enter hazardous and insecure work. At the same time, ASGM expansion reduces labour availability for cocoa production, increases labour costs for cocoa farmers and degrades land and water used by farming households. Mining income can meet urgent household needs and, in some cases, support farming, but these gains coexist with risks that are shifted onto workers, non-mining farmers and younger generations. These risks are unevenly distributed across generations, with younger people likely to bear a greater burden through depleted land and water resources, and the health and educational consequences of mining-centred livelihood pathways. © 2026 The Authors.
label: Social Sciences

title: Gesture benefits in second language learning take time to develop
abstract: Background: Multimodal enrichment can enhance second language (L2) vocabulary learning, but most evidence comes from studies with extensive training; it is unclear whether similar benefits occur with limited exposure. Aims: This study investigated how ten brief instances of gesture- and picture-based enrichment influenced adults’ learning and long-term retention of concrete and abstract L2 vocabulary. Sample: Fifty-two German-speaking adults were recruited from teacher education programs at the University of Leipzig. Methods: Using a fully within-participants design, each learner studied abstract and concrete L2 nouns under three conditions: listening only (no enrichment), listening while viewing related pictures (picture enrichment), and listening while viewing and performing related gestures (gesture enrichment). Each word was presented ten times across five training sessions. Word learning was assessed using free recall, L1–L2 translation, L2–L1 translation tasks at three retention intervals (day 8, month 2, and month 6). Results: Both gesture and picture enrichment significantly improved learning of abstract words compared to no enrichment. For concrete words, performance did not differ across conditions. Gesture enrichment did not outperform picture enrichment at any time point. Memory performance declined over time, particularly for abstract words, while concrete word performance remained more stable. Conclusions: Even brief exposure to gestural and pictorial enrichment can enhance the long-term retention of abstract L2 vocabulary. More extensive training may be required for gesture-based benefits to exceed those of picture enrichment. The findings establish boundary conditions for multimodal learning and inform both theoretical accounts of sensorimotor enrichment and practical approaches to language instruction. © 2026
label: Social Sciences

title: Extending animal welfare labels to plant-based foods promotes animal-friendly food choices
abstract: Plant-based foods are essentially animal-friendly, yet they are rarely labelled as such. We examined whether extending animal welfare labels from only being displayed on animal-based foods, towards also being placed on plant-based products, would better integrate plant-based products into the set of options consumers consider animal-friendly. Across two studies in a simulated online supermarket, we hypothesised that extending animal welfare labels to plant-based foods would promote animal-friendly choices via increased perceptions of physical opportunity to choose animal-friendly (i.e. availability of animal-friendly foods) and social opportunity to choose animal-friendly (i.e. social norms for choosing animal-friendly foods). We show that extending animal welfare labels to plant-based foods not only promoted animal-friendly choices within the animal-based category, but also significantly increased the number of plant-based foods chosen by 28% compared to the control condition, and 33% compared to the condition in which only animal-based products were labelled. Furthermore, we show that the positive effects of extending animal welfare labels to plant-based foods persisted even when consumers were exposed to multiple sustainability messages presented through a multidimensional label, which displayed animal welfare, biodiversity, and climate scores. The studies confirmed that label effects on animal-friendly choices were driven by increases in perceived physical and social opportunity to choose animal-friendly. Extending animal welfare labels to plant-based foods is an effective strategy for encouraging animal-friendly food choices. Labels, it turns out, do more than inform: They reshape the physical and social context into a more supportive environment for plant-based choices. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Effects of treadmill exercise with and without vertical traction on gait, pain, disability, trunk proprioception, and depression in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain: A randomized controlled trial
abstract: Introduction: Treadmill exercise may improve gait and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain (CMLBP), but the additional effects of vertical traction and partial body weight support remain unclear. This study compared treadmill exercise combined with vertical traction and partial body weight support (VT+TE), treadmill exercise alone (TE), and core stabilization exercise. Methods: Forty-five patients with CMLBP were randomly assigned to VT + TE, TE, or control groups (n = 15 each). All groups received conventional physical therapy and completed 24 sessions over 8 weeks. Body weight support in the VT + TE group was reduced from 50% to 30%. The TE group performed pain-tolerable treadmill walking, whereas controls performed self-directed core stabilization exercises. Outcomes included Timed Up and Go (TUG) performance, self-selected and fast gait speeds, pain intensity, pressure pain threshold, disability, trunk repositioning error, and depressive symptoms. Assessments were conducted at baseline, post-intervention, and 4-week follow-up. Results: Significant time-by-group interactions occurred for all outcomes. Both treadmill groups showed greater improvements than controls in TUG performance, self-selected gait speed, pain intensity, and depressive symptoms. Compared with TE, VT + TE produced greater improvements in TUG performance, self-selected gait speed, disability, and flexion and extension repositioning errors. VT + TE also improved fast gait speed more than both comparison groups at post-intervention. Improvements in pain intensity and depressive symptoms were maintained at follow-up in both treadmill groups. Conclusions: Adding vertical traction and partial body weight support to treadmill exercise may provide additional benefits for gait performance, disability, and trunk repositioning accuracy in patients with CMLBP. Interpretation is limited by the small sample size and the inability to distinguish the effects of vertical unloading from those of harness support. © 2026

title: Fatigue crack growth behavior of additively manufactured aluminum alloys: A comparative investigation
abstract: This study investigates the fatigue crack growth (FCG) behavior of three aluminum alloys, namely AlSi10Mg, QuesTek Al, and Scalmalloy, using compact tension specimens fabricated via laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF). Among these, AlSi10Mg specimens are manufactured with two feedstocks from different suppliers. The materials exhibit different fracture surface roughnesses due to variations in their microstructures which correlated with threshold stress intensity factor range, ΔKth . Scalmalloy exhibited the highest ΔKth , followed by QuesTek Al, with both AlSi10Mg materials being comparable but the lowest. Vertical specimens had higher ΔKth values (except Scalmalloy), while higher R resulted in lower ΔKth due to reduced crack closure effects. Stable crack growth behavior was comparable among both AlSi10Mg materials and Scalmalloy although their microstructures were different. However, QuesTek Al had significantly higher FCG rates due to its limited ductility. In the unstable region, the maximum stress intensity factor at failure, Kmax,failure correlated broadly with ductility obtained from tensile tests. Scalmalloy exhibited the highest Kmax,failure whereas QuesTek Al exhibited the lowest due to its limited plastic deformation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Obsessive compulsive disorder and depression change in a residential setting with the added role of quality of life
abstract: Co-occurring depression is a common aspect of obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) presentation, however, there are mixed conclusions on how depression influences treatment outcomes. Many studies lack accounting for temporal precedence, and do not account for both within person and between-person effects. This study utilizes a random-intercept cross-lagged panel model to examine changes in OCD and depression over the course of intensive/residential treatment for OCD in a sample of 311 adults. We build on past research by including quality of life in the model as well. Autoregressive paths reflected OCD symptoms predicting future OCD symptoms across time, and depression symptoms predicting future depression symptoms in the context of treatment. Contrary to past research on OCD and depression, there were no significant cross-lagged effects in either model except for a positive relationship between quality of life at week 1 and OCD at week 2. Limitations include constraints on generalizability given the unique nature of the study sample and patient population from which it is drawn. Future studies examining the nature of the relationship between OCD and depression with newer statistical models, examining other constructs involved in the OCD and depression relationship, and utilizing holistic and recovery-focused outcome measures are indicated based on these findings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Experiencing expanded minds in higher education: Critical thinking–based discussion sessions in the context of Hannah Arendt’s political thought
abstract: The uncertainties and multidimensional crises faced by today’s society also shape the civic qualities individuals should possess. Critical thinking skills, along with their public qualities, are the civic skills required by today’s society. There is limited educational sciences research on Hannah Arendt’s treatment of thinking as political action with moral responsibilities. This case study examined argument-based discussion sessions held by university students regarding Turkey’s social problems, based on Hannah Arendt’s understanding of citizenship. The analysis covered six argument-based discussion sessions on Turkey’s social problems, a discussion session based on general evaluations, written evaluation forms, and individual interviews. Participants included 44 teacher candidates enrolled in the education faculty of a university in Central Anatolia. Data collection was conducted during the researcher’s Critical and Analytical Thinking course. The findings suggested that discussions based on critical thinking had transformed into a pluralistic forum by creating a public context where individuals could express their uniqueness through words and actions. In the discussions, students—within their experience of political existence—tried to form ideas while expressing their individual identities and also being nourished and tested by the views of others. Plurality-based interaction supported establishing connections and clarifying personal opinions. The effort to understand different ideas entailed visiting the mind of another and thinking with an expanded mindset. Participating in discussions as a listener also provided important gains. The students who listened used their metacognitive thinking skills throughout the whole research process. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Connectivity in Written Personal and Fictional Narratives: The Study of Iranian EFL Learners and Native Speakers of Persian and English
abstract: The present study aimed to examine the use of different levels of syntactic architecture in written personal and fictional narratives in both Persian and English across three discourse communities, namely Persian native speakers, English native speakers, and Iranian EFL learners. To this end, the participants of the study were selected based on convenience sampling and were asked to write one of their happiest memories. Also, an English fable from Aseop's fables and a Persian story, chosen based on comparative literature and having the similar plot, were given to them to read and write whatever they remembered; there was no limit on the number of words and paragraphs. To analyze the data, the Berman and Nir-Sagiv's (2009) model was followed. The findings showed that in fictional narratives written by both Persian and English native speakers, isotaxis, asymmetric parataxis, complement (CMP), and parataxis levels were frequently employed; however, personal narratives in Persian were dominantly isotactic, paratactic, and asymmetric paratactic, CMP, while isotactic, hypotactic, and paratactic levels were frequent in English written personal narratives. Also, after receiving explicit instruction on different types of English sentences, the use of adverbial and relative clauses (hypotaxis level) increased in Iranian EFL learners' written narratives. It can be concluded that explicit teaching of syntactic levels enabled EFL learners to arrange their sentences correctly to express their intended meaning. Teachers can benefit from the results to gain a more comprehensive understanding of narrative connectivity and help EFL learners elaborate clause linkage in their written narrative tasks. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .

title: Modern artisanal gold mining practices and livelihood dynamics in Shurugwi, Zimbabwe
abstract: Artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM) is increasingly central to rural livelihoods in Zimbabwe amid unemployment and declining agricultural viability driven by climate change. However, in a context characterised by uneven access to technology, capital, and contested resource governance, ASGM assumes a socially differentiated and politically contested character with far-reaching implications for livelihood trajectories. Drawing on qualitative data from interviews, focus group discussions, and archaeological surface survey walks in Shurugwi, Zimbabwe, this article analyses how everyday mining practices, technological adoption, and socio-political relations shape livelihood dynamics. Using a historical materialist lens, the study shows that differential access to processing technologies and means of production structures participation and reward within the mining economy. Informal arrangements function as adaptive governance mechanisms regulating access to labour, markets, and claims amid regulatory ambiguity. Overall, ASGM emerges as a contradictory livelihood system that simultaneously enables accumulation, survival, and precarity, underscoring livelihoods as contested processes embedded in evolving socio-technical and political relations of production. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Thermal-hydraulic assessment of microencapsulated phase change material slurry for natural-circulation loops
abstract: Natural-circulation is widely used in passive heat-removal systems for nuclear reactors. Microencapsulated phase change material (mPCM) slurry is a potential working fluid because it can couple latent heat storage with phase-change-induced density variation. However, the viscosity increase at higher mPCM concentrations may raise flow resistance and offset the heat-transfer benefit. To evaluate this trade-off, a calibrated plateau-viscosity correlation accounting for temperature and concentration effects was incorporated into a one-dimensional steady-state natural-circulation loop (NCL) program, termed NCLS1. The single-phase natural-circulation solver was verified against pure-water experimental data and the Vijayan correlation. The effects of mPCM concentration, heating power, loop height, and pipe diameter were evaluated using NCLS1. The results show that mPCM slurry does not always improve natural-circulation heat transfer. Cooling benefit appears only when a phase-change circulation is established, allowing the slurry to melt in the heater and solidify in the cooler. Under the investigated conditions, the favorable operating region occurred at heating powers of 10–20 W and mPCM mass concentrations of 5–10 wt%, where latent heat enhancement balanced viscosity-induced flow resistance. Increasing loop height broadened this region, whereas pipe diameter required careful selection to avoid boiling and low-shear conditions. These findings clarify the coupled effects of latent heat, buoyancy, and viscosity in mPCM slurry loops and provide guidance for evaluating candidate working fluids in passive nuclear heat-removal systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Adaptive stewardship of understanding: Artificial intelligence and intergenerational governance in mining
abstract: Mining stewardship has traditionally focused on the governance of physical assets, operational performance, environmental impacts, and organizational decision-making. While these responsibilities remain essential, they assume that the understanding supporting stewardship is comparatively stable. In reality, understanding continually evolves as new observations emerge, assumptions are revised, stakeholders change, institutions adapt, and stewardship extends across increasingly long temporal horizons. Artificial intelligence further transforms this process by participating in how observations are integrated, interpretations are developed, assumptions are reinforced or challenged, and institutional knowledge is preserved and communicated. Stewardship must therefore address not only what decisions are made, but also how understanding itself is created, maintained, questioned, and renewed. This paper proposes adaptive stewardship as a framework for governing an evolving ecology of understanding throughout the mine life cycle and beyond closure. The framework distinguishes understanding from observation, examines the lifecycle of assumptions, introduces the concepts of time windows of understanding and observation boundaries, and argues that governance must preserve the conditions under which understanding can continue to improve across generations. Within this ecology, artificial intelligence is treated not as an autonomous decision-maker but as an evolving participant whose value depends upon transparent governance that maintains visibility of assumptions, uncertainty, evidence, and human judgment. The paper concludes that the long-term objective of stewardship is not to preserve today's knowledge, but to preserve society's continuing capacity to develop better understanding as mining systems, environmental conditions, technologies, institutions, and societal expectations evolve. title: Message scrutiny and claim verification: Changes in preadolescent reasoning about disinformation across AI-supported instruction
abstract: Digital information environments expose preadolescents to misleading content before verification routines are fully developed. This study examined pre–post patterns in disinformation evaluation across a two-session instructional sequence combining media-literacy orientation, guided news-analysis activities, researcher supervision, and interaction with Pimpoyo, a generative-AI chatbot using Socratic questioning and a ZPD-inspired rationale. The sample comprised 152 Spanish students aged 10–14 years. Longitudinal evidence came only from the pre–post group ( n = 80); a baseline-only reference group ( n = 72) contributed baseline information. The primary outcome comprised 24 measurement-equivalent indicators expressed on a 0–25 scale. Indicator-level changes were differentiated: the clearest increases clustered around cues available within the focal message, including sensationalism, alarmist format, writing quality, tone/style, and timeliness, whereas triangulation/lateral reading did not change reliably and externally oriented verification remained mixed. The overall composite increased from M = 11.90 to M = 15.90, t (79) = 6.18, p < .001, d_z = 0.69. These indicator-level patterns are exploratory and are not formal comparisons between psychometric reasoning domains. Self-perceived competence changed, whereas perceived task difficulty did not; these secondary findings do not demonstrate metacognitive recalibration. Because only one group was followed longitudinally and the sequence bundled several instructional components, observed changes cannot be attributed specifically to AI, Socratic prompting, or any single component. The findings identify a potentially important distinction between focal-message scrutiny and external verification for future controlled research. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Multi-fidelity methods for kinetic models of epidemic dynamics with uncertain contact structure
abstract: In this work, we develop a multi-fidelity strategy for kinetic models in epidemiology with uncertain contact dynamics. Assessing and controlling the population-level effects of contact dynamics requires the development of models for understanding observable effects of heterogeneous contact structures, whose formation depends on complex social phenomena. These can be captured taking into account high-dimensional uncertain quantities. The proposed approach combines high-fidelity kinetic solvers with a hierarchy of low-fidelity surrogates, including reduced macroscopic models and coarse kinetic descriptions, remaining applicable even in regimes where a macroscopic closure is unavailable. This hierarchical framework identifies representative parameter samples and reconstructs full solutions via projection-based techniques, enabling efficient uncertainty propagation while drastically reducing computational cost. Numerical experiments in high-dimensional stochastic settings demonstrate that accurate statistical estimates of epidemic observables can be obtained with significantly reduced computational costs compared to standard approaches. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: How social status shapes U.S. children’s beliefs about social mobility
abstract: Children grow up within social hierarchies that shape their everyday lives. Social mobility is a core mechanism through which societies either challenge or maintain existing inequalities. The present study examined how U.S. children’s social status—both experimentally manipulated and measured at the neighborhood level—shapes their beliefs about social mobility for themselves and their high- and low-status peers. Children ( N = 130; 3–8 years; 70 girls, 59 boys, 1 non-binary; 12.3% Asian, 6.9% Black, 11.6% Latine, 20.7% Multiracial, and 48.5% White) were randomly assigned to either experimentally advantaged or disadvantaged groups. They were then assessed on their (1) general expectations about social mobility, (2) effort-contingent expectations for mobility, and (3) post-hoc explanations for upward and downward mobility. We found that compared to experimentally-disadvantaged children, experimentally-advantaged children were more likely to have higher expectations for themselves and high-status peers, but lower expectations for low-status peers. With age, disadvantaged children (experimental and neighborhood) exhibited higher expectations for themselves and lower expectations for high-status peers, whereas advantaged children’s expectations remained stable. Older children were more likely to believe working hard leads to upward mobility and attribute upward/downward mobility to individual effort. This tendency was especially pronounced for their own upward (vs. downward) mobility, but less so when evaluating the upward mobility of high-status peers (vs. themselves). These results suggest that children’s beliefs about social mobility develop throughout childhood, differ by target, and are shaped by their own social status. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Compromise-age malware dynamics and shared-capacity defense on directed networks
abstract: Malicious activity and remediation efficacy change as an intrusion progresses, making both network position and compromise age relevant to defense. The modeling challenge is to retain both features while keeping threshold analysis and resource allocation tractable. We formulate a host-level compromise-age partial differential equation in which preventive hardening and reactive remediation share one instantaneous capacity. The interacting host process gives an exact marginal renewal boundary, and receiver–source factorization yields the deterministic closure. We establish well-posedness and reduce threshold analysis to a finite next-generation matrix. Its spectral radius determines the strict malware-free alternatives and, on an irreducible graph, the existence of a unique positive equilibrium. Stability criteria at that equilibrium are local for general age kernels. The continuous control problem admits a minimizer and first-order necessary conditions. A conservative cohort scheme and exact discrete adjoint support the computation of stationary policies for the fixed discrete problem. Finite-host comparisons show that agreement with the closure depends on the graph, initial state, and horizon, with substantial long-horizon supercritical discrepancies. In one synthetic scenario, delayed-peak output produced 66.6% more cumulative compromise than a memoryless model matched in mean duration and lifetime output. Across 12 paired initial conditions per graph, age-structured control reduced the common objective by medians of 10.67% on the synthetic graph and 8.75% on the authentication-derived enterprise graph relative to matched-memoryless control. Consequently, the findings offer insight into where and when to intervene by linking network exposure to the remaining activity and harm of compromised hosts. title: Identification of novel skin/sweat-specific CpG sites and development of a skin/sweat identification multiplex system for forensic analysis
abstract: Identification of the biological origin of forensic stains provides critical contextual information for crime scene reconstruction and evidence interpretation. Among forensic biological materials, skin/sweat is particularly important for distinguishing intimate from social contact in sexual assault investigations. Although DNA methylation-based body fluid identification has advanced considerably, reliable CpG sites for skin remain scarce. Here, we systematically screened skin/sweat-specific CpG sites using Illumina Infinium MethylationEPIC (850 K) array data from five body fluids and developed a multiplex DNA methylation assay for forensic skin/sweat identification. Following site prioritization and assay optimization, a 10-CpG multiplex panel based on amplification refractory mutation system PCR (ARMS-PCR) was established. The assay was comprehensively validated using single-source samples, simulated degraded samples, and mixed body fluid samples representative of forensic casework. The limit of detection of the 10-CpG panel was 0.25 ng. Integration of a random forest classifier enabled robust interpretation of methylation profiles and achieved 100% accuracy in distinguishing skin/sweat-containing from non-skin/sweat samples, including degraded, mixed, and casework specimens. This study represents a promising addition to the forensic epigenetic toolbox for body fluid identification, particularly in cases involving trace or degraded skin/sweat evidence. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: A long-term time series prediction model based on dynamic-order polynomial fuzzy information granules
abstract: Navigating the big data landscape, information fusion and data mining have become essential tools for extracting meaningful insights from complex datasets, particularly in the domain of time series prediction, which is crucial for fields such as finance, power systems, and environmental studies. Traditional methods often fall short due to poor interpretability, high computational costs, and an inability to capture complex patterns. Fuzzy information granule (FIG) has emerged as a solution, but current FIGs, especially Gaussian polynomial fuzzy information granules (GPFIGs), still face challenges in accurately representing data and adapting to varying trends. To address these limitations, a novel long-term time series prediction model based on dynamic-order GPFIGs is proposed. This model combines a Savitzky-Golay filter and autocorrelation function (ACF) for time series segmentation, effectively filtering noise and identifying periodicity. Subsequently, during the construction of GPFIGs, this study proposes an FMDL polynomial order selection criterion inspired by the trade-off principle of MDL. The proposed criterion employs nonparametric entropy based on the empirical distribution of residuals to measure the fitting uncertainty and introduces a parameter-number-based penalty to quantify model complexity, thereby adaptively selecting an appropriate polynomial order for different information granules. Hierarchical clustering is integrated into the fuzzy inference system (FIS) to reduce the impact of redundant rules and improve prediction accuracy. Extensive experiments on eight datasets demonstrate the model’s superior performance, achieving lower RMSE, MAE, and SMAPE compared to advanced models. For example, on the chaotic time series dataset, the model attains an RMSE of 0.0286, MAE of 0.0224, and SMAPE of 2.72% for a prediction length of 500. These results validate the model’s effectiveness and robustness in long-term time series prediction. Detailed information about datasets and codes can be found in the open-source repository: https://github.com/flyingbirdey/DOPFIG . © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Effect of source azimuth on the perceived annoyance of domestic sounds
abstract: Although noise-induced annoyance has been extensively studied, the influence of spatial factors on annoyance perception remains underexplored. A listening experiment was conducted to assess the effect of sound source azimuth on perceived annoyance, for a variety of common domestic sounds. 54 participants graded the perceived annoyance caused by seven sound sources presented binaurally, situated at 45∘ azimuth intervals around the listener. The results indicated that in most cases, laterally placed sources caused the highest level of annoyance, and rear sources were the least annoying. A significant effect of source azimuth was identified. However, the type of sound source and acoustic condition also affected annoyance levels. Conventional psychoacoustic annoyance (PA) models are computed using omnidirectional audio signals, so although they may accurately predict the effect of sound source, they cannot account for the effect of azimuth. As a result, a binaural PA metric is suggested demonstrating the potential to predict the effects of source azimuth and acoustic condition. Following further experimentation, these findings will inform the future development of an improved PA model, that considers the spatial features of annoyance, with applications in optimisation of room acoustics and annoyance reduction. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Family specific spatial borrowing in multimodal urban reconstruction: a leave one neighborhood out study of Cincinnati
abstract: Urban spatial models often assume that nearby borrowing improves prediction across target variables, but this assumption is rarely tested across distinct urban feature families within a city. We evaluate this question on a citywide hexagonal grid of Cincinnati, Ohio (2016 cells, 60 features in 14 feature families) using multimodal masked reconstruction. We compare four models spanning linear, local nonlinear, shared-gate graph, and selective-gate graph architectures under full leave-one-neighborhood-out evaluation across 50 neighborhoods, with primary summaries for the 36 neighborhoods having at least 20 cells. Median held-out-neighborhood R2 is the primary comparison metric. Cross-neighborhood transfer is family-specific, and no single borrowing strategy dominates. Ridge performs best for street structure, indicating that some spatially regular families are best reconstructed from local linear combinations. The local nonlinear masked autoencoder (MLP-MAE) holds the highest median for most families with positive transfer, though these differences are not statistically distinguishable from the graph models, indicating that local nonlinear multimodal fusion is often sufficient. Graph-based models help most clearly for topography, while the selective-gate graph model wins many individual neighborhood comparisons for several families despite lower medians, reflecting different error profiles. Graph models also produce more neighborhood-structured representations: contextual embeddings from the selective multimodal spatial autoencoder (SMSA) recover neighborhood structure better than raw principal components or local-only embeddings. Learned gates are stable across folds and provide interpretable diagnostics of context reliance, but not a universal ranking of borrowing regimes. These results show that the appropriate spatial borrowing strategy is target-specific rather than universal. For neighborhood-scale interpolation, imputation, and urban monitoring, one spatial modeling recipe can systematically misrepresent some feature families even within the same city. © 2026 The Authors

title: Reproductive numbers and traveling fronts in models of protest dynamics with police management
abstract: Protests often spread through social networks and across cities, a phenomenon that can be modeled using reaction–diffusion systems. Building on the model in [10] , which links protest activity and social tension, we study an extended model that also includes police protest management strategies. We focus on traveling wave solutions and examine how protest activity, social tension, and police density interact to shape the spread of protests [36] . Assuming the existence of traveling fronts in parameter regimes where the system is not monotone, we derive stability conditions for these traveling fronts, extending earlier results that assumed monotonicity. Through numerical simulations, we estimate how fast protests spread and identify threshold conditions, similar to epidemiological reproduction numbers, that determine whether protests grow or fade. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: A dispatch-aware framework for resource-efficient distributed electrification: A case study of photovoltaic-battery streetlights
abstract: The rapid deployment of distributed electrification infrastructure requires assessment approaches that jointly consider operational carbon benefits, life-cycle environmental burdens, and public investment. Using photovoltaic (PV)-battery streetlights as a representative municipal application, this study develops a dispatch-aware framework integrating time-resolved PV-battery dispatch, regional load-side carbon accounting, life-cycle assessment, and public-cost evaluation. Using the observed 2024 operating year as a repeated benchmark over a nominal 20-year service life, the representative retrofit achieves an attributional operational emission reduction of 4.58 tCO₂e and retains 3.56 tCO₂e of net life-cycle abatement per streetlight. Within the modeled study set of 22 municipalities, operational emission reduction is more strongly associated with regional grid‑carbon intensity than with annual mean solar resource, with the contrast amplified by the outlying-island regions. Simplified national-average assumptions shift municipal rankings by up to 20 positions. Static 2030 and 2050 grid‑carbon stress tests retain reference dispatch and hardware over the same horizon, without forecasting grid evolution or future equipment life cycles. The results demonstrate that the environmental value of this PV–battery streetlight retrofit depends on both technology performance and the carbon intensity assigned to reduced grid purchases. The framework supports municipal screening under a common observed-year benchmark. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: The Relationship between Classroom Justice, EFL Female Students' Attitudes toward Empowerment, and Their Self-esteem
abstract: This study investigated the relationships between self-esteem, empowerment attitudes, and perceptions of classroom justice among EFL (English as a Foreign Language) learners. Relative stratified sampling was used to choose the 329 participants that make up the research sample. The Cronbach’s alpha was used to assess the reliability of questionnaire. This study used path analysis within the framework of structural equations, using a descriptive-correlational methodology, to analyse data and test research hypotheses. Software such as AMOS22 and SPSS22 were used to analyse the collected data. The results showed a significant correlation between students' perceptions of classroom justice dimensions and their feelings of empowerment and self-worth. The implications extend beyond the confines of the classroom, pointing towards a holistic approach to education that considers both the interpersonal dynamics within the learning environment and the individual empowerment of students. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .

title: Public valuation of a partial transition from large reactors to enhanced-safety small modular reactors: Evidence from South Korea
abstract: This study estimates South Korean households' willingness to pay (WTP) for a proposed partial transition from conventional large reactors to enhanced-safety small modular reactors (SMRs). The scenario maintains total capacity at 1400 MW while replacing 700 MW of conventional large-reactor capacity with SMRs. A nationwide contingent valuation survey of 1000 household heads or spouses, conducted in early 2026, employed one-and-one-half-bound dichotomous-choice questions and a spike model to accommodate zero WTP responses. Mean monthly WTP was KRW 2677 (USD 1.74) in the model without covariates and KRW 2591 (USD 1.68) in the covariate model. WTP was positively associated with household income and prior SMR knowledge and negatively associated with the presence of children. The treatment of stated zero responses materially affects the estimated welfare measure, and the high prevalence of payment-vehicle protests underscores the importance of financing design and perceived institutional responsibility. The results indicate that the proposed transition has measurable non-market value; however, the estimate reflects households’ valuation of the bundled policy scenario—including changes in reactor technology, unit scale, capacity composition, and safety-related characteristics—rather than the marginal value of passive safety or any individual SMR attribute. title: Instructional approaches and content knowledge in teaching computational thinking: A large-scale study
abstract: With the ongoing digitalization of society, educational curricula increasingly emphasize the development of learners' computational thinking. Yet, there is little consensus on how best to achieve this goal in classroom practice. This study investigates patterns in teachers' use of instructional approaches to foster computational thinking, focusing on approaches identified in the literature as effective: problem-based learning, cooperative learning, and direct instruction. Using data from the 2023 cycle of the International Computer and Information Literacy Study in Flanders, the analysis focuses on lower secondary school teachers teaching eighth-grade students. Latent profile analysis is used to identify teacher profiles. Three profiles are identified, distinguished primarily by the frequency rather than the type of instructional approaches employed. Direct instruction is most prevalent, though often combined with problem-based and cooperative learning. The study further examines the extent to which teachers' computational thinking content knowledge accounts for variation in their use of specific instructional approaches. To address this, a regression analysis is conducted. The findings reveal a significant negative association between teachers' computational thinking content knowledge and the use of problem-based and cooperative learning approaches, suggesting that teachers with higher levels of content knowledge tend to apply these approaches less frequently. No significant relationship is found between content knowledge and the use of direct instruction. Drawing on extensive large-scale data, the study offers valuable insights into teachers’ instructional approaches, underscoring the predominance of direct instruction and the nuanced role of content knowledge in shaping instructional practices. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Successful modal reasoning depends on WHAT went WHERE
abstract: Modal reasoning requires quantifying over possibilities (e.g., categorizing events as necessary, possible, and impossible). This suite of abilities matures during the preschool years, but toddlers perform better in some modal reasoning tasks than others. We propose that these mixed findings reflect a cognitive distinction: toddlers perform worse when reasoning about ambiguous locations of objects (WHERE) than when reasoning about ambiguous kinds of objects (WHAT). In Experiments 1 and 2, we directly compared these forms of ambiguity using matched tasks. Consistent with the hypothesis, toddlers performed substantially better when reasoning about ambiguous kinds than ambiguous locations. Experiment 3 revealed a similar asymmetry in language comprehension, with preschool children showing better comprehension of modal terms such as “can” and “have to” in a What-based task than in a Where-based task. Thus, modal reasoning emerges earlier than previously suggested, and diversity in results reflects differences in how kind and location information are represented and processed. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and risk factors of pulmonary tuberculosis in a high-altitude Tibetan region of China from 2018 to 2022: A Bayesian modeling analysis
abstract: Background Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health challenge in high-altitude, resource-limited regions of western China. Ganzi Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, situated on the southeastern Tibetan Plateau, consistently reports the highest TB notification rates in Sichuan Province, yet fine-scale spatial heterogeneity and localized risk factors remain underexplored. This study aimed to quantify county-level spatiotemporal dynamics of TB and identify associated contextual and individual characteristics of reported TB cases from 2018 to 2022. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of 14,768 pulmonary TB cases reported in Ganzi Prefecture from 2018 to 2022. Bayesian hierarchical spatiotemporal model incorporating structured and unstructured spatial effects, a global temporal trend, and county-specific temporal deviations was implemented using the Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA) framework. County-level covariates were evaluated within a Poisson log-linear structure, while individual characteristics associated with residence in high-risk counties among reported TB cases were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Results The average annual TB notification rates was 251.2 per 100,000 population and increased over the study period. Persistent hotspots were identified in northern areas (e.g., Seda and Shiqu), while elevated risks were also observed in southern counties (e.g., Litang). Seasonal peaks occurred in spring and early autumn. At the ecological level, ultrahigh altitude (≥3500 m; RR = 2.52), higher natural population growth (RR = 1.87), and greater urbanization (RR = 2.03) were associated with increased TB notification rates, whereas greater cropland coverage was inversely associated (RR = 0.84). Among reported TB cases, herdsmen (aOR = 1.72) and children under 14 years (aOR = 2.12) were more likely to reside in high-risk counties. Conclusions Substantial spatial heterogeneity and dynamic temporal variation in TB risk were observed across counties in Ganzi Prefecture. The findings support geographically differentiated TB control strategies and highlight the importance of addressing contextual structural vulnerabilities in high-altitude settings. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Understanding situational fear of crime in context: a virtual reality interview approach to studying victimization avoidance strategies in nocturnal urban spaces
abstract: Most research on the behavioral dimension of fear of crime captures broad avoidance habits through surveys or retrospective interviews, leaving the in-situ risk management behaviors people deploy while actually present in a threatening space largely unobserved. This study uses Virtual Reality Retrospective Thinking Aloud (VR-RTA) to access this underexplored dimension. Sixty-one participants navigated a 3D replica of nocturnal Lausanne in scenarios developed with police officers. Analysis identified two types of in-situ avoidance strategies: anticipatory scanning and route management; reactive symbolic distancing from perceived threats, modulated by personal familiarity with the area as a dispositional factor, alongside three vulnerability dimensions (self, environment, others) reflecting the core components of Routine Activity Theory. Crucially, many routing decisions proved habit-driven rather than fear-driven (a distinction surveys cannot detect) and several behavioral adjustments operated below conscious awareness, recoverable only through VR-RTA video review of participants’ own behavior. Findings point towards a sequential process model of situational FoC: behavioral adjustment begins as routine cognitive appraisal and escalates to full fear engagement only when perceived risk crosses a threshold. They confirm and nuance existing qualitative typologies of avoidance behavior while identifying specific gaps in survey instruments for measuring the behavioral dimension of situational FoC. Based on these insights, new survey items targeting in-situ risk management behaviors are proposed to strengthen the measurement of fear of victimization events. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Contrasting growth and spoilage traits combined with antagonistic core-periphery network organization reveal distinct ecological strategies among dairy-associated Pseudomonas subgroups
abstract: Pseudomonas spp. is a taxonomically diverse genus causing dairy spoilage. Despite its high occurrence in dairy products, its ecology remains poorly understood. In this study, 89 Pseudomonas strains mainly isolated from dairy products were characterized using a high-throughput multi-trait approach that combines biotic and abiotic factors. The collection was dominated in equal proportions by the two subgroups P. fluorescens and P. fragi, followed by the P. gessardii subgroup. Under pH and NaCl stress, the P. fragi and P. fluorescens subgroups exhibited the lowest and highest growth capacity, respectively. The P. fluorescens subgroup contained a higher proportion of proteolytic and lecithinase-producing strains compared to P. fragi subgroup. Strains from P. gessardii subgroup displayed spoilage traits similar to P. fluorescens but with more variable growth behavior. The antagonism network exhibited a nested core-periphery architecture. The P. fluorescens subgroup formed the highly connected core, while P. gessardii and P. fragi occupied the periphery with marginal interactions. Overall, these results revealed that despite equal prevalence, P. fragi and P. fluorescens subgroups displayed markedly divergent ecological strategies. These findings pave the way for promising future investigations into the impact of ecological strategies on product quality. © 2026

title: Sex-dependent habenular dysregulation across the continuum of stress exposure and depression severity: A systematic review of preclinical and clinical evidence
abstract: Background: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is diagnosed at roughly twice the rate in women as in men, yet sex is still routinely treated as a covariate rather than a biological variable of primary interest in depression research. The habenula (Hb), particularly the lateral habenula (LHb), is an increasingly implicated substrate of depression, but two recent systematic reviews found sex-stratified habenula data sparse and reported sex effects inconsistent in direction. Objective: To determine whether sex-related effects on habenula structure and function are patterned by stress intensity or chronicity in preclinical models, and by depression severity or chronicity in clinical populations, rather than arbitrary. Methods: This review builds on two parent systematic reviews (Cameron, Weston-Green and Newell, 2024; Fortin et al., 2025), extracting eligible sex-stratified studies and supplementing them with an independent, two-phase search (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science) for comprehensive coverage of sex- and stress-related terms. Findings were synthesized narratively, organized by stressor chronicity (preclinical) and illness chronicity or severity (clinical), without meta-analysis. Results: Seventeen studies met eligibility criteria (10 preclinical, 7 clinical). In preclinical models, acute stressors produced modality-dependent, sometimes opposite-direction sex effects, while chronic stressors more consistently interacted with, and sometimes abolished, pre-existing baseline sex differences. In clinical populations, sex-dependent habenula abnormalities were largely absent in first-episode presentations and became more pronounced, often specifically in women, with greater illness chronicity, treatment resistance, or symptom severity. Conclusions: Sex-dependent habenula dysfunction in depression shows a patterned, chronicity-linked structure in both literatures, though the evidence base remains small and several conclusions rest on a single study. These findings are hypothesis-generating rather than establishing sex as a confirmed driver of habenula dysfunction. Estrous cycle stage, baseline circuit-level sexual dimorphism, and sociocultural confounds are identified as testable moderators for future research. © 2026 The Authors

title: Robust scheduling of a port power system with shore-power load uncertainty, dynamic shore-power pricing, and hybrid hydrogen–battery storage
abstract: Shore-power demand in ports is highly dependent on vessel arrivals, departures, berthing duration, and vessel-type differences. These operating features make conventional aggregated load models insufficient for coordinated scheduling. This paper proposes a two-stage robust scheduling model for a port distribution network–multi-microgrid system considering vessel-behavior-driven shore-power load uncertainty, dynamic shore-power pricing, and hybrid hydrogen–battery storage. By combining vessel-type classification, vessel-level parameterization, arrival/departure perturbations, and microgrid-level aggregation, a shore-power load model and its uncertainty representation are developed to capture the overlapping berthing effect of multiple vessels and the time-varying uncertainty of shore-power demand. Dynamic shore-power pricing is used to better reflect practical port operation, while a hybrid hydrogen–battery storage system is incorporated to leverage the complementary characteristics of fast-responding batteries and long-duration hydrogen storage, effectively smoothing multi-timescale power fluctuations, facilitating efficient wind power accommodation, and enhancing the intertemporal regulation flexibility and economic efficiency of the port microgrid. The proposed model is solved through a hierarchical ATC–C&CG framework, which coordinates the distribution network and microgrids and optimizes recourse decisions under worst-case scenarios. Case studies show that the total social cost is 20,632.50 CNY, the served shore-power energy reaches 7078.64 kWh, and no load shedding or renewable energy curtailment occurs. Comparative results indicate that the proposed uncertainty model can describe practical port operation disturbances, dynamic shore-power pricing improves shore-power revenue without reducing the service level, and hybrid hydrogen–battery storage enhances microgrid intertemporal regulation flexibility under wind power fluctuations. © 2026

title: Wideband active noise control for open-ear headphones via low-delay acoustic design with a coaxial loudspeaker
abstract: Open-ear headphones preserve environmental awareness but provide little passive attenuation, so broadband feedforward active noise control (ANC) is required. This paper presents a controlled measured-path offline study of a wideband ANC design using one device in one dummy-head wearing configuration, based on a design-oriented secondary-path delay budget. A coaxial offset 2-way secondary source with a tweeter placed in front of a woofer is used, and the control bands are assigned on the basis of frequency-dependent delay characteristics, where the woofer is favored at low frequencies because of its smaller mechanical delay, while the tweeter is favored at higher frequencies because of its shorter acoustic propagation delay. We investigated two implementations: one for a dual-filter setup and the other for a single-filter setup. In this idealized linear measured-path evaluation under controlled assumptions, the two-driver configurations increased band-limited noise-power reduction for broadband pink noise relative to the unfiltered single-driver baselines. At the nominal controlled virtual electronic delay of 104 µs, the background dual-filter condition Du-BpHp-Bg and the single-filter condition Xo-BpHp achieved 8.01 and 7.58 dB reductions from 100Hzto2000Hz, respectively, compared with 5.94 dB for Wf-Bp and 5.02 dB for Tw-Bp. For the tested device and wearing configuration, these results indicate that a design-oriented delay budget can support driver-band allocation for broadband feedforward ANC in open-ear headphones. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Pathways to peace: understanding the role of grassroots movements in countering radicalization and promoting stability in Jammu and Kashmir
abstract: Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), long marked by political instability, economic deprivation, and socio-religious fault lines, has become a fertile ground for radicalization. While mainstream counter-radicalization strategies have relied on state-led top-down developmental initiatives, grassroots movements have emerged as transformative actors addressing the root causes of extremism. This paper investigates the efficacy of grassroots initiatives in countering radicalization in J&K through a multi-theoretical lens and supported by field interviews. Employing models such as Moghaddam’s Staircase to Terrorism, Wiktorowicz’s Theory of Cognitive Openings, and Relative Deprivation Theory, it evaluates the structural and psychosocial conditions that fuel extremism and how locally-rooted programs neutralize them. The paper argues that the fusion of youth engagement, women’s empowerment, economic inclusion, and digital literacy has yielded a resilient counter-narrative that deserves formal integration into national policy frameworks. By analysing field-based insights and contextualizing global peacebuilding precedents, the study proposes a strategic reorientation toward grassroots-led deradicalization. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2026.

title: Vocabulary Size of Children Aged 5 – 9: The Contribution of Shared Reading and Screen Time
abstract: Language development is shaped by children’s exposure to linguistic input, which increasingly comes from both caregiver–child interaction and digital media. Although shared reading is a well-established predictor of vocabulary growth, less is known about how different forms of shared reading and temporally differentiated screen exposure jointly contribute to language development. This study examined the relative contributions of shared book reading, shared poetry reading, weekday screen time, and weekend screen time to passive vocabulary in children aged 5–9 years (N = 636). Children completed a standardized passive vocabulary test, while parents reported literacy practices and screen exposure. Hierarchical regression analyses controlling for age revealed distinct and context-dependent associations. Weekday screen time was negatively associated with vocabulary, whereas shared book reading showed the strongest positive association. Shared poetry reading also made a smaller but significant positive contribution. In contrast, weekend screen time showed a weak positive association with vocabulary. The findings demonstrate that children’s vocabulary development is differentially shaped by both the type of literacy input and the temporal context of screen exposure. The study advances current research by integrating differentiated forms of shared reading and screen use within a single model, highlighting the importance of context-sensitive approaches to children’s digital and linguistic environments. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .
