title: Gullibility, loneliness, exploitation or just bad luck? Exploring older adults’ perceptions of fraud risks, protections and victimhood
abstract: Exploring older adult victimisation of cybercrimes, perceptions of risk and protections using semi-structured interviews and a mixed interactional analytic approach, this paper assesses the implications of isolation, technical knowledge and trusted sources of protection advice. It explores perceptions of personal responsibility, fraud risk, fraud protections, the interconnected and dichotomous narratives of blame and empathy relating to victimhood, and how judgement rests on whether victimhood is perceived as acceptable (just bad luck) or not (gullibility). It highlights the importance social isolation and cognitive decline has in relation to older adults’ fraud victimhood, underscored by participants’ perceptions that youth, education and intelligence are key to resilience against threats. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Indonesian Teachers’ Perceptions About the Potential of Technology-Enhanced Language Assessment (TELA)
abstract: Technology-enhanced language assessment (TELA) has significantly improved language evaluation by integrating digital tools to enhance accuracy, efficiency, and accessibility. This study aims to investigate the role of TELA in language assessment, particularly its advantages, challenges, and implications for pre-service teachers and learners. A mixed-method design was employed, combining closed-ended and open-ended questionnaire responses to provide both quantitative and qualitative insights. The findings reveal key trends in TELA, including the use of artificial intelligence, automated scoring systems, and adaptive testing. While TELA facilitates personalized and immediate feedback, concerns regarding digital equity, validity, and ethical considerations remain significant. This study concludes that a balanced approach is necessary for the effective implementation of TELA to ensure pedagogical effectiveness and ethical soundness. Future research should explore strategies to mitigate the challenges associated with digital assessments in language learning. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .

title: Overcoming interlayer weakness in Ti2C MXene via 3D pillared nanostructures for enhanced compressive and shear resistance
abstract: The outstanding in-plane mechanical properties of two-dimensional Ti2C MXene nanosheets have made them promising candidates for advanced structural materials. However, the weak interlayer van der Waals bonding between MXene sheets limits the load transfer efficiency, leading to premature interfacial debonding and shear sliding under mechanical loading. Here, we propose a three-dimensional (3D) pillared MXene nanostructure consisting of Ti2C nanosheets covalently interconnected by Ti2C nanotubes, and systematically investigate its mechanical properties via molecular dynamics simulations. We examine the effects of nanotube diameter, inclination angle, atomic-scale vacancies, and multi-tube spatial arrangement on tensile, compressive, and shear responses. Under tension, the nanotube remains covalently bonded to the nanosheets and undergoes localized deformation. Under compression, an optimal diameter of 1.8 nm balances strength and deformability, while larger-diameter tubes show reduced sensitivity to point defects. A 15° inclination enhances compressive strain by 53.7% with only 19.3% strength loss. In multi-tube configurations, a systematic trade-off between strength and deformability emerges: Vertically aligned arrays maximize strength, staggered arrangements introduce progressive load release, and hybrid designs achieve the highest deformability. These findings suggest that 3D pillared nanostructures offer a promising route to overcome the interlayer weakness of Ti2C MXene assemblies with enhanced compressive and shear resistance, providing atomistic insights for the design of free-standing MXene-based structural architectures. © 2026

title: Can leisure travel help combat loneliness in later life?
abstract: Loneliness is a growing public health concern, particularly among older adults. Tourism research on healthy aging has largely centered on positive well-being; limited attention has been given to whether travel can alleviate loneliness. Drawing on longitudinal data from China and the United States, this study conceptualizes leisure travel as a form of activation and examines its relationship with loneliness among older adults. The findings indicate that greater participation in leisure travel is associated with lower levels of loneliness among this group over time. Travel also offsets age-related declines in daily social participation and the accompanying increase in loneliness, highlighting travel's activating role in later life. Leisure travel further serves as a compensatory resource for older adults with relational deficits. This mechanism varies across cultural contexts. By moving beyond the focus on positive emotion, this study demonstrates tourism's therapeutic potential for reducing loneliness and promoting well-being in aging populations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Self-report measures of mindfulness for children: convergent validity, predictive validity, and impacts of social desirability bias
abstract: Mindfulness-based interventions have shown promise in supporting psychological well-being in children. However, mindfulness is commonly measured using self-report questionnaires, a method that might be problematic due to its reliance on children’s accurate self-perceptions of their own mindfulness and the potential influence of social desirability bias. In the current study, we examined the convergent validity, the predictive validity, and the influence of social desirability bias on three mindfulness self-report measures for children ages 9–13 years (N = 109). Results showed that children’s self-reported mindfulness demonstrated good convergent validity and predictive validity, as higher levels of self-reported mindfulness were positively associated with higher levels of parent-reported executive functioning. Self-reported mindfulness also covaried with social desirability bias. However, controlling for this bias did not substantively affect the convergent validity nor the predictive validity of self-reported mindfulness. These findings suggest that children’s self-reported mindfulness also captures social desirability bias, but this bias may not affect conclusions about mindfulness when assessed as a latent factor across multiple measures. Future work measuring children’s mindfulness with self-reports should account for social desirability bias when possible, as well as explore objective methods of assessing mindfulness in children. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Life cycle assessment (LCA)-informed optimization framework with temporal fusion transformer for high-recovery hybrid semi-batch/batch reverse osmosis (HSBRO)
abstract: High-recovery desalination involves a complex trade-off between energy efficiency, brine management, and environmental sustainability. To resolve these issues, this study presents a novel life cycle assessment (LCA)-informed temporal fusion transformer (TFT) optimization framework for hybrid semi-batch/batch reverse osmosis (HSBRO). Unlike conventional approaches that use LCA for post-hoc analysis, the proposed framework incorporates environmental impact as a proactive surrogate model within the optimization loop, allowing for sustainability-driven decision-making prior to final operating condition selection. The framework was developed and evaluated using 72,649 time-series samples generated from 81 experimental scenarios on a bench-scale HSBRO system (10–20 m3/d) with NaCl and Na2SO4 feed solutions. The target-specific TFT models demonstrated high predictive performance in capturing dynamic process behaviors, achieving validation R2 values of 0.9913, 0.9998, and 0.9886 and test R2 values of 0.9694, 0.9995, and 0.9388 for cumulative specific energy consumption (SEC), cumulative permeate production, and post-purge brine concentration, respectively. By computationally evaluating unexplored operating conditions through this LCA-informed TFT optimization framework, optimal points that balance productivity and environmental impact can be systematically identified. To verify reliability, the optimum points derived from the framework were validated through experimental testing, yielding R2 values exceeding 0.96 for all key performance metrics, and the TFT model LCA values reproduced environmental trends with only an 11% deviation across the major impact categories. These results indicate that the LCA-informed TFT optimization framework provides a reliable and practical approach to optimizing HSBRO systems, effectively eliminating arbitrary trial-and-error and supporting environmentally sustainable operations in high-recovery wastewater treatment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Defining the relationship between housing characteristics, household demographics, and time-of-use demand response participation
abstract: As major energy consumers connected to the electric grid, the participation of residential buildings in demand-side management (DSM) programs, including time of use (TOU) rates, can help utilities with load management and support decarbonization goals. However, participation in these programs is influenced by a combination of household demographic and housing characteristics, which are often examined separately despite their potential interactions. To address this gap, this study develops and analyzes a linked dataset that combines demographic and housing characteristics at the household level, together with respondents' interest in adopting smart technologies (ST) and willingness to adjust thermostat settings. Separate and combined predictive models were developed to evaluate the influence of these factors on DSM related behaviors. Results revealed that combined demographic and housing models outperformed separate models (χ2 = 14.48–24.99, p < 0.001), indicating that jointly considering these factors better captures the complex drivers of DSM participation. Age, education level, tenure and dwelling type emerged as important predictors for ST technology adoption, while home size, dwelling type, and tenure status more effectively explained respondents' willingness to adjust thermostat setpoints throughout the day. Although 81.7% of respondents reported willingness to adjust setpoints at least sometimes during the day, only 11% were willing to do so during evening peak periods. Household income also seems to predict interest and willingness, indicating that financial resources may influence households’ ability to adopt and participate in DSM/TOU programs. These findings can help utilities tailor DSM and TOU programs to different household contexts, for example, by aligning incentives and outreach with housing types and tenure patterns, to improve participation and load-shifting outcomes. They can also guide policymakers in developing more equitable energy policies that expand access to ST across diverse income and housing groups. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: An efficient convolutional neural network model for classifying positive affective states from EEG data considering sleep condition
abstract: Background The recognition of affective states from EEG recordings considering the sleep condition can be an important supporting tool in therapy and in the treatment of psychological or psychiatric disorders. New method Since sleep deprivation changes EEG characteristics, a two-stage framework is developed for affective state classification. First, a classification between "Normal Sleep" (NS) and "Sleep-Deprived" (SD) is conducted using resting-state EEG data. The data are then fed into one of two newly proposed, lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to recognize four affective states. Results In the first stage, CNN-BiLSTM achieves 95.96% accuracy under window-level splitting and 70.46% under subject-independent 5-fold cross-validation, while in the second stage the proposed models achieve 93.40% (NS) and 90.95% (SD) under window-level splitting, and 38.98% (NS) and 38.97% (SD) under cross-validation. The lower subject-independent accuracies reflect the class imbalance and the clustering of scores near the class boundaries, which make cross-subject four-class generalization challenging. Comparison with existing methods As existing studies mostly classify momentary emotions without addressing sleep conditions, direct comparison with prior work is difficult; we therefore benchmarked our framework against several established baseline models, including SqueezeNet, EEGNet, ShallowConvNet, Support Vector Machine, and Random Forest. Conclusions This study suggests that considering physiological states can improve multi-class classification of affective states from time-varying neurophysiological signals such as EEG. The framework performs strongly under window-level evaluation, whereas its performance under the stricter subject-independent setting is more limited and should be interpreted accordingly. It can nonetheless contribute to more comprehensive research in affective neuroscience. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A JSCC framework with temperature-guided rate learning and multi-domain joint compensation for underwater image transmission
abstract: Underwater acoustic image transmission faces a mismatch between transmission-cost control and distortion mitigation. Although recent DeepJSCC schemes support variable code lengths, they often rely on auxiliary predictors, fixed temperatures, or simplified fading models, limiting their ability to couple rate adaptation with underwater multipath and frequency-selective fading. To address this problem, we propose an end-to-end JSCC framework that integrates temperature-guided rate learning with latent-domain composite-distortion compensation. The key design is to condition the relaxation temperature on channel state and jointly use retained-count bias and score calibration to learn adaptive code-length selection. Specifically, the framework performs pre-encoding feature recalibration through dynamic channel–spatial coupling and introduces progressive multi-domain latent compensation that integrates physical channel-memory priors with learned spectral and noise-robust calibration for transmission over composite acoustic channels. By coupling this channel-conditioned temperature with a retained-count bias and SNR-aware score calibration, the framework jointly shapes the training relaxation and code-length preferences, enabling content- and channel-state-dependent prefix selection without an external quality predictor or a manually specified SNR-to-rate lookup table. Experiments show that the proposed method achieves superior reconstruction performance and a better quality–bandwidth trade-off than representative separation-based and neural JSCC baselines under dynamic underwater conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: AAGP: An application-algorithm aware graph partitioning method via cost-sensitive graph neural networks
abstract: Graph partitioning is a key step in distributed graph computing, as it directly affects communication overhead and workload distribution across computing nodes. However, most existing methods are designed to optimize topology-based proxy metrics, such as edge cuts or vertex balance, rather than the actual execution costs of downstream graph algorithms. As a result, partitions that appear balanced in topology may still suffer from severe runtime workload skew in practical distributed environments. To address this issue, this paper proposes AAGP, an application-algorithm aware graph partitioning framework for workload-balanced distributed graph computing. The proposed framework first builds a vertex-level cost prediction model to estimate the computation and communication costs of graph algorithms. Based on these cost estimates, a cost-sensitive graph neural network is further developed to generate partitioning schemes that explicitly reduce bottleneck execution time and workload imbalance. In addition, multi-scale structural features are incorporated to capture intrinsic, local, and global graph characteristics, thereby improving the quality of partition learning. Experiments conducted on multiple public graph datasets and representative graph algorithms demonstrate that the proposed method consistently reduces execution time and improves load balancing compared with classical heuristic and learning-based baselines. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective and practical solution for performance-oriented graph partitioning in distributed graph computing environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Metabolic cost, mechanical work and efficiency of lateral walking
abstract: Purpose: Lateral walking is an asymmetrical gait, mainly used in sports or working tasks, characterised by higher oxygen demand compared to forward walking. Comprehensive analyses of its mechanical efficiency—the mechanical work produced over the metabolic cost—are lacking. The purpose of this work is to fill this gap of knowledge. Methods: Twenty-four healthy and active young adults (13 females, 11 males) completed controlled treadmill tests adjusted to their self-selected lateral walking speed (SSLWS) and free tests on a flat surface. Four treadmill speeds (±20%, SSLWS and +40% of SSLWS) were tested. Metabolic data were collected via indirect calorimetry, while mechanical work was estimated from 3D motion capture data. Data was analyzed by comparing the results at different speeds and using regression models. Results: Cardiorespiratory demand was moderate but, due to the low speed, the cost of transport (~7 J·kg⁻¹·m⁻¹) was more than double that of walking at self-selected speed. The mechanical work was comparable to walking, which resulted in lower estimates of mechanical efficiency (~12%). Treadmill trials showed higher metabolic demand than free overground lateral walking. Conclusion: In healthy young adults, the combination of modest absolute cardiorespiratory load with high metabolic cost per unit distance suggests that lateral walking may be useful for low-intensity training and merits further investigation as a rehabilitation gait in clinical populations, where metabolic demand without high cardiovascular stress is desired. © 2026

title: Ginsenoside compound K inhibits complement C1qA/C3-CR3-mediated microglial synaptic pruning and neuronal pyroptosis
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Ginseng (Panax ginseng C.A. Meyer), a classic traditional Chinese medicine, has long been used for “calming the mind and enhancing intelligence” to combat cognitive decline. Its major metabolite, ginsenoside compound K (CK), exerts neuroprotection, but the molecular mechanisms against Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain unclear. Aim of the study: This study investigated the molecular mechanism by which CK attenuates microglial aberrant synaptic phagocytosis and neuronal pyroptosis via inhibiting the complement C1qA cascade. Materials and methods: APP/PS1 mice were used as AD models and treated with CK (20 or 40 mg/kg/d) or memantine (MH, 3 mg/kg/d) by gavage once daily for 14 weeks. Morris water maze and open field tests were used to assess cognitive function and anxiety-like behavior, respectively. HE, Nissl and Golgi staining detected neuronal damage and synaptic integrity. Immunofluorescence and ELISA measured microglial polarization, activation and synaptic phagocytosis. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations analyzed the CK-C1qA interaction. Western blot, immunofluorescence and ELISA detected complement components (C1qA, C3, CR3) and pyroptosis-related proteins (NF-κB, NLRP3, ASC, caspase-1, GSDMD-N, IL-18). In vitro cellular experiments, including BV2 cell monoculture and BV2-HT22 transwell co-culture systems, were further performed to validate the causal role of C1qA. Results: CK improved cognitive and anxiety behaviors in APP/PS1 mice, attenuated hippocampal neuronal damage, increased Nissl-positive neurons, restored dendritic complexity and spine density, and upregulated PSD95 and SYP. CK induced microglial M1-like-to-M2-like polarization and reduced Iba1+/CD68+ microglia colocalization with PSD95+ synapses, indicating suppressed synaptic engulfment. CK was predicted to bind to the C1qA globular head domain, reduced C1qA deposition at synapses, inhibited C3, and CR3 expression, suppressed NF-κB phosphorylation, downregulated NLRP3, ASC, cleaved-caspase-1, and GSDMD-N, decreased IL-18 release, and alleviated neuronal pyroptosis. In vitro, CK suppressed C1qA expression in BV2 cells and reduced synaptic C1qA deposition in HT22 cells. Conclusion: CK ameliorated cognitive and synaptic deficits in APP/PS1 mice by inhibiting the C1qA/C3-CR3 pathway to suppress aberrant microglial synaptic phagocytosis and blocking NF-κB/NLRP3/GSDMD-mediated neuronal pyroptosis. These findings elucidate CK's neuroprotective mechanisms and provide scientific evidence for ginseng's traditional cognitive benefits. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Conflict minerals, institutional failure, and the limits of transparency: Resource governance in post-2001 Afghanistan
abstract: Why did the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI) fail to generate accountability in Afghanistan, which was declared EITI-compliant in 2012 and suspended in 2019? This article treats Afghanistan's post-2001 extractive sector as an extreme case of resource governance under a contested political settlement and examines it through an embedded single-case design. Drawing on interviews with senior officials of the Ministry of Mines and Petroleum, the national EITI secretariat, and civil society, together with interviews with miners, community members, and academics, focus groups, and documentary sources, it traces how neopatrimonial governance and elite capture undermined transparency. Three mechanisms emerge: the colonization of mining institutions by patronage networks; the exclusion of mining communities from participation and benefit-sharing, which sustains customary and insurgent revenue channels; and the invisibility of artisanal, armed-group-controlled extraction to payment-reconciliation mechanisms. The article's main contribution is a sequenced governance framework, derived abductively from the conditional-transparency literature and the case evidence, which holds that in deeply captured, conflict-affected sectors, security provision, elite incentive restructuring, and community empowerment are preconditions for, rather than consequences of, effective transparency. The article specifies the framework's scope conditions and the evidence that would count against it. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Effects of ambient temperature on flame propagation characteristics of methanol spray-hydrogen explosions
abstract: Methanol-hydrogen fuel forms explosive spray droplet clouds during storage and transport. Therefore, understanding the propagation characteristics of spray flames is crucial for safe application. This study systematically investigates the impact of ambient temperature, methanol concentration, and hydrogen addition on flame propagation characteristics and reaction kinetics. A spray combustion model was developed and validated against experimental data. The results indicated that hydrogen addition played a dominant role in the variations of flame structure and explosion intensity. Compared with pure methanol spray combustion, the flame with 10.0 % hydrogen addition exhibited a smooth and symmetric structure, resembling that of a premixed gas‑phase flame. Its average propagation speed reached 3.04 times that of the pure methanol case, and the explosion index increased by 223.38 %. Ambient temperature had a non‑monotonic effect on flame propagation. At excessively high temperatures, the evaporative cooling of methanol suppressed combustion. Chemical kinetic analysis showed that the H-abstraction pathways R84 and R85 dominated methanol consumption, while R1 and R30 had the strongest inhibitory effect on flame temperature. This paper clarifies the combined effects of ambient temperature and hydrogen addition on methanol spray explosions, providing a theoretical basis for the safe storage and risk management of blended fuels. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Modeling the interaction between labor and capital: a mathematical analysis of seasonality and periodicity
abstract: We analyze a model that establishes a relationship between labor and capital while incorporating seasonality and periodicity effects. Our study focuses on investigating the existence and asymptotic behavior of the solutions, considering the seasonal and periodic variations in labor and capital. We propose a numerical scheme using a meshless method, and its convergence is demonstrated. Several numerical examples illustrate the theoretical results obtained. © The Author(s) under exclusive licence to Sociedade Brasileira de Matemática Aplicada e Computacional 2026.

title: Loneliness trajectories and psychosocial, behavioral, and functional vulnerability among cancer survivors: A comparison of patients aged 50–64, 65–74, and ≥75 years
abstract: Introduction Loneliness is common among older cancer survivors and may contribute to depressive symptoms, adverse health behaviors, functional decline, and loss of independence. National data on loneliness trajectories and survivorship-related vulnerability remain limited. Materials and methods The study cohort included cancer survivors aged ≥50 years from the 2022 Health and Retirement Study, with age categorized as 50–64, 65–74, and 75 years or older. Loneliness was the primary exposure; 2020–2022 data were used to classify survivors as never lonely, or as having incident, resolved, or persistent loneliness. Survey-weighted logistic and linear regression models were used to evaluate associations between loneliness and psychosocial, behavioral, and functional measures after adjustment for sociodemographic characteristics, comorbidity burden, and self-rated health, as applicable. Results Among 2331 cancer survivors aged 50 years or older, mean age was 72.4 years, 59.5% ( n = 1387) were female, and 18.6% ( n = 433) reported loneliness. In cross-sectional multivariable analyses, loneliness was associated with higher odds of elevated depressive symptom burden (aOR, 11.21; 95% CI, 7.44–16.90), loss of independence (aOR, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.01–2.31), fair or poor self-rated health (aOR, 1.92; 95% CI, 1.35–2.72), and current smoking (aOR, 2.37; 95% CI, 1.06–5.29). In a separate adjusted linear regression model, loneliness was associated with a 3.10-point higher continuous Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression score (β, 3.10; 95% CI, 2.82–3.39). In longitudinal trajectory analyses, persistent loneliness (aOR, 15.78) and incident loneliness (aOR, 8.32), but not resolved loneliness, were associated with elevated depressive symptom burden. Discussion Among cancer survivors aged 50 years or older in the United States, loneliness was associated with depressive symptom burden, worse self-rated health, current smoking, and loss of independence. Persistent and newly emergent loneliness identified survivors with the greatest depressive burden, supporting repeated loneliness assessment to guide targeted psychosocial, behavioral, and functional support. © 2026 The Authors.

title: A Tale of Two Styles: Exploring the Compatibilities and Incompatibilities among Learning and Teaching Styles in Second Language Didactics
abstract: The process of teaching and learning is a complex interplay of multiple factors, including teaching and learning styles. A mismatch between these styles can lead to negative outcomes. The primary objective of this study is to investigate the learning styles of non-Iranian Persian language learners and the teaching styles of their instructors. To explore the alignment and discrepancies between these variables, a quantitative method was employed to provide a comprehensive understanding of the relationship between them. This research was conducted with a sample size of 116 Persian language learners and 25 teachers, and data on learning styles were collected using the Perceptual Learning Style Preference Questionnaire (PLSPQ). The same questionnaire was adapted and validated to collect data on teaching styles. The study revealed no significant difference in the prioritization of visual, tactile, auditory, and kinesthetic learning styles between learners and teachers. However, a notable difference was observed in group and individual learning styles. Furthermore, academic background emerged as a crucial factor affecting teaching style, with teachers who had completed a teaching Persian program (AZFA) prioritizing group-style instruction. The outcomes of this research underscored the existence of discernible disparities between the teaching styles of educators and the learning styles of students. As such, it was recommended that teachers adjust their teaching styles to align with the learning styles of their students. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .

title: Functional metagenomics yields insights into the adaptive mechanisms of microbial persistence in beef processing drains
abstract: Selective pressures within beef processing environments drive the persistence of microbial communities capable of withstanding repeated sanitation, yet the functional mechanisms underlying this resilience remain largely uncharacterized. To address this knowledge gap, a metagenomic study was conducted on 21 drain samples collected across eight United States beef processing facilities, evaluating the effects of spatiotemporal factors (processing areas and the 2019 versus 2021 sampling years) on functional potential and resistome composition. Broad functional profiling identified significant enrichment of KEGG pathways governing biofilm formation, quorum sensing, bacterial secretion systems, ABC transporters, chemotaxis, and flagellar assembly, with Pseudomonas spp. emerging as the dominant driver across all enriched features. Differential abundance analysis revealed significant (Padj < 0.05) enrichment of these pathways and multidrug resistance determinants in carcass storage coolers and in 2021 samples. This temporal shift may reflect several non-exclusive factors, including changes in sanitation pressure, natural temporal drift, shifts in cattle microbiomes, or sample storage effects. Antimicrobial resistance profiling using AMRFinderPlus and DeepARG further demonstrated that the dominant Pseudomonas populations exerted a disproportionate influence on the facility resistome, primarily via multidrug efflux systems. This profile coincided with a nearly two-fold increase in beta-lactam resistance annotations between 2019 and 2021, suggesting that environmental pressures may select for clinically relevant resistance markers. These findings provide a functional framework for understanding microbial persistence in built food-processing environments and highlight the critical need to evaluate whether current sanitation strategies inadvertently promote resistant, biofilm-forming communities. © 2026

title: Shaping street rhythms: Spatial context and the temporal patterns of pedestrian activity
abstract: Urban streets provide spatial contexts in which pedestrian activity unfolds over time, yet previous research has seldom examined how these street rhythms differ across space or how they are associated with local street conditions. This study addresses this gap by examining street-level pedestrian rhythms across Seoul's commercial streets. Using mobile phone signal–based estimates of pedestrian presence for 110,574 street segments in 2022, we extract 11 temporal features from weekday pedestrian time series and apply fuzzy C-means clustering to identify five street rhythm types. Multinomial logistic regression evaluates how these rhythms relate to 16 indicators of commercial hierarchy, physical scale, accessibility, functional mix, and surrounding populations. The findings show that street rhythm types are systematically associated with multiple dimensions of spatial context, rather than reflecting simple differences in pedestrian-presence levels or land-use intensity. Even among commercially active streets, evening-peak rhythms were distinguished by concentrations of retail, leisure, and entertainment-oriented functions. Midday- and afternoon-peak rhythms, despite their similar daytime profiles, were also differentiated by their spatial contexts: midday-peak rhythms were associated with office- and institution-based workday districts, whereas afternoon-peak rhythms were linked to production-related commercial areas. By revealing these distinctions, this underscores the value of treating time as an integral dimension of urban spatial structure. © 2026

title: SDE-IG: A robust malware family classification method based on graph invariance learning
abstract: While existing malware family classification methods achieve high performance on in-distribution data, they often overfit mutable features when subjected to different compilers, optimization levels, and advanced code obfuscation. This vulnerability significantly degrades their generalization under complex distribution shifts. Furthermore, applying existing graph invariance learning methods, which typically rely on random topological sampling, disrupts the strict semantic dependencies inherent in binary code. Additionally, a naive concatenation of dynamic and static features introduces underlying system call noise, adversely affecting the model's ability to identify core family logic. In response, this paper proposes SDE-IG, a robust malware family classification framework based on invariant subgraphs. A cross-environment invariant subgraph extraction mechanism is designed from a static perspective. By integrating binary semantic priors with parameterized graph neural networks, this mechanism decouples the program call graph into an invariant subgraph representing core semantics and an environment subgraph capturing noise. This separation is designed to reduce reliance on environment-dependent structures that may vary across compilation, linking, and obfuscation settings. To address potential static topology failures caused by extreme obfuscation, SDE-IG incorporates a dynamic behavioral view as auxiliary semantic evidence. During end-to-end joint optimization, a collaborative mixup strategy is applied to simulate unknown variants and broaden the distribution boundary. Coupled with an asynchronous two-stage optimization and a gated residual calibration mechanism, this approach effectively minimizes the interference of dynamic behavioral noise on the static backbone representation. Experimental results show that SDE-IG achieves improved cross-period classification stability under the chronologically separated temporal distribution shifts evaluated in this study. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Emotion Regulation in Language Learning: Strategies for Managing Foreign Language Anxiety among Iranian EFL Learners
abstract: This study employed a mixed-methods approach to examine the utilization of two emotion regulation strategies, namely cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression, among a group of Iranian learners of English as a foreign language (EFL) at universities in Isfahan, Iran. The investigation was based on the Process Model of Emotion Regulation, a psychologically-validated theoretical model proposed by Gross (2015). The study also investigated the correlation between emotion regulation and levels of foreign language anxiety (FLA), and as an additional area of investigation, the impact of emotion regulation on the association between FLA and motivation for learning a second language. A total of 295 learners were questioned using a quantitative questionnaire. The qualitative research involved the selection of thirteen respondents from three levels (high, medium, low) of FLA. The primary component employed in this study was a stimulated recall interview. Data collection was undertaken online due to scheduling constraints. The findings indicated a low frequency of utilization for the two emotion regulation strategies, with cognitive reappraisal being more commonly employed compared to expressive suppression. Learners with low English proficiency exhibited a lower prevalence and preference for cognitive reappraisal. There was a stronger positive correlation observed between expressive suppression and FLA. The study found a negative correlation between cognitive reappraisal and FLA. It provides evidence that understanding the inner workings of learners’ emotion regulation may inform pedagogical practices. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .

title: Multi-agent assisted co-evolutionary memetic algorithm for lot-streaming flexible job shop energy-efficient scheduling problem with asynchronous assembly
abstract: Mass customization increasingly requires flexible manufacturing systems in which component processing, material transfer, and multi-station assembly must be coordinated simultaneously. This study investigates a lot-streaming flexible job shop energy-efficient scheduling problem with asynchronous assembly (LS-FJSEP-AA). It integrates lot streaming and flexible processing with inter-stage transportation and an unpaced assembly line subject to precedence and blocking constraints. A bi-objective mixed-integer linear programming model is formulated to minimize makespan and total energy consumption, with energy accounting for processing, setup, machine idle/on–off, transportation, assembly, and assembly-station idle states. Based on the cross-stage timing relationships, two structural properties are identified to guide critical-operation adjustment and assembly prioritization. To efficiently solve the resulting strongly coupled problem, a multi-agent assisted co-evolutionary memetic algorithm (MA-CoEA) is developed. MA-CoEA integrates offline GEP-assisted initialization, objective-oriented cooperative evolution, problem-specific neighborhood search, and DQN-based adaptive control. Computational experiments show that MA-CoEA achieves competitive solution quality and convergence performance against state-of-the-art algorithms, while exhibiting stable performance across independent runs on representative benchmark instances. An industrially inspired case further demonstrates the effectiveness of lot streaming and cross-stage schedule adjustment in improving the trade-off between makespan and energy consumption. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: From Herders’ Knowledge to Ecological Insight: Reindeer, Voles, and Food Caches in the Arctic
abstract: This paper examines pistin, a little-studied forage resource for domestic reindeer previously mentioned only briefly in the scientific literature: underground stores of rhizomes made by voles on the Yamal Peninsula in the Russian Arctic. Drawing primarily on semi-structured interviews with reindeer herders and interpreting them alongside rodent trapping data, habitat descriptions, and genetic identification of rhizome samples from one available cache, we document a hidden trophic interaction among reindeer, voles, and tundra plants. Herders’ observations reveal reindeer’s seasonal use of pistin, its high attractiveness as forage, and its uneven spatio-temporal distribution across Yamal. Long known to Nenets herders in southern Yamal, pistin has only recently become visible in the peninsula’s northern part, where herders describe it as a new or still absent resource. We argue that pistin is both an overlooked seasonal forage resource and an indirect indication of vole presence across tundra subzones. The case highlights how herders’ knowledge can reveal connections between adaptations in reindeer foraging and vole range shifts, both shaped by climate-related change in the Arctic. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: From curated datasets to social-media reality: In-the-wild, multimodal, and generalizable deepfake detection
abstract: Deepfake detection has advanced rapidly alongside progress in generative adversarial networks, diffusion models, neural rendering, and multimodal synthesis. However, strong performance on curated benchmark datasets does not necessarily translate into reliable performance in real-world environments, where manipulated media are affected by platform compression, reposting, post-processing, multimodal inconsistency, temporal drift, and evolving generation pipelines. This review examines deepfake detection from the perspective of in-the-wild robustness, multimodal reasoning, and cross-domain generalization. It first clarifies the conceptual foundations of in-the-wild and generalizable deepfake detection, then reviews the data ecosystem, including benchmark datasets, real-world media conditions, multimodal data gaps, annotation quality, and benchmark aging. The review further analyzes the major causes of detector failure under realistic deployment conditions, including generator shift, platform-induced degradation, modality mismatch, language and speaker variation, and broader contextual diversity. It then compares major methodological families, including artifact-based methods, deep representation-based approaches, transfer-based learning, domain adaptation, domain generalization, and multimodal detection strategies, with emphasis on their relevance to real-world robustness. Finally, the review discusses evaluation practices, external validation, realistic benchmarking, and future directions such as continually updated benchmarks, missing-modality-robust systems, uncertainty-aware detection, provenance integration, and foundation-model-based approaches. Overall, the review argues that reliable deepfake detection requires a shift from benchmark-centered optimization toward robust, multimodal, and deployment-oriented evaluation and design. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: How do Self-Compassion and Cognitive Flexibility Shape Pre-Service English Language Teachers’ Resilience? The Path from Self-Care to Strength
abstract: The present study sought to examine the association between preservice second or foreign language (L2) teachers’ self-compassion (SC) and teacher resilience (TR), with the mediation of cognitive flexibility (CF). To accomplish this, a total of 353 participants voluntarily completed a set of scales. Results from a structural equation modeling analysis indicated that these three constructs are positively related. Specifically, SC was found to significantly predict TR, and CF significantly mediated the association between the constructs. The results also showed that the indirect effect of SC on TR through CF was significant, indicating that flexible cognition helps transform self-directed compassion into resilient professional functioning in L2 teaching. The findings imply that self-compassionate teachers of the English language are more likely to remain resilient in their profession, and this association is fostered when coupled with their flexible cognition in language teaching. Implications are offered for teacher education, including incorporating reflective practices that cultivate SC and activities that train flexible thinking and adaptive problem-solving. The study contributes to growing evidence that affective and cognitive resources jointly support resilience in language teacher development. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .

title: Electrochemical sensing of promethazine: A critical review of detection strategies, sensor architectures, and analytical challenges
abstract: Promethazine (PMZ) is a widely used phenothiazine drug whose accurate determination is important in pharmaceutical quality control, clinical monitoring, forensic toxicology, food analysis, and environmental surveillance. Although chromatographic and spectrometric methods remain valuable for confirmatory analysis, their dependence on sophisticated instrumentation and extensive sample preparation has encouraged the development of faster electrochemical alternatives. This review critically evaluates PMZ electrochemical detection studies published from 2010 to 2026, covering voltammetric methods, direct electrocatalytic detection, molecularly imprinted and DNA-mediated recognition, adsorptive stripping, and extraction-integrated electroanalysis. Particular attention is given to the effects of nanostructured materials, conductive composites, porous interfaces, and recognition layers on analytical performance. Comparative analysis indicates that nanostructured electrodes generally enhance sensitivity and electron transfer, whereas molecularly imprinted and DNA-modified interfaces offer greater potential for selective recognition. However, important trade-offs remain because high-surface-area and adsorption-based platforms are susceptible to fouling, affinity-based sensors often require complex fabrication and regeneration, and ultra-low detection limits frequently depend on prolonged preconcentration or sample pretreatment. Major research gaps include inadequate discrimination from structurally related phenothiazines, limited validation in authentic complex samples, poor inter-electrode and batch-to-batch reproducibility, and insufficient assessment of robustness, operational stability, total assay time, and cost. Future research should prioritize matrix- and fouling-resistant interfaces, simplified scalable fabrication, rigorous validation, and integrated sample handling. Combining reproducible disposable electrodes with microfluidics, portable potentiostats, and connected readout systems may facilitate reliable field-deployable and point-of-care PMZ analysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Analysis choices can produce apparent rich-club differences: an Alzheimer's disease EEG case study
abstract: Background The weighted rich-club coefficient tests whether a network's most strongly connected nodes are preferentially interconnected. Its interpretation depends on two often-implicit choices: how the randomised comparison networks are constructed, and whether the hubs are re-identified in each comparison network or held fixed at those of the observed network. When hubs are defined by connection strength, these choices change what the coefficient tests. New method We examined how these choices affect inference using resting-state EEG from 20 people with Alzheimer's disease and 20 controls. Holding the data fixed, we compared four analysis pipelines, crossing two ways of building the comparison networks (global weight reshuffle or strength-conditioned null) with the two hub choices, and ran a calibration study using data constructed to contain no preferential hub coupling beyond nodal strength. Results An apparent eyes-open group difference in rich-club organisation appeared only under the pipeline combining a global weight reshuffle with re-identified hubs. Under the empirical resampling ensemble, that pipeline reported a group difference in 43% of pseudo-studies, always higher in the Alzheimer's disease group, while the other three stayed near the expected 5%. Comparison with existing methods Unlike global weight reshuffling, strength-conditioned nulls approximately preserve nodal strengths; fixing observed hubs also retains the identity of the core being tested. Conclusions The same data can support or dissolve an apparent rich-club difference depending on these choices. No single choice is universally correct, but reporting which were made, and why they fit the question being asked, is essential to interpreting the result. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Reasoning-aware fake review detection via contextual integration of large language model generated rationales
abstract: Fake reviews on e-commerce platforms undermine consumer trust and distort fair competition. Their detection remains challenging due to the subtle linguistic cues and intentional mimicry of authentic reviews. Although neural models capture surface-level semantics effectively, they often struggle to infer deceptive intent or assess commonsense plausibility, which limits the reliability of fake review detection. This work introduces LLM-Augmented Rationale Integration Network (LLM-RIN), a rationale-aware hybrid framework that integrates motivational intent and commonsense plausibility rationales generated by a large language model (LLM) into a small language model (SLM) classifier. Through rationale-level auxiliary supervision, cross-attentive review–rationale interaction, and usefulness-aware fusion, the framework improves interpretability and strengthens the ability to detect subtle deceptive patterns. A contrastive review–rationale alignment objective is further incorporated to encourage instance-level grounding and enhance robustness to noisy or drifting rationales. Experiments on YelpZip and YelpNYC-20K show that LLM-RIN consistently improves fake-class detection over competitive baselines, while class weighting provides a more recall-oriented operating point. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: MT-MNER: A multimodal named entity recognition model based on multi-view contrastive learning and two-stage feature fusion
abstract: Multimodal Named Entity Recognition (MNER) is essential for extracting structured information from unstructured data, yet it faces challenges including insufficient coordination between multimodal alignment and fusion, as well as the difficulty of balancing fusion precision and information integrity in multi-granularity information integration. To address these challenges, We propose MT-MNER, an innovative model based on multi-view contrastive learning and two-stage feature fusion. Specifically, MT-MNER introduces a multi-view contrastive learning strategy that performs dual-granularity alignment: at the coarse-grained level, it aligns textual features with global visual features to unify the two semantic spaces. At the fine-grained level, it adopts a ranking-based contrastive learning strategy to promote fine-grained semantic alignment by prioritizing candidate image patches with higher semantic relevance to textual tokens. To further deepen cross-modal interaction, we design a two-stage feature fusion mechanism that incorporates a hierarchical feature fusion module and a global feature fusion module. This two-stage approach progressively integrates local visual cues with global semantic information, thereby ensuring precise entity detection. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that MT-MNER achieves micro F1 scores of 77.03%, 81.06%, and 92.06%, respectively, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. These results validate MT-MNER as a robust and efficient paradigm for MNER in complex scenarios. The main code is available at: https://github.com/Shy0418/MT-MNER.git . Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Uncovering emotion dynamics across human–AI interaction modes in programming: Evidence from facial expression and electrodermal activity
abstract: Emotions play a fundamental role in learning by shaping learners' cognitive engagement and influencing learning outcomes. In generative AI (GAI)-supported programming, learners interact with AI in different ways. However, limited research has examined how different interaction modes are associated with learners' emotional dynamics. This study investigated students' emotions across three human–AI interaction modes (i.e., AI-reliant, AI-independent, and human–AI hybrid) during AI-assisted programming. A total of 150 undergraduate students completed programming tasks with access to ChatGPT, during which video recordings of their facial expressions and electrodermal activity (EDA) were collected. Facial expressions were analyzed to examine both emotion distributions and temporal transitions using lag sequential analysis, while EDA was used to measure affective arousal. Results reveal that none of the seven facial-expression categories differed significantly across the three modes. Lag sequential analysis uncovers that the three modes shared reciprocal anger ↔ disgust, fear ↔ surprise, and neutral ↔ sadness transitions. Descriptively, the AI-reliant mode showed transitions between positive and negative emotions, the AI-independent mode showed a relatively neutral-centered transition network, and the human-AI hybrid mode demonstrated a relatively surprise-centered transition network. However, none of the transition probabilities differed significantly across modes. In terms of EDA analysis, the hybrid mode exhibited significantly more skin conductance responses (SCRs) in total and significantly more SCRs per minute than the AI-reliant mode. These findings suggest that emotion states can serve as signals for understanding how learners engage with GAI during programming. The study highlights the importance of designing emotion-aware AI-supported programming environments that balance technological assistance and learners’ emotional engagement in problem-solving. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: CasHyper: Modeling multi-factor interactions and asymmetric influence in cascade prediction via hypercomplex algebra
abstract: Cascade prediction aims to forecast the future evolution of information diffusion and is an important task in social network analysis. Most existing methods represent users and cascades in real-valued Euclidean spaces, which may offer limited capacity to model multi-factor interactions and asymmetric influence in complex diffusion processes. To address these challenges, we propose CasHyper, a hypercomplex-based cascade prediction framework that integrates hypercomplex algebra with graph neural networks and Transformers. CasHyper organizes user and cascade embeddings into multiple hypercomplex components, with each component encoding distinct latent factors, and uses structured algebraic operations to model cross-component interactions. The non-commutative hypercomplex product further yields order-dependent interaction representations, enabling the model to learn asymmetric influence among users. In the network encoding stage, a static heterogeneous graph channel captures user-user and user-cascade relations, while a Neural ODE-based dynamic channel models the continuous evolution of node states and edge weights. A hypercomplex Transformer with norm-preserving rotary transformations is then introduced to incorporate relative positional information into cascade sequence modeling. Finally, an interaction-aware module and a linear projection module are combined to estimate the probability of each candidate user participating next. Experiments on four real-world datasets show that CasHyper achieves competitive or better performance than the compared methods under the evaluated settings, including relative improvements of up to 43.24% on Android and 18.43% on Christianity in Hits@50. Additional analyses of architectural variants, graph incompleteness, computational efficiency, and different Cayley–Dickson algebras further demonstrate the empirical effectiveness of the proposed framework and reveal dataset-dependent behaviors of different hypercomplex structures. We release the code at https://github.com/MrYansong/CasHyper. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Ion-specific capacity–rate–energy trade-offs in graphite-based capacitive deionization: Beyond gravimetric performance ranking
abstract: This study systematically compares NaCl, NH4Cl, and CaCl2 on the same graphite-based electrode platform using a consistently defined operational endpoint and complementary gravimetric, molar, cation-equivalent, rate, and cell-electrical energy descriptors. The comparison addresses a key limitation of conventional capacitive deionization (CDI) benchmarking: although gravimetric salt adsorption capacity (SAC) is widely used as a performance metric, direct cross-electrolyte comparisons can be misleading when salts differ in molar mass and ionic valence. Moreover, SAC alone does not capture adsorption rate or electrical-energy demand, potentially altering the interpretation of electrolyte performance. At the reference condition of 0.10 N, 1.2 V, and 15 mL min−1, the 30-min mean SAC values were 64.87, 116.07, and 73.18 mg g−1 for NaCl, NH4Cl, and CaCl2, respectively. The corresponding operational endpoints occurred at 15, 10, and 30 min, yielding cation-equivalent uptake (qeq,op) values of 1.120, 2.170, and 1.319 meq g−1 and equivalent-normalized adsorption rates (ASAReq,op) of 0.075, 0.217, and 0.044 meq g−1 min−1, respectively. The corresponding cell-electrical specific energy consumption (SEC) values were 0.0212, 0.0153, and 0.0391 Wh L−1. Machine learning was retained as a secondary exploratory analysis, revealing strong observation-level interpolation but substantially weaker leave-one-condition-out transferability, thereby indicating limited generalization to unseen operating conditions. Overall, electrolyte performance depended on both the selected benchmarking metric and operating condition, demonstrating that gravimetric SAC alone is insufficient for robust cross-electrolyte evaluation. The coordinated assessment of adsorption capacity, equivalent-normalized uptake and rate, operational endpoint, and cell-electrical energy provides a more physically meaningful framework for CDI performance benchmarking across electrolytes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Aquilaria leaves (Thymelaeaceae): A comprehensive review of ethnobotany, traditional applications, phytochemistry, pharmacological activities, toxicity and quality evaluation
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Aquilaria species are well known for agarwood, while their leaves are also used in regional folk medicine and consumed as herbal teas in southern China and Southeast Asia, mainly for inflammatory conditions, infections, and stress-related symptoms. Aims of the review: This review summarizes the ethnobotany, taxonomy, traditional applications, phytochemistry, pharmacology, toxicity and quality evaluation of Aquilaria leaves, and identifies gaps that warrant further investigation. Materials and methods: Relevant literature was collected from Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, PubMed, CNKI, and Wan Fang Data, including journal articles, books, and dissertations. Flora of China and Plants of the World Online were consulted to verify species distribution and accepted botanical names. Chemical structures were drawn using ChemDraw 22.0.0. Results: A total of 185 compounds have been recorded from Aquilaria leaves. Phytochemical and pharmacological studies mainly involve three species, A. sinensis, A. crassna, and A. malaccensis. The major compound classes include flavonoids, terpenoids, benzophenones, organic acids, xanthones, and 2-(2-phenylethyl)chromones, with flavonoids (39) and terpenoids (43) predominating. Pharmacological studies have largely focused on crude extracts, with relatively few investigations of isolated compounds, and have demonstrated anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antibacterial, antidiabetic, laxative, and neuroprotective activities. Available toxicological studies generally indicate low acute toxicity within the tested dose ranges, although evidence on long-term safety remains limited. Quality evaluation has mainly relied on chromatographic profiling and multi-component determination, while standardized quality criteria remain to be established. Conclusions: This review highlights Aquilaria leaves as a renewable and underexplored medicinal resource by integrating evidence from traditional applications, phytochemistry, pharmacology, toxicity, and quality evaluation. However, current evidence is still limited by crude-extract-based studies, insufficient active-constituent characterization, and limited long-term safety and clinical data. Further research is needed to identify the active constituents, elucidate their underlying mechanisms, and establish standardized quality control and safety evaluation systems for the safe and effective use of Aquilaria leaves. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Prevalence and correlates of GenerativeAI chatbot use for mental health concerns in higher education students
abstract: Background: Large language model chatbots are increasingly used for mental health help-seeking, with general-purpose systems like ChatGPT becoming popular among young adults despite concerns about accuracy and misinformation. High rates of mental distress in higher education attending emerging adults make them an important focal population to characterize and contextual the use of generativeAI models for mental health in. Methods: Data were collected from the 2024-2025 Healthy Minds Study at a large, public 4-year university. Of 12,000 students invited, 2071 participated; 896 bachelor-level students aged 18–24 years were randomly selected to complete a module with generativeAI questions, and 809 (90.2%) had complete data. Measures included chatbot use for mental health support, perceived AI trustworthiness, AI knowledge, mental health diagnosis, perceived need for help, past-year mental health treatment, barriers to care, other forms of informal help-seeking, and demographics. Weighted logistic regression models examined associations between these variables and chatbot use for mental health support. Results: 15.4% of students reported using generalized chatbots for mental health help-seeking. Significant correlates included greater perceived need for help, experiencing more barriers to clinical care use, higher perceived trust in AI for mental health information, lower AI knowledge, and identifying as Asian. Specific barriers of financial constraints, limited time, fear of clinician mistreatment due to identity and privacy concerns were linked to chatbot usage. Conclusions: GenerativeAI chatbots are a notable source of mental health support for college students, especially among those facing access barriers and who perceive AI as trustworthy. Future initiatives should educate young adults about chatbot capabilities and limitations and promote equitable mental health support. © 2026 The Author

title: Duration of depressive symptoms prior to a cancer diagnosis and post-cancer memory function and decline: A longitudinal analysis of the US Health and Retirement Study
abstract: Introduction Depressive symptoms are associated with increased risk for cognitive decline in the general population, but less is known about how depressive symptoms might influence cognitive aging after a cancer diagnosis in mid-to-later life. We aimed to determine if the duration of depressive symptoms before a cancer diagnosis is associated with post-cancer diagnosis memory function and decline. Materials and methods Data were from 425 adults aged ≥50 with an incident cancer diagnosis from 2004 to 2020 and three waves of depression data prior to their diagnosis in the US Health and Retirement Study. Depressive symptoms were measured biennially using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D; range 0 to 8); a score of ≥3 was considered clinically relevant depressive symptoms. Duration of pre-cancer diagnosis clinically relevant depressive symptoms was categorized as never, 1 time point, or ≥ 2 time points. Episodic memory was assessed from the time of cancer diagnosis as a composite of immediate and delayed recall scores. Multivariable adjusted linear mixed-effects models estimated the association between pre-diagnosis depression duration and post-diagnosis memory function and decline. Results The mean baseline age was 68.9 years (SD: 8.6) and 52.7% were female. In the three survey waves (~6 years) prior to diagnosis, 56.7% (241/425) had no depressive symptoms, 20.0% (85/425) had depressive symptoms at 1 time point, and 23.3% of participants (99/425) had depressive symptoms at ≥2 time points. The mean follow-up time after cancer diagnosis was 6.2 years (SD = 4.7). A longer duration of pre-diagnosis depression was associated with a faster rate of memory decline post-diagnosis (−0.12 SD units/year, 95% CI: −0.22, −0.02). Discussion Increased duration of depressive symptoms prior to cancer diagnosis is associated with faster memory decline post-cancer diagnosis and may be a salient risk factor for accelerated memory aging among older cancer survivors. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Thermal property engineering of lunar regolith via spark plasma sintering
abstract: The extreme logistical challenges of Lunar exploration and habitation encourage in situ resource utilisation. Spark Plasma Sintering is a technique capable of rapidly consolidating Lunar regolith without additives, leveraging the vacuum conditions of the Lunar surface. The manufactured components could be used for thermal energy storage, construction, or precision engineering, applications that are sensitive to how the thermal properties vary across the Lunar temperature range of −120°C to 120°C. Understanding how the sintering process influences the thermal properties is essential for optimal design and performance. This study investigates the effects of SPS process parameters on the coefficient of thermal expansion, heat capacity, and thermal conductivity of sintered regolith simulants. Both a mare and a highland simulant were sintered to expand the current body of knowledge with this data and with evaluation of the implications for in situ utilisation. The findings show that sintering temperature is the most influential factor affecting all three thermal parameters. Variations in thermal conductivity and heat capacity with density suggest that engineering trade-offs are necessary to optimise the thermal performance of thermal storage systems, structural materials, and precision components. title: Same prevalence, different futures: Protective appraisal and fatigue in seasonal influenza dynamics
abstract: Behavior-disease models have established that awareness, risk perception, compliance, fatigue, and other behavioral processes can shape epidemic spread, and several existing frameworks already represent more than one behavioral mechanism. However, it remains unclear whether populations matched on both their current influenza state and their current realized protection can still experience different future trajectories because the hidden behavioral composition of that protection differs. We examine this question by distinguishing protective appraisal from accumulated fatigue.We developed an influenza transmission model coupled to appraisal and fatigue. The disease component was calibrated to weekly Hong Kong influenza case data from 5 January 2020 to 22 March 2020, yielding (Formula presented). The behavioral component was parameterized using contextual early-2020 respiratory-risk proxies combining survey-derived protection, Google-search intensity, influenza case intensity, and positivity. Because this window overlapped with the emergence of COVID-19, we repeated the analysis under alternative proxy specifications that removed Google-search and survey inputs. We then conducted prevalence-controlled and equal-current-protection experiments, epidemic-stage and fatigue-parameter robustness analyses, numerical-convergence and uncertainty checks, social-reinforcement ablation, and a direct comparison with an aggregate one-state behavioral model.In the principal equal-current-protection experiment, future peak magnitude ranged from approximately 0.099 to 0.109, time to future peak from 8.8 to 9.3 days, and cumulative post-snapshot incidence from 0.517 to 0.527. The qualitative ordering was retained under alternative proxy definitions, parameter perturbations, epidemic-stage changes, and removal of social-reinforcement feedback. However, the aggregate one-state and two-state models had similar short-window empirical performance. The two-state model reduced in-sample proxy RMSE by only 0.7% and had a 4.8% higher rolling one-week-ahead RMSE. Its demonstrated advantage was instead structural: once current protection was fixed, the one-state model produced one future by construction, whereas the two-state formulation retained future-peak and cumulative-incidence ranges of approximately 0.0100 and 0.0104.The contribution is therefore not the introduction of multiple behavioral states or a claim of superior short-window forecasting accuracy. It is a data-anchored matched-state framework showing that observationally equivalent current protection can contain distinct appraisal–fatigue compositions associated with different counterfactual epidemic futures. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Laser etching of flattened copper mesh for fabricating continuous capillary channels in flexible heat pipe with high durability
abstract: Flexible heat pipes suffer from an intrinsic trade-off between heat transfer performance and bending durability. Although thinning the flexible section can effectively reduce bending stress and improve durability, it generally compromises capillary-driven liquid transport across the wick, thereby limiting heat transfer performance. To overcome this conflict, this study proposes laser etching of flattened copper mesh for constructing continuous capillary channels in ultrathin flexible heat pipes. Ultrafast laser processing was used to generate continuous capillary channels on the surface of flattened copper mesh, and a liquid transport model was established based on three-dimensional surface topography to clarify the relationship between laser-induced morphology and capillary behavior. The results show that flattening a 200-mesh copper mesh reduced its thickness by 50% and increased wire width by 56%, creating favorable conditions for continuous channel fabrication. By regulating laser parameters, continuous V-shaped capillary channels with a depth of 35 μm and a width of 30 μm were achieved, exhibiting strong capillary pumping capability with a maximum wicking coefficient of 17.94 mm/s0.5. When applied in a flexible heat pipe, the etched flattened copper mesh enabled an ultrathin flexible section of 261 μm and a low thermal resistance of 0.84 °C/W at 5 W. A bending test platform was further developed to quantitatively evaluate durability degradation during cyclic deformation. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Masson SAS.

title: Comparison of visual tasks for assessing attentional bias in cannabis users and non-users
abstract: Attentional bias toward substance-related cues is a key feature of addiction and may contribute to the continued use of substances, such as cannabis. However, the sensitivity of different paradigms for detecting this bias remains underexplored. This study compared three visual attentional bias paradigms: dot probe (DP), eye movement (EM), and MouseView.js (MV) in detecting cannabis-related attentional biases among cannabis users and non-users. Thirty-one participants (i.e., 16 users and 15 non-users) completed all measures: DP (reaction time to probes replacing cannabis or neutral stimuli), EM (measured via eye-tracking), and MV (cursor-based dwell time). Linear mixed-effects models examined the effects of stimulus type, group, craving, and cannabis use severity. The EM and MV tasks revealed significant stimulus effects, with non-users showing greater attention to neutral images, while cannabis users exhibited more evenly distributed attention across stimuli. In the EM task, a significant stimulus × severity interaction indicated reduced attentional differentiation with increased cannabis use severity. MV results followed a similar, but less precise pattern. In contrast, the DP task showed minimal group or interaction effects and lacked sensitivity to detect attentional differences. These findings suggest that EM-based measures are more sensitive for detecting cannabis-related attentional biases, particularly when accounting for cannabis use severity. MV showed some alignment with EM patterns but demonstrated weaker effects. The DP task, despite its widespread use, may be insufficient for capturing cannabis-related attentional differences. Results highlight the importance of task selection in attentional bias research and the potential influence of individual differences in cannabis use severity. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Dual-regime molecular restructuring in vacuum hot-pressed briquette coal: Closing the fidelity gap for gas outburst simulations
abstract: Briquette coal (BC) is used extensively as a coal analog in the physical modeling of coal and gas outbursts. However, the intrinsically weak mechanical structure and elevated permeability of BC relative to natural coal introduce systematic biases. To close this fidelity gap, we report an integrated vacuum hot-pressing thermal conditioning protocol (150–450 °C) coupled with triaxial rock mechanics and seepage characterization. Correlative X-ray diffraction, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analyses are performed to decode the molecular engineering levers that govern BC evolution. Two distinct thermal regimes are identified. Below 300 °C, the selective scission of aliphatic C–C/C–H and oxygen-bearing side chains (C–O, C–OH, and COOH) generates plasticizing fragments that drive matrix densification and strength accrual, concurrent with intensified aromatic layer ordering (decreased d 002, increased L c and L a). Above 300 °C, accelerated polycondensation consumes these plasticizing moieties, triggering embrittlement and permeability rebound. The 300 °C optimum delivers the closest macroscopic parametric convergence in terms of the compressive strength and permeability. A uniaxial compressive strength of 7.79 MPa and permeability of 1.72 mD are achieved, which are comparable to typical ranges for natural coal specimens. This optimum is attributed to balanced depolymerization–condensation chemistry and optimized microcrystalline packing. These insights establish thermal processing as a quantitative molecular tuning strategy for coal analog fidelity, providing a mechanistic foundation to enhance the predictive reliability of gas outburst simulations. title: On linkage-based metamaterials with inertial regulation: benefits of using asymmetry for superior low-frequency broadband vibration suppression
abstract: Lightweight and compact structures in aerospace, automotive, and precision instrumentation are increasingly demanding vibration suppression solutions that are effective at low frequencies and over broad frequency range. However, conventional locally resonant metamaterials with symmetric linkage configurations for inertial regulation face a fundamental limitation: a persistent trade-off between achieving low-frequency vibration suppression and obtaining a wide broadband gap. To overcome this limitation, this study develops a generalized theoretical linkage-based metamaterial model for inertial regulation and derives two new key inertial regulation factors, which are related to geometric parameters and mass distribution. The analysis first reveals the inherent constraints imposed by symmetric models on these two factors, which restrict their bandgap tunability. Then, an asymmetric inertial regulation model is proposed. Remarkably, this asymmetric model not only achieves an ultra-wide bandgap approaching a relative width of 2, but more importantly, resolves the trade-off between low-frequency suppression and broadband width, exhibiting a resonant bandgap that is 1000 times wider than that of the symmetric model at lower frequencies. Furthermore, an innovative nested linkage mechanism is introduced, which significantly enhances the bandgap control capability of the asymmetric model under strict spatial constraints, a feature from which the symmetric model derives only limited benefit. Collectively, this study demonstrates the multiple advantages of asymmetric inertial regulation: it establishes a new design paradigm beyond traditional symmetry-based approaches, delivers superior performance compared to its symmetric counterparts, and offers a promising non-intuitive strategy for wide and low-frequency vibration suppression in engineering applications where lightweight and spatial compactness are essential. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: miRNAs: Current and future diagnostic biomarkers in liver fibrosis
abstract: Liver fibrosis is an abnormal response of the liver to various pathogenic factors. It represents a critical stage in the progression from chronic liver disease to cirrhosis and liver cancer. Without timely diagnosis and intervention, liver fibrosis can significantly reduce patients' survival rates and quality of life. In liver fibrosis, microRNA (miRNA) plays a dual role in disease progression by regulating gene expression and signaling pathways. Some miRNAs have antifibrotic effects by inhibiting the TGF-β/Smad signaling pathway or blocking the activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). In contrast, other miRNAs accelerate fibrosis by activating the HIF-1α/VEGF pathway or promoting abnormal extracellular matrix deposition. This two-way relationship establishes a basis for investigating miRNAs as potential diagnostic markers. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on various miRNAs associated with liver fibrosis and their molecular mechanisms. It also evaluates their potential applications in serological testing. Research shows that miRNAs, because of their high stability and specificity, are likely to overcome the limitations of traditional methods for diagnosing liver fibrosis. Furthermore, this article evaluates the strengths and weaknesses of popular miRNA detection methods, such as real-time quantitative PCR, microarrays, and next-generation sequencing (NGS), emphasizing that optimizing standardized processes and high-throughput technologies is essential for facilitating the clinical use of miRNAs. In summary, miRNAs are promising non-invasive diagnostic tools for the early diagnosis and personalized treatment of liver fibrosis. Nonetheless, additional research is essential to improve the technology and clinical validation of miRNA detection for its widespread use in clinical settings. © 2026 The Authors.
