title: Multi-scale adaptive frequency enhanced network with cross-domain disentangled contrastive learning for robust recommendation
abstract: Driven by the need to model complex periodic user preferences beyond the limited temporal domain, recent Sequential Recommendation (SR) studies have increasingly leveraged spectral information to uncover latent behavioral patterns. Nevertheless, existing frequency-based SR methods suffer from two critical limitations: (1) Lack of personalized filtering: most approaches rely on static filtering strategies that struggle to adapt to highly heterogeneous individual behavior dynamics; (2) Information entanglement and interest drift: long-term low-frequency preferences, transient high-frequency interests, and stochastic noise remain deeply intertwined. Coupled with the non-stationary evolution of user interests, current models cannot effectively isolate fine-grained interest drift hidden within high-frequency components. To address these limitations, we propose MaDRec, a Multi-scale Adaptive Frequency Enhanced Network with Cross-domain Disentangled Contrastive Learning for Robust Recommendation. Specifically, MaDRec leverages the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) to construct multi-scale adaptive filters, which dynamically extract personalized frequency-aware representations for individual users. Furthermore, a Cross-domain Disentangled Contrastive Learning (CD-DCL) module is designed to optimize joint time-frequency representations and suppress noise via cross-domain multi-granularity alignment constraints. Experimental results demonstrate that MaDRec outperforms state-of-the-art SR models across five benchmark datasets. It achieves average improvements of 6.54% on HR@10 and 6.75% on NDCG@10, while retaining stable performance even in non-ideal scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Multi-view aligned fused representation clustering network for unsupervised community detection
abstract: Community detection in attributed networks requires a representation that combines node attributes with local connectivity and community structure. We propose the Multi-view Aligned Fusion Representation Clustering Network (MFRCN) for unsupervised community detection. MFRCN extracts four complementary views from structural, attribute, and modularity information. An attribute autoencoder and attention-based graph encoders learn the view representations, which are aligned before fusion. The fused embedding supports attribute and graph reconstruction together with a self-training clustering objective. Experiments on Cora, Citeseer, and DBLP demonstrate good community detection performance. The ablation studies support the contributions of modularity information, attention, and view alignment. Additional evaluations examine computational cost, nonlinear fusion alternatives, and sensitivity to missing graph information. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: The location logic of informal retail: dual-scale evidence from street food vendors in Hangzhou
abstract: Street food vendors (SFVs) form an important part of nighttime retail supply in cities. However, they operate without fixed premises and change locations over time. Understanding these patterns is essential for designating vending sites and planning the nighttime economy. Focusing on nighttime SFVs in the main urban districts of Hangzhou, this study applies an XGBoost, SHAP, and GAM framework with spatial autocorrelation analysis at the block and street scales. The analysis identifies associated factors, differences across scales, and spatial alignment between designated sites and actual SFV locations. At the block scale, SFV distribution is positively associated with working population density, shop rent, and metro accessibility, converging on mature commercial cores. At the street scale, associations shift toward micro-scale nodes such as metro entrances and parking facilities. Designated sites and actual locations align globally but diverge locally. These findings extend the discussion of classical retail location theory to informal retail. Fixed premises, rental arrangements, and purposive consumption may take different forms in informal settings. Their relevance therefore requires explicit consideration. The findings support a spatial guidance strategy combining block-scale zoning with street-scale site allocation, offering empirical grounding for nighttime economy planning and urban governance. © 2026

title: FinSA-MoE: A parameter-efficient mixture-of-experts framework for cross-domain Chinese financial sentiment analysis
abstract: Financial sentiment signals from textual narratives are crucial for understanding market dynamics. However, heterogeneity across financial text sources introduces substantial cross-domain discrepancies in linguistic structure, noise patterns, and sentiment expression. In Chinese financial contexts, stylistic divergence between formal news and informal investor commentary further exacerbates these challenges, destabilizing representation learning in large language models. To address these challenges, we propose FinSA-MoE, a parameter-efficient mixture-of-experts framework for cross-domain Chinese financial sentiment analysis. Built upon a pre-trained large language model backbone, FinSA-MoE constructs domain-specific experts for financial news and stock commentary using lightweight low-rank adaptation adapters, while a mixture-of-experts routing mechanism dynamically selects appropriate experts to enable efficient and robust inference across heterogeneous financial domains. We design a composite training objective with regularization techniques to enhance training stability and cross-domain generalization by addressing class imbalance and uneven expert utilization. Furthermore, we introduce FinNF, a large-scale Financial News and Forum dataset comprising over 2.12 million high-quality Chinese financial news articles and stock commentary texts, which provides a solid data foundation for fine-tuning and evaluating financial sentiment analysis models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FinSA-MoE consistently outperforms existing deep learning approaches and financial large language models across multiple evaluation metrics on news, stock commentary, and mixed-domain benchmarks. The proposed framework effectively captures cross-domain financial sentiment characteristics and offers a scalable solution for Chinese financial text understanding. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Enhanced DNMF-graph integrated multilevel semantic factorization for contextual named entity recognition
abstract: Named Entity Recognition (NER) has undergone considerable changes in the recent past driven by the growing demand for models that are more robust, context aware and capable of generalizing across diverse textual domain. However, existing state of the art approaches primarily rely on local contextual representations, and often fails to capture corpus level semantic structures, particularly in noisy or low resource settings. To address these limitations, a unified NER system is proposed in the present work, that utilizes a Deep Non-Negative Matrix Factorization (DNMF) integrated with token level graph community discovery and a Transformer- Conditional Random Fields (CRF) model. The proposed model, named as DNMF-Graph-Transformer CRF, can utilize the strengths of various representation levels. By applying DNMF to the token-context matrix, several interpretable, low-rank latent semantic factors are obtained that not only complement neural representations but also help to improve the model's generalization when it has to work with a small amount of noisy data. Next, a token interaction graph is generated to represent the global relationships among tokens. Thus, community embeddings can be extracted that give structural priors at the corpus level. These features represent semantic neighbourhoods and functional groupings of tokens. Finally, the Transformer- CRF is adapted to learn the contextual aspects of the text. The performance of the proposed model is evaluated by conducting comprehensive experiments on CoNLL-2003, OntoNotes 5.0, and WNUT 2017. The results demonstrate that the proposed model significantly outperforms existing baseline models. It is observed that the performance gains are especially significant for noisy social media text. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Terror management and antagonistic personality: A network analysis of the dark tetrad, self-esteem, and fears of death and dying
abstract: Terror Management Theory (TMT) posits that self-esteem buffers death anxiety, but TMT is rarely explored in antagonistic personalities. In a university sample ( N = 571), we estimated a Bayesian Gaussian graphical network linking Dark Tetrad traits (D4; Machiavellianism, grandiose narcissism, psychopathy, sadism), self-esteem, and fears of death and dying (FoDeath-Self, FoDeath-Others, FoDying-Self, FoDying-Others). Self-esteem connected negatively to FoDying-Self and FoDeath-Others, but positively to FoDeath-Self, complicating simple TMT accounts. It also showed comparatively high strength but near-zero expected influence due to offsetting positive and negative edges. D4 traits showed distinct TMT-related profiles: Machiavellianism connected negatively to self-esteem and positively to FoDeath-Others, with lower strength and intermediate expected influence; narcissism connected positively to self-esteem but no fears, and showed the highest D4 expected influence; psychopathy connected negatively to self-esteem, FoDying-Self, and FoDeath-Others, but positively to FoDeath-Self, showing the highest D4 strength but lower expected influence due to offsetting positive and negative edges; sadism was unrelated to self-esteem and connected negatively to FoDying-Others, showing lower strength and intermediate expected influence. An exploratory directed acyclic graph yielded a tentative FoDeath-Others → Machiavellianism orientation, motivating a speculative “personality-as-terror-management” hypothesis. Overall, self-esteem was not uniformly associated with lower mortality-fear, and D4 traits showed distinct mortality-fear signatures. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Dynamic causal graph representation learning for neurological disorders recognition
abstract: The effectiveness of dynamic brain networks in diagnosing neurological disorders, which represent a worldwide threat to human health, is increasingly recognized. Numerous Graph Neural Network (GNN) models have been created to autonomously detect aberrant integration patterns related to specific neurological conditions in brain graphs. Nevertheless, most existing approaches exhibit primary drawbacks. These methodologies typically either employ predetermined statistical metrics (e.g., Pearson correlation) or depend on static brain networks. Moreover, the process of constructing dynamic brain networks/graphs concentrates on static or temporally invariant effective connectivity, resulting in a substantial knowledge gap about the dynamic aspect of dEC. Although statistically-specific brain networks are extremely efficient in identifying certain disorders, their performance may lack robustness when applied to other neurological diseases. To address these issues, we introduce a novel model termed the Dynamic Causal Graph Inference Graph Neural Network (DCGI-GNN), which can estimate brain networks and learn graph representation within a two-stage pipeline, facilitating the optimization and interpretability of each stage. The term “causal” in this work refers to directed, time-varying functional influence relationships, not intervention-based causality. Our model initially deduces the task-relevant graph structures directly from the data and later utilizes them to improve downstream task performance. We conducted extensive experiments to diagnose three brain diseases: autism spectrum disorder (ASD), Alzheimer's disease (AD), and Parkinson's disease (PD) using data from the ABIDE, ADNI, and PDD datasets. Our findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Beyond its superior performance, the model is highly interpretable, and its conclusions align largely with existing literature. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Mobility in ICU survivors: A concept analysis
abstract: Objective: Mobility limitations are common and clinically important among ICU survivors, yet the concept of mobility remains inconsistently defined and is often conflated with physical capacity, functional status, and activities of daily living. This study aimed to clarify the concept of mobility in ICU survivors using Walker and Avant's concept analysis methodology. Methods: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and Web of Science from database inception to August 15, 2026. Walker and Avant's eight-step framework guided the identification and synthesis of uses, related concepts, defining attributes, antecedents, consequences, and empirical referents. Results: Thirty-eight studies were included. One defining attribute of mobility was identified: purposeful transition in body position or spatial location. Antecedents comprised predisposing factors, critical illness-related factors, physical prerequisites and limiting conditions, and contextual and modifying factors. Consequences spanned functional and daily-life, psychosocial and participation, and care and service domains. Mobility-focused task measures were the most conceptually aligned empirical referents, whereas measures of muscle strength, exercise capacity, activities of daily living, disability, participation, and quality of life assessed related but distinct constructs. Conclusion: Mobility in ICU survivors is defined as patient-generated or patient-controlled movement that produces a purposeful transition in body position or spatial location following critical illness. Such transitions may be performed independently or with assistance. This definition distinguishes mobility from enabling physical capacities, passive repositioning, contextual influences, and broader functional and social outcomes. Implications for clinical practice: This concept analysis may help nurses and rehabilitation professionals distinguish mobility from physical capacity and broader functional outcomes, supporting more consistent mobility assessment, individualized rehabilitation planning, and the development of nursing-sensitive mobility outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Structure, functions, and mechanisms of Rodentia vocalizations across the lifespan
abstract: Vocalizations are an integral way that rodents and many other mammals communicate. Historically, research on rodent vocalizations focused on laboratory-derived strains of two species, house mice (Mus musculus), and brown rats (Rattus norvegicus). However, with over 2000 species, Rodentia is one of the largest vertebrate orders with many species available for communication research. In this review, we synthesize recent findings on lesser-studied species spanning five Rodentia families: Muridae, Caviidae, Cricetidae, Bathyergidae (including Heterocephalidae), and Sciuridae. First, we take an evolutionary perspective to compare adult vocalizations within and across these five Rodentia families. Then, we take a developmental perspective to characterize immature vocalizations and how they transition into mature vocalizations. Next, we explore the potential functions of rodent vocalizations by surveying the behavioural contexts in which they occur. Finally, we summarize recent work on the physiological mechanisms that underpin rodent vocalizations, from biomechanics to neuromodulator systems and neural circuitry. Together, this research shows that Rodentia is an excellent taxonomic group for exploring the diversity and evolution of vertebrate acoustic communication. © 2026 The Authors

title: Dynamic configurations and ecological fit: A fuzzy-set QCA analysis of effective data security governance in summer olympic games (1992–2024)
abstract: Against the backdrop of accelerating digital transformation, Summer Olympic Games have become mega‑temporary events generating massive volumes of data, where data security governance is critical to smooth event delivery. Nevertheless, existing scholarship mostly adopts fragmented technology‑centric or management‑centric perspectives, overlooking the synergistic interplay among multi‑dimensional factors. Drawing upon information ecology theory, this study applies fuzzy‑set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) to nine Summer Olympic Games held between 1992 and 2024. We examine how five antecedent conditions—data asset sensitivity, organizational management maturity, technological maturity, security deployment intensity, and external regulatory pressure—jointly shape high‑level data security governance. Necessary‑condition analysis shows that no single factor is indispensable for sound governance. Three equifinal configurational paths are identified: the Full‑Element Driven path, the Management‑Technology Dual‑Driven path, and the Low‑Risk Baseline path. Our findings demonstrate that effective Olympic data security governance arises from nonlinear multi‑element synergy rather than isolated single‑factor advantages, while governance failures stem from ecological mismatches among information‑ecology components. Building on these patterns, we derive a path‑contingent investment framework specifying what budget‑constrained hosts can compress and what they must prioritize. This paper extends information ecology theory to the temporary governance context of mega‑sporting events and delivers differentiated, resource‑constrained managerial insights for future Olympic host cities under the ecological‑fit principle. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: STGLR: Fusing short-term and group-level long-term sequential recommendation
abstract: Sequential recommendation focuses on forecasting a user’s next likely interaction based on their past behavior sequences. User interactions are primarily influenced by users’ underlying intents (e.g., purchasing a book to read), and effectively modeling these intents can significantly enhance recommendation performance. Specifically, users’ behaviors are driven not only by short-term intents (e.g., buying a new phone to replace an old one) but also by long-term stable habits (e.g., purchasing a book weekly to read). Existing methods based on cross-subsequences, although effective at capturing short-term intents, often overlook users’ long-term habits. To tackle this limitation, we introduce a Short-Term and Group-level Long-term Recommendation (STGLR) model. Specifically, the model first employs contrastive cross-subsequences pairs to capture short-term intents. It then introduces a group-prototype attention to learn long-term intents from groups of users with similar long-term habits. Finally, these two intent representations are integrated via a fusion module, yielding a holistic user profile that combines short-term and group-level long-term intents. Evaluations conducted on three public datasets show that our method consistently surpasses several mainstream baseline models across various evaluation metrics. Our implementation can be accessed at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/STGLR-main-D1C1. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Assessment of Drinking Water Security and Waterborne Disease Prevalence in Imphal East and West Districts of Manipur, India
abstract: Integrated assessment of drinking water security and the prevalence of waterborne diseases in the Imphal East (IE) and Imphal West (IW) districts of Manipur, India, using the water poverty index (WPI). WPI is evaluated across various dimensions, including the availability and accessibility of water resources and the use of safe, acceptable-quality drinking water; the socioeconomic capacity of the population to cope with water security challenges; and overall environmental challenges. The seasonal prevalence of waterborne diseases was assessed with respect to climate variables, specifically rainfall and temperature. The systematic, structured household questionnaire survey and focus group discussions were conducted to assess socioeconomic parameters of the representative population. Based on the integrated assessment, the study reveals a poor-to-moderate WPI, highlighting a significant challenge for people in accessing potable water in the region. This underscores the need to improve rural drinking water supply to ensure public health safety. Thus, the present study incorporates the interlinkage between climate variability, public health challenges, and their impact on the drinking water security in the region. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Negative and positive emotional eating and food cravings related to weight loss during weight management
abstract: Emotional eating and food cravings are common among adults living with overweight or obesity. This study investigated these in relation to weight-management success and reports on strategies for managing emotional eating. A quasi-prospective study design was used including an online survey completed by 3834 adults on a community weight management programme. Measures included negative and positive emotional eating (BEES) and food craving (CoEQ). Additionally, objectively measured body weight over the previous 12 weeks was obtained and participants were grouped into Higher (>10%, N = 962), Moderate (5-10%, N = 2156), and Lower (<5%, N = 716) weight loss groups. Open questions were used to explore strategies for managing emotional eating. Between-group differences were tested using univariate ANOVAs, with Tukey post hoc comparisons where significant effects emerged. Open ended responses were analysed using inductive thematic analysis and mapped onto the Behaviour Change Taxonomy. Respondents were mostly female (92.0%), mean age = 57.2 years, and BMI = 32.1 kg/m2. Results showed participants had lost 3.7 BMI units over the previous 12 weeks. Higher weight loss was strongly associated with lower negative and positive emotional eating, fewer food cravings and eating control difficulties. Prominent themes for managing emotional eating were distraction (31.7%) and physical activity along with healthier food substitutions, planning and positive mindset. Group social support was also highlighted. These data highlight the perceived importance of psychological and group-based social support in weight management. title: A combinatorial bidding based deep reinforcement learning approach for multi-agent job shop scheduling problem
abstract: The multi-agent job shop scheduling problem has become a key challenge in demand-driven manufacturing systems, where multiple consumer agents with heterogeneous scheduling objectives share limited machine resources. This paper proposes a combinatorial bidding based deep reinforcement learning approach to solve this problem under the centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) paradigm. In the proposed framework, combinatorial bidding allows each consumer agent to submit bundles of interdependent operations within a single round, enabling more expressive preference representation and effective resource utilization. A graph attention network based encoder is employed to capture interdependencies among unscheduled operations. An augmented pointer decoder is developed to generate coordinated operation bundles within each bidding round. Extensive experiments show that the proposed approach achieves competitive average social welfare and exhibits a scale-dependent performance pattern. Compared with evolutionary and reinforcement learning approaches, the simulation results indicate that combinatorial bidding enhances coordination efficiency and scheduling quality, particularly in larger multi-agent scheduling settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: HCl emission prediction in municipal solid waste incineration using a Transformer–XGBoost hybrid model with deep feature extraction and SHAP-based interpretation
abstract: Accurate prediction of hydrogen chloride (HCl) emissions plays an important role in efficient control of deacidification systems in municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) plants. However, accurate prediction remains challenging due to the dynamic nonlinearity, multivariable coupling and time series characteristics of MSWI process. This study proposes a Transformer–XGBoost hybrid model to predict HCl emissions in MSWI process. Firstly, a feature extractor based on Transformer model is designed to capture target-relevant temporal dependencies and complex interactions among process variables, extracting features and generating auxiliary prediction. Subsequently, a weighted feature fusion strategy is introduced to integrate the extracted features with auxiliary prediction result, thereby enhancing the representational capacity of features. Finally, the fused features are input into the XGBoost predictor to predict the HCl emissions at time t + 3. The proposed model is trained, validated, and tested using real industrial data from the MSWI plant. Additionally, the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis reveals model behavior and the importance of combustion air distribution and deacidification operating variables to HCl predictions. Comparative experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves optimal prediction performance, with an R2 of 0.974, a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 0.388 mg/m3, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.262 mg/m3, and a symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE) of 8.14 % on the testing set. These results indicate that the proposed method achieves accurate and robust HCl emission prediction in MSWI process, thereby providing critical data support for the precise, stable and cost-effective control of HCl emissions in MSWI plants. title: Energy equity under crisis pricing: the vulnerability-responsiveness paradox in Norwegian residential electricity consumption during the European energy crisis
abstract: Dynamic electricity pricing is widely advocated for demand-side management, yet its distributional consequences under crisis conditions remain poorly understood. We examine the equity implications of hourly spot pricing during the European energy crisis using metered consumption from 1136 Norwegian households (October 2020–March 2022) linked to socio-demographic surveys. Southern Norwegian wholesale prices nearly tripled (+192%), and mean household electricity costs rose from 484 to 1785 NOK/month. Energy poverty emerged from a zero baseline: no household exceeded the conventional 10% income-burden threshold before the crisis, versus 1.2% during it, and 6.8% exceeded a 6% burden. Impacts were steeply regressive: the mean burden of the lowest-income group reached 7.4%, against 1.9% for the highest — a fourfold gap. SHAP analysis shows that housing characteristics dominate income and price as predictors of consumption, indicating that vulnerability is structural, rooted in the building stock, rather than purely economic. We term this the vulnerability-responsiveness paradox: the households facing the greatest welfare exposure have the least structural capacity to adjust. Counterfactual simulations show that a 1.0 NOK/kWh price cap cuts poverty to 0.3%, and that pairing the cap with targeted retrofits of high-consumption detached homes performs best across cost, poverty, and inequality simultaneously. Crisis pricing policy should combine short-term price caps with structural building-efficiency programmes. title: Federated multi-view information fusion based on prototype and feature distillation: A privacy-performance tradeoff method for data heterogeneity
abstract: With the rapid development of distributed intelligent systems, federated learning has become a crucial research direction. Federated distributed training frameworks enable collaborative optimization of global models, while the ubiquitous data heterogeneity across clients severely degrades model accuracy. Although existing information sharing strategies can alleviate heterogeneous bias, they are prone to incurring privacy leakage risks. Achieving an effective trade-off between privacy preservation and model performance has thus become a core challenge. To address the privacy-performance trade-off problem in heterogeneous federated scenarios, this paper proposes a federated multi-view information fusion method based on prototype and feature distillation, termed FedTPF. Before the local model training on clients, FedTPF first trains a distillation model, and constructs dual feature views consisting of latent features derived from the distillation model and local prototypes. By minimizing the constrained distance in the latent space, dual-view feature fusion is implemented to extract minimal features with superior global generalization capability and filter redundant information. Each client leverages the well-trained distillation model for feature filtering and generates generalized features combined with differential privacy. The generalized features are further constructed as a globally shared view, which is integrated with the local data view for multi-view fusion training to mitigate data heterogeneity. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that FedTPF improves the global model accuracy without disclosing clients’ private information. Under the same privacy budget, it achieves a 3.7% performance gain compared with state-of-the-art methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Expansion toward risk: China's urban growth reshapes population exposure to compound environmental pressures
abstract: Rapid urban expansion is altering the distribution of environmental benefits and risks. As cities grow outward, newly developed areas may face elevated exposure to multiple environmental pressures, raising concerns about whether urbanization is inadvertently exposing population toward more adverse environmental conditions. To investigate this, we use population-weighted exposure model to quantify three key environmental exposures in China's newly built-up areas from 2000 to 2018: blue-green space exposure (BGE), PM2.5 exposure (PME), and heat stress exposure (HSE). By integrating SOM–K-means clustering and Bayesian Networks, we identify the evolution of typical environmental exposure combinations and examine their conditional dependencies. Results show that, from 2010 to 2018, BGE slightly improves, PME shows greater balance but persistent risks, while HSE intensified significantly. Clustering analysis identifies three distinct environmental exposure types: Ecological Deficiency (ED), High Environmental Cost (HEC), and Eco-Advantaged under Heat (EAH). In 2010, ED is the most prevalent type (1133 counties; 55.5%), followed by HEC (792 counties; 38.8%) and EAH (115 counties; 5.6%). By 2018, EAH increases to 386 counties (18.4%), while ED and HEC decline to 1052 (50.1%) and 664 (31.6%) counties, respectively. Notably, 466 ED counties transition to HEC, making ED-to-HEC the largest single transition. 146 counties transition from ED to EAH, indicating ecological improvement accompanied by greater heat stress. Together, these changes reveal a pattern of urban expansion toward risks. Bayesian Networks further reveal a reconfiguration in the conditional dependency structure of environmental exposures, moving from a relatively constrained dependency pattern toward a more interconnected configuration, with BGE becoming more centrally embedded in the network. This study contributes a novel integrative framework for understanding how urban expansion reshapes population exposure to compound environmental pressures and provides insights to inform risk-aware and equitable urban governance. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Bridging Conservation and Human-Wildlife Conflict for Coexistence
abstract: Human-wildlife conflict (HWC) poses a significant threat to conservation, particularly in the region, where dense human settlements and recovering wildlife populations compete for resources. This study examines HWC patterns in the buffer zone of Parsa National Park, where growing populations of large mammals overlap in their use of shared resources. We analyzed 454 official relief claims filed at the park office over five fiscal years (2018/19–2022/23), using the monetary value of claims as an indicator of damage severity, and found the following. Elephants accounted for 45% of reported incidents, followed by leopards (29%) and tigers (13.5%). Reported herbivore-related damage increased over the study period, while carnivore-related conflict declined, although relief claim amounts increased in later years, likely reflecting an increase in the valuation of losses at prevalent market prices. Total financial claims totaled ~ USD 80,275 (annual average ~ USD 16,000), with 55% of relief accounted for by elephant-related incidents. Claimed amounts differed significantly between carnivore- and herbivore-related damage (Kruskal–Wallis χ²=26.96, p < 0.01, η²=0.057) and among the five species involved (χ²=34.21, p < 0.01, η²=0.07). Generalized additive modeling showed that relief claims increased with distance from buffer zone forests (β = 0.0008, t = 2.6, p < 0.01) and were higher for tiger-related incidents (β = 0.52, t = 3.8, p < 0.01). Additionally, distance from water sources exhibited a significant non-linear relationship, with patterns consistent with wildlife activity centers and movement behaviors, suggesting a need for habitat management interventions within the park and at strategic corridor locations. Implementing a field-based damage assessment and dynamic relief mechanism could support a step towards human-wildlife coexistence in the region. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: A biophysically-inspired framework with spatiotemporal graph diffusion for EEG-based mental workload assessment
abstract: Ensuring operational safety in high-stakes environments necessitates the precise assessment of mental workload via electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. However, conventional data-driven deep learning models are often impeded by the inherent non-stationarity of EEG signals and typically neglect the biological topology of the brain. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel biophysically-inspired framework that leverages spatiotemporal graph diffusion for robust workload assessment. We establish a computational surrogate model designed to mirror the dynamic cognitive state of the user. In contrast to traditional approaches, we integrate biophysical priors derived from volume conduction and functional connectivity directly into the learning process, thereby ensuring biologically consistent feature extraction. Specifically, we employ a spatiotemporal graph diffusion mechanism that treats EEG channels as nodes within a dynamic graph. This process effectively denoises the signals and captures complex, long-range dependencies across both spatial brain regions and temporal sequences. By reconciling biophysically-inspired constraints with data-driven graph learning, the proposed model enhances robustness against the low signal-to-noise ratio characteristic of EEG data. Extensive experiments on three public datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior accuracy compared with other state-of-the-art baselines, offering a reliable solution for the real-time monitoring of mental workload. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: The social acceptance of agrivoltaics: Exploring the cognitive and affective outcomes of technological, contextual, and personal beliefs
abstract: Agrivoltaics -the co-siting of photovoltaic energy and agronomic production- has been promoted as a win-win solution to reconcile renewables expansion with food security, yet its deployment has raised ambivalence and public opposition. Existing studies have largely focused on farmers and experts, leaving lay citizens’ views underexplored. This paper addresses that gap by examining the determinants of agrivoltaics’ acceptance among non-experts. Acceptance was assessed through the integrated Sustainable Energy Technology Acceptance framework, further extended by introducing outcome evaluation as both a cognitive (perceived efficacy) and an affective (positive emotions) pathway to acceptability, and by incorporating anticipatory solastalgia, understood as present distress over anticipated landscape change. A convenience sample of Italian citizens (N = 849), mostly residing in urban or semi‑urban areas, completed an online questionnaire during the early phase of APV implementation in Italy, thus providing anticipatory evaluations. Hierarchical regressions and path analyses show that technological beliefs, especially perceptions of global and local sustainability, are the strongest predictors of agrivoltaics’ acceptability. Contextual beliefs, notably legitimacy, fairness, and trust in agrivoltaics’ technical-scientific actors, further enhance acceptability. Personal beliefs contribute as well: injunctive norms encourage acceptability, whereas anticipatory solastalgia significantly hinders it. The findings provide a quantitative baseline against which context-specific case studies can be interpreted as installations spread across the territory in the future. Findings suggest that policy and communication should highlight agrivoltaics’ environmental and socio-economic benefits and engage local experts rather than political actors; implications concerning landscape framing are advanced as hypotheses to be tested with affected populations. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Piezoelectric sensor based on MWCNTs/SEBS stretchable composite electrode for human motion monitoring
abstract: Wearable piezoelectric electronics promise self-powered sensing for health monitoring and human-machine interfaces, yet their practical deployment is hampered by a long-standing trade-off between stretchability and output performance. Here, we report a co-engineered strategy that simultaneously optimizes both electrodes and active layers. A MWCNTs/SEBS composite electrode forms a stiff, percolating network with metal-like conductivity, high tensile compliance, and hydrophobic stability, enabling robust charge transport under sweat and strain. Concurrently, BaTiO₃ nanoparticles induce a β-phase-rich P(VDF-TrFE) matrix, supplying a high density of switchable dipoles. The hybrid delivers open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current of ~20.1 V and ~4.33 μA, respectively. Demonstrated in a 4 × 4 sensor array, the system decodes joint motions and gait patterns in real time. This design offers a promising pathway toward soft-electrode-integrated, durable, and high-performance piezoelectric skins for next-generation wearable electronics. © 2026

title: Should I “stay” or should I “go”? Influence of an anticipated stop on cortical correlates of overground walking
abstract: Real-world walking frequently requires pedestrians to maintain proactive inhibition to safely navigate unpredictable environments. While cortical modulations occurring during locomotion under environmental uncertainty are well-established, the specific proactive mechanisms underlying this state of inhibitory anticipation remain unexplored. This study aimed to investigate the behavioral and cortical shifts associated with anticipating a stop during overground walking. Fourteen healthy young adults performed fluent and cautious walking tasks with an expected stop. Cortical activity and trunk acceleration were recorded using a 32-channel mobile electroencephalography and an integrated accelerometer. Step-1 latency and step-interval variability were calculated via heel strike detection. Gait-phase-related power modulations were computed, and spectral principal component analysis was applied to attenuate artifacts. The results revealed that cautious walking significantly increased step-interval variability, whereas step-1 latency remained unaffected. At the cortical level, left frontotemporal areas exhibited an attenuated and delayed theta desynchronization during the swing phase. Furthermore, centroparietal regions demonstrated an altered temporal profile of alpha and beta synchronization, characterized by enhanced late-stance synchronization and reduced swing-phase synchronization. The present findings suggest that anticipating a potential stop may alter the rhythmic consistency of gait and reorganize phase-specific cortical dynamics. Being prepared to stop may shift the neural control of automated locomotion toward active monitoring, highlighting the relevance of proactive inhibition during everyday mobility. © 2026 The Authors

title: Atypical early-life ultrasonic vocalizations disrupt the pup-dam communication dyad in the BTBR model of autism spectrum disorder
abstract: Alterations in early-life communication are a defining feature of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). While these deficits are well conserved in mouse models, few studies have assessed how aberrations in neonatal vocalizations affect maternal behaviors and disrupt the pup-dam communication dyad. To better elucidate the consequences of altered communication in ASD models, we assessed ultrasonic vocalization (USV) production in pups and the corresponding retrieval behaviors in dams using C57 and BTBR (autistic-like) mice. We first used the pup's dam as the retriever and found that BTBR dams retrieved significantly fewer pups than C57 dams. We then used a novel C57 dam as the retriever and found that BTBR pups were retrieved significantly slower than C57 pups. Follow-up analyses detected positive correlations between call duration and retrieval time and amplitude and retrieval time in BTBR pups. Similarly, we found that C57 mice that were retrieved the fastest had calls of a lower amplitude than slowly retrieved mice. In the BTBR model, we found that faster retrieved mice produced shorter calls with a higher pitch than slowly retrieved mice, displaying call characteristics more similar to C57 pups. Lastly, we found that a more diverse call type repertoire was associated with a faster retrieval time. Overall, our study demonstrates that altered USV production significantly affects the pup-dam communication dyad. Furthermore, we identified the USV duration, amplitude, and a more diverse call type repertoire as being critical factors underlying maternal retrieval. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Metacognitive monitoring in Kenyan, Chinese, and U.S. children
abstract: Theories of cognitive development propose that cultural values shape metacognitive skills. However, cross-cultural research on metacognition remains limited and often relies on verbal assessments that may lack validity across cultural contexts. The present study examined metacognitive monitoring in Kenyan, Chinese, and U.S. children (N = 95; 6–10-year-olds; 46% female) using a non-verbal problem-solving task in which children assembled objects according to a model. Across all three cultural contexts, children exhibited various monitoring behaviors (e.g., checking the model), and the frequency of these behaviors increased with age. Cross-cultural differences emerged in the specific monitoring strategies children used: Chinese children engaged in more thorough monitoring than Kenyan and U.S. children. These findings highlight both culturally-recurrent and culturally-variable patterns in children’s metacognitive monitoring. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Visualizing multiphase flow and vapor dynamics during microwave reheating of food
abstract: Microwave reheating of water-rich, deformable porous media, such as cooked meat, can produce abrupt vapor-release and sample-deformation events; however, the coupled thermal, transport, and mechanical processes underlying these events remain difficult to access experimentally. Here, cooked chicken was treated as a water- and lipid-containing deformable porous medium, and kitchen-scale experiments were combined with high-speed imaging, fluorescent fiber-optic temperature measurements, photogrammetric reconstruction, and coupled electromagnetic–thermal–granular–poroelastic simulations. High-speed image analysis resolved macroscale sample displacement and a visible two-phase jet-front displacement of (Formula presented) mm, corresponding to an apparent interval-averaged lower-bound velocity of (Formula presented). Non-metallic fiber-optic probes recorded an above-surface temperature near 372–373 K during sustained vapor release and a distinct subsurface thermal transition near 20 s, from approximately 360–374 K to 348–365 K. The absence of a simultaneous above-surface transition supports the interpretation of a localized subsurface venting and rewetting event rather than a sample-wide explosion. The reconstructed specimen geometry and measured phase allocation were used to initialize a coupled model of spatially non-uniform microwave power deposition, vapor generation, porous transport, lipid clustering, permeability reduction, and tissue deformation. The simulations identify contrasting dispersed-lipid and lipid-clustered regimes: open pathways support vapor percolation, whereas local hydraulic choking promotes pressure buildup and stress localization. An order-of-magnitude energetic estimate indicates that release of a sub-milligram vapor reservoir could supply the mechanical energy associated with a resolved upward-ejection event. These results combine direct thermal and kinematic measurements with a coupled modeling framework for investigating localized vapor venting, deformation, and splattering during microwave reheating of porous foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Evaluating role-prompted LLM responses on autism-related Theory-of-Mind tasks
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can perform well on social-reasoning benchmarks, but it remains unclear whether role prompting can produce distinguishable response patterns on autism-related Theory of Mind (ToM) tasks. This question matters for developing neurodiversity-aware AI evaluation, but any such work must distinguish behavioral output patterns from claims about autistic cognition or lived experience. In this paper, we introduce a ToM evaluation covering 11 established task types and four instructional personas: neurotypical and ASD Levels 1–3, labeled using DSM-5 support levels as heuristic anchors rather than validated clinical profiles. We curate 460 multiple-choice items and test state-of-the-art LLMs of varying scales. Baseline results show that in the original experiments, even detailed persona prompts do not yield reliable accuracy differentiation across model families, with smaller models often failing to meaningfully distinguish the imposed personas. A prompt-specificity ablation shows that explicit speech, cognitive-style, and response constraints substantially strengthen persona differentiation. Native-thinking configurations enlarge full-profile accuracy gaps and improve role-only accuracy, while some role-only conditions retain weaker, model-dependent ordering. To improve role fidelity, we implement an actor–critic workflow in which the actor produces in-character answers and the critic enforces persona constraints. After actor–critic, higher ASD levels exhibit lower accuracy on advanced ToM tasks and produce shorter utterances with fewer mental-state terms, matching the prompt-specified profile constraints. We further examine scale and alignment: larger models tend to increase overall accuracy while preserving role fidelity in our experiments, whereas general alignment tuned for helpfulness via preference optimization raises average correctness but reduces persona separability, collapsing the prompt-induced gradient. Overall, with targeted role scaffolding, current LLMs can produce role-prompted approximations of ASD-informed response patterns on constrained, text-based, multiple-choice tasks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Followership, teamwork, and wellness among nursing students: A cross-sectional study
abstract: Background: Effective followership is progressively acknowledged as an essential professional competency in healthcare. However, nursing education has traditionally emphasized leadership development, resulting in a limited understanding of how followership relates to teamwork and wellness during professional preparation. Evidence regarding effective followership among nursing students remains scarce. Objective: To examine the relationships among effective followership, teamwork, individual wellness, and organizational wellness among nursing students and to identify factors associated with effective followership. Methods: A cross-sectional correlational study was conducted among 325 nursing students recruited from universities in Jordan. Participants completed an online survey comprising measures of effective followership, teamwork perceptions, individual wellness, and organizational wellness. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, and multiple linear regression were used to examine the data. Exploratory factor analysis was conducted to evaluate the construct validity of the investigator-developed measures. Results: Students reported moderate levels of effective followership and teamwork perceptions. Effective followership demonstrated strong positive associations with teamwork perceptions (r = 0.66), individual wellness (r = 0.59), and organizational wellness (r = 0.59). Multiple linear regression showed that teamwork (β = 0.576, p < 0.001), GPA (β = 0.210, p < 0.001), and academic level (β = 0.083, p = 0.041) were significant predictors of effective followership, with the model explaining 47.10% of the variance (R2 = 0.471). Students demonstrating greater active engagement, accountability, and independent critical thinking reported more positive collaborative and wellness experiences. Conclusion: Effective followership appears to be an important professional competency associated with teamwork and wellness among nursing students. The results support consideration of the inclusion of followership development alongside leadership preparation within nursing curricula. Educational strategies that promote active engagement, accountability, constructive communication, and shared responsibility may better prepare students for interprofessional healthcare practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Patient education for older adults with cancer and their caregivers: A scoping review
abstract: Introduction Patient education is essential for older adults with cancer and their caregivers to support understanding of diagnosis and treatment. However, the evidence describing patient education interventions has not been comprehensively mapped. Our objective was to characterize the features, delivery approaches, and outcomes of patient education interventions developed for older adults with cancer and/or their caregivers across any study design, and to identify gaps in the evidence. Materials and methods A scoping review was conducted using the Arksey and O’Malley framework and reported according to the PRISMA-ScR guideline. MEDLINE, EMBASE, EMCARE, CENTRAL, PsycINFO, and Scopus were searched on January 23, 2025. Studies published from 2000 onward were included if they evaluated healthcare professional-delivered patient education. Results From 26,898 records screened, 93 studies met inclusion criteria. Most interventions were delivered pre-treatment (n = 63), with surgery the most common context (n = 31). Common aims included side-effect prevention (n = 32) and supporting treatment decision-making (n = 26). Caregiver involvement was limited. Outcomes were clustered into 20 domains. Frequent reported domains were satisfaction/acceptability (52 occurrences) and knowledge/understanding (46 occurrences), while caregiver outcomes and clinical endpoints were rarely assessed. Discussion Patient education interventions generally improved knowledge and satisfaction, but evidence for clinical or system-level impacts remains limited. Key gaps include minimal integration of geriatric assessment, limited adaptation for cognitive impairment, sparse caregiver-specific outcomes, and inconsistent reporting of unintended effects. Future research should better integrate caregiver needs and geriatric principles into patient education design. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Opportunities for mathematical reasoning within teacher-student interactions in a Thinking Classroom context
abstract: Developing students’ capacity to reason mathematically is a key aim of mathematics teaching. However, how such reasoning is supported remains complex. This study examines teacher-student interaction and students’ opportunities for mathematical reasoning in a Thinking Classroom context. While Thinking Classroom is designed to increase student engagement and mathematical thinking through substantial changes to classroom organisation, relatively little is known about how teacher-student interaction unfolds within this instructional context. The study draws on 34 video recordings from five upper secondary mathematics classrooms implementing the first three practices of the teaching approach Thinking Classroom, which concern task selection, random group formation, and work at vertical non-permanent surfaces. A thematic analysis of 124 teacher-student interactions identified four recurring patterns of interaction. Drawing on selected concepts from a complex dynamic systems perspective, these patterns are interpreted as relatively stable. The analysis further examines the students' opportunities for reasoning within these patterns. Opportunities for mathematical reasoning differed across the four patterns and often remained brief, even in interactions where reasoning was most visible. The findings suggest that, in the observed classrooms implementing the first three practices of Thinking Classroom, opportunities for sustained reasoning within teacher-student interaction were limited. The present study highlights the challenges involved in supporting mathematical reasoning and the importance of teachers’ interactional choices in creating and sustaining opportunities for reasoning. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Quantitative analysis of causation in flight operation accidents: Event logic knowledge modeling and decoupled Bayesian network inference
abstract: Aviation accident reports contain rich causal information for flight operation safety, yet existing methods cannot quantify multi-factor co-occurrence or cross-phase patterns, impeding phase-specific prevention. This makes a multi-state complex causation analysis framework theoretically valuable and practically urgent. A quantitative causal analysis framework for flight operation accidents is proposed. Multiple models are integrated to construct a multi-level event logic graph ontology, and core entities and relationships are extracted by evolutionary logic, forming a complete knowledge skeleton. A semi-automated strategy combining large language model pre-annotation with expert verification achieves low-cost, high-consistency transformation of unstructured texts into computable knowledge. Mapping rules from the event logic graph to the Bayesian network are established, decoupling multi-state nodes into binary nodes, enabling expression of multi-factor co-occurrence and joint conditional effects. Network parameters are learned in a data-driven manner, and the differential contributions of causal factors across flight phases are analyzed, providing quantitative foundations for differentiated safety management strategies. The innovative approach realizes an end-to-end transformation from semi-structured accident texts to probabilistic risk models and establishes a full-chain technical system encompassing ontology modeling, knowledge extraction, structure mapping, and probabilistic inference, offering a reusable methodological framework and engineering pathway for data-driven quantitative causation analysis. title: Rocky past, hazy future: Childhood adversity and adult prospection
abstract: Two preregistered studies tested whether childhood adversity is associated with hazy future thinking, characterized by reduced clarity and detail in imagined future events and a more negative emotional outlook toward the future, and whether it is related to higher levels of intolerance of uncertainty. In Study 1 ( N = 232; 77.2% female, 22% male, 0.8% other or not specified), when asked to consider the future, participants with higher childhood adversity reported less vivid, detailed, and optimistic future thoughts, with more hopelessness and negative emotions. In Study 2 ( N = 262; 79.4% female, 19.8% male, 0.8% other or not specified), higher adversity was related to lower confidence, persistence, and commitment regarding goals. Separating adversity into harshness and unpredictability revealed that unpredictability was more consistently associated with both cognitive and emotional aspects of hazy future thinking, even when controlling for harshness. Also, higher childhood unpredictability was associated with higher intolerance of uncertainty in both studies. These findings provide evidence that early-life unpredictability is related to less cognitively clear and more emotionally negative visions of the future. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Cross-language vulnerability migration in the rust supply chain: A survey of mechanisms, risks, and countermeasures
abstract: Rust is widely adopted in system software and critical infrastructure due to its ownership model and compile-time memory-safety guarantees. However, modern Cargo-based software systems frequently combine unsafe Rust code, foreign-function interfaces, wrapper crates, generated bindings, native C/C++ components, build scripts, and transitive dependencies. These mechanisms create cross-language vulnerability paths through which upstream vulnerabilities or vulnerability-relevant assumptions may become reachable, transformed, or amplified in Rust software. In this survey, we use cross-language vulnerability migration (CLVM) as an analytical term for tracing such paths, rather than as a vulnerability class independent of unsafe-Rust safety, FFI safety, or software supply-chain security. Following Kitchenham's guidelines for systematic literature reviews, we analyze 168 studies published between January 2021 and April 2026. Using an evidence-layered synthesis, we distinguish Rust-specific evidence from upstream, comparative-ecosystem, and general supply-chain governance evidence and examine how security-relevant conditions cross unsafe, FFI, migration, and native-component boundaries before being propagated or amplified through Cargo dependencies. Once a vulnerability or security-relevant assumption has crossed a language or native-component boundary, its impact may be amplified or obscured through transitive dependencies, incomplete metadata, delayed remediation, and limited supply-chain visibility. The evidence is strongest for individual mechanisms: translation studies mainly assess correctness and unsafe-surface reduction, while complete sequences from a foreign or native origin to Rust-side reachability, dependency-level propagation, and downstream remediation remain rarely analyzed. These findings reveal the limits of language-centric security approaches and highlight the need for boundary-aware, reachability-aware, native-aware, and governance-aware defenses for Rust supply chains. © 2026

title: Primary care effectiveness, multimorbidity, and hospital use in public and private health-care systems in Brazil: a cross-sectional analysis of data from the 2019–2021 Brazilian longitudinal study of aging
abstract: Background: Whether patient-reported experiences in primary care modify the association between multimorbidity and emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations remains unclear. We examined these associations across public and private health system sectors among Brazilians aged ≥50 years. Methods: This cross-sectional study used nationally representative data from the 2019–2021 Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Aging. Multimorbidity was defined as the presence of ≥2 of 13 chronic conditions. A 12-item patient-reported primary care effectiveness index captured access, continuity, communication, and coordination with participants’ usual source of healthcare. Primary outcomes were ED visits and hospitalizations in the past 12 months. Poisson regression models estimated associations with the outcomes, and assessed interactions among multimorbidity, primary care effectiveness, and health system sectors. Findings: Among 9058 participants (mean age = 66.3 ± 9.9 years; females = 55.3%; White race/ethnicity = 46.4%), 38.0% had multimorbidity. Overall, 12.5% reported an ED visit and 6.0% ≥ 1 hospitalization in the past 12 months. Multimorbidity was associated with approximately twice the prevalence of ED visits and three times the prevalence of hospitalizations. Primary care effectiveness modified these associations across health system sectors (three-way interaction p = 0.04 for ED visits and p < 0.001 for hospitalization). In the public system, higher primary care effectiveness attenuated the association between multimorbidity and hospitalization (interaction prevalence ratio [PR] = 0.74, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.63–0.87). In contrast, in the private system, higher primary care effectiveness strengthened the associations of multimorbidity with ED visits (interaction PR = 1.40, 95% CI = 1.18–1.66) and hospitalization (interaction PR = 1.75, 95% CI = 1.22–2.50). Interpretation: Associations between multimorbidity and healthcare use varied according to patient-reported primary care experiences and health system sector. title: Colors of perfectionism - How experimental feedbacks change physiology using Mandalas
abstract: Although the link between perfectionism, performance, and feedback has been widely studied, findings remain inconclusive, partly due to the lack of objective assessment methods. Biological correlates, such as heart rate variability, may help clarify these relationships. This study investigates physiological responses to performance feedback during a coloring task and examines the association between perfectionism and task performance. Eighty-three participants (Mage = 20.74, SD = 3.41), including 64 females, completed the study, with perfectionism assessed using the Short Almost Perfect Scale (SAPS). Heart rate variability (HRV) was recorded to assess autonomic nervous system activity. Participants took part in an experimental intervention involving a 10-min mandala coloring task, during which they received positive, negative, and neutral performance feedback. Higher High Standards scores were significantly associated with fewer correctly colored pixels (τ = −0.161, p = .036) and reduced overall coverage (τ = −0.153, p = .046), and these associations remained significant after controlling for age and gender. Higher Discrepancy scores were also significantly associated with fewer correctly colored pixels (τ = −0.153, p = .046) and reduced overall coverage (τ = −0.150, p = .049), although these associations were no longer significant after controlling for age and gender. Neither perfectionism dimension was significantly associated with HRV responses to evaluative feedback. Exploratory analyses revealed associations between HRV responses to evaluative feedback and overall coloring performance. The results suggest that different dimensions of perfectionism are associated with task performance, while physiological responses to evaluative feedback are related to overall coloring performance. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Managing Perils at Sea: a diagnostic analysis of occupational hazards among small-scale fishers in India’s southern coasts
abstract: Marine fishing is a high-risk occupation that sustains the livelihoods of coastal communities worldwide. This study highlights the occupational hazards associated with marine fishing, drawing on an empirical case study of the high-intensity, multi-day offshore fishing sector in southern India. Following the FAO/ILO/IMO joint framework on occupational health and safety of fishers, our research revealed significant deficiencies in the adoption of safety devices, communication technologies, and navigation systems by sample fishers in the study areas. These gaps, compounded by weak regulatory enforcement and low insurance coverage, pose substantial risks, exacerbated by climate change. The findings underscore the need for targeted interventions—including awareness campaigns, training, and financial aid—to foster a robust safety culture and mitigate economic barriers, leading to improved fisher safety and well-being in the coastal regions of India. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: DPIR: Dynamic propagation inconsistency reasoning for explainable fake news detection with large vision-language models
abstract: With the rapid dissemination of multimodal content on social media, fake news detection faces increasingly complex challenges. Although existing methods can leverage textual and visual information for multimodal analysis, they often focus on static cross-modal consistency while overlooking the temporal-aware semantic divergence between news content and propagation evidence during information diffusion. To this end, this paper proposes an explainable fake news detection model based on Dynamic Propagation Inconsistency Reasoning (DPIR). Specifically, a temporal permeation strategy is introduced to dynamically fuse multimodal information and capture temporal-aware semantics within propagation sequences. Local semantic communities are leveraged to identify inconsistency patterns, and evidence-aware semantic aggregation is performed from a dynamic defense perspective. Finally, multi-source information is integrated to generate robust news representations. Extensive experiments conducted on three real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the comparison methods in detection performance, achieving a 2.9% improvement in accuracy on the PHEME dataset, while providing reasonable and interpretable explanations for the detection results. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Closing the gap or transforming the crisis? A qualitative study on the mentoring model as a sustainable solution to instructor shortage in surgical nursing education
abstract: Background: Pressures on the global nursing education workforce and a growing shortage of clinical educators in surgical settings have placed preceptorship models at the heart of education. Viewing nursing education as a “revenue-generating commodity” raises concerns regarding the erosion of academic identity and the risk of disciplinary expertise being reduced to a technical craft. Aim: This study aimed to describe the effects of the mentorship model in surgical nursing education on academic identity, pedagogical processes, and workforce sustainability, based on the perceptions of academicians and clinical mentor nurses. Design: A study using a qualitative descriptive design was conducted to gather in-depth perspectives from stakeholders in academic and clinical fields. Method: Data were collected through semi-structured individual interviews; audio recordings were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using a self-reflective thematic analysis framework. The study involved 10 academics from the Department of Surgical Nursing and 10 preceptor nurses who supervise students in surgical clinics (Total N = 20). Findings: The analysis revealed four main themes: a shift in academic identity, highlighting the transition of academics from clinical expertise to administrative coordination; pedagogical tension, pointing to the risk of surgical nursing education devolving into the mere transfer of technical skills—or a “watch-and-do” model; a sustainability paradox, describing the invisible labor undertaken by clinical preceptors and the accompanying sense of burnout; and institutional disconnect, revealing—through the participants' own words—the gap between theory and clinical reality. Conclusions: The findings indicate that participants perceive a significant risk regarding the sustainability of the current preceptorship model. Key implications arising from these findings include the development of defined collaboration protocols between the university and the hospital, the recognition of the educational contributions made by clinical preceptor nurses, and the piloting of clinical-academic hybrid staffing models. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
